I don't know whether they need to clean their water filter or their ice machine needs a through cleaning, but something was definitely off.
 
All the personnel were friendly and efficient, from the hostess and server, to the manager.  Perhaps just an off day for them, as several of the other reviewers in the past seemed to have good experiences.

6/11/2019 Update
After my first excellent experience with this pizza parlor, I had a taste to try it again.  This time I ordered ahead for another large thick pizza, plain cheese.  During the course of the call the employee yelled back:  "Do we have any Long Island Grandma pizzas left?"  The person he was yelling to responded: "four."  I was wondering the first time how it only took 15 minutes to cook a thick crust pizza.  This made me think something was going on, like the pizzas were partially cooked already.
 
That all is beside the point.  This time the pizza was ready when I arrive to pick it up 20 minutes after placing the order.  The difference in quality was substantial from my first experience, and not in a good way.  The taste was rather bland, like mozzarella cheese with no seasoning or other added cheeses.  Also, where one corner of the pizza was warm (not quite hot). the opposite corner of the pizza was room temperature.  Time to drive home after picking up the pizza was 6 minutes, so that wasn't a factor.
 
So like so many other places, this one is inconsistent as well.  Not sure if I will give it another try.

I used to really like Ruby Tuesday in Valrico.  I decided to go there for lunch the other day and found out they have been closed for months.  I was very disappointed.  An internet search found that there was a Ruby Tuesday in Riverview / Gibsonton so I thought I would take the drive.
 
Parking was okay and although the restaurant was fairly crowded I was seated immediately.  I used to love the salad bar as an add on to my meal, but I knew my appetite wouldn't support it now.  I did pass by the salad bar and everything looked fresh and I was happy to see that it included cottage cheese which had disappeared from the Valrico Ruby Tuesday.
 
My server appeared promptly to take my drink order, delivered it quickly, and took my food order.  I decided on the special "Pick 3" of a half slab of ribs, fries, Caesar salad, cheese sticks, and cake for dessert.  I would have preferred some other appetizer, but there were only 3 choices and no substitutions.  Nothing to write home about for the salad or appetizer.  I hadn't quite finished the salad and appetizier when the ribs hit the table.  I hadn't had baby back ribs for a while so I was looking forwarded to them.  Unfortunately they were rather tough, and only medium in size.  There was no ketchup on the table (I like for my fries) and it took a while to catch my server and ask for a bottle.
 
My server saw I had finished with the main course and asked if I had decided on the dessert, or which there were 3 listed on the menu.  She added that they were out of the Apple Crumble (but they would have more delivered tomorrow!).  I decided on the pan baked cookie topped with vanilla ice cream.  This turned out to be a mistake, as it was in fact half a pan backed cookie swimming in the already melted ice cream.
 
All in all average service and very mediocre food.  A great disappointment, as I loved the Ruby Tuesday in Valrico.

I hate giving one star reviews and always feel a need to soften the blow.  Romano Greek Italian Restaurant was a Greek Restaurant, then added Italian, and now has banners that the offer pizza.  It occupies 3 store widths in a little obscure strip mall on Robertson near the Publix on west SR60.  I went today during lunch hour and the largish interior had many tables filled.  I got the sense that many of these were regular clients.
 
I was quickly seated at a table, and my server brought me a multi-page menu and a place setting and took my  drink order, Coke of course.   I'm really trying hard to find some good things to say here, but the coke was my first impression, and it wasn't positive.  Perhaps the fountain syrup mix needed to be adjusted.  It wasn't bad, just tasted like generic Cola, not Coca Cola.
 
I have included pictures of some of the menu pages, which included Greek dishes, Italian Dishes, even hamburgers and subs.  There were not any of the desserts listed in the menu that were in a vertical see through case near the front door (each covered in saran wrap, not a good sign).
 
For some unexplained reason I focused on the chicken parmigiana in the menu which came with spaghetti and marinara sauce.   There was also a choice of soup or salad,  I asked what soups were available, and in the list was French onion soup for a $1.50 up charge.  I don't know what possessed me, French onion soup it was.
 
The soup came first.  It kind of looked okay, covered in cheese, but the cheese was not browned at all.  Overlooking the cheese I took a spoonful of the broth, and it was so salty I grabbed for the cola-esque drink.  The cheese was rather tasteless, and the saltiness ruined it for me.  Suggestion:  don't order the French Onion soup.  
 
The  chicken parmigiana with side of spaghetti and marinara sauce came a few minutes later.  The texture of the chicken was soft, so much so that I cut it in half to make sure it was thoroughly cooked (it was).  But, the breading was unusual to my taste, and just not to my liking.  The marinara sauce was rather plain, so when the server came by to ask if everything was okay, I asked:  "don't you have Parmesan cheese for the pasta?"  She darted over to a serving station, grabbed a shaker of Parmesan cheese and brought it over.  Copious amounts of cheese made the pasta kind of okay.
 
The attached pictures will tell much of the story.  I fled the restaurant not really wanting to explain why I had eaten so little.
 
I think the moral of this story is that if you go to a restaurant that serves Greek food, order the Greek food.  Romano's has been in business for 40 years, so clearly many people like it.  I may return to try the Gyro platter, sometime in the future.  Again, there were lot's of tables filled with happy looking customers, so there must be some very good dishes?  They also serve pizza, but didn't provide a pizza menu until I asked at the end of the meal to see what was on it.

This update is for their chocolate milkshakes.  Stopped by today as I needed a fix for my addiction.  There is a lot more to a chocolate milkshake than mixing up some ice cream, chocolate syrup, and milk.  A true artist gets the proportion of ingredients just right and blends to just the right consistency.  Campbell's Dairyland achieved perfection today.  Bravo.

Stopped by one a weekday about mid afternoon.  I tried to avoid the crowd, and I was successful.  My primary mission was to satisfy my craving for some good fried shrimp, which they have on their hot bar.  About $8 got me a "small" order which was in reality more than a generous portion of large to jumbo fried shrimp with a tempura type breading.  The shrimp were cooked perfectly, and very tasty.  I also picked up some black and white cookies, which were more like small cakes.  These were a bit bland, not the same type you would expect to find at a Jo-El's or a Kosher bakery.  Price for the cookies were $2.50 each.
 
The service was top notch, and there is a vast selection of baked goods, with a smallish section of prepared hot dishes.

All in all a good choice, and I will return.

So glad they're reopened! This place has upped their game. The quiche option is always vegetarian, so I can count on it when I can't decide what to eat. Awesome cream cheese flavors too; I got the shallot, but will try olive pimento next time. The lattes are strong and extra shots are cheap. Service is greatly improved and the space is bigger than you first think- just take a peek around the corner. Plenty of parking on the side and around back.

I couldn't come to NOLA without going to John Besh's restaurant. 

We came here on a cold rainy day for happy hour and it was just perfect.

HAPPY HOUR

SAZERAC: rye, sugar, Peychaud's bitters & Herbsaint. To get me in the NOLA mood..
Actually hit the spot on a rainy day!

T. CHARLES STREETCAR: St. Germain, pear vodka & champagne. To get me in the NINA mood.. mmm..

50 CENT OYSTERS: Hello.. The cheapest oysters I have ever had in my life at John Besh's restaurant? $1 is as low as I have seen for happy hour. Not the best quality but hey, I'm not complaining.. love oysters.

**SHRIMP AND GRITS- roasted jalapeño cheese grits, andouille & green onion sausages. I Mean....

TERRINE OF SLOW COOKED FOIE GRAS - You better believe I ate Foie any chance I got once I left Cali. It is not cruel, it is delicious!This one was a little too pate-ish for me though.

*MOULES ET FRITES - Prince Edward Island mussels, steamed with garlic & thyme. Can't go wrong with that. Extra bread to soak, yes please and thank you!

**BREAD PUDDING - I mean whats not to love about bread pudding. This one was nothing short of fabulous. What a great way to end a great meal.

Only giving this 3 stars because everyone thought the cake was delicious. Customer service deserves 1 star. When I went to order the cake, the person who helped me, I believe Ali, was extremely rude and not very willing to work with me. It was a graduate school graduation cake and the graduation happened to fall on a birthday. We wanted her to write "Congratulations on your Master's Degree" and then add in "happy birthday" somewhere small in the corner or something. After dealing with Ali being very rude and unhappy with this idea, she agreed it it, and we left. I picked up the cake and it said, "Congratulations and happy birthday on your Master's Degree", which clearly makes no sense. I did not have them fix it as I did it have the time or energy to deal with them again. Cake tasted good, but will not be back.

Melt-in-your-mouth-five-star-goodness!

Magnifico! Bravo!

We ordered the LASAGNE ALLA BOLOGNESE: layers of homemade pasta smothered with meat sauce, bechamel and parmesan cheese. Perfetto! The meat is obviously home-ground, not any of this cheapo hamburger from the grocery. The flavor, perfect, the texture, perfect, the pasta, sauce, and cheese--all perfect.

We also had the SALMOME AL CARTOCCIO: salmon cooked in parchment paper with garlic, lemon juice, italian parsley, fresh vegetables. Wow! Perfetto! The salmon was not over done and not under done. Flaky but tender and juicy. Soooooo good. 

Oh, our anitpasto was the CAPRESE: fresh mozzarella (in water), organic tomatoes, fresh basil, kalamata olives, oregano and extra virgin olive oil. Great invention. Wonder who thought of that? "Hey, let's put mozzarella on some tomato slices and top it off with basil." But it works and it works well. Nice and refreshing.

Service was very cheerful. Loved our waitress.

Definitely a five star restaurant. And so reasonably priced, too.

Well this family is on a roll opening up all these great restaurants. He said they are not done yet, either, and that's good for Tucson.

We had the guacamole hummus appetizer and it was pretty good. Comes with home made corn chips and some dried? fried? plantain slices.

My wife had street tacos and she gave me a bite--delish! I had a Vida bowl with half grain and half greens. I also opted for the steak and salmon and my sides were the Brussels sprouts and the cauliflower. Very delicious! The Brussels were lightly crisply on the outside. How do they do that? The cauliflower was seasoned and very tasty.

Friends had an enchilada + taco plate and a Vida burrito. They both enjoyed it very much. 

The salsas are great. There was one that was orange-ish in color and was really tasty.

This is not a cheap place, but well worth it. Very nice atmosphere. The waitress really knew her stuff. There are so many decisions you have to make with almost each entrée and I jokingly said it was an interrogation. It will help if you check out the menu before you come so that you have some idea of what to expect.

5* = A top favorite. Mind-blowing good. I will definitely return and I will go out of my way to go here. Worth every dime of my money.
4* = Outstanding. Tucson-top-tier. Some elements not quite as good as it gets, but it still is worthy of my regular business.
3* = Good experience. I might do repeat business if it is convenient, the only option, the only one in its category, or on a whim, but would not be among the first thing to come to mind. Would definitely recommend you trying it to get your own take on it.
2* = Not so good. Would not recommend at all. Waste of money.
1* = How are they still in business? Stay away at all costs!

The owner reached out and apologized after our last experience and asked to give them another try, which we did.

One word--delightful!

The menu consists of "savory" or "sweet." They also have a breakfast menu. But all of that is just to give you an idea of what to order or make the decision making easier because the reality of it is that they will allow you to create your own crépe with any combination of ingredients. Yum!

We ordered a ham, Brie, tomato, and spinach crépe. We also ordered a Swedish Lindenberry with bananas. It came with whipped cream. Both were really delicious. The crépe itself was light and slightly sweet. Very tasty. The ham crépe came with a sauce the side that we couldn't tell what it was, it was so light. It was difficult to choose whether to use e sauce or not because the crépe tasted good with it and it also tasted good without it.

They have board and card games to play and we chose "Blink." We had fun playing while waiting for our order. 

At the time of this writing, this is their last day at their current location. They will be moving to Oracle Ave. and are shooting to open the first week of March. I wish them all the best in their move and at their new location. I hope they stay open for a long time.

After reading a review of Tucson Yelp's manager, Isabella J., on this restaurant, we decided to eat here for our anniversary last night. Here's a summary of our experience: Wow! 

Located in the upscale Casas Adobes Plaza, at Ina Road and Oracle, parking was ample and convenient. We had reservations and upon arrival and were promptly seated. The patio was enclosed with seasonal plastic panels and had outdoor heat lamps. We dined inside, however, and was given our choice of a comfortable booth that could sit five or six.

The exterior and interior design is upscale, contemporary though not outlandish, and very tastefully done. The layout was organized and did not seem crowded. Though there was a table of customers in casual dress, I recommend business casual and up.

The service was impeccable. Our server, Lexi, was knowledgeable on all of the items. I watched her and noticed that every time she came to a transition she would glance our way to check on us. Therefore, when we were ready to order, she knew to come to the table, when we were finished with our soup and salad, she cleared the dishes, when I needed a refill on my lemonade, she came and asked me if I wanted another, when we were finished with our main course, she cleared the dishes and asked if we were interested in dessert, when we were finishing with dessert, she brought the bill. 

A very nice touch was that after clearing used dishes and before bringing out the next course, she cleaned the table, too. When we ordered, we mentioned that we would like to share the soup and salad, she and her assistant brought it out in separate bowls and plates without asking. She was cheerful and not overbearing.

Our meals were incredible from start to finish. The table bread is served with a very tasty dip of olive and canola oil, infused with parsley and red bell peppers. We had the daily soup special of creamed vegetable and the butterleaf lettuce salad. Both were excellent. We had the lemongrass scallops and the seafood special which was barramundy, a mild fish similar to sea bass from Australia. Of course my wife and I split each dish.

The crusted scallops come according to your preference of doneness with "forbidden" black rice, melted soy butter, lemongrass and sautéed snap peas. The crusted barramundy came on a bed of risoto that had pine nuts in it. With every initial bite of each element (fish, rice, vegetable, etc.) we each said, "Wow!" It was "wow" through the whole meal. The crust on the barramundy was perfect. I don't know what it consisted of, but it was perfectly thin and perfectly crunchy. The black rice is so intriguing. It has somewhat of a nutty flavor and interesting texture. The scallops were perfectly done (medium well for us). Both dishes were heaven.

I had lemonade to drink. I only mention this because it is my drink of choice at restaurants, if they have it. I pass if it is the awful Coca-Cola Minutemaid product. I really got spoiled living in California where I used tree-ripened lemons and made my own. Most restaurants that make their own lemonade really do not make it that great. Either the quality of lemons used or the mix just doesn't taste as good as my own. Wildflower's lemonade was the best aside from my own that I've had yet at a restaurant. Nice balance of sweetness and tartness, and fresh flavor. I had four glasses.

OK, dessert--the donuts, of course! Who would have thought that donuts would be an excellent fancy dessert? These donuts, so light and fluffy served with créme fraiche, are much talked about in these reviews. Because it was our anniversary, the pastry chef penned beautifully in chocolate, "Happy Anniversary" on the plate. It was great! I don't know if it was because of our anniversary or if it comes with the donuts regularly, but we also had two chocolate covered strawberries, a homemade Oreo-type cookie, and another small cookie.

It was a wonderful experience and we highly recommend this restaurant to all.

I'm so happy that they have a location on the west side, now. It is only 5 minutes from home.

This location is as nice as their Wilmot restaurant. Nice decor, nice tables and chairs, clean, new. Plenty of room inside which kind of surprises you because it doesn't look that big from the outside.

Their pho here is as good as at Wilmot. I had the thin sliced rare beef pho. The broth is tasty. It comes with the usual veggies like bean sprouts, cilantro, jalapeño, something leafy, and a slice of lime. I ordered the large size. You will want to, too.

My wife had their fried spring rolls. It's one of her favorite things to eat. Here, like most Vietnamese restaurants, the spring rolls are appetizers. There were only two that came with it and so we ordered two orders for her. It comes with vermicelli, lettuce, and cilantro. And of course the fish sauce. But it looked a little skimpy on the veggies and it didn't come with bean sprouts. It was still good, though, but not the best spring rolls in town.

If you read my reviews, you know that I love my lemonade. I tried their soda lemonade and it is excellent.

I really do not see why everyone likes Miss Saigon's pho. Dao"s is definitely better in my opinion.

Oh. My. Gosh.
Oh. My. Gosh.
Oh. My. Gosh.
Wow!

Ever since I moved to Tucson 3 years ago, besides best pizza, best burger, best Vietnamese, and best Japanese, I've been trying to find the best Chinese restaurant. By "best," I mean knock-your-socks-off-it's-so-good-I-could-eat-there-every-day-of-my-life. FOUND IT TONIGHT! (Snoopy dance)

I ordered a couple of items for pickup: beef chow fun and ginger chicken. Wow. Now this is what Yelp is all about. I met Jenny Y. at a Yelp Event and she told me about this place. I'm so glad she did. This chow fun is the best I've had since I left home. (I love my Dad's chow fun.) The noodles are cooked just right and not mushy and falling apart. And the beef--HOW IN THE WORLD DO THEY DO THAT? The strips of beef were so melt-in-your-mouth tender. I mean, we do the silken stir fry at home and get it restaurant quality tender. But theirs is unbelievable.

The ginger chicken was delightful. Just watch out for the occasional joint bone and the chunks of ginger. Those caught me by surprise. But the flavor is wonderful.

My two remaining kids at home were both off at their activities for Friday night and my wife is out of town. I was going to enjoy some take out Chinese in front of a movie for entertainment. I brought home this food and put it on my plate. I took the first bite. I sat down at the table. The meal became my entertainment for the next 30 minutes. Oh it was soooo good.

The owner is nice and friendly. She is very proud of their product. When I went to pick it up, she had to open up the chow fun and show it to me. How cute is that? The portions are very generous. I didn't get the small, typical take out boxes. These were the large styrofoam boxes that you get when you are at other restaurants. The chow fun was a typical menu price of $7.95 and the ginger chicken is one of their very few menu items that crossed that barrier at $9.95. The two entrees, the box of rice (good rice, BTW) soy sauce packets, and two fortune cookies were in a cardboard box lid for me to take home. Nice touch.

She told me they used to have a restaurant at Broadway and Camino Seco, if that helps any of you out there in identifying who the owners are. Well, they sold that and started this one. Too bad for you on the east side--we get the benefits now. And I guess even though they haven't been open long, the word's out. They were packed and when I phoned in my order, she said allow 40 minutes because they were so busy.

I am looking at the take-out menu and the lunch combination is a steal! For either $5.25 or $6.25, you get steamed or fried rice, 2 fried wonton or 2 crab puffs, and egg flower or hot and sour soup, plus your entree!

The ambiance is not a dive, but it ain't pretty, either. Eh...who cares? The food is the ambiance here, ladies and gentlemen.

This Asian who is picky about what Asian food goes on his Asian taste buds says eat here. And order off of the Szechwan menu, not the American-Chinese menu.

I AM IN LOOOOOOOOOOOVVVVE!

Was finally at this end of town and stopped in. First tested Marshmallow Mash-Up - "marshmallow infused base mixed with homemade M&M rice crispy treats." WHOAAA! Then I tried Sweet Cream Honey Comb - "sweet cream ice cream with handmade honeycomb pieces." ARE YOU KIDDING ME???!!!!! Then for baseline, I just had to try their "regular" (nothing's "regular" here) Chocolate - "two blends of Ghirardelli chocolate for the perfect chocolate flavor." *GASP* EYES ROLLING IN THE BACK OF MY HEAD

I get two scoops. (Wish I could have gotten four or five.) Sweet Cream Honey Comb and Chocolate.

As I take a spoonful heading out the door, I exclaim in a semi-loud voice, "This is INCREDIBLE!"

Yeah, that good.

I really didn't enjoy this ice cream. However, for someone who is dairy-free, this probably would be ice cream heaven.

Ice cream made out of cashew milk has a distinctive and distracting flavor to it. I believe only a certain flavor combination can mask that flavor. For example, my wife had the Lemon Poppy flavor and that distinctive flavor was somewhat hidden. I had a very strong chocolate flavored scoop, but I could still taste the cashew milk.

I sampled about five flavors and I was not really impressed by any of them. My chocolate had a fine grit in it from the cocoa powder, no doubt. The worker there said that that was their best and most smoothest  batch of chocolate yet. Yikes! She also said that they are still learning about how to make their flavors. There were two batches on the counter that she said were messed up. One was cantaloupe and the other was strawberry.

If you are interested in dairy-free ice cream, my recommendation to you would be to wait for a while until they learn their craft. I know most of the other reviews give this ice cream a glowing report. But my wife and I both did not finish our single scoops and threw them away. This is from a family who considers ice cream and gelato a food group.

Like I said, if you are dairy-free, You will want to give this place a try. As for me and my house, we will stick to regular ice cream a la Sullivan's and Baskin-Robbins etc. and gelato from Allegro's.

This review is for their hamburger--yes their hamburger. WHICH IS THE BEST HAMBURGER I'VE EVER HAD IN MY LIFE!!! Well, let's add a few more exclamation points for more emphasis: !!!!! I will update my review when I try out their other items, maybe even their sandwiches.

So my wife's friend told us about this hamburger, which you have to buy at least 10 lbs. frozen, which they break up into 1 lbs. packages. It runs $2.99/lbs. Now when you look at hamburger sales at your favorite grocer or even what it costs at Sam's Club or Costco, you know this is priced competitively. But none--and I mean NONE--of the aforementioned grocers' hamburger is even in the same class as this meat.

Their hamburger is made from sirloin chuck and steak ends. This 75-80% lean ground beef is the most tender, juiciest, and flavorful ground beef I have ever sunk my teeth into. It was so good, I had grilled burgers four nights in a row! And looked forward to it every time. And was never disappointed ever.

There was not one speck of chewy gristle in any bite. The meat is so tender. You want a real "steak burger?" Make a burger out of this meat. I never need to go to any of my favorite burger places in Tucson ever again. Seriously. My grilled burgers were at least as good, if not better than, the likes of Zinburger, Smashburger, etc. etc. This is the same meat that Sullivan's Eatery and Creamery uses for their famed hamburgers.

You want a great burger? Start with great ground beef. There's no other way around it.

Nice butcher shop with small seating for their deli. I'm a fan.

Finally got to try the much-hyped Roadhouse Cinema with its electric recliners and dine-in service with waiters.

It was worth it.

It was a fun, luxury experience. Worth every penny.

One day, driving north on Swan, I saw their roadsiide marquee that said "$6.00 Tuesdays." I thought no reason to keep me from trying this theater now. So on Tuesday, I took my wife and daughter to see "Jungle Book' (wonderful movie) and we caught the 3:45 showing. First, it's best to purchase your tickets online. There is a $1 surcharge, but worth it. You get to choose your reserved seating, which is best because the seating capacity is limited and chances are that you will not be able to get in on a showing by just coming to the theater.

We arrived 30 minutes early, which I recommend, because that gives you time to get familiar with the theater, how the seats work, the menu and your surroundings. There really is not a bad seat in the house. And the first two rows are not bad, either as the first row is a decent distance away from the screen. And even if it was too close, just recline that seat, baby!

We ordered popcorn and had two flavors in the bowl, as well as their nachos and two rootbeers, which are home brewed in Arizona. It was really good rootbeer and it is one of the few drinks that are not bottomless (the soft drinks and tea are all you can drink), but it does come in a 32 oz. cup with one refill. Well, that's *plenty* of drink for me. The popcorn is homemade in the sense that it wasn't the usual stick it in the yellow oil popper kind. Just like I make popcorn at home, with real butter. (Mine is still better, though. Pat on the back.) The caramel corn was pretty good. Not the best I've ever had, but good to munch on.

I thought the nachos were pretty good. Cheese, beans, lettuce, tomato, and jalapeños top it off. We were there during Happy Hour, so this was one of the munchies that was at half price, so it cost around $4.00. I wouldn't pay $8.00 for it, just sayin'. There are about five munchies on the menu, a pretzel being one, and the potato skins are the only ones they do not do half price during Happy Hour. 

Even though their website says they serve Allegro's gelato, they don't. It is some other brand, I can't remember the name. And they have two flavors from Cashew Cow.

So one problem with eating food at the movie theater is that you can't see what you are eating. I had to fish around for a nacho chip, then fish around to (hopefully) get some topping on it. My wife does not like jalapeños on her nachos and she got a big surprise. So eating food other than popcorn is a trick.

The waiters are very conscious about moving through the theater delivering orders and keeping their heads down so as to not block the view. They also talk quietly. They are obviously well trained in their duties. This was also evident at the conclusion of the movie when an army of their employees came into the theater to clean. They picked up trash, swept, scrubbed the tables, wiped down the seats, etc. etc. Impressive.

I did not find any issue with the small night lights at every other seat to provide lighting to, I assume, read the menu or find the napkin, ketchup, or mustard dispenser. They are at head leve, but one was right next to me and I didn't even notice it.

Each chair has its own swing away table that has a drink holder. Between every pair of chairs, there is a swing away arm with two drink holders. The arm can be swung up and back if you want to turn the two seats into a love seat configuration. Between each love seat is another small table ledge that has the dispensers and a menu. You could also use this space to put items.

The screen is not a huge screen, but it is big enough for this venue and still made good viewing. The sound system is excellent. Again, there really are no bad seats in the house. I am very particular in arriving early enough to get good seats in the middle. Because of the reservation system, all middle seats were taken and we were just off center and I of our trio was the furthest off center. I had no issues at all watching the movie.

At the end, they put my remaining rootbeer in a take home cup. I somewhat sacrilegiously drank it in my A&W glass mug at home. ;) You take your bowl of popcorn to the concession stand and they will put it in a plastic bag and top it off for you to take home. BONUS!

I find that their concession prices are really no different than regular theater prices. Their ticket prices really are not too much different, either, especially if you do it during their special pricing times like on Tuesdays or before evening prime time when tickets are $7.00. What you do get is a great experience, though.

I recommend this theater! It is a lot of fun. I think I'm hooked.

Customer service sucks. Came in to dine on a Sunday afternoon. They had a good size crowd but was not packed. Walked in & stood in line for almost 10 min waiting for someone to acknowledge that I was there. There was an open table for 4 & I was a party of 2. They kept me waiting for a table set up for 2 to empty for another 10 min. While standing/waiting I asked if there was a reason I couldn't have that table. I was told it was their only available setup for 4 & that two other tables set for two were finishing up & theyd seat me when those customers left. WTF !!!  Last time I checked good business is taking care of the customers in front of you, not the ones you're hoping will come in. 

So I waited & got luke warm service. Placed my order & then while I'm sitting there another couple walks up & they break up the table for 4 to change it to seating for two!!!!  OK, now I have real issues with that. You make me wait as if my money wasn't good enough for the empty table for 4 you have open & then you wind up breaking down the table to sit another party of two. 

So needless to say I told them to cancel my order & took my $$$ elsewhere. Ridiculous!!! You lost a repeat customer behind some POOR customer service. Then when I ask you whose the manager you refuse to provide a name. Hope the real manager or owner reads this review #wontbeback

I have spent a very long time trying to find my favorite Mexican Restaurant in Reno/Sparks. 

I feel like to pick an ALL TIME FAVORITE, you have to try it more than once for consistency and also have a lot of others to compare it to. Well, I finally have decided that Bertha Miranda's is it! I have been coming here for years and ALWAYS have the best service, food, experience ect. Though the pandemic my household ordered a lot of different Mexican food and there was never one place that everyone of us loved our food and wanted to keep going back. It was always disappointing. For a while BM had shortened hours and we were unable to order for a bit.

Last night, I was craving Bertha Mirandas and we all agreed that "if it aint broke, don't fix it" and this is the clear cut winner. I called my order in and my food was ready by the time I drove there. The woman on the phone and who I paid with was SO kind and I think restaurants forget that sometimes this is the only person you talk to so they are representing your business.. and she would make me want to come again :) They were a little busy when I got there, but several waiters acknowledged me and let me know they would let them know I was there. 

Food was amazing as always...even after I got it all the way home. BM has the best meatball soup and homemade flour tortillas! The shredded beer chimichanga was the best I have ever had (starting to sound like a broken record!), and my husbands mole burrito was also the best he ever had. The refried beans are delicious and always appreciate when they throw chips in. 

I am done rambling.. just know, you can not go wrong with Bertha Miranda's and you can stop trying to find better. :)

Grimaldi's is where it's at for pizza!!!

Sticking with my trend of eating local in lock down, we tried Grimaldi's at Legends last week. We chose The Don-Traditional Pizza Topped with Italian Sausage, Meatballs and Pepperoni. The toppings were to die for-so think cut and didn't skimp! We ordered through grub hub and there showed an option for the crust to be "crispy", so I decided why not!? Always go crispy.. it was not burnt, but added a crunch. Only critique was the cheese could have been more melted, but that is no fault to the restaurant as it was a to go delivery order. Price on this pizza is pretty steep, but that is to be expected for "upscale" authentic pizza that is what you would find in Rome! 

I can't wait until we can actually go in and sit down to enjoy a pippin hot pizza fresh out of the brick oven! #quarantine

I've been to Slyce a few times but not since going gluten free last year. I had no idea they offered such delectable gluten free pizza crust. My main man and I took a walk along Indian Rocks Beach and worked up an appetite. We walked over to Slyce and didn't have to wait for a table yet sat at the bar to watch the Lightning game. We started with great drinks and ordered the Thai Chicken Wings appetizer. The wings were delicious with just a little kick to them. The order came with 8 pieces and side of ranch. We both ordered 10" gluten free pizzas. I ordered the Roasted Veggie, which is topped with tomato sauce, roasted peppers, caramelized onions, spinach, mushrooms and cheese. He ordered the Buffalo Chicken. Both pies were impressive till the last bite. The vegetables were so fresh. Prices were more than reasonable for gluten free pizza. Service was excellent. Looking forward to our next visit!

I was impressed with the sushi during my first few visits but it tastes like it's from a different restaurant now. Fish hasn't tasted fresh nor flavorful and the rolls seem created without TLC. Avocado shouldn't be unripe and hard to chew. Krab shouldn't be chewy like a gummy bear. It's very rare that I don't finish my entire sushi order but it sadly came to that recently. Its not the worst sushi I've ever had but next time I'm in the area and craving maki I'd rather hit up publix.

I would KILL to transport the Listening Room back to Honolulu. I made a reservation for $2 online and got a seat right up front by the stage. Worth it? Um...yes! It's not so much the decor that makes Listening Room amazing but it is the sheer amount of musical talent you're able to watch in Nashville which makes it completely worthwhile.

I came here twice to watch songwriter rounds during the Tin Pan South Songwriters Festival and was blown away both times. It's amazing to listen to some of my favorite songs of all time (multiple #1 pop and country hits) sung by the people who took part in writing them. It's always been my dream to be a professional songwriter and having these live musical experiences makes it only more of a reality.

My tips if you're deciding to watch a show at the Listening Room is to make reservations online. It's really easy and affordable to reserve seating with a full map of the venue. I wouldn't recommend sitting in the very front simply because the speakers are usually turned up pretty loud and you might go deaf. Instead opt for seating which is midway but still has a good view. The Listening Room is small so you can see the stage from pretty much any point in the room. 

Another tip is to eat somewhere else unless you enjoy bar food. I ate the beet salad one night which was not good at all, but found the chili to be pretty good the second night. Honestly I just don't think I'm cut out for Nashville fare in general because I'm such a picky eater. The food is a bit lackluster but the staff is very accommodating. They always did a good job of checking up on me and making sure I was able to get a fresh drink. You can find street parking but be prepared with a boatload of quarters or park in the pay lot across the street. It's a bit spendy so do your best to find street parking.

Yelp 365 Challenge: #202/365 (The Songwriters Round)

My goal in life is to have your Grandma cook for me. In my opinion there are few things better in this world than sitting down in a house and having a Grandma slave away in the kitchen. The meal rarely disappoints because Grandma don't play that. The center of her existence is making sure that the people at her dining room table are happy and stuffed til they can't walk. 

I don't know many people in Nashville and was not able to crash a family dinner, but Monell's was the next best thing! I walked in not knowing what to expect and was seated at a large dining room table next to two other guests. I left a chair between myself and the male guest but the server warmly scolded me "No hon, you've got to move down and sit right there." Then a lightbulb went off in my head and I realized THIS is what they meant by family style dining! 

I quickly got acquainted with my dining partners as we shared multiple sides, baskets of biscuits and fried chicken. You're instructed to pass to the left and then go from there. I was not told how much lunch was but get ready for your mind to be blown my yeoples! $12.95 (INSERT HUGE FLASHING LIGHTS HERE) for an all-you-can-eat Southern food extravaganza. Maybe this is an everyday type of thing here in Nashville, but in Honolulu there is no way you could get this type of dining for such a small price tag. In total we had about 15 different sides/dishes (dressing, cabbage, cole slaw, broccoli salad, biscuits w/ peach preserves, sweet potatoes, corn pudding, fried chicken, baked chicken, deep fried pork chops, green beens, strawberry shortcake) as well as lemonade and sweet tea. 

Some folks might not enjoy sitting down with strangers but it made the experience so much more interesting! Plus I'm vacationing solo and really enjoyed meeting some locals. They have a very strict "No Cellular Phone" policy at Monell's and I applaud this! The waitress asked the woman dining with me to put away her cell phone (very nicely I might add) because she didn't want her boss to ask the woman to leave. I guess the man who owns the restaurant grew up in a family where phones and television were not allowed during supper time and he brought that tradition over to his business. Man, we need that rule at all restaurants! 

In conclusion my friends, put on those stretchy pants and get ready to stuff your face with home cooking until you go into a self-induced food coma. Southern cuisine is not a part of my everyday existence and thank the Lord or my ass would be huge! Thank you Monell's for welcoming me to your table, showing me Southern hospitality and making me feel like I'm at Grandma's house! 

Yelp 365 Challenge: #193/365 (The Grandma's Table)

Provence provides quite the conundrum. On one hand there is a sort of charm that surrounds this French inspired cafe, but on the other hand it's badly in need of a cleaning. The staff is very nice (all men who I assume are also either college students or singers) but they're NID - not into details. Okay so maybe I'm a bit of a Mom, but honestly they need to sweep this store out and wipe down a few tables. Seeing table after table not being wiped down is a huge pet peeve because no one wants to sit at a dirty table with crumbs on it. And even after seeing me wipe down my own table with a napkin they still didn't wipe down other tables. Oh man! 

Onto the food, I got a fromage salad which consisted of field greens, strawberries, cheese and a light dressing. The salad was okay but I was unimpressed by the amount of "fromage" and strawberries. I really like a hearty salad that is more than just greens and eats like a meal. Maybe this was not what they had planned and secretly discussed that I needed to lose a few pounds? I am not sure. I also ordered the Iced Honey Bee, a honey cinnamon vanilla latte upon the suggestion of Amanda S. It's basically a sweetened milk drink and has a lot of calories, so beware that your ass will get fat off of these suckers. It was a-okay but I think I'd rather have a good old caffeine laced iced coffee or a few espresso shots. I spent about $14 on my lunch and the man at the counter was nice enough to throw in a roll. 

I unfortunately did not have the time to try their plethora of desserts and baked goods but perhaps on my next trip to Nashville. They were very beautiful when I peered at them through the glass. Although Provence does need a thorough cleaning, it does offer free wi-fi and it was not crowded during my lunch visit. It's locally owned and you can tell they are passionate about baking. But dearest Provence, if you want to have more customers and have them return over and over again, it would be good if you would be more passionate about cleaning. No more crumbs on my table next time, okay?

Yelp 365 Challenge: #206/365 (The Honey Bee)

Simplicity at it's finest! Being a fancy foodie is fun, but when that's all you've been doing 24/7 for days on end, it starts to get really old. We were bar hopping through the French Quarter when my boyfriend asked what I wanted to eat next and I replied: "A hamburger!" He replied: "Really?" I looked him in the eyes and said: "Trust me. It's going to be the best thing you've eaten in days." 

We sauntered into the Grill which at the time was completely empty. We were greeted with a smile by a big happy chef and his helpers. With a quick look at the menu we ordered up a cheeseburger, fries and a milkshake. The staff was so much fun to talk to which paired perfectly with the old school diner. We laughed and chatted with another couple who sat down a little while after us.

For $12 that little diner provided one of the most memorable and simple meals of our entire weeklong trip to NOLA. Fancy is fabulous but simple homestyle cooking will win every single time.

Wow, if this place keeps it up, they're going to be my number one cupcake stop.  

1)  The staff is pretty awesome
2)  Mini-cupcakes, for you curious types
3)  Awesome freaking cupcakes!

I ordered a mini gingerbread cupcake and a full sized coffee cake cupcake.  Eating the gingerbread one as I left the store, I almost turned around to get a full sized one, but you know, moderation and all.  Seriously, I think it was the best cupcake I've ever had.  It had an amazing little crunch while still being super soft with an incredible icing.  It kept me smiling all throughout my lunch break.  The coffee cake cupcake was also pretty yummy.  It tasted very home made, and the drizzly crumb topping?  You'll be going after every last bit that falls off the top.  

This place has a great variety of flavors, as well as two featured flavors every month (Hurry, ginger bread won't last!  Be prepared to be heart broken!).  The hot chocolate sounds promising, but won't be sampled till my next trip, which will probably be much sooner than it should be.

I had this place bookmarked for my next trip to the Tampa area.  I saw it on Emerald Legassie show we are he visits all these restaurants all over the state of Florida. This restaurant was really great experience, it has a really cool 1950s diner vibe to it.

I had a burger that was held together by cheese bacon and fried egg.  My hamburger was absolutely delicious.

My wife had a POX burger, she said, "it tasted like a high end burger from McDonalds."  I can't tell if that's a compliment or not. 

Oh, I forget to mention that two in my party had the wedge salad.  It looked amazing and tasted amazing.

We ordered the butterscotch pie. Meh.  Not a fan, but I helped my wife finish it anyway.

Cool environment in a very trendy downtown Tampa location.  Will I come back?  Oh yes, it was a great time, great vibe in the place., and the food was pretty decent.  I definitely recommend that you give this place a try.

The F2O in the Elliston 23 apartment building is the first in Nashville. A yummo salmon Panini filled my belly plumply white sitting at one of the Fresh 2 Order blue topped tables. The simple beige and brown walls and lowkey furnishngs goes with the flo of F2O deli restaurant. I mean it is ok decor but predictable with the most excitement from the flat screen TV on the far wall. Wild mushroom soup and Asian Salad are plans for next visit and will probably enjoy it in the dining area, although might do take out on other visits to the F2O in the E23.

Fire Engine Red! is the color theme which matches the heat of the hottest chicken at Hattie B's.  On the patio table bench seating the hue is Fire Engine Red, as is the garage door to the patio, the lite fixtures and more. It fits. To savor the sweet pain of Hattie B's Nashville hot chicken is cayenne endorphin heaven. Banana pudding & a cold craft beer help dull the heat and make the experience cooler for me. I took tiny nibbles from Hot level heat chicken alternated with swiggs of Yazoo beer. The combo of the hot baby bites and the cold brew made it sweaty fun. The battered and fried chicken delicacy was crispy on the outside and tender soft inside, and served on top of white bread with pickle chips. Hot but cool. American native music and Nashville native Hot! Chicken are 2 authentic Music City exports. If I could choose only one, well, it might just be our Hot! Chicken that the old mayor was ambasssabor for and hooked on. His Best Legacy! The pimento Mac and Cheese and the black eyed pea salad are 2 fixin's I like best. I'm so glad they took over this old Krystal's fast food joint for hot chicken heaven. By next year Hattie B's may be the most popular hot chicken joint in Tennessee.

Over ten tacos to choose from, some graced with made-from-scratch pico de gallo, special sauces, marinated escabeche. The Memphis taco predictably includes pork with BBQ sauce & slaw. General Homeboy taco is shrimpy with chili sauce and sliced veggies. Carnitas style pork taco has guac, cojita & more. All are good. Taco Mamacita has other things, most a la carte, but the tacos are what this place is about. Mamacitas has a full bar, with a few good specialty drinks. You can tell them you want to go nasty with a Durty Sanchez which is PBR with tequila.

A $10,000+ plank of bubinga wood on the circular bar contrasts whimsically with the cheap Mardi Gras bead chandeliers. I mean its like a French Quarter gastropub without the smoke. Bubbly Tenn Sixteen Food & Drink Co. is now the best pub in 5 Points considering its wine list, 17 craft beers on tap and fine food. The cajun influence continues in the southern sourced gourmet foood. Nashvilles' finest beignets with mascarpone cream and Whisper Creek chocolate will literally melt in your mouth! The Tenn Sixteen classic muffaletta sandwich consists of tapenade, prosciutto, mortadella and the usual other ingredients. I mean It. Is. Classic!  Other N'Orleans favorites feature jumbo prawns, and crawfish cakes or gumbo. The Crawfish Gumbo is made with Jackalope Red Ale, but won't make you tipsy; glad but not tipsy. Tennessee brews are available at the reddish-brown wood bar or with table service. Nashville area craft beers on tap also include Yazoo, Turtle Anarchy and Mayday.

I'd ordered out from here a few times before I had the delight of going to the actual restaurant, so I was familiar with the fact that their FOOD IS AMAZING. The menu is expansive and delicious. A few favorites: the hongo relleno (portabello mushroom with crab stuffing!! and cheese! it's creamy and delicious!), nachos mixtos, the enchiladas, their guac, and the chocolate cake (GET THE CAKE). 

Tip #1: Bring tequila. Margarita mix is free. I went there recently and arrived before the rest of my friends so the server had mixed drinks and poured shots for everyone before they even stepped foot in the restaurant. 

It's a wild ride of a place. The food is so worth it, as is (in my opinion) the (high) chance you will end up eating your entire meal wearing sombreros. As other yelpers have mentioned, the server makes it his personal mission to make sure you are stuffed beyond comprehension with delicious food, and makes you feel at home (home?) in such a bizarre and wonderful way that I've never experienced in another restaurant. He's probably bored, honestly, and restaurant patrons are an easy form of amusement. I cannot recommend him highly enough. I'm not even one for really hands-on waiters usually, but he is a gem. Even though he can't speak Spanish, he knows the menu like the back of his hand and will guide you as you will undoubtedly be overwhelmed from the sheer magnitude of choices. Fortunately, everything is so good, you really can't go wrong. 

Tip #2: Be open to wearing sombreros. It might happen.

I went today for lunch because I was STARVING and I needed somewhere that would be guaranteed yummy yummy and I remembered from a previous Yelp event that it was delicious. My intention was to take my food to-go and eat at work but I was way too hungry and the place was pretty empty so I just ate in the dining hall. I ordered the lean brisket on a sandwich and besides the little piece of fat that snuck in between the bun it was delicious. For my sides I got the green beans and the baked cheese grits. Green beans were good....I took a bite of the cheese grits and they were ok. A little dry but still good. 

The best part about the visit was the service. While I was waiting in line the girl at the register messed up someone's order resulting in the whole line of people being held up. I was probably two people from the register when this happened and all I could do was just stare at my sandwich hoping, wishing, praying they would hurry up. Like I said I was STARVING. I got my food and sat down and almost inhaled my sandwich. Mid-chew the manager came over and asked me how everything was and apologized for holding the line up. Definitely wasn't expecting that. Then he offered to buy me dessert and I said no! I know I know. What was I thinking?? I think I was still experiencing hunger delirium because normal me would have been all over that dessert counter. Oh well....next time. Great lunch. Now I need a nap.

This is the perfect little divey college bar. Cheap drinks and good food, how could you go wrong? I've been here to dance in the back, I've been for trivia night, I've been to play pool and darts, and of course I've been for their wings. Sometimes I call ahead just because they probably have the best wings in Tampa and when you have a wing craving you have to have the best. Get the Daytona sauce....you'll thank me.

I know I said it was a college bar but you will really find people of all ages in here. This is one of my favorite places to meet a guy I might have given my number to and might not have remembered what he looked like...*shrug* don't judge me...I usually sit at the bar and eat my wings and drink my Yeungling and call it a night.

I'd been scoping out this restaurant for a week or so now determining if I wanted to actually come here. I heard a few rave reviews but, when I demurred towards the city's famous Michelin-quality restaurants like Commander's Palace and Gautreau's, I read that Bayona was "different" and "unique" from these distinguished places, a once-in-a-lifetime sort of experience.

Nothing could be more true.

While Commander's offers you superb service and Gautreau's offers you superb food, Bayona is distinguished in offering you neither. This place is a production line of "good food", a restaurant designed to simply fool you into believing that you ate well in the same fashion that the emperor was too embarrassed to admit that he was, in fact, wearing no clothes. The service? Completely atrocious. The food? Lukewarm on cold plates. Want to complain? Forget about it, as the manager find such things to be your problem rather than his own. Bayona is charging you Manhattan prices while rendering you Bronx quality.

When I was making my decision to eat here, I came onto Yelp to check it out. I read how bad the service is and how hit or miss the food can be and I simply thought I was reading the reviews of some overzealous yelpers. What I can say without reservation -- and you'll need one to get in here believe it or not -- is that this is perhaps the worst meal I had in New Orleans. In a city famed for its culinary reputation, that's certainly a unique accomplishment in it of itself.

I previously gave them a 5-star review. My wife and I have been there a few times this year, including our anniversary. Unfortunately, we went for trivia night and that's when one manager's true colors showed.

As the host, he was constantly making jokes about deporting patrons for various reasons. My wife and sister-in-law were there with me, both of whom are Mexican. I told him he needed to shut up because there really were Mexicans here, and he replied with something to the tune of "then we really need to build a wall." More words were exchanged and it didn't get better. He later attempted to apologize by saying he thought I was joking. Yeah, forcibly separating families and ruining lives is *hilarious*.

I'm really disappointed because the wait staff is friendly and competent. But I'd recommend not supporting a restaurant that hires managers who make people feel unwelcome because of their race/ethnicity.

First time experience and most impressed I was. This is an old bank and still has the look of it. 
They have sections for groups and little as 4 people. But the highlight I think would be having dinner in the vault itself.  It has a certain look about it that says SHE'S SPECIAL. 

The prices are reasonable for a special date setting. But the food & service is worth the price. 

I had the lamb chops and they were extremely good. Taste,  the portions, the meat quality were all 5 star.  The sides are enough to share with couple people. 

The service was very good. I wish I had gotten the waitresses name. She was very helpful in deciding what to try and her favorites. Her attentiveness was perfect for any first time visitors welcoming.

If you have a special occasion or want to impress a special guy/ gal. Or just want a perfectly cooked steak. You will not be disappointed in this place.  

I'll be trying this again, again and again

Another one NOLA long line places.  There's 3 lines one for take out only, 1 for being seated and 1 bathroom line.  Yes and all 3 were long lol.  
We got a Beignet, hot chocolate and water.  
The beignet was good by far. Hot chocolate equally as good.

This is a prime example of never judge a book by it's cover or surroundings. 
Walked 1.5 miles to get here. To my unknown it is in the hood. And without trying to scare any readers. I uber to my next destination. . And not because i was full. 
8 out of 10 times I'm sure you will walk up and have to wait in line like we did.  On the same token.  I'm not sure how many of those times in line will a armed security guard be taking your reservation.  
Now remember what i said.  Don't judge a book by its cover nor surroundings. 
The wait was not long. When you enter. It is like a renovated house to restaurant. Possible 50-60 people can be seated at once.  
The menu is simple and the food is good.  I've heard it said while im seated that it's the best fried chicken ever. We ordered the fried chicken,  mac and cheese, peas, catfish string beans and rice w/ gravy.  The chicken at first look - looked hard. But once tasted it. It was juicy and tender all the way through.  The skin was golden brown and a light flaky. Seasoning was really good.  Didn't need no extra salt or pepper.  Hot sauce is optional to your taste.  And the biggest thing.  It was delivered hot and the chicken and fish stayed hot throughout the meal.  And there was no grease.  Even padded the chicken down and napkin came up empty. 
The catfish was perfectly cooked. Light fluffy and a nice crunch to the skin.  The portions were perfect. Chicken and fish gets 5 stars.  The sides on the other hand.  Nothing actually stood out. But they helped complete the meats.  
Now the sweet tea and lemonade.  That's some down south drunks. Southern sweetness.  But make sure you got a full glass of ice in them to water it down while your eating.  
Did not try the desserts.  So no comment.  But i believe there was 6 of them on the menu. 
Today they were offering nothing baked.  No bake chicken,  no baked corn muffins,  no yams, not sure why.  The yams i think would be really good there. 

For the first NOLA meal of my visit. It was good. And if in town.  Definitely do it again.

Since been in NOLA I've had chicken couple times. And each time when it comes out i always say that's dry. This was no different.  However let me tell you this place has the very best chicken yet. Super tender and moist and perfect with the waffles. I do not do chicken and waffles at home. But today I am glad I did it. So good and hard to not finish it all. Hard to leave the last half piece of chicken on the plate lol

The service is on point. And the folks are really kind. Great breakfast and lunch place. During the week the are open accordingly to the flow of business so they may close early. 
They are located across from the The French market flea market. 
With the 50's music playing in the air. You will leave here full, happy and bopping to some tune you heard

5 thumbs up

Very nice place.  
The quick menu for covid outside dining has a very nice array of choices. 
The coconut shrimp and Bang bang cauliflower for starters was very good.  Cooked perfectly and good portion given. 

The chicken copied salad was a winner to my test buds. The freshness was very taste able.  The portion was enough to fill me but not make me feel stuffed. 

The Banana Cream Pie.  A must try. Again a generous portion to share or eat alone.  Each bite you taste the flavor.  

The outside seating by the water is very good. Nice breeze from the water was felt. Even in the 96 degree weather.

The waitress was very tentative and had no problem answering all my questions.  

A very good ex experience and will be back for sure.

We were staying in downtown Tampa for the weekend and stopped in twice.  Several restaurants and shop owners who serve good coffee have told us they get their coffee from Kahwa, and we can see why.  We initially tried to visit the one on Ashley, but it was closed due to filming (not sure what that was about, but we could see the film crew and it looked like they wouldn't be opening any time soon this weekend) so we went to this location.  Both are equally convenient.  
The coffee was the best I've had in a long time (on par with Drica's in Lakeland). It's a small, bright shop and located next to the Duckweed Urban Market - both have patio seating.  It was ridiculously hot, so we stayed indoors during both visits.  The barristas were friendly, knowledgeable and efficient.  I got my usual Americano, and it was wonderful.  The 2nd day I discovered they had almond milk, so I tried a latte.  So rich, creamy and flavorful - both run about the same as you would pay at Starbucks but sooo much better,and local.  I enjoyed my latte while waiting for someone to arrive, and I noticed a tray of croissants come out.   They make all the pastries, and they looked so good, I had to try one.  I was not disappointed.  Flaky. buttery and delicious!  They also offer a wide array of vegan and gluten free choices.  We'll be back when we're in need of coffee in the downtown Tampa area.

We've been here many times, and the experience has been fairly consistent, except for last night.  We tend to stop in later in the evening and have only had the sweet crepes.  A nice variety is offered, and they are consistently well made and delicious. The coffee is excellent -- aromatic, rich, smooth and flavorful.  The cappuccino and espresso are excellent as well.

The problem comes with service.  The waiter we just about always have is  cordial and pleasant. Not the most attentive, often needing reminders concerning empty coffee cups but quick to refill upon request.  And never less than welcoming.  Crepes are made to order and arrive quickly.  

Unfortunately, this was not our experience last night. Mike, not our usual waiter, was decidedly neither cordial nor attentive.  We chose one of the many unoccupied tables inside -- only 2 were taken, and it was the same situation outside.  We ordered 2 coffees and perused the menu.  He asked for our food order when our coffees arrived, but we were chatting and hadn't reached a decision yet. When he returned a minute later and we said we wanted to drink our coffee for a bit, he replied by telling us, "that really affects us so it would be better if you cash out now." He returned within a few seconds and placed the check on my husband's saucer, upon which his cup was sitting, telling us he would continue to refill our coffee.  Needless to say, he never returned.  

If this had been our first experience here, we would never come back; however we will check to see if Mike is the waiter before patronizing this establishment in the future.

Overall....
Crepes: 4 stars
Coffee: 5 stars
Service: 2 stars (thanks to this visit)

I have been passing by this place on the way to Chesterfield every day with a "Coming Soon" sign hanging in front of it for the last six months. 
 I am very glad that they finally opened.  Apparently I wasn't the only one waiting.  We came on opening day, so many food items were out. We opted for drinks instead. They did not disappoint. 

The decor is quite whimsical.  A beautiful butterfly motif to your left and many stuffed pink pigs greet you upon entering.  It is a breath of fresh air to see a place like this on this part of Olive.  Normally, we would have to be in the de facto Chinatown of Saint Louis towards Olivette.  Rather than go towards that side, this will probably be our place to go since we don't have to fight with traffic.  We will be coming back. It is a relief that we have more and more places opening in Chesterfield. They will do great, provided they keep up with the outstanding quality and presentation.

*Update on 8/5/2019*

I noticed many reviewers mention the lack of availability of food items, as well as delays in receipt of said food items.  I went last Saturday (8/3) with dine in and I was able to get my food within 20 minutes.  I believe they're still trying to fine-tune their business at this location.

With that being said, we had the eel rice bowl and chicken tonkatsu rice bowl.  Both were outstanding in freshness, quality, and presentation.  

I've had their drinks previously and they did not disappoint the first time around nor this time.  The grapefruit tea was amazing; it's nice to have an option that's not just sweet.  They've got that figured out.

Give this place a little time to fine-tune their service and execution.  It's only been a couple weeks since they've opened.  I see great things for this place.  They just need to keep up with the quality and tighten up speed of service.

Such a lovely experience here at Crossing Vineyards.

My friends and I purchased a living social deal for a one hour yoga session outside along the vineyards followed by a formal wine tasting and tour of the winery all for just $20. It was wonderful. 

Walking up to the winery is a beautiful garden. Chairs and an alter were also all set up for a wedding, very pretty. Our yoga instructor Sherry arrived and we set our mats up behind the ceremony area which is also right next to the tasting room. She was bubbly, funny, and sweet. She catered to everyone in the class that had experience or none at all. It was relaxing, yet challenging enough. The weather was perfect and it was so nice to breathe in the fresh air and enjoy the beautiful surroundings. In the beginning of class she asked if there were any special occasions, birthdays or anniversaries.. While someone did have a birthday, Sherry offered up everyone to sing happy birthday to her before ending in Om. 

We then walked in to the tasting room to a dining room table set up where we all sat down together as a group. This tasting is not like any other that I have been to before, even after visiting the Finger Lakes which is basically referred to as wine country on the east coast. I appreciated the fact that the young woman explained the 4 essence of wine tasting to truly soak up the experience. We were also a given a small plate with two cheeses, two meats, and a pomegranate chocolate truffle in the center. Each to be paired with a particular wine of the 10 wines. I didn't particularly love the wines, but they definitely were tasty. More so with its pairings that gave a nice balance to the wines. We had our tasting notes and marked down which wines we wanted to purchase so we could pick it up after the tour. 

The staff were all very nice and by my friends request asked to try the Sangria, she and anyone else who then wanted a taste could do so as well. 

This winery is just 45 minutes away and I would definitely like to come back again.

I dont see the big deal about this place. The Chicago dogs and the italian sausages are just meh to me. There are smaller Chicago dog places in Tampa to me that are way better and alot cleaner.

Since the locals rave about this place I decided to try it and not only was the wait long, trash cans were over flowed, tables were disgusting and needed to be wiped off, but when I ordered a drink my cup was brought to me greasy and smelled like a sausage. Like someone was cooking in the back and handling drinks at the same time. I asked the cashier to change my cup and showed her the mess and she proceeded to have an attitude with me!

I can say I tried it but I wouldnt go back.

Mannnnnn.... this place is way better than Portillo's! I said what I said!!

This place has the most authentic Chicago dog on earth I swear! The customer service is always on point.  I haven't had a bad experience yet. There fries are so thick and super long, it's the best bang for your buck. Everytime I'm in Florida I visit this location and I bring people here because its such a friendly and lively armosphere.

I stopped in here this morning on the way to work after seeing on Jonathan Wright's blog on the RGJ that they were open.  I've been looking forward to this place opening, ever since hearing a few months back that Christian and Kasey Christensen of Sup were planning on opening a breakfast / bakery type place.

The space is a converted house, with light colors inside.  The front half of the house has two doors, one facing the street and the other facing the parking lot next to the now vacant Cyber Infusion building.  The interior is well light, with lots of natural light shining in, with a half-dozen or so hightops and four-tops scattered around, and a small bar in the front window, all of light, birch colors.  The remodel of the house definitely seemed to focus on brightening it up, and while not fancy, works well in the space - the floors are laquered plywood, the walls have some texturing with a light tan color, and things are generally light and airy.

When I walked in, Kasey was working the back, and greeted me with a smile while I looked over the chalkboard style menu hanging behind her.  I ended up settling on the Crepe Ranchero (Egg, cheddar cheese and black beans topped with guacamole, salsa and sour cream).  Kasey warned me the portions were a bit smaller than standard American restaurant fare and that the crepes were small, and asked if I wanted to add a crepe for $2.  I passed on this, and subbed salad for the fruit side.

While waiting, we chatted about opening the new place, and she offered me an almond vanilla macaroon.  While macaroon's have been surging in popularity, I've never been a huge fan, but this one impressed me.  The textures usually put me off, with the cookies usually being a bit too dense and chewy for me, but this was lighter, and while not quite fluffy, definitey not the chewy blob that I'm used to associating with macarooons.

I had the crepe to go, and didn't get to eat it till I got to work, but was impressed with the to-go pacakging - individual containers of salsa, guac, sour cream, salad and salad dressing, and the crepes sitting alone, all in a waxed paper box.
  Definitely appreciate the separation and keeping everything from blending together, especially as I still had a 15 minute commute to the office.  The crepes were definitely smaller, I'd guess maybe 6" circles to start?  The guac and salsa both tasted fresh and delicious, and complemented the crepes well.  The crepes were fantastic, with the perfect balance of black beans and eggs, though I didn't get much of the cheddar flavor.  Salad seemed to be the standard Sup house salad, with their wonderful vinaigrette.  

Overall, a warm, cozy space and a nice addition to the breakfast options in Midtown.  Definitely will stop back.

Don't know what happened to my review but I got a private message from Cyrina Abowd stating to be offended by my review and accused me of cyber bullying. They have good food, but she was very rude to our party and appears to enjoy belittling people. Our coffee was cold and there were lipstick stains on a coffee cup. I had considered going back have changed my mind since she sent me a private message.

Oof. Where do I start? 

I didn't expect stellar service, but man, this was just poor. The place was practically empty and it still took forever for anything to happen. We waited for a good 10 minutes to even get water while our half-naked server (seriously, her nipples were peeking out of the top of her american apparel tank-thong) chatted with her friends a few feet away. My friend ordered an adult shake, which arrived after I was already on my second beer, and clearly had been sitting around as it was half melted. Fittingly, our bill arrived with a Jameson on it that no one had ordered. Upon informing our server, she gave us a dirty look and said "are you sure?" before taking another 10 minutes to fix it. At this point the soundtrack inexplicably switched to mall-punk screamo circa 2002. Farce complete.

A good barrier island food off the Pinellas county gulf coast. Rick is look like back to normal after pandemic. The customer come back to enjoy the mixed cocktails and food. It is St. Pete beach area restaurant. I pick this place after my visit to my project. 

I order the grilled grouper sandwich. It come with the side. And I got the deep corn on the cob. I have not have a deep fried corn in Florida. I have deep fried corn once at New Orlean. Overall the service is good. I did not try their cocktails. But the food is good and has some unique item.

Very close to 4.5 stars. Fish guy is my place if I pass by again. It is great seafood market and restaurant. Seafood is fresh and delicious. You cannot believe a side street of Holiday area has this great seafood restaurant. Local know about this place. 

We start with 3-pepper crab soup. Plenty of crab meat. A bit spicy. Almost like Cajun style. We like this unique soup. We do have to send back the New England clam chowder.
