I like Kay's chicken because they prepare it fresh. They use light coating not like other fast food have thick coating that you cannot feel the chicken. Their chicken is Chicago style which is rare in Tampa Bay Area. So go get your own.

The loft is an interesting restaurant. A farm house turn restaurant on the northwest of Indianapolis. They host the farm tour during the day. And they have an ice cream bar. Because they call themselves a creamery and restaurant. The flavor of ice cream is also interesting. They have the regular vanilla and chocolate. But they have something you may not think of like cantaloupe lime and s'mores. 

We were here for the dinner. The ingredients selection from their farm or organic material. We got the bison noodle. It is bison short rib cook wine sauce. It taste like German Bavarian cuisine. The short rib is fork tender. It is the porcini rutabaga on it. I like this dish with dark  Scottish ale. 

Our second dish is a Great Lake Walleye. I have never have this fish before. You can said it has the firmness like grouper but taste like bass. The way they cook it with roasted with the skin. It has kielbasa potato pierogies. This make my favorite dish. Very unique at it on way. 

Services is good. Attentive. The price is high side but the experience make up for it.

It is about 3.5 stars. Not 4 stars yet. Restaurant is popular during weekends. We did call ahead for reservations. Parking to the garage is free first 2 hours. Not required validation to the parking ticket. 

We started with octopus salad. This salad has fried cauliflower, gigante beans, olives. It top with ricotta salata cheese and Calabrian hot sauce on the side. I like the octopus and I love the fried cauliflower. My wife entree is Naduja Meatballs pasta. It serve with tomato sauce and spaghetti. I think this dish is not impressive for the price that they label. It can be different on sauce or something. My entree is good. I have the the duck confit with pici pasta. This have good creamy sauce.

Our experience is good. Service is attentive. Food come in right time. Value vs price may need measures up on entree. Appetizers is good.

The begin of Sweet Bun I have try is at Gainesville. Since I have been to many oriental bakery, I would place this one a bit above middle of the pack. It is similar to Sweet Hut at Atlanta. It definitely cannot compare to Sweet Hut near Gwinnett Place at Atlanta but it definitely hold it own for Tampa Bay Area. 

They have sweet and salty bun on display. It is perfect location near USF. It is great to have bun for breakfast with lesser price. Even if you come for lunch, it is better than the choice of fast food. A bowl noodle definitely better than fast food with same price. 

The only thing they lack off is they need special drinks like fruit tea, boba tea, and WiFi. We were here for their pig feet noodle and the wonton noodle. Not the best but good enough.

Just to open this review. This is a 4.5 stars Indian restaurant. It has good use of spice, good enough spiciness, good enough meat dish, great choice of dishes. Since there is no 1/2 stars, I given them five stars. 

It is good to see somethings different along the Bruce B Down. This restaurant come in to replace typical restaurants along this street. Price is reasonable on the lunch buffet. The food is fresh and cook very well. We have the goat curry. They do not have heavy goat smell which is perfect. The chicken masala is good curry to go with rice or the nan. Their nan is not at the buffet tray which is I agree, they bring fresh from their kitchen which is a smart move. Somethings different from the other Indian food buffet is they provide the dosa to the table. It is good. 

Service is good and attentive. So far not many people know about it yet. But the crowd is coming soon.

This restaurant has high ratings. However, I found that not match the experience I have there. I visited the restaurant after 8 pm. Still have table waiting for food and some people order the take out. Not too busy. 

I have order the spicy drunken noodles with shrimp. I have specific order. I want my noodles dry which mean don't let the juice come out. I also order it to be Thai spicy hot. While I wait for the food, they do have special day combination or pre prix dish on holiday. Look interesting. 

When my noodles come out, there are wet sauce every where. Which mean it was not on the wok too long. Because no burn mark at the noodles. The dish is medium spicy. Not even close one step below Thai hot. This too difficult to fixed. One good thing is they have good size fresh shrimp. I didn't ask for redone due to time. 

This is been there done that.

Haven has been in my bookmark for sometime. Most of my friends been here has good time here. Mainly wine and cheese. But the happy hour is the most attractive. They have two parking area. If not street parking nearby is good too. 

The happy hour has great deal. People come early during this time to enjoy couple of wine or cocktails. The line is already build at entrance to be open during Friday night. Happy hour is for bar, lounge, and outside. 

We started with the Duck Confit Taco. The skins is different for the taco. Good enough. The second dish is the chargrills oyster. I like this dish. Somehow the oil in the oyster make this dish taste very good. The third dish is the grilled Shishito Pepper. With a bit sea salt oil and grilled over open flame is great for the wine and cocktails. Our board dish is charcuterie board with different ham. This is perfect dish with the slide cure ham. Our last dish is the chorizo fritter. Great ball fried with chorizo inside. 

Service is great at the bar. The server is very alert. I have cocktails. Both cocktails is welcoming.

Authentic Ethnic Food # 33

Finally we have very good Cuban Cuisine near Northeast Tampa. That cut a lot of my driving time if I am craving for this type cuisine. This place is close to the intersection Nebraska and Florida south of Publix. Plenty of parking at stand alone building. The exterior is not attractive but the interior is well decorated. 

We have order the Completa Grande. This did content three different types of typical Cuban food. It has Ropa Vieja, Picadillo Habanero, and Lechon Asada. The Lechon is well braise with mojo sauce. The sides include rice, black bean, yuca and plantain. This is a good dish for to try if you want to find out what is Cuban cuisine. We also has the Alitas de Pollo. This is the marinated chicken wings with garlic mojo sauce. It is about $1 a wing. 

Overall the experience is good. Like the food there. Definitely come back for their seafood chef selection.

This is the second restaurant they have open. The space is a lot beautiful than the YBOR location. They have a small room for hosting a special function or event. The restaurant is well decorated. I like the new space. 

We were here for their lunch special. Two roll with soup or salad is $11. It is a good deal. The restaurant is kind of empty. It need good promotion for the local Carrollwood to attract more customers. We got the two roll with Atlantic and Tokyo Rolls. The Atlantic roll is very nice. It is a Striped Bass with imitation crab meat and lemon slice. The lemon slice enhances the flavor. I would recommend this roll. The Tokyo roll has tuna and yellow tail mixed. The spicy sauce make it very nice. 

Our next dish is the baked mussels. But I like this dish better at YBOR because they bake till crisp on the top. Nonetheless, it is good big pieces of mussels. We also got the tempura bento box. The tempura is not measured up because they just dip the wet batter and fried. They did not add the tempura while fried to make it hairy. 

Overall is a good visit. Good service.

We were here for the restaurant week at Saturday. For Saturday night this restaurant is average busy. The tap house has good collection of whiskey. They have quite a selection if you want some southern whiskey. They can consider sport bar. I would they may need to add a few more in order to compete as sport bar. 

The service is good. I like the appetizers and the dessert. Their entree need to be work on it. We started with the knockout shrimp. This is fried shrimp with spicy creamy sauce. This serve over the cabbage salad. Our dessert is the chocolate bourbon cake. I also like this dish. The cake has good flavor with ice cream. 

Our entree are the 6oz filet mignon. The meat taste like sirloin instead of filet mignon. It is not soft enough. The meat also has no seasoning. We also has the grilled mahi-mahi. Again no seasoning. Both dish are not impressive.

Not yet 5 stars. It is about 4.5 stars. Since no half star, 5 stars is given for good service. Umami server to sushi chef are very young in age. Don't be fool by the young age. Their new intention and recreation is very trendy.

Start with weakness. The sushi is a bit above average on the three rolls special. I have the spicy tuna, spicy white tuna mango, and cowboy rolls. The spicy tuna instead grind meat, I would prefer dice meat. The spicy white tuna mango is interesting. The cowboy roll is seared beef in sushi roll. All are creative. I think need to work on the flavor. 

The bento box is amazing. The sashimi has very nice pieces of fish. They are very fresh and not fishy at all. The tempura bento also very nice. They have the best skill for tempura. A real Japanese technique is to glue each coating separately and creat needle type tempura look. If you see a smooth breaded coating, those are lazy type of cooking. He breading coating need to needle type. All bento box has very good fry rice. Love it. 

In addition, the sashimi has fatty tuna, king salmon, madai, fluke. Those are more choices on special type of fish. This choice make them stand out from other sushi place.

It one of good seafood place in Dunedin. This restaurant is about 4.5 stars. The reason they stay at 4 stars due to service during lunch time. They have one waiter and reception for the afternoon. I can see 6 table of customers but not enough waitress. Obviously this is a balancing act for the restaurant if they need to spend more overhead. 

With that said. The food are excellent. 5 stars. We started with fried crab crawl. This is special of the day. $12 for about 20 crawls. The crawl is fresh with great coating. Love it. 

Our main dish is oyster poboy and the blackened hogfish. They give a lot of oyster at the poboy. The oyster are great. My friend was not able to finish and take home. The hogfish blackened is ok. Not like the Cajun style. But the fish meat is good and tasty. It is good sandwich. 

Overall experience is good. Hope they continue the good food.

For weekday lunch. The selection is great. You also can make your own pasta. Choose the pasta type, choose the protein, and choose the sauce. I can said that they have great chef technique. It won't be able to go wrong. 

The lunch special is less than half of the dinner price. It great for the business people have lunch here with quick order and get out in 40 minutes. Food is extremely good. You are paid more than value, great food and great flavor. 

We have chef Complimentary tomato sauce over toasted bread. Our entree are Grouper Rosso and Prosciutto Linguine. Both dishes are excellent. The Grouper Rosso grouper is blackened over fettuccine. The fettuccine is serve on creamy basil tomato sauce. It includes the mushroom and scallions. Great combination. 

The best dish is the Prosciutto Linguine. The Prosciutto and the fried garlic make great combination. The Prosciutto release the cure meat flavor into the dish make this dish desirable. Lovely dish.

Keke's new location at USF area is less than 1 year new. We been want to visit for some time. Parking is very convenient. The line for weekend breakfast is not bad. At 8:20 am, there was no line at all. Lighting design and space is very welcoming with bright to see your food. 

We got Pina Colada with egg and bacon. The piña colada French Toast is French Toast stuff with pineapple, cream and spread with powder sugar and coconut flake. The food presentation is very nice. Colorful. The bacon is thick enough with good quality. The sunny side up egg was cook to order. Food is delicious. 

The food is a bit pricey. But it does show the potential for good food. Service definitely excellent in this place. The waiter is knowledgeable to recommend a dish.

The lunch special is very affordable and attractive. It is great to have lunch here with less than $10 on weekday. I like restaurant has multiple TV with many angle and channels. That's why you call them sport bar. The drink has special every day including the happy hour 4 to 6 pm. 

We got weekday lunch special with grilled salmon salad and grilled chicken Fettuccine. Both dish is big enough for lunch. The salmon come in the strips and perfectly grilled. The salad is great because they have good mixed of green. The Fettuccine sauce also good and the chicken is juicy. 

You may want join their lunch time gold stars punch card. After 5 visit, you got $10 free on lunch. The service is great. From reception to service is very attentive. Our food come out quick too.

I am excited finally to try out this restaurant. I have been many event that the restaurant involved in and try their food. Tuesday is good day to try since my friend said they have the prefix menu. Actually they have stop this offering long time ago. 

The night is busy. I like their bar and kitchen is next to each other. The action in the kitchen was presented in front you when you just a few feet away. I like the action and coordination between chefs. 

I start with lamb neck with over the dumplings top with salad. This dish meat was obtained from the neck area. The meat was braised me dumplings below is fried. The top salad was very delicious. The hot sauce below just accommodate well with the dish. 

The second dish is risotto with lobster. The risotto was cook with lobster and wild mushrooms. The edge was green color by caramelize fennel and top with lemon fraiche. This hot, warm and cold section make this dish my favorite dish. Very interesting. 

Overall close 4.5 stars. I think they can be better. I would said good restaurant.

Very interesting restaurant in the Lutz area. This is considering very good restaurant around this area. The seafood is fresh, good quantities, and affordable price. 

Tonight is the Thursday night and they have two special. Kid eats free and prime rib special. We arrived at 7 pm and the prime rib already sold out. We cannot beat retiree around that area that comes early. Just kidding. 

We start our night with the steamer. Nick is the experts in this area. He shows us how to eat it. The steamer is steam to cook first. The outer black skin need to undress from the clam body. Then it is clean in the broth or beer. Then dip into to butter and enjoy by eating it. Some has added pepper and lemon after clean it. This is a very adventurous item in the menu. 

I have the fried sea scallop and fried whole snapper. The snapper come with the batter coating outside. When come to whole fried fish, you want to make sure the meat inside is cook. This restaurant did it correctly. The only thing is the coating is tasteless. I prefer it to be season. However the fish is fresh and good. For fresh seafood, you do not require too much seasoning. 

The fried scallop is very tasty because the coating was seasoning with flavor. When you break the scallop, the meat of the scallop is like a string which means the freshness of the food. 

Overall the seafood is fresh, the portion is very generous, and the service is great.

This southern restaurant has majority customers is African Americans. If you there that much of people, it must be good. They do have lounge area next door. I like restaurant section to enjoy the food. They have southern food. The price was reasonable at the mark. 

We have rock the boat. This dish is smoke and seared Triple Tail fish. The blackened is spicy. But I like it. It accompanying the collard green and Gouda grit. I like the collard green. Very southern. Our second dish is the Never Too Much. This is the southern steak with frite. It is Kansas Strip steak. The steak is well marinated and grilled correctly to order. The bbq sauce is nice to dip. Good pink center. Meat quality is good. The sunny side up egg is good with egg yolk spill over the steak. I would recommend this dish. 

Service is ok. But the food is good. Definitely one of the restaurant will be back for their fried chicken and oxtail. Cocktails look good.

The first Bubba in Florida. It is sister company of Texas Roadhouse. But I think they are better than Texas Roadhouse and is a improvement. The best thing is affordable cocktails. $4 not bad at all. I got the midnight train and the Frozen All American Margarita. The midnight train is ok. But the Frozen American is wonderful. Next time I will try Long Island ice tea. 

We have the Rib-Eye steak 12oz and Signature Ribeye Steak 14 oz. the regular ribeye just grilled but the signature is marinated. Both are really good because good quality meat. The signature ribeye is marinated in sweet sauce. It is excellent. We also good 12" pepperoni pizza and the raspberry chipotle wing. The pizza is ok but the wing is really good.  

The only thing that need improvement is the reception. It need some work. When the table is available, they need to hurry up shorten the wait line. It just too much for reception to take phone order and lead to table. The service for the table is really good. They have enough people to handle the food delivery and tablE service.

I have been eating their food very often. However, I have never review them. Our company lunch meeting often order from this place. Some time is good and some time is off. This is about 3.5 star restaurant in my book. 

Today I have the calamari and Tazza Istanbul Shrimp. I have order the appetizer of the calamari is for me to chew while keep me awake during the lunch seminar. It is working. Although it is not the best fried calamari, but it didn't cost that much either. The Tazza Istanbul Shrimp have a good Turkish sauce to go with it. It accompanied well within the rice. The shrimp size is about 36 count per pound. It is not the big size. Food is ok. 

They offer very complete menu and many choices. Start with appetizer, salad, soup, sandwich, wrap, seafood, platter, burger, and their specialty.

This is our second stop happy hour restaurant. Malio is restaurant near Curtis Hixon park. If you happen to be there, you may want to check on their happy hour from 3 to 7 pm Tuesday to Friday. Their happy hour food item is great. 

I start with their high west old fashioned. It is a double Rye whiskey. It has some kick into it. Good deal at happy hour. Our selection for the appetizers begins with filet tips it was grilled very well. Good to share with friend. Our next appetizer is Ahi Tuna Tartare. It serve with wonton chip and pickles ginger. Tuna was good. Our last appetizer is the Shrimp Theresa. It is grilled shrimp with ponzu crispy outside. I like this appetizer the best. It come as six pieces. 

Overall we enjoy our time here. Service is good. Parking at the building is $6 if you want to park close. They do have coupons but still need to pay $6 for parking. I think it defeated the coupon.

It is 3.5 stars restaurant. It is not 4 stars. The service is good, the ambient is excellent, the food is par, and the wait is par. 

The restaurant does not take reservation. So you have to arrive and find out your fate. On the weekend is over hour to get in. However, they get your cell phone number and text you when the table is ready. Once they text you, you have 5 minutes to respond that you still want your table, then 5 minutes to show up. Which give you time to walk around the mall. If you need 10 minutes time to walk back. Don't respond immediately, response close to your 5 minutes is up. 

The decorations is definitely eye catching. I like many of the ambient. It is beautiful. It is fiesta atmosphere. Seem like you seat on open air restaurant with stars hanging over you. Music is good volume and still able to make conversation at bar area. 

The food is the main thing that they need to make the most improvement. Go from the bad to good. The taco are the area need to make the most improvement. We have order 4 tacos. The shrimp, blacken fish, cochinita (roast pork) and carne Asada (wood grilled steak). The pork is lack of flavor. The fish is dry and over cook, the shrimp is just broil and serve. The best is the steak that is a star. I would suggest control how the fish is cook. The pork may be need to marinate and cook in the thicker sauce and the shrimp grilled it before put it in the taco. 

The entrée is the ceviche and the grilled chicken with mole chocolate sauce. I like both of the dish. It is not a wow but above average. I do like their table side guacamole. They have options for the spiciness and chunky of the avocado. I like the chip because they have spice on top and tasty then the most restaurant. 

Overall is good experience. We have very good service. Our waiter is experience. I have read some of the reviews of my friend that some of the waiter are not up to the task. But our night was good may be it is weekend and they have the experience waiter.

Review # 2600 - this one go to Viet Kitchen. 

I have come to this restaurant several time. The fist time we have visited, the AC did not work. By the second time we visited, the problem solved. I like local own restaurants who do well. It is true 5 stars restaurant due to the cuisine, technique and unique food. 

We have try many dishes. The appetizer we have is roasted quail. This dish you need to call ahead to assure they have the dish at the time you visit. Because if they sold out that day, it will difficult for them to prepare for you because it need two hour marinated time. I like this dish very much. The salad dish we have is very unique. We have young jack fruit shrimp salad. I never thought use green jack fruit in salad. This my first I have it. I recommend this dish. 

The main dishes we have a few good one. The first dish is the shaken beef or sautéed cube steak is delicious. I think the beef can be more shaken will be better. The second dish is the crab meat fried rice. This is great dish to have. You can feel the crab meat. The third dish is my favorite. It is the salt and pepper prawn. Those are big prawn. The shell is on. The last dish is the Caramelized fish fillet. It is king fish with good caramel sauce. 

Overall we enjoy our night. It is delicious on all dishes.

Kao Thai is in my bookmark for a while. Finally I have a chance to visit the restaurant. The restaurant is well decorated. I like the clothing napkin setup on the table like bold tide. They have different menu. One is their regular menu and the other is the Thai street food menu. 

We Thee dishes from the Thai Street Menu. The first dish is the Yum Nam Kao Tod. This is salad dish with sausage, crispy curry rice that fried, peanut. To me, this dish is salty and sour to be eat along. The second dish is Hoy Tod. It s a mussels egg pancake and bean sprouts. It come with the dipping sweet chilies sauce. I like this dish. The third dish is my favorite. Kao Kook Ka Pi. This dish has seven combination items in one dish. The item I like the most is shrimp paste fried rice. I have this as Malay dish. But they carry it. This is the first I have in Tampa Bay. The dish also includes the caramelize pork belly, Thai sweet sausage, egg, onion, apple and string bean. It is well presented. 

Overall our experience is good. I really want to come back to try their main menu dish. This restaurant is about 4.5 stars since each dish is well decorated.

If look for late night dinner at weekends, this is one of the restaurant has full kitchen menu until 1 am. We were here late 11 pm dinner. This place has more people when we finish our dinner. I was surprised more would came late night. 

We got the Korean Japchae. This is glass noodle vegetable dish with shiitake mushroom. The sauce is right. The sesame oil is fragrance enough. It is good dish. We also got the beef bulgogi. This dish is a bit let down compare to my first visit. Because they beef quality has a lot tendon. Tough to bite. 

Overall we have a good night here. Service attentive is a bit behind. I have to flag down waiter or waitress to get attention.

I have visited this place three time. This is my first review on it. My first visit was good about 4 stars. My last visit is the worst from my company party 2 stars. Base on this combination experience, it is set to three stars. 

I believe Roy's has take a step back. When the food is not good, it will be no repeat customer. The reason as below. We start three appetizer crispy chicken spring rolls, Szechuan spice pork rib, and tempura crash Ahi Tuna roll. Among all three, only the tuna roll is good. The pork need major improvement. The meat not fall off the bone make this not a fine dinning experience. Obviously the rib was not slow cook longer allow meat to fall off. 

The entrée are the fillet mignon and macadamia nut crust mahi mahi. I have to send the fillet back because the meat was not cooked to order. This can corrected by putting a indicated stick not to mixed up the order. The mahi-mahi is just simply not fresh enough. The meat not show good sign. The crust is not fully cover to the fish. 

One good thing can said about this experience is the dessert. All other just ok.

Tara is not allowed dine in during pandemic. But the take out is available. The store open to customers who want generous on the quantity portion. 

I got the the stew Oxtail. This dish come with one side of choices and rice. I have the cabbage as side. The oxtail is stew in high pressure to separate from the bone. Number oxtail given was three big pieces and one small piece. The rice was given generously so you will have full stomach. Great for dinner portions. 

Overall experience is at average. Food is ok. Definitely is budget place in compare to many restaurants.

I was here to have a take out. I have this restaurant bookmark since my friends in yelp M&M has been here. The restaurant is well decorated with Bob Marley picture. They also has salt water fish tank. 

I got the their two best saler in the menu. The oxtail and the jerk chicken. The oxtail was well sauce marinated into the bone. The tail is braised till the meat fall off the bone. The jerk chicken is marinated till enter the meat. Then it grilled to perfection. When you use your finger to eat the chicken, you still can smell the marinated sauce at your finger after you have finished the chicken. Each dish come with rice, stir fry veggies. 

I also got their conch soup. It is a bit fishy but it is good. Love all the food here. Portion is big to feed the hungry person. Price is above the average Jamaican restaurant but the the portion measured up the price.

It is great tuck away neighborhood restaurant. Gino do bring the taste to the table. It is good to see local restaurant make it because they have quite number of customers.

My meal come with soup and I have selected the conch chowder. This Italian chowder is different taste than normal chowder. It has different the flavor with similar creamy soup. I also like the bread before meal. I have order the blackened sirloin with gnocchi smoked Gouda cream sauce.  The steak was cook to order. The Gouda is place on top. It is interesting way to do it. Good quality steak. 

My wife have the special of the day. Grilled steak salad. This is ok. However the portion is big enough. Service is excellent. Food come out good and good temperature. We think this is a good restaurant and we will be back.

Our revisit has make me to reevaluate this restaurant. I like to change my opinion review to 3.5 stars. It is not a true 4 stars. The revisit show the restaurant step backwards in compare to the first few months they just open. I am some what disappointed. The nigiri has show increasing of rice and thinner fish cut. The sushi roll is still in good shape but not the best as before. I wonder I am going to revisit this place. Although they have good price for all you can eat but the quality drop. Service is still good.

I love downtown. But most of the time is difficult to find great food with reasonable price. Fusion Bowl has solved many lunch office workers with affordable price. The location also is prime location next to county office building. 

I was surprised we able to find a "great" drink place with decent food. The drink. I have the mixed berry with condensed milk with coffee jelly. This is great drink. This drink has many berry type and herb. We also has a good lavender drink and mango drink. All these drinks were good. But the mixed berry is the best. 

I got the beef noodle pho, lemon chicken fresh roll and grilled pork bowl. I said they are decent and acceptable. The quantity enough for lunch and better than fast food.  Lemon chicken is good to start. 

The store owner was friendly. I like this small business. They have a lot customer visiting during Sunday lunch. Imagine weekday afternoon.

During pandemic, Yamato considered has good customer traffic during difficult time. This has to thank to their simplicity of menu and more combo price dish. It is more attractive in compare to my first visit. The combo menu make it more affordable and the customer can try more items. 

I got the Yamato Special. It has shrimp, chicken, and steak. The side dish includes fried rice, veggies, noodle, salad, soup. This is the first time I also bring home the left over. My wife have the steak and calamari combo. We like our food. I think the chef make it a bit too salty. 

We always like the show. It includes the egg roll and toss. I also like the big fire in the beginning, ops check your eye brown after the show. Did it burn off. The volcano onion is classic. We enjoy the entertainment. As usual, this is seat close to the tepan cook top. Expect the food smell will stick to you. Just wear easy to wash. Cloth. Avoid bring and leather items such hand bag, clothing. The food smell will be difficult to remove from leather items.

Very good lunch place. In addition, a good breakfast place. They start early and close before dinner. I would said this restaurant is definitely 4.5 stars restaurant. They located in a small plaza and may be they are the only restaurant. Which make the parking area basically for this restaurant since no compete restaurant. 

I got the two pork chop. They actually has plenty of food because it come with two eggs, side of your choice and toast. I have my egg sunny side up. Seem like their egg are not regular egg because the yolk is more yellow. May be farm raise. I like the pork chop seasoning with a bit sweet. It look like Hawaiian style cooking. The chop is good grade because it has good fiber when you break the meat. 

I would compliment the chef skill to Caramelize the pork chop. The service is excellent. It is definitely the destination for lunch and Breakfast.

This restaurant located at Riverview. It is a popular restaurant in the area. Lunch has many customers is a good sign. I would said this is 4.5 stars restaurant in my book not yet 5 stars. I round up the stars because they have the Jackfruit Smoothie that not many restaurant carry it. The smoothie is nice dessert. 

I got the pork chop, shred pork, meat cake and fried egg and rice. Seem like this is a popular dish that many has order. The combo of this dish is twelve dollars but it has everything thing I need. Pork chop is delicious. Meat cake is a fan. I also has the shrimp fresh roll. The roll is big can be share and come in to two. 

Service is good and attentive. If I am visiting again, I would try their chef special. Ban Bun Hue. It is tapioca noodle.

I like this brewery. It has good beer hall, stage, decoration, art and ambient. Please check their calendar for event and special. I encourage them to continue to do it to attract the customers. 

I got their watermelon mint wheat ale. It was interesting to have because of the watermelon flavor. Price is in the median. The stage has good three D decoration with the eyes look at you no matter where you seat. It has projected the fish aquarium on the wall. The art gallery is another way for me to stroll. 

We were here for the Asian food truck rally. There people at the bar serving are nice to customers.

This is one of the kind breakfast place. We like the restaurant because is local flavor. The outside seating is good but if someone smokes, may be inside is better. The host is very friendly. We were able to tell we don't like the seat beginning. 

Make sure you ask for the daily special. It is always interesting. We have the country fried steak and chocolate pecan French toast. These are the special of the day. The country fried steak top with meat gravy. It also come with hash browns and two eggs. It also has mable toast. The French toast topping is very special with chocolate pecan overlay. Good sweet breakfast to begin the day. 

Service is good. I believe they are very good on their food for breakfast and lunch. Coffee is great.

I am happened to be near the Air Force Base, and we decided to visit this restaurant. Usually I don't make a trip here.  I decided to clear my book mark since I am here. 

Big Ray Fish Camp has in my book mark for a while. I saw Nick and Tina review and wanted to visit this place. We have order their signature dish lobster corn dog and the blacken grouper sandwich. The lobster corn dog come with mince garlic cheese fried that is impressive. The lobster corn dog is special with a lot of the lobster meat. No cheap. I believe their fried  is more tasty than the lobster meat. 

The grouper sandwich is just average. I have better than this place. Overall their price is at the high side. Not many of indoor seats. When iris rain outside, the seat is limited since the outside seating is wet. This place is busy. Good but no wow factor. This is a 3.5 stars restaurant.

Solid 4 stars. Very close to 4.5 stars. If they have more creative side, they probably 5 stars. This take out BBQ place is Riverview jewels. Many come here for the pickup food. The peach cobbler should not be miss. This is the item I recommend. 

We have the family meal deal with three meat types and 3 sides and a peach cobbler as a deal. The meat are ribs, chicken and pulled pork. The best is the rib. I like the way the have the rib with seasoning stick to the surface. The sons is the chicken. The sides we have is the yellow rice, garlic potatoes and collard greens. The best is the garlic potatoes. 

The deal is good for $25. It is in good quantity. The wait is good to order on side. Many call in. The smoke house just right outside.

I would said their attractive food are actually at the appetizer. They are located on the new plaza. The place and interior are nice. It has good open space for dining. The thing is lack off is the parking. Even though there are some parking on the front. Most of the diner time, these spaces are taken. You may have to park on the neighborhood street. 

We start with fresh house made guacamole. I said this dish is ok. Our second app is the Puerto Escondido Seafood Ceviche. Puerto Escondido is at the south west coast of Mexico at Oaxaca region. The ceviche is good. The shrimp is tiny shrimp. I rather have larger shrimp and chop in pieces. Our third dish is the Ancho Seared Ahi Tuna Wonton Taco. The tuna is seared and dust with pepper corn. It stuffed in the fried wontons skin and top with home made wasabi paste. The fish accompanied with salad will mixed with edamame. Our fourth dish is the Blue Crab Tortilla Crust Crab Cake. It is good crab cake. 

My friend has the blue Chan dinner plate. I think they do need to work on the dinner dish. Services is below average. When the waitress want to joke, do not spill water over the table. It is not good impression. It is 3.5 stars in my book.

I would said this is an old folks restaurant. The reason I said it because of the way they cook the food. Mostly broil and less sodium. It is an Greek restaurant with many history in Bay Area. 

They an not advertised rack of lamb. Only ask and you shall have it. It is not in the menu. We did not go for it since we are getting the early bird special. We have the broil octopus and the broil dole fish. The octopus is not grilled. If the grilled it will be much better. It is serve with sour sauce. The sole fish is only broil with stir fry veggies. I think all dish lack of salt or seasoning. Great for senior people. 

Service is good at restaurant. May be the happy hour is less people.

I would said this is 3.5 stars restaurant. It is not a four stars restaurant to my opinion. Since we don't have 1/2 star, four stars was given. 

We select the Christmas for our visit at the hour of their opening of the door. This will take out the crowed conditions for serving and the busy kitchen situation. This will give them a fare review. 

We have order the two appetizer- the Roti and the Pla Muek Yang. The roti is two round roti cut in eight pieces. It has the Malaysian roti taste. Although this may be from packaged factory made but was pan fried perfectly. I like the curry dipping. 

Pla Muek Yang aka grilled squid. It marinated in curry or Cumming. It is flame grilled and you can see the grilled mark. The only complaint it the dish come out cold. Seem like sit a bit before it was brought out. It serves with sweet sauce. It is about three squid cut in ring. 

Our entrees order is disaster. It take three rejections before we got our order. There are three items they don't carry yet. But I did not count against them on this review. I have order the Phat Chinese Broccoli and pork belly and they have given me Asian BBQ pork and Pork Belly  noodle. I did not ask them to change since it look interesting. We also added the spicy chicken seafood noodle. 

The Asian noodle soup base is very interesting and different. I believe the ingredients was not the same as described in the menu. The spicy chicken noodle are very close to Thai street noddle but in the sweet side. This two dishes is just ok. 

Food is about 3.5 rating; service is about 4.0 and the kitchen crew is about 3 ratings. I believe the kitchen should not have any excuse because there only three customers when we were there. They should not busy and should handle the food better.

Bar Louie is more open connecting to outdoor. But I do not like darker corner when you seat inside. This bar is second stop on our progressive happy hour tour. 

We started with fried calamari. The calamari is a bit tasteless because the coating is not interesting. May be make more floppy and spice with be more attractive. The second item is the chicken quesadilla. This is more interesting. But still this two item are not attractive enough in compare to nearby happy hour restaurant. However I do like the martini. Their signature martini during the happy hour is very good. I have the Diva martini. I like that one. 

I think the drink is better than the food. They really need to work on the food to attract more customers during happy hour.

I am glad that a just newly opened restaurant reopen for the take out. This restaurant open just before the pandemic. During the pandemic, I was not able to call them for they are open for take out because they not able to reach through the phone. Until recently they announced in Yelp they open for take out. 

Although we could not try their in store BBQ on the Korean BBQ, but one day we will be there. In the mean time, we appreciate they proceed with take out menu for us to try their food. We got the bulgogi and galbi plate. This dish come with white rice and four side dish. I like Korean side dish such as the tasty beans sprouts and the Korean fish cake. 

The Galbi has great marinated sauce. Well grilled, good meat quality, good enough quantity. The food is good for me to

The food may be 3.5 stars, however the price match what they selling. Overall is 4 stars. Cheddar secret is affordable price for many and good enough food. It fit into the demographics of The Wesley Chapel. It is really do not matter about the rating. It is about right price for right food. 

I am at the bar area enjoy my dinner for the Sunday night football on TV. I started with the Texas Swirl Margarita. It is beautiful drink with enough frozen frozen drink over strawberry. My entree is the New Orlean Pasta. This dish come with sausage, chicken and shrimp. This dish serve over penne pasta and Cajun Alfredo sauce. It is big dish if you are hungry. 

The service on bar is average. Can be better. Food came out quick. Not much of wait. I like the drinks with different cocktails.

Movie night at the citrus park mall. It close at 2 am in the morning. It offer late night snack and beer. They all day beer special and after 10 pm special. At certain day they have all you can eat wings or tacos. 

The night we have visit they have combo special 2 people for $30. Very good deal. In the combo plater, it has 5 types of grilled meat. Pork rib, petite sirloin, smoke wings, grilled chicken breast and sausage. It also come with grilled onion and wedge potatoes. This item serves over the fire grill that keep the food warm. The grille has center plate to heat up the food. I like this way because many BBQ place has combo. At the of combo, the remaining food get cold. However, the device they have in this restaurant keep warm and heat up in the middle of grill. 

I would give them 5 stars for the food taste, keep warm on the combo, good service, nice open dinning hall, great price on the alcohol. I got 22oz Miller lite for $5.5.

This taco is number three in my list. My list is base on the authenticity, price range, taste of food and quantity of the food. This taco place has make all check marks I have set. 

This is a food truck at SR 60 and the Lithia Pinecrest. The location is located on the northeast quadrant of the intersection. Easy to fine. The hour is odd. Only weekend has longer hour. So check the time before visit. During the lunch and dinner time, many people call ahead so you need to be patient to wait for the food because of the take out. 

We got the shrimp, Campechano (Steak and Mexican sausage), Babarcoa (BBQ), carnitas, pastor, chicharon. The six Taco was prepared in giant quantity. Roughly $2 each. But their taco meat is enough for two taco in normal taco place. I like the babarcoa and the shrimp taco. Those are very good. 

Our wait is close to 30 minutes because it was dinner time. But it was worthwhile. Food is real good.

This restaurant do have the vibe to serve the Italian food. Their menu is constantly evolving on the availability of ingredients. This is very interesting Italian restaurant. I would suggest early dinning or reservation. Reservation is strongly suggested. Please call ahead before come here. 

The food serve of the day is written on the kitchen door in Italian. It give a chance for the waitress to explain to you what the dish make off. We start with insalata di Trota. This is Smoke Trout salad with orange dressing. This dish is delicious. Our entrée are Ossobuco Di Maiala and Seafood Pasta. The seafood pasta is just so so. It does has squid, little neck clam, shrimp, and fillet snapper. Big portion. The ossobuco is Beef shoulder braise in good sauce. It come with home made pasta. 

This restaurant total has 7 table of three. Maximum capacity of 21. AC need to be a bit stronger since kitchen and dinning hall are connected. I like the ideal allowing customers to bring their own alcohol or wine. It make dinning pleasant.

(vegan review)

pretty much a nightmare if you're vegan; don't go here. there's nothing on the menu that's vegan (egg-based noodles, meat-stock-based sauce.) if you decide to go anyway, don't be surprised if they flock around you startled with questions like you're the first vegans to ever show up in their restaurant. if you're vegan, forget it.

Stopped by for some lunch on Saturday afternoon after reading their glowing reviews. I love pastrami and I'm told they have the best and the reviews are completely accurate. 

I went with the highly recommended Rachel Sandwich which is a grilled hot pastrami with Swiss cheese, coleslaw, and Russian dressing and I chose rye bread. It also comes with some delicious dill pickle spears. 

This was by far the best pastrami I have ever had! So tender, juicy, and delicious! 

The line wasn't very long around 3pm and moved pretty quickly and all of the employees were very friendly and efficient. The only hard part was finding a seat because the market is very busy... especially on Saturdays. But it was definitely worth it. 

They were also able to validate my parking with a $10.00 purchase so my parking was only $4 at the Hilton Parking garage next door that was good for 2 hours... 

Definitely recommend!

Love their cupcake. The giant frosting is bit much for me, but the cake itself has nice soft crumb and delicate flavor. Try the lemon - mmmm good!

Also loving is the staff. As I walked into the store little nervously, late in the evening, I was greeted by two happy staff who recommended me the red-velvet and lemon among bunch of selection. Thanks guys, I'll be back!

Being right down the street from the office, we visit the Cheese Board pretty frequently.  It's a great lunch option when you want "lunch food" but something more than just a deli.  The menu changes daily but they also have a standard menu to choose from.  Others have mentioned that it can get busy at lunch, which is true, but I've never had an issue with ordering and having enough time to eat before my lunch hour is up.  It can get loud inside when the tables fill up but they have outdoor dining as well.  

Besides just lunch type food including soup, salads, and sandwiches, they also have a selection of specialty cheese, wines and handmade desserts.  Get the lemon bar - and you're welcome!  It's worth the calories and the guilt trip you might have later.   Everything we've ever tried, we've loved.  The options are fresh, tasty and a bit healthier than other lunch options downtown.  The selection is varied too so it's a great place to take a group.

Panda king hot pot is bomb!!! Such a cool concept to come to Nola. Each person gets their own heating element for their hot pot. You start by choosing off your broth: chicken, beef, vegetable, or tom yum. I chose Tom Yum because Yum. Unlimited broth as well. (PK hack, they let you bring your food to go if you can't finish it all). 

Next, you can order your meats and drinks with the server. We got the pork belly and the beef brisket. 
Three ladies roll around carts that you can choose items from, they stamp your clipboard hanging off the side of the table just like dim sum. One cart has noodles, eggs, random things like a million different mushrooms. One cart has all of the seafood: mussels, scallops, shrimp, clams. The last cart has all the veggies: Napa cabbage, Bok Choy, etc. 
It's all affordable too! IMO, at least. All dishes were either 8.99 or cheaper! Meats ran high, shrimp was 5.99, and veggies and such were cheaper than that. A little goes a long way with hot pot. 
There's a side bar with sauces, scallions, toppings. They had more Tom yum paste, and i definitely got some to add more kick to my broth. 
The shrimp was yummy and fresh. Can't go wrong with vegetables. We got the udon noodles and egg noodles.
Overall, it was a great experience. Great service, great food, and nice experience. The new marble tables with the personalized cooktops are sooo neat! I'd love to take my family back.

For some reason, I typically avoid restaurants inside of resorts, but after our lunch at BRGR, I should really reconsider. We came to BRGR for an early lunch after scoping out their menu on Yelp. I was craving a burger and burgers is what we got! 

The ambiance and decor of the restaurant is very modern and nice. The interior has tall windows that wrap around half of the restaurant overlooking the pool and there is a nice bar area towards the front of the restaurant. Sit where ever and a server will be with you. They had burgers, wraps, and "burger bowls" to choose from. I went with "The Attitude" and my date had "The Treehugger" (vegetarian burger). Both came with a choice of sides. The herbed fries are highly recommended! 

All of the burger options seemed so different with lots of different flavor options. Both of our selections were excellent. Hot, good flavor, large portion sizes, and decent prices. We also order champagne by the glass (celebrating our new house) and walked away with about a $50 bill. Service was great. They know the balance of being available and leaving you be. 

Overall, I highly recommend as a great lunch spot or a place for drinks and appetizers. Nice ambiance and great view. We'll visit again next time we're in Treasure Island!

Really good pizza served here. It's about $6+ for a slice depending what you want (starting at $6 for a slice of cheese pizza). Slices are big and price is pretty average especially since it's on Bourbon street. You can't expect to receive cheap food on such a busy street but I didn't mind the price as it was really good. There isn't enough seating and the restrooms are not well maintained so I took away a star. Perfect pizza to grab especially after a long night out on Bourbon street. They also advertise having the cheapest beer on Bourbon. $5 for their beers on tap (which isn't bad at all). No other pizza spot looked as appetizing as Crescent City Pizza Works. I wish I had found this place on my first day instead of my last because I would have definitely been there daily for a slice.

Finally - a degree of culinary sophistication hits the gulf shores!  No sign of grouper sandwiches or fish net decor here. Only a menu that offers us locals a fresh new taste sensation; in a bright and contemporary setting where local art adorns the walls.  What's more the staff were sweet and attentive.  I was desperate to like this place and they well exceeded my expectations.

Why you should go there right now: 

7:30am Sunday - Cupcake balls filled with a dollop of white cream, dipped in raspberry jelly, the rolled in electric pink coconut. Probably one of the best two bite confections I've ever eaten. I will be there this morning buying more. 

Post cupcake buying update: 
My son and I headed over promptly at 8:30 treasure hunting for more pink balls of happiness. The place was crowded as ever, and a ping of concern went through me. What the heck if people were actually reading my reviews. Yikes! Do I get dibs on my favorite items? We stood in line and nowhere did my eyes see an electric pink puff. I did spy something new, a peanut butter tastycake cake. Hmmm. 

Mrs. McMillan herself waited on us this morning, and when I asked about the cupcake bites, she informed me that they were one of her son's 'creations' and she'd give our feedback that we enjoyed them. I asked about the peanut butter tastycake cake, and she assured me if we liked peanut butter we'd love that. I told her that my son was a particular fan, and we've never been disappointed with anything we've ordered, especially her son's 'creations'. While she was wrapping that up we discussed how they are the lone purveyors of the granulated sugar cream donut, and she remembered Bredenbeck's in Mayfair when I mentioned it. Knowing how to work a crowd, she asked my son if he'd ever had their peanut butter brownie. He said he hadn't, and suddenly there was a small bag placed in his hand with a wink 'to try'. 

In the eight seconds (later at home) that the peanut butter brownie was visible to my eye before my son inhaled it and pronounced it 'great' I will say it did indeed look great. 3" square, a definite layer of peanut butter, a large walnut on top. Very moist looking. Yum. 

I spied a small chocolate mound in the case and asked what it was. "Oh, that's today's creation. It's a cupcake center with cream filling, iced in vanilla butter cream, dipped in chocolate ganace, dusted with white chocolate slivers with a dollop of chocolate mousse on top." 

O.M.G. 

So as my blood sugar soared past 200 just looking at this mountain of sweet (that she was wrapping up for me) I assured myself that the yardwork I would be doing today would offset the potential sugar coma this confection represented. The tab for all these items, plus donuts and a few danishes - $16.75. The free brownie and wink to my peanut butter loving son = customer for life.

I would give a 0 if I could. TheGroupon coupon is a SCAM-stay away. Instead of honoring the coupon they pointed to 24 hour fine print. Rest assured we will never eat there.  

Got a refund from Groupon

In person or take out, this place does not fool around with rare beef pho. Space for inside dining that is clean!
For take out, you get all the soups tightly wrapped with no spills in the car. The basil, and other veggies are also in a tightly sealed bag, ready for travel. The meat is still really cold and separated from everything else in plastic wrap. 
The flavor puts everything over the top. Lots of beef! Good portion of noodles, and lots of hoi sin and sriracha packets. Lots of hot peppers if you care to partake in that. You can choose not too. Just order and get some.

I have been wanting to come into this place for a very long time and finally got around to peeking inside,  and wow this place is awesome.

Right of the bat you notice all the character of the inside. Everything from the reclaimed wooden floors to the tiled historic-eque ceiling, down to the real tea candles lit on the tables. The decor is really something. You definitely feel in a different city coming here. Winslow's Home would be a hit in San Francisco because it reminds me so much of the little coffee shops they have there. 

I love that they sell little kitchen gadgets and mugs. I like the variety of different foods they have to sell in the back. Everything looks fresh and home made and I like the fact that they use locally grown produce. Have you tried the Chicken Pot Pie? OMG it is to die for. I love the crust and the price is reasonable although when I asked how to heat in the oven the Barista said 30 min at 350F. WOW really?

It took 1 hour at 400F just for you future Pot Pie eaters. I have also tried the Americano and the Toddy and those were really good. I especially liked the Coffee Toddy. My BF tried the Apple Pie and he said it was really really good. Is it worth the $5 price tag? Not sure. 

Overall I like the atmosphere and the vibe of Winslow's Home. Its a little on the pricier side when it comes to food and drinks but the ambiance is worth it though. I love that they have outdoor seating as well. I hope this business continues to do well and that people pour in because places like Winslow's Home are far and few in the area.

I could have sworn I wrote a review for this place but I guess it slipped my mind. Which leads us to the 2 star review. Everyone has already said what my experience was but I'll just add my two cents.

Why we left a perfectly good place to come here will always haunt me in my dreams. We got there about 12:30ish on a Saturday and the line wasn't too bad but once we got in it was way too crowded on the inside. I HATE not being able to move, LITERALLY MOVE, in a club. Since getting to the downstairs bar wasn't going to happen we made a quick turn to try and go upstairs...it HAD to be more room up there. Well I wouldn't know because the bouncer said we had to by a drink to even LOOK at the stairs.(Maybe LOOK is an over exaggeration but you get my point). Trying to explain that there is a 100% chance that I will buy a drink upstairs just to get out of this sweaty mass of hair gel and shiny shirts will get you no where. And honestly, why the F did I even HAVE to explain that. You know what? You were going to get a 2 star review until i remembered how DUMB a policy that was. Now we are down to 1.

Now I know the owner tends to get in little quips about people not reviewing this spot well, but don't even think about it until you can explain to me how you came up with such a dumb ass rule.

Has there ever been any dessert more instagrammable than the pops at Lil' Pop Shop? This little cafe in Rittenhouse Square is absolutely adorable, and their desserts are perfectly refreshing for any hot day. I ordered the strawberry mochi in a small, which was the perfect afternoon pick-me-up. Not too sweet and I loved the chewy texture that the mochi added. I can't wait to come back for more this summer!

After exhausting the brunch scene of Center City, I decided to branch out a bit and try out High Street on Market with a few friends. On a Saturday morning, we met up at about 10:30 and were seated immediately (!!!) at the communal table. The waitstaff was friendly and attentive. I was surprised by how small the menu was, but I have to say that quality over quantity was definitely clear in their presentation. My friends and I all ordered breakfast sandwiches. I went for the Hickory Town, which included Lancaster bolonga, egg over easy, horseradish cheddar, and fried red onion all on a seeded bun. I think I finished my sandwich in less than 5 minutes, it was that good. I ordered a chocolate chip shortbread cookie for dessert, which was delicious and not overly sweet or heavy. Overall, a great option for breakfast if you're ever in the Old City area!

We went there last Saturday evening for dinner. We chose this restaurant thanks to Yelp reviews. We were in Tucson only for the long week-end. We called around 7pm to see if they still have availabilities for tonight (they close at 9pm). They suggested 8.30pm. It was a bit late for us, but we wanted to eat an healthy diner, so we made the reservation.

We arrived at the restaurant, right on time. There is not really a reception area. So, you wait with the entrance door in your back and the kitchen doors on your left. We stayed there waiting for someone to welcome us (there was another couple waiting with us who arrived just before us). 2 waitresses exited and entered the kitchen more than once without even looking at us. One of the owners (I guess as I saw her picture on their website) did the same thing twice. The third time, she finally looked at us to say something like "Sorry, it will take a little bit longer". At least, she finally noticed us and spoke to us. The other couple didn't like the way we were "welcomed" either. They also had a reservation. They were seated before us as they arrived before. At 9pm, we were still waiting in front of the entrance door, with waitresses coming in and out the kitchen, not looking at us, not smiling... That is the first time I see that kind of customer experience in the USA ! To be honest, if I would have known the city better, I would have left. But it was late, we were hungry, in a city we didn't know and I didn't want to end up in a fast-food. That is why we stayed.

At 9pm, I went to speak with the owner to tell her I didn't like the way they were handling us. She said : "I can't ask people to leave." I said they could at least notice us instead of just passing in front of us without even looking at us. She didn't understand and said : "But, I spoke with you and told you you will have to wait."... Is it, really, the way you handle clients ?

We were finally seated just after 9pm. They have 2 rooms and we were in the back. We were seated in cheap folding chairs. You can find better chairs at Ikea.

A waitress gave us the menu. We ordered. She came back 5 minutes later to tell us that they didn't have what we ordered anymore. I can totally understand that, at the end of the service, all the menu is not available anymore. BUT it is the job of the waitress to ask that kind of things in the kitchen BEFORE giving the menu to the clients. It can happen, but, with the wait and the welcoming atmosphere, it was something else to add.

We finally managed to eat. As far as the food is concerned, it is good, but it is not outstanding. It is good because it is from fresh products. It is done with taste. You can feel that the owners like cooking. But, there is nothing exceptional.

When they gave us the check, I was surprised to see that they didn't even offer us the beverages to, at least, ease things up. I think it would have been a good gesture from them.

They didn't give us any other explanation. We paid. The waitress went to the kitchen. We were the last ones in the room and we left just like that.

During our diner, I heard one waitress explaining to another table that it was the busiest night they had until the opening. She apologized for the wait to them. At another table, it seems there was an issue with what they ordered (maybe they couldn't do it anymore, I am not sure). But, they apologized.

Would it have been difficult to explain what was going on to us ? I would have appreciate the honesty. I would have been less angry at them and more understanding. But, they didn't explain anything and never apologize to us. It seems the way they treated us is normal.

In my opinion, they love food and they love cooking, but they should learn how to welcome clients. Because, when you open a restaurant, you have to deal with people. And for that, you have to be friendly and know how to handle busy times and situations like that. A restaurant is not only about the food.

I live really close to Courtyard and come here often. I love that it is super casual and people who hang out here just want to drink good beer. Their beers are really good - as someone who lived in SD for a long time (where Scott the owner/brewer is from), I am happy drinking anything that they brew. That Sonic Youth one is probably my favorite. But really, I haven't had a stinker yet.

In addition to their beer, they have a nicely curated selection on tap and in bottles and cans. I love that they get a lot of West Coast beers in addition to beers from other small breweries in the area. Something for everyone for sure. 

The food truck schedule is also a plus - Taceaux Loceaux, Saigon Slims and St. Clairs Pizza are all top quality noshes.

Pro trip: get a plastic growler which holds 2 beers for your to-go beer pleasure.

November 20, 2009 @ 5pm

We're in Reno--Land of Cheap Buffets--but BFand I wanted  to share a quiet and non-mass produced meal.   Roxy's provided us with a  classy and romantic evening. 

AMBIANCE: Roxy's is an oasis in the land of kitsch and cheap food. The dining room is removed from the noise of the the casino that you can truly enjoy an intimate dinner.  Roxy's is a tasteful and sophisticated restaurant inside El Dorado Hotel.  I didn't want to ruin the classy ambiance that I turned off the flash of the camera and couldn't really take pictures. We had dinner in the main dining room but there's also a patio dining which is livelier.  http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/15BlJKQfD-SLJTebWa14EQ?select=dIQFyOiVQsehw8EuXY5t7g

DECOR: The restaurant is dim and heavy with dark wood and impressive iron chandelier. Along the walls are temperature-controlled wine cabinets.   It tastefully follows the Medieval decor.  http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/15BlJKQfD-SLJTebWa14EQ?select=vTv4ZW3MaH_QWGIQZGkDSg

SERVICE: Service was a notch above your typical restaurant. Professional and knowledgeable server attended to us the whole evening.  The wait staff never let our water go down 3/4 of our glass. A woman with the warm bread basket was making her rounds to serve us warm bread with butter. http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/15BlJKQfD-SLJTebWa14EQ?select=56wqtK_np45IwFY7zIcb0Q

SOCIAL SCENE: Well-dressed mature and older crowd. Young people in gowns and tux (Wedding party, maybe?)

OUR DRINKS:
BF: Pink Diamond Martini ($5 Happy Hour price)
Me: Flight of 3oz each Chandon, Cuvee and Domaine Laurent ($10) 

COMPLIMENTARY: WARM CHEESE BACON BREAD that we could have made a meal out of!  Freshly-baked, loaded with cheese and bacon and so good! Even my BF who dislikes bacon so much loved it!

APPETIZERS:
BF:  LOBSTER ESCARGOT( $14): Firm, meaty Australin lobster and soaked in butter! Really good. We could have eaten 2 more orders! http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/15BlJKQfD-SLJTebWa14EQ?select=EX3IF_yaV_tyusyQ0pmdzA
Me:  FOIE GRAS ($13): Really tender and buttery cmplimented by the earthy flavors of the chestnut. The portion was too rich and too much for me that I tricked BF into eating a whole chunk!

MAIN:
BF: 20 oz PRIME PORTERHOUSE STEAK ($35):  BF enjoyed his juicy and tender steak! http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/15BlJKQfD-SLJTebWa14EQ?select=GJvgc4D65yifI7ol0JWWgw
Me: SEARED AHI TUNA ($21) : Very fresh and generous slices of thick tuna served with delicious sauteed mitaki mushrooms, kale and miso butter. http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/15BlJKQfD-SLJTebWa14EQ?select=gPz3sHtho4kJbKLtzHk8Eg

SIDES:  SAUTEED MUSHROOM: BF wanted a side of veggie. The server quickly suggested this dish which is not on the menu and delivered us a generous portion of sauteed juicy mitaki mushrooms and only charged us $2.95! 

DESSERT ($6 each):
BF:  HOT CHOCOLATE CUP: Hot chocolate cake, vanilla bean ice cream and chantilly cream. 
Me:  APPLE SORBET:  A simple dish but refreshing dessert with big chunks of apple. Not my first choice but the only non-dairy dessert on the menu.

TAB: $150.00 including tax and 20% tip. For the amount and quality of food we had, I think this was a bargain! 

OVERALL: (5 Stars)
Dinner was terrific! The reviews were mixed but there was nothing I could find to complain about!  All our dishes were well-presented and well-crafted.   Very attentive service. Great value and generous portions. 

Our dinner at Roxy's was so pleasurable that I don't mind the 3 1/2 hour drive from North Oakland to  just to have dinner again.  Not at all the tacky and gawdy picture that comes to mind when "Reno" is mentioned.

MARTINI  BAR:  Roxy's is well-known for its vast martini selection.  We didn't sit at the bar that's  quite large and separate from the main dining area.  It follows the same classy ambiance of the restaurant.  The live jazz and vocalist were so inviting that next time I'll make a point to sit at the bar first before eating in the main dining room.

Just plain loved it!

After running around New Orleans all day and all night we needed something to satisfy our late night  cravings. Did a quick yelp search and came across this little Gem.
Located inside the 700 bar towards the back so we walked past it a few times without even realizing at first. Unfortunately kids are not allowed inside due to it being connected to a bar, but take out is always an option, or leaving your kids at home lol. 

Order at the register, pay, and find a place to sit joint. The menu has various options and we wanted to try everything but knew our bellies couldn't handle it so we settled for sharing the Everything Mac & cheese skillet, Brussel sprouts, Fried fish sandwich,Southern fried chicken sandwich, and the barbecue chicken wings.


BRUSSELS SPROUTS w BACON 4.75 - crispy sprouts with crispy bacon. 

BBQ CHICKEN WINGS 10 crispy and just the right amount of bbq sauce  4 stars***

EVERYTHING MAC & CHEESE SKILLET- 10.50 
Creamy five-cheese macaroni, melted cheddar topped with toasted panko bread crumbs 4 stars*** pretty darn good. The cheese was melted all the way through with crispy edges yum.

SOUTHERN FRIED CHICKEN SANDWICH 9.75
Comes with a perfectly breaded and fried piece of chicken topped with Garlic mayo, shredded lettuce, and house pickles. Omg this was my FAVORITE of the night. The bun was toasted and buttery the chicken had perfect breading all the way around. And the toppings were just right. Order this you'll thank me later 5 stars*****


FRIED CATFISH SANDWICH 9.75
A piece of fried catfish topped with Sambal mayo, sesame-sriracha slaw, pickled peppers, cilantro. Pretty good and was a decent sandwich in size and flavor. 4 stars****

Give this place a chance and try it for yourself.

I really had a problem with high end soul food when I first heard about this restaurant opening.   Most good soul food i have had has always been in sketchy areas and great prices.   It's things that don't usually cost a lot to make... Fried bologna, collard greens,fried fish... Well I decided to go with some co-workers to try it out and give it a chance.   We looked at the menu on line and wanted to love it so much.  We decided on a list of things we wanted to try out, but to our disappointment most of the items were not offered as the kitchen was still working out its kinks said the waitress.  

Well we placed our order starting with the rib tips to share as an appetizer.  Well to our dismay we got 3 small pieces of meat on our a tiny plate.  We were not even sure how to share the small bites of food we were about to try.  They fell off the bone and were moist but tasted more like beef stew than any rip tips  I have ever had before.  

The table setting was disappointing as well as they proclaim themselves as upscale per the website and the menu, yet our table was set completely wrong.  The service was unprofessional and a little embarrassing.  The silverware was definitely not set correctly.  The glasses were not kept full.  The people at the front hostess stand were constantly laughing hysterically, there were only 5 tables seated yet we were all sitting on top of each other all in the corner.   

The waitress kept telling us that she was short staffed and not fully trained.  It took us a long time to get our food.   So long that in the hour and half lunch break we didn't get our food in time and had to have them box it up.  Even after she said it was ready to be brought out, it took an additional 10 minutes to bring out to us in our boxes.   

The porkchops were dry.   The sauce was good but minimal but couldn't hide the fact that the porkchops were way way way overcooked.   The green beans tasted like they came straight from the can with more onions than green beans.   As far as the burger, you were better off going to red robin or bagger daves. Much better quality for what you are paying and that is pretty bad...  if you want some true soul food I would recommend driving a little further south into the city and getting some more taste, food, and experiences for your money!

For my 700th review, I wanted to write about something absolutely spectacular.  Sunday evening.  First of all, I would like to point out that I have driven through Nashville over 50 times in my life, and I only stopped once- I ended up being encountered by 3 meth heads and got food poisoning.  That left a reallll sour taste in my mouth.  

I was driving back home to MEM from SDF (sorry I use airport code, SDF=Louisville).  My car KEPT telling me to get rest.  But I had no idea about any hotels in Nashville.  I kept looking up stuff, and I saw this place.  So I looked at rooms, and saw the place had promise- so I booked a grand deluxe, on a whim, with a AAA rate.  Mind you, I did this about an hour from Nashville.  

I got to the city, and I was able to find the hotel fairly easily.  I packed light, with my backpack.  I pulled up to the valet (which should be valet only here), and told them I was checking in.  Very nice.  I walked into the hotel, and was amazed at the old world elegance this place had.  And the fact it was about 10PM on a Sunday night, it wasn't hectic at all.  

I gave the gentleman at the front desk my AAA card, my license, and my AMEX.  He asked me if there was anything special going on, and I just told him I needed to relax before my upcoming week of hell.  He told me he had good news for me, that I just got upgraded to the Presidential Suite!  I thought I had gotten punked, but it was for real!  I just wanted some extra space (as the grand deluxe is 590 sq ft).  He gave me the keys to room 812, and the adventure began...

I took the elevator to the 8th floor (out of 9), and my room was right there.  I couldn't find the door, (as it was labeled 812)- then I was realized, I had 3 to choose from. I entered, and there was some graceful music playing from a Bose sound system. The pics I took should be self explanatory, but let me tell you what- staying in one of the nicest rooms in the state, was truly a once in a lifetime opp- considering the price I paid.  The view of the Capitol was phenomenal- at night and at day.

The actual suite is about 2000 square feet- with the bedroom on the right (marble bathroom tucked away), a huge ass tv area and living area with dining room table for 6, and 1/2 bath there.  On that end is also the mini kitchen with tons of bar stuff and snacks.  I still couldn't believe it.  I could walk from one end of the suite to the other, and honestly get winded- it was that big!  

The bathrooms were equipped with Molton Brown amenities, the stuff I currently use to keep my skin clean- I was surely impressed!  I was also surprised to see they had a choice of buckwheat, latex, and memory foam pillows in the closet for your liking- but I just stuck to the 5 on the bed that were already there :).

After playing around in the room, I decided to walk around downstairs and soak in the rest of the place.  I started on the Mezzanine level, where the spa, fitness center, and Governor's Salon was.  There were also 3 ornate tables that could be used for chess, overlooking the lobby.

I had heard about the famous bathroom here, so I looked.  And when I went into the bathroom, I realized this is really nice- but not the one I had seen in the news (next review on that one).  So I went downstairs to the bar, got some food n drinks, and headed back up to paradise.

I had to take a shower, and that thing was awesome.  There were 2 handles, one for a handheld water stream, the other for a nice surprise- a freaking 4 head ceiling shower that felt like a rainstorm.  I fell asleep in the robe that night...

Waking up was hard, as the bed was so comfortable and I realized I had to get back to Memphis soon.  So I took another shower, and I was on my way.  Valet got my car in a matter of minutes, and they were as friendly as can be.

This place is on the high end, but I tell you what, there was absolutely no complaints here.  If I could give this place 6 stars, I would.  And it gave me an entirely new perspective of Nashville. So for that, I thank you dearly.

Cheers!

[M]ona: 3 Stars

Average: 3.75 Stars

+ Accepts Credit Cards
