Trader Joe's grocery has THE best pandemic precautious for seniors in the area. They offer special hours for seniors between 8-9 am daily. A masked clerk greets you outside with a freshly cleaned cart and smile and will politely turn away non-seniors. The automatic doors mean I don't have to touch anything. I felt safe. Inside the store is ultra clean and everyone wears a mask. 

I have been shopping here for many years. I love the vegetables, cheeses, meats, specialty items and wine selection. Prices are great. Some of the merchandise you can only find here. The products are high quality and many products focus on sustainability. I stock up on the 99 cent cards. And the fresh flowers are the freshest and most reasonably priced in town. 

The service is always friendly and efficient wearing cheerful Hawaiian shirts and a smile. I love the flyers they send out with recipes and articles about new products. 

The parking lot can be a bear during peak hours, but I shop early and have no issues.

The owner/hostess is so unbelievably rude it's hard to see how Stone House attracts return business. That said, I've eaten there 25 times or more -- never again. The location is the big draw. The food is good (though way overpriced) and the servers are always very friendly but Serena Aboud, the owner, is impolite. On a recent visit, with a large group for which we had made a reservation to celebrate a birthday, she insisted on separating our group between two tables -- one inside, one outside. She insisted that Stone House never accommodates groups of 14, even though this exact group has dined many times over the years on the patio. Needless to say, after some cross words, we left. Even though my family loves this place for breakfast we will never give Serena our business again.

Lees Deli is an amazing Deli that sells everything from Cheesesteaks to Korean good. The owners are very friendly and there is always a large selection of daily specials. I have been going to Lee's deli since elementary school. The best Deli in West philly hands down!

This place is so cute! People sent me pictures of it and I was so surprised to hear that it was in Reno so we had to go try! 

It's very simple Asian style soft serve ice cream on syrup covered cake. Sort of like a parfait. You can either select something from the favorites menu or build your own.

To build your own, you start by choosing your flavor: vanilla, chocolate, matcha (green tea), or ube (purple yam). You can also swirl 2 flavors to get a little bit of both!
Next, you select your cake: vanilla or chocolate.
Then, pick your syrup: strawberry (has pieces of strawberry in it), chocolate ganache, red bean, and condensed milk.
Finally, you can top it off with some Pocky sticks: matcha, strawberry, cookies and creme, or chocolate.

I chose to customize my own and got an ube and matcha swirl, on vanilla cake, with condensed milk. The ube and matcha was a great balanced combo. Everything had a mild flavor and wasn't too sweet. 

I'm really glad that we have something like KRĒM in town and I'm excited to see where they go and if they plan to incorporate more flavors and how they plan to expand their menu in the future! 

Don't forget to try a sample if you're not sure what you want and it's a little pricey so grab a stamp card so you can earn a free one!

The best brunch spot and it's local! I had no idea BJ's had such a delicious brunch menu and I'm so glad someone told me about it!

We went in around 11am on a Sunday morning and our group of 4 was seated with little wait time. First we started with a round of BJ's Bacon Bloody Mary's. This seriously one of the best Bloody Mary's I've had in Reno. There aren't a ton of toppings (celery, bacon, lime, olives) like other places but it really doesn't need all the extra stuff. It isn't watery, has great flavor, and the best part is the bacon rim. 

We ordered the corned beef hash stacker, the chicken fried steak, and biscuits and gravy with eggs, hash browns, and a side of hot link.

The corned beef hash stacker was tasty and the poached eggs with hollandaise sauce went well with the home fries and corned beef. I also liked the biscuit and apple butter that came with it.
The chicken fried steak was crispy and the gravy was flavorful, and the hot link was a good addition to the biscuits and gravy. 
All of it really gives you that "comfort meal" feeling.
The portions were huge and with the Bloody Mary beforehand, it was a very filling meal. However, you have to save room for dessert! We each got a cinnamon roll but just one could have definitely been shared by everyone but it tastes just as good warmed up the next day! Make sure you order this ahead of time because they do run out!

Overall I would definitely go back and it is currently my favorite brunch place in Reno. Even though I'm not a huge BBQ lover I can't wait to go try the rest of the menu for lunch and dinner as well!

I remember going to Taiwan Restaurant as a kid to pick up Dry Beef Ho Fun with my mom. It has been in Reno for over 20 years and the food still tastes just as good. It is run by the nicest family. The have always given large, affordable portions and everything is made fresh. 

Going back now, I have been able to try more of their menu. The best thing about Taiwan Restaurant is how many unique dishes they have. I have yet to find other places in town that offer some of the thing they do. One of the biggest highlights is the paper chicken appetizer. So good! The chicken is tender and flavorful. 

Another of my favorites are the duck dishes. While it has been getting more common lately, it was always difficult to find whole duck dishes in Reno since they usually had to be picked up from Sacramento. Both the Crispy and the Roasted duck are delicious! Both have their distinct flavors so it wouldn't hurt to try both. 

As always, the Dry Beef Ho Fun still tastes as good as it did 15 years ago, and you can't go wrong with the potstickers and crab rangoon. 

There is definitely something for everyone on the menu so bring the whole family or take it to go to share. Currently, the owners are trying to retire so what better time than now to check out the restaurant before it's gone!

This is a great place for a cheesesteak and I definitely recommend their truffle fries. They blend the cheese (go with Cooper Sharp) well with the meat and make eat bite a moment of pure indulgence. This establishment will definitely demonstrate that a cheesesteak is indeed a culinary wonder.

Service was great and the food was very good. I did not get the pizza, but it looked good (yes, I do notice the food as it passes by me). Fried mozzarella looks great, too.

I guess that this is a relatively newcomer to the Philly food scene and while it might not have the longevity of some of the other restaurants in this amazing city, but Cafe Carmela is certainly endearing itself to its customers and anyone that happens to wonder through their door in search of a great meal.

I definitely recommend Cafe Carmela. I also have to give it five stars.

While I never associated the Scottish with fantastic burgers (if anything, I think fish and chips, meat pies, etc.), the Ranch - Scottish Highland Burgers definitely offers some great burgers and if you find yourself in Boise, Idaho, you do owe it to yourself to stop in and grab one of their fantastic burgers.

Now I do think of potatoes when I think of Idaho and the french fries here are definitely something that this place has every right to brag about. They were cooked to perfection, crispy on the outside and pillowy tenderness underneath that crunchy exterior.

For the burger, I went with the Spicy Cowgirl, which was a quarter pound of grass fed, locally-raised beef topped with smoked gouda, jalapeno peppers, and mayo. Got some ketchup on it, too, because a burger needs ketchup. It comes with a drink and those tasty french fries, as well.

Prices are good and the service was friendly. If you are extra hungry you can get an extra hamburger patty. I will forewarned you though that this place is little more than a shack with a drive-through. Don't expect some rustic-looking lodge type grandeur to enjoy your burger and fries and since they associated with Scotland, with bagpipe players serenading you. No, the only serenading might come from the traffic passing by on Overland Road and the ambiance that she will feel is the front seat of your car as you eat a quick lunch. But that does not take away from the quality of these great burgers and french fries.

All in all, I definitely recommend this establishment. Stop in and get a burger and some french fries. If you want to hear that bagpipe music, turn on the radio and look for a Scottish station or Google bagpipe music on your phone. But these burgers are pretty amazing.

Five Daughters Bakery is an extremely popular place and after trying some of their baked goods, it is easy to see why.

Five Daughters Bakery is very good at what they do and the food they create is housed in a very cool, hip and inviting atmosphere. Add to that the friendly staff and you are in for a great experience.

This is a great place to begin your day at or to stop by and grab so.ething for a tasty dessert. Overall, it is easy to see why Five Daughters Bakery is spoken with such reverence by Foodies in the area and how it has been embraced by the community and sought by travelers (like myself) to the area.

I would definitely recommend Five Daughters Bakery to anyone seeking a bakery in the area. You really cannot go wrong with anything that you select from here. I am sure that you won't be disappointed. Go check them out.

First off, let me applaud this establishment for such a cool name. They try to capture that "Old Florida" atmosphere and offer a nice varied menu to appeal to almost anyone who ends up sitting down in one of their chairs for a meal or a drink.

Place has a cool vibe, there is no disputing that.   The view of the lake only enhances that whole experience. The food is ok, but remember a place like here is more about the atmosphere and the ambiance and the food kind of falls into a distant second place.

Still, this is a cool place to gather with friends. I ultimately would recommend it. Go there looking forward to the company of friends and a cool view and you will enjoy the meal.

Often time the crust of a pizza will either make or break that pizza place. Pizzeria Vetri has their crust down to both a science and an art and it really makes their pizza shine. 

Yes, it is a little bit more than what you might be used to paying, but their pizza not only uses top quality ingredients, but the taste of their pizza is top notch, as well.

You can't go wrong with any of their pizzas. I would definitely recommend here when you are looking for a great pizza.

Complete and utter disappointment. Portions of food were extremely small. Waaaay over priced. Spent over $50 in three dishes, all of which were under seasoned, lacked flavor, and lacked actual effort. 
They did put an effort into up charging me on multiple occasions. They up charged me for extra garlic? A whole dollar
They also up charged me for extra charges me for putting vegetables in my food, and serving me food with one piece of broccoli and one piece of cabbage. 
Oh, and I don't paid for poultry and meat in the food. I had three pieces of chicken in one dish. The chicken was bland, chewy, and tasted old
Overall, I highly regret ever stepping foot in this place. I hope you all head my warning

I hate to do this. But complete and utter unprofessional behavior as a business owner. You reach out and banish me from your establishment, as if I was gonna step foot in that over priced instant noodle house. You should be ashamed of your behavior, to reach out to me like that. Rather than try and reach out and tame the situation. You've been here for 4 years, I've lived here for 18 years. Never once thought to try your place because it didn't seem interesting. Sure enough we came across a Thai craving... 

We ordered takeout and you didn't voluntarily place utensils there? Really...you ask people at takeout after the bag is tied if they want utensils. You've been in business for 4 years and don't know how to split a check with $20 in cash and the remainder on two checks? 


Oh and to slander Chinese food for being delicious and affordable? Really... I've had delicious and affordable Thai food as well. You just have the blessing of being in a very busy part of town. Preach good business, not anarchy. You didn't enjoy your salon visit because it sucked, well I'm telling you my experience at your place sucked!

Tell ya what, here's the deal: for the low price of one dollar, I'll drop a steaming pile of half-digested Chinese buffet on a roll and top it off with a stream of hot whiz--not the cheese kind. Hell, I'll even encourage you to speak whatever language you wish. Then I will kick you in the junk until you vomit it all up. As terrible as this might sound, I guarantee you will be more satisfied with my offer than what you'll get at Geno's. 
 
Although, I suppose if you enjoy being surrounded by mindless masses whose insipidity is surpassed only by the overpriced garbage they're shoveling into their mouths, Geno's is paradise.

I think the fact that most of the reviews by Philadelphians average a generous 1.5 stars speaks volumes about this appalling place. Oh, and don't be confused to think that this is any kind of endorsement for that other hellhole Pat's across the street.

I've never written a review on yelp but I made this account just to write about my awful experience at the Clover Grill. My girlfriend and I stopped in last night in order to get something cheap and simple before engaging in a night of drinking on Bourbon Street. The place was not crowded and we sat at the counter. 

There was a guy cooking and another guy at the counter who was the "waiter" and "host." He saw us walk in and sit down but didn't say anything. We looked at the menu and waited for 20 minutes for him to stop talking to some people at the front who he was having a long conversation with. He then walked past us and started taking the order of another couple who had just walked in. He looked at me and sneered "I'll get to you eventually." He then began wiping down tables without even apologizing or asking if we wanted drinks. What the hell? All we did was sit there quietly and politely and this stupid hipster "waiter" blatantly told us he was going to ignore us. I've been to plenty of places where the service is slow, but never once did a waiter so obnoxiously ignore me. Over 25 minutes with no drink order? Seriously? He seemed to not understand basic human hospitality.

So we left and I can't review their disgusting food that was a frozen hamburger patty being thrown on an unclean grill. I should also note that the guy cooking wasn't wearing gloves and never washed his hands. He was touching raw meat and then making deli style sandwiches, which is cross contamination and something that anyone who has ever had a food service job should know. I suspect that the five star reviews on here are people who were "lucky" enough to be served and/or are unaware of food safety regulations.

Jumbo burrito ftw! With a name like this(that I can't even pronounce), can't go more authentic than this! 

Order online first for easy pick up!

Cake was delicious apparently, but if you want good customer service look elsewhere. I ordered a cake from Japan for a birthday in the States.  They admittedly left a word off the cake, said the person who picked the cake up (not the person who paid) didn't mind, proceeded to email me saying how everyone thinks it is a beautiful cake and then exploited the cake on social media after I told them I would do this when I wasn't given a ten percent refund on the order.  For 80 bucks the cake should be made well and if you need to ask a customer if it needs redoing, you should have redone it earlier.  I wouldn't trust this company as far as I could throw their cake. Direct from my email from them are these words, and as a consumer upset about an order, well these words could make your blood boil: We think the cake looks great and will be adding to our album! We received many compliments in store on the cake as well!

As you can tell from their comment below they are defensive and desperate to look good rather than admitting that from a design perspective the cake didn't look good. Also. The 80 dollar cake fed thirty not fifty people as they claimed.  I was told 30 on the phone and it was in fact 30 at the party.  We'll let the internet be the judge. I'm sure people who aren't detail oriented won't see an issue.

The NE Ale House has only been open for a short time so I guess they are experiencing growing pains. This establishment is within walking distance from my home so I was really looking forward to the grand opening as it is nice to be able to drink and not be concerned about driving. 

They did a good job in the renovation of the Old Schoolhouse. They added a nice deck for outdoor dining. The interior is a typical sports bar scene with many TV's and sports memorabilia. Unfortunately that is not my scene. I highly recommend it for people suffering from ADD who cannot focus on having a conversation with their dinner partners and who need to be distracted by a dozen TV's blaring with different shows running simultaneously. Seriously, in order to be heard you have to literally SCREAM at your dining companion. The acoustics are terrible. It is sooooo noisy! !!!
If that's your idea of a nice dinner, than go for it!

Oh yes, the food.... nothing to write home about and overpriced! Apathetic service. A ridiculously early happy hour (3-5pm Really?) My beer loving partner did comment that they had a good selection of beers. Unfortunately I am a wine gal. The wine list was common and low end, yet they have the audacity to charge $8 and more per glass. 

We really tried to like this place. We have come here several times to try different items to give it a chance ONLY because we wanted to like  a place that we could walk to. The build your own burger was $12.00 (YIKES!) The first time we had it we were very disappointed because it was a stingy meat portion. Since then they have hired a new chef and added a $5.00 Monday burger special which is much better but you have to order it as is and it has a lot of unnecessary ingredients.The chili was awful,salads boring and the seafood is bland. I hope the new chef makes some more improvements because it isn't worth the price. Especially when you can spend the same amount at Casa Ludovico up the street and enjoy a proper fine dining experience!

Bacon, Bacon and more Bacon. Ordered several menu items, however, the Heart Stopping BLT was the star. Thick cut bacon, along with a thick slice of fresh tomato and crisp head lettuce....AMAZING. We waited outside in line for more than an hour, but it was worth the wait. The Malts and Shakes are hand-dipped and were decadent. It's a little cramped inside for group seating. But the 5 of us squeezed in a little table and enjoyed every bite. This local hideaway was also featured on the Food Network for "Old School Soda Fountains".  Service was okay, but the food, decor and overall experience earned it 4 Stars.

Portillo's, originally called The Dog House, started out in a 12 foot trailer in 1963 on a bustling corner in Villa Park, Illinois. This quintessential Chicago staple, now serving in Indiana, Arizona, Minnesota, Wisconsin, Florida & California, is an uber efficient American restaurant chain that specializes in serving Chicago-style food such as Hot Dogs, Maxwell Street Polish, Italian Beef, Burgers, Salads and the iconic Chocolate Cake Shake. Here's the rundown on the Italian Beef-this juicy monster of a sandwich, known as "Chicago's #1 Beef" is about the size of an average man's head, and there is absolutely no shame in devouring every last bite. I suggest adding some zesty giardiniera & melted Mozzarella cheese...or in Portillo's terms...."hot with mozz". The Hot Dog with "Everything" includes yellow mustard, neon green relish, celery salt, freshly chopped onions, sliced red ripened tomatoes, a hefty kosher pickle spear and hot sport peppers piled high into a perfectly steamed poppy seed bun. And what could be better than a huge slice of decadent, rich chocolate fudge layer cake smothered in even chocolatier fudge frosting....blending that hunk of chocolatey goodness with creamy vanilla ice cream and calling it a shake... that's what. Doing it Chicago style.

Downtown Riverwalk views, on-site brewery, a patio with cozy outdoor fire pits, a trendy rooftop lounge and a Barbacoa grill....how spectacular is that? This open and airy rustic hot spot is housed in the renovated City Water Works building and serves up Native inspired seasonal food & spirits. It celebrates the vibrant fusion of flavors from the local Florida waters and land that once was home to many Native Americans. I met a friend for cocktails and hors d'oeuvres at the Community table inside and Ulele delivered. The portions were huge, the service was impeccable and the cocktails were hand crafted. The elegant Lobster Claw Cocktail was chilled and served in a martini glass with spicy horseradish sauce. Pulpo (Octopus) Carpaccio came thinly sliced & dressed with a piquant piri piri sauce. Ulele Pale Lager Beer was the base for the cheese sauce blanketing the decadent Crab Macaroni & Cheese. Crispy Okra Fries were tossed in lime and ready for dipping in a homemade ketchup. And local Gulf Coast Barbacoa Charbroiled Oysters were grilled to a smoky perfection. So, all of you foodies...pay homage to the city's past and explore this upscale menu.

Updating from 4 - 4.5 stars because this place is awesome. 

Have since tried more dishes and wanted to share, along with a pic of what continues to be my favorite and go-to dish - the beef tenderloin (grass fed) w/ risotto and asparagus (SEE PIC) - 5/5. Not on menu but can be requested. 

The tenderloin is always nicely crisped on the outside and delicious. The risotto is also delish. I do wish there was more asparagus though and always forget to ask for sauce on the side, which the dish really doesn't need, in my opinion. 

Also tried the eggplant parm, their homemade ciabatta bread and mussles in a white wine based broth. SEE PICS. 
- EGGPLANT PARM - 5/5 - Wow, I am impressed (not easy, in food or in life). The eggplant was perfectly crisped, sort of like it was breaded and fried like a chicken cutlet. The cheese was sandwiched between two thick slices of eggplant and topped with sauce. YUM. 
- HOMEMADE BREAD - 4.5/5- Crispy on the outside and soft on the inside, this ciabata that would be delicious w butter or to dunk in sauce or broth. Impressive for Florida (due to the water). 
- MUSSLES - 3.5/5 - Tasty mussles and broth was tasty but not close to my top (I've had some amazzing mussles). They also strangely replaced shallots with green onion, which impacted the taste.

This review is based on a 5 minute experience attempting to eat at this establishment.  Of the 95 reviews I've written, this is the 2nd 1 star, by far the worst, and hopefully the last.  

I just got back from a 4 day wellness retreat last night so was blissfully calm and relaxed. So much so that I walked into this place thinking it was City's Bistro, which is 1 block further down central!  Whoops. Had ordered from City's on Yelp so hadn't been inside either storefront and confused the two. 

Nonetheless, I sat outside and a friendly gentleman sat me and offered me a water. I then noticed that the sidewalk was sloped to the point that I was very uncomfortable so I told him why I wanted to move and check out the inside.  I sat at a booth and heard him tell the waitress bringing my water outside that I had moved. She was visibly annoyed, even taking a prayer like moment with her eyes closed to what seemed like center herself before bringing my water over. She looked very annoyed and smacked the water down but I  took it with a grain of salt as I can understand how that could be annoying!  

Another waitress walked over to show me the menu and I told her that I needed a moment to decide if I was going to stay as I noticed staff weren't wearing masks and place was busy so wasn't sure if I wanted to stay.  I didn't intend to eat indoors so needed a moment to assess. Ultimately, I told the 2nd waitress I was going to leave and apologized. Left a $1 on the table for the water they had brought me. 

In hindsight, I could have done this before sitting down but I do not think this 4 minute exchange warranted the extreme response that came next. 

As I was walking out, waitress #1 yelled angrily "THANKS, NOW THAT YOU'VE TOUCHED EVERYTHING".  I popped back in and said you're welcome and I did not touch anything actually. She began walking away screaming about me touching everything. At this point, the zen left my body and I yelled back that I had not touched a thing, that I even left a $1 for the 5 minute inconvenience and if she was so concerned with my touching things, why wasn't she wearing a mask. She then yelled at the top of her lungs that she didn't have to wear a mask, obviously missing the point I was trying to raise. I was shocked by this outburst and tried explaining myself to the gentleman I first encountered as she continued to scream.  

His response was basically that I can choose to eat there or not but didn't seem surprised, shocked or embarrassed by her outburst (perhaps a bit proud) which was very telling to me about the culture of the establishment.  Just from a basic human decency perspective, that attack was quite vicious and while I try to remind myself that we are all fighting our own battles, what surprised me most was that none of the other staff seemed rattled or apologetic. I did ask the gentleman I first encountered for her name which he declined to give me (which I never would have mentioned here btw) but wow what a horrific ordeal for myself and probably the other diners that all stopped and watched the scene unfold. 

It wasn't until I left and walked down the block a bit that I realized that I walked into Central Coffee Shop and not City's Bistro!!!  I ended up walking to City Bistro when the owner greeted me and asked me how I was to which I just broke down crying!  I didn't mention the name of the establishment I had this horrific experience at and she didn't ask, she was just kind and comforting, which is exactly what I needed in that moment. 

Moral of the story - I won't be back.

Review is based on 1 delivery experience.  2.5 overall.  

I'm really trying not to be too hard on this place as I'm an Italian American New Yorker, so rounded up rather than down, to make rating relative to what else is available locally. 

KEY TAKEAWAYS: 

- Delivery - I really appreciate how they take time to pack food for delivery with a lot of care, so food travels well. 

- Garlic Knots - 3/5 - Decent garlic knots with lots of oil, grated cheese, and garlic, and comes with sauce on the side. 4 huge knots for $4.50 - would get these again. 

- Meatball parm hero - 2.5/5 - Generous portion with a good amount of sauce (some places make these way too dry).  Meatball tasted ok. For the price of $8.99, a good value but Probably wouldn't get again. 

- Sicilian pizza - 1/5. Crust was soft, cheese was sliping off, extra salty. Just not good. I haven't been home to nyc much in the past 1.5 yrs due to COVID and have been dying for a sicilian slice. Got a small pie from here and ... yea... it was not tasty. I do have high standards when it comes to pizza, but I just couldn't eat it and had to trash it. For context, I've yet to find a really good sicilian slice in Tampa Bay.

- Price - Large quantities for the price.

This NYers go-to for bagels in Tampa Bay! 

KEY TAKEAWAYS - 

- BEST BAGELS I've had in Tampa Bay!  Various options including whole wheat everything. Great/affordable bagel w/ lox and cc (generous w/ the lox, which is always fresh).  I typically get my lox, capers, onions and scallion cream cheese on a sesame bagel.  This weekend I just got scallion cc - SEE PIC. 

- DELISH DONUTS - Assortment of yummy donuts. 2 standouts. The Créme brûlée donut is to die for - a thin caramelized layer of goodness on top and a custard-y filling - filling is not overwhelming and could eat around it if you are not a fan of filling. SEE PIC. The cronut dunked in tea or coffee is also a must try- just melts! 

- SERVICE is fast an efficient - a rarity in Florida and makes me so happy!!!  Have seen many of the same faces for years, always hardworking!  
 
- ORDER AHEAD - To avoid long lines, call ahead to place and pay for order - this way you skip whole line. If you just place your order ahead, will still need to wait on ordering line to pay. 

- TOASTY - If you like bagels toasted, you may need to ask them to double or triple toast, their standard is barely toasted - probably because they are turning out so many bagels/day. 

- DELIVERY available via Uber Eats.

- COVID - No seating indoors at the moment, all staff wearing masks (cannot recall if required but patrons all seem to be wearing as well). Still a few 2-4 seater tables outside.

Love this diner on Dale Mabry, where the gyros are slammin and staff welcoming.  Great for a quick bite at a real diner, closest to a NY/NJ diner I've come across in Tampa Bay. 

Close to Steinbrenner field, signed photos of Yankee players cover the walls of this charming diner. 

Helen a greek american from Queens, hubby George opened w/ his parents in the 80s, yankees used to come in all the time in the 90s. So much history. 

KEY TAKEAWAYS:

- FOOD - While everything looks good, I get the same thing every time because it is sooooo good. 

That is the GYRO PLATTER (lamb) w/ Greek Salad (8.95). I'm super picky with gyro and greek salad because I've had so many authentic ones living in ny and trips to Greece but this place does it well!  They have a rotating spit in the back (lamb only, chicken is not made on a spit).  The tzaziki is delightfully garlicky and feta moist and delicious. 

Compared to locally available options 4.5/5, compared to nyc 4/5, compared to Greece 3/5. 

Homemade stuff includes roast beef, daily specials, etc.  

- AWESOME SERVICE - This is the kind of place where the owners are always present, knowing customers by name and come over to chat. Also seem to retain staff as I've seen many of the same faces for years. 

Servers and owners are really delightful.  I even had an issue getting cash from their ATM which involved many calls to my bank and fraud alerts. The owner was so understanding about it and basically made me a tab, even though I said I wouldn't be back for months until my next car servicing. When I returned months later with the cash they were so lovely.  Really such a warm and inviting local place with great folks.

- CASH ONLY - They have an ATM inside.

- INDOOR SEATING ONLY - During peak of covid, they did seat every other booth but back to full capacity, as many places are. 

- ALL DAY MENU - Yes I do eat my gyro platter at 9am.

This review is based on 1 take-out order. 

ORDERING PROCESS- 2/5- I do not like that there is no option to place an order over the phone. You must order/pay/create an online account to do so. I honestly wouldn't have ever tried this place if I didn't already offer to bring lunch over to a friend's who had just had a baby, as this was the restaurant she chose. This is a big turnoff for me as I do not want to wait in line and then for food to be prepared onsite or order online, especially from a place that I haven't been, as I like to ask questions.  This approach may deter other first timers. 

WAIT TIMES- 5/5 (Pickup orders) Food does seem to be available quickly. My eta was 5 mins (impressive). Showed up in 15 mins and food was ready and waiting. HUGE PLUS. 

FOOD-
-- BUILD YOUR OWN BOWL - 3/5 - Farro base w winter veggies, broccoli, and butternut squash w/ lentils and feta, salmon garlic aioli - $16.  Salmon was cooked well and a good size and others were ok but not incredibly flavorful. Think I might try another sauce next time as the garlic aioli (not very garlic-y) was ok but not something I would get again. Overall, an ok meal that would work in a pinch, given that wait times are short. 
-- MAC AND CHEESE - 4/5 - Tasty with a good amount of cheese and a bit of a crunch from breadcrumbs? sprinkled on top. Pasta was not overcooked. 

SOURCING - Mostly sourced from local farms, which I respect. It is unclear which veggies are organic as they indicate that they try to get organic but don't always. Salmon seems to be farm raised and chicken free range. I would be more inclined to eat here more if all organic/wild. Great concept though!

See sourcing page for more info:

https://www.eatnakedfarmer.com/sourcing/

Brick & Mortar, how I love thee!  How have I gone 2 years since my last visit?  

Everything I love in a restaurant:

- Quality food perfectly executed, 
- Upscale without being overstated, 
- Great wine selection,
- Nice outdoor seating, 
- Fairly priced and 
- Consistent.

KEY TAKEAWAYS:

- OCTOPUS APP - Get it!  I do every time, and I am never disappointed.  It is the best octopus I've ever had. Seared to perfection and accompanied with a number of sides with flavors that blend together perfectly. SEE PIC. 5/5

- BURGER AND TRUFFLE FRIES - Best burger in St. Pete (since Locale closed)!!  Juicy and delicious burger with the combo of the white cheddar, bacon onion jam and garlic aioli making this perfection!  SEE PIC. 5/5

Truffle fries available for an up-charge or on their own. Good amount of truffle oil and they load parm on top of the fries - delicious!  SEE PIC. 5/5

- NO RESERVATIONS - This is the only downside and reason I don't eat here weekly.

South is one of the most distinctive venues I've been to in a while. Memorable- the design French provincial meets modern urban kitchen, complete with rugged white washed wood, an open lounge in the front, and an atrium ceiling in the middle of the restaurant.

The food was delicious, my shrimp and grits were perfect! The shrimp were sweet and fresh, the texture of the grits weren't too heavy or runny. The fried green tomatoes topped with gulf shrimp were the best fried green tomatoes I've ever had, could be a complete lunch or meal within itself. The blue crab toast was yummy, a crab salad (like tuna salad) on top of toast.  

The drinks were pretty good; crowd pleasers Strawberry Cucumber lemonade and the bourbon punch were cool and refreshing. A little disappointed with my lemon blueberry cake desert, just seemed store bought (not that moist) with added embellishments (jam and lemon curd). 

Jazz Lounge:
 
We saw there was a sound proof lounge with people having dinner and drinks on the other side of the restaurant  and this gorgeous diva of a woman was givin' Billie Holiday minus the white orchid on the side of her head. We immediately knew we needed to check her out!

Turns out Lauren Talese was doing a full set every hour and a half, so we were able to pay just $10 to gain entrance to her next show at 10pm. No cash accepted. So we had to get to the Ticketfly.com website by cell phone and order our seats.  

It's 10:00pm: 

Lauren hits the stage and my heart dropped! The voice of an angel; soft and sweet. She is a natural story teller and is not afraid to talk about the broken dreams that have come with heartbreak, belting out some well-known jazz standards as well as her own written pieces. She used to sing back up for Bilal and she did her rendition of Love Poems with that light airy voice, it was amazing. All of this a pleasant surprise. She performs at South on a fairly regular basis. Made my night, because we had plans to go elsewhere after dinner. The staff was awesome, the evening was laid back and the ambience is one that I will remember for quite some time. 

When in Philly HEAD SOUTH!

We climbed the 72 stone steps at the entrance of the Philadelphia Museum of Art, also known as the "Rocky Steps", well unlike Rocky I was not dancing around with my arms stretched to the sky like a champ, I was found leaning to the side catching my breath before entering the museum. 

The Creative Africa exhibit was $10, if you want to tour the entire museum it's $20, definitely have to make that clear when you get to the desk, because they will ring you up for $20 *side eye*.

The exhibit is located in the Perelman building, which we took a shuttle to from in back of the main museum. The Perelman has a modern art deco design all white with an atrium in the middle of the foyer. The staff is extremely kind and very helpful. It is known for having one of the finest collections of art books and periodicals in the region.

The exhibit included contemporary photography, fashion, and architecture centuries-old sculptures. 5 separate exhibits in one building. Vlisco: African Fashion on a Global Stage, The Architecture of Francis Kéré: Building for Community, Threads of Tradition, Art Splash, and Dancer Nora Chipaumire

Since I love Fashion and that's what we came for, here it is:  

Dutch company Vlisco (pronounced V-lisco) became one of the most well- known textile brands in West and Central African fashion. This exhibition explores the company's most popular designs, the creative process of making new textiles, and a host of absolutely gorgeous contemporary fashion that women and men are walking the runways in Africa and Europe right now.

Also on display, traditional African textiles with a movie that showed the complex and intricate techniques used to create them, including the process and history behind Kente Cloth, which is worn as a sign of wealth and prestige. 

After seeing this exhibition, I had to compose my attitude as of lately on the streets of DC I have seen this large influx of people wearing fake African textiles (sold on the street). I know everyone cannot afford the real stuff, afterall its the sentiment that counts. I get all that, but, one look at this exhibit and taking in the actual work that is put into African clothing that will basically last forever, will make anyone think twice before they purchase an imitation. The value is in the intense labor and  the spirit behind it. Authentic African Clothing is expensive, but seeing this exhibit is just a confirmation as to why it is sooooo worth it!  

Creative Africa will be available at the Perelman building until January 22, 2017.

City House food is really, really good. Last night was no exception, but several things happened that, combined, make me doubt if I can go there again.

City House has a policy of "family style" food for ten or more people. When I asked over the phone prior to our meal what this meant, I could not get a straight answer. After several calls, I was told don't worry, everyone loves it and everyone will have what they want, just in larger portions. Eventually I nailed someone down to say a limit of 3 appetizers, mix of pizzas and pastas, and 4 entrees--"but everyone can have what they want."

Things started to go awry once we were seated--late.

1. They should have been clearer about what family-style meant. 
- I had such a hard time getting a clear answer on the phone, but the server had no problems concisely explaining it to the table--and the answer was different. They were pushing to get a chef's tasting (that's fine, sounded like an exciting idea) even though we could choose our own: 2 appetizers, 2 pizzas, don't bother with pasta, and 3 entrees. The numbers were different, and the general attitude was it was now more about the kitchen than us getting what we wanted.

2. They weren't accommodating.
- When I made the reservation, I explained that a friend would be late. I was told that they would find a way to keep her food warm. When I brought this up to the server, she (rather snidely) said they didn't have a microwave (which wasn't what I was asking) and that my friend would just have to deal and miss out. I dropped the issue.

- I asked if we could do individual serving instead of family-style because we were 9. Nope, couldn't do it even though the 10th wasn't there and would miss out on half the food. I dropped the issue.

- My friend can't process corn, and we wanted a dish that had corn. Nope, they can't take anything out of their food. I dropped it and ordered a different pasta.

3. My glass of wine had a noticeably smaller pour. I put my fresh glass next to someone who'd been drinking from hers for a while, and mine had less. Didn't want to make a fuss, so I didn't bring it up with the server.

4. (THE BIG ONE) When we asked for our check, our server told the table to "not be angry with her and take it out on the tips." The table was flummoxed, and I was so embarrassed because I had been the go-to person. 

Your restaurant has rules and can't modify their menus? The inflexibility is a pain but understandable. I'm a rule follower. I did not complain, debate, etc. I asked questions once and politely accepted all of the negative answers.

Furthermore, I was on the receiving end of a slightly bullying and condescending server all evening.  To actually say that to the entire table was not only unprofessional but also rude and petty, particularly because, as a group, we immediately get charged 20% gratuity anyway. So why say it? We did not complain about her attitude throughout the dinner because we wanted to keep things convivial. It left a sour note for an evening that already had so many bumps. 

I honestly don't think my feedback will make a difference because City House food is stellar and that is reason enough to go. I realize there are two sides to every story, and she must have her reasons too, but restaurants and their staff shouldn't treat people like that.

I typically only write positive reviews on Yelp, but I will do my best to be completely fair with this review. I had heard about this place from some friends, and then I went onto yelp and read some great reviews. I don't care about ambiance as much as good food and that was all I wanted when we went last night. 

The place was packed and I always take that as a good sign, and we were seated on the patio. To make a long story short the Service left much to be desired. They were obviously busy but we had to wait for over 30 minutes to get a waiter. I had to ask what the specials were because we were never told. Honestly, the best part of Service was the gentleman filling our water glasses and giving us bread. He had a great attitude. 

The appetizer we had was the garlic shrimp and we were off to a great start. It was really good. After that it was really down hill. We had a simple burger (every solid restaurant should be able to make a decent burger), talapia, and Portabella mushrooms. I really hate to say this but it was all very bland. The presentation was great but the taste did not deliver. My wife's french fries were cold and hard,  and my mash potatoes tasted really bad. I can cook both of these things better at home by myself...I am serious. A 2 star review on Yelp means (Meh. I've experienced better) and that about sums it up. 

The waitress did give us a free piece of cheesecake which I really appreciate. She did say that kitchen was having issues that night. I appreciate that but between the 2 and 1/2 hours we were there and bad service and food it did not redeem the night. 
I think the restaurant may have been having an off night that night.  If I come back and have a good experience I will re-write this review to reflect that. Consistency for any place of business is where the rubber hits the road.
