- Watermelon with tomato and feta salad - Weird combo, tomato does NOT go with the watermelons. Where's the feta cheese? Cucumbers and butternut squash and aragula would have paired better. 

- Tomato spinach, and radish flatbread - Not bad, but not the best. Okay - looks a bit more appetizing than it sounds. 

- Cornbread: A bit too sweet, could only take a few bites.

We came here after Death & Taxes since it's pretty close, we didn't want to move our vehicles and wanted some food to soak up all the alcohol. We all wanted to sit outside and they have a nice outside seating area that fit all 7 of us. After taking a look at the menu we all decided to start with some starters and picked Brasserie Poutine with pork gravy and Crab & Artichoke Skillet. I then ordered my entree which was the Brasserie Braise. 

Brasserie Poutine- This dish was invented in Canada and it consists of fries, cheese curds and your choice of gravy which we picked pork. It was a nice light starter and the pork gravy was on point. 

Crab & Artichoke Skillet- This was the highlight starter for me! It came out piping hot and the toasted baguettes matched perfectly with the crab and artichoke dip. It was very flavorful and satisfying. 

Brasserie Braise- This dish looked amazing when it came out but was okay on my palate. This dish has short ribs & oxtail which is braised in dark ale and has some vegetables like carrots and finished with creamed polenta. The meat was really tender either and didn't fall off the bone like I'd expect. Like I said this dish was just okay.

I came here over the weekend right before the dinner rush at about 5pm. It was pretty empty when we arrived and plenty of parking and open tables. We were greeted once entering the restaurant and seated as well. For a Korean bbq joint this place is very clean and it doesn't have that meat lingering smell like some Korean bbq places do. Now let's get to the food...

Me and my girl both order the dinner ayce (all you can eat) which was a decent price. We started off with the spicy pork belly and the miso pork belly. Honestly the spicy pork belly was well seasoned but the miso didn't really have a taste. Next was a round of seafood which consisted of shrimp, octopus and calamari. Out of those three the calamari was our favorite. Very tender and well seasoned. I'll definitely recommend the calamari if you're into that! Last but not least was a round of beef. The highlight was the boneless beef short ribs. Soooo good! I ordered about 3 more times of that because the portions here are small which is a good thing. Helps you not waste food and also gives you the opportunity to try different things. Shout out to our waitress, she's was amazing and was A1 the whole light! This Korean bbq place had the best customer service out of any ayce Korean bbq I've been too! That says a lot! So if you're around Sparks be sure to give them a try and don't
forget to try the boneless beef short rice. You won't be disappointed!

Me and my old lady decided to try this breakfast joint out over the weekend on Saturday. The parking lot was full so I parked across the street at home depot. TIP*** Put your name down once you arrive if there's a wait and once you see people leave the bar tell the host and you'll be able to be seated promptly because most people are waiting for a table or booth. Now lets talk about the food...

The Whole Hog- This breakfast meal consists of 1 ham steak, 2 pieces of bacon, 2 sausages and 3 eggs with hash browns. The hash browns were cooked to my liking and I enjoyed the cherry wood smoked bacon as well. The portions are huge here so come hungry. 

Tuna Melt- The tuna melt with bacon was on point! The tuna had lots of celery which I don't enjoy but my old lady loved it. The bacon with the tuna melt went together perfectly. 

I highly recommend this breakfast spot but be ready to wait for at least 15 min over the weekend. This place get very busy!

So I decided I wanted some pho over the snowy weekend and wanted to check out a new and upcoming restaurant. This spot appeared so I decided to give this joint a try. I'm glad I did because the food and costumer service was on point. Upon arriving at restaurant, they still have it's Grand Opening signage on the building. Now, lets get to the food. 

First and foremost, at all pho places I always order their spring rolls. I love the presentation at this restaurant and I always like how their sauce is warm as well. When the sauce is warm it goes perfectly with the fresh roll. 

Spicy Beef- The spicy beef here was on point! The bowl was huge and it had a lot of tender beef. The loved the lemon grass flavor it has as well. 

Roasted Duck- The roasted duck with the chicken broth was delicious in the cold weather. The chicken broth worked very well with the roasted duck. The roasted duck was perfect especially with the crispy skin. YUMMY! 

I'd recommend this spot if you're feeling some pho or a place to eat some great asian food and wanting to stay warm. So give this new restaurant a try.

This is my favorite breakfast spot in Sparks, NV! This is my second time coming here and even though there's always a wait, it's never longer then 15 min for 2 people. Well that's been my case both times lol. Right now there's construction going on next to the parking lot so know that some of the entrances into the parking lot are blocked. Now let's gets down to the food. 

Carne Asada- This is my go to here at this spot. It comes with steak, beans, your choice of either corn or flour tortilla, sour cream, guacamole, has brown and 2 eggs to order. It's a huge amount of food for a great price. The steak was seasoned well and everything came out perfectly. The corn tortillas were piping hot which I enjoy my tortillas to be hot and it went perfectly with the meal. 

If you're in the area be sure to stop by this breakfast and lunch spot! You won't be disappointed, trust me...

I came here on a Tuesday evening with a group of 7 people and parking was hard to find due to the construction in Midtown but that didn't stop us from having a great time here. The bar has some of the best craft cocktail's around and tons of whisky which I enjoy. The ambiance is dark and classy and they have leather couches for you to sit in while you sip and talk story to people. 

I really love the names of the drinks and ordered Death & Taxes Old Fashioned which consists of buffalo trace, banana sugar, orange and bitters. I'm a sucker for any cocktails with bourbon whisky in it. Then I ordered Death & Taxes Manhattan which is Blanton's death & taxes barrel select, carpano antica and house bitters. Man o man this drink was on point. I really enjoy Blanton's bourbon whisky. It's amazing and very smooth. 

No matter what you order, I'm sure you'll enjoy your drink. Be sure to give this place a try if you're every in Midtown and want a a nice craft cocktail made by some knowledgeable mixologist's.

This is something of a destination must attend place if you are in the area. 
The famous and those who want to be famous are always stopping here! 
 This place is famous for their biscuits, jam and ham. The line starts before they are open!

It is easy to find right off main drag.  To park, you may have to wind through the parking lots if you aren't early.  Get there 30 plus minutes before you open and get in line.  Once we had our name on the list, we had time to wander through the various touristy stores they have and I even bought a t-shirt that has bacon scent made into the fabric!

It is an old style cafe so tables are close and small. The menu for breakfast absolutely sounded like something my Southern Ancestors ate for breakfast (even my grandparents).  I went with the ham, eggs and fried potatoes.

Plenty of biscuits and lots of great jelly!  When my order came out, I was very disappointed in the ham.  It was quite dry, tough and tasted like more salt than meat.  All else was good.  The others at the table absolutely loved their meal so I'm shading up a star due to me ordering a salted ham and expecting something better. 

There is seating outside and the view is pretty nice if the weather and flying insects will let you!  You have to check this one off so go ahead and do it!

Finally, kegs of beer later, I made it to the Budweiser Brewery in St. Louis.  I won't claim it was a religious experience, not this time anyways.  But it did bring tears to my eyes.  Seriously!  (I was walking on a broken hip without crutches.)  

Once our group got up to the counter, we discovered we should have booked the tour online hours earlier, if not days earlier.  No slots left. We opted to hit the gift shop which, not surprising to me, had a lot of cool items I liked and wanted. It had all of the current AB beers from signage, games, apparel, custom labeled beer and stuff only a marketing genius could imagine!.  After all, I've been drinking AB's brews for 50+ish years (don't do the math and trust me).  From church key open to ring pulls to flip tops to all of the beer bottle options (tops and bottle shapes and sizes). 

The web site has all the information you need to book a day of tours.  Plan ahead, don't be like us!   Try to get in the Brewmaster Tour and some of the others.  All I spoke to just finishing their day of tours absolutely were unanimous on what to see and that it was well worth the cost of time and money! A must see and do! (It is also what the ticket seller/guide said.)

How do I give 5 stars to this and not do the tour? The biergarten,  entry way exhibits, the gift store, the road signage, the parking lots, the friendly security guards, the web site and ALL of the information on the web site!  This is not just a tourist attraction. This is capitalism, marketing and consumerism in action!  

I HAVE to go back and you need to plan ahead and go!

I went here today for lunch with some vendors.  The service was exceptional and everything came out on time and perfectly.  We started with the crab and corn fritters.  They were full of crabmeat and the green aioli on the side with a little kick was amazing.  I got the black drum which was one of the best fish dishes I ever had.  Underneath was veggies and 3 side red potatoes.  The other person got the burger.  It was huge and delicious.  the other person got the croquet madam sandwich and was not a fan.  The ham and cheese on the inside were cold and not melted.  The cheese on top was, so she didn't like it at all.  The other person had the shrimp and grits.  Great large portions and very good just a little heavy and rich.  Spice was perfect. Will be back!

This was a new place for me and i always go into new snowball stands with a bit of trepidation.   I had seen the mardi gras colored king cake inspired snowball online and knew i had to try it.  The place itself was clean and we were two of only 4 people in the storefront when we arrived.  

I quickly learned that i had to choose between a king cake flavor or the purple (king cake) green  (??) and gold ( bananas foster) version i saw online. I chose all the colors! And then i was asked if i wanted cheesecake in it. Well who in their right mind would NOT want cheesecake in their snowball if given the opportunity! What was served was as wonderful as the picture in saw.  And the taste was even more than i expected!  The complex flavors of their snowballs was a plesant suprise. The flavor of the king cake truly mixed the cake and the cinnamon without either being overpowering.  And the cheesecake was light and fluffy and a great addition to a snowball. 

I am looking forward to returning soon to try even more options.

One my my personal favorites for years, finally got around to reviewing one of the great restaurants of the Hill neighborhood; straight up five stars.

Probably going to take some heat for this, but you can argue this is one of the best; if not the best restaurant on the Hill. I didn't say best Italian, because Anthonino's is a Greek-Italian fusion, but best restaurant. It's a restaurant that seamlessly melds the most popular aspect of both Greek and Italian cuisine in an expanded restaurant space. Once a proud neighborhood eatery no bigger than a shotgun house, it has been augmented to a spacious attraction of South city; no longer a "dive".

Half of the restaurant is the original space which greets you with its classic charm immediately upon entry, a throwback to the days of old. The rest is an expanded space with chiefly modern qualities but consistently maintains the overall mood of the restaurant; a relaxing feel. 

The first thing you receive is bread with olive oil, you could make a meal out of it if you're not careful, so be careful. With a healthy appetite you'd be cheating yourself without ordering the toasted ravioli, from there literally everything on the menu beckons a five star rating.  Nevertheless this one of the rare restaurant that actually serve Greek dolmathes, hearty and very filling. My personal favorite is the tutti mare with white, Jane packed with scallops, squid, and white fish; I've rarely wavered from this selection. If you want to share however, the pizza also received rave reviews; evidenced by the many surrounding tables that order the same.

I could go on forever, the only thing I miss is the kebobs but I never miss a meal here. Count me in anytime anyone even mentions The Hill neighborhood.

I've been to Grays a number of times, and honestly it has declined in quality of food and service over time.  My husband went there a few months ago and ordered the chicken and waffles and had the unfortunate experience of getting fish and waffles - a truly disgusting combination.  They immediately got him a new meal and gave him a $25 gift certificate to use which was very nice.

So last night I went with two gal pals so we could get some dinner and drinks and use the gift certificate.  Our waiter was, to be quite frank, an ahole.  He saw a table of three women in their 30s/40s and immediately assumed we weren't ready for what Grays had to offer.  He started out by telling us clearly "This is not a Chili's - our drinks are artisinal and hand crafted and take time to make.  You may like this one - it is like a cosmo."  Um, excuse me - that has to be the rudest thing I've ever heard.  He then went on to assume we must be teachers (lawyer, finance, and marketing execs actually).  It was masoginistic, offensive, and honestly between that and the lack luster "artisinal" drinks I will not be returning.

Absolutely love this place and make it a point to go whenever we visit. I use up live in the quarter and this was a special occasion type place. So, when I go back to visit we always makes reservations to eat here. 

It's easy enough to find and a short Uber ride from pretty much anywhere in the quarter. We were greeted right away and seated shortly thereafter. They have an open kitchen so you can see the chef teams at work. 

I had the crab, as I usually do cause it's delicious. Friends loved their meals too. Hubs had a shellfish allergy but they are always very accommodating and willing to cool things separate. Never had an issue. 

Staff is really nice and quick with everything from orders to refills. Our waiter made some great wine and beer recommendations. 

Overall: A
A higher price point but definitely well worth a visit!

We had an excellent experience here! Walking in you feel transported to a pub in western Europe. The wait staff all wear fun kilts and the classic pub bar is in the middle of the restaurant. 

We were greeted and taken to seats right away. Our waitress came over a few minutes later. I opted for the white sangria. He has the waitress' recommended blend of Angry Orchard and Hoegaarden beer. Both were great!

We got the Scotch eggs, which seriously we could have had a plate each and been totally happy. They were awesome! Main meals were bangers and mash and Shepard's pie. I enjoyed the bangers and mash most, but both are a must try. The cookie and ice cream dessert came out warm and perfect for a final shared sweet treat. 

Our waitress was completely on point the entire time and took really good care of us!

Overall: A
Highly recommend this fun pub! Scotch eggs are an absolute must.

After watching sunset on the beach we walked around to find a fun place to sit and snack and drink. We were hoping for a dessert but didn't notice until we were already seated that they have no desserts here. 

They had live music going which was fun and the singer was good. It's self seat so we grabbed one of the only open tables and a waitress came over pretty quickly. 

Since they didn't have dessert we went with chips and guac, and both got rum punch drinks. Guac was very good. Chips were stale drinks were just okay. 

As it often does in Florida, the weather rapidly changed and rain started falling so grabbed our check, met the waitress at the cash register and took off for our hotel. 

Overall: B-
No dessert. Good live music!

Amazing experience and an absolute must try for anyone in the area - local, tourist, or otherwise. We loved everything about or visit here, from the ambiance, to the staff, to the food. Just great. 

We started with the okra - which was probably our least favorite thing as we both felt it was a touch too charcoal flavored, but it was still a fun new thing to try!! I had the fish with cheddar sauce, which was seriously full of flavor and so good. It had mashed potatoes and asparagus as sides. 

Staff was friendly and awesome the whole meal. You could tell that they were genuine people and not just overly polite just for service. We enjoyed talking to them (we had a trainee and her trainer) at various points throughout as they checked on us. 

The place itself is super fun as it use to be the utilities building and many parts of it are still original. They have a long booth along one wall that includes old reclaimed church pews - super fun! There is sports memorabilia throughout the upstairs and downstairs, so be sure to look around and check it all out! 

Overall: A++
Loved this reused building, the food, staff and ambiance. Must try!

Meh. Headed here just for dessert and drinks. The hostess seemed thoroughly unhappy to be there. Our waitress seemed annoyed that all we wanted was drinks and dessert. The sundae we ordered looked nothing like the photo and was just okay. 

The restaurant was mostly empty and it wasn't hard to see why after we went. Considering the happy go lucky party vibe just outside on Bourbon street, it was a harsh contrast inside here. 

Overall: D
Head elsewhere on Bourbon.

A gem of a food find in NOLA! This location is a must-try for any foodie whether you're a local or tourist. We found this place listed on a bunch of food blogs and it obviously had rave reviews on Yelp, so we figured we should give it a go. We Uber over as it's a bit outside the "main quarter" area, but a short drive. We arrived at the doors, and it was a very unassuming location, as are most places in the Quarter. 

We were greeted immediately and luckily didn't have to wait for a seat, which seems to be common in other reviews. Just hit a lucky timing point and arrived later towards when they were closer to close. It's a risk to arrive late though - FYI - cause they may run out of certain sides. 

Of course, we all ordered the fried chicken...cause it's why they are famous! We each got different sides so we could try a variety of things and shared our picks amongst the table. I recommend doing this so you can adventure. The cornbread muffins are amazing - get these. Fried chicken was cooked perfectly. It was still moist on the inside, but had a crispy, crunchy fried crust. There was a touch of spice in the batter, but nothing overwhelming - more flavor than spice. 

The staff was really friendly and things came out fast considering how busy they were. We were checked on regularly and drinks were refilled before we even had to ask. They were on point.

Overall: A
Definite foodie place to try out if you are in the area! YUM!

This is a cute little small and casual place where you can get a good Taiwanese food fix.. The food is here decent and a lot better than most Asian places that I have tried in Reno. 

I always get the Mongolian Beef here, but the other stuff that I tried was the chow fun, crispy pork cutlet, and the fried chicken leg. They were pretty tasty. The milk teas are only decent,  although my cousins mentioned that their smoothies are pretty good... 

[SERVICE HERE THOUGH... ]

I have been here a few times and service decent; wasn't really that great, but it wasn't horrible either. However, my last time there made me never want to come back! My party of four walked in and no one greeted us so we just sat on the counter. We waiting for a while and our server never came. We were never greeted. We were finally able to pull over a server to take our order. My cousin ordered his entrée along with a strawberry smoothie. The server replied "We can't make that for you, we're too busy." Then I ordered my entrée and asked if I could have my vegetables on the side. Once again the server said, "We can't do  that for you, we're too busy." SERIOUSLY?!? Well excuse me, but is this a normal thing? My party got annoyed and decided to have dinner at another place. 

Personally, the food isn't good enough for me to come back or to get a "no we can't serve you." I suggest that they just lie to us and tell us that their blender is broken or they are out, instead of telling their customers that they will not make their drinks for them. I mean, seriously?  -_-

2 Stars. (Three Stars for the Food and One Star for the Service averages out to Two Stars)

After a stop for happy hour a few weeks back and seeing the shiny new location, I put a pin in returning for dinner. Thursday night I got together with a pal I hadn't seen in almost two years (thanks pandemic!)
With three floors of dining, my former coworker that still works one day a week over here advised that I request the courtyard or patio room. With impending weather, I chose the patio room with its simple decor and doors that open up to the courtyard's fresh air. 
Randy greeted us and got the feel for the kind of night we had in mind (going out later, headed to a show or just catching up?) We started with Madame Begue cocktails, my new favorite drink, and Randy decanted the wine I had brought in. First course was crab and corn beignets (savory, warm, soft, comforting), and crawfish crepes (delicate, cheesy, punctuated with crawfish tail texture.) Second, we split a wedge salad (I'd order extra cheese and bacon next time), third course was Shrimp n Grits and Angus Tenderloin (well rounded servings, perfectly cooked and seasoned.) We remarked that we prefer smaller menus so that the focus is to get the dishes perfect and to get it right every time. Lastly, we closed with creme brûlée and their award winning grasshopper recipe! Overall a phenomenal dining experience and I look forward to returning to try the pork pasta that looked so, so good that it had already sold out for the evening!

My wife and I have been coming to this wonderful place for more than five years and have always enjoyed our encounters with people from all over the United States and some locals as well...the place is always busy so. We have become used to waiting about an hour before being seated.

Last evening, we were told that our wait  time would be about an hour so we found seats outside and ordered libations which is our custom. An hour went by and we checked the list to determine how much longer we would be waiting. Only three more to go so we continued to wait. A new manager, Jason, came over to us and told us that he would try to get us in. As the second hour went by, I became impatient and inquired again wherein I asked Jason how much longer expressing my displeasure at the extensive wait. His arrogant response to me caused me to round up my wife and granddaughter to go elsewhere. My wife attempted to remediate the problem by holding a conversation with Jason who summarily dismissed her by telling her "we were through here!" 

We went over to Sloppy Joe's across the street where they too were quite busy but most courteous and seated us with high priority since it was now past 8:30PM and sensed that we were famished. Turns out, that Mr. Jason used to work for Sloppy Joe's and his arrogance followed him across the street to his new gig.

We probably won't return to VIP for many a moon as long as Jason resides there...the ownership of VIP will be adversely affected by maintaining his employ and what used to be a five star casual dining experience for us has now been reduced to 1 star for me and mine never to return anytime soon. I choose not to spend my money in a place while being insulted by a twit. For the staff at VIP, this is not an indicator of your performance at all...through the years, you have treated us with dignity and respect and we have enjoyed your company...

To quote Jason one more time, "You win some, you lose some!" Well Jason, you definitely lost some this time...I hope your proud of your performance. This insult to my wife and my family will long be remembered and recorded in the annals of your career history.

I just cannot recommend this restaurant as long as Jason continues there.

Hungry during the late night, no problem this place is a life saver until 3 am . Just remember that take outs only from 230 am to 3am. 
.
The crowd is big during the night. The place was packed on a Monday night. But it's fourth of July so yea not sure how it is if non holiday weekend. There is a lot of seating so no worries. 
.
Parking is on the side of the streets so parking should not be an issue.  Its walkable from harrahs and the major hotels. Which is like a five to ten min walk. 
.
One thing I like is they do make vegetables pho for my wife. She made sure they don't put chicken stock in it so yea it's pure veggie pho. Lots of veggies and tofu in it,  she wasn't complaining or doing a lot of talking while slurping away cuz .one it's good or she was hangry . 
.
On the other hand,  I was basic and got the number one meaning regular beef pho with all the goodies such as random beef parts inside like normally in a menudo. The first thing I taste when the pho came was the broth. The broth is good not filled with lots of msg or overly salty. The beef meat balls we're amazing and tons of tripe in it so I was a happy Camper. I would order this again because pho is a great hangover cure. 
.
Overall the food did take a while since it was very busy inside. I had decent service and coming to fill up our water cups. umm we just walked up and pay when we we're ready instead of waiting. They were nice about tab splitting. This is my to go to spot for asian food late night in little biggest city Reno. 

.

This is much different than any other standard Korean restaurant. Personally, I really think it's out of the box thinking in terms of a Korean restaurant. What they serve at Omoni are really some of the best basics of Korean cuisine. We usually order a dish that requires some cooking in the back so something is fresh like the kalbi (short rib) plate or the dolsot bimbimbap (stone bowl). 

I really like that there are so many different veggies that you can choose from. Other places they have fixed veggies for the day or for the dish. There are really so many things to choose from kimchi, radish kimchi, carrots, mung beans, mushrooms, etc. And you can top almost anything with sesame seeds. 

The only thing is I wish there was something like a standard ~3 banchan that came with each entree. I know that you can order whatever banchan right into your entree, but it would be nice to have that kind of separation between entree and banchan. 

I really enjoy this place since it's modern, clean, and delicious! And the staff is always very friendly and knowledgeable.

The first time I went to Santa Barbara in May of 2011 for a mom's weekend away we found this French restaurant, it was so charming and the food was so wonderful I wanted to come back.  This year I went to Santa Barbara for my birthday with my girl friends and this was the first place I wanted to go back to.  The food again was as wonderful as last time, the atmosphere very nice and the four of us had a great time.  I would definitely recommend it to others who are looking for French cuisine at a reasonable price.

This is unfortunately a two-day bad experience.  I am truly disappointed that I have to give such a bad review. My experience certainly deserves 0 stars, but Yelp forces us to give them at least one star for credit.  I truly enjoy the food, but the customer service is atrocious.  

On a Friday, I entered the restaurant at 8:15pm in order to make a carry out order.  Prior to coming in, I called and they said that I could not make a call in order and that I have to do it on Grub Hub or come in and order.  I tried to order on Grub Hub, but it was saying the restaurant was unavailable.  As stated, I decided to go in and place the order.  I walk in the store, and go straight to the cash register to make the order.  There were workers all around, and nobody acknowledged me or the other customers coming in after me at the register.  After about 12 minutes,  somebody finally comes to register and says they were out of shrimp, crab legs, and other items.  I did not make a big deal, but just wished that somebody would have came to the register earlier so I did not waste my time.  The next day I decided to give it a try again.  I ordered through Grub Hub for delivery (which I have done before).  In addition to the full plate that I ordered, I ordered extra side items.  As soon as the Grub Hub delivered my meal, it was missing the side items.  I looked in the box, which I am very familiar with their portion size, and noticed that it was a normal size portion, and that they DID NOT include the extra items in the box.  I have made the same order in the past, and received the extra items as ordered.  I contacted Exotic on the Run immediately, and let them know that I did not receive the extra items.  The lady on the phone had a terrible attitude, and informed me that I needed to call Grub Hub.  I said ok, but she did not realize that she did not hang up the phone after the call, and made some disparaging comments.  I proceeded to call Grub Hub, and they told me that they will contact the restaurant and let them know that they were missing items from the order.  The Grub Hub rep told me that they said they included the items in the box, which they absolutely did not.  They were unwilling to work with me to figure out a resolution. 

Ultimately, I would suggest order at your own risk.

We were here Saturday for a Party. While the customer service were excellent and the planners were excellent the room left ally to be desired.

We stayed in a suite at a pretty reasonable rate. There were 4 of us in the room. Upon arrival the customer service was very good and accommodating. I am happy with the experience in this hotel except for the room. We only stayed one night so it wasn't a huge deal. 

The rooms are very large but extremely outdated. Our sweet was a "throwback" it looked like something out of the early 90s. The couch cushions didn't even match. Again we only slept there so it wasn't the end of the world, it was just surprising. The rooms defiantly need some updating. 

I'm not sure if we would stay here again, I would probably look elsewhere in the area. Again the customer service was great but the rooms leave a lot to be desired. 2 stars for room, 5 stars for service.

We have been wanting to try The Kitchen Consigliere for sometime now. We've tried on a few occasions to get a table without reservations with no luck. Last night we planned ahead and made reservations. 

We had 5:00 reservations but were running late due to traffic. Angie was great! We explained about the traffic and she was more than accommodating. We arrived around 5:15, parking was a bit of an issue. They offer a small lot outback but it was full. We were sat immediately! 

Our server was great! He was attentive and everyone was on top of their game. The bread they provide was simple but beyond fresh and amazing. My wife went with the linguine with crab sauce and I had the chicken parmigiana. The crab sauce was packed with crab meat and had just the right touch of spice. Not sure if the pasta is house made but it was still good. The chicken parmigiana was huge! Very generous portion and it was fantastic. Half of it went home. The cheese to sauce ratio was perfect and it was just tasty. My wife and I left very satisfied. We cannot wait to go back! FYI it's BYOB so bring a cooler. Solid 5 stars all around.

Not a fan of Parx at all. First off is the parking, yes they have an extremely large lot but it's always full. They do offer valet but I hate others driving my car. Second is the smoke, the air filtration stinks! It's always so smoky in there. The casinos is AC seem to have better systems. Thirdly is the people in this joint. At times we felt like we were in a third world country. We're not big fans of casinos as is but this was just icing on the cake. They also charge you a cover to watch live music or you be like others and hover around the slots just outside of the 360 lounge.. stay away 2 stars

Got elote, asada, and adobada tacos from here last night and this will now be my new go-to for authentic street tacos. I'm a salsa snob when it comes to tacos shops and their verde salsa sold me. Just enough tang and kick but not too firefly where you need to guzzle a glass of water. 

The elote was DIVINE. Literally just fell off the cob and wasn't too heavy but just right in ratio of sauce and corn. Also huge portion of meat for street tacos! Worth the $3 price point per taco in my opinion and this is coming from a fellow Californian. I will definitely be ordering here again and looking forward to trying their micheladas some day

As a recent vegan, I was pretty excited to check this spot out. The menu looked great, but when I got my meal I was pretty disappointed. It tasted like hospital/ nursing home food. I made a better version of my meal at home a few days ago (and I'm not even a very good cook). I just hope people don't eat here and think this is what vegan tastes like. 

The dessert was pretty good, but over priced.. So I won't be back for that either (whole foods is less expensive).

Also the ambiance was a little weird. Lots of clearly fake, dark colored flowers, weird random pictures, and pretty awful music. 

Just not quite sure what all the hype is about, or why this place has such good reviews.

I can't believe that I'm not the first person to write a review for this place- they just opened today! Anyway.....
We came here for dinner tonight on opening day and I have to admit that I really was not expecting much because, well, things often go wrong on a first day. We live right around the corner and the moment I saw the stickers for "Pho" go up on the windows I took to passing by often to try and figure out when this place would be opening.
The Hours- 
They are open Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday from 11 AM - 9PM, Friday and Saturday 11 AM - 10 PM and on Sunday from 11 AM - 3 PM. They are closed on Monday. I also believe they are closed from 3-5 every day.
The Decor-
The place is fairly small with about 4 or 5 regular tables that will fit 2 - 4 people, 2-3 high top tables that fit 4 people, and a bar with about 7-10 chairs. The decor is modern and cute with nice colors and simple decor. It feels very cozy and clean, which I like a lot. There is a TV, which I don't like at all. Outside they have several silver tables with comfortable bright colored chairs. These tables will fit 4 to 6 people.
The Food-
Their menu is simple like their decor. They have "sliders" as a starter option which is something a little unusual and tasty. These are 2 steamed buns which are kind of flat like a taco shell (but thicker) and they are filled with meat, cilantro, carrots, cucumber and with a little sauce. They are similar to mini sandwiches and are tasty. They also have the usual fried spring rolls-but at a great price $3 for an order of 2. They also have a nice selection of Fresh Rolls, including the inventive "New Orleans Roll" ($4.00 for 2) which is a fried spring roll wrapped in a fresh roll. My comment upon trying this was "genius!" and my partner's comment was "weird!". I thought the combination was really tasty and I love that now I don't have to decide between the Fresh Rolls and the Spring Rolls! We also tried the Pork Fresh Rolls ($4.00 for 2) and they were divine. I have been a fan of Magasin, but these blew those out of the water! There was a lot of pork in them and the pork had a lovely Lemongrass flavor. The peanut sauce was also perfect. They have other rolls such as Shrimp and Avocado and Tofu as well.
For the main meal I had a Tofu Po Boy Sandwich ($4.00) and my partner had the roasted chicken sandwich. YUM!!! YUM!!! YUM!!! My sandwich was craveably perfect! The bread was fresh and crispy on the outside, soft on the inside just as it should be. The fresh veggies were plentiful and included Carrots, Cilantro, Cucumber and thin slices of hot pepper and the sauce was yummy-savory and sweet at the same time (what is that and how do they make it???!). My partner is quite picky and he devoured his sandwich. He thought it was way better than any others we have tried in the area. I did not take a bite, but I could see that it was shredded chicken and it had been marinated in a soy base of some sort. It was a nice large size and a steal at $4.50. Other items on the menu were the usual Pho Beef and Chicken soups, Bun (vermicelli noodles with fresh veggies and meat on top), rice dishes, a Lemongrass Tofu dish and I'm sure a few items I'm forgetting. I don't believe that they serve any Alcohol. As an update, I have now also had their Vegetarian Tofu Pho and it was delicious and filling with a good amount of veggies and tofu as well as a flavorful broth.
We left there stuffed and only $26 out of pocket including drinks and a tip. In short- recommended!

If you're hankering for pancakes as fluffy as clouds or jonsing for some perfectly cooked eggs, well then Shelly's Cafe is the perfect place. 

Once you walk into this establishment you're greeted by the friendly wait staff. The atmosphere is like going to a good friend's house for brunch. The decor is modern and artistic which is a pleasure to see in a breakfast/lunch place. The mural on the wall and subway tiles transported me to New York while the art on the wall was a nice touch of funky and class. 

Ok on to the food. I can't say enough about it. We ordered the pancake sandwich with ham, American cheese and 2 perfect cooked medium eggs. I was expecting the size of a "Golden Arches" pancake blast sammie, but was pleasantly surprised at the portion. It was huge Tampa, huge! And it tasted as good as it looked! The kiddos had the mini pancakes. One order was good ol buttermilk and the other chocolate chips. As I said in the beginning, I am not sure how they get the pancakes so fluffy with the perfect amount of crispy golden edges, but dayam! I had the off the menu steak and eggs which I saw someone previously order online. The temp was perfect, the taste was right on and the home style potatoes were full of flavor. I usually don't eat them without tons of ketchup but I enjoyed them sans the hienz. We finished off with some beignet bites...don't judge! One word - nawlans! They reminded me of Cafe Du Monde. The coffee was on point as well.  

As you can probably tell, I thoroughly enjoyed my first experience at Shelly's Cafe. If you're in the carrollwood, northdale, USF, Hillsborough county, state of Florida area, stop by. You'll be glad you did!

Only reason I gave a 1 star was because there wasn't an option for 0 stars. If you're looking for a bar/restaurant run by an incompetent unprofessional and slightly creepy owner then Look no farther. Long story short a group of us went here on New Years Eve just after midnight for a couple drinks to end the night. A couple of us got our first round when a guy ran up to us (later found out he is the owner) saying there was a private party that was just finishing up and if we wanted to stay our only option was a $40 all you can drink. He was slightly rude at this point but it's New Years Eve and he was sweating profusely so I gave him a pass. We really weren't trying to get #turntup so this didn't seem like a good deal but we were already there and didn't want to navigate to a new bar, so we started shelling out our 40 bones. 
I thought we were all squared away. 
Nope. 

He came back over and said he "wasn't sure about the $40 dollar deal and we just aren't setup to be a bar".  He seemed like he was having a mild to severe panic attack, so I ignored the stupidity of him saying we aren't setup to be a bar when that is the sole purpose of your place of business. He made it seem like we pulled a fast one on him with the $40 deal when it was his idea. I tried explaining that we had 12 people that had paid, or were about to pay, 40 each and likely only get 1 or 2 drinks(in other words, you're about to make a good amount of money off us) That seemed to get his attention and he left us alone.....temporarily. 

It turns out he has the short term memory of an infant squirrel, because 2 minutes later he was heckling more members of our group about whether we paid. Again we went through the process of explaining we were just following his rules and were happy to work with him if they have changed. During this conversation he kept repeating he was the owner and they aren't setup to be a bar. He had effectively made everyone feel uncomfortable with his attitude and excessive sweating. Then to top off the night he sends over a large patron of the bar, not an employee, to tell us he wanted us to leave and he wasn't setup to be a bar. At this point we were happy to leave and wished we hadn't wasted part of our New Years Eve there.

My advise to this wannabee business owner. If a group of people walk into your bar when you're having a private party, just tell them you're closed. Don't try and make up an all can drink deal, then get insecure that it wasn't a good deal, then heckle said group, then have one of your customers ask them to leave. 

Very strange experience.

They are just as horrible as everyone says.  They are mean, stoned, thuggy, and unaccommodating.  Dirty floors, counters, Folger's coffee is used, small portions, intolerable wait for small, cold food.  Too smoky due to a poor ventilation system, and all around bleh."  M" from company X was right when he says, "I give em a year".

Piss poor food, shady service, waste of time.

Don't ever go here. 
Waited an hour and 15 minutes for food that never came, and when we questioned the manager (owners wife as it turned out) she went to the kitchen, came back a few minutes later and said "it's been 42 minutes since your order was entered into the computer (what that has to do with when we placed our order, I'm not sure), and this is a fine dining establishment, so you should allow two hours". To which I replied "I don't think so". And she said "I'm a Christian and I don't lie". Seriously? You just lost my business forever.

#92 Review for the 2016 Yelp 100 Challenge 


Love my mini getaways.   Whether it's somewhere near the areas of San Diego,  Palm Springs,  Santa Barbara, Las Vegas, or San Francisco,  I am always overwhelmed with joy and feeling loved.  So on our recent getaway to San Barbara, we stumbled upon this place upon arrival with the help of YELP!

So happy we were seated right away.  Already +1star!  A good size restaurant with a full bar  situated within a hotel in downtown SB.  Another +2star!  The open wood beams on the ceilings definitely gave this place a lot of warmth which is very Santa Barbara.  Loved it!

We decided on-

Garlic fries with aioli.  Awesome start.  Seasoned well and with that creamy garlic aiolo?!  We likey! 

We also shared a skirt steak salad, cooked medium well as requested.  Moist and tender.  Perfect.

The yellowtail fish tacos was their fish of the day.   With all the traditional toppings,  the fish was very fresh and moist.  Not overcooked at all.  +4stars.

Our server was super sweet, patient, and attentive.   

Parking was at a parking structure,  which was a nice short walk to the restaurant.  

Definitely will be one of our spots to return again on our next visit.


#always#thankful#iloveSB

I love listening to a live piano playing.  Don't you? It just always sets a romantic mood.  And if that doesn't work,  then you're not with the right company. 

This was one of those weekend getaways that I always use to look forward to.  And he always would find an awesome place to for us to try.   I guess Yelp has a lot to do with that.  Hahaha.

He ordered- 
Ribeye 12 oz medium rare.  Amazing! With creamed butter of course.  Accompanied with aparagus and mashed potatoes.  He was happy.

I had -
The raspberry glazed crusted salmon with coos coos,  garnished with blueberries,  strawberries,  and blackberries on a bed of argula.  Trying to be healthy for once but I did enjoy our sweet potato fries with garlic aioli for dipping.  Both were fantastic!   Perfectly cooked and executed beautifully. 

We paired our meal with Napa's  Educated Guess Cabernet Sauvignon.  A little on the sweet side and I know bae would love it since he prefers a Merlot or a Red Blend.  Whereas Chel likes her Cab on the dry side like Silver Oak.  But it paired well with both entrée.  So we were both happy campers.

Definitely a must try when in Reno.

Noboru is the relatively new all you can eat sushi bar in Montgomeryville, back in the same shopping area as LA Fitness, Texas Roadhouse, Baja Fresh and at the back Costco. 

While I had eaten here right around the time the sushi bar had opened, it had been some time, and I went on a relatively quiet Thursday night. Prices for that night are 21.95 plus drinks. The buffet does serve beer, but I decided to stick with just hot tea and water. 

Other posters had complained about variety of sushi, but I overall thought the selection was acceptable. You had everything from tuna, mackerel, salmon, surf clam, squid, eel, sweet shrimp. I actually thought the maki selection was very poor, compared to other sushi bars. My other complaint about the sushi is it was poorly made, with seawad falling apart, and the sushi overall lacking that beauty that adds to the enjoyment of eating sushi. Frankly I have seen better at the supermarket.

The variety of other things to eat is pretty impressive. Again, comparing to other sushi bars I have eaten at, there are fewer salads and hot entrees, but instead they do have soba noodles, shabu shabu, habacchi and hot pots available. That variety is pretty impressive.  None o the othe salads or entrees I had were memorable. You seemed to have the same types of flavors being glopped onto the dishes.. sesame, spice and shoyu. There is certainly a wider spectrum of flavors that could be added to dishes. My other complaint which is the same at any buffet I have ever eaten at, is the temperature of the food. The hot tables do not keep things hot enough, but are able to dry things out. A chicken gyoza I had resembled a leather football, and I wondered if I would break a tooth eating it.

On a positive note, the service was friendly and attentive. The one thing I would say is they need to tell folks more about how some of the special dishes work such as the soba or shabu shabu. I was stopped by one caucasian diner, asking me whether everything was included. 

For the price Noboru is an acceptable place to catch a quick bite of sushi if you dont want to go to supermarket. It is by no means a substitute for some of the better sushi bars in the area, including Ooka or Blue Fin.

4/5 y'all know it's already good. 

this is another review among the congregation who are already praising this place. so just go. it's far, but just go.

i can't believe it took me about 6 months to finally try this place. if it's your first time, get one of the specials that let you sample the brisket, pulled pork, and ribs. my friend and i couldn't decide which among the three were our favorites, we'd feel one way, take a bite, then feel another...such a horribly delicious dilemma. 

beware, just because it's served in a basket doesn't mean it's a small portion...once you actually start digging in you'll realize there are 2-3 servings in there, so breathe. if they happen to be making the green chile, it's basically more pulled pork as a side. unlike other places where the meat will need the sauce, theirs is scrumptious on its own, and the sauce are enhancers. looking forward to my next visit!

Not sure what's happening with this restaurant. I used to visit a lot with some friends but not anymore. Had lunch there a couple of weeks ago & it was full of "morbidly obese regulars" that were overloading their plates from the buffet like they hadn't had a meal in a week. The dining area needs an complete overhaul & so does the kitchen. It hasn't been renovated (or cleaned) in twenty years. No restaurant should have carpet. This place gives me the creeps.

***CASH ONLY*** atm is located inside restaurant 

My friend and I came here on a random Saturday at shortly after 1 and the line was bonkers. There were people everywhere. I haven't see a queue like this since I don't remember when. TBH, I was concerned this place was overrated and my friend and I were setting ourselves up for disappointment, but I had to see what the hype was all about. 

First of all, this place is small as heck. It honestly looks like a remnant of the 1950s or something, when people were smaller. Either that or it was designed for people who don't need personal space. There are actually two lines inside the shop. You order on the right side and you wait on the left side. The menu is limited but they do serve other items besides cheese steak. The queue was freakishly long aforementioned. We waited about 40 minutes for our cheesesteak. 

I got the cheese steak with mushroom and cheese. Omg I'm salivating as I type this. The meat is thinly sliced to just perfection. The seasoning was perfect, not salty at all. The cheesesteak itself was huge and enough for two to share, but who would want to do that. Don't expect green peppers and other accouterments of cheesesteak. This one is simple but oh so irresistible. Worth the wait and worth coming back.

Philly is slammin' these cheesesteaks at every corner but the locals rave about Dalessandro's so you know I had to peep it out.  I was posted in Upper Darby for the week, so I had quite a trek to get out here.  Parking was tough but a playa ain't trippin, I found a residential area next to a football field and the walk was pretty short to the restaurant.  When you walk inside it feels like a smaller version of a Subway sandwiches, not a lot of room for eating especially for large parties.  I ended up going with a Mushroom Pepperoni Cheesesteak, it was good but it didn't knock my socks off like I expected.  I know two cheesesteak places back home and one in Philly called Sonny's that had better quality cheesesteak in my opinion.

I don't get what all the hype is about, because I've had better...maybe I ordered the wrong thing, maybe I just got strange taste...maybe cuz I'm not a local...the bay area has spoiled me...who knows, but next time I'm in Philly slammin I will try to order something different, who knows it might change my opinion...till next time playas!

Butterfly in the sky, I can go twice as high. Take a look it's in a book, it's a Reading Rainbow?!?....No No No you're uterrly confused my friends, this is the Reading Terminal not Reading Rainbow you won't find Levar Burton here either :(

Reading Terminal was the one of the many highlights of my trip to Philly. We ended up having a hotel nearby so we were about 5 mins within walking distance of the terminal.  The Reading Terminal is an indoor public market and a historic landmark building for Philly.  There's tons of merchants and vendors inside the terminal to choose from, too many I can't even count so I will list my favorites:

Beiler's Donuts - OMGOODNESS, the east coast knows how to make dounuts and this place is no different.  Make sure you stock up on Saturday because they are closed on Sundays.

Valley Shepherd Creamery - this cheeseshop is known for it's grilled cheese sandwiches.  The Somerset is a must!

Four Seasons - if you're looking for a health kick this is the spot for you.  An assortment of fruit smoothies to choose from.

Keven Parker's Soul Food Cafe - Food Network Rated Best Fried Chicken, this is a must stop at the terminal.

The Reading Terminal has it all, a wide variety of food to choose from, sit down restaurants, you can even do a little produce shopping for the house.  If visiting Philly try to get a hotel near the terminal as it will be your one stop for a quick and delicious bite.

At $7.2 million, the space is absolutely breathtaking.  Sophisticated yet unpretentious throughout.  There are several dining rooms all connected by pocket doors. One is even tastefully modeled after the old Solari's on Royal, featuring hanging meats and pickled vegetables in cases.  We were seated in the center parlor, which features murals depicting colonial New Orleans in beautifully muted tones.  The wide leather chairs are very comfortable, inviting you to a leisurely dining experience.  Our head waiter, Eric, was very friendly, knowledgeable and professional.  I think the best way to describe Restaurant Re'evolution goes like this: imagine all the best attributes of all of the Brennan restaurants melded together, and you get this unbelievable place.  I described it to James and Pam as "Commander's on mescaline." 

Must have apps: Death by Gumbo- it arrives covered with a silver lid- a server uncovers the lid while another server places the stuffed quail in the bowl.  I have gumbo in my blood, and this was the best I've ever had.  We also had the sizzling Oysters Re'evolution and the Beer Battered Crab Beignets with four remoulades.  Both of these were equally excellent
.
For entrees we had Sheep Ricotta Gnocchi with Lobster with Vanilla, Tarragon, Lobster Roe- amazing and perfect.  The Crawfish-stuffed Flounder Napoleon over
Artichoke and Oyster Stew with fried Crawfish Boulettes was outstanding.  We also had the Petite Filet, which was the best I've ever tasted.  For sides, the Creole Cream Cheese Potatoes, Dirty Wild Rice, and Grilled Asparagus with Parmesan Espuma (whipped up into a foam) were all incredible.  I don't typically like Asparagus but I loved it here.

At this point the meal was completely out of control in a very good way.  Here comes the waiter with a giant lidded cart containing about 20 varieties of cheese from all over the world.  At this point, I don't remember what we picked specifically, but they were great.  One was of a brie consistency made with Goat's milk by John Folse.  

A note about service: I have to add that there were about 20 different servers doing different things for our table under Eric's supervision- french service at it's finest, and not intrusive or distracting at all.  Service was amazingly flawless throughout the meal considering the restaurant recently opened.

For dessert: 

Banana Cream Pie à la Mode with
-Butterscotch Pudding, Lemon Buttermilk Sherbet, Burnt Caramel Foster Sauce, -Coffee and Beignets 
Chicory Mocha Pot de Crème,Coffee-infused Beignets, Black Fig Jam
-White Chocolate Bread Pudding Crème Bruleé 
Lemon-scented Apricots, Salted Bourbon Caramel Sauce
All of it was as tasty as it sounds.

As if we weren't stuffed enough, here comes some Profiteroles for my birthday, which were wonderful... and then the waiter brings over what looks like a jewelry box filled with about a dozen different house-made candies.

All of the above were a fresh and unique take on some of our classic creole and cajun dishes.  It was definitely the best birthday dinner I've had and the three of us agreed it was the best meal of our lives.  You know that's not a saying people who live to dine throw around lightly, and it's the truth.  Afterwards, Eric gave us a tour of the whole restaurant, which is so stunning that it's surreal. The whole experience was like a dream.  I'm still pinching myself.  A huge THANK YOU to my sweet mother-in-law Pam for taking us there for my birthday.  I'll remember it forever.

First, let me say a few words regarding the negative reviews.  I think, for the most part, those writing these reviews just don't get it, or maybe even don't get New Orleans.  This place is a time-warp, and an endangered species.  I can understand that some people do not like old-school places like Dempsey's- I would suggest that you just don't go if you're built that way.  Now, to the reviewers who felt they didn't get quality food: I really question that sentiment, having been a regular here for at least 20 years.  In those 20 years, I've never had a meal that wasn't at least above-average, and I can be highly critical.  I'll be the first to bitch the second Dempsey's lets me down, but 20 years of consistency is a damned good track record.  The place is like the fried yat version of Galatoire's.   Ok, got that off my chest- now to the review at hand.

I don't think I mentioned it before, but Jack Dempsey's clientele is always an even mixture of white yats and black folks, mostly from the 9th ward, Bywater, and St. Bernard parish, with a sprinkling of occasional yuppies, guppies, and yat yuppies looking for some good cholesterol.  We're all sitting comfortably together, like a good gumbo. Old photos of St. Pat's day celebrations, TV sets, and neon signs adorn the walls.  Tables have red plastic tablecloths with huge squeeze bottles of tartar sauce and remoulade on them.  This is serious blue-collar eating, but very high quality.  

Let me explain how I know this place is 5 stars- growing up in New Orleans, my parents dragged me to virtually every fried seafood joint in town, and I've been to many since. Dempsey's blows them all away, except for one- I'd say they're in a tie with Middendorf's in Manchac (which is really not in town- it's a pilgrimage, but that's for another review) quality-wise.  The fact that Dempsey's is right down the street from our house makes it even better for us.  Tonight's meal was perfection, as usual.  Had the "1/2 catfish, 1/2 erstas plattah" with a side of mac and cheese.  Perfect color, crispness, texture, and flavor.  Also had the obligatory frosty mug of Abita to go with it.  Our usual waitress, Cherine, wasn't there tonight.  A new waitress named Tammy served us, and she was awesome too. They're really all very friendly.  As we were leaving we were pushing on the door, and it wouldn't open. This yatty waitress says "pull the leavah!"  I had forgotten that the door locks after 9, and you have to crank down on this lever lock that came right out of the 1950's.  She jokingly said, "Ya gotta stay if it don't work.  At least we got a lotta food. heh heh heh heh."  Indeed they do- great food, and completely New Orleans.

The Gazebo Cafe is my kinda place...food + drinks + ice cream + live music makes for a perfect combination of happiness!

This review however is only for the drinks...the daquiri + ice cream drink to be exact! I decided to try the Nutty Irishman! It was delicious!! Cold and creamy. Tasty and toasty. It had just the right amount of alcohol to leave you wanting more...and those are always the worst kinda drinks, because 5 drinks later...all that alcohol hits ya! 

But overall I completely dig this place! Outdoor seating with a live jazz band playing some cool tunes. I could have sat there all day sampling all their ice cream daquiri drinks, if I had the time!

You can't go wrong with a place called Mother's!! Come on...the name says it all. Plus the long ass line out the door tells me that this is gonna be good. I've cleared my tummy (and by cleared, I mean took a dump) and I'm ready for some good food!

I came for dinner,  the line did go out the door, but it went pretty fast and it's fun just to mingle and meet some really cool people in line!! Mother's is served cafeteria style. You order your food, grab your drinks, grab a table and then they'll bring you the food.
