This was the most disappointing meal we have had in ages. Let me first say that our waiter, Eric, was great. He was very attentive and apologetic. 

Why apologetic?  Because it took AN HOUR to get our food.  No one could explain why. By the time we left we saw several tables walk out.  We would have but we had our kids with us and we knew we'd have to wait elsewhere. 

The so called 'manager' which I think was more of a frat boy on a power trip was a total ass. He was rude to people coming in and demeaning to the wait staff. One of the waiters came to the stand while we were waiting and told him it was taking 45 to get out food. I asked him if that was on going or if it was just one table. He said, and I quote, 'he's just a waiter. I'm the manager and I know more about what's happening in the kitchen than he does.'  Oddly when we were seated near the kitchen I never once saw him head back there. 

Will we go back, YES, but if this happens again we won't. And just a side note, what's the deal with female waitresses wearing black and other colored bras under thin white shirts. Really?

I came here for happy hour (which is 3-6pm Monday-Friday) and I was not disappointed! The service, food, location, and drinks were amazing. It's only about a block from the beach/pier and it has indoor and patio seating (pet friendly)!

To start of with drinks, I ordered the meggerz mule, If you love chili mango, you will love this drink. It was refreshing and delicious. This drink exceeded my expectations and not to mention only $7. We also ordered the buffalo cauliflower, margherita pizza, mini ahi poke tacos, and their chicken and waffle bites. These items were amazing and I personally can't even pick a favorite because all of them were so good and delicious!!

Their happy hour had $6, $7, and $9 food items as well as a $15 combo meal which comes with burger, fries, and beer (what a steal)!! Not to mention their craft beers are all $5 during happy hour!

Service was great and our server was very accommodating. We sat at the patio and we were able to enjoy our food with our four-legged best friend. What more can you ask for?! I can't wait to come back again to try more of their menu items & drinks.

On the western border of university city, Lee's Deli is a neighborhood institution. Their sandwiches and the house-made deserts are something to behold. When you stop by Lee's you'll enjoy generous portions and a very friendly staff who is more than happy to make recommendations. When the staff found out it was our first time there, they treated us to complementary carrot cake. 

They are very vegetarian friendly and feature two meatless cheesesteaks, both of which are delicious. I like the seitan cheesesteak a bit better than the black bean, but they're both quite good. The regular cheesesteak is amazing and tasted just as good the next day.

My previous review of Lyra was written in 2018! The restaurant was new-ish, and I based my review on my first experience at the restaurant. Since then, I have been back many times (at least four) for dinner and lunch. I've eaten on their patio (during COVID times) twice. And I've never once been disappointed by the food, the service, or the experience. It has become one of my very favorite restaurants in Nashville. 

The food is exceptional. I'd describe it as a shared small plates Middle Eastern restaurant with a definite emphasis on Lebanese dishes. 

They always have a selection of dips (always hummus with various toppings and then other options like muhammara, whipped feta, baba ganoush) with fresh pita or house-made crackers. Their muhammara is one of my favorites; I also love their hummus (the option with the lamb merguez especially). Their pita is to die for (soft, fluffy, with that air pocket inside, hot, fresh, and just a little char from the grill - sooooo good). Even their crackers are great! They also always have a selection of breads/pies like manoushe and fatayer. 

Then there are veggie dishes. They always have salads - I've had everything from a radish-y take on a fattoush to a light beet salad to a tomato salad with Turkish cheese. Then there are vegetable/vegetarian small plates; I've had charred broccolini, halloumi, roasted beets, and roasted cauliflower. These veggie plates are always good and quite small and meant to be shared and eaten with other dishes. I love a good veggie dish, and I've had several at Lyra that knocked my socks off. 

Then the meat. I've also had a range of these dishes: harissa braised lamb shank, Lamb Awarma, beef kibbeh stuffed with lamb Awarma, lamb kefta kabob, manti (Armenian beef dumplings in a yogurt sauce), lamb chops,... They're usually amazing, like look around before you draw your finger across the plate to get the last drop of sauce so no one sees you amazing. You'll notice here that they offer a lot of lamb dishes. It's a Middle Eastern restaurant, and lamb is eaten A LOT in the Middle East. I happen to love lamb and think that Lyra is cooking up some of the best lamb dishes in the city (is anyone doing it better?). But if you're not a lamb person, they have other meat dishes as well. There are usually chicken, beef, and seafood (last night they had octopus and prawns) dishes on the menu; I just happen to find it VERY hard to not order their lamb because it's so good. 

Then there's dessert. When a restaurant is this good, I almost always order it. So I've had a few desserts, too: chocolate honey cake, semolina cake, rice pudding... They usually have three or more desserts to choose from, and they're not huge, which I really appreciate, because I always leave Lyra having eaten WAY too much (because it's so good)!

The lunch menu is a little bit different than dinner. They still have the dips and starters. Then they offer salads and sandwiches with sides. Let me just say that if you are there for lunch and the lamb sandwich is on the menu? ORDER IT. OMG ORDER IT. It's a great lunch spot too - don't overlook its lunch and think it's only for dinner. 

Then the beverages. Their drink options are great. Do you like a cocktail with dinner? They've got great ones. Do you prefer wines with dinner? They've got a lot of options both by the bottle and the glass (including lots of options from the Middle East, which I love). They offer a few beers (including some local/TN options). They also have some great teas, house made sodas and lemonades, Turkish coffee, and bottled Sprecher sodas if you want a non-alcoholic option. Then they ALSO have amaros & digestifs and a small selection of arak. (If you haven't had arak before, definitely try it out at Lyra. It's a Middle Eastern spirit made from grapes and aniseed. It's clear but when mixed with water and ice turns milky white. It has a very heavy licorice flavor and is quite strong - hence the watering down. It's very common across the Middle East, but harder to find in the States.) So they have a little bit of everything, something for everyone. 

The service is also GREAT. Seriously, every time I've ever eaten here I've been impressed by the staff. They seem to really love and be passionate about the food, and they make a great food experience a great restaurant experience. The restaurant is small-ish but very modern and attractive. And the patio is excellent - one of my favorite patios in Nashville during COVID. (Another COVID note, they ask that you always put your mask on when staff come to your table which I really appreciate.) I recommend having a reservation.

I'm running out of space, but I have a lot to say about Lyra, because it's so great on so many levels. If you haven't been before, CHECK IT OUT. Lyra is just great.

I visited TennFold Brewing with a friend last week (a Thursday evening in spring), and I felt so-so about my visit. They had a good selection of beers (I went with a Pilsner and my friend got a hazy IPA), and we enjoyed the ones we chose. They have a lot of food (mostly gastropub fare), but we didn't eat on this visit. They have outside seating and, in nice weather, garage doors can be opened to make the inside open air (as it was on the occasion we visited). What I didn't love was really COVID-specific. It was crowded, really crowded. There was a 45-minute wait when we arrived, but there were three standing tables outside and we were told we could order beers at the bar and then enjoy them out there and there was no wait for those. We opted for that because the inside and the patio were crazy crowded anyway and we were cool with standing. We did have to order at the to go bar though, which wasn't so great. It's kind of tucked in a corner, and we weren't sure if we were in line or not. Many people were not wearing masks in line even though we were all pretty close to each other. It took a while to get up to the front to order. In pre-COVID times, I'm not sure much of this would have mattered as much. However, with vaccination rates where they are in Davidson County, TennFold was little too 2019 for me. I'll definitely pass on visiting again until vaccination rates are higher as this place is clearly popular and will likely be crowded. A cool addition to the Donelson area though.

I stopped by Sunflower Bakehouse with my mom and stepdad this weekend when they were in town since my mom is vegan. I think it's amazing that Sunflower Bakehouse is 100% vegan AND gluten free, because I think there definitely aren't enough options for vegan/GF folks in Nashville. I also love that it's very cute inside and has lots of parking. Service was great as well. However, we weren't super thrilled by anything we tried (blueberry muffin and scone). This doesn't mean that you or your vegan/GF friend/family member/date won't love it. I'm not huge into sweets (esp cupcakes), and my mom might be one of the pickiest vegans in the world. (My stepdad will usually eat anything but the didn't love what we ate.) So, it won't be a place I frequent, but for anyone that lives or works in Donelson, this is a great vegan/GF option in the area now.

My second experience was MUCH better than my first (it was still new when I visited the first time and my experience suffered from poor service not bad food). I went to Emmy Squared in Green Hills for lunch yesterday. My dad, stepmom, and little sister (and their cute pup) were driving through town, and we needed a restaurant where we could meet for lunch with a dog during COVID. It was a little bit of a struggle, but I'm so glad we decided on Emmy Squared. It worked out perfectly. Their patio is dog-friendly, so we sat at a table on their patio (the patio stayed empty as long as we were there). The service was great (our server was lovely and wore a mask throughout service). The food hit the spot. We shared two of their salads (the Caesar and the Italian kale, which were both good) and two pizzas. I'm a big fan of Detroit style pizza, because of that thick bready, deep dish crush (almost focaccia like?) and those corners with almost burnt cheese!? For our pizzas, we shared the MVP (vodka sauce, red sauce, pesto, and mozzarella) and the Good Paulie (caramelized onions, sausage, and smoked Gouda). The MVP was okay, but the Good Paulie was the hands down favorite of the day (all four of us preferred it). With a dog-friendly patio, great service, and yummy food, Emmy Squared was the perfect lunch spot for a meal with the family!

We stopped by Hawkers to get takeout for lunch yesterday. I think the menu is really varied and interesting, but we unfortunately didn't think much of the food we ordered. We stuck with small plates so we could try more items off the menu. We tried Yi-Yi's Chicken Dumplings (barely seared and a bit bland/underseasoned). Sichuan Wontons (this was one of my least favorite bites as I thought it tasted way more of peanut butter than any Sichuan/chili flavor), Bulgogi Beef Street Skewers (these were probably my favorite bites of food, because it was really simple and well-cooked), Siu Yoke - crispy pork belly with hoisin dipping sauce (the pork belly was crispy but also really dry and the hoisin sauce didn't taste homemade/seemed very over-reduced), Crispy Tofu Bites and Five-Spice Green Beans (the breading on both the tofu and green beans was strange - not light - and I like five spice in general but I'm not sure the heavy-on-the-cinnamon five spiced worked on the otherwise not very seasoned tofu or green beans; these dishes are also not great ones to take to go as the breading doesn't want to be steamed in take out containers; we tried the food immediately in the car, but it still had taken in quite a bit of steam), and the Seoul Hot Chicken Baos (the bun was good, and the chicken was good too, but it wasn't very spicy and had a sticky sweet quality to it that wasn't what I was expecting for a dish called Seoul Hot Chicken; still one of the better bites of food we had). (We stuck to small plates but their menu also includes sections for Rice + Curry, Noodles, and Noodle Soups; they also have two desserts on the menu.) This East Nashville location is one of many in several states (I believe it originated in Florida), so they're obviously doing well and doing something a lot of people are enjoying. I'm sure there's something to be said for eating inside their restaurant, which I imagine has a lot of style and cool factor. Unfortunately, we just didn't really enjoy the food much. Nashville doesn't have a lot of Asian/dumpling restaurant options, so this spot might be filling a need for a some people in East Nashville or other areas that don't have a favorite place for dumplings or noodles, but as we don't live very nearby to Hawker's, I don't think we'd go out of our way to eat from here again.

COVID UPDATE: I had lunch at Midori with a friend a week or two ago, and we enjoyed our meal. They require masks except when seated; they took our temperatures when we sat down; every other table was available for seating; and servers wore masks the whole time.

Midori is unassuming from the outside, but the food is delicious! And since it's Japanese and Korean, the menu has so many options to choose from! The first time I went, my husband had the bulgogi (which came with the traditional banchan - Korean side dishes), and I had a raw fish rice bowl that came with a couple kinds of raw fish, salad, and rice with Korean hot sauce. Everything was great.

On my second visit last week, my friend got a bento box (a huge amount of food - a sushi roll, some tempura, Teriyaki chicken, salad, rice, and orange slices!), while I had a couple of sushi rolls and some seaweed salad. We both enjoyed our food (and she had leftovers!).

Midori is unassuming looking, but the food and service are good! Definitely worth a visit! Or check it out for takeout or delivery! Very varied menu!

WHAT A MEAL. We stopped by Hai Woon Dai for takeout today and then stuffed our faces right outside the restaurant in our car (it's our new COVID thing), but it was too good not to eat hot and fresh (we live 40+ minutes away from the restaurant). We ordered online through Google via Postmates and got a confirmation text to let us know our order was confirmed and when it would be ready (with a link to check when the food was prepared and ready for pickup). The food was ready so fast - 15-20 minutes! And everything was delicious. 

We started with the Galbi mandu (A2: steamed dumpling), which were juicy and flavorful and delicious. We also tried the Teokboki (E22: spicy stir-fried rice cakes), which was a little (but not too) spicy and also delicious. After that, it was the Jjanjangmyun (N3: Korean-style Chinese noodle dish with black bean sauce), which was crazy delicious - so comforting. And we had to try their Galbi (B1: marinated beef short ribs), which were - you guessed it - delicious! 

We didn't in because of COVID (my vaccine appointment is right around the corner finally though), but my husband who ran in for the food said it was really charming inside! We'd happily eat in after we're both vaccinated (he's an MD that was vaccinated back in December). 

This was a great meal. I loved every bite. We visited Hai Woon Dai, because it was on my LIST (a sort of Nashville bucket list of things to do and restaurants to eat at before we leave Nashville in June of this year), and now I'm so sad we didn't eat at Hai Woon Dai sooner. We used to live in South Nashville, and Hai Woon Dai isn't that far. But we enjoyed our meal so much I'm sure we'll eat it again on a visit back to Nashville in the future when we're no longer residents! DELICIOUS. Whether you love Korean food or are just starting to learn about and enjoy it, Hai Woon Dai is well worth a visit! Based on our first visit and all the food we tried, you can't go wrong!

There is a certain Thai restaurant that I frequent and it's stopped me from exploring more of the Thai restaurants in Nashville (esp South Nashville), and that's a shame! Because I FINALLY checked out Siam Cafe this past Saturday for lunch with a friend, and it was GREAT. Siam Cafe is family-owned (by the Silpacharn family) and has been open since 1976! It's on McCall, just off Nolensville Road, in South Nashville (my neighborhood). They have a small parking lot out front (which had plenty of spots when I arrived around 1pm for lunch with my friend but was quite full when we left around 3pm). The restaurant is simple, charming, traditional, casual. We sat in the back room, which has some homey charm for sure. I had the satee (grilled marinated chicken on bamboo skewer with housemade peanut sauce and cucumber salad) and the tiger tear salad (grilled sliced beef with onions, seasoned with chili peppers, lime juice, and roasted rice powder on a bed of lettuce). Both were excellent. The peanut sauce that came with the satee was amazing, and the chicken wasn't dry! The beef salad was great. So peppery. My friend had the Panang curry with chicken, which I tried and really enjoyed. We also had Thai tea, which was very good. Everything we tried was good, and I'd be happy to go back and try more based on the quality of what we tried. And the service was excellent. You really feel at home and welcome at Siam Cafe! I definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a new Thai restaurant to try! Very good. Will be back.

If you're not doing at least some of your shopping at one of Nashville's two K & S locations (the other is on Nolensville Road on the south side of town), you're missing out. That's because their range of products is amazing (everything from Latin American to Southeast Asian products can be found in their market). If you cook international cuisine at home - K & S probably has all of those can't-be-found-at-Publix-or-Kroger ingredients! You don't need to use Amazon to find those ingredients! But the true reason I love to shop at K & S? THE PRODUCE. It's GREAT, varied, and so affordable. Seriously! Need Indian eggplant? Or maybe Thai eggplants? Or Japanese eggplants? They've got 'em. Need bitter melon? They've got it. Need ANY herb you can think of? They have it. I use a lot of herbs in my cooking. This past week, I was cooking a Persian recipe that required three bunches of cilantro, three bunches of parsley, one bunch of dill, two leeks, and more. If I had bought these herbs at Publix or Kroger, it would have cost twice or three times as much (especially the dill - since those stores only sell those little plastic containers for over $3 a piece) if they even had all of them at once! I went just for the ingredients for that recipe, but the produce looked so good, I ended up buying ingredients for a stir fry as well (tofu, eggplant, mushrooms, snap peas, etc.)! If you cook a lot, especially with some harder to find ingredients common in Asian or Latin American cuisines especially, you need to check out K & S - they might just have what you need!

I visited Diskin Cider with a couple of my friends last night for drinks, food, and trivia (they currently have trivia on the 2nd and 4th Thursdays of every month). They had both been before, but it was my first visit! 

The good: All of the ciders I tried were really good. I had a tart cherry and fruit tea cider myself - and really enjoyed both of them. I tried my friends' as well, and they were good! They definitely have a good range of sweet to tarter ciders. They offer flights so you can try a range of what they make! They serve food! It's such a pet peeve of mine when breweries/cideries/wineries/etc. don't have food - because you're presumably going to be drinking there for a few hours and eventually you'll get hungry and have to move on unless they offer food or food delivery. One of my friends got their lamb sliders, which she really enjoyed. My friend and I each got their mac and cheese, which was pretty good. They also had some more shareable items (popcorn, dip, etc.). The space is HUGE. In nice weather (it's full on winter now), you can sit at their outside seating, which has a fire pit. Inside is also huge and has a fireplace. 

The not so good? The service was meh. They had three people tending the bar last night, but until it got really busy, they seemed to be hanging out a lot (I think they were training someone, to be fair) - it could me a while to get their attention when trying to order a cider and open a tab (they were clustered all together talking and weren't looking in the direction of the bar). They also only have one "cash register" (that's definitely not what it should be called anymore since it's just an iPad, but I'm not sure what to call it), so they did the busy Starbucks thing of asking people their orders while waiting in line to open a tab/close out/add drinks to the tab. They definitely need a second iPad to run orders through - preferably on a different side of the bar. The line got quite long at times - but not because of bad service, just because they had to run every order through ONE iPad. The parking is just an unpaved lot behind the cidery (definitely full of puddles, so watch where you park if it's just rained), but at least they have parking! The cidery was busy last night, and street parking would not have sufficed. So I am glad they have a lot! Not a given in Nashville! And, last thing, I don't want to sound like an old lady, but the music was way too loud until trivia started. The space is really open and has super high ceilings and walls of corrugated steel - so sound BOOMS. The music was already so loud and the space just amplified it. I was shouting at my friends even though they were seating on either side of me and VERY close. 

I like cider, and Diskin is a really cool space. I'd like to come again in the spring/fall when the weather's nice but not too hot and I can enjoy the outdoor seating and fire pit and do a bit of day drinking. Nashville has a lot of breweries, but I'm glad we have a cidery now too! Check it out!

I know people love Trader Joe's. Like a lot. I personally think it's fine but not worth the hassle? If you're going to shop at this store, I highly recommend getting there close to when they open (I went at 8am this past Sunday). It's way less crowded - you can actually move your cart! And you park! Being in Green Hills, the location of this Trader Joe's is pretty brutal. But everyone once in a while you just need something from Trader Joe's. In those situations, just be smart (go early or late)!

I stopped by 615 Chutney for takeout for dinner tonight, and it was a really great experience. What I loved about the meal was that the restaurant specializes in South Indian cuisine, including dishes from the Chettinad region and the southern state of Tamil Nadu. Because they specialize in the cuisine of this region, the menu offered a lot of dishes I'd never had before. I had a hard time narrowing down what to order, so I just ordered A LOT and figured we'd eat it over a few days! Worth it. 

So what did we eat? From the starters section of the menu, we tried Egg Podimas (shredded hard-boiled egg tossed with veggies and Southern Indian spices) and Kyma Idli (shredded rice cakes grilled in South Indian spices and house-made masala with choice of protein - we chose lamb). The Egg Podimas was good - a sort of South Indian flavored egg salad since it was hard-boiled eggs rather than scrambled (which I found some recipes for online). The Kyma Idli was delish - well flavored and a good texture. I loved it.

From the mains, we tried the Chettinad egg curry (hard-boiled eggs in a Chettinad curry tomatoes and onions), Kothu Parotta (shredded parotta/paratha cooked in spices with your choice of protein - for this dish I chose paneer), and pepper chicken curry (boneless chicken cooked in South Indian black pepper sauce). All three were really good. It was the first time I've ever had hard-boiled eggs in curry - yum! The chicken was tender and delicious. But the Kothu Parotta was my favorite. 

Both the Kyma Idli and Kothu Parotta reminded me of an Ethiopian dish I love - firfir (leftover injera cooked in a Berbere-spiced sauce). The idli and the parotta cooked down in their respective sauces to make for interestingly textured and very tasty dishes. 

I also ordered a dosa, but sadly the filling/paste for the dosa didn't make it into my to go bag. I look forward to trying it for real next time (it was the Nethili - anchovy - curry dosa, which sounds so interesting!). For dessert, we tried the Ras Malai (soft cheesecake patties soaked in milk flavored with cardamom), which was a good way to end a spicy meal! 

Despite trying so many dishes, there are a lot more dishes I'd love to try! They also offer dishes that are more familiar offerings from Indian restaurants if you want a familiar/already loved dish (Paneer Tikka Masala, Butter Chicken, saag, Kurma, Vindaloo, Biryani, Chana Masala, Pakora, Samosas, dosas, and more). They have the dishes you already love and maybe some you haven't had the chance to experience yet (at least that was the case for us)! When ordering, they offer several spice levels for their dishes. We went with Spicy for our dishes and they were! 

I ordered online on their website. They texted me to confirm my order and then texted me when the order was ready. They have curbside if you prefer (I think you just call them when you're outside), but I just popped in to get my order after they texted it was ready. Their lobby area is pretty spacious, and no one else was inside waiting for their meal when I went in. It looked like they did offer dine in, but the few tables are really far apart and it wasn't busy inside. 

The menu is varied and exciting and the food is delicious. Other than forgetting a couple of items I ordered (the anchovy paste for the dosa and a drink I ordered), the meal was near perfect. And it's understand that certain items sometimes get forgotten with takeout and given how much food I ordered! I'll happily go back and get an absurdly large order of food again!

My husband and I had dinner at Abe Fisher when we were in Philadelphia for a day a couple of weeks ago. I had been looking forward to it for ages, because the food they serve is my happy food (things that remind of me childhood and holidays). 

We had a reservation but showed up a bit early. Our table wasn't ready yet, so we sat at the bar, which was perfect. My husband had a few cocktails, and I had a few glasses of wine. 

The menu makes it looks like you have to order the prix fixe menu, but I overheard that everything can be ordered a la carte, too. We had the challah Parker House rolls with housemade Boursin (very good); the latke fries with herb sour cream and applesauce (very good); the challah squash dumplings with brown butter, mushrooms and rosemary (very good); and the Montreal smoked short ribs with accoutrements (very good).  

Overall, the food was excellent. Our service wasn't so great, however. Our server was really sweet but seemed very scattered! When she showed up at our table for the first time, she didn't greet us or tell us about the special or ask if we had questions! She just kind of stood there, so we ordered everything. (I did wonder if she thought we'd gotten the spiel from the bar since we had drinks from the bar, but the whole thing was weird.) The food didn't come out very fast (especially the short ribs), which is fine, but we'd been waiting for our last course (the desserts) for a while when she came by and said that she'd never put them in and asked if we still wanted them. Honestly, we didn't, because we were so full, so we just said we'd skip them as long as we did a la carte and didn't get charged for them. She said we wouldn't, and I think it's 50/50 that we didn't (the bill wasn't very easy to read or understand). She was really nice, but maybe just having an off night? Also, the restaurant automatically adds a service fee, so we didn't know if we were supposed to tip on top of that or not. I asked (some from front of house, not our server), and she said that it was for front of house, so we did end up tipping over the included service fee, but I wish it was explained when we received the bill, so we didn't get confused. 

Overall, the food was everything I dreamed it would be. I would definitely return for more Ashkenazi favorites. A unique menu and restaurant for sure!

Reading Terminal Market is one of the largest and oldest public markets in the country, so when a friend and I were visiting Philadelphia last weekend, we knew we had to visit! The market is jam-packed full of different stands and vendors: baked goods, butchers, produce stands, fishmongers, cheese shops, etc. It's tight, crowded, hot, and full of delicious looking goods. Definitely worth visiting, but be aware that it's crowded during busy hours!

I visited Etc for dinner last night with a couple of friends and, while we really enjoyed some of the dishes we tried, the meal didn't really stand out from the crowd of Nashville restaurants for me. The three of us shared three starters, one salad, one entree, and a dessert, so we tried quite a bit off of the menu. We started with the carrot tartare (with celery lemon cashew aioli, pickled fennel, red onion, peppercress, and rice crackers), which was a surprise of a dish - definitely a standout from our dinner. The celery lemon cashew aioli was definitely the star of the dish - the carrot didn't do as much for the dish as I was expecting - but the dish was great overall. We also really enjoyed the lamb meatballs (with Greek tomato sauce, feta crema, tempura zucchini, and dill oil) - it was a delicious little dish! The mu shu duck tart (with Chinese eggplant, black bean honey butter, Szechuan sweet potato puree, and miso scallion sauce) sounded better than it tasted. The main sauce on the dish was really sweet and tasted pretty similar to jarred hoisin sauce you can buy at the grocery store. The other two sauces might have broken up the sweetness of the main sauce but we didn't really get the flavor of them because the tart was served in a bowl with the sauces smeared around the rim of each side of the bowl - making them difficult to get in each bite and really taste. I wasn't impressed by this dish. The roasted beet salad (with honey sambal goat cheese, greens, apple smoked bacon, golden raisins, pecans, cherry ginger puree, walnut oil, and a butternut lime leaf sauce) was okay. The beets were well cooked and the presentation was pretty. But with three sauces (AGAIN), the dish was overly complicated - and I thought the sauces fought with each other a bit. (The butternut lime leaf sauce led to a debate among the three of us; I was the only one that liked it.) (I don't really get why the salad was served with two different purees on the side. Is that a thing, dragging greens through purees? Didn't love it.) After our waiter recommended it, we tried the venison (with Moroccan coffee spice, sweet potato raisin olive phyllo purse, blood orange butter, ginger chickpea puree, chili basil sauce, cherry almond pesto, okra, and mint). The meat was WONDERFUL. Maybe the best bite of food we had all night. But - again - I thought the dish was overly complicated. This one had FOUR sauces/purees, which is just unnecessary, right? We liked two of them a lot and thought the rest didn't stand out at all. The dish also had some unnecessary garnishes - a whole sprig of mint, some random lettuce that hid half of the phyllo purse. I don't think there was any okra on the dish even though it was listed on the menu? We also shared the buttermilk panna cotta (with key lime curd, tangerine sauce, candied orange peels, graham crumble, and whipped creme fraiche) for dessert, and I thought it was excellent. A good balance of tart and sweet with some good textures. But I love a panna cotta. 

Overall, we thought that the dishes at Etc. were unnecessarily complicated. It annoyed us actually, because we'd be liking a dish quite a bit and then realize that there were three or more things on the dish that didn't make sense to us or that fought with other things on the dish. Why does every dish on this menu have three or four sauces and purees? Even salad?! We also found the menu frustrating. The menu basically lists ingredients, but it doesn't really describe how the dish is composed. We definitely relied on our waiter quite a bit more than I normally would because of this. 

Our waiter was lovely and one of the best things about our meal at Etc. The only service related problem I had is that we made clear that we were going to share all the dishes we ordered. And yet they brought all three starters and the salad AT THE SAME TIME. When sharing plates, I really prefer the plates to be a bit more staggered, because we definitely had to think about which plates were hot so that we could eat those first since four dishes were brought at once. 

The restaurant's interior is attractive. A little dark, modern, and classic. It's definitely not a huge restaurant. I don't love the location of the restaurant? It's on a street sort of behind Green Hills Mall. I don't love to valet if I don't have to (mostly because I have rarely have cash to tip the valet). I was able to park down the street and walk, and I walked past mostly closed businesses and a hotel. Just a weird spot. 

We had a reservation for 6:30pm on a Saturday night. We made it about a week out. I'm not sure if you have to have a reservation - even though the restaurant is small - because it wasn't full the whole time we were there. 

Etc. wasn't a bad meal. There were several bites of food that I thought were almost great. But the chef really loves their sauces and purees, and I didn't think they always made sense. Not a bad restaurant, but it didn't stand out for me and I won't rush back.

Talk about bang for your buck. Ordered pickup from here and it was so good. I love their Greek fries, but we opted for their greek nachos. They loaded up on those chips and those toppings. I got the Santorini bowl with Salmon and it's enough for two meals. The salmon was seasoned perfectly and the mix of the olives, rice, feta, and The rest of the toppings were so good. My friends got the gyros and they fill that baby up with enough meat for two pitas. They were quick and an easy pickup as well. Definitely coming back for my greek food cravings.

Had dinner here.  Oysters for appetizers-- they didn't taste the best but we still finished them.  Our entrees were cooked with love but I don't know if I would order the same thing again.

Our server was very attentive and sweet -- it's probably the one added touch in which made the experience pleasant.

This spot runs at the beginning of Bourbon Street so it's not hard to miss.

Check them out.

This is where I introduced my mom to po' boys in all their mighty crusted delicioutude...

I brought her and my stepdad here when they visited from Washington state during Carnival. It was a tough decision, deciding just what would be their first ever po' boy experience, but I'm a huge fan of Guy's grilled shrimp po' boys and felt my mom would love them too, more so than something fried or involving roast beef or ham or whatever because she loves fresh seafood.

So that was the plan, but a pleasant surprise greeted us however, in their special for the day which was called simply "The Bomb". This was a po' boy made not only with grilled shrimp, but also with catfish, and covered in melted swiss and cheddar. 

Eat this motherloving sandwich! Eat the motherloving hell out of it!

I know what you're going to ask.

Scott, did you love your special sandwich enough to introduce to your parents? 

Yes. Yes I did. And they welcomed the special sandwich with open hearts and expect nothing less than future special grandsandwiches.

Final verdict from my mom...

Scott's Mom: "It's about time you settled down with a nice sandwich. You're not getting any younger you know."

It's not every day that I go to a place on its first day open, but this was one of those special days. We even stopped by here the day before it opened to make sure it was going to be open when they said they were going to be. They said today would be the day, so we stopped on by for dinner tonight, and yay they were open!

With the excitement level appropriately described as context, here is the initial impression:

1) This place has a lot of unmet potential. It's got a great location, and the fact it has raw oysters really gives it an edge for being a go-to place in Mid-City for raw oyster fans.

2) They need to reconsider their oyster prices. $11.50 for a half-dozen raw oysters is a bit much. Meanwhile, $13 for a half-dozen charbroiled is also a bit much, especially when considering the fact Katie's isn't too far away and you can get the same there for $9.95.

3) We ordered a plate of hot wings and a catfish po-boy. Both were good, but nothing that can't be found elsewhere. I thought it was nice how the hot wings were the full wings and we got plenty of dipping sauce. At $11 the catfish po-boy was priced well and a good size.

4) Right now this place is BYOB. We stopped next door and brought in a bottle of Abita SOS to go with our meal. This was a good choice.

5) I have no idea what they are planning to do with this menu. Hopefully, taking into account that today was the first day, this menu is just entirely temporary. Maybe they just needed to start serving food and plan to introduce a bunch of stuff later. If that's the case, great, and I look forward to what they come up with. If that's not the case, this place is missing out on a huge opportunity to fill a real vacuum here in this area.

Thoughts:

1) It would be great if Half Shell aimed to be the Acme of Mid-City. Focus on oysters and other seafood. Make it affordable. Offer a unique gumbo and jambalaya among other local favorites. This would be amazing.

2) Embrace the idea of being a bar. Have a good selection of beers to go with the oysters, and go for a neighborhood bar feel. Offer outdoor seating as well.

3) Get creative with the menu. As of opening day, there is almost nothing unique about this menu. Almost everything here can be obtained elsewhere and for lower prices. Again, maybe this is just because it just opened. I don't know.

Final notes:

I asked if they were going to have some kind of oyster happy hour. I was told Wednesdays would be the day for that. So we will be back on a Wednesday for sure.

We will also be back in hopes of seeing some creativity added to the menu, and a place to sit outside and enjoy the neighborhood.

Speaking of being new to the neighborhood, the owner was in the restaurant with us the entire time we were there (about an hour), and never once came over to say anything whatsoever, even though we were the ONLY ones there. We were so excited for this place to open, and it just felt like kind of a slap in the face to be so ignored as a first day customer. If this place is to succeed it should probably consider treating locals like locals.

Although only currently warranting 3 stars on its first day, this place has the potential for a solid 4 or 5 stars in the future if certain decisions are made. I will update this review accordingly if and when that happens.

The lemonade here is awesome! Did they get a James Beard award for their fresh-squeezed lemonade? Cause that would make sense. What doesn't make sense is an award for the fried chicken.

Okay, I get how some people can really like it for whatever reason, though I'm inclined to believe a large percentage of the people loving this chicken so much are those who are perceiving it as awesome because others perceive it as awesome because they think they're supposed to. It's like The Big Bang Theory of fried chicken. It's got a definite target audience and they love it, but no one seems to realize it kinda sucks, and the only reason to eat it is because it tastes kinda like Kaley Cuoco.

Here are my beefs about the chicken. When you order the fried chicken, you get 3 pieces. I was with a friend so they brought us a plate of 6 pieces. Half of them were wings! One breast, one thigh, one leg, and three wings? Willie, Y U SO stingy?! That was one level of disappointment. Another, was that it took quite awhile, probably a half hour outside in line, and a half hour inside at the table, so at least an hour total from parking to the commencement of the chickening. Another level was that the breading wasn't spicy. Another was that the meat wasn't especially juicy. Really, I don't understand what all the 5 stars are about.

On the plus side, the service was friendly and personable, and they even gave us a discount, perhaps because of the long wait, which was really nice of them.

Long story short, I finally went to Willie Mae's and my favorite fried chicken is still at Coop's Place.

Do you want Chinese food?

Go here.

Do you want a lot of Chinese food?

Go here.

Do you want to be presented a plate for one person with enough food on it to feed someone exceeding 2,000 pounds?

Go here.

Do you want to eat so much food that there is the distinct potential for you to look into a mirror and question your life choices?

Go here.

Do you want to test your ability to consume more mass in the form of Chinese food than a full-size dinosaur resurrected through the miracles of genetic science and inspired by the Jurassic Park franchise of films and novels before every last bit of childlike joy was squeezed from their Hollywood dessicated viscera?

Go here.

Do you want to question the meaning of life itself and your place in the universe as a being unique and irreplaceable - miraculously bestowed with the gift to question your own existence - as you stare into the depths of a cauldron of noodles the size of an asteroid crater staring back into your own soy sauce forsaken soul in full knowledge you will never be able to ever finish this one meal even if you ate more of it every day until the eventual heat death of the universe?

Go here.

Do you want crab rangoons with bacon?

Go here.

I Had A Last Date Here Once...

These are the dates where they meet your folks on Valentines Day and you never hear from them again, right? Cause that's how I roll.

I would just like to preface this by saying I'm certain the quality of the food at Patois had nothing to do with things not working out. That's most likely the head-shaped growth on my ass that keeps laughing at the women I date while reiterating specific words they say. (Not cool, Butt-head!) Dinner itself was fantastic all around.

Here's everything we enjoyed that night other than my delusion of having any perceived value whatsoever:

- Potato Gnocchi: chanterelle mushrooms, blue crab & parmigiano-reggiano
  (I have a thing for blue crab)

- Crispy Pork Belly & Seared Scallop with a Steen's cane syrup & spicy mustard drizzle
  (My mom heard the call of bacon and scallop)

- Charred Baby Octopus: Chorizo, Kalamata olives with fregola & a Meyer lemon citronette
  (How can you NOT order something that sounds like a dare to Cthulhu?)

- Fried P&J Oyster salad: Spinach, ruby streak mustards, Benton's bacon, parmesan & a Meyer lemon buttermilk dressing
  (My folks needed their oysters - and more bacon)

- Smoked Rabbit, Andouille & Greens Gumbo
  (I needed my fluffy bunny meat)

- Delachaise Community Garden's Lettuce Salad: shaved local radishes, toasted pumpkin seeds, ryal's goat's milk cheddar & a local wildflower honey vinaigrette
  (My date needed to not feel guilty about never seeing me again)

- Spiced Muscovy Duck Breast: Lacinato kale, Cotechino sausage, duck confit & wild rice calas & a chestnut honey reduction
  (Tasty - possibly better than dying alone)

- King Cake Bread Pudding: Creole Cream Cheese Ice Cream, Ponchatoula Strawberry Compote, White Chocolate Garnish
  (Definitely better than dying alone)

My folks had a nice time and we actually enjoyed our evening so much we even overstayed our welcome and were eventually asked to leave. Funny, I was surprised it took them so long to say our sitting there just wasn't going to work out for them anymore and that they wanted to make room for someone else. But at least somebody said it. (Oh snap)

Anyhow, nice place, nice meal, and I will certainly return at some point for the brunch.

Before dying alone.

Don't wear masks. Beware. In bar when I asked bartender who went to serve me, to put one on, he reluctantly did but then it didn't cover his nose and upper lip. He Then went to table and all were looking at me. He must have said something to them Then I went to look for manager and before I could an older woman came behind the bar with her mask down around her neck. I decided to peek at the kitchen door which was open and no one in the kitchen had their mask on. This is a serious violation of health code. Needless to say I asked for my refund and didn't eat there. I will be reporting them.

Lloyd is a whiskey bar, and its selection does not disappoint. You can sit at the bar and try various whiskeys neat all night. The bartenders are knowledgeable and always able to recommend something great. If whiskey isn't your style, you can always go with a tasty cocktail, because Lloyd has a great selection of these as well.

If you're planning to drink the night away at Lloyd's, I recommend having some food as well. Get the crispy duck things - in fact, get two orders, because you won't want to stop eating them, and don't even think about sharing with a friend. They're like spicy buffalo wings, but duck, and they are crispy and hot and absolutely delicious. Just writing about them now is making my mouth water.

Lloyd's recently hosted the Burger Club, and provided several delicious burger options. The lamb burger was delicious, tender, and very unique in flavor. They struggled a little with timing despite knowing ahead of time how many people would be coming, but they made up for it with delicious food and extending the happy hour so we could continue imbibing in cocktails and, of course, whiskey.

As some other reviewers have mentioned, Grubhouse is off the beaten path for many. If you ask me, this only adds to its charm. They shut down the place to host a Yelp UYE for Sunday brunch, which was absolutely awesome of them. Considering the location and the volume of people they were serving with only three staff members, I have no doubt that this makes for a delicious, accessible (see: not waiting an hour to be seated) brunch spot even on weekends. 

The space is small, but even packed with people it only felt cozy, not cramped. There's a counter as well as the usual table-and-chairs setup, which is nice. I cannot stress enough how awesome the chalkboard walls are. In addition to lively, colorful drawings that make the place feel even more sunny and welcoming, they can print the specials in letters as tall as the average toddler. For those of us with poor vision, this is miraculous and a welcome departure from squinting awkwardly at menus printed in miniscule lettering behind the counter. 

I had the pancakes, which were sweet and fluffy and filling. Everyone I sat with seemed to really enjoy their meals too, and they smelled delicious (the meals, not the people, although they probably smelled fine too, I really can't remember). I was too full and sugared-out after pancakes to try any of the pastries they had on offer, but they sounded delicious. If you're looking for an inexpensive BYOB with great food for brunch, look no further!

A friend and I stopped here for dinner after going to Jam NOLA. I love the Bacchanal court yard! It is fun and whimsical creating a cool dining experience.  I went awhile ago when we were still in early phase restrictions and the restaurant did a good job spacing seating and putting COVID precautions into place. As you would expect, they have a great wine list. We shared a bottle of some delicious wine. In addition, the food was really good. We snacked on a cheese plate and bacon wrapped dates. We also could help ourselves and opted for the freshly baked bread which was worth every carb. I cannot wait to head back when the live music starts back up.

This place used to be fun. I would visit very regularly BEFORE all the greedy changes. I was typically there a few times a week. I was a platinum player. I earned that status. I would get weekly free play, invited to redeem free gifts, and usually 1 free meal for 2 at any restaurant.  Then they changed. The slots changed. You cant tell me they didnt change the payouts of the slots.  They put in place some crazy point system that earned you a few bucks in free play. Nothing else in the mail.  I used to feel appreciated. I would blow my cash, but got a little in return. Any time I was invited for drawings or gifts, I always spent money.   I continued to go- for a while. Once I finally realized that this was a permanent change, I was done. I read an article online basically stating they were trying to attract super high rollers. They werent interested in the locals. I know, after to talking to casino employees I am friends with, they are trying to get rid of the nickle and dimers- the people who got $5 in free play a week, who would ride it out all day and night, and walk out with $100. So that was it for me.  I pass this place daily, and dont feel the pull of adventure like I used to.  
I know the house always wins. The fun of gambling is the thrill of the chase. But when you lose $500 in 30 minutes, when it used to last for hours and hours, its time to quit.  They are the only game in town. So, if it comes to a vote again, get out there and vote to open up gambling. Once they have competition, they will BEG us little people to come back.

If anyone believes $5.50 ($.50 for each topping other than cheese) is too much for one slice of pizza and a drink, I could totally see where you're coming from. 

But it's also feasible to believe you've never been to Arizona Pizza Company in Vail, AZ. I've consumed pizza at No Anchovies, Brooklyn Pizza, Grimaldi's and just about every pizza place in Tucson and none of them serve slices as gargantuan as what were given at this establishment. 

The size of the slice does not come at the expense of flavor either. It was a perfectly cooked New York style slice with cheese then had just enough saltiness that enhanced its flavor. The pepperoni was like any other pepperoni (which isn't a negative remark at all; pepperoni is generally glorious every time I eat it). 

I also topped my slice with bacon, which was a nice addition to the cheese / pepperoni marriage that was taking place in my mouth. 

But aside from the specifics of the ingredients (which tasted very good, mind you), this place gets a 5-star rating on the size of the slice, the price, the service (which was unquestionably perfect), the cleanliness and the ambiance. 

Oh, and they had a flat screen inside with ESPN on. 

Next time, I will try something different; perhaps a calzone.

For a town with a plethora of Mexican food options, one must do something exceptional to stand out. And while Taqueria El Pueblito was great, what really makes it resonate in my memory is the fact that I can get two burritos in one value meal. Not one, but TWO burritos. 

Now that's something worth coming back for. 

Now for the food, I ordered two carne asada burritos and the flavor of the meat was actually surprisingly impressive. Not that I had severely low expectations (the vast majority of reviews on here are overwhelmingly positive), but I am always a bit apprehensive about trying different Mexican restaurants in this town due to the fact that so many come off as cookie cutter and / or generic. However, this place delivers on flavor, service and value. 

I mean, cmon...

TWO (quality) BURRITOS in one meal. 

SOLD

Welcome to Philly, fancy style, for a visiting New Yorker fresh off the train and famished after an early morning commute. Parc proved to be the answer to my mid-day hunger hangups, serving up slightly pricey offerings worth the dough on occasion, even if you live within a distance that does not require an Acela ticket.

A little lavish for a regular late afternoon lunch, Parc immediately mended itself to the bourgeois set in my mind, which did not stop us from settling down at a table on their sidewalk patio, sipping Sauvignon Blanc and enjoying the warm shrimp salad with avocado and buerre blanc. Light, crisp, fresh and reasonably portioned, there's enough reason alone to give this restaurant four stars based only on this salad. Really, it's perfect.

Heavens to murgatroyd this was good!!!!!

Coming over here on a recommendation from a co worker, the first thing I noticed is how packed this place is! ** tip ** this is a bar that sells food, so I would be aware if you are bringing kids.  

Anyways I followed the server's advice and got the "Hoosier Diddy" which was a fried pork sandwich that rated 10 stars!!! Balanced perfectly. 

We also sampled a fried cod sandwich-- and I left the cheese on as recommended---delicious!!! Healthy portions, we all were stuffed afterwards.   They also serve craft beers for the beer heads! 

Stein & Vine is worth a visit if you are out in the Tampa area!!! Thanks!

18/2017

Sushi Maru seems like the Tim Tebow of sushi--- looks good but swings and misses come mealtime! 

Walking into a cool looking restaurant I was immediately greeted by the sweetest gal who helped me make my order.  I noticed in addition to a sushi menu, they carry various Korean dishes as well.  I ordered a sushi combo that came with a CA roll and as I opened up the container I was pleased to see some massive portions of fish.  I got a chef's combo, so I got a variety of fish.  

Anyways as I start to inspect the sushi I could tell right away that the sushi wasn't fresh, and my concern just grew as I started to eat the food due to the fish smell that I started to notice.  So of course after a few attempts at some of the pieces I had to toss my meal.  Bummer.  The CA roll was ok, and of course the ginger didn't smell right either.  I probably could've ate the food as it was admittedly borderline, but the bottom line is I shouldn't be in that position to begin with :)  I am sure if I had the fresh fish this would be a 5 star review simply due to the presentation. 


1 star for the food and an extra star for the staff. Soho Sushi is still the boss when it comes to da raw fish around the TPA!

15/2017

After several attempts to eat here (near misses on opening timing) we finally made it!!  Sad considering we can walk here.  I digress however.  I liked the diverse menu, however the choices are a bit limited song would suggest checking things out online first.  

I had a blood and sand cocktail to start, which was a nice wintery cocktail.  Heat from the dewars plus a somehow slightly spicy fruit undertone- nice.   

We shared the shrimp meatball app, which was very fresh and had a nice light flavor.  The "meatball" part was actually like a dumpling you would normally get steamed in a dough wrapper.  This was a rendition of that, only impaled on a sugar cane stick and surrounded with a puffy dough.  Lettuce wraps, shredded carrot, and a tangy fish sauce accompanied.  I'd be happy just eating a couple orders of these gems for lunch. 

My son had the tacos, which I honestly would not have ordered for him had I noticed they were just avocado and slaw, but I'd already said "taco" and he heard me, so there it is.  He ate the tortillas.  And my super creamy mashed potatoes that came with my glorious spare ribs.  I would have liked more than 3 tiny carrots with it, but it's all good.  My ribs were quite tasty, and very tender.  A bit of a general pot roast flavor, but good.  

The hubs had the three pigs sandwich, which bacon, ham and a breaded tenderloin type cut, topped with an over easy egg.  He quite liked it and raved about the flavorful bread it came on. 

The service was excellent and our special requests to get my hungry child taken care of were met gracefully and quickly.  The food was great and I can't wait to come back to try more items from the menu.  And the extensive draft beer list!!

Came here literally only because I was persuaded by the Yelp reviews. I had no real reason to go to a meat market. But I did on search for some ground beef, given the rave reviews that it was "the best beef ever." Let me tell you something...BEST BEEF EVER!!!!!
I'm not even kidding! Bought 10 lbs for such a great price I was blown away. Made a 2-lb. meatloaf the first night and my hubs almost fell out of his chair at the first bite. Didn't believe me that it wasn't a new recipe. Same old recipe I've been making for the entire 10 years of our relationship, hubs. Only difference = THE MEAT! This beef is the real deal, folks! I mean, I wish I could say more but that's the only food item I'd purchased that day. The store is a little small, but I liked that they also had a deli and some other food options, a little shop area with prepared foods then, of course, meal galore! Next time I'll take hubs with me so we can pick out something a little more exotic. But seriously and for real....try the beef!

They deserve 4 1/2 stars... cocktails here are epic! If you want to not be disappointed, order the True Grit- it's literally the best drink I've ever had. Only downside is that they stay busy, and there's no happy hour. We ordered the Wylder Chopped salad, which is one of my new favs- salami, provolone, Crispy chickpeas and vinaigrette- easily shareable for 2 people. Summer squash noodles was good, but it's healthy, so be wanting healthy when you order. Then we had the honey badger pizza $18- it's amazing!!! Savory and sweet in one pizza. They know what they're doing. My one regret was not trying their pina colada drink.. sounds and looks amazing!

I thoroughly enjoyed my lunch experience. The wait staff is incredibly efficient and friendly. The fish was all very fresh, and the sushi roll was presented beautifully. I ordered the Cho Combo $10.95 and upgraded my roll for $2 to a spicy rainbow. It's also served with 4 pieces of sashimi, a salad and miso soup. If I lived in Tucson, I'd definitely be hitting up their happy hour 4-6pm Sun-Thurs and 5-7pm Sat-$1 nigiri, 1/2 off beer and sake and other specials on rolls. Very casual atmosphere!

Our Old City go-to restaurant every time! Small and unassuming on the busy stretch of Chestnut - Roe holds it own amidst the popular shisha spots and bars. I'm never one to notice these things but their plating, presentation and dinnerware are exquisite. After going here a few times, we've settled on our favorite orders:

Seaweed salad to start - tangy, sweet, just the right amount of crunch. 

Followed by the American Dream roll - fresh, affordable, and decently sized. 

Chicken Massaman curry and shrimp drunken noodle as entrees - perfect rice: curry ratio, spicy, chock full of vegetables that do not overwhelm the dish, and they don't scrimp on the shrimp. 

Mochi for dessert - delightfully soft and drizzled with bitter and sweet chocolate. 

Level four spicy can be a little bit much for those who don't eat spicy food frequently but the heat never overwhelms the other flavors and textures of the food.  

Around $55 for all of the above and it's BYOB. Service is fast, friendly and attentive.

After ice skating in Carmel we hopped over to Fishers to try this place.  The wife and kids have been to Blaze before in Clarksville but this was my first time.  I was not sure what to order since a list of available ingredients was not available on the big menu overhead.  Too many people in line blocked my line of sight to see what the little cards said.  So I just went with a meat lovers and told them I plan to customize it. 

Instead of pepperoni and meatballs, I substituted ground beef and smoked ham.  I kept all the other veggies it comes with and added bell pepper.  Kudos for offering ground beef but what they gave me was pathetic.  The amount was about a tablespoon dumped dead center.  I got 5 slices of ham and that's all.  It never ceases to amaze me that pizza joints will completely cover the top of a pizza with pepperoni edge to edge but when it comes to the other ingredients, NO.

I don't know if it is too noisy in the restaurant, the staff is deaf, or the masks muffle our speech, probably all three, but they got names, crust choices and more completely wrong after a lot of shouting back and forth.  Here is a suggestion.  Have order tickets available for the customer's to write their own selections down ahead of time while they are waiting in line.  I would be able to see every ingredient offered as well as crust, sauce and cheese options.  Subway should do they same thing!  I hate yelling all the answers to their questions.  I fill out a slip of paper with everything you need to know and then it WILL BE ACCURATE.

Another bottle neck in their process is the matching of the brown paper with each pizza while the pizzas  and customers just sit and wait.  I understand different pizzas take longer than others but even with the metal numbers in the pie, the staff seems overwhelmed with this task.  Maybe two folks would be better than one?

The pizzas were ok.  The wife ate one slice and didn't like the Keto crust.  The grandson and I almost finished ours.  The granddaughter ate half of hers.  I would go back but only if I was in the mood for pizza and no other options were nearby.

I searched Yelp for anything four stars and above for lunch Wednesday in the neighborhood by the Botanical Gardens.  I chose Frank's because they were primarily a breakfast place and my granddaughter loves breakfast sausage.  At a little after 11 o'clock the place was reasonably full which is always a good sign.  If I only see a couple of cars parked I generally steer clear of a place but this was not the case at Frank's.  The car in front of me pulled in and the car behind me followed me into the parking lot so I figured I was on to something.

The decor was hodgepodge.  Even the sign out front said "elegant dining elsewhere."  When you want good food and fair prices, the decor doesn't matter.  What struck me first though was how clean the place was and for an older place too.  It was obvious they kept this place clean right down to the syrup bottle on the table.  That syrup bottle looked brand new and had no drippings anywhere on it.  I challenge you to find one like it at a famous waffle chain.

She had a pancake and a side of sausage.  I was surprised to see the shape of the pancake in a famous Disney character (see photo) and decorated with butter placement.  She loved it so much she didn't want to eat it at first but she eventually ate the nose and all of one ear, lol.  She would never be able to finish the whole thing even at her most hungry.

I had the hot ham n cheese with home fries.  The sandwich was so good I could have ate a second one.  The tomato and hoagie bun were very fresh.  The tomato was ripe too not hard like you get at fast food chains.  I now have a new favorite place to go in this neighborhood.

My grandson and I attended the IMS Road Course race, aka Grand Prix of Indianapolis, in 2019.  Our seats were right on the finish line about five rows down from the very top.  Since we were directly across from the Pagoda we had a great view of everything going on.  Since I watch every race on TV, I was able to easily recognize the drivers without binoculars. But with binoculars you can see the faces of who they were talking to.

From our seats, we could see the entire front straightaway and turns one, two, three and four.  At the other end we could see turns 12, 13 and 14.  Since there are huge grandstands on both sides of the track, the straightaway has often been referred to as "the canyon."  IndyCars are already very loud so when they race at full speed, the "roar" is deafening and I wear ear protection.  I'll never forget the first time I heard IndyCars practicing at Mid-Ohio.  When they shift gears it sounds like they are breaking the transmission it is so loud.

Mr. Penske had not yet bought IMS when we attended in May of 2019.  I did notice the restrooms were outdated and I am glad to hear he addressed them right away.  For the road course race there were no open food vendors inside the track, however food trucks were available just outside the gate.  I didn't want to ride an elevator down 6 stories and walk that far so I sent the grandson to fetch us our grub.   I think at least one IMS food vendor needs to be open if they want to grow the attendance for the road course race.

Parking was super easy in Lot 2.  We waited until almost race time before arriving there was plenty of space to park because attendance is no where near that of the Indy 500.  If you hate crowds and lines like I do then I recommend the road course race.  We never waited in line to enter, go through security, or use the restrooms.

Next time we go, I'll probably purchase Bronze Passes for Paddock access.  But I'm used to having free access having worked for car sponsors and coordinating VIP tickets for our clients in the past.  I did miss viewing the cars up close and personal this year.

Something I was wondering was about parking and no one seemed to have mentioned it here.. So, there is a very small parking lot behind the building, maybe 8ish cars, and if it's full there is another parking lot about a street behind which is 2hrs during business weekdays. There is street parking, but you'll need to be comfortable parallel parking :)

Oh and bathrooms aren't inside the restaurant. It's downstairs under the most left staircases. Sometimes they will be locked so ask your server for the code.

Other than that- this new Korean fusion place is worth trying. There are a lot of great things to try such as the Arancini- basically a fried kimchi rice ball, and their fusion of beef bulgogi pasta. The burger they offer is pretty tasty too!

Service was amazing and made sure we had everything we needed, even wet napkins when we ate chicken wings.

Uber tasty and pretty decent sized serving.

Saw the hype on IG from my friends in Reno. It's a little pricey due to cost of materials and such but I think it's worth it IMO. 

I got the matcha + ube swirl with vanilla cake on the bottom and condensed milk. I added on pocky sticks and my only gripe was that it should've been placed cookie side up because when you grab it, you don't wanna grab the chocolate end, coating your fingers with chocolate that you gotta lick off now or wipe... that's just how I've seen it and rationalize it haha. But other than that, it was sooo yummy.

Friendly service that answered my questioned and made recommendations. I'll be back next time I'm in Reno!

Parking - spots in front of the store as well as around the building that is shared by others. It is a busy cross street tho so be careful getting in and out. 

Bathroom in the back- single occupant.

Definitely a cute little place that caters to a certain demographic for board games (think D&D, rpg games) but there are some other "mainstream" games available to play like Uno and Cards Against Humanity. 

They have a nice variety of beers and I first noticed the beautiful wood tables they had. Friendly service as well.

I think I saw some packaged snacks you could purchase but you can buy your own food to bring here as well.

I really liked how they have the game inventory posted online and signs for the games to indicate the level of difficulty and players. There's a lot to choose from so take some time trying out new games as you might find a new favorite. :)

Parking - street parking as it's Midtown but not too bad.

Definitely wanted to believe the hype, but it didn't live up to the expectations. This was my experience but YMMV. 

Service was friendly tho so that's a plus! The seating is spacious and not cramped. Looks like the whole floor space isn't really used as you can tell by dividers and boxes/chairs stacked on the far back. 

Ramen- while the charsu did have a a good flavor that had notes of the smoke, the broth was lacking in flavor. I've had my fair share of "authentic" ramen in Japan and non-authentic in the Bay Area, but none like this. My friends had to add extra soy sauce and sriracha (not on table, had to ask) to add any flavor depth to the soup.

We ordered some skewers and there was a mishap. We had two orders of chicken breast and they didn't let us know it was 2 on one plate so that was confusing. We didn't know, so we told them we didn't get our second order and that's when the boss told us. Definitely need to communicate with the customer on that regard.

Also- not having the spices and sauces on tables or not even bringing them out with the food is kind of weird. We can clearly see it on the unused counter in the back but we were not offered? Definitely room for process improvement there.

I read a review saying that this is the sort of place Tom Waits would love and I was sold on checking it out. Sadly the place was not at all what I would think of when conjuring up images of the mans NOLA watering holes.  

Is it a low key bar for the area? Yes. Unfortunately I think it has more to do with the fact that there is not a lot to draw someone to the place than anything else. 

The lighting relied a bit too much on florescent beer signs, the jukebox on the mood of the current crowd and the beer, while plentiful in bottled selections, didn't offer anything I haven't seen before and the prices were average. 

I suppose if you are looking for a mellow place in the crazy of the Bourbon street vicinity, somewhere more industry than tourist, this will do.... but I would recommend somewhere with a bit more character like the Chart Room if that is what you are looking for.

I went on a Sunday and kept reading that the lines get crazy as this was true, in my opinion the lines move so fast that it doesn't feel like a bother. They have stations set up that will prevent getting lost. There are a lot of eateries and I am def coming back to try more. Only thing is next time I will bring wet wipes because it can messy. I was fortunate to try 3 different places here. I got the Olympia Gyro's, Basset's Ice Cream and than to finish the food coma I got some cookies from The General Store. 

Olympia Gyro's- They were so good, soft warm pita bread with freshly sliced lamb. The Gyro sauce compliments the wrap nicely. Nothing over powers another its just the right blend you want.

Bassets Ice Cream- Massive scoops. I bought some for my sister and she was amazed when she seen her cone. I got the Butterscotch Vanilla in a waffle cone. It was both creamy and sweet and the waffle cone was satisfying. It was a big cone.

PA General Store- I got Top 3 best cookie I ever had in my damn life. I got the Lemon and White chocolate, The Turtle, and the Original Chocolate Chip Cookie. I would def shop by the pound next time. Don't make the mistake and not bring back extra for home.

I don't think I gave a restaurant such low stars. We ordered the house salads, blue cheese mushroom soup and shrimp garlic tostini appetizer with 2 alcohol beverages. We wanted to snack and watch the soccer game.
The blue cheese soup had a very pungent old moldy cheese smell. It was not tasty. My friend didn't care for it either. So, I sent it back. Then the shrimp butter garlic was actual oil and had a strange burnt taste. There were not crustinis but a sandwich looking roll. It was not edible. We ate 3 shrimp and left the rest. The food just wasn't good. Manger didn't come out. We were charged all but the soup. I do not recommend this place.

We were told it would be $20 for two to enter and were shocked because it's New Orleans and there are no shortage of places to drink. When we expressed our shock, the bartender told us "don't come back!" 

Honestly, it is the clubs prerogative to charge a cover; however, it is completely unacceptable for the staff to take offense. Such attitude towards possible patrons creates bad word of mouth, and that is something a business in this economic climate should consider.

Absolutely thrilled to have checked this place out!  My wife and I came here for dinner before a show at the Bruka and loved it.  First, well made, imaginative cocktails--I got a beet martini that was excellent, and she got a raspberry cosmo that was also tasty.  We love tapas-style dining, and started working our way through the menu.  We had 6 or 8 small plates, and not a single one disappointed.  Kobe sliders were nice, foie gras was terrific, ahi tartare and beet salad were fresh and delicious.  The mushrooms escargot (not snails, but 'shrroms prepared escargot style) were a standout, too.  Service was great, and our waiter, Lang, I think (?) was very cool and friendly.  The owners and chef made it a point to stop by our table to introduce themselves, and when we told the waiter it was our anniversary, he comped us dessert and moscato!

We will be back, and I highly recommend checking this place out.

Hipsterism has run amok in Reno's midtown district.  Came here with a group last night for a nightcap and left pretty bummed.

I really appreciate what they try to do here.  Classic and innovative drinks made with fresh ingredients and some TLC.  The problem is ridiculously small drinks at really high prices, served with a self-righteous attitude.  Basically, this place is a wanna-be Chapel Tavern.  Where Chapel also uses classic recipes and top-notch ingredients, they serve their drinks with a smile.  The "mixologists" (as a long-time bartender, this pretentious term needs to go away) at Death and Taxes act like you are an inconvenience.  And whoa is it to he who sends a a drink back because it was made wrong.  This secured a bad review from me:

I asked if they had ginger ale, as my wife enjoys a vodka press.  They said yes, so I ordered a press.  It came made with 7-Up, not ginger ale.  Because I was paying $10 for this drink, I thought we ought to get what we asked for.  I went back to the bar and told the tatty hipster "I'm pretty sure this is 7-Up."  He rolled his eyes and said, "oh? you wanted ginger ale?"  He threw the drink into the sink and poured a new one, only half the size and with virtually zero booze in it.  Apparently, asking the classically trained bartender to make the drink the classic way was a terrible inconvenience.  

When it came time to pay for my tiny old fashioned (maybe 2 oz.-$10), my mother in law's strawberry somethin' somethin' (chimney glass, 80% ice-$11) and my wife's miniature, garnish-free, attitude laden press (2 oz-$10), the bill was $31!  Not going to happen again when we can go around the corner to Chapel for a cocktail that is equally as good, almost half the price, served in a big boy glass and with a smile.  It's amazing how bad a taste my really delicious cocktail left in my mouth.

Last week, I picked up chicken chana masala for takeout with some coworkers and when we brought it back to work we realized that all 3 orders had no chicken in them. We were not expecting anything, but called the restaurant regardless to let them know of their mistake. The first person we spoke to argued and insisted "Are you sure there's no chicken?". 

Finally someone else took the phone who seemed like the manager and offered all three of us a free lunch the next time we come in. 

This week, I texted the manager (upon his instruction) to let him know we were coming to pick up our order - he phoned me and was VERY nice, however, asked if it were two orders and not three. I confirmed, that no, there were three orders that were wrong and he said "Okay, it will be waiting for you when you're ready to pick it up dear."

I was fairly impressed with how the mistake was dealt with and the customer service. But when we went to pick up the food, not only did they make us wait half an hour for something we called ahead about, they AGAIN insisted it was two orders - to the point where the manager came out from the back and said "We have two orders in our records, but if you want to feed someone free, we will give it to you this time," which he said in front of a long line of people. I made clear that there were three orders wrong the week prior and even offered to show him my bank statement so there was no miscommunication that I was trying to squeeze a free meal out of them (which HE HAD OFFERED to us in the first place). 

He then went on the explain that due to 'tax purposes' he could not give out 'free food'. I again, offered to show my bank statement and said "I just want to make clear that there were three orders." He then walked away and someone else brought the food out. I have never felt so insulted and irritated in my life and I definitely will NOT be going back to the Jasper Ave location. I wish I could rate lower than 1!

While all the food I had in New Orleans was amazing, I've got to hand it to Willie Mae's for serving up the best fried chicken that I've ever tasted! My only wish is that we would have had the time to dine in this homestyle restaurant instead of picking up to go as I feel like it could have been an amazing experience. Unfortunately, we had a super early morning flight to catch so we grabbed our order to go and headed back to the airbnb to pack.

The to go line wasn't nearly as long as the dining line and we only had a couple groups ahead of us. We still waited about 30 minutes for our food but it was well worth the wait! 

For my first visit to the South, I knew that I wanted to try some good Southern fried chicken and I did my Yelp research before the trip. Willie Mae's high stars caught my attention and I'm happy to say it did not disappoint! Hands down the best fried chicken!

From the first bite, I could tell I was not in the land of KFC. Everything from the blend of spices to the crunchy chicken skin was spot on. Case in point: I don't usually eat the skin but I ate every bit of this one!

Since we arrived less than an hour before closing, we were informed that we didn't get a choice between light or dark meat and it was simply chef's choice. I crossed my fingers for light meat, specifically a breast, and was relieved to see that each of our three piece boxes contained a breast and two wings. For my side, I chose the mac and cheese, which I learned comes with a side of green beans or peas. I don't care for either vegetable so I let my friends pick which they'd like. I believe it's just the mac and cheese and mashed potatoes that come with the extra veggie side. The mac was rich and cheesy and I was happy with my choice. The cornbread cost an additional 75 cents but was well worth it. Only downside is they forgot to include our requested butter and honey in our to go bag.

My mouth is watering just writing this review and now I want to find some good fried chicken in San Diego.

Having gone to India twice I can say that Tandoor India is on par with typical Indian cuisine.
