I am fiercely partial to the lunch time and dinner time buffet options.  The selections for the meat eater include goat and chicken.  I am particularly impressed with the meatless options that I had to choose from ever since becoming vegetarian.  Available during my visit were chick peas, hot spinach dishes, steamed cabbage, vegetables fritters all very very tasty.  

The staff is present attentive and well mannered but not intrusive and pushy.
I like the traditional Indian music that plays from the PA system. 

The current decor consists of framed currency from all over the world.
It's spacious enough that I have had several staff in-service meetings here but have also come here alone to feel as if I am transported to India for the length of my low lit flavorful meal and you can comfortably and not be rushed to leave.

This would be an ideal place to bring a date because the food is great and you will not feel crowded or overloaded with the modern day dining added amenities like a booming drowning television.  

-BUFFET-
When you arrive and are seated just know that you then have to get up, get a plate and serve yourself.  When you are done with your food leave your plate on your table, remove your eating utensils, and get up to get more food and your used plate will be removed by the staff.

The buffet is around $9.00 until 4:00pm and $11.00 after.

Shafi, the manager has always been good with me and aims to please his customers.  If this place ever renovates I hope it does not lose its attention to service that keeps so many people coming back for seconds.

I hate to do this. But the experience was terrible from start to finish and I'll have to post "buyer beware." I almost don't know where to begin...but let's start with the extraordinarily long line-it's Essence Fest so I get it, lines are everywhere.   But we were 7th on the wait list and waited over 2 hours.  We watch while "celebrities-not" breezed in from off the streets to be seated in front of myself and other paying customers who also had been waiting for HOURS for what would be a mediocre meal.  

We were told that the "owner was hosting them at his private table."  Problem is the place has 20 tables and a bar so if the owner wanted to pay for or host "celebrities"  -he/she should've closed for the day.  It's called, "closed for a private event." It felt exclusionary and demoralizing.  What happened to valued customer service?

And then I get inside and order and wait, and wait, and wait another hour before food finally arrives.  My sweet potato pancakes were dense-not moist or fluffy and my spinach and feta omelette was unseasoned and light on the feta. Everything was warm-not hot, not cold-just warm.  Did someone forget to grab from the window on time for a hot plate to arrive to my table?  It wasn't just me though the salmon, bananas foster, and shrimp and grits that my friends ordered all arrived warm.  The grits are dense and bland and not at all cheesy-really.

Once half of our order arrived the waitresses disappeared and we were hunting folks down to ask for silverware hot sauce and syrup.  Wait staff seemed uninterested in our polite feedback and dismissive.  

This is a new restaurant trying to make a good name but it left a bad taste.  I will not recommend and will not be back.  

Two stars because it was edible.
If you're ever in Philly and want to taste authentic philly cheese steaks this is the place to go! Portions are huge and the foods delicious. Definitely worth the money

About 20 of us stopped in here after a MeetUp, and they were AWESOME!  They were more than willing to push tables together for us, though we thought it better if they didn't.  So, we split up between 3 or 4 tables.  We all ended up with the same waitress though, and she KILLED it!  Our food came so fast, I didn't even get checked in!  Just came across the pictures on my phone and thought...  I don't think I ever did the review!  Had the Deviled Eggs with Bacon for an appetizer and those went down REEEAL quick!  Ordered a Salt + Smoke cocktail, which the waitress warned me wasn't a sweet drink, but a savory one.  I was good with that, but appreciated the warning nonetheless.  It was great!  I ordered the Fried Jalapeno and Cheddar Bologna Sandwich and it was OUT OF THIS WORLD good!  Picked it up to eat it and didn't put it down.  Green Bean and Tomato Salad was a whole lot healthier, and delicious.  Would LOVE to try the Pimento Cheese Toasted Ravs!  And the Cherry Smoked Salmon Sandwich???

Very interesting place. This place feels very authentic from the decoration to the music and even the servers.  If you are used to this type of food I'm sure you'll find something nostalgic on the menu. The menu is not too large and very simple to read. Everything here was pretty new to me and I was excited to try it. I went with some friends and had the opportunity to sample several of their dishes. Everything was very tasty. Some of the dishes feel odd because they are more new to me but I was happy to try them. If you are interested in getting the coffee its more like a small espresso shot with lots of sediment at the bottom. 
   All in all this is a cute place with unique food... meaning it differs from your standard American food. Haha It's worth a try if you're looking for something new or interesting.

Amazing! Definitely a great place for a cheat meal. From their loaded Mac and cheeses to all of the cheesy deep fried appetizers, this place has you covered for your foodie night out. Loved the size of the menu, and although most options are loaded burgers, Mac and cheese, loaded fries, etc you can find salads and healthy veggie options as well. Massive desserts and apps for sharing at awesome prices.

We came in on a Saturday night without a reso (resos not accepted) and got seated in 15 mins. The restaurant was busy and super lively. 3 of us got burgers, regular and 2 #25s- all had 2 3 ounce patties. One of us got the sirloin with 2 sides. The burgers have their signature stamp and come with a side. For sides we got fries, regular Mac and cheese (comes with a few Cheetos on top), seasonal veggies, mashed potatoes and the buffalo chicken loaded Mac. All were great and awesome portions! The brisket nachos as an app were a winner. Was PLENTY for 4 people and only like $12- a steal in my book. Burgers are about $10. Service was great, next time have got to try the brownie dessert bc from the pictures there's like 4 brownies and 5 scoops of ice cream, drool.


Food: 9/10
Service: 7/10
Price: 9/10
Atmosphere: 9/10

My first night in Tampa and I walked by this place on my way to the river walk.  There were a lot of people dressed up as pirates.  Anyway came back and decided to eat here. The bartenders, Chloe and Tyler were great. My sandwich was really good.  It seemed to take awhile to come out but it was worth the wait.  They have a lot of things on the menu that look good.  The atmosphere was nice.  I would go back if I was staying in downtown Tampa.  And they gave a military discount too.

Had a ton of fun here.   Food was good fries were incredible.   The bartenders were fantastic. 
The crowd was fun. It was about a ten minute walk from our hotel (Hilton at Penns Landing). Would love to live in Philly just to visit this place more often.

My first visit to Ybor, i took the free shuttle from my downtown hotel, and after walking around decided to stop in James Joyce for a drink.  The bartender Gabriel was fantastic.  I ended up leaving but came back later for dinner.  I got the Korean fried chicken waffles and wow. It was amazing!  Everything on the menu looked great.  The atmosphere was great. So glad I stopped in.  Would definitely go back if I was lucky enough to visit again.  And I also got a military discount.

Came here on our way from Philly because the reviews sounded good.   They don't have a full menu during certain hours so we got wings and fries.  They were ok.  Not great.  We had two orders of wings and shared an order of fries with two beers it was about fifty bucks.  The service was just ok.  Maybe go when they have there full menu and not during turnover.  
Every time the door gets opened it gets cold depending on where you are sitting.  (I know that's lots of places in the winter) but lots of places try to do something about it.

So happy we finally discovered this neighborhood gem! 

Even though Karma is in the midst of building out its new location, it's been open for takeout... takeout that we have now enjoyed multiple times in just a few short weeks because it's so good - and because the people are so nice! 

We have had a few go to Indian spots in each of the cities we have lived in, but I have to say Karma quickly has topped the ranks. We have had a number of dishes, apps and naan - and everything has been top notch. Since we have been in Philly, I've had some mediocre tandoori chicken and chicken tikka - but Karma has exceeded my expectations. I love the flavor of the rice that many dishes are served with without the surprise of the actual pods of cardamom (which I don't love). We even had a friend who doesn't like samosas say that he loved theirs - that is a pretty great compliment if you ask me! 

When things are more "normal" - whatever that may mean - we can't wait to do more than takeout. They've quickly become such a favorite that I expect our fondness to grow even more.

We had quite a few friends ask us if we had eaten at the new restaurant where the old Popeyes used to be next to the bowling alley in Harahan.  Everyone was raving about the food and telling us how it was packed for lunch and dinner.  Word of mouth is some of the best advertising, so we decided to try them last Saturday.  

Sure enough, walked in and the place was packed.  They told us, maybe a 20 minute wait.  OK.  We bought some wine and hung around the little bar until a small bench came free.  So we sipped on the wine and watched people come and go.  Finally we were seated.

The menu is not extensive, but had a nice selection of Italian dishes and homemade pizzas.  I started off with a slightly zesty Caesar salad while my wife had the soup of the day, a blue cheese and potato soup.  Both were good.  I ordered the veal parmigiano over a tomato basil spaghetti.  Excellent.  The veal was easy to cut with just enough spaghetti to compliment the meal.  My wife ordered the fresh frattura, which is braised pork in a bay leaf tomato sauce with red chile bits.  Again, a right sized meal.  She loved the dish.  

One thing we both noticed about the menu, was many of the pasta based dishes were offered in little plate portions.  Which is great when you want a meal, but not be stuffed from way too much pasta.  Because of the smaller size of the portions, we both had room for a dessert.  We were talked into the homemade pine nut caramel gelato which was just awesome.  

The staff was friendly and efficient.  We talked with one of the owners after the meal and learned that most of what they serve is homemade.  My wife was impressed enough with the restaurant that she went back this week with a girlfriend and they shared a shrimp and crab meat pizza.  She raved about it as I was served leftovers from the night before for dinner.

A nice restaurant.  It pays to listen to friends.

We came here with a couple of friends for the Coolinary dinner.  Since we've never eaten here before, my wife and I agreed to order different dinners so that we could try more of their menu.  For my first course, I decided I would try the Pulled Pork Mac N Cheese Tots.  Can we say Texas State Fair?  I've never had deep fried Mac N Cheese before.  I didn't want to share it with my wife who had ordered the Brisket Taquitos, but we had agreed prior to the start of the dinner to share.  So I did.  My second course was the Sausage Dog on a bun topped with pepper jack cheese and creole mustard.  It came with fries.  No problem not sharing this as my wife is not into sausage.  She had the 3 Pulled Pork Tacos option.  After 2 of the soft tacos, she was full enough, knowing that desert was coming. Both of us had the Elvis Bread Pudding.  I don't know what they added to it, but neither of us had any left on our plates.  The wine list was very weak, but if you are in to whiskey, the options were awesome.  There was at least a half dozen different flights you could order to try.  We enjoyed the dinner, were comfortable in the environment, the staff was masked, and tables were set for social distancing.

We had dinner at Gendusa's the other night as friends wanted to try out the restaurant and we didn't mind eating at a place new to us.  The restaurant is on Williams in Kenner's River Town area.  Plenty of parking right across the street.  The restaurant fits in with the ambiance the of the area.  It looks like an old cottage converted into a restaurant.  Inside, nothing fancy, just what you would expect from a neighborhood place.  The dining area runs along the side of the building all the way to the back.  The table tops are made out of old doors.  

We were lucky and got a table right away.  The menu leans towards Italian, pizza, and sandwiches.  We ended up having the Capone Calzone (me), the Chicken Parmesan (both wives) and the Pepperoni Pizza (him).  The Caesar salad that came with the meal was good.  And the salad dressing was home made.  All the meals were large sized portions.  There was plenty of leftovers to bring home.  

They do not have wine on the menu, so if you want a nice Chianti or Barbera to go with your meal, you'll need to bring it from home.  The upside is they do not charge a corkage fee to open your bottle.  Service was excellent.  We've been back there since then.

My wife decided that we would celebrate our anniversary this year at Morton's.  She informed me of our decision and made the reservations.  We arrived and was promptly seated at our table.  As a nice touch, the menu was titled Happy Anniversary.  I selected a bottle of Cade Cabernet Sauvignon for dinner and we ordered.  We both started with the Morton's salad.  For both of us, the entre was the filet mignon with a side of Lyonnaise potatoes.  Dessert we went our separate ways, I had the chocolate mousse while she had the key lime pie.  

The meal was what you would expect .  The steaks came out as ordered (rare and medium rare).  The desserts were just enough to finish the meal without the guilt of a massive slice of pie.  You knew you had a fine meal, but were not stuffed.  We liked the extra little touches for our anniversary dinner, such as the customized menu.  I know it is not a lot of work, but it was nice to bring it home as a memory.  Mai did an excellent job as our server.  I appreciated that she kept on eye on our wine glasses but didn't empty the bottle before the steaks came out.  All in all it was a very enjoyable dinner.

It's damn near impossible for me to go to Dragos and order anything other than the infamous Charbroiled oysters.  They are my favorite, and just the overwhelming scent of them even before you open the restaurant doors makes almost everything else on the menu a complete blur for me.  This is the easiest review in the world for me to write because the excellence of the charbroiled oysters gives Dragos  a 5 star without hesitation.   (I don't think I've ever taken a picture of my oysters because I never hesitate long enough to do so, lol). 

My other noteworthy menu selections are: 
the corn and shrimp bisque which I often get a cup of as an accompaniment to my oysters. 
the shrimp and eggplant stack which I'll occasionally get and split with someone so that I have room to enjoy my oysters and the additional half of the entree....there's so much, you could still take some home after splitting
And If you save room for dessert, the ice cream sundae and brownie a la mode are both enormous and delicious choices.  Get multiple spoons, trust me, you'll have plenty to share!

Oh, by the way, if you haven't been there this year (2017), they've expanded and added on a huge back room.  It has tall ceilings, open floor plan and lots of light.  That's in addition to the rest of the restaurant staying in tact as it was.  The addition is a nice expansion on the oringal floor plan.

I love this place because the concept is just so simple.  As a single woman, I don't want to order a full pizza and be stuck taking the rest home.   When eating out with friends or on a date, its not always easy to all agree on the same pizza toppings.  I don't know why other pizza places don't offer the pizza by the slice option.

I don't really count Sbarro as a comparison because that's truly fast food and in this area, we don't have any Sbarros that aren't in mall food courts and I prefer the ambience of a full service restaurant like Slice.  

The prices are quite reasonable and theres a good variety of selection of pizzas as well as wines and cocktails.  It's a great place to meet some friends for a quick bite and a great after work place.

No matter how hard I try wood fired pizza and I aren't very good friends. I ask for a thick crust, he comes back with something a little bit thicker than a tortilla. I ask for my crust to be soft. Wouldn't you know it he brings one back burnt and crispy. Sorry man, I shouldn't have to work so hard to be friends. It should just come naturally. The two of us split. It was a nasty one. It was the kind of split that had us planning out visits to our favorite places ahead of time to ensure we never crossed paths. I swore the friendship off forever. 

And forever lasted for a good two, maybe three years. But a little over a week ago forever ended abruptly thanks to a group of yelpers who planned a UYE at 900 Degree Woodfired Pizza. I made the concession because I was so psyched that a UYE was coming to my neck of the woods. But I made sure that I tempered my expectations immensely. I also made sure not to make eye contact with the wood fired pizza as I slunk into the establishment as inconspicuously as possible. 

The UYE group was seated outside under the heaters when I arrived. I took my place at the table and realized they had already ordered. I quickly went through the menu and decided on a tomato and garlic pie. I inquired about cheese on it (I missed the part where it said mozzarella). The waiter pointed out the cheese and then directed me to a cheeseless pizza that was on the menu. He was a fabulous waiter, one who seemed to be really invested in helping the customer make the right decision for themselves. He quickly picked up on my diet and sent me in the right direction. I ordered the cheeseless pizza, mighty impressed that a Tampa restaurant actually had a vegan pizza on the menu. Even my favorite pizza places in the City don't list such a thing, I have to take what's on the menu and modify it.   

Our pizzas all came out quickly (or maybe the company made time fly?) and it was time for the taste test. I loved the look of the crust as it had char marks all over it. Unfortunately char marks usually mean crispy crust so I was stuck in one of those conundrum holes that seem impossible to get out of. But one bite told me that this was one conundrum that 900 Degree Woodfired Pizza had figured out how to solve. The crust was soft on the inside! SOFT! Despite the charring marks and the crisp feel and the fact that it was cooked at 900 degrees, it melted right in my mouth. Score one for them.

Flavor wise, my pizza had a strong garlic taste that intensified the sauce. There weren't any other toppings so garlic is what resonated. I looked around at some of the other pies and I was quite impressed with the varieties of veggies that were offered. Artichokes, olives, red peppers, all beautifully arranged and sinfully tasty (according to the other guests). I found myself plotting my next visit, where I would take the pie I was eating and load it up with a variety of veggies. I called it garlic and veggies and a gay old time. 

Wait...had I really just planned a second visit to a pizza place that specializes in wood fired pies? Yes I did. That's the kind of impression that 900 Degree Woodfired Pizza had left on me. I was willing to rekindle a friendship that I had sworn off forever. Thank you, thank you, thank you 900 Degree Woodfired Pizza. You made being friends with wood fired pizza easy. That's a claim that a lot of other places cannot make.

This spot was amazing. They were really clean and followed Covid-19 rules by not allowing more than three people in the store at once. The food was flavorful and fresh. You will definitely need to take a nap once you eat any one of these meals because the platters are stuffed with food. You will not regret buying some food from here. I loved the the rule breaker cheesesteak with salmon and broccoli. The garlic parm cheese fries are soo good. I'm looking forward to eating here again in the near future.

The food is m-e-d-i-o-c-r-e!

Restaurants that serve mediocre or just average food are not worth writing a review about. Hence my lack of 3 star reviews. 

What makes this restaurant worthy of a review are the flies. THERE ARE FLIES EVERYWHERE, AND PLENTY OF THEM. At the first table we were seated at, there was a dead fly on the table. We requested a new table, and spent the entire time with our hands in the air swatting and trying to keep the flies from making a landing near us.

ill preface this with saying we didn't have reservations but at 7:30 we asked when there would be a table and they said 9:30. we went somewhere else and came back - a friend was in town and we all wanted to try this place. they didn't take us until 9:50 and gave us the late night menu, which starts at 10. this menu is basically a kids menu: BLT, grilled cheese, and about 3 other things.

now i used to work in the service industry and i know what a pain in the ass last minute customers are so i tried to understand why every waitstaff and the manager (who was there all night and who i actually caught making jokes about someone at our table with his waitstaff, then rolling his eyes when we called him out) seemed so miserable and rude. as people walked in while we walked out, we quickly realized that the attitude of the staff was actually just sour by default. and that's putting it mildly.

i come from chicago, where a beautiful meal is always complemented by beautiful customer service, so this was disappointing. the food wasn't good either. they used fettuccini for their ramen (they need to travel a bit more and learn about the ramen noodle i think) and they never once came by to ask how the meal, drinks, etc were. 

our group was awesome that night; positive people who enjoy dining out in celebration of a friend in town etc.. but this was a terrible experience for us and our friend, and apparently everyone we share the story with because they've had crappy experiences here.

my last thought is the way the evening was handled - if waitstaff neglected to bring something or rolled their eyes, and someone from our party alerted the manager, he went on IMMEDIATE defense and didn't give a shit if we ever came back. i've never seen such a poorly managed team and clearly the guy at the top is the reason for it. this place certainly won't last long in nashville, where many of us are coming from cities with a wealth of dining options and experiences. 

sidenote: i was a food critic in chicago and wrote restaurant reviews that even included the former first lady's dining spots. so you can rest assured that i know my dining or you can take a chance on a mean girls style dining experience. if the food was phenomenal it would be one thing, but when you don't even come to a disappointed table at the restaurant you own and manage to offer a free dessert or drinks on the house - you've dug your grave in the restaurant survival world.

Maybe my last order 2 years ago was sub-par.. I don't know. But I ventured back craving a chicken cheesesteak as I've stopped eating beef recently. 
This time I got the chicken cheesesteak with spinach provolone and special sauce. It tastes great with or without the sauce -- but I like that the sauce is really sour and spicy to give it nice contrast. Like other yelpers have said -- it's huge chunks of fresh chicken breast -- don't expect the usual minced up / cut up meat that normally represents a cheesesteak. I will say that, I do sometimes crave that cut up minced up because it's less dry and absorbs cheese much better. But this is a great alternative

I also go the shrimp and chicken cheesesteak one time which was also great.

Carrot cake continues to be $1.50 and deliciously diabetic.

Eat Ice Cream. Be Happy. 

Black and Gold. Cookie Monster. Cafe au Lait. Creole Cream Cheese. Lavender Honey. With so many choices, how can you not be happy?

Went for late night ice cream with friends. Sampled too many flavors. Nice to be able to split two flavors in a cup. The salted caramel was so smooth. Loved the creamy cashew butter with dark chocolate. And of course, brought home a pint of Cookie Monster for the kids.

We have been coming to Deanie's for as long as I can remember. As a kid, I remember my mom warning us not to fill up on the boiled red potatoes and butter while we waited for our salads, onion rings and blackened redfish.Now when we go back to visit friends with my family, I give my own kids the same warning.

Seafood, seafood, seafood.

Love the speckled trout, the blackened redfish or fresh catch of the days. Our friends love the seafood platters stacked high with shrimp, oysters, crab and crawfish. 

The fried artichoke hearts with Romano and pecorino cheeses are perfect to dip in marinara sauce. The colossal onion rings are so addictive. If your meals comes with a salad get the artichoke heart or fig dressing. Add the carrot soufflé as your side and take a pint of spicy potato salad to go. 

Not eating in? The seafood market is quick for a takeout order. Ordered speckled trout grilled on our last visit and the order was hot and ready in 15 minutes. The lemon meringue pie is worth the splurge, so good. Thanks also for the extra bag of red potatoes.

Great local grocery store in Metairie. 

Get transported back in time at Dorignac's. Founded in 1947, this local gem still oozes with old fashioned personality, great customer service and Creole charm. 

Great place to pick up regional specialties, like CDM coffee, Paul Prudhomme Magic Seasoning Blends, Creole cream cheese, Louisiana pecans and Zapp's potato chips. Having a crawfish boil? They are your one stop shop for all your supplies. 

Other specialties include a wide selection of gourmet wines and cheeses, crawfish pies, olive loaf and a bakery that creates custom cakes. During Mardi Gras, their bakery even makes Kosher king cakes. 

Plenty of parking and easy to find on Veteran's Memorial Boulevard about a mile away from New Orleans.

This is the 3rd time this has happened. I order a "SUPER" chicken bowl and I get the amount of chicken that is in a regular chicken bowl. I know this to be true because I have been alternating between the "SUPER" chicken bowl and the regular chicken bowl the past 5 visits and this is the last time I waste my money at Hana Kitchen.

I recommend to never get their "SUPER" sized option for meat bowls because it's just a rip you off. It's a blatant lie that the "SUPER" option is advertised as twice the meat. You're better off ordering 2 mini bowls.

After tonight I established quite confidently that this is a discriminatory establishment based on race and social status. Not quite sure on the name of the bartender who was working tonight, but his hairline was receding and also had some friends at the bar feeding into his demeaning remarks. If you are not Caucasian or from the area I strongly recommend that you do not give this bar/restaurant your business.

I have a strong temptation to include the specific racial slurs and offensive remarks mumbled by the bartender and the peanut gallery of his, but I will save that for a higher level of a authority to share with. 

I must say this single bartender working on June 3-4, 2017 is truly a disgrace to the establishment. 

Demeaning customers merely as a bartender ? What an embarrassment. I understand the concept of overcompensating, but please tell this little guy to take the stick out of his ass. I apologize if it was that time of the month for him. Maybe that justifies his actions?

Should you allow this racist employee continue to work at your establishment, perhaps you prefer to define yourselves as a discriminatory business.

The food and service is amazing however I will never dine there again. My family which was my 85 year old Dad, his wife, a relative visiting from the east coast, my husband and myself (all of us well over 60 years old) had a wonderful meal there last night with one big problem. Apparently the wife of the chef is surprisingly unhinged, unprofessional, and extremely rude. 
Our dinner party was seated about 10 feet from the restroom Corredor with no other dinner parties or guests in our path. When we were seated none of us were wearing masks even though there was a sign asking us to do so. About halfway through our meal I had to use the restroom and a woman followed me there, waited for me to come out and started yelling at me demanding that I cannot go into the dining area unless I put a mask on. Then she slammed the door which automatically locked us in the Corredor where I felt I was going to be physically assaulted. Thank goodness there was a young man that just so happen to have come out of the kitchen that she shouted at to go out the back door and around to the front and open the door to the dining room. I did put on the mask because I didn't want to be assaulted by this woman who claimed to be the owner of the restaurant about 10 times. Extremely unnerving to say the least. 
I told my husband what happened and he got up walked to the restroom with no mask and no problems and came back to our table so that kind of was strange as well. 
Not wanting to make a scene we finished our very expensive meal and left.
Around 8 o'clock I decided to call to speak to the manager just in case they were unaware that they had a person that was threatening their customers. I got the woman who actually did that to me on the phone who promptly hung up on me. 
So enter at your own risk !!! Plus when I was looking them up online a story came up that was on the news about the same type of thing happening in 2020 where the same woman said that she was assaulted by a group of people in their 20s that did not want to wear masks last year so I think this could be some kind of social personality defect this woman has.  
Treating people that go in for fine dining to an expensive meal like that is just bad business and frankly unforgivable behavior. Never again. We live in Eagle and Meridian so we are local and have lots of friends.

This place has some of the most exquisite and delicious chocolates that I have other had, other than Whetstone in St. Augustine. The store is very easy to find from the road, as it is the corner store in the strip. Upon entering, there are a few tables to sit at if you choose to die high tea or purchase an item to eat or drink there. They have items that they have made, in shelves and behind counters, all refrigerated to keep the chocolates or macarons preserved and tasty!

They have many different chocolates, such a mojito, bandanas foster, espresso, so many options! The salted Caramel has the perfect blend of chocolate and salt, and it's not overpowering one bit! The designs of the chocolate, as well as how they are made, are brilliant and aesthetically appealing.

Staff is super friendly and willing to take their time to talk about each of the flavors and what they all taste like!

The Barge Seafood Plate is always filled with perfectly fried goodness. I don't know that the Onion Rings are worthy of the best in America title, but they too are pretty good. The bartenders are friendly and work together well to provide attentive service. The drinks are a step above dive bar quality. If you're looking to indulge in fresh fried seafood, Mahoney's is one of the best in New Orleans.

From what I understand Bluebeard is one of the most popular restaurants in Indianapolis. Having dined once I'm a fan overall. While I didn't love the entrees, I really enjoyed the apps, drinks, decor, vibe and service. Don't mistake this short review for anything other than an endorsement. If you're in Indianapolis Bluebeard has to be near the top of your list of restaurants to check out.

A Big Mac with pesto. .. Cheddar Bay biscuits with American cheese. ..a White Castle slider topped with crisp lettuce and tomato. No. No and No. ..

Some things are just wrong. You don't mess with the classics, especially by cutting corners with low quality ingredients.

Chili's Crispers may not be as iconic as a Whopper, but are certainly a top seller. The light crisp batter is well known and distinct. I rarely eat at dine in chains, but made an exception during a layover. I understand airport restaurants use creative license, but these Tyson-like chicken tenders were an abomination. Completely inedible and salty enough to be used as bouillon. Trust all the bad reviews. Grab a Snickers instead.

Sushi Alive Asian Bistro & Raw Bar has one of the best Happy Hour drink & food specials in all of Westchase Area of Tampa!  However, make sure you make reservations a week in advance if you want to come on a Friday, because on Fridays it's a 2 hour wait even though you can see many open tables. We came on a Friday and left after being told it's a 2 hour wait and came back for Saturday's lunch time happy hour 12-3PM and we're able to get a table without reservations without any issues. The open table and reservation process is not very efficient here sadly. We asked if we could make a reservation for next Friday on a Friday and they said you can only make a reservation for Friday on the Monday of that week. Most reservations for Friday's 5-7PM happy hour are all booked by Wednesday or Thursday usually. 

Happy Hour Specials include $1 Nigiri, $2 Sashimi, $3  Hand Sushi Rolls, $4 Classic Sushi Rolls, $3 Draft Beers, 2 4 1 House Wines, Monday through Friday 5-7PM and Saturday through Sundays 12-3PM. On Tipsy Tuesdays, get 2 4 1 Wells, 2 4 1 Saketinis, and $8 Sake flights! 

The Chocolate Martini was made all wrong, did not come with Godiva Chocolate liquor or Vanilla Vodka, and was the worst tasting Chocolate Martini I ever had. I mentioned this to the server and she said she didn't make the drink. The server should have had the bartenders remake the drink properly. I mentioned it again and the server said she would bring additional milk and chocolate. The drink was still terrible. Do Not get the Chocolate Martini here! 1/10 

The Tampa Sushi Roll came with Tempura whitefish, Japanese mayonnaise, scallion & smelt roe. 8/10 

The Mexican Sushi Roll came with Tempura shrimp, Japanese mayonaise, avocado & smelt roe. 8/10 

My sushi rolls did not come with spicy mayo or eel sauce and I got charged extra for sauce on the roll which usually doesn't happen at most sushi places. Service was a little slow and it was not that busy on a Saturday during lunch time so do not come here if you're in a hurry. I really liked the feng shui decor with buddahs everywhere, Japanese red paper lit up lanterns, and upside down fans hanging from the ceiling. There is a large outdoor patio for those wanting dining in a lower risk open air area. If you're in the Westchase Area, and looking for the best sushi happy hour, I highly recommend Sushi Alive Asian Bistro & Raw Bar!

Jimmy's Fish House & Iguana Bar Clearwater Beach  is located off South Gulfview Boulevard on the southern end of Clearwater Beach next to Holiday Inn, the Edge Hotel, Opal Sands Resort, Jimmy's on the Edge, & Shephards Beach Resort. Jimmy's Fish House overlooks the Clearwater Pass, Sand Key Bridge, Sand Key Beach, offers views of tons of boats passing by, and offers pretty sunset views! During our visit there was free parking still available at the Holiday Inn, but theres only about 15 spots available, spots fill up quick, and free parking may not be available if its busy. 

The Island Coconut Shrimp comes with Jumbo Gulf Shrimp dipped in a special coconut batter and golden fried, Served with a sweet orange marmalade sauce. 9/10 

The Chicken Cobb Salad came with a generous portion of chopped, grilled chicken breast, with bacon, tomatoes, hard boiled eggs, red onions, & Colby cheese. 7/10 

The Shrimp Tacos comes with 2 shrimp tacos prepared with chili lime or Bonsai Thai peanut sauce and is served with cabbage, lettuce, Colby cheese, island rice and tomato with sour cream and house made pico de gallo. 7/10 

The Fish & Chips came with a generous portion of golden fried grouper fingers served with French fries and tartar sauce. 9/10 

Jimmy's Fish House & Iguana Bar Clearwater Beach's star of the show is the beautiful sunset view and the views of all the boats passing by. This bar gives complimentary sunset shots, features a sunset countdown clock, and features some great lives music to provide patrons with a fun key west style tropical laid back atmosphere with beautiful views. The food is nothing out of the ordinary but the views, live music, and service are fantastic! If you're in Clearwater Beach and looking for a casual spot for drinks or food and looking for a pretty sunset, definitely check out the Jimmy's Fish House & Iguana Bar!

Sea-Guini is one of my favorite upscale restaurants for Italian and Seaford with giant floor to ceiling glass windows offering pretty views of the the ocean water and pool at Opal Sands Resort on Clearwater Beach! There is a mix of low top, high top, booth upscale seating. I loved all the wall art and decor which really help make the place feel upscale and nice! There is a big bubble separator wall that changes colors and looked really nice! There is a large wrap around bar with a brick oven for pizza that is usually offered. Usually the menu is 2 or 3 pages but sadly the menu has been scaled back to just 1 page of offerings. The menu was missing lots of entree, appetizer, and all Pizza options that were present on previous dining occasions at this Restuarant. 

The Coconut Mojito cocktail's sweet coconut and tangy mint was not the best combination although it sounded good. 6/10 

The Strawberry Jalapeño margarita cocktail had a hint of sweet and a hint of spicy but was a bit too spicy for my liking 8/10 

The Blood orange margarita cocktail had a bitter taste like a grapefruit, was refreshing and a bit tart without being too sweet. 7/10 

The Watermelon martinis had watermelon slices hanging off the drink like I've never seen before. Watermelons don't offer a lot of flavor but it was a pretty pink drink. 8/10 

The Avocado Crab Stack Appetizer was beautifully played and tasty with a nice tangy and sweet sauce. 10/10

The Squid Salad Appetizer is not for everyone. I'm not that big of a fan of squid personally but they gave a large portion of squid in this appetizer. 7/10  

The Lobster bisque soup came out hot with a nice lobster & Sherry cream, had a great flavor, and even had some nice pieces of lobster! 10/10

The Chicken Penne alla vodka pasta came with a nice rich and creamy tomato sauce, fresh broccoli, heirloom tomatoes, & burrato with quite a large portion size. 8/10 

The Pan seared local snapper came in a delicious roasted florida corn broth, with sweet local gulf shrimp, smoke house bacon, potato hash and roasted cauliflower. 10/10 

The Citrus glazed local gulf grouper came with quite a unique combination of lemon-saffron risotto, sautéed baby spinach, pepperonata, and lemon burro. 10/10 

The Porcini crusted diver scallops came with 3 large scallops on top of lump crab, wild mushroom risotto, crispy prosciutto, and truffle burro. 10/10

The Tiramisu dessert came in a large clear glass bowl with espresso-soaked savoiardi lady fingers, mascarpone cheese, coffee liqueur, cocoa powder, fresh raspberry, and shaved chocolate. 9/10 

The kids get a coloring book with crayons titled "Kids are King at Opal Sands Resort" with a huge Sand Castle on it. The kids menu includes mini burgers, chicken tenders, Pizza, grilled cheese triangles, spaghetti and meatballs, chicken breast, Mac & Cheese, Gelato, and brownie sundae. 

Service was pretty quick and friendly. I hope management can bring back their full 2-3 page menu and bring back the pizza offerings for adults and not just the kids! If you're looking for an upscale spot to have nice Italian and seafood on Clearwater Beach, I highly recommend checking out Sea-Guini!

The Society Table Restaurant was formerly known as The Sea Porch and is an outdoor and indoor poolside restaurant on the first floor of the north wing of the Don Cesar Resort, aka the Pink Palace of St Pete Beach! The Society Table serves breakfast, lunch, and dinner in a casual but upscale resort setting with a great view of the beautiful resorts pink palace style architecture, pool, palm trees, and partial view of the beach. The Society Table is an ideal spot to catch a nice sunset while witnessing memorizing pool reflections  of the palm trees, colors of the sky, and the sunset!

The Double Cheeseburger came with thick cut bacon, pimento cheese, Bourbon onion jam, on a brioche Hun with French fries. The Burger was huge and not too dry. 8/10 

The Seared Scallops came with 4 huge scallops and charred corn, bacon, scallion, brown butter. The scallops were well Marinated and tasty. 8/10 

The Whole Branzino came with a huge branzino Fish that hung off both sides of the plate, grilled asparagus, confit tomato, roasted potato, lemon thyme vinaigrette. This is a very filling meal and not a fish you can find at many restaurants. However, you do have to be very careful for bones! 9/10  

The Seared Gulf Grouper is a locally caught favorite which came with parmesan herb risotto, melted leeks, zucchini, & shrimp butter sauce. 9/10 

Our service was on the slow side but we had a large party of 6. Our dinner party took about 2.5 hours start to finish but it was time well spent. If you're in the St Pete Beach Area and not in a hurry, I highly recommend visting the Society Table for a nice sunset and dinner!

Caddy's Beach Bar & Grill is located on the beautiful Sunset Beach on the Southern end of Treasure Island. Caddys has incredible live music every day which creates a fun festive vibe and is one of my favorite spots to have a beach day!  Caddys has its own private beach looking out on the Gulf of Mexico with clear waters and is a pretty spot to see the sunset from! Caddys offers complimentary comfy lounge chairs and umbrellas for guests and complimentary yoga 3 days a week! 

The Mudslide Frozen Cocktail came with Stoli Vanilla Vodka, Kahlua Coffee liquor, Irish cream, ice cream mix, and chocolate syrup. The Mudslide had a great chocolate flavor and was not too sweet but I couldn't drink more than one of these in a row! 9/10 

The Pain Killer cocktail comes with light rum, dark rum, creme De coconut, pineapple, orange juice and nut Meg. 10/10 

The Rum Runner cocktail comes with light rum, dark rum, blackberry brandy, banana liquor, pineapple juice, orange juice, and grenadine. This is Caddy's strongest drink but isn't the best tasting. 8/10

The Mahi Fish Tacos came with 2 tacos filled with lightly blackened mahi topped with lettuce, Pico De Gallo, mixed cheese, chipotle sauce, and fries. 8/10 

Do not come to Caddys if you're in a hurry or looking for gourmet seafood. Service is very slow. It took a long time to get our order taken, for the food to come out, and to close out our bill, but there was great live music playing and a pretty sunset to keep us busy! If you're looking for some great music, drinks, and sunset, I highly recommend checking out Caddys on Treasure Island! Caddys is what makes Sunset Beach one of my favorite beaches!

Rooster & Till offers gourmet tiny bite-sized farm to table plates with odd exotic pairings that will have you Googling what the heck you're actually ordering. Rooster & Till has a rustic farm vibe with old school drop down Edison bulbs that still manages to bring an upscale vibe to the place. The menu is incredibly small with only 13 items and does not feature steak or lobster or anything fancy that you would expect to spend a lot on. The menu definitely did not feature anything I would go out of my way to get but came here on the recommendation of a girlfriend. 

The Seared Foie Gras came with must 1 tiny piece of foie gras paired with Huckleberry minus 8 Gastrique, Cashew Pear Vanilla, & Vanilla Pear for $24. The Foie Gras was way too salty. For the price, I should have gotten 4 times the serving size. 5/10 

The Seared Scallops came with just 3 scallops paired with salsa Macha, Boniato Puree, Lamb Neck Agridulce, & Lamb Consumme for $30. For the price I should have got 4 scallops with more filling garnishments. 7/10 

The Gnocchi came with just 1 small plate of Braised Short Rib, Ricotta, pickled peperonata, Parisian style for $24. For the price, the serving size should have been triple the size. 6/10 

The Cobia Collar Plate came with just 1 small plate of fried Cobia, Nuoc Cham, Thai Chili's, & Cilantro and had a nice flavor for $21. This dish was over-fried and way too fishy smelling and barely edible. 4/10 

Be prepared to get tiny tiny dishes so you'll have to spend at least $100 per person with at least 4 small plates per person at Rooster & Till or you will end up leaving hungry. The Rooster & Till does not offer a large enough selection of options with just 13 menu items, is not the best value, portion sizes should be much much larger for the pice, but at least many of these dishes are filled with ingredients so obscure and unique you probably will not find them at any other restaurant! If you're looking for something different and don't mind spending $100 per person without getting steak or lobster, definitely give Rooster & Till a try.

Red Mesa Cantina Mexican Restaurant has been a favorite of mine for a long time! It never disappoints! Red Mesa is just a block east from Park & Rec and Avenue in Downtown St Pete off 3rd Street South and 2nd Avenue South. A lot of people that strictly hang out on the central strip, don't know what they're missing! 

The Chips & Dip comes with a large portion of tortilla chips, Queso Blanco, guacamole, refried bean dip. We got a house salsa too and it has a great oregano flavor but a bit of a smokey flavor that wasn't a hit with everyone at the table. 9/10 

The Ahi Tuna Tacos came with seared Ahi Tuna, orange coulis, Wasabi aioli, Pico De Gallo, and mixed greans. The Ahi Tuna was tender with nice thick cuts and the greens were fresh and tasty. 9/10

The Seafood Mofongo came with sautéed shrimp, scallops, calamari, tomato, cilantro, poblano peppers, and onions in an amazing tequila lime butter sauce, served over mofongo which consists of pork Carnitas, sweet plantains, and yuca mash. This dish is so tasty and one of my favorites! 11/10

Service was a little on the slow side and it wasn't even that busy when we went but nothing too bad to ruin the evening. A server should never let drinks go empty and we had a little bit of a wait in between drinks but nothing too bad. Red Mesa has a large outdoor courtyard with a pretty water fountain, comfy booth seating, lots of Mexican wall art, and a festive atmosphere. If you're in Downtown St Pete, you have to try the Seafood Mofongo and Chips and Dip at Red Mesa Cantina! I highly recommend it!

Oystercatchers Restaurant used to serve one of the best but priciest upscale seafood brunch buffets in all of Tampa Bay but sadly, due to covid, the brunch buffet is no longer offered. Just when you thought life was returning back to normal, you realize theres still no brunch buffets. I hope brunch buffets come back soon! Oystercatchers offers pretty views of Tampa Bay, has a private beach, dockside lounge, outdoor deck seating, and large floor to ceiling windows! 

The Nutella Kids Pancakes came with a whipped cream smiley for my daughter. She ended up eating more of the complimentary chocolate muffin breakfast pastries than her pancake. She  complained there were no blueberries or strawberries with her pancake. We got this boxed up to go and the server failed to include the biggest key ingredient, the Nutella or the syrup.  3/10 

The Pork Carnitas Tacos came with scrambled eggs, roasted tomato salsa, radishes, cotija cheese, and crema. This dish should have came from a warning from the server or on the menu that it is crazy spicy, even after taking the radishes off and I'm not a huge fan of spicy. 2/10 

The Smoked Salmon Avocado Toast looked pretty and came with all the right ingredients on the paper but was just too sparing in the ingredients. I like this dish with a lot of onions, capers, thick cuts of salmon, and thick cuts of tomato. I got 2 tiny baby tomatoes, no capers, and the avocado was slathered on way too thin. I can get a much bigger, more satisfying, and more filling salmon locks bagel from Einsteins Bagels. This was very very disappointing. 3/10 

The steak and eggs came with a 10 oz NY Strip Steak, sunny side up eggs, bone marrow butter, and breakfast potatoes. The steak was chewy, poorly marinated, most likely not marinated at all, not even seasoned, and lacking any kind of flavor whatsoever. My fella's cousin was not happy and had to ask for some basic seasoning as the steak was bland. She debating send the steak back but did not want to wait for another dish as service was very slow and unresponsive. 1/10 

Our servers did not bother to tell us that our entrees came with 2 complimentary mimosas. We only noticed towards the end of our meal after overhearing a different server tell their table the mimosas were complimentary. We then had to remind our servers 3 times to bring the mimosas, then had to ask the sever to serve the dessert, and ask the server twice to box up our stuff. We had multiple servers that came to our table at different times and did not coordinate with one another so we had to repeat ourselves for every request which was pretty annoying. Service was frustratingly slow despite having multiple servers and it took forever to close out our bill. The restaurant's temperature was freezing cold inside, and even my fellas cousins from Massachusetts complained about how cold it was and they're used to cols weather. We really were suffering to be at this place. 

I cannot recommend coming here if you're in a hurry. It's such a shame that the service and food quality has gone down-hill. We really loved the brunch buffet in the past. Not having the brunch buffet was so disappointing. I am sad to say that I can no longer recommend one of my former favorite brunch spots. I really hope management can coach the service personnel to coordinate and not send 3 different servers sporadically to do the job of one server. Maybe if we just had one server, service would have been better. I also hope management can improve upon the abysmal food quality, and bring back the brunch soon as I really used to love this place.

The owners make this restaurant the worst they are rude, the old lady that owns the restaurant had our party of 15 waiting for over 3 hours. She sits at her hostess box and doesn't move. I went to check on our status and she says I've called your party twice and no answer, we have 15 people in this restaurant and no one has heard our party get called. Now a party of 15 we understand will take a long time but the owner lying to our faces is unacceptable. What else is she going to lie about. So we got our names skipped and had to wait more and we watched her she never moved or called for any party louder than a whisper. She said she went into the bar and outside calling for our party, never happened. We come here twice a week for the food. 
The lady has told serval rude comments such as we can leave I have 1500 people waiting to eat here I'm not worried about 15 people.

If you has asked me to write a review for Sushi Garden six months ago, they would have gotten five stars.

Their food is outstanding and their all-you-can-eat deal can't be beat. The location is good and modern and the service was outstanding.

Well, that was before last weekend.

The leader of our party had made reservations for our large group at 8pm on a Friday, which the establishment failed to prepare for in any way. They seated us half an hour late, and the food took an entire hour to get to our table. There were no napkins, soy sauce bottles, utensils, anything on our table and I had to go retrieve most of it myself.
My friend didn't even get his entire order (his dinner was supposed to come with soup and a salad that never arrived.) 

It was approaching ten o'clock and the staff began to warn and hassle me about having my kids with me past their cutoff time. It was a struggle to react politely because at that point it was 45 minutes past the time at which we ordered and my response was something to the effect of "We don't want to be here past ten any longer than you want us here past ten. But if it's going to be this slow, what do you expect me to do?"

It was difficult to get beverages refilled and while the food was outstanding, smaller parties that arrived long after we did were getting served in a timely manner while we waited. 

After this complete disaster, they had the nerve to charge us compulsory gratuity for our party size. The manager was completely unapologetic and offered no excuses better than a shrug and complaints about being understaffed as if it were our own fault for wanting to dine at their establishment.

After all the good times I've been to Sushi Garden I don't have the heart to write them off forever, but they're on their last strike to be sure. We'll see if I wind up amending this review in the future. But they deserve to know that they messed up bad.

Edit: Let me be perfectly clear to the Management of this establishment. Our experience was entirely your responsibility and your fault. Not your servers and not your cooks. You set them up to fail and accepted no responsibility for it.

One word: Bad. 

I wanted to try this place out because it was AYCE kbbq and who doesn't like all you can eat? 

The food was terrible. The meats they had weren't even Korean marinades. This place uses like some savory marinade you'd taste in Vietnamese noodle dishes like Bun bo hue or Bun Rieu. How is that even Korean??? It wasn't even Korean inspired!! The only meat I recommend is the pepper steak. 

Service: HORRIBLE. The place was empty and these Chinese servers couldn't even speak English to us and we would have to ask for someone else. Not only that, but they were way overstaffed. I asked in the Talk Threads for the official food of Nashville and where to go and get it. The answer? It's "Hot Chicken" and one spot for it is Hattie B's. So for my final dinner in Nashville (for now), I met my buddy here for dinner.

"Hot Chicken" is a Nashville invention and there are a couple of different varieties. The main idea is that the chicken is marinated (sometimes in buttermilk) and then battered and fried. Generally, whole pieces, not just a chicken breast for example. Once removed from the frier, a cayenne pepper "paste" is applied. Depending on how much pepper is used determines the heat level of the chicken. At Hattie B's, the levels are southern (no spice), medium, hot, very hot and "Shut the cluck up!!!"

First off, parking isn't free. Expect to pay between $6 and $10 for your spot to leave your vehicle while you enjoy your meal. The machine will take credit cards and if you also give it your phone number, they'll send you a text reminder. My text reminder basically said, "The rest of the night's on us. Thanks!"

Second, expect a line. We got here right at 6:00, so we only had to wait a couple of minutes. But while we were eating, the line grew to out the door and down the ramp. I'm guessing those folks were waiting a half hour.

Third, be friendly. You can share your table with others. It's okay. They're here for the same reason as you are - great hot chicken.

Okay, and fourth: The food. I had the half chicken, white meat. This is a breast and a wing. I ordered it "hot" and while it had a little bit of heat, I think I might have to try it again a bit hotter as this was not really all that spicy. Also, all the spice is in the skin. None of it comes through to the meat and if you're someone like me who doesn't eat much of the skin (yes, I ate this one), you're going to miss out.

For sides, I chose the pimento mac and cheese, which was very tasty if maybe a little mushy. Lots of cheese and red peppers in there. Yum. And the potato salad, which I though was good but not great.

Excellent dessert, I had a portion of the banana pudding. I've never had banana pudding with meringue in it and that was really excellent. Very, very good. Still firm and not very wet. The wafers in there were mostly still quite crisp.

So... five stars for being a great chicken meal. Was it the best Hot Chicken in Nashville? That remains to be determined. I need to try more.

Indianapolis Motor Speedway is an American institution, as much a part of this country as the Statue of Liberty, the Empire State Building, the Alamo and the Hollywood sign. 

Home of the Indianapolis 500 and the Brickyard 400, it was built in 1909 and is the third-oldest permanent auto racetrack in the world. It has a seating capacity of 257,325, making it the highest-capacity sports venue in the world. Only 2.5 miles long as a rectangular oval with four identical turns, that's the main track. They also added an infield road course in 2000, measuring 2.6 miles. The Speedway was placed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1975 and designated a National Historic Landmark in 1987.

I took a tour from the museum and that brought me in a shuttle bus for a single loop of the track at a stately 20 miles per hour. No cars racing of course and we were the only ones on the track. The tour stopped at the famous line of bricks.

Yes, the Speedway was once completely bricked though that's been replaced and just leaving the three feet of the original bricks remaining. You're supposed to "kiss the bricks" but I opted not to keep up that tradition with my visit.

Well worth a visit and hopefully once this pandemic nonsense is over, we'll be able to be here to see an actual race!

Bogart's Smokehouse in barbecue joint a few blocks away from downtown St. Louis.  As the name implies, they smoke meats here.  They do it very well, and if you don't get there quick enough they may sell out.  If you're in the area for some fine barbecue, Bogart's is a must visit.

My Overall Rating - 3 1/2 Stars (Atmosphere, Service, Food, Return)

Atmosphere - You'll find Bogart's not too far from major landmarks such as the Gateway Arch or Busch Stadium.  It's close to a market - at least we drove through their lot - to get there.  There's one main entrance and limited seating inside.  Outside you'll find rows of picnic tables and people in line.  There's a nice smell of smoke around and inside there's all the makings of a classic BBQ joint - wood floors, chalk board menu, and hungry patrons.  1 Star.

Service - Bogart's only lets a limited number of people in at a time to order.  If you get there you may have to line up.  They have umbrellas stationed along the sidewalk to help provide shade, and as people file in & out, they'll let more people in to place an order.  It's a smart model, because it doesn't overwhelm the staff, nor will you find seat vultures who camp out on tables before they order.  On our visit, we wanted to put in a to-go order, and the staff were kind enough to let us order directly without having to go through the line again.  1 Star.

Food - The best items are the ribs for sure.  The ribs come with a nice sweet glaze on top and are served as half or full racks.  The meat is tender with plenty of smoke and a hint of sweet.  No BBQ sauce needed, but if you want some Bogart has 4 options:  Sweet, Voodoo, Vinegar, & Pineapple.  All are fantastic and change the flavor quite a bit.  Another standout is the house made pastrami.  Sliced thin, this was perhaps the tastiest and most tender pastrami I've ever had.  Now, many reviewers pointed out the Deviled Egg Potato Salad as a great side, to me it was just ok and a little bland.  But the house made chips were fantastic.  Fresh, crisp with a hint of salt & garlic, had I known they were so good I would have bought more to bring home.  These were the highlights.  Unfortunately, the other items we had was just ok.  The brisket & tri tips weren't my favorite.  Both were quite dry and needed quite a bit of sauce to make the bite better.  I prefer my smoked brisket sauceless to let the flavor from the bark/fat/smoke come through, but I was seriously disappointed.  Well, being that they are located in St. Louis, I guess the ribs should be supreme.  1 Star.

Will I Return? - Maybe.  The owners of Bogart's also run Pappy's Barbecue.  They have different pit masters and different menus.  While I enjoyed my visit to Bogarts, my next visit to St. Louis will include a trip to Pappy's.   1/2 Star.

My Yelp Rating Scale (Sum of all parts):
1 Star - Atmosphere - Is it a cool dive?  Perhaps an upscale place?  No matter the type, atmosphere plays a big part and I'll give a star if I like it or thinks it has great charm.
1 Star - Service - You can have a great meal with bad service.  But that's also what can make a five star joint drop to four.  It's important to the dining experience that service is great and on point.
2 Stars - Food - I'll award up to two stars for the food, since this is the main reason we dine out.  Sometimes the extra star is given for value, but it's really all about the food.
1 Star - Will I come back? - If I know for a fact I'll return, I'll give this a star. A place has to make an impression for me to return. 

Each Category can be given up to 1 star except food (2 stars) because I consider all these categories important to the overall dining experience.  I will sum them up to provide my final Yelp score.

Every meal comes with beans & rice (and I love both!), and you can get regular re-fried beans or black beans, but really - I do wonder - who are the people who get black beans? Gritty, pasty, and flavorless, honey if you're trying to save calories & fat grams why even have Mexican Food? Hahaha, umm no, just no. 

I am going back to SB soon for a visit, and Pepe's is on my list! Yummy! I am so hungry for some beef tacos & cheese enchiladas! 

See you at Pepe's!

PS ~ See you soon Maria!

I am 1/2 Italian, I just wanted to start with that...

I am also a Santa Barbara Native, there are only 4 Italian restaurants I will visit & recommend: Aldo's is second of these four.

Located in the heart of Santa Barbara, this beautiful restaurant offers great Italian food & a wonderful ambiance. This is the only restaurant where I will order Fettuccine Alfredo, please be prepared to leave full & happy! 

Next to this entrée, the menu reads: ''Don't tell your Cardiologist''  and rightfully so :) This dish is very creamy and delicious, I recommend adding chicken breast, because it makes this dish even better. Just be prepared to share this menu choice, as I have never finished it alone the portion is too large.And, as we all know, Fettuccine Alfredo does not serve well as a take out item :) 

Buon Appetito!!!

I try never to be late for a good meal.  

Knowing that Monell's at the Manor serves lunch until 2:PM and showing up at 1:58 PM, I was expecting to be turned away.  Quite the contrary, I was welcomed and served a lunch with wonderful southern leisure.

The very kind gentleman showed me to a table and poured me a big glass of Iced tea, he brought out the Cole Slaw, Cucumber & Onion Salad, Freshly Sliced Home Grown Tomatoes, Fresh from the Garden Green Beans, Mashed Potato's, Corn Bread Dressing and Monell's signature Corn Pudding, like they were waiting for my arrival.  

Before my plate was loaded with all these savory salads, vegetables and trimmings, the gentleman introduced himself as D.J. as he delivered the homemade biscuits, cornbread and peach preserves, Wonderful ! 

But that's not all, I'm no vegetarian.  The Pork Chops, Gravy Smothered Chicken and of course the Skillet Fried Chicken graced the table just in time for me to ask the family seated at the table, where are y'all from and how did you find this Hidden Gem of a restaurant.

Of course a Nashville local had told this Reno, NV family where to find a Great Meal and they were really enjoying the Southern Food & Hospitality.

My eyes were bigger than my stomach, but, I couldn't help myself and ate all that I had put on my plate.  I can still hear my Grandmother telling me to eat everything on your plate and you can have some Peach Cobbler, and sure enough, the very kind lady at Monell's came by the table and asked if everyone had saved room for homemade Peach Cobbler ?  
My reply, Yes Ma'am !

I Love Monell's, their Meals, Service and Hospitality take me back to Sunday Dinners around my Grandmothers Table, and the Beautiful 1890's Manor location was brilliant, a great addition to the Monell's growing tradition and popularity.

As Always, Thank You Monell's !

We sat in the bar for dinner and loved every minute. The bar is cozy with a few tables where you can watch the bartenders at work.

I had the cioppino and it was fabulous. The scallops tasted like scallops, the shrimp, like shrimp, the salmon like salmon, and so on. So many times I've had cioppino where the seafood taste was indistinguishable - not here. The tomato broth at the bottom of the bowl was perfectly flavored and enhanced the seafood flavors.

This was a perfect meal and atmosphere!

When this place first opened, I thought the food was really good. The last few times I've been there, not impressed. But the service is a bigger issue for me. Last time we went there, we were a group of 6 and it was Sunday brunch...obviously we knew we would have to wait for a table. The hostess told us 30 minutes and we settled into some comfy chairs and were happy chatting. She came to get us about 30 minutes later and said she could seat us now - this is where things got weird - but that the kitchen was backed up so we wouldn't be able to order for 20 minutes and our food would probably take about 45 minutes after that.

Restaurant fail.

I've been meaning to update my review. The owner contacted me via Yelp, apologizing for our experience. He claimed that since my review, they have made internal changes and their Yelp rating has improved. He wanted us to try them again, on him. 

I responded that of course, I would give it another shot and how could I claim this voucher? He asked for my email address and said he'd email it to me. I never heard back.

Uh - thanks?

I wish I could give 0 stars. If you've done brunch in D.C.... don't go here. 

I will lead with the positives the music was great, nice atmosphere and they draw a great crowd! HOWEVER, the service is horrible! 

1. We made reservations for a large party when we arrived they were not prepared to seat us. We waited for over 20 minutes only to be put upstairs in a makeshift area that didn't even have enough chairs for our group. 

2. Because of the inconvenience they offered us free bottomless mimosas. Cool. One pitcher had a hair in it, thankfully the manager (or whoever he was) replaced it. We were given plastic cups, not glasses. 

3. The wait for food was ridiculous. The server literally told us it would be a 2 hour wait. After waiting hours we decided to leave. As we are walking out our food ready, all of a sudden. (See photo) 

4. THE CHICKEN WAS NOT SEASONED!!! I can't make this up the chicken was so bland. I asked the man who brought us the food for some hot sauce or the sauce they use on their wings. He proceeded to tell me he doesn't work there  (Mind you he has a tray and brought us our food). The remainder of the food was also a disappointment. And to top it all off we were given plastic utensils. PLASTIC! Not sure if I was at a carry out or a restaurant.

This whole experience was comical. I think with better planning, better staff, BETTER FOOD, and more space this place could be great but they aren't there yet.

This is without doubt the one of the worst casinos I have been to. Just to give you a brief background I frequent Vegas and have seeked out casinos during my travels in Europe. Canada. America. This place is gross and the only reason I have gone a third time is because the cashier line from the second time was so long due to only two cashiers working at a prime Friday night time. The only reason I went a second time was killing time before picking up family at an airport. 
This is a heavily smoking casino. However the cleaning agents that they use will bother you more than the poorly ventilated smokey atmosphere. 
Their rewards program expires after three months of inactivity. 
Their table games have a very high minimum even during non peak hours and other tables empty. 
Their parking is a mess. However they are putting in a new garage. 
Slot odds are horrible. 
There is no cohesion in what slots are where and how to find them. Except of course the high limit. 
Having been to a few casinos (well many) I can determine this casino is catered towards the low income. This is sad. I am pro casino except when they run it this way. 
My recommendation: stay away and send a message. And by no means am I
Upset in losing money as it is such an unenjoyable experience I've never spent enough money to question my losses here.
Update. Nothing frustrates me more than a business taking an opportunity to sell their business and not address or be apologetic to the consumer. Case in point. I state their rewards program expires after three months. This lady tells me to stop by and ask about promotions. Another point. I am aware of table mins and their reasoning. This place has 15 dollar mins on three card pokers with many unused tables and tables used were not full also early Saturday around lunch. I can point out more but I feel I got my point across. Congrats hard rock you earned the 1 star I wanted to give from the beginning.

I've eaten here before, but never felt compelled to leave a review.  Now I've just got to chime in and say (in response to Ryan F, below) that I support any business owner's right (even obligation) to confront parents of unruly kids.  I've been in a restaurant once that was made so uncomfortable by screaming and running kids that a fellow patron finally kneeled down in the aisle to inform these kids that "This is not your rumpus room at home!" - met with restaurant-wide applause.  Hopefully Chef Nelson's initiative was met with a similar reaction; at the very least, I applaud after the fact.  Oh, and the food's good, too.

The menu is awesome and everyone else's food looked awesome, but the organization and service is absolutely terrible. We went in, watched people get sat out of turn in front of us, watched people get their food in front of us, sat there for 2 hours and finally got up without even eating. The last straw was when the waitress told us that "she doesn't work in the kitchen" and didn't know why we didn't have food yet. The least she could do was take responsibility and make it right.

It was really a bummer since the food looked so good. Too bad I'll never go back.

I went here only a few times before the staff began to recognise me when I come in. They are incredibly polite, make sure everything is up to standard for you, and make great food. They recently added additional space to the buffet, so the selection expanded. I am always greeted with a smile, and make a point of it to suggest this place when I go out with friends. I could honestly say this is my favourite restaurant in Philadelphia.
Ordered to go. Waited 25-30 minutes. Ordered lemon chicken. No sauce. Ordered shrimp fried rice no egg. Got combination rice with egg.... called back to complain, line busy....

Yamitsuki Ramen would have been the trendiest place in Chinatown 10 years ago. Unfortunately with all the up and coming restaurants and the vast amount of competition Yamitsuki faces, it just doesn't quite have the magic to really stand on it's own.

Just judging from it's competitors in Terakawa Ramen and Naoki Ramen, Yamitsuki benefits from an enormous dining hall. The establishment definitely uses this to it's full advantage.

The food is where this place falls short. Offering very little to imagine, with really weird bowls, cups plates (I felt the owners tried too hard to be trendy, but forgot how to be practical). The prices are just ridiculous for the quality and quantity of food you are receiving. I'd save your money and hit up another place. There's better places in Chinatown.

A colleague and I had 30 high school students visiting colleges in CA. We were supposed to spend the night at a little inn in Santa Barbara, but they lost our reservation. Stranded with no place to stay and 5 hours from home, I called the Hyatt to explain our situation and to see if they had 11 rooms. They wanted to charge is $250+tax, however when I went online to check the night's rate, they were charging $228+tax. 

How could you scam a high school group left stranded?!? I understand it's not your fault that we were left without a place, but a big company like yours should want to help out an urban school that spent hours and hours fundraising to go on this trip and not try to scam us. As it was, I was going to have to front the almost $3,000 on one of my credit cards to pay for my students to have a place to sleep. You disgust me! 

Oh, and I have a screenshot of the rate from when I went online to "book" a room with 4 people in it tonight.

As someone who has lived and traveled around Asia, I scrutinize Asian restaurants a little more than others. I look at noodle shops as "Asian fast food" and I'm used to hole in the wall places that are open until 3am. I find it a little unusual that people (hipsters) would want to have a dining experience with soup and noodles.

BUT Magasin does a fantastic job of blending East and West as well as bringing local Vietnamese food culture to Uptown. This is probably the only place that I have been to more than once in a month. I love, LOVE their BBQ pork spring rolls as well as, of course, their pho! The portions are a good size, my order came to me really quickly, and the bill didn't break my budget. 

They do close nightly around 9 pm but I hope they keep open later in future. They just opened and while their staff are friendly and polite, they seem at times a little overwhelmed. But that's OK because they will get even better once they hit their stride. They are going to be a strong Uptown establish soon enough!

When I first saw that they constructing this place, I didn't want to like it. I thought it was going to be just like that burger place across the street. And it's right next to Stein's and no body messes with that local institution. And Lower Garden now has so many coffee shops I didn't think we need another place. 

Then I finally stepped inside, had a coffee and I was thoroughly impressed. I hate to say it but their iced coffee is tied for 2nd place in my own ice-coffee rankings. And I'm not even talking about their Nitro ice-coffee either. That's in a whole separate category by itself. I usually drink my coffee with milk and sugar but not with the Nitro brew. That's good as is and it tastes like a coffee flavored Guinness. They should serve it in a pint, not a coffee cup!

I came back another time and had some sliders and was blown away! At first I was a little skeptical at first because I assumed "sliders" meant "smaller" in size but the taste was bigger than my eyes. The pork-belly slider would make your Chinese exchange student friend think they were back home in China! 

So check out this place now before it gets more popular and touristy (corporate)...like Dat Dog!

I want death by fried artichokes. Just bury me in them. 

I started my visit at Tavolo by getting seated by a friendly-as-hell server, who promptly brought me a fresh watermelon cocktail. It could not have been more refreshing on a muggy Missouri day. I ordered the fried artichokes, which looked pretty good in a photo I saw on Yelp. Well "pretty good" is a damn understatement. The 'chokes were meaty and coated in a crispy light breading. They were finished with lemon and parmesan, which brought all of the salty, crispy, sharp, citrusy flavors and textures together amazingly. 

My main course was the Tutto Mare. Hey, order this. The shrimp were of impressive size, and there was an overall generous amount of seafood. The sauce and pasta were both perfect - al dente and not overpowering. I imagined that I would have leftovers but instead I vacuumed the plate with my face. I highly recommend Tavolo!

The thought of having dim sum at Gee's Garden gives me a case of the drools. Not only are there plentiful choices of items, they are also FRESH.

The key to getting fresh dim sum is going to Chinese restaurants that are busy. They are constantly cooking new dim sum, rather than reheating old ones. Go on Saturdays and Sundays when they are the busiest. I had had to wait, but sometimes the parking lot gets full. On weekdays, you will still get your fresh dim sum, but you have to wait 15-20 minutes for restaurant to cook them because there are no crowds. 

For those of you who are new, here are some basic dim sum etiquette:
1) SHARE (do not take seconds until everyone gets a piece)
2) Wait for the cart to come to you
3) Use chopsticks or ask for a fork

Some staple items for any of you dim sum newbies:
- Har gow (shrimp dumplings)
- Shumai (pork dumplings with wonton skin)
- Sharkfin (shrimp and most likely pork dumpling. i doubt they use real shark fin)
- BBQ pork buns
- Cheong fan (rolled rice noodles with shrimp)
- Lo baak gou (turnip cake)
- Daan taat (egg custard tart)
- Stuffed claw crab w/ sweet & sour sauce

My other personal favorites:
- Roasted pork belly
- Haam sui gau (deep-fried glutinous rice dumpling with pork)
- Gai lan (Chinese broccoli)
- Sweet tofu w/ ginger dessert
- Lotus leaf sticky rice (with pork and mushroom)

For those of you who are daring order the CHICKEN FEET if you want to become a true dim sum lover.

Hope this review is helpful. Enjoy! :)

REDEMPTION!!!

HIGHLIGHT:
the salt aire foam is so delicious, I ordered a pineapple jalapeño margarita and requested the salty foam to be added to my drink and they had no problem customizing a drink for me.

The pineapple jalapeño margarita is ABSOLUTELY delicious and dangerous because you can't taste the tequila

COVID:
guest and staff wears masks, hand sanitizer provided at the entrance as well as on every table.

The tables were spread out and they did a great job at sitting people apart.

APPETIZERS:
We had to order the cauliflower again because omg it was so good

We also ordered the smashed avocado which is similar to guacamole but they add their own spin by adding corn and different vegetable chips - the best ones are the sweet potato chips

ENTREE:
I personally ordered the angry pig and the grouper taco.
The grouper taco was TO DIE FOR 

WARNING - the angry pig Is extremely spicy but super good

SERVICE:
To be honest the only reason we came back is because the service was so amazing last time.

This time we came our server was Tyler, he was very attentive, helped us with all the questions and even gave us recommendations. I really enjoyed his jokes through our meal
