We definitely got a great redemption after our first visit
I would absolutely come back here :)

This place is stingy. For fish pots you have to pay extra for garnishing side veggies, extra $3 bucks for EACH KIND (a few tiny pieces), such as napa cabbage, potato, mushroom. Excuse me??? 
The fish we ordered was the most expensive one - big mouth bass, nearly $80 along with the side veggies. It tasted good but was not enough for two people to share. 
And then the stir fried kidney dish we ordered doesn't require extra $$ for garnishing veggies, but it had only a few small pieces of kidney with a whole bunch of very chewy celery and carrot.

3 Stars for a prime location on Broadway, but food that just didn't deliver.

Acme is massive and has three floors of space for folks to enjoy, each with its own vibe. We walked by the stage of the first floor and the music was really great- a soulful trio of women. Ultimately, we opted for the second floor because we were all pretty hungry.

The decor and space is on point for the theme. There are booths, regular tables, and we opted for couches on either side of a table. The server was nice and quick, which was very much appreciated.

Unfortunately, the food was not great. The best dish was The Hatchery, which works for vegetarians in the group. I opted for a burger and sweet potato fries. After two years of soggy take out fries due to Covid, I was excited to bite into some crispy spuds. The regular fries and sp fries were the first thing to hit our table and they were suuuuper soggy and really unpleasant. Huge bummer... we left them and moved on to our main dishes when they arrived. My burger wasn't bad, but not something I'd order again. The bun was stale on the edges, and I had to rip them off. Overall, just really disappointing.

Would I return? Only if I really wanted to be on Broadway because they have so much space you can get a table pretty quickly. But otherwise, I would give it a skip.

4 Stars for Tex Mex in a surprisingly upscale environment and a great private space.

My fave things about Miguel's? The ambiance outside on the back patio (wall on through or you'll miss it) with twinkle lights and plants, and their private dining space for a group dinner. 

The private space requires a minimum order, but with 10 people, we hit it and then some. It's great that you can shut the curtains to make it more private, or open the blinds to see the inside and outside dining room.

Ok, on to the food. I'd definitely recommend the queso. One of the orders had meat in the cheese and it was glorious. We all ordered different dishes and everyone was happy, but not blown away. I think they waited to bring food for the whole group, so the fajitas, which I hear are normally sizzling, we're just warm. 

I appreciated the attentiveness of the servers and our drinks were well maintained! We had one person in our group with some tricky dietary restrictions and the servers were a bit wishy washy about ingredients of certain dishes. In the end, she was a bit stressed that they might contain soy, but she crossed her fingers! 

Again, love the space and this is better than typical Tex Mex. would I return over and over? Maybe not. But it was solid and perfect for groups.

5 Stars for a super hip coworking space that has inspiration (and bathrooms) around every corner. And did I mention the selfie-opps??

I was in town for a work conference and we worked out of Station House for the week. The restaurant was closed during this time, so this is specifically a review for the coworking space and coffee shop only.

Right as we got to the front entrance I knew I was home. Well, not necessarily my "right now" home, but more like my "dream-if-I-hit-the-lottery" home. The first floor has small conference rooms lining it (encased in glass, so not very private, but great for a shorter meeting), furnished beautifully. I'm talking different, beautiful chairs for each room and an overall flawless aesthetic. The coffee bar is also located on the first floor. It had a great selection of tea and coffee with specialty syrups as well as some light breakfast items (croissants, quiches, etc.). I ordered a decaf caramel herb coffee and enjoyed the unique flavor (of the syrups... I know very little about actual coffee...). The croissants I ordered were always warmed up and tasted fairly fresh.

Heading upstairs you'll see rooms and workspaces to fit any need. Some look more private and conventional, while others include desks hanging from the ceiling like a big-kid, slightly less fun rope swing. Every nook is expertly decorated and begs for a selfie (I may or may not have taken one in a room with palm wallpaper and a neon sign reading "i woke up like this").

I also appreciated the bathroom options. The floor we were on had a shared bathroom with stalls (shared with men and women), as well as a private bathroom which is useful for the bashful folks out there.

Just outside of our conference room was a kitchen that included a water-dispenser, old-timey fridge, and some snacks. There's also a rooftop, grassy area for when you just need to sit on pillows in the grass. As one does on a work day. #RemoteEmployeeLife

Overall, I'd highly recommend this workspace and felt like I was in some San Francisco paradise the whole time we were there.

3 Stars for great Cuban sandwiches but some 'meh' service...

You know those places that are so hip and always packed enough to not actually have to care about their patrons? That's the vibe I felt here when I went for lunch recently. 

We scoped out a table and chairs just outside by their outdoor window and ordered as a group. 

The Cuban sandwich is the fan favorite, but in an effort to add some variety to the order, I got the Pollo Asado (chicken marinated in coconut with pineapple chunks and avo). The sandwich was sweet and salty and pretty gosh-darn-delicious! I got a bite of a Cuban and was also thoroughly impressed.

But it's not just about the sandwiches, folks. The jicama salad, thought a bit spicy, was characteristically crunchy and packed with flavor. It cuts the fat and grease of the sandwiches and it's definitely a must. Another crazy-awesome side is their maduros (sweet plantains). I'm from Miami so I've eaten my fair share of maduros and yet this one was so different! It was perfectly cooked with lime wedges and the acidity of the lime was perfect to add a kick to the dish.

And finally, the location is amazing! Cute, walkable, tons of murals! Can't wait to to return with a better camera!

But, wait. Why 3 Stars...? I just found myself saying "oh, sorry," and "thank you" all the time. And getting barely a nod in return. The food may be awesome but nothing kills my vibe as much as staff that is just kinda over it. The guy running the food out to those who were seated in the vicinity was rolling his eyes as he took food over to the groups. At one point he and a few patrons were actually laughing at someone who just hadn't heard their name called. It was weird and kind of disheartening. 

Otherwise though, this place is pretty dang good and the surrounding 'hood is worth a stroll!

5 Stars for some of the best food I've had in Tampa. And a pork belly dish that deserves a round of applause.

We were able to snag a spot at the bar and ordered a few dishes, given that they are small, sharing portions.

First, we got the oysters. They are served with cherry ponzu, chives, and sesame. And it took me about 10 seconds to slurp 6 of those bad boys down because they were so good. I love raw oysters, but I'm partial to the ones with fun garnishes and flavors to bounce off the brine and salt. These ingredients were the perfect accompaniment for these fresh oysters. 

From there, we order the roast Brussels sprouts. The leaves are crispy, but also sweet from the burnt onions. The  Tasso ham and smoked aioli add a richness to what can sometimes be a bitter veggie. These are worth an order.

Surely there had to be one "meh" dish! NOPE. The gnocchi, served with short ribs, smoked ricotta, stewed tomatoes, and spicy pickled peperonata, was another winner. The acidity of the tomatoes and pickled peperonata balance the heavy richness of the rib meat, ricotta, and gnocchi. The gnocchi itself is delicate and not too dense. 

Finally, the fan favorite. That. Pork. Belly. Tho.

Perfectly rendered pork belly sits atop a cube of cornbread, drizzled with spiced honey and garnished with thin sliced pickled apple. This is a culinary monster. Sweet, salty, rich, acid, fattiness, starch, yaaaaaaas. I could have eaten three of these on my own. Not to say it's small, but more that I'm a bit of a fanatic for this hunk of meat. (That's what she said.)

You can't go wrong here. But you will go wrong if you don't order the pork belly.

5 Stars for exceptional sushi of all types and stellar service for a big, rowdy table!

Sue, our server, was a GEM. She took great care of us and made sure we got every order- which was a feat because everyone was ordering randomly and multiples of certain dishes. 

My favorites were the simpler dishes showcasing high quality fish, but the elaborate rolls were a table-pleaser! I would suggest folks ask about house favorites because there were a few recommended dishes that really shone as well as daily specials that were fresh takes on some of their classics.

You can't go wrong when ordering here. If you like simple- they've got you. If you like rolls with 10 ingredients- you're set. If you like bomb appetizers and side dishes- just ask Sue! It's clear the staff loves working there and she helps make the place so fun!

Overall, I've been here a few times, can rarely remember all I ate, but I always leave feeling satisfied and impressed.

I stopped coming to the Country Squire years ago at the first glimpses of decline.  Recently, I agreed to meet several families here as a central location. 

Something is clearly wrong when a diner is almost completely empty on a Friday night at 7:30 pm.  The diner opens into an alcove with an unneeded bench to wait. It is tired and dated and sets the tone.  Beware of the claw machine so every kid can get ripped off going for cheap stuffed animals. It's a sign of what's to come. 

Nothing feels clean. I inspected my utensils closely. I was cautious with the menu. I opted for snapper soup, figuring it comes from a can. They served it with sherry, which I didn't use as the stopper on the vessel was ill-fitting and caked in a sticky type substance. 

One of the teens ordered pizza. Should be simple. Except it had hair in it. I stopped at Wawa for him on the way home. It wasn't worth complaining or anything else. 

The service was good but the general sense of uncleanliness, depression, lack of freshness and lack of crowd ensures I won't return.

I use to like this place, but it is such a hit or miss when I come. 

My three friends and I came here for dim sum. We don't have a dim sum place where we live so we were super excited to eat here because I told them how it was pretty good! Of course, we ordered more than expected. We did two orders of shu mai. The first order came out and the second one never did. So before the check came out, I told the lady that we ordered two shu mai but we never got the second one and so we don't want it anymore because we are already full and wanted the check. Well next thing you know, she comes out with that second order like oh it's already made... like okay 15 mins later when we are done?! Told her that we didn't want it and she just looks at me and brought it too the back. Well she ends up just boxing it up and leaving it on the table with the check and walked away. Like how rude, just tell me that it too late and that you will have to charge me for it still, but she didn't. 

Food was okay. The prices must have gone up or something because it was ridiculous! 4 shu mai for $5.55?! 

Horrible customer service. Will not be coming back again.

I've been going to Dragon House since they opened their doors over a decade ago. Barry and Rosa, the couple that owns the restaurant, are excellent hosts. They are always hospitable, gracious, and make such an effort to get to know their customers. And the food...I'm not usually a huge fan of buffets, but this buffet is so good! Potstickers, lettuce wraps, egg drop soup, eggrolls, Cashew chicken, sweet and sour...all delicious. They offer both a lunch and dinner buffet. Lunch is 7.25 and dinner is 9.25. Great price for the selection and quality. I absolutely love this place for so many reasons, and it's obvious the rest of Fishers does too.

I was tickled pink to find this place while doing some shopping on Magazine Street. I had already consumed a lovely brunch down the way, but the thought of a deliciously smooth, silky Vietnamese coffee lured me in.

I was even more impressed that they had bottled Vietnamese coffee to go (similar to cold-brew coffee jugs), called Cafe Sua Da. It was about $8 and two full cups (though the packaging says 3, it's 16oz and I consider a full cup 8oz). I was able to enjoy one icy, creamy cup while continuing down Magazine Street and then again the next day after tracking down a cup of ice to pour the rest over. You can even bring back the bottle for a $1 off your next batch of VC.

The coffee was liquid decadence, sweet and rich!

Walking into Scott & Co. felt like a little piece of LA had followed me to Tucson. The dark, intimate bar boasted all the sexiness of LA's mixology bars but without the 'tude. The drinks were well crafted and I love the selection of tiki-looking glasses shelved discretely behind the bartender. Everyone does mason jars, but Scott & Co. is bringing tiki back!

This little wine tasting gem is located on a strip with other wine tasting options, but this one's got the most character out of the others, as evidenced by their Yelp check-in offer ("a magical high five"), quirky decor (filing cabinets hold the wine glasses behind the counter and they have commemorative mugs that say "wine" you can purchase for $7), spacious patio that often is flanked by the Burger Bus, the music selection, and the spunky staff.

A wine flight of five runs $12 or most glasses of just one varietal run about the same. Your prerogative, Bobby Brown.

Sipping wine on the patio as the sun sets on any day that ends in y is a good day.
Confirmed. It's my favorite place on the planet. Even on a Monday afternoon/evening, it's energy was infectious and the music, wine, and cheese plate were just as magical as my first visit.

It's ironic I came to support them, when they wouldn't do any necessary things to support me   Wearing a mask is not only a law for the people especially working in the restaurant, it's kindness.

What a mistake it was to go there to show kindness and support them. 

My first return visit since covid.  

The roaster would not wear his mask correctly it was down on his chin. I have multiple photos. I motion to him that it had fallen down. And he just gave me look . The staff seemed helpless. 

I asked who was in the back they the window. They said oh in the kitchen that's the boss or the owner.  He had no mask 

So if you don't care about proper hygiene and covid prevention from your food/drink establishment go here

The wait is worth it when you finally get inside to get serenaded by the kitchen staff belting out KC & JoJo. I'd have to say this is in my top five fave travel memories. 

So I mentioned there's a wait, you'll likely have a 45 min to hour wait in the sun for this hot chicken. Bring sunscreen and a water, there's no shade. 

It's an order at the counter place, you get a number, and they bring you your food. They definitely have a system down - it's a well oiled machine. 

I had the small white - breast and wing, medium heat, which left my lips tingling. The chicken was so tender and the skin was mega crispy. I grabbed their dipping sauce which is kind of like a garlic aioli. The lemonade is the most refreshing drink to pair with hot chicken. Just a hint of sweetness to counteract the lemony tart bite. I had the pimento Mac and cheese and coleslaw for my sides. The coleslaw was a crisp and refreshing contrast to the spicy chicken. Not too creamy either! The Mac was amazing. Creamy shells and little bits of pepper give it a touch of heat. 

There's a constant flow of people so we didn't have an issue grabbing a table. The outside patio was packed so we sat inside. 

Definitely a must visit if you're visiting Nashville!

There are times when you regret not getting mac and cheese as a side. This is one of them! 

I arrived in Indy for a work trip early so I took to Yelp to find a solid lunch option nearby. The fried chicken at The Eagle surely lured me in. Then, I saw photos of the grits. Oh my! 

I sat at the bar since I was a solo traveler that day. I got to glimpse some of the Sunday football games on TV at the bar and soaked up some people watching too. The place had a good Sunday afternoon crowd. I ordered the 1/4 fried chicken, grits, and coleslaw with a seltzer to sip on. The fried chicken was so juicy and tender with crisp flavorful skin. I could have eaten more! I loved the grits too - spicy with the kick from the jalapeños and oh so creamy. The coleslaw was lackluster - all around bland, which was a bummer because I love the tangy flavor paired with rich fried chicken. 

It was a lesson that reminded me to never abandon my first true love, mac and cheese. Go big or go home.

This is my kinda meal to start the day! There's nothing better than a fresh, filling smoothie. Natural Born Juicers did not disappoint. We had this for our breakfast option at a work conference so juice, smoothies, and acai bowls were the power foods we all needed to last the full day.

I had the Black Mamba smoothie (blueberry, banana, spirulina, agave, and almond milk). The almond milk makes it rich and creamy, the blueberries give it a rich purple color and the flavor actually works pretty well with almond milk. (I like to add a couple dashes of cinnamon too). The prices are crazy good here too! $7.50 for a 20oz. Not a bad way to get after fresh fruits/veggies in your day!

We had a magical team dinner here and I highly recommend crafting a pre fixe menu if you're up for the experience we had.

We had a set reservation and the table ready for us when we arrived. There were a few bottles of wine on the table for us to choose from as well as a few winter cocktails listed on our menu. I went for the red wine, which was lovely. 

The dinner was served family-style and I was so happy to start with a few cheese boards on the table, especially considering the creamery was right below us. We couldn't leave without sampled those cheeses! It was the highlight for me, mostly because I could live off cheese. Truly they make wonderful fresh and aged cheeses here and it's hard to pick a favorite, but the chevre and brie-style with honey on crusty bread are not to miss. 

After the cheese boards, we enjoyed a kale salad, then came root veggies and pork loin, followed by apple gallette for dessert. The pork loin was one of the best I've had (rarely a dish I order because it's easy to overcook). Not here! It was tender, juicy, and flavorful topped with a maitake chestnut sauce.

The space itself is beautiful! They nailed the rustic charm of building the restaurant space in a barn. Don't forget to check out the cheese aging room and the dairy bar!

Honky tonk at its finest. One of the only places worth going to on Broadway. Guitar solos that will give you goosebumps and live music performances that fulfill Nashville expectations.

There's usually a line to get in because it's popular, but it's worth the wait. I've been a couple times and both times only had to wait 30min max. If you have a couple beers elsewhere before you go, you'll barely notice the wait.

Once inside the stage is to the left in the front of the venue and bar on the right hand side. Grab a PBR (yay!) and soak in the music.

They also have food here - it was late and I was itching for 4th meal and ordered a burger and fries. Actually quite good late night bar food! Worth it!

Okay Tucson lets get a couple things straight.  I love me some coffee shops oh good golly do I love coffee shops.  I have lived in Portland and my parents live in Washington so I know great coffee shops.  First off if this is the so-called hipster young coffee shop this is sad.  I am all for artistic coffee shops but how bout clean ones?
Seriously the girls behind the counters were rude-I loved all the choices they  had for food and when I asked a question about it since it was my first time going they acted irritated because people were starting to pile up. 
Perhaps you should just answer my question and be polite.  On top of it one of the them wiped her nose and then started making my coffee....eeew!
Seriously, I wanted to like this place so much and it really bums me out to have this experience.
I seriously think that they are just playing on the fact that they are on 4th Ave because seriously that was the worst customer service that I have had in a long time.
No more Epic Cafe for me and if I do go hopefully it'll be a great experience so I can update this review.
Ugh

Okay Chocolate Iguana, I have a bone to pick with you. This past weekend my daughter, her best friend(14 year olds) and my son went to Tucson Meet Yourself.  Afterwards we decided to walk around 4th Avenue and kill some time. 
I couldn't help but notice a young couple walking down the street carrying a kitten. Seriously, I think they were only 18-19 year olds.  I watched them go up to people asking them for money.  
I offered to buy them food, I am jot one for handing out money but I am one to buy you a meal.  Right across the street was Chocolate Iguana. I told my daughter and her friend to go run over there and grab two sandwiches and a glass of milk for the kitten.  My son and I sat with the couple and waited for my them to get some food. So my daughter left with cash in her hand to go grab sandwiches.
My son and I sat for 15 minutes finally I called my daughter expecting to hear that they must be slammed. She said the food was almost ready. Just for a side note this places makes sandwiches so I made an assumption it wouldn't take too long. After that phone call we continued to sit with this couple for 20 minutes.  My daughter finally came so all together 35 minutes mind you she came with a vegetarian sandwich, a turkey sandwich, and a glass of milk with ice in it.  The sandwiches came with chips and all together was around $15.  Not too bad I thought.  The couple thanked us and we were on our way.
As soon as we were out of ear shot my daughter looked at me and said, Mom I am really upset right now.  I looked at her and thought we were about to have a teenage crisis.  So I asked her what was going on? 
She looked at me and said the girl working in Chocolate Iguana wasn't very polite to her.  
I started brushing it off and then both her and her friend explained to me the situation.
My daughter walked in and waited to order.  The girl working was talking to a guy and my daughter and her friend both confirmed they stood there for a few minutes.  The lady looked over and asked what they needed.  Not how may I help you or what brings you in, but what do you need.  Already as a mom I am starting to get worked up. What can I say I am definitely overbearing.
So she ordered the sandwiches and then they waited. While the whole time the lady spoke to the other customer in there not acknowledging my daughter again.  
She then hands the two sandwiches to my daughter and then said oh your milk.  Filled up the cup with ice and then filled it up with ice.  Strange.  My daughter and her friend felt uncomfortable in there and felt like they shouldn't be in there unless they were adults.
At first when I listened to my daughter's story I assumed she was exaggerating. 
I decided to go in and order a drink.  When I went in the gal was talking with a guy looked at me and said nothing.  I just looked around waiting for her to ask if I needed help and nothing.
Absolutely nothing it was the strangest experience I have ever had.
I then decide I should make a phone call and see if I could talk to a manager or owner.  This happened Sunday afternoon and I still haven't heard back.  It's Tuesday now.

Here is the deal my daughter was a paying customer all I am asking for is quality customer service.  Is that seriously too much to ask?  Unfortunately the food and beverages may be great but we definitely will not be back from the service we received.

I am so happy to have found this gem of a restaurant. Athena and her husband pour their heart and soul into the food that is prepared and served here. This was my first Ethiopian cuisine experience and I thoroughly enjoyed it. We started with the sambusa, one chicken and one beef. The closest thing I can compare this to is an empanada. The flavor was spicy and balanced. The crisp on the outside was perfect but there was still a little dough or softness on the inside to make it melt in your mouth. I think both the sauce and pastry provide the heat but from what I can tell jalapeños and sometimes habaneros are used for spice. I highly recommend starting with this and it comes with two per order. For our entrees we shared kitfo and chef's tibbs. Kitfo is super flavorful beef that is served raw with spices mixed in. I loved this!!! Mixing this with the different vegetables provides a different flavor experience each time you take a bite.  Chefs tibbs is a lamb dish that is so tender and perfectly prepared you just have to try it to fully understand. I loved the lemon and peppery notes. All entrees are served with veggies and ours included two types of lentils, cabbage and peas. There are so many combinations you can try so again each bite can be new and exiting or you can find your perfect bite and stick to that combination. I loved it all but I think the red lentils and cabbage were my favorite. I recommend trying the lager (beer) they offer as it was light and refreshing. We ended the meal with freshly prepared coffee. They do not have a coffee machine or use store bought. In fact, they roast their own beans and grind it daily. It is always fresh, bold and so strong!! Athena takes hers with two spoons of sugar so I tried it that way and it was perfectly sweet and a wonderful way to end a delicious meal. I can't wait to return and try a seafood option as my entree!

Mediocre at best. Went there last night around 5:45 assuming it would be no more than a two hour wait. They told us it would be an hour and a half but we didn't get seated till 8:30. Our pizza didn't come till 10. We were so hungry by then that we just wanted to eat and go home as soon as possible.

I understand that they just opened and are still working out the kinks. Sure, that's fine! The pizza wasn't amazing though. The crust on the bottom was thin, dry, and flavorless. It was just like a regular pizza but the tomato sauce and cheese were on top rather than on the bottom, and all veggies and meat were underneath the sauce. Nothing special at all! 

After spending $30.25 on a large mediocre pizza (bill with one appetizer and one cider came out to $50) and waiting almost 4 and a half hours, I was pretty darn disappointed.

Edit: After showing my fiancé pictures of the original Giordanno's pizza, he said that there was probably only a quarter pound of cheese on our pizza rather than FOUR. For real, we got jibbed.

Okay, im gonna keep it real - we all know why we all come here.

My advise, come at night. the courtyard is truly pretty. I love checking out the lights and the waterfountain. That being said, the hurricanes are not my fave in the city by far. However, check if the dueling piano bar is open - thats an awesome time, but watch yourself - it gets SUPER packed. Service is always good here, the staff was super nice!

*They tend to run out of the Eggo  waffle buns  often*

* free Yuengling when you check in *

I decided to throw away 1.5 years of not eating chicken to try the appetizer version of the chicken sliders with blue cheese topping, on a waffle fry bun. They were great and tasty for about $8 the waffle fry bun is awesome, perfect bite size bun ever. however, the chicken was dry, i think they need to drown the chicken in the blue cheese dressing. Seafood burger was on point also according to my friend.

The gaspacho is disgusting and made my stomach feel like it was doing flips


Really cool decor and a unique soundtrack going on up in this place. Staff was friendly, but kinda slow.

Lord where do i begin. 

I have been told about Mothers for awhile now, and ever got the chance to go after all the times ive been to NOLA. recently alot of people warned me its not the same, its kinda over rated. they were right.

i loved the home, cafeteria style of the place. no thrills here, just come an eat and find yourself a table.

however, the bloody marys were the worst ive ever had. i dont think there was any liquor in them and they were so syrupy, tasted more like thick tomatoe soup. i was just so let down, they were so sad and a pretty steep price too. The shrimp poboy wasnt much better. shrimp needed to be fried more, barely any fixings on it, and the breading was kinda soggy. my friend got the breakfast platter and i tried her grits. no flavor, grits were hard, and just no effort. the rest of the plate was meat based, which i dont eat, but lets just say she took 2 spoon fools and stopped. she was not happy.  my other 2 friends were kinda let down about their meals too.

we waited a good 25 mins to get served, it sucks because this is a legend but i just was not impressed at all....

This restaurant is in the uptown garden district. The area is beautiful. Upscale residential New Orleans for sure. The setting inside was really nice with high ceilings and good wine selections. 

The servers were very polite and professional. Enjoyed my first time eating a crawfish bisque. Very nice tasting appetizer. They also have a fresh oyster bar so that should definitely be an option for anyone wanting fresh oyster.

The strip steak looked really good but I went with the grilled white fish with vegetable medley. It was very good. Fluffy, light, healthy, and flavorful dish. For vacationers I would recommend a day on the trolleys to look at the amazing houses that are in the area, and before leaving cap off the night at this fine seafood restaurant.

No sorbet when I visited which is what I was really looking for, but ended up settling on Italian chocolate chip gelato.

The girls that worked here were nice, however the woman that I think was the owner was pretty rude and not nice to her employees which was a turn off.

The gelato itself was decent...nothing to write home about, but the waffle cone was yummy.

Two one scoop gelatos in waffle cones is going to set you back about $12 bucks.

I honestly can't even begin to describe how cool this place is, but I'll try. They have the biggest game collection I've ever seen, the staff/owners are super-friendly, the decor matches the setting perfectly, and the drink selection is astounding. They even have a very diverse non-alcoholic drink menu for those of us that don't drink a ton. And if that wasn't enough, they occasionally work with local creators to display their work for sale, which can be a huge help to independent artists. 

The only issue I have (if it can even be called that) is that it's occasionally packed and table space can be sparse. It's awesome to see the community embrace these fine folks though, so I don't begrudge them for being busy. 

All the owners ask for is that you be cool, be over 21, and play nice with others and you've got yourself a seat at their table. Reno is lucky to have this place here in town.

Stumbled upon Philly Cupcake on the way back to Patco after the Auto Show.   Loved the decor and the staff was very inviting!  They had so many choices, I didn't know what to pick.  I finally narrowed it down to chocolate Reese's peanut butter cup.  Delicious!  I'm looking forward to trying another flavor.  My only gripes are the price,  $3-$4 per cupcake, and there was no place to sit and enjoy my delicious dessert.

We have dined at Flemings on a couple different occasions and been pleased, but this time was a huge disappointment.  
My son graduated college last weekend so we chose Flemings because we thought it would be a great place for our special occasion.  We had a party of eight and had reservations two months in advance.  
They ended up being very busy and our table was in the middle of everything, this wasn't a big deal but not the quiet and more private dining experience we'd been used to there.
We sat there for quite some time before we were greeted and given water.  When our waiter (name was Toby) finally showed up he was cold, a smart aleck,  and condescending to us.  
We ordered wine, got through our soup and salads, and sat thirsty waiting for our water and soda refills.  We kept hearing "Sorry, the bread is in the oven".  I'm sorry but with this level of dining the service should be impeccable!!!  When the steaks came my son's steak (he had ordered medium rare) was overcooked.  He cut into it and told them it was overcooked.  The waiter and the guy who delivered his steak then proceeded to stand there and argue with him about the doneness of his steak.  It was obvious to everyone the steak was overcooked.  My son cut into it a couple more times to show them.  The waiter then told my son "Well, we can send it back for you, but I'm going to be honest and let you know it's going to be a long time before you get it back because we're so busy."  My son's Grandpa finally offered to trade steaks with him, since his steak was more rare.  The waiter also made some comment "thirsty much?" about my teenage boys' soda and water glasses needing to be refilled too often as though it was a bother. The tackiness of this waiter was ridiculous!   I just sat there in disbelief at how bad the service was in comparison to our previous visits where the service was very good, and regretful that we chose Flemings for this very special occasion. 
So, 90 minutes later we left, nearly $800 spent and sorely, sorely disappointed. 
I would give 2.5 stars if I could, but I feel as though 3 stars (A-Ok) is way too generous for this experience.

Nothing beats Lee's Deli regardless of dine-in or take-out! Their Asian fusion cuisine straight up slaps and would look no where else for cheesesteaks. Their staff are professional and take cleanliness very seriously, which I very much appreciated. Fries, sandwiches, cheesesteaks, wing dings, dessert, you name it and they do it phenomenally! 

I've been more than a dozen times with family and friends and they've all loved it just as much!

Upscale Mexican inspired restaurant in an up and coming area of Franklin! Nice spot for family dinner outings as it has tons of cozy booths, family friendly staff and music. There is also a cute coffee shop and custard joint across the plaza you can enjoy after dinner if you make it before 9 pm. Tito's has tons of parking, a menu with unlimited options, and portions that will have you in a food coma minutes after completion.

We came out on a weekday evening around 7:30 pm and had no wait time. Our waitress immediately brought us chips and salsa, and replenished them after we quickly chowed down. Careful, the mild salsa is really tasty and you will fill up on chips if you stuff your face with them immediately. By the time it came to order food I had changed my order from the spinach enchiladas to the guacamole salad because I wasn't as hungry anymore. The salad was still ridiculously filling with it's fresh guac, loads of crunchy green peppers, chopped tomatoes, and refreshing ice berg lettuce. I would definitely order again and I can't wait to come back for those spinach enchiladas.

My fam split the chicken fajitas which came on a large cast iron with tons of veggies, tortillas, chicken strips, and toppings. They said they get it every time because the variety is high quality and the portion is unbeatable. We all had to get to-go boxes there was so much food on the table. The waitress gave us another bag of chips to-go with a large container of salsa, as well. We were not only full until lunch the next day but also had left overs to replenish us at that time. 

All in all this is definitely a modernized, Mexican "influenced" style restaurant with an amazing variety of options. I would definitely recommend trying (on an empty stomach) and will be back again when I'm in town to try those spinach enchiladas.

If you're reading this in debate on whether to attend dinner here this evening, grab a drink with a friend, or treat yourself to a delectable post dinner sweet treat, read no further - Just Do It. Trust me, you WILL love it!

It's said that the coach is the backbone of the team and without a strong coach your team will not prosper. The same thing goes in a restaurant - Without a strong owner or manager the restaurant will not be a success. Ruben and his team totally kill it! Their genuine hospitality is indisputable and the professionalism that is displayed cannot compare with majority of restaurants in the area. I would come back just to be served by such an kind and knowledgable staff who make you feel so at home!

On top of that, though, their cuisine is far beyond magnificent. There is truly something for everyone made with (mostly Organic) farm fresh, local ingredients that pack each dish with unique, crisp flavoring you will be ranting about to all your family and friends. At times, I couldn't even comprehend what I was chewing but my taste buds were on a rocket ship journey to another universe. 

My guest and I had the abundant privilege of tasting a wide variety of items both on and off the menu during our visit. Each one carefully described in great detail and presented as a work of art. The best part? Well the taste of course! However, the affordable pricing for such fine dinning blew me away as well. I will go more into detail in describing each item on their image descriptions as I don't want to scare anyone away from the longevity of my review. 

Yet, I do want to touch on the favorites real quick! My guest thoroughly enjoyed the Beef Bone Morrow Bruschetta with its savory diversification of flavor and perfectly sturdy texture. He also mentioned he would come back with his buddies just to even sit at the bar and enjoy one of their 52 selection of craft beers, and munch on either the White Marinated Anchovies or Pommes Frites (Curry Fries). For more info on their beers and snacks check out the Black Sheep Happy Hour menu, accommodating guests from 5 - 6 pm 6 days a week.

My favorite thing I had at the Black Sheep was surprisingly enough my drink! Reuben suggested and served me this charcoal, kombucha styled beer that made me feel so surreal I can't even begin to describe it. I felt like I had downed one of those $45 gut elixir mixers that helps digestion and creates healthy bacteria in your body, but was also nicely buzzed. Being as health conscious as I am, I very much enjoyed this style of brew and in complementing him on it he suggested four others they have in the back just like it! I was astonished!! You can get healthy drunk at this restaurant, totally guilt free, and without breaking the bank. I don't know why everyone doesn't come here for happy hour. Alongside the drink I utterly enjoyed the delicate pork dumplings dipped in a piquant orange sauce - Coming Soon to a menu near you!

My guest and I had a 10/5 star experience at The Black Sheep and we know you will too! From the mystery of the name, the maturity of the staff, the ambiance of the environment, the convenient location right next to the Ortega/Anacapa parking garage (great for handicap), accommodating rooms for business meetings or large family parties, Happy Hour specials, and both vegan and vegetarian options this restaurant is truly suitably pleasuring for anyone and everyone. 

Thank you for everything Ruben and you can count on me visiting again very soon!

Endless Summer is one of the top dinner locations I suggest whenever I have family, friends, and other Yelpers visiting in town. It it right on the harbor so you can check out the boats, see some sea life, and enjoy the ocean views. The decor is insanely representational of Santa Barbara culture. And the food options are well diverse, somewhat affordable, and extremely delicious. 

I have been coming here for years, but my most recent visit was the best and most memorable of them all. My housemates and I stopped by for dinner and drinks on the night of my birthday and it was packed. While wait staff were running around frantically helping all the guests the hostess was trying to touch base with all them while also cleaning newly vacant tables and seating guests, we thought maybe another restaurant would be a better choice. After maybe 90 seconds of standing there, though, the hostess ran up to us and kindly offered to seat us right then apologizing for the chaos.

We got our seats, grabbed some popcorn while we waited, ordered drinks and food, and went to play pool on the deck while our food was being made. Pool did cost a little bit but with the free popcorn and decently priced Happy Hour drinks it was well worth the experience. The sunset over the water was gorgeous and we were loving the active crowd. 

About 25 minutes later we hear our names over the loud speaker and find out we have to go pick up our food at the window.. not sure if it is always like this, because we were not at our table, or it was super busy but none the less we picked it up and went to our seats no problem. I ordered the Seafood Louie Salad and it was probably the best/biggest salad I have ever had. I am not a Huge seafood person either but I was won over by this one for sure.

After we finished we grabbed boxes because their portions are so generous and then they came out with a massive mud pie topped with lit candles for my birthday surprise dessert. Best. Birthday. Dessert. Ever. It was massive too! Our table went to town on it thanking our waitress over and over again. The bill came shortly after and full tummies we stumbled out saying many thanks to all the hard working staff.

That's just one of the many situations here where the staff have been over worked yet extremely kind and on the ball. The food is always delicious as well and the portions will have you full for days. If you're not looking for a meal, come here Happy Hour and enjoy the harbor views. I'll definitely be back for that soon!

So if you haven't noticed I've been checking in here a lot lately. I'm a firm nonbeliever in first impressions and would like to give Breakfast a star bump up as they have definitely grown on me in the recent. 

The environment is so great for dialing in and getting work done, outside or inside. The ping pong table aspect is also pretty hip and groovy if you're bold enough to step up to the challenge. 

The positives lie at- Having plenty of seating, bike racks, Handlebar coffee, a pristinely clean environment, and ridiculously fast public wifi. The somewhat grandiloquent staff/crowd and lack of breakfast food items definitely still linger in the negative but I can work past it.

Would love it if Breakfast had a weekly tradition of some sort like ping pong and tacos night or open mic nights, etc. Something to bring the young and the restless community together!

This is my boyfriend's favorite place in Santa Barbara so to say the least, I've been here quite a few times! We've tried just about everything but his favorite is hands down the Goodland.. It's hard to argue with a burger that has onion rings in it! My favorite would have to be the classic Mesa burger with cheese and no onions. Although the Sandspit with no olives is a close second.

I'm not normally a fries person (I know it's weird) but if I substitute the regular fries with the truffle fries here I will eat the entire serving. They also offer sweet potato fries or onion rings that I hear normal people really love. One time we were feelin' extra saucy and ordered "The Pit," which is a never ending plate of fries topped like nachos with burger patty, cheese, chili, lettuce, salsa, you name it! It was definitely fun for the taste buds but would only recommend with a large group of people and not eating too much if you have a sensitive stomach - Oh boy!

The parking lot here is really tiny but somehow always seems to have spots open. If not, there's street parking as well and a big Lazy Acres shopping center parking lot across the street. The service is Very kind and honestly one of the top reasons I love coming here. They have tv's going with sports events and surf competitions, heaters outside on the patio, bar like seating outside as well, and spacious indoor seating.

It's a great family spot to grab a beer and a burger, or maybe a salad for the ladies and an affordable kid's meal for the kiddos while they play with the colorful wax bendy straws they'll get in line. Would make a nice date spot too if she loves burgers, the salads are good but pretty average for the price. 

Milkshakes are unfortunately not my favorite.. I had thought they used McConnell's for them like they do for their dessert scoops however after trying 3 or 4 of them I can 100% tell you they're either watered down or using a different ice cream as they are way too icy and lacking flavor for it to be fully McConnell's. Would love to try a Beer Float one day though!

I will definitely be back many times in the future because I love their staff, it's a great location, their burgers are yummy and I really believe in this local business. Annnddd my boyfriend is obsessed for life so there's no getting rid of us!

Killebrew is a cute little coffee shop with great aesthetic and a total Instagrammy vibe located in the oh so popular area of Nash called "The Gulch."

A couple colleagues and I met here for coffee one week day morning and it was packed. The Gulch is really up and coming right now so I expected nothing less, plus it's reassuring to know so many people love the place you're about to try. While waiting in line I had the privilege of being able to observe their food and merch items. They had everything from sparkling water and chocolate milks to cute branded coffee mugs, hats, and signs. 

When I got to the ordering counter my once decided order had changed now that I could see all the amazing fresh pastries they make in house there. I ended up going with an iced soy latte, banana, and a blueberry muffin (see pictures for awesome presentation). I'm not a huge soy person, allergic to almonds and try to stay away from dairy for my health (so high maintenance, I know) so I always hope coffee shops have Oat, hemp or cashew milk but unfortunately this cafe didn't have those as of yet. I know it's a not the most average thing to aspire so trust me I'm not too bitter, but I would love to see this place get one of those options as they're so unique, delicious, healthy and the perfect mixture with espresso.

My soy latte was pretty good though for soy milk and gave me a nice buzz that didn't overwhelm me or cause heart burn aftermath. The combo of my order items were the perfect breakfast and my only "complaint" would be that the muffin was a little crumbly and hard to eat properly at a professional meeting. I would definitely love to come back here and try more of their pastries, work inside on my laptop with the awesome aesthetic vibe, and explore more of the Gulch with all its new shops and murals.

Killebrew does have wifi, I believe I saw a couple outlets in there, there's indoor and outdoor seating, multiple free timed parking lots close by, tons of murals and boutiques, and the famous Angel Wings mural by Kelsey Montague is across the street! Check this coffee shop and this entire area out, it's got good vibes.

Unfortunately I don't have much good to say about RoCo. I've given it so many chances over the past few years and it always seems to let me down. 

For starters, their coffee & espresso always tastes burnt! I've had lattes, straight espresso shots, & even drip coffee here & every time it tastes over roasted & like it's been sitting out for days. 

I even mentioned this to the gal working & asked what she may recommend that wouldn't taste so cooked. She, sadly, had no idea what most of the coffees taste like & as kind as she was, was very unhelpful. 

It's so sad to me because the brand, logo, location, & shop decor are all so trendy & fun. Yet the actual products themselves I wouldn't recommend to my worst enemy. It's also very sad how bad of a reputation the company has as far as employee turnover rate and lack of brand education. 

I would love to give RoCo another shot sometime in the future but for now I will not be stopping by again to drop a crazy amount of money on bad coffee.

Green Table has been a family go to for years. They pretty much have something for everyone. Their drinks and meals are all Organic, and most are Gluten Free and/or Vegan. Not a big fan of any of that? They've got award winning mac and cheese (made with real cheese) that will blow your mind. Locally sourced and freshly made, really their options fit just about anyone's preferences. 

When they first opened, Green Table was known for their almond milk matcha specials. I'm allergic to almonds so I cannot review these, but I do believe, as of Fall 2019, they carry coconut milk as a substitute. A favorite amongst my friends is the Salted Mocha Ice Blended Matcha. My drink of choice here is the Skinny G which has spinach, kale, parsley, celery, cucumber and lemon. You can add shots and/or protein to your juices, as well. Their drinks are definitely on the pricier side but pretty standard for fresh Organic juices in Santa Barbara, between $7-11.

Food wise, I try to get something different every time but our family favorite has always been the lasagne made with mushrooms, eggplant, spinach and house made pesto in combination with marinara sauce. Most recently I tried the Cauliflower Crust which was two circular patties of cauliflower and cheese baked together and topped with avocado, tomatoes and eggs sunny side up. It was such a great flavor combo and I'd love to learn to make this myself. 

Green Table has inside and outside seating for 1-5 people. Would recommend dining in for small groups only. Their current Axxess deal is Buy One Smoothie, Matcha or Matcha Special, Get One Free. And their 2020 Axxess deal is Buy One Smoothie or Matcha Special, Get One 50% Off. There's some street parking out front and a parking garage on Chapala right passed Paseo Nuevo which is Free for 75 min. Nice little lunch spot, would recommend trying at least once!

"Good things come to those who wait." Don't be intimidated by the line, it's there for a reason! 

Handlebar Roasters will go down in history for me as the best coffee in SB. It is everything I want in a latte; rich, creamy espresso with a hint of chocolatey background and warm tones of woodsiness released in the breathe after ingesting. Not too acidic, yet strong in it's caffeine presence. Sensually aromatic, yet doesn't make you smell like an artificial candle after ingesting and/or leaving the premises. 

It mixes well with regular, soy, and (my personal preference) oat milk. It tastes good in all forms, my recommendations being the regular iced latte and the affogato. It gives you the perfect buzz for a healthy amount of time. And it roasts well at home when you buy their bags of beans to go. 

This Handlebar location has matcha, chai, charcoal, and turmeric lattes, as well. They also carry a wide variety of cold salads, avocado toast, chocolate croissants, bagels, cookies, artisanal donuts, almond croissants, and so much more. Breakfast is served until 2 pm (or as supplies last) and sometimes they have theme nights with craft local chefs coming in and serving things like ramen and tacos. 

This location is a lot bigger than the downtown location, though there are no outlets to plug in. Just charge up the laptop in advance and come enjoy the strong wifi, vast amount of seating options indoor and out, and delicious espresso + loaded avo toast. Heck, you can even grab a beer and work here, as this location has select beers on tap. Stay tuned for exclusive flavor releases!

There is a small private lot right next to the coffee shop, tons of street parking on or near De La Vina, and the Presto Pasta shopping center lot right next door if you're just popping in for a quick bite/drink. The owners are very sweet and almost always on site. Their staff have the brightest smiles and do a great job at getting all the orders done in good time and with great quality. I have never had a bad experience here and I can't wait to see what they come up with next!

There is sauce in the crust and the customer service is comically unique! That's what makes this spot different from the other pizza joints in Isla Vista. 

I've been posting up here with friends on Tuesday nights for their weekly Trivia Night festivities and during those visits have tried the pineapple/pepperoni pizza, strawberry topped cinnabread, and the vegan pizza with Daiya and loaded veggies. All were good, not great, but good and definitely did the job. Would recommend the cinnabread over everything, hands down.

The Trivia Nights themselves are very long and loud, but the questions are somewhat doable and the crowd is fun and lively. Teams are big and there are a lot of them, so if you are serious about winning and "fair odds" I'd maybe head to another spot. The guy that runs it is hilarious and definitely knows how to work the crowd. Stop by at least once and check it out!

As far as the pizza and the shop itself, I would not come just for my leisure. Would probably recommend Pizza My Heart or Dominos if you're looking for the best quality pizza for your buck in Isla Vista! But for a beer with friends, some trivia, and a cinnabread you can't really go wrong here every once and a while.

A Ralph's is a Ralph's is a Ralph's.. So let me tell you a little bit about this location specifically. 

I come here quite often for healthy cereals, organic green packaged smoothies on the go, bananas, ice cream, and holiday themed items. They have a massive selection of holiday themed items right in the front left section next to Starbucks and their prices are usually pretty great! Would definitely recommend check them out for at least ideas - They beat out the dollar store 9/10 holidays. 

The Ralph's brand foods are generally the most affordable and often come in Organic and Gluten Free options. My favorite are their cereals which are around 2.99 most often and beat out the prices of all the stores around town! 

The environment here is a little strange and you can really witness all walks of life at any time of day. I wouldn't say it's not safe but I also wouldn't advise letting your children run around by themselves throughout the store or parking lot.

They have a two level free parking lot for customers, which is very rare for Santa Barbara and definitely helpful when it comes to deciding where the best grocery to get in and out of quick will be. It's also located right across the street from the bus station, so if that's how you get around it's very convenient. 

The staff here are pretty typical grocery store staff. Not the nicest people in the world and don't know a ton about their products but they get the lines moving. I have done a lot of business with the floral and balloons department which doesn't have assigned staff so finding people to help is a little consuming and a small struggle but in the end it usually works out.

I will definitely be visiting often while I live so close and have my cereal, green smoothie, baking, and seasonal goody desires due to convenience and price preferences.

Two words: California Burrito! Where are my foodies at? They've got the OG french fries in a burrito combo here! Just stop reading now and head over to get one. 

On a serious note, what keeps me coming back here is the incredibly sweet customer service I have experienced every single time I am in shop. They deal with my silly replacement requests and adding extra cheese all the time without a bat of the eye, and not even charging sometimes. They're always smiling and on top of it, making the orders quicker than most places I've been and never having messed up one of my alterations. 

My favorite menu items here i would 100% recommend everyone trying are the #18 Breakfast Burrito, the Super Shrimp Plate, and the Diet Burrito with extra cheese. All are incredibly packed with flavor and reasonably priced, especially for the fact that it feeds me for two meals because the portions are so large. 

They have a large parking lot, are located next to the best frozen yogurt place in town (Loving Spoonful), have more options than you can ever imagine, are extremely kind, work very quick, have a popsicle fridge, and a self serve salsa bar! Also, would recommend following them on Instagram @supercucasrestaraunt so you can participate in their giveaways for free burritos and gift cards and other goodies.

*Only thing I would change is to add a queserito option to their burrito menu!

Pizza My Heart is a good stop for a very large slice of pizza with endless toppings and seasoning additions. The vibe inside is very lively and surfer themed! Staff are bubbly and tv's are blasting sports, surfing, news etc. every time I've visited. 

The pizzas are generally thin crust style (which I prefer), kind of greasy, stacked with cool toppings, not insanely fresh but definitely tasty, and come in a wide variety - anything from pesto to pineapple and ham. Slices range from $4.25 - $5.25 and small pizzas start at $13 for cheese but average cost is $16. 

At this location they have one of those fancy soda machines where you can basically add any flavor to any soda combination. Their drink sizes are plentiful and they do provide water cups upon request. I've never had a salad here and I've really never seen anyone order a salad here because they're so darn expensive.

Overall it's a cool place to hangout with friends, get a booth, grab some pizza slices and beer, and watch the surf or a game. I wouldn't recommend it to families looking to feed all their kids and such after a beach day, however, because it will break the bank and not totally fill everyone up.

I've always been a fan of the Caje brand in town! In college I would study at Caje in IV and sip Handlebar Coffee (when they had them), eat Acai bowls when I was too hungover for real food, and take IG photos on the wave wall. Look how far we've both come! New Caje is a fancy craft coffee bar who roasts their own beans and they turn into a "secret" speakeasy bar at night. And I've since graduated and been able to use that degree I studied for to get a good job, and afford the fancy coffees and cocktails they provide! 

New Caje is located adjacent to The Mill on Haley St. with timed street parking all around. There's tons of cozy seating for individuals and groups alike, outlets, strong wifi and great working vibes. You can order your average coffee drinks or spice it up with affordable boujee coffee cocktails. I generally get their regular coffee (which is fantastic) but this time around I tried the Twist drink. It's made with "double-strength" cold brew, which is funny because there's so little in there it really equivalates to a regular cold brew caffeine effect. They add lemonade, coconut milk foam and raspberry ice cubes to the cold brew and top it with a fruit slice (possibly charred blood orange). It was very refreshing and tasty but not practical for a work day because of the low caffeine content (and price). 

The staff here are so nice and well-versed when it comes to anything coffee. I asked them for a light-medium roast from a specific region and they went in the back to dig out the most fresh batch of what I was looking for. I was so grateful and impressed! It's rare to find fancy coffee bar like this with both delicious coffee and kind service. You can tell the staff's hearts are in it! I'd recommend trying this place out not just for the tasty, picture-worthy coffee drinks but also for the great environment and good vibes.

Have you ever pulled up somewhere and just immediately fell in love with it? Or maybe watched a movie that had been highly recommended to you over a long period of time and it was actually as great as everyone had previously advised? That was my first impression of Lucky Llama Coffee.

For years I had heard about this awesome coffee shop in Carpinteria that everyone loved to go to for meetings, study sessions, guitar jams, family outings, etc. and I had not gotten around to trying it. I am happy to announce that just a few months ago I tried the well built up cafe for the first time and automatically fell head over heels.

Like a newb, I parked on the street the first time, not realizing there is a nice open dirt lot in the back. I walked up the dirt road watching children run around in the grass, laughing and playing while the adults sipped their coffee and had their own little chats. I walked in the door and the staff were also laughing and conversing with each other, but almost immediately reached out to welcome me and ask if I had any questions. It was the happiest, most welcoming vibe I have ever felt at a cafe. 

I quickly reviewed the menu and was automatically lured into the creativity of "The Mullet." To this day that "Mullet" was one of the greatest forms of liquid to ever have tingled my taste buds. I have ordered many drinks here since and all have been charming, but if you're in search of something unique that gives you that perfect caffeine buzz, my friends, "The Mullet" will prevail! 

Amongst the happy atmosphere, spacious parking, vast succulent beauty, friendly staff, quick wifi, and dainty coffee drinks this cafe also serves acai and breakfast bowls, along with fresh pastries delivered each morning. I was not a huge fan of the banana chocolate muffin as it was hard, dry, and somewhat bland, but their bagels and scones have worked well for me in the past.

I also wanted to point out they no longer have "Castle Roasters" but instead carry "Dune Roasters" as their signature beans. You can also find trendy Dune and Lucky Llama branded accessories and apparel in shop. Love those white thermos bottles! 

You will definitely be seeing me back in shop here quite often. Would love to see Lucky Llama start a weekly tradition like open mic night or jam circle at the stump again.

Two Words: Vodka Lemonade

Really I should stop there.. Seven's strawberry and/or cucumber vodka lemonades are reasonably priced and ridiculously delicious for how buzzed you get it. It's actually dangerous! 

The rest of the cocktails on the menu are very pricey for me but they do suffice in the alcohol content ratio of things. The one I would not recommend is the Bad and Boujee - I was feeling extra spunky but that drink put me right in my place. There was nothing tasty about that one. Would've rather taken shots. 

The staff here are always super busy as this place is always packed but they try to keep things in order. I wouldn't say they're over the top nice but they make your drinks in a timely manner. The security guys are my favorite; they smile and are nice to people who don't give them trouble. 

A lot of people rave about the food here, particularly the brunch! While I've never had their brunch or the Mac Daddy (see menu for details) I couldn't see myself paying that much for drinks and food combined. One day I may try the Mac.. 

The bar is located in the Funk Zone outskirts so parking is primarily where you can find it on the streets, but with drinks being so strong I'd recommend Ubering. Try it out - Especially if you're visiting and want a cool bar scene with strong flavorful drinks.

This is such a beautiful addition to the northern region of lower State St. The interior, as you walk in, is just breathtaking, with everything from the light fixtures to the tiles on the floor being imported from Turkey. The staff are very friendly and greet you instantly upon arrival. They know their products and their service like the back of their hands and can answer any questions on the spot. 

Amazed at the beauty of the artisanal Turkish delight rolls in the display cases, it took me a while to narrow down which one I wanted to try. All of them look so beautifully delicious but I had to go with the banana chocolate to accompany my "bitter coffee." To clarify, there are 3 Turkish coffee options: the coffee with mastic (which was the owner's personal favorite), the hazelnut blend, and the standard Turkish which is best for those who like it bitter and black, with natural flavor. It was delicious and paired well with the very sweet, banana dessert. Oh and make sure to Google Turkish coffee fortune telling, if you want the ultimate cultural experience - shoutout to the Yelp SB CA, Richie D, for brightening my horizons with this knowledge!  

Lokum does offer Wifi and outlets for those looking for a nice classy spot to plug in at. I wouldn't suggest coming on an empty stomach as they don't offer any meal options, but they make for the perfect dessert and coffee spot, post meal indulgence. I was a little sad at how tiny the Turkish coffee portions were, as I love the flavor of coffee and would have enjoyed sipping on it a lot longer. However, I understand and respect their unique, cultural ways of serving Turkish coffee. If you're curious about the difference, just ask, they'd love to give you the full low-down and would do a lot better job than I could. The coffee was served with two little Turkish delight squares and a cup of water. 

If you're looking for a unique gift for dinner parties, holidays, birthdays, etc, Lokum has a custom gift box option where you can mix and match baklavas and Turkish delights. I love how on the gift boxes they give a little history and background info about the desserts. The cost varies per item additions with baklavas being an average of $4-5 a piece. Though I cannot recall the exact pricing of everything, I believe the Turkish delight prices varied per size and roll, but I do know they're definitely not cheap. 

Not a coffee person? They offer hot tea, as well! There are a couple vegan options for those who have no preference against honey. Want to make Turkish coffee or tea at home? They have all the pots and kettles, teas and beans you could ever want, all available for purchase and all imported from Turkey. I highly recommend trying Lokum! Great for dates, dessert outings, Instagram posts, working remote, and just trying something new. I will definitely be back to try more turkish delight flavors next time I'm around.

Was in Philly visiting a friend and catching the Duchamps at the Philly Museum. Had Sunday brunch at Fork, and it was quite outstanding. The staff was solicitous and warm, and the ambience is conducive to good talk. While the crowd was more blue-haired than hip, the interior look of Fork is more updated and artsy. And the food..... from the butternut squash soup to the smoked pumpkin tortolini to the lightly fried halibut and chips, great care went into the preparation and presentation of each item we sampled. Even the kale salad, which might have been expected to be boring, was brought to life with creme fraiche and sourdough chips. Dessert? Think spicy fig ice cream with Madagascar chocolate cake, which tasted even better than it sounds. A nice wine list rounds out one of the best bruch experiences i've had in a long time.

This is the ONLY fine dining option in St. Charles and it is much needed. As a food snob who lives in St. Charles under protest, I really appreciate their menu- locally sourced, carefully curated, and lovingly executed. Everything I had was phenomenal and the service was unparalleled. This restaurant is on par with St. Louis city peer restaurants like Blood and Sand, Farmhaus, and Five Bistro. It's about time St. Charles got something like it. This is not a cheap meal but rest assured- it is worth every penny. 

If you are a culinary adventurous person who is willing to give some new dishes a try, definitely stop by and enjoy.

Great customer service from our server and owner, each time we go. Their pad thai is one of the best in town, and their mango and sweet rice? Delicious! You won't be disappointed if you choose to try this place out. Been going here with family since they opened This has even been my place of choice when people ask me where I want them to take me for a birthday meal! Try the crab puffs, are another great option!

After hearing great things from the people I went with and from other friends, I was excited to try this place. 

It is a pretty small restaurant, and when we arrived there were only two other groups there. Oscar (who was friendly) showed us to our seats and handed us the menus. He took our drink orders and then came back for our dinner orders. My drink was flat the first time it came out and I think the syrup machine was broken. It tasted as though someone had dumped grenadine into my diet soda. He brought out another, that was carbonated but still SUPER sweet. I just put it to the side and stuck with my water. 

We ordered clams and the blue cheese breadsticks to start. I wasn't a huge fan of the clams, but my father seemed pleased with them. I did like the bread. I'd never had blue cheese baked onto bread before, it was pretty good. Unfortunately the night went from 'okay' to 'ugh' so quickly. My sister and father's food came out... they ordered the clams with pasta and the pork chop with winter mash. I had to wait for my mushroom tortellini, no big deal. He assured me it would be out soon. He came by the table three more times to tell me it would be out shortly. My sister and father finished eating by the time my food reached the table. They obviously forgot to make mine. It wouldn't have been a big deal but the food was awful. I had to add a ton of salt to it. The 'creamy' sauce was watery and the mushrooms were undercooked. I picked out some of the tortellini and let my father and sister pick at the rest of it. For $17 dollars this was a super disappointing dish. 

Save yourself some money and time and go somewhere else. 
I should also mention that they never came to refill our waters. My dad had to finally ask when he came to bring the check.

ODE TO A CHOCOLATE CHIP COOKIE DOUGH CUPCAKE

I'm a cookie dough addict, straight up. Chocolate chip cookie dough ice cream is a staple in my diet. 

That said, just as I was about to go on lunch break today, Sweetbox uploaded this picture of the most beautiful black, white, and tan thing I've ever laid eyes on. http://instagr.am/p/Lfz_jBmbsd/ Without even reading the description, I bolted to Love Park.

Fast forward 20 minutes, and I'm back at work, patiently (NOT AT ALL) eating my sandwich while gazing at the beauteous cupcake (because I'm a lady, and ladies wolf down our main courses before digging into dessert.) I begin by separating the top from the bottom, as is my custom. I take a tentative taste of the icing--vanilla. I then try the cake--also vanilla. I start to feel a little cheated--is this just a vanilla/vanilla cupcake with some chocolate chips thrown on top and a cute little cookie garnish? A little disappointed, I finish up the bottom part and move on to the top. Then, I note something under the top. It's mushy, tan, with black chips...

OMG FOR THE LOVE OF ALL THAT GOOD AND CHOCOLATEY--THERE'S A BIG GLOB OF COOKIE DOUGH WEDGED IN THE CUPCAKE.

I don't understand how it's possible. Wouldn't it bake in the oven? DOES THIS NOT VIOLATE ONE OR ALL OF EINSTEIN'S THEORIES?!?! Oh, who cares, because the fact is there is gooey cookie dough, of the same ilk as that which you dipped your fingers into when your mother wasn't watching and hoped to whatever holy baking entity you worship that you didn't get salmonella from. Not the fake stuff that you find in chocolate chip cookie dough ice cream (though as mentioned previously, that doesn't stop me from eating it.) No, this is REAL COOKIE DOUGH. IN A CUPCAKE.

MIND = BLOWN.

Don't get me wrong, Lovin' Spoonfuls has some of the best vegan food in Tucson. Their portions are adequate for the cost of the food and everything appears to have had close attention paid to it. The (mock) BBQ-beef sandwich is fantastic and all the sides are great. 

BUT

The owner of the establishment is one of the most awkward and awful women I've ever encountered. At least once a week I think to myself how I want to go to Lovin' Spoonfuls but choose another restaurant to avoid the owner. She's always there, she's usually rude, and she always makes me feel uneasy. My friends have told me stories of her going up to their tables and asking why they weren't eating specific parts of their dish. Almost every single person I know has the same opinion. It's unfortunate, but it's reality. Lovin Spoonfuls food is great, and their owner is a trip straight down Awkward Avenue.

New Orleans had many amazing brunch places, but as far as taste goes, this place was my absolute favorite!
The food: 5 stars it was filled with so much unique NOLA flavor, it was delicious. 
Service and wait time on the other hand: got them the 4 stars. No reservations and their wait time was over an hour. The workers were rude as hell and seemed like they wanted to strangle each of us to death and throw us across the street in the surrounding cemeteries.. or maybe keep us and make Lovett pies with our body parts (shoutout to Helena Bonham Carter)! 
The workers had absolutely no patience for us mere humans there. They gave us each about 3.5 seconds to order with the deadliest glares. So I chose quick.. and my life was spared. Lol
It's a tiny little cafe, the size of a box. It's not boujie in the least.. (which is what I normally prefer for my brunch eats lol). but the amount of customers they get in and out comes to show how good the food is.  
 I ordered pancakes!!! And the Montana platter which came with 2 eggs, sausage gravy biscuits and grits. I have to say I've never been more impressed. Everything was divine. That sausage gravy was absolutely AMAZING!!! I think that's one of the great things I'll forever remember New Orleans for. All the savory foods mixed together were heavenly. I highly suggest everyone tries this place!!! Try the biscuits and sausage gravy for sure!!!

I did a debut visit here with a group of 5 other friends of mine whom does Sunday brunch almost every week at a new place none of us have been before. I picked this place since I been buy many times and always wanted to go. At last we did!

1030am we got in and good thing as we got in line and ordered our meals from menu within 10 minutes. By 11am and after the line was 20 deep but they did keep it moving it seems.

I got the avocado toast with added bacon and that bacon is crack people! Get it at all costs. 

My dinning partners got items from pancakes, biscuits and gravy and daily quiche and it all looked really freaking good let me say that much.

Get there before 11am as it picks up really quickly. The portions are average but the quality is well above that. Very cool setting as a shop and restaurant all in one. I need to come back and try lunch or dinner now as well to compare that.

Outside: Divey Strip Mall
Inside: Hipster Chic
Food: Locally Sourced Breakfast Goodness
Service: Fast and Friendly
Price: Breakfast ~$10 Coffee ~$3 Smoothie ~$6

Yolklore serves delicious food with a focus on locally sourced products and it shows in their creative and flavorful dishes.

I found lots of options for people with dietary restrictions. My wife is a vegetarian and I do not eat pork yet we can both find something to love at Yolklore.

Their smashed potatoes are a great take on normal breakfast home fries. The fresh baked biscuits and ciabatta bread that they serve with their meals are extraordinary. 
Their smoothies are delicious - if pricey.
The coffee is good but nothing special in my opinion.

Every time we have been in here, the service has been fast and friendly. And that is no small part of the reason we keep coming back despite this place being a little more expensive than your average greasy spoon diner.

Though to be fair, it really ins't a good comparison. You are going to get great food here, locally sourced, served on compostable trays and you are always going to get it with a smile.  Most of the time, that is worth a couple extra bucks to me.

The owner would rather text her husband on her phone than help seat you at her mediocre-at-best restaurant.  Don't bother with this place when there are far better options, and their owners take pride in their product and service.

For the food, I'll give them a 4, but for their ethics, I will squeak out a 1. We had a funeral luncheon there. Everyone was pleased with their meals. We offered our guests wine, which we were paying by the carafe. The server poured the wine as though she was filling water glasses. When I asked if that is the typical wine pour, we were told no. Hmmm, that should have been the first red flag. The servers then went around and asked the guests if they would like coffee. Ok, coffee was included in the price per head. Oh wait, no it isn't. Coffee is only included AFTER the meal. So, $30 for coffee. Alright, it's been a tough emotional day, so let's not worry about the small stuff. When I was given the bill, 5% was added since I was paying by credit card. Ok, that's their policy. Although, a little steep since most credit card companies only charge 3%. So, I signed the credit card slip and we headed home. When I looked at the itemized receipt afterwards I saw that the gratuity that had been added was over 29% at $134.25 on a $456.15 bill! I called the restaurant and spoke with one of the owners, Jim that informed me that since our number of guests that we actually had was 7 lower than what we had estimated they needed to "make it worth their servers' time". He apologized that it hadn't been explained to us and I accepted the explanation and got off the phone. Giving it some more thought, I figured out what the bill would have been had we indeed had the 7 additional guests and even with that could not come close to their calculations. Best I could come up with was $120.
Regardless of how good the food is/was there, I can't in good conscience return to a place that I feel takes advantage of those at a time when they are at their lowest. Thanks Charlotte's, hope it was worth the couple extra bucks.

Stopped in for some shots just kidding I mean slots. My husband and I parked in the garage without an issue finding a spot.

Due to the 'rona they do a walk thru temp scan so it moves pretty fast. Upon entering the casino you walk into the non smoking section. However, honestly the separation of smoking and non doesn't really work well. The casino may want to invest in a better circulation system.

Overall I was not impressed with the casino. There was no new member free play, the slots were super tight, and way overcrowded.

Couldn't be happier that Chatime has opened in Tucson! They use real, fresh tea. I love being able to customize my sugar level--It makes me feel like I can go back more often. And we've already been there an embarrassing number of times. We have tried:

matcha milk tea with red bean and coconut jelly, 100% sweet
Chatime milk tea with red bean and boba, 50% sweet
oolong milk tea with pudding, 50% sweet
