roasted milk tea with grass jelly 50% sweet (my new favorite)
tieguanyin tea mousse, 100% sweet

I also had a 50% sweet matcha milk tea with just red bean once, which ended up being much sweeter than the 100% version I'd tried earlier. Maybe because it had more red bean? 

Everything we've tried has been great. (My partner didn't love the mousse on her tieguanyin tea, but she did like the tea portion of it. I liked the whole thing.)

Wi-fi, generous frequent buyer cards--we've gotten a free one already--and room to hang out and play a board game. 

They seem to still be tinkering with the menu, and they have been out of things when we've visited--mostly the add-ins. But that's to be expected with a new business.

My wife is pretty obsessed with Mission Taco. She takes any chance she has to suggest this as a destination for dinner. We have been to all of the locations in St. Louis. They all have similar high quality tacos. My favorite is the chorizo. I sometimes get the burrito, but without fail when I do I regret not just getting tacos. The chips and salsa (or guac) are great. The mixed drinks are also solid if you are in the mood.

The one negative for this location is that it is in Soulard. I like Soulard in theory, but then get annoyed with the lack of parking any time I'm actually down there. If you are in the area, then by all means go to Mission Taco. Otherwise I'd only go here in off times. Also make sure you look to check in online. The wait can spike during busy times. Avoid the lines.

When my wife and I first started dating she lived in Maplewood just a few blocks away from Side Project. At first it was just a quirky bar. It is in a modest building, and set just far enough Sutton that you can easily pass it by. Inside there are two bars and a handful of tables. It closes relatively early, so it never quite takes on the more rambunctious atmosphere you get at other bars. The always have a large selection of beers, particularly sour beers. I rarely look at the menu. I typically just ask one of the helpful bartenders for their suggestion given what type of beer I'd like. 

We have very much enjoyed going to Side Project Cellar over the years. The only negatives are that it closes early and there is not a ton of room. This is the sort of place where you go with one other person or perhaps a group of four. It is not an ideal stop with a large group. Go with a good friend, have a beverage, and just chill out for a couple hours. I'd also recommend checking out their brewery which is only a few blocks away.

Took a short weekend trip to SB, I was looking forward to ending the day with a delicious meal.... unfortunately things did not end well. For a restaurant with such good reviews and was recommended by so many, I was extremely underwhelmed. 

The combination of ingredients in their dishes just don't pair well in my opinion. My tastebuds were confused and not happy 

Saddest part of my night- the A5 wagyu was as chewy as a piece of ribeye. They should not advertise this as wagyu, nothin tender about it. 

I'm still upset we wasted our night out at the Lark.

This is a casual Asian-fusion restaurant that pairs it's Vietnamese cuisine with hints of Creole and Cajun cuisine which were born out of the melting pot that is New Orleans. I started out with their wings and they were excellent, and they were so good I almost ordered another to take home with me. The only item I did not care for was the Fresh Vietnamese Spring Roll and it was huge. I took two to three bites and I just was not enjoying it at all. I usually do not care for this style of spring roll, but when presented with traditional ones that are smaller and crunchier and that do not have a lot of sauce inside them, I can usually eat them without any complaints. Sadly this was not the case here. My next dish was a Shrimp Maque Choux and it was phenomenal. I also ended up ordering as an add-on two Crispy Pork Spring Rolls and these were definitely more to my liking. They have a good wine list and great food. My server was nice and accommodating. Highly recommend.
The food was horrible. Service was slow. Which is a shame because the atmosphere inside is pretty cool.

I do proclaim that Jack's Donuts are the best donuts in Indianapolis... and dare I say it.. the world!! 

Yes, I do love Jack's Donuts and have since I was two years old and began eating solid foods.  This shop started in my hometown of New Castle and luckily for everyone else, has begun franchising throughout the Indy metro area. 

I made a special trip from SoBro all the way to Carmel, just because I was craving my favorite caramel nut donut.  Did not disappoint. These donuts are gigantic and delicious. The donut itself has cinnamon swirls inside it and then when topped with the caramel icing, something truly magical happens. 

I like the interior of this Jack's too.  It's spacious, good selection of coffee and large amount of swag. I informed my boyfriend that he may purchase me a Jack's Donut t-shirt for my bday and I'll wear it around with pride. 

Anyway, to end my long-winded rant about Jack's Donuts... it's delicious. It is incomparable. If you haven't went yet, drop everything you're doing and go there now!

Amazing find!
The atmosphere kept us all night.

Group of 10, 2 servers and a party table right off the stage near open air.

It was upcoming song writers night and the 3 acts we saw were really good.

Good menu selection.

More than we expected!

Everything I loved about the Truckee location but right here in Reno!!! I can't believe it took me so long to stop in! The turkey day on Parmesan oregano bread is my favorite, it's equivalent to 3 sandwiches for $9, the soups are all fantastic as well. My only complaint is the hours because they are only open Monday through Friday until 3, if they could add on Saturday I would be so happy! Staff is friendly and attentive as most restaurants in Reno are but, the way go about learning your name and making sure your daily made bread is still available before placing your order is a cut above other sandwich shops. It's above and beyond what Subway or even Capriotti's can do because it's small town love of food and the perfect sandwich

Great find! Really enjoyed our meal. Our server, Liz made great food and beer recommendations. The hot chicken was delicious and the bacon Mac and cheese and bourbon sweet potatoes were terrific. Fun local beer menu! We'll be back!

This is the first time I have ever experienced Sabrina's, and now I know why! Came here before my friends and I did a scavenger hunt in the city, so we needed to fuel up! I heard this place can have a lengthy wait, but our party arrived at 9:30, and we had no problem in scoring a booth.  The restaurant was almost full to capacity, with the crowd enjoying their brunch.  

Major heat wave was in effect, so I wanted to get something healthy but filling.  While perusing over the menu, I ordered some coffee to start. Thank goodness for large cups! The menu had some great items, but I really looked at the brunch specials for something unique.  First off, the names of their specials are very entertaining to read! Very creative! I decided on the Dr. Octagon "First come, first served" omelet which showcased goat cheese, broccoli, and tomato. Cool. It came with potatoes and your choice of white or wheat toast. 

Food came out pretty fast! It's best to come extremely hungry because the plate is completely covered by your meal. And the plate is super large! (Or at least I thought so!) My omelet was good, especially with hot sauce. It wasn't spectacular, but enough for me to leave stuffed and satisfied.

If I'm in this area again, I'd come back. I'm a huge brunch fan, so I'll keep this on my list!

If there is anything that I love more than love itself, it is PIZZA. A really good pie does wonders for the soul and while it cannot cure cancer, it can certainly resolve those hunger pangs! A few girls and I decided to meet up for diner after work, and I was pretty excited since I have heard so many good things about this place!

Since it was a nice day, we sat outside. I ordered the Post Road, while the others decided to wash down pizza goodness with wine. We ordered the pizza of the day which was a slice of roasted pear, thyme, mozz, and gorgonzola with a dash of honey. That slice was seriously good, and I could have eaten a whole pie of that. But I didn't because we had ordered two pies and the arugula salad. (We were really hungry). The Renato was a simple, yet tasty trifecta of rosemary, olive oil, and sea salt. The Salsiccia was made with some serious love. Fennel sausage, tomato, and mozz. Lastly, the arugula salad! I really enjoyed this! Hearty potatoes married well with the pesto sauce.

I will always remember this dinner, and cannot wait to go back.

Viet just opened a few months ago and the locals were raving about the amazing food so I had to peep the scene for myself.  

The restaurant was surrounded by an Asian grocery store and two other restaurants in small strip mall. Walking in I noticed the chic decor and trendy furniture. It was rather small, but not overwhelmingly cramped.

The menu wasn't very extensive but as soon as I saw  the whole snapper I had to get it. I love to tackle a whole fish! (The cheeks are the best and most tender part of the fish)

The snapper came to the table Piping hot, extra crispy and delicious. It was displayed on top of a bed of fresh iceberg lettuce, tomatoes with a side of ginger scallion sauce. Loved it! Next time I'm in Tampa, it's going down again!

My husband and I had a great time here tonight. I usually don't care if service is good or bad because I go to restaurants for the food quality, but this place had notably great service. Our server was a great guy that was attentive but not overbearing. 

Food: 
Pickled vegetables- complimentary and refreshing. Nothing special. 

Pork riblet: Yummy. It was similar to "Kara-age", a type of Japanese fried chicken where the batter is very crispy and flavorful. If you like pork belly, you should definitely try it. I asked for a side of lime to balance out the oil. I recommend trying it with the lime. 

Yum woon sen talay/Cold bean noodle salad: It's a spicy fish sauce noodle dish with shrimp, lemongrass, onions, and celery. It was nice to have this since the rest of the meal was on the heavier side. I would have liked more variety in my seafood, but it was still good. 

Kua kling/ground beef: This is ground beef flavored with spices and sauces. It's a dry dish so don't expect a saucy dish. Husband liked this. 

Gaeng kiew/green curry: Very different from other green curries i have had. Probably my favorite dish of the night and my favorite green curry ever. It also has Thai eggplant which was sweet and a different texture from the usual eggplant. My husband hates eggplants but was able to enjoy this. 

Halo halo (dessert): jackfruit, corn, and jelly in coconut milk. This was so good! I don't even know how to explain this but it's creamy, the right amount of sweet, and delicious. I did not want to share it. Definitely try it!

Overall, we will come back to try more dishes. But I know we will get the green curry and halo halo again.

This place is, frankly, great.  I don't mean just great for a bar in a train station- for that, it's fantastic.  But it's great for anywhere.  The beer list, which is always changing, is wonderful.  If you only want bud light or high life, this isn't the place for you.  If you want to try lots of different great beers, with good advice from the staff, this is your place.  The food is also great.  Again, not great for train station food, but great full-stop.  The prices are low, too.  The food is interesting, often changing, and very nice.  I'm a bit of a snob about food, and won't, for example, eat anything at Penn Station in NYC and will barely eat at Union Station in DC, but I'm happy to get dinner at this place all the time.  The service is also good- I've mostly been in the evening, but the servers are always friend, knowledgeable, and honest with their advice on beer and food.  Service is fast, too, as it needs to be at a station.  It's worth a stop, whether your in the station for a train or just on its own.  Great.

Updated- recently, while back in philadelphia I went to bridgwater's again.  The menu has changed somewhat but is still interesting and good, and the food and beer are still great.  I was sad to learn (apparently) that the place no longer takes part in the United Mileage Plus dining program, as that was another big attraction for me, but it's still a very nice place to get a meal and a beer.

Im from New York and so I've always wanted to try a Philly Cheesesteak but in the end, im upset this was my first Philly cheesesteak experience because it was TERRIBLEEEE. I wish I had looked this place up before I got it cause it was so bad. The cheese wasnt even melted and it literally tasted like nothing. I dont get why people even buy this. IT LITERALLY WAS SOOOO BLANDDDD. I wish i had keptchup or ANYTHING to give this sandwich some flavor. I literally took one bite and stopped eating it. Complete waste of $10. Only pro of this place is that it is open late but NEVER AGAIN.

My brother wanted me to bring him back a philly cheesesteak so I ended up going across the street to Pats and the cheesesteak looked SOOO much better and my brother said it was delicious. 

DONT GO HERE. Cross the street and go to petes and save yourself some money

I wanted to try this place for a while, but was never downtown with time for a tapas style dinner. I had high hopes for an excellent dinner out. First, the food is over priced. Two scallops for $15?  I really wanted excellent scallops and these were perfect, but the risotto was so under done it was crunchy. Dish ruined. The brussel sprouts were excellent, as was my mojito, both pricey for what they were.  The tri tip special had potential, but very small and didn't have any nice char. Dinner was about $50 before tip and very disappointing. I didn't bother with dessert. The wait staff was like a roller coaster with some good and some bad moments. The chef yelled at someone in the kitchen because she knocked over something someone put in the wrong place. The bartender was good, but pricing and size of beverage poor. I paid my check, tipped my wait staff and left.

The owner pays for positive Yelp reviews and proudly advertises this by offering a coupon and membership into his five star club. That's not going to work on me. Excellent food, valuable dinning experience and professional staff are how to get my stars. I expected a high end experience all around and this disappointed. Will not eat here again and will not recommend eating here to anyone.

I decided to take a chance on Iztaccihuatl (for takeout) on a lazy weekday evening while craving Mexican food. I ordered the Enchipotladas which were surprising spicy but a good size and came with a nice complement of rice and beans. My fiance ordered the Tacos Al Pastor which she also enjoyed. We also ordered a side of tortillas and guacamole and the serving size of guac. is enormous. I'm not quite sure how they could even make a profit while serving such a large portion of guac. for under $7.

The delivery was dropped off prior to the estimated time and the quality was comparable to eat in (still hot and together). 

A great meal for evenings when you don't feel like like changing out of your sweatpants.

Having grown up in Mexico for large parts of my childhood, my expectations of mexican food are quite high. That being said, when I first moved to St. Louis I had been deprived of any real mexican food for 4 years while exiled in Detroit. 

When I first arrived I searched, questioned, begged and pleaded for people to send me in the direction of a traditional mexican taco. None of this chain crap, pico de gallo, make believe tex-mex.  I was directed to (a not yet discovered) cherokee district. After all of these years I have not felt the need to search any father.

I only order the tacos here because on the streets in mexico, that's all you get. This is why I come here, for mexican street food. It is 100% authentic. 100% cost equivalent. 100% the last mexican food joint I will ever need in St. Louis.

A friend of mine and I once went through the entire menu of a Taco Truck (which is were you get the good ones in CA) when we were in high school. She told me, eat it and then ask what it is. That way you are never afraid to eat the best part of the animal.

I 100% subscribe to that philosophy today and suggest that you do to. You won't be sorry you did.

NOT A REVIEW FOR THE CLUB
Came to Brew Brothers because the boyfriend and I wanted to sit down, stuff our faces and watch the Pacquiao fight. That was the plan, SO WE THOUGHT.

Our friend had asked a bartender about where the fight will be shown, the bartender replied every bar/ any restaurant that has a TV will be showing the fight. Boy, was that person wrong. =X I'll get back to that later.

OH MY, I'M..I'M IMPRESSED
We were seated after 10-15 minutes of waiting, not too bad for a Saturday evening. When we walked in I was impressed by the HUGE bar, and the brewery, which you can see right behind the bar/ through the window. Very nice! TVs are hanging EVERYWHERE, no matter where you turn your head, you'll always have a TV in front of you. 

FOOD
We ordered pizza and onion rings, both were very average tasting. I didn't see anything else on the menu that caught my eye. =T 

SERVICE
Service was a bit slow, I noticed the waitress rarely came by to check on us (TOOK A LONG TIME TO GET OUR BILL/  TAKE OUR BILL) and it took awhile for the food to come out. Both are things that annoy the crap out of me, the slow service more than the long wait for the food. 

YOU GUYS AREN'T WHAT??
After the final game of the Celtics vs Heat game was over, the boyfriend and I was wondering when they were going to turn on the Pacquiao fight (the main fight didn't start but there were other fights going on). So we flag down a waitress because our's was nowhere in sight to ask, and GUESS WHAT. THEY AREN'T SHOWING THE FIGHT!! WTF, REALLY?? You're playing all these other sports on your very MANY TVs, and you're NOT going to show a Pacquiao fight? So, the boyfriend and I quickly get off our chairs to make our way down to the casino to see if they're showing the fight (and thankfully the casino had the fight playing on every TV).

CONCLUSION
The food wasn't bad, the service was slow and they weren't showing the fight (which really erked me). BUT their bar area, the where ever you turn your head there'll be a TV in front of you and the brewery hanging out in the back, impressed me. So 3 stars, though I was very close to giving Brew Brothers a 2. =X

NO WONDER WHY THE LINE FOR THIS PLACE WAS SO FREAKIN' LONG!!          ((BOTTOMLESS MIMOSAS))

DARK CIRCLES AND SCREAMING STOMACHS
After a long night, we woke up tired and hungry. The BF suggested Sterlings for brunch and after checking out the reviews on Yelp, I quickly agreed! When we got here, low and behold, there was a freakin' line. We waited for a good 20-30 minutes until we got to the front of the line! Too bad the waitress who came out to the line to serve mimosas didn't come out earlier, it would have made waiting a little less painful!

DON'T MIND IF I DO
Best brunch I've had, hands down! They lay out your typical breakfast foods, eggs, bacon, sausages, bread, fresh fruits, and they have an omelette station (yes, someone will be making that for you). Then they lay out foods you'd be eating for lunch and/or dinner! Cheese & crackers, oysters, shrimp, king crab legs, sushi, beef, lamb, chicken and more! 

THERE'S ALWAYS ROOM FOR DESSERT
Want dessert for breakfast? Shoot, WHY NOT? Help yourself to their dessert station, chocolate covered strawberries, creme brulee, ice cream and like I said before, AND MORE!

CONCLUSION
5 STARS!!!!! I'll be back someday, hopefully that someday is soon! =X

This is a really cool wine bar in the funk zone. They have outdoor seating and indoor which is nice. We went there on a Sunday and there wasn't many people so it was nice. We got the rose and sparkling flights. Both were really good. The pours were healthy. We also got the cupcake flight. It was delicious. The staff was a little slow and busy talking with each other. I don't need the staff to be checking in on us every minute but a little attention is good. Overall highly recommend!

Avoid at all costs. This place was such a disappointment. We came for a nice anniversary dinner. We got the shrimp cocktail and the double eagle prime rib.  We ended up throwing up all night and the next day. What type of place serves spoiled shrimp? I called to complain and no one has responded from the business. What a terrible awful experience.

Wow, what has happened to the Brown Boxer. Always a must stop when I visit Clearwater, but it has changed. I came here in June and I noticed it just wasn't the same. Decided to try it again in December and nope.

Honestly, I'm quite bummed because I love the huge open air bar, people watching, and sports bar feel. It just seems the clientele has changed and the service and food along with it.  

Too many other options on the beach.

Simply outstanding, the best restaurant on the beach.  Gorgeous decor with an awesome view of the sunset.  Professional and knowledgeable staff that have never failed to make the perfect recommendation.

They make the best cocktails and the wine list is wonderful. They always have quite a few of my favorites and their price point on wines is very reasonable. In terms of their food I love the Mussels Arrabbiata and Bruschetta for appetizers.  For entrees I have tried the Gulf Coast Cioppino,  Rigatoni Bolognese, and Chicken Piccata.  All delicious!

Easily, my new favorite restaurant on Clearwater Beach and a must stop each time I visit.

Is it touristy?  You bet, but it's also damn good.

We ordered The Ferdi Special and Shrimp po'boy with 2 sides (fries and red beans and rice) and 2 cold ones.  The sides are oh well..sides.  The sandwiches were delicious and you can't go wrong with either one.  We absolutely love the bread and it puts the sandwiches over the top.

Super friendly folks working here that have no problem working a massive crowd. They have a great system moving people in and out so don't be deterred when you see the line out the door.

NEVER! NEVER! NEVER! EVER! EVER AGAIN!!! How dare you Parx???
So let me paint you a picture. My man and I were celebrating our anniversary the entire 4 day weekend of 4th of July. We came back from the shore a day early and wanted to continue the good times, so we came up with Parx. Now, it's 2 oclock on a Saturday afternoon on a holiday weekend. No one is in town. Also, it was about 95 degrees. I had the top off the Wrangler and we were a lil sweaty to say the least. When we pulled up into the parking lot, it was pretty empty as you can imagine. At this point the Boo mentions he's wearing flip flops and asks me if I think it will be a problem. I say "Hell no, look at the clientele". As we were discussing, a size 16 woman was walking by wearing a size 2 outfit, one guy looked like he just changed his oil, and a group of elderly folks around the age of 100 were flocking from their bus trip. I say "They should pay us to be here today". We go on with our journey for fun with a pocket full of ducketts and a positive attitude. 

We were starving. So the plan was identify a place to eat, get some cocktails and gamble. So, when we walked thru the glass doors, we immediately made a right to look at the info board to pick a restaurant. We decide, and start to walk. This is when I was treated so poorly, I just stood there with my mouth hanging open. 

So the "Greeter" a bitter, middle aged woman, with a power trip and a clear case of hatin, stops me and says "Excuse me, we don't let men walk around like that, so I can't let you". I'm like WHAA??? I don't understand. Looking confused she goes on to say "Men arent allowed to have their underwear out, either can you". Still shocked I said "my underwear isn't sticking out". She says "I know, but the back of your shirt is folded up, you need to fix that before going in". She uses a tone so accusatory, I felt like I was some street walker coming to Parx to peddle my goods.

Here, being sweaty, the bottom of my shirt flipped up, showing about a half inch of skin. No underwear, no ass crack, nothing. Just a tiny piece of skin at the bottom of my back.  And let me say, I was wearing a full length, to the floor, maxi skirt, white sleeveless shirt, and fancy flip flops. Nothing slutty about it. But I was made to feel slutty. On a holiday weekend. When business was scarce. Before I got to spend a dime. Thank Jebus for little favors.

Without speaking, the Boo and I just turned around and walked out. Went thru the door feeling like an ass. What did I do to deserve that?

After this, we drive across the street to Carabbas. We were so hungry at this point. We walk in and the hostess says "I love your skirt"! We just bust out laughing. We explained what just happened, and they were horrified. 

Since the incident, I sent Parx customer service an email explaining what happened and I included a picture of what I was wearing, front and back view. That was July 6th. I have yet to be acknowledged. Boooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooo, Parx. You stink!

My husband and I had been wanting to try Fire By the Monon for awhile, and when we finally had a perfect patio weather evening to take the dogs out for dinner we jumped on the opportunity. 

We went at prime dinner hours and were told it would be about a 45 minute wait, but only waited about 15 minutes before we were seated in the designated "dog patio" area. After trying just about every dog friendly-patio in Broad Ripple, I'll go out on a limb and say that Fire By the Monon is THE most dog-friendly restaurant here. Our waiter, Bradley, gave both dogs heaps of attention every time he came over which is bound to win over any dog owner. He also brought the dogs out an "appetizer plate" of milkbones which obviously was loved by the dogs and also kept them occupied while we looked at the menu. 

We started off with the Dirty Mac which was what drew us there in the first place, and it was incredible! VERY filling to split just between two as an appetizer, but I'm tempted to just order that as my entree next time we go!

If the dogs weren't already loving life, just prior to bringing out entrees out Bradley brought them each a giant Milkbone on a plate. Again, super appreciated by both the dogs and us as we were able to eat our meals with them occupied! I ordered the Bella Burger which was great, especially if you love Sundried tomatoes. My husband ordered the Tug of War and really enjoyed it. Neither of us were able to finish after inhaling the Dirty Mac, but my Bella Burger was still delicious as leftovers the next day. I also highly recommend getting the onion rings as your side!

Fantastic location, fantastic service, fantastic food. Can't ask for more!

Rattle ya dags and make your way to Burgerfuel! 
(How'd you like my Kiwi slang?)

The first thing you should know is that my friends and I have claimed this as "our spot" for the summer.  Burgerfuel is absolutely everything you could want in a Broad Ripple restaurant.  If you google "Burgerfuel", you'll end up with "burger restaurant" for your result, and that's just about as true as calling Dante a writer, Michaelangelo a sculptor, or Bruno Mars a singer (I like Bruno, hush it! LOL).  

Food is fuel, and Burgerfuel has it in delightful abundance.  From custom burgers to veggie patties, gluten free options to alcoholic shakes (Yay!) they've covered all the bases.  I'm particularly partial to the Kumara (sweet potato) fries, dipped in aioli.  Basically think of all the yums that ever yummed in yummville, and you'll have the deliciousness which is those fries.  I also sampled the motobites, which are a vegetarian's dream, and a wonderfully good chicken sandwich.  

The restaurant is located right off of the strip, near the BR fire station.  I actually love that location, because that means that free parking is just a few blocks away.  The back patio is sure to become a destination for the "cool kids" that call BR their second home.  Throw in a little cornhole, and a custom graffiti piece, and it's a hipster's dream.  If you're not so hip, go anyway, the Burgerfuel Kiwis (New Zealanders) will welcome you with open arms!

Cajun, but not Crazy (Hey there, Yats!)

I happened upon Borel's because an acquaintance of mine works there.  I'm always up for a new spot in Indy, so I thought I'd give it a try; I found myself pleasantly surprised.

Borel's has many of the Cajun mainstays that one expects from shrimp po' boys to everybody's favorite, Jambalaya.  I had the Cajun Chicken Pasta and was quite pleased.

There was ample seating and the restaurant itself was quite clean and pleasant.  I could definitely see myself and a group of friends taking over the place for the evening (hint, hint fellow YELP ELITE) ;-).

My one complaint for Borel's is that they don't have many menu options for non-beef/pork eaters like myself, and I imagine my vegetarian friends would leave with empty bellies and disappointed taste buds.  I'd love to see Borel's expand their menu options to include a few vegetarian options.  That could be the boost they need for that elusive fifth star!

Update: Visit #2 was just as good as the first, if not better. Got the scallop ceviche again, still excellent...the oysters, salad and gnocchi were equally enjoyable. The roasted chicken was the highlight, one of the very few places I'd order chicken regularly. And I will definitely be returning to this place on a regular basis.

My fairly high expectations were definitely exceeded this past Friday night. They've really done an amazing job transforming the old space. Our waiter went above and beyond to ensure a good dining experience, drinks were ridiculous and most importantly the food was delicious. 

The scallop ceviche, escargot and beef tartare were a pretty perfect way to start. Finished with the lobster bucatini and grilled shrimp, some of the best shrimp I've ever had...the lobster bucatini was good, but it was the least memorable thing we had. And anytime I can end an excellent meal with a citywide, I'm a very happy man. Looking forward to going back and trying the rest of the menu.

An excellent shop with extremely helpful owners.  Lindy has helped me every time i've been in and she is really friendly and enthusiastic about what their store brings to to average home cook or professional chef.

To me, the ability to buy spices by the ounce rather than having to buy a huge bottle that you may only use once, is extremely valuable.  Also knowing that the spices are fresh, only stored for a limited time, and any old spices are donated to the high school cooking classes to use, is amazing.

I've only tried a selection of their spices, salts, and peppers, but I intend on venturing into their teas the next trip in.

I hope this shop does extremely well and feel that it adds to Reno's charm and making it a foodie destination.  Thanks Lindy!

What a treat for breakfast or brunch.  I'm a big fan of crepes and their savory and sweet selection is an excellent mix.  On the last trip we sat outside so we could have our pooch with us. (They are dog friendly and even offered to bring out a bowl with water. (HUGE bonus points!)

I ordered the Los Caballeros (3 crepes) for $9.99 - (Eggs, bacon, ham, black beans, and cheddar cheese.) and you always get your choice of fruit or salad.  I also wanted to have a sweet finish and ordered the German for $6.99 - (Delicate crepes with lemon butter and powdered sugar) to share with the table. Their french press coffee is a must for only $3.00. (The hardest part is having to wait for the five minutes until you can depress the plunger and enjoy the coffee.) 

The service is friendly and attentive. (My water glass never ran out and we even ordered a 2nd french press.)

For the quality, price, and service, Creme is truly a jewel in the Midtown area and worth the trip if you live in other areas of Reno.

A few warnings before you go:
1 - Come here hungry
2 - Do not be on a diet
3 - Only order a whole sandwich if you are sharing or just finished a marathon.

My go to sandwich is the Dom Pastrami on their garlic cheese roll and add horseradish.  It is so good!  I had one just yesterday and paired it with their lemonade (not too sweet and a great thirst quencher!)

I've ready the other reviews and have NEVER had a bad experience or a "rude" owner.  This is a gem within Reno and I really enjoy going here.

I've been to Beachbum Berry's Latitude 29 before and had an enjoyable experience. Since we were in the area we decided to stop in for a drink and a small bite.

Opened in 2014 by Tiki expert Jeff "Beachbum" Berry, Latitude 29 is a great tropical get away featuring exotic drinks, tiki atmosphere, and PolynAsian cuisine. The diverse drink menu centers around Tiki inspired drinks and historic cocktails.

We sat at the bar where the lovely Natasha greeted us. She was very friendly and helpful and took the time to answer our questions about certain drink ingredients. I decided on the T.N.T. Swizzle and mom chose the Vodka Mai Tai. Both drinks were delicious. I really liked Natasha's attention to detail. All the drinks she prepared were beautifully presented with fantastic garnishes. We also ordered the Pork Ribs and the Thin Cut Fries with kimchi ketchup and Sriracha Mayo. Mom loves the ribs (she's had them before). She said they were tender and juicy with the right amount of sauce. The fries were perfectly cooked and seasoned. The dipping sauces were the perfect accompaniment.

In addition to the fabulous décor, the place has a great vibe and atmosphere. It's a nice little escape from the hustle and bustle of the Quarter.

It was Sunday evening in NOLA, which means a visit to Muriel's was necessary. A. to see the lovely Nicole and B. For my favorite NOLA cocktail - the Honey Child.  Most of the time I stop by to see Nicole, have my Honey Child, and some of their yummy house made bread but tonight dinner was in order. 
While waiting for our drinks Nicole brought us a little lagniappe. It was crunchy bits of fried shrimp on a bed of butter lettuce. The perfect starter. Light and tasty. 
In addition to amazing drinks the food here is also outstanding. The wood grilled filet with parmesan scalloped potatoes, grilled asparagus, roasted mushrooms, and a creole mustard red wine demi-glace blew me away! Hello! Talk about decadent in a good way. The filet was buttery and cooked to perfection. The sauce was amazing and the potatoes were so flavorful. 
When people ask me where they should go for a meal in the French Quarter Muriel's is always on the list. It's a beautiful place to have a meal, the staff are very friendly. Food and drinks are on point and the bartender Nicole is one of the sweetest gals in town.

I'll admit, I have my favorite spots that I always hit up when I'm in NOLA. Now, I'm committed to trying at least one new place each time I visit. I'm a bit sad that I never had a meal at Tujague's original location. However, I've had drinks at its historic bar a few times and even had famed mixologist Paul Gustings' improved Grasshopper which is considered the best amongst his peers and I must agree. Supposedly, the drink was invented at Tujague's in 1918 by Philip Guichet. He created it for a cocktail competition in New York where it won 2nd place. Paul put his own unique spin on it when he took over bar duties. (F.Y.I. Paul is no longer at Tujague's.) 

Founded in 1856 Tujague's (pronounced Two Jacks) is the second oldest restaurant in New Orleans. The establishment relocated in 2020 because it lost its lease. Unfortunately, the owner couldn't take the historic bar (America's oldest stand-up bar) or it's iconic sign with him. I was told that the bar was too fragile for the move and the sign was so old that if they tried to move it, it would most likely disintegrate.

Upon arrival we were greeted by a delightful hostess. She asked if we had reservations, I told her we did not. She said not to worry and checked to see if there was availability. She then escorted us to the elevator and told us someone would meet us upstairs to seat us.

On the way, I noticed how beautiful the new bar area was. There were also chairs at the bar, so people could sit and converse or enjoy some food. The room that we were seated in for brunch was lovely. I liked the bright flowers on the wall, which reminded me of a Mardi Gras Float. There were also other Mardi Gras themed decorations around the room.

Our waiter was Randy, and he was very friendly. He informed us of the specials and took our order. We had the $5 martini (vodka or gin), which is a special during brunch (be sure to specify the $5 martini when ordering). The bread arrived in a bag with the restaurant's logo. It was warm, crisp on the outside, and fluffy inside. I had the Tujague's House Salad with a side of biscuits and mom ordered the Hot Honey Chicken Biscuit. The biscuits came with a side of honey. They were big, soft, and fluffy. The salad was mixed field greens with baby tomatoes, cucumber, shaved red onions, and parmesan. It came with a sugar cane vinaigrette, which I asked for on the side. With the parmesan and shaved red onion the salad had a nice flavor on its own. However, the vinaigrette did enhance it.  Mom isn't a fan of spicy, so she asked for the hot honey sauce on the side, which was a mixture of Crystal hot sauce and honey. She said the coating on the chicken was crispy and had a nice taste but agreed that Randy was right and the sandwich would be better with the sauce on it. Her fries were delicious - perfectly seasoned. I dipped some in the honey hot sauce, which I thought was great. For dessert we had the Crème brûlée and another round of martinis since they were $5. The burnt sugar crust on the Crème brûlée was perfect and the inside was creamy.

On our way out I stopped by the bar to take a photo where I met their fabulous bartender - Angelica Sky. She had such a friendly, outgoing personality. Loved her! I'll have to come back and sit at the bar so I can watch her in action and have a conversation. I'm glad I stopped by.

This is the best Chinese food I have had in the greater NOLA area. The kung pao chicken was a great size for the price and spicy but also flavorful. The chicken was high quality, and my order was hot and ready in 15 minutes despite the restaurant being packed. I can't wait to try some other dishes from here the next time I'm in the area.

Ate there Tue night for the first time and it will be the last time.  The burgers were so over cooked that I thought they had slipped in a hockey puck.
Service was mediocre.  
NOT MUCH TO RECOMMEND HERE

Wowza this place is great. The interior is airy, with a distinct California coffee house vibes. The baristas were super friendly and helpful and made delightfully instagrammable lattes. The food was incredible- it sounds like such a millennial thing to say, but the avocado toast was to die for (crusty bread, tangy Dijon, slightly bitter microgreens- yas yas yas). Also, this shop had SO many attractive, young, hip people- it was like being in some kind of hipster lifestyle photo shoot somewhere slightly more artful than STL.

I wish they had more vegan options, but the two toast options are easily veganizable and allegedly they occasionally have vegan cookies.

Since I'm not from North Philly I hadn't heard of Max's until I saw it in the movie Creed. I finally made it there for Kevin Hart Day, with Kevin Hart himself making an appearance at his favorite cheesesteak spot. I had the basic Max's cheesesteak, which includes mayo, american cheese, and onions. Although service was slow it was worth the wait. A perfectly cooked, deliciously juicy authentic Philly cheesesteak. The steaks here are huge, so a half steak is good enough for most people. You can't claim to know all the best cheesesteak spots if you haven't been to Max's!

I like this idea of mixing a clothing store and a coffee shop. This new location is much bigger and nicer than the old location. I was able to shop their Black Friday sale comfortably and then sit down and relax with tasty cup of hot chocolate before heading to the next spot for Black Friday shopping. Clothing wise, they have a nice selection of outdoorsy type clothing. That's the best word to describe it, even though that's probably not a word. The clothes do seem pricey since it's not an established name brand, so I do shop during sales both in store and online. Besides coffee, tea, and hot chocolate, they serve pastries, the star of which is a cream stuffed donut which is the best cream donut I've had in Philly.

United By Blue pledges to remove a pound of trash from the earth's oceans and waterways for every product they sell through company-organized cleanups. This is a Philly based company I hope to be able to support for a long time.

I had been meaning to try happy hour at Forsythia since they opened, as I live close by. I decided to stop by for takeout and have my happy hour at home. I ordered the Burger Royale and the Apple Beignets. The first thing I noticed when I got home was that there were three items in my bag instead of two. The third item was some type of bread with a fancy butter. I thought to myself I don't really need more bread with a burger but I'll take a bite to see how it tastes. I put butter on that bread and took my bite. Next thing I know I devoured both slices of bread. It was that good! I was so happy to have it included in the meal. I dug in to the burger next. It's a double patty with cheese, fried onions, pickles and sauce on a sesame seed bun. The thing I don't like about double patty burgers is that the thin patties are generally overcooked. Not this burger. Both patties were a juicy medium! So juicy that the bottom of the bun got soggy towards the end. The meat to toppings ratio was slightly off as I had to make my own improvements by taking off a few onions and a pickle. But this was still up there with some of the top burgers in the city. Next up was the Beignets. I bit one and thought to myself it was nothing special. Then I realized it came with a cream cheese and Nutella dipping sauce. I dipped it into the sauce and took my next bite. What a difference the sauce makes!  That sauce transformed it into one of the best restaurant desserts I've ever tasted. It was so tasty that I was glad I was eating alone and didn't have to share them. They probably would have been even better if they were still warm.

I had a great happy hour at home meal thanks to Forsythia. I'm looking forward to trying more of the menu while seated at the restaurant. I wouldn't be surprised if I ended up updating this to a 5 star restaurant. The potential is there...

I enjoyed my  lunch here. Good ambiance, with excellent food and service. I had the Tredici burger and it was probably the juiciest burger I ever had. 8oz of Wagyu beef, with aged cheese on a brioche bun. Definitely right up there with the top burgers in the city. I always cut my burger in half to see how juicy it is, and the juice ran out all over the board it was served on. I had to move the burger to the bread plate just to stop all the juices from running all over the table. It was a perfectly cooked medium rare. I also had a taste of the chicken panini. The chicken was nice and tender but the sandwich didn't quite seem to be put together properly like a normal panini.

If you consider yourself a burger aficionado like I do, you have to try the burger here. I'm looking forward to going back to Tredici for dinner.

It's been a few years since I first Jump(ed) On The School Bus, and it is still as fun as ever! Whether renting it out for a private event, or joining in on one of their pre-established tours - JOTSB delivers every time! They've grown so much in the past few years, which speaks volumes in our tiny coastal community which sees small businesses open and close at the blink of an eye.

In addition to owners, Darin & Sierra, Danny is among my favorite drivers! He keeps things lighthearted but not at the expense of safety. In terms of reliability, JOTSB maintains their professionalism while creating a fun environment. That can be a difficult balance but they make it look easy. 

If you're heading to the Valley, throwing a party, ,or ever have the opportunity to Jump On The Bus to get you to and from an event, I highly recommend making their big, black bus your ride!

When I think of Barbareño my heart begins to warm, my mouth starts to salivate and my tummy rumbles. In truly Pavlovian form, Barbareño's exceptional food and stellar service, have successfully conditioned me with just the mention of its name. 

The dishes here, though deceptively not intriguing in many of their descriptions, are phenomenal. In general, I'd say that Barbareño has mastered combining simple ingredients with complex culinary techniques to create flavor profiles that are innovative, intelligent and most of all, delicious. Kudos to the Chef, sincerely!

The menu changes regularly based on what is fresh and in season. To date, some of my favorites are the Avocado Roulade, Basil Blini, Santa Maria Tartare, Wild Herb Risotto, Santa Maria Tri-Tip, Spring Lamb and Breakfast for Dessert (probably the best dessert I've had in Santa Barbara County - especially if you like sweet with a little bit of savory). 

They have an excellent selection of craft beers and wine. Everything from Modern Times will quench even the most discerning beer connoisseur's palette. My favorite is probably the Blackhouse. 

In addition to great food, Barbareño is really beautifully designed. It's rustic, casual elegance at its best - perfectly suited to Santa Barbara culture. The only constructive feedback I have on that note is the barstools - while very functional for the space and cute esthetically, they are a bit uncomfortable after sitting for a while and Hubby and I are the type of guests who like to sit and enjoy many courses and beverages while chatting with folks working behind the bar. 

Speaking of the staff, the customer service at Barbareño is incredible; rivaled only by Toma in my book. Every employee comes across as genuinely personable, expert on all things Barbareño, and attentive. I could not ask for more. Doug and Jesse stand out in particular but seriously, management/ownership has done a masterful job in hiring and training the right staff to represent the business. 

I'd highly recommend Barbareño for a romantic dinner, casual gathering with friends or family, or simple drinks and appetizers at the bar. But be careful, or you'll find you're just as easy to condition as Pavlov's dog too. ;)

Beautiful resort, but a far cry from Ritz-Carlton caliber customer service & travel experience. 

The Bacara is a gorgeous property perched on the cliffs of Santa Barbara's pristine coastline. I stayed at The Bacara several times under it's previous owner, and recently stayed again under the new Ritz Carlton brand. In addition to the occasional staycation, I frequent their spa and private events, basically I'm a regular. As a Ritz Carlton Platinum Rewards Member, I was thrilled to have a Marriott brand property in Santa Barbara, as I have been almost exclusively loyal to this brand for nearly a decade in my travels. Unfortunately, my excitement is beginning to wane after a series of subpar experiences at this property. 

The Good: The grounds are in excellent condition and the property is lovely. Angel Oak, under Chef Alexander Bollinger, serves exquisite, delicious cuisine. 5 stars unarguably! The cocktail program at Angel Oak is also amazing. Try the Smoke In Water. Todd, behind the bar at Angel Oak is exemplary of all things excellent in customer service. I've dined at the bar several times at Angel Oak with different bartenders and have been snubbed by the staff until my bill progressed to a 'remarkable balance.' With Todd, that was not the case. From the moment I sat down he was all smiles, welcoming, attentive, professional and genuine. Fani, in the Spa at the Bacara is another standout employee. In addition to providing consistent, incredible service, Fani goes above and beyond to meet the needs of her guests. Last month, I needed to get a mani/pedi on short notice ahead of a flight to Washington, DC. Fani came in at 7am (when she wasn't scheduled to work until 10am) to accommodate my schedule, so I could receive my mani/pedi before my AM flight. She is a gem and I would follow her to any spa.

The Bad, Dirty & Downright Ugly: 
During our most recent stay at the Bacara earlier this year, the check-in process was a nightmare. To be quite honest, the entire stay was amiss. We were not greeted or welcomed with a smile or warmth. The receptionist appeared apathetic. He half-heartedly took my information, gave me the keys and pointed me towards the direction of my room. 
- No acknowledgement or thank you for being a Ritz Carlton Platinum Rewards member. 
- No mention of the amenities on the property such as entry to the spa facilities, etc.  
- No mention they serve coffee/tea in the mornings in the lobby. 
- No mention the bottle of Pinot Noir in the room is complimentary. 
Nothing. We proceeded through our entire stay without knowledge of any of these things until checkout, when I happened to observe a different receptionist checking in a guest who explained all these offerings to the guest he was helping. I was dumbfounded. 

When we arrived to our room I immediately smelled the distinct odor of cigarette and cigar smoke. I realized one of our neighbors was smoking in their room and on the balcony; and it was seeping into my room. Even with the balcony door closed, the smoke was still entering my room. After awhile, my asthma began to flare up and I started wheezing and coughing. I called the front desk as the rooms were to be smoke free and they said they would send someone out to check on the situation, no one came. An hour later I called again and they said they asked the guest stop. Fast forward to the next morning, same thing happens again. My room fills with fumes of smoke, my asthma flares up, I have an asthma attack, albuterol, call the front desk, etc... This cycle progressed through the entire stay for three days and I was never moved to a different room, nor were any measures taken to stop the guests smoking in their room. It was miserable. It's difficult to ignore being unable to breathe. 

A few days ago, I was back at the Bacara, this time for a regular spa visit. I pulled into valet and man who gave me a valet ticket, took a look at me and a long look at my 2018 lux vehicle and said, "So what is this a rental or something? You borrowing this? Is this loaner vehicle?" - "No, it's my car," I replied, "I own it." When did it become customary for the valet to berate a guest with questions about how they acquired their vehicle? I don't get it. When I returned to the valet after my spa day, I walked towards a different valet who walked right past me to the gentleman who was walking about 4 yards behind me and asked him if he could get his car. I guess it's not first come, first serve. About ten minutes later I'm still standing there and he eventually saunters over and says, "did you need something?" "Yes, I need my car, I was waiting before the man you just helped." "Oh...-I thought you were together." Bologna. 

There have been other instances too - the manicurist who started my appointment 30 mins late, the masseuse who cut my massage 10 short, and so on. First world problems, yes. But imperative nonetheless for a 5 star, luxury resort to rectify when their rep is on line.

I love Santa Barbara Farmers Markets! The Tuesday and Saturday markets are my favorite because they are so close to my office and home, there is no reason not to buy local and organic. One of my favorite things to do is to interact with the merchants. I love telling them what I am aiming to make and then get their suggestions on what to buy to accomplish it. This week, it was easy, vegetable soup! I purchased fresh parsley, zucchini, yellow squash, potatoes, tomatoes, onion, green beans, corn, curly kale and carrots. All that ran me less than $15.00 and I made a pot of soup large enough to feed two people for two meals. It was delicious! The vegetables were so flavorful and rich they almost tasted sweet. I love eating nutrient dense food that is completely guilt free and the Farmers Market is the best place to find it. On the weekends, I like to buy local seafood from the fishermen, although on a few occasions despite my shellfish being packed on ice, it opened by the time I got home. I recommend preparing your shellfish right away if you purchase it from the FM. I always look for the grape stand and the Autumn Crisp grapes. They have a flavor reminiscent of lychee and are delightfully tasty! Bring your bags and cash. Try a sample of some of the fresh produce and you'll be hooked. It's that good! Ichi-go, ichi-e!

This block of Ortega was in desperate need of a restaurant. I eagerly anticipated the opening of Little Kitchen from the moment their notices of construction were posted in the window. I was like a child anxious for Santa to arrive, walking past the store front daily (it's near my job) for signs of life. 

Once it finally opened, it took me weeks to come in because I could not get past the putrid stench just outside its' door. Everyday there was this overwhelming order of urine, vomit, alcohol and whatever other secretions ooze out of the Wild Cat next door and on to their little store front area. It was like an invisible force field that repelled me back each time I tried to enter the restaurant. 

After what seemed like a couple of months, it appeared someone eventually got the notion to hose off the area and the stench subsided..for a brief time at least. Relieved, that was my cue that the force field was down and in I went. Once you get inside it smells like a restaurant is supposed to smell, not like an out house in the back of a brothel. The decor inside is earthy and inviting, the bathroom has the most adorable tiny sink and the tables are decorated with cute fresh flowers. One of the owners is often at the counter taking orders. She is also an accomplished chef and used to whip up some great dishes for Happy Hour at the Kitty. 

I ordered the Turkey Rosemary Club and substituted a wrap for the ciabatta. (Though ciabatta is delicious it always tears up the inside of my mouth, hence the substitution.) It came with a side salad and I added a La Croix sparkling water. The sandwich/wrap was delicious and very flavorful, filled with chunks of turkey breast and ingredients that tasted fresh. Yes! It was also super reasonably priced. I enjoyed sitting at a table where I could look out the window (but not close enough to the window where I could inhale any lingering stench.) The next time I came in, I tried the Tomato Soup and Half Sandwich, also delicious. 

The last time I was there and the reason for the two star review, is in regards to the kitchen. On a slow afternoon, I came in and ordered my Turkey Rosemary Club with Side Salad and Sparking Water and sat at a table with a view of the open kitchen. While I was waiting for my meal, I noticed one of the chefs preparing a take out order. In the midst of placing the food items in containers he let out a series of huge, snotty, wet sneezes and deep coughs reflexively catching the goo in his bare hands. He then took said once bare hands, now covered in slimy germs, and inserted them directly into a bin of tasty house made potato chips; grabbing two handfuls and placing them in the to go box for the take out order. Yum! Some folks got extra "seasoning" that day or maybe even a side of laryngitis. This scene had my stomach churning and although I had already paid for my meal, I couldn't stomach the idea of actually eating it given the lack of hygiene observed by the chef in the kitchen. I waited a few minutes to see if he would ever wash his nasty hands, but no, he didn't. He just continued to handle customer's food bare handed and covered in germs. 

If I was a restaurant owner or manager, I would want to know about situations like this so that I could re-train my staff. So I discreetly pulled the owner aside and shared what I witnessed. She seemed surprised, albeit aloof, and went back to standing at the register, but did not address the issue at the time. That was my cue to to let her know that they did not need to make my order. She offered to give me a refund. I told her that was not necessary. It was not about the money, it was about the cleanliness or lack there of in their handling of food. She insisted and gave me a refund. 

I'm sure things like this happen in kitchens all the time behind closed doors, but to see it on display in an open kitchen is just repulsive. I can't imagine how food is handled when customers aren't in plain sight, if this is how it is handled when they are. 

So, no more Little Kitchen for me, unfortunately, because I did enjoy the convenience and taste of the food. Who knows, maybe boogers, snot and saliva mixed in with a little virus, bacteria or allergies are the flavors that I unwittingly enjoyed.

Santa Barbara Brewing Co is my go to local restaurant for Boneless Buffalo Chicken Wings. They are quite tasty! Not amazing, but they're also the only restaurant in SB that I know current serves Boneless Buffalo Chicken Wings. Sometimes, especially on a work day, I don't feel like getting my fingers dirty or getting sauce all over my face. On those occasions, I want to be dainty and cut my "wings" with a knife, and carefully dip them in my bleu cheese dressing and place them elegantly in my mouth. Avoiding the dangers of red sauce splattering in my lap. This is where SBBC comes in! Piping hot morsels of chicken breast, battered, deep fried and doused in hot sauce, mmmm. They're often fried a bit too long, but I don't care. It satisfies my craving in the moment and that is good enough for me! I always substitute my fries for the vegetable of the day. It is green beans or a combination of green beans and broccoli, drenched in some sort of garlic butter. If you're really looking for a healthier substitute for fries perhaps ask for your veggies to be plain with no oil or butter. Sitting at the bar is pleasant. I like interacting with the bartender, Jared. He is friendly, attentive and always remembers my order. SBBC also has fun pool tables in the back of the restaurant. 

My favorite experience was going there after one of my first UYEs a couple of years ago with a ton of Yelpers for drinks and pool. If Greg W and the gorgeous Ashley E ever challenge you to a game of pool, do NOT be fooled by their warm and sweet exteriors folks. This dynamic duo are fierce competitors and they play a kick-ass game of pool, I love it! Also, Sarah S is a pool firecracker but less conspicuous because her custom pool stick is a dead give away she means business! 

SBBC is the perfect place to gather with large groups of friends whether you're sitting down for dinner or just want to hit up happy hour, play pool or catch a game on one of their multiple flat screen TVs! Check it out!

Adorable coffee shop in a prime, downtown location on lower Chapala Street. If you work in the area, like I do, you'll be thrilled to have a locally owned and operated business in your neck of the woods instead of hitting one of the commercial coffee mega giants. 

Breakfast Culture Club serves up delicious brew from Handlebar Roasting Company and yummy pastries from Flag Stone Pastries, including a vast selection of vegan treats. 

The layout is expansive with seating inside at multiple tables, outside on their patio overlooking Chapala St and a living room like area with a sofa and coffee table. 

The staff are warm and friendly. If you frequent French Press or Handlebar, you'll probably even recognize a few of their smiling faces. 

I love the art on the wall from Xst! Super cool portraits taken mostly with an iPhone. I could definitely see myself hanging art like this on my wall at home. 

They have plenty of merchandise for sale if that tickles your fancy, too! This looks like a great place to work remotely, study, read, chat with friends and/or just chill and people watch. 

There is a small parking lot in front of the shop or plenty of 75 minute street parking on the roads nearby. I'm so glad this is so close and look forward to getting my coffee fix regularly! On that note, I tend to be more of tea or matcha drinker these days and I did not pay attention to see if they carry either of those. If not, bring matcha please!

Convivo is a decent restaurant in my book and a nice addition to Santa Barbara's Eastside neighborhood for a casual, upscale meal. 

There is definitely room for growth and improvement but I'll start with The Good first.

Location: Cabrillo Blvd, Ocean Views, Lower Eastside, Directly across the street from the East Beach. 

Architecture and Design: Beautiful, new construction; Lovely neutral color palette with dark wood accents; Spanish tiles; Gorgeous outdoor patio under a beautiful pergola. 

Food: Standard but not amazing. Does not blow you away but it is good.  A few of my favorites are Octopus; Croquettes; Uni Toast; Fennel Sausage Pizza; and the Lamb Meatballs.

Happy Hour: They have a fair Happy Hour that is worth checking out if you're in the area which offers discounts on pizza, drinks and a few appetizers.  

Now for The Not So Good: 

Customer Service: In general customer service is consistently lacking. The first few times we dined here when they opened the customer service was good, but it has been on a steady decline since. I've noticed that the servers often start out well, attentive, pleasant, etc. ...but quickly become MIA shortly after placing your order. It has become routine during my last few times eating here to have to get up to ask for our waiter so that I can place a second drink order, receive silverware, condiments, the bill, etc. When I ate here last weekend, we had to wait an additional 30 minutes after finishing our meals for the waiter to bring the bill and again I had to go ask for it at that. A let down which discourages us from coming more regularly like we used to. 

Pesce Misto: A very small selection of grilled seafood for the price. Not worth sharing and not worth ordering. I don't recommend it. You'll find better quality and value at Lure if you're interested in fresh seafood.

Ranch Dressing: They do not offer ranch dressing. If you're one of those Americans who like to douse your pizza in ranch, tough. Not at Convivo, friend!

Located inside Lama Dog, Nook is serving up creative American fusion, like Duck Foie Gras Burger, Lobster Mac n' Cheese and Blackened Rock Fish Tacos, in a relaxed atmosphere tucked away in the Funk Zone.

The Lobster Mac 'n' Cheese is rich and creamy (but not runny thank heavens) and complimented with a few chucks of lobster throughout. The mini garlic crouton topping adds crispy, buttery notes to this deliciously decadent dish. 

The Duck Foie Gras Burger was tasty, although I could not taste any of the flavor of rich foie gras. It tasted more like a ground duck patty which was flavorful but not warranting of foie gras in the title. 

The French Fries are medium-thick, crispy and served in their own cute, mini fry basket. I recommend upgrading to the Parmesan Truffle Fries. 

For dessert, we tried the Milk Chocolate Cake topped with Coconut Ice Cream and garnished with a papaya compote. The cake was thick and dense, complimented nicely with the sharpness of the papaya and bright, coconut ice cream. I asked if the cake was served warm, and was told it was, however, ours did not come out warm at all. It was still good but I think it would have been better a little warm with the ice cream. 

I'm excited to try other items on the menu. There is a giant, Bavarian Pretzel on it that is calling my name. It looks like it is served with mustard, however, I think it would be lovely for Chef to create a beer based cheese dip perhaps with pieces of thick, crispy bacon or pork belly or pickled jalepenos it in. It would tie in nicely with the theme of Lama Dog. 

It's wonderful to have another dining option in the Funk Zone that is open all day and into the late evening. I imagine it will be very successful and I can definitely see myself becoming a regular. Go check it out!

Coast & Olive is my latest culinary obsession. I was lured in by the raving Yelp reviews praising the Lobster Gnocchi. On my first visit, this popular dish was completely sold out, so I ordered the Trout Almandine instead. Such-a-great-dish! Moist, flakey, white fish enveloped in a toasty, golden crust, all nestled in a rich, buttery bath. Served with Haricot-Vert (basically French Green Beans) and Creamy Mashed Potatoes. I've still yet to try the Lobster Gnocchi because I am hooked on the trout and order it every time. 

Not to be upstaged by dinner, is their amazing Baked Apple dessert. Imagine a whole apple, deceptively intact, yet somehow thinly layered beneath its crumble crust. Tender, tangy, served warm, and beautifully complimented with a scoop of rich, vanilla ice cream. It's finished with warm caramel sauce. Heavenly, simply, heavenly.

If libations are what you are after, you must try the Fogged Hog. Whistlepig Rye Whiskey (hence the hog), agave, walnut bitters, grapefruit, candied bacon, served table side in a smoked glass. On the several occasions I have ordered this drink it wasn't actually served table side, and didn't visibly appear to be in a smoked glass, however, I could taste the subtle essence of smoke. For true presentation of a smoked glass, I prefer Angel Oak at the Ritz Carlton Bacara. 

The ambiance is comfortable in light of COVID19 outdoor circumstances. I appreciate the inclusion of ample heaters at the tables. It does feel a bit risky at times sitting so close to bustling traffic on Coast Village Road, especially in the evening. 

For me, Coast & Olive is one of Santa Barbara's finest restaurants and I am thrilled they are here. I loved Monarch, it's predecessor. I do hope Coast & Olive fairs better in the long run.

Pre-COVID-19, Bettina would have earned a solid two stars in my experience, which was not pleasant at all. The food was mediocre at best - greasy, soggy crust, skimpy pepperoni, and bland flavors. It did not hold up to the competition in the pizza saturated community of Santa Barbara. 

Thank heavens I did not allow first impressions to prevent me from giving Bettina a second chance. 

In the era of COVID, a friend brought Bettina to my social distancing birthday party and it was delicious. I enjoyed it so much that I ordered Bettina twice more for take out only days after my party. The crust was perfectly doughy, the flavors rich, and the toppings were hearty. 

I recommend the Meat Lovers Pizza, the New Potato (try adding Maitake Mushrooms), and the Sausage (add Pepperoni if you're not getting the Meat Lovers). Order at least one pizza per person in your party as the pizza is conservative in size. 

I choose to skip the apps and salads as they've all been underwhelming in my experience. 

What would kick my review up to 5 stars? A bit more consistency in quality from order to order. There are still some days when our pizzas are soggy and the toppings slop off when a slice is picked up. I've noticed this is more likely to occur when we order around 7pm during the dinner rush. Perhaps there is less attention to detail in haste to have food prepared in a timely manner. On the occasions where we place our order around 5pm, the quality of the pizza is vastly improved.

I am a still a fan of Green Table's nutrient rich cuisine but I've noticed some marked changes in overall quality since the transition in ownership last year, so I'm updating my review to a solid 4-stars rather than 5. 

The Quinoa Mac N' Cheese is not as good as it used to be. It was perfection and now it is often inconsistent and tastes more like a science experiment. The last few times I've ordered it, there were massive pieces of raw garlic cloves, big chunks of raw cauliflower and a liquid of soupy consistency. These elements were better incorporated in the past and created a much more balanced dish. 

The Kale and Avocado Salad, while just okay now, was previously extraordinary. I can't quite pinpoint what the changes are but the recipe definitely is not the recipe that I came to love when Green Table was Boochies or Green Table was Green Table with different co-ownership.

Of course with new ownership comes change, and change can be a great thing. It's just tough when great things are changed for not so great things. 

I like the front of the house staff. They are sweet and provide good customer service. I do miss the warm, energetic and hospitable energy that the previous owner cultivated in the restaurant. There was often a line out the door and people packed shoulder to shoulder inside. I think that was a testament not just to the wonderful, healthy food but the inviting, personable experience customers had there as well. It's much different now. Ownership/management can rarely be seen interacting with their guests or staff, but can be found sitting a dining table entranced by their laptops for hours on end. They're probably doing necessary administrative tasks, it is just a dramatic culture shift from its predecessor. 

I am impressed with the ongoing expansion of the menu, however. It seems Green Table is really trying to expound upon what they inherited from Boochies and create innovative, exciting menu items. That's fantastic! I look forward to trying their new dishes and perhaps see a return of the crowd favorites that garnered their original popularity.

Damn near Santa Barbara perfection! Owned by locally raised, home grown SB natives. None of that big city money moving in with entitlement and snobbery changing the casual charm that has imbued SB for decades. 

The food is incredible! The Bacon Jam Burger melts in your mouth with a fresh baked bun sturdy enough to hold up to the beefy patty, but delicate enough to literally dissolve in your mouth. It reminds me a bit of a Hawaiian roll in taste and texture of better! Your tongue with dance with notes of slightly sweet, savory and salty on your palette in every time. It's the perfect combination! Served with a side of piping hot, seasoned shoe string fries or sautéed kale. This is my new favorite burger in Santa Barbara!

The Little Gem Salad is aptly named not only for it's ingredients but also because it is a gem! Crunchy Little Gem greens, cowboy beans, cheese, roasted red peppers, onions and shredded tortillas make this salad a meal on to itself. I added a side of their delicious falafel to pack in the protein, yum! 

Don't let my vegetarian salad fool you, I could not escape without ordering the Maple Bourbon Bacon Bites as an amuse bouche. Large chunks of smokey, succulent pork belly served on a two skewers with a side of maple bourbon sauce for dipping. So good, it's sexy! 

I love the laid back, inviting atmosphere created by the use of farm house tables, benches and canopies. It's all outdoor seating -- generally not a problem for SB's lovely climate. They have a nice selection of local beer and wine. It's family friendly. The Funk Zone Patio has been years in the making and it was definitely worth the wait! Congrats to the Shalhoob family! Looks like you have another local favorite to add to your legacy!

Incredible Mexican food! Chef Ramon has carved a gem into the Santa Barbara Public Market. I have been a major fan of Ramon's since his humble beginnings at Arigatos, followed him to Cielitos and then to his Sunday Pop-up inside of Three Pickles. I am so grateful he has found a home to launch his own creative, restaurant concept. The seafood is sushi grade, the tortillas are hand made and the Al Pastor is carved fresh off the spit. You can't go wrong with anything on the menu. A couple of my personal favorites are the La Gringa Quesadilla and Seafood Tostada. The fresh guacamole and chips are the perfect compliment to any meal. When you arrive, if you see a long line, don't get discouraged. That's a hallmark of a wonderful eatery. Just hop in the cue, order a beer and eagerly anticipate the foodgasm that awaits you!

My experience at Reds was one of the strangest experiences I've ever had at a bar. 

I arrived on a weekday evening around nine and was looking for a good late night wine bar to wind down after a busy day. My faithful Yelp app, came through with good reviews of Reds so I decided to check it out. 

When I walked into the bar there were an eclectic bunch of patrons clustered on the patio, in seats, at the bar and scattered throughout the venue. Good sign. There was a band playing new age folk rock. One of them was an employee of Reds. The crowd was a non-diverse mix of hipsters and old men. Reminiscent of the North Hollywood scene. 

I made my way to the bar and took a seat on an empty chair as I watched the bartenders socialize with the patrons. I sat there for about 10 minutes patiently waiting for one of them to acknowledge me but no one did. A few other people at the bar stared awkwardly at me with that "who are you glance" and I shrugged my shoulders, smiled and continued to wait. 

At this point I was committed to the task being that I had already waited so long for service. A tall, slender man with a broken foot and long hair approached the bar and stood behind me, ready for a refill. (He later introduced himself as Jason.)

This is where it gets really strange... The blond, short-haired bartender, also named Jason, then immediately turned to face him, unzipped his jeans (with no underwear underneath) and proceeded to pull out his wang teasingly at the Jason standing behind me. I was shocked. I got full frontal nudity from the little bartender. Tall Jason teased back verbally and the little bartender Jason, put his very, little friend back in his pants. Gross!

While all of this was going on, another bartender, a petite woman with short blond hair, was behind the bar talking to customers also. I found out later that her name is Dana, and she is one of the owners. I felt horrible for Dana because she seemed to have no control over Jason and his outrageous behavior. He just got more vulgar as the night progressed and talked to her in very condescending, smart-ass tones. It would have been embarrassing behavior for any restaurant professional and I can't believe she tolerated it. 

Okay, back to the story...tall Jason behind me, noticing I had been sitting there for quite some time without once being spoken to, asked if I wanted a drink and then gave little Jason my order. He said he was part owner of the joint and bought me a couple of glasses of wine. I chose a red, a Zin I think, and it was delicious. We talked story for awhile about how I was new in town and he said that Reds wasn't a good fit for me and that I belonged in a place like Cafe Lucky or Lucky's. I haven't been to either yet but I'll check them out. 

I haven't been back to Reds since, though I've told a bunch of people about my experience. I don't think I'd go back again but I'm curious if my experience was unique or not so I might give it a whirl...but probably not. I'd rather go to Blue Agave or Milk & Honey where at least I can get good service and not have to worry about being flashed by a cocky bartender.

When it comes to Carr Wines, two words come to mind, Cabernet Franc! It's delicious. Rich, full-bodied, slightly spicy with a hint of tannins...yum! If you like big, bold reds or Rhone varietals, you'll probably enjoy Carr's Cabernet Franc. 

The tasting room is expansive, with a few high top tables, a large bar and lounge type seating. It's the perfect venue for private events. I've been to several private events here and the space works seamlessly with catering and is large enough for dancing too.

It's also a great place to listen to live music. I like the acoustics. Check Carr's website for a full list of upcoming line ups.

In an era where bread has become the vilified, black sheep, Oat Bakery is its saving grace. With incredible, fresh-baked loaves and buns, Oat Bakery is making eating bread "cool" again. My favorite things to order are the Brie & Cherry Loaf, Spinach & Feta Loaf, Savory Hygge Bun (think Cheesy Monkey Bread with Herbs), Sweet Hygge (think Cinnamon Roll but better, made with dates) and their House Made Granola. I also love their Cashew Truffle Spread (think truffle cream cheese without the cheese.) 

The Gluten Free bread could be employed by the CIA and go under cover as traditional bread without ever breaking cover. It's that good! On one of my visits to the Ty Lounge at the Four Seasons Biltmore Resort, a group of tourists with Celiac Disease ordered their charcuterie board with a side of Gluten Free crostini. After taking their first bite, they flagged the waiter down and proceeded to admonish him for bringing them gluten bread. They were sure it contained gluten because it tasted so good. Nope, it was Oat Bakery's delicious, double-agent, Gluten Free bread. I couldn't resist chiming in and doting about SB's gem of a local bakery and vouching that their crostini was in fact gluten free. They finished their board and bread with delight (and NO anaphylactic shock)!

Many local restaurants and eateries procure their bread from Oat Bakery. Love the Fancy Avocado Toast at Caje? Their Charcoal Sourdough Bread is from Oat Bakery. Crazy about the Raw Cashew Toast at Juice Ranch? - Their bread is from Oat Bakery. Does Healthy Warrior's SuperFood Breakfast Toast make you Happy? - It's also from Oat Bakery! The list goes on and on. Oat Bakery is a hit not to be missed! 

The shop itself is quaint; tucked discreetly between a few other businesses off State Street on Guiterez Street. Blink and you could miss it. This is not a sit down and eat establishment, although their are usually a couple of bar stools inside along bay windows looking out onto Downtown Santa Barbara. Order at the counter and take your goodies to go. It's the perfect stop before a picnic, wine tasting or stroll to the beach. Not to mention before a dinner party. Show up with a few loaves from Oat Bakery at your next gathering and you'll be the Belle of the Ball!

How in the world have I not reviewed Monys Mexican Food, yet? This is one of our top go-to Mexican food restaurants. An establishment Hubby and I can always agree upon. Great food, great service, great prices - no contest!

Monys is family owned and operated and I have to agree with Mark F. (who wrote an excellent review on Monys btw), that when I dine here, I feel like family. Excellent customer service and the food is delicious. 

Sometimes I like to keep it simple, and when I do, I order tacos. There is an impressive selection of meat and vegetables to choose from. My must haves are: Adobada, Pastor, Carne Asada, Carnitas, and Veggie (easily the best veggie taco I have had in Santa Barbara). Hubby also loves the Barbacoa. 

When consuming the tacos, you must dress them with a douse of one of Monys incredibly tasty salsas. I recommend the Pistachio! A little heat and lots of flavor!
