Monys is located in the heart of the Funk Zone and is the perfect spot to grab your food to go and take it with you to Fig Mountain Brewery or one of the local wine tasting rooms. But be careful, you'll be the envy of all those in sniffing distance of you! There are also some tables in inside the small restaurant or outside along the sidewalk.

Unlike many eateries in Santa Barbara, Monys is very affordable so it is great for families, students or anyone interested in keeping more money in their pocket than someone else's while not compromising on quality or taste. 

Of its genre, Monys is as good as it gets in this town! I love supporting this family and this local business. Go check them out!

Another 5 star review to add to the Caje Coffee Roasters' repertoire. This coffee shop is fantastic. Cozy interior, beautifully decorated in farmhouse industrial decor. Lots of natural light pouring in from the store front windows. Lush foliage and greenery soften the metal and wood accents, while simultaneously purifying the air and adding a bit of zen. 

When I walked in, I was welcomed with a friendly greeting from the staff behind the counter. A practice I noticed maintained consistent for all guests who entered during my time there. It being my first time patronizing Caje, I naturally had questions and the staff were warm, pleasant and patient as they answered them. I just adore great customer service! Thank you Caje! 

To drink, I opted for the Yemen, a sophisticated cafe mocha with a blend of coconut milk, condensed milk and whole milk and garnished with a toasted marshmallow. (Marshmallow? Dang right, I'm not passing that up!) 

For eats, I chose the Chorizo Madelines and the Fancy Avocado Toast. You read that correctly, madelines, as in the cookies not the beloved fictional character I grew up reading stories about. The starch base of Caje's Chorizo Madelines are more reminiscent of corn bread in flavor and texture, than a sweet cookie, with small bites of chorizo baked into the batter. Sourced from Sama Sama daily, they are perfectly paired with honey butter and chives to garnish. The Fancy Avocado Toast is served on local favorite, Oat Bakery, bread, sliced thick. Unfortunately, the avocado on my toast was not fresh and had that bitter, earthy flavor that overripe avocado emits. Luckily, there were enough fresh garnishes (blueberries, cheese, etc) to make it palatable. 

Caje roasts their own coffee and makes their syrups in house. They also support reusable cups and presently do not offer a disposable cup option. Enjoy your beverage here in one of their mugs, bring your own vessel to take your java on the go, or use one of theirs for a nominal deposit. 

Caje is dog friendly, so bring your fur baby if you'd like. They also have free wifi although I was unable to successfully connect to it, and chose to create a personal hotspot instead.

How have I not reviewed this business yet? It has been one of my go to Chinese restaurants for years! Here is what keeps me coming back... La Zi Chicken - crispy, spicy, flavorful bite size pieces of fried chicken amidst peppers and green onions. (Thanks for the rec Lily Z.) Kung Pao Chicken and Shrimp Fried Rice. The prices are fair and the portions are good. We always feel full after our meal and generally have a little left over. 

Mandarin Palace has great lunch specials on a shoe string budget. You choose from well known mains like Orange Chicken and it comes with scary jello (that probably tastes great but I never try it), Fried Rice, an Egg Roll and a lettuce Salad w/ a tasty dressing. 

The staff are consistently attentive and friendly, even during the dinner rush. Though the restaurant is fairly inviting, I prefer to call ahead and order my entrees to go so Hubby and I can sit in front of the idiot box and spend quality time together.

I have to confess, I am a Mex Authenticholic! After eating here on several different occasions and practically licking my plate clean - I cannot deny, I have a problem - If you consider eating delicious Mexican food, frequently, with excellent service in a wonderful, welcoming, clean atmosphere a big deal. I might just need an intervention. And with such fair and reasonable prices for quality Mexican food, I can afford to support my Mex Authentic habit as often as I desire. (Which is like, daily.) 

A few of my faves are the Carnitas Jalisco, Carne Asada with Cheese Enchilada, Jalepeno Cucumber MEXarita, House Made Chips and Salsa. 

The Carnitas Jalisco are tender, yet crispy, large chunks of marinated pork. I hate soggy carnitas. Restaurants that seep and stew their carnitas without pan frying them at the end to give that crispy, caramelized pork goodness on the outside of the meat disgust me. The Mex Authentic does carnitas right. The entree comes with a generous portion of flavorful refried beans topped with a blend of cheeses, Mexican rice, a dollop of fresh guac, warm corn or flour tortillas and pico de gallo. Muy rico! 

Equally delicious is the Carne Asada plate with Cheese Enchilada. The carne asada is very well-seasoned, tender and prepared perfectly with a pink center. I've had it several times and it is usually perfect. Once it was a teeny, tiny bit chewy but in my experience that was an anomaly. The rich Cheese Enchilada is a wonderful compliment to the meat, as is the aforementioned sides. 

A surprising star, is the Jalepeno Cucumber MEXarita because it is actually not tequila, rather a wine based substitute due to the liquor license. It's incredible! Seriously, 90% better than any margarita that I've had in Santa Barbara. Not too sweet, not too spicy, refreshing and loaded with flavor. I can't taste or feel a difference from a regular tequila based margarita. It's very good!

The House Made Chips and Salsa are so yummy that we usually continue to eat them throughout the meal. You just don't want them to end, which works out great because they are "bottomless." 

The owners and staff are attentive, observant, and very personable. They keep the restaurant in great shape. The bussers do not miss a  beat. I saw someone walk-in and on the way to the table a minuscule piece of white paper fell from their person to the floor - the busser was on it in a matter of seconds immediately picking it up and placing it in the trash. They were prompt with refills when needed and clearing plates as we finished. 

This is not one of Santa Barbara's high end, gourmet restaurants yet I'd be remiss not to give it the 5-stars it has earned. For what it is, a delicious, casual Mexican eatery with great food and service, it's top in it's class. When I have a hankering for Mexican food, and especially when I don't want to endure the chaos that is Los Agaves (primarily the Miplas location which is declining in service in the absence of the owner's presence) - it's The Mex Authentic for me. I highly recommend. 

Btw, if you see me sitting at the bar with three different entrees for myself, greedily hovering over all the yummy food as if it's my first or last meal, then it's time for an intervention and I may need your help. 

(Pro tip - For the locals, or budget savvy visitor, they are on 2016 SB Axxess.)

Shang Hai has re-ignited my Chinese food addiction in the wake of the loss of Stone Age on Milpas Street. Nestled in an unassuming shopping center, one would not think much of this eatery from its humble exterior. Luckily, this is one book that should not be judged by its cover. Once inside, it feels clean, sanitized and precautious in terms of COVID19 safety measures, I am told by husband (who usually picks it up the order after I call it in.) 

Shout out to Helen for her fantastic pictures of the Salt & Pepper Chicken. Over the years of Yelping in Santa Barbara, I have come to rely on the reviews of Lily Z and Helen D, especially in finding great Chinese food. 

The Salt & Pepper Chicken is crispy and full of flavor with the addition of flash fried jalapeños and minced garlic. 

Another favorite of mine is the Sesame Beef (or Sesame Chicken). It is slightly sweet with nutty notes from the sesame seeds. 

Shrimp Fried Rice is another stable in our take out order. We like to substitute white rice for brown rice. Don't forget to ask for a side of Sweet & Sour Sauce! It is a family recipe made in-house from scratch with fresh ingredients opposed to the pre-packaged sweet and sour sauce used at many restaurants.

Sometimes I like the food, sometimes I like the service. The problem for me is the inconsistency, hence the middle of the road, 3 star rating. The Tuscan Sausage & Kale Soup is tasty. I prefer it when I am dining in as I ordered a bowl to go once when I was under the weather and the portion was smaller than a cup of soup. I also enjoy their hash on the brunch special menu. They could improve their breakfast menu by offering some a la carte options such as biscuits & jam, a side of bacon, etc. for foodies like me who love to add on to my entree (and increase the restaurants revenue). Once, I tried to order a biscuit in addition to my entree and the waitress told me that Chef said he only makes enough biscuits for the chicken and biscuits entree. It seemed silly to me to order two entrees just to be able to have a biscuit with my meal, so I chose not to order anything and went to Jeanine's next door for my breakfast after my husband finished his meal at State & Fig. Little things like that make the world of difference in how often a customer repeats business at a restaurant. They could have easily increased their sales by three times what we spent by having a few more accommodations on the menu. There is a lovely dog friendly patio in front of the restaurant. Depending on which server you have they will actually bring them a bowl of water too, which is a nice touch when it is offered. This establishment has lots of potential and the food is generally good, however, service is a large component of the dining experience and can bring down the rating when it is not up to par with common industry standards. If you're a tourist, it's worth checking out because it is tucked away in a cute courtyard in the La Arcada plaza and has a nice ambiance outside as do the several neighboring restaurants.

Delicious Turkish coffee, baklava and Turkish delights. Located on State Street in the heart of downtown Santa Barbara. The staff are hospitable and friendly. I tried a few of their Turkish delight flavors before selecting an assortment to take home. I also took home a variety box of baklava. All of the items are imported directly from Turkey. The Turkish coffee is rich and flavorful. I love the presentation. This is a wonderful addition to Santa Barbara

To date I've been back to Wildwood Kitchen about three times since my first review (all within one week) and I have noticed a major improvement in some of the recipes. The Baked Beans were fabulous! Perfect balance of vinegar and heat - and all the beans were cooked to tender perfection except the garbanzos which were a bit under al dente adding a little texture and crunch that I found quite enjoyable. The BBQ Sampler was very good - I think the chicken was my favorite of the meats. I prefer the Espresso BBQ Sauce. A real star for me is the chili on the lunch menu! Delicious, flavorful, rich, hearty chili - served with a trio of chopped meats for a small up charge. It's filing. It's satisfying. It's the perfect lunch! 

They have fabulous craft cocktails. On one occasion we sat at the bar and the bartender was phenomenal. I wish I remembered his name. He was personable and patient, knowledgable about the drink and food menus and prepared fantastic libations. 

The person who really stole my heart...was the baker! To say this woman can bake would be an understatement. If she owned a bakery, I would go there weekly and my belly would grow exponentially in kind, but I would not care because I'd be in a sort of blissful, dessert induced trance that would make it all feel okay. Just one bite of her Peanut Butter Pie and I was in love. It is creamy, rich, fluffy, decadent and airy - all in one. You must try it! You must! I want to go back and eat one of everything that she creates. It's the stuff dessert dreams are made of. 

If you haven't been to Wildwood since it's opening, I highly recommend checking it out again.

We had a wonderful meal at Yoichi's that truly felt like an authentic experience in Japanese cuisine. The customer service was impeccable from the moment we walked and maintained consistent throughout our entire dining experience. 

We each ordered the 7 course kaiseki menu. Every dish was delicate and delectable! We're lucky to have a restaurant of this caliber in Santa Barbara. The seafood is as fresh as it gets in this town. Follow Yoichi's on Facebook to see pictures of the daily catch or imports coming in. 

For my party, 7 courses was not quite enough to leave feeling full, but we were satisfied. I do wish the portions were slightly larger or there were a few more courses to fully round out the meal and not leave you hungry at the end. 

It was my birthday when we went and our waiter, Zack, sang the most beautiful, soulful, a cappella rendition of the birthday song that I've ever heard! Thank you Zack! I felt so special! 

Pro tip: Ask if you can keep a menu with you at the table so you can know what you're eating and accurately caption your picture on Yelp! (Unlike, me;)

If you're local, you're probably not reading this to determine whether or not you'd like to try Bouchon, as it has long been an established favorite in the Santa Barbara community. It's quintessential, farm-to-table, French cuisine at it's best. We've been dining here for years, so it's easy to take it for granted or veer away when something new and sparkly moves in. But like a great old pair of jeans, it's always comforting when you return.

It's perfect for a romantic or quiet dinner, which it's ambient lighting and French country side decor. I love their roasted meats, lamb to be exact and foie gras when they have it. Their desserts are also wonderful. The menu changes frequently based on what is fresh and in season. You'll often find Chef mining the Farmer's Market for organic produce. 

Service is generally good, though we've experienced instances of pretentiousness or negligence, hence 4-stars opposed to 5, but all in all the vast majority of our meals have been fantastic.

What can I say that hasn't already been covered by Buena Onda's stellar 5 star reviews? I don't know but I'll try!

Buena Onda tastes like it is made with love. It has that homemade, fresh-baked, family-meal feel. Upon first bite, I'm momentarily taken away from my surroundings and transported to an Argentinian dining room. The flavors, texture, and aroma ooze with culture. My favorite empanada is the Carne. I love dipping it in their Chimichurri and aioli sauces. 

I highly recommend ordering a dozen and trying a variety of empanadas. They reheat well on the off chance you cannot finish a dozen in one meal. It is not that they are small, it's that they're so delicious you'll want to keep eating them even after you're full. 

The outdoor patio is very inviting for being wedged in the middle of a busy urban street. It's a lovely place to dine alone or gather with friends. You can also enjoy live music a few nights a week under the twinkle of hanging outdoor lights. 

If you don't feel like dining out, call ahead and place an order to go, or have them delivered right to your doorstep via Grubhub. 

For those who have a sweet tooth like yours truly, the fresh baked cookies they sell are a must try! Easily the best cookies I have had in Santa Barbara. My favorite cookies are the Sprinkle and Turtle- moist, chewy goodness!

The food here is great. There is no denying that. That is the reason my wife chose TG's as the caterer for our wedding, We started the process in January and were married in July. It was a simple buffet to feed 120 people. I guess the catering assistant changed a few times so there was some confusion over who we were and what we were order, but that was no big deal. The one thing that the manager of our wedding venue stressed was that the caterer was to clean up and remove the trash, linens and tableware immediately after the wedding, He even went as far as to express hesitation at using TG's because he said that they have a reputation for not providing this service. Despite this, we had the manager, and Michael, the owenr go on a walkthrough of the venue, where the manager told Michael that he needed to clean up afterwards or he could not cater our event.

Fast forward to 3 days before our wedding. The catering assitant tells me that their workers have to leave at 10 and will not be cleaning up after the wedding because they only work for five hours. In addition, if we want the plates and trash removed, we have to have everything broken down at 9pm and we have to pay extra for trash removal and truck rental, because their trucks are being used at other full service events. Had I known this was the case, I would have paid for these services in advance. Michael told me that his priority was the other two events, which was an absolutely unprofessional thing to say given the circumstances. Not only did he not hold true to the conditions set forth by the venue manager, Michael apologetically acted as if he was doing me a favor and I was the reason why these problems were occurring.

I may eat here again, but I will absolutely never use them for catering and will emphatically suggest that others do the same.

My first taste of "real" Chinese food, near as I can tell. Cheap and delicious, you can go nuts and not break the bank. The food comes up pretty quickly too. Their Bao are nice, the tea eggs are awesome, and the noodles are really good. I think my favorite thing so far has been one of their board items, not present on the online or print menu - the braised pork rice. A bed of medium grain rice slathered in a brown five spice gravy with a bunch of tiny pieces of really soft pork belly. Delicious.

If you're tempted by the dumplings, but don't want 30 to yourself (you don't, unless you want to take them home), you can get a half order.

I have been around 10 times now, tried/shared, and taken home large portions to eat as leftovers, the following:
Braise pork rice - damn this is good. As described above
Chicken pea rice - Small diced carrot, chicken, peas and mushrooms over rice. Alright.
Pork noodle - pork stuff from the braised pork rice, some cabbage, noodles, soup base. Good.
Pork and green bean noodle - Similar to above, adding in chopped green beans.
Tomato egg noodle - pretty much exactly what you'd expect
Preserved egg and pork gruel - congee/juk/rice porridge, whatever you want to call it. Big bowl of rice cooked forever, mixed with diced preserved egg and ground pork. My first taste of preserved egg. not 100% on it, but it's good. And at $1.50, a no brainer for a meal on its own almost.
Cabbage and pork wonton - Wontons in broth.
Pork steamed buns - basically looked like har gao but made with pork instead of shrimp. Don't remember the actual name for that.
Mushroom bun - The most interesting bun, chunks of mushrooms and other veggies, these are my favorite.
Pork and cabbage bun - Wasn't sure on the flavor of this one
Meat bun - good but skimpy on the meat.
Fried leek dumpling - Very cooked dough containing a boiling hot center of chopped Chinese leeks. Maybe mine were over cooked, compared to pictures I've seen online. Not a huge fan of these.
Fried dumpling - potstickers, pretty much.
Leek and pork dumpling - Good. Filling not as flavorful as I had hoped, but still really tasty and crazy cheap at $0.50 per large dumpling. 
Tea egg - $0.50 a piece. If you're not familiar, these are awesome. Hard boiled eggs, shells cracked and steeped in a mixture of strong black tea and five spice. The white takes on a cool brown marble effect.

This is not a "stylish" place, but it is impressive for its food and pricing alone. And isn't the food what really matters at a restaurant? I'm thinking I might go try to tomato egg rice today, though I may have to break down and get the braised pork rice again.

I live across Broadway from this place. After Bunbuku, at the same location, closed two and a half years ago, I've been waiting for the space to be re-occupied.
I was excited to see the sign pop up "Coming Soon, Polish Cottage"
A couple weeks ago, I saw a couple folks working inside and pulled off Broadway. They said they would be opening on 9/23/11, and they didn't have a menu yet. Yesterday arrived, but we had some other plans, so we decided to come here for lunch today.
I splurged a bit and got a plate of six mushroom and sauerkraut perogi with bacon and onions, and an order of bigos, a polish hunter's stew.
The perogi were fantastic, the stew was quite good too. Be aware there's a LOT of sauerkraut and vinegar flavor in it, though, so be sure you're in the mood for such a thing.
The pluses: 
Affordable (no plates over $10)
Tasty
Everything made in house
Friendly
Atmosphere, lots of interesting things around, the whole restaurant is painted sky blue
Seems to be a family operation, the owners have Polish accents and names. Good sign!

The minuses:
Plating fell a little flat. Normally don't care much about this sort of thing, but the plating for both dishes was main order, with a bit of chopped lettuce off to one side, on heavy cafeteria style plates. 
Meals, unless specified, are totally ala cart. Perogis are just perogis. The bigos came with a roll. Ala cart is nice for trying more things, but I wasn't expecting it really. Maybe offer a "combo" with a side/soup and a drink or something?

A very easy 5 stars for me. I was greeted at the bar by Ira, who is the epitome of what a great bartender is. Right away, he asks my name and used it a few times that night. I like that special touch so few bartenders bother with anymore. My grandfather owned bars and he knew everyone's name and always used it. Ira, while not old at all, is definitely a throw back. Him alone will have me going back. 

Now the food, we decided to stay at the bar to eat. The crab meat cocktail was loaded with crab. It really was a healthy portion. The filet was cooked to perfection as well. 

This place has a secure place in my bookmarks. If you stop in and see Ira, tell him "Rich with the tie" says hello.

Eh...

I could honestly just end the review there. Pat's, the King of Steaks? Perhaps more like a naked Prince Harry? That works. 

Being that its notoriety spans the globe, I suppose I just expected more. It wasn't awful, but it definitely ranks in the bottom percentile among other cheese steaks I've had everywhere outside of Philly. 

On the plus side, it was as fast as a greased pig getting my order, even though the line spanned about 20 deep. For a quick bite, their execution was flawless. As for the taste, not so much....

Ready? Watch this: 5 fucking stars.

Where to start. Well, were in Tucson on business. We get told that if you want the real deal, you need to have Poca Cosa. Family owned, family recipes handed down, just solid food. I don't know what i was expecting.. That's not true, i know what i was expecting, i was expecting a better version of El Charro, because we ate there the night before. Wow. Was i wrong.

Have you ever tried to determine what your final meal would be? You're headed for the chair, one last meal, yeah, that game. I never knew. I am not exaggerating when i say I have now found it. Poca Cosa is incredible.

So, we show up wearing jeans, tshirts and ball caps. We walk in after looking at the specials board outside. I immediately recognize that we are severely underdressed. This is collared shirt, stem wear, evening dresses on a Saturday date night. We look like a couple of chimps. Auto-correct wrote 'chimps' there. I meant to say 'chumps' but either one works.

A lovely lady at the front asks us what name our reservation is under, we inform her we do not have one and, do we need one? She responded by laughing. She said she would see what she could do. Im thinking were getting the high hard one.

*Moments* later she says she is still working on getting us a table and, would we like to sit at the bar and have a drink? Why, yes, yes we would. After a absolutely smashing house margarita, the hostess stops by to tell us that our table should be ready by the time we are drunk. Alright, I'm starting to like this lady. One of the bartenders drops a sangria pitcher, she screams "your fired!" at him and then looks at us smiling, "it's ok, he's my son" she tells us. Holy shit, mom is awesome. Family recipes, we ask? Absolutely she tells us. We love mom.

We get a table, the waiter, Jeff, comes over and is carrying what i think is the specials board. He informs us that there are no menus and the specials board are the only choices and it changes twice daily. Holy crap.

3 chicken dishes, 3 steak dishes, 3 fish and or vegetarian dishes, *or* take the chefs choice of three for $25. Um, yeah, i think we gotta do that. Goddamn this is a good gimlet.

Food comes out and, wow, i just can't explain how good this is. The steak is slow roasted and smokey with roasted veggies, along with a peanut based mole sauce on the chicken and a tamale pie that would have laid down in traffic for. Mom stops back by. We ask if there is a room in the back we can both move in to. She doesn't think we would like it because as she puts it "she cracks the whip". At this point, i would willingly submit. Food is so. Goddamn. Good.

She asks if we want dessert. Im about to tap out but i figure, hell, everything else has been so good, why not? I ask her to pick and she sends out a flour less chocolate cake with fresh hot fudge on top with a handful of fresh berries. Do i even need to go into it by now?

The last thing our waiter Jeff asked (who, by the by, is also fucking incredible) was can he get us anything else. Why yes, i told him: a round of applause for everyone who works here.

Unfortunately, they are closed on Sunday's and Monday's, so we were unable to come back the days we were in town, but as Poca Cosa has now set the bar by which all other mexican dishes will be judged, we are absolutely going back.

And guess what? Mom is not only the hostess AND owner, she's the chef as well. Epic win.

We stumbled on this place when another nearby restaurant we were trying to go to was closed. We had no idea just how popular this place is or anything about their ordering system. I'm not sure if this is just how they operate during Covid or always but you will need to pre-order your pies on their site and pick them up because they have a limited amount of dough per day. Luckily for us they had extra dough that day and we were able to walk up and order. Service was friendly and so accommodating. We ordered a square white pie and a circle pie. Both were off the charts DELICIOUS!! 
Don't come unprepared like us. We got super lucky. We couldn't have been any happier with our pizzas!
There is literally something for everyone here. Huge variety of foods and drinks. It is pretty crowded and like most of these types of markets not much seating to really enjoy what you get to eat.

Mexican food near Marana! On UberEats! Aaaand GREAT food! Now that's a win/win/win. If you find yourself in this little town outside Tucson--OR maybe at the Ritz Carlton at Dove Mountain--and a craving for authentic Mexican food strikes, THIS. IS. IT.

We got tacos, cheese enchiladas, chicken enchilada, and our favorite of the night: ground beef quesadilla. Mind blown. I never thought a quesadilla could be so good. Sure, it sounds pretty basic, but it was perfect and reminded me of an exponentially better version of an enchirito from Taco Bell, which I happen to really like  (where my enchirito lovers at?!). Tacos were not great, but the cheese enchilada was good, the shredded chicken in the the chicken enchilada was pretty moist and tasty (even though it was suppose to be another all-cheese quesadilla), refried beans were good, and their salsa tasted freshly made and super flavorful.

It was annoying that they messed up our order, AND forgot one of our items but we still enjoyed our massive feast. (The bathroom did not).

But hey, we'd do it all again. Especially the beef quesadilla! And extra salsa :)

My work colleague stayed here at the Peppermill, so we met up at Biscotti's for lunch before we headed out to the airport. It may be a little difficult to find, we had to ask for directions from the hotel staff to find it.  It's near the pool so just go towards that and look for signs.

It's a pretty big restaurant, a lot of tables for small groups and large groups. Menu is huge so choose wisely. I decided to get the "Giardino Flatbread Wrap". I wanted something more on the healthy side and this was a pretty good pick.  It had quinoa, kale sprouts, roasted peppers, cucumbers, tomatoes, and some basil aioli all wrapped up in a wrap. Comes with a side so I got fries to make it even more healthy. It was all pretty good, huge sized wrap, you can ask for dipping sauces if you want.  

My coworker had the "Chinese Chicken Salad", it was absolutely a gigantic portion, it's like they opened one of those salad bags you get from the grocery store and put it in a fish bowl. No issues with the salad as she enjoyed it very much, but it was huge!  

Staff was fine, friendly, talkative and didn't take long to get our food and our lunch was pretty fast, prices aren't too bad but you get your portions worth with the pricing. Good option at this hotel if you don't want buffet style or fine dining and such. 

Glad we chose this spot for lunch, then we took the complimentary shuttle to the airport.

I stayed at the Whitney Peak on business and upon my arrival, I decided to check out the restaurant attached to the hotel. When inside the hotel, it's just left when entering. If you cant find it, ask the front desk or valet.

We decided to do take-out and eat in our rooms as we had some work to work on. Shared some foods so we ordered a few items from the menu. We started with the "Fish Shack Shrimp". It was pretty good, pretty simple. It's basically battered shrimp served on top of spinach and some dressing to dip. I'm all about simplistic. Shrimp was good, good amounts of shrimp, medium to larger sized shrimps, we killed it.  

We also ordered a "Dave's Flatbread" (I don't know who Dave is), it had chicken, caramelized onions, peppers, and a good amount of cheese. It was pretty much a pizza. Pretty tasty, good for sharing, they give you shredded parmesan slivers and chili flakes off to the side in your pizza box.

We had a drink at the bar while we waited for our food, bartender was super friendly, helpful and nice. Nice looking place inside, good for groups, nice looking menus, available for breakfast, lunch and dinner, they do the food for room service if you dare. 

Overall, glad we got food here.

Tucson finally has good boba tea where you can TASTE the tea. The other boba shops I've visited in Tucson uses powders and the boba is often soggy or frozen (as previously mentioned). A good indication that they care about tea is that they have a pop/hot tea section where they brew fresh tea individually for your drink. Teas listed include (to name a few) oolong, Alishan, iron goddess (tieguanyin), oriental beauty, matcha, sencha, pu-er, jasmine, green, black, roasted / brown rice, house, etc. The last places I've seen teas like this listed in Tucson is at Seven Cups and Ausperitea. Or course we can't compare those kinds of tea shops to a sweetened boba tea shop but it shows they care about tea and the flavors teas add. Also I understand teas like Alishan and iron goddess are types of oolong so one of these days I'll ask what is their actual "oolong" or "house" tea.  

Then to top it off they have good toppings like red bean, pudding (egg/custard flavor), mousse,  grass jelly, lots of flavored jellies, etc. Oh how I've missed red bean and grass jelly in drinks and shaved ice here in Tucson! Of course for those who like ... umm... added flavors there is taro, passion fruit, pomelo to name a few. To give you more options you can specify percentage of sugar added (I've seen 0%, 30%, 50%, 80%, 100% sugar). Wonder if they will do so odd number like 37.5%? 

The boba so far has been consistent and has the right amount of "chew". Something to keep in mind is that it takes them 2 hrs to make a fresh batch and as they don't freeze them (to my knowledge) if they run out 1.5 hours before close you will not get any boba. I totally understand and respect they make fresh boba.  

So far I've tried their matcha redbean and grass jelly, roasted tea with grass jelly (very complimentary), house coffee milk tea with boba, oolong with red beans and grass jelly. As the toppings are sweet I got 50% sugar and they still tastes good.  All a delight so far. 

Some of their teas are from Taiwan obviously as there is a sign that say, "Funky Original Taiwanese Flavors."  

I will be going back regularly until I've tried most if not all the combinations. They also have good size tables so I might have my game night there next time. Catan, Munchkins or Dominion anyone? ;)

P.S. Yes this is not a boba shop found in LA, NY, SF or asia but pretty darn close.  If you're doing a road trip compliment this visit with a visit to Phoenix Snoh Ice Shavery!

Niquan at the front desk really went the extra mile to make our stay at The W amazing! She was so accommodating. She sent a beautiful gift up to our room for my birthday- so nice! Our room was beautiful, spacious and so clean. Thank you so much Niquan!!

The food at Sasha's is OK and the neighborhood needs a spot that's outside of the business district to hang out at, but I have always received less than stellar service at Sasha's, to the point of being neglected.  

To make matters worse, I planned a large group happy hour there for a Tuesday night.  Terms were agreed upon with Tom the Manager in advance, but the night before the proposed event, he decided to tell us that the price would be higher, knowing that we had already advertised the event.  

When I tried to talk to him about it he was completely inflexible, didn't care at all that the event had already been promoted and said "you are not winning me over."  Sorry Tom, I didn't realize it was the customers job to "win you over." 

In the end, I felt it was in our best interest to move the advertised event last minute.  I hate doing that, but I was not comfortable with how Tom does business and was concerned that it would only get worse.  I have no plans of returning.  I usually give restaurants the benefit of the doubt when things go wrong, but a bad attitude from Management is unacceptable.  Better brush up on your people skills Tom.  You need customers to stay open.

BTW, the bar we moved our event to (The Heavy Anchor) was filled up by our group on what would have been a slow night.  They bent over backwards for us, made a ton of money and each of the bartenders made several hundred of dollars in tips, in 2 hours.  Not bad for a Tuesday night from 6-8 pm.  Your loss Tom.

Inside, McGurk's is like a true Irish Pub, except the customers are mostly American.  Unlike most Irish pubs in St. Louis, the owner flies musicians in directly from Ireland and puts them up in his digs next door.  They know how to poor a pint of Guiness (most bars in the STL don't) and you can usually find "Lucky" (the token Irishman) behind the bar.  

The crowd is pretty vanilla (yes, that means white). It seems that county folk will venture into the hood in droves, to visit McGurk's (Soulard is pretty safe and has their own security force, as well as, a solid police presence, but we still have scaredie-cats out there).
 
Inside the restaurant, it looks like a pub. The restaurant is centered around one of three bars.  There are brick walls and archways everywhere.  The restaurant is filled with Irish music, Guinness drinkers galore, and an occasional drunken Yank giving their best attempt to demonstrate an Irish jig.
  
Outside is an entirely different environment.  They have a massive garden patio in the back.  It's one of the nicest beer gardens in town that includes a pond with waterfall, two bars, and beautiful landscaping.  During the day, it's a great environment for an outdoor lunch, at night the patio is filled up with lots of young hotties on the prowl.  The patio is covered, heated, and enclosed in the winter.

The menu offers a variety of Irish and American faves.  They are known for their fish and for their Irish stew.  I personally recommend the mushrooms... awesome!  Nothing on the menu is bad.  Some of the entrees are pricy.  But, if you are on a budget, they have a great sandwich and salad menu that will not disappoint.

I'm so happy that the famous south city landmark Bevo Mill has been reincarnated into its restored form as the new restaurant, biergarten and event venue Das Bevo.  The Boo Cat Club, Majorette and Sugarfire Smoke House peeps have gone out of their way to create a real treasure.  This place is something to see.  Besides the obvious windmill feature on the exterior, it's grand hall is truly unique.  Now they are offering a full menu (under $15) and Sunday brunch.   I have sampled a few items like pork schnitzel  sandwich, roasted chicken, mac n cheese and some
tasty bevs and so far, they didn't disappoint.  American with a German twist!

This is a great little mom & pop Gyro house on Gravois, near Hampton.  They serve tasty wraps, subs, gyros, falafel sandwiches, specialty pita pizzas, salads and scrumptious desserts, including baklava and tiramisu.  There is not an item on the menu that is over $6.  Average price is $4.50.

They have a substantial carry out business; a small, no frills indoor dining area and some outdoor seating.  

The owners (a mother & her two sons) are incredibly friendly.  In fact, when we found out that they only take checks or cash (we had neither), they told us to go ahead and order and that we could come back and pay them later.  Say what?  We're customers for life now...

The doner kabob, gyro, salads, and desserts are pretty phenomenol.  I haven't tried the wraps or pizzas yet, but they are cheap and sound yummy.  The falafel is a little dry.

Bogart's is an awesome smokehouse that just opened behind the historic Soulard Market on 9th Street. Run by the same Chef that has made Pappy's such a hot number (no he hasn't left Pappy's).  Skip, decided to open his own place with blessings from the owners of Pappy's. 

The set up is different. Order at the counter, get your drinks and have a seat. Listen to some background blue grass music and Skip or one of his staff members will bring your food to you at your seat. I just met Skip today (their first day open). Total sweetheart. Service was friendly and excellent. The place was packed, but Skip took the time to not only sit and chat, but he also brought out samples of meats that we didn't order. 

Similarities to Pappy's: 
The pulled pork is the same 
Sweet Meagan KC BBQ sauce is the same 
Turkey is the same 
Beef Brisket (yum) is the same 
Potato Salad (not homemade) is the same 

Differences: 
House smoked pastrami (yum) 
House smoked prime rib (yum) 
Awesome baked beans (homemade) 
Good Slaw (homemade) 
Awesome ribs 
homemade sauces (except for the Sweet Meagan KC Barbecue Sauce)

Their hours are Tues - Sat 10:30 AM - "4ish"

The draw for this locally owned chain restaurant (3 locations) is that this particular location sits on the best corner in the Central West End (lots of action, people watching, etc.).  It is especially nice if you are lucky enough to get an outside table on a warm summer night. 

Another draw is that they have phenomenal happy hours, where most of the sushi, appetizers and specialty martinis are either discounted or half price (only in the bar upstairs). Happy hour runs M-F from 5:00-7:00 PM. 

On Wednesdays, they offer free sushi and pot-stickers via buffet from 5-6 pm (in the upstairs bar). You need to get there early to get a seat and plan to dine along side a hungry pack of starving college students who are pretty quick to empty the buffet. 

The down side of dining here is that while they have a large variety to choose from, much of the sushi is average, service can suck at times, and this location can be noisy. Also, they have no dedicated parking. 

I will admit, because of the location and great happy hour deals, I am a fan. I mean hey, reasonable quality maki for $2.50-$4 ea order ?  Now that's what I call a deal!!  Reservations are a must if you have a group.

Polite Society is a new restaurant located in Lafayette Square in the former home of Ricardo's.  They did a great job making use of an old building that has great architectural features. The menu is new American, steaks, burgers, tofu steaks with cauliflower rice, roasted chicken breast, sweet potato spaetzle, etc and  a full bar.  I had the mussels and they were to die for.  In fact, the best I've had in St Louis!  Great atmosphere.  So glad to have them in the neighborhood!  They are just getting started.  So, they are currently only serving dinner.

Elaia is a great new restaurant located in a 1930's filling station in McCree Town on Tower Grove Ave, just blocks from the MOBOT (Botanical Gardens).  The owner runs the amazing Salume Beddu on Hampton and has really made an investment in an area that bridges the Shaw and Southwest Garden neighborhoods to The Grove. 

The decor is industrial meets fine dining.  They have a wine bar (Oleo) connected on one side and a new bakery that is set to open across the street (the bakery may be owned by someone else?).  

Elaia has some of the crafted meat and cheese platters that you can find at Salume Beddu, as well as fresh food and great wine list.  I actually ate before I got there.  So, I only had a small sampling, but I plan to come back to try more of it so that I can give a more detailed review. In fact, I can't wait to get back!!  The entire menu looks awesome!  I definitely think that this is a restaurant worth trying.  The menu is small and consists of mostly cheese and meat plates, salads, some seafood and sandwiches.  They have a braised stew on the dinner menu.  This is a very small fine dining establishment better suited for a night without the kiddos.

When I say filth, I'm not talking about anything being rough around the edges.  I'm talking about dirt and grime, behind the serving counter, on the display cases, up and down the walls and on the tables.  The baseboards in the entry way and throughout the restaurant don't look like they have ever been cleaned.  And the area that they are making our smoothies and coffee drinks in have been covered with grime the last few times I have been there.

My favorite places are those little boutique style restaurants, coffee houses, and bars that are located inside neighborhoods, because I know that a lot of love goes into these businesses.  So, when I give a bad review about one of these places, it doesn't come lightly.  Dirty restaurants deserve to be criticized because it is a problem that is so easy to fix and they are putting our health at risk.

My personal view is that Kaldi's is focusing on new modernized locations and is ignoring the "Mother-ship."  I challenge everyone to visit this Kaldi's location and have a look around.  It's not hard to see.

Gattuso's is located in the heart of downtown Gretna on Huey P. Long Ave. As you walk in there is a bar, and to your left is the seating area. The seating area is meant to be an outside patio, but they have vinyl walls that allow it to be air conditioned when it is hot.

We grabbed a seat and our waitress took our drink orders. She wasn't overly pleasant, but she did quickly fill our drink order. I ordered the sloppy roast beef and my buddy ordered the brisket sandwich. Both came with fries.

The roast beef was excellent. Imagine a roast cooked till fork tender and cut into chunks. The bread was authentic (highly important). It ranks in the the top five roast beef po-boys I have ever had. It isn't giant, but with the fires, it is more than enough food.

The brisket sandwich was good and juicy, despite having no sauce.

I was not thrilled with the waitress. She wasn't horrible, but she wasn't phenomenal either. Maybe she had a rough day, but she could have been nicer.

The reason I give Gattuso's four stars is the roast beef po-boy. It was so good I wish I had ordered two. It was that good.

Our total with one drink and a water was $25 with a tip. I will definitely return.

Waking Bakin is a small, but great breakfast place in Mid-City. 

I am really a lucky guy. I have some pretty awesome Yelp friends who have steered me to some great places lately. In particular Danon, Charles and Michelle were all so complimentary of thins place that I knew I had to try it. 

There was some weird construction going on in the area so I worried that parking would be an issue. Luckily for me, I scored a spot right out front. It was apparently such a good spot that some of the diners out front even commented how awesome I was. Ok, I may have made that last part up, but it was an awesome spot. 

Inside was warm and inviting. The restaurant is small, actually tiny, but very comfortably laid out. Despite the small size, the tables were spaced far enough apart that I didn't feel like neighboring tables were practicing their eavesdropping skills. 

Food was simple, but very good. I opted for a make your own omelet with hash browns. The hash browns were perfectly cooked and not overly greasy. The omelet was thin with a perfect egg to stuff ratio. That ratio is vital to a good omelet and they got it right. My coffee was served in a mug that I think was originally a soup bowl with a handle. It held at least two cups. Considering my caffeine addiction, it was much appreciated. 

Prices were very reasonable for the product received. The staff were all helpful, friendly and welcoming. 

I really liked Wakin Bakin and think you will too.

This may be the most difficult review I have ever had to write.

I have wanted to go to Cafe Giovanni for years. In the mid to late 90's I worked down the street from Giovanni. Chef Duke would always come by, and was one of the nicest guys you could ever meet. From everything I have read, and heard on the radio, he is still a great guy who does a lot for the community. In addition, I have continually heard how great his restaurant is, especially the "feed me" special. All of this built up great anticipation for my meal which made my experience that much worse when it failed to meet my lofty expectations.

I assumed I would need reservations so I booked using open table (I love open table and think every restaurant should use it). The booking was simple, and when we arrived we were immediately seated.

We were seated at a two top on the side of the restaurant. It was comfortable, and since there was a wall behind us, it made us feel like we had more privacy. One drawback was that our view of the opera singers was a bit restricted. That's right, I said opera singers. There were three opera singers singing throughout the meal. They were incredible. While I have been to the opera, I have never been this close to such amazing singers. 

Our server was very friendly. She explained the special Lenten feed me menu which was priced at $55. She did say that there was no wine pairing option with this menu which seemed odd, as the website lists wine pairing for the Lenten meal for an additional $25. We wanted the full experience so we inquired about the full Chef Duke feed me meal. She explained that it had one additional course (dessert) that the Lenten menu did not have along with a few different entrees. She mentioned that this was also available with wine pairing, but never mentioned the price. I realize that I probably should have asked, but I figured one additional course wouldn't be much more, and since the Lenten wine pairing was $25, i figured the pairing for the full feed me would be comparable. Boy was I wrong (more on that later).

The feed me consisted of several small appetizer portions and included:

Oysters Giovanni - Three perfectly fried oysters atop a "stained glass" of sauces. This was a very good dish. I  am not sure what all of the sauces were, but mixed together, they complemented the oysters very well.

Spicy seafood caprese plate - This was the best dish of the night. Lump crabmeat, shrimp and crawfish mixed with a wonderful white sauce atop a tomato and mozzarella. It was wonderful.

Ravioli - This dish came with a red sauce and was my least favorite. After the first two dishes, I expected to be wowed by the flavor, but it was very underwhelming. While not bad, I didn't really care for it.

Grilled fish - This was my second least favorite dish. I was again expecting to be wowed, but wasn't. The fish was cooked well, but seemed somewhat ordinary. 

Duke's fillet - This tiny piece of fillet came atop a bed of potatoes with fried leeks on top. The fillet and potatoes were very good. The fried leeks added an odd texture to the food and I would have rather had the steak without this addition.

Bread pudding - This was a great dessert. 

Since we opted for the wine pairing we had four (or five, I can't remember) small pours of wine. I would guess these were around 2-3 ounces per pour. The wine wasn't spectacular, but did go well with the food it was paired with.

We really enjoyed the opera singers, a few of the dishes and the atmosphere. Several of the dishes were not bad, but weren't impressive either.

The main shock came when the bill arrived. The bill listed two feed me meals with wine at $65 per person. Listed under that wording was an additional line that read wine tasting $45 (or some similar verbiage). The total was over $240. Because of the way the pricing and explanation was printed, it appeared I had been double charged for the wine. I asked the waitress and she said "oops" and explained she must have double charged us, and would go and immediately correct the problem. Upon returning she told us that she was mistaken, and that we were properly charged. Since I hadn't inquired originally to the price, I didn't argue and paid the bill. With tip the meal cost nearly $300. Here is my issue with that:

1. We received one additional course, and possibly one additional pour of wine over what the Lenten feed me offered. Was this meal worth an additional $10 for food, and an additional $25 for wine? In my mind, no way. 

2. The food was not spectacular. For $300, I can dine anywhere in the city and receive stellar food and service. This meal did not meet those standards.

3. The server was incredibly uninformed since she admitted she overcharged us, then recanted upon speaking to a manager. Had she explained when I originally asked if I was double billed, I wouldn't be so frustrated.

I really wanted to like Giovanni. In the end, it left me feeling completely unsatisfied, and actually a bit mad.

I am a big fan of businesses that believe in truth in advertising. Trying to figure out what a business sells is occasionally difficult based on name alone, but that isn't a problem here. The location (District) and products (donuts, sliders and brew) are all part of the name. I sure wish other businesses would follow that trend.

I normally like to give new businesses a chance to work out the kinks before I spend my hard earned money. I made an exception for DDSB because many of the reviews, including sources I trust, have been very positive. So positive that I decided to drive into the city last Sunday just to give them a try.
People seemed to be milling about when I first walked in so I joined them. I apparently picked the correct place to stand since once the group moved, I was able to place my order. In the name of research, I ordered one of each type of meat slider that was available. At $3.50 per slider, they weren't cheap, but they were very good.

Cheeseburger Slider - This was actually my least favorite of the three I tried, but it was still good. It was dressed with a tomato, pickle, cheese and mayo. This mini burger was a significant step up from a Krystal or Castle Burger, but the other versions were more impressive.

Chicken Slider - The perfectly fried piece of chicken was very tasty. The addition of the coleslaw, jalapeno and unknown sauce really improved this slider dramatically. Without those additions, it would've been a reasonably good chicken sandwich, but with them, it was something much better.

Special Slider (Pork Belly) - If you are a fan of pork, you will love this slider. I have not fully embraced the pork fad that is sweeping the nation, but this slider may have changed my mind. The pork belly was tender and succulent which I assume is directly related to its high fat content. Once I took a bite I didn't care if it was pure fat, as it was pure goodness. The addition of the sprout looking stuff and the red onion really set this slider apart from the other two. I hope this becomes one of their regular menu items.

I regret that I did not try any of their coffee or kolaches. As far as I know, this is the first business to sell kolaches in the city. For those of you who have not tried a kolache, you must do that as soon as possible. You will thank me later. 
My one complaint is the size of the water I ordered to go with my sliders. I realize they didn't charge for the tiny cup they gave me, but it was at best three small sips before the cup was empty. That averaged out to one sip per slider which was definitely not enough to keep me hydrated. 

I really enjoyed my trip here and suspect I will soon become a regular.

My name is John and although I am scared to admit it, I was once a west banker. There's not much I miss about the westbank, but if I made a list, Salvo's would be at the top. I'm just kidding about being embarrassed to be from the 1.5, but I most certainly not joking about Salvo's. 

I've been coming here for seafood for longer than I can remember. This is one of the best, most consistent seafood restaurants anywhere in the area. If they u haven't been, you need to change that ASAP. 

The Place

Salvo's is not fancy. During lunch you order at the counter and dinner has servers who take your order and bring out the food. The parking lot is not paved, small and sometimes very crowded. None of that matters though because of the food. 

The Food

I have yet to have a bad meal here. The boiled seafood is especially good. On many different occasions I started my meal with boiled shrimp and just took my main entree to go because I ended up ordering more shrimp. 

If you're re not in the mood for boiled, their fried seafood is also very good. My favorite is their shrimp po-boy which I'd argue is the best on the west bank. 

In summary, Salvo's is the place for seafood. It's worth a drive from most anywhere.

There is no better coffee shop in New Orleans. 

Everyone knows that when you frequent a place you get to know the employees and customers, and they know you. It makes each trip a little more special and enjoyable. Mojo is definitely that place for me. 

When I leave town and have to get coffee somewhere else, I feel lost. Mojo has great employees, great customers and most importantly, great coffee. 

This is a great place to study, work or just hang out and people watch. 

It isn't for everyone, but Mojo is definitely one of my all time favorite places.

WTF Yelp?

I begin my review this way because CDM was one of my first reviews when I joined Yelp. In their infinite wisdom they decided to remove my review without telling me. Or maybe CDM made. New listing and got the other one deleted. Anyway, here I am, and here is my review. 

Cafe du Monde is a New Orleans institution. Talk poorly of it and you're likely going to be haunted by the bronze woman leaning against the fountain in the back. 

You come to CDM not because the service is the best, because it isn't. You come here for one of two reasons. Figure out your reason and you'll know what kind of experience to have. 

1. You're a tourist - This is a must see. Get begniets and coffee or chocolate milk. Take photos for your facesnap account and let everyone know you're in Nawlins. You will probably give it a low rating and complain about everything. Or you won't and you'll get why this place is so special. 

2. You've been coming here all your life - This is the category I fit into. I have been coming here since I was a little boy. The minute I walk under their roof I am filled with the fond memories of sitting here with my family, trying to blow powdered sugar all over my brothers, or them trying to blow powdered sugar on me. 

My most recent experience here was with my oldest kid on her birthday. We sat down, each ordered begniets, and had a chocolate milk. Service was ok, the begniets were ok, and the chocolate milk was great. More importantly, my kid and I will have a memory of sitting here on her birthday. That's what CDM is really about. 

So figure out if you're a tourist or a local, but come here and make some memories.

P & G is a great value at lunch.

A fellow Yelper suggested I try P&G and I am glad that I listened. The restaurant is set up like a diner. You enter, order at the counter, get your food, pay and find a seat. 

One of the daily specials was red beans so I didn't need to look any further. The portion was very large. In fact, my entire plate was covered with so much that it was difficult to carry back to the table without spilling some. I opted for hot sausage, but they also had plain smoked sausage. The red beans were very good. While not spicy, the beans were well seasoned. 

All of the staff I encountered were very friendly. Although there was no traditional server, employees were circulating asking if customers needed refills, etc. This was a nice touch since most diner style restaurants are self-serve for drinks.

There is a cool looking courtyard area towards the back of the restaurant. This area had at least six turtles crawling around. While you can't sit out there, the tables nearest this area are the best spots to sit.

I will definitely keep P&G in the lunch spot rotation.

If you are looking for simple, good food and don't want to break the bank, try P&G.

Forget the po-boy. Dong Phuong's Bahn Mi is the best sandwich in New Orleans. 

Before you break out the pitchforks I want you to hear me out. I will always be a fan of roast beef and shrimp po-boys, but DP's sandwiches make me question my loyalty to the traditional po-boy. 

Located in New Orleans East, Dong Phuong is a restaurant, bakery and sandwich stop. For years I've heard how amazing their sandwiches were, but I was rarely out in the east particularly not during lunchtime. But things have changed and I've found myself working in the most remote section of Nola. Just to give you an idea of how much I like this place, I ate here 3 days this week. 

The Bahn mi menu here is extensive. There are around 17 different types and all start at $3.25. That's right. $3.25. So far I've tried the Chinese roast pork, Vietnamese roast pork, BBQ chicken and Vietnamese sausage. Every one shocked me with just how good it was, but the Vietnamese sausage is my favorite. The sandwiches are very simple. The bread is baguette style and baked in house. There is a light coating of aioli on the bread, pickled vegetables and the main ingredient. It's so simple that you would think it would be dry and boring. But whatever chemical reaction happens upon combining those ingredients the result is heaven in your mouth.

I realize that the location leaves a lot to be desired because it is so far from civilization, but trust me, it's worth the trip. I can't think of anywhere else in the city you can get food this good for under $5.

Why are you still reading? Get to Dong Phuong now.

This is a review of the bar during brunch. When I think brunch, I don't think of a bar. Hell, when I think brunch I normally think of a meal that is a worthless invention. Luckily I have some friends who don't subscribe to my ridiculous views and they set up a fun brunch to meet and greet some Yelpers from Portland. 

When I walked up, I was a little reluctant. The door was locked and I had to be buzzed in. Normally that means I'm in a dangerous place, but once inside I realized I was not. The bar has a very neighborhood bar feel, but the owner/bartender was very welcoming and friendly. He was also making an excellent old fashioned for $5. Not only did he take his time making the drink, but he also tasted it from his stirrer to make sure it was just right. 

The bar wasn't very crowded and our large group had half of the place to ourselves. We were even able to play some great songs on the jukebox. It wasn't the internet connected variety, but there were some great, local hits. 

I really liked this bar. I hope someone else organizes more bar brunch outings here.

Do you ever want to start a review with a stream of expletives to exclaim your joy or disgust? I get that feeling often, but usually refrain to avoid seeming like a simpleton. It was ore difficult to abstain when writing this review because Blue Oak is mother lovin good. 

Food - Blue Oak served a damn fine brisket platter with a combination of fatty and lean brisket. The brisket was moist, flavorful and had a very tasty bark. The meat was not as smoky as I like, but that is a minor complaint. It was very good. 

The sides were not as good as the brisket. The potato salad needed more umph maybe from more creole mustard. It was creamy with firm potatoes like I like, but lacked flavor. The mac n cheese was ok and improved greatly by my addition of jerk BBQ sauce. 

While the brisket platter was a great supporting actor, the brisket nachos won the oscar. Those nachos took up an entire sheet pan and were loaded with chopped brisket, cheese and a plethora of goodness. My one minor complaint is that there were a good deal of chips left alone with no toppings, but damn those things were good. 

Service was friendly and helpful. The guy taking orders was welcoming and offered great suggestions. Seating is kind of community style if the place gets crowded, but was not bad when we went. Take that into account if you value privacy when it gets crowded. 

I need to get back sooner rather than later for more nachos and I definitely want to try their wings.

Mais Arepas is my favorite new restaurant. It is so good, that after trying it once, I came back at least four more times in a few weeks. It is not often that a brand new place earns five stars, but this place is truly wonderful.

The location

Located on CL-10 and Carondelet, parking is a bit of an issue. I suggest trying for a spot on Carondelet, or across the street on Clio if the spots in front are taken. 

The atmosphere

I absolutely adore the atmosphere inside. I think it has to do with the latin/Caribbean/world music they play. It is physically impossible to not be in a good mood while listening to that music. Every time I walk in, I get an ear to ear grin. 

The service

There is a woman who works here that is one of the friendliest servers I have ever had. Not only was she a great server, but she made me feel so welcomed that even had the food been just OK, I would still come back for more. Oftentimes overly friendly servers come off as disingenuous, but this lady was the real deal. OK, enough gushing, now on to the real reason for the five stars.

The food

I cannot believe that I have gone this long without ever trying an arepas. Imagine two pita shaped corn thingys surrounding amazing ingredients and you might begin to understand what it is. I have tried many on their menu, but the mechada and carnicera are my favorites.

I realize that my review does not fully convey how much I like this place. Just ignore my mediocre writing skills and get yourself there as soon as humanly possible.

Guy's is an excellent poor boy shop.

I am on a quest to find the world's best roast beef poor boy. Guy's version ranks very close to the top.

After reading the reviews, and passing this location numerous times, I was determined to try Guy's. I had tried getting a sandwich here numerous times before, but my timing never worked out. It seemed I always showed up after closing time, but this time I was successful.

Guy's is what a neighborhood poor boy shop should be. It isn't fancy, but their sandwiches are first class. One the day I visited Guy himself was making the sandwiches. From what I have heard, only one or two people are allowed to make the sandwiches. I think that is a good thing because the quality will remain consistent.

My roast beef was nearly perfect. Guy's version uses sliced roast beef and is obviously homemade. The meat to dressing ratio was excellent, and the regular size was more than enough food.

Their version was somewhat messy and required around 15 napkins to wipe the gravy from my hands. This is not a sandwich to eat if you're concerned with getting dirty.

Service was very friendly and prompt. 

I really enjoyed Guy's and think it will become one of my go-to spots for a great poor boy.

"Oh yeah oh yeah oh yeah"

Anytime you hear that coming from a neighboring table, you know one of three things. The food is incredible good, the people at the table are extremely irritating, or there is something going on under the table. On this particular night, I think it may have been a combination of all three. 

The Joint is my favorite BBQ restaurant in the city. It is the perfect combination of great food, funky ambiance and weird local vibe. 

The Food

This is real BBQ. The brisket, ribs and pulled pork are stellar. The brisket has the perfect amount of bite, smoke and flavor. This is the best brisket I have had other than a few places in Texas. The ribs are equally smokey, but so tender it will melt with flavor in your mouth in a way that only pork can. Speaking of pork, their pulled pork is also wonderful. Add the mustard based vinegar sauce and you have a smokey, spicy batch of awesomeness. 

Funky Ambiance

The joint is a small place. There is seating inside and at the bar, but you're likely to have people's junk all up in your area while they wait in line. If you just sit inside, sit at the tables to the right as you enter or at the bar. I highly recommend outside if the weather is decent. The outside ambiance reminds me of being in someone's backyard minus the dude making love to his brisket. 

Weird Local Vibe

The neighborhood is very unique. Directly across from the entrance is an empty lot with a large tree. Hanging in that tree is a swing and you should not be surprised if you notice some odd person deciding 10:00pm is a great time to swing from a tree yelling yippie. Another odd thing is the sheer number of bicyclists. I counted at least 50 that passed by my truck. I'm all for saving gas, but these folks seem to think the own the road. I'm talking zooming by with no concern for their own safety. Pardon me fine sir, but in the battle of 5000 lb truck vs 80 pound hipster, the truck is going to win. I'd use caution when disregarding a stop sign on your bike. 

In summary, the Joint is awesome. Come here and you will leave happy.

Le's Baguette Bahn Mi is excellent.

Located down the street from one of my all time favorite restaurants, I only discovered Le's because of Yelp. Shout out to Jen L. for cluing me into this spot because I loved it.

My visit to Le's was to place, and pickup, a to-go order. I arrived around 11 and the place was empty. That was a huge plus for me because it meant I was in and out in just a few minutes. The space itself is rather narrow with a small dining room on the right side as you enter. Despite that layout, the tables seemed well spaced from one another. I am rarely in this area of the city for long, but I could totally see eating in without feeling cramped.

Service was fast and friendly. 

The food ranged from really great to holly mackerel what is this amazing bite of food.Here is what I tried:

Shrimp Bahn Mi - Shrimp remoulade and slaw on a bahn mi baguette is a genius discovery. I know lots of people make shrimp remeoulade po-boys, but the baguette here (I am assuming from Dong Phuong) kicks the mundane remoulade po-boy into high gear. That extra bit of crunch with the creamy remoulade is delicious.

Lemongrass Pork Bahn Mi- Wow. I've had a lot of grilled pork when eating Vietnamese food. The pork here may be the best I've had. The smokey pork paired so perfectly with the veggies and jalapenos that I wanted another one. If left to choose between the two bahn mi, the pork wins every freakin time.

Pork Belly Bao - Ok. If you only read one thing in my review, read this. My first bite of this bao was pure heaven. After eating it I said (out loud to no one in particular); " that is the best single bite of 2017". It was that good. As I continued eating it I did encounter some chewy pieces of belly that weren't great, but overall, this was a great dish. Get two with a pork bahn mi.

Parking is street only and I had to make the block a few times to find a spot. Since I usually grab and go this is an issue, but if you're dining in just park somewhere and walk.

Prices for the bahn mi were more than Dong Phuong, but I think the $8 is still fair.

If you lie Vietnamese sandwiches, you owe it to yourself to check out Le's.

Neil McClure saved my life!

That may be a bit dramatic, but I'm well known as a drama queen around these parts, so let me explain. Saving my life may be an overstatement, but Mr. McClure and his new location at the Nola Brewing Tap Room sure helped me score some great BBQ which helped feed my addiction to smoked meats. 

The new location inside the tap room is a match made in heaven. Nola Brewing produces some of my all time favorite brews (Hopitoulas and Irish Channel Stout), so adding one of my favorite BBQ purveyors was pure genius. The layout is pretty snazzy with both bar height tand regular height tables. The bar located at the back is beautiful with all those taps, but I'm not here to talk about that. I'm here to discuss the damn fine BBQ. 

Ordering takes place at the window to the left of the bar. Orders are taken via iPad and your given a light up vibraty thing for when your order is ready. Today I was desperately craving brisket, but both McClure's locations were out. Since I was already at the window I decided on pulled pork, ribs and chorizo. While waiting for my food I was greeted by a man who I immediately recognized as the owner. I told him I was craving brisket and he humbly apologized saying it was his fault that he didn't make enough for lunch, but assured me he would have some for dinner. If I didn't have to be across the lake then, you can bet I'd be first in line for that brisket. 

The food was as good as I have grown accustomed to at the original location. The pork was tender, smokey and had several pieces of bark that I love so much. The ribs were absolutely incredible. They were perfectly smoked with just the right amount of give one expects from smoked ribs. None of that fall off the bone none sense here. The chorizo was perfect. I'm not sure why all BBQ joints don't smoke chorizo, but they should. That spicy sausage goes so well with smoke that I could probably live on that for the rest of my life. 

The BBQ stood on its own without sauce, but I want to comment on one of the sauces that I think is beyond anything I've ever had. Their South Carolina mustard based sauce is so damn good that I literally licked the top of the plastic ramekin to get every last drop. Imagine driving by me at work and seeing me shoving a plastic ramekin in my mouth. Yeah. That's how good it is. 

My one complaint is that there is no way to call ahead and place an order at this location. I also always worried that my company's prohibition of entering bars at work would prevent me from waiting around here for food, but don't let the name fool you. This is much more of a restaurant atmosphere (at least during lunch) and kids are even welcome. 

In summar, McClure's is awesome no matter which location you try.

Saints and Sinners is actually kind of cool.

Ok, there I said it. I am sure many locals will trash me for rating a celebrity owned bar/restaurant four stars, but it isn't as bad as people make it out to be. My first experience with S&S was at a recent elite event. The staff and management were very hospitable and truly concerned with our experience. My next experience came one night during the pre-Super Bowl festivities. The place was packed, and there was a cover. The good news for me is that the manager recognized me from the event and made sure I got in without a hassle. Being a nice guy apparently has some benefits.

From my previous visit, I knew that the upstairs is the place to be. Sure there is crazy velvety wallpaper, but there is also a cool couch, bar and balcony. Service was prompt and friendly. Beer selection was lacking, and prices were a bit steep, but it is the FQ.

My one main complaint is not that it is celebrity owned, but that they continually reference said celebrity. I guess some people are impressed by that, but I am not one of those people. I would rather the place stand on its own merits than be continually reminded some guy I've hardly heard of owns the joint.

If you are forced to be on Bourbon Street, come here. Just head to the stairs in the back and grab a spot on the couch.

Shawarma? Check
Gyro? Check
Hummus? Check
Running? Negative

Despite the name suggesting eating while jogging (never a good idea), this place offers pretty good food for very reasonable prices.

Alright. Alright. Alright. I know. Before you decide to explain to me that the name actually means picking up food quickly, I already know that. Sometimes I like to add my own brand of humor to a review. That humor often fails miserable, but you get my drift. Now back to the review.

I discovered this place while chatting with a co-worker. He told me that he had just come back from picking up shawarma less than a mile from our office and I was intrigued. Despite driving by this place thousands of times, I didn't know it existed. He told me it was good, and on Waitr, so I knew where my next meal was coming from.

I love shawarma and gyro so I usually get a combination of the two when getting this type of food. My order was ready in about five minutes so I headed over to pick it up.

Inside the restaurant there were at least four gyro/shawarma rotisseries behind the counter. Those cookers contained several different types of meat that all looked, and smelled, delicious. There were also several tables for dining in, but I took mine to go.

As shawarma goes, their version was very good. It had a great, almost, grilled texture on the outside of some slices, but was tender and juicy, and filled with flavor. The gyro was equally as good, but it seems more difficult to mess up. Getting the shawarma right takes more skill and they did a great job. I've now been several times (and will probably go again today), and their food has always been very consistent.

If you find yourself looking for some good shawarma in Terrytown, you need to check this place out.

What kind of moron goes to a pizzeria and doesn't order pizza? This moron right here, but I'll tell you why. 

For years I have heard how wonderful a place Slice is. It took me several years to finally visit and when I did I ordered a po-boy. This may seem like an insane choice at a business known for great pizza, but this wasn't just any po-boy. It was their New Orleans style BBQ shrimp po-boy. 

I love BBQ shrimp. When I saw that Slice put theirs on French bread, I knew I had to have it. Not only was it an incredible sandwich, the shrimp were some of the best of their type that I've had anywhere. The perfectly spicy and buttery sauce was so good that had to resist the urge to lick the plate clean. That divine sauce soaked into the French bread, but left it with enough substance that it could still be eaten using my hands. It was incredible. In fact, it was so good that on my second trip, I had the exact same thing. 

The only other item I have tried has been their Caesar salad. It was well made and had a good lettuce to dressing ratio, but get the po-boy no matter what else you try. 

On all of my visits here I have been waited on by friendly and professional servers. The food always arrives promptly and prices are very reasonable. The one negative is the parking situation. Since this block of Magazine is packed  with shops, the street parking is often hard to come by. Plan on circling the block a few times if you want to park somewhat close.

Another winner picked by Yelp.

I was in the area and wanted Thai for lunch. The Yelp reviews looked great, so my choice was made.

Cafe Equator is conveniently located directly behind Lagers in what I think was originally a bank. There is very little parking in front, but there are additional spots in the rear. The lack of easy parking may be the only reason it doesn't get five stars.

I ordered the shrimp red curry and asked for it to be prepared Thai spicy. The server recommended that I order the authentic Thai red curry since it was far more spicy than the luncheon special. It was also double the price, but wow, it was amazing. The curry was spicy, yet had an incredible flavor.

Service was wonderful, and the lunch specials are very reasonable. 

I highly recommend this restaurant. Just come prepared to search for parking.

When the facade of a building crashed into Singha it crushed much more than just the restaurant. It also crushed my dreams of Thai spicy cashew chicken. I realize that may sound a little dramatic, but I loved that dish. For the past year I have tried many different versions of that dish, but none came close to Singha. 

The new version of Singha is completely different. The staff appear to be all new and the building does not have the funky charm of the old location. I visited one day right when they opened and was seated with no issue. As my meal continued I saw the restaurant go from half full to completely full with a wait for a table. This all happened in a matter of a few minutes so make sure and come during off peak times.

Service was friendly and prompt just like the old location. The only thing I missed was the old staff who would remember that I really did like my food as hot as they could possibly make it. It always takes a few trips before servers at a Thai place accept that you can handle that level of spice, but I am pretty convincing. 

The food was good. Not as good as the original, but my cashew chicken had hints of greatness. I wish it had been a little spicier, but that will come in time. It also seemed as if the sauce was not as rich as the old version, but I still thoroughly enjoyed it.

The entire meal took under 30 minutes which was impressive considering how busy they got after I was seated. Street parking was a pain, but that won't keep me away.

If you miss Singha, just want some Thai food and you've only got a brief time, head to Singha.

Cooter Brown's is a cool bar.

I have been coming to this bar for nearly 15 years. While I haven't been in at least six, I am pleased to report that it hasn't really changed. The only noticeable differences are that the prices have gone up and the televisions are modern. Normally a business has to change with the times, but in this case, change would be bad.
