I would classify Cooter Brown's as a classy dive bar. While this may not make much sense, it is hard to call a bar with well over 100 beers a dive bar. What does make it a dive bar is the atmosphere. It is smoky, dirty and still has the love note I wrote on the mirror in 1998.

The selection of beer is amazing. I can't comment on the food because honestly, my memory of those days is a bit foggy. I hear the food is very good so hopefully I will get to return soon and sample some of it.

I highly recommend this bar. If you need a place to drink beer and hang out with friends, this is a great place. if you need a fancy cocktail, you may want to go somewhere else.

I was never a fan of Mother's. In fact, I considered it to be an over rated tourist trap. 

That all changed when I was staying around the corner for a wedding and needed a sandwich. I decided to try the famous Ferdie and I was so happy I did. 

Baked ham with roast beef and debris combined together caused my mouth pure ecstasy. This sandwich made me understand why all the tourists line up to eat here. I wouldn't wait an hour in line, but this is some very good food.

Mothers also makes a turkey Ferdie if you'd like. It is not as good as the original, but it is pretty good.

Service is not always the best, but Mother's is a must visit.

Mahony's may be my favorite poor boy shop. 

Sure lots of people complain about the wait, but every time I have been, my wait was reasonable. I think choosing your time is key. At 11:00 and 5:00 there was zero wait to order, and my food was out within 10-15 minutes. I did go once for take out at noon, but I had called ahead and my food was ready upon arrival. 

The food is very good to excellent. When I sampled the pot roast beef for the first time, I literally exclaimed "holy hell, this is the best poor boy I have ever eaten". Thankfully I was alone in my office and no one could hear me, but it was that good. 

Since then I have been back several times. While always very good, the roast beef no longer amazes me every time. It does still hold the title of John's favorite roast beef in the city.....for now.

A few visits ago, I had a cochon poor boy to change my routine. They recommended I skip having it dressed since it came with slaw. I wish I had disregarded that suggestion as the sandwich was a bit dry. The slaw and pork were perfect, but I would have liked some vinegar based sauce or something similar. 

The dirty fries with cheese are the best I have had anywhere. The fries are perfectly cooked and topped with roast beef, gravy and cheese (optional). The order is huge, and so good that you will be licking the basket clean (don't judge me).

I really like Mahony's. If you try it, I think you will too.

Surrey's is great.

I am very rarely in New Orleans when I am in the mood for a leisurely breakfast. because of that, I had never tried Surrey's despite every barista at my favorite shop down the street recommending it. So when a friend recommended we try it one late morning, I jumped at the chance.

I had heard horror stories about how crowded it can get, but on a weekday around 10 there was no wait.

Service was good, but the food was the star. I ordered the migas which was eggs, cheese, and chorizo. The spice of the chorizo went perfectly with the scrambled eggs. This dish might be my new favorite New Orleans breakfast.

The restaurant is very small and does get very crowded. Even though it is small, the tables are spaced far enough apart that you can have a private conversation. This is a huge plus compared to other small restaurants.

I really enjoyed my meal at Surrey's. If you are looking for breakfast in the LGD, you should definitely give Surrey's a try.

Bayou Wine Garden is my kind of place.

You know how in some reviews people claim to be experts because they are from wherever experts come from? I am not really an expert in much, but there is one thing I am pretty good at. Chilling. For real, I am like an expert at chilling. You can believe me. I am from the West Bank.

So what does being an expert on chilling have to do with BWG? BWG is a great place to chill.

I am not fond of going to bars anymore. I prefer sitting on my porch, glass of MD 20/20 in my hand, and chilling. A friend was leaving town and this was where a group gathered to bid farewell. 

Picture a friend's backyard patio and that is the vibe I got from this place. There were tables a plenty including some shaded and some not. We chose a long table under a canopy that was set up to seat probably 15 people. It was a weeknight so it wasn't crowded, but it was the perfect place for a leisurely cocktail with friends.

The thing that made it less like a friend's patio was that BWG has a pretty extensive wine and liquor list. In fact, they even had Blanton's and it was fairly reasonable for a heavy pour ($14 or 15 I think). 

I didn't eat, but the plate of gravy fries across from me looked so delicious I was seriously tempted to create a diversion, steal the plate, and flee the premises. I didn't though since that wouldn't of gone over too well. But what I am trying to say is those fries looked delicious.

In summary, if you want to chill with friends, and are in Mid-City, you should probably come here.

Arnaud's French 75 is great. In fact, it may be my new favorite fancy pants establishment.

The atmosphere of this bar is fancy, inviting and reminds me of a different era. An era where fancy people dressed up, drank cocktails, and smoked the occasional cigar. Even though it is close to Bourbon Street, you feel a world away.

The cocktails were excellent and bartender Chris Hannah was behind the bar. After reading all the reviews that mentioned him, I was a bit starstruck. Turns out he not only makes a great drink, but he is a nice, humble guy (more on that later).

I picked a spot in the corner by the cigar case. As others have mentioned, this is the best spot in the bar. You can see the entire bar, yet it feels as if you are a bit secluded. This would be the best spot to sit if you bring a date, or if you want to chat with friends.

I tried several old fashioneds, a sidecar and even opted for a cigar (see profile picture). I don't normally smoke cigars, or drink cocktails, but here, it just seemed right.

I liked this bar so much, that I didn't leave until they closed. As they were closing the bartenders broke out the moonshine. I didn't particularly care for moonshine, but I got to discuss New Orleans, our burgeoning cocktail scene and the bartenders life stories. Chris Hannah was very humble. Even though he is well known, he gave a lot of credit to the other bartenders who work in the bar. It was very cool. The other bartender was equally cool, but he didn't have a name tag so I can't remember his name.

I really liked this bar. I highly recommend it, and can't wait to go back.
Calzone isnt bad, but why charge 20 for a 16 inch pie that is mediocre at best?   I know .....to make a killing right?

Pups & brews, what more can I ask for?! 

Metazoa Brewing Company is one of the many breweries in Indianapolis but the only one I had the pleasure of visiting while I was there. My friend has a pup so we decided to have some girl time and let little Mochi run out her energy with some furry friends in their dog park.

They have both indoor and outdoor seating. If you are hungry, they have a BBQ food truck outside with some BOMB BBQ. That says a lot considering I'm not a huge fan of BBQ myself but their brisket was *chefs kiss*. 

The dog park is pretty spacious and has artificial turf. There are mostly big dogs (at least during my visit) that come here but everyone is super friendly with the best behaved dogs. 

I had a couple of beers but my absolute favorite (like absolute favorite beer of all-time) was discovered here. I love the Trash Panda- a vanilla latte-inspired blonde ale. I feel like coffee beers are usually porters so I was so surprised how light and coffee-like this beer tasted. I'm not the most well-versed when it comes to brews but if this is a usual thing, I am so in. 

Until my next trip to Indy, I will be craving the Trash Panda.

The restaurant reminds me of how damaging Yelp can be - this place has a 3 star rating average, where most people complain about the service.

I'm one to notice service, and what I noticed here was amazing service. We were seated immediately, got our drinks within minutes, ordered within minutes  - and even our food was brought out (by someone who seemed like a manager) within 5 minutes of ordering! 5 Minutes! 

If I had read the reviews beforehand, I would've most likely skipped out since we were pressed for time - and yet we were in and out of Eladios within 45 minutes.

To think that I might have missed out on the AMAZING Crab Cakes Benedict! 

Definitely a 5 star restaurant - in both service and food.

Seriously, try the crab cakes benedict.

Oh, is it pricey? Kinda - but you're sitting in a restaurant located right across the pier, right across the 25 cent electric shuttle, right near the Amtrak Station - it's worth it.

Did I mention the Crab Cakes Benedict?

I am extremely torn as I sit down to write this review. On one hand, it was fantastic and many parts of the experience were worth 5 stars. On the other hand, there were a few unacceptable details that I would give zero to if possible. Let me explain:

I had my eye on this place for a while after being less than thrilled with the beer selection at the Craft House & Beer Garden in Cherry Hill (food was awesome but the name is a pack of lies). Anyway, we sat at the bar for dinner around 8:00 on a weekday. It wasn't too busy, decent crowd for football but still plenty of seats. The very nice bartender greeted us right away and got us drinks and menus. She catered to our every whim and was super nice about it. She knew her beers and made solid food recommendations as well. Everything was going swimmingly until her boss showed up behind the bar.

I don't know exactly what his role is here, whether he is the owner or a manager or just there to make it more difficult for the bartender to do her job or the patrons to enjoy their visit, but he was just the worst. Our mouths hung open as we watched him walk around to people sitting at the bar, gruffly asking them whether or not she was tending to them. He didn't smile once at anyone. This was NOT in a nice professional "I'm the boss so I'm taking ownership of my job and making sure everything runs smoothly" kind of way. It was far more like "I'm micromanaging this poor girl, trying to catch her doing something wrong and prove that she is bad at her job." Uuuuuunnnnncomfortable.

We noticed several other patrons looking equally confused and taken aback by his attitude. A few, including myself, actually appeared astonished that he was behaving in such away and went out of their way to say something along the lines of YES FOR THE LOVE OF GOD SHE IS DOING GREAT AND WE ARE FINE PLEASE DON'T TAKE HER OUT BACK TO WHIP HER WITH YOUR BELT. If, god forbid, he got to someone who actually did need something, he barked at her in an unnecessarily nasty way as if she had purposefully neglected them (she was seriously on top of her game, this was so unfair). She was notably more relaxed and able to simply do her job when he was gone, and while he was there it was as if she were scared and looking over her shoulder afraid to breathe wrong. But, wait for the kicker...

This is obviously a craft beer bar and they truly have rare and unusual selections. Like I said, this is why we went to the place. But let me sincerely ask, what good is a craft bar with several rare beers on tap if you DON'T LET YOUR PATRONS SAMPLE THE BEERS?!? What the f%#k is this?! Are you not aware of how this works or are you honestly just that cheap? The lovely bartender permitted us one when we walked in, but once the bad man showed up after we had finished our first round and it was time to sample another, it was a different story. We asked to try a different one, and she nervously looked around to see if he was watching. When she saw she was in the clear, she quickly poured a small taste and whispered "please don't tell him" when she handed it over. I give her props for knowing good business and being willing to put herself at risk for the sake of making the customer happy (and I sincerely hope that this honest review doesn't result in some sort of trouble for her), but seeing a hardworking employee in a scenario like this just sucked. We ordered another two different beers without sampling first just because we felt so bad for her and didn't want to see her get bitched out again. Thankfully, they were excellent.

Like I said, overall I am torn. The food was fantastic, the beer selection was truly on point and the service was great (clearly I am speaking only about the bartender), but I am genuinely against patronizing any place that could possibly benefit that man. The entire experience with him was unbelievable (like I think we asked each other if it was really happening) and appalling, and I have never seen anything like it. If I found out that he was gone I swear I would go there every single day and bring all my craft beer loving friends to throw their money at the place, but knowing that it is owned or at least partially run by a dude like that just makes it awful. Sad to say, I'm not sure I would return unless I hear he has been relieved of his post as Chief Nazi.


Quick edit: After skimming other reviews I see that many people have had a similar experience with him. Everything from him staring customer & employees down, killing the vibe, calling you out on not tipping enough (I wouldn't tip as low as the 15% mentioned but it certainly doesn't deserve being called out), and again being awful to the staff are all mentioned. God I hope he actually takes a hint, this place could be an absolute gem.

Looking for a light lunch or dinner? Look no further! My girlfriend and I always get the gyro plate from here. It's much better than all of those chainfood restaurants. These are local people making food the way they learned at home. 

Thanks and keep up the good work!

I was happy they opened one on the westbank since I live on this side BUT this Legacy doesn't live up to its name.. My family had over $250 worth of gift cards and we said let's go out for dinner. I called ahead to reserve a table for 8. To my surprise, they gave us a private room. I came early so I check in at the bar for a Old Fashion. . 

Where do I begin with the food? It was horrible! Nothing was like the one in Metairie. Even the firecracker shrimp was blah. My niece ordered a medium well filet and it came out bloody. Everything else didn't have any flavor. Maybe it's because they had just opened but they sure aren't going to earn our business unlesss something changes. I'll be back to give them a second try in hopes of it being good but I wouldn't hold my breath on it. Our bill ended up being over $500. 

Moral of the story. Expensive food doesn't always mean good food.

30 minutes after eating the mahi mahi fish tacos at Crabby Bill's, I developed a red face, neck, and body rash, headache, nausea and itching. I am 50 years old and I have no history of food allergy. This is a classic presentation of scombroid fish poisoning. Incidentally, I am a physician (pulmonologist) and university professor. I confirmed my presentation and diagnosis with an allergist who is the chief of allergy and immunology at my university. 
     When I went to inform the manager that they may be serving bad fish, she asked me what I wanted. I told her I just wanted to let her know in case anyone else ordered mahi mahi and developed the same reaction. She was defensive and offered no apology.
    Scombroid poisoning arises when fish are improperly stored after being caught (temperatures greater than 40F]). Under these conditions, the fish undergo bacterial overgrowth, and sustain conversion of histidine to histamine and other biogenic amines by the bacterial enzymes. Toxic levels of histamine can accumulate within as short a time as two to three hours in fish stored at 20°C (68°F) or higher. The responsible bacteria are most commonly Escherichia coli; halophilic Vibrio species; and Proteus, Klebsiella, Clostridium, Salmonella and Shigella species.
    So, beware of the mahi mahi tacos at Crabby Bill's, and don't ask for anything if you get bad food. What is more, they were not served as ordered and had lettuce, not cabbage.

RESTAURANT WEEK AND TASTING MENU BEWARE! 

I'm not commenting on the food, since I didn't even have any while I was there. 3 of my friends and I came here on restaurant week. We had all looked at the menu beforehand and saw there were 6 courses we'd get, with some cool options. So we were really excited. 

After we were sat and ordered our wine, the waitress tells us that we pick one option from each of the 6 groups FOR THE TABLE to share! All four of us had to eat the exact same thing for every course - yet we all had to pay for it?? I have never, in my life, heard of such a thing. 

If that is their "policy" as they kept stating, fine - but no where - NO WHERE - on their website, or on the Restaurant Week's website, did it say that everyone at the table had to eat the same thing. I even spoke to the manager who was not helpful at all - she just kept saying "There's nothing I can do". Well, actually there is - you could have accommodated us and let us order what we want, but no. 2 of the people I was with didn't eat meat, and one was dairy free - how are we supposed to eat the same thing? Again, if they had disclosed this ANYWHERE - on their website, the restaurant week's website, or even the actual menu when we sat down??? Maybe that would have been understandable - but this was the absolute most ridiculous thing I'd ever heard. Apparently this is also their "policy" for their tasting menu, so just a heads up for anyone planning to go there, which I will never do again.

Don't let the chinese name fool you..  It's definitely not the same "Mongolian Little Sheep" as the one in NY, NJ, CA.... They only used the same chinese name, but a different english name. Even though I confirmed it with the NY location that this was not one of their branch, I still decided to try this place.. I'm not a traitor, I swear! 

I'm glad I made reservation.. Yes, they take reservation. At 7pm, it was already pretty packed. Didn't have to wait at all to get seated and we just zipped on in to a table thats already waiting for us.

I have to say, service was pretty slow. With all the servers they had, it was hard to wave one down to take our order.. It would help if they would look up when they walk...

Opt'd for the individual pots. Every hotpot place has that large single or double pot. It's kinda cute to get the individuals, just my opinion. 

Hubby and I ordered a table worth of of food.. lamb, beef (in addition to the ones included), 'shroom, shrimp, squid, tofu, gizzard... Both the herbal and spicy broth was lacking flavor. With so much ingredients floating around, I expected a taste to it. But it was bland. 

The platter of meats were larger than i thought so thats a plus. The shrimp was fresh even though we didn't order the "live shrimp". 


It's great to see another shabu place in Philly, but they will need much more improvement.

if you want to be blown away by some of the finest art in the world, you would travel to Musee du Louvre in Paris.

If you want to see the most incredible gardens you'd probably choose The Butchart Gardens on Vancouver Island or Cheekwood if you are visiting Nashville or live close by.

If you want to learn about the history of Rock and Roll, definitely head to The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame and Museum, located in Cleveland, Ohio.

An Elvis fan? No question - visit Graceland - Memphis TN.

Want to stroll the entire history of Country Music and every artist you can imagine? The Country Music Hall of Fame in Nashville is your destination.

BUT-
If you want to :
View the largest public collection of Johnny Cash memorabilia.
Experience a timeline of audio formats / video footage spanning his incredible career of 5 decades.
Read the Man In Black's personal handwritten thoughts, song lyrics, report cards, walls of awards, and many more interesting items. 
Get a glimpse into his personal life beginning with his childhood.
 
Find out why Johnny Cash is one of the most important musical and historical figures of all time. 
THIS is where you go. 

It's an incredible museum people of all ages will enjoy. 

You can spend an hour or an entire day being entertained by state-of-the-art audio and visual elements. The museum is self guided. 

Take the time to visit. You'll be happy you did.

Love the shop--the decor is a mix of pure fun and beautiful things. And the cupcakes...absolute nirvana. More like 11 stars out of 5. I had the Twix cupcake and brought one home for my husband. We both loved everything about the cupcake, from the chunks of Twix to the caramel drizzle, to the moist chocolate cake and wonderfully flavored and balanced buttercream--Philly Cupcake bakers know their stuff.

Also on my visit I got to chat with 2 super friendly gentleman, who I presume to be the owners. They were so nice and enjoyed talking with me and my friend about our fanaticism for cupcakes.

Can't wait to see what else they create. My only wish would be that the shop was bigger, to fit in a few vintage tables and chairs--but who knows what the future will bring!

After a hiking adventure in Montecito, my boyfriend and I stopped by Padro Beach Grill for a bite to eat. We ordered via Yelp app, fulfilled by Grubhub, to pick up our order and everything went smoothly.  Service was nice. Due to COVID-19 restrcitions, patio-dining area was closed and so we pulled up to a lot with ocean view to eat in our car.  

Fish and chips is a red snapper battered, with French fries and tartar sauce for $11.50.  Baja Fish Tacos was the same red snapper battered with shredded cabbage, tartar sauce, cilantro, pico del gallo on a single homemade corn tortilla for $9.95 -and tacos came with chips and salsa as well. Fish batter is a bit thick, but overall we were pleased with our food as price point is perfect for overall portion size. Great beach side cafe that I'd definitely recommend for bite to eat.  Thanks, Padro Beach Grill.

My parents wanted a seafood dinner, therefore my sister suggested my family eat at Santa Barbara FisHouse. 

I wasn't too fond of my tostada trio (the special at the time, bleh) as the seafood taste bland and watery.  My family and I enjoyed the fried calamari appetizer.  Portion size was good, large sized calamari rings and two different dipping sauces was nice.  

Our party of 6 was seated right away. Indoor and outdoor seating available.  Service was nice and attentive, as one of the two girls serving my family, was in training (therefore we had the attention of two waitresses).  Limited free parking at the back of the restaurant.  Located right next to the beach walkway, it's a decent place for seafood.  Stay safe and healthy (mind, body and soul) Yelping out there :)

Stumbled here in search of a king cake slice and I was immediately in awe as I walked through the door of Sucre. This dessert shop was aesthetically pleasing with beautifully decorated, delectable desserts. I walked up and down for a good 5 minutes, comparing each of the desserts and gelato flavors trying to pick only two items for the night.

The 'king cake slice' ($4) was delicious, so delicious that I made multiple trips to Sucre during my weekend trip to NOLA. The king cake was warm, fluffy and sweet; the slice had a thin glazed layer on top and tasted like a danish but much better. My boyfriend and I also ordered the 'triple chocolate streusel bar' ($7.50) which was a very sweet chocolate mousse cake. 

The desserts are packaged nicely in quality boxes and bags, so you definitely get what you pay for when you come here. Overall, I would recommend stopping at Sucre if you have a sweet tooth or if you're searching for a good slice of king cake.

There is really nothing like hitting a diner, late at night, after you have been out having a great time with friends. Unfortunately, there is kind of a shortage of diners in NOLA. Camellia Grill and Clover Grill would qualify, but they can get pretty crowded on the weekends and not exactly the perfect diner atmosphere. However, should you find yourself in lovely Metry on a late night craving some good old diner goodness, haul your butt on over to City Diner. Complete with the necessary booths and stools at the counter, City Diner is a setting pulled right out of the East Coast. Their menu covers everything. Sandwiches, burgers, hot comfort food, and of course breakfast foods are all accounted for on its pages. The waitresses are the sweet yet no shit-taking ladies you would expect them to be. I highly recommend the freaking pancake served on a damn pizza tray! Seriously, a pancake the size of a medium (maybe large) freaking pizza! I had a chocolate chip one last time that kept me fed for days! (Pro tip: Reheat pieces in the toaster oven) This may be the best place you can be in Metry late night on the weekends. It maybe the best place in Metry period.

I love this bar. I wish I lived in this neighborhood, I love it so much. They serve my favorite drink currently (besides an old-fashioned), the Baudin. Bourbon, lemon, and hot sauce Boom. I could spend every Saturday morning here. They serve a delicious brunch, have a relaxed crowd, and there's a bluegrass band. Bliss. I've also started going to Wednesday night trivia (Geeks who Drink). The crowd is always lively, but friendly. The bartenders are friendly, knowledgable, and great company if things are slow. The bar is smoke-free but there is a smoking patio out back (with tire swings). Overall, an awesome laid-back bar that I wish was closer to home.

There are just some experiences that are truly once in a lifetime. I thought that eating at Square Root was probably a zero in a lifetime chance for me but I happen to have amazing friends that will allow me to experience some of these things occasionally.
Words expressed through dinner included: 'Wow.' 'This is incredible.' 'I've never had that taste before.' 'I feel like that has awakened a part of my tongue I didn't know I had!' 'I'm so full!' 'When is the banana course?' 
This was truly an adventure. We arrived when they asked us to, which was early, so we enjoyed a cocktail upstairs. The Manhattan was wonderful, although it did take quite a while to complete. We made our way downstairs for dinner and were seated along the bar. I was impressed because although you are sat with the rest of the patrons along the bar, the service happens for your group individually. There were never any large group explanations or announcements made to everyone, which kept it a very intimate experience. My group all got the 'mixed' pairing with their meal, which included some wine, some cocktails, and some individual spirits. Your meal begins with finger foods. This was quite deceptive for me because for a minute I thought I might just make it through all the courses. Silly Lindsay, fooled again. By the sixth or seventh course I and another member of our party were begging for mercy and handing off pieces of our meal to our other friends. By the end of the meal we were hoping to be blinded and never see food again. Now, don't get me wrong, everything was AMAZING. The things they are doing with food are beyond your wildest dreams. I mean, fried chicken cotton candy. Seriously. The staff was also beyond anything I had experienced before. Every member of the staff, from the kitchen staff, to the hosts, to the sommelier was courteous, polite, congenial, and made each party feel comfortable and special. 
If you enjoy food and booze done to incredible new heights and are willing to be open-minded, I highly recommend having this experience at least once. Bonus points for those who can handle all the food and booze, for you are a better person than I.

Yelp No-Wait for the win! 

This place was packed with an hour+ wait, but we used Yelp no-wait for our trip here, OhMaGeerd! We were in and out the door while people were still waiting to be seated! Anyways...

First Watch is a great brunch spot, so it makes sense that this place is packed. I tried the biscuits and gravy, million dollar bacon, and a little bit of my son's "kids" crepes with bananas and strawberries. It was all delicious! The biscuits and gravy were delicious! It all comes in a large hearty bowl filled with two biscuits, covered in thick sausage gravy with a pile of eggs and potatoes on the side, yum! This was a gut bomb, but worth it. 

The million dollar bacon is a must order for the table. Sweet and salty peppered bacon, do I need to say more? My son's crepes were huge and could easy feed an adult. The crepes were great very light and airy. But maybe a little too much for a child?

The parking here is tough and I did feel a bit cramped in the restaurant, especially with the line of people crowding the door. First Watch is definitely worth a second visit!

Nothing ruined for me here.

I met my buddy here for lunch and we both loved the food and atmosphere. I got the avocado toast with a side of old bay waffle fries. The fries were fantastic and come with a french onion dip that I could have easily just ate with a spoon by itself. Hot crispy fries and a cold dipping sauce is my favorite! 

The menu here isn't huge and I didn't want a burger and a beer in the middle of a work day; so I opted for the avocado toast with extra bacon. Along with bacon this delicious toast came with a soft boiled egg and some delicious sautéed mushrooms on top.   This was easily the top five avocado toasts I've eaten in my life. Crunchy, salty, and chewy. This hits all of the textures I love! 

We got lucky and there was zero wait to sit down, but I have driven by this place and there's been a huge line to get in. My advice is come during the week and avoid those weekend crowds.

This is a Nashville classic and a staple of the hungover masses, but it's a tad dirty. 

This really is a no frills, no flash styled breakfast cafe. The only flash here can be found from the griddle as another egg is dropped into a pool of butter. I got the Philly cheesesteak omelette and my son got the grilled cheese. The omelet was very tasty, but the potatoes were super greasy. This omelette had big chunks or steak, onions and peppers in an eggy blanket... what's not to like?! I could have used a little more cheese! 

The Hermitage Cafe menu is small, but they offer all the essentials of a greasy spoon diner. Huge portions of biscuits and gravy, omelettes, chili-burgers, hot dogs, and even a 1/2 fried chicken! 

Breakfast is served all day and make sure to bring cash! No cards are accepted, but they do have an ATM in case you forgot or didn't read this review. ;) 

No longer open 24-hours. :(

They are only doing curbside pick-up at the moment and everything is contact free which I really appreciated. You pull up, pop the trunk, and they place your food order inside. What a weird time!

We ordered the Joystick, fried chicken on a stick with spicy momfuku seasoning and the Impossible sausage sandwich. The sausage sando, holy f*ck this thing was amazing! The handmade sausage patty was juicy, but not to greasy and the addition of the runny yolk and maple mustard was the perfect binder for everything. The Joystick is made of dark meat chicken so it was extra juicy and tender. This was surprisingly good, I wasn't expecting so much flavor... spicy, salty, and crunchy. The hat trick of mouthgasms!

I cannot wait for this place to open so we can dine in and get the full Joyland experience.

Nashville has some killer coffee shops and 8th & Roast is no exception! 

I came here to kill some time before heading into Downtown for a meeting. The parking is tough, but there are a few spots in front and a private parking lot on the side of the building. Inside there is plenty of space to sit and even a private meeting room you can rent for large groups. 

For the coffee I went with the usual, cold brew and a veggie quiche to eat. The quiche was ok, but could have used some spice. It was large and filled me up enough to get through the morning. The coffee was delicious, like two cup delicious. Smooth flavor and no bitter aftertaste. I drank it black and it was perfect. 

They roast everything at their second location and you can tell there's passion in every cup. When in the area, this will definitely be my go to coffee shop.

This place could be featured in a hipster coffee shop styling playbook. Keep it minimal, sleek and devoid of personality. That being said, the coffee and staff are great. 

I was here killing time between meetings, ordered an iced coffee and sat at the bar. This is definitely the place in the hood to soak up some Wifi and get some work done. It looks like people take over the booths or tables and stay put for awhile, so space inside might be limited. Once the weather warms up, definitely utilize their outdoor patio it's spacious and sun kissed. 

The iced-coffee was great! Awesome color and no bitter aftertaste. I drank it black, no need for almond milk or other creamers. I will say, I probably wouldn't active seek this place out, but if you're close by and need a pick me up, Steadfast has you covered.

Just like Wile E. Coyote's favorite brand of rocket skates, Acme Feed & Seed is my favorite spot on lower Broadway. Great food, drinks, and sweet rooftop views. 

I've been here twice now and their fried chicken n' waffles and smoked mac n' cheese are still my go-to menu items. The waffle is both soft and crispy and the chicken tenders are crunchy, salty and super juicy... a pure match made in Heaven! The smoked Mac n' cheese is very decadent, with the smokey flavor being very forward, but not overpowering. 

There are three levels to this bar. The first floor being more of a "family hang" and the second floor having that younger, fresh out of college vibe. The third level is the rooftop. Go up here for an awesome view of the river and the Titan's stadium. Also, a great spot for summer beers and just hanging. 

I know the Nashville natives hate on lower Broadway and say it's super touristy, but Acme Feed and Seed doesn't give off that vibe. If I have friends in town and they want to see LoBro, we usually start here. 

Haven't been in a while? Once COVID-19 is over, get here and snack it up!

No hate from me! Catch 22 is a laid back spot with amazing food and tasty brews. 

Our realtor took us when we were looking at homes during my initial visit to Nashville and I will definitely be back for the Bad Mother Clucker, chicken sandwich. This visit had met snacking on the filthy fries, the French dip and the fried buffalo cauliflower. The Filthy fries were off the hook! A mountain of tasty fries covered in bbq pork, beer cheese, green onions and bacon. There's wasn't a bad bite on this massive tray of food. 

The French dip was great, but the beef was a little dry... French onion au juis to the rescue! The au juis was great and the French roll was soft on the inside, but still crunchy from being toasted. Loved the different textures in each bite! The fried cauliflower was also delicious and a solid appetizer option for the table. Especially if you're going to enjoy a hearty dinner and a few beers. 

Easy parking, amazing local beer selection and ridiculous food. Catch 44, which will be my new pant size after a few more visits. Bring on the meat sweats!

Need booze for your holiday party? This is the spot! 

I came here the day before Thanksgiving to pick a few libations to pair with a day full of cooking. I picked up rum, absinthe, vodka, whiskey and three bottles of wine for $120! That's a score! 

All of  their booze sections are huge and everything is super easy to find. I was a little bummed they don't carry Pickers vodka, but I was able to grab a bottle of Wheatley vodka instead. Beyond liquor, the beer sections is decent with a large selection of local brews and don't forget to take a peek at the wine cellar area, right behind the wall of rum. 

The parking is tight and there's currently a lot construction going on here, so be patient and maybe do you holiday booze shopping during weekday hours. 

Party safe!

This is my 4th or 5th visit to the Goat for mostly dinner or happy hour. I didn't event know they were open for brunch. 

We got here right as they opened at 10am and we had the place to ourselves. We sat on the spacious patio and enjoyed some sunshine and I enjoyed a Bloody Mary. 

We ordered the Goat scramble, a quesadilla, and the "Devil On Goatback Scramble... a mouthful literally and figuratively. The Devil Goatback is huge and is basically a breakfast pizza with scrambled eggs, white cheddar, pork belly, dates, spinach, sriracha aioli, on a brioche pizza like dough. This was delish and plenty of food for two people. I wish the server would have told me how big it was, otherwise my wife and would have shared this and not ordered a the Goat scramble.

The scramble was tasty, but she liked the breakfast pizza much better. They don't have a kids menu, but my son did love the quesadilla and the side of scrambled eggs. 

A Bloody Mary, a cozy warm patio and a delish brunch. You really can't go wrong with The Goat at Providence!

I really love the 12-South neighborhood and it's because of spots like this. Burger Up is not just another trendy burger place, it's a great spot to kick-back, sip a drink and mellow out.  

The Black and Blue burger is a thick blackened burger patty with crumbled blue cheese, red onion and arugula. It seems a little plan, but the flavors were amazing and the blue cheese didn't overpower the beef. This portion is huge by the way, so eat half and take the rest home for a second meal! The Mac n' cheese bites, were ok, but seem over-fried and the batter was heavy. These are served with maple ketchup which was very good! 

Their beer selection is decent and they have a full bar, prefect for a Bloody Mary brunch. This place does get busy so be ready wait during peak times or use Yelp's No Wait which is what we did and it was a game changer! We walked right in, past a large group and sat down. Yay for technology!

Absolutely amazing brewery for the hop head or causal IPA lover. 

The outdoor area is solid for those cool summer nights and the indoor main brewing and seating area keeps the AC cranking and the beer flowing. I went with the Homestyle IPA. This was a very smooth IPA, with none of the bitterness that a lot of IPAs seem to have lately. I normally drink pales or blondes and this beer fit perfectly with my current beer palate. They do sell cans of beer to go and from what I saw they don't sell food. 

I really loved the vibe here and the benches against the wall were super comfy. The bartender (Molly) seemed to be having a bad day, but she was still very helpful with her suggestions and knowledge. 

I will definitely be back!

It might just been the tasty beer at noon or the country music coming through the speakers, but this place gives off major Nashville vibes. 

We sat in the empty bar area and I went with a Nashville Brewing blonde ale and the PoBoy Remix Sandwich. This is fried catfish and fried shrimp on a soft baguette. Amazing spices, decent heat and I loved the texture. The downside, this sandwich was incredibly hard to eat, It feel apart almost instantly. Even though I finished this sando with a fork, the flavor was still there and I would probably order this again. 

The deviled eggs were good, but not great. I could tell these sat in the fridge for a while and a little too much brine flavor. My wife had veggie Cobb salad and added chicken. She enjoyed, but said it could have used a little more dressing. 

55 South, come to Mount Juliet please! We need a better selection of restaurants out here!

Tried the drive-thru for the first time and it was easy peasy! The workers here were all wearing masks and keeping the vibes friendly. 

Ordered the iced americano and the biscuit breakfast sandwich for the first time. It was delicious and I highly recommend! Huge pieces of bacon, soft biscuit and and fluffy eggs. You can't go wrong. If you're not feeling the biscuit, you can switch it to a croissant. Ohh lala!

Great spot and great coffee!

The reviews are all over the place for this Martin's, but my experience at this location was great. 

First off, if you haven't already tried it, order the Brisket Burger. This was monster was delicious! A soft bun, grilled onions, tender brisket, pimento cheese, and a huge juicy burger patty. I don't think I was ready for this to be so good. The flavors were awesome and I loved the grilled onions with the brisket, such a great combo. 

The sides were good, but the Mac n cheese was lacking a flavor. The baked beans were the star of the show, very tasty and I loved the chunks of pork in each bite. My wife's brisket plate was good, but it was a tad on the dry side. Nothing that some BBQ can't help. 

All-in-all, the food was solid and we came at a great time. About 2pm just after the lunch rush, no wait and the food was out in about five or so minutes.

A solid hot chicken place in Nashville. 

I honestly think this place is better than the more popular spots in town, but that might be an unpopular opinion. This location has both an indoor and outdoor patio, plus an upstairs bar area. 

My last trip here I got the Nashville hot chicken and the beignet plate and it was delicious! Sweet pillowy beignets, topped with powered sugar and served with searing hot chicken. Such a great combo! This time around I got the mild chicken, Nashville hot is way too spicy, all inside of a huge quesadilla. This was off the charts good! Crunchy, spicy, and cheesy... all of my favorite things!  

We also ordered the fried rice balls and the poutine. The rice balls were good, but the poutine was a big miss for the table. Not nearly enough gravy and no cheese curds?! 

That minor poutine set back wasn't enough to to damper the party. It's happy hour all night on Tuesday's, so the half priced beers made up for it. Plus, our server Lilly was amazing and super friendly!

Hawkers. So hot right now. 

This place has been popping up on both my Yelp and IG feeds. So when I was in the area, I had to stop and get some goodies to go! I got a little bit of everything; spring rolls, dumplings, low mein and it was all delicious, but I'll focus on my two personal faves... the Po Po Lo curry and the pork bao buns. 

The curry had a deep rich flavor and some amazing heat. Nothing that scalded your taste buds, just that perfect heat that slowly builds. I would definitely order this again. You can't go wrong with boa buns and Hawkers' buns are super tasty. They didn't have the hot chicken buns during my visit so I opted for the pork buns. Tender, salty and ugh-mazing! I could take a nap on these pillowy buns. 

The decor in here is bright and engaging, as Will Ferrell would say, "it gets the people going!" I ordered my meal to go and sat at the bar while waiting. The bar staff here was great to chat with and very friendly. I would have stayed longer and had another beer, but my food was ready and my family was hungry! 

I highly suggest dining in for the full Hawker experience. PS - They are following all COVID measures to a tee!

You don't have to be high to love being baked...on 8th! My wife had been dying to try out this bakery since we moved here and well, when a pregnant wife summons a craving, you make it happen. I showed up unaware that it was preorders only. In a moment of panic I text the number on the signs posted in the parking lot and the friendly associate explained that I could place a online order that would be ready momentarily (phew!) 

They're online ordering process was super easy to navigate. I ended ordering a Toffee Pecan Chip Cookie, Chocolate Chip Cookie, Brownie, Rice Krispy Treat, and a Salted Caramel Apple Pop Tart. I gotta tell ya, everything was great! My wife and I sampled a bit of each treat. Her favorite was the brownie while mine was the Toffee Pecan cookie. My wife is a baker herself and she was very impressed, in fact, she keeps bugging me to go back. 

If your sweet tooth is calling Baked on 8th will definitely satisfy your craving!

Get the tomato basil galette! 

Three Brothers Coffee is the perfect place for a quick drop-in caffeine break or a stay awhile and get some work done. I got the cold brew and the tomato basil Galette. The coffee was good, but not the best I've had. The Galette was amazing! Crunchy, zesty, and tomatoey. A great savory afternoon treat! 

Parking wise, there's only metered street parking so bring some change! From what I saw, they are following all of the covid rules and regulations.

A cronut focused bakery gets me all hot and bothered. Hubba hubba!

Five Daughters Bakery is a small and brightly colored bakery that has a limited pastry selection, but that's a good thing! Because they hyper focus on what counts, flavor and consistency. My visit here had me sampling the The Drumstick cronut and a little bit of my wife's, guava and mascarpone cronut. 

The drumstick was incredible! I'm not a sweets fan, but I literally inhaled this and basically licked my plate clean. A soft cronut with all of the drum stick favs, minus the ice cream. Chocolate coating, crushed peanuts, and soft fluffy cream underneath the chocolate, delicious! The Guava Cronut was just ok. I'm not a guava fan, but the I did take the frosting off and eat just the plain donut part. Still so good. Shout out to the dude behind the counter playing QOTSA. 

If you live in the area, get here now and try those-fall flavors!

I knew the food was going to be good here, but I didn't expect the level of cooking and service to be so high! 

This was the first date night my wife and I have had since our new baby arrived. I chose Saint Stephen figuring it would be slow on Cinco de Mayo and it was, which was awesome. Everything we ordered is a must... Waygu beef tartar, black squid ink pasta, white asparagus and the focaccia bread. All of this was amazing, but the squid ink pasta and beef tartare blew my f*cking mind! 

If they offered that Waygu beef tartare piled on a Kaiser roll and charged me $150, I'd most likely eat it twice a month. It was that good! We shared the squid pasta bowl and we basically licked the plate clean. This pasta comes in a light red sauce and accompanied by alabama crab, calabrian chilis, and san marzano. Literally, just hook it to my veins and let me chase that flavor dragon all day. 

The service here was stellar and our waiter, Mort, was super hospitable and very informed on the menu. I love the open kitchen concept and I definitely need to come back for the chefs table experience with Chef RJ Cooper. 

Party on and eat well!

Five stars for offering me a much needed break as tour director for when all my out of town friends and family want to see Broadway. 

If you're solo or a party of two definitely sit at the bar. There's plenty of space here to relax and sip on a martini; which is exactly what I did! The vodka martini was delicious and the bartender made great conversation. To eat I ordered the double bacon cheeseburger with sweet potato fries. This burger hit every part of my belly and soul. Two huge juicy patties, thick bacon, and fresh veggies. The sweet potato fries where cut straight from source, massive and sweet and salty. The perfect combo. 

I didn't make it to the second floor on this trip, but if you're looking to get a little fancier, that's the spot. 

Crazy note, you can't really hear the insanity that is Broadway on a Saturday night.

Four floors of upscale diner food. I'm in! 

This was the go to for a late night out in DT. The Diner is open until 3:30am and is the perfect spot to soak up the booze after a long night out or cure that pesky hangover. 

We decided to eat on the first floor after about 30 wasted people loaded up the two elevators and we could still hear them on their way up. I ordered the Philly cheese steak and it was very good and a huge portion. Have I had better cheesesteaks? of course, but this scratched the salty, cheesy itch. 

The views here are pretty awesome and they only get better with each floor you go up. Plus, the staff here is on point! Everything we ordered was at the table within 5-10 minutes. Partying in DT? The Diner will take away those late night hunger pains!

Get the dumplings! 

I just hosted a Yelp event here about three weeks ago and I have to admit, I may have eaten here every single time I had meeting here or dropped off event items. I only ordered the apps every time, but they are enough for repeat trips. 

There are only two app options, dumplings and crispy tofu. The dumplings are tender, chewy and the filling with the sauce is amazing! The crispy tofu with the mango topping, **chef's kiss**! Such a great spicy and sweet snack! 

I really need to get back here and try a few of their noodle dishes, plus I really want to kick back and enjoy a meal in their awesome dining room!

Truly a unique find in the Nations or even greater Nashville area. 

This cozy coffee shop is a "blink and you'll miss it" kind of spot. Nestled next to an antique shop, this small but mighty coffee spot boasts some awesome flavors and friendly staff. 

I came here to work on my laptop and was very surprised at how narrow this place is. There's only about 4-spots to sit not including a tiny bench for guest or the outdoor patio in the back. The menu here simple, but focused. I order a cold brew and a cherry scone. The cold brew was awesome! A strong cup with low acidity and a just touch of bitterness at the end, just how I like it! This paired great the cherry scone.

The scone was the winner of the afternoon. Huge cherries baked into a dense crumbly pastry. The sweet flavor was a nice break from the flavor punch of my cold brew. 

I live in Mount Juliet, but if I found myself in the neighborhood again I would definitely make a pit stop here.

New ownership? New chef? New vibe?

My last review for the Mori Mori wasn't the best and as a reminder, we ordered it to go and during the middle of the pandemic. The last two times we have eaten here, once inside and one to-go order, have both been stellar. 

The food quality is much better and the staff here is awesome. Shout out to Justin! He was our server last time we ate here and he was great, very attentive and fast! We've literally ordered too many rolls to name, so I will just say get the Avocado Bomb and the Angry Lobster roll if you're dining in. I'm not sure how well these food items will travel. 

If you're ordering to for pickup; stay with the classic rolls. A few highlights for me are the Crunch Mania roll and the Caterpillar roll. Maybe add a some crispy calamari to that order?! 

Roll on, Mount Juliet!

The best bar on Broadway.

Cold beer, good food, and amazing music. Looking for that old school twangy country and $2.50 Miller High life? 

Robert's has you covered!

Love this bar! 

We only had one drink and then headed out, but I loved the vibe and look of this place. Apparently, it used to be an old laundromat company? There is food served here, most sandwiches, but the real reason to come here is for the bar and deep cocktail menu. 

Get here early to avoid the crowd and maybe leave the older parents at home because there are a lot of stairs. I suggest sitting in the balcony area to really soak in the look of this place.

When I asked a few Nashvillians, "where's the spot for pizza?" Beyond a few rando neighborhood spots, Slim & Husky's was the name that kept coming up. Let's do it!

This local spot is all about the thin crust, fresh toppings and a super chill vibe. You order "chipotle" style basically building your own pizza or adding items to a pre-made pizza selection and pay once your pie is in the oven. I made my own ten-inch pizza with chicken sausage, tomatoes, black olives, spinach, house mixed cheese and spicy Marinara. It was fantastic! You could taste all the fresh veggies and the crispy crust added some great texture! Each pizza comes with an option for two free drizzles. Do yourself a favor and get two of the cilantro, jalapeño ranch. It's drinkable, trust me! 

I did get a beer here and that was the only issue. The girl at the cash register, couldn't pour beers, she could only sell them. So I had to wait about ten minutes before I could grab my Kings of Leon brew. Not a huge deal, but I did get pretty thirsty after pizza square number four. 

I was definitely skeptical about this place when I first walked in, but became an instant fan after my first bite.

Their extreme awareness of how to create and market a gimmick is substantially better than the taste of the pizza. The ingredients seem very standard and the taste of pizza was pretty unremarkable.

Part of me thinks the owner laughs his way to the bank every day at the fact they don't even provide chairs for customers (which they care so much about?) and people will come stand in line to spend $20 on a plain "high end" pizza. 

I know plenty of pizza shop owners who put just as much care and craft in to their pizza while charging a lot less money for it, and will even offer you a drink as you sit and wait for your order.

Perhaps I had a different experience, but the guy making the pizza did not acknowledge us or even lift his head to look. The cashier said about 2 words and awkwardly stood there waiting for the dude to finish making our pizza.

Substandard & overpriced pizza, no chairs to sit in, and a rather pretentious vibe. But they did have good music playing, so there's that.

This place is a joke! I hate writing bad reviews but I had to write this one. My husband and I are from Columbus, OH so when I heard that Giordano's had opened in Indianapolis where my mom lives I was so excited. I LOVE Giordano's in Chicago! We decided that for my husbands birthday lunch we would go to Giordano's because he had never been there and heard so much about it. I'll start with the positives as there really are only three:

Positives:
-They really picked a GREAT location...82nd street area has everything which is great! 
-We were told that we would have to wait 1 hr and 30 min but we only waited an hour...I say only because we KNEW this being a new restaurant we would have to wait.
-Once we sat down we were told that we would get our pizza in an hour and ten minutes...yes that is a long wait but this was really expected to some extent... we were shocked when our pizza came 20 minutes earlier than expected. 

Now to the negatives:
-The wait... now I know that I had said that it was a positive that we were able to sit earlier but to be told an hr and a half for lunch?! THEN to be told 1 hr and 10 min for our food.
-Our server really lacked customer service skills...and this could really be due to the fact that he was so overwhelmed. 
-Now the BIG negative... WHAT THE HECK DID THEY DO WITH THE ORIGINAL GIORDANO'S PIZZA RECIPE?! This pizza tastes NOTHING like the one that I went to in Chicago. 
-Now the size of this location... REALLY SMALL... I am shocked by this because of how large the ones are in Chicago. The owners of this company were totally not prepared for the demand. I am not even sure how many people this place held but I would estimate maybe 90 people. I do however hear that they will be expanding out to the back patio. One of the servers told us that they estimated that they would do $50,000 the first week that they opened. They actually did $100,000... like I said this place was totally unprepared. 

It is really disappointing to me and not worth the wait. Honestly, I would much rather drive 6 hours to Chicago to eat there than to drive 3 hrs to Indianapolis and wait to eat at this location. Pretty sad and I hope that they can get things together fast or else this location won't last long. More than likely we will not return, maybe in a year when they hopefully have their stuff together.

Why spend 50 cents on a donut elsewhere when you can spend $2-$3 for one here? 

We'll get to that.

So, I first heard about this place while causally glancing over my trusted local news sites. They were all aglow with news about Indy's continued emergence into big citydom with the arrival of our very own gourmet donut shop! I'll admit it: my first thought was "slow news week," followed promptly by an acknowledgement of a primetime ready pr campaign when I see it.  Donut fever- and not just the run of the mill kind, but the kind of heat flashes that could only be quelled by gourmet ingredients and tender loving frying care- took Indy by storm.

And then a friend posted on Facebook about waiting in line for 20 minutes for some of these tasty goodnesses, complete with a picture of people lining out the door awaiting their turn. "For a donut?" I thought. Surely, there must be something to these deep fried rings of splendor that will awaken a love buried deep within my brittle soul. 

And it turns out there is! A thirteen point buck logo! THE Stumptown Coffee! Really awesome rustic and handmadeesque packaging! If only my taste buds shared the same values as my sense of design and aesthetic appeal. 

Oh, and the donuts tasted remarkably like...donuts. Okay, sure, it could be me. My unsophisticated palate may not be able to discern the nuanced stratifications of donut prowess.  I'll readily admit this is likely the case.

But about that logo with the thirteen point buck. What does this majestic woodland creature have to do with donuts?  Hell if I know, but it does remind me of the time my wife and I went to Portland a few years ago with a mission to have dinner at the Woodsman Tavern. We'd read about the place in Bon Appetit (I know, right?!? THE Bon Appetit) a few months prior to our trip. Oh, the place sounded so woodsy and smart and woodsy and outdoorsy and smart and beardy (and-hey!- I have a beard!) and culinary and sophisticated but not too sophisticated... right up our newly recognized ascension to Middle Classdom alley. Finally! We could feel what it felt like to live a life ripped straight from the glossy margins of an honest-to-goodness lifestyle magazine. 

When we arrived in Portland,  each time we were asked by friends about our plans, we always answered the same way.  "We're up for anything,  but we want to make sure to eat dinner at the Woodsman!" Our friends passed odd glances of curiosity towards us each time we said this, but we thought nothing of it. Surely, these poor souls had yet to meet an issue of Bon Appetit. 

The Woodsman Tavern was adorned with mounted bucks and other animals on the wall. This was not a place that messed around or was about to let you forget where you were.

As it turned out, our friends knew already what we would only soon discover for ourselves.  The Woodsman Tavern kindof sucked. And by "kindof sucked", I mean the food was decent, but everything else about it- especially the service- was abysmal.  In short, it was a place meant to exist only in the pages of a bullshit lifestyle mag. They'd spent a lot of time sweating the marketing details on how to capture the attention of a national media outlet and absolutely no time on how to actually make a great restaurant. Why bother making great food and a desirable eating experience when you can just pay a PR person to make everyone think you do that?

Oh, and I first tasted the trumpeted Stumptown Coffee at the Woodsman. And... I'll get to that in a bit.

As it turns out, the Woodsman out-Portlanded Portland. And for all their effort, they became a running joke in Portland,  ripe for Portlandia but little else. 

So it goes with our donut shop, I think. The logo is a bad harbinger. It has all the markings of a we-had-a-really-cool-design-and-needed-an-excuse-to-promote-an-idea-so-we-made-a-gourmet-cafe all over it. There's a lot of form, but at the end of the day, the function is a decent donut, and, well, those can be had at any of the other hundreds of places that sell them. 

And a word about Stumptown Coffee. I know coffee taste is subjective,  and while I think Stumptown is akin to swill, and to each their own, I just want to say this: those cold brewed coffee bottles sure look nice don't they? I mean, considering the bottle costs about 1000% more to make than the coffee it contains, it should.  

So how are their donuts?  Considering this is more of a lifestyle marketing shop, who cares? Plenty a upwardly mobile, mostly white, liberal, urban dweller will be waiting to throw their dollars at what these donuts represent. Let them. Take it while the taking is good.

So why would someone spend roughly 5-6 times for a donut here than you can get anywhere else? Because you can.

What a joke!

I've been avoiding this place for the year I've been in Tucson, in large part, based on the reviews here.  Last week I had jury duty and I thought, what the hey, let's give it a try for lunch.

I ordered the combination for $15.  A bit pricey, but if they could deliver the goods I could deal with that, in spite of the very Miami Beach 1990-ish decor. 

Chips and salsa were delivered and it was quite honestly the worst salsa that I've ever had in Tucson.  Zero chiles, zero flavor.  Something you'd expect to get in Omaha - not Tucson.  How is it possible to serve bad salsa in Tucson, Arizona?

My lunch entree consisted of a an extremely bland "chicken oaxaca," an extremely bland machaca and an overly sweet coconut and pineapple tamale.  But the most alarming thing was the salad, a big messy pile of undressed greens served on top of the other food.

Frankly, I had read about this but I still wasn't prepared for it.  Why would you do that?  First of all, the greens were completely undressed.  For $15, I expect a bit more. Secondly, they were plopped on top of my food, so they were mucking about in the bland "Oaxaca" sauce.  Unappetizing and just, well, stupid.

I had to empty out my chips plate to have somewhere to move the limp  cream sauce coated greens to in order to be able to get at the food underneath.  Ridiculously bad idea.

In addition to being bland, it's pretty obvious that whoever cooked the food has absolutely no idea what they are doing.  The chicken was cut  very clumsily.  Some pieces were 4 inches long.  Others were diced.  Sad.

All of the food was completely lacking in flavor.  No salt, no chiles, nada.

I did not encounter any of the famous attitude although I could certainly sense it lurking in the background.  They are very impressed with themselves here.  The New York Times gave this place a great review?  Are you kidding me?  

This is Mexican food for people who don't really like Mexican food.  I cannot imagine any circumstance in which I would return to this restaurant.  

The people who say this is "Mexico City" style must not have ever been to Mexico City.  I have and believe me, this ain't it.  Do yourself a favor and pass on this one.

The Garden Table is a local eatery that serves seasonally influenced and locally sourced food.  They offer simple, yet creative dishes, made from fresh and natural ingredients.  They also offer outdoor and indoor seating - with the interior having an amazing, laid back vibe.  

My wife and I recently visited The Garden Table on Easter Sunday, and thankfully we arrived just in time to beat the crowd.  Our server was attentive and friendly and did not make us feel rushed.  

I ordered the Stuffed French Toast (Baked Sourdough, Fruit Du Jour, Maple Syrup, Whipped Butter) and can honestly say it is probably some of the best French Toast that I have ever had!  The fact that they can take the simple concept of Fresh Toast and turn it into a mouthwatering meal packed with flavor and richness is incredible!  I also tried the Butternut Squash & Bacon, a healthier option that I recommend if you still want your bacon fix.  A cup of Fresh Fruit and a glass of fresh Orange Juice rounded things off to be the perfect meal!
Both the pork belly and a spare rib sliders were amazing. Loved the duck empanadas and the seared scallops.

Visiting this place 6 days after opening and on night #1 of bar service, I'll give The Row major kudos. You would never be able to tell this place was brand new. And I mean that as a compliment... as in, the service was like a well-oiled machine. Allison was our server and always made sure we were never thirsty, never hungry, and on top of that, made excellent recommendations.

To start, we couldn't resist the Pickle Flyte (1 for $4, 4 for $13): Crazy Carrots, Pickled Pipers, Bread & Butters, and Sour Dills. For our main entrees, I went with the veggie plate (choice of 4 sides for $13) while my date ordered the catfish ($14). LEGIT. If we're speaking sides, between us we can both recommend the Bourbon Sweet Potatoes, Braised Local Greens and Cheese Grits. (I had the Smashed Potatoes, too... good, but not enough to repeat.)

I selfishly deducted one star because their delicious cocktail menu taunted me when only beer and wine was available. Not that we could blame them on the bar's first night. /shrug

Our full tummies and empty wallets wouldn't let us try the flyte of dessert this time around, but let's be honest... we'll be back.

I'm dreading writing this review. Honestly, the food was fantastic (some of the best prosciutto the hubs and I've ever had), the drinks were well-crafted (hello, Secret Garden cocktail), even our waitress (whose name escapes me) made sure we were well attended to. 

So, why the one-star rating, you ask? Well, it's simple, friends. Customer service and human decency go a LONG way.

Basically, 16 of us dined this evening for my hubby's company holiday party. Several appetizers, entrees, and sides (and cocktails!) later, we racked up a $2000 tab and were well on our way to ordering desserts.

Relevant sidenote: The hubs' boss is undergoing chemo treatments for a bout of cancer that has left him with a cold sensitivity, especially with the typical hair loss. When he put on a wool beanie in the restaurant to keep warm, he was immediately asked to remove it... which he did. When his family mentioned his condition and questioned the treatment from Catrina, the assistant manager, they were told he could wear it if he presented a doctors' note... or if we had given them previous notice so we could be accommodated elsewhere. (Out of sight, out of mind?)

In short, what followed was shock/disbelief (can't say that I blame them) and the cops being called (huh?), and we were (all 16 of us) asked to leave.

On our way out, my protective spouse asked the manager if we looked like criminals. To which he responded, "the cops just patrol this area and decided to check in." Riiiight.

So. I reiterate: Customer service and human decency go a LONG way. I've been in Nashville close to 15 years and I really hate to think that the city I love has an establishment so pretentious that they would discriminate against someone with a life-threatening condition. Is a wool beanie on one individual's head that much of a threat to sales and ambiance?

Dining a Vault Brewing in the heart of downtown Yardley, PA introduces you to a new definition of taste. If you are in the mood for a cold beer on tap, you can SEE the beer being made in FULL VIEW right behind the bar. The kitchen, with it's wood fire oven is also in plain sight, and as you bite into your grass fed burger or wood fired pizza, you can see and taste the warmth, flavor, and scent that floats out of that oven. As you look around the space, you see iron fencing, high ceilings, and even an original bank vault door from the late ninetieth century now used as the entrance to the beer cellar. That said, Vault Brewing is a unique dining experience...where everything from the sites and smells all come together to really alter your taste buds, in a really cool and fun way! 

Introductory details:
 Vault Brewing dates back to 1889, where it once served the citizens of Yardley as their National Bank. It was the home of Bank of America until 2009. Then In 2012, the Cain Family transformed the old bank into a brewery and restaurant... and the magic began!!! 
I feel privileged to have had the experience to dine at Vault Brewing with my mom just the other day for the first time. I knew I was going to be in the area ahead of time, and messaged a very reliable yelp elite Gerald S who knows the area well and recommended the Vault! THANK YOU Gerald, your recommendation did not disappoint! 

The DRINKS:
I'm not a huge drinker, but when in Rome, well... you know :)  
I prefer dark beers, but I didn't want anything too strong since it was lunch time. I ended up ordering the Weizenbock, which is a dark wheat ale with hints of cherry, figs, plums, and toffee. It was a great choice for not having a beer in hmmm.... a year??? hahah!!! It SO hit the spot! Very flavorful!
My mom loves beer and ordered the Belma Blonde ASAP. It's a Session Ale with a lot of hops and with a very citrus taste. It actually tasted a lot like grapefruit in my opinion (mom and I shared sips of each other's drinks). But if you like citrus, this beer was BURSTING with flavor! And yes, we saw the beer flowing right from the brewing itself, to the tap, to the glass! haha! The process was in plain site! 
Water was given to us without asking, which is a huge plus. H20 is very important! I like it went restaurants provide you with a glass as soon as you sit down. 

THE FOOD:
The food here did not disappoint and the prices were very reasonable. We had such a hard time deciding what we wanted because everything looked good! My mom ended up getting the grass fed burger with a side house salad, and I got the crab cake sliders with a house salad. Both were excellent.  The crab cakes were not too fishy but still had that real crab cake taste. The burger, my mom said, was cooked just right. I do think that the bread on the crab cakes was a bit TOO big, for a I had to take off one of the buns because my mouth is just too tiny. LOL! Plus, I'm not supposed to eat bread (shame on me!) for health purposes, but I just decided to splurge! So worth it! 

SERVICE/ATMOSPHERE

Service was fantastic. The hostess who seated us was friendly and upbeat. Our server was informative, professional, and full of smiles the entire time. I also have to say, the other customers were fantastic! My mom and I dined the day of the Eagles Super Bowl Parade. We are both fans, but could not attend the parade because I had a doctor's appointment. But this place was truly a birds NEST for the customers were coming in complete eagles gear as the day went on! A lovely family sat next too us and we engaged in some great conversation with them. The family showed us pictures from the parade on their phones and close ups of the players... it was great! I love good food and good company. I'm also a die hard eagles fan and it was just so hmm REFRESHING to see so much GREEN in one spot! And, to be greeted with a smile instead of a snarl?!?! WHOA! I live in giants territory so I was just in my glory. Literally. Mom too :) 

Plus, the whole Vault concept really makes this place unique. The owners of the brewery kept just enough of the original bank in place so you know you are dining in a vault ;) It's really a cool and very unique experience.  

I'll be back! And, if you aren't an eagles fan, don't worry, we dined on the day OF the parade, so I was eager to have conversation with fellow eagles fans. If you want to dine in peace, you most definitely have that option. I'm the one who likes to talk talk talk! hahah! 

I highly recommend this place and the next time I decide to splurge it is going to be on one of their big pizzas!!!
