It's too cold to go out bare-chested. I get up and I put on my new blue merino wool hoodie that I have purchased from the Gap. It is new and it is perfect. It flows comfortably over my body and keeps me warmer than any blue merino wool hoodie has ever kept anyone warm before. I fawn over it in a way that can only be described as the love that hand model, Ellen Sirot, expressed for her hands to Katie Couric. Like Ellen and her hands, we are inseparable. 

Oh, we are good. The hoodie was on sale but together we are spectacular. We sit on the train to the city together and we walk to Mac's Tavern, padding and shunning the cold wind. We sit in the back of the bar and raise a hand to make a drinking gesture to the waiter that, in a different context, could land us in the back of a cop car. We make the gesture with such accuracy, and with such ridiculous beauty that the server surely knows to bring over a Jack and Coke without ever hearing a single word.

We await the arrival of our drink, in such an astounding fashion that my drinking buddies share the anguish and dire thirst. They wait too, looking around the room for the server to return. When he does, he douses the blue hoodie in Jack Daniels, stripping it of its perfect nature. The drink is too strong and garnished with a lemon. 

He does not look like a professional, like he never saw the inside of a bar prior to that moment. Patrons stop and stare at the spill. He walks away without ever saying a word. Later, he bumps into me and gets ketchup on the back of the tarnished hoodie. After continually ignoring my perfect requests for another drink and telling me to wait, he finally brings a second Jack and Coke. This one is devoid of liquor. He spills it on my hoodie, pants, and hand. Again, he walks away without ever saying a word. I sit and shake my head, gasping. No one has ever seen anything quite like it.

*Please don't sue me, David Eggers, for blatantly ripping you off.

If you take anything from this review, remember the next 5 words. Get. The. Garlic. White. Sauce. You'll thank me later.

This was the best pizza I've had in a LONG time. Usually I go to another local pizza place in the area, but decided to expand and give others a chance. Im so glad I did!!!! I ordered the Supreme pizza with garlic white sauce for delivery, with cheese bread. It was still super hot and fresh when it was delivered, and I live about 20 min away from there. 

This is now my "new" local place. Im still dreaming about this pizza and cannot wait to order again! Thanks for being so delicious and having great customer service!

My experience here got off to a shaky start.  I called up for a table for a party of 7 and was told, "You won't need a reservation, but I'll take your name anyway."  Fast forward to 8pm, we get there and the place is packed, looked like word from Sauce traveled fast, good news for a new restaurant.  But for my friends and I, we ended up waiting for an hour to sit down because they couldn't get 2 adjacent tables to open up and put together.

So while waiting at the bar, never ever hearing of something called 'oyster bread', ordered it.  The order got lost somewhere along the line and showed up 30 min or so later.  It's a garlic/oyster spread over some french bread, with a little spice to kick, it was pretty damn tasty.  

Finally at our table, we order half the menu, eat off each others plates and the verdict: this place was just about worth the wait!

The star was the seafood gumbo: rich, and complex, lots of seafood. only available Fridays.
Crawfish etoufee; dark, rich and balanced as another yelper mentioned, and it was generously jampacked with crawfish, I loved it.
Chicken gumbo offered a delicious alternative to the seafood gumbo, crawfish creole was well made, but I was expecting a little more...kick.
Meatloaf was solid, no real surprises.  And a beef poboy was good, but I think I'd go with a shrimp or crawfish next time, as their seafood was definitely the highlight.

Homemade bread pudding was piping hot and good, but not spectacular.

So after the gorging, we were still a little miffed about the hour wait and frankly, subpar, although extremely friendly service (which we chalked up to it being a new restaurant).  And then the manager (or owner), comes over and offers to buy us all a drink for the wait.  

Solid 4 stars, but there's some 5 star potential here after they work out the kinks.

I CONQUERED THE ADAM BOMB!  
well, actually a 1/3 of one.  

with 2 of my friends we took care of the full slab of ribs, pulled pork and brisket sandwiches, quarter chicken, sweet potato fries, deep-fried corn, baked beans, potato salad and a frito pie.  cleaned it off, we were complimented on our work by the staff.

right now your mouth just started watering or you're very concerned for my cholesterol levels (that's very sweet of you).

side note: can you imagine the doctor visits with adam?  

Doctor: your cholesterol's too high, your stomach's permanently distended, your pancreas is pooped out from pumping insulin, your arteries are clogged...for the love of God, Buddha and Chuck Norris, put down the fork!

Adam: but doc, if you take away my overeating, what do i have left?  i'm not good looking enough to stay on TV without eating and andrew zimmern already got the exotic foods covered.

Doctor: you're growing man-boobs.

Adam: ok, last season, i promise.

It was enough food for 4 people, with the 3 of us, it was enough to push us from happy-full to almost uncomfortably-full.  wasn't my first time here, but i never had the frito pie before;  with the baked beans, red onions and andouille, it was better than i thought, definitely a sleeper pick.

All these negative reviews kill me!! If I had the money I would open a franchise, and yes have looked into it.... 

This is not about being skinny this is about being healthy, as all the ingredients are natural but yes high in natural sugars as well.  People that love to eat here eat here because it's healthy and they want to be healthy not because they want to be skinny, if that's the case eat a salad with vinegar! Leave the amazing delicious energizing ingredients to the rest us!

Sorry for all the negativity, and just can't stand it when people head to the internet to ignorantly complain just for the attention
Honestly only ever went here in an effort to support small business. The reality is, the coffee isn't anything to remember; food is something that could be had for free at a homeless shelter.

Phenomenal experience! A most excellent place to meet friends for a pot of tea or study. Other patrons are normally very polite and conversations are quiet. Staff is patient, service is never rushed, and there are many different teas available to satisfy different tastes and pricepoints. Not a lot available in the terms of snacks, aside from little lotus cakes...so come thirsty, not hungry! :) If you find a tea you particularly fancy, they sell leaves for at home brewing. Great atmosphere!

What a neat independent coffee shop! 

From the kindness of the barristas, to the phenomenal baked goods and coffee, I can honestly say that I have never had anything less than a stellar experience here. There is seating tucked outside in a courtyard underneath trees, which even in the midday Tucson heat, always seems to have shade and a relaxing breeze. Inside, there are wood floors and plenty of 2 top tables...and, an added bonus...they play classical music lightly in the background! Great shop. 

And yes, as all the other reviews state, the scones are amazing. (I had a coconut chocolate chip one yesterday, and a fig walnut one today....so good!) Brava!  

PS: Parking lot is in the back!

PPS: They have ALMOND syrup! Do you like Vanilla syrup, but you want to branch out a bit? Try adding Almond to your latte - Best. Decision. Ever. It's so good, Yelp brothers and sisters. So. Good. :)

So many different varieties of teas to choose from - you will have no problem finding one that you like! In addition to traditional greens, oolongs, blacks, they have an abundance of flavored and dessert teas. Nice tea service, with non dairy options. This is a busy place...I wouldn't recommend trying to study here frequently; although staff is friendly and would welcome you, it is super busy on weekends and very often difficult to find seating. Weekdays during the day are much better. Desserts are very tasty. Also, they have a "tap" which features different iced teas daily, which are great to grab and enjoy on the run as you walk down University on a warm day.

....Nadine's Bakery. Oh man, simply typing the name makes my mouth water. Heck, simply thinking of the name makes me giddy and excited. 

I admit, the first time I went there, I was a little skeptical - the building looked like it was straight out of the 50's, a little run down, and past it's prime. Then, I tasted some of the almond cake....and thine eyes were opened. 

Everything is delicious; russian tea cakes, cookies, little petit fours, bars upon bars, eclairs..... In addition to the cheesecake bars, and other little delicacies which are there every day of the week, they also bake specialty things on different days of the week. (My favorite is this almond puff pastry bavarian cream thing they only bake on Fridays....to die for!) This place is a pastry wonderland. 

Oh, and did I mention the bread?!?!? Do you take your Rye dark, or light, seeded/unseeded? No problem, they've got all types. 

And the staff, so kind...and so patient. They never seem to get irritated with me as I take forever to decide what I want....so good. Outstanding!

Holy crap....you had me at Nutella latte. Seriously. So good. It was absolute perfection!

I came here around 7pm on a Tuesday night after a friend recommended it - I ordered my drink and found a little table by the glass window that looked out over Broadway, plugged in my laptop and looked out into the night, and for a minute I felt like I was far away from Tucson, somewhere on the east coast! It was absolutely divine! The atmosphere is welcoming and the staff is kind. I can't comment on the pastry selection, as I was here during the evening, and their stock was a little low. But, with a nutella latte, I had my sweet fix for the evening and was A-OK. Prices were reasonable, and the whole experience was outstanding. I will definitely return here in the future!

Holy Coconut Curry, Batman! :) This place is great, but be warned....that little chili icon by the dish? They're not playing around; they may give you the option of "hotness" by choosing a hot level on a 1-5 scale, but level 1 is still hot enough to blow your hair back a bit! My personal favorite: #32 Kang Ped - spicy red curry, bamboo shoots in coconut milk with chicken. It will set you back $11.95, but it's worth it. But, remember - please, heed my warning - Level one is still blazin'! ;)

This is breakfast diner perfection. There's a large menu to accommodate any tastes, and everything is great.  Be warned, the pancakes are gigantic. Best home fries in tucson...they are home made not frozen, grilled and crispy on the outside and tender in the middle...delicious, especially floating in maple syrup. If you get there before 0730, you can get a full egg/fries/toast/coffee breakfast for under $2.50. Not kidding! Coffee is good and Wait staff is attentive and hustles to keep cups filled and food served fast and steaming. Outstanding.

What a gem! I am normally not a big Mexican food fan (I'm one of those-kinda-peoples that don't like their food to touch...), but I am guilty of going to this place once a week for the past 4 straight weeks (I am not ashamed) which has yielded an opportunity to try numerous things on the menu. I have yet to be disappointed. 

The food is tops; the chile relleno is stellar - and HUGE. The tortillas are homemade and made on the grill while you wait. The machaca tacos are delicious - the meat is juicy and flavorful without being super salty. The chimi was perfectly crispy, without being overly greasy. Also, the Colorado red chile - thumbs up, superb. (Adventure away from your standard goto Cheese enchilada order and you will be thankful you were brave and went for it - delicious!)

I've gone here on either Friday or Saturday, peak of business hours, and my party has never experienced a problem with long waits or not being seated. The parking is plentiful, and the outside view is refreshing when you step out into the night air - it overlooks Tucson. Oh, and the coffee - I don't know what they add to their brew, but I've never had such a good cup of black coffee. I have never been here for breakfast, but I imagine it's tops, too. Give it a shot!

This place is great. Hands down my favorite coffee place in Tucson! The inside of the building is super cool, a renovated industrial space which backs to the train tracks. (Especially neat if you enjoy trainwatching!) The roaster is out in the open so the delicious aroma fills the space. The coffee is amazing...absolutely delicious, the best latte in Tucson. My friends all adore the chilitepin toddy...but it is too much for me, I prefer something milder. There is not a large variety of baked goods or snacks. The beans are available for purchase. Great tables seating for a party of two or less but there is limited seating for any group of 3 or more. (2 tables) Music is vinyl and genre varies on the barista.  Warning, it can get a tad warm in there because of the large windows and roaster...but nothing unbearable. Also, the city recently placed paid parking all around it...so bring some change for the meter. Great place!

Love the $10 one-topping carryout pizza deal! For someone with dietary restrictions, it is awesome to be able to order a specialty pizza and pick it up to take home for dinner. I have gotten pizza from here over 10 times - all between the busy hours of 7-9pm - and never had a pie I didn't like, or that wasn't outstanding! You can call ahead and order, or you can place your order in store and it will be done in 15 minutes. Fifteen yummy minutes - who can't kill 15 minutes walking around the Whole Foods - grab a drink from the bar, sniff some soaps/lotions, peruse over-priced merchandise...and then, voila, pick up your pizza and roll! Delicious crust, and fresh toppings, made with care and love. Any additional toppings is an extra $1 - so, even if you can't pick between two toppings, the price is still outstanding....and there are so many different options to pick and choose - from different crusts, to sauces (original red, garlic oil, buffalo, bbq, etc), to toppings and cheeses....great stuff. Looking for something a little different? Try the regular crust with buffalo sauce, and chicken and peppers! NOM! Bacon and pineapple, no sauce, was great too!

Sick of the same ole thing, I jumped on Yelp to find a lunch locale to meet a friend.  The 5 stars this new sandwich shop received in a few short months made up my mind, and what a great call it was!   

We both opted for the El Cubano, which comes in three sizes.  She choose a small, while I ordered a medium and the black bean soup.  They also had complimentary yucca chips that we both enjoyed.  My sandwich was nothing short of perfection, from the crispy bread to just the right amount of ingredients.  The soup was homemade and flavorful, with hot sauce available for those who prefer a little spice.  Other sides include plantains and rice, if you so desire.

The owners made a point to check to make sure everyone in the restaurant enjoyed their lunch, even offering samples of their fresh Cuban coffee and pastries to those who declined the espresso.  I'd be short changing him if I didn't say it was the absolute best coffee I've ever tasted.  Truly delicious.  Cuban coffee is already sweetened, he shared.  

The entire family was welcoming and hospitable, making for a relaxing spot to catch up with a friend over lunch.  There are several small tables and counter space, but this isn't a spot for a large group.  On the up side, they do have large sandwiches that can be carried out and they do cater!

Have been a customer for awhile but after tonight's experience, will never order from them again.   Judging by some of the reviews of the poor customer service, I'm probably not alone.  We placed an order for delivery, and 7 minutes later, called back to cancel due to a personal situation requiring us to leave the house.  The owner took the call and demanded to know what the reason was and I apologized and repeated that I needed to cancel. He continued to argue and then hung up on me!   What a jerk.  

There's too many great delivery options in the Downtown & University area, so I'll be happily taking my money elsewhere from now on.

Amazing unique creative and traditional flavored Latin dishes. Very large variety to choose from. Many vegan and vegetarian options. Which I was so excited for!

Hard time choosing. I picked Mexican squash soup. It was creamy and flavorful. Excellent. The Hibiscus taco (slow cooked Hibiscus flowers induced with spices). With pickled veggies and fresh herbs and avocado slices on top. Very good. The corn tortillas were thick and fluffy not thin, chewy or greasy. Both really really good. The Hibiscus was different, the spices were good. The tacos were doubled tortillas and piled high with fillings so I was able to make two tacos. And the Poblano Tamale was out of this world! My favorite.

The guacamole and the jalapeño creama was really good. But the chips aren't my favorite. I'm guessing vegan/gf. But the next day they were crispy and great! So scratch that just wait until they cool off. 

I want to try the mole tofu taco, a torta and the spiced tea hot and a couple other things. I'll be going back soon.

Check out their menu and order carryout or delivery. I highly recommend.

Sqwires is a delight to both the eyes and the tummy! We checked it out today for the firs time for post-mass brunch. Upon walking in, I immediately fell in love with the decor. I can't explain how beautiful and unique it is. From the bar, the lighting, to the massive indoor fireplace, I had something to look at the whole time. The restaurant was so clean, with everything neatly placed. Our waitress was pleasant and just attentive enough. 

The menu presented some delicious options for breakfast, as well as vegan and vegetarian options. Our meal came out within 10 minutes of ordering- so quick! I thoroughly enjoyed the traditional breakfast fare and ate until I couldn't any more. The portion sizes were perfect and the price point was really agreeable. I can say that we will definitely be back for dinner sometime and to enjoy the mimosa and Bloody Mary bar after lent!

Pappy's, my sweet, sweet Pappy's. Shall I compare thee to a summer's rose? No, that would be weird, but I will compare thee to other local BBQ spots. And... You shall take four stars! First and foremost, do not expect to get in and eat quickly, my friends. The line for a lunch at Pappy's is not for the faint of heart, and surely not for those about to pass out due to food deprivation. You WILL wait. But, you will be happy that you did. 

Ribs. Get the ribs and love yourself for ordering them and your tongue for tasting them. My first visit, the owner was walking around with, listen, FREE RIBS, just handing them out like candy to those of us waiting in line. It was almost too good to be true. I had some great conversation in that line, it made the wait fly by. The service was phenomenal and though we were worried we wouldn't get a spot to eat, we were relieved that they opened up quickly. 

This really is some of the best BBQ in St. Louis, you just can't beat it. But do expect a long line and to get out after you eat quickly, it's not necessarily a place you can sit and chat, relax.

ZERO STARS 
I must start out by saying this review didn't happen the moment I left this establishment due to me shaking from the treatment I received from this place, the owner who I had the terrible pleasure of coming in contact with, this is by far the most unprofessional, dirty and most disgusting run place I have ever seen. 

I came here on a recommendation for a great pasta place, well I couldn't tell you how well the pasta could have been as I didn't even get my order. 

I started out by calling as I was ordering for more than one person, to find out the specials as it was a lunch hour, and they were all curious. After I got myself together I took the liberty of reading the reviews on this place and it's sad to see this has happened multiple times, and even more terrible experiences.

Yes! One of the best brunches I have ever had! 

A self-proclaimed "brunch club" and I met here a few weeks ago and we were NOT disappointed! It was nice to be able to make a reservation for 5 and not have to wait for a table. The parking is ample (unlike Datz) and the old world New Orleans decorations are great.

Something unique to Roux that I haven't really seen other places is brunch happy hour (10-3 Saturday and Sunday in the restaurant) The hot crab dip was excellent! The crab beignets were alright but not the best I've ever had. Both of these were half price due to happy hour. The mimosas were 2-for-1 and the pomegranate and pineapple were both very tasty.

We also shared a large gumbo ($12) for our meal and it was great! However, we decided next time it would be more cost efficient to just get a bunch of the 1/2 price appetizers. They were huge and keep us full. I didn't try it, but my fiancé LOVED his 2-for-1 spicy Bloody Marys. (It appears to be the same mix as Datz). You can switch flavors on the Bloody Marys and mimosas which is nice. 

We wanted to try the bread pudding (the Buffalo Trace butterscotch sauce caught my eye) but we were just too darn full. Next time I will make a point to get it! We all paid separately without any issues. Thank you to our server for offering great suggestions and taking good care of us!

Oh man, Whiskey Cake! The best meal my husband and I have had out in a while! 

We met some friends here for brunch last weekend and grabbed a reservation on OpenTable, which actually wasn't necessary because there was plenty of available seating, but better to be safe than sorry. The restaurant is much larger than it appears from the outside and I love the library-style whiskey shelves and the little herb garden outside. 

Since I'm 6 months pregnant, I really appreciated that they had an assortment of mocktails on the menu so I didn't have to feel totally left out or just order basic water or soda. I really enjoyed the Hulk ($5) which was basically a virgin mojito. My husband was happy that they had a pretty decent selection of local draft beers. 

For my meal I had the OMG 2.0 Burger ($14) and OMG was it good. Despite me ordering it well-done, it was still juicy and seasoned well. I ordered the chile mayo on the side and didn't really care for it but the burger didn't need it with all of the other toppings. The house made chips that came with it were dripping with grease but our waiter brought another order to me after pointing it out and they were nice and crispy. 

After giving my husband half of my burger I ate half of his Farmers Breakfast ($12) which came with eggs, potatoes, jalapeño biscuits, cheddar grits, and candied bacon. Everything on the platter was delicious! 

Even though we were nearly stuffed each couple had to order the Whiskey Cake for dessert ($9) and out came this humongous, dense, chewy and gooey piece of heaven with house made whipped cream. The four of us could have totally shared one piece but we scarfed it down anyway. It's one of the best desserts I've ever had. 

Our waiter, I believe his name was Trevor, was especially helpful at helping us select things from the menu and we appreciated his honest opinions on some of the dishes. He kept our water glasses full and was friendly and attentive. The four of us decided we are already planning a trip back!

My favorite place to take folks who are visiting from out of town!

Come enjoy the free tour and learn about how their delicious fruit wines are made. The gift shop has a ton of wine accessories and other Florida items (jams, hot sauce, candles, etc.) The tour is about 30 minutes long and at the end you get to taste their five most popular wines, then three of your choice and three wine slushies. 

They have a ton of flavored fruit wines. You won't find grape wines here (I think they have two or three). You will find sweeter fruits like pineapple, mango, key lime, etc., and then some more unique flavors like carrot, orange/chocolate, and coffee. 

The employees are always friendly and helpful and we can't leave without grabbing a bottle or two. We joined the wine club and every 12 bottles you buy produces a free bottle of wine. The last trip I couldn't resist a bottle of the pineapple champagne which I can't wait to make mimosas with!

I don't even know where to begin....well, yes I do.  My trip to Vango began by getting a full pat-down at the front door.  Seriously, four polite, well dressed people getting patted down and having bags searched on 18th St at 10:00PM on a Friday night was absurdly comical.

Even before the TSA style entrance, I had problems with Vango.  We came down with a TravelZoo voucher that was unfortunately expired, so only the price paid was still valid as a gift certificate.  We were going to get four drinks and head up to the roof, but that plan was derailed when an obnoxious bartender started screaming (literally) for her manager to come and take care of "these people with a voucher."  

The even more obnoxious manager comes over and says, you can't use that after 9:00.  I told her that there's nothing on the voucher that says that, and it's not even a promotion since we're just using what we paid for it like a gift certificate.  Her response:  "We decided to put a policy in place and there's nothing I can do for you, have a good evening," and she just walked away.  

I will forfeit the cost of the voucher, and hop on the bandwagon of Vango bashers out there to see to it that this place doesn't survive another six months.  Do Not Go Here!

It looks like I missed the first review by a few hours, but that doesn't change the experience we had on opening weekend:  hit and miss.

We were massive fans of Stateside and couldn't wait to give Aldine a try.  The entrance is not marked and easy to miss, so make sure you're familiar with the surroundings when you stop by.  Upon climbing the stairs, we were excited to see the relaxed, warm, somewhat romantic ambiance, and we were thrilled with our two-top window seat.

The service was on point all night, but still a bit awkward and a little unsure of the menu, which is very simple and nondescript.  It's the the kind of menu that really forces you to trust the chef.  I felt the same way at Serpico and Noord recently, and both times, the chef won, but it wasn't always a success here.

We started with the saison draft, which was not too cold and a little flat, which wasn't a great start.  To pair with it, we had the rabbit and raw beef plates.  Each of us loved one and not the other, which was unusual.  I preferred the beef with it's jarring contrast of soft meat and crunchy quinoa, while my partner enjoyed the more cohesive taste of the rabbit terrine (never would have guessed it from the menu description).  

The star of the night arrived next, which was the sunchoke soup with apple crisps.  It was extremely flavorful, smooth and perfectly seasoned.  I will note that we asked for more apple chips, because there were only three on the plate, and they added a wonderful contrast that was needed for the entire dish, not just the first two bites.  Along with this, we had the squid/pork belly dish.  I felt that the pork belly was a little over and the squid wasn't featured at all.  It's really a pork belly dish with squid shavings and black rice crackers...not my favorite.

Our main was the duck, and if we would have had just this dish and the soup, this was an easy five-star review.  It was incredibly tender, spicy, and packed with strong duck flavor.  I really enjoyed it, but we should have stopped there.  Instead we went for dessert and two after-dinner cocktails.

The cocktails were great with the vodka slightly beating out the gin and pear.  I thought the price and the size of the vodka drink were very fair, and it seemed to get better as the ice melted.  Unfortunately, the fennel fritter with maple ice dessert was a serious disappointment.  It was five small fritters over unflavored snow cone shavings.  It was hard to finish, and after explaining our disappointment with our server, it should have been removed from the bill.  On the flip side of that, the apple/coconut/caramel sundae was delicious.  The best way I can describe it would be a high-end deconstructed apple pie a la mode.

We fought over a three or four star review, but the old method of: would we return or not settled the score.

So, I've been to the Drunken Fish a few times, at each location, and have never been blown away by any of the experiences.

However, I've decided I'm not going back based on my last one at the CWE location.

I've never gotten poor service at any of the Drunken Fish locations, but I'm usually on a date or otherwise dressed to impress. The last time I went was to grab a bite right before work. I was in scrubs and no make-up. Oh em gee an atrocity. 

When I went in the hostesses ignored me for a moment while they finished up their conversation. They were all gathered around talking because the place was pretty much dead and acted like I wasn't even standing there. Then looked at me..."Hi........just you?" Yes, just me. "Okay. Sit wherever you want." Okay. I sat at the sushi bar.

Sushi was fine, as usual; my actual waitress was sweet. But as people walked in behind me, couples, groups of friends, all dressed up to high CWE style, I kept hearing, "Hi, welcome to Drunken Fish! Would you like to try our happy hour?"

Wait, happy hour?! Then I realized their happy hour was 5-7pm upstairs. Cheap drinks and sushi. I came in at 5:30pm. Why the hell wasn't I offered the happy hour? I would have saved about half of my bill.

Then I had to think that it was because how I looked. That may seem silly, but that's the kind of place this is. That's how ALL of Munsok's restaurants are. Completely hung up on appearances. Sitting down there by myself paying for overpriced sushi when everyone else was yucking it up upstairs paying only half of what I was paying for the same thing made me feel like the girl in the 1st grade class that didn't get invited to the birthday party everyone else did.

By the way, when I left, I didn't get a "bye" or a "thank you" for my business, even though the same group of girls were all standing there not doing anything and just silently watched me walk out. That's cool. I just won't bring my business back. And I'll write scathing reviews on Yelp about it.

There are really no redeeming qualities about The Drunken Fish. It's not worth it. This place, and all of the places under this same umbrella, are pretentious and shallow as hell. That's why I don't work for them anymore and that's why I won't be back.

This was our first stop on a long weekend trip and wanted to start it out with some healthy eating! Definitely a great choice! I really love the open air vibe of this place. The space itself is huge, but they also have such large windows and everything feels very light and airy. We started out with some drinks, I got the Watermelon Lemonade ($5) and my fiancé Kale Aid ($9). These prices are definitely pretty steep, especially considering that these are non-alcoholic drinks, but I do think that everything is super fresh squeezed and made with quality ingredients.

For my meal, I got the Chopped Salad, we had some awesome ingredients such as dates, apples, manchego cheese, and a few other yummy things. The salad was very fresh. My fiancé got to the Ancient Grains bowl, which was super flavorful. I especially loved the green sauce that they had on them! It paired really well with the sweet potato.

I've got to say, that this definitely ends up being a pretty expensive meal. But considering the quality of the ingredients that you get, I think it's definitely be worth it once in a while. The food will definitely leave you feeling satisfied and healthy.

A giant, gourmet food court is basically every foodie's dream and that is essentially what you'll find at Reading Terminal Market. Right across the street from the convention center, it certainly gets packed when there is an event going on but most of the lines move quick. I guess the only issue would be finding seating to eat your food. Some of the restaurants have their own seating and waiter service, some just have a bar area, and some have nothing at all.

I ended up trying a cheesesteak from By George followed by waiting 45 minutes in line for Amish donuts at Beiler's. Aside from that, they have pretty much any cuisine you'd like as well as fresh groceries (fruits/veggies, meat, fish, seafood, etc). I would definitely like to come back one day when it isn't as crazy to try out more things!

THERE WAS A COCKROACH IN MY FOOD

i've read many reviews saying they'd give 0 stars if possible & i've finally found a place where the feeling applies... ZERO STARS.

long story short- we ordered food to go. although the food itself wouldn't have gotten many stars on it's own,  almost halfway through the meal we found a COCKROACH inside the rice. i can't even explain how disgusted i am. not even in third world countries have i gotten a bug, let alone a COCKROACH in my food. it's beyond disgusting & unbelievable. it makes me question what was hidden in my soup. 

COMPLETELY UNACCEPTABLE- absolutely no chance ill ever come back here. keep your cockroaches.

I WILL NEVER COME HERE AGAIN.

My first experience with Brazilian food was with a Brazilian friend in Queens in 2009...I fell in love with Picanha and mashed potatoes. I was tickled when I found a similar place in Northeast Philadelphia (Picanha), and I took the family. We went there when we wanted to relax, Fogo de Chao to splurge, and Chima with friends or for a night out with the kids.

Of course I was super excited to get a Groupon for Rodizio Grill in Voorhees, thinking that this place could become a part of the rotation, however I won't be returning. Rodizio is the Old County Buffet of Brazilian steakhouses. 

The salad bar is petty, the ambiance is lacking, the service is slow, and the gauchos lack the disneyfied luster found at higher end establishments. None of this would matter if the food had been delicious...unfortunately, the quality of the meat was subpar hence I did not indulge in my beloved Picanha. 

Rodizio might be "America's first Brazilian grill" but it seems that they are  masquerading as a Brazilian grill but are in fact just a typical mediocre buffet.

This place is horrific with high prices. I was there last Saturday night with a buddy of  mine. We sat at the bar to have a drink. After the first round my buddy decided to go upstairs to check it out. When he tried to go upstairs the bouncer informed him that he needed to have a drink to go upstairs. Well when he returned the bartender had already taken his glass so he asked for a glass of ice water. The bouncer told him that he still was not allowed to go up because he was only drinking ice water?!? Are you kidding me?!? Of course we see several young attractive women go up there without a drink but that is besides the point. I tell my friend let's go this is a no-class place for kids that don't know any better. That's when the bouncer decides to get in my face and threaten to kick my ass outside. Well I've outgrown this kind of testosterone driven kind of reaction and needless to say we left. Pretty scary when the bouncers are looking for a fight. Not too worry. Places like this will probably have a fight break out, someone will get hurt, and they will probably have their liquor license revoked for encouraging people to get drunk so they can go upstairs. 
Walk away people. This place doesn't deserve to be in business.

Urban shitina. The service was so outrageously bad that I will never ever set foot in here again.  The dimwitted waitress charged someone else's bill onto my credit card. then said she couldn't reprint an updated receipt after it was supposedly "corrected." and said "don't worry, it's taken care of." When I received my statement and there was no "Correction" the restaurant was called. Multiple attempts to get a manager on the phone finally found me listening to some asshat saying he can't retroactively credit a card.  What kind of 1980s system are these people using!? So I was told a credit would be mailed to me. You think that happened? hell no. I look forward to hearing that this place has gone out of business- it's just a matter of time.

I highly recommend this friendly winery.
Their white wines are so refreshing and perfect for summer. Luckily, one can sign up for a subscription service in order to have the wine shipped to your household monthly.

The moment the valet took my keys, I realized this was going to be a special evening.  The builder spared no expense to create a classy intimate space with great booths.  I ordered the 30 dollar steak special with mashed potatos and a Matt salad followed by a brownie desert. 
I paired that with a not bad white wine. The steak was cooked perfectly and the potatos really impressed me.  Someone brought some incredibly loud infant or wild animal with them but I can't fault the establishment. The waitress stumbled over the specials and a younger guy spilled the salad and was a little off that night.   I look forward to visiting again soon.

Outstanding wet hopped and well balanced beer and bratwurst that made my day.   My server patiently answered mty miriad of beer geek questions and brought samples of great offerings.  Very unassuming entrance opening into a well decorated brewpub. Nice!

My friends and I have been occasionally getting Katie's takeout as a part of our quarantine routine. Their pizzas and starters are yummy and great for sharing! If not for other factors, the actual food would have earned Katie's 5 stars.

Food: Caprese salad is my favorite starter from Katie's. It's very yummy, and their tomatoes are absolutely perfect! I also really liked fig pizza. The ingredients combine together so well.

Ambiance: I've never dined in, but their patio is basically in the parking lot of an urgent care, so I'd have to wait until the pandemic is over.

Service: I had one bad experience, where employees were really rude about bringing out the order. I had to wait for about 30 minutes for an order that was ready due to miscommunication on their part.

My new go-to spot in the area! Soulard Market is a bustling home of produce and local eats. You can buy some peaches while sipping on a Margarita (only $3!)or trying out some Cajun food. 

The market is open Wednesday through Saturday. While there are much fewer vendors on Wednesday (only around 9 I think), the prices seem lower. On a Saturday it's a full party! Added bonus is that they sell yummy local cheese for very competitive prices.

The most perfect bagel! I was looking for a good bagel in St Louis for a while, and Protzels is just that. It's a tiny store in Clayton that sells classic jewish food such as matzo ball soup. I'm definitely going to be dropping for some grocery items.

As for the actual bagel, it was just perfect. I got the poppyseed with lox, and it was very warm and fresh. I often struggle when bagels are too big, but this one proved to the ideal breakfast size that left me full for a few hours.

The meal started out ok.  The appetizers were pretty good - steak tar tar (the special) impressed, fennel soup was done well, and the goat cheese ravioli was good (though pretty standard if we're being honest, I mean cheesy pasta in butter sauce is always good, and I was hoping for more).  

Things went downhill with the entrees - my unbelievably dry cassoulet overshadowed any positive comments I could make about the rest of the dinner course.  Dessert was good.  Service was passable.

But it was the confusing encounter at the end of this meal that quickly and definitively turned my opinion of Le Cheri from "has some issues" to "NEVER AGAIN," because what happened was so unusual and off-putting that I'm still angry thinking about it a month later.

Quick timeline:

1. Made reservation in November, called to inquire re: bar/wine status, told to bring our own wine to the restaurant.
2. Brought our own wine to restaurant (duh).
3. Informed by the waiter (after the third bottle no less) that there is a per-bottle corkage fee.
4. We explained to the waiter what we'd been told, and he told us he'd try to look the other way on the fee for the last bottle.  It wasn't a big deal to us, we brought nice wine and we weren't upset about the fee, just the lack of communication (though I know plenty of people who would have had a major issue at this point, and with good reason). 
5. We finished dinner, and got the bill, which only had one corkage fee charged for 3 bottles - we figured our waiter took care of us, good guy.  Gave him the credit card.

That's when things got bizarre.  A few minutes later the owner shows up at the table with combative body language, rudely interrupting our conversation to begin a one-sided argument about the number of corkage fees on the bill.  Your guess is as good as mine why we were getting yelled at for the bill the waiter prepared, but whatever.  We explained to her that we were unaware of the fee, (not even trying to make an excuse, but genuinely trying to help her understand the nature of the mistake).

Well she didn't like that.  She proceeded to call me a liar, stating there was "no way" I didn't know about the fee (even though I learned soon after that they received the license less than a week before; maybe I was supposed to call everyday and check?)  Then, she told me in an accusatory way that I'd received a confirmation from Opentable the day before.  Before I could begin to contemplate the relevance of that comment, she asked directly "Well, did you receive the confirmation?" the insinuation being that Opentable must have informed me of the corkage fee  (The first thing I did when I got home was check the Opentable email, which of course made no mention of anything related to liquor status, why would they?)

Long story short, she made her scene, she adjusted the bill, and we left.  Everyone else seated within 20 feet of us was now painfully aware of the corkage policy, so mission accomplished I guess.

Just got your liquor license and now there's a corkage fee?  No problem.  Miscommunication about the bill that needs to be corrected?  Whatever, no problem.  Owner going from zero to CRAZY for no reason, and seemingly doing everything she can to make a scene?  No excuse.

I know I'm just another idiot writing an online review, "he says, she says" applies, I get it... but there was no justification for the attitude.  If it had been handled any number of different ways I wouldn't even be mentioning it right now.  In fact, even though there were some significant issues with some of the food, it was decent for the price point, and I probably would have given them another shot once they worked out the kinks.  But what she did is just bad business.  She's lost my future patronage as well that of several friends who value my opinion.  I hope it was worth the $20.

And since I've already burned the bridge I might as well say - I never really liked Bibou either.  I tried them early in their run, and was always confused by the high rating they receive.  I guess I always will be.

Elaia is yet another example of St. Louis' emergence as one of the country's most innovative (yet underappreciated) culinary hotspots.  Opened fairly recently in the Tower Grove neighborhood, Elaia and its sister bar Olio occupy an interesting property consisting of an old gas station attached to the former owner's house.

Olio is a bright and breezy bar occupying the service bay, with floor-to-ceiling windows stretched out in front of the compact bar.  Off to the right is a smallish dining area under a chandelier made of desk lamps, and flanked by the old garage door.  Olio offers many of the a la carte items from Elaia, but it a decidedly more casual space.  The bartenders are very knowledgeable, and while the cocktails trend towards the classics, there are a number of interesting innovations to be found.  Most impressive is their vermouth selection, with offerings that are sure to challenge your notions about the palatability of this misunderstood apertif.

Just up a staircase in the back of Olio stands Elaia, a very intimate dining room occupying the upper floor of the attached house.  The ambience is much more formal, but certainly not stuffy.  The cozy lighting plays well off the light gray walls, providing a warm and evenly-lit space that is inviting and flattering without being too dark.

The menu changes daily, and there are two options for dining: a four-course a la carte menu, and a 10-course chef's tasting menu.  Either way, you are sure to be treated to an innovative and downright delicious meal.  Highlights of recent visits include white anchovies over couscous, veal sweetbreads, and duck prepared three ways.  The presentation and plating is impeccable, and the drink pairings are thoughtful and well-matched, from a delicious absinthe concoction to complement the anchovies, to a glass of earthy wine to play off the duck.

The service is nothing short of phenomenal.  The staff are exceptionally knowledegable, having benefitted from trips through several wine regions across the United States and Europe.  The added depth of knowledge these experiences imparted was quite evident in the insight each member of the staff posessed about every glass that was being poured.  In addition, the chef made several appearances throughout the meal to explain the dishes and answer questions.  It is quite clear that the chef and owners see service as an essential ingredient in the meal, and it shows in the knowlegde and dedication of the staff.

For those who have complained that the portions are too small, I simply do not agree, and I think those diners who have complained are missing the point entirely.  The portions are generous, but not overdone.  Each is enough to allow you to thoroughly enjoy the flavor and texture of each dish without each dish outstaying its welcome.  The goal of a meal like this is not to stuff yourself until you cannot fit another morsel down your gullet.  If you want that type of meal, save yourself some money and go to Applebee's.

Is Elaia expensive?  Yup.  Is it worth it?  Absolutely, and then some.  Simply put, Elaia is one of the most interesting and innovative restaurants in the region, perfect for a special occasion.  Highly recommended.

This was my first visit to the Row Kitchen & Pub..I was actually going to the Soulshine Pizza but changed my mind. Wanted to try something new and different.  I checked it out on my Yelp app on my phone and they have great reviews. 

We actually opened the place and it filled up fast. 
We were seated in the bar area which is so open and airy. It has access to the outside patio area with garage doors that open the whole area up.  The bar is so big and long..fully stocked but Tony's beer was hot.  They must have not stocked the night before.

I ordered a Fresh made Root Beer. I forget the maker but it was so so so good and only $3.50. Tony ordered a Budweiser Light longneck for $3.50 but it was hot.   
I was also given a free appetizer of Fried Pickles given to me by the Yelp app. a great gift valued at only $8...not a big fan of fried pickles but it wasn't bad..

Tony ordered the Pulled Pork sandwich with slaw on the side.  With a side of bacon mac n' cheese..I tasted both and it was good. Especially the bacon mac n cheese. I ordered the Hot Chicken which was served on a pancake style cornbread drizzled with honey. They then topped with creamy homemade slaw, and placed the large piece of hot bread chicken on top of the slaw pile with a slice of pickle on top...the hotness of the chicken oozed down into the slaw and the sweet honey corn pancake..it was delicious..I also choose the brussel  sprouts with bacon for my side...OMG..i would do this meal again.

All in all the check was only less than $30 with taxes. Left her a 15% tip..she was very friendly and attentive. I would go here again and eat. I highly recommend. Let  me know what you think..

Food: 2 Stars
Service: 4 Stars

What the heck happened?!

Ben's original joint down in Maryland Heights, Big Baby Q, was a smash. Meats were juicy, seasoned perfectly, and trimmed thoughtfully. The sides were just as good and made great compliments to the main dishes. There was a lot of love that went into that food. You can only imagine how thrilled I was when The Midwestern finally opened their doors...

Conveniently located right in front of Busch Stadium and a few blocks from the Enterprise Center, The Midwestern touts a modern rustic vibe with plenty of seating for all of your family and friends. Their menu has been kept simple although if you ask for their alcohol menu, you'll find several pages of JUST whiskey (it's a heavy alcohol menu- don't break your wrist LOL).

The Roasted Beets caught my attention and it turned out to be the ultimate dish of the night. The tangy grapefruit and earthy beets were nestled in whipped ricotta, sprinkled with dill and drizzled with balsamic vinegar. This made for a perfect pallet cleanser and I could easily eat this every day/all week. My only complaint was that the beets didn't taste roasted at all. 

A handful of us ordered the brisket platter and what happened next was such a let down. All of our brisket were different in texture and taste. One was too dry, mine was nothing but fat, a couple had beautiful pink smoke rings, while another was gray as if it had been reheated. The bark lacked all flavor. What was in the rub? Who knew? You couldn't taste anything. In my opinion, good BBQ doesn't need sauce because there should be enough flavor in the meat by the way it's been prepared. But in this case, I needed to drown my plate in sauce except... Oh right, they only brought out 6 tiny sample cups for 8 of us to share. (Who does this?!)

Cornbread was pretty flavorless and dry.
Fries were limp, cold, and sad (you can see from the photo below).
Mac & Cheese was bland and cold.
We loved the potato salad (loved the addition of jalapenos to give them a kick) and the beans were solid.

I get that we arrived towards the end of dinner, but if the quality wasn't there, the food shouldn't have been served. Poor quality control, in my opinion. It's still early and there's plenty of time for improvement. I just hope that they bring back Ben's good ol' brisket...

Food: 3 Stars
Service: 4 Stars

My mother-in-law flew in from out of town and we had heard great things about Olive + Oak. Unfortunately, our experience was a bit underwhelming and I'm still scratching my head as I figure out where all the hype is coming from... 

We came in early and the ambiance was actually pleasant. Loved the cozy/warm feel and the decor. The space felt a bit tight, but that could also have been because we were seated right next to the kitchen. It didn't take long before the venue filled up and not only did the restaurant get loud, but the kitchen got busier. I actually felt a bit uncomfortable where we were sitting as there was a lot of foot traffic near us. It also made it difficult to hear each other from across the table.

On the other hand, service was on par. She was prompt and attentive and clearly knew the menu inside and out. 

The food was good, but nothing super memorable or outstanding.
- Oysters on the Half-Shell: Fresh and sweet
- Grilled Shrimp: The shrimp were smoky, tender, and juicy and served with a chipotle lime aioli. 
- Beef Tenderloin: Tender and juicy, but hardly memorable. Just seemed like your average steak.
- O+O Burger: Again, just your typical burger and fries.

Food: 4 Stars
Service: 4 Stars

Nestled within a generic strip mall along the hustle and bustle that is Manchester Rd., you'll find Nippon Tei. The menu is kept simple, allowing them to focus on what's important and what they're best at- sushi. 

You'll definitely want to start off with their Tuna Tartare. The Thai chili adds a nice kick while the shiso aioli will give it a slight creaminess.

I generally prefer that my sushi is kept simple and without all the extra sauces. The rolls we ordered were vibrant and colorful but I'm afraid the "lavish" usage of spicy mayo and eel sauce drowned out the natural fresh flavors of the fish. A little goes a long way, guys. If you need that much sauce for your sushi then a.) you're doing it wrong and/or b.) your sushi is terrible.

That being said, the nigiri were fresh with the flesh of the fish tasting buttery smooth and a little sweet.

Food: 4 Stars
Service: 4 Stars

West County has seriously been under-serviced compared to other areas of St. Louis, so you can imagine how my heart fluttered when I found out that Qui Tran was opening up a ramen shop in Creve Coeur. You can also try to imagine how excited I was to hear that they were opening a day early... I texted my husband and told him to scrap any plans we had tonight, we were gonna stuff our faces with RAMEN, baby!!!

With all the anticipation surrounding Nudo and knowing how well Mai Lee has done over the last 3 decades, I had pretty high expectations despite the fact that I had been let down by a few other ramen restaurants in STL. The broth is vital and without a good base, your supporting/complimenting ingredients don't stand a chance. Nudo House not only delivered an amazing mouthwatering broth, but they also chose the right noodles to pair it with.

But before I delve deeper into their ramen, let me talk about the physical restaurant... Qui Tran couldn't have picked a better location. At the heart of Creve Coeur you have several businesses with employees seeking  places to dine during lunch and to take their customers to. The area has been sadly under-serviced which forces businesses and residents to travel a bit to find a nice local restaurant. There's seriously less than 5 restaurants I would dine at on a regular basis within a 5 mile radius from 270 and Olive... There's a definite need here and Qui Tran delivered. THANK YOU.

The restaurant is open and airy with several smaller tables that line the wall and a few long tables that run along the center of the restaurant. It's kind of like communal dining where people grab a spot to sit and eat... you might be sitting next someone you don't know, but who cares? You're eating some of the best ramen in STL! :D

Now on to the FOOOOOD:
- Spring Rolls: for $2 a pop, it's not worth it. Don't get me wrong, they taste great but they're small and not as filled as I would have liked them to be for that price. Take my advice and make them at home. 

- Kimchi: We only ordered this because I'm Korean and I have to critique everyone's kimchi. I can't tell if they added fish sauce or some other brine, but it wasn't really my cup of tea. Since the ramen they were serving were full bodied, I would have preferred a clean and crisp "Seoul" recipe rather than adding another layer flavor in this side dish. I can see how some may feel this recipe would compliment the ramen, but it just didn't do it for me. If you need extra spice and texture with your noodles, go ahead and add this to your order. It's not terrible, just didn't fit my preference.

- Hebrew Hammer (chicken ramen): Qui Tran walked over with our trays and the moment he set them on the table, I got a healthy waft of the savory broth. I immediately started salivating and took a sip of the broth. Rich. Hearty. Savory. Bold. Nudo House did NOT disappoint. Although the presentation was simple with very little toppings (more on that in a bit), so many complex layers came through with that first sip. I was hesitant to let my husband try... I didn't want to share. Ha! I really appreciated the fact that Nudo House stuck to basics when it came to toppings: Marinated soft boiled egg, bok choy, tonkatsu chicken, menma. Each topping added a layer of flavor to the dish and left you licking your lips for more. Noodles were al dente and left a little chewy bit still firm to the bite. And don't let the bowl deceive you... It looks small but there's a hearty meal hidden in that broth!

- O' Miso Spicy (miso pork ramen): My husband said it was the right amount of heat. (I could have added a bit more to it!) That being said, the heat hits you in the back of your throat and leaves you feeling nice and warm. It's kind of comforting. Again, the broth is rich and hearty and goes down smooth. 

Can't wait to see how Nudo House grows and hope that other restaurants take note and come to West County. Thanks for a great experience, I'll be back soon to try that bahn mi pho dip!

Food: 2 Stars
Service: 4 Stars

After hearing about Beast Craft over in Belleville, IL., a bunch of us were elated to hear that they would be opening up shop in The Grove. What's really neat is the concept of having 3 spaces in 1: a restaurant, a butcher shop (The Butchery), and a chef's table/R&D space (The Skullery). 

The facility itself is modern and clean with ample space to host family or company sponsored lunches/dinners. Large monitors at the counter showcase their menu which include their well known Wagyu brisket and pork steak.

We both ordered the Lunch Combo which comprised of their Double R Brisket and 2 sides (I opted for fresh fries and potato salad- mistakenly doubled down on starch). Let me preface by saying that it's really hard to do brisket really, really well. It's even more difficult to mass produce and find a way to keep the BBQ without the quality taking some sort of dip. Unfortunately, I feel that's exactly what happened with the brisket we were served. You can tell in the photo that our meats were reheated as the color looks a little gray and extremely dry. Despite them being leaner cuts, I still didn't expect that I would need to use steak knives to cut a part the meat. I was so wrong. There also wasn't much of a bark or flavor which resulted in us reaching over for their sauce bottles. I'm a firm believer that great BBQ shouldn't require the use of sauce as it should merely compliment the meat. 

I enjoyed their creamy dill potato salad and could only stomach about a quarter of the fries as they were heavily saturated in oil and had gone limp. 
My husband ordered the red slaw and baked beans as his sides. For those who like vinegary slaws, they'll love the acidity and crunch in this side. 
My husband loved the beans but I wasn't a fan. For one, they were overcooked and mushy. Secondly, I felt like I had consumed all the smoke from a campfire. A little goes a long way, guys!

This place is still new and working things out. Will stop by another time and maybe check out their butcher shop as well.

*edit* After a brief chat with Dave, he believes "the gray color and surface dryness is from a heat lamp. Definitely should be tender, moist, and dark on the bark."

Food: 4 Stars
Service: 4 Stars

Layla's second location in Webster Groves is tucked away in the back corner of a building. Be aware as our GPS had us parking on the opposite of the building and it wasn't visible to us where exactly Layla was. Other than being slightly hidden, the restaurant itself is spacious with plenty of seating for large groups and posters that make for great conversations (when was the last time you saw Back to the Future?). Layla has such a warm and inviting space and it kicked off what would be a pleasant experience.

Our group of 6 ordered a little of everything. Some of our favorites:
- Spin Salad: Baby spinach, creamy feta and sweet and salty glazed walnuts tossed in a tangy balsamic vinaigrette and topped with a handful of sweet apples. I loved the crisp and crunchy textures.
- Spicy Smoked Brisket Shawarma on Traditional Lebanese Pita: I was skeptical with how spicy the sauce would be, but ended up being pretty impressed. The heat builds but doesn't overpower the flavor of the roasted red peppers. I also wasn't dying or losing my taste buds due to the heat. The shawarma itself was packed with tender brisket and fresh lettuce and tomato. I had a hard time finishing the second half, but I somehow managed.
-Fries: Perfectly fried to a golden crisp and fluffy on the inside, these are probably some of the best fries I've had in awhile. Paired with their tzatziki sauce, I'm a happy camper.

Food: 4 Stars
Service: 5 Stars

Joo Joo is conveniently located along Olive right at the intersection of Fee Fee Rd. It sits in the corner/nook of the strip mall (closer to Happy China) and is pretty hard to miss. They double as a karaoke bar as well, so after stuffing your face with all the glorious Korean food you can hop into one of their rooms and practice becoming the next Beyonce or BTS.

Despite the tightly packed tables, the dining floor is actually pretty spacious and airy. We came during lunch and although it got busy, we didn't feel like the tables next to us were hovering over our table and we definitely couldn't hear other conversations. 

For us, service has always been prompt and super courteous. Our drinks are always brought to us right away and I love the attention they provide when I bring new diners who aren't familiar with Korean cuisine. 

My husband loves the variety of banchan (side dishes) they provide (a courtesy with some of the items you order from their menu), especially when there is more than 1 type of kimchi. They're never over seasoned or salty and there's always enough to go around.

A few of our favorite entrees:
- Yukgaejang: This is a hearty and quite comforting spicy beef soup that will warm you from head to toe. The fiery and bold soup is perfect for a chilly or rainy day or if you're trying to recover from a hang over. This is generally my go-to meal as it satisfies my craving for something spicy.
- Kalbi: My husband loves the house-made marinade that caramelizes a little when the meat is cooked in high heat. These Korean short ribs are the perfect combination of sweet and savory which always has us wanting more.
-Dol Sot Bibim Bap: You could serve me anything in a piping hot stone bowl and I'd love it... I love the way the rice continues to brown at the bottom of the bowl. The natural sugars from the rice make it toasty and a tad sweet- it's my favorite part! Love the variety of vegetables and how hearty and relatively healthy this dish is.

Food: 4 Stars
Service: 4 Stars

If you're looking for authentic Korean food, Seoul Garden is my recommendation. They finally opened their 2nd location replacing their sister restaurant, Kimcheese, on Olive Blvd., east of 270. Family owned and operated, you can tell a lot of love goes into every dish. 

We started off with the kimchi pancake as an appetizer. These larger-than-your-head pancakes Have a nice crunchy exterior and are filled with kimchi and onions and are good on their own as a light meal. 

Both the bean sprout soup and short rib soup had hearty broths that warmed our bellies and complimented our dishes. 

Kalbi was marinated beautifully and my stone bowl bibim bap had a generous amount of veggies and meat.

Be sure to stop by for a delicious meal and definitely check out their all you can eat menu! :

Food: 3 Stars
Service: 4 Stars

Cobalt Smoke & Sea is conveniently located on Olive, about 1 mile west of 270. From the exterior, the patio is clean and spacious and they have added 2 large faux trees adorned with blue lights for ambient lighting in the evening. The interior is more spacious than I previously remembered and has been decked out with what I'd call a modern rustic/western vibe. They definitely created a warm and inviting environment as my husband and I felt cozy at our table.

Our server was bright and cheery- I love when you can tell that the staff love where they are and what they do. It makes the dining experience that much better. :]

Their menu consists of smoked meats with inspiration from around the world. Plating was impressive and beautiful with lots of color. For me, the flavors fell flat a little bit.

- Ginger Panko Shrimp: Their large shrimp were succulent with a crispy battered shell. I wasn't a fan of the finely ground panko as it reminded me too much of what you would find in the freezer section at your local grocery store. I would have much preferred the coarse panko crumbs. The plum sauce was also muted in flavor and tasted like a standard sauce from a jar.

-Burnt Ends: Loved the idea of bringing together burnt ends with soba noodles and baby bok choy. Unfortunately, I was disappointed with how fatty the burnt ends were (not enough of the fat had rendered off) and the Yakiniku sauce was salty. 

-Smoked Duck Ragu: My husband enjoyed the dish and mentioned that the duck was tender and smoked beautifully.

Food: 4 Stars
Service: 4 Stars

[UPDATE] After giving WuDon a few weeks to work out their kinks, my husband and I decided to come back. (We were also really hungry and happened to be next door shopping at the Asian grocery store.) 

We were seated immediately and our orders were placed. I noticed that they had made some significant changes to their menu including price adjustments and rules to their All You Can Eat option. I do feel they are being a bit stingy with their meat choices and should either eliminate the boneless short rib option from the AYCE and add it as a regular meat item instead. 

It didn't take long for our drinks (hot tea and beer- they finally have their liquor license!) and banchan (side dishes) to arrive. Not too long after, our appetizer and main dishes showed up. 

Spicy Tteokbokki: Rice cakes were layered with glass noodles, fish cakes, and a large boiled egg and garnished with scallions, a drizzle of sesame oil and sesame seeds. Not quite as spicy as I would have liked, but it did enough to curb my craving for the evening.

Dol Sot Bibim Bap: This is one of my favorite Korean dishes. It's a hot stone bowl topped with rice and several marinated, sauteed, or stir fried veggies. You have the option of picking out a protein for an additional charge. I went with kalbi and man, was it DELICIOUS! The addition of kalbi gave the dish a hint of savory and sweetness in every bite. If you want to try something other than Korean BBQ, you can never go wrong with this dish.

Saeng Galbi: This cut of meat was beautifully marbled and juicy after being cooked on open flames. The meat melted in our mouth and was best in a lettuce wrap.

Banchan: WuDon made some improvements with their side dishes by including a couple of other meat/fish items rather than serving all vegetable items. They were all seasoned well and nothing came off too strong, salty, or bland. I think I prefer their side dishes to any other Korean restaurant in town. [2 thumbs up!]

My only real gripe about this place is that it's not very well ventilated. You will walk out smelling like BBQ and will have to shower/take a bath and throw everything you were wearing into the wash/take it to the cleaners. It's annoying and I can say that it definitely plays a part in whether we decide to dine there. (i.e. We have plans later that night but don't want to show up smelling like a restaurant.)

After learning that Bareburger does not recognize or understand that all people deserve fair wages on their Instagram, I am choosing to no longer support this business (as I have done in the past. My avi here is at Bareburger.) I hope that bareburger will come to understand that their workers are their backbone. Their prices are already higher than I like, but as they said on their IG responses, they aren't serving prime rib. Their prices should reflect how well they pay their workers. Many restaurant workers struggle to make ends meet, and businesses like this that charge high for food should be putting their appreciation back into their workers. If they don't then workers have the right to seek higher income that supports their survival. My partner is a restaurant worker and his unemployment helped us keep up with our rent. Higher wages supports more workers ability to live and every person should believe in that.

We went there on a Sunday evening.  The place was somewhat empty.  I was hoping to get a good meal from some of the positive reviews on here.   I have to side with the reviewers that rated this on the negative side.  The food is pretty bad compare to other places.  Yes their selection (shabu shabu, hot pot, pho, etc) is nice but the food quality is mediocre.  The rice on the sushi rolls lack taste (vinegar or sugar).  The fish have a bland color to them.  They had mussels and oysters available but the mussels were spoiled and oysters tasted bad as well, it looked like the oysters were opened in the early morning and left to dry.   Heller Seafood Markets has better oysters.  

As we were finished with the tasteless dinner, we thought that they can't mess up dessert.  Well they can.  Ice cream station didn't have sprinkles for my kids.  Instead they have corn flakes???  The cake and brownies looks they something they purchase from Costco next door and cut into minute pieces.  No joke, the cakes were the size of a pinky finger.   Hard to imagine this place staying in business any longer if they don't get their act together.  Save your money and go somewhere else.   Minado is a but further but worth the travel.

Wow. That's all I can say.  My family including our twin 2 year olds and a four year old came here after driving over from Sacramento.  Hungry and ready for a good meal.  We were given the absolutely WORST reception from some lady I think is the owner.  It got to a  point that right after our food arrived we were asked to leave.  Not that our kids were acting out, screaming or making a mess.  ( I know that this is in the eye of the beholder). 

The attitude was ONLY FROM THE OWNER. the wait staff were all kind and very embarrassed for the scene that this person made.  

If you don't want kids in your restaurant, then post that, or don't have child booster seats available.  

Again the waitstaff were all professional and kind.   


I have NEVER been treated like this in my life by a person who seemingly is in a service business.   

I hope that the waitstaff gets wise to their boss and how she directly affects their pay by her terrible and Titus's towards her patrons.  

I would avoid this restaurant at all cost.

My first experience here and I would never return. I'm
Accustomed to coming to a rooftop restaurant where you pay for the service and ambience and not the food but that's not the case here. I paid for location. The service here is terrible. I made a reservation to sit in a corner by a bush and to wait for almost 30 minutes just to be offered a glass of water. The food and service were a zero for me.

This place is horrible with customer service!  It has always been even before it was the casino the casino just made it worse.  I was there for an event which provided valet parking.  When we were ready to leave no one was at the stand.  We waited for about 5 minutes then went to the front desk for help.  They called someone up to help us.  No one showed!  Now here is the kicker, there had to be at least 4 people who worked for the hotel that walked by us without asking (even one of the investors) and there were at least 2 other couples now waiting.  Then we had to be taken in a van to the Casino where there we were dropped off and was looking for the valet desk still no help!  They have to get their act together.  I will do everything to never go back again!

Let's not even talk about what it took for us to find our coat since they moved coat check without telling anyone.

Wish I could make the star even lower!

This restaurant has average burgers at best.    The service would maybe rate 2 stars.    With the great positive publicity they receive they definitely should rate no higher than one or two stars.   Stay away and save yourself some heartburn and heartache.

This is one of the highly over rated Tucson local restaurants.  After moving into their new swanky spot Care Poca Cosa never quite recovered the ambiance, quality of food, and service.
We arrived for dinner reservations at 7:30 on a Friday night.  The restaurant was quite busy so we decided to wait at the bar and have a drink while our table.was being prepared; 20 minutes later we are still waiting for the craft of red sangria that was ordered. Our table was ready but I was told that the tab was not transferrable so while the group sat down I had to wait for another 15 minutes just to pay $49 for a craft of sangria which was actually $15 more than the menu stated.... another 5 minutes to correct the price and then I was finally able to join the group.
We were sat on more of a private dinning room with a few other tables; the art on the walls was beautiful and the room was very nicely decorated however the ac was not working at all.  Looking around the room you could see everyone was uncomfortably warm including our server who was sweating profusely.   We asked the server if the temperature could be adjusted and he said he'd check. Meanwhile chips and salsa were flowing, thankfully since we were all starving.  The waiter finally presented the chalkboard menu which really didn't tell us much as he had to take 5 minutes to explain to us the five menu options.  We opted for the chefs tasting. 
Meanwhile the room is becoming unbearably hot and we are growing tired.  Now water refills and the sangria tastes more like a spritzer than anything else.  Right now the only thing that is worthwhile was the salsa. 
The owner stopped by the table.and asked how everything was,we informed her about how uncomfortable the temperature was and she said she would get right on it.... all I can say is that when we walked outside after dinner the 80 degree evening was cooling.
the food came out and I was shocked at all the foliage on the plate, it was beyond artsy but rather messy and just too much. I had to actually move lettuce around to find my food.  The salad dressing never came to the table and the rice and beans for the whole table of 9 to share came out in one cup of each.  There was a whole pineapple top in my plate with the spikes covered in a Chile powder.  I'm sure if the effort put into decorating the unedible parts of my dish were out into the actual food there is no doubt it would have been delicious.  
All in all the food was mediocre at best, the room was a sauna,  the service was horrible at the bar and good at the table, and the prices were absolutely outrageous for what you got.

I told him not to, but my good buddy and fellow Yelper Tom E (https://www.yelp.com/user_details?userid=g8j2ci2FcvmocszcO6ypNw) drove from the suburbs of Atlanta to my place in the city, during rush hour, to deliver a birthday gift that included one Pat's Original Philly Cheeesesteak. The cheesesteak had been flown in that same morning. Thank you, Tom.

For those who don't know, Pat's and Geno's are the most popular places to get a cheesesteak sandwich in Philadelphia. They are old and they are competitors. "Pat's King of Steaks" is the "inventor and originator of the cheesesteak sandwich." They've been in business since 1930. During one of my visits to Philadelphia, friends and locals steered me away from Pat's and Geno's, both of which are popular with tourists. Instead, I went to Jim's Steaks South Street: https://www.yelp.com/biz/jims-south-st-philadelphia.

It would not be fair to make a comparison of my experiences with Pat's and Jim's since I had to reheat Pat's cheesesteak at home while I had Jim's cheesesteaks fresh at the restaurant.

You can purchase Pat's cheesesteaks by mail-order through Goldbelly: https://www.goldbelly.com/pats-king-of-steaks. The cheesesteaks were shipped frozen with dry ice packs and reheating instructions. The cheesesteaks were already assembled and wrapped in Pat's signature logo'd white paper wrappers. The Cheez Whiz was packed in separate containers. At the time of writing this review, Goldbelly offered Pat's Original Philly Cheesesteaks in sets of four ($79 or $19.75 per sandwich), eight ($129 or $16.13 per sandwich), and 12 ($169 or $14.08 per sandwich). Shipping was included in the quoted prices.

Reheating was quick and easy. Instructions were to bake at 300 degrees for 10-14 minutes until the bread was lightly-crisped and the meat heated through. The Cheez Whiz could be reheated in the microwave or in a saucepan. I reheated the sandwich in my old toaster oven so it took a little longer than 14 minutes. I used the microwave to melt the Cheez Whiz.

I was impressed with how the sandwich turned out. It looked just like the cheesesteaks I saw of Pat's online. I had the "Wit" onions and Whiz version, but you can get "Wit-Out" onions and change the cheese to Provolone or American if you want. I think I may have baked the sandwich a little too long because the outside of the hoagie roll started to crack and it was extra crispy. That was okay, though, because the inside was warm, soft, and delectably chewy. The bread was good. There were plenty of tender morsels of quality ribeye, but what brought everything together was the melted Cheez Whiz. Mmm... That melted cheese coated the steak and eventually found its way to the bottom of the sandwich, soaking into the bread. This made each bite rich, flavorful, and really satisfying.

There aren't many ingredients - bread, meat, onion, cheese. Pat's found the right combination of quality, taste, and texture. If you're considering purchasing some of Pat's cheesesteaks via mail order, let this review be a vote of confidence. At the time of writing this, you can only get the Original Philly Cheesesteak via Goldbelly. The Mushroom Steak, Pepper Steak, Mushroom Pepper Steak, Pizza Steak, Fish Cake, Hot Dog, and Fries are not available online.

Enjoy.

We walked over to Tennessee Brew Works, one of Nashville's popular craft breweries, after hitting up Jack White's Third Man Records shop nearby. Both businesses are located in Pie Town, a neighborhood on the southern edge of downtown Nashville. There's not a whole lot of stuff in this part of town. These are definitely two of the highlights.

Tennessee Brew Works opened on August 18, 2013. It's popular. This place has won numerous awards and earned plenty of recognition including the best brewery in Tennessee according to Yelp. These folks are all about being local, green, and sustainable. The taproom is two stories with views of the brewery from both floors. There's a patio with both covered and uncovered spaces (mostly uncovered) as well as a small, string-lit rooftop patio. As this is a brewery, the property has an industrial, warehouse feel to it, much like the other businesses in Pie Town. It's clean and modernized. The first floor of the brewery features a small stage for live music (a band was setting up on our way out) and the room upstairs, which is much more spacious, has TVs playing sports and nice overhead views of the brewery floor below.

Brewery tours take place every Saturday at 3pm, 4pm, and 5pm. It costs $10 plus tax and a fee per person. Tickets for the tour can be purchased online.
