Along with high-quality craft beer, the brewery also serves food. Their limited menu includes apps/snacks like Baja fish tacos, Springer Mountain chicken wings, salads, burgers, and sandwiches (including a Nashville Hot Chicken Sandwich). Food prices range from $8 to $18 per plate.

We grabbed a few beers and hung out inside the taproom downstairs. Downstairs, they use barrels (some with tabletops) for tables with bar stools. We showed up around 2pm on a Saturday and the place was busy. It wasn't slammed or jam-packed, but most of the tables upstairs and downstairs were taken. Our group of six was lucky to find a table in a corner next to some brewery windows. The atmosphere was very relaxed and laid back. The staff was cool and friendly. We all enjoyed our time here.

I don't think Tennessee Brew Works has dedicated parking. We parked for free on the street (Middleton Street because we also went to Third Man Records). This isn't the nicest neighborhood so I wouldn't leave any valuables in your car.

tl;dr - Best Chicken Finger Fast-Food Restaurant. No bones about it (literally).

You see, Raising Cane's does not serve drumsticks, thighs, wings, or chicken "fingers"... Just chicken fingers made from succulent chicken tenderloins aka a fancier name for breasts. After all, chickens don't have fingers... unless it's that antibiotic-laden chicken from that colonel guy. 

Anyways, not much to really say other than that Raising Cane's has really good fried chicken. It's a shame that none have opened up in Northern California... yet. But with chicken this good, it's definitely just a matter of time. I guess for now, I will have to trek on over to Reno to get quality fried chicken without the bigotry like that place that closes on Sundays and where the CEO hates gays.                        

In regards to the price, Raising Cane's flagship combo is the "Box Combo", which consists of four generously proportioned chicken fingers, French fries, a slice of toast, a side of coleslaw, a side of sauce, and a drink that now costs around $8. Hardly a wallet buster compared to some of the competition. 

So, the chicken is described as 100% premium and the chicken is never frozen. For a fast-food restaurant this is a rarity. It's one thing to say your chicken is 100% chicken, but to also proclaim that your chicken is never frozen is a testament to the freshness and quality of the food being served. The breading was tasty and had spices infused with seasoning that yelped of Southern flavoring.

As for the coleslaw, fries, and Texas toast, they were okay, but kind of got in the way of my fingers getting to the chicken fingers. Also, I do like the cane sauce that is kind of like a thousand island base sauce with Cajun spices. However, I make the sauce better by asking for 2 packets of "The Original Louisiana Hot Sauce" and mixing it up. Instant oral Cajun party.   

In regards to the drinks, Raising Cane's has your standard Coca-Cola fountain drinks. But the real highlight is their sweet tea, which is really sweeeeeeeeeeeeet. Try this!

Tasty Chicken Fingers + Dog Lovers + No Bigotry = Winning... ahem Reno-ing!

* The name of Raising Cane is an ode to the founder's dog, Raising Cane, a yellow lab. They are also doing a Winter fundraiser right now where if you buy a stuffed animal dog or puppy calendar, the proceeds go to a local pet organization. 

* The first Raising Cane's was founded in Baton Rouge, Lousiana, where they are still headquartered. 

* This location is located next to Archie's Burgers. I guess people were parking in their lot so they got all angry and went full-on IRL Troll by hiring a security guard that will tow your car. There is a parking lot in the rear of this location that is accessed via North Sierra Street. And, if parking is an issue, go to the Raising Cane over on South Virginia or in Sparks.

The family often stays at the nearby and very dog-friendly Renaissance Reno Downtown when in town. As I took the furchild for a morning walk to grab some light roast coffee at See See Motor Coffee, I couldn't help but notice the recently opened Pine State Biscuits along Pine Street because there was a line out the door in 40 degree weather at 7:30 AM. What's crazy is that this building used to be a run-down motel and the space of the restaurant was under-building parking. 

Additionally, this fool (points at self) initially thought Pine State Biscuits said Pine Street Biscuits because it faces Pine Street. Anyways, Pine State Biscuits on Pine Street... the perfect fit. 

The Reno location of Pine State Biscuits is the first location outside of the Beaver State aka Oregon. Actually, let me be more specific. It's the first location outside of Portland! This is more proof that the Biggest Little City in the World is an up-and-coming city and foodie destination. ReNO is becoming more and more a ReYES! 

The wife and I ended up ordering the Reggie Deluxe and the Hash Ups. The Reggie Deluxe is this buttery biscuit sandwich served with a ginormous piece of southern-style fried chicken, bacon, cheese, and an egg. It also comes with a side of gravy and we ended up getting a mix of sausage and mushroom gravy. The Reggie Deluxe really lives up to its hype. 

Also, the Hash Ups were really tasty. It's a take on hash browns except the shredded potatoes are topped with grilled onions, mushrooms, and melted cheese. I think I'm going to make this at home now!

We're not really breakfast people, but Pine State Biscuits will always be our exception. The next time ReGo to ReYes - and there will definitely be a next time - we're going to try the Shrimp-N-Grits and pop tarts with a side of Bloody Mary!

* The address is officially 200 South Center Street, but the restaurant has frontage along Pine Street. It's located on the other side of the Patagonia Outlet store which happens to be one block to the north on State Street. Whoa... just had another epiphany... Pine Street... State Street... Pine State! 

* The restaurant is an order first and then sit down restaurant. Don't be a burnt biscuit and not follow the rules. Also, they are a breakfast place so they are only open from 7 AM to 3 PM. BTW, I did mention the dog earlier... Unfortunately the restaurant is not dog-friendly. 

* So I had to look into why a restaurant from the Beaver State was named Pine State. Well, Pine State Biscuits has nothing to do with the official Pine State, Maine. In turns out that the three founders are all from North Carolina and two of them met each other while working in a wine bar in a converted ice cream building in Raleigh that was known as the... wait for it... Pine State Creamery.

I'll agree with the reviews before me, this place is a real gem with great potential.  I've eaten here a few times as well:

Sweet & Spice Corn Fritter Mash:  The first dog i tried here.  Agreed that its got a real nice spice to it and the fritters are very tasty.

Italian:  Meh, the roll/bread they serve it on is WAY too big.  Wouldn't have this again.

Jersey Shore Breakfast:  One of my faves, especially with a little Sriracha on top.  They will put it on for you if you ask. 

Cool Burger:  Light and refreshing. Well, as light as a burger can be.

Slider of the Week - Mac the Slider....deep-fried bacon-wrapped Angus burger, mac & cheese, spicy sriracha sauce, pickles.    AMAZING!!

I agree with Jason C about the fries, but they are still damn good.   I will be eating at this place for a long time to come......assuming they stay open longer than Fat Jacks BBQ did in that same location.

I want to LOVE this place. I love the atmosphere - the comfy chairs, the cozy fireplace, the secluded rooms in the back and the outdoor seating for summertime enjoyment. This would be my instant place to go to for hanging out and chatting with a friend. BUT ... they have absolutely nothing I can eat as a person with a gluten allergy. Nothing. So I go on occasion and have a coffee or a wine (side note, this is not a place for good wine...they basically have a red or a white), sit by the fire and knit for some no-child-mama-needs-to-decompress-free-time. But I so wish I could stay for hours ... and that requires food.

From my gluten-free perspective this place is just A-OK. If they would just have one item I could eat I'd bump it up a star or two. Whine. Whine. Piss and moan.

I'm perplexed how this menu is so expensive for what you get and lacking the quality to justify the pricing. 

Let's start with valet. It's $3. Really? Have you seen a valet that charges these days? Once the attendant got off his cell phone, the guy backed up my husband's luxury vehicle on the curb and barely missed the rim. 

Once we entered, you see a grand staircase, the hostess stand, and a teeny tiny bar with literally like 6 seats and 2- yes 2- hightops. The main dining room looked dark and sleek. The hostess informed us since we did not have reservations it would be nearly 2 hrs. She said we could eat at one of the 2 hightops or go upstairs to the "concessions." We opted for the hightop. 

The menu was a little all over the place. Pierogis, octopus or $12 bread on the "firsts." We started with a licorice salad, supposedly a specialty of the chef. Our server said it was "weird, but good." It came with about 5 small bibb lettuce leaves with dressing drizzled on with a thin and very peppery wafer. To sum up the licorice peppermint dressing- it tasted like Burt's Bees chapstick. No other way to describe it. It was weird alright, and just plain awful. 

Moving on to entrees. We decided to share the French Onion Frites, which is a ribeye basically soaked in French Onion soup and topped with gruyere and a side of fries. We had heard about this dish, as well. The meat was so fatty, the cheese on top was just ridiculous. It's a dish that would be more suited at a Western Sizzlin. The fries. I mean how do you F up fries? Beyond words salty. I ate two, and the two I did eat, I gave a good wipe down and they were still  the saltiest things I've had in a long time. I told the server who was nice, but definitely screamed new. I said just to pass the info on, no need for new fries. He also said the chef suggests medium well on steaks. Having been a server, I know medium rare is the suggested temp. He said "oh yeah, my bad, medium rare." Gees. 

I could go to Kayne Prime and spend less on an amazing cut of meat. Where did these prices come from? They are not in line with the Nashville market. Heck, they're double NYC prices, and the food doesn't live up. Not even close. For sharing what little food we did have for $86+ tip was like throwing money away. We hit up Sweet Cece's aftewards since my husband was still hungry. 

Overall- overpriced, lacking quality to justify $ and a menu that needs revamping already.

Out the dozen or so restaurants I have eaten in Chinatown, this is one of the restaurants I have become a regular at. The food is excellent and the interior is nicer and more comfortable than most restaurants in Chinatown (though you still have Tru TV on during dinner). 

Note: check in on yelp for the first time, you get an appetizer order of dumplings which is pretty good.

The food is solid. There is nothing that I have had here that has disappointed.

Recommendations

Soups: a nice start and complement to any meal. The west lake beef soup and the chicken corn soup are good.

Apps:
Noodle with minced pork sauce - Stir it up, it is excellent.

Hot dumplings - a good dish, but again stir the sauce comes in. The flavorful part settles at the bottom.

Entrees:

Shredded beef long hot pepper - a very hot and spicy dish with fresh green peppers

Dry Saute Shredded Beef with celery - moderately spicy dish with the flavor of dried red peppers

Fish Fillet in Hot Spicy Sauce - white fish over a bed of napa cabbage in a mild-moderately hot sauce.

The vegetables dishes are reliable. Try the black mushroom Bok Choy and spicy eggplant dishes, the are on par with any good Chinese restaurant.

STAY AWAY FROM THE SPA!!!

I worked an event at this casino a few years back, and my experience was very poor. I had an okay time at the casino itself, and the food was okay. I probably would have walked away from this with a forgettable experience, except that my last day of my stay I decided to use the spa and facilities.

While staying here, I received a gift card to use anywhere on premises. Why not use this opportunity to treat myself to a nice massage and visit the sauna! So I made my appointment. Upon checking in at the spa front desk, you are required to put down a credit card that will not be charged until after services are rendered and the bill is settled. I did so letting the kid at the front desk know that I would be using a gift card once I was done. 

I had a nice massage and went into the sauna. Because my flight was not for another few hours, and I had plenty of time to kill, I was probably in there for about 2 hours or so. Apparently that was too long for them to wait, and they did NOT bother to make a round to see if I was still inside. I came out to find that my card was charged! 

No big deal, I thought. I'll just have them cancel the payment and I'll ring it up on the gift card instead. I received the voided receipt for the card and a receipt for the services. It was not until after I was already on my way to the airport that I realized the mistake made. Apparently, after voiding the first transaction on my card, the person at the front desk applied all charges to my card AGAIN. Not only that, but he took my gift card as well. So it was as though I was being charged double for the services rendered.

I called the spa to dispute, and got nothing but an unprofessional game of avoiding my calls and ignoring my messages on their machine. When I disputed through my credit card company, the credit card company required I provide a receipt to prove my case. But the receipt did not prove anything because of the spa's mistake of charging my credit card instead of the gift card!!!

It has been a few years since this incident, and I still have the sour taste in my mouth. I have told EVERYONE I know to avoid this unprofessional business, and I will continue to write poor reviews. I am absolutely disgusted that this is how customers are treated.

Sometimes,  when a boxer gets knocked down,  they are better off if they stay down,  though often they choose not to. 

In a previous life, this place was Marlin Darlin, a Baystar group offering that died a slow death, which was justified. 

This iteration,  Seaweed, is just opening this week. I had dinner with my wife (dined is too strong of a word), and we left unimpressed. 

Hopefully,  most of the issues can be attributed to initial shakedown problems,  but I fear not. 

Starting with the entry, there is a small outdoor bar. Nice feature,  but the bartender was loud and cackling like an adolescent.

Inside, there were more than modest redecorations. The sushi bar is across from the entry. There were a large nunber of booths in various sizes. The bar is long, there are several large flat screens, great for the bar, but too large and bright, such that they intruded into the dining room. 

The dining room is  pleasant,  but there is little sound muffling. 

The menu is a la carte. There are many eclectic choices in both seafood and meat. We thought that was little to appeal to someone who wants basic food. 

We had an 8 oz filet and a 16 oz NY strip. Side offerings were fries or mashed potatoes,  and a credible stringed zucchini. 

I am avoiding greasy foods, so I asked if I could substitute some ramen noodles.  Now, both items were listed as side dishes, but they declined to accommodate us saying that they don't substitute.

Not a winning strategy for a new restaurant!

Our waitress was a bit brusque,  not welcoming or warm or accommodating initially,  though she picked up a bit during the meal.

I asked for steak sauce,  it was not A1-like, but some runny, liquidy Ponzu or soy type liquid that did not enhance anything. 

While we were awaiting our dinner,  there was nary a roll or a breadstick. 

The manager came by to see how things were going,  and I told him "Not well"  and elaborated as above. He offered to remake my wife's steak,  which had the opportunity to bathe in the steak sauce. 

We declined as I do not like to be punitive. 

If a place is a la carte and pricey, the food quality has to justify that. This simply did not.

Some people may like this place, though unless you're drinking I can't imagine why. 

Overall Seaweed is a typical offering for the chain. Average food, overpriced, and with service measurably below adequate.

If you want eclectic seafood,  go next door to Bonefish, if you want good American cuisine, go around the corner to E & E, both of which are better food values. 

As I sit here writing this, my stomach is upset by the greasy fries that were not substituted. 

I predict that Seaweed will be going out with the tide by the time 2019 checks in.

Cheese steaks are good and creative. Just pricey for average cheapo take out. On other hand if you compare it to regular plain cheese steak prices at the likes of Steve's, Pat's, etc, it's pretty darn good! Their seitan is pretty neat too (and I'm a big meat lover so that's good praise!). I miss them at the Dollar Strolls, used to be one of my favorite stops.

I didn't see what the big deal was about this place. I came here after a theater production, with the cast, and was not all that impressed. 

It's very difficult to find a place to stand that allows you to avoid being bumped into by the bustling waiters. The bartender was pretty gruff. The options on tap weren't great either but I tried a hibiscus-flavored beer that was awesome--I wish I could remember its name for future reference. 

All in all, I was ready to go after an hour or so. It was flat out boring! The atmosphere, service, and selection were just not worth sticking around for.

Don't get me wrong: the selection at this location is fantastic. How could I possibly live without TJ's olive oil, veggie dip, soy milk, and cookies? 

The problem, unfortunately, is everything else. I made the mistake of driving here when I first moved to the area. The lot is absolute chaos on the weekends--good luck finding a space! These days, I just walk the half a mile each way. It's healthy, and also totally worth it to avoid parking.

Navigating this store with a cart is miserable. It honestly feels like an adult version of grumpy bumper cars. The aisles are just too thin. I try to carry my goodies in a basket, or even in my arms, whenever possible. 

The employees, I must say, are very sweet. My frustration with actually walking around this store usually disappears by the time I leave due to the cordiality and efficiency at check-out. Great customer service.

Honestly, if it weren't for the select few items that I basically need in my life, I would do all of my grocery shopping elsewhere. A few spatial adjustments to this store are definitely in order.

MUST GET THE PHORITTO! It's not on the menu so make sure you ask for it. I was skeptical at first when I heard about it but I'm glad I tried it. I barely even used the broth that comes with it because it was already infused with great pho flavor. It also comes with a side of hosin sauce & sriracha. The phoritto has everything that would normally comes in a bowl of pho. Brisket, noodles, veggies such has bean sprouts, basil, and jalapenos. It was easy to eat and wasn't soggy like I had expected. Will be back for more!

I also order a foot long banh mi (vietnamese poboy) and it was made with lots of flavor. A friend of mine recommended me to try it with their special aioli sauce and I did. It had the right amount of spiciness to it. My boyfriend tried it and he loved it! Probably the best we've had. 

This place is a convenient store with a few small tables if you decided to dine in. There is also parking behind the building which is a plus considering it is located on canal street. I'm ready to come back to try out their other items on the menu.

Hands down the BEST BBQ in town. It's located in a cute neighborhood, the bywater/marigny area. Friendly folks that work there. You order at the bar, they'll call your name when order is ready and bring it out to you. Fairly reasonable price for the amount of delicious food you get. I got the two meat plate (ribs and sausage) with a side of potato salad. The ribs was finger licking good and fall off the bone. Sausage links had a slight spice kick to it. Juicy and also delicious. Even their slices of pickles were good!! Potato salad had eggs mixed in which was a nice surprise. Ready to come back and try their other meats!

I'm very sad to write this review.

For years, when people asked where they should go for seafood I would recommend Deanies.  Nice people, good food, and schooners of Abita.

While running errands in Metairie I decided I would swing by.  I asked about their soul and was told they had a crawfish bisque that was good by the bartender, so I figured I would go for it. I always loved the creamy Crawfish soup here so figured it would be along those lines.

It came out and was basically an etoufee.  Dark brown roux, rice, and 4 crawfish bodies inside the roux.  That's not what I was expecting, but hey, I like etoufee so figured I would go for it.  The first bite I had was profoundly spicy.  The next bite was more of the same.  It's not like I'm not used to spicy food, I grew up in South Louisiana.  

I told the bartender (I was seated at the bar) how disappointed I was with it, and that I wasn't going to eat it.  She told me that it was house policy that they don't return items, and I would be expected to pay for it.  The manager came over and told me the same thing.  

I can't recall a more disappointing restaurant experience. I loved this place. But I've never, ever been treated like this at a restaurant, and I won't return.

I've had several folks recommend this place to me, but never seemed to be around at mealtime until last week.

It's a fairly typical neighborhood pub. Several TVs tuned to sports stations, but the volume was low enough it didn't interfere with normal conversation...and point in their favor.

My wife and both had a side salad to start our meal, and it was a cut above most pub salads.  A nice mixture of greens, and...oh, my, those croutons.  I can't say enough about them.  They're made in house and are absolutely fantastic.

I got the hand breaded tenderloin, and it's one of the best in Indy...or in the state.  Just the right size and thickness...not pounded out paper thin to the size of a hubcap,  and the breading is the perfect compliment to the meat.  Well done.

The fries, while good, were nothing special.  Just fries.

My wife and wings and I took a sample...fantastic!

The service was just a tad slow, so I can give them a 5 star review.  But I liked it a lot, and we'll certainly return soon!

Yeah.  It's a 5.

You should know...I don't drink alcohol, so I can't speak to their beer selection of the quality of the beer.

I CAN speak to the atmosphere, service, and food, and it was all stellar.  The menu is limited...food isn't their "main" thing, after all, but it was very good.  The service was stellar, and more than that, from the servers to the bookstore clerk to the owner himself, they all seemed like they actually appreciated  the fact that we were there.  That goes a long way.  We'll be back, and soon.

I'll keep this fairly short.

A 1 hour wait to even see a server.

A 2 hour wait to get our food.  Then my sandwich was cold.  Sent it back, (Which I NEVER do, but after waiting 2 hours I wanted a hot sandwich) and got another cold tenderloin.

Had to cut a significant amount of gristle out of the sandwich.  In addition, it was burnt to black.

No, thanks.

Great food and great front of house staff. I always love hanging out at the bar and chatting it up with the bar tender and other regulars who often hang out there. Everything is seemingly perfect until I came to realize how racist the head chef is, she certainly has some strong opinions on every other type of person that's not white. It's more confusing as to how the seemingly liberal owners would keep around someone who sympathized and even glorifies the Nazi regime and it's history both European and American. I don't think I'll ever step foot in this place again or at least until it gets new owners who don't tolerate racist assholes.

Last night my husband and I went out to Twisted Tree Steakhouse. Although I was not in the mood for steak, I  wanted to see what else they offered. The atmosphere was definitely crowded, especially at the bar. This is probably not most "intimate" place for a dinner date. We had:

Blue Point oysters (5/5), and their salad with 2 of their house dressings (5/5). I couldn't get enough of it!! My husband ordered a 14 oz KC strip with a side of onion fried potatoes and rated his dish a (4/5). He truly loved his steak and it was cooked perfectly. I made the mistake of ordering the charbroiled sea bass (3/5) that fell short but was complimented nicely with asparagus and amazing mashed potatoes (5/5). In addition, we wanted to try their batter dipped lobster tail (4/5) on a bed of frites that was delicious without the batter. It was waaaaay too salty and did not need the butter on the side. 

However, truly, the cherry on top was their wedding cake (5/5) with vanilla ice cream. GEEZUS. So fluffy, so gooooood. 

Our bus boy was on top of it, and our server was eh. 

I would probably return down the line for a steak, but as of now: been there, done that. 



Do: Take advantage of their complimentary valet. Parking is scarce! 

Do: Make reservations ahead of time!

After living in St Louis for 7 years, I finally made my way out to Alton around noon for some lunch time grub. As a *first timer, I was super excited because I heard a lot of positive things about this place. 

First things first, good luck with finding parking. We just happened to snag the last spot in the parking lot. Immediately as we entered, there's a guy in the front that checks your ID - THE NICEST human being in the establishment. Seriously. The line went so fast that by the time it was my turn to order, I had to quickly ramble everything to the rude cashier. Don't forget there's a one alcoholic beverage minimum per person - maybe that's how they compensate for the inexpensive food. For other first timers here are some tips: 

Tip #1: know what shit you want to order, especially how much SHRIMP you want. 

Tip #2: Try to come before the lunch rush. If not you'll be stuck waiting in line that wraps around the bar.

Tip #3: while you're waiting for food, grub on their popcorn. That will surely keep you ordering more beverages. 

I would definitely pass on the burger (2/5) and get their kebobs (3/5) and that are more on the salty side but at least has some seasoning. Their shrimp is nothing more than cocktail shrimp (3/5), but surprisingly their fries was the real winner (5/5). There's still some other items you can choose from that I hear are decent.

As far as seating they have both indoor and outdoor areas. Service is very lack luster. You'd be better off getting your own drinks from the bar or you'll never get acknowledged. 

Will I ever be back. Probably not.

Can you say, "AWESOMEEEE!"? That was my reaction as I walked down the Filipino aisle of Global Food Market in Kirkwood. A new resident to Missouri, I thought all hope was lost when all I seemed to pass was a Schnucks or Shop 'N' Save. My prayers have been answered when I was greeted with instant pancit noodles and sinigang seasoning. Woohoo! 

There's an aisle for a variety of countries ranging from India to Italy, as well as a wide selection of CHEESE and SAUSAGES. Woww. The store itself is intimate but big enough to satisfy all your needs.

This is my total comfort zone and will be back for those frozen edamame. Lol.

Vibes: small, unassuming, modern, casual-but-on-the-nicer-side BYOB; good for dates or small groups 

Tasting notes:
-Hong cho: topped with mint leaves; pomegranate flavor is subtle but not overwhelmed by tanginess of the vinegar
-Korean fried chicken: nuggets of hot, tender meat encased in that very satisfyingly crunchy exterior that is not too thick or overly flour-y; gochujang-honey coating gives just a bit of a spicy kick and stickness
-Galbi bourguignon bowl: fall-off-the-bone spoon-tender short rib meat with enough fattiness to add a lovely umami flavor to the rice; microgreens add more to the visual presentation than texture/taste
-Spicy pork in stone bowl: pleasantly surprised by large, thinly sliced pieces of perfectly cooked pork among fresh bell pepper slices and browned onions; loved the crispy chips of rice that came off the stone bowl surface 

Other thoughts:
-Food menu is short and focused and makes Korean cuisine accessible to those unfamiliar with common Korean dishes while staying very authentic
-Will have to bring some soju or light beer for my next visit!
-The few staff are very friendly and attentive

The lunch special burger was awesome! It was a lot of meat and a lot of fries. It beats the other burger places around... I will be back!! PS - as for dinner, i have not gone yet.. but i will one day..

The only reason why they are getting two stars is because the sashimi was fresh and our server was named Marc Anthony. Over priced for crap sushi. The eel and avacdo roll tasted like crap and you can never go wrong with an eel roll. The sushi rice was bland and mushy. This place was not good. I should have convinced my party to go to Morimotos... O Philly when are you gona have slammin sushi at decent price??!

I tried the cronuts a few weeks ago and they were bomb! Very very good. Too bad when i actually pre-ordered some they turned out to be CRAP, dried and hard. Not good at all. Wait in line for the 2 that you are able to purchase, at least they are fresh. DO NOT pre-order! As for cakes, i have not tried yet, but it is on my list!

We sat on the patio last night, the coldest night so far this winter. We ended up in a back corner, 30 feet from the nearest space heater, and we were chilly. All four of us wore our jackets throughout the entire meal. However, we did NOT complain because it was the only quiet-ish corner in the entire place.... the rest of the tables were basically communal, they were so close together.

The host (who we only met after walking past a long and unwelcoming bar and being hostilely stared down by a few servers) told us it was the 3-year anniversary and pointed to a gold "3" balloon as we walked in, but apparently that balloon was the extent of their celebratory preparations. Someone else in my party had been in a couple months ago and said that the specials board was the exact same as it had been when she came in the last time.

While we waited for the birthday boy to arrive, I ordered a cocktail whose ingredients were listed as premium vodka, lemon juice, fresh basil, and simple syrup. It came out pink, with a sugared rim and a strawberry. When I asked the server whether I had misread the drink list, he made some comment about grenadine, but did not balk when I asked for a glass of wine instead. My impression was that he had no idea what he was talking about, or that he had ordered a different drink from what I'd asked for, but he handled the situation to my satisfaction. The other person who arrived early with me asked about a lager he hadn't heard of (by the way, bottled beer only.... no draught at all) and the server's response was a sort of generic description of lager as light yellow beer--he clearly hadn't tried that particular one and didn't know much about beer in general. I dunno.... maybe the guy just doesn't drink. Lesson learned: only order drinks from the bar.

We got some garlic bread and portobello mushrooms for appetizers. The garlic bread really wasn't anything to be excited about--it was meh bread with olive oil, garlic, and some parmesan cheese. The mushrooms were nice.... served with some goat cheese and roasted (or maybe sautéed) seasonal veggies, they were well-prepared and presented beautifully. On a plate that was so hot that the food runner left the napkin with it in case we had to touch it. I dunno.... maybe they knew our table was pretty much the temperature of Pluto, and that dishes would cool quickly, so they heated the app plate to a Mercury temperature before launching off into the Solar System dining room.... I keep trying to give them the benefit of the doubt.

The server rattled off about 19 specials at break-neck speed (further evidence that they don't change daily) and 3 of us ordered from that menu: lamb, stuffed salmon, and seabass; the fourth of us got the pier stew from the regular menu. We basically ended up sharing everything, and were most impressed with the salmon; the stew was a close second. Just about everything was oversalted, though not to an unpalatable level. Nobody really felt very excited about the lamb.... underseasoned chops with garlic mashed potatoes. That was the only person who took leftovers home. I found it very interesting that when the meals came out, they looked very similar to one another: a pile of starch with protein displayed on top, and two piles of leafy veggies with two steamed carrots on the plate. They were different enough in flavor that we found them interesting, but I have a feeling that it's the kind of place that gets boring very quickly if you return a few times....

A few final thoughts: we had to park next door and then (LOL) duck through a gap in the chain link fence in order to get back to WGG. SO CLASSY. The wine glasses on the tables make Libby look like the finest crystal. For 2 bottles of cheap pinot, 2 vegetarian appetizers, 4 entrees, 1 set of leftovers, and no dessert, the bill was $215 before tip. The server was attentive throughout our meal, and had a cute little backup guy running around helping to fill waters and whatnot. The lighting has been upgraded since this was Sanchez, but the old fluorescent fixtures were just painted over on the ceiling before they hung Costco bistro strands everywhere. The open-flame space heaters are a nice touch! There is one single-toilet restroom for each gender in a space that sits at least 200, so go before you arrive 'cause you'll be waiting in line. The other 4 tables we could hear from our secluded little Arctic corner were also all celebrating birthdays.... clearly, this must be a special place for the grandest of occasions!

This is not fine dining; it is Olive Garden's new experiment in American Nouveau cuisine. I might go back if someone else is excited to try it, but I suspect that it will be much the same each time.

Oh. My. God. 

I was sure that New Orleans had no good Italian food until tonight. I found the perfect, mildly hokey, New York-style  Italian restaurant in Vincent's and I'm just going to quit my search for something better. 

When we sat down there was a vase full of breadsticks and a saucer of garlic butter. Divine. Why doesn't everyone do this?! I started with a lemon drop martini that was perfect- sweet but not sickeningly so, and not sour. After that I had the corn and crab bisque which is served in a bread bowl that wasn't completely stale. Crazy, right? The soup was sweet and although it didn't taste too crabby, it was delicious. The star of the show (and sadly/happily almost an entire meals worth of leftovers) was the chicken carbonara. It wasn't a true carbonara sauce (no raw egg), but for once it wasn't a bland alfredo sauce or a Cajun pasta sauce (delicious, but not what I was looking for). The chicken was so thin and fried PERFECTLY; it was exactly as my neighbor used to make for us back home and it was absolutely delicious. 

I have so much regret that I didn't make it to Vincent's sooner but I have the rest of my life to make up for it. 

See you soon, V.

Unfortunately, the majority of my reviews for the past couple of weeks have began with, 'if you're in New Orleans right now, you know it's cold.' And so I will begin....

It's cold. Though it might the increase in complaints and cars on the road, it doesn't stop anyone from going out and hanging out outside. Came here last night on the premise that 3 friends of mine (who don't know each other) claim that this is their favorite bar. Walked in and spoke to the chatty owner who steered me in the right direction for the type of wine I like. We bought our glasses ($6-8 ea.) and headed to the back to find a seat to listen to music, talk, and grab some food. The band was playing smooth jazz...not my favorite, but whatever, it was fine. The menu offered about 5 plates in each category (soups/salads, seafood, meat) and were priced very fairly. I ordered the red fish which came with caramelized leeks, cilantro and red onion and pecan vinaigrette ($16). The food was pretty good and the wine that the owner suggested went very well with the food.

Bacchanal apparently changes a lot, so here is how it was as of last night: outdoor seating space, window in the kitchen for food (cash only), wine store in the front that supplies wine by the glass or bottle (you can use your debit/credit card here), and a PERMANENT cocktail bar upstairs. The bar just opened Saturday and it will be open all the time. 

This place offers something for everyone: wine snobs, music lovers and foodies. Wish it was a little warmer but nonetheless, can't wait to come back!

I hesitate to write this review because (warning) it will be great and then people will flock and I won't have a space to work from anymore. But, they deserve a good review because it's a great coffee spot so let's continue...

Cherry EB has all of the essential qualities that make a coffee place great: a delicious brew, lots of outlets and table space, and sunlight. For coffee options you can't go wrong; all the classics plus the ability to have single origin coffee if you really know what you're doing (I don't). There are many two-seater tables, a couch corner, a long picnic table, and even some bar space. It's always full but I've never had to wait for a seat, somehow. The space itself is bright with lots of windows and the brick walls are hung with art. CEB gets its bonus points from the food which is fantastic and the baristas who are super friendly- the friendly chatter isn't rushed but damn do they work fast when they make your coffee. 

I live on the other side of the city but if I need to get work done I'm happy to drive uptown for some peace at CEB.

My boyfriend's brother invited us to join him at this little restaurant a couple of months ago.  We have since made it one of our regulars...

The restaurant: very tiny, maybe 10-15 tables.  Cozy.  The kitchen is off to the side of the room, where you can sit and watch the cook's prepare fresh meatballs and pasta to-order.  It's a BYOB too, so you can't beat that!

The staff: very friendly interactive with the guests, plus they remember your name when you come back making you feel like a very important guest.

The food: to die for.  Their portabello mushroom appetizer special was honestly the best food I have ever tasted.  Ever.

The price: the best part.  For 4 people, appetizers, salads, entrees, desserts, plus beverages & tips, our total bill was less than $90.   You cannot find this level of quality for half that price anywhere else (around here, anyway)!

I had a team dinner at this restaurant in Montecito.  It is supposed to be one of the top French restaurants in the area.  The restaurant is located in some back area obscure place off of the freeway.  It's a little old house converted into a restaurant.  The restaurant has an open-air concept, which means that if CA is having a heat wave, the restaurant is BAKING inside.  Our team  of ten had one of the private dining rooms and we were hot the entire meal.

Our experience started off with a bit of a twist.  The team arrived and the hostess was busy taking reservations on the phone.  We politely waited in the lobby check in area for several minutes and we weren't helped.  After about 5 minutes, we knew that we had a private dining room and we escorted ourselves to our seats and found our own menus.

Saving grace showed up when waiter Christopher (I think that is your name) showed up.  He provided some excellent customer service.  He knew the menu, he knew food pairings, he was very friendly, helpful, and made it a great experience!

Three appetizers were shared:  The first appetizer was the bone marrow.  I'm a huge fan of bone marrow and this dish was well prepared.  It was one bone marrow split into two main pieces.  Served with toasted crostinis.  Broiled to perfection, the bone marrow was soft and sweet.  It lacked flavor, but you got the flavor from the toasted bread.  Grade:  B

Second appetizer was the escargot.  Hands down, DELICIOUS.  Prepared with a French style herb butter and served with toasted crostinis.  Fabulous dish.  Grade:  A-

Third appetizer was the cured meats and cheese plate.  Very nice selection of salamis, cheeses, and dried fruits.  The selection of meats and cheese were typical and unevenful.  I was looking for a more unique ingredient to this dish.  Safe choice.  Grade:  B

For my main meal, I ordered the rib eye.  Instead of ordering it with the typical sauces, I asked that they serve it with the house herb butter that was served with the escargot.  WINNER!  The steak was tender and well done.  Enjoyable.  Grade:  A-

By the end of the meal, we were hot and exhausted from the heat.  It made enjoying the meal a bit difficult.  We enjoy the open air cocept, but it was a bit too much during this heat wave.

Food Grade:  B
Service Grade:  A!
Worth the Money Grade:  B
Overall Impression Grade:  B / B+

2 cheesesteaks both delicious they were just the way I wanted them drove all the way from NJ .....worth it . Thanks Mr.LEE
The chef here knows his meats, one of best burgers I have ever had. I was staying at Marriot and wanted to explore Center City, walked 10 min and found this place, Amazing!

What. A Shit Show.

Literally.

Let me start by saying, the people who work here are very nice. They're kind and polite and attentive and that's really great. It's not enough to save me from my experience this evening, but it should be noted.

I sat down and my server Jen was great. I ordered the charred broccoli, and after I ordered it Jen raved about it. When it came out, it was INSANELY undercooked. It wasn't 'al dente'; it was RAW. The florets were a little better fare, but the stems were literally inedible. I tried to eat a piece of a stem and sat there chewing it for several minutes, endeavoring to bite through with my teeth.

When Jen came back she asked me, you know "Wasn't I right about how great that is?" and I had to be honest and say it wasn't. I'm not really good about asking to have things removed from my check but I should've because this was garbage.

For my entree I ordered the casarecce. It's a twisted pasta dish with roasted mushrooms and a leek 'ragu.' Except it definitely was NOT that by any stretch.

First, "ragu" by definition contains meat. I assumed I was getting a leek and meat sauce, probably beef. What I got was a white sauce, no meat, and not a trace of leek flavor. It was overwhelmed by the mushroom flavor.

Now when I ordered this I asked if I could add a grilled chicken breast. I was told I could not. Apparently there is really NO way to add a protein of any kind to any dish at this restaurant. And that's fine, that's how they do. But after the broccoli issue, Jen suggested they could add some of the smoked chicken that comes with the rigatoni, "gratis", to compensate me. I said yes.

There were like MAYBE three or four TINY little pieces of chicken in my pasta. So. Thanks I guess. (Again this doesn't reflect on Jen.)

So I ate all of the pasta even though it was mediocre at best because at this point I only had 1/3rd of an edible broccoli app and I was really, really hungry. The actual pasta, made on site, was overly doughy and far too long (it should be cut in half like most casarecce.)

After this I just wanted to relax, and I never treat myself to dessert so I ordered the pumpkin cheesecake with a cappucino (made with cream) and also asked for the Budino to go. As I was ordering this I suddenly had the overwhelming, urgent and out-of-nowhere need to go to the bathroom.

So while I was waiting for the dessert to come out, I did go. And when I was done and stood up, I immediately had to go again. And I realized: something I ate has made me sick.

I don't know if it was the undercooked broccoli or the underdone pasta (the irony,) but my stomach was turning flips. And I had just ordered a coffee drink (brilliant.)

I do want to say this: the cheesecake was exceptional, and the cappucino was perfection. Honestly if this place was open earlier in the day I might come by for just dessert and coffee like EVERY day.

But as I was eating this dessert, I had to go to the bathroom again. Urgently. And I realized it was time to go home ASAP.

So I left my card, because at this point the place was getting full tables and Jen was very occupied. And things started just getting really more and more upsetting because I wanted to go home like NOW, because my body was NOT happy.

Fortunately Jen did see my card while I was in the bathroom. I came out and wanted to sign it and get the Hell out of there, and then her pen exploded all over my hands. It really was the insult to injury moment where I crossed the line from frustrated and disappointed to actively upset. I was clenching my bowels, desperate to go home, and there I was trapped because I had ink everywhere and couldn't sign my credit receipt.

Then in a true coup de grâce, just a chef's kiss moment on what had devolved into genuine unpleasantness, an employee had to open up the ground level double doors that lead into the cellar...which happened to be located directly next to my chair and bang against it as he went down. 

Clearly the hostess - again, just the nicest person - could see I was upset because she asked if everything was ok as I walked by. So I did take a moment to tell her: your food has given me diarrhea. Which is not something I would normally say to a stranger but it's just like...in that moment, I wanted to scream.

So listen. I dunno WTF was going on with the food tonight. People clearly love this place, and I wish I could give it another try considering it is a thirty second walk from my font door to theirs... but it seems unlikely.
I truly feel like for the most part I threw $62 (with tip) into the garbage...or should I say down the toilet. I'm literally still experiencing the GI effects of this meal; I had to stop writing this review briefly because of it.

I honestly want to know WTF WAS OUR WAITRESS' PROBLEM?! 

Before I begin, I just want to say that I remember our waitress' name very well, but I have chosen to omit it from this post because she clearly has enough issues. 

My mom and I went to the Cheesecake Factory in Willow Grove. We've frequented this specific location many times and never had an issue. Our waitress wasn't particularly friendly from the start, just lackluster. 

First, there was A HAIR in our appetizer. The manager came over, apologized, and brought us another appetizer to go. Our waitress did not apologize. Fine. Whatever. 

We got our entrees. I asked for bacon on my sandwich twice while ordering. Did I get bacon? No. Our waitress claimed she didn't hear me. Fine. I told her it was ok, I just didn't want to be charged for something I didn't receive. 

During her down time, our waitress sat two tables away from us wrapping silverware in cloth napkins as we ate. I could clearly see her. I felt like she was glaring over at us with a pissy look on her face. Or maybe she had a severe case of RBF. ‍

We weren't even halfway done eating when our waitress SLAMMED our check on the table, said nothing and sprinted away. No "would you like anything else?" "Would you like dessert?" Not even "I'll leave this here and take it when you're ready." Her actions said "pay and get out." My mom and I were looking at each other like "did that just happen?" 

A few minutes later, she SNATCHED one of our empty bowls off the table. She yanked it with such force that she actually startled my mom.

At this point, I lost my appetite and my mom lost her patience. We asked a different waiter to get the manager. The manager came over and my mom explained what happened. Suddenly our waitress appeared with one of our to-go orders and my mom, being an OG, flat out asked her IN FRONT OF HER MANAGER "why did you slam this check down?" Visually shocked and annoyed, she darted away in a huff. The manager said "that's ok, I wanted her to walk away. You don't have to have that conversation with her, I will." And the manager finished waiting on us for the brief remainder of our time there. 

Also our waitress continued rolling silverware and peering pissily at us. 

Out of our appetizer, two entrees, two to-go entrees, and two cheesecakes, the only thing that was taken off our bill was the appetizer.

I felt very uncomfortable and wanted to leave. I understand working for the public is difficult. There could have been some misunderstanding or something taken the wrong way. Or any number of things could have happened before she got to us or in her personal life, but you CAN NOT take your anger out on other people. She ruined an otherwise great evening.

In any other instance this situation would have received 1 star, but I've been here so many times in the past and had great service that I couldn't do it. I was actually apprehensive about posting this for the same reason, but it was such an unpleasant experience that I had to post it. The (hairless) food was still really good. And while this one waitress was a sour apple, she did not spoil the whole bunch. I'll more than likely return, but I hope I never get her as a waitress again.

My date and I went here to get a light dinner. He ordered a burger with bacon and I ordered the Maryland crab bisque. I also ordered a top shelf scotch. Our meals came out timely but there were a few problems which all added up to make a not-so-great experience. 

His "medium" burger was raw inside and the waiter agreed and kindly offered to bring out a new burger that was better cooked which turned out better than the first one. The fries that came with the burger were awesome. They where the best thing we had at the table actually. They had a nice crispy outside and were just delicious. I received the wrong soup which was odd because there were only 2 soups to choose from so the waiter must have momentarily spaced. I quickly received my crab bisque but it was only ok. I wouldn't recommend it or get it again. My scotch was also disappointing. I ordered a medium priced scotch, a Glenfiddich which was listed as $12. It was a cold night so I decided to go for it. Unfortunately my scotch was watered down and when the bill came, it was stated as costing $14!!

Our server Brian was nice about everything but we expected more from this restaurant and were disappointed with our experience. We don't anticipate coming back again when there are much better choices nearby.

So we just moved into this area, about 5 minutes away and we were looking for a good date night restaurant. So I pulled up my trusty yelp app and it led us here! Gosh this place was great. First off, when a place give complimentary bread baked in a cast iron skillet topped with Parmesan cheese and herbs... you know it's going to be a good meal. Our waiter was fabulous. He brought out some bread, asked if it was our first time, then brought us a complimentary appetizer which was edamame. And not your average sushi place edamame. This edamame was so dang good, topped with butter, garlic, some Asian spices. My husband, Joe, who is so picky absolutely loved it. I may have had to teach him how to eat edamame, but once he started, he couldn't stop. Next time we come here, even though it won't be our "first time" I have to order this again.

For our meals we both tried the tasting boards. This truly is the way to go if it's your first time here, or if you just like variety! I ordered the Surf and Turf board and Joe ordered the Filet trio board. The Surf and Turf comes with a filet topped with mushroom and Maytag sauce and crispy fried tobacco onions, chicken saltimbocca, mahi mahi with curry rice, and halibut with tappenade. So all were pretty good, each cooked perfectly. But my favorite was the filet. I hardly ever order steak, and I just couldn't get enough of that sauce. I didn't love the halibut, it just seemed a little bland to me. But the rest of the board was wonderful. Joe also loved his, and they were all cooked to his liking.

We ended the meal with a cookie baked in a cast iron skillet, then topped with cookie dough ice cream, and then topped with peanut butter mousse. You have to get this if you come here, but please, share it with 2-3 people, it's so rich. If you can finish that baby after a full meal, let me know... I would be impressed! 

Great food, impeccable service. You can see the kitchen cooking from your seat, which I think is really neat. If you sit right next to the kitchen, like I did, you might be a little toasty... just a warning! This place is really cute too, great ambiance making it nice for a date or get together with a few friends.

Yum! I really like Fuzzy's. Great prices, and really good food. I went with my boyfriend, his sister and brother-in-law, and their two kiddos. It was a good spot to bring kids, but you can also sip on a margarita or beer! To start you walk up to the counter and order, and then they give you a buzzer to come to the window to come and get your good. It was pretty busy on a saturday night, but they did a really good job with keeping the line moving. 

To start we had chips and guac, and also some queso, really good stuff. Can't really go wrong there. Then I ordered two fish tacos in soft tortilla, one grilled and one fried. Both were really good. I was starving, I probably could have gone for another one too. My boyfriend's sister and I split a watermelon margarita, really good! I would totally go back for that. 

My boyfriend's nephews are 6 and 8 and they both got orders of nachos, way to big for one person. They serve you a lot of food. It was pretty funny trying to watch them finish it. I totally plan on coming back, and would bring my family and friends. Go Fuzzy's!

Salt + Smoke, it's been a year since I first met you and things are going stronger than ever between us. You're still my favorite BBQ joint in the Lou. Not that I don't love me some pappy's, bogarts (just to name a few) but I absolutely adore S+S. Everything about you is wonderful. I love that they use a local soda company, their craft cocktails, and scrumptious appetizers. But more than anything, I really admire that nothing on the menu is an afterthought. Even every side item is a star. 

You really cannot go wrong from the potato salad, green bean tomato salad, garlic and herb fries, white cheddar cracker Mac and cheese, sweet potato chips, beans... Nothing is meh, in my honest opinion. Everything is extremely flavorful, unique, and high quality. I happen to LOVE their Mac and cheese, it's the best I have personally ever had. 

The toasted ravioli is my favorite appetizer at S+S. Not that toasted ravioli in St. Louis is creative, but they turn their rendition into a cleaver BBQ version. It's with burnt ends as the meat in the ravioli and then you dip it into a white BBQ sauce! A great spin on a St. Louis classic that totally works. I've also had the bacon cheddar popovers, fried pickles, and deviled eggs.... All are excellent. 

And to the meats!! Goodness.... Where do I begin?! Everything is highly flavorful. The brisket is so tender, the pulled pork melts in your mouth, and surprisingly the fried bologna is crazy good (coming from someone who doesn't even like bologna)!!! I have not tried their ribs, I am not a huge ribs fan, but I might just try them sometime just so I know.

The sauces on the table are so complimentary of the meats, but truly, you don't even need them. The meats are THAT good. I like the sweet bestie BBQ sauce, and the white BBQ sauce. Their is also a mustard based BBQ sauce, a tangy not as sweet BBQ sauce, and a hot BBQ sauce. 

And that's just all about the food. The place is super cute, but it does get very busy on the weekends. The service has been nothing but wonderful every time I've been there. If there is something that can improve on- it would be that when they are packed, they create a better/efficient way for guests waiting on a table to know when it's their turn... Maybe like a number/buzzer system?

All in all, amazing creative unique food at decent prices. You can't go wrong here.

I came here with a group of 30 a few days ago at lunch time. The restaurant had roughly 1 hour notice that we'd be arriving, but they accommodated us extremely well and the food was excellent. I had the Bulgogi, which was a first for me (Korean food in general is new to me) and it was delicious.  

5 stars for accommodating such a large group on short notice and sending out everything steaming hot and delicious. I work nearby, so I'll be back soon to try other items.

I was in Sunday morning for breakfast with my wife. After we shopped for a bit, we saw this on your shelf. 

http://www.amazon.com/s/ref=nb_sb_noss?url=search-alias%3Ddigital-text&field-keywords=that%27s+so+gay+sound+machine   

We found this very offensive and left after putting the items back we were going to purchase and paying our food bill. So much for keeping it local.  Denny's would've been preferable to the feeling we left with.

Unfortunately, we won't be back.  You don't have to agree with me, but I do get the option of spending my money for good rather than evil.

I drove across town because other Yelpers were rating this so high and saying good things about it. So we invited friends from St.Alabert and met half way. The drive was worth it. Tom our host lived up to his rating and the food was excellent. Green onion cakes were unique and salad rolls were really large...maybe too big.but they do not scrimp on serving size here.Pad Thai was great as was the red curry chicken stew. All was fresh,served hot and just in time. This restaurant will do well. It keeps prices in line in part with lower rent location and fewer fancy furnishings...all in all a 5 star combo.

Worst experience at a hotel, bar-none!

My wife and I decided to drive up to Santa Barbara for a night, as a getaway from our hectic work schedules. We decided on the Bacara, fully expecting a five star experience. That was the absolute antithesis of what we ultimately received. In fact, the only positive part of our stay was the striking natural beauty of the locale.

We were treated shabbily from the very moment we arrived. As we entered the valet area, the valet asked us whether we meant to stay at Bacara, or whether we were lost. We thought little of this, and proceeded toward the entrance of the hotel after handing over the keys. As we made our way toward the lobby, we heard the same valet respectfully greeting the occupants of the car behind us with a cheerful "Hello Sir, and hello Ma'am, welcome to the Bacara." Again, we shrugged it off, as it was an isolated incident. We were also left waiting for a rather obscene amount of time just to get checked in. Moreover, the people at the front desk were apathetic at best-and rude at worst.

When we arrived at our room, we immediately encountered two enormous, black, and very dead cockroaches in the bathroom. Honestly, we are both quite mellow, but this was a bit much-and it really disgusted my wife. Still, at first glance everything else looked tidy enough, so we let it slide. I disposed of the cockroaches, and we freshened up, and took the 15 or so minute drive to State Street. While there, we enjoyed fantastic customer service, food and drinks. We arrived back at the hotel somewhat early, and decided to order some dessert and champagne. We ordered the creme brulee and some sort of warm apple tart. The man who brought up our order was the only staff member we had come into contact with who was actually professional, and who treated us warmly. The creme brulee was quite good, but the apple tart was mostly cold and tasted stale.

As we were getting ready for bed, I noticed that the bedding was unclean; it was dotted with black granules and small brown flakes. It was sickening really, but we were so exhausted that we just fell asleep (though without getting underneath the covers, and after covering our pillows with our own shirts). 

The next morning, as my wife was taking a shower, a third gigantic cockroach made itself known by crawling onto her foot. I lost my patience at this point, and I called the front desk and explained what happened. I was told that I would get a call back. I never did. When we checked out, I attempted to talk to someone. However; no one was available.  

At this point, all we wanted to do was leave. During our drive back, I called and asked to speak with the manager. The manager, Dave, was condescending, rude and combative--he displayed absolutely no managerial skills at all. He interrogated me by asking why I didn't call to report the first set of cockroaches, if I was so disgusted. Dave was incredibly dismissive, arrogant, and made clear that he thought of my concerns as illegitimate. His response to me was simply that: "People are all very happy here that stay with us, and you only stayed one night." Great. 

The upshot then is: horrible service (come here if you would like to be treated poorly), sub par food, and a marked lack of basic cleanliness. 

The last hotel my wife and I stayed in (the St. Regis, Monarch Beach) was comparable in price, but a diametric opposite of the Bacara on every conceivable dimension. Bacara: you stand to learn quite a bit about even the very basics of serving your customers.

Living the luxurious life!!!

We didn't stay here overnight...just came for the breakfast buffet.

If you get the hot foods and cold foods, it's about $35/person.

We skipped the omelet bar and etc, and just got the cold breakfast for around half that price. 

Cold breakfast included: assorted croissants, muffins, and other pastries. Cold smoked salmon, capers, cream cheese, butter, onions, assorted bagels, mixed berries, cantaloupe, honeydew, watermelon, pears, pineapple, bananas, apples, yogurt&granola, mixed cereals.

Lots of coffee, orange juice, delicious fresh mint tea, carrot juice.

View was beautiful and we had a nice 160 degree view of the ocean. 

Service: extremely nice and befitting of any ultra-expensive location.
They gave the toddler in our group crayons and coloring books without asking which was really sweet.

Food was tasty and fresh but not out of this world. I would return here but you're really coming here to enjoy the beautiful view and live the high life. 

Overall a great light and healthy meal to enjoy for the holidays!

I probably just found one of my new favorite Tampa places.  Nestled in a hot spot of Seminole Heights this unimposing restaurant sits on a corner I haven't noticed before. And that was my loss and now my gain after trying it out! I showed up to Front Porch for lunch with a friend at her recommendation. I didn't know what to expect but was excited to try a local, small business. They beyond impressed me with their hospitality and food. Our server Land was so nice and readily available to answer questions and provide recommendations. I'm a little needy so it was nice having someone provide recommendations based on my preferences! I tried the honey ginger smash cocktail and fell in love. They pulled fresh mint for the cocktail which was a nice touch. This drink is dangerous and refreshing. I could have multiple cocktails and not realize how much I was drinking. It was a refreshing drink to enjoy on the front porch! For lunch my friend and I split French fries (again homemade never frozen) and the goat cheese flatbread. If you're like me and love cheese, this is the flatbread for you! It was delicious and had caramelized onions. We ate it so fast I almost wanted to order a second. There was some parking and it had plenty of socially distant seating that I am definitely come back. I need to try the whole menu. Shoutout to Land for being an amazing server and giving us the best recommendations. 11/10 recommend this place!

Being born and raised in France, you know I had to try this place.
The place is small with a few tables inside and outside. I immediately saw some things in the display case that I haven't seen anywhere other than in France, which made me hopeful. A young man took our order to find out he was the owners son, and yes, they are all actually from France.
We opted for the Croque Monsieur and the plate of charcuterie.

That Croque Monsieur was HUGE for $5 (more on that later). The taste....what can I say....other than I'm drooling writing this review thinking about it. You can tell the ham and cheese they used was definitely not the cheap stuff. But it's $5!!!!! How can that be????

The charcuterie was very French. Again, you definitely can tell the cheese and meats were imported and not something you can find at a local grocery store, no matter how nice the store is. WOW!!!! (Drooling even more now, thanks a lot!!!).

Couldn't leave without tasting some pastry. Pain au chocolat, and have to try the chocolate mousse (do you see a pattern here? Yes, I'm a chocolaholic, and fell off the wagon. STOP JUDGING ME!!! LOL).
The pastry was amazing, and the mousse was thick yet light and so FREAKING good! (Am I going to ever stop drooling? I got to end this review. I'm getting weird looks).

Talked to the owner. Super nice! He showed me around, and the crates with the cheeses he orders (yep! Imported), and said he was frustrated with French restaurants being so expensive everywhere, and wanted to show what normal French people eat, as most can't afford a $100+ meal.
Aaaahhhh, that explains the prices. Wow! I have a lot of respect for these people!

This is definitely going to become a weekly weekend place for us to go to. Awesome!

Let's get this straight. 4 stars for food only and 0 for service. We arrived at 6:30pm. Got seated at 7pm not because there was a wait, because tables were not clean. They had two servers and one cook working! 

It took 10 mins for drinks about 45 mins for appetizers and an another 30 mins for dinner. After hour and a half we all finally got our food. Unless they make these improvements ASAP I don't think they'll last. The waitress was nice and friendly and it wasn't her fault for lack of manpower. 

For appetizer we ordered Hummus, Falafel and Kibbeh. Hummus and falafel were both good. But falafels are much smaller in size compared to other Arab restaurants.

We also ordered Kibbeh - a torpedo-shaped fried croquette stuffed with minced onions and finely ground beef very good, delicious and flavorful. It almost reminded me of a smaller hot pocket but WAY better. 

The chicken kabab sandwich - grilled on skewer and stuffed inside of white pita bread with fresh vegetables was pretty good.  It was priced well at $7.99 but it was small with no sides. The Lamb sandwich cooked same way as aforementioned was also very good but again no sides and priced at $8.99. 

My friend ordered the mushroom swiss burger and she said it was very good. The sandwich was huge with a thick slice of beef patty served with lettuce, tomatoes, onions and fresh fries.  

An other friend ordered the kabab entree which came with bland yellow rice and juicy five pieces of grilled chicken. Same type of meat this is inside the chicken kabab sandwich. 

For dessert we ordered Kanafeh - made from long thin noodle threads, spread with soft white cheese and topped with thick syrup of sugar and diced pistachios. It was the closest to the authentic Kanafeh I've had so far. Very very good and fresh. 

I would only visit this place after staffing is fixed.

Hubby and I were in Santa Barbara and were staying at the Bacara Resort and Spa for a Company event ...... luv those!  The first night we had a romantic dinner at the Angel Oak At Bacara restaurant.  The restaurant is modern, inviting and has a chill atmosphere.  We were greeted with smiles even though we had no reservations .... very nice.  We were seated at one of the lovely booths and ordered:

(1)  Drinks
I ordered my Cosmopolitan which was made perfectly and Hubby had a Dirty Martini.  A great start to our evening.

(2)  Complimentary Bread and Seasoned Butter
OMG, the bread was house made, warm  and was so delish.   After you add the butter you will find heaven.

(3)  Blue Crab Cake
Pan seared, celery root and apple remoulade, caviar.  I had a taste of Hubby's crab cake which was mostly crab, fresh and perfectly seasoned.

(4)  Pancetta Wrapped Dates
Lamb, pickled cucumber, house made yogurt dip.  The lamb was so tender and served with pancetta made it a perfect appetizer.  Very tasty!

(5)  Roasted Bone Marrow
Bone Marrow with Oxtail marmalade, pistachio gremolata, herbs, grilled sourdough.  OMG, this is a signature dish.  Bone marrow and oxtail meat?  What?  Total genius because it was so rich and full of flavor.  Please order this!

(6)  Lobster Bisque
Saffron rouille, pumpernickel, lobster.  My bisque had lil chunks of lobster ..... luv that!  It was seasoned well and prepared perfectly.

(7)  Caesar Salad
Pecorino romano, boquerones, radishes, herbs.  Hubby's salad was a lil underwhelming.  He didn't like his lettuce shredded.

(8)  Bone In Ribeye
18oz., USDA Prime.  I wanted the AAAAA Kobe Certified Steak but they ran out for the night =(.  So, hubby and I decided to share the Ribeye and add a lobster tail.  The Ribeye was perfectly cooked to medium rare and was SO juicy.  The lobster tail was tender and was the perfect match for our steak.

(9)  Lobster and House Made Gnocchi Gratin w/ local lemons
Our lovely server recommended the Gnocchi to accompany our Ribeye.  OMG, the dish was so DELICIOUS.  The Gnocchi was creamy and the dish was full of lobster pieces.  I could had ordered this dish as my main entree ....... yes, that good!  Order this!

(10)  Candy Bar
Dark chocolate cremeaux, peanut butter crunch, salted caramel ice cream.  If you luv chocolate and a decadent dessert, the Candy Bar is for you.  This dessert will definitely make your palate dance.

(11)  De-Caf Coffee
The restaurant's coffee was perfect with my dessert.

I had a romantic dinner with Hubby at the Angel Oak at Bacara.  Their food is delicious and the service was attentive and very friendly.  5 Stars!

5 Stars for the super friendly service and delicious food!

It's tough to find a place that has so many reviews AND maintains a 5 star rating. Well, this place does and deserves it! The owner was incredibly nice and the prices are very good. I ordered the 12" Mojo Heaven, a side of black beans, and chips n guac (made in house). That was way more food than I could eat but it was so delicious. I'd suggest getting the Mojo Heaven and an Imperial (Costa Rica) beer. Great combo! 5 stars all day and we'll be back for sure.

A side note - don't worry about getting a side of mojo sauce like I did. The sandwich was deliciously moist without it.

Another awesome experience at Sea Salt. We went on a local helicopter tour and we were told that Sea Salt would give us an appetizer or dessert and two glasses of bubbly for free. So, we headed to Sea Salt without a coupon or code or any evidence that we were told that and I figured it would be dismissed by Sea Salt. Well, the bartender had never heard of that deal but called over the manager. The manager promptly authorized 1/2 dozen raw oysters, 3 oyster Rockefeller, and two glasses of bubbly. How awesome! Wish I would have gotten their names but failed to do so. It's nice to have great service and for the record, this is our third time going to Sea Salt. Every time has been a great experience. Thanks Sea Salt!

4.5 stars for the ambiance and delicious BBQ

I really like the building and the decor. Very open inside that can easily sit 200 people. So, don't get worried about a full parking lot- there'll be room. The food - very good. I had the pulled pork sandwich and I have to say, the bun was super soft. The pork was smokey, moist, and tender. The two sauces on the table were tangy and I preferred the spicier version. With the sandwich, I got the banana bread and the Mac n cheese sides. Both very tasty. A couple of other things- I like the clean/sterile restrooms, different seating options, and the quick service. Fair prices and they sell bottled beer. The dessert case looked delicious. We'll be back when in that area again and should they open a location in Pinellas we'll be there.

I don't know why people are all excited about this joint but after my visit tonight, I won't be back.

We ordered the pretzel strips and garlic fries for our meal.  Though the pretzel strips were pretty good, the garlic fries were awful.  The only way to describe the garlic fries was they tasted like burnt popcorn.  You know, you can't get the taste out of your mouth no matter how much beer you drink???  Yeah, that gross.  Something was said to the server about the garlic fries being burnt and awful and her response was, "Well, you ate half of them.  Couldn't have been that bad."  That comment sums up Juniper in 12 syllable or less.

We won't be back.  With all the options in downtown Boise available, we can cross Juniper off the list for good.

It's been a while since we've been to a restaurant that we'd consider coming back to, especially for brunch. Food here is simple, but done pretty well and without pretense. 

We were lucky to walk in when there wasn't a line - as soon as we began to order, the line quickly filled to the door. But apparently, for a Sunday, if the line isn't to the parking lot, it's considered slow! Get there earlier I guess.

The pastry displays looked pretty good - normally we'd pass but were starving and split a cinnamon roll and a danish. Both hit the mark for looking and tasting as you'd expect. Not too sweet, baked well, good spice, etc. 

The farmhouse breakfast came with verrry crispy potatoes, juicy sausage patties, and a pretty fluffy biscuit. No complaints there. My salad with my chicken pot pie was appropriately dressed lightly, and actually super tasty and not some side afterthought other restaurants would throw on the plate to take up space, not that I'm naming any namesthelivingroom. 

The pot pie itself I expected a thicker stew, not necessarily encased in pastry on both sides, but certainly a thick stew that you'd be able to hold in an edible vessel. What I got was a mug of brothy chicken soup, and a very thin layer of pastry on top. I didn't mind the soup, actually - it was seasoned, and tasted like chicken soup. Not the hearty entree that I expected on a rainy day, but idk I guess some people might actually like that it's lighter? Though for me it sort of defeats the purpose of pot pie, and I'd rather have chicken noodle soup with some oyster crackers or something. Oh well. Still tasted good, at least, false advertising or not.

Anyway. Pretty good food all around.

The only complaint I have is that their drip coffee is worse than a diner's. But next time I might just get an espresso drink. I think we'll likely be back though!
Coffee was ok but didn't like the uptight environment and loud music. So many rules. (Photo attached is just one of many signs) Kind of uncomfortable. Pricy too.

I ate at this establishment on Friday during the New Year's banquet. Unfortunately, my boyfriend and I along with 100 other guests became incredibly ill shortly after our dinner here. Some of the guests even had to go to the emergency room because of their symptoms. We all believe that came down with a serious case of food poisoning. I will never ever eat here again and 4 days later, we are still recovering.

Prices of Ritz Carlton and stay was worse than a motel. Their COVID restrictions include NO coffeemaker in room, no glasses, mugs, no amenities like mouthwash, shoe shine, slippers, sewing kit. I don't understand how COVID lives in a coffeemaker but not in towels?? Their restrictions make no sense. And this was disclosed upon check in. No prior email about any of this.
Basically you buy their over priced coffee. Do not even think about ordering room service. We ordered breakfast that came in paper bags.. coffee in a paper cup that was already cold and I paid $60 for that!! 
We left 2 voice mails to book tennis court, no one got back to us. 
Self or valet parking are $30 per night.. resort fees $25 and another $75 in taxes per night.. 
Horrible service, no assistance with luggage, we had to haul our own bags, going uphill and downhill. We requested assistance at check out but they told they were busy :(:( 
The grounds are pretty and it's an ocean front property but not worth the money and insane restrictions

I was working in the area and decided to stop by before they close to grab some ginger cookies for the kids. They had 4 left so I grabbed all of them. I also grabbed a mini key lime pie as I absolutely love these and they remind me of travelling. 

The atmosphere in the store was good, very clean and organized but I miss the hustle and bustle of the place. I remember a time when this place was always packed and not a seat to be found! 

The ginger cookies have chunks of candied ginger baked right into them and they are delicious. The lady who was helping me suggested that I try the frozen, ready to bake ginger cookies to take home and enjoy. I didn't even know they had this available so I'm so glad she suggested this! I bought the small size 8 cookies for $14.95. I have yet to bake some at home but I'm looking forward to the warm delicious cookies! 

They have a ton of provisions you can buy to make delicious goodies at home as well. The staff is super friendly and helpful and just a wonderful experience!

One more update! Do you really want to spend your money at a place where the owner gets on Yelp to call his customers a liar? That is in fact what has happened as I did submit a receipt (over a month ago) and the owner has not returned my email. Please continue reading the reviews for this place and read how disrespectful the owner is to people who criticize his establishment.  There are WAY better ways to spend your hard earned money.

Be careful who you shell money out to for a great dinner. I will tell you the food is awesome but Roberto talks a bad rap against his customers. Complains about them when they leave restaurant. Been there, done it and seen it happen. Just saying.

I had an overall positive experience while dining here. We were seated right away and 
provided a server who had a great personality and made sure to greet us right away. 

I ordered the salmon as my entree and the cauliflower wings as an appetizer. I especially enjoyed the cauliflower which I requested to be topped with a bbq sauce. Other options were a mild or hot sauce. I personally love anything barbecued, so this was a perfect starter for me. I should note that a few at my table commented that the sauce was too sweet. I figured I should share that. I thought the salmon was well cooked, the mashed potatoes were buttery, and the broccoli was huge.

I also love that they have a margarita on the menu that doesn't have Cointreau or Triple sec, both of which rarely sits well with me. 

Hard Rock Cafe is always a sure bet.
