By far my favorite restaurant that we visited while in NOLA. I hear, at times, the line to get in is crazy, but we were lucky to walk right in and get the first table to the right of us. I could tell our server was busy, but not once did that affect the quality of his service or of the food. 

I ordered the fried catfish with yams and mac n cheese. It also came with peas which I ate because they were there. Peas are peas. The catfish and yams were so good! The catfish was well seasoned, nicely crisp on the outside. The yams were soft, not too soft, and had a flavor that reminded me of home.

I would absolutely recommend this place to anyone who doesn't want to be disappointed. I hear the fried chicken is what they are famous for. I can't tell you if that's true or not, but feel free to let me know if you get it.

I'm torn right now, because I want everyone to try this place out; however, if I say the 'v' word, many people may decide not to. Our server was so awesome and thorough. He knew the menu from front to back and made everything sound so damn delicious. This place proves that vegan food CAN be everything you wanted (or didn't realize you wanted) and needed in a meal. Our party consisted of both vegans and meat-eaters... all were satisfied. Well done, Charles.

The beautiful historic townhome that houses the Standard looks a little out of place on the street's odd mix of buildings. First thing we notice arriving at the small bar in back is strong smell of smoke from club upstairs.  Smell is much less noticable in dining room.  Small place, only 8 tables in the restaurant.

Everyone on staff was very friendly, but the entire experience felt amateurish. No bartender, just whoever happens to know how to make a drink. They were fishing beer bottles out of a plastic tub. Making my drink, wait person dunked their entire hand deep into a large jar of cherries to fish one out. Yuck. 

As other reviewers have pointed out, the wine list is surprisingly small and uninteresting for a place that would seem so upscale. 

Appetizer and soup/salad course brought out at same time. Ok, maybe we should have specified, and waiter was apologetic, but again, that feel of amateurish.

Waiter bragged on their steaks, saying they were known as one of the best steak houses in the country. Well, no, the run of the mill cut of strip steak was way underseasoned and way overcooked. 

Sides - brussel sprouts were overcooked. Potato hash too small to share, and cold.

On the positive side, the fried green tomato appetizer and crab bisque were both absolutely delicious, so someone in the back knows a thing about flavor (apparently not the same person working the steaks).

Bottom line, this place looks fine dining and advertises fine dining, but has a long way to go to reach that level.

They should have paid us to eat this food.  Huge disappointment.  It was a new chef and the food was disgusting.  Would you eat calf brain bisque with clumps of brain and ball of cream cheese in a bisque?  The consistency was horrible. Or Martin's chicken wings, bone and all cooked down to a jelly, then topped with Cod sperm?  Yes cod sperm.

We have eaten at iron chefs' restaurants and like to try new things but this was like eating leftover parts of animals and fish that not only didn't taste good but the thought of eating it was disgusting.

Not worth $250 for 2 people.  One other couple left after 4 dishes and said "life is too short to eat this disgusting food". They paid and left without eating the rest of the meal.

The servers said the dish"s name so quickly as they put the dishes in front of us.  I think they didn't want us to know what it really was.  Even if we didn't know what it was, the flavors of the dishes did not work well together,  either bland or gross combinations.

They should have given everyone a refund and a gift certificate to eat at another restaurant.

Stopped here on my Way up to my Dad's last week.  Was going to go to the nearby burger place, but it was too crowded so opted for Dargan's instead.  It is tucked away off State Street, hidden behind a busy burger place and some overgrown vines.  The food here was decent, I think I should have ordered the fish and chips, but I went with their signature Shepherds Pie; it was a very small portion.  The place was short staffed and one waitress was masterfully working the entire pub; give that girl a raise please.  

I would go 5-stars save for the wobbly tables, unclean tables just left there gathering flies, and the lack of staff.  The food was decent, not the best but not the worst either.  I might return, but think this place needs a little work.  Still a fan though.  

Also, Santa Barbara, you all need some better parking.  Your 15 minute green zones are not well thought out and a little abusive to your patrons who you so depend on for your livelihood.  Build a few Parking lots for goodness sake.

Someone please call restaurant impossible, this place is gross! I hadn't been in over 2 years, I used to go with co-workers at my last job, and I remember it being very busy and really tasty! I went for lunch today with co-workers and the place was empty, and eerily quiet. We probably should have taken that as a warning, but instead sat down. I ordered a water, sweet potato fries and a chicken hot sandwich with peppers and onions. The water tasted gross, none of us really drank it, and then they brought out the fries about 10 minutes before our sandwiches. By the time the rest of our meals came they were cold. Not very good sweet potato fries either. My sandwich was ok, the chicken was dry, marinara was straight out of a can, and the onions and peppers were too overcooked and soggy. I will not be going back here.

Not to mention, the whole establishment is gross. There is sports, movie and music memorobilia everywhere, but none of it has ever been wiped down, dusted or maintained. Vinyl record covers are literally falling off the ceiling. 

When we came back to work we told some co-workers about it, one suggested that this restaraunt could be a front for something else. I wouldn't doubt it! There is no way they could stay open if at 12:30 on a thursday no one is there. yuck!

This was my first time to Diablo Burger in Tucson, although I was a strong supporter of the one in Flagstaff before I graduated NAU in 2010. I was EXTREMELY excited when I saw the highlighter green liquor license application go up on the empty store front (I may have been drinking at the time) and remember prancing around saying how excited I was that a little taste of the small town I miss so much was coming to T-town.  

Once they opened, every time I thought to go in, they were packed, so I opted to wait til the storm calmed a bit. My birthday was mid-June and on a Friday, and since I work just around the corner, I planned to have my coworkers join me for lunch at Diablo to celebrate. There ended up being about 12 of us, which was a little more than the restaurant could accommodate, but some nice guys moved to another picnic-bench community style table so that all of us could pile in at one table. 

When the server came, she got everyone drinks etc, answered questions and everything was great. I was the second person to place an order, and I ordered "The Blake" (burger with homemade hatch chile mayo, roasted green chiles & sharp cheddar).  She asked how I would like it cooked and I said "medium well." She then said, "Our chef recommends that the burgers are cooked medium-rare." I said, "That's ok, I think I'll stick to medium well." End of conversation, right? No. She then began to tell us about how the beef was not "regular" beef, that it was special and from northern AZ, grass fed, blah blah blah.  I know a lot about the restaurant and how it started, I lived in Flagstaff just up the street from it, and although I fully support the cause, I felt like she was arguing her point to get me to select medium rare.  She ended her paragraph by saying, "so that's why we recommend medium-rare." 

I felt embarrassed that she was arguing with me about it, and really didn't want to hold up our 12-person-on-our-lunch-break table, so I was like, "whatever is fine." I was obviously disgruntled, for god-sake it was my birthday and i brought in 12 people to a nearly empty place. The LAST thing I wanted was to be "put in my place" by a server. UGH.

As we waited for our food I tried to change the subject, my friends and I discussed the decor of the restaurant, I knew the artist of a couple of the prints, so that was exciting. We also liked how they served coke in the glass bottles, a nice touch. I was also a fan of the Vespa on the wall. 

Once the food came I took one bite into my burger and was completely disgusted by the bloody mess it left behind.  I just nibbled around the edge and then ate my fries. The fries were yummy. She came to take my basket and noticed the mostly-uneaten burger and didn't even say anything or ask me if I wanted a to-go container. 

Next time I will just say, "Hey look, last time I heard the whole story about Diablo burger, got my burger med-rare, and it was disgusting...medium well please!" Although the Flagstaff location would get a 5-star rating in my opinion, this Tucson one needs to learn what's up!

I had a hard time deciding how to rate this experience so I'm going to break it down into two parts.

I'll start with the best part. The food and drinks get a 5/5. I have had this spot bookmarked for awhile because I kept reading how amazing their Korean chicken is. My boyfriend is Korean and I lived in Korea for four years so we really miss Korean chicken. I don't know what Koreans do to chicken to make it so damn good. We ordered it at least once a week when we were living there. So when I told my boyfriend about Umami, he was skeptical but willing to try. We ordered the large size which consisted of 20 pieces. There are two options for sauces: soy garlic and spicy. We ordered half spicy, half soy garlic. When the plate came out, I think both of our mouths dropped open. It was a lot of chicken. 20 pieces is definitely enough for 2 people. The chicken is topped with green onion and comes with a side of radishes. This is how you do Korean chicken. Don't let the smell of the radishes scare you. They are perfect to take away some of the spice. I took a bite of the chicken and wow...it was legit. I think I saw a tear form in my boyfriend's eye after he took his first bite. A halo of light formed around the chicken as the heavens sang. My boyfriend said in Korea there is a saying, "I want to cry because it tastes better than my mother's cooking." The skin was crispy, the sauce was flavorful, and the chicken was moist. The spicy is spicy, but not too spicy. It's not Nashville hot chicken. My favorite was the soy garlic. My suggestion, take a bite of the chicken with some of the onion, then eat one of the radishes. It's the perfect mix. If you like chicken, you have to try this. Korean chicken is the best chicken I've ever had. I will add that their beer prices are also pretty good here. Most of the beers are $3-4. In Korea, they actually have a name for drinking beer with chicken because that's just what you do. So get a cold one with your chicken. You'll thank me. 

Now for the not so great. I would give the service here a 3/5. The hostess was very friendly. However, the server was just ok. He was nice but not attentive. Now I'm all about giving people their space when they are eating, but a check in every now and then is nice. It took us awhile to get another drink. The place wasn't busy so it just seemed a little strange. I always feel rude waving people down but that's what I felt like I needed to do. Another thing that was a little strange was the prices on the menu weren't right. The menu said $19 for the large chicken set but then we ordered, we were told the price was actually $24. I don't think this is too much. It's a lot of chicken. It's just weird to be told the price is more after you order and without explanation. I'm guessing they are getting new menus printed. Or at least I hope so. The inside of the restaurant is ok. It's clean and I liked how they had a big screen playing music videos. A lot of the music was K-pop so it set the mood to chow down on some Korean chicken. 

We will definitely be ordering chicken from here...a lot. Probably too much. My boyfriend texted me the day after saying he missed the chicken already.

After being here about 4 times after my initial review, I felt the need update. Hai Woon Dai is a small Korean restaurant in Antioch. It is in a small strip of businesses, most of them being Korean businesses. There is plenty of parking out front, even when it's really busy. 

The restaurant itself is nothing fancy. Minimal decorations and the seats and chairs are pretty basic. This is always a great sign for me. The focus is on the food and it feels very authentic. After living in South Korea for 4 years, this place feels like home (or what used to be my home). Because it's smaller, it gets pretty busy on the weekends. However, I've never had to wait for a table. They ask you how many you have in your party, you're seated, and then given a menu. The menu has a lot of options including Korean Barbecue. They don't have the big fancy built in grills like a traditional korean bbq, but instead comes on a tabletop grill. It seems to work just fine. I'm a huge Korean soup fan so I usually order the yukgaejang. It's a spicy red broth with glass noodles, shredded beef, and vegetables. I'm kind of wimpy when it comes to spicy things, so to me the soup is pretty spicy. Perfect for a cold winter day or if you have a cold. The soup comes with a side of rice so I suggest eating some of the soup and then adding the rice. I've also had the bibimbap, normal and hot. I would suggest the hot bibimbap (dolsot bibimap) because it makes the rice nice and crispy. Before you get your main food you get the traditional Korean banchan (small side dishes). The ones here are amazing. I sometimes don't like kimchi but this kimchi is very good. Try them all and get free refills on the ones you love! As far as drinks go, they have some alcohol like beer and soju. You can also get some hot tea. 

The prices here range from normal to a little pricey. It really depends on what you order. I believe my soup is usually $11 or 12. The meat is where it can get a little pricey. I know they have to import a lot of their ingredients so I can see why they would have to charge a bit more. However, if you want authentic Korea food, this is your place. My boyfriend is Korean and he gives it two thumbs up. They also offer take-out if you want to eat on the go or order larger amounts for a business party or something.

If you live in Nashville, you've heard of Frothy Monkey. If you're visiting Nashville, it more than likely has popped up on your recommendations. To say it's popular is an understatement. And you will feel this when visiting most of the locations. The 12 South location is a bit smaller but to me has the most charm. It's in an old house (or what I can assume was once a house). There is an outside patio with a few seats and then the inside is one level. There is seating in the front part of the shop and then a side room with more seating. While there are a good number of tables, everything fills up fast. It doesn't matter what time of the week or day you come, this place is busy. To me, this almost deters me from coming here to get work done. It's a bit too clustered and busy for me to focus on something. However, if you're coming here just for the food or coffee and to meet some friends, it's nice. 

I really enjoy Frothy Monkey's drink menu. I don't drink coffee so I appreciate that they offer a nice assortment of delicious non-coffee beverages. During this visit, I tried their seasonal special. It was a sparkling raspberry matcha. It was reallllllllly good. Sometimes matcha can taste too...green?...but with the raspberry and carbonation, it was sweet and bubbly. Perfect for summer and gave me the caffeine kick I needed. I also had a taste of their breakfast. I wanted a little bit of everything so I ordered the Farm Breakfast: 2 farm eggs, bacon, red potatoes, fruit, and toast. It was a lot of food. The best part by far was the bacon. It was thick and slightly crispy. Some of the best bacon I have had. The eggs were...eggs. The toast was also thick and pretty good. I will say I was slightly disappointed with the potatoes. They had little to no flavor. They needed a lot of salt and pepper added to them. It was a good breakfast but I might try something else on the menu next time. Their sandwiches look extra good. A sandwich with that bacon would be heaven. 

If you're willing to fight the crowds and test your luck with getting a table, Frothy Monkey is a nice place to check out. It fits in well to the 12 South neighborhood and the service is always really friendly.

I was very disappointed to see that the casino is charging $10 to park.  I think they're making a huge mistake.  This is by no means a "destination" or upscale casino.   There is really nothing there except a second rate casino.  The restaurants are average at best.  
I read the casino's response to other yelpers commenting on the parking fee.  Claiming that it's to improve security is definitely something I don't want to hear.  What casino doesn't make security a number one priority?  Whether or not they are charging a parking fee should have no bearing on the level of security they are providing to their guests.
Good corner sandwich spot. I've had the Korean BBQ cheesesteak, which I'd recommend, and the chicken cheesesteak with spinach and onion is good too. Mr. Lee is a really nice dude!

This is a terrific little, and I mean little, place.  I'm sad it's in Boise, and not next to my house in Santa Monica.  :( 

They definitely don't need any more glowing reviews, but any place that puts pots of fresh coffee on the sidewalk for the poor bastards sitting outside waiting for a table gets 5 stars in my book.

Rip off food, not worth it's perceived prestige. I hate ripping on crappy dining establishments, but this one I have to put my foot down and be a downer. I got the fish special which unbeknownst to me was charged $38 dollars for. I scrapped the entire fish - it's description of light flakiness was more like extreme rough fishiness. I was waiting for Ashton Kutcher to come out of the corner and tell me I just got punk'd. You may ask, why on earth didn't I take this back? Well, we ordered it go because that's what my husband wanted to do on his birthday. We ordered at to go because we were tired and calling to exchange/complain was too much of a drag and defeated the whole purpose for staying in the comforts of one's own home. One reason why we went to such a swanky place is that we'd expected everything to be perfect. Also, might I add, I arrived at the time they said the food would be ready, but then almost scurried to prepare everything as I sat there waiting for about 20 minutes. 

Continuing on with the food, my husband got the filet mignon which, tiny and expensive. Priced at $36, this steak should have been like butter heaven. Not even close. We split the cheese plate which did not come with everything it was promised to have. The crab cakes were probably the best thing, but not enough to make it a-ok. 
Sadly, my husband regretted his decision to have his birthday dinner (plus $120 blown) made by Farmers Daughter and not Benihana (seriously!).

Rating: 3.5/5.

Food network's advertisements of "Tommy Dinic's" brought me there. The roasted pork broccoli sandwich was more tender and enjoyable than the beef brisket one. 

The highlight of the crowded and touristic Reading terminal market was the honey sampling at "Bee natural". Their raw honey was so delicious and came in so many unusual and interesting flavors! I ended buying a big container, which lasted me years.

The market had a miniature train track, which was a hit with children.

While it was a fine place to get your steps in, nothing was outstanding. I may have been spoiled by places such as the Boston Public Market or Eataly. Those luxuous markets offered more samples and surprising products.

If I were to have lunch there again, I would try the Carmen's shop selling cheese steack sandwiches.

Vegan food in this area of Delco is really hard to come by.  When I read the menu, I was immediately excited to try Frankie's!  I had the Bahn Mi Panini which was delicious and HUGE.  The vegan options come with sweet potato fries, which aren't my thing, but apparently others like them.  

I have had their catering a few times at work.  The sandwich trays, salad, and pasta salad are always a huge hit with everyone.  I have yet to hear anyone say they didn't like something.

Bravo, Frankie's, for offering dishes that are outside the norm for this area!!

I can't even tell you how excited I was when I saw the sign for Pho Street.  We were really in need of something like this around these parts.  I am, by no means, an expert on Vietnamese cuisine but I am a huge fan of Fu Wah's tofu bahn mi and Pho from several places in Philly. 

Since Pho Street opened, I have tried their pho, bahn mi, spring rolls, bun, and summer rolls.  They have always been happy to sub tofu for meat, when possible, and have recently added a veg spring roll, tofu bahn mi, and tofu pho to their menu.  Big clap for that!

I have probably had Pho Street's grub a dozen times now and have always walked away happy!  Keep it up!

Yea, I too had a problem with inattentive service.  Looking for the server, waving down a passerby server or bus-person for assistance or refills, refilling your wine glass after dropping a small fortune on the bottle, is not something one should have to do in a restaurant of this caliber with 5 star food, stuffy ambiance and big price tab.

That being said, the food was excellent, top 10 in the city, and I expected such after being to Bibou.  The food delivered on my expectations.  The service did not.  And, the stuffy ambiance is just not my type, I prefer Bibou's coziness and quaintness, but that is just my personal preference. 

For appetizers we had a fish (arctic char) mouse stuffed ravioli with the perfect amount of truffle flavor in the light  but most delicious wine sauce.  And the foie gras was magnificent, so silky, so melt in your mouth, so delicately rich.  

There was a Dover Sole entree for 2, de-boned tableside which was amazing in tenderness and gentle flavors of sauce which was drizzled to your liking.  The sides were a chopped asparagus, crisp and tasty, a clever way to serve asparagus in my opinion, and  a Parisian gnocci.  The gnocci were fabulous in their own right, tender, soft mashed potato rolled, cut and pan seared to excellence.  I could eat them every day.

My honey-almond creme brulee was a great choice, as was the poached plum, goat cheese, port wine tart served with honey ice cream.  The latter was difficult to eat however, first of all only being served with a fork, and secondly the plum slices were so firm they had to be cut to mouth-size with a knife.

Overall, I am a big fan.  If they deliver on consistent service and if you are looking for a large, formal dining experience, then you have perfection.

OK, I have to get over my dislike of Bridget's in Ambler to write a fair review of this place.  I used to frequent The Blue Bell Inn in the 90's and 2000's under old ownership, where the food was a consistent 'superb', the steaks melted in your mouth and the calves liver was decadent and tender like soft butter.

I heard about the interior remodel, the new entrance, the outdoor patio, etc. awhile ago and just this past week decided to grab a friend and get some drinks at happy hour to give it a shot.  

I must first say that the service at the back bar was excellent, with a positive attitude and desire to assist in beer and wine selections.  And the choices of beer and wine available were very good.  That was a great way to start off.  Catching up with an old friend is most difficult on servers as they never know when you want something, ready to order or how long you are going to want to be there.  There was NO problem whatsoever for our server, she got it, adapted and served with a smile.

We ordered a couple of small plates.  The boneless chicken tenders with crumbles of blue cheese and tangy hot sauce were A-OK, and the flatbread special with shredded short rib and arugula was just-OK.  Not much short rib, not much arugula and the crust a little soggy from sitting in it's own condensation from the heat on the plate.  I wouldn't order the flatbread again, but the chicken could be a repeat.  

Other than a couple beers and a couple of wines and those two small plates, that's all we tried the first time back.  I was pleasantly pleased with the service and the new digs.  I will have to return for a full dinner and see how that goes.

I was the 2nd youngest person in the place from 5:30 till 8:30 last night, and I ain't no spring chicken.  The blue hairs were abound, the wrinkles, the hobbling along, the creak of old bones, where life is no longer giving, only taking away.  And that includes half of the wait staff.  Good for them.  I  too ain't just sittin' around waiting for the grim reaper!

Anyway, went to the bar for these reasons:
1)hardly anyone sits at the bar, I guess a bar stool is too high for the shrinking old people to climb, and no safety rails
2)it was very quiet, like at a funeral, so I could hear the very private conversation of a great friend without asking her to speak up
3)beer selection on tap was very good
4)no one I know would see me there, as anyone I know at those ages are already dead

In addition to the West Coast Green Flash I was sucking down, we split two apps.  The fried bang bang shrimp was tasty, too much bread coating, but not too greasy.  The mini crab cake bites were very good, great tender pieces of crab, not much else other than crab.  Well, I heard they are known for their crab cakes, and they delivered.  Service at the bar was good, the bartender had nothing better to do. ;-)

Boy, I haven't been here in at least 6 months and they obviously missed me,  the place was empty and the food was suffering.  

The beers on tap, while a decent selection, tasted funny, like they have to clean out the taps.  Don't they know this?

The couple of app's we ordered were enough to call it quits.  The wings have taken a nosedive, tough chicken, no excuse.  The hummus was ehhhh, blah.  That was enough for us.  Outta here, hopefully not to return anytime soon, or until I at least see a crowd again.

It hit me like a lightning bolt as to why I haven't returned here in many years when I used to frequent this restaurant in a historic building(s) located in a secluded setting off of the busy RT 463.  (This is also a B & B, with a couple of small cottages surrounding the main buildings).  Why?  It was the service and the priorities of the servers.  Deja vu all over again.  :-P 

There is a room off to the side of the main dinning room in which there seemed to be a private party going on.  This dark hole sucked our server in never to be seen again. Our server, although very polite in the beginning of the evening before that side room filled up, couldn't help very much with our selections, didn't understand a simple cocktail order and thus got one of the drink orders wrong, and then couldn't be found AT ALL once our appetizer was served.  The rest of the evening was spent waving down one of the many, and hard working I might add, bus-people "can you please find our waitress".   Still nothing.  I wanted another drink, couldn't find anyone.  I wanted another  piece of grain bread (very small chunks  of bread were offered at the beginning of the evening,  I needed another, and it was good).  After dinner plates were cleared, the dessert menu was dropped off and no one returned for at least 20 minutes to see if we wanted to order something.  There was a manager, or hostess, or some other server, I couldn't tell as they all dressed the same, who was kind and listened to my explanation of the lack of service, and she did comp our drinks and dessert, but the excuse given to me was that our server has been busy with this private party.  Not a very good excuse for me to have to beg for service throughout the evening.  Whatever!  1 star service

The food:  An excellent black bean and sausage soup du jour started off the evening.  It was very spicy and I like it just like that.  And served in a large white bowl, just this serving of dark brown colored thick soup against the plain whiteness.  Without getting too picky, it could have used a little garnish, even just chopped parsley, the presentation lacked, but the flavor delivered. 4 stars

Entrees: I had the pan roasted Chilean sea bass with a lump crab and sweet pea risotto.  The medium sized piece of fish was cooked properly, nice crisp sear on the outside and tender white meat within.  The risotto was overcooked, the flavor was OK, the peas were crisp, but the little bit of "lump" (ha) crab was almost mush. 3 stars 

My date for the evening ;-) had ordered the Maine lobster cake.  It was very good, I tasted it of course, nice lobster flavor served with wilted arugula, fennel basmati rice with a lobster reduction.  4 stars

We shared a piece of caramel apple cheesecake for dessert, the cheesecake itself was creamy, delightful, excellent, the caramel was an OK add, but there was only two 1/4 inch dice of the apple to be found.  Maybe the apple was also serving other people in that private party.  Who the hell knows.

I was running a mercy call for a friend, and dog knows I do that without thought, it's my nature to do shit for people, even people who are a pain in my ass, when I came across this cute little pub right across the street from the train station.  Lunch was on my mind.

Beer selection I thought was OK, could have been better, but I was in the Northeast where I think Guinness is still considered a craft beer.

Another OK experience was the Italian grilled chicken wrap...fresh, interesting.  Of course the best part of the dish was the potato chips... thick, dark, crispy.

My friend had the Gluten-free Cajun turkey burger with sriracha mayo on a gluten-free bun.  Again, OK I was told.

The place itself was cute/pub-y, with monkeys hanging around.  Looks like they have a nice outdoor patio, but it was too cold to sit outside.  And if I ever am in the Northeast again I may stop in.  It's not cheap but tell me where it is cheap these days.

"bop" is definitely an attempt to lure those millennials who (1) do not have a sophisticated palate (2) are attracted to the "cover" but not the contents of the book (3) who run up the steps of the Philadelphia Museum of Art but never go in.

Yep, the food is similar to any other Asian infusion place you've been.  The decor is attractive,  atmosphere open and lively, especially during happy hour.  You will see hot young women with middle aged guys, young couples with wrinkled shirts and skinny jeans, the air of the beautiful people who want to be seen.  But beyond that, food and beverage are average.

There are no draft beers, but an OK selection of bottles.  The service was efficient and overall very good but came with "attitude".  However, I know that waiting on a group of 6 or more is sometimes difficult and the server has to be assertive to get the job done.

For food, we ordered a bunch of items to share.
Cheesesteak eggrolls -- 4 stars... Very good, would order again
Wings-- 2 stars...Large in size, but "sweet" dominates; and overcooked/stringy/tough
Rock shrimp -- 2 stars...  Decent flavor but shrimp was overcooked
Edamame ravioli -- 3 stars... Similar to any other dumpling
Bulgogi -- 3 stars...Nothing new here
Stir Fry -- 3 stars...All stir fry tastes the same

Don't get me wrong, other than a couple items being overcooked, the food was fresh and presented well.  It just wasn't special.  I will return for drinks at the bar and try another few things on the menu.  Location, location, location!

Megaphone to the kitchen staff:  When management chooses to list the ingredients one by one on the menu, make sure you include them in the freakin;' dish!!!!!  Mother of dog!!!  The "Florentine" salad lists fresh spinach, pine nuts, golden raisins, croutons and Gorgonzola cheese, in a sherry orange vinaigrette.   There was NO Gorgonzola cheese NOR pine nuts in the salad served to us.   NOTTA!   Also, there was absolutely very little flavor in the dressing, you could have fooled me that there was anything orange or sherry flavored in it.   We were not off to a good start.  

My gorgeous blonde dining partner for the evening, one of the few intelligent blondes I know,  and I also split the gnocci appetizer in a browned butter sauce.  The gnocci had a nice sear on them, but they were very mushy and had NO taste whatsoever.  Good thing there were sundried tomatoes and pancetta  in the dish, the couple of things which actually had their own flavor to tickle the tongue.

The pizza was very very good.  We ordered the "Frankie" artisanal pizza with spicy pork sausage, sundried tomato, pesto, tomato sauce, basil & mozzarella.  It had a great thin crust and excellent meld of flavors.  Let me give that pizza 4 stars for that area of the burbs.

Service was there, not helpful, just there.

I will return for the pizza/beer/wine and nothing else.  Maybe takeout will accomplish the same thing.

Happy Hour review -- 5 PM to 7 PM

A friend wanted to show me how great this place was for happy hour.  It was not.  What WAS "great" was Christine, the bartender for the evening.  She was the only person servicing the entire restaurant and busy bar at happy hour.  And she is very professional, not overwhelmed, attentive and generally a nice person.

An average beer selection, with some having happy hour pricing, and some not.  What was a bargain was a top shelf martini for $6.  You will not beat that anywhere. 

Now for the happy hour food, there is a small menu with, what looked like, an adequate selection.  But to simplify the reality of it, there were no bargains here.  Everything, although priced lower, was a small serving in proportion to a regular size.  The old adage, you get what you pay for, about sums it up.  For example, wings with thai sweet chili sauce were 5 wings for $7, that's over a buck a piece, and they were average at best, the best part was the sauce, the wing itself was small and chewy.  The spicy tuna roll was small, not much to it in ingredients nor flavor. Nothing stood out as a do over.  The fish was fresh, but in my opinion, nothing was special in prep nor flavor.

Blue Fin in Plymouth Meeting has it all over this place for food.  If it wasn't for the discounted martini thing, and the $3 drafts I would not see any reason to return.

From the smartest bartender, to the wonderful, creative food and presentation, M proved to me it is worthy of 5 stars.

Starting with the cheese plate, 6 choices from soft to hard, the selection was perfect.  Presented by the cheese sommelier with an introduction of each, added to the anticipation of which proved to be an extreme highlight.

The "cavatelli and fiori pasta" had both rich and fresh flavors, which made your palate yearn for the next dish.  And so it came, the short rib.  Tender, no fat, melt in your mouth, warm, delectable, comforting and probably the best short rib this side of Gramercy Tavern in NYC.  

The wine list was not overwhelming and not extensive...so be it.  The selection was adequate.

A varied crowd, from old to young, but certainly respectable and relaxed "up scale".  Perfect for a Saturday evening.

Oh my, I am going back for more.  I loved this place.

What's all the fuss about this place?  Drinks and food, for what you get, are expensive, flatbreads are overpriced and overrated, and the entrees have low flavor in keeping with the low calories bullshit.  

A mediocre start with the beer selection and the bartenders, who think they're "cool".  A sexy ass doesn't make you cool, your service and attention to the customer does.  They are found staring over your head at who is around the bar then who is at it.

The $12 flatbread is quickly becoming old.  I would say the cost of making one of these is about $2.  And Season's 52 is no exception, sounds good on paper not translating to the plate nor the palate.

The Tiger shrimp dish over penne pasta was bland.  The scallops were boring.  Do we need fat to add flavor?   

And on a Friday night, it was a fair crowd but not the wait I read about here.  I guess the fad is passing.

Don't waste your time and bucks, not worth it!

Let me see, hmmmm, "I've experienced better" (Yelp's "two star" description) at almost everywhere, including, but not limited to, other Vetri places.

When I walked in, I actually liked the cafeteria style long tables, it made me feel like I was in for a NYC fine pizza experience.  Even ordering an overpriced, lightweight, 500 ml carafe of their house Sangiovese made the anticipation climb...pizza and red, can't get better than that, right?

We had the Heirloom tomato salad to start.  I'd have to say the baby kale was tender and not bitter, with a nice balsamic reduction.  The tomatoes were average in taste and the small ones, not the meaty heirloom tomatoes to which one may be accustomed.  And the flatbread served with the salad was totally worthless, dry, stale, tough to chew.

Then came the bubble buster, the friggin pizza.  We ordered the  Salsiccia (fennel sausage, roasted fennel, mozzarella and tomato sauce).  If there was 3 oz of sausage on the entire pizza, I would be surprised.  Other than a couple sprigs of fennel for decor, the roasted fennel was absent any taste, let alone a roasted flavor.  The tomato sauce was nice and light.  But the beautiful looking thin crust was soooooo soggy, you couldn't lift it up, it required a knife and a fork.  Wet crust sucks!!!!!!!!!

There is a way to avoid that from happening, serve it on a raised mesh screen, this will prevent the crust from steaming.

I have no reason to return here.  Now over at Osteria, they know what they're doing.  ;-)

This was my first trip up da street to this newly opened pub in downtown Maple Glen :-) .  There's a large rectangular bar with TV's all over the place, hooks for your bags and outlets for your phone chargers under the bar are really nice touch.  Tables to the right as you walk in, but I won't be needing them.

As far as the food goes, the Brick and Barrel wings "tossed" with rosemary and onions were OK, a little too wet for my liking.  The wings weren't jumbo like the menu stated and the onions were smothering the wings on the plate.  The wild mushroom pizza with smoked provolone and truffle oil had a nice crust and flavor, not mind blowing as I expected.  

Service at the bar was excellent and the draft beer selection very good too, plenty to chose from.

Glad I found a new hangout close to home.  I got tired of the old dirty Fireside Bar in Ambler with less than necessary parking and I exhausted the menu at Tex-Mex in North Wales.  So this is a welcome addition to the neighborhood.  But I still miss the Drafting Room.  :-(

Last night (07/12/2019), the oldest pub in the City that Loves You Back enforced an illegal policy that discriminates against the LGBTQ community. 

I happened to be in Philly for my birthday, and after some research, I chose McGillin's as the venue for my celebration, since it was near the Convention Center. George was super helpful with the planning and Nate was super helpful on the day of, getting us set up in the upstairs bar.

All was well...until one of my guests needed to use the bathroom, and was denied access. Upon protesting, she was asked for ID, which I was repeatedly told is policy at McGillin's. Somewhere around this time is when this guest, who is transgender, found me and asked for help. After an extended negotiation that was heavily informed by my cisgender privilege, the security staff held a huddle before they ultimately decided to allow her to use the bathroom--but only after they emptied it out of all other patrons, and stood guard to make sure nobody else entered while she was inside.

It was far from ideal, but my guest had been trying to pee for about half an hour at this point, so she used the bathroom under these humiliating circumstances. Ultimately, my guest and two others, were forcibly removed, compounding their embarrassment. This effectively ended my party, as nobody in my group cared to remain in such a climate.

I knew in the moment that this was wrong and discriminatory, but what I now know, by the light of this morming after, is that it was illegal.

From Philadelphia's official government website:

"In Philadelphia, it is illegal for employers, housing providers, businesses, providers of public accommodations and City services to discriminate against anyone because of their gender identity, sex, or sexual orientation. People can use any bathroom consistent with their gender identity and any single occupancy bathroom in a retail establishment must have gender neutral signage."

When I visited McGillin's earlier in the week to see if it might work for my celebration, I noticed a Pride flag outside, as well as marketing materials (coasters) touting the bar's support of the LGBTQ year round, not just during Pride. I was happy to see such things as I value inclusivity above all else. As a person of color, I have to.

Most of the staff, at least in their interactions with me, did seem as though they were just toeing the company line, even if they didn't necessarily agree with the policies. However, that wasn't enough to save my guest from being humiliated, and it doesn't make these events any less illegal. One staff member, however, insisted that the city's law doesn't apply to the establishment, saying they were "grandfathered in." Surely there is no "grandfather clause" for discrimination like this. 

It's also worth noting that McGillin's doesn't have an ADA-compliant restroom.

A police report was filed by my guest immediately, and next steps are being contemplated. This is not how anyone should be treated, anywhere. I'm still in shock over this blatant human rights violation. Nobody should have their rights debated and trampled in this manner. 

Philadelphia's legendary spirit of "brotherly love" apparently doesn't exist in McGillin's, if you're trans. What a disgusting display of bigotry.

The website is so aggravating. 

I have been to the Roadhouse about 10 times. The seats are comfy, the drinks are good, I love that they have Cashew Cow, the food is acceptable (if not great), and the service is generally good. That all puts it up in the 4-5 star range for me -- maybe more like a 4 since it is pretty pricey and I am a fan of the Loft. 

BUT! There is a really big but that knocks the experience down: the loathsome website. What are the problems? Showtimes are listed out and you have to click through a screen to choose the number of tickets and then...(spinning icon forever)...sold out. Or only front row seats on the sides. Okay, let's try another showtime: click 'Change Tickets' and it dumps you back on the main page. Click 'Change Show' and it does the same. Huh?

For a newer release or on weekends, this means clicking through then being disappointed and starting over again and again and again. On top of that, the site itself is clunky and slow even beyond the spinning icon. How hard could it be to grey out times for sold out shows? Or perhaps have the page list the available seat charts for multiple shows in one day? It is an inefficient and poorly designed purchase process that often makes me reluctant to choose Roadhouse, especially when there is something new I am excited to see. Oh well, off to the Loft.

Nirvana. Arcadia. Heaven. Perfection.  These words do not properly describe The Flying Pig.  

If you love...I mean love in a way that some would call unnatural...pubs, traditional bars, or good old fashioned watering holes...you will love The Flying Pig.  If you go to some crappy chain place where you can get 3.99 buffalo wings and 2 dollar draft bud...then you will hate The Flying Pig...and guess what...The Flying Pig hates you.

The Flying Pig is for people who want to watch sports, listen to a great jukebox and drink some of the finest beer this planet has to offer. Yes, you will pay 5,6, sometimes 7 bucks for a pint...and if you believe in the healing power of beer...you will know that it is a cheap price to pay. 

The food is good, I wouldn't say outstanding, but it is very good. The sandwiches are excellent, the mozzarella sticks were great, and the cheese fries were good, but not crisp enough.  The food is all about one dollar too much for what you get, but it is what it is. 

They have at least 6 or 7 tv's to watch the games, the decor is rustic and comforting.  

This is one of the finest bars I have ever been in...and I have been in a lot!

Pica's Italian Restaurant fell into my lap unexpectedly like all great things...classic novel, fine wine, or a big bottle of propranolol and a comfy pillow...you know, the great things.

One day I am walking out of this bar, as I am one to do...I am drunk, as I am one to be, and I am holding a Domino's pizza bag, hat, and a huge clump of hair from a delivery boy, as I am one to do. I am cursing, as always...I am angry...as always...I am gorgeous...as always.

I am muttering something about the fall of civilization, the lack of quality, the death of true artists when this beautiful girl walks up to me. She is amazing. A vision.  She gently takes the items out of my hands and hugs me...pressing me hard against her breasts...I smiled...I was in.  She whispered something sweetly in a french accent with seriously heavy lisp...it was disturbing...I, Rex Marvin, was disturbed...am disturbed...but more disturbed.

She led my by the hand to her car where she performed the most acrobatic love maneuvers a woman can perform. After 6 minutes of passion she was unsatisfied and hungry.  She told me would eat at her favorite place...we pulled up to Pica's...as I got out she screamed something about my manhood...I don't think it was nice...something about a thumb...and drove away. Truthfully I was glad, she looked like heaven but sounded like Porky Pig...it was all too much...much too much.

I went inside and ordered their famous pizza. It was a revelation. Cheese on the bottom, sauce on top and a great slice of real deli pepperoni.  I ate the whole pie. 

Over the next few times I tried the fried ravioli, several pasta dishes (veal in red sauce being the best), and various appetizers.  The food was always good.  It is not great, but the food all seems to be made with care and pride, and that goes a long way.

I wouldn't go too far out of my way for anything except the pizza, which earned this place an extra star, but it is a good place to eat if you are near by.

I saw that girl again...she cried. I cried. She licked my tears. I confessed my love..."I love you, Porky" I whispered..."I love you, Thumb."  Four days letter she moved back to France and took my favorite blow up Betty White Golden Girls love doll.  C'est La Vie.

This place is way over priced and really needs to work on details. The "surf and turf" consisted of a small, unevenly cooked filet on par with what is served at a budget steakhouse. One end was well done, and the center was underdone. The filet came with scallops that had the strangest metallic after taste and we're also not cooked right. Two were overdone and two were underdone. This combo was explained by our waitress as a combination. However, the price was the two separate entrees added together. If this is the policy, then I should have gotten double the sides too! Oh, and lest I forget: the Manhattan style lobster chowder consisted of a runny, herbal broth with chunks of veg-all and rubbery "lobster." This really disappoints me as I love local restaurants and this one was highly recommended. I doubt I will try it again.

The day before dining at Mr Ed's I'd sat beside a local who gave this advice:  "In any restaurant, always ask what their specialty is, what they're known for, then get it".  

Here was the answer to that question:

"Louisiana Crawfish Bread and Charbroiled Oysters"  

During Mardi Gras, we couldn't find Louisiana Crawfish Bread ($10.95) on the shortened, though still extensive, menu they were serving.  They made it for us anyhow.  Indulgently rich, this is definitely something worth trying but be careful:  with a base of bread, this starter might overfill you.  It's an amount probably best suited for 3 though 2 of us vacationers had no problem consuming the entire 1/2 loaf.  

I couldn't bring myself to order Charbroiled Oysters (with garlic butter & parmesan, $18.95/dozen) as my love is the raw stuff.  Here at Mr Ed's, the raw Gulf Oysters are presented beautifully (Acme, take note) and as if the shucker understood the way to my heart, I was delivered 14 oysters when I'd ordered a mere dozen ($14.95).  What Gulf oysters lack in brine they make up for in size.  Beautiful specimens, all, and one of the best reasons to head to NOLA.  

I admired the size of the Catfish Po' Boy ($13.95) which is served here without fries.  As the server said "there's lots of bread though", and she wasn't joking.  If you're starting with the Crawfish Bread and moving on from there, perhaps a platter rather than a Po' Boy is a better option.  By the end, the filling was being pulled out of the Po' Boy and the bread left for dead on the plate.  

Mr Ed's did an admirable job of operating efficiently and effectively while serving the mobs of Mardi Gras-goers.  I sat at the bar/counter (recommended) and enjoyed observing how staff were handling requests like "2 Hurricanes, more rum, less juice" and offering to-go cups and top-offs on those drinks which outlasted a meal.  

Mr Ed's, I'm told, is a small, local chain serving very good and satisfying fare.  A lot of other places in town serve similar menus but as you try to get through them all, Mr Ed's should definitely be on your list.

In the era of "ethical eating", where "food is politics", I feel like I should announce my love of Luke while hiding my identity.  For those unaware, Luke is one of the restaurants in the John Besh empire and this empire was reported, in a 2017 article in the Times-Picayune, to "foster a culture of sexual harassment".

I assume that the problems reported have been addressed by now, 2019, and don't wish to perpetually punish the restaurant, its workers, or the general public by simply pretending that Luke doesn't exist.  

Luke exists and has an amazingly satisfying happy hour.

Served in a sparkly atmosphere with a buzzy vibe, Luke was my favorite happy hour experience in NOLA.  One dozen fried oysters ($15), 3 dozen raw oysters ($27: 75 cents apiece), Jalapeño Grits ($5), Crispy Potatoes ($5), Crawfish Bisque (bowl $10), and Bread Pudding ($9), there was nothing not to adore here.  Did it help that the Champagne was half off during happy hour as well?  At $4.50 per glass, you can bet that added to the joy.  

Luke's happy hour (4-6 daily) is popular.  Arriving a bit past 4 p.m. I waited for a seat until 5 p.m., when more tables were opened up.  The wait is worth it:  75 cent Gulf Oysters and 1/2 price alcohol are worth waiting for.

I love a happening atmosphere in a busy, buzzy place with decor that makes me feel special.  Luke has all that and good deals to match.

Soleil Ho, the San Francisco Chronicle's newly anointed restaurant critic, has already introduced many changes to the practice of restaurant critique.  One of the most noteworthy changes is the new "no star" policy, which leads one to actually have to read and intuit.  

Here on yelp I have no such option and though I mostly enjoyed the food at Sukho Thai, I'd be unlikely to return were I making a repeat visit to NOLA.  Why?  Despite Thai food which was quite satisfying, I was put off by the staff who spent their between-serving time sitting around the bar area engaging with their phones.  The service might not have suffered but my impression of the service did; diddling with your phone during working hours and in plain view of diners shows disrespect to diners and the job and influences the way I feel about a place.  In essence, it is "goofing off".  

After leaving a tip upwards of 20% I walked down Frenchman Street and stopped to watch a fabulously talented 6-person band (Holy Locust) and regretted that I couldn't leave even half that amount for a larger group of talented people more engaged with the public they're trying to reach.  

Off of my high horse, but this is my long-winded way of saying that this review would be 4-star were it based solely on the food.  

Forget about the Fresh Rolls ($7.95).  They are vegan and I'd say tasteless, but whatever taste they imparted - there was some - was not great.  The Green Papaya Salad ($8.95) fared better; a simple version of a classic with nothing to highly recommend it but a most acceptable version nonetheless.  

My favorite parts of the order were the Drunken Fried Rice ($12.95, with beef) which was wok-fried in a spicy chili-paste and featured sweet basil, garlic, onion, bell pepper, broccoli, cabbage and egg.  A Red Curry ($13.95, with chicken) also proved to be a nicely satisfying version.  For both of these we got to specify heat level and taking it one notch below super-hot, our noses ran and our taste buds danced.  

The above food proved adequate for 3 people though none of the servings looked, on their own, to be very substantial.  

Were one living in the area, I imagine that this Thai place would be an attractive variance from the heavier fare typically found in town.  Perhaps in that case, as a weeknight neighborhood joint, I'd also not mind seeing staff cuddling up with their electronic devices after taking my order.  But I'm a tourist, always will be here, and I expect more out of service professionals:  Put down the phones.

With its shelves of jars filled with fermenting vegetables and a dry aging space for proteins, Maypop feels very current.  Its servers express pride and enthusiasm in what they lay before you, from the surprise amuse-bouche starter right through to the complimentary dessert nibbles at the end.  I felt nothing but happiness the whole time I was at Maypop and somehow, that also seemed to mirror the feeling I got from every worker there.

It was my intention to have dinner at Maypop but I arrived earlier than planned and during their happy hour (M-F 4-6 p.m).  Though the dinner menu was available, the happy hour menu is a great deal and a fabulous introduction to the place.  I went with the "we'll try everything on the HH menu" approach.  We did, and then we tried a little more.  No wonder I had such fun at Maypop.  

Cream Cheese & Pepper Jelly Toasts, sounds pretty basic until you read that it is actually whipped cream cheese and shellfish pepper jam atop grilled Annatto bread ($4).  Spicy Marinated Cucumbers ($3) were marinated with Thai Chilis, topped with sesame and puffed rice and were such a blast of flavor and texture that I ordered a second serving.  

Two versions of Steamed Buns (Shrimp & Ginger Ravigote and Laotian Chicken Sausage/Turnip Kimchi/Spicy Ailoi) will do the heavy lifting toward filling your stomach.  At $3 each during happy hour, overlook them at your own peril. The Shrimp Steamed Buns merited a second serving though both versions are excellent.  

Vindaloo Curry Hot Wings & Marinated Cucumber ($7) with added Coconut Ranch ($1) completed my tour of Maypop's happy hour food menu, leading me to conclude that this restaurant well understands how to make optimal use of their ferments and deliver big pops of flavor.  

During happy hour, beer is $4, wine is $5, and a couple specialty cocktails are offered at $6.  Even looking at the happy hour alcohol specials it's clear that the choices are well thought out.

I might've recently proclaimed that another place served up my favorite happy hour in NOLA but I should've clarified.  They were my favorite raw oyster happy hour, a category in which Maypop doesn't compete.  Maypop was my favorite non-oyster happy hour and I loved every minute of it.

Dumb luck can still be good luck.  It was dumb luck that my NOLA home for the week was in the Marigny, not the French Quarter, a mere block from the wonders of Frenchman Street.  In the other direction, a few blocks deeper into Marigny, there were riches to be found, New Orleans Cake Cafe & Bakery amongst them.  

This is the sort of place that you wander by in the late morning and do a "hmmm... why are there so many people here?" then wander inside.  You might get a little sweet something and a little savory something as we did.  You might also anoint it with the words "we're coming back here for breakfast before we leave".  

At NOCC&B you order at the counter and food is brought to your table.  The menu is enticing, the place feels like a labour of love, and all of the little sweet treats they make can derail you.  My son insisted on eating something while waiting for his breakfast then pronounced himself too full to continue midway through his Fried Catfish Sandwich.  I can attest to the don't-miss flavors of the Corned Beef Hash and the fresh-made Boudin with eggs was a runner-up.  

This is the sort of place you wish was right down the street from your home.  For one week, it was, and the mere thought of that just makes me happy.  

Good place.

Woke up this dreary Sunday morning and thought to ourselves, "Selves, today seems like a great day for a delicious and relaxing breakfast."  We really disappointed ourselves, as Winslow's Home offers neither of those things.  It started by ordering at the back counter.  We felt very rushed, as there were people waiting behind us and the cashier seemed to push us to order.  I remembered reading that the breakfast sandwich was good, so I went with that and a coffee.  My girlfriend went with the breakfast burrito and a coffee.  $22 later, we had a number and two coffee mugs.  Time to wander around the store/restaurant aimlessly until a table opened up.  Nothing like being in the way and having nowhere else to go.  Just what we wanted to do right after rolling out of bed.  After finding a dirty table that took about 10 minutes to be cleared off, we came to realize just how annoying this place is.  It's like sitting at The Cheesecake Factory or something.  Loads of women squawking about wedding plans and the horrible outfits that their friends wore on Friday night.  My head still hurts.  At least I had the food to look forward to, right?  Wrong.  Although the quality of ingredients appeared to be excellent, the sandwich itself was extremely dry and bland.  I mentioned to my girlfriend that an Egg McMuffin is a much tastier breakfast sandwich than whatever this thing was.  Her breakfast burrito was equally as boring.  After eating these small and overpriced meals, we commented on how good the coffee was.  We had no desire to get a refill though, as we couldn't bear to stay another minute in this place.

Adriana's is another St. Louis sandwich shop worthy of a visit.  There can be a long slow moving line during peak lunch hours.  I usually visit in the summer when I am less rushed and outdoor seating is available.

My favorite item on Adriana's Menu is the Gorgonzola Dip.  The Gorgonzola Dip is served on crusty seeded Italian bread toasted with beef and melted Gorgonzola Cheese.  Dip this sandwich in Au Jus and you will be happy all afternoon.  The salad comes dressed heavy.   

#EatLocal

Absolutely fantastic coffee.  Sump is a go to coffee shop for a jolt of caffeine.  I especially appreciate the Cold Brew at this location.  You can buy coffee beans and drinks at Sump.  Sump is currently only taking online orders for coffee and delivering them to you curbside.  In this very scary time, this curbside pick-up option is appreciated.  You can text on arrival, for someone to bring your coffee or coffee beans out to you in your car.  Thank You Sump for going the extra mile during this Covid pandemic.

Casa Juárez is a very large Mexican Restaurant and Bar.  When you enter, you find yourself inside a huge Gift Shop with Mexican Decor, Day of the Dead Sugar Skulls, and more.  Keep walking to the right and you will find the Hostess Stand.  If you want to sit at the bar, it is first come first serve.  The bar area has high top tables, bar seating, and weather permitting a very large outdoor patio.

Casa Juárez can accommodate large families, office parties, and girl's/guy's night out.  They have a private room and in the main dining area table after table than can be put together for big numbers of guests.  Each time I have been the service has been amazing.  The employees all work well together in an organized way.  Café Juarez has thought of many nice touches such as charging outlets in all of the booths.  

Casa Juárez is one huge fiesta.  On Weekend Nights, a Tequila Cart goes from table to table with an array of Shot options.  Margaritas from Slider Size to Pitchers are available in a variety of flavors frozen or on the rocks.  I will return to work my way through the margarita list.

When a food establishment makes you crave leftovers...it is TO DIE FOR!

SOTS is hands down- amazing.  The food is fresh, innovative, well prepared, and delicious.  Portions are large.  I only eat half of my calzone so I can relish in delight with leftovers a day or two after a visit.   

The salads at SOTS are very good.  If I worked closer I could see just having a salad lunch now and then.  Fresh, filling ingredients and well paired dressing.  SOTS is worth a trip for salad alone.  

Now let's get to the calzones.  They have a monthy special, SOTS Creations, and The Fold.  The Fold is a Create Your Own Calzone.  It comes with two cheeses and you go from there.  The sauce is literally ON THE SIDE.  Choose carefully from their list of sauces.  They have about ten to choose from.  The calzones are big enough to share---but I warn you---you will want your own.  My fork would be up as a battle weapon to anyone trying to come near my Calzone.  I think the Figgy Piggy is my ultimate favorite- but it is hard to say...

The Mud House makes long workdays much more pleasant.  We order Take Out from the Mud House often.  Every order has always been correct and well packaged.  I love the Breakfast Sandwiches, The Club Sandwich, and The Strawberry Fields Salad.  If I dine in at the Mud House I have to order French Toast.  Their French Toast is warm, buttery, and topped with fresh fruit.  The Mud House uses high quality ingredients.  I look forward to my next visit.

Antonino's is a staple in the St. Louis Hills Neighborhood.  It sits at the corner of Macklind and Dempsey Avenues.  Antonino's is able to handle everything from two person dates to large family dinners and private parties.  The interior is warm and welcoming.

Antonino's serves a mixture of Italian and Greek foods.  The Toasted Ravioli is one of the items that people travel from all around to try.  Toasted Ravioli are warm pillows filled with meat, cheese, spices fried to perfection and served with Marinara Sauce.  These will make any St. Louisan proud.  Bread Service was included with our order.  The Chicken Parmesan Sandwich and Buffalo Chicken Sandwich are large and in charge.  Both Sandwiches come with a side and could easily be shared.  I had leftovers from this meal.  

I hope to return soon to try some Pasta Dishes.

Ranch Lovers...Twisted Ranch is now open for LUNCH ONLY.  Current hours are Tuesday-Sunday 11:00-3:00.  They will be adding evening hours in the near future.  

Here is a fact- I am not sure I have ever requested a side of Ranch in my entire life.  I am a full on Buffalo Hot Sauce type of girl.  Twisted Ranch has a Homemade Buffalo Ranch!!!  They have Avacado Ranch, Bacon Cheddar Ranch, Garlic Ranch, Southwest Ranch...and on and on...   Sandwiches come with fries or a side salad.  There is no up charge for a side salad with your sandwich (very cool).   Sandwiches come with one Homemade Ranch Sauce and the side comes with a second Homemade Ranch Sauce.  

Now let me talk about the Twisted Ranch French Fries.  Holy wow!  The team at Twisted Ranch sprinkles Dry Ranch Powder on the French Fries!!!  Do you hear me...I think these may have been my favorite fries ever.  I ate every single French Fry on my plate (don't tell anyone).  I had fun dipping my fries in the Buffalo Ranch and the Greek Ranch. 

I cannot wait to go back and try more of the flavor combinations at Twisted Ranch.  Great new, locally owned place in Soulard.  Plenty of street parking.  Check them out soon!

We had a group of 13 for dinner and felt like we were at home as we ate. The chicken tenders and fried chicken is better than the famous Nashville chicken (I was just in Nashville, and this is much, much better). Chef Lewis has studied and perfected food service and makes even picky eaters clean their plates.

The groups favorites this times were the Chicken Tenders, Fried Chicken, Greens, Fried Green Tomatoes, and Nothing But The Kitchen Sink Salad. No one had any leftovers because it was so good we had to finish it there.

The staff was amazing even helping us seat all 13 people together. There was constant walk-up business at the window and the staff handled all of the patrons with ease. I will be back soon.

Seamus McDaniel's in Dogtown is a St. Louis staple.  There is a small parking lot in the back and street parking all around.  

Walk into Seamus McDaniel's and immediately feel at ease.  From single diners to large groups, Seamus has a seat for you.  There is bar seating, table seating, booth seating, and even patio/enclosed patio seating depending the time of year.

I recommend the Buffalo Chicken Sandwich or Burgers.  Ranch is King at Seamus; you must try their homemade Ranch Dressing.  Fries dipped in Ranch Dressing are a total win.  Caramelized Onions make the burgers that much better.  I will be back soon.

Ernesto's Wine Bar is a true neighborhood gem.  This is the perfect location to enjoy wine.

Stop by for Ernesto's Happy Hour.  You can have intimate conversations is this small, quaint, and romantic bar.  Ernesto's offers wine flights, by the glass, or whole bottle service.  

During the Spring and Summer the patio makes a great spot for conversations.  

My favorite Menu Item is the Ernesto Flatbread.  Goat Cheese, Figs, Prosciutto, Baby Greens and Balsamic Reduction baked on Flatbread just pairs with my wine choice perfectly.  

It is really hard to leave Ernesto's.  It is a fun place to stop and stay awhile in the City.

I was at Guido's twice with very large groups in the past year.  Both times the service and food made for many happy diners.  One of the groups I was with was a Yelp International Supper Club.  The interior is dimly lit so it feels cozy and warm even with a large group.

Every time I arrive at Guido's I am greeted by Nonna.  A sweet little Italian Grandma who just makes you want to sit and stay awhile.  There are long tables, small tables, and round tables in the main dining room.  Guido's offers Tapas, St. Louis Style Pizza, and Italian foods to its patrons.  

A few of my favorites are Queso Borracho con Salsa de Escalona, Gambas al Ajillo, Toasted Ravioli, St. Louis Style Pizza, and Guido's Salad.  The Guido Salad is served with lettuce, Parmesan, tomato, pimentos, red onion, black olives, and artichokes.  Guido's Caesar Salad is also a good choice.

During the ISC I orders a White Wine Sangria.  A friend and I at the ISC shared the Datiles con Tocino (Bacon Wrapped Stuffed Dates) and the Queso de Cabra  (Baked Goat Cheese).  The Baked Goat Cheese was my least favorite of the items orders.  Our waitress Donna was more a star of the show this night than the food.

When planning a trip to Guido's bring along someone who will be adventurous in ordering Tapas with you.

St. Louisians are very protective of their favorite BBQ Joints.  I know I must tread lightly with this review...

Salt + Smoke deserves a spot in high up on the list.  The meats are smoked and so flavorful they don't even need sauce.  Salt + Smoke is known for brisket.  They offer brisket three ways: lean, fatty, or burnt ends.  You must try THIS brisket.   The pulled chicken and pulled pork are both amazing.  The Bestie Platter allows you to pick two meats, which is a total score!  The Bestie Platter is so much food we have a whole other nights dinner with the leftovers.  The Mac and Cheese is even better the next day.   

This is a table service, full bar, open later...BBQ must try.

Public Service Announcment...

The floor is like an ice rink, be prepared to SLIDE to your table.  I had on wedge sandals, which I wear all the time without issue, and almost fell twice!  This is not good when you have people getting up and down walking to a food line.  Watch your step.  

In my opinion this is an over priced chain.  Name changes don't help "GC" aka Granite City Food & Brewery at all.  People don't know where this restaurant is located due to its name.  Coupons on Facebook help offset the high prices.  I don't mind paying for quality...however nothing I tasted was of high quality.  In fact the waitress suggested we try the "famous" cinnamon rolls...they were not fresh.  In my estimation they were frozen and not made in house. 

The same waitress when describing the brunch to our table of four, told us that "there may be some leftover soup on the buffet...but she was not sure"!?!?   Ummm...gross.   Thanks for admitting to the food not being cooked fresh.  

Drink refills were not made in a timely manner.  We had to ask for the check multiple times.  Maybe rather than four hostesses on staff, they should have two hostesses and more wait staff.

On small business Saturday we wanted to show some love to one of our favorite family take out dinner locations. We ordered online and reserved the date and time we wanted to pick up amazing Dewey's Pizzas. Having Family in town for the Holidays we had a lot of mouths to feed. After several days of Thanksgiving leftovers everyone was more than happy for PIZZA! Dewey's reserved parking spots makes curbside pickup easy as pie.

We ordered five 17" Pizzas for our dinner pizza party for over twenty people and had leftovers. The 17" size is perfect for a crowd. The pizza was hot, fresh, and flavorful. Dewey's has amazing high quality pizza ingredients. Our family is forever debating with of their pizzas is the best...Meatball, Figgy Piggy, Don Corleone, Ryan's Inferno, Bronx Bomber the list goes on and on. No one can decide, they all are amazing in their own way.

I am sure we will be ordering again soon. This is the Third Dewey's Pizza Party we have thrown in a few months' time; I am sure there will be another before the new year. Small Businesses-like Dewey's help make family time even more enjoyable by taking the stress of cooking off the hosts hands. Thank You for such quality products time and time again.

Southern Food gets me every time and Juniper has my heart.  

Hot Crispy Fried Chicken is the King of the House at Juniper.  Shrimp and Grits follows closely behind.  These dishes evoke good times and good conversation.  I also have enjoyed the Deviled Eggs, Salads, Chicken and Waffle, and Chicken with Pimento Cheese on a Biscuit.  Juniper's Biscuits are not to be ignored.   I would happily order any of these items again.  

Service has been stellar, even for a private event I attended.

I am looking forward to my next visit very soon!

It's Fried Chicken.  Fried Chicken only.  Served on styrofoam plates.  Sorry, I don't get it.  

The sides we ordered were for the most part- terrible.  The baked beans were lower in quality that a can of pork and beans from Aldi.   The Mac and Cheese was squishy.  Coleslaw straight out of an industrial tub.  The collard greens were the only side anyone finished.  

For all the people doing amazing things with Fried Chicken in STL this is does not compare.  Many places are able to serve their chicken piping Hot.  There is no reason for me to return to Gus's.

I attended a Yelp International Supper Club at Apollonia and had a wonderful time.  They were able to seat our party of 14 with ease.  I would consider this a place to take a family since they did such a nice job our with group.

My Bestie Alison N. and I ordered a Cheese and Olive Plate to start.  The plate was more than two people could devour.  It came with Olives, Pepperoncini's, Cucumber, Feta Cheese, and Warm Pita.  We both ordered Deluxe Chicken Pita's for our meal.  I ordered extra Tzatziki Sauce and would recommend that as an option.  The Tzatziki made me open my Gyro and attack it more like a salad.


I was very envious of the Hummus Plates and would return just to try that alone.  This neighborhood is a bit outside of my normal stomping grounds...but I hope to return sooner than later.  Apollonia has Street and Off Street Parking.

This event was a blast and is one of the reasons Yelp is so much fun.  Dinner with people you would never meet if it were not all for this Yelp Lifestyle.  I hope to dine with this group again soon.

We were lured into Slider House thanks to Steven B. awesome photograph of the Slider Mary. Unfortunately it was kind of like an online dating situation.  The picture was great...in real life, it was a one drink and run.

Upon pulling up and parking not one but three Slider House employees were smoking in the main lot wearing logo wear.  I tried not to let that bother me, but it did.  

The place was empty but our waitress decided to tell the Happy Hour specials to the table next to us and us at the same time??? Ummm...really.  Service went down from there.  The icing on the cake was after delivering our fried pickles she left the bill on the table.   We may have ordered three or four rounds of drinks...but hey, we can go down the street for drinks, no problem!

The mix used on the Bloody Mary was not to our liking and the Blood Orange Mimosa just did not work in this setting.  None of the food we tasted would bring us back. 

I don't need to return but then again I am a big supporter off local burger joints like Carl's Drive In, The Dam, Stacked Burger Bar, and Baileys Range.

Beast BBQ has made a name for itself in a highly competitive market in St. Louis.  The first item I must mention at Beast is the Smoked Cauliflower.  This is by far the stand out item on the menu.  This Smoked Cauliflower is offered as a vegetarian meal or a side dish.  This smoked cauliflower has a deep BBQ flavor that is one of a kind.  Other favorite items are the Brisket, Pulled Pork, Turkey Breast, Wings, Smokehouse Nachos, and Collard Greens.  Beast is hearty comfort food.  Every meal I have had at or from Beast BBQ has had leftovers.  Beast has great to go boxes, containers, and lids.  They are currently offering curbside pickup as an option for customers.

Serra's Pizza is St. Louis Style Ultra-Thin Pizza with Provel Cheese.  This pizza is really like a cracker crust it is so thin.  The space is small and packed with regulars from wall to wall.  Take Out during peak times is ideal.  On busy nights, pizzas will take over one hour to come out of the kitchen, real talk.  You will not get any sympathy from the wait staff with long wait times...you know what you are in for.  Once your pizza arrives you forget about the wait.  The creamy Provel Cheese, warm meats, and crispy crust all come together in pizza harmony.  

This pizza makes great leftovers.  Serra's is a hometown, casual, family pizzeria.  Come as you are and experience this Mom and Pop Eatery.

Read my lips...Order the Mac and Cheese.  This Ritz Cracker White Cheddar masterpiece is great the day it is made and even better as leftovers.  Salt and Smokes take on Mac and Cheese must be tasted to believe how delicious it is.  This Mac and Cheese is perfect along side smoked meats and other stand out side dishes.  

My favorite thing to order is the Bestie Combo - Two Meats, Two Sides, and a Cheddar Jalapeno Popover.  It is hard to choose between the Pulled Pork, Pulled Chicken, and Lean Brisket, I love them all.  The meat has just the perfect amount of smoked flavor.  This meat does not need sauce it stands on its own, but house made BBQ sauces are all nice and can be a good dipping sauce for Fries as well.  I always have leftovers, which make a perfect second dinner.

The best part of this location is the tiered patio seating.  I love all of the Salt and Smokes in the St. Louis Area and will return soon.

Pretty sure I tried one of everything on the menu at Suzy Wong's and I'm pretty sure it was really really effing awesome. Thus the appeal of going out to dinner with a massive group--you order a massive amount of food so you can all sample a bite or two of everything. WIN!

The highlight of my dining experience had to be the wonton nachos. Brillz! Crispy wonton skins topped with a queso, lots of veggies and a delicious bbq pork--I could have eaten a whole plate of these all on my own, no problem. I was also a huge fan of the red curry cheese dip, also served with those tasty crispy wontons. Maybe I just really love wontons? Yep, that sounds about right. Other highlights: coconut-thai chili chicken wings, spicy tuna & cucumber hand roll, and the chicken katsu bites. There was really only one dish that I didn't really dig on and that was the Philly roll. I think it was just so plain compared to all the amazing flavors and textures I had been eating.

The drinks here are also supurb. I had two different cocktails and I'm sad to admit that I don't remember what they were and I can't find the drink list online to help me refresh my memory. However, they were both DELICIOUS. In fact, I heard mostly positive murmurs from my dining companions about their cocktails, not just the food. Winners all around!

The space is cool. Like, COOL. Dark and hip, soothing purple accents, lots of Asian art touches. I really felt comfortable and happy there. Full of yummy food, tipsy on tasty cocktails, and surrounded by a great group of folks. This meal was definitely one of the highlights of my trip!

Came here for a team dinner while in Indy and had a truly wonderful experience of delicious food, tasty beverages, and the most beautiful barn setting, complete with cow milking and more! 

We kicked things off with a terrific cheese plate featuring the incredible cheeses from Trader Point Creamery followed by a delicious kale salad then a main course of the best pork I've ever had. Flavorful but not gamey (like some can be), perfectly cooked (not dry in the slightest), and with a wonderful herb rub and maitake chestnut sauce for the topping. Amazing! 

Before dessert came around we took a break and enjoyed watching the creamer cows get milked, getting a crash course in dairy from the awesome staff. 

Dessert consisted of samples of their tasty egg nog and an apple gallette with vanilla ice cream and cherry marmalade. So delicious! 

Seasonal cocktail were fantastic (I had the sugar plum and it was excellent!) and the staff was unbelievably helpful and kind. I would certainly go out of my way to return if I have the opportunity while in Indy again.

You'd miss this place walking by but it is truly a gem. There are so many menu options to choose from and you won't go wrong with any of them! Your best bet...you'll just have to try them all. They'll customize anything in the menu to suit your fancy!
