DO NOT COME HERE for legit Chinese food. This is a pricier, slightly fancier version of Panda Express. Do not expect the food to be like anything from an immigrant-heavy city like Houston or Boston's Chinatown. It's honestly a tragedy. 

The honey walnut shrimp is the only decent dish here. Almost all the dishes were overpriced and poor quality. I'm really puzzled why this restaurant has decent reviews because the food was really just overpriced Panda Express. There was not a single Asian family dining there. 

The restaurant on the outside looks very cute but doesn't look like how a typical Chinese restaurant would look. I appreciate the location near the waterfront- it's a nice date spot. For the actual food, take a hard pass.

On our way through Delaware, we pulled into the potstickers parking lot, for a quick bite to eat while we were heading northwards. We weren't sure if we were going to eat at the gastropub, the Mexican food or pot stickers, but we picked potstickers based on what we thought would be a quick meal, which it ended up not being.

When we walked in, we immediately noticed that it seemed like equal parts restaurant and nightclub. We also noticed that they had a Tuesday evening girls night promotion which included very inexpensive alcoholic beverages for females, making it a quite loud evening. We were seated quickly, and met Nancy our server, who gave us our menus.

I was surprised at how much potstickers tries to do with their menu. They have an extensive Japanese menu, a sushi menu, a Chinese menu, and items that are Korean, Hawaiian, and even Thai. The interior is extremely eclectic, with themes that remind me of PF changs and also nightclubs of my past including uplit bars and rotating mirrored balls.

I started with a hot green tea ($3.50) and then we ordered the scallion pancakes appetizer ($6.95), and for our entrees we chose the Kung Pao chicken ($17.95) and bok choy with shiitake mushrooms ($12.95). While we waited for our food, I went to the bathroom to wash my hands. The lady's restroom was interesting to say the least, with the giant I mean Costco sized Listerine bottle, multiple body sprays, perfumes, toothpicks, and other items that I'm not used to seeing in bathrooms in restaurants. Very odd unless you think of it in the sense of a "spruce up between songs at the club" sort of way.

The tear arrived first with the scallion pancakes. The tea was good but nothing special, and the scallion pancakes were extremely oily and soggy, not the crispy and flavorful onion dotted crisps I was hoping for. The scallion pancakes did however come with a side of kimchi which I thought was interesting given that it was Delaware, and the kimchi was surprisingly pretty good, but that was the only part of the dish that was enjoyable. We left most of it on the table uneaten.

When the entrance came out, we thought we had another shot on the restaurant redeeming itself. Hubby had the kung pao chicken with a side of white rice, and he stated that it was about the same or worse than Panda Express, which I thought was saying something. 

My bok choy with shiitake mushrooms and a side of brown rice was the only real dish that earned them any stars. The bok choy was fresh and sweet, but even so the mushrooms seemed like they were either dried and rehydrated or pre-packaged. Either way they were not fresh and they were very rubbery. Shiitake mushrooms are packed with flavor and health benefits, but I couldn't get past this texture, and I cook them frequently so I don't know how they would have gotten it this way if it wasn't rehydrated or pre-packaged. The sauce over the dish was very mild and plain, however it was quite healthy in terms of being low sodium and I tried to think of it in those terms to try and eat as much as I could.

The service was friendly but not very fast despite the fact that by the time our food was coming out, most of the people were only on drinks. Also, I felt like the dishes were overpriced, given their lack of quality and general lack of presentation, especially for the $18 plate of Kung Pao chicken which was mostly vegetables and peanuts. The ambiance was lacking, given that it had an extremely clubbing vibe, and parking was difficult even on a Tuesday late evening. I'm not sure what the food scene is in Delaware, but this restaurant did little for us while we were passing through and if we were in the area again we would not return.

Wow! Fantastic Mexican food right along the waterfront! This place is the real deal if you are a mole fan. The outdoor patio is fantastic and the vibes are phenomenal. The servers are super friendly and our food came out quickly. This place gets packed on weekends so I would recommend getting a reservation.

I got the Taquitos de Pato en Mole Coloradito and it was delicious. The duck taquitos were so crispy and the duck meat was so tender. It went perfectly with the mole, which was rich and super flavorful. I also got to try the Enchiladas Oaxaca and it was superb. I'm normally not an Enchiladas guy but the mole made the dish for me. The presentation of both dishes were great and I would definitely come back.

I'm glad we waited as long as we did. It was definitely worth it!

Located inside Lama Dog, the Nook provides patrons of Lama Dog a terrific option for food. Serving mainly burgers and fries, you can't go wrong with any to pair with your beer. 

I got the lama burger with truffle fries ($1 upgrade) and I was pleasantly surprised with how juicy the burger was. The patty was so juicy and the bacon was terrific. I love how the brioche bun held its integrity too. I was highly recommend getting the chipotle aioli to put inside your burger. The fries were great but a little on the salty side. I guess that's why you have your beer to drown out the saltiness. 

All in all, the Nook serves up great burger options while you enjoy your beer at Lama Dog.

Ooka is exactly like Benihana (teppanyaki restaurant) when you can't find Benihana anywhere in the area. Dining here is definitely an experience. The chef prepares your meal right in front of you, performing food tricks to keep you engaged. It's definitely a treat to see these talented chefs perfect their craft. With that said, the service is excellent. Everyone was friendly and you feel welcomed.

The restaurant wasn't too crowded and there is plenty of seating. If you don't want teppanyaki, you can sit on the other side of the restaurant and opt for a more traditional sit-down seating. The menu on that side is more of your typical Japanese sushi. We dined on the teppanyaki side and marveled at the great chefs!

For teppanyaki, there are a bunch of different combinations you can choose from. If you want teriyaki chicken only, you can have that. If you want a little chicken with steak, you can have that too. You can pretty much have any combination imaginable between chicken, steak, fish, lobster, etc... I would definitely suggest ordering a combination so you can try multiple things. I decided on getting a combination of the chicken and NY strip steak. Personally, I don't think the food compares to Benihana but the ambiance certainly makes up for that. The chicken was a little on the dry side but the beef was good. It was prepared medium-rare, just the way I like it. It can get a little pricey depending on what you order.

Ooka is a decent place for teppanyaki. I wouldn't say it's the best teppanyaki ever but the ambiance and cleanliness of the restaurant is great.

When in Rome... How can you go to Philly and NOT get a cheese steak?! I was recommended Jim's by a Philly native and I'm glad I listened to him! The interior is a very diner-type feel. There are a bunch of photos of celebrities who have made the trek to Jim's which I thought was pretty cool. The first floor is all about food and the second floor has all of the seating. I like how the seats are indoors, especially when it's chilly outside. 

When you're ordering, you gotta order the Philly way. I got a "whiz wit" which is a cheese steak with cheese and onions. The cheese is the type of nacho cheese you get at the ball game and the onions are grilled which provide a nice crunch to the sandwich! I love how the steak is tender and chopped up. Tons of flavor! I heard that the steak is prepared differently depending on the place you go and I'm a big fan of the way the steak was prepared here. The bread was also amazing. It's soft, fluffy but still kept it's shape. You can definitely tell the difference between the bread here and outside of Philly. The only thing that I wish was different was the amount of "whiz" that was on the sandwich. I wish there was more cheese!! I guess next time, I just have to ask personally for more cheese. 

Jim's is a fantastic spot for a cheese steak! Trusted by locals!

I get into ruts and dine in the same places. Well I broke out of my shell and went here with my husband for dinner. I wish with all my heart I'd been here sooner, the food is amazing. The first visit here we left, because the host told us (despite open tables) the kitchen was an hour out for incoming orders; nice to know since we had somewhere to be at 7:30. The interior smelled so great we made a point to come back for dinner as soon as our schedules allowed. The restaurant is tucked away in a strip mall and a bit tricky getting into off crowded Grant Rd if coming from the freeway. Our next visit to Yamato, we both ordered sukiyaki. After ordering it took a good long while to come out (30-40minutes), during which time we were served soup and (a great!) salad. The food was so very good and the long wait was immediately forgiven. I've since been twice for ramen and sushi. The place is an open room with a sushi bar with a flat screen TV playing sports on the wall above the sushi bar and on the opposite wall; so if you don't like TV playing you are out of luck. There are tables to accommodate large groups and the service is consistently good. At present this is my favorite Japanese place on Tucson.

This afternoon I went to the China Pasta House on Park off of 6th/St. Mary's for the second time. In December I went with a group of YELPer's for the international super club. Today I went all by myself with a mission. Since my husband is eating low/ no carbs and he was out of town for the night, I was going to carb up!
I started with a bean paste and a pork steamed bun which I wasn't able to try the first time I dined at China Pasta House. I had no idea what I was missing. Perfection. 

They were absolutely mouthwatering. The end. 

Please order the pork steamed bun, because if I could time travel back to when I was ordering I would have ordered 4, so I could have pigged out royally; went home and rolled into a a drunken happy tummy slumber. Usually I love bean paste steam buns, but the pork was SO good, I am ruined for all else.  I also ordered the spicy rice cake shrimp dish which I recommend. I can't remember if the last time I had this dish it was nearly as spicy; I have no need for medication to unclog any sinuses. I have an utterly happy runny nose.  I am a big fan of a warm burning mouth,ears and tummy after eating spicy food. They also have tea eggs, which are hard boiled eggs soaked in Chinese five spice tea; which I ordered to have for breakfast tomorrow. The eggs are cracked after being cooked then soaked. The flavor is pungent and pleasant tasting (cold) hard boiled egg.

I absolutely intend on returning to try their soup, but it's going to be tough because so far I've liked everything I've ordered a lot.
The location has about 15 parking spots at best and the inside is a bit dated and cramped. Despite being so the customers were Chinese students making no noise, studying in the corner.   I had fast customer service and my food was ready in 5 minutes. So food is a 5 out of 5. Eating in is a 3 out of 5. Service was 5 out of 5.

Since I work of Speedway this little gem is just minutes down the road when I get off work. I learned about it while in nursing school, as the students would take up all their tables and delight over nachos while studying. This is healthy Mexican food if you ask them. They have a cute sign that says "Tamales=mexican power bar!" The inside of the restaurant is a on the industrial side with 20 foot tall ceilings. During the summer the place is quite warm to eat in. However, the food is consistent and wonderful. The menu is designed to please any sort of customer and they even have vegan options which are easy to identify. My most favorite thing is their drinks. My husband delights in their horchatta and I love their limonada. They have a huge freezer with buckets of freshly prepared drinks. In years past I could bring in bags to recycle and they would reward me with a free drink, and so frequently I will come with a travel mug or cup and they will fill it instead of using their togo cups. They are all about living green in Tucson. So far I haven't brought my own containers for food, but I have a feeling they would be delighted to accommodate.  
Tanias 33 offers a huge variety of foods to go. $3 dollar to go plates with a burro, tamale or 2 enchiladas with rice n beans. Killer deal. Every time I go I leave smiling. Every time I order I always get extra items so I can take it to work to enjoy the next day. Their soup especially is good for my soul. I always get a 1/2 gallon so i'll have some for a day or two afterwards; unless it's albondigas which we always eat up till it's gone. I biggest downer is the store front only has 4 parking spots off of Grande so be careful getting in and out.

I love Guadalajara Original Grill. I consistently bring out of town company because it's a basic mexican place that sells, what people think they want, huge platters of food with beans and rice on the side. I love the table side salsa, and they customize it to your tastes(Spicy extra cilantro). They have huge margaritas.  More than once,  I realized I was beyond buzzed trying to finish one of their house margaritas, just as I happily ordered my second drink. 
My favorite dish they offer is their tropical Chilean sea bass. It is absolutely in my top favorite dishes in Tucson. My husband and I went this week and both decided to order combo plates(comfort food) and both combo plates just knocked my socks off! I ordered the two item combo of  beef taco and chicken flauta. My dining experience rocked; the service was great, the food was excellent and it was not loud; which it can be if a game is going on in the bar or mariachi's are strolling around. Overall, it can accommodate large groups, and it's consistent in the quality of food. The service is not always consistent and we have walked out discussed due to lack of service before, but we couldn't break the ties, since the food kept us coming back.

I am torn. The patio area and live music should have made for a wonderful night; however it's location is surrounded by low end trailer parks. The cocktails and food should have made everything perfect. I arrived for dinner at 5 and had the server was obsessed with taking away our food and drink menus; even though there were no other diners there and we had not ordered any food. She then in grabbing at the menus for the second time  tipped over our drinks spilling two out of the four on us.  Our waitress was so out of it, she picked up the tipped over broken glasses, the big pieces of glass  and then left glass under our seats. No sweeping up of glass, no wiping off of the table we were sitting at. Although she did hand a single wash cloth to my husband who got the most alcohol spilled on him.  We moved tables since we didn't want to continue to sit over broken class; zero effort was made to clean the table, chairs or glass under the table.  The food for sitting outside on a patio on Miracle Mile was pricey and not memorable. I ordered fish tacos and they had no flavor; literally no taste to it. I couldn't tell what I was eating. If two diners at a table tell the waitress the food was bland, shouldn't someone ask questions as to why, instead we were offered something else on the menu and a box to "take home" food I don't want to eat. Our meal appetizer of crab cakes were good, but over priced for happy hour at $12 for two patties. Our cocktails were very nice. The live music was nice but not the genera of music I normally like, plus it was very loud, to the point our server couldn't hear us and basically had to be mouth to ear to know what we were ordering. My husband ordered the shrimp scampi and loved it. So I should give this place another chance. However after paying $60 for such a disastrous experience, it's going to take some grace of heart to give it another try.

What a lunch truck gem. There was a lunch truck round up at Cartel last month, and immediately this was the place, I couldn't get enough of.

My husband and I both ordered the Banh Mi Dat Biet sandwich ( which includes: pork, ham, pate, butter,cucumber,daikon,cilantro and jalapeño) and it was so fresh and clean tasting, on a fresh roll. It's been so long since I've enjoyed a Vietnamese sandwich, that I was blown away. It had a nice kick to finish the sandwich due to those few jalapeños tucked inside. Despite having many other lunch trucks tempting us to spend our dollars, we ended up ordered a second sandwich to go, for breakfast the next day! 

The biggest surprise is that it was only $3.75. What a deal.

I first came across this place, at a booth atTucson Meet Yourself. I was aware El Rustico had a regular spot at the Tohono O'odham swap meet. Now this fantastic food is right in Central Tucson. Clearly, with social distancing, not an ideal time to open a brick and mortar place. Today, I went with my friend and got tostadas la malinche, bursting with delicious avocado and my choice of meat, I picked pastor. Absolutely fantastic. Jose, the owner was already out of some things, but El Rustico has had pop-ups on and off since Tucson Meet Yourself, and my favorite discovery of 2019 might have been his pineapple slaw. It's something I have never had elsewhere, that is refreshing and a great side to any meal. There are vegetarian options available and burritos, tacos, gorditas, slopes, quesadillas, caramelo, tortas, lorenzas, parilladas with choice of filling. I was told a good pick is the red beef, which Jose was sold out of before I got there at 3 pm today. Others suggested the tripe. I've had his chicharon, costilla, and today bisteq and have been delighted each trip. So, if you are headed downtown along Oracle Rd, do yourself a favor and stop by.

Porterhouse ! Since moving to Marana in 2004, i've not found a steak house i've liked better. They grill the meat outside on mesquite and the menu is so basic, they don't even print it up anymore. I used to tell everyone I met, to go here, and some have thought they liked Daisy Mae's more since there is a larger menu variety including prime rib. (I guess the same ownership connects the two). All I can say is you get a little salad with a slice of onion on top DRENCHED in dressing, ranch beans and texas toast with anything you choose. You are very likely to have a hard time seeing anything since it's basically inside a cabin with few windows. You are likely going to sit at a picnic bench, which isn't ideal for families or persons who have limited mobility. However this meal is an experience that is out of this world. Consistently prepared perfection, if you love ribs, T-bone steaks, porterhouse, beef or pork ribs, chicken, filet mignon and new york strip(I think). I have always split a porterhouse with my husband. They offer few sides, baked potato or corn on the cob. I'm pretty sure the offer hotdogs to children....but I am so engrossed in what i'm about to receive I sort of get tunnel vision waiting for my meat to arrive.They have a bar, in the last 2-3 years give you a menu of wines when you are seated and have live music on the weekends. This is a very casual place, with wall to wall graffiti & old license plates mounted everywhere and a dirt parking lot. The restrooms might be a bit tricky to navigate if you have mobility issues, since the tables are packed closely inside, but for me I just love it. If you haven't been and love beef, go. We take all our out-of-town meat-eating guests here and so far it's been to rave reviews.

I came to the soft opening of Pin Wei last week, and I have to day it was a real treat.  I've been to other Szechuan restaurants before, especially to places like Han Dynasty in Center City, but PW just stands out in so many ways.

My parents and I ordered the cucumber app, the dumplings app, the pork hot pot, the scallops, and the ma po tofu.

First, we were all surprised by how fresh the ingredients were.  It could be that the freshness was due to the new opening, but typically "fresh" is not something I directly characterize with Szechuan food. From the cucumber, which was just crispy goodness, to the scallops that were walloping in size and clean to the taste...I was quite pleased.

Second, the decor of this place is very...tasteful.  No pun intended. This is the kind of place that I wouldn't mind taking my clients to. There is some serious artwork on the walls that surprised me.  But moreover the place was clean and well designed, yet accessible for the casual meal. True, that doesn't define how good the food is.  I'm actually a fan of the "best food is in the ghetto" philosophy, but this place doesn't conform to that adage.  OK, I know it's not an adage, but...yeah.

Third, this place is authentic!  I eat a lot of Chinese food.  I was in Szechuan province last summer (even attended cooking class there), and I'm happy to say that nothing I ordered was a disappointment on the cultural side.  The pork hot pot I had actually had real pork giblets.  For my taste, this was a nice surprise.  Score!

If I had any complaints, they should probably be directed to myself. I probably ordered a bit too much spicy food, but that was entirely my doing -- I was on a mission to see how "Szechuan" they could get. The waitress offered to give me spicier versions of everything and I actually agreed.  Oh well, at least it was good!

Overall, I'd definitely come back to Pin Wei.  I had an excellent meal.  I wouldn't be surprised if this place is packed a few months from now.  True, it's in a strip mall in K of P, but that means there's ample parking.

TIP: Go early or you will be waiting a while. 

This place is solid. If you're in New Orleans and wondering where to eat, look no further. This is the spot! Trust me when I say, get there early. We were there around 7:45 and there was a mini line already. By the time we finished eating, the whole block was busy with people waiting to be seated. It's worth waking up for. 

Here's what we ordered:

Banana Foster Pain Perdu: French bread-based French toast with rum flambeed banana and raisins. If you have a sweet tooth, this is made for you. This was really sweet for me and can only have a few bites. Definitely meant for sharing if you want something sweet in the end. 

Classic Brioche French Toast: This was sooo good. Also on the sweet side. My kids shared one order and they still had a hard time finishing. 

We also got the Crawfish Benedict, I don't think it's on the menu. This was delicious and would definitely order again. 

This is a must visit and would go again and order the other amazing food they offer on their menu. Only if they have one in Los Angeles!

Pros: Bartenders were very friendly. 
Cons: Slow service. Overpriced

I had fried oysters, shrimp cocktail, and lamb chops. The oysters were good, perfectly fried and seasoned with good tarter sauce. $10 for an order that included just 3 oysters. 

The shrimp were big and fresh but for $16 I expect more than 4 shrimp. 

I was there for happy hour. I ordered a dirty martini. I was charged $14. 
I've been to plenty of happy hours in my day and I've never paid $14 for a drink.

My lamb was $36 and included 2 chops, about 10 green bean pieces and a small handful of fries. The lamb had a burnt taste. It just wasn't worth $36. 

I felt robbed. The new owners or new managers are clearly cheap. The food was ok but just not worth the price. I would never go back in a million years and I don't recommend anyone giving them a shot. Why are the owners so cheap, someone needs to explain to them that in this economy people want to feel like they are getting something for their money.

Dear Customers,
After 17 years we are regrettably to inform you that Red Pepper is closed indefinitely due to family health issue. Both Sue and David of Red Pepper wants to thank you for your patronage year after year. Red Pepper maybe gone but the food and the love will live on forever. 

Daughters of Red Pepper

I had a really upsetting brunch experience on 4/13/14.  
My fiance and I often come here for snacks and decided to stay for Brunch this Sunday.  At 12:30pm, we placed our order for a Daffodil omelette brunch, mango juice, and turkish quesadilla. We paid at that time.  We let them know we were sitting outside, and the guy told us to hurry and reserve the spot so we could enjoy our breakfast.  

After about an hour, I wondered about the delay as I had not received my coffee, and went in to ask if it was OK that I at least got my coffee while i waited for the brunch which a girl said was coming soon. 
After another 30minutes my fiance started to become angry as were missing an appointment we had scheduled for 2pm. I asked what was going on with our order, and the girl and cook looked confused and said I had no order in. 
I pointed out that I already paid for my meal, and it took an hour just to get the coffee, which they didn't seem to be confused on giving me without question.  
It turns out the male who took my order was only "helping out" and his shift wasn't starting til later, and he forgot to put in the order for food. (I found him outside around the corner smoking a cigarette - waiting for his shift to start i guess).

Anyways I started getting frustrated and panicked and said at this point we are in hurry, and starving and need to leave. They kept saying it's already on, it's already on.  15 minutes later I hear the girl yelling at the cook, and apparently the food was not on or anywhere near serving.  At some point the cook was running back inside from outdoors and still had not prepared anything for us. (After 1.5 hours wouldn't you drop everything and get my order out first?) I told them I couldn't wait any longer, and the cook said it's coming, it's almost out, i'll put it in the to-go container! 
My fiance had already left at 2pm in hopes of catching our meeting.  15 minutes later, the food was getting put in containers.  I had to remind the girl about the additional item (bread) that was missing from my omelette, and in the whole 2 hrs, i had 1 cup of coffee.
Exactly 2 hours later at 2:30 I'm leaving.  The food was overcooked and obviously rushed, it was a disaster in the containers and not good at all.  The chicken in the quesadilla was weird texture, like it was deli meat that you would slice, not real grilled chicken.  I should have walked out, unfortunately i had already paid, and they weren't offering a refund.  
I've sent 2 emails to the owner, and to the cafe fulya email address, and have not received a response

I only went there once and decided not to go back. The help were really friendly and nice but the place was filthy and really run down. I had heard so much about this place and how great it was, so was disappointed to say the least.
Since the place was so dirty I passed on ordering any food and just had some coffee.

I really like their white BBQ sauce, it is very good, they're homemade ketchup is spicy and their homemade red BBQ sauce was just average! I had their fish tacos, very good... but I was really impressed with their Brunch, not a huge portion size (small really), and a little pricey, but very good taste! I would recommend it, if you have a few extra bucks to spare.
They have a lot of beer options, which I like!

Love,love,love this place. I had the lucky experience of finding this place when I moved to Santa Barbara and was fortunate to live right down the street. My favorite item is the challah french toast but everything I had there was excellent and the service was always good.

I've thought about that breakfast burrito an absurd number of times over the last few weeks. Literally every morning I think "breakfast burrito," and my brain says, "You should go back to Big Ed's."

First of all, it's a Reno staple but it was my first time. I'd heard about it and figured it would be over-hyped and not worth it. I was wrong. It's definitely got the divey vibe, but on a Sunday morning we were able to find a seat at the bar easily.

We had the breakfast sandwich and burrito, both of which are phenomenal. The burrito definitely won the entree challenge, though. There's a ton of well-melted cheese, super flavorful ground beef, and enough things inside that you don't get bored with any one bit. The tortilla is soft and crispy all at the same time, and the potatoes are a nice addition to the mondo burrito that we swore we wouldn't finish but ended up mopping up the plate with potatoes like Cinderella before the ball.

Also got a bloody mary, which while I'm not a huge fan, the receiver said it's one of his favorites in Reno so far--you'll have to give it a shot if you haven't already.

I went here for the first time last Friday, and I've asked my husband every day if we can go back. We ended up there accidentally on the way to Renown (husband's job), and it was a beautiful, beautiful accident.

First of all, the atmosphere is cool, industrial-chic. They had a local craftsman make the bar, stools, tables, etc., and they are beautiful (they paid him in beer!). It's a place perfect to meet your buddies for an after work drink or to sit and read a book while you beverage.

The beer is excellent. We tried probably five of the 12 they had on tap and each was a delicate (and successful) balance of hops and malt, sweet and bitter, clean and lingering. They also have a nice variety of beers, as opposed to some of the other locations in town that may focus on a specific type.

They fill growlers and half-growlers, and even will give you what's called a "crowler." It's a 32oz. can that you can recycle when you're done with it (filled like a growler, not already filled). Those are free, the glass growlers cost moolah. Definitely a lot of options for taking the beer with you.

Staff was friendly and willing to chat about the location, their plans, and the beers. They offer $2 tasters, and are more than happy to give you a sip if you want to try a beer before you commit to a pint. 

I'm thrilled about all of the awesome new beer places opening up in Reno, and this is definitely one of my favorites of the bunch.

Ah, the French Fry. Such a humble and simple food item, yet so many places try to tart them up and in the process ruin them. The basic French Fry is a square slice of potato deep fried in oil (though lard provides the best flavor), sea salt, and a touch of grease. Nothing more, nothing less. No green stuff, no garlic, no cheese curds (though I admit having a weak spot for the Bridge's Poutine); just potato, salt, and grease. I have been looking for a decent french fry in Reno for over five years now. I have had acceptable French fries, mediocre French fries, and truly horrible French fries. I love the shoestring potatoes at the Old Granite Street Eatery, but they are alternative-shaped potato chips and not truly French fries. 
I finally found very good French fries at Niko's Greek Kitchen. They were tasty, a bit crunchy at the outside, yet with a soft heart, the right touch of salt, and just a hint of grease - heavenly! They are almost good enough to receive the coveted Patat Frite of Reno designation, but not yet quite. I will continue in my quest for best French fry in Reno, but when I get a real craving for the tasty treat, I will go out of my way to Niko's for his version. Will need to bring my own Frite sauce, though. It just isn't right to despoil such a lovely dish with tomato ketchup.

The Gas Lamp has a country-feel atmosphere, that reminded my a bit of auberges in the French country side. It has an understated kind of elegance that may feel a bit dated to some, but was quite comfortable to me. It was like having dinner in an old-world family's kitchen. The staff was friendly and attentive. We were seated quickly (it helped that there weren't a lot of guests, yet) and were served water almost immediately. The server visited within an acceptable timeframe and ask for our drink order. The drinks were served fairly quickly and she presented us with the off-menu specials. My wife was corrupted by the chicken piccata special and ordered it, but I showed great strength of character and stayed with my initial decision and ordered the Jambalaya. The waitress asked me for my spicyness preference as the chef, if left to his own devices, makes it very spicy. I ordered it to the chef's preference.  

The jambalaya contained generous amounts of fish, hot andouille, veggies, and shrimp (I can't understand why chefs insist on keeping the tail shell on shrimp that is not intended to be eaten with my fingers). The stew had a nice bite to it that seemed to increase in heat as it lingered in mouth, but was not so overbearingly hot that it overstayed its welcome. The Icky certainly helped tame the fire to some extend.

Overall I was very happy with the atmosphere, the service, and - most important - the food. Gas Lamp is definitely on my list of many returns (specially since it is next door to Reno Little Theater).

When 30 Main arrived to our neighborhood, I was instantly curious.  A visit to their website tickled my curiosity bone even further.  This restaurant boasts itself as being "stylized" with "class and fun" with a calendar full of fun events.  What's not to like?  That would be the actual experience.

On the many occasions that I've come to this restaurant, it is almost entirely empty.  When driving past during peak hours (weekend brunch, evenings, etc)., this place still looks empty from the outside.

The menu is far from exciting - just your generic, run of the mill offerings.  This is a shame because compared to other local eateries, there is really nothing setting this place apart.  Food was okay but service is exceptionally slow, even as the only (or close to only) customers.  When dining at the bar, we literally waited 10 minutes for our bartender to pick up our bill.  This was even more disappointing when we were being ignored so they could use their cell phone on what looked like personal business.

The ambiance is grim.  In a space that is practically empty, this restaurant has a dark and somber feel to it.  I can't imagine a less appealing locale for any event, be it brunch, dinner or even just an after-work cocktail.  Do yourself a favor and just stay home.

This place is a taco lover's dream! 
Delicious house-made masa tortillas with a variety of taco options. My go-to's are the fried Baja fish taco and the portobello with goat cheese and crispy onions, but all of them are good. Plus, all of the tacos are under $4. Pair a couple tacos with a side of their street corn "off the cob" and you can't go wrong!

Don't get me started on Mission's new frozen margarita machine. I'm usually cautious when getting drinks from a slowly churning machine, but these margaritas are amaze. It's perfectly blended so you won't take a sip and be left with flavorless ice slush at the bottom of your cup. They make the mix in-house and it's just the right amount of sweet and sour. 

BONUS:
They have a late night Happy Hour from 10pm - close. $2 tacos & tequila shots!

I was out of town visiting friends from Tampa and we came here for the late night menu. The drinks were hit or miss. The late night menu was limited and the service was okay. We went up stairs to the rooftop deck and it was nice but a really random bunch of people. This place was fun for visiting but I wouldn't return back to this place.

Nashville classics and live music. The hot chicken is crisp & flavorful. The cobb salad was huge and filling. The cocktails disappointed me though. I thought the whiskey nelson was too sweet & the black jack julip had blackberry seeds - so many that it was annoying... Overall though a very pleasant experience with excellent service & atmosphere.

DO NOT GO HERE. By far the worst experience I have ever had at a restaurant, especially in New Orleans. The service was horrific, the food was straight up gross, and the OWNER was downright rude, unprofessional, and condescending. 

We tried to call over the manager (who we later figured out was the owner) to simply share the experience we were having. After we asked to speak to her, she purposely avoided us for at least 5-7 minutes. Once we talked to her, I truly couldn't believe she was the owner of a business. She was raising her voice at us, CUSTOMERS, and tried to compare their busy evening to what it would be like during Mardi Gras. I cannot reiterate how rude she was. 

Save yourself a trip- it's a terrible place all around.

Best beignets we had while visiting New Orleans! I had a few gift certificates from family so we ended up trying three different locations of Cafe Du Monde. We stopped in to the original French Quarter location early one morning (around 9 am or so) and there was no line. You seat yourself and then a server takes your order. There's also a walk up window where you can order to go. 

The menu is basic, they only serve beignets (three per order), coffee, cafe au lait, and a few other beverages. It's cash only so bring some money. My boyfriend and I got one order of beignets to split and each got a cafe au lait. Our order came out quickly and we paid our server right there. The beignets were fresh, hot, and pillowy and light! Not dense and chewy like some other beignets we tried. The mountain of powdered sugar make them pretty messy to eat so be prepared. The cafe au lait was perfectly creamy and with the addition of some powdered sugar, just the right sweetness.

I'm really glad we got to check out this location of CDM and would definitely go back on future visits to NOLA. You just have to!

We found another brewery within walking distance from our Airbnb while staying in Indy. I read a few reviews of Upland Brewing that mentioned the nachos so my boyfriend and I ordered those along with a couple flights. Our server was great and gave some good recommendations for beer. I loved the fruity Komplex sour! I noticed another server carrying a glass of something that looked fruity and asked what it was since I love a good fruity sour. She told me since it was Sour Saturday they were doing $6 pours from any sour bottles that they had on site. I ended up getting a glass of the cherry sour and it was delicious, with a really great sour cherry flavor. I also tried the Polar Bear Kisses, which is a bourbon barrel aged imperial stout with cacao & peppermint. It was pretty tasty! I liked the chocolate and mint. It really made it more drinkable for me as I'm not a huge BBA stout person.

The nachos unfortunately were not my favorite. It was definitely a huge portion but the pile was so high everything kept falling off as we were trying to grab from the main plate. We did have a second plate that helped a bit, but it was still messy. Then underneath the pile there were so many naked chips, which is my biggest pet peeve when it comes to nachos. I wouldn't order them again but the salsa was really good and very flavorful. I'd definitely come back in the future to try more sours!

I'm really glad I read all the glowing reviews and ended up at Bacchanal! My friends and I stopped in one afternoon while visiting New Orleans and were pleasantly surprised at the lovely vibes in the courtyard. 

From the outside, it doesn't really seem like much, just a small house. Walking in, you enter a small wine shop and select a bottle (or two) or order by the glass. You can pick cheese and charcuterie from the cooler and they'll arrange a cheese board for you, or you can order more food from their full menu in the back. Then head through the back door and enter a dreamy courtyard full of people enjoying food, wine, and music together. There are ice buckets, ice, and water readily available in the courtyard. There was a really nice band playing some music that wasn't too loud while we were there - so key as I hate to have to shout over any band. I was a little sticker shocked at the cost of the cheeses since I had to purchase two boards with an $11 plating fee per board (plus the cost of the cheeses). The two boards totaled around $70, but it was a lot of cheese to split amongst the four of us. They come with a LOT of bread, I would have preferred some different options (crackers). I really liked the pickled veg, olives, and tapenades/spreads that came with the board.

The relaxing vibes and perfect weather added to our time at Bacchanal. There's quite a bit of room but it was starting to get pretty busy when we left and there was a line to get in. We spent quite a bit of time here and I'm so glad we made the trek to do so. I would definitely come back and try some of the other food -- I saw a whole fish and other items that looked great. Definitely a must-visit if you like wine!

Usually when people think to eat indian food it's mostly north indian food (such as naan and dishes like chicken tikka masala), but this place is super unique because is specializes in a southern indian cuisine which is hard to find around the city! (They also have the typical north indian food, but i've never had it so I can't speak to it, although a place that specializes in south Indian i'd definitely suggest to step outside your comfort zone and get that instead). I would suggest getting dosa (basically an Indian crepe) and there's various fillings you can get to dip in the chutney's and sambar, ask the waiters if you're unsure what to get they're very nice (but they can be a little slow to come around so ask all your questions at once). The food is amazing and very authentic and they give huge portions

I have always appreciated Rick Caruso's ambitious commercial real estate concepts & luxury retail mixed use developments.. Just look at his portfolio holdings & see what he has created with Rosewood Miramar, Palisades Village, The Americana, Westlake Promenade, etc!

Heard wonderful stories about this posh 5 star beach front resort. I had never visited while it was the prior Miramar property, before Caruso redeveloped it.

The resort grounds and pathways are beautifully manicured with lush gardens. The railroad crossing to get to Miramar Beach Bar & Caruso's (with frontal access to the shoreline) is a grandfathered, yet historical piece of Montecito.

From Miramar Beach Bar, you can walk down the stairs to the lower deck to enjoy the sand and white water views..

Wonderful dining options, retail therapy with James Perse, The Webster, Goop, or playing bocce ball. Located close by the Montecito Country Mart & San Ysidro Ranch.

Valet parking for overnight guests. And plenty of convenient street parking along South Jameson Lane for visitors.

Was thrilled to visit the rotational Dior Pop Up (prior to their anticipated closing after Labor Day weekend). Looking forward to coming back again very soon!

What do you do when hunger pains hit at 11:00 pm on a Saturday night, with a party of 12, and realize you are about eat at a restaurant that has two 2 & a 1/2 Yelp stars? Well......
My brother called a few restaurants to check the wait times and if they could accommadate a large party at the last minute. Luckily Lakeview Harbor was the only one who had availability.
 
We were greeted, seated immediately, and the server took our drink order. We all were hungry and did not take long to review the menu. I played it safe and ordered a cheese burger well done with a baked potato. I prefer my burgers cooked between medium and medium well but the server stated that would have blood in the middle. Ok no need to second guess on this one because I don't do blood!!!!  

Impression of the burger:
1. I prefer sliced cheese than shredded. 
2. It was a bit on the dry side and hard on the ends however; the vegetables and bread were fresh. 
All in All: It was edible and satisfied my hunger. The baked potato was pretty good.
Lakeview Harbor is a relatively small restaurant with decent food and service.  Parking is limited in the front so take advantage of the street or neutral ground.

What do you get when you mix grapefruit, vodka, basil, and mint in a little glass? Haha a great time at Brick Top's. Our server Shalik recommended their signature drink, Charred Grapefruit. I looked at the ingredients and immediately cringed but he assured me that if I didn't like it I can return it. Ok deal!!!! Surprisely it was refreshing and had a good amount of alcohol. 

Love the service, warm ambience- "Houston's on St. Charles in New Orleans vibe," and delicious food. I normally don't cheat on my diet but when I do it is for good reason like receiving a $100 BT gift card.

I ordered the Grilled Trout topped with crab meat, champagne beurre blanc, capers, and served with broccoli. 

My husband ordered the BBQ Pork Baby Back Ribs, served with cole slaw and french fries. 
The ribs were tender and seasoned to perfection. Yes I had one, two, ok three and it had licking my fingers. 

We both enjoyed our dinner.

I declined dessert and decided to have a second Charred Grapefruit cocktail since I wasn't driving. 

Overall a great restaurant for date night, a business meeting, drink after work, or for any occassion. There is a private parking lot with spaces on the side and back. BT is upscale so appropriate attire is recommended. 

All in all, was it worth the cheat? Heck yeah!

My first time at Darfone's and I will be back. We (party of two) walked in on a Saturday evening and were seated immediately, no wait time.

Darfone's offers a casual dining experience ideal for a families, couples, groups, and business meetings. 

Our server Kaylan was excellent! She was knowlegable of the wine and dinner menus and attentive to our table. 

The complimentary bread and flavored olive oil dipping was pretty good too. 

We ordered a plate of ribs with a side of fries to share. Drinks- Moscoto (me) and a Wise Stout beer. The ribs were served hot! I highly recommend the ribs they are tender, full of flavor, and absolutely delicious.

I enjoyed the customer service, food, and atmosphere. Too bad they are closed on Sundays.

Nashville has definitely stepped up the nightlife scene. LA Jackson sits on top of the four star upscale, Thompson Hotel. It is a trendy rooftop bar and lounge with a beautiful view and relaxing ambience.  A group of us went on a Friday night at 7:00 to celebrate a friend's birthday and it was packed. They offer bar, indoor, and patio seating. 90 mins. later we were able to grab a table on the open seating patio. Everyone enjoyed their food and drinks underneath the clear sky. The drinks are pricey but strong. The catfish chips were hit.  Feel like dancing?  There is a small dance floor in front of the DJ booth. He played 90s hip hop, pop, and R&B music. 

We had a great time and will definitely return. Our server recommended that we try brunch as he mentioned that food and mimosas/drinks are just as good but with less of a crowd.

After nine be prepared to possibly be waitlisted to receive a token to the rooftop. Patrons must be 21 and up. 

There is a Premier Parking lot across from Bar Louie but make sure your time doesn't expire or you will get a $65 ticket.

This relatively small venue with indoor/ outdoor dining and bar area must be one of Nashville's best kept scerets, because I never knew it was there. It is located on the Cumberland river where you can enjoy kayaking, paddle boarding, sailing, and biking. 

Parking is located on an unpaved lot. Its a short walk to the restaurant but you have to  cross a dock and floating barge 1st. Ladies be mindful of footwear as unleveled ground can be a potential hazard and/or injury in heels.

It is a very casual restaurant meaning shorts, flip flops, and bikinis with appropriate coverups are welcomed.

Our table ordered the Fried Calamari $9 and Crab Cakes $11 appetizers. Both were good, but the Calamari was to salty for my taste.
I took a chance and ordered their signature dish "Good 'Ol Po-Boy"- fried shrimp served with lettuce, tomatoes, onions, cajun remolade sauce, and a side of sweet potato fries $12. Surprisingly, it was delicious!

Everyone in our party of 20 enjoyed their meal, the A+ service, and the overall waterfront experience.

I absolutely love Vege-Licious. I have been several times and am pleased with consistency of the friendly welcoming staff, delicious southern comfort vegan food, and soothing ambiance. 
It is a small restaurant with four tables that seat two comfortably, outside tented seating is available as the weather permits. Enjoy sounds of jazz as you dine-in or take out. 
I always tell myself that I am going to try something else on the menu but steer towards the Soul Food Plate or newly added to the menu the Soulchic Plate Hot. 
They are that good!!!!
*The Soul Food Plate comes with barbecue tempeh, sweet potatoes, greens, macaroni and cheese, and a roll. 
*Soulchic Plate- Hot soy, mac and cheese, roasted seasoned potatoes, greens, and a toasted bun. 
So from that description, how could one choose?!?
I love the Sorrell and Ginger Beer. I try to drink one every two weeks to take advantage of its many health benefits. 

If you haven't tried it you don't know what you are missing and yes meat eaters are welcome. ;-) 

I just can't get enough of Vege-licious.

Fun, fun, fun!!!! First time at Top Golf with a  friend and her co-workers and we had a blast.
This is such a cool concept and great addition to Nashville! Topgolf is a huge venue, so ladies from personal experience leave the stilettos at home especially if you plan on playing. There are HDTV screens, multiple bars, good food, helpful staff, and cool ambience. Let me start by saying that I am great at a lot of things, but golf is definitely not one of them. You can be a novice like myself or Pro, it doesn't matter it is all friendly competitive fun at Topgolf.

The prices: open to noon $25, noon to 5pm $35, and 5pm to close $65. Our party of 12 arrived at 6pm on a Friday. We were told that it would be a 90 minute wait for two available bays, so we grabbed a table on the 2nd level and ordered food and drinks. By this time is was extremely busy and our server Mercedes apologized in advanced for the wait since the bar and kitchen were already backed up.

You can do two payment options: Cash pay to close out after every order or provide a credit card for an open tab. 
I ordered the Veggie Burger and a side of fries $10.50 and a Pineapple Punch $16.
Their drinks are strong which is why they don't allow you to purchase two strong drinks at a time. Everyone in our party enjoyed their food and drinks with no issues. 
 
Two hours later we received a text that our bays were ready. After checking in at the front desk, our party was escorted to the 1st floor bays by a staff member who gave us an overview of the games available, terms, and rules of play.

The line-up is limited to 6 players per bay. Each player swiped their $5.00 lifetime membership card, completed the entry information- first and last name and email address, and then swiped a credit card for payment. Each participant gets 20 balls. It was recommended that each person take turns hitting 5 balls each round to get through all 20 in an hour.

For all of you expert putt putt golfers, this experience will make you consider moving your golfing skills to the range. After a few warm-ups with the driver, an improvement in my form, and another Pineapple Punch I was able to hit the "sweet spot" more than several times. Although I came in last of my group (6th place) it didn't even matter because I had fun! 

After an hour of golf, we wanted to give the rest of the place a tour. Level 3 was my favorite it had live music, a lounge area, more fun activities like fooseball, and an amazing nighttime view of the range.

Some tad bits to mention: Every weekend so far this place is PACKED and I can't see it dying down no time soon.  The parking lot is massive and you will probably struggle to find a parking spot so car pool if possible. They do offer complimentary shuttle service and valet parking for a fee. You will most likely wait an hour or two (or even more) for a bay so plan accordingly. 
If you are military it's a 10% discount of the Top Golf fee.

I highly recommend this experience to everyone of all ages.
Overall, I'm a fan.  I can't wait to get a group together and go again!

A friend recommended that I give Nicholetto's a try, so I conveniently placed a to-go through their website. 

So many options, I chose...
Choose Your-Own Pasta bowl:
*1 out of 9 Pastas- I chose Spinach Fettuccini but wished I lived on the edge and picked Garlic Linguine or Red Pepper Bucatini.
 Just gives me a reason to return ;-)
*1 out of 6 Sauces- I picked the Pink Sauce that was absolutely delicious.
*Pick up to 5 Protein or Veggies for an added charge-
I chose the sauteed Zucchini and Squash for an added $2.95 and
Vegan meatballs $4.95
*Parmesan or Basil topping- I chose the Basil.
Added a side- The Chicago Chop Salad. Veggies were nice and fresh. 

My friend warned me that there is limited parking and it is in a sketchy neighborhood, so I scheduled pick up an hour before close.  I had no issues parked near the entrance and my order was ready when I arrived. Staff was friendly and the restaurant was clean. 

My food was well packaged and still warm when I arrived home. Nice-sized potions that I was only able to eat half and saved the rest for lunch the next day.  Actually it tasted better the next day, guess after the seasoning had time to sit. All in all it was really good and the garlic bread that came with it was perfect.

Support local small businesses and more than likely will return to try other delicious options.

I haven't been to this location since the much needed renovations and remodel so I must say, I like it. My girlfriend and I ate dinner here on a Saturday afternoon. We were seated immediately and greeted by our server, who brought out complimentary salsa and warm chips. I ordered my favorite a small Mango Margarita and Bean Burrito Especial without cheese or Sour Cream.

****PSA******Their margaritas are that good that the alcohol will sneak up on you so drink responsibly. For real. ;-)

The food came out quickly. It was warm, the veggies were fresh, and I enjoyed every bite. Our server was attentive to our table and often asked if we needed anything. Street and private lot parking is available but not the AT&T lot or you will get towed. Reasonable prices with vegetarian options. You can't go wrong with Mexican food or this Las Palmas.

I was blinded by the fire lamps in the parking lot, romantic ambiance, and good reviews that had me hyped that this may be my new favorite dinner spot.
My husband and I walked in on a Saturday night 30 minutes before close to be greeted by the hostess and seated. As we were walking to our booth we had to be extra careful because the floor was very slick. 

Our server introduced himself as he sat down the complimentary chips and salsa. Let me warn you that this is a Tex-Mex restaurant with more of a Texas influence so the salsa has as a mesquite smoke flavoring, but I personally prefer the traditional one. Their in-house made guacamole is pretty good however it is served on a bed of lettuce that made the texture a crunchy. I should have went with my first mind and ordered the table side guacamole, it just looked more appealing. 

As I glanced over the menu the drinks looked more desirable than the food but we ended up ordering the Cozumel Shrimp Tacos to share. Unfortunately it was not as good as I thought and we did not finish or wanted it to-go. Our server came back and attempted to rectify by asking if we wanted to order something else. We really appreciated his efforts.  I just asked for the check as I was ready to go. I placed my card down without even looking at the bill. Our server hands me back my card to say, my manager took care of the bill. 

Although the food was not what I had expected I did appreciate the excellent customer service and friendly staff. I would give UJ's a second shot for for some Table Side Guacamole and Happy Hour specials.

A night out with friends started at Bar Louie for food and drinks. We sat at the bar and enjoyed some laughs and friendly conversation with their awesome bartenders. I had two of their signature martinis, The Diva. I got my buzz on and was ready for some food. I had my pallet set on trying the Impossible Burger but unfortunately our server/bartender apologized and stated that they were out at all three locations in Middle Tennessee. I browsed through the menu and settled on ordering the Roasted Veggie Flatbread without cheese. It was -ight. 

Bar Louie offers Wi-Fi,  outdoor seating that is dog friendly with a leash, closes at 3am on the weekend, Happy Hour, Saturday and Sunday Brunch, and Weekly specials. 
The Gulch on Saturday night typically gets crowded after 6pm so plan accordingly and parking is available on the street for free or pay in a nearby lot or garage with the first hour free. 

Overall Bar Louie is always a fun place to unwind after work, kick it with friends, or host your next big event.

Thanksgiving dinner at Ruth's Chris

I decided early November that I did not want to deal with grocery shopping and spending countless hours cookingThanksgiving dinner this year for only three people. I conveniently booked on open table the last available slot at 11:15am. 

We arrived on time, valet parked, and seated immediately. The ambiance was nice and service was outstanding from start to finish.

They offered the Ruth's Chris classic a la carte menu in addition to a special multi-course Thanksgiving Dinner menu. Each came with warm complimentary bread. 
I ordered the Thanksgiving dinner, of course. Lobster Bisque, Oven Roasted Turkey, Stuffing, Cranberry Relish, Green Beans with roasted garlic, and for dessert Pumpkin Cheesecake with Vanilla Ice Cream. Everything was absolutely delicious. I was stuffed for the rest of the day. 
As an appreciation Ruth's Chris gave us a Take home box of Thanksgiving dinner to eat later or after Black Friday shopping, like I did. 

All in all, it was an overall perfect 5 star holiday experience.

Lazy take out on a Friday night using Yelp Eat24 has made food ordering simple and easy. I did not have to talk to anyone, worry if my order was taken correctly, or guestimate pick up time. I had everything at my fingertips. 
I ordered the Hot Tempeh Sandwich with seasonal rosted veggies. You can choose between mild and spicy. Don't underestimate mild it does have a lil' spicy kick.

Proceed to answer more questions??? 
Pickup time? ASAP
Payment? Cash 
Confirm your telephone number

Estimated time 10-35 mins. 

Click place order and a confirmation is sent to your email.

I was able to check the status of my order and it was ready 12 mins. later. 

Staff greeted me as I walked in, I proceeded to the pick-up counter, paid $13.38, and left with my food. 

Graze is a small restaurant with a 98 health rating and friendly staff. It is a nice chill spot for breakfast, lunch, or dinner. They offer smoothies, snacks, and desserts catered to a vegan diet. 

When I arrived home 40 minutes later my food was still warm and no microwave needed.
It was filling that I was only able to eat half of it. I try not to eat bread but couldn't resist the french bread that comes with it- my own little vegan po-boy. I enjoyed my dinner and will continue to utilize Yelp Eat24 as it fast and easy, just the way I like it.

I never thought I would be writing a review on a vegan restaurant in New Orleans but here I am and my goodness the food was absolutely fantastic. I was indecisive so staff offered samples of my choosing. 
O-M-G everything I sampled was so darn good. Staff was helpful, friendly, and offered supreme customer service. 

I love the buffet tables that you can see all of hot food and salad on display. I ordered a pick 4: orange cauliflower, cashew mac and cheese, greens, and stuffed bell pepper with corn bread, bread pudding rum, and praline candy. Everything was seasoned and cooked perfectly. 

My carnivore loving parents were curious, so I gave them a little bit of everything to try and they too loved it so much that they went for lunch the following day. 

The overall experience is five stars: food, service, presentation, and store cleanliness. 

Highly recommend whether you are Vegan or Meat and dairy lover. 
You won't be disappointed. 

Please check their Website/Facebook/ Instagram page for daily menu, updates, catering, and changes in store hours. 
https://www.sweetvegansoulfood.com

House of India is a casual restaurant that offers a great selection of authentic Indian cuisine with reasonable prices, dine-in/carry-out, attentive staff, and an extensive menu selection not limited to; vegan and vegetarian options. The food was generously seasoned with Indian herbs & spices. 

I ordered the lunch buffet for $10.95 that comes with a basket of delicious Naan. The Naan was warm, light and fluffy. I enjoyed every bite of my meal with no complaints to mention. The buffet was well maintained and stocked. The staff was attentive by keeping my table clean and glass filled with iced water. 

This was my second time here and it was a great experience. House of India is a clean restaurant, with friendly staff, offers a comfortable dining experience, and delicious food. It is worth a visit!

Hollyhock Hill is chock-full of Midwestern charm!  Family-style (big platters and bowls of delicious food).  Everyone in our family prefers white meat, so we specify that when making reservations.  Speaking of reservations, MAKE THEM... especially if you're going for lunch.

I know people who don't eat meat with bones in it, who make an exception ONLY for Hollyhock Hill's fried chicken.  Same goes for their beets... even beet-haters love the beets at Hollyhock!  

In warm weather you'll get cold tomato juice before the meal, and in cold weather, expect tomato soup instead!  I didn't notice any previous Yelpers mentioning dessert, so I'll let you know... everyone gets a dish of vanilla ice cream, and the server brings a caddy with chocolate, butterscotch, and mint syrups so you can top your ice cream as you like it.

Folksy murals of hollyhocks on the interior walls, pretty grounds.  You can buy a bottle of their light, sweet salad dressing to take home with you... or to send someone as an Indianapolis souvenir!

And Finger licking is what I did.... I love that this place is hidden in Ybor city and there are live chickens running around. It added a primitive effect to what I knew I came here to do... Which was to eat smoked meats, probably use my fingers and look barbaric since I will have sauce everywhere.  I ordered a meat trio because I am greedy like that and I have to try everything at once. Ribs, Chicken and Sausage with Collard greens and Mac & Cheese. I enjoyed every moment eating this meal and will be back again when twitching for some BBQ.

Being that my family is from Georgia and I was raised on this stuff, I  have to say their collard greens were on point. They had just enough spice that worked with the additional pepper sauce I like to put on my greens. This  places is laid back with just the heavenly smell of smoke and sounds of the meat cleaver.  I would recommend coming here when in the area and in need of a tender, juicy and flavorful meal!

I have had this placed bookmarked for a while. When my company told us they were going there for lunch..GREAT! and that the company was treating us because of our hard work...OMG EVEN BETTER!! 

The first thing I noticed was their awesome door and decor. I was told to check out the restroom as well, if I thought the door was cool. We made reservations and were seated immediately. There was a total of 7 of us. We started off with a bottle of wine, recommended by our server. It was a very smooth pinot noir. We also started with a variety of appetizers.

We ordered the following to share:

Okra Fries- Not overly battered or greasy. Just right. It tasted so good by it self, you won't need to dip it into the house made ketchup.

Lobster Claw Cocktail- It had a small kick, if you like spicy, you may not even notice it. There was a lot of cocktail sauce, which I like, but it was a bit overwhelming. My acid reflux was acting up because of the amount that was in it. Still delicious though and the claws were huge.

Fresh Calamari- Good- it  just wasn't anything memorable for me. 

Crab Mac & Cheese-  YumI was glad we were sharing this. Two bites was enough as this is very rich and hearty. I needed to make space for other food! 

Charbroiled Oysters- I love my oysters raw, and have had my share of charbroiled oysters. But THESE charbroiled oysters were amazing! I couldn't just have one, we ordered another half dozen! The garlic butter was on point for my taste buds!

For my entree, I chose the Gouda Grouper. The fish was cook well but I wish there was more Gouda. The fish didn't take any of the gouda flavor, so they didn't really mesh together uniformly. It was like eating fish. Then eating Gouda. 

For dessert we ordered the following to share:

Flourless Chocolate Torte- Yummy! I love anything chocolate, but this was a great consistency as well as taste. I could've eaten more!

Key Lime Key West Ice Cream Stack- I will start off by saying I am not a fan of Key lime, it's too tarte for me, so that is just a personal preference. But I will say, however, that this was good in taste, it wasn't too tart for me. Some places are

Candied Duck Maple Bacon Ice Cream- This is their famous dessert. I wanted to love it, but I don't. The ice cream was good, the added duck bacon bits was good as well, but the cinnamon corn flake tasted a bit stale. 

Overall, I would say come and order a bunch of appetizers (tapas style) as they were all so good and you get a wide variety of flavors to choose from. Next time I will try other apps that I didn't get to this time. The decor is trendy with a nice view. It is a bit noisy as it can and does get packed. But it's a fun environment and a cool place to check out.

C'mon.

That's about all that needs to be said about Bogart's. It's too good to really try and put words to it. I think a lot of people want to find the "best ever" here, and honestly, you just might. That being said, BBQ is one of those creations that can't possibly have a "best ever" -- but if you're in St. Louis and love BBQ, this is definitely a "can't miss" spot.

Tip: seating is limited, but on a nice day you can walk your order to the park and enjoy. Also, you can order ahead or get it delivered if you're not too far -- all good options.

The only reason I'm not giving them 5 stars is because when asked the girl said their waffle comes are not homemade. A homemade waffle cone MAKES an ice cream, IMHO.

The salted caramel was labeled as a favorite and it lived up to its reputation. So good!  I tasted some nuts in their too. 

It's a cute, clean shop located on a canal of Hudson Beach. If you're in the area, it's worth the pit stop.

If I could give this review 0 stars I would. 

We contacted the Birchwood for a business dinner nearly 1 month ago. We met with the GM, Todd McNulty, who informed us this would be a great venue and he knew how our night needed to run since he use to work at Roy's (and use to run this type of business meeting there). Great!   This was exactly what we needed to hear. 

After not hearing anything after I left several messages stating I was ready to book it, I took a trip to Birchwood to see Todd. He apologized profusely and directed us to Susan, the event coordinator. I told Todd I was concerned with the lack of communication and was worried this was how my experience was going to be. Todd assured me that we were in good hands. Ha!  That was so far from the truth. 

After contracting, passing out formal invitations to my guests, I received an email from Susan informing me that Birchwoood was canceling my event. Mind you this was 2 WEEKS prior to my event. And how unprofessional was it for them to cancel on me via email...not even the professional courtesy to give me a call. 

What a POOR way to conduct business. 

Nearly 24 hours later and still no follow up from Birchwood. I shouldn't be surprised since this seems to be how they operate. 

I will never give The Birchwood any of my own money nor spend any of my business dollars there. 

The establishment may be beautiful but that doesn't mean anything if you can't run a business. 

BEWARE!! Run to Parkshore Grill, Cassis or 400 Beach Drive for a fantastic experience.

What a great addition to the neighborhood!  Forget Starbucks down the road, this is the place to be. 

The owner, Richard, was so friendly and was proud to tell me about the ingredients they use in their products. The sweetener for the coffee drinks is a corn syrup free concoction from France. France?  Sign me up. I loved Paris and anything french automatically makes my heart skip a beat. The interior is warm and inviting. Richard put some serious thought and cash into this place. 

Packed on a Saturday morning, I decided upon the veggie frittata while waiting in line to place my order. It was great. Not a huge serving, especially for this pregnant woman, but really good. I haven't had a coffee since finding out I'm pregnant, so I decided to splurge and order a French vanilla latte. The drink was great-hot but not scalding, and the flavor was robust. 

I'll definitely be back to support this neighborhood business.

I'm giving this place 4 stars because of its uniqueness and the need for this type of establishment in Tampa. 

We arrived at 630 on a Sunday night and immediately checked in for your reservation. We waited about 10 minutes to be sat, which was great considering this place was hopping and quite busy. 

The menu is "floridian" and local. There was menu items with gator, cornbread, grits, pompano etc. 

We opted to place an order for the jalepeno cheddar quick bread muffins. There was 4 in the order and they were quite tasty and went will with our side salad. 

For our entree we ordered the pompano, the grouper and the flank steak. The winner was the flank steak, sadly the pompano wasn't all that great and I wouldn't order it again. The grouper looked pretty tasty. 

After dinner, our server walked us outside. What a lovely set up!  It's right on the water with a huge field. Big enough actually that you could host a private party on the grounds. There is also a Biergarten and a hidden roof top bar. So cool!  We took a mini tour of the brewery and had samplings of the wedding beer (get this!) and the pale ale. 

This is definitely a place to take out of towners and locals alike to give them a true taste of what Tampa has to offer. Well
Done, ulele!

I have to admit, I wouldn't have found this place on my own but I frequently check out Rich's profile to see where he's been. He has a knack of finding the hidden gems especially in Clearwater.   When I saw that he's checked into Manos 2x recently, I had to check it out. 

Manos is located in a small strip center on the corner of Hercules and drew street (there is a westshore pizza in same shopping center).  Upon entering I immediately fell in love-the smells, the menu board, the pastries on display and the warmth and friendliness of the owner and cashier. 

They immediately offered me a sampling of their spinach pie and a cheese like phylo pie-sold!  Ill take one of each. Their tempting displays were like a force I couldn't conquer.  "Here try this"!  Yep ill take a container of those heavenly cookies. 

Manos offers sandwiches and salads too, unfortunately I couldn't get past the goodies on display. 

I will definitely be back to this wonderful bakery where everything is homemade and made with love and pride.

Marginal at best and sadly this place won't last. We so desperately need a great Mexican restaurant  in the oldsmar/Westchase area and this is NOT the answer. I will gladly drive to Besito or Casa Tina for authentic food. 

From the moment we walked in the vibe was off. We sat outside on a Monday and it took forever to get someone to acknowledge us and take our drink orders. For $15 margaritas I expected some great libations and we did not receive that. Ingredients were missing, presentation was off, even the water glasses were odd and difficult to drink from. 

The chips and dips were decent but that was were it ended. Our table ordered the green enchiladas, the veggie fajitas and the chicken fajitas. None of the options were good-the veggie fajitas had nothing more than onions and peppers. The Green enchiladas had dried out chicken and the chicken fajitas were boring. To top it off, the shells served with the fajitas were cold, grocery store style and the rice and beans tasted like rice a Roni and out of a can. 

At 9pm, they turned the music off and basically made it so we had to leave. 

Will we return-absolutely not.

Don't pass this place up. It looks like nothing on the outside, but the food it fresh and delicious. Authentic and a high value. Very friendly service and there is a big selection to choose from. I really like the little taco/tostada that is made with the fresh corn tortilla and the grilled pasilla peppers. Yum.

Our visit to Downey's exceeded all expectations. We knew it was going to be an expensive fine dining experience at one of Santa Barbara's elite restaurants. Our expectations were sky high when we walked through the door. And somehow, they still turned out to be a very pleasant surprise. The service and the food were outstanding. It compares will with the most elite restaurants in California. They also maintain a personal touch that's not the least bit pretentious. Every part of the meal was excellent. Food, service, and atmosphere were all top notch. The next time we visit Santa Barbara, a visit to Downey's will definitely be in our plans.

Is it enough  just to use the word WOW!!!???  This place was amazing! My friend and I went to their bourbon dinner this evening, along with Wild Turkey Bourbon.  This was my first time there, and they certainly did not disappoint! The tasting menu was beyond my expectations for a bourbon pairing. Make sure to look at the menu picture I posted.  The menu was a complete feast of surf and turf... Everything from scallops to turkey and filet mignon.  Then adding an amazing bourbon with each one was over the top. But wait, then came the fifth course of dessert... grilled honey pound cake with peaches and ice cream, and American honey bourbon to compliment it!  Now, since I have never been here before I know that I will certainly be back to try the menu. The event coordinator, Elizabeth, was fantastic for the evening! The chef, Ricky, knocked it out of the park!  If you ever get an email inviting you to any of their dinners just say yes! It was worth every single cent!

You know, all I can give it is a 3...I've now had, pie, cake and a cookie from here and it's always the same reaction - eh.  Then I look at the prices and ask myself what am I missing...then I realize it's the $ I paid for a great piece of pie/cake or a cookie.  The berry pie I had wasn't even juicy, the cake was dry and the cookie unremarkable.  The only thing that adds to it all is perhaps the "gold dust" that seems to be everywhere.  I don't know, maybe just me, but I most likely won't be back.  I want what I paid for...

My friend had come here before, and she wanted to take out the gang for lunch. Her son lives out in Reno, and has become one of the locals, this Vietnamese Restaurant is popular here. I'll have to say, it's quite clean, floors and tables. Menu selection is pretty wide, and you'll find some of your favorites. 

None of us went family style as each of us were craving something different. Some items that were ordered, and I apologize if I don't have the correct names off the menu, were Beef Pho. Spring rolls, won ton mein, a chicken vegetable dish, and two of my friends both ordered an Iced Vietnamese coffee. I normally drink coffee, but only on work days. From my seat, it looked so good as they poured condensed milk into their glass of ice coffee. 

Lots of free ample parking right out front. None of us needed to use the restroom, so no actual review on that facility.

Most Trader Joe's are located in the suburbs of a town or city. This one was outside of downtown in a nicer neighborhood of Reno inside of a strip mall. October was definitely a Halloween/Fall month and there were pumpkins laying out store front, end-aisles and displays of everything and anything pumpkin. Picking up groceries was mainly the purpose of the day. From snacks to salads to basically anything you might have forgotten in your toiletry bag. Price is always right, service from all clerks and cashiers are very consistent whenever you visit any Trader Joe's in any state. What I didn't expect to be such a good product, was their Pumpkin Overnight Face Mask. Coulda, shoulda, woulda bought more than one because another Trader Joe's that I went to stopped carrying it on the shelf :-(

Many think of BBQ when they visit the south. I think of fried chicken. 

This Nashville chain right here happened to be our last stop on this trip and have I had it earlier on, I would've eaten here more than once. Let me tell you why. First off, their southern hospitality is on point. We got our food to-go and as we left, they said bye to each of us by our first names. If you're not impressed by that, let's talk about their chicken. Fried until beautifully golden on the outside while remaining to be juicy from the inside, the flavors are indeed worthy of praise. Their chicken tenders were pretty darn amazing and you dare not miss it if I were you.

Crinkle-cut fries anyone? Oh yesssireee! Done just the way I like 'em. How about the most amazing honey mustard dip ever created? They got that one covered, too. Pimento mac n' cheese? Eh, not my favorite. But guess what? Everything else made up for it.

Offering Southern breakfast fare with a twist, this restaurant was named after Stanley from the play "A Streetcar Named Desire" by Tennessee Williams, where the setting is at the French Quarter. As it is only appropriate, Stanley is located in a prime spot in Jackson Square with a grand view of St. Louis Cathedral. And that's only a bonus! The main attraction here is the food and stellar service. 

You may have to wait a bit to get seated but next door is Stanley's Cafe where a cup of cafe au lait could be enjoyed, or you can kill time admiring all the street art in this plaza until you get a text message that your table is ready.

We knew what we wanted right off the bat and shared the following items between two people as Stanley and Stella probably would:

LOUISIANA JAMBALAYA ($8.50/sm) may have been the best jambalaya I've had, ever. Yes, I'm going there. The seasoning, the texture of the rice, and the combination of flavors from the Andouille sausage and spicy chicken was like watching a star-studded play of love, hate, and betrayal where each component portrayed its role resulting in dramatic ups and downs of emotions.
