The room had been booked for two hours, but the event ended up going almost three hours because of how long it took for the food to be served. We ended up not having time to play one of the games we had planned, and many of the attendees had to leave before the event actually ended due to it running late. 

While Brio impressed me with the food, I would really be hesitant about organizing a party here myself.

Very pleased with my recent dinner experience here! The sushi was delicious, the restaurant is clean and polished, and the staff was very friendly!

My friend and I walked in at roughly 5:45pm and were quickly seated at a table for two in the back of the restaurant. The table was nicely arranged with pretty dishes, white cloth napkins, and menus. After reading through the menu, we decided to share two appetizers and three sushi rolls. 

The appetizers we chose were the Fried Gyoza and Crab Rangoon. The gyozas were alright, at best. They were kind of flavorless to be honest. The rangoons however were fantastic! They were fried perfectly and filled to the brim with creamy crabmeat. They came with an outstanding dipping sauce that was so good that we had to ask the waitress what exactly was in it. Coconut and cucumber is what we were told and oh my gosh, it was divine. Wish I could buy a jar of it to keep at home!

The rolls we ordered were the Fire Cracker and Kani Kamakazi off of their speciality menu and the Spicy Tuna Crunch off of the maki menu. Out of these rolls, the Fire Cracker was my least favorite. Although the menu said it came with spicy tuna, I didn't taste spicy at all. It tasted rather... fishy to me. My friend and I both agreed that the Kani Kamakazi was definitely the best! The crab that came in this roll was delicious. I also really enjoyed the honey wasabi sauce and tobiko that it was topped with. At $17, this was the highest priced roll that we got and it was worth every penny!

Although our waitress was a total gem, service was very slow at times. The restaurant really started filling up fast towards the end of our meal, which is about when we started struggling to get our waitresses attention for extra napkins and for the bill.

I'm not in Chestnut Hill too often, but I definitely wouldn't hesitate to return to Osaka next time I am! I enjoyed my meal very much. The only thing I would change next time is skipping over the gyozas and instead getting another appetizer or sushi roll!

This was my first time visiting this franchise and I was not disappointed! I was craving Mexican food but something with a bite and the Korean bbq bowl that I got totally hit the spot. It came with rice, fajita veggies, sweet and spicy Korean bbq sauce, slaw, sriracha and pork. Everything was great but the pork was definitely the best! The entire dish was really flavorful and for sure gave me that spice that I wanted. My fiancé had the California sunset bowl (which seems to be their staple) - I tried a bite of it and liked that as well.

I would say California Tortilla is similar to a Panera in that you place your order at the counter, grab a table, and they'll call your name when your food is ready. The restaurant was pretty crowded when we went but our food was still prepared quickly. This was perfect for us because we didn't have too much time on our hands and wanted a speedy lunch. 

My favorite part was the "Wall of Flame" which has shelves upon shelves of hot sauce bottles! From mild to "mouth on fire" hot, they've got every kind you can imagine and you're free to grab as many as you want to test out and add to your meal! I love this fun and unique concept!

My only complaint was the portion size. Both of the bowls we got seemed a little small compared to the  bowls you would get at any other fast-casual spot. Still, I'm glad to have finally tried California Tortilla and will happily add it to my list of quick and casual go-to spots!

I was here with friends for Sunday brunch and I'm sad to say, it was a huge disappointment. The menu wasn't very extensive, but it still took me awhile to decide what to get because nothing was screaming out to me. I ended up getting lox and eggs, which tasted bland. It came with multi grain toast with no butter, no cream cheese, no jelly... just plain toast. The poor presentation did not help in any way. For such a well known restaurant, shouldn't the meal be somewhat eye appealing?

The ambiance was pretty, but I was really disappointed with the customer service. I got there before my friends and asked for a table for 4. My friend brought her 6 month old along as a surprise since we hadn't yet met him. Little did we know, the restaurant would cause a stink about having to find a table for 5 instead. It was astonishing that this was such a big deal when they weren't even that busy. All they had to do was push a small table next to our original table for 4 and provide a high chair. 

Poor customer service was not a good way to start what was supposed to be a nice and relaxing get together. I wish I could say a good meal made up for bad service, but it definitely did not.

THIS PLACE! Ahh, I'm so happy to have found it!

My boyfriend and I were looking for a casual spot to grab dinner and decided on Destination Dogs. We hadn't heard much about it so all we were expecting was to walk in, get some hot dogs, and walk out. When we went in and realized it was a pretty large, spacious, and very contemporary establishment, we were rather surprised! Little did we know that our quick "pick up and go" was going to be a lively dinner outing instead.

After reading through the very extensive menu, I decided on the The Oscar: Los Angeles which came with avocado, cabbage, tomato, chipotle mayo, and scallions. It normally comes with chicken sausage, but I chose to get chorizo sausage instead. It was delicious and definitely hit the spot! It was loaded with chipotle mayo which I really appreciated! The hot dog came with house made chips which were just ok. I couldn't help but wish they were fries instead. :\

Service at this establishment was great. Our waiter, Craig, was fun, energetic, helpful, and accommodating. My boyfriend chose to get the Mighty Duck: Anaheim, but wanted to make some minor adjustments, and Craig was more than happy to do so. We definitely took note of his great service!

As if good food wasn't enough reason for us to love this place, we made our way to the game room after dinner. Yes, they have a game room! It is located on the first floor, by the bar, and has a pool table, darts, and arcade games. With something to keep everyone entertained, I will surely be returning to Destination Dogs with friends in the future!

I've been here twice now to do work and both of my experiences have been lovely. The WiFi is strong and the café is cozy and just so darn cute - totally Instagram worthy! The coffee and treats are such a delight too. 

During my most recent visit on a blistering cold day, I had a dirty chai and a slice of pie. Although the dirty chai was good, it probably could have used a bit more chai spice. Still, it was the perfect drink to warm me up. The pecan and brandied fig pie that I got was phenomenal. In my opinion, you can never go wrong with pecan pie but I usually only have it on Thanksgiving. When I saw it on the menu at Lil' Pop Shop, I knew I had to get it. The crust was perfect and I really liked that it was topped with an ample amount of fig. They really took a basic pie to the next level!

I'll keep this place in mind for next time I'm in the area and need some caffeine and a place to stop and get work done. Lil' Pop Shop is a gem!

When looking for some Thai delivery options, I came across AmeriThai and my boyfriend and I thought we'd give it a try.

Our order consisted of Crab Rangoons, Massaman Curry, and Crazy Noodles. It was delivered in an appropriate amount of time, but sadly, the packaging was a disaster! The curry and noodles were both delivered in disposable aluminum foil containers with white paper lids and were literally DRENCHED in oil and curry. It was such a mess! I don't think curries should be stored and delivered in this kind of packaging. 

As far as the food goes, I would rank it as follows: #1 Crab Rangoons, #2 Crazy Noodles, and #3 Massaman Curry. 

In my opinion, you can never really go wrong with rangoons, but these were probably some of the best I've ever had. They were fried perfectly! I loved how crispy they were. 

The Crazy Noodles came with broccoli, carrots, cabbage, onions, and mushrooms in a hot chili oil. They were good, but as I said above, drenched in oil. Way too much. 

The Massaman Curry was just alright. The vegetables in it were all fresh, but the curry was pretty flavorless. I tasted more coconut milk in it than any of the spice/seasonings. I wish it had a bit of a kick to it. Our protein of choice was pork and I did like how tender it was. 

Unfortunately, this place didn't really do it for me. Maybe their food tastes better fresh out of the kitchen than through delivery, but either way, there's other Thai restaurants I'd much rather choose than this one.

I used to go to the Sabrina's in University City a lot during my Drexel years, but a lunch date with my mom was what brought me to this location. We were both overall pleased with our meal and experience, although there were definitely some reasons why I couldn't find myself giving it a five star rating. 

We were both craving some kind of sandwich for lunch, so we decided to get two different ones and share. Although everything on the menu was pretty enticing, we ultimately decided on the Mel's Chicken Cutlet and the Tuscan Chicken, both from the sandwich menu. Since we had a choice of bread, we decided to get the first with multigrain and the second on a sarcone's roll. We also had a choice of regular, sweet potato, or Parmesan fries with both orders, so we got the last two. 

Our meals were served relatively quickly, and we were pretty floored with the presentation! Not only were the sandwiches HUGE, but they were very well presented! 

While both the sandwiches were good, we both agreed on some setbacks. The Mel's Chicken Cutlet which came on the multigrain bread was so tough and hard to chew. It appeared to be a little burnt on the edges, which tells me this thick bread was toasted a bit too much. The chicken was delicious, but since it was cornmeal encrusted, it added even more of a crunch factor. I usually like my sandwiches well toasted, but this was almost painful to bite into. The Tuscan Chicken was very tasty, but we were disappointed with the lack of sun-dried tomato pesto spread they used. The spread was fantastic, so it's a shame that they skimped out on it. 

Overall, this place is a win when it comes to staff, service, prices, and atmosphere. I would love to return for lunch again in hopes that the food will show a little improvement next time!

I'll be honest, I haven't been to too many Chipotle locations in my lifetime, but out of the few that I have, this one is my favorite. The meats and veggies taste fresh and the employees don't skimp out on them at all (even on that GUAC! Totally worth the extra $2!)

I usually go here in the evening and there is always a line. No need to worry about having to wait too long though because the line moves quickly! The staff really keeps things going!

The space is big, and although I always take my order to go, I wouldn't mind grabbing a seat and dining in. Everything is kept clean and tidy which is normally a concern for me with fast food chains. 

As long as the staff stays just the way they are and they keep giving me healthy portions of that guac ;), I will definitely be keeping this location my Chipotle of choice!

I have fallen in love with this Lebanese comfy, casual, cute cafe in University City! Beautiful atmosphere, superb staff, and delicious food are all the reasons why I plan on making this one of my "go to" spots. 

The establishment is so clean and spacious, with cute trinkets and decor scattered around. Seating is very causal which will make you feel right at home. As you walk up to the counter to place your order, you'll notice just how nice and friendly the staff is. They are very accommodating and patient with their customers. After placing your order, grab a seat as you wait for them to call out your number. 

I ordered the Chicken Tawook Kabob Platter with rice which came with two sides - I chose the Lebanese Salad and Muhammarah. I waited about 15 minutes for my meal to be prepared and to pick it up from the counter. The chicken was perfectly grilled with ridiculously good seasoning. The Lebonese Salad came with fresh veggies and mint. It was so refreshing and light; a wonderful side to accompany the heavier items (being the meat and rice). Lastly, the Muhammarah was SPECTACULAR. This red pepper and tomato spread was of such unique taste! It also had walnuts which added a great crunch to the creamy spread.

After finishing half of the platter, I was beyond stuffed and had to bring the rest home (which I definitely did not mind - it made for a great midnight snack!). Not only was I walking out with leftovers though - my boyfriend and I were sure to get some baklava to go! We chose one pistachio and one walnut which were both just as delicious as our entrees! Flakey, buttery, sweet, and the perfect dessert size portion. I personally took favor to the pistachio so that will be my choice for next time!

All in all, I had a wonderful first time experience at Manakeesh, and am already looking forward to my next visit! Highly recommended to anyone with a zest for eclectic food!

Beautiful and luxurious. Those are the first two words that come to mind when I think of Parc. Everything about this restaurant makes it a five star experience. 

I've been here a few times now. My first experience was to celebrate the engagement of two of my lovely friends. After that, it was for celebratory lunch outings. Parc served as the perfect restaurant for all of these occasions. The restaurant is gorgeous. I love the beautiful and decorative set up, high ceilings and the spacious seating arrangements. 

My favorite dish is the warm shrimp salad. It is so simple but tasty and just the right portion size. It can be the main course but will leave you with room for hors d'oeuvres or sides. I recently had the French onion soup before my salad and it was excellent. Hands down, the best French onion soup I have ever had. I devoured every last spoonful. The presentation for both of these dishes was flawless. 

Given the overall feel of this restaurant and the fact that the prices are a bit steep, this makes for a wonderful restaurant to visit for a special occasion. It's always packed so I would recommend making a reservation. I know I'll be keeping Parc high on the list for where to go for all future occasions!

I've been to Little Nonna's for dinner a couple times and it has never disappointed. The food is phenomenal, staff is friendly, and I really like the ambience and atmosphere. This place is definitely a keeper!

During my most recent visit, I had the Wild Mushroom Bruschetta for an appetizer. I'm honestly not usually a fan of bruschetta because I tend to think it's TOO touch and crunchy, but my boyfriend and I decided to give it a shot here since it was their special for the weekend. After just one bite, I was SO happy we had gotten it! It was to die for good! The bread was absolutely perfect - toasted well but NOT too hard to bite into. It was topped with pesto which really added to the flavor. I hope this special will one day be added to their daily menu! Until then, make sure to get it when you can!

Here's the breakdown of the entrees I have tried:

1) Spaghetti and Meatballs:  This ever so classic item is a total winner! The B+V+P Fontina stuffed Meatballs are absolutely incredible. They are HUGE and sooo flavorful and juicy! The entree is enormous which made it impossible for me to finish in one sitting. I took the leftovers home with me and this $19 entree made for 2 meals! SCORE. 

2) Sunday Gravy: If you are a meat lover, be sure to get this! This entree comes with braised beef short rib, hot fennel sausage, AND that incredibly tasty B+V+P meatball. These meats come with a side of the house macaroni. Once again, I'm biased towards the meatball, but the beef and sausage were also fantastic and super filling. Another entree that is sure to have leftovers. 

3) Bucatini Cacio E Pepe: I was extremely happy with this entree as well! Shallots, parmesan, black pepper, pistachios, and shaved foie gras all combined to make this entree creamy and very unique. I especially loved the pistachios which added a nice crunch to the macaroni. This entree was definitely less filing than the previous two, but just the right amount for one meal. 

Service at this place is prompt and staff is very warm and friendly. I was happy with my experience both times. 

I've sat both inside and outside (they have a patio at the back which I didn't know existed until my second visit!). I was a fan of the ambience of both. In my opinion, the indoor seating has more of a quaint, romantic, "date night" feel while outdoor seating is more vibrant, loud, and a little more casual. Both offer dim lighting and have a charming feel. I would recommend choosing between indoor and outdoor seating depending on the vibe you're going for. :)

I highly recommend checking this place out if you're looking for a nice Italian dinner spit! I know I will for sure be returning!

I met Michelle C for coffee and breakfast at Miles Table on a cold winter morning and I really liked it! The cafe has a very comfy, causal feel to it making it the perfect spot for us to meet and get some work done. 

We both ordered omelets with just slight variations in our three add-ons. I asked for onions, mushrooms, and provolone on mine which are staple omelet choices for me. It was very simple but delicious and huge! I enjoyed the whole grain toast and potatoes it came with and was happy sipping on my hot coffee between bites. 

I don't live on South otherwise I'm sure this would become my go-to breakfast joint. For now, it will be a good meet-up for both of us!

I've passed by Moriarty's several times, but for some reason, I was never interested in stopping in until just recently. I was craving some wings and remembered when my friend had told me they were some of the best she's ever had... and WOW was she on point or what. 

These wings were, hands down, the best I've ever had in Philly! I'm not a huge fan of bone-in meat, so I ordered the boneless wings (they just recently started offering boneless! Yay!). They don't have any options for seasonings/sauces, which I was kind of disappointed about at first, but later realized it was not a problem at all. Their wings are so delicious and flavorful, I was fine not selecting my own sauce!

I also want to note that my boyfriend got the bone-in wings and said they were fantastic and some of the best he's ever had (which says a lot coming from him - this man loves his wings!). 

Staff is wonderful, prices are great (just $10 for boneless wings, $13 for bone-in), and the atmosphere is exactly what you would expect from an Irish pub. I wasn't feeling a drink, so I can't comment on that, although they have a full bar and a huge amount of beers on tap so I'm sure there's nothing to complain about on that end. 

After just one visit, I know where I'll be going when craving wings!

This was my first time at SPiN and it certainly won't be my last! So happy its made its way to Philly!

It is located right beneath the WeWork building on 15th, next to &pizza (how fitting for those who get the after hours beer munchies after SPiN!). The bar is quite big with several ping pong tables, a huge bar, and even a private room (the Red Room). They had a pretty solid DJ the night I was there who was SPINning (see what I did there?) top 40s as well as the best 90s hip hop and rap jams. I spent about an hour there in total, and the crowd was continually growing throughout.

They have an interesting drink menu with some  innovative and memorable cocktails; some of which are even Philly themed including the Gin Jawn and Fishtown Throwback . I decided to go with the Gin Jawn which was good, but honestly, not quite worth the $13. 

In summary, I really enjoyed my first experience and will definitely be returning. This whole concept is new to Philly, so I can absolutely see SPiN becoming the next new hot spot. Whether you want to put your ping pong skills to the test or just want to grab some food (yes, they have food!) and a drink with your crew, it is definitely worth a try!

Easily one of the best new brunch spots in the city! Great vibe, amazing food, friendly staff, and reasonable prices. What more could you ask for?

The restaurant is very spacious with a cool and casual vibe. Exactly the kind of place I'm looking for when brunching. 

My friend and I couldn't make up our mind about whether we wanted a sweet or savory dish so we decided to get one of each and split them both! In my opinion, this was totally the way to go. We decided to get the Classic Benny (we subbed the ham in for bacon) and the Red Velvet French Toast and oh my gosh... UH-MA-ZING. The Eggs Benny was great, but to be honest, I've never really had a bad experience with Eggs Benny. It's a pretty basic brunch item that can be found pretty much anywhere. On that note, I was VERY impressed with the Red Velvet French Toast which is quite a rarity (I've seen Red Velvet Pancakes before, but never French Toast). It was extremely rich with just the right amount of sweet to balance out the savory Eggs Benny. The cheesecake filling was to die for. Full disclosure: towards the end, I was eating it by the spoonful. (Place embarrassed emoji face here).

My boyfriend ordered the Short Rib Hash and it was delicious. The IPA cheese sauce it came with was amazing! The short rib was of a very generous portion. 

Our waitress was nice, giving us food suggestions when asked. Service was fairly quick which our group of 4 really appreciated. Prices are very reasonable. 

I will definitely be back to The Little Lion for my next brunch rendezvous. My boyfriend and I have already decided that we will be splitting the Red Velvet French Toast and Short Rib Hash next time!

After hearing (and reading) so much about Pizzeria Beddia, I was itching to check it out. I finally did and I couldn't help but wonder what all the hype was about. 

My friend and I walked in at exactly 5:35 pm on a Saturday (we must have lucked out because there was no line). Let it be know that they open at 5:30 pm. After taking approximately 3 minutes to decide on what to order, we decided on one regular pizza, half with sautéed onions and the other half with jalapeños and one broccoli rabe pizza for our group. After jotting down our order, the guy told us our order would be ready at... 9:20 pm. I REPEAT... 9:20 pm!!! After picking our jaws up off the floor, my friend and I realized he was being serious and reluctantly agreed to pick it up then. We had been warned that their wait time can be pretty lengthy, but almost 4 HOURS?!?! Insane if you ask me. 

After picking up our pizzas and taking some pictures (had to), my friends and I dove in. Our first reactions were how perfectly crisp both the pizzas were. Not soggy, no doughy, just crisp and perfect. As far as the pizza sauce and toppings go, both were good but we all agreed that the broccoli rabe outplayed the regular pie. 

We were over all happy with the pizzas, but I couldn't help but think "did we really just spend 60 bucks for 2 pies and wait 4 hours for them?". In comparison to other pizza joints I've been to in Philly, this was definitely the steepest in price and the wait time was by far the longest. I understand that the pizzas are made fresh to order, in one oven, but come on! They just weren't worth it to me. 

If you want to check this place out to make your own call about whether it lives up to the hype, take note of the following:

1) Cash only! It's approximately $30 a pie, so bring cash accordingly. 
2) They ONLY accept orders in person at the establishment. Don't bother trying to find a number to call because they don't have a phone.
3) Make sure you go long before you actually want to pick up your pizza. Like, hours before. In fact, maybe even BEFORE they open to avoid a possible line. 

Personally, my one visit to Pizzeria Beddia was enough for me. Am I glad to have checked it out? Yes, but I'll get my pizza elsewhere next time.

Green Eggs is primarily known for their brunch, but this review is based on the lunch I had here the last week of 2017. 

This place is always packed, so I was thinking 1:00 pm on a Wednesday during the holiday season would be a slower day for them... but wrong I was. Just as usual, it was swamped. After about a 15 minute wait, my friend and I were finally seated. 

Service was good. Our waiter was prompt in bringing us menus, taking our orders, and serving us. My la Colombo coffee came quickly, same with our food. 

I got the chicken caprese sandwich with Spanish fries. This sandwich comes with grilled chicken, mozzarella, tomatoes, and balsamic aioli. Although normally served in focaccia, I asked for their toasted, thick cut, whole wheat bread instead. 

The chicken was well grilled and the mozzarella was fresh. I also liked the balsamic aioli, but felt like there wasn't enough of it for this thick sandwich. All in all, although the sandwich wasn't anything extraordinary, it was good, quite big, and of a reasonable price ($14 to be exact). The Spanish fries came with sautéed veggies (onions and peppers) and definitely had a kick to it! Between both the sandwich and fries, I only got through about half of my meal but was happy to bring the other half home with me for leftovers. 

It's a bit of a disappointment that Green Eggs is cash only, but it's helpful that there is an ATM on premise. My suggestion is to bring cash with you so you don't have to worry about a surcharge to take cash out!

Although Green Eggs doesn't have a lunch to necessarily crave or rave about, it certainly did not disappointment and I'm sure I'll return again sometime!

I had passed by Bistro on Bridge several times but my first time going in was just recently when my husband and I were searching for a restaurant with outdoor dining in Phoenixville. We were hoping to find a causal place to grab some bar food and drinks, and this restaurant was the perfect fit. 

Bistro On Bridge has upgraded their second floor rooftop beer garden with pandemic restrictions and cold weather in mind. All tables were set more than six feet apart. They have added several heaters to make sure their customers are warm and cozy. Staff members were required to wear masks, as were all customers unless actively eating or drinking. I noticed a hand washing station in the corner of the room which I thought was a cool touch given the current times. My husband mentioned that he thinks that used to be a bar!

While I was there, I kept it simple and sipped on some house red wine. My husband got a few different 6oz pours and was pleased with all of them. 

The food we got was really great! We started with a bavarian pretzel which was crispy on the outside, doughy on the inside, and served hot. It had the perfect amount of salt! It came with three dipping sauces. I will definitely be getting the pretzel every time I go here! 

For our mains, we go the turkey and brie sandwich and smoked gouda burger, and we split them both. Although both were delicious, I favored the burger and he enjoyed the sandwich. He said it reminded him of a dressed up version of the all famous Thanksgiving gobbler from Wawa which he is a big fan of! 

Our waitress wasn't overly friendly but very prompt and respectful. She made sure to keep a distance when taking orders and serving us. She also checked in on us throughout our meal. 

I'm looking forward to my next visit to Bistro On Bridge!Although I wish I had discovered this place during the winter, I'm excited to check it out in the warmer weather!

During my most recent visit to Reading Terminal Market, I heard a gentleman say "everything here smells so good" and that's when I realized that's just how I wanted to start this review - everything here really DOES smell so good. 

This market is a Philadelphia staple. Whether you're a local or a visitor, this is one of those places you just have to stop in to at least once. Whether you want to actually grab a meal, just take a walk around to see what all they have, or are looking to stock up on vegetables, fruits, meats, breads, or sweets, this is a great place to go to. Besides the delicious food, they also have some wonderful stands set up to buy great souvenirs and gifts. 

No matter what time of day you're visiting Reading Terminal, be prepared for a large crowd and lines. This is not the place to go to if you're crunched for time. I would recommend stopping in when you have time to spare. If this is your first time visiting, my other recommendation is to walk around the entire premise to see what all there is before you make any purchases. There are ample food options so it's nice to see what all they have to offer before making your decision. Just a few places that stand out to me include Meltkraft, Tommy DiNic's, Beiler's Bakery, Famous 4th Street Cookie Company, and Termini Bros Bakery. :)

If you're in or near Philadelphia, be sure to put Reading Terminal on your list of places to go to so you can take in just some of the greatness our city has to offer. Lastly, be sure to bring your camera/phone to take some photos and don't forget to bring along your appetite!

I've been here a couple times now. My first experience was for food and drinks and my most recent experience was for drinks after a comedy show at Punch Line. Factoring in both experiences, I'd give this place three stars. 

Goose Island Brewhouse is pretty big and well maintained. It has a cool set up with seats both inside and outside. What is lacking is their staff and service. When I went with my boyfriend and friends for dinner (group of four), it took so long for us to be seated. Apparently we arrived during a shift change and nobody knew who was to seat us. As a customer, very frustrating. Once we were finally seated, it took quite some time for us to get our food and first round of drinks. There was also a long wait for my friends to get their second round of drinks. 

As far as food goes, my boyfriend and I split the Smoked Chicken Wings which were alright, but way too spicy. My boyfriend has a pretty high tolerance for spicy food and even he felt like they were too much. We ended up not finishing our meal. 

My friends got the Fried Chicken Sandwich and Fish and Chips and weren't too crazy about their food either. From what I was told, the chicken in the sandwich was far too tough to chew. They seemed content with the fries that came with their entrees. 

Nothing to complain about as far as drinks go. I had the Rosé Cider my first time which was great. Second time around, I just stuck to wine. 

I wouldn't go out of my way to make a trip back here and I would definitely pass on the food. If I am to go back, it'll probably just be either before or after a show at Punch Line since it's right next door.

My husband and I stopped here for a quick dinner after seeing Tom Segura at Parx Casino. We wanted to catch the end of the Sixers game so Buffalo Wild Wings fit the bill. Unfortunately, our experience was anything but pleasant.

The boneless wings I got were some of the most poorly prepared wings I've ever had. They were tough, not juicy and needed a lot more of the sauces that I asked for. I was also really disappointed with the service. Although our waiter was nice, there were multiple occasions where we had to flag him down for water, to place our order, and for our check. I spotted him in the front of the restaurant chit chatting and mingling with the rest of the staff. It made me wonder what other customers felt about their service too. 

On the rare occasion that I'm in this area, this location wouldn't even cross my mind on places to go for a quick bite and to catch a game.

When giving a 5 star review I think, "Is there anything that could make this place better?".   I could complain about the lack of parking or wait time, but Pinky's is exactly what it should be for a little breakfast nook.

I like the fact that you can get self service coffee while you're waiting.  Every option on the menu is priced just right.  There are options from $6 to $15.  

Their menu is filled with healthy and protein filled options.  I feel like they have local culture based menu with options like breakfast cuban sandwiches or jalapeño bacon grits.  I always leave here feeling having a satisfied stomach and coffee buzz.

Went for dinner on a friend's recommendation. It was a great interactive experience. AYCE option at 26.99pp is a steal considering the amount of meat served. It included banchans, scallion pancake and tofu soup, rice and lettuce.

We got Spicy chicken, Spicy Pork, bonelsss short ribs( can be ordered only once) and Beef bulgogi. Loved the Spicy chicken!

They bring 2 meats at a time and there is a 2 hour limit to AYCE. But the meat portions are plentiful and well marinated. You cook them in the grill yourself which is bit of a challenge till you get a hang of it!( After burning a few portions,lol!).
We came out smelling but it was so worth it!

Food-5
Service-5
Ambience-4

I use to come here weekly back in the mid-90's through the mid-00's when I first lived in the area always getting the chicken cheesesteak.

Came back a couple years ago and the now "OG" Chicken Cheesesteak is just as good. The owners are no-nonsense but the service is quick. As of March 2021, no indoor dining and it's better to call ahead, especially during prime times. A staple of the dining community.

I saw that a new boba tea shop had opened next to my favorite Chinese restaurant and, of course, I had to try it.  My first experience there was fantastic!  The employees were very nice, helpful, and patient.  I ordered the house milk tea with boba balls and it was so tasty.  I love that they make their drinks out of real tea rather than from a power.  I also love how I can customize the sweetness level of my drink.  The decor is very nice and the atmosphere can be quite tranquil.  I could and did spend a couple hours here just reading.  Add in the free wifi you've got a great new addition to the Tucson beverage scene.  Be sure to get a punch card.

Perfect for our family. Everyone can get something they like, the food is fast and fairly priced, the casual ambiance is perfect for kids, and it's freakin yummy!

The tortillas are enough to bring us back again and again. The chili relleno with pork verde burrito is my favorite. Sometimes I get it without meat if I want it a little lighter. But it's got a little kick from the chili which I like. If it's not spicy enough for you, they have hot sauce you can add. The tamales are a little dry but still tasty. Tacos are always good, the veggie ones are surprisingly filling. 
Be sure to check out their featured specials, once there were tachos ( tator tot nachos) and they were awesome!

As a Taiwanese, I can guarantee that this is the most authentic boba tea you can find in Tucson. It tastes exactly the same as I used to have back home. My favorite is Chatime roasted milk tea with boba or pudding. If yoh are a big fan of boba tea, you must try this!

I randomly stopped by Lochel's to satisfy a sweet tooth craving and was unexpectedly surprised by how disappointed I was with my goodies.  The bakery wasn't busy at all and the workers seemed to have cared less that we were waiting.  Not good.

The items looked pretty good.  They seemed fresh with a very homemade look to them, but looks can be deceiving.   We ordered a black and white and a slice of banana cake with cream cheese frosting.  The latter was good - the cake was moist and the icing was just right.  However, that black and white was absolutely disappointing.  The cake was too dry and the icing was too thin.  I admit I am completely biased when it comes to these "cookies."  If you ever had the most glorious pleasure of tasting a black and white from Cheryl Ann's up in Boston, all others will fail - miserably.  

Prices were decent.  I doubt I'd come back again.  Given the abundant choices of other bakeries in the area, I imagine I can get better tasting goodies with better service.

Make no mistake, this hilariously named Indian/ Pakistani joint is the real deal. It may not be the center of fine dining in New Orleans, but they food is delicious, the dudes behind the counter are friendly and the food is dirt cheap. 

While I have eaten in better Indian places, these cats aren't far off the mark. The samosas are off the hook and they have a ton of vegetarian options. I don't know if I'd venture onto the "American" side of the menu but all of the Indian dishes are on point. 

Salt N Pepper is defiantly a dive. It's not fancy and it's a little grimy. But what more can you ask for out of a dive than friendly staff and cheap killer food?

FYI: BYO9FR (Bring your own 90s female rap). However, current Indian pop videos are provided.

UPDATE: After leaving an honest review I gotta say the last thing I suspected to find in my inbox a slew of insults, homophobic, and racist slurs. Real classy *Brian W.* I say that because this user did not exist before I left the review, I still hope this place does well.  

I always like to start with something positive before I divulge in anything negative so pros first. 

Pro the food here is great with a new feel to tapas with an Japanese flair I've almost never left a plate untouched. Its a refreshing concept that as a college student I could totally use since my ramen varies only from beef or chicken. 

Pro the bar downstairs is beautiful with a very warm feel i love the decor the warm colors were inviting and the price wasnt half bad either. 

Con the service is literally the absolute worst thing about this place. I know how high volume restaurants work as both a previous waitress and hostess and neither the staff, manager (young man in a suit with red hair), or servers knew what good customer service was. The hostess (young lady with black hair) not only lied to me and my party about the happy hour policy but admitted she lied the sat a group in front of my party and approached us about it as if she deserved an apology for being approached about the error. Typically what happens in these mishaps is the general manager comes to the party and finds out more about the situation, apologies for the mishap, and asks if there is anywhere else we'd prefer to be seated or tell us we are next but none of those things happened my party was largely forgotten about and because there was no more room for the last person of my party to sit we decided to dine at Cheu instead( great ramen place). 

We aren't even going to talk about the multiple other times there service has failed from the bartender being to occupied with his conversation with the hostess at the hostess stand about school (because he was literally right behind me) to give me a drink menu or acknowledge he had a customer. 

It sucks because I want this place to do so well the concept is so pleasing and the prices are great but for me to go back to that place would take a complete staffing makeover.

12/19/13 -- Re-posting this review under new restaurant name.

With a new chef at the helm, I decided to pop in for Happy Hour at the newly re-opened Agustin Kitchen (formerly Agustin Brasserie). I'm not sure of the reason for the name change. I like fancy sounding French names, personally. It sounds so much more glam. If it means I have to spend less money because of an American  name, though...hey, so be it...lol. 

$5: Crispy, crunchy calamari, red bell peppers, and cilantro in an ultra spicy red sauce. Very flavorful! I loved the breading -- it was different than most places I've experienced. It reminded me of cornmeal fried green tomato-type breading (lovers of Southern cooking will appreciate this) with an extra kick! The mussels in garlic white wine broth were a great value at the Happy Hour price of $5, as well. Both dishes are large enough to split between two people. And, for $5, you can have them craft you an interesting infusion, grab a glass of the house wine, or imbibe a magnificent margarita. (Try the pom sour with corrido, Grand Marnier, pom jam, local pom-white vin, and citrus -- so good!)

I love the lush, beautiful location of Agustin at the Mercado. The restaurant is a lovely modern and luxurious addition to the the neighboring shops. I am sure I will stop by for lunch or dinner soon to try the new menu. I'll update my review (and perhaps my rating) when I have a better scope of all the new changes as a whole. 

Happy Hour at the Kitchen is Monday - Friday, 3 - 6 pm, Friday & Saturday, 10 pm - close.

The elegant, yet relaxed...sophisticated, yet simple atmosphere at Wildflower makes it one of my favorite choices for dining out in Tucson. I find it to be a perfect spot for creating memorable "special occasions," but also for simply enjoying socializing and catching up with good friends.

Social Hour - 2:30 pm - 5:30 pm Daily

$4 Sangria! (cab, raspberry, brandy, cassis, & lime), specials on wine, drafts, and cocktails. They feature several fab apps to go alongside, as well -- try the wild mushroom toast with roasted garlic, arugula, and goat cheese on grilled ciabatta - so good! I rarely can make it over during the week...so, I love that Social Hour pricing is available on the weekends.

The Mains 

New American with nuances of European and Asian cuisine. Tender estancia grass-fed NY steak, luscious lemongrass skewered scallops, and succulent steelhead salmon are just some of the tempting offerings. I am still mourning over the fact that the lamb ravioli is no longer on the menu. On one of my last visits, I tried to console myself with a short rib ravioli in truffle cream instead. I still prefer the lamb, but the braised kale that accompanied it was divine! The fresh seasonal salads are wonderful during warmer weather, or when you feel inclined to have lighter fare. The wine list is plentiful, so you will surely find a nice pair for your meal.

Dessert

Some of the best 'I-don't-need-all-these-calories-but-I'm-going-to-have-it-anyway-I'll-do-4-extra-squats-tomorrow-to-make-up for-it' desserts I've indulged in. Anywhere. Creative, innovative twists on traditional favorites, along with an ever-changing chef's selection. I adore the current selection of warm pineapple upside-down coconut lime cake with anglaise, cilantro reduction, and coconut gelato. The warm apple crisp with crunchy, chewy manchego crumble, dulce de leche, and vanilla gelato is also noteworthy. Sometimes, I stop by just for one of these delectable creations! 

Wildflower can get busy rather quickly, so be sure to make reservations during peak hours!

Approximately 2 months later..."I remember you. You ordered a Hotel Nacional Especial..." This was the surprising greeting I received, as I pulled up a chair to the bar at Saint House Rum Bar in the fall of last year. 'How on earth did this bartender remember me and my order (from at least 2 months ago), on an evening with a packed house...and very low lighting, no less,' I wondered? He didn't reveal how he recalled this bit of information...but, with that type of memory, I am sure he should try out for some type of game show or work for the CIA, lol. This level of service has enticed me to return on several occasions since. 

Food glorious food...

I find myself thinking about Saint House when I am in the mood for a light, but satisfying meal. The sweet potato street taco has come to be one of my favorite vegetarian dishes in town. The sweet potato is cooked just enough retain a firm structure, and is complimented with a tangy Caribbean taro slaw and cashew crema. You can mix and match your order with Brazilian steakhouse (chimichurri, fried potatoes, caramelized onion, arugula, cojita) and mahi (avocado crema, mango pico de gallo) tacos. I am also now highly addicted to the banana ketchup! It is a marvelous, tantalizing concoction of puréed bananas, vinegar, and curry seasonings. It is served with light, crisp taro chips, but I've taken the liberty to slather it on all sorts of things. Delish! Roasted Mexico City street corn with lime aioli and cojita is a tasty starter or light dish, as well.

Les Poissons, Les Poissons...

The restaurant is noted (obviously) for it's plethora of rums, but also for it's fresh fish  and seafood offerings (such as almond-crusted tilapia and blackened catfish). The ceviche is refreshing and flavor-packed! Try the trio sampler plate, if you cannot decide which style to order. My favorite features scallops and mahi with mango, pineapple, and red bells -- a nice contrast in flavors and textures. The calamari is also quite good, with a house sauce, mango, and arugula.

New-Fashioned Style...

Saint House has a bit of a swanky, upscale, island feel to it, with flowing curtains and wicker -- like a fine plantation. It almost seems as if it would be more at home somewhere like La Encantada or Casas Adobes, instead of what's becoming a very urban, hip Downtown district. Still, one can feel comfortable in casual attire, a business suit after work, or a bit decked out. The bar area is rather sizeable, and I love the big, comfy booths. We held a small party in the private dining room (anterior to the main dining area, facing Congress), and it turned out to be a fantastic night.

Rum's the word....

If you are overwhelmed by the sea of rums and rum cocktails, the well versed bar staff and servers will happily make a recommendation for you. In my experience, the drinks have been strong and quality. My last visit, I enjoyed the El Presidente, made with Flor de Cana dry 4-year white rum, Dolen vermouth, Bauchant orange liqueur, and pom grenadine. The Hotel National Especial (remembered so shockingly by the aforementioned bartender) is also fabulous, and features Banks 5 island rum, Rothmen & Winter apricot liqueur, and pineapple and lime juices.

 Make sure to check out the rum-based desserts, such as flan, or warm rum raisin cake a la mode!

C'est Magnifique! 

Hot Lunch Jam...

I was a bit hesitant my first visit to The Parish, as I was in the mood for something healthier and light. I didn't know how many options a "Southern-fusion gastropub" had to offer. But, ooh wee! I was pleased to find a warm, spicy, chile & garlic bowl of edamame on the menu, as well as an appetizer of 'build-your-own' crostini with chilled pecan smoked ruby red trout, onion marmalade, roasted garlic, and Dijon. Perfect portion sizes for a light & delightful meal! Another visit, I decided on the grilled petite NY steak salad and was sorely disappointed that it came out in 'wedge' form. I usually do not like to have to deconstruct a salad -- I want it chopped & ready to go, lol! After tasting it, though, I would have gladly spent hours taking it apart...bit by glorious bit. Perfectly cooked med rare lusciousness, with romaine, red onion, gorgeous heirloom tomatoes, anchovy vin, and to-die-for bleu & cream cheese croutons. Alas, even though I initially came in seeking healthier fare, my favorite creation has come to be the Drunken Angel pasta. This exquisite dish is SO rich, with burgundy-bathed angel hair, succulent shrimp and crawfish, lobster broth, and saffron & red pepper cream sauce, that I cannot even finish a lunch portion. Worth every single guilt-laden calorie, haha!

The Music of the Night et La Vie Boheme...

Music and art seem to be part of the heart and soul of The Parish. They often host musical performers, so make sure to check their website for upcoming events. This past Mardi Gras, we were treated to great live Dixieland and rock-a-billy shows along with a crawfish boil. (I ordered a $12 sampler of Cajun delights -- ooh wee! -- red beans & rice, chicken & andouille gumbo, spicy crawfish hushpuppies, collards, and smoked shrimp étouffée.) They are strong supporters of local art, and rotate the pieces hanging along the walls. Right now, they have some wonderful, very vibrant pieces by Liz Weibler. This past December, they shut down for a few weeks, to expand the operation (located in a strip mall on Oracle). It is indeed roomier and still has an inviting 'Southern pub' feel to it, with bright colors and distressed wood. I often sit at the bar and have had only one occasion that I was unhappy with the service. 3 bartenders -- at a half-empty bar -- failed to offer a food menu (after a very long period of time). They had offered a drinks menu, however, and that was served. Finally, when asked for a menu, they failed to ask if food was indeed wanted (after another extremely long period of time). They were busying themselves cashing out the drawer, etc. This was the only time I can say that I left (without ordering any food!) truly unsatisfied with my visit. 

Cocktail Counterpoint...

In a previous review, I stated that my favorite local cocktail had a rival. Well, it's still a battle...but, as a gin lover, Parish's Dutch Well Water (house-infused cucumber gin, lime juice, peach bitters, and lavender water) is a sure contender. It is incredibly refreshing, and it's perfect for those hot AZ summer days and nights! I believe one of the bartenders said it was his own concoction. Merci! If you're not partial to gin, try the Aqua Vita with Deep Eddy vodka, mint, peach bitters, lemon, and cranberry. Delish! They also have an array of craft & import beers, spirits, and offer 2 gluten-free beers. 

Happy Hour @ The Parish is Monday - Friday, 3 - 6 pm, $3 wells, drafts, and $4 house wine.

For poker players, the room always needs a separate review from the rest of the property. And this is certainly one that needs a full discussion.

There is so much that is great about Hard Rock poker: The size of the room, the ability to game select because they do so much volume, and the lighting and comfort of the chairs are all excellent. It's one of the few places in the Southeast that can get a 2-5 PLO or a 5-10-20 Hold 'Em on a weeknight. Plus the average player skill-wise varies between bad and mentally incompetent to stand trial, so you'll never find a softer field at the lower limits. And recently they've made an effort on some promotions that have some value. This July 20 hours of play between Sunday and Thursday in a week will get you a $150 gas card, which is a very sweet deal by any standard.

But there are so many places where they could improve I don't know where to begin. The rake is 10% up to $5, plus a $1 drop for the jackpot even without a flop. And that jackpot pays for quad 10's or better cracked, with pairs only in your hand if playing quads, and both hole cards working if playing a straight flush... so, ya know, simple (riiiiight). But hey, enjoy the $500 for a royal, because that'll totally make up for it.

The quality of the dealers varies as widely as you'll see anywhere, as there are some I wouldn't let deal Go Fish at my kitchen table, and others that would be fine in Bobby's Room. The same goes for the floor: some get every call right, and others do things like say "well I don't know who wins, so we're gonna roll this pot over to the next hand." And yes, that actually happened. The comps also stink (0.60 an hour for 1-2 and below, $1 per for 2-5 and higher), and as in the rest of the casino, the booze is by purchase only. 

Plus they are full of silly and pointless rules like you can't sit backwards in your chair unless you're getting a massage from one of their massage girls. And you can't get your first buy in from the table, but rather must use the cage. You also can't buy the button. And the silly betting line is 100% live and any chips that cross are considered action, even if they're in your hand and you're cutting your bet. Which is just inane. 

A lot of the staff remains from when you weren't allowed to wager more than $2 on any street (yes, it was $2-$2 limit Hold 'Em, it was like watching paint dry), and they still treat the room the same way despite the fact the stakes and play has increased exponentially. There are so many people that don't understand how a major poker room can and should promote the game, as well as treat players. However this is the only option if you want to play 24 hours a day in Tampa (the dog and horse tracks are forced by state law to close 6 hours a day), and they've pumped a ton of money into the facility. It should be one of the best places in the country to play, on par with The Bike, Borgata, or The Venetian. But they continue not to get it, even though it is better than it was just a year or two ago.

So come for the marshmallowy soft play, which is by far the room's biggest draw for a seasoned gambler, but don't expect the same perks or treatment you should be used to if you play with any regularity. As of now, the Hard Rock continues to be all hat, no cowboy.

The greatest college bar in the history of the world, and any USF graduate that denies this needs their diploma revoked. Though, to be fair, this place almost kept me from graduating in the first place.

They run a different type of drink special every night of the week, and they never have a cover. The food specials are usually pretty solid as well. The bar has every type of mixed drink you can imagine, and the bartenders and wait staff are fast, knowledgeable, friendly, and often pretty hot as well. They also have specialty drinks that are really good.  The Joey Drink (strawberry vodka, grape liqueur, Red Bull... I know it sounds lame but trust me) is awesome, and I probably spent as much on it as I did tuition some semesters.

The place is huge, has over 10 pool tables, as well as a row of a dozen or so dart boards along the far wall which are often so full you might need to challenge someone that's playing to get a chance yourself. Peabody's was famous for having you and your clothes smell like an ash tray covered in chimney dust when you left, but they finally did something about the ventilation, so it's a fraction of the problem it used to be. 

Next door is The Falls, a mini-nightclub that's attached and also generally doesn't have a cover. The crowd there the last few times I went has gotten a little rougher, but it used to be a fun place to dance and drink the night away. I'm not sure how it is recently. Having a great bar with pool, darts, etc, attached to a nightclub is awesome. As you slowly become more inebriated, the better a bad idea like dancing sounds, so this place gives you the perfect balance no matter what kind of night you want to have.

Nowadays since I'm older, I only go there to watch their NFL package on Sundays, where they do $10 all the beer you can drink and have good deals on wings and burgers as well. It's a heavy football crowd of older people, and the local Jets fan club meets to watch games there. If you head over during the day, the lunch specials aren't bad either, and it's not a bad place to catch day baseball on Wednesdays and Thursdays.

I can't discuss this place rationally because it had such a large affect on my life. My friends and I once decided that living within walking distance to Peabody's was too much to pass up, so we moved to Camden Live Oak next door so we could stumble back and forth. It was one of the best decisions we ever made. I met a girl there playing pool one night who was only in Tampa for the summer working on her doctorate, as she lived in San Diego. We fell hard for each other, and six months later I quit my job and moved out there to be with her. Eventually I moved back, because Peabody's relationships never last. As they shouldn't. I spent so much time there I learned how to throw a bullseye from behind the short wall that separates the dart area. That trick paid for a few bar tabs. One night my intern walks in with some friends, so I offer to buy her a drink. We walk to the bar, and she starts deeply staring at me. I ask "what...," and before I can even finish my sentence she drunkenly makeout/attacks me in front of multiple co-workers. I had to fire her the next day. But I didn't blame her... after all, she was at Peabody's.

I lived in Vegas for a while, and some friends from USF came to visit. We were at Pure in the VIP section chugging bottle service, and some famous DJ was spinning. It was everything that ideal nightlife is supposed to be. Peabodys has a text number where you can send a message, and it will appear on the monitors throughout the bar. I sent this message: "I'm with models and bottles in Vegas right now.. but I'd rather be playing darts with all of you. Peabody's rules." And I meant every word.

997th person to review Resturant R'evolution. This is my 470th review on Yelp. This place came highly recommended by a friend and co-worker, Lee, and I will forever listen to her! 

Allow me to paint a picture for you. my friends. My first time in NOLA. The city will encompass and embelish all of your sences, feelings, and desires. For those of you that know me, and have followed me, I had a weight loss surgery 2 years ago and eat small bites only. Why does this matter? This place is dangerously good. The wait staff takes very good care of their customers. Our waiter went over the entire menu and explained what is in each dish, which at the time was outside of my comprehension. The thought of cutting open a bird and gumbo falling our wasn't quite appetizing or turtle soup (although I did have some later on in the week from another location).

Again, any locals that haven't been-- I am in town every few weeks and I love to meet up for a meal-- 

Thank you Resturant R'evolution.

I found myself in the heart of NOLA, in the French Quarter, and the only place that I knew in the area is Villalobos Rescue Center, which is home to Animal Planets, "Pit Bulls and Parolees". They have a restaurant near the French Market, along the Mississippi River, where each time you drink you feed a dog! Tahyo means big hungry dog in Cajun and pronounced TAY-YOUR. 

68th person to review Tahyo and my 468th Yelp review

In 1987 a terrible attack involving a Pit became highly publicized making Pit Bills the new American misfit as many know-- a stigma that still surrounds the breed. Villalobos cares for hundreds of Pits, providing medical care and getting forever homes. In addition to that, the owner, Tia, hires parolees to help foster their development and acclimate back into society in the hopes of lessening recidivism. The Pit's seem to be therapeutic for people, and the "parolees" find a purpose and specials connection with the animals-- as it is, they're both the underdog, living in the shadows of past mistakes. 

I digress-- this review is on the restaurant, but I wanted you to have the backstory as to what the mission is and who Tahyo exists.  

I approached the corner lot on a cold day. I felt a little lost and overwhelmed by all options available, enticed by the many bars, clubs, music, and people but I pushed through and made my first meal in NOLA here at Tahyo and you know what, I'm really glad I did. And I will again, and again, and again. 

The inside is smallish. They have a bar-- friendly, genuine people. I sparked a conversation-- FREE DRINK WHEN YOU CHECK IN ON YELP! I had a Lucky, which was super good. There weren't any other customers in there when I was there, but the echo of "Who DAT" was a reminder that the majority of the town was at the Saints Game at the Super Dome less than a mile away. As I sipped on Lucky and watched the Saints game on the television inside the bar area, I could hear the chants of the fans coming from the stadium just down the road-- that was super cool for the record and somewhat surreal. 

I wanted to try something different-- after all, I am (was) in the Big Easy! 
I ordered their southern take on curry-- and I am so glad I did. I didn't eat too much of it but I took it back to my hotel and ate it over several days. They gave me a doggy paw bag to place my leftovers in-- cute pun (see photo). 

They have drinks named after real dogs at the center-- Each time you drink, a dog gets fed. I don't know about you, but there is nothing better than good libations, food, and giving back, especially to the underdogs-- the ones that can't speak for themselves-- 

I encourage you to check out both the television show and this restaurant. Be sure to visit the rescue center, too, if you're in the area. You can help walk some dogs, or clean up if you'd like. 

Anyone local that hasn't been? I am in NOLA from Idaho every other week and I'd be happy to meet you for an UYE!

92nd person to review Main Street Burger in Meridian, Idaho on Main Street and Franklin across from the Rite Aid Center. This is my 427th review on Yelp. 

If you live in Meridian you've probably driven by this place several hundred times like myself. I've had this place bookmarked both mentally and on Yelp for quite a while and today was the day! I'm glad I went and I will go def go again when I need a good cheapish meal. 

A bright sunny day, the perfect weather for outdoor seating, not too hot, not too cold; however, the sun was uber bright but with the Main Streets outdoor covered seating we were kept quite comfortable. 

The important stuff that you really want to know, right? The FOOD! Well, it's certainly not 5-star food, but it is a good overall 4 I'm a fan kind-of- place. 

The menu: Burgers, fries (sold separately), other sides, taco salads, finger steaks, tots (which I hear are super good), hot dogs, and milkshakes. All average pricing. 

I ordered the Taco Salad-- a generous portion of lettuce, tomato, well-seasoned meat, and cheese. Served with either ranch or Italian as opposed to sour cream and guacamole (either would have been fine) and salsa and made in-house tortilla chips, which were seasoned well, but were hard and stale. I ended up throwing the chips away. 

Ranch is ranch some say-- well, not this guy! NOPE.  However, don't like paying for ranch or other condiments, especially at chain restaurants, but I understand that this is a small business and they do provide a good serving size, so $.50 is fine. 

My son ordered a crispy chicken burger. He thought it was good and that's all that matters, but it's three crispy chicken strips placed on a bun. The chicken strips are nice in size, crispy and thick. 

My other child got a kids meal and her chicken was super hard that she cut the roof of her mouth on-- the inside was "mushy" but it was replaced without question. Perhaps it was a one-off-- just beware if you have a toddler. 

There is a limited amount of seating inside. The tables are small and won't accommodate all body sizes, beware of that. 

The parking lot has ample parking. 

All-in-all, I liked Main Street Burger. I like the locally owned and operated aspect and would be happy to spend both my time and money there again.

The last time I ate here, the BF and I decided to come here to celebrate a milestone.  The waiter could care less.  For real, dude, really!  He was so nonchalant, it was like to he wasn't even at work. He took our order then rushed off.  I'm sorry, I wasn't finished!  Anyhoo, he came back and I finished my order.  

Food came, it was ordered right, but it tasted so wrong! I couldn't believe it, I  kept saying, "I love this place!"  Then after a few more bites, I realized the problem, The Chart House had changed.  Such a shame.  

We finished our meal and on to the dessert..............LAVA CAKE *insert back flip here*  Up to the point of dessert, my dining experience was not good, but I did not care, I knew the cake would change it.  And at least I could still come for dessert.  Well, they cooked the cake to death, I mean back to death as it was never alive.  Poor cake and my poor taste buds.  That was it!

I was furious!!  We paid and left.  Oh, did I complain? No, never got a chance the waiter was gone in a flash.  That was fine with me because I'm good for writing a letter.  I went to the website as the Chart House is a part of a chain.  BLASTED them all over the place!  Yeah, I did it.  

I got a call from the manager.  I explained my dilemma, during this time people do not have money to spend $100 on a bad dinner, etc.  I was so surprised and dismayed.  Such a shame.  Yadda, yadda, scoop.  He said, "I've been manager here for three months now and we are not getting nearly as many complaints as we were before I started."  I said, "Oh, okay."  WHAT ARE YOU SUPPOSED TO DO WITH THAT!  He offered me a gift certificate, told me to ask for him, etc. 

After the call, I told myself it would be a cold day in hell before I went back there. These idiots do not know how to maintain a "fine dining" establishment, so no need to waste my time.

There is a light, can you see it?  The BF and I are in Baltimore a few times a year.  We bless The Chart House in Annapolis with our presence.  And I must say, they are always happy to see us. *smile*  The food is still good, there is a nice view, the decor is not as dated, the wait staff are experienced and friendly and the lava cake is the ultimate!

New Orleans Marriott is not the cozy property that some downtown Marriott's can be.  Instead, it is large and quite bustling on most days and nights.
Located right on busy Canal St, it puts you right in the heart of where you want to be to explore this marvelous cultural city!  Just a few blocks and you'll be on the Mississippi River where you can walk for some distance enjoying the ships traversing the river.  A few blocks in the other direction and you'll be knee deep in the historic French Quarter!

The rooms are not as spacious as the Marriott that is located in the warehouse district, but the concierge lounge at this location is perhaps the best I've experienced at all of the many Marriotts that I've stayed!

A beautiful rooftop pool area that is probably quite enjoyable in the muggy summer months in New Orleans, and a large fitness room with tons of equipment, are just more of the nice amenities that this location has to offer!

Having stopped here before, but finally realizing its really about the spices they sell, the seafood is just blah!  The grilled catfish po boy was overpriced at $15, and just really a ton of bread!  The flavor of the catfish was good, but the French Roll is so thick that it completely takes away from the fish!

Of course Cafe Du Monde is getting five stars!  Why wouldn't it?  

A legendary beignet spot that everyone who visits New Orleans stops in for those incredibly fresh beignets!  Is it a bit of a tourist trap?  Perhaps!
I will say though, they are incredibly good, always fresh, can't help but be messy, but coupled with a fresh cup of cafe au lait...it's monumental!

It's funny to see people stop in, grab a seat, and then look for a menu!!  They ONLY sell beignets with either coffee or milk!  Cash only so don't get caught having to run across the street to the ATM!

Tip:  Eat outside in the covered seating area for the true European experience as they constantly have pop-up jazz bands playing!

What more can be said about Hattie B's!  Nashville Hot Chicken at it's absolute finest!

Located a block or two from the Aloft hotel I was staying at, it was a no brainer to experience some Nashville Hot Chicken!  Due to Covid, we took it back to the room for the experience!  The three large chicken tenders that I got as a medium heat were not only large, tasty, juicy, but also the right amount of heat!  The added pickles to the box was a nice addition to combat the heat!

I tried the Pimento Mac and Potato Salad as my sides.  The Mac was outstanding, while the potato salad was just average.

This isn't a long review as there's not much that I'm going to be able to add to the outstanding rating they already have to this point!!

Fantastic pizza on Bourbon St?  You bet!  Crescent City Pizza Works is the place, right on Bourbon St amidst all the craziness, serving up NY style pizza!  The Cheezeburger as they call it with the pickles, onions, sirloin burger, tastes exactly like a wonderful burger!  The dough here is incredible, and the scene going on outside adds to the fun of it all!

An incredible little shopping village that at the holidays is decorated exquisitely!  My first visit here as family brought us here for the decorated holiday experience! While all of the shops are cutesy and niche oriented, the experience is well worth the visit! If coming here during the holiday season is an option, I'd highly recommend it!

My first thought was this place is pretty fancy for a Mexican food joint.  I definitely appreciate the art displayed especially the masks.  I came with some friends after a quick  hike at Picacho Peak.  

Cafe Poca Cosa pushes out 2 menus daily according to our waitress!  To start our group decided to order a pitcher of margaritas; aside from H2O I definitely needed a drink to wet my palates!  The margaritas our phenomenal here and with over 7 selections you should be able to find one that tittles your totes!  The complimentary chips and salsa was probably one of the best I've ever had....I think I can say that not to say I want to bolster up this place, but seriously good.  It was fresh, sweet, with a hint of spice.

For our food I order the Asada En Salsa Brava, cause you can't go wrong with chopped flank steak doused with salsa.  The steak itself was tender and well cooked.  The salsa again was not spicy at all but provided a sweet creamy sauce; which I gather the meat was cooked in.  My friend gave me a taste of her tamales which she swears by is the best.  Needless to say, it was one of the best.  I can't say it's traditional like grandma used to make simply because of the ambiance, but also the way it was plated.  I need to unwrap it myself!  However, it was meaty, grainy, and full of girth to say since it was quite large in size.  I think I could maybe eat 1 and 1/2 of these and call it good for they day.

In the end, Cafe Poca Cosa deserves my love since they provided me with such.  I think it's one of those gems you find in Tuscan and never forget! - Enjoy!
Great breakfast, lunch, and dinner. Lee's Deli always has the best food specials and great snacks. I have been going here for years.

Very disappointing dining experience.  Waited 90 minutes for two orders of grouper tacos that cost $43.  Yes, you read that right, 4 tacos for $39  + $4 extra for avocado which they forgot to put on the tacos.  Ouch, and they were not even good tacos.   The grouper pieces were almost absent -- hidden under mostly dry lettuce & cabbage; definitely not what I expected.

The wait staff was very apologetic about the long kitchen delay; stating  their kitchen staff was new.  But that's a management issue, not a kitchen issue.  Why would you train new kitchen staff on a busy Sunday afternoon?
Strangely, management didn't even offer to discount or comp the food as a courtesy for the inconvenience of waiting.  I was entertaining relatives visiting from out of town which made the situation even more awkward.  Sadly, I can't recommend The Getaway as they're overpriced and the food is not great.  I realize the location is awesome,  but that doesn't make up for the deficiencies in basic food service.
Add one star for wait staff effort to keep us informed of the delays.

This is likely my new favorite Distillery/Brewery in town. 

1. Killer service. The bartenders are always super friendly and are quick to serve. I've met the head brewer a number of times and he's just a delight. Always cracks me up.

2. Fresh, clean, and new. The building has all the trappings of a micro-brewery, is always super clean and comfortable (except for maybe the stools), and is just a welcoming, impressive space.

3. The taps are tip-top. Okay, I'm pretty embarrassed about how much of a dad joke that came out as, but I'm keeping it and you can't stop me. My favorite beer is the Dayman, not only a tasty Pilsner but a clever reference to the popular show Always Sunny in Philadelphia. And, if you're not much into beer, they have 3 or 4 cocktails on tap as well, all of which I can attest are super drinkable.

So... visit, what are you doing? Put your phone down and pick a glass up!

Stopped in for Brunch on a Sunday with reservations right when they open at 11. They were able to seat us immediately and were very attentive.

We love the cornbread fritters and ordered some for the table. Our friends were equally impressed by them. 

I was bummed to see the chicken and waffles no longer being served, but our waiter suggested the Spicy Chicken Sandwich instead. I'm a huge fan of Nashville hot chicken, and the waiter expressed that he thought it was the best version of it in town. Well... now I had no choice in the matter.

It was a good sandwich... but I can't say it was the best. The chicken was hammered thin before being breaded and fried, so what I ended up tasting was the breading and seasoning, not really the chicken itself. If you asked me if they were store-bought patties or made in house, I couldn't tell you because the chicken was hammered so thin.

The breading, while crispy, was also a bit oily, and I can't say that it was particularly spicy... but I'm a bit of a sadist with my heat, so don't go solely off my standards.

That said, I ate every bit of my sandwich.

Now, what I should have done was ordered the stuffed french toast. My buddy ordered it and let us take a bite once he was finished and it was AMAZING. Crispy and rich. I couldn't imagine eating a whole plate by myself, but my wife and I will be splitting that next time we do brunch, Fo Sho.

From the first bite into my chips and guac, I knew that this place was gonna be a winner. 

I went with my wife and we were able to get a table on their enclosed patio. It is sheltered from the sun, but with a nice cross-breeze going through, so it was very refreshing to take our masks off and enjoy the evening. 

We started with their chips and guac. Fresh... fried... chips. It's hard to argue with that. They were perfectly crisp and salty, and the smooth guac blanketed in crumbly queso fresco was amazing.

We followed up with a collection of tacos and quickly established that the shrimp here is what you gotta go for. It easily outpaced the spicy lamb and shortrib, even though those were still tasty. We also established that one should go for the street tacos and leave the crispy ones in the kitchen. It wasn't that they tasted bad or anything. Quite the opposite. But the street tortillas capture the juices of the meat, and delivery everything in a solid, delectable bite. The crispy ones crumble after the first bite, the juices dribble down your arms, and make a mess. 

I did ask out waiter for their spiciest salsa, and I was given a bit of the oil they braise their lamb with. It's a bit disappointing for me to get street tacos with little spice, but I'm a masochist with my spice, so I understand that most restaurants don't cater to my kind.

Finally, churros baby! Get em! ORder them! Maybe come here just for them. Shit, I love churros so much, and these are the bees knees. The sharks park. The monkeys plunkey... they're good.

Five star experience from start to finish.  The worst thing about this restaurant may also be the best.  It is SO hard to get a reservation!  But that also must mean that they are doing something right if the are booked to the gills every night.
    I started the night with an espresso since I was pretty beat.  Nice kickstart to the meal!  My wife couldn't pass up the raw west coast oysters (east coast available as well).  I had a nice bowl of beef and potato soup.  Which was deliciously beefy, rich and reminiscent of beef stew that I enjoyed as a kid.
    For our entrees my wife got the gnocchi with lamb ragu (which was absolutely delicious) and I got a green goddess salad that I devoured like peter cottontail having a feeding frenzy.  My wife and I both literally considered licking our plates clean.  Oh yes and the beets.  These beets are the best beets I've had for awhile.  In fact they beat the best beets I've had in awhile!
    Food aside I would also like to just comment on the details.  The devil is in the details as they say.  Energetic, light, casual atmosphere even at our table situated by the kitchen.  I actually enjoyed watching the bustle of the kitchen staff.  The water service was prompt, the used dishes were removed quickly, the waitress was friendly and attentive.  The owner stopped by to see how we were doing.  I loved how they had a nice sized menu for children as well.  Very family friendly.  The owners children were there eating with his family at the same time as us!  
     We finished it all off with a Sunday that had apples and pecan streusel topping on vanilla ice cream.  Then headed off happy and content to see the Garden Glow.  
     This restaurant truly shines as an example of what all restaurants should strive to accomplish.   Make reservations early.   Remember there is a reason its hard to get a reservation.  Its because it's a five star restaurant!

If you have ever thought to yourself i wonder what it would be like to have a seat at the judges table on Iron Chef, this is as close as you will get and that is ONLY IF YOUR LUCKY..... My girlfriend and I went to Nashville in December and overheard some folks talking about the place, once we returned back to the Hotel for the eve I immediately went online to try and get a reservation. I will give you a piece of advice, if you know your going to Nashville anytime in the future I HIGHLY recommended that you go to the website,here I have it for you - http://www.thecatbirdseatrestaurant.com/reservation.html . The restaurant only seats 32 and is not easy getting a spot just the night before or hell the month before at that. I'm one of those that lucked into a spot.

Be prepared to have at least 3 hours set aside once you walk into this HOT SPOT. The menu - ( there is no menu) these 2 chefs , Josh Habiger and Erik Anderson already have your menu planned for you, 9 courses with each course also having a drink pairing from the amazing beverage director Jane Lopes. 

Once inside you know instantly you are in for one WEIRD experience, you walk through the front door and are immediately greeted from a lady behind a curtain and ushered up a elevator into a pink hallway before being sat down at one of the 32 seats that surround the 2 chefs. 

Your night has begun , our first course was a small Oreo, but a bite into this  informs you otherwise: It's whipped Parmesan between porcini mushroom wafers as a starter and then from here the dishes had me AMAZED..... I mean we had just about everything you COULD NEVER IMAGINE from the best play on Nashville Hot Chicken: a shard of crisp cayenne-spiced chicken skin brushed with sorghum, dotted with dill pickle salt and Wonder Bread puree to Pigeon yes I said it Pigeon......... I was shocked how not only every course was so well mastered but how each drink was  designed to awaken and tease the palate and harmonize with the food.

If you don't try this place atleast once in your life you should not be reviewing food on Yelp....... Simply put this place changed my life and I don't know if that was a good thing or a bad thing because now everything is just below this place.

What a hidden little gem! 

I was out and about and I needed to go to the restroom and on my way I noticed this little pizzeria.
