I was a little hungry so I decided to get a slice. I was worried about how long the pizza had been sitting out so the gal offered me a slice that just came out of the oven. I was very happy and pleased about that. Such great customer service. They have seating along the wall which was perfect to just sit and eat then go. When I am out again and need a slice I will definitely be coming back here trying their other many options! Oh and their Pizzas are New York style which is my absolute favorite type of pizza. Mmmmm

Yum yum, been here once before. And if I can remember we had the lobster escargot and it was divine! 

This time we tried their sushi for an appetizer and we got the lady in red which was seared tuna and spicy tuna. Amazing. We definitely want to come here and try their sushi. 

I got the bay scallops for my entree. It was amazing and huge. I felt like I got my money's worth. Great sized portions and the price was normal for an all seafood dish here in Reno. 

The waiter was awesome super nice!! I got their buy one get one martini Yelp special. It was a coffee martini that you were supposed to get for free but I didn't see that but the waiter still have me my second martini for free. 

We got the mushroom ravioli for an appetizer also. It was amazing. The sauce was perfectly creamy and savory. Enough sauce also to drench each ravioli. 

My husband got the prime rib. And that was a very tasty prime rib almost just as good as they liberty bell. If anyone remembers that restaurant. They were the best prime rib in town. 

All in all amazing meals and drinks. No doubt about it I will continue to come here for dinner!!

Alex wanted to check out a new brewery so he heard about revisions. I was hoping they had a porter or a stout or saison but they had a single IPA, double IPA and a pale ale. 

I tried all 3 and I really enjoyed the double IPA. I was shocked! I usually do not like hoppy beers. Although I do enjoy lagunitas IPA and the arrogant bastard IPA. I can't wait until they have events with food trucks so it'll bring more to this venue. 

Very spacious and a lot of benches. The art is also appealing. Give a little simple flare to the place which I enjoyed while drinking my Minnie IPA. The brewing fermenters are ginormous and beautiful at the same time. Odd to say that they are beautiful, but if you go there the shine of the silver is just so pretty. There's a certain appreciation to certain things in life ya know. 

Anyway can't wait to come with more friends and drink and eat at this awesome new place.

Love love love this place. Funny thing the first time I came here was on a blind date with someone. He liked beer and I like beer and this was a good location for the both of us. And ever since this had been my go to place for beers on tap! The manager Kieran, he is the nicest guy. He always recommends my beers and has me try them. I like stouts and porters I just like how smooth they are. He will have me try a few before I pick the beer I want to drink for the night. 

I always end with the steigl which is a grapefruit radler!!!! I love grapefruit and it seriously tastes like grapefruit. I feel like this is the perfect ending beer to a night of drinking. 

Kieran the manager is from Ireland I love his accent. He's so nice and personable. I enjoy having conversations with him. Anna the bartender is usually there also when I go she is very nice and will also help out with what tastes of beer you like. 

I just met Joe and he is nice also. Very nice and will chat with you if he isn't getting pulled to help the other customers. 

Debra, now Debra I've known her for a while. I used to work with her and I seem to run into her everywhere from time to time.

I spoke with the owners on the phone once to set up a Christmas party for my work and they were very nice. I met the husband once and he is also doing a sponsorship for my work I believe. I just saw a flyer near my time clock that's a picture of him and his facility. 

Anyway love they're beers and oh almost forgot they don't just do beers. 

They have champagne flights, Bloody Mary flights and much more. Such a sweet place to go to. You can order food and bring it in too.

Ok time to update!

I don't know why I gave them 4 stars before. 

I've been here maybe a handful of times whenever I'm in the Sparks galleria area. And I have never been disappointed. Even the service is great. The little Asian girl that greets you is the nicest person ever. 

I got the BBQ pork with rice and it comes with fresh sliced cucumbers and pickled cabbage, bell pepper and carrots. 

That on its own is so yummy when you eat it with a bite of the rice and pork. I'm not sure if everyone knows that's the reason why it comes with all that. Because they want you to eat the rice and pork or whatever meat and take a fresh bite of the veggie. 

Not trying to toot my own horn, but Asian people are food geniuses. 

It reminds me of my own culture. Why do you think with our food they give you a little bowl of rice with your main dish, meat, fish whatever tofu. And then all those little crunchy veggie goodies on the side. It's a condiment, that compliments the food your eating. Hello kimchi!!! It goes great with everything. So the cucumber and pickled veggies are like the kimchi for us. 

Anyway. Also got the pork egg rolls. Not sure if it had pork inside of it, but it was still good. Husband got the noodle wonton soup. Very good and flavorful even when I can barely taste because I'm so sick. 

I've tried their tapioca drinks also and I loved all the ones I've tasted. The honeydew is my favorite. I definitely love this place and will be coming more often.

Very Nice!  Our Server, Danielle was on fire and sweet as could be.  For the true experience... dine outside as patio dining is perfect and sooo much nicer.  Grilled Octopus Salad appetizer devine and our lunch entrees enjoyed!

If you're in the Tampa/St Petersburg area and Truly love a working market... yous gotta hit up Mazzaro's!  An Italian market lovers dream...From grabbing an expresso, pastry, cheeses, wines, produce, homemade pasta of every kind, meat/seafood, wine, ++  or prepackaged prepared food to go .... You'll be in heaven!

Wowsie -  great classic burger and heck of a bang for the buck! Flavorful and delicious easy Linner. Ms. Jill was friendly and welcoming while hoppin' and serving every guest quickly. Perfect outdoor seating and the warm evening breeze was ...Dreamy.

1.  Upon calling to inquire if reservations needed - I should've known by the snarky and rude response this wasn't the place to gift my money to.

2. Should've known upon arrival by the careless attitude of personnel - I should've turned around.

3.  I should've known by the lack of any breakfast-related aroma in the restaurant - from fresh brewed coffee, to bacon to slinging hash -  nothing was authentic ...

4. I should've known that when all of our breakfast orders arrived within seconds of order... something was off.

5.  Upon staring at my overpriced plate that consisted of carton/scrambled fake cold eggs, limp and cold toast, weird plop of something involving potatoes and 2 strips of perfect looking bacon (that the Restaurant  didn't have the faintest aroma of) ....  And with 1 forkful  and taste of the eggs - I should've said - thanks, but no thanks .. 

Don't be a "should've" like I was ..  there's too many Places in this town that can deliver a fantastic meal/experience.

Based upon reviews - stopped in for lunch .. not too packed and seemed like a winner and perfect... and how quickly that changed. 

Short Version:
To save one the grief ... there are wwwaaaaayyy too many other places in New Orleans that know their craft and how to do it right - run the other way and go elsewhere.

Long Version:
If a zero could be awarded - it would.   This was beyond a huge disappointment and Desire Oyster Bar for this first and last visit - was fuhhggedable.

1st time I've ever experienced or said that from inept and uncaring staff to undercooked and dissppointing items sent out from kitchen ... EPIC FAIL!  

From a manager who continually walked thru restaurant yet never made eye contact with any customer to only exit quickly out another door.. from servers who seemed put out at any request yet felt free to divulge their life problems tableside or bicker with coworkers... to assembly line kitchen staff that plated Uncharred oysters, served lukewarm red beans and rice and cold rubbery fries... only to get another chance to do it right and send it back to table in an inedible state ...Really?

One of my favorite hotels .. tucked away on Chartres Street yet walkable to everything.  Stayed here for a few days, room was great, restaurant breakfast fantastic  but wondered what happened to the overall W experience since the last trek .. so a downgrade on rating.

Did a cloak of doom come over the W Team?  The Customer Service from Front Desk, to 1/2 the bar staff, to Valet were either MIA, discombobulated, junior or ??   

Was I called as promised when room was ready for check in?  Nope. Was facilities around to address the bar restrooms that were beyond filthy?  Nope.  Did front desk allow a guest to walk their non-service dog into bar and restaurant? Yup. Was it 95% of the time the W personnel were MIA  at front desk or valet (and the concierge stand was never manned during this stay) Yup.

Here's what sealed the deal - upon reaching front desk the skies opened up and I asked if there's an umbrella to borrow to get to courtyard room and the answer was "no, but can we have your room key?"    Huh?... umm no.  (I'm the kinda girl that leaves the do not disturb sign  on my door entire time).  I asked why the room key was needed and it was for them to go into my room and take  the umbrella out of mini bar... a double  huh? Huh?  Was then informed "the $14 umbrella in guest room mini bar can be used without charge as long as it's returned". I mentioned that's nice, but unfortunate it's not mentioned or written anywhere and ...front desk concurred.  

My interaction was the Front desk could care less.....nor seemed interested in helping any way... So, we ran across the flooded courtyard and reached our guest room drenched.  Really? 

My experience at The W this time was disappointing and not what they're known for.

Was so hoping this would knock it out of the ballpark. Quick and to the point:  service started out decent and quickly slid off the radar...food was just ok...and the infamous fried chicken was greasy. Not memorable nor worth a repeat visit...

I just learned something amazing about Total Wine's coupons.  Much like those at Bed Bath and Beyond, Total Wine's coupons don't actually expire.  They may have dates printed on them, but the barcode numbers never change in their system.  So if you get a coupon in the mail or find one online, it is probably still good!

I'm uploading an expired coupon that I just used.  I didn't even have to print the coupon, I showed it to the cashier on my iPhone and she accepted it!

Really, this place has a great selection of wines, beers, and other beverages.  I like this place a lot better than BevMo.  Total Wine even lets you make your own six packs of beer from any beers on the shelf.  If you are looking to try new drinks, then check this place out.

I used to eat here when they were located on Oracle, and I have to say as good as they were then everything has only gotten better since the move.  I can say without any doubt in my mind that this is some of the best Thai food I've had in my life.  I rank the food hear higher than many similar restaurants in New York and San Francisco.  They are that good.  And their prices definitely won't break the bank!

It was a little confusing going in the first time, as it's not obvious that you order at the counter (came in from the door facing the street), but other than that mishap, everything here is very good.  The young man who is generally behind the counter is extremely friendly, remembering regulars and treating new comers just as kindly.  The service is efficient whether ordering your food to go or dining inside.  

I've only had their Thai food, but everything I've ever ordered has been delicious.  The Pad Thai is excellent.  The Thom Kha is to die for, seriously.  Rich, creamy coconut soup with lots of garlic and yummy shrimp and veggies.  The Bangkok Delight is truly that, a delight.  In fact, all of their curries are delicious.  The Panang Curry and Thai Curry are great, but their Green Curry is absolutely out of this world good.  Their lunch specials are very special and I absolutely love their the prices during lunch.  But even their dinner prices are good, and they don't skimp on the portioning.  Good portions, great prices, and amazing food.  They are a winner in my book.

Mr Lee is a very nice business person running a great business.He is about to introduce a vegetarian sandwich made with Michaels savory seitan. A all natural vegan and vegetarian sandwich which is very popular in the Phila region and areas.You must taste his creations and you will see this is truly a delicious no fat low sodium all natural tasting veggie steak sandwich. Be ready for the next best sandwich coming out of Phila with Mr Lees SEITAN STEAK SANDWICH. He is using the best tasting Seitan on the planet being made from a local vendor and seitan maker for the past 20 years or so.Please try his creations and support the local farmers and vendors and eat healthy.Learn where your food is coming from and care for your enviornment support local eat local.Michael

This has to be the best Mexican place in Philly. My favorite dish here is the carnitas enchilada burrito, but I have never heard anything but terrific things from other people I've eaten with who've tried a variety of their dishes. Prices are also extremely reasonable and I've never had any problems with either delivery or pick-up orders. If you want really flavorful, delicious Mexican food, this is your place.

I cannot express how bad of an experience this place was. The manager on duty this ast Saturday evening acted like a complete jerk, so much so that I told him that to his face. I am normally a VERY understanding and calm individual, but could not help reacting to this situation. 

Here is what happened:

Arrived slightly after midnight on Saturday night, paid $10 cover each to get in with 3 friends, one of whom is pregnant.

Got upstairs, 3 of us ordered drinks, one ordered a water (aforementioned pregnant). I got a goose and club, which I paid $13 for (sucker).

We asked to be let up to the skybar. They said our friend with water couldn't go because she didn't buy a drink. We explained that the rest of us had, and that she couldn't drink, but they still refused. 

We asked for the manager. The guy WOULD NOT EVEN SPEAK TO US DIRECTLY but instead asked his employee to explain. He said that we couldn't go up, and just ignored us as we threatened to take our business elsewhere.

So we exited. Since this was within 10 minutes of us arriving, and since they were being so unreasonable, we asked for our covers back for the pregnant woman and her husband. No dice. 

Cops came and heard us out, and we're very professional (even offered to pay back the covers out of their pockets) while this total jerk of a manager just stood there and smirked. Real jerk. When we said that we were going to write reviews about this he said and I quote, "You won't matter." 

THE. WORST.

It might be helpful to distinguish between four and five stars, because I often feel the line might seem arbitrary. 

A four star place is the kind of place where I'm a regular. If I rank a place four stars, it's in my regular routine. I would be sad if it closed.

A five star review is the kind of place where I'd take someone from out of town. It's a phenomenon that deserves to have its story told. It's the kind of place I'll be telling my bored nephews and nieces about at a BBQ in ten years. 

Kukhnya is a five star place. 

It's where I brought my brother first when he visited New Orleans for the first time. Not because I thought it would be a  representative sample of New Orleans cuisine or because it was going to fulfill his expectations, but because I knew it was going to blow his mind. Kukhnya is something I could only imagine in New Orleans: a cheap slavic soul food place at the back of a crust-metal dive bar. 

On the evening I brought my brother from the airport, a noise-metal show was about to start, and so I swore to the bouncer "II won't listen to the music, I promise. I'm just here for the food." He understood and let us skip the cover. While waiting for a transcendent beet reuben and a delicious and substantial plate of pierogis, we giggled into our beers as the band did the most Dadaist soundcheck conceivable, walking from mic to mic and screaming precisely into each one, then electrifying their guitars with great careening arm-swings. 

Kukhnya has a bunch of great things on the menu: a great burger, the aforementioned beet reuben [and plenty of other veggie options for you people with a conscience], awesome pierogis, and Sunday specials that are so lovingly crafted, you would swear that your grandmother was both Ukranian and loved you more than she did.

My only caveat is that you want the head chef and proprietor working. When he's not around [bearded young guy often wearing a hat], the quality suffers a bit. It's his vision, and his dedication and genuine care shine through. Someday, he'll open a fancy restaurant and I'll be first in line [even if I'm a little sad I can't get incredible food for under ten bucks anymore].

Wow, this place is great. We were able to get in without a reservation, out hotel gave them a call and they had a space for us. The place is huge, but it was quite crowded. It is located in an old bank building and is stunning. Everything about this place is great.

They have great steaks, no question, cooked exactly as ordered and so tender. The cuts are huge. But what I loved, just loved, was the seafood. We had a crab salad which was so fresh and yummy. The dressing was perfect and there was a lot of crab. We also had a crab cake and it was just as good as any I have had in Baltimore and for me that is saying a lot. We also had lobster mac and cheese and I so wanted to eat it all. We were all sharing so we got to try a lot of dishes, but that one, I wanted to grab for myself. Next time, I am getting my own. It is amazing.

The wine list is extensive and expensive so get ready for that, but they have great California reds. The servers are so great. They know everything about the menu and even the wine. We were so so happy, and now I am hungry again.

We had lunch at City Tavern and loved every minute of it. I think it is one of the oldest or the oldest tavern in Philadelphia. It is just lovely. There is this great grandfather clock and the entire place is dressed with blue and white tablecloths. The service is friendly and very nice. The prices are within reason for what they serve.

We love the salmon and the braised rabbit. Our meal came with 3 different types of bread with lovely butter. It is comfort food at its best. I am told some of the recipes date back to the 1700s. Have the best time.

Here's the thing, I have had better cheese steaks, I have had better fries, I have had better everything that Pat's offers on their menu, but the place has been there forever, it is said that they invented the steak sandwich--on a long roll with grilled steak inside. So go there and share a steak sandwich with a friend. Don't get stuffed there, there are so many better places for later.

Pat's is super cool looking, it is a place where you order outside, there is no inside seating. There is outside seating but not a lot, there is no bathroom and parking is a bear. But you can walk to Citizen's Bank Park for a baseball game from there if you want. The building is all silver metal, like a silver lined trailer, sort of. The menu is on the outside and they don't take credit cards so have cash ready. The service is very nice.

Some people order their steak with Cheese Wiz. Now, that is some junk that comes from a can and is put on your sandwich. If you have never had it, I would not even bother to try it. I find it just gross. I don't want cheese out of a spray can. I don't even know if it is real cheese. So, just don't. Yuk. Also, their American cheese is not great. Play it safe and get your steak with Provolone Cheese. That is real.

The meat is cooked well done, which I find boring and it is not great, but it is fine. So, I guess I just told you this place is not very good. It is fine. It is fun. For what it is, and for the adventure of it all, you should go there. It is good and you will be able to say been there done that, moving on. Have fun. It is a cool area.

Tried it for the first time last night and was not disappointed!! The Superdome was so delicious and everything was perfect, from the crispy onion rings to the creamy mashed potatoes to the AMAZING, flavorful sauce and all the seafood. Ordered ahead to pick up and it was ready in 15 minutes. They made it so easy and convenient, and I will definitely be returning very soon to try some other things on the menu! This is definitely a new favorite spot for me.

Is there another city in America that celebrates brunch with the same fervor as New Orleans? 

To me New Orleans', brunch is the standard restaurants across the U.S.A try to live up to. 

Restaurant R'evolution is elevating that standard even more. Located inside the beautiful Royal Sonesta R'evolution is serving one of the most traditional yet progressive brunch menus anywhere in this brunch mad city. 

My Sunday fun day started with Death by Gumbo a beautiful stuffed quail bathed in a light yet flavorful roux which satisfies to the last spoonful.

I followed that with the Buffalo Quail and Waffle which is a fun contemporary take on the chicken and waffle. The mixture of the buffalo sauce, syrup and cloud like waffle ate great! 

For my main course I had the Debris Grillades and Gravy which is fancy way to say short ribs, pimento cheese grits and baked eggs. Short ribs were braised to perfection, grist were creamy and the egg perfectly runny. All in all a great dish but rich and heavy which did not leave room for dessert :-(.

Now I bet you're asking why I didn't give R'evolution five stars. It had great food, beautiful setting and lovely live jazz trio. 

Here's why, there was some miscommunication going on between front and back of the house that day. Our second course took forever to come out while we waited on those we were brought another tables main course which was similar to ours. Hopefully this was just a strange occurrence along with how warm the room was that day.

I will return to get familiar with bar!

No one loves a good Hot Dog more than me; well maybe Drunk me does ;-) 

Been feeding my drunken cravings at Dat Dog for years. Everything about the place is easy like Sunday Morning. 

Want a Crawfish Sausage Dog? They got that! Want fries covered in chili, sour cream, jalapeños and pico de gallo? They got that too! 

This place will never lead you astray just pick your sausage than your toppings and you're set! All combinations are good regardless of how weird they sound.

My favorite is the Alligator Sausage covered in Creole mustard, Jalapeños, Mayo, Bacon, onions and tomatoes. Once everything is place on that sweet toasted bun and you take a bite you will hear angels singing! 

So don't be shy step up to the bar and get creative you won't regret it!

Hibachi is not my first choice when I go out with a large party as the seating isn't always conducive to true conversation.  I was in Franklin for work and we went out with a group of 14.  Sorry for not having photos but I don't take many when traveling with work. 

We have a great place near home in South Florida so I have high standards. 

We walked in and the first thing I noticed was it wasn't very busy.  

We headed to a room and we were seated. The floors are oddly greasy or slippery as the chairs slide around. 

The service was friendly. 

The menu didn't contain much. There seemed to be several smaller menus with sushi and apps, but it was just placed in the corner and not given to everyone so no one really knew what else there was other then hibachi. 

Food:  the soup was a clear broth. Mine had a singular  thin slice of mushroom. It was a bit cold. Salad was okay. It didn't have a gingery taste I am used to.  I ordered the veggie hibachi made with no butter. I also ordered a side of mushrooms. I was hoping it would be portobello mushrooms, but they were not. It was generous and nicely cooked. The chef also made me a lot veggies. I did like that the carrots were not coin cut. They were thinly sliced. The veggies were not over cooked.  The ginger sauce did not have a lot of flavor. 

The portions of meats for the others seemed pretty generous and although no one was happy with leaving smelling like smoke, they enjoyed their meals.  

The chef was okay. Not overly entertaining. 

I felt a little rushed.  The server came out with a tray of ice creams while we were still eating.  He left when he realized he was too soon.  He came back with the same tray of ice cream a bit later.  He didn't take an ice cream order, he just had 14 ice creams and passed them out, never asking what flavors anyone may want.   I found it odd that we got fortune cookies. Typically that is a Chinese food item not Japanese. 

All in all it was okay. Nothing exciting. I wouldn't have this place on the top of my list if I return to the area.

Slowest grill ever for a to go order. They used to be so much better than this and am hoping they improve. But I won't be back to see it, this has been terrible. We waited 40 minutes for a to go order of two burgers. When I demanded a refund, the guy told me they were plating it. I asked to check that and the kid on the grill shook his head and so no, he hasn't even cooked the burgers. This type of service will keep me from making them my grocery store and from ordering good there ever again. Such a huge waste of time and disappointment

Wow, phenomenal experience for my friend and I. 

I was meeting an old friend for dinner and wasn't sure what we were going to have. This place came up as having good gelato and good pizza, that pretty much sold me. 

The storefront is interesting because the gelato shop is up front and the dining area is in the back, it doesn't even look like a restaurant from the store front because you can't see the seating area.

First off our server was wonderful! Absolutely wonderful. He was this preppy younger gentleman who made our experience so enjoyable and hilarious. 

He offered great suggestions for food and even wine for my friend. Between the two of us we shared a pizza, the special gnocchi and the arancini as an appetizer. 

I loved everything we had. The pizza and the arancini were on the same level, gnocchi was good but it was different than what I'm used to. It was also in a red sauce, which wasn't bad, just not what I was hoping for. 

Pizza was lovely, the mushrooms were good and the pie itself was cooked well. The arancini had great risotto in it and was so warm yet crunchy and soft. And the gelato was amazing! Their amish sweet cream ice cream (which I forgot the official name for) was so light yet flavorful. Our server suggested that versus the vanilla as it was lighter and more similar to sweet cream, which I had mentioned I really enjoyed. I paired it with hazelnut and it was divine. My friend did an affogato with the chocolate hazelnut with nuts in it and really enjoyed his as well. 

Overall, we were very happy with the entire meal. We were checked in upon frequently and even seemed to be greeted by management just to ensure things were going well, which I appreciated from a business standpoint.

My wife, son and I had dinner here. The food and service were good. However, our server wrote a little "love note" on our check (see attached photo) insisting on an 18% tip. 

I appreciate that servers need to make a living and tips are important. However, this was completely inappropriate and we left with a terrible taste in our mouths. It was completely unnecessary because we would have left a healthy tip and left happy and eager to return. Instead, I'm pissed off and sharing this story on Yelp!

If you require an 18% gratuity from everyone (not just large parties), then put that on your menu. This is incredibly insulting and no way to treat your customers!

The food is really good! I've never been there as we usually order takeout and get it delivered but I can say that the food is delicious and big portions
We usually get the goat curry and the jerk chicken 
It comes with copious amount of rice and veggies and a delicious bread

I've heard many great things about Frangelli's Bakery. They have cronuts, ice donuts and donnolis. But I've been unable to try any after two attempts.

First attempt: Last summer, I went there during business hours. But instead of being open, there was a taped up piece of paper that had written on it that basically they had "Gone Fishin" and won't be back for several weeks.

Second attempt: Again, went during business hours that were reported on Yelp. Tried to confirm but they don't have a website or answer their phone. Turns out they started new hours and are closed on Mondays. Really wished they picked up the phone on Sunday when they were open to let me know this.

Bottom line:
 - No Website
 - Don't answer their phone
 - No greeting on their voicemail. 
 - Close shop for weeks when they go on vacation
 - Incorrect hours on Yelp

I'm still holding off on giving them one star since I really hope to try their baked items. Maybe my third trip will work out.

Defn salty but authentic, some good finds

Beck's CAJUN caught my eye amongst the chaos of the Reading Terminal Market, and I wasn't looking back like Lot's wife

Chicken & Andouille Gumbo - over rice, not bad, good spices, tender chicken and hearty sausage, but tad salty
Gator on a Stick - didn't get it, but looked good. "Gator dun" Thanks Larry. 
Alligator Gumbo - VERY SALTY. alligator tastes like.. chicken? yea, chicken with a beefy taste.. beeficken-like
Blackened Chicken Alfredo - gf went nuts, claimed it was cheesiest pasta EVER, too cheesy for me, got sick of it

Popular picks are muffuletta and jambalaya. They also have plenty of soups, etouffee, other gumbos, seafood chowder and good ol' fried po' boys!

This place is a restaurant, bar, danceclub, and a SPEAKEASY, all in one!

ENTER drink
Coat check in front, then a square bar. Weirdest bar ever. Looks like a dive bar in one corner but also a bouji nice bar in another haha

Past the two-faced bar is a dancefloor with a stage for DJ's and live performances, and in the back is a beautiful elegant dining room.

DANCE
As we walked in, there was a local country band doing a live performance on the dancefloor and people were gettin' turnt. It was a great time!! We came back after we ate too lol

EAT
We slurped some nice oysters that were fresh and not sandy. And for dinner, our scallops on a bed of shredded brussel sprouts was phenomenal. Great wine selection as well. 

Went back and danced. Lights dim around 12 and becomes a club with dj pretending to spin a track while actually playing off iTunes lol. Great vibe and really chill

SPEAKEASY
In between the dining room and dancefloor is a shadowy staircase to the basement. There is a door. a phone next to the door. You pick up the phone. you hit the only button. They ask you, "What's the password?" We didn't know! Apparently, there is a new password every hour and you can only get it from someone who was inside before. We got lucky after some people left, rang the phone, said the password, crossed our fingers and went in. 

It was actually lame. Just kidding. Nice chill place to relax before or after you go upstairs for dinner/club. Faux-lounge feel in the back with few couches. Cocktails here are pricey though ~$15

Overall, Vesper was awesome! Eat, dance, drink, play, Vesper!

Treehouse, tria, tryst.. Anything that starts with "tr" just sounds amazing! Lol!

Tria houses a modern European wine bar aesthetic with simple cheese plates and bruschettas. Perfect lighting for that romantic-intimate vibe while you IMbibe. The wine? Not bad, I needed a good 4 tastes to find something I liked. Settled on a juicy Cab. The bartender never complained however! She was, in fact, happy and eager to help me! What a gal! (I'm so hardened by the curt NYC attitude that this was actually a real surprise)

TURKEY CLUB
Ok.. so what? It's a club, whoopee. No.   If only it was. 
My gf ordered it. I rolled my eyes. I tasted it. And my eyes almost fell out. 
This was, The TASTIEST club EVER. The turkey hella moist, Lettuce crisp but sauced, bacon crunchy oily goodness, cheddar aged and nutty but not dry, and the tomato HERB AIOLI added an elegant creaminess to every bite. I wish I tried more of the food!

Shoutout to Kana K. for telling me about Tria! Thank you!!

Tria has several locations throughout Philly metro area. A perfect spot to start or end the night! Defn coming back on my next Philly trip!

Long time customer growing disillusioned with worsening food and service:

I've been a routine customer at King Buffet for the better half of the last 4 years, since I work at an office across the street and make it part of my lunch rotation once or twice a month. Over the last few months, I've been more and more dissatisfied with the food offerings as well as the non-chalant service that fails to meet even my minimum expectations for a buffet style restaurant.

King Buffet used to be summed up like this: OK food, good selection, great price (8.05 for lunch after tax). 

As the restaurant has gotten more business from the senior citizens in the area who typically don't eat as much and are less picky about the quality and service of the food: 

King Buffet now has become: Below Avg food, Stale selection, mediocre price 

Below-average food (health and quality vs. other local but good options like chipotle, whole foods, chik-fila subway), stale selection (as the menu has not been recycled since i've started going which is more than 3 years ago) and mediocre price (subway is 5.30 for footlong, chipotle burritos/salads are 6.84 - 7.23), and even a good and healthy whole foods bar is only 9-10 dollars.


This restaurant used to be an occasional lunch indulgence for me and many of the other employees in the nearby office complexes but I think I can speak for most people when I say my experiences with this place are getting worse and worse. In fact, I think I am done visiting here, as I have better and healthier choices right around the corner.

P.S. I consider myself a foodie who appreciates all types of cuisine at all price points, and I have nothing against buffet style food. In fact I think that many other Chinese people like me enjoy the buffet aspect culturally and it's a shame to see this place slip from what it used to be. The management takes it customers for granted, often seeing them as daytime squatters (many of the senior citizens) and treating the rest of its customer base as high consumption types who hurt the profit margin of its food business.

OMG, if you have food on your mind, this is the place to go.  You can find ANYTING here and I mean ANYTHING.  The variety is overwhelming and it seems to never end....you can eat your way in and out,.  Fresh produce, jerky any kind, fish, meats, cheese, gourmet selections, breakfast, lunch, dinner, cheesesteaks, cookies, doughnuts, drinks both non alcohol and alcohol, you name it, I am sure you can find it here.

This is an amazing place to experience if visiting, we had the best breakfast in Philly here and a great cheesesteak as well.  The cheese selection we found was out of this world from fresh cow, to sheep to goat and the staff will give you samples to help you decide.  

I did not find anyone here who was not warm and friendly from workers to shoppers, all we very cool.  If we had more time or if we make it back to Philly in the future, this will definitely be a stop on our list to try some of the amazing items we saw but did not try this trip.

We did not find a lot of organic items especially in the produce stand but it all looked really good.  If you are in Philly and have the time, you have to put this on your list of places to experience at least once.

This place sucks.

*drops the mike*

Ugh, I cannot recommend this place at all. When we walked in on a Sunday night, it was more like a club than anything and the Eminem wannabe staff didn't help. We sat at the sushi bar and Not the real Slim Shady #1 just looked at us and walked away while #2 ended up "helping us". When we asked for anything....soy sauce, napkins, plates....he would just look at us very confused wondering why we were asking for stuff. They are just rude, vapid and really don't care here. The only reason why I'm not giving them one star is because the sushi was pretty good. The sushi chef who was hustling was the nicest person there who actually greeted us and said thanks for coming in. Walk a little further and go someone else for a sushi experience in Tucson.

I went to Parx for the very first time this past Saturday and it's safe to say I won't be returning. I had been the cohost of a joint bachelor/bachelorette party and there was about 30 of us. We even paid for a VIP area in the 360 club. My poor experience started in the parking lot. I pulled in and almost instantly popped my front tire on a beer bottle that had been left in a seemingly empty brown paper bag. I will take ownership of my misjudgment but when I went to follow up with the incident report that was filed I was basically laughed at and told that nothing would be done. I have also been informed that they staff people SPECIFICALLY to make sure the lots are clean. The "risk management" team deems this as something they cannot be bothered with. I am not able to get past speaking with a receptionist who can never find her director. All I want is for them to even apologize and take responsibility of their property that was not appropriately maintained. On top of all of this I have even been unprofessionally contacted by one of the security guards who filed my incident report. 

So long story short Parx casino doesn't deserve my patronage or anyone else's for that matter. They don't care about their guests or about taking responsibility for their experience.

Oh my oh my oh my!! I feel cheated that I've gotten here for the first time @ almost 51 years old! Ha ha! I have always heard people sing the praises of Zwahlens!  The exterior so cute and unique compared to the boring nondescript strip mall area that surrounds  it. You'll see this adorable chalet- that's IT! Once you enter the sweet confection smell will pleasantly overwhelmed with the sweet scent of waffles, cookies and chocolate. I was amazed by the attractive display of chocolate covered graham crackers, dipped marshmallow pops, adorable cookies, patriotic rice crispy treats shaped like stars and dipped & festively sprinkled red white and blue, and decadent chocolate dipped rods- just to name a few. Don't forget to ogle the breathtaking dipped apple display!


I ordered the Belgium waffle with vanilla ice cream and chocolate chip cookie dough sauce which was delicious. Little dollops of whipped cream too!  They have a featured flavor every day and the flavor yesterday was cookies and cream. 6/27/19. I ordered my standby vanilla I really enjoyed it!

The only reason I knocked off 1 Star was because I asked for water and did not get it. Also the table we sat at was sticky. 

I can't wait to go back and I know that extra star will be earned in my next review! I highly recommend Zwahlens and I hope they do wedding favors !

Cascatas you have redeemed yourself in my eyes! Bianca was a very attentive server along with a team of server assistants who were quite attentive with refilling our bread baskets and water goblets. It's a BYOB and our party brought assorted wines to share. The server brought us wine glasses and they even opened the bottles for us.

I ordered the shrimp lejon, it was delicious, shrimp wrapped in bacon lightly fried and served with a creamy horseradish sauce. Out. Of. This. World. For my entree I ordered The broccoli rabe pasta. It was delicious. I chose capellini pasta and the entree came with chunky fresh tomatoes, and lots of minced garlic, in addition of course to the broccoli rabe. I have had this broccoli rabe as an appetizer and it was spectacular. The entree did not disappoint. Husband had the baked gnocchi Florentine with crabmeat in a cream sauce. It was one of the best entrees we have ever tasted there hands down. The portions this time were extremely generous. Entrees came with a choice of soup or salad. 

Desserts! Many great choices. Our group ordered up big- Reese's peanut butter cake, decadent dark side of the moon, limoncello cake, Italian rum cake, creme brûlée cheesecake (that was mine probably the most boring dessert of the night! ) , cannoli and the tiramisu.  Delicious.

We had been there for a while and a lovely young server assistant was tasked with asking us to leave because they needed our table. We were wrapping things up and we had spent almost 3 hours there and we were ready to leave anyway. I felt bad that she was put in that position. I feel like the manager should have asked us to leave. When we left there was a ridiculous amount of people waiting and you could barely make it out the door!

I recommend reservations and going EARLY!! Excellent experience and a nice increase from a 2 to a 5 star review!

4/17/21 well my last review said I wouldn't come back but my husband was celebrating his 20 year work anniversary and picked Capital Grille.  

This time was much better than before. Our server James was attentive and effervescent. He was excellent, and polite. At these prices everything has to be impeccable and impeccable it was!

We were seated in a semi private room. I was digging the privacy. There was another table of 6 in the same room but it was fine. 

Most got cocktails at my table except me- I had sparkling water. The cocktails were elegant and amazing, not just the price but the craftsmanship.

Appetizers -terrific! I highly recommend ordering the lobster and crab cakes the cream sauce that comes with them is amazing too. Chunky lobster and crabmeat. I highly recommend this as an add on to the dinner! We also got our standard calamari and the prosciutto wrapped mozzarella cheese. Oh. My. GOD! That was terrific. Most at my table started off with Lobster Bisque with sherry that they loved!  I declined because dessert is my thing.


I got the special-2 ten ounce lobster tails-succulent and delicious but I truly wished I would have ordered the filet Oscar with the mountain of crabmeat, asparagus, and hollandaise. That looked incredible and three at my table ordered it. We ordered up the creamed spinach, Sam's mashed potato's, asparagus w lemon, mushrooms, and the lobster Mac & cheese which was amazing. I enjoyed everything thoroughly as did everyone!!

We finished w desserts, creme brûlée, cheesecake, flourless chocolate cake and some cappuccino rounded it out nicely!

It's extremely expensive but this time they gave us the world!

It was a wonderful celebration. I would love to go again someday.

Another day another brunch review. I'd been hearing good things about Sofia for a while, so when I discovered they had brunch it was a done deal. 

Very cute spot, that's pretty popular, so be sure to make a reservation if you can. Their brunch menu isn't very extensive, but the options that they do have (based on what I tried) are amazing. There's also a bottomless mimosa option which is always a "yay" in my book. 

If you enjoy sweeter brunch options (and honestly even if you don't), you have to try the ricotta pancakes. They are light and fluffy with a cinnamon swirl and cream cheese glaze *cue the Homer Simpson drool gif*. They are soooo good, and not too sweet so if you'd like to enjoy a breakfast/brunch cocktail it won't be too much. I also had the steak and eggs which was very tasty. I'm a medium/medium-well gal when it comes to my steak and it came out perfect; eggs were scrambled just right *chef's kiss*. If you haven't checked out Sofia yet, I encourage you to! If you've been and never had those pancakes, you're doing yourself a disservice.

Salsa bar is loaded but you only get two picks with each entree and my chicken enchiladas were terrible! The chicken was grill than diced to make my enchiladas and it was not the right type of cooked chicken for this dish. I've only had it with shredded or pulled chicken with I love! Bummer, wasted a meal on dis, so non authentic! Boooo
Chips were really good though but my main course sucked.

Awe!! 

That Bonnie and Clyde thing! But a ok. Many ruby slippers around town and this was the one I chose! It was right next to my hotel after all! 

You have booths and shared bar seats! There's almost always a wait! Menu is mainly brunch! They close at 2 pm! Or 3 on some days. 

Food: my fried cat fish with grits cake and tomatoes sauce came out hot! A ok!

Their shrimp special on poached eggs were a ok too! Faster food! A few friendly waitresses. Maybe 2! A ok place! Mimosa and bloody Mary's  are the draw!!

To bitch directly at Ikea and avoid the 800 number: Call Direct Line 215-551-4532. I hit 1111 then 0 to get to a human receptionist. Also try extensions 1452 or 1930 to get a live person. I'm pretty pissed off at Ikea right now. Hopefully this will help you avoid getting any more pissed off by trying to call the 888 number on the website.

Updated on Aug. 13th.  i received a private Yelp message from a rep @ Parx. She assured me that I would be hearing from someone soon to rectify my poor experience.  STILL WAITING !    

First time here. Encountered a problem immediately. When I obtained their points card, with $25 pre loaded, it was not being recognized by the slot machine(s) and i say machines in plural because I was advised by the staff to keep trying another slot machine. Without exaggeration I tried at least 20 machines. The staff finally decided to give me another card. Same problem with 7, yes, 7 cards. This all took an hour. By this time I lost my urge to give them my money. I played slots for another hour, then packed it in.  BY THE WAY, as a New Yorker, having to contend with smokers here and all the smell that goes with it doesn't induce me  to come back. All in all, I felt as if I wasted my time here.

I have visited this place many times, and each time it is lousy. The food is okay, but the service is terrible, so it doesn't make it worth it. First, they never wear gloves, even when handling the cash register and then touching loaves of bread. Second, I'm allergic to eggs, so when I ask them for egg-free bread, they have to go to the back freezer to get some. Each time, they tell me how I am inconveniencing them and that I should have called ahead.
The worst part of this is that one time, I found a RUSTY TACK baked into my bread! I took it into them, and they just said sorry and gave me another loaf. 
Yes, they have good gluten-free bread. But if you want someone to explain things to you or talk to you about what you need, don't count on it.

I'm a pretty frequent customer at Natural Born Juicers -- I think I stop in about once a week on average. I love their blended juices (which they describe as a smoothie/juice hybrid made with fresh juice + "fresh frozen" fruit.) The Black Magic Berry and Homespun Heaven are my go-to  blends and I highly recommend them.

The composition of the blended juices seems to vary slightly each time, which makes sense, considering that the taste depends on the characteristics of the fruit they happen to have that day, and I'm not sure if there is a set ratio of ingredients that they use in the blends. As a result, the sweetness/tartness profile can vary considerably from visit to visit, but this is less of a complaint than it is a heads up to other customers -- if you're expecting a drink to taste exactly the same as it was at your last visit...probably not going to happen. 

So, I love their juices. If I were rating NBJ based solely on their product, I would give a higher rating.

Unfortunately, their customer service is just ... generally sort of nonexistent? I second Matthew H.'s comments from his March review: I'm not sure if I've ever received a greeting or smile or any sign of acknowledgment from any employees when I've entered the store. Sometimes they don't even ask me what I'm interested in purchasing when I step up to the register -- they just wait for me to speak and then they only speak to inform me of my purchase price. I'm paying almost $6 for a drink -- at least humor me with a hello, a goodbye, a thank you, something, rather than giving off the impression that I've interrupted your afternoon? Maybe they only hire total introverts at their Mass Ave. storefront, or maybe I'm just routinely stopping by the store at the wrong time?? 

In contrast, I've had great, friendly customer service when purchasing from the juice truck. 

Juices: 5 stars
Customer service: 2 stars

This store is super cute! The decor doesn't make it look much like a cupcake shop though. Their cupcakes have this crunchy cookie-like top which tastes great. It is also offered at a reasonable price, about $3 at the time of writing. The staff is extremely nice.

They offer vegan cupcakes.

The owner of this establishment is extremely rude. She is blessed by her amazing staff for why people return. 
If you want good food but to be treated like you are an idiot sure stop in. Hopefully your visit is lucky enough not to run into Serina. 
The bad taste of her can almost ruin the great food. 

This would be a 4 or 5 star rating establishment if she would kindly stay away from it.

I have been anxiously waiting for this restaurant to open up since I first heard about it on Foobooz. Anyone that knows me, knows that I LOVE Jose Garces' food. After months and months of anticipation (and web stalking), I finally made a lunch reservation to try out the new Garces spot. 

My meal started with a chicken, roasted pepper and cilantro empanada. The empanada was good but you could not taste the cilantro. I also ordered the guacamole which was amazing. The guacamole had small chunks of smoked pineapple and was served with plantain and yucca chips. The smokey flavor was very interesting as I have never tasted that in a guacamole. The pineapple added a little bit of sweetness to the guacamole. From now on, every guacamole I eat (which is a lot) will include smoked pineapple. As my main dish I ordered ceviche with red snapper fish (fish of the day) and a side of frijoles negros. The ceviche was delicious and the flavors complimented one another well. I stole some of my friend's plantain chips and used the chips to accompany my ceviche. The frijoles negros were small but filling enough. I was too full for dessert but decided on a traditional cafe con leche to end the meal. 

If you are a Garces groupie you will notice some favorites from his other restaurants such as the ensalada verde, croquetas and Cuban sandwich. 

The decor is different. At first you think you are walking into a diner with the booths, takeout and diner counter. The back room looks like a restaurant in Little Havana. I would like to see some improvement with the bathrooms. There are two unisex bathrooms located at the back of the restaurant. You cannot tell if the bathroom is occupied or unoccupied. When inside the bathroom you forget you are at a Garces restaurant and think you have been transported to a diner in Jersey. This bathroom could use some upgrading to be on par with other Garces bathrooms.

I was very happy with my Garces/Cuban food experience. Next time I would like to try a batido, arroz con pollo and a slice of tres leche cake. Yes, I already have my next meal planned and I am not ashamed.

I came to Ampersand 27 (where Murietta's uesd to be and inside/attached to the Varscona Hotel) yesterday with a group of Yelpers to try out their newly created signature cocktail in honour of the Edmonton Opera's upcoming opening of Lucia.

Ampersand 27 created a fabulous dark and mirky drink, reminiscent of Scotland, called Lucia's Loch ($13) by bartender Janice Bochon:

1 oz. Kahlua
1 oz. Bowmore 12 year
1 oz. Lavender Simple Syrup
2 oz. Milk

And let me tell you, it was the perfect mix of sweet and dark!

The hubs and I ordered the Maple Pork Belly off the Share & Syhare Alike menu for $17.  Four small pieces of perfectly cooked maple butter pork belly came alongside southwestern mequite corn, baked beans, green pea & fritters.  The flavour combinations and presentation could not have been any more perfect.

We also tried the Arctic Char Crudo ($18) with fried avocado, sesame crisp, asaparagus, truffle & soy.  I had never seen avocado with a light tempura before but it was delish.

I wouldn't hesitate to order any of the above again!

Their menu itself, is absolutely adorable, and I love the layout.  

The inside of &27 is just gorgeous with numerous seating options ranging from tables, to booths, to barstools around the bar.  I adore the variety of lighting fixtures here in the clean and modern and bright atmosphere - everything from an array of twinking lights above nestled/intertwined in almost a bramble bush like fixture hanging above the dinine area to the funky chandeliers in the bar.  Near the bar, there is a funk white marbled and unusually shaped table with tall chairs around it that easily seats 8 and low backed white couches for relaxing.  There is a small room to the side, separted by a frosted glass wall perfect for entertaining a gathering of 30ish people.

P.S.  Have you checked out their website yet?  If not, you NEED to.  Whoever designed/runs their site, knows what they are doing!  It is G-O-R-G-E-O-U-S-!  http://ampersand27.com/

This place used to be a Chuy's, so I was hoping that the new business that took its place would be comparable. 

Nope. 

Mediocre food, high prices, and small portions. 

I was born and raised in Brooklyn, New York, so to go into a place that calls itself "Native New Yorker" should make me feel nostalgic or remind me of home, right? 

Nope. 

The food here is more comparable to Applebee's than something unique to New York. Oh, and this place is inspired by Buffalo New York, not New York City. And if I want Buffalo Wings, I can go to Hooters for a fraction of the price and much better scenery.  

If you want a place that serves great food at reasonable prices, this isn't the place.

I am a big fan of Vietnamese food - but before Philly I had mostly gone to Viet restaurants that sells the more common dishes: banh mi, pho, vermicelli, egg noodle, fried rice, etc. 

I was so excited to see the Viet restaurants here have more variety. This place especially had many amazing choices. We got the lotus salad instead of the common papaya salad we would usually get. We also ordered shaking beef and clams sautéed in black bean sauce. 

Lotus roots salad: well done dish and looks so aesthetically pleasing with the shrimp chips. The waitress said the papaya salad doesn't come with the shrimp chips, only lotus one. I'm not used to the flavoring of this dish - so wasn't a big fan. Definitely an acquired taste.

Shaking beef (bo luc lac): tastes sooo good, wow I haven't had shaking beef that disappoints. The seasoning is just right - and it pairs so well with the lemon/pepper dipping sauce. This is my new favorite viet dish! 

Clam sautéed in black bean sauce: amazing!! I love clams dishes in Asian cuisines. So flavorful... the black beans are not your typical black beans, they are fermented black soybeans used in most Asian cuisines. (Similar sauce used in Chinese or Korean style black bean sauce noodle - jajangmyeom) 

This place is very spacious, if you have a small party, you won't need to make reservations. However, they also have those family style lazy Susan sitting areas for big groups! If you're coming with a group don't forget to make a reservation!

Wow this place might be my next obsession. I've come to really enjoy the Vegan/Vegetarian options. So many people in the city have told me great things about this place.

Everything here is vegan friendly! We got the ziggy and smoked house burger, along with the pumpkin pie milkshake. 

Ziggy burger: your good old classic burger ingredients (tomato, pickles...)

Smoked burger: the smokey taste is really good along with the melted cheese but not much ingredients inside 

My boyfriend who is a meat lover - ate the beyond meat burger and was amazed at how good it tasted and could barely tell the difference. I was also impressed by everything we ate, and the milkshake (which has no dairy and consist of mainly soy beans) was probably one of the best milkshake I've had. Being lactose intolerant, I can't help but feel guilty every time I try a milkshake. This soy milkshake made me feel good! 

So happy this place exists! Will definitely be coming back to try different items on the menu.

Expect a 30 minute + wait when you come on a weekend brunch - every time I bike by there's always a line. They also don't take online reservations, you have to put yourself in line in person. We finally came for brunch since we've heard great things about this place. It's BYOB - and they'll provide you with a nice tub of chilled water & ice. 

My SO was deciding between a couple French toasts and the waiter suggested the cannoli French toast. It was delicious but a bit overly sweet for my taste. The French toast was also HUGE - very carb-y dish. I think French toasts are always the best paired with fresh fruits (for the refreshing taste) and the cannolis didn't come with fruits but had jam on top instead. 

I order the special: pesto chicken bowl (served with quinoa, brown rice, arugula, and eggs + other veggies). It was disappointing as my dish had turned out to be majority arugula. Instead of a bowl, I felt like I ordered a salad. When I asked, the waiter told me they didn't put brown rice because they ran out (lol). He was kind enough to put in a different order for me. I switched for the huevos rancheros instead. We had waited for a long time for our first order to come out and by the time my replacement order came out I was already full from eating my SO's French toast. (I'm telling you, that French toast is big enough to feed 2 people!!) Huevos ranchero was good, but nothing special. 

Overall: expect long wait to get food & seated, larger portions, friendly staff, food was okay

We got the chicken and beef manakeesh which are Lebanese flatbread pizza. The flavorings were very unique, I thought the chicken one was better. The beef one was strange because it was ground beef pieces instead of slices of beef. I wasn't a big fan of that. 

The left side of the store is a cafe where you order meals and the right side is a bakery with many baklava selections and other Lebanese desserts. They even had coffee, tea, and fruit juices. I didn't get to try anything from the bakery but will definitely be back to try more items.

Make sure to make a reservation! This place is popular and they only have  7 tables for indoor - however they have plenty of outdoor seating.

Staffs were nice - we were seated quickly after promptly arriving for our 6:30pm reservation. We ordered the Wild mushroom Arancini, Rigatoni Alla Vodka, Pan Seared Gnocchi, and Campanelle Nero (squid ink pasta with shrimp).

The Arancini is amazing!! I have never eaten this before and now I'm obsessed. It's crunchy yet soft on the inside, smothered in delicious aioli sauce. It's a MUST order appetizer.

The Gnocchi and Squid Ink pasta were delicious. I like the squid ink dish the best - the sauce was light and didn't have dairy. Tasted more tomato-y base. Gnocchi was nicely seared and the corn and mushroom paired nicely. 

I did not like the Rigatoni with vodka sauce. The best part of the dish was the sausages which were amazing!! Rest of the dish consisted of carbs and sauce. Maybe some vegetables would have complimented the dish.... The dish was so simple I feel like anyone could have gotten vodka sauce from the grocery store and make it themselves. 

Overall had a great experiences. We sat outside in the "covered" sitting area that were built on the roads. The downside with those seating is that there were NO airflow!! It was a 90+ degree day in Philly and we were sweating during our meal. I suggest getting an indoor seating or come during a cooler time.

When we tried going the first time it was on a weekend. The line was so long it stretched around the corner to the other side. We decided to come back on a week day another time at 4pm to see if lines will be shorter. 

We were right! If you wanna try this place, don't come during a busy hour on a weekend. Go during the week, it'll save you some frustration.

We got the Philly cheese steak with onions, peppers, mushroom, and whiz. They pan fry the ingredients right in front of you and takes seconds to prepare your food. The line does go pretty quickly as long as people are decisive on their orders. 

Ask for these spicy peppers on the side, it's the most flavorful stuff in my cheese steak. I was definitely not impressed with the cheese steak - it was lacking some flavor. I don't think they season the steak well. Maybe I'm just not a fan of Philly cheese steak in general? 

Seating upstairs is nice, but they also have standing tables outdoors.

Overall: no line during the week, average cheese steak, CASH ONLY

Very nice hibachi and sushi place me and my family eat here a lot I love it here probably the best hibachi grill in Indianapolis Indiana I would definitely suggest this to anyone who loves #1 sushi and #2 hibachi grills the atmosphere is amazing with the fish pond in the back ground  I love it here

Ps your cup will never run dry they always refill it when it's half gone chefs are very funny and willing to engage in conversation with guests if you get sushi I suggest the dragon roll it is delicious

Alright, I had to go with four stars simply because it's not a place I'd ever find myself CRAVING to hit up again- mainly because of the price tag. Poor PR girl here, come on. But, this is nothing like Nashville has ever seen and it's a great addition to our city's dining landscape - I would suggest everyone try it once. Despite having to eat Ramen for two weeks after that meal, I'm still SO glad I did it.

Atmosphere: A friend and I "gifted" dinner there to each other for Christmas this year - it was a perfect pick for two restaurant-loving best friends. We were greeted outside of the building (we read on Yelp not to arrive early or you'd be forced to wait around in Patterson House until your reservation time - there is no waiting area), which was slightly creepy because the hostess knew our name and called out to us as she exited Patterson House. She welcomed us, took our coats and led us to our seats on the end of the dining bar. The interior is simple - a perfect backdrop for the artistic courses that would come our way throughout the evening. We had plenty of space and the noise level was perfect to not feel like we were alone in the room, but still maintain a good conversation.

Service: The chefs are incredible and so friendly, as are the other staff members. We were jovially greeted by one of the Goldberg brothers, who laid out the plan for the evening and ensured we were settled in and looking forward to a great evening. We were. Chef Anderson was particularly friendly - when he heard I was headed to Copenhagen in the coming months (the location of his last culinary residence), he wrote down some dining recommendations for me - can't wait to try them!

Drinks: I gotta be honest - my palate is way below this place, so I'm not sure can totally appreciate the drink pairings. But that doesn't mean I didn't LOVE them. We both ordered the regular drink pairing ($35/person) and loved every beverage that was placed in front of us. Some seriously unique and tasty concoctions. If you go, just suck it up and add the drink pairings - it's worth it.

Food: Like I said, my palate isn't that sophisticated, but each course brought something new for us to try - which was SO much fun. I couldn't begin to tell you half the things I ate that night and would have to refer to the "menu map" they gave us at the end of the night, but everything was fun to try. This place is definitely not for the un-adventurous soul.

Overall: If I had unlimited funds, I'd return here regularly since the menu changes based on the whim of the chefs. Even those of us without a deep appreciation for the variety of ingredients found in each dish can still appreciate the great sense of adventure that is going to The Catbird Seat. Definitely give it a try at least once!

The seafood here is so delicious and fresh! NOM NOM NOM *

Be prepared for about an hour wait because this place can get so busy, but hey - the food here is so good! Definitely worth the wait!

What we ordered:

1. Seafood pasta - huge sea scallops and shrimp sauteed with garlic, lemon, white wine, tomato, basil over linguini noodles and Parmesan cheese. Yummy! This is a very filling dish. You can definitely share it with 2 people (5/5)

2. Swordfish - served with rice pilaf (my bf's choice) and guacamole and salsa. The swordfish tasted delicious. Definitely everything here was served fresh! (5/5)

3. 1/2 Dozen Oysters - add some cocktail sauce, squeeze some lemons, slurp and yum! What more can I say? (5/5)

4. Fried Calamari - fresh and scrumptious! It tastes great with the tartar sauce dip! (5/5)

The entrees that we ordered came with your choice of soup or salad, rice or french fries. Unfortunately the seafood pasta doesn't come with the french fry option - only soup or salad. So I opted for the clam chowder, it was decent (but I've had better). There is an extra charge if you choose to split dishes, so just don't mention it to them and you'll be fine.

Parking can be limited. There's 90 min parking available in a small lot nearby. The restaurant is right by the water, so depending on where you sit - you can have a nice view. Service is friendly and the food was delicious!

Yelp Check-In Offer: Buy 1 Get 1 free drink!

The group of us came here feeling parched after a workout/double surrey race on the beach! We ordered the fruit smoothie, which costs a whopping $5 for a large size. You have the option of strawberry or mango.

My bf and I got the mango and a friend got the strawberry. The mango smoothie tastes much more refreshing; the strawberry mango tasted a bit bland for us. But overall, the BOGO is worth it.

I dined here recently with a group of friends for dinner. I ordered the Pumpkin Agnolotti (a ravioli-type dish). The menu said it was $16, which seemed reasonable for pasta, although less reasonable when I was presented with a portion sized for a baby bird (strike 1). I could have overlooked the size if I had been presented with something truly spectacular that wowed my taste buds. Unfortunately, the pasta was drowned in a thick cream sauce that completely overpowered what was supposed to be a pumpkin filling (strike 2). For all I know, there wasn't even pumpkin in there. It's sad to say but I've had better pasta at some chain restaurants. Still that too could have been overlooked because I was having such a nice time with my friends. You win some, you lose some. Until I received the check and saw I was charged $32 for the dish (strike 3). It says nowhere on the menu that the price shown is for an appetizer. However, apparently everything in the PASTA section is priced for the appetizer portion. While our server was friendly and attentive, I deducted his tip severely (something I vary rarely do) for completely failing to mention that the entrée size of pasta was $32. 

The best part is that before posting this review, I decided to check out other reviews and see what people were saying (normally I would have done this prior to selecting a restaurant but I didn't select this place). In response to one unhappy yelper, the owner commented, "We also charge what the menu says things cost." Nope. Not so much.

2-24 Update: I just reviewed my credit card statement and it appears that the someone adjusted the tip amount and charged me more than I had authorized. Disputing with my credit card company. Would NEVER recommend this place.

Like a life long friend India Kabab & Curry is always there for you!  To be honest, I've never been except for their lunch buffet....but every time I've been including this most recent visit everything has been great.  I'm a sucker for masala and today they had veggie and chicken masala along with aloo, veggie fritters and tandoori chicken which are some of my favorites.  The garlic naan was good as always.  I was seriously worried when they expanded a while ago that things would change but no!!  Keep being awesome!  :)

This place gets 10 out of 5 stars in my book! 

I decided to check this place out after seeing some good reviews in my news feed. The concept of nitro brew also intrigued me. I showed up today around 1:30pm and noticed that they were actually just about to close. Womp womp...but the awesome owners Josh and Derek saw that this was my first time there and I had all my work with me, so they were kind enough to let me work there even though the place is closed from 2-4pm. This awesome gesture of great customer service was enough to give this place 5/5 stars but it gets better.

Next they let me sample all of their nitro brews since I've never tasted nor even heard of it until recently. If you are a coffee aficionado who generally drinks coffee black and appreciates the unique flavors of the various coffee beans...this will be heaven for you. The nitro cold brew as they pointed out REALLY bring out the different flavors of the coffee beans.

I tend to drink my coffee with some milk and sugar because the taste of the coffee alone is too bitter for me so picked the expresso which tasted delightful. 

They also have doughnuts from Datz doughnuts of south tampa. I picked the creme brûlée doughnut which has browned sugar coating and a vanilla pudding center. Might not be a good idea to eat the whole thing in one sitting unless you like the sugar coma. ;) super delicious nonetheless. They were $2 off when I ordered it. 

This place is a great spot to get some work done since they have plenty of seating and free wifi. I think this spot just made it to the top of my list of " study spots in tampa". 

This location is a coffee shop by day (until about 2pm) then a bar by night (called pour house). The owners of the coffee shop and bar are both fantastic, kind and friendly people. I wish them the best of luck and I will definitely be back to fill out my loyalty card like it's my job. :)

Being a vegetarian for 25 years, when any new vegetarian restaurant opens, I get excited.  I've been anticipating the opening of this place since the announcement came that they were opening, and tried to dine there within the first few days.  Unfortunately, even though they were supposed to be open for lunch, and said so on their Facebook page, when my sis and I drove 20 minutes out of our way, we found a sign on the door that said "opening at 5".  This left a bad taste in my mouth, and I probably should've listened.  But I wanted that curried chickpea sandwich, so I tried again.

When I arrived today while my fiancé was parking the car, I walked in and wasn't sure wether to seat myself or not.  The bartender just stared at me, so I went and found an open table.  I sat.  Sat.  Sat some more.  I sat as many staff members leisurely strolled by, never saying a word to me.  After a while, my fiancé came in, and then suddenly I was visible.  The waitress came over and when asking questions about the menu, we discovered that they were basically out of everything, including the curried chickpea sandwich.  I wanted to walk out then, but the fiancé was hungry, so we stayed.  

We ordered the fried beets and pan de queso to start, and then a chopped salad and veggie burger to share.  The beets and bread were fine.  There was far too little sauce which I found out later was because they were running out.  Just buy a few bottles of organic ketchup why don't you?  

The veggie burger was also fine, as was the salad, but again, more sauce was needed.  When I asked for more, the waitress completely forgot.  She was in la la land, and also continued to lean down really close to us ( more him ) which was super weird.  She also came over and refilled his drinks a few times while mine stayed empty.  We asked someone else for our check, and asked to box the food ourselves since I watched her box people's food against dish crates.

The check came to 55 dollars for lunch, which is laughable considering the service, the fact that we didn't really get what we wanted because they were out of everything, and that the food wasn't mind blowing.

Go to The Agrarian before it closes if you want innovative vegetarian food, and then head to OR Juice, Gokul, Local Harvest, or any other ethnic place on Grand.

It's been a year and this place has solidified its place in my heart as my favorite Indian restaurant. Prices have gone up $1 ($10 for cash, $11 for credit) for lunch buffet, but I still consider it very worth it. 

There seems to be even more variety since the last time I came. The butter chicken is still my favorite entree. The wraps with meat inside are AMAZING. I also drank so much mango lassi and chai tea while I was here. I really cannot complain about this place. It is so amazing. Makes any trip to St. Louis worth it. EVEN WHEN I LIVE 4 HOURS AWAY!!

Wow has this place gone downhill! Used to have some of the best ribs in town. No more. Now they are overcooked, dry pieces of jerky hanging off the bone. Not even the best sauce could save them so it didn't matter that the sauce that came with them was completely uninspiring.  Sorry that I ordered them. A long way from the old days here and at the Lil Abner's Express at Ft. Lowell and First. 

Steaks are a different matter. Better than average but not much to brag about. Some of our steaks were tough. Others not. All properly cooked. 

The pinto beans are served in unlimited amounts, but who wants them? They were as bland as beans could possibly be so I reached for the salsa. It was like slop: looked like splattered tomatoes in a bowl with not much else and too tasteless to help the beans. 

One bright spot was the Texas Garlic Toast. Thankfully as much as you want.

Finally, beware of the lack of menus.  Really, one must ask why there are no menus? Too expensive to print at the prices they charge? The spoken menus are tacky, an annoyance and unfair to the customer. Rattled off so fast that some of the spiel has to be repeated. Incomplete too. Not all the options, such as steak and rib combos, are  verbalized by the wait staff. Nor do you get to see the outrageously high prices given the mediocre quality. Especially in such kitsch, neglected and run down surroundings. 

This place needs a facelift and serious upgrading in order to return to its old glory days.

Stopped through Nashville on a family road trip and stumbled upon this place and we are so thankful we did! Absolutely the delicious! The food was fantastic, the beer was cold, and the service was delightful!

Definitely check this place out if you're ever in town!

HOW DID I NOT KNOW ABOUT THIS PLACE!?

Omg. It's exquisite.

I did a search for "gluten free cafe" this morning, called to make sure they were allowing people to come work there for a while, and found... heaven.

Actually, as I pulled in, "It's A Beautiful Day" by Michael Buble played on my radio and that was definite foreshadowing. ;)

This place is GREAT!!!!!

A couple things I particularly love about it:

- Staff is super kind, really really friendly.

- Plenty of seats... and they WELCOME computer workers! There's another location 2 doors down from the main cafe where computer workers can go to work. HOW SPECTACULAR. I also go to The Coffee Room in Newtown, and like it there, but they're only allowing visits to max out at an hour.

- So many gluten free options!! OMG. I want to try it all.

- The coffee was great (and super generous portions). I got a large cappucino with almond milk and it's massive.

- Soundtrack in the main Be Well Cafe was my jam (lots of pop songs I was dancing to as I was working). I don't love the tunes in the other cafe as much but that's OK, I can pop in my AirPods. :)

- I love the artwork, the overall vibe, the "You Are Loved" picture on the wall. EPIC.

- It's great to work from here - there's fast complimentary wifi and lots of outlets.

I'm super surprised to find this place in the suburbs and I am SO GLAD I did.

Love, love, love it here, and can't wait for their Richboro location to open which is even closer to home.

I went into Duchess for the first time ever at 2:00pm today. I've heard such amazing things about this place. They've been opened for years and have the most amazing baked goods. 
I get in the store, it's a super long line and everyone is in a buzz and cant wait to get to the counter. 

I get go the counter and I ask "is there a list of what I can order?". The lady looks at me and in a snarky tone says "what you see is what we have". I say... So I can't get a crussant or anything else? She says "we don't have any right now, all we have are macaroons". 
I asked "what's a macaroon?". She couldn't give me an exact answer. 
So I walked out extremely dissapointed with both the service from this lady and the lack of product. 
You'd think a well established and world known backery like this place would have ongoing supply from their backery, or have made enough supply to support their business hours. I don't know if this place is amazing cause I couldn't get anything!!!
My thoughts exactly: I will not return. I'm not going first thing in the morning because a reasonable business would ensure they have stock for the business hours. Not enough for the first 100 customers. 

Don't like this? Think of it this way. If Mary Browns Chicken only had enough chicken for a select few customers, they wouldn't be in business. They can inflate their costs to keep the store open. But they're going to lose customers because they never have enough supply. Is that a good business model?

When we're in Reno, we enjoy coming here for one of their delicious Martinis. Located in the El Dorado casino....Roxy is swanky, sexy, cool. It has a romantic vibe but you don't have to worry about dress code. After all, it's in a casino and most of the clientele are there to enjoy something other than gambling. 

There is a pianist playing Jazz that kicks the evening off to a great start. There's 102 different Martinis, it's hard to decide. They have a Happy Hour every day from 4:30-6:30, which includes all their Martinis along with some munchies. If you don't like Martinis, that's ok because they have other alcohol drinks as well, including wine!

We came back again and I'm glad we did because I needed to update my review. This time we ordered: 

BLAT-bacon, lettuce, avocado, and tomato. This is our fave! 5/5 Stars 

Club-grilled rosemary chicken, bacon, lettuce, and provolone 5/5 Stars 

Both Sammie's came with salad with their delicious dressing 

Minestrone-5/5
