Chicken tortilla soup 4/5 i forgot that I ordered this soup last time and didn't really like it. 

The place is small, you order at the counter. The line may be long but it goes quite quick. There's plenty of seating both inside and out. The service is friendly and the wait wasn't too long to receive our meals. The price is very reasonable for the quality of food you get.

You ever wish you could just walk out of a place as soon as you walk in? Well this was it. Upon walking in, it was dimly lit with only natural lighting, the lady points towards a table. The interior could use some cleaning. My daughter asked to go next door to the ramen shop leaving me with my mom to dine here. I wish we followed her. 

The lady brings over water with no ice, the water was room temperature, so that was a bummer. 

We ordered: 

Scallion pancake-3 stars, was too oily and doughy.

Popcorn chicken-4 Stars, fried perfect, little too sweet for my liking. 

Mongolian beef-2 stars don't know how to describe it, had an almost sour taste to it, didn't like it at all. Never had Mongolian beef like that, we barely ate any of it because we didn't care for it. 

I'm not sure if it's what we ordered but sorry, its a three star place for me

With CA having so many restrictions due to COVID, it was quite refreshing to get away for the weekend, and Charlie's is where I wanted to go! We have eaten here before but that was more like eight years ago so I needed to refresh my memory.

We made reservations for dinner and it was quite easy with many time slots available. We arrived on time and there wasn't a wait when we arrived. 

Our waiter was good, but we didn't  catch his name...he never introduced himself.  As a matter of fact, this is the reason why my experience falls short of a 5 star experience!! We were Easy, as far as sales goes. We knew what we wanted, we didn't have any special requests or dietary adjustments. With that being said, wish he was a bit more personable. It's not every day you spend over $200 on dinner only to have less than stellar service. 

Our food came out in a timely manner. My colossal shrimp cocktail was HUGE. The mixed greens salad my hubs got was a bit underwhelming. It needed more vinegarette and maybe some different textures in the salad. Both our filets were cooked perfectly and my lobster was sweet. 

I highly recommend Charlie Palmer's, the food was definitely worth every penny.

We gave this place a try before heading home. It's open 24 hours and it's your typical coffee shop with a lot of your favorites. 

When we arrived there was a fifteen minute wait. Anyhoo, it was quite busy in here for a Monday. We ordered the clubhouse sandwich and pancakes. 

The clubhouse sandwich was probably the best we've had. There was a generous portion of high quality Turkey breast. I took some out because there was so much. How often do you complain about that? The bacon was crisp and not greasy too. My only mistake was ordering it on sourdough. The bread was super thick and it was a challenge eating it. I asked our server if I could have two slices of wheat bread and she offered to give me a whole new club but I declined since I didn't want the sandwich to go to waste. I ended up assembling it myself and it was much better on wheat vs sourdough. 

The pancakes were Huge and the eggs were cooked to specs. 

I also want to add that the green salad I ordered was super fresh and big. Sometimes when you order a salad at a coffee shop, it's usually not the best. But not here! They do have an AYCE soup and salad bar which I might try next time.

If you're in Reno and you're a foodie, this is where you need to be! Yeah, it's a little pricey, but it's so worth it! We came here on a Sunday, a party of six, were seated, immediately! No standing in line, maybe it was the time of day? But, a place like this in Vegas would surely have a line formed out the door! 

At $35 per person, your brunch includes unlimited mimosas! Our server, Eric, was meticulously efficient on making sure that our glasses were full! Yes, us Yelpers go to brunch quite often, and we have been to places that offer bottomless mimosas, but sometimes, the servers are difficult to locate, when we want to replenish our drinks. Not here. You have your cold station with salads, seafood, granola, fresh fruit, and cheeses.  Hell, you can make your own butcher board, with the different cheeses, olives, cold meats, and pickled whatever. The hot food station with the prime rib and ham, was divine! Next to that, you have salmon, lamb chops, schnitzel, oysters rockefeller, and more. There is a dessert station with chocolate covered strawberries, creme brulee, cheesecakes and a huge array of different breads, danishes, and baked goods, you can imagine! There is a kid station, omelette station,  and an ice cream sundae station. 

After careful scoping of the layout, my game plan was to eat the meats and seafood first. I had the prime rib, shrimp, crab claws and oysters, as an app. After several trips, I made my way to the cooked foods, pasta, veggies and schnitzel. Then, I went for the desserts, I don't like sweets, but they looked so pretty, how could I resist? I am proud of the fact that I ate $35 worth of food, lol! 

I am quite aware of the buffets that Vegas has to offer. But, when my hubby didn't care to stand in line for thirty plus minutes at our last visit to Vegas, this was a long overdue alternative. Sterling's offers everything that Vegas has to offer without having to stand in line, and it's much closer in distance for us than Vegas!

When you walk in you will be immediately captivated by the ahhhhmazing mural on the far wall. It's an artistic expression of some of our city's awesomeness. I won't spoil it with specifics you'll have to visit Tavolo V for details. Scott & Selena were just lovely servers! They were super super hospitable, accommodating and gave great recommendations. Actually Scott wasn't my server, Selena was my assigned waitress but they apparently work as a team here...I love it! 
 
I started with the roasted cauliflower...to die for! Perfect texture & taste. Next up, Salmon special with Parmesan crusted tomato, arugula pesto & a crab chutney (devoured). Lastly, my sister and I shared the Coconut Gelato & Tiramisu (both of which we took a single bite and left u finished). Neither was bad I think we just weren't in the mood for dessert after all. 

Other amenities:
*Both street & secured parking available
*Patio 
*Full Bar
*TV
*Exposed brick 
*Linen napkins 
*Tea lights  
*Beautiful wood detailing 
*Partially open kitchen 
*Groovy background music 
*Prime location 
*Me....I'll be a regular going forward

~Christy

I love Winslow's goat cheese cookie! I could stop my review there but there's a few more awesome things I'll share about Winslow's. It's sort of like a General Store/Diner/Winery/French Bakery type of spot. So much goodness in a single location.

The feeling you get when you walk in is like a down home restaurant or tiny version of Cracker Barrel. Grab a patio seat on a beautiful summer day or a window seat inside on a brisk winter morning. They serve breakfast and please know the pancakes are splendid! They also prepare my egg whites to perfection with a house made strawberry preserve that makes me wanna slap my mama. If you'd like to take some of their goodness to-go do check out the cooler for pot pies, cheeses, soups, desserts and more. Now that I've got that out of the way let's talk service; it's great! Very hospitable, accommodating and friendly. I don't eat a lot of different things when I stop by Winslow's so to say I visit for variety would be a stretch...however the staples & excellent service do keep me coming back for more.

~Christy

PuraVegan is an amazing little Central West End vegan cafe! They offer everything from breakfast, lunch, small treats, smoothies, juice, supplements such as hemp, grab & go prepped meals, beverages, seeds and more.

The customer service is very friendly, warm & welcoming but be aware, you will wait. Depending on your order the prep time can be a bit slow so I recommend you not be in a hurry when visiting PuraVegan. Also, it's not going to be light on your pocketbook. My smoothie alone is $10. Add food and you'll be looking at approximately $30 per person. 

The décor is super cute. Vibrantly colorful wall art, bamboo plants, lanterns, funky furniture and plush window seating. It's a great place to have a quite meeting, study or grab a healthy meal that's good for your soul. 

~Christy

Courtney was a excellent bartender/server. Pleasant, prompt and made the perfect suggestion when I explained what I was in the mood for. She didn't flinch at my requests for substitutions which is always appreciated. Nothing but smiles. The food was delicious; arrived fresh, hot & and exactly as I ordered. There's ample parking and plenty of inside/outside dining space to accommodate distance or seating while waiting for your takeaway order.  

Highly recommend the spinach avocado Benedict. Their house potatoes were superb (and I'm not a potato fan).  

~Christy

Authentic & delicious Vietnamese food located on South Grand. It's centered in the international food strip just across from BP gas station; between Basil Spice Thai and Gelataria Del Leone cafè.  I'll get straight to the point with this update...

Excellent service provided by knowledgable, attentive wait staff. I highly recommend the Pho. Please note although I get the vegetarian option they only serve beef based broth. The curry is superb I've tried both the tilapia and scallop versions. The dishes are filling but not so much that I'd consider sharing. Besides, the cost is so reasonable you could feed a family of 4 for u set $50 here. 

The restaurant is spacious enough to accommodate an intimate or small group setting. 

There is a full bar to compliment Pho Grand's full menu book. 

~Christy

Samantha, the barista was super welcoming, knowledgable and full of personality. I appreciated her genuine hospitality so much that I decided to start my review in her honor. Thank you Samantha, you're a doll.

Moving on...Kitchen House is located at Shenandoah & Compton in the Tower Grove East neighborhood; caddie corner to Van Gogh. This isn't some little coffee shack to grab a cup of Joe and hurry off to work; you'll want to relax, connect to WiFi, take in the view and savior your experience here. Everything from the chicken coop to the beautifully varnished antique tables makes the Kitchen House is a cozy home away from home.

They have comfy sofa chairs, small tables for 2, window seats and a long table for large groups to spread out. There is a book shelf in back if you want explore a new topic or need to occupy the kiddos. The restroom even had character, equipped with a chalkboard for your doodling purposes.

They sell local goods such as Kakao Chocolate, Blueprint Coffee and South Compton Soap. I love this hometown glory! 

I ordered the Monkey Breakfast Smoothie (slightly modified the Christy way). It was a delicious blend of espresso, nonfat plain Greek yogurt, banana, peanut butter, honey and almond milk. I also had to have the Thumbprint cookie which was superbly tasty & light. 

I enjoyed Kitchen House from beginning to end and cannot wait for my return trip. 

~Christy

This was my second visit to Cantina Laredo; I hadn't had a chance to review my first visit before returning so I'll clump them together.  This may be bitter sweet but I enjoyed my first Sunday Brunch visit a lot more than my Monday lunch return.  

Winners:
1. Decor is super nice
2. The complimentary salsa and chips are delicious 
3. Outdoor seating with flat screen TV 
4. Great space for groups

I won't display a list of "Losers" because I don't want anyone to misinterpret my experience with total dissatisfaction. What I did not particularly care for during my second visit was the service.  The server wasn't very personable or helpful in describing menu items.  She often disappeared and took an extended period of time to return with drinks (we were 1 of 2 tables in the entire restaurant during this time) while she swept the floor and congregated with co-workers.  The food was served hot and with a nice presentation.  My Mahi Mahi tacos were tasty; only 2 in a lunch order.  I could have had 2 more; they should consider expanding the dish.  2 tacos is a joke,  My guest had the chicken fajitas and stated they were also good. 

The mimosa was very good ($7.50) and the Patron Margarita was poured proper ($12.50)

If I return it will be to enjoy drinks and conversation in the chic establishment versus to have the dining experience of a lifetime. Cantina Laredo has a purpose...

Sat at the bar and was treated like royalty by the amazingly adorable Dominic. She was very welcoming and made sure I received my food just as I had requested. Small and intimate setting however there is window seating, sushi bar and bar top seating available. Not recommended for large parties but perfect for date night. 

Started with the house-made special sticky bun; crafted with crab...it is a perfect starter for pescatarians like myself. Next I devoured the veggie ramen; delicious veggie coconut broth, egg, mushroom, scallion and chunks of seasonal vegetables. 

Chilled my palate with their Cold Brew coffee when ch came served with ginormous ice cubes in a Rocks whiskey glass. Lastly, I finished with the Lemongrass Basil ice cream, a light & refreshing dessert garnished with 3 mini ginger snap cookies. 

Overall lovely experience, I can't wait for an encore.
~Christy

Scarlett's immediately reminded me of Sasha's upon entry. Gorgeous bar area, plenty of wine bottles to select from and the signature iPad menu. My server was pleasant; as was the Beet Salad. However, I wasn't blown away. For the price I thought the portion was pretty stingy. Nearly $15 for a lunch salad, no wine...not in my recession-free budget. 

The kitchen is semi-open and located in the rear of the restaurant where you can also find more seating. Scarlett's is nice for groups, couples or solo if wining & overpriced dining is your thing. Personally, I'm not in a rush to return. 

~Christy

This review is going to come in the form of a wordy "TIP". 

Not my favorite location but it works best for family brunch meetups. I love the coziness of Ladue. The fireplace and bright lighted OPH letters above the stone wall make me like I'm in a destination cabin.

I highly recommend using No Wait if you plan on going any time after 10AM on a weekend, otherwise you'll be one of the 100 people standing outside or inside crammed like sardines at the entrance.

If you're dining solo or on a casual date hit the bar to avoid waiting. Seated on a first come first serve basis, you can usually grab a stool without a hitch. Service is a little less personable at the bar but then again unless you luck up on one of their few great waitresses...the table service is a little shabby as well.

Please refrain from sitting your children at the bar. Not OPH policy but more of a Christy Peeve. Babies 3 and under need to be properly seated, not taking up space at a bar. 

If you are caught in the waiting line feel free to help yourself to a complimentary beverage in the sitting area, after checking in with the hostess. 

Parking is plentiful however so are the shops in this plaza. Prepare to walk a short distance as the lot fills up fast. 

The pancakes are delicious, almost addictive. 

~Christy

Hometown glory in the center of Old North St. Louis!the entire area is so rich in culture and beautifully preserved I feel warm inside whenever I hit St. Louis Ave.  I'll save my neighborhood spiel for a separate review and focus on selling you Crown Candy for now. 

This place is like an old monument; reminiscent of a 1960's candy/general/convenient store all wrapped in one. It's a family owned & operated business. The workers are always super personable, very efficient and knowledgable about product.

I encourage you to try the food, the malts and the chocolate here or you'll regret it.  I personally adore the Tuna (bread less), the Chocolate Banana malt, the Heavenly Hash, Dark Chocolate Blueberries and award winning Chocolate Covered Strawberries. 

Don't let the long line deter you, it moves fast. The booths are tight compared to today's restaurant seating but Crown Candy's nostalgia is what makes it such a cool place. 

Thank me later.
~Christy

When you see 5 stars you immediately want a review that'll definitely support that rating.  So won't bore you with subliminal content:

1. PUNCH CARD perks!
2. Location is convenient and easy to spot on the corner of S. Grand and Humphrey
3. Food fresh & cooked to order
4. Delicious vegan options even carnivores will love
5. Pleasant customer service

Those are the top five reason LuLu's gets 5 stars across the board in my book. But I'll go on...

-Portions are plentiful. 

-iPad on a swivel stand for expedited checkout. 

-Hippy spot, awesome music, clean restroom, good for groups or a casual date night.
 
-Inviting space with plenty of sunshine and openness to people watch on S. Grand 

-Patio is large as well.  

Other coolness includes a few of my favorite dishes; Black Bean Burrito (I sub the brown rice for quinoa), the Buffalo Cauliflower (AMAZING! you'll never want buffalo wings again), General Tso Bowl. They have hard plastic cups for the general public but I ask for my H2O in the chilled mason jar with ice balls.

You can also catch their Food Truck at one of the truck stop events.

As the Duchess of Layla it pains me to report that I am officially parting ways with them. The service today was so extremely, horrifically insulting and blatantly disrespectful. I've received shabby service in the past but honestly Layla doesn't employ the cream of the crop so I focus on my reason for coming...the hummus. 

Welp, I'll have to go elsewhere from now on. It was a gorgeous day so my mother and I decided to hit Layla's patio for (you guessed it) hummus. Half way there it started pouring so we ended up inside. There were 2 parties waiting ahead of us to be seated and the hostess/server glanced over it was too busy waiting tables to greet let alone seat anyone. We all looked confused after approximately 6 minutes which seems more like 30 when you're hungry. Anywho...finally seated we order 2 hummus plates immediately to avoid any further back & forth for the server. After 30-40 minutes I inquired about our order. The server responded in a very frustrated manner, "It'll be a while we're really behind". I respond, "Oh no worries we'll take the check, you can cancel the order". 

Tone changes to, "Let me go check on it". I'm thinking duh...that's what you should've done initially. She returns a few moments later with our hummus plates, slammed them on the table and started to walk away. I said, "Excuse me, are you upset"? Now a bit of a distance away she replied short & rudely, "No do you want this on one check"? 

While at the bar creating our ticket I notice the server talking to 2 co-workers and gesturing over to my table. I walked over, "I'll take the check please with to-go boxes you're making me very uncomfortable". One of the co-workers she was venting to came behind me as I walked back to the table to gather my things and introduced himself as the owner. He asked what the problem was. I acknowledged that the server was clearly multitasking and working very hard but once I inquired about the order her mannerism was completely unprofessional and downright nasty. He made excuse after excuse after excuse. From "Well she didn't know your order was almost ready" to "She has to tell me if there's an issue". I'm not a restaurant owner but servers shouldn't speak prematurely on an order they don't know the status of. Secondly, issues are to be discussed behind closed doors not in the presence of guests. Once he realized I was much more intelligent than he'd imagined, he too stormed off yelling, "Have a good day ladies"! 

You're mad too? Is all I could say before boxing my food and running out of this hellhole of a business. 

~Christy

Patty is a gem! I haven't had service so genuinely pleasant in a while. She was such a breath of fresh air and I appreciated it.

The place nice, large with plenty of seating both indoor as well as outdoor. The menu was amazing; so much I want to try yet so little time & appetite for just one visit. So I'll be back...

I like the open kitchen, how accompanying the cooks were and the mimosa was top notch! My veggie egg white omelet was huge, I had to take half to go.  I wasn't a fan of the buttermilk pancake so after 1 bite I swapped for the a slice of French toast and was pleased. 

Did I mention how delicious the mimosa was? 

The black coffee was exceptional but it all made sense when I glanced at the mug and it read "partnered with Kaldi's Coffee" my favorite coffee joint! 

I love this place...I'll be back for the shrimp & grits ASAP!

I have never been more eager to do a review update than now. The Preston has made Christy a believer *spirit fingers*. So I still think $48 brunch is ridiculously extravagant but I'd gladly fork over twice that amount for the dinner offered here. A brief synopsis before I dive into specifics:

*Food: Magnificent
*Service: Stellar
*Ambiance: Gorgeous 
*Cocktails: Impeccable 
*Overall dinner experience: Extraordinary 5/5  

Our server, Glenn (I really hope it's Glenn with 2 n's) was a spectacular server. Wanna know what made Glenn (with 2 n's) so spectacular? Well I'll tell you...his knowledge of the menu was extremely impressive, he had the ability to not only properly convey the ingredients in each dish but he was very detailed in creating a perfect visual of its presentation. I was a bit indecisive on both cocktails and dessert so I requested Glenn surprise me. He arrived with winners on both occasions. I could actually go on & on about how awesome Glenn was but it wouldn't be fair to The Preston lol. I just wanted to wrap him up in a doggie bag and take him home. 

Here's what you should order:

1. Octopus with house-made Gnocchi  
2. London Calling cocktail (ladies will love this)
3. Cheese Plate (varies)
4. Pretzel Croissants (you won't want to share)
5. Bronzino (a deliciously delicate white fish)
6. Chocolate Melt (real crowd pleaser) 
7. Mussels (Irresistible)

David, the manager was very hospitable. He came over to give a warm welcome and made several excellent selections for dinner. He described the menu items to perfection. Waiting for my dining partner to arrive I started with a cocktail. The London Calling was just what the doctor ordered; cute, light, citrusy refreshing & chilled. We shared and enjoyed every bite of dinner. The portions are more generous than tapas yet smaller than a course. I suggest picking several items and have a sampling of savory selections over cool cocktails, conversation and company. I did...

~Christy will be baaaacccck!

I regret to report...Big Sky was a Huge Flop. I've been anticipating a wonderful experience as I made special reservations for my family to celebrate Mother's Day here for brunch in the Garden area. We were one of several groups to arrive for the Sunday brunch dining experience. In short it was not at all crowded...yet we waited in excess of an hour for our meals to arrive and when they did they were all pretty much cold to the touch, lacking the look of freshness and no longer appetizing at all. 

The service was pleasant. She even apologized and advised us that the head chef was coming out to speak with us. Dominique came to the table with sincere apologies and stated there was a mix up in the kitchen that delayed our food and ultimately compromised its presentation & freshness. Although I appreciated his honestly I would've appreciated a heads up before the food arrived cold. Had this been the case we would've had the option to decline service and go elsewhere to enjoy Mother's Day brunch or won't for our orders to be remade. 

Needless to say we left Big Sky with stomachs growling, moods deflated and time wasted. Maybe I'll give them another try in the future. 

~Christy

There was hair in my food. I was more than halfway done with my delicious crab cakes when I noticed a dark piece of hair intertwined with my crab patty! 

I didn't overreact. I calmly placed the fork aside, shimmied the plate away from me & asked my dining companion to take a gander. She says, " Yeah Christy looks like a beard hair. You have to say something."

I called over the server and brought the hair to his attention. He immediately apologized, removed the plate and stated he'd have another prepared. I declined.

I really didn't feel safe eating anything else from the kitchen at this point. He returned a few moments later and asked if I'd like anything off the dessert menu. Again, I declined; as I'm sure it'd come from the same kitchen as the hairy crab cake. 

Well...it wasn't a total bust, the crab cakes, ambience, service and price point made for a great lunch. The crab cake was removed from the bill. 

FYI,
~Christy

Exposed brick

Beer on tap

Doughnuts 

Cold Brew Coffee

T-shirts stuffed inside mason jars, Jelly, Pickles & Jalapeños for retail

Oysters

Shrimp Rangoon 

BLT

Booth & bar seating 

Awesomely hip & helpful employees

...are just a handful of the extraordinary things District has to offer.

I couldn't help but try the Special Donut-la-mode which was a concoction consisting of a raised (unglazed) District donut sliced in half layered with lavender honey ice cream, graham cookie crumbled inside, the donut top replaced and drizzled with a mint sugar to form a donut ice sandwich supreme thingie! Taste so good I felt bad about it. I washed it down with their cold brew coffee and was ready for a nap. 

If you're in the Garden District or not; it's imperative that you make it by this spot before leaving NOLA. You'll thank me later.

~Christy

Not the greatest cupcakes you can get around town but definitely not the worst.

They do have a nice selection of cupcakes whenever you're feeling froggy or need a quick single for someone's birthday...that's usually when I'm here.

They even have candles at the register for your convenience.  It's nice to sit inside, maybe even a small group outing. Nice and quiet.  Wi-Fi accessible. Coffee available for you to enjoy after you finish your cake. 

Parking isn't the best so prepare to walk if the 3 spaces out front are occupied.  

I particularly like the look of The Cup, it's cute and the customer service is on par.

Kelly was the BEST server I've had in a very long time city wide! Awesome personality & service.  She wasn't pushy or overbearing yet consistent and prompt, it was actually the perfect balance for my sister and I (who can be easily annoyed lol)

This was our first visit to Wild Flower.  The occasion was to celebrate my sister's birthday.  We both decided on the salmon special which was absolutely delicious.  I was on a diet at the time and the chef prepared my meal just as I asked.  I always appreciate having my dieting needs accommodated. 

We both enjoyed the food, ambiance and service so much we decided to definitly return.

Decent service & food; great wine selections & ambiance. Tim was a pleasant server once we knocked the chill off. Upon entry the staff was extremely distant...preoccupied with whatever was needing their attention is the back room area took precedent over our arrival. I literally had to walk back & ask for service once seated. I didn't like that. It was drab, uncomfortable & dry. Although we were the only 2 guests for at least 40 min until others gathered in for after work drinks would've been nice to feel welcomed. 

Annabella is a pleasant red blend. 

Hummus was bland & pita luke warm. 

Vegetable soup & vegetable salad; both decent. 

Great Shaw Neighborhood location to meet up for a drink. Outdoor patio on warm weather days. Tighten up the service and this location will be awesome.  

~Christy

Great little tapas joint located in the heart of The Grove neighborhood. 

The décor is super caaaute! I really feel South American when I walk in and wanna cha cha all the way to my window seat. The outdoor patio is also a great option on a nice day/evening out. 

Anywho, the drinks are superb and very well made. The service is right on que and the food selections are delicious. 

It's tapas so try a little bit of this and a little bit of that to get more bang for your buck. 

Small restroom but it'll do for a quick lipstick check and face blot.

Hiro has been on my list for some time now so I decided while in the area I'd give Sunday Brunch a whirl.  It was decent...the menu options consisted of approximately 5 items (no exaggeration)

I went with the Chicken & Green Tea Waffle. The waffle was nice & thick and really did have a hint of green tea flavor along with its off-green color. I thought this was pretty cool. The chicken was flavorful, juicy and cooked to a crisp perfection. I requested all the topping on the side and didn't bother adding them to my dish because it was tasty just the way it arrived.

I also ordered a hot green tea which came in a cute little pot with fresh leaves steeping a delicious green tea.

The restrooms were nice & clean; located on the dimly lit lower level but bright enough to find your way without breaking a leg. 

There's a full bar equipped with flat screen tv for your entertainment purposes. The service was very pleasant. Although I definitely wouldn't return for brunch I can't wait to try Hiro's dinner menu ASAP! The space is super cute and I'm just feeling like I need to be there for cocktails & hot sake!

~Christy

I love it!

If I could, this would totally conclude my review.

Sump Coffee is just what I like; intimate, excellent coffee, with minimal yet dramatically chic décor. The A.B.E. (all black everything) effect speaks volume without saying a solitary word. Black walls (white stenciling), black drapes (drawn for a touch of sunshine), black uniforms, black matte coffee machine, black eco sleeve, black lids, black stools, black boards, black drops, black windowsill and black t-shirts for sale. There's plenty of seating and enough quietness to work in peace.

Lindsay, created the perfect Ethiopia pour-over. She's the sweetie pie you'll find focused on crafting brews at the bar. Pull up a stool and watch her work magic. The gentleman taking my initial drink order was a real charmer except I forgot his name (shame on me). Along with the coffee, ABE and superb service, I'm beyond excited to visit Sump again in the very near future.....like maybe tomorrow. 

~Christy

This location had to grow on me. I've always been a fan of the original Lafayette Square location but there was just something really "commercial" about this downtown junction. 

Today I finally realized I like it. Not so much for the assortment of goodies because the case is often borderline empty. It's the space that does it for me. I like the positive vibe it exudes. There are signs everywhere reminding you that you; yes you...are a good person! When you walk to the restroom the gender signs read "good person" not male or female. The full length mirror in the restroom reflects a message of "Good Person" and I freaking love that!!!! 

Yes, the coffee is good. The gooey butter cake is amazing (go to the Lafayette location for variety and availability) the seating is plentiful; offering both outdoor tables as well as leather sofa chairs inside. There's a message board to keep you in the know and guess what? They serve a delicious variety of hot teas. 

Park Ave is the place to be for coffee, tea and even a moral boost. 

~Christy

What happened??? Or have I outgrown cupcakes? 

Either way Jilly's offers super overpriced, nicely decorated, basic cupcakes.  There's nothing exclusive about the taste therefore leaving nothing to write home about in my opinion.  

Children may love the sugar rush. Curbside service available as well as indoor & outdoor seating.  

Purchased a dozen PRE-PACKED mini cupcakes for a celebration and the grand total was a whopping $27.

~Christy

Super friendly, pleasant & prompt service.  They had exactly what I needed to provide a delicious morning treat to my co-workers as a random act of kindness.  Needless to say the donuts were devoured. 

Packed in a cute little box. Priced appropriately. Variety of options along with beverages to wash the sugar rush away. 

Clean, COVID friendly.  Masks required upon entry and worn by employees.  

Ample parking in front.

Becka was a jewel, very sweet and took great care of us during lunch. Wasn't extremely busy so we were able to get seated & served right away. I ordered the lunch special 1/2 Fried Artichoke & Asparagus Salad & 1/2 Pear pizza minus the prosciutto of course....washed down with a glass of Prosecco. Everything was divine. 

My dining partner went with the basic Spaghetti & Meat Ball dish & cleaned the plate. I enjoyed the earthy ambiance, semi-open kitchen, spacious dining area & full bar.  There tons of outdoor seating so when the weather breaks I know exactly where I'll be hosting happy hour gatherings & summer brunch dates.

~Christy

No clue why I return.

Some lessons in life are simply inevitable; like Walmart Stores.  We all know how poorly staffed they are, how overcrowded the aisles are with stock crates that hinder our ease of movement, how strange the patrons are (not you and I, the other patrons lol) the parking lot sucks...yet we still return time after time.

Walmart is convenient, open late and with reasonably priced merchandise.

I'll be back but I shall proceed with caution.

Beautiful NOLA inspired restaurant with a seductive ambiance. Think dim lights, exposed brick, purple and gold bunting cloth, linen napkins, Fiji or sparkling water, open kitchen, 2-story dining with an elevator and perfect view of the French Quarter. 

If you're thinking this is bliss; you're absolutely correct! NOLA Restaurant was a delightful dinner experience with extremely pleasant service. I opted for the special salad of the evening which was a thinly sliced, sauteed eggplant stuffed with delicious mascarpone cheese and sweet red peppers, lightly drizzled olive oil, topped with fresh anchovies. This dish was served cold and mouthwatering is the best way to describe it. I highly enjoyed the mussels along with the BBQ shrimp. The portions were small so I was able to dibble and dabble without being stuffed. My dining partner ordered an lovely pasta dish. For dessert we decided on the brulee trio...to die for!!!!!! 

Do not leave NOLA without visiting NOLA. 
~Christy

Grab a window seat at Stanley and you'll have a bird's eye view of beautiful Jackson Square and Basilica St. Louis of France. Located in the heart of NOLA's French Quarter Stanley is a great place to grab breakfast. I waked in and was immediately greeted with southern hospitality; a huge smile, a vibrant "Good Morning" and told I could pick the seat of my choice. 

Needless to say I snagged a window seat for people watching purposes. My server was just as pleasant as my escort and extremely accommodating; as I am notorious for altering menus to fit my specific desires. She didn't flinch a bit and kept a smile. 

I ordered the Oyster Benedict without the hollandaise or English Muffin and added a pancake. The oysters were TO DIE FOR!!! Lightly battered and seasoned to perfection. The pancake was decent, nothing to rave about. I'd definitely recommend Stanley as a great way to start your day. 

~Christy

Psssst...Real quick, while I have a free 5 minutes to write, let me whisper something sweet in your ear.

On my way over to Fritanga I noticed really cool artwork protruding from Milque's front doorway. It basically called out, "Christy, please come in." 

So I obliged. The space is small & quaint with tons of charter. The exposed brick walls are beautiful and even more so the colorful, decorations from chalk to paintings. They get a lot done in the space they have to work with. 

My first visit and Amanda was a jewel! Super hospitable, very informative, a sweetie pie. I told her I loved coffee and she informed me that they offer Mississippi Mud's blend, which I enjoy. No-brainer! I'll take a coffee with a splash of almond milk please. Whoa...guess what we actually make our own cashew milk right here, how'd you like to try that? Whaaaat??? Amanda, don't mind if I do. 

It was light, a dash of sweet in my strong black coffee. If you like more sweet don't worry Milque makes their own syrups in house as well from vanilla to blueberry cardamon they'll flavor you right up. 

Oh, lest I forget, this is a toast bar. Like toast? Come here. Savory Mushroom (smoked right out back), Goat Cheese Toast. Sweet S'mores Toast for the kiddos. This place has something edible & fun for all ages. Who knows I may try a piece of toast one day but for sure I'll be back for a cup of that Mud.

~Christy

Decent restaurant but overpriced for sure. Best thing about Sqwires is their beautiful Lafayette Square location and the Banana Foster French Toast available during Sunday brunch only. They have a wide variety of wines, outside seating which is very nice during summer months and plenty of parking available on the shared lot. The lot is open to residents and several other businesses in close proximity so on gorgeous days it can fill up fast. Fret not, there's street parking and other small lots close enough to park and walk a bit. If you're in the area stop in, the building alone is worth seeing. The service and food aren't necessarily wow factors. 

~Christy

Came in for the first time yesterday super excited about trying the extraordinary items other Yelpers had raved about. 

I decided on House Wings and Sweet Fries which were superb! The wings were nice and crispy, the sauce was very tasty & the fries OMGJUST HEAVENLY.

I enjoyed my experience so much that I returned the following day with a guest extremely excited to share the experience & great food. 

Then BOOM!!!!! I asked for egg whites and got a flat out "NO" then my guest asked for hash browns on the side instead of on top and got "Our kitchen is pretty picky so they probably won't do that." I asked if my pancakes could be cooked in Pam instead of butter and got "Sorry, no." Complete turnoff...I won't be retuning. 

The lack of accommodation was totally disappointing and unreasonable.

Vegetarians can have a great meal here. I loved the veggie tacos on a corn tortilla with grilled peppers, red onion, sweet potato & fresh avocado. Black beans were flavorful & complimented the tacos well. I came with an appetite and ravished the complimentary chips & salsa dip.

Todd's service was exquisite and Margaritas were a real winner! The space was group friendly with booths, table tops & full bar. Plenty of parking for your convenience. Sarah S. rarely disappoints; glad this location made the ISC cut before closing.  

~Christy

Upscale bar/restaurant with an adjoining elegant dining area. The establishment is large, has a full bar equipped with TV's and fresh oysters clearly on display for you to witness the art of shucking.

Daily Chef Specials are available Monday-Friday. I visited on a Monday and therefore went with the Honey Tabasco Chicken special. However, I started with a cup of Crawfish Bisque soup; a delicious choice to get my palate fired up for the main course. The Honey Tabasco Chicken was the perfect combination of sweet & spicy atop a succulent lightly battered chicken breast, accompanied by red beans and rice, putting a southern twist on a classic dish. I enjoyed it immensely but could only eat a small portion. My eyes are always bigger than my tummy. Jackson, my server, was a real gent & wrapped the remains for me. 

Lüke is a perfect NOLA spot for date night, business meetings and hour happy.

~Christy

Literally a walk-in walk-up coffee shop. So tiny I can't even call it a coffee housekeeper café; it's the size of a large closet. 

Super duper service.

Super delicious Cortado (mix between a macchiato & cappuccino).

4 Super cool barstools.

Super tiny handwritten wall hangings.

Super radioactive music.

No food, no restroom, no frills... grab your espresso & jet. All of Bourbon Street is waiting for you just around the corner. 

~Christy

I personally found the green interior to be refreshing upon entry. Hostess stand is immediately adjacent the front door so you're greeted without delay. 

The showcase window allows you the spectate as the noodle maker crafts your noodles by hand using rolls & flips, spins & slams before tossing the dough string la into huge boiling pot of water. Pretty cool to watch him work. 

I ordered the stir fry hand pulled vegetable noodle dish. Delicious, light but filling. What I like most is the absence of high sodium saucy stuff. What I like least is the amount of vegetables. I actually had to request additional veggies. For this to be titled "vegetable stir fry" it lacked vegetables. 

The red bean sesame balls are award winning. BIG so share or get a doggy bag to warm up at home later. But you need them in your life for sure. 

Lastly they offer a variety of boba tea drinks. I opted not to try because they're all made with whole or condensed milk. No almond, coconut or soy options. I suggested they level up. 

This is my go-to noodle joint. 

~Christy

Its a cool spot to hook-up for groups and happy hour.  It's space and hopping, plenty of tv's, draft at your disposal and the food is decent.  

Lately though I haven't been too impressed with my food.  The wings were mediocre and so were the sweet potato fries.  I had zero complaints about my Merlot.  

The salads are delicious, especially the poached pear.  The turkey burger arrived with a cool "Circle 7" branded into the bun; nice touch.  

Parking can be a real hassle so wear your walking shoes or have your driver let you out at the door.

Totally neglected this wonderful review! Came here for an ISC evening out and absolutely loved the place. We ordered several dishes to share but I went with the Shrimp Tom Yum Noodle Soup....EXCELLENT choice if I must say so myself. It was a heaping amount of succulent shrimp, rice noodles, fish ball, fresh bay leaves and flavor bursting additives. The spring rolls and fried corn fritter thingies were also pretty mouthwatering.

The ladies serving us were very pleasant and attentive. I couldn't finish my Tom Yum so the young lady kindly packaged it to-go and turned my plain ole brown paper bag into a beautiful swan. I appreciated that.

Thai Country Cafe is located in the Loop just west of Shell gas station and east of Mission Taco. Give it a whirl.

~Christy

Gabby was a stellar server!  She handled our ISC party of 12 like a champ; drinks stayed replenished, orders taken and delivered with ease and her bubbly personality made for an outstanding first dining experience at Anthonino's.

Now on to the food...

Garlic Chicken Pizza was deliciously "garlicy" so if you are a garlic lover, you'll really enjoy this.  The hand tossed crust was a perfect mix of thick and thin (if that makes sense).  It wasn't Pizza Hut thick but it also wasn't Imo's thin.  Never mind.

Nero Pasta with Squid was superb!  I only had a bite of Mel's dish but I found it entertaining how the squid played hide & seek amongst the black pasta noodles.  I felt like I needed more but who wants to be the mooch of the group.

STL Tosated Rav...GET IT!  I simply don't have the words to explain how amazing they are.

Calamari....GET IT!  Self-explanatory.

Yogurt & Pita was delicate and tasty.

The dining room was large, open and well lit.  The ladies room was clean and properly equipped with a shiny full-length mirror guuuurrrrrls!

I'll be back to tackle that Goat Cheese Pizza.  

P.S. Parking was  doozie, be prepared to walk.

I like Texas Road House because I can order off the menu and have my food prpared just as I would if I were at home.  I'm picky and demanding when it comes to what I eat so I need the freedom to order according to my diet.  TRH cooks my chicken breast and broccoli to perfection.  The rolls are sinfully delicious (don't judge me I only take a teeny weeny corner) so soft and warm and melt in your mouth like butter.

The best part about TRH are the nuts (no pun intended) lol...

Latin tapas restaurant located in the beautiful and eclectic Garden District. This cute little spot is spacious enough inside to accommodate a small crowd as well as outdoor seating for those who prefer to catch a few rays. 

Being a tapas restaurant the portions are small however; the dishes pack a mean flavor punch! Tapas is just never enough food for me so I go with the intentions of snacking not complete satiety.

I started with the succulent Crab Cake accompanied by a delicious Beet Salad...I wanted a second order it was so divine. I decided to try the Salmon Ceviche served with addictive crisply tortilla chips. I enjoyed the magnificent food and friendly service. 

~Christy

2 stars for being open to serve curbside during COVID-19. Walk up or call-in service available during quarantine. This is a trying time for many many service workers (myself included) Having food available is appreciated when there is no time or opportunity in the work day to do it yourself in the comfort of your home.  

-2 stars for the unnecessarily hostile, nasty attitude I received from Andrew after returning with an incorrect order.  I've been a patron of Pickleman's for many years and service is usually just fine.  However; this does not mean I will condone unreasonable treatment.  I sent coworkers who were already returning to Pickleman's for an item left out of their original order to pick up my Veggie sandwich. I was very specific about what I wanted on my sandwich. 

Whether it be the fault of my coworker or Pickleman's the sandwich included mayo (which I do not consume). I returned for what would have been a 3rd time trip for my coworkers.  I kindly explained the issue & asked if I could please get another Veggie sandwich without mayo. 

Andrew gave so much heat! Wanting to argue about who was at fault, how the sandwich normally comes, I need to be more specific, what he heard vs. what was said, who paid...so on so on blah blah blah. I watched him in agitation then politely asked that he either give me a gift card of refund my coworker because I didn't feel like it was a good day for me to order and would try again another day. 

A refund was given. 

Needless to say I'll never darken the doorstep of Pickleman's again. Service this poor is never permissible. I don't have the time, interest or energy to fight over mayo. 

~Christy

Pretty good Veggie Pad Thai for the take-out. Fresh vegetables & tasty sauce came in a plentiful recyclable container. Also optes to try half order of vegetable egg rolls which came 2 to an order with sweet & sour sauce. Service was prompt & pleasant.  Located in a South County strip mall parking isn't an issue. Dining tables inside but no outdoor seating available. I'd visit again.  

~Christy

Overall, I enjoyed Mango. I had to marinate on this for a while because my feelings were rattled by a few things during the experience...I realized I was being petty and it shouldn't be reflected in this review. 

Anywho, our server was very nice (slow but nice) (forgetful but nice.) She made great recommendations and had a pleasant personality. The new space is gorgeous. Located on Washington across from Prime 1000 now; so do not go to the old building expecting to get in. Parking is hit or miss however there's a lot in the rear or meters along the front and side streets. I went on a weekday and valet was not available. Spacious with plenty of room to spread out. There is a private area for groups wanting a little more exclusivity. 

I enjoyed the plantains tremendously and the Grouper Ceviche was superb. The mussels were decent; much too tiny and not as plump & juicy as I would have liked. I wouldn't go back with the intentions of ordering the mussels again for sure. I also tried the Parmesan Truffle Polenta which was mouthwatering delicious. Oh! Almost forgot about the Mango Sorbet with Quinoa..don't leave without it. 

Thank me later,
~Christy

Southern hospitality from the door. More notably, it was held open for me by a gentleman employee. He also greeted me kindly & handed me a menu. Once I advised him I was vegetarian he went on to detail their vegetarian options and special Pumpkin soup of the day. 

The Heirloom salad was spectacular. Aside from colorful; it was very fresh, flavorful and the greens were delicate like butter. I left off the farmers cheese but appreciated the chopped chives. 

Heirloom tomato salad
Cup of pumpkin soup 
Banana puddin' (hidden cookie on the bottom, caramelized topping was so good it made me wanna slap my mama (twice). 


Grand total: $18. 73

Although this was a $14 experience at best due to portion size I enjoyed my meal & service therefore the overcharge didn't sting as bad. I do want them to offer more vegetarian dishes in the futurw to assure I have an encoré experience. 

Thanks in advance,
~Christy

There was a slight wait 15-25 minutes, which is typical for a Saturday afternoon at this Kirkwood location. However, if you're left with this dilemma, I highly suggest patiently waiting...it's totally worth it and plenty of coolness to explore in close proximity to pass the time. 

Jeff was a great server; personable, prompt and accommodating. We started with a glass of delicious red wine proceeded by a delcious fall salad (spring mix greens, figs, boursin cheese and candied pecans) I stuck with my usual Billy Goat while one of my dining guest opted for something a little "meatier".

The atmosphere is decent; with a full bar, enclosed view of the pizza kitchen where you'll see the cooks handtossing, spinning and twirling dough and well lit natural lighting from the windows along Kirkwood Road. I already have a favorite Dewey's location but I'm definitely a fan of this one as well.

~Christy

The customer service is RAW, hardcore friendliness (I know hardcore sounds rough) but that's exactly what I intend to deliver. It's nice-sty service.  The employees don't put on a nice act or pretend to be hospitable.  They'll say hi, grab your order and answer questions if you should have any.

The oatmeal is pretty good as are the lattes.  I enjoy Becky's Bitchin' Brew.  They have homemade vegan brownies and chocolate chip cookies to die for.

There's free Wi-Fi indoors, upstairs and outdoors.

They're open later than most cafe's at midnight and won't rush you out.  

Sunday brunch is available, although I've never indulged personally.

What an amazingly warm family owned establishment. Everyone from servers to Mr. Bartolino himself works to make your experience magnificent. 

My party was greeted with a smile & immediately seated by Mr. Bartolino. Shortly after Mary, our server came over with more pleasantries as well as daily specials and recommendations.

We all tried & LOVED to Carrot Soup of the day. It was the perfect amount of sweet and savory, yet light and tasty cup of deliciousness. I followed up with the Sole. Also a winner! My fish was prepared to perfection just as I'd requested. Broiled, a touch of olive oil & garlic accompanied by large broccoli florets. Needless to say I cleaned my plate. 

The restaurant is spacious, well kept, perfect for intimate crowds or larger parties. Although the lot is shared with a hotel, parking is not a problem as Bartolino's has designated spots and valet for your convenience. Definitely won't be my last visit. I'll be back sooner than later actually. 

~Christy

Down home NOLA restaurant with local flavor you can't deny. The place is small with lots of seating to maximize clientele. Pretty much setup for a grab & go or dine-in at your own risk experience. 

Arrived right before noon on a Sunday and only had about a 5 min wait but the dining room was packed with guests (on top of guests). During that time I had an opportunity to give Lil' Dizzy's a quick once-over. I noticed the owner (a short, handsome, well groomed older gentlemen) greet customers entering, thank customers leaving, shout orders to get staff moving, buss tables, grab menus, run food....this man wore many hats; I was impressed. Wasn't long before we grabbed a tiny table close to the door, I took my napkins to wipe the access water from the wet wash cloth used to clean our table before sitting. Lil' Dizzy observed this and thanked me for helping him. 

There was a brunch buffet happening that seemed to be a fan fav. Everything on the menu & additional options were also served in the $17.99 buffet, however it was too much food for me. I opted for the Shrimp & Grits (no cheese) and my dining guest went with the French Toast & Bacon which she LOVED! 

My Shrimp & Grits arrived with a glob of American cheese which saddened me. The server apologized and asked if this was OK. Due to the state of emergency (hangry) I took the order as-is, ate around the cheese and was able to actually enjoy it. 

In a nutshell: 
Service was a little slow & staggered. The facility was old with lots of character. The food was good. Lil' Dizzy himself was amazing. 

~Christy

You simply can not leave NOLA without visiting Sucré, PERIOD! This little French Quarter café is the most lovely, delicate, delicious shop I've ever patronized. Sure the offerings are all very tantalizing but what makes Sucré extraordinary is the amazingly pleasant and patient customer service. This was my first visit and the young lady assisting spent her sweet time making sure I got everything my heart desired. Anything I was uncertain about she either described in great detail or offered a sample. 

I decided on an assortment of macaroons to go while I nurtured a tiny dish of gelato & black coffee in the adorable dining room. The space is immaculate. Very simple, clean design with pastel pink, gold detailing, small tables and get this....DOILIES! (I'm a sucker for doilies) It just adds to the all around elegance of Sucrè. 

Find the nearest location and go...now! 
~Christy

Cafe on steroids. Companion doubles as a full cafe & school for soon-to-be Baker's. Lovely location, super spacious for those dining in or outdoors with tables galore. But what's most extraordinary about the place is watching the team of students work from the open-view glasses teaching area. You can literally see individuals stirring, kneading, folding, tossing dough. Aprons filled with flour and your lunch literally being made with T.L.C. right before tour very eyes. 

Onward, I stopped in because I wanted to give the place a once over & grab a croissant to go. I've got a thing for comparing croissants all of a sudden. Well, the croissant was decent; I wanted it to be more flaky on the outside & dense on the inside...but this isn't about me.

Highly suggest Companion for those looking to host a lunch meeting, mid-day date or if time is limited; grab a pastry, coffee, t-shirt and roll out. 

There's plenty of Companion paraphernalia to choose from: apparel, Mugs, sauces, dressing, baguettes, granola, soup, soft drinks, YOU NAME IT. 

Service was fast & friendly. I got plenty of camera ready smiles as I snapped away. 

~Christy

The current 5 star raving reviews are pushing it lol...

A little quick perspective: Medina is decent Mediterranean on the go however, seating is available.  The cooler-stored pre-prepped hummus, gyro, salads & wraps just remind me of fast food. When I think Mediterranean I don't want to think fast food...seems like an anomaly. Nice and clean, colorful décor, pleasant service, convenient corner location in the heart of downtown and OPER is accepted. Lastly, I enjoyed the hummus and warm pita. 

In summary, I'd probably go back but my socks definitely were not knocked off. 3 solid stars on the Christy Scale. 

~Christy

Donna was a jewel; personable, spunky & very knowable of the menu. She made great recommendations that I had the opportunity to enjoy amongst fellow Yelpers during ISC dinner. 

Guido's was a nice choice on the Hill. The space was warm & cozy yet open & inviting. Plenty of seating, a full bar, private dining areas for groups; even intimate arrangements for couples. 

The Mussels were succulent and delicious. The Spanish. Cheese tray was also delicious. A mix of goat, manchego & a blue cheese paired with olives for savory and apricots for sweetness. 

The menu at Guido's offers both Italian and Spanish tapas; very unique approach to dining. I approve.

~Christy

A year has gone by and yes Fiddlehead Fern is still my favorite cafe.

It's really very simple: staff is superb; personable, pleasant & passionate.  Food is delicious; made with freshest ingredients and lovely presentation. Space is serene; live band on Sunday's, crisp white, wood, greenery throughout is inviting & peaceful. They offer a variety of hearty toast, salads, soup, pastries, coffee, teas, sparkling wine. Such a wondedul addition to have within walking distance to Botanical Garden. 

~Christy

The Handle Bar is literally an art museum/bar/restaurant/pool hall/haberdashery of cool! 

Ever sat in a pew? Like patio seating? Are you a dance maniac? How about ahhhhmazingly delicious food, crazy cool bartenders & servers? Play pool? Ride bicycles? Enjoy good music? How about vibrant art? If you answered "Yessss" to any of these questions, I highly suggest you run over to the Handlebar.  Located in The Grove neighborhood and within walking distance to so much awesomeness it'll make your head spin. However, Handlebar will leave you dizzy enough. 

Oh, before I forget to actually review my experience let me say the Roasted Brussels topped with goat cheese were very good, a little salty so if your sensitive to sodium dully note. The Russian Salmon flatbread was award-winning tasty too. 

I'll be back to handle this bar ASAP!
~Christy

I'm particular and I'm always cautious at places I don't usually frequent because I hate to make the staff uncomfortable with my demands but the waitress was completely unbothered with my order today.  I must say I was impressed....

My order came out EXACTLY as I requested and was served with a smile.  The egg whites and pancake were absolutely delicious.  Even the water with no ice was tantalizing; I think I was just in an "easily pleased" mood today.

Hammerstone's has a new fan.  Great service, great food, great outdoor seating for my people watching and sun bathing purposes and located in the heart of Soulard.  What more can you ask for.

Lovely ambiance & delicious menu selections for the non-carnivore.  Perfect for lunch, date night, dinner meetings and weekend brunch.  Thoroughly enjoyed the Brussels sprouts salad...flash fried to perfection and paired with pistachios, thinly sliced goat cheese & herbs. The risotto dish was amazing. I enjoyed the mushroom combination as well as the filling portion size. 

Cocktails, wine and beverages available. Window, dining room & bar seating. I opted for window to people watch along busy South Grand. Beware: parking can be a doozie. Tree House really is a great spot for any type of eater.

I know there's a lot of good pizza to choose from here in St. Louis and depending on the type of pizza you prefer you may even disagree with the following statement I am about to make but here goes nothing....

"DEWEY'S IS THE BEST PIZZA IN TOWN"

The crust is as soft as a baby's bottom, the Green Lantern and the Billy Goat are perfected with the topping of goat cheese (my favorite cheese in the whole wide world) and the service is consistently consistent.

This is the newest location and I like it because they have outdoor seating unlike the other's.  Wait...the seating could belong to Five Guys with is right next door.  Nonetheless, I sat there and enjoyed my pizza.  I say they should share the patio furniture and everyone'll be happy.

100% Vegetarian = WINNING

I dropped in for lunch and to my surprise there was a special All VEGAN BUFFET taking place (**Bankhead Bounce**)

Pleasantly greet upon entry and seated without delay. Buffet items were fresh, flavorful and VEGAN. Ranged from masala to fruit, soups, grits, beans, cabbage, roasted vegetables, naan of course and much more.  Small price to pay for $12

Spacious, clean, libations available as well as student discounts and Grub Hub.

It's taken me years to get by for lunch. Better late than not at all right....I'm a big fan now.

~Christy

Saturday Happy Hour, I struted right in for open hightop seating in the bar area. Lovely interior and rustic decor was quite inviting. Perfect ambiance for a group get-together, meeting, date or solo outing. 

Lydia, our server was very pleasant and made great recommendations to suit my vegetarian diet although Juniper is pretty much carnivorous. 

Happy hour limited menu until 5pm. We ordered a variety of fresh oysters to hold us over...light & tasty. Upon dinner time we were anxious to order. My dining companion ordered the baked chicken main course & added a fried leg on the side. The verdict revealed both were delicious & well seasoned. I opted for the mushroom main course paired with a pumpkin puree (risotto style) dish. I LOVED IT! Perfect pairing & pleasing to my taste buds. 

Cocktails were decent but honestly I was not impressed by either the Paloma nor the Sazerac. Next time I'll likely stick to wine. Cheers to this $150 weekend happy hour. 

~Christy

The décor was earthy, plenty of indoor tables for dining, bar seating & outdoor bench for waiting line guests. There were plenty seats & no one waiting however my party of 2 were told it'd be a 15 minute wait. 

*Scratch that* 

We'll opt for the open bar sir. "Sorry it's not available."

*Why are they making this so hard*

How about ordering to go? "Ok, head over to the bar."

So.....we retreated to the bar for a fresh green juice (Super 8 to be exact) & Lemonade. Our juice-tender was helpful & efficient. We were served in no time flat with 2 refreshing drinks for a whopping total of $17!

I nearly choked on my Super 8 when he mumbled my total. Good lawwwwwd what did I order again? That was rhetorical but he repeated the grand total in all seriousness. 

The drinks were mediocre at best. Paired with the hefty price & blasé host I was disappointed overall. I don't mind paying for whatever it is that I order however; it's gotta make sense. 

I'm stumped. 

~Christy 

.

A joyous experience...the food and service just made me all warm & fuzzy inside. This Webster Groves wine bar/restaurant has done the neighborhood wonders! I'll get straight to the point so you all can justify scurrying over in a heartbeat...

Service:

*Hostess was adorable 
*Kyle (our server) was simply awesome
*Bus Gentleman was prompt & pleasant
*Mark (proprietor) very hospitable & welcoming

Food/Cocktails:

*Cous Cous & Shrimp - Mouthwatering delicious cold dish
*Caesar Salad - Had one you've had 'em all
*Catfish - Lightly battered, pan seared, flavorful; I heard it was very good
*Bronzino - Whole delicate white fish cooked to absolute perfection!!!!!!
*Cauliflower & veggies - Standard
*Butterscotch pot de creme - Superb, just the right amount of sweet
*#94 - Cute, tasty, mild (I had 3 and felt totally sober) 
*Jack & Coke - Standard
*Presentation was extraordinary - Indicative of an excellent chef 

Décor:

*Gorgeous 
*Lots of mirrors 
*Bay doors (Captures an amazing breeze)
*Multiple seating options
*Semi-open kitchen
*Coat check area 
*1 TV (Less is more)
*Immaculate restroom (The wall paper was the work of a great decorator)

Nutshell:

Olive + Oak is perfect for dinner celebrations, date night, happy hour cocktails; there were even guests dining with children. Clearly it's an establishment for all. I'll be going back very soon. 

~Christy

Not a P.F. fan at all but since my little sister wanted her birthday dinner here; I obliged.  

The menu is not my cup of tea at all; I mean nothing here is actually an authentic Chinese meal.  It's more-so a fast food chain restaurant with much more space and a chic ambiance to attract a certain crowd.

Anyway, I broke down and got a mini order of the crab wontons just so I wasn't sitting awkwardly as everyone ate their mediocre looking entrees.  The wontons were tiny, filled with a teaspoon amount of crab type cream cheese dip substance, wrapped in a wonton and deep fried.  It was garnished with a sweet and sour sauce.  They were pretty good and all I needed to pass the time,

I didn't order dessert but what I saw on the menu were all of 2 options total.  They were ordered by other guests at my table and arrived looking really small, friend and pathetic.

The waiter seemed a little testy and overwhelmed by the crowd but said he was doing his best with the 5 tables he had going.  

The experience reminded me why I do not like P.F. Chang's.

Lunch was a delight and so was my server (who's name I can't remember) this is why I shouldn't leave my drafts unfinished for more than 24 hours.

I digress, located in the beautiful Lafayette Sq. Neighborhood, Polite Society fits right in. Upon entry you'll be swept away by the gorgeous well-stocked bar. Making your way through the dining areas the exposed brick, filament lighting & rustic design are quite captivating. Lots of character here making it a great date night, lunch meeting spot. 

The food was plentiful & delicious as well. I enjoyed the mushrooms (although heavily battered) I simply peeled away the crust and devoured the core of my meal. Their beet salad was a great pairing item. 

Loved lunch but can't wait to return for an evening happy hour outing. 

~Christy

I had the pleasure of experiencing Apollonia's during an ISC event. Let me preface by saying 
aside from hummus I am usually not a Greek food eater however, I must say, I enjoyed Apollonia's tremendously. 

It could've been the ambiance which was quaint yet inviting, a full bar decorated for the holiday season's cheer, the immaculate restroom, delicious food, splendid service or the absolutely amazing group of Yelper's surrounding me! 

Whatever the reason I am now a fan of a new Greek dish, Shrimp Saganaki. Saganaki consisted of succulent grilled shrimp over a bed of sautéed vegetables in a white wine & tomato sauce topped with premium feta cheese and served with soft, warm, light pita bread (did you get all that). Ummm ummm ummm! This $8.50 dish was pretty priceless in my book.

The hummus was authentic; I could taste my beloved chickpeas in every bite. The texture was light and delicate. The warm pita made this an astonishing starter dish.  

Apollonia's, you have a new fan.

~Christy

Lovely little Kirkwood diner! Reminds me of Eat-Rite, Courtesy or Mel's...except bigger, charming & cleaner (no shade). The girls are super adorable, very pleasant & great cooks. I enjoyed a blueberry pancake, a cup of black Joe and a glass of fresh tap (no ice)....all of which were good.

I enjoyed the feel of this diner. Red, white, black & chrome décor, comfortable booth seating along with bar stools on the swivel. Cool crayola art hanging over the oven hood, mirrors, t-shirts and gum balls really bring out the nostalgia in this place. I like it for a greasy spoon upgrade type of dining experience.

~Christy

I was in the mood for Thai and my friend wanted Chinese;  what were the chances we'd find both in a one stop shop????  Well we did, right here at Pho Manchester and we loved ever bite!  

The service was very friendly.  We were greeted with a warm smile and "hello" immediately upon entering.   Our server was an adorable young lady well versed in the menu.  She was attentive and prompt.  

The food arrived piping hot shortly after placing our orders.  Presentation was pretty, and the serving sizes plentiful.  I got a total of 3 meals out of my Chicken Pad Thai and my guest 2 servings of his Chicken Fried Rice.  Our meals were extremely fresh; the vegetables were colorful and delicious.  There was no greasy/oily residue or taste.  The Crab Rangoon were an amazing starter.

I appreciated the linen napkins and precise table settings.  It made my dining experience feel like more than the typical Chinese grab & go restaurants I'm use to.

I'll definitely be back to try more dishes; I'm especially looking forward to the Pho.

Think Pastaria but mid-grade. Porano Pasta is awesome!!! I wasn't super excited to try them because I'm generally not into pasta.  Decided to take one for the team while dining with a colleague and what a pleasant surprise. 

Porano's interior resembles Pastaria almost to a T.  Where are you spacious, beautiful wall murals throughout the dining area, woodwork, filament lighting, semi-open kitchen, amazingly fresh ingredients and cold treats on display. There are two levels for your dining pleasure and a wide open section with killer view of Washington Ave. on the first level next to the entrance. 

Ordering is pretty simple: pick a pasta (Gluten Free available), pick a sauce, pick a protein, pick 2 toppings and violà!

I crafted a delicious concoction consisting of noodles, pesto, roasted Brussels, sweet peppers and carrots. My finding partner chose something more carnivorous and was very pleased as well. 

Had I neem in a dessert mood I would've loved to have tried one of those tantalizing chocolate pops...maybe next time.

~Christy

I love the ambiance here. It may seem a little dark to some but it's just the right "dim" for me. It's located in the plaza next to Hot Shots. 

The sushi is delicious; a bit slow at times but delicious.

The bar seating is super tight so I'd suggest choking a table unless you're solo.  There's also a private dining area for groups and privacy. 
l

Jason was a gem. I was welcomed with a smile behind his mask of course  

Seated outdoors without hesitation and pleasantly served. I enjoyed sort of an a'la carte dish which included scrambled egg whites, sautéed spinach & half stack of semolina pancakes. Washed down with a delicious aperol/cava/OJ. 

Reasonably priced, tasty, friendly midtown eatery with outdoor seating = winning. 

~Christy

Erica was our precious sever. Very pleasant & accomdating. 

We enjoyed an array of tacos. Personally I devoured the Portobello sans sauce for the perfect vegetarian option. My companion left no evidence of the Baha & Fried Chicken tacos (murdered'em). 

Presentation was lovely as well as overall decor. It's a pretty happening, vibrant, spacious place to have a drink, watch a game, take a date or just a load off solo. 

The classic margherita was decent; I had to request an additional shot (don't judge me).

~Christy

Usually not much of a Latin food eater but today I was feeling saucy! I decided on Fritanga because it's been in my radar for yeeeeears; as I use to live just a block over in the McKinley Heights Neighborhood.

Zucchini Empanadas 
White Rice & Black Beans 
Maduros
Lime Margarita

TV above the door, fiery red walls, ceiling fans on light rotation, Latin music in the background, beautiful Pop Art all over the place. I wanted to take every single piece home with me. 

Service was A1, award winning, 5.0 on the Christy Scale & definitely something to write home about. 

This Latin haven blew me away with their delicious food & drink: Amazing Maduros, black beans & white rice, zucchini Empanadas, Lime margarita. Everything was literally amazing. The awesome service matched the art filled, flavorfully decorated restaurant. Red walls, extraordinary murals, Latin music in the background, personable service, all made me feel like I was on a Nicaraguan getaway.

I'll be back on a regular. 
~Christy

I like The Shaved Duck, I really do. The food is delicious, the space is nice, but the service needs some serious attention. I won't name drop because I think the young lady may have been having a bad day or she was simply ready for her shift to end. I arrived around 3:10pm to grab some late lunch...specifically the Shrimp & Grits. Once I walked in the young lady stood behind the bar and said nothing. We made eye contact for a few seconds in silence (which made it feel like a 30 second stare-down lol.) Finally she says take a seat whenever you like. I obliged.

She dropped off a glass of iced water and walked away so fast I didn't have a chance to tell her I hate ice in my water. Anywho, when she finally returned I asked if I could order the Shrimp & Grits...she said, "That's after 5pm" 

Welp, moving on...I ordered the House Salad & Crab Cakes instead. I sat for what felt like 30+ minutes unattended. She totally disappeared, never to be seen or heard from again. I got up to leave and saw a gentlemen walking in my direction with food so I sat back down as not to be rude and leave my order uneaten. 

Again, no one ever came by to make sure my order was satisfactory, if I needed more water or needed anything additional. I waited and waited for someone to come by with the check; I was clearly finished. A different gentleman came by to grab my dishes.

Waiting....waiting.....waiting.... I got up to find someone! ANYONE! to settle my check. At this point I just wanted to get out of here. I spotted to gentleman who picked up my dishes and asked if I could please have someone check me out, he politely said yes. 

The same guy who dropped my food off returned to the table and sat the check down. Ummm sir, I'm over here....standing at the bar....

After this experience I highly doubt I'll be returning to the Duck, much less recommending it to others. 

~Christy

Houlihan's is a decent spot to grab group drinks and happy hour apps....that's totally it. I've never been ecstatic about the place but they've managed to be consistently mediocre over the years; hence the 3 star rating. The employees are usually pretty nice and make a solid effort to show a little personality with service, I appreciate that. I always love an establishment that greets you at the door and Houlihan's has that covered. Plenty of seating for large parties, TV's and a full bar. 

Food: Stuffed Mushrooms, Calamari, Goat Cheese Stuffed Artichokes, Ahi Tuna. As I said hit the apps and roll out. 

Drinks: The house Cabernet has a nice, slightly sweet touch; I suggest a bottle over glass. Malbec is tasty as well; a bit dryer than the house. Merlot is always a GO! 

Enjoy,
~Christy

Great first experience! Seated for happy hour in a nice dimly lit booth table in the bar area. Service was prompt & friendly. 

I enjoyed the grilled artichoke & $5 Prosseco. My friend loved the chicken wings. Warm towels served for hand cleansing after meal...nice touch. 

Located at the Clayton entrance on Plaza Frontenac. There's outside seating during pleasant weather months & cozy options in the brutal cold. Plenty of parking on the open lot. Definitely a new happy hour spot.

~Christy

Tracy was a real trooper today! She pretty much reinforced my 5 star update.

I tried at least 6 flavored and asked a sum of about 8 questions and Tracy didn't blink twice, snarl once or quit.

Let me say this "YOU CANT LOSE NO MATTER WHAT YOU CHOOSE."

I couldn't pass up the Coconut Chocolate Fudge (don't get disappointed if it's not as "coconutty" as you may imagine) the coconut is purely from the coconut milk used and not actual coconut flakes; so it's not potent. It's soooooo good though. 

The Lemongrass was infused to perfection and paired well with my Chocolate and Manchego Honey flavors. 

Lastly, Yelp was kind enough to extend a hand with 1 free topping. I took advantage of the Salted Pecans. Couldn't have topped my creams off any better but next time I'm trying the Pistachios.

2.5/5

Severely mediocre Mediterranean. Located in Lafayette Shopping Center just a few doors down from Dierberg's. The place is spacious enough to accommodate small and large groups but not sure there's enough staff to make any group experience go off without a hitch. I was 1 of 2 tables and it took a little longer than anticipated to get my simple order. Although, the young lady serving was very nice she was often M.I.A. 

The hummus was decent, the baba was on garlic overload and the grape leaves were just OK. Nothing knocked my socks off so I definitely won't be back for a second visit. The most disappointing thing about my visit was the luke-warm pita bread I had to keep asking for after 2 bites of hummus because I refuse to eat cold/crispy pita. 

The décor screams Middle East, there is outside seating and a TV that displays a repetitive slide show. 

~Christy reporting live, 2/100

The best southern hospitality I've experienced in a very long time. Walking through the door was a breath of fresh air. I was immediately greeted by Kerry; the sweetest lady server with the cutest New Zealand accent. 

The place is quaint; filled with plenty of tables, jazz photos, mirrors and instruments hanging to adorn the walls. There is an open kitchen, colorful chalked menu boards, and enough staff to make this restaurant flow like an assembly line. 

I opted for the Banana Pancakes (short stack) which consisted of 2 large cakes in my opinion because I could only eat 1 before I threw in the towel. Let me just say this was the BEST damned pancake I've had in my life!!!! Super superb!!! Buttermilk so smooth, fluffy, moist & tasty you would definitely slap ya mama. I washed it down with a Mango Mimosa & Black Coffee; both of which were also pretty splendid.

Day #2, because one visit to Café Fleur De Lis was not enough, I ordered another banana pancake along with a blueberry pancake (both heavenly). This little NOLA nook has been a true highlight. You MUST experience it for yourself. 

Thank me later. 

~Christy

I wanted to slurp from the bowl!

The only thought that saved me was NOT wanting to look too desperate. 

Nudo is Ramen done right! Loved that I had an option to order a vegan dish (shroomed out). It was literally pickup your bowl, throw it back & engage in full-on, annoying loud, slurping delicious. 

The service was super cool & welcoming as well. I requested more Nori which was brought right over with a smile. Decor is fitting of an Asian themed establishment; red, black, teenie weenie sink, chopsticks Voltran...you catch my drift.

Semi open kitchen so you can watch them work, adult beverages & dessert available as well. 

~Christy

Subpar seafood with a great happy hour. FYI the calamari is exceptional. 

My review would've ended there except for the fact that I aim to please. Therefore, I shall carry on. 

The dining area is nice & spacious. Perfect for a date night with intimate booth seating or large groups with open table seating. The bar area is totally out of the way of the dining room so not to bother the less spicy crowd of people patronizing the restaurant. Servers/bartenders are "nice enough" however, the food prep staff are the one's with real personality (I know because they often deliver food out to guests which gives me a chance to interact & ask my foodie questions). 

The coolest part about this location is that it is docked on Union Station's basin. You can even feed the fish for small change. Park on the secure lot and have your pass validated by the Landry's hostess. 

Ladies beware: if you're wearing heels be cautious walking along the wood ramp leading to Laundry's door not to get your heel stuck in between to slats. That would be ugly! 

~Christy

Very nice restaurant/wine bar/gift shop! Yes this little spot packs a mean punch...offering a variety of things from salads, macarons, mussels, wine for purchase as well as consumption, sauces, pottery, t-shirts, beverages by the bottle and more.

There's a large backyard patio, bar seats and tables to accommodate guests of all sizes. 
Service was hospitable.
