I enjoyed a delicious salad that consisted of two of my favorite ingredients: fresh greens & goat cheese! This salad was a real winner and totally justifies several follow up visits in the nearest future. Finally, the mussels were finger licking good...and that's a I have folks.

Until next time. 
~Christy

Stopped in to grab a dozen of deep fried doughnuts for community friends because as seen on TV...World's Fair Donuts rock! 

It's nostalgic...seems like everything from the display case to cash register is an orignal from the 60's. The elderly owners still run the place like a well oiled machine. Very pleasant service and they offer tons of flavor varieties for those sweet tooth cravings:

Custard 
Cake
Creme
Glaze
Round 
Long
Fritter 
Twist 

And more!

Beverages on ready for a chaser. 

CASH ONLY! So come correct.

~Christy

From the moment I walked in it was apparent that this place was owned and operated by some really rad people! I bet really rad people hangout here too.

I digress, Whisk has been on my radar for quite some time. I've experienced their delicious products via other local establishments in the area such as Rise and Kitchen Coffee House. Today I was feeling froggy so I jumped on the first item the super helpful employee suggested; Salted Caramel Brownie Pie! Took one bite and literally drifted off to heaven. This was an amazing concoction of 2 soft baked brownie cookies with a light-airy salted caramel filling that formed a mouthwatering mini pie. 

The pastry case had so much unique goodness to choose from...gooey butter, popcorn and ginger cookies, gigantic brownies, lemon curd pop tarts, caramelized onion & asiago scones, vegan cupcakes, gluten-free banana chocolate chip muffins and so much more you'll have to go see for yourself because I'm not running the entire menu here.

Now on to the cool fixtures and furnishings. I loved the leather sofa perfectly positioned at the floor to ceiling window which offers a great view of Cherokee Row. There were world globes serving as tabletop centerpieces which I found extremely attractive as not only a traveler but a lover of globes. The walls were adorned with some of the most rad articles which can make wonderful conversations pieces.  I walked around the place, taking pics and engaging in conversation with two adorably pleasant young ladies sitting at one of the tables. Only to find out one was the owner. 

~Christy, (Officially Rad) because I'm going to hangout at Whisk more often.

Goody Goody is probably the best greasy spoon in town! The service is always A-1. They have a team of pleasant, personable, efficient employees who work effortlessly to make your dining experience enjoyable. Food is delicious! Kitchen staff makes no qualms about accommodating requests. Keep in mind they can get extremely crowded during peek hours and weekend mornings so prepare to wait a bit. It's a first come first serve type of setup and generally the line moves quickly. Also, the parking lot is not very big however, there is off-street parking along Natural Bridge as well as the rear on Hamilton. 

What to try:
*Coffee
*Grits
*Waffle
*Catfish 
*Chicken 
*Eggs 

Plenty of seating available inside. If you're solo avoid wait time by snagging a bar seat. Great dining choice for the entire family. Price point right on par.

~Christy

Well packaged takeout & I appreciated it. I was in the mood for a light meal and of course I'm hibernating with all other health-conscious human beings so I had it delivered via Uber Eats. Ordering was effortless and efficient with regular updates. Fair pricing for jasmine rice + vegetables and spring rolls. Flavorful & enjoyable. 

I'd dine-in if we weren't experiencing a pandemic for sure.  

~Christy

Overall Retreat is a decent lunch spot but the tiny portions left much to be desired for my taste buds. I was more impressed with how the place had been transformed. I remember when this space was occupied by 6 North Cafe (a small coffee house) so to see the hanging filament lighting, concrete bar top and wood work seating was refreshing. The interior is on the small side with closely positioned tables however, the bar and outdoor patio allows for more seating. Personally, I like a little elbow room when I'm dining. The lunch menu was not huge but offered a variety of dishes pretty much anyone could choose from..burgers, salads, soup, seafood, vegetarian, carnivore, you name it.

I decided to go with the Beet Carpaccio salad; a tiny bed of arugula, approximately 5-6 thinly sliced roasted beets, a few sprinkles of goat cheese, almond slivers and a light sherry vinaigrette. My dining partner opted for the lunch special: beer battered shrimp, slaw and fries as well as Retreat's chicken wing dish. We enjoyed the food but still left feeling pretty hungry and unsatisfied. I'm thinking dinner is probably a better option for my huge appetite or maybe Retreat Gastropub is aiming to do things on a small scale (space, portion, seating), just saying.

~Christy

Amazing authentic Bosnian food restaurant located in the heart of Dutch Town. Grbic has been on my To-Do List for years (I know it's quite pathetic). I finally got the chance to check this gem off my list on an ISC outing. 

From the outside the restaurant appears small compared to its spacious interior. There's seating for large parties, couples, kids, banquet sets and outdoor during warm weather months. There's a cozy fire place burning Yule logs and beautiful holiday decorations to create a festive feel. The restroom is even roomy, very well kept with a warm feel. All in all I love the space. 

Now on to the food. Ahhhhhmazing! 

That's it. One word sums it up....Ahhhhhmazing! 

The generous 9oz tilapia was cooked to perfection and served with a delicious vegetable rice blend that was very flavorful and filling. I ate this dish over 2 meals; taking half to go. For dessert I opted for the Nutella stuffed crepe that was so good it made me wanna slap my mama! Although the crepe was filled with Nutella it was very light in terms of a dessert. The house made whipped cream was tasty and complimented the crepe well. 

I can not wait to return to Grbic for their superior food with service to match.

~Christy

This is my favorite Wasabi location. I love how the staff is so pleasant and patient; making sure each patron is properly served. Shardea was a jewel, I appreciated her warm welcome and amazing service today. The restaurant is always immaculate. Donned with gorgeous traditional Japanese décor. 

My go-to dish is the Chirashi which is always different in appearance but unwaveringly delicious each time. The presentation is beautiful but not so much that I don't devour the entire dish. The chef likes to put a slight spin on it that keeps me guessing. The rolls are all great as well, namely the Chow & Kim rolls. The Hawaiian Poke Tower is another must try. It's small but tasty and filling. The tuna tower is atop a bed of white rice, crab meat & fresh greens. Together this forms a superb salad.

~Christy

Ordering takeout was a breeze. Service was decent upon arrival and the Tamarind soup is an absolute MUST TRY! I opted for the vegetarian version which was loaded with veggies, tofu, herbs, & pineapple. The broth was phenomenal. Served with a side of steamed rice this dish was very satisfying. Easily a new favorite. Well worth the $16 price tag. 

~Christy

Vin de Set is the sister to Eleven Eleven, the cousin to Moulin and mother of PW's. Although I absolutely adore them all and treat each as extended family; they offer something totally different.

What makes Vin de Set extraordinary is their amazing rooftop view (I'm a sucker for rooftop views) which creates a magnificent ambiance and gives an amazing view of the Lafayette/Downtown neighborhoods. The dimly lit dining room is super chic as well. What I enjoy most at this location is the Sunday Brunch. Superb assortment of food from omelettes to waffles and fresh juice to mimosas.

Perfect in the spring/summer months for couples, family and girls day out. Staff is great and the price is right; give it whirl.

~Christy said so.

I've been eager to experience Olio since I discovered how the former garage was transformed into this amazing restaurant.

The decor did not disappoint; it's beautifully put together both inside as well as the outdoor garden area.  

Gretchen was nice; meek but nice.  I mentioned I had an itching for hummus and she recommended I try the Eyal; it was delicious.  The shrimp in the Eyal hummus was sauteed and seasoned to perfection it also came with plenty of dough; pita as well as ciabatta..but I truly felt like I probably could've dressed up a container of Trader Joe's Mediterranean Hummus and not known the difference.  Don't kill the messenger I'm just being honest here.  There was a lot more oil than I prefer and the serving size was quite small for $12 before tip.

Next, I wanted to try the roasted cauliflower but Gretchen advised me they were out.

Then, I wanted to try the Roasted Beets salad but Gretchen advised me they were out.

Finally, I gave up ordering anything else however, Gretchen did advise me they were out of Romaine Hearts.  I thought to myself, "Why are you guys open?"

Maybe I picked a bad day; but in the restaurant business a bad day can cost you 2 stars on the Christy Scale.

It was OK. I'll elaborate...

ISC brought me here, so this was a group dining experience. Staff seemed a little taken aback by 13 Yelpers (maybe unprepared) but definitely made aware prior to our arrival. Clearly understaffed, our server did his best. Although it wasn't quite on point, he was running from one side of the restaurant to the other serving, bussing, prepping takeout orders, ringing customers and answering the telephone. 

Once we finically got our orders in, it didn't take long for food to start rolling out. They forgot several servings of rice, making it impossible for many of us to eat our meals. Indian just isn't complete without the rice or naan. 

Anywho, I ordered the Mushroom Matter. It never arrived. Another dish arrived that was clearly not Mushroom Matter. I advised the server, he examined my dish, apologized for the error and stated a Mushroom Matter would be out in 5 minutes. 

Fast forward 10 minutes... no Mushroom Matter. I'm filling up on naan & samplings from from dining partners.

Fast forward 15 minutes....no Mushroom Matter. I'm ready to go, disappointed and completely full. It's also getting late & I've lost the desire to eat. 

I caution the sever that I'm no longer interested in the Mushroom Matter. He pleads the meal is almost ready, already prepared, on its way out. Fast forward 5 minutes...no Mushroom Matter.

Again, I advise the server to cash me out. He returns with Mushroom Matter. I ask for a takeout container and the check. 

This dining experience was a slight disaster simply because I didn't eat my desired meal and communicating my disappointment to the server was to no avail. What saved Signature India was my company. Great company can turn an otherwise bad situation into a laughable moment. 

I won't be back, but the memory shall live on. 
~Christy

Delicious & authentic Mediterranean food! Great service with plenty of seating both inside as well as outdoors. They have a bar for adult libations. Nova is a wonderful meeting spot. Works equally for lunch and dinner dining out at a reasonable price.  I highly recommend the hummus and even higher the salmon special.  

Enjoy,

~Christy

Yessssss!!!!

Graze for President!

This vegan joint is what every city needs. Swankly-hip ambiance, super cool service, nice quaint tuck-a-way location, clean restroom, plenty seating options (bar, window, center stage tables) and drum roll please....

ALL ITEMS VEGAN!!!!!!

Places like this are sooooo hard to come by. I've noticed since becoming vegan that many restaurants either incorrectly advertise vegan or simply don't want to bother with offering vegan options. Graze was a breath of fresh air. 

I thoroughly enjoyed the Vegetable Root salad. Very filling & flavorful. The assortment of veggies went well together. They didn't have the banana pudding when I stopped in during Sunday brunch so I doubled back Tuesday to grab a takeout order and it was so good it made me wanna slap my mama! 

Graze STL (pretty please with a cherry on top).

~Christy

Very welcoming, friendly service! Beautiful decor, colorful & clean. Outdoor seating available for prime Central West End people- watching. Lunch buffet is plentiful with selections ranging from chicken for carnivores & chickpeas for vegetarians. Dessert (usually) rice pudding as well as salads & fresh vegetables available. 

Bonus features:

Full bar 
Television 
Private dining area 

I'm a fan!
~Christy

Must've picked the wrong night to try this joint.  They were out of nearly everything I wanted to try.

They don't serve chicken

The sides all looked dry & old. Needing replenishment. 

The customer service was terribly sour & rushed (namely Jess at the register) 

Explained it was my first visit and the protein guy didn't give a damn...kept it moving like an assembly line. 

First experience was a busy and totally not what I expected since everyone compares it to Pappy's which is my fav (not just today, check my review) I love Pappy's because all things are properly aligned: food, service, freshness. 

My sister liked the brisket and I thought the turkey was pretty good.  Both were well smoked in our opinion.

I have issues with Sugar Fire's sanitation.  The tables needed to be busted, the sauce containers wiped, floor swept and food wells cleaned.  Jess dumped the container of pickles sitting at the register for customers into the a larger batch of refrigerated pickles that stored the bulk of pickles for replenishing.  Can you say contamination hazard!  

A random young man (maybe the friend of a coworker strolled through the kitchen area with FroYo)  

And 1 last thing, the gentlemen I assumed to be a manager began counting cash on the pie counter surrounded by food.  I threw my hands up!  C'mon guy, you've got to have an office around this place for business such as tallying profits and completing paperwork.  Can you say unprofessional and tacky simultaneously! 

No thanks I'll pass...FOREVER!

All-you-can-eat is all good with me!  

Sushi was good and arrived on target every time.  Very filling.

The server was pleasant and punctual on water refills.

So I've finally finished my assortment of 17 different macaroons.  Some were tastier than others, I particularly enjoyed the bluberry, chocolate coconut, pistachio, Nutella, lavender, rose, Macha tea, red velvet & chocolate. 

I did not care for the pumpkin (lacked flavor), earl grey (bland) salted caramel, tropical, tiramisu, boysenberry, lemon (tasted like fruit loops cereal) & mint.  Don't get me wrong, they were all edible and extremely cute but where some had the perfect airy shell and soft inside construction, others where hard shell hollow inside.  Hollow macaroons indicate a baker's error and should be tossed rather than sold.

I like my macaroons fluffy inside La Bonne Bouchee.  I realize it takes skill to make the perfect macaroon  but if your establishment specializes in macaroons I expect perfection.

Gonna give the place another twirl.

5/5 Food was nothing short of amazing:

*Shrimp & Grits 
*Ahi Tuna stir fry 
*Beet & Goat cheese
*Bottle of bubbly 

Nate, server extraordinaire was awesome. 
Hostess with the mostess, Quinta was superb. 
Other staff Shirley, Donny were equally hospitable. 

I enjoyed my first dining experience so much so that I returned the very next day for takeout. However it was a completely different ballgame. 

Erin, bartender was like a jab to the gut. I arrived to the bar to place my takeout order and he was a total jerk. Without going into great detail Erin was rude, dismissive & a horrible representation of Cafe Amelia, considering the amazing service provided the previous evening. 

Being the type of customer I am, I requested to speak with a manager. Danny, came out with genuine concern & apologies. He rectified the issue with professionalism, compassion & gratitude. This was another reminder of what I loved about the establishment. Hence the 5 star review. There nothing like great food, beautiful ambiance, amazing service and classy management. 

I'll be back a third time whenever I'm  back in NOLA! Danny ROCKS! 

~Christy

Over 200 solar panels...

Over 60 gooey butter flavors...

Free wifi...

Delicious coffee...

Grounds for sale...

Tea too...

Outdoor seating...

Hippest coffeehouse on the Hill...

This location is very Eco-Chic (I just made that term up on the fly).

~Christy

Think Jay's International but in Kirkwood.

Think World's Market but only a grocer.

Think United Provisions but bigger.

Think Dierberg's but on an International scale.

Don't think, just go!

Global Foods Market is superb no matter what your taste buds long for; they have it.  The aisles are categorized by regions so your items are easy to find.

Have fun, explore and thank me later.

Per usual service was on point; this evening in particular Bradley was a gem. Knowledgeable, accommodating, attentive & prompt. I enjoyed the oysters to start and Chilean sea bass as a main course.  Although the patio area was open, it was pretty crowded so we opted for a cooler ambiance, indoors near the bar. 

Valet available. 

Absolutely returning soon for drinks.

~Christy

Got a whiff of The Sweet Divine at Sauce Magazine's Food Truck Friday event in Tower Grove Park.  The trucker girl was super cool & very helpful in my decision making. I mean... everything looks tantalizing wrapped in pretty pink boxes, topped with decorative icing, sprinkles, powered sugar with flavors ranging from pumpkin to Oreo cookie. 

I went with the Gooey Butter Cookies which were delightful. The texture was perfectly "ooey", soft, sweet and doused in powered sugar for a beautiful finish. I also couldn't leave without a Pumpkin Muffin and Chocolate Chip Muffin. It just seemed like the season and they were so cute.  Unfortunately, I decided to freeze them for a later sweet tooth crazing. The cookies sent me over my weekly limit lol..this further let me know that I have no need to go inside the actual store. I'd leave out 20lbs heavier for sure. 

Sincerely, 
~Christy

al pastor tacos
hot hot sauce almost killed me
breakfast burritos

California tacos is what it says it is... and burritos, chimichangas, churros, horchata, etc etc etc. A couple things to note: the breakfast burrito is awesome--which I've been craving since I was last in California. The al pastor is awesome. The hot is way hotter than the medium. The fried fish tacos are incredible, but are not the model of what would be a healthy taco item. 

The tortillas! OMG. As I was slowly and painfully eating my overly heated taco, I noticed, "These tortillas are amazing." They have a nice chew and sweetness to them, they don't fall apart or taste grainy like the store bought kind. They actually taste fresh. The price is right. The radio outside blasts oldies that pretty much anyone could karaoke to, and I love it. 

Remember: it's all take out. There is no indoor seating, and it can get busy. Be prepared to eat in your car if you're starving. It might be smart to order ahead an pick up. So far, my fav Mexican food in Tampa.

I was refused entrance to this diner with my service dog unless I produced "papers" for the service dog.  By ADA  and DOJ  federal law there are no "papers" required for a service dog.  I tried to politely explain this to the manager who stood in front of the door and refused my entering until I gave papers.  I decided to leave and returned to my car very shaken up.  This manager  came to my car, banged on my windshield and yelled to get off the property and he was calling 911.  A complaint will be filed with the ADA.  A very upsetting experience.

Oh, Vango, we are SO OVER. I thought I used to like you, with your snazzy roof deck and all. But it turns out that the roof deck is your only good feature, and sometimes even the roof deck is unpleasant when underage girls are vomiting all over. What's the point of lounging on a roof deck bed, when as soon as you get cozy there's some teenage vomit everywhere. Yeah, I'm mad. I'm mad because it didn't happen just once. It happened THREE times in a 45 minute span pre-midnight on a Saturday. Three different people vomited! On the roof deck, on the stairs, on the dance floor. Are we serious people? How old are you? No, really, how old... because I kind of felt like I was placed in a time machine that brought me back to high school, except I didn't get any younger, and I was crashing a prom queen's party. Damn there were a lot of fake tans and sequins. But here's the issue, Vango: I wouldn't have wanted to go then, and I sure don't want to go now.

The bad experience starts at the door. There are other people in line who don't have a table so we have to wait until they get sat before we get in, despite the fact that my friends already have a table inside. My wife think its shifty behavior to make people think that it's more popular than it really is - this place always has a line out the door when I drive by.
Horrible logic and time to rethink the experience - the first and perhaps the most important customer touchpoint. 

Inside now... it's not full. Where is everyone?

Talked to the owner/bartender: He doesnt want it to be like a Broadway bar, elbow to elbow, people fighting for a drink. Fighting their way to wench a drink from the alchimist to quench the raging bends. This is a neighborhood bar, unlike a Broadway bar, yet they insist on lines, they stamp your hand, and they treat the place like a club. Maybe this is the new east Nashville? Or maybe they take themselves less seriously, and don't consider their bar space as the center of the universe. Maybe you craft the space for the customers to have a good night out. I saw a mom yelling from the barred door to her two sons waiting in line that the appetizers were getting cold. They yelled back, trying to explain the mandatory line policy of Pearl Diver.

It's not about Pearl Diver, its about the people that meet there, and the moments they have together. The bar is like any other place, a watering hole of mixed drinks, but with a slightly above par environment. If you go here, expect to be confused and annoyed by the out of ordinary entrance ceremony. Hopefully, they'll change this and people don't have to wait outside so the bar doesnt get overwhelmed. Maybe they'll actually get wait staff so the bar isn't a forced interaction point. The current method of operation doesnt appear to be about the customer, it seems to be about coddling the bar's ego.

GONE DOWN HILL ! 
I use to really enjoy going to this place and refer people to here. Service was always ok, but the food used to be worth it. Things have gone down hill in the last few months 
The last 3 times we went, a waitress had her 2 yr old in the dining room-she lets him roam, play, jump in the booths with patrons, eat from their chip bowl. Then came the clincher. Last time, right after she brought our check a COCKROACH climbed up the wall next to our table. Never Again !

Our experience at this restaurant was a bit awkward. We walked in and there was no host. After waiting several minutes and debating with the host if we could check in with open table (it costs about a dollar to the restaurant), they walked us by the kitchen where one of the staff members was being treated after cutting himself while cooking. The food was okay, decent red sauce Italian. Service was a bit odd- they were attentive, but awkward. Different people stopped over, we weren't sure what was going on. Hope they've improved since we went.

They bill themselves as having classic NY pizza, I've never been to NY so I can't say but I can tell you it's damn tasty.  Like, super yummy good.  Thin crust, fresh ingredients, and cooked to perfection every time. 
Thus far I have always tried some combination of basil, garlic, and olives, and cheese of course :D That garlic - WOW.  So good, so potent.  Make a pact with the people at your table, you know the rules if one person eats garlic, everyone eats garlic. A large pie is insanely large. I've finally convinced myself to get a small next time, I know I will still have leftovers.  

Ok, what you NEED to know about this pizza - the more toppings you pile on the more likely it's going to fall apart on you. Classic NY pizza is sauce and cheese and that's what that crust is made for.  Once you start adding greasy meat or heavy toppings you can kiss any structure goodbye. 
*Unless you get the Sicilian style thick crust.  Don't say I didn't warn you!

Did I mention their mission statement: to create hope and meaning in the lives of people with disabilities?
Not only do you get a great pizza but you're also supporting some great, great people.

In N Out grilled cheese is the best vegetarian food at any fast food place. You don't just get a bun and cheese you get everything that's on a burger without the burger. Lettuce, pickles, tomato, onions, cheese, and sauce. Animal style makes it even better!

Located smack dab in the middle of hipsterville Death and Taxes is the epitome of hipster bar.  If you are looking for a PBR and a shot of Jameson-this isn't the place for you, if you are looking for a drinking experience then head over.  Each cocktail is handcrafted with quality ingredients and attention to detail.  Ivan and crew pride themselves on their house made simple syrups and their use of only the best mixers as well as fresh fruit and herbs (grown right out front).
The first time I went to this bar I felt it was a little "too cool for school" but once you get past the ultra black inside and the uber pretentious drink menu you find yourself in a bar that truly cares about the craft and the guests enjoyment.  
Over this past weekend I took a bartending class at Death and Taxes and was delighted to learn how easy it is to make the best Margarita I've ever tasted!  I highly recommend not only the bar but the classes as well.

Updated my review to 5 stars because they've maintained the same quality beverages and amazing customer service every single time I've been there.

Yes, yes, yes! I have been wanting to try Midtown Tacos for MONTHS and finally stumbled across it and I am so pleased I did. 
First, can we talk about the adorable setup? Tucked around the back of Death and Taxes, Midtown Tacos is really just an enclosed walk-up counter-style restaurant but they have done it so well.  The glass doors make it feel larger than it is.  The outside seating area is cozy but plentiful.  The family-vibe behind the counter makes me want to give them all my money.  I just fell in love with this place and all of that was before I even tried the food!
Ok, the food. I had veggie tacos (they are street style) and they were so freaking tasty. Cauliflower, jalapeno,  and green apple? What? YES! Oh, it works in the best way.  My friend had a burrito sans tortilla and pretty much licked their plate clean.  
Stop reading and go give these people your money!

Just thinking about this place makes me full!! 
Korean food has been a favorite of mine for a very, very long time.. Mind your business!! I said it was a long time!!
I've always said that if I could only pick one city to return for a visit, it would be Seoul.... And what's served at Dolsot is just a piece of what I remember from there, and they make some great dishes. 
While beef bulgogi is a must, I usually start with a spicy rice cake and vegetable soup. The broth is the star of this dish. 
This place was one of my pandemic takeout restaurants. The bonchon alone is enough to make me happy. Especially the spicy cucumbers and daikon. The servings of everything are pretty large, so  I had to cut back by just ordering bowls. Spicy pork bulgogi with fried egg. It has rice and vegetables. This helped cut back on leftovers and the boxes of rice that come with each dish. 
Normally I don't like waiting in line to eat anywhere... This place is one of my exceptions. The restaurant is pretty small. But there's a parade of people coming and going for takeout... You'll find me among the takeout crowd.

Several people have said that this is the spot on Washington Ave for a great Vietnamese meal. So instead of going with my usual trusted places, I decided to give them a try... 
First off, it's a huge place. Plenty of tables spaced out where youre not back to back or rubbing elbows  with other diners.. 
Service was prompt, but not pushy. Table cloths that were changed after every meal (not the norm, and greatly appreciated). 
A huge menu full of any meal you could think of, and a bar menu for drinks. 
I chose a vermicelli bowl with a combination of different meats and shrimp, and an order of summer rolls. The meal came out pretty quick,  and while it wasn't mind blowing as some have described, it was a decent meal. 
I'd definitely go back for meals in the future...

So, a friend and I decided to have a late meal here one night... The diner close at 1am, we got there roughly at midnight. The orders were kept fairly simple. I got a cup of chicken noodle soup and a side Greek salad. My friend ordered mussels marinara and the same soup..
The waitress was fairly friendly. Possibly even pleasant.. 
Well, out comes the soup... The soup is great. 
Then comes the salad and mussels..
Waitress returns to ask how is everything. Since I knew the mussels we're between cool and warm, I told her it was served cold.. 
Really??, she says... I told her that it hadn't been on the table no more than a minute or two.. Grab a fork and try it for yourself... Then comes the excuses about how it's almost closing, and the cooks were putting things away... But I'll ask my manager what he can do.. This chick comes back and said the manager took it off the bill but I have to take the plate of food!! Straight effin insulting, considering that I brought up the cold food to be taken back... It was one thing that this was about as unprofessional as a manager could get in a restaurant when an issue is brought to him. But it also suggested that something was wanted for nothing... I ordered another salad anyway. But told the waitress that if a suitable meal can't be served an hour before closing, then why don't you guys just close and not take any orders..... 
I sat on this for a few days since this really is one of my favorite places to eat... 
But with service and a crappy attitude from a manager like I experienced this night, eff em!!
I know where subpar food is served at other places that wouldn't give horrible service like this... I'm not going there.. But they're more likely to get my money than Seven Star would again

I've been to Corrine's possibly 10 times in my life. Two times dining in. The rest was Sunday buffet takeout...
The full menu is served everyday except Sunday. With the Sunday buffet, I received a round takeout container with 5-6 sides an 5-6 different meats, a roll, potato salad, and a piece of cake. All for $19.00. This meal is large enough to share with 3 people, or it will take two days for one person to finish it. 
Call ahead for takeout on Sunday. There's usually a line to get in.

Sometimes I get so caught up in convenience that I become too lazy to venture too far from my neighborhood... It was a nice night out, and the sidewalk tables at the restaurants while driving through Pitman were calling my name... Well, not really. I'm not a fan of dining on public sidewalks... So I parked and walked into Mannino's Pizzeria for a meal.. 
First thought.... I forgot that there was such a thing as a clean pizzeria!!Seriously... But that's another topic for another day...
Nice, modern Italian interior.. An huge brick oven that's visible from most of the seats. and plenty of tables that were spaced out in a way that nobody felt cramped or that their spaced was being invaded..
I put in an order for loaded tater tots, and a pepperoni pizza with half sausage.... The tots were fried and finished in the oven with a couple cheeses and bacon.. The pizza was very good... Really good ingredients used, and the crust was thin, but not overcooked, and able to hold the toppings without having to use two hands to make sure nothing winds up in your lap... I wish every pizzeria used top quality ingredients and had an environment like this one does.. Especially since they're charging not much less than this place... 
Great for a planned meal out, before or after a movie or show, or just to meet someone for a nice, relaxing meal...

So I saw this bar on a Facebook video.. I had no clue that this place was tucked away in a neighborhood that I pass through from time to time... Once I saw the name and location, I stopped in for a late lunch and a beer. 
First impression... "That is one sexy bartender you have working that afternoon shift"!!
But I'm here for their famous kielbasa cheesesteak. I placed my order which came with fries, and I ordered a beer after tasting a couple that were on tap... I have loved kielbasa sandwiches since I was a kid ordering them at either Marty & Barbs or The Rainbow Inn Bar in Clayton... 
The phrase "lost in the sauce" applied to this sandwich... The melted cheese sauce really took over the whole sandwich.... 
But those fries!! They were frighin phenomenal. Eaten with malt vinegar and  added salt, I could've just sat down to that and the beer..
Great local spot. Friendly patrons. Good service.

Yeah, I've read a few reviews about suspect service being given here. But there weren't enough of those opinions to keep me.from trying this place. 
This is a great looking neighborhood deli/sandwich shop inside and out.. Plenty of not the norm sandwiches on their menu. All of them would make deciding what to get pretty hard.... Good thing I had my mind made up months ago when I first saw this business page and saw pics of the shrimp po boy..
I placed my order, and out came this roll with huge shrimp on it... The shrimp were seasoned well and not overcooked. Thankfully I didn't order anything else as a backup just in case I didn't care for this. I will probably try one of their other meals next time I come since this one didn't disappoint. 
Parking is virtually non-existent. Wherever you can find on the street or side street. 
But this seems to be a favorite for workers close by. 
Well worth going out of my way to try.

I've heard of meat sweats before. But I've always thought this was an exaggerated myth...
This is no myth!!
I was heading to another Korean restaurant that I hadn't been before when I saw the Ten Hot Pot sign, and I swerved into the parking lot. 
I had never been to an ayce Korean bbq before..
After being seated, I was given the run down by the host and the server.... I got the bbq and hot pot combo. I chose my broth and meats for both..
Then out comes the appetizers.. Kim chi, diced daikon, edamame, and a couple other palate pleasers that I can't remember.  
Out comes the meats... and it's a lot of it. The server lights the grill and adjust the hot pot heat and left me grill and cook away. I got several cuts of pork, beef, and some seafood... 
When you read ayce, you think you can put away a lot and enjoying it... I couldn't make it anywhere near the two hour limit that's given. I ordered a second selection of different meats and pretty much regretted it... I stayed about an hour and fifteen minutes... an enjoyable 1hr 15 min!!
I left stuffed and ready for a nap...
As much as I thought I could eat plenty of these thinly sliced meats, I really couldn't!
Maybe this is something I could try annually. But definitely not on a regular basis..

What's not good to say about this place...?
If you like bbq, this here is a must stop in at least once business... Even if you don't come back, it won't be because you weren't satisfied. 
Just want lunch? They got you covered with various sandwiches, sides, and platters... Have a taste for bbq? The smokey smell when you enter this place will tip you off that the ribs, brisket, and chicken is fresh made and will also start the time consuming debate on what to order... Wanna cook at home? Take a look in their refrigerated display... Prime rib, steaks, chicken, burgers, and other items.. They do their own dry aging. 
So far I've only stopped in a few times for lunch. Burgers, ribs chicken, and sides... Had recently just stopped in to purchase their smoked candied bacon, bacon wrapped jalepeno, and chicken tenders which are the size of a half of chicken breast.. Considering they're all fresh made, it's a bargain at $2 each..
From customer service, to product, and even packaging, this little kuntry themed business is a place that I can walk into and not question whether I'm throwing my money away...

I can't believe I haven't written a review for this place... living a minute away from here, this restaurant and bar has one of my favorite items on Earth!! Smoked whiting... If you've never had it, smoked whiting is the perfect bar food... 
If you've ever been to a truly old school seafood bar, then this place would be perfect.. Old wood paneling. Nostalgia items nailed to the walls. A long curved wooden bar, and everything you'd expect to eat at a place like this... 
Surprisingly, I never think about coming in here often for a sit down meal or drinks. But when I do, I always regret not stopping in more often..
I have to rethink how I spend my time at home since this is within walking distance. I usually stop in for takeout. But I'll be stopping in more often for some decent seafood, drinks, and social time.

Yep... This is a 5 star bakery. If you only ate one item, and that would be the cream donut, you'd still give it 5 stars. The donuts are sliced and filled with this cream that will make you forget that you were supposed to be at work shortly. My advice would be to to get the donuts with granulated sugar... The powdered sugar will wind up all over your clothes, no matter how careful you are. Seriously good cakes that are reasonably priced. A large variety of Danishes and cookies. There's a bread pudding on the display  that looks pretty good. 
This place is a dieters nightmare. But a necessary stop in the morning. 
Also, do yourself a favor and park on the street. The 3 car space that's considered a parking lot is an accident just waiting to happen.

By leaving that lone, menacing fly that was checking on customers at every table out of this review,  I like this place....
My daughter and I stopped by for a late dinner.. 
I sent my young scout in for a menu while I rested my eyes for a few minutes... Out she comes and the menu looks great. It has most of what both of us liked, including the smoothies that she required to even dine in... I just drive. She does the planning and navigating!!
We ordered a couple glasses of water, our smoothies and the meals... The interior is pretty comfortable and modern. Booths and tables. Not too many of either to be crowded by. Two large TVs that can be seen from either direction you're sitting. 
Our meals came out staggered, as it should. All was hot, well cooked, and plenty of condiments were placed at the table. The salt and pepper shrimp were huge. I have to say that this will be my reason to return, and possibly try the salt and pepper squid also. 
The pho bowls came in one size and were pretty large... I was sort of proud of myself that this was one time that I didn't make a mess on my shirt with the wet swinging noodles!! The summer rolls were good also, especially with the addition of cucumbers, which isn't in most places I go. 
The gentleman serving was a one man show as far as making sure every table was satisfied with their meals and checking to see if anything else was needed. 
This was a pleasant experience from start to finish.

A nice place to pickup several types of banh mi sandwiches. I also like the spring rolls and desserts. 
I've always gotten one banh mi and was still hungry. Regretting not getting two. 
, I found out during a recent visit here that eating two was all in my mind!! Although I enjoyed having two types of sandwiches, it was more than I could eat. 
A nice, clean takeout business that makes all of the sandwiches fresh. Plenty of other sides and desserts in a few open cold cases.

Everyone should have a Yelp friend like Jess J.. When you can get a credible, no questions asked recommendations, Yelp.friends like this become very valuable and appreciated..
Hot On D Spot is great place for roti and doubles... (I've driven this far two times for this). Over the years I've been fortunate to have been surrounded with friends from Trinidad and Grenada that have made their specialties from home countless times..
Because of this, I can spot a fraud or a place that is flat out stealing money be serving poor renditions of Caribbean food.. 
This place here is about as authentic as it gets. The smell from the spices will have you wanting to order everything. But the portions are so huge that you couldn't possibly eat it all. My first visit, I chose the beef roti..
The second, I had two doubles.. shrimp and chicken. The pleasant change in what to eat is worth the drive.... the menu is pretty large, with all of your favorites made daily. 
 If they had some place similar close to where live. 
Until.then, the 45 minute drive up 295 will have to do.

I have to steer away from this place in order to not stop here.. This bread and pastry bakery has become my current go to place for banh mi. I've tried several and all have been great. Freshly baked rolls, equally fresh vegetables on several varieties they have... It's pretty hard to choose once you've had them all. Chicken, BBQ pork, pork belly are just a few.... An inexpensive and enjoyable meal at any time of day.

Personally, I think that most bbq places are stealing money, serving subpar, not trimmed, and overcooked meats, with a great smelling sauce to mask the robbery that's taking place while you're paying for your meal....
But Big Daddyz.... No thief here!! 
I was recommended this place a couple/few years back, and never found the right moment to stop in... Fast forward to the past few weeks, and I walked into what's basically a corner shack that pumps out some of the best BBQ I've had in a long time...
Out of the choices to choose from, make sure the brisket is one of them. It's sliced much thinner than usual. But this cut of meat will make you want to place another order of it!! It's that tender and good tasting. The other choice I've made was the chicken breast... Once again, this piece of meat was seasoned and cooked perfectly.... I won't bother wasting my money stopping anyplace else when this here is a convenient option. 
No seating. Just enough room inside to take two steps in to place your order... So bring some wet naps and be prepared for your car to smell like bbq for a couple hours after you finish eating in it!!

Well folks... I finally made it to this bar/restaurant. I stopped by one weekday for a late lunch and got exactly what I expected... A near empty bar, a friendly bartender, and the three people who were at the bar were as friendly. 
Large window surrounded the spaced out tables behind the bar, and a decent sized deck towards the rear... 
I was pressed for time (as usual) and chose one of their lunch specials instead of settling in for something off the dinner menu... For a quick inexpensive lunch, the pulled pork sandwich I was served was a bargain. 
While I initially stopped in for the wings that I've heard so much about, I was more than happy with the choice that I made... When I stop in again, I hope the wings are as good as the first meal I had.

Having a 10 year old that prefers Taco Bell quesadillas to anything else makes having a meals out a daily negotiation...
So on our way bowling at Pinsetters she suggested we eat there while bowling.. Their food actually isn't bad for a bowling alley. But that was far from what I wanted my first meal of the day to be..  So my bookmarks showed that we were close to Turning Point, and the debate ended... They closed at 3, and we walked in at 2. Plenty of time to have brunch.. She chose the OMG French Toast. That came loaded with candied pecans and chopped bacon. I went with the Huevos Rancheros... Both we're very good choices. Her dish was, well, sweet!! What else would you expect out of a 10 year old... My dish was great. It was huge... I thought I was hungry, so I ate the whole thing.... Savory and spicy.. Avocados and sour cream on the side to balance the meal... I enjoyed this meal so much that I needed a nap in Pinsetters parking lot before going in....  The service at Turning Point was attentive, but not overbearing. The menu offered plenty of dishes with enough of a twist to not make it the norm, as if you were at an average restaurant or diner. 
I don't really remember how this place got into my bookmarks. But I'm glad that it was there when I needed it.

I have to preface this with I've never sat in the dining room for a meal... Always on the go, I've sat at the bar for a happy our meal and drinks. 
The bar staff are equally as friendly and pleasant as they are professional... The drinks here are beyond generous and are pretty inexpensive on the happy hour menu.. The same can be said for their bar menu choices. The menu is pretty large compared to most bar menus, and the food quality is excellent. 
Relaxing atmosphere and great conversations with the surrounding patrons and staff. 
This happy hour is in the top two in this Deptford/Woodbury area in my opinion. 
Come for the food. Have a decent drink while you're there!!

First impressions hopefully are lasting...
I've only been here once, and it was for lunch. 
Great old bar... The bartender was pretty attentive to everyone that was there, and it only took me a few tastings to decide which craft beer I was going to have... 
The wings with the house sauce were pretty much spot on with what people have claimed this bar is famous for... Bring an appetite, because these wings are large. 
Once my parking tickets are paid off and the fear of my car not being where I parked it, I'll definitely be back...

The coffee was hot......
.......
..............
.....

You know that there's something great, or something not so great going on at a restaurant when I immediately log on to review a place.... Any guesses?..... Anybody??
I have never had a tasteless breakfast before in my life... This is actually my third time here in about 10 years... Well, one was under the influence of alcohol, so let's make it two. 
The last time that I was here was for a late lunch. Nice atmosphere. Very clean place and friendly, helpful staff. I don't remember what I had. But I remember leaving disappointed with what I had... Who knows.. It could've just been that I was tired from a long day working. Either way, I was still unimpressed.... This brings me to today's meal. I order coffee, the omelet of the day which was the western omelet. It came with home fries and toast. Still remembering the last meal here, I ordered a side of scrapple as insurance. The omelet comes out just looking sad and dry, and over cooked.. The home fries were cold and dry... Looked as if they were hard enough to use as backgammon pieces... Toast cold, yet burnt...  So I taste the omelet... Then taste it again... After all, this is a $10 meal that I have to pay for.... Nothing but a rubber like texture. No flavor whatsoever... I tried the home fries... Same thing. The coffee was ok. But better could be gotten at Wawa or Heritage's up the street. 
I almost felt bad for telling the woman at the cash register that everything was fine when she asked how was my meal.... What was I supposed to tell her?? I didn't receive bad service... Their food just wasn't good... It isn't like she could fix it...
Anyway.. This review is pretty much just an observation of what I received and paid for. 
I just don't get what people have raved about here
 for decades... I even asked a buddy of mine before I stopped here what he thought of their food... "Good.. Very Good" he said... Maybe he's drinking the Kool-Aid here also... 
I wish these people (and their customers) well.. But I won't be back to waste my money.  
As a matter of fact, I'm gonna add back my alcohol influenced meal here and make it 3 not so great meals.  
Oh yeah.... The desserts looked great on my way out..

BEST. POUNDCAKE. EVER


enough said!

I passed this place yesterday on the way back to work from El Vez. It's been on my mind ever since so I decided to look it up on here and see what kind of reviews there were. Well, I did not expect the uproar of discussions going on involving the owners, bad reviews, etc. Despite this,  I decided to have an open mind and go and check this place out for myself.

The place at first sight is to die for. It's a little girl's dream spot for a tea party - the cupcakes are displayed beautifully in what apears to look like a built in hutch along the side wall. The hutch was not only stocked with snazzy cupcakes but chocolate covered pretzels, chocolate covered peeps and other chocolate covered novelties.

The staff was super friendly. I was told to take my time looking and someone would help me as soon as I was ready. I intended on going in there for 2 cupcakes but ended up walking away with 4. The guy at the counter who helped me who I believe may have been the owner took the time to explain some special instructions for some of the cupcakes I chose and offered me their card. 

I got back to work and couldn't wait to eat one! I went for the Oreo cupcake. Wow, I was in love! The owner gave me a heads up that the cake itself may appear dry but as a fellow baker in my spare time, I know that a cupcake like that is usually on the dryer side. Not so much the case as  took a bite! The chocolate cake was poundcake like in density and the oreo icing was to die for!!! It's taking every ounce of will power that I have not to eat one of the 3 remaining cupcakes I have!

Now many people will argue that $3-4 is rediculous for a cupcake and sure, I could easily create a similar cupcake msyelf as I do bake occasionally but in my opinion, if the cupcake is as good as the one I had today and the whole experience of picking them out and feeling like a little girl again is fulfilled- then it was worth every penny.  It's not like I'm getting them once a week.

Although I haven't sampled every cupcake boutique in the city- the few that I have tried- did not compare to Philly cupcake. Even with the first cupcake I tried- the icing was soft and fluffy, not tasting like a stick of butter.

I'm not sure what to make of the big uproar that happened regarding this place but based on my experience alone and no other influences- I give this place 4 stars and will most definitely be returning!

My favorite pizza place. Love the Wild Garlic pizza with Wild Garlic sauce, mozzarella cheese, chicken, red onions, pepperoncinis, roasted garlic, and grated Parmesan. Served with or without the ranch dressing, it's a hot, garlicky, sumptuous, munch fest. 

The hubs prefers the Everything with Al's tomato sauce, mozzarella cheese, pepperoni, salami, Italian sausage, black olives, mushrooms, tri-color peppers, red onions, and roasted garlic. Happy, contented sounds follow as he enjoys this one. 

I also ordered the individual Caesar salad with crispy romaine hearts, shredded Parmesan, and herbed croutons, tossed with Creamy Caesar. It's big enough for two. Fresh crispy greens and a Caesar dressing that is perfectly spiced.  

Lest I forget, remember to save the crust for dessert.  Dip the ample crust in honey for another taste treat or order one of their knots orders. Either way you will not leave hungry. 

Staff here is friendly and courteous. Fun to chat with while your order is prepared, too. 

***There's also a vast selection of beer for those that like beer with their pizza.

Came to Noble Pie with my friend who raved about this place and I have to say, it was just as awesome as described. We shared a medium pie with some wings on the side plus ordered a few drinks from Pinon next door and it was just perfect!

For the pie, we went with the Steerhead which features housemade meatballs, caramelized onions, olives, bell peppers, garlic, and pecorino. The combination was the perfect bite of sweet, savory, and salty! I also loved that was brought out PIPING hot. If you a gooey cheese lover, you'll LOVE this pie just for that!

When it came to wings, we got a half pound. Ooowhee! Do these pack a punch! Definitely get yourself some dipping sauces to balance it out. Don't worry, there's definitely a generous amount of meat on the wings to rip and dip. We went with the ranch and blue cheese.... unfortunately blue cheese didn't have any blue cheese (like, not even a hint of funk and it was super watery). Ranch was a winner though! 

All in all, Noble/Pinon was an awesome spot to hang out and chill. I loved the ambiance and would definitely recommend a try if you're in Reno!

Cheap. Breakfast for 4 (buns and hot drinks) cost less than $7 TOTAL. 

Buns are located behind the glass casing as per usual and looked pretty appealing. They had a good mix between more American styles (ham and egg) versus Asian styles (pork sung, roasted chestnut, etc). Buns are at room temp though unless delivered fresh from the kitchen.

I thought my salted egg custard bun had all the right flavors but because it wasn't hot, it didn't have the desired runniness. My dad and brother both thought the pork in the pork buns were obnoxiously dyed bright apple red, as we are more used to natural dark red/brown colors at home. Mom remarked that at least the bread was fluffy and soft, as it should be.

Tried an original cheesesteak ("whiz steak, wit") and found the meat to be rather tough and the whiz not generous enough. I actually can't believe that I'm saying the latter cause really, cheese whiz is not something that has been in my realm of food for...a very long time.

Geno's slices their steak long and thin, but if they stick together, as they did on our sandwich, the cheese whiz has a difficult time getting between each slice. This means that you don't really get the right balance between meat and cheese. Overall, it was the least favorite cheesesteak we had while in Philly.

Walking up to Pat's, there's a nice big sign that "teaches" you how to order your cheesesteak. I believe point #4 tells you to go to the back of the line if you do it wrong. I didn't really take the sign seriously, but when I got to the counter and started off by saying "cheesesteak" the guy raised an eyebrow at me like I was speaking a foreign language. I glanced back at the sign and tried again:

"whiz steak...wit?"

"WHIZ STEAK WIT" he nods in approval and becomes more friendly

So given my new found knowledge, I also proceed to order a "provolone steak wit" and he gives me a chuckle and yells "PROVO STEAK WIT". Two sandwiches are wrapped and shoved out the window in record time.

Totally part of the experience.

Upon unwrapping my sandwich, the original looked tantalizing despite it's use of cheese whiz. You could see it hugging ever crevice of chopped steak and onions. It honestly tasted really good despite being really really greasy. In fact, it blew the provo steak out of the water...which was almost disappointing. How did fake cheese beat real cheese? I will not have this!

All in all, Pat's wins second place in our cheesesteak trials.

I cannot tell you how much joy it brought me to see a Pine State Biscuits in Reno! This was definitely one of my favorite spots in Portland so to get one significantly closer is a real treat!

Of course I had to go for the original Reggie and man oh man, was it worth every calorie!

Everything was cooked to perfection from the buttery fluffy biscuit to the perfectly seasoned fried chicken breast. I also liked the the mushroom gravy featured chunks of shitake mushrooms which are much more hearty and flavorful than button mushrooms. This was definitely an improvement compared to what I had years ago in Portland (maybe they also used shitake mushrooms, but it definitely wasn't chunky quarters)!

All in all, Pine State is comfort food supreme and it would absolutely CRUSH on a colder snowy day. If you haven't tried it yet, you have to...at least once! Even though the menu seems heavy, there are some lighter gems too - the cornmeal pancakes were also a fave 9f mine in Portland. I didn't try it in Reno but I will assume it also brings it's goodness here too!

There's just something about soups and curries that always hits the spot on colder nights.

My friend recommended India Kabab & Curry and I have to say, it's pretty great. I went with my favorite paneer korma. I will say that it lacked some of the nice surprises that my all time favorite has (stumbling upon a golden raisin or a cashew here and there is fun!) but it was still on point with flavor! The curry is also velvety smooth and pairs nicely with the basmati and naan.

Speaking of naan -

Hello? Blue cheese naan? Where have you been all my life? It's different and funky but contrasts very nicely with the curries. A surprise hit for sure!

I also tried a bit of my friend's chicken tikka and coconut korma. Both were also quite delightful!

Parking may be a bit confusing - there is a back lot but even Google was very confused getting there. When I finally found it, the tavern's side had clearly marked stalls but India's side was not and seemed very haphazard with cars almost parking wherever there was room. I ended up finding street parking which worked out fine.

I loved our visit to Reading Terminal Market! There is no shortage of things you *want* to try so it's just a matter of figuring out how to try the most of everything. It's concept is very similar to places like Pike Place (Seattle), Grand Central Market (Los Angeles), etc...

Lines for some vendors were certainly much longer than others, but most still moved fairly quickly. Staff at most food stands were also incredibly friendly and willing to chat up locals and tourists alike. Most visitors to Reading Terminal Market are also very friendly - I really only had one passing negative incident where a man pushed me out of his way and into one of the display cases at the Pennsylvania General Store. 

Of all the things we tried, my favorites were easily:

1. Beiler's Donuts: the fritters are a must. We even flew some back across the country to the Bay Area. A little reheating and they were just as fluffy and springy as bought fresh!

2. Herschel's Deli: while the pastrami was good, the corned beef was the real winner. Excellent flavor, stacked nice and high, good slaw. Yum.

3. Carmen's Famous Cheesesteaks: wiz is cool, but I like my real cheese. Their provo sauce is made with a mixture of provolone and cream cheese. Their steak was also of a much better quality than that of Pat's/Geno's.

We also tried:

1. Dutch Eating Place: probably should have gotten something sweet as it seemed like this is what they are really known for but the chicken pot pie was still pretty good.

2. Hunger Burger: fresh lobster mac and cheese came our when we passed by...it was a non-negotiable order at that point.

3. Miller's Twist: I don't know of a baked pretzel I've adored more as of recently...

4. DiNic's: The roast pork was okay, definitely not the best sandwich I've had

This place definitely has great tacos for a great low price! Make sure to check into La Tejana Taqueria from your Yelp app to get a free taco!

The tacos that I got were the Tinga, Chorizo, Campechano, and the Al Pastor.

My favorite taco would have to be the Al Pastor.
My least favorite taco was the Tinga.

First, all of the tacos had a lot of meat and it was definitely well worth the $1.99 for the taco! There are other options on how you can get the meats (tostada, sopes, etc). Second, definitely squeeze the lime and ask for their sauces! They will bring out two sauces if you request it. I forgot to ask what they were made of, but one of the sauces was red and one was green. The red sauce proved to be very spicy for me, but the green sauce was less of a kick. Third, the service was great and they all were very helpful in waiting on us. They took over orders and the food came out very quickly!

Haters gon' hate.

First of all, I'll be completely honest here. I've been avoiding writing a review for a very long time even though I'm a huge fan of this place. Why? Because of all the haters. With PYT, there seems to be a distinct line drawn between most people who've been here: people only love it or hate it. Now, I figure -- haters can just hate it.

There are those that just can't get over what they consider terrible or lousy service. That's fine. They had bad experiences. But guess what? The place has distinctly gotten better over time. Also, another thing that helps me get over the idea of bad service -- servers can be replaced.

What can't be replaced though is the awesomeness and creativity I've seen time and again from Tommy. Every single damned thing on the menu is just phenomenally genius.

I don't even like mushrooms but what ultimately led me to write this review was the Shroom Burger. I was just taking a look at the menu as I'd invited a vegetarian friend to join me there, and the concept of two portabella mushroom sandwiching cheese, and then the whole thing is beer-battered and deep fried and put on a potato roll? HELLO? That concept is worthy of four stars alone.

People like to cry and moan that the damned standard PYT burgers don't come with fries. I can somehow wake up in the morning and get over the fact. Though, to be honest - I'd prefer it fries with my burger but I'm not going to moan about it.

All the food here? Absolutely delicious.

Burger of the Week? Best idea Tommy's come up with since opening the place. I've had the Thanksgiving Turkey Burger, the Blue Cheese Burger, the Tijuana Burger, the Mac 'n Cheese Burger (my fave so far) and tomorrow I'm headed there with a few folks to try out the Cheesesteak Burger on a friggin PRETZEL ROLL.

Genius, pure genius.

So, really this place gets the full five stars on its phenomenal food alone. And honestly, I don't care what anyone has to say about Tommy or PYT's service. If you legitimately voice your complaints calmly and maturely, they will be dealt with in appropriate manner if your experience left more to be desired. That's just the truth. My experiences with the service have maybe one or two times where they kinda sucked out of roughly 30 visits.

Wait, I haven't written about Federal Donuts yet?

That's a crime.

I guess I was too busy eating up their delicious donuts, and most recently, their most-amazing fried chicken. Truth be told, I was a big supporter long before this place ever opened. I'm a big fattycakes and I'm down with whatever food that will proportionally kick my lifespan down a few notches for how good it sounds. That, and an admiration of the most spectacular Felicia whose smile is known to make hearts skip beats. We also can't forget Mike Solo, one of the best chefs that our city has to offer (Zahav is still one of my favorite restaurants), and the Bodhi Coffee folks.

Despite my bias, being a fan of all the respective robot cats that form this sensational restaurant Voltron I can objectively admit that this place blows my mind. I admire the creativity in each one of their products. I will stand by every item I've taken a bite out of. I will even defend the sometimes absurd wait times or unavailability of products at unexpectedly early hours.

It's that good.

The donuts are dense, delicious. I've only had the pomegranate nutella tehina, key lime and indian cinnamon, all of which rocked. The pomnutehina is perhaps my favorite, followed closely by by the indian cinnamon.

Last weekend my girlfriend and I arrived at 11:20-something in order to get a ticket to buy fried chicken at 11:45. We didn't actually walk out of there until 12:00 or so. That's at least a 40min wait for some fried chicken. Worth it? Hell yeah it was. They even came with some plain honey donuts, which were dense and delicious as the others.

We had the harissa and chile-garlic fried chicken. Some of the best fried chicken I've ever had? Yes. Perhaps the best in the city? Could be.

Anyhow, lucky for me (unlucky for my waistband) I live within walking distance. I'm a fan, to say the least.

Uh-oh. I just discovered Suri's last week. And I work at Renown. This combination could be dangerous. We've been two times in as many weeks. 

First of all, it's very pleasant inside. It's clean and minimally but tastefully decorated. And it smells like delicious food. (Spoiler alert: that's because of the delicious food they're making inside.)

I've had the lamb gyro platter both times. Eventually I will try something else but currently I am so hooked on that particular dish that if someone said to me right this minute that I had to pick one thing to eat for the rest of my life, hands down, this is it.
You know what, it just makes sense. It's got meat, vegetables, starches... And garlic. (Garlic is a food group, right?) Also it is absolutely delicious and it's filling and you can even justify that this isn't ruining your diet (that much) so yes, it's ok that I want to go here once a week. YES IT IS. 

My husband had the philly steak wrap and I had a bite and can attest to its amazingness as well. 

They've got Persian tea, which I was unfamiliar with until the nice lady at the register suggested it. Persian tea and I are now planning our wedding. It's good iced or hot. It smells of cardamom and tastes of awesomeness. 

To sum it up: go here. You won't be sad.

Tonight I needed to eat my feelings and they tasted like a bacon cheeseburger. My husband called in an order at Juicy's and I picked it up on the way home. 

The place itself is a little dive-y. Nothing fancy, smells like fries. I didn't have to wait long. The price was reasonable for the size of the burgers and bags of fries.

I burnt my mouth while sneaking fries out of the bag on the way home, so they were super fresh. And oh maaaaan were they good. I usually don't like thick cut fries but these are exceptional. They're very crisp and  taste like rainbows and magic. 

So, I get home, half a bag of fries gone, and we sit down to eat our burgers. So good! Craving completely fulfilled. This was one of the best burgers I've had in a while. The one and only thing I could complain about is that they didn't have pickles. Still though, SO GOOD. I like that they use cheddar cheese. Melty cheddar cheese on a burger is perfection. We all enjoyed our burgers. My  seven year old son... He's a bit of a cheeseburger fanatic and he said I should give it 1,000 stars.

I'd heard much buzz about Trip's Diner for years but have only recently been able to call myself a fan. After a failed attempt a few months ago to dine at their St Pete location (long wait), I was excited to realize Trip's had a newish restaurant in Seminole Heights. Initially, the main draw for me, aside from breakfast, was their dog-friendly covered patio. And now that I've visited a few times, and have tried a few things, I feel comfortable finishing my review. 

We've arrived anywhere between 10am - 1pm on Saturdays, and have never waited for a table outside. Their patio is covered, with a few ceiling fans, and at least 6 tables. Some of the tables seat 6+ people as well. Even late morning in mid-June, I felt comfortable & not sweaty. I really appreciate that dogs are welcome here & bowls are available for water!

While I haven't yet tried lunch or dinner at Trips, their Macaroni & Cheese meal with two sides (collard greens?!), beer selection, and some kind of seafood bisque have caught my eye for future visits. That said, breakfast here (all day, I think) is outstanding! First, I LOVE their cheese grits. I'm not crazy about the home fries, however hubs loves them. And I do want to try them loaded with bacon & cheese. I've enjoyed the Mr Crabs omelet more than once... and I still can't get over how much crab is packed into this omelet, nor how delicious crab is with eggs! I'm also obsessing over Red's Shrimp & Grits. Quite possibly the most perfect of its kind for me; this dish is literally creamy grits, melted cheese & unbreaded fried shrimp, topped with an egg (I loved mine over-easy). And, it was great for lunch at work a couple of days later. Oh, I almost forgot they have mimosas! 

Service has been consistently good at Trip's. Parking seems plentiful & hasn't been an issue on our visits. The bathroom is always clean, with some fun Florida-themed decor/art. We will definitely return to Trip's again, and often!

My only complaint is their west-facing glass (or plexi-glass) garage door allowed the setting sun to blind everyone at our table. PLEASE, Ford's Garage, invest in window tint or a shade! The glare was nearly unbearable, and made conversation uncomfortable & awkward for over a half hour, until the sun dropped behind trees. 

Expecting a group of 15 at 4:30pm on Sunday to celebrate my son's 23rd birthday, I tried to call ahead but their phones were not working on that day. Luckily, as usual, my mom showed up 10-15 minutes before everyone else & the hostess already had her at a table by the time we arrived. Our server John, was outstanding, and easily handled family arriving late and our oddly separated checks. 

To my delight, Ford's Garage serves A LOT of Florida craft beer. As I'd been in Bradenton the day before but couldn't stop in to Motorworks, I was excited to see several of their brews on the tap list. I chose Pulp Friction, their grapefruit IPA, and thoroughly enjoyed it (http://motorworksbrewing.com/pulp-friction-freshly-squeezed-6-packs/). Hubs also brought me a Tequila Sunrise from the bar, which I didn't like, mainly because I don't usually drink tequila. 

I ordered the Jiffy Burger ($12.50), medium-rare, after our server John assured me peanut butter on a burger with bacon & cheese tasted better than it sounded. And, WOW, was he right! I was also happy to substitute white cheddar mashed potatoes for fries... So good! I was able to try the the fries as well, & while they were very good, I thought the portion size was small considering the price of the burgers. For dessert, I ordered funnel cake fries ($5.95), which came with two sauces: raspberry & white chocolate. They were crazy good, and I really couldn't decide which dipping sauce was better! 

I'm so glad Ford's Garage is close to home, as they give us a fresh option for chain-consistent meals. #ProTip: avoid sunset until they resolve that window issue. Their outdoor patio is also on the west side of the building, so I imagine that being similarly unpleasant as the sun goes down. That said, I am curious if their patio is dog-friendly, and I'll update here when I find out.

UPDATE: Yes, Ford's outdoor patio is dog-friendly! (Apologies for not updating this sooner).

We've been here quite a few times since they re-branded to Crabby Bill's, and service still seems to be an issue. I'm not here for a quick meal but I expect to be greeted & find clean tables after previous guests leave. On every visit, we've brought our dog, Gilligan, so we sit outside, and the patio has a fun vibe. We've actually never dined inside here!

Friday nights are brutal, though, and patio tables aren't bussed in any kind of timely fashion. Rather recently, we were waved on to sit anywhere then sat at a table for 20+ minutes before dirty dishes were removed, and another 15+ minutes before our server wiped down 1/3 of the table. And then another length of time passed before she came back to take our food order, after hubs had gone up to the bar to order drinks. By now, these kinds of issues should've been sorted, but evidently have not. That said, all of our servers have been very friendly & personable.

The reason we keep returning, aside from their awesome dog-friendly patio, is the food. Every meal has been incredibly delicious, and I do love their fried fish. Their fries are also tasty. However, my favorite menu item (so far) is their Florida Stone Crab Chowder... sooo good!!! On one of our first visits, hubs' meal was not right but the server replaced it almost immediately & the manager came over later to make sure we were satisfied. I also enjoy their specialty cocktails & find the prices to be reasonable.

In spite of the the table-bussing issues, we've never had to wait for a table outside. Parking isn't terrible, even if it ends up being nearby on the street. We'll definitely continue patronizing Crabby Bill's Off the Hook because its always a fun time with great food & drinks.

Really mixed feelings about this review... 3.5 stars would be more appropriate. I do love small neighborhood cafes! And our meals were delicious & filling! Yet, being warned food service would take an HOUR on a Saturday around noon tells me something has gone awry. Empty tables were plentiful inside & out, and they seemed to be very well-staffed, with no queue to order. Since we weren't in a hurry, we decided to wait it out. I sipped my coffee & caught up on my social media, while hubs enjoyed reading a tbt. Unfortunately, The Grind's free wi-fi doesn't reach outside to their patio tables, as my phone kept trying to connect to Maloney's slightly stronger signal across the street. I ended up having to turn off my wi-fi because neither network was connecting well for me. 

Our meals were brought out in about 45 minutes, so our wait was a bit less than predicted. My Grits Breakfast Bowl was very tasty, and a good size - I almost couldn't finish. But I did have to separately request a spoon... which should have been a no-brainer with their runny grits. Hubs said his omelet was good, but he was disappointed his requested toppings were ON TOP of his eggs, not inside like a typical omelet. I almost wondered if the cook had forgotten to include them. And he had to ask for the side of bacon that he'd ordered. The server requested to see his receipt which sort of felt like she was politely accusing him of possibly lying about the bacon we didn't get. Of course, that's just my interpretation, as she was apologetic & helpful. And she did promptly bring out his bacon once she'd confirmed we had indeed paid for it.

Overall, our meals seemed fairly average, and not quite worthy of such a wait. Also, prices seemed a bit high for breakfast fare, but, this is Westchase. We certainly enjoyed a relaxing early afternoon here, and would probably eat here again if we're in the area on a Saturday morning. But knowing about the potential lengthy wait, this isn't somewhere I'd come for a quick breakfast, and definitely not on a weekday when I have to get to work.

My co-worker & I were moving our office again (2nd time this year if you're keeping track), and found ourselves starving mid-afternoon on a Thursday in May. As my colleague pointed out, one of the best things about working in Tampa is the endless Spanish food options! So we chose The Floridian for lunch on this day, and easily found parking right in front. I later noticed a rear entrance with a ton of parking behind the plaza.

Once inside, we placed our order. We received our beverage cups, filled them and found a table. My chair had crumbs from a previous diner and I brushed them away. We sat for quite a while, and I watched two separate solo customers order & receive their food before ours was ready. This surprised me since it was around 2pm and not a super busy time for lunch. I'd added a tip, which I don't often do before service is complete, and noted that it didn't seem to affect efficiency. 

Slow service aside, our food was really good. I'd ordered the 5" Cuban combo with stuffed potatoes as my side, plus we added deviled crabs to share. Everything was hot & delicious. Note, my Cuban was pressed, and sans lettuce & tomato - exactly how I like it. My co-worker had chosen rice & beans as her side with the same Cuban combo, and she commented that she enjoyed her lunch as well. We will definitely be back!

Skyway Jack's offers a solid breakfast with lots of choices on a big menu. Unfortunately, not everything is made to order. I wanted to try their Breakfast Pie sans onions & green peppers, but was told this item is pre-made & those ingredients could not be removed. Maybe that kind of request doesn't happen often, but I was definitely disappointed.

Although we were told the wait would be 10-15 minutes, we found ourselves waiting more than a half hour for a table on a Saturday after noon in January. Had we agreed to sit at the bar, our wait would've been about 20-25 minutes. Plenty of seating is available outside for those waiting, although it was quite brisk that day & we stalked the inside benches for a warmer spot to wait. 

Our server was efficient and pleasant enough. But since the restaurant was very busy, someone else brought out our food... and the meal I was served was not what I had ordered. After waving down our server, she realized a nearby table had my omelette & I had theirs. She was very apologetic, both while taking away my plate and when she brought my correct omelette. It was just OK... most of my toppings were inside, but some ham & shredded cheddar were on top like toppings and not cooked with the eggs - I wasn't a fan of this presentation. Also, the potatoes were greasy and didn't taste thoroughly cooked.

Now that I've covered what I didn't like, I want to make a point of mentioning what I loved... the excellent grits! They were thick but not dry... almost creamy, but still grits. So good! Their biscuits were also really tasty, and I ate more of mine than I'd expected. I was surprised to see beer is available, but hubs frowned upon my ordering one with breakfast, even though it was after 1pm!

I doubt we'll drive out of our way to visit again, but we do love the kitschy decor & ambiance at Skyway Jack's, so we will definitely return.

On a Saturday night, six of us came here with Downtown Crawlers. As part of a large group, the entire upstairs dining area opposite the stage was reserved for us. The atmosphere here is incredible; it's loud and festive, and so much fun!

Because we had been on the third of three buses to arrive, we were among the last to order, partly because we had to wait more than 10 minutes just to place our order. Our server took our beverage & food orders together, so I thought that would expedite things. When our beers arrived after another 10 minutes, I requested a water at our server's convenience, and that appeared within two minutes. Unfortunately, our food was much less timely. About 30 minutes after ordering, we asked our server where our food was, and he seemed confused that we hadn't already received it. He then tried to blame the kitchen and multiple large parties downstairs for the delay. Most of the rest of our larger group had finished eating and were leaving by this point. About 15 minutes later, we spotted another server, and asked her about our food. Since she hadn't been at our table at all previously, she had no answers. Finally, nearly 50 minutes after ordering, our food arrived, with no explanation nor apology. This was disappointing considering the restaurant is huge, it was a Saturday night, and they knew when our large group would be arriving.

Several of us in our smaller group of six had expressed our frustration with the severe delay in food service to both our server and the other one working our area, so near the end of our meal, a manager came by to discuss the shortcomings.
