After apologizing, he offered all of us a 20% discount on our checks. Personally, I felt this was satisfactory, especially since it applied to our entire check, including our already-discounted .5L beers. And the food was quite delicious!

To start, I ordered Hefe Weizen for me and the Hofbräuhaus Original Lager for hubs, both .5L. Interestingly, I enjoyed the lager better, but both were pretty good. For our meal, we ordered Weisswürste for $13, which was two veal & pork sausages and a pretzel that was fairly large with sweet mustard from Munich. Since we were sharing, I also ordered a side of spätzel for $3 & a bowl of kartoffelsuppe for $6. The spätzel was outstanding, and a good size, although interestingly served in a different dish than my friend who had ordered exactly the same thing at the same time. The kartoffelsuppe had an excellent rich flavor & was also a good size, but I was disappointed to not find any sausage in our serving. The sausage with our Weisswürste were better than I expected; they were in fact quite tasty. The pretzel was good, but almost too salty... and I say that as a salt fiend. But the dough was soft and yummy!

The festive atmosphere is contagious, and in spite of the service issues, we still had a great time. The music was loud but fun, and added to the overall experience. I will definitely return to try other menu items, and more lager, spätzel & kartoffelsuppe.

Mixed thoughts on my experience at Sam's with three of my girlfriends on the last Saturday in February...  for context, our weather has been very hot lately, with comfortable nights in the low 70's. I'll start with the things that are really out of their control, but worth noting so other diners are prepared. First, parking was a challenge! Having never been to Hudson, I circled more than once just to figure out where the public parking was available, then another round and a lot of waiting in line in two different lots before I finally found an open but very tight spot (I found small scuffs & scratches on my door the next morning, possibly from people getting into their car next to me). Then, our wait for a table was nearly an hour and a half (which was not terrible for us; more on that later), but once inside I noticed they really didn't have many tables due to social-distancing. 

Upon joining the wait list & issued a pager, the hostess advised that we could not order drinks while we waited. However, my girl was not accepting that situation on our girls night! After walking through the parking lot toward the beach, she spotted a bus boy and asked him to find a server so we could order drinks. A few minutes later, a friendly server leaned over the railing to get our drink order (no specialty drinks on the sly), and brought them back very quickly with a payment device. We took our adult beverages to a picnic table at the adjacent public park to chat. Time flew by and then we were buzzed.

After we were seated, I had to wander to another part of the restaurant to find the chalkboard list of beers on tap for my beer flight, which wasn't ideal, and then not all were available. One of my friends & I had substituted a side with our meals but we both received the fries AND the grits. Not a big deal, especially since neither of us were charged extra, but noted. Service was relatively slow, but it WAS a Saturday night and we weren't in a rush. The 80's music vibe was great and overall we enjoyed a fun night!

Because of COVID, I'm going to update my review with some current notes. First, let me say that this is still my favorite beach bar restaurant in the Tampa Bay area. My experience last Friday night was hopefully not indicative of normal service going forward. That aside, all staff wore masks & social distancing was evident.

We arrived on Friday evening, 09/25/2020, around 5:30pm. I was disappointed to see they now have parking meters, instead of a guy collecting $10 to park & giving a coupon to be applied toward food & drinks at Caddy's. Also the meter was a bit confusing so we ended up only paying for an hour, thinking we'd just come back & add more money later. After walking in, the hostess offered to seat us inside downstairs. Hubs asked if the upstairs bar area was open - the hostess advised that it was, and we could seat ourselves. 

We went upstairs & realized the slowly setting sun was rather blinding so we found seats straddling a far corner of the bar, quite a distance away from the other groups clustered around the large square bar. Almost immediately, the bartender came over & admonished us about something, though I couldn't quite hear her above the crowd noise & music. Some of the words I heard: she didn't want us to get in trouble, she'd been a bartender for 18 years, and she asked for our drink order. So we kept our masks on until our drinks arrived, because we weren't sure what she'd yelled at us & she hadn't pointed or given any other non-verbal clues. 

Several minutes later, she asked if we wanted anything else so hubs asked if we could get food there or if we had to go downstairs. She said we could get food, so we ordered the grouper nuggets appetizer to split. After our food came, and we'd been eating for a few minutes, she came over & told us that she had gotten in trouble for us eating at the bar and we had to move away from the bar. So we slid our bar stools back just far enough that we could still reach the bar, since we were still eating & drinking. Right about then, the couple on hubs' side, about 8-10 feet away, had left, and the same bartender waved over to a couple of guys that the spot was open & they could move there. Then they ordered some food. Right after the food arrived, she yelled at them about eating at the bar. One of the guys asked to speak to the manager - she pointed across the deck, and he went over to talk to him. Then he came back & continued to eat his food, without moving his stool. A few minutes later, she told us we weren't supposed to be eating at the bar and reiterated that she'd gotten in trouble. We were so confused at that point, and felt very unwelcome, so we asked for a to-go box & our check, and just left. Side note: the women's bathroom smelled horribly, and I informed the manager on our way out.

I've been to Caddy's so many times over the last 30 years that this one experience will not affect my likelihood of visiting again. However, it was uncomfortable enough that I want to warn my fellow Yelpers. Also, it was my birthday, which we never had a chance to mention in any context, but will be memorable. I still don't know if the bartender was having a bad afternoon, or if Caddy's has some rule(s) in place regarding congregating and/or eating around the upstairs bar. The square bar was huge, maybe 20 feet on each side, with at least 7 separate small groups around the bar, all adequately distanced. Our corner was empty, AND IN THE CORNER, 8+ feet away from any other person, so I'm not sure what we did wrong, if anything, but the whole hour there was simply weird and I regretted not sitting downstairs at a table. Those fried grouper nuggets were outstanding, though.

When I was tasked by my boss to find a restaurant in the Westshore area to host a 3-hour lunch meeting for 25 people, I started by emailing several restaurants meeting our criteria. Becky from Brio Tuscan Grille was the first to respond, answering all of my questions almost immediately, and even providing details that I hadn't considered asking about yet. Extras such as a large TV/monitor & WiFi were included for free, unlike other nearby restaurants with similar facilities. We only needed to meet a minimum food & beverage purchase, without any additional equipment fees.

Service was nearly invisible, yet impeccable. I noticed only because the content of our meeting didn't apply to me. A server frequented our room every few minutes, before our buffet lunch was served, to refill water glasses. During lunch, two servers were present throughout to bring sodas & coffees, refill glasses, and clear plates. When I needed to leave early to set-up at the next venue, finalizing payment for our balance was quick & easy.

Our lunch was served buffet-style, at our request, and at the time I specified. The food we chose was plentiful and quite delicious! Becky & her team were very accommodating to meet our ever-changing requirements, and I highly recommend Brio Tuscan Grille for private lunch or dinner meetings.

This is a really big bar, with lots of pool tables & dartboards! On our Friday night visit with my girlfriends & their college-age daughters, we enjoyed reasonably priced cocktails & Bud Light pitchers. Service, however, was marginal.

When we arrived, around 7:30 on a Friday night, we easily found a high-top table near the dartboards, right next to the table my friends' daughters had claimed. After seeing a check-in offer for a free drink (one of my friends installed the Yelp app just to take advantage of this deal), we went to the bar to order our first round of drinks. However, it was nearly a half hour later before a perky gentleman in a nice polo shirt came over to check on us. Upon hearing that we were starving but had not seen a server at our table yet, he seemed genuinely concerned & promised one immediately. And within a few seconds, a server arrived to take our food order. After meeting our server, one of my friends commented that she'd seen her standing near the bathrooms chatting with another server since we'd arrived. Of course, that was disappointing to realize. Once we had our food, our server returned to get a new drink order from us but then we didn't see her for quite some time. Not until the friendly man stopped by again to check on us, after we'd been ready to box up our left-overs & pay for a long while, which we told him, did we then see our server doing her job.

Even incredibly hungry, the food was just OK. My loaded fries weren't very hot, and the fries were soggy. I tasted one of my friend's mozzarella sticks, and it was barely mediocre. My other friend couldn't finish her wrap. Maybe I wasn't drunk enough to appreciate this bar food, and coupled with the service we experienced, I just wasn't impressed.

In spite of all that, the atmosphere here was fun. Plus, the location is decent for those of us that don't live nearby, so it's a good meeting spot. And I may not have emphasized this earlier, but the drinks were GOOD! I'm sure I'll be back, and hopefully I can add more stars to my review.

In the area for a CYE at Scream-A-Geddon, we tried using Yelp to find a restaurant as we drove. Maybe my cell signal is spotty around here, but we passed right by On Q Smokehouse without seeing it on the Yelp map. Since hubs was in the mood for wings, we turned around & headed back. 

Not sure what's cooked in the smokehouse, but nevertheless, I thoroughly enjoyed my meal. We started with a pair of Bud Light bottles and an order of Fried Okra. Our server also brought us Ranch for dipping. First time ever for me, though, I passed on the Ranch and ate those delicious okra pods *plain*. They were sooo good & tasted very fresh!

I ordered the Pulled Pork Sandwich platter, which was served sans sauce & therefore perfect for me. But I also tasted their House,  Mild, & Sweet sauces, and liked each one more than I expected as a non-BBQ enthusiast. Since I'm unappreciative of BBQ sauce flavors, I can not endorse any one of them because each was a bit different, and I don't feel qualified to recommend anything. However, since all of their sauces are available at every table, my opinion is less necessary. You can decide for yourself.

For my sides, I chose Greens and Mac & Cheese. Their collard greens were very crisp & quite good. I loved that they didn't have a sharp spicy bite as many other BBQ places perpetuate. And in that vein, their Mac & Cheese was amazing! Rich & cheesy, with plump pasta and zero heat, it was possibly the tastiest I've ever had; definitely the best Mac & Cheese in recent memory. 

Thanks to Rachel M's review from several years ago, I see their porch is dog-friendly. Unfortunately, we don't get out to this area often, so I'm not sure when I'll have the opportunity to return to On Q Smokehouse. But now that they're on my radar, I'm certainly excited to dine here again as soon as I can!

Drago's has been lauded over many times as the best oysters in NOLA, but I can't say that holds true any longer. The food here is really enjoyable, but I'd argue that it's not a must-visit if you are from out of town!

We ordered a dozen chargrilled oysters, a spinach salad (oddly and fantastically probably the best part of the meal), and alligator tacos. Oysters were doused in so much stuff that it was a little hard to enjoy any oyster since all you could taste was mouthfuls of way too much seasoning and sauce, but hey, I'll eat 'em all since I came to NOLA for chargrilled oysters! (Smoky flavor was nice.)  Alligator tacos had nice flavors, but it's reminiscent of being chewy, overcooked chicken without a distinct flavor.

This place is huge and never seems to stop being busy! Service was sweet with that nice Louisiana hospitality.

A great place to get some consistently good, fast Italian American food.
I think their highest points are the pizza (pepperoni mushroom was great) and the tiramisu. The crust is slightly crisp and nicely chewy. 

Pasta here is a bit less exciting. Of course it's a mass manufactured noodle (the corkscrew one, my favorite), and the basic tomato one isn't very saucy and is a bit watery and bland. Mac and cheese is good, but I'd add a meat topping to it to get more flavor. (Also, a side of their pasta is HUGE.) 

Salads on the menu look delicious, and I'll have to come back for it. As of now, free cookie for Yelp check-in... at least until then run out! Would gladly come back for a quick pizza fix.

The eating environment is cool and the dishes are unique and can be found nowhere else in town. I would try this place if you live in town and it makes a nice date spot if you get the small table by the window looking out at the street. The service is excellent.

Unfortunately the meat here was nearly flavorless. The shrimp is void of any ocean flavor, or really any flavor at all! The tastiest was the bulgogi and only because of the sweet marinade, which isn't even good. Intestine is consistently my favorite meat to order at KBBQ's but this one had a rubbery texture and was literally nearly impossible to chew; I spit it out. Sadly I did not enjoy one meat.

The salad dressing was not tasty. What was it, some soy sauce mixture? It was just pure salty and brown, and lacking in any dimension.

Banchan were okay. I normally ask for seconds of kimchi but ate less than half of the small dish. We also had seaweed salad, sprouts, and mac salad, which has raisins in it.

By far the worst thing....the Korean dumplings...They are cheap frozen gyoza with bland, mushy-paste fillings.

The best thing I ate was the fresh veggies - onions, mushrooms, and zucchini, which we grilled to add some flavor.

As this restaurant has been under three different ownerships lately, it is like a sad joke how dissatisfying the food was. Service was good, but seriously, how do the people behind Kimchi think they can do business here if their food is no better? Because of the expanded menu, which was a total letdown, I was even more disappointed with Kimchi than I was with iGrill. 

Helen D's review is highly questionable. She gives it five stars but two of her comments say that the meats were not tasty, including the shrimp. It doesn't matter if there isn't competition in town, the meats here are inferior for the price.

Renaud's is just about as good as it gets for croissants on the West Coast. They are one of the edible standouts of Santa Barbara.

The almond croissant is the most popular. My favorite though is the apricot, which is slightly less sweet with a plump fruit in the center of a square-shaped flakey pastry. This one in particular lends to a distinct crackling sound when you bite into it because the outer layers are crispy, while the inner layers are light though rich and buttery. And it's composed of dozens and dozens of these paper thin layers. It's a very attractive treat and engages the senses further with the scent of toasted butter. 

The entrees are pretty good, and especially the croque-madame if you like grilled cheese. It's a perennial French favorite with Béchamel sauce, Swiss cheese, ham, and a sunny side up egg on homemade sliced bread. 

For a no-brainer breakfast, get the "Renaud's," which is a croissant of your choice with a seasonal fruit salad and cup of Numi tea or self-serve Peerless coffee. 

Available coffee flavors are organic French Press in decaf or regular, Kona blend, or Mexican.

Other foods here are mostly good, and few things are terrible, like the bran muffins. The salad is organic but clearly isn't a speciality, though it's a good side to cut the fat of a cheese sandwich or sausage.

The folks at Renaud's place detail in the quality and presentation of their foods. Expect a wait in the morning and pastries to be mostly sold out by the afternoon.

"This sucks." I kept saying that the whole meal. And not because of the price or there being small portions; the sizes were comparable to other local restaurants.

First I witnessed much confusion about how to even eat here. Multiple people tried to sit at the bar, but you must first wait in line to sit there. 

We did not enjoy the Hangover Noodles with beef or the Long Tail Boat noodle soup. Neither had a complex taste. The beef was so tough it was tiring to chew. The noodles were all broken into short pieces about the width of my spoon. They were too soft. I don't recommend it at all. The noodle entree was okay, rather bland. More flavorful noodles with more tender meat can be had at Galanga and Your Place.

Did I mention there was a short dark hair with a follicle on it in my soup?

Empty bowl for me was not achieved.

The service was unusually good. The staff prepared a table for us on the back patio because it was crowded Sunday evening. It was quite cold too but the heaters did the trick. The patio was charming with a margarita bar, glowing mason jars hanging from the tree, and pillows in the sitting area.

We only tried the food: Classic 7 Burger for him and Chicken with Waffles for me. Both came with classic fries, which were similar to those of In N Out, but a little crispier with more seasoning. 

The burger was not bad, but it tasted very fatty and went soggy fast because of all the sauce. I preferred it to the chicken and waffles though. The chicken was chicken pieces, void of any flavor other than dry white chicken meat and some bland batter.

If you know Indian food, you will know the food at Tamira is awful and hardly authentic.

You could tell the employees were desperate too because they were trying to persuade a large group of EF International Language students to come in, even though lunch had already officially ended. This made my experience even more pathetic. 

Tandoori chicken was dry and bland, veggie curries lacked flavor, and the naan - We asked for a second helping of the bread, and it was obviously different from the first batch. This one tasted distinctly like Pillsbury dough. It is my suspicion they cut their recipe with the instant dough for whatever lame reason.

It's times like this when I see reviews for Tamira that I seriously question either fake Yelp reviews or the standards for ethnic food from some Santa Barbarians. This place would not fly in San Diego.

The best Indian food in Santa Barbara is at Flavor of India on Upper State, 100% certain on this one. It's not in the main downtown tourist area, but it's worth it to go just a tad farther up the street.

EDIT: Yeah, I just did a quick scan of the Tamira reviews to see a wad of five-star reviews from people who have written only one review. Desperation indeed.

In short, this is a nice addition to IV for quick Asian snacks and boba that's open until 2 am. But it cannot be compared to similar places in LA or even San Diego. Maybe it is better than Hana Kitchen, but not by much.

I had the lychee green tea blend with boba and lychee jellies. My cup had fewer boba pearls than usual, which was disappointing. There were more jellies of a firmer texture. Both the boba and jellies weren't quite the right texture, not dense enough and barely even chewy. Something about my drink tasted dirty too, almost as if it was made with dirty water. I doubt it was, but the flavor was just off. 

Even more difficult to finish was the Hawaiian popcorn chicken. The dish comes with potstickers. There was nothing Hawaiian about the chicken. The pieces were bland and oily, the worst popcorn chicken I've ever had. Maybe try adding some seasoning or basil leaves? Popcorn chicken is sort of a staple at boba places.... Potstickers were tasty, not that you can mess frozen potstickers up. 

My boyfriend was confused when the employee called his order for the chicken and potstickers because they were served in two separate containers. 

I don't like to tear apart businesses, it's just a matter of experience having tried other boba shops that do it better. This is a nice location and students who love boba will continue to come here. But unless the drinks (food would be nice too) improve, then I don't plan on returning. 

On the bright side, the menu board was large and attractive. I like how the top five drink flavors were ranked. We also liked the screen displaying song lyrics. This place has potential and I would return if it improves.

La Pizza, you may be small, but you are mighty. 

Upon pulling up to this storefront my friends joked, "are you sure this is a sit down joint?" but oh is it ever. We were greeted by two chill looking guys who I felt a little bad for--they were working New Years Eve after all. We took a seat and while we decided what we wanted, I enjoyed humming along to some Modest Mouse. 
   My two friends and I decided on a Sausage, Pepperoni, and Green Pepper concoction that would keep us happy all through the wee hours of ringing in the new year. My friend Joe was feeling extra hungry and said we needed the 18'....so we did.....and we were brought face to face with what I can only call mammoth pizza. Mammoth Pizza made my jaw drop. Not only from it's large circumference but also from the taste---yum. yum. Yumyumyum. 
      I had 2 slices (which was honestly impressive) of this New York Style pie and couldn't handle any more, but it was oh so good. Groan worthy for sure. And I enjoyed an empty little restaurant that I still got to watch get tons of take out traffic. 

This is a spot not to be overlooked!

Quaint and Quality are two words I can use to describe this little gem. 

      With an Ernies Blues martini and a Screaming Bloody Maria cocktail under my belt, I was loving the vibe and the chalkboard wall sections of this little spot. It's the perfect spot for a friendly group gathering or a laid back choice for a date night. The martini I had was strong but delicious, with blueberry infused vodka and a blueberry nestled in the bottom of your glass, it was classy and just the right amount of sweet. The Screaming Bloody Maria was in a class all its own. I never thought I could be intimated by a name, but this one got me. I debated for a good thirty minutes whether I was ready to take this drink on, but once it hit my lips I was screaming praises. The Bloody Mary's spicy sister was a hot, tasty choice. 

   I also tried their Ernesto's Flatbread while I was there and I can't rave about this enough. Firstly, if something has figs or goat cheese--I'm sold. But something with figs AND goat cheese? Say no more. It also had a balsamic reduction, olives, and spinach which really complimented one another and made for a fresh, filling snack. 

   Another thing I want to note is that the bartender, who was waiting on our group of about 12, was extremely attentive, funny, oh, and when I closed out? He remembered my name--well played, bartender, well played.

      I can't wait to bring my friends here to try even more (ehem--everything) off their menu!

I have been whisked away!

    This new, aqua-accented addition to Cherokee Street couldn't be more precious. There's a small couch area in the front by the open window that is perfect for relaxing or studying, and several tables that are just as cheerful with their vintage feel.When you walk in you are greeted by the owners with their enthusiastic "Welcome" mixed with the mismatched thrifty decor (probably a blend of the owner's creativeness and Cherokee's Antique Row finds---like the "How to Eat A Lobster" platter or the "My First Mitt" picture frame that houses a well-worn pink oven mitt) that make you feel all warm and fuzzy inside. But not as warm and fuzzy as after you take a bite of one of Whisk's baked goods. 

     There's a chalkboard menu on the right wall that tells you the prices of the goods they will be dishing out, along with the beverages (like tea and hot chocolate!) Going up to the counter, there are whisk shaped lights, a shelf full of colorful cookbooks and adorable vintage cake pans hung on the wall...seriously, I could suffocate in all the cuteness. I decided I couldn't pass up the "Cinnamon Pumpkin Cupcake"--I mean, how could I? And my friend decided to try the "Double Vanilla Cupcake"...naturally we split them down the middle so we could double our taste testing. 

   We paid (when you use a credit card you use an iPad--LOVE IT) after talking to the owner for a few minutes (she also went to SLU and was an English major...she's basically me in the future) and then settled down at a cheerful yellow table to dig in to our sweets. The vanilla cupcake is indescribable. I don't know what they put in to their icing (hearts, stars, and unicorns? Crack? I'm not sure) but it was truly the most delicious icing--so smooth and creamy, that I've possibly ever tasted. It wasn't overwhelmingly sweet and didn't take over the vanilla of the cupcake, they just melted together in to a perfectly delicious little morsel. Then, on to the pumpkin cupcake. After that existential experience with the vanilla half, I could hardly wait. I bit down in to the pumpkin and flavor bursted merrily on my taste buds. The cinnamon was perfect, matched in the icing (different from the vanilla icing, but still good) and the pumpkin cupcake was cake-y, spiced greatness. They definitely know how to dish up some absolutely delicious baked goods, and the best part is that they are sustainably created. They offer vegan and gluten free options and I really love that aspect, I can't wait to try more! 

  With this only being their second day of full businesshood, I am so impressed and excited to go back and tell every single person ever about this spot!

Want to really put the fat not only in Fat Tuesday but every day of the week?

Come to Mother's. Mother makes over 30,000 pounds of homemade sausage a year, over 150,000 lbs of ham and roast beef, and serves over 1500 gallons of creole mustard annually. Ah yes.

Mothers will take care of you like a mama should.  She may not be sweet or smile, but when you come a crawlin' on Ash Wednesday, Mother will be there to nurse you with whichever food cures your hangover. I like a simple bowl of seafood gumbo-I know it's strange at a place reputed to make the world's best baked ham, but it's an excellent gumbo and doesn't make me feel like I'm going to balloon up and deprive my brethren of oxygen.

Happy Mardi Gras! Wish I were here!

This is simply the Best Japanese food in ALL OF NEW ORLEANS. I've been going here for the past 17 years. I always make it a point to come here when I'm in town. I never skip the crunchy roll, hibachi fried rice, broccoli salad, and omakase if I'm in the mood to indulge

I'm usually an adventurous eater, and have tried even the strangest menu items here, but I always have the crunchy roll - it is seriously the best.  

The sushi chefs are beyond amazing, especially if you are considering the Omakase -- just remember to call the day before if you are planning to do the omakase.

If you're looking to save money? Try the hibachi during lunch! But DO NOT skip the hibachi rice. I have never found a better fried rice, even after living many years abroad -- for there is truly nothing that compares to Shogun! Maybe that's nostalgia speaking, but that hibachi rice is killin' :). 

One of my favorite to-go orders is salmon sashimi, hibachi fried rice and crunchy roll. Tip: eat salmon sashimi with hibachi rice = buttery goodness

First and foremost... if you get a chance to try this place out ask for the waitress Lindsey... cute, friendly, and attentive.

This is one of the better places I've tried recently.  They offer really good Italian dishes.  I had the Pork Oso Bucco... it was really, really good.  The shank is served upright so everyone in the whole place is looking at you when it's served.  Yeah... see that tower of pork... that's all mine.  

I have to digress a bit... my dining experience was muddled by a barking dog at the next table over.  Yeah... one of those little lap dogs.  The family on the patio thought it was appropriate to bring it to dinner.  And sit it on a chair.  And feed it stuff off their plates every time it yipped.  My rules for dogs and kids in restaurants are the same. If your little creatures can't behave themselves then take them to the park, not a restaurant.  I don't want to hear your dog yipping any more than I want to hear your kid screaming.  What are you thinking.

Now if your youngins or pets keep to themselves and act respectable, I'm all good.

The table with the pup ran out of scraps.  I swear it was eyeing up my pork shank.  I really wanted to drop kick it like Jack Black does to Baxter in Anchorman.

The food is really good here.  Service was great.  And the ambiance minus yippie skippy was open and relaxing.

Oh... and they have a lot reserved for dining patrons... a great thing for those of you that hate parking in the Loop.

First let me say, the area around Crestwood Mall is depressing. It's like a different world now. Most of the well known businesses have moved out. Poor Crestwood. We've got to do something with this area. 

There's a new plaza across from the mall in which San Jose is located. PLENTY of parking as there are only a handful of open businesses here. It's a newer building and inside is bright, with more of a southwest feel than Mexican flair. We were seated at a booth by a window. I like the way they set up the place. There are more booths than tables which gives each table a more intimate feel. 

The salsa is definitely hand made and good. It was a little mild for me so they brought me a different hotter version. We started with cheese dip. Nothing special... but it was good. For entrees, I had the Pollo Guadalajara. This was a chicken dish with chorizo and a side of beans. The flavor of the meat was awesome... although a bit greasy. The beans were average. I also tried a few bites of my girlfriend's tilapia dinner. The fish was very flavorful and topped with a white cheese sauce. It was equally as good. Hers was served with rice and vegetables. The top-shelf margarita was great. The sopapilla with ice cream was ok. 

Overall, the main dish items were very good, but the sides were sub-par. 

Service was very, very good. I didn't get his name but he offered his suggestions, was always around but never intrusive, and was super nice. 

Value was awesome. An appetizer, two entrees, drinks for two and dessert was $35. 

A couple of negatives... 

The first vegetable we bit into was still frozen. Obviously their veggies aren't fresh, and in this instance weren't prepared correctly. 

The rice and beans were just average.... and maybe I'm spoiled but I expect each Mexican main plate to have both, not one or the other.

India's Kitchen is easy to miss.  It's nondescript from the outside and in a strip mall next to the Uncle Sam's military surplus store just down from Uncle Bill's.  Inside is nice.  The tables are all set with silverware, stemware and tablecloths.  But last night when we walked in, there was only one other table seated in the place when we entered.  

Service, was decent... with one annoying flaw.  Three different employees waited on us... one lady and two older dudes.  Both of the guys mumbled, and even continued talking to us as they were walking away.  It was hard enough figuring out what they were saying through their accents, but the mush-mouth dictation was frustrating.  I just shook my head yes every time as they walked away.  For all I know, they could be saying, "Do you like to have sex with goats, and eat piles of poo?".

The girlfriend and I ordered beef samosas to start.  They were handmade, and good.  Flaky crust and a hint of sweetness in the meat.  That's one fun thing about eating Indian food... they use spices that you can't quite identify.  We followed the appetizer order with the #10 feast for two.  Go ahead and judge.  Only a glutton would order a dish called Feast for Two AND and appetizer.  Whatever, this is my review not yours.

The 'feast' consisted of Tandoori chicken, Chicken Tikka, Shrimp Tandoori, Sheesh Kebab, Lamb Curry, Vegetable Korma, naan, a boatload of rice, two desserts, and coffee.  All this for $37.  It was monstrous.  We were sitting at a booth for four and our table was FULL.  Which got me thinking, they should offer this item as a novelty.  If there is any way one person could eat all of this, they should get it free.  The two of us hadn't eaten all day and I don't think we made it through half of it.

Anyway.... all the items were good... but the veggie Korma was awesome.  This creamy pink broth was so yummy.  It had hints of coconut milk, almonds, and cashews.  I would order this one by itself next time.   After dinner we were served some rice pudding mixture that reminded me of horchata, and little pancake balls covered in honey.  They were interesting, but I doubt I'd order either if it wasn't included in the feast.

Value - great
Food - good
Service - decent... but get ready to play a game of 'what the hell is he saying'

This is wildly off the mark if you are expecting Mexican street tacos.  Also, if you're expecting to choose from an eclectic menu, you'll be let down.

Fort Taco serves two things... tacos and enchiladas.  And they're both odd.  

Their taco is similar to a Taco Bell chalupa... or a puffy taco if you've ever had one of those.  Basically it's a fried shell, much thicker than a traditional taco, stuffed with seasoned beef, lettuce, tomatoes, and cheddar cheese.  It wasn't what I was expecting, but I liked it. 

The enchilada is even more off the wall...  it didn't have any meat... it too is stuffed full but have you ever eaten an enchilada with potatoes and peas?  That's what this is.  It was filling.  And oddly good.

One taco ($4) and one enchilada ($3) would fill anyone up just fine.  The food here would be great for a hangover.  

Totally not what I was expecting, but I like they they are unique.

The food here was pretty good.  We were next door watching the US Womens soccer game and decided to take advantage of The Dam's delivery option to Amsterdam Tavern.  

But unfortunately a good product was turned sour by a single employee's rudeness.  I hate to give such a poor rating when the food and service up to that point was fine, but unfortunately one event can ruin a good experience.  

The Dam was busy.  We waited in line for 10 minutes before being able to order food.  There were probably about 20 people in line.  The cooks were busy in back, and the lady taking orders was pleasant with everyone.  While we were there the counter lady's family came in, unaware of the soccer game next door.  They were hoping to grab a bite, but due to the crowds decided it was better to move on.  We ordered 3 sandwiches... an "eye opener" burger with chili and a fried egg, The Dam burger on sourdough, and a "mean green" garden burger.  For sides we had fries and asparagus tempura.  We paid and were handed a number card and told that the food would be delivered next door.  The order came to ~$45 including tip.  

The food came within about 15 minutes.  There is a lady that carrys all the food across on cafeteria trays and calls out your name or number so she can find you.  She dropped our three burgers and fries off without any napkins, ketchup or forks.  I walked over next door and asked for the items at the counter from our delivery girl. 

All three burgers were good... a little greasy, but Damn good.  ;)

My wife joined us towards the end of the game and asked about food.  I walked her over to show her the ordering process.  We followed the same delivery girl and when she noticed we were following her in she told us they were closed.  I asked if the Imo's across the street delivers and instead of any normal human gesture, she shut the door in my wife's face and flipped the open sign to closed.  I walked back to Amsterdam frustrated and confused about why this employee chose to be this rude.  I decided to head back and ask. 

It was 8:58... I found out after a quick check online that they advertise that they close at 9pm.  I totally understand turning away a customer this close to closing.  But I still was angry about the attitude.  As I reached for the door the same delivery lady was coming out.  I held the door open as she was carring food and as she came outside I asked why she shut the door in our face rather than just politely handling the situation.  She blew up.  Then I told her that I didn't appreciate her bitchy attitute.  Probably not a great choice of words, but I was pissed.  

Realizing that I wasn't going to get anywhere with this person, I joined my friends back at Amsterdam.  I noticed that the next few orders were delivered by a kitchen employee or manager rather than the delivery lady we dealt with who had been delivering food up until then.  

And then the kicker, 5-10 minutes went by and the Amsterdam bartender yelled "last call" if anyone wants to order food from the Dam.  WTF.  

I really hate to give a place a one star review.  I understand that negative reviews can dissuade others.  I have over 1,100 reviews and less than 3% are one star.  And if you are reading this far, you should know that I have no problems with the ordering process, the food, or any of the other employees.  In fact, I would suggested that you visit if you are in the mood for a good, greasy burger.  But I'm sure the owner/management would like to know that this single employee is killing you... I can only assume that others have experienced her attitude as my interaction with her came unprovoked.  And I'm sure you would have been just upset if a door was slammed in your own face.

Before Zaatar moved, it was a nice, quick place for take-out at reasonable prices. I'm so sad for their changes. Since they have moved, they hiked up the prices about 10-20%. See my photo with the sharpie marks all over the menu for the differences. The Yelpers that are posting that they have the same prices are unfortunately mistaken. The owners probably need to pay their rent for the bigger building so it's understandable. However, I probably won't be visiting anymore because last time I placed an order to go, they told me 20 minutes. It ended up being over an hour wait, and I missed an appointment because of it.

If you wrap up everything I hate about Awfulstin, TX into one restaurant, it would be Mopho.

They get an extra star because they carry Bud Light.  I only ordered it so I could snobbily be told "we don't carry Bud Light" but was shocked when the waitress returned with a cold BL.

I searched the menu for 15 minutes trying to find something to eat...

This "Asian inspired" restaurant is the brainchild of owner/chef Michael Gulotta.  Formerly chef de cuisine at Restaurant August.  If his name does not sound very Asian, that's because he is not.

This might help to explain why every ingredient has been hand selected with the utmost douchebagery.  Instead of a lamb dish, he instead offers "A slow roast lamb neck with smoked tofu and creole cream chese roti".  I think I gagged a little just reading most of the descriptions.  How about some lamb lardo with your Pepper Jelly Crusted Braised Cedar Key Clams.  Seriously?  Yes, seriously.

To begin, we shared an order of the wings and the crispy fried P&J Oysters.  The oysters tasted like any other fried oysters in New Orleans with a dipping sauce so nothing to write about.  The wings were horrible.  The chickens they come from  must be genetically mutated (or in the case of hipsterness, they were probably hand raised by a Brooklyn transplant living in the Bywater who raises chickens in his backyard).  They are HUGE.  HUGE is not a good thing in a chicken wing.  I've microwaved better wings that you buy frozen from Friday's.

As an entree, I ended up ordering the grilled jumbo shrimp over the popcorn rice (with much customization).  Actually all five of us ordered the grilled jumbo shrimp over popcorn rice because no one wanted anything else on the menu....

To be fair, the grilled shrimp over popcorn rice wasn't bad.  The popcorn rice was perfectly cooked and quite delicious.

If only the place didn't have to try so damn hard to be a pretentious, foodie, douchebag, hipster, foodspotting, mixology hell hole I'm sure Mr. Gulotta is a talented chef with creative ideas.

For those who wait in line to eat at Mopho, you can have it.

Friendly Staff, Beautiful Location...plenty of outdoor seating, which made me feel comfortable! I'm thinking I didn't order well...maybe the seafood is the way to go. I ordered the tri-tip sandwich. The tri-tip was tough and seasoned with a bunch of garlic salt.  I tried a small piece of fish from the Fish and Chips, which seems like something I would enjoy more.  The buttered bread from my sandwich didn't taste like anything. I'll try them again, and try the seafood next time, because I really love this location!

California Pasta is located in the heart of downtown Santa Barbara within Paseo Nuevo mall. It's a more casual downtown restaurant without the crazy downtown prices. Locals, nearby workers and tourists can all enjoy delicious and garlicky pasta dishes here! Come hungry, or you can make your order 2 meals because portions are generous too, which I appreciate! Zucchini noodles or regular pasta are both available. There is nice outdoor seating for people watching, or take the piping hot food somewhere beautiful in Santa Barbara. I almost forgot about this restaurant during Covid, but remembered them yesterday! The Cajun Shrimp Pasta was delicious, and shrimp was soo good. I also like the Seafood Pasta here. Your meal will always come with a yummy piece of garlic bread as well. Enjoy!!

Rusty's you can do better! We are very loyal customers, and pizza was burnt tonight. One employee was making the pizzas. I think that worker needs more help on a Friday night! In the last year, multiple locations have given me burnt pizzas. What is going on? Our family member who picked up the pizza observed that multiple pizzas were coming out burnt tonight. That's not ok! Give your pizza maker some backup,  and give them incentives to be motivated at all locations.

We ordered recently for dinner. The portions were generous, which I thought was appropriate for the price paid. We ordered the Vegetable Fried Rice, Kung Pao Shrimp/Spicy, Cashew Nut Chicken and Cream Cheese Wonton. I thought the veggie fried rice had good flavor, and it looked like it was made with care. My Kung Pao Shrimp needed more spice and garlic, but the shrimp portion was generous! I didn't try the Cashew Nut Chicken, but I'm told it had good flavor. The Cream Cheese Wonton were good, we would have liked a little scallion or crab mixed with cream cheese. Our order was takeout, and as I checked the order, a lot of liquid fell out. Maybe better containers can be used for takeout? *I miss the previous owner and old Red Pepper, but will try this new version of Red Pepper again!

We were in Old Town Goleta and smelled the aroma of The Original (the first) Hamburger Habit. The aroma was enticing, and caused us to crave burgers from this location. This is the first location my mother brought me to as a kid.  She always loved getting the steak sandwich and ate it with little yellow chilies. Seating at this location is all outdoor patio seating, with some heaters to keep you warm. I ordered a Double Char with cheese and Chili-Cheese fries. The original location is the only location where one can get a Chili Burger or Chili-Cheese fries. I had my chili fries with those cute little yellow chilis, and all that was missing were some delicious white, raw onions on my fries. At first I looked at the fries, which appeared over overcooked and lukewarm (which I dislike). The chili seemed lukewarm as well. When I combined them however, they were perfect and hit the spot!! I was totally craving chili cheese fries. The patties on the burger initially seemed overcooked, but the burger was delicious and also hit the spot! The burger had delicious shredded lettuce, and yummy tomatoes. I put the residual mayo lettuce on top of my fries, and it was great! If you're craving a burger, try the first Hamburger Habit location in Old Town Goleta!!

Chubbie Burger is a nostalgic treat. They have definitely been around since my childhood. Once upon a time they had a downtown location, along with the current location on De La Vina. They are pretty yummy. On certain days, I order my burger with grilled and raw onions for fun! Yesterday, I ordered my fries "light," and they came out perfect. Burgers come with mayo, lettuce, tomato, onion and pickle. The Chubbie Burger comes with double meat and cheese. Try the Chubbie Combo if you're super hungry. The meat quality seems a bit better than In and Out. Enjoy! (They have shakes too)

Fun Meal for takeout! The rolls were beautifully made and fancy. The rolls we ordered honestly looked like unique works of art to me (nicely presented!) The Mexican Roll reminded me of a California Roll, with a Tempura crunch. This roll had a nice and subtle spicy sauce, and can easily be a meal for one person. We shared the Snake Roll, which had a sweet sauce, avocado and delicious Eel on top! I heard the Hawaiian Roll was good as well. The Hawaiian Roll also had a sweet sauce. The Mexican Roll was filling, while the Snake Roll was lighter but still filling and satisfying in it's own way. It was nice to try a new Japanese restaurant. I recommend the yummy and beautifully presented rolls!

Lunch until 4 pm is offered!! Are you looking for kind customer service and a delicious lunch? Then come to Mandarin Palace! The man who took my order was very nice, and our food was hot and tasted good. It's great to grab your food to go, and take it home or to a park. We each ordered the Cashew Nut Chicken, but there are MANY options for you! Enjoy a flavorful Chinese-American style lunch (or dinner).

Healthy? Not really.
Bomb af? Hell yeah.

We pit stopped in Indianapolis during our Thanksgiving weekend road trip and stumbled upon The Eagle after wandering the nearby area. The two things we had to try here... The fried chicken and the mac n cheese! Both definitely I would say lived up to the hype. Be sure to put a healthy amount of that signature spicy honey all over that crispy fried chicken.

We did also try the chopped salad to kinda balance things out. The figs in the salad were a unique touch and overall a really great salad as well. They do have a nice selection of local beers on tap, so be on the look out for that. All in all, I'd say this one's an excellent Sunday brunch spot.

'Til next time, cheers!

321/365

Great experience! 

We were doing some shopping in the area and found this great restaurant on a quiet Tuesday night for dinner thanks to Yelp! Atmosphere is classy, intimate and comfortable. They have a large cozy bar and many oversized booths. Good setup for groups.

The service was impeccable from start to finish. We were warmly greeted and our server came by multiple times to check in on us. They even pack up your leftover food for you and kindly offered extra rice at no charge!

The menu was extensive and can be quite overwhelming. Everything sounded so good! We were given complimentary bread chips with an array of 4 chutneys. We ended up sharing an appetizer of meat samosas which was a tad dry but quickly remedied with the delicious chutney. For our entree, we ended up sharing the Tandoori Mixed Grill platter from the charcoal fired Tandoori Oven including Tandoori Chicken, Chicken Tikka, Seekh Kabab, Malai Kabab, Tandoori Prawn, Served with Rice, Raita and Naan Bread. The meats were impressively served on a hot slab covered with foil. The soup, naan, rice and sweet rice dessert were all delicious. Some of the grilled meats could have been a tad dry but most were flavorful and delicious! Portion was also very plentiful and we left with a ton of leftovers.

Overall, great experience and I would recommend to any Indian food lover! Can't wait to come back to try more entrees and even check out the lunch buffet!

the older woman that worked there (the owner maybe?) was incredibly rude and made us feel so uncomfortable and unwelcome. my friends and i (3 latinas) went there after our breakfast to get some coffee and study, and so when we walked in i was holding my brown paper bag full of our breakfast leftovers and we went to try to find a seat in the back. i was going to go put my stuff down and get settled in before i got up to go get my coffee, but not even 5 minutes after we walked in the lady came up to us and said "i noticed you brought food in from outside, i hope you still intend to support our business and get a drink," automatically assuming that me and my friends weren't going to buy anything. i politely replied "yes i'm going to buy something i just wanted to put my stuff down first" and she left. i got up to buy something, feeling pressured to at that point. also, me and my 2 other friends were sitting at one small table and we had books and our laptops out so obviously we were very squished, and we noticed that the table next to us (who had been there longer than we had) had pushed together two tables even though they also were only 3 people. Me and my friends decided to do the same, assuming this was not a big deal. 5 minutes later the same woman came outside and told us we had to move the table back so that other people could sit, and she turned to go back inside without saying anything to the table next to us who were doing the same thing, and who were also white. we pointed this out to her and she simple said she hadn't noticed, even though the other group had been there much longer than we had. we found it interesting how it only bothered her when we did it. overall, a very bad experience and i will not be returning.

So Many Bad Reviews? I personally found that all of the BAD Reviews are mostly Legit!. 

This place should be famous for serving Way-Overpriced Portions of Uninspired Cuisine by a Waitstaff that would rather be somewhere else.  

Add one side-item, a cup of coffee plus tax & tip to your Breakfast Entree and you can expect to pay between $25 & $33 per person... for a half decent, small-portioned Breakfast!   

$18 FOR FRENCH TOAST? ($14 menu price plus 9% tax & a 17% tip: rounds up to around $18 and I just can't see this entire plate costing them more than 85 cents in total food cost, plus or minus 15 cents).  The texture of the french toast was a bit weird with mush bananas and the Rum-flavored syrup had little flavor. I saw $10 sandwiches that came with a side dish that had more sustenance than the $18 French Toast. French Toast is Cheap (bread, milk, egg, butter, banana & syrup), for $20, you can serve French Toast to a lot of people at home. 

The Hamburger was a disaster. The bun was overly crisp & dry to the point that it was difficult to eat. While trying to fit the burger in my mouth, the unseasoned hamburger patty fell apart into about 9 pieces. I had to eat it with a fork... pathetic!  The shoestrings Fries were good!  

My biggest turn-off about the Menu here is the constant repeat of the word "Shane-Made" as a combination spin off of the Chef's first name and the word "homemade" or "housemade". This was more annoying than it was cute. The Chef Owner's EGO seems to be larger than his ability to serve a decent, fair cuisine at a reasonable price. "Shanemade" has become our new word to describe a Restaurant's Cuisine that is Highly Overpriced and Underwhelming. 

Upon reading Chef Shane's Bio on his website, I learned that he had previously worked as a head chef under Emeril, but, on his own, he seems that he lacks the business knowledge and self-discipline to run an effective restaurant. Then I decided to Google 'Shane Pritchett' and learned from a (NOLA dot com) article that he and his wife were running a 'Ponzi Scheme' out of their Magazine Street Interiors Shop. These are NOT Good & Honest People look it up and decide for yourself. AVOID THIS PLACE.

I very surprised that this restaurant has very low rating reviews went the food is so amazing maybe it is because it is a bit price. The decoration is seen like you are in the vibe of the Caribbean. 

Crab and Curry Fried Rice a REEF original long grain rice, lump crab meat, stir-fried with brunoise vegetables and steeped in crab stock infused with curry and coconut essence. The rice has a bit spicy taste which gives it an authentic flavor and super tasty, the amount of food is pretty big enough to feed two people but the price is a bit too much for only rice which seafood. 

The staff is pretty good, and they have a full bar and a few tvs, the place is pretty big. 

Another plus is located in a good area of Philly. A bad is that a bit to the price but maybe is the price to be in that location.

I have been here twice and both occasions I have been disappointed in the food in both the quality and the quantity.  Let me start saying that went I order the basil mix chicken and shrimp and didn't want to have white rice, I ask if I could have more vegetal instead, the answer of the server was I am not the chef. Kind of rude, but I let it slide. My food came with tom yum chicken soup, which had no taste and was cold worse I had tasted.

Went my main course arrived, I saw that my petition was denied and that not even that, the amount of shrimp was very minimal, and the portion of the vegetable was less than my friends. I ended not eating the dish because I was very disappointed with the food and service that I received. I highly recommended not to eat here or make any request because like the service told me "I am not the chef".

My friends and I, made a quick pix stop in this Dinner. Hank's serves diner-style food, but a bit  little less greasy, they have a good selection on their menu,  I order the 10 oz. charbroiled chopped sirloin steak, made with choice lean hamburger and charbroiled to your liking, server with French fries or home fries, the meat patty charbroiled  It's  a simple burger that just tastes incredible!  And their fries have a good taste. The servers, they were very efficient, they were on top of the table with water and coffee.

I will stop again if I near the area, to explorer more the menu.

One of my go to go bars while I was working on a project in PA, the staff are very friendly, and their beers selection is one of the best I have seen in that area.  Millers must have the best happy hours in this town, 10PM-12am while offering a good special every day of the week. 

Some option of food is delicious and the half price of the happy hour make it better, I will recommend getting the buffalo shrimp and calamari but the French fries are not good don't get it, but they also have a good variety of others plates. 

PS. I recommend looking at the bill first before paying sometimes staff forget to add the happy hours special.

Visited Sunday 9-2-12

The food was great, unfortunately our waitress, Ana, went on a lunch break immediately after serving us. She was sitting behind a propped up tray where the staff pick up the food. Licking her fingers, talking on the phone, getting herself refills.

We had to ask other wait staff for refills (5 min after running out of our drinks)and then we had to ask for our check. Other customers had to walk to the kitchen to give their check and order dessert. She pointed to another staff member who had to finish the woman's transaction and help her order dessert to go.

Then when she brought the ticket and asked how her service was "now that shes off break" we said it was great other than feeling ignored. Then she proceeded to argue that she deserved a break and it was a team effort. Then she came back again and tried to argue that she's sorry we felt that way.

Update. So Needless to say, we did not leave a tip. But, the waitress or someone else at the restaurant seemed to sense it warranted a tip. After we put a zero on the receipt, I balanced my checkbook the other day, someone gave her a tip. We tried to call the restaurant on 9/8/12 at about 8pm the phone was busy for at least an hour. So we called on Sunday 9/9/12 and we asked to talk to the owner, we were told they were not there, so the manager, Katie, said that was already processed. Hello....someone stole from us. So we pushed a bit, and were told we could come pick up the $2. Hello...you have an employee stealing, if they steal from one customer are they stealing from others or the business. We pushed a bit more and she offered a $10 gift card. Heck no we aren't coming back. 

Not once did she offer to look into it or apologize. So we did not take her up on it. Instead we called our bank, now they will take care of it. At the very least we will get our $2 back. At the worst, the credit card processing company will investigate for theft. We obviously won't be told. But be wary of this place.

I wish Nam Son's banh mi were a person so I could fly it to Las Vegas and marry it. Is it legal to have an actual husband and a Vietnamese sandwich husband? I sure hope so.

I honestly don't think you can go wrong with any of their options. You could pretty much put a sweaty gym sock in between that fantastic, crusty roll and still have your socks knocked off (pun intended). And don't discount the tofu! I, and my carnivorous actual husband, both preferred it to the BBQ chicken, which was also extremely tasty.

Other things you need to know:

1. Come hungry! Banh mi isn't the only thing you're gonna want to get yourself into. Seriously. That whole counter of delicacies. All the drinks. And don't even get me started on the items in the refrigerated area.

2. Come prepared to get it to go. It was not at all crowded when we went on a Saturday afternoon, but there are only like two tables. And if this place's Best of Philly shout out is any indication of future popularity, those seats probably won't be available when your banh mi craving hits.

3. Stop your Tindering now, you've just found your life partner. Better get your Elvis suit and Vegas flights ready.*

*No, you cannot make the Vietnamese coffee your maid of honor. Thanks TSA.

Let's taco bout Heffe baby. Let's taco bout you and me...

On second thought, let's just talk about me. Because if we talk about you too, I'm just going to have to wait longer in line for those yummy tacos. And no one should get in the way of me and tacos. Luckily, I visited on a cold, rainy night so the crowd was minimal with plenty of covered seating compared to the tales I've heard.

Now onto the tacos (because you know the taco emoji is in my most frequently used section)...

The kraken is everything. And definitely "doesn't suck." Octo can be hit or miss and this was a hit all the way.  The chimichurri and the spicy tomato jam were lovely flavor accompaniments.

Sadly, I can't speak to anything else on the menu due to an aggressive night of taco debauchery elsewhere, but the Tijuana Poutine and Willie Make Burrito have my name all over them on another night.

So should you go to Heffe? Yes. Today if possible (unless of course today is a day that I will be there).

"I'm in town. Want to grab dinner?"

"Well I just had two drinks and split two apps, an entrée and a dessert, so I'm not really hungry."

"So you want to do the 8-course tasting menu at High Street?"

"YES!"

This will go down as both my best and worst decision all wrapped into one.  I left this meal so full that I couldn't even stand up straight.  When I got home, I'm fairly certain my dog thought this was the last night we would spend together on account of my incessant "WHYYYYY?"s I continued to utter into the wee hours.  But on that note... I'd do it all over again.  I'd do it without hesitating. Because YOLO... or something like that.

So I thought their brunch was good (it is), but their dinner.  Good god.  I kept waiting for one of the eight courses to be a dud.  But everything was a 9 or 10.  My tastebuds died and went to heaven that night.  The highlight for me was when the fried zucchini came out topped with my beloved chow chow (see previous review). Be still my heart!  For $45, this was a steal.

So my takeaways from this experience?
1. I will never be a championship food eater.
2. There is a reason Bon Apetit Mag made High Street the #2 best new restaurant.
3. My dog has no faith in me.

Get the carrots!  These are not the "Have you ever seen a rabbit wearing glasses? No?  Well then finish your carrots or you don't get dessert!" carrots from your youth.  These are the kind of carrots that once finished, you shed a small tear because you think the deliciousness is over...

...but it's not!  Of the small plates, the beets and the sweet potato are also quite lovely.

Medium plates?  Octo all the way!  I wanted to take a bath in that congee.

Large plates?  If you are deciding between the pork shoulder and the lamb, go pork shoulder.  It was incredible and I found the lamb to be a bit dry in some areas.

Dessert?  Despite finishing (read: devouring) my carrots, I didn't get there *sad face* Maybe next time (and there will be a next time).

Let me start off by saying if you're planning a trip to Hollyhock Hill you're probably at home watching Matlock or Murder She Wrote instead of perusing Yelp for reviews.... but I will write this none the less.

My family and I have been going to Hollyhock Hill for YEARS for family dinners celebrating special occasions. I can remember going as a child and being in awe of all the twinkle lights at Christmas time, enjoying the delicious food, and old fashioned family bonding experiences.

That will NEVER happen again.

My family of 5 went last night to celebrate my grandmother's 87th birthday. We even drove from Ohio and made a reservation especially at Hollyhock for this occasion.

Our waitress (Sherry) was wonderful. Even though she said she had only been there a short time, she was attentive, polite, and wonderfully caring.

The food itself is generally the same. Great fried chicken, delicious sides, and what you would come to expect from this Indy staple.

I would also like to add that in years past, the sides were plentiful and you got PLENTY of food for your party. Last night, we asked for more sides as the dishes brought out were not nearly large enough to serve 5. The second round were drastically smaller. Come on y'all. I shop at Kroger.... I know how much a pound of potatoes and canned corn cost. At $20 a person... there is still plenty of profit to be made. My husband ordered the shrimp and received 6 breaded shrimp for $23. WHAT?! Yeah... that's not a typo. 

The real problem lies with the new management (or possibly, new owners).

The woman who seemed to be a helicopter manager, started the evening by directly coming over to our table prior to ordering and corrected Sherry about what "family style" meant right in front of us. Very unprofessional. 

We ordered 5 dinners, drinks, and an extra side. We asked that our waitress take back the Mac and cheese. After which, helicopter manager came over and interrogated us as to why we sent the Mac and cheese back. We informed her it simply wasn't good. She then further asked what specifically made it not "good." Now, if she was asking to perhaps make a better product, I get it. But the reason she asked was to see if we were "trying to pull a fast one and get some free noodles." This was made apparent when she asked if we were still taking the side home with us. I informed her we told the waitress that we didn't want to take it home.

Now, knowing we are a party of 5... ordered alcoholic beverages, and take home sides already... one familiar with the menu would know our bill was well over $150. Do you really think I'm trying to pull a fast one and get some free $1 a box spiral noodles? NO. The side just plain sucked.

Never in my life have I been interrogated like that by a restaurant. I felt like I did something wrong. A manager should NEVER make a customer feel like that. It was just unbelievable.

Also, I'm sure that since you're such a helicopter manager, you probably stalk Yelp and other websites to see the reviews. So, yeah, you made our experience pretty crappy. I understand you're trying to run a restaurant and make a profit... but you seriously need to get a grip. 

So, if you want a dining experience with good food... and are willing to put up with a Spanish Inquisition during your meal... go here!

If not, Indy has so many other options to make your family gathering just as memorable.

And that's all I have to say about that.

Serious disappointment! cockroaches in the room! Front Desk service was similar to the airport TSA uninterested. I asked for an upgrade and was told not going to happen, yet the folks next to me were told, many cancellations due to the storm and we have plenty of rooms available, interesting....... When I pressed for the upgrade again I was told to check back tomorrow, I did first thing and the same uninterested person said the same, not going to happen.

I must add that the location was perfect and the Acura car service was great.

Oh and the restaurant no longer exists and was told I could have menu's to restaurants that deliver if interested! I would have stayed some place else had I known this in advance so I asked why this is not told at the time the reservation was made, they said well you have to click here then click someplace else and your right its not very easy on the website to get that information.
Bad service, bad food, bad beer selection, bad liqour selection. Tried it a couple times. Never again, don't waste your time
Amazing food... Great customer service... This was my first time trying Lees but I Will definitely be back... Nothing like delicious food and great service

I like to think that I have a good heart. I'm a self proclaimed nice girl who has been known to walk thousands of miles to raise awareness for cancer, help dust kids off when they fall at the playground, I recycle, and I sing in the church choir. There isn't the tiniest bit of frost to hint at my having an icy heart, but I have to say that if I keep eating here my heart is going to melt away to nothing and that leaves me in quite a stupor. 

Last night I found myself once again in the Sycamore dining room in almost the exact same seat in which I sat months prior on my first visit. Once again I was surrounded by some of my best friends though this time around it was a group who put their trust in me to take them away from their safe bubble of Center City restaurants. To them the suburbs are uncharted territory, Regional Rail is a foreign vessel transporting them to lands unknown, and Sycamore is just a tree. I think I made adventurers out of them, with the help of Sam and his kitchen staff of course, as they surrendered their zip code and culinary limitations to the Wednesday night prix fixe.

I could go on for days about the amazing food that was prepared for our table, but that would only provoke jealousy and rage by those who were unable to attend my little birthday soirée. I will say without going into much detail that we were spoiled (in no particular order) with the riches of prosciutto wrapped rabbit loin, braised beef short ribs, wild boar shoulder, sea scallops with a pear chutney, sweet potato gnocchi with sage brown butter,  twice fried poussin with corn bread and bacon loaded collards, lobster bisque, a fully loaded charcuterie plate, a perfectly selected artisinal cheese plate, lobster welsh rarebit (from which I was awarded a history lesson from my fellow diners), the famous wild mushrooms on toast, an amoretto cookie crumble topped butternut squash bake that I promise tasted like heaven and though I was told by our waitress that this was not dessert can attest that I would eat it for breakfast, lunch, dinner, dessert, and as snacks in between every day. Just when we wanted to raise the white flag of defeat and say enough is enough, dessert was laid out and again we were plowing our way through sticky toffee pudding, chocolate cake, bread pudding, and sweet little salted chocolate cookies.

I've said it in the past, but really there is no other word for this restaurant except for charming. Whether it is the warm and cozy interior, always smiling waitstaff, or the ever accomodating and friendly chef who makes his way out of the kitchen to socialize with the nights visitors, the combination will have you feeling so at home that a birthday dinner meant to only last two hours had us relaxing at our table for almost three and a half before we realized we needed to catch the train back to the city. 

With many accolades to its name including making it to the Diner's Choice Top 100 restaurants in America by Open Table, Best of Philly top new restaurants in 2010, the top 30 of 50 restaurants you should be eating right now by Philly Mag in 2011, and the fact that Craig LaBan actually had positive words on the restaurant which solidly confirms what dozens of amateur critics on Yelp are raving about, it's no wonder the first recommendation to anyone asking for a quiet BYO is Sycamore.

Man what an awesome place! From the moment I walked in I was greeted with a friendly welcome. The servers behind the counter are so helpful and kind. They don't rush you and because they knew I was new they explained the menu and told me I could try anything from the menu before I order. Then at the table the manager came by to make sure everything was alright, and she continued to almost every table. It's so refreshing to receive such wonderful service. 
I went with the brisket sandwich and a side of coleslaw. I am so pleased to say the brisket was cooked to perfection. The bark was all kinds of greatness! The brisket was tender and not too dry. It had just the perfect amount of fat too. The coleslaw was also great because it wasn't drenched in mayo like most places. It was fresh and went nicely with the brisket. 
The brisket, along with all the meat and food are cooked on the spot. The brisket is also smoked in house. Nothing is frozen or microwaved. You're really in for a treat when you go in to Mission. I'm so happy that I live so close. I can't wait to go back again!

Oh, R.T. Weilers. 

If you were only your food, I'd give you 5-stars. Your burgers are divine. Quite possibly the best I've had in St. Charles. Certainly any burger on your menu is ten times better than any 12 dollar pre-formed patty from Llewellyn's across the way. I go out of my way to get people to get your burgers. You also have a great beer selection, which is nice to see in Old Town St. Charles.

But! 

There's a problem we need to talk about, R.T. 

No, no, it's not the noise. I know you're a bar. When I made the mistake of bringing the family there for lunch on St. Patrick's day, and there was a drunken ten-top molesting each other and having a yelling contest, I thought, "Hey, that's my fault. Lesson learned." 

It's not the dog bowls, either. I get it. It's your schtick. Good on ya.

It's your service, R.T. Your service has been abhorrent since the first time I entered your doors after you took the building over from Kriegers (which, coincidentally, had the exact opposite problem). /If/ there happens to be a hostess on duty, I still end up waiting an unimaginable amount of time to be greeted by a server (who always seems upset that I've shown up). Same interminable wait to get the first beverage round. Eventually, by the time I get to order my food (Any burger and homemade chips, delicious!), I'm so hungry that I feel like I need an appetizer, but I'm afraid I'll have to eat my main course for tomorrow's breakfast at your glacial pace of delivery. 

Also, why are your servers so very surly? I just don't understand? Actually, let me rephrase that.  Why do your servers treat me like I sat down and told them that I would not tip them unless they ignored me and imitated an alcohol poisoning victim? Seriously, R.T. perhaps your waitstaff should enter a 12-step program...

...or at least crack open a customer service pamphlet.

Wow, this is an easy one. Five big ol' stars for a super tasty dinner in a wonderfully laid back atmosphere. Let me borrow from Yelper Extraordinaire Richard R. to continue (imitation = the sincerest form of flattery, RR!)...

THE SCENE

My friends and I had just taken a transcontinental flight from snowy Seattle to steamy South Florider, and once we dumped our stuff at the hotel, we went out in search of some local eats. We were hungry like the wolf...runnin' on empty...Starvin' like Marvin...and [record scratch] we got to some highly recommended restaurants near the touristy area along the water but found them all slammed full and not a parking space in sight. 

Fortunately, the trusty and intrepid Yelp app led us away from the madness to Bodega, where parking was easy to find and the brightly lit, rustic little restaurant welcomed us to its walk-up window. Though there was seating available on the sidewalk, there were lots of folks waiting for take-out orders and everyone was relaxed and happy and enjoying the warm evening. Things were looking good. 

THE MENU

Bodega serves Cuban-style street food (or so I must assume, having never actually set foot upon, nor eaten food upon a street in Cuba). They do sandwiches or platos (a main plus rice, black beans, slaw, and plantains), and they have various sides plus fresh juices and booze. The sandwiches and mains are primarily of the chicken/pork/beef variety, but for the veggie types they also have tofu and tempeh offerings, which may be all vegan...? They were out of tofu on this night, so I hungry-hungry-hippo'ed me a tempeh plate along with an unsweetened tea.

THE FOOD

Our very cool and friendly server brought out our dishes; I don't even know what my two friends ordered because I basically just went face-first into my amazing tempeh plate. The tempeh was nicely grilled and lightly seasoned, and was nested happily on a bed of sweet but tangy slaw; the beans and rice were perfect in every respect; and the plantains made me hear angels singing. There was also a lime wedge, and a half of a red chile pepper in the mix. Over the sound of my own ravenous eating, I heard my friends offer some vague warning that the chile was hot. "Mmmf," I replied. I took a bite of the end of mine, and it was fine, a little kick but fine. Took another bite a while later, still fine. Took a third bite, and by then I was getting up to the seeds, and my brain briefly melted. Fortunately, all of the other goodies on the plate helped to fight back the heat.

FINAL THOUGHTS

I would eat here all of the time if I lived in this area. The food is filling and delicious and seems to be made in a very healthy way, not a lot of fat or sugar. The people who work here are fantastically nice and chill, and you can tell that they know they're making their customers happy, and are proud of it. The atmosphere of the walk-up window and the low-tech sidewalk dining is perfect. I hope to come back while I'm in town and have some of the tofu and wash it down with a Michelada.

5 stars all the way.

Racist assholes. If it wasn't for tourist these bitches would be broke. I hope they get shutdown rude and obnoxious. I'm sure if these bitches were in NY shit won't be going like that with all these racist signs. Since were best known as the melting pot. I drove from Brooklyn for this shit hole I'm sure fucking eating cat food would of been better worst money I've ever spent. Fuck Gino's these fake Italians and fuck ya weak ass steak. I would've got better steak at "Home Depot".

The Worker Bee Cafe is a family-run restaurant in the heart of Carpenteria, with a nice relaxing country feel. The decor of bee's makes the restaurant look cluttered, however the good food and friendly service is what makes this spot A-ok to patron. 

For brunch, I ordered the Bee Keepers Delight-- French toast, choice of 2 bacon -or- 2 sausage, with 1 egg and a side order of Hash browns. My meal was served nice n' hot, portions were large, coffee touch-ups were not neglected! 

Just like Carp, this cafe is kick back, a nice place to enjoy your breakfast, brunch or lunch.

My favorite late night spot! This place is so good and makes my mouth water just thinking about the food. I've ordered food from here twice and both times the food has been amazing as well as the service. The first time I placed a to go order and got the dragon noodles with chicken and my boyfriend ordered the teriyaki chicken. The dragon noodles were so soft and tender and had a great flavor, they add siracha sauce on the side for an extra kick. 

The second time, we actually visited the spot. It was difficult to find since it's by the horses on earl warren show grounds. We called to get directions since gps isn't very helpful. There's a sign right outside with the SB munchiez logo on it. It's a nice little hidden spot. The staff was very nice and made our food fairly promptly. Two words: FRIED RAVIOLI. I've never tried fried ravioli and boy was I missing out. The ravioli was super crunchy, cheesy and delicious. I'd recommend this place to anyone looking for a yummy late night bite!

Wonderful experience here!  Came in with my son for a 5pm reservation.  They seated us upon arrival even though we were early.  The places is cozy and fun - very speakeasy.  Nice spot to grab dinner or just drink and snacks and not too noisy.  The staff are friendly, helpful, attentive, and knowledgeable about the menu.  Parking wasn't an issue - there's a lot half a block away.  

Absolutely get the Charlie's Sliders and the potato croquettes.  They were the stars.  The gnocchi was good, and the pickled root veg weren't anything to write home about.  For dessert we shared the raspberry creme brûlée and the chocolate pudding.  The creme brûlée was ok - the pudding was INCREDIBLE.  

Will definitely return to try other things!  Thanks for a wonderful dining experience.

I am officially in love with Doormet!  This is a perfect example of why I'm so glad that I frequently use Yelp.  I have driven by here literally hundreds of times and had absolutely no idea that this business even existed (and it has been here for years!).  I saw a review of Doormet on Yelp and knew that I had to try it.  

Doormet offers delicious gourmet food for dine-in, take-out, or delivery.  It was actually hard for me to find the first time.  It's on the side of a strip mall not visible from Dale Mabry.
