If you're dining in you place your order at the counter and they will bring it out to you shortly.  There are a good number of tables inside and a few outside.  The first time I went I tried the pizza and thought that it was very good.  The second trip is when I really started to appreciate how special Doormet is.  I had the chicken piccata and I literally cannot remember the last time that I had something so delicious.  It was off the charts fantastic.  And I can get this type of food delivered to me?  Pinch me, I must be dreaming.  I have yet to try anything that I didn't like.  The rustico sandwich was also wonderful.  The fresh focaccia bread was top notch and tasted so good with the pesto and balsamic that was added to it.  My half a sandwich had a generous amount of meat on it.  That and a hearty soup made me completely full.

They have several items that they temporarily add to the menu as monthly specials.  This can be great for trying new things but could be heartbreaking if you really like one of them because it won't last long.  Enjoy it while you can!

The only (minor) complaint that I have is that the pasta dishes are a little pricey for a lunch ($15).  However, the chicken piccata I had was so good I will definitely be splurging on it once in a while.

I consider Doormet a hidden gem that I'm glad that I found.

Brace yourself because this is going to be one strange review.  Despite some complaints I have (one serious) I still love 4 Rivers.  It's understandable why there is always a full line (sometimes out the door) whenever I come here.  Those people that are repeat customers have the chance to earn free food from their loyalty program, which is much appreciated.  

I feel that since this is a BBQ place that most reviews are going to concentrate on the meat (duh!).  Since I'm not a big meat eater (although theirs is excellent) I'm going to turn the spotlight on the sides and desserts.  Still with me?  

mac n cheese - Definitely not the best mac n cheese I've had but it's the best mac n cheese I've had from a BBQ place.  Does that make sense?
4R BBQ Beans - Love them.  Just love them.  Exactly how I like beans.
John's potato salad - Not bad but nothing remarkable.
coleslaw - See potato salad.
smokehouse corn - They add tomato and other flavoring to it.  Quite delicious.
bread pudding - They actually have two flavors that they rotate.  One is bananas foster and the other is made with Krispy Kreme donuts.  KRISPY KREME DONUTS.  I'll save some of this for a second day and heat it up. One of my new favorite desserts.
sweet potato casserole - Good but I have an issue with it.  (Oh the suspense)

When I heard that 4R had a "Sweet Shop" I just assumed it was a place you could get some cookies or soft serve ice cream.  I wasn't expecting a full-blown bakery that produces such a variety of desserts.  If you look at all of the pictures I've posted it really shows the impressive variety of treats they have.  It seems like every time I come in I spot something new to take a picture of.  If you like a flavor of cake there is a chance they also make it in a "bomb" (mousse inside) or as a cupcake.  My two favorites are the grasshopper (complete with thin mint cookie on top) cake and vanilla bean cake.  I'm not a big vanilla guy but this cake could convert me.  As good as the desserts are I've been frustrated with quality issues.  Several times I've gotten home and realized that the dessert I got had been sitting out on display for too long and was getting stale.  It's quite frustrating when that happens.  When their desserts are fresh they are fantastic!

As for my other complaints I do not like the seating arrangements.  Most people have to sit at very long community tables.  I am just not a fan of sitting elbow to elbow with strangers as I eat.  I don't mind eating off of paper on a tray, but I don't like how empty paper is put on the trays and then the trays are stacked up.  So the dirty tray bottom that has touched who knows what is rubbing on the clean paper.  Ugh.  I also wish that they were open later.  Eight pm seems like such an early time for a restaurant this popular to close.  Thankfully they're open later on Friday and Saturday.

My big complaint revolves around a little red symbol.  On my second or third visit I was trying to decide what side I was going to try.  I noticed the little red peanut symbol by the sweet potato casserole but didn't pay much attention to it.  I eat peanuts all the time and enjoy eating sweet potato dishes.  It was good and I ate my serving pretty quickly.  Not much later I realized that I was having an allergic reaction.  It was one worse than I've ever had.  I was completely bewildered as to what was happening.  The nurse I dealt with seemed convinced it was a food allergy.  I couldn't understand how that could be until I remembered that little red peanut symbol.  When I looked it up on the website I learned that it was a generic nut warning.  There were no peanuts in the dish.  They were tree nuts, which I am allergic to.  I accept that it is mostly my fault that I didn't investigate what that symbol meant.  I still don't think I was off base for thinking that a peanut symbol meant peanuts.  That mistake cost me 2  1/2 days of misery and ruined a family holiday for me. I wish that they would change it to a "N!" for "Nuts" or "A!" for "Allergen".  If this would have happened on my first visit I never would have come back.  I warily returned and have been fine ever since.  They had me at "Krispy Kreme bread pudding".

I love finding places to eat through Yelp.  Sometimes it's by searching, sometimes it's by places they've featured, but sometimes it's just as simple as seeing a Yelp friend check in to a place over and over again (Hi Jerry!). I've had Flying With Jerome bookmarked for so long but it's located at what I politely call "the other side of the world". I finally decided to make the hour drive to try it.  You just don't expect to find a stellar French bakery in an older strip mall next to a laundry service, but that is the case here.  I can confidently say I never would have found this place in a million years on my own. It was interesting to read the background of the owner. He's been a pastry chef in the French military and around the world. I purposely didn't look at the beautiful treats in the display case too much because as a dessert fiend that's all I would focus on. We were able to sample both the French toast and the waffles, both of which had fruit scattered amongst the servings.  It was a delicious breakfast! 

As for the desserts there was an overwhelming amount to choose from. There were tarts, cakes, macaroons, brownies, donuts, flan, croissants, etc. I ended up with a chocolate eclair and it was wonderful. In probably the most tragic mistake of the year we forgot to buy any desserts to take with us. That gives me the excuse to make the drive to the other side of the world to come back here again.

I had been following the progress of Hiccups before the pandemic. I even stopped by there and peeked into the windows one time to try and see how construction was going. The combo of boba tea, churros, pho, and other savory dishes sounded like heaven to me! I felt so bad for them having to deal with opening during a pandemic. I'm glad that they were eventually able to open and have found success in doing so. The biggest surprise with the savory dishes was the garlic noodles. I never would have thought to pair parmesan cheese with stir-fry noodles but the combination totally works. The pad see ew was pretty good also. I ordered a churro but didn't try it because of a problem with the packaging on my delivery order. I've been told that won't happen again and that's good enough for me. I'll try one when I visit in person eventually.

I loved my dinner from Las Palmas so much I went back for dinner the very next day! I got something different and loved it just as much. My eyes almost popped out of my head when I bit into their cuban sandwich.  The bread had the perfect amount of crunch to it and the meats were so flavorful.  It wasn't surprising for me to learn Las Palmas had been winners at the cuban sandwich festival. This is my favorite cuban in Tampa now. The next night I got the grilled chicken and it was so delicious. The man that was helping me was really attentive and even brought me some dipping sauce he thought would go good with my plantains I ordered.  I think he was the owner and was such a nice person. For dessert I had a guava pastry.  Next time I'm going to sample their decadent looking chocolate cake they have in the display case. Las Palmas puts the "hidden" in hidden gem. I had trouble finding it even when I knew where it was.  When you pull into the strip mall off of Bruce B Downs you'll be looking at a row of businesses that have a gym and a grocery store.  What you're looking for is the other row of businesses that will be behind you.  That's where they are. This is a new location for them and although it is small it looks wonderful. I can't believe that this amazing cuban food has been around here (in another location) for quite a while and I didn't realize it.  I will be coming back again and again.

I had a rocky first visit here but the ice cream was good. I love ice cream and had really been looking forward to trying out Astro Ice Cream. They've set up a cute little storefront near Hemingway's in Armature Works' Heights Public Market. I would recommend that they put up signs describing their different flavors and also what types of cones they offer.  There were four different types of cones on display (including a red one!). I assumed I would be asked if I wanted one but that didn't happen when I ordered and I forgot all about it. A cup of ice cream it was then! Since they didn't have signs up you had to decide what you wanted when you got to the front. This is important because this isn't a place that you walk up and look and the tubs of different flavors.  The ice cream is flash frozen with liquid nitrogen in front of you.

I was in line with fellow frozen sugar addict Brett N.  Apparently Brett gets "deer in the headlights" syndrome when faced with choosing his frozen sugar. I actually moved in front of him because I know that chocolate mint is the greatest flavor of all time.  I ordered the "flying saucer" off of the menu, which is mint ice cream, chocolate chips, chocolate crumbles, chocolate syrup, andes mints, and mint leaves.  After a while longer Brett finally ordered something. I was surprised when his order came out before mine. We waited, and waited, and waited some more. I waited so long at one point Brett went back to our group and I was the only customer standing there. When I was finally about to ask if they had forgotten me they handed me my cup of ice cream. I was a little frustrated because at this point it was pretty melted. At the time I had never had ice cream made with liquid nitrogen before so I didn't know if this was normal or not.  Now that I've been to another place like this in California I know that it is not. 

The ice cream combination actually was quite good.  I understand they're a new business and they'll probably get more efficient with orders.  I'll definitely want to try some more flavors upon future visits to Armature Works. But with a cup of ice cream costing me $9.10 it would have to be a rare treat instead of a regular occurrence.

There is a new chick in town and I hope that she stays around for a long time. I liked this franchise way better than I thought that I would. I was expecting a small place that only does take out because who builds a restaurant around chicken salad? Well, apparently they do! Not only do they have a good amount of seating, but there's also a private room in the back. A lot of the menu selections are off-limits to me because I have a nut allergy but that's not a big deal because I already found "my flavor". "Olivia's old south" has egg and sweet pickles in it and is simply delicious. I like getting the special called "the original chick". It contains a scoop (or sandwich), a pickle spear, a side item, and a cookie. 

A lot of really smart design decisions are in play here. There's a long, comfortable bench for you to sit on if you are waiting for a to go order. They've also got an app that you can use to scan a QR code on your receipt in order to accumulate reward points. Thanks to the bonus for signing up after two visits I've already accumulated almost 50 points. When I get to 100 I'll get a free small cooler! On my first visit the owner stopped by our table to talk to us and was friendly and engaging.

In a humorous way they play up the feminine side of this restaurant.  In the men's room there's even a sign that thanks you for putting up with it.  As a guy I have no hesitation about coming here. I'm able to get a big scoop of tasty protein with some fresh fruit on the side. As far as I'm concerned this is a rock solid lunch choice. I'm happy they've extended their weekday closing time to 8pm.

Sept 2017 update: I hate doing this because the people are so nice and I love their chicken salad but I'm dropping my review to a four. They used to have a rotating selection of cookies that ranged from "great" to "I can't eat this because I'm allergic to it (nuts)".  I absolutely loved their snickerdoodle and lemon cookies.  The chocolate chip wasn't half bad. Even better was the fact that they were huge.  After a menu change they now have switched to a single flavor of a single tiny cookie covered in frosting.  Anyone that knows me knows that I love dessert and I simply can't stand these new cookies.  They taste like you're eating a pound of sugar.  They're just way too sweet.  Even worse, these tiny cookies came with a price increase. You can ask for "The Chick" to not include a cookie but it doesn't lower the price.  I wish corporate HQ would reverse this decision.

I can't express how excited I am that the owners of Yummy House decided to open a Chinese bakery in the USF area. I don't know how we got so lucky because their restaurants aren't anywhere near this area. Not that I'm complaining because I'll be able to go to this bakery all the time! This place is a food photographer's dream. When you walk in there are multiple display cases holding the most beautiful pastries and buns. They also sell cooked items behind the counter. You can look up on the menu boards to see what they currently offer. So far my absolute favorite pastry has been a sweet bun that's filled with Bavarian cream. I swear I could hear angels singing the first time I bit into one. My other favorite is the "sponge cake crumble bun" that has sponge cake, sweet milk cheese, jam, and powdered sugar. I tried a good variety of the desserts and they all ranged from great to good. The only one that I absolutely did not like was a packaged cake slice with four different colored squares. Considering how many desserts I've tried that's great odds. I still need to try their refrigerated desserts, such as mango pudding. They have savory items in the display cases ranging from BBQ pork to chicken sausage in buns, croissants, etc. I was surprised what a great value everything is. The buns and desserts are usually around $2. If you get a soup it's less than $8 and you get a great portion of noodles and meat. If I was to offer some constructive criticism I found it strange that they had chicken listed as a topping you could get for noodle dishes, but when I tried to order it they told me they didn't have it and erased it from the menu board in front of me. They didn't have it the next time I visited either. That's the topping I would have wanted the most. Also, at many Chinese places you have the option of getting shrimp or pork wonton. Many people don't like one or the other but here you have to get them combined, which I don't like. These are minor quibbles though and overall I think this place is wonderful. I may or may not have visited five or six times during their first week. I will be coming here regularly without question.

Went for Mother's Day- The hostess (the older one) was quite rude about the fact that we did not have a reservation.  Over 30% of the restaurant was empty.
We sat down and were greeted immediately.  It took 10 minutes to get 3 waters and 1 mimosa.  We were then told about the buffet. That was the las time we saw our waitress.  
The food was boring and cold.  The dishes sat on our table and I was not able to order another drink until a half hour passed.
We presented a Restaurants.com Gift Certificate and were told that it would not be honored because it was Mother's Day.  The waitress said that it was not in the writing on the ad or the email or any terms of use, but it was still not honored.

Will not go back!

When we first walked in we thought the place looked great, somebody obviously spent a lot of time to make the place feel welcoming and they succeeded there... That was where our pleasant experience ended.

We go and sit at the bar, first thing we see is the bartender pouring unused shots back into a tequila bottle. As if this first impression wasn't bad enough we waited about 10 minutes for her to come over and acknowledge us. Clearly pouring the shots back was a higher priority.

When we finally had our order taken, we ordered a simple side of guacamole and some chicken fajitas. Somebody bought us out the usual complementary chips and salsa.

The guacamole came out not long after but was pretty bland so I asked (more like shouted across the bar as it was the only way to get our shot pouring back into the bottle bartenders attention) for a couple of pieces of lime to liven it up.

I nearly fell off my chair when she told us it was $1 for slices of lime, anyway we went along with it since were trying to salvage our night.

Fajitas came out... Beens looked and tasted like they were from a can, the rice was overcooked and mushy, the chicken was ok but who can mess up chicken. No cheese, and servings of guacamole and sour cream so small, you could barely even make fajitas out of them.

Anyway, after forcing our way through the rest of the dining experience, and waiting what seemed like yet another excruciating amount of time for our check from an increasingly unfriendly (back pouring) bartender, we got our check.

At this point I was thinking in the back of my head "I always tip 20% but this might be one of the 5 times in my life I might actually not do that, maybe I will leave 10% and that would be generous relative to our experience"...

On our check it seemed unusually high so I start to tally it up ... On top of our food (including $1 lime slices) they actually charged for the "free" chips and salsa ($3) and, get this... They added a mandatory 18% service charge.

Then it dawns on me, their service is so bad that even they know they completely suck... Their only remedy is to force their customers tip. If that doesn't speak volumes I don't know what does.

I live less than a mile from this restaurant and will never spend a dime there again.

Do yourselves a favor, don't waste your time here. It was laughably pathetic... There are many other great restaurants in town that will appreciate your business.

The Rusty Nail is my go-to neighborhood bar.  The staff is friendly (what's up, Lee!?), the scotch selection is great, and the patio is amazing.  It also doesn't hurt that it is walking distance from my apartment...

I have taken my parents, coworkers, and out-of-town friends here, and everyone has enjoyed themselves.  The patio is key for nice warm NOLA evenings!  And, you can bet the televisions are playing the relevant sporting events of the day...  The crowd is chill but diverse:  I can come in dressed up or down and yet not feel out of place.  And a food truck parked outside!?!


All in all:  solid.  Rusty nail, don't ever change.

PS-  the Movember mustache competition is some of the best fun I have had in New Orleans to date.

From everything that I've heard and read, Donatello's runs hot and cold. My experience was atrocious, this is coming from someone that occasionally worries that his reviews are generous. 

To start, my mother and I walked in for dinner one night. Donatello's was vacant aside from one younger man, facing away from the door, playing on a tablet or something. We didn't know if he was an employee or not so for a solid minute we stood, not sure what to do, gazing around. Finally, I said, "Excuse me...?" to which he startled and turned around. 
"Oh... Are you here to eat?" He asked.
"Yes, but when do you close? We don't want to keep you open." I said. 
He told us that they were open for another hour and a half so we sat down. A woman came out to serve us, we discovered later that she is the owner. We ordered an appetizer of the cheese ravioli. It didn't suck but it didn't blow either of us away, which it should at least come close to for an Italian restaurant's pasta dish. It was smothered in a cheese sauce that was almost gritty. 

Now to entrees... My mom's pasta bolognese was pretty inedible. The sauce was decent but the pasta crunched in your mouth, obviously undercooked. The owner was unfazed when she was told that no, my mom wouldn't like to take home three quarters of the portion. 

What I ordered was a filet mignon with a garlic and shallot butter. What I received was a steak smothered in a brown gravy, that frankly looked like it came from a can, and sliced mushrooms. I was a little dubious and asked if this is what I had ordered. "Yep," the owner told me with her lip jutted out and proceeded to walk away. I cut into the steak and the inside was blue. I am not  exaggerating, this steak was bluish purple. I ordered it medium, so I was pretty alarmed. Five minutes later, we counted after some point, the owner returned and when her attention was pointed to the steak she literally reached across me, grabbed my plate, and took it back to the kitchen without a word. It came back medium with MORE of the awful brown gravy-sauce and mushrooms on top in addition to the original amount- on the same plate as the first time... The sides on the plate were now cold, the steak was heaped with the bland gravy sauce and mushrooms... I paid 22 dollars for this entree. It was ridiculous. When I asked about the garlic and shallot butter sauce (my preferred way to have a steak) the owner pointed to the brown gravy and told me that was it. Again, this gravy was obviously from some kind of store bought can. I work in a restaurant, I know how things sometimes go. 

There's more to say but I don't have the patience to type it and you probably don't have the patience to read it. We will never be back, I suggest you don't waste your time or money.

If I could give this place 0 stars I would.

This was my first time coming here. My boyfriend likes the pizza and so we met some friends here for dinner and some drinks. We got a table one the patio and we orders a couple drinks while waiting for the rest of our party to show up. I got the "belly button" which is pretty good. Everyone else got different kinds of beers. 

They have the check-in special of half off an app and so we ordered onion rings. They were average at best, the breading didn't have super great flavor but they were fried and the ranch made them better.

3 of us shared the "Frog and Firkin" pizza, it came out really fast and personally i thought it was lacking in flavor. The crust was pretty tasteless and the sauce didn't have great flavor but the ranch would've have made it better had our server brought it out as requested. She never did. Others had burgers and fish and chips and all were liked (I think). 2 of our party had left and one more joined. We had shared with one and the other paid his bill in cash. As time went on we ordered a couple more drinks and more food.She never brought the last drink I ordered and when asked said "oh you did want one?" Uhhh yes I wanted another, that's why I asked!  When it came time to get the checks we explained how we wanted them divided and waited. 

And HERE is where they got "1" star!....When she brought out the checks the other 2 were right and there was an extra 2 beers one ours. We explained there were extra on ours and she right away said that if they were there she brought them. NO SHE DIDN'T! We then asked to speak with the manager who was a complete A**hole. He looked at our check explained that that meant she would have had to bring them out and we offered maybe she made a mistake a took them to another table but nooo. He said  and i quote "I'm not calling you liars but she said she brought them and I stand by my coworker" well, you're coworker can make mistakes too. No one's perfect but I will not pay for someones mistake ESPECIALLY after being "not called a liar". He then left and she came to get the checks and said for us to "not get hostile" excuse me?! I was just called a liar, I'm paying for drinks that nobody at our table drank, I'm pretty calm and you're going to accuse me of being hostile. (For the record nobody was even a little hostile, the manager on the other hand was). 

Most the people in our group have worked in the business and were appalled by the way were were treated, especially by the manager. In the end she did take them off and say she "payed for them herself" (YEAH RIGHT!). 

I, nor the rest of my party will be back. A restaurant that treats you like this doesn't get my business. I can get the same, gross pizza at many other places in Tucson and not be called a LIAR!

Lulu's really doesn't need my two-cents review but the food warrants some appreciation because everything I've ever had here has been delicious. The Buffalo Cauliflower Wrap with a side of tots is my goto lunch when stopping through this charming spot. One word of advice is to take the time to stop and enjoy your food in-restaurant; because everything here is so flavorful and succulent, it can very quickly get soggy and not so crisp, so slow down for while and have a nice meal and enjoy your selection while it's still hot and fresh just like Lulu intended.

Gus' has made the move to STL without losing a single step in the process! So often smaller/regional chains aren't able to expand/duplicate the success and(or) food of their original locations and I'm elated to report that this is most definitely NOT the case at Gus'! 

I have been a big fan of Gus' chicken of Memphis for many years and could never complete a trip down I-55S without grabbing a 3-piece wing for the road. With baited breath and watering mouth I awaited their arrival in STL and I couldn't be more thrilled that they are here and pumping out the same hot, fresh, delicious food to which they've made me accustomed. 

On this the second day of operations for this location, the line remained as long and briskly moving as it had been in the first. I see things being quite busy for a number of weeks but if standards remain at their current levels you can expect that the food will be as fresh, hot, and delicious as mine was today no matter when you're able to make it out to try Gus' Chicken - Maplewood!

I'm afraid to say anything negative about this place, but I'm going to anyway. 

I would like to say that the bartenders are ALWAYS nice and accommodating. They are swift on their feet and know how to pour a good drink. Also, the venue is awesome. It's full of old-timey charm and it's a nice change from the cookie-cutter bars on the East side. 

With that being said, there is something about the clientele  that makes me feel a little uncomfortable. I know that's kind of a broad statement, but every time I come here, I get this overwhelming sensation that I don't fit in. I feel like a crowd like this should be a little more less judgmental of others who don't look exactly how they do. For example, I feel out of place because I don't have half of my head shaved like Skrillex or have something tattooed above my eyebrow.  I mean, am I alone in this feeling?

Nonetheless, I like coming here, but just on nights where it's not a** to a** crowded.

when i first moved to Cedar Park (which i only recently discovered was the name of my neighborhood...i'm still not convinced), my landlord told me to go to Lee's to get a bagel breakfast sandwich.  he added that they were deliciously greasy.  and it was.  i don't do a "cup of fruit" or "bowl of Special K with skim milk" for breakfast...i'm not that kind of girl.  hell, i'm not that kind of human (i know plenty of male-folk who like these pansy breakfasts).  i do, however, need to wake up before i properly grease my intestines.  so i suggest waking up, taking a stroll down to Lee's (parking is never easy on the corner of 47th and Baltimore), and ordering up a bacon, egg, and cheese bagel sandwich.  it'll get you going.  i also heard through the grapevine (ok, my roommate's dad), that their cheesesteaks are the best in the CITY...fine....in the two block radius from my house.  i believe it.

PLUS, the guys behind the counter and in the store (i assume the regulars) are super nice.  AND while you wait for your sandwich, you can check out the different varieties of "RapSnacks" they carry.  i venture to say they have them all.  it's amazing.

Not new to First Watch, but new to this location! Was looking to grab a late breakfast with my mom while deep in corporate shopping land (sometimes you just need to hit up a West Elm, ya know?) and found this location on Yelp. We were about ten minutes away and hopped on the Yelp waitlist while heading over. Our table was ready for us as soon we we walked in--I seriously *love* this feature!

First Watch has a totally enormous (almost overwhelmingly so) menu, but I can appreciate the fact that they serve breakfast all day and have some good healthy options. I went with the avocado toast + the green tonic juice as I was feeling under the weather (plus about a million cups of their unlimited coffee). Both were great! The toast came with two eggs which made it really hearty. My mom had a salad + sandwich combo and liked her meal as well. 

Service was fast and helpful and the total was very affordable. There are two fancy malls nearby to do some shopping and burn off your meal!

THIS MUST BE THE PLACE. The place to escape when you book a trip to NOLA not realizing it's actually Mardi Gras. The place to cool off from the unending heat and humidity with a crisp glass of Pinot Grigio. The place where I plan to go every single day of my next trip to the Big Easy. 

I heard about Bacchanal from some pals with great taste and knew I needed to check it out. As I mentioned before, I booked a trip to New Orleans without realizing the city celebrates Mardi Gras for an entire month (rookie move). While the craziness in the Quarter is worth experiencing, it can get a little overwhelming. After 24 hours of parades, rum, beignets, and the like, I was ready for a seat in the shade with some real food and wine. 

This building in the Bywater is worn and unassuming, but charming from the second you walk in. We made our way through the dreamiest wine shop and ordered a glass of Pinot Gris and a beer. Their wines are really reasonably priced and you can buy by the glass or bottle (might I suggest bottle?). We headed over to the food window and put in an order for the grilled bavette steak and the mussels before finding a shady spot near the little stage. 

A little brass band started playing while we sipped our drinks and dove into our steak and mussels. Live music, patio seating, wine, and good eats--can you say DREAMY AF? The mussels came in a creamy coconut milk sauce that was perfect for sopping up with crusty bread. The steak was juicy and perfect pre-nap food (which is exactly what happened shortly after). 

I wish there was a place like this closer to home! Bacchanal is my #1 reason to get back to New Orleans ASAP.

Just a couple blocks away from Santa Claus Beach, this is the perfect place to grab some food and drinks nearby whether you dine in the park-like patio or do take out. 

A friend and I were happy to have found the spot after a couple hours at the beach and walked over to dine in the patio for a quick and filling lunch. The patio is nicely sized with many bench style tables around that are nicely spaced out. They have umbrellas to block the sun and there's nice night lights for the evenings. The only thing better would be if the hedges were shorter so you can see the ocean right behind. 

Service is pretty quick after ordering and the food was ready in a timely manner even with a busy lunch! Nice staff and easy to deal with experience. 

Parking seems to be street only should be free. 

Their menu consists of various appetizers, fish/seafood specialties, salads, burgers, sandwiches, sides, and drinks (sodas, lemonade, waters, beer and wine) They have a vegan friendly menu available as well. 

Baja Fish Tacos - Fried snapper, cabbage, pico de gallo, smoked tartar, cilantro w/chips and red salsa on the side. Fried had these and liked them!

Calamari - Lightly breaded and fried, house tartar and cocktail sauce. Calamari was pretty good and I really liked the tartar sauce served with it. 

Fish & Chips - Fresh red snapper tempura beer battered and lightly fried, fries, homemade tartar sauce. Fish was nicely cooked and flaky, batter was crisp and light. Really good!

We stopped in for some coffee and to try something new. This was definitely a unique and new experience - I've only had Turkish coffee a few times and if you're not aware they're supposed to be very strong. 

The shop is nice, grand, bright, and with nice products all around (coffees, teas, various drinkware and sets, etc). They sell coffee, teas and all kinds of baklava and treats. 

Great experience and customer service. While browsing the menu we were offered a sample of one of their lokum's. We did a couple Turkish coffees served with a couple Turkish delights and water. The coffee was rich, bold and yes strong. 

Looking forward to a next visit and trying some treats!

For a no fuss, straightforward, fresh delicious meal, On The Alley is a perfect stop. They're located at the harbor and are located near Brophy Bros.

It's first come first served and there's only a couple communal outdoor tables, so takeout and going elsewhere seems like good idea.

We stopped in for a quick bite and had a good experience here. The line wasn't too long for a weekend afternoon when we stopped in. Food came out nicely prepared and served in a timely manner. 

Fish & Chips - These were great! Well cooked, golden brown, perfectly crispy with a good batter and flakey fish. Fries were crisp and soft on the inside. Served with tartar, ketchup and a lemon slice. 

Friend had some fish tacos which were enjoyed and we also had the calamari which tasted fresh and was cooked well. 

Parking is at the harbor with a per hour price, about $2+ or so.

The quiche is amazing! Flaky crust, silky egg custard, and delicious flavors! Today's quiche had ham and green chilies, yum! I took my teenage daughter for the first time and she loved her bowl of tomato soup and the grilled cheese sandwich. Service was, again, friendly and warm. I just love this little bistro and hope they never change!

Finch and Fork is a restaurant in a high-end hotel serving expensive food. I'm not "in" on its 4-star Yelp rating, as I found it to be merely average, especially at its price point.

The "Potato & Leek Soup" was competently-prepared, delivering the basic earthy and salty flavors you want in a potato-based cream soup - and I enjoyed the vinegary poblano relish topping they put on it as a nice foil for its heavy cream broth. However, I want any cup of soup I spend more than $10 for to be more refined and fancy, and to have some special rare ingredient if no meat or seafood.

If I'm paying nearly eleven bucks for a vegetarian soup made of cream, leeks, and potatoes, the restaurant is making a killing off of me. So surely the service must be appropriately fussy and proactive? Nope, not really. This isn't the type of place that's going to fold your serviette when you excuse yourself to the washroom.

The "Sea Scallops," again were well-prepared with a decent sear though not exactly filling - a miniscule entrée for $33. Also, the scallops themselves were not as clean-tasting as I'd expect, they were at the "stew scallops" stage in my opinion. Nonetheless, I felt this dish could have been improved with a greater presence of the chorizo vinaigrette and less relish. Admittedly, I was weary of the relish from eating something very similar on my soup appetizer. 

Overall, I wasn't very impressed. As a hotel restaurant, I'd eat here if I were staying on the property, but this is not destination dining. There are superior options in downtown Santa Barbara if you're looking to spend this kind of money for dinner.

Food-Décor-Service: 3.2/4.2/3.7

Barbareño is a BBQ joint like no other, and comfortably sits in the upper end of dining experiences that Santa Barbara can offer. Even if Barbareño's menu is focused around smoked meats, calling Barbareño a "BBQ joint" is probably a huge injustice. The owners have a stated aspiration for Barbareño to represent the micro-regional cuisine of Santa Barbara, similar to in French or Italian culture where each town or city of the country has its own distinct style of cooking based on the bounty of the region and the local traditions.

Head Chef Justin Snyder, who has cooked everywhere from immensely-popular "George's at the Cove" in San Diego to duo-Michelin-starred "Ta Vie" in Hong Kong, has assumed chief kitchen responsibilities from co-owner and original chef Julian Martinez, bringing additional refinement to an already solid dining operation. Martinez and Snyder's menu is built around leverage of an outdoor Santa Maria grill, a style of grill common in this region that evolved from South American asado-style grilling of meat over an open flame. What gives the Santa Maria grill a distinct look is its turn-wheel apparatus that allows precise heat-control by enabling cooks to easily raise and lower the cooking grate over the flaming coastal red oak that burns below. Barbareño takes it a step further and adds a smoker, an enhancement that one can taste in the rich, slow-cooked meats served here, which are more heavily-smoked than typical "Santa Maria"-style BBQ.

The featured meat of the "Santa Maria style" is 'Tri-Tip,' a relatively lean but flavorful cut of beef from the bottom sirloin that responds well to indirect cooking. The "Santa Maria BBQ" at Barbareño is the dish to order here -- the Tri-Tip is smoked for 2 hours, then cooked sous vide for another 12 hours, and finally finished on the aforementioned Santa Maria grill. A barbecue fusion of the old methods and the new, this multi-step journey results in what is definitely the tastiest, smokiest, tender chunk of Tri-Tip I have ever dreamt about.

I know what you may be thinking, kind reader: at $27, this is REALLY pricey for a barbecue dish, even if it is as spectacular as Jay K. claims it is. But know as well that it's served by pleasant people in a delightful setting, and that Barbareño is serious about sourcing. Their avocados are grown on-property. The Angus choice-grade tri-tip is sourced from local butcher shop Shalhoob Meat Company. The creamy (but not mushy) pinquito beans that form the legume bed on which the Tri-Tip rests come from Rancho Gordo, a local grower of heirloom beans that I've been ordering from for years. The gorgeous deep red tomatoes on the Tri-Tip plate have been lightly roasted so they've started to caramelize and become sweet -- providing a nice balance to the savory beans and beef.

As my starter, I enjoyed the flavor of the refreshing "Cantaloupe Gazpacho," but feel I may have overpaid for $10 of cantaloupe juice, and missing the unique texture of gazpacho I expected of olive oil and bread. This minor miss was later redeemed, however, by the "Duck Fat Beignets," which are INSANE and served with bacon custard and caramel made of whole-grain mustard. I'm not even a donut fan, but as a fan of food, I can't imagine ordering any other dessert off of the menu when I come here next. No, I won't be sharing mine, order your own!

I've visited Barbareño several times for lunch, and I've had their various lunch sandwiches, including the tri-tip, pulled pork, and smoked burger. Of these, I recommend sticking with the peppery tri-tip sandwich which features the same "house" tri-tip as I rave about above, but with a biting mixture of garlic butter, jalapeños, and cilantro on a ciabatta roll.

I'm sure there are better "Santa Maria"-style tri-tip BBQ restaurants around the Central Coast, but Barbareño's presence in downtown Santa Barbara means that a great rendition of this style of barbecue is close and convenient for city-dwellers, tourists, and business-travelers like myself. Also, BBQ aside, Barbareño is one of the best places to dine in Santa Barbara regardless of cuisine. The owners have achieved something very special here, creating a successful restaurant that is very much 'Santa Barbara' while keeping the venue and prices relatively humble.
 
Food-Décor-Service: 4.4/4.0/4.5

Mexican food in California has significantly changed since Julia Child endorsed La Super-Rica Taqueria as her favorite place to eat in Santa Barbara. How has this no-frills teal-colored Mexican outpost stood up to time? Is it worth a visit, or is it shockingly over-rated?

I would personally not wait in the reportedly insane peak-hour lines to eat here, but I'd definitely return for an early Wednesday lunch when it opens at 11am, to dine among local newspaper-wielding seniors, which is exactly what I did when I visited La Super-Rica Taqueria. There was virtually no line, and I was eating within 10 minutes of my arrival.
 
The "Super-Rica Especial" was the most expensive dish on the menu at $6.80, but worth it. Chunks of al pastor pork that have been marinated all-day share a plate with fire-roasted pasilla peppers stuffed with queso that melts and tastes like a Oaxacan cheese or dry mozzarella (and could actually be one or the other). The cheese acts as a binding agent, tempting attacking forks to pick up cheese, pepper, and meat all at once. With just a hint of delightful piquancy in each bite, this humble dish is not about heat as much as it is about the earthy, lush, multi-layered flavors of a Mexican home. The "Super-Rica Especial" is grade A certified "comida de abuela." 
 
I was much less impressed by the "Frijol Super-Rica," which is perhaps unfair, given the fact it is a side dish merely advertised as pinto beans with chorizo, bacon, and chilies, and is offered at a measly $2.55. However, I'd expect these beans to be more strongly flavored than they are with the chilies and pork products, but they're just slightly-above-average pinto beans by southern Californian standards.

Both items are served with homemade corn tortillas, which are heated to an ungodly temperature and wrapped in foil in a way that makes them a hazard to handle when they're hot - so be careful. I was not and nearly became a statistic. 

I have admittedly been long-intrigued by the surprising shout out to "La Super-Rica Taqueria" in the second verse of Katy Perry's "This is How We Do." I must confess, I too was excited by the possibility of a wild night at this Santa Barbara institution, "scarfin' tacos," and "checkin' out hotties." But I can assure you, my friends, this really isn't that kind of place, and hopefully never will be.
 
Food/Décor/Service: 3.9/1.8/NA

When I think about fried chicken, Hattie B's has become something of a national benchmark for me. Pictures don't do it justice. Word of mouth doesn't do it justice. Reviews don't do it justice. As with other national fried chicken benchmarks Willie Mae's in New Orleans, or Gus's in Memphis, Hattie B's needs to be experienced to be fully appreciated.

Like a sleight-of-hand artist who shows you exactly how he does his trick yet still gets you every time, Hattie B's is relatively open-lipped about how they make their product. According to them, the chicken is initially hit with a dry brine in salt & pepper, then a double-battering process consisting of a buttermilk and egg dip, and a flour-based dredge. Then the chicken is deep-fried at a relatively low temperature (300-325F) until it is cooked. The lower temperature results in a lighter batter and a higher margin for error in terms of extricating  the precious chicken parts before they dry up.

Before being served, the fried chicken is brushed with used oil from the fryer that has been blended with brown sugar, paprika, and a varying amount of ground hot pepper that is marketed on a scale from "Medium" to "Hot!" to "Damn Hot!!" to "Shut The Cluck Up!!!" The "Medium" level should be sufficient for most first-timers, even those who enjoy dangerously spicy food. Be careful, the STCU-level has been measured at over 1 million Scoville Units (SCUs), or approximately four times hotter than a habanero pepper.

It is this final step that makes Hattie B's hot chicken a bit greasy as fried chicken goes -- since additional grease is literally added to it. Still, the double-batter creates a thick enough crust that it holds up well to the oil, maintaining its crispiness. Inside the chicken, pools of chicken juices wait for your teeth to liberate them due to the brining step and disciplined temperature control throughout the deep-frying process.

Served with refreshing pickles and slices of white Wonderbread, Hattie B's fried chicken is some of the finest, moistest, most tongue-pleasing fried chicken in the land. The fact that it can be made hot enough to kill pets and small children makes it legendary in my book.

With the way their menu is priced, Hattie B's wants you to try their sides -- the Southern Greens and Black Eyed Pea Salad being two of my favorites. That said, you should not come to Hattie B's for their mostly forgettable sides.

Yes, annoying tourists like me create a long line here during peak hours. Yes, there's a "scene" that's developed around this place given its proximity to a large college. Yes, the parking situation sucks so you'll want to Uber or walk if possible. No, I'm also not interested in using this review to compare Hattie B's to Prince's or other old guard hot chicken restaurants. I live in San Diego, so virtually anything in Nashville is on a whole different tier than what I'm used to. Besides, this Hattie B's location is conveniently walkable from the hotel I typically stay at when I'm in Nashville, and with all of the top hot chicken joints in Nashville operating at such elite levels, proximity wins.

Hattie B's is one of the very best fried chicken restaurants I've been to in this country, and giving it five stars on Yelp seems short of doing it proper justice.

Food/Décor/Service: 4.5/3.7/NA

Yoichi's is one of the best restaurants I have dined at in the United States. My initial meal here was so superb that I went back a second time and had virtually the same exact meal the very next week. If I actually lived in Santa Barbara and not San Diego, I'd be back at Yoichi's again RIGHT now, and just thinking of this restaurant makes me want to jump in my car and drive 3 1/2 hours to be there.

When I saw reviews of Yelpers claiming to break down into tears of fulfillment and astonishment in the middle of their meal, my B.S. detector went off, but having now been to Yoichi's twice, I get it. Everything here is great, but there are a few very spectacular dishes that transcend greatness - and if there were ever two dishes that are so good I could cry, they would possibly be Yoichi's "Grilled Duck Breast" (Kamo no Yuanyaki) and "Rock Fish in Sweet Broth" (Kinki no Nitsuke). The former of which features an expertly-grilled duck breast, soft and luscious, with sweet soy sauce caramelized on the meat, and the latter a silky fish in a delectably sticky broth that easily breaks apart on your tongue, imparting its flavor throughout your mouth as it disintegrates into joy itself.

Run by Yoichi Kawabata (Chef, formerly of Nobu Tokyo) and his wife Mogi (Maître d'), Yoichi's offers only one way to dine - for a prix fixe rate of $100, a 7-course Kaiseki dinner. Kaiseki originated in the 16th century as a Japanese tea ceremony. It is about more than food, it is a deliberate presentation of the food across a number of servings, each morsel of which is intricately placed in ceramic plates and bowls specifically chosen for it. Kaiseke is the most refined cuisine of Japan, strictly reflective of the seasons before "seasonal" became a thing. Kaiseke is typically "light" fare, meant to be paired with sake or tea - but, at Yoichi's, a full Kaiseki dinner will satisfy even the hungriest eaters.

Yoichi's Kaiseki is a mixture of sushi, grilled plates, boiled plates, and (of course) dessert. You do get a few choices on menu options. Aside from the aforementioned dishes, I much enjoyed the Hamaguri Shinjo Sumashijatate (Clear soup with Hamaguri clam fish cake) and the Sakura Buta no Kakuni (Braised Pork Belly) with Moromi Miso, though I'd suggest the Rock Fish over the Pork Belly. Also I suggest pairing with the Denshin Natsu (Junmai Daiginjo Namazake), a seasonal licorice-y sake, and one of my favorites I've had either in or out of Japan. I had the opportunity to meet with two friendly gentlemen from Denshin who co-hosted my complimentary sake tasting during one of my visits here.

For the rest of my meals here, I had over 20 different bites of food, enjoying a variety of specialties including water shields, Japanese sardines, abalone, jellyfish, miso-marinated scallops, simmered taro, local Santa Barbara sea urchin (uni), bluefin tuna, salmon belly, with Japanese ice creams and fruit gelatins for dessert.

I am grateful to Yoichi-sama, Mogi-san, and their staff for putting together such an exceptional dining experience. Both times I ate here were humbling meals, food events that I will treasure and remember always. For those still wondering: put simply, this is THE dinner to drop some money on if you visit Santa Barbara. Don't think twice about it, put yourself in this restaurant's capable hands and prepare to have your mind blown.

Food-Décor-Service: 4.8/3.9/4.6

The pork belly is better quality than Ijji 4's and the marinades are mostly quite good.  The grills are more non-stick so they don't need replacing nearly as often as at other AYCE Korean BBQ's.  The service is also very accommodating and earnest.  So why the 2 stars?  They're due to 3 huge cardinal sins that I (as a Korean-American) cannot/will not forgive:

1) The rice.  We received dry, boring Chinese rice.  C'mon!  It's IMPERATIVE that you offer sticky Japanese or Korean rice at a KBBQ.  I understand the owner is Chinese and this is a cost-cutting measure, but why open a Korean-themed restaurant if you won't do something as fundamental as serving the rice that Koreans (and frankly, most asians) like to eat?  Fluffy glutenous rice soaks up the grease and flavor as well as adds a very comforting texture to the meal.

2) The sesame oil.  Seriously, open a Chinese restaurant if you're using an influx of Chinese ingredients in your offerings.  It's like I decided to open a taco stand but used Old El Paso and hot dog buns.  The sesame oil dip was light-colored and bland compared to the smoky look and roasted flavor of Japanese or Korean sesame oil.  That lack of depth was also totally obvious in the marinades used for the meats.  Again, the meats are pretty solid in quality which is pleasantly surprising.  But treat them with respect by seasoning them with better (albeit slightly pricier) ingredients please.

3) Lastly, the wraps.  Or, more specifically, the complete absence of wraps of any kind.  I'm not asking for perilla leaves, but ALL Korean BBQs at least provide red leaf lettuce to wrap your meats (and stick rice:/) with.

Again, I appreciate the meats (especially the miso pork belly which is delicious) and the service and price are on point.  However, I can't see myself eating at Siu again until they begin to embrace the nuanced yet crucial aspects of a Korean BBQ.  This place is recommended if you're a full-on carni who only wants to eat straight meat without the accoutrements.

My husband and I each ordered a cheesesteak (to try 2 each) and were not disappointed. The seating area is small, but we were sat at a booth, our order was taken and served our food quickly. I'm not yet an expert in Philly cheese steaks, but the original and the belly buster - with American cheese and all the fixings as recommended - were delicious. Can't wait to come back.

Great Lobster Roll, fresh and plenty of Lobster.
Next time I am in Florida I will be visiting again.

Since there's no good fish markets nearby in orange county, I have to order from Santa Barbara Fish market. The order arrived in a Styrofoam container. The smoked salmon looks amazing. Not sure about the Ahi poke, it tastes kind of slimy and the tuna it doesn't look like the same deep red color as it should. I'm thinking maybe I shouldn't eat it?

I wasn't supposed to come here, but I walked the wrong way and was hungry. 

There were people waiting outside, but there was a empty spot at the communal table so I grabbed it. I waited forever for a menu and then even longer to order. There's a tv right in front of the table, but they don't get cable so the options were quite limited. 

The mimosas here are tasty but weak and not worth the cost. When my meal came out, the Veggie Bene Florentine, it was average and needed salt and pepper to punch up the flavor. 

Service was slow and hard to get anybody's attention. Since I had a short time in Nashville, I wish I picked somewhere else to dine so I had better food and a better experience.

his place is way over-hyped and not worth your time and/or money. To be fair, when I entered, the staff was clear that the wait was about 20 minutes to stand in line and order, not including food prep time. Since I read such good reviews for this place, I foolishly stayed, my fault. 

As I waited in line by myself, groups of more than one got really into claiming all of the tables in front. The joke was on them since there are plenty of tables on the second floor and in the back, so you don't need to worry about finding a spot. 

After ordering, I grabbed a table I got my double mimosa after about 5 - 10 minutes. My mimosa was the worst I've ever had. Something about the taste of the oj with the champagne just didn't work. It was so bad, I didn't even finish half of the glass. 

I ordered the California eggs, and I was not a fan. The salsa and sprouts went together terribly and left an awful taste in my mouth. Additionally, people around me had ordered and sat down before me and expressed their concern that I got my food first. I understand I'm one person, and it might be easier to get my food out, but I didn't feel right cutting the line either and felt the need to apologize for the mistake on behalf of the restaurant. 

I also ordered a side of fruit after being told it was made up of strawberries, blueberries, and raspberries. When it came out with pineapple, which I despise, I sent it right back, and they quickly corrected their error with other delicious fruit besides pineapple. 

After the staff drops the food, nobody checks in on you again, so make sure to ask for everything when they bring your food, or you are out of luck. 

All in, I spent well over an hour here from entering, ordering, getting my food and finishing my meal as a party of one.

Don't know what to say here, this wasn't a positive experience for me, and it wasn't cheap.

Oh, how I loved my dinner here. I ate at the bar and experienced some of the very best service ever from all of the bar staff. I got there around 4:45 pm and was starving for some strange reason. I mean, I had brunch and beignets so there was no reason to be hungry, but I was in NOLA and had been walking around all day and might have had a cocktail or two throughout the day.

The bartender brought me out some bread and put in my order so it would be out as close to 5:30 as possible. The kitchen opens at 5:30 and they only offers a lite menu prior to opening. 

Now, Muriel's had come highly recommended but I never expected it to be as good as it was. My meal was out of this world. I knew I didn't want the multiple course option and I simply selected the one-course Cajun Demi-Poulet. I can't say enough amazing things about this meal. Every bite was delicious and heavenly.

Also, I need to speak ever so highly about the exceptional service. The entire bar staff was incredible. I don't understand how they so calmly handle all of the drink orders they were given constantly. 

I loved the decor here. While Muriel's is in a touristy location, you forget you are in the French Quarter once you are inside and I loved the vibe of this place. 

Staying in NOLA? Stop here, you won't regret it,

Was staying at the Union Station Hotel, and this was a close brunch option (about .2 miles). I typically like to go to Sunday brunch around 12 or 1, but I was up and knew Nashville was a brunch town, so I figured earlier was better, and I headed over around 9 am. 

This place was packed, and there was already a line of at least ten couples/families waiting to sit. I could see a few empty bar seats, so I headed over and grabbed them. Yes, it was busy, yes it was a Sunday on a holiday weekend, but there wasn't enough help. Everything was slow, including the service and the food. 

My order, a simple egg sandwich, came out bland, and the hash browns were nothing special. After eating almost everything, I was still hungry, and I ordered a lemonade - for six dollars and having to wait for 10 minutes, it totally wasn't worth it. As I waited, I began to notice the massive amounts of people in line and surrounding the bar area. People were literally staking out positions to get the next open seats. It was getting ugly, and people were pretty intense, making it very uncomfortable to sit waiting for a simple lemonade. I had two couples fighting over my seats, and I hadn't even paid yet. 

I left my seats for the couple to fight over, and it took forever to get out the door since people were packed inside, waiting to sit. I had to push my way out after saying excuse me 20 times. This has to be a fire hazard and is wildly unsafe.

Solid 4.5 stars. I loved their texting system and how they let you know exactly when your tables is ready. I only waited about five minutes and was seated upstairs at a table. Those stairs are steep and there are a lot of them, you have been warned. 

Service is quick and friendly. The menu has so many options it's hard to choose. They offer everything from traditional breakfast platters, NOLA specialities, omelettes, lunch, sides and more. It was hard to choose what to get, but I ultimately went with the avocado omelette and I was impressed. 

My meal was was huge and was way to much for me to eat. My omelette tasted very flavorful and fresh. The grits were ok, but I'm starting to think I'm not a grits person. My flaw, not theirs. I also ordered a mango flavored mimosa. Tip, it still comes with OJ, and they just add in some mango purée. 

The decor here, or more so upstairs, is minimal, and could use some NOLA decor, especially in the French Quarter.

There were so many people there you literally couldn't move. People were always bumping into one another, and you were pushed out of the way if you tried to stop and read anything, especially at the beginning of the exhibit. 

I guess there is no alternative since this is a tourist town and nobody wants to miss out on this attraction, but I've never seen so many people crammed into such a small space. Because of this. I couldn't enjoy the museum and experience. Additionally, I didn't find the exhibits to be interactive enough to keep my attention. I felt as if everything I saw, I could have seen on the internet. 

What's worse is the gift shop, which was still crammed with people and offered seriously over-priced memorabilia and tank tops for like $40.00. No thank you. 

Despite everything, this still checked off an item on my bucket list, so I'm glad I came.

I looked around a long time for where to eat tonight, but I kept coming back to Saint Lawrence in my search. Saint Lawerence is located right on the boarder of the French Quarter and a five minute walk from the Sheraton hotel. 

I made my way over around 8 pm on Friday. They weren't super busy, but it was the weekend before Christmas. For my drink, I ordered a Black Betty, but subbed vodka for Crown Royal. It was good but my substitutions I'm sure messed it up a little. 

They have a great menu that highlights some great Southern food. It was hard to decided what to order but, for my meal, I finally decided on the Creole pasta minus the shrimp. My dish was huge and so flavorful. Eating here reminded me of what NOLA food is all about. 

I sat at the bar and liked the atmosphere here as well as the multiple TVs for entertainment. 

In NOLA? It's worth planning a visit here for dinner!

If you're looking for a delicious hot chocolate spot, THIS IS IT!!! 

I can't believe I've never been in here before and I pass by it almost every day! This was recommended to me by a friend so I had to stop by. I've been craving for a good hot chocolate after having some in NYC last year and this is by far better than the one I had in NYC. Saves me the trip to NYC! 

I ordered the Spicy Volcano Hot Chocolate and the Marshmallow Brulee Hot Chocolate. The spicy hot chocolate had just the right amount of spice! The marshmallow was a little too sweet for me but the hot chocolate was good nonetheless. They both had chocolate shavings in them, which added an extra flavor of richness! 

It is a bit pricey but the quality is there! The most amazing hot chocolate ever. I'm definitely going to be a regular here. The staff and owner was lovely as well!

Side note: This is better than Max Brenner and Magnolia Bakery Hot Chocolate. (Don't get hot chocolate from Magnolia Bakery - Tastes like instant Swiss Miss)

Hmmm...WHY have I let Shell-i Deli linger with four stars for so many years? Dunno, but I'm going to fix that right now. I've tried a lot of delis in Reno since my first review, and this one is definitely my favorite. Last year, my bread choice changed from Dutch Crunch to Swiss Onion, but other than that, everything is the same. Same great bread, great meat, great cheese, great everything. I still love the huge variety of sides, chips, and drinks. I love that I can go Dagwood crazy on a sandwich ("I want everything...just, EVERYTHING"), and they still manage to smash it all together into a neat package. I just brought home a sandwich last night, and it was so good. SO. GOOD.

A tip: Their sizes are very generous, and I have never been able to finish the medium, even when I think I am especially hungry. A small should be more than enough sandwich for the average eater, and a mini for kids.

I never forget a food recommendation, so imagine my delight when I realized that this sushi joint in the mall specializes in sushiritos! I heard the voice of Michael T from the not-so-distant past telling me: "Traaaacy...you've GOT to try a sushirito if you get a chance!" There may have been a glowing blue figure pointing at Santa Cruz as well...

So I did!  Husband tried to argue against it, because the combination of sushi and burrito to him sounded unnatural.  Let's just say, he sure was eyeballing my sushirito later, and I REFUSED TO SHARE! Is it the greatest sushi I've ever had? Certainly not.  In fact, the amount of fish in the roll seemed a little skimpy (I had the #4).  But overall I thought it was a really great meal for $10! I very much enjoyed the texture over everything.  The perfectly cooked soft rice and the smooshy crab combined with the crunchy veggies was so nice.  I went with a sauce that the cashier recommended, but I still found the first half to be a bit bland, so I went back to the counter to grab some soy sauce, and a few squirts of that really brightened up the second half.

In a town bogged down with AYCE sushi restaurants, this is a nice alternative.  You can get a quick sushi fix on the cheap without worrying if you're hungry enough to get your money's worth.  Also, sushirito is a lot more portable!  Although this won't replace a visit to one of Reno's many, many, many sushi bars, it does fill a new niche, and for that I will happily give them my business again.

A recent outing to a different restaurant put Island Buffet in my mind, and then I realized that I haven't ever reviewed it!  Looking through these reviews is surprising to me.  We always have good experiences here, but it would seem that not many people agree.  So Island Buffet, here's a little much needed Yelpy LOVE for you!

I get the pleasure of seeing this buffet through the eyes of a child.  You see, Kid LOVES buffets, any buffets; even the continental breakfast buffet at a hotel is enough to get her heart racing.  So when I brought her here for the first time last year, her little head just about exploded.  Upon seeing the spread, she clutched my hand and whispered, "Oh Mama...it's WONDERFUL!"

And you know what?  It is.  It really is.  If you can't see the magic in this place, then you might be a bit jaded, and it's time to spend some time with little kids who will set you straight over massive, DIY ice-cream sundaes.

A kid will teach you that sure, not every dish is perfect, and there are going to be some you don't like--but if that's the case, YOU DON'T HAVE TO EAT THEM.  Simply push the plate aside and go back for something different.  Wasteful? Yes.  But Buffet 101 dictates that you don't take a heaping serving of a dish you're not sure about--just take a small sample! You can always go back for more.

And at this buffet there are plenty of dishes to love.  I'm pretty sure some of the Chinese food is the same as what's on the menu at Chi, because I've had the amazing Honey Walnut Shrimp at both places.  I never pass up the fresh pupusas.  I have to pick up some grilled spicy sausage from the carvery and nestle in some mac and cheese, because yes, I freaking love mac and cheese.  And the Chinese dumplings.  And the sticky ribs.  And the mind-boggling array of desserts. And...and...and...

It's just SO MUCH FOOD.  So many choices.  "SO WONDERFUL!"  If, like me, you don't need the heaping mountains of crab legs to enjoy a buffet, go for lunch (local's price: $13) or weeknight dinner (local's price; $17) to avoid the higher seafood extravaganza prices.  I mean really, how can you look at a twenty-dollar bill, and look at ALL THAT FOOD, and not feel that you are getting your money's worth?

Sure, the decor is dated...REALLY dated (hello, 1980s! I've missed you!), but it's also incredibly comfortable.  I have had several meals here crowded around a big cushy booth or a huge round table with padded chairs, laughing, having fun, and enjoying the tropical rainstorms.  Certainly, if you're looking for a fancy date night, this is not the place to go.  If you are looking for a spot to take a big group, particularly a family group or a slightly intoxicated group, Island Buffet is perfect.  It's a place to set aside any food snobbery and just have fun with sheer volume.

REVIEW NUMBER 200!!  Whoop!

In honor of my 200th review, I would like to whole-heartedly recommend my gym.  Sports West is in a great location (at least for me) and is always full of the nicest people you would ever want to meet.  As mentioned below, this is not a meat market--all the people there are really friendly in a PLATONIC way.  I often have someone introduce him/herself just to chit-chat.  They have a fantastic pool area, really great locker rooms with all of the amenities, and lots of machines.  It is overall just a fun place to hang out.

But the BEST thing about Sports West is their family-friendly policies.  First of all, they have really great and affordable child-care.  I pay an extra $10 a month for the child-care, and it is worth every penny.  They also have "family time" on the weekends after 2pm when the kids are allowed in the gym itself...so you can work out with your kids, or play with them in the gymnasium, or even take them swimming in the pool.  And best of all, they have Friday night Kids Club.  Every Friday night from 6pm to 11pm, they will watch your kid while you go have fun.  They charge $10 to cover the cost of your kid's dinner.  That's right, they will watch your kid for 5 hours and feed them dinner for only $10.  For me, that alone is worth the price of membership.  My kid LOVES going to the gym!  She always has a lot of fun and I get some alone time.  That is great motivation to work out!

We hadn't eaten Mongolian BBQ in a long, long time, but Husband got the idea in his head that nothing would do for dinner except a self-styled meat bowl, so away we went.  It only took me about five minutes to remember why, exactly, we hadn't been into a Genghis Grill in so long.

1)  Atmosphere.  The seating isn't much better than a fast-food joint, and between that and the corporate-scripted service, I kind of feel that I'd rather this all just be a serve-yourself kind of place with a tip jar for the grill operators.  Except then I guess you wouldn't be able to order the fish bowl full of alcohol.  Also, the decor theme here is ad-chic.  Everywhere you look are big, glaring posters shouting at you to EAT HERE JOIN OUR FREQUENT DINER CLUB EAT HERE.  I'm here already...you don't need to beat me over the head with it.  Other posters dictate the many rules of bowl construction: DO NOT PUT MEAT ON TOP OF VEGGIES YOU WILL BE CHARGED EXTRA.  Even in the bathroom stalls:  EATHEREEATHEREEATHERE.  Just stop.  Stop already.

2)  The price.  You have to spend a lot of money for the privilege of constructing one bowl.  No AYCE, no discount on a second bowl...you get one shot.  I'm not saying that a large isn't enough food; if you pile that sucker up--and I mean really, really stuff the food in there until heaping--you should get enough food to satisfy.  But what if you make a mistake?  What if you create a monstrosity of ingredients that just doesn't taste good?  Well, kiss your money goodbye.  I don't prefer AYCE because I want to eat the company into bankruptcy; I want AYCE so that I can experiment with multiple small combinations.  As is, the pressure to fit $15 worth of food into a tiny metal dish overrides any kind of culinary creativity that Mongolian BBQ should provide.

3) The line.  It wasn't terribly crowded when we were there, but I imagined what it must be like when it is.  Even with only three other people in line with me, the lady behind me was nudged up into my personal space breathing down my neck because apparently I wasn't moving fast enough for her.  Then, when I got to the grill, the guy took my bowl and my card and shooed me away.  I remember long ago with my first Mongolian BBQ experience, how fun it was to create your bowl and then watch the griller cook it up.  None of that here.  GO SIT DOWN WE WILL BRING IT TO YOU.  It all just starts to feel that you are in a cafeteria.  And not the good kind of cafeteria where you get to have fun choosing all different foods, but the institutional kind where you step forward, take what you're given, and move along.

When we got the check, it suddenly occurred to me that the Island Buffet at the Peppermill has a Mongolian grill.  I did the math and realized that our bill at Genghis Grill (with NO drinks, desserts or appetizers--bowls only) was only $5 less than it would have cost for us to eat at the buffet--as much food as I want, with drinks and desert included.  Suffice to say, I think it will be another long stretch of time before we ever set foot in another Genghis Grill.

EDITED TO ADD: Looks like Peppermill does NOT have a Mongolian grill (did they used to? I'm not sure), but Toucan Charlie's in Atlantis definitely DOES.

I'd honestly never heard of this restaurant until recently because, who goes to Somerset? Amiright?! But when my fellow Yelpers heard of my Great Sushi Search, the recommendation that I got most often was to try Sakana. So, I packed Family into the truck and headed into the hills.

After going in circles for a while (quite literally...it's easy to get lost in Somerset's maze of roundabouts on a dark and rainy night!), we finally found Sakana only to realize we'd parked in the back of the restaurant, and Holy Hell, where IS this place?! But finally we made it in the front door, slightly damp, and were greeted by many enthusiastic and friendly employees.  Their warm attitude, along with some hot tea and miso, soon had us feeling happy and relaxed.

The first thing we noticed were all of the interesting and unusual items on the menu! Although there were a lot of the traditional rolls we are used to seeing in Reno, there were also many that looked creative and appealing! Husband was happy to see the number of choices that didn't include avocado...it's not that he doesn't like avocado, he just doesn't understand the need to put it in EVERY roll. We skipped over our usual nigiri orders to start with a few of the long rolls that popped out at us.  The Sakana Roll was delightful, but my real favorite was the Samurai! Another great choice was the Crouching Tiger Hidden Dragon, and although I was not a huge fan of the Wipe Out, Husband did enjoy it. We did eventually switch to nigiri, and my two favorites, hamachi and tai, were both excellent, made from beautiful cuts of fish.  One thing that really struck me about all of the sushi we tried was the real distinction between each order. In flavor and in size each roll was very different, really challenging our palate with each dish. 

Eventually I started in on the extensive appetizer menu. There were lots of cool choices on there, and it was all included in the price! I was thrilled with the takoyaki...so flavorful! The mussels were also very tasty, with some sort of slightly BBQ-esque finish that I couldn't quite identify. Because I was sitting right next to the server station, I got to see a lot of other dishes come out, too, and they all looked wonderful.

And of course then there's the ice cream. I don't usually think of ice cream as a particularly Japanese dish, but when it's homemade and included in the price, you can bet I'm excited about that! And it was worth being excited over. I had banana, Husband tried apple streusel, and Kid went with cinnamon. All were amazing, with fresh, bold flavors and perfect texture.

We were really pleased to spend the first dark, wintry night of the season in this excellent sushi bar. Between the bright smiles of the servers and chefs, the excellent and inventive sushi, the selection of wonderful appetizers, and the super-fun ice cream finish, we felt good about spending more money here than at most sushi places in town. The price here is steep--$24.99 for dinner--but with ALL of the menu items included, it is actually pretty reasonable! I should also mention that not only does the kids' menu go up to 11 years old, they have a special "little kids" price of only $6.99! That is a nice touch, which was really what struck me about Sakana...lots of nice little touches that together make for an overall wonderful experience.

Ok, so I actually used to be a big fan of this restaurant until about 30 minutes ago when they tried to steal my friend's phone. It really was a great spot to go to for after hours, but after tonight WE WILL NEVER COME AGAIN! 

We had left Jade Harbor and had gotten like a block away when my friend realized he forgot his phone. He'd been texting on his phone prior to being served, and there was no doubt he left it on the table. 

So he goes back to the restaurant, and the hostess tries to turn him away saying "oh, I don't know about a phone, you come back tomorrow." My friend tried to explain he was here like 30 seconds ago, and she pretended not to recognize him. After realizing that she was trying to shoo him out, he quickly walks past her up the stairs despite her protests ...

Once there he sees all the employees who had been working, sitting at a table with his phone in the middle (while playing with their own phones). He looks at them for a second, says "Fuck you," and grabs his phone and leaves.

The worst part of this is that we have been coming for past couple months and they definitely know us as regulars. I don't know what we did to piss them off (I thought they liked us?) but we certainly won't ever go again!

Please, if you have a nice phone-or are just outraged to hear about this happening-don't come to Jade Harbor!  It's just so offensive..

** The following Yelp memory review reflects an experience I had well before the shelter-in-place order currently in effect. ** 

As I'm watching tropical storm Cristobal make landfall in Louisiana on CNN, I was just thinking back on a wonderful trip Jamie W. and I took to New Orleans years ago. Luckily I reviewed all the places where we stopped, or at least I thought I did because when I checked out my Louisiana list, I noticed my review of this classic tourist stop was missing. Say what? Gee, did Yelp delete it because I wrote something borderline offensive? Was I particularly sassy and wrote something like...

"Why bother eating the beignets here when I should apply them directly to my thighs?" Well, coincidentally, we were in NOLA soon after Katrina because we had just taken a tour of the Ninth Ward when we found ourselves across the street fully aware that a stop here was a must. I never forget good fried dough especially when it's dusted so liberally with powdered sugar. You can get three for just $3.40 now (photo: https://bit.ly/3f19K85), and I doubt if it was much cheaper back then. I remember thinking how ironic that my cup of Coffee with Chicory cost more, now $4.30 (photo: https://bit.ly/3h6YaKi).

I also vividly remember how bustling it was in what was essentially an expansive patio with a roof, and we were sitting at a table with full view of a strolling jazz combo on the sidewalk, not an unusual sight and sound in this city (photo: https://bit.ly/2XHQWVJ). However, our stop was brief as there was a muffuletta with our names on it at Central Grocery up Decatur Street. This was a Yelp memory review (hands fluttering down like Wayne and Garth). Ah, those were the days when my carb intake was not even on my radar. Not anymore but New Orleans is still very much on my mind.for a post-COVID-19 return.

FOOD - 4 stars...it was a nice, decadent coffee break but I don't recall it being extraordinary 
AMBIANCE - 5 stars...this was the strong suit here with the jazz and convivial spirit in high gear
SERVICE - 4 stars...nothing I remember with disappointment 
TOTAL - 4 stars...everyone needs a beignet

RELATED - Going to New Orleans? Here's a collection of places I've visited and reviewed: https://bit.ly/2BArJ6P

I knew amid the crazy-aggressive itinerary I set up for Jamie W. and me for our one day in Nashville that somehow, somewhere, we needed to try the city's most famous specialty, hot chicken. I really didn't know how to fit it in since we needed to spend time at the Johnny Cash Museum, stroll through the honky tonks on Broadway, pay homage at the Country Music Hall of Fame & Museum, and of course, watch a show at the Grand Ole Opry. It was at the end of the show that I thought we could satisfy some near-midnight munchies at Hattie B.'s. We had heard it was a toss-up between her place and Prince's for the real thing.
