Since Prince's closes at 10PM, Hattie won since they don't close until midnight.

'Hot chicken', if you didn't know already, is fried chicken with a flavor kick since it's slathered in a sauce rife with cayenne pepper. The meat is particularly tender because it's been brined first, a tried-and-true technique the chefs on America's Test Kitchen would heartily approve. It's served on white bread with pickle chips which brought to mind my favorite fried chicken in the world, Harold's in Chicago. How I miss shouting my order through their bulletproof glass. Here it's a far friendlier place with a clear menu of choices and even merchandise to buy (photo: http://bit.ly/1GyJGO2). That may have to do with its proximity to Vanderbilt University since we noticed most of the diners here are young and tired-looking.

Jamie and I both went with small plates given the lateness of the hour, he with the $9 Breast & Wing and me with the $8.50 Leg & Thigh. We were asked for our heat level as there are five to choose from: Mild, Medium, Hot!, Damn Hot!! and the pinnacle, Shut the Cluck Up!!! You'll be disappointed to know we could only register Medium since we were going to be in a car for most of the day after, and I certainly didn't want to be externally combustible when I was in Dollywood. With surprising ease, we secured a patio table where our order came quite quickly (photo: http://bit.ly/1GwQ7hK). As part of our orders, we both got two side dishes and decided we needed to try four of he seven listed on the menu.

Mine came with Pimento Mac & Cheese and Homemade Cole Slaw, excellent choices I might add (photo: http://bit.ly/1Fqg8Rf). Jamie ordered the Southern Greens (tasty and not too salty) and the Black Eyed Pea Salad (just too vinegary) (photo: http://bit.ly/1DOWt8h). The chicken was prepared to order with a nice crunchy crust, tender meat, and a spiciness level that was probably a level lower than we could have handled that night. No matter as we liked it, and the portion was just enough for us not to suffer any morning-after indigestion. I heard places like Hard Water and Trick Dog serve heir version of 'hot chicken' in San Francisco. That may have to do until my next trip to Nashville.

FOOD - 4 stars...nicely rendered example of Nashville 'hot chicken' at the midnight hour
AMBIANCE - 3.5 stars...a little less down-home than I expected but it worked, not too crowded at that hour
SERVICE - 4 stars...friendly and quite helpful to out-of-town poultry eaters like us
TOTAL - 4 stars...Miss Hattie. yo' chicken is mighty fine

This is a classic East Nashville dive, one I would have completely bypassed were it not for Anthony Bourdain and his local posse who praised it as an essential stop on his "Parts Unknown" CNN series. It didn't look like much from the outside, a relic from sometime in the middle of the last century, and it frankly didn't look that promising on the inside either (photo: http://bit.ly/2H6r0HL). Jamie W. and I made a beeline here after strolling through the Vegas-level excess of the Gaylord Opryland Resort. We didn't score one of the parking spaces in front, so we parked in the Sherwin-Williams paint store lot nearby.

The menu was typical greasy spoon fare with no evidence of a salad or veggie plate. Nope, you come here for the burgers of which I have not had in, believe it or not, over two years with the exception of a random Impossible Burger. But I was willing to indulge to get the full Dino's experience. It was indeed the $6 Dino's Cheeseburger with a slice of melted cheddar, lettuce, tomato, sliced pickles, and onion (photo: http://bit.ly/2stmezJ). For an extra $2, we both got a side of fries (photo: http://bit.ly/2Jod6Gg). The burger was fine medium and on the smallish side. Not White Castle small but definitely not as big as an In-n-Out.

It was good though and juicy enough and bereft of the mayo and ketchup you would find at most burger joints. I was grateful for that omission since the extra lubrication was not needed. Bourdain's squad referred to the fries as "redneck poutine", but we didn't have any gravy on ours. They were crispy and seasoned in a spice mix that made it taste a tad healthier than what you would find in a fast food chain. Jamie threw caution to the wind and ordered a $3 Cup of Chili which used the same beef and was quite tasty (photo: http://bit.ly/2H8Scpk). Was it the hidden jewel of the Nashville dining scene? Not sure but it was certainly better than we could have found on Lower Broadway.

FOOD - 4 stars...no culinary art here but they man the grill and fryer with skill
AMBIANCE - 3.5 stars...pure dive but it fits the food
SERVICE - 3.5 stars...friendly enough
TOTAL - 4 stars...definitely had better luck here than we did at Bourdain's other recommendation, Bolton's

I knew Jamie and I were in trouble the minute we saw Adam Richman's smirking mug on the wall. That's the cherubic "Man Vs. Food" guy who keeps getting into those food-eating contests at various dives throughout the country. I don't think he did his Big Easy contest at Mother's, but he must have tried one of the sandwiches here, which immediately labels this place an instant emporium of unhealthy gluttony in my book. 

Mother's does have a reputation for its $10 Debris Po' Boys, which use the meat that falls off roasts as the basis for the filling. That sounded like pure gristle to me, so we both went for the $10.75 Famous Ferdi Special, which puts their home-baked ham, roast beef, shredded cabbage, and yes, the debris, together into a soft roll that was then doused in a watery gravy (see photo). Our verdict...it was alright, kinda on the ho-hum side for all the meat provided, especially what they proclaim to be "the world's best baked ham".

I was not feeling it, although the $3.50 plate of French Fries helped (see photo) since it was quite a pile and piping hot to boot. I also had a $5.25 Garden Salad, which they inexplicably put in a bowl way too small to mix any of the ranch dressing in there with ease (see photo). Rather outdated and probably proud of its traditions, Mother's is a surprisingly small place considering how long it's been on this corner of Poydras Street. You order your food at the register and pick up your beverages there as well. Overall, it just wasn't a memorable experience.

FOOD - 3.5 stars...hearty sandwich but not all that exceptional in flavor
AMBIANCE - 3 stars...feels old and tired in here
SERVICE - 3.5 stars...it was alright, not all that friendly to newcomers, just to regulars
TOTAL - 3 stars...not what I was hoping for, but maybe I just need more debris in my uncluttered life

Honestly, the only reason Jamie W. and I stopped here is because I was intrigued by the multi-story structure which reminded me of Tokyo's Ginza District where restaurants were piled on top of each other in tall buildings crowded next to each other. The Diner spreads its expansive 18,000 square feet vertically over six floors (photo: http://bit.ly/2Jg0Jru), but we stayed on the main floor where the coffee shop is operated since we weren't looking for a dining experience in the middle of the afternoon. Each floor is apparently devoted to different cuisines with the top floor offering oysters and sushi. We just came for the $3.25 cups of Drip Coffee (photo: http://bit.ly/2KRbrdN) which we found satisfactory. Even though Yelp feedback appears tepid, it's good to know this is a 24/7 operation just in case we grow tired of the honky-tonk music in the middle of the night.

COFFEE - 3 stars...readily available when you're in the area
AMBIANCE - 3.5 stars...fancier than most diners, clientele not so much
SERVICE - 3 stars...on the perfunctory side
TOTAL - 3 stars...am I in Tokyo?

There were plenty of things for me and Jamie W. to do during our brief visit to Nashville earlier this month, so whittling the list down to the must-see's wasn't easy. If, however, you had to choose one thing to do in this city, I say go to the Grand Ole Opry for a show, but a close second would be a visit to this tribute to the Man in Black. I'm a late bloomer when it came to appreciating his music and legacy. I remember his ABC-TV variety show when I was a kid, but it really just started with me with the superb biopic "Walk the Line " preceded by his late-period renaissance with producer Rick Rubin. For just $16 admission, what this tight-fitting but extremely well-organized museum does is make you appreciate the entirety of his life and career with very little filler (photo: http://bit.ly/1drkU6b).

It's only two years old since there was a museum at his home in nearby Hendersonville, but in true Cash fashion, it burnt to the ground. This one is in the heart of the Downtown area on 3rd Avenue near the honky tonks on Broadway and across the street from the Goo Goo Shop. Sponsored by the Cash family, a key differentiator from other celebrity museums, the exhibits span all the different periods of his life from his childhood through his Air Force years and then onto his salad days as a musician where he got his break at Sam Phillips' Sun Records recording with the Tennessee Three. Of course, his long-standing marriage to June Carter is well covered here down to her performance gowns (photo: http://bit.ly/1zmSpRb). There are several interactive exhibits which present Cash's music through all his periods.

Two separate areas are devoted to viewing vintage footage of him throughout his career, one focused on his music performances, the other on his many appearances in films and on television. For instance, I had no idea he played a homicidal maniac who terrorized a very young Ron Howard in a sleeper called "Five Minutes to Live". What I did learn more about were his mid-80's recordings as one of the Highwaymen (photo: http://bit.ly/1bcYSlT) and his last years when he made the American Recordings with Rubin, a quartet of albums that served as a fitting epitaph. An unassuming door leads you to the well-stocked gift store  (photo: http://bit.ly/1DVfR3v) and the small adjacent cafe. It's amazing how comprehensive the collection of artifacts is here and all of it done in a respectful tone.

I keep a close watch on this heart of mine
I keep my eyes wide open all the time
I keep the ends out for the tie that binds
Because you're mine, I walk the line.

Pretty much your typical local, suburban casino with a surprisingly lively atmosphere.

We swung by the casino for our 1st time here on a Saturday evening at 11pm and, to our surprise, the casino floor was popping. Although the casino was very crowded, it was also very small compared to other Pennsylvania, NJ casinos. What probably helped in livening up the environment was the fact that the bar/lounge/club (if you can call it a club) was located smack-dab in the middle of the casino next to the table games and slots. There was a live DJ where the bar was and people were dancing away. Since King of Prussia is a relatively quiet city, with a lack of nightlife, we attributed the rowdier crowd to the fact that most people probably came to the casino to hang out and drink since there was nowhere else to go.

As mentioned, the casino floor was very small, but what made it worse was that it was smoke-filled. We only encountered 1 small area for non-smokers and there was even a smoker there! A majority of the casino was occupied by smoking and that made the place a major turnoff for us. There were a decent amount of table games, with blackjack starting at $15/hand, and slots scattered around, but not much to choose from.

This was definitely a casino we will probably never visit again. There weren't many games around and the smoke was the nail in the coffin. Plus, the other bigger casinos in PA aren't too far off.

Great pastries-  orgasmic even .  I give them 5 stars for  everything  they make.  Honest /fair/stable pricing of the merchandise is the issue with  this review.  I went into the shop alone  and was charged $15  for 2 cannoli and a babarum cake ( single  serving size) in addition to  being ignored  by 3 women behind the counter ( I was the only customer  in the store). No prices listed on any of the items.  I had a gut feeling I was  being  charged  "the not-from-the-neighborhood" rate.  So I went back with a guy friend and  we bought the exact same items and were charged $12.50    


Price gouging- it really sucks whenever  and wherever it happens (  this has happened at other businesses in Philly too ( sad to say)  and it is a real shame because  if this place would  have an UPFRONT  price list   displayed  on their items and play fair I would  be  coming back again and again.

Want the best Pho in town? Then look no farther than Lilly's.

My 'usual' is a large, steamy bowl of Pho Ga. Why do I vote this Pho the best in town? Cuz every single time I consume it, I'm amazed by all the flavors. It needs to pull no favors from hoisen, hot sauce, fish sauce, or any other additive you could think of putting into any other bowl of Pho around town.

Sometimes when I'm completely famished, I'll start off with an order of Egg Rolls. They're fried until they reach crunchy perfection, filled with yummy meats and veggies. They're good, but this is when I get my hoisen fix in. 

If the food wasn't enough to sell you, the super sweet, attentive, and quick staff will seal the deal.

Vincent's is a New Orleans institution with every right. It's old school, with a warm and intimate setting. The dim lighting and candles create a dinner atmosphere that is a solid romantic outing. 

The waitstaff are friendly and extremely knowledgable in their food and wine offerings. You won't see a pad and pen when placing your order here. They're quick to provide suggestions and recite specials. The food is generously portioned, with many entrees coming with a side salad and/or soup. Be sure to have a stomach that is ready for the rich intake.

There are very few points of Vincent's that I do not like. So few, that there really is only one: the intimate setting is also cramped. The restaurant is small and packed with tables. Do not expect to move about freely or have extra room between tables - it's just not a reality here. Waiting for your table here (even when you have a reservation) is excruciating when there is bad weather outside. You try to find vacant space and shuffle about as people need to squeeze by. Hopefully you're lucky and able to grab real estate at the bar.

The food and service totally make up for this though. The chicken fettuccini alfredo and veal parmigiana are my absolute favorites. My friends also rave about the chicken parmigiana and the eggplant parmesan.

Put Vincent's in your rotation. You won't regret it.

I was BEYOND disappointed with my experience at House of Cards this evening. Having been to the Magic Castle in Los Angeles, CA I was expecting a similar experience, but I was severely disappointed. 

This is a long review, but I urge you to hang in there.

Lets start at the beginning of my experience. I'm celebrating my birthday this evening, so my best friend wanted to take me to a dinner of my choice. I had seen billboards for House of Cards and it was on my yelp list of places to try, so I made a reservation for 2 at 7:45 on my birthday. I knew there were many things to see and experience at the restaurant, so I wanted to come early to enjoy the attractions before being seated for dinner. We arrived to the complementary valet at 7:10 only to be told that the garage they park vehicles in couldn't accommodate the SUV we were driving, so the valet recommended we park at the lot on the corner. We went around the block and parked at the lot closest to the restaurant, paid $30 for parking, and went inside. When we got into the restaurant and checked in around 7:15, we were told that they had a table ready and they could seat us early. Awesome!

We were seated at 7:20 and it took 20 min for our waitress to come by and pour us water and give us drink and dinner menus. It was about another 10 min before she came back and by that time we were ready to order drinks and dinner. I ordered a cider, but unfortunately, they were out, so I asked for a sour instead, and we ordered dinner. We were excited by all the magicians placed around the restaurant, so we decided to leave our table while they prepared our food, and watch some of the shows that were taking place, keeping an eye on our table, so we could return when the food was there. About an hour later, our waitress found us and told us that the ticket for our food didn't print in the kitchen, so she was asking them to put a rush on it and it would be out soon. She also brought us two glasses of champagne on the house. 

After about 45 more min, we returned to our table, still no food, so I asked for a manager. The bar manager, I believe his name was John, came to our table and said that the kitchen was backed up and they were making our food now. I explained to him that there was a difference between the kitchen being backed up and us waiting two hours and still not received our entree. At that point, he said "well the food is cooking now, I'm not sure what else you want me to do." I then expressed to him that for what we were paying, we expected a certain level of service that I didn't feel we were receiving. I also explained that it was my birthday, and that's why we chose this restaurant for the evening and it wasn't turning out to be a great night. Mind you, at this point, there were several tables (including a party of 8) that had been seated after us and all already had their entrees.

Shortly there after, our waitress brought out a salad for us to share until our food came to the table. Just a few minutes later our food came out, it wasn't exactly what I ordered, but at that point, I was just happy to have food after over two hours of waiting.

We enjoyed our food, I got the 8oz filet and my friend got the pork chop and we ordered a side of the three cheese macaroni to share.  Both entrees were cooked well and tasted great. After we ate, they brought us two desserts on the house, the cheesecake and red wine soaked pears. While I appreciate the gesture, I don't eat cheesecake and the pears weren't my favorite. My friend enjoyed the cheesecake and when it was time for the bill, our waitress let us know that the meal and drinks were on the house. We asked her to run the card so we could leave her a tip, as I had a feeling that the meal was going to be coming out of her tips for the night, and we didn't want her to be punished for the problems we had through out the evening. She said she could charge us for one of my beers ($8), and when she came back with out card, we had been charged $53. She went and corrected the problem, and we left her a tip along with our $8 bill.

At the end of your dinner, you receive tickets to a magic show in another room. This evening, the main entertainer was Dan Sperry, and HE WAS WONDERFUL! Very entertaining and kept us all entertained. Overall, if it wasn't for the ambiance and the experience of House of Cards entertainment, I wouldn't have spent 3.5 hours here.

My recommendation, go to House of Cards Nashville, have drinks at the bar, enjoy the experience, and go home. I was severely disappointed with my experience, and I'm not sure if I will be going back or referring HoC Nashville to friends. I'm leaving my 2 star review because the restaurant did try to make things right, but I wish I would have had a better experience to begin with. 5 stars for the ambiance, and 1 star for the service from start to finish.

Wow...just had a very uncharacteristically awful (truly awful) lunch experience here. Is this place under new management?  ...or has the current management just stopped caring??

The four of us arrived before noon for lunch today (Sunday). Seated right away and greeted by an unfriendly server. Whatever. Took our order (which by-the-way included a request for "very lightly" toasted bread on my turkey club) and then disappeared. 

The food took forever. There was another table of four looking a bit irritated by the fact their order hadn't yet been taken. Feeling sorry for them and wanting to help, I suggested they leave. It was too late for us, but I thought they could at least get to the friendly safety of Vince's Restaurant down the street and save themselves. 

When our food finally did arrive, it was cold. Or at least we thought it was cold....the unfriendly waitress explained to us that our food was not cold. So I guess that's still an unresolved issue. But I'm pretty sure it was cold...and there were four of us and one of her and the four of us were all of the same opinion. Whatever. We did ask that she stop arguing with us and please bring us the check. We actually had somewhere to be and we were already late, having waited an extraordinary amount of time, for our cold food to arrive, served by our unfriendly waitress, which included by-the-way one turkey club on very over-toasted bread. The sandwich crumbled away with every bite I took. She delivered the check, without an apology. Without a word said, actually.

So we left and I let the hostess know our experience was awful. Even though the dining room is small, the fact that customers were sitting around with no food in front of them I guess she missed. I'm very certain that will be our last bad experience at the Continental Tavern only because I will never go back. If many more people share similar experiences, I'm very certain there won't be customers for much longer.

Tried this place for the first time today. We definitely have a new go to for sushi! Probably the most amazing shrimp tempura I've ever had. My husband got the teriyaki chicken which was fantastic. The service is stellar and the price is great! It wasn't busy today (Sunday, lunch) and we got right in. Will definitely be back next weekend!

Love this place! Especially since I'm on the super low carb diet. My go to is the bison collard green wrap with brisket, onion, dill pickles and a side of buffalo sauce. Yass!!! Prices are great and food is always good. Oh, and the decor is super cool. Full bar as well. 5 stars!

Yum!!!! This place is is so freaking cute, we're a little obsessed! I can't divert away from the carne tacos and my fiancé is loving the enchiladas! To quote him "they're the best he's EVER had"....including mine! Womp womp! And the love that it's vegan!! Yea!!!

Anyways, kudos to these guys! 5 stars hands down!

Yea!!!! They finally opened! Ok, this place is certainly my gluttonous, however, they're also delicious! Our go to order is the original sliders and naked fries. At only $2.50 a slider, you can satiate your cravings and still not feel terrible about yourself after! They're the perfect size:) the fries are to die for also! The menu is a little limited but if you're in the mood for burgers and fries, you probably won't find a better place, especially for the price! Welcome to the neighborhood Shoo-Fry!

Tried this place out after reading some interesting Yelp reviews. Most are accurate, the place is fairly small , but I found it just fine to manage when it visited around 11am. I was pleasantly surprised to find several items at really good prices:

1.) bag of basil/parsley/mint $1.00
2.) 2 cloves of garlic $1.00
3.) large green peppers $0.75
4.) large bag of lettuce $1.50

I found some other good deals on veggies and a couple of spices. They also had my veggie sticks which I love! This place has saved my butt on many occasions when I realized I was out of an essential element for my recipe. As much as I love Di Bruno's, this place has far better prices on many items:) 

Oh and let me end by saying how super nice the employees are! I've gotten to know them quite well and they're always such a pleasure! 

Ps, they take card now (no more cash only) with a $10 minimum!

Are you kidding me??? Do they ever get anything right? 85% of the time the order is ALWAYS wrong. Today, I'm in a hurry and of course my order is wrong again, then they LOSE the other half of my order! I ask them three times for my order and they're HIGHLY confused. Cut to 20 minutes later....still NO order! I have to SQUEEZE through about 20 people in their insanely tiny room to get to the front and ask for my cash refund. When they give it to me you would think there's an I'm sorry, right? NOPE! Nothing. No apology zip! 

I'm done with this atrocious place. Honestly, this is the WORST customer service and WORST restaurant I've ever been to! DONE!

Why did I have to move so close to this place? C'mon, I'm going to gain 20 pounds this month alone! This place is freaking amazing. Their pizza is seriously to die for!!! My go to...cheese pizza and the plain tomato w/out cheese. 

The staff is super friendly and sweet and the restaurant is clean with plenty of seating. The prices are on point too! Highly recommend!!

Obsessed with this place!!  I love everything here! From the buttermilk flapjacks, to the chicken and biscuit, tater tots, crinkle cuts fries, and house made potato chips. The staff is amazing and so are the prices. Oh, and did I mention the make your own Bloody Mary bar???? Hands down one of the BEST restaurants in Philly!

Another AMAZING experience tonight! We had the honor of having Steven as our server and we were so happy with the stellar service that I needed to write another review! The service was absolutely fantastic, Steven went above and beyond helping us make the best decision on the speciality steaks, and the experience was perfect as usual! This is definitely the best service and food in Rittenhouse! Thank you Steven!

So much fun to frequent, especially during the holidays!!! It can get busy so be prepared. There are some great finds here and I love buying cooking gifts for my FIL here. Definitely a must if you're new to Philly or haven't been yet!

Rudest service I've ever encountered. Wth. I know this place is packed, and people can be annoying, but I don't think that excuses being a patronizing ass to everyone in line. There was a incredible sweet, soft spoken, Texan young man in line in front of us. He dared to ask if they have espresso. The gal at the counter replied in a harsh condescending tone "that's an espresso machine right here isn't it" while jabbing her finger in the general direction of the machine. Then, I paused for not even half a second to ask my husband what he wanted to drink, and the same gal doing a great Soup Nazi impression shouted out "NEXT". Really, it was just one second at most that we delayed. 
The beignets were really pretty good. It's worth trying out, if you don't mind being verbally abused and waiting in a long line.
2016 #27

Let me start by saying I've eaten her at least 15 times and I promise you that as a "salad expert" this place has THE BEST Greek Salad you will ever taste anywhere in the state of Pennsylvania.

I don't know if it's the dressing, the seasoning, the fresh ingredients, seasoned chicken or the perfectly warmed pita bread, but it is worth traveling for.

Is a salad worth a 4 out of 5 rating? Ok, so i've tried other menu items and they're pretty much as good.

Why not a 5 out of 5? Dinner menu is a tiny bit pricey and the atmosphere is a little antiquated BUT its BYOB...

Philadelphia deserves great vegan food, and we have a lot of it. This is the land of legends like Vedge, V Street, Blackbird, and Dottie's. We crush it. But The Tasty is a major step back, and honestly depressing. 

- Coconut chai sounds amazing, but don't let that fool you. Watery and bland. I don't know how they made Dona Chai and coconut milk taste bad. It was a sign of things to come. 
- The chikn sammie used old-style faux meat (think typical Chinese soy meat). It had no flavor despite  all the coconut bacon (tastes like Dorito powder, bad especially compared to the fabulous Coconut Club at Memphis Taproom), and was dry despite the mayo. At least the tomato slice looked fresh, and the tater tots were the best part of our meal. [This is not The Tasty's doing, props to Ore Ida for making such a wonderful product.]
- The Dirty Jersey contained the worst fake meat I've even had, and tasted like nothing. Daiya couldn't save it. We attempted to resuscitate the patient with salt and pepper, but it was no use. Tried ketchup, still a goner. Ugh. 
- The toast with walnut pate sounded great, but NOPE. We added even more salt and pepper, still not worth eating. 

The Tasty is cute and relatively affordable, but that's about it. The service is nonexistent, the food is bland and texturally challenged, and the whole experience made me sad. This restaurant will make people think that going vegan means saying goodbye to flavor and happiness, which doesn't have to be true. 

Step it up.

My favorite Italian restaurant to order takeout from.

My usual is their chicken fettuccini with spinach and mushrooms. My boyfriend always gets their spaghetti and meatballs with extra meat sauce. Their serving size is perfect where we both have enough leftovers to eat for lunch the next day. Each entree either comes with a house salad or minestrone soup. We usually opt for the soup, it's the best minestrone I have ever had! It's chunky with lots of vegetables and has outstanding flavor. The meal also comes with bread (of course) which is even better when dipped in the minestrone soup! It's about $37 each time we order takeout, not bad for a nice Italian dinner.

I've never dined in, so I can't comment on their waiter/waitress service but everyone is always friendly whenever we pick up our order for takeout. 

Oh, and their homemade Strawberry lemonade is phenomenal.
I know you're probably thinking to yourself, "who goes to an Italian restaurant and orders lemonade instead of wine?" But trust me, it's worth it!

A true and delicious soul food restaraunt is hard to find. Corinne's is excellent. The food is amazing, the staff is always pleasant and welcoming and the prices are very reasonable considering the quality of the food and the size of the portions. You will not be leaving hungry. 

I have been going to this establishment for the last 20 years (I'm only 30 years old) and have yet to have a bad meal. The chicken is delicious and pretty much any side you choose is bursting with flavor. I am a huge foodie and have been to several soul food places, including Sylvia's in NY, which seems to be the benchmark for this type of cuisine. I can honestly say there is no comparison in my opinion. Sylvia's gets the publicity and the marketing since her establishment is located in up and coming Harlem, but Corinne's food is several notches above. It's unfortunate that being located in Camden deters a lot of people from trying this place. It's not the best neighborhood but I have never once felt unsafe. I grew up in a town as white as can be just to give perspective. You can park directly in front of the restaurant and never once, have her children or anyone related to her behaved like animals. 

Corinne's is definitely a diamond in the rough. Considering how long this modest establishment, with exterior signage you can easily miss, has been in business, it is a testament to how delicious this place is and word has spread. It would behoove you to go try it! You won't be disappointed.

Wright's is a South Tampa institution! It's my favorite place to get lunch catered at the office. The ham and Swiss sandwiches are my favorite. The bread is super soft and fluffy. When I go in to the restaurant I like the Paris (turkey and Brie pressed) and the turkey Reuben sandwiches. The cakes are also wonderful! The carrot cake is extra spicy and the cream cheese frosting is perfectly sweet. You really can't go wrong with anything on the menu!

Parking can be difficult and there is often a line out the door. They are closed on Sunday and close at 6p on weekdays. Try to call ahead and place your order to go if you can to skip the line!

Drove up to Santa Barbara last weekend  to get away from a terrible heat wave.  We stumbled upon this Caribbean restaurant while walking along State Street. The restaurant now has dining tables on the sidewalk as the entire street is closed off to vehicular traffic. All tables are spaced out to comply with State COVID Standards. All employees are wearing masks. Food was very good and they had RED STRIPE beer!  Service was good as was customer service. My kids really liked the calamari sandwich that they both ordered, my wife enjoyed her Curry Tempeh and I liked my Jerk Chicken. Very good food along with great customer service, great weather, and the precautions they are taking when it comes to social distancing and live music they had playing I give 5 Stars

This place is just an institution in the French quarter for drinks. I believe it's where the hurricane drink was invented. After having a few hurricanes already though, we opted to try a rainbow drink that they had on the menu. As with all of New Orleans, you can get the drink in a to go glass. Sadly the to go glass doesn't give you the best presentation for a multi layered glass full of colors. And of all the drinks I've had in this wonderful city, I think this may have been the worst tasting. Stop in grab a drink in the amazing courtyard, but I wouldn't stay long as there is too many other great option.

If there is one thing you just have to get here, it's their biscuit with maple butter. I can't remember the last time I had a biscuit so big, and so good, that is was the star of the plate. This place is a really cute place for breakfast right outside of the French quarter. Although I believe there are 3 locations, this one will be the closest if you are staying near bourbon street. 

The service and food were just spot on. I opted for a very simple breakfast after eating and drinking all weekend, and I really enjoyed the food. They serve French Truck Coffee which the local with us said was great and it didn't disappoint. This place does get busy, so if you're getting here anytime after 8:30, plan on waiting a bit. Well worth the wait though. My southern breakfast also came with a fried green tomato which was a nice touch. Very flavorful breakfast.

Absolutely loved this place for breakfast. And those that have had the beignets at cafe du Monde, forget about that tourist trap and get here for theirs. You'll skip the outrageous wait and you'll like these even more. 

The breakfast was absolutely perfect. Potatoes cooked with andouille sausage. Giving them a nice flavor and richness, while also accompanied with some green peppers and onions. Probably one of the best potatoes I've had for breakfast. I kept thinking why couldn't we get potatoes like this up north. The scrambled eggs that cam with it, were in omelette form. Cooked perfectly. And lastly with the meal was a slice of French bread. The French bread was perfectly toasted. Not something you would really think about, until you bite into the perfectly toasted and buttered bread and realize how amazing it is. 

The beignets were great. Bigger and better than the competition. You've got to try cafe du Monde, but after you do, come here to see the difference. The coffee was also excellent, but lacking the chicory as CDM has. This location I've heard was the best of them. You feel like you've stepped into a little French bistro. I'd definitely come back. Especially for the potatoes!

Location, location ,location! If you're looking for a hotel within the French quarter, look no further. Stayed at this hotel multiple times and have always had a good experience. If you happen to stay here during the month of December, you'll definitely enjoy the holiday decor. This hotel is positioned right on bourbon street. So you can't get a better location. You step out either of the doors and have everything you want within walking distance. Also very close to my favorite bar in the quarter, Erin Rose! 

There is a nice pool that is open during the warmer months. The hotel also has a couple restaurants and a jazz club with regular shows. The staff is always friendly, and the rooms are nicely decorated. Most of the hotels in the French quarter are on the smaller side due to the age of these hotels. But these actually aren't that bad and they are very pretty. 

When you're booking your room, make sure to not get one that is on the street side. Bourbon street is loud at night, and when you get back to your room, you will want some peace and quiet. Always opt for the interior room. If it's in the summer months with the pool, get a room that exits on the pool patio.

As someone who managed a restaurant for two years myself, I hate leaving a negative review. Because I know that it ruins a manager's day to read it. But in this case, I don't mind a bit...

Last night I was meeting a group of 15 people around 10:30PM. I was a few minutes early and the first to arrive, so I thought I'd order a drink at the bar.

The bar was less than half full, with two bartenders behind it. I sat for two minutes, and a drink menu appeared in front of me. I sat for another two minutes, and two middle-aged women saddled up on my left. THEY sat for two minutes and were then greeted by one of the (male) bartenders, and were served their drinks.

I sat for ANOTHER two minutes and said bartender slung a bev nap in front of me while flirting with some blonde a few seats down. He then proceeded to serve two guys sitting to my right, who also arrived AFTER I did.

All in all, it was a full 10 minutes before he bothered to make eye contact and speak to me. And when he did, it wasn't a friendly "Hi, what can I get ya?" Instead, it was a shady, "Did you want to order something...?"

So I ordered my usual Johnny Black and waited for my friends to show.

Once they arrived and got settled in the next room over, I paid for my drink, and begrudgingly left a dollar for Romeo. (It would've been a quarter if I'd had one in my pocket.)

On my way into the other room to meet my friends, I passed by what appeared to be the manager on duty. (It was too late and too slow for them to have kept a hostess on.) The look that she gave me spoke volumes. "Who the hell do you think you are, barging into the dining room?"

I ignored her and took a seat at the table.

So let's recap: I and 15 of my friends dropped a few hundred dollars at the Washington Street Ale House on a night when they CLEARLY could've used the revenue. And in return, I was treated like a red-headed stepchild by a bartender and then by the manager.

Hospitality 101: You don't make the guest feel like they're bothering you.

(And perhaps a lesson for me as well: In life, it's okay to be more assertive.)

Laura's Candies is a chocolate and candy store. They have been around since 1913.

I'm in love with their Mississippi Mud and my favorite is the Cajun Bark, which combines my two favorite things: white chocolate and macadamia nuts- so rich, with a little kick of that Cajun spice. 

 I've also gotten to sample their pralines, which are pretty good. I have yet to try their ice cream. 

There is so much good stuff here! When I visit New Orleans, I'll have to drop by again. 

Happy eating!

Willa Jean...

A spot you definitely need to check out on your trip to New Orleans. They are known for their cookies with vanilla milk. 

I decided not to order this item since I was craving cornbread, and they had it on their menu... so why not?

Unfortunately, the cornbread was one of the worst I've had. It was presented beautifully, a whole block of it with pure cane sugar surrounded by butter on the side. I spread it evenly on my sliced cornbread, but it didn't make much of a difference. It tasted like it wasn't cooked all the way and it was chewy. I had to drink a lot of water with it. 

I also got the Fresh Daily Catch of the Day Fish and Chips with Old Bay seasoning, which was very good. My favorite were the fries, seasoned perfectly. The fish was soft, but the batter could have been cooked a little more for crispness.

I will come back to try other dishes. 

Happy eating!

What a great addition to the growing SoBro neighborhood! Open Society is a sleek wine and coffee bar that serves caffeinated beverages, pastries, and eventually alcohol. I highly recommend the Mate Latte, their Latin American twist on a chai latte ($5). The shakerato is also unique - maple syrup and espresso. Pastries were complimentary during the soft opening, so I enjoyed a lemon poppyseed loaf and a savory breakfast pastry - both delicious! Service was extra friendly and they warmly welcomed us into their establishment. 

Great place to spread out and cowork - strong wifi and a variety of seating arrangements available. 

When happy hour hits, visit the bar space next door (must be 21+ to enter) for some adult beverages.

I went here three times in one week.

First time: blown away by the rich flavor, dual menus, and authentic dishes. Texted all friends to tell them.

Second time: brought acupuncturist friend who has visited China. Verdict - as authentic as he's ever had in Tucson.

Third time: brought another friend that's traveled in China (and married Asian). He agreed - it's up there.

I can't tell you a thing about the American Chinese menu. I've only ordered off of the Szechwan menu. I've had:

  * Cucumbers in Garlic Sauce - like nothing I've ever tried in a Chinese restaurant
  * Ginger Chicken - super authentic (and delicious)
  * Twice Cooked Pork - addictingly delicious
  * Eggplant and Pork - the most tender eggplant ever
  * Spinach & Garlic - similar to cucumber dish - very original (and tasty)
  * Green Beans - they're green beans. But delicious!
  * Kung Pao Chicken - Still great, but lowest score out of the rest

Personally, I've never had anything in Tucson this good, as far as Chinese food goes. And, I've been on the search.

I know of only a few others that MIGHT compete, one of which I've been to - Chopstix (in Marana), Ba-Dar, and the new Jun Dynasty. I've been to Ba-Dar. China Szechwan has them beat.

Main complaint: they use MSG. Ask for them to keep it out of your food. We did and it was still outrageously delicious.

Service? Eh. It's fine. You'll get through. They're nice. Ask for Sandy - she's awesome.

Ambience, hmmmm.... NO.

But food, god yes.

Seriously, don't even think twice on if you should give this place a try. Decide after your first visit if it deserves a second.

Oh yeah... check out Tucson Foodie. That's me!

St. Lawrence is the perfect neighborhood bar, even though it's in the French Quarter. This place is perfect to make it a local hangout spot, and is the perfect place for tourists. The drinks are always good, and poured correctly, there's a nice assortment of beers on tap, 0bottled, and the food is amazing! 
So, my main admiration about St. Lawrence is the food! It is 100% amazing. Sure, the pictures and menu both made my mouth water, but actually eating the food, made me fall in love, as I was not expecting much, as bar food was concerned. Everything here is worthy of writing home about. 
While I do have strifes about their daiquiri machine always being broken, not a rotation of daiquiri flavors, and their happy hour menu can be encompassing of more mixed drinks and cocktails, St. Lawrence is one of the best everyday, neighborhood bars in the city. It's a cant miss for visitors and should be staple for locals.

Located on the first floor of the Intercontinental Hotel, Trenasse is one of this city's gems when it comes to new modern Cajun cuisine. 

I went to Trenasse for brunch and indulged in their $10 bottomless mimosas. While I will agree that you must go for their blue crab omelette,  you'll stay for ever other menu item, because they're all good! I started off with the crab bisque and a friend ordered the boudin balls, which are served with a colorful side salad.
We also ordered the lamb chops and grits and grillades with breakfast potatoes. Everything was delicious and priced more along $$-$$$.
Service was excellent, even though it was a little slow due to the full house. 
Looking forward to coming back for happy hour and dinner!

Meh.  Too many things here are just ok, too many to be offset by the extraordinary service.

We waited 1.5 hours for a table, which is a testament to the popularity of Brophy.  The view is spectacular, and the location is as charming as any waterfront pier can be.

The WORST: Calamari is so bad I wanted to send it back. It might as well have been frozen onion rings. And the portion was barely enough to cover the bottom of a bowl. 

The OK: All the seafood, starting with the selections--way too few items on a small menu. What, too far from the water to bring in fresh fish?   First we had oysters, they had to be blue point because that's all they had. Fresh but not remarkable. Tasted cold.  My guests had seafood pasta, $19.  The amount of seafood in the dish was ok, but it looked like spaghetti with things just put on top as an afterthought. I had Mahi Mahi, one of the few fish dishes. It was just ok, mostly flavorless.  

Best: Clam chowder. I thought it was ok, but my guests went on and on about how good it was. Their opinion counts!  

GREAT: The service was one of the most responsive and attentive experiences I have ever had.  

We will go back, but only for the (less expensive) lunch menu and only when it's not crowded.  And only if we have to. The restaurants downtown and the dining nightlife in Santa Barbara rival any SoCal town.  That's where we will go next time.

UPDATE: Just a note to say the owner or manager contacted me privately, and he was very gracious. Both he and the staff have great customer service skills.

Shakespeare once asked ""What's in a name? That which we call a rose by any other name would smell as sweet." Hummm. I do believe that somehow the name we were given might determine a bit of how we approach life... after all--throughout one's life everyone reinforces that word every time they speak to you...or about you...or call you. Could destiny be engraved in our names?

Happy Fish would have never ever being a choice I would have made for this incredible restaurant because I found it misleading. I did not want to go there. A Peruvian place with an English name??? PLE_ PLE_PLE_PLEASE! A couple of my fabulous friends had recommended it consistently, but I kept my Mona Lisa smile and nodded my head fully knowing there would never come a time in which I would go.

I am inconsistent often. Luckily. Happy Fish is a place I would return to plenty of times. The quaint corner place in the side of a shopping center deceives you. My GPS kept repeating "You have arrived at your destination" as I caught myself mouth wide open and left eyebrow rose in mocking incredulity. I became immediately skeptic, but as I opened the door I saw the place was packed with Latin American foodies. I breathed and returned smiles welcoming us. We were lucky because we took the very last table available and then a line began to form outside. People did not seem to mind the wait. The little place is decorated with colorful murals or Peruvian landscapes. The music was perfect too. We were greeted by the owner, Kevin, who cleaned, served, cashed, ordered, greeted and waved goodbye. He is on top of this very busy and wonderful eatery. Even when waiters had assigned tables they moved around and asked and served whoever needed anything.

Of course we had Ceviche. We ordered two of them: Fish and octopus. Fresh seafood like few around here... The Sangre de Tigre (the white sauce of ceviche made of a tad of evaporated milk, tons of lemon juice, garlic, fish stock and onions) became the perfect gravy for the tostones (crunchy fried plantains). We could not have enough of this sauce. We asked Kevin what we ought to order and he recommended Peruvian usuals: Jalea de yuca (a huge platter of calamari, shrimp, oysters, fish topped with Yuca smothered with onions and lemon juice), Pargo frito (the best red snapper I have had since I moved to Tampa from Puerto Rico), and Arroz Chaufa (Peruvian style fried rice.) Please refrain from eating anything since the day before so that you can try to finish any of these dishes... We ate as if the Apocalypse was near; and we brought a lot of food home. We had seen our neighbor's dishes and were cautious with our ordering. There were five of us. We ordered for four... and Kevin has not realized how much money he could save if he was a tad less generous. Costumers would still flock regardless of the size of the portions. The seafood is so fresh. The taste so unique and truthful.
As I roughly shook the glass sangria jar to enjoy my last glass of it, I pondered about the name... Happy Fish. I should have asked Kevin... or maybe not. I would use my existential probing as an excuse to return. Come to think of it, my seafood was perfect and it made me happy... then again Pescado Feliz does not sound as cute.

Don't ever eat here. The food is greasy and nasty. Was surprised how fatty all 3 dishes were. French onion soup was a bowl of cheese with a little soup for garnish. A flat bread was similar, heavily cheesed and hard to eat much, no finesse at all. Worst of all just heard that the owners have decided to be mercenaries for the vaccine companies and aggressively force their own healthy customers wear masks in the restaurant, even to the point of telling customers to leave the restaurant in the middle of dinner for not wearing a mask to the bathroom. Smart business. You can keep your nasty food. If you read the insecure owner's bizarre replies to anyone criticizing the quality of the food or service, she blames them for her issues.  I guess the joke will be on her when the doors shut soon on this place.

Certainly a Locals Bar, but there is nothing wrong with that. 

We came in for some pre-game drinks after breakfast, and ended up coming back after we left the game for one more drink.  Bartender was really nice, and definitely poured a much stiffer drink then most of the places I went to over the weekend.  Everyone was friendly and chatty and we weren't treated like outsiders.  

The bar is very diverse and you can feel a sense of community with all the locals, everyone knows everyone and seem to get a long well at this local watering hole.  We didn't eat but it seems on Game Day or maybe it is just Sunday mornings they offer a little complimentary breakfast buffet which was a nice touch.  Pricing was fair on the liquor, and they have $2.50 pints of PBR.

If I were a local, this would definitely be my jam.

Great Service & Great Food!!!

This was our first stop on Broad Ripple.  We decided to order a couple of appetizers while we hung out waiting for some of my husband's colleagues.  We ordered the the fried Wisconsin Cheese Curds, and a bit later ordered the loaded fries which they let us customize (Axed the nacho cheese and got melted cheddar cheese instead and added brisket).  It is bar food, but it was pretty dang delicious.  I mean how can you go wrong with fried cheese curds?  And our loaded fries were delicious, and definitely glad we switched out the cheese.  

They have a massive bar, with a massive selection.  They are known for the large variety of Long Island Ice Teas, seriously there was like 20 to chose from and they serve them in a picture.  They looked amazing, but that really isn't my jam.  Service was great and very friendly, definitely felt welcomed here.  We ended up coming here for one more drink after we had left the piano bar, and again though much busier everyone was still super friendly and the service was pretty dang fast.

I would definitely come back here if I were in the area, would be a great spot to watch some games and have a Sunday Funday.

This place is great! 

They have the best tasting chicken wings and fried chicken tenders in the area.  The sauce options are all delictable and well varied to appeal to many different tastes.  I love the pepper jelly.  It is my favorite.  I need to try some different ones but the pepperjelly is so good I have not really gone through them all.  I have tried the thai chili glaze and it was delicious too, but, pepper jelly is better. 

The onion rings are made fresh, well seasoned, and thick sliced.

The French fries are what I classify as steak fries but they have a nice airy texture and are really good.  They are served tossed in house made cajun seasoning.

The restauraunt is very small with a few bars to eat at long the walls and two larger picnic tables outside.  They do a lot of togo business.  The drink selectioms are primarily glass bottles.

A note on the chicken wings: they are not those freakishly huge chicken wings; they are on the smaller side.

The experience here was top notch! I came here with my family for my sister's birthday. They decorated the table with rose petals and balloon shaped confetti. The restaurant also gave her a card. All the servers and staff wished her a happy birthday, which she really appreciated! It is definitely a great place to come if you are celebrating something special.

I ordered a glass of wine. They have a huge selection! I settled on the New Zealand sauvignon blanc and really enjoyed it. To start, we shared the calamari and truffle fries. The truffle fries were perfectly crisp with a great thickness. The calamari at first glance seemed a little plain. It does not come with any sauce, but it is so flavorful that it doesn't need it! The red peppers with it are very spicy. I like spicy but be warned if you don't!

For my entree, I had the American Maine Lobster tails. It came with two good sized lobster tails. They were so tender and the melted butter was super warm and tasted great with the tails. We shared mashed potatoes and asparagus for our sides. Everything was top notch! Even thought the items are a little pricey, it is what you would expect at a steakhouse and the quality is worth the price. 

We were too full for dessert, but they brought over a complimentary dessert (small versions of their cheesecake and flourless chocolate cake) with a candle for my sister's birthday. It was very nice and she was kind enough to share. The cheesecake was amazing! It has bruleed sugar on top which made it really unique. Next time, I will save room and get a piece all to myself!

Overall, this restaurant exceeded my expectations. Matt, our server, was excellent, as well as all the staff that helped us. We will be returning for sure!

It is moments like this (or everyday actually) that I thank Yelp for existing. While in Philly for the weekend, my boyfriend and I decided to be on the quest for the perfect Philly Cheesesteak... (okay, we only had room to stomach sandwiches from two different locations) and Yelp lead me right to Dalessandro's. Although it was a 30 minute detour backwards from where we were going, I knew from the hundreds of positive reviews that I would not regret my choice. On the outside, Dalessandro's looks a little run down and nothing out of the ordinary. A small diner with seating around the kitchen, and not much standing space. But inside, the place is full of energy with non-stop people coming in and out, the delicious scent of the cheesesteaks being cooked, and the ladies shouting people's names and people getting their order taken.

Pro tip: Call in your order while you are on the way so you do not have to wait as long. The wait was about 20 minutes for me and I only ordered one cheesesteak with no additional toppings. Also, when they ask you if you want seasoning in your sandwich.. that means salt and pepper, so yes. You probably want salt and pepper on it, they also give sweet peppers on the side for free!

So when you get into the little shop, it's a little confusing. There's just a whole bunch of people standing around and you think they're trying to order.. but they're not. If you haven't called in to make an order, just walk all the way to the front and someone will happily take your order. Once you've had your order taken, just take a walk outside(there's outdoor seating) or just wait at the back of the store, because your food will definitely not be ready yet. It gets kind of crowded inside so I recommend waiting outside (my anxiety was kicking in from how close people were getting and how many people were just walking in and out.. strange I know, I'm a  New Yorker.. I should be used to it). 

The first bite out of the cheesesteak reached my expectations and far exceeded it. The meat was soft and warm. The cheese was melted. The bread was crunchy with mayo (my kyptonite). I only had a half but thought that it was extremely filling for an amazing price! For the popularity, they could definitely put a premium on these sandwiches but they don't!

ALSO, if you give them a tip they will all take the time to say thank you to you which I thought was very nice. As others have said, this is a CASH ONLY establishment. There is an ATM in the front of the store.

I initially did not want to go to Two Ten Jack for my birthday.  I'm generally averse to checking out a new place within its first month.  Man, am I ever glad that my wife talked me into it.  (I've only been proven wrong once, and that was with Josephine)

You're really going to want to have a reservation.  Here's the catch: You have to have a part of 6 or more and they stop seating reservation parties after 6:30.  I have never felt more lucky to have a reservation in my life, because by the time that we were seated, there was a two hour wait.

And I understand why.  Like a true Japanese izakaya, you're going to be sitting here and drinking and eating for a loooooong time.  And that is a great thing, trust me.  Our entire meal played out over the course of just under 3 hours, and the pacing was excellent for the most part.

While were waiting for the rest of the party to arrive (and watching the bemused faces of the poor schmucks finding out how long they were going to have to wait), the hostess started talking up some of the cocktails.  They batch-make all of their cocktails, a program that is another fine creation of the team from PourTaste.  What that means in practice is that basically they have mass quantities of mixed drinks or punches if you will available on demand.  This speeds up booze service and makes life easy for both sides of the bar and is all the rage right now.   They also have a ton of beer, both draft and bottles, sake, shochu, and other booze I will probably judge you for ordering.

We finally got our shit together and got seated and we were off.  Drink orders went in and the first course was a delicious moist towel. I opted for the Shochu pineapple/ginger tonic as my first bevvie (the New Belgium Yuzu I split with some friends didn't count as we weren't seated yet).  The server misunderstood me, because I said "I'll take the first batch cocktail" which he heard as "I wanted the Number 1 cocktail", which was actually number 3 on the menu.  It wasn't what I wanted, but was booze, and you're not going to see this guy complain.  I did get a chance to try the pineapple/ginger tonic, and it was exquisite, as was the Bourbon and Spice Beer (the second batch cocktail on the menu, but not to be confused with the No 2., which was actually number 4 on the menu.  Confused?)

Next came the ordering of food.  Unfortunately, there have been some fucking morons who have written reviews bitching about portion sizes here.  Which is what I just hate about Yelp sometimes; everyone has an opinion, even the idiots who just don't know any better.  Guess what?  That's how this place is supposed to work.  Get a shitload of small plates, eat them over hours, share, and be merry.  And at the end, kill that bowl of ramen to sate any last hunger doubts you may have and waddle away with a sloshy belly.  And that is why the small plates are $6-8 mainly.  The Yakitori is $4-6 for the most part.  It's enough to taste and share - not enough to fill you up (that's what the ramen is for, assholes!).

For the first round, we a ton of small plates.  Yeah, so the Takoyaki and Brussells sprouts got left behind.  That's ok.  Here's the deal.  The tofu is great, but you're going to have to distract your fellow patrons if you want to stand a chance to eat from the plate and get every morsel off.  The dumplings were freaking perfect.  And I would recommend getting a couple of orders, because ours didn't last long.  The Wagyu beef is tender, delicious and may be still mooing if you listen carefully.  And the fries.  I didn't order the fries.  I didn't ask for them.  But I'll be damned if they aren't delicious.  They are like deep-fried mashed potato spears served with an amazing sauce.  You're damn right we ordered more.  (and some more dumplings)

Next up I got some sushi rolls, and while some didn't arrive, I was a bit too tipsy to care at the time.  And frankly, I was already thinking about the yakitori too much.

The yakitori?  Everything was perfect.  It was exactly what my body needed at this point in the evening.  It's like the restaurant knew.  Everything tasted so good.  We finally got our Takoyaki, which was freaking amazing, especially with the butter, and the Brussells sprouts, which frankly I think are WAY overdone, but these guys piqued my interest on this cabbage cousin for the first time in YEARS.

Which left us to ramen.  For those that bitch about Otaku South's pricing, guess what, it's more expensive at the $12-14 range.  And also, stop bitching.  What can I say, I got the pork bowl, it was full of lovely things, and made my night complete.  What else is there?  The vegetarians loved theirs too.  

This place is simply amazing but  get a reservation or you'll be standing outside in your lady jeans, scarf, ironic oversized glasses, stupid hat that only Pharrell can pull off, and smoking American Spirits looking all mopey.  Oh wait, you're already good at that.

I think that the people who have left 1 or 2 star ratings here are complete and utter morons. I notice that quite a few of them are from users who have only reviewed one or two places, so the probability is high that they have some competing business that is nearby possible spamming them with negative press - and it sure looks like that if you check the filtered reviews.


First up - the ambiance is fantastic here.  I arrived on a cold-ass day and was craving only comfort food - they delivered.

The cocktail program is ridiculous.  When the server compared it to Patterson House, I think I scoffed out loud, but after seeing the menu and trying out a drink or two, I can honestly say that they are doing some amazing stuff in the craft cocktail sphere, and they beat the shit out of any other place in town, certainly Red Pony; they give a bunch of places in Nashville a run for the money.  They focus very much on brandies, which is something I love, and looking through their selections of cognacs, armagnacs, calvados, you name it - these guys have a very well-curated list.  I was explaining to my fellow guests how back in the day, most of the US used brandy instead of whiskey - so that Mint Julep or Old Fashioned you love was originally made with cognac instead of bourbon.  The server was very well educated and made some outstanding cocktail suggestions.  I didn't get to try their "French Press Cocktails" but have been messing with a hot cocktail infusion siphon for the past few months.  So while I get the concept, I am amazed that someone is trying it in a commercial setting, and again, like nothing else anyone is doing in town.  Which may anger the denizens of Franklin in Spring Hill because it isn't some shitty cocktail made with vodka that is flavored from a chemical factory in New Jersey.  Or shitty draft beer.  Whatever the hell it is that the mouth-breathers feel doesn't make this place "Country Mc Fried and Stuffed Buffet" or whatever else it is they are accustomed to.

When it comes down to the food, since I was just there for lunch, and having eaten at Red Pony the week before, I have to ask "What the fuck were the low starred people thinking?".  Everything was delicious and beautifully presented.  I also loved the plates and cups - clearly everything was chosen with purpose.  And our server Brock was super-knowledgeable and helpful.  Not only was he on top of the history of the building, he was all over the cocktails and food.  And that dude was fast.

Great food, great service, and badass cocktails all served in a venue that is loaded down with character;  I can't wait to get back here.

I'm just going to lay it all out there.

The reason I haven't written a review on this place is that I just didn't want others to find out about it.  

I know, I'm a jerk.  But look, this place is a hidden treasure.  Nowhere else in town can you find a place that sates your Asian grocery, jewelry and Lao food needs UNDER ONE ROOF!  That's right folks, King Market DOES IT ALL!

I had seen this place pop up in my feed a few times, and especially because of the recommendation of Ryan O., but I had never actually made the trip down there.  Then one day I was down that way visiting So Gong Dong Tofu House, only to find out it was sadly closed that day (on a Wednesday?!?).  Did a quick search and  found out that King Market was right down the road!

It's really a cool place.  You walk in, see the Asian market part and off to the right is a full jewelry store - like a mini slightly budget Jared Galleria in there.  And right around the corner from there?  A nook with a bunch of tables and TVs.  As soon as I got there, pretty much every table was packed, but the lady who runs the show, Nina, got me seated right away.

I'd say Nina is one of the great parts about going to this place.  She banters in multiple languages with the regulars, she will remember who you are pretty quickly, she can guide you through the menu very well, and she will help you find new foods based on your previous experiences there.  And she is just a sweetheart.  I'd give her a job in a heartbeat.  So, no reason to be afraid there - Nina's got your back.

The first thing I got there was the Khao Soi with some spring rolls on the side.  The spring rolls were filled with fresh veggies and a nice soft uncooked wrapper with a yummy dipping sauce. And the Khao Soi... oh that soup.... It was a glorious bowl full of veggies, meat, and rich rich broth.  And when I asked for it extra hot, they gave it to me extra hot!  A nice film of hot oil floated at the top and made every bite that much more magical.  It was really one of those moments where by the end, I was ready to lick the bottom of the bowl - no shame.

Oh and the sticky rice - so perfect in texture.  I got the beef larb once, such a cool melange of flavors that I just didn't care about what beef parts they were.  And one day when I was going to repeat an item and Nina steered me to the Chicken Noodle Soup (again, extra spicy to my specifications) and I am convinced that brew could fix anything that is ailing you.  Crap.  Now I can't stop thinking about that soup.  I really need to come up with some new reason to get down there.  This place is vegetarian/vegan-friendly too; my wife has enjoyed the heck out of it so far.

So, as much as I want to keep this joint to myself, I have to share it with the rest of the world.  Or install a soup pipeline from Antioch to my part of town.  Or both.

I really wanted to have an amazing meal here.

I did not have an amazing meal here.

Came here with the wife on a Friday right before we saw Brandi Carlile at the Schermerhorn.  I was also very glad that I had gotten reservations.  I had heard from all of my friends that this place is amazing and that especially Sunday dinner is the jam. 

We started off with cocktails, and I have to tell you, the list is impressive and inventive.  Whomever is consulting with them on this list is doing the right things.  I started off with the "Buzzy Beer" because I've had a bottle of Art in the Age's "Root" sitting in my liquor cabinet for two years, and I have no idea what to do with it.  (side note, it was a delicious cocktail).  And then the server tried to give my wife a suggestion or two on libations, whereupon she mentioned that she loved Yellow Chartreuse the best.  At this point, being the bantery type that I am, I opined that Green Chartreuse was the superior of the two, and that I'd fight her over it.  I was completely kidding.  Just being a goof.  It was like a record scratched.

From that point on in the evening, the server was very pleasant to my wife, but a turbo bitch on rollerskates to me.  Seriously.  It didn't matter how many times I thanked her or said "ma'am", or how polite I was, she treated me like I was made out of dog shit.

So while I wanted to enjoy the cool ambiance, or while I wanted to talk about how frigging delicious the bresaola (cured dried beef) with strawberries was, or how tasty my tri tip I had was, it was all kind of over because of the attitude of our waitress.

I tipped her 20%, even though her attitude towards me ruined the meal, and I'd have to say that if I happened to come here again and saw her serving, I'd turn on my heels and head to Rolf and Daughters, or hell, just about anywhere else.

Last but of advice, bread gnocchi is really not good, especially if you are expecting the delicate, tender, moist, morsels of potato gnocchi that most are used to.  It is like wads of dry bread that will suck the moisture from your head - much more sauce is needed here.

Got a chance to go back to The Catbird Seat, and this time I completed the transaction.

First of all, what really made this night was the company I kept.  I got to take my wife plus some foodie friends that were visiting from out of town.  We had been plotting and saving for this excursion for months.

I'll break it down two ways - One way for the relatively inexperienced, and one way for the bon vivants out there.

For those that are less experienced:

The thing that makes The Catbird Seat work so well, is that everyone, and I mean, everyone knows their shit here.  Seriously.  It would not work if this were not so.  

Don't be intimidated by this place.  Everyone working here is a professional, and you should trust that they are going to take care of you and the food decisions they make will take you somewhere you have never been before.

You have a couple of opportunities in your life.  A chance to do something amazing, to see something, to taste something, to experience something exceptional.  That time is right now. It is here in Nashville.  Seize it.  What the hell are you waiting for?

I've eaten at some of the most amazing places in the country.  I've never seen such a great value for what you get, especially with the beverage pairings.

Do it now.

For the foodies:

Again, everyone working here is not only a pro, but also have social skills.  Let's face it, a lot of people working back-of-the-house are incredibly skilled, but are social mutants.  This gang, Josh, Erik, Mayme, Tom and Jane, all are not only pros working like a Swiss watch together, they are also are great to talk to and not intimidating in the slightest.  I really appreciated all of their friendliness and willingness to show or tell what they were doing. They also didn't hesitate to give me crap for bailing out on my last visit, and I frankly deserved it (and it was funny).

And to add another layer to my trip, I went on the weekend after they spent the week going to the James Beard House in NYC and serving dinner - I have no idea how the hell they were even standing after all of that.  You never would have guessed by the way they were working.

The meal was heaven.  My favorite parts were the oyster with yuzu and cucumber plus the cornbread ball filled with Benton's bacon cream, both from the first course, the short rib with horseradish cream, and the foie gras with snickerdoodle crumbs and blood orange preserves - best meat dessert evar.  And while I am not generally a dessert guy, the real dessert of the oak ice cream, vanilla cake and cherry crisp candy was mind-blowing, especially with the bourbon gel balls that EXPLODED delicious rye-forward whiskey in my mouth.  It was equal parts scrumtrulescent (http://www.hulu.com/watch/3524/saturday-night-live-inside-the-actors-studio) and naughty at the same time.

I should add that my wife came along, we gave them advance notice about her dietary restrictions, and they were able to not only accommodate them (kosher, lacto-ovo pescatarian), but they actually looked (and tasted) amazing too, not the half-assed pile o' fish and vegetables she's used to.

And the incredible part was that even with beverage pairings and a tasty apéritif, (plus a cocktail I grabbed at the Patterson House right before), I was not at all messed up at the end of the meal.  Jane Lopes, if only you could manage my personal drinking life.

And honestly, we had been saving up for a while to get back here, this was my birthday, some of Hanukkah and Valentine's Day all rolled into an amazing evening, easily once of the best gifts I have ever been given and no regrets.

These are good people doing amazing work.  I can't wait to get back to there.

To be clear, this review is just for the bar, Bar 12*21

As one of my pals put it, "It's really just an upscale Applebee's"

THE MOST EXPENSIVE BOOZE IN THE WOOOOOOORRRRRRRLLLLLD.

Seriously, for the price of a Martini, I could buy a fifth of good, dry English gin.   I'm not sure of the accounting that goes into computing their cocktail pricing, but I am pretty sure there are hidden fees and taxing structures - the wife works for the Dept of Revenue and can't figure it out.  

I've never had a bad drink here, but I always look at my check and scratch my head afterwards.

On a side note, I've never had a bad dinner at a Morton's restaurant.

I was so excited for Whole Hog Cafe. I've heard so much about their award winning bbq that I had to try it for myself... I wanted to love this place because I wanted to have a bbq spot that I loved near my home. But this isn't it.

I wasn't impressed with Whole Hog for these reasons

1. The meat was thoroughly unimpressive. We both got the Hog Platter, and it just didn't do it for us. The meat was dry, the beef was too salty for my taste.

2. I expect a bbq place to have a variety of sides to choose from. I like bbq for the sides just as much (if not more) as I like it for the bar-b-que meats. They only offered baked beans, potato salad, coleslaw and cheesy corn. Where was the mac and cheese?

3. I tried all of the sauces at the table and couldn't really find a favorite because they were all pretty boring. 

Another things to point out that are not pros or cons is that they don't have table service, you order at the counter, find you seat and they call you up when your order is ready. 

Pros:

The wait for our order was really short. 

I don't think we'll come back.

The Reading Terminal Market is one of Philadelphia's gems. If you're indecisive (like me) it can be both a dream come true and a nightmare. I found myself in Philly today and thought I stop by to brainstorm on dinner. I found some good cuts of meats, walked around and came up with some side items to go with the entree. There are so many choices that it took me entirely too long to decide but having too many options is hardly a problem (or it is a quintessential first world problem). I grabbed some coffee and lunch while I was there, browsed around a bit more and left satisfied. You can count on finding high quality goods here with prices that rival any supermarket and restaurant, bakery, etc. 

When I left this morning I thought I don't take advantage of the fact that this amazing place is so close to me often enough. It was then that I made a promise to myself to come back soon (and often).

We had a wonderful business dinner here. We were placed out on patio so we had a great view of surroundings. More upscale than most of the restaurants inside the dome of Gaylord. Everything is ala cart.  Be prepared to drop some cash. 

4/5 New York strip, ordered Med rare but was more medium. Great crust and seasoned well. I wish it was cooked better but still enjoyed it. Good size portion 

4/5 filet Med rare but also over cooked. 

3/5 vegetarian in group had cauliflower steak but was not impressed. It's a steak place...but they still need to do a better job on veg due to clientele. 

4/5 Creamed spinach. Very luscious and creamy. Lager potion in bigger bowl than we expected served family style or shareable. 

5/5 Sharable Sauced mushrooms. Larger bowl and perfectly cooked. Small button sized mushrooms in rich deep sauce. 

4/5 Shareable asparagus. Still slightly crisp and seasoned well 

4/5 service. Had main waiter and then his assistant. They poured our wine, kept water glasses filled. Food was not presented to us like you expect at this price point but was ok.

What an incredible surprise!!!  Staying over by Gaylord and specifically took my associates there for dinner while there on business. This is an amazing Thai gem in a town.  Nashville is trying very hard to become a foodie town. Get away from all the fancy touristy places and get the Thai meal of your dreams and come here. Wow!!

5/5 Tom Kha Gai coconut soup w chicken. Smooth soulful refreshing and delicious. Great start to a magnificent meal. 

5/5 crispy duck on curry sauce. If I could give 10 stars I would. Crispy, juicy, delicate yet sitting on silky red curry with veg and colorful ornamental carrots. Came w heart shaped rice. A must try and truly unique.  Not found on many menus in USA. 

5/5 Pompano with herbal sauce. Ordered Thai hot (5 on a 1-5 scale). Whole fish fried then topped with a very authentic Thai herb sauce with fresh green/ black peppercorn on stem, real birds eye chili's whole along with chunky sauce of your dreams. Fish was crispy outside with soft white flesh inside. The fish was grinning from eye to eye while I feasted on it. Very happy. ( I was very happy too!)  

5/5 Mussels in curry sauce. Arranged in large circle with plump juicy mussels and ornate veggies. Curry was silky smooth, sour sweet and hot. 

5/5 service was amazing. Very gracious ladies. Very attentive. Packed house and they served us like we were the only ones there!  Loved them. 

5/5 Ambience. Ok. The place is a recycled old building that has been there for ever. You know what?  They have just enough nostalgic old Thai items hanging and on shelves that when you walk in you go....yep this is going to be really good. You know that feeling right?

Ask for spice tray. It has a bunch of options. Sambal, thai chilies in fish sauce, ground Thai peppers etc. 

Don't be intimidated. They have your standard Americanized Thai dishes. There is a color pic of every item on menus. But get a little out of your comfort zone.... get something you can't pronounce and try it. You will have a great experience here. I will be back very soon. This is a gem. You are lucky to have the Nashville!! Cheers.

Ok, I'm not a huge fan of beer, but my husband really wanted to try this place and now we are both hooked! 

Trying the Basil Ryeman and when in season Walk the Lime are both musts! I am obsessed with the Basil Ryeman and it is definitely my go to beer there! 

I wish they would open a store in Murfreesboro where we live! I believe they have started serving a small array of food, but they always have Moose Head Kettle Corn and try it or you'll be sorry you missed out. They pair so well with the beer!

It's an awesome place to chill out. They have a lot of room inside as well as outside. They typically have some kind of live music and there is a dart room in the back. 

Reasonably priced and the staff is very knowledgeable as well as friendly.
