From a dance club- a "Party Bar" uses a big dance floor, DJs playing recognizable dance hits and quick serve (limited selection) bottle beer & mixed drinks.

Yes, I see "Woo girls" http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woooo!_(How_I_Met_Your_Mother_episode) , bachelorette parties and tourist wanting to party and I understand that.

Yeah, I thought of this my last visit while sitting back enjoying the 1/2 priced Buffalo Chicken Nachos for patio happy hour till 7 PM.  I find it funny that I gained perspective away from the Big Daddy's Landing weekend late night chaos.  (I am a fan of the late patio happy hour & sometimes the weekend after midnight insanity.)

BONUS- Buy a "I'm a virgin (this is an old t-shirt)"

Who doesn't love a hot bowl of pho on a cold rainy day? This place is right across the street from Harrah's and has minimal street parking. Lucky for us we found a spot right across the entrance. 

Looking at the menu their prices are way cheaper than the bay area which made me wonder if the quality or portions would be compromised to reflect the prices. I was pleasantly surprised as they had really good food and standard portions. One thing different about this place compared to the bay area was that it takes a long time for your food to come as in 15- 20 minutes long.  

We ordered: 
- Fried wontons (8) $3.95: this was actually very tasty. What I loved about the dish was that they took the time to leaf then wash romaine lettuce to pair with the wontons. Their sweet and sour sauce dip was ok, but I was surprised at how meaty the contents were and how crisp the wonton skin was. Definitely a must try. Just writing this makes me crave it!
- #1 Xe Lua large $7.50: rare slices of steak, well-done brisket, flank, tendon, tripe, and beef balls pho. They had good meat portions with deeply rich soup. The soup wasn't oily or murky, but rather clear and rich in flavor. This was a good dish, but the noodles were slightly under-cooked.
- #7 Pho Tai small $6.50: rare slices of steak pho: as with the above dish the meat portions were good with very good soup flavor. I can tell they spent a lot of time making the soup and it was well worth the time waiting for our order to arrive. The noodles for this dish was perfectly cooked. 
- Iced condensed milk coffee $2.50: pretty standard drink. 

Overall, great spot for a hot bowl of pho and amazing price point and quality. Just make sure that you have the time since the wait time is longer than other pho places.
From the other reviews. Line is long but fast, service was pleasant and relaxing and what I needed for a breakfast. Omelets and biscuits and pancakes were good and filling.

For a coffee shop, the taste of its coffee is just as important as the aroma of its environment.  I would say that Shaw's Coffee LTD has both of these qualities to make it as one of the top coffee houses in St. Louis.

I visited Shaw's on a Saturday and I just loved its cozy setting for a lazy afternoon.  I always get the house coffee for my 1st cup at a coffee shop to test its flavor and my 1st cup of Shaw's was full of boldness and smoothness.  Loved it!

One thing that I do like about the setting was that there are a lot of seats & tables inside and outside the shop.  Whether it may be their high tables with bar stools or the corner couches with low coffee tables, each section of the store has its uniqueness to it.  (See pic)

Only downside is that the coffee shop closes at 6PM on weekdays (Mon - Thurs) - which is way too early for a grad student like me, who needs to stay up late to finish my readings.  But I am definitely coming back here!

It seemed like the place had it all - a variety of caffeinated drinks, special pastries, hot sandwiches (expensive - $9),  LCD menus, a fire place, outdoor seating, etc.  But my experience was just "A-Ok."

I tend to evaluate a coffee shop with its house coffee and I would say the coffee was just average - slightly bitter.   I was doing some reading on a late Tuesday night and the indoor was packed with SLU students - which was expected.  But there are just too many seats - especially high bar stools that were closely placed together.   I was literally touching elbows with the person next to me - which felt awkward as a junior high swing dancing time in P.E. 

Glad to find another coffee shop that's open til midnight, but I will probably be going back to Coffee Cartel.

Recently featured on Man vs. Food - I drove 30+ mins from the West County to check out this popular place.  Me and another food enthusiast arrived around 7PM on a Fri night, so we had to wait about 30mins before a table opened up.   But we spent our entire waiting time to  decide on what to order.   Let's just say that since their menu was filled with innovative and out of the box items, this research time was needed.

So here's our verdict after ordering ~$60 worth of food between the two of us:
We are definitely coming back again and again to try all of their unique smaller items (other double dogs, sammiches, and sides) instead of ordering big items like Prime Rib, Roasted chicken and such. 

We ordered:
1) Prime Rib - flavorful and respectable, but I wouldn't say that it was the best that I had.
2) Zarzeula - again good, but not the best Seafood stew that I had. 
3) Monte Cristo Double Dog  - now this was absolutely fabulous. Being a Chicago native, I do have a high standard of a dog.  But this double dog still has me drooling. This awesome creation was made of two double franks, topped with melted cheese, and served with a generous amount of strawberry jelly.  It offered a perfect combination of salty & sweet flavor!

I am planning to go back in a week, so more reviews on their items will be posted!

My biggest downfall on writing Yelp reviews is that when I like a dish from a restaurant, I always order the same one.  And I become loyal to it and I remain faithful to it forever.  So you may not get a comprehensive review on this one, but you will definitely know one fabulous dish to order from Lemon Grass.

Lemongrass is a Vietnamese sit-down restaurant located on South Grand along with other Asian restaurants.  The menu is not overwhelming and the items are quite inexpensive.   The reason why I go back to this place over and over again is their:   RICE IN HOT POT.  It is somewhat similar to Korean Dolsut (hotpot) Bibimbop, but it does have a unique flavor with their brown sauce.  (see pic)

The whole idea behind a hotpot is that your food will stay hot until you finish your  meal and the best part  is that the layer of food that is closer to the surface of the pot - usually the rice - will cook longer creating a different flavor and texture until your last bite.  You gotta try this delicacy for $9.99.  

My friends ordered other dishes - lamb curry & sesame tofu - and they were pretty good too.  I would say Pho is a hit or miss. Sometimes, it was good and other times, it was sub-par.  

The service is just a-ok.  It's not the friendliest or the most efficient, but I really do show up here for their food - to be specific:  Rice in Hotpot. :)

I would not usually consider eating a dinner on Sat night at an unknown pizza place in Maryland Heights, but what a pleasant surprise Serra's turned out to be!  I was thankful for another Yelper's choice to eat here!

The atmosphere is definitely good for family & casual  dining.  You just gotta show up and enjoy their St. Louis style thin-crust pizza.  We ordered the Serra's Supreme pizza and it was loaded with sausage, pepperoni, onions, bacon, and mushroom.  Simply delicious! And I would say what places this pizza joint over Imo's or Cecil's is the quality of their ingredients.  All the veges were fresh and the sausage reminded me of Lou Malnati's in Chicago (the best deep dish pizza IMHO).  

The service was prompt & friendly. Our bill came out to be about $9-10 per person.  Not bad at all.  Random favorite oldies that were played from the jukebox were charming as well.  Highly recommend it.

Nam son? More like Damn son!
This here, ladies and gents, is the best banh mi shop in all of Philadelphia. 
The bread is straight up perfection - so soft, so crunchy, and so fresh. I would recommend that you eat your banh mi right away to completely bask in this amazing experience. I took it to go one time and it wasn't as crispy compared to eating it on the spot. I've always ordered #1 because that's just how I take my banh mis, but my partner recommends the BBQ pork (note: flavorful, but a little fatty). 

I've also ordered their iced Vietnamese coffee, avocado smoothie, and mango smoothie. My favorite out of their drinks is the avocado. They use half of an avocado and it's extremely creamy and not overly sweet. The Vietnamese coffee was also notably good.

I think every time I chow down on a banh mi/smoothie combo, I'm in a severe food coma afterwards. Their serving sizes are nice and hearty - and for ~$9 per combo, how could you not eat here every day?

The service here has always been very pleasant. The employees always have a smile on their face and seem to enjoy working at you know, only the best banh mi shop in Philly. NBD.

There's only two tables in the bakery but that doesn't mean you shouldn't bring your whole squad here. 
But really, bring all of them here so you can all be part of a great banh mi bonding experience.

Well if you like bartenders who make fun of you and talk sh$t about you to other patrons. Go here. 

This was my first time here and I had been excited to check it out. I didn't know what the bar theme was just that it was this cool new place. So I joined my friends. I had heard from my friend their specialty drinks were pretty sugary, which isn't my thing. No big deal, I was digging the vibe and and since they have a FULL BAR and I saw they had Bullet bourbon - on the FRONT SHELF, and that it was nearly empty, I obviously wasn't the only person who had visited there that had ordered bourbon. I asked for an old fashion, as fall is in the air and it seemed like just the right drink to warm me up. The bartender offered their "rum" version, I kindly said I'm not really a rum drinker and say just the regular would be great. He then begins to complain that he'd have to go to back to get the ingredients, ok that's odd, so then I say "I'll just take it in the rocks then if it's easier" he then states no, no I'll do it. Ok I figured, well I offered. As I wait for my drink and watch him make it, first I noticed he never went to the back, AT ALL...but the real kicker here is.... he starts talking to the patrons NEXT TO ME about "what idiot comes into a rum bar and orders bourbon" I looked at my friend and was like "are you kidding me???" I say loudly "I can hear you" and he doesn't notice....so he continues to BASH ME thinking I can't hear him saying "why don't you just go somewhere else" and even states "it's like going into Hattie B's and asking for something other than chicken..." - news flash it's NOT at all like going to Hattie B's because they literally don't have anything else!!! You have a FULLY STOCKED BAR YOU F-ING idiot, but I'm not allowed to order what you literally have??? 

At this point I am fuming, and highly offended. Apparently he kept saying sh$t and I had walked off to find some type of management. Literally all I did was order an old fashion, THAT IS IT! ...not.one.other.word.

I found someone and calmly explained that one of their bartenders was out of control. Explained along with my friend that it needs to be addressed. Don't be a bartender if you only want to make certain drinks. So the woman was super nice of course and seemed genuinely sad this had happened. I showed her who it was, she got us shots and we stayed to finish our drinks. 

Still being pretty upset over how ridiculous this guy was, my friend realizes this isn't just any bartender, this guy who was RUDE, DISMISSIVE, MADE FUN OF ME, was none other than....wait for it...THE OWNER OF 308!!!! THE OWNER!!!! ...and a partial owner of Pearl Diver...whhhhaaattt??? Now I'm officially pissed, because I love 308 and always have a good time there. I couldn't believe it was the owner himself who was so horrible to me for just ordering a drink. Some example to set for your employees. I took a pic of him so I could show you the bartender to never order from...even more sad this guy owns businesses and he thinks this is an appropriate way to treat people. 

Look if I was rude, wasted or caused a scene, sure I could see it. But this was my first drink there, and like I said, I offered to just get it in the rocks. I'm still so offended as I had to sit there and listen to him make fun of me. Unreal. 

I just have no words.

FANTASTIC! This place is the real deal. An awesome seafood place literally across the street from the beach. It's super cute on the outside and inside, and all the staff are super friendly. 

I tried the seafood creole and HOLY COW was it fantastic! Like literally SO good. The seasoning was just perfect and it all tasted so yummy, it was a party in my mouth that I didn't want to end. The coconut shrimp are really good too. The key lime pie had a great flavor, but the crust wasn't the best so it didn't have the whole effect in my opinion. But I really enjoyed this place- it's a great post beach option or if you just want some dang good seafood!

Whatever* you want, I swear that Whatever Pops will have it.. If you want a refreshing sweet treat, they have it all- açaí bowls, smoothies, milkshakes, grilled cheese, waffle on a stick, handmade popsicles, coffee, do you get my gist?

Don't "whatever" me on this review, because I am so serious. This place is wholly amazing. It's quirky and full of personality, and holds one of the best açaí bowls I've had to date. I take my açaí pretty darn seriously, and I don't give out compliments like that lightly. But this was so FRESH, so bursting with flavor and just perfect. I wish I lived closer so that I could stop by at least several times a week just for the bowls.

The grilled cheese was fantastic too- again, just so fresh and real and setting the standard for how a grilled cheese should be. The coffee was okay, and I was so tempted to try literally everything on the menu. Waffle on a stick? Come onnnn. Whatever man, I am certainly coming back for more!!

I thought I knew beignets. I've tried them before a couple of times at different places. And then I came to the famed, deep-rooted Cafe Du Monde. Game. Changer!

If there is somewhere to go to know what a real, true beignet tastes like, then it's this little old cafe right here. I think sometimes people come in with way too high of expectations for the overall experience. This place is anything but fancy, very straightforward.

It's not a visually appealing cafe. The well known green and white stripes are everywhere, but that's about as far as any decoration goes. The outdoor courtyard is quite spacious, and covered, but it stays filled up. This is as bustling a cafe as any you'll come across (for obvious reasons).

The menu is equally stripped down and simple- beignets, coffee, and water. But baby, that's all you need when you're coming to Cafe Du Monde. Oh, well, you can actually buy some merchandise too, of course! And at home beignet mix- how fun!

I just still can't even believe how good these dang beignets were. We probably waited 15-20 minutes in line to order, but it was well worth it, and the beignets were still hot and fresh as ever when we got them. And prepare for a MOUNTAIN of powdered sugar- there is no such thing as "not enough" here! It can make for quite the messy eat as well so beware of the clothes you wear. But once again, totally worth it.

As long as you don't expect a picture perfect visit, I think any person will love Cafe Du Monde. It's not an extravagant place, the workers can be a little brash and unfriendly, but the product speaks multitudes for itself!

The German Knodle is a splendid little place tucked into downtown St. Pete. It's probably a restaurant I've passed a handful of times without ever really noticing it, but it is certainly worthy and pulls its own punch.

It made me so happy how authentic it is- our waiter, who I assume is part owner? was so sweet and genuinely excited to share the menu with us. When we ordered he kept saying how we made such good choices and how much we'd love the food. He wasn't wrong.

I got the currywurst. The curry sauce was absolutely phenomenal- I wish I could've taken home just a pint of that to use on all kinds of food. Though I wouldn't say German is my cultural food of choice, this place serves it about as good as it comes. Support local small businesses!

I was nervous that the food wouldn't be good as the restaurant is very hyped up, but my worries were for nothing! The restaurant is set up super modern and cool, the decorations are so pretty and fun to look at. The fish bowl drink was absolutely delicious and so fun, not too sugary like I expected. The food was pretty good too! It's definitely nothing mind blowing but it could also be a lot worse. The sliders were normal burgers but still alright, and I really enjoyed the pancakes. 

The desserts are the show shopper for sure though- we got a strawberry and cheesecake one and a s'mores shake and they were both DELISH and had such amazing presentations, it was delightful. The workers were very friendly, especially Donovan, one of the tables bussers, he was so kind and funny and enjoyable. 

This place is DEFINITELY on the spendier end, more of a once-in-while, celebratory place to eat than a casual dine in, but I had so much fun! Also a heads up it is located in the Hard Rock Hotel in Tampa on the second floor right above the Elvis piano, which I added a picture of.

For fast and friendly service, hit up the SCD on Carrillo! Its central location and online ordering makes it a great place to grab a fast lunch in downtown Santa Barbara.

I ordered my usual, a chicken caesar salad sammie on Italian, online and by the time I got there 10 minutes later, my order was nearly ready. Because there aren't a whole lot of seats there, most people were also waiting to pick up salads or sandwiches. It's very smart of them to have a giant, fully stocked drink fridge, pastries, and chips lining the counter at the front, because in the few minutes you're waiting for your order, your stomach starts rumbling and you start eyeing those kettle chips a little ravenously.

Chowing down on the sammie, I was pleased to learn that this location also has giant portions and doesn't skimp on the dressing, either. Their breads are typically toasted very well and have plenty of structure to them. And thankfully, unlike one of the last times I got SCD in I.V., my chicken came fully cooked. But to balance it out, this chicken was oversalted and somewhat overseasoned, making me really thirsty and causing a stomachache later on.

That aside, I love SCD and I'd happily come back to the Carrillo location over the I.V. one. Massive portions for $10 just can't be beat.

Sushiya was once a formidable foe for healthy gut bacteria. Ever since its ownership takeover in 2016, it has since become a formidable foe for my wallet. There were certainly lumps and bumps along the way, from my co-workers' experiences with the place, but it seems to have truly improved in quality.

I ordered a dragon roll and California roll, while Emily L. purchased a snow cone roll and tempura California roll. Paying $20 (including tax) for just two rolls left me with a bit of sticker shock, even if it made for a nice dinner and midnight snack. No bowl of miso soup would ever make me reconsider that thought! I think the quality for our food, however, was solid. The eel was broiled wonderfully. While the roll was drenched in too much unagi sauce, I think it was a solid choice given the crunchy shrimp tempura and crab meat. Crab salad was mixed with quite a bit of mayo. Both rolls were incredibly filling.

I tried some of Emily L.'s snow cone roll, only to find out shortly after that we got the wrong roll (hence the star subtracted). We ended up with something with baked salmon and broiled cheese, with a hint of spicy crab salad. Nonetheless, it was tasty. 

New to the menu is a wealth of Korean dishes, including promising spicy seafood ramen and tofu stew. These dishes all fall within the $10-20 range, topping out at a platter of bulgogi for $17.99. It's way more expensive to order on SB Menus, so you should suck it up and place an order in-person.

Who knew that one of the best places you could take your parents for a nice lunch was an unassuming seafood restaurant in Goleta?

In town for a day, my parents were there to celebrate some good news. My mom picked this place for a not-so-pricey lunch that would satisfy us all. For $50, we got three salads, a grilled fish sandwich, grilled sea bass plate, and a special seafood pasta.

The veggies in the salad were pretty fresh, as others have noted. We steered clear of the crab salad and it appeared to have been a good choice. The fried/mashed potato pancake side was also tasty, according to my parents.

Entrees themselves were cooked thoroughly and in delicious sauces. I highly recommend ordering the seafood pasta, which is tomato-based and comes with a slice of garlic bread. Seafood in the dish includes mussels, clams, squid, baby octopi, shrimp, and a white fish. My parents, who are much healthier eaters than I, also thoroughly enjoyed their grilled fish options. The main detractor was how salty all of our entrees were -- although I totally dug the tomato-based pasta sauce, it felt like my seafood was still drowning in the ocean it came from.

I'm not surprised by the tough reviews, though. It was waaaaay empty when we were there, but definitely slow considering that we were the only table in there. Our waiter seemed pretty out of it when he took our order; my dad ordered a smoked salmon sandwich and got a grilled white fish instead. We didn't want to run it back for fear of it taking too long.

The lowdown: go for the handwritten menu items on the trays littered around the floor by the register. Hate crowds but love eating creatures of the sea? Come here.

We muddled through the meal, alright. So did Chili's.

They have a slammer of a combo: two smokehouse items, roasted 'street corn,' fries, pickles, and a 'chile' garlic toast for $15.99. It's $2 more if you want a half-rack of ribs, or if you want to add a third item. I ordered the smoked bone-in chicken breast smothered in BBQ sauce and crispy chicken crispers. In perhaps a superhuman feat, I finished all of this save the pickles, which my friend reported as having a slightly tart cucumber flavor rather than tasting like a true pickle.

In order from good to bad, I'd rate the chicken crispers as the best chain restaurant take on chicken tenders and the best part of the meal. The fries were well-seasoned and plentiful. The roasted 'street corn' has quotation marks around it for a reason: while one side was slathered in butter, mayo, cotija cheese, paprika (...?) and lime, the other was plain and merely steamed. The garlic toast was just some soggy Texas toast with garlic butter, living up to Chili's reputation as the microwavers-extraordinaire. Don't talk to me about how dry and weird that chicken breast was.

I only got through all of this because of their weak $3.13 margaritas, which they offered on their 43rd anniversary on March 13. But hey, with roughly two margaritas in me, it was more than enough food to absorb the damage the cheap Presidente tequila did.

The service was admittedly awful. While our server was very friendly, he constantly forgot about us: five glasses of water took one reminder and 20 minutes to come out, two to-go boxes turned into one, and we were unable to even locate him in the restaurant half of the night. Seriously, I see why people spend so long here.

A fast place to get a sandwich, that's for sure. My review is mostly for grabbing pitchers and fries here, since those are the only times I've ever encountered the service here.

My friends and I came on a Wednesday, bummed that the crowd at Woodstock's had ran us out of pint night and unanimous in avoiding Rincon, where we'd been a few too many times recently. Sam's serves one of the most expensive pitchers in I.V., but it's on Pardall, and we didn't feel like venturing down to Pizza My Heart or dealing with the loud people at Lao Wang. If you want a cheap pitcher, don't come here.

They were out of their only cider option when we came at 8 p.m. (Boooooo.) We went with a little-known IPA that we can't remember the name of anymore, but it was fairly strong and not the worst tasting of beers. Despite having such expensive pitchers (we paid $25 for one and more than $20 for the other one), they provide flimsy plastic disposable cups for use. I mean...I'm not about moderation or ruining the environment. It can't be that much harder to get some non-disposable plastic cups if we're concerned about breakage, right?

They ran out of our second-choice beer the second time we went back for a pitcher, but they at least gave us what they'd tapped out in addition to the pitcher we eventually went with. 

On the bright side, the fries were fresh out of the fryer and delicious.

I'd heard some pretty sad things about the KBBQ place that inhabited this location prior to Kimchi's arrival, so I was more than willing to make the occasional trip out to Gen for quality AYCE. 

Let's talk meat. Honestly, you won't need to purchase anything more than the $16.50 package, because that comes with the essentials: brisket, bulgogi, beef belly, and pork belly. All meats are fresh and marinated in-house, according to the servers. With enough patience and careful flipping, the miso pork belly easily stands out as the best, due to the sweet marinade.

The $16.50 package also gets you access to warm japchae, steamed egg, spicy tofu stew, and sweet and spicy fried chicken. A friend who's never had steamed egg loved watching it come out bubbling in clay pots, and enjoyed the sprinkle of green onions so much that he ordered two more. Those platters of Korean fried chicken also made the rounds more than once.

As a party of six, we understandably had a lot of complications with orders and demanded different things at different times. However, I feel like there could be a better system in place for servers at Kimchi, given how small the establishment is. It seemed like our orders were constantly being taken by different servers, which could have resulted in a 20 minute delay in getting our last plates of meat at the end. The servers were very friendly, though, and accommodated our large, somewhat last-minute party.

Street parking isn't too hard to find, but if it is, their private lot is in an alleyway around the back.

The lack of ventilation and grotesquely loud music makes dinner more of a shouting match than quiet affair. But hey, we're here to stuff our faces, not make small talk.

3.5 stars rounded up for me. Although I'm a big fan of the food they serve and the happy hour pricing, I wish I'd gotten better service.

This trip to Enterprise Fish Co. started as a mission to investigate whether they still did $1 oysters during happy hour on Wednesdays. The simple answer? Yes. Emily L., Sama R., and I ordered half a dozen for starters and ended up getting a whole dozen, which was more than we wanted in the end. Cocktail sauce here is spicy, and the oysters are pretty fresh. I'm not a big one for raw oysters, but they were cheap!

The entrees, on the other hand, got much pricier. My fried seafood platter, which came with calamari, fish, shrimp, scallops, and baby octopuses, was a hit at $24. Dipping the shoestring fries it came with into some of Emily L.'s lobster bisque ($9 with a golden puff pastry topping) was absolutely heavenly. I also tried a bite of Sama L.'s scallop risotto ($27.50). That bite was, without a doubt, more creamy and rich than I expected from high quality mac and cheese, no less a good risotto.

Service, unfortunately, was really hit-and-miss. We were seated in a section that had an assigned server, but our server didn't come by very frequently. My friends and I ran out of warm bread quickly, and upon our attempts to flag down our server and check on our missing drinks, we didn't have one to find. When we could find her, though, she was very sweet and accommodating.

We checked in on Yelp for a free glass of their house lager, but were told that it was only one check-in per table. Our server also had no idea this was a thing until she consulted her manager, which delayed our happy hour plans a bit.

Enterprise was still a really funny dinner experience, though! Mishaps aside, it's a good place to get a seafood dinner around here that avoids the roar of other touristy destinations.

Yellow Belly's brunch menu prices are by far some of the most affordable in the county. I'd put them in a different sphere than Cajun Kitchen Cafe, I think, because they do trendy at a really low price (especially if you use your Axxess card).

Before driving back home for the holidays, my significant other and I came here to grab brunch. Saturday at 11 a.m. is high tide in this neighborhood, but we snagged a parking spot in their back lot. They weren't at capacity, so we chose a table on the front patio, watching sleepy stragglers stroll into the breakfast and coffee options on this strip of De La Vina for a hangover fix. Our waitress took our orders and brought out drinks swiftly. Love the fact that they keep the menus on the table. There's never a shortage of menus or awkward waiting around for someone to pick up enough menus and a notepad and bring you to your table.

In next to no time, our dishes were out. He got the breakfast sandwich with roasted potatoes, which was gooey, eggy fun once the yolk broke and ran all over the toast. The arugula was fresh, a big plus. Unfortunately, the cook had committed the sin of forgetting to season the potatoes. We had to hit it with a good shake of salt and pepper, and it would have really benefited from being tossed with some herbs or garlic to brighten the flavor.

I got the cornbread benedict with bacon and fruit cup. Having heard so many things about how amazing this dish is, I can certify that it is indeed, pretty awesome. Red pepper flakes made for a good kick when mixed the hollandaise, and despite my apprehension about the softness of cornbread making a messy base, the flavor pay-off was worth it. I especially enjoyed the thick-cut, practically candied and roasted bacon. 

A big draw of Yellow Belly's brunch is that the affordable plates and limited menu give way to their expansive drink menu, including non-alcoholic ones for people like us, who were about to hit the road, and fun booze, like beer floats and cheap bottomless mimosas.

This place is probably more fun late at night, so I'll have to update this review if I ever come out here for drinks.

When places like WakeCup and Ice Milk Company first moved into Isla Vista, I deemed them acceptable for the area. However, when Highway moved in not too long after, the allegations that this was the best boba out here in the Goleta/Santa Barbara area piqued my interest. Having tried their drinks a couple of times now, I can confirm that their taste can't be beat.

The not-so-great: the drinks are expensive, reflective of imported tea leaves and rent. Customer service is sorely lacking. On my last visit, there were two people at the front -- one woman who was aimlessly surfing the Internet on her laptop, taking up space right in front of the register, and a male employee who had to reach over her to punch in my order and make it. Hey...if you're not employed, maybe sit in the back or at the limited seating so that people don't get confused.

Working my way up the chain of good stuff, though, the karaoke comes next. My friends have booked one of their karaoke rooms before and said that while it was expensive and the song selection isn't the best, it's still a good experience and possibly the only one of its kind. Like the drinks, it's also a lot to pay. Booking an hour runs upward of $30 a person.

The drinks I've had here (all one-size only, by the way) are the sea salt cheese roasted oolong tea, Thai tea, and golden milk tea, all with boba. Here's my definitive ranking of the three:

Sea salt cheese roasted oolong tea with boba: Skip the boba, but the rest is delicious. The cheese acts as a filter for the brewed tea, adding a savory, rich quality that is so addictive that you can't stop sipping. Even without the cheese, though, the tea itself is great. Very nutty, very full-bodied flavor. It's over $5 for this one, though. Ugh.

Golden milk tea with boba: First thing on the menu, and it's $4.75 for a cup. Ask to turn down the sweetness on this. Although not listed on the wall, getting it at 75% sweetness is the best way to taste the tea. Pearls here are made fresh and laden with brown sugar syrup, so it'll kick your full sweetness cup up to like, 125%.

Thai tea with boba: Average. Tastes like your typical Thai tea, creamy orange color and all. I'd go to Ice Milk Company in I.V. for this drink instead.

They have a stamp card, so if you plan on making many happy returns, I would pick this up. Large selection of magazines, if you intend to loiter, but this place gets drinks out very quickly, so I recommend you grab and go.

Get. The. Torta. Cubana.

Carrillo is one of the busiest streets in downtown Santa Barbara, yet Cuernavaca has gotten away with being a bit of a hidden gem in plain sight. At dinner time on a Friday, the line was just starting to pile up, and there was no doubt that it was the kind of place where the locals know best. For less than $20, we ordered three tacos and a torta cubana.

I have never felt such an urge to marry a sandwich. The thick layers of avocado, marinated pork, and milanesa, in conjunction with the ham, tomato, and cheese, really made for the best dang sandwich I've had in a long time. Not only did it make for a beautiful stacked sandwich photo opp, it also was the first sandwich I thought was well worth the $8.95 price tag in a long time. 

Surprisingly, the tacos were the most disappointing part. I ordered a lengua taco to accompany my torta cubana and was not impressed. While the lengua was soft, it was incredibly fatty and chewy, which I was unaware could even happen when the tongue is a muscle. There was too much liquid, which soaked through and tore my tortillas in half. Adding onions helped with the textural problem, but didn't salvage it.

The interior was clean and had ample seating. There was a decent salsa bar (no free chips, sadly) as well. We noticed that the lighting was kinda funky inside. Although dark and almost romantic, the lights there were shone directly down on the tables, causing us to squint to make eye contact. But hey, no lighting's going to stop me from eating another torta cubana.

Wit wiz! 

I've been here twice and I keep coming back. It it's any consolation I drive from NYC Just for one of these sandwiches, and I'll continue to do it!

Unique, flavorful, with a special surprise for dessert. 

I was amazed by the range of options at Lee's Deli, and all were delicious! I had the Rule Breaking Cheesesteak (with fish and shrimp and grilled veggies) and it was SO GOOD! It had some kind of special mayo that I loved (and actually used for my fries because it was so good). 

At the same time, my girlfriend had the chicken fried rice, which she loved, my mom had the Korean BBQ Cheesesteak, and we had the New Bay fries which were so flavorful too. Everyone's food was so different, but we really liked all of it. 

For dessert, we loved the carrot cakes, and bought a few to take home. The carrot cake icing is even better than the icing on the fancy cupcakes I am used to in New York or DC. 

Lastly, I was really impressed by the staff. They were kind, helpful walking us through the menu options since there are so many, and really nice about helping us wrap up some leftovers at the end (you get lots of food for your $). 

While this was my first time at Lee's, I will definitely be back and start to work my way through the menu.

When we visited Suegra Saturday night it was with much anticipation.  We had read all the articles hyping the upscale farm to table "authentic" Mexican fare created by a James Beard award winning chef.  Has to be fantastic, right?  Mind blowing even.  The reality.  Way underwhelming.  And at almost $150 for two with tip, way over priced for the execution of the food.  So many other places in Tampa Bay for great and creative Mexican for far less money.  Having said that the restaurant just opened last week so it may be working on getting things right.  I can tell you we will not be back until they receive a ton of credible, positive reviews.

The Interior:

The interior is nice enough.  Not surprising since the investment to convert the former Cityfish over to Suegra is evident.  This is intended to be a big impact place.  Unfortunately they have several things to fix to get it right.  First, they need to pay more attention to their reservation integration with Open Table.  We had the option of selecting an outdoor or indoor table and selected the outdoor option.  We were seated at an indoor table nonetheless.  And the entire section we were in had incredibly poor lighting, causing us to have to use our phones to illuminate the menus.  The waiter apologized and told us they were aware and going to fix the issue.

The Food:

Our meal started with a complimentary trio of dips served in what appeared to be small pewter pots, served with tortilla chips.  The bean dip was touted as the star and it was.  Sort of a dip version of frijoles, or refried beans. Along with this was a red salsa that came with a warning that it was spicy and a green dip that was vaguely familiar.  The red salsa was good but far from spicy, even for the more timid.  The green dip reminded me of a weird variation of a tomatillo based salsa verde.  More on the sweet side and not spicy at all.  Over all the three dips were good.

For our appetizer we ordered the red snapper ceviche.  Now let me mention I love ceviche, my favorite being the Peruvian versions.  I have also had Mexican, Puerto Rican, Colombian, Spanish, and many Americanized versions of the dish.  What I have not had was a deconstructed version of the dish, until now.  It kind of worked.  Kind of.  The fish was fresh and by itself had very little flavor having been only slight marinated.  Most ceviches have seafood marinated in citrus, garlic and or onions, chilies, cilantro, etc.   In this case the ingredients were all separated on the plate.  The fish in one area, grilled avocado in another, sliced citrus in another, some cilantro leaves on top, and a couple habanero slices and a whole pepper rounding out the plate.  In order to get the flavor profile of a traditional ceviche one has to take a slice of each ingredient on the same fork.  Individually the ingredients were far less than the sum of their whole.  Overall not bad, but definitely not going to sway me from a great finished ceviche.

For our entrees I ordered a filet accompanied by a chipotle sauce.and my girlfriend ordered the chicken fajitas.  The quality of my filet was readily apparent and the only win on my plate.  I ordered it medium-rare and it was, tender, juicy, and with a better preparation the potential for a knockout.  Unfortunately it was served over two uninspiring flour tortillas and drowned in an absolutely cold, overly sweet, and thoroughly uninspiring brown sauce.  It reminded me of the interpretation of a mole sauce by someone definitely not of Mexican heritage.  I love chipotle peppers and cook with chipotle en adobo frequently.  This was awful and I would have to see it made to be convinced there was any chipotle included in the preparation. 

I'm definitely not a fajita fan, but my girlfriend felt like this was worth a try.  The biggest miss on the chicken fajitas was the clunky cut of grilled chicken.  Since the concept of a fajita is basically a wrap, the slices of chicken should be conducive to that.  In this case it consisted of huge strips of unwieldy, chicken finger sized strips.  Beyond that it just wasn't very interesting.

Since the idea here is semi-a-la-carte we ordered a couple of sides, the Mexican Street Corn and plantains.  I wish we had asked more questions.  If you Google "Mexican street corn" you will be directed to dozens of hits on elote, an amazing Mexican version of grilled corn on the cob with crema, white cheese, and chili.  What we received was what happens when an American takes something magical and tries to one-up it to a complete failure.  A bowl of corn and other ingredients that just wasn't inspiring.  Worse yet all the sides were cold.  The plantains were served in a weirdly sweet brown sauce, like a bad platanos maduros.

Another bad sign was the table next us returned their entrees, so this was not a one off that night.

The best part of the entire meal was the $15 Picante Margarita, which was delicious if pricey.

Overall, massive miss.

Life changing is how I would describe this meal.  If we had these up North I'd go as often as I could.  I had been dreaming of this ever since I read about it   The line wasn't too long and we got in relatively quickly.  I ordered the hottest sauce and my Daughter got a medium.  We each had fries.  I got the black eyed pea salad and she got the Mac and cheese.  You get a number find a seat and they bring you your grub.  Mine was awesome from the vet first bite.  The flavors and juiciness beyond compare.  Then can the heat which was up there and made me sweat but did not suppress the flavor of the hot chicken. The pickles were the perfect accompaniment as was the white bread.  Beer selection of local brews was quite good as well.  You can sit outside or in.  We sat outside which was great at the picnic style set up.  Merchandise available for purchase as well.  Got a shirt next time I'm getting a hat.  Must visit if in Nashville.  Please come up North you can literally print money if you do!

I love St. Louis BBQ.  Pappy's smokehouse is my new fave.  Waited in line to get in which didn't take too long.  There was a sign indicating they were already out of burnt ends.  So if you want then get here early.  We were directed to the register to order and pay.  We ordered a full rack of ribs, one brisket platter and one pick two brisket and pulled pork.  Each platter comes with two sides.  We each got slaw and fries.
We were seated inside right near the smokers which were outside.  You could tell this was serious BBQ.  The food came out relatively quickly.

The ribs were in a word delectable and might be the best I've ever had the meat was succulent, cooked well, nicely seasoned and came right off the bone.  Fries were nice and crisp and the slaw was a very vinegar based slaw which I prefer to creamy slaw.  The full rack was too much to kill off so I took it to go.  My wife had the brisket platter and was mad their were no burnt ends left but she enjoyed her meal.  My Daughter had the pulled pork and brisket and was very pleased.  It's a lot of food.  Next time 1/2 slab for me.  Water is serve yourself.  The place is great.  I'd come back again in a second.  My only advice is fine early and be ready fir a nap afterwards.

First off no reservations.  Deal with it so worth it!  We put our name on waitlist on line and checked in with the hostess.  She let us know we could sit at bar right away or wait.  We chose to wait and it wasn't long before we were seated.  I had been dying to try the ribs but they were out.  So I ordered the Bestie combo of brisket and smoked chicken wings with braised cabbage and fries.  My Daughter got brisket and pulled pork with fries and Mac n cheese.  Massive delicious plates were delivered.  Also we ordered fried pickles.  Surprisingly they had fried chips and whole smaller pickles.  I liked it while she preferred the chips.  The food was so damn good.  The wings were dry rubbed and juicy with that smokiness I love.  The brisket was fantastic I left not a crumb.  The braised cabbage was very tasty but I couldn't finish it.  Fries were outstanding and needless to say no room fir dessert.  Also combo comes with a yummy popover.  Service was top notch and I appreciated it.  Also tried one of the excellent bourbons the Four Roses small Batch 2020 who was delicious and worth the price.  Next time I'm in St. Louis I will be back here and I'm getting my ribs as well as all their sauces.  Huge fan hope they open a franchise in north east.   If you're in St. Louis run don't walk and enjoy.

We had olio recommended as a must visit.  We booked a spot on the patio not knowing a chilly and blustery night awaited us.  There was a heat lamp and an umbrella but it was fairly miserable outside.  I was surprised that they didn't offer us indoor seating as restaurant wasn't full.  Be that as it may the meal was excellent.  We started with Moroccan olives, shisito peppers, and Tzatziki.  Small bites to get started.  Next we got the hummus deluxe with lamb and pitas.  Never had meat in my hummus before but I am a fan now.  Every bite a sheer joy.  We also had the burrata served with focaccia which was yummy.  Then we had the Jerusalem bagel with Labne and pomegranate which was exquisite.  That probably was enough food but we had ordered main courses as well.  I had the Musakhan which was a delicious turkey thigh with a sumac spice rub.  Couldn't finish it but it was wonderful.  My Wife ordered the Chicken Sunnis Kefta meatballs which she said were fantastic.  My Daughter got the gyro sandwich.  The desserts looked interesting but we couldn't eat a thing.  The drinks were excellent as well.  We had the Amaro Manhattan which was damn good.  So in shirt, food excellent, service very good, street parking available.  I'd come back.  My only negative was sitting outside in the rain but the food is top notch so I'd come again for sure.

We came here after a big lunch at Hattie B's that was a mistake.  Not because the food wasn't delicious but because we were stuffed.  Started with the biscuits and jam which was sublime.  The fluffy buttery biscuits were amazing.  The jams: Strawberry; peach; blackberry; tomato; grape; and butter were so good.  Then we had the deviled eggs with: bacon; pimento mayo; pickles; chow chow; and I forget what the other one was.  Delicious but then we started to hit the wall.  Had a nice Tennessee pilsener which was light and refreshing.  I ordered the Southern Burger which was a pimento cheese burger with a fried green tomato on top.  It was really good but after two bites I was so full that I had to call it a night.  Ditto for my Daughter who got the enormous pork shank which she said was delicious as well but she couldn't finish it.  I'd come back here just for the biscuits alone.  Servers were nice and friendly.  Live country music was great as well.  Lot of fun I. The Gulch.  Check it out.
Just moved from Cali missing great sushi. This place is amazing not missing Cali sushi anymore. Go here even if you just like sushi you may leave loving it!!!!!!

Photos/videos DO NOT do this food justice OK! And one thing's for certain! Pretty girls CAN cook! Well these ones sure can! 

I've been trying to get to this place and see what all the hype was about for months now. This past Sunday we took a chance and prayed,yes prayed lol, that it wouldn't be crowded. It was! Lol but luckily we were able to grab 2 open seats at the bar. 

Decor is too cute! I love pink so I COULD be a bit bias but it's so adorbs, from the gold accessories and pink diamond lanterns adorning the bar to the pics and wall of some of the most influential African American women ever, it was a pleasure to dine in an experience PGC. 

Soo again they were crowded! But if it's not crowded that's when you should rethink your decision. Glancing at others plates on our way to the bar- yes I do this all the time lol- I knew we were in for some good eats! Food took about 25-30 mins . These pretty ladies we're moving fast! Waitress was personable and grabbed us waters before we even asked. While I'm on beverages, try a half lemonade half sweet tea. Thank me later. They also offer mimosas but I didn't see a drink menu.

So about the food, my mouth was watering watching other people's plates come out- if you sit at the bar you have a front row seat to the pretty girls cooking. Ordered the Aquarius jawn ( that's me btw. I'm an Aquarius and a philly jawn lol) which is shrimp and grits in a nutshell...amazing!!! The creamy sauce was everything! The hash brown casserole was scrumptious and bubbling when it came out. My bae ordered the crab omelet which had great flavor but could've been cooked a lil less;was a lil dark for her taste 

I plan on returning for the fish and grits and French toast. 

Trust the hype and just go! 

Wasn't too hard to find street parking a half block away off girard ave.

LOVE this new location. Lots of shaded outdoor seating, and the option to sit in indoor seating open to outside or fully inside (if that makes sense). It's walkable to tons of midtown shops and bars, including a new bar next door. Friendly service and great pizza, as always. Came here with a group for lunch and got the PB&J which most of us already knew we loved, along with a couple of random slices. One friend got a side salad that looked delicious. They lost one of our slices on the way to our table and quickly replaced it with a slice twice the size. So even the bad turned out good, which is one of my favorite ways to identify good service. Overall, a great addition to the neighborhood.

I went to Larry's again this past weekend for the first time in a couple of years and I was really turned off. Gripes are as follows:

1. Where are the drink options? It's 2010 get a fountain already... 80 cent cans of soda or $1.50 for orange/apple juice. I can't look the other way on this because Larry's is DINE-IN or takeout. A can is cool with a slice otherwise it's uncivilized for a sit down spot. A can is for sitting on the front steps of your house.

2. $6.45 for a cheesesteak? The meat was SPARSE! I had a bald spot at the end of my roll. WTF? Some places have the decency to cut the bald spot off as to not offend anyone. It's like damn am I not good enough to have the steak cross my whole roll? You're gonna do me like that? The fries were great nice and crispy, but also SPARSE for the price ($2.50 I think?).

3. Flies... no matter what time of year I go this place has flies (guarding the pickles, peppers, and ketchup). Are they imported? Where do you even get a fly when it's 30 degrees out? I don't trip over a fruit fly or 2, but these were the real deal. The 1st time I came here to dine-in this fly would NOT let me be. I think we got reacquainted this past Saturday.

4. Given how busy the place was and how many people were coming and going they should have been more diligent about keeping the floor, tables, and utensil area clean. When I came in I had to wipe my own table... (last one available) no problem. When I left half tables were freed up, but they all needed wiping. A line has to be drawn somewhere. A cloth has to be whipped out sometime.

Overall, I spent like $12 for a steak with no bells and whistles, fries, and a drink. I know they have money over at St. Joes but C'MON. If I ever go back, I'm gonna stick to the slices (plain mind you...) and grab a drink @7-11 around the corner.

And I apologize if I missed the fine print for a steak and fry combo. It would make me feel better somehow knowing this was my fault.

I came here on a Friday night because this is one of the few spots that play my kind of music, hip-hop. We were going to do a round of drinks and check out other spots. Walked in and ran into an old friend who happened to be celebrating her birthday party so I decided to stay. Big Mistake!

Birthday girl was sitting at a table (which was not a VIP section). We ordered one round of drinks from the waitress. When the bill came, I didn't even look at it. I just paid and tipped her 20%. We've been in the industry so we always give a good/fair tip to fellow food/beverage servers. 
After the first round of vodka and tequila, me and the girls started dancing. We were ready for a 2nd round. Waitress was no where to be found so we ordered from the bartender. Paid her and tipped. The waitress finally came around. She then gave me and my friends an attitude. She said "You are not allowed to order from the bartender. You can only order from me or you can not sit at the table." Excuse me, If that's your policy, you can explain it nicely. On top of that, we weren't trying to sit at her table; we wanted to groove. AND, it's not a VIP table, we should be able to order from anyone. I'm looking at everyone that is sitting at her tables, no one was ordering drinks; they were just sitting around babysitting their one cocktail. 
I ordered a 3rd round from waitress with the attitude and this time when the bill came, I looked closely at the receipt. They automatically put 20% gratuity on their bill. THIS AIN'T MIAMI!!! This is Philly. That killed my vibe especially since her attitude was stank. I was trying to celebrate with my old friend so I put on a happy face anyway. But this whole time I've been tipping you 40% that you did not deserve
My last round I ordered from the bartender because the waitress couldn't be found- again. Tipped her cash and paid with credit without realizing that she too stuck 20% gratuity on the bill automatically also. 

Unacceptable in Philly. Unheard of in Philly. Especially in Vango... It is nowhere near fabulous in case you're wondering. Service was not good. Go to Rumor instead. They have a hip-hop room.

Goodbye Vango. You just lost a hot customer who drinks well and tips well.

So, Brasserie had closed for a bit and is under new management I believe. Brasserie has always held a special place in my heart; the beer: phenomenal. The environment; rustic and relaxed. I wanted to surprise my boyfriend with a date night to the newly opened Brasserie!

It seemed like much hadn't changed and things were business as usual. (This is not a bad thing. I'm a creature of habit and was excited to see some of my favorites still on the menu.)

So, let's talk beer first. My boyfriend ended up with the Framboise Sauvage to start. It was a tart sour! Still very good, but if you're not into your sours being superbly tart, you may want to skip this one. I started with the Migrating Tulips. I found it had a big raspberry flavor but that was about all I got out of it. I ended up with the Framboise myself.

We started off with the Housemade Soft Pretzels. I do not think they treat their pretzels with the baking soda/water mix that would give them a toasty color common for pretzels. Our pretzels were good. I would say though, a little gummy. While I did not care for the beer cheese, my boyfriend loved it. I'm a mustard girl all day. Overall, we found these pretty okay. I don't think we would order these again; it's all about the Brasserie Poutine.

For dinner, my boyfriend ordered the Seafood and Sausage Jambalaya. I'm a spice wuss and this definitely wouldn't have been something I could finish. Every aspect, in my opinion, was hot. The only complaint we shared was that the muscles tasted very briny/oceanic. When I get muscles, my usual desire is buttery/melts in your mouth. Overall, my boyfriend enjoyed the meal down to the last bite.

I ordered the Argentine grilled flank steak for my entrée. My meal sort of missed the target for me. My over mashed potatoes came cooled off, which was a slight bummer. The Chimichurri had a massively vinegary/garlicky taste. Now, I'm not a chimichurri expert so take what I say with a grain of salt. I felt like it just overpowered any other flavors. I was glad to be finished with that at the end of my meal as I'm not one to leave my plate with bites left. I'd ordered the flank steak medium rare- sadly, there was not too much pink. The last couple bites were pink, which had this steak been totally medium rare, it would've amped up the plate tons for me.

Last but not least, we got the hot housemade brownie. From the previous, my boyfriend remembered an ooey-gooey brownie. We felt like this came slightly dry and our bourbon caramel sauce tasted... burnt.  :(  We looked at each other right after tasting the sauce and were a little disappointed. The ice cream though, was amazing.

Overall, I think Brasserie is still figuring some things out. They kept the menu but haven't got things dialed in quite yet. I look forward to going back. We did eat everything and we did not send anything back. Good food still, just a couple misses.

7/10 recommend

I will say that I loved going into GADCO for their instagramable moments. The space is so eye-catching and the plants in the window are an amazing view. 

I would always get a donut or two but honestly, they were never anything special. Just a fried yeast donut with a glaze over then an Oreo or some other kind of candy propped on top. Again, nothing special. 

But, I cannot keep supporting their mediocre donuts after how terrible their owner is on social media AND in person. I understand Yelp is about the food and service but the way a business operates and interacts with the community IS JUST AS IMPORTANT AS SERVICE IN THE RESTAURANT. 

This business owners literally asked someone "if they're were r*tarded". WHO SAYS THAT?! It was so disheartening and so uncalled for. I just can't support that kind of language from anyone and I definitely will choose not to give my money to them. 

Please see the screenshot attached to this review as the owner has since deleted all their comments on their social media. It happened. It was wrong. It deserves to be called out. 

CHEERS!

Café Milano never disappoints so for my lite evening snack, I combined two items from the Flavors from the Far East menu, Shrimp Chow Mein Cantonese and Shrimp Chow Mein Cantonese and my choice of soup was the Egg Flower Soup. 

Everything was delightful however the pan fried noodle was a bit too crispy to my liking.

DO NOT OPEN A TAB HERE THEY WILL TAKE OR LOSE YOUR DEBIT CARD.  If I could give this review 0 stars, I would.  The incompetence and attitude of the staff and bartenders was enough to safely say that we will never return to this establishment again.  

I was in town for a bachelorette party and our Uber Driver highly recommended we check it out if we love dive bars.  The atmosphere was a really cool outdoor messy garage type bar with dollar bills and bras hanging from the ceiling and old couches and school desks for seating.  We loved it at first...

We ordered 3 shots from one of the bartenders, who we quickly realized that he was under the influence of something and wasn't remembering anything we asked him to make.  I opened a tab and asked if I could still order from the other female bartender on the patio side of the bar and he said yes.  She made a stink about it, but I understood and told her I'd order inside no problem.  

As the night went on, I went to go use the one-stalled ladies bathroom and saw that there was a plastic holder for a toilet bowl air freshener that fell into the toilet so I went to the bartender that had opened my tab and told him of the problem and his answer was "oh I'll deal with it later".  I warned him that all the drunk chicks at this place probably weren't going to be courteous enough to wait and his answer to that was "yea women are disgusting".  Cool bro... way to screw over your co-worker who I ran into later in the bathroom plunging out a crap storm in the tiny little stall with a huge line of ladies waiting to use it.  Unbelievable.  We then all had to take turns watching the door to the men's room for each other while the guy struggled to clear the mess in the ladies room.

When I went to close my tab at last call, the female bartender looked for my card and told me that there was no tab or card with that name.  Seeing as I needed to fly back out to Chicago the next day, you can imagine how panicked I was.  I told her who I gave my card and she said that they had sent him home.  I asked if they could call his cell and see if he accidentally put it in his pocket or where he remembers putting it, she looked at me like I had 5 heads.  Then two "bouncers", if you can even call them that, started yelling at everyone to head towards the exit.  I said I need to wait and see if they find my debit card, their response "not my problem, time to go".  EXCUSE ME... but YOUR employee either took or lost my debit card in YOUR establishment.  Who's problem is it then?  

Then as our party left, one of the bartenders drunk friends shoved me as I was walking out... ARE YOU FOR REAL?!?  WHAT IS THIS PLACE????  Don't over-serve your employees and their friends.  

It's such a shame that they are so inexperienced at owning and running a business because the place could have been cool.  Another customer told me that it was a family business that's been passed down a couple generations and that it's slowly being run into the ground... tragic.

This restaurant might be great for the wonderful snowbirds, tourists, or the retired, as they do seem to make up most of the clientele.  It's not very catering to the locals and the younger patrons. 

I live about 30 miles away and often fish at Anclote with my kids. If we don't catch anything, we then grab something to eat, usually at Hella's or Rusty Bellies. I was with my youngest daughter this time, we didn't catch any trout as we hoped (although you never know what you will catch at Anclote), and I wanted to try a different place. I asked a gentleman who works with the dolphin tours to reccommend a place and he suggested Dimitri's.

I was wearing light sweats and a tank top and my daughter was wearing shorts and a shirt with short sleeves. She was wearing sandals and I was wearing sneakers sans socks. This is normal average apparel for those who come back from fishing, and matched what other patrons were wearing, give or take. After being seated by a female at the front of the house, a male manager (possibly the chef) about my age told me I had to wear a full shirt or we would be thrown out and he didn't want to embarrass me in front of my daughter. (Please remember, we had already been seated.) He had his hand on my shoulder and suggested I wear my daughter's shirt as I have a larger chest than my daughter.  (We both had our dry swim clothing over our shirts and pants.)  Nice manners.

I ordered the leg of lamb and rice without tomato sauce. I love Greek food, but it's a personal preference to not have tomato sauce. Both were doused in it. My daughter's octopus was drowned in olive oil and was mushy from being boiled too much. The grill couldn't save it. Our waiter insisted we order certain things such as the Saganaki that we simply weren't interested in. 

I will never again return.  The service was aggressive to put it mildly.  If you're in your 30's or younger, especially with kids, I suggest you go somewhere else.

So first off I want to say I am totally rooting for Morrow's. Black owned business in an area quickly becoming gentrified. I love the idea of local black people keeping tradition alive throughout New Orleans.

That being said... service was absolutely terrible. I came in with my friend from Chicago who works in the service industry about two weeks after opening. My friend tried to parse through what could have been going wrong but it really just turned out to be a mess.

1) we ordered drinks and food at the bar immediately. Our drinks took 15 minutes, well my friend's did. Our bartender came back with my friend's drink and told me she didn't have what I asked for. So I ordered something else. That took about 10 minutes. This all while the bartender talked casually with her friend at the bar. The bar was completely packed yet she thought she had time to talk with her homie sitting at the bar. So 25 minutes for a drink. Strike one. Don't forget we had already ordered our food, me chicken wings and my friend ordered a cup of gumbo.

2) 45 minutes later, my friends gumbo finally made it out. My wings were no where in sight. When I asked my bartender about my wings, she looked confused, almost like she didn't know that I ordered them. She went to the back and appears to have put an order in on the fly for me because something had went wrong. Strike 2. Meanwhile a man sitting at the bar next to us knew the manger and had saw us waiting for now what was almost an hour for chicken wings. He told the manger and the manager/owner offered to bring me a cup of gumbo on the house while we waited for the wings. Gumbo was pretty good, wasn't mad at it.

3) finally the wings came. They had a good flavor and appeared to be tender but they seemed to be undercooked, raw. So I ended up picking at the skin. Strike 3. We finally were able to get our check between the 2 breaks our bartender managed to go on during our time there. She charged us for the comped gumbo. I just knew that was going to happen. Clearly the manager never told her about comping my gumbo. Strike 4.

Glows: food is hit or miss but the gumbo was good.

Grows: please get some type of training for staff. It was a hot mess of confusion for all involved. 
Put professionalism first. There seemed to be a lot of talking and socializing of staff and very little customer service going on during a very busy time. To go orders were mixed up and sat for almost 20 minutes before the second part of the same order came out.
Turn the music down. It was almost club level loud. It's a restaurant. There is no dance floor.
Look at the price points. A salad with iceberg lettuce shouldn't cost what it did.

I will give another try because I really want to support black owned businesses in NOLA. My boyfriend's separate experience was slightly better. Service makes or breaks a restaurant and I would hate to see this one go down because of a lack of training for staff.

It truly saddens me to write this, but I now have no love for Al & Stellas.  After my first visit we enjoyed the food so much my fiancee and I tried to set up our rehearsal dinner for our upcoming wedding.  We were about to put down a deposit when my mom asked if the price of $55 a person would include tax, tip, NA Bevs and desserts.   The woman who I was dealing with seemed to be offended that my mom thought $55 should include these things and just responded "we are not going to do this, wish you the best".  This was after a month of planning with the restaurant, including picking the menu, wines and other options.  :(

Thanks, we were at the point where we were about to put a deposit down literally that day, then because my mom tries to negotiate on the price you tell us to take a walk.  I now have to start all over because you do not know how to operate a business.  Great food will only get you so far, this is the hospitality business and your actions were some of the least hospitable I have ever experienced.  They have great food but don't expect the staff to be professional or hospitable.

Stella I will miss your gnocchi.

An hour away from one of the parades in NoLa, we needed something to eat before we kept going for the night.  All restaurants were packed, and with long waits.  Thankfully we saw Dat Dog.  There was a line but it moved fairly fast and we were able to get the last table, by the bar next door to the ordering counter, and enjoy our food.

I got a regular hot dog, and cheesy tater tots on the side.  
He got a gator dog with creole mustard and craw fish etouffee on top.   this was interesting and actually good.  

For a quick meal, without the long waits, this was pretty good, and a place I would keep in mind next time I'm in town.

This review is specifically for the bakery. I recently got married and of course, needed a cake. I was stunned about how expensive wedding cakes are (and I only wanted a small cutting cake, not a big fancy tiered cake). I decided to check out Whole Foods and found out that they have an awesome bakery with experienced, professional cake decorators. I set up a tasting, and it was a great experience! My fiancé and I were able to taste all the cakes, fillings, and frostings. Because we ordered our cake there, this didn't cost anything! 

We picked out flavors and the baker also had some decoration suggestions. I felt confident that my cake would be great, and it was (see picture for proof)! It fit in perfectly with my wedding and got a lot of compliments, and it also tasted incredible- better than any wedding cake I've had. If you're getting married (or need a cake for anything really), look into getting your cake at Whole Foods! It will be less expensive and better tasting than anywhere around.

This was a cute little coffee shop with a relaxed atmosphere. It was a mid-Sunday afternoon and it was somewhat busy, but tables were still available. 

It was my first time going here and my barista suggested the Aero Cappuccino since it was hot outside and I was in the mood for something cold and refreshing. It definitely hit the spot! The aero cappuccino is not like a Starbucks Frappuccino at all. It wasn't as sweet, but one could tell it had less ice and had more of an "airy/cloud" texture to it. It was delicious and something I would definitely order again on a hot summer day! Their menu had some very different ways of serving coffee, so it was intriguing enough to make me want to come back and try their other menu items. 

Service was very friendly and I didn't feel rushed at all. Instead of just presenting me with their new/specialty drinks, the barista asked me what my personal coffee preferences were - thumbs up for that! She got started on my drink right away and it was served quickly.

A great staple on Howard Ave. known for their packed bars and sushi we grabbed a seat outside and were immediately greeted by our server, Aaron, who was wonderful. I have been a handful of times and remembered their magnificent Champagne Sangria, may as well order by the pitcher! 

Aaron guided us through the menu and we let him take control of our meal, what a fantastic job! We had a couple of sushi rolls, never a let down here. The most surprising was the chicken wings, they were unbelievable! Honestly, I think they must be the best in town. Who knew! We were in and out in less than an hour, just before the sparkly shirt D-bags started showing up. 

Watch for Groupons, also their Free Shot Check-in was honored. I will be back for the Wings and great service from Aaron!

ENHALE ONLY

My very first visit to Naw'lins Cafè du Monde French Market (est 1862) was back in 1994. Back then all the table servers seemly were Vietnamese. Made it an early morning meeting spot for friends and colleagues back then.

I call their piping hot power sugar covered beignets "cocaine donuts". As for their iconic coffee, it's coffee black or au lait (with milk). Roasted and grounded root plant called Chicory is added to the coffee to tone down the bitterness.

It's open 24/7. My favorite times to are on rainy day, early morning and late evenings. There's something very enlightening about view of the horse carriages in front of Jackson Square and St.Louis Cathedral.  Maybe it's the Chicory and "cocaine donuts" taking effect. LoL

JAMES BEARD AWARD KING CAKES

Four decades ago "Village de l'Est" was home to several thousand Vietnamese. The common denominator was Versailles Arms Apartments where many of them were housed and the Catholic church (Mary Queen of Vietnam). A hurricane and oil spill has done its economic toll on this Vietnamese community. 

Dong Phoung manages to stay put and continues to make their banh mi, traditional Vietnamese street food and their award winning king cakes. Now there are many other Vietnamese bakeries and restaurants in the Delta.  However, Dong Phuong still remains the gold standard.

HAVE MY CAKE & EAT IT TOO

This wonderful market is stocked with all sorts Louisiana groceries that I just can't find in Las Vegas. Plus whenever I do need pasteries or a cake (my fav chocolate thunder) for a birthday, their bakery is as good as it gets in my books. Other things like cut flowers and Mardi Gras decorations are much more reasonably priced.

Its not far from my hotel on Canal Street, and many of my favorite restaurants are within several block radius of this market. You might surmise that I take the time to walk there.

IT IS WHAT IT IS

If I didn't have so many dang gummet early morning meetings; and I could have a client within walking distance of the hotel; and if they were open on weekends ... I WOULD ABSOLUTELY EAT HERE EVERYDAY.

A second generation diner serving blue collar home cooked cajun styled grub that will make you want to sing "Hallelujah". If it's your first time, definitely try their infamous CBB Special (Cajun Egg Benedict). There is nothing dainty or pretentious about their food or portions.

Amen ... nuff said.

Umami Craving? Try Pho Eden

Umami is the "fifth taste sense," that flavor that isn't sweet, bitter, salty, or sour, it's something else. I often crave umami (a piece of fresh mozzarella with fresh basil is very umami, for example) and I think a lot of folks do, they just don't have a name for it. Umami is a satisfying richness found in meats, cheeses, and certain kinds of mushrooms. Pho Eden restaurant offers a variety of dishes that offer fulfillment for your umami craving.

If you live in Camden County or nearby parts of Burlington County, you needn't cross the bridge to find great Vietnamese food. If you aren't sure what "umami" tastes like, your next meal out should be at Pho Eden in Cherry Hill. I eat at Pho Eden at least twice a month, sometimes more, and never tire of it.

It is a shame that I have been there probably 100 times now and cannot tell you about 95% of the menu. Here's the problem: once you find something you like, you will start craving it and ordering it every time you go.

I almost always order the vegetarian summer rolls, #102, to start off--they are just beautiful--fresh and fragrant with a delightful peanut sauce for dipping. The fried spring rolls are also fab; it's fun to wrap them in lettuce before dunking in the sweet and spicy sauce. 

Pho is a rice noodle soup. It comes in a huge bowl and is a meal in itself. You can get it plain or with several different kinds of meat, including eye round, chicken, brisket, seafood, or pork. Some friends of mine swear by the #304 Pho Tai (rice noodle soup with eye round steak). It comes steaming hot with the pink steak floating on top; the steak cooks in the broth and turns brown before your eyes. I have been trying not to eat meat, but I can never resist taking at least a spoonful of this sublime broth. It is not greasy. It just tastes so full and satisfying; I think it defines "umami."

For a while I was getting the Pho Ga (chicken noodle soup), which if you like chicken is fabulous. You can also get the vegetarian version, #302, pho rau cai, which features a variety of fresh vegetables and a tasty tofu. The soups are all served with a side dish of fresh coriander, bean sprouts, hot peppers, and lime, so you can adjust the taste to your preferences. Many also add hot sauce to the equation. For me, the sprouts, coriander, and a few squirts of lime add yet another dimension to the flavor. With prices ranging from $4.00 for a small plain noodle soup to $7.25 for the large seafood version, a meal of pho is a delicious bargain.

In another review of this restaurant here on Yelp, I recently read that #652, the hot and sour tofu soup, is also fantastic and addictive, so I will be trying that next time. Thanks for the tip, Brandon! 

For those who like chicken, I recommend the chicken lemon grass, #206. For vegetarians not in the mood for soup, the #700 (tofu with curry and lemon grass) is one of the best tofu dishes I have ever tried anywhere, though if you don't like spicy food, let them know to make it mild (even then it is sometimes a little too hot for me, but I am kind of wimpy when it comes to spicy food).

If you order an entree, be sure to ask for a side of broth--a small cup is free with the entree, though the staff don't bring it unless you ask. 

Another great bonus: unsweetened hot and iced teas are free with your meal.

The only dishes I have tried that I didn't care for are those with meat balls. I think they are just an acquired taste, and we westerners have a certain idea in mind when we hear "meatball" and this just isn't it. The Vietnamese version might seem rubbery to those accustomed to the Italian-American variety.

A "bun" (big bowl of rice noodles) is a good dish for newbies. Both meat and vegetarian varieties are available. I like the #200, bun cha gio--it has spring rolls in it. It may not be calorie-conscious, but few comfort foods are as satisfying. And at $5.75 for a large bowl, it's another great choice for those watching their budget.

To top off your meal, try a fried banana--though I am usually so satisfied I don't need anything except coffee. The hot espresso with condensed milk is a coffee and a dessert in one--smooth, sweet, and strong. There are also a variety of fruit smoothies available.

The prices at Pho Eden are so reasonable, the food so irresistible, why not try this taste sensation tonight and discover your new craving?

I'm so sorry Cafe Du Monde!!! You're a NOLA landmark, but, Disneyland in CA does it better. I found the beignets served here to be hard to chew and lacking in comparison to the same ones made at Disneyland using your mix. Almost like they weren't just freshly made and stale. The upside is that the coffee was excellent and the staff brought everything to us shortly after ordering. Is it worth going to? Yes, because of the coffee. Are they the best beignets ever? My husband and I wandered about the French quarter one cold morning. On our way to Congo Square we came across this coffee shop. The staff  was so welcoming and made us feel right at home. They didn't take long to get us our order. We were off before we knew it! I really liked the drinks we ordered. I will be by again on our next trip out to NOLA.

Easily in my top 3 best places we ate in NOLA! We ate here just before we left to the airport. I really regret not eating here more during our stay. I went for brunch and we ate outside. It was beautiful and peaceful and just everything I wanted outta New Orleans. I really thought the pasta was perfect and the desserts were great! We had a few other items that were good, but, for me the pasta and desserts stood out the most. Our waitress was very knowledgeable, prompt, and courteous. Coming in here on a Wednesday probably explain why a place is empty, but can't help but judge when many other food places are packed with people and this one isn't. 

Came here because one of my friend recommended coming here for their price and food portion. So I agreed. For a $7 burger, they need to step up their game. 

The burger looks amazing from the outside but right from the first bite, it's a bit dry. And I thought maybe going deeper I would change my mind, but really no--- it's a dry burger throughout. And it's not that they lack sauce, because the whole burger is filled with sauce. It's the meat itself.
