With the lack of Filipino restaurants in Reno, this was a must-try for me to support Filipino businesses. But they are new and in severe need of improvements before they expect any advancements. 

My first visit was on quite a busy day; half the restaurant was full and a party of 6+ was present. I suppose this could've posed a problem for the new staff, but it still wasn't worth trying to get the attention of the staff just so I could see the menu and order. This place seems to be self-serve, in that you seat yourself. But there is no way for patrons to know that because there is no sign. The staff was not attentive to us and we did not get any drink refills (and we only had water). 

Onto the food. Be sure to ask what is available before ordering, because they could've run out. We ordered sisig (a skillet of pork and chicken), crispy pata (deep fried pig parts) and tofu with pork drenched in soy sauce. The presentation of the food was appealing, especially the crispy pata which was served on top of a banana leaf. But everything was lacking in flavor. It wasn't the best representation of Filipino cuisine. 

I do believe that this place can be a long-standing Filipino restaurant in Reno, but they need to pay attention to their customers, put up some signs and improve on the taste.

After a long hiatus from reviewing I have awaken from my 6 mouth yelp hibernation and my tummies a grumbles with an insatiable hunger for the cacophonous symphony of flavor that is Indian food. Like an all too familiar pattern, I go back to Mohammad Butt, my main man for marsala.
But whats this? 
There are whispers that he no longer cooks for "Best Taste of Asia," that he is gone, never to return; some sort of falling out.

No.
No, it can't be! 
I need to score - one .. final .. hit..

Life ceases to have meaning, existential murmurings dog the mind. Who am I?
Why am I here?
What is Cheeze Wiz?
Its done, over, a round falls into the chamber and just as I prepare to end it all and pull the trigger- steps in ZAIKA.

Zaika - meaning the art of taste -  stays to to its name. This is a place where the Paneer (cheese) is made fresh in house, resulting in a cheese that's silky in texture. Especially when in contrast to the prepackaged rubbery bone-white LEGO blocks most small Indo-Pak places purchase from Indian Grocers in attempts to reduce prep-times. While at Zaika such shortcuts are not taken,  the Chef takes the extra steps needed to ensure a dish comes together as a whole. For example, the Chicken Makhani uses Smokey Tandoori Chicken, which I have never seen done before but it certainly aids the chicken to cut though the rich buttery tomato sauce and elevates the dish as a whole. Even entrées like Dall Fray or  Palak Paneer  have so much flavor that they will leave you not missing animal protein in the least should you choose to go the vegetarian route. 

Zaika 's appetizers, like the Veggie Samosa and Aloo Tikki, (spiced potato patties) are generally large, peppery and well spiced - the latter of which remind me of something my own mother would make. Though I must warn others to avoid the items that occasionally pop-up as specials like the potato stuffed chili peppers, unless they have a iron stomach or are a gluten for punishment. These peppers are spicy, not deveined or even seeded. Further, I find the fish pakora to be far too fishy.
 
I've become rather taken by Zaikia. Even the simply things such as the naan are good there. Just right in elasticity, the bread does not have too much give and yet isn't too soft. It's nothing elaborate, just properly risen with a light texture and  no egg or yeast flavor. The only complaint being that it lacked that signature faint sweetness naan has. But hey, I use it mostly for mopping up the other good stuff on the plate anyway and the sweetness gets lost in the mix, so I don't mind at all.

The menu has nearly 120 different items, all numbered to order by, making take-out phone orders convenient and should eliminate any fears anyone should have of a language barrier problem. Furthermore, it has short descriptions of each dish - something all ethnic places like this should have.
Though some items like Lassie (a frothy yogurt drink) do not appear on the menu, that too is offered - both a salty and sweet mango verities. 
The head chef speaks English quite well and should be easy to deal with should you want to inquire more or want to setup large orders.

I have already noticed parties negotiating catering for Ramadan as I anxiously awaited my own order.

The bottom line here is this, Mohammad Butt has expanded on the menu he once created for "Best taste of Asia," and taken an all HALAL meat approach. 

Only good things can come of this, only good things.

P.S.
ZAIKA is right behind Nifty Fifties on Grant Ave., so you are all set for dessert should you want a milkshake. 
However, I would suggest getting the Ras Malai if available. These riccotta cheese dumplings flouting in soaked in sweetened, thickened milk are delicately flavored with cardamom, a very some amount of rose water and then garnished with pistachios. They are ungodly good.

I have heard about this place for years and years, and I've passed by it probably a million times, but it wasn't until recently that I actually tried it out. I ordered a plain cheese pizza because that's how I can truly tell if a pizza is exceptional. When I went inside pick up my pizza they were quite a few people behind accounts are working for such a small place, I'll be it it's during our stay at home., they were super busy but that didn't stop them from welcoming me the minute I walked in the door. I thought quickly this is a place that I want to come back to once the stay-at-home order is over. Anyways grab my pizza and headed home. I opened up the box and was shocked to see that they cut their Pizza in squares, this is kind of cool. I took a bite, now this pizza is perfect for those folks out there that don't like a lot of oil; I happen to love oooey gooey cheesy oily Pizza. The cheese is good, but not completely melted, it still has some substance. The sauce, when I could get a good bite with enough sauce in it, tasted really good. I really wish they added more sauce. The crust is crispy but not burnt. I would go back because this place is such an icon in the Seminole Community. I will definitely try another of their pizzas with more toppings

This is mold that was at the bottom of our crushed red pepper.I couldn't figure out why every time I poured crushed red pepper on my pizza it was causing me to cough...I dumped out what was loose on top,  and there was 2" of mold on the bottom.  Yuck

This is a cautionary tale about our experience at the Hub restaurant in Tucson.  Sadly this is not a review about the food, but rather the experience we had with the Hub.  I'll present the facts and let you draw your own conclusions.
 
14 of us stopped at the Hub for dinner late one night.  
After dinner we all paid separately for our dinners. 
20 minutes after the Hub closed 3 of the people in the group were victims of stolen credit cards or numbers. Three people from the same party, that had not been out together until that night had their credit card accounts compromised immediately after leaving the Hub!
All three had charges of $101.00 at a Circle K just a short drive from Hub in Tucson.
In checking with the victims the only place that all 3 had used their credit cards, was at the Hub.
When I called the manager then next day all he did was deny and refuse to investigate.
 
As the group leader it seemed clear to me that the Hub was the common denominator, and the conversation I had with the manager pushed me to write this review.  Rather than respond in a concerned and interested manner, the manager just denied, diverted, and ignored the problem.
 
I will not return to the Hub.  You have to make your own decision about the staff and management of the restaurant that appears not to care about it patrons. In fact, I provided the "Ass't Manager" the names and phone numbers of those that were effected and to this day nobody from the restaurant has ever been in touch! The violation does not go away if you ignore it. 

I have attempted to reach the owner but have yet to hear back from him, forcing the posting of this review. 

If you too have had a card compromised after eating at the Hub, please contact me.

This place bills itself as "The Cupcakery Boutique".  I had to stare into the window for a few seconds before figuring out that, yes, it was actually cupcakes they were selling in there, because it looked like some combination of a jewelry store, a clothing boutique, and my grandmother's living room with a baker hoarding supplies in the back.  

"Be still my heart!" said my heart as I walked through the door and laid eyes upon the glass-windowed cabinets filled with a veritable bombardment of baked extravagances.  I was greeted with a good deal of enthusiasm and directed to a menu.  There is quite a good selection, with all the obligatory classics.  My opinion, though, as always, is that if you're going to get one cupcake right, it had better be the red velvet, so red velvet it was.  The man at the counter packaged the adorably Christmasy-decorated cupcake with its shiny red foil wrapper into an inverted cup with pop-on lid and gave me the cupcake to go.

I wanted to eat this cupcake on the spot, but I wanted even more for this cupcake to be as perfect as possible, so I waited until I got home and put it in the microwave for a few seconds (which I highly recommend).  "Please, cupcake," I whispered, as he stared up at me from the counter.  "Please don't let me down."

He obliged.  Holy cow, did they get the red velvet right.  This was probably the moistest cake I've ever tasted in a cupcake, but the cake also had a sorta-crunchy outside layer which was both pleasant and useful in holding the cupcake in one piece.  The cream cheese icing was perfect (I think the microwaving set it off).  It was normal sized, but slightly small for the $3 price-tag; however, it was more than worth it.

Welcome to the city, Philly Cupcake.  Welcome to the city and welcome to my life.

I'm compelled to write a review only because I've read some of these reviews that are completely misleading.  

First of all, it is authentic Thai food.  I mean, it's as Thai as you can get.  Like any regional food, everybody's gonna have their own take.  Not every authentic food will taste the same.  But one thing that good Thai food will always have is a balance of sweet, salty, sour, and spicy.  

Now, if you THINK they're Laotian, you are completely wrong.  I grew up with Laotian people and ate Laotian food practically my whole life.  Their take on Thai is by having the spice front and center.  There is rarely any sweet or sour in Laotian cuisine, even their take on Thai cuisine is extremely spicy.  

That said, I think Thai Phooket is the best Thai restaurant I've tried so far in Nashville.  I've tried a few, but none comes even close to Thai Phooket.  Their chicken larb salad is the best.  They roast their own rice powder, so it tastes so much better than the one I make at home with prepackaged seasoning.  Thanks a lot, Thai Phooket!

I also enjoy some of their other dishes, like their red curry chicken, pad thai, papaya salad, etc.  And their vegetable soup is SOOOO DELICIOUS!  I detest tofu and anything soy, but I'll eat the tofu in this vegetable soup.  It's so flavorful, I try to guess what they put in the stock every time I eat it.  Maybe I'll ask for the recipe.  Haha.  They have a really extensive menu, including a red snapper bathed in red chili peppers and a bunch of Thai spices and herbs which I really want to try next time I visit.  

MSG is a staple in my family's seasoning (it's right up there with salt) - so I know how it tastes like.  I don't mind it so much, but I have to have MSG in my papaya salad.  The papaya has a bitter after taste because of the lack of MSG, so it doesn't taste completely right to me.  So MSG-haters, you have nothing to fear.  

Anyway, this is a good restaurant to explore your palate with Thai cuisine.  Some Asian restaurants may water down their menu for the American palate, but not this one.  Once you're done trying the safe dishes, there are so much more to try.  And everything tastes good.  I can't complain.

**JOHN BESH IS MY HERO**

Seriously. This man knows n'awlins food. 

Service was very good. Staff was nice, friendly, but not over the top. Ambiance was French-Bistro-ish, but with a touch of New Orleans flair. Can get loud; especially on the weekend.

I decided to take advantage of their *EXPRESS MENU* which is their prix fixe offerings of cup of soup, their specialty entree of that day, and dessert for $23.

Had the following:

(1) Seafood gumbo a la creole - Can I get a *WOW*, please. Incredible stuff. Flavors, balance, ingredients worked out perfectly inside my mouth.

(2) Redfish "court-bouillon" with crab, shrimp, oysters and rice - Tasted similar to the seafood gumbo, but has more OOOMPH. Generous seafood chunks and the amazing sauce had me soaking it all up with the leftover table French bread.

(3) Bread pudding - Tasted like a pecan pie disguised as a bread pudding.  Which was beyond amazing since I am a dessert freak.

One of the best meals for $23. Come on. I almost felt bad (that guilt only lasted maybe 2 seconds).

Cocktails are also fantastic. Try the French 75 ($9.25) or the St. Charles Streetcar ($9), both have champagne and tasted so lovely with the crazy humidity.

HIGHLY RECOMMEND the EXPRESS MENU and their refreshing cocktails.

**BEST LEMONADE AND MOST OVER RATED FRIED CHICKEN**

Waited 30 minutes or so for a table.

Surrounded by tourists. 

Sat at the front window.

Clean and cute inside.

Super friendly service.

ORDERED:

*LEMONADE ($2.50, no refills) - Best lemonade. Ever. Freshly made and squeezed with love. Highly recommend.

*FRIED CHICKEN ($7.50) - Over rated much? Seriously. What was so great about the fried chicken here? The batter was too thick and greasy. The best piece was the thigh and it was borderline dry. Where were the true NOLA cajun flavors? 

We waited 30 minutes for our fried chicken. Not cool, Willie.

I definitely preferred Jacque-Imo's fried chicken over this. 

Maybe even Popeye's.

Don't take my word for it.

If you have the time and patience, give it a shot. You might like it, you might not.

But there are better fried chicken establishments out there without lines or tourists.

**FROSÉ ALL DAY**

Their frosés and slushy cocktails is good enough reason to stop by.

AMBIANCE
=========
Noisy and crowded,
especially for weekend brunch.

Brick walls, natural lighting, and 
friendly people.

FOOD
======
CRAWFISH + GRITS - $19
Gulf shrimp, etouffee gravy, grit, and slow poached eggs with cheddar biscuits was flavorful, rich, and wonderfully good. Loved the poached eggs.
RATING: 4/5

BEVERAGE
==========
FROSÉ Y'ALL - $11
Had two of these and felt pretty good.
RATING: 5/5

Tasted DRUNK IN LOVE and actually liked that better,
but they ran out.

SERVICE
========
Accommodating and did not rush us at all,
although there was a line outside.
RATING: 5/5

OVERALL
========
Price point, thought it was a bit pricey for NOLA, but it's bougie brunch food,
so I get it.
Otherwise, a solid brunch spot with friends and your morning-after date.

RECOMMEND.

**NOT THE BEST, BUT STILL OK**

Looking for something nearby,
we strolled down to Mother's.

AMBIANCE
==========
Bit dark and dingy,
but it has it's authentic charm.

and wait for your waitress and food.

FOOD
=====

Fried chicken lacked that spicy cajun seasoning
that I've been craving for. The rice and
beans and the greens weren't that memorable either.
But I loved that biscuit.
RATING: 3/5

MAE's FILE GUMBO - $6 (cup)
Chicken and smoked sausage was again "OK".
The sausage lacked any real spice and it tasted
like it was just being reheated in a pot. Not too
fresh.
RATING: 3/5

STAFF
=====
Super friendly.
RATING: 5/5

========
My husband enjoyed his Po Boy more than I did
my fried chicken and gumbo. So maybe that's
a better bet next time.

Not awful, but definitely not the best I've had.
Especially for New Orleans.

Plenty of other options around. But still a good
spot to support your local restaurant.

RECOMMEND if you want to get a Po Boy and you're around 
the area.

**EXCELLENT MEXICAN FOOD IN SANTA BARBARA**

After eating lackluster Mexican food in Palm Springs,
it was a relief to finally eat here.

All about their 6 salsas, including a spicy habanero and a peanut salsa, goes well with their street tacos, tortas, mole chicken and barbacoa beef dishes.

PARKING
========
There's a side lot or street.
Can get packed on weekends, so be patient.

=========
Cute and clean.
Specials on the chalkboard wall.
Order at the counter and they'll call your number and bring your items to you.
Casual, unpretentious, and friendly.
2 small tables inside.
4-5 tables outside.

FOOD
=====
SALSA AND CHIPS
Enjoy their salsa bar.
Love that pistachio flavored salsa the best!
Super fresh and delicious.
RATING: 5/5

CHICKEN ENCHILADAS WITH MOLE SAUCE
Simple and delicious.
Chicken meat was tender and the mole sauce flavorful.
Beans were my favorite! Fresh and different.
That rice was fluffy and fragrant.
RATING: 5/5

BEVERAGE
=========
HORCHATA
Refreshing, not too sweet.
Great on a hot day.
RATING: 4/5

SERVICE
=======
Friendly and spot-on.
Food came out piping hot in 10 minutes.
They refilled our water pitcher.
RATING: 5/5

OVERALL
========
Weekend lines and the wait can be intimidating.
But worth it, trust me.
Our now to-go spot for Mexican food in Santa Barbara.

HIGHLY RECOMMEND.

**NEED TO BE A RICH BOY TO BUY A PO BOY**

Seriously?

 $11+ for a SMALL sandwich with fried shrimp?

Seriously?

In a divey shack, too?

I don't get it.

But let's say that I did.

Was it worth it?

No.

My Vietnamese sandwiches back home are better. They're $3 and we pay California real estate prices, so go figure.

Sure, it was tasty, but not worthy of the price tag.

**EXCELLENT CRAWFISH AND SERVICE**

Even some NOLA locals haven't heard of this 
place until I came along and dragged them here.

PARKING
========
Be sure to park on the street and not
in someone's driveway 
(that happened to us - I wasn't the driver).

AMBIANCE
=========
Charming, divey, and quaint.
A few tables here and there.
There was a party going on next
to us but we didn't mind because they played
good music and was entertaining to watch.

FOOD
=====
CRAWFISH
Perfectly spicy, juicy tails, and hot from the 
boiler. Added on corn and it was heaven.
RATING: 5/5

I think I ate 3 pounds because I lost
track.

We were supposed to order beer next door
but our lovely waitress took care of us.
Above and beyond service with 
understanding genuine smiles.
RATING: 5/5

Returning next year for sure.

RECOMMEND for all of your crawfish cravings.

**SOLID SALSA BAR AND GOURMET MEXICAN FOOD IN SANTA BARBARA**

PARKING

Street.

Certainly did not care for their "cleaner supplies" smell upon entry.

FOOD

AGAVES ENCHILADAS (MOST POPULAR) - $12.50
