It pains me to write this review. My husband and I have been faithful, devoted patrons of their other establishments for years. We always recommend Barbuzzo to friends and family, and have spent a pretty penny there ourselves over time. I'm still kind of in shock, with how our Friday evening ended. 

Let me start by saying our server was wonderful. Incredibly knowledgeable about the food and drink menu, and her recommendations were spot on. This is the ONLY reason I gave a second star. What I was most disappointed in was one of the owners - Valerie. We arrived about 20 minutes late to our reservation. She called at 550 (reservation was for 530) & informed me that if we weren't there in 5 minutes they would have to release the table. Totally understandable. So, I did what any respectable young woman who doesn't want to miss a reservation would do. I ran a block & a half to get there within that 5 minute time frame. We were seated with the stipulation that we had to be done dining by 7:30. No problem. As we ate our fast paced meal we were very pleased with our food and our server - who was super apologetic about the rushed service. As 7:30 approached we politely left the table for the bar so that the next table could be seated - who never arrived; and my girlfriend overheard Valerie call them as well to let them know their table was being released. Anyway, after we ate, we waited about 15 mins for seats to open at the bar. Our dinner tab for four people (including tip) came out to about $315. Once we were seated at the bar, we easily spent another $75 or so. We took up 2 bar stools, the gentlemen stood the entire time. We were probably seated there for about 45 mins (empty handed for maybe 15), when Valerie informed us that if we didn't order more drinks we would have to leave so that a couple who walked in (without a reservation in their opening week) could be accommodated. Even the bartenders looked a little shocked by the incident. 

It saddens me that their empire has grown so much that the emphasis is on turning tables (or bar stools) over quickly to get the most bang for their buck, rather than growing a loyal fan base by keeping regular customers happy. This review easily would have been 5 stars, had Valerie not treated us like we weren't "worthy" enough to sit in their establishment after spending $400. After our meal and after we were respectful of the 'be done by 7:30" agreement (despite the next reservations no-show), no one was rushed from the bar for us so that WE could sit. We did what anyone would do when there are no seats available; wait. I'm baffled by why this particular couple was exempt from that unspoken rule. 

Even more bothersome is when my husband approached her to express his disappointment (respectfully). She shrugged her shoulders and said "you were late". So, sadly - we will not return. Here or any of their restaurants (yes, even the beloved Barbuzzo). Nor will we recommend their restaurants to any of our friends. They have, simply put - become too big for their britches; putting themselves first instead of their customers.

I don't even know how to label this place.  It isn't quite tiki-islandish, hippie, punk, nor is it country.  Maybe a fusion of all those.  And then some.  It comes off as kind of crude, strange, and incredibly trippy.  And even though I'm still not sure what to make of this place, all I know is that it's Mahuffer and it's the motherfuckin' shit!

On the way home from the beach, my BB and I drove by a coffee shop and decided that we needed to get caffeinated, so we pulled into the nearest parking lot.  When we looked at the building of the lot, we saw some strange, strange things.  Strange things that were eerily reminiscent of the hippie haven in Marin County back in California.  

The building looked like it was about to collapse.  There were colorful blobs, stripes, dots and graffiti all about, plus a bunch of beach bum paraphernalia.  Parked next to us was an old school, rusted up, door-less Buick with a very DIY tie-dyed paint job and a death skull spray painted on the hood and a banner proclaiming "We Do Not Sell Budweiser" hanging on the side.  On the rainbow fence, "FOLLOW THE YELLOW BRICK ROAD TO FOOD, BOOZE AND BULLS__T" was painted, and another sign said, "Warm Beer, Lousy Food, THE WURST PLACE ON THE BEECH!".  We had to investigate.

After a couple of minutes of scouring the perimeters and searching for the entrance and finding no aforementioned yellow brick road, we finally stumbled in through what we thought was the back, looking all bewildered because of all that we had seen on the outside.  "Come on in, don't be scared", said the Scott Ian look-alike behind the bar, who would later introduce himself as Mikey to us.  We stepped over a big, cute, white, lazy dog, found ourselves a couple of seats at the bar next to a bunch of old time regulars and soaked in the environment, which was A LOT to take in.

The inside of Mahuffer's is like... a dark, rainbow junkyard; it's full of shit!  There were signed dollar bills stapled and tacked all over the place in tiki bar-esque fashion.  The bar was painted in bright colors in trippy designs.  There were Christmas lights and all sorts of random shit strewn all over the walls and ceilings.  There was Sharpie graffiti everywhere.  There was a green parrot, and the aforementioned big, white dog named Dot Dot.  Random signs that said things like, "If you raised your children right, they are welcome till 6 PM, and we congratulate you!  Unattended children will be SOLD AS SLAVES!".  It smelled heavily of cigarette smoke.  The place was just an absolute mess.  But for Mahuffer's, it works!  Oh, and there WAS a yellow painted trail inside the bar.  Needless to say, it was pretty overwhelming.

Mahuffer's food menu is pretty carnivorous, so I just got a rum runner and a cole slaw.  They also have burgers, pulled pork, pulled chicken, and fish spread sandwiches and some other side dishes.  My BB ordered a soda and a Sloppy John, their pulled chicken sandwich that came with two different sauces which she said was delicious.  Our bill came to about $15.  

Mikey pulled up a stool next to us and chatted us up for a bit.  He is HILARIOUS and totally the shizzle.  Upon my telling him about my food restrictions:
Mikey: Well, we could make you a sloppy lettuce.
Me: Wouldn't that just be like a cole slaw?
Mikey: Yeah, but it'll be in between two buns.

Upon sitting down and realizing that there was a penis-shaped bar/shaft of soap two inches away from my face:
Mikey: Haven't you ever been to prison before?  This is the soap that they pass out in prison.

We also talked a bit about politics.  In a land filled with SUVs with proudly displayed McCain/Palin bumper stickers, it was soooo refreshing to find someone who lives here who shares the same sentiments about them as I do.

How did we not know about this place before???  Upon googling, I found out some fun facts, like how Mahuffer is over 30 years old, that Mikey is the grandson of the late owner, who the regulars told me was "Old Man Mahuffer", and is now part-owner of the joint, how they were once sued by Budweiser, and how the crazy name Mahuffer came to be.

Oh yeah, apparently, at Mahuffer, "nothing's worth a damn", and "insAlts are free".  I can't stress how AWESOME Mahuffer is, and I really can't wait to stop in for a few!

While waiting for my friend's car to get serviced at Toyota, we got hungry, so we asked Mr. Mechanic for suggestions.  "Um, the shuttle could take you to Mom's Place", okay, whatever.  We hopped onto the shuttle, and literally 30 seconds, we were at Mom's Place!

Oh wait... they closed at 3.  Darn.  But hold on, right next door is Pop N Son's, and they're... OPEN, and 24/7 at that!  So to Pop N Son's we go :)

Pop N Sons may look dingy and bleh from the outside, but inside is a surprisingly clean and spacious diner with all sorts of muscle car memorabilia.  I ordered a feta cheese and spinach omelet, which was kind of dry, and it came with a choice of bread and a side.  I got a yummy biscuit, and a not-so-yummy fruit cup.  Their fruit cup is fruit cocktail from out of a can and the sliced banana in it... tasted like a raw plantain.  Ick!  My friend ordered a chili dog that was bigger than the size of her head: http://www.flickr.com/photos/aloveletteraway/2913718095/in/set-72157607735561008 And she says that it was pure amazingness.  And then some.

The best part: After all the food, a couple of OJ's and a couple more sides, the bill came out to $18.54.  Nice!  The food was run-of-the-mill diner food at 3 stars, but the waitress was a sweetheart, the price wasn't bad, the place was clean and had a nice atmosphere, and they're open 24/7!  That deserves at least a 4.

Oh, and bonus points for this dude sitting across the restaurant from us: http://www.flickr.com/photos/aloveletteraway/2913717077/in/set-72157607735561008/  It was kinda creepy, but his long beard and wizard hat were amusing and seriously intense!

I wrote one review already but it was pulled by Yelp HQ due to my being too mean in regards to our server.  I won't name names but his name rhymes with "Spaniel".

Anyway, I enjoyed my food. I did not enjoy our terrible service.  Read on.

Our server was rude and dismissive, continuously dropped silverware, and actually SCOLDED us for not giving him our 100% attention while he was reciting the dessert specials.  Lame.

We spent just about $400 on dinner for eight of us and unfortunately, 18% gratuity was already included.  Too bad.  He did not deserve even close to that amount.

Pros:  crispy potatoes with gorgonzola, the white beans in red sauce served with the octopus and my pasta dish, which was wide noodles in a chicken/pork liver bolognese.

Cons:  No bread, and poor service.

Update, one week later:
There were eight of us and we were assured that we could split the check evenly, and we did so, providing eight credit cards.  We all signed our own receipts, for a total of about 50 bucks each. Later, we found out that one of us was charged the entire amount on her debit card which is just too ridiculous.  She discovered the problem on Friday 1/29 and has left repeated messages with City House Nashville.  No one has gotten back to her yet.  IT'S BEEN FIVE DAYS.

I've had better service at Pizza Hut.

Update, Two Weeks Later:
My friend filed a claim with her bank and she was refunded $350.  The rest of us were all each charged $50.12, as originally agreed upon.  Am I happy?  No.  Tammie should have gotten a phone call from the terrible management at City House Nashville, apologizing for the mixup.  There is no excuse for this.

I usually like eating here, but recently they had a very bad inspection. 37 violations, including 5 HIGH PRIORITY.
See https://www.myfloridalicense.com/inspectionDetail.asp?InspVisitID=5298678&id=3232824
Once I see another better inspection report, maybe I'll return.

I do want to say that normally, I really like this restaurant.

The fat in our drinks was better than the fat in our food.  Aesthetically, the dishes were plated nicely, however some of the execution fell short.

DUCKHUNTER OLD FASHIONED 2.0 = my first cocktail ever with duck fat-washed bourbon!  It was silky, muted the usual sharpness when alcohol first hits your tongue, and allowed the flavor to linger with a pleasant aftertaste.

DEVILED EGGS = beautiful presentation with a pink exterior.  Unique twist with a small shred of trout.  Tasty, but pricey at $2 per half-egg.

SHORT RIB & SWEET POTATO HASH = tender beef with sweet potato cubes, topped with fried eggs.  A layer of chimichurri was distracting and I would've enjoyed this dish more without it.  Most noticeably, there was a large pool of grease at the bottom of the bowl.

ROASTED PORK BELLY BENEDICT = the eggs were poached perfectly and the hollandaise was creamy with a kick.  Unfortunately, the main part of the dish, the pork belly, was a let-down.  One slice was all fat, the other slice was 75% fat.  I recognize that pork belly is a fatty meat, but did not expect to get only the fat layer; the sauce was a veil for these inferior cuts.  IMAGINE YOUR EGGS BENEDICT TOPPED WITH BLUBBER SLICES.

We dined during an off-peak hour, mid-afternoon on a Saturday.  Dining room was mostly empty, so we had very attentive service.  Food came out promptly; appetizer and entrees delivered in just over 10 minutes.

Location is on the corner of Carrillo & Chapala, to the left of a parking structure with free 75-minute parking.

So with an hr to kill in downtown Nashville, I first went to the obvious choice... The Country Music Hall Of Fame.  After gagging in disbelief at the $25 admission fee (I'll admit that corporate perks have largely shielded me from knowing what admission costs in any of NYC's museums), and quickly consulting Yelp, I was led to the Johnny Cash museum.

You don't have too be country to get Cash.  You don't have to be religious to get Cash.  Cash is eternal.  Cash transcends. Cash rules everything around me... dolla dolla bills y'all (I'm convinced that Wu Tang worked with Johnny Cash in 36 Chambers).

Johnny Cash made music across multiple eras and this place showcased it all.  This is a great little museum... definitely worth a look if you're in Nashville.  The items in the store seemed pretty pricey so I took a pass on that.

As a resident in the area, we were excited to have this open up.  Went there on opening night and it was pretty bad.  The waits are just like people are saying as we were sat in about 15 minutes and waited about 75 minutes for our food.  But we decided to give it a second chance, and chalk it up to opening night.

Went again and the place was pretty empty.  Food was ordered which was two appetizers and 2 sushi rolls as well as an entree that came with soup.  Appetizers came out, and they were average, the tempura was cold, but its okay.  In the meantime the server basically ignored us.

Then the sushi came about 40 minutes later.  It was decent.  I wasnt great and it wasnt bad, just average.  Then all of the sudden the entree comes out, which was just awful.  Korean short ribs which were just all fat, the plate was cold and it was such a shame.  Manager strolls up and says "How is everything" and we say its great to see the business going well and he goes on and on about how amazing business is and then we say this dish is inedible.  The response was "Well you know what not to order next time".  What?  What is that?  I wasnt hoping to get a freebie or even a replacement, but that was amusing.

Best part is I say "we never got the soup" and while he was telling us more about how great business is, the server comes over and drops off the soup, 15 minutes after the entree and we already had napkins on everything.  Manager standing there says nothing and walks away.

We wont be back.  They got two chances and there are a dozen sushi places in the area that have as good or better food.  The place looks great, but my gut says its gone with in the next year.  People in this area expect better treatment and quality food to survive and Sushi Alive is offering neither.

Overall the view from the upper deck was great,  A beautiful day. Now to the food, just average, you would think being at seaside town that the seafood would be much better than this. But it's not I could've been in the middle of the desert and the food with it tasted the same. Now to the service I would understand if they were busy then I would except being as slow as our server was, but since they weren't busy I don't understand why the service was so slow. Overlooking the service and the food I just kept thinking about the view , My company, and the Guinness which pulled me through. Lol lol

I enjoy coffee.  That's no secret.  Up until today, I had been enjoying ReAnimator coffee from my normal shop in CC (HubBub) and buying it at Whole Foods.  After deciding that I needed more Fishtown in my life, I made the pilgrimage and I'm happy I did.

It's located on a great corner.  With the other spots right around, it makes ReAnimator easy to get to and a great spot for an after meal cup of joe or shot.

I visited on a Saturday morning and it seemed completely peaceful.  If you're the type to sit, read, work or just relax this shop will work for you.  It spacious, nicely designed and the coffee they are turning out is some serious product.  I didn't recognize the espresso machine they were using but it pulled a beautiful, velvetty shot and was exactly what I was looking for.

More wonderful coffee in Philadelphia, what's not to love?

I like The Bagel Place for several reasons.  They are (unordered)

- I can walk here
- Fresh bagels
- Stroller friendly
- decent prices

I've been in several times and have always been greeted by kind workers.  The place has a really nice look and feel to it.  It's comfortable regardless if you are just there for a few minutes or even if you linger a bit.  In my opinion, it's warm and welcoming.

Of all of the bagels I've tried, I've been most impressed with the Rosemary and Black Pepper.  That paired with plain cream cheese was a really good meal.  I did my normal routine of picking this up to go and taking my son to the park so I can eat with one hand and push him on the swings with the other.

The fridge to the right of the counter has a number of selections of water, juices and La Colombe draft lattes.  They also serve brewed La Colombe which is a nice touch.

This is a very good addition and filled a real gap in our hood.

As I sat at Rosa Blanca,and took in the sights, sounds and colors, I considered pouring one out for my homeboy Chifa.  After I took my first sip of a 12 year aged rum, I reconsidered.  It was delicious.

The entryway of Rosa Blanca is a diner.  Silver colors abound and a long bar with what looks like a breakfast counter is the first thing you see.  There is a small kitchen off to the left side which has empanadas and other small tasty delights ready to go for the counter crew.

We took our seats in the dining room which has an island like feel.  Straw hats sit above some of the the booths and the whole design of the place lets you know it has a more casual vibe than a stuffy one.  On a packed evening, be prepared to shout at your table because this place is very loud.  If you're looking for quiet, seek elsewhere.

We began with the guacamole and pulpo.  The smoked pineapple in the guac made it so we demolished that app quickly.  The pulpo was cooked perfectly.  Charred on the outside, soft inside and we rejoiced.

For entrees I went with the Masitas de Puerco.  Essentially, it was a pork shoulder cooked using a sous-vide machine and then quickly fried for a crispy exterior.  "Wow!" was pretty much all that I could say upon tasting this dish.  When I had it, I believe it was draped in a chimichurri or something that had parsley, cilantro shallots and lime.  Many times, I save part of my meal for another day.  That was not the case with this dish.  The other people in my party raved about the ropa vieja and the churrasco.

If you're a bourbon drinker like me, you will be interested to try some of their rums.  I went the aged rum flight and I was really happy I did.  I didn't know rum could have such incredible flavor notes.  I became a fan that night.

I'm ok embracing the change and I hope that Rosa Blanca stays around.  I'll be back for breakfast and lunch.  While I think doing 3 meal service each day is an ambitious enterprise, I'm confident that they will get the food traffic and staff retention to pull it off.

They make a pretty mean mole.

After having been here a few times, I'm a fan.  The prices are excellent, the staff is nice (and they are used to putting up with lots of rude customers) and the food stands up.  They definitely make concessions for vegetarians and vegans and I really like their al pastor.

BYO, cash, card and LEVEL UP which definitely gives you a healthy variety of payment options.  I promise that if you get the chicken mole burrito and you're still hungry, your appetite is not human.

Give it a shot, just watch out on Friday/Saturday nights for the 30 deep college party that shows up looking to turn the place into a frat house.

Ok, so now I've found my second favorite popcorn in Philadelphia.

This place is super popular.  Fortunately, the people we were dining with got here much earlier and put their name in.  If we didn't, the wait would have been 1:30 at 9 pm on a Friday.

The bacon grease popcorn is truly delicious.  I went with the two meat bbq sampler for my entree.  The brisket was tender and moist.  The one rib (yes 1) that came was tasty but I wish I had a few more of them.  My sides were collard greens and coleslaw.  Both were excellent.

The beer list here is great.  Very fitting for a bar in Philadelphia.  They re-invented the space and definitely came correct with the menu.  I really like this place and I'll try to make it back midweek so I don't have to deal with the weekend Olde City crowd.

They need to make this place bigger.

I arrived on day 3 of the opening week of federal.  As I parked on 2nd and walked over, I could see a line at 6:55AM.  This my friends, is devotion.

In the shop, which is quite little, the staff was working frantically to keep up with the amount of people craving coffee and sugar.  When I finally got to the front, I got my dozen, bid them farewell and off I went.

The smell of donuts filled my car on the way to work and my mind ran as to what I would be experiencing.

I tried a taste of all 4 varieties and they are delicious.  These are not your run of the mill, light, airy donuts.  They are cakey, cooked properly and delectable.  Some have fillings, some have glazes.  They are addictive.

Coffee is killer too.  From what I've heard, it's a custom blend from PT's so it looks like you can only get it here.

Forget camping for the iPhone, camp for Federal Donuts.

After a few times at Grubhouse I'm calling it a 5.  I had the best breakfast sandwich of my life here.

It was a special, so I'm not sure when it will make its way back on the menu.  It did have sausage and pork roll and banana mayo and bacon fat onions and a bourbon pineapple sauce.  It was absolutely amazing in all aspects.  It didn't fall apart when I ate it (which is a pet peeve of mine) and this sandwich hit all five elements of taste for me.

Let's talk other breakfast items.  Even one of the simple, two eggs and homefries is taken to another level here.  There are plenty of places that phone this one in, but not Grubhouse.  It's done right.

Another time, I opted for the special of grits with hot sauce, cheddar and fried chicken skin.  This was just another world of good.  The spice level was perfect and the fried chicken skin was simply marvelous.  Indulgent, but marvelous.

You're going to get great food here for a reasonable price.  The food is made the hard way where the key ingredients are time and love.  I think the staff here is putting everything they've got into their product and it shows.

You have to love a place that can put 3 awesome tacos on a plate for 6 bucks.  Personally, there is a special spot in my heart for these kinds of establishments.

The ambiance here pretty much defines casual.  You walk in, grab a menu yourself, order from the window and sit down while your food is prepared.  The chips and salsa come out and the salsa verde has both flavor and a kick.  It's a little addictive.

I grab the al pastor, chorizo and beef.  You simply can't find stuff this good in most other places.  Squeeze of fresh lime and I am in Mexican street food heaven.

You leave, with part of your meal saved for breakfast the next day (everyone has tacos for breakfast right?) and your wallet is only slightly lighter.  Sounds like a win win to me.

On a dark, dreary, rainy, cold miserable evening we stumbled into Valanni famished, beaten down by the elements and looking for sustenance.  I'm really happy we did.

After leaving Varga not a few minutes before because they weren't serving food (Calendar Party), our hopeless faces said to the nice hostess at Varga, "where should we eat."  She suggested, you could go to Valanni.  My eyes lit up.  "I've never been there!" I exclaimed.  Off trudging through the rivers on Spruce Street we went.

We were seated near the window in one of the their oval shaped booths.  I enjoyed this seating arrangement because it allows you to sit very close to the person you're with.  Whether that's a good or bad thing all depends on your particular situation.

With the awful weather, I was in a gin mood.  My dining partner selected the Ecstasy which I tasted and I wasn't a fan of.  We ordered the lobster mac and cheese, grilled merguez and the spanikopita.  All of these entrees completely  and utterly hit the spot.  The lobster mac had ginormous pieces of lobster in it (large claw pieces) and the bechamel was held together by both small crab meat and jumbo lump.  Simply stunning.

For dessert, we selected the bread pudding which came a la mode.  While the ice cream was a bit melted, the bread pudding was delicious and I was happy with the selection.  It was also a small enough portion so I didn't feel overly stuffed after said meal.

Our waiter was very nice, and attentive to all of our dining needs.  The design and decor of the restaurant is very lively and I can certainly see myself returning here for drinks and bites.

Personable, friendly but this place misleads customers with erroneous claims of organic food.  I have purchased meats, produce, and sandwiches here but won't again until things change. 

On my third visit, the friendly chef Chad told me that the poultry in the meat case that was labeled "organic chicken" was not actually organic.  He didn't blink an eye and saw no problem with mislabeling.  When I asked why it was labeled organic he said it was from an Amish farm where they do things "old fashioned".  Next he bashed Whole Foods for mislabeling their grassfed beef and then gave me a definition of grassfed that was inaccurate.

I don't seek out a store like Tela's for the trendy decor, but for the actual products.  I'd like for you to label your products honestly so I can make informed purchasing decisions.  Amish is not the same as organic.  Organic is not the same as pastured.  And natural and old fashioned mean nothing.   

A note to the owner Dan Greenberg: Please educate your staff, from the chef to the folks working at the counter (who told me "I think our beef is vegetarian" - whatever that means), about what kinds of products you are selling, where they come from, and how they are raised.  

I was so looking forward to being able to support a local neighborhood market.  When you raise your standards, let me know.  I will gladly erase this review, write a new one, and begin shopping daily at your store, and spread the good word to my Fairmount neighbors. 

Here are some good links you can use to teach your staff about food terminology:

http://www.phillycowshare.com/grass-fed-beef

http://www.ams.usda.gov/AMSv1.0/ams.fetchTemplateData.do?template=TemplateC&leftNav=NationalOrganicProgram&page=NOPConsumers&description=Consumers

The dude behind the counter wiped his nose on the back of his gloved hand as he cut and toasted my corn muffin.   Yes, I saw the hand then get all folded up with the wrapping of my food.  Why the hell after all this I bothered to even take a bit of my corn muffin, I don't know.  So not worth it.  It was the nastiest tasting corn muffin I have ever had.  I threw it in the trash after one bite.

I don't like to slam a restaurant with one star.  But I also don't like snot in my food.  Clean up your act please.

Food is good but I can't take the lack of customer service and disregard for people's time. Call ahead and you still end up waiting another hour+ for your food...and no one seems to acknowledge how unacceptable that is! Then you get your order and it's wrong.  can't run a business this way....

I gave it a few tries, several tries...but I can't!

Neighborhood specialty coffee shop and micro bakery that has a from-scratch kitchen and bakery. Use a majority of locally grown agricultural products. Have their own chicken in the back for eggs

Came in again today to do some work and got a decaf "Cafe-Au-Lait" and the Easter Egger sandwich.  I had never seen a decaf Cafe-Au-Lait drink before, but it consisted of decaf coffee and hot milk. I enjoyed it. The Easter Egger sandwich consisted of egg casserole, cheddar, and greens on a bagel. It was delicious, and the bagel was much higher quality than I expected

Lots of outlets and friendly staff

Married couple that was selling their sourdough and brioche bread at farmers markets for a few years before they raised $30,000 toward opening a bakery and cafe on Kickstarter. 

Sell loaves of bread and have a counter service breakfast and lunch as well. The pastries behind the counter all look delicious. Serve breakfast until 11 and lunch after 11. I came with my friend for lunch and I got a half turkey sandwich and half Kale + Mulberry salad. They were both delicious, especially the bread that the sandwich was on. I also bought a chocolate chip cookie which was great as well. They also have a delicious and unique drink menu. I got a decaf coffee and it was fantastic.

Some communal tables inside a a few outside on the sidewalk of a parking lot.

I came her for my first experience with pho, as all of the other pho places in the vicinity seemed to be closed by 8:30 on Saturday.  I'm glad we stumbled upon Le Viet because it was pho-nominal.  I swear that will be my only pun.  

The decor is beautiful, clean and open, just dark enough.  They seated us right away even though we didn't have reservations and the service was attentive and friendly the whole night.  We choose a few things, but honestly everything on the menu looked amazing and I can't wait to try more. 

We started with the spring rolls and spare ribs for appetizers.  The spring rolls could have had a little more shrimp but they were very fresh and had great flavor nonetheless and the peanut dipping sauce on the side was stellar.  The spare ribs fell off the bone and were delicious as well, the portion size is also pretty large for the price. 

The pho itself just hit the spot, my friend got the House Special and I got the seafood.  Both were amazing, I liked mine a little bit better but maybe because I made it more spicy.  Both were filled with meat and veggies, and the broth was deeply flavorful.  This was a perfect meal for a cold night as it was hearty but not heavy, it really warmed me up. 

All in all the prices are surprisingly reasonable, the atmosphere is very nice, the food is pho-resh (sorry I had to) and extremely flavorful and the service is great.

Spoiler Alert: this is a restaurant week review.  I have wanted to come here since it opened and finally came for restaurant week last night.  Each plate is a delicious, well thought out work of art.  

We had all of the appetizers but the carrots.  This included chicken liver mouse, spicy buratta and a whitefish (almost carpacio style but I can't remember exactly what it was called).  The chicken liver was rich and cut with sweet cherries, served with fresh rustic bread.  The buratta  was served in a cast iron plan melted over the same type of rustic bread, it had so much flavor and was just slightly spicy - tip eat this first if you are sharing things because it gets a little mushy if you leave it till last like we did.  The whitefish had so many flavors and layers it thrilled us all! 

For the main course we had the veal, pork shoulder and tuna.   The sauces must be mentioned - each plate had their own sauce that complimented so perfectly, I could have eaten each with a spoon.  The best part is that they put more than enough on the plate, I hate when there is just a tiny bit of an awesome sauce. 
The tuna was just OK it was a bit fishy and somewhat over cooked, but not bad by any means, the sauce, as on all of the dishes, was unbelievable.  The veal was cooked beautifully, and is served with lots of vegetables, all of which were perfect and complimented by the best, somewhat tangy, sauce ever. The absolute star of dinner was the pork shoulder, if you go do not miss this.  The outside was perfectly crispy, the meat fell apart the sauce was earthy and rich and there was just enough vinegar to cut it and compliment, we couldn't stop eating it!  One of the best things I have had lately.  

The desserts were good too, a rich chocolate tart, "soft serve" ice cream with caramel sauce and a brownie and a rum babba.  All were good, the babba was very different and we couldn't decide if we loved it or not, but I kept going back.  

All in all I would come back in a second.  The food is delicious, the service was good, and the atmosphere is quiet and cozy.  The drinks are on the expensive side, but that is the only complaint I can make.  This is definitely one of my new favorite places, and in my opinion one of the best new comers in Philly.  If it has been on your list (I'm sure it has) you need to pull the trigger and get here!

I have been waiting for a concept like this to come to Tucson for years...and it's so cool.  The remodel looks great, the staff is super friendly and attentive, and the food and drinks from the bar came up really quick.

Online ordering is super convenient too!  I ordered the tickets on my phone, got to pick out my seats, and paid for them in seconds.  When we arrived, I just showed my phone to the nice kid behind the counter, and we were in.

So why three stars?

Long story short- eat before you get there, & enjoy a beer and a comfortable seat while you watch a movie

The food.  It wasn't just bad because it was prepared poorly, it was bad all the way down to the ingredients in some cases.  Also, I fully understand that you have to serve everyone all at once, and that it's got to be really hard...but not selling low quality food would make it easier. 

My girlfriend and I shared the pretzel with dipping cheese and mustard.  The pretzel was literally wet with butter...so much so that you couldn't taste anything else.  The dipping "cheese" was obviously from a can (or maybe a powder?) because it was grainy and tasted metallic.

She got a black bean burger that fell apart, and was bland in flavor, though the fries were good.

I had the Mac and cheese....which was literally a cup's worth of mushy pasta, and (although the cheese wasn't grainy as it was in the pretzel dish) but had the same "cheese-like substitute" flavor and for that, I paid $10.

When will new restauranteurs learn that we'll pay a couple of extra bucks for better quality food?

So why not just 4 stars?  Because the opening menu is a representation of who you are...and this one says cheap...it says microwaves and high profit margins at the expense of the customer's experience.

Please make sure you check your receipts. Especially in the dark!

I have been here on two occasions and on both occasions they  managed to get the bill AND food order wrong. 

The first time, I gave them a PASS since the movie was packed with patrons and it seems everyone was ordering a drink or food. The second time, however, no excuses. There were a total of 6 (yes, six people) in the entire theatre since it was a matinee. They forgot our dessert then proceeded to overcharge for a few items.

Great concept, terrible execution.

This is another one of those gems hidden in a strip mall. I almost didn't go in the first time as the area this restaurant is located in doesn't exactly have curb appeal. But just a take a peak inside and you'll instantly see that the restaurant is worth a stop in. 

They didn't skimp out on the decor, and the cozy dining area is filled with warm colors and comfortable season. The location works perfectly for more intimate dinners as well as parties of up to 10 people. They get busy, and I had tried to stop by once for a valentine's dinner without a reservation and there was just no way we were getting a table. 

The food was phenomenal and each dish has a unique fusion twist to it, making what you eat here a one of a kind experience. They also offer carry out, so you can sample the menu from the comfort of your own home. 

This is a wonderful place and can't recommend it enough.

I think I finally found my go to spot downtown. 

This place wasn't too packed: we got served rather quickly and didn't have to step on people's toes to get around, but there was enough people that the vibe was good and you didn't feel too awkward alone on the dance floor. The music selection was also the best out of any small bar. I'm so tired of typical dive bar music. They had a good dance playlist going (good classics, and again, nothing too wild so that you felt like you're at a rave but just enough to get you to want to dance). 

The Moscow Mule I had was perfectly made and I looked over the food menu, there were so many good choices but I ended up not ordering any food anyway. I definitely will the next time I come though. 

Really hope this wasn't a one time good experience, I'm hoping to make this a repeat spot.

Total FAIL.  

I went here for a big group lunch - since we were told we didn't need to pre-order ahead, 20 or so of my co-workers ordered their lunch from their "20 minutes" lunch menu, that was exceedingly simple. Mostly sandwiches, soups, salads, fish & chips and the like. Our orders were in at noon.

A lot of time goes by. 

The group of six ladies beside us were finished by 1pm; a few other tables (3-4 people) were still waiting for their lunches as well.

By 1:20, we were told "10 minutes more" for most of the remaining orders. A handful of our group had received their food, so it's not like they were waiting for everyone's food to be ready before bringing it out. 

By 1:35 pm, several people had left because they never got their food.

What's so hard about making stuff that you have to deep fry or assemble is beyond me. Okay, food preparation can get slow sometimes, but the fact that CSH served the same food we ordered to other people that arrived at the restaurant way after we ordered was just ridiculous. 

Apparently, our "large group size" warrants the longer wait...which is strange because I'm pretty sure you're just serving the same food. If our orders are in and the same dishes are being made, shouldn't they go to our table? Do they deep fry things lovingly in single batches? 

Avoiding at all costs in the future for any groups bigger than 1.

This was my first time having "Peruvian" styled food. I learned that Peruvian food was greatly influenced by various other countries. 

I was in a group of 10. We split multiple appetizers. Also My first time having ceviche. I really liked it! I love the spices and flavor in the sauces and dips. 

I had my first piscos sours (delicious and dangerous). I ordered a beef plate with rice, veggies and fries (Asian influence/stir fry). Also had dessert which was amazing! Ice cream with a subtle nutty flavor from a fruit that also makes the ice cream very orange, and shortbread cookies. 

I recommend trying it! It's not too pricey, depending on how much you order... group of 10 though. Can only imagine, right?

This place should get negative five stars. 

I can be critical but fair, and it is very rare that I go somewhere and almost completely lose my appetite. 

First off, it is a depressing place. I can't explain what it is about the ambiance but it has a vibe like a government service building. Think of it like a glorified soup kitchen. I don't know if it is the layout, the color temperature of the lights, the lack of any attempt to at least make it look a like a restaurant, or something else, but it is a very depressing vibe. Even the tables themselves have a very run down, public cafeteria feeling about them. Sadly, many of the patrons looked (and smelled) the part. The section where we were seated literally smelled like stale urine.


Then you go to the buffet stations, hoping to get something at least on par with the quality of an Old Country Buffet or something. You don't get it. In fact, what you do see once you reach the stations is more akin to what you'd expect in a minimum security prison than a restaurant. Try making a salad with wilted, brown lettuce and then you go to throw a few garbanzo beans on there - if you wish to scoop them out from a slime bath that is. I forced my way through the salad, trying not to let the smell of urine and the slimy garbanzo beans combine to make me truly nauseated. At least enough to get to a main course. 

Wading through the crowd of sweatpants-wearing, slow moving, mouth breathing knuckledraggers, I found what looked like a Tex-Mex station. I figured it couldn't hurt to make some nachos. Yeah sure, if all you expect to put on them is some scuzzy meat and some shredded cheese that will not melt. Why isn't it melting? Well, you learn that when you get to your seat and start trying to eat...it turns out the meat is room temperature. 

Now with an appetite all but completely gone, the last thing you want to bite into is a bit of meat that is not only scuzzy looking, but also room temperature. (In the business we call this the "danger zone." That means that bacteria can freely multiply and make you sick.)

Rather than take the chance at foodbourne illness, I decided this was enough. I looked at my wife, apparently trying to saw through a piece of fried chicken and said, for the first time ever in a restaurant, "I can't eat here. We have to go." The fact that she just nodded in agreement and said, "Yeah me either," told me everything there is to know about Golden Corral. 

I have given a few negative restaurant reviews on here, but never have I said that you should avoid a place at all costs. My previous negative reviews have been because I simply didn't like the food or a restaurant's concept. I have never before felt compelled to tell you that it would be a serious mistake to even walk into a place. That is how awful and stomach-turning the Golden Corral really is. Please do yourself a favor and heed this warning. Even if I'm wrong, it isn't like you're missing out on some premier ritzy restaurant. It's just some crappy buffet in Bensalem. Simply avoid it, and live well.

I had an appointment at the Center For Advanced Medicine today and decided to have lunch at the fish. Colin was my server and he was great. Very friendly, explained things and answered questions. I ordered goyza (dumplings), shrimp tempura and a shrimp tempura roll. Everything was delicious but the asparagus inside the roll were hard to chew. Other than that it was a wonderful lunch. If you go, ask for Colin.

I started eating Beast when it first opened over in Belleville and was so happy they opened a great space here in the Grove. They have the best BBQ in St Louis and serve actual ribs versus the baby back "rib" that everyone else serves. They are fall off the bone huge, super meaty ribs with an outstanding smoke and flavor. The pulled pork is also fantastic as is all their other meat options. The sides are good, pretty basic BBQ place sides but the one item I didn't care for were the fried green tomatoes. I love fired green tomatoes but these tasted like fried green oranges. They tasted like they had been soaked in orange juice and were served with a small piece of orange on top. I would not recommend them but you have to try the meat!!

Rarely do I bother to update my reviews, much less in a city that isn't my own, but I had to here. Genghi's Grill continues to be as amazing as ever!

While in Tampa for business, I passed by on my way back home to South Florida. The location was as I remembered it. Clean, ample, with friendly employees.

Gilbert took care of me and even looped me into some of the changes happening since the last time I had visited three years ago. For one, they now offer triple starch and you can mix and match. You can do fried rice and noodles and who knows how many other combinations. Me personally? Triple spiral pasta!

Another change is that they now give you a receipt with your starch preference that you write your name on and leave up at the gong. Oh, and apparently it doesn't seem to be standard to ring the gong anymore. I had to ask about it after tipping a dollar, in which case they appeased me and rung it for old times' sake.

Anyway, given all that starch, they give you two mini cups where you choose your sauce. I'm forever in love with the sweet and sour, so I chose that, although I probably could've had two different sauces. Oh, and as far as how to stack goes - your best bet is meat first, then vegetables. Have fun.

Also seeing as I've gotten older, my food preferences have developed, so I had plenty of chicken, sirloin steak, and shrimp in my bowl. Add broccoli, potatoes, sugar snap peas, bell peppers, jalapeños, and some heavy helpings of cilantro and you had my lunch. Oh, and with some strawberry lemonade to drink.

Wound up with many drool-worthy photos I sent to loved ones, and more so, with a plethora of leftovers. Definitely ended up remembering many good times as this chain is one that's been one with me for years, and ah, I yet again ask myself why they won't refranchise down in South Florida.

Sigh. C'est la vie. A girl can dream and cue all the rest of those clichés.

It was a Tuesday. I was in town. Talking in person to Alexandra M. was a must, and so, the idea of a Taco Tuesday was perfect. At least that was my line of thinking. It probably helped I had this in my bookmarks for ages.

That being said, Besitos is a Mexican restaurant in the Tampa area that is next to Maggiano's Little Italy and has an impressive amount of free parking. It seems to be located in a strip of a variety of restaurants. You also can't miss it with the stream of cute lights it happily displays outside.

Anyway, I got there first and was served complimentary chips and salsa. These were pure perfection. The chips were crisp, the salsa had good flavor, and overall this combination just felt light and appetite-opening. Soon after my girlfriend arrived and we met our waiter, Facundo, who was super nice and attentive.

We started off with drinks. She had a margarita, while I wanted to try some tequila. A note to anyone wanting tequila: they have an entire menu dedicated to it! I had trouble choosing, but fortunately Facundo came through and recommended Don Abraham, which ran smooth as I drank it neat and it left a punch reminiscent of bourbon. Needless to say, I loved it as bourbon is my absolute favorite.

In terms of appetizers, we shared elote de la calle and tamale de elote. The elote de la calle was ultimately hearty pieces of corn that seemed to go on forever. The tamale de elote, a tamale made out of corn, in comparison was smaller and sweeter, but both were great starts to our tacos. I ordered the shrimp tacos, she had the carnitas tacos. 

The tacos were immense. I know that with mine I skipped out on some of the soft shell as I wanted the goods inside. Turned out to be a fantastic call as I got super full and we couldn't even finish the elote de la calle, which we ended up leaving as it made no sense to take home (or in my case back to the hotel). All in all, this one is worthy of a repeat performance and I'm saddened that there isn't one in South Florida.

Came into town on business and flopped on my hotel room bed, exhausted, and desperately seeking comfort. 

Given my need for comfort, I immediately thought of pasta because it is INDEED comforting. Specifically fiocchi di pera. As a result, I searched everywhere for a restaurant that delivered and had pear pasta. Enter Bella's.

Bella's has a unique take on pear pasta called the pera satchel. It's fiocchi filled with pear obviously but topped with peas and prosciutto. Admittedly I was hesitant to order this as all the ingredients overwhelmed me, but it's honestly probably one of the better ones of this dish I've had.

Also, can we talk about their huge portions? Typically fiocchi is served as a dozen purses of pasta, but after ceasing my eating, I had eighteen left for the next day. Yes, folks, eighteen! I am still flabbergasted to this day.

And to top it off, in typical fashion, I went overboard and ordered bread and dessert. The bread was probably the one thing I didn't enjoy as I found it bland, but the dessert was godly. The Vesuvio, or their take on molten lava cake, is extremely rich and unless you've got a major sweet tooth, prepare for leftovers of that and the accompanying vanilla ice cream.

Needless to say, I think the only reason I didn't end up in food coma was because I managed to stop eating. So sheer willpower! That and I had work early the next day and was just grateful to have food and not bother hunting in downtown Tampa with the subpar weather we've been having. Anyway, this was just my experience with Uber Eats. I'd love to try the actual restaurant next time I'm in town.

The highlight of signature India was that they were open on December 25. Aside from that it was all down hill.

There are two dining areas - one with table service and the other with counter service and cafe seating. I can't speak for the sit-down side but the cafe side was dirty. Tables clearly hadn't been wiped down in a long time.

The staff was unfriendly and I felt unwelcome. I tried to phone in my order ahead of time but everything I asked for the guy seemed to not understand or claimed to not have despite it being on the restaurant's online menu. I gave up and ordered at the counter.

I tried to order a little variety for leftovers but ended up with one of my dishes wrong. My chicken tikka masala was missing replaced with a paneer, green pepper, and onion dish in a thin gravy. I love paneer but with my other dish a paneer dish it killed the variety. Both dishes were just okay. Only one spice level which was very mild.  The rice was over cooked and completely flavorless. With the abnormally thin gravies it didn't hold up at all.  The bread basket (three naan varieties) was just okay.

With all of the other west county Indian restaurants this one won't go into my rotation.

I'm a sucker for good eats and drinks on the go. Mosey on up while shopping, order a muffuletta, cava with a straw, and keep on keeping on. I hear the sangria is pretty damn great too. The point here is sustenance and this place is a perfect spot.

Mind=Blown! When visiting New Orleans, be sure to take this tour. I took the 3-hour afternoon Historical River Cruise on the mighty Mississippi and it continues to be one of the most memorable experiences of my stay. This might be the best $34 you'll spend while in town. 

Not only will you sail downriver to the Jean Lafitte National Historical Park on a paddleboat, tour the Chalmette Battlefield with a National Park Ranger, but--hold on to your hats--enjoy $10 bottomless mimosas and bloody Mary's for the entirety of your trip. Oh yeah, there's also a $14 buffet if you want to fill your belly. I stuck with the bottomless, bought some snacks at the bar, and took it all in. If you want, you can purchase commemorative photos that are taken right before you board. Oh yeah, the bathrooms were clean and well-stocked, too!

If you can, book the tour when Charles is on duty. He's a native USMA grad that will give you a first-hand account of the events that occurred before, during, and after Hurricane Katrina. I, along with others on the tour, were brought to tears. Be sure to tip him well, as he masterfully blended the psychosocial and political elements of this tragedy with the resiliency of the people of this great city. Haunting and beautiful.

Oh Gazebo Cafe, you kept me coming back for more. Super friendly, tasty drinks, good music. We found ourselves here time after time for some hurricanes and Irish coffees. Beware, they are potent and you will get some pretty good bang for your buck. So sit back, relax in the open air, and take in the music.

If I were to be reincarnated as a chicken, I'd be one of the first to peck my beak on the dotted line and request that I'd be sent to Willie Mae's. There, I'd rest comfortably knowing that I brought people together, fed them well, and would be talked about for years to come. If you've gotta go, might as well go out in style. Am I right, ladies?

That said, I'm not a chicken this time on the merry-go-round of life and got to experience the joy of eating at this poultry house of deliciousness. Here are the standouts: Everything! The fried chicken speaks for itself, rice, beans, mac and cheese, cornbread, mashed potatoes, and fries are all insane. Luckily, we came on a Thursday afternoon and had no wait whatsoever. I highly recommend it! Oh yeah, the service was brilliant as well. Until we meet again, Willie Mae's, in this life or the next!

I have visited 5 breweries in Nashville this weekend. Tennessee Brew Works is by far the best. The beers were really good, but what sets it apart is the staff. The people working here are naturally friendly like friends giving advice and being helpful. Whereas some of the other breweries felt like I was part of a business transaction. 

The stage up front had great music and the 2 story taproom with dart boards and seating inside the brew room was great. The outside 2-level seating looked great but it was a little too hot/humid for us to be out there. 

Go here over the other brewery spots. You will not regret it.
In January 2020 ECSS had a fire and has been closed since due to health code violations and the damage from the fire. That was in the local paper. Hopefully, they will reopen.

I haven't been here for awhile. Oh my Goddess! What has happened to Portillo's? Whoever bought this company from Dick Portillo needs to stand up and put his own name on this establishment because he's, so far, tried to ride on the coat tails of Dick Portillo's name, and it's not working! I was so totally dismayed with the level of service, execution of delivery, down to the taste of the food (from cutting corners), that I am not sure I'll ever return to this long time well-known Chicago institution!

Here's what happened: I placed my simple order at the drive-thru: Beef Sandwich, dipped/hot peppers on side, gravy on side; 
Cheese Fries/Sauce on Side
Breaded Chicken Croissant Sandwich/ALL condiments on side which include mayo, lettuce, tomato. 
Chocolate shake. Simple order.

For some strange reason, even though the place is empty, it still takes a team of at least a half-dozen workers on walkies, card readers, earbuds, etc., to decipher my order as I inch along to the front of the line, 3 separate people along the way repeating my order differently, with me correcting them and having them make the necessary corrections, I pay, get to the front and get my order, ask the girl to repeat it - I check my list as I have it written down, it SEEMS RIGHT. First thing I notice wrong is the receipt is not stapled to the outside of the bag, as is customary. Normally I wouldn't care, but the girl wouldn't give me the total stating, since I was paying part with a "Gift Card" I would "find out" the amount debited when I got my food. Say what? Are we playing a game here? Wtf...lol 

I get to the first stoplight going home and find out there is no straw in the bag for the shake. Come on. Portillo's would've never forgotten the straw. Okay, what did you do with Portillo's??? I want them back...NOW! I reach inside to steal a fry while they're still hot...what the heck??? Did they keep walking by the fries, adding more and more salt to these fries because they are waaaaaay over salted! Yuck!

The CROISSANT Chicken Sandwich came on a GNARLED HAMBURGER SLIDER BUN OR WHAT WAS LEFT OF IT!!! The chicken looked hacked up, too! The first bite of my beef was pure gristle and fat and I spit it in the sink, but the rest of it was okay! I put the rest of it away because frankly, I just lost my appetite...

This guy, whoever he is, needs to train his people better, because I do believe it can be done, tighten that quality control, fire all those people running those jobs who don't really care whether or not they have a job, and if you don't want to step up to the plate and do these things, put your own name on this company so you don't end up tarnishing Dick Portillo's good name!

The Stein & Vine is amazing! Even though it's located in the middle of a strip mall, marked only with the word "P U B", once inside, you  will be happy you're there. The atmosphere is casual bar, but it's a bar which just so happens to serve sophisticated food. 

Even though this spot is technically a bar, Stein & Vine's food is anything but mere bar food. It's exciting because the cook makes imaginative, inspiring, fresh and delicious dishes. Plus, there are new blackboard specials every day, which guarantees you never get bored with their selections. One of my favorites, which they have quite often, is the Lobster Mac & Cheese. It's loaded with large pieces of lobster and is creamy and delectable.

The crowded bar scene is noisy and lively every lunch hour, and every night of the week. Seating includes a large bar (in two side-by-side rooms), and lots of 4-seater tables on both sides that can be pushed together for large groups.

Management is right on top of things. Once, when my take-out order was accidentally given to another customer, the issue was addressed quickly and corrected by management by getting my order to me very fast with a smile. In a goodwill gesture, I also was given some perks for my next visit. 

Stein & Vine also has a great Caesar Salad with homemade salad dressing. Their Chicken & Waffles comes with maple-sriracha syrup, and also is very good. Even their "Tots" are homemade! Everything here is delicious, and drinks are strong. You WILL have a good time here, no matter what meal you have!

*****FIVE FABULOUS STARS!!!!!*****

Florida jumped on Trader Joe's bandwagon, and "allowed" TJ to open its first store in 2012. Clearly, Florida wasn't ready then, and it isn't ready now, for the excellence that Trader Joe's stands for. When TJ's opened in Florida close to four years ago, they instantly realized they had an immediate, horrible parking problem (at this location). It was at that time that management promised that the problem would correct itself once the initial crowds died down. That's a laugh.

Anyone from California, who has seen how well-oiled the TJ machines run there, knows the crowds are never gonna die down! In Florida, the crowds remain the same since 2012, with no recent talk about changing this conundrum anymore. Why? And why do the workers at this Trader Joe's have such a bad, snarky attitude toward their customers? 

Since opening its very first store in Pasadena, California in 1967, Trader Joe's has always prided itself on excellence, product value to customers because they never made their suppliers pay for their shelf space (as other supermarkets do), they give customers the promise of fresh, wholesome food, as well as having low prices that go along with their laid-back theme of people helping people. 

At the same time TJ's was created in California, a fun atmosphere of customer respect, friendliness, smiles, all the while wearing a colorful Hawaiian shirt while packing your groceries or loading them into your vehicle if you wished was also created and is still held to that same standard today. (In California, not Florida.) While customers shop, they know there's always a knowledgeable person available to help them to answer any questions about their products that are a little bit different from the norm, because many unusual TJ-brand items are made from international recipes. (In California, not Florida.)

So what makes this Trader Joe's so different? I don't know. Complacency maybe? All I know is while shopping there, I continually found myself shocked at the behavior of the snarky employees, as well as the occasional person also shopping, and trying to pick a fight with someone. Shockingly rude, and no one made a move to stop any of this. I couldn't wait to get out of there.

It was pretty disgusting trying to enter the parking lot (cars were entering from both sides down the street), while watching nobody letting one another in (take turns maybe?), people honking because you chose not to just barge in, and a parking lot worker, supposedly 'directing' traffic, all the while making it worse by ignoring a potential argument between customers erupt. It's unsettling to see this.

No thanks. Floridians should visit a Trader Joe's in California to see how it's supposed to be done. Maybe some of that San Diego kindness will rub off on some who seem to walk around here with a chip on their shoulder.

Not Sure why this place has 5 Stars??? The rolls we had were not fresh, they were kinda fishy. This really surprised me because I expected a five star sushi place. This place is supposedly the best and is consistently filled with guests.

Everything we had was A-OK, but the main sushi item we wanted to try, the Crunchy Salmon Roll, was on its way out. Salmon wasn't fresh, and it had imitation crab. Eww.

I don't know if it was because it was a takeout order or what. Since I'm the sushi lover I ordered this kind of as my main meal & to munch on it in between a plethora of treats such as the Egg Rolls (ALL cabbage). The egg rolls had a vinegary sauce for them, which was watery and just a bad choice. We also had a couple of the Miso Soups (which had no thought put into them), and the soup had an off-putting acidic taste, too much of something was disturbingly cloying. Finally we had a couple of Dinners of Chicken Katsu (this was the highlight of the meal), and sadly, our Regular Fried Rice wasn't anything special & lacked seasoning.

Would I go back? Maybe. Only if I ate there because of the takeout sushi. When I want sushi, I want to be able to get takeout and have it be really fresh. I had to use a lot of my Thai Chili Sauce at home.

I've honestly gotten much fresher sushi rolls at Publix Grocery Store.

With a charming ambiance, some great food, and even better company, Primebar will always stay in the back of my mind, and I will go back to it when I find myself in Wesley Chapel again. Wesley Chapel is an upscale little town, containing Winegrass shopping mall, and a plethora of beautiful homes, where it's clean and pristine, sparkling and urban-ish. And there's Primebar.

We order an appetizer of Mac and cheese egg rolls to share. These are something else, and in a good way. I want to smack his hand and eat them all myself! because they are deliciously crisp on the outside, creamy and gooey on the inside, making a perfect little open egg roll. There aren't enough of these in an appetizer, but get them! 

He then orders a California Chicken Club sandwich, while I order a Primeburger Special. My cheeseburger was cooked perfectly as I asked, with an egg on top (of course!) and was solid. He exclaims that his sandwich is delicious! and offers me some, but I declined. The cheeseburger I had was pretty tasty. The meat was juicy, the cheese was melted perfectly and the bun was toasted ever-so-slightly. I like my buns toasted ;). It's not easy to find a place with a good burger! Get this!

Our server couldn't be nicer or any more accommodating. She did bring me the wrong drink three times, but once she realized my Coke was 'off', and I mean it tasted like *shudder* - 'diet'!!! because the lines were dispensing incorrectly, she immediately corrected the problem when she figured out the bartender needed to fix it ;).

The ambiance here was pretty cool, though in the afternoon it wasn't exactly jumping! I can see that it would be more atmospheric during the evenings, and especially at happy hour, when alcohol drinks are priced much better.

Boca Brandon has a farm-to-table concept that truly works. You really should come and try Boca Brandon. No matter what you order here, from alcoholic drinks down to the food, be it Lunch, Dinner or Brunch, you will love what they're doing here; providing delicious food at a reasonable cost. You can't do better than Boca Brandon.

Pizza! One of the five food groups, right? It is if you go so far as to go out for pizza at least once a week or make it by scratch (including the crust) at least once a week! Doesn't everyone? Yaaasssss :XD

When you live in Florida, the pizza gods must have something against peeps having that ooey gooey, delectable goodness called 'great' pizza! I say this because obtaining good, Midwest pizza in Florida is like an elusive butterfly that darts away whenever you try to catch one.

Enter New York, New York Pizza. Now, the East Coast (New York) and Midwest (Chicago), who both love their pizza, are certainly divided on whether New York pizza or Chicago pizza is the better of the two. Who cares as long as it's close enough to what we are both used to from the Midwest! 

New York New York Pizza comes close, Yelperazzi! 

We have ordered from this location a few times and have always enjoyed their pizza. The pizza has a good crust, firm enough to hold the toppings, yet pliable enough to fold the slices in half to eat it Chicago-style. Customer service here is great, everyone is nice. On my regular visits, one pizza maker in particular always makes me feel so welcome. I don't know his name, but he is always talkative with me, never fails to ask me how my day is, and engages me in conversation, without slipping on his job. Employing kind people at any business is always welcome and highly appreciated! And as if that wasn't enough, he always insists on walking my pizza out with me to place the pizza in my trunk! Thank you for that!

We will return again and again.

Shells is a Florida seafood restaurant, located in a decidedly sketch neighborhood of a dusty and dirty strip mall, in the sometimes-good-food-town of Brandon. Back then, we ate the Shrimp Pasta ($12.99), the dish they're famous for, and it was delicious. The Baby Lobster Pasta ($15.99) also was excellent and both were very tender and tasty, with soft, buttery fettuccine noodles. 

However, the Chicken Pasta ($10.99) last night had uncooked chunks of garlic that were so unappealing it created a gag reflex, plus the dish was overpowered by white wine. The only redeeming item on my plate was the 5oz Salmon ($11.99). It was just ok though. I asked to have it "blackened". It had seasoning on it, but it was not blackening; very disappointing. To top off our meal, we ordered 2 desserts: Chocolate Cake ($6.99) and Key Lime Pie ($5.99). You walk in and immediately recognize that the dim lighting, stone work and dark woods inside Stonewood are as gorgeous as the outside of this free-standing, elegant building! You should consider yourself "fancy" when you go out to dinner here! Stonewood Grill & Tavern is about the only restaurant I know of within a five-mile distance of my home that IS fancy! You see, you have to understand. Fancy is not common in this town. Fancy I can only do myself at home. OR we go to Stonewood *wink. 

Grouper is well known and abundant in Florida, fished right on the Gulf, and is served widely in restaurants here. At Stonewood, I had their herb-crusted oven-baked Grouper with balsamic reduction drizzle over top. It was served with fluffy, moist rice pilaf and al dente French green beans sprinkled lightly with garlic crumbs. It was all done to perfection. Fish was tender and flaky and broke apart easily. Rice was so fluffy and puffed. It had great flavor. Green beans had snap to them, al dente, cooked just enough. 

Their Shrimp and Scallops were heaven. Each shrimp came wrapped around a single buttery grilled scallop, the scallops and shrimps done to perfection, accompanied by fresh broccoli with Bearnaise on the side, and fluffy rice pilaf. Their rice pilaf is really yummy, not just an afterthought like at most restaurants; they do something more.

I've also tried the Blackened Chicken Pasta. It's base is a Chardonnay cream, and has bow-tie pasta with fresh spinach, asparagus, sun-dried tomatoes, and grilled garlic bread for dipping into the rich cream sauce. 

For desserts, I've had creme brûlée, which is excellent, creamy and smooth in taste, with its little flecks of vanilla from the vanilla bean, but it doesn't travel well, *(more on to-go later), and their tart key lime pie, which comes with a sweet-but-tart, indescribably unforgettably delicious raspberry coulis that will knock your socks off! Both are rich as diamonds and creamy as mousse. You won't be disappointed with any of their desserts. They also have a great chocolate cake.

Every meal also includes a house bread basket, with delicious choices of pre-baked (outside-sourced) breads. Their Caesar salad, with homemade house dressing, also is a big hit with me. I order it every time, because all the elements that combine this salad, including the croutons, are all homemade, and I just can't resist an excellent salad.

Stonewood Restaurant opens at 4:00pm for Happy Hour nightly, until 10:00pm, except for Sunday's, when they close at 9:00pm. The bar area here is relaxing and casual; dress is casual-chic. Please do not come here dressed in flip flops and shorts, as this is more a casual-chic restaurant. 

On all occasions I've been here I've interacted with the barkeep. Happy Hour has great deals on drinks and food on the HH menu, which changes occasionally. The bar is lively and full - always a crowd, and many people seem to prefer to eat at the bar. Past the bar are booths with luxurious seating. Relax here and have a good time. This is one place you're not supposed to rush through your meal.

*Note: All of our meals have been packaged "to-go" so far. The wait staff have brought out all our meals ceremoniously on a tray, with them going over each item, so as not to miss anything that was ordered. It's a very good system for to-go orders. I must give Stonewood props for that because it works so well!

I heard a lot about Ciccio Cali from friends (all good), and decided it was time to try it. I quickly scanned their very minimalist menu of salads, bowls, wraps & stir-frys & decided on the Short Rib bowl. 

We ordered take-out, because I did not like the atmosphere of the place at all. It is hard to describe, but let's just say cheap multi-colored uncomfortable-looking chairs & tables made of cheap plastic, and cheap minimalist decorations to go along with it. Bland, boring & uncomfortable seating to say the least.

The food was a-ok, nothing I would write home about. I feel if you are going to offer an exotic touch such as a short rib to a meal, you need to bring out those bold flavors, and Ciccio Cali just did not bring them together. Kinda sad, because I expected more. 

The dish was served over yellow rice, which was also nothing special. It was a little bit dry, and had I eaten it alone, it would have been boring. The side salad was chopped lettuce leaves which were already browning on the edges, and they did not make a great presentation. But they were crisp and the salad dressing (blue cheese) was tasty. That was the highlight of the meal.

I also had a chocolate cupcake. The cake was good and moist, but the frosting was too sweet. The frosting seemed as though it was made with shortening, something I don't like in frosting. I'm not sure if that's a fact, but it tasted as though it was.

Would I go back? I don't think so. I just don't see anything else I would like to order.

Although my daughter said her burger was really good, my Marco Polo chicken sandwich wasn't the knock-your-socks-off type. I've had much better for less money.

In fact, I was slightly irritated when I received the check for our lunch. The total lunch bill was $48.00. It also minorly bothered me that there was an additional charge for MY order, because I switched out French fries for onion rings. I wasn't advised there would be an up-charge of $1.49 to change the fries out when I ordered lunch. I think that is something that should always be pointed out during the ordering process. When I ordered, I do remember asking her if I could replace the French fries with onion rings and she said, "Sure", but that's when your server should tell you there's an additional charge to do so, if that is their policy. Not a large amount of $, but it's the principle of the matter. Service otherwise was cordial and friendly, although I had to ask for a second (endless lemonade) refill.

I've been to a lot of Red Robin restaurants over the years, but I don't remember a lunch for two people ever being in the $50 range there. That's one expensive burger and chicken sandwich. To justify that price, it would've had to have been excellent, and that, it just was not.

We chose several items. A long loaf of Cuban Bread, a couple of cuppycakes, a half pound of cookies, a chocolate eclair, and a peanut butter cookie. 

My cuppycake choice was a perfectly made Mint Delight cuppycake, which reminded me of a Thin Mint Girl Scout cookie, only better. The chocolate cake was moist and the buttercream frosting perfectly balanced, with just the right amount of mint-to-buttercream ratio. It was not overly-sweet. It had a small center of lush chocolate about the size of a coin. It was topped with a half-piece of an Andes Mint Candy. I have to say, this was the best cuppycake I've ever had, and it was so rich and large, it needed to be eaten in intervals. Lol. My eating buddy chose a caramel/praline cuppycake. I tried a bite, which was very good. The praline encircling the cuppycake tasted like the praline of the South, New Orleans to be exact. Yummy. 

The Bow Tie cookies, which mainly comprised puff pastry with a hint of cinnamon and doused in powdered sugar, were light and fluffy. The chocolate eclair is waiting in the fridge for us to share for dessert tonight. You can eat only so many sweets. Lol.

This bakery is very good, and lines move fast. There is a lot of retail help, some who are very helpful and perky, and one sour apple in the bunch. To be expected. Carry on. The system of pulling a number and waiting for it to be called works efficiently here.

When we return, I'm dying to try the Cubano. I love a good Cubano! There are endless great looking food items to try here. Can't wait for the next time!

I'm definitely not the first person to say how great of a market this is. For years my family has been coming here to get pastries, pizzas, meats, cheeses, lasagnas and more and they are always a hit. Surprisingly (or not really actually) I hadn't been until recently and the reason for that became abundantly clear once I got there. Since I only visit on the weekends, the only day for me to go is on a Saturday and, man, does it get wild. They're open from 9 am to 2 pm and they aren't open on Sunday so it's not hard to see why it gets so busy. 
I wanted to go get my mom a birthday cake and I wanted to get in and out as early as possible so after reading reviews I decided to show up around 8:30. I waited in my car after getting one of many open spots until 8:45 when the line started to grow more than I expected. I decided I didn't want to wait behind more people at the bakery counter. 
By the time they opened the parking lot was totally full and line had grown past the parking lot entrance and down the street!! When they opened I went straight for the bakery in a rush as everyone stampeded in. I got an Italian Rum cake which was AMAZING. They offered to write something on there which was nice so I got happy birthday written on it. I also got some fresh sourdough, tiramisu, and a cannoli there. All of which were delicious. For breakfast we paired the sourdough with some goat cheese I also got and it was so so good. 
I also got a pizza to cook for later and some more cheeses.

You could honestly walk around for so long and find some really great gems among the cheeses, ready to cook meals, sides, produce, wines, pantry items, fresh pasta, and deli. Aside from groceries you can also get gelato, coffee, and sandwiches to sit and have there. It's a food lovers dream. I highly recommend stopping here. It's definitely worth the craziness even if you can only go on a Saturday!! I will say that even though it was super crowded as I was going in and it was a little stressful trying to pick what I wanted and order at the bakery counter, it did die down after that initial rush. I went by later before I left and the bakery area was mostly cleared out. The deli counter however is always the busiest!

High points (HA!) for being on the cutest little block - right near my favorite co-op and favorite book store. But aside from location, the crepe and coffee that I (regularly) get at the High Point Cafe is always the perfect thing that I'm in the mood for and so tasty. 

This is a pretty tiny spot, and I would recommend against going when school is letting out (its right across from some school, and apparently kids like coffee and crepes... who knew?). The prices are so so reasonable and the guys behind the counter are always cool and chatty. 

I'm kind of salivating just thinking about the crepes - sweet and savory combinations like caramelized apple and cheddar, or spinach, onion and chevre. And I've been told to try their sticky buns...apparently, they are awesome!

Been here a total of three times its one of my places I always eat every time I'm in Reno. The food here is good, prices are reasonable and service has always been good here. My favorite here is the brisket it has this good BBQ flavor to it is so good.The ribs are also good here there not to fall off the bone ribs but there pretty tasty. Sides I really like the beer braised chili  beans they have jalapeños and onions and cheddar cheese, also like the black beans and rice. Will be back here to try more stuff out on my next trip to Reno

Came here for a Burger cause most places always got a good burger but I was wrong the burger was Pretty plain. Here what we order The fried chix Pasta And Burger The food looks good but don't taste good. If I ever come back here think I'll stick to French toast or pancakes or maybe just a good ol   Eggs and bacon breakfast.

This is everything you want in a noodle shop: bright, very clean kitchen, and GREAT food.  Love the pad thai, the Tom Yum soup and the mango smoothies.  But hidden gem was the seafood nuggets appetizers.  Everything is made even better the host/owner Tom (or Tommy as his friends call him). He is so charming.

Not far from the Avenue of Nations but easier parking and friendlier host that most located there.

Major Bummer. Our neighborhood go-to for sandwiches is usually Roma Imports, but they close at 6pm and the craving hit us at 6:15pm. We figured  we'd give this a try. I got the eggplant parm sub and my husband got the Italian sub. The eggplant was thin and stringy, the bread was doughy. The entire sandwich was the same mushy texture, no crunch to anything. My husband said his sandwich was gross- overly smothered in vinegar and subpar meats. We didn't finish them. Money wasted, craving unsatisfied, and now we both just feel yucky.

I resurrected my yelp account from the ashes to write this review. The last time I wrote a review was in October 2012. I hate to write this, bc I only used Yelp for positive reviews, but Im just getting fed up. 

We've lived in Fishtown for 8 years. We have been loyal customers of Pizza Brain since it opened its doors. We loved it and rarely got pizza anywhere else in the neighborhood. We always told people to go to Pizza Brain and were proud to take out-of-towners there.
