Not anymore. Things have really gone down hill. When the pizza is made right, it's still very good. But there have been too many times when it's been made poorly. 

Tonight they sold us very burnt slices (pictured). The place was not busy, so thats not the cause. It feels like there is no quality control there anymore, which is disheartening.  

A few weeks ago, they sold us a pie that was so messed up it was the shape of a D. They gave us a slice to compensate (didnt really make up for it, since the pie was about 5 times more expensive). Im sorry, but that D-shaped pizza should never have been sold. Same with the burnt slices tonight. Which they didnt notice or mention. 

Do the owners still care about this business? If so, they should do more to be consistent. Consistency was not a problem like this in the past. 

Heres this scene from the movie Chef: 

"Should we serve that sandwich?"
https://youtu.be/9a7cX7fJ4Yo

I hope you watch it.

I've been a frequent and happy Coffee Market customer for some time, always enjoying the excellent coffee, delicious pastries and easy-going and inclusive atmosphere -- a diverse neighborhood crowd spanning ages, races, styles.  The baristas have been warm and welcoming, cheerful and seemingly open-hearted and open-minded.  All in all, Coffee Market had seemed to me be everything West Philadelphia should be and is.

Until this morning, that is, when, one of the young women behind the counter launched into a hostile, sarcastic and just plain ugly rant about white people.   In a loud voice that penetrated every corner of the Market, she asserted her view that all white people are racists who've acquired privilege and position built on a shared history as slave-holders.   Her tone and language were nasty, laden with invective, filling the morning's calm, sweet atmosphere with meanness.

As we left, I approached her at the counter hoping to engage her, even briefly, in conversation.   I guess something in my look hinted that I wished to comment on her speech, but before I could get a word out, before she could have had any idea of what I was about to say, she launched into another diatribe, this time against me personally.  She hollered that I had no right to intrude into her private conversation (a conversation that was in no way private, given her loud voice and the intimate size of the place -- I'd even hazard a guess that she actually intended to provoke someone into reaction).  She went on to rage at me that unless I was a person of color I had no right to speak to her at all, that as a white person (yes, I am) my views and opinion were unwelcome, and she then virtually invited me to leave and not return.  

Well, then, okay, we will not go back to Coffee Market.   Though this was a totally unexpected, rare and, I'd hope, one-off experience, who'd want to chance it again?  There are other places for coffee and pastry in our wonderful neighborhood, maybe not as good but, one hopes, where we will feel welcome and at ease.  As we left, so did another customer who'd been present throughout all of this, he a person of color who rushed up to us on the sidewalk and said, "I guess it's time for me to find a new place for coffee, huh?"  Yeah, I guess so.

A final comment: the irony of all this is that what I hoped to say to her was that, while I might not have appreciated her tone and language, and whether I agreed with her or not, I had found her perspective important to consider.

Last Sunday, trusty ol' Yelp suggested (turn your push notifications on people!) this place for brunch and it was a SPOT ON recommendation. 

I don't know what it is exactly about this place, but I found it to be the coziest little restaurant that made for the perfect start of my weekend day. Now, I wouldn't bring the whole gang here simply because it is a small restaurant but I think it's perfect for 1-4 people. We were in line around 11am--and it was a full house--you could tell all the other patrons in line with us were scoping out tables that would hopefully clear out by the time they gave their order at the counter.  Also, there are paper menus available at the counter, so pick one up and figure out what ya wanna eat to keep the line moving faster!

Hubby and I both got the traditional breakfast sandwich--he got his on bagel, I wanted mine on English muffin but they were out so I swapped it for sourdough toast and omg, I'm so glad they were out of the English muffin because that was hand down the besttttt breakfast sandwich I've ever had! We got potatoes and grits as our sides and both were very good. Like others have said, the grits were exceptionally good--unlike the bland, gritty yet tasteless goop you're likely to find elsewhere, these grits were fluffy, airy, and actually had a taste to them (I still sprinkled salt and pepper on them). Now I see why they have a "Make-your-own-grit-bowl" on the menu..it's easily their star item! 

I also loved the restaurant's decor and dishware. The coffee cups were so cute in their geometric variation and cold beverages like ice water and iced coffee were served in stemless wine glasses. The vibe of the restaurant is really appealing--laid back, casual, post-run meal/ pre-shopping day/pre-girls day/meeting up with a few friends kinda place! Slightly on the pricier side but the quality of the ingredients and superior taste justify it. I'm going back this weekend for sure!

Beautiful, pretentious and stiff.  The newly finished grounds are beautiful, but there is an air of pretense everywhere.  Men in black suits talking into their sleeves far outnumber the visitors, so the facilities do no feel casual or inviting.  Nobody's very friendly.  Valet parking is a must, there is no self park.  

We put our name in for lunch and were told it would be a 15 minute wait.  They took our phone number so they could call when our table was ready.  30 minutes later we returned to see if our table was ready.  The same woman who took my number said she had no record of it and that it would be at least another 30 minutes or more before we could get a table.  We decided to leave and it took 30 minutes to get our car from valet.  We gave the man our ticket and apparently nothing was done with it, as 15 minutes late a driver asked to see our stub.  Then they went for the car, which took another 15 minutes.  Our experience was disappointing and we do not feel a desire to return to try again.  

There are far better options for locals seeking fine food in a comfortable atmosphere.
Costumed hostess and wait staff. Reasonable prices for a hearty lunch. Historic beers and dishes.

after hearing a lot of hype on this place, i decided to check it out for an eagles game (bc according to all the email and fb messages, the piazza is THE PLACE TO BE for sunday funday) fine. i went. 

when we walked in we were told to sit wherever but since there was only one table left, our selection was easy. we sat down and waited. and waited. aaand waited s'more. finally we flagged someone down. i was reallly craving a bloody mary to get me started before i inevitably spent the day drinking beer cheering on the birds! after ordering our drinks we waited at least 10 mins before our server came back only to inform us that they didn't have any bloody marys. ok. i was about to tell her that i'd just take a beer instead when she ran away. so we were left waiting, again. as we waited, i looked around. the game was well into the second quarter and yet the volume on the tv was at a whisper and only two people in the whole place even seemed to be paying attention to it. our table was at an odd angle to see the game anyway, and my limited vision was blocked every time a server/patron walked by. after asessing the situation and because we had been there for at least 15 minutes with no drink we decided to bounce. 

shame too bc i was really looking forward to trying some fancy style junk food and possibly an adult shake for dessert. also, i just wanted to ask. why does the world effing champion burger use venison from texas with foie gras and truffles, etc etc. i dont know, that just seems sooo not what philly is about. shrug.

Everything was good but... so let me give you more context the food is really tasty and we did not get any plate or wrap. So everything was small for sharing... my favorites for sure Mohammara, Deluxe and Burrata, but we had more, Morrocan Olives, Baba ganoush, Tzatziki, Israeli Bruschetta, Marinated beet salad and Magic. My drink was the winter daquiri which was really good. Also went here for dinner at one of private "green houses" during winter/covid. 

If you order similar I think the problem is lack of texture I think that's way I like the burrata so much (and bruschetta) the crunchy texture because everything else is deeps with pita, which don't get me wrong were very tasty but gets boring.
Asked for some fresh vegetables at the end to have with deeps and turned out to be an excellent companion. 

The drink and service were good.

I hate steakhouses. I especially hate steakhouses that serve up grilled vegetables as their entree du jour pour vegetarien. But what I hate most is when these ghastly gastronomic horrors show up on your plate without the slightest flourish. Case in point - my dinner at Mortons consisted of bushes of steamed broccoli, and whole, boiled, skinned tomatoes and whatever little real estate was left on the plate was haphazardly crammed with gigantic asparagus, spinach and mushroom - appetizing? Mashed potato and green beans just became delectable!  Seriously, how hard can it be for these establishments to spend a fraction of time that it takes to serve up a filet mignon or a prime-rib, put a smidgen of effort to come up with something more palatable and at least pleasing to the eye for a herbivore? This isn't a review, it's a rant - damn them steakhouses!

After waiting patiently for the beautiful what lifts you mural down the block, we were eagerly craving a drink and something flavorful. I spotted the Pub and we wanted to escape the chilly air, so we thought a nice drink to warm the spirit would do. The ambience was loud, in a good way! Families were here, groups were filling up in every corner, and the liveliness was in full effect of charm and happiness. The back area has a dart board and fuzzball table to play after some drinks and chatter with friends. We miraculously caught two stools at the bar as we were going to leave, and as they exited I asked what they ordered. One guy told me his Bloody Mary was amazing. So I'm traditional faction of my trip I placed that as my order and we added pretzel with cheese for an appetizer. The drink had some real kick and I was pleasantly surprised, the pretzel was warm and buttery almost melted in my mouth and the cheese was not gooey more like a spread, but rich with flavor. Service was pleasant and quick, location was in a hotspot of a popular mural and with plenty of people all over. Great stop!

I am VERY sad to say we just can't order from Toto's anymore. Ill be honest, the pizza is really good, and is our favorite in the area. Unfortunately, the ordering and delivery process is a huge pain in the butt far too often. Several Times we have called and been left on hold for huge amounts of time and completely forgotten while we listen to the girl who answers the phone have a personal conversation in the background.. A few times our pizza order took well over an hour with not even an apology when we called to inquire. Twice, their online ordering system failed to work and our food never came even though we were charged. Another time we called in our order and when we called an hour later they had forgotten our order entirely. Finally, there were two occasions where they brought the wrong food completely. 

Why have we tried so many times? The pizza is the best we've found in the area. Unfortunately it's just not worth the hassle. As I type I'm waiting for an order I put in well over an hour ago...and when we called...the girl told us it was only 45 min. We didn't even argue. Just not worth it to eat from Toto's. Bummed.

FANTASTIC!!! I was SOO excited to have found Korean food so close to the house. This restaurant is small, but the food was great and the lunch specials are such a great deal. They do lunch specials even on the weekends, which is great! we started with a few orders of mandu (fried dumplings), that were very good. I opted for the Kalbi combo ($12) that came with salad, rice, large portion of AWESOME Kalbi (some of the best I've ever had) and Jop Chae, which are these glass noodles tossed in sesame oil with little bits of bulgogi and vegetables. My wife and son both had the spicy pork bulgogo, which they enjoyed as well. GREAT restaurant with the great service. i'll be here quite often!

I have wanted to try this place so many times because none of my friends like sushi. I wanted to be really hungry to try the all you can eat. As you know most sushi rolls range in price between $7.99 to $11.99. For $19.99 you can have all you can eat. You can choose from soup, salads, appetizers, nigri, 3 rolls sushi, dessert, and over 20 speciality rolls (8 pieces- are in a specialty roll) I first ordered the one piece roll. The one piece roll is the nigri sushi, but it doesn't say that on the menu, but I asked what it meant. I ordered spicy crab, spicy tuna, and  red snapper, and yellowtail. While eating I ordered the Broadway. While that was a good roll with spicy tuna, crab, and avocado. It was 8 pieces of alot of rice with yummy spicy tuna on top. I didn't come to eat alot of rice, so I stuck with individual raw sushi pieces. It was amazing sushi and fresh tasting. I ended up eating 25 pieces which was equivalent to 3 rolls. I kept eating Red Snapper, Yellowtail,, White Tuna, Regular Tuna, Spicy Crab and Spicy Tuna, and 2 pieces of Octopus in the end. I should have ordered the Octopus sooner. For $28.00 with tip it was all you can eat sushi and ice tea.. I ate like a queen and wish I had a sushi buddy like I did in California. I will definitely be back for the raw sushi. Oh the 3 roll sushi is your regular sushi, rice on the outside with fish, cucumber, avocado inside. I wasn't looking for that kind of sushi you can get really anywhere. The staff is very nice the one girl didn't speak hardly any English so thank goodness you mark the paper and hand it to them. For a new restaurant one of the bathrooms was broken, and the paint on the border needs to be fixed. They must have taken over the spot from another business/restaurant. There fresh fish speaks volumes.

This restaurant has amazing authentic Italian food!  Not only is the food incredible the service is great as well.  It's a small restaurant so prepare to wait a little.  Don't worry though, it's worth the wait and you can drink at the wine bar next door. 

We ordered the pear, walnut, and Gorgonzola purses, meatballs, and calamari salad for appetizers.  My husband said those were the best meatballs he has had in his whole life.  They got a half order since not everyone on the table could eat it.  

The service is so great you can order half portions of items and mix and match even things that may not be on the menu.  They are honest and let you know if it's something they can do for you.  

The table got an order of the clam linguine in white sauce, lobster and crab pasta in red sauce, braised veal and beef ravioli and I ordered the gnocchi in pink sauce.  

The gnocchi is stuffed with cheese and is one of the best I've ever had.  The sauce for every entree was different and all delicious in their own way. I highly recommend this place.  It's a little pricey for some but it's definitely worth it.

This place is a gem!  It is part of the Sand Pearl Resort. They have great food, drinks and it's right on the beach! We went with our cousins and had a great time. 

We all enjoyed our food-  the impossible burger was delicious- I added onions to it as well.  Their guacamole, quesadillas and sandwiches were good too.  

The staff was friendly and they had good service.  The ambiance and view the beach makes is even better! 

I would highly recommend coming here for a quick bite and view of the sunset anytime you're at the beach.  Bring you're guests here too!

I tried to use a groupon here and they would not take my reservation because they had a groupon "quota".  Of course, this practice is not supported by the fine print of the groupon.  In my opinion this is a very poor business practice.  I will NOT be trying this restaurant in the future. There's plenty of good Italian food in Philly.  If La Fourno doesn't want my business, so be it.

I'm always on the lookout for budget friendly options in this city... places where I can grab a good meal with a friend (or date) while still having enough dough left in my pocket for other things... like my light bill. So, when I discovered Pagoda Cafe right in my neighborhood (thank you Yelp app!) and I saw that the most expensive thing on the menu is $9 (you read that correctly... everything on the menu is $9 or less), I knew I had found my perfect spot! 

I had 2 breakfast tacos which came with some delicious, although spicy, homemade sauce. I also had iced chai with almond milk, which is nice because most places have soy milk or regular milk and that's it. My friend got the chicken salad and also commented on how fresh it tasted, especially the bread which was buttered and grilled right before our meal was served.

All in all, I love this place and will definitely be back again before the summer is out. Even if it is just to sip some iced chai and people watch on the patio!

The yelp app helped me find this little coffee shop gem one morning when I arrived at work and realized I needed caffeine... bad! The barista was super helpful and friendly and the tea was delicious! They also had a huge piece of red velvet cake for sale, which had about as much icing as it did cake (a big plus for me). Since it was 9am, I did not get a piece but promised myself that one day I would come back there for dessert... so stay tuned for an update!

I barely had any of the food and drink. I tasted some of my moms and sisters drinks and appetizers and they were okay. If you are black or brown don't go here. It's not safe or welcoming. As soon as I walked in with my mom and sisters all eyes were on us and not in a good way. It's like we had invaded everyone's space. 

The waitress was very short and didn't bother to explain the menu or anything about the place to us. I'm also vegan and they didn't have anything on the menu to accommodate me so I ordered delivery. And I fully intended on eating it in my hotel room but my mom asked me to ask, what's the worst they could say. So I walked over to ask our waitress and as soon as I approached her she looked scared. And immediately 2 other white male employees walked over like I was about to beat her down. She was completely frazzled by the fact that I wanted to ask her a question. Ultimately I was told no outside god or drink which is fine but the behavior displayed was the worst. 

As a person of color this is definitely not a safe space for us. It's unwelcoming immediately. If you want somewhere to hang without feeling like you're being watched or rushed out you're better off enjoying the hotel restaurant on the 2nd floor. 

If I could give it zero stars I would.

Although we have been getting take-out from some of our favorite places in Philly, this was the first time we have actually eaten at a restaurant in Town since this whole pandemic thing began. What an excellent experience it was from beginning to end.

We ate at one of the covered outdoor tables that line the street - with most looking like they can accommodate a party of 4. A few may hold more. After checking our temperatures, we were led to our table.
Because our reservations were for 5:45, we just snuck into Happy Hour prices for some of the items. 

Under "Small Plates" we enjoyed:
Focaccia with Bee Pollen and Honey Butter, Farmer's Cheese and Whipped Tuscan Lardo.

Tuna Tartare with Celery, Apple and Truffle.

Snapper Crudo with Fennel, Horseradish and Lemon.

Asparagus with Prosciutto, Mint & Shallot.

Gnoccho Fritto, Puffed Pastry with Prosciutto and Candied Red Pepper.
All were very very good with the Tuna and the Gnoccho at the top of our favorite list.

Under Pasta we enjoyed the Spring Pea Agnolotti with Mint and Smoked Pecorino. This was one of the best pastas we have had in a long time and should not be missed. If it's on the Happy Hour menu, as it was while we were there, order the full size portion - you won't regret it.

For our Main we shared the Roast Suckling Pig with Kale, Sunchoke Mostarda and Rosemary. Perfectly cooked with crisp skin and moist, tender meat underneath.

We had mentioned it was our Anniversary and were given a delicious complimentary Blueberry Sorbet with candied nuts and marinated cherries.
Because many of the small plate items were on the Happy Hour menu, surprisingly the bill, with1 glass of wine and 2 beers, only came to around $130 before tip.

All of the Staff could not have been more fun or informed about the menu. Can't wait to return.

If only I could select 4.5/5 stars (*sighs* - remaining hopeful for that option)!

Second time @Al's w/my hubs & it didn't disappoint at all from the soul food to the hospitality! The first time I brought my whole familia here after working up an appetite from exploring Ybor.

Aunt Mary's Triple Threat Meat Platter really is the way to go if you are looking to try different types of meat. Everytime we go, I always order ribs, a must have for myself; they give you gigantic slabs of smoked ribs almost as wide as my shoulders (no joke, see pic.)! One of the ribs ended up being extra crispy, prob. an end piece & a little smaller. Also, we got Pulled Pork & Sausage for my hubs.

Al the King of BBQ was behind the scenes in the kitchen & pulled out his trustry clever & chopped the pulled pork smoothly like Michael Jackson cuts music w/his vocals except w/his knife for utmost freshness. Personally, none of the meat tastes complete to me unless you try their 3 homemade BBQ sauce. My favorite...you guessed it correctly is the spicy one that creeps up on you; I thought at first I'd be fine & it was too mild, but you'll def. be in for a good surprise. The beers are a really good price point too, so my dad, mom & I ordered one each.

They wore masks while preparing the food during the pandemic.

The Cole Slaw was better than the Okra and Tomatoes, which was simply made. The Cole Slaw was fresh, light & not soggy...very refreshing!

You can eat your food inside where there is a/c. There's limited seating & pretty paintings. One painting includes a rooster, an iconic bird that represents Ybor; The rooster usually roams in the front or back of the bungalow. Sometimes I even like to sit outside where they have high top chairs even though it's insanely hot! I'm a Floridian, so I just love being outdoors given any chance I get :-D!

I got their Coconut Chia Seed Pudding & it was such a delight! It's the kind of tasty treat from your first bite to the last one that makes you want to go in for another spoonful - the coconut milk gives it a really nice flavor - def. Better to me compared to the matcha soft serve because it wasn't too sweet at all.

I really couldn't help myself and kept eating it! 

Parking is plentiful and wraps around to the back.

The employees weren't wearing masks as of 5/26/2021. Personally, it's weird to me because they're the ones serving us our food & I like the extra caution during a pandemic...

The Summer Dreams iced infusion drink tasted as good as it looked and gulped down a medium size, which was delicious to the last drop!

I met my friend and it's been awhile, at least a yr. since my last visit to Kaleisia, so happy we choose this place to catch up!

The purple/blue layer is an herbal tea called Blue Butterfly followed by Limeade that is a little tart, but mixes well with medium sweet level you customize dependent on how much sugar you prefer and lastly followed by peach puree. I added lychee instead of boba for texture and it provided another fruity sweetness to the drink that went very well with the other flavors. I really loved the different colors that were beautiful! I've had their Chai Latte with boba, which is always a good option, too!

There's a good number of tables although quite a few students were occupying them and there's outdoor seating with potted plants, but it was too humid and I was more comfortable inside with glorious a/c! They have a quieter room that I've visited that requires you to remove shoes before entering with low tables and love this option!

They have a frequent customer rewards card, too, so make sure to pick up one!

I love sitting at the bar, which is the center of the restaurant and wraps around the kitchen where you can have a peek of behind the scenes cooking of the women hustling to create your dishes! There's enough seating even during lunch, which brings in a fair number of people and outdoor seating with umbrellas for shade. 

BEEF PANANG CURRY: The curry was too loose and runny for me, prefer it to be reduced for a thicker sauce. I liked that they let me substitute broccoli instead of carrots and appreciate the flexibility, but wouldn't reorder this dish and not a fan of their version.

Their CHICKEN GREEN CURRY is probably the tastiest with strong, sweet coconut flavors and loved dousing rice with the curry, which isn't as runny compared to Panang. The bamboo shoots complimented the other veggies really well, thinking of this dish makes me want to go back soon!

CHICKEN FRIED RICE: This is a large serving and I couldn't eat it all, best savory chicken stir fried rice, made to perfection that I don't need to add additional spices and depends on how salty and spicy you like it.

THAI TEA: There's cinnamon sprinkled on top of a generous serving of whipped cream; It's everything and more than what I hoped for, definitely a sweet treat you must order (I don't wanna hear excuses, so just get it!).

They serve an array of meals including noodle bowls, traditional noodles, stir fry noodles & fried rice, curry, fish & seafood, etc.

Yes, in one of the pic. we have a napkin tied around our neck acting like a bib because we're messy eaters!

I feel like I've eaten here enough to write this review truthfully now.

First things first: I have never been to India nor do I have any baseline knowledge of what different regions' foods should taste like. I have a beautiful Indian friend named Robin K. so he's my main frame of reference. 

The Yelp check in offer is GOLD! That mango lassi is the best I've ever had! Omg. It's so good. I've tried the cheese naan, butter chicken, chicken masala and the vegetarian dish with lentils...yummmm! Everything that I have had has been delicious. I usually do take out and have not had the pleasure of eating in the restaurant but whenever I go the staff is always very nice and welcoming.

I am so lucky to have this place in my backyard so I can eat it as often as I want. I wish they sold that mango lassi by the gallon!

I really didn't want to like this place so much, as I really loved Anthony & Dandelion Deli. They were a staple of my neighborhood for 25 years, & served good food made with lots of love. 

I said I didn't want to like this place so much, but I REALLY do! It is right across the street from my nail spa & I have to hold myself back from going in every single day!

I had the Chanini & it blew my mind! Geez Louise! So stinkin' yummy, I ate the entire thing! (and I can't eat that much at once) 
You definitely get enough food for your money!

I went back a few days later & had their scrabled egg sandwich. AGAIN- super delicious!

The owners are so nice & have jazzed up the place nicely. I'm going back again today to try something new!
Welcome to the Wells Neighborhood, Walden's!

Really great coffee and chill atmosphere. I tried their iced coffee with oat milk and it was freakin great; Strong and delicious. They offer a variety of non-dairy milks and syrup flavors which I love. Variety is the spice of life. I also tried their country breakfast bowl which was pretty good. It was really creamy and rich filled with sausage gravy, cheese and potatoes...it was really filling. I found them to be a little on the pricey side...I spent over $20 on just those two items. Will go back!

The manager, Stacy Lyon, was incredibly rude to us. She would constantly come around telling us to take our check and get out. She yelled at us to leave and said security was coming even though we got our food only 20 minutes prior and agreed to leave. On the way out I asked to speak with another manager and she continued to yell and said she would delete any review we posted. The majority of this was recorded by myself and friends. She also got very close to our faces a few times during a pandemic which was concerning.

Mister Gregory's is a great little café with French inspired New Orleans grub.  We were spoiled with amazing food in New Orleans, and this place was good, but paled in comparison.  The space has a fun artsy hipster vibe.  There are a couple of tables inside and outside to eat at.  Their menu offers breakfast all day, Poor Boys, baked egg dishes, hot plates, waffles, and more.  The service was OK.  I think they forgot my order, as everyone else in our group was almost done eating, by the time I went up to ask about mine, and they said it was on the way.  The bread on the sandwiches was hard, and lacked flavor. The backed eggs were OK, but not great.  The food just lacked flavor overall.  They claim to have the best Cold Brew Iced Coffee in the area. Maybe I am spoiled by the awesome Cold Brew in Texas, as this was good, but wasn't great.  I think the price you are paying for the OK food and great ambiance is due to the location. There are a lot of tours that start from here thanks to the close proximity to the cemetery and trolley line.  It seemed that everyone was doing the same thing as us, grabbing a quick breakfast before our tour started from nearby.

Thank you Yelp for this amazing gem of a find!  It was within walking distance of our HomeAway.  Fry and Pie is located behind the Hi-Ho lounge.  For those from Austin, this feels like home.  A food truck and dive bar partnership.  This is a delux food truck experience. They have a stunning outdoor indoor covered seating area.  You can eat in or order from their walk up window and take it away.  If you eat in, the dining space is fun!  The décor is boho chic - fun and artsy.  They had games at some of the tables that you could play while you wait.  You can order drinks inside the bar, and bring them out to enjoy with your food. If you love loaded fries and handmade pies. This is the spot for you.  You can order the fries loaded, or naked to enjoy with their uniquely flavored dips.  I ordered the fresh cut fries loaded with amazing gourmet toppings. My mouth waters remembering how good those loaded fries were. They were SO cheesy, and delicious.  The best loaded fries I have ever had.  Save some room because the individual pan dessert pies are also good. But, if you only have room for one, the loaded fries are by far the best.

Café Amelie was started in 2005 and is named for Amelie Miltonberger, the mother of Princess Alice, the first American Princess of Monaco, who lived in an accompanying townhouse in the mid-1800.  The cafe is open for lunch, weekend brunch, and dinner.  It closes for a break between the lunch and dinner meals. It is highly recommended to have reservations to eat here during the busy season. We were lucky to squeeze in a late lunch here right before they had their afternoon siesta.  The space is mesmerizing.  You walk through a gate and immediately feel transported to another time. The green courtyard garden provided the perfect oasis from the busy streets outside.  It is surrounded by three towering townhouses that were built in 1836.  One of the occupants introduced the trend of large cast iron galleries on the French Quarter houses in the 1830's, and had Henry Howard design the hexagon tower. As there were no tables in the courtyard.  As awesome as the courtyard is, there is a romantic historic vibe inside as well.  The service was friendly and prompt. My group of friends all ordered different dishes. The salad was incredible, fresh and tasty. Everyone was happy with their food. Another great meal in NOLA.  They also had some tasty cocktails.  I would love to come back and just enjoy a glass of good wine out in the courtyard with a great book.

Topa Topa is a brewery that I've wanted to visit in person for over a year now. I found out about them at a few of the Surf n Suds beer festivals in Ventura county, and have had them on my bookmarks since then. Recently I headed over to the Funk Zone in Santa Barbara (an area right before the beginning of downtown Santa Barbara's State St.) to check out some places on my girls Axxess card, Topa Topa has a buy one get one free coupon.

First and foremost their beers are amazing, out of he five beers I tried I didn't have a single complaint. Very smooth and well balanced beers. The inside has a cool set up with a nice small outdoor seating area, inside/next door is a Llama Dog where you can get food (but you can't bring you Topa Topa beer over).

I don't recall seeing any board games like a lot of other breweries had, but it's still a really cool brewery to hangout in. Even though I've only beer here once I've got to say Topa Topa is near the top with the best overall beers at a brewery that I've hand in Santa Barbara so far. The Nitro Milk Stout & Chief Peak IPA we're mind blowingly good.

Mr. Ed's Oyster Bar is always busy because the food is so good. We had the seafood platter w/ jambalaya (jumbo fried shrimp, Louisiana fried oysters, southern fried fish), 1/2 dozen charbroiled oysters, and the Louisiana crawfish bread. Everything tasted so fresh and delicious. The crawfish bread was amazing and these were the best charbroiled oysters in NOLA. We totally regret not getting a dozen oysters. Husband and I agree that this was our favorite and the best meal we had in New Orleans.

You must stop by Cafe du Monde when in NOLA. The beignets are good and I love their frozen cafe au lait. They definitely go overboard with the powdered sugar though because it's everywhere! I do like Cafe du Monde's beignets, but prefer Loretta's praline filled beignets.

I'm so glad Verti Marte is open 24 hours because this is exactly what you need after a long day or night of drinking. We had the All that Jazz po'boy (grilled ham, turkey, shrimp, Swiss & American cheese, grilled mushroom, tomato, wow sauce all on grilled French bread). My picture doesn't do it justice, because this sandwich was packed and so tasty. All of the ingredients and sauce went so well together and we definitely needed to use a few napkins while eating it.

OMG...this is the BEST fried chicken we've ever had! The batter was so light and crispy and seasoned perfectly. The chicken was super tender and moist inside. I ordered the fried chicken (dark) w/ mac and cheese, husband ordered the chicken tenders w/ fried okra (loved the fried okra!). 

Definitely make time to stop by Willie Mae's Scotch House if you're in NOLA. We didn't want to miss it, so we went extra early before they opened and were first in line! Soon after we got there, the line kept growing.

We stopped by Dat Dog while walking along Frenchmen Street. We weren't even hungry, but just had to stop by Dat Dog for their amazing gourmet hot dogs. They have so many different types of sausages and unlimited toppings to choose from. I had the house special crawfish etouffee dog (crawfish sausage, crawfish etouffee, sour cream, tomatoes, onions, creole mustard) and absolutely loved it. If I didn't eat so many beignets earlier, I would have tried more items from their menu.

Definitely check out Dat Dog if you're in NOLA - cool spot with friendly staff and exceptional hot dogs!

I was super excited to try this place as it is super close to where I work. Of all the times I walked by this place it was always busy which made me want to try it even more.

I went on a Tuesday at about 1230 pm with a friend and was pleased that there was a table for 2 available for us. They also had bar seating but we opted for the the table. Our server greeted us with menus and for a restaurant that was less than 3 months old, she sure didn't ask us if it was our first time there or if we had any questions at all. We ordered the pork belly pork buns presented in a taco style (interesting concept) and found it to be disappointing for 3/$10. The portions were quite small and the filling in the bun taco was skimpy.

I ordered the pork ramen and can I say green onions galore? The pork broth was a little too salty for my liking and the flavor of the broth seemed like it needed more time to stew and sit. The noodles were outsourced and not made in house. The umeboshi egg was probably the tastiest thing in that bowl. The corn tasted like it was from a can. The mini pork cutlet pieces also was lacking flavor. By this point, I already knew I wasn't coming back.

To top things off, our sever handed us the bill without asking if we were interested in dessert or anything else. Then her sidekick (co-worker) came by and swooped our glasses of water away without asking if we were even done. I made a point of telling her this when she walked by after that we were not done with our waters. She did bring us new ones after apologizing but I think she was more annoyed that I asked for new waters and had to bring us new ones.

Eeek! Me really thinks NOT EVER again!!!

I have been to several Gordon Biersch Brewing Company restaurants in the past in several States and locations. I always enjoyed my meals and experiences at this restaurant chain. 

I was staying at the adjacent Hilton Hotel Riverside. This Gordon Biersch was across the street, therefore, I decided to give it a try for dinner with my family of four. I am glad we did. As you can see from my pics I started with my usual Jalapeno margarita with salt. I also enjoyed my favorite Jambalaya although my serving size could have been a little larger. Service here was also good. We all enjoyed our dinners here. When I return to this Hilton, I will definitely return here for another margarita and Jambalaya.

I would definitely return to any other Gordon Biersch.

I came here because I stayed at the nearby St. Louis Union Station - a DoubleTree by Hilton historic hotel. Lombardo's Trattoria was across the street and highly rated on Yelp. Also the Lombardo Family's legacy of fine food at moderate prices goes back almost 75 years. They own and operate 5 locations including this one. The original Lombardo's was at a different location. They are known for their famous home-made toasted ravioli. They also have their own house marinara sauce. The place has a bit of upscale atmosphere.

I just arrived in St. Louis for a convention. My hotel room was not available so I decided to eat lunch here. Very few people were here when I arrived so I decided to eat at a table for two in the bar area. Only one other patron was eating lunch at the bar.

Chris the female bartender and my waitress recommended the highlighted toasted ravioli's for only $8.95. I thought what a deal for only $8.95. The Housemade oversized beef, chicken and spinach Ravioli's are served with their own marinara sauce & romano cheese. The ravioli's were served almost immediately and then I realized why. They were not toasted, but, deep fried. I don't like to eat deep fried food often and as it turned out I was not impressed by their toasted (really deep fried) ravioli's or their marinara sauce. 

Chris, on the other hand, was very nice to explain that deep fried foods are very popular here in St. Louis. Now I know not to order anymore toasted food here. One of my Yelper friends Clarice expressed interest to visit St. Louis and Lombardo's recently. I cautioned her regarding my experience. I told her she should not rely on my review, because maybe she might like their deep fried ravioli's. I will probably give them one more chance to prove themselves with a different item on their menu. So I rated the place as average, because they must be better than my only one experience.

As you can see from my prior reviews, I enjoyed my dinner at Firebirds down in Gainsville, Virginia. This was my first time here at this location for lunch. My party of four did not have a reservation. We were seated immediately when we arrived around 12:30. I started with my usual Pom Ginger Margarita for $11. I enjoyed my Kobe meatloaf for $14.50.

Caroline served our table needs well. My total bill was $101 less gratuities. I would return here again given the chance or even another Firebirds location.

I enjoyed my stay here years ago, when I enjoyed my riverview room. I could not confirm a room here for my first night stay, therefore, I stayed at the nearby Marriott near the convention center. After my first night at the Marriott, I drove my rental car a short distance from the Marriott to the Hilton. The Hilton self-parking garage seems very confusing and complicated because they seem to have more than one self-parking garages. This is a very big hotel. I was lucky to park in the correct parking garage on the 4th floor so that I could access via the parking garage elevator to the hotel's check-in area located on their 2nd floor.

I returned here again for a conference located in the Hilton's convention area. I reserved two queen beds with riverview. The Marriott only offered two double beds. I prefer two larger queens over two double beds. I tried to check into the hotel using the Hilton app, but, it only offered me a single king bed city view room, which I did not reserve. This time I required two beds so I texted the hotel staff to complain about my reservation. They said two beds or riverview rooms were not guaranteed at the time of my reservation or available this day. So much for the value or importance of a Hilton hotel Gold member reservation. I was not happy. When I checked in early to the Hilton around 1pm I was lucky that Ayn was able to give me a room with two queen beds with riverview, namely 1622 for $223 inclusive of all taxes and fees, which I greatly appreciated. Ayn made my day and relieved a lot of my mental and physical stress, which had built up prior to my arrival to the Hilton. 

As most Hilton's offer this hotel also offered a digital key. I opted for the physical key cards. I was able to enter the room on my first try, but, when I returned with my luggage I found that none of our key cards would work. The hotel security was able to open my door, but, our key cards still did not work. Anyway the hotel had to change the key card lock on our door, which took several hours. This never happened to me before. 

As a Hilton Gold member I was entitled to two daily continental breakfasts in Le Croissant located on Level 1, a $10 food & beverage credit or 1,000 bonus points. I opted for the continental breakfast, which the hotel normally charged $21 per person. The hotel credited my hotel bill for my continental breakfasts. This Hilton did not have a lounge as did the Marriott. I actually prefer a lounge rather than a continental breakfast. Complimentary WiFi or premium Wifi is available for an additional $5 per day. I opted for the complimentary WiFi. 2 bottles of water per stay and late check are also provided, which I requested late check out at 2pm. The Hilton app would not allow me to checkout of the hotel, therefore, I resorted to texting the hotel staff again to check me out.

When I tried to vacate the self-parking garage my key card did not open the self-parking garage gate exit. My self parking was $29.95 per day. I called for assistance so that they opened the gate for me so that I could exit the self-parking garage. Now off to the MSY airport to return home.

When I received my hotel bill via email, I noticed that the hotel did not credit my last continental breakfast. Since the hotel bill was already charged to my AMEX the hotel had to issue a separate credit to my AMEX. As you can see, I used the Hilton's app for texting a lot during this stay due to many issues during my stay. Despite my many issues I would still recommend this Hilton especially if you get one of their riverview rooms for under $200. I really enjoyed my riverview room. Hotel room views are most important to me even though I spend so little time in my hotel rooms mostly to sleep.

Tony's is located in an office building near the Arch. I was here for a business dinner during a convention. I was the first to arrive for a 7:30pm reservation of 
10 people. The entrance and reception area was quite impressive. Fresh flowers were on the reception desk. Since I was the first to arrive I enjoyed a glass of chianti near the inactive bar. 

When some of the others arrived they also enjoyed a glass of wine near the inactive bar area. Eventually we were all seated at a great table and some great table service started. 

I truly enjoyed the carpaccio, with arugula and truffle oil for $12 and the spectacular lobster albanello entrée for $35. Several others enjoyed the lobster albanello as I did. It was a great 4-star dinner.

I ended my dinner with an espresso. This was my best restaurant in St. Louis.

CAVEAT: I WAS THERE ON OPENING NIGHT SO GIVE THEM WHATEVER SLACK YOU ARE INCLINED TO GIVE THEM FOR THAT.
Our visit was mostly a train wreck. Place has a nice decor but nothing too spectacular.  It is noisy, even by modern standards.
We started with shared apps of meatballs (very good), stromboli (good), and roasted peppers (poor).  
Specialty cocktails were flat and too sugary. 
Service was laughable.  We had to ask three staff for bread while others had it automatically brought to their tables.
My companion had the veal parmigiano.  It came out (no exaggeration) 8 minutes before my entree with no parmesan cheese anywhere on the plate. When this was pointed out to server, he offered to sprinkle parmesan cheese from the shaker on the table.  We, um, declined that offer.  Server then mumbled some sort of apology and an assurance that he would "look into it", but he never acknowledged the error again nor was any further action taken or offered to correct the error.  I had the Lobster Fra Diavlo.  Lobster was horrible.  Virtually inedible.  
Back to the service:
- water glasses sitting empty
- dirty plates left sitting on edge of table for exceedingly long time as empty handed staff walked by
- we were brought wrong entree (above) and a wrong dessert
- your "check" is brought to you on a tacky handheld credit card reader. Small screen display that the server scrolls thru for you quickly "in case you want to take a look".  Your card then scanned and you're presented with tip options, the first of which is 25% LOL! 
This all came to $30O for 2 people (5 drinks total).
Despite all this, I'll give it another shot and hope this was just opening night kinks.

I have had my fair share of authentic Mexican tacos, but never Tijuana style. After a friend from Tijuana recommended El Original, my husband and I decided to try it! We were told to try a mula, Tijuana's version of a quesadilla: 2 tortillas(your choice of flour or corn) with your choice of meat(I chose Al Pastor with pineapple), cheese and grilled onions. It was, frankly, delicious!! I also ordered 2 tacos, 1 chorizo and 1 carnitas, both greasy delicious. The chorizo had a dab of guacamole and green salsa. The carnitas just with green salsa and of course,  both with onions and cilantro. The whole order came with an extra plate of grilled onions and peppers to add to make your tacos even more fantástico!! My mouth is wishing it was back there right now just thinking about it!  

Things to note: 
1. They do not serve alcohol(my husband and I were a bit bummed about this as we prefer our tacos with a lip-smacking, ice cold Corona with lime and salt), but they do have a full variety of Jarritos flavors and Mexican Coke(made with real sugar! None of that corn syrup crap!) in a glass bottle. 
2. If you're looking for upscale, this is not a place for your fancy pants! I say the bright pink and lime bathroom coupled with the small paper plates snd plastic cafeteria trays on which the food is served gives the place extra character! It's clean and functional which works for me! 

If you want scrumptious, authentic Tijuana style tacos, definitely check this place out!

The world needs more Naked Farmers! After spending majority of our time in DTSP eating all the things, we were looking for something healthy for dinner. This was hands down, the best meal we had all weekend in DTSP and it was takeout!

Naked Farmer was only a block or so away from our hotel. I placed an order online. You can choose from one of their naked favorites or build your own. We ordered the following:
Build your own (with salmon) $15.40
Seasonal salmon $15.40
Local farmer $11.87
Kids mac $8

I couldn't believe how something as simple as salmon, brown rice, broccoli, and avocado could be so amazing! So flavorful and so filling! My husband's was a build your own with salmon, farro with winter vegetables, and a roasted turnips, quinoa, and arugula mix. He raved about his bowl, too! Their (un)dressings really bring all the flavors together. Our kids loved their bowls, too. The portions were generous, but we ate every single bit of it.

The food was packaged well and ready for my husband when he arrived. I wish I had gotten a chance to see the restaurant, but we will definitely be back next time we're in St. Pete!

I've lived so close to this place forever, I regret not going in sooner. I stopped for a big to go order and everything was great. Crunchy rolls and snow crab rolls had an actual taste, and they were delicious. A lot of times, those two rolls from other places can be pretty bland. The spicy tuna, which is my all time favorite, was absolutely fantastic. I loved the texture and flavor of the tuna, you could taste the quality. Sometimes I feel like the spicy is masking the lower quality fish...but not here! The hibachi rice was flavorful and tender, very good and no soy sauce needed! The stuffed jalepenos were better than the stuffed avocado in my opinion, but both were tasty. Both are stuffed with crab salad and tempura fried. 

I will definitely be going back. I spent $50 and don't regret a penny of it. The one waiter was very friendly and managed to juggle serving the few tables eating in, to go orders, and take out orders. Very impressed!

My hubby and I dined here last night with friends who had been twice before and enjoyed it. 

The atmosphere is cozy and romantic, service is personable and attentive and the food is good. That's right, good. There was nothing we had that really blew our minds or that I am still thinking about today but it was a nice experience. 

Well, maybe I am still thinking about the baked goat cheese special. 

Oh, and the bread service! It was generous and memorable in light, fluffy cheese puff like rolls. THOSE get five stars. 

In perusing the menu prior to dinner, I recall thinking the price point, while not cheap, was not overly expensive, either.....but then I saw the portions. 

Yeah, yeah, we Americans eat GIGANTIC portions but I'm not referring to the opposite extreme - and if the portions are small, I'm expecting something gourmet, something that says, "A little of me goes a long way" or "I might be small but you won't forget me anytime soon." That's not the case with what we had. 

In addition to the goat cheese, we also started with the mussels. These were good but there weren't  many of them. Split among four people and another appetizer, it didn't feel like enough. 

I ordered the lobster bisque which was flavorful and included bits of lobster (not always the case) but it was just as good as my last bowl of lobster bisque at another place I can no longer remember. Not a standout. 

My hubby did their special house made sausage (their French take on bangers and mash). The server warned him that it was spicy but my husband enjoyed it.  

A friend ordered the lamb chops and was very pleased; another went with the gnocchi and seemed to think it was "fine." The gnocchi was a very small portion (it *might* fill a saucer plate...it's like a side dish, not an entree, except they bring it with one of those large, wide brimmed "I'M AN ENTREE!" plates). While I realize it is a rich dish, it was so small that when she offered me and my husband a bite, I felt guilty for accepting. 

For my meal, I didn't want an entree and so I had the gem salad (too much tarragon) and escalloped potatoes (very good). 

We did enjoy two great bottles of wine, however, my husband noted that the prices were, $55, $75, and then it jumped to $180. Not a huge selection of comfortably affordable options. 

Would I go back? Maybe. And the four star review is a nod that it is above average but it's not the type of experience that stays with me and St. Louis has a lot of great dining that does.

For the 600th review I think that it's only fitting that I write a review for another milestone celebration.. A dinner to remember.  

It was a rainy outing in Santa Barbara. I had some dressy clothes on that wasn't a comic book or threadless shirt, so perhaps that in itself should tell you that this place was special. 

Hidden behind a green wall of plants is Bouchon, upon walking into the establishment it was clear that this was going to be an intimate dinner. Especially with it being a Sunday night and the place wasn't too busy. Which worked in our favor as it was nice and quiet which lead to some great ambiance. 

Looking at the menu and the specials a lot of items just struck out. Namly the Foie Gras. Ah, my hidden love.. you that was a forced fed animal to plump yourself up to levels of deliciousness that should be criminal.. and sadly will be outlawed in California in 2011/2012, I will miss you, but on that night, you were my friend. 

Started the meal off with the F.L.T. Which, while I'm not a big fan of B.L.T's as I see bacon as an opening band and not a headliner, I was very much thrilled to see Foie Gras in its place on this F.L.T. It was amazingly good. Highly recommended. 

That was along a Lobster Gratin. Which was pretty good but it was gone a bit too quickly. Oh well, the taste will live on. 

We got a half glass of wine to go along with savory flavors that was recommended by the waiter and it was beyond sweet and tasty. Really was well paired to go with the meal.  

On to the main course. I got to taste the Pork Chop plate which was insanely good. A pretty big portion size, which packed on the flavor on all fronts. 

I choose to go with the Duck breast with maple bourbon sauce. I can't say I regret much of it. It wasn't like the general duck I get at Sam Woo, that's for certain. The sauce was amazingly delicious. The darker meat wasn't my favorite but the dark meat didn't take up much more than a couple of pieces on the bone. The rest of it was tender and very tasty. 

Since we were in the area of the Santa Ynez wine country and that's one region that, while I live within a two-three hour drive from, I don't venture out there all that much. So I put the trust in the waiters hands in recommending the wine pairings and I have to say they were great hands to put that trust in. 

The service was amazing. From the recommendations in wines to the general service over all, they were in top form and I loved the treatment given. Even went out of their way to ask if we were celebrating an occasion when calling in to place reservations and doing some extra measures because of it. They were on their game on all fronts. 

From the food to the setting, it's an amazing time eating here.

I live near this restaurant and was very excited to have a new place to try --and, hopefully frequent.  But, I was left feeling a bit disappointed after having visited it. 

The food is ok.  Nothing special. Prices are high, portions are small.  It seems the menu has no real focus or anything really interesting going for it. 

You wouldn't know you were in a Mexican restaurant by sitting in this place.  I understand minimalistic and understated decors, but c'mon folks--how about a little decoration of some sort!  Very boring space, reminds me of the last two businesses that were here and failed.  The current owners spent so long and what seems like a lot of money redoing this place to have it look 90% the same as it did before.  Yes, the ceiling of repurposed Amish beams is nice, but it looks like Restoration Hardware, not a Mexican restaurant.

The story of El Poquito is very interesting, but I had to read about it online and through my own research!  How about including some fun facts on the menu about it, and perhaps some interesting tidbits of info on the food and its ingredients, history, origin in Mexican cuisine, the restaurant's and the chef's personal twist on its preparation, etc?

It's just your usual Mexican fare here: tacos, fajitas, tortilla soup--, without any real twist or changes--for high prices.  I can get better and cheaper Mexican in almost any restaurant in the area.  You need to try something new, folks!  It may be the location and the building, too. It seems to have bad feng shui, no business lasts long here, and I, unfortunately, predict the same fate for this new business.

Oh, and the margaritas are tiny and cost $9. They were good, but in two gulps mine was gone.  And, I am always a little leery of Mexican restaurants that don't plunk down a bowl of tortilla chips and salsa as soon as I sit down (this is done in 99% of Mexican restaurants in Mexico).   With the price of those margaritas, you could afford a few tortilla chips to munch on while scanning this very limited and unimaginative menu.  

Sorry.  I really wanted this place to be good.  I really did.  I don't think I will be returning.

As a woman who prides herself on eating healthy, I make a point to include something from each of the basic food groups at all meals.  In my order of preference, these food groups are:  wine, pizza, chocolate, meat and beer ;-)  It had been far too long since I had polled down to #3 on my list, so I took it as a sign when we found ourselves walking past Chocolate Maya one Saturday.  This place was actually recommended by a dear friend who knew about of my dedication to healthy eating.  That by itself would have been enough to get me to pay them a visit, but even without a personal recommendation their stellar Yelp reviews would have pushed me over the threshold for sure!

It took only a few moments and several whiffs of Maya's delightful chocolate for me to realize I was going to become a regular.  The selection of handmade, delicious chocolates was outstanding, and the service was exceptional.  All my questions were patiently and knowledgeable answered :-)

I ended up buying three boxes of four chocolates at a cost of $12.50 each.  That's actually quite a bargain for handcrafted chocolates that are as good as these.  My favorites thus far are the caramel, the chipotle, and the crispy almond chocolate.  All the chocolates I tried were nothing short of fabulous; I'm glad I found this wonderful place to attend to my list of healthy eats ;-)

Before leaving for our next wine tasting appointment, I got to try some of the dark chocolate almond bark.  It turned out to be absolutely delicious - I'm planning to come back and buy some as a gift for the friend who recommended this place.  Why didn't I buy some right then?  This way, good manners will provide me an excuse to return really soon!

As an unusually difficult year full of professional challenges was drawing to a close, I got word that there was an amazing opportunity on the horizon, so I set out to find an appropriate venue for a very special dinner.  Bouchon turned out to be the perfect place for a celebration!

The atmosphere was lovely and the service was impeccable.  The staff was wonderfully attentive without being in any way overly obtrusive :-)

Over and above the service and the ambiance, the food was the unquestionable star of the evening.   Our soup was simply Devine, the Duck was sheer poetry, and the wine our server recommended was the perfect pairing for an outstanding meal.

The prices are decidedly on the high side, which is what you'd expect for a high-end white table cloth venue, but the quality of the dining experience you'll get here makes it more than worth the freight :-)

Highly recommended!!

Another long line to brave, but they've got a strong Nashville reputation for excellent cheap eats. The quinoa and sweet potato tacos were great. Also loved the grilled corn and fried plantains. The line looks intimidating but moves relatively quick, a good place to grab a snack while waiting for sit down service across the street at The Pharmacy or a quick and tasty meal.

So, being a recent member of the gluten-free Club, this was the first place I tried that actually served normal food. Boy was I glad I gave it a shot.

First of all, the appetizers were awesome. I ordered the gluten-free fried pickle chips and dipping sauce. They were amazing. I wanted to drink, so I got a Tito's Bloody Mary. Also gluten-free. Phenomenal. For dinner I got a jalapeno cheeseburger with fries. The bun was a tad bit Bland, but I've noticed a lot of gluten-free buns are. The fries were stupendous and the burger was just right.

Normally a meal like this would destroy my stomach and give me all kinds of gluten-ey (is that a word yet, haha) problems. Aside from being full, as one would expect to be after a meal this large, my heartburn and my normal gastric issues were completely absent. Pricing was very fair; staff was phenomenally attentive and wonderful. Being a longtime yelper, I don't know how I hadn't found this place sooner.

Keep it up, I'll be coming back more, especially since I'm the perfect candidate for your menu.

We showed up to Walt'z at 5:00 sharp, their opening time, and there was about 10 other people in front of us waiting to experience what would soon become a nightmare. We waited for what felt like an eternity to actually step foot inside the small, congested shak, and as we sat down and asked the hostess/bartender/owner/manager Sue (MUCH more on her later) to pull up a chair since we had a party of five, she flashed us a snobby look and reluctantly brought the chair. As my 10-year old daughter moved her chair over to sit near me, the woman shot her a patronizing glare and scolded her, stating that we were not allowed to move chairs around then actually MOVED HER CHAIR WITH HER SITTING IN IT!!!!!!!!!!! (what kind of person\business woman would do that??????) Due to a lack of AC, my husband requested that he position the fan so that he could get a breeze towards him, but she once again scolded him for doing so. And this was only the beginning of the madness. So our drinks come out and my daughter, who ordered a Coke, complains that it tastes very flat, and she passed it around the table and we all agreed that there was something wrong with her Coke. So we ask our waitress, who told us that we weren't wrong; the Coke they serve comes from a can. We understood, despite being a family that does prefer being served fountain soda, So we asked if we could get it taken off our check, once again, no. Our appetizers (asparagus soup and crawfish patties) come out and although we couldn't complain one bit about the patties, the soup was very bland. A family of tourists from Wisconsin got the table next to us, and brought in a stroller for the 2-year-old son. Immediately after, Sue scolded this family for bringing in their stroller due to the shak's congested space. 30 minutes or so after putting the stroller in their car, the baby started quietly crying then quickly stopped. Sue came over to the table and started screaming at the baby and his family for "scaring away four tables". Absurd. At this point, the family was fed up and were about ready to get up and leave, but thought to give them a second chance. Ten minutes later, the baby started to fall asleep on his grandmother's lap. When they asked Sue if they had any highchairs, she resentfully responded with "This is a fish shak, not a place for a baby to take naps." OUTRAGEOUS!!! The grandpa paid the bill and they all left without saying another word. Feeling empathy for them and being  absolutely fed up with this woman and her attitude towards everything, we also left before being served our entrees, of course after paying for our drinks and apps. I will NEVER be back here due to the lack of respect and dignity shown towards my family as well as those around us. This is one of many negative reviews on this site about this woman and her restaurant, so trust me and everyone else who has blasted this place when we advise you not to waste your time and money by dining here.

Where do I begin? First this dinner was for my husband's birthday. The hostess said she would make a note of this when I mad my reservation. Nobody from the hostess to the server said anything to my husband. Our reservation was for 7:45. We were not seated until 8:15. Unacceptable...,if  you cannot honor reservation times then don't make them or take them from customers. There was a rude man who kept telling us people wouldn't leave. Not our problem, Don't book reservations so tight. Place was very noisy.  After waiting 30 minutes past our reservation, the hostess led us to a crappy little table staring at the fire alarm on the wall which was at eye level. It looked like they stuck a table somewhere to make extra money. The service was very mediocre. Our server was nice enough but seemed to be going through the motions. Had to ask for a wine list that was not brought with the menu. Had to ask what the salts were as well, we were not told this until we asked. We sat with an empty bread bowl at our table for 15 minutes. No offers to refill it. Was shocked to see server assistants on the floor in jeans... for an upscale restaurant that was pretty unprofessional looking. The food? I love oysters. I saw the oyster menu. The server did not offer to explain it but did tell me they were already out of a lot so I should order the Chef's selection. These were also mediocre, and nothing special. How could a restaurant specializing in oysters be almost of  them on a Friday night?????? The fish we had was pretty good. Enjoyed my salmon, and my husband liked his fish. Overall, this place is nothing special. The hostess and wait staff should be trained at Capital Grille or Ocean Prime. Those places offer crisp service, excellent food, and not this "I can't make them leave" nonsense. Save your money and go to Ocean Prime in Tama for seafood...not impressed at all, and really wanted to like it here. .

Unlimited delicious Sushi for the win! And for a good price!

QUALITY MUCH BETTER THAN EXPECTED
I like my sushi relatively pure so I was excited that amidst the choices of mutated, fried Sushi Rolls covered in oceans of Sauce, there were also a good number of Sashimi. You're only allowed up to eight pieces of each... but PFFFFTT that was enough. We tried each type and the cuts were never skimpy. The Salmon was my favorite--a thick cut, great color, and delicate but good flavor on top of a chunk of Rice. The Beautiful Girl Roll was somewhat beautiful but definitely not my style with its squirts of Spicy Mayo and Fried. Other Rolls like the Top of The World were a little simpler but with strong flavor. The Rolls were made well and normally held a good balance of flavors albeit a bit sauce crazy.

PRESENTATION OVERALL
Since there's a cost for each uneaten piece, we ordered slowly and not all at once. This allowed us to receive several very well decorated plates. Saki uses big plates and in the space our food didn't cover, they used sauces to draw dragons, trees, etc in the empty area. Awesome little touch!

The service provided by our waitress was also very friendly and she arrived at the perfect times--always to take our next order as soon as only a few pieces were left on the plate. The appearance of the restaurant is also very nice. Mildly modern with soft blue lights near the bar and wood accents. This is a great place to bring friends and groups without this place being too kitschy or selling out.

On Saturday, October 6, 2012 we attempted to have dinner at Agostino's.  This was my third visit.  The first visit I chose to sit in the bar and had hoped to have appetizers.  They had just opened and told me that no food was served in the bar.  I enjoyed a glass of wine and went to one of the other non chain Italian restaurants in the area.
The second time we visited it was ok, yet as it was still fairly new we decided to wait a bit and return for a true evaluation.

On Saturday night we entered at 6: 30 to 6:45 pm.  We were looking forward to a great evening as we knew that they had added music on the weekends.  Upon arrival we asked the ladies at the hostess desk if we could have drinks and an appetizer in the bar before going to the dining room.  The bar was about 50% full.  
The hostess stated that the bartender told them not to seat anyone else in the bar as she was "slammed".  We hesitated at that response but asked if we could get a table in the dining room.  Again, we could clearly see open tables.  We were then told that they could not seat anyone there either.  What a shock!  We were dressed appropriately, 50 something couple.  After watching them remodel, place a very costly sign on the interstate, adding music you would think they would not turn anyone away when there are open seats. 

We then left and went down to exit 16 and enjoyed dinner at a fairly new Italian restaurant.  The wait was 30 minutes but we were welcomed at the bar.  With appetizers, drinks and dessert our tab was significant as it would have been at Agostino's-----if they had only welcomed us!

The pizza here is tasty and calling her order and was a breeze. They have locations all over Santa Barbara, ideal for kids and families. Prices are fair and the food was ready quickly. Generous in size and toppings, for now it is to go only.

I was really hoping to enjoy the coffee here. My iced mocha, for tonight asked light ice for, was all ice! When I inquired about this she dumped most of it and just filled it up with milk which left me with a chocolate milk instead of a mocha. I cannot taste bit of coffee. Their hot coffee tasted better and burnt, are usually enjoy groceries because of the fresh flavor, none of that to be found here. Service was also very slow, Prices are way too high for the fact that I wanted to just throwing it away. Such a shame, not worth returning.

This is definitely one of my favorite restaurants for date night or special occasion! Service is always impeccable, as does the food. I really love their salmon, as well as their salads and sides. My husband really enjoys their steak. They have a wonderful drink menu and are always very well run. Beautiful ambience, be sure to make a reservation. Highly recommended!

Such a cute little coffee shop on the way to Santa Barbara, I'm so glad we stopped here! Service was wonderful, they have a nice variety on their menu as well as a little gift shop in the store. Very cute seating area outback and easy parking right out front. Prices are fair, the quality and flavor of their coffee was fantastic. Worth trying if you're in the area.

Al's has long been one of my favorite BBQ spots in Tampa Bay. They keep it simple and delicious. I stopped in Saturday for a lunch plate with their pulled pork and mac + cheese, served with a drink for just $8. 

You really can't beat the price when some bbq places in town are charging upwards of $15 for a plate.

Noticeable is the way the meat is so tender and flavorful. Their sauce is also excellent and just what you would expect. I can't eat BBQ all the time, but when I do Al's is always on my mind in Tampa.

I recommend Al's if you're hungry for BBQ and near Ybor City.

I love everything about Anise Gastrobar. The decor is very unique and definitely not something typical of Tampa. I love the mural at the bar - the owner used real pictures for it and it just gives the place an extra touch of personality. The lighting, tall windows exposing Downtown Tampa, paintings, I could go on and on, but it is just an experience you will have to go have for yourself. They have outdoor seating, but I definitely would not a miss a chance to sit inside this restaurant.

There was a DJ playing some music when I came in - but not your usual DJ. The music certainly makes me think lounge, but with a hip twist, like I am watching a 90s Pringles "Jump Around" commercial by House of Pain - but better. The music isn't too loud so you can definitely still have a conversation with your friends/date. 

Speaking of that - I think Anise Gastrobar is a perfect location for a birthday party or get-together with friends before hitting the clubs or nightlife on Kennedy or SoHo. There is plenty of seating space inside and it doesn't feel crowded thanks the great layout design by the owner.

The waitress we had was excellent. She was very charming and seemed very in control of what she was doing. She consistently checked on us and brought us food and drinks as we ordered to the best of her ability and overall I was just impressed that a new business could have great servers already. The owner of Anise Gastrobar is the former owner of Bamboozle Cafe in Downtown Tampa and also owns the Stinky Bunz food truck, also working in a number of other restaurants and food businesses in town - so she is certainly experienced in owning restaurants and working in them.

I appreciated that even the soft-opening features quality service and food.

Now on to the food. It was absolutely delicious and I was just in love with how each dish has such great complexity. The menu names and descriptions just are not enough to give you a clue into how great each dish is. 

The coconut curried wings were awesome. Just the right hint of sweetness from the coconut, followed by what smells like Indian curry, but it brings just an entirely different spice into your mouth. It isn't hot by any means, but just packed with flavor! I would highly recommend this dish - honestly one of the best wings I have ever had.

I actually started with a papaya salad though and this was just a completely interesting dish. Certainly spicy, but not overwhelmingly so. The flavors were unbecoming of a papaya dish and I could taste hints of Vietnamese flavors in the dish, but wasn't exactly sure what it was. The salad actually seemed a little small (most things seem meant to be shared) - but I couldn't finish it. 

The portions are about the same as Ciro's Speakeasy and Supper Club. Things are meant to be shared and it's more of an addition to your cocktails then an entree setup. I'm not sure how the menu will be expanded in the finalized version. Speaking of Ciro's, Ciro's was actually consulted for the creation of the cocktail menu at Anise Gastrobar! Ciro's easily makes the best cocktails in Tampa Bay, therefore I'm sure Anise can also now hold it's own.

I wasn't actually drinking any cocktails during my visit because I was still in my work clothes and I wasn't in the mood for a drink. However, they made me the best fresh-squeezed lemonade I have ever had a restaurant. It was great because I was craving lemonade all day, but the stand at the event across the street seemed questionable so I held out for lemonade all day, little did I know I would be having one a few hours later at Anise Gastrobar.

Go to Anise Gastrobar! Try it, indulge, experience. You won't be sorry you did.

This new ramen shop is showing lots of promise and is a welcome addition to our city. I tried the Shoyu Ramen on my last visit and it was refreshing and affordable at $10 for a big gourmet ramen bowl. The restaurant gives you sporks that help chopstick impaired diners like myself. 

The ingredients tasted great and the broth goes perfectly with the noodles although the broth by itself is a little salty due to the soy-base, just for your information. My friends udon noodles looked tempting and I'm thinking about getting a shrimp tempura udon next time.

The dining room could use some work as far as seat arrangements/efficiency and the turnaround time for ramen sent out can be improved, but for a new business that is paving the way for ramen in Tampa - I can be patient.

The appetizers are affordable at under $5 as is the sake with many prices at around $6. Complimentary barley tea is available which is a very Asian kind of drink, but anyone from Asia will appreciate the added item. The green tea mochi ice cream dessert was $2 and was delicious.

Parking is limited so try to carpool. I'm hoping the hours will be extended as business picks up as well. Ramen for lunch would be amazing. 

I will definitely be back soon!

If you're going to sell an avocado toast for $9 it definitely should not be using fully ripened and bad avocados. I complained about this to the staff which masked it with spinach on top, but they are refusing a refund. This is not good business. I like Caffeine and want to support local, but don't sell rotten avocado toast guys.

I was excited for this place when I first heard it was opening. It's pretty popular over in Orlando and it seems like there is a good amount of new Puerto Rican places opening lately.

Unfortunately the food was just okay and quite expensive. Over $5 for some arroz con gandules. The quality of the chimichurri steak and sides was good, but we could've easily went to another place in town for less and had way more food. 

That being said, the atmosphere inside was really nice and the waitresses were great. They have some cocktails there and there was a ton of people celebrating birthdays there so it has promise. 

I'd recommend it but after recently going to Rice & Beans in Wesley Chapel, I think Pal Campo should re-evaluate their prices and portions.

Chipotle is nowhere near real Mexican food - and the taste isn't much better than Moe's, Tijuana Flats, Qdoba, or other fast food Mexican joints. The price isn't cheap either at $9+ for a combo. What really turned me off was the service I experienced today while making my order. An employee rolled her eyes at me as I told her what I wanted in my burrito and had the nerve to tell me "next time order things from left to right" while rolling her eyes. Then when I took my order to the register - the cashier gave me a dirty look as well. The manager should watch who he hires to represent his franchise of this business. Eh, I don't think I'll be back.

Flamestone serves some excellent food that gives big Tampa names like Bern's a run for their money and is much more affordable as well. My first encounter with Flamestone was at a cookoff between SideBern's and Flamestone during a Wal-Mart event. Participants tried samples of steak cooked by both restaurant chefs and voted based on color which was the better steak. Flamestone received at least 90% of the votes and I, myself, was surprised how great the steak tasted. The chef made it to the finals in New York.

My next visit to Flamestone was for a food event that served some excellent saucy and Chile Olive Oil creations. I was impressed by the chefs excellent creations and how some dishes were truly products of food ingenuity that you by chance only witness a few times a year if you are lucky.
