This meal came to me during a difficult time personally and I have to say that for the couple of hours I was at Flamestone, I truly found a great peace of mind while eating their food.

What's there not to love about a restaurant that can take your mind off the world with excellent food?

I had the opportunity to visit the Locale Market earlier today for a sneak-peek and wander around their 20,000 square-foot facility and was super impressed with what I saw. A focus on local farmer's and vendors from around the State of Florida. 10 kitchens with all kinds of fresh food and some mighty tasty gelato and sweets. A craft beer bar on floor 2 with a wine cellar close-by. If you want to describe a foodie destination, the Locale Market is just that. 

It's somewhere to go on a Saturday morning or Sunday afternoon with a family member or date and explore the intricate local vendors that have only been loosely connected in St. Petersburg until this market appeared. The tasting room on the second floor is something I really forward to dining in soon as I return for some more of this local action.

Prices are fair for the local connections and won't venture above what you'll find at Whole Foods Market or other similar concepts. The 10 kitchens pretty much ensures there will be plenty of value in returning often to the Locale Market to try different things or even visiting the place in a large group to taste the various things the place has to offer.

The Locale Market opens to the general public on Dec. 17th, 2014 at 3PM and will be open daily. The two chefs who joined forces for this project have been very successful in the restaurant industry and I truly wish them the best in helping transform Tampa Bay's food scene. They have been in hundreds of television shows and Chef Michael Mina manages 18 restaurants which is a talent I am extremely impressed to find has found its way into our lovely bay area.

Another great addition to Downtown St. Petersburg's growing food scene and to Tampa Bay itself.

I've heard a ton about this place on social media and finally decided to try it this week. I ordered a Cuban Sandwich (El Tampeno) and a flan to-go. I was glad they were able to bring it curbside and the staff member was wearing a a mask.

The Cuban Sandwich ($10) beat my expectations. The bread was perfectly toasted and flavorful. The ingredients inside were all nicely matched so that each bite was an experience. It was big enough to share with my Mom, so consider splitting it and ordering some sides if you want to try more things on the menu. The thing that really sold me on this was the pork or lechon, which was perfect - soft and juicy.

The flan was great too - we had the Cafe con Leche flan ($4) and the Guava flan ($4). The Cafe con Leche was delicious, but I had been eyeing the guava. The guava was more like a pastelito and less like a guava puree, which I would have also enjoyed. Overall - it was delicious and tasty flan, but I want to try more flavors to find my favorite.

Definitely recommend Flan Factory, I wish I would've tried it sooner - but I am happy I finally did! Go and try them out, you won't be sorry. They have delivery and also through their website you can order takeout. 

Looking forward to one day being able to dine-in!

Sake House was on the ABC Action News Dirty Dining List for having over 300 roaches last year (both dead and alive) in the restaurant. It wasn't their first offense either and the state closed the restaurant for a day or two because of the critical violations. Like most places, after the incident they fired someone and then claimed they had cleaned up the mess. I admit that these things might happen, but repeat offenses and 300!? I am just too grossed out by the violations to ever step foot back into Sake House though. No specials (no matter how cheap) are worth your health you know? 

Tokyo Sushi and Ichiban aren't far and there are other sushi restaurants within a few miles as well.

Lee House Chinese Restaurant has re-opened on Brandon Boulevard after closing off Bloomingdale Avenue in March. I first read about Lee House online and was intrigued at the positive reception. The first thing we noticed upon pulling up to the restaurant was that it smelled great outside the restaurant (a good sign). Once we entered we were seated immediately and given menus and water. The waitress was an older woman who knew the menu well. After much deliberation (the menu is a few pages), we decided to order the Lee House Special (similar to Yummy House's 3 for 20 deal). We selected Salt & Pepper Calamari, Beef with Broccoli, and Young Chow Fried Rice which came to $21.95 total. Quite a deal when you dine with some friends.

Plenty of warm food came out quickly. The Salt & Pepper Calamari was delicious. My favorite calamari dish now belongs to Roy's, but this calamari was still quite delectable and was a good stand-in for the calamari at Yummy House (my favorite until recently). The calamari was a little chewy instead of crunchy, but had lots of flavor. I was a little concerned that it had jalapenos on it (I can't take spicy food), but the jalapenos brought the calamari a great taste. We finished this plate down to the last bite.

The Beef with Broccoli was also fantastic. The sauce was made just right and the beef was tender. I am not much of a vegetable consumer, but my friend loved the veggies on the plate. The Young Chow Fried Rice was a nice complement and wasn't dry. I am not much of a rice eater, therefore anytime I actually enjoy eating rice, I know I am having a good meal.

The food was enough to fill three guys and I was impressed with Lee House. There are very few good Chinese restaurants in Brandon and dining at Lee House was enjoyable. I really want to try their Dim Sum in the future. From the Dim Sum menu the Deep Fried Taro, Custard Cream Buns, and Juicy Pork Bun caught my eye. Glad this place was able to find a new home in Brandon. I will be back!

The Filipiniana Philippine Café just had their soft opening yesterday and I couldn't have been more excited. It's great to see Filipino businesses opening around town like the PAO Truck, it makes the wait for PhilFest easier to bare and its fun having new exotic things to try. 

The cafe sells bubble tea (boba), Halo-Halo (Filipino shaved ice drinks), Filipino coffee, Filipino baked goods, smoothies, and more. Things on the menu are fairly prices and the cafe itself has a modern feel to it. 

I enjoyed a Halo-Halo Supreme yesterday ($5) and it was excellent. All the ingredients tasted fresh and my Filipino friends were definitely enjoying it as well (and coaching me on tips for mixing everything together for the best flavor). The Halo-Halo has flan in it which is awesome and shows the roots of Filipino cuisine in Spain. 

We also tried the Ensaymada Ube Bread (~$3) which was excellent. It is a baked dessert that is stuffed with Ube (purple yam) which is perfectly sweetened. The bread itself was soft and enjoyable and could also pair well with some coffee. 

The location is next to the original Saigon Deli on Waters and Dale Mabry behind the La Quinta hotel. It's hidden from the road so you should look for the Saigon Deli sign. 

I'm excited for all these new businesses in Tampa and look forward to spending lots of time hanging out and enjoy Filipino sweets at the Filipiniana Philippine Café.

Kaiko Sushi and Ocean Blue Sushi merged together earlier this year. The son of Kaiko Sushi pioneered the new restaurant and each time I have visited has been a good experience. My friends normally come in large packs to late-night spots (think maybe 20 or more people) and Ocean Blue Sushi handles the crowd pretty well. All the bartenders are friendly and bring your drinks quick. The service is good and if the servers make any mistakes, they are quick to fix it. 

There aren't many late-night sushi spots in Clearwater (or Tampa Bay in general), but Ocean Blue Sushi offers this to customers, with occasional DJs and karaoke nights making it a cool place to be at night. They offer a 1/2 off sushi and drinks menu after 10PM that has quite a few sushi rolls for $3/$4. They also have 1/2 draft beer, wells, house wine. In addition to shot specials, such $2 kamikaze shot, lemon drops and $3 sake bombs (delicious) and upside down cupcake shots.

The sushi quality was pretty good, they don't serve you spoiled fish drenched in sauce like some other late-night sushi restaurants do. I really liked their appetizers (also half-off) with the crab rangoons being my favorite.

The atmosphere inside is inviting with booths and tables on one side of the restaurant and large tables for groups and a dance floor/DJ booth on the other side. There is also patio seating as well. During big events the place occasionally gets slammed with lots of customers, but overall I think the experience they are offering deserves a shout-out.

It's not too far from The Venue so not a bad place to hang out before heading to the club. Bring on more late-night sushi spots around Tampa Bay!

M. Bird has so much potential, but falls short. Let's start with the positives - the bartenders are seasoned and know what they're doing. The sunset views here are top-notch - there is not enough happening on Tampa's waterfront (yet!) besides Remedy Tampa and Sparkman. 

Now for the downsides. Expensive! I just had a Mai Tai in San Francisco and it was $11 at one of the top 40 bars in America where minimum wage is $15 and rent is 10x whatever it is in Florida. Mai Tais are $14 at M. Bird and in general the drink menu is very expensive as is the food. You're paying Miami/New York prices but not getting that experience.

I'm not opposed to spending money if I feel like the vibe justifies the spending. Unfortunately I think M. Bird is not quite there - it would make more sense if it was a Miami-style bar with DJs and a party-like atmosphere - but it's lounge-like atmosphere doesn't really justify these price-points.

The view isn't even complete, there's still dirt field views and an eyesore like Blake High School obscuring the view. This is definitely not an issue at night when you can't see those things so well.

I don't even want to mess around with the service staff here, but the bartenders are equipped thankfully.

Then there's the pretentiousness of this place. The line to get in. The ID checkpoint. You'd think you were going to a nightclub or something, but it's not that. It's very SoHo and not in a good way. Bull Gastrobar has a rooftop bar that overlooks Downtown Tampa at night and they don't have a line or ID checks even though they're actually much smaller. Same goes for Mole y Abuela.

Maybe Tampa people like feeling self-important...I don't know. I just know it's laughable that people will wait in line 30 minutes to an hour when there are bars downstairs at Armature Works and across at Ulele and on the Riverwalk...pretty much all around here.

I have driven past this restaurant about a thousand times on my way to USF from my house. A curious Victorian-looking building that I usually blink and pass by. I finally got the name down and looked it up on Urbanspoon. It had pretty good reviews there...however, no Yelp page. I decided to check them out on New Years Eve night for dinner. 

Walking into the restaurant you feel like maybe you should be entering a house or store in San Francisco. The outside patio area has an area to dine outside, perfect for lunch during the day. Inside, the restaurant is nicely decorated. There is the usual gold decorations in the front. Turning right is a large dining room with a stage for live jazz players. 

Bangkok Jazz has live jazz music Thursday-Saturday nights from 6:30pm onward. It's the first time I ever hear of the two mixing, but it sounded like a great idea and worked well. Something different then those oriental jingles (which can get annoying) that almost all Thai restaurants seem to play.

The walls in the main dining room are red and lighting is dim...I couldn't help thinking that this place would be perfect to bring a date while dining. Impressionistic paintings were on the walls near the bathroom and gave a nice touch to the restaurants decor. The ceiling was covered in patterned tiles.

I was quickly seated and the waiter was taking my order within a minute or two. I decided to have my usual Thai Tea ($2.95), Thai Coconut Soup ($2.95), and Chicken Pad Thai ($9.95). Thai Tea took only a few seconds to come out. The Thai Tea was good...but not the best I have had. It could have used some more creamer, they filled it to the top of the glass and it actually lasted me my entire meal for once.

The Thai Coconut Soup was savory, but also not the best I have had in terms of flavor of the broth. I enjoyed the ingredients inside which really brought it some zest with the exception of the mushrooms they used...which I really didn't care for. It was pretty big bowl for the price so quite a good deal.

The Chicken Pad Thai came out quickly. Probably not even 10 minutes after ordering. The Pad Thai looked much darker than the Pad Thai I have had at any other Thai place in Tampa. There was plenty of sauce and flavor to it and it was large. The chicken was great, probably some of the best I had in a Pad Thai. They used lots of vegetables, plenty of peppers, bean sprouts, and scallions.

The waiter was satisfactory, but he had a slight language barrier. The musicians were just testing their sound when I got there, so I'll have to come back again to checkout their music scene. 

Overall, Bangkok Jazz was a good experience. I want to return for lunch and try sitting outside, lunch prices here are pretty cheap ($5.95). I'd recommend Yelpers to give it a shot.

Yo! Sushi is a totally new concept for Tampa. It's conveyor-belt sushi also known as kaiten-sushi or kaiten-zushi or sushi-go-round in Japan. You sit at a booth and grab the sushi you want and pay at the end.

My first experience with this kind of sushi was in San Francisco when I first tried sushi as a 5-year old at Isobune Sushi in Japantown and I have longed for a conveyor-belt style sushi place to come to Tampa since I moved here in 1999. Yo! Sushi is finally making that a reality.

The style of Yo! Sushi is modern and different from Isobune. The focus is on fast, fresh, and convenient and the setup of the place follows this focus. When you walk-up to the restaurant it's open and easy to get a seat at. Call-buttons are placed at each table to make it easy to get service and close your check.

Sushi is constantly being rolled and made by the sushi chefs at the restaurant and the open-kitchen let's you watch the chefs in action. I have faith a high-traffic area like the International Plaza will help ensure the freshness of the fish at Yo! Sushi. 

Plates range from $3-$6 and contain a variety of cooked and raw sushi, cooked Japanese food, and dessert. There's a little bit of something for everyone depending on your tastes. 

One of my favorite things I have tried so far is the Chicken Katsu Curry which comes a small plate with rice below and about 5 cuts of katsu for $5. I often want to order katsu at restaurants, but find it hard to justify spending $15 on dinner for one - especially when I also want sushi with my food and end up just ditching the katsu. This meets me halfway.

As far as the sushi is concerned - it tastes fresh and is certainly above what you would find at a buffet or something like Koizi/Saki Endless Sushi. It's not quite the highest quality of sushi which is understandable considering the price and focus, but still satisfactory to me for the taste. Most of the sushi leans towards salmon, tuna, and imitation crab/crab special or California Roll-creations. 

I also liked the Popcorn Shrimp (tastes more like Bang Bang Shrimp), Takoyaki (hard to find a decent one in Tampa for sure!), and the Kimchi Salmon Steamed Bun (bun was just right and salmon pretty good quality!). There are plenty of things to try though so repeat visits will need to be made!

For me, Yo! Sushi is great for a quick and tasty meal when I'm in a rush and don't necessarily want to spend as much time/money at a regular Japanese sushi restaurant. I can see how someone who wants a really high-end Japanese experience may not approve, but then one should also consider price and time into factors of that justification.

The service is friendly/approachable and the managers clearly really love working for Yo! Sushi which is something plenty of restaurants in Tampa Bay seem to lack and may come from them being an international company.

Definitely check it out even if it's just to try something new for fun with some friends or family. I know I'll be back often!

Given that the line was half way down the street during a downpour, I was intrigued, but also resigned to the fact that I'd be eating elsewhere. I asked a guy at the end of the line if he had any idea how long the wait might be to which he replied that he did not, but guaranteed it'd be worth whatever it was. He then went as far to say that if I didn't agree that it was worth it, to find him and he'd buy my meal. I don't know if he owned stock in this joint or what, but how could I walk away after that. Despite the long line, it moved fairly quickly; maybe a half hour wait from the edge of the building. 

The masses have already made it clear that Hattie B's is doing something special and I fully concur. Anyone can add heat to chicken, but their cooking process is clearly the differentiator.  The outer coating is fried to a perfect crisp while the inside remains remarkably tender. I went with the mild and found it to have just the right amount of bite. I'd probably try one level up from mild, but wouldn't dream of anything more than that. It's been rumored that the Shut the Cluck Up has put good Cajuns on the ground. As for sides, I had fries, a crinkle cut variety, that was perfectly fried and delicious. I also had the Mac and cheese which to me was decent, but not special. 

It's been said many times, many ways, but there is definitely a wow factor to Hattie's chicken. I'm glad for the experience and especially for having it in Nashville, the birthplace of hot chicken. Order ahead to skip the line. You can still eat inside even if you ordered ahead.

My dearest Anna - It is with immense pleasure that I have the opportunity to write to you once again. As you know, one score and fifteen years hath passed since we were tasked with locating and mapping out the Nation's finest burger establishments. The journey has been long and arduous to say the least. Our current expedition started late last spring out west in California Territory and took us through the Republic of Texas by mid summer before finally arriving here in Confederate Territory last fall. There was no shortage of spectacular and noteworthy finds along the trail. It was however here, in the outpost of Nashville (Cumberland River Valley), that our eyes were awakened to a truly special establishment by name of Jack Brown's. It is our understanding that there is more than one location of Jack Brown's out here in this part of the country, but you'd never know by the atmosphere, hospitality and service we found here at this location. 

I cannot recall ever, a tougher time making a decision than here at Jack Brown's. Never have I seen a burger list where every one sounded so desirable. With much deliberation I went with the Cobra Kai. I suspected these Southerners were just confused as I've never seen cream cheese on a burger prior. Confused and lucky perhaps; I do not know, but the cream cheese is truly a magnificent touch. The cream cheese combined with jalapeños (a pepper brought up from Mexican Territory) and jalapeño jelly made for a burger that will not be soon forgotten. I cannot even begin to explain the abundance of flavor I witnessed. The beef, a USDA Prime 100% Wagyu sourced from Snake River Farms in Fort Boise (Oregon Territory), was absolutely remarkable. The quality of the beef makes an undeniable difference. From my seat, belied up to the bar, I watched as cookie masterfully prepared the beef on a flattop (undoubtedly smuggled down from the North). Each side of the burger was seared and specially seasoned before going under the steaming dish for final preparation. The bun was perfectly toasted while the toppings were all well appointed. The sight of this burger alone reassured my belief in this expedition. Dare I say that the flavors were mighty as the Mississippi. As with all of the burgers here, things got messy in a hurry, but no one seamed to mind. 

While here I also partook in a sampling they refer to as the Greg Brady. We are not sure who this Greg fellow is, but surely he must be a southern dignitary of sorts. The Greg Brady is topped with mac n' cheese and barbecue potato chips. Let me just say - Whoa nelly little momma!  I also had a sampling of The Ponch (possibly the moniker of one of their yellow-bellied Generals) a burger topped with a house-made guacamole (smashed and seasoned avocados from California Territory), applewood smoked bacon, white cheddar cheese and Sriracha mayo. Again, a burger that will absolutely delight your taste buds and leave you longing for more. 

While the burgers are the priority, it should be noted that I partook in a side offering of fries that should not be slept on. The fries are a Yukon Gold, crinkle cut variety that was fried to a perfect golden crisp with nary a soggy one among the bunch. They don't cheat you none on the portion size either. Then there's the fry sauce; different than any other I've encountered, I have no idea of how it is concocted (possibly mayo, ketchup, mustard and other spices) but will swear to you, it is heavenly. 

If it were possible, we'd just remain in camp here and eat Jack Brown's burgers night and day throughout the rest of winter. Unfortunately, we must continue on though. I have sent letters back to the President, bestowing a top recommendation for Jack Brown's Beer & Burger Joint. The Chief would be crazy to not immediately get down here and witness this one for himself. 

With new sense of untold vigor, the troops have been rallied once again and we are homeward ho. Baring any further orders from the President or trouble crossing Indian Territory, please expect me by the onset of spring. 

My thoughts, my prayers and all my love be upon you. 

Sincerely,

Col. Jarrod R., 7th Calvary Regiment

Wow...not good! The food here was bland as can be. Mac and cheese with bacon and panko no less had NO flavor...how is this even possible?! Don't know but The Row managed it. On top of the food being entirely subpar, our waitress was rude. She messed up my order and then I heard her acting to the kitchen staff like I was being difficult. Definitely not a place I'd return to.
One star for over priced pizza. In no way is this pizza worth double the price.  I will pay more to support locally owned business but not at this level.

I love STL BBQ. Good BBQ is so plentiful, so sometimes it is hard to decide on where to go. but Adam's is a to do - especially for STL Ribs. The service is very very friendly and fast. Remember to order first and then sit policy! 

Pros:
1) Must order Ribs - very fall off the bone ready. Yes, they are better than Pappy's. 
2) Brisket - but this doesn't come close to the Ribs
3) Pit Beans - but it is laced in a sweet caroline bbq sauce
4) Catering options, but it closes at 4pm on the weekdays  - so you can't cater for Happy Hour or dinner
5) Favorite side sauce is a Caroline Cajun and Sweet Jane. The Caroline vinegar is just too much vinegar for me. 

Cons:
1) Cold Sides are mayo based. This is just a preference that my cole slaw and potato salads are vinegar based. 
2) Small place, so try to come on an off-time.

STL hits another home-run for BBQ again.

It has taken me forever to write this review, b/c I didn't know where to start. With a personal love for farmer markets from Boston, San Franciso, New York to Dayton, Cleveland, and Detroit. I have very high expectations, but this place stacks up to the rest. 

Things to Note:
1) Relative large farmer's market, but the best day to go is on Saturday from 7am-11am. 
2) Some stalls are closed in the winter.
3) Not all the produce is local from MO/IL, etc. - so I would ask or look. This is just a personal preference.
4) Spices, Meat, Bakery Items and other goodies sold inside
5) ATM on stand-by but do yourself some favor and bring cash & your own bags.
6) Grab a bloody-mary before you start
7) Find the Vietnamese Egg-Roll Stand outside. I always do this. 
8) Find the Asian lady with homemade mini-donuts!
9) Grab some local balsamic vinegar and foccacia bread

Very inexpensive, non-pretentious with all types of goodies. There are always some serious dollar store items, so pass on that unless you are in need of useless gadgets.

So - this place is like Panera ( I mean the STL Bread Company) for Ramen. It's pretty standard. You order at the counter and they bring it to your table. I do appreciate it that you don't have to get a pork based broth - which is very hard to find sometimes at Ramen shops. But if you can eat pork and it's your first experience - do the pork broth!

But the Tonkotsu fell short for me. Where is this Umai flavor that I am desperately seeking? The ramen noodles were clearly not handmade and/or they stuck together. It was good overall, but honestly not worth the special effort/price to get here. But they do have wine/beer and I really do like the casual atmosphere. 

Things to note when you go to a Ramen shop- there are no Asians that are eating or working here! It should of clicked for me, but this is a great place to go if you are craving Ramen, but it's not the best in town.

Located in a beautiful area of Germantown, you must come here if you re in Nashville for some Southern experience/cooking!

Things to note:
1) Family Style. No I mean, really family style - unless you have a group of like 12-15, you will most likely sit with other parties at a large round table. The concept is to sit with your family and strangers. You must pass on the left and if the basket/dishes are empty- they will immediately fill it back up for the table.
2) Set Menu and it changes everyday for Breakfast, Lunch, and Dinner
3) Vegetarians will have a hard time here. Even some of the sides like collard greens are cooked in some type of meat fat. I would absolutely call and ask if this will be a problem for that particular day. 
4) If you don't eat pork- you might need to ask if they cook some of their corn pudding in non-bacon grease.
5) Pay at the front counter. 

Pros:
1) Family style and the ability to try lots of things. Dim Sum and Tapas for Southern food!
2) Catfish. Love the seared catfish. 
3) Fried Chicken!!! OMG Yes!
4) Biscuits and Gravy
5) Sweet Potato Pie with Whip creme!
6) Mac N Cheese
7) Fantastic Collard Greens
8) Sweet Tea!

Cons:
1) It's heavy. Everything is generally heavy, but this is the point. You need to come and then come home to get in a food coma.
2) So you can't or people don't take home doggie bags. I wonder what happens with all the left over food b/c they give you sooo much!
3) No reservations.
4) Breakfast is only until 11am on Sunday and 1pm on Saturday. I feel like I would want a longer breakfast hours on Sunday!
5) I'm greedy and wanted some home-made butter vs. what they had for my biscuits.
6) No alcohol, but who needs it for brunch if you have sweet tea!

This place is fantastic and the people are so nice. They are nicer than the usual southern hospitality. This is where people come if you are visiting from out of town or if you live down the street!

So, I love love Peruvian food. I spent some time down in Peru and the history, culture, and people are so beautiful. In addition, Peruvian food has a lot of fusion flavors (lots of Chinese/Japanese influence, Spaniards, and many others). Chifa's or Peruvian/Chinese food is very common down there - so I was slightly sad when they didn't have one dish (that is soooo common in Peru and a lot of Peruvian restaurants I have been to in the States have) to show this fusion. But- this place truly deserves 4+ from the service to the food in STL.

Pros:
1) Free plantain and verde salsa chips. And it was delicious. Ask for more!
2) Lomo Saltado - This is the Peruvian staple. Beef tenderloin with rice/veggies/fries.  I absolutely loved this dish.
3) Aji de Gallina - Another chicken Peruvian staple, but this was very rich for me. Be aware that there are nuts in this.
4) Solid plaintains
5) Delicious Quinoa salads and all there salads are very circus based and refreshing - especially the Ensalada de Palta (lots of avocados!)
6) Mussels has delicious flavors
7) Service was generally excellent. They split checks here and what I appreciated is they even split a birthday girl's bill among 13 of us. Much appreciated. They even had Happy Birthday Menu's Printed for us!!!
8) Great Pisco Sour - the peruvian drink to get
9) Beautiful atmosphere and reasonable price for a semi-upscale dining experience. 


Cons:
1) No Chicha morada. Where is my purple drink damn it?
2) Parking. There is no lot, but there is a $5 lot around the corner and I did not see any valet for a weeknight. In addition, there are relatively a large amount of meter parking. 

But honestly, I understand why most people love love this place. Especially if you have not had Peruvian food- you must come here. And if you have had Peruvian food- there are just a few things missing from the experience. I will def. come back again and next time- I need to make sure I get the ceviche.

Been here a few times, but this week during the Protest made me want to support them more. Supporting local businesses that support the community is important. Pi for Lunch today again! Plus - this is damn good pizza. It's a STL staple. I also actually think this location is the best out of Downtown and the Loop.

Since I have probably had everything on the Menu, there are several things to keep in mind:

1) This is not East Coast Pizza. There is thin crust (which is delicious) - but it is cornmeal based. Since I'm from the Eastcoast originally, this was new to me. New Yorkers don't hate me.
2) Love the deep dishes, but they took a lot longer to cook (15-20m)
3) Online ordering available
4) Able to split Pies with thin and deep-dish
5) Lots of pork-based options, but there are chicken/plenty of veggie options available
6) Special pizzas like Korean-town is actually not bad. I was so hesitant with beef bulgogi on my damn pizza. 
7) Call me old-fashion, but the best pizza is the classic Margarita (oil based)
8) Lots of outdoor patio seating if it isn't like 90s-100s out.
9) Happy HOUR from 3-6pm at the Bar and outside.
10) Most people love the Pi Squares, but I'm not a huge fan (which is like a version of breadsticks with Kale/Cheese)
11) Love the Salads and enough to Share (especially the Kale)
12) Everyday is 8'', $8 any pizza plus add a $5 salad for lunch!

Thanks Chris for making our community great!

Pure comfort Chinese American.

The is the best take-out/sit-in casual Chinese American in the Central West End/near Barnes area. It is so inexpensive (from $5-7 lunches to $7-10 dinner combos or entrees). Do you remember we are in the CWE? Plus, they have a punch card rewards program! It is also sooooo fast. I never feel the need to call in an order b/c it really does only take about 5 minutes for them to prepare it and people are incredibly nice. Service at a Chinese-American establishment? You know on Olive St. this is rare. It is also clean/simple inside if you wanted to sit in. There are several tables and bar stools. 

As an ABC, I get that once a month craving for Chinese-American from General Tso Chicken to Beef w/Green Beans to Hunan Chicken (ask for it spicy) to Crab Ragoons and Hot n Sour Soup. FYI. I don't love the springrolls - but that is just b/c I'm bias and I prefer lumpia or Southeast Asian ones. This isn't Olive Street - so there is no real authentic Chinese food happening here. But, this place is consistent and I never feel like it's overly salty or over-cooked. Cheers to the folks making it accessible and reasonable in the CWE.

Bonus points: There is WIFI!!!

Being listed as one of the top restaurants in STL, I had you on my list for sometime and it's hard to get prime-time reservations. Although I liked this place, it's not an everyday meal because of the 1 month reservation wait time for F/S and I like to eat at prime time w/o a wait - but there is a bar and outdoor patio for some cocktails on a first come first serve basis. Try coming at grandma dinner time or a late night post 8:30pm treat to get in without a reservation on weekdays. This is really a solid place to bring a date. The pictures don't justify how cute it is inside. 

Highlights on several occasions:
1) Servers know what is on their menu and the ingredients that goes into everything. 
2) Honey bread
3) Dover Sole with minted pea creme. It just wasn't as pretty as the other dishes, but def. large enough to share.
4) Flank steak was very very tender and moist
5) Entrees do not come with veggie sides, but always get a side of charred veggies. 
6) Solid O & O burger options (made this an appetizer to share)
7) TVs in the bar area and the game is always on
8) Excellent unique cocktails. They have Japanese whiskey!
9) Fried oysters are a pass unless you like them heavily breaded
10) Asian Pho inspired soup fell flat for me. 
11) Always get their special (sometimes beef cheeks, scallops, fish, etc.)
12) Gnocchi is light and fluffy
13) Extremely reasonably priced and well-ranged for large parties
14) Children friendly for a restaurant of this quality, but this is mainly due to the beautiful story that Olive + Oak were children of the two chefs that died of congenital heart defects. So - you will notice the decor and the heart pins. 

This popular place is well worth the trip b/c the food is well executed with a beautiful story and exceptional service when the Owner(s) stop by every table to check in on you.

Beautiful space for just a drink or come in for dinner. This is a great place to take a date.  The bar is right up in front and completely separate from 2 large dining rooms, but nevertheless with really knowledgable and friendly people. I recommend making reservations even for a weekday.

The Food:
1) Devil Eggs - yum
2) Mussels (very large size as an entree) - get this!!!
3) Brussel Sprouts (meh - pass on this)
4) Cuccous ( to die for!!)
5) Burger and Frites (Fantastic)
6) Chicken Wings (Delicious with their cocktails)

You come here for the ambiance and you stay for some mean cocktails. The end.

If you do not eat red meat or at least seafood, this is not the place for you. Vegetarians find another place or sit at the bar for a cocktail and a slice of wedding cake. But - you come here for a steak. This is better and less pretentious while being still upscale over Chop 801.

Pros:
1) HH from 3-6pm (Bar only). Lots of food options.
2) Perfect aged steak and prime rib
3) Thin crispy frites
4) Cold plates for salads - but the dressing is heavy (ask for it on the side)
5) Free valet parking on the weekends
6) Excellent whiskey cocktails and wine selections
7) Almond Moist Wedding CAKE!!! 


Cons:
1) Pass on the veggie sides. Some how, they can't get the charr right or it's overcooked for my al dente needs.
2) While this is a beautiful restaurant and a sufficient bar area, the dining room chairs are not that comfortable. 
3) Pass on the fish/seafood entrees unless you are doing a lobster surf n turf. Although, the salmon did look on point. 

Again - you come here for a perfect aged steak. Meats. Meats. Meats!

If you have been to Rise, Kitchen House, and many many other coffee shops - they carry Whisk bakery items. This is because they are the gold standard for a sustainable and local bakery company that can accommodate allergies. Sustainable means they compost 90%, use green products, and locally sourced ingredients. They have many vegan, gluten free, and dairy-free options.

The bakery itself has a few tables and a couch to hang out in. It's a great place to hangout with friends, but I don't know about doing some work.

The Eats!
First and foremost, this was a cupcake/cake shop prior to all the delicious bakery offerings. To be honest, my favorite thing is not the cupcakes - but the scones and biscuits. They also have bottom-less coffee here with whoopie pies. I LOVE whoopie pies b/c it pays patronage to my Massachusetts roots. Is it a cake or pie? It's a Whoopie! So besides Peacemaker, I haven't found a place except for Whisk that makes it NE right with unique flavors like pistachio/raspberry. 

Thank you Whisk!

You come here mainly for the atmosphere. It's a beautiful and intimate restaurant with a fireplace, dim lighting, lots of bar seating, and an outdoor patio that is covered/uncovered with a view of the Arch. For April, you are not able to have dinner on the patio yet - but just drinks from the bar.

Things to Note:
1) In the Fall on every Thursday, they have a Chef Tastings from around the World with wine pairings, but this stops in October for $25-$35
2) In the Spring on every Thursday, they have fish flown in from around the world and it is grilled on their open patio
3) HH in the Bar only from 2-6pm on T-F, 1/2 price crepe and apps with drink specials.
4) No view of the Arch if you are sitting indoors.
5) You must take the elevator to get to Vin de Set from a hidden corner entrance through the parking lot. 

The Meal:
So - I opted for a 3-4 course tasting ($35-$41) with a choice of crepe. The Beet and Pistachio had a fantastic flavor and the crepe was very thin and perfect. My creme brûlée was also fantastic. However, the main Grilled Swordfish entree just failed. It didn't have the right grill marks and although it was not under/overcooked - the accompaniments were not ideal. The spring carrot puree was visibly off-putting and the kale was still raw with an awkward vinaigrette. It didn't have a spring fresh taste. Thursday is fish day and it just didn't work. 

Even though my entree failed, I would come back to Vin de Set on a hot date, brunch, wine and for some HH crepes. The staff are knowledgeable, nice, and you feel sexy to be French for a few hours.

I have now been here for brunch, lunch, and dinner. While the hype has died down and it is easier to get a prime-time table for dinner, it is still one of the harder places to get into (so reservations!)

But the real reason for the update is on the casual/fast efficient lunch service. Generally, I don't take a lunch and when you do - you know you are only doing it because it is a lunch meeting. So I generally stay away from places like Sardella - b/c I think it will take too long or I'm not in a mood for a richer meal mid-day. Not the case!

1) Perfect place for a business lunch meeting or get together. It's not really crowded.
2) 1 Larger round tables for groups of 8
3) Beautiful decor
4) If you are not in the area, free parking in the garage
5) Green spinach tonics for a pick me up besides coffee. 
6) Sump Coffee
7) Big Heart Tea
8) 1/2 Sandwich, soup, and Salads options. The bread is slightly on the harder french banquette vs. warm roll sides. As a preference, I don't love the sandwhich carb options. 

So if you haven't been here for dinner, come for dinner b/c it's intimate and sexy with a date. Or sit at the bar and have a fantastic Happy Hour meal by yourself. But, if you need a professional business lunch and superior service - this is the deal too.

Coal oven pizza right off of south street with lots of fresh ingredients. 

What else do u need?

On my - I love this place. 

1) order anything that has lamb, anything 
2) always ask for more fresh pita 
3) get a fancy cocktail
4) lovely date place with wonderful outdoor seating... get reservations!!! 

The only thing to note is you order and pay via an app, all good and u still have waiter service but it gets cumbersome if u want to keep ordering. 

I recommend for a date night or a group date out with friends. 

Omg - I'm hungry thinking about this place.

Hidden in a strip mall on Olive next to a Korean Market, this is the new "hipster" and cute Korean BBQ restaurant. It is first and foremost delicious. The banchan (side dishes) were plentiful. I particularly loved the fish cakes, kimchi slaw, bean sprouts, etc. They have plenty of seating, but it is pretty full during prime dinner hour. We were able to call in a reservation. I don't know if they only do this for large groups, but give it a try regardless of party. If you have to wait, go next door to the Korean market and/or grab some soju/beer/wine at Olive Market. It is still BYOB for now. The only real critique I have is the ventilation. Yes, it's slightly smokey in here due to the BBQ sizzles. This is the deal, I knew I was going to smell like Korean BBQ - so leave your dry-clean only jackets in the car. But, they could use some improvements. 

Things to Note and Procedures when you get here.
1) BYOB your wine/beer/soju. I don't know how long they will have BYOB. Call!
2) Get a table with the Grill (especially if you have at least a table of 4). I prefer the table grills vs. the grills they bring out to you
3) You must get the BBQ, although I'm sure the rest is delicious too.
4) We got a side order of Japchae (glass noodles with beef bulgogi) and Rice Cakes. Good Stuff and plentiful to share.
5) Next- do you want ALL YOU CAN EAT or a set order. We did not opt for AYCE. 
6) Pick your meats. The small order that saids it served 2-3, really served about 4 comfortability and maybe even 5- especially if you are like us and ordered noodles on the side. Also note that all traditional banchan sides are always refillable. 
7) Order the Marinated Beef, then you get a seafood pancake with the order, then you get a egg souffle dish, and you also get to choose a soup (bean paste or kimchi paste).
8) Ask for larger plates. They give you little plates to put everything on. 
9) Choose a designated BBQ person to grill the meats on the table. Once it's grilled to your liking, you eat it in the delish lettuce wraps with some rice, onion/sauce/add some banchan in the wrap, and then you add your Gochujang red pepper paste in the bottle. 
10) Ask for more lettuce wraps b/c you are going to need it!
11) Ask for them to change out the grill when you are on your second set of meats. You will need to do that if they don't do that for you instantly.

On a side note, I loved, loved the grilled korean squash. 

We were stuffed for four and it was probably the most inexpensive meal for the quality and experience at around $20 a person (especially b/c we got a side dish too). The AYCE is around the same price, but I think we got some higher quality marinated beefs and I honestly don't think I could eat more than what we had. The service was also nice. 

At the end of the meal, go to the Korean Bakery down the street and get some creme puffs if they are not closed! We will def. be back with more people to try more items. I'm still full from all the BBQ I had - yah protein!

Yes, the Blue Duck serves Duck!

Across from Gus's Fried Chicken, this is the second location opened from Washington, MO and it's not a home-run yet. But, they have some awesome comfort food. 

Things to Note:
1) HH from 3-6pm from Tues-Fri with a full bar
2) No huge difference from the lunch or dinner menu
3) It's very large inside for groups, so go ahead and bring your kid's little league team.
4) Because of how large it is inside, it isn't very cozy the way you need a place to serve comfort food would be. But, it's clear they are trying with a mix of very high ceilings and random rustic touches. I hope they dim the lights at night. 
5) No Parking, but go ahead and park across the street
6) It is right next door to a construction-site, but don't be afraid and walk in.
7) If you sit at the high-tops, the bartender will take your order.
8) Pricey for comfort food
9) Service is off

The Food:
1) You come here for the duck. And I love duck, so go for the duck entree or the Duck - DLT. The DLT is good and not chewy, but just very messy with the extra buttered crisp bread. 
2) The pork belly Bao and bites were actually delish too, but overly dressed.

Overall, great comfort food in an awkward atmosphere with slow service.

Lilly's, I used to love you, but it's all over now. 
I was there when you opened and came there frequently when I used to live uptown. Loved your food. The spring rolls with strawberry? Great!
But why you gotta be so rude? 

The last few times I've gone there, it's mostly been call-in, take-out. 
Disclaimer: I've waited tables and I work in customer service. I understand a packed house and I know how not to be an a-hole on the phone. 
That said, the first bad experience was in 2011-2012, in the winter. I ordered a few very common things for takeout, as I was introducing some visting Scottish friends to Vietnamese food for the first time. They wanted to eat at home, so we did that. 
The young girl on the phone took the opportunity to try and be didactic with what I was ordering, trying to imply that she didn't know what I meant when I ordered the regular spring rolls & the Lilly spring rolls. She was saying "which kind of spring rolls? There are many kinds of spring rolls. You could mean any kind. You want them fresh? Fried...?"And it was not helpful tone of voice, rather someone that was pissed off and all but calling me stupid.  So I asked for the goi cuon, with shrimp & pork. She went back into her willfully uncomprehending series of questions, in fact getting really rude at the end and getting into a weird mini-fight on the phone with me as I was trying to finish placing my large takeout order. I almost cancelled, but I had 4 hungry Scots in the car wanting soup, so I thought maybe she was having bad day, and maybe it's busy, and I understand crappy days in a restaurant. 
I got there to pick it up, and when I went inside, the place was dead, she was on her phone, and when I said who I was, she went back to the kitchen and 4 other girls popped their heads out from the back,  looked at me and started laughing and nodding. Seriously. 
We got home and although we'd ordered 2 orders each of the contentious spring rolls, we only got one order of each, so 4 rolls to split between 5 people.  We had 5 soups, with really skimpy garnishes, and my friends were wondering why I was all gung-ho about vietnamese food,  until I took them to a restaurant in the East. 
So I thought this was a one-off. I gave it a few months before I gave them another try. Not rude the next time, but it took almost an hour for a small takeout order to be ready. 
Then one more time, sitting down at the restaurant, the waitress looked new and somewhat shell-shocked and was being audibly reprimanded at in the back of the house. And it took forever. 
This last time was just two weeks ago. It's been a couple of years since I last tried Lilly's, and I was getting takeout to surprise my best friend who is a schoolteacher on her birthday. School teacher = short lunch break. I called an hour ahead of time. I brought a bag in which to carry everything. I ordered 3 soups, 3 spring rolls, 3 iced jasmine teas. I got there when I said I would, and I still waited more than 20 minutes...for them to pack it up and pour iced tea into cups.  They put the straws in the iced tea cups and put them in a plastic bag, which they then tied so all the straws were bent & broken when I unpacked them, and half of the tea was spilled, as they were squished up against each other an not standing straight up. I ordered three of everything...and they only gave me two sets of spoons & chopsticks. The soup broth also spilled in the bags, and the lids came off the peanut sauce so it went everywhere. I brought my own bottle of sriracha  and they accused me of taking theirs, even though they watched me carry everything in, and when I told them I brought it from home, she still looked at me like I was stealing until I showed her that my bottle had condensation from being refrigerated.  And because it took so long, we only had about 15 minutes to surprise my friend before her students came back in the room after lunch. 
It's just the last time. 

Sorry Lilly's,  but as convenient as you are, and as much as I was your biggest fan when you first opened, I don't pay money for people to treat me like crap, mess up my orders, make me wait a super long time when I call ahead, and spill half of my food. 
I gave you more chances than I give my boyfriends, but I'm sorry, we have to break up.

First Monday back from the holiday break and we were right back to the age-old, "Where are we going for lunch?" question?  Well, the ROTD on Sunday was for Jaws Jumbo Burgers- so I figured that would be a fine suggestion.
We work in Southfield, so Jaws is a little further than we normally venture for lunch - but not ridiculously so.  We were the only ones in the joint at this time, which was okay by me since I hate fighting for a table - but made me a little nervous b/c super-yummy places usually have super-long lunch lines.  Whatever- maybe New Years Resolutions weren't being broken yet.
Panic set in when we saw the Cash Only sign - but everyone checked their wallet and amazingly had cash.  That never happens.  The lady working behind the counter asked if it was our first time and gave us a VERY thorough description of how things work, what the menu consisted of, and the days specials.  Mondays you can get a 1/3 lb ground sirloin hamburger, fries and a pop for $5.75; that's $6.10 with tax.  Not too shabby.
The burgers were finished pretty quickly- with some hot fries on the side.  I appreciate the use of ground sirloin, and was pleasantly surprised that the burger was still pretty juicy.  Condiments were good - I really liked the grilled onions.  The burger was pretty messy, but I guess that's half the fun.  I was VERY stuffed after this meal.  It didn't help that the pop cups are large and I like to drink fountain Coke. :)  We got a chocolate cookie to share in the office later- and that was also pretty good.  I don't know if it was $2.75 good, but it wasn't bad.
The staff were fantastic, they made sure we were satisfied and were very friendly to boot.  The shark fish in the tank were pretty cool.  The 5 TV's in the little space was kind of funny - but was unfortunately playing the Mummy 2.  I DID NOT know that on my own, I had to be told that.  I wish something else had been playing.  The Jay Leno burger thing and all of the Jay Leno hype was kind of amusing.  Did they decide to do this because the business is named Jaws and Jay Leno has a big jaw?  I don't know.
I would have no problems coming back, but I don't think it will be part of our regular lunch rotation.  Maybe if it were a smidge closer to our office???... I don't know.  After I came back I checked out their website and saw that this is actually a training store and that they are trying to get people to start Jaws franchises.  I thought that was interesting. Good luck to them.

Late edit: I forgot to mention the bathrooms- Man have I lost my touch.  So, the bathroom is one singular - being male/female usage.  Ususally that idea really bothers me, but this place was so clean and constantly being cleaned around us - so I was okay with it.

America's #1 Fried Chicken? 

Okay so I may not be a fried chicken connoisseur but I honestly felt like it tasted no different than Popeyes. Actually a little bit saltier than Popeyes. The parts were there aren't any meat and it's just fried skin, it was incredibly super salty. Luckily it came with sides so it helps to wash down the saltiness with it. The butter beans complimented the fried chicken pretty well, the mac and cheese was so and so, not spectacular but not terrible. I recommend going for the extra white meat for $3 more because you'll get more than you bargain for. There was barely any chicken in my order it was just two measly wings and a breast. 

Verdict: Not worth the wait but I suppose worth trying if you're visiting Nawlins. Try to come early in the morning or around opening time. I was seated immediately when I arrived but when I left around 1, there was a long line outside the window already.

If you havent had a chance to check out Russell's, what are you waiting for? This locally run business is a gem tucked away in Fenton. Even driving up and seeing the sign you know this is going to be a delicious experience. Walking in we were greeted by the sites and sounds of happy satisfied customers enjoying their breakfast selections. There was plenty of seating both inside and out despite the busy morning. The cashier that greeted us was very friendly and engaging. Mom ordered the Southwest breakfast wrap and a Chocolate Dipped Raspberry Iced latte and I chose the breakfast grilled cheese and a Iced Peppermint Mocha Latte. Being a St louis native I couldn't pass up a chance at a piece of Gooey Butter cake, so I chose the BlackBerry to go. He quickly boxed it up and then gave me our table number and said our meal and drinks would be out soon. We chatted with others sitting next to us and before long our order was delivered. The coffees were delicious. Mine was so minty which j love and their coffee blend balanced it nicely. Mom really enjoyed hers as well, in fact she finished hers long before I did. Our sandwiches were beautifully plated on wooden boards accompanied by fresh fruit. As good as it looked , it tasted even better. I never would have thought to add fresh basil to my breakfast sandwich. It reminded me of a caprese salad sans the balsamic with an egg. 
Before we started packing up our leftovers Mom decided she also needed a piece of gooey butter but she chose the chocolate chip. I also struck up a great conversation with Missy, the head Baker.
We look forward to visiting many more times and taking home a gooey Butter cake to Florida for friends to enjoy!
Happy dining!

I have come to this place since I was in high school (I'm now 33) and since I have moved from Tucson it was always somewhere I looked forward to visiting when I came to visit family.  This place has sadly gone so downhill, and I think it really has to do with the culture of the employees that work there.  The employees, especially the black haired daughter of one of the owners, are rude, dismissive and unfriendly.  They act like you are being done a favor by doing their jobs.  Hilarious considering their point of sale system asks you to leave them a tip after you swipe your card.

Recently I witnessed a man who obviously had never been to Raging Sage before asking for a "grande coffee," which of course, is Starbucks speak for medium coffee.  This is pretty common knowledge.  When he was handed a large coffee, he said, "Oh you I thought I ordered a medium."  The nasty daughter of the owner with the black hair and tattoos responded, "you said grande, grande is large is Spanish so I charged you for a large."  I've seen this same child scold other guests for being unclear on their cellphone policy (you aren't allowed to use them or you'll be asked to leave).  

The scones have gone down hill, their coffee is bitter, but really its their disgusting morning staff lead by the head Ms. Nasty who thinks its okay to treat people who are spending their hard earned money on their overpriced coffee like they are worse than dirt.  Do yourself a favor, go one of the other lovely local coffee shops Tucson has. A coffee shop that appreciates your business and treats you with respect because you are a paying customer.

Came here with a couple of friends that visited this place before. I saw this place pop up everywhere in social media and I was excited to finally check it out! It's located near the Lakeside Mall in a small strip. It has only been open for a little bit more than a week and I heard a lot of good things about it.

The workers were extremely friendly when we walked in and offered us samples of their ice cream. I tried the Cookie Monster and Matcha Green Tea with White Chocolate Ganache ice creams. After seeing how cool the bubble waffles looked from friend's pictures, I decided to get the Bubble Waffle with Cookie Monster ice cream and almonds. My friends had gotten an Ice Cream Flight with three different flavors to enjoy. I thought it was cool how they have flights of 3, 6, and 12 for those who like to enjoy different flavors or to share. The bubble waffle had a nice fluff, slight crisp, and a perfect amount of sweetness. I ate a bubble for each small scoop of ice cream and it was just wonderful. The ice cream and waffle wasn't overly sweet like some places, so they really went well together. 

Overall, this place is an awesome place to get some dessert at any time of the day! The staff is nice and the inside looks pretty cool! I really appreciate the fact that their ice cream are homemade and that they don't make them too sweet. I'm shocked that they have perfected everything for grand opening and up until now. I have no doubt that they'll be even better in the future and I can't wait to try them again!

The lines can be awful, especially when there are a million kids that none of the bourgeois parents feel like dealing with, because they're too busy posturing to try to look like a Real Housewife, and working hard to stare at everyone else around them (which they think intimidates people and makes them cool, but which really is just vile and offensive).

This people-who-live-in-the-little-houses-but-act-like-they-live-in-the-big-houses complex is a real turn-off, and actually a bit of a deterrent for us, BUT Handel's works to process the line quickly, to cure this pain, and then you have ice cream at the end of it!  Besides, most of the anorexic-wannabe women don't order anything big or time-consuming anyway (they get a child's cone and take one lick because they're so mentally disturbed).  What a relief.

That said, all in all, Handel's is still a great place for delicious ice cream!

At Handel's a cone is not big enough, a pint is not big enough, noooooo, it takes a QUART (each) when Handel's is concerned!  Excellent, excellent, excellent ice cream!

This is probably why, despite the fact that they are 3 miles from our home, we cannot allow ourselves to go too often, lest we fail to fit out the front door for subsequent trips!

Seriously, we don't finish a quart in one sitting, but we do each get one, and greedily guard and savor it for days after, like rabid children.

This is some of the creamiest, richest ice cream I have ever had.  Cold Stone, I would say, is creamier, but theirs is so creamy it makes me a little ill.  I would place Handels' creaminess between Cold Stone and Brewster's.  But for us, the freshness and overall taste of Handel's exceeds anything else.

I tried cookies and cream (I believe they call it vanilla Oreo, or something) the first time I went, and in many many trips since, I have not changed to anything else.  I am not yet ready to be over this flavor, and I may never try anything else.

My husband tries something different each time, and is always thoroughly pleased.

The employees are normally very friendly.  The owner's family is most professional.  One time we had an issue with the quarts not being packed very well, but Buck, the franchise owner, called back, immediately, and took care of everything, with generosity.

Only one star because they comped our meal.  Poor service, empty drinks, paper towels out in bathroom, wrong food delivered, table of 5, one meal never delivered.  Fajita veges looked like salad, under cooked on a cold platter.  When wrong meal finally delivered we had it boxed, got home, WRONG meal again.  

What a shame, beautiful place, awesome patio, lots of potential.  I like the original location.  This one is a disaster.  Our table was not the only one with issues.  Manager was apologetic, but it was nearly 2 hours into this.
Great food! You would like it if you enjoy Vietnamese Food! Th e folks are friendly and prices are very reasonable.

I don't write a ton of reviews.  I'm your typical selfish Yelper who reads only.  However, in this instance I am compelled to write about my experience(s) with shoefly.  I love supporting local start-ups but this one needs to get their sh*t together. 

My first two times eating there were in the restaurant, and they were decent (worthy of 3-3.5 stars).  The food is slightly over priced  for the quality/quantity, and the service was OK.  

I work close by, so I was excited to have a neighborhood spot.  After ordering carryout twice, it has been the worst carry out experience I've ever had.  

The first time I ordered a cup of soup and a side of fries (total: $10). I received a half cup (measured) of the tortellini soup (which isn't good) and 13 fries.  It looked like less than half of what I actually ordered.  I also had to remind the server at pick up that my fries came with a sauce to get it.  The fries were tasty.  Regardless, spending $10 on fries and a cup of soup, I was frustrated that the order was extremely light and I called in VERY politely just to inform the servers that the kitchen made a clear error and that I wasn't trying to cause trouble but that they should know BECAUSE I like their place and want them to do well.  The woman on the phone informed me that she was grateful for my call and would remember me and make sure to give me a free drink next time I was there which I thought was cool.  She also said she'd talk with the manager and get back to me about potentially doing something else - never happened.  

Today, a week later, I just ordered carry out again (a sand which and salad for $14) and picked it up only to find that the side that was supposed to come with the sandwich hadn't been put in my order and the sand which was cold.  The salad was barely edible (normally good salad though).  

The place was nearly empty both times I went and both times the kitchen screwed up the order and ultimately screwed me out of food for my $.  The lady who I spoke with on the phone looked me right in the face when I picked up my second carry out order and mentioned nothing of the first order incident or the drink she promised me. 

If you can't get carry out right - don't offer it.  If you charge a lot for your food - make it right.  Deliver on your promises.  Care enough about your patrons to follow through and give them their $'s worth or you'll lose them.  And the last customer you want to lose is the one who works a few blocks from you.  

Here's the thing - I'll go back again.  I want to believe they mean well and they're just working some things out.  I'm going to make it a point to write a follow-up review soon.
Sorry to write all of this Shoefly but you had it coming.

***UPDATE: They still suck.***

Came here for dinner and was delighted by the hearty and tasty menu. The Caesar salad is served "wedge" style here, and almost every single pasta in the menu is made in-house. I chose the fettuccine with Bolognese.... Beautifully prepared noodles tossed in a rich, powerful ragu.

My friends' eggplant rollatini is delicious with sliced eggplant rolled with ricotta and spinach, then baked in a lovely marinara sauce. 

Totally surprised and will have no hesitation returning. 

Service is friendly.

Well I'm no Italian food expert but I know I def like restaurants that cater towards vegans and this one def does get that part right. 

Our first time dining here was on Valentine's evening.  Of course we made reservations as obviously it's the most busiest night of the year for most restaurants. 

Entering the restaurant we noticed tables were close together but didn't bother us so much as we've experienced dining like this before. The hosts were extremely friendly. All the women in the restaurants were given roses on this special day. 

Vegan tips: they can make almost make anything vegan - just call and ask ahead of time. The servers have knowledge and great suggestions. Reserve a vegan cannoli. And don't forget Byob if you want that experience. Don't come here expecting you'll be in and out of the restaurant quickly. You come here for the experience.

Very friendly place, clean and welcoming. The prices here are also very good. I had big hopes.

For me I think the sirloin prevented me from loving the burgers. I appreciate that sirloin is healthier and leaner but my burger lacked the extra flavor you find in a higher fat content patty. The toppings were great and added a bit of that oomph I was looking for but for someone like my husband who prefers a plainer burger it was not as happy. My bite of his double pattied cheeseburger was not nearly as enjoyable as my loaded up single version with the tasty grilled onions. His was just too dry.

The fries were decent enough, hot and crispy. The service was terrific. A nice place but not one that will have me making the trek from my house specifically. 

If you like a loaded up burger you will probably like this place better than if you are a person who prefers it plain.

I have found a cure for claustrophobia. Reading Terminal Market. Crowded and bustling but everywhere you look there is something new to see and you are assaulted by mouth watering smells and temptations every few paces. It makes the volume of people jostling you entirely bearable.

My fave samplings:
Termini Brothers for tasty cheese cannoli, fig bars, sfogliatelle, pignoli cookies and biscotti.
Fisher's for Amish pretzels with butter
Lancaster Co Dairy for fresh squeezed lemonade
Salumeria for gourmet meats and cheese which made for an awesome midnight snack
Dutch Eating Place for food that is similar to Grandma's and a kick ass apple dumpling.

If I lived in Philly I would be in here all the time, the shopping looked incredible, super fresh products of all sorts. So sad to miss DiNic's though, I will have to return at some point. Thanks to Bobby P, Andrew T and Mira V for the suggestion.

Was taking a road trip down to Maryland for the long weekend. My boyfriend and I decided to stop here for dinner after constantly hearing about Pats (and Gino's) on Food Network. Really wish we didn't make the stop...

A complete waste of time and money. You wait on this long absurd line for crap food. When you get to the first window you order wit or witout (onions) and chose your cheese. Plain, American, provolone or cheese wiz. Then you pay. The worker gets your sandwich out in under 60 seconds. The next window is for fries and beverages. Kind of a waste of time in my opinion for two windows doing different things. If both windows had everything, things would be quicker. 

My boyfriend got a philly steak wit American. He said it was dry and the bread was nasty. I ordered a roasted pork witout provolone. Driest pork I've ever had. 

Fries were super ..meh. 

Everything lacked flavor. 

Don't believe the hype! 

Pat's??? More like Crap's.

Came here with a friend for a bite to eat. 

We waited about 20 mins to sit down. There's no wait to sit at the counter, but that's a first come, first serve area. 

It's a cozy little restaurant with tables both inside and outside. 

Each table gets their own pitcher of water, which if you drink a lot of water is very beneficial because you don't have to wait for a server or bus-boy to refill your glass. 

They serve breakfast items and lunch items here. Different types of coffee drinks, smoothies, teas, etc are also available.

My friend and I shared the avocado toast appetizer. It was two slices of bread cut into triangles with avocado, tomatoes, and sea salt on top. It was delicious! As I write this review I really want another bite! Mmm! 

For my entree I went with zucchini "zoodles" spaghetti. It had zucchini, artichoke hearts, mushrooms, red peppers, a little Parmesan cheese tossed in a pesto reduction. It was very light, tasty, and very fresh. The portion size was big. 

My friend went with a breakfast dish. She got Acai Crepes. It was a special of the day. The acai was drizzled on top. Inside the crepes were bananas, blueberries and strawberries. She didn't mention how it tasted, but she ate the whole thing! So...I'm pretty sure she enjoyed it! 

Our server, (I believe his name was Anthony) was great. He didn't rush us, and he answered any questions that we had. 

The prices were reasonable.

Heard you had to go here for a muffuletta. So this is where my boyfriend and I found ourselves for lunch. For those that don't know a muffuletta is both a type of round Sicilian sesame bread and a popular sandwich that originated among Italian immigrants in New Orleans, Louisiana. It has Swiss, ham and salami and green olive salad. 

Although a little salty, it was delicious. A "full" comes with 4 large pieces. My boyfriend and I split a half, which is two pieces and it was more than enough. It was very tasty. 

So why only 3 stars? Service. Our waitress kept trying upsell us on getting more and more when we specifically said we only wanted half a muffuletta. She kept saying it wasn't enough and tried getting us to get a whole one, fries and a calamari appetizer. It was very unwelcomed. She did the same when we only ordered water and soda. Kept trying to upsell alcohol. 

Oh! And the plate was extremely hot! I burned my fingers on it. It's common courtesy for the server to tell the patron if a plate is hot! This did not occur.  

Also, we overheard another employee complain about being sick after getting her booster. If you're sick, stay home! 

Food was good, but service was less to be desired.

Bottom line is that Mimi's is one of my fave spots in the neighborhood. Grabbing a table right next to the window with some great company is second to none. I love doing Mardi Gras here for St. Anne's and the St. Patrick's Day parade too!

The crowd is eclectic, but leans toward the hipster side of things. I always take my first dates to Mimi's because there's enough going on if a distraction is needed. 

Since the Reno upstairs, it has been extra lovely to sit up there and eat off of the great tapas menu. Mimi's has the best $9 steak you will ever eat and everything else is great... the potatoes, the mushroom manchego toast, and the empanadas especially!

Spending some time at Mimi's makes for a great look into the neighborhood and to the people that make NOLA fun! Chat up anyone! I've found that everyone is down to earth and friendly.

The spot is basically the go-to place to eat at the beach, hence, the name "the spot". It is located several meters away from the blissful beach in Carpinteria. The weather is always cool and relaxing here. 

 Surrounding the spot are side streets to park and a nice little area vented with a/c. I felt like being in a corner was a great place to put the restaurant. 

 The spot is a burger/fried food for convenience. The area has been here for years and I can see why. Plenty of locals come to eat their food. 

 The prices for this place are on the expensive end. I ordered onion rings for $6 and I felt that I didn't get much. The other items like their fish and chips are quite tasty and amazing. 

 There are small bathrooms located on the side. But you can go to a bathroom stall a couple yards away. Overall, my experience here was awesome. Going to the beach with a nice breeze and eating this food makes you feel calm inside. Also, the lines are long, but it goes by smoothly so you won't have to wait long, I love this type of service.

I was up in Santa Barbara/Goleta area with my cousins, and we scouted out this seafood place.  We had a bad experience at Santa Barbara Shellfish on the Wharf, so we wanted to hit a good seafood place.  Nikka is on Calle Real near Kingston in Goleta.  For those of you unfamiliar with the area, UCSB is actually in Goleta, which is about 15 min North of DT Santa Barbara.

We ordered grilled salmon ($13.95 | inc grilled veggies, rice or fries, and mango slaw; steamed clams ($13.95), and cioppino ($13.95).  The latter two include soup or salad.  To drink, I had a Summerland chardonnay from a local winery ($8).

First of all, my salmon was really good.  The fish was very fresh, it was not overcooked, and the mango slaw complimented, not overpowered the fish.  BTW, I hate places that serve tartar sauce w/ grilled fish.  Likewise, the grilled veggies were crunchy, and included baby bok choy - a nice surprise.  The rice, eh:  4 Stars overall.  Secondarily, I tried the steamed clams.  While they were not as good as The Deck in Laguna Beach, they were better compared to SB Shellfish.  The broth was more tasty vs SB, but was missing the garlic & portuguese sausage in The Deck's version:  4 Stars.  Lastly, the cioppino was a good rendition of a SF classic.  It was reasonably priced, the seafood was fresh & plentiful, and the broth went well w/ the garlic bread.  Again, not as good as The Deck, but it tasted good just the same:  4 Stars.

Regarding the ambiance, its located in a strip mall.  You walk up and order, and they bring your food to you.  Nonetheless, they display the fresh seafood in a case upfront:  4 Stars.  Likewise, the service was friendly and efficient.  It was a real pleasant experience:  4 Stars.

Like most oceanside places, avoid the touristy pier and go where the locals go when you are in Santa Barbara.  The food is better, and less expensive.  You're welcome!

I stopped by Cava for a quick lunch before a work function around the corner at Montecito Country Club.  Some positive signs:  As I drove by to check into my hotel, I saw a fair number of people sitting outside.  I also Yelped it, and saw that my yf Steph H. wrote a positive review.

I ordered off the tapas menu:  Small tortilla soup - $8 and the tamale trio - $11 (chicken; pork; and chile & sweet corn).  They also have traditional tapas like tortilla espanola (potato omelette), and entrees like enchiladas suiza or mariscos.  You also receive complimentary chips w/ two types of salsa.  

Unfortunately, the chips and salsa were disappointing.  The chips were not fresh, and the red salsa was weak, although the corn and bean salsa was very good:  2 Stars.  On the other hand, the soup was very good, and it was a large portion for being the small order.  The broth was thin as it should be and there was just the right amount of chicken. The only thing that I would have changed is offering some lime on the side:  4 Stars.  The tamales were also very good.  They were the right size to just have a taste of each one.  The masa was fresh and there was a fair amount of ingredients in each one.  The only downside was the pico de gallo was not fresh:  4 Stars.

My waitress Katherin was really good also.  I told her I was under a bit of a time constraint, and the food came out quickly.  She warned me about the bowl being hot (just like her - lol!), so I didn't burn myself:  4 Stars.  The ambiance was OK.  I liked the Latin music in the background, but the decor was nothing special:  3 Stars.

I would definitely come back here w/ a date or business associate. I would like to try more tapas, and have some drinks next time the way a Madrileno would do tapas!!!

Stella Mare's advertises French cuisine, but the meal we had for a Team Dinner was more continental.  We had a three course meal that started w/ a choice of salad or soup, steak or chicken, and there was one dessert:  Apple tart w/ vanilla ice cream.

I ordered the caesar salad, NY steak w/ potato and vegetables, and obviously the dessert.  I asked for anchovies on my salad, but the waitress said there was anchovies in the dressing.  What dressing?!  I could hardly taste it and the lettuce was not that crisp:  2 Stars.  The steak was OK. It was prepared medium rare as requested. But the sauce did nothing for the steak.  The potato and veggies were just OK also:  Both 3 Stars.  On the other hand, the dessert was really good.  The tart was good sized, and the apple flavor came out nicely.  I would have liked it a little warmer, but I understood that the foregoing is hard to execute with a party of 20ish:  4 Stars.

The ambiance is quaint and the restaurant has its own wine label:  4 Stars.  The service was really good.  Our two primary servers deserve kudos for handling a large group so well:  4 Stars.

3.5 Stars overall.  I would definitely come back if I was in the area, spend my own $, and bring a date here.  I would also like to try some Frenchier dishes next time!!!

Its Mediocre Monday again!!!

My cousin went to UCSB, so on a recent trip to Santa Barbara, she wanted to show us around Isla Vista next to campus.  Woodstocks is on El Camino del Norte & Madrid in Isla Vista.

We ordered the #1 special ($7.95 | one topping individual pizza w/ unlimited drink), small organic spinach salad w/ bacon ($3.50 | sorry, forgot to take a pic), 1/2 dozen buffalo wings ($6.25), and a large meat lovers pizza ($23.25).

First of all, the #1 is a good deal.  However, the pizza is very average.  It is interesting to note, that they fold the edge of the crust over, making the pizza look puffier.  Nonetheless, what it really accomplishes is less surface area to put meat & cheese on:  3 Stars.  On the other hand, the salad was surprisingly very good.  The portion was large for the price, the spinach was fresh, and there was a lot of bacon:  4 Stars.  

Thirdly, the wings were so-so.  They weren't bad, but they also weren't spicy, nor were they fried.  Regardless, they had a fair amount of meat:  3 Stars.  Lastly, the meatlovers was average like the individual pizza, but it looked more like a medium vs a large:  3 Stars.

Regarding the ambiance it is typical pizza joint w/ booths and tables.  However, they do serve beer, including locally renowned 805:  3 Stars.  Contrastly, the service was very good.  The young staffers who were probably UCSB co-eds were supah nice, and the food came out quickly:  4 Stars.

Woodstock's is your, I am in the area craving pizza & beer place.  They do a decent job, and the location is ideal, so just go with the flow.  However, if the service was bad, it would have made my TST Two Star 2uesday list.

Great pizza if you don't mind a large portion of "pretentiousness" served with it.

Greeter had to wait for my wife to enter, so she could  present the menu, then bows and waves toward a chalkboard and stands there with an awkward silence.

They have a bar in front of the preparation and pizza oven. With signs that read "You know that song - Lean on me - Well don't" 

What's the point of a bar if you can't lean on it.
There were three empty tables but they had reserved signs on them, nobody offered us seats so we were just standing there awkward AGAIN!! So we just took the pizza to go, which was not our original intent when we went "OUT" for dinner.


It was very good pizza and certainly better than anything I've tried locally and more expensive too, but I doubt I'll be visiting again, its pizza your making, not Haute Cuisine, get over yourselves

Pretty good burgers! We weren't able to decide so we got the 3 sliders and fries. 

The sliders were Mesa burger, montecito and mission burger. Mesa burger was the regular burger, Montecito had the mushrooms and grilled onions and the mission burger had the pico and tortilla strip- kind of like a southwest burger. They are all very tasty and just the right amount. My friend got their regular burger and it looked humongous! The sliders were perfect size. 

Plenty of indoor-outdoor seating. Order first then take a seat.

Oysters for dayzzzz... 

That's all we got, we sat at the bar, came in for oysters and a drink. They serve Modern Times beer here so that was a plus. The oysters were super juicy and briny. Delicious!
