If you make your way to the pier, stop here for drinks and oysters, it'll be a little cheaper than places on the pier.

I'm glad my friend recommended this place as it's in a good area with a lot of things around to do after dinner. 

Make your dinner reservations early if you want to get a seat. We overheard the hostess telling someone it'll be a 2 hour wait. (Seriously?) I guess that's how popular it is on a Saturday night. And it's probably because the food was sooo good! 

The menu is such a fun menu to order from. The entrees and small plates are all meant for sharing as you'll be disappointed if you didn't... portions are on the fancier and smaller side. We ordered: 

-Hamachi crudo
-Brussels sprouts
-Duck confit
-Wagyu flatiron
-Diver Scallops
-Grilled octopus

It all was amazing. Exquisite and unique flavors for a lot of the dishes. My favorite was their Brussels sprouts and the wagyu flatiron and diver scallops. The drinks were also very good and strong. I had the mule and the JP Paloma. Dessert on the other hand was super too weird for me. It was good though but I felt they were too much, like one dessert they put coffee grinds all over... felt like I was eating ash. The other 2 desserts were still very good. 

Service was superb. Our server was really accommodating and cool. I would definitely come  back and try other items if I had the chance! When we left, it was still super packed around 10pm.

Why is Superior so superior you ask? 

Prime location on the streetcar line on the corner of St.Charles Ave and Napoleon Ave. Not riding the streetcar? Let the free valet take care of you as you pull up to the front door- just tip him a couple bucks on your way out. Its worth the vip treatment and convenience. Plus you dont want to waste any more time when youre so close to deliciousness. 
As you walk in, the atmosphere is classic Uptown New Orleans from the tile floors to the long oak bar and ceiling to floor windows. Big bar area consisting of about 6 booths, 6 hi-boy tables and a long bar with ample seating. The tables to the left of the hostess stand have the best streetcar view if thats your thing. Coming for happy hour (everyday 4-6:30) ? Sit anywhere you like, the special is offered throughout the restaurant. 
Happy hour- the happiest of hours- which they have so generously extended to saturday and sunday is awesome. 50 cent raw oysters shucked to order and frozen french 75's (champagne,gin and lemon) and frozen pomegranate mojitos are 2 for 1. So you pay $7 or $8 for a double. Lets all take a moment of silence for the two mentioned drinks. 

They are so tasty and strong! You will be loving life and planning your return visit. Im sure there are plenty of other happy hour drinks but I just couldnt tell you about them. Im in a monogamous relationship with my French 75 at this time. 

Everything we've tried off the menu was good. The fried alligator app and angels on horseback poboy were the standouts. The alligator is tender and flavorful. The poboy is oysters wrapped in bacon then fried and served on soft french bread dressed with tomato, pickle and remoulade. You heard me so make good decisions in your life and order a half or a whole. 
The service has been consistently pleasant and professional. True southern hospitality.  

Side note for Mardi Gras season: They offer a balcony package with drinks and apps upstairs for the major uptown parades. Thurs thru Mardi Gras day their happy hour generosity pauses.

Oak Oven is a precious little place with walls adorned with family photos that make you feel comforted as you sit down. They serve herbed bread and dipping oil as you peruse the menu. I find their wine menu a little disappointing. It's a range of cheapo wine to over priced higher end wines/champagne.  Small beer list but enough variety I'm sure the guests can find something they like. 
My husband had a seasonal soup on our first visit that he still talks about a year later. Kids were happy with their pepperoni pizza choice and even though the crust is soft and thin, the fresh sauce makes up for it.  My husband also enjoys the ny strip served with truffle butter and marscapone mashed potatoes. On our most recent visit, the steak was overlooked and tough so unfortunately he ended up eating a deconstructed version of it that wasn't as good. Thank goodness that wasn't his first time ordering it because he probably wouldn't again.  I've never tried their homemade pastas but one of these times I will, I'm sure they are good.  Their Caesar salad is one of my favs especially topped with fried oysters:)  
Since it is a small place, I also recommend making a reservation.

I had been hearing about Mo's pizza for years. We had a rare visit to the West Bank so we seized the opportunity. 
We ordered a large pepperoni half light sauce thanks to a yelp review that I read standing in line to order. We also ordered an italian salad and 2 cookies. 
The place was about half full and a couple people picking up to go. We didnt have to wait long before our number was called. 
The pizza was huge! It overlapped the pan! I counted 16 slices. We conquered half, thank you very much, and boxed up the rest. 
The salad was ok. Canned olives always dissappoint. 
We thought the cookies were made in house with the way they were wrapped but we were sadly mistaken to read the Pennsylvania made label on the back. 
Back to the pizza, the sauce is on the sweeter side which I like but highly recommend requesting light sauce. We ended up throwing away the half that had the regular sauce portion. 
I enjoyed the pizza and would return if ever in the area again. The prices are decent so I can see how they are a popular place. 
Plus, there is Pac-Man in the front.

Let me tell you about my recent visit to Lilette aka Anniversary dinner. 
We made a reservation for 8:30 on a sat nt after reading about their awesome crab claw with passionfruit butter appetizer. It looked like the perfect place to celebrate and treat ourselves. 
We arrived promptly at 8:30 and were told( when the hostess appeared 5 min later)  that they were basically waiting for a table to get up. That would be understandable if we werent looking at 3 ( 4 top ) tables open and set. When my husband inquired, she said no we have to hold that for at least a 3 or 4 person party. 
I asked if there was anything open in the courtyard and she said sure, if you dont mind, so out we went. She did not walk us out there so we just figured out where to go on our own. 
A server saw us looking at the only open tbl( which was awkwardly placed in the middle of the small courtyard). We decided to sit there since we really had no other option. The server offered to tell the hostess for us which we thought was very nice. He took my husbands drink order and gave me the wine list. 
He never returned. We didnt have food menus so we awkwardly sat and sat and sat.  Then a manager approached our table who was apparently very annoyed. He says he didnt know we were going to sit there and that we have to move to a (now open) 2 person tbl in the corner of the courtyard. He sets down 2 menus at the smaller tbl and walks back inside. 
Now its 9pm and we felt so unwelcomed at this point and still had not received a drink or saw our server again that we decided to leave. 
We passed the server on the way out and he said Sorry I didnt know the hostess didnt approve you sitting out here. Then we pass the hostess and she says sorry for the miscommunication. What? 
    Its just unfortunate that our anniversary had to be ruined by such unnecessary rudeness.

I love poke bowls so naturally I was excited to try a restaurant dedicated to this lovely dish. I studied the menu before my first visit so I would be ready to order when I arrived. I created the bowl of my dreams and it was everything I hoped it would be. So much so that I duplicated my order on my second visit a couple weeks later. 
Their blueberry pomegranate tea is super good. I cant wait for their Metairie Rd location to open because the Magazine St location can be a little stressful to park being on a busy corner thats under major construction. 
I noticed a quaint yard with string lights on my second visit that is accessed by their rear door.  Everyone is very patient and helpful if you happened not to study the menu first too;)

My daughter and I love a good coffee shop so we were anxious to try Perks out when it opened. My daughter even bought Perks coffee flavored chapstick as a preface to our visit. 

Unfortunately, our drive thru experience was rather disappointing. 
I turned rt from Clearview into the drive thru. We informed the employee it was our first time and that we needed a minute to look over the options. Even though no one was in front or behind us, she kept insisting that we order. Totally understand the sense of urgency in a drive thru so no big deal I guess. When I turned the corner to approach the window, I had to back up to get closer because the turn was so tight. The window is so high up that I thought my camry turned into a corvette we were so low. Im not even sure if sportscar drivers could reach. 

I ordered a frozen green tea- it came out half frozen and an orange color that played tricks with my mind. I have never seen an orange colored green tea. My son ordered a frozen strawberry lemonade- it was also only half frozen and had an overly sweet artificial taste. Maybe too much syrup? We both threw our drinks away after forcing ourselves to drink half. My daughter ordered an iced mocha which she said wasnt the best but she did at least finish hers. I also ordered an egg salad sandwich on toast. This held up the process and we sat in the car for a while after paying and getting our drinks. They did apologize for the delay and when I opened the box, it was not worth the $7 I paid. It maybe had 1 1/2 tablespoons worth of saltless egg salad on it. 
The drinks did come with cute straw shapes that I thought was a nice touch and I liked the variety on the menu. 
Im just not sure when we will be ready to give them another try.

Delicious bread, yummy coffee, cute spot, tasty tea, oh and you can have beer too! All this goodness topped off with a very helpful and sweet barista made for a great visit. But come a little later or stay a bit longer because the hours lested on Yelp are incorrect. (I tried to take a picture but the white lettering with white window linens were not my friend.)

Amazing bakery and very reasonably priced!!! We first used them for my fiance's brother's rehearsal dinner. I was in charge of the dessert table so we ordered lemon bars, brownies and two 8inch round cakes with designs on them. Village bakehouse was so easy to work with. Everyone at the party raved about how great the cakes were. 

Fast forward a few months my fiance asked the head baker if they could make a vanilla rose water cake. My family is from Jamaica and we use a lot of rosewater in our desserts. They had never done this before but were willing to try. My fiance took over the rosewater he wanted to be used and left it in their hands. I was so surprised at how delicious it was. I think I must have had close to 10 pieces of cake that weekend. It was sooo delicious and extremely moist. The icing was vanilla buttercream and was to die for. Thank you Village Bakehouse

4 1/2 stars. I heard from a local who grew up in New Orleans that this was the hottest ticket in town for dinner. I lucked out and made reservations for dinner on a Monday evening. Restaurant R'evolution is located at the beginning of the French quarter which was nearby my hotel and within walking distance.

The interior is upscale and even the bar area is beautiful. Restaurant R'evolution is a joint venture of award winning chefs John Folse and Rick Tramonto and put a twist to classic Cajun style entrees. We started off with the beer battered crab beignets with four different four rémoulades - 5 stars, followed Death by gumbo which is a boneless stuffed quail, andouille, oysters and filé rice. Our waiter poured the soup on the quail   table-side and it was quite tasty - 4 stars. All tasted nicely with a bottle of Napa Chardonnay.

For the main entrees I enjoyed the Triptych of Quail  - southern fried, boding stuffed and absinthe glazed - 5 stars. I also sampled the crawfish-stuffed Flounder Napoleon - artichoke and oyster stew and fried crawfish boulettes. I didn't care for the way the crawfish was infused with the flounder although the oyster stew was yummy. For sides we chose the brick oven brussel sprouts with bacon and gruyere potato au gratin (my fave side). For dessert we went for the banana creme pie which was totally different from what I'm accustomed to and unfortunately this was my least liked item of the meal.

Service by our waiter and his entire staff was impeccable and friendly - definitely 5 stars. I was glad I tried R'evolution and if you can't get a reservation in the dinning area, the large bar large does serve small bites and entrees.

After a local hike we wanted a decent lunch that was pug friendly and casual. Cuernavaca is the sister branch of their location in Oxnard and is located in small corner strip center which has private parking. I called about a patio and the worker advised me they had one outside table which wasn't occupied.

The minute I stepped into to place my order I had a good feeling about this place since their clients were - 99% Hispanic. I ordered the El Fortachon plate and a El Pastor and Lengua soft tacos. The plate had a variety of protein including chorizo and was topped with fresh slices of ripe avocado that was a home run. The tacos were also solid and packed with pork and beef tongue that was delish.

I would definetly sugest this eatery and the price was resonable for being in Santa Barbara.

Say what you will about the El Dorado Casino as a whole, but Hidden Pizza is where it's at for late night eats. This is a welcome casual eatery with excellent food and a friendly, efficient staff. 

I'm not sure about their daytime operations, but when we came in at midnight it was stripped down to a couple different offerings on display. I went with the "all meat" option while my friend, a vegetarian, went with cheese. The slices are massive in size and super affordable, so forget all-night buffets or off-strip eatery options. Mine was perfectly heated and tasty, with an especially scrumptious crust. 

Perhaps the biggest inconvenience was funding the place. We scoured two floors and asked an employee and a security guard before finally finding the place. It seems they really want stay hidden, either for mystique or marketing purposes!

This spot was a home away from home for me in Nashville and made me wonder just what other yelpers were complaining about. Maybe the food? As far as the incredible music, layout and drinks are concerned, this is one of my favorite bars in the Broadway area. 

I, like many, had no intention of popping in until I heard some classic country tunes emanating through their large, open-air windows and played expertly by a quartet midday on a Monday morning. I walked in, sat at the bar directly across from the stage, ordered up a beer (it was 5 o'clock somewhere) and gave the band a deeper listen. Every tune they played was incredible. I ended up sitting and drinking through their entire set. My only regret is that I didn't catch their name. 

You see the name "Johnny Cash" and you immediately think it's a gimmick or some place more touristy. In reality, if you like classic country and good musicianship and are tired of the hot mess that is Kid Rock's bar a block away, this is your spot.

Here's why ACME is better than most of the Broadway hangouts: location, location, location. You'll find most visitors want to be a couple blocks up where the action is, but honestly, the view from this spacious upstairs deck is unbelievable and the best location on the strip!

My friend, a local who knows all the best spots, brought me here. It was a rainy Sunday night and there wasn't a lot going on besides football games, so we had a perfect opportunity to avoid the crowd and soak in the space. 

There's a big downstairs where folks come to eat. I didn't try the food but I wasn't there for that. Ride the elevator to the top floor and you'll step out onto an extremely large deck. Drink in hand, you can admire both views of the river, the Titans stadium, the pedestrian bridge and all the action on Broadway. Just like anywhere, we met plenty of nice folks who were very welcoming. 

Yes, it's downtown. Yes, it's overpriced. But when comparing apples to oranges, this is one of the sweetest in the bunch.

Party Fowl was my home away from home on a recent trip to Nashville. That's because they make it easy to enjoy the place, from the welcoming atmosphere to the food to the bar that is perfect for sports viewing. 

It being a Sunday, my buddy and I needed both a comfort food lunch and a place to catch a couple games and escape the torrential rain outside. Party Fowl was close to downtown and checked all those boxes. We bellied up, ordered a couple local beers and some hot chicken sandwiches. 

I'm from California and expected a version of the hot chicken I get there. This was ten times better and made me realize the "Nashville" in Nashville hot chicken is there for a reason. The chicken was moist yet crispy on the outside and packed both flavor and heat. Along with the requisite pickles, it was the perfect ball game food. 

Party Fowl checks all the boxes if you want an experience like ours, plus they serve a broad array of breakfasts. Really, what more could you ask for?

If you're looking for a surefire formula for culinary success, check out Saint Stephen. From the upscale eats to the exemplary service, they know the meaning of a memorable dining experience. I thank my friend, a local, for bringing me in. Otherwise I would have never discovered this place!

We sat at the bar on a quiet Tuesday evening and basically got a private meal. The chefs were friendly and welcomed us to try anything on the menu. The hostess, Ashley, was also incredibly sweet and made us feel right at home. 

It's a revolving menu with too many amazing dishes to recall, but I do remember the pork belly (with sweet potato pave, herb salad and blood orange lacquer) and a roasted purple potato dish being the two standouts. Really, you can't go wrong with anything on the menu, especially if you pair it with a local beer on tap or one of their expertly crafted cocktails. 

It's a modern, spacious aesthetic that feels homey at the same time. I won't hesitate to return next time I'm in Nashville!

If you think Broadway is just loud honky tonk bars, think again. This hidden gem of a restaurant is smack dab in the middle of all the action yet sports a chill, welcoming vibe and some damn amazing late night eats.

We stumbled in (not completely sober, I will admit) as many probably do - straight from a night at the bars. The first advantage was this spot is open late. The second was that we were able to sit at the bar and order food directly from the friendly bartenders. Naturally, I went with the prime rib because I've had my share of good prime ribs, but never one from Nashville. The cut and the cook were absolutely perfect, not too fatty and paired with tasty greens and mashed potatoes. It was honestly one of the better prime ribs I've ever tasted. 

The bar itself was a handsome horseshoe style where you can easily get the attention of the bartender and watch the game. I enjoyed their gin and tonics. It all equals a return visit next time I'm in town!

I begrudgingly have to agree with most previous reviewers. The 6-floor concept is very cool and on the surface this is basically a place that should appeal to everyone. My food, unfortunately, was mediocre. 

I was looking for a breakfast option while exploring downtown and The Diner was about the closest place I could find to my hotel. I proceeded straight to the top floor (for the views, naturally) and took a seat at the bar. The server was nice enough in a sort of no-nonsense sort of way. I went with the breakfast burrito. 

The burrito technically had everything you'd want, from eggs to bacon, but the flavor wasn't there. There was a lot of tortilla to get through. The potatoes were bland and slightly undercooked. And the small container of prepackaged, unappetizing salsa made it feel less like something you'd eat there than a pre-made to-go meal. 

The view, on the other hand, is indeed amazing, so my suggestion is to come here for drinks and check out the sights. There aren't a lot of public places downtown with a view this high or expansive.

I'm from Sacramento, which also has a claim to fame in Johnny Cash in that his most famous album was recorded at Folsom Prison. So naturally I wanted to see what Nashville was doing to honor him. As it turns out, a lot. 

The museum tour is not cheap. It's 20-something bucks and you have to gamble as to what you are about to see, but in the end I found it worth it. There are basically two different timelines that follow his life with a good amount of memorabilia. All tastefully put together. If you are already a big fan of the Man in Black, this tour will satisfy you. If not, you may find it a waste of time or money. 

The store is your typical museum store with a lot of expensive JC items, from t-shirts to album reprints to little statues and everything in between. Basically a lot of stuff you never thought you actually needed. Again, this is a place for fans and casual visitors should stick to just perusing the shop.

Do you love Kid Rock? You better love him with a passion. Because that is really the only reason I see to check out this joint vs. so many other less-crowded and more musically diverse spots on the Broadway strip. As far as I'm concerned, Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk was a big honkin' mess. 

I'd walked by the place twice already while exploring the rest of the street and curiosity got the best of me. The place was always packed, even on a Monday afternoon, which is fine but means longer wait times. Walking in, I was immediately struck to see many patrons in Kid Rock hats, Kid Rock memorabilia everywhere, and a cover band playing the exact same Kid Rock song ("All Summer Long") that another band played earlier that morning and another band played as I walked by the night before. Apparently it's the song  Kid Rock bar patrons come to Nashville for, as people can't seem to get enough. 

After a long wait at the host stand, and then unsuccessfully trying to communicate I wanted a seat and eventually yelling "Bar!" because it was so loud, I ventured in looking for a place to sit. Nothing was available so I stood at the downstairs bar. I was ignored for so long that I finally left. 

If only the Johnny Cash bar halfway down the block, with incredible musicians playing well-crafted classic country songs, had half as many patrons. A guy can always dream.

As far as I'm concerned, Jason Aldean's is the best of all the Broadways bars because it captures the concept better than any competitor. The place is well-designed, spacious, perfect for live music and sports maybe the best upstairs deck for viewing the street below. 

Most people automatically head straight to the second floor. This is a massive room in which they have a big stage which is always occupied by a top quality band, a massive horseshoe bar and tons of tables which could also be cleared out for dancing. There's another floor above it with a little shop, then the top floor, where there is yet another big stage and bar and the deck. The deck is more spacious than most with a lot of seating and centrally-located views of the town. 

Like any bar on Broadway, expect pricey drinks. The ones I got here after two visits were at least well-made with a heavy pour and the bartenders were nice. But really, who is coming for the quality of the drinks. The music and the scenery alone are what drove me in the door.

It's a fancy Habit with table service and twice the price. If the service was better and the food was at a higher level maybe, but as it was I doubt that we'll be regulars. Simple requests were forgotten as the servers were congregating and talking rather than paying attention to the floor. 

The place does look nice though.

Wow, this place is absolutely adorable.  Whoever decorated it- kudos.  We were lured in by their gorgeous display of perfectly decorated cupcakes in beautiful glass cabinet, like little treasures.  

I got a cookies and cream cupcake, which set me back a somewhat shocking $4.  I think that's the highest I've paid for a cupcake in the city- and it was only about half the size of the generous-portioned Brown Betty cupcakes for $3.  The cupcake looked pretty basic, but maybe there was more to it, maybe some interesting flavor combinations like at Betty's Speakeasy... 

Now, keep in mind, it's RARE that I meet a cupcake that I don't like.  I love 'em.  Unfortunately my cupcake from Philly Cupcake was incredibly dry- like it was more than a few days old.  The icing was basic buttercream icing with cookie crumbs in it, and the cake was just a regular chocolate.  I kind of feel duped for paying $4 for something I could probably make better myself.  My friend got their red velvet cupcake and it was the same.  Totally dry and I couldn't really taste the cream cheese in the icing. Luckily hers was only $3, but that's still more than we should have paid for the quality.

I will say, however that another friend of mine got the gluten-free Chocolate Coma or something and it was really yummy.  The cake was moist and not too sugary sweet.  The icing was really good (although again, nothing too special) and it was kind of dipped in chocolate to make a crispy chocolate shell on top.  Maybe they should stick to denser flourless cakes for now.

God, I want to love this place.  It's so pretty, it's in a great location and everyone seemed really nice and helpful.  But I've had cheaper, more complex flavors with more exotic ingredients at a number of other cupcake places in town.  Their actual cupcakes better catch up to the adorable decor- cause I'd rather go to the ugliest storefront you got if they have an excellent cupcake.  For now right I'll stick to gaze into their cute little window.

I wish I saw this forever ago. How professional...yes my husband and friends were members so I used their guest pass. I also do give out good reviews and I prefer to. My karma is better for reporting the truth. If anything I said was false why hide behind a message? Have the men's locker rooms been done yet? Or is the same guy still pissing in them all trying to get your attention??  Unfortunately, yes. very true. I'm far from a princess thank you...I believe that's your crew of ladies there. Handed down that property...no wonder marketing is great. yet still empty businesses all over. And employee turnover?? Just talk to the members. Keep it up ladies!! My one review is doing nothing compared to what you are doing yourselves!

This was the first stop on our night out in St. Louis. We stopped by another bar called Lush and it was empty. We asked the valet guys at Lush "where do all the fun people go? not the posers". They suggested we go to Lucas Park Grille. Good suggestion.

They had some kind of a special on sparkling wine and we ended up ordering bottle service. Our server Tabitha was awesome. She came back frequently to fill our glasses and chatted with us. We asked her to suggest an appetizer and she recommended the mini sliders made with Kobe beef. Excellent suggestion. The mini-sliders came with sweet potato fries. Delicious!!

We went back the next day for lunch. I ordered the smoked chicken sandwich with sun dried tomatoes. My partner got the prime burger and our friends got a tilapia blt and the burger. All dishes came with fries sprinkled with shaved parmesan cheese. Fabulous. 

The food is good. The only inconsistency was the fries. My friend's fries were cold and tasted stale. Our fries were fine. 

The crowd is very typical for an upscale restaurant minus the diversity. I was the only colored person on premises on both days. it doesn't matter to me, just an observation. There was a sea of blond hairdos. 

The outside seating area, although not open, looks beautiful. I bet it will be a nice place to sit and have a drink once the weather gets warm. 

The service on both days was impeccable. Both our servers were cheerful, pleasant, and professional. Overall, a fun place to eat and drink with friends.

The man and I have an agreement that we have to fly out for dinner at least once a month. This way nobody gets hurt :) We picked Nashville for our monthly dinner date out of Chicago. We heard about City House from a friend and decided to have Saturday night dinner at the restaurant. Imagine my surprise when the earliest reservation I could get was 9pm, that was a sign of popularity.

The restaurant looks like a dilapidated house on the outside, but modern and sharp on the inside. It is an old house converted in to a restaurant. There is a bar area near the entrance, you then walk in to a cavernous living room with open kitchen, and head up the stairs to a more intimate area with 4 tables in each room. The ambiance was energetic even with only 4 tables in our room.

We started off with drinks. I ordered the Moose - Cynar, House-Infused Lemon Vodka, Peach Bitters, and Bitter Lemon Soda. The man ordered the Junior - Death's Door White Whiskey, Creme de Violette, Dr. Enuf, and Lemon. Two perfect drinks that set the stage for our meal. We started our meal with the octopus: roasted octopus, october beans, chow chow, and parsley. Two long tentacles of octopus roasted with a very light breading on some areas, served atop beans. Pure bliss. it is probably the best innovative octopus dish I have eaten lately. The meal started off on a 5 star note already. 

Since I like variety, just like my men, I convinced the man we should do tapas style and order different appetizers and share an entree. Next, we ordered the eggplant - Eggplant Caponata, Tomato, Olives, Peanuts & Raisins, and Pecorino. Sensing that we are in an Italian restaurant, we ordered a cured meat appetizer - House Cured Bresaola, Sliced Tomato, Sea Salt, Pepper, and Parmigiano. Both appetizers were quite delightful. The earthy flavor of roasted eggplant was perfectly balanced by peanuts, tomatoes and olives. The bresaola had a nice kick to it and the tomatoes provided the perfect accompaniment. 

For an entree we shared the anchovy pizza - Anchovy, Mozzarella, Tomato, Garlic, Chilies, and Oregano. Sounds very simple, but it was impressively delectable. Thin crust pizza with just the right amount of anchovies (one full anchovy per slice) made with fresh mozzarella. It was a definite winner. The pizza is big enough to share for two. We also ordered a side of roasted okra to go along with the pizza. It completed our winning entree section.

By this time I was in the mood for a Vesper. Their cocktail menu didn't have one and the bartender did not know what a Vesper is, but after I told our waiter what goes in a Vesper, the bartender made the perfect one. Impressive. The man decided to go with wine, he liked his Chardonnay.

Since we both are dessert fiends, we decided to order dessert. Part of me was hoping that nothing on the dessert menu would interest me, so I don't have to ingest any more calories, but my wishing failed once I saw the buttermilk pannacotta with peach preserves. The man ordered a caramel cake. We both inhaled our dessert before you could count to ten, they were that good. 

Service was stellar, we never felt rushed or intruded. Chris allowed us the right amount of privacy while checking on us at regular intervals. We stayed for almost 2 hours eating and drinking without feeling rushed at any point. 

Who knew Nashville would deliver when it comes to incredible food? That's the beauty of America, you go to a town expecting country music and southern food and you are surprised/ impressed with delectable cuisine.  

Thank you City House for making our date night lovely. We will definitely return.

Finch & Fork really is a cool place to grab a bite to eat.

Details:

Lunch on Friday, June 27th with my hubby on son.  We stopped on our way back to L.A. from the Central Coast.  It was showing a rating of 4 1/2 stars and all the photos looked pretty darn good.

Food:  4/5 Stars

My hubby and I decided to split the F&F Burger ($15) which comes with fries.   They gladly accomodated us with our request to change the regular fries for garlic and herb fries.  We also got a larger portion of fries to split for a minimal charge.  We both loved the burger and fries.  My son ordered the special for Fridays which was the Crispy Market Fish Sandwich ($15).  He devoured that in record time.

Atmosphere:  4/5 Stars

I really liked the decor and this restaurant is on the bottom floor of the Canary Hotel which is just beautiful.  The booth that we were seated at was very comfortable and I really liked the interior.    To get to the restrooms you have to go downstairs into the hotel and I loved all the vibrant colors.  Apparently, the hotel has a roof top pool and they allow dogs who get beds and other little treats.

Service:  4/5 Stars

Our server was quick to bring us water, take our order, bring our lunch and check promptly.  The hostess was quick to seat us as well.

Parking:  4/5 Stars

We parked in the structure to the east of the hotel and had free parking for less than two hours I believe.

Misc Info:

It is right in the middle of Downtown Santa Barbara and close to lots of shopping and about 11 blocks from the harbor.

Recommendation:

If I am passing through or staying in Santa Barbara again I would definitely come back to Finch & Fork.

YUMMY GERMAN FOOD & BEER
==========================

We met my son and his girlfriend at The Rathskeller for lunch on the way to the Indy Int'l Airport.

If you are trying to avoid carbs turn and run the other way because you will veer off your path of avoiding carbs with their warm pretzels.

My son ordered one of their German specialties and he loved that.  I can't remember what my husband ordered, but he like that.  I was in hog heaven with a big bowl of their French onion soup.  It paired perfectly with one of their beers on tap and their fresh pretzel.  The pretzel was so good I ordered another one to go for my flight home.

You need to check this place out if you are in Indy.   Good place to go before your flight if you want to avoid airport food.

I doubted I could find flavorful pho in New Orleans, but boy was I wrong. The beef pho broth is 10x richer and more savory than any I've tried in the San Francisco Bay Area. Really hit the spot after a week of eating nothing but biscuits, gumbo, and blood marys.

The owner, Lilly, was so kind to us, even ordering us a cab so that we'd make it to our next engagement on time. 

Clean bathrooms.

Would come here again in a heartbeat!

Id like to leave them a good review but my experience was horrible. 
I made Valentines Day reservations 1 1/2 months in advance. 
I was excited to try this place after seeing it featured in Creative Loafing. Upon our arrival at 8:20 i was asked if it was for the Main Dining area or the Ballroom. I asked which is nicer and i was told the Ball Room by several employees. This wasnt an option when making the reservation since they didnt anticipate opening up the Ballroom for dining until after i made my reservation. They said they could not seat us there immediately and to give them 30 minutes to get us a table. 
we watched the Olympics for 40 mins. i went back to the hostess stand to ask about our table. I was told sorry for the wait but we have your table ready. They attempted to seat us at the main dining room. we specifically waited to get in the ballroom. i worked in the industry before so i was pretty cool about it. they said sorry for the mix up and they will be right with us.
another 20 mins go by (reservation was 830pm its now 930pm) and the manager on duty Kevin comes to tell us that he is sorry but they cannot seat us at all. he said he was sorry and that if there is anything he can do to contact him. 
now being in the industry myself before i was expecting him to say "hey its our fault we weren't prepared tonight, you already paid for your drinks at that bar, so please atleast let me comp half your meal, or if you come back we can give you a great dining experience at our expense" 
as a customer i think its awkward to ask for any type of comp. so i gave him back his card and said sorry but we will never be here again. 
seeing as i made the reservaton well in advance i would hope it would take precedence over walk in's.

New Year's Day, tried a place with noodles for 'long life' celebration, so found an excellent and newer Asian restaurant in the Loop!  2:00p on a holiday we had a 15 minute wait, but it was worth it!  Wide menu variety having freshly made dumplings, wontons, noodle dishes, and more.  Plenty of veggie or meat/seafood options, so think you'll find something to enjoy (or try) if you are a fan of Asian cooking.  A solid 4.0+ experience for me with friendly and courteous servers, and you can eat here for ~$10pp!  Ambience was casual, bright and a nice diverse clientele with lots of local students.

Ordered 2 starters, pan fried handmade dumplings and the Green Onion pancakes.  Dumplings were fantastic, served with a soy chili sauce - good with or without sauce.  The Onion pancakes were just like I remember at home, but I think needed more green onions to enhance the dish even more.

Shared a few entrees, the Shredded Pork in Garlic chili sauce, the sauteed Green beans, Hand-cut noodles with beef stew, bok choy and pickled veggies, and a Hand-shaved noodle with Chicken and veggies.  Plenty to share 'family style', we enjoyed all of them.  Would only mention the shredded pork had a nice spicy kick with a tinge of sweetness, so recommend to eat with a bowl of steamed white rice! 

This is definitely a go-to place for fresh homemade dumplings and noodles. ENJOY!!!

Very good food menu with friendly, efficient service! Think it was louder tonight with live music (on Saturday 730p); and ambience was casual, relaxed but quite dim.  For sports fans, they have several TVs around the bar/restaurant but not so many it overtakes the atmosphere.   

My first try here, enjoyed sharing the fried green beans appetizer.  Basket was served hot with 2 dip sauces; liked the aioli but my favorite was the wasabi dip - really nice flavor if you like a little hot spicy kick!  Also tried the Gumbo soup which was heavy with smoked sausage, shrimp, large diced veggies and a flavorful gumbo taste.

For dinner, shared a Caesar salad that had tasty, creamy dressing and The Brick sandwich, tender roast beef slices with jalapeño cheese plus I added grilled onions and mushrooms on grilled Texas toast - enjoyed both!  The fries were just OK (had much better) so I'd suggest ordering Coleslaw, chips or a different veggie side next time.

Overall solid experience for a quick casual meal out, and there are plenty of other dinner and menu selections to choose, so I'd go back and try again.  Enjoy!

Shack is one of my morning starter favorites, a go-to breakfast/brunch/lunch spot for me!  Love the relaxed atmosphere, but gets super busy on weekends so expect a wait.  Has a wide, creative menu selection with large portion size meals will suit guests of all ages - and believe me, you won't leave hungry!

Today, ordered the Kitchen Sink skillet, yummy perfect if wanting a smorgasbord!  Diced cut Ham, Sausage, Bacon grilled with freshly cut mushrooms, green peppers and onions atop crisp hash browns with 2 eggs your way!  Loved it!  Had a freshly made biscuit and side of fresh fruit as well.

In the past, have enjoyed Hash-n-Eggs, Mrs. Denver omelette and their large blueberry pancake.  Definitely enough for sharing or a doggy box, but everything was flavorful and filling.  Their 'benedict' options are also really good, and I like the salmon and eggs too, as well as the excellent bacon!

Service was friendly, and food came out quickly, hot off the grill and just as ordered!

Overall experience was great, and if I could, I'd eat here every week!  Also want to mention prices are moderate-high for breakfast, so expect to pay $10-15 for a meal without beverages. But if you like big breakfasts, casual eatery with full bar or fun gathering spot for a group, don't miss this place, ENJOY!!! ...and remember to autograph your name on a wall to know you've been there!

Read all of the reviews and you'll see that the food is really good, the restaurant is really small, and the owner is a jerk. Their website says "ask for our daily specials" with the phone number below. Just don't call and ask the owner. I called and asked what their special was today and he asked "what do you want". He then hung up on me when I ask if they had chicken parmesan. I called back thinking we may have gotten disconnected, but when I politely asked what his recommendations were he tells me "you're bothering me" and hung up again. I've only had their tiramisu once and it was really good.

I visited the new Trader Joe's a week after the grand opening and found it to be way less crowded than anticipated. I went around 9 am on a Saturday and around noon on a Friday. According to staff, mornings are the best time to go to avoid the crowds. 

TJs is much smaller than a typical grocery store, so don't come here expecting an abundance of variety. Rather, you will mostly find unique Trader Joe's brand items that you'd be hard pressed to find elsewhere at these prices. Tons of organic and natural products, as well as a solid selection of gluten free items.

I find that the funnest part of Trader Joes is discovering new products every time you go as well as swapping recommendations with other TJs shoppers. 

Some of my favorite items include:
- Cookie butter (and cookie butter swirl -- which is mixed with trader joes take on Nutella!)
- edamame hummus
- blue cheese pecan dip
- spinach and kale Greek yogurt dip
- peanut butter pretzels
- any of their chocolate covered nuts
- balsamic glaze
- quinoa and black bean tortilla chips
- roasted coconut chips
- chocolate covered potato chips (sinful!)
- frozen mango
- Shredded Brussels sprouts
- raw almond butter (much cheaper than anywhere else)
- frozen falafel 
- frozen chile rellenos
- vanilla coconut milk (boxed in refrigerated section)
- light coconut milk (canned)

They have an awesome cheese section and it's hard not to buy all of it. You can find great deals on nuts, dried fruit, and their frozen entrees. Flowers are really cheap too. 

Beware of the amazing chocolates they strategically place at the check outs! The cookie butter dark chocolate bar is out of this world.

Staff is super friendly and proud of the brand and the products. Both times I've visited they tipped me off to some of their favorite items. 

Downside: Yes, parking sucks. The store layout is a little tight but shoppers seemed to do a good job navigating the aisles in an orderly fashion.

I drive by here all the time and had no idea it was here until a friend suggested it for lunch. The restaurant occupies one of 4 spaces in a small two story plaza next to Hank's BBQ on Dale Mabry. You'll be surprised at how nice it is inside. 

According to the menu, they specialize in arepas so that's what I went with. The have quite a selection of arepas stuffed with different meats and veggies. I ordered one stuffed with chorizo, chicken, steak and avocado. The melty cheese inside of it was delicious (Does anyone know what kind of cheese this is? Almost like a fresh mozzarella as far as texture). It was so good (the grilled meats are excellent!) and I swear there was an entire avocado tree inside. I have nothing but love for a restaurant that errs on the side of too much avocado. There was so much deliciousness stuffed into the arepa that it was kind of hard to eat. I had to attack it with a knife and fork but wish I had been able to pick it up and eat it like a sandwich. When I go back I will probably try one with less ingredients in it for that reason. 

My friend ordered a beef burger which is actually a piece of steak, not ground beef. Score!

HUGE portions here, too. 

It takes a long time for the food to come out (you can be sure it's all made to order!), so definitely not a good place if you're in a rush.

This place is a foodie's paradise. The attention to detail here is nothing less than you'd expect from the Bern's restaurant family. 

I visited Haven the first week it opened and was impressed by how well things were already running. Our server told us the staff had already been employed for 1.5 months before they opened, so I guess that explains how everything was already going so smooth.

They have done a really nice job with the renovation from Side Bern's. There is a mix of your standard tables and booths, plus more casual seating that encourages people to share food and drinks and just hang out. The patio area is gorgeous. There are no "regular" tables out there, it is more of a lounge type of atmosphere. From what I could tell the left side of the restaurant is more upscale/traditional and the right side is more casual. 

Now on to the food...

CHEESE + CHARCUTERIE
While I can appreciate that they have around 60 cheeses to choose from, I was a little overwhelmed by the chore of selecting a few cheeses to start with. The cheese selection is organized by strength (mild, medium, strong, blue), type (cow, goat, sheep) and country. I do wish they also included just slightly more info about each cheese, especially regarding the texture. While some are no brainers for what texture the cheese would be (ex. brie), it was unclear what the texture was like for the many cheeses we were unfamiliar with. As you can imagine, trying to go through 60 cheeses with your server would be a little ridiculous. There is a chef's suggested cheeses of about 10 (even that felt overwhelming though!). Our server did recommend the 1-year and 5-year goudas, which ended up being the best of what we tried. Each cheese is just $5 for an ample portion. 

The charcuterie selection is less overwhelming, with about 10 items to choose from. The duck summer sausage is made in house and outstanding. I enjoyed the extra flourishes served with our cheese/charcuterie board, such as pickled cauliflower and house made mustard and horseradish. 

SMALL PLATES
According to our server, the menu will be changing often but they will keep a lot of the same types of dishes on it. For example, the mac and cheese is probably going to be different each time you dine here, but there will always be mac and cheese on the menu. While they consider their portions to be small plates, I found them large enough to be enjoyed as an entrée on their own. When you consider most plates cost $12 - $20 dollars, this is very reasonable (exception: the $54 Delmonico). Of course, I think the fun in a place like this is sharing multiple things. 

The two best things I tried:
1) Cobia Carbonara -- I still can't believe how good this was. Packed with umami flavor. The cobia was completely unnecessary, although tasty. It was all about the pasta, sauce and egg yolk for me. 

2) Bone Marrow and Skirt Steak -- This is a generous serving of bone marrow and sliced skirt steak. You can eat each piece on its own, but I recommend building your own meat bruschetta using the toasted bread served on the side. Spread some bone marrow on the bread, top it with steak, and then drizzle some of the Malbec sauce on top. Unreal. How was this only $18?

DESSERT
The Bananas Foster is ridiculous. I'm not even sure how to describe it since it is most definitely not what comes to mind when I hear Bananas Foster. All of the flavors of Bananas Foster, but in a totally different form. Most of the desserts were just $9, which is much lower than you'd find in most upscale restaurants, even in this area. 

SERVICE
Our server just so happened to be a trained chef, so having her guide us through the menu was extremely helpful. The sommelier was also great and brought us a taste of the wine he recommended before we made our choice. They have a lot of wines by the glass in addition to the extensive bottles you'd expect from Bern's, so the sommelier's guidance can make it feel less daunting. 

PRICE
I'm a little surprised another reviewer complained about the price here. Anyone coming to a Bern's restaurant and expecting an Outback price needs to get a reality check. A ridiculous amount of food for two people was about $200 and that included a decent amount of cheese and charcuterie, 4 small plates, two glasses of wine, a $50 bottle of wine, and two desserts. You could easily eat here for much less and still leave satisfied. Since it was my first time I kind of overdid it trying a lot of the menu, so I think this price doesn't reflect the average dining experience here.

With much anticipation the Tiki docks Is open! They have more than exceeded my expectations. The atmosphere is like a margaritaville with a local vibe. They are still working out being a new establishment but the service made it seem like they have been working together for years.

As someone who was a server/bartender/manager in the restaurant business, and  part time critique in the hospitality  industry, I have come across a situation at "Tony's Place" that has been a FIRST in my entire experience. 

A dear friend and I met for drinks and appetizers, to catch up. We asked our server how the mixed drinks were here, he said great, we ordered double mojitos (after he let us know they are very good here). When we got them, they were served in large white wine glasses, but we decided to let it go since we did see mint floating in them and decided to give it a go. There was NO flavor except for rum (the mint was not muddled to release the mint flavor and there was no simple syrup). 

We really tried to deal with the drink, even added 3 sugar packets, which did nothing since sugar does not dissolve in ice cold drinks. We let our server know that they were not good, and asked for a white wine and tomato juice/vodka to be safe.

WHAT HAPPENED NEXT WAS SHOCKING AND EMBARRASSING!!!

5 minutes later the server comes back with the mojitos!!??!! He said that we need to try them again, since we ordered doubles they can't replace our drinks, and the bartenders poured half of the mojito out and poured triple sec and sprite - WHAT?? We were just told that our mojito that we no longer was partially replaced with 2 ingredients that DO NOT belong in a mojito. We tried it to be courteous (since we were still in shock) and we still obviously did not want it. The server stated that he needs to get the manager. 

In the mean time, the bartender starts talking to us from across the room, asking us how we like the "improved" concoction, which at that time I let him know that the first one was not a mojito, and the second was a complete insult - to which the bartender states "you don't know a mojito then". WOW. 

The manager comes over, and at first he basically told us since we first ordered doubles we had to pay for them, to this I replied with letting him know how his bartenders just poured out half of it, replaced it with soda, and sent it back to us. Thankfully his customer service kicked in, he spoke with the bartender, we not only didn't pay for the 'faux-hitos" but he also bought us the new round of drinks. 

After my friend and I left, we ran into a few people outside that asked us why we were leaving (joking around), to which I stated don't order mixed drinks - to which one of the gentlemen stated "The bartenders are not that great, especially not the woman bartender, she is rude and tried to "fluff" drinks". 

It's a shame, but we will not be coming back here.

The short version: The owner is disingenuous and a liar. He treated our party with no respect, no concern for our experience, and showed us the ugly side of philadelphia. He needs to learn some customer service skills, and care more about his customers.

The long version (still condensed): We had reservations for 8 for 6pm, that kept getting pushed back and we ended up showing up at 5:45. Half our party was running late. They seated our initial 4 anyways, and only came around the table to fill water and ask us where the rest of our party was. 

Once we ordered some apps, they finally brought us some bread and asked us about drink orders.

We were further pressured to order our meals - and finally did before the rest of our group arrived. They were about 45 minutes late, and ordered quickly. 

At just before 8pm we were asked if we wanted dessert or coffee and we declined. We were given the check. We asked about splitting and were told we could use 4 cards equally, which was fine with us. A minute later the owner came over and said the credit card system was down, and they could only accept cash. He pointed us to an ATM across the street. A number of us from the group walked over to get cash, and another asked about writing a check which the owner said was fine. When we came back from getting cash the others in our group said they saw other customers paying with credit cards. We asked the owner about this and he got hostile quickly saying we had been in his restaurant for 4 hours, and half our party was very late, and that we must pay cash! A couple of the guys in our group were not happy with this and argued with him, and it got heated and the owner yelled and made it clear he lied about the credit cards being down and that paying cash was his way of getting back at us. He was completely unprofessional.

Before a fight could break out, we left cash to cover the tab and got out of there. Never have I felt so badly about spending money (it was not cheap either), on a dining experience. I could never recommend anyone visit this restaurant as long as it is owned by the current person.

I was really looking forward to this based on the reviews, but the service was really poor. Servers didn't seem to know what food went to what table and on more than one occasion were auctioning off plates to tables by calling out the name of the dish. Our waitress did just about everything she could to suck the joy out of this culinary experience, and had to be reminded to bring items we ordered multiple times. One member of our party ordered a half bottle of wine. She was brought one glass. When we pointed this out to the server, she returned with a second glass. However, the half bottle was still on the bill at the end of the meal. The server also had to be asked to bring a clean glass after we were served one with several flying bugs in it. As a result, out of the 3 people in our party, 2 chose not to tip and I was one of them. The other member of our party left a $12 tip out of guilt. 

Imagine my surprise when I looked at my credit card statement and found $12 added to the total I charged. It took my bank interceding to rectify this. A lot of restaurants will place a hold of anywhere from 8-10% on the initial charge, and it falls off later once the charge goes through. This was not that-- this was extra tip being added by the restaurant that I did not authorize. And since we were only 3 people, it wasn't a gratuity added for a large party. It was just fraud.  Make sure you check your bill carefully after dining here.

I am not a vegetarian in any way, but I enjoyed my meal. I ordered the tacos with the mushrooms and cheese sauce. My friend got the curried vegetables. We finished off with a maca smoothie, lemon cookie, and brownie.

My favorite selections were the tacos and the lemon cookie. The tacos were two heaping, flavorful tacos that were perfectly spiced and piled with delicious toppings. The cookie was dense yet had a light, lemony taste. I left feeling satisfied that I had eaten delicious food that was probably better for me than my usual fare.

If it weren't 100 degrees outside, it would have been nice to go enjoy the patio seating.

Service was warm and efficient. I'll be back. Next time I'll be tempted to get the tacos again, but I want to try something new.

You will die with regrets if you're in the city and choose not to stop by here. I don't care how far you have to go, because if I got here on foot under what felt like 110F, then I have faith in you too my friend.

SERVICE

ENVIRONMENT

* Refreshing and brighter lit seating in the back

FOOD (menu)
* Something for everyone [2]

OVERALL
Cafe La Maude is a one of a kind breakfast joint! Tucked away a little distance from all your typical Philly tourist attraction sites. But like I said earlier, it's worth the travel. Because if I could, I would maximize every criteria for a review. 

Breakfast is the most important meal of the day, so make it worth it with a trip and splendid dining experience here!!

[1] The owner does a much better job than any teacher/professor I've had at remembering your name and face, regardless of how many people there are waiting for a seat. Even if the line goes on to the other side of the street, he will do whatever it takes to hunt you down and get you that seat. They do a fabulous job of getting customers seated, served, and out for the next customer, and craving for more in a heartbeat, without the slightest bit of pressure to rush.
