Every order was the definition of a perfect breakfast; included carbs, proteins, veggies, fruits, etc., which so many breakfast places tend to forget and just load you up with potatoes. Huge fan of the exotic menu that differentiates it from other typical breakfast joints.

[3] Prices run on average of $15-16. Worth every bit  for the amount of food you're getting, for the quality, and for the photogenic food presentation.

[4] Avocado spread, mascarpone cream cheese & creme fraiche, smoked salmon, tomatoes, cucumbers, radish, arugula, chives, onion, and capers; served on pumpernickel bread; with a side of potatoes & a sunny side up egg

[5] This does not receive nearly as much hype as it should, and that's coming from someone who's a picky salmon eater. Nothing all too overpowering. Perfect balance of everything on your nice and chewy bread..mmm...yum~ And you also get your fair share of egg porn.

Nice stop if you're visiting Philly. A great location in Chinatown with a nice lounge space in the back and with a large menu of options for everyone, even those who are lactose intolerant. I had the Red Bean Matcha ($4) special drink which was satisfying although difficult to reach all the red bean and tapioca because of the mountain of ice on top. Do check out if you're in the area and need some hydration.

Cajun boil,
Don't come in a foil.
No need to toil,
Don't let your appetite be spoiled.

Okay, so I suck at poetry but you want to know a place that will totally rock your seafood socks off?!  Look no further than Storming Crab! As a new addition to the Kirkwood restaurant scene, this place does not disappoint.

We came in closer to 6pm tonight, we were immediately seated and was assigned a strange yet attentive waitress to give us the DL of this place.  We ended up ordering the #2 Cajun boil dinner ($48.99) which came with 1 lb crab, 1 lb shrimp, 1 lb clam with your choice of seasoning and spice level and some potatoes and sausages.  The whole boil was enough for 2 hungry people. Then to our surprise, came the seafood bread slices which were absolutely delicious. It was 2 slices of what I have come to know as garlic bread but topped with melted cheese and fresh seafood spread. It was absolutely delicious and you can even order them as an appetizer! We ordered our meal with the Cajun classic seasoning at hot spicy level and ooooohhhhh my Loooooorrrrd... It was finger-licking delicious! I mean, I literally licked my fingers to savor the fantastic taste of the seasoning we have chosen.

The boil turned out delicious. I am actually hungry thinking about it now. The service was good but our waitress was a bit strange.  She was attentive though and helpful even if she seemed a little strange. She kept explaining things that were not at all necessary and was a little anxious almost. Nevertheless, I completely enjoyed our visit and would definitely be back in the very near future. I highly recommend this place to those who are into cajun boils or seafood in general.  If you aren't into spicy foods, you can get it prepared without any spicy flavors at all and with other options than the classic Cajun spice. Come check this place out!

Olive + Oak is a farm to table type of upscale restaurant producing freshly prepared, delicious meals for their client to enjoy.

If you're looking for prime dinner time reservations, be prepared to wait a while (as in a few weeks maybe?) but if you enjoy going to dinner early or very late then you might be all set.  I prefer going to dinner early, it doesn't bother me at all.  I am hungry around 4:30-5pm usually and will generally want dinner around that time. But trust me, whatever sacrifice you make will be rewarded tenfolds by delicious beverages of your choosing and a meal to remember.

We had a 4:30 dinner reservations on a Friday night.  The place was not as crowded but it eventually started to fill in as we sat and enjoyed our first drinks and apps.  We started with manouri cheese (roasted peppers, dill, cured olives, crispy capers served with some toast).  I enjoyed our appetizer, it was delicious.  They also brought over some dinner breads from a local bakery.  I enjoyed a California cabarnet sauvginon while we waited for our entree and took in the surroundings.  

It's a fairly small restaurant but well-lit with a more modern decor, a sizeable bar and a communal long table right by the bar.  

For my main entree, I ordered their pasta special with some sweet crab.  It was really good and our waiter was right, the crab meat pieces were very good.  I'm glad I went with his recommendation.  For dessert, I had a sort of upside down pineapple cake with cream.  Angel food cake type of cake soaked in cream for a couple of hours and that really was nothing like I have had before! It wasn't overwhelmingly sweet but it had a very rich flavor complimented with a few pineapple slices, a drizzle of caramel, then sprinkled with whole macadamia nuts. Such a lovely end to our dinner.

Service was excellent.  I cannot stress this enough! Our waiter was funny yet very attentive.  I really did enjoy my first visit here and I cannot wait to come back!

For my 400th review and to mark a special occasion, I give you the Twisted Tree!

My deepest, most intimate food love is steak. Twisted Tree is a place to satisfy all your beefy cravings. 

We had a 5pm reservation and were seated in a cozy, roomy booth upon arrival. Waters were filled quickly and the waiter came over to take drink orders and explain what Twisted Tree is all about. I had a glass of cabernet and we started with their onion rings. The onion rings came with their housemade sauce, however, the breading was flavorful enough that the sauce was sort of unnecessary.

Their garden salad is served family style with servings of croutons, 2 types of dressing (french and sweet onion vinegarette), and some cheese.  You can tell the garden salad is made fresh and definitely not your pre-cut variety.  I enjoyed the sweet onion vinegarette dressing quite so.

Now for my main course, I opted for the smallest cut of their aged ribeye which was a 16oz for $41. Very reasonable for a steak currently at 205 days in the aging process. Very tender and very flavorful, succulent and melt in your mouth steak deliciousness. The filet mignon (63 days) was also very tender and flavorful.  I got to try a piece and I highly approve. For my side, I ordered their vegetable of the day which was a corn and green bean casserole. It was very tasty and well-prepared.

Dessert was a little bit difficult but once he said the wedding cake to be almond cake, I was all in.  It was your traditional 3-tier wedding cake with a scoop of their homemade vanilla ice cream. Definitely more serving than 2 people already full of steak can ever consume but we did make a dent.  The cake was delicious and not super sweet.  The icing was a bit much so I ate around it.  

Overall, we had a lovely dinning experience and will definitely be back for a non-special occasion in the near future.  Service was fantastic and I am definitely glad I finally got to try it though!

As far as the meat goes, winner! I have only been here once but was immediately impressed by how tasty their barbecues are. I tried their brisket and wow! I would have to say, that was probably the best tasting brisket I have had so far. I got the 8 oz portion with 2 sides. I ended up picking some slaw which was pretty much bland though at first sight, it looked creamy and delicious, and I had another side that was actually good. I don't know what it was called, it looked good and I asked the guy what it was called but he was soft-spoken and it was too loud to hear so I went with my instinct and told him to put some on my tray.

The tray -- so, I found that very interesting. They serve your food on a metal tray lined with brown liner paper. It was a surprise to me when they cut up the brisket and placed it right into the tray without any plates. As for the sides, they do put them in containers before putting them into the tray. 

It does get very busy and I can see why so if you are planning on eating in there, you might have to share the table with other people. It's also pretty noisy but overall, I am giving their meat a 5-star just because they make really good barbecue meat! The sauces were okay, wasn't too impressed with any of them but luckily I didn't think I needed any except to try them out.

I think I might come here another time soon and get a to go order of meats and go home and make my own sides. It would make for a great meal!

Discovering new places is so exciting and this week, I made a point to drive to La Bonne Bouche for two reasons: 1) to check out their cafe and try their french onion soup and 2) acquire a variety of macaroons to bring to a Thanksgiving dinner tomorrow. As a guest, I would not want to bring something to a dinner that is subpar so I made sure to check out the reviews before making the commitment of bringing these macaroons to the host's dinner. So far, there are dazzling reviews pertaining to the bakery.

Now it's time to share my very own experience. I came in around 11:30am and was seated right away.  Water and rolls & butter basket were brought to the table but I don't really like bread so I passed on that.  Since this is my first time, I wanted to try a variety of things even though I know I wouldn't be able to eat everything. I started out with a cup of french onion soup. What a delight! It was oozing with cheese and the base was very tasty and flavorful. I was not at all disappointed.  Then for my entree, I ordered something I could not pronounce (which is a shame since I work for a French company): Les crepes aux fruits de mer et aux epinards. In short and less fancy terms, seafood crepes -- baked crepes stuffed with crab, shrimp, spinach and topped with tarragon lobster and mornay sauce.  I ordered the large portion which was a mistake because they gave me 2 stuffed crepes which were not small by any means.  After finishing off the cup of french onion soup, there was no way I could have eaten 2 stuffed crepes. Needless to say, I ended up taking the other crepe home with the steamed carrots and cauliflower that came with the meal. That's right, I am ashamed to say but I actually did not eat my vegetables during lunch. The stuffed crepe was so good and flavorful, though and the sauce complemented the dish very well. I loved every single bite.

I also had a cup of latte with my meal and it was fine. Service was excellent. My waitress was quite attentive and brought my orders quickly. She even warned me about the sauce over the crepes bein really hot (it was still bubbling when she brought it to the table).

I will have to say, I did skip desert because I was way too stuffed. Rest assured, I will edit this review once I sink my teeth into the delicious-looking truffles and rhum balls I took home with me, not to mention the macaroons. The bakery was such a delightful scene to me. All sorts of different delectable cakes and pastries! My eyes feasted upon them but I knew I couldn't buy them all. The bakery service was great!  The woman helping me was so nice, informed me about their already packed variety of macaroons and the price difference if I choose my own flavors.  I did and at check out, she explained to me how to keep the macaroons from getting too dry after I told her I am bringing it to dinner tomorrow. I will be back.

Verdict on the pastries:

The French macaroons were a hit at the main Thanksgiving dinner.  I brought 4 different flavors: milk chocolate, Venezuelan chocolate, vanilla, and cherry. I think I liked the Venezuelan chocolate the best but the milk chocolate did not quite live up to the expectations. I did not try the other 2 flavors but everyone said they liked them. They were definitely a hit mostly because they were different and quite delightful to look at.  

The rhum balls were quite rich that if I was to eat 2, it would have been way too much.  Lastly, the truffles were good but did not quite blow me away. In short, I have had better truffles. With that said, I would love to go back and try their creme brulee and some of their cake varities!

I wrote this last night on Facebook. 

Just finished having a pizza at Smiling with Hope Pizza. My wife had the NY style Pepperoni and Peppers, My daughter had the mushrooms, olives and peppers and I had the NY style Ricotta. The place is very cute and the staff is great, everyone smiling and friendly. My wife and daughter loved there pizza. I adored mine. It was amazing. When a pizza is done right with quality ingredients you don't need a lot of flashy toppings. It was simply Ricotta, basil, oregano. So amazing I ate the whole pie by myself. I had to grab a pizza to go so I have lunch at work tomorrow so I grabbed a Sausage, mushroom, ricotta and anchovie pizza. If you are ever in the area or in the mood for a great pizza I highly recommend them. I will definitely be back. Stay Sweet.

Stopped by here for lunch with the wife this afternoon. Lovely outdoor dining area, perfect for these beautiful St Pete fall days. Started out with the meat platter, which had a great array of meats, olives and pickles. The pesto served with sliced baguette was the star of the show.

My wife had the croque monsieur, and her only (minor) complaint was that she wished it had a little more ham on it. I had the pho, which as other yelpers have pointed out, was quite delicious. Looking forward to heading back for breakfast in the near future.

Whewww Chile... the ghetto . 

This place is overpriced and beyond corny. Save yourself the money and time. I will never think about coming here again. Yesterday was my first and last time. The place is nice but the vibes here are just weird . Food menu was limited . Drinks were ok but overpriced.

The worst part of it all is... in order to access the rooftop you MUST order a drink from the bar on the lower level. Mind you... there's a bar on the rooftop.  

Views were a 2 on a scale of 1-5. You really only see the liberty place buildings. This really isn't a rooftop. 

Music was cool. Tbh that's the only reason why I gave them 1 star.  

"It's a no for me, dawg"

I'd like to give 1.5 stars for the quality of meat that they served and for the far away concept that the food coming out of the kitchen LOOKED good. The rest of the meal was ruined by the service.

I saw assistants zooming around the room. A customer was standing looking for his friends' table. An assistant zoomed by him and yelled, "ON YOUR RIGHT." The elderly man jumped from being scared by this guy yelling at him.

We saw an assistant take two full water glasses off a table and at the insistence of the woman who sat us, he poured the water back into the pitchers that served all customers. Once you put it on a table, it shouldn't go back out for others. I also wouldn't want anybody's uneaten bread but I don't think they give you bread here.

The outdoor seating is "cooled" by a giant misting thing that looks like it was bought second hand off a music festival. This creates a hum and humidity that attract mosquitoes. We ended up well-bitten. And let's also be clear that this "cooler" doesn't cool the room. It was hot and humid in the post-thunderstorm evening.

Our table ordered three medium rare burgers. We received three medium well burgers. One of my friends was not happy about this but we all ate them anyway.

When the waitress checked on us, my friend said the burger was disappointing. She had been looking forward all week to their medium rare burger but this was overcooked. While my friend was still talking, the waitress said, "I apologize," and walked away. No questions, no solutions, just walked away WHILE she was talking.

Despite his manic pace and the number of times he blew by us, the assistant never came back to refill our waters, which sat less than half full for some time. Since I was sitting next to the water pitchers, I just grabbed one and filled up our glasses. Nobody seemed to care. I should have gone and cooked our burgers.

At the end of the meal, the waitress came back to clear and asked how it was. My friend said again that although we all finished our burgers, it was disappointing that they weren't cooked how we had asked. Waitress said, "I'm sorry about that," took all the plates, and walked away.

The woman who sat us dropped by (maybe she's a manager?) and asked how our meals were tonight. As you might guess, my friend said she was disappointed that her burger was overcooked but we all ate it anyway. The manager couldn't look her in the eye, said, "I'm sorry" to who knows what since the eye contact wasn't there, and walked away.

Kudos to the people writing reviews here who got actual care, sympathy, a suggestion that something be re-made, or a free dessert! We got a lot of looking away and walking away. 

Which was what we did next. Drowned our sorrows in Frost, which always works. :)

Despite the really nice meat they seem to have for their burgers, there is no reason to go back here.

I discovered Lilly's Cafe in Yelp and Urbanspoon and am thankful I did! I've been there three times in the past two weeks and have eaten in twice (during lunch diring the week and then dinner on a Saturday night) and ordered takeout once. As an Asian-American I'm very picky about my Asian food and have to say that Lilly's Cafe has one of the best combination pho around! I also enjoyed their eggrolls (with homemade plum sauce) and crab Rangoon! Both times I dined in I had NHI as a waitress who was quick, friendly, and efficient. Also, the owner, Lilly was very professional and pleasant! I'm a regular now and will keep driving from Mid-City to the Lower Garden District for awesome Vietnamese food!

So I saw my Yelp buddy Danon H checked in here earlier in the day and it gave me an idea to take my friend here for her birthday (albeit 3 months late-hey, don't judge I'm a social butterfly!).  I called ahead to make sure they had vegetarian options for my friend and check out the specials. The vegetarian options were a go and the special sounded great!

Turns out my friend had eaten there once before but didn't remember the name of the joint. She said her meal was previously forgettable but this time around they wowed  her!

See my pictures for the delicious vegetarian burrito my friend ordered (black beans substituted in), the "crepecakes"=thin pancakes, bacon and sunny side eggs I ordered and I forgot to take a picture of the delicious biscuit and amazing homemade strawberry preserves!

Crystal was manning the front and she was super friendly on the phone and in person. She helped me decide between the sandwich biscuit and the crepecakes! My friend thoroughly enjoyed her burrito and liked the homemade preserves that came with the biscuit! Oh, I forgot to mention that the water dispenser had apples to flavor the water-yummy! Meanwhile my crepecakes were yummy with several strips of bacon, sunny side eggs and real butter and syrup! I indulged and ate it all! Plus I ended up putting some of the strawberry preserve on the think yummy pancakes (three). Divine!

Bonus that they also sell meat, homemade preserves (Crystal said the blueberry is amazing as well) and they even deliver! Yeah, you heard me, they deliver! 

All I know is this place can be dangerous for my goal to lose weight and maintain it!
Only downside is that there are only 6 tables inside so it gets a little cramped but hey, the food is worth it! Plus there is outdoor seating which is cool.

Happy Breakfast Eating!!

I gotta tell ya this is the Asian market on the westbank or perhaps NOLA for that matter. Growing up down here there were a few scattered Asian markets to buy the Filipino stuff my family enjoyed eating. We would have to drive to Vietnamese markets or Aling Ely's Filipino store but all that changed when Hong Kong Market opened. Everything Asian foodish you could possibly want is here!

Now don't get me wrong I couldn't do all my food shopping here bc I need a salad bar and almond milk with flavors etc but darned if I don't love their banh sandwiches, frozen food (especially the mochi) and snacks (love me some Pocky!) etc. And my mom loves the discounted produce which she ends up freezing some of them or cooking right away. She tells me it is much cheaper than the regular grocery stores and I believe her. The best is when they get the fresh mangos! Nothing tastes better than a Filipino mango but these come pretty darned close! 

Happy Asian shopping!

Omg Laurie and Jarod made this dinner so special for my cousin, her fiancé and me!

We've all been wanting to go to this restaurant for a long time but it always seems packed. So thankfully we picked a Saturday evening during thanksgiving break when the LSU game was on so it we were able to get in!

My cousin and her fiancé were so sweet and wanted to take me out to dinner bc I helped decorate the spot where they got engaged last week!

Laurie made us feel like queens  after I joyfully told her that my cousin and her fiancé just got engaged last week and I was a part of it! She told us the specials and gave us awesome recommendations! She even served us the best crab cake appetizer I've ever had outside of Maryland!

My cousin and her fiancé enjoyed their Bellinis and I liked my glass of rosé! We also went with laurie's recommendation and got the crab cake appetizer. Omg she knew exactly what she was talking about! Y'all when I tell you my cousin's fiancé was closing her eyes when she ate it bc it was so good! We joked that it's like watching how I eat good food bc we enjoy it so much and get so much pleasure from food!  It was fresh crab meat with not a lot of breading so you could really taste the crab!

My cousin got the whole fish special with mashed potatoes and a crawfish sauce on top and squash. The fish was so tender and flavorful, she ate the whole thing and we never finish our food bc we usually save room for dessert! Hehe  

And her fiancé got the chicken piccata which we were shocked bc normally she gets chicken Parmesan. I got to try her dish too and it was tasty! You get an entire plate of chicken and a bowl filled with pasta!

As for me I got the eggplant Parmesan which came with a bowl of pasta! Their red sauce is so good they even sell it in glass jars at the front. Hint hint for Christmas presents!  

And for dessert we got the delectable chocolate cheesecake with raspberry sauce and chocolate flakes on the side! This is when I closed my eyes while eating it! Haha 

And Jarod was so sweet opening up the Pygmalion room so that my cousin and I could look around! They can open the doors to connect the Dean Martin Room and the Frank Sinatra room you're host a huge reception! In fact Jarod said they hosted a rehearsal dinner the other evening. We even liked the wine room which reminds me of Antoine's with the smaller rooms for intimate parties!

The main dining room is an elegant space with lush red booths in the corners, plush chairs, gorgeous chandeliers etc.! Even the bar is sexy and I could watch the LSU game from my seat! Haha 

We're definitely coming back and this time we're trying the surf and turf with that exquisite crab cake over a steak!

Happy Italian and steak dining!!

Oh dear Lawd and butter! This review is strictly on their Sunday brunch which is quite frankly, amazing!

Thanks to my buddy and first Yelper friend, John L. H. (Aka Steve's friend hehe) who arranged a UYE for Sunday brunch last weekend. My fellow elite Yelper friend, Mr. Danon H. Has always raved about their bbq so I tried unsuccessfully once before to partake of said deliciousness. But last Sunday was the day I triumphed and tasted the bbq eggs Benedict! Oh man, everything was so darned good I had to deconstruct it to make it last longer and savor the taste! (See my picture).

First there is the buttery biscuit which is the basis of the Benedict. Then there is the perfectly made sunny side egg (just like I like it bc I like to break the yolk and make it ooze out). And the creme de la creme, the BBQ! Aww yeah! Mr. H has never steered me wrong and this BBQ was delish!  It even tasted good the next day when I had it for dinner!

FYI, you order at the bar and are given the option to start a tab, they give you a number, and then you take a seat. They were very gracious in saying the kitchen was backed up but this, my dear friends, is worth the wait! Fellow Yelpers tried the frittata and enjoyed it so there is another option! And one Yelper enjoyed the build your own biscuit!

Oh, and there is a huge water dispenser near the door with cups.  I will definitely be coming back again to eat!

Happy brunching!

Covid-19 update: For some reason I thought I already wrote a review for Blue Oak bbq  . Forgive my oversight! Oh man, I'm so glad that Blue Oak BBQ is in my neighborhood and doing pickup! Like Jen said, it's super easy to place your order and pay on their website. They even give you a time estimate of when your food will be ready!

Last week I wanted to bring my parents a treat so I ordered from Blue Oak bc I knew how delicious their bbq is! Plus I saw them on the local news donating food which made me want to support them even more!

I forgot to take a picture of my latest order but I got the 3 meat combo with 2 sides. I picked the ribs, pulled pork, and brisket along with macaroni and cheese and potato salad. My parents loved the food and so did I! My favorites were the ribs and macaroni and cheese! 

Btw it was super easy to pickup my food. They have tape on the ground to guide people to follow social distancing. You just park, let them know your name, and you can sign the receipt and pickup your food!

Happy bbq eating!

NEW FAVORITE PLACE! This place is my jam, y'all! My bestie, Mary Elizabeth W. have come here for lunch after mass for the past two weeks and plan on coming forever! Hehe...we have it down to a science where I get my slider, iced chai latte with almond milk and a specialty donut and she gets her iced chai,  slider or sandwich on a donut (Monte Cristo was delish!) and the "American" waffle fries with slider sauce, onions and cheese (divine!). Then we split the fries and donut!

The first week we both tried the fried chicken slider which was good. The second week I tried the pork belly slider and OMG it was divine!! Who knew they could pack so much goodness in a little slider? Hehe and my bestie had the Monte Cristo which I got to taste and it was yummy!

For our specialty donuts the first week we had the cookie dough with a cream filling which was tasty. And the second week we had the Nutella filled one with bananas on top. Can I even tell you how much I love Nutella? And to think I hadn't discovered Nutella until my college friend introduced me to it back at LSU!

FYI, this place gets packed but we've always been able to snag a table. There is a parking lot next to the restaurant, outdoor seating and lovely indoor seating! 

The people are friendly like Jackson who took our last order and I should have caught the name of the nice lady who took it the first week, the food and drinks are delicious and the service is fast! What more can I say? It's the trifecta and they've got it! 

I plan on becoming a regular! 

Happy Donut Eating!!

A Latin American friend recommended this restaurant to me and said it was authentic Colombian food. So when a girlfriend asked me to think about where I wanted to eat dinner this joint was on the top of my list. Especially since I had never tried Colombian food.

Since my friend is my Weight Watchers buddy we tried to order something relatively healthy and ended up splitting two appetizers and saying them family style. We ordered the ceviche which was delicious but be forewarned it has jalapeños so it has some kick! Then we ordered the sample Arepas and let me tell you it was pretty darned good! My friend normally avoids bread like the plague but liked the Arepas "bread" so much that she ate it! We tried the Arepas in order from the chicken which was ok, the pork which was delicious and the mechada (beef) which was frogging mind blowing! You know how you eat something so good that you actually close your eyes and savor it? Yeah, that good! Now I know why they run out of the machada Arepas! 

The service was also excellent with Jocelyn helping us decide what to order and being attentive. Plus the thee waitresses pitched did and made sure our water glass was never empty. I enjoyed it so much I asked Jocelyn if I could meet the manager and she told me both of the owners were there and introduced me to Alex and the other co-owner. 

Overall I really heart this place! They have a bar with drink specials and the restaurant is romantically lit which would make a great date night! 

Happy Colombian Eating! Can't wait to go back and try more food!

COVID-19 update: one of my best friends who is like my brother absolutely loves this bar and I can see why! It's a local bar that has really yummy bar food, strong and relatively inexpensive drinks, outdoor seating, tv's, fans, parking etc.! What more can you want?

I appreciate that we can eat outdoors, our waitress was super friendly and efficient and wearing a mask. I really like their burgers and cheese fries. My bestie has ordered other things on their menu and has liked everything!

They have disposable paper menus so you can look for what you want and then throw away the menu or take it with you and recycle it. 

They've even put up an additional tent to add more outdoor seating which I appreciate bc this is one of the few places that is open later in the evening during this pandemic. It's been so bizarre but understandable that there aren't many restaurants to go to later in the evening so this is a godsend!

Happy bar eating and relaxing!

Ahhh I long for spring evenings, long summer nights and beak fall evenings so I can have an excuse to enjoy Bacchanal! 

I can't even tell you the countless wonderful days and nights I've spent here with friends! On cold nights I've sat upstairs which has a bar and feels like a beautiful lodge with the tall ceilings!

And on those warm nights I've sat around the mismatched tables listening to live music, relaxing with friends while trying a new white wine, cheese, and small plate. I really can't think of a better way to spend an evening besides relaxing by candlelight and various white lights with friends and loved ones around. If you know me well you know that I can be very territorial and if I like a place I will NEVER take a date there bc I consider it mine! And bacchanal is that kind of place! Hehe it feels like a little piece of heaven right here in NOLA. 

The people that work here really know their libations and will pair your tastes for the perfect cheese, tasting plate etc. I have brought various kind of friends and even the one that went to culinary school at Johnson and Wales and used to work at Emeril's was impressed with their wine selection. In fact we selected a wine that he said he couldn't find anywhere else in NOLA. Score one for bacchanal! He was also impressed by their small plates and the homemade concoctions in the bar upstairs!

So if you want to relax somewhere and be amongst friends then come over to Bacchanal. You won't regret it! As other reviews have said this is like being in a friend's backyard. It's eclectic, homey, and endearing like the Bywater always is!

Happy carpe noctum!

ALAS they put up a sign recently! It seems to be getting more business as well :) Loveee this place..and it's in my top boba places: 
-85 Degree Bakery 
-half & half 
-CHATIME

i've also had: 
-lollicup
-class 302
-7 leaves 
-bing's boba
-volcano teahouse

A great outdoor dining experience in the suburbs! Would definitely like to come back and try more of their pastas and wood grilled breads.
Atmosphere: Had an outdoor seating area with a tent overhead. The servers were very friendly and all the staff were in masks.

Food: Ordered the wood grilled octopus and whipped ricotta and honey with sea salt bruschette. I thought the bruschette was a bit too salty, but the wood grilled bread had great texture. Octopus had amazing flavor and paired well with the olives and sauce - would order this again! Also tried the pappardelle with wild boar ragu, which I loved! The pasta tasted very fresh - just wish the portion sizes were a bit larger given their prices.

Overall: 4/5 - glad I was able to try this Italian restaurant, and it's a great choice for a nice outdoor meal out in the suburbs. Just thought it was a tad pricey for portion sizes.

The acid test for the Indianness of an Indian restaurant is how well they make their naans. And I am happy to report that Taj makes their naans so fluffy, they might as well open a mattress store as a side business. Seriously, when the bread shows up on the table, there will be naan violence!

For the meat eaters, there are tons of options just as there are for vegetarians. I am a big fan of their vegetable samosas. They are the perfect bite-sized masala buns of tongue orgasms as they are meant be. I was severely disappointed and depressed at their pani puris. After a session with a  shrink, I allowed myself to forgive them for over salting the potatoes, and butchering the pani (the spiced water) that goes into the little hollow fried dough balls. If you want to see how they should be done, head down to Chauhan's, stop on the way at the bank, take out a loan, and then order their Gol Guppas. That's the benchmark in this city. Both Woodlands and Taj ruin pani puris by half-assing it. 

Their main course fare is pretty darn good, and if you are adventurous and feel like slapping on a few pounds here and there, go for the methi matar malai, an innocuous looking bowl of fenugreek and peas swimming in creamy gravy. But with every mouthful, you'll feel gravity grow stronger as the delicious flavors collide and explode in your mouth. Between eating the fluffy clouds of naan pieces and this ambrosia, you'll have to loosen your belt/skirt, and just ooze onto the chair.

Table service leaves a lot to be desired for. You'll have to flag them down explicitly to catch your attention, but it's a small price to pay in exchange for the quality of food.

Seriously, this is the hidden gem of Indian restaurants in the city. And don't order the pani puri.

I was sad one evening. I sat outside Edgehill Cafe. Rain everywhere.

I saw a white rabbit dash into Taco Mamacitas, and I followed him. His coattails flapped in the drizzle.

"I'm late. I'm late," he kept muttering, checking his clock, looking on fleek in Imogen and Willie jeans. 

I opened the door, and saw him scurry down a passageway, and I bounded after him. I chased him down a dark passage and opened a heavy door, and stumbled into Wonderland.

A giant metallic shell stood in a corner, grabbing my neck and yanking it upwards. I searched and couldn't find the ceiling, so high it was. Concrete slabs laid crudely everywhere, like a giant's playpen. People milled about amiably. I looked for the White Rabbit, but he was busy ordering a drink at the bar.

I walked around, unsure whether I was in a bar, or in some trippy Brooklyn underground scene. The music poured from everywhere, and for a second, I was sure that the DJ was inside the metallic chimney. He wasn't, but he should be, replete with disco lights, spinning tunes from his Rapunzel tower, letting down his golden beats and taking us all higher.

I have no words for this place, except a great sadness that it didn't exist before. The drinks were well priced and the options many. Food came in from somewhere, but I didn't feel like eating at that point. The place has all the class, and none the pretentiousness that such joints typically attract...for now.

Later, the White Rabbit and I did shrooms in the restroom and all was well as we walked back into the normie world.

My wife and I got a takeout order from Mortons last weekend. Our salads were nothing but lettuce and the lobster bisque had one lobster claw in it that tasted like rubber. I picked up the order in the bar area and had on sweats and a Northface hoodie. I was looked at and treated terribly by the bar staff and manager. Save your money and go to Kayne Prime. I will never go to Mortons ever again. What a terrible experience!

Updating my review on this place since i'm always here. Han Dynasty is hands down the best place to eat in Cherry Hill. This place is all about spicy and flavorful food. If you don't like spicy food you can always turn the heat down on your dish.

 All the food on the menu has a spice level already picked out for the dish. The spice level starts at 1 and goes to 10. The highest i've ever went is an 8 and the flavor was amazing and the spice was outstanding. Han is the only establishment i've been too where the food was spicy enough for me.

 Most entrees you can change the "protein" as well. Examples such as; Fish, pork, shrimp, tofu, chicken, beef etc. The portions are family style so get ready to share some big dishes. Some apps I recommend for this place are, Dan dan noodles, cold noodles in chili oil, pork wontons, spicy crispy cucumbers and scallion pancakes. Entrees; Kung Pao tofu or chicken, double cooked chicken or dish, garlic sauce style; chicken and black bean style; shrimp. 

 Manager Mark is such a treat to see every time I come in here. Always has a smile on his face and going out of his way to help all customers. He really takes charge with the restaurant and making sure everything is perfect. Staff is awesome and knows who I am at this point. Super friendly and always there for some recommendations if its your first time or you're just looking for something new. 

 Out of the 7 locations that Han has (NYC, PA, NJ) the Cherry Hill location is the best. I have visited one of the Philly locations and loved it but it couldn't compare to the relationship I have with this location and the staff that works here. By this review you can tell I will be back for more.

The Tasty is located in South Philly on the corner of 12th street and Reed. This place is so cute and cozy on the inside. Everything is self serve since this place gets super crowded and there are only 3 workers. Before sitting down you have to order at the counter. There is limited space for people to sit so a sign pretty much tells you to get up once you're done so other people can sit and enjoy. 

 You buss your own tables and get your own sauces, silverware, drinks etc. I honestly don't mind the self serving concept because when you need something you don't have to wait on your server you just go get it. Tasty has two different bar/islands to sit at along with maybe 6 tables. Bathroom in the back and an open kitchen so you can watch your food being made. 

 I've never had a problem with the food or drinks here ever, I really did enjoy everything I ordered and always willing to try something different when I do come here. Tofu scramble is awesome, I do recommend getting it without the "bacon" unless you like coconut give it a try. Vegan omelette is also super good but doesn't necessarily resemble an omelette. Deluxe burrito is to die for I highly suggest this dish. 

 Only reason i'm giving this place 4 stars is because of the last time I came here. All 3 workers were kinda of snippy? One yelling at me not to sit down when I myself didn't know that rule untilI I came back this time. Other staff worker yelled at me for leaning on the counter and the other worker yelled at me for "blocking" the way of the kitchen when I was just watching him cook. Having all 3 workers yell at me wasn't very inviting and made me super uncomfortable. I understand the place is small but I wasn't really doing anything wrong. I wasn't really sure where to stand to be honest. I will be returning but if the service is the same with the staff that will be my final time eating at The Tasty.

If you want to feel like a hipster and think that entails paying top dollar for a weak cocktail in a beautiful setting, then this place is your new home bar. 

Being from a certain Oregon city with a certain reputation, I take my bars very seriously. I appreciate a place that attends heavily to their atmosphere and ambiance. However, a well-designed bar needs to bring more to the game than great wallpaper and an impressive chandelier. I ordered a mixed drink rather than a cocktail here, being that I like alcohol to drink at bars and not liquid wedding bouquets, and it was weak. Yet, it still cost as much as their premium cocktails.

Now, about the service. I understand the ethos of a disdainful mixologist. See above: I live in Portland. But these guys were seriously pushing that point to its logical conclusion. I may not be a fancy-looking, middle-aged something or other, as most of the patrons I saw here were, but I am still a paying customer. Don't treat me like I don't belong in your bar. 

The overall vibe I got from this place is that it is trying to be cool, and instead of being cool, it is acting out some version of cool that it learned by watching network television.

Yuck. This place was so full of racist and ethnically hostile political signs against immigrants that I couldn't even bring myself to buy a cheesesteak from them, but I have tasted their steaks.  They're not very goodl.  I'm never going back to the place...

When I first moved to Philly 5 years ago, a few friends from NYC visited and wanted to try Pat's and Geno's.  They're across the street from each other.  They seem like mostly tourist places.  At that point, I had never tried either.  Most of my friends ordered steaks at Geno's first, because it's the first place we encountered on our walk there.  So, I waited in line with my friends (prepared to order my own), but was shocked by all the extremely prejudiced and ethnically/racially hostile signs all over the place.  Seriously, I'm embarrassed this is a celebrated Philadelphia "establishment," we should all be embarrassed about that type of "in your face" prejudice.  The people working behind the counter also seemed rude, so I went across the street to Pat's and picked up a cheesesteak.  

On the upside, Pat's wasn't full of offensive signs.  But both steaks were comparable, and not that great. 

Now I know that Jim's on South St. and Steve's Prince of Steaks in NorthEast Philly are the best classic cheese steaks in Philly.  If you want a good cheesesteak, try Jim's or Steve's: They're much better (delicious) cheesesteaks.  Plus, you won't be supporting that kind of blatant prejudice!

This establishment is a fabulous (and boujee) steakhouse in Newtown. White peach cosmo was icy cold and stiff, just how I like my martinis. I always try the calamari when I see it on a menu and I feel like I'm a connoisseur now. The breading to squid ring ratio was perfecto along with the seasoning. Didn't even need the lemon juice, hollandaise nor pomodoro sauces. But I'm a natural food dipping kind of gal, so I dipped lol! Gf and I decided on the 3 pound porterhouse. The nice thing about the menu item is that it came with 2 steak sauce choices, 2 salads and 2 sides since it is meant "for two." Steak was delish as is although I did enjoy the chimichurri and bearnaise sauces on the side. Asparagus and garlic spinach accompanied our ribeye. The Caesar salad was dressed just right and tasted scrumptious! I am already anticipating my return.

We went here for happy hour to celebrate a friend's birthday. Tip: If you check in on Yelp you get a free beer or well drink. I had the James & The Giant. It was a nice beer, with a fruity flavor. I ordered off the appetizer menu: the poutine, and the brussels sprouts, and some of the spicy mustard on the side. The poutine was good. The meat was nice and tender, and the cheesy curds were tasty. The only thing is that the gravy was not very hot. Poutine is best when the gravy is nice and hot and starts to melt the cheese curds into the fries. The brussels sprouts were amazing, as was the mustard. I highly recommend ordering these! They even go well together. The brussels sprouts have a sweet taste to them due to the maple and sherry vinaigrette. We got a few orders of them, and they were a table favorite.

A great spot for lunch!

I have been here a number of times and the food has been consistently great. The popcorn chicken is AWE-SOME, and the beef pancake is to die for. If you are looking for a good vegetable dish I recommend the green beans, YUM! Recently we have discovered they have a great lunch deal. For $5.95 you can get a 101 bowl with your choice of entree and side, and a soup (the beef tomato is great!). If you are feeling a little more hungry you can opt for the 101 plate (2 entrees, a side, and a soup), or the 101 deluxe (1 entree, 2 sides, a soup, and an egg roll). What a deal! 

The only negative about this place is the service. I would only recommend it if you have time. It can be very slow. On numerous occasions we have had to remind the waiter to bring us the soup that went with our meal. Other times we have been brought the wrong items. That being said they are always friendly and quickly correct the error.

Miranda Lambert's "Casa Rosa" Tex-next restaurant has opened. The Carnitas tacos were very delish. I ate so fast I forgot to take a photo. Sorry Yelpers ...  

Will have to try a few other items in my remaining days here in Nashville.

Loved this place!  Excellent street food.  Great low prices.  And free entertainment.  

Highly recommend you try the Cheeseburger Taco and the Bacon & Shrimp taco.  Finger lick'n good.

A good place to stop for a quick snack and refreshment,  Who knows, you may stay awhile...

Tried again. Terrible. 2 of the 5 orders were wrong (either the waitress is incompetent or the cooks can't read). The cook can't cook. Hot rods - hire a chef for your huge menu or simplify your menu. 

Chicken was burnt - majorly. It's not that hard to grill - come on. Other chicken had tons of salt on it. Everything was BLAND, there was nothing Southwest about the chicken sandwich, I tasted absolutely no chipotle mayo, and everything seems to come from a frozen recipe or is cooked in really old oil. 

And as the other reviewers said - even though there were only two other tables in the place for lunch it took 40 minutes for a few sandwiches.

I don't want this place the close since there are barely any restaurants in the area but they really need to step it up. I suggest the owner hire a new manager and a new chef.

I'd heard the hype. Seen the NY Times article. Nevertheless I was skeptical. Mainly because most people have at best, two reference points for donuts, Dunkin Donuts or Krispy Kreme. Neither of which really makes truly great donuts.  So after waiting for the crowds to die down a little, I traveled over to see for myself last Saturday.

It's a small shop that blends into the surrounding neighborhood. Inside there are a couple of seats at the counter and a wide window well that two people could sit in. I ordered my donuts. I went with the Indian Cinnamon, the caramel banana, the pina colada, and the halva pistachio. The ladies behind the counter worked as fast as they could given the decent sized collection of people waiting for orders and bopping in. My order was processed quickly, and I got my coffee right after I ordered it. The coffee was one of the only things that was a disappointment besides the lack of seating.

 Since there was no room to sit, much less stand I took my donuts and coffee out to a park just off of Federal between 3rd and 4th St.
The donuts were truly transcendant.  Each donut was a symphony of flavors on my tongue.

The Indian Cinnamon-Very light on the cinnamon, coated with sugar. Hot, fresh, and so moist that it pinched in half when I started to eat it.

The caramel banana-A delicious meld of flavors with something added to the banana chips that made them more tasty than I"d imagined.

The pina colada-The donut I though I'd enjoy the least. However it tasted like the Rach 3 and Beethoven's 9th all rolled up. A complex mix of flavors that together was truly amazing. And unlike the current generations, I don't use that term lightly.

The halva and pistachio-the final movement. More subtle flavors that nevertheless worked well. I'd never had halva before, but I liked it.

Believe the hype. Believe the NY Times article. Federal Donuts makes some of the best donuts I've had.

Crampled aisles: CHECK

Completely random aisle placement that makes the maze in Harry Potter look easy: CHECK

Pizza by the slice that caused me intense GI problems: CHECK

Crappy selection of overpriced cheeses: CHECK

Annoying customers: CHECK

Feels like you need to take a shower and report a robbery after checking out: CHECK

Great already... and they are still spreading their wings.

Chop 40 took this space from a pizza & burger that was good, but not compelling.  
Both the rustic, planked diniing room, and the cozy bar area got clever and subtle upgrades that improved the feel of the space.
The backyard dining area got a reboot, too, better furniture, but keeping the beautiful sky.

- but not everyone will care about vibe and furniture, let's get on to the food! - 

The menu is already solid, and slowly expanding at the same time.

I'm there for the output of the smoker:
The Chicken Bomb, smoked bacon and chicken wrapped around a hot pepper has ruined me for all other 'poppers'.

They have a smoked salmon burger like no other, I suspect they smoke the salmon first, and then reconstruct it as a patty, and grill it.

I've not seen the Chops alluded to in the places name make it to the menu yet, but I keep checking in, waiting for that happy day.

We came by after swimming with the two daughters... The service was quick and helpful, & the food was amazing... aaaaaand now I'm afraid I want one of their tex mex burgers in a lettuce wrap every night. :-)

My first review of 2017! No better place to do it than Morgans!

My love for seafood only started within the last four years. Growing up I was incredibly picky and honestly afraid to try new foods. One fateful day my mom force fed me crab and I've been hooked since! I especially have had an undying love for lobster. The second I heard a lobster shack had opened near me in Reno I bookmarked the location, waited for the opening kinks to be worked out, and head over. 

Parking is a little confusing if you're not already aware where to go. Parking is in the back, not at the parking lot next to it! Once we head inside we were welcomed by a delicious scent of lobster, and immediately seated. Our waiter was patient and knowledgeable, offering suggestions and his opinions which was really helpful for our first time here! I had looked at the menu before coming, and read reviews, so I knew I wanted the lobster grilled cheese. The boyfriend ordered the same and we got the crab quesadilla! Food came out in the time we would expect, and was cooked to perfection. The quesadilla didn't have a super intense crab taste, but it had a lot of crab in it, so I think my taste buds just didn't pick up the flavor with the other flavors the quesadilla had. Next came the lobster Grilled Cheese. WOW! Was that good! The Cheese and Lobster mixed together so well, and tasted amazing. I never would have thought of that combination! I took a piece of the lobster out to see how it tasted alone, and it was so buttery and delicious. I can't wait to come back, and try another dish!

Another tip- come during their happy hour! I found their deals to be great and more competitive than other restaurants in midtown!

I am going to do my best to put into words my experience at Sterling's but words will never exactly describe just how amazing this place is. 
My boyfriend made a reservation for Sterlings a week prior to our anniversary, and did it while he was on a break from work (he works within the tri-casino property). Remember this as you read.
Evan and I sat down for our dinner reservations and were in awe of the professionalism of the staff, and of the decor within the restaurant. We had looked at the menu prior to coming so we knew exactly what we wanted, although Evan changed his mind with the recommendation of the manager and server. We ordered a German Riesling for our bottle of wine as a celebration of four years together. For our appetizer we got the Oysters Rockefeller. They came out hot and I was dying to dive in. I think these were the best oysters I have had in my life, hands down. They are so, so good. If you are reading this and considering getting them, stop reading and do it! For dinner I ordered the Filet and Lobster combination and Evan ordered some kind of steak I can't remember now (oops). Evan raved about how delicious it was, and how he never has tasted anything so good. I can say the same thing about my meal. The taste was beyond words. 
The manager stopped by our table and asked about our food, and asked Evan how things were going at his job. It was so nice that they remembered him making the reservation a week prior and that he worked there as well. Their customer service here is phenomenal. The manager came back and gave us an American Riesling to try and compare to the German Riesling. I thought this was beyond kind. 
If you are thinking about going here, just go! I can't wait til I can go again.

Please, please do not go to this casino if you value your money.  The slot machines pay absolutely NOTHING!  It's not just some are good and some are bad, they are all bad.  The playtime is horrendous and total ripoff.

I predict this place will not survive the 1st six months.  Went there last night and the word must be out because there were very few suckers playing the slots.  Unfortunately, I was one of them.  Came home and put membership and players card in my drawer and will never return.  What an awful experience.

Always wanted to give these guys a visit and just happened to have B-Day gift card from a previous lifetime. Made it through the first half of the century with ease and wanted some high quality Steak to feed the tiger inside.

This particular Tucson location is definitely nicer than the one by our house in north Phoenix. It appears like they spent more time with both the architectural design and the decor inside.

Brought my Mom and my partner in crime and made sure to make reservations around 6:30 on a Saturday. Good thing we did since they were packed to brim with tons of hungry patriots.

Ordered the Baked Garlic Shrimp for a starter and enjoyed dipping the complementary bread in the melted leftover butter. It was pretty good but nothing to write home about. Maybe it needed some bigger sized shrimp for the wow factor.

Decided on the 10 oz Tenderloin wrapped in Applewood Smoked Bacon and served with Béarnaise Sauce. It was out of this world crazy good. My wife ordered the Surf and Turf which came with two Tenderloin medallions and a smaller sized Lobster tail. She loved it very much and was tempted not to share. LOL!

My Mom has special eating requirements with no seasoning or sauces. She was able to order a Caesar Salad without the dressing and then had them put some unseasoned Grilled Chicken on the top. A little drizzle of EVOO and she was in 7th heaven.

Unfortunately this restaurant is only open for dinner and the place get really busy quickly. The dining room area was very loud for us and we had a hard time speaking to each other. Consider sitting at the bar or on the outdoor patio for a more intimate setting. You can order off the full menu in both places.

Definitely a place that we would easily enjoy again without hesitation. Just make sure you get me a prepaid gift card first and then it's my treat and all on me. MEAT GROUP!

4.25 STARS

Everything about this place is amazing. 

The service from the time of ordering, quick delivery of food to the table and vibe they exude is just the start of what will be one of the best meals you have had. 

I ended up with the ropa vieja plate. This thing was a huge helping of salad, rice, beans, pico, avocado, fresh corn tortillas and that was all to kiss the main entrée. Out of this world flavors, not too heavy and if you ask for their homemade hot sauce you have a reason to excuse the tears of joy. 

If you even dare a pouty face for no meat you have to leave that feeling behind you. If you did not once you read all ingredients for the dishes your excitement will mount, from scratch. 

My partner was pleased with her meal and finished the plate without me tasting anything and there was no jealousy my side. I had an espresso too and I did taste her horchata latte. Both solid and the latter was not too anything except satisfying. 

One consideration is parking. Not too many spaces and a little tricky to not get in the way of 6th street so be safe. 

Bring on the food coma, loved it.

This place has become one of my favorite German restaurants. I would gladly travel an hour and a half from Orlando to get to it. It's a fun atmosphere. There's live music during the weekends. The staff is incredibly welcoming, helpful, and engaging.

Prices are great. Most German places charge a lot for their food, but Old Castle's lunch menu is one of the best I've seen. They serve generous portions at a reasonable price.  We shared the stake:  three bratwursts of your choice surrounded by spaetzel. It originally comes with pan fried potatoes but we substituted them for cheese spaetzel. I love cheese spaetzel. I could eat it all day.

Anyways, they offer a variety of German beers. And I am really loving the decor.

5 stars for their attentive employees, good authentic German food, and fantastic beers.

4 stars.

I was initially wary, but it turned out to be way better than expected. It's a spacious establishment decorated with a lot of baseball memorabilia. I'm new in town and I heard this is a St Louis icon.

Menu is extensive and they serve pretty much your standard sports bar food. They are known for their deli sandwiches. Try the pastrami--it's quite tasty.

The soup and salad combo is cheap and filling. You can't go wrong with it. Their chili contains chunks of turkey meat and plenty of white beans. Let's just say, they are generous with their portions. Cool atmosphere and speedy service.

Originally we planned to go somewhere else, but we left after not feeling the other place's vibe. We went up and down Brandon Blvd. Finally we decided on going to O' Tooles since it seemed like a fun place. 

You sit wherever you like. Our waitress was great! I wish I could remember her name. She was perky, funny and attentive. 

Prices are reasonable. They have good food and drinks specials. They serve your typical Irish pub grub.  I ordered the fish and chips. This was one of my favorites. It was great! I loved the batter and the white flaky fish. Portion size was big. The fish is served on an entire plate of fries. 

We were informed that Fridays are their busiest nights. 
We went on a Saturday evening and it was pretty quiet.  It was a cozy and relaxed atmosphere. 

5 stars!

Well-known for their turkey chili. Even the waitress was boasting about it. Well, I tried it and loved it so much, I bought a quart of chili to go. Sportsman's has a great sporty, fun, neighborhood feel. It's decorated with classic sports memorabilia. This place is a tradition. I need to visit again and get more chili.

Reading Terminal Market is the most magical place on Earth, not Disney.  I don't think words can express how much I love this market.   It is one of the oldest public markets in the USA.  It's been around for 126 years.  You can find anything here.  The market has a wide variety of ethic products, Pennsylvania dutch products, homemade soaps, local spirits, locally sourced produce and meats, international and domestic cheeses, exquisite chocolates, and much much more.  

I am obsessed with Downtown Cheese, a shop offering an overwhelming selection of cheeses and cold cuts from all over the globe.  Mueller Chocolate Co. was my second favorite shop.  They have a chocolate covered onion and other unique chocolate offerings.  I personally enjoy the truffles.  

This place is also foodie heaven with all the little quirky restaurants offering from American, Mediterranean, Italian, Vegan, Caribbean, I think you get the picture; they have whatever you fancy.

5 stars! My new favorite spot in Philly.

There is a song by Buster Poindexter called "Hot Hot Hot" that kept running through my head as I enthusiastically shoveled mass quantities of nuclear warheads into my mouth last night. What a trip, I kept waiting for a coyote with the voice of Johnny Cash to appear as my spirit guide, but alas no groovy visuals. The thing that stood out most to me was that none of it was hot for the sake of hot. The flavors of every dish stood out despite the little red devils sticking their pitchforks into my tongue and my bodies water works foreman deciding to open up the flood gates and turn the sweat dial to full blast! In fact, I think it was because everything tasted so good in addition to the heat that I committed a slow act of suicide by impending ulcer. 

Quick run down:
Won ton &/or Dumplings in chili sauce were amazing
3 cup Chicken fantastic, although the tiny bones created their own unique minefield 
Flounder in dry pot was incredible and incredibly spicy! There must have been 5 flounders in the dish and the various mushrooms put this over the top for me.

4th of July - 9:49pm. The sign reads OPEN TILL 11! So, I decide to pull in and take my "new to Boise" friends to my favorite ice cream spot in town. The guy behind the window said, "sorry bro - we're closed" with a smile on his face. I told him, "the sign says you're open until 11 and it's 9:49...So, do you close at 11 or 10 and if that's the case you're still open for 10 more minutes." He responded, "it's Fourth of July, bro...there are no rules". I hope you get fired you arrogant brat. If you were my employee, I would fire you in an instant. When I worked in a shop, I worked until the store was closed and if I still had customers - I stayed open, because it was the right thing to do. I was so embarrassed standing on the street with my friends. So, flabbergasted by the laziness of Boise's minimum wage crowd. I'm not sure I'll be visiting Fanci Freez ever again. :/

Alright look....Nobody expects the food at these places to be Emeril's quality, but one of two things have occurred since the last review in March of 2010.  Either this place was sold to new owners, or you people have no idea what food is supposed to taste like.  Today I visited on the direction of fellow Yelpers giving this place good reviews.  What a HUGE mistake.    I now hesitate to even think of trying the North Redington Beach location, even with its outstanding reviews.

The hollandaise sauce on my "Mock Benedict" was repulsive, inedible.  My wife's omelet had cheese so greasy I wouldn't feed it to my dog.  To any reviewer in the past that rated their home fries anything but waste from the bottom of a dumpster should have their eyes and palate checked.  We were utterly disgusted.  Our server, a young Russian/Ukranian girl was extremely nice, and as stated to my wife, very attractive, and enough reason to go there just to see her.  

I won't go into the coffee, other than to say it was burnt, or more than 25 scoops for a 12 cup machine were used, undrinkable.

Do yourself a favor, if in the St. Pete Beach area Yelping for breakfast, look no further than across the street from here...a pink building called "Beverly's la Croisette"...best breakfast in SPB....I don't know why we went to the Reptile Pool...should have just stuck to what was good.  

As an addendum...my wife vomited her breakfast no more than 45 minutes after leaving.  Wow...just wow.   

Yelp !!!!!

There was one buzz word as I entered this New Mexican buffet: PANCHOS. People from all angles said it, and were anxiously awaiting to give this place the stamp of approval or the cold shoulder. I have to say, most people left this place with a smile on their face and a feeling of regret, just like good OLD Panchos (not whatever that was that opened in '09). 
2 Amigos was a blast from the past. We waited in the longest buffet line I've ever seen, but it was so well managed that it only took us about 10 minutes to get to the food. All of the food was hot and fresh; they were constantly putting new pans out. Have 10 plates filled with things you don't know the name of, smothered in cheese? No worries, you don't even have to carry your tray! A server shows you to your seat and carries your tray. The flag has been replaced with a nifty light on the table, which you tap on if you want to eat more of your feelings. 

Chile rellinos  were very small and flat, but still good. Tamales could have been a bit meatier and bigger, but overall tasty.

The owners are FOR SURE going to have to invest in a bigger building. With the crowds I saw tonight, there's no way they are going to be able to handle the capacity of people that are coming to this place.

2 Amigos definitely brought me back to my childhood. New Orleans missed Panchos. Even though this is not the same name, it definitely holds the same standards and hope it stays around for a new generation to know what a love/hate relationship with a Mexican buffet  is really about. Now excuse me while I run to the bathroom.

Thank God there is a good Mexican spot near me. I've eaten in the dining room and had take out numerous times. Being from Los Angeles I'm pretty picky with my Mexican food and everything I've gotten here has been delicious. Not to mention my orders are always correct and service is always good.

We've had their tacos, enchiladas, homemade guacamole, steak and shrimp fajitas, and burrito. I really like their perfect margarita as well, it's so good. I have had their shrimp cocktail and it was good but not my style. 

They also have a nice outdoor patio and a lunch menu. 

Great spot for Mexican food and drinks.

Renee's Organic Oven was our first meal on our half country road trip, on our way to YSBSA.
We were pleased to find something local and organic with accomodations for our dog on their small outdoor patio. The restaurant owner even reserved a table for us!

What we ordered:

Arbuckle's Apricot Tea - Local coffee and tea purveyor
Spinach and Artichoke Dip - Local made in house. 
Chilies & Cream Pizza - Local house roasted green chilies, local organic beef, Sonoran jalapeño cream sauce, zucchini, pesto, onions, garlic and mozzarella. 
Isabella's Ice Cream - Local handcrafted and natural (free with Yelp check-in on this day).

Yelp, thanks, WOW!  The tea was refreshing and crisp,  the dip was hot and creamy and the pizza, well, those chile's made it a Southwest dream. These items were the BEST, BEST, BEST I've had ANYWHERE! The service staff was attentive and shared info on the local vendors.

I look forward to a return to Tuscon to eat at Renee's Organic Oven again, as it really doesn't get much better than this!

There is a Rat in Bar Les Freres.

Let me preface this review by saying that we love all of Zoe's (the owner) well thought-out restaurants and have enjoyed them for years going all the way back to Café Zoe.  We recently celebrated my wife's 40th birthday at I'Fratellini (another Zoe creation), and it still is one of our all-time favorites in St. Louis.
Now let's get to the "Rat".  The rat is not hairy disgusting vermin, but the 6'2" hairless man that greeted us at the door.  He was inviting and told us his name was Mike.  He introduced us to the bartender Tommy (nice guy) and HIGHLY encouraged us to eat at the bar.  We told him that we would get a drink at the bar, but that we preferred to wait for a table to eat our dinner.

Since I followed the restaurant's construction on the internet and even drove by to see how it was going, I was eagerly anticipating the opening of Zoe's new place.  I was looking forward to another great dining experience that I have learned to expect from Zoe, so we waited for a table.
That meal never happened.

We sat at the bar and had cocktail.  We expected to wait.  The restaurant doesn't take reservations, which was fine; we knew that going in.
Then it began.

The first table for two opened up, but it was not offered to us. Instead, a couple that arrived after us was given that table. Even though I was annoyed, we were enjoying our cocktail, so I didn't say anything.
A while later, another group that arrived after us was given a table, so I started to get really annoyed. I asked the Rat, "How is our table coming?" His response was that some tables should be turning over in a little while. A few minutes later another table for two opened up, so we thought there was no way that table would not be ours. The table sat empty for about 5-10 minutes. By this time, we had been waiting for 45 minutes for a table. Then a new couple arrived at the restaurant and was seated immediately.  Unbelievable!

So I handed my credit card to the bartender to pay for our drinks and told him that we were leaving. As Mike the Rat walked by I asked him why he seated three groups that came in after us. He ignored us and walked away. That is when I got really pissed.  The people taking our table were mortified that they were put in that position and offered up the table to us (thank you).
Needless to say we didn't stay.  Mike the Rat refused our credit card for the bar tab but offered no apology (sorry Zoe).  He just got more combative, yelling at us that there are "Lists".  

The thing that we can't understand is why we were snubbed at a restaurant for the first time in our lives. We were nicely dressed and well groomed. We were not loud, obnoxious, or drunk (we each had one drink at the bar, our first of the evening). We were not cursing, making out, or causing any type of disruption to anyone. We were just sitting politely at the bar waiting for our table. 

My wife and I have a hobby of trying almost every new and exciting restaurant that opens in St. Louis.  This place blew my mind, with the rudeness of management.   So, I guess if you aren't on the "list", you shouldn't bother. 

As a side note, a large group of twenty-somethings were seated near the front window drinking and having a good time.  Mike the Rat actually went up to them and told them that they need to order some food or leave....really? It's called BAR Les Freres for a reason.

Okay, dudes, let me lay it on the line. Around the corner, at Memphis Taproom, they serve AMAZING food. They have creative, skilfully cooked, locally sourced, organic, from-scratch, highly varied, kiss-the-tips-of-your-fingers fusion down-home cooking. They serve this amazing food, moreover, alongside an ever-revolving smorgasbord of craft beers. And their service is both comradely and intelligent.  

This is your direct competition. So you had better listen closely when I tell you that we spent EXACTLY THE SAME AMOUNT OF MONEY on a memorable, delectable and deeply satisfying meal for three at Memphis Taproom, including beer, that we spent on a deeply banal, beer-free meal at Mugshot. 

Please let this sink in. You are charging damn-near-Manhattan prices for freezer waffles, stale bacon (previous reviewer was right), canned vegetables and iced tea. You can't get away with that. Either significantly lower your prices or significantly raise your quality standards. Right now you've altered our cost-benefit calculations so aggressively that we're going to Memphis twice as often.

I saw this place emerge from a closed Bennigans to this new restaurant, the food was pretty good, the drinks were watered down, but the service was absolutely awful.

There was a group of 6 of us comprising of 3 couples, they sat us with another group of 5 around the same table so elbow room was at a premium already.  The problem with the seating initially is that the chairs are a little too low from the counter in which you eat from already so try to sit on the bench instead, those seats sit a little higher.

We ordered drinks and upon receiving the drinks mine got spilled across mine and my wife's plates, no apologies nor clean plates presented (we were required to clean the spilled drink off our own plates).  The mai tai was watered down and too much on the sweet side.  

We started with appetizers after the drink fiasco and decided to order sushi, we received our sushi and it was very hit and miss, but the bigger problem was we had no chop sticks.  We asked for chop sticks, on the first and second trips back to the table the waiter forgot the chop sticks, finally he brought them back on the third trip.  The tuna roll was pretty good, but the sushi cuts were not very good (seems the person who cut the fish needed more practice in cutting fish) and the grouper was dry and tasted a little less than fresh.

We started into soup and salad portion of the meal, the miso soup was incredibly oily (you could see the oil slick in the soup) and did not taste like much at all.  The salad while simple was very good, the ginger dressing was one of the best I have had anywhere.

I had the fillet and scallops which was in all pretty good, but I have had better.  Also the when had some of our courses during the meal I could taste some of the charred pieces of the previous course on my plate, they need to do a better job of cleaning the gill and also not use the spatula when cleaning off the grill scraper because the burnt char pieces get stuck on the spatula.  Overall the main meal tested pretty good.

We tried the fried ice cream for dessert, I think next time I will just get the fried ice cream from a Mexican restaurant, much better when they prepare it.  

Now comes a more painful part, the check, remember when I said that there were three couples?  Well all of our bills eventually got messed up.  When I ordered sushi I ordered some unagi for my wife as well, that got billed to a different couple.  We called the waiter to resolve the issue, the problem got worse.  When we got the revised bills the unagi got billed to the other couple out of the three of us and on top of that they charged the wrong cards for the meal, the second couple (the couple which now was billed the unagi) was billed on my card and my bill was billed on theirs.

We called which we assumed was the manager to try to resolve the issue, the card charge was resolved, but the unagi charge was not.  About 20 mins later we finally got some sort of remedy on the unagi charge when the manager just pretty much said here's your 5 bucks (the cost of the unagi) now get the heck out of here (not her exact words, but the impression that I got).

I am a big component on service when I have to pay this much for a meal, while I might go here again with friends and maybe for a rare special occasion I will not be back here as a casual diner.  I imagine I have had a bad experience and I imagine if/when I go back it will not be this bad (or at least I am hoping), but the management response on this was inept and pathetic.

Hokkaido is the northernmost and second largest island in the chain of islands that is the country of Japan.  While the land mass is large, Sapporo is the only major city in the prefecture and even has some smaller islands on the Northeast side disputed by Russia due to proximity.  Large Japanese island with Russian climate?  Brrrrrrr...... Let's have a hot bowl of ramen!

Dosunco's menu consists of 4 core items, which coincidentally happens to be the same number of tables that they have in the restaurant.  Miso Ramen, Spicy Miso Ramen, Shoyu Ramen, and Abura Soba (not actually a soba) are served as well as a few udon selections.  The miso tastes very similar to a fatty, porky tonkotsu ramen that you may be used to; there is still a stewed pork base to this dish.  The only thing missing is the corn and pat of butter.  Spicy miso ramen is the same miso ramen with red oil dumped on top.  The shoyu (soy sauce) ramen is definitely the best broth at Donsuco, with more roasted garlic flavor than the other options.

The good:
Novelty wood ladle and real ceramic bowls, make for a more enjoyable bowl of men.  
The staff speaking Japanese in the kitchen and to the customers is something Tampa folk do not hear often. 
With the open ramen kitchen and commotion, the only differences between eating ramen at Dosunco and eating ramen in Japan is the missing food ticket vending machine at the entrance and the same flavor of food.  The experience, other than that, is almost identical.
Prices are lower than other places I have been to in Tampa Bay.  Just an FYI- the most expensive bowl of ramen I've consumed in Japan was 900Y.

Issues that ALL of the soups have:
Pork:  
There is pork, that does not resemble anything like the rolled chashu pork, or even typical ramen pork--- this Dosunco pork disintegrates into pork flakes when touched, due to the cut of the meat.  It would be great if they switched to the rolled traditional version to help edumacuate the Tampa crowd.
Hard boiled egg:
Overcooked and served cold on top.  Yes, cold.  It's gross.
Noodles:
The frozen, curly variety.  Not the worst I have ever had.  The only sticking issues I have had with these noodles is when the broth starts to cool.  Since the broth is so fatty (and delish), there is a thick layer of grease that solidifies on the noodles and causes them to clump.

Do you really want me to talk about the other food?  Karaage is not good, no amount of lemon or mayo is going to help the limp, rubbery meat.  The Gyoza appear to be the frozen variety.  However, I recommend ordering a side of Ebi Fry instead (3 tempura shrimp).  

When we visited, there was a free tea of the day--- non sweetened genmai.

For a restaurant of this size, they should consider adding more seating.  There is plenty of room to do so.  Because the line of hangry customers waiting outside the door is not getting any shorter as time goes on.  Luckily, we did not have any waiting or service issues, since we arrived as soon as they opened.

May return, or may not, time will tell.  My favorite in Tampa Bay is made by an old Thai lady on Central Ave DTSP and is way too expensive.  Maybe I'll see you at that place instead.

Pho Kien Giang is in the same broke-down plaza that it's always been in.  I arrived after dark, and it is pure sketch.  However, the food here is so damn good.  The waiters here are so damn jolly that you will never feel unwelcome.  

It's freakin' cool that there are so many Vietnamese restaurants in Pinellas Park, yet each place has a specialty and difference in flavor.  If you know about Vietnamese dishes that you like that are not on the menu, try ordering off menu.  You would be surprised that they are often willing to cook up some secret items, if you are not a total jerk.

My favorite dish here, is one that I usually dislike everywhere else, which is the cold noodle salad bowl, Bun Thit Nuong.  Mostly because the house sauce here is the best, loaded with lime juice (not the sauce in the bottle, the sauce in the bowl).    Also, the Bun is loaded with thinly shaved cabbage, which stays crispy throughout the entire meal.  No soggy lettuce here.

I'm not even a beer fan, but I can get down on a Rapp flight anytime.  They have so many strange and seasonal beers to choose from that I always find something that is fun to try. 

There is an open garage area that has the largest amount of seating.  The actual bar is a smaller climate-controlled area.  As most breweries in Florida, it is located in an industrial/office area.

There are different foods trucks outside, depending on the day of the week.  I think that any type of food is good with beer.
