Arirang is too expensive, and if the owner comes up to your table be careful what you agree to.  Being a little familiar with cultures, I assumed that we were being given "service" by the items that were being suggested, as small tiny tastes to try the menu.  On the other hand, items were being totaled up at full size and we were soon loaded with dishes and expensive teas on our table.  The bill was in fact, as terrifying as I expected.  

Table of four for lunch $150.00 not including tip.

For this kind of high cost, I would have expected something spectacular.  That did not happen.
The meat portions are pre-cooked and skimpy.  Beef cooked until gray, not charred and bland.  So, if you are a vegetarian, I recommend Arirang for you.  

Random noodle dishes were loaded with sugar, too sweet for any savory dish.  For example; the Jajangmyun (Black Bean Sauce Noodles) and Bibimnaengmyun (Spicy Red Cold Noodles) were doused in corn syrup.  It is very sad, but I could make better noodles at home and I am not even a good cook.  

The food at Arirang is the most "Americanized" Korean food I have had in Tampa Bay so far.  I was previously warned about Arirang from my friends, but still wanted to try for myself.  

On a positive note, they do serve SamGyeTang--- whole chicken ginseng soup, the chicken is stuffed with tender rice.  Like everything else; it is expensive $24.95, slightly Americanized, and sweet.  By Americanized, I mean that the broth is punched up with additional flavorings, and salt and green onion is already added for you, and the chicken is dissected for you away from the table.  Traditionally, the customer takes apart the chicken and the seasoning and onion is served on the side for you to add as you like.

If I do return, it will be for the SamyGyeTang, because it is a rare find in Tampa.  But, I will be very wary of the hospitality given.  Maybe I can keep my lunch under $20 next time.

All of the foodies I know had eaten here, except me.  So, I figured it must be good and was time for me to give it a try.  We were here on a Saturday afternoon, and there were only two other tables of patrons.  The atmosphere is heavily decorated, but still has a home-style appeal.  The owner will come by to check on you and the waitresses are in traditional attire.  

The Beef Sambussa appetizer consists of one small triangle of meat wrapped in a tender crust.  I would pay $2.99 for two of these, but since it was only one it left me wanting more.  The hot spiced tea was amazing and I highly recommend it.

My husband and I ordered the Queens Eight Platter for two, which is $26.99.  It comes with 8 dishes of the Chef's choice.  You can ask for all vegetable or mostly meat etc.  We had a half and half mix.  I was not fond of the lamb entrees, since they were too musky for my taste.  My favorite items were the lentils, the mushroom, and the cabbage.  They are very nice when it comes to dietary needs here.  Most of the vegetable dishes are also vegan.   I am definitely not vegetarian, but I think that their vegetable dishes are their strength, so I will be sticking with the veggie dishes only in the future.

All of the dishes come served on top of bread, which is amazing solo even without the stews.  The bread serving is very generous, but I do not know if it is unlimited or not.

You must try to eat it with your hands, scooping it with the bread for the authentic experience.  But, if that makes you uncomfortable then you can switch over to a fork if you must.

Yeah, I'm under 60 and eat at the Melting Pot--- so what?  Fawn-doo was popular with my parents in the 1960's, but this vintage celebration of cheese and chocolate did not stop with the hippies.  Plus, this location has hidden rooms and reeks of wine, and looks like a hobbit hut.  boom

Who does not like melted cheese?  Not even a vegan can turn down this hot pot of bubbling beer cheddar!  (They can dip their veggies in it.)  Seriously, it is hard to eat just one cauldron of golden cheese, when there are so many different types to choose from.
I like to just get the Crave Combo= Cheese Fondue + Salad + Chocolate Fondue.  It is like $21.00 a person.  There are a ton of add-ons to jack the bill up, like premium dippers and sides.  None of that crap is necessary as the regular sides keep-a-flowin' like banchan in jeongju, so you can always ask for more and they are complimentary refills with the cheese or the chocolate.  Just gimme that cheese with some semi-stale bread to dip in it and I'm content.  KTHX
My favorite salad has always been the California, maybe for sentimental reasons but after many years it still holds up.

Last time, we did all of the add-ons like the weak Rosemary Fries and the Premiom Meat Dippers.  Nope.  The meat jumped from $44.00 to $88.00 real fast.  Skip it.

Also, found that the alcoholic drinks here are expensive and not tasty.  I'd even skip the dessert drinks as well next time.  Let's keep it simple and affordable.

MNM BBQ is a big restaurant with three parking spaces.  All other parking spaces are noted as tow-away zone, so be careful.  So, unless you plan on Ubering here, good luck.  

I really liked the dive bar atmosphere here, but the prices are really high for the small amount of meat you receive.  The meat was alright, nothing phenomenal and mostly had a reheated texture.  

The side dishes are also overpriced and not that great.  The potato has been reheated so many times that the butter is separating into oily bits.  The BBQ beans were broken down and not that much was added to dress up the original canned flavor.

If you are ordering a sandwich; the bread, rolls, and pita are very dry.

There are not many barbeque restaurants to choose from in the area, that must be why they have so many customers.  Maybe I just tried them on an off day.  The staff was really nice, and there are some dive bar customers that come here to sit for hours.

Do you like ramen served in a paper cup?  
Does it remind you of the best $13 cup noodle you've ever had in your life?

I'm sorry people, but I just can't get down on this porta-paper box of broth.  Maybe if I lived close by, I could reheat the soup and put it in a proper bowl.  There is just something about eating ramen out of a bowl, with hot steam blasting your face as you slurp down noodles.  

If they were to give me a bowl, I promise I will return it.  I won't try to steal it or anything.

Hong Kong House is exactly what the name states, a Hong Kong style restaurant.  Just like many Cantonese restaurants, they specialize in seafood and banquet dishes.  However, Hong Kong House also serves up some excellent fresh dim sum items and garlic sautéed vegetables.  

My first visit was during opening week, so I am proud to see the Hong Kong Powerhouse of a business they have become.  Backed by MD Market in the same parking lot, and the innovatively amazing Flushing/NYC bubble tea stronghold ---Kung Fu Tea right next door--- it has all become a one stop location for anyone wanting a relaxing Saturday or Sunday morning dim sum brunch and shopping with the family and friends

If you dine during dim sum hours, not all items are featured on cart and will be made fresh at your request.  The main two fresh items I recommend are Salt and Pepper Pork Chops and Snow Pea Leaf with Garlic (or Ong Choi, depending on the season).
I have not had a bad dish here so far, on cart or off, so let your eyes wonder and pick something you have not tried before.  You just might like it.
The only dishes I am not that fond of at HKH is the barbeque items; honey roast pork, roast duck, crispy pork belly, etc.  They are not terrible by any means; you can just have them cheaper and better tasting elsewhere.

Do not speak Cantonese or Mandarin?  Having issues? Just look the items up on your phone and show a photo of what you want, they will probably make it.

Even if you are not into eating delicious Chinese food, you have to visit just to see the bubbling LED rainbow spectacle that is the entrance foyer.  The floor bubbles and changes color, and the bubbles flow upward into a lobby wall that divides the dining area from the entrance.  It is tacky-love-hotel-baller.
The dining area is also a full wedding banquet facility--- complete with a red velvet back wall and dragon and phoenix in gold.  Like I said before; B A L L E R.

Want me to come and eat with you and order for you?  I'll be your guide, anything for a free meal.   Call Coty's Cantonese Caddy Service at 1-444-CBA-LLER.

Paul's has pretty much nailed it.  
Now, a much appreciated addition to the North 4th Street restaurant row, with a:
- convenient location right off of 275
- festive family atmosphere 
- excellent thin and thick crust pizza
- other quality food items
- beer and wine bar with the vanilla favorites
- great service
- ample parking
- addictive chicken wings
- all the flat screen tv's you could ever need

They have the Chicago staples, down to the tamales.  

Thanks to Yelp, Paul's and I have a little history; after attending the Elite event at their other location a few years ago, I have driven many miles, many times to that location for a specific pizza fix.  Now, that they are right by my house, my cheese intake will double.

Paul's thin crust pizza is an ultra crispy cracker, never soggy.  You will not find anything this texturally satisfying in the area.
While the deep dish is also unique--- somehow they manage to build this hard cracker crust into a thin shell bowl that somehow holds pounds of cheese, toppings, and sauce inside.

You will find me here at least once a month.

Better Byrd could be my favorite once-a-week fried chicken fix with a few refinements.  Not quite there...

Another eatery in the Ciccio Restaurant Group.
Customers start to line up in front of the confusing menu and just stare forever.  Then, other customers line up behind them and are even more confused.  I have watched so many customers just walk out because the menu is so intimidating and kind of expensive. 
With all that being said, there are still plenty of customers.  It is very difficult to find seating inside during peak hours.  The seating situation mirrors their parking situation here.

For a chicken sandwich, fries, and some donuts at Better Byrd, I have paid the same amount of a nice steakhouse for dinner ($54.00 for two people).  It takes a few tries to figure out how to work their menu to make it more affordable.  However, they are still about double the total cost they should be, in my opinion.

Since the menu is not very specific, it is very open for interpretation.  For example: the taco photos that quickly flash on the TV screen show them with pico on top.  However, when you order they want to charge you extra to have pico.  It is inconsistent, and up to the person that is taking the order whether they want to charge you or not, and then up to the person making the food at the time if they want to add it or not.

The donuts are very underwhelming and also expensive.  Tried ordering the matcha twice now and still have not received.  The first time it was not on the menu, the 2nd time just received sugared donuts with no matcha topping.  Hope to try it someday.  My family really dislikes their donuts, so then I am stuck eating them all by myself usually.
So far, the best flavor topping is Horchata.

Let's see how many different types of food can be made with the same fried chicken breast here.  There is one pulled chicken option.  With so much emphasis placed on their cage free and anti-biotic free chicken, you would think that they would have passed on the processed fries from the local food service provider.  
Just cut the potatoes and put them in the deep fryer ya'll!  Then, you can re-fry them to make them extra crispy when the customer orders.  It would be so much better than those pre-fab fries, and pair better with your chicken.  The fried chicken finger chain across the street has fresh cut fries, they have figured it all out, just sayin.'

I know, it is a Vietnamese restaurant.  But, it is my favorite in the Tampa Bay area.  And, when I lived in NYC (ate in Flushing every weekend), I missed Halong Bay's Fried Bean Curd Rolls and White Egg Rolls, because I miss the extra punch of cilantro at Halong Bay versus the jiggly and flavorless dim sum served at more traditional places.

Cart service only is the best, so you must come during brunch to early afternoon hours on Saturday and Sundays for the best experience.  There are two cart waitresses that speak both Mandarin, Cantonese, and English.  All other staff speaks English and Vietnamese.  It is nice to have so many languages spoken in one place.  

If you are looking for Dim Sum on cart and not interested in paying ridiculous prices or waiting in line at TC Choy, then this is the place for you.  The reviewer before noted that TC Choy has a larger range of items, I disagree.   I have waited over an hour at TC Choy after asking them to bring me some Gai Lan or duck, and ended up leaving before it came out.  Also, Halong Bay has an entire cart just for congee, 4 kinds, all with different toppings.

Halong Bay has the cart during lunchtime on Saturday and Sunday, however they DO have their full dim sum checklist menu items available all day everyday, even at dinnertime (like Ho Ho Choy).  This place opened back in summer 2008 and I have been going there all the time ever since.  Beware of the "Chef's Special" items that are on the cart, which will range in price from $8.95-15.95.  You may get a surprise on your check if you grab one of these delicious plates of food off of the cart.  It might be worth it to you at times, since they have yaki udon, Chinese sausage sticky rice, clams in black bean sauce, etc.

Sometimes the cart will go by and it has not been restocked, so there will be some items missing.  If there are, ask the wait staff and they will be more than happy to bring you the item fresh from the kitchen as well as restock it on the cart.  They do this for me all of the time, it is not a problem.  All other dim sum places that I have been to have the same thing happen frequently, especially when they are a good restaurant that is going to be crowded full of customers.  Roast duck, gai lan, u choy, water spinach/snow pea tips, roast pork, not on the cart?  Ask for it!  One time they were sold out of sesame balls because someone ordered so many earlier.  This is actually a good sign, since they make them there and they are not the frozen kind.  They cannot just go into the freezer and get more.  If the carts are not having what you want, then look on the checklist menu to see what they have available and ask.

Their full non-dim sum menu contains a large selection of Chinese food, such as; roast duck, noodle soup dishes, noodles, eggplant, and fresh seafood from the tanks located in their dining room.  Noted that the sea creatures in their tanks are the most well kept that I have seen so far in a Chinese seafood house, since the water is circulating and the fish are swimming against the current, thanks are clean, and the fish are active.

Vietnamese food is also on their menu, of course.  They have Pho and a decent Bun Bo Hue.  The Garlic Butter Chicken Wings are also pretty good. 

Note that they DO have bubble tea, and the menu is located in a stand on your table.  They only have assorted milk teas that come blended as a shake.  And they only have traditional brown pearls to choose from.  Sometimes they are sold out of pearl.  If you are looking for a place that specializes in bubble tea and has Banh Mi, then Thuy Café is next door and they can hook you up.

I always come to Halong Bay between 10:30-11:00am on the weekends for brunch and dim sum service.  Otherwise, it is totally slammed.

Favorite items:
-Fried Bean Curd Skin Roll-  with shrimp and cilantro inside
-White Egg Roll-  same filling as above roll
-Fried Taro- with shrimp and pork filling
-Soft Tofu Pudding- with ginger sauce
-Snow Pea Leaves w/ Garlic or Water Spinach w/ Garlic
-Salt and Pepper Squid- they have updated their toppings to taste more like Yummy House style

I'm a regular at the original Gainesville location of Sweet Buns, so I didn't expect the massive assortment, packed with customers, and savory dishes available at the Tampa location.

This is Tampa's first legitimate tong-grabbing-goodies bakery.  Yeah sure, there is a terrifying Chinese bakery in Evergreen Plaza... but Sweet Buns is clean and modern with so many goodies to choose from.
My favorites are their savory breakfast themed buns, mango pudding, and cheesecakes.  Also, their Hong Kong hot milk tea is so delicious!!!  It tastes just like the milky version that I've gotten in breakfast shops in Hong Kong.

There were many customers here eating soups and menu items.  But, I just come here for the prepared baked goods, sweets, and a hot tea to wash it down.  I just wish that they had more extended hours.

This is the only Chinese restaurant that I have found in the Brandon area that serves up decent food.  It is hidden in a Publix plaza off of Brandon Boulevard, tucked behind an Arby's (in the same plaza as The Rack Brandon).  I used to frequent their Bloomingdale location before for dim sum and their delicious Seafood Chow Fun dish.  I was sad to see that location closed and I thought I lost them forever!  But, just this week I found them again at this new location.

The tinted windows and glowing signs, plus the strip mall location make it seem like just another take-out place.  But, it is in fact much different.  It is not as good at Yummy House or China Yuan, but comes in a close third and conveniently located in Brandon.

They have a great dinner special where you pick three dishes from a menu for $21.95.  It is a pretty sweet deal condisering that the dishes to pick from are no joke.  Like; Seafood in XO, Roast Duck, Sliced Beef with Gai Lan, etc.  We ordered the Sliced Fish Filet in XO, it was a great dish and the fish was delicate, but still held up well with the XO.  The Salt and Pepper Squid was just ok, but still better than some other places.  The Crispy Peking Pork Chops were _perfect_...

Their specials menu is also posted on a board near the front door and they have Ong Choi (Water Spinach) fried with garlic for only $6.95 here.  Some places charge $14.99 for this dish!

Kao Thai Kitchen is an expectedly perfect romantic date night spot in the most random location.  Located right next door to one of the most overrated Italian restaurant in Tampa Bay makes me want to show them even more love.

Magnificently brined chicken wings, curry tuna pasta, homemade coconutty deserts, and rich coffees and teas will keep me coming back for more.  While the crinkle cut fries were quite basic, the salty shrimp paste dipping sauce full of sour tang was addictive.  Prices are the same as any other Thai restaurant, but the added value is in the atmosphere and unique menu options.

Cannot wait to return for more on another date night.

Do you know what Izakaya is?  Some people call it the Japanese equivalent of dim sum, I call it small plates of bar food.  At I Ai, it is more of a family atmosphere than a bar atmosphere, but the small plates are where its at.  Not as good a those yakatori houses at St. Marks (NYC), but it cures the cravings.

It was a little difficult to find, located in an office complex called Fountain Oaks off of Waters Ave. near the intersection of Dale Mabry, next to an Albertsons.  We arrived here as soon as they opened, and the was only one other table there, so we were able to get fast service.  The entire dining area could hold probably 40-50 people if maxed out.  Decorations are quaint and the atmosphere is quite comfortable and family oriented.  The menu posted here on Yelp is just their to-go menu, their dine-in menu is way more extensive.  Also, make sure to check the overhead dry-erase boards when you enter for Chef recommendations, specials, and in stock-items that may not be on the menu as well.  We were not charged for free refills on pots of delicious hot green tea.

Their sushi is decent and to the point. So don't come here expecting anything creative or inexpensive because it is exactly the opposite at I Ai in the case of sushi only.  The said that their most popular roll is the Special Mexican Roll ($9.00), so I gave it a try.  It was very solid, with the perfect rice to filling ratio and decent flavor.  However, it wasn't nearly as exciting as their kitchen items, and not much different than sushi I could find closer to home for the same quality and price.  

In my personal opinion, I will not order sushi here again, because their cooked kitchen items are so delicious and inexpensive- it is  like nothing else you will find in the Tampa area.  Don't get me wrong, the sushi is solid, but there is so much other food there that I prefer.

If you are looking for homemade Japanese food, then this is your place.  Nothing is too fancy.  It is great to taste and experience foods that Japanese people would like to enjoy on an everyday basis, not just special occasion.  My husband referred to some items as "diner food."  The Okonomiyaki ($8.00) is a Japanese pancake similar to Korean Pajeon.  It is a vegetable pancake that contains pork and covered in a sweet brown sauce and mayo, then a sprinkle of dancing bonito shavings.  The serving is very large, enough for an entire meal with maybe a side of soup or salad.  This pancake only comes in one house flavor, usually shops with specialize in this dish and serve up many custom and specialty flavors, but I Ai just has one for you to try.  It is delicious and crispy, while being creamy, tangy, and smokey at the same time.  

The Age Tofu ($4.00) is served up my favorite way, where the cubes of fried tofu are floating in dashi broth with shaved radish on top.  So you eat it with a spoon to get a bite of tofu and some delicious broth at the same time.   The Sunomono ($4.00) was bright and refreshing with cucumber, crab stick, and a sweet shrimp on top- all covered in a sour citrus dressing.  I always have to order the Omusubi (Onigiri) if it is offered, especially when they are only $2.00 each for your choice of mouth-watering bonito, plum, or salmon fillings.  They are the side of a small hamburger and just as filling, so watch out.  The Soy Sauce Ramen ($7.00) was a large serving and the noodles were perfectly chewy with flavorful broth.  

I was a little confused from the other photos posted here of small vegetable side dishes, which made me assume that I Ai served up complimentary side dishes with an entrée.   That is not the case.  Most of the side dishes (similar to Korean banchan, but not complimentary) range from $2.00-$4.00 per serving.  We tried the Yama Sengiui ($4.00) which was julienne strips of slimy mountain potato-like root.  Sally recommends trying it graded with tuna for the same price next time, and we will.

The Shabu-Shabu is what I came for.  While they had many stone pot soups- the cook at your table experience of Shabu-Shabu was $28.00, and I just was not ready to pay that much per person yet on my first try.

I can definitely see I Ai having many regulars because of their cheap menu, delicious food, cute atmosphere, and fast service.  We will definitely return to try more items, since we probably just scratched the surface here today.  As I said before; it is impossible to find everyday Japanese food like this in the Tampa area.  Maybe in New York City, but not here, so I feel very lucky to have found I Ai.  I was very impressed when dining here, and also had a fun time.  Compared to other establishments in Tampa- 5 stars.

Tons of food $44.41 before tip

If you search "ramen" in Tampa Bay, surprisingly this is one of the places that pops up in the search.  So, I just had to give them a try.  Yes, I have eaten ramen at every restaurant in Florida and Georgia (also eaten ramen in Japan, Korea, NYC, etc)--- so far The Mango Tree's miso or miso tonkotsu ramen is my favorite in Tampa Bay.  Even better when I order the set with the little basket of ebi fry on the side.  It is expensive, but totally worth it when craving ramen.

Even though this is ramen is not Japanese made, the chashu pork is cooked tender and perfectly rolled.  The egg is not a tea egg, salt egg, or even soft boiled.  I recommend adding corn.

The service at Mango Tree is TERRIBLE, aloof, and unorganized.  Last time I visited, they were open at 11:00AM, doors open.  Waiter and sushi chef did not arrive until almost 12:30!!!  We watched many customers arrive, wait around and leave.  But, I was determined to stick it out for the sake of the two sweet old ladies working in the kitchen-  they were so desperately trying to help us, even gave us a salad to calm our nerves.

Being really unimpressed by the Hokkaido ramen served at that other place in Tampa, I would prefer to come to DTSP instead anyday.

I have only been here twice, and twice felt the cold airs put on by both the female owner and the lady working behind the counter. The pastries were great, and the coffee and drinks are better. The place was very clean, and it is certainly a go-to for many in the North End, and very busy on the weekends. I just couldn't overlook the fact that the service was just lousy--they acted dismissive, arrogant, and unkind. I also happened to witness a very rude conversation that went on between the female owner and her employee, with sarcastic comments about "how smart" people were in Boise. This was after a lady had come in asking a simple question about the desserts. 

Great desserts, but not enough to justify the attitude towards customers in this place.

I'm going to say it... I've never been to a poke bar before, but I really enjoyed this experience! The fish quality was nice, the price reasonable, the service friendly, and the decor was cool. They definitely have a few processes to optimize along the way, but for Day 2 this place ran really well. 

I was so excited to see this place finally open up after walking by the "opening soon" window decals for so long. We need an alternative to AYCE sushi in Reno that isn't prohibitively expensive, and this really fits the bill. It also helps that this spot is only a couple blocks from our home, so we were definitely hoping we would love it. 

There are two main styles of this to get here: poke bowl (rice bowl  + diced seafood + toppings) or burrito (wrap the former in nori). The menu is kind of hard to read from the beginning of the bar, so it makes the ordering process confusing. There are two main types of rice, and you want the purple rice for sure (red bean paste mixed in?) because it's freaking delicious. There was a nice menu of burrito options, though I was really unclear on if you could order the burritos as a bowl. As a poke novice, I would have appreciated a curated bowl so I could be more informed about what I liked and disliked the next time. I opted to just order the poke bowl a la cart, and got tons of yummy vegetables with my salmon, tuna, and yellowtail (easily the best of the bunch) "scoops". They had a ton of sauces (I did their house sauce) to top it off, but could have used sriracha at the tables to add as you go. 

Its a bit confusing where to go when you walk in, but the start of the line is on the side of the bar closest to the entrance. This makes a lot of sense for how things flow, but it would have been helpful for there to be a "Start Here" sign. We saw a few other folks enter and wander for a minute trying to figure out where to start ordering! 

They were the bowls on a plastic tray with a piece of parchment-y paper under it, presumably to keep the trays clean. They're kind of big and jabbed me a couple times while eating, but also beware that they're slippery against that plastic tray and plastic poke bowl!! I clumsily dropped my bowl on the floor and made a messy rice pile that the staff were extremely gracious about cleaning up. Oops. 

We will definitely be back here, and hope they have or get a nice system for ordering takeout! Love seeing new businesses coming to Midtown and seeing the seafood scene extend beyond AYCE.

California Pasta is super simple, and quite amazing. Located at this outdoor mall area, and can be missed if you don't deviate from the main street. While it may not look like they get busy, they do. People were coming and going while I was eating, and all the tables just outside of the door were filled. It may not look like a fancy place, but the food is great. This is where you go when you want great quality food for a good price, and as quickly as possible. They're quite efficient and we had our food in front of us in no time.

I had the Chipotle Chicken Panini, which comes with a side of pasta salad. While the panini was delicious, I advise against the Pasta Salad. There's little to no flavor at all. I don't remember if there is an alternative to the pasta salad.

Okay, everyone has a bucket list right? This was the only reason I traveled to Philly from NYC....so I could eat a phillycheese steak IN Philly. One of the most disappointing experiences of my life, other than trying to walk around in the humidity. This place is a complete tourist trap, because the only people you see here and across the street are tourist. Everyone's shoving a soggy roll of bread with some flavorless meat into their mouths. Dry or juicy, they'll take it. I even saw a table that brought their own Pringles and drinks. It's really that serious....

$11 for a Cheese Steak. I took 2 bites and tossed the rest into the trash. I can't justify ever eating another one in this life time. You literally walk up to the window, tell them what you want, and they hand it to you. That's how big of a trap it is, lol. It's also cash only! The number of tourists coming here, and it's cash only. Now, THAT'S how you avoid paying taxes :-) Just saying...

First time trying Peruvian food and it lived up to the hype. We were greeted with fried corn which was light and a great snack. The CHICHA SOUR is a great drink, supposedly similar to a margarita but nothing like it. It reminds me of the Jamaican drink sorrel with a hint of cinnamon and tequila. 

The ceviche (CEBICHES) is the best you will ever have. Peruvian CEBICHES comes with spice. I choose medium which was hot. 

I ordered the Jaleas which was the fried white fish w/calamari, shrimp, mussels and octopus. Possibly the best fried fish I have had, it was so light and flaky. I will definitely be back to go through the menu. 

Also loved the ambience. See ceiling...

I should have checked Yelp before we came here. Maybe it was good that we didn't so Yelp had no influence on my review. 
Came here with my best friend for a very early dinner. It was only 5 PM and, of course, we were the first ones there. 
We started off by sharing a spinach salad. It was delicious. Spinach, pine nuts, tomatoes and bacon. For our entrees my friend had clams and linguine and I had gnocchi in pomodoro sauce. The clam dish was so salty I begged my friend to send it back but she refused. She ate 1/2 and set it aside. I am like her in that I am always to shy to send something back. I don't think I have ever ordered gnocchi in my life but I thought with that light sauce it might be good. Wrong! The sauce was even heavier then what you get in the South Philly red gravy restaurants. The gnocchi was good enough but the sauce weighed it down.
Since we ate at Melograno 2 nights ago and the check price was the same, we wont be coming back here again.

Aaah sweet ReAnimation!! 

Great espresso extraction, brown sugar notes, berries, sweet not over roasted  and for that it keep the fruit notes, sweetness and great balance of acidity. Now, this is how it's made! I use to love Ultimo Cafe in Phily, but about a year ago something changed and even though it's getting a lot of hype is not my favorite anymore. (Not consistent enough and terrible service...: "Ultimo Cafe")

I have bought ReAnimator coffee bans before and they have proven consistent over a one year period. I'm so exited that I finally got to come to their coffee shop. It was as good as you can expect.  The hipster Baristas are friendly, knowledgeable about the product and therefore getting the optional taste on their extractions and brewing. 

The place is industrial looking with great ample space for savoring and concentrating on work.

Caffeine, the name tells it all...Its all about the sweet sirupy elixir! 

This place is really an example to anyone's standard. Their brewing methods they use are the aero press, V-69, Chemex, cold brew and of course regular drip and the star of all... espresso.

I have tried all of their brews and with three of their baristas and also by their lovely manager. I tell you, they are right on point in every one of them. 

I've recently did a review of another local coffee in Tampa and I criticized their method and pricing. It's very refreshing to come back to the second coffee place I've tried since I stayed here, and do it with great pleasure. Their single espresso is a 1,50 and the double 2,50. Their price is half of their competitors and not because of its quality, but because is just at the right price. 

Caffeine is simply a classic, all you need to feel like in  Napoli,  Italy having a coffee is simply  to ask for a single espresso, give it a sip, close your eyes for a moment and your are going to be transported immediately there. I have not asked but I'm quite sire they use the European standard ratio.  

The atmosphere is also very welcoming; small, intimate, inviting but at the same time with your own sense of space. I belive they use their space to its full potential. Not to mention how well trained their Barista team is, super friendly and informative.

If you are a local this is your place to have your morning brew or come and catch up with some emails and work while enjoying the feel and their wonderful coffee. If you are like me, just passing by, then skip the museum and just  come to Caffeine  :))

Happy ! 

It's such a nice feeling to see a small family run business grow and improve. One can not give nothing but five stars to a place that in a years time, not only have they kept their personable service, but they are even friendlier( if that's even possible) but they have improved in many points all while keeping everything that makes them special and their price point. 

1-They have purchased a commercial espresso maker !!  
2-Are more efficient and have more items in their menu. 
3- looks like they have an AC unit(didn't feel it working but it's installed) I guess for next summer they will have it blasting cool air. 

This is truly a gem of a place, that makes you feel like they known you from years and have EXCELLENT products. 


Love this place!

Elusive Ginger Beard! 

I walked by it a couple of times and getting ready to try it again. Luckily I'm not the only one that can't  find the place and a nice gentleman with a smile, asked me: are you by any chance looking for the coffee place ? 

It turns out the Ginger Coffee is actually named Pour House!!... not the smartest thing to do. 

In any case, I order my red-velvet doughnut which was delicious; fluffy moist and not so sweet. For me, the star of the place. The espresso in the other hand was just bland, lacked flavor, aromas and the syrupy magic that makes a great espresso. The cappuccino was a big bowl of milk and some espresso. I'm sorry to write this review because the big  red bearded guys that work there are Great! Unfortunately not their barista skills. Nice latte art but bad ratios. That cappuccino tasted like hot milk. 

I guess is made for locals that know to come here for a great doughnut and latter stay for a good  selection of two beers. From the Salzburg Stigel beer to their home made in Tampa beer. 

My suggestion, have a doughnut and pair it with a good stout! 

P.S. 
For the owners:  lower your coffee prices. 
That was not a 3 dollar  espresso nor a 4 dollar cappuccino.

When my friend and I visited Kyuramen for dinner this place was absolutely packed! Long story short I wouldn't be surprised if Kyuramen became the next go-spot for people in the SJ area.

What I really enjoyed most about Kyuramen were the vibes I was getting. There are open table seating areas, seats at the ramen bar, and also individualized/separate booths in the back for larger parties.

We were treated so well by the staff and they were very attentive, checking in on us frequently. When it comes to the food, Kyuramen has a but more items on the menu than other nearby ramen places which includes specialty drinks (both the Thai Iced Tea and Cucumber Lemonade were delicious) and the omurice, which they cut open in front of you and dress with gravy.

My favorite item on the menu I will say was my Sapporo Miso Ramen. I really don't think you can go wrong with the ramen. I do wish the noodles were firmer though. Out of all the appetizers, I liked the takoyaki the most followed by the pork bao bun and potato shrimp. The despite the fancy presentation, the omurice was just okay.

At the end of the day, Kyuramen is a great place to hang with a friend and eat some good ramen. Definitely has a lot of potential too! Excited to see how this place grows and changes over time. Will be back soon : )

Let me start this review with a brief description of my coffee credentials, starting with my equipment: I have a Rancilio Silvia espresso machine, a Technivorm Moccamaster drip coffee maker, and a Sterling Pro French press. I have a couple of Moka pots from Italy that my sister gave me, but I don't use them because of the temperature at which they make coffee.

I also have a Baratza Virtuoso grinder, and a Capresso grinder. If you know coffee gear, you will know from the equipment I just listed that I am a borderline coffee fanatic. Serious fanatics would have spent three times what I have on the grinders, and at least twice on the coffee makers. They typically roast their coffee themselves, whereas I buy my coffee already roasted.

I have also traveled to countries with serious coffee cultures, such as Italy, France, Japan, Korea, Mexico, etc. Lastly, I have had scones from many different establishments in the UK, served with clotted cream and jam, in other words, the proper way to serve scones.

I do not understand the negative reviews of Raging Sage. The coffee is amongst the best I have had anywhere. Let me repeat that point: the coffee is amongst the best I have had anywhere. This little coffee shop and micro-roastery has good suppliers, skilled roasters, and expert baristas. I recommend their coffee, unequivocally.

I first visited on Friday, August 26th, for a meeting with a colleague and fellow coffee enthusiast. As I am new to Tucson, he recommended Raging Sage for its coffee and its sage scones (covered in jalapeno jelly). Since that initial visit, I have been back three times, once to pick up a pound of House Blend and Ethiopian Yirgacheffe, another time to pick up sage and jalapeno scones, and a third time to pick up a pound of Tanzanian Peaberry (which the manager, Kay, had set aside for me at my request). The running joke in my household has become my dog Ellie complaining we drive to Raging Sage too often.

If you will forgive the pun, I have become a raging fan of Raging Sage.

Yes, the premises are small and often crowded. Yes, they run out of scones very early in the day. No, they do not serve clotted cream with their scones (not many places in America do), and no, their scones are not authentic British scones. They're better.

As for service, I have nothing but praise for the baristas and Kay, the manager. I have found my go-to coffee roastery in Tucson. I am a happy camper.

So I came here for dinner with some friends a bit skeptical knowing the hype that's around this place (and knowing a lot of the time the hype is a bit overrated). Butttttt, Suraya is the REAL DEAL! As for logistics, I would 100% recommend a reservation. We had a res for 5 PM on a Saturday and there were already a bunch of people waiting when we walked in at 4:50 PM. 

Service was excellent the whole time. We were seated right away. Water was full the whole time. Our server was attentive but not hovering. She was super sweet and made great recommendations for us first-timers. 

Now for the food... everything was AMAZING! We ordered some drinks (a beer and the Poet, a gin drink). Both were great. For apps, we got the baba ghanoush, labneh, crispy potatoes, and sumac fries. For entrees, our meat eating friend ordered the lamb kebabs and loved them. My only gripe is that there were no vegetarian entrees available on the menu. The chef was able to prepare an eggplant dish that I believe is from their tasting menu -- this was the only dish that wasn't a hit for me. I won't ding a star for this because they were accommodating and able to prepare a vegetarian entree.

Overall, I know I'll definitely be back! I'm hoping to come for brunch and try that amazing cruller I'm always seeing.

i can see how people would think this place has spotty service - but i think its part of the charm.  they literally make your food when you order it, which explains the timing complaints. my service was fantastic though. 

upon entering this warm and cozy little spot we seated ourselves and informed the server that we were vegan.  she straight up said - we can make almost anything vegan - we can sub tofu for anything - just tell me what you like and we can customize it for you. 

we ordered eggplant parm and gnocchi and broccoli rabe.  it was delish. the next time i go back i'm going to call ahead and order tofu Marsala and ravioli. 

vegan pro tip:  call a day before you're coming in and they will make you a vegan cannolli.

OK OK OK .... the reviews for this store are HARSH.  i think it's because most of the grad hospital residents / yelpers are from the serious suburbs and have no concept of living in a larger city.  as far as traditional city/neighborhood grocers go, this place is truly four stars.   

* comparing the produce to rittenhouse market - it's def. a little cheaper.  
* comparing the produce quality to trader joes - it's def a little bit better quality.  

As a vegan i primarily shop at whole foods and farmers markets but who *always* has that kind of time?  if i missed something or if i need something immediately i typically find it at south square.  

also i feel that they are trying to be better.  they now have all types of organic, and veg based mock meats, a whole section of newmans fair trade chocolates, they have dibruno brothers pre packaged foods, (which i dont eat but i have friends obsessed with them) they have sales and you can use coupons - i mean whats really here to hate on?  

yeah they are more expensive than superfresh - but where is the closest superfresh? south and 10th? i mean factor in the time to walk or the cab and you've immediately lost your competitive advantage. and honestly south square and that specific superfresh are pretty much on even footing.  

i appreciate that this is a place i can pop into on my way home from work, pick up some almond milk, a seltzer, maybe organic chips and bobbi's hummus, and walk away with an organic tomato.  maybe i'm just simple? or maybe i just manage my expectations of what south square can offer in relation to their building size and location.  

for all of you complaining, maybe you should speak to the manager of the store about what you want, because i have found that when i have asked for things, they have magically appeared.

Best pancakes in South Jersey.  I'm going on record and I will vouch for it.  These pancakes are only rivaled by those at the Fountain Diner in Hartsdale, NY.

If you're not a fan of pancakes... I think you'll still find something on this menu that reads like a short story.   This menu is MASSIVE.  It's a South Jersey diner, I guess that's par for the course.

I've been here a half a dozen times and I haven't had anything I didn't like it.  If you can dream it and it's breakfast related, they will make it.

Sometimes the service can be slow because it is a busy spot, but regardless, I love this place. 

Forget the Pop Shop, this is the place in the Collingswood area for breakfast.

So dissapointing.  Having read recent glowing reviews on Yelp and Urban Spoon, I decided Bricks would be the place to have my birthday dinner.  We started with the escargot stuffed mushrooms.  This was the best of the evening and even that wasn't quite right.  The dish was overpowered by the blue cheese, but I love blue cheese so I scarfed it down.  Next up, our entrees.  Husband had the veal.  It was "breaded" and overcooked.  It was accompanied with pappadrelle noodles that my 5 year old eats with garlic and butter, these noodles didn't even have that going for them.  I had the lobster thermador.  It had the right seafood in it, but that is as close as it comes to lobster thermador.  Rather than a creamy white wine sauce with a broiled parmesan topping, this was cooked in a creamy dijon mustard sauce that took over the lobster, shrimp and scallops (did I mention they were like eating rubber?).  We decided to forgo the deserts, I just could bear anymore disapointment.

p.s., At $30-100 per entree, I would expect a restaurant that has ballcapless clientele, but alas, it is Reno.

Worst meal ever. Meatballs mealy, mushy. Pasta cut up and of course, not al dente. Asked for bread twice before receiving it and then it was cold and served in a paper dish. 
So very disappointing after all of the hype.

My review stands. My $10 drink (yes, it was ten dollars after tax), came in a small glass. It may have been "vintage", but it was small. This was not during a crowded time, as the owner suggested. This was at 8pm on Monday or Tuesday. 

Maybe if the management spends less time second-guessing the less-than-stellar reviews left by its clientele, their food and drinks would be better. Docking a star for the Spanish Inquisition-style approach to following up on negative feedback.

I'll jump on the bandwagon. Ordered food to go the other night after reading the reviews. I ordered, the Burrata ($5.95), the Spaghetti Vincenzo (Shrimp cappers in a cognac pink sauce for $14.95), the Ravioli of the Day ($16.95) today it was the saffron with ricotta, then both desserts Cannoli ($2.45) and the Tiramisu $4.95. We were going to get the lasagna to go, to cook the following night, but they didn't have it available that day.

When I got to the restaurant, they have the tables spaces around the edges of the walls, and there were two tables taken. The restaurant is clean, and has updated check out system with the digital pad. There is a cold case by the register with take out containers of to go pasta and sauces. The portion size I saw for one of the pasta dishes looked huge! There were 4 or 5 employees, which actually surprised me, but i took it as a good sign. Dishwasher, I think a chef or two in what I am assuming is training, and I think the famous Paulo, as well as another older looking chef. There was a bit of confusion with my order, one of the items got messed up so I did have to wait a tiny bit longer than normal, but overall, everyone was super nice, and I didn't mind waiting. 

We dug in when we got home, the pasta come with portions of delicious finely crumbled cheese and little rolls of sliced bread. My husband annihilated the raviolis, i got a half of one, and they were indeed tasty, and decadent. My shrimp pasta was hearty and filling and the flavor was something I've never personally tasted, a little sweet, a little tangy, slight creaminess, the tomato was not overpowering at all. I really enjoyed the  taste profile, different than anything I've been exposed to as far as italian goes. Also my pasta was perfect, I was hoping the chef would account for the travel time, and I wouldn't have soft pasta and it was perfectly aldente. 

The burrata was so damn fresh and light. The tomato had flavor imparted on it from the olive oil, seasoning and pesto, and the burrata itself was creamy, light, and barely tangy. A really nice addition to the pasta. 

The cannoli also was filling and hearty, a single one is a lot! I think we both preferred the tiramisu though just barely. Not heavy, light and creamy. 

Overall, we really enjoyed the meal, my husband also gave it 5 stars, and we both want to try other sauces, especially the lasagna or the Bolognese sauce! 

Great addition to the food scene, I hope that by having this simple yet expertly done menu, that they stay alive. It is a good model for to go right now, the food doesn't suffer at all, and once covid ends, can't wait to dine in. Also the to go packaging looks to be sustainable friendly. A lot of is is recyclable or paper, another plus!

So I guess I need to eat my words a bit from my last review, saying I didn't consider it for a nice dinner out. Well New Years 2022 and 2+ years of covid, we needed something to kickstart the year. A couple friends and us decided to try out a pre fixe menu this year and out of many good look choices, Washoe Public Houses was the most intriguing.

For appetizers we tried the lobster egg rolls and the venison tartare. I don't think I have ever had tartare before and holy smokes, this version was delicious! Just enough seasoning and coating (I believe its egg), with a crispy baguette slice and a pinch of freshness from sprouts. I found the flavor of the meat to still come through while not being overpowering. And not gamey at all considering it was venison. The lobster egg rolls was a good portion size, only a bit surprised at shredded lobster (was it imitation then?) instead of chunks which was more what we were expecting, but once again, a perfect blend of flavors in one bite. 

After a good start on appetizers, we ordered between us the lamb chops, the bison prime rib and the duck meal. Everything I tasted, the meat was melt in your mouth delicious. I didn't taste much more of the duck dish but it was a hefty portion. The bison primerib came with mashed (creamy) potatoes and some roasted root veggies. The lamb, was Borda Ranch lamb which is local, and some of the best I've ever had. The chops sat atop a bed of cheesy, creamy polenta that I couldn't get enough of. 

Lastly we had a few desserts, I had the creme brûlée and tried the dark chocolate cake, both were decadent, but the creme brûlée hit the spot as usual. 

Overall the service for the dinner was outstanding, we were taken care of well and checked in with often. The food hit the spot and we left very very happy. 

This experience has reopened up this restaurant for me as far as an option for a date night. The chef does seem to be super creative and personally, love a changing menu. We will be back!

Wow. 

If you follow me, you'd clearly know I have a true sushi addiction. I came here after returning something at H&M, but really I only hauled myself to the mall on a Friday night so I'd have a reason to try this out. I can eat sushi for basically any meal (or snack)... any day, any time. But I figured to save a few pesos, I'd try this out (I had my own ingredients at home, but still needed to prep and that felt like blah after a week of work) and hopefully hedge off the basic continuous sushi craving existing in my body. 

I ordered the spicy tuna, without avocado and added lemon. While the service is pretty good, I mean really hard to judge at a food court/cafeteria style place, but the boys were for the most part polite. The roll is about $10.52 after tax and I added a small tip. 

I watched the assembly line making of my sushiritto. I was impressed as I felt they did put a lot of stuff in there. The crystal shrimpies are small though. I incorrectly assumed that there would be some automatic sauces, not that I need sauces to enjoy sushi. I got ponzu thinking soy sauce was a given, its not fyi. I stole some soy sauce packets from one of the Chinese places a few spots over.

I notice they like glue the paper around the sushirrito with a smeared triangle of smashed to oblivion rice. I don't care for that, it makes it even more messy, we aren't eating the paper, so why have is so tight around it? I took my first bite and was definitely disappointed. Even with the crystal shrimp, the texture was all pretty mushy. The lemon rind was pretty large and therefore, made the roll fairly bitter. There just wasn't a sushi flavor at all for me. Even the crab seemed like it was off or different, like maybe its American made imitation crab instead of Japanese (yes, there is a difference). 

I obviously would never make a trip to the mall just for this, but I suppose if I was stuck in the a mall I would have another go, there is something about mall food, almost its own food group, and I don't mind the Wetzel's pretzels and Tokyo Grill stuff, so there is actually some competition, revisiting isn't completely out of the question, but only if in the mall.

Two stars for being a Taiwanese restaurant in Indy. Taiwanese restaurants are hard to come by in the US and although this one is hardly Taiwanese, for one that is in Indy it isn't the worst. It would be unfair, I guess, to compare it with restaurants in Taiwan or Sacramento. I really really wanted to love this place, being from Taiwan, but I must speak the truth. I regret not having talked directly with the owner while I was there, but I sincerely hope that he will read these suggestions from a Taiwanese person who truly wants the restaurant to succeed.

1. The tea drinks contain zero tea. The almond milk tea tasted like almond powder blended with creamer. Now, I do understand that perhaps a non-Asian palate would enjoy a not so tea-y drink, but such tea drinks absolutely cannot be enjoyed by someone like myself.

2. The menu was scarce with Taiwanese dishes. The only items which were Taiwanese are the fried chicken nuggets, fried pork. Everything else was regular Chinese food.

3. The quality of ingredients are fine, however none of the dishes tasted Taiwanese.

One may argue that the dishes and taste are altered to suit Americans, since this restaurant is not in an area where a large Asian population exists. However, if a restaurant's intent is not to deliver what it claims to, then simply don't claim to deliver any such thing. For example, if you had changed the name to something that has nothing to do with Taiwan or tea, then I wouldn't expect you to have Taiwanese tasting food and drinks that actually contained tea.

I hate to say this, but this was one of the worst Taiwanese style meals I have ever had. And I feel almost embarrassed that patrons of this place would be inclined to think that what they serve is Taiwanese. In all seriousness, my mom and I can both cook better Taiwanese style dishes than what's served here.

I believe that the owner, who is Taiwanese, knows that what's served isn't good. This review is left with good intentions and I hope that he will take my advice to heart.

Chewing over which bakery in Tampa to visit for a small wedding cake was tiring day in and day out leading up to our flight. And the fear of disappointment of buying a stale, tasteless cake was real. 

When hubs found out his nephew and his new wife didn't plan on having a wedding cake (¯\_(ツ)_/¯) after dinner, I came across a few that were closed for the Holiday season- but we certainly lucked out on this one on Cypress St in West Tampa. Hubs stepped it up and got them one they would appreciate to celebrate their special day. 

Aside from the long-standing history here, hubs ordered and paid by phone from NY with ease. And when we came here to pick up the cake, the smell of sweets was all around even with my mask on. Glass shelving with fig bread, cookies and unusual pastry+fruit combinations I've haven't seen at any NYC Italian bakery I've been to. 

The price is right, service is plentiful from any counter you go up to and the Strawberry Shortcake hubs got for his nephew was very good. The cream seemed like a lot on top- but it was actually good, the cake itself was spongey-soft and strawberries tasted like strawberries. 
 
I may not be Italian, but I feel like a neighborhood isn't complete without a family-run spot for fresh-baked bread, cannolis, cakes, zeppoles, paninis, Pignoli cookies and the obligatory rainbow cookies. This one is it.

¿Dónde está la fiesta? Right here on Davis Islands! This was an excellent Friday night end to hub's nephew's wedding earlier that morning. Since we had dinner a few hours prior to coming here, drinks were the only thing on our minds. Located on E. Davis Blvd in Davis Islands, Margaritas was all that and then some. We sat outside. Period. Plus coming from NY, the palm trees and weather all said, "Tropics in December"- much appreciated.  There was no way to argue that since this was our first time in Tampa. 

The server accommodated us right in front  of the Latin salsa band and to be honest, the music wasn't thumping in our ears like you'd think. To add, we were talking for hours on end the entire night without yelling and popping a jugular. 

Two large complimentary tortilla chip baskets and salsa were placed on both end of the tables. Chips were large- but on the thin side and salsa had good flavor- but loose. Frozen Margaritas ordered were packed real good and my classic-ish, salted rim, French Chambord Margarita had a nice kick too. Sounds like their food isn't a standout, but for a Friday night drink spot, it did nicely.

Just a short bridge over from downtown Tampa into Harbour Island is all it took to come here and enjoy what we thought will be a lite nosh before our flight to NY. I had been eyeing Watervue on Harbour Island for my family as well as my nephew-in-law and his wife for lunch, but since our trip was an extremely short one, lunch without the newlyweds before flying, was in order. 

I almost feel Watervue is a hidden Harbour Island gem because there weren't that many people dining in. Or maybe it was the time we came in. But its full frontal view of the water, adds a dramatic pop when you're dining in or out. Randy was a sweetheart over the phone and she gave me the green light for my party of 5 to come right over. Watervue's layout is grey, black woods, glass windows (and lots of it) and the hexagonal dark grey tiles, add another showy pop. 

The menu is simple, not incredibly big- but sounds very nice. Hubs loved his sandwich Cubano that was filled with perfectly thin sliced meat. His auntie had the Fish & chips and loved it, hub's sister had the Lobster Fritters, her 12 yr old grandson had a burger and I loved my Arugula Salad topped with Shrimp, my Truffle Brussel Sprouts with Parmesan cheese were exceptional. I also ordered the Lobster Fritters- but they should've been called 'Lobster Hush Puppies'. No ill feelings- I just expected a bigger lobster presence in the 'Fritters' because they were either microscopic or had the 'flavor' of lobster. Good though- with that slight crunch outside and moistness inside. 

Randy was awesome and was patient with my sister-in-law's grandson's burger request. Overall, the food was awesome and Watervue offered us a moment of calm before heading to the airport.

WOW!! This place met my expectations. M3 DELIVERED!! I was cruising around yelp one day and pictures of M3 caught my eye. After looking at the pics and reading the reviews it was a must try!!!  
The Atmosphere was very nice, I love the water glasses so cute. I ordered the Salmon Tacos and was not disappointed. What I loved the most was the fact that they were served on a white corn tortillas and they were crunchy!! I hate soggy tortillas...not this one they were perfect. I had the clam chowder as my side....Oh My Chowder!!! It  was delicious. I was kind of sad I couldn't eat it all in one sitting, but very happy I had more to enjoy later. 

The manger Bill came to our table and talked with us for some time, he is a very nice man. I cant wait to return and try more of there delicious menu.

What do you do on your first night out of lock down? Drag Queen bingo of course, at The Emerson Bar"!!! I cant think of a better way to celebrate!! But for real, I had so much fun last night.

I was really impressed, buy this place the atmosphere was so nice, it's a beautiful bar, I love the Vibe, it's light and fun. I heard the food is amazing, but unfortunately last night they were not serving, I hope I get to try it soon.  

The cocktails were amazing and have a beautiful presentation. I only tried the  "The VIRGINA St" it was AMAZING!!! SO GOOD!! I WANTED 15 OF THEM. I really enjoyed this place, I will be back!

There is some serious burger competition here in Reno, Juicy's is usually my go to burger stop! I cant turn down their bacon cheeseburger, it just the right amount of deliciousness in your mouth. From the meat to the cheese, from the bun to the lettuce, tomatoes and onions!! ITS JUST SO DANG GOOD, and the right amount of juice is running down your hands.

THE FRIES, OHH THE FRIES....Juicy's hands down, has my favorite fries, they are fried to perfection. Everyone you put into your mouth has the perfect amount of crunch, I cant stand soggy fries. The fries dipped in the ranch, will make your mouth seriously happy!

Lets talk about the real reason I come to this burger joint, THE KILLER CHICKEN SANDWITCH!! It is KILLER,, its a juicy chicken breast, covered with cheese and bacon. With mayo and mustard, lettuce, tomatoes and onions on there sesame bun. It's the best chicken samich I've ever had. TRY IT PEOPLE!!

Oh, Burger Up, where should I begin? I've given you more than a few fair shakes - four to be exact and every time I walk away disappointed and angry. Let's start with my personal biases - I hate large table seating. When I go out to dinner and intend to sit at a table, I generally expect it to be a personal table, an intimate experience between my guests and I, not a picnic with strangers. But I get it, it's a small space, and communal seating is an easy way to maximize volume. Also I hate the napkins. As someone who has worked in the industry for many years, seeing bar rags on my table (regardless of their cleanliness and starchy feel), touching my cutlery and, ultimately my face, disgusts me. 

Moving on to the food. Three out of four times, I've gotten different variations of their burgers. Fool me once, fool me twice, fool me three times - I just feel stupid. For the past twenty years of my adult, burger eating life, I have been ordering burgers medium rare. This temperature, in my experience, is extremely attainable. Sure sometimes its on the rare or medium side but who cares - it's not a filet. Nope, not for BURGER Up, medium rare somehow always turns out well done. Now, maybe I'm being picky, but if you are bold enough to name your restaurant after your main menu item, you better figure out how to cook it properly. The last, and final time I went to B.U. I ordered the citrus salmon burger, which managed to be bland and fishy without  any sign of citrus. I actually had to ask my server for a lemon wedge to cut through the terrible flavor. Luckily, my server was near by! Literally. He was sitting at the table next to me, hanging out with his off-shift coworkers. The only thing that could have made my experiences worse would have been food poisoning.

Since writing the review below I've received 4 messages from Yelp users calling me an idiot and accusing me of never having eaten at this restaurant. The strange thing about these messeges is that they have been sent by Yelp users that have no history having posted here. My suspicion is that they were written by employee's or the owner of Sup.

To clarify my review for the owners that are butt hurt that I hate their place. I have eaten at your restaurant 3 separate times. The first time was 2 weeks after you opened. I had the cheese/brocolli soup with a side salad. The salad was good and I thought the addition of currents was a good idea. The salad dressing was so tart that I thought the acid would burn through the lining of my throat. The cheese in the soup tasted burnt .. the brocolli wasn't a factor.

The second time I went I had the tortilla soup. It was under spiced and served luke warm. The seasoning seemed off.. There was a bitter after taste that I couldn't place. I'm thinking it was oregano but may be mistaken on that. I also had a cheese sandwich. I was really looking forward to this as I dig soup and grilled cheese. The sandwich came out, like the soup, luke warm. The cheeses used didn't compliment each other and the sandwich was dry. How a grilled cheese with all that grease could be dry I have no idea, but it was. Strike 2...

The last and final time I tried your restaurant was the day before I wrote the review below. On this visit I had the posole... what a joke. Have your cooks ever actually eaten posole? The flavors were completely off on what should have been a rich flavorful soup. I suspect that the base of this soup was the same as the tortilla soup I had tried on the privious visit as it had the same weird after taste.. again.. too much oregano? Not sure... 

As for the people that write amazing reviews here for this place I say good on ya for loving bland under flavored soups. 

I just want to warn those that do appreciate complex dishes to stay away. Open a can of Progresso and save yourself the $8...








I hate this place.. Sorry but I've been 3 times now and every time I think 'I'm gonna write a review on Yelp'.. This time I am writing one.

First off this place is all location, location, location. They thrive off of the same idiots that think sushi is Japanese cuisine. If you were raised eating bland Midwestern flavorless food you'll love this place.

However if you appreciate complex flavors stay away. I can't believe with the myriad of soup recipes in the world the best a dedicated soup restaurant can come up with is cheese and broccoli and weak ass tomato bisque. 

It just saddens me that people love this place. Just goes to show how little Reno has progressed 

If you want good soup go have Thai.

Stopped in for a quick lunch on Saturday.  Very friendly staff.

Had the posole and it was delicious.  Also had a smoothie that was quite nice as well.

Would gladly return if I am in the neighborhood.

We chose Datz in St. Pete due to the fact that it had an interesting food and drink menu, it was casual, and that it was literally a block from our hotel (and we were exhausted). Since this is the "Time of Covid," we were very happy with the fact that they excelled in the art of Social Distancing and Cleanliness. It was very warm that evening so we chose to sit inside and we had a lovely booth/table combo inside. I was pleasantly surprised because the pictures online did not do this place justice, it is quite lovely.

Our waiter was a lovely young man, Skyler, who had an excellent sense of humor and took great care of us. Very grateful for that since we discovered that the cocktails served here are STRONG. I convinced my husband to try the Night Fury Cocktail and I had the Blackberry Sage Margarita. His was a citrusy vodka with edible glitter (teehee!!!) and mine was just delicious. We then had an appetizer called the Nom Noms which was a silly name for warm, soft pretzels with a queso and a stone ground mustard. Very good but the queso was a tad bit thin. Nothing beats a fresh pretzel though.

With dinner, we had a draft beer and cider to drink in nice, tall chilled glasses. Skyler also kept our water glasses filled as well.

Dinner was Spaghetti-IN-Meatball (not a typo) for my husband. It was silly but he enjoyed it. He said the meatball was rather meatloafy in taste and texture. I thought it was good. The sauce and pasta tasted good as well. It was fun food, especially if you're drinking.

I had the April in Paris sandwich. It was like a grilled cheese/caprese sandwich, but better! A grilled sourdough with BRIE, tomato, arugula, and a thin layer of pesto (just enough for a taste, not overpowering). It was HEAVENLY! The chips on the side were a disappointment. They were sweet & salty with a melty blue cheese drizzle. I'm not a fan of sweet potato chips. If I had known, I would have asked to substitute something else.

For dessert, we splurged and had the best chocolate cake in the world. It might be the booze talking or I might be right. I want to go back and try it again. It was called The Horse Soldier Bourbon Chocolate Cake. Yes, you could taste the bourbon IN the cake. Perfect combo. The cake was so decadent, but it wasn't heavy, it was light and fluffy. Seriously. We were so tempted to lick the plate clean. Mmm...

My husband asked Skyler if he could make him a cappuccino with a shot of bourbon in it to go with the cake, and once again, Skyler delivered. What a guy! I had a taste, perfect combo with dessert. I would have had one too if I wasn't such a lightweight. We had a wonderful time.

In fact, we had such a great time, when we woke up in the morning, I asked my husband where he wanted to go for breakfast and he said "DATZ!" LOL Well, no booze this time, we did have to eventually drive home.

The weather was gorgeous and cool so we asked to sit outside. I didn't realize that the patio was covered! Turns out, I had completely missed a whole section of the restaurant the evening before - there was a breezeway with tables and a very large patio off to the side. We sat in a booth in the breezeway area. Perfect temperature for a lovely day. Our waitress, Holly, took excellent care of us.

We had a carafe of water and my husband had plain drip coffee this time. I had the Salted Caramel Cold Brew. Wow, that put all other cold brew coffees to shame. It was SO GOOD.

Hubby ordered the Breakfast BLT. It was made with 2 eggs that were cooked just past medium, to the point where the yolk is still loose but not runny, so you can enjoy it in a sandwich but it's not dribbling down your chin when you eat it. Wow, talk about masterfully cooked. I had the Cheddar Encrusted Breakfast Tacos. WOW. They were HUGE. Yes, I ate them all. I didn't plan on it but I ended up eating them anyway. They were so good. The bacon on both was small, but thick and crisp. Good quality.

As for those cheese grits that came with both our breakfasts? Those were slap yer momma - no - slap yer grandmomma good! Holy mackerel, we both declared those the best cheese grits ever. Made with cream cheese, they were just so, so good. That is nothing new, I've added it before, but mine didn't taste anything like that. I would love to know their secret. (We had grits a few days later and my husband literally lamented the fact that they weren't as good as Datz's...)

We really had such a good time and enjoyed coming here. Everyone was very friendly and very proactive about cleanliness and sanitizing, etc. I know there is another one in Tampa that is closer to us, so we will try and see if we can visit that one soon! 

TL;DR? Try Datz! It's Great!

I see this place has gotten low ratings but I think its a good quiet place to get some breakfast. I went here a couple of times and enjoyed the food and staff each time. The staff is made up of elders, they are very nice. 

The food is good and cheap. The service is quick. Maybe I just had a better experience than other yelpers.

When I moved to New Orleans one of my first objectives was to find "my" Asian supermarket, and so I've found it with Hong Kong Food Market. A little bit of a hike from New Orleans proper, Hong Kong Market is situated well into Wank territory, but fear not it's worth the travel. 

This market has a great variety of fresh produce that range from the pedestrian to the strange. All of which are at a good price, $1 for a head of romaine lettuce, yes please! Although, the prices do vary during the week depending on freshness... later in the week better deals, but not bright and crisp produce. 

Also, you can't beat their seafood selection. They have huge tanks teaming with live tilapia, crabs, and many other sea beasties. Along with these fish, they also have cut to size Salmon and Tuna steaks, which are great for grilling season. Additionally, if you look through their frozen fish they have some great finds, I found a bag of shelled periwinkles! I haven't had any in years. I secured a bag, and I'm going to call Nana to get her old recipe.
 
For the bonus round, the market sells a selection of baked good from Dong Phuong, which makes some great breads and pastries. Also, as other reviewers have said, their $3 banh mi sandwiches are both delicious and a great deal. Get there early if you want one because they do sell out. 

Overall, I leave the Hong Kong market with a grocery cart full of food for less than $100. I'm a fan.

Let me give you some background.... I don't usually go out for coffee, however, during a recent visit by my darling family (4 sisters at one time, can you say crazy!) one of them decided it would be a good idea to break my French press. Deep breath.....now I wouldn't call myself a coffee snob or a caffeine addict, but I do enjoy some coffee in the AM. Mojo to the rescue! 

Mojo is perfect distance from my house so that I can hit it up on my morning run. It opens at 6:30 AM on weekdays and often times there are coffee zombies queuing up outside waiting for the doors to open. 

Once inside it has the quirky coffee shoppe vibe, rotating art on the walls, magazines, outlets, ect. Also, this place has tasty iced coffee. One large with almond milk please! I take it to go, but I find the chairs and table outside a charming location for Magazine St. people watching. 

As previous reviewers remind, Mojo is cash only.

Twelve Mile Limit, I love you. 

Delicious Brunch. Delicious Drinks. Delicious BBQ. Is there really anything more a gal can ask for? Oh yes, you can escape here with a reasonable bar tab!

The BYOB (Build Your Own Biscuit/Burrito) is brunch heaven. Their biscuits are moist and huge. For the price I thought it would be closer to a biscuit sliders.... nope! Full size sandwich biscuits. My star combo is the caramelized onions, spinach, and brie with a side of hash brown. So good.

Also, another winner from their BBQ list is the loaded tater tots. I tried the the veggie version, as per Vicky's recommendation, and I was so glad I did. The tater tots came out with all the tasty treats the kitchen had to offer. The menu said it's good for two people, and they mean it (although I'm sure if someone made me I could manage alone). I have been curious to try the meaty version, but the veggie one is so good I feel my alliances are already forged. 

Now, I keep going on about the food... isn't this place a bar? Yes. The drinks!!!! The Bloody Mary's here are great. They are super spicy and come fully loaded with okra, string beans, olives, and lemon/lime. Also, their drink the Baudin is one of my new favorites! I need to start paying more attention when they mix it, so I can learn the secrets of this beverage to make at home. Along with all the great cocktails they have a couple beers on draft (including Irish Channel Stout!) as well as a solid canned beer selection with the standard American favorites...mine being the classy Mich Ultra. 

As per other reviews, Twelve Mile Limit is non-smoking, which endears it to me even more. And as I gush... sigh, there is no reason why I shouldn't be here all the time, besides living on the other side of town. Having a long distance relationship is hard.

Oh Rusty Nail. Thanks for being you. I don't know what I would do without my trusty neighborhood bar, besides go home before 2 AM. 

The vibe of the Rusty Nail is not what you are expecting when you initially happen upon this place. Kinda dark, yes. Behind the warehouse condo, yes. Is this a dive bar? No it most certainly is not a dive, despite some people's allegations.

The inside is cozy, the outside has a great patio. Both have excellent vibes. It has great music acts here, along with Opera on Tap when it's in season. Also, I like the food trucks and pop up kitchens that visit often. 

Drink prices are on par with the area, except the Crispin Cider draft. For some reason it costs $7 here where everywhere else it's $5. Also, like Lindsay A., I love me some Disco Lemonade... sweet disaster awaits......

Coming off my third visit here, I can't say enough good things about Arnaud's French 75. The ambiance is both inviting and romantic with the decor harkening from 1920's motifs and designs. Since there are only a few tables open at any time, I have never seen the bar "packed" only full. My favorite seat being in the back corner near the cigar case, so you can get an entire view of the space and people. All these aspects make it ideal for unwinding and enjoying the company of friends. Also, with the relaxed atmosphere it is easy to strike up a conversation with neighbors, and learn new things about the city.  

My routine for the French 75 always seems to include an Old Fashioned and cigar after a dinner in the Quarter. Although, during my last visit I branched out and explored the cocktail menu, which were all well made and enjoyable. The bartenders all know their craft, and wait on you attentively. As always I'm looking forward to my next date at Arnaud's French 75.

The cupcakes ( red velvet, carrot cake and vanilla)  I had were Ok. The cake & the icing were NOT too sweet *major plus*, but my real find was the cookies!! I tried oatmeal raisin and the  peanut butter variety. The oatmeal was soo gooey and soft. Don't forget to try one too. They get an extra star for the yummy cookies!!!! 

PS: They also had Pup-Cakes for doggies which was cute....

Ugh.  We had been in Tucson for a week.  We had eaten great Mexican food all week, except for that day.  Since I wasn't feeling so hot, we decided to get pizza.
The place is cute, located in a shopping plaza.  When you walk in there is a chalkboard with an assortment of pizzas.  
We ordered our pizza, paid and were given a number to wait.  The pizza came out not tasting so great.  The crust tasted like the oven and the rest of the pizza, although, overflowed with toppings, did not have much flavor.  
We won't be back.

Lüke. One of the first restaurants in NOLA I chose to call my fave 4 years ago. 

This thought still holds true today. 

It's my fave because so many dishes have been my go-to since the beginning. Eggs in a jar...go-to, shrimp and grits...go-to, pain perdu....still shouting from the rooftops. 

It's also my fave because of this reason, always changing and bringing the best to the table. Softshell crab BLT, croque monsieur, and beignets oh my! 

I can't leave out the bevs... French pressed Joe and a French 75 to start your adventure in New Orleans. 

Did I mention they have a spectacular looking bar? Go see for yourself.

My husband and I were so thrilled to try this new place but it was awful. My husband ordered the Fish and Chips and they came out raw in the middle. He then sent them back and 30 mins later they brought him out the chicken dish which was way too salty. The service was ok and the manager who came over to speak to us said that they will be taking the fish and chips off of the menu since this is the 7th one that has been sent back. REALLY? Anyway, we will never go back!

My dreadful burger streak continues, this time in St. Louis. 

Grounded has got a lot of nerve in trying to market themselves as a gourmet, independently owned chain. 

For 7 bucks you are not getting what you paid for. In fact, this burger was probably worse than McDonalds, and I've had better at BK. The meat was so bland, dry, and the patty was incredibly thin.
