The baja crunch was far from being crunchy. I asked for extra avocado but it seems like they did the reverse as there was barely any. The tortilla chips in it were soggy and everything was thrown together on top of a few pieces of lettuce. 

Don't fall into the trap of the branding or name - it is no where close to being gourmet or worth the $7 price tag. At best, a burger like this should only be found on a dollar menu.

The only thing I can agree with is that they serve "handcrafted" burgers, because a burger this bad can only have been handcrafted on purpose. 

Avoid at all cost.

The only real tough thing about going to Santa Barbara is deciding where to eat, right? There are a handful of good options, do you want casual divey Mexican food, seafood or a sit-down restaurant. What condition will you be in when you arrive for your rezzie? 

I knew we'd be out wine tasting for the day and then making our way back down the coast, so something about being out all day made a couple Montecito options a bit less desirable, especially since my other half surely wasn't in a tie, to which I asked him why he has an amazing Hermes tie from me that he rarely wears ;) but that's besides the point though. Here at Finch & Fork you can pretty much get away with wearing whatever you want. It's not a super casual restaurant but there definitely doesn't appear to be a dress code suggestion of any sort.

We stopped in for dinner with a reservation and we seated at a comfy booth beside high table top seating which quickly became a bit loud once a large party of college kids was seated.

We shared the deviled eggs with smoked trout. I really like deviled eggs but these didn't really win me over, for someone who doesn't necessarily care for "simple" when it comes to food, I think these were a tad too jazzed up for my taste. They weren't bad, but not my fav. 

We shared the roasted beet salad, which had golden beets and red beets which is always a plus in my book since I love both and can't really understand why you'd do one without the other :) This dish was very nicely done and I'd definitely recommend it.

I had the sea bass which was quite filling for a fish dish and very tasty, served with brussel sprouts, sweet potatoes which may be nice puréed but fine cubed.

I also tried a little bite of the Sunday special, Pot Roast which was ok but I don't care for a lot of meat so this isn't a dish I'd ever order.

The cauliflower skillet could have been a tad bit warmer but carried great taste from the lemon and capers.

We oddly skipped dessert which pretty much never occurs but I think this was due to how filling our dishes were.

Service was great and the food came out really quickly from the kitchen.

There are plenty of public parking lots but this restaurant is located within a Kipton hotel so I'm sure valet may also be an option if you'd like.
I was in the area and popped in quickly for an iced oat latte. Service was quick and friendly, can't ask for much more than that. If I lived in the area they'd definitely be in my regular rotation.

We whole heartily agree that any business with a liquor license who doesn't have a margie flight on the menu is doing something way wrong.

We'd arrived to Carp to grab a late lunch before hitting the sand only to realize our restaurant of choice had closed a bit early for the day. 

We wandered around contemplating where to dine, scanning QR code's until we stumbled upon Jakes I quickly pulled up their menu and glanced over their yelp pics when I spotted the margarita flight. Ummmm... yes yes yes! Now don't get me wrong, you can totally make a bad margie but I eyeballed these pics pretty well and felt confident they would be worth my wild. 

We decided we'd dine here. Walked up to the host stand and were shown a perfect patio seat for two immediately.

I glanced over the menu and everything sounded good but I ordered my summer staple, fish tacos! One grilled, one battered. I liked the grilled best! 

I started with the margarita flight, of course! I'd never had a prickly pear margarita but I love spicy margs and this one was it! Soooooo good! All three were very tasty, but the seasonal spicy prickly pear with a Tajin salt rim and jalapeño is very similar to the delish spicy version I've been creating at home. Yummm yumm yumm. 

We had a great time! Service was exceptional, crowd was great.

This is the perfect spot for any occasion, ranging from super casu (us Sunday) to something celebratory, girls date, solo spot, friends or fam meal or just aps and drinks (the buffalo cauliflower and lobster Mac and cheese looked very tasty). 

I can't wait to return, I texted my Mom right away to tell her I'm bringing her here.

We walked here but I'm sure there's parking near by.

Order the margie flight or the seasonal prickly pear if you love spicy, it's as close to perfection as they come.
Waitress was not wearing a mask. Said she was sweating. Salad was overpriced. Four shrimp in their Shrimp salad. $15. I was not comfortable there at all.

I tried Lotus for the first time tonight. Being a vegetarian, it's nice to be able to pick from the entire menu and not be limited to one or two items.

The atmosphere is casual, but nice and clean. It's not ornately decorated like most Thai restaurants. The service was very friendly and attentive, and I appreciated the multiple styles of hot pepper sauces on the table to add to the food, if desired.

I started with the summer rolls, and they were delicious, warm vegetables and sliced tofu served with a sweet peanut sauce. Very good. For my meal, I ordered the rice vermicelli noodles with tofu and mixed vegetables. It was in a very tasty brown sauce, and not spicy. (I added some of that yummy pepper sauce on the table.) I was extremely satisfied with this dish, and the portion was very large. 

The prices are extremely reasonable, with meals ranging from $5.95 to around $8.00. They have a variety of Thai iced tea drinks as well. There are some items on the menu that indicate chicken or pork, but they are meat substitutes. The whole menu is vegetarian (I asked, just to be sure.)

I would give Lotus 5 stars for the food, with the only tiny bit of criticism being average decor, and a TV that was kind of loud.

Service was terrible. Came in with a party of four and it took 30 minutes to get our food which is a long time for some burgers. But that is not the worst part. Not once during that time did our server come to check on us or offer to refill drinks. When the food finally came on of the sides of fries was missing and i was told "sorry but we gave your burger to the wrong table." It took another 25 minutes to get my food by which time the rest of my party was done eating. Then finally the missing fries were brought out. To finish of this horrible experience, it took the server an additional 20 minutes just to bring the check after we asked for it! Ridiculous! Avoid this place. And the food was only ok; nothing special. The service is straight up garbage.

Carrot cake is honestly the best I've ever had.

I've tried a few things from here and all have been good so far. Their Homemade burger is very big and filling. Today, I tried their new Parmesan and Garlic fries, very good.

Lee was at the counter and was very friendly and sweet.

Looking forward to more great food!

Do you like food so spicy that it leaves you sweating like a sumo wrestler in a sauna? If not, xiao xin! This is probably not the spot for your Szechuan fix.

They have a gringo menu and a more classic style menu. All the dishes will leave you clamoring for a water refill in the most delicious way possible. My favorite is chicken in classic style, a stir fry consisting of chicken, bamboo shoots, bell peppers, mushrooms, and a massive quantity of whole dried chili peppers. Yowza!

I loved EVERY aspect of this restaurant..... from its interior decor, exterior patio, the salsa, guac, and of course, our entrees.  HUUUUUGE portions, but everything had WONDERFUL flavor, well seasoned, and all very fresh.

My husband ordered their rock shrimp tacos, served with a huge amount of shrimp that were so well seasoned.  Beautiful presentation with purple cabbage, long strips of tortillas.  Picture worthy, but more importantly, it tasted fabulous.

As for me, I ordered the Shrimp and Scallop Enchilada.  Huge chunks of seafood, a delicious sauce, wrapped in a soft tortilla, served with rice, black beans and a papaya salsa.  The flavors were amazing, and the best part?  I get to have leftovers for lunch.  CAN'T WAIT.

Montecito is a good hour north of us, but trust me when I say we'd make that drive any day, especially for the excellent food that awaits us.

It's interesting to me that on very rare occasion, I've been accused by other Yelpers (establishment owners moving about the website incognito?) of enjoying when I write a bad review, and that couldn't be further from the truth.  I hate when I have to write a less than stellar accounting of my dining experience, and I especially hate when I'm one of only a few who claim a bad experience of mostly 5 star reviews.  Well, thank goodness I'm not alone here, but I am not in the majority, either.  Most people love The Lark.... and I truly wish I was one of them.

 I will say the food presentation gets 5 stars.  Every dish was very artistically presented, so much so that I didn't want to cut into the beauty of their design, but we did anyway.  They were all beautiful, and I took pictures of each to make sure I always have them to reference, and nothing pleases me more than having something beautiful to photograph.  This place surely did not disappoint.

 The menu was eclectic, if not daring.  I'd like to think I'm open to trying new things, and even dishes with some more unusual food combinations.  Nothing scary or weird, but not my usual cup 'o tea, either.   For instance, gnocchi with crabmeat and chorizo...... to me, not something I'd typically order...or find elsewhere, but it "could" have worked masterfully.  The dish also boasted the use of navel oranges, castelvetrano olives, lobster roe, chili flakes and cilantro, but I have no idea if they were actually there or not...... I couldn't tell.  Unfortunately, the dish was overpowered by too many chili flakes (not the chorizo), and thus, was way too spicy.  A dish like gnocchi, so delicate, doesn't seem right that it should be so spicy.  Maybe I'm crazy.

 We also ordered an asparagus dish, which came with preserved Meyer lemon, soft poached egg, spicy coppa, pinenuts, summer blossoms.  The asparagus, while cooked to perfection, had absolutely NO flavor, which annoys me to no end.  The spicy coppa was not all that spicy, but it didn't do anything for me to eat it with the asparagus, either.  I don't like poached eggs, so I didn't eat that.  I'm not sure what the summer blossoms were, or IF they were even there.  The pine nuts were more for decoration.  I didn't avail myself to eating them with the asparagus..... or without.  This dish just didn't work for me whatsoever.

 We also ordered the slow-cooked lamb ribs that came with Medjool date caramel, salsa verde, crushed pistachio, and fennel pollen.  This was incredibly flavorful, but again, a bit spicy.  Yet, this time, while it was still too spicy for me, at least it made sense with the lamb.  With lamb, it can handle strong flavors.  This definitely had a Middle Eastern flavor, and I loved the sweet, perhaps cinnamon-y flavor.  I just would have preferred it be a little less spicy.  Also, while the lamb fell off the bones quite easily, it was oddly a bit dry.  I was chewing way too long on some of the pieces.

 One of the prettier dishes was the stone fruit & burrata, which had pickled bing cherries, nectarines, plums, peaches, with a dollop of roasted cashew praline, set among red mustard greens with Persian lime gastrique.  The fruit, while mildly cooked, was topped with a little dollop of burrata and some of the roasted cashew praline, which pretty much tasted like cashew butter.  The dish was nice to look at, but the flavors didn't appeal to me, nor did they add anything to any of the fruit.  Sure, separately they did...... but not together.  While beautiful to look at, thus ended its appeal after that.

 Lastly, we had the Grilled Spanish Octopus with roasted cauliflower, sea beans, blistered grapes, toasted almonds, squid ink, grapefruit, and rosemary.  OUTSTANDING.  It had perfect flavor.  It wasn't overly spicy.  It had texture.  The octopus and cauliflower were wonderful, especially when dipped in the squid ink.  The grapefruit could have been left out, but certainly nothing to detract from the dish.  We all loved it the most, and I'm just sorry we didn't order another.  I think this was my favorite restaurant version of octopus.  They got this dish RIGHT !!

 I happened to love my cocktail........ I got their version of the Mule....cucumber infused vodka, yellow chartreuse, and ginger beer with slices of lime and cucumber.  VERY refreshing, tasty, and sweet...... just how I like it.  Speaking of sweet, since it was my birthday, they brought out one of their goat cheese profiteroles with a candle.  It was decent........ not my favorite, but decent.  My husband and daughter ordered funnel cake, but I'm so not a funnel cake fan.  They both liked it, but they weren't raving, either.

 So overall, we had some hits and misses.  Honestly, for all the positive press I've read and for the prices they charge, I expected perfection... or near that.  I didn't think it was close to it.  Good, yes... but GREAT?  No way. I'm comfortable with awarding 3 stars.  Wish I could've given more.

I was quite pleased with the atmosphere of this establishment. Free street parking was easily found about a block away, I might have gotten lucky since there are a lot of bars around this area.

There was no line when I came in around 11 PM on a Saturday. And my group got lucky because we were able to snatch a TV/game station area on the 2nd floor right when another group was leaving. The joint was popping, got a DJ spinnin' some beats and lots of people chilling/gaming/dancing all over.

Cheap drinks - boozy popsicles ($5); doesn't cost money to play video games upstairs (as long as you order food/drinks). They had N64 games like Mario Kart, Smash Bros, Mario Party, etc. Made me miss middle school dayz.

Only complaint was they kept running out of flavors of the popsicles..I asked for like 3-4 different flavors and they didn't have any of it..had to settle with a red sangria flavored popsicle. Also, remember to check your tab closely! They charged me for an item that they ran out of so I pointed it out and they fixed it for me.

I originally chose to come here because of their menu I saw online, however they unfortunately only have a very limited menu right now. I overheard a server tell another table it is because of a kitchen staff shortage. I know all restaurants are struggling with right now, so while I do understand, it was still a disappointment. 
That aside, service was great and super fast. They were busy and the workers were running around and working very hard to serve everyone as quickly as they could! 
The salsa was delicious, a little kick but not too much. I ordered the street tacos, which have a lot of potential, but not quite 5 stars. I ordered chicken and pork - the meat was a bit dry and a little greasy. They did provide lime slices which helped, but they were quite small and wasn't really enough. I preferred the pork over the chicken. The burrito was massive and with all the extra ingredients, the meat didn't come off as dry or greasy.
I moved to St. Louis from Texas, and I was so happy to find a place serving ice cold Shiner! The house margarita was also very good. 
I hope they are able to get more staff hired on soon so I can have the full menu experience!

Locally Grown Gardens plays continuous reggae music. I don't mean that its on from time to time. I mean demma rampin' reggae always an foreva mon. To my way of thinking, this is a beacon of cultural nuance and bravado that earns LGG hands down 5 stars - in perpetuity. It wouldn't matter to me if they sold only Saltine Crackers soaked in milk (which I'm told isn't terrible). 

On this visit, with reggae in the background, I had the great fortune of ordering the smoked salmon with ginger coleslaw. Oh   My   God! The salmon is cooked perfectly and has a brown sauce that is .?. tangy and very good. Then comes the slaw with a ginger milky coating that is .?. fan-freakin'-tastic - might be the best coleslaw I've ever eaten. But the combination of these two offerings and their separate sauces mixing together during the eating is beyond words. This is one of the best single-plate values in Indianapolis - bar none.  At first, I questioned the absence of starch (bread for example), but after I started into the meal I began to understand the perfect blend of textures and flavors on the plate would only be diminished with any addition or subtraction. Bravo chef!

A friend tells me about this tamale place around 16th Street - said it was recently visited by the Food Channel and the tamales are supposed to be fantastic. They are. The tamales are big and corny goodness surrounds delectable fillings.

The Tamale Place is building a new ''place" just next to the current one, but I'm glad I visited the current digs first. Its basically one big open room - all kitchen except for the warmer and cash register by the door - everything is out in the open. There is a small ledge of counter top if you want to eat in. Pure ambiance.

The tamale is the centerpiece. They make about 8 varieties - for example chicken and green chillies or beef and red chipotle. When they run out, they stop selling. A dry-erase board keeps score.

Speaking of scores, this is a big one. I'll be back - a lot.

Maybe it's because I'm always partial to a good curry, but Veda is one of my favorite restaurants in Philadelphia.  After trying their weekend brunch, lunch buffet, happy hour, dinner, and takeout for dinner, every meal is both interesting and tasty.  I gravitate towards the sweeter and not as spicy dishes, but my friends who can handle the spice say their dishes taste pretty authentic.  The interior is decorated quite nicely, service has always been great, and I've never needed to make a reservation.  The one thing to note is that the prices tend to be on the higher side of the two dollar sign range.  Overall, I will definitely be coming back, and would recommend this restaurant to any and all who are in the area.

600th review!

I have experienced food markets before in Baltimore and DC, but boy is Reading Terminal Market is on a whole other level.  I would describe it as a cross between a food court, a carnival, and Grand Central Station. Given the many options and people watching opportunities, I can see why it's an iconic Philly attraction that everybody talks about. Come for the food, brave the crowds, and have fun exploring!

The guy at the front was pretty disrespectful in letting us know the kitchen was closed already....

Instead of verbally telling us... he points to the sign he was standing in front of (which is obviously blocking our view of it anyway) as if we were unintelligent and incapable of understanding a kitchen close time.. 
He then proceeds to "explain" to me as if I was a 5 year old that the kitchen was closed.

No thanks..

With Mohegan Sun and Foxwoods being the caliber of casino we are used to, we prepared ourselves to be underwhelmed.

In an effort to avoid the $10 fee to get in, we consumed $160 worth of food and drink (and drink, this made sense at the time) and got some free cards to scan ourselves through the turnstile.  I half expected the 6 train to blow through the wall.  

Disappointingly, it did not.

There were...not that many people in there.  A sparse selection of tables and machines.  Very few reasons to stay very long.

Who knew there were so many brands of sweatpants?

I will give the place some credit, for with the business it lacked I was able to jump on an empty craps table and learn how to play.  After some lessons, a few examples, some betting, some losing, some ATM visiting, some more betting, some winning, and some overall breaking even for then night..I got out.

At least I learned something....but I can't say i'll be going out of my way to come back.
Best snacks and food in University. Great service, Mr. Lee is the man!

This is one of the great museums!  A must see if in the area!  Not only do they have great paintings but they have entire rooms on exhibit!  It is amazing to walk into a room with the ceiling, floor, walls, furniture, paintings from the 16th century as it was in some place in Europe for example.  Just incredible.  They have an entire "outdoor" fountain scene from 12th century Spain.  It's the next best thing to time travel!  You kind of get a sense of the era.  The suits of armor also must been seen.  Only other place that compares is the Tower of London for the armor.  I only wish I would not have waited until my last day in Philadelphia to see this treasure. Next time I am back I will put this place on my to do list much sooner in my stay there.

I remember reading on Noshvilles website a few years ago how a group of "investors" went around New York and tried all the great "Delis" there and how they wanted to bring that back to Nashville. What I would like to know is what delis are they basing their so-called New York style sandwiches off of? 
  
   This is a place I want to like. I want it to be a place I can tell people to go. I want to say "Hey go to Noshville, not Jasons Deli." Unfortunately after giving them chance after chance I can say that I'm giving up. I don't mind paying $10-$13 for a good corn beef, reuben or pastrami sandwich when its properly executed. The Noshville "standard" doesn't meet or exceed my expectations in quality or quantity. 
 
   The corn beef and pastrami is not properly trimmed of fat and is somewhat dull, too thickly cut and chewy. Ok, they have an extensive b-fast menu. Who can screw that up? They have lox & bagels. But!! The one thing you dont do when your proclaiming to be a "New York" style delicatessen is screw up the sandwiches. C'MON! When I gotta shell out almost $16.00 for a "standard" $11.00 sandwich in NY with better meat, then you've lost me. 
   
Maybe the investors had a good idea, but I guess thats why they're investors and not owner operators.

When the weather is beautiful, and you're looking for a great tacos, @valsnola is the place to go. This place is very modern, clean, and great for what felt like a great outdoor picnic lol.
The menu is very simple, and yet they seem to always have a special to offer something new. Whether it's a drink, taco or a dish, it always adds a nice surprise!

 I ordered three tacos: beef, pork & sweet potato. Yes, that's right, I said a sweet potato taco, and honestly that was my favorite. The sweet potatoes were great with a crunchy outside and soft inside. The cream was a nice add on and the corona cheese was just a great choice. 

 The "crispy beef belly" taco was heavenly if you love a little pork fat. The "carnitas pork shoulder" was even better!

 I also ordered the "Queso Fundido with Chorizo" which was balanced really well. The chips weren't my favorite, but they weren't the worst. 

 Finally I had their frozen strawberry margarita, which was their daily special and I was not disappointed. 
Michelle was the best. She moved very swiftly and precisely. She definitely catered to all my needs!

The updated one star review is for the total lack of public safety and concern during the corona virus outbreak. My partner and I decided to go for a walk and stop in since we know lots of local businesses are struggling during this time. We now live close enough to walk. We've seen local restaurants posting what they are doing to help stop the spread and stay open. Star Bagel seems to be encouraging the spread instead of easing fears. 

The first thing I noticed is that there is no large menu posted, only handheld menus in the basket - tattered, worn, and clearly not being cleaned between guests use. It wouldn't take much to tape a menu up so people can look and decide but not touch. 

I didn't want to touch the menu myself, so I asked the younger guy behind the counter what kinds of cream cheese were available. He said the menus were behind me and I reminded him no one should be handling menus. He begrudgingly told me what the options were after I asked again. We really should have left then. Clearly this is just the right place for a virus to spread. 

While we waited for our bagels to go, I also noticed no one cleaning off the tables as people left or any sanitation stations around. 

Good luck staying open during this time with so little regard for the community supporting you. We won't be back. 

They also don't boil their bagels so no one is missing out by going somewhere else.

The Vampire Cafe is fun, unique, and awesomely decorated. They are highly responsible in requesting not only proof of vaccination but a photo ID as well. The food is delicious - the Baked Brie was warm and creamy, and the Fried Deviled Eggs were original. The only downside on the later is each had a different topping, and they were hard to split. The Vampire Chocolates were well tempered, but if I had to do it again I would try something else. Maybe if they had "blood" in the center, but at present they're solid chocolate.

OMG! I'm never going here again! First of all, when the waitress dropped off our check several roaches emerged from her "booba" and fell onto the table, making us all jump and run from the table looking like fools - really embarrassing. Second, the waitress made us wait for far too long before we got our water, and when it did come there was no lemon. Finally, the steak I ordered was a bit underdone, although it was excellent.

Nice place, but the incident with the waitress, forgive me, was too much.

One of my favorite restaurants. I knew I would like it from the start when I noticed they had placed a fine spiked wire all along the ledge outside and on their sign to keep birds away, and also a much needed and commonly overlooked air curtain, which is a device establishments place between their doors to keep insects and birds out - a powerful, toupee dislocating, downward blowing fan. After walking through the air curtain and realizing El Diablo is possibly the most anti-bird restaurant I've ever visited, I didn't even care that my carefully styled hair was blown all over the place.

Once I gave the staff my anti-bird hand signal (cross your hands over one another, link your thumbs and flutter your fingers like wings, then transition into the "blow it up" move that has become a popular finale for a fist-bump), and it was returned, I decided this was the place for me.

Anyhoo, the braised short-rib is unbelievable, as is the citrus braised pork. If you're looking to dine on an avian, try the chicken with the chipotle barbeque sauce - it's a doozy. All of El Diablo's ingredients are fresh and absolutely fantastic, and the sauces and dressings make me want to punch Taco Bell in the face.

El Diablo might mean "The Devil" in translation, but no burrito more heavenly has ever crossed mine lips. They say Jesus resides inside each of us - well I hope he likes burritos, because that's what he's going to get.

In closing, a quote often associated with the legendary cartoon heroine Jem - El Diablo, you are outrageous. Truly, truly outrageous.

The Philly Soft Pretzel Factory's (PSPF) no-reservations front room is that rare space that's sexy enough for a date but comfortable enough for your grandparents, assuming they are comfortable sitting on the window ledge, and the menu is so thoughtful it's like an act of generosity. The pretzels are born of meticulously sourced ingredients and crafted into one of the most resplendent foods EVER created.

More often than not, PSPF is filled with people having a very good time. No surprise, since the menu offers an up-to-the-minute snapshot of what young Philadelphians have been scarfing down their cold weather/second rate city mouths for decades. Pretzels - from traditional Philly twists to the longer classically phallic "torsion longue" - are a draw, as are the pretzel dogs; it's hard not to fall in love with a pretzel that has a strip of processed pork belly riding inside it like an amputated finger. Choices of several different dipping sauces, including several varieties of mustard, round out the menu choices.

If I were a ball of dough, salt and yeast, I would be a Philly Pretzel.

If I were a better person, I wouldn't have thrown my ambien into the dough bin while the employees weren't paying attention.

I feel like I keep discovering little gems in St. Louis that I barely hear anyone talk about. And Lulu's is definitely one of them. Lulu's is setup with the popular trend of "fast casual" where you order at the counter and they bring you the meal. And they aren't kidding. We received our first entree in under 5 minutes of ordering.

To preface, I'm a carnivore and could probably eat a steak everyday and be pretty happy. I was pretty impressed by how delicious all the food was and the last thing I was missing was meat. The Buffalo Cauliflower had all the tastes, textures and familiarity of a meat dish, but I think I enjoyed it more because it was so unique. 

I think Lulu's is a fun place that a lot of people would enjoy. And I'd love to hear their name mentioned more as one of St. Louis' best restaurants.

I order delivery from Iztaccihuatl quite frequently and am never disappointed.  The food is always delicious!  I've become addicted to the esquites (if you ever had grilled corn with sauce and mexican cheese, this is the soup version) and manzanas con crema (so.good.seriously.).  Of course, their guacamole and chips are perhaps my favorite in the city.  I can't wait to order again!

A co-worker's wife ordered cupcakes from Philly Cupcake this week and I have to admit - they were amazing!  I tried the carrot cake and the crumb (with strawberries on it).  Both cupcakes were extremely moist with the most delicious icing.  I can't wait until someone else's spouse at work orders them a dozen cupcakes...

Wow! They say appearances can be deceiving, and Waffles on Maple is a prime example of this. It saddens me to do this review, as I had rather high hopes for the place.

Product: It's basically breakfast/brunch fare. We went there this past weekend for breakfast, because we had a Groupon (I think it was $10 for $20). I had, basically, a waffle with blueberry sauce a la mode (they had some fancy name for it that I don't recall), and she had a savory crepe with fake crab product. We shared our dishes, so I can say with confidence that both were decent enough dishes that weren't stingy portions. The prices on the dishes weren't too bad, but you get slammed on side items and drinks. The cold coffee drink I had was miniscule (maybe 4-6 oz), with the cup being more than half whipped cream, at over $5 before tax. The lady had a side salad as well, which cost way too much for lettuce, cucumber, and tomato. I think the cost before the Groupon was applied was just shy of $40!! (2 stars, due to poor value)

Service: Although Yelp only allows us to rate overall a minimum of 1 star, my personal subvalues can be lower. To say the service was poor was an understatement. You order at a counter, and they deliver the items to you. Well.......if they every get to you. The side salad we ordered came out WAAAAYYYY after our main course, and only after we prompted at least two servers on its absence from the table. 

Our main dishes took like what felt was a dog's age to get out, considering there looked to me like a half-dozen people in the kitchen area working. I was scratching my head as to what they were actually doing back there. My coffee also took way longer than it should have. I must mention that there were like maybe 4 parties here at the time, so it wasn't like a busy lunch at Commander's, far from it. 

I wouldn't go so far as to say the employees were rude, but I certainly felt like the customer was the last thing on their mind. (0 stars)

Facilities: If there was any saving grace to the establishment, I suppose this was it. It is a cute little place far Uptown, past the universities, but before the Riverbend area on Maple. This block has a number of eateries and selection of cafes, so it doesn't really stand out. The design and decor was a simple postmodern, with lots of that wood/metal/glass feel to it. The inside is kind of tight, with stool seating along the side wall. All the real seating was outdoors. Thankfully, it was a beautiful day and there was a table available, or our experience would've been even worse. It looked mostly clean, but the poor service includes lack of expediency on bussing tables as well. 

The only parking you'll find that I could detect was on Maple itself. Once again, fortune was on our side, and we got a prime spot almost right in front the restaurant. Otherwise, it is slim pickings, and I didn't notice any place to lock up a bike either. (2 stars)

Double-Edged Sword #1: This place is kosher. If that's your gig, good for you. For me, that meant no bacon with my waffles, which was rather disappointing (not that I'd want to pay for a side order of bacon at the prices they charge).

Double-Edged Sword #2: It's vegetarian (ovo-lacto friendly), but they didn't have any *real* milk when I ordered a coffee, only that soya bean juice some folks pass off as "milk." Like the kosher limitations, I'm sure it's cool if you're into a meat-free life, but it ain't for me.

Overall: I suspect the ownership/management thinks it's okay to bilk people with high prices and cheap service, as most of the people I saw coming and going were trust fund college kids and tourists who know no better, but any diner with at least a minimal level of savvy should be able to see right through to the fact that this place isn't worth the effort. Hit up Chais Delachase next door---better menu and some awesome happy hour and Sunday brunch specials. Heck, even the Starbucks at the corner here is a step up, and I don't like Starbucks at all. Do yourself a favor, save your money, and skip this joint. (1 star)

Ah, Metry! You might not be the prettiest town, but, damn, you got some pretty good local eateries! If you're around here, check out Bevi for twists on local grub. You won't be disappointed.

Product: Louisiana-style local foods---fried seafood, po'boys, and the like. My date and I each got a sandwich for lunch and split some fried green maters. To me honest, we could've split a sammy, because they're each a footer in length!!

The maters were cooked to perfection, and the remoulade was made perfectly, coming out piping hot! I got a cochon de lait poboy; she got a ham n cheese. I demolished mine. It was, without a doubt, the best CdL sandwich I've ever had---cooked to shredded perfection, with a sauce and slaw to die for! She ate half her HnC, but told me she loved it and doggie bagged the other half. There was nothing but crumbs left of the maters.

The drinks were generous. We each ordered a beer (Canebrake and Blue Moon). F'n fishbowls, I kid you not! 

2 entrees, shared appy, and 4 fishbowls of beer clocking in at under $40. Good value.

(5 stars)

Service: We went at an off time for a late lunch (2ish?). There was no crowd. Wait was nonexistent. Service was speedy and we talked with the friendly staff. Def old school Yats. 

(5 stars)

Facilities: It's a little corner affair on Airline near the ball park. Place is totally unassuming with an antique flair to it. It looks like a fresh seafood place because it is, on top of being a restaurant, domed glass countertop and all.

Place is neat, inside and out. Fun, traditional outdoor wall painted artwork/advertisement. Large screen TVs placed strategically around the place. Bar and table seating. Bathrooms were clean.

(5 stars)

Overall: GO HERE. Go here, go here, GO. HERE. If you don't like it, you don't like Louisiana cuisine. The waitress let me know the cooks at Cochon in the Warehouse District eat the CdL here, if that gives you any idea how fuggin' good it is!!!!! 

(5 stars)

Although the selection of Middle Eastern and Greek/Mediterranean style food, Lebanon's is basically the "grande damme" of this cuisine in New Orleans. I've been frequenting the place for over 2 decades.

Product: Good quality Eastern Mediterranean fare at a decent price is had here. This isn't "super fancy" like Shaya or the old Byblos on Magazine, but it'll take care of your craving. The portions are large, so if you're getting an entree, you truly should split any appetizer you purchase. The pita and hummus is good, and I've tended to gravitate to the generous and delicious kebabs, either beef or lamb. Their "Lebanese Tea" with rose water and pine nuts is yummy and doesn't need much if any sugar. You won't leave hungry. (4 stars)

Service: Regular sit-down service with a waitress. I've never found them to be exceptional, good or bad. (3 stars)

Facilities: Located on a corner on South Claiborne Uptown around the Black Pearl neighborhood, Lebanon's is in a more traditional storefront one might see here in New Orleans. There is seating inside and out, and the wide windows gives a good view of the street traffic, streetcars and all. 

Seating is comfortable enough, but not glamorous. Decorations are, of course, of a Middle Eastern bent and quite appropriate for the space. The area is clean inside and out.

The biggest downside to this restaurant is lack of parking. There are a few spots nearby on S Claiborne, but, other than that, you'll have to park back in the neighborhood. I'd say bike out here, but I don't recall any bike racks, so be warned. (4 stars)

Overall: I suggest this restaurant to anyone looking for this type of food in the city. Although there can be a bit of a rush at lunch, wait times aren't so bad, and the food more than makes up for that. Check it out if you haven't already. (4 stars)

We watched with great anticipation the progress of this place, when it finally open, we paid them a visit to our great disappointment.

Esthetically the establishment is visually appealing.  There is ample lightning and the tables arrangement is such that allows for great flow and a sense of ample space.

Regretfully when it comes to the food and staff there is much to be desired.  The Pho (flagship product of the establishment) is below mediocre, the broth is made out of powdered based vs. the traditional method using bones and spices (star anise, cinnamon, etc).  The temperature of the broth at serving is not high enough to properly "cook" the beef.
There is very little, if any, flavor to their pho.  Their noodles are gummy and turn to paste half way thru your meal.  Our meatballs were cold once we bit into them, again a result of the low temperature at serving.

Due to the lack of leadership, the wait staff walks around in circle often trying their hardest to do what "they" think they should be doing.  It is obvious that the management team did not take the time to assign roles and responsibilities.  They also lack the understanding of what condiments go with what dishes. 

When we flagged down one of the two managers to ask for condiments we were quickly told to ask the wait staff rather than them addressing the situation.  We felt they were in reactive mode more so than proactive.

We will take our business elsewhere and perhaps give them another try after they modify their tactics, techniques and procedures.

Advice to Managemet:  take a step back, hold a training event with your waitstaff, educate them on all the dishes, stress the importance of following up with your customers after food delivery and avail your time to your patrons.

The best Brussels Sprouts I have had!!!! The Luke salad is probably on my top 3 favorite salads so far. Just those 2 reasons right there are enough for me to come back here next time I'm in NOLA!

It was raining cats and dogs when we arrived. Not sure if that's the reason we were able to be seated right away during their brunch time without a reservation. The restaurant has 2 separate seating sections I believe. The decoration is very French colonial type, classy and beautiful. 

For starters, we got the Brussels Sprouts and Luke salad. They are must try here! The Brussels Sprouts have so many flavors going on, but not in an overwhelming way. Everything compliments each other so well. They are cooked perfectly too, nice crispy texture outside, a lil soft inside, not too greasy. The salad was super fresh and pair so well with their delicious dressing!

For the main entrees, I got myself the chicken cordon blu sandwich. It was huge and super hot with each bite, the hot lava cheese would almost burn my mouth if I eat them too fast. Definitely have to eat with a fork and knife. My SO got the shrimps and grit which I think I enjoyed more than my sandwich lol.

We ended the meal with the hazelnut Paris Brest which comes with pate a choux (not sure what that is lol), passion fruit, coconut. The ice cream and passion fruit were really good. The pastry (maybe that's wat pate a choux is?) that's supposed to bind everything together was too dry for me and didn't have much taste. 

Overall it wasn't a bad experience, except the super slow service at the end of our meal, it took our waitress a good 15-20mins to give us our check and another 10mins or so to complete everything. We would definitely come back here again for their salad, Brussel sprouts, and maybe try other entrees on their menu next time.

Aesthetic, extremely friendly staff, amazing creative food, casual with an upscale taste but won't break your bank (unless you're me and order a crap load of food)

It's not easy to create beautiful but still tasty vegan dishes without relying heavily on meat substitutes, but this place has mastered it.

I loved my wild mushroom ravioli with crispy Brussels sprouts. The presentation is of a fine dining level, and not from a cute café/restaurant type. I'm not entirely sure what's all inside the ravioli or the sauce, but boyyyyy it was creamy goodness with lots of favor. The Brussels sprouts add a nice contradicting taste and texture to the whole dish.

Their avocado chocolate mousse with meringue dessert really topped it off for me. I loved it so much and so amazed of how good that meringue and the whole dessert tastes, I asked the waitress what they use for the meringue. She delightedly told me it was chickpeas brine with cream of tartar. Who would have thought? Definitely not me lol

The only thing I wasn't too fond of was the beet fries which a lot people crave about. Maybe it was a little too greasy for me and not as crispy as I thought it'd be. Regardless, this place is definitely on my top 5 vegan restaurants I have been to. Too bad I don't live anywhere near St. Louis to come here more often :(

This restaurant was not what I expected at all. I usually order something simple when I try new Thai restaurants like pad Thai or pad see ewe but this place did not impress.

I went with a few others and together we ordered pad Thai, pad see ewe, yellow curry, and "spicy" noodles.

My pad Thai did not have much flavor. It also did come with any veggies like pad Thai usually does. I had to add some yellow curry to give it some flavor. However, the portion was good. I also ordered the Thai iced tea with boba and it was super good! 

The yellow curry was not spicy at all. It tasted decent but no spice. They also do not ask what spicy level you'd like for the curry. I guess it just comes as is and we have no option to adjust the spice.

The "spicy noodles" were not spicy at all. It also has two peppers next to it on the menu so you'd think it'd be spicy but no. 

The pad see ewe was probably the best dish. It tasted pretty good and had some more flavor than the pad Thai. 

The servers were great and friendly so I appreciate that.

The first time I came here was about three years ago. I moved away but still remembered how good the food was so when the gf and I came back to visit St. Louis, we stopped by this bomb restaurant! 

Honestly the main reason we came was because the golden mashed potatoes were so good! We used to come here and get to-go orders of just the mashed potatoes. Literally the best side dish ever. During our recent visit, we ordered them again. To our disappointment, it was not the same. At all. They used to be very moist and flavorful but now they're dry and bland. Not sure why they changed the recipe but something definitely changed...and it wasn't a good change.

Other than that, we really enjoyed the other food! We came for their happy hour and was excited about the $5 dishes and drinks. 

We ordered the avocado & chicken egg roll, shrooms, Margherita flatbread, calamari, and of course the potatoes. Everything was super good but my favorite was the egg rolls! The chicken was cooked perfectly and the breading on the outside was phenomenal. 

For the drink, we ordered the Moscow mule (amazing) and the blueberry lemonade with vodka. Both were super good and had a good amount of alcohol. Absolutely would recommend getting these drinks. 

One of the best happy hours in town! Good food and cheap drinks! Also our waitress Jennifer was awesome!!! She deserves a raise!!! Best employee you have. She's super friendly, efficient, and quick!!

Pat O'Briens is the type of restaurant you should avoid all together while out in NOLA. Why? I'll tell you why. The service here is ridiculously SLOW (snail slow) and the food is not good. Yes, I said it, you trendy tourists! I made the mistake of stopping in while wandering Bourbon St. I should have known better than to dine at a place smack dab in the middle of NOLA's party central. 

I asked for a table (for 2) and was led to a section of the outdoor restaurant that was right under a heat lamp. I asked if there was anyway of sitting in the patio area near the bar and water fountain. I was quickly shut down and told that area was reserved for drinking -- only. I was not only planning on drinking but was also going to do a bit of eating and more drinking. 

We were offered a table that was so narrow, an ashtray and one glass were about the only items that could fit on the table. Was this guy kidding me? Unless the food portions were tapas-style, then give me a normal table! I moved to another table nearby and was quickly intercepted by another waiter; "This is for parties of 4. Sorry." I basically parked my sweet ass in that table and the waiter backed off. What's he going to do? Throw beads at me??

Pat O'Brien's is known for their fruity cocktails; most famous is the Hurricane. I went against the tradition and got a Mint Julep. Strong Bourbon love right there. I also ordered the Rainforest which was a beautiful layered drink with subtle boozy flavors. It's the type of drink you don't know what it's made of nor do you want to know. The interesting thing about Pat O's is the way you somehow end up purchasing a souvenir glass. The very same glass they use to serve your cocktail, miraculously ends up as a purchase (in addition to the drink) on your bill. Sneaky? Yes. But I know own two Pat O'Brien glasses. 

I also ordered the alligator bites. I have never had alligator or crocodile or any sort of reptile...but the bites were pretty decent. Sort of tasted like chicken nuggets. For my entree, I went with the Creole Shrimp. It was a pretty basic shrimp and rice dish that offered very little flavors but a lot of HEAT. 

Pat O'Brien's is very busy at night and mostly occupied by tourists who want to get their drink on. I wouldn't recommend dining here at all. You can find much better restaurants that are not adjacent to seedy strip bars and night clubs.

A New Orleans staple with southern hospitality and soul food written all over it, we went to Mother's by the recommendation of a Yelp friend or two and well, of course, Man vs. Food. 

The Good:
- Friendly smiles 
- Quick Service
- My first ever Po-Boy (i.e. a southern style sub sandwich)

The Bad:
- Long line can go all the way down the block
- In the hot sun, it can get sweaty fast
- Fear not, the line moves quickly.
- A tad pricey but 

The Delicious:
- grilled shrimp po -boy
- potato salad (divine!)
- bread puddin'
- the most refreshing lemonade you have ever tasted. 
- juicy famous ferdi with succulent meat. yum.

have your order ready. study the menu while you're in line. you wont want to miss ordering anything tasty.

I met up with a friend outside for a brunch date and she has been recommending Sabrina's for forever, so we finally ordered it together! I am so, so glad we did because it truly does live up to its hype. Everytime I walk by here, there's always a huge line on the weekends. It's truly THE brunch place in the museum/Fairmount area. I ordered their chicken and waffles and my friend ordered their eggs benedict (it's not on the menu but you can just call and order or just ask for it). We also split their cannoli French toast.

I was truly in heaven- the waffles were soft and fluffy, the syrup was not too sweet, and the chicken was incredibly crispy and juicy. The herby butter they gave with it was fabulous and all together just a crave-worthy combo. The French toast was made made challah bread, which meant it didn't get too soggy at all and I preferred it to normal French toast I've had. The cream and cannoli crumbles and fruit toppings were delicious! 

My experience with Sabrina's was beyond amazing, we carried out and ate it on the lawns around the museum area but Sabrina's does have some very limited outdoor seating if you want. The takeout experience though was easy and great, and I'm already thinking about the next time I can carry out their brunch! The menu options are extensive and all look delicious- Sabrina's won't disappoint!
Excellent vegetarian sandwich and several good vegetarian pasta options. Owner was really nice. Food was fresh and ready quickly. Will be back.

Great Peruvian cuisine and fresh seafood. Since moving to Tampa I have tried numerous South American restaurants and "Go Fish"ranks in my top 3. Primarily because of the excellent food and top notch service. 

The menu is large but our waitress pointed out some great dishes. Per our server's suggestion, my wife tried a seafood platter with a lime based sauce. I tried the Loma Saltado with chicken. This entree included grilled onions, tomatoes, and french fries. The perfect combination of healthy and unhealthy food. The sauce was spicy, salty, and delicious. Peruvian sauces are unique and made our dinners special. The only downfall for this restaurant is the location (in a strip mall next to Winn Dixie), but the location probably keeps prices competitive.

Disgusted is almost an understatement. I found a gigantic, cockroach-like creature in the bottom of the chips that accompanied my takeout order. We used to love this place, however, after reporting this atrocious incident to the restaurant and being rudely dismissed, I guarantee you that I will not be dining at this restaurant as well as will be reporting them to the Department of Health.

As someone who is originally from South Jersey/ South Philly area which have the best cheese steaks and hoagies ( yes we call them hoagies in that area) around ...must also give a nod to NY as well ...I am always interested in shops out here who think they can replicate what the East has mastered in terms of the bread, steak n lunch meats...well needless to say this shop is not it either! I ordered s 16 inch cheese steak with fried onions n cherry peppers n an order of hot wings.....the wings were the only positive....cheesesteak was flavorless and there were more peppers on the sandwich than meat! Terrible....provide your customers with a packed flavorful sandwich  like you find back East....sorry , but u guys fall very short in quality and don't have the right to call your shop East Coast Subs...ur owners should take a trip to the Philly area to see and taste what a REAL cheese steak is! Next stop Serial Grillers!

My coworkers come here every week for lunch, even though Mai Lee is just a few miles south. However, my heart has been stolen by Pho Long. The pho broth is much more savory and flavorful, which is crucial for a good bowl of pho. I would say PL's broth is very unique in flavor. I think they have some magical ingredients in the soup because I daydream about this bowl of goodness in the office.One thing I wished they had more of is the toppings. A few times they've skimped us out on the basil or cilantro. Regardless, I love the pho. 

Also their dry noodles is another great alternative if you want something that doesn't make you have a major food coma at your desk. The menu is limited and might not be as extensive as Mai Lees, but there's a reason why people come back every week for the pho. 

Also the staffs are rockstars.

I had brunch here with my sister today. We've only stopped by to get pastries or cakes here, so we were excited to try the meal today. However, we ended up feeling disappointed with our brunch experience, and we ended up cheering ourselves with a fruit tart and a cookie at the front. 

La Bonne Bouchée is a small, quaint place with a cute outdoor sitting area, and you're greeted by tempting pastries and cakes that are too sweet and delicious to pass. 

My sister and I were the first two people waiting to be seated. We had to wait five minutes to be seated. We miss the busy lunch crowd, so waiting to be seated for five minutes is unacceptable, especially when we saw more than three tables opened at the restaurant. We took a seat inside close to the entrance. We were rudely greeted by our server with long black frizzy hair with an European accent. Actually scratch that. There was no greeting, just "what do you want to drink?" We kindly told her that the water was fine, and she tossed us our menu and responded "I'll be back" with a sour attitude. WTF- What the French! 

My sister ordered a petit portion of Adriatic Chicken Salad and I ordered the Quiche du Jour. After our rude server took our order with an attitude, we watched her waltz around table to table. A couple minutes later a table with three people were being seated near us. My sister and I watched our impolite server take their order. We were shocked to see how quick her attitude changed. It was like seeing a whole new different server. She greeted them with a smile and "how are you." Also recited the Soup of the Day and the Quiche of the Day. My sister and I were very confused and irritated. 

Enough about our rude server, more importantly the food: 

My sister's Adriatic Chicken Salad looked like something any dummy can make it at home. It's just grilled chicken breast over some greens, tomato, olives, red onions, feta cheese, and balsamic vinaigrette. The salad had way too much feta cheese. More cheese than lettuce. The salad was average, but it wasn't worth the $8.80 (a full is $11.75).

I ordered the Quiche du Jour which came with the vegetables and the choice of a side salad or a soup. I ordered the Soup du Jour which was a vegetable and noodles soup. The soup and the quiche wasn't too bad. The soup was mediocre. 

Overall, the experience was horrible. The service was horrible. The food was mediocre. We tipped probably less than 15 percent. I am a server and I've always treated every customers with a smile even if they are down-right rude to me. We did not want to order desserts from our server, so we went up to the bakery to order it ourselves and ate it outside because the weather was beautiful today. The dessert was delicious. I had the petit fruit tart (strawberries and kiwi with cream on top of the tart) and my sister had an oatmeal cookie. I don't know I'll ever go back to eat a meal there again, but maybe I'll make a quick stop once in awhile for a pastry.

Tried it and won't be back.  $15.95 eel masterpiece roll described as being topped with eel only had 2 small pieces of eel topped on half the roll.  Spoke with the owner/executive chef who said eel
Is expensive and said there's avocado on the other (non-eel topped) pieces.  Sorry, I'm not trying to pay $16 for a California roll!!  I told him we wouldn't be back.  He was like "just because of 1 roll?".  He insincerely  said sorry and walked off.  Can't believe he didn't even offer to take the roll off my bill or offer me another roll.  That's why we won't be back!  Stay away!   Go to Umu Sushi instead!! They'll take care of you and prices are more reasonable especially their 3 for $15 sushi roll lunch special!

How did Chandler's do with a first timer such as myself? Let me tell you what makes this place so special is the EXPERIENCE, even on a Sunday night they didn't cut any of it short. It's no secret I am one of Yelp's toughest critics, because it's hard to hide mistakes from someone who knows how to cook fine dining.  My official score is 4.5 yet I am swayed by the exceptional service to push it to 5.  

*Pre Dining-  Chandler's phone service was the very appetizer to what I would soon experience. I called a few times just to get information, each time the lady was friendly and so knowledgeable.  She had no problems telling me menu items, specials, and suggesting we set a reservation (I'm glad we did) 

*Atmosphere- We both enjoyed the live jazz music that added to the ambience of an already classy place.  The lighting is dim and each table flickers with a oil lamp to give that extra intimate feel. Everything is done so you FEEL like you want to spend money ... and then you do lol The lighting is not the best for pictures as you will notice, but hey not taking a selfie for a few hours won't kill you or will it? 

*Service- My favorite thing even over the food was our server Lucas and how personable he was.  He was full of information and answered all of our questions, it really felt like we were at a friends house for dinner. He took extra time with the menu explaining items and finding out about us.  Every step of the way he was there throughout the meal, also our drink was always filled which we appreciate.  

*Food- Since it was our first time we wanted to ease in and went for the Sunday night special $30 for 3 courses.  (Amazing deal for the experience).  

App- Lobster Bisque/ creamy, well seasoned, tender chunks of lobster with a nice bread for dipping. 

Entrée- Duck two ways/ My friend enjoyed this it was cooked perfectly, the duck confít tasted similar to dark meat turkey.  He didn't care for the polenta just a preference of taste and texture.  Mac n cheese was not my favorite, seemed it was over powered by herbs and a tangy mustard like flavor. 

Entree- Lamb/ My lamb was nice thick chops oven roasted to perfection (medium rare) It was very well seasoned just a tad to much salt from the rub but the apple mint chutney mellowed it out.  My baby carrots were sautéed so they had a bit of bite, the weakest element was the potatoes au gratin very bland and needed help. 

Dessert- Lucas was able to get us the chocolate soufflé  as it is kinda famous...WE HAD TO TRY IT!  It did not dissapoint either in SIZE of flavor. It is accompanied with a whipped cream w a hint of orange and a chocolate ganache (sauce) you pour over and it is heaven. Well worth the money and a perfect ending to a great experience.  

  Thanks Lucas! You are a Rockstar and I would come back and expect the same service from any other one of Chandler's servers.

Ever since I happened upon Cajun Kate's (http://www.yelp.com/biz/cajun-kates-boothwyn#hrid:skqZ3A9CURSkZdk3pVbzGw/src:self) I'm always a bit grumbly when I have to pay High prices here, but I shouldn't be: the price reflects the purpose, and each restaurant serves it's purpose very well. At High Street Caffe, you're paying of course for the haute cuisine spin on creole cooking, but also for the luxury of sitting in a chair.  High Street is where you take your friends in West Chester if you want to have a delicious high-class dinner in a dimmed, richly hued hip atmosphere. Cajun Kate's is where you go if you want to wear sweats and shove your way onto one of the 6 hotly contested stools to shovel down the best authentic cajun food from here to Nawlins. 
Different purposes, as you can see, but I love each one equally.

High Street Caffe is my favorite restaurant in West Chester, hands down. It's flavors and style really assert themselves, and I've never, ever had a bad meal here. The service is friendly, even the mild roar you encounter on the weekends when it's completely full has a convivial charm to it. High St's 3-courses-for-30-bucks prix fixe menu is the best deal; most of the entrees featured on the prix fixe menu hover in the 25 dollar range, so you'll make out like a bandit (albeit one who's bitten off more than he can chew, quite literally: the portion sizes are very generous). The blackened red snapper, lobster ravioli, alligator sausage, lamb, etouffee offerings, bananas foster...these are all fantastic dishes. Just make sure to get extra bread- it's sublime.

So...I stumbled upon a review of Terrain At Styers' cafe at 8AM this morning. I got so giddy about the idea of visiting such a magical-pixie-flora-faerie-dust world that I HAD to take a half day and go, as cafe service ends at 2:30 PM (coffee bar open 'til 6). I couldn't go another day knowing that this was in existence and that I wasn't THERE. 

Let me explain: the last time I was in Anthropologie (coincidentally, the last time I had money...) I said to my friend:
*standing in front of what appeared to be an ensorcelled tree a'drape with tea cups, faux fauna, and tinselly tees*
 "I'm going to open a restaurant that's decorated exactly like Anthropologie . C'mon, who doesn't want to be served dainty foods by birds and nymphs while sitting pretty in an enchanted forest?"

Something like that. Yes, I say some very vapid and nonsensical things occasionally. 
BUT!
TERRAIN AT STYERS IS EXACTLY THAT!! Imagine my astonishment when I read that the Urban Outfitters Co, which of course owns Anthropologie, has a new "brand" in this nursery/garden/home decor store called Terrain at Styers, and that there was a cafe on site in a greenhouse, decorated just so and serving up delectable dainties on a daily basis. The birdies and wood nymphs at Anthro HQ read my mind!!!
So I went, immediately. I made a beeline for the cafe and was promptly seated. Oh, my wildest dreams and fancies were dancing aflutter and they were not disappointed. My olfactory senses were singing as Styer's is bathed in a most sumptuous smell of pine and gardenia...the look was all I could hope for...akin to a Longwood Gardens and Anthropologie love child. Birdhouses hung from the rafters of the greenhouse, dappled sunlight poured in from every direction, gravel crunched ever so pleasantly under my soles, beautiful plants sprung all around, fronds and flowers dangled artfully from antique doors. A true sight to behold. Just like my imaginary restaurant! 

Once I got a grip and stopped grinning like an idiot, I busied myself by looking at the menu. Lovely selection, with an emphasis on fresh, seasonal, local, and chic. Kennett Square mushrooms, pumpkins & beets (somewhere, Michael W wearily shakes his fist), all featured heavily. Because it's a clause in my contract with my stomach that if Mac&Cheese is on the menu I have to order it, I ordered that (6 bucks) along with the flank steak sandwich with caramelized onions and boursin (12 bucks). A large cup of La Colombe coffee too, if you please.  A flowerpot-ful of fresh-baked, still warm honey bread (see picture) arrived before me and I was almost overwhelmed with how chewy and delicious it was. I was in heaven; the silly grin was back. 

Now, the reason why I had to remove a star: The Mac & Cheese was a true disappointment. Although the cast-iron skillet it came in was hot to the touch, sadly, the food was lukewarm. Even more sadly, upon my first foray into the dish, I was dismayed to find pools of melted butter puddled in the crevasses and in the depressions that my spoon left. eeyuk! The cheese, while tasty, was very grainy. My spirits flagged. However! The steak sandwich was glorious: A very generous portion with creamy, rich boursin cheese, good bread, no scrimping on the steaky bits...fantastic. The fresh greens dusted with flecks of ParmReg cheese that sat at the sandwich's side proved to be excellent as roughage goes. I wish I had room for a) dessert or b) one of their amazing-looking specialty drinks but I was more full than anyone should be at 2:00pm. I paid the tab and sauntered out, taking in the beautiful sights, smells and sounds all around me and vowing to come back once I hammered out that pesky clause with my stomach.
Please, please go, it's truly a delight.

(For this review I will be handing over the reins to the very capable Ignatius J Reilly as his fine, discerning tastes and inimitable knowledge about Nawlins cuisine far outstrips my own. Pardon his tendency to drone on.)

Dear Thoughtful Reader,
Today was thoroughly unpleasant; a sloshy mud puddle of a day, abominably cold and damp. On days like these I am doing well if I have enough spirit to straggle out of the swaddling in my bed,  but Fortuna's sweet promise of treats and savories, whipped up in the fashion known to my beloved home city was enough to set me down the road to the godforsaken corner where the dross of Delaware and Pennsylvania collide, Boothwyn. "Booth's Corner", as it were, my eventual destination. Inside this Ali Baba's cave (in warehouse incarnation) somewhere, a stand called Cajun Kate's was beckoning with it's aromatic toothsome fare.

I was terribly enervated along the way; travel by automobile does horrors to my valve, which was sending out distress signals when finally I happened upon a space in the expansive, buzzing parking lot. Booth's Corner, a place heretofore I had never witnessed, is a veritable hotbed of activity, a sprawling chaotic market of sorts where all manners of merchandise are sold to the masses: young grabbing harridans, the watery-eyed aged, and everything in between shouting orders and taking slips of paper to endlessly queue up for produce, tchotchkes, fowl and Fortuna only knows what else. I was immediately lost.

Passersby in this gigantic agora had the hurried, glazed look of those unconcerned for the man in peril, so finally I ventured to call upon a rather bored looking retailer ( he was hawking faux flora, bored I would be too) to point me in the direction of the stall in question. I finally happened upon it, the so-called "Cajun Kate's" showed to be a simple counter with a handful of stools lined up in front. Every stool was occupied save one, so I settled my carriage precariously onto this and took to scrutinizing the menu. The men behind the counter were cheeky, ruddy types with the air of  true denizens of the Crescent City (whether they ever stepped a farthing's worth into the fair city or not I felt a mild kinship with them immediately).  As I learned, this rudimentary counter took naught but cash, and since I was not sufficiently well-coined to order a smorgasbord I settled on jambalaya,  "gator on a stick" , beignets and a cafe au lait. They took my order and tossed it between them until what was once a straightforward selection was now a patchwork of their own kitsch jargon.

Presently, my food was delivered to me. I sniffed the fumes issuing forth with great sensory pleasure, the vibrissae about my nostrils taking in the smokiness of the alligator sausage,  the serene aroma and pleasing hue of the cafe au lait, and the piquant spice of the jambalaya. I found the rice in the latter to be a tad mushy, but I will magnanimously forgive that offense because the rest of the dish satiated my hunger, as did the scrumptious sausage. After washing down my meal with the cafe au lait I accepted my beignets. Inquiring after the recipe I was told it was a Kate's original. Fair enough, but this did not prove to dethrone that of Cafe du Monde's. Still, I gobbled them down with great rapidity.

I was deeply satisfied and settled my bill, and then set off home. I shall spare you, dear reader, from the account of the various atrocities and offenses to taste and decency I encountered on the way back to my warm bed. I daresay I will venture out to Kate's again, but I shudder to think of the journey involved. 
Until later, 
Ignatius J Reilly


(Lisa's note: Booths Corner is great (as of course is Kate's). Do not read too much into Ignatius' vituperation )

Lisa's edit part 2:

Ignatius can shove it. On subsequent visits, I savored the amazing tomato soup, the FANTASTIC fried mac&cheese, rice and beans, gumbo, and EVERYTHING is delicious. 
!!!!

5 STARS!!!!

Even though the reviews here were enough to dissuade me from ever stepping foot into Hank's, I agreed to go when some of my people insisted on its merits and invited me to breakfast. I got there about 20 minutes early so I stood in line to commandeer a table for us. After 15 minutes or so waiting in line, I was coldly & summarily dismissed with a "we only seat full parties!!" , and a swift turn of the heel. 

The others eventually arrived, and we were eventually seated (fade-in to clock, another 30 minutes have passed). Our booth was filthy, little egg bits and toast crumbs scattered to all four corners by the single harried wipe of the busboy were menacing us and our elbows. My ears were filled with the din of the packed restaurant...cacophony & clatter, complete with children screeching. (My least favorite noise in the world). Hank's was terribly stuffed with people. And I really don't know why, because the food wasn't anything above the label of "sustenance". 

Others may like it because, as they say, it's "an institution" , but I'll never go back. At least it was relatively cheap.

My husband and I had dinner reservations at another nearby place, but stopped in for a couple appetizers and beverages. This was my first time here and the atmosphere is cozy, quaint, and covid safe. We didn't want to take a real table, so we sat at a high top in the back bar area. I could see they had ample outdoor seating as well. 

I ordered the octopus and O.M.G. it was the best octopus I ever had. It was tender, light, and loved the orange segments, pickled onion, and drizzle. I ate this a couple of weeks ago and I'm still thinking about it. I order a glass of pinot grigio and it paired very well. The menu looks so good; I can't wait to go back and try more of the menu.

Service was excellent as well. They offer valet parking.

My BFF and I went to the Twisted Tail for dinner (Restaurant Week) and wow, was it seriously good. Parking in the area can be a challenge, so if you're driving in, give yourself plenty of time to park. After circling around we stumbled upon a great spot. Great start to the night!

I started with a glass of champagne, because it's a Tuesday - let's celebrate! 

As I mentioned it was restaurant week and what drew me to this menu was the 4 courses, dessert is typically wasted on me so I liked the fact there were 3 courses with savory options. 

1st course - Quail and Smoked Wings - Yes to both! I ordered the quail, it was small, but the pesto was incredible. My BFF ordered the smoked wings. You.must.order these! Tender, smoky, and needs nothing to accompany it. 

2nd course - Foie Gras and Meatballs - I have not had foie gras in a long time. Why? Oh wait, it's not the healthiest option and it's nice to indulge occasionally. The presentation was beautiful and the figs were perfect. The meatballs were tender and good, but I could have eaten 2 more plates of the foie gras.

3rd course - Swordfish and Fried Chicken - I ordered the fish and it was cooked perfectly. I loved the radishes and used it more like a taco. The fried chicken was so stinking tender. The only thing is everything on the plate was fried, it would have used a vegi or starch that wasn't fried to break up the heaviness. But you can't go wrong with it, it's amazing and a very large portion. 

4th course - Remember when I said dessert is lost on me. Not here. I ordered the panna cotta - perfectly set, not too sweet, creamy. Just a perfect way to end the meal. I did also try the beignets and they were great. 

It was a fantastic meal and hit the spot of craving indulgence without walking away hating myself for eating so much. The menu was balanced with options for those who want to watch their waistline along with those who are craving some good comfort food.

This was such a cool looking place! I went to support a friend for the art bazaar that they were having all weekend.  They had the whole upstairs full with art displays.  Ironically, the place gives off an artsy vibe.  It was such a cool looking bar inside and out with the industrial look (sorry no pics). 

The bartender was also very sweet and was patient with us while we sampled a few beers to find the ones we liked.  They also serve 4 oz. glasses which was perfect for me since I was tired that day and had a long day! Just enough for this lightweight :-)

I didn't stay long but long enough to notice that they have connect 4 on the tables and corn hole outside on the balcony. There was also a seafood food truck which smelled really yummy but I had just ate. I definitely will come back to make a night out of it.

So much to say and wish I had many good things to say, but I don't.  The good news is, I will definitely give Mimi's another try in the future.  I am just going to wait until they work out some of the kinks.

Let's start with the positive things about our experience:

AMBIANCE:  Great.  Loved the interior.  

LOCATION:  Mass Ave really needs some new late night restaurants to draw business to that end of the Ave.  Great to see.

PARKING:  Even with so many businesses closed on that end of the Ave on a Monday night, street parking was still very slim.  Fortunately, there is a large lot behind the building across the street.

SERVICE:  I honestly thought the service was great.  We were asked multiple times by many if we needed any help with the menu, suggestions were offered and also asked how our dining experience was.  See my negative service comments in the additional notes below.

Now, onto the not so great things about our experience:

DRINK MENU:  I was very pleased to see five local craft beers on tap, in addition to PBR and an extensive wine selection as well.  Unfortunately, after ordering our beers, we were notified that only one beer was remaining on tap for the night.  We ordered one of those and also a bottled beer (the bottled selection was pretty decent too).  The draft selection we ordered came out half full.  Apparently the keg blew.  So, this left NO beer on tap for the evening.  

DINNER MENU:  It is a meatball place, so I guess it is normal to see most everything meatball related on the menu.  It is just a little weird; somewhat.  To get just a meatball dish, there were two options:  3 meatballs (all with the same sauce) for $8 or 4 meatballs (mix and match the type of meatballs and sauces) for $11.  A friend was exiting as we were reviewing the menu and said, "Did they tell you yet that the 4 meatballer is not available tonight?".  They hadn't.  Kind of weird too.  If you can make a three meatballer, why can't you make a four meatballer with the same ingredients and sauces?  So, the three meatballer, it was going to be.  They were also out of several side dishes as well.  Among our limited menu options, here is what we ordered:

1.  Wedge Salad:  The server suggested the balsamic dressing, which was very good.  Other dressing option was "Sweet".  The salad was decent, but it was NOT a wedge.  It was 4-5 uncut pieces of romaine with halved cherry tomatoes and the dressing.  Boring, but decent.

2.  Dirty Mashed:  Flavor was great and I truly enjoyed them, but they were served a little cold.

3.  Turkey Meatballs with Spicy Cilantro sauce:  These meatballs were good, but the sauce had a spicy kick to it.  I wasn't expecting that and really didn't enjoy them for that reason.  

4.  Classic Meatballs with Marinara sauce:  These meatballs were a little dry and the sauce was just okay.

5.  Beef Meatballs with Spicy Bolognese sauce:  These meatballs were also a little dry, but I loved the sauce.

*Meatball Note:  I didn't think any of our meatballs really came out hot enough.

ORDERING:  At Mimi's, you order kind of similar to a sushi restaurant.  You get a marker and the menu is a dry-erase menu.  This gets really tricky when you want to order multiples of one meatball offering having different meatballs with different sauces.  I had to draw lines and arrows to everything and just hope they understood our order!  Not sure that I like this ordering style.

VALUE:  For what we got, I felt like it justified what we spent.  We didn't feel like we ate a lot, but couldn't finish everything and left super full.  The meatballs aren't extremely large either.  I am still stuffed 2 hours later.  Our check was $50 with our food and two beers.

Additional notes:

1. SERVICE:  I felt like they should have told us the menu items that weren't available upon handing us our menu.  This way, we wouldn't waste time ordering things we couldn't have.

2.  SERVICE:  We had to ask for extra plates to dish our meatballs and sides onto.  This should just be a standard delivery with the food.

3.  SERVICE:  No spoons served with the meatballs for serving.

4.  Not a huge big deal, but my chair (back up against the kitchen) was in a very awkward place.  They were carrying food and bus trays behind me and I just felt like I was in their way.

5.  Apparently, the veggie meatball is deep fried, so save your calories and get a meaty one.

Again, I will definitely give Mimi's another try.  I am always hesitant to visit a new restaurant so soon after they open for fear of writing a review like this.  I can't wait to go back and try them again and hopefully increase my star rating.  

Unfortunately, I forgot my phone tonight, so I have no pictures.  The menu markings to place our order were pretty entertaining too!

Good luck, Mimi's!

PLEASE READ ***** Do not ever patronize this establishment. 

My husband and I wanted to go somewhere different for our Anniversary, so I found this place on Groupon and purchased the deal. Since the website offered very little info, I called to confirm their closing time and was told the kitchen closes at 9:30 and they close at 10pm. (according to yelp they close at 2am). 

Upon our arrival at 8:40, it was evident from the looks on the patrons and workers faces that they weren't accustomed to serving people who looked like us. We were immediately told the kitchen was closed to which I responded not according to my phone call earlier. She went and "checked " with the kitchen and returned saying we have appetizers. I explained how I called, spoke to someone, checked the website and then purchased the Groupon they advertised, none of which stated appetizers only. The response I received was "Well the average person who comes here knows that". Realizing this is my 7th anniversary, I'm in a suburban area, and I don't have bail money, I politely said you're right, we won't be back and promptly called Groupon for my refund. 

Partially pissed, partially appalled, but completely proud of how I handled myself.

I left this place feeling totally bummed.
