I couldn't have been more fired up about finding a Japanese noodle shop near my office. I waited until Friday to join a co-worker for a lunch out. We both thought this was going to be something special, and perhaps a great and inexpensive addition to the weekly lunch rotation. 

First off, the ordering process and the service is confusing. We walked in and had no idea what to do. Although we did get some direction from a cashier(?), uh, waitress(?), maybe attendant, it still seemed that there was no obvious flow to ordering. This could be remedied with a simple sign with some directions: "seat yourself and order at the bar," "please order at the bar before seating," "yo! order grub in the rear and sit down!" Anything to avoid the obvious confusion that we, and other patrons were feeling after walking in. Is this a buffet? Are we waiting for table service? What the heck is going on in this joint?

Then, I started to feel like I was being nickel and dimed. $11 for a bowl of udon noodles with chicken. $3 for a cucumber salad. $3 for two pieces of tempura. $2 for a drink. I figured what the hell, it's going to be really good! But that's a $20 lunch y'all and honestly, that ain't gonna work for me on the regular. At first glance I was excited because I thought you got to choose one of the appetizers with your ramen bowl, but then I saw the prices on each label, and was a little shocked. In addition to the base price on each appetizer item was another charge for toppings and sauces. Whoa! Take it easy, noodle guy, with your fingers in my wallet. No thanks! 

Lastly, I can say that I did enjoy the noodles themselves. Clearly they were homemade and of high quality ingredients. Unfortunately, this alone wasn't enough to make the meal. The traditional fish broth lacked flavor, and the bowl came with only the udon and a few slices of chicken. You are expected to add your own toppings at another bar, and the choices here were a little slim. 

There's just not enough taste, decor, and service at Maru to justify the high price of a visit. I'm excited by the concept of a more or less "self-serve"noodle shop, but the price would have to be more on par with a lunch at Subway for me to return.

Was very disappointed and here's why. First, prices are pretty high for most everything. Fisherman's Platter (didn't order) - Flounder shrimp, crab cake, scallops  = $25. Really?
Saw another table order mussels. They came out in a large container but we could see half way down and saw no mussels. 

Ordered the Calamari app. flavorless...and I do mean flavorless. Served with some type of marinara sauce, also flavorless.
Right away waitress told us that they were out of some clam dishes since the Ocean has been very cold, supply has not been good. Man, that was some excuse!

Ordered the Stuffed Shrimp Platter - also flavorless and the 4 smallest shrimp we ever saw. Served with double order of string beans - terrible and only single order.
Full rack of ribs - huge portion and EXTREMELY meaty. Waitress told us that getting them was a hit/miss. Flavor was fair but they were incredibly tender and thick. Cole slaw was "spit it out in your napkin" bad!
Two people = 1 app, 2 dinners, 2 beers and 1 wine = $75 ! Unfortunately will never go back. 
Service was very good though. 

If the quality and portions of the food remains, this place will be out of business in one year.

A while ago I reviewed this pizza place on Yelp. The owner sent me a message thanking me for trashing his pizza place. I have since deleted that honest critique in which I had hoped he would possibly learn from the critique, rather than lash out at a paying customer. The below review is in fact me trashing his pizza place. Enjoy:

Wednesday rolls around and I wander over to Beddia....because like a bunch of assholes they are only open Wednesday to Saturday. Apparently no one eats pizza Sunday, Monday or Tuesday. 

A few things one NEEDS to know before dealing with this place:

1. They don't take phone calls. You have to walk in and order. Dumb.
2. They only take cash. 
3. The wait is ridiculous.
4. Their are no chairs to eat your pizza or wait.
5. Their pizza is expensive as hell. 
6. They are assholes.

I walk into this pizza hole at 5:30 as they open. I walk up to the counter, were I am met by the counter douchebag. Before I am able to say a word, he hastily tells me the next pizza won't be out of the oven until 6:35. I walked in at 5:30. I was confused, because I didn't fucking order anything yet. I said "oookay" and ordered a sausage and onion pie. They only make one size, which is around a medium anywhere else. The pizza starts at 19 dollars before tax. 4$ for sausage and 3$ for roasted onion, the pizza came to 28+ with tax. 

28$ dollars for a medium pizza. This is where "Bob" the owner tried to take me to task. He cries about how if I knew how much organic flour and locally sourced farm produce costs then I wouldn't complain. Well Bob, I would, because after an 8 second Google search I discovered that a 50 pound bag of organic flour costs right around 78$. 

Bob....you're doing it wrong. 

Lets pretend that your organic flour is breaking your budget. Do you really have to charge 4$ for sausage and 3$ for onions? 3 FUCKING DOLLARS FOR ONIONS. Bob.....please tell me you unearthed these onions after a Sherpa leads you to Peru on one of your many off days. Bob...are these Peruvian onions???? Maybe that would explain why a minimal amount of flavorless onion would cost THREE FUCKING DOLLARS. Bob, organic onions cost around 3$.....A POUND. There were MAYBE a handful of onions chopped up on my pizza.....I honestly didn't really taste them, because they were either terrible or weren't there. 

4$ for sausage? Is it unicorn sausage? Did you hunt and slaughter a mythical horned horse to make this sausage? That MAY explain the price...on second thought, it doesn't, because unicorns don't exist. I will say it's probably easier to find unicorn sausage than it is for you to find a Goddamn phone in your pizzeria. 

All in all the pizza was just standard pizza. Not very good, especially for the cost. 

Lets talk about their weird rules...

Pizza Club Rules:

1. Don't talk about Pizza Club Rules....no, seriously. They don't like it and get really rude when you question their bullshit rules. 

2. They don't take phone calls. On what planet does a pizza place not take phone calls?  Is it a matter of not paying the bill, I doubt it, they charge 3$ for Peruvian onions (most likely from the nearest Aldi), they can afford it. Nope...maybe the near condemned building they reside in doesn't possess the proper infrastructure for you know, wires. Or--OR......they are trying to be like a shitty, pizza version of a speak-easy. Christ, I wish Elliot Ness would raid this shithole. 

Hey dumb-dumb (talking to you Bob), Take phone calls. Don't make your customers wander into your pizza place to order. It's really, really bad customer service and only the douchiest of hipsters will think what you are doing is cool. 

3. Put some chairs around the two tables you have for people who BYOB and/or have to wait for literally hours for a pizza. It's like you are going out of your way to make your customers as uncomfortable and annoyed as possible. What's next Bob....a waiting room at GITMO?

4. Take other forms of payment for your pizza.....like debit cards, credit cards, 401K's, IRA's....gold and other precious metals. Because....YOUR PIZZA IS EXPENSIVE....FOR NO REASON.

This place is just pretentious. Tries to be something they are not. After reading Bob's Yelp handle it actually explains a lot.  Bob writes; "i've eaten 3 michelin star sushi and you haven't"

Hey Bob....no one cares. Not one single person cares about what you have eaten. 

Reduce costs in your pizza place, pass the savings onto your customers, take phone calls, put some chairs in and first and foremost....treat your customers with a little Goddamn respect.

Until that happens (and it never will)...I'm going to Pizza Brain...because they are flat out the best pizza in Fishtown.

******UPDATE******

The owner of Pizzeria Beddia Bob "Joseph" Beddia called my place of employment after I posted this review. He did so in an effort to adversely impact my standing at my job. He sent the link of this review to my HR rep and general manager to read.

They thought it was hilarious.

THIS place. I will give it 5 stars after one visit, because I had a really great first experience. I will leave it at that until something changes. I would have never found it on my own, as it is tucked back in a tiny little shopping area. I was close by and needed something a little low key to grab a bite to eat without it being a hassle. Here's where Yelp came to save my day, and it definitely worked out. 
It's cute and funky on the inside. Mismatched couches and assorted tables to hang out at. I walked straight to their counter to look over their lunch menu. There were a lot of amazing choices, and I did have a hard time deciding...especially with their bakery case taunting me. The counter help was really pleasant on greeting me and didn't rush me at all. I told them it was my first time there, and they happily gave me a run on what they liked and what they're popular item was. They also gave me a complimentary "breakfast bar" for being a first time customer. I went with the butternut bean burrito and a big ol' cup of coffee. I enjoyed my breakfast bar while I waited, which was amazing enough. It tasted like a warm oatmeal and banana cookie of sorts. I probably could have eaten 10 of them, even though they are a pretty decent size. I was also in heaven with the coffee. It was strong and burning hot (really hot coffee is harder to come by than you would think). I also give brownie points for them having stevia on hand. My burrito came out shortly thereafter, and it was amazing. I hadn't been that pleased with food in awhile, so I was pretty fricken happy. I left that place in a damn good mood, knowing that I'd be back.

It is a little expensive, but I don't care. I don't mind forking up extra money for delicious food. Their bakery items looked absolutely amazing, and it's definitely something I'll be trying in the future.

had always wanted to try The Parish but had never managed to make it over there and then one day they donated a bunch of food to the hospital I was working at ( respiratory department) during the beginning of the pandemic and I was blown away. There was a bunch of different foods so I got to try a bunch of different things and WOW. The next week I was ordering to go from there for me and my daughter.This has easily become one of my favorite places to eat in Tucson. I actually can't think of anywhere I'd rather go every time I think about going out to eat. The drunken angel dish is amazing and what I am stuck on at the moment. I also LOVE the pulled pork pibil thing they have going on. They have a really cool little bar with different infused alcohols. I come here at least once every couple weeks, very grateful to have this place to go eat at :)

I had a great weekend at the Belmond El Encanto. From the moment I arrived, I felt especially taken care of by the staff. They are a member of Fine Hotels & Resorts so be sure to book through them to get the upgrade, complimentary breakfast and resort amenity. 

We were able to check into our room at 1pm, which was great. There was a fireplace and a view of the ocean. It was an upper bungalow and felt very private. I loved that they give a complimentary bottle of local wine in the mini bar. 

The gym was nice with new equipment and the grounds were very well manicured. 

The pool was on the smaller side and packed while we are there. I think they could have used a larger pool and pool area, or perhaps an adult pool as there were quite a few children in the pool. The hotel movie selection was nothing to write home about. 

Room service for breakfast was better than expected with custom organic green juice, chicken apple sausage and a fruit platter. It took longer than expected to arrive, but I didn't mind as we had a gorgeous patio to enjoy. 

They are very dog friendly and brought a dog bed and bowls to the room for my dogs. 

The highlight of the stay was using the Faraday electric bikes and heading into Santa Barbara. These bicycles are incredibly high-end and so easy and fun to use.  I was able to explore State Street, the Warff and more all by bike. 

I would stay here again and definitely recommend this property.

The quintessential breakfast spot for the Montecito area. Lines tend to get pretty long on the weekends, but they move quickly. 

I ordered the salmon benedict and was not disappointed. I was particularly impressed by the side of fruit, which was all super sweet, fresh and tasted like it came straight from the farmers market. 

I also took a bite of the chorizo omelette and the buttermilk blueberry pancakes. Everything was great. The chorizo omelette came with a biscuit on the side. 

Their orange juice is great, coffee drinks are great and they have a very cute setting with ample outside seating. Prices match the real estate in the Montecito area. Breakfast for 4 was $60.

I really wasn't crazy about Blush.

We sat on one of the high top tables with a fireplace in the center. 

It really went down hill with the appetizer. I ordered the poached pear "salad" with blue cheese and beets. The beets were offensively pickled and really strong. There were two tiny pieces of blue cheese. They were so stingy with it that you would have thought it was caviar. The pear had been soaked and lacked any natural sweetness. 

For my entree I had the salmon over a bed of quinoa. It was decent enough and they did prepare it medium rare as I had requested. The sauce was too buttery for me. A little bit of citrus would have helped a lot. 

Overall pretty mediocre food for a city that is supposed to have great restaurants. I wouldn't rush back.

Since this was my first visit to Nashville and Tennesse, I really wanted to enjoy some classic, southern BBQ. I was driving towards Knoxville and found this solid BBQ lunch just outside of Nashville. There are several locations in the area and this location is complete with an outdoor patio.

We lined up around 12:30 and looked over the menu while we waited to order. The Redneck taco (yes that is really what it's called) was recommended by the man in line ahead of me, and boy it was good. Moist pulled pork atop a corn pancake topped with coleslaw. You can choose chicken, pulled pork, brisket, turkey or sausage but I think the pulled pork is the way to go. 

We also ordered a 1/2 slab of dry baby back ribs. The rub on the ribs had incredible seasoning and flavor and the meat was tender and fell off the bone. Sides of mac and cheese, green beans and potato salad were all decent but the real star of the show is the meat. The Redneck Taco was my favorite by far. 

Martin's is casual with great food and really friendly service. A great place for classic BBQ!

I am now happily on a Mexican kick thanks to this place.

The nachos were ridiculous! Smothered in sour cream, guacamole, chicken and cheese, I couldn't hide my smile while eating these. 

We shared the fajitas and they had great flavor. The chicken was moist and seasoned well. You can tell a lot of thought and care goes into their dishes. We sat outside on a beautiful summer day, enjoying the sunshine, an arnold palmer and great service. Definitely recommended!

Tacos seem to be all the rave in Santa Barbara. Many of the popular spots can have long wait times, so I was happy to see that Corazon had no line on a weekend. Located within the Santa Barbara Public, parking was free and easy and there is indoor and outdoor seating.  

We ordered several items to share including the guacamole, mole taco, seafood taco, fish taco and tostada de ceviche with the local ahi, watermelon, pomegranate and avocado. Ingredients really stood out as being top quality. The highlights for me were the mole taco with Mary's organic chicken, rice, onion and cotija cheese as well as the Sal De Mar ceviche. They have a very nice spread of complimentary salsas to pick from.

Prices were higher than your average taco shop, but I can appreciate that this is because they are using quality ingredients. A great place to get fabulous tacos in Santa Barbara.

Pretty good. This one's a 3.5. 

First off, the decor and ambiance here is downright cool. Super modern, chic, and open. Definitely unique with good vibes. Great for groups too. We came to celebrate my friend's 30th birthday and it was definitely a good pick. 

Food? So so. Some was very good, some was just okay. 

Let's start with the very good... THE RICOTTA BOARD. So f-ing good. A must-get. Delicious wood-fired piadina bread served with a jar of creamy honey ricotta. The combo is beyond perfect. The piadina bread is baked just right - perfect chew on the inside, warm and crisp on the outside. The ultimate vehicle for the amazing honey ricotta mixture. Every dip into the jar created a perfect bite of creamy, savory, sweet, goodness. Perfecto. 

Another pretty impressive dish is the seafood fra diavlo. Unfortunately I didn't order this for myself, but my friend did, so naturally I munched on hers, ha. Plenty of seafood with a solid sauce. Yum!

For me, some of the "just okay" items were the truffle mac n' cheese, cheesesteak eggroll, and the wild mushroom truffle pizza. All seemed a bit dry or over cooked. The mac n' cheese was definitely the driest of them all. Good truffle flavor, but the pasta was crunchy. Wouldn't get this again. The pizza wasn't too bad but just seemed a bit on the bland side. The cheesesteak eggrolls were pretty underwhelming too. The steak was dry, not so cheesy, and not so plentiful. 

Overall, LaScala's a good joint for a get together, offering a nice selection of foods that's easily sharable. Some improvements can easily make this into a five star pizza spot so I'll keep my fingers crossed for now and check back in when I'm in the area.

Some hits, some misses, but overall a 3.5ish if ya ask me. 

I love me a small, refined menu - which is what you'll find at Zeppoli. It's like a showcase of one's masterpieces, amirite? I really wish this was the case at Zep, but unfortunately I think a few things could use some tweaking. 

The meats. My main gripe. Cooked beautifully! But what's a perfectly cooked piece of meat when it's under seasoned? It leaves much to be desired. Our stewed rabbit and grilled lamb chops were tender and cooked perfectly, but just slightly on the bland side. Even the broccoli rabe could've used a little pizazz, like garlic and salt. Being too bitter and too bland, it pretty much went untouched. A little more oomph with the seasoning would've really brought these dishes to their full potential. 

I did say there were some hits remember? 

The pasta! Hands down I'd come back for the beautiful plate of pesto trapanese made with an almond-pistachio pesto. Delightful and delicious. 

As you may have already guessed, the zeppolis too! These little tiny doughnuts were perfect. Crisp, light, and incredibly fluffy. 

Although slightly on the noisy side, this small, intimate, BYOB restaurant is perfect for date night is ya ask me. Even with a few missteps, I still enjoyed a lovely dinner thanks to a yummy bottle of wine and most importantly, great company.

If a Chinese girl told you this is one of the best Chinese joints in Jersey, are you willing to believe her? If yes, then continue on my friend!

Oh wow... you have a lot of faith in me. 

Let me start by saying there's a loyal fan base for Joe's and for a very good reason. While it's nothing fancy shmancy on the inside, it's a great spot to sit comfortably, sip some tea, and stuff your face with delicious, great quality Chinese food. All for a very reasonable price too. If you're lucky, you'll catch Joe himself making his rounds and greeting all of his patrons, especially the loyal ones that keep coming back. Oh yes, there was many of them. 

If you're a newbie here, go for Joe's specialities. You guessed it... the duck! Joe cleverly put together set menus for parties of all sizes which include duck, fried rice, wonton soup, and additional dishes depending on which set menu you order. A great bargain if you're rolling deep and feel like enjoying a delicious duck meal family style. The way any traditional Chinese meal should be enjoyed.

It was a chilly rainy night when we visited so we went with something different, the wonton and duck egg noodle soup. The bowl arrived piping hot with al dente egg noodles, flavorful wontons, and tender, fatty duck. As expected from traditional Chinese broths, it was light and mild, allowing me to spice it up with their hot chili oil. Best of all, the broth had plenty of roasted duck flavor. So even after we devoured all of the duck, we still enjoyed the delicious smoky flavor in spoonfuls of broth. My mouth waters just thinking back to it. 

Another one of Joe's specialities that came highly recommended is the spicy szechuan beef udon noodles. It's unbelievably good. Every bite was saucy, spicy, peppery, and overall flavorful. While it's listed as a soup noodle, the light, clear broth is actually served separate from the noodles and used as a palette cleanser. I was skeptical of the broth at first, but it turned out to be extremely satisfying in between all of the slurp-slurp action. Yes, definitely get this. 

For me, the most surprising aspect of Joe's was how good they make "American Chinese" food. We decided on an order of the grandfather chicken, which was essentially their version of general tso's. What a fantastic dish. For once, there was more meat than breading and best of all, it was all tender white meat. Kinda unheard of nowadays. The portion was plentiful and the sauce was just right - thick, sweet, and spicy. The best general tso's I've ever had! 

If you've made it this far into my novel on how much I love Joe's, then I'm sure you're already contemplating a visit. Like Nike... JUST DO IT.

We stopped by Nashville for one night halfway during our road trip and so glad we tried this place with our local friend. Although the line wasn't short, it definitely worth the wait. 

Three of us got dark meat, white meat, chicken tender and several sides. There was lots of food, and the hot chicken was to die for!! Skin was very crispy with not too much extra grease. Meat was hot and juicy. Not to mention the smell was so appetizing, which made me hungry while waiting in line. The only thing I didn't really enjoy on my plate was the bread, but I guess it was there mostly to absorb the extra grease. 

Overall, Nashville hot chicken was so delicious!

We stopped here for a drink after having dinner at Barbuzzo down the street. The place was jam-packed and very loud. Which is pretty much what I expected at late night. The cocktail I ordered was great. The service was all hands on deck and saw manager taking orders from the tables to accommodate the guests. I'd go back here for dinner.

PS: If you like to explore your cocktails, I recommend going off menu and give your server your favorite liquor and answer a few questions about flavor profile. The bartenders are fantastic and you won't be disappointed by their artistic freedom!

I just went to Brennan's for the 2nd time. The first time was for my roommate's college graduation. It was wonderful. His father is a very wealthy lawyer, and thus tipped the hostess a couple of Benjamin's to get us a table without a reservation. We were thereafter treated exquisitely (even more so after each time he ordered a $100+ bottle of champagne).

This time, I took my Bride to Brennan's for brunch the morning after our wedding. We showed up at 10:50 for an 11am reservation; we were told our table would be ready shortly, and that we could wait at the bar. The bartender told us that we couldn't sit at the bar if we weren't ordering drinks as there was a line, so we stood along the wall. A crowd guys who were obviously very drunk then walked in (11 am, folks). They were all wearing shorts, flip-flops, and baseball caps; they looked like they should have been at taco bell, not a supposedly "fine dining" establishment. One of them ordered a [very large] Milk/Brandy Punch. He was so drunk that he dropped it immediately upon purchasing it. The glass hit the ground, and shattered; the drink went everywhere... all over my white linen suite. I stood there in shock until some employee shoved me out of the way and said "Move!" They said nothing more to me, but they made this guy another drink at no cost to him.

I was pissed and I realized it was now about 11:15-11:20, so I walked over (drenched in punch) to the hostess and asked if we were going to be seated soon. She told me that it was a 30 minute wait for a table. She said that she knew that and had we not had a reservation it would have been an hour and a half wait. I explained to her that I had a reservation so I wouldn't have a wait, and anyway it had now been over a half hour. I went to get my wife to leave and someone rushed over to tell us that our table was now ready... total B.S.

The waiters were completely absent, but to take our order in the beginning. A different server brought us our food. My wife didn't get her drink until dessert. The food was delicious, but then again not that much drastically better than when I do Eggs Benedict at home. My fried trout is better than theirs. The ice cream in my Bananas Foster was melted by the time I got it.

We went to Galatoire's for dinner to make up for our miserable experience here. The kicker, breakfast at Brennan's for 2 with no drinks - $100+, Dinner for 2 at Galatoires with drinks - $70.

Some friends took us here on opening night. Opening night typically a bad time to go to a restaurant. We went anyway, and it was definitely not a mistake. Granted, they do have a couple things to iron out, but that should take no time at all, and none of the problems were even big enough to knock it down from a full five stars.

The number of places the serve good Neapolitan style pizza in this city are growing (Mondo, Domenica), but this is the first place to specialize in it (along with Salumi), and I'm lucky to have it only a few blocks from my house. Chef Adolfo Garcia even came and chatted with our table for a while.

Best Margherita pie I've had in this city.

We had a long wait it was busy but not busy that we had to wait for 2-3 hrs.  I am having hot tea  I had must of asked for sugar from our waitress that when she didn't  get to it I had asked the manager. I ordered a French dip it was good.

Barcelona Tapas is awesome!! As soon as you enter and see the beautiful mosaic bar and the dark stained wooden beams and doors you feel like your in a Tapas restaurant in the Barrí Gotic of Barcelona. 
My wife and I had an assortment of Tapas small plates that were excellent and fresh. The attention to detail showed the passion that Chef Xavier has for his food. 
Garlic shrimp were wonderful 
Ceviche was generous and delicious with a hint of citrus served on a bed of lettuce. 
Garlic mushrooms were fresh and my wife's favorite 
Patas Bravas were just as good , if not better than the many ones we had in Barcelona 
Garlic tomato toast with manchego cheese was very good and fresh
We also had an excellent bottle of Tempranillo and delicious chocolate flan.
The service from Tanya and staff was great and they had some very good recommendations . We can't wait to return and enjoy another slice of authentic Barcelona.

I was on a business trip and decided to stop for a meal before getting back on the road.  I wouldn't say that it was in the best location but I was hungry.  The place seemed a bit dated but very clean and the staff was friendly enough but very occupied restocking after the lunch crowd.
As for the food, I ordered pork Pad Thai which was good.  What I was very impressed with was how fast I received my food - it was just as fast as going to a regular fast food restaurant......and for that I thank you and if I am in the area again I will be back.

Just tried out 1864 for the first time.  Very cool place.  Bartenders were super friendly and welcoming.  Great selection of bourbons and whiskeys and good selection of beer as well.  Décor is very cool and true Nevadans will really appreciate the details.  Had a great time on one of the couches playing Nevada trivia!  We can't wait to go back!

Quaint and charming little spot. Total hidden gem. 

We've had Ethiopian food before in South Tampa and at a couple of spots in Orlando. This particular place is very close to my house so I know we'll be here more than every 6 months. The owner was a sweet heart and the service was excellent. 

We had just finished up a late night cultural performance and we were starving ... go figure it's Sunday and everything in Tampa closes at 9pm... we were hungry at 9:30pm and finally had time to think about food. We didn't want to be those people that just showed up at a venue so we called ahead to find out what time they were closing. She said they close at 10 and asked how far away we were. Our answer to distance was 10 minutes and she said come on down. We were warming greeted even though it was almost closing time. 

We had a wonderful meal with a mix of beef and veggie dishes. She explained all the dishes as she presented it and that added to the restaurants charm. =)

I actually found a ramen spot in the Bay Area that is finally decent! 

I've been here a couple of times since and the food has still been spot on. Their ramen broth is something that warms your heart when its cold out. 

If you didn't know what you were looking for you would pass this place. The building is black and has no writing or markings to make it look like a restaurant. The inside has a cool 'hipster' motif with a very interesting mural on the bar wall. It's dark and mysterious inside but luckily they have tall windows and during the day it's filled with light, at night your table is dimmy lit with a small candle and a low watt overhead lift fixture. 

They have a very posh-cold vibe inside that sprawls from the hostess to the waiter all the way to your bartender. Don't let that deter you- the food is good. =)

They took off the most amazing ramen they had on the menu which was the Ox-tail so I'd rave about that but it's not there anymore. I can truly tell you that the broth in all the ramen dishes is so flavorful and feels like something you've been missing in your life when you slurp it. This is the only ramen I've had in the Tampa Bay region that is on the same level as New York's ramen spots. I've had a few of the cocktails- all delicious and their whiskey section is up to par.

This place is more of a small group of people dinner date; not a full out invite 6+ people coz chances are you won't sit together. We brought the baby the first time and it's not family (well baby) friendly as they did make it a point to say the ramen is VERY HOT as my newborn sat at the end of the booth. O-o The next time we sat at the bar and the bartender wasn't as engaging as you would think so we just kept to ourselves and ate our food. 

If i lived closer I'd visit more often but in all honesty parking in DTSP is a b*tch and sometimes a random weekday is the best time to go.

What an awesome new lunch spot to add to my rotation. I know that dinner is a bit expensive (it is meat after all) but Lunch prices are right up my alley! I was craving steak and decided to try it out. It's more business men (thus why it's called Executive Lunch) during normal lunch hours but if you go after 1 then it gets the more laid back crowd. 
The staff is super friendly and eager to help you with the menu items. I can't wait to try everything on the menu. I got the 8oz Picanha Grilled Sirloin- it was cooked to perfection. It was accompanied with rice and salad. The amount was perfect and I was totally satisfied afterwards.

Being Jewish, the only thing that I love more than Hanukkah is a really great deli. I'm not talking about a corner store that only sells hoagies, I mean sandwiches that are piled SO high that you can barely fit it in your mouth. I mean a deli that serves breakfast all day with 10 different omlettes, 5 different kinds of meat/seafood salads (tuna, chicken, whitefish, egg, and shrimp), soups that make your mouth water on the hottest of days, and a customer base that ranges from those that can barely talk to those that can hardly walk anymore. Basically, I want the ideal Jewish deli. 

Now maybe I'm a bit biased because I have grandparents who live in the Mecca of all things deli and diner (South Jersey) or maybe it's because I basically grew up in Famous' 4th Street, but I really didn't get my mind blown as much as I had hoped for with here. It did meet my bare-minimum requirements that I listed aboved but none of it really stood out. My boyfriend and I got the Perfect Match and A Spice of Life sandwiches respectively and while they were both big and good, something was just off. There was a bit too much Russian dressing and cole slaw which made it sweeter than necessary. The chicken noodle soup was good, but the matzo ball soup lacked something. Granted, every Jewish person is partial to their bubbi's recipe but these were a bit too dense and it almost seemed like they weren't cooked long enough. 

That being said, the service was fantastic and all the employees were genuinely sweet. Being in the service industry as well, that is always something I appreciate. 

I also kind of like how it's almost communal style. It gives you a chance to potentially meet people in the neighborhood who long for the same thing that I do - a good nova lox bagel and/or reuben. 

I will say that I'll probably go back here if I'm craving something hearty but don't have the time to get down to Famous'. Otherwise, you'll see me down on 4th and Bainbridge scarfing down Matzo-Brei like the world is going to end in 5 minutes.

There are 2 reasons why I fly to Philadelphia International Airport versus Newark Airport when going back East.

1. Cost: Savings of up to $100-200 per ticket 
2. Reading Terminal Market:

Definitely not one of the largest markets in the nation, but sometimes less is more. There are some "hot spots" that were featured on Man vs Food and the Travel Channel's named DiNic's Roast Pork and Beef "Best Sandwich in America" and Beiler's Bakery are my absolute favorite to dine at.

I can see why DiNic's sandwiches was honored that award. I had the roast beef with peppers, provolone, and broccoli rabe that was an excellent sandwich. This sandwich used simple ingredients with the right balance of flavor and the freshness that you can taste and see.

This market definitely made my criteria as one of my all time favorite markets to visit. Don't let the size fool you. It may be small but the cultural diversity of merchants, activities offered (check their calendar), and location in downtown Philadelphia puts this on top of my list. Chinatown is ONLY a walking distance away!

TIP: $4 parking fee for 2 hrs with $10 purchase and validation for a quick bite.
Fantastic food! I can't believe it's all vegan, I went with the Walnut shrimp and it was very tasty!

My homies and I did God's work ate four versions of Nashville Hot Chicken in one night (also using a double-blind study aka ate it at the same time on the trunk of a Toyota Prius) in order to determine the best one. Hattie B's tied for third in our universally agreed upon power rankings. 

Judges consisted of three men of different races, ethnicities, native languages, and styles of dance. Each person, though, has a strong passion for poultry. And no woman that night wanted to eat with us.

To control for as many variables as possible, we tried a mild flavored chicken breast at each one. This test did not take into account service, ambiance, and decor, or prices. It also did not factor into the overall ranking. 

Criteria and corresponding scores below:

*Spice (2/5): Not sure if we tasted a wrong type of Nashville Hot Chicken, but Hattie B's lacked any kick, whatsoever. I looking for you, Miss Cayenne Pepper.

*Meat Juiciness (3/5): It had some juice in it, but it didn't stand out when compared to the others we tasted. 

*Skin (3/5): It had a nice crunch and a slight sweetness. Not sure if it incorporated some sweet tea or sugar, but it is unique when compared to others. 

Overall Score: 3/5

Other tidbits:
- This Hattie B's location resides in a hipster part of town. 

- They cater to folks who have a below average spice level.

- Very touristy.

I plan on building a church... in the shape of an arepa. It will have a colorful and ornate stage with a statue of each one of these 11 chicks. I feel so blessed to have experienced one of the most remarkable sandwiches in my life. And I'm 33. The inspiration is flowing through my stomach, hands, and other places in my body. Like Michelangelo painting the Sistine Chapel. 

In my 33 years, I've destroyed plenty of arepas (that's what she said). And then one day my very vanilla friend, who for fun listens to sport podcasts and wears cargo shorts on the reg, asked if I wanted to dine at this restaurant with a 4.5-star rating thanks to over 100+ reviews. He put a gun to my head, so I agreed. So was it as good as advertised?  

Do I use chopsticks to eat spaghetti? Yes. Yes I do.

I don't consider myself religious, but spiritual. Because I felt the spirits after I ate the Chick #8 (Paisa) -- consisting of carne asada, pork, fried egg, sweet plantain, chorizo, avocado, some homemade sauce, and a special Venezuelan cheese. After the third or fourth bite, I started crying. Ugly crying because I...

1) Got my protein intake for the week.

2) Never felt more like a man (ironically, from a tasty place called 11 Chicks). I also grew some chest hair shortly thereafter. 

3) It was only $9.50.

Each bite felt like a mindf***. Like in Avatar when those giant blue elves hook themselves up to glowing trees and their magical, sorta sexual electrodes. I went somewhere else. You could say heaven. I'd like to think I visited Pandora. Yeah, Pandora.
*****
After reading The Subtle Art of Not Giving a F***, I give no f***s for my honesty because this place was fantastic. And if you visit St. Pete, happen to be hungry, and don't visit (and know about it), you have been judged (by me) as a person who doesn't enjoy good food or support local businesses. Shame on you. SH-AM-MEEEE.

And if that's the case, you're not allowed in my church. My tasty, tasty church.

***PRE-COVID 19***

Plant-based or not, I love me some non-dairy ice cream. Their coconut ice cream is straight-up delicious, and I would weigh 900 lbs more if I lived in St. Pete. (I would hit this joint up on the reg.) 

I tried four of their flavors and especially loved their coffee caramel bold, yet slightly sweet (like my attitude). I also would recommend their cookies and cream, and let me tell you they do well paying homage to one of the best flavors of all time. 

Plant Love, I hope you expand across the country one day. Y'all make fantastic stuff. 

Other tidbits:
- I believe the owner served us, and he's one of the friendliest folks ever
- Reasonable prices for single or double scoops
- Fantastic date spot inside

I hope they survive this crisis!

Oh, hey there, tourist. You're reading my review to see where else to eat beignets? Luck you! Here's the quick and dirty:

- In comparison to Cafe Du Monde, their beignets taste a bit thicker and doughy-er. Objectively, I preferred Du Monde's.

- Cafe Au Lait is good, and it's perfect to sip while watching folks walk up and down Royal Street.

- They serve more than beignets, such as breakfast and other pastries, but why order anything else? That's like going to a Vietnamese restaurant to ask for Chinese food. "No, b****, we don't serve egg foo young, here."

- Prices are relatively affordable, for a cafe au lait and beignet.

- They have a cutesy seating area, with heart-shaped seats and all, outside. "Cash me on the heart-shaped seats. How bow dah?" 

- It's located next to a police station, so it's relatively safe. lol.

Overall -- it's a great place to satisfy your beignet fix, but I wouldn't travel out of my way to eat there again.

Rename the B&M Burger to BDSM Burger. This naughty nom temptress will satiate your deepest foodie desires. Role play time:
*****
At your first (innocent) glance, you'll notice it looks a bit... different. You consider yourself more of a traditionalist when it comes to America's favorite food, but that's because you've only had potato buns for most of your life. But you pause.

You can't help love the darker bread-melanin of its big pretzel bosom. And despite the small frame, the BDSM Burger is stacked: 3x3x3...inches.

You gently caress your hands on its top and bottom (that's what she said), but then something savagely overpowers your brain. You can't resist. Your teeth sinks into that bosom, and it's everything you imagined. 

Unbelievably soft and savory tenderloin filet and short rib meatiness. Perfectly paired sweet from the bacon onion jam. Gooey-ness from the white cheddar (that's what she said). And a little spice from the arugula. Everything is perfect together. Just like Matthew Perry and Salma Hayak in Fools Rush In. 

You bite. You bite. You devour it and now there's nothing left except the grease along the rim of your mouth. 

You thank BM for the BDSM Burger and a good time. You even leave them the tip. (Not that tip.) Your experience leaves you wanting more.
*****
The octopus appetizer is a must, too.

I would consider converting to Islam, if it were the only way I could ever eat Surrey's Bananas Foster French Toast ($9.75) again. (I'm sort of Buddhist.) After eating a piece of this gorgeously quartered, super air-y, banh mi-like masterpiece--which rested on this PG-13 wet dream-sauce of rum, brown sugar, and butter, and dusted with white powder--I almost started crying. Like, when Scar clawed Mufasa's paws on that cliff and then savagely watched his brother get trampled to death by a heard in the Lion King-crying.

But happy crying. Not sad crying. So there's a better analogy here...

Each bite reminded me of the first time I lost my virginity. (TMI?) "Is this happening? Is this REALLY happening, and am I using protection (napkins)?" my mind asked. Immediately soon after the self-questioning, my brain answered its questions: "Yes, Jonathan, their naughty French toast took you to this part of your sub-conscious." Oh my goodness. How did I not blackout?  

Then I wanted more with Surrey's. Not a fling, but a full-out relationship, which would include hand-holding and love themed memes. So I ate their Shrimp and Grits ($13.25).

"JEE-SUUS! Hashtag blessed." --Bruno Mars.

The grits, smooth and creamy as a light-skinned baby's ass, probably ranks as the best I've ever put in my mouth. (It doesn't hurt they garnished it with savory bacon, freshly chopped green onions, and homemade croutons.) Also, the Gulf shrimp didn't taste frozen and oozed juices with each chomp of flesh and had enough Cajun kick.

My boo ate their Crab Meat Omelette ($12.95) and loved every bite, too. I believe she said she's never had a better omelet. 

They also have fresh vegetable and fruit juices:

-Carrot, apple, orange, grapefruit at $5.25 and $6.50 for a 12oz and 16oz, respectively. 
-Kale, celery, beet, or cucumber additions for .55 cents. 
-Ginger for $1.05. 

Everything tasted great, but it's rare I find a healthy juice super memorable. (Fresh squeezed juices usually taste excellent, yet the same, every time.

OVERALL: Don't mistakenly order the wrong dish, aka something not special, at this legendary NOLA eatery. Only order off of the Local Favorites section of the menu, which consists of the three dishes I mentioned above. And guess what? My boo and I ate them all like gangstas. (Cash me inside eating all da calories. How bout dat?)

It was the best American breakfast of my life, and I'm not embellishing.

Why 4 stars? Because I was happy to finally try Pisces.

   ---   ---   ---

Now that dine-in is once again allowed, I've made a pact to try all of the restaurants I've always wanted to visit, but never have for one reason or another. I don't even remember how long ago I bookmarked Pisces, but I finally made it over for dinner.

It was interesting to see that the menu had a bit of a latin flare to it. My favorite ended up being the Monfongo Bongo roll, partly because it was so unique and partly because it was just delicious.

We ended up ordering the Aloha Broha, Spicy Tuna, Dunedin Dream, Pink Panther, Spider, Mexicali Blues and the Volcano rolls. None of them quite stood out like the Monfongo Bongo, but none of them were bad, by any stretch!

I will say that more rolls here had an element of spice to them than you'd usually see, which I'm not a huge fan of, but none were insanely spicy. I don't think we ordered anything with jalapeno, but there were definitely some spicy sauces.

We tried to order the lobster tostones as an appetizer, but they were out, so we subbed in lobster rangoon instead.

Happy to see these folks back operating - my visit was long overdue!

Why 5 stars? Because the hype was big, but the product delivered.

   ---   ---   ---

Is this the most hyped a restaurant has been in my near-decade in Tampa? If it's not #1, it's at least on Mount Rushmore. And sometimes hype can lead to over-hype, which is no fun for anyone involved.

But over-hype didn't happen. Goody Goody delivered. Big time.

I moved to Tampa Bay in 2007, a couple of years after Goody Goody closed down. To be honest, I'd never even heard of it. But I think the idea of resurrecting of an old, beloved brand is absolutely amazing. That being said, I knew nothing about Goody Goody, before my visit this weekend. I actually thought it was primarily a burger place. Boy, was I wrong.

It's hard to truly classify Goody Goody. It's like an upscale diner, but still very casual. When I say upscale, I strictly mean in quality of food. This is far from Waffle House. But the menu is wide and varied - they did a great job creating a menu that tempts me to come back at least a dozen times to try everything. 

But on our first visit, we ordered two POX Cheeseburgers, fries, onion rings and mac-n-cheese. For dessert I grabbed a slice of butterscotch pie and a cafe con leche to help me awaken from my food coma.

Everything ranged from good to great. In terms of the burgers, I think Goody Goody will be Tampa Bay's version of In-N-Out. It's not like an In-N-Out burger, but it's very addicting in its own way. I could definitely see these burgers having a cult following. 

I actually didn't want onion rings, but my fiance thought they looked great in the photos, and decided to order them. This was an excellent choice - they were the best I've ever had. Sometimes onion rings are so heavily breaded/fried, that they sit in my stomach like a rock afterward. Not the case with these bad boys!

The fries were far from basic - thick and seasoned, just like I like 'em! And the mac-n-cheese had little bits of ham in it. It tasted simple but delicious.

The butterscotch pie was indeed sweet, but that's what dessert is supposed to be, right? The cafe con leche (from Naviera!) was as amazing as expected.

The interior of Goody Goody is exactly as you'd expect - the classic diner look, revamped and modernized. It's not a a very large place, which definitely leads to some long wait times. But I have a solution for you!

*****Here's the most crucial PRO TIP I've ever offered*****

Download the No Wait app (just recently purchased by Yelp), put your name on the list a couple hours before you want to eat, keep tabs on the wait time, and show up when it tells you to. You can completely bypass all the craziness and waiting!

I'll be back here. A lot. Thanks to the Gonzmart family and everyone else involved for bringing this local treasure back to life!

Why 5 stars? Because "Feel Great Food" is the perfect slogan.

   ---   ---   ---

I absolutely do not eat fast food. I treat it like the plague. It makes me feel awful immediately after consumption, usually for the remainder of the day, so I just gave it up cold turkey. If you see me in a drive-thru, it's probably just for a drink. (Chick Fila and PDQ don't count, right?)

But I definitely think Evos manages to fall as an exception to the norm. I don't eat it and instantly become filled with regret. And... it tastes good! Like, really good.

I started eating Evos when I first moved to Florida, about 7-8 years ago. I probably visited the South Tampa location at least two dozen times. It was my jam! But then I moved around a bunch, and lost touch with my healthy burger-servin' joint.

After recently moving to Carrollwood, I'd been tempted to pop into Evos for a while now, and finally got the chance. I'll admit - I was nervous that my previously unrefined palate had deceived me into thinking Evos was better than reality. The reviews were unspectacular, and maybe it wasn't a coincidence that my fond memories were all had long before I was Yelping on the regular.

Those fears were all for naught. Evos is still amazing, plus, the decor of the Carrollwood location is super cool! I want to steal the large, wooden table. Think they'd notice?

The bacon cheeseburger probably isn't the healthiest, but I it tastes superb, and definitely contains less calories (by default) than the nearby competition. And the garlic ketchup with the fries? Thumbs up emoji.

Why 5 stars? Because this is my favorite new discovery in 2013.

   ---   ---   ---

As someone who eats out more than the average bear, sometimes the meals can begin to run together. Anise was like a spiritual experience.

The stinky buns were utterly phenomenal. I definitely had a favorite, but now I am confusing them in my head and can't remember which one that it was. Oh well, I guess I'll have to return and try them all again... for research. And science.

The looks of the place made me feel like you're at a a high-end joint too classy for myself... but the prices are incredibly moderate. $11 for 3 Stinky Bunz? My friend and I split some truffle tator tots. Um... yeah. They're other-worldly. 

I'd go as far to say Anise might be in my top five restaurants in Tampa Bay. That's after one visit. And I haven't even tried the duck tacos or the cocktails yet... two of the top staples.

What a gem.

Why 5 stars? Because I was dumb originally rating it 4.

   ---   ---   ---

When I first visited Mazzaro's, I honestly had no idea what it was. I went straight to the hot sandwich counter, and just kind of walked through the rest of the market with my eyes closed.

In reality, Mazzaro's pretty much has everything edible that's ever been created. There's a great beer selection, they roast their own coffee beans, there's an entire room of cheese, it's a meat market, and they have all kinds of niche items like fancy olives and local honey.

This place is a Tampa Bay treasure, and I am ashamed of my original 4 star rating.

Why 5 stars? Because this is now my favorite diner ever.

   ---   ---   ---

I've wanted to visit the original Trip's Diner in St. Pete for years but just never quite had the chance to get over there. Then, they finally opened a location in Seminole Heights but I just kept on skipping over Trip's in favor of other restaurants on my to-do list. After binge-watching Comedians in Cars Getting Coffee on Netflix, I was suddenly craving diner food and immediately put Trip's on the top of my priority list. I recently made it in and loved my experience!

First off, I saw a line of people waiting around outside and feared that we would be waiting for quite a while. The guy took my name down and wrote "40" next to it for a wait time, but another person working nearby said that it would more than likely be 25-30 minutes. Not bad, but I was still planning to sit for quite a while before being able to eat.

6 minutes later, they called my name. What a pleasant surprise!

My wife and I had been scoping out the menu online ahead of time and knew exactly what we wanted. I went with a custom omelette with a bunch of stuff added in, cheese grits and an english muffin. She opted for chicken fried steak and mashed potatoes.

Omelette: 4-stars. I think all omelette's are basically 4-stars. I can't think of a time I ever didn't enjoy an omelette, but I can't think of a time where one stood out as being *the best* I've ever had.

Cheese Grits: 5-stars. I read that this was the highlight on the Yelp listing at all 3 locations and I can see why! These grits are so incredibly creamy that I just could not believe it. I wish my portion size would have been doubled because I was absolutely in love with these!

Chicken Fried Steak: 5-stars. My wife orders this every time she sees it on a menu and we agreed that it was among the best we've had in Tampa Bay. I think I could convince her to visit Trip's on a very regular basis just for this dish alone.

Mashed Potatoes: 5-stars. Delicious and perfect with the gravy. An ideal counterpart for the chicken fried steak.

Cost: 5-stars. Even after tip and a couple sodas, our total was $32. That bill was quite the pleasant surprise!

The menu at Trip's is about as large as I have ever seen at any restaurant. If you can't find something that interests you here, I don't think you like eating very much. I hope to come back many times and work my way through that menu!

Why 5 stars? Because the wait(s) were long, but oh-so worth it!

   ---   ---   ---

I've had Konan BBQ on my to-visit list for quite some time. Usually I end up visiting a place pretty quickly when it gives me this level of intrigue, but I kept finding myself letting another week pass without visiting Konan. Recently, I decided to put my foot down and make it happen! I was a little a nervous when their phone number just kept giving me a busy signal, but I made the trek down to Hubert Ave anyway.

If you haven't veered too far off of Lois Ave when heading to/from International Mall, you might be surprised at the neighborhood that lies within. I've definitely been in neighborhoods that were in worse shape, but this one is a little eye-opening, considering you're just about a mile and a half from a Louis Vuitton store. 

The parking lot is not very large, so I actually drove around the block and waited for someone to leave from one of the handful of spots that was available. 

Once inside, the menu was pretty simple - a few meats, a few sides, a couple desserts and a couple drinks. I asked what their specialty was in terms of meats and the guy closed his eyes and started air-pointing, as if to say, "all of the above." I opted for ribs, pulled pork, coleslaw, mac-n-cheese and sweet pineapple tea.

I then headed into the dining room and waited for about 20-25 minutes. I was not alone - there were quite a few people who were also waiting quite a while for their food. As much as I was excited to eat, I was willing to wait because I knew that my food wasn't prepared until I ordered it.

Eventually my order was called and I headed home. About 15 minutes later, I opened my box-o-goodness and I could not have been happier. I'll sum it up with this comment:

This is some of the best BBQ in all of Tampa Bay.

Ribs - Some of the best I've had anywhere. They were that perfect middle ground between fall-off-the-bone and chewy.

Chopped Pork - Very solid and the perfect compliment to the ribs.

Coleslaw - A bit watery, but absolutely delicious!

Mac-n-Cheese - Seriously some of the tastiest and cheesiest mac I have ever had. And I order mac every time it's on a menu.

Sweet Pineapple Tea - VERY sweet, but definitely worth ordering! And this is coming from a person who doesn't like overly-sweet drinks.

My one and only gripe is that I wish I had more sauce - especially with the chopped pork. After getting through the initial top layer, the meat was pretty dry. But if I had dined in, I'm sure I could have gotten some more.

Definitely don't come to Konan if you're in a hurry, but if you're for some great BBQ, you will not be disappointed!

Why 5 stars? Because the Miguel genetics are flawless.

   ---   ---   ---

Miguel's is my 2nd favorite restaurant in the Bay Area, so when I heard that they were opening a sister restaurant with some new menu items, you can imagine how much of a delight this was for me. Maybe I went in with a bias, but I think they backed up my internal hype.

Where Miguel's is more of the dinner/platter type, Miguelitos is the go-to for tacos, burritos, tortas, and bowls. Depending on what you're in the mood for, the Miguel's family provides the undisputed best Mexican food in Tampa Bay - and in my mind, it's not even close.

What TB makes up for with delicious Cuban and Latin American cuisine, it lacks in the Mexican variety. Miguel's family hails from Houston, as do I, where good Mexican food is found within every square mile.

The interior is swanky, to go along with a similar outdoor patio that you find at Miguel's. They did a really phenomenal job with the decor - it feels like a party in there. Much like 98% of restaurants in Florida, you can come here for a date night, or visit in shorts and flip flops.

As is the case with Miguel's, be sure to order some queso with your chips upon arrival - it's also the best in the area.

I enjoyed a torta and some street corn, and next visit, I'm definitely going to knock out a bunch of those tacos. I tried a bite of my fiance's filet mignon taco, and it made my cry tears of joy. Maybe that was the spiciness of the street corn, but I was also really happy.

Miguel, if we ever meet, can I give you a hug?

Why 5 stars? Because looks can be deceiving.

   ---   ---   ---

I'd wanted to make the trip to Stein and Vine long ago, but had never actually seen it while driving down 60. When I arrived, I couldn't believe that THIS was the place I'd read so much about. From the outside, it looks like a old man's dive bar, as it's in a strip mall, positioned next to a Big Lots. Never good. Well... except this time.

Stein & Vine had two great qualities: phenomenal burgers, and a huge beer list. Huge. 

It's hard to really describe the burger, other than when you have that deep hunger craving, and are searching for something to "hit the spot," for me, this is the definition of hitting the spot.

In suburbia where chains rule the roost, Stein and Vine is a great escape. Trust me, it's nothing like it looks like from the outside.

Why 5 stars? Because this might be my new favorite coffee shop in Tampa Bay.

   ---   ---   ---

I was really excited to see the old Chinese restaurant that occupied this space for years, be turned into something useful. But unfortunately, Drama Burger was just kind of... weird. I sadly was not surprised to see its life span be as short as it was. 

That excitement was re-newed when I saw that this building would now house a coffee spot. I was even more pumped when I scoped out pictures of their food options! There are some really great coffee shops in the Tampa Bay area, but we have a shortage of those that deliver 5-star coffee and 5-star food. Caffeine Roasters kills it on both fronts.

First off, the coffee menu is amazing. They equally serve hardcore coffee fanatics, as well as those who enjoy coffee doused in sugary stuff. I could come here the next ten days and order ten different drinks that I'd be in to. For my first experience, I could pass on the iced aero cappucino - three things I love in coffee, all in one! It was as delicious as I could have hoped for. And for those that like your coffee sweet, there seem to be quite a few options for adding syrup that aren't necessarily on the menu. We heard a lot of orders being called out with various flavors added.

And then the food. Oh, the delicious food. I couldn't pass on the avocado aioli ham biscuit, and it was just as amazing as the description alludes to. The person who took our order mentioned that their biscuits are made from scratch in-house, and it shows. They are so soft and really melt as you're chewing. There wasn't a thing I'd change about it. Meanwhile, my wife was equally as pleased with her caprese baguette. Just like the coffee menu, I could visit several days in a row and order something new each time, because there are so many great options. 

After just one visit, this is one of my favorite new business openings of 2017 - I will be back many times!

Why 4 stars? Because I did enjoy it, but still came away disappointed.

   ---   ---   ---

This was a tough one to designate a certain number of stars for. I was extremely excited to try this place, and definitely came away underwhelmed. That being said, I'd still prefer to eat here again, over many of the places that I've reviewed 3-stars, so I went with 4.

But why the disappointment? I went with Notorious P.I.G. which had pulled pork, onions, cheese, etc. My issue is that if I had been blindfolded, I definitely would not have known pulled pork was on this sandwich. I definitely couldn't taste any, and I could barely actually see it.

I personally love Tom + Chee's grilled cheese sandwiches. I know that some people aren't huge fans because they wish it was more like traditional grilled cheese. If you're one of those people, I think you'll love Central Melt. But for me personally, I prefer Tom + Chee's thick Texas toast, melted cheese, and plenty of stuff in the middle. Central Melt is a traditional grilled cheese sandwich that your mom would make for you as a kid, with a pinch of other stuff in between.

I will say, my fiance got the traditional grilled cheese, and I thought it was tastier than mine. I'd also like to come back to try the Roast Beef on Fleek.

Why 5 stars? Because it's the perfect marriage?

   ---   ---   ---

My love for Jet City and my neighborhood, have now combined into one. If I could have chosen any business in all of TB to open a location in Seminole Heights, Jet City would be right at the top of the list. And this version is a full-on cafe! 

I have my own espresso maker, which provides my caffeine boost on most days. But sometimes, I like to change it up, and unfortunately, Starbucks was the only other option in the neighborhood. And Starbucks is far from my favorite. Far.

I always want to try something different, but the Cafe Borgia is so good that I can't stray! It's one of my all-time favorite coffee drinks :)

Jessica, the owner, is probably the nicest human being I've ever met. Even if she's swamped, she will manage to make every person who walks through her doors feel like the only customer in the house. That's a pretty amazing ability, and it's no wonder both locations are rated 5 stars overall.

Why 4 stars?  Because it stands the tests of time.

   ---   ---   ---

I am not the guy who thinks the idea of camping sounds "fun."  I don't think that we would be better off as a society without technology.  I get annoyed when a business only takes cash because it's a cool novelty.

El Cap DOES take credit/debit, but they maintain all of the cool parts of a retro burger bar.  Old school everything is El Cap's game, and this burger is awesome.  It tastes just like 1950 - delicious with a side of Leave it to Beaver.

Appropriately enough, an older co-worker introduced me to the place, because he used to eat there as a kid growing up in St. Pete.  I'm glad I can enjoy the tastes of his childhood, without having a pacemaker (yes, he has a pacemaker, and yes it's funny to watch him get "manually" searched at the airport since he can't walk through the metal detector.)

El Cap continues to be my go-to burger joint in the 727, no matter what year...or decade it is.

Why 4 stars? Because their pizza is definitely the most creative.

   ---   ---   ---

This is definitely a place that could be upgraded to 5-stars after another visit.

I came here for week 2 of the NFL season because it's a Browns Backers bar. Unfortunately, it was incredibly hot outside, and outside is where the Browns gathering was. I was in my very toasty jersey, and didn't want to sit in the heat for 3+ hours, so I headed inside. I missed out on the ability to cheer on the action with my fellow Browns fans, but it was a much more enjoyable experience with AC.

They have some of the craziest pizzas you'll ever see, and definitely won my heart by having Southern Tier Pumpking - one of my favorite pumpkin beers. There are tons of TV's here, so it's definitely one of the best spots near the beach to check out a game. I'll definitely be back!

We tried the french dip pizza, the beach bird pizza, and the wings. All were super!

Why 5 stars? Because finally, we have another great Tex-Mex option in the Bay Area.

   ---   ---   ---

For years, my wife and I have felt that the only place in Tampa Bay that even remotely reminds us of the wonderful Tex-Mex in Houston has been Miguel's. Like both of us, Miguel grew up in Houston and he does a phenomenal job of bringing home that sweet H-town nostalgia in the form of fajitas, quesadillas, queso, etc.

And then Chuy's opened up and now there are two!

Chuy's checks every box of what you want in a Tex-Mex experience.

Queso: While it's a little bit spicier than we'd prefer, they have a freaking help-yourself-nacho-bar, which saves you several dollars from ordering queso from your server. We ended up trying the queso with beef in it, but preferred the plain. Either way, it was delicious.

Fajitas: This is a giant platter of high-grade beef, peppers and onions and it comes out smoking. They then provide you with some buttery soft tortillas, rice, beans, guac, sour cream and all the other veggie accompaniments. The beef has the exact flavor that I hope for every time I even think about a Mexican restaurant.

Price: A++. My wife and I got more food than we could eat and the total came to $34 before tip. Two days earlier we visited a significantly less awesome Tex-Mex spot and paid about $10 more for less food. 

We don't spend a lot of time in the New Tampa/Wesley Chapel area, but this will be our absolute go-to when we are checking out the outlet mall.

Thank you Chuy's for coming to Tampa Bay!

Why 5 stars? Because this is why I love Ybor City.

   ---   ---   ---

When people come to visit, I always send them to Ybor, because Ybor has something for everyone. Fine dining, casual dining, beer bars/breweries, dive bars, cocktail bars, clubs, ghost tours, etc etc. 

And now they have a (re-vamped) arcade!

I remember visiting the old Game Works, years ago, and it was fairly unmemorable. Actually, it was very unmemorable because I don't have a specific memory about it. 

But GameTime? I'll never forget it!

Buy yourself a blue card, which gives you one hour of play on a majority of the games. You'll be worn out by the time you're done, and it's only $15! A couple rounds of Pop-A-Shot are incredibly tiring, but I did my best to play as much of that as I could during my hour. I made it to the final round a couple of times, which was even more exhausting. I can say this with a completely straight face - GameTime can be a good replacement for the gym, when you spend a lot of time playing basketball.

But there are definitely plenty of other games as well: air hockey, duck bowling, Deal or No Deal, beer pong, the thing where you hit something with a giant hammer as hard as you can, the one big punch on a punching bag game, etc. I'm telling you - many of them require a decent amount of physical force/activity! Of course, there are plenty of standard arcade games as well, if you're not looking to break a sweat. 

As I said in the beginning, GameTime is another reason Ybor is so diverse, and a place I'll continue to send people who fly in to visit Tampa Bay!

Why 5 stars?  Because it was one of the best and unique dining experiences that I've ever been a part of.

   ---   ---   ---

Ciro's completely knocked it out of the park!!!  

The service was about 150 stars.

The food was absolutely insane.

The cocktails were perfection.

The atmosphere was like nothing else I've ever experienced. 

Ciro's is on my very short list for the best of the Bay Area and definitely a place I would recommend for tourists and residents alike.  

As for my recommendations, I have to say that the gourmet popcorn is an absolute requirement when visiting Ciro's.  There is nothing like it on the planet.  It will make you think of popcorn differently for the rest of your life. 

We had the chicken & waffles - if you like spicy, this is the order for you.  It is definitely a couple of notches higher on the hot scale than your typical chicken and waffles.  The cheese platter is super as well.

As for cocktails, you will get a 10 minute explanation and run through about what is best for you.  I will let the professionals guide you on this train.

Ciro's = Stupid Awesome.

Why 3 stars? Because I found the food to be original but a tick off.

   ---   ---   ---

After discovering the Restorative via their amazing Yelp reviews and stunning Instagram photos, I was incredibly excited to check them out. It's not often that I find myself in Dunedin during the early evening of weeknight's, but I went out of my way to get here so that I could experience this place first hand.

We arrived around 5:30p on a Thursday and were able to grab a seat at the bar. My friend and I made some pretty quick menu choices and our orders were taken within a couple of minutes. Here's what we had:

Meatballs - This was the first thing we had and it ended up being the best. There was some veal meat mixed in and some sort of bread crumbs on top that really set these apart from most of the meatballs I've ever had. 5-stars.

Ceviche - This was solid, but a bit pricey for the portion size. 4-stars.

Salt Cod with black squid ink spaghetti - Definitely very flavorful and tasty, but just too salty. Obviously the name of the dish is "Salt" cod, and while I love salty things, this was just a bit too much of a good thing. 4-stars.

Poached Chicken - This contained fermented black garlic puree, mushrooms, asparagus and foie gras-truffle jus. To be honest, I like all of those things individually, but I didn't love the flavor that the combination of all of those things produced. My dining partner liked this more than me, so it could have been more of a personal preference. 3-stars.

Double Creme Brie - A pretty big miss. This contained a pasty, some pineapple chunks and a giant slice of brie. It honestly didn't even really taste like a dessert. I definitely wish we would have gone with another option. 2-stars.

Overall, I'd give label our experience 3.5 stars, but I'm rounding down to 3-stars because this was our third trip to the Restorative, but the first time I was actually able to patronize the business.

Trip #1 - I went to the Restorative's website to see if they took reservations. Their website is very basic - it's pretty much just one page with a few facts about the restaurant. One of the things noted is that they do not have a phone, but answer emails quickly. I shot them an email that I was driving from Tampa, so I'd love to know what time they recommend I arrive by in order to secure a seat. They are only open 4-9p with 18 seats, so I knew it might be tough to just show up at any time and expect a seat. One of the owners did end up responding right away and said that there's no way to guarantee anything, but they recommend I arrive between 4-6p. Sadly, I ended up not being able to leave my house until after 6, and even more sadly, they'd run out of food by when we got there at 7:30. We were bummed, but completely understood that this was a risk we took. 

Trip #2 - The previous visit was on a Friday, so on Monday (they next day they were open) we made sure that we were going to get there much earlier. We ended up leaving the house around 4:30p, which allowed us to arrive at 5:20p. The tough thing about leaving at that time is that it was during awful rush hour traffic, but we were happy to finally eat here after all the build-up. I walked up to hold the door open for my wife, who had our 3 month old in the stroller, only to be told by the owner that they don't allow kids under 5. I told him that we just got turned away on Friday and that we drove from Tampa just to come here twice, but his mind was made up. He said that their rules are written on their website.

We got back in the car and were really upset. I thought it was really crappy of the owner to turn us away when we'd driven that far to check them out twice, but I also understood that if they posted the rules on their website, it was really my fault for not looking. Once we were about halfway home, I pulled up their website on my phone, which only made me more upset.

The website said, "Well-behaved children five years and up are welcome to order off our dinner menu."

First of all, that verbiage does not say, "kids under five are not welcome." And secondly, when I saw this text, it triggered my memory. I, in fact, had already read this information a few days earlier when I went to their website to contact them. If they clearly stated that they did not allow babies, I never would have wasted nearly 3 hours commuting back and forth to their restaurant. I emailed the owner about this, and he said, "sorry for the confusion," which of course, annoyed me even more. Because in this situation, they used poor verbiage to get their point across and it cost us a lot of wasted time. I checked the website again a few days later and it was changed to, "Well behaved children over the age of 5 are welcome join us for dinner."

The fact that I made this commute a third time after this says that I really, *really* wanted to experience and enjoy the Restorative. Unfortunately, I didn't end up loving the food, but I am still glad I was able to check them out.

Why 5 stars? Because this is the best brewery I've ever been to.

   ---   ---   ---

One year ago, I would have never found myself in a Seminole industrial park at a place with 20 beer taps and no food. But thanks to my girlfriend introducing me outside the world of Bud/Miller/Coors, I've now become a full-fledged beer snob.

We've spent the past year trying every different kind of beer under the sun, and specifically on a trip to the great northwest this summer, we found ourselves going to brewery after brewery in the mecca of American beer -Portland.

But Rapp far surpassed all of the Portland breweries... and any that I've been to... ever. The selection is phenomenal, and Greg Rapp really makes magic with what's on the other side of those taps.

Before the end of the night, I sampled about 10 beers, and I really loved almost all of them. I found the Maple Wheat to be the standout for me, although the Pumpkin was a very close 2nd favorite.

Can't wait to go back, and can't wait to see the fellow beer fans of Tampa Bay check it out for themselves!

Why 3 stars? Because the pizza was ok.

   ---   ---   ---

I've been living a pretty healthy lifestyle recently, which has led to the scale getting about as low as I ever see it. When this happens, like clockwork, I start craving certain foods with an intensity that is borderline torturous. One of those cravings recently has been pizza. So when the wife and I were heading out to Dunedin to hang with a friend, I decided that we needed to make a quick stop at Safety Harbor along the way.

We started off with some garlic knots, which were alright. The marinara has a very strong flavor that I can't quite put my finger on, but I did not love it. The knots themselves were pretty average.

Two of the slices of the day were the Surf and Turf and the Just Peachy. The Surf and Turf was my favorite part of the meal - I would definitely order that again. The Just Peachy was unique and enjoyable, but for my extra-crazy cravings for pizza, I would have just ordered something more traditional if I could go back and do it again.

My wife ordered a small Margherita pie, and it was pretty uninspiring. 

We finished off with Gigi's Monster Cookie. My wife said that it reminded her of a Cliff Bar, and once she said that, it's all I could think of. Don't get me wrong, I enjoy Cliff Bars, but not necessarily when I'm ordering dessert at lunch.

Overall, I'm sad I didn't love this place more. The people working here were quite friendly and I love all of the local businesses of Safety Harbor, but it just didn't click for us. I think the biggest disconnect was the very chewy, flavor-less crust. If they could make a couple of adjustments there, I think they'd be onto something. The uniqueness of the daily slices is pretty rad!

Why 5 stars? Because I didn't want the vermicelli to end.

   ---   ---   ---

After recently moving to the neighborhood, I've been spending a lot of time with my contractor in the new house. And said contractor will not shut up about how amazing Simply Pho is. I got so sick of him telling me that I had to check it out, that I just gave in and went for lunch today.

He was right! I was full long before finishing my meal, but I just wanted to keep shoveling it down my gullet like the glutton that I am. I have nothing to compare it to, because I believe it was my first time eating vermicelli, but it was amazing. It's basically a bed rice, noodles, and some veggies, smothered in a combination of meats: shrimp, pork, sausage and shrimp wraps. Of course, that's the vermicelli combination... if you aren't a fan of any of those, you can opt for just one in particular.

I wanted to try the pho here, but I decided against it. First of all, it may be October 1st, but it's still thoroughly summer out there. And secondly, I've never been a huge fan of pho when I've tried it in the past. Maybe I'm just not much of a soup person.

But I learned today, I am definitely a vermicelli person.

Why 4 stars? Because my acai bowl was solid, but not my absolute favorite.

   ---   ---   ---

My fiance and I are obsessed with acai bowls, and trying all of the different places around Tampa Bay that offer them. When we saw "Acai Bowls" on the sign at the Enerjuicer, we knew we'd be stopping in soon. A few days later, there we were.

She ordered a small cocoa bowl. I ordered a large rainbow bowl with peanut butter. Unfortunately, we got two bowls of the same size (not sure if it was 2 smalls, or 2 larges) and mine didn't have peanut butter. Also unfortunately, by the time I realized I was peanut butter-less, there was a line of a few people waiting to order, and I knew it wouldn't be worth the trouble to wait around to inquire about PB. Mistakes happen though, so no biggie! 

I ended up liking her bowl more than mine, though, I very much enjoyed mine as well. I just really wish I could have had peanut butter :) 

I also picked up a couple Mother Kombucha's, and enjoyed browsing through all of the healthy snacks that they had near the front counter. I would definitely love to come back and try almost everything that Enerjuicer carries, between the smoothies, acai bowls, and various snacks. 

4 stars instead of 5 just because the acai tasted a bit more frozen than fresh, and my favorite acai bowl to-date comes from Fit2Run in International Mall. After trying a couple of bowls at Enerjuicer, that's still true, but I will definitely be back to try more!

Why 5 stars? Because I learned about the Benedictwich.

   ---   ---   ---

I've been to a couple different Ciccio's over the years, and to be totally honest, they always struck me as solid, but unremarkable. But after trying the Benedictwich, I've been converted to a believer!
