I'm pretty much a complete sucker for eggs benedict, and I love sandwiches more than the average bear. Combine the two? You've got my attention. And the benedictwich was everything I'd hoped for, and more.

Not only that, but I definitely felt the urge to come back a couple of times, while reading the brunch menu for this location - specifically the "From the Grille" section. 

Oatmeal Chocolate Chip and Strawberry Pancakes? 

Natural Chicken & Egg Club Sandwich? 

Big Chorizo Egg Wrap? 

Lanza Burrito? 

These are all things that make me excited about life.

Why 4 stars? Because I do love a good Chicago dog.

   ---   ---   ---

I don't really eat spicy things and I hate mustard, but for whatever reason, I do love Chicago dogs. You'd think I would have never given them the time of day, but instead, I just trade out the mustard for ketchup and mostly eat around the hot peppers. I did the same at Portillo's, and was very satisfied with their version of a Chicago dog, despite the fact that as a Cleveland Indians fan, I'm not super happy with Chicago things right now.

Aside from the dog, Portillo's itself is quite the unique experience. The walls are as thoroughly decorated as any business you'll ever patronize. I'm impressed that they are able to replicate this look at so many different locations across the country - it can't be cheap.

The ordering process is a bit dis-jointed. It's not obvious what line to stand in for ordering and where to go for your food. Every few seconds, someone is yelling out order numbers on mic: 

"#28 it's time to eat something great!" 

"#35 you are live!"

"#49 it's your time!"

You pick up certain food items from one counter and other items from another. If you order dessert, you go to another counter altogether. I'm sure they have their reasons for wanting to do it this way, and I suppose it IS unique, but I'm not sure I loved it. Especially when crowded, I could see it actually being a bit annoying with lines backing up into other lines.

But one thing's for sure - they make you feel like you're in the mix of a big city hustle and bustle when you're inside. If you're into that sorta thing, you'll love it.

As for the other food, we found it to be a bit unexciting. The italian beef is very bland - it's basically meat and bread with nothing else involved (or at least it tastes that way.) I thought the chopped salad was solid, but the wife didn't enjoy it. We were tempted to grab dessert but it appeared to be previously frozen pies sitting in a cooler all day, so we passed on that.

For what is probably technically considered fast food, it's not bad. But I probably won't be rushing back either unless I'm craving a Chicago dog.

Why 5 stars? Because the food was great, but the people were better.

   ---   ---   ---

My bulgogi was solid, and all of the sides were very good, but the people at Arirang were second to none.

I asked the woman I assume to be the owner what in the world I do with the lettuce that was brought out to me. I couldn't figure out how to incorporate that into my meal, so how did she show me? By making me a little bulgogi lettuce wrap and literally feeding it into my mouth. That alone was probably worth the 5-stars.

My girlfriend had a fried rice dish that I couldn't stop eating. Could. Not. Stop. Eating.

I can't wait to return on a weekday, or weekend for dinner when they serve Korean BBQ! That's my absolute favorite, and I have a feeling Arirang will end up being my new go-to!

Why 5 stars? Because a Mexican Fresh Kitchen is like if you combined cake and ice cream but it was healthy.

   ---   ---   ---

I've always been an enormous fan of Fresh Kitchen and have said that if they open one in our neighborhood, I will be there an embarrassingly high number of times. 

My wife and I consider Mexican food to be our favorite cuisine. If we could eat it every weekend, we would. No joke, if it wasn't for the calories, we'd probably eat it 3x a week.

So with those two things in mind, the Gods have heard our prayers and answered them with Taco Dirty. Mexican food from the people who brought us Fresh Kitchen, that can actually be decently healthy.

As I was walking out, I spoke with someone that I assumed was one of the owners and I told him that if they open in Carrollwood, I will be their best customer. That was not a lie, Mr. Owner. Sign me up for rent in the back room because I will live there. Also, apologies for hitting you up to open a 2nd Taco Dirty when you literally just opened this one a couple of days earlier. You should probably enjoy the fruits of your labor for a few minutes before you're onto your next project.

But as mentioned above, this truly is the Mexican Fresh Kitchen. Most of the options are bowls, which are highly customizable with different bases, meats, veggies and sauces. As is the case with Fresh Kitchen, everything just tastes better than you'd expect it to. I don't know how they cook their meat, but I do know that it's the best way imaginable. 

I'd like to come back and try the non-bowl items like the torta, but it will be like torture not to order another All-In bowl because it was so perfect on my first visit that I'll be dreaming about it for weeks. They have guacamole sauce, you guys.

Taco Dirty, you guys really do make dreams come true.

Why 3 stars? Because I wanted to love it so bad, but it just missed the mark.

   ---   ---   ---

My lovely wife woke up one recent Saturday morning with a craving to go out for breakfast. We rarely go out for breakfast, but I couldn't have been more proud to see her spending so much time researching our destination on Yelp, that I couldn't help but immediately agree. After much deliberation, she chose The Grind.

We walked in and noticed a very unique set-up. It looked and felt like a regular ol' coffee shop, but you could actually order some pretty legitimate breakfast entrees. There was so much more to choose from than the standard pastries and croissants that you'd normally see at a place like this.

They had eggs benedict on the menu, which pretty much will always end my search on any breakfast menu. I've never had an eggs benedict I didn't like.

WELP.... until now.

I have to be totally honest - if I were rating the taste of my eggs benedict alone, I'd really debate between 1 and 2 stars. The flavor of the hollandaise sauce was just not pleasant, and very unlike anything I've had before. If I took over ownership of this business, the first thing I would do is replace the hollandaise sauce, before I even learned all of the employee's names. It was that odd.

The wife ordered the grit breakfast bowl, and I didn't really enjoy hers either. She liked it, but I thought it also had a strange taste.

So why even give 3 stars? I legitimately would like to visit again. I would obviously order something very different, but I do really love the concept of a coffee bar with legitimate breakfast options. I also enjoyed my coffee and thought that the drink menu had a ton of great options. The service was very friendly, as well.

I'll be back at some point, and hope my second visit is an upgraded experience.

Why 5 stars? Because this is one of the best burger spots in Tampa Bay. 

   ---   ---   ---

I can't believe how long it had been since my last visit to Engine No. 9 and also can't believe that my original review was penned more than 5 years ago. 

I've been here several times since that original review was written and have tried multiple burgers - they always tend to range from good to great. When I recently stopped in, I ordered a medium rare Demi God and it was one of the better burgers I've had in Tampa Bay. I don't think I'd ever tried it before, but it always caught my eye on the menu because I love anything with horse radish. It did not disappoint.

Virtually the entire menu is just a bunch of different burger options, so if you like meat betwixt buns, it's impossible to not find something you'll enjoy here. Anytime I'm hungry in St. Pete, this is one of the first places I think of!

Why 5 stars? Because these popsicles are serious.

   ---   ---   ---

I have a serious popsicle problem. I once at a 100-pack of Pop-Ice's in less than two days. When I buy a 12-pack of those Philly Swirls from Publix... it is absolutely a "one-sitting" occasion. I think popsicles are God's way of saying that he loves us.

Whatever Pops delivers a high-quality product. If Philly Swirls are Mich Ultra, these are a Belgium dubbel. You couldn't eat twelve in one sitting, because they're just too rich for that kind of keg-standing.

Whenever I see Whatever Pops out at a food truck rally, it's required shopping. I highly recommend you do the same.

Why 4 stars? Because it was elevated above the norm.

   ---   ---   ---

I don't know how many years I've had Chef Li bookmarked. I feel like someone initially told me about them in like 2013ish? Either way, after Christina G's blessing came in, it was reiterated to me that it was finally time to make the trip to Oldsmar.

My wife and I struggled to decide what to order because if you're going to drive nearly 30 minutes one way for carry-out, you better make sure you fully scratch that itch. We opted to order small portions of a bunch of things that we could try as many items as possible.

Teriyaki Chicken: 5-stars. I could eat this all day, every day. The wife thought it was just okay, but anything covered in that sauce would hit the spot 10 times out of 10 for me.

Sweet and Sour Pork: 3-stars. This kind of missed the mark. It reminded me more of the cheaper Chinese takeout that I've experienced over the years and not comparable to a place like Yummy House.

Pork Fried Rice: 4-stars. It was fine. It didn't stand out, but fried rice is not usually very unique from place to place. But it's always tasty.

Teriayki Beef Sticks: 4-stars. Very solid, I would definitely order these again. I'd also recommend just sliding them off of the stick because it's easier to eat that way, rather than trying to chew around it.

Shrimp Lo Mein: 5-stars. I love lo mein and they hit this out of the park. Everything I'd hoped it would be.

Chinese Donuts: 3-stars. Upgraded to 4-stars once I microwaved them. Reminded me of cheap fair food.

This is definitely a very good option for those that live in the area. It feels like it takes about 10 minutes to scroll through their entire menu on your phone - if you can think of it, they can probably make it!

Why 5 stars? Because they're worthy of the 5-star overall rating!

   ---   ---   ---

My biggest rule on Yelp - when a place has a 5-star rating and more than 50 reviews, I make it a high priority to visit. In this case, it's even better than a 5-star rating - they're listed as the #25 rated restaurant on Yelp in the entire country for 2017! 

I had to go with the Cuban sandwich, because obviously. I'd put it neck and neck with Bodega for the best Cuban I've had in Tampa Bay. One of the most telling things for me is that I'm not a fan of mustard, but accidentally forgot to tell the server to hold the mustard on my Cuban. But despite the mustard, which I really don't like, I couldn't escape the wonderful flavors of this sandwich. A real phenomenal job by Barracuda.

The place is small and unassuming - really the typical establishment that you'd never think twice about if it weren't for Yelp. But my favorite part is that it's a 5-star restaurant near the beach, which is incredibly rare in the Tampa Bay area. While most eateries near the beach are the definition of tourist traps, Barracuda is really bringing the extra TLC, and it's obvious.

If I were closer, I'd visit often. But instead, I'll recommend anyone in St. Pete Beach to put this #1 on their hit list.

Why 4 stars? Because my first experience with Russian food was a good one.

   ---   ---   ---

I am always up for a foodie adventure where I'm trying something new. I was hoping Nick S would join me, but he's not legally allowed to be away from his dog for more than 45 minutes, so he had to decline and I went on a solo mission.

I really did not know what to order, as I had no frame of reference for what I would like. I came to the conclusion that I wanted to try a Blinchiki due to some amazing looking photos I saw. I was also intrigued by the okroshka, which is like a cold vegetable/potato soup. Lastly. I actually *had* tried a Pirozhki before, so I finished with one with peach filling to end on a sweeter note.

The okroshka came out first, and as people warned, it's a bit of an acquired taste. It definitely was not bad, but I don't know that I'd order it again. It had a unique flavoring that I couldn't really describe if I tried.

Then came the blinchiki, which was the star of the show. It was kind of just like a super buttery burrito with a little beef inside. It came with a dollop of sour cream and was delicious with or without that. I will definitely seek these out if I ever see them on a menu in the future!

The peach pirozhski was okay - probably bland more than anything else. I'd forgotten that I had a piroshki (spelled a bit differently) in Seattle a few years back and remember it tasting similar to a kolache. I think that was the goal here too, but it ended up being almost flavor-less.

I'd love to come back again and check out some of the other breakfast/pancake type items.

Why 5 stars? Because I want Moonlight Boba in my life often.

   ---   ---   ---

I recently sent my wife the Moonlight Boba Yelp listing because her office is not too terribly far away and she loves boba. The reviews are pretty amazing, but I'm not in Pinellas Park very often, so I figured she'd be able to enjoy it before I would. Fortunately, we actually happened to be in the area, so we stopped by and I'm completely in love after one visit. 

At first, my wife just had me run inside and order a taro boba for her. I planned on grabbing a couple drinks to go and heading home, but I saw the waffle ice cream concoctions on the menu and thought that it would be much better to eat-in. Every waffle looked amazing, but the 
"Rainbow In My Hand" with cotton candy ice cream, gummies and mochi's really caught my eye.

The saying "explosion of flavor" is cliche, but I don't know any other more accurate way to describe this. You got creamy, sour, sweet, mushy, hard and dense in every bite. It's quite a lot for your taste buds to process, but I liked it. With that being said, I'd opt for something like the Cookielicious or the Snow White next time, just for a bit more continuity.

Also, my coconut boba smoothie and her taro milk tea were both top notch.

But then as we were leaving, my wife pointed out a sign off to the side that showed ice cream boba's. And I have to tell you, outside of a sign that said, "Brett, you've won a new car," I don't know if I could have been happier to see that particular set of information.

I'd recently been introduced to ice cream boba's in San Francisco and fell head over heels in love. I was told that they only recently made their way to the United States and were super hard to find. I knew that probably meant I wouldn't find them in Tampa Bay until about 2024, when they'd be old news in SF. So to find them about 3 weeks later in Pinellas Park, I was ecstatic. 

I'd already had a small dessert before arriving at Moonlight Boba + ordered a boba smoothie and an ice cream waffle here. I wanted to fully enjoy this ice cream boba, so we hopped in the car, drove about 40 minutes home to Tampa, froze them and ate them the next day. They were still just as unbelievable as I remembered, despite nearly melting away in the car the day before. Do yourself the greatest favor and go to Moonlight Boba for many things, but especially for the ice cream boba's before they sell out!

As I said, we aren't in Pinellas Park often, but if timing/circumstances work out, I know exactly where I'm coming for my sweet fix.

Why 3 stars? Because this is an epic case for a half-star.

   ---   ---   ---

I get why Yelp doesn't have half-stars. Keeping it simple... um... keeps it simple! But Drama Burger is the perfect example of a 3.5 star experience for me.

My first visit, I tried the Berlin Burger. It's a monthly special, and the photos just looked to good to pass up. The result? One of the most photogenic, gigantic burgers that I've ever seen. But the problem was that it was just too much. It was basically impossible to eat because it was about 3x the size of mouth. (Giggity)

In addition to the physical impossibility to eat this thing, I never thought I'd say this, but there is such a thing as "too much." When you take like 15 ingredients and pile them betwixt two buns, it just becomes a hodge podge of a mess. Even if all of those ingredients are awesome things like bacon and several different kinds of cheeses, they get lost when paired with too many other things. It's like a suicide at the soda machine. Coke, Dr. Pepper, Sprite, and Red Fanta are awesome... but when mixed together? Meh.

I also when with the thin cut fries, and while I like thin fries, these were so thin that you couldn't even really pick them up and dip them in ketchup. Between the burger and the fries, I needed to take a shower after attempting to eat this meal. I did see a photo from Bo W that the skinny cut fries are no-longer microscopically skinny, which is good to know.

But I didn't feel that my visit as sufficient enough to write a review. I did order a special, after all. So I made it back and ordered the double BBQ burger, with the thick cut fries. This was a massive improvement. The burger was delicious, and the fries were a tad on the thick side, but still delicious. The dipping sauces are wonderful - I love the truffle ketchup and chipotle mayo.

My fiance had Adam's Cheeseburger. I felt like it had a very strange taste to it. I'm not sure if it was the sauce or the cheese, but I definitely cut the chord at one bite.

I'm very excited that Drama Burger renovated such a previously-dumpy Chinese restaurant. They did a great job with the decor of the place. And I hope my review doesn't dissuade people from visiting. I definitely did not hate Drama Burger, but I do think there are better burger options out there. Especially for the price. The deciding factor for me was the price tag. Our most recent visit was $47 after tip for 2 burgers, 2 fries, 1 soda, and 1 water. Our first trip led to an even higher bill than that.

Why 4 stars? Because it's a great option if you're craving German food.

   ---   ---   ---

I've noticed the amazing reviews for German Bistro for years now, but I just don't find myself in Largo all that often. But I've been on a mission to  check off all of the restaurants that I've always wanted to visit in Tampa Bay, so I met my wife after work here on a Friday night.

We started off with complimentary bread, garlic butter and coleslaw. The coleslaw tasted like it had some horse radish in it, which I love, and the garlic butter was an excellent accompaniment to the bread.

The Veal Schnitzel was the #1 highlight on Yelp, so I was excited to try that, but it turned out to only be a special and not a part of their regular menu. In its place, I ordered the regular weiner schnitzel, while my wife went with the jager schnitzel.

I really enjoyed mine - if you're not familar with schnitzel, it's essentially a German pork chop. It's a pretty "basic" entree, but mine was delicious. My wife's had a gravy/some sort of jager sauce on it, which was pretty strong and neither of us were huge fans.

For my sides, I ordered spaetzle and potato salad. The spaetzle was pretty plain pasta, but I dug the potato salad. 

And for dessert, we ordered the apple strudel, but to be honest, this was a miss for us. I would not order it again.

Our service was great and the food was pretty good, so I wouldn't mind returning here again when I'm in the area or craving a good schnitzel!

Why 5 stars? Because I'm so glad there's a place for dessert at Hall on Franklin!

   ---   ---   ---

While we were waiting for a table, we decided to use our time to stroll by each vendor and scope out the menus. I had a couple educated guesses on what my wife would order, but as she often does, she surprised me and declared that the ham and cheese croissant from Bake'n Babes was going to be her choice. We visited Europe earlier this year, and that was one of our go-to's for many-a-breakfast. As soon as it was served to us, she said, "this literally smells like our European vacation." I smelled it, and she was right. And the taste totally hit the spot for both of us!

After ordering a few hearty things from various vendors, I started scoping out spots on Yelp nearby where we could find some dessert, without even thinking about Bake'n Babes for some reason! Then I saw those beautiful Liege Waffles being served, and I figured the answer was right under my nose. At the recommendation of our server, we went with Bourbon Blueberry Coulis as a topping, along with vanilla ice cream. Our server was a smart man, because that was the absolute perfect compliment to the waffle itself! And by the way, we ordered a Liege Waffle in Brussels, and this one was better than that!

I can't recommend Bake'n Babes enough as a grand finale to your Hall on Franklin experience.

Why 5 stars? Because it was worth every bit of anticipation.

   ---   ---   ---

I have an on-going, ever-evolving list of restaurants on my to-do list - Wildflower has been near the top of mine for a while. The two things holding me back were proximity to my house, and the fact that I'm not a huge breakfast person. But I was determined, and it finally happened.

The result? It was worth every mile. 

Let's start with the headline: Wildflower Cafe is home to the best waffle I have ever had. Do not come here without getting some form of waffle. The whipped cream, powdered sugar, and melt-in-your-mouth waffle is a combination that makes life worth living. I hate using cliches like "melt in your mouth," but there's not a non-cliche way to accurately describe this euphoric experience. 

Along with the taste of this heavenly waffle, I love the ability to order a smaller waffle, in conjunction with some hearty nutrition, via the Wildflower Triple. When I visit breakfast restaurants, I often times *WANT* to order the panckes/french toast/waffles with like 5,800 calories of sugar goodness piled on top. But I also know that I'll be useless for the rest of the day after eating something like that, especially as my first meal of the day. I always yearn for a mini portion of such things, and at Wildflower, you can get just that! The Triple comes with eggs and bacon to help prevent diabetic-like symptoms of too much sugar, too early!

Other things I loved:

-The biscuits with honey butter are as amazing as one would hope. Just a warning, they crumble easily, so they're a bit of a mess to eat, and not meant for an amateur butter-spreader!

-The peach tea. It's very sweet, so if you're into that sorta thing, don't hesitate to order one of these.

-The grits were some of the best I've ever had. 

-The ham and cheese melt was very good. If I HAD to pick something I enjoyed the least, this would have to be it, by default. But let me clarify, it was like a 4.8, while everything else was a 5.0. And the waffles were an 11 on a 1-5 scale.

Why 4 stars? Because I liked it better than most.

   ---   ---   ---

The good:

-They carry several local beer taps.
-They have two of those 1,000 flavor soda machines.
-The burger (custom-build) was tastier, IMO, than that of its competitors.
-You put your buzzer on the black pad of the table, which transmits the data to the person bringing you your food. This makes it easy for them to find you, and is actually a really good idea!
-The fries were delightful. Five Guys esque, minus the grease.

The not so good:

-I'm not a huge fan of having to valet to eat a burger.
-It's a pet peeve of mine to ask for a side of BBQ sauce, and then be handed one of those little mini-cups that's 25% full. Then to ask for another one, and be handed the same thing. 

I would definitely come back (to try a concrete), and think that they did a phenomenal job with the space. The last time I drove past this, everything was under construction. It really boosted up an area that was already very nice.

Why 4 stars? Because the sides were better than the meat, overall.

   ---   ---   ---

I've had MNM on my radar for a while now, but I just don't get to St. Pete as much as I used to. But now, having a one-year old, it's actually kind of nice to have something to do like drive to St. Pete for a meal because it's something to shake up the normal routine. And if I've learned anything about one-year old's, they do not like the same old, same old.

MNM has the vibes of an old school bar that hasn't been renovated in decades. It's dark and smells of cheap beer. It was kind of charming in a way, because it's been so long since we've been to a place like that.

My wife and I both ordered a two-meat + two-sides plate so that we could share a bunch of things. I'll rate each of those:

Brisket: 3.5 stars. 

Ribs: 1.5 stars. Tendons all throughout every bite made them almost impossible to eat.

Pulled Pork: 3.5 stars.

Pulled Chicken: 5-stars. Easily the best meat we ordered, and normally I'm not really a fan of ordering chicken at a BBQ restaurant.

Baked Beans: 4.5-stars. Definitely not just your standard baked beans. 

Potato Salad: 4-stars. Ditto to above.

Twice Baked Potato: 5-stars. Possibly the most delicious overall item. My wife certainly thought so.

Bacon Mac-n-Cheese: 5-stars. Also, a must-have.

And we really liked the option of choosing garlic pita for our bread. That was definitely a unique touch.

Overall, we enjoyed our experience. I'm glad to see the culinary scene of St. Pete expand a bit north of downtown.

Why 5 stars? Because good Mexican food is a rare find around here.

   ---   ---   ---

My fiance and I both hail from Houston where 14 great Mexican restaurants can be found in any given square mile radius of the city limits. In Tampa Bay, this is sadly not the case. Instead, we're blessed with tons of Cuban, Latin, and South American fare that Houston does not possess. So you take the good with the bad, but when you find a place like Besito, hope is restored.

Besito is far from your traditional Mexican restaurant. The menu consists of a large amount of dishes that I've never seen before. But different vs. familiar isn't important... the bottom line = deliciousness wins!

After visiting Besito for a Yelp event during my first trip, I knew I had to return and get a full experience. The guacamole is possibly the best I've ever had. And the queso fundido is one of the most addicting substances you can put on a plate. 

But the main dish was incredibly impressive to me - the Costillas al Piquin. I almost never enjoy short rib because it tastes a bit more like stew, than good ole' fashioned ribs. But these were easily the best short ribs I've ever had. I had almost sworn them off forever, until Besito saved the day :)

UPDATE

I made a crucial error from my original review and mixed up the burnt ends and the brisket. The burnt ends are my new absolute favorite thing at 4Rivers, and one of my favorite things to eat in all of Tampa Bay! The burnt ends at 4Rivers are a mix of the shavings from brisket and pork, as I was explained.

I am still going to try to complete my mission of eating every single item on the menu, but today after my third visit, I managed to at least finish ordering all of the regular meats and sides. The stackers and sandwiches are next on the to-do list :)  But in the meantime, here are my ratings and notes on each:

==========

MEAT

Burnt Ends - 5 - One of the best things I have ever consumed. Perfect flavor and texture.

Sliced Pork - 5 - Like a less-fatty bacon. I would have never tried this is if it weren't for my quest to order everything.

St. Louis Ribs - 4.5 - Not too mushy, not to hard to pull off the bone. Just right, said the wolf!

Pulled Pork - 4.5 - My go-to order at BBQ restaurants, and 4Rivers doesn't let me down.

Texas Sausage - 4.5 - Another item I wouldn't have normally ordered, but this sausage is juicy and not overwhelming with spices, as most sausage tends to be, IMO.

Smoked Chicken - 4.5 - I don't know what they flavor this with, but as soon as you bite into it, it's true love.

Brontosaurus Beef Rib - 4 - It literally looks like it came from a dinosaur. Its texture is definitely of the "melt-in-your-mouth" variety, but IMO, a little bit too melty.

Smokehouse Prime Rib - 4 - I enjoy this, but it's on the higher end cost-wise, and I think they are better options.

Smokehouse Turkey - 4 - Some of the best turkey I have ever had. It's juicy, and not tried out like turkey typically is. The only reason my rating isn't higher, is just that I'm not a turkey fan.

Pulled Chicken - 3.5 - The only meat from 4Rivers that I'm not in love with. If you're looking for pulled meat, go with the pork. If you're looking for chicken, go with the smoked!

==========

SIDES

Bread Pudding - 5 - This should definitely be served at The Sweet Shop, as it's definitely more of a dessert than a side. But that does not take away from its perfection. Every bite is just stupid good. But you better like banana and sugar if you order it!

Smokehouse Corn - 5 - Some of the best corn I've ever had. Mixed together with about a hundred things, and they're all delicious.

Cornbread Salad - 5 - Basically the same as above, but with lettuce.

Fried Okra - 4.5 - I have only recently discovered that I enjoy me some good fried okra, and the 4Rivers concoction is a pleaser of my taste buds.

Biscuit - 4.5 - I don't know what kind of bread it is, because I'm dumb, but I know that it's the perfect compliment for BBQ!

Mac-n-Cheese - 4 - I think this is a bit of an underachievement here. It's still tasty, but it's very, very basic. If I could change one thing about 4R, this would probably be it. Fancier Mac! Bread crumbs! More cheeses and alike!

Fried Pickles - 4 - Big and not overwhelmingly bread-y.

Sweet Potato Casserole - 4 - Solid, but if you're looking for a sweet side, bread pudding is the only way to go.

Smoked Jalapenos - 4 - You only get two when ordering as a side with dinner, but they are definitely very tasty, as they're wrapped in cream cheese and bacon! I don't like spicy things, but I didn't even get a hint of spice in mine.

Texas Cornbread - 3.5 - I kind of range from solid to unspectacular on this, and the next few items. None of them are bad, but I wouldn't call them memorable either.

Coleslaw - 3.5 - See cornbread.

Potato Salad - 3.5 - See cornbread.

4R BBQ Beans - 3.5 - See cornbread.

Baked Cheese Grits - 3.5 - See cornbread.

Green Beans - 2.5 - I feel that green beans are tough to prepare to my liking, and it usually involves a lot of non-healthy additives. These are pretty basic, and I don't love them.

Collards - 2 - In defense of collards, I'm not a huge fan in general. Maybe these would be appreciated more by a lover of collards.

French Fries - 1 - Definitely the least appealing item at 4Rivers that I've tried to-date. They appeared to be grocery store bought, baked in an oven, and served cold to me. 

==========

DESSERTS

Oreo Cupcake - 5 - By far my favorite cupcake I've ever had at any 4Rivers location. There are actual pieces of oreos baked in to the cake.

Bayou - 5 - Some sort of pecan, buttery concoction. I have no idea what it is or how they make it, but it's insanely tasty. It's also as sweet as possible, so if you don't have the tooth for that, avoid it!

Red Velvet Cupcake - 4 - Solid but it's no oreo!

==========

Next up: Signature Stackers

Why 3 stars? Because I think my first visit was the exception.

   ---   ---   ---

I hate to do this, because I love their "Mission," no pun intended. But that mission is probably the only thing keeping this rating at 3 stars instead of 2. The food has really gone downhill since my first experience.

The brisket has definitely taken a turn for the worse, and I have no idea what happened to the coleslaw. It went from great to tasting like wet lettuce. The pulled pork is average. The ribs were about worth about 2 stars.

The one thing I will give them superb credit for is the mac-n-cheese. It's some of the best in Tampa Bay. But everything else has been average or worse in my last two visits.

I'm rootin' for ya Mission, but I hope the quality of these things improves!

Why 5 stars? Because lunch is just as awesome as dinner.

   ---   ---   ---

I have been to Ulele three times now - once for dinner and twice for lunch. All 3 times were really great experiences, but I think I liked lunch even better just because of the surrounding views in the daylight.

I will say this - there is no better place in Tampa to have to wait for a table than Ulele. You just take a stroll down to Waterworks Park and sit on a bench overlooking the Hillsborough River. Ulele texts you when your table is ready, which is so much more convenient than having to worry about a buzzer that might not be in range 100 yards or so away at the park.

I also happened to visit Ulele twice for lunch during a streak of about 3 consecutive weeks of perfect weather. Sunshine with temperatures in the 70's and a nice breeze. Ahhhhh... I love living here. 

But there's just no nicer place to sit either outside, or inside with the "barn doors" open than Ulele. I am in love with the look of the place, and everything that they did on the grounds and with the park. It's just perfection.

But in terms of the food - I ordered the lobster roll and the Ulele burger. Both are really great choices, and I would recommend letting your hunger level dictate your choice between the two. The lobster roll is not a ton of food, so don't order that if you're starving. The burger is absolutely delicious, as are the fries. 

As much as the burger is more filling than the lobster roll, it's not the kind of burger and fries that make you want to roll over into a coma afterward. I'm no food scientist, so I don't know exactly what it is in a burger and fries that make you feel like your energy is zapped afterward, but all I can tell you is that it didn't happen here. 

So to summarize - Everything looks great. Everything tastes great. And afterward, you feel great.

Ulele = *insert thumbs up emoji here*

Why 4 stars? Because this is now my favorite pizza spot in Seminole Heights.

   ---   ---   ---

So let's review the pizza situation in my neighborhood.

Currently open:

-Cappy's
-Hampton Station
-Heights Pizza

Now closed:

Stephanno's

   ---   ---   ---

I'll be honest... I don't really enjoy Cappy's at all. It's the coolest looking place, but I have just never enjoyed the pizza. And the cash only aspect is just silly at this point.

Hampton Station is a solid addition, and super close to my house, but I don't *love* the pizza here. 

I really did like Stephanno's, but I learned that they recently closed.

So that leaves the newest member of the club, Heights Pizza. This was definitely my favorite of the group. We ordered a half supreme and half pepperoni and it was really solid. I was interested in some of the more unique pies like the Colombian, but the girlfriend is less adventurous :)

The delivery driver refused a tip, and insisted that the best tip I could offer is feedback. Well... here's my feedback! I really enjoyed the pizza, and can't wait to try you guys again, and hopefully add that 5th star!

Why 4 stars?  Because the key to my morning heart is a good omelet.

   ---   ---   ---

2+ years living in Seminole Heights

Several hundred occasions driving right past Three Coins Restaurant

Zero trips inside.  

I just wasn't sure what to expect in there.  It recently dawned on my curiosity to check out Three Coins on Yelp, and the reviews guided me to finally stop in.

What I got was a better version of Denny's, that's closer to my house...and most importantly...locally owned!  Mmmm....local....(Homer drool sounds)

The girlfriend needed to catch a 6:55am flight, which meant I was up at 5:30am on a Sunday.  This typically would cause me borderline schizophrenia, but I suffered through waking up when it was still pitch black outside, knowing that a new Seminole Heights gem was on the docket for the morning.

I braved this venture alone, as not only were none of my friends awake at that ungodly hour, but I believe only 11 people in the city of Tampa were conscious during this time.

My omelet hit the spot, big time!  The fact that I was sitting across from a prostitute that was just getting off "work" for the night, was a bonus.  I got to listen to her haggle with the waitress over how much extra jelly cups would cost and why she couldn't do substitutions for free on certain menu items for take-out orders.  I couldn't tell if these silly restrictions were legitimate, or if she was a regular trouble maker that they were trying to eliminate from coming back.  Either way, I got dinner and a show.

Why 4 stars? Because this is a great spot to grab a burger in between 'The Heights'

   ---   ---   ---

I use the term 'The Heights' because Thee Burger Spot is located pretty much right on the border of Tampa Heights and Seminole Heights - two 'hoods that are appropriately named as they both are seeing their popularity rapidly ascending. I think a burger joint was the perfect addition to this neck of the woods because as much as it seems like a new restaurant is opening every other week here, where could you go for a good old fashioned burger? Well, now you can come here!

The menu is quite large - you can get anything from a basic cheeseburger to something a bit off the wall like a donut burger (on Friday's only) or a burger with peanut butter. As tempted as I was by the latter, I'm a sucker for burgers with grilled onions and BBQ sauce, so I went with the Tangy BBQ Bacon Burger. My wife was a great dining mate because I was tempted to order the Big Smack Burger, and I was debating between the two, she mentioned that she wanted the Big Smack. Perfection!

Both burgers were really solid! I took my bag of fries and doused them in the seasoning left on one of the common tables, which was such an upgrade - I highly recommend doing the same!

Thee Burger Spot is a really great addition to the area - and an affordable place to grab a casual lunch or dinner!

Why 4 stars? Because this is another solid Latin eatery in West Tampa.

   ---   ---   ---

Cuenelli's was on my list for quite a while, but I was finally able to make it out. I normally order steak over chicken, but I wanted to try both since the name of the business includes "Peruvian Style Rotisserie Chicken" in it. 

I enjoyed my meal. It wasn't the best I've had in Tampa Bay, but it was a job well done. I thoroughly enjoy anytime I have the chance to gobble up some South or Central American goodness, and this was no exception.

Why 3 stars? Because the pizza was fine but not the star of the show.

   ---   ---   ---

5-stars overall with 50+ reviews? Pretty much an automatic for me wanting to visit a place shortly after I notice. I think I bookmarked this on a Friday and was there Saturday for dinner.

We started off with the cheese roll and it hyped up my anticipation for the pizza even more. This cheese roll was absolutely ridiculous. It's essentially just a cheese calzone if you're struggling to picture it. And it's perfect. I'd go as far as saying it might be the best cheese-stuffed dough that I've ever had.

However, the pizza is what we came here for. And sadly, the pizza was just ok. My wife made the point that it seems like they use high quality ingredients, at least. And she might be right about that. But overall, I just wasn't super impressed. 

We ordered half extra cheese, half pepperoni. I was kind of regretting ordering extra cheese because it was actually an overwhelming amount. It was essentially collapsing the dough and making it soggy. But when I tried a slice of my wife's pepperoni, it was the same thing.

I wouldn't mind stopping in here again for the cheese roll, but I don't know if I'm a big enough fan of the pizza to try it again.

Why 5 stars? Because the pancakes with macadamia sauce is one of the best tasting things in the Bay Area.

   ---   ---   ---

Seriously, the macadamia sauce is utterly ridiculous. It's the perfect tasting substance.

When my fiance and I decided to plan our wedding in Hawaii, I quickly discovered that an unknown benefit of this destination: the food. I'll had virtually no knowledge about Hawaiian cuisine, but after perusing Yelp listings in Hawaii during wedding planning, I've quickly discovered the realization that I might not ever come back after the nuptials. 

Quickly we began hunting for the closest thing we could find to authentic Hawaiian food, here in Tampa Bay. Sadly, it's almost non-existent. By the time I remembered Ohana Cafe from our 2015 Yelper Party, they closed up shop and were in the process of moving to Dunedin. So we sat by for weeks, waiting for this paradise to open. And after checking Facebook about 65 times for a status update, finally, it did.

As you can imagine, there was a lot of hype built up in our minds. And guess what? Those freaking pancakes with macadamia sauce exceeded it. And it's not just because the sauce is great. The quality of pancake is just as high. And the popover is excellent as well. Teresa's mom makes these herself every day, and they are served until they sell out. How do I know this? Teresa told me herself!

Oh, and who is Teresa you ask? Probably the sweetest business owner I've met in my 4 years with Yelp. During our time at Ohana, she spent the morning just walking around table to table and making sure everyone's experience was as wonderful as it could be. She gave out at least 50 hugs in the hour. Ohana definitely has the feel of a place where everybody knows your name, and if they don't, she'll soon learn it. And hug you.

After one visit, I think Ohana is my favorite breakfast spot in Tampa Bay, the best Hawaiian restaurant in Tampa Bay, and the best restaurant in Dunedin. I know that might sound pre-emptive, but I was that blown away.

Why 5 stars? Because this isn't your grandma's ice cream.

   ---   ---   ---

Not that I don't love traditional ice cream, my favorite is Blue Bell after all, but I am not a fan of nearby Bo's. It's so basic that it's boring to me. During my time living in Seminole Heights, I was always disappointed that Bo's was the only option, so I usually would just pass on ice cream altogether. Now that I've moved to Carrollwood, I'm bummed that Revolution wasn't around sooner!

The flavors are funky here! Porky's Delight, Mint Want Cookies, Chocolate Habenero, Euro Trash, etc. You probably don't even know what some of those are, which is half the fun, to me. Even the simply flavors have great names, like "the best dang vanilla you ever had in your whole life." From there, you can essentially convert any of these flavors into a sundae, which is exactly what I did and it was damn delicious.

Parking is a bit tight in this parking lot. Since the whole building is new, I wish they would have built it an extra 10 feet off the road so that the parking lot wasn't such a crowded mess. Even in a smaller vehicle, you'll feel like you're pulling up in an F350 - it's that compact. But that's the price for the most delicious ice cream in the area, and I'm willing to pay it. 

Tampa Bay doesn't have a ton of local ice cream establishments, but this might be the #1 best in the Bay Area.

Why 5 stars? Because everyone who knows me, knows I am one of their biggest fans.

   ---   ---   ---

One of the most detailed reviews I've ever written was for the 4 Rivers of Carrollwood. If you want a breakdown of all breakdowns, use that as your guiding light through the BBQ desert.

After one meal at this location, I'm going to assume that the food will be identical here to what is served up at all of the other 4Rivers' in the state of Florida. I will say that our food was a smidge on the cold side, but I'll chalk that up to this location being brand-spankin' new, and our visit coming on the coldest night of the "winter" so far.

How this 4Rivers is different than the others is it's incredibly small parking lot. Is it just an illusion, or is this lot like 1/3rd the size it should be for a 4R parking lot? It seems microscopic, and I don't even know where overflow parking would go, so good luck visiting at peak hours.

The decor, as usual is great. The friendly service as usual, is great. And the meat is top notch. As is my lone gripe with 4 Rivers in general is that the side dishes leave a bit to be desired. I enjoy the cornbread salad, and the sweet potato casserole (which is infinitely more dessert than side) but that's it. The rest of them are very average at best.

That being said, 4Rivers is easily the best BBQ in Tampa Bay. I could never quit you, 4R.

Why 5 stars? Because I really just loved everything, despite a small mishap.

   ---   ---   ---

I was excited to try out Deviled Pig, but when the reviews started rolling in, I noticed that they were somewhat mixed. That tempered my enthusiasm a bit, but the kinks must have been worked out, because I noticed them jump up to 4.5 stars and I was right back on the excitement train!

I ordered a platter - Burnt Ends, Pulled Pork, Panko Crusted Mac-n-Cheese and Pig Powder Fries. I have to say that I loved all of it! I'd probably give the Mac-n-Cheese 4-stars, but the rest were no-doubt-about-it 5's! My wife and I both really loved the regular BBQ sauce. I tried some Alabama White and didn't enjoy it as much, but was not upset about it at all with how tasty the regular sauce was! It had a hint of sweetness to it and was extremely addicting!

Both meats were amazing. Honestly there was nothing to critique there - the seasoning, the texture, etc. It was all perfect.

And shoutout to Michelle M who mentioned the seasoned fries in her review. I ordered them just because she raved about them and she was not wrong - I could have eaten ten pounds of those things because they were wildly addicting.

My wife ordered a special that was called something like the "Mac Daddy" sandwich, and to be honest, we thought it was a pretty big miss. I *never* send food back, but we each took one bite of this thing and I immediately went back to the counter and asked for something else. I don't know what kind of meat was on it but it tasted about 5x saltier than it should have, almost to the point where it seemed like it might have gone bad. I asked them to just replace it with a brisket sandwich and it ended up being an infinite improvement.

I enjoyed the BBQ place that was here before, but I think Deviled Pig is even better!

Why 4 stars? Because the variety is second to none.

   ---   ---   ---

If the man who invented pizza was brought back to life, and taken to a Mellow Mushroom, he'd probably be pissed off. "WHAT IS THIS?!" He'd likely exclaim.

But that's ok. I'm sure the first pizza would taste awful, if we were able to try it today. Same for the first burger, the first donut, etc. 

So I'm all about evolution. The die-hard pizza purists might not like it, but I love what Mellow Mushroom has done.

Normally I don't write reviews for chain businesses, but I had actually never once been to a Mellow Mushroom in my life, until my very recent visit. It didn't "feel" like a chain because of that. They also had a fair amount of Tampa Bay area beers, and certain "this location only: items, which gave it the local feel.

We ordered an appetizer that was half muffaletta bread and half cheesy bread. The fiance was in love with every bite of her muffaletta, but my cheesy bread was just okay. 

The pizza, however, was top notch. We went with the ricotta and meatball pie, and it was delicious. Anything with ricotta is normally going to make me the happiest boy in all the land, and this was no exception.

I probably won't wait 31 years before my next Mellow Mushroom visit :) It's a great spot!

Why 5 stars? Because this was a great choice for a first meal out 54 days.

   ---   ---   ---

I really missed eating out. Even though it is definitely my favorite activity, you really don't appreciate how much you miss something until it's gone. 

I don't know why I never visited Clear Sky before. Pre-coronavirus, I added it to my list of restaurants I wanted to visit, but once everything shut down, I figured I would wait until I dine-in for my first experience. So my wife and I got up early and ventured out to Clearwater to arrive right when they opened at 9am.

Even if it weren't for coronavirus, we would have opted to sit outside because the weather was so perfect. But for those who would feel more comfortable, there are a few tables outside and a few tables kind of quasi-outside under an enclosed tent.

The food itself was a huge hit. I ordered the lobster brie benedict, but without the brie. It really hit the spot and wasn't too heavy, which is normally my one gripe about benedicts.

My wife ordered her normal go-to - country fried steak. We were both incredibly pleased with it. There was a certain kind of seasoning on the breading that really made it stand out. 

And we shared some chocolate chip pancakes. While I would have opted for a different flavor of pancakes or french toast, I ended up really loving these. Just like the other things we ordered - they weren't too rich/heavy, which normally results in the feeling of being bogged down for hours after a big breakfast.

It really was a beautiful and therapeutic experience to return to something we love. I very appreciate why and how the world changed for a bit and it's certainly not over yet, but for a brief time this morning, Clear Sky was my true happy place.

Why 5 stars? Because Bodega opening in Seminole Heights is a dream come true!

   ---   ---   ---

Okay... so it would be even more of a dream come true if I still lived in Seminole Heights, but my commute from Carrollwood to Seminole Heights is much easier than driving all the way down to DTSP.

But the thing is, the Cuban Sandwich from Bodega was never something that led me to regretting my 50 mile round trip commute - it was that amazing. 16 miles is just a bit nicer :)

As soon as I heard that they were building this location, I stalked them like crazy on social media and was able to visit within a few days of them opening their doors.

Because the wife and I are huge fans of Bodega, we went a little crazy with our order:

2 Cuban Sandwiches
Rice and Beans
Jicama Slaw
Mango Smoothie
Guava and Cheese Pastelito

As is the case with the original location, this Cuban Sandwich is perfect. I don't know what they do to these things to make them so amazing, but they make the best Cuban Sandwich in Tampa Bay, in my opinion.

The Jicama Slaw and Rice and Beans are great sides to give you some variety in between bites of that heavenly Cuban. As expected, the mango smoothie was great, because why wouldn't it be? And the guava and cheese pastelito was a decent way to end the meal on a sweet note, though I might opt for something else next time. 

As for the space itself, it mostly consists of outdoor seating, just like the DTSP location, but there is a small indoor space with a few tables for those hot afternoons. There are a couple of shuffleboard courts off to the side of the main seating area, which is totally an awesome thing to take advantage of while you're here.

If I ever move away from Tampa Bay, Bodega will be one of the restaurants I'd miss the most. Now with locations in the coolest/trendiest neighborhoods in TB, they are legitimately one of the cornerstone local businesses of the Bay Area.

Why 4 stars? Because the games... oh the games!

   ---   ---   ---

Ok, so what holds me back from a 5-star review here, is that I basically don't really love the beer. And I mean, a brewery is kind of centered around the beer. But I tried the wheat and the beach blonde. Both seemed a bit on the hoppy side. Pretty much, the less IBU, the better, for me... but these didn't taste too low.

However... outside of the beer, this is by far the best brewery in Tampa Bay. Sounds kind of dumb, until you show up here They have basketball, cornhole, darts, foosball, ping pong, and I feel like I'm even forgetting something. 

Even if you don't love the beer, you'll it here. I've always said, the best thing to mix with drinking is moderately athletic activity that doesn't involve cardio.

Why 5 stars? Because what was on my plate came straight from the heavens above France.

   ---   ---   ---

I've seen to many of my fellow Yelpers sing the praises of Flying With Jerome to pass on venturing here myself. The verdict? Absolutely wonderful and worth every inch of the 20 mile drive from my house.

My fiance and I shared a Ham & Cheese Croissant and an order of french toast. Both were utterly perfection. The croissant was typical, but amazing with its flaky outside and cheesy center. But I think the french toast was the star of the show. it was a bit different than your average french toast, which started with the brioche bread. At first I wasn't sure what to think about it, but it grew on me with every bite. By the end, I felt like singing in my booth, which would have made for a poor experience for the other customers. 

If you haven't been to Flying With Jerome yet, put it very high on your to-do list!

Why 5 stars? Because this was an incredibly pleasant surprise.

   ---   ---   ---

I really had just about no expectations for VIP. Walking in, I thought, "oh boy... another Tex-Mex spot in Florida, that's much more heavy on the Mex, than the Tex."

While my assumption was correct, the difference between this and a normal Tex-fake-Mex experience, was that food was actually... good.

The chips and queso were really solid, but the fajitas were prim-o. I was so skeptical about how this meal was going to go... but every bite just kept surprising me more and more. 

Solid effort VIP... you're now my go-to when I'm on the beach in South Pinellas.

Why 5 stars? Because this is the best schnitzel I've found in Tampa Bay.

   ---   ---   ---

I've been checking off long-time bucket list restaurants recently, and just as my list was narrowing down to only a few remaining, my wife and I drove past German Knodle. I looked it up on Yelp to see that it had exclusively 5-star reviews and I added it to my list! About a week later, I stopped in for lunch. 

My wife's go-to order at German restaurants is schnitzel. The problem with this is that it's also my favorite German dish, but ordering the same thing is such a tragic act - you've gotta try multiple things on the menu!

I was very tempted to order the prosciutto panini, as it looked mighty tasty, but I felt weird ordering a non-German dish, so I opted for the kasewurst, which the owner said had cheese in it. While I did think it was solid, I didn't see or taste any cheese within it. And while I enjoyed the garlic fries on the side, I actually asked for potato salad, but I believe he mis-heard me or forgot. The sauerkraut was okay, but I'm not really a sauerkraut fan in general.

But the star of the show was my wife's schnitzel. I was lucky that she wasn't super hungry and let me eat a pretty decent amount of it. It's hard to say what made it go great exactly, but every bite was perfection. It might even be the best schnitzel I've ever had!

The knodle's for dessert are only available during dinner, which is a bummer, but I'll definitely be sure to check them out in the evening next time!

Why 4 stars? Because this was the total package.

   ---   ---   ---

So I guess this is going to be one of those reviews where I list all the features and then say "check" next to each one that was present.

Wide-ranging menu -check

Great food from said wide ranging menu -check

Friendly employees -check

Prompt service -check

Calories - check


I went with the redneck benedict and a small side of french toast, because I felt like being really fat this morning. PLUS, they bring out a "danish basket" which is the equivalent to getting a bread basket while you wait on your dinner to come out. This is the most genius idea ever for a breakfast joint. Not only is the idea golden, but the hodge-podge of breakfast treats were all phenomenal.

As for my meal - the redneck benedict is an eggs benedict, combined with biscuits and gravy. It was very solid, as you could imagine when combining such treasures.

My french toast came with almonds sprinkled all over it and was one of the better pieces of french toast I've ever had.

My server was quick, as was the food prep time. The guy who cashed me out told me about a bunch of interesting items they offer that aren't on the menu, for my next trip to enjoy a fat breakfast.


All in all, I'm not in Clearwater for breakfast often, but this will be a top choice next time the situation arises.

Why 5 stars? Because the aesthetics match the taste.

   ---   ---   ---

I have driven past PSOMI countless times and I honestly just assumed it was not a restaurant. I thought maybe it was a Marketing Company... maybe an Architectural firm, maybe an art studio? Am I alone in this assumption due to a weird glitch in my brain or did anyone else think that? 

Either way, speaking of an art studio, it might as well be a place made for Instagram that happens to serve (really great) food too! Seriously - the place is beautiful from corner to corner. And I hope that this is the start of more trendy spots like this popping up in the NoHo neighborhood.

Ironically, a few days earlier, I visited a vegan restaurant for lunch and ordered a gyro. I assume it was some kind of soy "meat." I thought it was just ok, but would have preferred an actual gyro. So when I found myself at PSOMI, I knew a real-deal gyro would really hit the spot. And it absolutely did. It kind of made me retroactively like my vegan meal a lot less.

In addition to the gyro, I love Greek fries and these did not disappoint. And the coffee selection here is elevated above what you expect from a restaurant - honestly it's a bit above what some coffee shops are offering. But possibly the highlight of the whole meal was the Baklava Crumb Cake. Granted, this was much more crumb cake than baklava, but it was perfect. And large.

Psomi, you've won me over after one visit.

Why 5 stars? Because we have ourselves a new treasure.

   ---   ---   ---

I'm gonna make a bold statement: this is the best Perry owned restaurant. And I love Datz.

We are desperately starving for quality cajun food in Tampa bay, and now it's finally here.

First of all, coming to Roux and not ordering the corn bread is like buying a lottery ticket and not scratching it off. You are sitting on a metaphorical gold mine once you're inside the threshold of Roux, don't miss out on the gold, man.

Paragraph number two about the corn bread, just in case you skimmed the last one: it comes in a skillet. It has cinnamon butter. I SAID SKILLET AND CINNAMON BUTTER.

For the entrees...

ME: not your ordinary shrimp and grits

SHE: double-cut kurobuta pork chop

The shrimp and grits is absolute not your ordinary. They bring out the shell of a shrimp the size of a small dinosaur with the guts still in it. I know that sounds gross, but monster shrimp guts are like regular shrimp, but tastier. The grits were perfection, and there was even a bit of what looked like marinara sauce. I'm not a marinara guy, and the combination seemed weird, but it worked very well together. From now on, instead of saying, "they go together like peanut butter and jelly," we'll be saying, "they go together like dinosaur-sized shrimp, and marinara sauce!"

Her meal was tasty, but I choose the better option since I'm a professional reviewer. 

We desserted with a baked alaska and bread pudding. If you don't like whipped cream like substances, then I probably don't trust you as a person. But if that's you, then you definitely should not order a baked alaska. If you do enjoy creme de la whip, then order like four of them. They actually taste even better as leftovers! 

And as much as I loved my baked alaska, I liked the bread pudding even more. This time, the amateur's selection won out.

I also attended lunch here and tried the alligator bites po boy at the recommendation of our hostess and server. It was easily the largest po boy I have ever seen. It honestly seemed illegally large. It was a bit spicy, but delicious... and also the messiest sandwich of all time. 

I don't consider "messy" a bad thing with a sandwich... quite the opposite actually. Just probably try to avoid this for a business meeting, and opt to eat it around someone that you're comfortable making an ass out of yourself around. There's no way to eat this giant bread bowl of goodness without getting a lil bit of the cajun secret sauce all around your hands, mouth, and clothes. 

5 stars.

Why 5 stars? Because this is cold drink of water in the middle of the desert. 

   ---   ---   ---

I try to see the good in all places, especially parts of the Tampa Bay area. But I don't think it's untrue to say that Largo is not exactly the trendy epicenter of TB. Don't get me wrong, there are definitely some gems in Largo (shoutout to Barley Mow) but overall, there's a lot of Old Florida here.

However, the Haus could fit in to any part of the Bay Area and not look out of place - Seminole Heights, DTSP, etc. Maybe in ten years, when Largo has become a hot spot for cool local businesses, we'll say it all started with the Haus aka the pioneer of the Largo movement. And what's crazy about that, is that it's in the middle of a strip center, but is still super cool!

As for details on the place itself? The drink menu is very extensive, so it's hard to imagine coming here and not finding the drink for you, whether it's coffee or tea. 

We did not eat during our visit, but we did hang out here and work for a few hours. My favorite thing about a coffee shop that I need to work in, is when they have comfortable seating. The Haus definitely checks that box, as there are more traditional tables to sit at, or couches/padded chairs if you're looking to alleviate that pressure on your back. They even have outside seating, which we were tempted to take advantage of on a lovely March afternoon.

Next time I'm in the area and need a boost of caffeine, this will be my destination for sure!

Why 5 stars? Because they have like 30 gourmet popsicles.

   ---   ---   ---

You guys. 30 gourmet popsicles.

This is going to be one of my shortest reviews, because - what else do you need to know?

You walk in. There's like a 142 square foot lobby and a counter. In the counter are 30 different types of gourmet popsicles. 

You agonize over which flavor, as if you're deciding something with life or death at stake. 

You pick a flavor (in my case - Guava Peach.)

You take the plastic wrapper off, and you thank your God that gourmet popsicles are a thing. 

What a time to be alive.

Why 5 stars? Because I left here so pumped that it exists.

   ---   ---   ---

My girlfriend got a gift card here for a Christmas gift from her boss, and was really pumped to try it out. As we were walking from our parking spot across the street, I was already impressed. I was in the love with all of the interior design that you could see from a distant through the doors and the windows.

It's kind of like a mini-Whole Foods. You can get a variety of rare, specialty products here, fresh food, wine, cupcakes, etc etc - the list goes on and on.

To the point of the critics, yes it's a pricey place. But I generally try to live by a quality over quantity philosophy in life, so it appeals to me. I was so excited to find bottles of Stumptown iced coffee here... something that you don't see every day in Florida. If I were to list all of the neat things like that I found throughout the venue, my review would be over the 5,000 character limit.

Upstairs, there is a second dessert case, as well as a huge wine bar, and more beer for sale. It was pretty unexpected to find the nice bar on floor number two.

But back on gound-level, I ordered the St. Petersburger and a side of pimento mac-n-cheese. The burger was solid, and I liked the pimento mac more than I thought I would. We dined outside and were able to take in the gorgeous surroundings of the new sun dial. I hope that round two is more kind to the businesses here than the first attempt, because they did a helluva job with it.

With Locale Market and Mazzaro's, St. Pete is definitely dominating the specialty market game. Now... if we could only achieve my dream of turning the site of Tropicana Field into a giant market for local vendors, we'd totally be set!

Why 4 stars? Because my first Ethiopian food experience was a great one!

   ---   ---   ---

Myself and a group of friends descended upon Mitmita to celebrate the first of many Nick S birthdays in 2019. I'm really glad he chose Mitmita because I'd never had Ethiopian food prior to this and I thoroughly enjoyed it!

I was educated on the fact that Ethiopian cuisine is supposed to be enjoyed sans silverware. Every dish is served with this "bread" that you use to pick (or scoop) your food off of the plate with. I put bread in quotations because this is like no other bread I've ever seen. It's thin, but also shares the texture of a sponge. Because of this, I consumed *a lot* of this bread, so I hope it wasn't wildly unhealthy. 

As for what I actually ate, it's really hard to place exactly which dishes were what. We were in a group of about ten people and Nick had them bring a ton of different items out. But I'll do my best to shoutout the highlights:

-All of the sambusas were great, whether it be the chicken, beef or veggie. I've had these at many Indian restaurants and I always enjoy them. For those unfamiliar, it's comparable to an empanada.

-We had a few different lighter plates brought out to share, which were all enjoyable - Buticha, Ye-timatim (Ethiopian tomato salad), Ye-miser (Lentil Salad), and a couple servings of various veggies.

The only thing I ordered on my own was the Kay Watt, which was beef in garlic, ginger, onions and sauce. I thought this was okay, but I'd probably opt to order something else in the future.

My favorite part of this experience was the owner who doubled as our server. She was not only the sweetest person ever, but she handled our crazy table with ease. The patience she expressed with Nick when he was trying to take over and control everything was impeccable. She deserves a medal! I hope Tina was taking notes to apply some of those methods at home.

I'm so glad I was able to experience a brand new cuisine and look forward to round two!

Why 5 stars? Because I would die a happy man if they opened a location closer to my house.

   ---   ---   ---

I have a lot of Top 10 lists on Yelp: Top 10 Asian Restaurants, Top 10 Places In Ybor, Top 10 Cuban Sandwiches, etc. 

But it might be time for a new list: Top 10 Places I wish were near my house.

It's a different list than just my Top 10 Overall Favorite Restaurants. For example: as much as I absolutely love Brick & Mortar in DTSP, I would probably not be eating there on a weekly, or even monthly basis. It's delicious, but the price point/calorie intake calls for it to be a spot I visit a few times a year, and I'm willing to drive to St. Pete for that.

But Sandwich on Main? 100% if they had a Carrollwood location, I would be eating here on a stupidly regular basis. Safety Harbor isn't that far of a drive, but it's definitely more of a weekend destination, and less of a "it's 7p on a Tuesday and I'm hungry - let's drive to Safety Harbor" place.

What I love about Sandwich on Main is that you can go here when you're looking for deliciousness over everything, or if you're calorie counting. They have an insane menu of sandwiches. Insane. I could visit 10 times, order a different sandwich every time, and still be excited to try something new on my 11th visit. This made my first trip feel like a root canal, as I tried to decide which sandwich to go with. It was so difficult, I actually ordered two - and ate one the next day for lunch. But more on that, in a minute.

Here's the kicker why my dream is for location #2 to be in my hood: any of these wonderful/amazing/life-changing sandwiches can be made into a salad. 

Yes, I know you can do that at places like Jersey Mike's and Subway, but um, those places are like my 2 year old nephew and Sandwich on Main is LeBron James, in terms of sandwich shops. These are high quality, creative 'wiches, made with love. There will be no Sisco trucks backing up to SOM anytime soon.

Back to those Tuesday's at 7p - all this Yelping I've done over the last few years has not come without consequence. I try to limit my cheat meals to maybe a couple on the weekends, which is why finding a salad with delicious meat (and subbing oil & vinegar in for the dressing) is the key to my weeknight dinner heart. 

As for what I ordered - the midnight Cuban, which doesn't come on Cuban bread, but is still delicious. I also ordered the Main Beef to be eaten the next day. Both were as tasty as I would have hoped for - they even specially prepared my Main Beef to be best for the next day.

The selection of fancy sodas always makes me happy/nostalgic. I have gotten to a point where I can't drink super sugary sodas, but I do enjoy the diet versions - and my diet cream soda was the perfect compliment to my meal. My only complaint were the chips that are supposed to taste like they're seasoned with Old Bay - they were a bit spicy and honestly, the seasoning was far from ideal. Obviously these are not made by SOM, so no big deal. My wife had the dill flavored chips, and those were awesome.

The service here was also amazing. We sat outside, and the girl who served us could not have been more pleasant and personable. She's the type that could bring you out of a mood, she was so nice.

So yeah... Sandwich on Main - you're my new crush. I hear Carrollwood is a great place for local businesses looking to open a 2nd location :)

Why 5 stars? Because I'm so glad this is finally a part of my neighborhood.

   ---   ---   ---

I feel so badly for the owners of Hiccups & Churrholic. They seemed to be on pace to open this restaurant nearly a year ago, right before this little thing called COVID-19 showed up in our lives. The trials and tribulations of small business owners in this time cannot be overstated and these folks are a prime example of that. I cannot even begin to understand what they have been through in the last year, but fortunately we live in a state that is doing its best to help businesses make the best of a bad situation. 

To add to that, I visited on the third day Hiccups opened and it was packed. After all they've been through, I couldn't be happier to see it! But I was happy that I'd called in ahead, as my food was ready when I arrived.

The thing my wife and I knew would be the #1 priority on our list were the garlic noodles. We added the shaken beef as our protein. We had garlic noodles in Hawaii a few years ago that we still talk about to this day, so we were pumped to see them on the menu. Unfortunately, they didn't quite taste like that, but they did taste like really delicious lo mein noodles. We wished the veggies were sliced a little thinner, but overall, it was an enjoyable dish.

We also ordered popcorn chicken with fried rice. The rice was as good as it gets. The popcorn chicken was quite tasty and plentiful. You get a ton of bang for your buck with this dish!

I actually think my favorite thing I ate were the cajun wings. I will definitely be ordering them again!

I also loved my taro smoothie with boba. They actually ran out of regular boba, so I had to replace it with crystal boba, which I'd never had before, but really liked it! It was a bit more chewy than regular boba... I might have to order that on purpose next time!

And we finished it off with a coconut chocolate churro, which was wonderful.

All in all, we will probably come here quite frequently, especially for boba and other treats. Kudos to these business owners for persevering and making Carrollwood just a little bit cooler than it was before January 8, 2021.

Why 5 stars? Because it successfully helped with me severe case of missing-Hawaii-itis.

   ---   ---   ---

After getting married in Hawaii a month prior to this writing, we've been visiting every Hawaiian restaurant that we can find in Tampa Bay. The Honu is definitely one of my favorites so far! I ordered the Manu Kea & Keck I & II, which is a long way of saying beef, spinach and rice. The beef had a phenomenal flavor to it, and despite its basic nature, I really loved it and could eat it every day.

For dessert we shared a couple of things: the macademia nut ice cream and this cookie crumble thing that was served inside a glass. I was really glad we ordered these two things together because they complimented each other nicely. If I had to pick a favorite, I'd have to go with the ice cream.

As for the vibe of the Honu, they definitely did a great job of making you feel like you're actually in Hawaii. If only we could add some mountains in Dunedin, we'd be all set. We sat outside with our dog, and they even brought him a meal of chicken and sweet potatoes for $3. If Moose could type, I'm certain he'd be offering a 5-star review as well.

Why 5 stars? Because the hype was great, but it was met!

   ---   ---   ---

I've been stalking Casa Santo Stefano's social media for months and I'm sure if not for the terrible year that 2020 brought us, these doors would have been opened much sooner. Even in normal times, new restaurants have to bend over backwards to get all of the proper permits and everything that goes into opening up, so I cannot even imagine the hassles that have taken place this year. But now that it's open, Ybor City just got a little more awesome.

As soon as you walk in, you feel the love. If you didn't know any better, you might think this place is an old school Tampa staple that's been around for decades. What throws you off is that 'new building' smell that hits your nose every few minutes. Every detail is perfect in the marriage of the classic and modern details - even the bathroom is amazing. On a 1-5 scale, the design and ambiance scores a 48.

The first question we were asked was one of the rare negatives about our experience: would we like sparkling or still water? We opted for still, which we later found out meant a $6 glass bottle of Acqua Panna. Was $6 a big deal to add to our dinner? No. But it kind of felt like we were tricked a bit into an upsell when we would have been perfectly fine with tap water. Either way, we loved everything else about our experience.

We started with the bread, which was very unique. Our server (Carlos, who was excellent) said what it was called but I did not retain it. Rather than butter, this bread is accompanied by olive oil and seasonings, which is the Sicilian way, apparently. My wife and I were both given our own large bread serving and our own oil, which was nice. While the bread was a bit different, the result was the same as any other time I eat bread at an Italian restaurant: I could eat it all day but used maximum willpower to save some for my meal and not fill up.

I ordered a Limonata cocktail, which was so refreshing and original. I would not have even known there was alcohol in this glass and could have had four of these. Maybe I would have known about the booze after three and they would have tasted even better? Next time.

We ordered a cesar salad to start and it was a total home run. The lettuce was pillowy soft, the dressing was perfect and the croutons were among the best I've ever had. I recently listened to two hosts on a podcast debate cesar salads. One's point of view was there is almost no variance between the worst cesar salad you'll ever have and the best. I agreed with him at the time, but now that I've had this one, I think he needs to take a visit to Ybor.

While my wife and I love Italian food, I don't know that we've ever actually been to a Sicilian restaurant. I ordered a squid ink pasta (called Spaghetti Al Nero Con Polpo), which I've had at other places, but never quite like this. My one regret is that I wished realized to ask for no olives, as I am not a fan and there were many in this dish, but I still very much enjoyed it. 

My wife ordered the Bracioluni, which I had never heard of. It's three giant meatball type substances with some pasta and diced potatoes. The tomato sauce has a hint of sweetness, which was different but very pleasant. The "meatballs" have steak, sausage, pancetta, hard boiled egg and cheese all mixed in. Again, I feel like this is the theme for everything, but it was definitely a unique dish!

Overall, we're so glad Casa Santo Stefano is finally open. Based on this visit alone, I now want to visit Sicily!

Why 5 stars?  Because it's easily, my favorite breakfast place in Tampa.

   ---   ---   ---

It can get really crowded, and that is where the negatives end.

Right off the bat, you know you are in a good place when you venture over to the self-serve coffee bar.  They have about five kinds of coffee to choose from, which is awesome for someone like me who enjoys coffee but is no connoisseur.

But the BEST part of the coffee bar is the collection of 1980's mugs to choose from.  They have to constantly raid garage sales every weekend in search of the most random mugs available on Earth.

My first visit, I went in a group of four, and all four of us walked out knowing we found a new treasure.  I had the ultimate fried egg sandwich myself...every bite more miraculous than the next.

What really separates Pinky's from the rest of the pack is that EVERY-THING on their menu looks like it will change your life.  Stuffed French Toast?  Breakfast Quesadilla? Oatmeal Waffles?  All kinds of Frittatas? PANCAKE SANDWICH??

I hate typing reviews when I haven't eaten in a while.  I want to live at Pinky's.  I would do dishes and clean the parking lot for a permanent corner table.

Why 5 stars? Because it's absolutely delicious, but be cautious of the wait!

   ---   ---   ---

My first trip to Icesmile consisted of about a 7-10 minute wait to get up to the counter, with the line being about halfway between the counter and the door. Not bad, I thought, for a place that has built up quite a reputation for having long waits. But what worried me was that there were no less than 20 people who appeared to be waiting for their order to be made. I asked the person at the counter about how long it would be, and he said 40 minutes to an hour. We promptly left.

I came back the next day (a Friday) at about 3:30p-4:00p and there were only 2-3 people in line and 2-3 people waiting. MUCH better! I was in and out in less than 15 minutes.
I had a sick wife at home, so I actually just took a couple of bites and then put my lids on and headed home. I thought that the cold ice cream would be great for her sore throat, and I couldn't allow her to have to eat ice cream alone, right? So I put it in the freezer for later consumption.

Fast forward a couple hours and it was finally time to bust these bad boys open. I have to say, it was totally worth all the hassle of going twice, waiting in line 1.5x, and then it still tasted wonderful after sitting in my freezer for a while.

If you watch how they make it, they pour cream onto some kind of pan and mix things together. You can definitely tell while eating it how creamy it is and how well things are mixed together.
