I think it's definitely the best ice cream in Tampa Bay, but I don't know if it's worth the hour wait. Be sure to visit during an off-peak time and be ready for happiness.

Why 3 stars?  Because I had myself some average food.

   ---   ---   ---

3 stars isn't a bad thing.  2 stars is bad.  1 star is awful.  3 is an alright joint.  I feel bad giving 3 to a cool business that I desperately want to be a 4 or 5, but don't sweat it Stone Soup - a 3 isn't bad.  I'll be back.

I've had the Cubmanti and the Clam Chowder.  The Cubmanti is a combination of Pittsburgh's famous sandwich - The Primanti, and Tampa's famous Cuban.  It was tasty but a bit dry.  That being said, the Primanti is a bit dry in itself, so I guess I can't knock Stone Soup.

The Clam Chowder was very thin and not the rich and creamy I was expecting.  If I were on a diet, this would be a great soup, but I wanted to get me some fat soup!

I haven't ordered their ice cream yet, but they get bonus points for carrying Blue Bell - the greatest ice cream ever made.

The people are nice, the concept is neat and the building is cool.  See ya next time Stone Soup.

Why 5 stars? Because this is another future cornerstone of Tampa.

   ---   ---   ---

I'm sure many people will mention Armature Works in their review of Sparkman Wharf because they have many similarities. They both house many mini-versions of some of the top local restaurants in Tampa Bay. They are both located in the urban core of Tampa. They both opened their doors in 2018. And they are both amazing additions to our city that will serve as central meeting spots for people to come together, hopefully for decades to come.

But these two amazing places are also very different. Sparkman Wharf is completely outdoors. There are many shaded areas with the giant Beer Garden and many chairs with umbrellas like you'd find at the beach, but everything is definitely outside besides the restrooms.

The primary highlight of Sparkman Wharf are the nine local vendors that operate out of repurposed shipping containers. These shipping containers are beautifully painted and perfect for 2018, as there will be thousands of photos uploaded to Instagram every month with these as the backdrop. The list of vendors here is highly impressive, and especially appealing as some of the concepts are a bit different than what you'd find at the main restaurant for each biz owner. A couple examples - The Rooster & the Till guys are running a taqueria and the Ichicoro folks are serving Detroit style pizza. 

Seven of these vendors are serving up mostly savory options, but if you're looking for coffee or something sweet, you can find that at Foundation and/or Whatever Pops.

The tenth vendor is a giant beer garden with 30 taps. I counted 12 of the 30 to be from Tampa Bay area breweries on opening day, which is a pretty solid representation. As mentioned above, the beer garden casts a pretty large shadow of shade if you're looking to escape the sun.

In the middle of the the lawn area, you'll find one large shuffleboard court and a few spots to play cornhole. There's also a stage for live music, which I'd imagine will be full of different performers on many weekends in the future. If I could change one thing about Sparkman Wharf, I would have voted for at least a couple more shuffleboard courts because one is definitely not going to be enough for the giant crowds that are sure to congregate here.

If you're looking for water views, you'll have to head to the edge of the property, where you'll also have the opportunity to play more cornhole, if you're looking for a more scenic game. Although, the surroundings near the water are a bit more industrial than "pretty" with the type of ships that are docked nearby.

As for parking, the giant Channelside garage is probably your best bet. I was here for about an hour and it cost me $2. If you're planning on staying longer, there's a table near the entrance that will valet your parking ticket to give you a discount.

Overall, I think that there was a ton of hype built around Sparkman Wharf but the hype was lived up to. This is an amazing upgrade from the old Channelside Plaza and I cannot wait to see what the future of this part of Downtown Tampa holds. There are so many cranes nearby that it's hard to even keep track of all the new high rises popping up!

Why 5 stars? Because this is the best Italian in Tampa Bay.

   ---   ---   ---

I usually don't write a review the same night I eat at a place. I have so many other reviews I need to write from places I have visited weeks ago, but I could not contain my excitement to give this place 5 stars!

The service was over the top. We felt like an old family friend let into someone's home. 

The food was incredible. The girlfriend had the Sacchtetini and words cannot describe how rich and creamy it was. 

I went with the Lobster Ravioli. I've had this dish where places have really skimped out on the Lobster meat...but not here. It was all sprinkled on top of the Ravioli, as well as thoroughly stuffed inside.

All in all, I could not have been happier with this dinner. BRAVO Osteria Natalina!!

Why 2 stars? Because it was a really disappointing experience.

   ---   ---   ---

This review pains me. I really don't enjoy writing negative things about local business, but I just have to be honest about our experience. I heavily debated going with a 3-star to soften the blow, but I had an experience at a Tex-Mex restaurant a couple nights later that was so much better that it provided clarity on what Don Julio's could be.

Starting off, we were given chips and salsa, and while I liked the deep fried chips, they were actually pretty cold - like below room temperature cold. We also ordered queso and guacamole - both were pretty average. The same goes for the rice and beans that we'd later receive. 

The unfortunate part of our meal was when our fajitas came out. I cannot stress enough that I'm just being 100% honest with my description - they looked like packaged/frozen fajitas that were cooked on a George Foreman Grill. I've had countless orders of fajitas in my life and these were easily the worst looking and tasting that I've ever had. Even the pepper and onion slices looked like they were poorly sliced because they were much thicker than you'd usually see. If you look at the photo I uploaded, there's just no way around labeling these to have been pretty terrible.

Not only do I hate to write negative reviews, but it's even worse when it's a business that doesn't live up to its great Yelp rating. I'm hoping that I visited on a day where things in the kitchen went greatly awry and our experience was not the norm.

Why 5 stars? Because this is one of the better Cuban sandwiches I've had.

   ---   ---   ---

When I provide a recommendation to Chris W, one of two things happen: he either never visits a place or he does so after approximately 180 days. But when Chris gives me a recommendation, it becomes an immediate priority for me. This is how things work and I've accepted that.

Chris's review was as such, "I just had the best Cuban sandwich I've ever had." When I hear that kind of praise, it's going to be hard to keep my away.

So I filled up my tank, packed my suitcase and headed up to the land of the great north called "Wesley Chapel." I guess it's technically not Wesley Chapel, but it took me 4.5 days of driving from Carrollwood. It's kind of like driving to Maine, but the weather doesn't change.

When I arrived, there were a few people ahead of me waiting to place orders. When I ordered my Cuban sandwich, I asked how long it would be and was told 20-25 minutes. I considered that good and bad news, at the same time. On one hand, that's a long time to wait for a sandwich, on top of the 10 minutes I'd already waited to order. On the other hand, it probably means that this sandwich is going to be high-quality.

Well, it did turn out to be 20-25 minutes and it also was, indeed, awesome. 

The first thing I noticed was how thick this sandwich was. Usually when I have a Cuban sandwich that's very hearty, it ends up just being a bunch of meat jammed in between the bread for effect. But in this case, it the bread, mayo and pickles were not lost amongst all of the pork and ham.

I had to eat this sandwich while I was driving south back to Florida because I had my baby with me and he was prone to wake up angrily at any moment, because he only knows one speed when it comes to his wake-up moods in public. When I got home, I noticed that I had lost quite a bit of pork in my lap, which I was not mad about. Lap pork is the best, especially when you think you've already eaten everything.

I don't know if it's the best Cuban sandwich I've ever had, but I'm going to put it on my Tampa Bay Mount Rushmore. Job well done, Las Palmas! I see why you had a line of people on a Saturday afternoon and I will definitely be back next time I'm in the area (Canada.)

Why 5 stars? Because the wait and anticipation was worth it.

   ---   ---   ---

One of the quickest ways I can determine if I love a place, is when it's pain-stakingly difficult to decide on what I'm going to order. I feel like I could return to Better Byrd half-a-dozen times and order something equally as awesome and appealing every time. 

On this trip, I ordered a SmokeyByrd (sans jalapeno) and a side of brussels sprouts. I also sampled my dining-mate's tater tots, which were so damn delicious. They came with some kind of marshamallow/cream/butter sauce, which made them more of a dessert than a side dish. If sweet potato fries are your fancy, you'll be very glad you ordered these.

Speaking of sides, my brussels sprouts were stupid addicting. You know when you're at a Mexican restaurant eating chips and queso/salsa and it feels literally impossible to stop eating them? That's these brussels sprouts. But the good news is that they are not nearly as filling as those delicious thin chips covered in salt dipped in melted cheese.... I digress.

The SmokeyByrd is roasted/pulled chicken, BBQ sauce and coleslaw. It's as delicious as it sounds. My only *complaint* is that it's so much food. (Not really a complaint.) But it does make it a little tough to eat. With every bite, I could only assume that there was sauce and chicken all over my face. It was quite tasty though!

I badly wanted to try some mini doughnuts, but I behaved myself. There were some samples on the counter, and my bite left my wanting more. 

I will definitely be back!

Why 2 stars? Because this is the worst movie theater I've ever been to.

   ---   ---   ---

From start to finish, I really did not enjoy my visit to Studio Movie Grill. 

The parking garage was, what the kids call, a hot mess. It was dirty. There were people lined up on the side just starring at you as you walked in. People were blaring music loudly. Babies crying. Kids yelling. The whole deal.

Once inside, the theme of everything being dirty continued. And when I say everything, I mean everything. You know when a place is so dirty, you feel like you have to wash your hands, even if you haven't touched anything? That was me. 

And not just dirty, but sticky. My shoes were sticking to the floor, and my hands were sticky after opening doors. It legitimately felt like nothing had been cleaned in at least a week. The escalators were especially disgusting - I've never seen escalators with that many stains.

The bathroom? Plugged up toilets, water all over the floor. And it was so narrow, that it was tough to avoid the giant puddle. 

The theater itself was not what you'd typically experience, in that, the screen seems smaller and farther away from the seating. The audio quality during the previews was poor, and it was tough to hear dialogue. Once the show started, they just turned the volume up so loud, that it was impossible not to hear. But again, the quality was very poor.

I can't see myself ever making a return.

Why 4 stars? Because this is one of the better options in Clearwater.

   ---   ---   ---

I've wanted to check out Cristino's for years, but the Downtown Clearwater area is just not a part of town I'm in very often. Outside of driving through en route to the beach, I can't say I've ever spent anytime here. But when scanning through some Yelp bookmarks recently, I made the decision that I really needed to check out Cristino's, so the wife and I popped on a podcast and made the 45-ish minute drive.

Our favorite thing to put on pizza is prosciutto, so as soon as we saw that as an option, we knew what we were doing - a margherita pizza + prosciutto! We also decided to share some chicken parm, at the recommendation of a friend who lives nearby and comes to Cristino's often.

Much to our surprise, the food was at our table somewhere between 3-5 minutes after we ordered it. I've been to Chick Fila where it takes at least double that. This was shockingly quick. 

The pizza was solid - there were certain bites that were super cheesy and I couldn't get enough of those. 

The chicken parm was okay - not something I'd order again on a future visit to Cristino's.

The service was excellent. We mostly had one guy coming to our table, but a woman also stopped by a couple times. She also brought us some gelato samples at the end of the meal, which was such a nice touch. We definitely would have taken her up on the idea to order gelato, but we had plans immediately after lunch. 

Since I'm not in this area often, I don't know how soon I'll be back, but it's nice to know I have a go-to now!

Why 5 stars? Because after one visit, this is already one of my favorite 2020 discoveries.

   ---   ---   ---

I recently came across the Flan Factory when looking up new spots and new that it would not be long before I ended up stopping in. The gap between finding Flan Factory on Yelp to sitting in the dining room was about one week and it was everything I hoped it would be.

I ordered El Tampeno (their version of a Cuban) which was delicious. It was a bit lighter than your typical Cuban, which was nice. I'm not sure if it was the airy breading or the fact that it just wasn't as jam packed (maybe both?) but it was a nice lighter meal.

I also couldn't leave here without trying Timba - fried cheese with guava dipping sauce. It's as amazing as it sounds. I highly recommend it!

And I definitely had to grab a couple of flans to-go to bring home to the wife. I was planning on ordering coconut and guava, but coconut wasn't on the menu when I visited, so I went with salted caramel instead. Both were unbelievable. No wonder the name of this place is the Flan Factory - these were the definitely the highlight item, IMO!

On top of the delicious eats, the people here were incredibly nice. They also really play up the puns. They sell t-shirts that say "Only Flans" and when you go to tip on your credit card, 20% is labeled "Flantastic!" That alone is worth 5-stars, but the food matched up to the pun-itry.

Why 4 stars?  Because it looks like a dive bar that wouldn't serve good food.  But it's actually a dive bar that serves good food.

   ---   ---   ---

It's THE Irish Pub of Tampa.  If that's what you're looking for, this is where you need to be.  The thatched roof alone makes it an appealing choice when debating where to grab some lunch and/or a Guinness.  

In my opinion, Wednesday is the best day to go for lunch.  The special is a roast beef sandwich that comes with horse radish and onion ring shavings.  It's the bees knees.  

The bees...ummm...calves on the other hand, is a part of the regular menu.  I've never had a better Corned Beef Reuben than I had at Four Green Fields.  I find them to usually be a bit dry for my tastes, but that was not the case with this piece of heaven.

I lived in Tampa for 5 years before discovering this gem of an establishment.  It's easy to drive right past, but don't make the same mistake I did.

Why 5 stars? Because they have the best juice/smoothie variety I've ever seen.

   ---   ---   ---

I feel like the official slogan of Xtreme Juice should be, "If you can dream it, we can juice it." It seems like there's an unlimited list of smoothies and juices at this place, for no matter what it is that you're craving.

My first visit to Xtreme Juice was eye-opening, and not just because of the menu, but because of the popularity. The line was literally out the door, and this was on a Sunday night. I'm not sure if we just caught them at a weird time, but the line did not really die down behind us as we moved through it. The good thing is that it moved relatively quick, and I needed most of the time to narrow in on my choice.

Both myself, and fellow Yelp employee Katie S, were feeling a bit under the weather, so we ordered the Xtreme Acai Antioxidant. Not only was it delicious, but I can confidently say that I felt MUCH better by the next morning. Sadly, Katie had some form of the swine flu, which all of the antioxidants in the world could not help.

I'll absolutely be returning to Xtreme Juice in the future. I'm kind of disappointed in myself that I'd never visited them before. What a horrible person I am. I wonder if they have any smoothies good for self-loathing.

Why 5 stars?  Because it's a local champion.

   ---   ---   ---

The best Cuban Sandwich I have had in Tampa.  Hands down.

I know it's a pretty simple sandwich, but I've been on the hunt for my clear cut favorite for years.  The target has now been discovered, I will be a returning customer for a long time.

Why 4 stars? Because I was pleasantly surprised with my oysters!

   ---   ---   ---

I have to admit - my expectations were low for the Getaway. I took it to be your typical tourist trap/divey beach bar, but I was really happy to be wrong in this case.

The wife and I had just finished paddle boarding, and were looking for a snack before heading back home. I'm always in the mood for oysters, so when I saw them on the menu, I made a quick decision to order a dozen.

These oysters were on the cheaper side - $15 for a dozen, so I imagined they'd be pretty small. It turned out that they were some of the biggest oysters I've ever had - and really delicious too! The only thing I wished would have been different is that I think the cocktail sauce had a lemon flavor to it, and it was a bit too over-powering for my tastes.

My wife ordered crackers and fish dip, which was decent at best. I'd probably avoid it in the future.

But if you're looking to eat on the water, and if you love oysters, The Getaway is the place to go!

Why 5 stars? Because this is some of the better fried chicken in Tampa Bay.

   ---   ---   ---

I noticed Kay's Kitchen's really strong reviews popping up several months ago, but never actually made it over to stop in. This morning, my wife stumbled upon its Yelp page and suggested we grab that for lunch. She headed over and picked it up for us to enjoy at home.

I ordered a chicken strip basket. We were actually worried it might be fried fish because the strips were long and thin and did not look like typical chicken strips. But it indeed was chicken, just different looking chicken. 

My wife ordered some wings, breasts and thighs. It was a great combination when paired with my chicken tender basket because it allowed us to try all of the different chicken offered. 

I honestly loved all of it. The wings and other fried chicken from my wife's order had this great flavor that was just a tad different than I've had before. I wish I could explain it, but it was very unique.

As Boon pointed out in his review, my favorite part was that the chicken had a very light layer of breading, which is all that's really needed, especially when it's that flavorful. When chicken is covered in three inches of breading, you also end up feeling like crap about an hour after you eat. That did not happen with Kay's at all.

For sides, the fries and black beans + rice were solid, but the star of the show was the mac-n-cheese. My only regret is that my wife and I didn't both order our own portion because I would have loved even more of this.

I ordered a peach lemonade for my drink, which I didn't realize was a frozen drink until it was in front of me. I was completely okay with that because I love frozen drinks and this one was great. It was kind of like a slurpee from 7-Eleven, which I'm a big fan of.

We finished with a red velvet cake for dessert, which also seemed a tad on the lighter side than I expected. Once again, this was ideal because I didn't find myself deep in a food coma shortly after eating.

My only minor complaint is that my wife asked for three different kinds of sauces, but we only got one. And the four containers of sauce were barely filled about a third of the way, which means that they didn't go very far.

But overall, next time I'm craving fried chicken, Kay's Kitchen is probably going to be at the top of my list!

Why 5 stars? Because it's to declare it: this is the best Cuban Sandwich of all-time.

   ---   ---   ---

I have been to Bodega countless times since my initial visit and review, and this is the thing about that damn Cuban sandwich - it's always exactly the same as it was the time before... perfect.

I noticed recently that my review stated that Bodega was on the Mount Rushmore of Cuban Sandwiches, but that truly does not do it justice. It's head and shoulders above the others.

The bread is perfectly crispy, the meat is portioned exactly as it should, and the cheese is present enough to be noticed, but subtly. There is absolutely nothing I would change. It's exactly what I hope for every time I have ever bitten in to a Cuban Sammie.

In addition to that, everything I've ever eaten at Bodega is top notch. The jicama slaw is my favorite side to accompany the Cuban, and I always love to order one their juices as well.

I recently took 8 family members here, and everyone at the table was totally blown away. Saying everyone *enjoyed* their meal would be an understatement. All 8 people were legitimately blown away. That's hard to do. My dad was the only one who strayed from ordering a Cuban, as he went with a Frita, which he thought was even better than the Cuban! I guess I'll need to actually stray from my favorite next time and try that out.

But overall, Bodega is easily my favorite Cuban Sandwich, and easily my favorite restaurant in all of St. Pete and Pinellas County. To anyone responsible for this restaurant and the deliciousness that emits from it, I salute you.

Why 5 stars? Because the Barbie-Q is the best chicken salad I've ever tasted.

   ---   ---   ---

Not only is it the best I've ever had, it's the best I could have ever dreamed of. The flavor is so perfect, it's hard to fathom that I'm actually conscience and that it's actually real life. I don't know how they do it because you'd think it's just regular chicken salad mixed with BBQ sauce. But no, it literally tastes like magic. 

Despite the amazing-ness of the Barbie-Q, I will definitely be trying some of the other appetizing options during future visits, because the menu truly offers a great variety. I will say though, I might have to go with the Barbie-Q at least two more times before I branch out :)

The person who took our order was very friendly and offered us as many samples as needed, until our choice was made. Barbie-Q was my first choice, so I only needed one sample, but my fiance tried a few. She went with the Fruity Fran, which I also enjoyed very much.

The only thing I didn't *love* was the cookie. It very much tasted like something that was mass-produced and came from a Sysco truck. That may not have been the case, but it definitely didn't taste like it was made with any of the magic dust that was sprinkled into the chicken salad.

Shoutout to Chris W who beat me down mentally with endless pitches for me to try Chicken Salad Chick. Turns out the Yelp Tampa Bay ACRONYM knows a thing or two about a thing or two. Now, if we could only get him to plan a UYE here...

Why 5 stars? Because the hype is real.

   ---   ---   ---

Anytime you see a place with 30+ reviews and a 5-star overall rating, you pretty much have to go out of your way eat there. Absolutely a contender for best Thai food in Tampa Bay. I usually order beef green curry at a Thai spot, but I was in the mood for Pad Thai during this visit, and wow... it went down eaaasssyyyyy. I did not want it to be over.

I'm not sure how long they've been around, but I've probably driven right past this place 50+ times in the last couple years. I don't know that I will ever be able to do that again without stopping by and stuffing my face hole. 

I'm writing this review from a plane, and I have 3 hours until we land. That was a gruesome mistake, as I am now painfully hungry. Do you think they have Kombo Kitchen on the drink cart?

Why 5 stars? Because looks can be deceiving.

   ---   ---   ---

It looks like a tourist trap. It's in a location a tourist trap would choose. The enormous menu screams "this is a place that has so many options, that they probably aren't very good at any specific thing."

But it's not a tourist trap! As a matter of fact, it's REALLY good. I have no idea how they manage to maintain such a large menu - it's seriously like Cheesecake Factory's size - but they did a heckuva job on everything we ate. 

Anytime I see a lobster roll on a menu, I'm going to order it. It's just a rule - I love those things with all my heart. It ended up being solid, not spectacular. I would have gladly shelled out a few more bucks for more lobster. That's probably my only gripe, because the flavor was great.

We ordered some zuchinni fries to start, and they definitely hit the spot. I see why they made it into the review highlights!

There were a ton of other things I would have loved to order, which is always a good sign of a solid menu. And my dining mates were very happy with their choices, as well.

Overall, definitely a place I'll return to. And it's definitely the most tourist trap-looking, non-tourist trap I've ever been to! In an area like North Pinellas County, you have to be constantly on guard for these things!

Why 4 stars? Because it's hard to imagine a Dim Sum UYE lower than that.

   ---   ---   ---

Beautiful dim sum, how much I enjoy you. How much more I enjoy you in the company of Yelpers...especially those guiding lights to the Dim Sum World. I basically have a 3rd grade education when it comes to dim sum, but it's great to be able to experience the awesomeness with people like Coty, Michael, etc that seem to have a PhD!

As usual with my dim sum reviews, it's tough for me to even say what I enjoyed...because I don't remember what the names of the balls of goodness were. I do think Ho Ho Choy has a leg-up on the best in the area, but it's a very close gap. 

Long live dim sum and long live these UYE's!!!

Why 5 stars? Because I want to pay rent and sleep here.

   ---   ---   ---

Chris W, the person solely responsible for all of my Yelping north of Busch Gardens and east of 275, has kept me thoroughly up-to-date on the construction updates of Sweet Buns. When he let me know that it was finally open, I made it a priority to visit that upcoming weekend.

The cliche "I felt like a kid in a candy store" is overused, but I don't know what other way I can accurately portray what it felt like walking in here. I felt like a kid in a buns store?

The setup here is that you pick up a tray and a set of tongs to grab whatever you like from the cases. One case is full of sweet options, while the other case has plenty of savory snacks. I came primarily for the sweets, but was actually even more impressed by the savory items!

I'm going to do a very bad job of mentioning the particular items that I ended up with because everything here has something in common: its name is just like 2-3 words that sound heavenly, especially when paired together. Names like "Butter Cream Cake" and "Coconut Mango Crumble" are prevalent here.

For savory snacks, I picked up something that was essentially a hot dog inside of a croissant and another thing that was pretty much a biscuit with ham, onion and chives. Both were stellar. The hot dog was pretty simple, but reminded me of a kolache, which I love very much but are hard to find in Tampa. The other biscuit was perfect. It reminded me of something you'd find at Callie's Hot Little Biscuit in Charleston. 

For sweets:

Something in the shape of a hot dog bun with oreos and whipped cream. It was everything you'd hope for given that description. And very large.

Taro Bun - I love taro. I love sweet buns. This was what I hoped it would be.

Some kind of coconut taro thing - do you like how I use the word "thing" to describe something? It most closely would have resembled a sponge cake size/shape. I didn't love this as much as the other things.

Mango Pudding - I also didn't love this one quite as much. It was pricey for a very small portion. Probably the only thing here I found overpriced.

Some kind of coconut crumb cake - A texture one dreams of. I was actually checking out with my existing order of everything listed above when they came out and started re-stocking the shelves. This was the thing on the cart that caught my eye and the first thing the employee was re-stocking. I had to have it. I finished checkout, grabbed one and walked right back into line to pay again. It was absolutely worth it.

Sometimes Chris W likes to point out that I say in reviews that I'll be back often to a place but then three years go by and I have two check-ins. This will not be one of those places. Mark my words if you're reading this in 2022, I'll have returned-a-plenty!

Why 5 stars? Because my favorite restaurant in my neighborhood - how could it be better?

   ---   ---   ---

The question, "What is your favorite restaurant" is such a tough one to answer. How can one compare a Mexican restaurant to a poke spot? Or sushi to pizza? Italian versus a burger joint? It always depends on what you're in the mood for. If you've had tacos five days in a row, chances are you aren't going to be jazzed about tacos on day number six.

But when I'm asked this all-important question, I have a default answer: Samurai Blue. Why? Because the consistency is absolutely remarkable. I've been eating at the Ybor location since around the time I moved to Tampa Bay in 2007 and the sushi has been *exactly* as awesome every single time. 

Samurai Blue is owned by possibly the nicest two human beings on the planet - Yung and Rosa. Yung wakes up at an un-Godly hour to come into the restaurant and prepare the secret sauces for the sushi. Anytime you're up for some kind of crazy-early flight, or if you've stayed out at the bar until last call, know that at that moment, Yung is at the restaurant making sauce. That's a ridiculous amount of dedication to do that for this many years, but it's also a testament to why the product is so precisely perfect every time. 

I was going about my business one day, when Yelper Chris W texted me, "did you know they are building a Samurai Blue in Carrollwood?" My first instinct was to assume that he was mistaken. There's no way that could be happening without me knowing about it, right? But the next day, I specifically took a ride up Dale Mabry just so I could look for it... and sure enough... there it was, in all of its pure, unadulterated glory. A Samurai Blue less than 2 miles from my front door. How have I been so blessed?!

But for folks who don't care to hear me wax poetic about my 11+ year love affair with the history of Samurai Blue and just want to know what to order: well, first off... you cannot go wrong. But don't miss out on ordering the Blue Crab Rangoon as an appetizer. It combines so many flavors together in such wonderful harmony. When I visit Samurai Blue, I'm always tempted to order a different appetizer just so I can sample something different, but I always order the crab rangoon and I never regret it.

If you flip the sushi menu over to the back side, you'll notice some more expensive rolls, but I assure you, they are worth every penny. I've had almost all of them at one point over the years, but on my first visit to the Carrollwood location, I had the Tokyo Rock-n-Roll, the Blue Moon Roll and the Love Roll. My wife and I agreed that they were all amazing and that it was tough to pick a favorite from that group. My wife is not a really big sushi fan, but at one point, she said, "Oh my God, it's all so amazing," and it warmed my cold, dark heart.

For dessert, we tried the vanilla and green tea mochi, which is something I'd never had at the other location. I really liked these, and I may be alone in this observation, but the vanilla mochi tasted like root beer. That's a good thing, because I love root beer. But my wife doesn't like root beer and thought I was crazy to make that comparison, so maybe my palette is just a little wonky.

I can't wait until word gets out and I see this parking lot full on a regular basis. I still can't believe it's real - there's a Samurai Blue in Carrollwood.

Why 5 stars? Because I feel more qualified to write this now.

   ---   ---   ---

When I first reviewed Bella's back in 2012, it was a simpler time for my palette. This was before I'd ever had the pleasure of visiting Italy and discovering the true greatness that comes in the form of pasta that's well  prepared. These days, my eye goes straight for the pasta section of the menu when visiting an Italian establishment. In 2012, I just kind of randomly selected something. Oh how ignorant I was.

I recently read some favorable reviews of Bella's and wanted to re-visit now that I have such a newfound respect for the cuisine. My wife and I really struggled to decide what to order because so many of the options looked amazing. We ultimately decided on...

Arancini: 4-stars. These are essentially little fried dough balls with rice, cheese and some other delights packed inside. While I enjoyed them, I wouldn't classify them as an absolute must for a return visit.

Confetti Spaghetti: 5-stars. This was the star of the show. The closest thing I can compare it to is carbonara, but it's a bit different than that. Maybe just a bit less smokey? Either way, this is a dish we enjoyed every bite of and I'd happily order again in the future.

Pollo Milano: 4.5 stars. My favorite part of this dish was the balsamic vinaigrette that really brought out a distinct flavor to separate the profile from the confetti spaghetti. These were great dishes to kind of bounce back and forth from as my wife and I shared.

Our service was great and the slightly louder atmosphere was helpful to provide a little more margin for error for us since we had our 10 month old. Bonus: we've never seen him happier when trying food. We've obviously passed down our appreciation for Italian food via DNA.

Why 5 stars? Because the queso fundido was worth it alone.

   ---   ---   ---

My wife and I love chips and queso nearly more than we love each other. We usually just opt for plan ole' queso, but fundido was the only option on the menu, so we happily went with that instead.

I have to confess: those chips and that queso fundido might be the most addicting thing I've ever eaten in my life. Just writing this review the next day makes me want to drop everything, drive to Oldsmar and order a table full of nothing but queso fundido.

There was a very subtle hint of sweetness to it, which our server said comes from the chorizo poblano vinaigrette. It may have ruined all other queso for me. I can't speak highly enough of it - I wish I could fill up my hot water heater with it and show in this queso fundido. 

Did I eat anything else? Did anything else matter? Yes... and I guess?

We ordered a bunch of tacos - I enjoyed them. I'll rank them from favorite to least:

1) Grouper
2) Korean BBQ Beef
3) Kobe Cheeseburger
4) Short Rib + Barbacoa
5) All Day + Breakfast

But the truth is - there wasn't a ton of separation between #1 and #5. I wasn't head over heels in love with any of them, but I also didn't dislike any of them. If we could rate with decimals, I'd say that they all were between a 3.5 and 4.5 stars. Just a warning: if you don't like spicy food, most of the tacos do have a bit of a kick. We ordered everything spicy that we could on the side and nothing was too overwhelming. I ended up using most of the spicy dipping sauces anyway.

We also ordered the wings with the sauce on the side. Even my wife, who dislikes spicy stuff more than me, didn't think the sauce was spicy and actually really enjoyed dipping her wings in it.

Lastly, we added in street corn and that was the ideal pairing for all of our tacos - I'd definitely order this again.

Next time, I'm literally going to order four rounds of queso fundido, some more street corn and then try out one of those bowls. 

Bless you, chef who created that queso fundido recipe. Bless you infinitely.

Why 5 stars? Because it's even better than the best burger I've ever had!

   ---   ---   ---

After my 'best burger ever' experience, I had to take my colleagues here for a regional conference I was hosting. I was a tad nervous, because I'd only visited B&M once, and while it was amazing, I wasn't sure how the non-burger items would be. It turns out...

Everything. Is. Awesome.

My colleagues were in absolute heaven the entire time. My top favorites were the octopus, the ahi tuna and the poutine. They were all absolutely unbelievable. 

One funny note: we had a group of 9, and the private dining room for groups of that size is very unique. It looks like an old school conference room. It's a very sterile environment and not typically what you'd experience at a restaurant, but the food more than makes up for it. I was just appreciative that they were able to host our large group, when the restaurant is so small.

In two visits, Brick & Mortar is now not only my favorite restaurant in DTSP, but in my Top 5 for the entire Tampa Bay Area.

Why 2 stars? Because I hate doing this... but yikes.

   ---   ---   ---

I really dislike giving out reviews below 3-stars, but there's no way I can justify anything but this after my experience.

I hadn't been to Ceviche in years, and when my friend told me her birthday party was here, I was excited to be reunited! It's one of the more popular restaurants in the area, and the last time I'd been, I remember liking it, but it was long before my days of Yelping.

Unfortunately, I tried about ten dishes, and thought one of them was good. The rest? Anywhere from awful, to average at best.

It was a large group, and food was being passed around left and right. All I know for sure is that the one thing I really enjoyed was some kind of cheesy potato. I ordered the house ceviche for myself, as well as the steak with chimichurri. Both of those things were just utterly terrible. There's no way to sugarcoat it... the ceviche tasted like it had been soaked for 6 weeks in 50 gallons of lemon and lime juice. The steak tasted gamey... I'm not sure if there was goat cheese in there, or that something in the mix just tasted like goat cheese. Either way, it tasted like it, and my taste buds aren't friends with gamey things.

As things were passed around one by one, I would take a bite, and wonder... "how does this place remain so popular?" I really disliked everything... including the flan and the coconut ice cream. How does something that simple get messed up?

And before I end the review, I just want to say that the menu stresses me out. It seems like there is no rhyme or reason to the layout of it. Maybe I'm just dumb, but I could not figure out the pattern, and it felt like a full-time job to dissect the menu for what sounded the most appealing.

Again... this is not why I Yelp. I love giving rave reviews, and hate giving poor ones - see my rating distribution for proof of that. But there is just no way around it... this was one of the worst meals I had in 2013.

Why 4 stars? Because this might the best BBQ in Tampa Bay.

   ---   ---   ---

I've been on a long and on-going hunt for good BBQ out here in Florida. This area is phenomenal for many things, but I've found that BBQ may not be one of them. I don't know what it is, but I often times find myself longing for higher quality when I'm out grubbing some 'Q. I'm from Texas, and this is one of the few times miss I feel even remotely "home sick."

That being said, BJ's might be the best I've had here. This is definitely more of a 4.5 star review, after my recent visit found me practically licking my plate. The ribs were good, but I think the pulled pork was the best. The sauce was phenomenal!

That being said, you go to BJ's for said pork and sauce...not for the ambiance. It's the definition of a dive, but that doesn't bother me one bit. I'd eat in an old closet if it meant I was in for a good meal.

The hunt goes on...but I may have found my winner.

Why 5 stars? Because I want to live in here.

   ---   ---   ---

I do my best to avoid reviewing chains, especially major national chains. I have nothing against businesses that are successful enough to operate numerous locations, but I just don't normally find reviewing them to be very helpful for anyone. Have you ever visited (or not visited) a Starbucks because the reviews swayed you one way or another? No, you have not. Starbucks are what they they are, and the differences aren't of enough consequence to be worth penning, nor reading a review.

But here's the thing - all Whole Foods' are not created equal! I did not know this, until I began frequenting them more often. I only recently moved to Carrollwood in the last few months, and after visiting this location a few times, my eyes have been opened. In particular, this store seems to have everything that the South Tampa and Clearwater locations have... and more! 

The hot food bar is about 2-3x bigger than South Tampa, or it at least feels that way. They likely have the best selection of local beer that I've seen, outside of a couple of bottle shops. Specifically, it seems that they have just about every Tampa Bay beer that's canned. Even the coffee bean selection is plentiful. 

Of course it's not the cheapest place to buy groceries, but the quality of inventory is second to none. I would like a group-hug with the founder of Whole Foods, the person who decided to bring this location to Carrollwood, and the person in charge of ordering the products for this location. You are all saints.

I believe I have only been here three times, which makes it very exciting because I still feel like I'll be discovering several new things with every visit.

Why 5 stars? Because this is more science than food.

   ---   ---   ---

I'm convinced that instead of a kitchen in the back of Rooster & the Till, there's actually a science lab, where experiments of the human tongue are constantly being performed.

I admit, I was skeptical of the microscopic portions here, but I've been twice, and left content each time. That being said, R&T is undoubtedly more expensive than Bern's, if you plan on eating something close to a full meal. (I'm obviously not including the potential for massive, expensive wine consumption at Bern's.) But my two tickets tallied to $100 and $132 for a normal, human-sized amount of food.

You don't leave here without trying two things:

-The Oysters - Assuming they have the Old Bay ice. It's the most genius idea I've ever seen. It's so amazing that I feel like it's a craze that will soon be sweeping America.

-Pork Belly - Probably the most laughable portion I've seen. The amusing part is that they bring it out on a plate that would hold an entire cheesecake. But, I tell you this... it's incredible and worth every cent of the $11 it costs.

-I'd add a third item to the must-have list, but the dessert menu constantly changes. But for both of my visits, I was lucky enough to have some sort of salted caramel parfait with orange Hooker tea, and a whole bunch of other items straight from the pearly gates. 

While enjoying many of the items at R&T, I find myself thinking the same thing, "I'm feeling parts of my tongue that I didn't know existed."

One of the best foodie experiences in Tampa Bay, and I'm oh-so-lucky to have it in my backyard. My love for Seminole Heights grows more and more every day. 

And as a bonus, I think the decor is as awesome as the food. I want my house to look like R&T.

Why 5 stars? Because this might be the best pizza in Tampa Bay.

   ---   ---   ---

This was one of my favorite dining experiences of 2017 so far. Safety Harbor isn't the most convenient 'hood for us to visit, but we'd wanted to try this place for quite some time. The wife didn't want to make the drive, but I convinced her that it would be fun because we'd be able to listen to the newest episode of "Missing Richard Simmons" on the ride over. That worked, and now Richard can say he's affected another person's life in a positive way.

I've had mixed reactions from other wood-fired pizza spots, but those places are mostly chains: Anthony's, Grimaldi's, etc. This one has the owner working the oven himself, or at least he was during our visit. The only reason I know this is because there was a photo of him in the restaurant that was either the guy working the oven, or someone who looked damn-near like him.

And this was no Anthony's. It seemed to taste better with every bite. I was in absolute euphoria the entire time. I ordered the Special #2, which I'm not sure how often it appears on the menu in this form. It had meatballs, mushrooms, ricotta and maybe another item or two. It was very thin, so I ended up folding it in half, which made it like a little heavenly pizza sandwich. 

To drink, I had a Graffiti Orange, which comes from nearby 7th Sun in Dunedin. They had maybe five beers available - all local. My wife also ordered something called Garlic Schoop, which it's basically a garlic dip for your crust. This is the only thing I regret about my experience, but it was punch-you-in-the-face garlic. It tasted fine... very strong, but fine. But it lingered on my tongue all the way until breakfast the next morning. I don't recommend it, unless you LOVE garlic.

We sat outside, which added to the loveliness of the experience. It was a beautiful Florida evening in mid-March, and just another reminder of why we are so luck to live here. While we waited for our food, we browsed other nearby eateries on Yelp, and came to discover that we really need to spend a lot of time in Safety Harbor. What an amazing little pocket of Tampa Bay, that apparently has become quite the restaurant haven!

Why 5 stars?  Because this isn't your grandmother's Chinese food.  That's right, I went cliche in the opener.

   ---   ---   ---

One thing I've always said about Chinese Food - basically no matter where you go, it's the exact same thing.  It's hard to get REALLY good or REALLY bad chinese food.  You will usually get a solid 3.5-4/5 star meal if you're a fan of something standard like Beef Lo Mein.

Well, the Beef Lo Mein from Yummy House is better at Yummy House.  I don't know how they have defied physics to create a better tasting dish than the rest of the world.

I don't know how they did it, but they've changed Chinese food forever for me...and hopefully the rest of the world.

Why 4 stars? Because the french toast and fried chicken alone was worth the visit.

   ---   ---   ---

I've had 7th + Grove on my to-do list for a while now and was finally able to stop in for brunch. I used to live in Ybor and really love seeing new businesses flourish here and add to the awesomeness of this unique neighborhood.

I'm not totally sure what this building was before it became 7th + Grove, but they did an excellent job at giving it a unique character. The decor is all quite lovely.

We started off with the Love Galore, which was basically three mac-n-cheese stuffed fritters. While the ingredients had us thinking that this might be spicy, it actually had a decent amount of sweetness to it. 4-stars.

My wife and I split two entrees, but technically my dish was the Everyday People aka Shrimp & Grits. This was not a bad rendition of shrimp & grits but not my favorite either. I'd give it 4 stars, but rounding down to 3.5 because of a pet peeve of mine - leaving the tails on the shrimp in the dish. This forces me to either cut the tails off and miss out on part of the meat or stick my hand in my food and make a mess while peeling them off. I've never understood why restaurants don't remove the tails beforehand. 3.5 stars.

My wife's entree was the fried chicken and french toast. This was some of the best fried chicken either of us have ever had. We were marveling at how it's even possible to produce chicken that's so juicy it almost doesn't feels like we're dreaming. I've only had chicken and waffles, but french toast is equally as amazing as an accompaniment. I can't see ever returning to 7th + Grove for brunch and not ordering this. 5-stars.

The service was friendly but a bit slow, which is similar to what I read in some other reviews.

Welcome to Ybor, 7th + Gove - keep up the good work!

Why 5 stars? Because freaking General Tso's Pizza!

   ---   ---   ---

Mei's has been on my to-do list for an embarrassingly long time. I was told years ago that they have General Tso's Pizza, which combines two things that I love deeply, all into one cuisine. I don't live that far away from Mei's, so I'm really not sure why it took me so long to come here, but I finally did, and my God, was it as amazing as I hoped it would be.

The area around Mei's isn't the best, but don't let that scare you away. Trust that hundreds of people come here to eat every day without incident. But you know what they do get when they come here? Happiness.

If you like General Tso's Chicken and you like pizza, you will undoubtedly love this combination. But the best part might not even be the chicken or the sauce - the dough is absolutely wonderful. I want it on every pizza that I have for the rest of my life. It's so soft and addicting. I don't know what they do here, but future pizza restaurant owners should take note.

My wife wanted to try something else on the menu, so she went with the pork chop rice. Neither of us loved it - the pork had kind of an interesting, but strange flavor to it. It was all kind of dry, as well.

But you're not coming here for the pork chop rice. You're coming here for one of the most unique things you can ever find on any restaurant menu. Don't be like me and put off your visit to Mei's. Expedite it to the top of your to-do list and share the gospel of this phenomenon!

Why 5 stars? Because this is some of the best Italian food I've ever had.

   ---   ---   ---

I'm so happy to have discovered Da Sesto. It was an accident really, but it turned out really well for me (and other Yelpers.)

We had a couple Italian vendors on board for our annual Yelper Party back in May, until in the same day, both of the backed out. I didn't really know who else to ask, so I went to Yelp and looked for Italian restaurants that had good reviews.

Da Sesto had phenomenal ratings, so I just went to his website and sent him a generic email from the contact page. Lucky for me, Sesto responded quickly.

He killed it at the Yelper Party, and then killed it again at our recent Elite event. But in between those two, I decided to pop in and see what all the fuss was about. 

FUSS = WORTHY

I have been disappointed with Italian food more than I've been happy with it over time, but Da Sesto just simply serves amazing food.

My go-to is lobster ravioli, and I was not disappointed. My girlfriend had the Capelli D'angelo with scallops It was also wonderful.

Da Sesto is easily my favorite restaurant in Pinellas County.

Why 5 stars? Because I am so happy I came here.

   ---   ---   ---

I recently saw Viet Kitchen pop up on a search for new businesses in the area and was excited to check them out. It's already difficult enough to open a small restaurant - I can't imagine how trying it must have been to do so during a pandemic. But you would have never known of any high stress levels from the people I interacted with in here - they were so incredibly nice and lovely. And the world needs nice and lovely more than ever right now.

My first two attempts to call in a pickup order were met with a recording that said the number does not have a voicemail setup. It didn't even ring, so I assumed the number posted online wasn't correct and just got in the car to place my order in person. But I called one more time on my drive over and it rang + someone picked up. I guess that means they just don't have call waiting? So don't get discouraged if that happens to you - call back in a few minutes!

But because my call was placed when I was already en route, I arrived before everything was ready. While sitting and waiting for my food, two different people came to check on me to make sure I didn't mind waiting. The second lady brought me a cup of ice water. There was just a vibe of generosity and sweetness here that went above and beyond normal cordial behavior. Again, maybe it was more palpable because we're living in tense times as I write this. But either way, they left an impression on me.

As for the food, we ordered a few things:

-Viet Kitchen Noodle Special: 4-stars. I enjoyed this, but would have liked it more if the noodles had been warmed up a bit. Maybe colder noodles are typical on this type of dish, but I was just kind of surprised by that. The meat and egg roll bits were great!

-Pork Fried Rice: 4.5 stars. The wife added a little bit of soy sauce, which made it even better. The pork was perfect. I preferred this to my dish.

-Viet Chicken Wings: 5-stars. The best thing we ordered. I would happily order an entree version of this with rice if it were available. The crispy exterior is what dreams are made of.

-Pina Colada Boba Slush: 4.5 stars. I've had a lot of boba in my life, but never pina colada. I loved it. Their drink menu is a bit more unique than most - I'd love to work my way through the menu over time because there are a lot of options that look great.

-Vietnamese Iced Coffee: 5-stars. I don't know what they put in here and I don't care. It's amazingly tasty (even black) and gave me a very needed caffeine rush, even after eating all of this heavy food. I wish I could have this every day.

I live nearby so I will definitely be back - so happy to have this option so close!

Why 5 stars? Because these are probably the best wings in Tampa Bay.

   ---   ---   ---

There's really no other way to say it: the wings are bad ass.

They're giant. They're flavorful. They're juicey. They're tender on the inside. They're crispy on the outside. Everything you would imagine when you close your eyes and imagine the ideal wings, these are that. Don't consider coming here without trying them. We ordered 12. Half were Korean BBQ and have were Korean Dry Rub. We loved both. The Dry Rub came with some kind of sauce for dipping - I'm not sure what it was, but I enjoyed that too.

We ordered way too much food for two people, but we wanted to try a lot of things. On top of the wings, we also went with the bulgogi and the kimchi fried rice. The bulgogi was great. The fried rice was fine, but if I could go back in time, I would have opted for the chicken sandwich instead. That would have added to an already over-hearty meal, but the wings were so good that they left me wanting more chicken. Again, not because I needed to eat more, but because I was addicted to the deliciousness.

I used to live incredibly close by when I had a house in Seminole Heights. I couldn't even remember what used to be here, but when looking at Google Street View from 2019 - surprise: it was an old car mechanic shop! They did an incredible job with the interior and exterior of this building - as soon as I walked in, I thought it reminded me of Hawkers in St. Pete. If I still lived in the area, I would definitely have Gangchu strongly in my cheat day rotation.

Why 5 stars? Because of delicious food and friendly people.

   ---   ---   ---

I live so close to Cool Mo's that I'm embarrassed it took me so long to visit. My wife seemed to be going every Saturday, but it wasn't in the cards for me to join her until recently, when we took a super early flight home and were in desperate need for caffeine. 

In addition to my delicious cafe con leche, I ordered the Mo's Huevos, which is basically Cuban bread, eggs and cheese - I also added in some ham. It was the perfect accompaniment with my coffee. We also ordered a cheese and guava empanada, which came with tons of guava inside. My wife went with the simple cuban toast and cheese, which always hits the spot.

As we were leaving, the guy cooking in the back offered us a couple beignets on the house! This was super nice, and amazingly convenient because we were thinking about ordering some anyway. We'll have to do so next time because only getting to try one, definitely got me excited for more!

But what really makes Cool Mo's special is how incredibly nice the people are. I'm going to assume that this man and woman were the owners because my wife said that it's the same people every time she's gone in. They were absolutely lovely, and I'm not just saying that because of the free beignets :) After just leaving our families over Christmas, they made us instantly feel like it was Christmas all over again. A man in military garb came in while we were eating and it started a whole conversation between him and the other two couples in the restaurant. It really felt like such a tight knit family during our short time here.

The people of Cool Mo's are easy to root for, and I look forward to seeing them continue to grow!

Why 5 stars?  Because this was the definition of a 5-star experience.

   ---   ---   ---

Roy's....what was once a place I drove by without a second glance, is now one of my favorite restaurants in the Bay Area.  I sampled all kinds of goodness during my visit, but here are my highlights:

-First of all, nothing is bad.  Everything ranges from good to amazing.

-The good: All of the Sushi and Dim Sum

-The amazing: The scallops, the Butterfish and the Pineapple Upside Down Cake

The scallops were some of the best I've ever had!  So buttery...so tender...and cooked to perfection!

The scallops did not hog all of the butter in the restaurant, because the Butterfish lived up to its name.  That may have been the best piece of fish I've ever had.

The Pineapple Upside Down Cake was absolutely killer.  I was so stuffed after dinner, but as they say, there's always room for dessert.

Roy's, you've earned yourself a new fan.  Bravo.            *

Why 4 stars? Because I probably owed them a more recent visit.

   ---   ---   ---

I don't like to be one of the few people who outwardly opposes a local favorite. That's been my stance on Wright's for a while. But after seeing them win the Yelpie this year for Best Sandwich in Tampa Bay, I felt like it was time to re-visit.

The verdict? They wouldn't be on my short list of the Best Sandwich Award, but my recent experience was better than my first couple. I ordered the Monte Cristo, and it was very solid. It was nothing like the traditional, dessert-y Monte Cristo, but I really enjoyed it. It was almost more like a reuben. My fiance had the grilled cheese, which had some pretty intense cheese. I didn't like that one as much as my own sandwich, but if you like sharp cheddar, you'll love it.

We also enjoyed a slice of butterscotch pie for dessert, and it was absolutely as ridiculously delicious as it sounds. Even when I gave Wright's a 3-star reviews for their sandwiches, there's no denying that their desserts are Hall of Fame worthy.

Why 5 stars? Because I can't believe it took me so long to visit this Carrollwood gem.

   ---   ---   ---

I feel like I've pretty much driven on just about every major road in Tampa Bay, but somehow this was my first time ever finding myself in this area, despite it being very close to my house. I've been through Original Carrollwood several times, but this little pocket near North Amenia Avenue was like a brand new world for me. I guess I always assumed that it was mostly residential back here, but who knew that Gino's was rocking this spot?!

While it took me a long time to make it over here, it definitely will not take me nearly as long for visit #2. Gino's won us over right away.

The restaurant is divided in half - the right side requires you to be sat by the host, while the left side is open seating. We saw an empty table on the left side as we walked in, so we quickly snagged that as soon as we found out what the ground rules were.

While we waited for our entrees, we were served bread and salad. Both of these were absolute home runs. The salad had some amazing dressing on it that I wanted to bathe in. And the bread was smothered in butter and garlic. The bad thing is that the garlic stuck with me for the remainder of the evening, but it was ridiculously tasty going down.

My wife ordered the Sampler #2 - Lasagna, Chicken Parm and Linguine Alfredo... what a great idea to offer basically a "flight" of entrees! It's so painstaking to choose what to order at Italian restaurants, so this was really a no brainer for one of us to try.

I had my heart set on the chicken parm sandwich, but unfortunately found out that it was just on the lunch menu. While I was tempted to just order the chicken parm entree, because the wife had it in her sampler, I opted for the smoked gouda gnocchi with sirloin. While I loved the gnocchi and enjoyed the beef, I'm not sure that these two things made the greatest pairing. I'd go with the chicken next time. 

This was a fun and memorable meal - one that we will definitely have to try to repeat in the future!

Why 2 stars? Because it was what I thought it was.

   ---   ---   ---

I believe in second chances, and I hate giving businesses poor reviews. These are the reasons I recently visited Tijuana Flats, after years of labeling them as one of the worst and most overrated restaurants that I've ever been to. 

I also believe in constructive criticism, and phrasing things in a way that do not offend those involved... but I'm not going to sugar coat this one - I've referred to Tijuana Flats as the Alpo of Mexican food. I know Mexican food is somewhat hard to come by in the Bay Area, but you can do (MUCH) better than TF.

So if I hated it that much, why did I return? Well, in addition to the reasons I listed above, one Drew Garabo of 102.5 FM, the Bone, has showered TJ's with praise over the years. And across the many times I've been fortunate enough to be on his radio program, we've shared many of our favorite restaurants with each other. It's uncanny how our opinions on things are almost universally identical. Tijuana Flats is basically the only place we don't see eye to eye on.

I brought this up with him on the Yelp Tampa Bay Podcast (shameless plug: search Yelp Tampa Bay on iTunes or anywhere you listen to podcasts) and vowed to return to TJ's, if he provided me an exact list of what to order. His suggestions:

-Carnitas Burrito... or if I'm going all-out with unhealthiness, the chimichanga. And smother it in queso.

Fortunately, you can get mini versions of the burrito and chimichanga under the "2 for $10" menu. Done! I then returned to the table, where my fiance had chips and queso already waiting for me.

As I chowed down on the chips and queso, I was excited and hopeful that my opinion would be changed today. After all, I love Mexican food and this location is only a couple of miles from my house. How great would it be if I had another nearby place to add to the list? And the chips/queso certainly was a great first step in the right direction - I loved the seasoning on the chips, and the queso was perfect.

But then my order was delivered to the table... and it was just as I remembered.

---I don't eat at fast food places like McDonald's, because I feel like the meat is so disgusting, that it makes me feel ill. A burger may cost $2.99, but it also tastes like that's how much it's worth. 

This is how I feel about the meat at Tijuana Flats. It just tastes... off. And when I say off, I mean it's gross. It actually makes my appetite vanish.

I ended up ordering Steak for my chimichanga, and while the meat was a little better, the combination of veggies and over-loaded sour cream did not have a good taste. I liked the texture of the lightly fried burrito, but that's where it ended.

I tried a few bites of my fiance's double cheesy tacos. The first couple of bites were much better than anything on my plate... but then the next couple of bites tasted, again, "off." Like the vegetables were either stale or just didn't combine very well together.

We left feeling disgusting/bloated, without even eating half of our food. This will absolutely be my last visit to Tijuana Flats, for the rest of my life. 

Again, I hate to kill a small business, but my message to all patrons of TJ's: this is a horrific version of what Mexican food should be. Any alternative is a better one!

Why 5 stars? Because this is some of the best deep dish I've ever had.

   ---   ---   ---

My wife and I are huge fans of Chicago Deep Dish, but it's not something you can find at too many places in Tampa Bay. We have a go-to place (Paul's in Clearwater) but Tikanis proved to be pretty awesome in its own right.

I must have bookmarked Tikanis at least a year and a half ago, but I just don't make it out to this part of St. Pete very often. After many times where I considered making the journey out here, it finally happened!

The funny thing is that I had actually just been in Chicago the three days prior to my visit, but my wife was super jealous of my food photos and wanted to get some Chicago in her life when I came home. This pizza turned out better than what I had up there, actually! The crust was a tad crispier than I'm used to with deep dish, which made it easier to eat.

We also opted for the fried mushrooms, which were solid, but I'd probably opt for an alternative next time. Garlic knots, maybe?

There were a lot of beers on tap, but there were plenty of the Bud/Miller/Coors type products of the world with a few Florida beers mixed in.

I'd definitely come back here again if I find myself in this part of town! If you do opt to order the deep dish, definitely call in the order ahead of time, even if you're dining in because it takes an hour to make!

Why 5 stars? Because this is some of the better BBQ I've had in Tampa Bay.

   ---   ---   ---

With the Heights Public Market just recently opening, it's understandable that things are going to be a bit crazy for the vendors in the beginning. We visited opening night and it wasn't crowded at all, but our 2nd trip was on the weekend and was a different story. There were more than a dozen people hovering around Butcher 'n' Barbeque and it was tough to tell who was waiting to order, who was waiting for their food and who was just browsing the menu. Some stanchions or more signage would definitely be helpful! And it's certainly not the cheapest BBQ you'll find around town.

But you know what? That's literally "the price" you pay for the convenience of finding more than a dozen food vendors all in one place. And I'm sure the kinks will be worked out, once the vendors and the market get accustomed to the crowds.

In the meantime, I have to say that we really enjoyed the food! We ordered brisket and pulled pork, mac-n-cheese and cucumber salad. The brisket was the star of the show in terms of the meat, and the sides were really tasty. I also loved the variety of BBQ sauce that was offered, though I wish we were given a bit more of it. The cartridge with one squirt of sauce left a bit to be desired.

You can also order meat from here to take home and cook yourself. While I don't know if I'd realistically see myself driving here just to buy some steaks, I could definitely envision picking up some meat for the grill if I'm already here.

I want to make the rounds to every market vendor, but Butcher 'n' Barbeque will definitely be very high on my list for places to check out again!

Why 4 stars? Because our 2nd visit was distinctly different than the first.

   ---   ---   ---

After my first trip to Shelly's, I was convinced that I'd just discovered some of the best pancakes that Tampa Bay has to offer. I absolutely loved everything I ate, but the highlight of the experience was Shelly's Pancakes, which were out of this world. I've thought about them ever since I was lucky enough to be in their presence.

But unfortunately, visit #2 to Shelly's made it seem like there were some definite changes made in the kitchen since visit #1.

My wife and I shared a Western Omelet combo with eggs and bacon, as well as the aforementioned Shelly's Pancakes. The eggs and bacon just looked... for lack of a kinder word... pathetic. The eggs tasted fine, but were super thin and just looked like they were mass-produced at some kind of low-end cafeteria. The bacon was sadly even worse on both fronts. It looked and tasted like it wasn't even real bacon that was cooked in a microwave.

The western omelet was similar to the scrambled eggs - tasted fine, but just looked unappealing. The one saving grace of our meal were the home fries which were unbelievably delicious! I wish I could have those with every breakfast for the rest of my life!

But onto the main event: Shelly's Pancakes. Last time, these were so wonderful that I wanted to get up and dance between bites. This time? Run-of-the-mill pancakes with fruit on them. I was so bummed!

But because my experience was so epic on the first time around, and everyone in here has been incredibly friendly during both of our visits, I'm rounding up and going with a 4-star review. According to Shelly's expert, Chris W, he's had many 5-star experiences here, so I'm hoping that we just caught them on a weird day where the primary cook was sick, or something along those lines.

Why 4 stars? Because this is a great local brewery.

   ---   ---   ---

I don't make it out to Northern Pinellas County much, but I feel like Dunedin is easily my favorite town in that part of the Bay Area. I haven't spent a lot of time in the area... but what I have seen I've really enjoyed.

7th Sun has some really unique flavored beers like graffiti orange (creamsicle), kiwi cherry coconut, and mango black peppercorn really set it apart from the competition. It's small, quant, and cool with friendly people working there.

Overall, I sold and will definitely check them out again!

Why 3 stars? Because it was better than most, but fried food is still fried food.

   ---   ---   ---

I want to write this with two caveats:

-I'm not putting Big Ray's in the same class with the hot garbage that they serve at a place like Long John Silver's.

-I realize that Big Ray's serves fish that isn't fried.

That being said, this was my experience:

I ordered a fried grouper sandwich and onion rings. The onion rings tasted significantly better than most, as they were going down. It's once they got to the bottom of the my stomach that the trouble began. Most food goes down there, and just starts digesting. But many fried foods will just sit. And sit. And not digest. And sit some more. Even hours later, I was still filled with regret. Literally.

The fried grouper sandwich had a very odd flavor, and I'm not even talking about the fried portion. The very middle of the fish just tasted incredibly different than it should. I'm not sure how to exactly describe it, but it wasn't normal. 

I hate writing this review. I'd wanted to come here for quite a while, and based on the other reviews, I feel like I caught them on a bad day, and/or, ordered the wrong things. But something was definitely off with that grouper, and I do want to offer my honest feedback.

I will definitely be back, and I'll go the grilled or blackened route next time

Why 5 stars? Because it's a shame it took me so long to come here.

   ---   ---   ---

After restaurants reopened, I've made a concentrated effort to visit places that I've had bookmarked for years and just never went to for some reason. 1200 Chophouse was the final local bucket list spot to check off. Don't get me wrong, there are still places I want to visit, but I'm talking about only the top, top tier of restaurants that I've really always wanted to check off. Other new places will open, but as of now, I feel like I've pretty much been everywhere. And I saved a good one for "last".

This time around, Anna M made sure to set her alarm properly, so we arrived a few minutes before 5pm on a Saturday when doors open. We were the 2nd people in line, but by 5:00 on the dot, there were several other customers ready to enter. After only a few minutes of being seated, pretty much every table was occupied. We arrived at 5p because I have a young child at home and I wanted to help with bedtime, but I'm glad we came when we did, because otherwise we would have been in quite the wait. When we walked out around 6:30p, there were many people waiting - some sitting on the couches outside near the road.

This part of my review is not an indictment of 1200 Chophouse - they are simply following the rules. The rules are 10/10 silly. You must have a mask on inside, unless you're seated at the table. The dining room is not large at all - it was about 8-12 feet from the doorway to our table and another 8-12 feet from our table to the bathroom. So we put on our masks, took about 6 steps, sat down at our table and talked/ate/drank for 90 minutes with no mask on - like every other patron. When I got up to the bathroom, I had my mask on for the 6 steps in route to the single person toilet room. Again, mask on for the 6 steps back to the table. And finally, mask on for the 6 steps out the door. At one point, a server asked a man to put his mask on. The man said, "what about all of these people?" The server said, "they are seated and dining. So he literally grabbed the bar chair that was within arms reach and sat down. Standing? Mask needed. Sitting down, 10 inches to the left? No mask necessary. Again - nothing against 1200 Chophouse, they don't want to get shut down. But the rules themselves? It's just good science.

Onto the food...

We started off with steak frites and bacon wrapped scallops. The scallops were the highlight of the evening. The smokiness of the bacon complemented the bacon perfectly - I wish I could eat these every day. The streak frites were delicious and the sauce was ideal, but the bacon wrapped scallops stole the show.

Anna and I shared the prime bone-in ribeye special and upgraded to oscar style. This worked out well, as they evenly split the plate for us and removed the bone, but still brought it out for us. We both enjoyed the steak very much. The only gripe I had is that oscar style kind of overwhelmed the flavor of each bite and took away from the natural steak flavor. If I were to return, I'd maybe do a traditional surf and turf where the seafood is separated from the steak.

The bread and honey butter that came with it was amazing and the salads were great too. I opted for a loaded baked potato as my side dish, which came with big clumps of butter and sour cream to add at my leisure. I added. A lot.

I'd definitely love to come back again, especially for future special occasions. This was definitely one of my favorite dining experiences in the St. Pete Beach area!

Why 4 stars? Because I was pleasantly surprised with my first trip ever to Waffle House!

   ---   ---   ---

Let me start off by airing out a pet peeve: I don't understand why people review huge, national chain businesses. I have to tell you - every single Starbucks is the same place. No person in the history of Earth has ever craved a trip to McDonald's, but thought, "let me check the Yelp reviews first." 

And penning this statement, "ugh, the customer service is so awful at *THIS* Taco Bell," translates to: "the 19 year olds working on the particular Friday night I visited did not possess as much courtesy as the 19 year olds working at the other location I visited 17 days prior." 

That being said, Waffle House is different, at least for me. For the almost 31 years I've been on this Earth, I did not visit a Waffle House until July 4, 2015. Because I'm hilarious, I decided that my first visit should be on the night I got engaged. But because of those odd circumstances, I feel like my experience should be documented. Plus, Waffle House is like the PBR of diners, right? It was so un-cool, that it became cool?

The overall summary? I've heard that Waffle House is a disgusting place that's only tolerable at 3am when you're hammered. I must disagree with that narrative. I was damn-near tempted to rate Waffle House 5-stars. Everything was phenomenal, and of course, c-h-e-a-p!

-I never heard the phrase, "scattered, smothered, and covered" before, but you better believe I won't forget it. That's how you order hash browns at Waffle House, if you're cool. They were top notch! 

-And of course, I had to order a freaking waffle, while I'm at Waffle House. I went with the pecan, and it was great. They even have the Waffle House logo built in to the griddle so that the the logo is actually on your waffle. Branding, yo!

-Every surface in the restaurant felt like it had at least a 3% level of stickiness. Years of syrup molecules just floating through the air will do that to ya. 

-And finally, the people watching was about as you'd expect. Between the employees and fellow patrons, we definitely paid for dinner and a show. I'd have a tough time choosing between the meal and the entertainment if I was only able to pick one.

My pledge to you, the Yelp community, is that this will be the only time I ever review a Waffle House. If I ever return to another Waffle House, it'll be my little secret.

Why 5 stars? Because this is my new all-time favorite breakfast.

   ---   ---   ---

Surrey's Cafe goes in to my hall of fame for one of the best restaurants I have ever been to. I hate to over-hype things, but it's really hard to hold back with this place. It's just on another level of jaw-dropping.

I wanted to enjoy some shrimp and grits during my visit to NOLA, and thought that this was the perfect place to try it. One of my friend's ordered french toast, and I was kind of surprised by that, as it seemed like there were so many other better choices.

Then his french toast came out and I tried a bite.

The next thing I knew... I was on the ground in an orgasmic coma. 

PERFECT TASTING FOOD LIKE JESUS HIMSELF MADE IT FOR ME?!?!

I feel like this french toast could cure any disease, bring peace to the middle east, and solve the U.S. debt crisis. It could fix the the class war in San Francisco, stop all natural disasters, and make puppies potty trained instantly.

And here's the thing: if it weren't for the french toast, the shrimp and grits would have scored Surrey's a 5-star rating on its own. It was absolutely unbelievable, and it's a shame that it became so overshadowed by the item created by none other than the son of God.

After finishing my shrimp and grits, I absolutely had to order a french toast for myself. There was no way around it. I ate two breakfasts, and I could have had another.

I almost committed the cardinal sin of vacationing in a new area, and considered going back to Surrey's the next morning for seconds. I didn't actually do it, but I think it's the first time I've ever been tempted.

If you go to New Orleans after reading this review, and DON'T order the french toast at Surrey's, I will consider it a personal insult to my family.
