Why 5 stars?  Because if you look on my profile, this is listed as my least meal on Earth.  It's hard to top that praise.

   ---   ---   ---

Samurai Blue...my favorite restaurant on the planet, and my first review on Yelp after being a prominent lurker for 2 years.

Here is what you need to know:

1) The greatest thing I have ever tasted in my life:

Tempura Lobster Roll - Order, and everything you thought you knew is changed.

2) The second greatest thing I have ever tasted in my life:

Blue Crab Rangoon - The best appetizer ever created.  The only bad thing about it is that there are only four little rangoons to go around.

3) The thing that is almost as good as the best two things in the world:

Blue Moon Roll - Usually the Tempura Lobster and Blue Moon rolls are ranked #1-2 amongst my friends on the all-time list.  It's probably a 50/50 ratio for which one is preferred, but this is my personal ranking.

4)  Live, breathe...and EAT the back side of the sushi menu:

Samurai Blue incorporates a lot of crazy sauces on the more expensive (but well worth it) back-side of the sushi menu.  The regular sushi, while tasty, is nothing out of the ordinary.


Aside from the food, the building itself is amazing.  I believe it is an old bank building.  From your table, the roof towers about 4 stories high above you.  It's very industrial, yet can be a romantic setting or just a place to take a friend for the best sushi of his/her life.

This is a default stop for anyone coming to town to visit- when my Mom comes to town, she wants to eat here every meal.  And my Mom's opinion is pretty important.

Why 5 stars? Because if you're looking for hearty, you've come to the right place.

   ---   ---   ---

My efforts to enjoy newer spots in the DTSP continue with the bier boutique. This one is technically a pinch outside of Downtown, right off of Round Lake (least creative Lake name ever). It reminds me of a small town because it's mostly more residential here, but with a few businesses sprinkled in. The restaurant itself is on the ground floor of what looks to be an apartment building. The interior is very new and trendy, but not cliche. I dig the vibe!

We couldn't say no to the beer candied bacon, which turned out to be just as delicious as it sounds. I can't endorse coming here and not enjoying this. The first couple of bites led me to think,"wow... this is intense" followed by wife saying, "wow... this is intense," because we finish each other's thoughts at this point. But after the initial intensity became normalized, I savored every bite of this and said, "how amazing would it be if someone who had never tried bacon, took a bite of this. Their world would be forever changed." I'm full of profound observations when you put me near a place like Round Lake.

For my meal, I opted for the Thurman Merman burger and the loaded tater tots. I felt like I shortened my life by 2.5 years between this and the bacon, but it was worth it. My advice to anyone who feels like they are constantly starving and looking to put free themselves of that feeling - go to the bier boutique and order all of these things. You will be the opposite of hungry for a prolonged amount of time. Oh, and also, it's all quite delicious.

We finished off with the salted caramel shortbread, which fit perfectly into everything else we had: very rich, very hearty, very tasty. 

I dig what these folks are doing and will definitely be rooting for others to discover that the good eats of St. Pete extend beyond Downtown!

Why 5 stars? Because I'm so ridiculously lucky that this opened in my neighborhood.

   ---   ---   ---

I've heard of the MSBC lore for quite some time now - their original location has even shown up on Yelp's Top 100 Restaurants in the country lists over the years. I was finally able to visit one when they opened in St. Pete, but I've been stalking this location for months. If I really wanted to, I could walk to this location, which is less than a mile and a half from my front door. Carrollwood isn't total suburbia, but we usually don't get things *this* cool. My lucky stars are counted!

I was quite tempted to visit on opening day, as they had some pretty lucrative prizes for the first group of customers to walk through the doors, but me and a 6:30am don't get a long very well, so I settled for day #2. 

My wife and I plan on making our way through most of the menu, so we wanted to try a couple of different things than we had in St. Pete, despite loving our first experience. I went with the Farmer and Mac-n-Cheese, while she ordered a Flip Flop and Hash Brown Cake.

Farmer - Everything I could want in a biscuit. I ordered the Five and Dime the first time around, but I think I liked the Farmer even better, because I prefer Maple Street's syrup over their gravy. This item is almost like chicken and waffles, but instead of waffles, you get a delicious biscuit. 

Mac-n-Cheese - The fact that they sprinkle a few Cheez-Itz on top was kind of strange and unexpected, but this was some damn good mac-n-cheese. Come to think of it, it was honestly some of the better mac that I've had in all of Tampa Bay. It was simple, but ideal.

Flip Flop - Much like the name of this dish, my wife and I flip flop on our opinion on this: she prefers gravy over syrup. I tried a couple bites of this dish, and while I enjoyed it, I would have preferred the syrup/chicken version aka the Bam Yo Yo. However, as a gravy lover, she was in heaven with this dish.

Hash Brown Cake - A solid upgrade from your typical, basic hash browns. I believe these had chives, or something else to give it a very subtle kick, but I really enjoyed whatever it was. Next time, I'll definitely be ordering the super loaded version with gouda, egg and other delights.

Even after visiting today and writing this review, I still can't believe this is right by my house. This parking lot is a bit awkward and Maple Street is located a bit out of view from Dale Mabry, so I hope that the community is sure to support this location. If it weren't for the calorie count, I'd be here every weekend, but I guess I'll have to compromise with a visit every few weeks!

Why 5 stars? Because it's a different type of Mexican food, but we loved it.

   ---   ---   ---

My wife and I are from Houston, so we have an affinity for Tex-Mex style cuisine. This is definitely not that, so I was a little worried that we might not love it, but it turned out to be really great!

Chips & Salsa: 5-stars. These might be the best chips in Tampa Bay. They are seasoned perfectly with just the right amount of thickness. The salsa is a tad on the runny side, but delicious. The only bad thing about these chips is that I didn't want to stop eating them and was practically full by the time our entrees came! 

Mixta: 5-stars. They have a lot of these fruity drink concoctions and they all looked amazing. The mixta is appropriately named because it comes with a bunch of different fruit mixed in. It tastes just as good as it sounds: Papaya, Banana, Cantaloupe, Lime Juice, Passion Fruit and Nectar.

Guacamole: 2-stars. This was really the only thing that missed the mark. It was pretty flavorless guac, to be honest. I would definitely opt for another starter next time.

Steak Burrito: 4-stars. I was hesitant to order a burrito because I've had enough fast casual burritos in my time that I kind of feel like most burritos taste the same. But this was definitely a step up from the Chipotle's of the world. I added the Smoked Ancho Chili Sauce, which the server suggested I put on the side because it has a unique flavor if you're not used to it. I was glad she suggested this because there was a precise amount of this that was ideal in each bite. One time I poured too much and it was kind of overwhelming. 

Crab & Roasted Poblano Enchiladas: 5-stars. Had my wife not ordered this, it's definitely what I would have gone with myself. I stole a few bites and it was just as heavenly as I hoped it would be. The next trip back will definitely consist of me having this all to myself.

Overall, we really enjoyed this experience. Yes, the parking lot is hilariously narrow, but no expense was sparred on the inside of the building. We really even liked the high quality silverware, tables, chairs and plates. 

Seminole Heights strikes again! It must be some sort of city ordinance that every restaurant that opens in this neighborhood must be approved by a board of professional eaters before serving the public.

Why 5 stars? Because this is one of my new favorite coffee shops in TB!

   ---   ---   ---

As soon as Roberto from Blind Tiger told me about the plans for The Lab, I was counting down the days until they opened. A collaborative coffee roastery? Get out of here! These kinds of places make Tampa feel like a big city.

I had a work-related meeting with someone I was meeting for the first time, and there was a lot of loud construction going on outside. This made for unideal meeting circumstances, but guess what? I forgot all about that as soon as my Aeropress arrived. I'd never heard of an Aeropress, and when I got the explanation from the guy behind the counter, I realized it was pointless for me to even ask. I'll explain it for my fellow people who aren't smart like me: it's a complicated way to make coffee, and it's super caffeinated. As I was drinking it, I realize that I was READY TO GO! I thought I was decent with my espresso maker, but that's childs play compared to the Aeropress.

This is definitely a coffee drinker's drink, FYI. If you like whipped cream and caramel on your coffee, then this is not the drink to order. However, the cool thing is, I don't like black coffee, but this was so smooth, it didn't need anything added, IMO. 

The Lab: my new go-to coffee spot!

Why 5 stars? Because it's healthy and delicious.

   ---   ---   ---

I enjoy the ritual of eating out, but I also try to be healthy more often than not. So when I find a place that combines those two things, I'm, as the kids says, "all about that life."

I went with the poke bowl, and my girlfriend ordered the BBQ chicken bowl. I thought mine was solid but hers was absolutely amazing. It comes with corn, beans, onions, cheese, and you can substitute zucchini noodles for rice, which is what she did. Zoodles are God's gift to the human race, when trying to limit those calories, but not sacrifice on taste!

We will definitely be back when we're looking to break up the monotony of our own healthy cooking!

Why 4 stars? Because the coffee was great and the waffles are a nice touch.

  ---   ---   ---

I discovered Cafe Vino Tinto on Yelp a few weeks before I was able to visit, and it was hard to get it out of my mind from the moment I first saw it. Those freaking waffles looked so amazing - especially the guava cheese & coconut. My wife wasn't that thrilled about driving to Safety Harbor for waffles, but I just kept persisting, and eventually wore her down.

As we walked up, I eagle-eyed the menu and pretty quickly my heart dropped. No guava & cheese! The woman working behind the counter (maybe the owner?) mentioned that they change up their menu and that the guava and cheese was taken off a few months ago. This made me super sad, but I couldn't be too upset - the menu literally says that it's seasonal.

Fortunately they still had banana maple pecan, which definitely would have been my next choice. My wife opted for the mixed berries with raspberry and a lemon glaze.

I'm not a huge fan of lemon glaze so I didn't love hers. She liked it more than me, but wasn't smitten enough to finish the plate.

My banana maple pecan waffles were definitely our favorite of the two, but they just didn't quite live up to the hype that I had created in my mind. They were definitely tasty, don't get me wrong, but I was anticipating an extra level of awesomeness.

I definitely loved their coffee, however! I saw a photo on Yelp of an iced coffee with caramel and almond milk - it looked so amazing that I opted to order it, despite the fact that I'd normally choose something else. That photo sold me and it did not let me down! I don't know what they put in their coffee here, but it's pretty amazing. I would definitely come back many times to try out all of their different concoctions, because there were plenty of different options that I would have loved to try.

Bonus: When someone brought us our waffles, they asked if we wanted any water. I said I'd take one, and assumed they would be bringing a cup of tap water... but out came a full-sized bottle! That was a nice, unexpected bonus!

Safety Harbor is such an awesome little town and Cafe Vino Tinto is just another thing that makes it so great!

Why 5 stars? Because I love that the 'Best of Orlando' is now right around the corner from me!

   ---   ---   ---

*****STORY TIME***** (not a review)

I lived in Orlando for about 9 months, a few years ago. This was a pre-Yelp time in my life (it's hard to fathom there ever was such a thing!) I made this weird decision that I was just going to stay in a little 2 mile radius of my apartment, and go out of my way to avoid ever having fun or enjoying myself. What a weirdo.

But the one place I truly did experience and enjoy (due to it being so close to my place) was Jeremiah's. Everybody loved Jeremiah's. I still loved frozen sugar, despite all of my other outward-lameness. It was easily the thing I missed the most about Orlando.

Fast forward a few years, and I've developed a love of 4Rivers from afar. BOOM - 4Rivers opens in Tampa! Fast forward one more year, and BOOM - Jeremiah's opens next door. Right before Jeremiah's opens, BOOM - I move about one mile away.

I now have the best of the 407 in my backyard. Sometimes life throws you a bone :)

*****ACTUAL REVIEW TIME*****

This will be anti-climactic compared to the story above. That's because Jeremiah's is simple, and sometimes simple is better.

I love sugar. Frozen sugar is the best kind of sugar. At Jeremiah's, you can combine about 30 different flavors of frozen sugar ice with ice cream, or you can just take it on its own. Whatever your choice, there is no wrong answer. 

My favorite thing about this particular type of dessert, is that it doesn't go down as heavily as regular ice cream would. Don't get me wrong, I love Coldstone, which is down the street. But it's also an event for my stomach. I can eat Jeremiah's and swim afterward, without even waiting the full, designated 30 minutes.

Why 5 stars? Because I have a new favorite coffee shop in Tampa Bay.

   ---   ---   ---

After only one visit, it's official - this is my favorite coffee shop in the Bay Area. Let us list the reasons for this this high praise:

1) I love nitro cold coffee. They have 4 taps, which is by far, the most I've ever seen at once place.

2) They also serve your more standard Joe fare, if you're a crazy person that dislikes the nitro cold brew.

3) They sell 16 oz growlers of their nitro coffee, which is an ideal size for such a lovely substance. 32 oz growlers are generally going to be overkill, as the coffee can definitely lose its freshness rather quickly. Unless your large growler is to be shared with multiple people, it's going to be tough to consume all of it at its highest quality. If you do consume 32 ounces of this in one sitting, you'll likely be tweaked out enough to either solve Einstein's Theory of Relativity or be arrested. It's not safe!! But long story short, 16 oz = no stale coffee and no arrest record. Everybody wins.

4) There are doughnuts. Delicious, wonderful doughnuts.

5) The owners are great. They both have gigantic ginger beards, hence the namesake, and are not hard to miss.

6) There's something cathartic about being in a bar at 9am, completely uninhibited. (GBC is inside of the Pour House.)

7) I live to support small, local businesses - and this is as small and as local as they come. It's just a couple of guys with corporate jobs who are trying to make it on their own. The good news for all of us: they are masters of their craft.

If you haven't tried nitro coffee before, it's basically like a Guinness, but coffee. It's best when fresh off the tap with all of the foamy goodness. The Cubano was the smoothest and milkiest of the four flavors they had during my visit. Unless your palate requires 10 lbs of cream and sugar in your coffee, the fresh nitro pour needs no additives. Tap-to-mouth is good-to-go.*

*That phrase is patent pending.

Why 5 stars?  Because Argentina is winning my heart.

   ---   ---   ---

I think Argentinian food is now officially my favorite of all-time.  The churrasco....OH THE CHURRASCO!!! 

I will say this, I have had a better Churrasco.  Not much better, but it Renzo's has been topped.  The chimichurri was good, but definitely more oily than I am used to.  I couldn't decide if I liked that more or not.  It was interesting, but a bit too greasy. 

However, the overall experience at Renzo's is more highly superb in many ways:

1) Renzo's service is extremely quick.  I love El Puerto to death, but the food takes painfully long to come out.  Our meal at Renzo's was ready in 1/4th the time.

2) The portions are manageable.  A lot of similar Latin restaurants have portions so large that you end up eating twice what you should.....and then it's sleepy time.  Not that one should complain about "too much food," but I don't have the willpower to put my fork down when something tasty is in front of me.  I need the restaurant to do my thinking for me when it comes to portion control!  

3) Renzo's doubles as a store.  They sell meat, wine and other various items.  I was incredibly excited to be able to purchase myself some Churrasco de Entrana, the seasoning AND the chimichurri that they use at the restaurant!  I was surprised that they were willing to give up their "secret recipe" and sell me all of the ingredients like that.  But regardless, I made myself some churrasco tonight and it was good.  It was not Renzo's, El Puerto or Arco Iris quality, but it was solid.  I would rate my own cooking 3 stars.  Decent flavor, but the server was a real jerk. :)

4) I was too full during my first visit for dessert, but I stopped back in a couple days later and had to try one of their desserts that looked so phenomenal, I hadn't stopped thinking about it since I I first laid my eyes on it about 48 hours prior.  It was called Postre Chaja.  I am happy to report that it tasted every bit as awesome as it looked.  Wow, was in unbelievable!  It's described as vanilla cake, caramel milk, peaches, walnuts and chantilly cream with meringue on top.  

Renzo's is officially on my favorites list!  I drove right past it for 5 years without having any idea what I was missing!

Why 5 stars? Because that brunch of RIDICULOUS.

   ---   ---   ---

The brunch at Oystercatchers had been on bucket list for a stupid amount of time. I recently proposed to my girlfriend, and while I was planning out that weekend, I knew that the OC brunch had to be a part of the festivities.

The verdict? Absolutely worth all of the hype. The only negative was the price of $55 a person. And that's not to say it wasn't worth every penny, but it's just definitely not something you can do every weekend. This is a special occasion destination, for sure.

But let's talk about the components of that brunch, shall we?

-Carving Station
-Pasta Station
-Omelet Station
-Other pasta fixins
-Typical breakfast items: bacon, sausage, benedicts
-Mimosas
-Steak Salads
-Oysters (of course)
-Shrimp
-Giant cakes
-Banana Fosters station
-A table of nothing but various forms of sugars/candies

The service was top notch, and the views are really great. Of course, the food is unbelievable. I've never been to a brunch like this before. It was fairly mind-blowing.

But again, it just can't be done on a regular basis. My bill after tip was $140 for two people that just drank soda. 

So it's easily the best brunch in TB, but you're definitely going to pay for it!

Why 5 stars? Because the pesto with smoked salmon was a religious experience.

   ---   ---   ---

After reading so much about Piccola, I knew that I had to jet it up to the top of my to-do list. Holding a 5-star average is not easy once you get north of 100 reviews, and after one visit, I can definitely see why people love it so much! Not everything about our experience was of the 5-star variety, but the good stuff is so amazing, that I can't help but do what so many others have done, and leave a 5-star rating. But breaking it down item, by item:

Prosciutto E Formaggi: 3-stars. This was a pretty standard anti pasta plate with some different meats and cheeses. One thing that threw me off was the presence of goat cheese, which I have never seen at an Italian restaurant. I know that I'm in the minority, but I despise goat cheese. Just a warning for others out there that feel the same!

Bread: 5-stars. This bread was a bit unique from the typical offering - it had a little bit of firmness/crunchiness to it, which made it quite addicting. It was already buttered, which was nice, and made it me wish that it was more commonly done.

Pesto with smoked salmon: 5-stars. This was possibly the best pasta dish I've had in the U.S. Every bite was more heavenly than the last. Creamy pasta with a perfectly smoked fish flavor - I hope they are serving this in heaven one day, because if not, I might leave and come back to Earth.

***Carbonara with meatball: 3-stars. My wife orderd this, as carbonara is her favorite Italian dish. Unfortunately, it was actually really bland. It was kind of shocking, especially after trying my dish, which was packed heavily with flavor. 

Tiraimisu: 5-stars. The lightiest tiarimisu I've ever had and absolutely delicious. It almost had the texture of a coconut cream pie, in that, it was very airy. While it was different than the norm, I loved it.

Price: 5-stars. $55 after tip for all of that seemed like an incredible deal. Yes, it's BYOW, but we definitely scored a lot of food for $55!

Service: 3-stars. It's always kind of strange to me when someone in the service industry doesn't generally seem to like talking to people. Our server, who was the only person waiting tables in the small dining room, had a couple different instances of seemingly wanting to be anywhere in the world, other than talking to us. 

  The first was when I noticed that they had one appetizer with prosciutto and another appetizer with mozzarella, so I asked if there was any alternate order to combine the two that might be available. She offered me a gruff. "NO" and just starred impatiently waiting for me to request something else.

  Later on, when it came to ordering our entrees, I was torn between a couple different things, I asked if she had a recommendation for what they were known for more, and she just gave me a very annoyed, "oh honey, it's all great." 

  As the night progressed, she seemed to lighten up a bit, and I could see that the dryness of her personality was just sort of her way, it's just not pleasant to ask questions to a person in the service industry, and be met with a confrontational attitude. I don't need a person to charm my socks off - I'm quite content with a person who is just cordial. 

Server issues aside, I loved my meal so much and hope to see Piccola continue to shine!

My experience here was fine. This restaurant is the size of a post stamp, so if you're coming with a large group make sure you make a reservation.

I decided on the tamale entree, with one being pork and one being chicken. The pork was tasty, juicy and spicy, but the chicken was dry and somewhat flavorless. The black beans on the side were fine but the rice was a bit dry as well. I think it would have been better to just order the tamales a la carte for significantly cheaper than getting the entree. The prices here are very steep, most ranging around $15 for things you could get at most other restaurants for about five dollars less. 

If you're in the area I can see this place being convenient, but it's not worth traveling for. It's alright. On a side note, it's byob which I appreciate, and they will provide you with margarita mix if you want. The margaritas other patrons were making looked pretty good, gotta say I was a bit jealous as I drank my beer.

Honestly, I was not impressed by this place. I'd heard good things so I was expecting a typical brewery experience. Unfortunately this place is really only a brewery by default; it's just a restaurant masquerading as a brewery to get a certain demographic in. I wish I'd known that before hand so I could have planned accordingly.

Anyway, I was disappointed in how few beers they had on tap. It seems they will only have five beers on at any given time, and one of the beers happened to be kicked so I only had four to choose from. At least the beer itself was good; they have a sweet potato ale which is extremely unique. It tastes very autumnal in that is has the typical spices found in pumpkin beers, but the sweet potato makes it far sweeter (obviously) and gives it a heavier mouth feel. Their imperial IPA was also decent, very floral and fruity on the nose. However it was kind of forgettable. 

I might have been interested in the food but the prices scared me off. Even for Yardley the prices on food here were obnoxiously high. Plus aside from the pork belly fries, not much of it sounded all that unique or tasty. Perhaps I'm missing a huge piece of the puzzle by not having had the food? Okay, maybe - but for a place that specifically refers to itself as a brewery I come mainly for the beer. Four taps is just not enough. 

It's just not my thing. The atmosphere is stuffy and stuck up, so unlike any other brewery I've ever been to. I would come back, but I'm really not dying to come back unless they add more taps.

I can't believe I haven't reviewed this place yet. It's almost crazy that such a good Thai place exists on little old Brownsville road, but it does. I've never had a bad dish here, and some have blown me away. Their fried garlic offerings are amazing, super savory and made with all fresh ingredients. Their drunken noodles are amongst the best I've ever had. Sure, they're a bit expensive but you get a large portion and the quality of the food can't be beat. I just love this place! No matter what you order you can't go wrong.

I'm on a never ending quest for the world's best tiki bars, and this is one of many in New Orleans. Since this place is so well known, I had high hopes. I wanted to love it, but it fell a little flat for me. The drinks here are fine, but nothing special. They seemed a bit short staffed the night I was there, and the food menu seemed very generic and a bit unappetizing. Aside from the map they have up behind the bar, I wasn't too impressed with their aesthetic either. Oh well. It's not a bad place, it just isn't the best tiki joint around.

Truly a gem in this neck of the woods. Other reviewers say the same thing, but it's very much true.

What can I say that hasn't been said? Not much but I'll try. Their flavored teas (all unsweetened) are the greatest thing. Off the top of my head I can tell you both the blood orange and passion fruit teas are delightful, and you won't miss the sugar or artificial flavors. They have an array of smoothies, and while their smoothies are good, they aren't the stand out menu items in my opinion. If nothing else you absolutely must try their baked goods here. Their key lime tart was possibly the best one I've ever had. Their cakes and brownies are super rich and packed with flavor. It might seem like empty calories, but it's so worth it. 

On top of this they offer a ton of vegetarian and vegan options, and most of their menu is very healthy in general. Whenever I want a guilt free lunch I head on over here. The quality is top notch, the service is attentive, and their new and improved spot is a cute and cozy place to have a snack and relax for a bit.

Do you like dancing? Do you like no cover charge? You'll love this place!

Sure the dance floor is not very big and you have to go upstairs to get there, but it's still a lot of fun. It seems most people stay downstairs, where there is definitely more of a bar feel as opposed to a nightclub scene. This isn't a problem, since it means more room on the dance floor. The downstairs also has a dueling piano trope, so you're never without entertainment here. Drink prices and variety are typical for the area. 

My only real complaint is that the bathrooms are set up in an odd way so that any lines end up blocking the stairs and sometimes even winding down them. It's hard to explain, but let's just say it's annoying to try and break through a line of people to get to the bar. A decent place, I really like it here and plan on coming back.

Ugh, Geno's is the worst. For an outrageous 10 dollars per sandwich you can get a nasty, subpar cheesesteak. Take that ten bucks and go literally anywhere else in the city and you can get two decent cheesesteaks for that price. 10 dollars a pop? You must be kidding me. Even if it is a tourist trap that is an obscene price.

Every time, and I mean EVERY TIME, I get a nasty dry sandwich. Cheesesteaks are supposed to be juicy and greasy, not dry! They can't even melt the cheese properly! When I get a cheesesteak, the cheese better be melted nicely on the meat. They can't even do that right.

Add to this how in-your-face bigoted they are and I am extremely turned off by this place. Pat's across the street is only a 3 star joint, but their food is ten times better than any of of the disgusting products here. Don't even waste your time.

So I have Anthony Bourdain on the TV telling me how great this cheesesteak is, and Anthony Gargano on the radio telling me the same. Honestly, I'm disappointed that men of influence are saying such misleading things. The best cheesesteak in the Philly area? Give me a break.

I admit that I can often get swept up in hype, but for this particular cheesesteak, no hype is warranted. Let's start with the good. The kaiser roll they use seems to be of good quality, and I appreciate them using American cheese. It's rare to find an American cheese cheesesteak, and I think the overly processed dairy product actually compliments the steak. The bad is the actual meat. The way they cut their steak is horrendous. It's just thick like a patty, and extremely chewy and full of gristle. This could be a good sandwich if only their meat was cut differently.

If you want a good kaiser roll cheesesteak please take yourself to McNallly's in Chestnut Hill and order the Schmitter; it's far superior in every way. That being said this place isn't a total loss. The service here is quick and friendly and they do have other things on the menu. But the cheesesteaks are nothing special.

A jazz club in Philly? Is that really something worthwhile? That's what I asked myself before making my way to South, and I can tell you now that yes, it is worth taking a look.

While I'm a sucker for live shows, I'm also not a huge fan of jazz so I wasn't all that pumped. But let me tell you, the band playing that night (Arpeggio Jazz Ensemble) put on a great performance. The cover was seven dollars, which is really not expensive at all for some good entertainment. Apparently almost all of the sets performed here and roughly in the same price range. Keep in mind you won't pay the cover at the door, instead they will tack it on to your bill.

This place is super cute in decor. Clearly they put a lot of thought into the interior design and it pays off; sometimes this place feels like a secret garden with lots of plant life and string lights in the main dining room. If you're going to see a show, you go down into a dimly lit front room, which is reminiscent of a speakeasy.

Bear in mind that the edible goods here are a tad expensive. They have a limited bar menu you can choose from if you're catching a show, most of which is typical Southern fare but will fill you up if you're hungry. On the night I went my group was feeling oysters, but unfortunately they had ran out of oysters, and I'm not sure if that's a common issue. However, I have to hand it to them with the drinks. They offer a lot of Southern inspired cocktails (Sazeracs and Juleps for instance) and despite the higher price (think $13 for a cocktail) they are quite tasty.

I would definitely go back to South and I look forward to it. The ambiance is great and you can support local jazz acts in the process. Great idea for a restaurant.

I set my expectations low since this appears to be a chain in New Orleans. It was a recommendation from an acquaintance, and while I was skeptical it ended up being one of the best recommendations I got.

My meal, the Bam Bam biscuit, was absolutely delicious. The biscuit itself was moist and fluffy, the candied bacon was superb, and even the fried tomato was top notch. My husband got the Migas (almost like a Mexican style omelette) and that too was on point. It had just the right amount of spiciness, and seems like a great was to nurse a hangover. None of their dishes were all that expensive, so it won't break the bank. Come here for breakfast sometime, it's a great little place.

The pizza gets a thumbs up from me.

No, it's not as good as my all time favorite (Gearo's!!) but it actually comes pretty close. I like the texture of their crust and the fact that their sauce is just a little bit sweet. Despite being sauce-on-cheese style they have not burnt my mouth up yet, something I find happens to often with other places. The pizzas could stand to be a larger size, especially for the price, but it's fine.

The only other thing I've had is their mozzarella sticks which were good, no complaints. I guess I have to try more off their menu but their legendary pizza is worth a try.

This restaurant is very touristy but it still has decent  food. I don't think there was a single local dining here on the day I came, so that tells you something. I got a fried catfish po-boy and it was not bad, but not really memorable either. My husband got the crawfish etouffé which was considerably better than my sandwich, so I recommend trying it if you're here. Overall not a terrible place for food, but there's better within walking distance.

First things first - Red Butler is an absolutely amazing beer and they need to make it a staple. I fell in love with it, but sadly it is a Curiosity series (their limited releases) and will be gone shortly. If any of you folks behind the scenes are reading this, please make more! I will drink a lot of it.  For those wondering, it's a wit beer that's aged in red wine barrels, and way better than it sounds.

Anyway, I have to say, I love the little schtick they have going here. Their mascot Growler is oddly adorable despite having three eyes, and the boardwalk theme is sure to keep me sated when I'm nostalgic for summer in the winter months. There's old timey music playing on the radio and a bunch of games to play inside the tap room. They get an A+ for effort on the branding side.

The rest of the beers, you ask? The beers are pretty great too. I've already sung my praises for Red Butler, but its predecessor What the Butler Saw is a solid wit. It's not something I would drink gallons of, but it's good when you're looking for a nice cold pint. The second best beer I had was their saison, which is crisp and clean but also very fragrant with notes of spice, just like a saison should have. Others have already said this but I'll reiterate; Funnel Cake is just a fanciful name, and you won't get any taste of funnel cake, or sweetness out of this brew. I had it on Co2 and couldn't even get any vanilla in the aroma. Though believe me, it's still a good beer, just not a sweet one like the name would lead you to believe. I'm pleased that they chose a cream ale for their flagship as opposed to a pale ale, and it shows they are definitely going for something different. My least favorite beer was Lady #6, which was infused with cucumber and ginger. Honestly it was just a little too herbal for me, though I can see others liking it.

This place went above my expectations. The staff here is friendly and knowledgeable, and the service is great. I really wish they were a bit closer to me, because I would be there all the time.

Holy cow. This place is off the hook. 

Everything, and I mean everything, that I tried here is delicious. I knew that it would be good food based on other Yelp reviews as well as local word of mouth, but frankly I was amazed by the quality. 

I had the unsweetened mixed berry iced tea and could not ask for a more perfect house brewed tea. It was slightly sweet due to being infused with berries, but this was perfectly fine, and the flavors were on point. My group started with the tostones, fried mashed plantains, and they were very tasty and plentiful. One plate was enough to feed a table of four, and it came with their house made guacamole. Their guacamole has a little bit of spice to it, but nothing unbearable. 

Feeling drawn to the Buddha tacos I ordered them and wondered if they would be any good. Now I find it unbelievable that some of the best tacos I've ever had come from a vegetarian joint. I got them served on the blue corn Johnny cakes, and liked that they had crisp edges with a more cake-like interior. The filing my consisted primarily of sweet potatoes, avocado and peanuts. Don't let that deter you, it was a combination that was beyond delicious. I would never think to mix them but it worked! Add a little bit of lime on there and it's even better. These also come with the signature guacamole. 

I also got to sample some of my dining partners' foods, all of which were equally tasty. The ginger ramen is done well, with a nice little kick to the broth. It's true to typical Japanese style ramen while being its own unique recipe. The falafel has an interesting grainy texture (as opposed to a smooth, doughy one) but it works. Last but not least is the Velvet Verde, comprised mainly of spaghetti squash. It had a lot of particular flavors going on but it all pulled together to make a tasty dish. 

I can't wait to come back here! Now I feel like I should try everything on the menu since every dish we got was outstanding. Even if you are not a vegetarian I would still suggest trying this place just once. The food is so good you will not miss the meat.

There's things I both like and dislike about this location. I love their sweet breakfast items, and they're all very unique. I'm not feeling much else about what they serve, and feel like outside of brunch they don't have much to offer. Their coffee isn't great (I feel like coffee often makes or breaks a breakfast spot). The rest of the menu is just fine. I'd say only stop in for breakfast, and make sure to get one of their pancake or waffle options.

I have to agree with other reviewers. This is a good idea with poor execution.

The pros:
-Cheap booze for brunch! Mimosas and Bloody Mary's are only $5.
-The reclining seats are nice and make minimal noise. 
-Theaters themselves seem clean. 
-Our service was good.

The cons:
-The food is absolutely terrible. Worse than your average theater food, honestly. 
-Aside from the aforementioned drinks everything is way overpriced. 
-There isn't much separating this from a regular theater, and now that most other theaters are catching on to selling alcohol it doesn't have that as a sole selling point anymore.

For my husband and I to do brunch and a movie it cost us $74. Tickets were $26 and food was $48 before tip. That's kind of crazy, especially since there's theaters in the area that do matinees for just five dollars a ticket. I would have been just as happy going somewhere like that, since this Movie Tavern isn't a luxury experience or anything. For food my husband ordered pancakes, and these were the saddest looking little pancakes I ever saw; like from a school cafeteria, and he said they were ice cold. I got the breakfast burrito and it was similar in that the ingredients were of low quality. The bacon was full of gristle and the eggs seemed like they were poorly reheated. 

I would come back and get drinks only. The food is a waste of time, which is a shame, because if the food was good this would be a great "one stop shop" for a night out. And, like I said earlier in the review, other theaters are starting to sell booze so it's not like you absolutely have to come here. I was a bit disappointed, but I'm glad I got to experience this place.

I had heard a lot about this place over the years, and was very curious about their pizza museum. How they can call what they have here a museum is beyond me? It's mostly just a small collection of pictures.

The pizza itself was okay. The slices are huge which is a plus, but they're also kind of greasy and very floppy, so they're hard to eat. Also they only offer a few different slice varieties a day (around 4 were being offered when I was there), so keep in mind a lot of topping options won't be available to you. It was fine I guess, this place is more hype than anything.

My husband was adamant that we come here to eat while in New Orleans. He said it was famous, but I had never heard of it. Being up for anything I agreed to go, and was a bit surprised by the huge crowds gathered here on a weekday afternoon.

We split a 'Famous Ferdi special' (around $14) and it was delicious. The slaw they put on the sandwich is what really sells it, giving it a crunchy and tart aftertaste which somehow goes perfectly with all the meat on the sandwich. I'm sad we didn't get to try more! Their menu is fairly large and it all sounds good. I'll be back when I'm in the area again, it deserves its fame.

J'adore Parc!! This is a fabulous restaurant. I wanted a somewhat romantic location for my anniversary dinner and had heard this was a very versatile establishment; I did not regret my choice.

If you're lucky you'll get a window spot that faces Rittenhouse Square (like I did), so you'll get some attractive views of the city. The service we received was wonderful, from the hosts to the bartender to our servers. 

The food is amazing. I got the cassoulet, something I had never tried before, and it was so delicious. If you're not in the know, it's a stew made of three types of meat with beans. Maybe it doesn't sound all that special but it was cooked to perfection and just thinking about it makes my mouth water. It's the Sunday special, so be sure to try if if you're there on a Sunday. My husband really liked his steak au poivre and said it was perfect. I was very pleased with our desserts, which were brought to us in a dazzling display of sparklers, which I greatly appreciated! The creme brûlée was on point, and the baba au rhum was an interesting take on rum cake. 

I will be back in the future and I can see why this is often touted as the best Steven Starr restaurant.

If you're looking for a 'hidden gem' this might be it. It's smaller than some nearby farms but it still has a lot of charm. I've never seen it get overly crowded here, and that's even during the autumn festivities. They have a wide variety of ice cream and treats available to purchase, and a small menagerie of farm animals who live on the premises. Their mini golf is affordable and fun, and once again, I've rarely seen it crowded. I'm glad that this cute little farm has managed to thrive in its location, and it's worth checking out.

When I moved to the area I was downright amazed by the huge crowds that seemed to gather here. Every day this past summer it has been mobbed with people, all spilling out onto the front porch. I figured the treats here must be really tasty.

The ice cream here is good. It's not amazing, it's not 'huge crowd' worthy, but it's good. I like the fact that they have some unique flavors here. For instance I had banana ice cream with chocolate chips and peanut ripple. I've never really seen anything similar elsewhere. They also have vegan ice cream if you're into that.

I would come back but I'm not running back, especially not on a night when they're mobbed out.

Maybe I'm just a big softie, but I love this place! I'm a cat person to begin with so getting to hang out with some furry friends is always a good time. Add in some fun drinks to the mix and it's even better. I love the pink and purple aesthetic and the whole establishment is just too cute. The cat room itself is pretty small, so it can get cramped if there's a lot of people inside, but there's ample seating at least and every spot is good for cat watching. It's $11 an hour to reserve a spot in the cat room, but it goes towards a good cause and helps to socialize all the kitties. Be careful though, you might just end up taking one home since they're all up for adoption! It's just too darn cute.

This is the strangest location for a restaurant I have ever seen, but somehow it works. The dining room is quite small, and it's strange to be eating at an apartment complex, but if you get there early seating should not be an issue. Most of their food is like a Mexican-fusion style, and I would suggest going for the savory dishes to get some interesting flavors. Their sweet menu is extensive as well, and while it reminds me of things you can get elsewhere, it's all been tasty so far. Of everything I definitely recommend the chilaquiles, which come in a large portion and are very tasty. This place is unique, and not a bad choice for brunch.

I think I prefer this dim sum location as opposed to their neighbor next door. Their soup buns are top tier for sure. Everything was tasty, I recommend the spicy dumplings which are very aromatic if you're feeling something different. Will be back.

So, Parx. The center of Bensalem, and possibly the Northeast Philadelphia area. First thing's first, it's an eyesore. Those terrible outdoor screens are blinding at night, and the hideous horse head they've erected looks like the false idol of some sort of cult. The inside isn't as atrocious, but honestly, it's just not interesting. 

Their slots really stink, I've never once had a payout. Like, not even a ten cent payout. So I've stopped going there to gamble on machines. 

Their saving grace is the horse track, which I love going to. That's where the payouts are, my friends. Plus watching a race is a better waste of your life energy then sitting in front of a slot for hours anyway.

After hearing a whole lot of hype about this place I can tell you that it's good pizza. Not necessarily great pizza, but good pizza. It is vastly overpriced for what it is, but that's typical amongst artisanal pizza places.

The rotolo is probably their best offering. It's unique and low priced, and a great starter in general. I love their use of pistachio, and it just all comes together to work well as a dish. The pizza is good, but nothing groundbreaking. The crust is fluffy but also floppy when you pick it up. The speck pizza I got was very tasty, but this was mostly due to its toppings. The speck was salty and flavorful, and the onions and pistachios gave it an interesting texture. 

I would have the pizza here again, but it's not something I would go out of my way for. If they dropped their prices just a smidge, I might be more willing to drop in for round two. Pretty good overall.

Like most other farms, this place gets absolutely insane crowds in the autumn. At least they have a large parking lot and parking lot attendants to match, which is something most other farms do not offer. Their ice cream and other food items are delicious, so make sure you get some before you take a look around. I have to say though, twelve dollars for a corn maze, really? That is steep. Aside from that I think they set it up quite nicely for fall fun, so if you plan accordingly it should be okay.

They're fine, and if you want tacos or any variety of Mexican styled eats there's something waiting here for you. I wouldn't say they're spectacular but they're okay.

My quesadilla was a little bland. The chicken was cooked and seasoned well but that was about it. Make sure you ask for extra hot sauce. I'd heard good things about this chain so I was a little disappointed, but they're alright for fast casual.

9 days ago, this place got three stars from me on a take out order. And I still stand by that. 

Two weeks ago, this place was around a three star experience. 

If the meal I had tonight is any indication, they're figuring it out. 

I'll preface this by saying that I realize this place may still have kinks to work out. Your experience may still vary.

But I can tell you this based on my experience tonight of the full atmosphere in the dining room. I experienced no service issues. The food came out in a timely fashion. The items I ordered were prepared right. Everyone working there was very nice to me. 

I really hope they keep it up. 

The details... Tonight I went for Chicken Maryland. The Crab Imperial on top of the chicken was fantastic! There was plenty of meat inside, and not too rich. I didn't feel like I was eating too heavily. It complemented the chicken nicely. The wife had Stuffed Shrimp with the Imperial and raved about it. 

I actually think this is the most important part. They didn't kill the side orders. So many Delco restaurants half ass the side orders, serving you shriveled veggies in a dish. These green beans were fresh and flavorful. The red bliss potatoes were prepared perfectly. It worked. 

Some people have said that they didn't offer enough side choices. This still seems to be true. I was offered only the potatoes and green beans. I could have had French fries and cole slaw I was told when I asked if that was it. I forgot to ask about pasta as I had that last time as the side. But it's not clearly stated on the menu. I publicly urge the owner here... Fix this problem.  People want better choices for sides, and you should be offering them more easily.

We tried the Shrimp Lejon. 4 pieces for around 9 bucks seems to be the norm. Damn, Shrimp Lejon is expensive. But it was quite tasty. 

The only taste miss was the New England Clam Chowder, which was simply passable. But keep in mind, I spent the better part of 10 years living in Boston. I've been spoiled. 

My one year old son was with us, and he couldn't get enough of the Mac and Cheese. He started grabbing for it. I tasted it. It definitely doesn't suck.  I'd eat a plate of it happily too. 

Here is what I know for sure. If AJ Stephens keeps doing what they did for me tonight, and tweaks a couple of things, they'll be around a long time. I'm rooting for them to do it. 

They've proven to me that they're capable of getting it right. Now they have to do it every day and do it consistently.

I wasn't sure what to think at first. 

The concept here is so unique, I knew I had to try it once. But my fear was that I would wind up in a world of "Main Line pretentiousness". 

If you're not sure what I mean by that, well I'm not sure either. Just know that I know it when I see it. 

The truth is this. As far as food quality goes, I can't say enough good things. Everything I ate was simply fantastic. From the hummus to the chicken liver kale sandwich to the cinnamon apple scone, the eating experience itself was nothing short of phenomenal. 

But here's where I hesitate to go 5 stars for them. 

I didn't come here expecting that my lunch would be hummus and a chicken liver kale sandwich. In fact I'm fairly certain that if you ever see me in public ordering that combination, I've been kidnapped and replaced by an alien clone. 

I had to eat that here. Because in the end that was the choice I was given. 

They only give you a few real lunch choices, and they all have some form of unique ingredients. Basically, if you don't like what they're offering, your lunch becomes unlimited toast and a pastry. That will be the only option you have left to eat. 

I wasn't even sure I would like a chicken liver kale sandwich. But I wanted a sandwich and talked myself into it. The fact that it wound up being incredibly tasty to me is fortunate. 

Also, if you're like me, you want to try a few different things to get the true flavor of a place. Unfortunately this means lunch becomes a $25 outlay. It's not something I'd do every day. 

Basically, the food is phenomenal. But you have to be in an adventurous mood to walk in the door. Don't expect to customize your order. You have to be willing to trust them and eat what they have. 

If this is you, then go for it!

So ever since they were in Creed, it's been on my radar to come here. I was up this way yesterday, and decided it was time. 

This is a really good cheesesteak. Good amount of meat. Not dry at all. Not too tender. Not too rubbery. The meat had a nice feel to it. And the onions caramelized on the grill with it infused a nice flavor. 

They used a straight Amoroso roll here. Nothing fancy. But it didn't have to be. I'm more of a Sarcone's kind of guy. But nothing wrong with this. 

On my cheesesteak top 10 list, they are now in my top 5.  

1. John's 
2. D'Alessandros
3. Philip's 
4. Tony Luke's 
5. Max's 
6. Joe's
7.  Jim's 
8. Steve's
9. Pat's 
10......

You'll have to see my next review to see who just claimed the 10 spot.

I haven't reviewed this place in 9 years. Time for an update. 

And I've decided they need more love. 

Back story... my late Uncle Rich introduced me to this place years ago. I've been back a few times over the years. Always loved it. 

I just love the flavor and texture here. When I'm in the mood for square pie, this is a favorite. I wish I got down here more often. I should. 

But the biggest reason I upgraded it to 5 stars is that my 6 year old boy housed an entire slice with pepperoni and asked for seconds. Pic is for proof. 

He ate more than me. But I blame my weight loss surgery. Still, when I want a good slice I want what i love. And La Rosa is pizza I can crave. 

8.4 on the Dave Portnoy scale. It's not Angelo's or Tacconelli's. But it doesn't have to be. And three huge slices, two with toppings for $7.25 is a bargain.

So let me get this straight, Harrah's....

On a Saturday night, at 6:30pm, for letting me sign up for your Players Club card for the first time, you're going to let me have a free buffet, and $25 in free slot play which I can then turn into $22.90 of actual cash to walk out the door with?  

Gee, why don't you twist my arm?  

I've been to Harrah's a number of times in my life, just never gotten around to reviewing them.  And please don't let the fact that they just bribed me with $50 worth of freebies make you think that this is clouding my judgement.  It probably is, I just don't want you to think that.  

Truth is, of the major casinos nearby in Pennsylvania, I'd definitely come to Harrah's over Sugar House, over Parx, and I'll even throw in over Delaware Park.  I've liked Harrah's in general since day 1.  

Now, are they perfect?  No.  The buffet hasn't always been good.  Although tonight they had several things I liked.  They had a couple of things I didn't like.  But tonight I'll say they pulled off a majority.  If a previous review is to be believed, they may have improved the quality here.  

I don't think they have enough great slots that hold my interest, but they have more than enough mediocre slots.  I'm not a slots guy anyway so don't ask me.  

I am a table game player, and I'll put Harrah's tables over Sugar House's easily.  Probably on par with Parx, but I've only been to Parx once.  I was happy to see $10 tables earlier on a Saturday because I'm a cheapskate, but by the time I left they were $15.  That's par for the course.  Higher tables could be had.  Whenever I've played, I've been able to get a seat, which seems to rarely be the case when I visit Sugar House.  

But the funniest thing... my wife and I both signed up for the Players card, as did two of our friends.  We all got the free buffet, so a $100 food bill was comped for us.  They all got $10 in free slot play.  For some reason I "won" $25 in free play.  I suppose they have a random thing going behind the scenes that gives out higher rewards for the heck of it.  That higher amount actually gave me a chance to build up some cash which, after I played the free play, I was able to cash out and leave with.  

So I got a free night at Harrah's on a Saturday night and walked home with some of their money.  But I'm certain that was a one time deal.  And I don't know if the deal changes from time to time or not.  But, you could do a lot worse on a Saturday night to keep yourself occupied.  And it will talk me into coming back again.

One last thing... a couple of weeks later we get coupons for comped rooms during the week in Atlantic City.  They're really giving away the farm to get your business.

I was in the neighborhood for a volunteer event. Yelp guided me here for lunch. 

One plate of jerk chicken with rice and peas and macaroni later, and I will gladly drive back up here from southern Delco sometime to eat it again. 

It was insanely good. Amazing! 

I love these types of places more than fine dining. The flavors are intense here.

I know my fellow Delco Yelpers have been watching this place as it was being renovated. 

Well, I'm first to review. I win! Yay me!

So, I am always in favor of new styles of food in this area of Delco. Anything that isn't the same ol sports bar type of place is an immediate improvement in my book.

Of course it isn't going to matter if the food isn't good. 

So I've been driving past here watching for this place to open. I finally noticed activity here this week and had a chance to stop in at 9pm tonight. They've done a nice job with the interior, I noticed right off the bat. 

And it turns out tonight was grand opening night to the public. So have at it, gang!

I am no expert in Vietnamese cuisine but I have had it several times. I did notice that the menu was quite extensive. I don't think you'll complain about the variety. I know there are a lot of Pho lovers on Yelp, and they've got a lot of Pho choices.  I'm a sucker for wonton soup so I went for the big bowl with noodles. As I was waiting, I noticed plates coming out of the kitchen and each item looked better than the last. 

The wonton noodle soup came with shrimp and all of the good soup trimmings. Gang, the bowl was a meal in itself, and was as good as anything I've had on Washington Ave in Philly or even Chinatown. From the broth to the wonton filling, perfect flavor! 

I also sampled the chicken curry appetizer. It's a small portion but priced right and quite tasty. It's a good small plate sample. 

Gang, we have to give this place a chance. I don't think you will regret it one bit if you're a fan of this cuisine. Have at it, Delco Yelpers!

After a recent trip to this strip mall to eat at Han Dynasty, I noticed this place on the way in.  I immediately put it on my future "to try" list.  This week was the week to try it.  

Now, I'm going to judge two different visits.  My first visit was a solo visit for lunch.  That visit was simple.  I chose two dishes I happen to love, which are Samosa Chaat and Gobi Manchurian, with a Mango Lassi of course.  They all pleased me very much.  But, what struck me the most is while I was looking at the menu, not only did I see a bunch of items I wanted to try in the future, I also saw some items that the wife would go crazy for.  

You see, being that she was born in Mumbai, and since I have visited Mumbai with her, I have come to know a little bit about the legendary Mumbai street food.  So I recognized a few items that I know she doesn't get very much around here, and I knew I'd have to bring her here.  So, after telling her about my find (after she gave me the requisite guilt trip about eating Indian food without her which I'm used to by now), she determined that we would go there for dinner tonight.  

So, tonight the wife and I ordered up several more dishes to try.  To satisfy her Mumbai street food cravings, Vada Pav and Dahi Batata Puri were ordered, as well as a Masala Dosa (my wife seems to be on the search for the perfect dosa lately which I have happily joined her for), and for my meat cravings, I gave the Chicken 65 and the Chicken Biryani a try.  

Of all of these dishes, I loved the Chicken 65 and the dosa the most.  Chicken 65 is apparently a popular South Indian bar snack fried and marinated in 65 spices (take that, Colonel Sanders).  Consider it the "boneless buffalo wing" of India.  It's wonderful to say the least.  The dosa might be my favorite thus far in the area.  Good subtle crisp to it.  

Meanwhile, the wife was going crazy for the  Vada Pav and Puri.  My samplings of the dishes found them to be pretty darn tasty as well.  The Puri is a flavor explosion in the mouth.  I won't describe it, just experience it yourself.  

If there was any dish that damn near killed me with the spice, it was the biryani. I tasted a very strong clove taste at first (which I'm still burping up as I write this), and as I ate more of it, the spice hit me like a delayed reaction.  In fact, I'm fairly certain the power of the spice temporarily made me disoriented to the point that I almost spilled a cup of water on me as I drank it.  Damn, the food made me lose motor skills briefly.  Now, this is not to say it was bad.  Far from it.  It just crossed my personal threshold of spice, which is better than it used to be but not as high as others.  And, judging by the amount of Indian people who were eating here, and how many of them I saw ordering biryani while I was there, I have to think that this dish is tailored more to the hardcore Indian palate, which is fine.  Me, I'll just order it more mild next time if I can.  

Oh by the way, we took some of the desserts home.  We have a pound of Indian cookies which we haven't sampled yet (but looked awesome).  However, we did sample the Gulab Jamun when we came home.  And it's quite possible that we just found the BEST DAMN Gulab Jamun in the area.  In fact, I think my wife is still doing a Bollywood dance in her head over it.  If you know nothing of Gulab Jamun, I implore you to try it from here.  You will thank me later.  

A very solid 4 stars from me.  My wife would probably find a way to give it 6 stars if she could.  In fact, I think she's already calling her relatives in this area to meet her here.  And I think she wants to move to Exton now.  

Thanks, Indian Hut, for potentially increasing my future mortgage payment.

After years of having this on my bucket list, I found the opportunity to check it off a little over a week ago.

It was on my bucket list because I'm a wing guy. It's my favorite food to eat. So if a place is famous for wings, it gets my attention. 

So no more beating around the bush. 

I went for the medium garlic wings. And I must say, they're exceptional. I love the breaded style of wings that they serve. The crisp on the outside was phenomenal. The sauce was bold. I could do these again and again. 

I had my young son with me. He liked the pizza. I found the pizza to be basic. But it tasted really good when I dipped it in the blue cheese flavored with the wing sauce. 

I'll give it my seal of approval.

I saw this place pop up in a recent Yelp search, and I wondered how I could have missed a place getting such great early reviews. 

I must be slipping. 

Well, I just finished eating here minutes ago. And I'm compelled to write this while it's fresh in my mind. 

This place is a true gem in every sense of the word. 

You see, 5 star dining experiences don't have to be fancy. Sometimes they come from places you least expect it. 

You know, like a Sunoco gas station. 

The other reviews have described what's going on here accurately. I'll just get right to the point. 

First of all, the ladies running this business are a delight. They love cracking jokes with the customers. They treat you like friends. You don't get this everywhere. 

It was recommended I try the Buffalo Chicken sandwich. For $5.50 I got fresh chicken chunks in a buffalo sauce with crumbles of blue cheese on a Kaiser roll. The chicken overflowed the roll. I needed a fork to get it all. 

It was spectacular. And it was most spectacular because of its realness and simplicity. It wasn't some chicken patty slapped on a roll with sauce from a bottle. It was home cooked goodness. 

Now, I noticed one thing as I was there. The meatball sandwiches are majestic looking. I saw many go out over the counter and I couldn't believe how hearty they were. The ladies were kind enough to let me try a meatball separately. It is apparently a Sicilian recipe of theirs. 

It was unbelievable, and again it was because of its simplicity. Just good fresh ground meat with a few seasonings and a fresh homemade crushed tomato sauce. 

They didn't have to do too much to it. It's just wholesome real food that goes together so well. It's real and it's spectacular! 

Oh by the way, the Nutella cheesecake brownie... GET IT!!!! Just trust me.

I'm coming back again this week and I'm bringing friends. Thank you ladies!

We need good barbecue places in Delco, and no I'm not talking about Famous Dave's. 

Gave them a shot this afternoon.  Had the place pretty much to myself at 3pm. So I sat at the bar, ordered a beer, and talked them into making me a combo platter with pulled pork and baby back ribs with sides of mac and cheese and potato salad. 

It came out very quickly. So here's the verdict. 

The pulled pork had a similar taste to what you might find in Crock Pots all across Delco. I don't necessarily think that's a bad thing. I've had better, but I'd eat it again. 

The ribs had a bit of a chewy exterior crust, but once you get past it, the meat was tender and juicy. Slight hint of smoke to it too. Once again, I've had better but I'd eat it again. 

The sides were a hit. Both were well made and fresh. Nothing wrong with the cornbread in my mind. 

I'd say the food was 3 1/2 out of 5. I'll give them the fourth star because an afternoon of eating pretty good barbecue with a beer while watching sports at the bar is damn near heaven. 

They may not be the best I've ever had, but they're worth a trip. Definitely a better choice than the chain up the street. 

And oh by the way, they're my 600th review. I made it a point to pick a special place for that.

This is the Chipotle of pizza. Nothing more, nothing less. 

After hearing hype from a few work friends, I had to give it a shot. In basic terms, here's what I experienced. 

The assembly line moves well. It's a very Chipotle-like style of food assembly. You'll find that out when you come here. 

The crust is pre-made, and almost too perfect. It's also quite flat, like flatbread. I understand that it has to be that way for the service model to work. But it reminds you that deep down this is not a mom and pop place. It's maybe the one drawback. 

Flavor-wise though, it's on point. I tried the Dominic which is basically a white pizza with tomato and sausage. The good part about the flat crust is that it comes out crisp, and it's not too heavy if that's what you're in the mood for. It's a perfect portion. The ingredients came together very well. I polished mine off in record time so that means on some level I loved it. 

I wouldn't choose this place over my favorite local places, much like I wouldn't choose Chipotle over a South Philly taqueria. But I would come here with work friends for lunch again.

Being a HUGE fan of Thai food, I am always on the lookout for a new place to try. As soon as I found out about Ginger I had to go. Rumors of deliciousness AND close to my place? Uh, yes please!

First off, the portions are humongous. If you're the type of person who loves to get the biggest bang for your buck... this place is for you. 

I tried the Priew Wan and it was out of this world. It was a delicious mix of cucumber, pineapple, bell peppers, tomatoes, and carrots in a Thai sweet and sour sauce on steamed rice. Bellissimo! *kisses fingertips like an Italian* 

As for desserts, they offer coconut, green tea, taro, or ginger flavored ice cream accompanied with purple sticky rice. I wasn't a huge fan of the taro, but the others were pretty good. 

All in all, I am so happy to see a delicious Thai place bring some life and some spice to Thompson Lane!

So this morning I woke up to something particularly interesting. 

The UG owner's "son" yelped me to say that he doesn't see how my experience could have happened, he listed the reasons why, gave some half empty excuses for them and then said I needed to not run my mouth about their restaurant. He also continued on to say that if my review "did" happen, he's sorry. Hard to hear the truth much? I understand reaching out trying to understand what happened, but instead he took the theme of my review and wrote a snide message back in the same "strike one, two, three" fashion. If he hadn't of been so rude, I would have just continued to go about my day. 

After the original review, the executive chef contacted both me and my friends about our horrible experience and I thought I'd definitely give this place another chance. These things DO happen. His message was inquisitive, warm and sincere. He even offered our entire table a free dinner if we came back in. Very nice of him.

After receiving the "son's" message, I was furious. Shortly after I received another message on behalf of Urban Grub apologizing for the message and my past experience.  

All in all, let's chalk it up to a bad experience and move on. I'm sure plenty of people will enjoy this place, I however didn't. Ying and yang.

I'm going to be honest: I probably would have made this a 4 star review, except my entree was phenomenal.  

We stopped in on a Saturday evening and were greeted by a lovely server.  We ordered the chicken wings and some shrimp spring rolls to start, and then between us got an order of rare beef pho, some chicken steamed buns, and I got a small order of duck.  The chicken wings were tasty and the meat was tender, though it still can't touch the wings of MOPHO.  The spring rolls were pretty basic; I was looking for more fresh herbs and a bit more spice in the peanut sauce. The pho broth was rich and deep with the traditional Chinese 5 spice and lots of herbaceous notes, and the chicken was tender and juicy, served with briny and spicy kimchi.  Both very good.  But then I tasted the duck. Holy hell.  

For a small portion, it looked like half of the animal.  The meat was cooked perfectly and very moist. The fat was rendered and the skin was slightly crispy and not rubbery at all.  The seasoning of the duck was so good I didn't even touch the au jus, and just dipped my rice cakes in the duck drippings. I left with enough leftovers for another substantial dinner, and I have to say, it was almost as good on day 2.  We left stuffed, groaning, and happy. Best duck I've had in a long while!

Stopped on for a Wednesday night dinner prior to seeing Phantom at the Saenger (Quentin Oliver Lee was PHENOMENAL!) and were immediately hit by the delicious smell of grilled meats.  The restaurant itself is quaint and unassuming, with a lovely blue exterior and eclectic furniture and tableware.  We sat down and were greeted with water and the menus.  I unfortunately forgot my phone and was unable to take photos, but the daily menu included a curried fish hot pot of sorts, a grilled salad, crispy pig ears, and a pork shoulder special. 

Having heard about both of the aforementioned pork specials, we immediately ordered both to share.  We also ordered two of the salads off of the regular menu, hers a simple kale and arugula salad with some sort of sauteed onion vinaigrette, and me an Asian-inspired pressed veggie salad (double spicy!) with a lime-fish sauce-cilantro-ginger type sauce and dried shrimp.   

The crispy pigs ears came first in a small bowl.  They were cut into thin shoestring-like strips and had curled into all sorts of shapes.  They were crunchy, chewy, and fatty with a very large amount of seasoned salt that paired well with the house cocktail.  A little saltier than I prefer, but it sure didn't stop us.  The salads arrived next.  Hers was a more simple salad, but the vinaigrette had that nice smokey charred onion flavor that one craves.  My salad was spicy and fresh, full of acid and fresh herbs, and so many different pops of flavor from the different components.  

Finally, the main.  Two GENEROUS portions of pork shoulder seasoned, grilled, and sliced thinly, surrounded by bib lettuce, fresh parsley, cilantro, and mint, and a limey garlicky sauce.  We were instructed to wrap the meat in the lettuce with the herbs and dip, and dip away we did. The flavors were spectacular, and had none of the carb guilt.  I had the happy idea to try dipping my wrap in the leftover sauce from my salad and I have to say it may have been better than the original sauce.  Phenomenal.  We did our best in finishing the meal and feigned interest in dessert but realized we were simply too stuffed for more.  Ended with a bill of $75 for 2 cocktails, an appetizer, two salads, and a gigantic shared entree, so no complaints about value!  I'm looking forward to coming back and trying the daily specials on a different day.  

Tl;dr: very delicious, carb-conscious, filling meals for a good price in a quaint setting.  Try the pork shoulder special.

The western village is a classic staple for my parents. They enjoy hitting the slots and scoring some 2-for-1 dinner at Pancho & Willie's, which is what brought us in! While this restaurant is labeled as a Mexican restaurant, they have a fair amount of variety and offer other dishes such as chicken Marsala and salmon. 

Outside of having to walk through a casino to get there, the atmosphere is nice and fairly quiet with comfortable booths. We really enjoyed our waiter, Tanner, as well. And hey, if you enjoy throwing. $5 bill into a slot machine, you can snag a free drink from a cocktail waitress and bring that into dinner with you. 

We all started with a round of margaritas, previously known as the famous $.99 margs have increased to $2 a piece, but they are still well worth it and quite strong! Available blended or over the rocks. Complimentary chips and salsa are provided as well. I chose to order the chicken Marsala, one of my favorites, and I was pleasantly surprised. The flavor was great and the mashed potatoes went well with them. Sadly, I am consistently underwhelmed with their side of vegetables, which taste like they came straight from a frozen bag.

With the 2-for-1 coupon, dinner and drinks for 5 came to $53. A great deal if you ask me!

This is by far my favorite diner any where in NE Philadelphia. In all honesty, I can't even think of one in Philly that I'd rather go to. It's a diner, it's up to date now, and it has nice clean, simple menus. My usual M.O. at diner places is breakfast, regardless of the time of day. 

My favorite dish here is the creamed chipped beef on toast. It's the best of its kind that I've ever tried. Served with a massive helping of home fries (hash browns) that are savory and delicious. You can taste and see the carmelized onions mixed in there, this is not cardboard diner food!

The Balgian Waffle gets an A+ from the 12 year old and the pancakes are tasty and satisfying; fluffy and malty, just how you'd expect pancakes to be. 

Anyway, as many times as I've been to this place, I've never been disappointed with the breakfast food.

Now service....lol....service is kind of entertaining here.
Usually they kitchen flies the food out, and it's good. The last time my family went, it didn't come out for a while...not sure if it was the server or the kitchen, but regardless, it was worth the wait because the food was better than usual.

The server this time was a young guy, obviously new to waiting tables as he made the usual n00b mistakes like getting silverware, blaming other servers for not getting us things that he sent them to do even though it is actually HIS job, etc etc. But he made one unforgivable mistake....and this is something that even a person who never waited tables in their life shouldn't make.....he touched the lips of our coffee mugs with his nasty waiter fingers. I have waited tables before...I know what things you touch when you are busy waiting tables.....and you dont' have time to wash your hands after every action you perform. Please for the love of all that is sacred, don't ever touch my cups where I put my mouth!!!!!! I didn't have the heart to correct him. This time. I did some wiping after he left the table though. But hey....the coffee is good.

The visit to the Mayfair I had before that, there was a wonderful young lady waiting on us but then we got to listen to a server argument about the sanity of one of the elder waitresses. LOL I mean this one older woman just went on and on about how she was treated/perceived/etc and the other girls were trying to calm her down and critique her performance in a different way so that she wasn't flipping the eff out....hahhaa the whole place was kind of looking around at each other but in the end the waitstaff rolled their eyes and laughed it off with apologies to the diners for the outburst and I laughed and chakled it up to the character of the Mayfair. Gotta love it.

P.S. I'm taking my mom here for mother's day, so if you're gonna try this place out....do it any other day but mother's day...I will be hungry and I don't want to wait in a line. :D

Also, this is a great spot to gorge on not as greasy as you'd think comfort food after a night of drinking.

The Philly cheese steak is a classic and taste absolutely amazing.  There are two stations, one for the sandwich and one for the fries and drinks.  The service is quick.  The whiz cheese with the steak on a sandwich was an amazing creation.

Place is gorgeous inside. All new. A lot of open room though but at the same time tables against the wall with the bench seating were way too close together. Bar is awesome. Lots of tap beers. Service was good. Friendly service. Baked Clams- they forgot to put seasoning on them. Very disappointing. Mussels in a white sauce. More like mussels in a chicken stock. Was waiting for the garlicky kick. Nothing. Fried calamari- cooked perfectly but the marinara dipping sauce seemed like a canned product. Seafood pescatore. 3 unopened little neck clams. That's a big no no serving them. Scallops were rubbery like it was a frozen item. Shrimp were good. Crab cakes were iffy. Lots of filling. Cheap crab meat. The bar area started blaring the football game which was quite distracting. Not an overall great experience.

When on Bourbon... CCPW!

I first checked these guys out in 2018! I remembered them this time around and was so thrilled when I spotted the building on this infamous street. Naturally, I went twice during this trip. Crescent City Pizza Works is a contemporary counter-service pizza joint offering beer + slices of classic and creative hand tossed pizzas! And trust me, you should def be standing in line for the creative ones. Check out what I got below. 

Classic Pepperoni

Chizzaburger
Angus Beef + Onions + Cheddar + Mozzarella + Pickles + Ketchup + Mustard

Chicken Bacon Krunch
Chicken, Bacon, Kettle Chips, Mozzarella, Provolone + Ranch Sauce

Buffalo Blues
Buffalo Chicken + Blue Cheese + Green Onions + Mozzarella + Buffalo Ranch Sauce

I loved them all! The ingredients are quality and flavor profiles are exaggerated with each bite. If I had to choose one it would be the Chizzaburger. The pickles really really take the pizza to a next level burger slice!

A local resident and employee at Regarding Fresh, Ty, recommended this place to my posse and me. I couldn't have been happier with this cute little joint.
