Located in the LGD off Magazine. Surrounded by cute houses and fresh healthy breathing from neighborhood trees. Surrey's is an eclectic, funky cafe and juice bar. Did you know this is the oldest organic juice bar in New Orleans?! They have a sweet and savory menu that specializes in local food items with a hint of latin flavor. It's all the quality you need, not to mention healthy. 

Fresh pressed juice of the day was Orange Mango Pineapple. So refreshing and naturally sweet! Expect light pulp and a well mixed juice. 

On the special menu I saw a crawfish omelette and on the regular was a crab omelette. I asked them to half it. Btw, this omelette is stuffed with fresh avocado slices and a decently sliced piece of Brie. It's the topped with a lump crab meat sauce (white and creamy, I'll add). The crab meat sauce is insane! Served with toast or a biscuit. I opted out for a fruit bowl cup. The fruit was so fresh and cut into perfect bite size pieces! My only complaints as the crawfish sauce. It was decent. I would eat it but once you get ahold of that crab meat sauce it's game over! 

Love Surrey's!

I spent many a night in Four Green Fields in my younger days.  They used to have a rooster that ran around the bar, and an Irish singer named Patrick, who we called the Irish Willie Nelson.  At one point during the night, the bartenders used to stand at attention while they played the Irish National Anthem.  They also didn't serve food and smoking was allowed.

On a trip to South Tampa recently, I convinced everyone to stop by there for a pint or two.  I was happy to see that they still have some great Irish music and I am glad that the smoking is gone.  I think everyone had a good time, and hopefully I can get a few more trips there out of my friends.  I am not a fan of the South Howard scene, and Four Green Fields in definitely my type of place.  Next time I will try some of their pub food.

I just don't even know what to say about this place... my inner fat kid just did the happy dance!  This market is AMAZING!!!!!  the wine and cheese selection is out of this world and they have a little area of the market where they have fresh, handmade pastas!!!!! There is a little café area in the center that we didn't check out this time because we wanted to get all our goodies we were buying home, but it looked and smelt yummy. We will definitely have to eat at the café next time.  The big building next door to the market is their kitchen store.  It is loaded with kitchen wares and all kinds of gifts.  I cannot wait to go back but I think I need to wait until payday :)  if you love Italian food.... you will love this market! (it is easy to get lost in there for a few hours looking at all the yumminess!)

Im pretty shocked this doesn't have an all around five star rating. We found this place looking on yelp for somewhere new to visit and let me tell ya they delivered. My expectations were high after hearing they had build your own MacNCheese. (You see I live with the worlds biggest MacNCheese fan.) We took the kids and even they were overly happy with our food, kinda of a big deal they are six and seven. 
I had the bacon wrapped meatloaf-minus the mustard sauce. I am pretty sure if I was on death row I would ask for this for my last meal. Even the leftovers rocked my world. We got chirzo egg roles before our meal and the jalapeños were spicy and delivered a wonderful punch that was welcome. My boyfriend had the lamb burger, which I stole a bite of, also top notch.
We did not get beverages because we had the kiddos with us, but I loved the beer list and the atmosphere. Its super clean and open in there. So we will for sure be making this one of our normal spots in the rotation.

Lee's gave me just another reason to love living in West Philly.

I was wary of all the great reviews because I was afraid of hyping up the chicken cheesesteak too much and ending up disappointed. Despite that, I finally caved and got a chicken cheesesteak with spinach a couple weeks ago and it delivered BIG TIME.

As promised, the chunks of chicken breast were plentiful and juicy. The spinach was chopped into small pieces (possibly sauteed with garlic?) and stuffed into an incredibly flaky roll that perfectly toed the balance between soft and crunchy. 

The coup de grace? The sweet chili sauce that I proceeded to pour all over my cheesesteak (and then dip my cheesesteak into the few drops of sauce that were left in the container). Make sure you order extra sauce or you WILL regret it. I've been craving that sweet, spicy, tangy deliciousness ever since I finished my last bite...

Plus, Lee is a super nice guy and clearly works hard to make his customers happy.

At under $7 for one of these bad boys, I will be a regular at Lee's Deli until the sad day when I move out of the area.

I stopped by this morning to "take" an espresso and I am excited to say that there is finally a coffee that matches if not surpasses La Colombe.  I travel to Abruzzo at least twice a year and I can tell you that this place is 100% authentic and is made from true Italian passion. If you want to go to Italy without taking a nine hour flight just walk through the door. To the owners I say grazie for bringing this amazing café to Philadelphia! I can't wait to come back for dinner!

Update: I visited Gran Caffee a second time for dinner and it exceeded my expectations. They have arrosticinni.  If your born in Italy you may not know what this is because it is only from the region of Abruzzo. It was amazing and to date except for one restaurant in New York I have never found arrosticinni anywhere.

Pro tip: stack all your veg on first, then pile your meat on top. Get that bang for your buck!

GG is a good choice when you are just HUNGRY. The pricing is pretty fair for the sheer amount of protein you can pack into a bowl as well.

Service can be dismally slow. I've had to flag down the nearest staff just to remind them we were there. But once you get your bowl from the server, it's pretty quick. You create your Frankenstein's monster of a bowl (or follow their suggested menu items) and wait for the cooks to fry it all up- about 10 minutes from when you drop it off. They'll ask which starches you want (noodles, rice, etc.), and you can tell them if you want to add an egg. You can also choose to go healthier with cabbage.

If you love garlic, I highly recommend dousing your bowl in the provided garlic water. It brings a ton of necessary flavor! And be heavy-handed with the seasoning. There will be none added during the cooking process that you didn't provide them.

Now, I'm not lactose intolerant, so I was blind to the plight of those who are until I met my friend and roommate. Every time we get coffee or a frozen treat, she has to be really careful not to get any dairy. And for the first time, I began to notice that dairy dominates everything! Every single time, she'd have to settle for the one non-dairy option that wasn't very satisfying or forego altogether. (Dessert is supposed to make you feel good!)

Enter Sweet Soul! This is the only dessert place she could spin around, randomly point to a menu item, and definitely be able to eat it. It was so great! 

As far as our orders, I got the Sweet Tooth smoothie, which I guzzled in approximately 8.9 seconds. It tasted fresh and delicious. I tried my friend's matcha/vanilla charcoal swirl bowl and, while I found the coconut milk flavor to be too overpowering for a delicate flavor like matcha, it wasn't a bad flavor at all. 

I would like to see the staff more regularly clean the inside eating area, which is prone to getting wet and sticky, given the business being conducted. There were five people behind the counter working very efficiently at their tasks, but a little cleanup throughout the day goes a long way! Also, there were only three stools at the bar, which is awkward considering most people who dine in don't come alone. There was always one stool empty, and couples opted to stand outside rather than have one person sit and the other stand (particularly since standing persons can get in the way of the tiny amount of space there is to stand in line).

I really like the Ciccio restaurants, and Sweet Soul is a great addition to their offerings. It's also different from the onslaught of unhealthy ice cream and froyo chains. This place is definitely worth a visit, and I'm looking forward to trying more treats!

Being Japanese, I'm super critical of ramen. Only Dosunco has given me comparable ramen to Japan, and that's because it's owned and operated by Japanese!

That being said, Wooden Ladle's tonkotsu shoyuu was excellent! The noodles are likely not made in house, but they have a nice, firm consistency, even the day after! The broth could benefit from more salt (or just more shoyu) and butter, to ramp up the richness tonkotsu is known for. WL definitely gets props for including black garlic oil, which deepens the flavor profile of the broth.

For $11, it's a solid bowl of ramen. And I didn't mind the prices for the extras. $3 for another slice of chashu (pork belly), $2 for extra noodles, and $1 for an extra ajitama (seasoned soft boiled egg) is excellent! I ordered extra ajitama and chashu, and my ramen lasted for two meals!

The chashu was thick, with the perfect balance of fat to meat, and sliced in perfect spirals.

My favorite part about this ramen was how well it stood up the next day. The flavors came together nicely, and I actually enjoyed it even more than in the restaurant. I'd definitely go back to WL.

Wait, I forgot to mention the gyoza! They were crispy, fat, and delicious! The cold garlic dipping sauce they come with was surprising but very tasty. Definitely recommend if you like your gyoza on the crunchy, instead of soft, side. 

As a final note, the staff were all very pleasant! Okay, now I'm done. :)

Excellent. So good. Five stars. I've had The Lab bookmarked for a while but decided to make the trek out from Citrus Park just the other day. I left the gym and immediately thought, why not drive 10 miles for coffee? That's just what I did, and I was not disappointed.

The interior of TL isn't fancy. There's a decent amount of seating, however, and the barista I interacted with was very nice. Also, dogs are allowed! A couple people had their puppies there, and it was awesome.

Now, for the best part: the espresso. See, I am a Buddy Brew Believer. I had to pass BB on the way to TL. I nearly stopped and gave up my trek to try out TL for the first time. Imagine my sweet surprise when I tasted my iced latte from TL... and it tasted exactly like BB. I was over the moon. I'm always hesitant about trying new coffee places. I don't like the beans at Caffeine or Blind Tiger, so I was hesitant about TL. Unwarranted, it turns out. The espresso is incredible.

I also decided to indulge in a Hangover Cure, a delicious sandwich comprised of sausage, bacon, egg, hash brown, cheese, and sriracha mayo. It could have used a dash of salt, but this greasy and piping hot number was exactly what I needed after hitting my second leg day of the week. My stomach was noooot happy with me afterward, but I still highly recommend this delicious gut bomb of a sammich.

I might have also bought a humongous cinnamon crumb cake to go. I thought it might be lackluster, being vegan, but it was actually very moist and pretty tasty.

I won't be making any 10-mile trips again, but if I'm in the area and BB has no parking, I'll definitely head back to The Lab.

Let's just be real; I'm a sucker for a great cup of coffee and this place fit the bill! This is a new spot that took the place of the defamed "Drama Burger," and if I'm being honest, I'm happy about it! Stopped in after I took my car to get serviced, and I was impressed how trendy the interiors are. Plenty of open seating, really cool fixtures, relaxing color scheme. 

Walked up to counter, got help right away! One thing to note is they roast their own coffee beans and when that's the case you def go for the pour-over option. I ordered an El Salvador and an Ethiopian Yirgacheffe coffee. I also figured I should try a latte while I'm at it so, ordered one of them too. 

While I waited, I just hung out with the barista as she explained why she chooses to make coffee one way; the Hario V60. She said it opened up the flavor of the coffee and really made it taste better and once I tried it, I'm sure glad I chose the V60 for my pour-overs. 

The latte was delicious but a little too milky for my liking so next time I'll be ordering mine with 4 shots of espresso and a 12oz latte instead of a 16oz one. Besides the coffee I think I should mention that have appetizing pastries; croissants, muffins, parfaits and a few salads. 

I def see myself coming back here and just taking a day to enjoy the coffee and relax a bit.

This little shack is easy to miss but if you know, you know! They have amazing local grass fed burgers and brats. It's the best quality "dad burger" you can get in Boise. When you get a burger from here it's like you're at a backyard BBQ with a grill master dad who bought a locally raised grass fed cow. (Buying a cow, or portion of a cow is such an Idaho thing and once again, if you know you know). 
This is probably the best quality meat you can get in a burger. If you take your meat and burgers seriously, you've got to try this place out. 
The fries are just as great and local as the burgers. Hand cut Idaho potatoes, fried up when you order and the seasoning on them is amazing! 
I didn't even get to try the fry sauce because my partner used it all up before I could get to them! So, I bet the fry sauce is good but cannot confirm for myself. With that, I only wish that more fry sauce came with every meal.

Very solid establishment and even though we had to wait a little bit due to being short staffed it was still worth it...walking in you immediately feel how homey this place is and the local vibe of all the regulars is pretty awesome...came here this past week on a trip to Boise and was really impressed with not only the food but the service as well... 

For breakfast I had the Basque chorizo had with green chilies, jalapeños, tomatoes, and cheddar cheese atop Moe Joe potatoes with two eggs any style and toast...I asked for a few more peppers so was pretty spicy and well worth the burn. My wife had the 2 eggs and bacon (yes she's a creature of habit) and really loved them as well. What was great is the homemade jams that accompany your toast which really made this place just a little more special.

We came here this last week for our son in law's birthday and super glad we were even able to get in. Even Pre Covid this place is really busy especially on Friday nights.  Now at 1/2 capacity makes it even more challenging so glad we booked this 3 weeks in advance. Before anything else I have to mention that what made this place special was our sever Matthew B he was so awesome and we were all so impressed...we did have a delay on our reservation due to people lingering longer than they should.  

Immediately after being seated Matthew came by apologized for the inconvenience and let us know he put in a complimentary order of their fried asparagus fries which I will tell you if you come here get this or your missing out. Perfect shareable appetizer that is lightly breaded served with homemade ranch dipping sauce. We also had an order of their house made chips served with their version of frie sauce which is basically mayonnaise and ketchup but this one is a whole new level homemade from scratch with fresh tomatoes and veggies. 

For dinner you can see the pics and everything was super delicious and everyone raved how their food tasted. I personally had the Huli Huli roasted chicken. This is a 1/2 organic chicken that is house bribed then slow roasted to perfection. It is served over brown butter mashed potatoes, roasted baby carrots and Huli Huli pan sauce.  I don't what is in the Huli Huli pan sauce put it is and so delicious.  This dish is probably one of the best chicken dishes I have ever had. All the flavors were so good I polished off everything even the carrots lol...

They pinnacle of dinner was and what my son in law loves to come here for us the Forks's signature warm butter cake. It is served with Cloverleaf vanilla ice cream and fresh Oregon fruit. This dessert is so amazing I only wished I saved more room for  sharing. If you are a local Boise resident and haven't been here you are missing out on a piece of life. If you are visiting then don't miss out on this special treat and ask to sit in Matthews section you won't be disappointed.

We have now been here a few times and every time has been a great experience. Even tonight being severely short staffed these lady servers worked their butts off. The wait tonight was a little longer and despite this the servers got us everything and hustled to ensure we got everything we needed. 

Tonight we had a great meal...my wife had the carne asada and camarones (shrimp) platter and I had the carnitas plate. Everything was super delicious and my plate was cooked perfectly with the right amount of crisp on the carnitas. I ended up sneaking a bite of the carnitas and cooked perfectly medium rare. Also to wash everything down were 2 top shelf margaritas. This is such a great local Boise spot and will add everyone needs to be patient with restaurants based on staffing problems. These folks that are showing up to work their shifts deserve our grace and patience.

This was a great experience last night!!! We looked this place up feeling like some Chinese food and this came up. So glad we came here because everything from from to service was a 5 star. Our waitress Luck B was over the top awesome. She made the whole experience and despite waiting a little longer just did an amazing job!!

For food we had a smorgasbord of items including shrimp pineapple fried rice, pork Yakisoba, orange chicken, spring rolls chicken yellow curry and chicken Pad Thai.  Everything was great and tattered completely fresh. I would highly recommend this place to any local or any traveler to the Boise area. Great local find!

Gonna give 2 stars and give them another try on another visit but we came here this past week while visiting Boise State with our youngest daughter and our oldest daughter. Came in here to just grab a couple appetizers and a few drinks.... walked in and the place is totally dead literally dead. I walked up to the hostess stand and a very non helpful hostess says with the most un energetic "can I help you"...party of five people in almost an empty restaurant..yeah that's gonna be like 25-30 mins? Really?? I am super patient with all that's going on and people not wanting to really work but at least be up front and say everyone called in and I am the only one here...but to just be like warm them for me and my money we are going somewhere else.

Ordered A vegetarian banh mi through Uber eats.  Came quickly, however halfway through the sandwich I bit down on something hard.  There was a 2" metal screw in my sandwich.  Tried to contact them but their phone number is apparently out of service.

BE VERY CAREFUL ABOUT ORDERING FROM HERE.

Quick Read: Claustrophobic in all the right ways - the best ingredients for a delicious meal.

I'm not even going to pretend like you're not going to bump elbows and make uncomfortable eye contact with other people as you jam through the tight corners and packed shelves of delightful products. This market has some of the best wines, cheeses, meats, fresh pastas, and baked goods that I've ever encountered in the bay area. Parking and crowds are completely worth it! I recommend getting some fresh ricotta, mozzarella, pasta, fig and sage sauce, and prosciutto!

Or everything. Just get everything.

I've been holding off on this review trying to figure out what to do. Within 1 week, I went twice for lunch and had 2 very different experiences, mostly due to service. But we'll get to that in a minute ...

For starters, the food is wonderful! I had read the many reviews and agree, it's among the best Italian in Tampa. A pretty small menu of well cooked dishes, with a smattering of daily specials to choose from. The first time I visited, I had one of the specials - Italian Sausage and Zucchini Raviolis with a saffron and marscapone sauce. The raviolis were perfectly cooked, and the saffron was fragrant and robust. My coworker had the Amatriciana with meatballs. I had a small bite and it tasted fresh and zesty. I was a little taken back by the lack of side salads on the menu, but we asked politely and were at least able to wrangle some bread. I also had a tiramisu to go. OMG. This was, quite frankly, the best thing I've ever tasted. Amazingly light. 

A week later, also for lunch, I had the Chicken Carbonara (the sauce was creamy and the peas and pancetta were welcome pops of distinct flavor). My coworker (a different one, I had been raving about the food!) also had the Amatriciana with meatballs.

So food, clearly a 5.

But the service ... sigh ... the first time it was just the chef (until the sweetest young lady appeared toward the end of our meal and checked us out), and the chef waited on us and prepared the dishes, so I was willing to overlook the fact that he forgot both the sodas we ordered and it took a little bit for our lunch. 

But the second time ... ugh ... another woman was serving and when we entered the restaurant loudly says "well I'm here all the time and I've never seen you before!" in an accusatory manner. (She said the same thing to the guys who came in after us, so guess she's really not there all the time after all.) Anyway, she was very loud. Kept calling us "girlies," which quite frankly is obnoxious and disrespectful. And did I say loud? Something had very obviously happened before we got there and she kept going on and on to the Chef about how she couldn't believe someone said something, who did he think he was? Over. And over again. And we heard every word of it from the kitchen for our entire meal. And the 5+ minutes it took her to get our drinks while she stopped and talked again (we were the only table).  And then waiting for our check. And then when I had to go hand her our credit cards to check us out. Anyway, both my friend and I agreed, if we walked in again and she was serving, we'd leave. Just not pleasant or professional and the volume honestly was distracting from our meal.

Service = 4 the first time, 2 the second. 

So ... will I go back? For the food, yes. But I may call first to see who is serving.

This is my kind of place! I've passed Prohibition a bunch of times and from the outside (and the location), I chalked it up to being a cheesy dive bar... I was totally wrong.

Rumor has it this place is owned by the same owners of Cafe Lift and it makes perfect sense; the food is amazing, everything has a "foodie", gastropub-feel and the beer list was second to none. We had a beet salad, polenta fries and deep fried green beans. As if that doesn't sound appetizing enough, we didn't "polish it off with a cool Budweiser", but hand-pumped firkin... It was firkin great... and I'm a firkin loser...

This establishment is located in the college town of New Orleans.  The whole area is very quaint.  Beautiful uniques houses and trees everywhere but still the city.  

After a long stroll at "The Fly" we, well I convinced my partner to come here for happy hour and wow this place did not disappoint.  

Parking:  We ended up valet since we didn't want a parking ticket or/and miss happy hour.  The valet girl was cute so yeah it's all good! 

Ambience:  Very lively!! So New Orleans like everybody was happy and eating.  Reminds me of a Kings Fish House but with swag.  Loved it!! 

Service:  The service was great we were posted at the BAR since it's super super BUSY but amazingly the 3 servers are so efficient and ON it.  We got our drinks and oysters like super quick. 

Food:  Okay the 50 cents oysters were pretty dang good.  I can taste the freshness difference odd but true.  Although it's not the yummiest oysters I've consumed it's Good.  The grilled oysters wasn't on the HH menu but it was interesting not for me but good. 

I highly recommend coming here for HH!!  The drinks and oyster special make this place worth a visit.  The great service, vibe and food will definitely make you come back.

So- I like the food, but this location is dirty. Every other table is marked as not to use because of covid- and those tables are the only ones that were clean. I tried to wait to ask if someone could come clean our table but you can stand at the pickup counter and be completely ignored. My sister's order came out pretty quick- but my order took forever. Even the guy who ordered 5 minutes after me got his order within a couple of minutes. Then the worker who was wrapping the food was talking to a customer and the cashier just stood there staring off into space instead of jumping in and working the food line. The woman apologized when she finally stopped talking and handed me my food- but I was a bit annoyed. I ordered the cuban sandwich- and it was good for the price. My sister's food was fine too- but she couldn't eat slow enough for me to eat with her. Because my food took 20 minutes to come out (15 of that was spent on an employee conversation). I don't like the locations where I live and was so excited about eating here and it left a lot to be desired. Most orders were completed quickly, but the dining area being filthy is something they need to work on.

Dinner at Cheddar's was the kids idea- this is where they officially started dating, so it was appropriate to dine here the night before the nuptials! The only ding was the wait- we were quoted 20-25 minutes and it was 47 minutes. I actually popped in to make sure we weren't missed. Once we were in and seated- life was good! Drinks all around and those croissants- good gracious I forgot how good they are. Then the food arrived! I ordered the chicken pot pie, John & Crystin both got the country fried chicken with gravy on the side and various sides and Connor got his 8 oz steak cooked medium-rare. Service here was stellar- the food was perfect and surprisingly didn't take too long to come out. They only lost a star for the wait time.

The burgers are always on point at Ford's Garage- but this time I tried their meatloaf and it was interesting. I was told it had brown gravy- but it also had the red sauce top under that brown gravy- a bit of conflict of tastes, but not bad. Crystin got pretzel sticks and the boys both got burgers. Even my niece got a cheeseburger. My drink though- wow, the Motor-jito was delicious! Not big enough, as I ordered 2 and they ran $10 each- ouch. I may need to attempt to recreate that drink at home. Our server checked on us throughout and the decor is fun as always.

I am going to be blatantly honest- I have only had their to-go gallons of margaritas and sangria. But I have had it several times now and ordered and picked up some for my sister's surprise birthday party! About the only positive thing about the pandemic is the opportunity to grab cocktails to-go and take them home! Or in my case- to my sister's place since I don't live in the area. I absolutely LOVE their sangria and the margaritas are always a hit! Ordering online is easy- I set a pick up time and arrived early and someone came out to ask my name within a minute! Jugs of cocktails dropped off in my passenger window! Now that's service. My sister and her family loves this place for dinner too~ so maybe one of these times I will actually eat something instead of just drinking!

I fell hard for this place when it opened! Tiny shack of a kitchen, outdoor seating, no where location in front of a cow pasture- but they make da best crab cakes! This was a once a week lunch when I used to live here & my boys were addicted to the crab cakes & the crab bisque! Crab cakes- no fillers, no peppers, onions, bread crumbs... Just crab & old bay & whatever they use to hold it all together.

I used to chat with the owner all the time I was such a regular! I was thrilled to grab my son and run over for an impromptu lunch! We ordered the crab cake sandwich and a bowl of the crab bisque to share and 2 lemonades- did I mention their lemonade is delicious? And very complimentary to the seafood. 

Service is always with a smile! And in the years I have been in Jax- they have built a roof to cover the outdoor picnic tables~ making it better to avoid that hot Florida sun. It is a BYOB if you choose. I REALLY miss eating here regularly! Locals- this is a crab cake treasure right here!

Finally. 
NOLA has legit Ramen.

Recently - I have resorted to having my own fresh Ramen Pasta overnighted from NYC. 
A bit of a pain but worth it when you just need some damn ramen in your life.
(Clearly - I obsess over shit sometimes)

Decided on a lunch date with my beautiful wife at Kin, today.
It did not disappoint. 

Before I get into it...I should point out that they make their own Ramen Noodles, fresh, in house. 
Looked like it was to-order as well.
That is no small feat.

For me, I ordered the Tonkotsu.
About as traditional as you can go...had some amazing Porchetta floating in a delicious pork bone broth. 
It was savory AF.
The bowl was also filled with a mélange of pickled veggies that cut the fattiness of the dish. 
The egg wasn't the Shoyu Tamago I was expecting but more of a Onsen Tamago...which was cooked to perfection. 
The yolk made the broth creamy AF.
To top off the dish...was a cluster of Tempura Enoki. 
Never seen them served any which way but raw. 
They were sexy AF.

My wife ordered the Miso.
Essentially the same broth as the Tonkotsu but cut with some Dashi to give a little more depth and saltiness.
It was perfect. 
Along with the perfect broth were the usual suspects found in the Tonkotsu.
Main difference was the Confit Chicken.
Left a nice grease slick in your mouth that I think Im still feeling.

The lunch aspect of this tiny spot is a new concept for them.
Yes - THEY SERVE LUNCH.

Dinner seems to be more of a unique experience from lunch.
I took a peek at their menu.
(SIDE NOTE: Both of their menus change on the regular)
The dinner menu seems to lean towards a more non-traditional Japanese direction. 
A fair mix of the new and the old. 
I will surely go back to fill up on said menu items.

If it is still BYO there...then they are in trouble.
I may not leave.

Hall & Oats.
Liquid nitrogen. 
Wu-Tang.
Immersion thermal circulators.
Led Zepplin. 
Hydrocolloids.
Slayer.
20 month cured leg-o-pig 
Outkast.

What the hell am I talking about?

Awesome shiz that can be found at Square Root. 

Downstairs: pre fixe chef's table for 14. $95 for 9 courses during the week and $150 for 14 courses in the weekends. The menu is over the top and constantly evolving. Can't justify it? Then stop reading my review.

Upstairs: awesome bar with small plates. Their happy hour(5-7) is just plain wrong...$4 cocktails! You know what that means, d-r-u-n-k. The small plates are delicate and delicious. Order enough and call it dinner. I know we do. Side note: they use liquid nitrogen to chill their glasses for every cocktail. Why you ask? Who cares, it's awesome.

The staff is mad cool. They make for good conversation (things discussed: food science, predator movies, weather and which direction to properly wipe your ass).

If or when you go, wave to me and my wife. We will likely be getting our gluttony on there.

I know, I know, I KNOW.
They just opened. 

Guess what though?
I LOVED IT.

Im waiting anxiously to sample their actual brews (damn legalities) but in the meantime I have no problem sipping some classy brews they have hand chosen for my pleasure.
And my pleasure alone.
As is usually the case.

The first night was packed with some funky folks getting their sippy sippy on.
That includes me and my wife.
When we heard they were opening on our block we decided to go introduce ourselves.
...if you know what I mean?

Short story long:
Drank some great brews.
Taceaux Loceaux was present and accounted for...they may be a regular sight there.
Bakers Dozen was also present and accounted for...they had a table, errr, mountain of free donuts there.
(if you know me - thats a huge plus - Im a declared donut slut)

All in all though, a great and much needed addition to my hood. 

Now I have more than one place to make an ass of myself.
You're welcome Barrel Proof.

I cannot believe this place has such a strong rating on Yelp. I just had lunch here and it was a terrible experience. I was with one other person and we ordered two very plain sandwiches and had to wait over 30 minutes for our food. We ordered water only to later find out that they charge three dollars for each bottle of water they bring you. The bottles are the larger glass bottles you put on your table and share. They are clearly refilled with water as the seals are broken when they come out. Typically this is done so waitresses don't have to keep refilling your glass so I didn't think to ask "are we paying for this water?" and we certainly were not told by our waitress. Our sandwiches had very little meat on them and were a terrible value. Overall I ended up paying 35 dollars for two sandwiches and water.  The place was literally empty at 1pm, I guess everyone else in downtown Tampa has had the same lunch experience as us. Maybe they do a better business at Dinner based on the reviews here but lunch is overpriced and very slow. I will not return.

I had breakfast in the open outdoor bar area this morning...simply delightful! Do yourself a favor and order the Le Country Boy Benedict. I can confidently say that it was one of the best breakfast combinations I've had. Travis, our server, made the experience one to remember.

One hundred percent an honest review: 

I am not vegetarian or vegan. I can assure you after my meal that I did not feel as though anything was missing by meat not being included. I ordered the chickpotle bowl and paired it with the Halloween sauce and mild. Both were absolutely delicious hot sauces. At first with the portion I thought I would be left a little unsatisfied, but I was definitely surprisingly full. It was so incredibly flavorful. I appreciate that the kitchen is also open so you can see everything being prepared in front of you. I will definitely be returning to try more of the menu.

I am not giving Bayona 1 star because the food was bad.  It was good.  

I am not giving Bayona 1 star because they took so long to cook our entrees that we had to leave before eating dinner so we could make a 9 o'clock Preservation Hall show.  (note: we sat down at 7 and when I asked when the food was coming at 8:30 they admitted they hadn't started cooking it yet).  

I am giving Bayona 1 star because they treated us TERRIBLY when we realized we would have to leave before we ate so we didn't lose our reservations at Preservation Hall.  Our server came over TWICE to tell us that it was our fault and that we should have given them notice that we had only 2 hours to finish the meal because their restaurant is SO FANCY (emphasis theirs).  (note: during the trip we also ate at Sylvain and Herbsaint, which I would recommend over Bayona and were able to finish up in well under 2 hours.  Amazingly, they can somehow be really fancy and get you out the door in under 120 minutes)

The manager also came over to shirk any responsibility and let us know that he was basically sorry we were sorry.  Thanks for that, as the person who made the reservation I wasn't already feeling bad enough.  Then, for one final kick in the ass on the way out the door, our server admitted she was a "salesperson at heart" and asked if we would be interested in buying drinks for the road since they don't sell them at Preservation Hall. No thanks, I'd rather drink the sludge on Bourbon Street then patron their business.

There are too many great restaurants in New Orleans where the staff and management actually treat their customers with kindness when things don't go exactly as planned.  I'd give them zero stars if I could.

Used to like this place, but my last visit, the staff was incredibly rude.  It was a half hour before they closed and they were obviously irritated that they still had customers.  I mean, it's not like I was there to have an hour long meal, just wanted to take my gyro and go.  The cook flat out said "guess no one knows how to tell time" loud enough for their customers to hear..... maybe if he'd complain a little less and work a little harder he'd get through the line of customers faster.

The cashier wasn't particularly warm and bubbly either.

Good food, but I will never be back after that experience.

Of course we couldn't leave Nola without trying the famous Hurricane drink. In fact, we started off our day-drinking at Pat O'Brien's. The place is pretty big...with different bar areas. we sat in the courtyard area and were attended to super quick. We each got one of the hurricane drinks (plus the glass) as a nice souvenir. This drink reminded me of jungle juice during the college days but way better and scarier because one was enough for me!

One of the cute bartenders hooked us up with some shots before heading out. He made us do the shot without using our hands. It got messy! 

Dinner: Honestly - my meal here wasn't the best. I had the pasta and it lacked flavor and was on the colder side. The service was on point for dinner as well. I would def come back but only for the drinks!

UPDATE: The manager replied to my post and offered a free meal because of the issue we had. Great job!!

They changed the tortilla on the catfish tacos from a corn tortilla to a cheap flour tortilla that I'm pretty sure you can buy at Wal-Mart... Very disappointed. Please bring back the original corn tortilla. 

Great beer selection and libations.

When FF Crafthouse opened in December, those of us living in the neighborhood were so excited. This was a good brewery opening in a beautiful space. A few of us went the first weekend it opened. We waited more than 40 minutes for the appetizer and more than an hour for our main courses. It was pretty busy and it was the first weekend so we cut them a lot of slack.

I've been back three times since then. Only one of those times did the food come out in under 40 minutes, and during none of those experiences was the restaurant packed. A small detail that shows the lack of attention to detail by FF Crafthouse: every time we were there, they didn't have enough menus for the amount of people in our party. And again, it was never close to full. That's a very small thing, but these menus are paper - how hard is it to make sure you have enough for all the seats at the restaurant?

Onto last night's visit. We ordered our food and we waited more than 40 minutes for it to come. Here's how you know it was taking a while - our server came up to us and apologized multiple times for the wait. It should also be noted that our server was great and we had zero problems with her. During our wait, one friend tweeted that he was frustrated about the long wait. Another friend asked our server if she could speak to the manager to let the manager know that the long waits were a trend.

Once we got our food, my friend was given the wrong meal (a fish sandwich instead of a chicken sandwich) and tweeted that he was frustrated and that he'd continue bashing FF Crafthouse for their poor service. He never actually tweeted anything else while we were eating.

Then the manager came over to speak to my other friend, who very calmly explained that the long waits are an issue there and that we want to come back because we live in the neighborhood, but need the service to be better. The manager told her we hadn't really waited all that long and basically told us we were wrong to complain. Because we all had our meals and just wanted to eat, we moved on and would probably have come back at some point in the future despite the poor service and manager not being helpful.

Then, as we're about to ask for our check, out of the corner of my eye, I see someone - Brian Duffy - storm up to our table and slam his business card down next to one of my friends. In the moment, I thought he was going to apologize for the poor service. Instead, he starts yelling at my friend, saying something along the lines of: "If you're going to bash my restaurant on Twitter, you can leave right now and never come back." That friend hadn't been on Twitter at all.

My other friend pipes up and let's Duffy know that he has the wrong guy. So Duffy picks up his card, goes around the table, slams down the card, and starts yelling at him. At no point does he ask us questions about our experience. He just kept yelling at my friend and at the rest of us to be quiet when we tried to explain. He said that we need to pay our bill and get out.
Not having any interest in staying, we said sure. So he brings us our bill. Then as the 6 of us are trying to figure out who owes how much, he storms back over and yells at us for taking too long with the check. He says he wants us to just pay and get out because we're not welcome there. We try to explain that we're attempting to do that, but he interrupted us by coming back to yell at us. If it wasn't for not wanting to stiff our server, we would have just left without paying the bill.

Then he comes back over with our bill and says: "I apologize for the bad service - I've opened 83 restaurants and customer service is very important to me." To say you value good customer service after that display was galling.

Here's the kicker - he didn't even know we had spoken to the manager and received poor service from her. He had seen my friend's tweets and come storming over to the person he thought was him (wrong guy) and just started yelling without knowing anything about the situation. So after we told him about the manager, he said he'd talk to her, as if she was the biggest issue. He also kept saying phrases like: "your boy needs to grow bigger balls and come talk to me face-to-face". So you can probably ascertain the type of guy we're dealing with here.

He later tweeted at my friend both from his personal account and the FF Crafthouse account. From the FF Crafthouse account, he said that it's okay because my friend clearly has no influence. When my friend pointed out that he has more than 1K followers on Twitter and the Crafthouse has like 200, they deleted that tweet.

It was the most unprofessional customer service I've ever received.

Awesome Mexican food!

Located in the restaurant area of Westshore Plaza, this is really convenient to the AMC theater in the mall. Parking is insane in the area directly in front of the restaurant, but if you're going to the mall too I would suggest you park in the garage. 

We decided to eat lunch outside since it was one of those nice breezy fall Florida days. Its was really nice, with a fountain, trees, and mini cacti on your table. 

Our waitress was extremely friendly and knew the menu really well. She was training another waitress and she was also so nice. I was pleasantly surprised at the service!

For an appetizer, we ordered the guacamole. It was really good. Nothing mind blowing, but still delicious. It was free with a coupon we had, but I would still pay $10 for it... especially considering there were three avocados. 

For my entree, I tried the enchiladas suzias. It was sooooo good. They were so big...it comes with two but chips, salsa, and guac fill you up. I took one home for lunch the next day. The sauce was the best part. It was a tangy and creamy tomatillo sauce. It was simply an amazing combination! 

Our party also had the quesadillas calabazas. They had squash blossoms which were interesting, and the cheese was tasty, but I still preferred my enchiladas :)

They also bring out rice and beans for the table. Both were tasty and the rice was interesting--I think there were pumpkin seeds in it. 

At the end of your meal they bring you churros and a worry doll. The worry doll is cute and a cool touch. I was so hyped up for the churros based on the reviews here. I mean, they were tasty, but not WOW. But who could pass up free dessert??

I was really impressed by this place. I'm normally anti-fancy Mexican food (I like it cheap and authentic) but this was just great. I don't think I would come for dinner, but for lunch we paid $28 for two entrees and a margarita (our guac was free). 

I really enjoyed this restaurant and I'll be back!

I'm so happy this place is pushing my reviews into the three digits. 

Seriously, this place is AMAZING. I truly feel that I have been blessed by the Cuban sandwich gods by eating here. 

Situated on an unassuming corner of Central Avenue, this place doesn't look like much. Street parking is free down here and there is plenty. 

During lunchtime there will be a line. We waited for about 10 minutes, but that made me see that if you check in, you get a free cortadito or cafecito. 

I chose the cortadito (sweet Cuban coffee with a dab of milk). I also ordered a Cuban sandwich and a Lechon sandwich. 

The wait for the coffee was short, but the sandwiches took a while. While waiting I found the back seating area (very tropical and cozy) and enjoyed my cortadito. It was delicious, and I could see all of the bricks of Cafe Pilon in the kitchen. 

When the sandwiches finally came, I was foaming at the mouth. Once I rushed to my table and sat down, I dug in. 

Oh my goodness. I swear I saw the light. It was easily the best Cuban I had ever had. The pork was so tender, juicy, and flavorful. The Swiss cheese and the La Segunda bread were amazing, and the ham just made it better. I am craving one so badly right now as I write this. 

Keep in mind there was no salami, which is more of a Miami style Cuban than Tampa. But that doesn't matter. It's mind blowing. 

The lechon was good, but nowhere near the level of the Cuban. 

The only "fallback" about this place is the price for a sandwich ($8). There are cheaper, but none as good as this. However, if you're not super hungry you can easily take the other half home because they are huge!

This place is one of my favorite restaurants ever. Everything was just so perfect. I can't wait to go back!

Hey, I like football. And I like meat. 

I also like long strolls on the beach and the sound of children playing but that is neither here nor there.

Dining at Shula's was definitely a memorable experience. Just a few paces from the InterContinental Hotel's lobby, it was definitely the most convenient place for me to eat after a long day.

The restaurant itself felt a little stuffy and quiet, but the staff was not at all. Although extremely polished and professional, they were patient answering questions and explaining steak choices. As mentioned in other reviews, they actually start by bringing out the menu on an official NFL regulation football, with the weight and cuts of each steak. They even do a little presentation when they bring out all of the steaks, rare and wrapped so you can actually see what each steak looks like.

I ordered a lovely, medium bodied Cabernet - not too dry, not to sweet that tasted oh-so-good once it hit the lips. They also brought out plenty of warm, fresh bread for starters.

My steak was cooked to a perfect medium and was absolutely delicious. Just enough seasoning, juicy with each bite more succulent than the last. I'm not even a big steak eater, but this hit the spot.

The lobster mashed potatoes were also amazing and to my surprise, had more lobster meat than I anticipated. Just a heads up on the sides - they are enough for two people at least, which at least makes up for the price.

Overall, an exceptional meal with impeccable service.

Star Wars memorabilia, subtle bathroom humor and liquor nitrogen cereal puffs to go with my morning coffee? Yes, please! 

I first visited Happily Ever After a few years ago, when staying nearby at The Monaco, and was immediately smitten. The quirk level here is highly appealing to someone like me, that is a nerd *and* that still has their inner child ever present. This cafe taps into a level of magic that I only feel when watching The Labyrinth or Goonies or while eating a Pop Tart. 

Not only is this place filled with color and fun, but delicious and reasonably priced food and beverage. While I typically just get an iced coffee for the road, this past visit I couldn't help but be drawn to the sign outside and the images on Yelp of the Dragon's Breath - liquid nitrogen infused cereal puffs.

To my surprise, when I ordered it I was promptly given a laminated page filled with safety info. For a second, that alarmed me a bit, but as I read through the details, I realized they're just playing it safe. While most of the information was common sense, it's still important to read carefully.

It only took about 5 mins for my smoking cereal puffs to be brought out to my table and much like a bubbling cauldron, the visual is exciting.

Like anything very hot, or very cold, you've got to take your time a bit. The puffs are super cold and biting into one of them too quickly can be a little shock to sensitive teeth. Waiting a few seconds before taking a bite will take the slightest bit of chill off, so that you can eat them like the Real G that you are. 

Even when doing that, I was able to bite into the puffs, close my mouth and easily have the smoke released through my nose like the good little dragon that I was that morning. 

I love this place so much, that I'm pretty much making it a rite of passage anytime I'm in town. Can't wait to see what they'll be up to next time I visit!

If nothing else, order the Cheese "Hold The Beef" Burger. Instead of a beef patty, you're presented with a hunka, hunka, chunk of grilled halloumi cheese, topped with fresh tomato, avocado, romaine and lemon aioli. It's auh-mazing. (Plus, "halloumi" is just a fun word to say!)

This is truly a case where, "the cheese stands alone!"

Seriously, this was one of the best burgers (although it was kind of a non burger) that I've had in a long time. 

It's hard to remember what else was ordered other than that. In fact, I had to look up the menu on Jones' website just to jog my memory that I also ordered the Calamari Salad. Not too much to be said about it, since it's pretty much how you would imagine - fried calamari on top romaine with corn, onions and a spicy chipotle. The calamari was fresh though, and the batter not too heavy. The salad is HUGE.

But in the shadow of my halloumi sammich, the salad meant little to me. 

Overall, I really like Jones. It's almost like a sophisticated diner - it's open late, serves comfort, Americana and is a quick, cool and casual spot for just about any occasion.
The owner has responded to my yelp review SEVEN (update, 10) times.  He is insane.  I will never dine here again, not even for the mediocre pizza.

i went into pizza brain very excited! I came out extremely slighted, and angry! I was offered a free sample and it was a mediocre sliver of a slice with blue cheese and brisket which is a SACRILEGIOUS combination, and it tasted like burnt turds. Then as I was leaving I was ordered to "make sure and leave a tip" for my FREE slice of pizza!!!!!!!!! Not only was I appalled at the audacity of the owner to make this remark, but she stood in front of the door way to make it awkward for me to leave until I gave her husband a dollaR! THEY NEED TO WORK ON THEIR DINING ETIQUETTE  AND THEIR PIZZA SKILLS BECAUSE THIS PLACE IS UNPREPARED FOR PUBLIC INTERACTION!!!!!!!!!!

This visit started out so good.  When we arrived at 4:35 the 4 people at the hostess stand said we were 4th in line for a table for 4, and it would be 30-35 minutes.  It was crowded and busy.  They took my phone number and the 2 of us sat at the bar to wait for college friends we see about once a year.  I was encouraged by the bartenders, 3 of them checked on us and swiftly had our drinks to us.  They were delicious but the $10 for a margarita in a plastic cup was a little steep.  Our friends arrived 15 minutes later and we sat at the bar for another 30 minutes, checking a couple times while we watched empty tables of 4 nearby us.  At 5:30, after checking several more times, we were escorted to one of the tables we had been watching.  As we set down, a waitress and 2 of the hostess crew stood next to us having a vigorous debate.  They then told us (did not ask) that our table was committed to a group of 8, and we had to get up and move.  We were walked through the waiting crowd, past the bathroom and out to a table in the sand.  There we were seated, (at a table for 8), with totally inappropriate adirondack chairs around a picnic table where the now setting sun shone directly in our faces.  Since we now had nearly an hour in this place, we decided it couldn't get worse, and we didn't want to move to another restaurant, so we stayed.  It got worse.  It took nearly another 30 minutes to get a bucket of beers (we decided to keep it simple, since it seemed that was all they could handle).  No water or silverware yet.  Several more trips to inquire on our 6 beers and a wine eventually resulted in the wine and 5 beers brought to our table.  Another 10 minutes before our order was taken and we asked for water and silverware.  Another half hour later, and several more trips to the bar and hostess table, another server approached our table and asked us what we had ordered...  WOW!  Now it was ridiculous.  We watched the table next to us that sat down 15 minutes after us receive their food, and finish...  The food  finally was set down and was ok, but no apology, and no acknowledgment about the numerous mistakes and abysmal service.  The staff seemed under-trained and immature.  Waitress Elli gave rote and rushed apologies and then was off to spend much more time chatting with her friend.  No visit from a manager or a hostess, but a hefty bill that we all felt should have been comped completely.  Nice venue but other than the physical space and the bartenders, I do not recommend this place.

A blast of color, life and fun on this block! Today was the opening day and it was buzzing with excitement, happiness and cupcakes. Free samples galore and the attentiveness of the people who work here is unmatched. It's a cozy little place and full length windows allow you to see the baker hard at work =] I had the carrot cake and gingerbread cupcakes. Oh - my favorite thing about this place: They have MINI cupcakes. You can have one and not feel guilty - freaking genius.

Confession: I'm a sucker for fryer food. And Lee's does it right.

True, this place doesn't look like much. It's one of those gems that most people don't even seem to know about because it doesn't look like the kind of place that will serve up anything special. There are cigarette ads on the windows, cases of sodas stacked up, and plenty of outdated flyers for the lottery. But don't let appearances fool you: Lee's serves up some of the best cheap eats in the neighborhood.

The menu is solid, the soda selection will satisfy any of your carbonated cravings. And then there's the carrot cake. As a cream cheese frosting junkie, the Carrot Cake Man's offerings make any place worth a visit or ten.

And I'll echo what was said before about the pride the owners take in this place. In fact, they encourage everyone who visits to go on yelp and see what people say about the food (and the cake!). They ask, I oblige.

I had "The Game Over" chicken cheesesteak w shrimp & spinach & it was perfect. They make their own sauces & I had a spicy one that went well with my steak. As a kid in the 80s, I remember this spot being a classic diner with mini juke boxes at every booth. So it's pretty cool to see that although it's a different business, I can still get a decent burger, fries, & Coke.

I went here today for breakfast and I enjoyed myself. I read the reviews before I made a decision to give it a try and the reviews were all positive.
I utilized the option on here to add my name to the wait list and I must say it was useful.
When I arrived, I confirmed that they received my wait list request and then I proceeded to wait.
I ordered the 3 pigs omelette. It came with a choice of side and a biscuit.
I changed my choice of cheese to cheddar instead of Swiss. My omelette was delish.
However, I did not care for the biscuit because it was a bit doughy.
Overall this place was quite satisfying!

After watching the years of renovation I was excited to see the Rosewood completed. Situated on one of our favorite local beaches, we were excited to experience the new bar after a walk on the beach. My first experience - despite the welcoming message our community has received - was a really odd and cold experience. We weren't greeted us neighbors but felt shunned by security in suits as we tried to navigate to the bar, so much so that we honestly thought we weren't allowed. I have never felt more out of place in our own community. We tried to come back and had similar experiences and were even criticized by guests while we walked our dog on the beach as we have for years. Disappointed to see what such a special place has become such an unwelcoming environment.

This is the first time I've wished for a 6th star! What a delight Renee's is! We were our usual quartet of crazy gals, fully loaded with questions, special orders and Celiac and this place did not disappoint. The food is so incredible. Nothing GF actually tastes GF. Everything is fresh and locally sourced as much as possible. This menu is sure to please any tastebud or craving and their desserts look delish! I wish I had room to try the GF carrot cake but my entree was so good I couldn't stop eating in time to save some room for it. They have private booths and plenty of parking. Make reservations at Open Table for inside seating but you're always welcome to sit outside or grab takeout. This food is SO worth it, however you can get it! I absolutely completely and totally recommend Renee's Tucson.

I was excited about going to LUVi, but disappointed in the whole experience. The atmosphere is cute and cozy, but upon being seated, things started to go downhill. 

We ordered a bottle of sake, and it took more than 20 minutes for our server to fetch it from the fridge. My boyfriend and I both ordered the "Feed Me" omikase, and we're excited about balling out with some creative sashimi. (They're are 2 "Feed Me" options - $45 per person for raw and cooked food, $60 per person for just raw. We got just raw.)

This consisted of 5 teeny tiny dishes of raw fish. 2 salmon, 2 tuna, and one snapper. They were sooo small, and there was nothing special about them - just topped with some ponzu and mango purée. They had obviously made an effort with the presentation - there were tiny flowers cut out of mango slices and one tuna dish had the fish arranged like a rose, but these decorations weren't enough to distract from the rather boring taste. 

When our waiter came over to ask if we needed anything else I was so surprised I literally said "wait, there's no more food coming??" I did not feel 'fed' at all. Please at least throw in some rice or something!!

My boyfriend and I were very disappointed that a dinner that cost over $200 left us feeling completely unsatisfied. We went straight to Company Burger and each devoured burgers and tater tots. 

Who knows, maybe ordering the "Feed Me" was a mistake and ordering off the menu is better, but that makes me sad because typically omikase is a chefs opportunity to impress guests and really blow them out of the water. 

My tips to LUVI? Cut the price in half for the "Feed Me" or kick it up a notch with some more creativity and carbs.

Shaker & Peel is definitely making food right.  At our table we all ordered 2 tacos each, & all of us agreed the flavor combinations were brilliant.  Flavors are spot on.  The only issue was that the tacos were tiny & the prices were high.  I ate each taco in 2-3 bites & was done eating in 5 minutes.  And so I was still hungry.  
   My first taco was jerk chicken.  I could taste all the familiar jerk seasoning spicing & enjoyed it being paired with plantain & avocado.  So tasty.
    My other taco was grouper.  It was paired with mango & hoisin sauce & the combination was delicious.
   I want to give this place 5 stars for some incredibly great tasting food.  But I have to deduct a star for the tiny portion/price ratio.  I seriously wanted more because it was that good.  But the price prohibited that.

Church was canceled this morning due to the virus, so a bunch of us rode our bikes to Safety Harbor & stopped at CVT for waffles.  I gotta tell you I'm not a breakfast eater, but these waffles were amazingly delish.  I got a Guava Creme Waffle.  The waffle was not dense & covered with a good amount of guava sauce & melted cream cheese.  It was also sprinkled with toasted coconut.  Guava & cream cheese make a marvelous pairing, & the waffle was the perfect vehicle to deliver that pairing.  Lots of other cyclists sat outside with us at the metal tables scattered all around.  It was fun & tasty..& of course we all washed our hands a couple of times.

My husband and I took my parents to Adele's in early October and, I'm sad to report, it was quite a disappointment.  I've given it two stars (vs 1) for the following reasons:

The Good:
1. The burger was delicious (though I wish we had also tried the chicken).
2. I've had a number of friends who have gone and insist they have improved (and that the desserts are to die for) and perhaps I should give it another chance....however, there are the following things to consider:

The bad and very ugly:
1.  The services was atrocious.  From the minute we stepped into the restaurant we were not greeted with a smile, but rushed to a table next to a very crowded bar (essentially engulfed by the crowd).  Now, I realize we had an early seating (around 6:30 pm)- we were with my parents afterall, but it was hardly the blue plate special crew.  I politely asked if we could be seated at one of the many open 4-tops on the floor and the waitress scoffed, rolled her eyes and walked away.  She returned to reluctantly show us to a new, albeit not much improved, table.  The poor, mediocre at best service continued throughout the night with a less than enthusiastic staff and inattentive staff.  What is SHOCKING to me is that Chef Waxman was actually present at the restaurant that night, working the kitchen and his staff were not on their best behavior!  Sad for you, Chef Waxman!

2. My steak was super fatty and cold. There's just no excuse for that.

3. I ordered prosecco,as I was in the mood for some bubbles.  However, the waitress first poured it into a mini carafe and then into my glass leaving most in the side car where most of the bubbles went up, up and away.  When I inquired if this was normal and if was even indeed prosecco as it tasted more like flat, white wine, my inquiry was again met with a roll of the eye.

Hopefully those in the kitchen and management pay closer attention and show a commitment to service moving forward.

Oh and one more thing, I can't believe I almost forgot as this was really just the cherry on top of a sub-par evening...Toward the end of the meal, though with plates of food still in front of us, my Dad got up to go to the bathroom.  About 30 seconds after he left the table, a waiter swooped in, taking his chair from the table and handing it to another guest at another table.  The waiter walked away without saying anything to us.  We had to call a waitress to let her know about the chair hijacking.  By this point, my Dad was back at the table, standing, awkwardly, while his meal sat cold.  Without apology or explanation the waitress finally found another chair.  What a cluster!

Don't let the reviews fool you, there are much better places for food in New Orleans. The location is convenient for tourists, the service is friendly, the decor is cute, and they are open Sundays. The food though? Very forgettable.

Their Po-boys are made with seeded bread. Why?! Maybe if it were flakey and soft like the plain Leidenheimer bread, I wouldn't have minded the change. But no, it was dry and way too thick. At least the Fried Shrimp in the Po-boy was good and very generous.

The Gumbo with Shrimp, Crab, Chicken and Andouille was enjoyable, but it wasn't outstanding by New Orleans standards. The best gumbos have intense layers of flavor and this wasn't at that level. I could barely detect any crab either.

Yes, the food is still tasty and it's probably awesome for unknowing tourists...but if you are experienced in eating Cajun food, this will be a letdown.

You know those pleasant classmates at your high school reunion that you vaguely recognize, but don't remember ever interacting with? They weren't your BFF, the lovable class clown, the hot jock, or the annoying know-it-all, they were just there.

That's how I would describe Compère Lapin. After a week of nonstop feasting on my recent NOLA trip, I would rate my dinner here as solid, but forgettable.

I probably had higher expectations from all the accolades, and I wasn't blown away, but I did enjoy my meal.

Complimentary Biscuits - Served with honey butter and bacon butter. The butters were delicious, though I couldn't taste much bacon. The biscuit itself wasn't flaky enough and was slightly underdone.

Caribbean Seafood Pepper Pot - Very small portion, but large in flavor. Wish I had some bread to soak up that broth!

Spiced Pig Ears - A great app for sharing. Heavily seasoned, fried crunchy goodness. Served with smoked aioli.

Hamachi - This was the first time I had raw fish with guava and papaya, and I loved this combo!

Trio of Pork - My favorite main dish. That pork belly was so good - fatty, yet bright.

Jerk Black Drum - The fish was a tad overcooked. I'm obsessed with sunchokes, so I loved that part.

Roasted Half Chicken - Juicy, flavorful chicken served over rice. Loved the cilantro.

Semolina Gnocchi, Collard Greens - The gnocchi was too gummy in texture, though I liked the addition of collard greens and the general creamy comfort feel. 

Roasted Banana Zeppole - These were like banana beignets. Crunchy shell and delightful with a side of rum caramel sauce.

Soursop Semifreddo - A unique and more savory dessert. The celery and cucumber added an interesting green note. It tasted very healthy, but being a green smoothie type of person, I found myself liking this.

Service was pleasant though could be more attentive, timing was a long between apps and mains, and drinks took a while.

And that's all I have to say. TBH, my review is pretty forgettable.

We had brunch at Kenton's a couple weeks after they opened. Other than the smallest of missteps, the food and staff seemed like seasoned pros. Perhaps not surprising, as the husband and wife team own a whiskey bar and a tapas place in NYC.

First off, the restaurant design is stunning. A gorgeous marble bar runs along the length of the restaurant and showcases the 150+ whiskeys. A multi-panel graphite on glass drawing divides the bar from the dining area. Brilliant daylight shines through the large windows.

A proper New Orleans brunch demands booze, and Kenton's delivered. They have an impressive bourbon selection, even Pappy 12 and 15!...though they supposedly just ran out when we tried to order it. I'm more of a cocktail gal, so I got a Bourbon Bloody Mary and loved the smoothness.

Our table got the Island Creek Oysters to start. If you like briny, cold-water oysters, these were particularly good.

I had a Citrus Glazed Donut. They serve it as an appetizer. Hell yes - delicate sugary goodness with bright orange flavor.

My entree was the Grits with Pulled Pork. I love Carolina pulled pork, and I was in heaven with Kenton's extra vinegary version. The tang cut through the creamy grits and mornay sauce perfectly. And those greens! Omg take me back please.

I also tried some of the Chef's Breakfast which is your standard eggs, bacon (house-smoked), and potatoes. The star of the dish was the biscuit though. 

The BISCUIT deserves its own mention. This was literally the flakiest biscuit I've had. There must have been a whole stick of butter in there. The inside was undercooked, but the outside was perfection. Perfection I say! Ask for the Black Pepper & Honey Butter. It takes it over the top. If you are on a diet, this is worth breaking it for. Seriously.

Even in it's opening weeks I was very impressed with Kenton's and can't wait to go back to New Orleans to try them for dinner.

My last meal on Earth would be fried chicken. So of course I was excited to finally try this NOLA icon, but it didn't live up to expectations. I had my doubts when multiple Uber drivers said it was just okay, but being a fried chicken devotee, I had to at least try it myself.

We arrived early Monday afternoon to a 30 minute wait, with 10 people ahead of us in line. Not too bad. It took another 35 minutes for the food to arrive after placing orders. This was the slowest fried chicken ever! Luckily I had Mr. B's BBQ shrimp (one of my NOLA favs) for first lunch so I wasn't hangry.

Fried Chicken - As greasy as everyone described. Nicely crunchy outside, tender inside, and a hint of heat...but that oil was overpowering! Not my scene, but I can see why some people love it. 

Fried Okra - My favorite side. A traditional flour batter done right. Extra crispy and hot.

Butter Beans - Mediocre, underseasoned, and the rice was mushy and underseasoned as well.

Cornbread - This was a sweet cornbread, which I love. A tad dry, but solid.

Fries - I didn't have any, but my friends said they were average frozen fries.

Bread Pudding - A mushy, completely soaked style and very rum sauce forward. I enjoyed it, my other three table mates did not at all.

I wasn't impressed with the service - very apathetic and not friendly. This especially stood out in such a hospitable city.

We were also asked to move tables 30 minutes after we ordered to make room for a large party. I sort of felt like cattle, hah!

At least I checked this off my fried chicken bucket list. Next trip, I'll try the other spots recommended by my drivers - Mr. Ed's (I had a bad experience years prior but did not try their fried chicken) and Dooky Chase (another NOLA classic).

This review is solely for the hotel, not the food or bar scene. 

It's clear the Columns was once grand and happening. Now it's old, mildewy, and still happening. 

We stayed here for a weekend and the condition of the hotel was disappointing. Clearly the focus of the staff was on the night/brunch scene. The bar scene was lively each night, a wedding reception was held here, and brunch on the porch was popping as well. The Columns has maintained its status as a place to be seen.

Staying overnight here is another matter. The rooms are outdated and in need of renovation. The ceilings have settled unevenly, the paint is cracking, and the bathrooms are ancient (and not in a charming way).

We stayed in Room 16, the Sweetheart Room, the first night and there was a private balcony complete with nesting pigeons and a build-up of bird poop. Gross.

The bathtub was difficult to shower in - no place to set soap or bath products and a wrap around shower curtain. The supplied bath products were low budget.

The second night we moved to Room 10. While this room had no balcony and a smaller bed, it felt newer and marginally nicer.

The bed and sheets were comfortable. Guess that's one plus.

The check-in process was dreadfully slow. Their computer system was supposedly new, but loaded extremely slowly, and the staff was even slower. I understand being technically challenged, but this was a little much. 

I would not recommend Columns as a hotel. Perhaps the bar and brunch scene is worth it, but I had no desire to find out after seeing the condition of the rooms.

Not sure why this location doesn't have better reviews. I can only speak from my own experience - coming here twice.

The ATMOSPHERE is amazing. It's so open and spacious with high ceilings and tons of seating. On a beautiful Nashville fall day it's the perfect environment to work in with a lot of natural lighting and a great breeze when the big garage doors are open. The only downside to working for here - and general warning for those that do - is that they keep the music blaring throughout the day. Not sure why they choose to have it on max volume but I had a few calls for work in which I either had to go outside or keep my mic muted so that other parties weren't distracted by the loud music. Maybe that's their goal to not have people making those kind of calls/video meetings inside, but I wish it wasn't the case.

The COFFEE is genuinely really good. As a disclaimer I pretty much only drink cold brew now, but I really enjoy theirs! It's easy to drink, smooth and delicious. And their biscuit sandwich with sausage and jam in the mornings is also really good!

The SERVICE there has always been good - in my opinion - and the people behind the counter have been genuinely friendly.

I'm excited for this new location in Germantown and hope it stays a great place to work. Definitely check it out if you're in the area!

I make it a point to stop here at least a few times every time I'm in town, because I love the atmosphere and their cold brew is delicious! There are always a ton of people working and it tends to be consistently busy. Definitely worth a stop in to try.

Their food items are always pretty great too. The biscuit sandwiches are a delicious breakfast choice, and I really like their muffins. 

It's great how easy this place is to get to, there's always parking around, and the people that work there are super friendly. It's becoming a favorite spot in Nashville.

Not sure why I'm so late on reviewing Burger Up... it's one of my favorite places in Nashville. 

Obviously the burgers are great. But I also love the Turkey burger. The kale salad is one of my favorites in town. And their truffle fries are amazing. 

I think I also love this place because the vibe is great. Always good music. Friendly service. And it's not at all pretentious or trying too hard. 

Definitely hit this place up if you're in town. Obviously it's in a great area too!

Overall a great addition to South Tampa. However, the food was a little uneven. Loved the watermelon bruschetta, really enjoyed the veggie charcuterie and cheese plate (caulilini was the stand out, I would skip the turnip one next time). The triggerfish was ok--solid, but not up to the standard of our appetizers. However the brussel salad was so salty I couldn't eat more than a few bites. I should have talked to the waiter-- he was great--but I hate confrontation so I'm just writing a review like a coward.

Overall, we will likely go back, but at this price point I don't like having to worry every time I order something new that I might hit one of the landmines on the otherwise enjoyable menu.

I have always loved the cupcakes here.  That said,  it seems Jill needs to take some responsibly for the hostile workplace that has developed at her business.   Sensitivity training isn't a novelty and it's not difficult to procure.  Apparently the staff really need it.  Some will claim that anyone can sue for anything but my position has always been that if you get sued someone dropped the ball somewhere. 

I'll have to hear some positive developments on this front before I buy from Jillys again. I have no interest in contributing my cash to a racist workplace and there are plenty of other cup cake places around.  Besides,  cup cakes are a splurge,  not a need. Suck it up and do the right thing.  It's 2015 for crying out loud,  not 1915.

My daughter loves Scoop Froggy Frog.  My wife loves the Orange Smash.  Our dog loves the puppy scoop of vanilla.  I like all three of the aforementioned treats.  So not sure if I have to say more...lol.  For a nice cool sweet treat in the Florida heat, this is a great place to fill the need.  They have plenty of tables and seats with a bathroom onsite.  The employees are cheerful (I would be too if I got to sample ice cream and italian ice all day...lol) and there is a reward program!  Make sure to download the app and head over for something sweet!

Finally, a good BBQ place close to home!  I just hope it lasts. The menu was interesting with appetizers like hot tots which are tater tots and jalapeño peppers wrapped in bacon with sour cream to dip. It was as good as it sounds. The bacon was smoky and tender. Then I had a brisket sandwich with coleslaw. The cole slaw's crunch was a perfect contrast to the tenderness of the sweet brisket. The sauce tasted of honey and molasses. It's on the sweet side but very good. They smoke everything out back on the premises. they have a liquor license so I washed it all down with the champagne of Delco (miller lite). 
The bartender was polite and told me a bit about the operation. The waitress was friendly and attentive. I'll definitely be back soon. 
They've been open about 3 weeks.  Here's to a thousand more!

I enjoyed their drink so matcha that I actually went back the next day to get more! If you're ever visiting SB, def check this place out. They have a variety of aesthetic drinks and the taste is spot on. Drinks are pricey, but if you check into yelp for the first time, they offer 1 free BOGO drink of your choice. 

Bela Rose: 5/5 ($8.50)
All matcha drinks need to look and taste like this!! It's undoubtedly one of my favorite versions of the strawberry matcha latte so far. The matcha is mixed with strawberry-elderflower syrup & grenadine (syrup made from pomegranates), giving it the perfect sweetness. They make their own syrups in-house, so you won't be able to find this drink anywhere else! The matcha was subtle and not too strong and the drink was on the milkier side. Note that the drink only comes as an iced version. But I love how they garnish the side of the cup with rose petals - so pretty & aesthetic!

Jupiter's Forest: 4/5 ($9.25) 
Made with iced oat milk latte, cold brew, juniper berry, sage syrup, and infused with grapefruit. This drink was also super aesthetic - garnished with a golden flower, grapefruit peel, and sage. Personally, I'm not a big fan of cold brew coffee because it tastes more bitter than regular lattes. However, for those that appreciate cold brew, this drink may be for you!

We were so caught up doing some of the best restaurants in New Orleans that on get-away-day we realized we hadn't had a proper old school po'boy. We saw Serio's a couple days previous as it is next to where one catches the bus for the St Charles Street Cars. One of our crew mentioned he had been years ago, and it was one of his favorite po'boy shops. After several days of NOLA debauchery I am surprised we even remembered that conversation. See, we must of not overindulged too much, huh?

Definitely a well worn old space, but in a good clean way. We we greeted very enthusiastically at the "order up" counter. Liking this place already. The friendly lady recommended the fried oyster/shrimp po'boy, and I of course chose a local Abita beer to wash it down with. After you place your order you take the few steps to the other side of the counter to pay. There we were met by Mike the very hospitable 3rd generation owner. 

Yep, great po'boy indeed. Hot, fresh, and I dowsed it liberally with locally made Crystal Hot Sauce. As the label states: "Louisiana's Pure." Perfect get-away NOLA lunch. 

So step a few blocks away from The Quarter and enjoy lunch in relative quiet with mostly locals.
