Alrighty, I guess I am one of many that now shun the venerable Acme across the street, and may be joining them at Felix's for my preferred oyster bar in The Quarter. I say may, because some of the staff on the night of my visit should not be front of the house ppl. Standing around showing each other pics on their phones, ignoring customers, forgetting requested beverages, you know the drill. Luckily the one gentleman that seemed to give a damn came to the rescue to help save the day. I was close to walking until he stepped up.

I have been a loyal Acme fan for nigh on 30 years, with countless visits. Went there on a birthday weekend a few years ago, and most of the food was just plain not good. The oysters had a dull grey color, didn't taste fresh, and the Chicken/Andouille Gumbo was not up to par per their glory days past. Take into account that Acme always has a line, and Felix rarely does, well the decision was easier than I previously thought possible. Sorry Acme.

The char-grilled oysters last week at Felix's were plump and the buttery-cheesy-garlicky sauce was as decadent as one would hope for. The seafood gumbo was lacking any discernable seafood, but the incredible roux made up for it to the extent I barely longed for any actual pieces of sea-creatures. The fresh bread delivered with was begging to be dipped in both the oyster sauce and the gumbo. This meal was shortly after I arrived for my 4 day weekend, and it was a mighty fine way to get into the NOLA Spirit. Well except for the slackers on staff. In case mgmt. cares, I was there around 7:30 the night of September 21st.

I will give old Felix one more shot, and depending on how that goes I might have to resume my search for another old school Oyster House.

Of course with a name like WINO, this was on my must hit list for our recent NOLA trip. It has the same type of enomatic self serve system like our beloved OC Wine Mart here in Orange County Ca. This place has at least three times as many choices though. Unfortunately we just came from a fine dining experience with a lot of wine, so I couldn't take full advantage. But we did what we could. Unlike OC Wine Mart you don't need to pre-load your smart card. When you are through tasting the attendant plugs the card into his POS system and walla, pay the man. You can also set your limit ahead of time to avoid any surprises at checkout. There are tastes from $1 on up, with some great wines, and not so great. Definitely a good variety of offerings. 

The space itself is split into two small separate seating areas, both very chill and comfortable. The one staff member was a little standoffish at first, but warmed up after we engaged him a bit. I jokingly called him on it and he sheepishly agreed, and said it was because he was from Boston. He humorously stated that he is comparatively more cheery and that his fellow Bostonians used to ask him where he was from. Funny! 

A great after dinner stop with a friendly mostly young and female clientele, at least on the recent Saturday night of our visit.

If you are a wino like moi, definitely worth a stop. Cool area of NOLA btw.

This was our adoptive local dive bar over this past New Years Weekend, and the staff and regs were very accepting of us outta towners. IMO, not really a dive as it is a very clean well run establishment, with a professional caring and hilarious staff.

Over our 3 night stay, we prob stopped in 5 or 6 times. Quick drink on our way to hit The Quarter, and for our nightcap before stumbling back to the hotel. Later in the evenings they cranked up the jukebox and the whole bar loudly sang along. Reasonably priced drinks with several craft beers in the mix as well. Supposedly they make a mean po' boy, but I only tried a very late-night cheeseburger, and it was tasty, I think. It was after 1 in the morning for cri' sake. 

So if you are fortunate to have your hotel nearby as we were, this should be your ground zero watering hole. BTW - open 7 days a week from 11:30am - 8:00am. Gotta love those hours!

After countless trips to my favorite American culinary city, I search out at least one new spot on each subsequent trip. I really hit pay dirt this last time. 

I perused the Eater NOLA e-newsletter, and Bacchanal immediately grabbed my attention. After looking over their entertaining website I was pretty much sold on fitting it into my itinerary. After exchanging messages with long time Yelp Bud Qui C, who had paid a visit back in 2015, I was further encouraged to make it a must visit.

On a hot September noonday visit I arrived to an almost empty front of the house store like space, with a variety of wine and charcuterie choices. You make your purchases at that time, and pick up your food from the window facing the backyard. It is an actual old house with a spacious backyard, with live music daily from noon until 10:30 or so by 2 or 3 different bands. Check their website calendar for details. On my visit it was a local duo, the Tangiers Combo: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=B8xODK4FFlE. Perfect music for a relaxing hot New Orleans afternoon away from the bustle of The Quarter. 

My charcuterie plate was assembled with high quality ingredients of my choosing out of the refrigerator by a friendly staff member. See pic. It did get busier towards the end of my 2 hour stay, and it is supposedly packed to the gills in the evenings.

Bacchanal has been added to my must do list for all future NOLA trips. Thanks Eater and Qui!

Having been to New Orleans many times I try and search out a new spot on each subsequent visit.

This past weekend we chose Boucherie. I had read once that this was one of Anthony Bourdain's favorite NOLA restaurants, and from there decided to research further. Chef Nathanial Zimet previously started out with a truck he called The Que Crawl. And just like some of our most ambitious and creative young chefs/restaurateurs here in Southern California, he worked his way to a unique brick and mortar place of his own where he could better assemble a team to help with his vision and passion.

Unlike SoCal, Boucherie, like many other great NOLA restos is housed, well, in an actual house and not some random strip mall. Not only was the ambiance warm and inviting, so was the host and our waitress, and every other staff member that we encountered. 

Boudin Balls were mentioned in several other reviews, so after the refreshing amuse-bouche we requested an order. Loved the contrast in textures, with the fried crispy outer and soft slightly spicy inner of the mixture of pork and rice. They came with a tasty homemade garlic aioli sauce on the side for dipping. 

My entrée of choice was what was called Jerk Chicken. I have been to Jamaica twice and have had it several times here in the Lower 50, and this did not taste as though it had any traditional jerk seasoning. Semantics schemantics! Once my brain got over the fact that what I was tasting was unlike what I had before, twas a non-issue. Whatever seasoning that was used resulted in possibly the best chicken recipe in memory. Not only tantalizing to my taste buds, but so juicy and mouth watering. Will remember this for a long long time. Included alongside was a 'cheesy arepa, plantains, & wilted greens.'

We shared some wonderful collard greens that had grit fries resting atop, that we agreed were the best greens also in memory. 

Definitely worth the drive, or Uber fare, if you are staying in The Quarter, can't recommend highly enough. Now added to my NOLA must hit list for future trips to this incredible culinary city.

I've been here in the past with a white girlfriend (her race will be revelent in a sec) for lunch. We used the Axxess card bogo in 2015. Service was good, the duck burger was meh for me. Just an OK experience for us. Altho' I think it's a super cute and romantic place.

My son and I went there last night for dinner using the Axxess card bogo for 2016. I am white and my son is mixed but looks black. He has a mohawk and has piercings and tattoos. We were dressed nicely.

We were seated around 7:40pm. It took them almost 10 minutes to just come to the table to find out if we wanted drinks. The waiter was nice but over the course of the evening was very inattentive and took super long to bring anything or clear dishes or fill water glasses, etc.. 

My son and I kept joking about it being because of his skin color. There was another couple in the restaurant (50ish) probably with money and the woman kept looking at me. We've experienced this before in a less obnoxious way. People are curious what the nature of our relationship is. A couple of times, folks thought we were on a date. Anyhow...

As I thought about our experience, I wanted to write a review because I've lived in a lot of different regions of the country but the racism in SB is not like anything I've experienced, even in the deep south. I really believe that this server was ignoring us (whether consciously or unconsciously) because of my son's skin color.  When the check came, I told my son (he was paying) make sure to tip on what the bill would've been before the bogo. I think a fair 16% tip would've been fine, doubling the tax on the whole check since we didn't get great service. However, my son tipped him 35% to to disprove a stereotype. 

I applaud my son for his willingness to go above and beyond and show kindness to a server that gave really sub par service (BTW-we both have worked and do work in the hospitality industry). 

If the manager of Stella Mare monitors this page, I would be happy to talk to him or her about this. 

As far as the food last night, the escargot was delish. The Coq au Vin was meh. I don't know what it's supposed to taste like but the flavors were weak at best. I had a little bread and butter soaking up the yummy garlicky oil from the escargot and that was good. I had 2 glasses of champagne, also fine. My son loved his casseolet (sp?).

My message to the restaurant and the greater SB area is, not everyone is a rich white person, get over your racism and exclusivity and embrace diversity.

After skimming the other reviews on here by white people, a lot mention excellent service. so that does kind of reinforce my suspicions.

So many YUMS here. 

It's bright blue, you can't miss it. And more importantly, you shouldn't. Their hours are convenient and the service model works so well for social distancing. 

My sis and I have been desperate for some pupusas for literal years. I've attempted to make them, she's tried looking for them on several menus. We knew Pupuseria was out there. It just never felt ~convenient~ 

Fortunately we felt wild, while out running errands. Instead of driving by, we made a sharp left and turned in. 

There is a decent amount of parking, especially considering how small the actual restaurant is. The menu is posted outside so that you can call it in. They will bring it out to you. 

We only ordered pupusas. Mostly because it wasn't meal time and this was the mission-literally. We ordered chicken, cheese, and chicken + cheese. 5 stars for all 3. The 3 pupusas cost about 8 bucks. We placed our order inside and he gave us the impression that they require a minimum for credit cards (though he wouldn't say) so we did have to pay cash. 

I will be back to venture to the other side of the menu. Heck-maybe even the breakfast! They have a wide variety of Latin cultures represented both in decor and menu. Including many house-made beverages like horchata!

Donuts are a perfect food. 

Yet, they are so easily destroyed when not made with proper care and love (and yeast, because if there's no yeast it's not a donut, it's a cake, I will not listen your arguments with this statement). 

Jupiter Donuts is taking the responsibility of making a donut seriously and doing it total justice. They have a crazy wide variety of flavors. I appreciate the scarcity in that once they run out of a flavor on a day, she gone-they don't make more. Because of this it is important that you arrive early in the morning if you're hoping to have the full selection. 

The menu has all sorts of other food goods: fritters, sandwiches, CAKE donuts, and more. Sadly, no kolaches-however, they recognize and are aware of what a kolache is. For their acknowledgement of this southern delicacy, I have major respect. I only have tried donuts from Jupiter..I am intrigued and may dabble into the other items sometime. 

The flavor that blew me away the most was strawberry coconut. How have I never had a strawberry coconut donut before!? 

Okay. That's enough donut talk, now I'm sad they're gone.

Every star is earned on food alone. Seriously. We don't even need the ambiance or the service, heck we don't even need the complimentary table bread. We just need this sensational food ON THE BEACH.

I had the pleasure of dining at Grace on a Friday night with a reservation. We were seated immediately and greeted shortly thereafter. In fact everything about the evening was incredibly speedy. Personally, I prefer longer wait times for food so I wasn't over-the-moon about it, but I can see how most people would probably love that. 

The cocktail program is pretty groovy if you like sweeter drinks. And if you don't, the wine list is thorough! 

The food is what we are here for and by goodness I couldn't be happier just typing this and reliving it all over again. The best bite of the night has got to be the scallops with leek sauce. In fact the sauces overall pretty much blew me away. The orange blossom reduction for the cured tomatoes WOW. The lemon butter sauce on the mushroom pasta WOW. Dare I say....this place is....AWESOME SAUCE?! (Nope, sorry I can't I take that back, I tried it on, the phrase just doesn't sound right coming from me, sorry you had to suffer through that). 

It was fantastic to see the Chef making his rounds just casually scoping out tables. You could feel his sense of pride and passion. Everything tasted even better after seeing him. 

Grace is very special.

Okay I see, I understand now. Alessi Bakery isn't just an icon...it's actually awesome. Really stinkin' awesome. 

Alessi Bakery officially takes the cake - this pun was fully intended - for Tampa bakeries. E V E R Y T H I N G under the sun is available. Modern gourmet cupcake flavors, retro candies, traditional Italian desserts, Cuban staples, gorgeous custom cakes, old school fruit pastries. Did I miss something? I don't think so. I was a kid in a candy shop. It all so kindly priced too. I got a half sheet pan cake for under $30. I am still trying to do figure out how that's even possible. I have spent more at Publix! 

Now I know what you're thinking. Okay, Ginger the only reason you're jumping for joy is because they put a Yelp burst on your cake. YES. They did that, and YES it was awesome, but trust me...it's more than their technical abilities. It is the service. Everyone was friendly, especially the fellow named Jason that helped me. My cake artist if you will. He was enthusiastic, kind, patient, and so helpful. Jason even offered to walk my cake out to my car after carefully wrapping it and protecting it with parchment paper. 

And this brings me to a whole extra chapter about why Alessi Bakery is wonderful. It is massive. The parking lot is bad driver friendly, there's tons of spaces, and there is a ramp, so it's accessible. Attached to the bakery is a full dining room, again, massive and there are tables outside. The shop was hopping at 12pm on a Thursday and I didn't feel cramped or rushed at all. 

I love this for us.

The ideal coffee shop. 

The shop is cool and urban which makes it a perfectly Instagrammable moment, without being too ~trendy~. Because of this it's a place you can actually enjoy time and time again. 

The coffee is supposed to be the most important feature to address in regards to a coffee shop. And for Caffeine Roasters it is definitely the star of the show.  The brews themselves are simply wonderful. And if you're looking to be fancy, they got that too! The menu is actually really diverse. They have a solid lineup of flavors that are always available. The best by far being the orange cold brew (okay, yes this is just  my opinion). They also consistently produce seasonal flavors. And though they are called caffeine there are plenty of decaf options (both tea and coffee). 

Caffeine 
I have never tried the food, I must admit. But I can assume based on level of bevy quality that it probably holds its own. 

Caffeine Roasters rocks.

Hello yes #YelpsBigNightIn part 2 of part 2!!! 

This BIG night got huge with this pizza order. We called in the order a couple hours in advance knowing it was going to be quite a large order. 5, 18 inch pizzas to be exact. Ordering in advance gave them plenty of time to execute because we requested a 5pm pickup and just like clockwork they were ready right when we arrived. Loved that. Loved that so, so much. 

In fact the only thing I loved more than the promptness and accuracy of this ordering process, was the taste of these pizzas! 

The pizzas:
-2 White Pizzas, yummy as yum gets! They were full of big scoops of ricotta and had an awesome garlicy punch
-2 Plain Cheese, HOLY CHEEEESUS, they load this up with cheese. Totally my style of cheese pizza. The red sauce was pretty thick too.
-1 Meat Pizza, nice zesty sausage 

Overall these pizzas were large and in charge. The crust was nothing special, but it wasn't a throwaway. The pizza was great and the service the same, and the real standout of this experience was what a value it was. For all 5 pizzas we spent just under 70 bucks. This will be a go-to pizza spot when there are a lot of mouths to feed for sure. 

Really glad to have such a great New York Style pizza over here.

Y'all...it's Chuy's. If you've been to one you should know what to expect. This Chuy's does justice to the brand. The design is great. Probably the best waiting area I've ever seen for a Chuy's. You can wait outside, inside, or at the bar (I recommend the bar because the Texas tini...duh). I was delighted with our service. Everyone had a big smile on their face. The chips and salsa never sat empty before being replaced and our order came out hot, speedy and accurate. Pretty solid and satisfying experience. 

If you haven't been to Chuy's it's pretty simple: funky design, cheeky tshirts, margaritas, free chips and salsa, pictures of dogs, the word Texas a hundred times, oh and there's food-Tex Mex ~style~ . Basically, you don't really go to a Chuy's for the food.. it's definitely more about the experience. With the exception being the tortillas, because the tortillas are really great, almost pita-like. They're also super passionate about their sauces. If you're an enchilada person, this is a great place for you (unless you're some kind of an enchilada purist). 

Chuy's is a fun time and it's cool that we have one in Tampa Bay now. For me it's a nice blast from the past.

File this one under tried and true takeout. 

This is a small family run business. Calling in an order for takeout is like calling your uncle. It was an easy, cheerful process. They didn't even ask for a name for the order! Which I thought was crazy seeing as I was sending someone else to pick up the meal for me, but somehow it made it feel more personal? I can't explain this. 

We ordered a kebab platter for takeout. The meal comes with rice 6 kebabs (2 chicken, 2 lamb, 2 Kefta) and 2 sides. There's also some roasted veggies in the rice...roasted tomatoes are my love language so you know I was all over that! I really enjoyed that you get to choose your sides. They have many to pick from. If you're going to try a Mediterranean restaurant for the first time I feel like you gotta get the hummus. It's kind of like a benchmark right? And so we did. We got hummus and tabouli as our side dishes. Okay so dishes not so much as samples. The tabouli side was pretty teeny tiny. The hummus was very tahini forward. It was good but not like the super garlicky hummus I think most people are used to. 

I loved everything I ate, truly. BUT. I probably wouldn't order the hummus again. Also if you do order the hummus as your side I would recommend ordering extra bread. 

This was a solid meal. An easy process. Oh! And they give a little extra side of tahini.

I am just going to call myself out before anyone else can. Yes, I do have a pizza obsession. Whether I'm making it at home or ordering it as takeout, I eat pizza once a week. Minimum. Please don't tell my Dr. 

This pizza spot has been bookmarked for a minute. I love the menu because it has a lot of creative combinations. The photos on Yelp led me to believe the crust would be soft and fluffy and on the thicker side. 

I called in my order. One (complicated as usual) large pizza half Bianca, half goat cheese, add chicken to all. I was quoted 30 minutes. I arrived 29 minutes later and it appeared that my pizza may have been ready for a while before that. It makes me think that 30 minutes is just a standard "CYA" kind of thing. 

Very little to say about the customer service. It was pretty meh. Nobody was at the counter when I approached and the restaurant was completely empty...It was a touch awkward. It looks like a cozy space though, I could see how it would be fun for a little date night. 


Bianca Pizza: EVOO, garlic, mozzarella, ricotta, Parmegiano Regiano, and mushrooms. This was the better pizza. But still not my *fave* 

Goat Cheese Pizza: Their homemade tomato sauce, mozzarella and sun-dried tomatoes and duh goat cheese.

It's 2 of my favorite foods side by side. I don't even know how I could possibly complain? 

I love the atmosphere of this restaurant but there are a few less than choice tables. And frankly every time I have gone the host has attempted to seat me at one of those womp womp spots. Fortunately/unfortunately I speak host so I am able to be seated elsewhere. The back room is the best room FYI. Request it if you can. The music, the temperature, the vibes, everything really clicks. 

Before this re-brand I thought this was my least favorite Ciccio concept. It has easily stolen 2nd place for me now. The flour is better than the water, I can't deny it. I mean frankly the pizza options are totally amazing and what really sets it over the edge is that they use Gulf Coast sourdough crust. 

If you are looking for:
-Happy Hour
-Gluten Free
-Vegan 
-Cool vibes
-Funny servers 
-Pretty IG pics
-Delicious sauces

Water + Flour would be a great choice. 

Parking is painful, that is the nature of this area. They do allow people to park at Sweet Soul in the evenings!

Another spectacular, awesome, wicked, special concept by Ciccio Group...show of hands who is actually surprised? (no hands went up, I can assure you). 

Taco Dirty proves to be a testament to Ciccio's dedication to wholesome meals that feel clean and somehow incredibly ~dirty~. I only say dirty because it felt like too fun of a pun to ignore, what I mean by that is: delectable, rich, indulgent etc... it's food that feeds your body and your soul. I can't get enough. 

There are so many options and combinations. Despite feeling like a "small menu" there is going to be something to satisfy every palate here...so long as that palate enjoys southwestern flavors. 

I have never had the same thing twice here, and that is not something I can say often. It is the P E R F E C T stop for lunch. It is very much so quick service. Which makes it easy for to-go meals. I have never tried uber eats or postmates, but I can imagine they are a great choice for those services. 

Now, it's an equally awesome choice for dinner just keep in mind- if you're looking for a leisurely meal at a spot you can hang out at for a couple hours, this may not be the restaurant you choose. It's on a busier part of the street and is quite compact..so lounging here isn't totally an option. 

The ONLY literally only "criticism" I have is that the salsa is really a ~standard~ sauce option, if you don't realize this you may end up spending extra money for sauce on the side..I mean um salsa. So skip the chips and salsa and let your imagination go wild with everything else. 


Dang-I really need some Taco Dirty now.

Once upon a time this was the sleepiest little beach. The parking was cheap, coin only, and plentiful. The waves were nonexistent. And the sand was littered with shells on shells on shells. It was heaven. 

So now it's not totally the same. It's some of the most expensive beach parking this side of Clearwater. And finding a spot can bar darn near impossible. (Life hack: go sit at the very end of the beach on a side street and just watch for someone to leave.) It is still a perfect beach, somehow. The best beach for shelling and the best beach to bring a family. There are bathrooms, lots of food options, and since the water is so peaceful it is a great beach for parents with young kids. 

Pass-a-grille is my favorite beach, forever and always.

First time trying Engine No. 9, which seems to be a crowd favorite here in St. Pete! 

I knew what I had to order the moment I saw it: XXX Burger. For one reason and one reason alone, the pretzel bun. I have a soft spot for a soft pretzel bun. 

Called in my order and was quoted a 10 minute wait. Sure enough I arrived within 10 minutes and it was ready to go! It was packed well and included mayo, ketchup and mustard. The burger itself was really great and the pretzel bun totally delivered. I ordered the regular fries. They were decent enough. 

It was nice to exchange smiles and waves with another human. I am excited to return for a traditional dine-in experience.

First time ordering takeout from BRGR and I must say BRAHVOOOO! Their packaging is exceptional and the pickup is flawless. Everyone is in mask and gloves. We called in an order while on the road and were quoted a 20 minute wait. Since we got there before "20 minutes" I went ahead upstairs to pay and wait. My food was in my hands exactly 20 minutes after hanging up that call. It's almost spooky. 

But of course the food tasted great. I'm almost as excited about my fave dish: the Fish Monger, from my kitchen table as I am about it poolside at The Treasure Island Resort. The portion of greens seemed to be a leeeeeetle sparse tonight which is not a big deal because the serving of fish was still excellent, but when you pay $22.00 + for a salad you'd expect a little more salad... 

Important please read: ORDER THE FRIES.  I'm a sucker for their fries. I don't know if I even realized how much I miss French fries until tonight. Fries are friends. 

Glad you're back, BRGR!

If you have never enjoyed a freshly peeled and sliced apple that has been drizzled with thick honey and coated with cinnamon powder, then well your restaurant choice has just been made for you. You must go to Mykonos. 

Mykonos is one of the first restaurants at the entrance to the sponge docks, it's adjacent to a parking lot and has plenty of seating. For these reasons alone it's a practical and smart choice. 

Thankfully we live in a scrumptious and experience-centric world, where decisions don't always get made on practically alone. And definitely don't need to. Not when places like Mykonos exist. The best part of this restaurant is certainly the service. It's a family joint-and you can feel it. Nicole is the owners daughter, you'll see her here serving, prepping, clearing, cleaning, greeting...just about every "ing" there could be she's doing it, and she's doing it with grand, welcoming smile on her face. The entire team is working right along with her to ensure you are not only taken care of but truly enjoying yourself. 

The food is a hero in its own right or well gyro? Anyway the point is, it's sooooooo yummy. Each table gets presented a basket of house-made fresh and fluffy country bread. I would urge you not to eat it all until you get a flaming plate of saganaki because that is when the spongy bread comes to life! (You can also purchase loaves of bread to take home). The charbroiled seafood platter was a masterpiece. The octopus maintained so much integrity even after being hit with the high heat. The sauce it is served in is seriously good. In fact the lemony sauce is also a perfect accoutrement to that bread! If you're a large party this appetizer is huge and therefore a great sharing option. We are not a large party, just a party. Therefore, for us we made it a shareable entree by adding a big 'ol greek salad (with potato salad, sorry, we are those people). The salad was stacked high and topped with gorgeous thick blocks of feta, it was drizzled with oil that ran into all the crevices of the cheese and sprinkled with flecks of pepper. 

The building itself is not glamorous. The A/C was cranked painfully high (probably to keep the cooks from over heating). And the locks on the restroom stalls were all broken or missing. So if you're looking for a fine-dining experience, this is not your spot. If you're looking for fine-food and the charms of a family restaurant then this is your perfect little island.

This Wednesday deserves a little #ThankYouThursday magic.  And so here it is. 

Thank you Fray's for being the closest donut shop offering me a real authentic yeast raised, deep fried, red dye 40 topped, donut. For a Texan gal a donut is real business. I can't be bothered with boutique-y cake donuts, or pistachio scented creams. Sure, there's a time and place for those shenanigans...but if we are talking donuts there's no dobuts about it Fray's is the top of the top around here. 

This location is arguably the best (Keep reading time see my argument for this). The drive thru is convenient. The service is wicked friendly. They are never out of red iced donuts (when I go). They give you a heck of a lot of napkins. Which on that note, why do donut places always have the lamest little, wafer thing napkins? If I'm getting a donut and actually wearing pants and shoes (I was recently informed that driving without shoes is illegal- so much for my perfect record) the parking situation is sufficient and the spaces are wide. 

Fray's is the St. Pete donut CHAMP. Please note, they are closed on Monday (ICYMI Mondays are optional according to St. Pete bizs) because absence makes the heart grow fonder.

Some people love a scoop of traditional vanilla ice cream. Maybe topped with a little hot fudge and if they're feeling wild sprinkles. Those people are not me. 

Minimalism is a great food trend and I am here for it. But when it comes to ice cream (and cereal) I am a total maximalist. Give me every topping, use every mix-in, and surprise me with the whackiest flavors...I believe you can probably guess where I am going with this. Revolution Ice Cream fulfills all my frozen dessert dreams. I don't want to brag but I might be their ideal customer. 

This artisanal shop scoops out the raddest flavors. Goat cheese, blueberry muffin TOP (yes just the top, it's the only part that matters after all), and pancake, just to name name a few. They're always experimenting and adding seasonal flavors to the mix, if you're not following them on Instagram (alternatively I would recommend stopping in weekly) you're seriously missing out. 

You'll also find classics like Oreo and mint chocolate chip on their lineup. And yes they do have vanilla. All of which shouldn't be ignored because they taste just as sensational as their more unique neighbors. Revolution also serves sorbets(strawberry basil? Yes puhhhlease) and vegan ice creams. The coffee vegan ice cream is the best coffee ice cream I have ever had, it's also the best dairy free ice cream I've ever had. Don't take my word for it-try it! 

And do you know what the cherry on top of all this ice cream goodness is? The people! The team is energetic and engaging. Talk about ice cream ~social~.

Thanks Rev, for being my friend.

I have been feeling super bitten by the travel bug and so it was time to take a little tropical vacation. A culinary vacation that is. 

The Floribbean is exactly what I needed to scratch my itchy (tavel) bug bite! The whole experience was a breeze. I mean a fabulous beachy breeze! The current takeout setup for COVID-19 is as easy as placing an order online (including payment), walking in and picking up your order. There was absolutely zero face to face contact. 

The actual space is totally cute. I can't wait to enjoy future meals there with friends. The colors are bold and graphic and the outdoor dining area is awesome (or rather will be when we can use it again)! This fits in perfectly with the vibrant Grand Central District. 

The biz model is "build your bowl." Yes, super trendy. Overdone? I don't think so. If there is anything I love, it is customization. Tonight I chose to start my bowl with the smoked paprika chicken as a base. The meat was tender, cut into perfect bite sizes and flavored very well. I was anticipating more heat but it was definitely very mild. I added the pineapple quinoa, plantains, and sweet potato. The sweet potato tasted like a patatas bravas and the quinoa was super filling! (my husband got the slaw, I stole a bite and I wish I chose that over the quinoa). I ordered the chimichurri sauce, but didn't end up using it at all. The meal itself was saucy and zesty enough without! So I plan on saving the sauce and drizzling it over some eggs in the morning, or maybe mixing it with some hummus? 

I also ordered the chips and guacamole. THANK GOODNESS. Because woah, these are a can't miss. In fact this might be topping the charts for St. Pete guacs in my opinion. The chips are also definitely worth it. Big flakey pieces of salt and a subtle hint of lime. I am ready to eat them all over again!

Thank you, Floribbean for being my instant vacation.

They say north Howard is going to be B I G and with businesses like PSOMI coming in I do believe they might be right! 

PSOMI is Mediterranean like I've never experienced before: ultra modern, totally playful and to be honest just kind of fancy (I felt like a fancy lady eating there (idk)). Of course as Mediterranean food typically is everything is super fresh and vibrant. An indulgent meal because of healthy fats and flavorful oils but it doesn't leave you feeling useless and miserably stuffed! 

Parking: not great, but worth the hunt. Be patient. And be prepared to walk. 

Service: there was a bit of wait for a table past typical lunch peak which leads me to believe there might always be a wait. The server was exceptional, he was friendly and made gentle recommendations. They employ one of my favorite service elements: boxing your food for you (the server took time to wrap my sandwich in parchment paper, seal it with sticker and put it in a proper to-go box!) instead of just throwing a styrofoam box at your table. The water glasses are small which is another testament to the service because it never sat empty. Remarkably enough while there was a wait for the table the food service was very speedy! 

Food + bev: yummy in my tummy. As I mentioned before these flavors are fresh and just good in a natural way. My favorite part of my meal was actually the latte (I have since been back multiple times for that alone). I ordered the Farm on Your Table my lunch date got the Pork Gyro and generously let me steal some Greek fries, as I opted to get the dressed greens on the side instead... because health (eye roll). This is my one note of advice-maybe don't get the dressed greens unless you really are trying to watch the waistline. The little salad was just ok and as far as value for money goes it definitely falls flat in comparison to the fries. Okay wait one more piece of advice! Order dessert! Even if you have to take it to-go! The baklava coffee cake was one of the happiest bites of my month, and I want everyone in the world to experience it. 

PSOMI is the real deal, treat yourself to a luncheon out!

My family held a Celebration of Life for my late grandmother at Currents this past weekend. What was a really difficult day was made a bit better by the exceptional service and care from Currents (and the spanakopita, we cannot forget the spanakopita). 

We filled the event room with lots of pink, pictures, and poems. The staff kept the food coming, the water topped off, and even serviced the room for the cash bar. I was really appreciative of their care. And really impressed by the space itself. Tarpon Springs is so lovely and this unassuming building boasts a dope event room! Who would have thought?! The event room is fully AV equipped. There is a large projector screen, and it has it's own restroom.

Updating this review because Ted Peter's has never missed a beat when transitioning into takeout only and then back to "dine-in" or rather patio dining. 

I love to buy whole pieces of smoked fish instead of the plated "meals." You can purchase per pound and it's a great way to feed a crowd. Just keep in mind instead of going to the restaurant part you actually purchase the whole fish from the smoker. You will have to go the restaurant to purchase dip. 

My family and I did a blind fish dip taste test with a few locally made dips last weekend  and every single one of us were able to pick out Ted's within seconds..it is just that good. 

Seriously cannot sing enough praise for this smoked fish dip.

Hello yes it's me eating dinner at 9:30pm because it took 3 hundred years to get tacos today. Was it worth it? I mean yeah? It was worth it! If anything I feel like I was really a part of something today! Which is so refreshing after feeling so isolated for so long. 

Okay, so Don Pancho Villa, that's why we're here. My review is based on food alone... YUM! AUTHENTIC! CHILDHOOD! This is what I am talking about. Thank you for bringing me a little nostalgic flavor fiesta tonight! 

It's Cinco de Taco Takeout and so obviously I indulged in some tacos. The tortillas were nice and warm even after making a 30 minute trip home. I was super stoked to see how generous the dressings were on top. I am rarely satisfied with the amount of onions I get on tacos but they really nailed this one. 

The fajitas were a standout! The peppers were cut thick enough to keep a crunch which is very important in a good fajita. The chicken was smoky, flavorful, and totally not dried out. The accoutrements for the fajitas were a meh. But fortunately they tasted good enough without sour cream and cheese. 

Honestly, I'm stoked about this place. There's a lot more to discover. I have just scratched the surface. 



I feel it's unfair to factor in experience when a) global pandemic and b) taco holiday. I will share with you that I do not at all recommend Don Pancho Villa for anyone that is at high risk right now for COVID-19. They do not seem to have the infrastructure necessary to accommodate safe social distancing.

If I was a musician I would probably write a love song about Osteria Natalina.

There's absolutely everything to fall in love with about this restaurant. It's unpretentious and delicious. It's warm and relaxing. It's hospitable and unfussy. It's somehow as relaxing as it is enchanting. I mean how often is it you get to feel enchanted, transported, dazzled, and energized without feeling all of your senses rushing. In fact the experience is so understated that you can actually allow your taste buds to get all the action for themselves! 

I loved loved loved the princess sauce, so much so that it reminded me that I do LOVE simple pasta after years of convincing myself it's not for me.

They serve beer and wine and have several specials available. AND serve yummy table bread with olive tapenade. 

For any Italian food lovers and skeptics this is a MUST GO.

Another amazing, brilliant, remarkable 5 star business here in downtown St. Pete. Their current processes for health and safety are sheer perfection. 

How this works right now: 
-Only 1 customer is allowed in the restaurant at a time.
-You can order at the counter and have your food brought out to you
-  You can order ahead and take advantage of their contactless pick up. They even have the code to scan the menu outside so that you can order once you're there. 
-Plenty of picnic tables outside for dining! 

Highlights: 
-Speed of service is mind blowing. Sometimes I wonder why we ever bother with "fast food" when great food can still be SO FAST! 
-The fully vegan friendly menu has a wide variety. 
-The dessert case is stunning and makes you want to get everything (maybe this isn't a highlight maybe this is a negative idk) 
-The food tasted AWESOME. 
-The price is approachable. 
-They have recycling and use compostable packaging. 

I chose to order the G-mash lettuce wraps, the Love Burger, and a lavender lemonade. The burger (black bean and beet patty on sourdough bread) came with a side and I wildly chose potato salad...BEST DECISION EVER. This was my favorite part of the meal honestly. The potato salad is loaded with dill and has just enough faux mayo. I want to order buckets of it. The only part of this meal that I wouldn't order again is the lemonade. It was good but not worth it. Does that make sense? 

All in all this is a special place. I am so impressed by how friendly and lovely and wonderful everyone was AND how seriously they are taking health and safety. This is a role model business. Everyone should be taking notes.

This was everything and nothing that I expected all at once. 

Yelpers are spot on by capturing the atmosphere. It's old school, it's unchanged, it's unbothered, and it's kinda fun. When I visited it was pretty empty, I wish it was a little busier because it would have given the place the energy I think it thrives from. We came for steamed blue crab, and steamed blue crab only. Of course we were also reeled in (yes please laugh at this pun) by some other menu oddities, like cheese curds and tater skins...

The crab was the star of the show! Even my Maryland born and raised father-in-law was impressed. I like to think this is probably a great spot when it's a prime hour. 

Service was a little slower, it might be that the food takes a while but if you're going I wouldn't plan to rush! We had a solid 2 hour experience.

Buya is dark, artsy, moody and brooding, for a second there I thought I was describing all my ex boyfriends. 

It's great though and it makes you feel A+ about yourself, okay so it's nothing like my ex boyfriends. 

Where were we? Oh yes, restaurant atmosphere. It's insanely vibey. I was looking forward to a summer hanging out at the bar to chill out and COOL down with their awesome cocktails and even though that's not happening it remains a great restaurant for takeout! 

The pro menu moves at Buya:
-VEGETABLE GYOZA If this sentence isn't enough to convince you go check out the presentation in the pics...that's right now you're ordering it. 
-The Chicken Ramen (add an egg, do it for me please).
-The Chilled Ramen, yep that's right, can I get an Amen from my Floridians? 

Mushroom ramen is my favorite of the ramen world, however at Buya I do fully believe the chicken is much much better.

This food is really just okay, I am not surprised that it was mediocre - the people of Yelp have informed be. But I was dining with a friend with several allergies and a vegan friend they knew that they could eat here as they had dined there before. 

As soon as we started talking to our server my friend disclosed all the allergies. One of them being a very serious dairy allergy. Couple that with the vegan friend (this is a no cheese zone). We ordered the guacamole (she had it before) and he insisted we do the tableside version instead. It was several dollars more but we thought heck - lets amuse him. 

So he made the guacamole "tableside" we kind of watched but not really, it was a lot higher than the table and we had soOooOOoooO much talking to do. Imagine our surprise when he presented the guacamole and there was obvious CHEESE in it!?? I know what you're thinking - cheese in guacamole?! GENIUS and while I agree, my poor friend with the dairy allergy does not. When we asked he said he would bring them some of the guacamole from the back (the cheeseless one we asked for from the beginning and should have stuck with), he asked me if I could eat it and I shrugged and said I guess. Sooooo he decided that me alone would be eating a family sized portion of  $$$ guacamole?? I got stuck with the bill for a bowl of guac that nobody ate, and frankly it was super annoying. Even though the guac was good, my fish tacos were not. 

I can handle mediocre food but expensive mediocre food is a super no go in my life. One of my friends ordered a burrito that looked to be a good way to go for value at least. 

This whole review is a little TL;DR the table side guac has cheese, entrees are expensive, service is a little odd, I'd come here for drinks and salsa.

I had the pleasure of hosting a private event at The Hammocks at The Getaway. 

Firstly, going into this was extremely overwhelming. Having a party during a pandemic?! Should I? Could I? Turns out, I could. I am so glad I did. I pulled together a pretty tight guest list to surprise my husband with a little party. Even though the guest list was small, I wanted to ensure folks felt safe. Which is why I had some pretty specific requirements: private venue, outdoors, with activity elements, and somewhere easy to get to for people from Orlando. 

The Getaway provided a perfect check for all my boxes. From there it only got better. Working with Brett was easy, he took my (many) calls and responded to my emails. He helped me set up a pre-order for our large party. The order included their pineapple wings which I would recommend to any wing aficionado, I also ordered the fish dip (My husband and I order fish dip every time it is on a menu, this is one of our mega lame games, I can't explain it.) which I was equally impressed with.  Brett also facilitated day of coordination by filling in the team and ensuring our space was set up and ready to go. (My guy, if you ever read this. You are an angel. Thank you.) 

Now as far as the actual party went? So fun! Wildly fun! The Getaway is an awesome place!!! It's well maintained, super cute, there are sooooo so many activities. We were able to bring our own paddle boards so that folks could jet off in the water for some playtime. There are plenty of hammocks. They provide jenga and cornhole. It was a hostess' dream. AND I didn't even have to fill my guest's drinks, because the awesome service team was totally on top of it. Major kudos to Matt and Aaron for being A team, even in the Florida heat. 

Things to keep in mind if you plan to host an event at The Hammocks at the Getaway:
-There isn't music, so bring speakers or maybe ask if they can set some up? Luckily the live music was loud-ish so we were able to hear it a little bit. But the lack of music was the only hindrance to the vibes. 
-The contactless menu thing was a little rough for the setting. If you're hosting an event I would print out little drink menus to provide your guests with, this way they do not have to scan the codes or waste the server's time asking a bajillion questions.
-Most importantly...bring bug spray. Lots of it. The bugs were out. 

I can't believe it took me having to throw a party for my husband to finally pay a visit to The Getaway. The name is crazy perfect. It was literally like being on a mini getaway. The experience was completely immersive and genuinely so enjoyable. Knowing how incredible it is...I cannot wait to go back.

I keep going back to Bodega and expecting slash hoping for a 5 star experience and it just never quite happens. 

I love the vibes. Even the shiny new location is poppin and feels mega cool. For me the food is just meh. Cuban sandwiches are a sensy topic. So I won't even say it's not my favorite Cuban. Because beyond that I find all the food to be just good.  The chicken sandwich is a great example! It sounds amazing: citrus, cilantro, mustard, chilis, and then you get it and you're like oh okay. 

It's a fun spot, the prices are a huge relief especially as you start getting closer to downtown on Central. The location is amazing. And so I will be there again and I would say you could should go too! If you are going to get a sandwich I recommend the Cuban over anything else.

I have been interested  in eating here since I first saw them listed under hot and new on Yelp. After following them on Instagram I knew a night with Shaker & Peel was going to be a priority. So how did I let so much time go by before getting my tush over there? Are we human or are we dancer?? I don't know y'all, I just don't know. But now that I have finally gone I can assure you I will not let so many months go by before returning. 

Basically even if the food was mediocre this place would rock. It's social media presence is fun and engaging, the space is awesome, and the service is A++++. Oldsmar needed this, and even though I am super jealous, I am glad they have it. 

We had a leisurely dinner here recently (during social distancing), and felt completely safe and taken care of. The tables are spaced far apart and even though they don't take reservations they are doing a great job managing crowd control. 

Our server was the bees knees. Not just because she put up with our shenanigans and didn't even flinch when we pulled out a deck of cards to play a rousing adaptation of Gin while enjoying a killer gin cocktail (Calm Before the Storm, earl gray infused gin and lavender simple syrup, oh she's cuteeeee) and a mezcal margarita (Smoked-Kiss Margarita, which has a deeply magnificent floral nose-it's like a fancy smoked meat on an expensive charcuterie board). She was a genuinely friendly and cool person-like I should have friended her on Facebook friendly. 

For every round won, winner got to put in an order. In the lead with 3 wins I chose the manchego queso, and asked them to hold the chorizo. I wasn't confident this was something they would be able to do-from
My experience most quesos with meat cannot be customized but you know what!? They could and they did and the server didn't even care! In fact she responded by recommending her fave vegetarian dishes on the menu...which led me to my next pick: the flower power taco. The Flower Power Taco is every IG Influencer's  dream and something every foodie would easily give 5 stars to. It's pink because they use hibiscus in the tortilla and it's flavorful like you wouldn't believe because they put their street corn in the taco. SOBBING. 

My winning streak came to an end, my husband rounded off the meal with a few selections. The Korean beef BBQ taco, which we customized again by asking for the kimchi on the side. This taco was far from traditional tasting. It was super tasty, super unique, and okay-super spicy, if your palate is sensitive to spice get the Sriracha mayo on the side. We asked for the grouper taco to be served on lettuce (I promise we don't modify everything everywhere but I guess we were in a super tailored taco mood this night), it's a .25 up-charge for lettuce substitution, just something to note. It was worth it because the fresh crispy lettuce was a nice balance for the tempura fried fish. 

I could have stayed here eating chips and salsa all night. Oh, I didn't even mention the salsa comes with a verde salsa in addition to a regular red tomato salsa. Even though I literally despise having to pay for chips and salsa at a restaurant I didn't totally mind considering we got ~2~. The meal ended with some churros, and by some I mean a ton, for real if you're with a group (hopefully not more than 10 because social distancing) this is the perfect dessert to order. 


Already planning the next visit. A special taco shout out to our server, Gabriela, who made this night such a blast.

This is every 2014 hipster's dream restaurant. And that's because 2014 hipsters had great taste! 

This food blew me away. 

We chose to go on a Saturday for an early dinner and sat at the bar. They were pretty empty when we arrived at 5:30 but were totally full when we left at 7. The lesson  here is to go early! If you do have to wait for a table you can order a drink at the bar and wait with it outside though, so this wouldn't be a bad option. 

I loved the wine list. Including natural and organic wines. There's even a daily wine special which is a premium wine that they offer at a generous rate by the glass. The food specials when we visited were so enticing! The menu looked amazing but I couldn't resist the sound of the pesto gnuddi and salmon specials. 

This dinner delivered in every way. Visually stunning, big portions, and so darn flavorful. A truly wonderful meal. Worth every dollar, star, and rave review.

I've said it before and I will say it again. Maple Street Biscuit Company does the best I said it BEST job staying hyper local despite being such a big brand. It is not lost on me or this community. 

My first visit to the Seminole location was effortless. From the easy access and ample parking, to the just 6 minute wait for food, and the helpful staff. I ordered the sweet potato fries for the first time and WOAH BABY I have been missing out! I think they are the best sweet potato fries I have ever had, it was like a Thanksgiving meal with chicken instead of turkey altogether. 

Maple Street Biscuit Company is a gem.

Updating this review to a full 5 stars because seriously this place is great! I love the service and everything always tastes perfect. This was my first visit back since January and I genuinely couldn't have been happier. 

Things I love most:
Goat cheese dip 
Spanish tortilla
Happy hour dealz
That bread, oooooh goodness that bread 
The pesto with the bread 
Service, it's beyond 5 stars easily 

Keep in mind that Happy Hour is only available in the bar area.

I am currently typing this review as I stand at my kitchen counter eating a piece of  leftover margherita pizza from TuttoRosso. Did I even bother warming it? You bet I didn't. Cold pizza is one of my ultimate guilty pleasures but even if it wasn't this pizza is good enough that I don't think it even needs to be warmed! 

I dined at TR on a night amidst a busy spring break week here in St. Pete beach. No table sat empty and the front was full of sunburned tourists waiting for pies to-go. We almost bailed-until we saw 2 free spots at the bar. 

The bar tender quickly brought us some menus and spieled a rather intense list of specials, probably at least 6 dishes to compliment an already diverse menu. We needed time to absorb all that information, obviously so we started with beer and sangria. The sangria was delightful! With no sweetener added it was refreshing and warming all at once (it was also a hefty glass-full and pretttttty strong). 

We eyed the garlic knots on our way over to the bar but decided not to order any because ~carbs~ . We felt content with the decision but apparently the universe wasn't because wouldn't ya know it! The salad we ordered instead actually CAME with bread! 2 pieces of focaccia and 2 knots: this is serendipity. Note: the dressing comes on the salad unless you request otherwise. Oh and the bread? WORTH THE EXTRA CARBS. 

The pasta options look great but we were there for pizza (as you know). We chose to get 1 pie split, half bianca and half margherita. I can't say whether I preferred 1 to the other because they were both fantastic. The crust was the star for me, personally. I also really liked how much cheese you get. I am a shameless "xtra cheese pls" kinda gal so it's rare that I find the ratio of bread to cheese this perfect, unaltered. 

A totally surprising bomb pizza place over here in the beach side. I look forward to many more visits. And, yeah-you should too!

Something about family-run businesses really do it for me. 

My visit was short and sweet. My order was small. I really enjoyed the summer rolls. I went in at a really peculiar time (like 3pm?) and so I got to watch as the team enjoyed their family meal before evening service really picked up. Even while there was an obvious lull in business and they probably rarely *have* to help anyone during this time, they gave us great attention and the service was speedy! 

The lunch specials are on the very back of the menu-I highly encourage you take advantage of those. The prices are totally on par for a sushi spot like this. But those lunch specials make it super affordable!

Find me a millennial who doesn't liiiiiiive for a fully personalized, customized, romanticized culinary experience and I will give you a $100*. But for real any restaurant that finds a way to make it your way earns major stars in my book. And when they can do that sans an assembly line...BONUS stars. 

Lolita's makes it all about you. They don't even have a wine list. You tell them what you like, the style of wine you're in the mood for, and the name of your pet (kidding). And they bring you a few wines to sample. They work with you to find your perfect wine. 

The experience gets even more custom as you move on to the menu. A full page of "build your own." This cheese board is all yours. From the pickles, jams, to the ratio of meat and cheese. In addition to the main event (the board) you can compliment your meal with a variety of tapas. The dates are the best dates I've ever had. I'm screaming still. Can you hear me screaming!? Order the dates! 

The music is at the perfect level. The lighting is slightly moody. The tables are spaced well. The service is relaxed and still refined. 

There is nothing that could have made this dining experience more or less magical. 


*Monopoly dollars

Even amidst a pandemic this business SHINES! I heard they started doing deep dish pizza as takeout became so necessary and so I had to scope this out of myself. 

It is TRUE. The menu is super abbreviated  at this time (considering how big it was before especially) but the addition of pizza is a total game changer. Now I can indulge in a proper martini AND pizza. My 2 favorite things. The deep dish itself is great, its a build you own style, so we love that! I chose to add onions and spinach. They let us do a half and half so that my husband could also add sausage. Overall it was solid. There was about 30 minutes between placing order and receiving pizza. They did give us that heads up. We had plenty of boozy martinis to savor while waiting, and so it wasn't even an issue. 

I genuinely have so much respect and adoration for O'Bistro. There are zero gimmicks or trends or cool points. It's just simple, timeless, and lovely.

I think I was really supposed to like this restaurant. I didn't. 

I actually had a relatively bad experience overall. The space is super cool and made me feel like I was in episode of Gossip Girl. The cocktail list is pretty cool. You could convince me to come back for drinks I think. 

It could have just been a really off night. 

Our server was not happy to be there at all. The service time was painfully slow. The cocktail took longer to come out then our first sushi roll. The fish in the sushi dinner tasted like it possibly got really dried out. They were all rubbery. Maybe they sat an expo counter too long. Maybe it wasn't great cuts of fish. Who knows. We waited for our bill for 27 minutes. Literally sitting there with empty plates and drinks in front of the whole time. It was odd. And it was uncomfy.  Beyond that we were so close to a table next to us that I could smell the gentleman's BO. 


The Kamikaze Roll is what intrigued me the most to go here, and it was actually the most redeeming part of the meal. It was super spicy, and super exciting tasting. The prices are impressively low. The sushi dinner comes with a house salad and miso soup and comes out to under $25.

Hooray for #FirstTasteFriday! 

My culinary adventures took me to Asiatic Street Food and Noodle Bar after it has been sitting in my Collections collecting dust for much too long. 

The ordering system is so easy and it's even adapted for mobile browsers! HALLELUJAH! And picking it up was just as seamless. There's 2 entrances for this restaurant. When you're looking at the building, go to the left for takeout. A gentleman opened the door for me, my order was sitting there waiting for me. They offered hand sanitizer and had plenty of smiles to share as well. 

*I did have to ask for chopsticks and napkins for my takeout order* 

For my first taste of August's First Taste Friday, I went with the steamed dumpling. Aka gyoza. Pretty pleased with my decision. This bite was so nice. Great proportions, it stayed warm and the flavors were gentle. It was everything you need from a stuffed pillow of tasty joy. My second bite was another dumpling, the potstickers. This version was fried, served with a slightly more garlicky sauce and just as delicious as the steamed one. Each order comes with 5 pieces. While it would have been nice to have some variety in the fillings (veggie, pork, shrimp) it's cool to see that they offer chicken, which is definitely more of a rare find for potstickers and gyoza. 

A lotta love for these little guys. Totally successful takeout trip!

I have had Florida Orange Groves Winery bookmarked for the longest time. I was saving it for a fabulous girls' weekend...and then all weekends got canceled... 

Instead of waiting around to do a tour of the winery I decided, to heck with it! I might as well try their wines! So that is what I did. This week I picked up a bottle of Hurricane Class 5. Which is a bottled sangria. The packaging is totally what drew me in initially-I mean come on this is so on brand for Florida! LOL. 

The sangria is a blend of 5 of their signature fruit wines: key lime, pineapple, passionfruit, mango, kiwi and watermelon. The most forward tasting in my personal opinion is definitely the watermelon and lime. It's super light and sweet. 


Someday soon I will experience the full essence of Florida Orange Groves Winery. Until this I will enjoy all the fruity essence on my palate! Thankfully they offer curbside pick up AND they ship. A lot of times you can catch a free shipping discount code for purchases over $100.00.

I can't even explain through typed words how badly I have been wanting to go here. 

Alesia has funky town hours and so between the prices, the hours, the global pandemic, and just a multitude of options available it kept getting put off for another time. Finally, after years. Literal years it happened. 

Our last #FirstTasteFriday of 2020 was the perfect chance to try Alesia.

From my understanding they have only somewhat recently opened up for dine in again. Granted dine in is only available to patio. Sooo it's like dine with rather. The patio itself is gorgeous, and with the thinly string lights it made for a particularly lovely date night. We even added bubbles (in flutes) to make it that much more romantic. 

You order at the window and are given a number. From there it's self seating and the food is brought to you. For COVID reasons this is great. For leisurely date night it wasn't totally ideal. They did allow us to leave a tab open so that we could sit and relax as we decided on things to order. 

It was a brisk night. We couldn't resist the pho! The soup was lightly flavored. There were a ton of noodles. I loved that you get your flavor enhancers on the side so that you can choose your own heat adventure. The shrimp rolls were meh and the Vietnamese donuts were like fine. 

This dinner was exceptional. But I really attribute it to my company, the ambiance, and the kindness of the service. Because if I'm being super honest the food was really just okay. The prices are noticeable on the high side. I'd like to go back and try some of the more French inspired dishes-the monte cristo is calling my name. 

The menu has extensive coffee/tea options. While the beer and wine is relatively limited. There are a few BTG options all ranging from $13-$16 a glass. 

Maybe I over hyped it after years of yearning. Any-who it's earning 4 solid stars from me.

Apparently, I'm the only person in St. Louis thus far who was less than impressed with Grbic. What am I missing?

The boyfriend and I headed to Grbic with a Hot Sauce certificate in tow, secure in good anecdotes and reviews. Yummy dinner with a movie afterward? Yes, please! But the "yummy" didn't quite happen; it was more "meh."

We walked in and were greeted with cigarette smoke. Great. Yet another restaurant that makes you enter in or near the smoking "section" (in quotes, since the smoke doesn't really stay in its own section. Restaurants, if you're reading this, THIS IS A BAD THING.). The hostess seated us without much pleasantry, and we were left waiting for menus for a bit. The restaurant was pretty empty in the "non-smoking section" (again, quotes used purposefully) -- only three other tables were full. That made the already-large room feel cavernous.

Our server, who was nice enough, finally brought us menus, and we started looking. It didn't take us long to choose our food, but it did take a while before we could order it, as our server disappeared for a while. Eventually we ordered, and then our server brought bread to us. This was pretty plain bread -- basic baguette served with cold, hard individual butter. 

Soon after that, our salads arrived. We ordered basic side salads, nothing special. That's pretty much what we received, though I liked the basic vinegarette well enough, and it was cute that the salad bowl and plate were dusted with some kind of herb. Unfortunately, the salads were the best parts of our meals.

Roughly 40 minutes passed between the time we ordered our entrees and time time said entrees arrived, which we didn't understand, considering how few people were dining that night. 

I ordered the cauliflower schnitzel, which tasted good at first bite, but then it just started tasting... odd. Heavy. Indescribable. I couldn't quite tell that it was cauliflower inside. My boyfriend thought he detected a vinegar taste, but I couldn't, really. The two large slabs of schnitzel were served with a side of spaghetti marinara, which wasn't memorable. I ate less than half my dinner and didn't box up the rest.

My boyfriend ordered the veal wienver schnitzel, which also came in large, breaded, fried slabs. He opted for pasta with white sauce as his side, and though I couldn't try his items (I'm veggie), he didn't find anything remarkable about them.

Baklava and other desserts were on the menu, but we were just done with the place by that point. Our drinks were only filled once in an hour, and our server frequently was nowhere to be found.

I really wanted to like this place, as I've visited Eastern European restaurants in other cities and liked them. Grbic also is a local, family-run business, and I love supporting those. This visit, though, just left us feeling like "What on earth did we pay for, especially for those prices and AFTER the Hot Sauce certificate?" I felt like we were in a Twilight Zone, considering all the praise this place gets. Did we go on a bad night, Yelpers? :(

I came here tonight to celebrate my graduation from the University of Arizona and had very high hopes for what seemed to be one of Tucson's better fine dining restaurants.. The ambiance and decor were elegant and cozy but aside from that there wasn't much to rave about.. The service at this restaurant is lack luster just like its food and for the money you pay to eat here they could stand to learn how to tend to their customers better.. They served us our food and brought utensils only after I complained that I wouldn't be able to eat my steak with my hands.. What fine dining restaurant drops the ball at this level? Usually steakhouse waitstaffs are on top of everything since they charge you $40 a plate! One other aspect of this restaurant that seemed very unprofessional to me was what the female waitstaff and hostesses had on.. extremely short mini skirts/dresses to the point that you could almost see their behinds.. This isn't Hooters so please cover yourself up..

Now on to the food.. I made my reservation in advance with high anticipation for some seared ahi tuna and steak.. Little did I know that I would be so disappointed with their seafood.. We ordered the tuna tartare as an appetizer and it tasted as if there was no seasoning on it at all.. If they had just put some salt and pepper on it it would have been much improved, but overall not the best I've had.. Our entrees came with a caesar salad, spinach salad, and french onion soup.. I requested a lightly dressed caesar salad and I guess the chef took that literally because the dressing was pretty much non-existent.. The spinach salad was good but the dressing was a bit on the sweet side and overpowered the great flavor of the red onion and bacon.. I didn't get a chance to try the french onion soup but my guests enjoyed it.. For dinner we had the sea bass prepared Hong Kong style, seared ahi tuna, and the 16 ounce ribeye.. The sea bass was cooked perfectly with just the right amount of pan fried crisp on the top.. The seared ahi tuna was just as disappointing as the tuna tartare appetizer and lacked flavor.. The ribeye was probably the best dish that we ordered and the only thing that I would bother to eat again if given the opportunity.. It was prepared medium rare and very tender and juicy.. Although I enjoyed my steak all the other dishes were just so poorly executed that I wouldn't bother wasting my time or money dining here again.. Luckily my ribeye was large enough to share with everyone because they weren't as happy with their own selections..

So if there's one note to leave it would be that they certainly live up to being a great steakhouse, but they definitely don't do any justice to their ahi tuna options.. How can the one dish that is served raw be the one that they mess up? That's something to think about before you decide to dine here.. Take your hard earned money and eat somewhere better!

**Update: I have been contacted by management and they assured me that they will inform their staff of these issues and correct them. This is what I call excellent customer service, even if it's after the fact it still counts!

Aside from being sparkling new, what really distinguishes Noboru from the more well known sushi buffet in the suburban Philly area (Minado) is the selection of Korean dishes.  You can get a made to order stew (i.e. Korean seafood tofu).  The person behind the counter will give you a number and when it's ready, a server will deliver it to your table.

The salmon skin pressed sushi triangle was delicious.  The wings in the hot foods section was also pretty good.  I will agree, that the sushi selection seemed limited in comparison to Minado, but I thought it was of the same quality. Sushi was A-OK and sushi rice was not hard.  In the states, buffet sushi is hardly ever going to be spectacular... that's just the truth! 

Lunch on weekends is about $17/person, a fair price.    Will be back to try the shabu-shabu offered at dinner time.

Wonderful cafe food, excellent service and Keno runners to help you stay connected.  We really enjoyed the friendly help by everyone.  Fast food service even with a full restaurant.  My fish and chips was delicious and the wife's BLT reported as very good.  We found out way through the free parking, down through the casino and into the restaurant with no problem and very quickly.  Highly recommended.

This is one of the premier museums in the country with a continuous serious of exhibits that maintain the imagination and interest.  The current exhibition, Cezanne and Beyond, is certainly worth a trip to Philadelphia.  What can we see in Jasper John that evokes Cezanne?  Come to Philadelphia and take a look.  Remarkable exhibit, highly recommended.

Just next to our hotel we did a walking tour then loaded up with a salad and some cheeses for our room.  Clearly a well earned reputation for a most-see spot in city center.  Lots of local color and foods with a mix of locally grown produce and fruits, plenty of places to eat diner style with counter and stool and a remarkable set of gourmet speciality shops with experts to help you with selections.  Fantastic place to checkout just as all the other reviews said.  Amazing!
Great spot.   Always killer food and great service .............we go here all the time.   Close little dinner place with amazing food

Lyra has been on my list for a while. It was a nice experience to have for my birthday dinner week. I think the service was the best you could ask for, but what lacked was dinner. I was not insanely impressed by the menu. I think they have a lot of things that seem very similar to each dish. Lots of fried options with meat in a bread-ish capacity. I don't know if I would be rushing back, but I am glad I got to experience it and good to know they have happy hour on the weekends.

I really like Yeast. It is a complete hipster joint in East Nashville offering breakfast items both savory and sweet. Their emphasis is on tacos, coffee, and kolaches. 

I loved my cream cheese kolache and my best friend had their bread pudding. I took their beef sausage and egg kolache to-go. With the one bite I had of it, I like what I tasted. 

Yeast is probably better to take things to-go than dine-in. They have seating, but it can be a little cramped due to limited space. The line was out the door.  They also have limited patio seating. We felt sardined in there. 

Ask for the specials because due to the space limitations, you really can't see what they're offering.

I'm looking forward to returning. Customer service was great, food was good, and prices are reasonable.

Your 500th review. You're welcome. 

 I had the opportunity today to sample some of your delicious donuts. I have no earthly idea the cost of them, I don't know what your brick and mortar location is like, frankly I have no earthly idea about anything other than that you make some damn good donuts. 

One of our church members bought 5 boxes of assortments. My biggest turn on was having a donut with bacon on it. Dude, they had bacon on a donut! Granted, this is no new concept, but one thing remains steadfast was that by far - this had the best donut with bacon I've had in my life. Another one I had was filled with gooey deliciousness inside of it. Again, no idea the name, but it was a THICK layered donut that was also moist. Omg, I hate that word, but there is no better description. 

I can't imagine these were cheap. There is a threshold I am not willing to cross with certain items, and a donut is not one of them. They will need to be priced just right for me to spend big. So, I'm curious what it costs per donut. That will be a quick google search after this review.

These donuts were crafted with care and you can tell someone knows their art behind their baking. You have a new follower! Be guaranteed I'll be visiting soon, too, if the price is right.

This place is severely overrated and I was unimpressed with it. All of the hype failed to meet even the basic expectations. 

For starters, I am not sure what they're going for. They are casual, hipster, use paper plates and plastic cups for everything... I can't really follow. Maybe it is a dive taco joint? Please note I am not complaining about any of this. I am just trying to follow the direction they are going in.

I forgot to bring cash but used their on-site ATM that charges you $3 for the withdrawal. Make sure to get funds before coming here to avoid the fees. They also accept checks.

Let's talk about the food. I had 2 tacos, elote corn, plantains, and a pineapple margarita. My grand total was $20. Price is on point for the quantity of food you get, but not for the quality. Quality was not there. I swear I walked in open-minded until the food was in front of me. I didn't feel that the pork offered any flavor, the vegetarian taco was not flavorful, the drink was watered down despite asking for little ice in my cup, and the corn wasn't amazing. I liked the plantains the most. I showed up hungry because I wanted to eat a variety of their offerings. 

I picked it up from the pick-up window and took it back to the bar where I was sitting. They serve you as it becomes available so your food won't be coming out all at the same time. I got my sides before my tacos. I made 2 trips. You can order your food from the bar if you are sitting there, but otherwise, you order it at the walk-up window and pay there, too. I feel everything is a bit disjointed. You serve yourself water as well. I still left a 20% tip, but frankly, I do not know what I was tipping for when I got one drink and really everything else is your own self-service. Maybe I have a skewed view of how this works? Like I said, I do not fully grasp their direction.

When people say this a 'must visit', I am going to say that's a very hard pass. I will send them to my neighborhood for real Mexican food. Real street tacos and authenticity with flavor. Mas Tacos is more in line with Taco Bell for me. That might be such an insult for some, but sorry not sorry. I wasn't feeling this place.

3 stars because I am in the holiday spirit.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------

Este lugar está severamente sobrevalorado y no me impresionó. Todas las exageraciones no cumplieron con las expectativas básicas.

Para empezar, no estoy seguro de a qué se dirigen. Son informales, inconformistas, usan platos de papel y vasos de plástico para todo ... Realmente no puedo seguir. Tal vez es una articulación de taco de buceo? Tenga en cuenta que no me quejo de nada de esto. Solo estoy tratando de seguir la dirección en la que están entrando.

Olvidé traer efectivo pero usé su cajero automático en el lugar que cobra $3 por el retiro. Asegúrese de obtener fondos antes de venir aquí para evitar las tarifas. También aceptan cheques.

Vamos a hablar de la comida. Tuve 2 tacos, maíz elote, plátanos y una margarita de piña. Mi total fue de $20. El precio está en punto por la cantidad de alimentos que recibe, pero no por la calidad. La calidad no estaba allí. Juro que entré con la mente abierta hasta que la comida estaba frente a mí. No sentí que el cerdo ofreciera ningún sabor, el taco vegetariano no era sabroso, la bebida fue aguada a pesar de pedir un poco de hielo y el maíz no era increíble. Me gustaron más los plátanos. Aparecí con hambre porque quería comer una variedad de sus ofrendas.

Lo recogí de la ventana de recogida y lo llevé a la barra donde estaba sentado. Te sirven a medida que está disponible para que tu comida no salga todo al mismo tiempo. Tengo mis lados antes de mis tacos. Hice 2 viajes. Puede pedir su comida en el bar si está sentado allí, pero de lo contrario, pídala en la ventanilla y pague allí también. Siento que todo está un poco inconexo. Te sirves agua también. Todavía dejé una propina del 20%, pero, francamente, no sé qué propina cuando tomé una copa y realmente todo lo demás es su propio autoservicio. Tal vez tengo una vista sesgada sobre cómo funciona esto? Como dije, no entiendo completamente su dirección.

Cuando la gente diga que es una visita obligada, voy a decir que es un pase muy difícil. Los enviaré a mi vecindario para una verdadera comida mexicana. Tacos reales de calle y autenticidad con sabor. Mas Tacos está más en línea con Taco Bell para mí. Eso podría ser un insulto para algunos, pero lo siento, no lo siento. No estaba sintiendo este lugar.

3 estrellas porque estoy en el espíritu de vacaciones.

Darfon's is a fun family-owned restaurant that has a steady dedicated clientele. It's been owned for nearly 30 years and counting all the while remaining in the same family operation.
