My friend and I dined here where we enjoyed a vast spread of food and wine. We ordered roughly 4 courses and split it. Food was exceptional and melt in your mouth. My favorite part of the meal was the finish with the tiramisu. I loved it. It was light, fluffy, and had just enough taste to the cream.

What really turns me on about this place is that they locally source most of their ingredients. They are dedicated to promoting local and by using local. The freshness is tasted through each dish.

Service was exceptional with no beats skipped. We were very satisfied with the time and effort put into our visit even having the manager stop by to see how our meal was. I liked how they paid attention to the small details especially with the sizable restaurant, you do not always get that privilege.

It is worth noting that this place was packed and had a wait to get in. If you plan to get in, call ahead. They do they reservations. Lastly, make sure you save room for dessert. That is the most important part of the meal.

I enjoyed myself here. Food and drink were delicious. If I had any complaints, the only thing it would be is that they used way more ice than I cared for in my drinks. Otherwise, everything from Logan (our server) to dining outside on a patio in late November couldn't have been more perfect. 

A solid 5 from me.

To basically repeat what Kat V. wrote...

You can't get local produce from our "local" farmer's market. It frustrates me that vendors will buy their produce from one single whole saler and then resell it to you. They just purchase the food to sell at a higher price to the public. It's a complete sham and bullshit! I think if you're going to be local, then sell your local items. 

I went home last weekend to TN and got real LOCAL produce. The farmers themselves were selling what they grew. Their own crops, their own meat, their own breads that they made. I hate the "fall off the back of the truck" type sales. You can see the difference in the quality of food versus what was home grown. Plus if you don't eat what you purchase immediately, it will go bad. Think shelf life of 2 days max. Soulard Market has a lot of that.

I like the historical significance of the market itself and the fact that it has such a vast selection of items. However, why I would I make a special trip here to get "local" produce when it's not their food and it is upcharged. If I want organic, I will go to Whole Foods or even Schnuck's. 

It really does disappoint me. It doesn't meet my expectations, and I didn't think my expectations were that high to want quality grown food from a farmer's market.

I do love me some Tower Grove Park. This is where I come for a long leisurely stroll when I was a change of scenery from my park that I live across the street from.

Tower Grove was developed by the same man who created Botanical Gardens. Thank you Mr. Shaw for you delightful tribute to the city. Its namesake originates from the tower-eque feature that Shaw has located in the Botanical Garden itself.

The park has 11 original Victorian pavilions that can be used for leisure or group settings for a small fee depending on which pavilion you choose. All the pavilions offer a little piece of history that the date and the name of the pavilion itself on the plaque in front of them. 

Tower Grove runs two miles long which gives it plenty of walking trails and room for all the extras. Within the park, there is a green house called the Piper Palm House which is used for weddings, brunch on Sundays, and the St. Louis symphony will have free performances there during the warmer months.

One of my favorite things is the pool pavilion area. Over there, you have the farmer's market that takes place every Saturday from 8am til when ever, two playgrounds, a water area for kids that has a small fountain that shoots out water, tennis courts, and if you're lucky, a band will play free shows on occasion.

The "ancient ruins" are original to the park created in 1872 and restored in 2010 by Emerson. It has a picturesque water fountain that is on year round. Also, some reflection pools where the ducks insist on leaving their dropping for everyone to step in.... Benches for people to enjoy the scenery and it lies right next to the Piper Palm House. The stone hedges are very popular for kids and even adults such as myself to sometimes climb on just for the fun of it.

I genuinely love this park. Filled with history and just wonderful nature in general. Beware of the awful yellow speed bumps though. They're not very forgiving to your car.

To say this place was busy was an understatement. I couldn't find a spot in the parking lot for over 10 minutes, and this was on a Tuesday evening! I am glad that I got there 45 minutes early because I heard from my best friend that this place can be a mess any given night with crowds. Despite the crowd, I was happily relieved to see that everyone on staff were wearing masks and practicing appropriate protocols for COVID-19. Sumner County got rid of their mask mandate, but the restaurant still enforced them at the time of my visit.

My friend and I were more focused on their drink specials during happy hour than we were food, but we did opt for their crab cake app and their shrimp skewers that we split between the both of us. Drinks were solid. I got the basic rails and he got beers. My drinks were boozy and cheap for the cost during happy hour. Can't every complain about the good mix of both. 

The best part of the visit was being able to sit on the patio. We enjoyed the covered patio and the view of the lake that they have right on the water. I also want to add that there are benches for patrons to sit on out in the area as well while waiting for your table to get ready. With the volume that rolls in here, there is a very strong probability that you will be waiting, so I suggest getting a drink and take it outside (weather permitting) and enjoy the view. You are allowed to take drinks out there. 

Service was good. She didn't miss a beat and was accommodating to our requests. We closed out our bar tab before getting a table and opened up a new check with our server to make it easier. They did offer move it, but we opted for the first option to give our dues where it was respected with our bartenders.

This is a solid spot for Hendersonville. I will visit again, but will probably make a point to come earlier in the day to avoid the crowd.

Café Du Monde is one of those places that everyone recommends and expects you to have the exceptional time that they had. It is a HUGE NOLA staple. No one can deny that. It has enriched the city for over 130 years. Nothing can change its legacy and it will never go out of business. No Yelp review will have an influence on its future either way because of the reputation it holds internationally. It is just one of those places that will forever be here until the end of time.

Why is it so popular? Well, it serves up French donuts and chicory coffee. There's no debate about the product. You can get the beignets in orders of 3 or 6. Guarantee that powdered sugar is going to get all over you so dress accordingly. If you get them to-go from this original location; head to Jackson Square to enjoy them since the actual cafe is always busy. Getting to-go is better than dining in and my reflection won't change on that.

I do not drink coffee, but chicory coffee is very much a NOLA tradition. Louisianans started using chicory in their coffee when the Union Naval blockade cut off their access to the New Orleans port, therefore, forcing people to acclimate to a new way of preparing their coffee. After the war, the new adapted way of making their coffee supply stretch became a new norm of how they enjoyed their coffee. 

There are several locations in New Orleans, but checking out the original one is always my plan since it offers authenticity and the historical component I love.

I have been sitting on this review for nearly 3 weeks and I am literally wanting to pull my hair out for giving this wonderful historical site a 2 star rating, but honestly I have no choice. I thought about it and contemplated... can I honestly say it was a 2 star experience, and unfortunately it was.

Starting off it wasn't so bad. We were greeted and sat by this wonderful hostess dressed in Colonial period garb along with her co-workers to make the experience more authentic. The initial thought of coming here was very exciting for me since I love history and this is what history nerds do -- they go to the tavern where their forefathers dined.

Well... yeah, that quickly went down hill. Our server was lacking and pretty AWOL. He was fine initially but when he got a table of 8 and was already dealing with a large party prior to our arrival (we didn't order alcohol despite his urging...) he took his schmoozing elsewhere and we became second rate citizens. 

Yes, I fully and wholeheartedly understood he had large parties to tend to, but when you're standing there with the water pitcher 2 inches away from me and I had already asked you 4 times to please refill my glass -- you cleared the other tables who needed refills still with a pitcher half full and you walk back inside leaving me high and dry. This did annoy me and I did have to walk into the restaurant and say, 'hey, I know you're busy, but....' I needed some damn water!

He was pretty absent for a great deal of the meal and tracking him down became a regular habit through out the time spent there.

Our food was also not that wonderful. Everything sounded nice on the menu, but ultimately our rabbit was less than appeasing. My friends and I both ordered the same dish. I like gamey dishes when available and the followed suit. 

The only upsides to our meal was the cider I had, table bread, and the soup they ordered. They had the potato soup. The bread was super good and for it to be from an original recipe from way back when made it interesting.

The money spent was not my money's worth. I was really disappointed. I would like to give this place a second chance because I really want to like it, but I don't know if it is worth a second chance after a lackluster first experience with a lasting impression.

I had a lovely experience last night at Bourbon Steak. It was an unexpected visit that was both surprising and enlightening at the same time. Andrea, our server, was wonderful and accommodating. She provided recommendations from the menu of which we took her advice to heighten the dining experience. 

By far, the pineapple dessert and mac and cheese were the high notes for me. I can't forget to give an honorable mention to the view from the top of the JW Marriott and tuna tartare as well. The experience is not one to be forgotten.

Lastly, the executive chef is female! Her name is Quentin and certainly a lovely soul to share the elevator with at midnight. That is what happened with us. I love seeing a woman of her expertise over a restaurant with such notoriety. It's a compliment for sure.

There is no better way to give this an intro - my bestie and I had a helluva time here at O-Ku. Much to my surprise this place is a chain restaurant based out of Charleston, but each location has their own concept and menu variety. Speaking of variety, that is exactly what we got here - we let the server choose our meal items. 

Clinton, our server, was the life of the party. When I made my reservation, I asked for someone to spice up the meal for us and O-Ku delivered their best for my birthday night. Clinton was hilarious, honestly, he had the best sense of humor. He didn't miss a beat in service and served us up a great meal with a lot of amazing ingredients. Him and the chef had either had a good time creating different items for us or we were a pain in their ass. Not sure which it was, but either way, they delivered and at topnotch. 

By far, we loved the sushi. The sushi is fresh, and probably the best in Nashville. Finding sushi in Nashville that is worth anything is like finding a pearl in an oyster out in the wild. We also loved their wild poke roll ups that they came out with. No ingredient was spared. They even came out with a shrimp and short rib one. That was delish and funky at the same time. To end the meal, they brought me out a matcha cheesecake that is not on the menu. I died over that. It was soooooooo good and should be back on the menu.

Covid guidelines were exceedingly followed. Expect to have your temp taken at the door + every employee is properly wearing their masks. Do your part and wear one properly as well. 

If you want a sleek restaurant to celebrate a night with great vibes and enjoy yourself with an adult environment, this would be the place to come. Nothing against kids, but it was nice to find a place that I could dress cute and come and enjoy without the screams of children. This is also a great alternative to the bachelorette scene and perfect for a local's night out.

Side note, parking is a pain. Street parking is available along with paid parking. Arrive early to get street is you're stingy like me and do not want to pay for a paid lot or Uber here. I am not sure if they do parking validation. Also, if you're feeling adventurous, there is a boba tea place next door to enjoy after dinner non-alcoholic liberations.

Shout out to Clinton again. Thanks for making my birthday night memorable for my bestie and I!

Dude! I love me some MoKaBe's, but this bitch who was running the register totally killed it for me on this latest visit.

I ordered a strawberry lemonade for $3.50. I asked her if there were refills on it, and she replied, 'yeah, if you pay for it.' She said it in a very sarcastic and dry tone with a smirk on her face. That smirk really didn't do anything for her face.... She then proceeded on to just roam around behind the counter letting out very noticeable loud and unpleasant sighs to make sure everyone know in the down stairs area she was having a crappy day. I get it. People have sucky days sometimes and it makes things worse when you have to work on them. HOWEVER, that does NOT in any form justify you to give shit customer service. Get the chip off your shoulder. Leave your personal problems at the door and do your job, don't be so dramatic.

For what it's worth, the strawberry lemonade was good. I just wish there would not have been so much ice in it...

That's my rant.... 

Good day.

Peninsula is back and with a vengeance. This place has always rocked my world and one of my favorite East Nashville establishments. The last time they were open was March 14th, 2020. They opened their doors again last night for the first time last night. I feel Peninsula has a closeness to my foodie heart. 

The owners are the best ever! Yuriko & Craig are very hands-on in the day-to-day dealings of the restaurant and with their customers. When I came in tonight, we greeted each other like a day hasn't past. It's that kind of love and familiarity that goes into their food, too. Everything you taste will offer huge flavor.

This Spanish meet Asian tapas influences collides the best of both worlds. Lots of their ingredients are locally sourced. Have expectations coming in here because they deliver beyond it every time.

Currently, open 3 days a week and will reopen to 5 in a month or so.

*Come in, sits down. Sets up laptop. Sits at laptop for 3 minutes to set up some stuff. Barista walks over with menu and says "Let me know when you are ready to order something."*

Now let's make something very very clear. I do not go into a business and utilize their resources without buying something. I do not think it is appropriate nor acceptable if I am using their wifi. I think it is important that I give to their business. Seems like common sense, right? Yes! But, in the mean time, please do not rush over to me to buy something immediately. Let me get settled and use the honor system. I am sorry if you have not had the best of situation when it comes to having non-paying patrons come in and use your space and wifi without purchasing stuff, but one would argue that you can't really use your stuff unless you do purchase something. Wifi password is on the receipt of your purchase.

Now that I have gotten that out the way, I want to say they have some decent choosings. Don't plan on eating here, but rather get a hot or cold beverage. They do have some small snack items, but I do not think they are worth the pricing. A hot chocolate alone can run you up to $4 especially if you want to use soy or almond milk instead of the traditional stuff. A substitution is $.50. They have better hot chocolate than Fido, and Fido will charge you $5 for hot coco and add-ons.

If you want to do some Instagram photos, their patio is perfect for that opportunity. They have some bar stools out there, too, if you wish to work outside when the weather suits the opportunity.

Parking is on the side lot by Montana Grill or street parking. They never check the meters on the street, so you can go there without paying if you so dare. Don't say I told you so, just decide for yourself if you want to break the law. I will pay it before I don't want metro after me.

3 Brothers gets 3 Stars. Yay for puns....

I prefer this location over the others. For whatever reason, I am a lot more able to find what I am wanting than the others. Maybe that answers my own question, but it is totally possible to come here at 9pm at night and them still have the 100 layer bacon donut. Guilty pleasure, indeed.

I still find it oustounding that I am paying nearly $5 a pop for one of these suckers. I think it is okay to sometimes divulge, but if you think about it - you're spending a ton of money if you want to get a dozen. I know, I know. I am not saying anything really different than other people when talking about price, but it does amaze me people (including myself) will pay the price. The other thing that amazes me - the taste. MMMMM the taste.

Anyway, calories galore or not. Know that this treat hits your midsection and your wallet at the same time. If you accept that at the beginning, then you'll be wooed by the wonderful opportunities ahead of you when you have your adventure at 5 Daughters.

After coming here a few times now, I can legitimately say that their food is beyond words for classic American fare. I have tried them for lunch and last night for dinner plus drinks. Man, oh man! What an experience.

Let's talk about the place a little bit. The first floor is an American 'bistro' which offers sandwiches, soups, jambalaya, burgers, more hardy entrees like rotisserie chicken, prok chop, and steak. The second floor is a classic steak house. I haven't tried that yet, but I hear it is good.

When arriving, my mind was pretty set on a steak going into it. The server, Jameson, said that if I want to try their best dish - the pork chop was it. I took the recommendation, and needless to say, I wiped that plate clean. It was delicious, especially with the chutney. My friend got the chicken and really enjoyed it. She said it was a little dry, but nonetheless, she said it was very flavorful.

I think my favorite part of this meal were the drinks. Completely blown away. You have to keep in mind the same guy behind Patterson House and Bastion drink program is the genius behind the drink menu here. Maybe it is a couple of people, I don't know, but either way, I know he is tied to here. I loooooooved them. Yum! Who says you have to drink trash when on Broadway? Just make your way here and be swooned by Merchant's drink offerings. 

I know that it isn't everyone's preference to dine at classic establishments. This is where I differ. Though I enjoy eclectic, clean lines, and airy restaurants, sometimes getting back to the basics are okay. Merchant's isn't dated by any means, it just has a charm that can be appreciated by the old and the young. To expand on that, I mean anyone can come here and have a good time. It isn't limited to a certain demographic. To top it off, there is a real genuineness to the place than just come in and eat and split. They really do care about their patrons and the quality of service you are provided. I noticed that.

With all that being said, thanks for giving me a great birthday meal. I had a great time and look forward to dining again with you.

This place is a bit complicated. It is basically Mexican cuisine with Korean influences. I would love to know the backstory because there is obviously one meant to be told. 

I will give you the short story - get the margaritas as you won't go wrong with any of them. Spending is thick. You'll be spending a pretty penny for what you get, but product exceeds expectations. Save money for this visit simply to drink. The tacos are everything plus some. it would be ridiculous to get anything else as an entrée beyond the tacos. They have such a variety of options and apparently they have an evolving menu when it comes to certain tacos. Did you say Chesapeake crap tacos with Old Bay? YESSSS! This suits me being I was a DC girl for a few years. I love me some Old Bay any day.

Service is solid and so is the hospitality. Everyone is being covid cautious and wearing their masks properly. That was exceptional to see considering Florida has largely relaxed their restrictions on Covid. I do not understand why since we are not out the woods with the pandemic, but that is my soap box that I will stand on.

In any event, come here and enjoy drinks and food. If you're a coconut fan, get their coconut margarita. It rocked my world.

Hands down one of the best cideries I have ever been to. Ciders are awesome and they have everything for every palette! 

I tend to lean on the sweeter side of ciders. I went out with my friend the other day to 16 Tenn in East Nashville where I tried their draft Daydream from Diskin. Once that little number happened, I made it my mission to check out the cidery over the weekend. Again, Daydream is my favorite, but unfortunately, not on their regular menu. Though I am not sure if I can really say regular menu item when they do switch up their ciders regularly to go with the seasons. 

Daydream is sweet with a slight tang. Diskin is offering that particular cider on behalf of the LGBTQ Chamber of Commerce where proceeds of the sale of Daydream goes to the organization. Super cool!!

Service - now let me tell you about Coy. He is an absolute trip. He's also very attentive to the needs of his customers and flexible with his patience. I did not want to buy a flight. I wanted to sample them to see which one I wanted for my growler. He was very generous to let me try most if not all of the ciders. They were small small samples, but I am very specific about what I like and what I wanted to taste.  

Why breweries and cideries are family-friendly are beyond me... this coming from a single 30 something childless person, but I digress. They are child friendly! The space is large and if your child wants to run amok, you toddler has room to do so! Please just watch your child in the process to ensure their safety from that college frat bro who thinks it is a great idea to get wasted on a Thursday night. 

They have patio seating. Score for patio seating and cool cider drinking nights!!! I am going to make that a habit for my fall activities. Does any else love cider and fall? It is the millennial thing to do. #ThisIsHowIDoFall

Everything is reasonably priced both in food and drink.

Flight - $15 
Cocktails - $11
Ciders - $6-8 
Food - $11-16 

Street parking is limited, but they do have parking behind their space. 

Come, drink and enjoy!

Cute space for business lunches, dinner with friends, happy hour and date night.

Why 3 stars? Service. I have managed to have different people each time I go serve at my table all who end up seemingly being stand offish or aren't very attentive to our table. This has now happened on 4 different occasions in recent memory. This tends to be a go-to place for my work lunches, and it is usually just 2 or 3 of us who goes so it is not a large group matter or anything. When we go, it is also not during prime rush hour. We will go around 11:30 when there are still many tables that are open. 

I want to like this place more than I do. I appreciate their 'quicky' they have to offer which is a menu item of the day that other wise might not be on the regular menu... call it their special item for the day. Their housemade chips are seriously addictive, and their burger is a taste of heaven. You really can't go wrong with their sandwiches. 

Prices are a bit higher than I would expect to pay for an eatery such as this. Example - their Seoul bowl is $17. It might be a large amount of food, but for the contents, I can't justify the price. Charging $13 for a burger in my mind makes sense especially with the quality. I could justify in my mind paying for $14-15 for it. 

Beers on tap are generally regional with a wide selection of local beers too. I haven't drank here yet, but I want to. 

At the end of the day, the service can make or break the experience. Please look into this because if this is happening to me routinely, this is bound to be happening to other people. 

As you know - I will be back!

REVIEW #1,900!!!!

I am slowly falling in love with East Nashville. I find that I am also addicted to their vegan sister restaurants Graze and Wild Cow. What's the difference? Wild Cow will put cow cheese on your burger if you request it. That is literally the only thing that makes it vegetarian. Graze is solely vegan.

A number of years ago, you would not have caught me dead stepping inside a vegan restaurant. "Why would I when I was a meat eater?" I used to think when I was less lightly to venture out of my comfort zone. But times have changed, and I am a lot more willing to go out my way to try things that are 'different' than to stick to the beaten path. 

I love that Nashville actually has a food scene I can be proud of it and it isn't all fatty southern comfort food. The new comfort food expands to all different types of cuisines - including vegan. That is where Graze comes in.

I've been here a few times. I am a sucker for seitan -  it consists almost entirely of wheat gluten, but it is still a nutritious food that is high in protein and minerals while low in carbs and fat. This obviously wouldn't work if you are gluten-free, but guess what! They have options for you folks, too. Their seitan 'steak' & potatoes were sooooo good. Melt in your mouth deliciousness. I think that was one of the most hearty meals I have had in awhile. Pair that with a great local beer they have on tap and you're good to go.

I also enjoy their hot tempeh sandwich with their house ranch. That sauce is something I need more of in my life. It has a slight kick to it, but not in a bad way. It is flavorful. I had them make it mild since I generally cannot eat too much spice without it affecting me later. To be honest, you can't really go wrong with anything on their menu.

They do not accept reservations.

Service is generally good. I usually sit at the bar since I enjoy people watching and I fly here solo. I have met some very interesting people dining here alone. The latest person I met was a woman who was the executive chef for Pink's latest US tour. She was self trained and cooked vegan. I asked her why would she come to a vegan restaurant when she was a vegan chef (this is probably a DUHHHH response from her, but...) she said that she liked finding a restaurant that could cook as well as her. I laughed and we cheered our drinks. 

The crowd is full of hipsters. East Nashville is full of hipsters. If you are cool with their chill vibe then they will be chill with you. Everyone is welcome here and come as you are.

House-made $4 a popsicle that are really good tasting with a huge variety of flavors. You can't complain about their not being enough assortment because they have endless amounts! 

My rec would be to come here and get your popsicle to-go. The place is small with limited space, and you do not want to find yourself waiting in line too long and standing with people eating them in a small confined spaced. 

This is a cute day date place or somewhere to come and get a grab-n-go treat. If you're an instagrammer - make sure to use your popsicle as a prop! There area ton of murals in the area. Why not take a hot photo with a cute little cool-down treat? 

Enjoy!

Really cute space, but drinks were mediocre. Prices for the mediocre drinks were a little too much, too. I feel the range they're in from $9-$14 are better off being $7-$10. I couldn't get on board and I had 3 of them. Will I return? That's a possibility. Maybe it could have just been the bartender. I wasn't blown away though.

This place totally caught me off guard. My church and I had walked in the Walk With Shawn event and we decided to grab dinner thereafter. We stumbled upon Urban Grub when we had planned to dine at Bartaco. Well, turns out we made a great decision to keep searching for place instead of settling for Bartaco. I love Bartaco, but I LOVED Urban Grub. 

Service was super fantastic. We really enjoyed having Ashley serve us. She and Kristy took good care of us, but Ashley was our primary person that came by periodically. She has great personality and very hospitable. We didn't find ourselves waiting for anything. She was very diligent about keeping her social distance as necessary and explained to us the new policies that had been put in place since reopening due to Covid-19.

We walked here from dropping off our cars in a local neighbor quite a distance away from the main drag of 12South. If you are lucky, you can find parking in their lot, but otherwise, parking is going to be off street neighborhood parking. Keep that in mind when planning your visit.

Everything we had and tried was exceptional. Dishes, service, the dining area we sat in that was separate from everyone else - everything was spot on and delicious. I particularly enjoyed my oysters and charcuterie board. Everyone else was speaking very highly of their meals as well.

I feel that if you want a good date place, night out with friends or simply a place with a strong variety for different palettes, this is your place for new American cuisine. Budget friendly items can be a challenge coming here, but if you have some the finances to blow - you'll do fine by visiting here.

This came as an unexpected pleasant surprise when my friend recommended me to come visit for some desserts for our afternoon tea party we had. She had me pick up some macaroons and a couple of slices of cake that were delicious. The shop has been opened for over 20 years and hopefully won't be going anywhere. 

The owner is French and has been in the US for 40 years. Having a legit French bakery really was a lovely treat to encounter. The offerings I brought home were well liked by the tea party goers and nothing was left after the 
conclusion of the party. 

Don't speak English? No problem. They have staff that speak French and Spanish to accommodate the diverse population that surrounds its neighborhood. 

Honorable mention for being decked out for Pride month! I loved that this was friendly and inclusive to the LGBTQAI+ community. Additionally, they had people on staff that were of the community.

This place is completely overrated for what it is. I'm glad that I got to experience it for the fact that it as a tourist attraction in Nashville. But, I do not get all the hoopla.

 The food that was had was bland and overpriced. The drinks were no different. Even after asking the bartender to remake a drink due to it lacking proper balance, it still came back tasting flat. They do you truly capitalize on this being a Southern thing by placing drinks in Mason jars. At the end of the day, the drinks tasted like they were made from someone with no bartending experience. 

 I feel the only redeeming factor about this venue is that they had some good musicians playing the particular night that my friends and I had went out. You can find a place that serves good food, drinks, and good music elsewhere,  and that is exactly where I will take my business - elsewhere.

Always a clusterfuck when in this place no matter what day or time. I come in here because I like their drinks and select food items. This location is preferred over others. One thing that is always a truth is the line. Wait time is never less than 10 minutes and if you're in a crunch for time, you'll never make this an in and out visit. 

Parking is behind the establishment along with limited street parking. This has covered patio outdoor seating, indoor seating, and limited covered heated seating. Customer service is slow, but friendly.

What a fun little donut shop! I love me some Best Donuts in Town, which has closed and makes me sad, so when this place opened up, I was really excited to try a new donut shop, with some flair! I didn't go in opening day or opening weekend as I knew the place would be packed. I went the Monday evening after opening and while there were only 6 types of specialty donuts and some glazed, I was able to get a half dozen of my choosing.
Holy crapola batman were these donuts amazing! I loved the varieties they had on hand, and I'm looking forward to all the future fun varieties they'll come up with!

Since moving from Korean food heaven (aka. Los Angeles) to Philly a few months ago, I've tried over a few dozen Korean restaurants and I've been fairly disappointed in every single one of them. All of them had ok to terrible tasting Korean food and they were all overpriced for the quality that they served. I was about to give up on all Korean food in the East Coast and write it up as a hopeless endeavor.

And that all changed when I came here.

I was told about Jong Ka Jib by a friend who knew I was looking for good soon doo bu and how I'd been so disappointed in all of the Korean places around the area. I honestly didn't think this place would be any different but I was thinking, "Hey, at this point, I might as well start conditioning my mind into thinking this is good Korean food." and I went.

I was blown away. Not only is Jong Ka Jib the best Korean food I've had at a restaurant since moving out from LA, but I would definitely consider it one of the top ten soon doo bu places I've ever been to in my life. Granted, it's not in the top 3 in my opinion but it's definitely up there. I had the pork soon doo bu extra spicy and ordered a side of kalbi ($15). The soup base was very tasty and it wasn't too watery or thick. And the tofu was cooked to perfection. They give out perfect portions too so after you finish eating, you should be pretty full.

Don't be surprised or put-off when you come in and see a ton of non-Koreans eating here (white and Chinese) if you're not used to that. I myself, coming from LA, if I went to a Korean place and saw the customer base were mostly non-Koreans, I walked out because from experience, the food did not taste like Korean food but very Americanized. This place doesn't follow that trend.

The service here is just ok, or maybe even below ok but that's what I've come to expect and experience when I was in LA going to good Korean restaurants. It's rare to find a Korean place that has great service and great food. The galbi was terrible though. Don't get it. First off, it's not marinated very well and the flavors come across a bit funky. Second, it is way overpriced for the amount and quality of the meat. I shared the kalbi with two other people and we didn't even finish the galbi. That's how bad it was. As long as you stick with the soondoobu, and the occasional pajun (Korean pancake), you'll be very happy.

After my oh so amazing experience here, I came here two more time thinking maybe it was a fluke. And no, it wasn't. I think I've found my home here.

Parking: Limited lot or street
Price: $10 per person
Wait: 10 mins after order (during rush hour you will wait an hour to be seated so beware)

Amidst the chaos and closures inside of  Circus Circus, Silver Legacy and El Dorado properties we found this gem.  There is a fifty million dollar renovation going on at these properties so lots of venues have been closed.

Fortunately we found The Buffet open and for a measly $12.99 we enjoyed a very tasty buffet.  Now there was nothing special as far as buffets go but the food was well prepared and had good flavor which is more than can be said of most buffets.

Our favorite was the brisket which we found smokey, tender and juicy.  If you are looking for someplace to eat at these properties and don't want to spend a fortune The Buffet is a good option.

Wow i am so glad I decided to explore spots in Sparks today!  Located a bit off the beaten path JJ's is a few minutes from Legends outlets inside a Safeway shopping center.  

There is a large U shaped sushi bar with small tables surrounding the bar.  We came at an odd time 2:15p and were expecting slow service since only one server and one sushi chef were present.  Nope we were greeted, seated, brought drinks and ordered appetizers in the span of a few minutes.  The lone sushi chef was masterful preparing scrumptious rolls while checking on everybody at the bar with round robin efficiency.   

The all you can eat lunch includes appetizers. The lunch sushi selection and one desert per person for $16.95.  Everything was fresh and yummy but several items left a lasting impression.  The jalapenos, mussels and hunger games appetizers were great.  The upside down shrimp, mickey mouse and donald duck sushi literally melted in our mouths with tasty goodness.

Desert is sort of a let down since the mochi ice cream is literally one piece of mochi cut into four tiny pieces lol!

Overall this us as good as an AYCE sushi place can be, great service, great food and reasonable pricing.  Don't hesitate to come check out this awesome spot.

Another cafe hidden away in a old house on a quite street.  There isn't much room here maybe 20 people or so tops unless there was another room that I didn't see.  Daughter's serves breakfast lunch and dinner but we came for breakfast.  

Right off you could tell most of the customers were regulars as everybody knew each other and there was a very casual relaxed feel to the place.

We tried two of the house specialities:
The egg in a hole french bread: a soft fried egg stuffed into the middle of crispy buttered french bread served with fresh fruit, bacon, mini donuts and a square of spice cake.  This was my first encounter with egg in a hole technology and I was very pleased.  The bread was crispy but not to crunchy and the creamy gooey egg was delicious together.  A little salsa with olives also provided some extra kick to the dish.  My only thought was wow if they could squeeze in some ham and swiss cheese to this dish it would be a foodgasm!

Beignets served with bacon, spice cake and fresh fruit OMG I have had beignets at Cafe Dummond in New Orleans and these beignets killed them!  The beignets secret was their custardy center inside each crispy beignet. Hands down these were the best beignets I have ever had and worth a trip to Daughters just to try them.  

In sum everything was yummy here and thus was one of the best breakfast experiences I have had in quite sometime.  I highly recommend checking out Dayghter's .

4.5 stars  This was our first trip to Hiroba Sushi.  The place is small to medium sized with seating for around 30 people.  

The AYCE is $18.95 for lunch and includes appetizers and all sushi on the menu.  Sadly items like tempura and teriyaki are not included.  We tried a ton of items.  For appetizers we had the calamari, cucumber salad, mussels, Donald Duck, Mickey Mouse, miso soup and crystal shrimp.  All of the appetizers were very good.  We tried many rolls which were good to average and a couple of  spider hand rolls which were excellent.  The rolls are small but have many pieces so keep this in mind if you want to try a lot of different items.

For desert we tried the green tea cheesecake, fried bananas, mochi ice cream and green tea ice cream.  Unfortunately our server did not point out that only 1 desert is included with each lunch so we got charged $2.00 each for every extra order.  In addition although our server was prompt and friendly many of our rolls were mixed up.  We got two OR three rolls we didn't order and had to ask for the rolls we did order. The service miscues are why I did not give Hiroba 5 stars. Even so  Hiroba is a great option for AYCE sushi and I highly recommend checking them out.

Located inside the Peppermill Casino in Reno NV, Island Buffet is our go to spot for AYCE crab!  The snow crab is always sweet and plentiful and the prime rib is not bad either.  If you gamble you can take advantage of Peppermill's players club card. We often receive free rooms and food credits which make AYCE snow crab that much sweeter!  If you love crab, I highly recommend checking out Island Buffet on a Friday crab night at $35 or so you can't go wrong.

I should have heeded the warnings of other reviews! The waiter was pretentious, the ambiance was so-so, the $50 dollar steak was subpar. I understand steaks and the such costing more, but how can a glass of coca cola cost $4.25? Is the soda at Mortons of a finer quality than that of McDonald's? I will never return here. I am so upset that I wasted the time and money here. This was special trip for my wife and I and I asked the hotel staff for the best local steak house. This was their suggestion. They were wrong don't waste your time or money.  Two steaks, two cups of soup, one soda, one tap water $122.  What a waste.

Excellent food, reasonable price ($9.25 for adult at dinner, including the drink) and selection is pretty good.  Always an ample supply of egg rolls, general tso, fried rice (the 'staples'!)....my favorite Chinese buffet!

I love me some Philly. 

Sure, we've got gogo dancers here in NYC. And yea, we've got bacon mac 'n' cheese. But then again, I don't know where I can eat that and watch a bare ass jiggle and keep my appetite. Love the 60's inspired throwback dancers shakin' what their mama gave 'em on the lit stage blocks here. Throw in some awesome music, fans blowing everyone's hair back and it is instant music video time. 

And then I find out that drinks are $4 and I figure that I'll have to make a pilgrimage here at least every few months. Yep.

We had only planned to come here for one morning breakfast on our 3 day stay in Clearwater, but Kelly changed our minds by showing us an exceptional experience. The food is AWESOME. Wildflower cafe definitely does not skip on quality. The food here is clean, fresh and not to mention tasty. The first day we ordered the french toast... DO NOT MISS THIS! It's decadent there's just no other way to describe it! Kelly also recommended the Blueberry lemon muffin and grits. I have never been a grits fan.. never... until I tried the rich , creamy grits here. I will forever dream of them. The fresh blueberry lemon muffin is also something I would typically never order but.. OMG ... I ordered it both days I went!!! So fresh and so so moist... a must! 


On Sunday we returned and I ordered the Spanish Breakfast burrito. with a pomegranate mimosa..Hallelujah... so so good! 

All in all if I could give this place 10 stars I would. The service Kelly gives is special. She loves her establishment and it shows. She is a people person. The genuine heart she has shines. She is the cherry on top of this place and if you get the pleasure to have her serve you.. just know it will be one of the best breakfast experiences you have.

They need to scale down the menu.  The burgers are good the rest is pretty  much  horrible.  Drop the seafood and definitely drop the prime rib which I ordered this time. I ordered  medium, it came out p raw. They took it back and cooked it but it had no flavor at all. The marinara that came with the fried artichoke hearts tasted like a mix of cocktail sauce and tomato paste. The fried oysterS tasted like thEy were fried in old oil.

We had a great time at A J's!  I forgot to make a reservation and I didn't think it would be that crowded.  Think again.  It was bustling on a Friday night.  We waited a short while but got a small table near the front.  The evening started slow after our server took our order and she seemed a little frazzled.

Things started well when the Maryland Crab soup came out.  It is very similar to Manhattan Clam Chowder, but with crab and Old Bay seasoning.  It was on the salty side but still flavorful and I love soup in almost any form.  Then we didn't see our server or anything for almost half an hour, even though we had ordered Baked Clams as an appetizer.  By the time our entrees came out, she said that the kitchen forgot to make the clams, but I suspect the order didn't go in.  Even so, we said we still wanted it and it came out later.

The food was pretty good and worth the wait.  The wife had the Fisherman's Dinner broiled with a good variety of flounder fillet, shrimp, scallops, crab cake and clams casino.  My AJ's Classic Steam Pot was pretty massive and was bigger than anything I've had at Joe's Crab Shack.  It came with a whole meaty snow crab (2 clusters), lots of shrimp, mussels & clams and completed with red potatoes, corn on the cob all in a spicy broth.  It was a lot of WORK cracking those crab shells, but it was worth it because the meat was succulent, sweet and perfect.

What made the evening even better was live music on Friday nights.  Steve Cofield & Sweet sang Motown hits and any requests that was in their repertoire.  They even got the crowd singing along to "My Girl", "Stand By Me" and "Stop In the Name of Love" going from table to table with their mikes making everybody guest vocalists.  A fun and enjoyable time was had by all!

You know what's real American? Capitalism. Freedom to decide what business I give a dollar to. Geno's is gung-ho about "freedom fries", making sure I'm aware that white people originated in the America's, and that I should glorify a police officer who was slain in 1981 when there is MUCH more to that story.

I'm spending more time discussing the politics and marketing of Genos over their cheesesteaks because their cheesesteaks are not worth talking about. Maybe at one time 30 or 40 years ago they might have had more flavor, used higher grade cheese, and the "cute" rivalry with Pat's across the street for who's best was relevant. 

Times have changed and the area is more diverse now. The blend of cultures is apparent  and in 2013, with ways to learn of a business through social media, its not all about you (the company) anymore. I shall take my American dollar and mouth elsewhere. Oh, and I'll put my American middle finger in the air facing Geno's while I'm at it.

I have been to this restaurant on several occasions, for lunch and dinner. Lunch seems to be the better choice here as they have lunch specials, and it is much cleaner. By dinner there seems to be a smell of many young people sweating and not bathing. I am not sure how it can smell so stale.

My visit a couple of weeks ago, there were not many customers when I came in, but there was trash on the floor and tables that were not clean. My visit tonight, there was a stack of what I am assuming were dirty plates on a table on the balcony and trash strewn on the balcony. Once inside the restaurant, there was only me and a couple of other customers there. Fewer of the tables still had not been cleaned than last time. Both recent visits the restaurant just smelled stale. Like dirty laundry piled up. Service was just ok. In the past, service was better. This location opened less than 5 years ago, but service has just gone downhill. Last visit, there were about a dozen or so boys, I would guess aged 12 or so, in baseball uniforms, running amuck, not paying attention to where they were going, so much so that I was run into twice by two different boys. Neither apologized. I am unsure where the parental units were, but someone from the wait staff should have stopped them if no one else was paying attention.

The pizzas were good that I have tried. My most recent visit I had to catch the waitresses attention to get a beverage refill. The restrooms were clean enough. The parking lot is shared with the other businesses in the building, but there are always spots available. I do not think I will be back. What was once 4 stars easily is now a solid 2 stars. Such a shame.

I really like this restaurant. It's a bit on the dingy side, but is exactly what I expect out of an Indian food restaurant. The parking lot is shared, but there is usually always a spot within walking distance. There is a sign on Metairie road, you drive in, park in the angle parking and go in. I have never been to India myself, so I am unsure what anything looks like there, except for what I have seen in movies. The interior of this restaurant reminds me of the scenes from movies, where there are bright colors, mirrors, gold and white. Other Indian restaurants I have been to have had more muted colors. Again, I have never been to India, so I do not know what restaurants there look like, nor what authentic food from India tastes like. The food here is like all other Indian restaurants I have been to.

Lunch time they have a buffet, which is always my favorite because of the variety. I am unsure if you can order from the menu during lunch, but it seems like they have rotating dishes on the buffet. 

Dinner, you order from the menu, which is quite extensive. Last time I was there for dinner, I had the mango chicken. I had never had that before, and let me tell you, I did not regret it. It was wonderful! Seriously! And get the garlic naan, it is really great. I have not had anything bad from here. Seriously. 

The wait staff is always friendly. I have seen families come in with several children, and of course kids can be rambunctious at times, but the wait staff never got flustered. That was awesome. Granted, this is not a weekly excursion for me, but it is the enjoyable meal occasionally. I look forward to the occasional visit in the future.

This is a local chain restaurant that has great service at every location I have been to. There is plenty of parking in front. You walk in, go to the counter and order. They have a rotating pizza of the month. After placing and paying for your order, take the order placard they hand you and have a seat. They will bring your food to you. They do serve beer, and soft drinks.

The restaurant is neat and clean, as is the restroom (I did not get a chance to snap any pictures, it was a single stall and someone was waiting to come in). I do like this location. The staff is friendly. There is some outdoor seating, and there is more than enough seating inside. I usually go for the pizza of the month or the blue cheese and bacon pizza.

I have been here on several occasions the last couple of years, and the service and food have been awesome. You are paying more for the ambiance and the relationship with the WW II museum it is attached to, but the atmosphere is awesome and takes you back. It is industrial looking on the inside and is very neat and clean. Their Moscow mule stands out as the drink you must have.

You have to pay for parking, it's not validated. This is part of the museum. Walking up from the front, you see their beautiful patio with outdoor seating. Walk in, and it's like a warehouse that has been converted to a restaurant. The bar is in the middle. There is seating at the bar, and at tables around the bar. There is also some seating at the entrance on the other end heading to the museum. If you are here going through the WWII museum, this is really the place to eat.

On a recent visit, the oldest nephew had the milkshake, while it was large, he had it finished in a matter of minutes because it was that good. All of the dishes were large servings, and I have not heard any complaints any of the times that I have gone in groups.

Everything is neat and clean, and the wait staff is attentive, even during peak busy times.

I'm giving this 4 stars knowing that this is a chain restaurant that is attached to a mall. In my opinions, chains are a horse of a different color and are to be judged differently than a small local restaurant. I've eaten at this location only a handful of times now. Having also eaten at locations in other cities, I know the menu can vary from city to city. But that's probably in part due to the dining patterns of other areas of the country. New Orleans is known for Cajun/creole. More variety in vegetables is more west coast. The list can go on.

My most recent visit with a friend, we got the lettuce wrap chicken, where you have to wrap your own. It was a bit too messy in my opinion, I gave up on trying to keep my wraps together and just ate the insides with a fork. I've had the firecracker shrimp as an appetizer in the past here, and that was awesome, so yummy. The sweet and sour chicken was nice, light and flavorful. My friend had the honey shrimp and chicken, and she enjoyed her meal. I did not finish mine, but the reheated leftovers were just as good the next day.

Parking is shared with the mall, which can be tricky at times. The restaurant is neat and clean, and the staff is friendly and not overbearing.  The restrooms are also neat, clean and well stocked. If I am in the mood for mild food, this is the place to go!

Well, the best thing I can say is that the nearby neighborhood has vastly improved from empty, vacant buildings to renovations and people living and using said buildings in the last 6 years or so. Even though there is life in the area, and a variety of stores, restaurants and bars are opening in the area, there is still an air of something being off in the area, just on the bad side. The parking lot in front is HUGE I tell you. There is a building in front, on the eastern side of the parking lot that is filled with police cars, so I do feel safe somehow.

Fully stocked aisles (and yes, in Louisiana, you can purchase hard alcohol in the grocery stores, and in the Wal-Mart **shocking**, get over it). You do have your people of Wal-Mart here, and the people watching is wonderful. The few times I have been here, I have come at peak times. But the checkout lanes are usually quick.

I don't really have much to complain about here other than the usual suspects.

A friend of mine loves to look at pictures of food and dream about them. He lives in Portland, Oregon, so I am not sure what he was doing when he stumbled across an article about the Oreo beignet they make here, but he told me about it several months ago and asked me to come check them out and let him know how they were. Well, like I told him, they were wonderful. I happened to be off work one day during the week and in the area, so I stopped in then. I also got the iced coffee, and that was good.

My second visit, I had the bacon, egg and cheese breakfast sandwich, fried brussel sprouts (yes fried!) and fried bell pepper round slices. Oh. My. Goodness. I am in love with those brussel sprouts. Though the meal did come to just over $20, so it is on the pricey side.

Everything comes in a paper boat thing. If you can not finish your meal, you are given a sleeve to slide the whole thing in for protection. How cool is that? Saves on packaging!

The parking is all street parking, but it is in a primarily residential area, and next to a cemetery, so the parking does not seem to be an issue. From the outside, this restaurant does not look like much, but they do have interesting metal creatures in front. Inside is kitchy. There is a single stall unisex restroom with the sink just outside the restroom. There are some tables to eat at outside, but the interior is surprising with the great amount of seating they have. The interior was neat and clean, and they were not busy when I showed up about an hour before they closed for the Oreo beignet, but the two employees were busy cleaning, which is always good, in my opinion, when employees can keep busy, even when they are not.

This area is not one I am generally nearby for, but if I happen to be in the area again when they are open, I look forward to coming back.

Set on the north west corner of 18th and Cleary, the entrance can be easily missed. Parking here is tight, and handicap access is tricky. This cafeteria style French café is so cute and comforting somehow.

I have always had a soft spot in my heart for La Madeleine's. My first visit to this chain was some 20 years ago or so, when I came to visit my older sister, and she brought me to one for lunch. You walk in, go through the cafeteria type line, pick what you want, pay and order, then pick your seat. Any food that needs to be made will be brought out to you. The staff are all friendly, even when the line seems to be a million miles long. The cookies and baked goods all look so delicious.

Their soups are wonderful, and made in house. Their sandwiches are all good, as are their quiches.  During peak periods, it can get a bit messy inside, but there is always someone walking around, sweeping the floors and bussing the tables. The restrooms are almost always clean and well stocked.

An attempt at a sterile St Roch Market in prepster-ville CBD of New Orleans. I came with my aunt around dinner time on a Monday early evening, but they were closing at 5p. Which is kind of odd, but there weren't that many customers. A few people sitting at the bar drinking hoity-toity beverages. One other table with two ladies doing what looked like business. Walking in, there are a couple of kiosks with food. We got the garlic noodles, I had the chicken, she had the shrimp. The food was fresh and good, and reasonably priced.

Everything was white and clean. Decor and customers. If I happen to be in the area, and this is the only thing open, I might come by.

I am a proud TJ's reusable bag carrying member of the Trader Joe's cult. From the maple cookies to the wedge shaped cut watermelon slices to the 4 unisex restrooms that are individual rooms with a toilet, sink and baby changing table in each room, I am proud to say that I love Trader Joe's (TJ's).

This is the first location in the greater New Orleans metropolitan area, and having it here makes me happy. They have only opened in the last couple of months, the nearest other location being in Baton Rouge, about an hour away. It is on the small side, and I expected that it would take up the whole building, but it does not, and a Jefferson Feed store has since opened in the eastern half of the building. The parking lot will be tight when all of the stores open in this tiny strip mall. They do have the "Find this TJ's character in the store" as a distraction for the kidlets. There is the usual spread of seasonally appropriate foods, well organized.

This is the home kitchen Vietnamese restaurant that you can either get your Americanized food, or a more Vietnamese meal. Seriously. For those who don't have your own mode of transportation, be warned, this is in the middle of New Orleans East. If you Uber or taxi out here, it might be difficult to get a ride back. Seriously. Way out of the city proper. The parking lot is dusty, and can be worse depending on how dry the weather has been.

That said, this is so worth the trip. I have dined at the restaurant side and gotten food from the bakery side to go.

The restaurant side has a wide variety on the menu, from your more American choices like sweet and sour chicken to what I got on my most recent visit of beef and rice. The service is just perfect. To eat in the restaurant, go to the door on the left when facing the building and wait to be seated. They do have boba tea. 

On the bakery side, it is small, but they are always bringing in fresh baked goods. You can also get a Banh Mi sandwich that is freshly made right in front of you. The Asian club at the University of New Orleans would order a ton of the Banh Mi from here for their events, which is awesome. The cakes are amazing looking. I have only ever tried their cupcakes, but I am in love with them. They are known for their king cakes during Mardi Gras, and several places in the city proper sell them. They sell out quickly every where. Seriously within minutes at the beginning of the season, within hours in the middle, and back to minutes by the end of the season. Get it while the getting is good.

I think this is a winner for anyone. I am not sure about the vegetarian options. I am so glad a friend of mine dragged me here for the first time a couple of years ago. It is also near my workplace, so it is convenient for that when I have to go in to work.

I rarely go to the French Quarter. I live nearby, and the Quarter is just annoying and nerve wracking. But, I came in recently with a friend who was visiting from out of town. She and her daughter had eaten here a few days before, and they loved it. So we came. Parking is not specific for this restaurant, as is typical in the Quarter, it is all meter street parking or paid parking lots, though there are plenty of both nearby. There is a short step up to get into the restaurant. The restroom could use some attention and takes some maneuvering to get to. You walk to the back of the dining area, thru an alley, stepping up and down to get to this dingy restroom that doesn't really match the brightly lit dining area.

She and I split the muffuletta sandwich and the daughter had a roast beef sandwich. The service was good, and the food was great. I am glad she suggested we come here, and I suggest that any one come here for a casual sit down meal while in the Quarter.

Neat little restaurant. The interior could use a deep cleaning, but the service is really good. I have been here on several occasions now. In the front. on Veterans BLVD, there is a small parking lot, in the rear is a larger parking lot, so do not be afraid if you pull up and the front is full.

Walking in, there are three sections. The main dining area, the sushi bar, and the hibachi side. They are very popular for their hibachi side. Their hibachi portions are on the larger side. All of the food is very good, I have not had a bad item from here. The meals are really worth the money, but I do think they are a bit on the expensive side.

The restrooms are clean enough. The service is what sticks the landing for 3 stars for me. Yes, they bring you a drink, but the refills are non-existent. I do like full glasses of water while I am eating. They do take your order and clear your plates quick enough, but they do not do much else. I have never been asked if I wanted dessert. They don't even really ask if you are done with your meal, they just clear the plates and plop down the bill. I don't like overly friendly wait staff, but I do not like the cold shoulder either.

This place could be bad, very, very bad for me. The breakfast sandwiches, the plain biscuit, the sliders for lunch/dinner, the fries, the soda, the ambiance, the atmosphere, just everything. I have come on several occasions now, and have never been let down. I am not sure I have one item that is an absolute favorite, but I do know that there has not been anything that I absolutely did not like.

On the times I have come, there always seems to be only a couple of other parties of customers. I have not been when it was packed.

One thing that I like is that the employees are always busy. Even when there aren't many customers in the restaurant, everyone is always cleaning, preparing food, washing the windows. No employee is standing around, gossiping or talking. They may be talking, but their hands are always busy. It is amazing to see. Everything is just clean.

I look forward to coming back frequently!

It had been a long time since I had come in here when I last came in a few weeks ago. Not because they are bad, it had simply been awhile. When I came in with a friend, who I had come in with in the past, we were immediately greeted with kindness and questions of where we had been. I don't remember the waitresses name, I suck at remembering anyones name. They more than likely didn't remember my name. And that is all right.

This is in a strip mall at the corner of Severn and West Esplanade with plenty of parking. I have never had bad service here, nor have I had any bad food here. They do have an all you can eat sushi deal that is quite good.

The restaurant is neat and clean. The restrooms are also neat and clean. Although this is not a frequent stop for me, this is a great place to grab a quick meal.

I have been on several occasions, some for dinner, some for dinner and drinks, some just drinks. The restaurant is divided into four parts. Entering from the Bourbon street side, there is a bar on the right, where you can also order food, straight is the hostess stand to get a table in the courtyard and food and drinks. From the St Peters entrance, there is a hostess stand in the middle to be seated in the courtyard, to the left is a bar, to the right is the dueling piano bar. This bar is dark, but all of the drinks are strong. You can enter and exit from either side. In order to get cash back for that glass the hurricane came in, just return it to the bar.

While the food can be sometimes bland, the atmosphere is what Pat O'Briens is about. And the hurricanes. And the dueling piano bar. On weekends and holidays, there is a line down the street for the piano bar. I don't think you can order food in the piano bar, but you can in the courtyard and the other bars. This is truly a tourist experience that is enjoyable. Have a hurricane! Or two or three! If you drink them quickly, do not be surprised to find the sidewalk under your face, as you will probably fall over from the strong alcohol!

I have been here on several occasions now, and it's been an enjoyable experience everything time. They do not have a dedicated parking lot, it is street parking, and there are several other restaurants and bars nearby, as well as the fact that it's in a residential neighborhood, so parking can be an issue. The next issue is the entrance. There are about a dozen steps up into the restaurant and I saw no ramp for those who might be wheelchair bound. The front door opens out also, which may be another deterrent.

There is some outdoor seating, which would be nice on days when the weather cooperates.

The interior is super cute and clean. You get a menu, get a table if your dining in, and order at the counter. I came this last December with my parents and sister, and my mother, who is picky, loved the pizza. I have tried the BBQ chicken, vegetarian, meat lovers. All have been good and the beers were  ice cold. The crust is thick, not greasy or limp. The small pizza is not exactly small, and when my parents, sister and I, we just got through one small pizza essentially and took the rest home, which was nice.

There are 3 unisex restrooms, which is cool. The last time I went, all were occupied by employees, which was a bit odd, but maybe they all had to go at the same time. I think its great pizza, great service. The only down part is the parking and the entry, in my opinion.

The parking can be difficult. Its as if some of the customers just pull in the entrance of the parking lot and just want to stop right there. Really unpleasant. Just maintain your slow speed to a spot, please don't just stop at the entrance. I don't get it.

This is right across from Lakeside Mall, and right where Family Gras happens, so traffic can be unbearable at times. Their selection of vitamins is wonderful. There are several stations throughout the store to have a quick meal prepared for you, and a lovely salad bar. The food is a bit on the expensive side, but it is all a better quality over your regular grocery store.

Now comes the fun part!

This Whole Foods saved my life! I was sleeping on a futon mattress and frame at one point in time that was poorly assembled and my back was killing me! I came in here, knowing there was a chair massage station in the store. A mere 30 minutes later ($30), and I walked away feeling much better! Not the same as an actual full body massage, but it worked in a pinch!

I will come to this location, but now that there is a Trader Joe's in town, I will save Whole Foods for the stuff I can't get there!

I am impressed at the interest in dietary issues of the customers. They have gluten free options for the crust. I do not have a need for any dietary concerns, but it is nice for those who do.

Parking is in front, and is the diagonal parking. It can be difficult to leave, because even if you pull in and you think you will have a clear shot leaving, you might not, depending on the size of the vehicles around you as your trying to back out. Keep that in mind when your coming in as Metairie Road is quite busy at times. You walk in, there is a sign to seat yourself for table service. On the day the St Patricks parade was going by, they had limited options, and you ordered at the counter for your food, and they were cash only for that day. 

The interior could use a deep cleaning, as could the restrooms. The restrooms are single, so I imagine that they could be gender neutral, but they are not specifically designated as such. There are gambling machines in the corner, walled off. During the evenings, it can get packed with families and kiddos sports teams celebrating or just walking it off and eating.

The pizza itself is good, the crust is not greasy, it is thick (how I like it) and not soggy from what I have experienced. I came recently as a reminder as it had been awhile since I have come. I have never not had a good food experience. I would come back for the food, I just hope they give the interior a good cleaning.

What a novel idea. A DIY ice cream place that mixes together any variety of flavors for ice cream, milkshakes and other delights and uses liquid nitrogen to freeze it. And the kids that were there were delighted to run through the cold fog that was produced. When I went in, there were a bunch of customers that were just finishing and getting ready to leave. Once things settled, an employee promptly came out and cleaned everything. It was amazing.

You walk in, look at the menu board, make your decision, order and pay. Then watch as the magic happens. It was all quite the show. The prices are a bit steep, but knowing what work they put into it, the price is worth it, in my opinion. Everything inside is well maintained and brightly lit. I may not be a regular customer here, but I will be back!

This place is just the absolute cutest! There is plenty of parking, the store situated in a small strip mall that can be easily overlooked. My first visit, I got a chance to talk to the owner. They make all of their flavors in house. The cotton candy flavor was so awesome. About a dozen ice cream flavors, homemade macaroons, cookies, everything looked wonderful.

There is some seating outside, and more inside. I have had the freshly made bubble cone. The doughnut stuffed with ice cream can be messy, so grab more than enough napkins. Everyone was so friendly. My second visit, I was glad to see they were busy, though I felt a bit rushed ordering.

Bring your family for a local sweet treat. You will not regret it!

I have been here a handful of times. Looking for appetizers and finger foods, a special cheese, wine or champagne. They have a large variety with everything well labeled and sectioned off. Employees seem friendly enough. I have eaten at their deli and that is pretty good also. No cheap Boones Farm to be purchased here. Everything seems reasonably priced and everything is neat, clean and well organized.

In my opinion, this is some of the best Thai food in the city. Seriously. I have been here on several occasions. There is a small parking lot in front and a few spaces in the back. DO NOT PARK in the Breaux Mart next door! The least they will do if they catch you is yell at you, the most, they will have your car towed! Seriously! There is some street parking, or park in the lot of the mall across the street and walk over.

Walk in, and you are greeted by a member of the wait staff. Most of the light inside comes from the natural light through the windows. The Thai iced tea is wonderful, although they have an extensive beverage list, I have only had that and water from here. The Thai Basil Chicken, the Eggplant Basil with chicken, and the pad tai are all wonderful. When in season, the mango with sweet sticky rice is wonderful as a dessert.

The women's restroom is neat and clean. Come and enjoy a reasonably priced meal with good service.

I freaking love their cakes and king cakes. Delightful. Easy access on the north of Veterans, while heading west. Parking is easy. The cakes are light and fluffy, icing that is not overly heavy. I wish they made the geode cake they have on display in a smaller size, but the lady I talked to said they were only made to serve 500 people or more. None of the staff members seem happy to be dealing with people. They can be downright rude to customers. I overheard an employee curse a customer out for not wanting to put the cake in the back of the car because the cake would slide around too much for the customer. Do not expect service even remotely pleasant.

My second visit here was a couple of months ago, both of my visits were with a friend of mine. This is a great small shop. It is all street parking, so keep that in mind, but no meters, so that is good.

The food is healthy, and is a great little shop to sit and talk with friends or to use as a study spot while eating. From what I understand, there is a patio area to sit at out back, though I have not seen it. The restrooms are neat and clean. They do have free appetizers on occasion. All of the food I have had has been quite delicious. For some reason, despite the fact that this is a down to earth type place, I want to use larger words to describe the atmosphere.

You walk in, go to the left, grab a menu, pick what you want, order and pay at the counter. Once you have paid, find a seat and get settled in. The sandwiches are all made to order, and the baked goods at the counter will tempt you into delicious town. The dining area is neat and clean.

Their fresh baked good are good. I look forward to coming back and bringing friends with me.

BYOP? What is this BYOP you speak of?

Bring your own parade? NO!

Build your own pirate? NO!

Bring Your Own puppy? NO! 

Bring your own pop (as in soda, not pop as in your father, do bring your father)? NO!

Bring your own pork chop? NO!

Bring your own popcorn? NO! 

Bring your own popscicle? NO! 

Build Your Own Pizza? YES!

I first encountered Blaze Pizza a couple of years ago, the location in the CBD. I was impressed. But, about this location. It is along a busy section of Freret, filled with all sorts of shops, restaurants and stores. A very popular area. You walk in, and are at the head of the line. This is like the Subway of pizza places. You decide the type of pizza from a standard menu, or you can pick and choose your toppings as you go. You get to the end, they put your pizza in the brick oven, you pay, get your beverage of choice, and get a seat. They will call your name when your pizza is ready. Too cool! My first visit, the interior was neat and clean. The music was a bit loud in my opinion.

My second visit, I got a meat lovers pizza and a brownie warmed up. Both were awesome. But, they wrote down the wrong name on the order and belittled me for not responding in a timely manner.

Despite all of the cool aspects of this franchise, there are some bad things. Because of the noise levels, it is difficult to hear the employees as you are building your pizza. I am not sure if they are attempting to make the customer speak louder or what, but having to ask them to repeat themselves is unpleasant. Also, they will misspell your name on your order (much like Starbucks does) and then belittle you for not hearing the name being called when the pizza is done cooking. I wouldn't necessarily say that the cost is cheap, but the ingredients do seem to be fresh. The quality of food and the clean restaurant are noteworthy. But, in the end, I'm just not sure that this is the greatest thing ever. If I am in the area, I will stop in. If not, then I am not going to go out of my way to come here to eat.

There is a free parking lot in back for customers. There are handicapped ramps, as in two of them. This is on a popular area of Freret Street, filled with neat shops, stores and restaurants, very much an up and coming area of neat things.

I am right in the middle of the road here. The parking lot is ample. They are closed on Sundays and Mondays. I would think they would do a lot of business on Sundays, but I am not a business owner. There is outdoor seating on the front porch. Walking in, the hostess stand is immediately to your right, the bar is to the left, and the dining room is on your right. They do evidently have poker machines in an enclosed room. Everything is neat and clean, if a bit dark. The restrooms are neat, clean and well stocked.

Last night, I had their special, which was the seafood lasagne. Layers of cheese, noodles, shrimp, crawfish, clams and yummy-ness that when I couldn't finish, it reheated nicely for lunch today. The rest of the food is just ok. You can expect the same at any other chain restaurant, which they are not a chain, but it is just the same. They have no sweet tea, but depending on the waitress, they will add simple syrup, though not all of the wait staff will. Pieces of room temperature bread will be served with your meal, with butter that you can add, but it's not warm enough to melt the butter and does not seem to be homemade.

I will continue to be an occasional patron, but it isn't going to be a regular visit for me.

Pulling up, there is plenty of parking in front of the restaurant. It is at the end of a strip mall, but don't let that deter you from trying it!

All four stars truly go to dim sum on the weekends. Not that the buffet is all that bad, but it's the American version of Chinese food. The dim sum is the cart service. This is the only cart service dim sum in the greater New Orleans metro area. I love dim sum. Seriously. And it is depressing that this is the only choice, but it is a very good choice. On my most recent trek to the west side, I was so craving dim sum, and forgot that it was the Chinese New Year. The place was packed, but I only had about a 20 minute wait about noon. That is awesome! The dim sum is fresh, and is the standard fare. The service is quick, and the servers and wait staff are friendly.

The buffet side is well stocked, 6 tables, mostly hot tables, a cold table of fruits and desserts. There is also a hibachi grill and a sushi section. That is a nice touch. This also holds the standard fare.

The restaurant itself is neat and clean. The furniture on the buffet side could use a touch up as the chairs are a bit worn and broken in. But, service is quick as are the drink refills. I look forward to continuing my love affair with dim sum here.

This is the cutest little store. It can be difficult to find it as the sign in front is small. It is located in the building with Another Broken Egg Cafe and the French Truck Coffee place, on the north side of Magazine Street. There is paid parking by meter in front and a paid parking lot.

Walking in, you are promptly greeted. I was celebrating my birthday week and wanted some more sweets. I got the Sweet Potato cupcake, Red Velvet, Yellow with chocolate frosting, Wedding cake, strawberry and the birthday cake. Honestly, all of them ended up being my favorite. All of them were perfectly moist with the perfect icing to cupcake ratio.
