This was a tough one to call but if I was grading the over all food, sauces, sides, lines & staff, I would have to say Pappy's Smokehouse was the winner in this foodies opinion.  Bogart's defiantly has it going on & I wish the staff the best of luck as they continue to smoke pigs & serve up high fives!

Meh.     I can't give a 4 star review to a Mexican restaurant that 86's guacamole when they have avocados and the ingredients to make it.  After getting past the fact that my server said "I just work here", we ordered a round of cold Coke a Colas in a bottle & looked over the menu.  I began to place my order as the server informed me they were 86'd on marinated pork & Al Pastor tacos, wow, it was getting harder and harder to not show my frustration.  We finally agreed on the beef & chicken tacos and pork tamales that were new to the menu.  The pork tamales were OK, kinda dry, a little bland and by the time I finished unwrapping them of the the 3 layers of corn husk they were pretty small.  The chicken tacos with cilantro, onions & lime were good but nothing really spectacular.  I wish I had more positive things to say about La Vallesana's but they made it hard for me to do that.  This area offered several different local authentic restaurants, I can't help but wonder if I choose the wrong one or if they were having an off night.

---------- Spoiler Alert -----------
This place is a joke. 

We decided it was time to give Italian a try and read the reviews for Vito's & thought we would give it a try.  We entered an almost empty restaurant and were thrown in a corner to wait for our server. We started off with 3 appetizers.  Arranchinis (fried rice balls filled with cheese), calamari & bruschetta. The arrachinis were ok, but cold, the calamari was small, cold & had pieces of calamari that got stuck in the fryer for hours & was accidentally fished out for our order. The brushetta was pathetic. Cold baguettes that were sliced so thick it made it impossible to bite in to. The bruschetta toppings were way to salty to eat & of the 6 baguettes I think we ate 2.  The server was obviously having a rough night as she threw down our entrees before she even attempted to clear the appetizers. She noticed how much of the appetizers were left & felt compelled to ask how they were.  I told her they were cold and the bruschetta was salty. She said nothing & dropped off our beef tortellini & pizza.  We sat there for a minute wondering what we did wrong.  A couple minutes later I had to flag her down for utensils to serve the pizza up & dish out the pasta. She was so flustered that was the last time we seen her till we got our jackets on.  I asked to speak to a manager & had to wait another 10 minutes.  The manager apologized and took the apps off the bill. Another 10 minutes later we still have not seen our server with the bill.  So we got our coats on & flagged down the manager who was having some drinks at the bar.   Come to find out this was "Vito" himself.  He then went to find the server and get our bill. I couldn't believe how we were being treated. I told Vito if I was the owner I wouldn't charge me anything for the food or service we received.  He begged me to pay for the tortellini.  The tortellini was the only decent thing we ate, even though they served it with ham and not prosciutto, kind of big difference if you ask me.  I can't believe I wasted my birthday dinner eating here. I'm not sure if this night was a fluke or what but this was the worst dinning & server experience I have had in years!

Other notes: 
No bread baskets??
The water they poured us had no ice & was room temperature.
Large pepper mills at server stations, never offered! 
No fresh grated cheese? Even Olive Garden does that.
Never offered desserts.

In reply to your reply Vito, just go sit back down at the end of the bar & have another drink buddy :)

A fun, free educational tour for all ages. 

If in St. Louis I think a trip to tour Budweiser is a must.  The tour starts with the Clydesdale's & Dalmatians, which is a great outdoors spot for some photos.  You are then quickly guided through the plant where you are right smack in the middle of where your beer is brewed & beach wood aged.  The tour moves quickly & is very informative.  At the end of the tour there is two free glasses of beer (I tried the Land Shark beer, and enjoyed it), hand poured by the fine folks of Budweiser served with free pretzels.  Don't worry parents, there is pop for the kids & I'm not sure if any of the previous reviews mentioned this tour is FREE!!! Lol. This is also home to the clock tower, which I was informed on my tour that it is the 2nd most photographed spot in St. Louis to the Arch.  We had a great time & again, a must do if in the area on vacation.  If you have kids & your curious if this tour is appropriate for kids I think the kids had fun & would do it again.

You can catch me here at Superior seafood half off oyster and frozen drinks HAPPY HOUR from 4-6pm . 

2 dozen raw PLEASE! 

Spinach & artichoke dip $9.50 .. comes with fresh warm chips, salsa, and sour cream.. such a delish and cheeesy appetizer. 

Crawfish mac & cheese.. sorry I forget how much it was, but you can find it under starters/appetizers! OMGOSH, so creamy, hardy, cheesy, gooey, hot, delicious! I'd actually eat this as an entree since it's so hardy. 

Crabmeat stuffed mushrooms $10.50 .. I didn't really care for these, but my girls thought the flavor was good. 

Crawfish & corn bisque $10.50 for the bowl sized entree and I believe $6.50 for the cup. You would think a seafood joint would have bomb bisque.. right?! I was wrong to order the large entree size. I wouldn't order this again. I've definitely had better. The onions just weren't cooked down enough in my opinion. 

Pear Salad $11.00 .. I love arugula and i love pears and did I mention i LOVE Arugula?! This salad also has walnuts, Cambozola cheese, tossed in a sweet honey vinaigrette, over some thinly sliced pears with slices of prosciutto. Kind of a small portion, but I'd definitely order again.. the flavor was so bomb!

Tchoupitoulas Chicken.. $21.00
Grilled juicy chicken breast, topped with crawfish tasso cream sauce and smoked mozzarella cheese, served with six grilled asparagus... was so yummy up until I tasted the whipped BLAND mash potatoes. I will probably ask to substitute the mash for something else next time around. 

Side of herb - roasted potatoes $5.00 .. the spice level was just right for me. I love love spice! 

Crème Brûlée..  $6.25
Madagascar vanilla bean custard brûléed with turbinado sugar, served with assorted fresh blueberries.. I've honestly had better, but it was a nice super sweet way to end dinner between 2 other lovely petite ladies. 

All in all, service is always good, parking can be a pain, but they do have valet service, food = AWESOME and AFFORDABLE, ambience is usually loud.. and casual, but can be fancy for occasions. 
I'd totes recommend!
Cool place to grab a great breakfast. The hungryman .. sure does satisfy the hunger haha The pancakes and crepes are nice and fluffy.

I'm disappointed after reading other customer reviews as my experience was no where near as pleasant. To start when we ordered our food the waitress was unsure what was available, we were trying to order BBQ pork which was unavailable so we settled for the BBQ chicken. We ordered 2 Bihon pancit, lumpia, and 2 BBQ chicken. After 35 minutes we finally got one order of pancit and the lumpia, another 20ish minutes we got the second order. It took us over an hour from when we ordered to receive the BBQ, which we took several bites, noticing something wasn't right. I took chicken off the stick to find out it was RAW. If everything had gone right except for undercooked chicken I would say the experience was ok, but today nothing about going here was ok. The service was slow and when it was brought to the managers attention about the chicken he said "I'd agree that's raw, I'll do anything make you happy" but never did he apologize. We were treated like we didn't know what Filipino food should look like but all 4 of us Filipinos do know what raw chicken looks like. Unfortunately, we will not be returning.
Stopped by to grab a light bite afternoon snack Caesar salad  and crab cakes.  Caesar very so so and crab cakes are gross even the iced tea is watered down ugh very disappointing

After months of hype, I really wanted to like Chauhan Ale and Masala House. As far as Indian restaurants go, though, this one is decidedly mediocre.

I'll start off with the good: the decor. It's really impressive how this place blends the classy, upscale lounge look with more traditional Indian design features. Points to Chauhan for being unique and experimental here, and totally pulling it off.

The food leaves a LOT to be desired. For all the anticipation and publicity, the food isn't anything better than what restaurants like Bombay Palace or Sitar offer for a fraction of the price.

I ordered the 'meat and three,' which turned out to a terribly bland fish curry, white rice, daal (lentils), and broccoli rabe. It's pretty disingenuous to call that an 'and three'; calling rice and daal two side dishes is like calling the complimentary bread and olive oil in an Italian restaurant two appetizers. Most Indian restaurants throw in rice and daal like a Chinese restaurant gives out fortune cookies or burger joints, fries. $20 for some bland fish and broccoli rabe, when I could have an entire buffet of comparable quality for ~$10? Pass ...

I can appreciate that Indian food in Nashville isn't going to taste as authentic as something out of Bombay, but this is Indian cuisine without its distinctive flavors, sharp spices, and frankly .. without taste. If you know anything about Indian food, it's hard to be impressed with this stuff. Chauhan Ale and Masala House bills itself as being Indian food with a Southern twist ... but there's really no unique quality or fusion of tastes on this menu. Just some average, unimpressive Indian food intended for an audience that doesn't have much better to compare it to.

I could do better in my own kitchen. And if you look up the nearest Indian grocery store and pick up some basic supplies, I'm sure you could, too.

What a phenomenal brewery!

TBW is one of my favorite craft breweries in Nashville, offering some fantastic selections like the Basil Ryeman, Walk the Lime, and Country Roots. These are really great quality beers that experiment in pretty creative directions, and it totally, totally works. If you're a first-timer, try the 5-beer sampler for $10.

Beyond the beer, TBW is an awesome place to hang out. There's live music, plenty of balcony seating with nice views of downtown Nashville, and tons of board games (including a giant Connect Four!) What a great place to get together with friends and hang out, or just relax with that special someone--either way, TBW is a good time. Definitely recommend it, and absolutely will be back.

I came here one weekend with my twin sons, Bradley and Bryan. Their mom (my ex-wife Cynthia) and I recently got divorced and I moved into an apartment in Manayunk. They live in Glenside in a twin -- it's not that far away but I'm only entitled to see them one weekend a month. This as my first weekend with the kids.

At first I wanted full custody. After all, I'm an actuary and in a management position so I make a decent amount of money. But money isn't everything. My sons need a father. I admittedly wasn't there for them. And it was because of my fear of fatherhood. My father was a wonderful man (and taught me everything I know about being an actuary, although I thought maybe I wanted to become a writer) and never thought I'd be as good a father as him.

I took B&B there because they LOVE Chinese food -- used to love getting some General Tso's with them and playing Monopoly, before work got in the way. It was tense at first -- the kids weren't really talking about their new school. Bryan then started calling me a jerk and telling me to shut up and then screamed out "YOU'RE NOT MY REAL DAD!" before going to hide in the bathroom. Thankfully, the hostess (older Chinese lady) helped get him out of there! 

This is going to be a rough transition. It took the end of a 14-year marriage to really appreciate my wife and my family. There's a lot of pain on both sides (I know Cynthia's upset even though I saw her profile on OK Cupid and even sent her a message LOL). 

Anyways, Han Dynasty lives up to the reputation. We got some family style food -- I got the Dan Dan noodles at a 4 because Bradley hates spicy food and it was pretty hot. We also got the cucumber and cumin style pork -- all at a 4 and DELICIOUS!

I would recommend Han Dynasty to anyone who is in the Manayunk area who has their kids for the first weekend after the end of your 14-year marriage and is having a hard time communicating with your twin sons and finding it difficult to live up to your father's lasting imprint.

Went here for Sunday brunch by myself. I was pretty exhausted from the night before since I was alone in my new apartment up a few blocks for the first weekend night and binge-watched CSI: Miami on Netflix. I used to watch this show a lot with Cynthia (my ex-wife) but she was always more of a CSI: NY fan. 

I know that's not what caused us to split, something so trivial. But it just became a thing where I'd come home from the office (I'm an actuary). I mean, I love my line of work. Risk valuation is a constant challenge. And I just got some new responsibilities training kids just out of college starting out as actuaries. But I let the stress get to me, I guess. But we have some deadlines we have to meet for our client before they can start constructing that parking garage in Conshohocken and the risk modelling can get a bit difficult. 

I really needed to learn to not take my job home with me. I wish I had a better work/life balance. I mean, what's more important -- being there for Bradley and Bryan (our twin sons) for their dance recital or staying home to crunch Excel spreadsheets? I just really messed a lot of things up and I know that no but it's too late. 14-years of marriage gone. 

Anyways, the brunch at Cactus is TREMENDOUS. It's a simple little buffet -- nothing too fancy, but all of it so tasty! The western hash browns were cooked just right, scrambled egg bin was done to perfection and they even had some soft-shelled taquitos. I had a Bloody Mary and it was too spicy, but to be fair I made it myself at the Bloody Mary bar so it was my fault, like everything has been for 14 years.

What an amazing Father's Day experience I had at this place. First off it was my 2 children 7/9 my wife and myself, the environment was totally kid friendly and even had board games for them to play. So we get there and Zach the manager (which we didn't know at the time he was the manager) takes care of us personally, we order a cheese plate and a flight of beers, he and his coworker did a great job describing the characteristics of all the beers to us. Time to order food, the kids menu is rather small so Zach personally made my youngest chicken tenders. All in all the bill was nothing compared to the service and food we got, and they give a military discount!!! We will be bringing many people here soon!!! I highly recommend and it's close to the farmers market so so that's where we usually come from.

Not sure how this place has so many high ratings when my experience here was horrible. 

Came in with my boyfriend to grab breakfast since he said its a new spot that just opened up near him. 

We came in and weren't even acknowledged by the staff, so we just stood in the line waiting to order. It took them some time to actually ask us what we wanted, to me this was a bad start! 

So we ended up ordering the farmers breakfast, which was eggs, toast, and potatoes, my boyfriend ordered the french toast. I also ordered a peach tea. 

It took so long for the food to come out, and when it did, only half of our order came out, which was cold, so we shared it until the other plate came out, which took even longer.

When it comes to the egg platter, it was cold, and when i went to eat the toast i bit down on waxy paper, which appeared to be the paper that is on the butter, smh! it was the worse! and when my boyfriend was trying my iced tea he sipped up plastic! It was from the tea bag--  we think anyway... 

So after we picked at the one plate and were annoyed, we sat and still waited for the other plate to come out, it finally did but was missing the bacon! SMH The worse experience ever! 

Other people who were in there, looked like they were having issues as well and I heard a few other people complaining about their experience. 

I wouldn't come here again!

Came in for brunch with a few of my friends after we were at a pool in the area. We were seated right away which was cool and we were really hungry so we ordered very quickly. 

I ended up getting the stuffed Brioche French Toast and shared a pork roll sandwich with my sister that came with roasted potato home fries. The french toast was mouth watering but the pork roll and potatoes were just eh, and the potatoes were luke warm. 

As far as service, the waiter kept disappearing when we needed refills and more napkins, and when it came to paying our billWe had to wait almost 20 minutes for him to come back so we can pay our bill.

Pizza was great! 

My sister told me about this place so we decided to order some today. We called it in since they have pick up only right now and it only took about 30 minutes for it to be ready. 

I ended up ordering a large white pizza with garlic and ricotta cheese- It was sooooo good! The crust was cooked perfectly and had big bubbles like I enjoy! 

I really wanted a small pizza, but for some reason they were only selling large pizzas, so I guess ill have more pizza the next few days for lunch. Id  order from here again since the pizza was so yummy.

The performance I saw here was amazing! 
Food was decent and staff was friendly. 
The waitress we had kept forgetting about us though which made ordering food difficult, so if we wanted more food, it wasn't happening because the waitress never came over to us. 
Luckily the performance was that good, that it didn't matter that we didn't get to order enough food or drinks while there.

These donuts are incredible! 

They are made on site and filled in front of you with the different fillings that you want. 

The donuts (shells) are crispy and soft and so fresh! 

When I came on this visit I got the jelly donuts and the peanut butter and jelly filled, with some cream, we also picked up some donuts with cannoli filling and I must say they were so delicious!

Not a huge fan of this place for steaks, its more like a place to go if you're a tourist coming to Philly for the first time. 

When I went, the meat was just thrown on the roll and it wasn't even cut up, there was gristle and it was hard to chew. Not a fan of steaks not being chopped up. When it came to the grease.... it was soaking in grease. I don't know how tourists and people who aren't from the city rave about this place. 

The best thing about the cheese steak was the roll. The roll makes the sandwich, but it wasnt enough to make this a 5 star review because the steak and the cheese just wasnt doing it for me.

Incredible food! 
Must try this place, good for families and dates! I went in with a party of 11 and had a reservation. The staff was friendly and helpful in suggesting what meats were tasty and the best to try. The waiters walked around with huge slabs of meat that we could cut off and the steaks were so flavorful and tasty. They also had a salad bar with all types of salads, potato, cole slaw, more meat, chicken and fish. 

This place is also BYOB which is always a plus. We went during restaurant week and got all the food for such a low price. The food was literally so much that I felt like I couldn't move after I was done eating. I thank God I was wearing stretchy pants because I know my stomach was expanding. This is a type of place, I wont feel guilty eating like a beast because the food is cooked to perfection and its all prepared fresh and you can tell it wasnt just sitting around for long hours. 

The dessert is a lso a must have, I had the chocolate cake! and it was so MOIST! My family had the flan, chocolate flan and some type of custard. Everyone was happy with the restaurant my sister picked and we all walked out needing to maybe hit the gym every day the rest of the week, due to how much food we consumed.

This place has the best BBQ food in this area. The baby back ribs, and BBQ chicken are the best. The meat literally falls off the bone and tantalizes your taste buds. The last time I ordered from here, we called ahead and placed about 6 different orders and surprisingly the employee was fine with us placing so many different ones and there was no confusion as of whose was whose at pick up time. We opted to take out because although they have seating, there's not very many seats and its small inside. 

We ordered 3 bbq chicken meals with french fries and baked beans, and 1 baby back ribs combo and 2 chicken and ribs combo meals. The food boxes were so heavy and you can smell the aromas while taking the boxes to the car. Our mouths were watering as we drove about 20 minutes home to finally enjoy our meals. 

Everyone was chomping down on their meals and were raving about how tasty they were. I had the ribs and chicken combo and the meat tasted so fresh, the bbq sauce on top was so flavorful as well. I had a side of cole slaw and onion rings which were so tasty as well. 

Ive also had their bbq chicken wings in the past and they are also prob the best Ive had in Philadelphia with lots of meat and they filled you up.

Worse experience the last few times I came here, today was one of the worse times too. So I went in with my party of 6. We were seated sorta right away which was the only plus about tonight. 

We arrived around 530pm and must have had a new waitress because she was terrible. She was constantly dropping our items and bringing us the wrong things. She basically dropped the plate of chicken fingers and fries all over my mom and the fries were on the table, she didn't offer to bring us new fries or anything like we were supposed to just pick up the fries and eat them off the table. 

We also ordered a white pizza that was supposed to have crushed tomatoes on top and the pizza came and had nothing on there, we had mentioned the missing tomatoes, to only be told we basically looked at the menu wrong and that wasn't an ingredient on the pizza (um okay, yea right). So we were upset about it not having the right toppings, and the cheese pizza we had was burnt on the bottom.

 When the waitress was going back to grab us bread, my sister was watching her on the cash register, then going to cut up our bread without gloves after she just handled the money. When she was delivering the pizza to the table, she then again touched out pizza now, and then again to put our pizza and bread in a box to take home. We just wanted her to stop dropping our food and touching it with her dirty hands. 

This was the worst experience I have had here, and the food seems to be going downhill as well. The pizza was soggy, burnt and tasted gross. More than likely this is my last time I come here to eat.

Pretty good spot to bring the whole family, and that's exactly what we did, we were about 20 deep and took up mostly all the seats in the shoppe. 

The interior is really nicely decorated, open and spacious and there are a variety of toppings, flavors and cones to choose from. 

I ended up ordering  mint chocolate chip on a cake cone and my daughter got a mint cookie ice cream on a cake cone, and the flavors tasted so good. 

Along with the ice cream, they sold pretzels and had a popcorn machine which I thought was pretty cool and it gave the ice cream shop a vintage feel.

Amazing food and service is impeccable! 

Came in for a Saturday morning brunch and left completely satsified. Service from start to finihs was great we never needed anything, and didnt wait too long for the waitress to come over to help us. The service was on point here and we were able to get seated and served in a timely manner, even though the place was a bit packed already. 

The decor and environment is very clean, spacious and bright. Tables are set up nicely and you have a ice amount of space in between each table. 

When it came to the food, we got the scrapple to share, which to me was the star of the meal! deep fried and crispy but not soaking with oil- it was cooked perfectly. We also got pancakes, and a special french toast, which was called the everything french toast, which was made up of different types of pastries- yea it tasted as good as it sounded! Kinda like a piece of heaven in your mouth! The french toast was so good, but also so filling and it was a huge portion! We shared the french toast between 2 people and still had leftovers! 

This place is worth the 5 star rating, since the service was outstanding and the food was a perfect match as well!

Wasn't impressed by this restaurant. 

Portions were very small to share between 2 people and they were even skimpier on the chips and salsa. This is the only Mexican restaurant Ive been to where the chips and salsa weren't endless and weren't even tasty. 

The salsa tasted like blended beans but was very watered down. The service was just ok but when it came to the plates coming out on time for each person in my party, they didn't! Some people had meals while others watched and waited. 

The restaurant wasn't crowded and was hidden in some apartment complexes and you wouldst have thought a restaurant would've been in the location it was in. I ordered the chicken quesadilla, and they weren't anything spectacular. 

I could've made the same ones at home and they would had more flavor. The only good thing about this place was the fact that they were BYOB which is always a great thing. You literally have to have a buzz to eat that tasteless chips and salsa and the greasy quesadillas they serve.

I like the fact that you can enjoy some good food while sitting and enjoying your favorite artist, but the service was just eh... i had better. Our server took forever with our food and when it came to refills or ordering more food, forget it! There was no luck with that, so I guess we will just continue to be parched and hungry as the waiters walk past us numerous times while we attempt to get your attention. 

I came with my boyfriend to see Jon B and the show was great, but I didn't like how many people came in late and got in the way of us watching the show. 

We also were seated by the loudest women ever who talked the entire time and were so annoying. 

As far as the food, we got the chicken wings and they were very tasty and we shared the egg rolls, wasn't a big fan of them, and we had the Bavarian pretzels with different dipping sauces like a cream cheese, some type of mustard and I think a buttercream. The pretzels were just okay, but the dipping sauces tasted really weird and had a strange after taste. 

I would try this place but just go to the restaurant because it seemed to be more intimate and like it would be a better time versus coming here to see a show again and being annoyed with the people and the waitstaff that are terrible.

Came in with my boyfriend for the last day of restaurant week and had a great time! 

We were seated right away since we had a reservation and I can not say how  wonderful the staff was. The waitress was on point with service and was so pleasant. We  started off with drinks,  I got the Neshaminy Brewing Company IPA, and my bf got a rum and Coke. 

The drink prices were great too- we have been to other restaurants downtown and rum and coke was like 10,11 dollars, here it was only 7! When I needed a refill  I was shocked that the waitress came over and refilled it for me.... definitely not something I'm  used to but I  liked that touch. 

They brought out bread and butter which was warm and tasted so good to start, and I got the salad, the roasted chicken and carrot cake. My bf ordered thee pork belly, crab spaghetti and he got the lemon dessert. The salad I had was incredibly delicious and had just enough cheese and Caesar dressing, it was a large salad too so I shared it. The chicken was so tender and juicy- I was surprised about how juicy I it was, one of the best chickens I've had in a long time. 

The carrot cake though was lacking otherwise I would've given this place 5 stars. It was pretty to look at  and looked like it was going to taste good, but it lacked flavor and sweetness like I'm used to. I tried some of the lemon dessert and wasn't a  fan of that either/ it had a strange aftertaste I didn't care for. My boyfriend was raving about his meal and was very happy with it.

Ordered some delivery when I was with my boyfriend during this quarantine craziness since we had a taste for fried chicken. First time having this restaurant, but I am very pleased! 

We ended up ordering a 3 piece fried chicken, with cole slaw, mash potatoes and some biscuits. The fried chicken was very flavorful and juicy, just wish they were extra crispy and had more crust to tear up. The mash potatoes was tasty, cole slaw could've been better though-tasted too much like vinegar. 

The biscuits were more like thick dinner rolls, but were really yummy. After I finished eating, I wished I ordered more food cause everything tasted pretty good, I wanted more. 

I would order from here again and try the other sides and add more chicken to our order.

I regularly write a review on Prince's chicken, in hopes to save tourists from a horrible experience.  Now that Hatties's is in West End, there's no reason for tourists to go Prince's and get an A-hole impression of our city.  

I've tried the "damn hot" and there's no place for my ego to ever order it again.  If you like to enjoy the taste... of anything ever again, then you should be fine with medium or less.  

Don't expect this place to be "fast food" fried chicken.  It's not.  Each order is cooked fresh.  No piece of chicken is ever sitting under a tanning bed before being served.  So patience is required, 20-30 mins; lesser time if you order tenders (I could explain why, but it involves surface area, mass, and Archimedes).  A long wait is normal for Hot Chicken across the board, so don't crucify the staff for the for how long science takes to cook your chicken.  

Hattie's gets a five star review for their service, cleanliness, and execution.  Hot chicken generally tastes the same in Nashville; only the locals are gonna notice a major difference.  So if you're gonna experience Hot Chicken, then you should have it somewhere with great service.

Was the food good?  Yes. Was it the best I ever had? No. Was it worth the 45 minutes to 1 hour wait? No. Maybe a 15-20 minute wait time is worth it. Have a lot of famous people eaten there?  Yes, but I didn't see any pics of any newer celebs (within the last 10 years) that have dined there. I get it.  Bill Clinton came through and ate a shit ton of food and I would capitalize on that also but the wait is ridiculous.  

Drinks were good, food was good, service was good.  If you don't have to wait try the place out, if you do, don't be surprised if you aren't thoroughly impressed. 

More like 3.5 stars but I will bump up.

Honey Walnut Shrimp with Combination - Chicken, Pork, Beef & Shrimp Fried rice. Legit homies!  I came here twice, during my visit and the food was good both times, service was lacking the second visit so they are at 50/50 with me. Served family style but the prices are fair. They also set you up with some complimentary tea, upon being seated.  If you want to peruse the menu, check it out here. http://orderemeirestaurant.com/ 

I would give this place a try if you are in the area. You won't be disappointed.

I was visiting friends in Reno and wanted to treat them for hosting me that weekend.  I told them that my only caveat was that we needed to go somewhere with seafood, so they decided on this place.  This was more of a 3.5 star for me, but I'll round up since the service was really good.  

The decor here is cute, and the ambiance is pretty casual.  It's inside of a casino, so the outside of it reeks of cigarette smoke.  The wait staff was friendly and on top of it.

We were served sourdough bread and butter, and boy, was this really good!  I wanted to eat half a loaf on my own!  So much for that low carb diet.  I ended up ordering a Chef's Mixed Grill ($24.99), which came with a jumbo shrimp, a jumbo scallop, a small portion of sea bass, and a small portion of salmon., as well as a choice of starch and veggies.  I enjoyed everything but the salmon, but only because it was pretty dry, and I like mine a bit under-cooked. Everything else was delicious and not overly salty. Even the sweet potato fries had a nice crunch to them.  I ate everything off my plate.  My friend had the same thing, and her boyfriend had the AYCE sushi for $27.99.  My stomach did feel a little weird later on that night, but I wasn't sure if it was from the seafood I ate her or something else, so to be fair I won't factor that into this review.  

We received good service, and the food was better than I expected.  Credit cards are accepted here, and if you're staying at the casino they allow for room charges also.

Let me start by saying, This has always been our favorite place to eat Chinese food!!! However, this is the second time that we have driven out of our way to dine here & when we arrive they tell us that they are closed! The first time (BEFORE Covid) we arrived 30 minutes BEFORE they closed & when we walked in, we were told that they were closed. When we said that we called prier to heading there & were told that they closed at 9, they said "oh well y'all can sit wherever you would like.  Needless to say, we decided to leave! Tonight the same exact thing happened! When we asked for a table this time we were told the kitchen was closed. When I told her that we called ahead & were told that they would be open until 8, she then responded with y'all can sit over here with an eye roll and sigh! As much as we loved their food, we will never  attempt to dine here again!

This is my absolute last & final time going to Ming's!!! They have the worse customer service ever...The food was so substandard & they were actually upset when we asked for "hot" food??? The soup was even cold...If you care about being a valued customer, this is not the place for you...The food is not worth going either, a true disappointment...

When we arrived we immediately noticed how cold the temperature of the restaurant was. We were also really disappointed in the feel of the place. It wasn't what we expected - we are fans of the old Sushi Alive in Carrollwood. After ordering we waited 30 minutes for the tuna avocado salad and the taste and portion size of the salad was way off. We waited another 15 minutes for the rest of our food. Again, taste was off. We actually grabbed the manager on our way out and we mentioned that we were disappointed, especially with the tuna salad. Her response, we have a lot of people in training, what do you want me to do? We had to suggest that we be refunded for the salad or a portion of it at least since it was an $11 salad. She ended up offering us a $5 gift certificate so we took it and left. I'm so sad to say that this was totally not what I expecting. Sushi Alive was my #1! :(

TIP: PACE YOURSELF... that's the trick to getting the return on your investment :P

WARNING: The cheese bread, mashed potatoes, fried polenta, and caramelized bananas are TRICKS to get you full FASTER!!! Use sparingly! No wonder they're bottomless!

Ensure that you take advantage of the salad bar, which has the finest ingredients ranging from sundried tomatoes, smoked salmon, aged parmesan, pickled artichokes, and roasted peppers, but DON'T go overboard despite the temptation to do so! Unless of course you're vegetarian, which then raises the question as to why you even bothered coming (stick to your carrot sticks and imitation meat, BOOM) Must keep space for all that MEAT!! :D

Okay, so frankly, I think it's a WASTE of stomach real estate to get anything but the finest cuts they have available... i.e. you can SKIP out on the chicken and sausages, because they're nothing to write home about :P If you want chicken...go to POPEYES...at least then you can get your love handles on a hold of some biscuits... *jiggles*

BE SURE to flip your green card for:
Garlic Picanha - very tender, very fatty, and savory chunk of meat
Rib eye - Mouthwateringly juicy and a slight marbling texture of the fat
Lamb chops - fun to eat off the bone, good change from all that BEEF
Pork Ribs - Salt crust adds to the porkiness and brings out flavor..plus, who doesn't like ribs right!?!?

After every few cuts, take a breather. You can easily spend 2 hrs there and maximize your value for money. Also go for lunch $35 rather than $50 for dinner... it's the exact same thing.

I would never dream of taking my date here... it becomes almost primal and barbarious eating this much meat in one sitting...I sometimes feel like a dinosaur ^^... I would also never take my kids here unless you enjoy wasting money...

Meat lovers paradise... 5/5

Always a favorite place to meet either Coworkers or close friends, very laid-back atmosphere, yet for a brief business meeting, this space works, it has everything you need to conduct a business meeting, WIFI + Coffee !  Not to mention beautifully prepared food items. When it is Summer temp, they have a hidden and beautiful courtyard to hang out in. Love this place !

We have tried other similar Pizza places in town, although some people like them better than My Pie, my personal preference is that My Pie got the dough just right ! It has the chewiness and "Burnt" places that I love so much on my pizza. Price point is about the same, environment is clean, great selection. But The Dough ! That is what will bring me back next time ! Worth of every single ounce of carbs that I put in my body...

Very nice surprise, we were trying to eat only Uni and Oysters for lunch but Santa Barbara Fish Market did not have their shucker/Uni-slicer in until 12 and the kids were getting hungry, we walked right in at 11:15 and originally sat out on the patio with a great harbor view. We ended up moving to the inside to avoid getting roasted by the SB sun.

Blue Point, Long Island raw oysters: I was worried about these since our experience with east coast and south coast oysters were briny. They are HUGE compared to Kumamotos but had a very mild taste that was immediately appealing to our palettes. Loved these.

Fried Shrimp with fried and coleslaw. I can't get over how good the shrimp was, not soggy, not oily just nice and crispy with great tasting shrimp inside. The coleslaw was fresh and a perfect balance, fries were well cooked.

Clam Chowder: Think with plenty of potatoes and clams, it was very good with the free sourdough dipped into it.

Came for the Uni, there are places that sell live sea urchin and also freshly unshelled but we wanted the unique Santa Barbara variety, it's so infamous it's even shipped to Japan and is often hailed as equivalent to or better than Hokkaido Uni.

We were originally going to get our whole lunch here but the Uni-master wasn't going to be in until 12 so we ate elsewhere and then came back for a little Uni for dessert.

It was literally opened seconds fresh and served to us on a tray of ice, we were super excited and I even recorded video of my wife taking first bite. The seaweed sacs were well cleaned and the uni was neatly splayed in half, our big problem was not enough cold water was used to clean it and the salty ocean water left inside overpowered the more subtle uni flavor.

For first timers note that most Uni has been solidified and firmed up using Alum, fresh Uni "melts" like butter as soon as it's open so eat it fast, hopefully yours will be better washed!

I don't understand some of the negative reviews and nitpicking here. If you ask me, Philly Cupcake is great.

I first heard about the company through their Facebook page several months back. About two weeks ago while I was hanging out in Center City, I decided to stroll down to 12th and Chestnut to see what this place was all about.

The first thing to catch my eye, even from the outside, was the decor. How could it not? It's unique and adorable -- almost has a "tea party"-type theme to it. The cupcakes are displayed in cabinets with glass windows. The staff was very helpful, not to mention very patient while I took way too much time deciding which of the many flavors I wanted to try.

I decided on a box of six: Vanilla and chocolate for myself, coconut and Jewish apple streusel for my mom, and carrot and red velvet for my brother. It was a hot day (in the mid 80s) and I had to walk several blocks to get back to the train station and back home. But even in the heat, the frosting held up well.

Once I finally got my cupcakes home, the only issue I had was that the chocolate buttercream began to slide off one of the cupcakes. I wasn't ready to eat them yet, and even though there was a sign in the shop advising not to refrigerate the cupcakes, I did so anyway in an attempt to save the icing.

The next day, I went to eat my chocolate cupcake. (I had the vanilla one first. Absolutely delicious.) My intention was to let it sit out on the counter for a little while to let it come to room temperature, as I know the cake often becomes dried out after spending time in the fridge. But let's face it: If there was a chocolate cupcake sitting out on the counter, you wouldn't be able to resist digging right in, either. Much to my surprise, the cake was still completely moist, even after spending overnight in the fridge. Not to mention, the taste of the chocolate buttercream tasted exactly like the kind I used to eat as a kid from a local bakery.

Sure, they are a little pricey. For the price you spend for a box of six cupcakes, you could go to a grocery store bakery and buy a whole (maybe even two) cake. But you're not going to get the same quality. Clearly, much time and effort goes into these cupcakes. They aren't just baked and frosted -- they all have something extra. They were all decorated in some way. (Candy, chocolate drizzle, sugar flowers, fresh fruit, etc.) Were they worth the price to me? Absolutely. In fact, after spending $19 at Philly Cupcake on a Friday, I returned again that Sunday and spent another $16.

Take my advice: At least try this bakery. Just once. It may be the first time you go there, but I bet it won't be your last.

My wife and I ate at the Lamb Tavern years ago and did not have a good experience so we never went back. I recently bought a Groupon coupon because they had a remodel / name change so I thought I would give the "Porch" a chance. When we walked in we were lead to our table by a young lady that was not friendly at all. We joked to each other that we hoped it was not a omen. Our waitress came promptly but did not introduce herself and we were not impressed then or later.... Anyway... The "Jumbo lump crab cake" starter was good but don't mistake "jumbo lump" for jumbo lumps of crabmeat. I had the "Veal & Pappardelle" - the veal was very good but I could not taste any prosciutto or asiago which were in the description - it was just veal parmigiana to me. My wife ordered the "Cavatappi & Grilled Chicken" which was very good except for the piece of plastic wrap she found in the bowl. The waitress never checked on us - she totally ignored us throughout the meal, never stopping to see if everything was ok. My wife had to ask the busboy for coffee and I would have had a second beer had our waitress paused long enough to ask. I asked the young lady who came to take our plates if there was a manager on duty and she hesitantly said yes so I gave her the bit of plastic and asked her to bring it to the manager's attention. 
The waitress walked by after leaving another table, and I finally had enough and said "EXCUSE ME" loudly as she walked by our table again without so much as glancing in our direction and she stopped and asked if there was anything she could get us. I asked for a coffee refill for my wife and then asked what we had to order to get bread (I noticed some tables around us had baskets of bread) She said we had to ask for it and could she bring us some. I was done dinner so declined but take note of you want bread - maybe they charge, I don't know since I was disgusted... 
A short while later, I saw the busgirl give the plastic to the waitress and then the waitress came over and apologized and asked if we would like a dinner. (Never saw a manager) I wasn't certain what she meant so I told her I was already full and she said we could take it home with us. Really? I said no thanks - I didn't want to wait (maybe I should have asked for the prime rib ;-)) Maybe a dessert to go? No - we don't eat desserts. You would have thought they would have taken the appetizer off but no...  In short, the food was OK but the service sucked. My wife (a former waitress) wanted to leave a penny but I couldn't do that so we compromised and left two dollars and a note on the ticket "Horrible service". I hate to ding a restaurant for a bad waitress but she was so bad... Won't be going back.

Oustsnding service, Excellent customer service, very nice place for a quick grab if you're in the area..! They have parking meters if you like to dine inside.! I had  a nice big bowl with brown rice and 3 entries.

As a 20 year NOLA resident, I have tried numerous times to embrace Gambino's. I have tried to love this New Orleans staple. 

I tried to believe that every one telling me that they are the best, could not be wrong. After repeatedly being subjected to rude service,when I would stop in for a slice of cake or a cookie, I decided to order my daughter a birthday cake thinking that maybe I would be better appreciated if I was dropping more cash.

I let my daughter pick out a cake online. I went in and ordered  the cake I wanted. It had lot and lots of trendy scroll work on it. I asked If the scroll work could be done in purple. I was told yes. Of course, I was not spared the rudeness but I had gone too far to stop now. 

When I went to pick up the cake, the scroll work was minimal at best and it was a bright royal blue. I had a purple birthday party to go to and a royal blue cake!

The final sucker punch was the name on the cake was wrong. I explained that for 100 dollars the name and scroll work should be correct. I even pulled the picture up on my phone  and showed them how the scroll work did not even resemble what was on the cake. The woman agreed.

I was stunned when the woman at the counter told me I WOULD pay for the cake whether I wanted it or not. 

Not wanting to ruin the party, or create a scene, I paid for the sad cake and took it to Rouse's and asked them if they would they write the correct name on my Gambinos cake if I bought a cake there.

Thankfully Rouse's understands customer service, the lady there was polite and sympathetic to my plight.

It bothers me that Gambino's appears completely unwilling to do anything to make their mistakes right.

Short Stop Po-Boys has been turning out yummy sandwiches and fries for 50 years. They are actually the first Po-Boy shop I visited when I moved to New Orleans in 1997. I always compare debris style roast beef to Short Stop.

The ordering system is a bit confusing for first time customers. You order your food at the tall counter, then you mill around near the counter until your food is ready. Then you go to the short counter to pay for it. The staff isn't super friendly, but truthfully, they are very busy. 

It helps if you have someone with you to grab a seat while you are waiting at the counter because seats go fast! So do the parking spaces at peak hours. Sometimes there are people parked on the neutral ground or on the side of the road.  Don't let this discourage you from trying them, there is a great reason for the crowd, and spots open up fast.

People are in and out of here ALL DAY. The sandwiches are excellent, they have a wide variety.  I have never had one that I didn't like. (Except that one time I accidentally got a roast beef with mustard. Who does that?)   When they call your name and you get your treasure wrapped in layers of paper, it is time to eat! I love the texture of the bread and how the meat falls out. I love the smell and mmmmmm the taste. They have the ratio of meat to bread down to an art. The po-boys are pretty close to perfection. The French fries are always fresh and they are never skimpy on anything.   

If French fries are not your style they have chips on a couple racks. My favorite drinks are the unusual ones they keep in the coolers by the register. They have drinks I have never seen anywhere else. 

The restaurant is simple, clean, no frills. The walls are lined with booths so you can lean over the table and keep your shirt clean.  Short Stop has been around for 50 years for a reason. They are excellent!

I have to start this review with the disclaimer that I ordered a pizza "to go", therefore, much of this review will be based on my 20 minute wait at the bar, information provided on their website (which is an excellent site) as well as the actual taste of the pizza I ordered.  Anyway.........here I go.
     Mellow Mushroom is located at 3131 Veterans Blvd, which is 1 block east of Causeway Blvd and occupies the entire second floor of the old Borders bookstore and they claim to be the originators of the "Classic Southern Pizza".    Even if I had not been hungry, I had the opportunity to work up an appetite as I climbed the 36 stairs to the second floor entrance.  (There is an elevator available for the physically challenged, elderly, strollers or those who enter in a drunken stupor.)
     I'm not sure who the jewel bedazzled statue holding the disco ball represents at the top of the stairway, but it gives you an idea that this place is all about the "atmosphere".  In fact, every Mellow Mushroom restaurant is unique and original, and I don't think any two are alike. (Kind of cool to me)  So I wasn't too surprised to see a jazz / Southern / Mardi Gras theme when I entered the restaurant.   The main dining area is "partitioned" by a small wall that incorporates a few tables near the bar.  This wall gives enough privacy to feel like a dining "room" but offers enough visibility of the entire restaurant and bar to keep that open and airy feel.  I would have to say that the focal point of this restaurant is the huge ceiling fixture in the middle of the dining room that is actually a suspended band set up consisting of a piano, drums and assorted wind instruments.  Definitely a New Orleans feel to the place.  There are also numerous pictures of jazz legends on the wall, one of which is framed in bright red lights.
     Mellow Mushroom has 15 specialty pizzas to choose from or you can create your own.  They also offer 14 different hoagies, 3 different calzones (or create your own), 5 different salads (or create your own) as well as 11 different appetizers (aka munchies).
     VEGAN ALERT - For all you vegans out there, Mellow Mushroom offers 6  "no-meat" pizzas: Gourmet White, Kosmic Karma, Magical Mystery Tour, Mega Veggie, Holy Shiitake Pie and Mellowterranean.
They also offer 5 "no meat" hoagies: Portabello & Cheese, Righteous Portebello Reuben, Tofu, Tempeh and Avocado.
     GLUTEN ALERT - If you have a gluten allergy, Mellow Mushroom also has you covered.  Aside from featuring 7 all natural salad dressings, every single salad dressing is gluten free.  They also serve gluten free pizzas (12" only).  According to the website,  the staff is trained in cross contamination.  When a gluten free pizza is ordered, the staff re-washes their hands, puts on fresh gloves and a fresh apron and only use gluten free dedicated cooking utensils and ingredients.  Furthermore, the gluten free pizzas are prepared in a separate area of the kitchen and a screen is used so that the gluten free crust never comes into contact with the pizza stone.  They even offer a gluten free beer to accompany your gluten free pizza.  Kudos Mellow Mushroom.
     I'm happy to report that I was immediately greeted by the hostess upon walking in the door, and she pleasantly pointed me to the "to go" counter where I could place or pick up a "to go " order.  The "to go" counter is located next to the bar, so I decided to have a seat while I waited for my pizza. The full bar is really a nice set up and features three flat screen tv's for sporting events.
     I had only been seated at the bar for what seemed like a few minutes when my was pizza finished baking.  I like the fact that the "to go" cashier opens your pizza box in front of you so that you can actually see that you are getting the right pizza, as there's nothing worse than getting home and discovering an incorrect food order.  I was overruled by the wife for the "Mighty Meaty" pizza (yeah, I'm a true carnivore) and settled for the "Holy Shiitake Pie" pizza which consists of an olive oil and garlic base, shiitake, button and portebello mushrooms, carmelized onions, mozzarella and Montamore cheeses.  It is drizzled with garlic and black truffle oil and garnished with fresh chives and shaved parmesan cheese.  The pizza was still pretty warm by the time I got home but I still put it in the oven for a few minutes to get it truly hot again.  I have to admit that this was a pretty darn good pizza, even if it was meatless.  There was plently enough cheese and mushrooms, and just enough oil oil to be tasty, but not greasy.
     What sets Mellow Mushroom apart is their crust.  The dough is made with whole wheat flour, Appalachian spring water and no refined sugar.  It's initially crispy upon sinking your teeth into it, but then is wonderfully soft.  Almost like a Bahn Mi or french bread.  They definitely got it right.
     I'm out of space, so I'll review the dine in service next time.

I'd been hearing good things about Brown Butter for quite some time but never pulled the trigger on actually going there.  After repeated kudos from a co-worker regarding their food, I decided to call them one night and ask if they were kid friendly.  Not only was I greeted by a pleasant hostess whose name escapes me, but she also informed me that not only was it kid friendly, but kids actually eat for free.  What the what?  I nearly hung up the phone with excitement.  I told her we'd be there in 10 minutes, and we actually made it there in less time than that.

I was impressed with the decor and although not overly fancy, it was nice enough to lend an air of "casual sophistication"; if there is such a thing.  There is lots of deeply stained and varnished wood throughout and lots of deep rich colors on the walls.  

The food: 

My son got the kid's Brown Butter burger (brisket/short rib blend) on a brioche bun with fries.  Thank goodness he only ate half of the burger as I got to sample one of the most tender burgers I have ever eaten.

My wife got the braised beef short ribs with yellow stone ground grits, crispy onions & arugula peanut salad.  Although the portion was a little small for my liking, she was gracious enough to let me sample it, and I was not disappointed in the least.

As I frequently do at most restaurants, I chose one of the daily specials, which was the mascarpone grits with pork belly.  The dish was utterly delicious; however, the portion was as small as it was tasty.  In fact, I could have easily eaten 2 entrees and still had room for dessert.  However, I have a HUGE appetite, so perhaps it would be enough for a small appetite.  

Overall, this was a great restaurant and I plan on returning.  However, next time, I'm eating a snack before I go.

3.5 stars

Royal China has been a solid choice for Chinese food for several years now; especially if you're not looking to spend an arm and a leg.  I'd like to set the record straight and address a few reviews that stated that Ms. Shirley (the owner) is rude.  I'll admit that she may speak a little too loud and a little too fast, but she's running a fast paced business that does just as much, if not more in take out service than it does for patrons who dine in.  I have yet to hear her be rude and I have eaten here no less than a dozen times; not to mention all the take out I've picked up.

I have yet to have a bad meal here or a bad meal that I picked up to bring home.  I don't stray too far from the basics here so I haven't had a lot of items on the menu.  As far as the soups are concerned, I've sampled them all and there are no real surprises here.  Nothing bad mind you, just exactly what you would expect.  They offer plenty of ingredients are can almost be a meal to themselves.

For appetizers the egg rolls are hot, fresh and chock full of goodness; and their home made duck sauce brings it ti another level. Don't settle for the imitaion stuff in the packets, even if you are picking up food to go,  Insist on the home made stuff. You can't go wrong with the marinated beef short ribs or the paper shrimp either.

For entrees, I've tried a few of the "Chef's Suggestions" but these are moderately priced and don't really excel over the basic staple items.  I prefer the basics and have enjoyed the Moo Goo Gai Pan, Mandarin Chicken, Marinated Beed Short Rib entree, combination egg foo young and garlic scallops to name a few.  Just an FYI  that all poultry dishes are white meat.

For all you vegans out there, there are over 17 vegetable offerings, including tofu.  If you're a fan of green leafy vegetables, you have to try the baby bok choy or the yo choy, which is a little leafier. Both are so savory.

Now let's talk fired rice.  I've sampled the pork, chicken and shrimp varieties and they are some of the best I've ever had.  Flavorful and almost fluffy wihout being overly doused in oil.  If you are getting fried rice to go, Royal China has managed to defy the laws of physics and cram what seems like a never ending supply of rice in each container.  I'm just going to dismiss this as some sort of Chinese magic and enjoy this "asian lagniappe"!

The real treat here is the dim sum menu.  Having lived in Los Angeles and enjoyed dim sum in Chinatown for 7 straight years, I know my dim sum.  While the staff here doesn't push the dim sum around from table to table in the cool stainless steel carts, they do offer what I'd say is some mighty fine dim sum.  The shrimp hai gow (har kow), pork shumai, beef flat noodles, shrimp flat noodles and chinese broccoli are among my favorites and Royal China's version did not disappoint.

The only reason I give this place 3.5 stars is that the service is a little lacking, especially if they are busy.  It seems that they just can not keep up once there is a full house.  The decor is also a little dated but the food makes up for this.

All in all, it's good Chinese food at a good price.

Living in Southern California had a lot of benefits, and Trader Joe's was one of them.  Trader Joe's was one of my favorite places to "make groceries", and I was a loyal shopper for 7 years.  (If you are not from New Orleans, don't try to figure out how to "make" groceries").  But I digress. 

When we moved back to New Orleans, there wasn't a Trader Joe's to be found.  And even when they opened a store in Baton Rouge, LA a year or so ago, it was over 75 miles to get there and wasn't convenient enough to shop there regularly.  Fast forward 7 years to 9/23/2016, and Trader Joe's opened up store # 755 in the heart of Metairie (in the NOLA metro area).

We arrived on day 2 at 4 PM and the parking lot was almost filled to capacity.  When we got inside, the store was even more crowded, but nothing was going to break more spirits or knock me down off this Trader Joe's high.  I bought some beautiful rib eye steaks and all my old favorites.  They brought in personnel from around the nation to assist them on opening day/week, and it's a good thing they did, as there were people everywhere.  However, the employees were stocking the shelves as fast as the customers were buying them. Even though the checkout line wrapped around the entire store, there was a sign holder indicating the front of the line, the back of the line and a greeter guide you to the next open cashier.  The line only took 10-12 minutes from back to front.  

For those of you who have never been to a Trader Joe's, I liken it to a smaller, friendlier Whole Foods. Trader Joe's are not huge stores and average between 10,000 -12,000 square feet.  Whereas most supermarkets carry around 50,000 items, Trader Joe's carries about 4,000 items; and about 80% of everything they sell bears their own brand name.  But don't let this comparatively small number number fool you, as they have just about everything you could ever want or need. 

If you are in to making healthier choices, "Trader Joe's has said its private-label products contain no artificial flavors, no artificial preservatives, no colors derived from anything other than naturally available products, no genetically modified ingredients, no partially hydrogenated oils (adding trans-fat), or MSG. In addition, its private-label dairy products use milk from cows not given the artificial growth hormone rBST."

The people here are friendly, the prices are good, the choices are numerous (& healthy) and the parking is ample.  If you've never been to Trader Joe's, try them out, as you are likely to become a customer for life.

The only think that took longer than me finally going to Blue Oak BBQ was getting around to writing my review.  The wife, son & I split a 3 meat plate for lunch recently and we were definitely not disappointed.  For our 3 meats, we got the St. Louis spare ribs, the pulled pork & the "USDA Prime" beef brisket.  

The St. Louis spare ribs were delicious, and we mainly ordered them for our son, as he loves him some BBQ ribs.  For those of you wondering what the difference is between St. Louis spare ribs and baby back ribs, here's the quick & dirty answer. Baby back ribs are cut higher nearer the spine and are smaller and have less meat on them.  However, they are extremely tender.  The St. Louis spare rib is a lower cut.  However, they are larger, meatier and have a higher fat content, but I digress.

The pulled pork was solid and extremely tender.  However, the brisket was the winner of the day.  In fact, it was awesome.  The brisket was extremely moist and had just enough fat to keep it buttery tender.  There was a nice bark on the outside, but I do agree with John L.H. that it could have been smokier, as the smoke ring did not permeate too deep into the meat.    Be that as it may, I think it is one of the best briskets I've ever had, as it literally melts in your mouth.  There is definitely no need for a knife here. 

We also got a 1/4 chicken (white meat) to make sure we had enough meat.  There was no wow factor with the chicken, but then again, it's just chicken.  However, kudos to it being fully cooked yet so juicy, as nothing ruins a chicken breast more than drying it out to the consistency of jerky.

For our sides, we got the Asian Sesame slaw, the Shepherd's pie and the Brussels sprouts. The slaw had too much vinegar for me, as I prefer a sweeter slaw.  However, this is just my personal preference.  However, even my wife (who enjoys a tangy slaw) said there was a little too much vinegar.  I'm not exactly sure what made me pick the Shepherd's pie, but I think it was my fond memories of it being served in my grammar school cafeteria.  It definitely brought me down memory lane but it wasn't everything I remembered.  However, this is a hearty side that will definitely "stick to your ribs".  Lastly, as an afterthought, we ordered the Brussels sprouts, which happened to be the best of the side dishes.  I highly recommend you get them, as they are incredible.

Blue Oak has three basic BBQ sauces, the house, the jerk & the spicy Carolina. After trying all three, I stayed with the house; however, I would have preferred an additional offering.  Overall Blue Oak is a great choice for BBQ while in New Orleans.  While I don/'t think it's quite 5 stars, it an easy 4 star pick and I will definitely be headed back soon.
.

Having long had its roots established in Metairie, Pho Orchid was our go to place for the longest, as it was one of our first Pho experiences after having moved back to New Orleans from having spent nearly a decade living in Los Angeles.  Conveniently located on Houma Blvd. just off of Veterans Memorial Blvd., this location is very easy to get to and there is adequate parking as well.

We were fortunate on our very first visit to have Matthew as our server.  His was very personable and was friends with the owner, took his time to explain the menu, and checked on us frequently while we dined.  The restaurant is pretty big, but a bamboo wall in the middle separates the dining room in two and lends it to feel a little smaller than it actually is.  

Some of our favorites are:
1. Spring roll w/ grilled pork: This is our favorite appetizer, as the pork comes out hot with just a little crisp to it.  The peanut sauce is delish.

2.  Spring rolls w/ shrimp: Served cold, these vermicelli rolls never fail to satisfy.

3. Grilled pork Bahn Mi: This Vietnamese style po-boy starts with a "French" bread that is crispy outside and oh so soft inside.  The grilled pork is perfect and the accoutrements that "dress" it all add to the perfect sandwich.

4.  The Pho:  We have tried so many of the Pho's, but it all starts with the basic broth.  The recipe here is top notch and has one of the best flavors I've eaten.  I've eaten the white meat chicken, the round steak, the brisket the meatball, the soft tendon and even the trip (1 time).  As a certified carnivore, I like the round steak and the brisket equally. 

5. Clear noodle soup is a favorite of my wife's and her generosity always allows me to sample.  The portions, even the small, are very generous and will leave you satiated.  

We have never had a bad experience here. However, with so many new Pho restaurants in the N.O. Metro area, we don't get here quite as often as we used to; only because we like trying new places.  However, we always come "back home" from time to time.

Quite recently, the family and I decided to take a ride on the St. Charles Avenue streetcar starting at Carrollton and Claiborne, and rode it to the end of the line so that we could enjoy a late breakfast at Ruby Slipper.  We arrived a little later than expected, as the restaurant was slated to close in approximately 1 hour; however, the restaurant was packed and in "full swing", and we were seated immediately.

Our server, whose name escapes me, was super friendly and appreciated the fact that we were locals.  My son got an order of their classic buttermilk pancakes, and kudos to him for being such a light eater, as I was able to polish off the remaining 1/2 platter of fluffy delicious hotcakes. My wife got the "Southern Breakfast" which looked like the typical egg/bacon/biscuit breakfast you'd find nearly anywhere south of the Mason-Dixon line.  However, their "made from scratch" biscuits are definitely worth mentioning.   I opted for a more flavorful fare and ordered the Peacemaker, which gives you the flexibility to mix and match any 2 of their Signature Benedicts.  I got the Shrimp Boogaloo Benedict and the Chicken St. Charles, both of which left me wanting to come back ASAP.

Ruby Slipper is not where you want to go if you are looking for a quiet breakfast spot, as the restaurant is crowded and loud; but not so loud that you can't have a normal conversation without yelling.  Our food was great, our server was good and she even sent us on our way with three (3) "to-go" beverages.  It's a win-win in my book.

My dad first brought me to eat breakfast here in the 1970's and introduced me to owner Johnny Majoria.  Even as a young child, I loved the buzz about this place and still enjoy going here 40 years later.  Although Mr. Johnny is no longer with us (RIPv - 2013), his son is still following the same "blueprint" of his dad's that made this place so popular.

I'm a sucker for feeling nostalgic and everything about Commerce screams old school diner, especially the availability of counter service.  As soon as you walk through the door, you are immediately transported back several years.  The walls are covered in brown panel-like bead board, the tables are covered with red & white vinyl checkered tablecloths, the steam table is loaded with specials and the counter is old school Formica.  

This is a breakfast & lunch spot only, as they close at 2:30 PM. But for locals and tourists alike, this place is a gem.  Commerce offers a great value and fast service.  Their Original Commerce Breakfast Biscuit (CBB), which consists of sautéed breakfast sausage, seasonings, jalapenos in a delicious cheese sauce laid over an open faces biscuit and topped with over-easy eggs, is a meal among meals.  This feast packs enough carb laden energy to keep you going all day, even if you have to skip lunch.  And if you are recovering from a long night of partying, the CBB, along with a few cups of coffee, just might get you through the day; especially if you have to work.  

Like many diners, Commerce has daily specials from the steam table, salads, po-boys and sandwiches. One of my favorite po-boys here is the hot sausage.  The French bread is super soft inside with a crispy crust.  But what sets it apart from most other hot sausage po-boys is that Commerce uses link styled sausage whereas most other restaurants use patty style sausage.  The link style is definitely a meatier offering and Commerce's po-boy will definitely fill you up.   Commerce also serves super spuds, which are stuffed baked potatoes (served open faced) and are a meal in themselves.

There is nothing negative to say about this place, as it's simply awesome.   However, if you are not a fan of crowds, get here early, as this place fills up quickly, and the line will be out the door before you know it.  However, it's worth the wait.

Some of the best fried chicken I've ever tasted.  The peas and cornbread were ok, and the mac n cheese was good, but that chicken!  Wowwwww.

And that's all I have to say about that :)

What a charming, cute and quaint bistro, as you make your way from the hostess table, across the courtyard, up into the house and to your awaiting table.  It feels like you're eating at a rich friend's estate as you look out to the other diners littered across the front yard

And the fare is every bit as good as the aesthetics, from the succulent chicken atop a supporting cast of fingerling potatoes and asparagus to the thick pork chop floating on a bed of andouille sausage, grits and fancy corn smatterings.

I bid adieu with the chocolate cherry bread pudding made from croissants and crowned with a plume of whipped cream... because I'm a little lad who loves cherries and cream

Well, I've visited New Orleans 3 times in my life and I believe I've been to Mimi's 4 times. Sooooo clearly I'm a big fan! If I lived nearby I'd certainly be a regular. Everything about it is right up my alley.

First of all, the atmosphere is rad. There are 3 levels (I've only experienced the main level and upstairs). Old building, exposed brick, dim lighting, big heavy wooden tables (I know a guy who made a few of them -- hi Danny!), candlelight. Downstairs you have the main bar and a pool table, but I like to go upstairs for tapas, the smaller bar, a window seat looking out (great view of parades) and a slightly quieter environment. Upstairs can overall be a little more romantic, but for me it's really about ordering those tapas!

Mimi's has an amazing menu and they serve it late into the night. They easily and happily accommodate dietary needs -- I've seen them put together some lovely gluten free, vegetarian, and vegan options. My favorites are the cheese plate (they give you a really decent and fresh selection that doesn't leave you starving), the steak (6 oz sirloin cooked medium-rare with balsamic drizzled over it), the marinated olives which are addictive, and the grilled romaine. All really simple and prepared just right. I pair my tapas with a glass of whatever red wine they're featuring, and I'm happy as can be.

Cash only for the time being at Mimi's (they have several ATM machines incase you forget). Order your food and drinks at the bar and enjoy the ambiance and people-watching.

I had such a memorable lunch here... I can't believe It wasn't more crowded considering how insane the food was and how reasonable the prices were. Ugh. I can't wait to get back to New Orleans and bring Jon here. 

The atmosphere is bright and modern and airy and breezy. You could probably describe the food and drinks that way as well. We started with the gluten free fried oysters, which were so outstanding! You get six of them and they're perfectly breaded and fried, paired with beautiful crunchy radishes and a beautiful coconut based sauce. It was nuts. Order 2 servings! We also had the acorn squash appetizer -- mashed squash with house cured coppa and pepitas, served with a roti bread (gorgeous but gluten) and lettuce cups. It was sweet and salty and perfect. Sooooooo good. 

For my entree I had the pork belly with grits with a sort of coconut curry sauce. It was beautiful and super-rich. Please try It!!

Lovely cocktail menu and wine list as well. And seriously great prices for such wonderful flavor and delicate presentation. Everything feels really special. The chef even brought us a little dessert sampler of house made caramels dusted in cocoa and espresso. I fell in love with every dish!

The shrimp! The grits! The shrimp and grits. I feel like every other photo and review on Surrey's Yelp page is of their shrimp and grits, and that's totally okay with me because their fame is well deserved. 

It says right on the menu that the shrimp & grits are gluten free (you'll just get them without the little pieces of toast), so I told our waitress, "GF, please." When they brought me my plate, however,  it had the toast on top.. so unfortunately I had to send it back for a new plate. They were really nice about it and it only took about 10 minutes for my new dish to come out, and I appreciated how hot and fresh it was. Sooooo delicious. The shrimp are perfectly cooked and they're of plenty, covered in a creamy, spicy, rich New Orlean's style barbecue sauce. And of course, this is all slathered on a bed of perfectly textured and buttery grits. Seriously so incredibly good, beautifully seasoned, and addictive. Just really fun to eat, which kinda sums up NOLA cuisine for me.

We also ordered a fruit plate for the table, and it was so rad! No wimpy watered down fruit here, but big fat slices of honeydew and cantaloupe and really great pineapple chunks and grapes and bananas and apple slices. All the fruit you could ever want and all fresh and bright.

This is a tiny place, so large parties are gonna have trouble squeezing in. Our group of 4 had a really hard time fitting our plates and glasses on the table. Amazing food and a colorful, casual vibe, but super close quarters.
Aside from the fair type dessert, the food wasn't that good. The desserts were delicious!

We were really excited to try this place so we brought friends. All of had food poisoning later in the afternoon. This was the only place we ate so we knew it had to be from the food. I ordered a Sangria and my friend had the mango saki drink. They were both the same. The waitress said they were different. The chef seasons the dishes to her liking and they had soy sauce ( you had to ask for it) and they did not offer low sodium soy. Sorry. We tried.

Since moving to Tucson, I have frequented Anita St Market at least twice per month because their flour tortillas here have changed my life. You go up to the counter and tell them what size tortilla you want and 10 seconds later, your hands are full of WARM, paper-thin goodness. Yes, they are thinner than most tortillas and sometimes have small holes in them. I primarily buy the medium-sized tortillas and use them to cook burritos. Since they're so thin, I typically use two tortillas and melt oaxaca cheese in between the layers. Yum. They also make great tortillas for quesadillas because they are not too heavy like some of the thicker tortillas around Tucson. They also make great gifts for out-of-towners. I go back to the East Coast often to visit my family and friends and every time on the way to the airport, I stop at Anita St Market and buy an obscene amount. They're always a hit.

And sometimes, I'll buy the small flour tortillas and wrap them around strips of panela cheese. This makes a great breakfast... lunch... and dinner... I work out to earn this, I promise!

I've also tried their salsas (the red one is SPIIIICY!), mild chorizo (great, but nothing mind-blowing), and their empanadas (2 dozen for $20 makes these a great bring-to-the-potluck food, try the chocolate and pumpkin ones!). 

Anita St Market is tucked away in a residential neighborhood, and the interior feels like a home. Word of warning that they're not open on Sundays and sometimes they close a little early if business is slow or they've run out of things. Service has always been prompt and friendly. I really have no reason to seek out other tortilla places in Tucson. I've tried to branch out just to see what their is and I'm always disappointed!

Taqueria El Pueblito is currently my favorite place for breakfast burritos and tacos. It's a quick-service order-at-the-counter no-frills type place. Their breakfast burrito has been reviewed to death - you really just have to try it. It is the cheapest life-changing experience you will ever have.

Their tacos are also really extraordinary. My favorites so far are the green chile pork (tender pork slow-cooked in this green chile sauce with just the right kick), rajas con crema (roasted poblano peppers tossed with cream, onions and corn) and their barbacoa. I've tried several of their other meats and they are all among the best I've had in Tucson. I couldn't quite handle the spice level of the rajas con crema so I asked for a side of sour cream and they gave it to me free of charge. The tacos are ~$2-3 depending on the kind. I tried the barbacoa in a dorados which is basically a deep-fried corn tortilla. It's ends up being somewhere between a soft and hard-shell taco and is a bit oily for my taste.

We typically come around weekend lunch-time - there has always been a healthy crowd but we've never had to wait more than 15 minutes between walking into the restaurant to sitting down and eating. The restaurant itself is always clean although we typically sit outside on the patio tables.

One note: their salsa bar isn't as extensive as other places (1 green mild, 1 red HOT, and 1 guacamole HOT) but you don't really need salsa because their meats have all the flavor in the world.

Places like Taqueria El Pueblito make me absolutely love living in Tucson. I really can't wait to try the rest of their menu!

Can I eat here every day? I love the pizza here. you can tell they're putting LOVE into everything they make. The toppings are fresh as well as the dough. I'm in love with the perfect crisp and thickness of the crust. 
My boyfriend and I went in here pretty close to closing last weekend and got excellent service.
