We ordered the Tour (give me all the goat cheese!), the iron man and the buffalo wings. All so delicious! We only wish there had been a little more sauce on the wings, but they were so crispy and fresh we didn't overthink the sauce thing. The best part had to be when one of the young guys working came out with our to go food and said "is 4 ranches enough?"...I am a ranch addict and those words were music to my ears. 
Great business can't wait to go back!

I've been here a few times to catch a show, and I have to say that this place is not worth the time or the effort just to park.

What a very odd concept for a great location.  Taps and Tapas - without tapas, and with just a handful of local beers on tap. With just a few overpriced "tapas" (nothing spanish here!) and then the "shared plates" (starting at $10), one person cannot get a full meal for less than $20. IMHO, I believe that a restaurant can get away with a limited menu and high prices if: 1. the quality is superb, 2. the portions are generous, or 3. the food is inventive.  I have found T&T to be none of these things.  I do not think there is anything creative or inventive about fried green tomatoes or a caprese salad. Mac and Cheese for $10? I think I'll go to J. Alexanders for that dish - it is far better and less expensive.  And the prices for a chacuterie/ anti-pasta assortment are astronomically high. A quick warning: the menu was a little different each time I went, so don't get your heart set on any of the dishes from the website.

I hesitated between giving this place one star or two, but went with one simply because of the service. Do not expect to be served outside. After finally having a server come over to ask me if I would like a beverage, and requesting the wine list, he brought the list and never returned. He did not return once during the entire three hours I was there watching the performance!  After a half an hour of waiting, I finally went up to the bar and ordered my glass of wine.  It is a good thing that I didn't have a friend with me or was not looking for a seat.  The management staff had spread out their computer and paperwork over half of the bar and remained seated there the entire evening. That evening was not my first experience with the management taking up the seats at the bar, and I am certainly confused as to their motivation and/or lack of concern for customers!  I wonder if the architect just forgot to put in an office for the staff?  Most importantly, when your servers are scared of the management, it makes for a very tense environment.  My first trip to the restaurant was just after the entire wait staff, bar staff and kitchen staff had all walked out. In my later visits, the servers seemed resentful and contemptuous.  I've been in the industry before, and it is always easy to tell when servers are enjoying their work and having fun, or are scared, or are bored, or are frustrated.  These servers seem scared.

Uninventive, bland, boring.  Expensive.  Poor service and poor attitudes. If you like singer/songwriters, whiskey and tears, then go for a beer; but be sure to eat before you go!

Being that STL has Forest Park, all of the other parks are sort of at a disadvantage, as there really is no comparison. That being said, Tower Grove Park has its charms.

Tower Grove is a nice sized park (I won't say large because Forest Park is large (massive); but Tower Grove would be considered large if it wasn't living in FP's shadow.) that runs from Grand to Kingshighway in length. The grounds seem to be nicely kept, but I've never used their restroom facilities so I cannot speak on those.  It's a lovely location for festivals, such as my favorite, the Festival of Nations. From spring til autumn you can catch bridal parties posing away to the backdrop of blossoming flowers or beautiful fall foliage.  It's also a great place for a leisurely walk or cardio workout, yoga, play dates/ real dates, picnics, teaching your teenager to drive, or Pokemon Go hunting, the later of which is how I typically spend my time here (as of late).  There are lots of pokestops and at least a dozen gyms. If you're walking your dog, they have doggy water fountains!

I am unsure if they have particular hours like the parks in Arizona.  The TG website only says from sunrise to sunset.  However, we've come by a few times after sunset and there were lots of cars still there and the park rangers drove by and didn't say anything, so... ?  It does get quite dark after sunset though. There aren't any lights aside from the street lamps, so if you're running, catching Pokemon, etc. just be aware and alert (as always). I will say that I have never felt unsafe here, no matter the time.

Tower Grove is a beautiful park (especially in autumn) and a lovely part of St. Louis history.

I really should've been going home (the hotel), but time in NOLA was limited and I really wanted to try their vegan dogs before I left.  So at 2am, our Lyft driver dropped us off and I stood in a long, but fast moving line.  They took my name and I had a seat while awaiting my carry-out order.  

I ordered the Chipotle vegan dog with chopped onions, jalapeños, Creole mustard (it is vegan friendly; made with a horseradish), and ketchup. I also got seasoned fries.  The hot dog was delicious! The seasoned french fries were delicious! I'll certainly return to Dat Dog!!

To buy cold bottled water, order from the bar; it was $1.66 per bottle.

It's a very popular place, so if you're coming with a group, have someone stand in line while the others find a table.  Cool hang out spot. They also have a balcony, so if you can find a spot, snag it, and do some people watching!

I wanted to love this place, I really did. It's super close to my house, the food is different from what other places in the area are offering, It sounds like a great concept, and has a huge amount of potential. 

If only they could get their act together.

I went here with 10 friends on Sunday night. I don't think it will do much good to list every single thing that went wrong that night, but will try to be specific enough to make this review useful.

Incorrect or extra drinks appeared at our table throughout the night. Beers which arrived sometimes were not the beers that were ordered. After he brings the beer, he proceeds to tell us they are out of the beer that was ordered. I thought most waiters could tell the difference between an IPA and a Stout by looking at it. Apparently not in our case. 

Extra cocktails magically arrived that belonged to no one. We were told to keep them and that they'd be free.

With the food things just went downhill. The meat wasn't cooked to order. Medium-rare Prime Rib doesn't look that shade of brown. And they ran out of prime rib, so our friend had to get some other cut of meat as a replacement. Potatoes were mealy and over cooked. My plate came out 20 minutes after the rest. (I was told it would be free for the mistake). The lamb was dry. The burgers were terrible. By the end of the meal, everyone agreed that the food in general was overpriced and not that great of quality. 

The reason I gave them two stars instead of one? The ice cream. Maybe the owners should have just opened an ice cream shop, because this was the one thing that was absolutely perfect.

To add insult to injury, when the bill arrived we noticed the waiter didn't comp the mistaken cocktails, beers and meals that he'd promised. And he refused to split the check. 

That scumbag still got his automatic 18% gratuity, even after messing up just about every thing we ordered.

Never. Again.

I should be featured on "Half-Ton Mom" considering all of the donuts I've eaten from Beiler's.

Some of my favorites are: Banana Cream, Apple Harvest, Maple Bacon (sells out fast), and Mocha Creme. I always come here with the intentions of buying 1) a slice of sour cream cheesecake from the gen. bakery section 2) two or three different doughnuts from the donut display. 

It seems like the line is usually wrapped around the corner and as soon as you turn the corner facing the registers, the salesperson is ready to take your order. I'm always like "Oh crap... I haven't really had time to see which ones I want....." LeSigh. That's when I just bite the bullet and randomly call out the first few I see. This method hasn't failed me yet. 

It's funny how I'm just reading here on Yelp that they have an actual donut menu to cut down on my self-induced madness. Eh...maybe I'll grab one next time and maybe not. When it comes to dessert flavors, I'm not super finicky. I like sweet stuff...and Beiler's does sweets right :)

Adam's Smokehouse has been on my list ever since I learned that this is another spin off creation from the staff at Pappy's & Bogart's, while the original team is not behind this location the staff had worked at Pappy's and received full support in getting things going and I have to say they have done a great job. 

I arrived mid afternoon on a Saturday and was promptly greeted by the friendly staff, I quickly decided on the Burnt Ends special, which was great so tender and perfectly smoked but what really made the sandwich stand out was the sauces. There are three types of sauce, Carolina Vinegar, Sweet Jane, but the best is the Cranberry Cayenne just a little bit of sweet with a kick. I think that this sauce has become my new favorite, it is delicious! Sides are pretty simple, I went with the baked beans which offered a good flavor and were quite filling.

Much like Pappy's in the early days if you want the best selection its best to arrive early because they will sell out., which I learned on my second visit when I arrived late on Friday evening and wanted to try the brisket. They were out of the brisket, chicken and ribs! It was recommended to me to get the Tri-Tip instead, so I did and while waiting for my order they brought out a sample of the Tri-Tip and it was awesome tender and flavorful! I think that this might be my newest obsession, especially when paired with the Cranberry Cayenne sauce!

Prices are fair and reasonable, however the inside is rather small, there is enough seating for about 8-10 tables however most people seemed to be ordering carry out.

For those that are not familiar, The Midwesterner is the creation of the most recently acclaimed Big Baby Q Smokehouse, which closed in December so that the owner, Ben Welch could focus on The Midwesterner. 

I hate to admit it; I was a little concerned after Big Baby Q announced they were closing and opening a new concept downtown. I was hopeful and optimistic, but I mean, St. Louis already has a couple of bbq joints in the city. Now with that being said it only took one visit for me to remember what made me fall in love with Big Baby Q, and I am happy to say that I enjoy the Midwesterner so much more.

I arrived on a Saturday afternoon for lunch with some friends, unfortunately, that Saturday happened to fall on Mardi Gras, so it made parking a little complicated. Once inside I was blown away with the work that was put into the venue in such a short amount of time. The Midwesterner will be the new hot spot, before and after Cardinals and Blues games! 

We were promptly shown to our table by our friendly waitress. I looked over the menu and confirmed that my Big Baby Q classic s were still available, but wait what is this a burger, a chicken biscuit and so much more! The menu itself was impressive and left me struggling on what to get, but ultimately I decided to go with the Fried Chicken Sandwich, which was a fried chicken thigh served with sharp cheddar cheese, country gravy and a sunny egg on a delicious homemade buttermilk biscuit. I went with the Mac "N' Cheese for my side, it was creamy and cheesy, just like like it should be! I was also able to sample a small slice of the Fried Burrata Toast, which was phenomenal! I am already planning my next trip so I can try the burger, which looks incredible. If you are feeling adventurous, you can pre-order the Crispy Pig Head, but be warned it's only available on the weekends. If you are a vegiterian there is no need to feel left out; there are several options that would work; however, the focus here is on the meat!

Overall The Midwesterner is a welcome addition to downtown (mostly because it's closer to me now). I have doubts that the owner, Ben, has created one of Downtowns newest hotspots!

The Mack is a small family friendly, neighborhood bar and grill located on Macklind Ave in South City's South Hampton neighborhood. By the looks on the outside you wouldn't really expect much, there are a few seats which provide limited outside seating but when you walk in you discover a good size bar with three unique sections. You first notice the bar section, however there are two more slightly separated spaces with more casual seating perfect for a drink with a friend, or even a quick meal with the family.

The atmosphere here is low key, there are more than enough TVs so you don't need to worry about missing a second of the Cardinals game either! There are also dart boards and even a basketball game which can allow you to challenge your friend to see who is a better shot! The staff here is friendly, and the beers are cold. Be sure to check their menu for the weekly specials, to save a few dollars. For example on Friday, you can get $1.50 domestics and a 8oz burger with fries for  1/2 Price, or on Saturday you can get a half priced pizza! Specials are dine in only, so no carry out at discounted prices!

The food here is equally as impressive, I have to admit that The Mack possibly serves one of the best burgers in Saint Louis and best of all, it's cheap starting at only $6.50 with the most expensive burger being $8.00 with fries! I ordered the Bacon Cheeseburger which is an 8oz burger topped with cheddar cheese and smoked bacon. The burger itself was seasoned perfectly, and cooked to perfection the bacon was crisp and delicious. The fries were perfectly crisp and seasoned and paired well with the burger, my meal was so good I came back the following Sunday to take advantage of the Sunday pizza special! The pizza is good, and served thin crust just like Imo's however I actually preferred the crust at The Mack over Imo's. The toppings are good, and appeared to be quality ingredients in fact the pepperoni had a unique spicy flavor without being too strong. I also tried some of their Toasted Ravioli, which were equally as tasty.

Overall The Mack offers great food, cold beer, family friendly service at a reasonable price (especially their daily specials). I really wish Yelp had I  1/2 star ratings, because I feel that The Mack deserves a solid 4.5 review, anyways I highly recommend adding The Mack to your list of places to visit!

Bay Leaves is basically a second location for Curry Leaves, and it located almost within walking distance of where I live. I am extremely glad they opened in this location. I love good Indian food, and Curry Leaves has always been a favorite! The food at Bay Leaves is a little different (regionally) but still has some of the same dishes that make Curry Leaves so popular. 

The new location is nice, and much larger. The staff is wonderful, very friendly and always willing to explain the menu items if need.

The food? OMG... I have a new favorite.. the Malabar Curry. So intense, with layers of flavors.. rich, creamy, and delicious! The Coconut rice was perfect, with a lot of whole spice, peppers, and grated coconut in it. The Garlic Naan was wonderful... soft tender fluffy Naan with lot of butter and garlic, some of the best I have had. The appetizer we ordered to share, the Samosa Chat, was very good... wonderful samosas cover in a variety of fresh topping with a tasty, spicy gravy mixed in.

My girlfriend ordered the Chicken Sag (Chicken cooked in Spinach and Yogurt and Spices) and it was delicious, and yes.. I helped myself to some of that too! lol!

I had come here for lunch also.. the same day (which is why we came again for dinner) . The lunch buffet offers a large number of different dishes that were all delicious, and yes.. tried them all, and waddled out the door! The tandoori chicken, tender and tasty! The Tikka Masala, sweet and yummy! The lemon rice was phenomenal, as was every dish I tried. Great place for lunch!

This is my new favorite place to go for superior Indian cuisine... it is wonderful. They just recently opened, and there are not waiting lines out the door yet, but there will be.. when Yelpers discover how good this place is!

HIGHLY Recommended!

Tried the Italian beef sandwich, which looks awesome on the Portillo's website... not so much in real life! It was ok... I have had much better. . I was not asked if I wanted Giardiniera on the sandwich, I just assumed it came that way... or at least with the peppers that the website says it comes with.  Not anything to make we want to go to Portillo's again.

Service was ok... nothing special there either
Great service, great coffee, and a really nice place to sit and just take a break from the world!

I have been meaning to get by Red Bowl and eat for quite a while. I used to eat at the same location (under different name) often. I love Sichuan food, and as Coty S. points out... this is the only game in town. Some of the other restaurants do have some good Sichuan dishes, but this is the only all Sichuan menu.

Had to try the Dumplings in Chili Oil ( I make these at home)... and they were pretty good. Meat filling is pretty basic, but the sauce makes up for it. Dumplings are always good!

I love any kind of dredged or battered fried chicken, so had to get some of the Salt and Crispy Chicken too. It was good. Dark meat chicken that dredged in corn starch and deep fried. Possibly marinated before cooking. 

Service was good, food was good. 4 stars all the way!

GOOD BURGER! Or should I say hamberder, like someone else recently did?

Seriously though... one of the best burgers I have had in Tampa! I ordered the double bacon cheeseburger, loaded... and man it was good! Normally I don't care for mayonnaise on a burger, but it works here. Big burger too... just perfect. Fries that came with the burger were good too... I enjoyed them! 

I had also ordered a side of Onion Thangs, as I love any kind of fried and battered onion. These are awesome... and they use tasty sweet onions, too! Almost like eating candy, they are so good!

Ordered a crab cake too.... because I could.  Excellent... lots of crab, and very tasty!

I can see why Tampa Bay loves the Burger Spot!

Wow... I enjoyed this. From the initial order over the phone to finishing it off at home, it was a wonderful experience.

When I called, they answered quickly, were helpful and answered any questions I had about the food. I was surprised at the time it took (they told me 45 minutes)... but some of the cooking techniques do apparently require that, and it tells me that the Injera bread was cooked when I ordered it, rather than being pre-made. Good things do take a little more time, right?

I arrived to pick it up, and the staff was very friendly. A darling young girl was in the front (obviously family). I love small family owned and run restaurants... and this one is definitely that.  My order was ready on time, and I discussed the alleged lack of traditional heat with the lady who checked me out... and she stated (as mentioned in other reviews) that they try to keep things mild since many Americans don't like spicy heat.  But she did offer to get me a small container of the Berbere spice to take home (good stuff... wonderful flavor and a nice heat level).

Arriving home, I took pics of the takeout containers (as usual) and we sat down to eat. The injera was very good.... as was my Kay Wat Fit Fit. I thought the red lentils needed more spice (and flavor)... greens were very good. 

My girlfriend loved her Doro Wat,  but was not too sure about the Injera (she has texture issues with some foods, lol)... but did enjoy it. 

The sambusas were delicious as was the Buticha.  

This has inspired me to learn to make Injera so I ordered some Teff flour. I will be using the Injera from Mitmita as a standard though, and suspect it will be hard to beat.

Be adventurous... try some cuisines  you have never tried. Enjoy life... and be safe!

I have not been to a Red Robin in probably 15 years. I might wait another 15 years to try again, if they still exist by then.

Too lazy to cook after having to work today. So we went out. Red Robin was fairly close, and usually used to do a decent burger.

Difference I noticed... Burgers are MUCH smaller than they used to be and more expensive. They now run less staff, and have a tablet at each table to do some ordering and pay by credit card.

We were seated almost immediately. Service looked promising.

I ordered an El Ranchero burger and upcharged sweet potato "Bottomless" fries, and a coke. Girlfriend ordered a Smoke and Pepper burger with Garlic fries (another upcharge)... and a iced tea.

My burger arrived. Took a bite, and discovered the burger was room temperature... or colder. I waited a bit and tried to get someone's attention... and gave up.  I guess I could have gotten up and chased someone down...  but chose not to. Fries were hot and crispy and delicious. Coke was adequate... tasted a little off, light on syrup.

Girlfriend said her burger was warm.. not hot. Her Garlic fries were hot and crisp. Her tea was tea.  

Continued to eat... after giving up on someone coming by. Burger was tasty... would have been great if it was hot. Ate all my fries, drank all my coke... no waitress. Burger gone.. still waiting. No waitress... wanted more fries, more coke. None!

Finally just decided to pay and leave. Paid on tablet, left feedback. 

Then I asked for a manager... explained everything. She offered some coupons for a free app on next visit. I told her no thanks... there would not be another visit.

Maybe it was an off night.... or maybe I should stop eating at chains that have less than 4 stars?

I have been trying to get to Sweet Buns since they opened... and something always came up, and I didn't go. Today... I made it, and am glad I did. But now I wish I still lived over in the University area, so I would not have to drive so far to get to Sweet Buns! 

After all the yelp reviews, I need to try their soups, and other lunch items. Today... just picked up some buns to get by on for a day or so (although I doubt they will last that long without being eaten!)

Already munched on the Red Bean bun... and it was perfect! So good! Trying to be good and not eat the others yet... lol.

I know I will be back here when in the area...

First time at Shaker & Peel. Good service, very friendly staff. Even had a manager stop by to say hi, and check on me. Even gave me a coupon for a free app on next visit. That is always appreciated.

I ordered a Lemonade to drink, and it came quickly. Lavender Lemonade... lovely color, but a little sweeter than I had anticipated. Not unusual with America's love for too much sugar. It was still good though.

Ordered the Hot Chicken Taco, Grouper Taco, and a Volcano Shrimp Taco, just to see what they were like. The grouper taco, and the volcano shrimp taco both had a strong fruit salsa flavor (again, very sweet) that sort of hid the shrimp and grouper flavors to some degree. You could tell them apart... but the common ingredient was that salsa.

The Hot Chicken taco... plenty of spice, and the coleslaw that was on it also had a strong tangy, sweet fruit flavor... enough to where I could barely really taste the chicken.  This seems to be a coming thing in tacos, though... as one other restaurant I recently visited has the same type of taco.

Nicely decorated interior, and a beautiful bar area. Again, the staff rocked! I had four or five different people stop by to fill the water glass, bring my food, and just say hello. 

I will be back, but I might request a slight decrease in the salsa application, lol! That or get it on the side...

I stopped by for lunch, because I noticed some of the Yelp photos of some gorgeous looking Onion Rings. I love the darn things, and am always searching for the best. These looked awesomely good.

So when I arrived, I ordered a Black and Bleu burger (medium rare) and asked to sub Onion Rings for the fries. I was told that they no longer have onion rings in this location (although other locations still do). So POO! I said fries will fine! lol! 

SURPRISE! When they brought my burger out, the manager had also made me some hot, fresh Onion Rings.... I was shocked! But happily so. And they were indeed very good (dipping sauce was excellent also). My waitress/bartender told me she had mentioned my order to her manager... and they helped me out! How many places will do something like that?

Burger was really good too... lots of bleu cheese, and very tasty. Fries were spot on too (I ate all of my delicious Onion Rings first, though!)

Excellent service, both from my waitress, and from the kitchen and management staff!  I was told the Fish and Chips uses the same batter they used on the Onion Rings, so I will be going back soon to try that.

Highly recommended... 5 stars!

Good times, good food, and fun people to hang with!  Hats off to Coty S. for setting this up! Great event... lots of different delicious Taiwanese food to try! We all ordered different dishes and passed them around. The Pepper Fried Chicken was good, the Pork Chop Rice looked delicious (didn't get to try that one, darn it!), Pepper Steak was very good. The Curry Pizza and General Tso's Pizza's that were ordered looked good (didn't try those either.. trying a low carb DIE with a T!) The buns and dumplings were well received... and Yes, I had one dumpling.. I could not resist and it was delicious!

I have been to Mei's before... and love the Beef Noodle soup also. Scallion pancakes are also excellent!

Thanks to Mei's for putting up with, and providing a wonderful time!

I received word that Miss Tara (the owner of the shop) passed away this morning. I know that everyone in the YELP community that has ever eaten the wonderful food here will miss her. Not sure what will happen to the shop. Just wanted to let yelpers know.  5 stars for the food and the memories....  

Update (according to the business facebook page, the family and staff will keep the business open)! If you love good food, you really should try the doubles here... the goat curry rocks, as does the channa curry! Some of the best Roti I have had... love it buss up shut style!

I have been to Mel's many times... I was surprised that I had never reviewed them before. Shocked even, lol!

Great hot dogs and sandwiches, huge orders of tasty fries, and wonderful and friendly customer service! This place is a gem! 

Today I had a classic Chili Cheese dog, upgraded to the Mighty Mel 4oz. dog... and a large order of fries. Very tasty, and plenty of food!

One of the reasons I love this place, is the help behind the counter! Always smiling, friendly and they really do seem to be happy to be there serving you great dogs! 

C'ya at Mels!

Margarita day event, UYE I think. I think I am the only one that showed up, lol!  Oh well! 

Good service... seated immediately, and friendly staff! Maggie (our waitperson) was on top of it!

Ordered the YELP Strawberry Margarita (later in the day I would have chose the house marg, BOGO)... but at 11am, even one margarita is pushing it for me. It was delicious, very refreshing... and not overly strong. Tart and tangy! 

Chips and salsa.... good. Chips appear to be a hybrid between a corn tortilla and a flour tortilla. Very crispy, light coated with a taco salt that was tasty. Salsa was good with a nice chipotle flavor, but badly needed some salt IMO. 

I ordered the grilled shrimp tacos. Very good... although kind of heavy on the mango/pineapple/whatever salsa, which was really sweet. But i would order again. Portions were decent. Salad that came with it was excellent.

GF ordered the Mahi-mahi tacos... and said they were good, but she would probably order something else on repeat visits. She did like her Mango iced tea! 

All in all a nice meal, a good drink. All I was missing were more Yelpers!

3.5 stars. I loved Pine State Biscuits in Portland, so I was excited to eat here in Reno. Unfortunately my experience at the Reno location wasn't quite on par with my experience in Portland. 

I ordered the Reggie deluxe and it didn't live up to the fond memories I had of my Reggie deluxe in Portland. The chicken and biscuit were dry. My friends said their chicken strips were dry as well. I love over medium eggs, but the yolk of this egg was dry and cooked through (hard boiled like consistency) without any crispiness to the whites. 

The gravy helped with all the dryness, though I asked for it on the side and there wasn't much of it. I got half sausage/half mushroom gravy and loved the mushrooms. I asked for my Reggie deluxe to be spicy, so the side of buffalo sauce helped with the dryness as well. 

The girl behind the counter seemed annoyed by my questions for clarification. However the girl that was on floor was really friendly and helpful when we were moving tables to accommodate our party. We came around 1pm on a Saturday afternoon with no wait which was a nice surprise. Pine State Biscuits can be a good option (if it's not too busy) for groups since you order at the counter and seat yourself. 

I might not have had such high expectations if I had never tried Pine State Biscuits before, but the overall dryness of the food was disappointing. I'm rarely in the area, but may consider giving this location another try next time I'm in town.

Like many of us on the East Side, I had long awaited the opening of The Treehouse.   I watched the local artisan-crafted furniture and tableware arriving, saw menu teasers, and spied on the construction over the fence on my way to 5 spot dancing. After my first visit, The Treehouse certainly did not disappoint!

My friend and I were lucky enough to snag a seat at the bar so we could watch everything that was going on in the open kitchen.  (Note to whomever those girls were watching said kitchen by pressing their faces to the stained glass window from the patio: the bar is how you do it. Your way was creepy.) 

 I started with a glass of cava and a high-grav for my beer only companion. The drink list and wine selection was well thought out and featured several great choices that won't break the bank. We had several dishes, all delicious,but the tiradito was definitely my favorite. The flavors popped and the presentation was stunning.  We ran out of appetite before we ran out of dishes we wanted to try so we will definitely be returning.   

I would recommend The Treehouse to anyone who wants to stay in the Points (because, let's face it, who ever wants to cross the river?), and have a great meal, or share a small dish and a bottle of wine with friends.

Have been debating on stopping by for about five years, finally went for the first time during a weekday when they were not busy to try them out. Soon as we walked in I was impressed with the decor and the island like atmosphere. Don't expect to be seated, you just walk in and find a spot, walk towards the back and let them know you are there if they don't come to you. That's a strike imo. An acknowledgement at the very least falls under the common expectation category. 

Anyway, the tables were not cleaned out, the cash only deal is a bit of a turn off as well. They do have an ATM inside just so you know. Wouldn't be surprised if they owned it, that's smart business. 

The service was slow but friendly, the Chattaway Burger is what was raved about, I'd go back if just for that, but would probably take-out the next time around.

No longer as good as before. The felafel wrap lacked flavor, a little on the dry side. Id much rather go with the felafel all by itself... The spinach pie was greasy and not very appetizing. Fries are boring, nothing Lebanese about them. Children menu options are way too limited, such is the case for the fountain drinks. Nothing special here... If you want true authentic Lebanese go to Fresh Bites down by race track ave.

Yes, the reviews on this place appear to be on point. They offer the hand tossed style and the Detroit style, being this was my first visit, I decided to try both to compare the two. The hand tossed was decent, nothing really to brag home about, it didn't taste much different than other hand tossed pizza that I've had in the past. 

The Detroit style was a totally different story. This Pizza was pretty unique. I loved everything, from the dough, the crust, the cheese and most important, that sauce on top is just right... You add all that up, you have yourself a home run. Would stop by again for sure. Skip the hand tossed and go for the gold.

First of all, ABEC is a fantastic restaurant, you have to consider it a top 10, heck! you could argue that it's a top 5 in the breakfast category. It's really that good. Only tried it once thus gar, I usually wait to post a review just to be sure the consistency is there and the review is fair. But when you have a breakfast this good, why wait. 

The Western Omelette I ordered was just perfect. The menu offers such a variety, making a choice can be challenging. Was not crazy about the coffee, was better than most but I much rather go a few doors down and grab me a cup at cafe caribe. I'll try one of the specialties on my next visit. Service was terrific, waitress was friendly and attentive.

So why four and not five? The parking and the pricing. The lot is congested and the dishes though very good are a little high for a breakfast joint. Four sounds about right. I shall return.

Nothing to brag home about. The food tasted homemade. Not bad, not great. I'll start out with the food, Wifey and I ordered a good variety. 

The gumbo was on the salty side and was also very light on the seafood. (To be honest... Im not sure It even had any) Broiled Oysters had a bit much parmesan, just ok. Fried Alligator wasn't bad, properly fried. Red Beans and Rice could've been creamier, but came out ok, again very homemade. Ditto on the Corn on the cob. I've had better. 

The best dish was probably our dessert. We had The bananas foster, it was perfect. It truly helped balance out all the different flavors. 

The establishment and the service was fantastic. The staff was attentive and very friendly. I would recommend SE for a happy hour and a quick bite, just don't set your expectations too high.

Pretty good spot for a quick bite. Cuban Foodies passed the breakfast challenge so I had to try them out for lunch before adding my review. 

In a nutshell. It was all good! Nothing mind blowing here, just good, fresh, made to order Cuban cuisine. A few critiques for me: My hash brown was slightly overcooked and the empanadas (though not bad) didn't meet my expectations. Would love it if they offered a variation on the Cuban Toast for breakfast. An egg/cheese sandwich would be nice.

Started off the morning with the mezclado, a combination of scrambled eggs, cuban toast, and hash brown. Not a bad selection, enjoyed every bite. Im more of a coffee for breakfast type of guy, Im usually picky when it comes to my coffee, have to say I enjoyed their cafe con leche here, it was the perfect temperature, a bit strong (thats not a complaint) and tasted just right. 

For lunch, I went for the picadillo bowl with maduros. Again, delicious, zero complaints. Also tried Wifey's, she went for the chicken bowl with yellow rice and a salad, and the regular flan at the end. Delicioso!! Everything was fresh, and authentic, everything is made in house. 

My rating, is based on a number of factors: Value, Service, Simplicity, and Tasty food overall. Though there is room for improvement... they've only been open for a short period of time. In talking with the workers here, I can say the potential is certainly there. 

Cuban Foodies can be a four or a five star, Ill go with the latter for now. Cuban Foodies deserves an opportunity. Plus the coffee and the flan hit the mark for me. Can't speak for the other items on the menu, but my experience here was a good one.

An instant favorite. Went on opening day and already looking forward to going back.  4Rivers has the perfect formula, that cafeteria style is awesome for BBQ, there's nothing else like it in Tampa Bay, reminiscent to Chipotle. 

I wanted to try the entire menu, it all looked and smelled so good. I went all out and ordered a little bit of everything. Tried numerous sides, corn, sweet potato casserole, bread pudding, baked beans, collard greens, and I must say it was all very delicious. The bread pudding was phenomenal, didn't expect it to be that good. Trust me, it's worth going to 4Rs for this one side alone. Then we go on to the Brisket and the Prime Rib, in one word, heaven.  

The location is excellent, good parking, comfortable seating, you can dine in or order take-out, they also sell cupcakes which is a nice touch.... they also have to go boxes and lids right by the soda fountain, so instead of waving someone down you can grab it yourself when you're ready, how fantastic! I'm not one to drop the big 5 on just any business but 4Rs is well deserved.

Ideal for just about any special occasion, birthdays, anniversaries, etc.. Tried Fleming's for the very first time for the Mel's 14 year anniversary and I couldn't find any major flaw even if I tried. 

Ambiance & Service was world class. Upon our arrival, they offer complementary valet parking... so convenient. The kitchen was all white and looked squeaky clean. We had a great seat arranged for the occasion. They added a greeting card, gave us champagne, took our photo and had it ready for us within minutes, about four different staff members walked by to wish us a happy anniversary, topped off the night with a box of truffles at the end. So needless to say, Fleming's went above and beyond expectations. 

Our waiter Jaime did an outstanding job. He was very pleasant, attentive, offered suggestions, and made sure the night was a special one. 

Now on to the menu. As any high end restaurant, The food will cost you an arm and a leg. But if you appreciate and love steak, I'd say look no further. Wifey went with a surf and turf and I did the dry aged bone in ribeye. Both were phenomenal. You know you have a good ribeye when the fat melts in your mouth. This was as good as any steak I've ever had. Truth...

Far as the sides. We had the Fleming's potato, chopped salad and sautéed mushrooms. With the exception of the chopped salad, I wasn't crazy crazy about the rest. Not that I didn't enjoy them, I just wasn't crazy about 'em. 

All in all it was a great night, we went home happy. Fleming's is what every steakhouse should be. I'd rank Fleming's second or third best steakhouse in Tampa. I must try the tomahawk steak next time.

One of the better Latin restaurants in all of Tampa Bay. The overall rating on Yelp is well deserved. Hard to believe it took so long for me to try them out. Awesome food+great service equals 5 stars.

Funny thing about my first visit was the fact that I was going in with nothing but the arepa sandwich in mind, then came across the menu. Everything looked so good that I went for a little bit of everything and ended up bypassing the arepa. 

The Palmitos salad is one that you must order, it was truly divine. Everything from the tostones, the parrilla, the chicken and beef skewers, were on par. The cachapa queso de mano was in a class all by itself, that cheese was like butter. 

They did a great job in making the establishment have an upscale feel. If there was a downside, it would be the limited space. I can also see parking being an issue during a busy day. But don't sweat the small stuff, come for the food and you wont be disappointed.

GSB is quite nice. The service was friendly, they offer a nice atmosphere, felt like being in a beach house. Food wasn't bad. They also have a live guitarist that'll play happy birthday upon request. All in all the experience was good.

So why the three star rating? Well despite the decent meal, it just didn't match the price tag. It wasn't unforgettable, it was just decent. The $26 duck roast had high expectations, which was met half way. 

I did enjoy the Bison chop steak, still a similar deal to the duck. Its lean ground beef with a pretty good wine sauce, the potatoes and carrots that came with it were excellent, but again, the Bison being the star of the show for me, was nothing over the top.

The Shrooms and Saganaki were delish, but a bit small for the price, especially the Saganaki. 

Anyway, GSB is worth checking out once or twice. Either increase the quality of the food or decrease the price tag, and Ill bump up the rating. 

keep in mind there is an automatic gratuity added to the check. FYI.

After trying out Elizabeth's oner the weekend, I became an instant fan. I loved the coffee, loved the pastries, solid service. 
Establishment was clean, on the small side with outdoor seating. Prices were a touch bit higher than expected. 

This is a solid spot for anyone looking to skip a heavy breakfast. A coffee and pastry is my type of place. Elizabeth's is a strong four stars for me. 

They also sell loafs of bread. Tried the soda bread, it was very good, tasted a lot like a cornbread. Hope to try some of the other options at some point down the road.

This rating is solely based on my first experience. I do plan to try them again in the future to try other dishes. Anybody that truly knows me will understand my love affair with Plantains. I've been eating it since I was a kid growing up in the islands. 

Wifey picked up some Tostones Nachos to try, and this is my take. I was a bit surprised to learn this wasn't an appetizer but a meal which is fine with me, long as it's good. 

I had mixed feelings, if you love the taste of Mayo then stop reading and go buy these Nachos. I personally don't care for Mayo, if it's in a sauce and it's not overpowering, I'm game. Unfortunately that was not the case with these Nachos.

For one, the actual plantation was cooked very well, it tasted great, if anything, I felt they could've added a few more tostones considering the price. Now the topping was what ruined it for me. It was Mayo overload. I can still taste it. 

I'll try a few other dishes at some point and bump up the rating if necessary. But for now, it's a two for me.

Tara's is just right up my alley. It's got that island feeling that you can only get out in the caribbean. Nothing fancy, just fantastic food. The five stars is based solely on that fact and nothing else. 

Just had the stewed oxtail (buss up shot) and roti, and man!! It was just divine. One of the best comfort meals I've ever had. The fatty gelatin around the oxtail melts in your mouth.. the gravy was just right. 

The hot sauce is super spicy, a little bit goes a long way. 

Loved the curry shrimp as well. I would recommend coming in for lunch on an empty stomach, you'll leave full, assuming you can finish it all.

So happy to know JJI is making out ok in Tampa. It's hard to find good  Caribbean food in the area. Glad to know that JJI appears to be here to stay. My all time favorite Jamaican dish is the Oxtail. If you can make this dish correct, you'll get a high rating from me (hence the four stars). 

On my latest visit, I went for the roti and Oxtail, neither one disappointed. 
They ran out of rice and peas, so I'll need to come back on another occasion to report on this, though I don't see how they can possibly mess this up. Plus they sold out hours before closing, that could be a good sign. 

As I said before. The Roti and Oxtail here is very good, not the best I've ever had, but still rock solid. Just be careful with the Roti, cause it comes out extremely hot, so go easy. I'm sure I'll be bumping up my rating once I a chance to try a few other dishes.

Really nothing short of five stars. Cant speak for the rest of the Chefs, but try to get in with chef Kevin Belton. He makes it fun and is interactive with everyone in the crowd. 

They offer recipes and seasonings to take home. Also, enough Abita, Lemonade & Sweet Tea to go around. 

Great experience overall, its plain and simple. Good way to spend a couple hours during your visit to NOLA. Chef Belton was awesome. He deserves his own cooking show on the food network. Enjoyed every minute.

Just ok, 2-3 star range is about right. Used to be a fan of SB in Clearwater, this location is more on the up and down. I hate inconsistency, seems like you just have to cross your fingers when you come.

The Brisket here is decent, I'm not crazy about much else they got going on. Tried the crispy chicken salad for the first time, it was completely drenched in honey mustard dressing, yuck!

Service here is ok, parking is not a problem, I hear they have Bingo on Tuesdays as well. SB is really nothing special. Wont be rushing back.

Not the best - so the search continues.

The poundcake is extremely dense, looks and feels as heavy as a brick.  Their signature poundcake is covered with vanilla icing.  

Now for the verdict - SALT & BUTTER ABUSE!  

With every bite I took, I kept hoping that it was a section that just wasn't mixed well and that a new bite would taste less salty.  No luck.

I do NOT want to eat a salty cake.  Barf.  
Then again, Philly tastebuds have become de-sensitized by salt so the locals might not even flinch.

Pound for pound it is just too much - too much salt, too much butter, too much sugar, and not in a good way.  If you cut yourself a slice and eat it with your hands, you hands will be quite moisturized from the butter or lard.  Also, I'm fairly certain they use sour cream in their recipe as well.  Be prepared to have a beverage while consuming this because as moist as it is, you might choke on it because it is so dense.  I would have preferred the cake to be a little softer and cake like. 

They weigh the poundcake. Ours came out to $9.44.  I have no idea how much a pound costs because they don't have a menu nor do they display the prices or tell you (not that we asked). 

We also had their shortbread butter cookies - now these are better but just as rich and heavy.  One cookie probably has about a half a stick of butter that goes into it, if not more, which is how it is able to stay so soft and dense.  These cookies aren't crumbly like you would find at other Italian bakeries but again, it is due to the crazy amount of butter in it.  


Also, expect zero customer service from these guys.  They look up to see who is walking through the door, do not greet you, then they will rush you, even when it isn't busy at all.  Not a pleasant bakery experience at all, but then again, most mom and pop Philly bakeries want you to keep it moving - get in and get out.

Definitely not worth the trip out here.  

Parking - street

This Sunday marked the 4th Tampa Brunch Tour stop at Oystercatchers located inside of the Grand Hyatt, Tampa. Ever since I moved to Tampa, Oystercatchers Brunch was on my "must do list". Myself along with 5 other Tampa Food Bloggers set out for an early Sunday morning brunch.

Upon arrival we had an introduction about Oystercatchers brunch from the talented Chef de Cuisine, Hector Pabon. Chef explained that he changes up the menu every week and during this visit, we experienced a Florida Cuba style brunch.

Finding ourselves among unlimited mimosa's & champagne (hooray for Chateau Ste. Michelle bubbles!). Seriously, our glasses did not go beyond half empty once.

A fully stocked Bloody Mary Bar with three different concoctions - traditional, clammato and extra spicy. Two different flavor rimmers and multiple options in the stuffed olive category. Oh - and BACON.

Walking to our table, I instantly fell in love with Oystercatchers Brunch - my caviar obsessed eyes went straight to this line up and I will be honest - if I were not here on a blogger brunch, I would have sat here for hours consuming this goodness. Oh caviar, I have missed you so!!! What goes perfect with caviar? The most perfect smoked Salmon one could ever get their hands on, paired with everything a lox fan could ever dream of.

Then, my eyes focused on the cheese and caricature board. One of the cheese selections was "drunken goat" and I am currently in hunt for what may be my new favorite cheese.

Let's move onto breakfast items, shall we. Our fantastic server greeted us with bubbles and explained the various stations. Breakfast, Lunch, Raw bar, pasta bar, salad stations, sushi and of course everything I mentioned above....oh and a dessert bar not to be missed. More on that later. He explained our omelet station would have every topping one could desire (it did) and various eggs, egg whites and QUAIL EGGS! I decided to get a spinach, mushroom, garlic, bacon and quail egg omelet. While it was delicious, I am generally an egg white kinda of gal and this was a bit rich for me. Also on the plate below is.....drum roll please......a lobster egg Benedict. My breakfast gods have died and gone to heaven.

One of the tables favorite items on the menu was the spring rolls with every dipping sauce you could imagine. I have a weakness for spring rolls - I don't feel guilty eating them and these were delicious. Oystercatchers had two different sushi rolls available this day, tuna and California.

I was beyond impressed with the pasta station. Offering house-made pasta - everything from linguine to ravioli to gnocchi. I opted with a unique concoction - gnocchi, vodka sauce, prosciutto, sun-dried tomato, chicken and asparagus. I lost all self control. My flavors were a bit odd but the sauce and the gnocchi were very good.

Let's take a visit over to the dessert bar. I went in with a full stomach and wide eyes. If you ever go to Oystercatches on your birthday - let them know. You may get a special treat! The dessert bar was out of this world and you must visit it. Bananas Foster, Ice Cream Bar, Patries galore. You name it. 

Is oystercatchers worth the brunch price? Absolutely!

I hate this place. 
I use this word sparingly.
I hate this place.

The mister and I patronized this establishment a few years ago.

The place was very crowded and loud. 
We were seated pretty promptly.

The waiter greeted our table 35 minutes, I shit you not, after we were seated -- without an apology.

We received our appetizer 45 minutes after we put in our order.
To this, we expressed our disdain for the service or lack thereof. 

The staff were extremely pretentious. 
We told them we were going to leave and didn't care to eat the appetizer, which was an effing salad! and didn't care to receive our ordered entree.

The obviously annoyed waiter left our table to get a manager that informed us that we would still have to pay for our meal although, we weren't interested in waiting to receive it. 

They charged us a little over $90.

Most people wouldn't pay. 
I sure as HELL didn't want to pay but my husband is an honorable man, so we did. We paid but vowed that they would pay in the end.

I've always walked past this place but never gave it a second thought, it's located on a random part of the block and the front of the restaurant is not much to look at in terms of aesthetics.  Our friend recommended this place for lunch as he was pretty hung over and couldn't figure out what he could stomach.
The place is more of a take-out quick lunch/dinner spot then a dining destination. The décor is dated, but let me tell you- the food was delicious! I was very pleased with everything that we ordered. I actually filled up with the starters that I couldn't finish my lamb kabob sandwich.  
I highly recommend the tabbouleh, so yummy, I couldn't stop eating it! The hummus and meat was really filling too. I've never had hummus served with meat before, but it was a lot more filling then the normal- we actually tried both the regular hummus and with meat appetizer, you can't go wrong! Our friend was raving about this 'garlic dipping sauce' out came this thick white yogurt, I took a large scoop, boy did it pack a punch! They should really bottle it and sell it, I would grab a couple of bottles! I highly recommend you request an extra side of it! DH had the mixed grilled platter, which really gave you a bang for your buck, it was an assortment of rice, chicken, beef and kafta. He was raving about how nice the spices complimented the food and was very pleased with everything he ate. Our waitress was very chatty and took great care of us. She was always filling our glasses and made great recommendations on the food selection.  

We grabbed a take-out menu as they deliver. This place is going to replace the delivery place we currently use for Lebanese/Middle Eastern food!

I've only ever ordered take away here for lunch and the food is always delicious and filling! 
My husband took me here for my birthday | anniversary dinner and the evening was wonderful! We were directed to go downstairs for dinner, after a decending the stairs and making out way past framed images of Italy, we emerged behind the curtain to see a long bar with patrons quietly enjoying their drinks and conversation. The ambience was that of a swanky speakeasy- dark and sultry- almost a little too dark, I could see other diners breaking out their iPhones for the flashlights to see the menu. We were seats at a unusually small table in the corner or a banquette.

Our server was awesome- I greeted us with complimentary Prosecco for our 'birthaversary' it was so sweet of them to add that special touch to start off our evening.  Everything was serviced family style so the portions were more than enough for us to share. We started out with the beef carpaccio, it was so beautifully presented, a bit on the salty side but we devoured every bite. Then came the octopus, I loved the combination of the acidity of the fennel paired with the tender octopi. The starters were beginning to fill us up but then we had to make room for the veal parmigiana, crispy veal under a generous covering of marinara sauce and mozzarella cheese, it was so unbelievably good, the dish was large but it easily when down our bellies. We always order the wild boar bolognese- oh my goodness, the decedent sauce and the delicious boar meat was just divine. I highly recommend this dish for any diner on the fence about whether to order it or not!
Our waiter was attentive and kept the plates coming at a good pace. We were too stuffed for dessert but there was enough room for the homemade limoncello. It was excellent, the liqueur was bright and sweet with a subtle bite of the alcohol- it was presented in this beautiful etched cordial glass. Dispite passing on dessert- we were presented with this sparkling cannoli to celebrate our big night out! It was a wonderful finishing touch to a really nice evening.

Bacio gets a 5-star rating for their consistency.  I've been here maybe 5 times since they've opened, and every single time I've had a delicious meal and a nice, un-rushed time.  

It is a very small space, but I've never felt cramped or uncomfortable.  The food is fresh, the service is friendly and not too rushed, and the vibe is relaxed.  It is the perfect "date night" BYOB.  

Bacio is a gem.  Mt. Airy-ites are lucky to have it in their neighborhood.

On July 10, 2017, my hubby had arrived to Sparks, NV for a next day delivery.  With much needed rest, I decided to reserve a room in the Western Village Hotel and Casino which was adjacent to the truck stop where he had parked.  Temperatures were about 98 degrees and trying to rest inside a truck (even with the engine idling to keep the A/C running) would have been uncomfortable.

Approx. 12 pm, I called their 800 number and the rep who answered was courteous and took my reservation with no issues.  He gave me a price of $79.00+tx (later on I was told that truckers get a discount, which it lowered the price to approx. $66.00+tx). However he never mentioned that check-in was until 3:00 pm.  I'll admit, I should have asked.

Approx. 1:30 pm, after talking with my hubby and telling him to walk over to the hotel, he arrived at the hotel and after giving the front desk rep (unknown name) my reservation number, he was told that check-in was not until 3:00 pm.  He walked back to his truck with his belongings and waited in his truck. While all this was happening I was sending in the credit card authorization form and called back to confirm.

Approx. 2:50 pm, I called my hubby and told him to start heading over to the hotel, this would have given him enough time to arrive and begin checking-in at about 3:00 pm.

At 3:05 pm, my hubby messages me telling me the room was "not" ready and to come back in 30 minutes to an hour.  He returned to his truck "again" in 98 degree weather with his belongings.

I called their front desk (upset of course) and their front desk rep (Mat) answered, he apologized (a whatever kind of apology) and said he would look into it and hung up.  That's it!? no, info?.... no, I see what happened here?... no, this is what's going on?.... Nothing!

I called again, guess who answered?... Mr. Mat.  I asked him what had been resolved about my reservation, he said, the room was not available and that my hubby wasn't around (of course... because he went back to his truck for the 3rd time in 98 degree weather!) I finally had it.... I asked him if he was aware that it was 98 degrees outside and his sarcastic answer was, "yeah, that's what it seems like".  That was it!

I simply told him it wasn't right for them so keep sending my hubby back and fourth on 98 degree weather.  I told him that he had been there twice and and twice he was turned back. Mat  simply gave me an "I really don't care attitude".  I finally asked for his manager and after a 4-5 minute wait, Monica (front desk manager) answered the phone.

As I began to  explained what was going on, she began talking to me without paying any attention to what I was saying (similar to when you talk to an operator from India).  She kept insisting that my hubby had arrived too early and that rooms are not ready until 3 pm.  As I explained to her that my hubby was not just there early, he was there around 3 pm and he was told that his room wasn't ready.  I asked her if there was anyone above her and she said (of course) no... she was it.  She finally apologize (not really meaning it) and decided to simply give me a $20.00 discount. I went quiet for a few seconds (couldn't believe it). I didn't want a discount, I just wanted a respectful service and for my hubby to rest!

I accepted the discount (not really happy about it) and my hubby got his room at approx. 3:40 pm :|.  I was not happy with the outcome.  I finally got hold of Jim Moritz (someone supposedly higher than Monica) and explained to him of my experience, he apologized, said he would look into it (which gave me the sense that he won't).

Today July 11, 2017, I checked my credit card and to my amazement there is a $108.74 pending charge from none other, "Western Village Hotel and Casino".  I called and requested their accounting department (to request a copy of the bill) and of course, I had to leave a message.

My next step..... Consumer Affairs... Motel 6 may give you the same treatment as this place, but at least you know what you're going to pay for it... definitely not $108.47.

Will definitely will be returning with my hubby.  Great vibe and fantastic food.
The restaurant looks so clean  and in a great location.

I love to hate on my vegetarian/vegan friends because I'm such a meat lover but this place was delightful!

Located near Rittenhouse Square, I walk by this restaurant all the time and finally got to try it recently. It's an inviting sleek space with many windows that open up during warm months. The entrance leads to a slightly narrow bar area which then widens into the dining room. It's visually pleasing, and I think a perfect spot for a group of 4 vegetarian/vegan friends to dine at. Also a datey option but the tables are fairly close to each other not sure if it confers enough privacy.

The food itself is tasty. My favorites were the huarache (celery root, grilled maitake mushrooms, parsnip escabeche, radish) from the Snacks section and the buffalo cauliflower tacos (with avocado-green goddess dressing, butter lettuce, carrots). 

The meal can get pricy if you really want to be full, but that's to be expected when there's no meat! :P I thought it was reasonable and enjoyed my time here!

If you are looking for Nashville hot chicken, check this place out! They do Nashville hot chicken right! And they give you the option to name your heat--mild all the way to super hot.

I had the Tattoo Brick Chicken (grilled chicken w/ goat cheese over veggies) because I was trying to be a little healthy. However, I likely negated my "healthy" choice by partaking in the amazing nachos, wings, and other entrees my dining group ordered. All winners, btw! In fact, I imagine it's hard to go wrong with anything they offer.

One final note: The service at Fowl is A+!! Kudos to the management there for training the staff to excel. I did see, however, one or two of the wait staff who were slack with their masks (Apr 2021). I would encourage management to keep the masks going until the CDC clears for no masks for indoors.

Hit the post-lunch rush, pre-dinner crowd for a quick bite. Most everything about the experience rode between meh and A-OK.

The cashiers make their disdain towards customers pretty apparent as my two questions (with nobody behind me, mind you) seemed to chafe the gal behind the counter. Opted for the Ferdi, a house specialty po boy layered with their famous baked ham, roast beef, debris and a heavy ladle of gravy. I mean, I guess it was fine - a regular is definitely a hearty meal - but I wasn't bowled over by the meats, the bread desperately needed a good saturatin' by the beef drippings, and the whole shebang (sand sides) rang in at $13. Bloody Mary in an 8oz plastic cup tipped this kinda just okay meal over $21, and I know I could have spent the same for better.

She was completely unimpressed with their three stack of pancakes. One of the two questions I asked: "can she get a side of bacon with her 'cakes?" You'd think I ran over her dog. "We do NOT serve bacon."

** If you learn nothing else, learn this: Mother's does not serve bacon. That is all. **

Okay, not all. We went sausage instead and I actually preferred the house-made links to anything else on the menu.

The last and most peculiar point: you order at a counter, a server brings you the food. There are signs everywhere that says "We at Mother's do not accept gratuities." There's a story about it in the menu. So you can imagine how squirmy we got when our server mentioned said signs, and said, "While it's the restaurants tradition, we do actually accept tips." Well, this is fucking awkward.

Three stars because nothing was outright bad, it was just a mediocre meal. That said, it's New Orleans - I'm in no rush to go back.

Lemon blueberry goat cheese pancake stole the show. A show that went on. Way. Too. Long. 

I get the brunch rush, and a prolonged wait even twice the quote time. It's the weekend. It's brunch at a brunch spot... I truly understand. But once we had butts in seats, it still took near an hour to get food ordered and served. Inexcusable.

The Bloody Mary tasted like lime-squeezed hot sauce and little else. The chicken and biscuit breakfast sandwich was hearty, salty and comforting - proper fried breast, moist and well-seasoned, a "broken egg" that wasn't and cooked hard, and a tender biscuit with savory sausage gravy. I wish I was hungover, but wasn't and enjoyed it nonetheless. 

The wait murdered the whole experience, though. I felt bad for our server who was being burdened by high-maintenance tables. That said, there was only a passing apology and a definitive write-off to our table's needs. Definitely dampened an otherwise four star meal.

A friend mentioned this place to me so I decided to check it out. I went in during happy hour. During happy hour the tacos are $1 off and the salsas and drinks are discounted as well. I got a clasico margarita and it was pretty good. I also ordered the Yucateca Habanero salsa. It was very good. A little sweet and kind of fruity then the heat hits you on the tail end. It's watery though but I like watery salsas as opposed to the chunkier ones. I would like to try the others. I ordered 3 tacos: the Baja fish, cajun fish, and the black bean. To my surprise, my favorite of the three was the black bean. It had the most flavor out of them all. It had pico, sweet potato, and cotija cheese. The Baja fish was also pretty good but needed a little punch so I added some of the habanero salsa to it. My least favorite was the cajun fish taco. I think the piece of fish could've been a little bigger and had more seasoning. It was quite bland. The tortillas on each of the tacos were nice and fresh. I had both corn and flour. I prefer the flour. For whatever reason, I did something I rarely do and ordered dessert. Apparently, the chef does different types of sorbets and I chose the cactus sorbet because I'm all for trying something new. I was pleasantly surprised. It was sort've strange but tasty. It definitely tasted a touch grassy or plant-like but that's to be expected because...cactus. It was sweet but not too sweet and a bit tart. The consistency was a bit.....viscus I guess I would say. I would get it again. The decor is very cute. It's small and cozy inside. The location is hidden away on a side street so they'll definitely need word of mouth to get people over there. I did notice that they had a chalkboard sign out on the sidewalk at the beginning of the street, which is good. Our server was super nice and very attentive. She was refilling water and asking if we needed anything every time I looked up it seemed. I hope this place does well. It's only been open since New Year's.

I was extremely disappointed by this place. It came highly recommended by friends and co-workers. We went on a Saturday evening, early around 6. First thing I noticed was the number of tables around me that were not bussed. Generally, when it a busy night like Saturday, you'd expect the tables to turnover, but there were about 3 tables that were around me that weren't bussed for over 30minutes, so I had to try to enjoy My meal looking at dirty tables for the majority of it.

Ordered the Prime Filet Medallions- disappointed. The veal Demi on it was NOT good, I couldn't eat more than one bite. When I sent it back, the waiter was not pleased and basically disappeared for the rest of the trip. I had to get another server to refill my drink. My wife waited 15minutes for her wine refill.   We had the Kobe sliders and the Mac an cheese. Both were underwhelming. 

We were very disappointed given the word of mouth the place got. I've had way better food at Liberty Food & Wine Exchange & Campo, and DEFINITELY better service.

Wanted to find something new and out of the ordinary.  When you live on the Riverview Brandon line, that ain't easy.  It's the mecca of chain restaurants.  And while Thai food isn't my favorite, when I am in the mood for it, this will be my new go to spot.  Even though I got what I wanted when I asked for out of the ordinary.

When my GPS told me to take a left off 301, I was skeptical.  When I was told to take another turn onto a tiny narrow unlit street that won't allow for 2 cars to pass without one moving off to the side, I was sure the address on Yelp was wrong.  But when I got to the end of the road, a hidden redneck paradise was found.  Clearly a spot only the locals know about.  There was no parking to be found so I had to improvise a spot under a tree and keep any eye out for a tow truck.

On my right was a redneck bar doing a karaoke night.  A tiny shack about 50 feet away was Kombo Kitchen.  They've only been here for a month.  Catering to the bar crowd their menu has 2 sides... one for Thai and the other for basic American foods like burgers and hot dogs.  4 employees were crammed into this shed and they were overwhelmed with orders.

On their specials board it says, "If you don't want to wait, don't."  Problem is I already paid.  45 minutes after I put in my order for chicken pad thai, I finally got to see if this place lives up to the hype here on Yelp.  For the most part, it did.  I can't give it a 5th star... it's just not quite a 5 star experience.  It's unique though ... I'll give ya that. It's not often you can enjoy good Thai food at a redneck karaoke bar.  People drove up on their tiny cheap boats and climbed over the bank. There was a rusty old pickup truck with "I love boobs" on the back window..  You get the idea.

By the way, per their agreement with the bar, you have to order drinks at the bar.

The setting along a river though is pretty cool at night.  But just don't be in a hurry.  To their benefit, they gave me an order of vegetable egg rolls (normally $3) for my patience. (I never complained about the wait... that's what Yelp's for... they did this just to be nice.)  The Thai woman running the show was super nice.

I'll definitely be back.  But not on my lunch hour.

It's next to the Red Roof Inn. 

Not socially distancing parties at all. Hmm. I am sitting on the same side as my hubby to create some distance and luckily one end of the booth is not near another table for 6 feet. 

We ordered a spicy chicken bulgogi, cold barley (boricha) tea, tteokbokki, stone bowl bibimbap. 2 person minimum for the BBQ. 

It's chilly inside, we grabbed our jackets 

The spicy chicken skillet was sizzling on its way to us. It's quite tasty.

The spicy chicken bibimbap is also good, piping and smoking hot. The rice was getting nicely cooked and hard. Cooked the egg yolk some on the stone pot, luckily it cooked fully. 

The tteokbokki tastes good, just the rice cakes are overcooked and rather soft to me.

We were at Taylor's Bakery and were looking for some Chinese food to eat. Queue House of Cheung. I have not had really good Chinese food like I used to have as a kid in awhile. This place is so clean, so friendly and the menu reminded me of a place my parents used to take me to as a kid. 

The place is only open from4:30-9. The ladies that worked there were honestly a pleasure. We were impressed that they knew the drink orders of so many that came in and even their names. You can tell this place treats people like family. Even my kids noticed it and are sad we don't have a place like this in our town. 

The food was hot and the taste was amazing. No grease to it. And so many leftovers. 

We will be back.

We absolutely LOVE the Avenue Cafe! We bring all our friends here that come visit NOLA. It's a safe airy open and inviting cafe with great coffee, even better service, and pastries ready to be warmed up; they even have vegan samosas!!!!! The coffee is quality, hot every time. Service is fantastic, everyone who has ever served us has been friendly and genuinely happy to be there and helping you. They have lots of books around for browsing and lovely outdoor seating along historic St Charles Avenue. Also, Mardi Gras Alert - this place is RIGHT on the parade route  We came here Mardi Gras morning before Rex and had THE MOST AMAZING fresh squeezed orange juice mimosas right before the parade rolled by, it was literally perfect. Prices are fair and good too. Even during the pandemic, Avenue Cafe has been there for us! We highly recommend checking it out!

Excellent pizza. Fast delivery!

We ordered the Greek pizza. It was massive.

Very flavorful! Like eating a salad, only better. 

Will definitely be ordering again!

This place is super cute and the staff is amazing!!! Always friendly and very eager to help. I have had several flavors such as the banana split, red velvet, sweet potato, strawberry lemonade, black velvet, Jewish apple, the coma, and the vanilla. I never got a cake that was dry, but I do think some of the icing can be too sweet at times. The Jewish apple, sweet potato, and black velvet were amazing! They also have excellent scones! While they can be pricey, occasionally they have sales at the end of the night where you can get cupcakes for as low as a $1. Become friends with them on Facebook!! 

Overall excellent service and fun atmosphere! Definitely worth a try.

Saturday Sweetness

Food

Black Sesame, Matcha, Ube!? It was a little different than your typical visit to Dairy Queen, but real good.

I opted for the Matcha / Ube swirl with, Vanilla Cake, drizzled with Condensed Milk. And to top it all off, Pocky. Because I was feeling a little extra that night, I opted to get them all. Cookies and Cream, Chocolate, Strawberry, and Matcha.

Service

By chance I got the opportunity to meet one of the owners, Casey. He took the time to let my girlfriend and I ask all of our curious questions and sample every flavor available before we made our selection. 

I would reccomend this place to anyone looking for a light sweet treat.

I Guess I'll just Go Fuck Myself

It was 10:30p on a Monday night and I'd placed an order for take out. Little did I know it would be my last time ordering from one of my favorite local spots. 

My Order
Bamboo Chicken not spicy
Shrimp and Pork Fried Rice
Imperial Rolls. 

Arriving at 11:15 I picked up my order, paid, and left with no problems. Once I got home I noticed my bag was light. The Imperial Rolls were missing. Checking my receipt I noticed the order taker had failed to actually place my order for the appetizer.  

Now normally I would have just brushed it off as a simple accident and let it be. But this wasn't the first time they had forgotten at item and I was tired of this happening. I felt they needed to know about their mistake so steps could be taken to correct this type of behavior.

So I took action and made a call to the restaurant. 

I spoke with a woman claiming to be the owner. And went on to explain that she had forgotten to place my order for Imperial Rolls (I recognized her voice, and indeed she was the person who took my order)

This is where the story gets interesting...

 Instead of being apologetic or even humble about the situation she does what I believe she shouldn't have done. 

She accuses me of not placing the order at all. 
After explaining to her that I clearly remember placing the order she goes on to remind me that I wasn't charged for the order of appetizers I didn't receive. 

Now of course I'm glad I didn't pay for an item I never received but that still doesn't change the fact they made a mistake at which I now had to pay the price. 

She then gets frustrated when she comprehends that her explanation of me not paying for the rolls has failed to satisfy my call. 

She asks, "What do you want me to do?" in a tone that says she's out of options and it's now up to me to figure it out. 

Well a couple of things since she asked:

1) Apology would have been nice

2) Instead of accusing me of not ordering the Imperial rolls. They should have taken ownership of their mistake and offered compensation. 

3) Take the time to read back every order you take over the phone and don't get complacent when it comes to customer service

I've given Golden Flower my business for years. But now no more. There's plenty of other restraunts in town that ensure order accuracy and don't waste my time. 

P.S. If you're craving good Asian cuisine with the right amount of customer service I recommend a Taste of Thai and 2D Wok.

Brewery with a Buzz

Had a late night dinner here on a Friday night around 11pm.

Service
 The waitress was nice and didn't mind splitting checks when it came time too pay. She made a small mistake and forgot to bring me a side of lemon for the fish, but no big deal. 

Food
  Fish and Chips $13.49
The beer battered cod was cooked to a flakey golden brown texture. It's been been a while since I indulged in tartar sauce but it tasted creamy and had crunch with the pickled veggies. 

Drinks
  Coffee $1.75
  The coffee was served hot and they made sure to bring the side of half and half I requested. 

$3 shots of the month. Dangerously scrumptious!  Tasted just like a pink Starburst. 

Pecker Wrecker Draft Beer $5.00
  Cold beer poured to the brim that was amber in color and had a label that would make my mama roll in her grave. 

Overall Recommendation 
  Had fun checking it out. Hopefully you will too.

8:30am Monday morning I strolled into Cafe Milano for breakfast.

Atmosphere 
The interior is warmly decorated with white rose bushes, framed stock photos that look like they're from the 90s  and a Roman/Italian influence interwoven between it all. 

Bratwurst Benedict

Poached Eggs on top of a Bratwurst Bun ( aka Toasted Upside Down Hamburger Bun brushed in butter) with Dijon Hollandaise Sauce. I did not enjoy the flavor profile. The thick seasoned sausage patty combined with the sweet Hollandaise, and Dill garnish made me second guess my choice. As soon as I could get my severs attention I had it sent back. 

Southern Biscuits and Gravy

It came with Housemate Giant Buttermilk Biscuits, with Country Gravy, 2 Long Strips of Bacon and Hash Browns. A much safer bet. The bacon was crispy and the hot country gravy made for a heart warming start to the day. 

Service 

My server had great customer service. After I told Jose that I didn't care for the benedict he didn't hesitate to put my order in for the Biscuits right away. And when I inquired about their coffee selection he was knowledgeable of the available menu items.

Overall

I had a nice time at Cafe Milano. Food was at an average level but the customer service shown by Jose made the experience shine.

Authentic Delicious Cuisine

Food
  Appetizer - Kanom Jeab 

Soft little balls of meat with panko bread crumbs on top. The panko added a necessary crunch and the sweet soy sauce created a tasty marriage. The meat was marinated chicken shrimp steamed dumplings served with sweet soy dipping sauce.

  Entrée - Kang Karee Curry

You get the option of choosing your heat level when you order. 1 being the least spicy and 5 being the most spicy. I opted for a 2 and found myself self eating one spoonful after another of this savory yellow curry with potatoes, sweet potatoes, and onions.

  Desserts - Thai Taro

The dish had the consistency of a chilled slightly sweet custard with bits of nutty texture nestled in every bite. 

  Drink - Hot Ginger Tea

One sip of their ginger tea seemed to warm my soul. It had slivers of actual ginger dancing in the bottom of my cup. A welcome change from my normal green tea.

Overall Recommendation 

Visiting Bangkokville Thai was a great decision. I'd come back here in a heartbeat. 

If you're in the area and looking for a change from the abundant options of deep fried cuisine stop by for a night to remember.

I was so excited to try Crescent City. I treated a friend to dinner to celebrate her graduation, and after talking with a few locals and reading reviews, I was ready for a local, old-school steakhouse. 

No reservations were needed for a mid-week visit. We walked in and were told pick any seat available. Our severs were fine; everyone was pleasant and prompt. Their wine list is decent; my Malbec was good, and you need something that bold to cut through the richness of the butter. 

We ordered:

T-Bone - Rare
Ribeye - Well Done
Spinach Au Gratin - shared

I noticed the table next to us and they all ordered the Filet wrapped in bacon. God, they looked great. The woman closest to me cut into her steak, and it was the perfect shade of red. Then ours came.
