My steak, which looked suspiciously like a thin cut I could have purchased at Rouse's on sale, was far from rare; it was medium, and not even brown. My friend's well-done looked more like dead. I couldn't tell the difference from the charred outside or inside. The spinach au gratin was OK, definitely house-made, but using frozen spinach detracted from the cheese sauce.

I wish I could say it was an off night, but considering I could spend the same amount of money at Morton's or Ruth Chris' , it's too expensive to take another chance.

Had to try out this wonderdul, female-driven space in the CBD (Viva women enterprueneurs!). Both the interior design and the menu are spartan: just five coffee items on the menu and a few revolving pastry selections from Gracious Bakery. The staff is informative and friendly. If you tend to shiver from the meat-locker level A/C, there's compliementary shawls to use while you're enjoying your brew. 

My pourover was delicious, and kinda' sad it's not closer to home. So the question is....

Why four stars?

IF you want dairy in your coffee, as I am want to do, there's only two options: whole milk and almond milk. That's wonderful for vegans, but I want half & half for my pourover. All. The. Time.

Ruth's got a happy hour thing going. While they're not truly HAPPY hour prices, it's far less expensive than the regular menu. They do make a damn fine martini. The staff is there for you at every unspoken thought. And yet...

A crab BLT sounds great in theory, but its execution is sorely lacking. The bread is too bulky for delicate crab, and I had to lift the bread to actually see the teeny-tiny dollop of crab. This may work better as a slider.

Pepper Pot. This sticks in my mind because you went to the grocery store on vacation and saw a can soup sitting on the shelf with this name and thought, "What's that? Who would eat that?" Well, stop what you're doin', 'cause I'm about to ruin the song and the soup that you're used to.

Unless you cannot eat seafood, make sure you get this! This amazing velouté will transform your life. You won't want to share, so get a bowl for everyone.In fact, if you love seafood, this and the pristine crudo on the menu will make a divine dinner. 

The biscuits are great and I should just pull an old lady and wrap them in my purse to eat at home the next day. The cocktails compliment everything and the wines by the glass unique and delicious. The staff does exactly what you want them to do: serve you, leave you alone, and yet somehow surprise and delight simultaneously.

Looking forward to my next visit!

Finally ended up here for lunch a couple of weeks ago. Packed with a great slice of humanity, I sidled up to the counter and ordered. Had I known to plop down at the bar,  I would have gained 10 minutes of my life back and had witty repartee with the bartender.

Speaking of ten, I think that's the weight of the plate I ordered. It may be what I gained after eating here. Hearty eaters, fear not! You will leave sated!

The sides are OK; I was told the standout collard greens were sold out (by 1PM!). The meat was quite tender and the sausage were delicious; the sauces left me lacking in flavor and substance.

It was a sunny Sunday, and a perfect day to walk over and check out my new neighbor. I was the first in my group to arrive, and after observing the groups at the other tables, I turned on my heels to leave. See, I feel if you're a restaurant or bar owner and none of your patrons are smiling, laughing or giving a vibe of conviviality, then something's amiss. 

We sat down and ordered:

Signature Breakfast
Huevos Rancheros
Coffee
French Toast

The food was fine. Tiny portions and let me just say, Huevos means eggs in Spanish. Something on the plate should suggest the aforementioned item. You know what the real offense is?

Coffee. Tepid coffee. You're selling a pour over at $3 a pop and it arrives lukewarm? And no actual dairy to drink with it? No wonder no one was smiling.

Your drink list looks great. We had to ask for it. Because the table tents weren't on the tables. Sunday brunch - who wants cocktails? I do!

The servers were great and apologetic. If I were one of those servers, I'd spring for an electric tea kettle to make hot water for a proper cup of coffee. Why let poor management hurt my ability to earn tips?

Bright, airy and modern, these new girls are taking over the block! It's their first official day, so kinks are expected. And the kink was being over-serviced, so no tears :-)

My savory focaccia was fantastic! The tomato tasted better than any I've had at the farmers' market this year. Why four stars? 

This is a restaurant that happens to offer outstanding baked goods. My pastry & coffee was over $10, excluding gratuity. This means with my budget, it's a treat rather than a regular stop.

Sometimes you have to head to a tourist trap to see if the out of towners know what they're talking about. In this instance, 45% would be correct. The other 55% should keep eating at Red Lobster and delete their Yelp account.

I'm not sure why my friend and her husband wanted to eat here, but I'm going to blame it on hormones, as she's currently 8 months pregnant. From the time we sat down, I wondered why it wasn't just a bar that offered simple seafood. Why?

There's No Such Thing As GULF LOBSTER!!!!

Of course the pregnant lady ordered lobster. Over- cooked, dry, lobster stuffed w/Sysco jambalya and rice that had been re-heated by sticking it in hot water. 

Her husband ordered the prime rib, which actually was tender, and cooked well. The appetizers of calamari, onion strings, and crab fingers were either undercooked or bland. 

My oyster platter was decent: nice-sized oysters and fries twice- cooked for that extra crunch. But you can have this cheaper and better elsewhere. 

Our server was pleasant, though sitting through the attempted upsell of the $79 seafood bucket of non - Gulf seafood was more than irritating. 

If you want a something fried for a snack while you're on the Riverwalk w/out-of-town friends or family, plop down here. They'll like the scenery, and you'll know not to order anything else.

I've met people who make intelligent, even convincing arguments against immigration. (I usually don't agree with them, but I can respect some of their points.) The owner of Geno's Steaks is not one of them. The man is clearly intimidated by the throngs of excellent Mexican and Vietnamese restaurants that have otherwise been warmly welcomed into the "Italian Market" section of the city.

Here's the evidence against him: 

a) The famous sticker on the window: THIS IS AMERICA: WHEN ORDERING, SPEAK ENGLISH.

b) The t-shirt displayed in a window across the street: "I'M AN AMERICAN SO I ORDER IN ENGLISH."

Geno's owner Joseph Vento is the grandson of immigrants from Sicily, who faced their own struggles with the English language when they landed in America in the 1920s. Of course, Geno himself is too far removed from that struggle -- he, after all, is a REAL American -- to know how difficult it is for many people, especially adults, to learn a second-language.

Cute and intimate. Attentive and helpful staff. Very clean. Went for brunch today and it was PHENOMENAL. I had The Row Eggs Benedict, which were served on a biscuit instead of an English muffin and I honestly don't know why that isn't a standard practice with eggs Benedict. We started with an order of the biscuits with blackberry, strawberry, and tomato jam and their biscuits are INCREDIBLE. I loved the tomato jam- kinda sweet, kinda savoury, kinda spicy. Awesome. Tried their grits and they tasted like THE TRUTH, y'all. And they have the best fried pickles I have ever had in my entire life. Also: mimosas the size of yo head. 

It's a bit pricey, but it's not outrageous. Definitely worth it, considering how good the food was. The only reason it's 4 stars instead of 5 is because the coffee wasn't very good. 

Amazing food, though!

Updated: Order the Brussels and bacon. FOR THE LOVE OF BACON, DO IT. 

Also, their pulled pork and jalapeño corn cake is DIVINE. The pork was very tender and smoky and juicy, and the corn cake was spicy without being too spicy.

POACHED PERFECTION

Breakfast that tastes this good deserves a standing ovation.

This multi-purpose restaurant is located west of the Soulard district in St Louis, though it wins no flare points when it comes to their name.  They serve morning fare by day, and in the P.M. hours they transform into 'Spare No Rib', a taco/BBQ joint with a much more amusing moniker.

Needing something in our bellies before a Budweiser tour on 3/26/19, Nichole C picked this place off of a Yelp listing; there's no big signs so you might have a tricky time finding Egg at first.  Once we got seated, she ordered herself a latte ($4).

Our food arrived pretty quickly, all things considered.  My 'El Americano' ($8) came with 2 poached eggs, potatoes, 3 strips of thick-cut bacon, and brioche toast with butter & jam.  The eggs were spot on, the bacon cooked masterfully and the jam tasted homemade.

NC got a half order of the french toast ($5), which came swimming in berry compote and a dollop of mascarpone cheese.  She also got a chorizo breakfast tostada ($5.75) topped with a fried egg and salsa verde.  Both received rave reviews from my better half.

Bread = 5
Circuses = 4

Service was speedy, but our guy disappeared at the end while we waited for the check.  The dining room has a huge vaulted ceiling, and the decor/light fixtures inside could use a thorough dusting.  Lots of cobwebs hanging around doesn't set the ideal mood for eating (unless it's a Halloween brunch).

Being the stickler that I am for typos, I noticed a few spelling errors on their menu -- "fruit campot", "mascapone" -- which isn't a huge deal.....but a minor revision wouldn't hurt.  Just a thought  :)

* TL;DR *

The eggs are picture-worthy, the lattes beautiful and the prices fair.  Aside from a quick cleaning there's not much I'd change about Egg (okay, the name needs changing.  Whatever brilliant mind thought that one up needs a creativity enema!)

Overall I'd say this place lives up to its namesake.  Totally recommended.

SATURDAY NIGHT.....LIVE!

One of downtown Nashville's trendiest bars is a multi-level hotspot of great food & incredible live music.

Though this review is long overdue (cut me some slack, I've been busy), I visited with Nichole C on the night of 3/24/18, our first full day of spring break.  I'd heard positive things about Acme Feed & Seed from both friends and coworkers, for good reason.

We made our way up to the 2nd floor where nearly every seat was taken.  Flagging down a server was next to impossible and placing an order at the counter seemed impractical.  Eventually someone came to us, but it took a LONG time to request a couple beers and an order of sushi.

The Acme Roll ($16) was what you might consider a 'rainbow roll' elsewhere; it had avocado, yellowtail and salmon topped with black/red/green tobiko.  We also got a spicy tuna roll ($10) and a couple beers.  Everything was tasty, but expensive.

While the upper level made for some terrific people watching, it was on the ground floor that things really came alive.  After putting in an order for beer belly tacos ($12.50) and grilled Mexican street corn ($6), we found a seat at a table facing the stage.

Tacos were outstanding and came with picked daikon radish, sweet chili sauce & cilantro, served with black beans.  The "esquites" were equally incredible, rolled in cotija cheese, with lime mayo and chili powder.  From the taste and looks of things, Acme has a kick-butt kitchen.

Bread = 4.5
Circuses = 4.5

Once the band started, things got crazy!  The music was some of the best we've ever heard, and the quality of sound was unmatched.  They played some Kool & the Gang, a cover of Sia's "Chandelier", and a handful of Bob Marley tracks.  Really outstanding stuff, made our 1st night a memorable one.

* TL;DR *

Awesome vibes, great food, and a bustling crowd.  I'd definitely recommend Acme Feed & Seed for those in the Nashville area (especially large groups, bachelor or birthday parties), and I hope to return again some day in the future!

WHEN WORLDS COLLIDE

Expect an unusual combination of Italian and Greek fare at this restaurant in west St Louis.

Per the recommendation of a friend, we stopped for an early dinner on 'The Hill', an Italian-American neighborhood just south of the St Louis Zoo.  With a handful of delis, trattorias and pizzerias to pick from, Nichole C and I settled on Antonino's -- one of the highest rated and most popular business in the Saint Louie area.

Once seated on 3/25/19, they brought out bread & olive oil for us.  Thirsty as hell following a day at the zoo, I got a tall Peroni ($5.50) and my better half got a Schlafly blonde ale ($5.50), since they were out of Stella Artois.

To start, we settled on their famous toasted ravioli (6 for $10) which were served with marinara.  Described as "puffy pillows of meat", I honestly found them underwhelming.  Though crispy on the outside, the two ravioli I ate had an anemic amount of actual filling and the taste was mediocre at best, certainly not worth $1.75 each.  Bummer!

Highly touted by the staff, the toasted ravioli even got featured on the TV show Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives (which of those Antonino's falls under, I'm not entirely sure, but the more things Guy "FlavorDouche" Fieri recommends, the less I'm beginning to trust what that pointy-haired yabbo has to say.  Also, his face is very punchable.)

Nichole's gyro sandwich ($10) was outstanding; the lamb meat was juicy and the tomatoes perfectly marinated.  The warm pita was great, plus the fries that came with it were nice and thin.  My salsicca ($10) sandwich tasted pretty good.  It was a spicy italian sausage split in half, with peppers, onions, provel cheese (a cousin of provolone, perhaps?) and a balsamic drizzle.

I was stunned that for an Italian place, they didn't have giardiniera anywhere on premises, mild or otherwise.  Thankfully my sausage sammy got some major help courtesy of their homemade spicy tzadziki, which come to find out, was just regular tzadziki (cucumber yogurt sauce) with sriracha!  Gonna have to try that at home next time.

Bread = 4
Circuses = 4.5

Gabby was energetic and attentive throughout our meal.  The atmosphere inside Antonino's is perfect for a dinner with family or close friends.  Pizzas seem to be something they do very well, as nearly everyone around us ordered one.  If we had a fridge in our hotel room capable of storing leftovers, we totally would've gotten a 'za.

* TL;DR* *

Antonino's Taverna is just one of several great options on The Hill, along with Zia's, Charlie Gitto's, and a few others.  I was tempted to order a saganaki, but when I saw that they used halloumi cheese instead of the standard kasseri, kefalograviera, or kefalotyri -- not to mention they served it GRILLED -- I elected to pass.  I'll stick with the traditional kind of cheese that gets properly flambéed, thanks.

That said, I'm not 100% sold on the idea of Greek-Italian fusion, but everything was tasty enough.  The gyro was fantastic, something I'd definitely recommend.  Not bad!

THIS BUD'S FOR YOU

Crack open a cold beer in celebration of Life, Liberty, and the Pursuit of Hoppiness.

***this is part 10 in a 10-part series as I count down to my 1,000th post.  These are local legends, places of international intrigue, historic businesses, and unforgettable opportunities.  All five stars, of course.***

As I pondered over what my penultimate review should be leading up to the big 1K, I asked myself the seemingly simple question, "what do I love?"  Since I can't officially review my fiancée and I already wrote about the Chicago White Sox -- as well as their stadium -- I had to skip down the list a bit to #4.

Anheuser-Busch HQ was one of our final stops during a spring break trip to St Louis, marking the fifth time we've visited a distillery or brewery (Jack Daniels, Miller Brewing, Bacardi in Puerto Rico, Geikkekan in Japan).  Budweiser checked all the boxes for a good time, and then some.

When I visited with Nichole C on 3/26/19, we took the 'Bud Light Tour' ($10/person) which was a happy medium between their general tour (free) and Beermaster Experience ($35pp).  Included in our admissions were two small on-tour samples, a beer that was bottled earlier that day, and a 16oz draft in their biergarten.  Not bad!

Our tour guide knew her stuff and threw out plenty of interesting factoids as we traversed the grounds.  We saw the stables where the famous Clydesdale horses are kept, got an up-close look at the brew kettle process, and saw the packaging facility where Budweiser churns out millions of bottles a day.  That last part was especially rewarding, since my normal job deals with manufacturing.

After the tour concluded, we perused their gift shop which was packed with every imaginable beer-related souvenir.  There must've been at least 50 different types of drink koozies, T-shirts, hats, make-your-own 6 packs, keychains, bumper stickers, and lots more.  The selection of merch was even better than Miller Coors.

In the beer garden, we shared an order of beer-battered fried pickle chips ($6).  I got a 4 x 6oz flight of Michelob amberbock, Stella Artois, Budweiser Agave Wheat, and Shock Top for $8.  My girl enjoyed a few glasses of straight-from-the-source Michelob Ultra for $4.

All in all, the tour was an excellent way to spend a couple hours.  It was fun, informative, and most importantly VERY affordable.  The beer garden was festive and the menu looked appealing; unfortunately we had a hefty drive ahead of us and couldn't linger long.

* TL;DR *

I'm 60% German and 40% Czech, which means at any given time there's about half a pint of beer stored in my body....my blood type is 'IBU'.  If I'm being honest with myself, yeah, I've got a bit of a drinking problem.  The problem?  I keep running out of beer!  The fiancée shakes her head in disapproval of that joke, but we've all got our vices.

Support 'Murrica, support 'Murrican brewers, buy Budweiser (or if you're a lightweight collegiate co-ed, Busch Light).  Though I'm a Silver Bullet man by choice, I still grab a case of Bud from time to time, with Michelob Ultra being our household's preferred light beer.

Along with their fantastic zoo, this brewery tour is a must-visit when in St Louis.  Let's end this with one of my favorite toasts:

"Here's to a long life and a happy one. A quick death and an easy one. A good woman and an honest one. A cold pint and another one!"  Drink responsibly out there, cheers!

SMALL BATCH PERFECTION

A tiny space equates to better quality control over their fantastic dishes.

In seeking "the best" hot chicken sammy in the Nashville area, I crowd sourced opinions and Subculture was mentioned.  Though Hattie B's in midtown was the frontrunner, it was too far out of our way so these guys got the culinary nod from myself and Nichole C.

We were stunned to see this place sandwiched (hah!) in a strip mall between an H&R Block and a Babies 'R' Us.  The commercial space was tiny, about the size of a standard studio apartment.  We walked in and placed our lunch order, a pair of sammies and a few brews.  I was impressed that, for such a minuscule venue, they had quite a few beer taps.

It took a while for our food to come out to us, but then I considered that there was probably one dude in the back making all the lunchstuffs.  Our cheese empanada ($2) was the first thing to come out, and it was delicious.  Following that was NC's lunch choice and my Nashville hot chicken.

Her churrasco sandwich ($11) was very tasty and came topped with a fried egg, along with chimichurri, avocado, tomato and mayo.  She got fries for an extra $1.50, and they were pretty good.  The steak slices were cooked perfectly medium-rare and all the accompaniments paired well with the tender beef.

My hot chix sammy ($10) was heat level 3 out of 4.  I opted not to get the "stupid hot", as I knew my butthole would be whistlin' dixie afterwards.  Mine was plenty hot enough, and the coleslaw with sliced avocado helped to cool things down, so to speak.  The fried chicken breast was juicy and the sandwich was excellent overall.

Bread = 4.5
Circuses = 4

We also got an 'alfajor' ($2.50) filled with dulce de leche and coated with powdered sugar.  Pretty yummy.  There was only one bathroom on site, and it was small, though who honestly cares?

Note: a Yelp check-in gets you $1 off your choice of coffee or beer -- I chose beer, since I'm a borderline alcoholic and had *3* brewskis during lunch.  #vacationdrinking

* TL;DR *

I'm very glad we stopped at Subculture instead of Prince's, as I imagine that line would've stretched down the block (not unlike what we experienced at Biscuit Love Gulch).  This place is pretty hidden, so keep a sharp eye out when driving past!

Their sandwiches have won several local & state awards, for good reason.  If you're in the Nashville area, consider stopping here instead of the wildly popular (and I imagine, crowded-as-f*ck) Hattie B's.

Oh hell yes I'd recommend!

Yay! I am loving having another Asian food joint to hit up that is close to base. I got the lemongrass noodle saute with pork. The service was super attentive and it was obviously a family run business. I really hope this business does well! The food comes out quick, it is inexpensive, and the portions are quite large! I shared mine with my hubby.

They give 10% off for military and today they hooked me up with a drink and spring roll for the free. This is a wonderful establishment that provides personable service and quick food that is pretty tasty. I can't wait to come back and try everything else!

My favorite sushi in town.

Always great service, and even more important great fish. I usually stick to a lot of nigiri, lots of sake(salmon), and the cut on the fish is always clean. I find it really important that the fish look as beautiful as it tastes. It always tastes fresh and has a good rice to salmon ratio. 

I can't say enough good things about Hiroba and it's staff. I love coming here and leaving full and happy.

I have been referred to this establishment a number of times. Today, I finally had the opportunity to dine here. 

There is indoor/outdoor seating available. Masks are required. Menu is available by scanning the barcode on the table. There are lovely partitions in between the tables inside. This is my first indoor dining experience since last year, and I feel very comfortable and safe. 

As a pescatarian that has an appreciation for vegan food items I love this place. Ann Marie our server was phenomenal. I inquired if any food items included peanuts because my daughter has a nut allergy. There are NO peanuts in house, which put me at ease. There are vegans that may have a nut allergy that will appreciate this accommodation as well.

The lunch combos are awesome and so delicious. We even went on to order individual items after our starters. The presentation is lovely, and the food is so flavorful. I could go on, but I would suggest to just come yourself. I will definitely be returning here on a regular basis.

City House is in a charming brick building in Germantown. (Oh my god, is it ever loud in there.) I chose this place for dinner for a party of eight based on the strength of the Yelp reviews. Most of the reviewers must have had better service than we had. We were there FOREVER. The waiter dropped a dirty fork on me. Blah, blah, blah. You know what bad service is.

The starters were delicious. The house-cured salami was yummy. I wish I could have just ordered a salami sandwich. This would have been a very different review. The crispy potatoes with gorganzola were super crunchy but not dry. The crispy octopus with white beans was delicious.

For my entree, I got the something crusted catfish with the something potato puree and garlic pesto with something. The catfish was tender and moist but the crust was lacking flavor and seasoning. The potato puree on top was delicious but cold. I had the grits with pecorino as a side. The grits were also a little cold and pretty boring with just a little bit of pecorino thrown on top. All the other sides sounded unappetizing.

Actually, all of the other dinners sounded unappetizing, which is why I ordered the catfish to begin with.

Two friends ordered the belly ham pizza, which was good but too fricking spicy and was served with an optional over-easy egg in the middle. That's just weird. Two friends ordered the pumpkin pasta, which they thought was disappointing and bland. One friend ordered the chicken liver and pig liver bolognese pasta, which she liked very much. The friend who ordered the roasted chicken also enjoyed her meal. I forget what the other one ordered.

None of the desserts sounded good either but I did like the orange mint sorbetto one of my friends ordered. I didn't think the chocolate caramel cake was anything special.

Oh, I did like my cocktail. I ordered the Bandit. It contained grapefruit juice, ginger ale and some booze I can't remember.

A Bad Service Epilogue
I just found out that, even though we got separate checks and split evenly among eight cards and all signed our own receipts, one person in our party was charged the entire $400. Way to go, Daniel (the bad server). He's lucky the 18% gratuity was built in; we certainly wouldn't have tipped that much.

A Bad Service Epilogue Sequel
After five days of leaving messages with City House and not receiving a phone call from them, my friend final got a $350 refund from her bank by disputing the charge. And, I removed one star from this review. And, I added them to my boycott list.

I love this place for happy hour! I've come here quite a few times with friends, family, and my coworkers (who are both friends and family)! The prices for the cocktails, beer, wine are fantastic! The food selection for the happy hour is absolutely amazing! It's a great price and you can have a full dinner on the happy hour menu without breaking the bank. 

I told the bartenders today that I could come and order 20 orders of the whipped ricotta, it is just that good. The negronis are my favorite drink on HH and are so freshly made with perfect ratio of ingredients. All of the other seasonal cocktails and small bites are great, as well. 

Above anything else, the staff there are so nice, hospitable, and accommodating. I have been there a few times and chatted with John and have even started asking for him by name, as he is so sweet! I met Andrew today and he was so welcoming and cheerful. It's so great to meet great bartenders in a center city area that remember regulars, since it is such a busy area! I will definitely make this a regular spot to go to!

Pro tip: get freshly shucked oysters from here and eat them by the beach. There's a small shucking fee if you don't want to shuck them yourself but even with the fee, the oysters were cheaper than most restaurants. They were unbelievably fresh and sweet, not too briny. They also came on a bed of ice with lemon, cocktail sauce, and horseradish. SO GOOD, especially with the beautiful ocean view right in front.

I love my pastas, bread, and just carbs overall. This is the perfect place for all of that. Wine, pastas, seafood, and overall great food. The atmosphere of the restaurant is very nice and cozy. For the appetizers I ordered the Oysters Almondine, these were fried oysters with lemon terragon cream sauce. It was heaven. I also ordered the corn and crabmeat bisque, which was served in a bread bowl .This was so good and creamy. I ordered the Veal Parmigiana as the entree, this was also delicious, creamy, and tasty. All a perfect combination. They had plenty of options for you on the menu and they also have a large specials menu that night.

We always go to Nana's for the true tastes of Mexico. We always start with their wonderful chips and salsa.  make sure you get plenty of guacamole.

There are so many choices on the menu but I always seem to end up with the flautas which are delicious. The cheese is very high quality. I like to end my work week with a nice stiff margarita, which is perfectly crafted by the bartender. This family knows Mexican food, and they know it well. We lived there for 10 years and we recently took a trip back home.

Service is second to none.....

Great Food, Great Service, Great Value!

The food they prepare has Flavor!!!!  Nothing here is bland!

I set up a dinner here for my dining group and everything was perfect!  There were ten of us foodies feasting on:

Egg Rolls - Very yummy!
Fried Chicken Wings - They looked odd, but tasted great!

Grilled Beef Salad - Must try! So fresh, clean tasting & flavorful, ordered a second plate!

Simmered Spare Ribs - Fall off bone yumminess!

Fish in Clay Pot - Another fave of the group! Rich, spicy, sticky, sweet & melt in your mouth goodness! No one guessed it was catfish!  Most everyone thought it was salmon!

Salt Pepper Shrimp - So good!

Special Fried Rice - Very tasty!

Sweet & Sour Fish Soup - Not really a fan favorite, but good! Catfish again, but tons of little fish bones & the pineapple made it a tad much on the sweet scale

Overall, exceptional!

Man, this place is good!

I had been dying to try the fried beets...I got them...they were delicious, even more delicious than I could have even imagined!  I want them all for myself!

You can tell they use high quality ingredients, along with the chef's touch, every bite is flavorful and delicious.  Every detail is paid strict attention to.  I happened to just pop in by myself one evening, it was a bit later in the evening, but the place was packed!  I took a seat at the bar, the bartender was slammed, but he was very pleasant and managed everything the best he could.  I ordered a glass of wine, instead of a cocktail, just to help him out a bit ;-)

 While I was sitting at the bar waiting for my fried beets and enjoying a really good glass of wine, one of the chef's came out from the kitchen and offered me a taste of their broccoli soup...hands down the best broccoli soup I have ever tasted!

Two small observations...the staff bickers amongst themselves a bit too much.  Very snappy with each other, which was a bit uncomfortable to watch...I'm sure the folks that were seated in the dining room at tables would not have noticed, but sitting at the bar gave you a front row seat to the show, especially since the place is so small...which bring me to my next observation...the place it too small!!!  I love this place and have total faith that they will do extremely well, so I am hoping that they can either expand or move to a larger space at some point!  I, for sure will follow them wherever they go!  We are so lucky to have a place like this in St. Louis...I've been waiting and my prayers have been answered!

I was looking for someplace that took Sunday brunch reservations, so we landed on Adele's Nashville, a restaurant by Jonathan Waxman.

Adele's got off to a rocky start for me...  to park in the lot adjacent to the restaurant, I had to use the valet.  But the lot was empty, and the valet drove the car like two spaces down and parked it.  I would later have to wait a ridiculous amount of time for said car to be retrieved despite being able to see it from the door; it was downright comical.

In addition, we had to wait probably 5-7 minutes for the hostess to acknowledge us, because of a busy phone and them dealing with a lady with a cake or something.  We stood there for quite a while before we could be seated.  But everything was smoother after that!

Adele's looks like it's set in an old car garage, and I like it.  I like any kind of repurposed, hipster-ized building these days!  The concrete floors and metal bar stools, glass garage doors, and more... excellent.  And the dining tables and chairs were so stylish, I would put them in my own home!

The buffet had a ton of options... charcuterie, biscuits, eggs, carving station, veggies, fruits, granola, French toast... and then there was a pudding and pastry table too.  Overall, it was really good, probably competitive in my regard with the buffet at Omni's Kitchen Notes.  (In case you're curious, the buffet was $23/pp.)  The biscuits and banana pudding weren't my favorites, but the rest of the selection made up for it.  I highly recommend the eggs and the French toast, which may sound basic, but if you can nail those things as the foundation of a good brunch, the house will be great too!  (And in this case, it is.)

I thought the bar was beautiful.  Dan had a beer, and I had a pineapple juice mimosa.  I'd love to come to see what Adele's offers for cocktails and dinner, too!  Our service was great too, very attentive!

Overall, Adele's was a great place to have brunch.  The tables and restaurant give enough space to not feel crowded, the food was delicious, and it's pretty easy access for a Gulch restaurant.  I love that they allow reservations, so if I ever have houseguests I can guarantee them a good brunch somewhere vs. risking 30-90 minutes in line someplace else.

My coworker and I walked in for lunch on a weekday during the first week of this restaurant being opened.  (So take that as a caveat... it was brand new!). The building has had a full renovation since its days as Buffalo Wings & Rings.  It's very chic, modern, with tons of grey, with booths that give your group nice privacy.  There's also an event space with TV screen that will soon have a door; they said it would be tight for 40 people so probably ideal for like up to 25 I'd guess.

No issues getting seated or served quickly.  It wasn't crowded due to being newly opened, so we had constant attention from different folks refilling waters and checking in.  Our server was swift and cheerful.  Everything was fast; we were in and out in under an hour at lunchtime!  If they can keep this up once the crowds roll in, they'll do great!

I ordered the California Burger.  I ordered it medium-well, but it came more medium; that said, I didn't care!  The server was apologetic, but I was fine with it.  It was really tasty, and a large serving.  Total with tax came to almost $19, which isn't cheap, but I'd say that it was a larger portion size than other burgers/fries in the area.  I also would say this is more upscale than any gourmet burger joint, so you pay for the ambiance too.  My coworker ate the lobster roll appetizer as her meal, and it was huge too.  Good value for the amount of food at an upscale place.  I'd say comparable to J. Alexander's in terms of price, value, and feel.

I'll likely be back, most likely for happy hour and appetizers, or a business meal.  I am also interested in the private room, because those are useful in this area with lots of corporate offices.

La Vecchia is one of the best italian restaurants in the Reno area and has been for years! The entire experience is well worth it with great food options, excellent view of downtown Reno and workers that are friendly and knowledgeable about the various menu options. The fried calamari is a great starter to your meal, followed by chicken parmesan and one of the many fantastic dessert options. La Vecchia is also a great spot to grab a quick lunch if you are in the area looking. 5 STARS!!!

This was my favorite place for beignets. I know this isn't the popular choice but hear me out....

It's fried dough...I mean it can't be horrible. These beignets are just as good if not better than the place down the street. The thing that sets this place above the others is the customer service. The staff were polite and helpful. Although the line was long, it was managed well and kept people moving. 

The shop is super cute and although packed, it's comfortable. Tables are cleaned quickly and the ordering process seems more efficient to me than the grouchy folks down the way.

After tearing it up on Mt. Rose.  We headed to Eclipse in the NW searching for "A total eclipse of the heart" pizza experience and came across a cauliflower pizza crust option here as well. 

**Cue the music and sing along in your big padded leather jacket and shaggy hair #ilovethe80s

Turn around, every now and then I get a little bit lonely cause pizza wasn't in my life.  

Turn around, every now and then I get a little bit bloated from the gluten pizza in my gut.  

Turn around, every now and then I get a little bit nervous when I'm eating healthy 
And then I see the look in your eyes!

Turn around, every now and then I get a little bit terrified of my cauliflower pizza looking and tasting burnt AF.  

And there's nothing I can do
A total eclipse of my burnt cauliflower pizza crust in gut!!!

Our group decided on an Eclipse Combination and I personally wanted to try the cauliflower crust option on the Luca$h Delight from their "secret menu".  I won't make this mistake again.  

This crust is from the brand Califlour Food in Chico needs to be baked at a low temperature so it's golden brown.  It's not a dough...it's mashed cauliflower and cheese!  

Bottomline.  Next time I'll stick with the regular pizza crust they make.  Me personally I only had one slice of the regular pizza Eclipse Combo we ordered and it was very good with a spicy tomato sauce.  But due to the burnt aftertaste from the cauliflower crust I couldn't really truly enjoy it.  Burnt food does bad things to me.....

On the bright side.  The tang from the goat cheese with the pesto and toppings on the Luca$h Delight combination are quality.  Definitely would order this "secret menu" combo again but only on their regular crust.  

Once upon a time there was pizza in my life
But now there's only burnt crust that gave me gas in the dark.

Nothing else I can say
I am afraid I'm in an eclipse of a fart.

I maybe an ABC...but if I grew up as an ABCD (American Born Confused Desi) this would've been the kind of Indian influenced American comfort food that crosses over to several cuisines that I could get down on and it's smack dab right outside of downtown.  You ain't going to find this kind of fusion fare in many major cities.  So much we wanted to try but so little time so.....

The apps....Tandoori Chicken Poutine and Lamb Nachos.    It had to be done.  Purrfect to soak up the suds.  The portion on these two apps alone...just come hungry!!!!!   

The Lamb shank was shankalucious perfectly spiced and fall off the bone tender love with that onion sauce and fluffy tomato rice was quite nice.   

I need to be back here for their happy hour specials.  A reason to come back to Nashville.  Great service.  Come here and channel your Ice Cube cause "we be grubin".   Get ya grub on (We Be Grubin)

The iconic PSB is now in the BLC Downtown!  It's a beautiful thang!  Enjoy the lines and the experience.  

Normally I'm in a gravylicious mood when I think of fluffy biscuitliciousness.  Since I've had the Reggie before in the OG PDX location.  I went with the sweet and savory Chatfield.  Fried Chicken, bacon, cheddar cheese slathered in apple butter on a fluffy made to order biscuit.  

This Apple butter spilled over to my plate and I likes  that a lot.  It had a hint of cinnamon.  I wouldn't hesitate to butter anyone's biscuits with their special Apple Butter any day of the week.  There's a reason why this Apple Butter sells out like hotcakes or should I say biscuits!

With that subtle hint of cinnamon aftertaste from the Chatfield.  Why not try a piece of their popular cinnamon roll as well.  Now if they don't sell out and it's available hell yea you need this roll.  Take it to go if the button just popped on your pants from biscuit overload.   Ooopsy it happens.  Oh PSB your definitely a gut buster.  Time to pick up some loose fitting gear at the Patagonia Outlet a block away!

BAB also means punching bag?!  Well than...welcome to the Punching Bag Cafe.  BC has been a welcome addition to come across here in Downtown!  

My first time just happened to be on a monthly #meatlessmonday.  So tofu bibim-BAB it is with extra kimchi and with comes with a nice cup of miso soup.  

It was delicious.  Lots of flava and filling.  Gojuchang sauce in the self serve pump was gojutastic!!!!  Pump it up!  There's plenty here.  

The interior is modern and well thought out.  Seating arrangement is great for groups.  

If your sensitive to MSG.  Just know their kimchi, japchae and certain sauces do carry MSG.

I'll definitely back with my carnivorous eating ways next time.  There is a nice dog park across from here to work out your food coma problems with your furbabes.

I aced the Introductory Course in Taiwanese 101 in college so when we arrived I figured my personal and professional skills would get me through our experience here.  I managed to sit in the back of the classroom half asleep taking notes and never got picked on by the professor!  #winning

Here's what I learned.  Taiwanese food for dummies.  
Taiwanese food is similar to some of what we call "Chinese" in America - although many so-called Chinese dishes were invented in America and the Chinese namesakes of others don't remotely taste like the American version. 101's food is quite good!  There's a limited selection compared to many Taiwanese restaurants I've been to.

The classic night market street food Oyster Omelette was forgettable.  The only dish I would not order again.  Everything else we ordered came out great!  Braised pork with rice.  No extra charge for more mustard greens came out good.  Nice flava in ya ear!  

The service was extremely friendly and polite.  Service was relatively fast and portions are about right.  

Be back to try the boba when I'm Downtown.

We noticed the "Now Open" banner hanging off the side of the building yesterday, and decided to stop by for a quick bite.  We arrived around 4 pm.  First, this is a nice space.  The downstairs bar area is modern, classy and welcoming.  A huge ceiling fan spins in the center of  a black painted ceiling like a giant cosmic spider.  Artwork features 60s and  70s musicians - and Redd Foxx?  The facade is brick and glass, very cool. 

Upstairs, another bar, and a stage.  While we were there a band was doing sound check, not sure the name of the band - but they clearly knew how to rock.  The hostess told us that the rooftop balcony would be opening soon - when it does we can easily see how Soulshine will become the "in" spot to hang in the midtown district.

We were seated in a booth downstairs.  Another musician (keyboard) had set up downstairs and was singing the blues - very well I might add.  Our waiter was quick, friendly and efficient.  We ordered the pulled-pig nachos and two personal pizzas.  The nachos were very good - fresh ingredients, and the half order was sized right to be split as an appetizer - and they came quick. The pizzas came quick too, one was good, the other suffered from a very dry chicken topping.  About the pizza, if you have ever eaten at the Memphis Pizza Cafe, then you have eaten similar pizza.  For those who haven't - the crust is almost "biscuit" like in texture, and the toppings are fresh and liberally applied.  Overall very good - but not "traditional" NY style pizza.  I had the Milano [very good] she had the Bob Marley [good but for the overly dry chicken].

Overall, we could hardly believe that this was Soulshine's second day of business - hat's off to the management and staff (hey Aura, you guys need to send your staff over to Soulshine for some training!)   My only suggestion relates to my pet-peeve - shoddy flatware.  My fork came to me MANGLED, and hers wasn't much better. This made eating our otherwise delicious cheesecake dessert a chore. 

We will be back.

Not for Locals

In terms of atmosphere, think Cracker Barrel with beer and, really, really, really bad country music. We get the fact that the intended vibe here is "old Nashville," but this place doesn't come close to pulling it off. That being said, the tourist (complete with matching white cowboy hats) eating at the table next to us LOVED it. Yee-haw!

We tried the Cobb salad and the beef brisket plate. The Cobb salad was excellent, one of the better Cobb's in town. The smoked chicken made it special. Presentation was also excellent. Beef brisket was decidedly mediocre. Sides were above average. On food alone, we'd rate between 3 and 4 stars. 

Our waiter was new and he messed up our simple order twice. We heard him bitching about it in the kitchen. Not professional.

Value wise, we felt it was a little over priced, but we didn't feel violated.

Okay, you guys... you're right, this place is amazing. I didn't go and didn't go and thought to myself "no way it's as good as everyone says. That's a lot of hype. I don't know..." Well, I'm an idiot. This place was just fantastic. We started out with charcuterie of Smoking Goose meats, Amelia's bread, spicy whole grain mustard, and pickles. Very tasty. We also had some great cocktails with house-made sodas. Next up were medium plates of fried green tomatoes (with crab, goat cheese, and delicious sauces) and duck confit. omg. yum. Because we couldn't resist, bread pudding happened. so much yes. I'm so sad I didn't make it here sooner, everything was amazing and the atmosphere was very cool too. We were very very lucky to get a seat at the wine bar on a Friday night. Next time I hope to come on a less busy (and less rain threatening) evening and sit outside.

I've been here for breakfast, lunch, and dinner---and I know I'm gonna meet my burrito/taco craving! Forget about chipotle. This is the place to be. It's cheap, delicious, and flavorful. They make their own special hot sauces and pickles. 

For breakfast, I recommend the chicken tacos with sausage.
For lunch/dinner, my personal favorite is half chicken and half sweet potato burrito! This burrito is by far the best combo.

Also, how cute are the animated burritos and tacos on their menu board? Space is limited so try to go at off times. :)

Boy oh boy, where do we start. We were really hungry and no place was open. We found this deal on groupon for a restaurant that's 30 minutes from the Tampa International airport and we decided to give it a try. We were welcomed by Gino and his amazing staff. We asked for recommendations and his suggestions were the Plato Mexicano which was 10 out of 10. He hooked up my husband with a special enchilada which consisted of a la crema, ranchera and verde. People need to know this is real authentic Mexican food!  There is nothing like this in Tampa. But wait there is more, the sangria and margarita we're the GREATEST. They use natural ingredients and they make their own salsa. All their ingredients are fresh and authentic. Best restaurant in Tampa!!! Almost forgot, :-) the music was really good!

When a business has a great concept and the best product in the area, they are sure to succeed!  Smiling with Hope is all centered around the people with disabilities that they train and employ. It's really cool to see full inclusion operating in such a positive, functional and proactive manner. More than that, the pizza is AMAZING!  Really, this is the best pizza I've had outside of NYC. Perfectly thin, crispy, chewy, flavorful crust, tangy fresh tomato sauce and salty, gooey, and just greasy enough cheese. Add glops of ricotta and.... (Insert angels singing). Yes, it's that good!  The hubby and I shared a large and it was so good we were tempted to eat the entire pie!  Finally, a real NY pizza place in Reno!!  And a mission that's well worth supporting!  Can't wait to come back for another special splurge.

My friends and I started going here for the bobas back when the restaurant was one unit in size and mostly to-go. Bobas in Reno were scarce back then and we often resorted to -gasp- making them at home! Then this place opened and we were saved! Their sheer variety of beverages and combinations was astounding: so many permutations! I think we must have consumed a different fully-loaded, 9000 calorie beverage every day for a full semester (possibly an exaggeration...possibly.) Not only can you add boba ("bubbles" of giant tapioca for those of you who have yet to try this decadent concoction) but also a couple of custard options and other mix-in's. Additionally, you can add the upgrades to slushes, smoothies or traditional milk teas. So many choices! And when I saw that I could add boba to Thai iced tea my mind was blown. Best boba drinks in Reno, hands down, including those weirdo places that feature "bubble counters."

It seems like decades later that any of us thought to try the food. Taiwanese food is certainly different than regular Chinese food in many respects so go in ready for something new rather than with visons on Panda Express dancing in your head. Do that and you're set because anything on the menu is a win. I love the lunch combo (permutations!) and the fried bread appitizer.  Of course with a giant sugary boba.

I've never had a bad experience here and all my family and friends have long since become regulars as well. Emily has been amazing for years and remembers me no matter how long I've been away. For always being so pleasant and delicious, I award them the double-secret bonus prize of 10 stars!

I went to Cheu Noodle Bar with a friend and it was packed, especially for a Tuesday.  It was small, so we were told that the wait time would be 20 minutes and we were seated exactly in 20 minutes.  Everyone there seemed to work together and the restaurant was a well oiled machine.  I don't know if it was because we were seated at the bar, but they made everything so easy.
I really couldn't decide between the Brisket Ramen or the Coconut Curry Noodles.  Then I saw their Ramen Release.  It was the Laksa Tantanmen, so I took a risk and I'm glad I did.  It was so good that they should make it on their main menu.  It was chicken sausage, egg with wide noodles and coconut curry broth.  It was one of those dishes I would be craving long after I ate it.  Now that it is colder, I will be back, especially if they have the Laksa Tantanmen!

I used to work at a bakery, so I can look at baked goods and not really have the urge to eat them.  However, sometimes I have a sweet tooth and I saw these sugar cookies.  Sugar cookies to me are so over done during the holidays. I find myself eating them because I need that sugar fix, but mostly I don't think they taste that good.  I tried Swiss Haus sugar cookies and I have to say these are the best I have eaten.  They have such a good sugar to butter ratio.  Now I know I'm stopping here during the holidays, so I can get other people hooked on these and I can stop having bad sugar cookies during the holidays.

I lived in Philadelphia when Fergie's opened and I have fond memories of this place. I've played many rounds of Quizzo here, had many pints with friends, and even took my boss to dinner. I usually went for dishes like burgers or fish and chips, and they never disappointed.

I returned during the Eagles victory parade and I was happy to see that Fergie's hadn't changed. Still no TV's! They still had Yards on tap, one of my favorites and which is unavailable where I live. A friendly patron bought my friend and me a round (I was playing the "flew in from California" card a lot that day) and we even got a picture with Fergie himself.

We weren't hungry, but I saw some items on the menu that I don't remember from the 90's like the seitan steak sandwich and other vegetarian and vegan items. Good job, Fergie's!

Check out their website: "A traditional Irish Pub serving pub fare and local beers to satisfy any taste." If this sounds like your kind of place, then you should check out Fergie's.

I live in California and was visiting my friend who has a number of dietary restrictions. Sabrina's was recommended to her so we decided to check it out.

This was right after the Eagles victory parade (woo-hoo!) so we received a brunch menu that was special for the occasion. I loved the names of the dishes and decided on Fly Bene Fly, which consisted of poached eggs, spinach, and Hollandaise sauce on an English muffin. I got the veggie sausage with it. I chose wisely. Everything was done to perfection, and it was so hearty that I almost couldn't finish it. I'm glad I did, though, because it was delicious and because I wound up walking about eight miles that day checking out a lot of Philadelphia sites that I hadn't seen in years. I don't remember what my friend got, but she was very satisfied. I hear this place is really popular, so don't be surprised if you have to wait a while for a table.

Got a special diet? Dairy-free, gluten-free, vegetarian, vegan? Come to Sabrina's and they will hook you up. 

Almost forgot: our server was really cool, too. This was easily one of the best brunches I've had in years. I can't wait to return the next time that I visit your fair city.

Yo, Yelp spell check! I totally spelled Hollandaise correctly!

When I first heard about Stock's, I wondered if a pound cake could ever be THAT good? How could something so seemingly simple and classic taste any different than anything else I've tried?

OH, but it does. I never thought I'd enjoy this brick of a cake as much as I do. It is deliciously dense and with such a beautiful and uniform air/crumb structure that only a baker could appreciate. The pound cakes come in either classic vanilla or marble (vanilla and chocolate) flavors, with or without icing. They sell them by the brick and are priced by weight. Typically, each brick costs about $11-12 each. 

They sell many other items like babkas, pies, and decorated cakes. All of which are popular and regularly sell out quickly. So, always try to get here earlier than later. The lines are long, but move fast because people already know what they want. 

For large holiday or special orders, I'd recommend pre-ordering to guarantee they'll have what you want.

I love the fact that people are starting to recognize the history of old Miracle Mile!  This is an old motel that has been turned into gallery spaces, shops and a great cafe'!  They even have a stage for musical performances.  Went to the cafe' for Mother's Day lunch and had a yummy grilled veggie sandwich. Lots of interesting offerings on the menu including a good number of vegetarian and gluten-free items.  There is a great mix of shops including local artisans, jewelry, clothing and antiques and some upscale art galleries as well.  There's even a gourmet doggie treat shop!  I'm so happy developers are starting to see the potential of this area!  Keep Tucson history alive!

IBG overheard the drunken whispers of these chosen dudes and built Center City's seasonal (NOT Pop-up) Beer Garden. They figured that they'd add some class with cheese plates, fish tacos and something French (Trois croque monsieurs pour les hommes? Parfait!) And, just like that, a star was born. 

Sure, it's often crammed with recently minted 21 year olds looking to day load. But sometimes, that's exactly what you're looking to do, too. The bathrooms in the back are kind of sloppy, which (given the vibe) wasn't a terrible surprise, and most of the food I've tried has been pretty tasty, albeit a little lacking in flavor (minus one star). Dealing with an unexpectedly warm October evening, our initial plans of "warming up with some yummy broth" were not necessary, but we had a craving, and the only thing that could sate my buddy and I was ca-noodling at Cheu. We strolled in around 7:20 and the place was nowhere close to full. There were about 3 people at the bar and two sitting down, so we were immediately seated at the window. The inside of Cheu is warm and welcoming, the chalkboard showing off the daily specials (tea, beers, food, etc). A carafe of ice water was brought to our table, menus placed in front of us, and we were excited for a night out.

Cue when things took a turn for the questionable. I'm not sure if this is standard fare for Cheu, or just due to being a little bare bones, but we had two servers visiting our table periodically. I initially thought maybe one would just be to refresh our water, but they (a man and a woman) would follow after the other often less than a minute behind, asking the same questions. 

"Have you decided on a drink?" ..... "Can I get you ladies some drinks?"

Wait. Didn't I just tell that guy we weren't ready yet?

"Can I get that plate off the table for you yet?" (Oh, no, we're still working on it, thanks.) .... "Hey, want me to clear that plate for you, girls?"

No, we haven't even taken another bite since that lady stopped by... what is happening?

If they looked even moderately similar, I'd have felt insane deja vu that would've suggested that I, too, was insane.

As far as food goes, we enjoyed the shaved kale with dates, pepitas, and cheese curds, coconut curry (for my vegetarian pal) and classic miso ramen with pork shoulder. The curry was spicy and delicious, heavy on the broth and the heat. The more classic-style ramen was definitely jonesing for a little kick, added with chili oil and sriracha. Our duo of servers were attentive, almost to a fault. Like... interrupting us to check in, desiring seemingly bite to bite updates. That being said, the bites were quite tasty. The pork shoulder was a little tough, but otherwise all quite good. We enjoyed our cans of beer and our food, which was swept away immediately the second we finished our food. Our male server came over to let us know that, despite receiving our check, "No hurry though, take your time."

Five minutes later, the moment after we placed our card down for the check, the female server came over and, despite our earlier server letting us know "no hurry" she  told us, in no uncertain terms, that "because we have a waiting list, we need you to leave the table."

Ex-SQUEEZE ME? WHAT IS HAPPENING?!

Shocked by the sudden change in what we were supposed to do, we left, my friend just barely finishing the last of her drink.  I felt like this behavior totally ruined the experience for me, which was not going too poorly up to the point. But now, whenever I think of Cheu, I won't remember the ramen slipping through my chopsticks or the curdy kale. I will remember a rude, confusing waitress hustling me out the door as soon as we put down our tip. 

If I had the ability to take the tip back and reduce it, I would.

The first few times I visited PYT (soon after it had opened), it was interesting, but obviously a fledgling business. The menu was still in need of work, and the wait staff was hardly prepared for how popular the place had become. On a number of occasions, my table's waiter/waitress or the bartender seemed to forget about us, or there were problems with the orders we placed. Regardless, the newness & the overall concept of the restaurant made a lot of the problems forgivable.

Fast forward a couple of years, and we still see a lot of the same issues. While the menu is definitely much improved (the special burgers introduced often pique the curiosity of friends of mine who claim to be "done" with the place), the wait staff & bartenders are still in need of a lesson on how to pretend like you care. I realize the hipster vibe that PYT has grown into, but "I used to like to serve customers, back when it was underground", is not the attitude you want from the guy serving you drinks.

One particular situation that I recall was back in December of 2010. A friend & I were discussing the Krispy Kreme burger, which I had never tried, and decided we would head to Northern Liberties and get one. It was close to midnight, so we called ahead to verify that the kitchen would be open when we got there. The person who answered the phone said "get here by 12:30, we'll keep it open until then". We arrived at roughly 12:20AM, and were promptly told by the bartender that the kitchen had been closed. When we told him we had called in advance, he acknowledged that he was the one who answered the phone, but that "the kitchen is closed... maybe if you speak Spanish, you can convince the cook to open it back up". Class & professionalism to the max.

I went to PYT for the last time in January of 2011. It was mid-day, and there were only a few other people in the entire place, none of which were seated at the bar. A friend of mine was in town from Atlanta, and I thought I'd show her this neat little burger joint with an array of "different" burgers on the menu. While the Krispy Kreme burger we split (I'm not eating one of those by myself haha) was delicious, the bartender didn't seem like he wanted anything to do with us, and often had his back to us while he watched whatever movie was playing on the television. I had to continually flag him for additional drinks, which is upsetting considering we were the only customers at the bar.

A couple of weeks later, a friend of mine posted a short, but inclusive review on Google about PYT, explaining that while the food is good, the service is awful and the hipster-heavy crowd can be a bit much sometimes. Tommy Up, the owner of PYT, actually confronted my friend about the review on Twitter, angry that she wasn't singing the restaurant's praises. In a surprising customer relations strategy, he actually told her to never come to PYT again, because he didn't want "passive-aggressive customers". I'm sure Tommy's making money hand over fist with this venture, but by no means should he be treating a customer that way. It shows that the attitude of the staff at PYT comes from the top down.

I don't think I'll ever go to PYT again. I'd say I've given them enough chances.

One other observation. I've noticed any negative reviews are being commented on in a very harsh tone. Constructive criticism should be welcomed not attacked. Yelp is not for bullying.

How has it taken me this long to write about Mazzaro's Italian Market? We're here at least once a week, often more to pickup fresh bread and an easy, inexpensive lunch.

Mazzaro's is a landmark to locals, but somehow a secret otherwise. Seriously, every travel guide for St. Pete should recommend it. Mazzaro's has:

- A vast selection of fine imported cheeses. The greatest variety and quality I've seen anywhere (and we moved here from NY).

- A wine room with many imported and domestic varieties, but especially fabulous are the little-known Italian wines that are available. After last summer in Italy, I appreciate that local Italian "table wine" is cheap and amazing. Of course you can buy to take home, but they'll also provide glasses and uncork for you. The husband and I have been known to come in for a focaccia and afternoon drink on their outdoor patio...

- An outdoor patio where you can sit to eat/drink any of their wares. Not air conditioned, but they have huge fans running, and complimentary ice water available.

- An indoor bar; that's bar in the Italian sense, where you order espresso drinks and sit quickly to sip and have a pastry.

- homemade gelato

- a bakery, baking fresh breads with traditional Italian recipes EVERY DAY. And it's inexpensive! Get a Tuscan miche, you won't be disappointed. Actually, get anything and you won't be disappointed. It's all so fresh and so good. They sell honey wheat loaves, french and italian baguettes, sourdough, ciabatta, dinner rolls, focaccia, and homemade pizza. This is not the round kind of pizza Americans would typically expect, it's made on a sheet tray, but it's common in Italy, and vey quick and portable for lunch. The bakery also makes fresh pastries, cakes, cookies, and so much more. I would highly recommend to everyone who goes to Mazzaro's to try their biscotti. It is the best I have had EVER. In the world. It is the perfect texture, not too sweet, and comes in many varieties. My favorite is the Anise biscotti, though I understand it's an acquired taste. The biscotti is dairy-free (rejoice!) for any lactose-intolerant friends. And there is one Gluten-Free item, a chocolate... bomb? Chocolate thing. It's all chocolate. I remember it being great, just not what it's called. Canoli's are delicious, lots of cinnamon in the pastry shell, though not freshly filled. My husband has ordered a few of their non-Italian items, cupcakes, scones. All have been edible, but I give you this advice- you're in an ITALIAN market. They're good at what they know, stick to the specialties.

- a deli and fresh pasta counter, where you can get as little or as much fine sliced meat as you like, and fresh homemade pastas in many varieties.

- a sandwich counter, where you can order one of their menu staples, a daily special panini or soup, or some by the pound house-made salads and prepared foods. For those in a hurry there is also a fridge here with packaged selections. The sandwiches are always so fresh, stuffed full, and a fabulous value for lunch or an early dinner ($5 for Italian Turkey sub? Yes please.) They are also very patient with my "customizations" ie. adding extra Italian Slaw to ALL THINGS.

- a fresh produce area, stocked full of all the staples and then some. Prices are competitive, and it is totally feasible to do your regular shop here.

- a coffee bar where you can pour your own freshly brewed java to go, or pickup some of their roasted beans in many flavors and varieties.

- a grocery/market area, full of many specialty items, as well as stocking the standards, and some small italian appliances like Bialetti coffee pots and their replacement parts. Highly recommended: Buy your olive oil here. Mazzaro's has a special house blend that is incredibly delicious and affordable. We had a chance to speak with the merchant who sources it and they worked for a while to get the right flavor. It is an amazing value, and the best tasting oil I've purchased in the states.

- a Meat and fish counter that stocks an impressive selection, with knowledgeable butchers.


Notice a trend of the words "fresh" "homemade" and "specialty"? Mazzaro's is doing it right across the board by stocking high quality products, and using those to prepare spectacular food in house, from scratch, using traditional recipes and methods.


Mazzaro's is NOT A RESTAURANT. The other day I was having lunch, a lady and her friend walk up to the bar and ask "is this where I order?" The barista said he could offer espresso drinks and they could sit there to eat/drink anything from the store, but sandwiches had to be ordered and picked up at the sandwich counter. The woman scowled rudely and walked away. ??? The place packs a lot in, but it is easily laid out and by no means a warehouse. The sandwich counter is maybe 20 ft. from the bar. Maybe she was expecting a full service, sit down meal? It's not complicated- pickup your stuff and ENJOY. Mazzaro's is the greatest.

Great menu, excellent service, great ambiance and excellent Craft Cocktails and Brews. The SB location is always packed and for good reason. I like their other locations (Westlake) as well. Upon entry I was blown away at the decor and vibe. Very modern and super clean. the food vendors are located along the side of the space and a bar located right bang in the middle of the space. The seating is beautiful with marble counter tops and gold chairs! Absolutely stunning. In addition to the great space, there are waiters/servers that pick up your plates and serve you water.(nice touch). 

The food vendors include but are not limited too a :
- Sushi type place that serves poke bowls and sashimi. ( Called "Aloha Lei)
- A sandwich and salad place
- A Mexican style place that serves the most delicious Empanadas! ( Empanola)
- A seafood place that serves fresh seafood (Elysian Seafood)
- A Greek place that serves small plates of humus and pita, etc (Alpha)
- A dessert place that serves delicious macaroons and icecream ( Mac & Moon) 
- A coffee bar - Coast Roast Coffee
- A "create your own" salad type of place

Not too strong. 

The market impressed me so much that I took my hubby there the same evening ( Friday evening). I tried the spicy tuna Poke Bowl ( without fruit) and he has the empanada taster plate. This consisted of 3 empanadas of your choice. The empanadas are freshly made so we waited about 15 minutes for it to come out. 

The poke bowl was fresh and tasted amazing! The spice on there was just enough for me and the owner made it specially spicy for me as they didn't have a spicy tuna on the menu. What a GREAT guy! 

The Empanadas - OMG! I still have dreams about them. If you go please try the spinach and artichoke one. Absolutely amazing. 

The trading hours of the market is :
Sun - Thur : 7am - 10pm
Fri-Sat : 7am - 11pm

Lets talk about dessert. I chose 5 macaroons (cookies and cream, pistachio, red velvet, cream brullee and smores flavor). Lets just say...... DELICIOUS!!! 

Do yourself a huge favor and make a turn here to try the delicious food and drinks.

In my previous review I mentioned that I had the pulled pork, bbq sauce-topped hot dog, which was really good.  Both of these blew that away.  

I really can't wait to bring friends here.  It isn't often that I get excited to try something new every time I go somewhere.  Normally I find one or two things I like and stick with it.  Not here.  The selection is so good that I want to try something new each time I visit.  I would eat the menus if they put cheese on them.

Go here.  Now.

Classiest place in Reno. I ate at the bar with family, what a bar! Loved the ambiance, polite and knowledgeable staff. My brother is a NYC man, likes the finer things and he approved of this place - it was up to his standards, it was the wow factor for Reno.The appetizers  we ornate, beautifully displayed and did I mention delicious? I will defiantly go back for lunch or dinner. It is a place to bring family, classy friends, and a date if you do that thing.

I was in town for the Reach 2016 convention and my friend suggested that we try this Indian restaurant. This place was amazing!!! If you can go, then GO! Mr. Curry's was one of my favorite parts about visiting St.Louis! This place is so authentic and fresh, everything was so delicious. It's a buffet style so you could taste so many different combinations of things. Usually I like to over eat, but this place was so delicious that I was satisfied with the ONE plate I had! Of course I kept going back for the ultra smooth mango drink though! The price of a meal here is amazing, especially when you taste the quality of the food!

Sadly, Memphis is the new Atlantis. Until the flood waters recede, you can cruise in to St. Louis for your BBQ. In contrasting Bogart's (the upstart challenger) to Pappy's (the proven champion) I have two practical reasons for leaning toward Bogart's. First, I was pleasantly surprised that in response to my questions about choices for Gluten-free Girl, I was handed a menu of gluten-free choices, given a verbal explanation by a member of staff, and offered a photocopy to take home. According to the menu, if you avoid the smokey au jus, then ALL the meats are gluten free. At Pappy's, I could get that assurance only about the beef brisket. A second reason for leaning toward Bogart's is its convenient location for those who live on the Illinois side of the River.  It's just north of the confluence of I-44 and I-55, one exit south of the Poplar Street Bridge, an easy exit off and entry on the highway by Soulard Market, made even easier with GPS.  Pappy's midtown location means I have to be a little more determined to get there when it's not really on the way to my destination. Bogart's is not only on the way to places I go, but also tantalizingly close to the east side; I might be tempted to daytrip for the sole purpose of satisfying my inner carnivore.

In 3rd grade, I learned to count to 10 in Spanish, so I know a LOT about Mexican food ... JUST JOKING, trying to get a rise out of my amiga Tracey W. On to the review ....

Visited on a Monday night, encouraged by the review of another friend Chris Z., who said that the "new building" is open, thus assuring Madonna's younger classmate HIPster Girl that she would NOT have to sit outside on a cool March evening. As it turned out, there's still work going on for a new dining area (with the faint smell of varnish, worth the price of progress, I think). Still, the smallish dining area near the kitchen had maybe eight or nine tables for two, lots of window stools, and was only about 1/3 full, so we were just fine, there was plenty of indoor seating.

After determining that the nacho chips are NOT gluten-free (yes, some corn chips actually contain wheat flour or derivatives, or are cooked in non-dedicated fryers), we decided on three tacos each, with a side of guacamole and diet cokes. As it turned out, this was a pretty good introduction to NLV. I ordered "tongue," "beef," and, after asking the friendly server for her favorite, "al pastor" (of course!). "With cilantro?" she asked. "Yes, please." Out they came, served flat on TWO soft corn shells, so you squeeze your lime wedge over the meat, and divide between the two shells, resulting in DOUBLE TACOS. Tracey W., that's "dos" tacos for the price of "uno"! Tongue was smooth and tender with a good flavor - I recommend. Beef was standard, good. "al pastor" was very good - I DOS recommend.

There's a couple of sauce bottles on each table, "red" and "green." "Red" had a medium heat value, and was sort of smoky. We were told "green" was hot, but I thought it was pretty mild, like a mild cilantro sauce. Therese H., aka HIPster Girl, disagrees. She says the heat sneaks up on you in the aftertaste. 

*Parking? Suburbanites, take heart. In addition to street parking, you'll find a metered lot a few steps east and north, about 25 cents for 20 minutes, I think. 
*Do they take charge cards? YES! But I left a cash tip. Do any of you ever write "cash" in the tip line on the charge tape, like me? It's like I want to be given credit by the manager if someone pockets the tip without sharing. 
*Finally, WHAT A DEAL! Tacos $1.99 each, Diet Coke about the same. You can do the math. Left full, not stuffed, a good value. On to dessert ...

It's been a while since a first-time experience at a relatively local place impressed me this much. I could say it was the live music on the patio and/or the cocktails, and I enjoyed these very much. But really, I was most surprised by the good food.  I ordered the "Mixed Grill," which sounds commonplace and simple. Yet, each of three meats was excellent: Code 3 grilled chicken breast, IPA brisket, smoked St. Louis ribs. In such situations, typically I'll find one meat I like most, but this time I can honestly say I'd eat any one of them as part of an entrée and not be disappointed that the other two were missing. It takes a lot of skill and attention to prepare meat this outstanding, especially at the same time other dishes are coming out, so I applaud the grillmaster, whoever she or he may be. Good food, good drinks. Thanks Old Herald, our group of eight had a very good time.

This is my second time at this restaurant 
First time we had scallops and were done perfectly and the risotto and green sauce was amazing 
This time the scallops were not done good and the risotto was without flavor (just boiled rice) and the green sauce was so bitter (too much vinegar)
So disappointed for not being consistent

Over before it ever began. First off, let me start by saying that my boyfriend and I were very excited to try this place because we saw poutine was on the menu. We also thought were going to a restaurant. So you walk in and are awkwardly "greeted" but more like bombarded with a "bouncer" of sorts asking for ID. My boyfriend made a silly joke about our IDs being freshly out the bootlegged or something like that and we both laughed and proceeded to show ID. The guy said why would you say that as soon as you walk in.. my boyfriend clarified, hey man, it was just a corny joke here are our IDs and tried to hand it to him. The "bouncer" said no you guys are done here, refused to check our IDs to see whether they were real or fresh out the bootleg machine. He told us to leave. And so we stepped outside, called and asked for a manager to come to the door to talk to us about our experience. We stepped back in and he said.. I told you guys to leave. I told him we're waiting for a manager so relax. He went over to the bar and "talked to the manager" & returned to say he said we have to go. We refused to leave without talking to the manager on duty. So he went back to the bar and talked to someone else who then came to talk to us. This person said there was no manager on duty but he could help us. We described to him our experience and he said "oh well, it's a legal thing. If someone says they have a fake ID the guy has a right to check it and refuse entry". My boyfriend explained again that our IDs were never even checked. We just were told to leave. He said "oh well you know this guy has to deal with so much surely you guys can cut him some slack". Ha! I know nothing of the sort. I do know he's being paid to do a job and if that job isnt for him maybe he ought to seek employment elsewhere, but I know as a customer it's not my duty to cut anyone slack after they were EXTREMELY rude. He tried to turned things around finally after going back and forth with us and said lets have him check your IDs (which he should've done from the inception) and we'll get you a round on the house and put this behind us. Now had he said this from the beginning MAYBE we'd consider it. I said that's not enough I'd like an apology because he was out of line and we feel discriminated against based on our race. The "bouncer" who was directly behind us laughed . The bartender said well i cant make him do that the offer is the best i can do. (Important to note he never even asked the "bouncer" to apologize since he was "acting manager you'd think that was the least he could do). 
I looked around at everyone who so just happened to be white and i walked out. Better training is needed to handle customer complaints especially when a customer feels they are being treated unfairly and it's motivated by their race. If you're of African decent or just non white you can probably understand why this felt disgusting to us and racially motivated. Racism isn't always this very overt exchange of words. It's just the little things sometimes. Never going to this establishment and would not recommend it to a soul.

In Nashville there are a lot of food options. 95% of the food in Nashville is southern style cooking. Very delicious food but very unhealthy. If you are like me, you can only take a few days of eating this kind of food then you need a change. Urban cookout is one of the only fast casual healthy eateries in Nashville. I was very impressed with there menu and gluten free options. Everything seemed to be made or as much as they could was made in house. 

Food. The food is healthy almost everything on the menu is around $10. I have eaten 2 items here. The grilled veggie wrap and the turkey panini with fruit. The veggie wrap was very good for a fast casual place. The turkey panini was also very good. We sat outside and you could see people walking and biking up and down the street. Vanderbilt university is with in walking distance. I noticed a lot of younger people out and about. Urban cookout does offer beer. I can't remember if they have imported beers but I know they have beer from local craft brewery's on tap. Beer in a fast casual resturant... Umm yes! You heard right ! 

The service. was fantastic for fast casual. How the ordering works. You order what kind of food you want. Then you seat your self anywhere inside or outside. Seating is first come first serve.
