One of the Urban cookout staff makes your food and brings it to your table. When you are done. You can leave your plate at the table. 
I recommend saving room for desert. Lea makes the deserts herself and they are very good. 

Overall. The urban cookout is a nice addition to Nashville. It's healthy fast casual. I would recommend coming here and trying urban cookout. I will be back next time I'm in Nashville.

Dropped by on a Friday evening following a thirst-inducing round of bowling.

Found the place packed, not just with people, but many folks accompanied by their pets. There were families, couples and groups and  they all found their own type of fun.

For some it was sitting with others and sipping beers. Corn hole had fans competing in some lively matches and some of the younger set were happily engaged in electronic games.

There are plenty of choices of beverages among the beers, ciders and even wines served here. And a food truck parked just outside the entrance made it easy to order and eat without having to go elsewhere.

This is by far the largest craft beer facility I have found locally. That enables it to provide a lot of seating options and display some very large artworks on the walls.

The spacious space is good for the crowds who are here for the beer but the open area makes for some not-so-ideal acoustics. There was a musician gamely playing the night we were there and we enjoyed the playlist he performed but had a tough time hearing him sing and play guitar.

Looking forward to checking out some of the other activities that occur here and having a chance to check out some more of their outstanding beers.

Let me start by saying I'm only giving two stars here because I've eaten here before and it's been good. Let me start by giving the background info. 5:30 pm Monday night, it's pretty dead and we like it here so we brought our two year old with us. She's good at restaurants. 

Our server started out with such an attitude I wanted to get up and leave before our paper menus were handed to us.  He continued to be so stone cold that I regretted coming here. In fact he ruined my meal by making me feel uncomfortable and he didn't say much.

We ordered their $16 burger and $15 meatball pizza. Both have been great in the past.  Tonight the burger was awful.  No flavor not even the cheese.  The pizza was soggy with cold meatballs. Yuck yuck yuck. 

I totally regret coming here and won't be back in the future. I could have gotten a better meal at Toni Roni s and chances are they'd have less snotty service. I ll let my friends know too about this bad experience.

Rrrrressstaurant Revvvolucion! I could barely contain my excitement when we were able to get a reservation at this fancy spot. Bring on the brunch! First things first, wear your nice clothes my fine ladies. This is a no jeans, no flip flops, no tanks kind of place. There are ladies dressed up here like its Sunday church in the 50s so you'd feel silly in your NoLa street garb. There were hats, people. Big hats. And it wasn't the derby. 

You'll be treated to some live music as you peruse the menu -- mostly jazz but some contemporary tunes too. And when the whole restaurant breaks into song along with Let's Stay Together (including those ladies) it will totally make your morning.  We ordered lots of dishes -- each of us trying something different. The Death by Gumbo, Fire Roasted Oysters, the Lobster Gnocchi, Shrimp & Grits, Crab Beignets, Duck Confit & Beef Debris & Coq Au Vin. 

Standouts? Gnocchi, Shrimp & Grits, Crab Beignets. Skip Outs? Duck Confit, Beef Debris and Coq Au Vin. For some reason, those three were just kind of lackluster. The Gnocchi though. That I would go back for in a heartbeat. Rich, creamy, delicious, big pieces of lobster and gnocchi that were more like soft dumplings of love. 

They had some good cocktails to accompany our meal (their spring sparklers!) and the service was impeccable (of course.) Other than those miss dishes, it twas a beautiful brunch and one that I'd recommend to anyone looking for people looking to ditch beads and Bourbon for something legitimately memorable.

Could not be happier that this place is right down the road from us. We have been here at least half a dozen times and the food is always spot on and quick. The chips and salsa are a great start to the meal and the salsa has a bit of a kick but not too much.The service has been great in the restaurant and the bar and they have great TVs in the bar if it is the game you want to watch. I can't speak on the beer selection but I have had the margarita a few times and it is delicious.

Previous experiences with Ming's have been positive.  Ordered take out for three tonight, and the food was tasteless.  The dumplings were good, but everything else was devoid of flavor.  I was very excited to enjoy the Ming's of the past, but was ultimately disappointed with this evening's experience.  The food packaging and temperature, for our short trip home, was more than sufficient.  I just wish the flavor had been as good!

So one star isn't even how bad this place really is. I keep trying and they keep getting worse. Root beer I ordered taste like shit, fires , cold, milk shake melted like water, and 20 minutes in the drive through. So do as you please but this place sucks I give it one year before the doors close if they can't figure fast food out 


So I will say this don't come here at 5 or 6 pm you may die before you get anything 


Okay back again are you fucking kidding me this girl has been picking her hair for the last 15 mins. I will be sharing this with your corporate office get your act together wtf people

I think it has been 10 years since I've visited this restaurant. We tried it one time after our favorite Simply Thai on Bloomingdale closed. I remember the coconut ice cream with lychee fruit was very good but I didn't remember anything else. All I know is that mom thought her sweet and sour dish was just okay so we never went back. Jasmine Thai had also been closed for renovations when I tried to revisit a second time. It was all bad timing on my part. I just had to go back for my first review of 2022 and try it again as it seems to be a local favorite in that area of Brandon and the most recent reviews all look promising. The other reviews with the low ratings seem to be more about the Pad Thai which I wouldn't order anyway. I love peanuts but not in my stir fry or noodle dishes. I had Pad Thai once or twice and I'm pretty sure I don't like it.

So, I placed a takeout order over the phone and had one very important request. I asked her, "Please, please make the Thai basil spicy Thai hot for my husband, and don't give him the Americanized version or he will be very disappointed." Well, they totally delivered because he was so happy with his Thai basil with pork. So much so that he said, "Why haven't you told me about this place?" This is a guy who loves it when he breaks out in a sweat because the food is spicy hot, and has enjoyed eating spicy peppers all his life. His dad used to grow hot peppers and they would eat them off the vine. Yeah, I don't get it... but he loves it. Also, it wasn't just about the spice for him. It also has to have a good taste and it obviously did.

My pineapple curry with crispy duck was good. I've had better curry at other Thai restaurants in the area, but I appreciated that there was a good quantity of pineapple and protein. The duck was also crispy which was great. What I missed was the fresh Thai basil in the curry. It was just missing that one ingredient, and I do love that basil. I also may need to order it with a medium spice level next time. I forgot to do that. The spice level was very mild but the curry  and coconut flavors were there. 

The Thai spring roll was very good. We both agreed that the wrapping was chewy and not crispy. Maybe it's the wrap that they use. The ground pork and shrimp inside was wonderful. It had a little bit of a smoky taste as well. The fried banana coins were very yummy. This is on their dessert menu. I loved the honey sesame seed sauce. It almost tasted like there was a little wine in it but I think it was just the type of honey. It went so well with the crunchy banana bites. I would totally get this again. Which means we have to go back but next time we need to dine in. 

The décor is so beautiful and bright. I think it would be a great dine in experience. I immediately noticed that the service was wonderful. Also I love that the hostess was wearing traditional Thai clothing. She looked so beautiful and elegant. There were other diners in the restaurant when I was picking up my order, and the fact that it was busy didn't seem to faze her. She handled everything professionally, and even went back to get more spices for me because I was a little concerned that my husband's dish wouldn't be hot enough. This is not a concern anymore. I see more visits in the future, and I won't wait another 10 years to go back.

I've been wanting to try this place but never got around to doing it. My first impression (atmosphere and cleanliness) wasn't the greatest. I know you should never judge a book by it's cover, but it's just difficult to overlook sometimes. There was this running waterfall feature that has seen better days. It's not attractive and it's the first thing you see when you walk into the restaurant. That's another thing. No one really sees you come into the restaurant because the takeout counter is on the other side of this water feature. I think they should just get rid of it.

Anyway, I looked at the menu and noticed that the pho is separated into Southern and Northern style. Apparently there is a difference. I ended up getting the Southern Style pork and shrimp pho. I also got the wonton wrapped shrimp as an appetizer. It was all prepared in a good amount of time. I didn't have to wait too long. I was actually quite impressed with the takeout plastic bowls for the pho. The disposable bowls were very large and I didn't even need to move the contents over to another bowl. All I had to do was pour the chicken bone broth into the bowl. It had bean sprouts, lime, sliced jalapeno peppers, Thai basil, green onions, cilantro, lots of thin slices of pork, and about 4 shrimp. This was much meatier than any other pho I've had in the past. The broth was very mild and still very hot when I poured it into the bowl. My mother mentioned that one bowl was enough for 2 people. She was right. It was very good, but I'll have to try the Northern style pho one day just to compare the two. We also liked the wonton wrapped shrimp. I will go back to try other items.

Where have you been all my life? I've read about it and read many wonderful reviews, but you don't really know how wonderful it is until you go there for the first time. This place is amazing, and full of all kinds of unique items. Every aisle had something of interest. So much so that I wish I had bought more items. I already regret not buying the chocolate croissants in the frozen food section. But I did find a lot of things that I'm already crazy about. 

I found some great spices, crackers, strawberry yogurt covered pretzels (which are teeny tiny by the way), Italian Bomba hot pepper sauce (calabrian peppers), and Everything but the Bagel nut duo with almond & cashews. I also got the orange chicken from the frozen food section. I haven't tried it yet but I hear it's totally worth the hype. The prices are good too. The employees are so friendly and eager to help you. I mean really nice people. They all seem happy to be there. You can tell that they love the products because they know everything about them. 

The minute you walk in you are treated to a colorful display of fresh flowers. It even makes you forget all about the the small parking lot. Which I have to say was not a big deal in my opinion. I found parking right away under a tree in the back of the lot. No complaints from me. The store itself is very organized and they give you lots of eye candy on the top shelves as you're strolling through the frozen food section. So many things caught my eye. I was lucky to walk out with a purchase under $50. I could have made a bigger dent for sure. In a way, I'm happy we don't have a Trader Joe's in Brandon because I'd be there every day. 

I will most definitely be returning for more yummy items. I didn't really get a chance to look at everything. I think I was more in a dazed & confused state of mind that day. My shopping companion was showing me the Trader Joe's Kibbeh which looked a lot like the Dominican kipe (quipe). Why didn't I get it? I saw many unique cheese combinations, and fresh fruits and veggies. I don't know why I didn't buy any of the cheese or the kibbeh. They have a huge wine and beverage section. I need to spend more time in this store, and I'm so looking forward to it. Just go when you have a lot of time to peruse the aisles. It's worth the drive.

It has been a while since I have been back to Sunflower cafe. I can't remember why I haven't been back, and it may be because there have been so many new restaurants popping up all over the area that I wanted to try. I recently visited twice within the past 3 days. Now I remember why I liked it so much. The service and generous portions are what I remember the most. 

Many of their menu items come with 2 sides. It's always more than I can eat in one sitting. The hibachi items, fried rice, and yum yum sauce have always been great choices. Mom loves their sweet & sour chicken, and that is what she ordered this past Friday at dinner time. The yum yum sauce was included with the fried rice (without even asking for it). I was looking for the tonkotsu ramen that a Yelp friend had recommended to me recently. I didn't see it on the menu but decided to try the tempura udon noodle soup instead. I'm glad I did. I've never had wheat noodles in this type of broth before and now I understand why people like it so much. It really does soak up the flavor of the broth. It was tasty, and the portion was huge. Did you see the size of the spoon they gave me? I've never had a spoon that size. Anyway, you'd think that the bowl of noodle soup would be enough. Nope, they also give you a plate of tempura shrimp and veggies as well as two extra sides. I'm not joking. I got the steamed veggies and salad with ginger dressing (trying to make healthy choices). LOL! 

After the whole meal, I asked the server about the ramen. She said it's normally served at lunch but that it can be requested for lunch or dinner. I guess it's kind of a secret menu item or something. I was curious so I placed a takeout order today for lunch. It was another generous portion. The noodles and broth filled up a large white bowl. A bigger portion than other recently opened restaurants that have ramen in their name. It wasn't as fancy because it didn't have the mushrooms, seasoned egg, and black garlic oil. With that said, the pork broth was still creamy and tasty. Thanks Lisa for the recommendation! There was a difference in toppings which made it unique to Sunflower Cafe. It had sweet corn, fish cakes, and these little fried onions that added a crunch to it. It had lots of great flavors. I definitely would order it again. It's not the best I have ever had, but it's still a very good contender. They need to put it on the menu. I'd also like to one day see a vegetable option with sweet potato or kale noodles. That would be awesome! 

I won't wait to come back this time. It's also a place where the staff remembers you. I hadn't been back since 2016. They still remembered  me and that I love the yum yum sauce. How great is that?

I've only had Vietnamese food from 2 other restaurants in this area. So, I'm definitely no expert. All I can say is that everything I ordered was very good. I was even offered water while I was waiting. The takeout service was fantastic. There wasn't much of a wait at around 4:30 on a weekday. 

I ordered the grilled shrimp rolls as an appetizer, and 2 small bowls of shrimp pho (#23a). It was difficult to decide because they have so many different topping combinations. I picked the shrimp pho because they offer it in 4 different sizes. They have combos with lobster, seafood, scallops, mussels, and even filet mignon. They are pricier but are also larger servings (medium and large bowls). The small bowl was more than enough for me. It was so filling. So much so, that I'll probably just get the baby pho next time. Yes, there will be a next time. I thought the broth was pretty awesome. It was good to the last drop, and I totally mean it when I say that. It was so comforting. I know others have said it's not salty, but it is. It's not detectable in the taste, but I definitely felt it later that evening. I'd still order it again in a heartbeat. The flavor had a good balance of savory and sweet. More savory than sweet. Loved it! The Thai basil and other veggies were super fresh. I love that they gave me lots of basil and cilantro. 

I must admit that I was a little disappointed when I saw the shrimp roll appetizer. I thought I was ordering the crispy shrimp rolls, but they were the ones wrapped in rice paper. I have never met a fresh spring roll that I liked, and that's what it looked like to me. You know what I'm talking about? The ones served with that thick peanut sauce at other restaurants. Well, this was like no roll I've ever tasted. It had grilled shrimp in it which gave it so much flavor. You could actually see the chargrill marks on the shrimp. I didn't even need to dip it into the sauce that they gave me, which was also very yummy. This one wasn't a peanut sauce. They also make these rolls with chicken, beef, and pork. This was a unique treat that I will continue to get in the future. I can't wait to try more menu items, and definitely other pho combinations. Looking forward to my next visit.

What an amazing experience! I don't think I have anything negative to say about it. It was my first experience with Izakaya style food. I've had Spanish Tapas before in Barcelona, but never had Japanese Tapas. It was a real treat! I'm still thinking about all the yummy things that we ordered for lunch. The menu is full of appetizers, small plates, sushi, sashimi, ramen & udon, rice, grilled fish, meats, and veggies. You can even have a low carb feast here as they have so many skewer options. They have all kinds of unique snacks. Things that I would only imagine seeing in places like NYC. It really does have that whole Japanese pub feel about it. Very comfortable and unpretentious. The service from Joy and other staff there made it even better. Joy had awesome recommendations for us starting with the spicy octopus cups and the strawberry nigori sake. Her description of it sounded perfect and she was right on target. Definitely get the Homare strawberry nigori if you like that hint of sake mixed with a strawberry smoothie taste and feel. I shared the bottle because it would have been too much alcohol for me (yeah I'm a lightweight), and my friend also loved it too. They offered to give us 2 sake glasses without even asking. Great service!!

Anyway, it was so difficult to decide. The menu is extensive and there are just so many things that I wanted to try. I ended up getting the spicy octopus cup. It was exactly what I wanted. I normally get the scallop but the octopus was perfect. I also got the fried oysters after others raved about it in the reviews. They were so right. The oyster tasted so light and fresh. The panko coating was super light and crispy. I was also blown away by the eel skewer. The eel was so tasty and meaty. I'm used to having very thin slices on top of a sushi roll. This eel was thicker and had some fat on it. I loved the sweet eel sauce coating as well. You will want another skewer so you may want to order 2 of them.

I did get the tonkotsu ramen lunch special that comes with a salad. I probably didn't need it but I couldn't pass it up. The ginger dressing was very good, and the salad was cool and fresh. The ramen was excellent overall. I know some places have a better presentation, but not all of them have a perfectly marinated egg. This egg was delicious! The yolk had that custard consistency and that salty umami taste was present as well. That's what really made the ramen stand out to me. Oh and that huge slice of braised pork belly was seriously calling my name. It was a fattier piece of pork belly than I'm used to. I won't lie, there were times I was just chewing on fat but it really was full of flavor. The broth was your average tonkotsu broth that I love. I've only had it at 4 other restaurants. I can say that the broth on this day wasn't as salty as others I've had in the area. I tasted more of the pork which I'm happy with. I only wish that it had black garlic oil added to it. That would have put it over the top for me. The noodle to broth ratio was good. In fact, I didn't eat all of the noodles because I had to try my friend's appetizers. Yes, that was my excuse for not eating all of it.

I sampled the Lollipop Roll which is your typical Naruto roll, but it was presented beautifully with lollipop sticks. The Passionate Salmon Roll was excellent. I love salmon but never thought to pair it with passion fruit pulp. It was very refreshing and light. Oh, and I sampled the bacon wrapped scallop. That was also good as well. It was all perfect including the atmosphere. Just a chill and relaxing place where you can unwind during lunch or at the end of the day. I got NYC vibes there, but that may be just because I saw a couple of people wearing Yankees caps and the décor on the walls and the bar area reminded me of the city that doesn't sleep. 

So, parking is kind of weird. There isn't much of it around. It's really typical of South Tampa restaurants not to have a lot of space for that. They do have a parking area around back which is for all the businesses in that plaza. I haven't been there during peak times but I was able to find a spot around back. I can't wait to go back and try the Shiso Rangoon, Seafood Ceviche, and Garlic Butter Bok Choy. I had such a wonderful lunch experience!

I love this place! It's a gem located in an unassuming part of North Howard Ave. I'd say NoHo instead of SoHo but that just doesn't sound right. It's in a neighborhood that is part of North Hyde Park. Who knew? I'd never been to that part of Howard before and it looks like they are constructing new complexes in the area. It's actually starting to look trendy.

Anyway, I'd seen reviews from other Yelp friends and it just looked fantastic. I met up with a friend for my first visit. For your first time, I'd suggest going for breakfast on a week day. It's just not as crowded during that time and it makes it even more comfortable. It's counter service at breakfast. Just place your order and find a seat inside or outside. They bring everything to you once you're seated. The service has been outstanding each time I've been there. I tried the mama's baklava and the fresh fruit filled bougatsa pastry. I loved how the baklava had a clove honey taste. It had a great flavor and it was moist and not dry. The pastry was so light and heavenly. The fruit was perfect and not a single blemish. I was also loving the baklava latte with oat milk. We sat indoors for this visit since it was a very hot day. It was a very delightful visit.

My second visit was at lunch and the parking lot was full, as well as every seat in the house was occupied. More of a casual business lunch setting at the time. I ended up leaving and going somewhere else. But that didn't keep me from going back for another breakfast this past Thursday. I just had to try the BYO focaccia boat. I'm so glad I did. It's so unique and I loved the feta and mozzarella cheese mixture baked inside the boat. I decided to add an egg and their house cured smoked salmon. It was all delicious. The host noticed right away when bringing it out to me that it didn't have the salmon. He didn't give me a chance to discover that for myself which is great. He apologized and went back to get the smoked salmon. I'm kind of glad that it ended up being served on the side. I got to taste it separately and liked it better that way. The egg was good and you can order it cooked the way you want it. I honestly didn't need the egg. It was so filling that I just couldn't eat it all. It was a large bread boat. I also loved the arugula salad with a touch of dressing and sea salt added. I'd get this again. The double espresso was also a very nice treat. 

I didn't leave without getting some baked goods for the road. This time I got the plain bougatsa that is loaded with this amazing and light custard filling. The giant chocolate chip cookie was good but I didn't really taste the chocolate pieces. I could see lots of chips but not a whole lot of chocolate flavor. I'll get a different cookie flavor next time. Other than that, it was a fantastic experience each time. Especially sitting in the front patio in this cool fall weather. It's so pretty out there being surrounded by the beautiful potted bougainvillea. It was a very relaxing morning. Just try it for yourself one day.

We had a very nice meal at Shells last night. We've been not-so frequent customers since the day we moved to this area (back in 2006). The restaurant at this location closed suddenly for quite a while, but then reopened again about 4 years ago in the same spot. We visited when they reopened and basically ordered the same things we ordered last night. Then we went back another time and I had something different. It was the grilled mahi-mahi. I added the big fish topping (I think they call it Italiano now) for an additional charge. The topping ruined it for me. It was so salty and covered everything. Mom had the Shrimp Mezzo Mezzo and didn't like it. Hadn't been back there until now. 

Well, our visit last night was way better. Emily was our server, and she was fantastic! I was happy to hear that they have a classic mojito. It's not on the happy hour menu, but that's okay. She asked if I had a preference for rum, and I told her Bacardi. It was a very good drink for the price. Not as good as others I've had but I'd order it again. We also got a dozen steamed oysters. The menu says steamed with an attitude. It was a mild seasoning. Not as good as the oysters at Hot N Crazy Crab, but it was good that they have an option to have them seasoned. I don't remember them having an option before. I can also say that their raw oysters are very good from past visits. I never can pass up the oysters. 

We decided to order the Classic Seafood Pasta (no scallops for mom) and the Grilled Swordfish with parsley buttered red skin potatoes and a side of asparagus ($1 extra). Mom loved her pasta dish. She said it was very tasty. I took a bite of it and it was very flavorful and full of seafood and garlic. The garlic bread served with it was also very good. My swordfish was buttery and tender. I'm so glad I didn't get any toppings this time. It would have ruined it. The potatoes were better than I remembered them to be. The asparagus was mushy but good. All in all it was a good meal. I give them 4 stars because of previous visits. Their veggie sides are nothing special. It can get loud in there because it's always full of people. We tend to go early to avoid the wait. The service has always been great, and the seafood is very affordable compared to other places that specialize in it. We will return. We'll try to be more frequent customers this time around.

I'm giving it 4 stars. It's a theme restaurant with all kinds of Ford memorabilia and cars. It deserves a star for the atmosphere and theme. On cooler days they have the garage doors open to the parking lot. Having the doors open brings in a lot of street noise, but isn't that the whole point of the theme? It feels like you are in Ford's Garage. There are vintage Ford cars hanging over each bar area. The wheels on the car spin slowly. My first visit was with my mother. She really got into the whole theme. It brought up discussions about my grandfather who had a black Ford back in the day. She also loved the honking of the horn at the bar, and the overall décor (restroom included).

Other than that, the service can be hit or miss. There were times that we had to wait a long time to get our check, but for the most part the service has been friendly and helpful. At one time they would let you sample a new beer on tap if you were undecided. I'm not sure if they still do that or not but they certainly do have a good list of craft beers. I also remember being disappointed with a burger I ordered when they first opened. I felt like the burger wasn't seasoned enough. I think it was called the Cali-Rocker burger and it was a special burger for Breast Cancer Awareness month. I did like all the toppings which included goat cheese and avocado. I also liked their rum cake. It was a nice moist yellow cake soaked in dark Bacardi rum (with a walnut topping) and served with vanilla ice cream. I don't see it on their menu anymore, but get it if you do see it.

My most recent experience was for takeout. My husband had a business lunch there the other day. He asked me what I wanted and brought it back to me nice & warm. I got the Estate Burger which was actually quite tasty. It was better than the burgers I had my previous visits. This one had smoked gouda cheese, onion jam, arugula, onion straws, and white truffle bacon aioli on a half pound black angus burger. I know, it's just a burger that you can make at home and I have to say that my husband couldn't believe the cost. I have to agree. The burger by itself was an estate price of $15 (just for the sandwich). The bill actually came to about $20 when adding tater tots plus tax. It's hard to justify, but it was a tasty burger. It was also cooked a perfect medium which is what I wanted. The tater tots where just tater tots. Yes, I'd probably get the burger again but my husband not so much. He was not impressed with his fish and chips, nor with the Firestone shrimp appetizer that he had during lunch. He said it was okay, but just didn't think it was worth the price. You'll just have to see for yourself.

I'd say it's worth a couple of visits but I'd pick the less busier times to go there. It gets very busy and service is lackluster at peak times. The parking lot is always full, but there are plenty of places to park. There is outdoor seating as well. If anything, it's nice for picture taking, and you don't even have to go inside to do that.

I thought I had already reviewed Cali-Brandon when it was Ciccio Cali, but I guess I never did. Shocking to me because I absolutely love their Hot & Crunchy Tuna bowl. 

This restaurant is part of the Ciccio Restaurant Group (or CRG) which has multiple restaurants all over Tampa (Daily Eats, Fresh Kitchen, Green Lemon, Taco Dirty, and the list goes on). They started out small in SoHo and have basically built an empire. Okay, I'm exaggerating but they really do have a lot of wonderful restaurants that I have been to and love. Yes, it's a local thing! Anyway, Cali was the first to start the whole bowl concept in the Brandon/Riverview area. Everyone said it would be a fad, but guess what? Now we have bowl restaurants popping up everywhere in Brandon. This is why I had to go back just to be sure that I wasn't dreaming about the quality and flavor. I'm glad I did this just to reacquaint myself to the original.

Anyway, the Hot & Crunchy bowl is exactly as I remembered it. I always stick with the original protein which is the marinated and seared Ahi tuna but you can add whatever protein you want. The tuna by itself is full of flavor but the hot & crunchy style just elevates everything up a notch. The fresh cucumber, jicama, scallions, soy sauce, guacamole, crispy tempura onion, toasted sesame seeds, and sriracha aioli make it amazing. Oh and every bowl is under $10. I usually get it with the spaghetti squash but today I got the coconut avocado rice. It added even more flavor. They do suggest sticky rice as the base. To be totally honest, I think I like it best with the spaghetti squash because there already is a lot of flavor even without the base. I love that they even offer spaghetti squash. I know I'd rather have that as a non-carb option instead of just kale or cauliflower rice. Just my preference really.

I've also had what was at one time called the Tampanian Bowl that may have been off a daily special bowl menu. That was back in 2015 so hopefully my memory hasn't failed me. I don't know, but it was terrific and had all these yummy Cuban flavors in one bowl. It had mojo chicken and a creamy garlic aioli with crispy garbanzo beans. I don't think they offer it anymore but maybe a bowl can be customized to something close. I've never been good at making my own bowl so I do love that they give you different bowl styles which makes it easier for me to decide.

So another thing that I love is that they have 2 entrances. One for pick up orders and another for dine-in. It's so easy to use the app or call in a takeout order. It's ready in 15 to 20 minutes. You walk in, pay, and then sit in one of their many waiting chairs away from dine-in customers. Not many places have that and I think it's great. I felt super comfortable doing that. They also have a very nice outdoor dining area as well. It's at the Winthrop Town Centre so there is plenty of parking. It's super busy but if you don't see any parking in front then you can park in the back. Yes, super busy all the time and that's great. Try it for yourself.

It's time to update my review since I wrote it back in 2017 (when they first opened). It's still 5 stars. Wish I could give it more after multiple visits and takeout orders. This is my favorite Thai restaurant. I love that they have a separate vegan menu with way more choices than any other restaurant. I'm not vegan, but I like the option and have found many wonderful items such as the eggplant basil stir fry, veggie spring rolls, and vegetable noodle soup. Everything they make is homemade including the sauces. There are no store bought sauces with added preservatives. They cook healthy and with lots of fresh veggies even in the regular menu items. They also don't skimp on the heat level. If you ask for it, you'll get it at whatever level you want. My husband won't go anywhere else but this place for Thai food. He's a Texan who loves spicy food. He gets his beef basil stir fry in Thai hot and absolutely loves it. He was actually the first person to recommend this restaurant to me. He happened to go there during one of my hospital visits. He said Preeda warned him of the spice level, and apparently was even impressed that he ate it all with no complaints. I asked him if it was Thai Boat. The previous restaurant that occupied that space (which was also good).  He corrected me and said that it's under new ownership and called Thai Legacy. We've been going ever since that time along with my mother.

We've been to all the other Thai restaurants in the area. They are all unique in their own way. I just like this one the best because of the variety. I've come to appreciate it even more after my recent visit to the Thai temple. I was drawn to the noodle soup and the flower teas at their Sunday market. I was craving that soup during the week so I pulled up the Thai Legacy menu and noticed that they have many variations of this soup on their menu. So far, I've had the pork noodle soup and the veggie one with tofu. The pork noodle soup has 4 different noodle options (small rice noodles, large rice noodles, yellow egg noodles, or clear bean noodles) and the veggie one has 3 types (no egg noodles). I got the clear bean noodles and asked for the spice tray on the side so that I could add my own heat. The takeout soup orders come with chili pepper spice, paste, and pickled jalapenos. It's a huge portion that can definitely be 2 meals or split between 2 people. It was so good, and reminded me of my morning at the Sunday market. It so comforting and I'm so happy that I can get it Tuesday thru Sunday when needed. I was also happy to see that they are now serving exotic iced teas such as Roselle Hibiscus, Butterfly Pea Flower, and Lemongrass tea. I've had the first 2 teas and they are refreshing. It's unlimited refills during lunch.

This restaurant gets better and better each time. It's a wonderful and hard-working family that owns it. They cook with love and health in mind. The service is always friendly and welcoming. They remember us every time we come in (especially my mother). We'll continue to return often.

I normally wouldn't give 5 stars for a takeout order, but I was impressed with the service and the food. This is my first time experiencing this type of seafood boil concept. I'm looking forward to dining in next time. The restaurant looked very clean, and the people up front taking my order were super nice & helpful. I didn't have to hang out too long waiting for the food to be prepared and packed. I think I was out of there within 15 minutes after placing the order. Impressive!

I ordered the combination seafood boil. The one that allows you to select 2 types of seafood (a half pound each). Mom and I love mussels so it was a no-brainer to order the mixture of green and black mussels for the 2 of us. I also got the fried oyster basket which typically comes with fries. I substituted the fries with sweet potato waffle fries instead. No extra charge. Can you believe that? 

Everything was great! Mom really enjoyed getting her hands dirty with this meal. She ate most of the mussels, and I didn't hear a peep out of her until we were done eating. They give you gloves and bibs for takeout orders, but we didn't need to use them. 

My only disappointment was that I didn't see any healthy sides (like some kind of veggie other than corn or cole slaw). The fried seafood baskets have generous portions but it's just too much fried food all at once. The seafood boil on the other hand was fantastic with the garlic butter. They have a number of different seasonings like lemon pepper, cajun, and the hot & crazy sauce. I chose to keep it simple. I thought the sauce went well with the mussels. The 2 red skin potatoes and corn that comes with the boil mixture tasted pretty good with the garlic butter as well. I was blown away by the size of the green mussels. It was a nice and colorful presentation (even in the bag).  I will definitely order it again.

There are now 3 seafood boil places in Brandon. I haven't been to the other 2 yet, but I'm curious to try them out. I have this feeling that Hot N Crazy Crab is better, and I'm basing that on other Yelper reviews. I do hope they are here to stay. This particular storefront of this super old plaza on Bloomingdale & John Moore hasn't had much luck keeping it's tenants. They did a great job of renovating the space and making it more open and inviting. Another good thing is that there are plenty of parking spaces. I'm looking forward to trying more items. Maybe they'll add more veggie sides to the menu later.

This was a first time visit, and it definitely will not be the last one. I was super impressed with this new pizzeria. It's unique in many different ways. First of all, the smell of the wood fire oven immediately draws you in. The second thing you notice are the fresh loaves of Italian bread that they have displayed by the cashier. Yes, they make them fresh all day long. I was already hooked even before being seated. 

Anyway, mom and I had a wonderful meal. We started with their toasted bread that's served with a spiced olive oil for dipping or spooning it over the bread slices. It was delicious. It had lots of fresh garlic and spices. I'd definitely get that again. We had a difficult time deciding on which specialty pizza to order. They had so many unique combinations. Some with toppings such as burrata cheese, clams, calabrian peppers, artichokes, fig jam, wood fired red peppers, prosciutto di Parma, and so much more. These are gourmet rustic wood fired pizzas. The type that I remember having when traveling through Rome and Sorrento. We finally decided to try Nonna's White Clam Pizza. We took the advice of the owner and added bacon. It was so good. It was even topped with about 6 whole little neck clams in their own shell. I've never seen a presentation like it. I was also happy to see that my mother ate 3 slices of it. She never eats more than two. 

I also felt like it was a family owned and run pizzeria. The staff worked like a family. Every member assisted us at least once during our meal. Siara was wonderful from beginning to end. I even got a loaf of bread to take home. They also make panini's with their homemade bread. I may have to try their Caprese panini on my next visit. The bread is so soft, but hearty. My husband really like it. We had it for breakfast the very next day. Better than Cuban bread IMO. We'll be back to try The Rock and other specialty pizzas.

It was my first visit to Revolution Ice Cream. I've read so many good reviews about the ice cream and chill atmosphere. I wasn't as amazed as others, and maybe it was the flavor that I chose so I will be back to try other flavors. I probably should have asked for samples.

The store smelled like cinnamon when I walked in. A very pleasant smell. Service was good, but it was clearly a one person show that day. She was working hard and was very super helpful. Not a single person was there for ice cream. But I did see quite a few people coming in to pick up their Matt's Fat cookie orders. They must be pretty darn good because they were picking up boxes of cookies they ordered online. These are the half pound cookies that you can only order online when they are open to take orders (or able to bake them), and they'll do a drop off delivery to the Revolution store of your choice. Anyway, I'm telling you this because I would so love to see an ice cream made with these cookie pieces or have some way of purchasing just 1 cookie. I'm not quite sure if the smell of cinnamon was from the cookies or the Matt's Fatty Roll ice cream. I'll have try that flavor next time.

I ended up getting the seaward ice cream. I could barely see the description of it on the menu overhead and I even had my glasses on. It was difficult to choose a flavor with the lack of descriptions. I recommend you view the menu at revicecream.com ahead of time. The seaward sounded good but I really couldn't taste the salted caramel or coffee flavor. It was more cinnamon and cardamom, and very little of it. It was very basic but tasted good. The atmosphere is kind of a thrown together artsy and eclectic feel. They have local art on the wall for sale. There's plenty of seating and lots of parking out front. It's in that old 2 story looking strip mall on SR60 near Moon Ave. They have a couple of other locations around the bay area. This store in Brandon is the original location. It's worth a try if you happen to be in the area. The flavors are unique, and it's a popular local ice cream spot. I'll give it another shot one day soon.

This is another place that I can't believe I've never reviewed. I've been going to Wright's for years now. It's an iconic local and family owned business that all the locals know about. I've never had anything here that I didn't like. It's my favorite sandwich shop in the area. I was introduced to Wright's when I started working in the Westshore area back in 2006. Our company uses their catering service and we've had many Wright's birthday cakes over a period of about 12 years. I think I've had just about every flavor. I love them all. 

They bake their own bucket bread. The bread is round just like the big bucket pan.  My absolute favorite sandwich is their "Beef Martini" specialty sandwich. It's a rare roast beef sandwich served hot with mushrooms marinated in wine, bacon, and this garlic herb buttery spread. It's so wonderful!! I usually have to split the sandwich with someone. It's huge. My mother was a big fan of the hot corned beef sandwich on rye with the mustard sauce. She said it's the only sandwich that has come close to the ones she had in NYC since she moved to Florida 60 years ago. That says something. Mom was very picky, and she loved the sandwiches here. My brother who was born in NY loves the Pete's mustard sauce and gets extra sauce on the side of his sandwich every time I take him here.

Well, this most recent visit was no exception. It was still as good as I remembered it. Maybe even more crowded than I remember. I hadn't been since the expansion. Oh my, this place is huge and they need every bit of that space. The line is out the door. I think this place is always busy. It's more organized than it used to be. They have a separate area for call in orders and grab & go items. I suggest using it because you will have to wait in a long line for an impromptu visit like the one I had. I was going to eat it there but it was just way too packed for me. I'm still not quite comfortable dining in crowded places yet. I think I've become a germaphobe during the pandemic. Anyway, I  ended up getting an orange spice tea (unsweetened) while I was waiting for my order to come out. This is a great tea flavor! There is a smallish area to wait for your order. I took the goods to the overflow parking lot (where I parked) and had a wonderful meal in the car. Yep, there's plenty of parking. It was actually quite nice as I got to see a bunch of butterflies and blue jays in the vegetation nearby. All I can say is I'm glad I don't live in this wonderful and rich neighborhood behind the deli. I'd be walking to Wright's on a daily basis.

I will continue to bring relatives and friends here for a visit. They have plenty of seating available. Everything seemed spaced out in the dining areas. It was all very clean. Always has been. The employees were all wearing masks. I was surprised by that but appreciated it. As you know, Florida is totally open and patrons don't have to wear one if fully vaccinated. Most patrons don't wear masks unless a business specifically requires it. If this bothers you then I suggest calling ahead with your order. The bottom line is the employees are taking precautions and that's all that counts. Stop by and see for yourself. I was impressed.

I really like this place. As others have mentioned it is in a gas station on the corner of Causeway Blvd and Falkenburg Rd in the Lake Brandon Shoppes. They have a steady flow of regular customers. I've been going there off and on for a couple of years now. They have great sandwiches with their homemade mustard and cilantro sauce. It's a very hard working husband and wife team who compliment each other very well. Service is always with a smile and they genuinely would do anything to make your experience a good one.

I totally love their cold brew café con leche made with Bustelo coffee. I can't go there without getting one. I also like their empanadas which they've added since the last time I was there. They make dessert ones too. I got the Cuban sandwich and Nutella banana empanada. Both were served hot and they were still warm when I got home. The breakfast steak and egg sandwich was also a winner. I honestly could only eat half. It was a whole steak and not chopped up like other places. There was a very generous portion of egg as well. They grill up everything right there where you can see it. Everything is open. The bread was also very good. These sandwiches are worth the price. 

A 4 star review for a Cuban sandwich place is very good coming from me. I grew up in Miami eating Cuban and PR food. I'm super picky when it comes to my Latin food so don't be mad at me. I don't think I've given any Cuban or Puerto Rican place in the Tampa Bay area a 5 star review yet. So take that for what it's worth. Visit this place if you happen to be in the area, and be patient if there is a line. Consider yourself lucky if there isn't a line. Everything is made to order and people love it.

Well, I know this is a popular bakery in Brandon but I really don't understand why. I don't think there has been one visit when I haven't been disappointed with something that I purchased. First of all, everything looks fantastic. But looks can be very deceiving. In this case, you buy it because it looks fantastic and then you take a bite and it's nothing like what you imagined. The guava pastries are dry. I've never been able to get one that tasted fresh. The crust is like sawdust. The decorated cookies are dry and stale. The frosted brownies are heavy and taste like pure fudge. Don't bother using a plastic fork because it will break into the brownie. Yes, this happened to me and I hope it was just an off day. It went down into my stomach like a piece of lead. The pan de bono was chewy and tasteless. The mallorca that I purchased the other day didn't taste like any mallorca I've ever had. It was a dense pastry that was wet for some reason. Maybe it was melted sugar. I don't know what it was, but I know what it wasn't. It didn't even taste like any of the ensaïmadas that we had in Barcelona. They are supposed to be a light pastry with powdered sugar on top. This was not it.

Now that I've emphasized the negatives, I'll end with the positives. I think the only sweets from this bakery that my mother and I like are the chocolate brownie cookies. We go there every now and then for the brownie cookies and a cafe con leche after dinner. The Cuban sandwich has a unique special sauce that I like, but sometimes the way the sandwich is made can be hit or miss. The service is good. I've never had a problem with that. I probably should be giving them 2 stars because I've had way better. I'm giving an extra star for the service, the sandwich, and the brownie cookie. I keep saying that this will be my last visit, but I still have hope that one day I'll find something really delicious like everyone else in Brandon.

A friend has been talking his place up for a couple years. Always telling me I need to try the place. Couldn't stop talking about the steam pots, how great the staff treat you...on and on. 

Tonight he was in town I decided to give it a try....let me tell you something. The steam pots are where it's at. We sat at the bar, they cooked them right in front of us. They smelled so good while cooking. 

Once they where finished...one word AMAZING!!!!

My friend lives in AZ so is only on town every couple months. All of the staff remembered him, they came up and say hi asked personal questions on how he was doing they really remember him. For me the entire experience was awesome. 

If you want to try the best oyster bar in town try this place. They are truly second to none!  Will definitely be returning.

This is the perfect antidote for the downtown State Street nightlife scene. It's a casual, comfortable, and laid-back atmosphere, which isn't surprising since it's a converted house: the main bar area will make you feel like you're drinking brewskis in a buddy's garage. There are several rooms to relax in and a patio out back if you want to enjoy the Santa Barbara weather. 

It's a beer-and-wine, cash-only bar (ATM on premises), so don't expect fancy-shmancy cocktails or expertly crafted appetizers. In spite of its hipster-ness, you do get good service and a terrific spot to relax and enjoy your friends' company. You can also shoot a game of pool (free!), play some Ms. Pac Man (still only a quarter!), or eat some Pop-Tarts (seriously!).

Elsie's is an excellent neighborhood bar. I have a lot of fond memories of hanging out here over the years and I always try to stop by whenever I'm in town.

Highly recommended.

Years later and I am still on a hunt for the best cheesesteak in Philly. . 
Just a FYI, this review is getting a 4, only because of the pizza fries. We heard about this place from someone that goes to Philly all the time. I am just confused on why it got so much hype about their cheesesteak when it does not reach the "standard" that I know of. It does not deserve a 4 for the cheesesteak. So let's just knock that part out right now:

The South Philly Cheesesteak: To be honest, it was a little dry. My visionary of a philly would be CHEESE .. cheese. . and grease. In this case, the cheese factor was not up to par and .. my bread. . was not .. "leaking". I've had better cheesesteaks at Non-Philly locations, so the hunt continues. 

anyway, 

The Pizza Fries: WHY DID THE PIZZA FRIES HAVE MORE CHEESE THAN THE CHEESESTEAK? i just want to know because .. okay. The fries were already seasoned .. nicely and the sauce and cheese added the "yes" factor. 

The cheesesteaks didnt "wow" me, but the pizza fries .. did.

When you're not from somewhere and you're looking for a place to go, you always ask the locals. This time we asked our lyft driver on the way home from dinner. . and she failed us. 

We get to the door & we were told $10 for a cover. When it comes to clubs that you can't even see / hear the "fun" happening inside. . you're kind of sketch and questionable. So we walk away and went to walk into a nearby bar. My friend goes outside for a phone call and the security guard told her that we can get in for free. So okay. .

We walk up the stairs and hear music, cool. We get to the top and well, the question "where is everyone". For us to be pushed for a cover charged .. whew. Then, when we were trying to get on the roof. . the security guard said "you must buy a drink" in order to go LOL. what? okay. My friend bought a drink. . $14 for crown and coke. . that was maybe like 6oz. A waste. . he then went upstairs and it was EMPTY. . no one. 

So basically what we got from this place is that 1) it's not popping 2) security guards try to scam you 3) the bar is a scam. . but 4) decor was nice. 

Will not be returning.

After a festival (Made in America), my friends and I were walking downtown trying to decide what to eat. As we turned the corner, this elder couple was like, "are yall looking for something?" then I explained to them we were looking for a place to get dinner. He then recommended this location. "Just go down this street.. make a left. BAM." then he walked away with his wife with their walkers. So cute lol.

Anyway, we walked up to the building and I felt as if I was in a movie or tv show. The feeling was surreal. . was I just hungry or? Okay Okay. So I heard their pizza was bomb, however I couldn't eat that. I knew I was going to do heavy lifting the next day, a two a day matter of fact so I needed something that would provide me with energy. Spaghetti of course. I actually got the eggplant parm with spaghetti. I am a sucker for eggplant. It's so good to me. Petes was really good. Sometimes when you go to places, the sauce is bland. However, theirs was very flavorful. They placed it in a brown paper bag with parm and garlic bread. I believe I paid like $12? Which isn't bad because the portion was huge. I couldn't even finish it. I did eat some later on lol. The only down side is that their machine to get water was broken so I had to buy a bottle.

Low and behold, I had my best run the next day. 

According to their signs, they deliver until 12! 
 
Thank you Pete's. Will definitely be back. Thank you to the elder couple also!

Heeeeey Sabrina. One of the best places to dine while in downtown Philly. My friends and I found this gem on Yelp when looking for places to eat without catching an uber. We ended up walking from our hotel for dinner. 

Sabrina's Cafe had so much to offer. As always, I love asking what the popular items are that so many people get. What I got was from the Signature Breakfast Items. I ended up getting the stuffed challah french toast. It was a blend of cream cheese, bananas, and honey. It was topped with vanilla bean syrup. Man, I just want to go back just for this. My boyfriend got the same thing .. and we shared home style fries. yes carbs. Great thing that Sabrina serves breakfast all day. 

The playlist that was bumping was really nice also! I had to ask what playlist they were using lol. At the time we went, we did not have to wait. .we were basically the only people in there lol. Our experience was great, therefore I know we will be back.

**Inside the Reading Terminal Market** 

A couple days before going to The Reading Terminal, I had to figure out what I wanted. Well, I didn't "have" to. . I just like going places and know what I am going to get. Anyone else like that? Anyway. I am currently on a health kick meaning, I am watching what I eat. In the Reading Terminal, we can all agree there are not a lot of places that serve healthy options. However, Four Seasons Juice Bar provides are great alternative. 

I ended up getting a strawberry, banana, and pineapple drink. It was only $5.25 for freshness. They had different sizes that you could choose from. It was really good. They have so many ingredients to choose from for your smoothie, and I kept it simple. This establishment served as a great alternative.

*cash only!* ATM inside that charged $2. 

Philly, you're known for cheesesteaks and I feel like I've been on a search for one every time I come to the city. It's weird to me, well I take that back, it's cool to me how everyone has a preference in where to get the best Philly. 

This trip, we tried something we were told to go to from our Lyft driver. As we walked to the restaurant, the line was WRAAAAPPED around the building. So I decided to have a little fun & time it on my phone. 48 minutes from where we started until we got upstairs to grub. 

While, we waited. . it was nice talking to the people around us and reading the stuff on the wall! So many signatures and photos to look at. 

Before you order, it's important to know .. what you want to order LOL. DOOOO NOT be that person that goes up to the window and "uhhhh" your life away. Anyway, it's important to also know the kind of cheese that you want for your philly. You can pick from Whiz. American, or Provolone. OF COURSE, the Philly way is with Whiz, however I am personally not a fan of it. So, I always get provolone. 

Since I'm "not supposed to eat bad", I decided to shared my other half of my philly cheese with someone. I let him fix it anyway he wanted. He asked for grilled onions, mushrooms, aaaand forgot the mayo so we had to put it on after. Overall, it was good. 

My friend cannot eat meat so he got the Meatless version. He finished it and was surprised at the fact that it was really good. 

I was disappointed in THREE things: 
1. They don't really season the meat. 
2. As I walked upstairs in the dinning area, I saw the big cans of mushrooms. I don't know, for some reason that was a turn off 
3. THEY DON'T SELL FRIES. I was going to be a baddie and get some but. . they decided to control that for me :)) hahha. 
If in the area, I would pick this place over other. . locations on the same street *wInk. ....* 

Please get frieeeees.

Horrible service! Staff is rude. Terrible product. Would never go back. Asked for a general item at most coffee places and was ignored and acted like my service didn't matter. Also rude to other customers as well.

We were in the neighborhood on a Saturday night and looking for dinner.  A lot of the restaurants had an hour wait and this had no wait.  Should have taken this as a bad sign.   The service was quite slow.  We ordered drinks and they took forever to come.  I was thirsty and I saw Agua Fresca on the menu which is something I never see and really love.  Well save your money.  For $4 I got a ginger ale with some pomegranate juice in it.  No lie.  For an appetizer we tried the queso which I had high hopes for but it wasn't great.  It was like melted cheese but hardened so it literally broke the chips when we went to dip.  It had chorizo in it but it was flavorless and actually kind of cold.  So eh.  I wanted some comfort food for dinner so I tried the pulled chicken.  The flavor was okay but the chicken was dry and they had this aioli drizzled on top that was really laid on thick and it was awful.  Reminded me of straight mayo.  No flavor and ick it threw me off.  The plantains were good though so once I scraped off the aioli and put a bite of plantain with the chicken and rice, it was decent.  We skipped dessert.  We just wanted to go home at this point and everything took so long we just didn't want to wait anymore.  Maybe I'd come here for Happy Hour for drinks and an app at the bar but never again for dinner.

I'm sadly disappointed I from New Jersey garden State graduate Belleville high School back in 1979 I was looking forward to your place I drove in from Phoenix and I dropped my daughter off at u of a and I came to your place and it was closed with Saturday 1 I was wondering why so I called your phone up and your answering machine said Happy Thanksgiving but we can be closed Wednesday Thursday and Friday and reopen Saturday at 11 a.m. I said okay but I got there at 1 and you're still close I'm hoping everything's okay it won't stop me from coming back but I got to tell you I'm slightly disappointed that I couldn't try my East coast subs which people we're bragging about

Tip: two lines. One for the rooftop bar and one for the 1st floor stage and kitchen

1st floor had an amazing band playing on stage.
Rooftop bar had a line directing you to the bar which was helped keep social distancing and the bartender can concentrate on one order at a time without crowding the bar

I just got into Philadelphia and wanted a classic cheesesteak. Time to check out the Geno's-Pat's rivalry. 

Which was better? Well, I could only eat at most one sandwich so I went with Pat's, the higher rated cheesesteak shop on Yelp. Plus, there was no line. 

I read the "how-to" sign and still screwed up ordering. I said "wit cheese whiz." Oops, sorry, I'm a tourist! Please just give me my cheesesteak with ("wit") onions and cheese whiz.

With money in hand, I paid and got my sandwich. A good sized cheesesteak filled with sliced beef, grilled minced onions and cheese whiz. At first glance I loved it, especially the cheese whiz part. Then I took a bite and noticed the meat was dry. There was also not enough cheese whiz on my sandwich. It would have been better if the meat was mixed with the cheese beforehand. One bite would be ooey and gooey, then another bite would be full of tasteless, dry meat. I want more cheese whiz! I threw away half of my sandwich in disappointment. 

Price: $8.50 for a cheesesteak, tax included.

Where do you head for a post-workout food splurge? Freebirds.

I ordered a chicken burrito with rice, cheese, lettuce, salsa verde, black beans and pico de gallo. It was pretty awesome, especially the fresh guacamole. I liked my burrito so much I ate the whole thing! No leftovers. 

This place reminded me of Chipotle, but better. The menu was simple: choose a burrito or a plate of nachos, pick a meat and add whatever else you want to the meal. 

Cost Breakdown: 
$7.15 chicken burrito + $1.65 guacamole + $2.55 horchata = $11.35 plus tax.

Skip the drink and you have a meal for under $10.

I discovered Sump through a Pecha Kucha presentation by Scott (the powerful bearded coffee demi-god of St. Louis). His presentation was amazing in that he was so passionate about coffee. I had never met anyone who was so into coffee. Not even other coffee shop owners, he's a different breed. This made me want to check out the venue and see what the big deal was.

Fast Forward several months later, I get to Sump to visit the locale and holy crap it's amazing! For most of us who drink coffee, we have to add sugar, cream and pixy dust to make it bearable (or as my father in law calls it Candy Coffee). The coffee is so good you actually enjoy the flavor. The brewing process and the fact they can explain it to you sets it apart.

I don't ever plan on learning about coffee but if I need to learn, I'll go to Sump. Seriously the coffee is the best I've tasted. I wish they were closer to me or opened up a location in Midtown. 

Outside of the coffee, not a ton of food options but that's ok. Usually you are here to get some coffee, read a book (or study) and relax. Easily worth checking out if you haven't been yet. And if you have gone, you should return again. Easily the best coffee you'll taste in St. Louis City.

Looking for a classy yet casual Cocktail Bar with a rooftop option on Broadway in Nashville? The Valentine has you covered in spades.

The Valentine is a self-described 'upscale saloon' boasting three interior floors of food, drink and live music, along with a rooftop patio located in the center of all the action in Music City, Tennessee. I found myself at the bar thanks to a corporate event complete with open bar and appetizers and would argue there isn't a more distinguished or well appointed interior on the Broadway strip thanks to the giant chandler, prohibition era vibe, and illustrious service. Thanks to the open floor plan design on the second level it is easy to watch the nightly live music without blowing your ears out and the 3rd floor begs you to belly up to the bar to catch your favorite sporting event. The rooftop bar and patio closes any argument on what Bar is the most elegant and chic in the area.

I had a wonderful time at The Valentine and suggest that this is the spot to start any Broadway Bar Crawl.

A great location and atmosphere is marred by disappointing service and barbecue. 

While researching what to nosh on while in Nashville Jack Cawthon's Bar-B-Que popped up on nearly every list in the local rags and magazines so needless to say I was excited to try their brand of barbecue that has been churned out on Broadway since 1996. From the flying pigs neon sign in the shadow of Nashville's iconic AT&T building to the old school and well worn interior, Jack's certainly looks the part. I ordered my Texas Brisket with great anticipation but noted the employees ran out of damns to give many years ago and were gruff at best.

No matter as long as the Brisket is exceptional, right?

Well, to be brutally honest - the Brisket was mildly terrible. Sure, there was plenty of smoke packed into the meat but it was laughably overdone with charred bits here and there but worst of all was the dryness which added a gummy chew to the mouthfeel that could only be remedied with copious amounts of the supplied sauces. The white Bun was perhaps the best part of the sandwich. At $5.99 it is hard to argue affordability of my lunch but there was no thrills to be had at Jack's. My companion tried the Tennessee Pork Shoulder Sandwich and had a similarly disconcerted experience so both left Jack's with a large portion of our sandwiches uneaten.

There are several other purveyors nearby that offer superior barbecue even if at a higher price point and I would recommend you explore other options while searching for the fix to your smoked meat hankering.

Longboards Grill is a fantastic place to grab a drink and take in the Santa Barabra coastline but you will certainly find better dining options nearby.

I recently stopped at Longboards Grill while strolling the pier in downtown Santa Barabra, and if nothing else, you simply cannot beat the vista of the northern Santa Barbara coast that the second level offers. The tables are placed very close together which can make maneuvering a challenge for both your party and the waitstaff but I suppose that is the case at any bar located on a large pier, right? 

The drink list is extensive and offers artisan Wine, Craft Beer, and mixed drinks at relatively inflated prices which are to be expected at any tourist trap. A quick scan of the menu revealed absolutely zero surprises and the costs per plate are absolutely obscene ($19.99 for a "Gaucho Salad" and $17.95 for a Turkey Salad? Calm down now Longboards...). The plates that were coming from the kitchen looked laughably rudimentary and highlighted the elevated pricing and kept me from putting in an order for a Calamari appetizer - well, that and the fact even the Calamari weighs in at an outrageous $17.95. 

Final word: Longboards Grill. Come for the Beer and view, then leave.

Finney's Crafthouse has it going on. 

My group of friends descended upon Finney's Crafthouse during an impromptu State Street crawl that ended at the beach in Santa Barbara. This is an interesting "corporate" looking Gastro that turns out to be a small local chain and from what I was told is beloved by locals and tourists alike. I actually went to college at UCSB and had not heard of Finney's Crafthouse before so I assume they are rather new. 

There is a full kitchen but we came for the libations and Finney's has a notable list of Craft brew both on drought and bottles/canned. The prices are a bit outrageous but welcome to DTSB, right? Even with the inflated prices everyone in my party thoroughly enjoyed themselves so I guess you get what you pay for and the servers were extremely jovial. I can't complain about my visit to Finney's Crafthouse and would advise anyone on a similar crawl to make the stop.

Rusty's Pizza Parlor puts together a decent pie.

After an afternoon of day drinking that led into night our group decided they wanted a simple Pizza & Beer spot and Rusty's had the best aggregate Yelp score in the area so -- that was that. The restaurant is outdoor dining only thanks to COVID-19 and there was plenty of space even on a Friday night which was great. The staff seemed really friendly and engaging plus the price point was fair considering the location. 

Our table ordered a Pepperoni Pizza to share along with a several Craft Beers and everything came out with fast enough efficiency and I was really impressed with the woman that was so bone ass wasted that her friends left her in a dark corner swaying just trying to stand up straight (thankfully nobody fed her any more alcohol). 

The pie itself? It wasn't bad. Rusty's puts on a straight forward football-style Pizza with limited flop, cheese stretch and a somewhat thin crust which I understand has won local awards. The Pepperoni was what you'd expect and nothing you wouldn't -- and perfect for soaking up Beer with. Cost of admission is $16.50 for a 16 inch that fed 4 of us nicely. 

If you are in the area and looking for a Pizza on State Street I would argue Rusty's is as good as any. 3 stars all day long.

A kitchy vibe and generous portions await you at Bar-B-Cutie on the fringe of NashVegas proper.

I walked into the awkward but somehow appropriately named Bar-B-Cutie with the company of foals in winter coats/white girls of the south in tow. The ambiance was in stark contrast to what I am accustomed to with accents of raw wood, twangy melodies in the air along with ultra friendly employees that are quick with a smile and no quarrels with referring to you as "Dear" or "Sweetie" - a perfect start to a day that would surely end with another afternoon of country tunes, inexpensive booze, and cheap shots from the familiar (yet trite) on Broadway street in downtown Nashville. 

A mammoth amount of breakfast can be had for the insanely cheap here; $10.00 will net a plate that would make an incredibly corpulent man on the Vegas strip blush. I went with what I felt was traditional southern options: 2 Eggs (sunny side), Hash Browns, and the ridiculously obvious - Biscuits with Sausage Gravy. All was cooked to order and seemed to welcome me even with a hungover stomach. Even though I picked at the plate like a bird thanks to my ailing state I throughly enjoyed everything available, most notably the Biscuit slathered with the supplied Gravy and then dipped in Egg yolk. For whatever reason the western music in the background acted as a gratifying umami for the ears and I felt like a native southerner for a single meal. 

Thank you Bar-B-Cutie for embracing me in my state of need. I appreciate you and I would bet locals do even more.

The hype is real. Run out and tell a friend. 

So I end up in Saint Louis for a wedding and naturally I need a food story to tell the people at work when I get back and it must be amazing or I have failed them miserably. After asking a few locals where the real deal Holyfield is for barbecued meats I decided that Bogart's would make the best candidate. The long line out front solidified my gut feeling and braving the 35 minute wait was well worth it. 

Once a table was secured and the Barbecue ordered in the tiny smoke house, it took no longer than 5 minutes for the plates to come out and the moment the smell of the food hit my olfactory receptors I knew I was in for Barbecue that would blow Bludso's into extinction. 

I started with the Burnt Ends, a personal favorite. The smoke to moisture ratio was spot on and the bark was deep and intense. A masterstroke in Que. The Brisket was also top notch, and with just a lick of the supplied "Mad Maddie's" Vinegar another level of complexity is discovered making for the most interesting juxtopozistion involving savory, smoky salty and tangy I recall. Being from California, I had to try the Tri Tip and again my mind was blown. The smoke ring was 1/4 deep at its thinnest and the wood smoke permiated the entire piece of meat. All three offerings deserve a standing ovation. 

This is outstanding Barbeque people!

The sides were also first class with the Deviled Egg Potato Salad being a dish of legend along with the Pit Baked Beans which boasts chunks of Barbecue in each bite. Even the Applesauce brings on tears of joy. 

Bogart's Smokehouse is an absolute gem and a must stop for any culinary adventurer with a penchant for red meat, barbeque and the love of what happens when execution meets ability. BRAVO!

Freebirds World Burrito gets the job done. 

If you are to ask any UCSB student where to eat in Isla Vista chances are Woodstock's Pizza, Buddha Bowls, and - you saw this coming - Freebirds World Burrito. This is because all of them offer one hell of a value proposition thanks to the portions and none of these options will break the bank. 

As far as the experience goes, Freebirds World Burrito is no different than Chipotle and competes at the same pricing schedule. Choose your base, protein, toppings, and salsa and within 5 minutes you will have a Burrito the size of Shaq's right arm in front of you for under $10.00.The Steak tends to get the most love although I would argue the Chicken is equally as good. I was perfectly content with my Burrito but must admit that Freebirds was so much better when hungover after a wild Thirsty Thursday at some of the dives on the loop. 

For me, Freebirds World Burrito is more about nostalgia than a culinary conquest as IV doesn't offer much - it is a college town after all. That said, it was fun to reel it back to the time I had little in way of experience in life or responsibilities to concern myself with.

If you are looking for impressive presentation and impeccable culinary execution in downtown Nashville, your search ends at Etch Restaurant.

Thanks to having friends in the area it took me little time to become aware of the CIA trained local heroine Chef Deb Paquette and her brand of forward thinking American cuisine. Etch is located a stones throw away from the Bridgestone Arena and made a perfect spot to enjoy a magnificent dinner before catching a Predators game. The service is impeccable - an exquisite blend of southern hospitality with a unique flair that seems to suit the spotless open kitchen perfectly. I cannot imagine a better spot for a first date while in Nashville. 

The menu is diversified with flavors from every corner of the earth represented from Ponzu to Tapenade and everything in-between. I recommend starting with the outstanding Charcuterie Salad featuring thinly shaved Tennessee Prosciutto, Sausages (house-cured no less), smoked Gouda, a yellow beet Dijon schmear, mixed Greens tossed in a spiced Vinaigrette, smoked Lima Beans, pickled Onions, Apple Confit, and fried Oyster Mushrooms that is expertly plated and equally as balanced and delicious as it is beautiful. 

For lovers of Filet Mignon (and who isn't?) Etch puts together a strong one. Boasting a 7 ounce grilled Steak that is slathered in Cabernet Sauce and topped with horseradish and laid upon a caramelized Onion Tart, with Parmesan, Broccoli, and Mustard Seed Tarragon Butter. This dish is rich and decadent to be sure - but chances are you are visiting for a special occasion or on vacation, right? Live a little. 

Another sure shot lies in the Grilled Lamb Loin where a Pomegranate Walnut Sauce shares the stage with the adroitly seared protein. Zero hints of gaminess were detected and the grilled Okra that flanks the meat reminds you that you are still in the south after all. I would go on record to say that this may be the best Okra I have ever had. 

I could go on gushing ad nauseam about Etch but I am certain you get the point already. If you are headed to (or living in) Nashville - this should be on the short list.

Nearly 40 years later, Woodstock's Pizza Isla Vista still serves the students of UCSB up with their brand of Pie. 

Woodstock's Pizza Isla Vista will always be nostalgic for me. It was the first dinner I had as a gaucho freshman and I frequented Woodstock's nearly weekly for years. Freshly made gigantic Pies at a reasonable price, the staff is almost all UCSB students, and even Pint Night? What twenty one year old wouldn't love Woodstock's? 

The only question was how would the Pizza fare years later now that my palette and disposable income situations have vastly changed. The truth? Better than I expected. 

I was passing through Isla Vista which is a quintessential college town if nothing else. I decided to relive yesteryear and stopped into Woodstock's which has been a permanent part of UCSB culture since 1982 and not a damn thing has changed. Well, they did add new menu items and flatscreen. Outside of that - not a damn thing has changed. I was tempted to order the famous Wildebread with Cheese but did not want to overeat so I went with the classic Pepperoni which is $20.00 for a very big Medium (they also offer Personal Pizza for $10.00). It took roughly 10 minutes to arrive.

The moment the Pie was sat before us I felt like I was transported back to my freshman year. It looked and smelled just as I remembered. The crust is thick and doughy; a texture I adored back in the day but find a bit hum-drum today. However, the marinara is better than I recall thanks to a zippy Tomato flavor with the right amount of Garlic and Seasoning. The toppings were all plenty fresh - notably the Mozzarella - and the Pepperoni offered an almost spicy kick without being overly greasy. It was an all-around honest Pie. It would compare well locally with Sgt. Pepperoni in Newport Beach.

Let's peel back the nostalgia and give a subjective determination. 

Look, Woodstock's Pizza is not something I would seek out very often based on the Pie alone but 16 taps worth of Craft Beer and the outside deck certainly don't hurt Woodstock's argument. Besides, even a bad Pizza is pretty good, right? Well, Woodstock's has a good Pizza in and a great ambiance. So with that logic, 3 stars it is. 

Oh - and Yelp: 3 Stars is a positive review. Please remember that.

Divvy is a Carmel, Indiana Gastro that largely misses the mark. 

I was invited to Divvy by numerous folks at my corporate headquarters lately that seemed enthralled with the idea of visiting a Tapas and Craft Beer/Full Bar concept that would remind most of us here in Orange County of Pueblo or (to a much lesser extent) Playground. The interior (and exterior for that matter) is modern and nothing if not clean. The service is spot on and quite warm to boot.
