Even the prices are absurdly inexpensive - at least from a west coast perspective - for whatever that is worth. 

Countless plates were ordered, and even more drinks over the course of the night. That said, let's get to brass tacks.

The first bite I sampled was the Pimento Puffs which feature Jalapeño, a dollop of Cream Cheese, a load of Monterey Jack, all dredged in a Cucumber Buttermilk coat and seasoned with "Taco Dust". I'll be real, all that was detected was deep fryer and Monterey Jack with a hint of heat. Cheese Curds lovers would be dazzled, but sadly I was not. 

Next up was the Cream Corn Brulée that is a creative mash-up of sorts that takes a typical Midwestern Cream Corn too the next level with the addition of Jalapeño, and heavy hand worth of Romano Cheese and a nearly muted amount of Red Sea Salt (I only knew it was there - or should be - by the menu). Creative? Yes. But unimpressively so. 

I tried another 4 items and could drag this on just to beat the hell out of the kitchen but there is no point in that, right? They did have one item I did enjoy, so let us move on to the positive...

The Porterhouse Teasers were legitimately a solid contender in the art of Steak and I love that they force the patrons (or at least try) to enjoy them at Medium Rare. A perfectly seared New York Strip is mated with Applewood Smoked Sea Salt & Garlic Butter and served with superb presentation. Salty, savory, and oh-so-juicy. There was absolutely nothing wrong with this Tapas offering. 

Look, I think the ownership is doing big things and love the fact that they are pushing forward-thinking concepts in Carmel. That said, my self-described snobby palette was less than blown away and perhaps that is my own issue to tackle.

As far as Tapas/Gastropub/Wine Bars go, I have done much better.

A Chef inspired menu that celebrates the flavors of California's central coast. 

Walking into The Lark felt pleasantly familiar to me. From the interior to the indoor and outdoor seating areas and even the long Bar beckons memories from Los Angeles's highly praised Bestia. The menu is served a la carte family style - anyone in Orange County would instantly think of Santa Ana's Playground. If you are being compared to restaurants such as these, you are obviously getting something right. And, just as these direct comparisons also have, The Lark employs the European seating arrangements I so deplore as fellow diners seem to be sitting literally in your lap which can come with unintended consequences. More on that later.

The Lark showcases the work of Executive Chef Jason Paluska formerly of Anchor & Hope and Michael Mina's RN74 fame. The menu is broken up into segments highlighting the ingredients being employed. Think: From the Land, From the Sea, From the Farm, et al. 2 to 3 orders should feed a table of two and naturally the bigger the crowd the more you will order. Prices range from $7.00 to $40.00 per plate and there is are ample Wine, Craft Beer, and Mixology options for those ready to imbibe. 

Our table kicked off dinner with the Rosemary & Brown Butter Cornbread that is served with Aleppo Chile Honey Butter and has a welcome saltiness to it thanks to the generous use of Sea Salt. The crumble was perfect and with the Bread being served in a cast iron pan you know the bottom is nice and browned. 

If you are a fan of Pasta see no further than The Lark's Hand Cut Pappardelle which boasts English Peas, Hen of the Wood Mushrooms, Sugar Snap Peas, Piedmont White Truffle, Pine Nuts, and Parmesan shavings. The balance of this Pasta is incredible - no worries about the overuse of Truffle so common in the last few years - each ingredient is well represented. I wouldn't think to order Pasta at a Gastro, but I will going forward. 

There was no way I would leave The Lark without being able to say I have tried their 72 Hour Marinated 8 ounce Prime Flat Iron which came heavily suggested by the concierge at the Hotel I stayed at in Santa Barabra and it was the easily the star of the meal. The thick cut Steak is prepared to an expert Medium-Rare and served with Caramelized Gigante Beans, grilled Zucchini & Spring Onion, a confit of Heirloom Tomato, crispy Sweet Peppers, and a Black Garlic 'Bordelaise' to dip the Steak in to take things to the next level. This offering really shows off the culinary chops the kitchen exhibits and is a must try if you find yourself in the Funk Zone of downtown Santa Barabra. 

The meal was fantastic, of that, there is no question. The only downer was the aforementioned European-style seating. I get it - this is to encourage you to engage with those around you (or a lousy way to squeeze in an extra table or two on the floor) - but the fact is I don't always want to know those I am dining amidst. Case in point: at the table next to mine sat a couple of the ugliest, rude, and ignorant diners I may have ever experienced. They were talking down the kitchen, the city of Santa Barabra, and those around them throughout their visit and because I was 2 feet away from their conversation I was forced to listen to the constant flow of negativity. I even asked for the check early just to make the mindless drivel come to an end. 

Look, if you know you are an unpleasant and relatively unhappy person just do not travel or dine out. It is better for everyone involved. 

Obviously, the world's douchebags are no fault of the kitchen but being forced to endure those at neighboring tables almost outshined the cuisine itself. If this may be an issue for you, it may be worth the wait to secure one of the 3 booths available. That will be my strategy upon return. 

The Lark is easily the best Gastropub concept I have enjoyed in the Central Coast.

Bar Louie is a great spot for cocktail and a all game when visiting the financial area of Nashville. 

I found myself in the center of The Gulch area with co-workers who demanded we find a lively bar with stiff drinks and a friendly crowd to watch the NFL playoffs at and it was settled on that Bar Louie would be the perfect venue. Bar Louie suited our needs perfectly. Nearby free parking (unheard of in The Gulch) can be had at the adjacent garage located mere feet away so don't bother with valet or fighting for street spots. 

The interior is handsome, smart, and modern plus the service is top notch. We nestled into the lounge seats that offered excellent sight lines to the numerous flat screens located throughout the bar and put in our drink orders and immediately started to decompress from a long day of break out sessions, networking, and group projects. Our waitress made sure that no needs went unattended to and that the glasses remained full during the visit and made excellent recommendations for restaurants in the area. 

Bar Louie is a sure shot watering hole if you are looking for an upscale spot in the southern end of Nashville's downtown.

Is Carmel, Indiana the last place you think of when it comes to phenomenal Pizza? That is for good reason. 

I was recently in the area on business and when I checked into my hotel at 9 pm I knew that finding a decent bite at that hour would be challenging. Faced with deciding between Convivio and a neighboring Mexican restaurant I reasoned to myself that I would be more disappointed with the latter since I am from Southern California. I think I was dead wrong.

Located in the center of a newly erected and monstrous strip mall on Spring Mill Road, you will probably enjoy the cleanliness of the surfaces and suburban-Italian kitsch of Convivo's interior along with their friendly Midwestern servers throughout your experience. The menu is large and offers handmade Pasta, Pizza, and artisan Entrees along with a notable Wine list and ice cold Peroni on draught (for a pretty penny). Wanting something quick and easy I went with my Pie standby, the illustrious Margherita. It took roughly 10 minutes for the Pizza to make itself to me. 

For the record; Convivo does have an in-house Pizza hearth that they fire the Pies in and a group of amiable cooks manning it that had my expectations up, but sadly I would be in for a great deal of disappointment. Their Margherita is a simple, classically prepared number featuring Tomato Sauce, Mozzarella Cheese, and fresh Basil on top of a handmade Dough. All the of ingredients seemed to be of superlative quality as well. But, it just wasn't meant to be...

The dough itself was laughably undercooked/soggy with zero char to be detected which is a real shame considering they are using said hearth to begin with. The Tomato Sauce hardly made the grade in the flavor department thanks to a scant use of Garlic and left the Mozzarella as soloist in the flavor profile unless you bit into one of 3 Basil leaves. Once the Pizza cooled and the Cheese coagulated, there was no vestige of their sauce in any bite. Convivio is my early favorite for worst Pie in 2017. 

I am aware it can be argued that I came on an off night for the kitchen or perhaps my Pizza cook was in training but man - that was a very, very poorly executed Pizza - and since I am only in Indy once a year, this is a solid 2-star affair in this Yelper's eyes for life.

Scotty's Brewhouse is a great place to grab a cold one in downtown Carmel. 

I stopped in Scottys Brewhouse with at least a dozen of rowdy coworkers on a busy Thursday night to catch an NFL game and a light buzz. Scotty's came through on both accounts. The service was spectacular; our server seemed to be on his A-game through the night. For a watering hole Scotty's makes high marks.

As far as the culinary offerings: I only tried the nachos which were a standard affair that was better than stadium nachos but offered no surprises and once the cheese hardened became boring, if not entirely lifeless. 

I don't know when my travels will bring be back to Carmel but I would be happy to have another craft brew while taking in a game at Scotty's.

I love donuts and really wanted to love this place, but I can't now.  The first thing you smell when you walk in is greasy oil smell, this almost made me walk out.  You can actually smell it on your clothing when you leave3.  I realize they are new and still have things to work out.  The French toast donut was an over cooked brick! It was hard to even break in half as a cake donut that is shameful.  The frosting had great flavor though.  The Capt'n Crunch one had good vanilla flavor, but as a raised donut was oily.  Lastly, we tried the Samoa donut, it was great and the only reason for a second star.  The devils food donut was soft and cakey and topping were very flavorful.  We will try again in a few months, I really do want to love them.

We've wanted to try this place for a long time, so when my wife said she wanted fried chicken for her birthday dinner.  We knew where we were going.  We started with fried okra and hush puppies.  OMG! Those hush puppies were so flavorful.  We both enjoyed the cornmeal crusted okra.  I've never had, but really enjoyed.  For dinner, she ordered the fried chicken dinner with mashed potatoes and macaroni & cheese.  I ordered the fish dinner with catfish, sweet potatoes, red beans & rice.  Seriously, there isn't one thing to complain about. The chicken was juicy and the catfish crispy perfection.  I could've eaten a whole bowl of the red beans and rice.  I am so grateful for a birthday dinner that wasn't ruined by service or food.  Our waitress, sorry no name tag and it wasn't on our bill either, was GREAT!  A young lady with dark hair, huge smile on her face.  She was very attentive and friendly.  The owner was out greeting patrons, but didn't make it to our table, still good to see.  We finished up our meal with an order of beignets with warm  maple syrup.  Thank you for such a great experience.  We live in the neighborhood and will definitely return!

Terrible staff and management. Food is decent.

 I have eaten at The Fat Hen twice now.  My first experience was ok, I ordered the Chicken Pot Pie and was told they were out of that dish and that they were serving Chicken n' Dumplings instead.  Since I love both I opted for the Dumplings.  They were  good but portion size is small and overpriced ($16 for lunch). 

Upon returning over a month later I tried to order the Pot Pie again and was given the same story of "we are out but are serving Dumplings instead".  Again, I ordered the dumplings.  When my food finally came about 45 min later the presentation was laughable.  There were literally 2 miniature dumplings on the miniature cast iron skillet they serve it in and very little chicken.  Without taking a bite I called the waiter over to take a look...he said he'd speak to the chef.  He came back 10 min later and said "I spoke to the chef and he said he put 4 or 5 dumplings in there". (??!?!)  First of all, NO HE DIDN'T.  Secondly, is that considered a generous amount?? 4 or 5??  How about at least doubling that before you try to justify charging $16 for a lunch portion. 

He then said he'd speak to a manager.  Never happened.  He dropped the check at the table 5 min later without adjusting the bill.  I asked if he bothered to speak with her and he said "no she's busy but you can talk to her if you want."  This was the rudest most clueless waiter I have ever encountered.  

I left hungry and fuming.  I called and asked to speak to the manager.  Someone by the name of Juliet answered, listened to my complaint and apologized profusely.  Without telling her who my server was she said "I know exactly who you're talking about, he's had several complaints"....if that's the case why hasn't he been let go??  She then asked for my email and said she would send out a gift certificate right away.  It's been several days and still no g.c.  I even called to remind them yesterday and gave them the email address again in case it was misspelled.  Still nothing....

Avoid this place.  I wonder if they even take the time to read these reviews because CLEARLY there is a general consensous that the service is awful.  Get it together Fat Hen!  You're making a horrible impression in a town known for great restaurants.

Boys night out, hard to believe this place just opened as they are in a groove already.  Great location in Da' Gulch; if you live in the building thank whoever brought you Prima!

Appetizers
Lobster gnocchi was a nice play on mac n cheese. Just enough lobster to make ya happy. The gnocchi is really a pasta shaped like gnocchi so don't expect the potato texture to melt in your mouth; it's semolina based made inhouse.

Octopus was cooked to perfection with just enough kick to make you notice it but not so much that it destroyed the plate. I could have ate the other seven tentacles.

Main Course
We both ordered the lamb osso bucco. If you're Italian you know it's either HIT or MISS; there is no in between. This plate was a lil' bingo. The waiter had me worried when he brought out the knives; thankfully we didn't need them. If it was Nonna's house I'd be sucking the marrow out of the bone but this ain't the place. Spinach side was perfect. 

Dessert
I had a macchiato and the espresso was very good. They use coffee from Crema also downtown. We whacked up a pistachio thingy with white chocolate, vanilla mousse, and a cookie bottom. Great with the coffee. 

Wine List
I bought my own because the list wasn't available online but they have some fairly priced selections from all over the globe that will certainly continue to grow. 

Service
Spectacular and they are open a week. Very knowledgeable staff who were in total sync. Black or White napkins sir? Complimentary bottled water? First impressions! Some delays and gaps in the timing but that was expected for a new restaurant and were minor. Kudos to my paisane Angelo who is the GM we remembered from Kayne Prime. This guy is a pro.

Cost  was under $70 a person without drinks (soup to nuts) which is more than reasonable for this caliber of dining experience. - YOU GET WHAT YOU PAY FOR. The only negative - the decor is well done but the high ceilings remove some of the ambiance. Sinatra sounds like he's singing in Hoboken. The huge chandelier helps. The bar should be closer to the front door. Just sayin'

Observation not directed at Prima specifically
Maybe I eat out too much but the menus are becoming repetitive in Nashville.The menu choices are very limited and basically the same in every restaurant but with the 'chef's take'. I miss the list of 'specials' in New Jersey restaurants. If you visit a Nashville restaurant 3-4 times you basically ran the menu. Now what? Start eating the same thing over and over or look for a new restaurant?  Perhaps it's all geared towards tourists? I dunno. Hence no 5 star ratings yet.

Okay, okay, I realize that finding Mexican food in Tucson is as easy as...sweating in July. Maybe you're even a little tired of it. But once in awhile, you have to admit to getting that certain hankering for a hot, steamy, burn the roof of your mouth enchilada. If you have extra time, and extra gas in your car then make the drive and get yourself here. 
Place is small, almost always full and not the greatest to look at but the food is reasonably priced (figure if you have the $ for extra gas than you won't mind spending an extra dollar or two for good food) and delicious. Family owned and operated well (meaning execution and service is good). 
Get the enchiladas. Get the enchiladas. Get the enchiladas. Well I actually get a small $3.50 shredded beef burrito but I get it enchilada style for $1.50 more. The above mentioned enchilada sauce is pretty awesome if you couldn't guess.
If you're a local (to the Ajo/Kinney area) like me, takeout specials are super cheap and so good. Don't think tacos travel well so I don't recommend them if you have far to take them. Wait, I suppose if you spent all your $ on gas to get here, then you could eat them in the car??
Word to the wise: they'll give you a hot salsa and a mild. Mix the two for a perfect medium.

Well, well , well.. They say 3rd times a charm , in this instance they are right. We really wanted a cappuccino after yoga so, we popped in again at Falora and were happily surprised . Great service , great drink & a spoon & sugar free sweetener ! Yay!

Come if you love a dark, mysterious ambiance 
Come if you love immaculate service 
Come if you love mouth watering dishes and fresh seafood 
Come if you love jazz
Come if you are trying to impress a date 
Come if you want to sit at a bar and meet people 
Come if you love leather, wine, oysters, creme brûlée, a changing menu, a kick ass beet salad, interesting food combinations , not being disappointed!

First night in New Orleans and we had a wonderful dinner. Our server was attentive and the sommelier was inviting and very knowledgeable. We bought several bottles of wine, and were delightfully impressed with a wine from Oregon! Who would have thought!  The bread is SO good, loved the meatballs app and a spicy sausage served in a mini castiron pan was fantastic ! The dinner portions are small but SO flavorful and delicious.
I had the penne pesto and would highly recommend that one. The catch of the day was good. We had a great experience. The unicorn made from driftwood is beautiful, the ambiance is modern chic with an amazing playlist. Great for group dinner, date night and work dinner. Will definitely be back!

Made reservations as a group of 10 to celebrate and enjoy New Orleans, we had an amazing dinner the night before at  another restaurant so we were ready to eat and enjoy. We were greeted and seated upstairs. 
After ordering 3 bottles of wine, cocktails and apps we were ready to order dinner. The oysters left little to be desired as did the bread. That excitement quickly faded as we were served 3 bowls of lukewarm gumbo. The salads were ok, I had a shrimp salad that consisted of 4 shrimp smothered  in a peppercorn honey mustard dressing- the shrimp were cold and mushy- I'll pass. Right as dinner was being served, the waitress made an appearance. She offered to exchange the gumbo for fresh hot ones. ( what happened to the server being visible, a touch back after the durst bite)
The dinner entrees came out almost WARM.... the fish entrees were good, the duck was nice and fatty as duck usually is, the meat dishes( sirloin or tenderloin) was not too good. The request to have them cooked Med rare and rare failed- one was even charred black so we returned it. The food was almost warm which meant it was sitting in the window. So much for having it made to order. 
    *I pulled the waitress to the side and inquire about the lousy service, her response was along the lines of " I wouldn't eat the food here, people come here for our wine".
I was shocked that she was so blunt. What a waste of time and money. The tab was over $700 for a mediocre experience in the 2nd oldest restaurant in New Orleans. Never saw a manager. All of our dealings was with a server and  the 
" wine expert".  Earlier we asked for separate checks for each couple. That didn't happen.  In fact it took close to THIRTY MINUTES to square away the check in which we all blindly gave our CC and left. The meek apology didn't help. This dinner and experience was so far gone, nothing could have saved it. I would NOT  and DO NOT recommend this establishment.  This place lacks communication, ownership and dedication to providing a good dining experience .  
" I wouldn't eat the food here" - server.

This used to be my favorite restaurant in town. Out of town guests? Take them to Winslow's Home! The food is consistent and the atmosphere is excellent.

Why the 3 stars? Their service sucks!!! Their wait staff is incredibly unhelpful and borderline rude. We've had three recent run-ins that have made me think twice about eating here. I recommend a staff retreat where they watch customer service videos all weekend. Their attitude towards families with kids is unacceptable. No high chairs? This is a neighborhood restaurant not the Four Seasons downtown.

I am disabled and utilize a Service Dog to assist me with my disability. I went to MOM's with a friend who also is disabled and uses a Service Dog. We were told that we had to "fill out paperwork" and they wanted to see those ID's to show they were certifird. There is no certification for Service Dogs under the ADA. Nor can they ask to see any documentation. 

CERTIFICATION AND REGISTRATION
Q17. Does the ADA require that service animals be certified as service animals?
A. No.  Covered entities may not require documentation, such as proof that the animal has been certified, trained, or licensed as a service animal, as a condition for entry.

The manager comes over and says that he has no idea where he is going to put us. He failed to ask us where we would like to be seated rather said he has to call the owner. He was obviously upset that he had to let the dogs into the restaurant. He finally got a round table from the back and sat us there which was nice. 

Then to make matters worse, the kitchen got my order wrong. I ordered a plain hamburger with no cheese. When it came out it had cheese on it. I sent it back. It returns, it was obviously that the chef just scrapped the cheese off the top and flipped the burger over. A perfect situation for someone that allergic to cheese. 

The food quality is outstanding but costumer service this visit was HORRIBLE!

You sell Goods to Tanners and it's not their fault but your last batch of scones I got three huge ones. I should have trusted my instinct and no that scones are not huge. I bought them anyway but they were disgusting too much baking soda or baking powder is what made them too big and they tasted like glue whoever baked them should have ditched them and started over. I am not blaming tanners as they are simply a distributor. I am blaming Lochel's because you know better.

Dined at Muriel's on our last night in New Orleans. It was meant to be a special dinner. Highly recommended, we landed a table and unfortunately, that was the highlight of the evening. Our appetizers were delicious but at first bite of my chicken cassoulet, I discovered that the chicken was under cooked and by the time it was returned cooked, the vegetables were soggy and ruined. The experience continued to go down hill when my husband discovered that two of the three beef medallions he ordered were on the very raw side of cooked. So the tempo of the evening and the experience were lost. There was a frenetic feeling to the dining room with wait staff rushing everywhere and the final special moment was the crash we heard from the kitchen, as we finished paying our high price bill. Very much of a let down.

Two  things -- 

1. I LOVE that because of 'Creed' Max's is finally getting the love and respect that it deserves
2. I HATE that now -- it's a tourist attraction.

BUT, overall the corner of Broad and Erie is the best cheese steak you're gonna get in Philly period! 

The reality is that this is not your typical, hipster, free range, organic BS. It's connected to a neighborhood bar and the service is as such. Just go in, get your steak, turn down the Muslim oils when they try to sell them to you, and leave.

I guarantee you'll be a happier camper!

HORRIBLE CUSTOMER SERVICE!!!! 
We just got lunch to go through the drive thru. When we got home, three of our five orders were completely wrong! My husband called back to let the management know. He spoke to two people and we were not offered compensation or anything. They wanted us to drive back the food, which we told them would take us 20-30 minutes to get back. Finally they told my husband that HE shouldn't be picky!!!! They tried to make it sounds like it was OUR fault that they messed up our order. 
This has happened almost every time we use the drive thru. Normally we would brush it off because the food is good, but this is unacceptable. 
I WOULD NOT RECOMMEND NACHOMAMA'S BECAUSE OF THE TERRIBLE MANAGEMENT AND SERVICE.

If were possible to give negative star reviews this is the one time I would actually do it. Baja Sharkeez and Tara blew it, BIG TIME.

I had a bachelorette party of 14 in town so I called a few days before to make reservations as the website boasted "Decorated and reserved seating and complimentary appetizer platters". I called Tara GM/Promoter..?? And she took down all my info for a reservation. I was very specific about having it on the patio because the weather would be so nice. She assured me everything would be ready on our arrival, and she would call me the day of to sort out a few details. I didn't hear from her the day of so I called and spoke to a young guy, he said Tara was busy but they had us down.

Where do I start? We cabbed it there, so the first group arrived about 20 minutes before my group. When they got there the seating was inside, (not on the patio as requested) and the 20 TV's were BLARING sports was so loud you couldn't talk/hear over them. The "Decorations" consisted of a few balloons. When the girls told them we were supposed to be seated outside they were met with eye rolls and sighs. They moved the balloons to filthy tables on the patio (think sticky spots from drinks, salt covering everything, cigarette butts on tables..) and left.. 

I arrived about 20 minutes later and walked out to the patio.. I was disappointed in the shabby decorations and dirty tables, but when I saw no one had drinks, disappointment grew into puzzled curiosity. I asked the ladies and they told me no one had been out to see them since they got there.. I walked in to the bar and stood there for about 3 minutes while the people (at least 4 of them) chatted to each other without making eye contact with me. When I finally got someone to come over I asked them to send a server outside and was rudely advised we were to walk inside to order. (You could have told us that 20 minutes ago jackass). 

I asked for Tara and stood there another 5 minutes or so, she hadn't come out so I went back out to the patio and we made the group decision to leave. All 14 of us stated walking out and on our way out Tara finally appeared. 

Before I could finish explaining what happened she let me know it was a no service patio. That's not the point, the point is no one told us and we sat there for over 20 minutes with at dirty, sticky tables. You just lost the business of 14 people who would have spent a good amount in your bar..

To her credit she called later to apologize and asked us to come back, but at that point we were already seated and dropping cash at a much nicer place that actually acknowledged us when we entered. 

If you're considering having a party at Baja Sharkeez save your time and go somewhere else. The place was unprepared, the ambiance is set for obnoxious jocks, the overall setting was filthy dirty and the service.. Well you read the review. Big Fail.

9 Roses is always my go-to for Vietnamese home cooked dishes. My friends even make the drive to the Westbank from Metairie, Kenner, etc, some visiting several times a week! You can't beat the flavor-filled home-y dishes! 

What I recommend:

-Bo Nuong Vi: A tabletop grill for cook meats of your choice (beef, squid, shrimp) in which you can wrap into your own custom made springrolls. Served with herbs and vegetables

-Bo Tai Chanh: A beef tataki dish, served with herbs, thinly sliced lemons and onions and a "mam nem" sauce. SO DELICIOUS. Probably my favorite appetizer here.

-Suon Rim Man: Sizzled pork riblets in a brown sauce. This is my son's absolute favorite. It is eaten with rice. He loves to take the sauce and put it on his rice.

-Canh Chua: a sweet and sour soup eaten with rice. It can be served with catfish (my favorite), shrimp, or with just the vegetables. The soup has tomatoes, celery, a sponge-like celery-like vegetable, bean sprouts, pineapples, and a couple other items. 

-Ca kho to: Vietnamese braised catfish in a clay pot. It has a brown sauce, a LITTLE similar to the Suon Rim Man. They're similar, yet so different, and both so delicious. This dish is also eaten with rice.



Every dish here is really good. I haven't had a dish I haven't liked, but those above are my staples, that I get at almost every sitting. It's a family-style restaurant, so groups will easily be accommodated here. There are booths as well and smaller tables, so a dinner for two is fine too, but you just wouldn't be able to order all the dishes to try!

Love this place, since I was a kid. Still a regular. Oh, and I'm Vietnamese. That has to mean something! =D

Holy Shawarma-oly! 

Can you say delicious!?!? And suchhhh a bang for your buck (portion and quality is great) so how can you go wrong!?

The restaurant in clean and sparkly and shiny. Very modern decor and even very modern technology! They're definitely doing things right. 

Had the Lebanese tea here and it's probably the best I've ever had.

Got the combination platter with gyro (ding ding, this one's a winner!!!) and beef (good but too dry for my liking). It came with a side of hummus and a side Greek salad! Yummy and such a good portion for the $! 

Also tried the chicken wrap, which was recommended by the worker. This was a huge tongue and tummy tickler!!! The garlic sauce is definitely what takes it off the chain! NOMS!

I will definitely come back here. I had it for lunch---- should I return for dinner!? Stay tuned ...

It's been a month and a half into this new year of 2017, but I think I've hit my personal "favorite new restaurant of the year" already, and I don't think it will change! If another restaurant this year beats Trinity, it would be a VERY hard feat. The food, service, ambiance, everything, the whole package ---it is just SOLID. I would give Trinity 6 stars if I could. 

A group of friends and I decided to throw a surprise birthday dinner for a friend here. The hostess was very welcoming and accomodating. The staff as a whole was excellent! Every staff member we encountered was extremely friendly. Our server constantly checked on us. The bartender/mixologist tweaked a couple of the menu drinks and made them even better! The manager also came in and cleared dishes as well as checked in on how we were enjoying it. The chef saw that we were struggling to take a group selfie picture and asked to help. Everything about this restaurant was just great.

We ordered many small plates and a few entrees and shared it, family style. Each plate had a presentation that was as aesthetically pleasing on the eyes as it was on the palate!!!

SMALL PLATES WE ORDERED:

-Oysters --- there are several ways they prepare oysters (I think 5 ways). We ordered the raw, which was accompanied by a very delightful mignonette! It was so tasty that we were just loading it on top of the oyster! We also ordered the smoked oysters, which were garnished with deviled eggs, horseradish, & cajun caviar. ---YUM. 

-Bone marrow was delicious! It is topped with light and crispy bread crumbs! We ordered 2!

-Beef Tartare - I really enjoyed this here. It was minced finely and was served with white beans, crackers, & an itty bitty tabasco sauce.

-Crawfish & Fontina Beignets with a green tarragon aioli -- friends loved this. I didn't care too much about the beignets, but the aioli was delicious!

-Pommes Frites with Butter Milk Aioli ********* This. Is. My. Favorite. Fry. Ever. Okay, I am a fry-lover. But these win the gold medal of the city! They came out super hot and stayed hot with the container it was served it. There's something about these fries. They're cooked just right...crispy in some areas, but was sooooo creamy and well seasoned. I don't know what they do to their potatoes..... and the sauce. Oh, i love the sauce. I love condiments. I live for condiments really. And this sauce. I'm drooling.

-Crispy Pork Belly -- There was a pretty strong consensus among our group that this was probably the best pork belly we've ever had. It was crispy as you took the bite, and it just melted in your mouth after. 

-Duck Liver Pâté ---- I enjoyed this dish and all the garnish it had! If you're not pate lover, you can probably skip this dish. 

ENTREES WE ORDERED:

-Seared Scallops with smoked corn puree, roasted mirliton, pine nuts --- scallops were seared perfectly with just the perfect amount of color and crisp! I wasn't too crazy about the puree because of the smokey flavor. 

-Grilled Short Rib--- I didn't try this dish, but the guys devoured it. 

-Grilled Wagyu Strip Loin --- This Wagyu beef was so tender, like butter. Of all the entrees, this is a must!!!! 

-potatoes au gratin --- at the end of the dinner, we were so stuffed, but everyone had room for a spoonful of this creamy potato side dish, just so none of it went to waste! 


If you haven't been to Trinity, I highly suggest you put it at the top of your list! You won't be disappointed!!! We had such an amazing experience dining here, and honestly I can't wait to go back!!



P.S.---- There's also an upstairs section with a small bar that looks like a perfect place to throw a small dinner party! It even has access to the balcony!!!! Maybe rehearsal dinners?!

Made it just in time for their soft opening to claim the last bowls being served. Yup. They completely sold out. 

Although I felt bad for the many that came after us who had to be turned away, I respect Nomiya much more for it. For them, it means each bowl they serve is top quality, top ingredients. It shows the pride in their work. For us customers, it means that we can count on each bowl always being fresh, scrumptious, & satisfying. 

The staff is quick to greet & super friendly. There's nothing amiss in the service, that's for sure! & service can definitely make or break the whole dining experience for me. 

The vibe & atmostphere is super cool here too. Very neat decor (lots of thought into details). There's a standing bar along one wall, for those who choose to stand and eat. There's also an option for sitting.

Fiance got the spicy broth & I got the regular. I love both & I think I'd get half/half next time! Spicy is pretty spicy! You can always add spice to your own liking!

I think this is the best ramen the entire South of the U.S. has to offer! I mean, if the owner is going to move to Japan to learn the art of ramen, this bowl of ramen is the closest you'll get to being in Japan yourself! If you're a true ramen lover, you'll appreciate every burst of flavor Nomiya has to offer. Everything is done perfectly. 

Tip: add the garlic oil. Yums.

Also, there is no liquor license just yet. I'm not sure when or if there will be one. Is it BYOB? I'm not sure. I'll have to ask. I forgot amidst my hypnotizing meal. 


To all Pastafarians:
After finishing every slurp of the savory broth & upon completion of my bowl, I realized I have truly been called by the Flying Spaghetti Monster & touched by His noodly appendage. Thank you, your Noodliness for the amazing meal opportunity here in NOLA. R'amen!

This place NEVER fails us!

i've come here a few times. Each time, the group I've gone with try almost everything on their menu and we all share pieces of our entrees so every one can have a taste. 

Everything is amazzzinngggg!

My favorite:
1. SHRIMP & GRITS! The best in the city! The best I've ever had! The best EVER! Nothing compares. Cafe Amelie's shrimp and grits were the first I ever had, and I fell in love. I thought all shrimp and grits were the same. I went to the festivals, other restaurants, and all have failed, most probably because Cafe Amelie has set the bar so high that I've always been disappointed since. After countless failed attempts of finding a decent "shrimp and grits," I've finally chosen to not order it anywhere at all anymore and if I really want some, I would just make a special trip to get them here. THE BEST. My son inhales it in minutes. 

2. Tuna. Cooked to PERFECTION.  The portion was quite filling also!!! 

3. Salmon. Also very good, but the tuna won! Just by a little...

I love this place. This is a place I would definitely recommend to anyone, a native born New Orleanian or a visitor. Such fresh food, a fresh atmosphere, and good time!!!

RACIST BARTENDER!!! DO NOT GO HERE IF YOU'RE ASIAN! 

The bartender made up some elaborate story how my ID was bending so it was fake, and how my friends' IDs weren't! What a bunch of BS because I'm freaking 26! So she starts cussing me out and bending my ID and telling me to GTFO! I know it's a bar on Bourbon St, but YOU should never cuss out at customers!

She took my ID to the back room, probably to scan it or something. The security guard and the other bartender saw what was going on and they tried to calm her down but she was just out of control! 

When she gave back my ID it was all BENT, and she didn't even apologize! I was so upset because that was my driver's license and the identification I was going to use to fly back home!  

She should be fired for what she did! I knew she was racist when she ignored my friends and I was serving other customers that came after us!

What an unlikely place to find culinary perfection.  The memory of the bumpy parking lot where I had to turn around that almost took the underbody off of my car is still fresh, but a cup of Chicken Florentine healed that and many other small emotional wounds...  Creamy without a hint of a clot.  Smooth, perfect amount of salt.  Fresh spinach that looks like it was only allowed to just wilt.  Noodles at the perfect degree of firmness.  

The Blintzes with apples, just like the soup, contained nothing that I could identify that was not just made from scratch, including simmered cinnamon apple slices and cottage cheese filling and, of course, the crepes.  

The hard part of any cooking, especially commercially, is not to overdo the salty, the sweet and the obvious flavors.  Mother's Table, you succeeded and got a loyal customer today.  Looking forward to trying six pages of omelets, pancakes, crepes, sandwiches and salads.

Two journeys to Bluebeard proved to be my favorite kind - a mini vacation from reality into quirky atmosphere spiced with gastronomical surprises at every turn.

"Dark and stormy" cocktail boasted home-made ginger beer of such strength of ginger flavor that after one sip you could feel the burn travel up your sinuses and down your esophagus (great feeling, but you must be a fan of ginger to stomach it).

The server helped us navigate through cheese choices - from local to regional, all proved a great start.  Grilled octopus provided an answer to: "So, what's the taste difference between calamari and octopus?" (Octopus was less chewy and with more concentrated flavor).

Orecchiette with crab won my favor out of shared plates of this pasta, quail and scallops, but each one was excellent.  Usually, if one dish delights with innovative flavor, I am already  happy.  At Bluebeared there were no "blands" at all!  

Even at the end of the night, my over-impressed  and over-indulged palate was won over once again by the crown jewel - bread pudding.  The reaction of everyone at the table after the first bite was similar - our eyes opened wide and small muffled sounds started escaping.  

As a finishing touch, I do appreciate a strong fresh coffee at the end of dinner.  The results are spotty - anywhere from a surprised "OK, I'll start some..."  to lunch-old burnt bitter brew.  At Bluebeard - the simplest of solutions - a nice French press with a roast of great balance.

Every one of the five stars well earned.

Reading Room has a really interesting theme going through out. The menus are binded into old copies of Shakespeare books, and then cups look like (or are) candle holders. The meals on the menu are separated by chapters. 

Looking around is pleasing as well because the decor is interesting, and the staff are nice. There's a garden outside, and I'm not sure if we are to infer that they grow their own vegetables that they serve there. No one said as much, so I don't know. 

I had a dish that was dark and white chicken meat cooked into these medallion things. It was served with corn, some glorious kind of sauce, and two slivers of zucchini. The meal was absolutely tasty. 

Normally, when I destroy a plate of food, I show off that fact (because being chubby is fun), but here is where I explain why they've lost a star for me. Yes, I did murder my food, but only because it was an absolutely tiny portion. Now if that's worth $25 to you then by all means, come here because the food is really good.  But if you broke as a joke, stay away.

If you haven't been here, change that now. Right now. 

This place is wonderful. The food is very good. So far I have tasted their pizza, garlic knots, and gyros. Wonderful! As if this wasn't enough, they serve craft beer! There's nasty old domestic drafts too, but lots of craft beer. 

They have insane happy hour deals from 4-6. The deal includes pizza slices, wings, and beer. There are a bunch of other fun things like trivia nights, too. 

The best part of all of this is that Brad the bartender is a pretty awesome dude. I love this bar!

Beer Revolution is the best place in town for craft beer.  What I am most stoked about is that they don't really care to keep boring macrobrews like Stella Artois, Guinness etc. on their menu.  Let's start of with the beer list.  I've been here about 5 times now and I quite like the list.  For the most part though, the breweries they carry seem to be awesome. They rarely have the best beer of each of those breweries, but that's okay. They mix and match it well. Also, the way they display their beer menu, like a flight arrivals/departure screen at an airport, is great.

The food is pretty decent but also quite pricey, in my opinion. I don't mind spending that money occasionally, because some of it is really good. The Bavarian pretzels are crazy good and an awesome side order to get. The blistered shishito peppers are divine, especially with the generously shaved dose of parmesan.  These sides are exactly what i'm looking for when I drink beer here. 

The pizzas are definitely above average. Many people love them a lot, but I still crave a chewier crust with more holes (basically higher temperature baking). Since they are not an exclusive pizza place, I must say that I am happy to order a pizza if I'm busy drinking (note, however, the calories do add up REALLY fast :D). 

All in all, it's a solid 4 star. Perhaps the best place in town for craft beer, but with expensive food, it's not a chill place to come once or twice a week because you'd be emptying your pockets faster than you'd notice.

Like everyone else says, no one from Philly actually consistently goes here. it's a tourist spot. The only time it's acceptable to go when you're actually from Philly is at 2am when you're drunk. The people are rude and the cheesesteaks are wayyy over priced. And btw not everyone from Philly talks like an idiot and doesn't know how to pronounce their "h" in with. The few times I've gone I make sure to accentuate the h when I've ordered...it always pissed them off.

And like you've been reading, they're racist and have no issues telling the world that and their stances on political subjects with all the signs and posters they have up the most popular being "this is america order in english". Like honestly get over yourself Bill O'Riley  the world doesn't care what your stance is on the country's immigration policies...stick to what you're good at which is selling over priced mediocre cheesesteaks. Douchebags.

This Cafe is across from the Prince Conti Hotel using the same driveway.  The morning we left, we decided to run in here and get a little bite to eat until we stopped for food on our journey.

This is a really cute little cafe!  I enjoyed checking out the decor while we waited for our to-go order.  It has graphic red and white printed art & what appears to be matching printed valances, and a huge cool looking framed picture on the wall above a fireplace.  

Don't come here if you are in a rush.  The service was really slow.  It took much longer to get our two crepes to-go than it should have!  The girl who took our order was rather put off that we showed up.  She really didn't want to be there and it was quite apparent.  Not a great way for customers to be treated first thing in the morning, or ever!!

We ordered a sweet crepe with Hazelnut Spread & Banana slices for my daughter and she said it was too sweet and didn't finish it.  I believe it was an okay crepe since she didn't say anything else about it.  I got the Spinach, Bacon and Egg Crepe and I did NOT like it at all.  I think it was the creamed spinach that was kind of gooey that I didn't like.  I can't really explain it very well, but maybe it wasn't fresh and it was very unappetizing.  Basically, I ate the egg and bacon with a little bit of the crepe.  I felt bad wasting the rest, but I just couldn't eat it!  I wouldn't order what I ordered again!

With the slow service to the not so great food, I will eat elsewhere.  This wasn't a cheap breakfast, either!  I'm so sorry, but from my experience, it seems like I am just about the only reviewer to disagree with the majority of Yelpers!

Walking from the hotel to find a good place for steaks, we asked a local horse & carriage driver for recommendations.  He suggested Tujague's and a couple other places.  We thought he said "Two Jacks".  The founders of this restaurant are Guillaume & Marie Tujague, from Bordeaux, France.

We passed Cafe du Monde and walked past this place because nobody was dining, the place was empty!  By the time we were done with dinner, there were plenty of people in the restaurant!  We decided to roll the dice and give it a go.  So glad we did!!  Such a great little place!  We thought it would be really expensive since they had white tablecloths & cloth napkins!  It was a little pricey, but we enjoyed ourselves!  ( www.yelp.com/biz_photos/tujagues-restaurant-new-orleans?select=XyEeBpvGKsnZF5TS7FMcMg#XyEeBpvGKsnZF5TS7FMcMg )

We were unsure of this place at first, but we settled in and were fine!  We were brought out 2 warm, medium sized loaves of french bread and butter, which our daughter was completely pleased with!  ( www.yelp.com/biz_photos/tujagues-restaurant-new-orleans?select=KHRNytAFBpeyixu6TSujyQ#97GDspCwyczo01Lj5HwPEg )

We decided on a Seared Jumbo Lump Crab Cake appetizer, it came with Tri-Colored Peppers and Ravigote Sauce & a small salad.  It was okay, but I think we were expecting it to be fried or baked well, not just seared (we overlooked that part of the description!).  We also ordered a Corn & Crab Bisque Soup which was perfect!  I really enjoyed this!!  The corn kernels sweetened the bisque and made for a nice texture as well.  

Then we thought we should take advantage of their 5 course meal by  adding on $25 to an entree. ( www.yelp.com/biz_photos/tujagues-restaurant-new-orleans?select=oQAsilMAT8S3ERguNkmxzQ#oQAsilMAT8S3ERguNkmxzQ )  So, we got the Gumbo, Brisket Appetizer, Entree, and Chocolate Pecan Pie.  The Gumbo was good, but it didn't compare to my husband's mother's gumbo!!  We really weren't a fan of the brisket.  It is a popular item, but we'd skip it next time.  The pie was very sweet!  I think we really were overdoing it with the dessert because we were stuffed by the time we got to it!  

Our daughter ordered the 8 oz Filet Mignon which came with mashed potatoes & veggies (squash).  The filet had an excellent char on the outside and was still nice and medium rare on the inside.  It was most definitely one of the best grilled & flavored steaks we've had (and we've eaten a lot of filet mignons)!!  If you ever come here, this is an item you really should order!

Hubby & I split a Blackened Shrimp Alfredo.  It was good but the shrimp had a bit too much salt for our taste!  Nothing too memorable, though.  

Since we almost always have leftovers, we asked for a to-go container.  When it arrived at the table, I noticed it had  "Who Dat?" on it.  Cute!  Who Dat fans!

One thing I noticed throughout the French Quarter is that the staff (waiters & chefs) are seen out in front of the restaurants hanging out!  At Tujague's, they walked right through the dining room, out the door (not to be used by guests), and were chatting away with people outside, as if they were on break.  Then, they'd come back in and tend to you.  It is a different culture, I suppose.

There is one guy at this place who is very hard to understand.  Our daughter had been searching for someone with a thick accent on our trip from CA to AL and finally found what she was looking for!

If we ever make it back to NOLA, I think we will definitely be back!  If only for another taste of that succulent filet mignon!

We went to Sea Salt last night to celebrate my husband's and one of our friend's birthdays. We had a lovely night in this beautiful venue with great service and delicious food. As this is a new restaurant to St. Pete and the Sundial, we knew it would be in high demand and expected it to be bustling and packed, which it was. But we enjoyed hanging out at the gorgeous marble bar and chatting while we waited for our table. The decor is very modern and eyecatching and the two story glass wine room (or whatever you call it) is a pretty cool feature in the middle of the restaurant.

For starters they brought the table a selection of sea salts (Hawaiian red, Himilayan pink, and one that was very sulfurous (?) and the tiniest bit gave a strong egg flavor...surprisingly good) along with bread and olive oil. We loved all of the salts. We also were brought a birthday surprise of a delicious huge tempura prawn for each of us. For the table to share we ordered the fried oysters (perfect, with a sort of corn relish), the octopus, and the foie gras fries. All were very good, but the foie gras fries were a definite stand-out. They were so golden crispy and just perfect topped with shaved parmesan, bits of fois gras, and an aioli. 

For our entrees two of us got the black grouper which is served with veggies and salted fingerling potatoes in a butter sauce. It was great it its buttery goodness. My husband got the salmon on a bed of lentils, which he said was not really that great. He thought the cut of salmon was sort of sub-par (like the little tail end), and just did not measure up to all of the other things we were trying. The other birthday boy got the red snapper which he said he enjoyed. 

For birthday desserts we shared the pistachio tiramisu, which I can not adequately describe in such a way to properly convey its awesomeness. It is like a bowl of creamy pistachio tiramisu with little crispy fried ladyfinger balls plopped on top. Man, that description is lame. There was also some sort of sweet dried fruit in there...raisins? plums? Whatever, the combination of the crispy balls and the creamy pistachio was just perfection. This dessert, along with the foie gras fries, were the two huge winners of the night in my opinion. The other dessert we all shared was the chocolate dome with caramel sauce, which any chocolate lover would adore. The dome was sort of like an oversized truffle with a chocolate mousse center, and the caramel sauce just took it over the top. Also in the bonus dessert category, all tables are served a heaping bowl of fresh warm cotton candy! And this does not even compare to the carnival cotton candy you've ever had. It was pure spun sugar heaven.

Of course Sea Salt is a pricey night out, but in our opinions it was worth it and we can't wait to go back and sample some of the many other enticing offerings on the menu. Thanks for a very nice evening Sea Salt!

We had to try the newest hottest place in St. Pete! Unfortunately it was a bit of a womp womp really. The two-story location is sprawling and chocked full of interesting food type items and gadgets, all extremely overpriced and most I had seen elsewhere such as at Fresh Market. There are multiple food-procuring stations throughout the Market, such as a grill for burgers, a fresh fish case, meat case, salad area, etc. The bakery and bar are upstairs. 

I had a custom salad with grilled salmon, which cost $13 (plus a $4 kombucha), and I have to admit I was pretty disappointed in my little $17 lunch. The grilled salmon seemed totally unseasonsed and the house-made blue cheese dressing didn't have much blue cheese flavor that I could detect. The kombucha was great. My husband had to wait forever in the grill line. If you go with a group of people, I don't see how everyone could actually get their food and be seated to eat together at the same time. Half of our party was done eating before my husband even got his food. The grill is the only area that seemed to have a huge line. 

We were very disappointed in the amount of items that were prepackaged to take home. We were hoping to buy a bunch of things to take home to make for dinner as well as some prepared side dishes. There really aren't many prepared side dishes. We got a small package of the pimento mac & cheese for my kids to try, but otherwise there was nothing that seemed like a suitable side dish to take home. The veggie selection was really pretty small and overpriced. We did buy some blue nose bass to grill up for dinner. It was on special for $12.95/lb., but rung up incorrectly as $14.95/lb at the register and that involved a hassle to get corrected. All of the other fish in the case was at least $20/lb.

I don't see Locale Market being a big destination for us in the future. I may browse all the tchotchkes the next time I happen to be at the Sundial, but it is not somewhere that I would make a point of returning to. But if money is no object and you don't really care about having a meal actually WITH your friends all at the same time, then check it out!
food was ight but served quick, fresh and hot. customer service could use some work so be prepared if you go.

I'm a little partial to my Chicago food as a native of the city. This place has it right though. Vienna beef hot dogs with the right fixings. The $5.25 price for a full-fledged Chicago dog is more than normal but totally good with me to get my fix when I need that taste of home. They have a wide range of speciality hot dogs to choose from as well.

I also got a gyro sandwich. I always forget to avoid feta on it but the meat was good and the flavor was pretty on point. Could have used a few less onions, no feta and more tzatziki but I'll get that right on my next order.

I will be back for sure to try some more of the sandwiches and the pizza. I am really hoping this place stays open forever so I can always enjoy my favorite Chicago foods in Reno.

I'm just reviewing the prices.

Honestly kbbq has been my favorite thing for YEARS! & let me tell you.

This type of food where I come from is usually all you can eat. The prices here are ridiculous. You'd save money buying all the meat you want at a Asian market.

I feel like the owner was trying to bring something new to Idaho and maybe thought everyone here has never heard of something like this but I posted a picture of an all you can eat kbbq menu for one of my fav places . You get a variety of meats for one price. I'll pass on this place  waiting for so long for absolutely nothing. If the prices were more reasonable I'd probably be a repeat customer but no thanks, doesn't seem like it's worth it to me ‍

I have mixed feelings about this place. I always sit down to eat and a server never comes to take my order. It has happened the last three times, I got up and walked to the counter to order yet they say to sit down and someone will be with me shortly. Don't come here with limited time on a lunch break unless you have a to-go order. 
The food is reasonable and yummy- I've had the pho and chicken pad thai and both did not disappoint.. The servings are huge! The menu is rather extensive and will accommodates all diets/allergies (GF/vegan). 
They do not accept American Express.

Not sure what's happening with my fellow Tucsonans rating this place so highly. 

BROADEN YOUR PIZZA HORIZONS or have your tastebuds checked...

For the people rating 5 stars then saying things like "it gets the job done" regarding your pizza craving...simply being edible doesn't warrant 5 stars. 

That being said I'm not above grabbing pizza in a pinch, $5 hot and ready anyone? But again, not going around rating them 4 or 5 stars.  

The inside is clean, spacious, counter where you order and where pizza is made is very Subway-esque. 
I don't like Subway, it grosses me out. 

The concept of being able to put whatever I liked on my pizza intrigued me. That combined with the positive yelp reviews and pictures depicting what looked like delicious brick oven style pizzas drew me in.

Those pictures are good angles. 

Have you ever been to Peter Piper Pizza?
Yeah, this is that pizza. 

Don't get me wrong, Peter Piper Pizza is not half bad. But 5 stars? Not so much.

First off, they spray the pizza dough with something that looks like pam and then flatten it in a tortilla press.

What?

My dining partner who spent his younger years working in places and LOVES, I repeat LOVES, pizza, saw that and just about walked out. 
The kid performing this skillful action didn't seem to be banging them out in record time or anything so what is the point of that?

When they asked what crust we would like (wheat or traditional), he made sure to ask for the traditional that was just placed on the pizza dough holder rack thing, so it wouldn't be dried out. 

The next steps are straight outta Chipotle/Subway territory with sauces, cheese, etc. We got regular sauce, mozz, pepperoni. Kept it simple so we could really get Pionic's pizza essence. 
We also ordered the Buffalo Chicken salad. 

The salad came out pretty much as soon as we sat down, dressing on the side. Not sure if it was ranch or blue cheese dressing, but it was straight up gelatinous in it's little cup and a pinky dip sample pegged it as low quality, cheap. 
I poured it over the salad and dug in. 
It was alright. 
Not something I'm going to crave or probably ever order again, but edible.

Edible seems to be Pionic's calling card.

The pizza came out a minute or two later. 

The swiftness seems to render the pizza sort of soggy. The bottom of the pizza was crisped just fine, but the sauce/cheese/pepperoni combination was sort of wet. 
I happen to live for when a pepperoni or two gets sort of crispy and chip-like on a pizza, there's zero chance of that happening with whatever method they're using, I assure you.  

A pet peeve of mine is when a pizza can't hold itself together. 
You pick up a slice and everything comes sliding off. 
We had one cheese and one topping and this happened with every piece, even after cooling off.
I'm not sure what causes this (didn't happen to ask my pizza connoisseur partner if he happened to know) but if people are loading up the toppings onto their build their own pizza, it's no doubt becoming a fork operation. 

I can see the appeal of this place I guess, it's cheap, slightly more variety than some pizzerias in terms of sauce/toppings. But that's about it.

There are better pizzas for cheaper, and there are better pizzas period within walking distance of this place. 

Is it just that it's quick that makes people rate this place so highly?

I'd rather wait 15 minutes on a pizza joint's plastic chair than have the pizza I had tonight in 5 seconds...but maybe that's just me?

Service was fine, teenage robots. Again, Subway-esque.

Unfortunately, nowadays, good buffets are hard to find. It's as difficult, if not more difficult than finding a decent guy. 

24.99 for dinner AYCE. 18% gratuity on groups of more than 6. 

::.From what I remember, December 29 dinner menu::.
Meat station: sausage, beef brisket, prime rib, chicken, broiled sirloin steak 
Salad station (I don't eat veggies so I can identify the species), cocktail shrimp 
Dessert station: cheesecake, chocolate cake, carrot cake, gelato (mango, strawberry, coconut, pistachio, chocolate, cookies and cream, cherry), macaroons (not macaron, there's a difference), raspberry custard tart
Asian station: beef/broccoli chow mein, eggroll, Tom yum soup, 
Italian station: lasagna, ravioli, fettuccini, pizza, Parmesan chicken 

All the food were ok... It was either under salted or over salted. Nothing really stuck out to me. Desserts were decent but even the gelato were plain in flavors. 

Got there at 5:45pm on a Tuesday, and there was a long line out the door already. Surprisingly it moved super fast but I think it was because we had a group of 12.

Nothing beats taco and watching people bat. Only in SoCal, only in SoCal. 

.::Food::.
Triple Play $9: choose any 3 tacos 
+Batter Up: Battered cod, cabbage, radish, cilantro, pico de gallo, east beach aioli, flavor tortilla. Probably my favorite one out of the three. Cod was nicely fried in the batter with a good kick of spice. All the flavors tied in nicely.
+Carne Asada: Marinated skirt steak, cabbage, pico de galllo, guacamole, queso fresco, and flour tortilla. Probably my second favorite. The steak was perfectly cooked and everything meshed really well together. 
+Gangnam Style: Korean style marinated short rib. cabbage, cilantro, green onion, pickled daikon, carrot, cucumber, jalapeno, spicy chili, vinegar, east beach aioli, corn tortilla. VOWED to not eat anything Asian, cuz SB, you good for a lot of things but lacking in the Asian department. Unfortunately, I only took one bite out of this and I stopped. The marinade was just off putting on the short rib. It tasted like a weird sweet wheat of some sort.  It looked just like a Vietnamese bahn mi more than a korean dish. 

.::Service/Atmosphere/Parking::.
Service was great. The cashier was friendly and welcoming. You order up front, give them your name, find a seat (outdoors only), and then wait for them to call your name to get your food. The food was made in a timely matter, about 15 minutes. 
Atmosphere was outdoorsy, where you can watch people bat. The place has no indoor seating as it is just a kitchen with seating outside. 
There's a small parking lot but enough to fit the flow of people. I had no trouble finding parking on a Sunday.

It's more like a 3.5, but the Gangnam Style made it impossible to overlook.

Rocky & Carlo's is my favorite place to pig out in the whole wide world and quite possibly beyond.  That said, let's get the negatives out of the way.  Outside of purchasing live bait or the occasional gun show at the Civic Auditorium, it is the only reason anyone should even consider venturing into St. Bernard Parish.  

The atmosphere is nothing to write home about.  It's a bar and a cafeteria that were slapped together long, long ago.  It's busy and loud and you often times can't hear yourself chew, much less what the person next to you is saying.  Just assume it's "holy sh*t, this is delicious!" and keep that fork a-shovelin'.  

The aforementioned din isn't something that manifests itself.  The place is typically wall-to-wall tummy grumblers and the line to the serving counter and around to the register can occasionally reach the front door.  As with any popular dining establishment, the trick is to get there when others don't, so think whatever the 3:40pm CST equivalent to brunch is (lupper?) and plan accordingly.  

Also, ladies ARE invited!  It says so right on the window, as well as on their plastic to-go beverage cups.  So, if you're thinking about treating the missus to some grade-A baked macaronis, you're not going to wind up being asked to leave.  On account of her gender, anyway.  I can't speak for your behavior in public.  Kids are also invited, even though they don't advertise it.  Keep that on the DL and don't let them sit at the bar.  Even if a few of them could pass for a miniature Norm Peterson.

Ah, yes.  The baked macaronis.  Macaroni may be plural, but in this case you're going to get enough to cover the superfluous s.  If you're not in the mood for macaronis, there are plenty of other menu options, like a sloppy, gravy-dripping-down-your-elbows roast beef po boy or hearty muffuletta.  But you're in the mood for the macaronis.  Trust me on this.  Now, what you want ATOP your macaronis is entirely up to you.  There's brown gravy, like you'd find on the roast beef po boy mentioned earlier in this paragraph, or red gravy, which most civilized people call tomato sauce.  

There's also a wide array of entrees, including the infamous stuffed peppers that landed them in hot water with the Louisiana Board of Health many moons ago *coughsalmonellacough*, but we won't dwell on an isolated incident.  I'm damn big on the veal parmesan.  MAMA MIA!  *kisses fingertips between bites.  BUT (Kim Kardashian sized but)  if you happen to be there not-so-late on a Wednesday, by all means, inquire about the brucciloni.  Srsly, it's Little Sicily on the Get in Muh Belly tip.

Or skip the imaginary trip to that other boot-shaped place all together and getcha some down home Louisiana seafood, dawlin'.  You got a hankering for some golden fried shrimps and ersters witcha baked mac?  Oh, dey got all dat, too!  Not to mention stuffed artichokes, creamy cole slaw ... heck, damn near anything you can spot on the working side of the Plexiglass, you can call yer meal.  And I only say "damn near", 'cause some of them pretty little things serving you prolly got gun-toting bfs back home that you ain't gonna want to mess with!

I also highly recommend the Wop salad, which is the politically correct name for the Dago salad, if I'm not mistaken.  Again, this is the same place that likes to hammer home the point that anyone bearing multiple x chromosomes is welcomed to dine.  With that in mind, feel free to call the side dishes whatever you damn well please.  I'm fairly certain you're not going to offend anyone behind the counter.

Oh, and the Bananas Foster Ice box pie!  Not sure if this is a seasonal thing or what, as I've only had it a couple of times.  But if they got it, you gotta get it.  

One of the big perks with any cafeteria-style restaurant is that you pay upfront, gather your own utensils and carry your tray to the table, assuming there are any vacant (good luck with that).  This equates to a smaller sense of obligation, as far as gratuities are concerned.  At least in my admittedly frugal mind.  In short, despite the magnificent portions on your plate(s), you're not (necessarily) looking at an additional 18%.  If I'm feeling particularly generous (and before waddling out of this culinary Valhalla, I often am), I'll slip the little lady who took care of me at the counter a couple of bucks to put towards a new pair of shrimp boots.  They smile real purty when you do that, camo-wearing bfs notwithstanding.

All in all, R&C's is a fantastic place to take your family or a group of friends for lunch or dinner.  For tourists in particular, it's light years off the beaten path of French Quarter establishments, where you're bound to pay twice as much for half the grub.  Well worth the excursion, should you have the means to get there.  As a former resident of the New Orleans area, I try to make it down there every time I'm in town.  I'll go so far as to say my trips home feel incomplete whenever that doesn't happen.

I use to love this place? What happened? The service with a smile is gone! We sat at the bar and barely was acknowledged. Then we were told someone was sitting in one of the spots? Hmmmm ok and left, but maybe she could have tried to serve us? Whatever... One would think in these trying times bartenders would be on their A game? Disappointed.

You are at the airport wondering what kind of crap food you will be able to find? 

Hello Harry and Izzy's!! This is a fantastic restaurant in the airport! The wine and beer list is great if you just have time for a drink. 

The best value... Yes, I said value in an airport restaurant is the Izzy plate. 3 shrimp cocktail, Caesar salad, and 2 sliders. I of course have the filet sliders... All for $22! The filet is tender and flavorful. The shrimp will clear your sinuses as H & I believes in horseradish and A LOT of it! Now the wine of my choice is pretty close to the cost of the meal, but HEY a girl has gotta do what a girl must do! Lol! 

The salad menu is great! Caesar and the Wedge are my favs. 

The BBQ chicken pizza is also very tasty! 

Thank you for giving airport restaurants a good name!

Ordered in for a night off. Went with some favorites and decided to try two new orders. They were quick to answer the phone and take our order, giving a 15 minute ready time. Beautifully packaged, my kids loved the personalized stickers. The appetizer sampler was mainly fried goods, so I was pleasantly surprised that they were still warm and crispy. The pad thai was good, and just the right amount of spice. The masaman curry was delicious, but a bit more spice than I would've liked, along with very little rice. The larb was very greasy, and that carried into the flavor overall.

I've been here twice now for a quick lunch and haven't been disappointed. I've only had the lamb, as I can't resist meat sliced off a spit, but really it's all about the numerous sides you get with a platter. They offer items like roasted potatoes, saffron rice, cucumber salad, tzatziki  sauce, and hummus. The flavors are rich and though you get full, you don't feel weighed down like after a greasy meal. The staff are proud of their product and the manager is quick to smile and offer suggestions. He was also kind enough to give me extra pita bread when my cranky toddler wasn't interested in anything else on his plate.

Upon coming into this coffee shop, I was shocked to receive the treatment that I didn't assume at first was openly racist. I saw that this woman was rude to me and I confronted her about the reason. I sat down for five minutes where the owner proceeded to "pretend" to me nice to me by offering me internet. She then proceeded to come back and say I won't be welcome in the store without buying anything. After my interaction, I began to notice that the woman singled me out for the way that I looked and dressed (discriminating) against the other individuals in the coffee shop. She did not treat me equally although there was plenty of other people in the coffee shop. 

This business does not follow OFFICIAL LAW or basic business ethics. After reading more reviews, I saw that this was a pattern and treatment in behavior and felt stronger in my case. This business is monetary and self centered, does not serve all students equally/treat all humans the same (with respect) and brings personal biases into the workplace. As a small business, I hope they know that UCSB as growing and diverse community admits ALL STUDENTS, not just those who are white (also, it's 2021)

This business spoke to me as if I was a dog, who couldn't afford anything in their place. I HIGHLY DO NOT recommend this place and hope that adequate measures are taken in place to ensure that the business does not operate

This place is an absolute hit! 

1st lets start with the layout and décor. Its HUGE!!! Lots of bar and lounge window seating...two dining rooms and an outside courtyard. It was nothing short of amazing. Not to mention the breathtaking pieces of art placed throughout the restaurant. 

The food....okay. I was already pretty excited to try this place so I kinda went for it. Ordered the pork belly ramen AND the pork belly sliders as an appetizers for the table. They both were equally amazing. The ramen broth lacked a little in flavor and the eggs weren't soft boiled so I didn't get that runny yolk I was hoping for. 

The scallop small plate (my friend ordered) he said was pretty tasty. Other ppl at the table who ordered the phat rice weren't too pleased with preparation of the dish. Said it was kind of charred. 

Our server Paul gladly replaced them with other options with no problem. He was awesome...explained the menu to us. Making sure to note some of the more popular items...as well as pointed out some items were not available because they were being revamped. 

Not much on the menu is geared to vegetarians...but items can be subsitutted to a vegetarian option by request. 

Overall I thoroughly enjoyed every bit of my experience. Looking to come back in the near future...as I read something about half of bottles of wine for happy hour :)

There's so many places to get seafood while in the New Orleans area, but what sets this place apart is the service. Omg. The service is amazing and it'll make me frequent more based on just that. Everyone welcomes you...not just the hostess or your bartender...EVERYONE. You can get help from just about anyone...not just your designated waiter/waitress. 

The food and drinks are spot on...always fresh. I love the Cadillac margarita and the Mardi Gras pasta. We stopped in on Fat Tuesday just as street cleaning was over in Metairie and scarfed down everything in front of us. Needless to say I've been back alone lol. 

This place gets it right on all accords.

Easily the best fried chicken I've ever had! 

I was skeptical because I've heard mixed reviews from friends but a coworker wanted to give this place a try ancestries it's walking distance from our office. Great idea! 

We got here a little before noon...seated immediately and ordered. Service was quick but not rushed and the staff were very nice. 

The food..A1! The chicken was seasoned perfectly and juicy. I'm not a fan of Mac and cheese from restaurants because I lean more to "true" home cooked dishes like this, but I was pleasantly surprised. Very creamy and seasoned. Some folks don't think to add actual seasoning to macaroni and it ends up being bland but this was not the case. And the mustard greens...fresh and on point. 

I even had a small cup of gumbo that was the perfect started! 

I even had leftovers to give to my 2 year old and he ate every morsel. 

Overall a great visit. I would say to go early and shy away during festive times of the year if you don't wanna wait and deal with an overwhelmed staff.

Excellent south Philly mexican BYOB. They are open late (until midnight I believe) and  seem to be known for their delivery via GrubHub.

The interior is nice and clean enough for a hole-in-the-wall joint. The inside is surprisingly big enough for groups.

The food here is great. Complimentary chips with red and green salsa. If you want something spicier, ask for the hot stuff from the back.

I recommend:
- Alambre Iztaccihuatl
- tacos al pastor
- sopes (try it with carnitas)
- tostada de tinga
- Torta (milanesa or heuvos/chorizo)

Don't forget to bring some beer, wine or tequila with you!

My bf's bday is on Wed so his parents took us to Tavolo V for dinner. It had just opened the night before so I was expecting the service to be meh and the food to be decent at best. I was pretty excited when the service was really nice and friendly and the food was scrumptious. Unlike other places with outdoor seating, the flow between indoor and outdoor felt natural due to the garage-like doors that could be pulled open. I could feel both the warm breeze and chilly AC from where I was sitting. Not great for the electricity bill but definitely great for my happiness!

We started off with the funghi and calamari appetizers. The mushrooms were tasty and the baby arugula made is nice and bright. I thought there was a tad more oil than I would like in the dish and I wanted more varieties of mushrooms. It was good though. As for the calamari, delicious. Lightly battered rings of squid sat on top of delicious tomato sauce. I loved how they even gave us the tentacles. I really enjoy eating calamari with tentacles. :P 

We then got some salad (good but not amazing) and some bruschetta. The bread was firm but good and the tomatoes on top were flavorful. There were real slivers of basil and that made the entire dish perfect for me. 

As for an entre, the bf's dad and I got the risotto of the day (crab and shrimp with asparagus), my bf got the lasagna, and the boyfriend's dad's wife got the cannelloni. I enjoyed my risotto but it was a bit more brothy than I'm used to. I thought the crab flavor could be a tiny bit stronger. The asparagus was perfect. I had some leftovers, so I took it with me and ate it for lunch the next day. Wow. It was so good when I reheated it, I gobbled it all up. My guess was that it was good but I was just too stuffed on appetizers to realize it the night before. 

As for the lasagna, I had a bite and really enjoyed it. My bf loved it and dug in with so much gusto. He had some leftover too -- which is a pretty good indication of how much food we had. The cannelloni looked really tasty and the bf's dad and dad's wife were trying to identify the filling. I think they decided it was spinach and ricotta. They were pretty blown away by the flavors. 

It ended up being about $125 for four of us including tax and tip. That's 5 appetizers and 4 entres. not bad.

So I came here before I saw the average reviews, before I was biased against this place, and I'm really glad that's how things worked out. I love soups and ramen. I came here with really high expectations and I wasn't disappointed. 

My friend and I walked here from University City because we wanted to work up and appetite. Upon arriving, I immediately loved the communal feel of the place. You were forced to sit by people you didn't know and as an extrovert, I enjoyed it very much. 

On your table you will find a sesame dispenser, a small jar of salty pickled ginger, and some chili powder spice mix. All of them are fantastic with the food. 

My friend and I each got a pork belly bun. Really good -- rich, juicy, melty, meaty. And we shared two ramens: the black garlic and the regular.
