Both broths had that perfect richness one would expect from ramen -- you know, the kind that leaves your mouth a tiny bit sticky and greasy. The garlic one had this wonderful mellow and warm garlic flavor. I liked the garlic one slightly more... but my super power is being able to ward off vampires with my breath alone... so i'm biased. 

Things that annoyed me and I hope this place works on: I didn't find bamboo in one of the bowls even though it was on the list, the ginger was SO good we ate most of what was at the table and there was only 1 jar instead of 2 for a LARGE table, we only had 1 slice of meat even though some photos showed 2. That's really about it. 

Do i recommend this place? YES! Do I think you should come here with high expectations? SURE!

Every time I come here, I lament how far away this place is from where I live. 

I still LOVE the tea section and this is still THE BEST place to get stroopwaffles in st louis. 

On top of that, I still love their candy aisle and they have my favorite ginger soda here (unfiltered, YUM). Their fresh herbs are still pretty fantastic too!

Also, ever since I requested turkish hazelnut butter, i've been able to find it here. so WIN. 

One piece of advice: if you're looking for masala chai, don't go to the tea aisle, go to the indian food aisle. It's on the top shelf the last time I checked. :)

I rarely give out a 5 star review but my latest visit here certainly earned it. 

We made reservations for 11:30 Sunday brunch. We were seated immediately and promptly greeted by our server who explained the happy hours deals.

I had a Groupon and know you can't mix deals but you can..sort of. You can get the 2-4-1 mimosas and $1 oysters as long as you spend at least $30 in addition to it.

I started with a pink fairy drink while my brunch partner chose mimosas. We opted to try half a dozen chargrilled oysters.  These babies were so good. Nice large size..covered in cheese and garlic butter served with grilled lemon and charred toast. 

They were in fact the best oysters I have had in my life.

Next cocktail was a french 75 which is always a winner in my book.

For brunch I opted for the alligator hash with Sunnyside up eggs and a hollandaise sauce. The alligator was nice and crispy and cut it large pieces..the potatoes were still firm but not too much and I was super impressed that the sunny side up egg was cooked perfectly.

He chose the breakfast wellington which I luckily got a bite of and it was yummy. His sunny side up egg was perfectly done as well and the pastry was nice and flaky.

The bill was around $70 to which we applied the 30$ discount and felt like thrives paying a mere $40 for all that goodness.

We've  already made reservations to go back next Sunday! 

Oh and our server was efficient and friendly.  Not over bearing and super helpful.

HAve you tried this place yet? It's soooo good. Seriously the best hummus I've ever had. I also tried the falafel, haydari, sagara  boregi, and they were kind of enough to let me try an appetizer size of the kibbeh. It was all amazing. I also had a nice turkish wine to go with it that was light and went perfectly with the meal. 
Service was spot on! He even offered to walk me to my car with an umbrella because it was pouring down rain.
Seriously, try this place

This is by far one of the worst hotels I've stayed internationally.  Really surprised Hyatt would put their name on a piece of garbage like this.  We got a room on hotwire for Sat night stay.  The room was tiny with a built-in cheap wall AC, the kind you would  buy at Walmart for $75.  The furniture was really run down and the overall appearance of the room was at best that of Motel 6.

I woke up at 2am from a loud noise coming from the air conditioning unit.  Called the front desk - they moved us to a different room ("last room left in the resort").  They helped us move to room 163 in the same building.  When arrived my girlfriend checked the bed and looked up with utter disgust - there were pubic hair on the sheets!  We showed this to Chad (the employee helping us move), and he offered to change the sheets or provide a roll-away bed.  

They finally put us up at their longer term stay apartment like room (which took 2 hours to get air conditioned so we could finally sleep at 4am).  This was only after jerking us around for 45 mins and telling us there were no more rooms left!  

I would not ever stay at Hyatt if I can help it!

Walking into Daughters Cafe had a very homey feel to it. The cafe is located in a bright red house near the river. I loved how the home was decorated with family photos, bright colors, and how the kitchen door was wide open for every one to see. You walk in and seat yourself, I ordered some coffee while looking over the menu (it was nice fresh and bubbly hot)! The waitress and staff were all very friendly and kind. I ordered the shired egg it was delicious and creamy- this came with a lot of tasty fruit and home made donut. If you are coming here for breakfast you need to try their donuts or beignets, they are the best! After our meal the owner came out and thanked us for coming in. I really appreciated eating somewhere that was family owned and operated. I felt like I was eating at a friends home. I would recommend Daughters Cafe to anyone looking for a new breakfast spot or looking to try something new I really enjoyed my experience here- nothing like (what feels like a) home made meal, friendly service, and fresh food.

Pint Size Bakery is OFF THE CHAIN !

I had to come and try this place after reading all the love it was getting on Yelp. The bakery is amazing!  

This morning the line was out the door with a short wait in the cold. It was worth it. 
We took  a small variety to try. A Breakfast Cookie, 2 Oatmeal Cremes, a Cranberry Crunch cookie and a Carrot Cake Loaf. My eyes wanted more but being my first trip here I figured I better stop. You know how somethings look good but then fall short on taste. Well, not here. 

Driving down Watson eating out of a brown box was not  how I  invisioned this mornings bakery visit. I will spare you all the verbage of my expectance. I was not able to control myself until I got home, so the munching began. Each bite was spectacular- Each one of our choices out did the other. I can not even describe the creme between the Oatmeal cookies- delightful and fresh!  

I came close to trying the Sea Salt Carmel Scone, I had to laugh when the sign by it said "Limit 2", I mean who limits a sale on anything these days...

Truly, these bake goods are baked from the heart with quality ingredients and no short cuts. 

I will not make any star deductuons even though I am disappointed that there is no seating inside. 

Pint Size  what do you think about a Quart Size or a Gallon Size location?

YUCK!

Unfortunately my  husband took a mystery shop at this place, so I went with him.

A Baja Frat House of sorts- neon bright yellow and blue everything with "eat me" on the tops of the tables and on the walls. I wish someone would have yelled "food fight"...

I ordered the Fajita Plate. It came with 2 sides. I chose the Borracho Beans (pinto beans with beer and bacon) and the Cilantro-Lime Rice. The sides were big but bland. All I could smell was warm beer (from the beans), so I had to put them in a relocation program. The rice was devoid of Cilantro or lime. The Fajita mix portion was very small. The tortilla's were dry. 

Even the Diet Coke was lacking carbonation. 

Missing the customary chips and salsa provided at most Mexican restaurants,  I went back and ordered some. Mistake! They season the chips with something, but all I could think of was Lawry's Season salt. The salsa was flavorless. I was asked if I wanted the salsa hot or cold. Who eats hot salsa? 

On the way out, I had the urge to belch and chest bump the guy coming in.

Now didn't reading this make you feel all warm and FUZZY!

OK- I just read Elaine M. review of Saffron. I will tell you that I was sitting right behind her yesterday at lunch. We do not know each other. I did witness the offensive way she was treated over a plate of some unfinished food. On my way out I stopped and said *Yelp It*. She said she was going to, so  of course I have been looking to spot her review. I am updating my review to validate her poor review. After the way the man in question spoke to her, he did disappear never to be seen again. 
I too, left uneaten food as some of the things I opted to try did not appeal to my taste after sampling them. That is what comes along with offering a buffet. People often take things they may not eat. I have not eaten her in quite awhile, but I did notice business seemed slower than what I have seen before. 
Perhaps some customer service refresher course should be offered!

What a bunch of Jackwagons!

Went in for lunch today. After ordering I handed the gal our Entertainment coupon. She said, "OH, we don't take these anymore!  She seemed surprised when we opted to leave.  What is this bait and switch? They get you to come in the door and then assume you will be to embarrassed to leave.  Not me.    How about a sign on the door or window if you choose not to honor your coupon.

I hate to say this but PYT has become that child at school who started out great but after not getting their ego stroked they started to act out and misbehave. 

A few years ago when I first ate there it was great. But it had gone down hill. I now will not eat there. The last time I was there was 2 days before the McCoy incident. I left being very unhappy with the service. The food was ok. And I couldn't even just chalk it up to them being busy because there was only 1 table aside from me. The server did not know all of the beer list because when I asked for something on their list they told me they never carried that beer. But when I pointed it out to her she smacked her teeth and went and got it. She never checked on us and when it was time to leave she opted to hang with her friends and didn't give us our check for what seemed like forever. Then took forever to cash is out. 

Their gimmick burgers will draw in a crowd but it's a shame that their service will be just 1 time customers. I have worked in the restaurant industry for 10 years in the back of the house and if I ever knew that the front of the house was delivering this poor of service I would get out before it ruined my reputation.

Gary and I (2/3 of our Dining Trio) have been watching GMG Chinese Bistro prep their space. We finally saw the Grand Opening banner, and happily dined there. The waitress said they've been open for about two weeks now. 

The restaurant is attractive, with marbletop tables, wooden brown chairs, and sage greens and brown tones. The ceiling has a few contemporary touches, with inset domes (no idea how to explain this) that change colors. GMG has a comfy bar area to one side. Looks like they are still finishing the bar wall area.

Service was friendly and fast. The menu is an attractive, heavy affair on heavy stock. We liked the variety of choices, but stuck with some traditional dishes to get a feel for their culinary interpretation. We ordered two family dinners, that come with egg roll, soup and crab puff appetizers plus fried rice and the entree. The appetizers took a little long to arrive, but were good. My hot and sour soup could be a little more sour. Gary's wonton soup was very tasty. The entrees arrived on dishes along with a large, attractive "ball" of rice. 

The sesame chicken was excellent, with just the right texture and flavor. The cashew chicken was a little less exciting; a bit tasteless and lacking any special vegetables (looked like peas and carrots that come pre-prepared). It could've used more garlic and sauce. The chicken was tender. The fried rice was nicely prepared but simple--not the type of fried rice with lots of veggies and/or pork in it. We took a few photos and will get them out of our cell phone shortly. I would go back, and we enjoyed the ambiance and overall, the food. It is a new place and all new restaurants evolve over time to perfect the nuances that make them special. I can tell that the owner in the front was working very hard at the bar, helping to serve, as well as to greet and seat people. Parking is easy; the restaurant is on the east side, in a strip mall just south of Lambert Lane.

Gary and I celebrated our anniversary here, along with mom, who treated. Lucky us! The Dining Trio was in full force, excited to try a new and much anticipated establishment. It just opened one week ago. Five Palms Steak and Seafood is the vision of owner Nino Aidi, who I met at the end of the meal. He has created an experience in the former Cafe Terra Cotta building, that overlooks all of Tucson with incredible views.

The building houses multiple separate experiences, including both fine and casual dining, two bars, a boardroom to be (that will seat up to 18, I think) with fine views of the Catalinas, and yet unfinished meeting room. Nino himself is the fine artistic hand behind the interior design and finishes, which he said have taken a year to orchestrate. You are met by a stunning HUGE stained class piece of art and inlaid table, and multiple friendly hostesses. You have walked into a different time and place; the desert fades away as you spot huge framed copies of 18th and 19th century artwork replicas. For our special evening, we had reserved a table in the fine dining room (thanks so much again, mom!). You walk through dark carved wood arches into a beautiful room. Actually, TWO beautiful rooms-a striking blue carpet and walls of carved curving dark woods with mirrors and (in one of the rooms) also walls of tasteful windows. (See photos I shall be uploading).

The ceiling was also striking, decorated with a HUGE stained glass custom piece that covers nearly the entire length. Both fine dining rooms have a stained glass ceiling. I felt like I was in an elegant cruise ship, with its wooden walls and the beautiful finishes. My mother could not put her finger on the type of design, but suffice it to say it's a tasteful Baroque style meets classy contemporary. The silver, dishware and crystal are also a step up from your everyday dining.

I better cut to the chase or I'll run out of room: Excellent onion sour dough bread, freshly baked-served with little butter (you can get more) because you also have delicious oil and balsamic vinegar for bread dipping. You can order fine wines here, even served in decanters (the type that aerates the wine--forgive me; I am not an expert on wine) and drinks. The friendly server was well informed and guided us to ordering great choices. Mom enjoyed the fresh Five Palms salad, which includes mint. Gary ordered the French onion soup, served in a bread bowl. It had a distinct tarragon flavor (I think), a unique twist. We all opted for fish dishes, although steak is a specialty as well here. You can choose your preferred sauce for fish. Gary enjoyed a blue-nose grouper with an Andalusian sauce (tomato-based, with peppers, olives, shrimp, a mussel, etc.) while mom and I really enjoyed our Chilean sea bass. It was perfectly prepared, with a sense of a caramelized top and a spinach/Parmesan cheese sauce. Rich and delicious (it also tasted as good the next day--I had a few bites left over). We did not get any vegetable sides. We had to save room for dessert!

Check out the photo I will upload-the server wheeled over the freshly baked cakes, which change day to day. Classy way to serve. I was told the cakes are baked locally just for Five Palms. Mom had the tiramisu (EXCELLENT-one of the best ever, she said) and we had a yummy multi-layered chocolate-raspberry cake. I would've loved a taste of the Black Forest cake as well. Our experience at Five Palms was classy, fun, tasty and memorable. My mom pointed out the only thing we could fault (hardly a "fault") was that she felt that being a fancy place, they should "crumb" the table (remove crumbs using a table crumb remover). I do remember those silver items in the old days. Not sure they do that anymore anywhere? We toured the rest of the restaurant and look forward to coming back. Do try Five Palms, and enjoy the artistic ambiance and the tasteful food created with joy by the owner. We left feeling well taken care of and happy!

Gary and I (2/3 of the Dining Trio) made our first visit to this recently opened restaurant.  It gets a hearty thumbs up! Wok & Roll features rows of serving tables featuring many Chinese dishes, PLUS an entire sushi bar. The sushi features both raw and cooked varieties (so everyone can eat it) and was excellent quality. My husband is Japanese, and was pleased with the sushi. The sushi chef is Japanese, and one of the owners, a gracious man.

You get tons of variety (like other Chinese buffets) but this one has that sushi bar and a dessert/salad/fresh shrimp/mussels bar as well. Everything was clean and fresh, and plentiful. And although this restaurant just opened around 10 days or so ago, it had plenty of people! It's a big place, so plenty of seating abounds.

I noticed they also will prep food for you off a menu if desired instead of buffet, and you can do take-out of the sushi or Chinese type.

And yes, they do have a senior discount, so do ask for it, if you qualify. It's $12.95 dinner M-TH and $15.95 Fri./Sat. Lunch is $9.95. Kids have discounted pricing. It's a good value for the quality and quantity of food that you get.

The place has a good, friendly vibe, the servers were friendly and professional -- all positives. We will definitely return! Good luck to the new owners -- we wish you great success!

Cafe du Monde haterzzz (multiple z's) oft cite Cafe Beignet as the alternative place to jones on a dough pillow fix. I figured it was high time to put this place to the test.

If you like your lines shorter and sweeter, your food options variable and savory, and your beignets doughier and chewier, Cafe Beignet is a good choice. The Parisian cafe-style seating makes for a much more relaxing experience than the frazzled, stress-inducing lines and airplane-style seating at Cafe du Monde. Cafe Beignet also has a full menu of savory breakfast and lunch items, plus alternative desserts for the discerning sweet tooth.

That said, if you're in it purely for beignets and coffee, Cafe du Monde does it better. There's personal bias in that statement. Cafe Beignet's beignets are much more doughy and require effort to chew, whereas Cafe du Monde's melt away like butter. Some like gooey cookies, some like snapback cookies. I personally like Cafe du Monde's airy beignets.

That said, the cafe au lait is miles better at Cafe du Monde. Unquestionably.

It was a cold snowy day, but I was craving for sweets sUper badly, so I decided to check if Gordon's Milkshake was open today! In the past, the hours of operation were a little hard to figure out since his hours aren't posted on the door, but luckily he had amazing communication through Instagram direct message. In the future, it would be nice if the hours are posted in front of the store door or wall, that way it'll avoid inconvenience for other customers in the future and potential bad experiences.

There was a few milkshake that caught my attention, which was the cookies and cream one! I am a huge fan of Oreo, so can't go wrong with that option! Gordon, the owner himself, was very personable and knowledge on knowing what flavors and ice cream mix well together. He asked personally if I liked cheesecake and white chocolate and I told him yes, so he customized a milkshake that was white chocolate cookies and cream cheesecake for me! Wow, didn't think I was able to taste all the flavors in one drink! I'm really happy that this location was opened and part of the Mass Ave. family! 

This location does warm desserts too such as beignets and brownies! I'm excited to try all the desserts in the future! Thanks Gordan for the memorable experience :)

Yujo is ramen and bubble milk tea shop that just opened recently!

This shop is unique; you have to line up to order, get a number, and then you seat yourself. This is like a eat and go situation; not your restaurant style more like fast food.

The customer service here was really friendly and the amount of time to make my order was very fast! 

I ordered the Tonkotsu ramen and jasmine milk tea with boba! 

The Tonkotsu ramen broth was really flavorful and the noodle amount was good to keep you full for a little, but I was expecting a little more toppings on bowl on noodles. At Meet Noodle @ Castleton Square, for the same price, there was fish cake, more meat, more noodle, corn, and etc; this location you have to pay for more topping. 

The jasmine milk tea with boba was delicious, but the boba could be better in terms of sweetness. 

This is good place to eat if you're looking to have your lunch break, catch up with a friend or family member and even eat alone! I would definitely come back here if I'm looking quick and easy lunch or dinner!

This is not your typical steakhouse. An décor in tribute to 1920's Hollywood, with low lights and dark woods, my special date and I were instantly transported to a long-gone era. Have you ever walked into a place and knew you were going to love it? Well this was the case at Butcher's and Singer's. This is the story of my 90 minutes love affair with the best steakhouse in the city. 

We ordered the 28-days aged, porterhouse, medium rare for two ($86)- Cooked perfectly with precise temperature and seasoning. It had a sublime tenderness and mineral complexity that most steaks aren't able to execute. The contrast between the charred exterior and the warm, juicy center was mouth-watering. Worth every penny. Highly recommend the hashbrowns ($9). You have not lived until you've eaten this simple, but crazy delicious side dish. Stuffed with sour cream, more potatoes, and onions, I would come here to just to eat this.
 
Save some room in your stomach because the BAKED ALASKA ($12) will take your breath away. It's essentially a meringue-topped dome of a baked Alaska hiding housemade banana ice cream and apricot compote. So heavenly...HMM. Our server, Amy, was professional and knowledgeable. Her smiles and positive demeanor were a joy to see. Impeccable service. 

So schedule your cardiology appointment, gulp away your lipitor, and spend your entire days at the gym because Butcher and Singer's quality of food will keep you coming back for more. Next to Capital Grill's, this steakhouse is good as it gets in the city of brotherly love.

Kung Fu Tea is taking over the US with their awesome teas.

And thank goodness there's one in Philly now! When I found out KFT opened one in Chinatown today, I was beyond excited. This KFT, unlike most of the others, offer plenty of seatings as it's spacious and will definitely accommodate the expected countless patrons. 

The drinks are priced similarly as the other locations. Roughly $4. Take credit cards. Keep your ticket, trade for your bubble tea at counter when its ready.  Though they don't seem to be very organized or prepared for opening weekend, as showed in their friendly but slow service. I did wait half a hour for my drinks but every sip was worth every minute. And I'm confident that once they get things going service will be as good as their other chains.

My favorites and recommendations are the delicious taro milk bubble tea (tapioca is perfectly soft, chewy, and sweet) and grapefruit green tea (refreshing with yummy floating pulp). Lactose-intolerant? KFT uses lactaid milk. On a healthy diet? You can adjust amount of sugar in your drinks! 

Absolutely give KFT a try! It's a very good and popular bubble tea franchise for the various reasons I listed. But If anything, it's not another bubble tea place in Philly that starts with Tea.....

The Vietnamese food here will change your life. Seriously. You'll sell all of your possessions, shave your head, and chant at random times during the day. The stuff is heaven. 

That being said, the dish to get at Nam Phuong is the Ba Vi Platter ($24).

A large round plate assembled with crisp lettuce leaves, sprigs of mint and basil, along with cool English cucumber slices and thinly sliced, slightly pickled carrots and daikon radish. A bed of vermicelli sat on the other side topped with shrimp mousse grilled on sugarcane(1), house-made pork sausage(2) and a bundle of ground beef wrapped in grape leaves, then grilled(3). Absolutely delish.

The pho, bun bo hue, goi cuon, and banh xeo are also all equally high-end compared to other Vietnamese restaurants in the city.

If you have to ask about the service, you've obviously not been to a lot of authentic Vietnamese places. They shout "What you want" and if you don't have an answer within three seconds, they'll probably give you the death stare and walk away, returning fifteen minutes later, begrudgingly, to let you continue your order. 

Highly recommended authentic Vietnamese food.

Oh gosh, if you sincerely love noodles, spicy and sour flavors, this Chinese restaurant is definitely a must try for you. Xi'an Sizzling Woks cook up some scrumptious authentic food originating from the Shaanxi province of China. The noodles here are thicker, wider, and longer than the norm. Knowing all this, I was more than excited to finally eat here.

THE FOOD:

CHINESE HAMBURGER ($3.50)
Aka "Rou Jia mo" or meat burger. Served by many street vendors in China for around a dollar, it's also possibly the oldest sandwich/burger in the world. Usually the pork is stewed for hours and seasoned with dozens of spices and stuffed in a flatbread called "mo." Muslims in Shaanxi have also substituted pork for beef or lamb. But we ordered the one with "braised pork" and it was tasty. However, I thought the burger was on the dryer side. And Although the bread was well cooked and the meat was tender, it was lacking in terms of flavors. 

XI'AN LIANG PI ($4.95)
Literally translated to "coldskin." This noodles dish was mostly sour, a tad spicy, and tangy. Although I was underwhelmed by the flavors. I recommend trying this dish once.

DUMPLING IN CHILI SAUCE ($5.95)
Steamed and made with pork and chives wrapped inside dough skin covered with chili sauce. It was really delicious. The meat was flavorful and the sauce gave a nice kick to the taste. 

SPICY MINCED PORK NOODLES SOUP ($6.95)
Curious on how this bowl of noodles compared to other noodles soups. Firstly, it's sour. Not too spicy. The noodles are well done in terms of texture. But I'm not a fan of scattered meats floating in a bowl of soup. 

BIANG BIANG NOODLES WITH GARLIC SCALLION SAUCE ($5.95)
WOW, these noodles are GIANGANTIC. Being the noodles addict I am, my eyeballs almost popped out of its sockets when my chopsticks started to lift up these noodles. Though not completely tasteless, I wasn't a fan. It lacked a certain richness in terms of flavors and texture. But you should order it once if you never had it. 

FYI- it's called Biang Biang Noodles because it's named after the sounds chefs make when they pull an slap the dough on the table. How cool, haha. 

THE SERVICE:
Our servers were very friendly and gracious. This is not the case of the most restaurants in Chinatown! These four dishes are probably their most popular ones. Prices are very reasonable as the two of us shared five dishes of food for $29. 

Overall, the food here can be summed in 3 words:
Authentic
Affordable
Awesome

I'll have to return a few times here to test other items from the menu, but they've made a good first impression.

I absolutely love noodles. 

So I just had to come here once I heard about Cheu's existence. Reading the reviews and descriptions beforehand, I knew the noodles and food aren't authentic in origin but rather the creations of an excellent chef's culinary imagination. That chef happens to have cooked at one of the best restaurants (Matyson) in the city. Despite my general apprehension of Asian fusion cuisine, I ventured into Cheu's Noodle Bar fearlessly..fueled by my obsession of noodles. 

The inside is really small. Exactly how a noodle bar should be like. There's about 3-4 tables besides the stools. Overall, clean and modern look and yet had a very nice cultural and down to earth feel about it. Great first impression as you walk into the place.

We ordered the following appetizers:

*Black Garlic Wings w/ shishito peppers (4) $ 8: Great tasting garlic flavors on the outside. Had a nice crunch. Although lacked flavors inside. 

*Burger & Pork Belly Buns $7: The buns are fried briefly on the outside. The pork belly was absolutely delicious. It was tender and flavorful. Really melted in your mouth. Exactly how it should be. The bun itself wasn't anything special. 

*Eggplant w/ crispy garlic, herbs, tamarind  $7: I'm not a huge eggplant fan so I can't really comment. Maybe you are and will love this dish!

We ordered the following noodles:

PORK BELLY RAMEN W/ POUCHED EGG, SEA BEANS, GREENS $12: 

THE GOOD: Once again, the pork belly was really good. Definitely the standout of the entire experience. 

THE BAD: The broth wasn't horrible. If you never have authentic ramen before, you might actually think it's delicious. My taste buds are spoiled from the likes of Ippudo and Totto. The broth lacked a certain richness and depth. 

THE UGLY: The ramen was chewier and harder than I liked. Not used to eating ramen with this type of noodles. 

DUCK PHO w/ FOIE GRAS MEATBALLS $13: I don't really understand why this is called Pho because nothing about it taste like Pho. Instead of the traditional rice noodles, Cheu decided to use the exact ramen noodles for the duck "pho" as well...speechless. Aficionados of Pho will be offended. The meatballs were tasty. If you are a fan of pho...be warned! 

Prices are on the heavier side. Service was friendly and accommodating. 

Ultimately- Come here with an open heart about how the food here is conceptionized and prepared and you'll love it more. Read this: Nothing about Cheu is traditional. I genuinely attempted my best to like the noodle bar but years of eating authentic ramen and pho ruined this experience for me.

I wholeheartedly laud owners Ben and Shawn for coming up with this uber cool idea and having the courage to make it a reality. Wish them nothing but success! Will definitely come back one day to see how the food has evolved!

I must announce my love for this place. This is a breakfast destination I've fallen deeply for. I can be picky when it comes to brunch food because let's face it, it's universally known to be the BEST meal of the day. But Cafe La Maude sure know how to get to my heart. Incredible food and wonderful service. What more can a guy ask for? 

Dishes are always beautiful, delicious, and very filling. Attentive service with a smile. Gabby and his wife are both unbelievably friendly, graceful, and caring. Also great ambiance. And the food has a lot of creativity. One example of a must try is the Parisian Za- An open-faced croissant topped with French ham, warm goat cheese, avocado, caramelized onions,jalapeños, drizzled with truffle oil, eggs any style, and potato croquette..MMM! 

Bring your dog, toddler, loving parents, significant other, or anyone else because I can guarantee they'll love it here. So next time include Cafe La Maude in your discussions of where to eat brunch in the city!

The Korean food here is pure awesomeness. 

Must order the sundubu jjigae (Korean stew) here! It's a hot and spicy soup made with uncurdled dubu (tofu), vegetables, mushrooms, onion, scallions, various combination of tasty seafood and gochujang (chili powder). The soup is made and eaten right in the serving bowl, which is typically made of solid stone. Served with a raw egg to be cracked into the soup. It comes out still bubbling vigorously. You are also given a bowl of cooked white rice and several banchan (side dishes). The banchan are so addicting that you'll ask for seconds! A true Korean meal is never complete without banchan. And the ones here are crazy delicious. Also highly recommend their bbq meats. 

I worship this eatery greatly. You might as well stop reading this review and ask me about it in person. Because chances are that if you go here now, I will be there eating my sundubu and banchan!

I'm so ashamed. What's wrong with me?

Being a lifelong Philadelphian, it actually took me years before I found Dalessandro's. Just ate here literally for the 5th time this month. What diet? I'd write a lot but I'm so stuffed I'm just focusing on breathing right now.. But oh my god, come here for the best cheesesteak ever ($6.50). Perfectly chopped and cooked steaks stuffed generously inside a fresh, home baked tasting bun with the cheese melting it way through the sandwich.  Its a pretty small place, so be prepared to wait during busy times. Order a Hank's soda with your cheeseksteak and it's instant pure happiness.

Who doesn't love a happy ending with amazing fro-yo?

Happily Ever After is totally awesome for people who like to have tons of different toppings and control over the toppings on their fro-yo. I can't deny I am one of these people.

Reasons why Happily Ever After 's will give any fro-yo lover a perfect ending:

1. Creative flavors such as 100% organic green tea and nutella! 
2. Lots of toppings - cookies, nuts, cereal, fresh fruit, mochi balls, tapioca, marshmallows, syrups
3. They're happy to give out free samples
4. Self-serve, pay by weight, 38 cents/ounce
5. Frequent buyer card
6. Friendliest fro-yo service ever
7. They also have bubble tea, smoothies, orangettes, cherry mice, and caneles!

So with the explosion of high-end frozen yogurt stores in Philly and the continual rollout of frozen yogurt-type desserts, Happily Ever After truly stands out from the ever growing crowd. My new favorite place along with Yogorino!

To all lovers of meat out there- this AYCE Korean BBQ Buffet is legit. Although it's located in a shady area of Upper Darby and the decor and ambiance leave much to be desired. The food here is really tasty! And you can eat as much of it you want until your gastrointestinal system explodes.

Anyways, we were hungry and attacked the buffet like the carnivores we are. They have everything here. From authentic bone-in kalbi, bulgogi, daeji bulgogi, chicken, baby octopus, and shrimp.  Everything was well-seasoned and looked extremely fresh. Also plenty of rice, kimchi, and banchan dishes go with too! I kept thinking "they aren't going to make any money off of us!" 

Owned by an adorable old Korean couple, they were more than helpful. When we asked for extras such as butter and lime, they were more than accommodating. Being a cold December night, they even brought out a heater right next to our table.

It's only $25 a person! That's a really great deal considering how much meats we ate. You can also bring as much beer or soju you want as it's BYO. 

You will not be disappointed and will be leaving with a food coma for sure ;)

Foodgasm (Urban Dictionary)- "Eyes rolling back in head and moaning while possibly shouting "this is so freaking good!!"and taste so overwhelming you have to take breaks between bites to keep from shutting your system down."

Now to experience the pure foodgasm just described above, go to the Reading Terminal Market, and stop by Hershel's. Order the reuben sandwich with pastrami AND corned beef, Swiss cheese, sauerkraut, and Russian dressing, grilled between slices of rye bread. The juicy, fatty, tender freshly cut meats compliment perfectly with the flavors of the sauerkraut and delicious dressing. Truly mouthwatering stuff. 

Oh, and add a can of Dr. Brown's black cherry soda and a donut from Beiler's, your life will be forever changed.

***Caution, if you start, you may not stop. This place makes some tasty fried dough confectionery desserts. 

Their donuts melt in your mouth and are just absolutely delicious. I recommend the banana creme donut. Just thinking about them right now is making me hungry! They have a bunch of different kinds of donuts that are all amazing. If you're looking to lose weight (who isn't right), DO NOT WALK PASS THIS PLACE in the Reading Terminal Market. At 0.90 cents a pop, you won't break the bank here unlike a certain other place. 

The texture of the dough here has perfect amount of chewiness and density. The fried-ness and extend of frying was excellent. The fillings and toppings were in synchronized harmony. Appearance was super enticing. And most importantly, the  flavors had a delicious balance between the dough, filling, and fried-ness. 

I loved this place and I want to go back as soon as I can. 100% stone cold lock you will as well.

Growing up, I craved for chè when other kids wanted cookies or brownies. For those who never had it before, chè is a sweet porridge or cocktail dessert made with a variety of fruits, milk, and ingredients. Unfortunately, living in the east coast there isn't really a place that specialize in making these delicious sweets besides the comfort of my home. So when the Bambu franchise opened one in South Philly last week, I was most likely the happiest guy in the city. 

There is a nearly endless variety of named dishes with the prefix chè. This is quite evident in Bambu's extended list of combinations. Like a child in a candy store, I wanted to try everything! It was heaven for me. I recommend #6 and #10 ($4.50): 

#6 is Chè trái cây- lychee, longan, red tapioca, jackfruit, palm seed, pandan jelly, jello, young coconut. The consistency was so perfect! Pure happiness in my mouth.

#10 is Hat lu sng sáo bánh- tapioca, grass jelly, pandan jelly. Perfect blend of sweetness and glutinous goodies. 

For opening weekend, they were fairy organized. Customer service was friendly. The overall process was quick and easy. Everything tasted wonderfully sweet yet refreshing. My foodie routine from now on in South Philly will be pho or bun bo hue followed by Bambu Desserts & Drinks!

Mind blown.

High Street is a prime example why I feel so happy and lucky to living in Philadelphia right now. Came here to brunch recently and let's just say...wow. The pastrami hash sandwich ($10.50) is pure foodporn. I fell in love upon the first bite. The combination of the shaved pastrami with the crispy spiced hash, roasted peppers & onions, fried eggs, and Russian dressing inside a freshly baked bread is unbelievably delicious.

Service was great and decor speaks refined and elegant. Very comfortable dinning environment overall. Loved it. Our city has become such an exciting place to eat out. There is an entire new generation of young chefs with fresh ideas who are transforming Philly into an amazing food town.

Moral of the story: Haters gonna hate

Story: My lovely mother decided to finally eat at a place that does not serve Vietnamese food for once in celebration of her birthday. Excitedly, I asked which cuisine she had decided on for me to take her to. In her cute Vietnamese accent, "CHEESECAKE!," she announced. In my head, I cringed. Aside from their cheesecakes, I have not eaten here for a long time. So I then silently chanted these thoughts during our car ride:

+Ridiculous long lines
+Horrible service
+Fusion food gone wrong
+Uneatable humongous portions 

On this particular night, all of my preconceived notions about CF were defied. We arrived on a weekday's night and were seated immediately much to my amazement. We avoided the usual hordes of hungry patrons holding their buzzers standing around the entrance and exit on any given weekend's night. 

The quality of food was well-executed. I ordered the bang-bang chicken and shrimp served with brown rice, chile, curry, coconut, and sautéed vegetables. It was very flavorful. I finished it all! Also ordered the vegetarian burger and salads and enjoyed every bite. Washed it all down with a glass of delicious red wine sangria. We then finished off with a heavenly slice of dulce de leche caramel cheesecake. 

Our server, Olena, was extraordinary. Her genuine friendliness and helpfulness was truly appreciated. She paid attention to the small details of our dining experience. It was truly exceptional service for any restaurant, especially a chain. 

Lesson learned- so whatever mom wants she gets. And moms are usually right.

Matyson is the quintissential BYOB restaurant. Here's why it's my favorite in a city bustling with amazing BYOBs. 

It's located in one of the nicest areas of town. Cozy and intimate atmosphere, yet with ample space to create a perfect romantic setting. Although specializing in seasonal, new American cuisine, there is undoubtedly old French inspiration. And by far, the star of the show is the fois gras appetitizer, which is served with banana bread, crispy duck skin, sprinkles of fresh halzelnuts and coffee. I would dare to say that there is no better fois gras in our great foodie city. 

But what sets apart Matyson is it's $45 tasting menu served on weekdays which features themes such as lobster and pumpkin, whatever the chefs find most fresh and in season. The last time we went here we were blown away by the perfectly cooked Long Island duck breast served with delicious coconut curry, leek, and sweet potato. 

Service have always been attentive and extremely helpful. From the décor, to the well-executed food here, Matyson is the first BYOB I talk about whenever the topic is in discussion. So I will definitely be back with wine in hand to try more delightful dishes!

Quite possibly the best meal I have ever had!!  I took my mom to Twisted Tree for her birthday and we were both amazed at the service and the food.  Both of us ordered the 6 ounce filet.  The garden salad that came with the meal was excellent...the vegetables in the salad all tasted very fresh and the Pear Tree sweet onion vinaigrette dressing was one of the best salad dressings I have ever tried.  The filet was cooked absolutely perfectly (I ordered it medium well) and it literally melted in my mouth.  I ordered the asparagus as my side and the béarnaise sauce on it added a great complimentary flavor.  We had a slice of the wedding cake for dessert, which was large enough to share.  Although the restaurant is on the pricier end, the first rate service and the excellent food makes it a special treat!

Bacio is one of our favorite restaurants in our Mt Airy neighborhood; what a gem!  

We've even had a dinner party there for my birthday a few months back, and the restaurant was very accomodating.  We were able to choose a number of entrees in advance for our guests to choose from, so that the kitchen was prepared and did not have to worry about running out of food.  Service is great and it's more of an intimate restaurant, where the staff and owner knows you by name.

We been there many times since.  I am in love with their handmade pasta.  Also their menu is great- vegan and vegetarian! So it's a great place to take my non-meat eating friends.

You suck we want to spend one day without listening to your music we can't sleep you're annoying all your neighbors we don't even want to taste your food. (The name of your restaurant is wrong in all languages).

Food poisoning!!

I LOVE sushi, and I eat it all the time!  I came here with a friend to get dinner. We got tempura and Las Vegas roll. The tempura came out SUPER greasy, and I thought the roll was meh at most. 

The highlight of my night, of course however, was 2 hours later when I got the worst stomache I've ever had, following that, common food poisoning symptoms ensued...

I've been on the lookout for great AUTHENTIC Mexican food in Philadelphia. Who would have thought that I would discover this place near the Italian district in South Philly.  

I came here with Ashley L. and we ordered some guacamole as an appetizer. First, I love that you get a full bowl of guac! They don't skimp you on any avocados. It is also delicious! Great for a party of four to share as an app.

I ordered some pastor tacos, amazing! I had to go with a classic for my first time. The tortilla was awesome, I'm not sure what it was made of but it wasn't your standard flour or corn tortilla. So good! Would definitely go back for the tacos.

I was amazed at the list of specials they had, we were told about the different dishes that they make including steaks and fish. Everything in the restaurant looked delicious, will definitely be back to try something else!

THE BEST BAGELS in Philadelphia! Finally!!! My search has ended. I have found a great bagel spot, where the dough is thick, fresh, soft... and you don't need to toast it! 

Everything at this place is homemade, even their cream cheeses.  They have such an extensive list of homemade cream cheeses, some could even be considered food (white fish, sounds scary but is absolutely delish). They will let you try different cream cheese flavors and you can combine them on your bagel.  It was recommended to combine the scallion and jalapeño... incredible, so flavorful but nothing overwhelming.

I have also tried their falafel sandwich. Falafels are always a hit or miss with me, some places deep fry them too much, others try to make them overly healthy. Their homemade falafel was the perfect balance! So delicious and you can choose to have it spicy or regular on the sandwich.  I went spicy! The spice does not deter from the falafel flavor, really good balance with the veggies on the sandwich. Last, their pita bread gets five stars on its own. It was so thin and fresh, but didn't break the still could hold the sandwich.

 Breakfast or lunch, this place is great! Can't wait to try their kebabs next.

I really love this place. Its my favorite diner thats in walking distance of my house. 
I love it more for the feel it gives off and people that work at this place. The food is of your standard diner quality and thats perfectly fine. You get what you pay for here. I will say though that their chocolate milkshakes are scrumptious, I get one every time I go! 

Its clean, fun and a great place you can go to at any time you want.

Now the reason i give this place 2-stars is for two reasons CUSTOMER SERVICE & a personal opinion on the gratuity. Let's start with the positives:
PGC is a great concept and executed well- decor is cute, space is small (emphasis on small) and quaint. It's cool if you are more interested in ambience and good food. I recently went for brunch to celebrate a friends birthday, we were on the larger side for a reserved party so we ordered almost one of everything on the menu- you can imagine what the bill came to be. No one complained about their food so that was a major plus. i personally had the shrimp and grits and although i could tell the fish was most likely frozen it wasn't the worst I've ever had.. the grits were good (not as hot as I would have liked) but it wasn't a reason to complain. A few other food compliments I heard were for the Shrimp and grits, the crab omelette, sweet potato and salmon hash, and the potatoes. Good job Chefs.  A cool aspect is that you can watch the cooks prepare your food as the cooking station is open and repurposed as a breakfast bar. They played good music too. 
Our service was terrible- there was one server who reportedly held a bad attitude since our group arrived. The reservation was for 9 people but 10 people ending up coming out to celebrate. for some reason the establishment would not accommodate providing an additional chair due to "it being their busy time" (there were PLENTY) of open chairs bc it wasn't busy, "not wanting to take chairs from the bar" and other excuses they came up with. The waiter was especially unprofessional as her demeanor was aggressive and she acted like she didn't care to serve our group. While distributing drinks her approach was "who got a lemonade? who had a tea?" As a server, protocol is that you remember who ordered what and distribute it accordingly. Anywho, I arrived a little later than the rest of the group (i was the one without a chair)& ultimately sat for over an hour without a drink or having our food orders taken. I finally called the waiter over to ask for a drink and to ask if they would accommodate one more chair per the response of the manager/owner. With an attitude and eye roll the girl responded, "no. she never told yall she would bring the chair. she said she would see what she could do but she never said she was bringing y'all another chair." when asked when someone was going to come over and give us a full and true answer she again responded. " well she can't come out on the  floor so if you want you can sit at the bar but we not bringing out another chair." Well this caused a firestorm. to shorten the story, about 30 min later someone of authority came over to the table to smooth things out- one of my friends left eliminating the need for an additional chair. The woman assigned a new waiter (who was much better, so thank you) but this did not come without confrontation between the rude girl and one of my friends from the group. There was a loud and public argument between the two- very distasteful all around. 

Once we had the new waiter, tensions eased and things got better. But my personal opinion was for the gratuity  included on the bill. a whopping 20%. Now i consider myself a good tipper and the good waiter did deserve to be rewarded but I think they should reconsider this included fee given the inexperienced workers they have, 15-18% is more acceptable as this is a far cry from fine dining where the servers deserve 20% as they are TRAINED correctly. They say never discount your worth but you also have to be real. That is a bit much in my opinion. now had we kept the rude waiter, she wouldn't have gotten a penny from me.

A note to the manager/ owner of this establishment: This isn't your first negative customer service review. While your food is good, it's not that good where people will return if they're treated like trash and expected to pay you and KEEP YOUR BUSINESS IN SERVICE. I'd hate to see a minority owned business fall to terrible service. Please fix it.

Seems anyone who voices a less than stellar opinion gets berated by the owner. 
He apparently is in denial, and his food is mediocre, and would rather belittle his customers than make necessary changes to better his restaurant. 
I noticed today that they have to advertise for business. Good restaurants need no advertising to get customers. Gordon Ramsay would have a field day here. 
Oh, BTW, I am a certified professional chef, have worked for a Master Chef, and renoun Executive chefs. I trained under culinary olympic instuctors, and a multi Food Network winning chef. I might know a thing or two about cooking food and quality. 
This owner needs to take a step down, and instead of defending the poor food, LISTEN TO THE COMMENTS, and make changes. Usually it is the untrained owners who have no experience in the restaurant industry that offend customers instead of listening. 
Coming from the city of Chicago, which is a food mecca, people of Land O Lakes leaving good reviews just have not experienced good food. Mediocre is all they know, because LOL is not loaded with restaurants. Oh, and lobster bisque SHOULD HAVE LOBSTER CHUNKS IN IT, NOT PUREED LOBSTER. Simply, bisque is a smooth soup. Lobster bisque should have small bits of lobster. If not, they are just cutting corners. As for advertising that they have the best lobster roll in land of lakes, that doesn't mean much because they are the only people that have a lobster roll in Land O Lakes.
Word of mouth, good or bad, is worth more in advertising than taking an ad out in the local paper. 
How about having an ounce of compassion and a sincere apology to those who take time to give feedback. Personally, I would take the comments and strive to make a better restaurant. Pissing customers off only drives them further away, and makes them tell others. 
So please take a moment to hear the complaints, stop defending the food, hear what people are saying, and make some changes. 
Your business has the opportunity to be great, but it takes a great respectful owner to be flexible and make positive changes.

Ocean Hai is a one of a kind, top notch, upscale, hot, new, Asian Fusion Restaurant located in the newly built Wyndham Grand Resort on Clearwater Beach. If you sit on the outdoor covered balcony, you can enjoy beautiful views of Clearwater Beach, Pier 60, and even a nice sunset if you time your visit just right! Ocean Hai does take reservations but they are not required. We were greeted by concierge and seated in a comfy booth without any wait, with no reservations!  The decor of the restaurant is very modern, open, and chic.  

We ordered the Hai Roller Deluxe Sushi Roll which featured a Lobster Salad, topped with Sriracha,Truffles, and Beef Carpaccio, the Yamada Deluxe Sushi Roll which featured Yellow Tail Tuna, topped with Sweet Chili Blue Crab, Lemon Zest, Fried Onions, and Lime Mayo, and Chinese Meatballs, which featured Pork, Crispy Onions, Serrano, and Hoisin.  The Chinese Meatballs featured 5 large meatballs, had a nice flavoring, and was very filling. The Hai Roller & Yamada Rolls were both very tasty. However, the Hai Roller was my favorite dish of the night.   

On another occasion, I had their Tandoori Spiced Scallops with Cauliflower-Yogurt Puree,  Florets, and Crispy Chick Peas, Chilean Seabass with Baby Bok Choy, Jasmine Rice, and Black Bean Sauce, Rack of Lamb with Wasabi Crust, Braised Leeks, Japanese Eggplant, and Pan Juices, Lobster Fried Rice with Saffron Rice, and Sunny Side Egg, Baby Beets with Ginger Coffee Soil, Mizuna, Goat cheese, & Caramelized Onion Spring Roll, and Fried Brussel Sprouts with Wasabi Peas, Shallots, Shitakes, & Nuoc Cham. Of those, I most highly recommend the Tandoori Spiced Scallops,  Chilean Seabass, and Fried Brussel Sprouts while I would recommend skipping the Lobster Fried Rice, Baby Beets, and Rack of Lamb.       

Our order came out in under 10 minutes and service was friendly and informative. Unfortunately there is no parking lot on site for guests to use. The valet charge is a hefty $25 and the restaurant will not validate the charge for dining there, so I'd recommend finding street parking nearby, although finding a parking spot can be a challenge on the beach.  I look forward to coming back to try the Indian Spiced Wings, Ahi Tuna Tataki, and maybe even the Kraken Roll, featuring Spicy Octopus, Salmon, Oshinko, Avocado, Wakame, Wasabi Mayo, and Eel Sauce if I can muster up enough courage on my next visit!

Kiwami Ramen & Sushi is located in a brand new Plaza off Causeway and Falkenburg next to Strand Hill Public Irish Restaurant and Canopy Road Cafe in Brandon in the Tampa Bay area. 

Lunch Specials run Tuesday through Saturday 11am til 3pm and include $4.50 select sushi rolls, $12 Sushi Lunch Combo with 5 pieces of Nigiri & Calornia Roll, $12 Sushimi Lunch Combo with 10 pieces of Sushimi, $10 Ramen soup & Rice Bowl Combo, $10 grilled shrimp rice bowl, $10 shoyu pork or chicken Ramen soup. 

The Firecracker sushi roll included spicy tuna, yellowtail, tempura chips, smelt roe, & sesame seeds. 9/10 

The Florida Sushi Roll included tuna, salmon, cream cheese, avocado, tempura chips, smelt roe, and spicy sauce. 8/10

Tempura Shrimp Roll included Shrimp Tempura, avocado, and Eel sauce. It sometimes goes by the name of Mexican and is a classic and never disappoints. 9/10 

All the sushi was fresh, I was able to get seated immediately, and the food came out in under 10 minutes. Kiwami Ramen & Sushi has a rustic vintage vibe with elegant decor and has a nice ambiance. It doesn't have the best lunch specials compared to other spots but the better decor makes up for it. Look forward to trying more sushi rolls here in the future!

The Mill Restaurant is located off Armenia at the former Ceviche Tapas Restaurant spot in the Soho District of South Tampa. We came for lunch on a Saturday and were very surprised to the place was completely empty except for 2 other patrons watching college football at the bar. Perhaps it's the college football effect! Perhaps it's because the drinks are top dollar at this location and there are no game day specials and tvs for football only at the bar. We managed to watch a little bit of the Gators game but there was no volume on the game unfortunately. I was a little disappointed the Mill's lunch menu is pretty basic with light brunch and sandwich options and not nearly as extensive as their dinner menu. 

For brunch / lunch, I got the House Smoked Turkey Sammy for $13 which came with Grilled Avocado, Sunflower Aioli, Pickled Watermelon Radish, Red Tomato, Spinach, and Sweet Onion Focaccia with a side of French fries included. The portion size of the meat in the sandwich was pretty generous and the sweet onion focaccia paired very nicely with the sandwich. 8/10 

For brunch / lunch, my friend got the BLT Sammy which came with Candied Bacon, Gem Lettuce, Tomato, Chicken Egg, Avocado, Basil Garlic Aioli on Cuban Bread with a side of French fries included. My friend was pretty pleased with the freshness of the ingredients and the unique basil garlic aioli topping. 8/10 

For Drinks, we got the healthy hangover for $14 and the house margarita for $10 which is a bit pricey for lunch. 

For Dinner dishes are divided into salads, charcuterie, first plates, second plates, third plates, and primal cuts so patrons could have a 3-5 course meal sampling if you wanted to. 

For dinner, I got the "first plate" of crispy spare ribs topped with Pineapple, BBQ Sauce, Cornbread, Creamy Ranch Slaw for $13. For $13, at most other establishments you can at least get a half rack of ribs so I felt a bit ripped off to only get 2 ribs but the ribs were longer and thicker than average and this place is considered fancy so there is a considerable up-charge. The flavor of the sauce had way too much sweet pineapple and not enough BBQ to it. I had to ask for a sweet or smoky BBQ to fix the meal but unfortunately all they had was more pineapple BBQ. 7/10

For dinner, I got the "third plate" of seared diver scallops with curried cauliflower purée, sun dried tomato exotic mushroom ragout, preserves lemon tatziki, pomegranate molasses, and carrot hay for $27. The dish came with 3 large scallops but most scallop dishes at other restaurants at least include 4 scallops. I found the mushroom ragout and curried cauliflower purée to be rather bland and requested additional spice to fix up the flavor of the meal. 7/10

I really liked the steam punk industrial style wall art of every wall of the restaurant, the old school locks hanging everywhere, and the cool industrial style bathrooms. 

For brunch / lunch, our bartender was friendly and quick to greet us, bring our food, and close out the bill as there were only 2 other patrons at the bar. 

For dinner, the bar area and restaurant were very busy but I still got great quick, friendly, service without a wait to get seated. I look forward to coming back to try the smoked apple butter grilled shrimp, pork tomahawk, and the naughty bits seared four grams. There really were a lot of items on the dinner menu that looked good! I just wish they offered them for lunch too! However, the portion size and pricing of the Mill's lunch dishes are much more reasonable and do offer a better value.

Ebisu Sushi Shack is located in the hipster Seminole Heights district of Tampa off Nebraska across from Ella's Americana Folk Art Cafe. Ebisu Sushi Shack is located in a small residential house that seems to be converted into a restaurant. This sushi restaurant abandoned the typical black and red authentic Japanese color scheme and opted for a Sushi bar area made of light wood, light wood dining tables, light wood floors, and an odd olive green colored walls. I'm not a particular fan of light colored wood. It seems a bit cheap to me. Unfortunately the metal chairs were not too comfortable, the tables were a bit too small to fit all our food, and the lighting was way too bright, not really creating a welcoming atmosphere. 

We ended up getting the ginger salad, the Godzilla Deluxe Sushi roll which featured a spicy salmon and cucumber roll, topped with spicy tuna, tempura chips, spicy mayo and Eel sauce, the Red Dragon Deluxe Sushi Roll which featured a tempura shrimp and avocado roll topped with tuna, roe, scallion, spicy mayo & eel sauce, the Electric Eye Deluxe Sushi roll which featured a spicy tuna avocado and cream cheese roll topped with smoked salmon, jalapeño, and sriracha sauce. Everything was pretty tasty.  This is a small place so I definitely recommend reservations if you don't want to wait. We had reservations and so only had a 5 minute wait, our food came out pretty quick, but closing out the check and getting refills on drinks did take a little while. Prices were very reasonable. Aside from the spot lighting, small tables, and uncomfortable chairs this place is not too bad And probably the only option for the Seminole Heights Hipster crowd for sushi.

Wow! Genghis Grill really blew my socks off! If you haven't been yet, you have to try it ! We came here for an office outing on a Friday and it was pretty busy but we got seated quickly without waiting. We all went with the famous "Build Your Bowl" option where you can select amongst over 80 fresh ingredients to make your own favorite bowl to be cooked up by the Grill Masters. 

1. Choose Your Bowl Size: 
Small, Medium, or Large 

I went with the Medium bowl and its enough to split or for 2 large meals! Id say the small bowl will give you 1 meal and the large bowl will give you 3 meals. 

2. Choose Your Protein:
Sliced Beef, Mongolian Chili Beef, Chicken Breast, Fiesta Lime Chicken*, Spicy Chicken*, Cajun Chicken*, Spicy Sriracha Chicken*, Shrimp*, Calamari, Ham, Pepperoni, Sausage, Bacon, Pork, Korean BBQ Pork, Khan's Krab, Garlic Lime Marinated White Fish, Salmon*

For he proteins I got the Mongolian Chili Beef, Spicy Chicken, Cajun Chicken, Korean BBQ Pork, and Garlic Lime White Fish. I would have chose the shrimp and calamari too bt they're only available for dinner. 

3. Season Your Protein:
Salt, Black Pepper, Yellow Curry Salt, Citrus Garlic Herb, Cayenne, Lemon Pepper, Red Pepper Flakes, Ginger, Garlic, Cajun Dragon Salt, Sweet Ginger Garlic

For the seasonings, i like it spicy so I got red pepper flakes, cayenne, pepper, and Garlic 

4. Pick Your Veggies:
Cabbage, Tofu, Onions, Bell Peppers, Carrots, Squash/Zucchini, Jalapeños, GG Peppers, Peas, Baby Corn, Water Chestnuts, Mandarin Oranges, Spinach, Bean Sprouts, Corn, Banana Peppers, Broccoli, Green Onions, Tomatoes, Potatoes, Green Beans, Pineapple, Mushrooms, Cilantro, Mint, Basil, Asian Chili, Garlic Water, Ginger Water

For the Veggies, i got Jalapeños, Peas, Spinach, Bean Sprouts, Broccoli, Onions, Mushrooms, Basil, and Cilantro. 

5.  Select Your Sauce:
Honey Soy, Sweet N Sour, Roasted Tomato, Island Teriyaki, Roasted Garlic, Thai Peanut, Mongo BBQ, 3G, Dragon, Khan Pao, Khanzu

For the sauce, I got Khan Pao which is sweet and spicy 

6.  Call Your Starch:
Steamed Rice, Brown Rice, Fried Rice, Spiral Pasta, Udon Noodles, Cabbage, Tortillas

For the sauce, I got udon noodles and steamed rice. 

After packing the bowl, the grill masters cooked it up and it was huge and delicious ! My biggest recommendation is that you put the veggies in first and put the meats on top because I put the veggies on last and they were falling off the bowl. Look forward to coming here again soon!

Fresh Kitchen is a great option for those looking to eat healthy in a casual atmosphere. You can make your own custom healthy bowl by picking 1 protein, 1 veggie, 2 bases, and 1 sauce. You have to stand in a line and pick your ingredients for your bowl, then get rung up at a register, and then can pick a table to sit and eat your custom selected healthy bowl. While the concept is similar to Chipotle, there are many more unique options as ingredients and hence its a couple bucks more too at $9 per bowl vs $6.50 for Chipotle. The decor at Fresh Kitchen is very artsy and cartoon-like with tons of health conscious things written on the wall that explain why they're so healthy for you. There's a funny sign that says "feed me kale and tell me I'm pretty" and the tables have a funky graphic of green Grass. I have to say, Fresh Kitchen is very popular with the ladies. It's about 98 percent ladies in here. I felt slightly out of place not wearing yoga pants hahaha. I've never had a bad combination of ingredients here. My favorite bases are the sweet potato noodles, sweet potato mash, and vegetable quinoa. My favorite veggies are the roasted Brussel sprouts, roasted mushrooms, Parmesan broccoli, and the sesame green beans. My favorite proteins include the chia seed tuna poke, herb grilled steak, and the Thai chicken. My favorite sauces include the coconut sriracha, cucumber jalapeño, and creamy white ginger. Although the line may look long sometimes when you first enter, I've never waited over 5 minutes in line. There's only 3 parking spots facing Kennedy in the front of Fresh Kitchen but there's tons of extra parking behind Fresh Kitchen in the back. I look forward to many more healthy dishes from here!

The Columbia Cafe Cuban Restaurant at the History Center on the River Walk in Downtown Tampa offers some of the same great Cuban food of the legendary original restaurants location in Ybor City but at a much smaller venue with no live music, no live dancing, no beautiful historic architecture, and not nearly as much air conditioned indoor seating but is accessible by boat and offers some pretty views of the water and Harbour island! 

Make sure to ask for a table at the 2nd floor terrace which has a way better view than the 1st floor terrace and has much better breeze. The 1st floor terrace has a huge thin tarp roof over it that is incredible hot during the lunch hours and is not advisable to sit there during the lunch time hours. Our hostess did not ask us if we wanted to sit in air-conditioning upstairs or at the upstairs terrace so we only learned about these options after complaining about how hot it was. If you really want to be comfortable, get a table upstairs & indoors in air conditioning but seating is pretty limited with just 6 tables in the inside area and 5 tables on the upstairs terrace, so you may want to call ahead and reserve a table in advance.

My friend got Columbia's famous "Original Cuban Sandwich", which was created in the 1890s for the cigar workers and underwent changes as immigrants from different countries came to Ybor City. The Spanish brought the ham, the Sicilians brought the Genoa salami, the Cubans brought the mojo-marinated roast pork, the Germans and Jews brought the Swiss cheese, pickle and mustard. Put it all together between sliced, freshly baked Tampa Cuban bread from the Cuban La Segunda Central Bakery and life is great. 9/10

I got the Ropa Vieja which was originally introduced to Cuba by Spanish sailors. The name means "old clothes" because the choice beef is shredded, sautéed and simmered with onions, green peppers and tomatoes, served with platanos and white rice. The Ropa Vieja was well marinated, spiced just right, a large serving, and not too salty like La Teresita's. 10/10

Everyone else in my party opted for the award winning Columbia 1905 signature salad, named for the year the restaurant was founded in Tampa's Latin district of Ybor City. The 1905 Salad was inspired by the immigrants to the Cigar City including Romano cheese from the Sicilians and the famous garlic dressing used by Cubans to marinate fresh roast pork, plus Florida tomatoes, iceberg lettuce, julienne of baked ham, Swiss cheese, and Worcester sauce. 7/10 

Everyone was pretty pleased with their meal and the view of Harbour island was nice from the 2nd floor terrace but it was pretty hot and service was super slow. Perhaps next time we will call ahead and reserve seating indoors in AIr conditioning. If you want the full 5 star Columbia experience with the flamenco dancers, live music, historic Cuban style architecture, and a more full menu of dishes, be sure to catch an uber or trolley to the original Columbia at Ybor City! If you want a quick bite downtown with a nice view this is still a nice option although not my favorite option.

Texas De Brazil Churrascaria is an amazing must try upscale Brazilian Steakhouse offering unlimited cuts of Brazilian steaks and is located off West Boy Scout Boulevard across from International Mall in Tampa next to Coopers Hawk Winery & Restaurant, Kona Grill Sushi Bar, Del Frisco's Grille, & Thai Prime Kitchen. While Texas De Brazil is pricier than most other steakhouses, the steaks are unlimited and have unique Brazilian marinades different than most other traditional American steakhouses. Texas De Brazil offers patrons a good opportunity to try all the different cuts of steaks in one sitting and if you come hungry, it can actually be a somewhat good value, especially if you come for a weekday lunch. 

Unlimited Dinner steaks are $46.99 per person, Dinner Salad Bar Buffet is &29.99 per person, Weekend Lunch with unlimited steaks 12pm-330pm is $39.99, while Weekday Lunch with unlimited steaks is $27.99. Children 2 years and under are complimentary, children 3-5 years are $5.00 and children 6-12 years are half price. For Happy Hour, Monday through Friday from 4:30pm to 6:00pm, enjoy $3 Domestic Beers, $5 glasses of TDB private label wine, $5 caipirinhas & well cocktails, and $7 premium martinis. 

The Unlimited Meats buffet includes table-side cuts of Herb-Marinated Pork Loin, Picanha, Brazilian Sausage, Leg of Lamb, Chicken Breast Wrapped in Bacon, Alcatra, Lamb Chops, Filet Mignon Wrapped in Bacon, Parmesan-Crusted Pork Loin, Garlic Picanha Braised Beef Ribs, Barbecued Pork Ribs, Parmesan Drumette, Filet Mignon, and Flank Steak. 

The Buffet Self Serve Salad Bar Area includes Sushi, 
Shrimp Salad, Smoked Salmon, Crispy Bacon, Pineapple Carpaccio, Garlic Mashed Potatoes, Moqueca Fish Stew, Brazilian Black Beans, Lobster Bisque, Sweet Fried Bananas, Brazilian Cheese Bread, Sautéed Mushrooms with Wine, Potatoes au Gratin, Steamed Asparagus, Malagueta Peppers, Spring Mix Salad, Hearts of Palm, Roasted Red & Yellow Peppers, Tabbouleh Couscous Salad, Roasted Jalapeños, Marinated Artichoke Hearts, and a cheese and meat charcuterie spread. 

My favorite cuts of meats included the Leg of Lamb, Filet Mignon wrapped in bacon, Picanha, Alcatra, braised beef ribs, and shrimp but I thought all the meats were pretty tasty. While I recommend not filling up too much on the side items on the salad bar, there's definitely quite a few can't miss dishes there too. My favorite items from the salad bar included the sushi, bacon, shrimp, asparagus, Moqueca Fish Stew, Lobster Bisque, Sautéed Mushrooms & Potatoes au Gratin. It can be challenging to get a hold of all the different meat servers to make sure you try all the different meats on your visit because there are so many options. If your card is flipped to green, servers keep coming to your table with all the meats. Once you flip your card to red, the servers stop bringing meats to your table. For dessert, I got the chocolate mouse cake and it was delicious. The decor of Texas De Brazil is elegant and modern with a view of a huge floor to ceiling wine cellar on the left and a large fountain and the water on the right. There is patio seating available as well. I look forward to coming back here to try more on a weekday for lunch soon! There are so many options here I doubt anyone can try them all in one visit!

Pho Viet Vietnamese Restaurant is located in Brandon just 3 blocks east of i75, 2 blocks east of the Brandon Mall, and is right across from O'Tooles Irish Pub in an old Pizza Hut building with the signature red hat style roof. The decor inside Pho Viet Restaurant is definitely a little outdated with a funky mix of over 5 different colors. The tables are cherry wood with teal seat backs, the floor is a very old school small pattern of medium brown, the walls are aqua, the door is red, and the the To-Go counter is an odd shade of purple that doesn't match anything else. There's bamboo half see through separators between one section of the restaurant and the other with funky led color changing back-lights. While the decor choices are a bit questionable, service is pretty quick and the food is pretty good with large portion sizes! 

We came with coworkers on a Friday during lunch time and the restaurant was approximately half at capacity for business. We were immediately seated without wait and our food came out in under 10 minutes. 

I ordered the D6 Stir Fry Steak Lemongrass Chili with Bell Pepper, Onions, Ginger, and Cilantro (Xao Xa Ot) served spicy. The serving size was very large with a large plate and the rice served on the side! I could only eat half in one sitting and had plenty of leftovers for a second meal! The spices were unlike any I've ever had and we're pretty good! 2 of my coworkers got the same dish and we were all raving about it! (10/10)

My other coworker got the chicken fried rice combo platter with peas carrots bean sports and eggs (Com Chien Hai San) and was pretty pleased with his meal. He put some hot Chilli pepper, housing, and soy sauce on there to give it a little more flavor. (7/10) 

The rest of my coworkers got large bowls of Pho Viet Northern Combination served with Rare Steak, Well-done Brisket, Well-done Flank, Tendon, Tripe and Beef Meal Ball, also served with onions, scallion, cilantro and your choice of meat below. Thai basil, bean sprouts, slice jalapeno and a wedge of lime are served on a side to be added by patrons at their own pleasure. The portion size of the soup was very large and everyone was pretty happy with their soups. (9/10)

I look forward to Stir Fry Steak Lemongrass Chili again and trying more off their menu soon!

Ciccio Water is located off Howard in South Tampa 2 restaurants down from the Green Lemon and offers a great alternative to Green Lemon's Taco Tuesday if you happen to catch them when they are too busy. On Tuesday's Ciccio Water serves awesome $2 Cali Flats which are essentially open faced tacos, $2 sangrias, and beers! One of my favorite drinks here is a slamgria which is a large glass of sangria with mini bottle of wine or champagne upside down in it that give a cool unique look to the drink. Ciccio's margaritas are also top notch! Ciccio Water offers a large selection of unique specialty sushi rolls and has some great stir frys which I think are way better than their rice bowls because all the ingredients are fully cooked. The rice bowls have some raw vegetables thrown in there and are much like the rice bowls at nature's table down the street at Hyde Park. Ciccio Waters' Red hot Thai chicken Stir fry is delicious with the Thai red curry paste and authentic tasting while offering a nice spice and is one of my favorite dishes. While the stir fry's taste pretty good they skimp on additional ingredients other than sauce, chicken, onions, and rice. Normally I'd expect a traditional Thai stir fry to include Thai noodles, nuts, carrots, and other vegetables. For sushi, I've had their Volcano, Dino and Jimmy, and Cherokee rolls and they were all pretty good. Ciccio water is also great for brunch on the weekend with their $12 bottomless mimosa special 11AM-3PM. The only catch is, the bottomless mimosas are only while you are eating so eat slow lol. Ciccio Water has a private parking lot onsite with ample parking and optional valet which is refreshing for soho. The decor is modern with blue led lighting outside and blue and pink led lighting inside. My only gripe is that the inside of the place is too open with no sound barriers and it can get very loud if you are at a middle table with whiny high pitched Soho girls all around you.  Every other Monday at 630PM, Ciccios has bikes and brews! This place is usually less busy than Green Lemon but can also have some long wait times. I recommend calling ahead to get reservations at least 1 hour ahead of time. Otherwise, you can always sit at the bar first come first served! Service has always been quick and friendly. Will be back again. Thanks! :)

I am so thankful Taco Dirty took over the vacant space on Platt and Howard in the Soho district of South Tampa! The building formerly was a worthless tiny gym that never opened and before that it was the Soho Tavern. While I do miss the Soho Tavern, another taco spot is a welcome addition to Soho! 

I'm pleased to announce that Taco Dirty now features $2 tacos $3 beers and $4 margaritas all day for Taco Tuesday and Weekdays 230pm-530pm for their Happy Hour !! On weekends if our show a Facebook post, you can get breakfast tacos with any purchase! We came for taco Tuesday and the tacos did not disappoint!

For my wrap, unlike many other taco spots with the exception of the Green Lemon, Taco dirty offers tacos in lettuce wraps instead of flour or corn tortillas to save you some calories ! 

For my protein I chose the grilled lime and sour orange chicken, grilled green poblano chicken, and sautéed pineapple pork. Additional proteins include: poblano pesto tofu, scrambled eggs, vegan beans, grilled steak, lemon fried shrimp, bbq tinga chicken, and crispy fried chicken. Steak and shrimp topping are an extra $2 per taco. 

For my veggie toppings, you can choose 2 for each taco so I got different combinations of black beans, jalapeños, rojo radish onion cilantro mix, lime jalapeño corn salad, and grilled pineapple onion salad. 

For my sauce it was a tough decision because taco dirty has a whopping 6 sauces and I could only choose 1! I went for the charcoal infused jalapeño and paid an extra quarter for some lime yogurt sriracha that was a lot lower calorie than traditional chipotle sauces that have mayo in them! There was an additional red hot sauce at the table for no extra charge. 

Everything was delicious and I'll probably order it again next time! It was so good I might even order 4 tacos so I can try the bbq and shrimp next time! Even not on taco Tuesday, taco dirty's prices are very reasonable. I look forward to many more visits in the future !

Passe-A-Grille Beach is located South of Treasure Island & St Pete Beach and North of Shell Key Island & Fort Desoto Beach and is one of my least favorite beaches in the entire Tampa Bay area.  Pass-a-Grille begins where Gulf Boulevard passes The Don Cesar Resort. Located on the southern tip of Long Key, Pass-A-Grille features old fashioned restaurants, old fashioned small inns and eclectic shops.

Pass-A-Grille got its name from Cuban fisherman, known as "Grillers," who camped along the water's edge of the island and would smoke their fish before returning home. Traveling through the pass, you could see the fires on the beaches, hence Pass-A-Grille.

Passe-A-Grille Beach has just 1 waterfront bar and restaurant named Paradise Grille but it's old fashioned & no frills serving basic burgers, sandwiches, and fried seafood outdoors on picnic tables. There are 2 old fashioned rooftop bars which offer obstructed views of the water, Hurricane Seafood Restaurant & Berkeley Beach Club. 8th Avenue has an old fashioned mainstreet type feel with 2 blocks of old fashioned restaurants including Brass Monkey, Paradise Sweets, Shadracks, the Berkeley, the Dewey, and the Sea Horse but none of them are anything to write home about. Boat tours to secluded Shell Key Island Preserve depart from Merry Pier which faces the intercoastal waterway. 

Although Passe-A-Grille Beach is approximately 4 miles, there is a very limited number of parking spots available to visitors which makes parking a very frustrating and expensive process.
