We had to circle the parking area 2 times before finally finding a spot and all street parking in front of any houses is completely prohibited unlike at other beaches. Parking fees have spiked from the typical $1.25 to 3 times the price at a whopping $3.25 an hour which adds up quickly if you're spending the whole day here. The actual area of sand between the beach entrance and the water is very small, one third the size of St Pete Beach's, not allowing for enough space to distance yourself as well as on neighboring St Pete Beach. The sand is not smooth like St Pete Beach's sand and is very rough, rocky, and quite uncomfortable to lay on with a towel. Showers are not at every beach walkway entrance. We had to walk quite a long way to finally find a shower. For these reasons, I really can't recommend Passe-A-Grille Beachbeach. I recommend neighboring beaches St Pete Beach and Fort Desoto over this beach for better facilities, smoother sand, and much easier parking options. If you want better beach bars go to St Pete Beach. If you want a complete unspoiled natural oasis with plenty of free parking, visit Fort Desoto Beach.

Surprisingly, contrary to the name, Sushi Alive does not serve any sushi that is alive. Sushi Alive Asian Bistro & Raw Bar is located in WestChase in West Tampa off Race Track Road, north of Country Way Boulevard, next to WestChase Pizza & Pasta Company, Fresh Bites, Spice Kitchen, China Bistro, Senor Tequila Mexican Grill, Hungry Greek, Grain & Berry, Village Inn, and Dunkin' Donuts. Sushi Alive is one of the biggest Sushi Restaurants I've ever seen with a very large indoor area including a very long 3 sided Sushi Bar area at the center of the restaurant, a long Bar on the right side of the restaurant and plenty of indoor high top and half booth seating. The decor at Sushi Alive is very elegant with a blend of modern and authentic Japanese. Sushi Alive features a large covered and uncovered patio area for outdoor dining as well. 

Sushi Alive has a great happy hour 5-7pm Monday through Friday with $1 nigiri, $2 sashimi, $3 select happy hour hand rolls, $4 classic rolls. The catch is, a minimum $10 order is required. Every Tuesday, Sushi Alive has 2-4-1 Sake-martinis, 2-4-1 Well liquor mixed drinks, and $8 Sake flights. 

We came on a Sunday for lunch and sat at the right side bar. Our bartender was very friendly and helpful in recommending dishes and cocktails. To drink, we ended up getting a Chocolate martini featuring Godiva chocolate liqueur, creme de cacao, & vanilla vodka and a Maui Maui cocktail featuring Mount Gay rum, Malibu rum, banana liquor, pineapple juice w/ a Meyers dark rum floater.  Our bartender told us it gets pretty busy during their happy hour and invited us to come back for it. For our entree we got the chicken pineapple teriyaki, the Tampa Sushi Roll with White Fish, and the Mexican Sushi Roll with tempura shrimp and avocado topped with spicy mayo and eel sauce. The entrees came out in under 10 minutes and were very tasty. The portion size of the chicken stir fry was very large and is big enough to split into 2 meals.  I look forward to coming back for happy hour soon!

Tokyo Japanese Restaurant & Sushi Bar serves a large selection of Chinese dishes, Japanese dishes, and Sushi with something for everyone off Hillsborough Avenue and Town & Country Boulevard in the Town N Country area of Tampa. Tokyo Japanese Restaurant is a great value for to go orders, but I really cant recommend the place for dine in. I usually get the 2 roll sushi combo for $9 and pick the Triple sushi roll that includes yellow tail tuna salmon cucumber and the rick roll which will never give you up or let you down lol and includes crab shrimp spicy mayo and cucumber. For those with bigger appetites, you can get a 3 roll combo for $13. For Chinese, I recommend the Kung pow chicken, szechuan shrimp, and sweet & sour shrimp for $5.75 which can't be beat for the price. My coworker complained that placing an order over the phone can be frustrating but we order online now and it's not so bad that way. We usually order to go. The actual restaurant leaves a little more to be desired. The tables were sticky, tables & chairs looked worn out, and the decor had a traditional Japanese look but you can tell they went for the cheapest possible decorations. The patio looks onto the wing house and the parking lot which isn't the best view and the patio area is old and run down. The Service was on the slow side. It took us a long time to close out the check and get drink refills. I was missing traditional Japanese music to complete the experience. I recommend this place for to go orders but definitely not for dine in.

Lucky Dill Westshore is a Deli and Bakery specializing in New York style sandwiches & desserts located off Boy Scout across from International Mall in South Tampa. I'm a big fan of the Lucky Dill in Downtown St Pete so I've been looking forward to the opening of this location in great anticipation for quite some time. Unfortunately the opening got delayed by 1.5-2 years allegedly due to a lien on the property from previous tenants and liquor license issues. The Lucky Dill in Downtown St Pete has $8 sandwiches and $2 domestic beers, which is pretty reasonable. However, we were a bit disappointed that this location has sandwiches for nearly double the price at $14.99 and domestic beers at quadruple the price at $8. 

The inside of Lucky Dill is decorated to look like Yankees Stadium and there is several pictures and references of New York. There is a large covered outdoor patio with string lighting and a bar that has seating in the patio and inside the restaurant. When you walk into lucky dill, there is a bakery on the right with tons of dessert options displayed clearly behind glass. What isn't displayed clearly is the price per slice for any of the desserts. After asking, it comes out that most pie slices are $6 and up. There was no wait to get seated on a Thursday evening. We got a half booth against the wall. The booth seated was comfy at least on one wall. However, Full booth seating with padded seats on both sides would have been preferred.  Our sever was very nice but the service was a bit slow and the kitchen took forever. How hard is it to put together a sandwich? Our server told us they are usually packed for lunch and the earlier dinner hours 6-7pm. 

To eat, I got the Reubenettes which come with 3 Mini Reuben sandwiches with Swiss cheese, corned beef, Sauer Kraut, Russian dressing, chips, and a dill pickle. The sandwiches were quite meaty but for the price, the quantity of food wasn't quite enough. I could have ate another mini Reubennette. I also got the Monte Cristo Sandwich which consists of thick stacks of ham, turkey, cheese, and toast dipped in egg like French toast with sweet potato fries. The monte cristo was pretty good but not really worth the price for a simple sandwich. I look forward to coming back more often to try more items on the menu when the prices go back down to the Downtown St Pete Lucky Dill levels. My suspicions are that management raised prices to make up for all the money lost during the opening delays. In the meantime, I have to recommend visiting the Downtown St Pete Lucky Dill location over this location for way better deals on drinks and sandwiches or visit Wright's Gourmet Deli or Mcalisters Deli next door!

Crazy Burrito Authentic Mexican Grill is located off West Columbus and North Armenia near Antonio's Latin Cravings, Ho Ho To Go, Taqueria Emanuel, El Tropical Cafe, and Chile's Mexican Restaurant. Crazy Burrito is a divey no frills small restaurant with 6 really old tables, old chairs, old flooring, not much wall art, and no music. The atmosphere is not very festive and the chairs are not too comfortable. This restaurant is definitely one of those restaurants where i would recommend ordering your food To Go and would not recommend eating your meal here. Crazy Burrito is most famous for their huge $10 burritos but they also serve quesadillas, tostadas, flautas, taco salad, and tacos. Crazy burrito offers tacos with Steak, Chorizo, Al Pastor (Pulled Pork), Barbacoa (Shredded Beef), Lengua (Tongue), and Campechano for $2.30 to $3, which is a tad bit pricier than their next door competitors Taqueria Emanuel and Chile's Mexican Restaurant who both serve tacos for just $2 every day. I ended up getting the Steak, Al Pastor, and Barbacoa tacos which came with cilantro and sautéed onions. I appreciate the sautéed onions which had a good flavor. The tacos came with 3 kinds of house made hot sauce including 1 red sauce and 2 green sauces. The hot sauces were not as good as Loli's Mexican Cravings or Taqueria Emanuel and therefore I'd have to recommend those taco shops over this one. They also have a larger variety of meat options.

A dear dear secret friend took me to Rasoi Indian Restaurant in ybor city to celebrate my birthday! Rasoi Indian restaurant is located on 8th Avenue and North 17th Street, just 1 block up from the main 7th ave strip, next to Game Time, Habibi Cafe & hookah lounge, Crowbar, Berninis Italian Restaurant, Lions Den, Kelly Days Firehouse Tavern, and Sahlman Seafoods.  Rasoi Indian Restaurant has outdoor and indoor dining options. Indoors, Rasoi has elegant chandelier lighting, wall art with all the types of spices, and blue led backlit Bar area but not a lot of Indian statues like other Indian Restaurants. We got the chicken saag and chicken madras Indian hot and both came out spicy and very tasty! We also got naan and pauddam. Rasoi holds a lunch buffet for $10.50 on weekdays and $12.50 on the weekend days from 11am-3pm! Get 10 percent off your bill with Yelp checkin ! Our server was friendly and quick to give us drink refills. Our food came out pretty quickly in under 10 minutes! There was only 4 other people at the restaurant on a Saturday night which was kinda sad because this place is so big it really seemed empty and the food is so good ! Please come out and support them so they can stay open ! Look forward to visiting again soon !

Pho Hoang Vietnamese Restaurant is located off US Highway 301 South & South Falkenburg Road in Riverview near Tampa in a shopping plaza next to Pizza Hut, Subway, China 1, Crazy Cafe, GNC, and Publix Supermarket. In fact, you really have to have GPS on to know where to look because there's a huge tree blocking any visibility of the restaurant sign from the road. Pho Hoang Vietnamese has 42 variations of Pho Soups, 29 variations of vermicelli noodle bowls, 29 variations of rice platters, 11 variations of banh mi sandwiches, and even bun bo hue. The Pho Hoang restaurant chairs and tables are pretty basic and divey but the pretty Vietnamese wall art of waterfalls, beaches with cliffs, and a charming Vietnamese fishing village really elevate the decor out of the dive category. 

I got the Steak & Shrimp Rice Platter with green onions, dried shallots, pickled daikon & carrots, cucumbers, and broccoli. For a $1 up-charge, I added a sunny side up fried egg to the order. The portion size was very large and the steak was lean, crispy, and well marinated. The shrimp were pretty good too! Mixed up with the provided spices, the dish was very good. 8/10

My coworkers got the medium beef pho soup which actually came in a huge 60 ounce soup bowl so big that no one was able to finish it. The medium pho is enough for 2 meals. If you're not super hungry, a small 40 oz bowl of pho is perfectly adequate. Pho soups come in baby size in 20 oz, small in 40 oz, medium in 60 oz, and large in 80 oz. The pho is a Vietnamese soup made by boiling beef stock for a very long time. The pho consists of flavorful spices, thin noodles, topped with steak, cilantro, onion, bean sprouts, Thai basil, cilantro, lime, and jalapeño peppers. The soup was very flavorful and a large serving size. 8/10 

On another occasion I had the vermicelli noodle bowl and I definitely have to say I prefer the rice platter over the noodle bowl because the rice absorbs the spices better. When compared to the other Brandon Vietnamese restaurant, Pho Viet, I'd say that Pho Hoang is on average $2 more per dish but Pho Hoang has larger serving sizes and uses better marinades and spices. The Pho Hoang Vietnamese restaurant is very large to accommodate many patrons with 2 separate rooms. During lunch on a weekday, there was no wait to be seated, our server greeted us promptly and food came out in under 10 minutes. I look forward to coming back to try more dishes in the future!

Sea Salt Seafood Restaurant is located in downtown St Petersburg in the 2nd floor of the Sun Dial Plaza next to Locale Market off 2nd Street and 2nd Ave. Sea Salt has a spacious outdoor patio offering nice views of the Sun Dial Plaza water fountains, Dolphins, and downtown high rises. When you first walk in the door of Sea Salt, you are greeted by the freshly caught fish of the day which sometimes even includes a Swordfish, a large spice rack, and the concierge. The entire decor of this restaurant oozes perfection and upscale style that really puts a bow on our restaurant visits. We came for their happy hour which runs 4PM-7PM and includes half off wines, beers, liquors, appetizers, and select entrees. We ended up ordering the Chilean Sea Bass Fish Tacos, Swordfish Sandwich, Wagyu short rib beef burger, and baked oysters. Our server greeted us in under 5 minutes, offered refills promptly, and checked on us to see if we liked our meals after they came out. Our food came out in under 10 minutes and all our dishes had generous portion sizes, came with fries, and were quite tasty.  Usually swordfish comes out dry but this one was well marinated and just right. I was a little disappointed sea salt didn't offer any other hot sauce besides tabasco for the fish tacos but they were still quite tasty. I was very impressed with the modern nautical decor of the place. The large wrap around bar has an elegant marble white bar surface, while you look onto fresh seafood chilling on ice. Even with the half off discount, their margaritas ended up being $5 while their martinis were $7, so their drink prices do run above average. I came before for a seafood and scotch pairing special event and had a wonderful time. Their happy hour is an incredible deal. Where else can you get swordfish and Chilean sea bass for $7? I look forward to catching their happy hour again and coming back and trying their Brazilian fish ribs when they're back in season!

Bollywood spice Indian cuisine restaurant is located in Clearwater right next to countryside mall off us 19. There is a private lot for parking. There's an Indian market next door too! We got the Chicken vindaloo, a spicy dish from Goa, India with chicken ,potatoes, tangy and a spicy brown sauce and the Chicken Kadai which features marinated chicken, sautéed onions, bell peppers, and tomatoes. We got the king fisher premium lager beer from Bangalore, India and it taste remarkably like a heneiken beer. We were seated quickly with no wait when we arrived and our food came out in under 10 minutes. It took a little while to get our check to close out but I didn't even mind because I loved the traditional Indian dance videos and music displayed on screen!  We got our food Indian hot and it was definitely spicy! Probably my favorite Indian restaurant yet. It was large and I felt really the most immersed in the culture! Can't wait to come back and try more dishes !

Why 3 stars? Taste of India buffet had some good Indian dishes but only offered 2 chicken dishes, 1 fish dish, no beef, no goat, and too many vegetarian dishes. Most other Indian buffets I've been to have had at least 5-6 chicken and beef dishes. 

Comparatively, the value for this place was not as good as the buffets at curry leaves or Kennedy Indian grill. I did try all of the vegetarian curry dishes but I ended up having 2 helpings of the Chicken dish, the butter chicken. The other chicken dish, the tandoori chicken, had too many small bones and was quite cumbersome to eat, so i didn't bother. 

Taste of India buffet is located in a huge building with lots of great indian wall art. I liked the indian place-mats with their map of India. I really liked the pancake balls for dessert! They were so tasty! It was great to try a large variety of dishes in one spot. 

So far, the Indian buffet at curry leaves and the Indian place off Westshore were both better than this place but the food I had was still good. 

None of the dishes were spicy and some would say the sauce was kinda watered down but the waitress brought me some extra spice to remedy the lack of spice. 

Unfortunately the hot sauce the waitress brought out was not enough and the waitress never returned for me to be able to ask for more hot sauce. Unfortunately, there's only 1 waitress for the whole restaurant but since there's a buffet, this won't really effect most patrons too heavily. I Look forward to trying more indian buffets in the future to get a better basis for comparing indian buffets.

Ulele Restaurant and Brewery founded by the owners of the Columbia Restaurant brings purpose to the most northern end of the Tampa Riverwalk and is a great addition to the mostly undeveloped Tampa Heights area just north of Downtown Tampa.  Ulele offers beautiful views of the Hillsborough River, is next to the Ulele Spring, & Waterworks park.  Ulele Restaurant has brick on the outside and a real industrial theme with the gears on the entrance door. The outside of the restaurant's bike racks feature sweet metal dog statues. Ulele was named after a native american princess and features a vibrant fusion of ingredients from Florida waters and land once home to many Native Americans.  Many moons ago, I came to eat here with family. For the appetizer, we got the famous Alligator hush puppies which featured alligator, country ham, bacon, corn, jalapeno, honey datil pepper sauce and fresh ground horseradish aoili. For the entree, I got the Seafood Risotto which featured horno-roasted stuffed lobster, butter poached lobster claw, 2 head-on gulf shrimp, saffron parmesan risotto, and a charmed corn cream sauce.  My step-dad got the Mahi Mahi Oriente which featured bronzed Mahi with anjou pear salsa, fresh watercress tossed with craisins, sliced almonds, sunflower seeds, and a spicy jalapeno pear vinaigrette. Service was quick and cordial although the food took a bit longer to come out than usual. My opinion of the food was that it was a bit over-priced at $28 per plate and I was not amazed by anything in particular. The menu pricing would warrant a more elegant atmosphere than the industrial theme that was at this establishment but I appreciated all the cool art here. They had glowing seahorses by the grill, a cool fish made out of motorcycle parts, and a cool glass fish by the inside.  Since Ulele is located on the Hillsborough river, there are some docks that you can dock your boat at. These docks are officially part of the Waterworks park next door but they can be used for dining at Ulele if needed too.  

On a more recent visit on bikes, I tried a flight of brews from Ulele Spring Brewery which included: Rusty's Red Ale, Water Works Pale Ale, Ulele Light, Magbees Honey Lager, Maple Infused Black Beer, Bourbon Barrel Riverwalk India Pale Lager, Seasonal Deadeye Rye and they were all pretty good! My favorite was the Magbees Honey Lager. We got a tour of the 2,100-square-foot Ulele Spring Brewery in front of the beer garden which creates 15 U.S. barrels or 465 gallons per brew.  We had the pleasure of meeting Head Brewmaster Timothy Shackton who originally was a brewmaster at Hops Brewery under John Schwarzen of Anheuser-Busch and was very knowledgeable in explaining how the brews were derived from malted grains, hops, yeast, fresh fruit and locally sourced honey. We witnessed how a freshly made margarita and mojito were made without pre-made mixers like at many other lesser establishments. The difference was definitely noticeable!

Wow! $3 margaritas, martinis, and sangrias? Sign me up! Tequilas Mexican Restaurant features amazing happy hour deals including $3 Margaritas, sangrias and martinis from open until 7pm every day! After many visits, I decided to honor tequilas with a review! I usually just come here for drinks but after seeing their loaded steak fajitas, I had to try them! For only $10, you get unlimited servings of steak fajitas w grilled onions and peppers. I normally can barely finish 1 round of fajitas but I was up for a challenge. The steak came out perfectly, as it was well marinated, a good thickness, flavorful, tender, lean, and not chewy! With such good steak I was able to conquer the fajitas and get a second helpings to get my money's worth for sure! A guy next to me  was able to get an incredible four rounds of steak fajita servings which was pretty impressive. With enough training, one day I hope to follow in his footsteps. Our server was pretty friendly and kept the drinks and food coming. Our food came out in under 15 minutes and there were 5 kinds of hot sauces which paired nicely with the fajitas and is sure to be a good crowd pleaser. I saw quite a few tables get the enormous steak nachos and it looked like a great serving size. It's definitely large enough to share with a friend. My friend got the shrimp, spinach, and cheese Empanadas which looked delicious and was pleased with his meal. We were treated to some talented live music by a guitarist. There is plenty of free street parking available in ybor city but It can be tricky to find a spot sometimes. Tequilas features Mexican star lights hanging high from the ceiling, several parrots hanging from the ceiling, and even the traditional mexican sugar glow skulls. I look forward to trying the nachos on my next visit!

We managed to catch the tail end of happy hour at the newly opened O Cocina and Flights Restaurant and Bar on Friday night. O Cocina's happy hour runs from 4:00 PM to 6:00 PM Monday to Friday and includes $5 margaritas, select appetizers, house wines, and well drinks. I really wish they'd extend their happy hour til 7 because it is tough to take advantage of it. O Cocina was not too busy on Friday at 530PM and we still managed to grab 3 seats at the bar and order our drinks pretty promptly. Our bartender was very knowledgeable and friendly. The bar features cool cacti growing vertically on the wall and upside down on the ceiling. The color pattern of all the cacti based on how different cacti were planted together is really interesting. O Cocina features one of the coolest bar designs I've seen in a long time. The restaurant features several modern circular booths, rustic circular drop down lighting, and a separate party room for large parties with lots of stone and earth tones. The vibe of the restaurant is more earthy and natural than modern which is a welcome change. The outside of o Cocina has 5 rows of cacti and looks pretty cool. The margaritas are really good here and my friends enjoyed their Cabernet Sauvignon and Pinot. There is a large private parking lot on site and we had no trouble parking. There is a valet offered here but it is optional and not forced which is nice. O Cocina is located in south South Tampa off Henderson, after S Dale Mabry next to the Blind Goat and is a welcome addition to this underserved immediate area. Much like Blind Goat, their happy hour ends way too early. Their drinks after happy hour are a bit spendy, averaging $12. You can get 3 tacos for $18 and their entrees run $20-$28. As a new restaurant 2 weeks in business, they definitely have some growing pains. I called their phone number listed and it was disconnected. I thought: Have they gone out of business already? I had to message them on facebook to confirm that they were still open. Not everyone will do this and they need to fix this quickly if they want to stay open. Evidently they're having internet issues so their phones don't work. Not a good start or making it easy for people to make reservations. O Cocina also had no music playing on their visit. It's still not setup after 2 weeks in business. If you want a 5 star experience, you might want to wait another couple weeks until they work out their opening issues. I look forward to trying some tacos bocaditos or ceviches on our next visit!

Why 5 stars? Because they got the best complimentary salsa, amazing taco Tuesday shrimp tacos, amazing shrimp quesadillas, and I keep coming back for more!! This one of my favorite go-to spots! 

Urban Cantina is one block north of Kennedy and one block east of Ashley in Downtown Tampa, just a couple blocks from Curtis Hixon Park. Urban Cantina is a great place for California style Mexican food if you're in the downtown area. We came for Taco Tuesday and ordered Carne asada, shrimp grilled fish, and avocado bean veggie $2 tacos. The tacos were bigger than Catrinas and Bar Taco and more closely to the size of green lemon which was nice. We also took advantage of the drink specials which included $3 coronas, $5 margaritas. Our meal came with amazing home made thick chips and salsa. Our service was pretty quick and courteous although it was pretty busy. I really have to subtract points for decor as the tin ridged walls makes the place feel like a cheap tool shed, the chairs or tables were not comfortable or stylish, and the lighting was a bit harsh because it was a bit bright, overhead, and yellow spot light style. We really couldnt get a good vibe going as the music wasn't too great and was way too soft. If they could improve the music, increase the volume of the music, and dim the lights a scotch it would definitely go a long way! For now, I definitely prefer the home base for Ciccios and Green Lemon in Soho with a more lively vibe and more chic feel. If I lived in downtown I'd definitely frequent the place but I wouldn't go out of my way to go back. Especially due to how difficult it can be to park downtown. I might come by on bike though. They have a pretty good brunch deal going on the weekend 11AM-2PM which includes a breakfast or regular burrito and unlimited mimosas and margaritas for $20 which is pretty inticing however.

Rouen Thai Restaurant is located off West Gandy, 2 blocks east of the Publix and Target on Gandy in South South Tampa. Rouen Thai featured some great authentic Thai decor by the entrance and throughout the restaurant, lit up with holiday lights, to create a festive atmosphere. Rouen Thai features a large sushi bar and has lots of sushi options. Unfortunately Rouen Thai only has 4 booths and all the booths were taken when we visited. However we were able to take a non booth table without a wait. The parking lot was full yet the restaurant had 4 open tables so I see parking potentially being an issue here if it gets any busier. Happy hour included 2 for $3 domestic brews which was a plus! 

We got the Alaskan Roll, Steak Pad Thai ordered Thai hot, and the Garlic Pepper Chicken. Unfortunately the Steak Pad Thai that I ordered to be Thai hot was not spicy at all. Unfortunately, the Rouen Thai's spice rack only had 3 spices instead of the traditional 4 thai spices and was missing my favorite Red Garlic Chili paste! I like it so much I even have it at home! If I can stock it, they should be able too as well. Currently Rouen Thai is offering Sriracha as a substitute for the Red Chili Garlic paste. While I do enjoy Sriracha. I enjoy the red chili garlic paste more with Thai Food. Unfortunately, I couldn't spice up the pad thai quite to my liking. The Garlic Pepper Chicken didn't have enough pepper spice and came out with a bit too intense Garlic flavor in a garlic soup of sorts and also was not the best. However, I must say the Alaskan sushi roll was top notch with the tempura salmon, avocado, spicy mayo, eel sauce, and crispy Japanese bread crumbs! 

The wait for food was a little long at 20 minutes but our server gave good Service and a couple refills on our drinks. The Thai tea was a little too sweet for my tastes and they offer good drink specials which is nice. I'd come back for the Sushi, just not the Thai Food because they're lacking the proper spices. Management, please stock some red chili garlic paste and make your thai hot dishes spicier!

The WTR Pool & Grill overtook the spot formerly known as Hogan's Beach Bar, the Beach Bar, and Crabby Bills Beach Bar. WTR Pool & Grill added a resort style pool, hot tub, and private cabanas for the ultimate Miami style pool parties, with an indoor restaurant, and an outdoor restaurant chill lounge area separated from the pool party area. 

On the restaurant side, not much has changed since the renovations of the beach bar named establishment other than a couple menu additions and the seafood is not the best. On the restaurant side, patrons can still enjoy cocktails in comfy lounge chairs with a fire and enjoy a nice view of the sunset. I highly recommend coming here for drinks or to see the sunset on the chill restaurant side during the weekdays. 

WTR pool & Grill is located on Rocky Point just off the Causeway less than 8 minutes from the Tampa Airpot next to The Godfrey Resort and offers views of the water and Whiskey Joe's Waterfront Bar & Grill. 

Monday through Friday 4-7, WTR has a $5 happy hour, Thursday nights are for karaoke, Friday's feature live music 11am to close, Saturday's feature $4 rose 11am to 5pm, and Sunday's are their biggest funday Sunday pool party days. 

On Saturdays and Sundays, WTR Pool & Grill charges $20 admission for guys, $10 admission for ladies, and $20 for valet to access the pool party area. During the weekdays there is no cover charge or valet charge to access the pool area. I highly advise parking at Whiskey Joe's next door for just $2 and walking over to save some bucks.

If you're coming for the pool party, be prepared to dish out some serious dough as drinks are not cheap. If you want a private cabana there's a $300 spending minimum. If you order a bottle, the whole squad of lady bartenders comes out in celebration blowing whistles carrying WTR letters, carry flags, and a guy comes around blasting smoke everywhere to let everyone know you spent too much on a bottle lol. It's a nice touch to say they appreciate you spending that kinda money on a bottle and it creates an air of festivity and excitement that is similar to many pool parties in Miami. When it gets busy it can take quite a while to get table service or drinks at the bar. During the pool parties, the DJ plays some great music, the sound system sounds great, everyone at the pool gets really into the dancing with some serious twerking going on, and everyone seems to be in great spirits. 

Although I ended up spending way more than I would have liked to during WTR pool parties, it was a lot of fun. I definitely will be back to enjoy more sunsets on the chill restaurant side or during the weekdays when there is no cover or valet charge.

Izakaya Tori Japanese Restaurant is a new Japanese Restaurant that serves Sushi, Ramen, Grilled Skewers, & Japanese Tapas and has taken over the former JoTo Thai Sushi spot in South Tampa off South Dale Mabry and Azeele, Across from LA Fitness Gym, Cycle Bar, Ciccio Cali, and next to Sunshine Spa, Blow Bar Express, Press Box Emporium Sports Bar, & Shells Seafood. 

To drink we got the Kirin Ichiban Japanese lager & Summer Breeze with Raspberry syrup, Yuzu juice, club soda, and sake. 8/10 

For an appetizer, we got the lotus root chips with ponzu Guacamole. The guacamole could have used a bit more spice and flavor but was not too bad. The lotus root chips had a unique flavor. 7/10 

The Mexican Sushi roll came with tempura shrimp, avocado, spicy mayo & smelt roe and was pretty tasty. 8/10

The Spider Sushi roll Soft shell crab, avocado, asparagus & scallions, smelt roe, sesame seed with eel sauce. 8/10 

The Futomaki sushi roll consisted of shrimp tempura, cream cheese, jalapeno, avacado, tobiko, scallion, spicy mayo, and eel sauce. 9/10 

All the sushi was fresh and tasty. Service was quick and friendly. The decor of the restaurant looked festive with lots of Japanese writing everywhere, exposed brick walls, and sumarai armor on display. The Music playing was mostly light contemporary pop and was not traditional Japanese music like most of other sushi restaurants. I look forward to coming back soon to try more off the menu!

I'm so glad to welcome Psomi Greek American Bakery & Eatery to the North Howard NoHo South Tampa neighborhood! I've been eyeing the construction of Psomi for quite some time in eager anticipation of its opening as I pass by the area often on my way from Soho to the interstate. It's a shame Psomi is only open until 3pm because they're closed most of the time I pass by in the evening and it's been a tough place to catch open. Psomi elevates the entire North Howard Avenue area with its brand new beautiful building and helps make North Howard no longer just an area you pass by on the way to the interstate. Psomi is located next to another new California style building, Clinical Research of West Florida, and is across the street from a recently renovated Bryan Glazer Family JCC Fitness Center.

Our server told us Psomi literally translates from Greek to "bread" but its essence refers to the best bite, the "choice" piece, the crumb that everyone at the table fights over. The Decor of the Psomi restaurant is very modern, open, and elegant with large slide out glass panels that extend the open air feel through the back patio and Greek wall art everywhere. However, unlike Acropolis Greek Taverna, off Kennedy, Psomi does not feature any live music, napkin throwing, or belly dancers. 

We came to Psomi for brunch on a Sunday and it was packed with an hour wait for good reason! Psomi is the new hot spot! Psomi's parking lot was full and 2 blocks of cars lined both sides of Cass street. Luckily, there was patio seating available for us to wait and we could order coffee or to-go items from Psomi's bar. Due to the ability to purchase to-go, our wait for a table ended up being much less than an hour, and only about 25 minutes. I definitely recommend making reservations in advance here! 

Our multiple servers that stopped by our table were friendly and knowledgeable but did not seem to communicate between each other as we had to tell 3 people the same thing of what we ordered and that someone already took our order. Once we ordered, food came out in under 10 minutes which was nice. We found it a bit odd that Psomi did not have the most famous best Greek appetizer on its menu, Baha Ganoush, but it turns out they just call it melitzanosalata and it also has eggplant in it. Unfortunately, one of our many servers brought the entree out before the appetizer so we just canceled the appetizer because it missed the whole point of being before the entree.

The Pork Gyro came with hand stacked pork, tzatziki, tomato, red onions, on a pita with some amazingly spiced fries that were some of the best I've had in a long time! The meal was filling and the pork was lean and not greasy. Aside from all the fries in a container, there were additional fries inside the Gyro too which I'm not sure is sloppy or meant to be a cool new thing. I'll give them the benefit of the doubt,and chock it up to being a cool new thing. The fries were so good, I don't mind getting more of them. 10/10 

The Chicken Souvlaki also came with tzatziki, tomato, red onions, on a pita with some amazingly spiced fries! The marinade on the chicken was very unique and good! 10/10 

For dessert, we split the baklava coffee cake. It was a pretty big serving enough to adequately split between 3 people, was surprisingly not dry, and not too sweet so I liked it. However, if I do order dressert, I prefer something with chocolate in it. But when in Greece, you gotta try theocal specialities! 7/10 

Although service was a bit off and the place is a bit pricier than average, all our food was really good and I really like that this place elevates the entire North Howard area! On my next brunch visit, I look forward to trying the Psomi bagel special with salmon, avocado, cucber, tomato, & cream cheese!

Epicurean Autograph Collection Hotel by the Marriott is nestled in the heart of South Tampa just off South Howard across from the legendary Berns Steakhouse and features cooking classes led by professional chefs, couples massages, facials, a rooftop bar (Edge), rustic restaurant (Elevage), and patisserie (Chocolate Pi), over 1,000 wines in their wine shop (Bern's Fine Wines & Spirits), 3 event spaces, catering services, and even pool parties! 

On my most recent visit, I had the pleasure of celebrating a dear friends baby shower on the 2nd floor deck under a large royal tent which accommodated 6 tables with parties of 6.  We enjoyed 5 different kinds of macaroons, cupcakes, charcuterie, fine cheeses.  Servers brought around horderves including a veggie sushi roll, scallops, and cheese balls. Our very own personal bartender served some excellent wines and whiskey's and was quite friendly.  

For brunch, I ordered the brunch burger with dry aged beef, fried egg, country ham, tomato, and espresso mayo. A friend of mine got the shrimp and grits with peppers and a soft cooked egg.  Another friend of mine got the fritatta du jour which featured broccoli, cheddar, and bacon.  Our food came out in under 15 minutes and everyone liked their meal. Service was top notch! I look forward to coming back to the Epicurean Hotel again soon for another great event soon! The Epicurean Hotel provides the perfect compliment to the Soho District of South Tampa, bringing an heir of class and sophistication with all its many offerings, filling many previous voids to many Soho residents, and has offered nothing but a pleasure on every visit !

Roux is the best spot in Tampa Bay to enjoy authentic Creole cuisine in an atmosphere reminiscent of historic New Orleans. Roux brings a little bit of New Orleans to Tampa. Once you step inside and leave the strip mall exterior behind, you are transported to a charming historic Bourbon Street atmosphere with brick walls, a pressed tin ceiling, and elegant nostalgic gaslight fixtures. The bar & lounge area provides an atmosphere reminiscent of the New Orleans Latin Quarter.  Roux's carefully curated menu brings the best of Creole cuisine to your plate. The term "Roux" is used to thicken sauces and made with flour and fat or butter cooked together. 

I highly recommend making reservations at least a week or two in advance for those wishing to get a table or for those with large parties. I called the night before and reservations were fully booked for Saturday so definitely call further in advance. The dining room area only seats 8 or 9 tables and this place is always pretty busy on the weekend for good reason. The food is well worth the wait! Luckily, the bar and lounge area is first come first serve and we managed to snag some seats at the bar area which feature some elegant marble granite countertops without waiting. 

For our entree, we got the classic shrimp and cream cheese grits which featured pan seared gulf shrimp in Abita beer gravy on top of some delicious creamy grits.  The creole style seasoning provided a hint of spice and the cheese in the grits was truly recognizable and made the dish so good. 10/10 

For our other entree, we got the Andouille Crusted Wahoo which featured creamed cheese yellow grits, Roux butter Coulis, chive aioli, and even some crispy country ham. Our server brought out a little extra side of spicy sauce for me to spice up the dish and it was a large serving and very tasty! The serving size is a bit bigger than the shrimp and grits. However, I dare say I like the spices on the shrimp and grits a little better. With the extra spicy sauce I got, it's a pretty close tie!  10/10 

For our dessert, we got the bread pudding featuring baguette, pecans, poppy seeds, Buffalo trace bourbon butterscotch sauce in an amazing flavored combination! The dessert was very large, served hot, and we couldn't finish it with 2 people. You might even be able to share this dish with 4 people as we had to take half of this dessert home. 9/10

Our bar-side servers Carissa and Taylor were very friendly, knowledgeable, and attentive. If you sit at the bar, you'll be in good hands! I look forward to coming back soon to try their snapper Oscar, grouper meuniere, crawfish etouffee, or butter seared scallops! With all the great sounding seafood options, it was pretty tough to decide on a dish! Make sure to come here for some top notch Creole! You'll love it!

Sea-Guini is an upscale Seafood and Italian Restaurant located at the Opal Sands Resort on Clearwater Beach featuring beautiful views of the resort pool and beach. Even at night, when you can't see the beautiful views outside as well as during the day, you are treated to beautiful modern chic decorations that really pop with led back-lighting. When we first arrived we were greeted by concierge and immediately noticed the cool color changing led back lit fish that was comprised of smaller shaped fish, a glass semi see through wall of wines, and modern sculptures that really had our interests peaked in checking out this restaurant before we even walked through the entrance. We were seated at a high top table for four next to a stunning glass partition that contained water and bubbles flowing through it in cool patterns around balls in the glass. It changed colors slowly from Blue to green to red to purple to pink and back again. Behind this partition there was another dining room with a wall that featured coral on the wall, accent paint and led back lighting. There was a private party room separated by a glass wall so you could get a peak at the unique decor but I didn't take a picture of it because it was occupied. At the wrap around bar, there were interesting backsplash tiles, interesting modern pendant lights, a brick oven stove built in for pizzas, and a clear window to see the chef work his magic. For the appetizer, on the house, we were treated to 3 types of fresh baked breads with 2 types of Mediterranean dipping sauces. For the entree, I got the Cajun style grouper Tacos with pepper truffle fries that paired nicely with hot sauce and honey mustard. Before we were greeted by concierge, I saw it on their lunch menu and it was not available on their dinner menu but they still let me order it, so I definitely appreciate the kitchens flexibility. Others in my party got the Mediterranean tuna salad, lobster crab cakes, lobster bisque, and Opal Sands salad. Unfortunately, there was a lengthy 5 minute wait for a spoon for the soup sitting right in front of us, so the soup had to be sent back because it got cold. When the soup did arrive, at the correct temperature, it was good. Sea-guinis bill finalizing procedure is unlike any other restaurants because they ask for the tip before taking your credit card. The waiter explained that this provides greater security because the waiter can't add a zero to the tip and that we can see the final bill. The waiter brought out our receipt and it was much higher and for another tables! We were assured that they ran the correct card for the correct bill even though they brought the wrong bill with the right credit card to the wrong table and provided no proof or double checking of the billing... This lack of reassurance kind of left us uneasy... My step dad will have to check online just to make sure that we were in fact billed correctly... Aside from the hassle of seaguini staffs sloppy billing procedures, we had a great time at Sea-guinis and look forward to our next visit!

Ichiban Japanese Sushi Bar is located off Fowler and Bruce B Downs near USF in the North Tampa area behind Chili's, in a shopping Plaza next to Chicken Salad Chick, Grain & Berry, Tijuana Flats, Wingstop, Goldstone Creamery, China 1, SoFresh, Pho Quyen Vietnamese, Taj Indian Cuisine, Boba cup, First Watch, Fire House Subs, Jason's Deli, and Five Guys. 

I got the Lunch Special Bento Box with a Futomaki Roll, Lighting Roll, Mexican Roll, Crab Salad, Black Seaweed Salad, and a Cucumber Seaweed Salad. Overall it was very filling, fresh, and tasty. 9/10 

The cucumber seaweed salad came with clear noodle, crab, seaweed and ponzu sauce. 7/10 

The Sweet Black Seaweed Salad came with black hijiki seaweed salad in sweet soy. 6/10 

The Futomaki roll came with Carrots, cucumber, fish powder, hijiki, egg, crab. 8/10 

The Mexican roll came with fried shrimp, avocado, carrot, smelt roe. 9/10 

The Lightning roll came with baked spicy salmon skin, cream cheese, scallion, smelt roe, asparagus. 9/10 

There was no wait to get seated on a Friday for lunch and our order came out in under 10 minutes. The decor of Ichiban Japanese Sushi Bar is a blend of traditional Japanese style, modern, and upscale. It definitely would be a good spot for a date meet up. They don't have the best lunch deals in the area but the decor and atmosphere make up for it! Look forward to trying more off the menu soon!

Red Robin's gourmet burgers restaurant is located at citrus Park mall off Gunn highway and features tons of Art, even on the ceilings! Red Robin has a nice air conditioned indoor patio with a view of mall patrons  passing by, a large bar with a sparkling unique maroon style granite, and plenty of TV's for watching sports. I sat at the bar where I was promptly greeted by the bartender who gave me a menu. It was tough finding the right burger as there was a whopping 3 pages of burgers but my bartender steered me in the right direction. I ordered the A1 peppercorn burger which came with pepper jack cheese, pepper seasoned bacon, crispy onions, lettuce, and tomato. I added sautéed onions, mushrooms, and jalapeños to the burger to give it a little sizzle and quite a kick! For the fries, I got a side of Chipotle and honey mustard in addition to the ketchup which paired quite nicely. I ordered my burger medium rare and it came out perfect with a touch of pink, was quite tender, and the condiments were all great. The burger was so big I could barely eat it, but I managed! My bartender even came by to ask if I wanted more fries which has never ever happened to me before and I thought that was a nice touch. Wrapping up the bill was a quick process as well. There are plenty of parking spaces on site available in the citrus mall parking lot by the food court area that is not on the side of the movie theaters. I look forward to my next visit!

Pinky's breakfast restaurant is located in south tampa off bay to bay. We got the best damn Benedict which comes with all natural turkey sausage, English muffin, spinach, soft poached eggs, and a savory tomato thyme hollandaise with rosemary potatoes. We also got the Tuscan frittatas open faced omelette with prosciutto, all natural turkey breast, rosemary, spinach, onion, tomato, provolone cheese and rosemary potatoes. For the side, you can choose rosemary potatoes, geechie boy grits, fruit, or whole wheat toast. You can substitute egg whites for an extra buck. 

Pinkys features an outdoor patio and has an old school diner feel with some old school 1950's pop rock playing. The waiting list clipboard is on a pair of pink legs which is kinda funny. Pinky's has a wide variety of old school funny coasters for $5 each. Theres a fox and a pig head on the wall with some creepy looking eyes. The coffee is self serve for $3. The parking spaces are way too tight. The car to the left of me and the right of me were over the line. Pinky's was pretty busy on a Sunday at 1030 but we got seated within 10 minutes.

The Oceanaire Seafood Room is a top of the line debonaire Seafood Restaurant in Downtown Indianapolis, Indiana. The Oceanaire Seafood Room was established in 1998 with a mission to provide guests with the Ultra-Fresh Seafood Experience, featuring seasonal and sustainable seafood that is flown in from all over the world fresh daily and featured in a chef-driven changing menu that makes seafood truly exceptional.

The Raw Bar custom platter is made to order with shrimp, lump crab, king crab legs, Australian lobster tail, Russian osetra gold caviar, chef select oysters & stone crab claws. Our Raw Bar platter selections included Alaskan King Crab legs, Australian Lobster tails, and chef select oysters. Everything was fresh and tasty. 9/10

The Shrimp cocktail appetizer came with 5 jumbo shrimp and cocktail sauce. 8/10 

The Shrimp & Grits came with just 4 jumbo shrimp, Grits, and cajun butter sauce. 7/10 

The Filet Mignon & Shrimp came with 3 jumbo shrimp, filet mignon, and 2 pieces of asparagus.  

The Seared Massachusetts Sea Scallops came with 4 large diver scallops, Squid Ink Linguini, Scallion Cream Sauce, Parmesan. The scallops tasted nice but the portion size of this dish including the pasta is small so while this is tasty, I can't recommend order this if you're super hungry. 8/10 

The Surf & Turf came with 10 oz center cut Filet Mignon & West Australian Lobster Tail. The steak was cooked medium rare, wll marinated, and not overcooked and the lobster paired nicely with the butter. 9/10 

The Chicken Fried Lobster with Grits came with fried Lobster, Grits, Truffled Honey, Cheesy Grits, and House Hot Sauce and the as absolutely delicious! This is a one of a king dish you won't see at many places but so good! 10/10

The Baked Alaska Dessert came on Fire and is quite the head turner when it's lit up. It's great for a photo opportunity but the fruity ice cream combined with the chocolate sponge cake was not my favorite combination and I can't find a full description of the contents of this dish anywhere to tell you what exactly is in it. 6/10 

If you're in the Downtown Indianapolis and looking for upscale exotic seafood flown in from the best spots around the world, I definitely recommend you visit Oceanaire Seafood Room!

I'm so happy that Sparkman Wharf has successfully brought back crowds to the Channelside District like back when it featured Banana Joes, Margarita Mamas, and the AMC theater! After 3 weeks of being open, there's still big crowds here and a lively atmosphere with some great live music! Im happy Sparkman wharf bulldozed down the restaurants blocking the view of the bay and really opened up the view of the bay! I like the open areas of green and all the games they have out which include giant chess and Corn-hole! With the crowds it can be a challenge to find seating. Id encourage management to add more seating options. The idea of having to wait in a line for 10-25 minutes to order and another line for 10 minutes to pick up your food and then spend 10 minutes trying to find a table isn't the best experience. If management could add a table service option that would really put them over the top for another star! With tons of food options people should keep coming back again and again! 

Shipping Container Restaurants include: 
- Boat Run Oyster Co features oysters & seafood 
- Gallito Taqueria features Tacos & Mexican food 
- Edison's Swigamajig features a dive bar & fish kitchen
- Flock and Stock features burgers & chicken tenders 
- BT-in-a-Box by BT Nguyen features French-Vietnamese fusion
- Montados by Mise en Place, features  Spanish tapas and wines
- Whatever Pops features gourmet popsicles 
- Foundation Coffee Co. Features local coffees 
- The Corners Pizza
- Fermented Reality Biergarten features 30+ drafts 

Stand alone restaurants include: 
- Hooters sports bar featuring wings 
- Splitsville bowling alley featuring a revamped design and new southern comfort food menu

I'm Looking forward to coming back again and again to try more and more dishes! I am also looking forward to hearing all the new stand alone restaurants coming soon!

The Jotoro Kitchen & Tequila Bar is the latest new hot spot to open at the Sparkman Wharf in the Channelside District of Downtown Tampa and has over-taken the old Hooters location. However, you wouldn't be able to tell Jotoro's building used to be a Hooters because the outside and inside of the building including the patio area has been completely transformed. There are garage style roll up windows to create an open air atmosphere for even the inside dining area. There are 2 seperate patios with plenty of outdoor seating with a view of Downtown and pedestrians passing by. There is a large rectangular shaped bar that wraps around the entire center of the restaurant with tons of bar seating and booth seating available. Unfortunately, the Booths are just wood and don't have any plush comfy padding. There is Mexican inspired wall art all over the walls, dim lighting, and lively music playing to create a nice festive atmosphere that reminds me fo the last Mexican restaurant that was here before the Channelside Plaza was transformed into Sparkman Wharf.  

The Korean style bbq beef wood-fired tacos came with slow braised beef smothered in Korean spices on 2 corn tortillas and an optional side of rice and beans for an extra $5. For the price, there should have been 3 Tacos included. The meat was not spiced or as flavorful as I would have liked either. Don't order this dish. You'll leave hungry and wanting more. 5/10 

The Texas-Style Steak & Cheese Enchiladas was cooked on a wood-fired grill & smothered in salsa Ranchero, crema, and Mexican cheeses with an included side of rice & beans. The red salsa that topped the enchiladas was incredibly plain and not spiced right. I was incredibly surprised the enchiladas didn't even come topped with tons of cheese which is the very definition of an enchilada. This dish left me wanting a real enchilada at Miguels Mexican Cantina. 5/10 

The Pineapple mangonado frozen cocktail came with Pina colada, chamoy, mango, and tajin. 9/10

The Pretty Boy Margarita came with Patron silver, pineapple, lime, raspberry puree, Grand Marnier, and was garnished with raspberries. 9/10 

The Blue Wave Margarita came with cazadores reposado, blue curacao, Cointreau, pineapple puree and was garnished with a pineapple. 10/10

The Prickly Pear Margarita came with Dobel Diamante, prickly pear syrup, fresh lime, agave, and was garnished with an awesome exotic pink Dragon-fruit. 9/10

The Mi Casa Margarita came with Dobel Diamante, fresh lime, agave, and was garnished with a circular cut of lime. 8/10

The Peanut Butter Sundae came served in a large goblet covered with chocolate on the glass, vanilla ice cream with hints of chocolate and peanut butter, reeces pieces peanut butter cups & Waffle cone, topped with whipped cream & a cherry! 9/10 

While the drinks are pretty good, they do look way better than they taste and I can't say I recommend the food. The margaritas did not come with a salt brim and were made way too strong, taking away from the flavor of the drinks. The meat on the tacos and enchilada didn't have a lot of flavor on its own and was not well spiced or marinated. Sadly, the food is way overpriced for the portion size you get and just not that good. $14 for 2 Tacos is outrageous. Almost anywhere else you can get 3 Tacos for less. Charging $5 for beans and rice is absolutely outrageous. Enchiladas that don't come topped with tons of cheese is completely unheard of. A Mexican restaurant that does not make their own house hot sauce or serve fajitas is also unheard of. Chef Joe Isidori may have earned a Michelin star but it was for burgers and not Mexican food. I encourage Management to make their own house made hot sauces, marinate the meats longer, provide larger portion sizes, put cheese on enchiladas, and serve fajitas! We will be back for the drinks but not for the food. For much better Mexican food, try Miguel's Mexican Cantina off Kennedy.

I'm glad to welcome the long awaited Sugar Factory to Tampa's Hard Rock Casino Resort. Sugar Factory offers a retro glitzy diner atmosphere with big retro Hollywood dressing room style circular bulbs, fancy chandeliers, granite white bar & table countertops, retro comfy red velvet half booth seating, and a black and white retro small tile floor. There's a Sugar Factory in Orlando, Miami, New York, Vegas, and all the big cities. It's about time Tampa got one too!

Sugar factory has huge overpriced $36 smoking goblet drinks, over the top $18-$31 huge milkshakes with chocolate on the glass, $17 martinis, $15 cocktails, 8 types of burgers, a donut burger, a waffle burger, 5 types of sandwiches, 5 types of pastas, 4 types of steak, a big brunch menu, $99 King Kong sundae that serves 12, $151 chocolate silver fondue, $396 red velvet fondue with champagne that serves 4, $1000 chocolate gold fondue that serves 6.

Since Sugar Factory is so small, theres a 36 minute wait to get in even though there weren't even a lot of people there. I can only imagine the wait to get in on Saturday and Sunday will be much longer. There were maybe only 7 tables in the place and the biggest table was reserved for people that never came and was not in use at all, making a cramped tiny diner feel even smaller with the biggest table out of commission. I imagined a much larger venue that would be 4-5 times the size of this tiny sad diner. To start, we got the sampler platter which included 5 onion rings, 3 chicken fingers, 5 buffalo wings, and 3 Mac and cheese pops. It was not bad but for $26 I'd expect twice as much food. 7/10

The pan roasted salmon salad included avocado, mango, cucumber, roasted bell peppers, red onions, pine nuts and a lemon vinaigrette and was healthy, and filling but a little bland. I added some salt and pepper and that helped but it could have used a better salad dressing as some bacon goat cheese and nuts. At $26, it was one of the most expensive salads I've ever had. 6/10 

The rainbow burger slider appetizer was pretty colorful and nice for a photo with 5 colored buns and the rubber duckie but I can't say it was worth $23 or the most tasty. The burgers were very basic with just cheese tomato lettuce and the patties were dry and burnt. Luckily a lot of ketchup fixes that. You're better off getting a big regular burger with more quality toppings for less if you wanna wind up with less carbs although you won't get the famous signature colored buns. 6/10

The watermelon patch meloncito goblet with lemon and citrus soda and sour gummy beads by Pit Bull was pretty good although not my favorite. 7/10 

The peace love & harmonie hypnotiq margarita was probably my favorite drink of the night and the least expensive although it didn't smoke. 9/10 

Aside from much higher than average drink and food prices and a cramped atmosphere, the music they were playing at Sugar Factory was all so old, played out, or just plain bad that I barely could enjoy spending time there. Management, please play newer upbeat hit music and not stuff that no one has ever heard or has been played out for years. Most bars have a dimly lit atmosphere but not the Sugar Factory. This place was way too bright, like daylight, which kinda gave you the feel of being in a supermarket, not chill at all. The diner felt very very small and cramped with only 7 tables and spot lights everywhere. It's funny that there are neon compliment signs on the Walls saying "beautiful", "gorgeous", and "wild thing" to people over-indulging in humongous triple serving sized drinks, milk shakes, desserts, and burgers. Perhaps it's psychological so people don't feel bad for over-indulging here with this over the top stuff. Our server was pretty nice and helpful although they were very busy. The kitchen was a little slow to bring out food but that is understandable as they just opened and were super busy. I prefer the vibe, decor, lighting, music, and more space offered by Toothsome Chocolate Emporium in Orlando over this place but for those that want to have over-the-top decadence closer to home, this may be the spot you seek!  I hope Sugar Factory will introduce some happy hour specials, better music, dim lighting, live music, and a more chill vibe in the future!

Whiskey Cake Kitchen & Bar serves southern comfort food in an upscale setting and is located at International Plaza Mall on the pedestrian-only Bay Street strip next to a bunch of other bars and restaurants including Brio Tuscan Grill, Doc B's, the Pub, Taps Burger Bar & Gastropub, Roccos Tacos & Tequila Bar, Frankie's Lobstah Trap, Cheesecake Factory, and Capital Grille Steak House.

Whiskey Cake has one of the best happy hours at International Mall with $5 bar bites including short rib poutine, duck confit taquitos, mini local charcuterie board, dips and spreads trio, and wagyu corn dogs. Whiskey Cakes also serves $3 beers, $5 glasses of wine, and $5 craft cocktails. 

For happy hour I had the great escape cocktail with pineapple infused plantation rum, guava, pineapple ginger syrup, and lime. It was pretty tasty! 5/5 

For happy hour, I also got the short rib poutine with fries, beef pan jus, local goat cheese, pickled vegetables, and a sunny side up local egg. According to the bartender, this is their most filling appetizer and it did not disappoint. The short rib was tasty and I was glad the chef didn't drown the fries in gravy like some other places do. 4/5 

For brunch, I got the OMG 2.0 burger with Onions, mushrooms, goodness, crispy onion straws, melted crimini cheese, grain mustard, chile mayo, lettuce, tomato on a challah bun with house made chips. I was a bit disappointed That for a $14 burger, Whiskey Cake can't include fries or mixed greens on the side without an extra up-charge. The burger was very filling and tasty although a bit greasier than I would have liked. The bottom of the burger got soggy from the burger grease. 4/5 

For dessert, we got the famous Whiskey Cake that the restaurant is named after with toffee torte, bourbon anglaise, spiced pecans, and house made vanilla whipped cream. It was pretty tasty but not my favorite as far as desserts go. The toffee torte is kinda like soggy bread with a hint of bourbon and pecans and a bit on the dry side. Charging $9 for a simple dessert is outrageous. It should be half the price. 2/5 

Whiskey cake is a great deal for happy hour but otherwise a bit on the pricey side. Everything at International plaza mall is above average price so that goes with the territory. Our service was pretty quick and friendly on my visits. There is an outside bar and an inside bar for happy hour so they can accommodate a lot of people, which is nice. Whiskey burger serves 3 kinds of burgers, 4 kinds of sandwiches, soups, salads, and BBQ. I look forward to trying more craft cocktails during Whiskey Cake's happy hour, perhaps another burger, the grilled Mauritius redfish, or the whiskey braised short rib on my next visits!

Tate Island Waterfront Grill is located right on the beach at the SandPearl Beach Resort in Clearwater Beach and offers Seafood, Wraps, Salads, Sandwiches, Frozen Cocktails, Beer, Margaritas, Mojitos, Wines by the Glass, and kids meals with an amazing view of the beach, and the resort's pool. You can enjoy your drinks or meal in a padded lounge chair poolside, at the restaurants outdoor patio, or inside the restaurant with air conditioning which is a nice break on a hot day. 

Valet Parking is $23 at the SandPearl Resort for 3 hours but you get $10 off with validation from dining at Tates Island Grill or you can park at the garage across the street for $3 per hour. 

The fruit plate appetizer came with a vanilla yogurt and a surprisingly large amount of seasonal fruit including Blueberries, honeydew melon, cantaloupe and pineapple! The pineapple and honeydew melon were both sweet but the cantaloupe was not. 8/10 

The grilled chicken Quesadillas came packed with tons of cheddar jack cheese and sides of salsa and sour cream but was missing guacamole and black beans or any other side. Do not order this if you're hungry as it is not that filling. 7/10

The Causeway Caesar salad topped with blackened Ora king salmon came with a good amount of veggies and a generous cut of salmon with it. The blackening season had a nice flavor! 9/10

The Grouper Sandwich came with a generous portion of blackened grouper, lettuce, tomato, tater sauce, and a side of chips for no up-charge. 9/10

The Pina Colada Cocktail came frozen with bacardi black rum, cream of coconut, and pineapple juice and was the real star of the day! 10/10 

The Blue Pearl Cocktail is Tate Island Grill's signature cocktail and came frozen with bacardi black rum, creme De banana, coconut, and blue curacao swirl. It's a cool looking drink but I'd have to recommend the flavor of the Pina Colada over this drink. The curacao didn't mix the best with the coconut. 8/10 

It took quite awhile to get our drink, get our food, and close out our bill. It was a bit longer than usual but it was busy and everyone is on island time at the beach. 

If you're in the Clearwater Beach area, not in a hurry, and looking for some great seafood and nice views of the beach and susnet, I highly recommend checking out Tates Island Grill, although it is a bit more expensive than other options on the beach but it has more of an upscale feel!

Ciccio Cali Brandon is located off Bloomingdale Avenue, 1 block from Providence, in Riverview, next to Boca Kitchen, The Egg & I, and Nothing Bundt Cakes. Ciccio Cali is inspired by food tours of California and serves 15 types of healthy made-to-order rice bowls, 6 types of tacos, 6 types of juices and 6 types of wraps with antibiotic free meats, fresh veggies , and high protein options leaving you feeling lighter and healthier. 

We came with coworkers for lunch and had to wait in line to place our order at a register but the line moved quickly with 2 cashiers and we were able to order in under 5 minutes. Drinks are self serve and they have a cucumber infused water on the house which is pretty nice. The decor of the restaurant is very nice with white high back leather booths along the back of the restaurant with a cool large blue rose painting that kinda reminded me of a chic Miami vibe. Upbeat music house music was playing in the background and was not too loud but enough to create a nice festive atmosphere and be able to talk. Our food was brought to our table in under 10 minutes which was nice. For dinner, the atmosphere is more formal, a server can take your order at your table which is nice. 

For the bowls, you can pick your base of: yellow rice, quinoa brown rice blend, sticky rice, coconut avocado rice, mixed greens, Japanese udon noodles, spaghetti squash, haves Brussels and kale blend. 

For the bowls, you can pick your protein of: seared ahi tuna, grilled shrimp, chargrilled steak, blackened chicken, chargrilled chicken, crispy chicken, and roasted veggie blend. 

I got the Hot & Crunchy rice bowl with grilled shrimp, coconut avocado rice, cucumber-jicama mix, scallion, soy sauce, smashed avocado, sesame,Sriracha aioli, and crispy tempura onions. I added a side of Sriracha and peanut aioli from the Thai bowl for best of both bowl and a hint of sweet and spicy! For $11, it was a great deal and so tasty! The serving size was huge and I could barely finish it! 12/10 

On another occasion, I got the Thai bowl with seared Ahi Tuna, Japanese Udon Noodles, Mango, jicama, carrot, scallion, cilantro,crispy wontons, peanut aioli, and togarashi. The serving size was very large and the ahi tuna was seared perfectly and very tender and tasty! 12/10 

My coworker got the Fajita bowl with chargrilled steak, quinoa brown rice blend, seasoned black beans, sautéed onions, sautéed bell peppers, guacamole, jalapeño jack cheese, and a side of salsa and he really like his meal as well. 

For dessert, I got the chocolate s'more cookie and it was so good with large chunks of chocolate, large chunks of marshmallow, a soft texture, and really tasted like s'mores! 12/10 

I look forward to coming back soon to try the spicy Brazilian bowl, having more hot & crunchy bowls with shrimp or ahi tuna, and making it back for taco Tuesday to try some of their tacos! If you haven't been yet, I highly recommend trying Ciccio Cali! In addition to this Riverview / Brandon location, Ciccio Cali has locations in South Tampa, Tampa Palms, and St Petersburg!

Why 3 stars? The Hard Rock Cafe is a tourist trap with above average prices, so-so food selection, & a stage with no live music on my 2 visits, although they do display some interesting rock related memorabilia. It is worth checking out at least once. 

The Hard Rock Cafe of Tampa is located in the Seminole Hard Rock Resort & Casino. We came for happy hour which is Monday through friday 4-7pm and includes $4 blue moons, goose island ipas, and Yeunglings, $1 wings, $7 bang a gong shrimp, chicken empanadas, and chicken quesadillas. The bar has built in computer slick machines which is kind of cool but he screen takes up 90 percent of the bar table so space is kind of limited when you get Food and drinks. 

We ended up getting the bang a gong shrimp with sweet chili sauce which was really good but the portion size was tiny so not a great value 7/10, 

heavy metal wings which came with a nice smoky flavored hot sauce that left my mouth on fire 9/10, 

and chicken empanadas with a onion garlic ranch dipping sauce. The sauce wasn't flavorful enough for my tastes but my buddy liked it. I preferred dipping the empanadas in the heavy metal hot sauce for an extra kick 6/10. 

I initially wanted to get the chicken quesadilla which only comes with chicken and cheese but it would have been a $2 up-charge for jalapeños and $3 for beans so I opted for the shrimp and wings instead. In contrast Bar Louie doesn't charge extra for extra vegetables in their happy hour quesadillas so they definitely have the better value. 

The Hard Rock Cafe has a real cool led backlit color changing orb with concert fan hands in the air that makes you feel like you're under a concert bandshell. The band stage is backlit with color changing leds and there's another bar closer to the stage and the band with very high elegant ceilings. Even the bathrooms have the live concert musical feel to them with concert hands built into the mirrors! The detail that went into designing this place is amazing. By he entrance they have an homage to every generation of music from the 50s, 60s, 70s, 80s, and 90s!

Back in my day, I remember when burgers were just $6 at the Hard Rock. Now you can't get a Burger here under $15. My have times changed! By the time happy hour was ending at 7 there was a line of patrons waiting to get in. The band was supposed to start at 7 but unfortunately they wasted so much time fine tuning their instruments that we left at 8 without even hearing them play a note! 

You do have to recognize that all hard rock cafes are kind of a tourist trap with some unique ooo and ahhh elements and as a result Food pricing does come at a premium and it may not be the best value but it is a cool experience to check out.

After much anticipation, watching the progress as world of beer international was built from the ground up, I'm so glad World of beer International is finally open to the public! Wob international is located off spruce a block away from international mall across the street  We watched the heated Monday night  match up of the Bucs versus Panthers. It was right down to 3 seconds but the Bucs won with a field goal. We had the draft of the month, the lightning bolt, which is a blonde ale by 81 Bay brewing locally made in Tampa off Gandy! It's nice to see that world of beer is supporting local breweries. Wob International has a cool infusion tower with jalapeños and citrus that changes daily and a daily real cask ale. This world of beer does have a full liquor and wine bar unlike South Tampa. However, Wob hides all the liquors from plain site and only showcase the premium whiskies. There is a huge selection of locally made Tampa Bay brews at this location from copper tail, motor works, cigar city, sea dog, cycle brewery, hoffbrauhaus, 81 Bay and  pair o dice. World of beer has a cool rooftop balcony with comfortable couches, 2 fire pits, and another upstairs bar. Happy Hour runs 3-7 and 10 til close Monday through Friday and includes $3 drafts, and $5 Tavern bites which include beef Barbacoa street Tacos, chimichurri, Chipotle BBQ chicken Flatbread pizza, Tavern taters, and Southern fried pickles. Infused beer shots are only $1! The current flavor was lime and cherry IPA and wasn't bad but not my favorite either. For lunch on the weekdays 11AM-3PM, Wob international offers 2 meals for $8 which is a great deal! On Mondays, wob has a $5 brats and burger night. On Fridays and Saturdays they're open til 2AM and but only open til 12 during the weekdays. Wob international has different colored wood plank walls, exposed ac ducts, brick walls, high ceilings, rustic hanging Edison bulbs, and a cool dark brown and black rustic multi textured bar. Wob plays a mix of music ranging from old school punk rock like welcome to paradise by green day and thriller by Michael Jackson at a medium volume which wasn't too loud or too soft. The parking lot is a bit small on the ground floor due to other businesses next door but there is additional parking available designated for wob on the second floor of the parking a garage next door. Staff was very nice and attentive. I look forward to my next visit to try some of the bar bites!

Come to La Teresita Restaurant for Delicious, authentic, inexpensive, Cuban food with large portions, served quickly, and with daily food specials. I recommend their Ropa Vieja (Shredded Pork), Filete Salteado (Sauteed Beef Tenderloin), Churrasco (Steak), Cuban Sandwiches, Black Bean Soup, Tres Leches, and Flan. Service is really quick. The service is not the world's friendliest as most of the servers can't speak too much English, but that's not a big deal. LA Teresita has a full liquor bar now and serves good sangria, mojitos, and margaritas! There is plenty of parking available in a private lot right behind the restaurant.  Dress code is casual. They have live music on some nights but they did not even have background music playing when I was there.  

The cafeteria style eatery has really dated divey decor. La Teresita is not a classy or upscale place and it is not the best place to bring a date. I do not recommend their Chicken Noodle Soup. It is a bit bland.  La Teresita is kind of far from where I live in South Tampa and kind of far from the interstate, off Columbus and a block from Macdill.

We came for the grand opening at trophy fish seafood restaurant and bar, downtown St Pete at 10pm. Unfortunately the restaurant was already out of food. Trophy Fish's current menu includes red snapper and red grouper with your choice of tacos, plate, sandwich, or salad, prepared grilled, blackened, or with citrus marinade! Trophy fish also serves fish spread, fried pickles, hush puppies, grilled shrimp, key lime pie, and root beer floats. 

Trophy Fish has a huge list of custom craft cocktail drinks including "if you like pina coladas", blood money, gone fishing, pistachio mai tai, salty dawg, fin and tonic, passarelle, dark and semi rainy, yacht club lemonade, calm before the storm, banana hammock, greasy skirt, abandon ship, aloe ha, import white wines, red wines, and craft brews. We ended up getting the peroni from Italy, borgo conventi Pinot Grigio from Italy, and the rock brothers 311 amber ale! 

The male live musician sung a an acoustic version of a Taylor swift song which was really funny to hear with a guys voice. The live musician they had was pretty talented and they had a pretty good crowd. The entire restaurant is outdoors with only a roof over the bar and the kitchen. Don't bet on coming here if it's raining. I don't even see umbrellas over the tables. I Look forward to coming back here soon to try some of the food !

Why 3 stars? Because it's nothing special for Brunch and basically a plain-Jane average experience that's reminiscent of Village Inn with its basic menu options and old school 90s decor. 

Samaria Cafe is located in downtown Tampa next to First Watch. We wanted to try something different and not much else was open so we gave Samaria Cafe a shot. Samaria Cafe has kind of an outdated interior decor that reminds me of a village inn restaurant. Just like village inn, the brunch menu options were pretty basic although they did have 4 different Benedict options. I was a little disappointed that the menu doesn't have a lot of seafood options. 

We ended up getting the mushroom Benedict and the Reuben with coleslaw. The server told us they're known for their Reuben and it did not disappoint. The mushroom Benedict came out a little runnier than expected, so if you like yours well cooked, make sure to specify that! Our food came out in under 10 minutes and there was no wait to be seated. Service was pretty good and friendly. However, unfortunately, No alcohol is sold at this establishment so you won't get the full brunch experience.

I enjoy coming to the new Bern's upscale yet business casual off-shoot, Haven, for the chic modern atmosphere and to sample their ever-changing Happy Hour Menu selections 5PM-7PM Mon-Fri which include $3 amazing unique Cocktails, $2 Craft Brews, $4 Wines, and $5 exotic bar bites. After trying the specialty cocktails on multiple occasions, I can say that I've never had a bad drink and have always been impressed to try something new and different that I still like. To drink, I have had Haven's Lavender Collins with ford's gin, lavender bitters, and lemon, the Paloma with tequila cabeza, agave nectar, grapefruit soda, and the Haven Sangrai with house blend sangria, cinnamon, and fresh fruit. On another occasion I had Haven's Jasmine cocktail with aviation gin, campari, cointreau, lemon juice, the Ronkonkoma with flor de cana, nox alpina, espelette, banana liquer, and the Hemingway Daquiri with flor de cana, maraschino, grafruit, and lime. I've had their charcuterie board, three cheese board, elk skewers, and bruschetta and they've all been pretty good. Haven boasts a large selection 300 bourbons, 40 wines by the glass, 60 cheeses, and a variety of charcuteries. Haven also has top notch Margaritas! Haven is located off South Howard Ave and Morrison in SoHo walking distance to my place across from a Sunoco Gas Station and Ciccio / Water, south of the Green Lemon.  Haven has a private parking lot with a $3 valet which is pretty reasonable. There is no free street parking available in the immediate area surrounding this establishment. Haven has chic modern decor, a rustic unique lighting setup, and a large wrap around bar that can accommodate 18 people sitting. The bartenders have been very knowledgeable in explaining the drinks, friendly, and prompt to bring drinks, unlike some other bars in the area where you might be waiting over 20 minutes for a drink. I heard they get slammed on Friday's happy hour, so expect slower service on Friday or just try Mon-Thurs. Looking forward to my next visit! Thanks!

Platt Street Borough is a newly invented restaurant and bar located at the location formerly known as Hyde Out and The Rack. Both previous restaurants at this location served sushi and were well beloved by soho residents. Unfortunately, for some odd reason, platt street borough left sushi off their menu this time. 

I suggested to our brunch group to visit platt street borough, but with nothing unique on their brunch menu aside from a fatty glazed donut with fried chicken, a gross gravy cream cheese salmon waffle, and the highest bottomless mimosa price in town of $16, we ended up deciding on going to the blind goat which had a much more extensive and unique brunch menu and a lower bottomless mimosa price.
