The decor changes made over the previous restaurant, hyde out, were sadly a considerable downgrade. Platt street borough feels nowhere near as chic, classy, or polished as the Hyde Out. The new arcade room was filled with the worst possible games: skee ball and golf. To no surprise, the arcade room was completely empty.  For some reason, the floors looked filthy or perhaps that's just the unfinished concrete floor style. 

For lunch, the St. Louis ribs sounded nice but my server informed me the restaurant only gives you a meager portion of 3 pieces. That wasn't enough to satisfy my hunger and I was not about to order 2 meals for just a half of a rack of ribs, which is about a half meal at most other restaurants. Their rib serving sizes are absolutely ridiculous. What person will be satisfied with just 3 ribs? I had one overpriced craft brew and left frustrated. 

For dinner, Platt street boroughs menu is seriously lacking of anything unique or healthy with 4 types of burgers, wings, nachos, 4 basic sandwiches, a basic chicken dish, some gross gravy potato dish, and a meatless Italian dish at double regular price. This place fails as a fancy gourmet eatery with only basic sports bar or sandwich shop options. This place fails as a sport bar because other sports bars like hooters and duffys offer way more tv screens, more wing flavors, and much more food options. Unless the menu changes, my return visits will only include drinks. 

Management, for the love of God, provide a more extensive menu with a greater variety of seafood, salmon bagels for brunch, salmon or lobster Benedict for brunch, fish tacos, Peruvian, Argentinian, Japanese, Brazilian, other ethnic foods, and at the very least something other than the most basic fatty unhealthy bar food!

Ocean Blue Sushi is located off McMullen Booth and Enterprise in Clearwater in a shopping Plaza with a big Sushi sign. The outside of the restaurant has a shark with horns for the logo outside the main entrance.  We came here for a buddy's birthday who lives in the Clearwater area because this is his favorite sushi spot in all of Clearwater! I had the ginger salad, ha ha roll, and Mexican roll while some others in my party had the spicy salad, sweet potato roll, spider roll, Ramon noodles, and hand rolls. This restaurant also serves udon noodles and bento boxes. Everyone was very pleased with their meals and the food came out in a timely fashion. We were sat in a large comfy circular booth with high leatherback chairs. The sushi bar can hold about 8 people and is pretty well decorated. The restaurant had authentic Japanese music playing in the background and Japanese art on the walls. The waitress told us they have a half off happy hour after 10 and a dj on the weekends. Our waitress was able to quickly split our checks without hesitation which is nice. I Look forward to my next visit!

The Rooster & the Till Restaurant offers fancy looking, "farm to table", "local", tiny bite sized plates at a rustic dining space. Rooster and the Till is located in Seminole Heights hipster district of Tampa off North Florida Ave, south of Sligh and north of Hillsborough. 

While all the food seemed well presented and featured odd pairings, none of the dishes really knocked my socks off and the portion sizes were way too small. Each small dish goes for $17 to $26  and is the size of 1/4th of an appetizer at another restaurant. Each dish was at most 2-3 bites and left me hungry. Its kind of hard to tell the size from the pictures but trust me when I tell you the tiny pieces of food they bring you is laughably small and quite frankly insulting for the amount of money they charge. There was no filet, scallops, or lobster or anything warranting such a high price point. None of the dishes are a must have. It's gonna at least run you $80 to get full at this place. The chef tasting will run you $75 and another $40 to pair each dish with wine but the menu does not say how many dishes are included or what is in each dish if you pick that option. Be prepared to spend a lot or have a second meal elsewhere before or after coming here. The decor of Rooster & the Till is not bad with its rustic style but it certainly does not have a wow factor or feel like a $80 per patron restaurant with white table cloths. If you want a truly spendy fancy meal that feels a lot more elegant Id recommend going to Eddie V's Steak House, Ocean Prime Steak House, or Berns Steakhouse. Evidently the critics that named Rooster and the Till as the best restaurant in Tampa Bay had a serious lack of appetite.

We ordered: 
Grouper cheeks with glowing smoked trout roe & braised collard corn pone

Gnocchi short ribs with smoked ricotta, stewed tomatoes, & spicy pickled peperonata 

Pork belly with corn bread, spiced honey, & pickled apple 

Foie gras (duck liver) with sous vide pear, cashew pear butter, Nutella, & minus 8 huckleberry gastrique

For Dessert, we got the Silken Coconut Milk with Coconut Milk Soaked Berries, Milk Crumb, Milk Ice, and Dulce de Leche.

My favorite dish of the night was the pork belly followed by the foie gras. The gnocchi, grouper cheeks, and silken coconut milk dessert were a bit disappointing and underwhelming. I love seasoning but the grouper cheeks were just way over-seasoned and to salty. The coconut milk dessert reminded me of a fruit yogurt parfait and wasn't something I'd order again. Most disappointing was the serving size of each dish which left me hungry. I opted to finish the night with a real meal somewhere else.

We had an awesome time at Brio Tuscan Grille, at international plaza mall next to Doc Bs and across from the British Pub. We came for the happy hour that ends a bit early at 630PM Monday through Friday. Sadly, Brio's happy hour drink prices increased from $5 to $6 and their apps increased from $4 to $6 but what we did end up having was very good. The shrimp and egg plant appetizer was amazing and so was the berry margarita and french cucumber pineapple gimlet! The drinks are a bit pricier than bar louie next door but their apps are amazing!! Look forward to my next visit! Brio tuscan grille has a nice patio overlooking passers by and a new rooftop patio that is open only on Wednesdays for some mysterious reason. Brio's Decor is rustic, elegant, and upscale. Brio has plenty of parking onsite at the mall. Service and food was top notch! Look forward to coming back for $5 Martinis on Wednesday, $5 glasses of Wine Thursdays, or another time for happy hour!

Wow! Best food ever in a lively chic modern atmosphere right in the heart of downtown St. Pete ! I'm gonna have to make this my new regular spot! 

Red Mesa cantina is located in downtown St. Pete right under the new rooftop bar and has an amazing lively courtyard great music, led mood lighting, and is all around a top notch spot! We sat at the bar and got amazing service from a nice blonde bartender. We got seated with no wait and got drinks and food quickly. At my buddies suggestion We got the seafood mofongo because it's his favorite and it did not disappoint! 

I'm going to have to be a regular here now 12/10! The seafood mofongo came with sautéed shrimp, scallops, calamari, tomato, cilantro, Rojas in tequila lime butter sauce, served over pork carnitas, sweet plantain and yuca mofongo! So Good! 

Our bartender also recommends the salmon a la lpancha palomilla and crab and shrimp quesadilla! Look forward to coming back again soon !

Thai Terrace Restaurant is located off South Dale Mabry just a block north of the interstate, a block south of the stadium, next to 2001 odyssey, scores, and the Howard Johnson. 

We came for lunch and got the steak pad Thai hot 4/5 spicy with spices on the side. The pad Thai dish was top notch, tasty, and a generous serving size that I could not finish in one sitting surprisingly. 9/10 My buddy got the red curry shrimp dish, liked his meal as well, and had leftovers for another meal as well. 9/10 

The restaurant had various Thai artifacts on the walls to add to the Thai charm of the place as well as lantern style lights strung across the ceiling to create a warm festive atmosphere. Traditional Thai music played in the background at a reasonable level to create a authentic style atmosphere. There was no wait to be seated, our food came out in under 10 minutes, service was great and friendly. Most Thai places also serve Sushi but this place does not. Look forward to trying more dishes next time!

Malios Prime Steakhouse is an upscale Steakhouse located in Downtown Tampa on the Riverwalk with indoor and outdoor patio seating offering pretty views of the Hillsborough river, the Riverwalk, the sunset, and University of Tampa!  Malio's Prime Steakhouse has a happy hour that runs 3pm to 7pm Tuesday through Friday! 

Filet Mignon Steak Tips came with a tasty bearnaise sauce, was well Marinated, tasty but the portion size was a little on the small size at approximately 5 oz.  8/10 

The Truffle Burger came with an over-easy egg, arugula, provolone, and truffle oil which gave the bun a tasty flavor. The burger was very tasty and was a pretty generous portion size. Unfortunately the burger did not come with a side of fries. 9/10 

The Ahi Tuna Tartare came with pickled ginger, soy, 3 Cucumbers, avocado, & wonton chips. I was able to distribute the Ahi Tuna and ingredients evenly over 3 big Cucumber slices which were 2 bites each for a total of 6 bites. This dish was not bad but was missing any kind of memorable sweet or spicy sauce. 8/10 

The Tennessee Lemonade came with Belle Meade Bourbon, Fresh Squeezed Lemons, & a daah of Agave. 9/10 

House margarita on the rocks with salt was pretty tasty. 9/10 

The chocolate martini came with chocolate liquor, vodka, bailey's, and chocolate syrup and was also pretty good. 9/10 

Malios happy hour food options includes  6 kinds of burgers, cheese board, filet tips, chips, Applewood smoked bacon, shrimp Theresa, shrimp ponzu fired, ahi Tuna Tartare, potato skins, mozzarella Malzone, & heirloom tomatoes with burrata cheese. 

Malibu happy hour drink options were a little disappointing with just 3 cocktail options for $7-$8, just 2 options for martinis, just 2 options for wine, and no options for beer. 

On another occasion a long time ago, I came for filet mignon steaks and they were pretty good. However, recently the prices on a 10oz filet mignon have nearly doubled for $69. In comparison, the 5oz of filet mignon steak tips for $8 during happy hour does seem like a much better deal. If you get 2 5oz, you can get 10oz of filet for $16 instead of $69 but it doesn't come with any sides of course. 

I ended up spending quite a bit more than I wanted to due to the lack of drink options on the Malios Happy Hour menu and the higher than average drink prices. However, I would not say Malios has the best happy hour in downtown Tampa as many have said. Malios happy hour prices have increased againbsince the last menu I saw posted just 3 months before. I much prefer American Social's $4 margaritas, steak Quesadillas, burgers, and larger portion of steak tips. However, I might be back to try the ponzu fired shrimp in the future.

I was initially glad Rocco's Tacos and Tequila Bar took over the old geyser hangout, Blue Martini, but was a bit disappointed in what they had to offer. Rocco's Tacos is located at International Mall Plaza next to Bar Louie, Brio Tuscan Grille, Doc B's Fresh Kitchen, Taps Burger Bar Gastro Pub, Capital Grille, Cheesecake Factory, and the Pub. We initially came for their opening night which was supposed to provide complimentary salsa and guacamole for everyone. Arriving only 1 hour into the opening night, they were already out of guacamole and overcharged us for our brewskies by double. It's a good thing we called the bartender out on this. The owner was walking on the bar splashing salsa on people and pouring tequila in girls hair and dresses. Many people were not happy lol. On another occasion,  we came for the new happy hour which is 4-7pm on weekdays and includes $1 off drinks and $7 bar bites at the bar. We tried the the beef flautas with avocado ranch and salsa Chile de arbol, camarones patron which feature shrimp tortillas sautéed in tequila, Rojo Chipotle, with Padron  peppers. The shrimp tortillas are good but we had to assemble them ourselves and didn't have enough room on the plates or condiments for the tortillas. I wish they would have came prepared instead of making us do half the work! We also had the 2 Carne asada Tacos, and the jalapeño rollenos which are stuffed fried jalapeño peppers with cotija cheese lime crema avocado ranch cilantro. Each of the Bar bites isn't enough to fill you up on its own so I recommend ordering at least 2 if you're hungry. The decor for Bar taco is really cool with angels hanging from the ceiling, Mexican Star Wars art, Mexican Gouls, Mexican weapons everywhere, and they play Star Wars in the bathroom which is nice. Roccos tacos also featured a Dj booth in a Vw bus but not a lot of people ever dance here. It's more of a high spirited casual bar than a dance club. I usually come here for drinks instead of food. Usually there's a 1-2hour wait just to get seated so We just try to find spots at the bar! I'd give this place 3 stars for food and 4 stars for the crowd decor and atmosphere. It's a welcome addition to international mall and brings crowds back but I think their Orlando location is way better.

Another Broken Egg Cafe is located in a brand new plaza next to Smash Burger, Tijuana flats, Buffalo Wild Wings, Jeremiah ice cream, and Crunch Fitness. We had an amazing brunch but the calorie counts on the menu were pretty rough. Im not sure how a salmon salad came out to 920 calories and the banana waffles comes out to 1600 calories! What are they putting in there? We got the salmon Benedict which was one of the lowest calorie counts on the whole menu with 600 calories. The crab cakes Benedict was an astonishing 1300 calories but very tasty! Id describe the food as southern comfort soul food. There was a 30 minute wait for a table but we used the yelp app to reserve our table and had no wait when we arrived! Our table had a cool unique shiny bronze finish and the place had a southern beach vibe with a large picture of paddle boards, canoes, and various other beach related decor throughout the restaurant. They are dog friendly with a large open outdoor patio. They even bring dog bowls filled with ice for the doggies! Management, for the love of god, bring your calorie counts down or take them off the menu so i dont have to fast for the whole rest of the day! If you want a cheat meal, this is the place!

Pacific Thai Cuisine has some of the best authentic decor and Thai food in Tampa Bay, after my current favorite, Ploy Thai in Brandon! This is definitely the top spot in the Oldsmar / Westchase / Tampa Road area. Ploy Thai is located off Tampa Road near the Westchase area of Oldsmar in a renovated plaza next to Bufallo wild wings, Wendy's, Applebee's, and is across from McDonald's, Brass Tap, and Flamestone American grill. Pacific thai cuisine has some really cool Thai style bungalows with dim lighting to create a top date night atmosphere. However I must say the wooden booths could use a little padding to add some more comfort. Pacific Thai Cuisine does take reservations but it usually isn't necessary unless it's Friday or Saturday night. We came on a Wednesday night and were seated without a wait. Our server was pretty quick and friendly although closing out the bill took awhile for some reason. I diverted from my usual pad Thai and red curry and tried the green curry and pad woon sen. Both were pretty tasty. I look forward to coming again soon when I'm in the area!

Roys is an upscale Hawaiian Fusion Restaurant located in the international mall area off Boy Scout next to Flemings and Eddie Vs.  There is a private parking lot on site with complimentary valet! We were greeted promptly by concierge and seated immediately. Unfortunately, while they do have 2 private party rooms, they do have a lack of comfy booth seating. 

On my most recent visit, we tried the Chef's tasting menu, which is also known as a price-fix menu, and included a starter, entree, and desert for $36! This was quite a deal, considering that most of the other entrees went for $30-$40 alone!  

For the starter, we had the watermelon salad which included pickled red onions, mache, burrata, and a delicious Meyer lemon vinaigrette. The burrata provided a real stand out flavor! (5/5) 

For our entree, we got the rosemary crusted grilled ahi tuna which included shaved brussel sprouts, swarnadwipa ginger emulsion, and an amazing crispy pork belly! (5/5)

We also got the Kalbi flank steak which included kim chee mac & cheese, Teppanyaki oyster mushrooms, sesame spinach. The steak was surprisingly tender, plentiful, and very flavorful with an incredible Asian style marinade! (5/5) 

For our dessert, we got the macadamia almond praline molasses tart topped with vanilla ice cream and blackberries! Our waitress was even kind enough to write congratulations on the plate! I was pretty full but I could not leave this on the table! So good! (5/5) 

I look forward to coming back and trying more dishes during happy hour soon! For Roy's Aloha Hour / Happy Hour 3PM-7PM and 9PM lil closing on Monday through Saturday, you can take advantage of $3 beers, $5 wells, $7 craft cocktails, $8-$12 bar bites including Kalua Pork Sliders, Szechuan Spiced Pork Ribs, Lobster Potstickers, Lump Crab Fried Rice, Hawaiian Tuna &a Salmon Poke, Wagyu Burger, and $8-$14 sushi rolls including a Lakanilau Roll which comes with wagyu beef and snow crab, the surf and turf roll which comes with wagyu beef and butterfish, the dynamite Maine Lobster Oshizushi, and the Lobster California roll.

I'm so glad the long awaited M Bird Rooftop Tapas Bar has opened at the top of the beloved & widely popular Armature Works at Tampa Heights with great views of the Hillsborough River and Downtown Tampa Skyline! 

M Bird brings an elegance and aura of sophisticated not yet seen in Tampa. M Bird is a lot like the the best rooftop bar in Downtown St Pete, the Birchwood Canopy, except there's no fire pit, no vip tents with views and you're looking onto a Construction truck, a huge dumpster, a pile of dirt, and have the challenge of getting it out of the picture when you try to take a picture of the water and the downtown skyline. Its a shame Armature works has been open for over a year and they cant get rid of such an eye sore in front of the pretty view! The half of the rooftop bar that is covered only offers partially obstructed views of the parking lot and the Hillsborough river. The birchwood canopy does a better job offering shade while not obstructing the view through their vip tents. The birchwood canopy is also much bigger and barely ever reaches capacity as M Bird does. After 8pm, a live DJ plays louder house style music like Birchwood Canopy but it doesn't quite turn into a dance club. 

I recommend going early before 7 if you dont want to wait in line to get in because M Bird reaches capacity quickly and cant let anyone else up until people leave! 

M Bird serves a small list of 17 tiny tapas or small plates  including Steak Tartare, Vaca Frita Tostones, Jerk Chicken Egg Rolls, Jerk BBQ Duck Confit Leg, Pulled Pork Burger, Providence Bavette, Octopus, Mussels Billi Bi, Mofongo Shrimp Bites, Branzino, Panzanella, Roasted Cauliflower, Falafel, Warm Marinated Olives, Papas Bravas, and the Artisan Green Salad. From the tapas I've seen, the portion sizes of all the tapas are way to small for the price, so I can't recommend getting any of the tapas if you're hungry. 

M Bird serves 3 Desserts including Baklava with pistachio walnut and strawberry sauce, Lemon Olive Oil Sponge Cake with basil whipped cream, and Forbidden Black Rice Pudding with fried bananas and a salted caramel sauce. 

M Bird serves 9 custom cocktails for $10-$13, 7 draft beers for $5, and 8 glasses of wine for $7-$10, and Social Intoxicants that serve 3-6 guests for $51-$59. I highly recommend "I left my wallet at La Segunda" which has quite a large unique cracker garnishment. The 7venth sun graffiti orange wheat beer brewed locally in Tampa, and the Francois Montand Spakrling Rose from Jura France did not disappoint either.  I look forward to coming back and trying more off the menu soon!

Acropolis Greek Taverna is located in downtown St Pete off central ave and features two stories, an outdoor street side patio shaded by umbrellas, and a 2nd floor rooftop patio also shaded by umbrellas. We got a half off CL deals deal and thought we should check out how the acropolis st pete location differs from Ybor and south tampa. The St Pete locations seems to be the biggest out of all the restaurants. We were treated to live dancing by the staff, napkins flying around, plates breaking, a belly dancer, and bazooka Greek guitar player. We were promptly seated without waiting. Our sever got our orders within 5 minutes of taking our seats and our food same out promptly under 10 minutes. The acropolis salad which features a greek salad and a gyro is no longer on the menu for some reason but they let us order it anyways. We also got a geek soup and the complimentary pita with tzaziki sauce appetizer. As with the other greek acropolis restaurants I've visited, Our service was good, food was good, and atmosphere was very lively! We Look forward to our next visit !

Nico's Arepas Grill has a food truck that frequents many downtown Tampa festivals and also now has a stand alone restaurant located on Armenia about 20 min North of South Tampa. Nico's Arepas Grill's serves unique Venezuelan food and has an interior decor that features cool blue led orbs on the ceilings, lively Spanish music, polished light Grey concrete floors, light blue walls with a city skyline silhouette backdrop, and light wood colored tables.  The dress code and vibe is casual. You have to stand in line to place your order at a register and a server will bring your meal out when it is ready.  They allow your order to be placed to go or for dine in. I'm not sure if they offer delivery. I don't think they serve alcohol.    

We got the Nico's Sampler which included 2 mini cachapas, 2 mini arepas, 2 tequenos, and 2 mini empanadas. All of them were quite delicious and unlike anything I've ever had before! We also got the 3 Mini Arepa slider combo deal with beef, pork, and chicken.  I was still left a little hungry after splitting those two, and our food totalled $20. I think next time, instead of a mini arepa slider, I'll just get a large arepa, which will have more meat in it, and be more filling. I was impressed that Nico's had quite a few tasty hot sauces to choose from. I look forward to trying more of this menu soon!

Acapulco Mexican Taqueria y Groceria is a no frills laid back taco joint located in a Mexican super market off Macdill just north of Kennedy and south of i275, just barely in South Tampa. The great thing about this place is that they have $2 tacos not only on Tuesdays but on every day of the week! They also have some top notch house made green and red hot sauces that compliment the tacos quite well. However, this is where the positives of this establishment end. When you come in, no one greets you and you place your order at the grill area with the grill master and when you leave, you go to the supermarket to pay. I ended up getting the fajita steak taco, carnitas taco, and the steak quesadilla. They were pretty good with the house hot sauces I must say but they took about 20 minutes to come out from the kitchen with only 4 other people in the restaurant on a Tuesday.  I had to ask the grill master for a cup of water and no one asked me if I wanted a drink. I was quite frankly shocked when the guy at he supermarket register even asked if I was leaving a tip as there is no table service whatsoever at this establishment. This place gets 4 stars for their hot sauce and tacos, 2 stars for the incredibly slow kitchen , 1 star for the no frills drab decor, 1 Star for no music, and 1 Star for no table service. If I ever come here again in the future it will only be if I place a to-go order a half hour in advance and consume these tacos in a nicer more festive atmosphere. Manuel taqueria is way faster, way more festive, way friendlier, and also always had $2 tacos so I'd have to recommend that place over this one for those seeking an alternative to this place. Otherwise I highly recommend placing a to-go order a half hour before you come here!

Thai Island is located on Davis Island on the East Davis boulevard strip next to 220 East, Fountain Mediterranean, Margaritas Mexican, Farrell's on the Island, Islands Pizza, Anchor Bar, and Molly Malone's Irish pub. Service and the Kitchen was painfully slow even though the restaurant was only about half full. I had to ask for a drink refill, the spice rack, and the check twice. The decor of the restaurant is on the low end of the scale. Not sure why they have these crazy frog statues everywhere. Aside from the crazy frogs, the tables and chairs looked very old and worn out and the place is in need of a severe renovation. Our table had a booth on one side and chairs on the other. Both the chairs and booth were not that comfortable and could use a bit more padding. I got the steak pad Thai and while the portion size was good, there was a much greater proportion of noodles than vegetables and beef so I was left with many servings of noodles absolutely by itself. The Thai Island Scallop dish had some large sized scallops but they were a bit chewy and the sauce was not quite as flavorful as I'd like. If I lived on Davis Island, I'd go here a lot just because it's convenient. For Davis Island residents, thai Island provides a convenient addition to round out the restaurant options of the island. For non Island residents, I would have to recommend instead trying  Si Am Thai in downtown Tampa for better food and Service, just a short 5 minute drive away!

Samurai Blue Sushi & Sake Bar was one of the best sushi bars in Tampa Bay but sadly the quality and service has fallen quite considerably on my most recent visits. 

Samurai Blue Sushi & Sake Bar is located on The 2nd floor of Ybor Centro in Ybor City next to Hamburger Marys, Cento Cantina, Tampa Bay Brewing Company, and Muvico / Amc Theaters. When you first walk into Samurai Blue you are struck by the super high brick ceilings which create quite an aura of elegance. There is a very long sushi bar with 3 Sushi chefs on the left side of the restaurant with dojo Japanese style booths on the right side of the restaurant, and a dimly lit sale bar in the back of the restaurant. 

For the appetizer I got the traditional ginger salad and it was not bad but I have to say that the ginger dressing has a tangier zestiest flavor at most other places I've visited including Soho Sushi, Ciccios, and Sushi Ninja. 

My biggest mistake was getting the infamous volcano roll without even reading the contents of the roll from the menu. Usually, you can't go wrong with this roll as it is he same at every restaurant. However, I was shocked to see that it came topped with conch instead of crab meat. Sadly, Samurai blues conch was baked and quite chewy unlike Hula bays tempura conch which was tasty and crunchy. Unfortunately I ate too much of the conch roll dish by the time I realized how bad the conch was, so I couldn't send the dish back. I'd rather have the traditional crab meat topping like the one from Soho Sushi. Restaurant staff should really warn patrons that they are ordering a non traditional volcano roll. It is a complete mystery to me why Samurai Blue insists on calling this the volcano roll when it is not a true volcano roll. It really should be called the conch roll. The name is definitely misleading. 

I also got the Kyoto roll which consisted of salmon, lemon slices, avocado, spicy shrimp, crab, topped with smelt roe, scallions, and sesame seeds. On another occasion I got the ocean blue Tempura roll and the rainbow roll and those were pretty good but didn't knock my socks off. 

I've had some amazing and unique rolls here in the past. I just wish i could remember which rolls those were. Sadly, Samurai Blue's sushi rolls are kind of hit or miss, so if you do come here, make sure to get the crowd favorites and avoid the rest. 

Aside from our server failing to warn us that the volcano roll comes with conch and our server failing to  offer a substitute crab meat for the volcano roll, our service was very very slow. Our server kept us waiting for an excruciating 20 minutes to ring up the bill and it wasn't even busy. There was only 2 other people sitting at the bar and another 6 people in the whole restaurant. Sadly, I Just blew a ton of dough on some less than stellar "deluxe" rolls and I'm still craving a real volcano roll. Our server said they do serve the volcano roll topped with crab meat by request. Maybe next time I'll order the volcano roll with crab instead of conch or just skip this place and go to Soho Sushi, Ciccios, Lure, or Sushi Ninja which are all much closer to home, with better service, and better rolls.  Sadly while most upstanding sushi restaurants do not charge extra for a side of spicy mayo and eel sauce, this place does.

Backwaters is a great seafood restaurant located on Sand Key island, just 1 Island south of Clearwater Beach. I got the Grilled Snapper scallops and shrimp blackened cajun style with a side of fries, garden salad, and lobster bisque soup and everything was pretty tasty. My friend got he rib eye and enjoyed it as well. I'm not a big rib eye fan myself so I really can't comment on the quality of the cut of meat. Service was quick and friendly. We sat at the bar and talked to some tourists visiting from Michigan. There is an on-site parking lot with plenty of parking available shared by other businesses in the plaza. This establishment has a Full liquor and a large variety of seafood. The decor of this place is a bit old school southern touristy, casual, and aquatic with a shark and fish hanging. We had no wait to get seated and the food came out in under 10 minutes which is always a plus! The outside patio offers pretty views of the inter coastal! I look forward to coming back again soon!

Cheap Soho's advertised Yelp checkin special for a free shot is a farce but management hasn't taken it off after a year because they like the extra yelp business!  Don't let the name of this place fool you, Cheap is anything but Cheap! The drink prices are the highest in all of the Soho strip! Their sushi used to be cheap when they had half off sushi night on Wednesday's but now they're not even open on Wednesday's anymore... They replaced their sushi deal with a lame $5 bar bites menu of food from which each party is limited to only 1 selection and the menu items do not appeal to me. Cheap management is so lazy they still have the sign up for their "summer hours" which are only Thurs Fri Sat and its February now, 6 months after summer has been over lol. At least print a new sign that doesn't say summer on it or be open more than 3 days a week lol. Cheap is an eye sore when it's closed with their lights off and a drag to the vibrant Soho strip because it's hardly ever open. I look forward to the day when new management takes over and either makes this 2 seperate bars or keeps this place open more than 3 nights a week. It's a real shame that this once great establishment has gotten rid of its sushi deals, can't honor yelp deals it has left up, and can't stay open more days per week. If this place would return to its old ways I'd gladly give them 4 or 5 stars in a heartbeat.

Cheap has the most chic decor of any bar on the Soho Strip! Theres a cool Tetris wall,  upholstered couches like car seats, upside down hanging lamps from the ceiling, and Cheap removed the 3 pool tables in the middle room in lieu of some more dining tables and chairs. With 3 rooms, 3 indoor bars, and 1 outdoor bar this place is pretty spread out and never gets too cramped or overcrowded. So Cheap can serve as a cool chill place for a date but who really wants to have a date at a place called Cheap? There is never live music here and no one ever dances here, so if you are looking for that you're better off elsewhere in Soho. Service has always been pretty quick and courteous as this bar never gets too busy because it's so spread out. The live DJ plays pretty good music.

Asiatic Thai Street Food & Noodle bar is located in Ybor City's Ybor Centro right next to Tampa Bay Brewing, Improv, Muvico Movie Theater, Hamburger Mary's, Game Time, and Hyppo Gourmet Ice Pops.  Asiatic Street Food is from the same owners as Thai Thani in Channelside, one of my favorite Thai restaurants ever, so I had to come here for some Thai!

We started off with Ground chicken pot stickers w ginger chestnuts red pepper green onions, Ground chicken gyoza pan seared with chestnuts red pepper ginger & onions, Pho with brisket meatballs basil. I had the Penang coconut Orange curry beef and it was amazing! My buddy had the Kao soi curry noodle w yellow curry and my other buddy had the Phad Kua Kai with chicken and squid and everyone was pleased with their meals. We were seated without any wait and our food came out in under 10 minutes! Service was very quick and friendly and the food couldn't have been better! Look forward to coming back again soon!

Sorry to say it got off to a rough start when arriving on a week night at 6 pm, with the place 1/2 empty the hostess asked me if I had a reservation, i said no, she looked at me somewhat confused and said i would have to go to the bar area even though it does look full we have a lot of reservations! 
I mentioned to her that i know the owner and she whispered in front of me to her co worker then sat me down at a table. 
I notice for the next two hours the tables that were availble never completely filled? 

Just dont like the send me to the bar game, especially if the business isn't really happening!!!

Food was good, table service was great. 

Prices are a bit high. 

Chicken dish which was nice should come with bigger portion of grits! 

Otherwise ill give it a second chance.

--- Short Synopsis ---

Pats and Geno's are a must stop (tourist) destination for any Philly visitor! Geno's is across the street from the Pats and Pats has the better cheesesteak in my opinion.

Geno's cheesesteaks seem to have more emphasis on the (firmer) bread and onions than Pats. Pats cheesesteaks have more meat and juiciness though. 

--- Detailed Review ---

For parking, there is street parking nearby as people come and go from Pats and Geno's. Geno's is cash only and a normal cheesesteak is (currently) $10. This price (~$10) seems to be the norm around Philly.

Moving onto the cheesesteaks, I ordered wiz wit (cheesesteak with cheese whiz and onions). Geno's keeps the meat in slices instead of chopping them up like many other cheesesteak institutions. This means the meat takes up less space. This is analogous to having 8 pieces of stacked and flat paper versus 8 pieces of shredded and crumbled up paper. Still, it just felt like the meat was lacking something, whether it was volume or taste. The bread was a little firmer and tougher than I would have liked, but held the cheesesteak together well.

I did enjoy the other aspects of the cheesesteak though! I liked the onions that were not overcooked to the point of no taste. Instead, I could actually taste some onion flavor and texture. Geno's puts a nice amount of onions on as well. The cheese whiz was nice and tasty. It was also put on the bread (instead of the meat like Pats). The cheesesteak was cleaner and easier to eat than Pats, but lacked the juiciness and flavor from the meat that Pats has. 

On another note, one of the more controversial aspects to Geno's is their sign stating "This is America. When ordering, please speak English." 

I definitely needed this sign, because I was going to order in Chinese (Mandarin). Of course, I am being sarcastic. I feel like this sign has caused Geno's a great deal of (racism) trouble and tension. I feel like the sign doesn't belong here. In fact, I am not sure who the sign is for, because people who generally can't speak English, cannot read English either. As always with English, there are exceptions to this and some people may be able to read and not speak English. The sign did not bother me drastically, but it was something to note.

Regardless, I would suggest trying Pats first, as it is better and the original. Then, if you still have room, maybe try Geno's across the street to compare.

The new owners are construction people only thing they know about a restaurant is ordering a meal. They didn't want to pay Lou the great chef of Catelli so the food has gone way downhill. They are trying to hire cheaper employees yet charge the same. 

This place was unbelievable when Lou was the chef, the owner is in over his head, The guy who claims to be the GM is the most disrespectful person Ive ever dealt with at any local establishment, they have ruined this place! 

Sell it and bring back the people who really stood for CATELLI!

The last time I was in this place was 10 years ago, when I had a whole lot less saggy skin and wrinkles, and a smaller belly. 
But luckily my larger belly allows me to enjoy more of the food this time around.
On a random weekday early evening, I sauntered into the space. Right from the beginning the service was lovely. 
We ordered a few things from the menu. Standouts for me were the chicken liver mousse. Light and rich all at once. The bread was toasty and warm.
The salad was well made and the beef tartare was tasty but not one of the standouts. The pasta dishes were also perfectly al dente. The corn ravioli special was so good but a little bit oversalted.
They sent out an extra cauliflower dish which was great!! The panna cotta was a lovely flavor but texturally a bit firm. 
Overall this place is a place I would return to again and again. So glad it's open.

i am literally so livid with this place that i needed to come home and write this right away.

so it's a wednesday night, about 930.  i heard about david ansill becoming the chef of this place, so i'm very excited to try it out again.
my friend and i meet at the entrance and walk in.  we were ignored by the hostess.  literally.  so we sat down at one of the high top tables.  a server walks by to get to the station, but doesn't say a word to us.

so my friend heads over to the bar, and the bartender knows nothing about whether or not there's a server for the table, what time the kitchen closes, and doesn't offer us menus.

the server walks by our table again.  she says she's no longer serving.  the kitchen closes in 5 minutes.  she doesn't offer us menus or tell us where to order.

and that's when we leave.

seriously?  this is no way to run a business.  your website says you are open until 2 am.  you have a late night menu that starts serving at 10 pm.  your server and bartender offer none of these choices to us.

i'm sorely disappointed.  and like the bitter vengeful person that i am, i now hope that this place either replaces everything about its management, or it closes its doors.

My colleague said this was their favorite new restaurant, and so of course I had to go. 
The space is so lovely. The bar in the front is beautiful, and I love the open kitchen in the back.

Don't refuse the bread. It's so good. The butter is amazing. Get the beignets. They savory, fluffy, and perfect. I could have this and a glass of wine every night. Divine. 

The hen of the woods is also another dish not to be missed. Perfect with the ricotta. 

I was disappointed by the foie. The ratio of bread to foie was off for me, and the bread was a bit too... dry?  While the pasta was good and would be a standout dish at any other restaurant, it definitely took a back seat to the duck we had. The pommes anna were super fun with the perfect amount of crispiness and the aired foamy cheese. I don't know if I'd get it again--i would probably just get a second order of beignets instead. Ha!!

I love how the menu changes, and I'm looking forward to happy hour at the bar!

My 400th review and I'm so glad it's this lovely place. My friend and I came for lunch on a weekday--if this place were in center city it would be packed! Instead it was busy but still easy to get a table.
The setting is gorgeous, airy and light. Service was amazing, fast and courteous.
But obviously the highlight is the food. It leans Mediterranean but there are some more global dishes (such as the pork ramen). We had the zucchini hummus, tomato soup with grilled cheese, the above ramen, pork belly, and coconut pudding for dessert. Every bite was flavorful and complex. 
The hummus was fresh and light; the pita was perfectly grilled. The tomato soup was so rich and flavorful and the crustless grilled cheese was perfectly cooked. I just wanted more. 
The pork belly was everything that it would be, rich and not chewy. The fattiness was perfectly cut by the grilled peaches.
I wish this place was in the city, I'd be there frequently!

I've been visiting New Orleans for more than forty years, and in that time, I've been a frequent, enthusiastic and grateful customer of Verti Marte, but until I started this review, I didn't realize that not only have I never been inside the place, but I don't even know where it is.

Because going to Verti Marte isn't what Verti Marte is for. 

Verti Marte is for it's 3:30 in the morning and you've just returned to your hotel, having finally remembered where you're staying, and your buddy says he's hungry and you realize that you guys haven't eaten since noon the day before, and you're starving and you're thirsty for beer, and you need cigarettes. Also, your hotel room is out of toilet paper and you don't want to bother housekeeping, it being 3:30 in the morning.

The little man in your brain that keeps you from killing yourself every time you drink reminds you that Verti Marte delivers poboys, beer, cigarettes, and toilet paper, and that you've had the store on speed dial forever. He also reminds you that Verti is cash-only, and that because you're about to drunk-dial a deli to order an unreasonable amount of stuff delivered through the dark of night (in the rain, for God's sake), you should tip, and not be cheap about it.

Yep. All of that. That's what Verti Marte is for.

The best food-related thing that happened to me in 2019 was that when I tried to book dinner at Philadelphia's award-winning Zahav Restaurant, the place was unable to accommodate my request.

My dining companion, a local Philadelphian, suggested that we try Suraya, a Lebanese restaurant well-regarded by Philly's food press. Though I was skeptical of Suraya's newness and trendy popularity, I am a sucker for good Lebanese cooking, so I booked a reservation.

As a result, I enjoyed the best meal I've eaten in years. Thanks, Zahav.

[n.b. I'm about to sound ensorceled by Suraya's charms, so to maintain some credibility, here's my single complaint: Suraya's cardamom-scented kouign-amann was good, but not as good as one I had earlier that day at ICI Macarons & Cafe. That's it. That's all I've got.]

**********
Our meal began at Suraya's tidy bar, where, on the recommendation of our barman, Jesse, we ordered Old-Fashioneds made with Sazerac Rye. Mine was the smoothest and most elegant Old-Fashioned I've ever tasted. Jesse is a boss.

My buddy and I had arrived with a plan in mind. The flexibility of Suraya's tasting menu and the range of choices it offered appealed to us, and we'd already made our selections.

But then we were shown to our table, a perch set slightly above the main floor that provided a view of the open kitchen, where a wood-burning oven was cooking the dinner I didn't know I wanted.

As she took our order, our server, Nena, asked if I'd like the special: slow-roasted young goat with stewed chick peas, Swiss chard, garlic and cilantro, finished with crispy shallots, lemon yogurt and goat jus.

Are you kidding me?

Does a stranded man long for his lover's embrace? Do birds enjoy a light thermal lift as they cross the sea? And, speaking of birds, do Eagles fans revel as Tom Brady slips into aged decrepitude?

The answers, of course, are "yes," "yes,"  and "Hell, yes!" 

I thanked Nena and asked, "May I please have the goat as a part of the tasting menu?" She said, "Sure," then left for the kitchen.

Soon, Nena brought our mezza, then these things happened:

- Substantial but light and slightly lemony hummus that reminded me of the hummus my Teta made by hand, fifty years ago

- Baba ganoush, whose charred eggplant was seasoned with tehina, lemon, garlic and a special treat: sweet and smokey urfa biber chili

- Muhammara, a smooth spread of roasted red pepper and pulverized walnuts blended with chili and cumin 'til it was dense and rich, like pesto, but spicier and more appetizing 

- Labneh, an Arab dairy respite from smoke and spice, a purpose served in other cuisines by lassi, tzatziki and kefir
 
- Tabouli, a usual hearty and cooling salad of parsley, cucumber, tomato, scallion and mint, made unusual by a tart drop of pomegranate molasses

Nena, a skilled and personable server, was unstoppable, as was the mezza, which also included: fried kibbeh (beef and bulgur "dumplings" stuffed with raisins & pine nuts); fattoush (another salad, dressed with lemon-pomegranate vinaigrette); and baskets of fresh-baked Arab bread or "khubz" that was just-chewy, tender and good enough to eat on its own, all night long.

**********
Here's how to eat at Suraya: bite, savor, look around, order more, take a different bite, chat, sip, then do it all again.

Dining at a Lebanese table is a creative endeavor that requires one to engage; "What should I taste next? How would this taste if combined with that?" We're also asked to appreciate the art on the plate; not gratuitous "look-what-I-can-do" decoration, but actual food, placed in such a way that the eater is enticed not to gush and take photos, but to eat.

By now, seven stellar dishes into the evening, I'd abandoned my usual pessimistic expectations. I was persuaded to trust Suraya's chef and his cooks to respectfully interpret recipes handed down by the owners' grandmother - the eponymous Suraya - and developed in consultation with her daughter, Maude.

It was clear that they weren't trying to improve (or, despicably, to "reimagine") Suraya's food in some Millennial way, but were instead doing as they'd been taught, then ever-so-slightly tweaking, using best-quality and authentic ingredients that took their food from what one might find at home to dishes one might find in the best hotels along Beirut's Corniche.

**********
For his main course, or "mashawi" - a rough equivalent to the Italian "secondo" - my friend ordered kawarma - Suraya's grilled and slow-roasted lamb, which was rubbed with "baharat," a mixture of black pepper, allspice, cardamom and other savory spices.

I tasted his meal, which was delectable. Then I savored my own fork-tender, succulent, almost buttery portion of goat ribs and loin. I'm embarrassed to say that I gloated as I announced that my plate won the evening.

Finally, as a bonus, Suraya only offers roasted goat every few weeks - ten orders per night - and by coming across it when I did, I lucked out. 

So really; thanks again, Zahav.

Suggested by a friend who's a taco connoisseur, my girlfriends and I decided to check out Honest Tom's. 

It's right off the beaten path in University City and has lovely outdoor seating near the road. There's more than just tacos, there are burritos too! We came for the tacos and, between the three of us, we tried the pork and chicken tacos. I love the assortment of sauces that they offer and really enjoyed the Halloween sauce. I also love that the tacos come with guacamole and fresh veggies. Being able to eat outside and just enjoy our tacos really made our visit to Honest Tom's worth it. 

Overall, they are solid tacos and a great bang for your buck. It can get quite busy but they get to you quite quickly and efficiently. I thought that the seasoning for the meat was a bit lacking but it was made up by the fresh ingredients in the guacamole and veggies. I wish they didn't sell out of fish tacos when I went but I will just have to return to Honest Tom's to check them out.

Did you ever leave a restaurant angry at yourself because you hadn't eaten there sooner? Well that happened to me when I left Salt + Smoke. 

Sugarfire, Stumpys, Hendricks, Pappys. and all the rest. Well, they're kind of like the girls you date until you find the one you want to spend the rest of your life with and that's Salt + Smoke. 

I had the combo with ribs and brisket. Having lived in Texas I'm a brisket snob and I'm always hesitant to order it anywhere but Texas. Salt + Smoke doesn't disappoint other then the disappointments out feel when you're full and realize you can't eat anymore of that juicy, succulent, perfectly cooked brisket, the ribs were just ridiculous, and don't get me started on the best Mac n cheese I've ever had. 

Thank you for ruining every other BBQ restaurant for me!

I absolutely love this place!  So far I've had the chocolate/chocolate and sweet potato cupcakes.  Great!  Just enough to fix a sweet tooth and not too much that kills the diet.  I first thought they were too pricey at $3-4 for a cupcake, until I had my first bite at home, and thought well worth every penny.  No cutting corners here with ingredients which can ruin any good recipe.  Been to some of the other shops to try them out, and they were good and lower price, but I want great baked goods when I want them and I'm willing to pay good money for it!

Seriously, the best Schezuan around. I think it beats Han Dynasty simply because it has so much more variety. It's as authentic as it can get, and the service is top notch. The owner always teases me for getting the same things (in a sweet, "grandpa" type of way), so whenever I get a recommendation, I do try it out. I've never had anything I did not like!

My favorite go-to's are:

*SPICY*
Wontons in Chili oil 
Dan Dan noodles
Poached pork (or fish) and cabbage in chili oil
Twice Cooked Bacon (pork belly) with Spicy Sauce
**NOT SPICY**
Salt & Pepper Jumbo Shrimp (to die for!)
Poached fish with garlic and scallions
Tea-Smoked Duck
Vegetable Delight (with extra tofu)... when I feel I need more veggies in my life

There are definitely dishes for people who can't handle the heat, but Schezuan food is not for the faint of heart, so most of the menu is for the fire-breathers out there. 

Also, if you're looking for Americanized Chinese Food (Egg Foo Young, Moo Goo Gai Pan, etc...), this is not the restaurant you want.  They have some of these dishes, but why would you get these here if this places specializes in AUTHENTIC Schezuan dishes?? Go somewhere else for that greasy, cheap Chinese food.

I've had the take-out and also dined in. Super friendly & fast service, with amazing food and a trendy, yet family friendly ambience (considering the type of food). I think this place is the total package. But I'm also Asian, and this type of food is my all-time favorite, so I'm a little biased! Just go! If you're into Asian food, you will NOT be disappointed. 

Didn't think it could get better? Bonus: This place is a BYOB!

In Ali Wong's recent standup special on Netflix (Baby Cobra), she goes off on the lack of authenticity of the Vietnamese restaurant her then boyfriend took her out to on their first date, a place called Pho Sho.  I'm paraphrasing, but she proceeds to rant that this place clearly is not authentic since the name of the restaurant does not include a number, one is not publicly berated by the servers,  and the bathroom does not double up as a supply closet with gallons of bleach and a Vietnamese grandma with glaucoma sitting in the corner.   

While one has the option of the veritable Pho75 within a 2 minute walk of here, one could make the argument that Le Viet would be the superior option for date night without making significant compromises in authenticity.  Sure, there's no number in the name and at least they resisted the urge to interject a pho-gettable bún, I mean pun, but when one walks in, the modern  decor, well-stocked bar, and open window into the kitchen definitely makes one suspect he/she is dining at [insert your favorite non-Asian Top Chef]'s take on Vietnamese fusion, since it looks WAY too nice and clean.  However, upon opening their menu, one sees that this is most definitely an authentic Vietnamese eatery that include the usual classics (bún, pho, spring rolls, stir fries, rice plates) but also include native favorite appetizers such as Hn Xúc Bánh Đa (baby clams,beef, peanuts served atop sesame rice crackers), Bánh Xèo (savory crepe), Chim Cúc Quay (deep fried quail), and Bò Tái Chanh (vietnamese take on carpaccio).   

Not only is the plating beautiful often with intricate knifework on the garnishes but they care to go the extra mile in the details, whether it be broken rice and a bowl of broth in the rice plate, bone-in chicken for the pho ga, and a set of signature cocktails to elevate the dining experience.   Our experience was capped by more hits(the deep fried soft-shell crabs with ginger and onions (62) and the house special pork chop rice plate served with egg quiche, shredded pork, and an exquisite fried egg atop broken rice) than misses (avoid the papaya salad; pho purists seem to be underwhelmed based on other reviews).  My advice would be to go a little off book with less traditional offerings that can be shared family style and save room for some drinks/dessert.  You can always head across the street to Pho75 and pay your respects to the grandmother lurking in the bathroom when you are recovering from a cold in need of a steaming bowl of pho.

P.S. Credit cards accepted, and in case you were wondering, service and bathroom are stellar (pho sho)

For my 200th review, I figure it would be apropos to share my experience at Monell's which is located a stone's throw away from Nashville's BICENTENNIAL Capitol State Mall Park.   Believe me when I say after one eats here, you will definitely need a place to walk off them calories. 

Located within a Victorian style mansion with an outdoor garden and koi pond, one feels like they received an exclusive invite to a Nashvillian socialite's fancy Southern thanksgiving smorgasbord as you and any additional guests are seated at a communal table for 10 so if you're coming alone, you have 9 other guests with whom you get to know fairly well in the course of passing a wide array of Southern classic foodfare in a clockwise fashion until you turn in your ticket where it fittingly states "I've eaten and I can't get up!"

I came in for the lunch option on a weekday since I was drawn to the daily special of chicken and dumplins', a personal favorite of mine growing up in the South.  The meal proceeded with the following progression:

Starters: Fresh biscuits and cornbread squares- the biscuits definitely are the standout as they are hot, flaky, and punctuated with delicious sawmill gravy or house-made peach preserves whereas the corn bread is decent but nothing to write home about  

Beverages- options include both the traditional Southern sweetened brew (always brewed with the sugar so that it has some time to caramelize with the tea), the unsweetened option, and lemonade.  Feel free to titrate sweetness to your liking or go wild with some Arnold Palmer action.

The "Salad Courses"- perhaps the least unhealthy portion, try not to waste too much room in your stomach since there are much more exciting options to follow.  Our meal consisted of cole slaw and broccoli salad with pecans and raisins, but other options may pop up include a pea or macaroni salad, all with the collective theme of a mayonaise-based dressing.    

The "Warmup Round"- corn pudding, squash casserole, green beans, baked beans; hearty sides that really hit that comfort zone of overcooked veggies done right to absorb the flavors from the cooking liquid

The "Contenders"- a murderer's row of stick-to-your-ribs comfort foods including meatloaf, slow-cooked pork shoulder, the aforementioned chicken-dumplings, along with sidekicks of creamy mac and cheese and buttery mashed potatoes;  brace yourself and loosen your belt, this is why you skipped your previous meal in order to make room for the heavy-hitters.  Meatloaf is as juicy as it could possibly be with the perfect accent of ketchup to bind all the flavors together, the pork shoulder is fork tender breaking off like fresh fallen snow with each successive bite titivated by the decadent mac and cheese/mashed potatoes.  As for my beloved chicken and dumplins', I have to say it was a slight letdown for me since I was hoping the dumplins would be the hand rolled squares of dough dropped into the boiling cauldron of chicken stock rather than pieces of biscuits that is the lazy-man's version since I've already had the biscuits earlier and the best part of that dish is the mother-f-ing dumplings since they have that al dente/qq quality that everyone loves in a solid Italian gnocchi or Korean dukbokki (team chewy prevails over team fluffy in terms of my personal preference).

"Crunchtime"- Just when you think you've reached your limit, that's when they bring out the piece(s) de resistance, classic Southern fried chicken.  Succulent meat that has been seasoned/brined in buttermilk, perfectly crisped skin, and some closely guarded secret mixture of herbs/spices bastardized by a neighboring colonel, the real McCoy resides here rather than Kentucky.  I think every diner reaches that epiphany where they regret having eaten everything before since there's only so much room left in the belly for the amazing fried chicken.  

"Overtime"-  The desserts usually consist of banana pudding or a slice of chocolate fudge/chess/pecan pie.  Fairly traditional, but clearly outmatched by the previous dishes.  Don't feel bad if you can't get in a bite, since if you get a second wind upon departure, The Cupcake Collection a few doors down is the perfect sweet epilogue with their array of sweets. 

Monell's is definitely a Music City must-do and quintessential Nashville experience since it  hits all the high notes of Southern hospitality- warm, sweet, welcoming, decadent, charming, communal, gracious, traditional, satiated...done and done.

The figurative cherry on top:  all this can be had for under $15 for lunch/breakfast (except for Sunday lunch ($21) and dinner (Tues-Thursday $16, Fri-Sat $19).

Absolutely avoid.

Service could be most charitably characterized as abysmal, and the front of the house manager is a jerk.  The parking, listed as "free after 6" is incorrect, and they were too lazy to correct in their web site or on Open Table.  When a $20 parking ticket was incurred (parking directly in front of the restaurant), the manager was obnoxious in dealing with me, despite admitting that (for 6 months!) the town had changed its parking time limits, and he had not bothered to update the information posted.

Food not worth the extremely poor attitude and customer service.

AVOID...

AVOID...

AVOID!!!
Poor service. Limited menu. Food was hit or miss. Stay away from the cochinita torta.

As a worker in the restaurant world, I never leave reviews on yelp. But Lee's Deli is such a great place and somewhere I feel truly deserves a review. The food has always been great- whether a regular cheesesteak, the Korean BBQ cheesesteak, homefries or a bacon egg and cheese (always on a kaiser roll), it's all delicious. But where I think Lee's stands out is Mr. Lee himself. He just such a nice guy. They only take cash and sometimes I forget that, or just don't have cash on me. Every single time that's happened Mr. Lee has generously given me a dessert on the house, or told me my coffee was on him. He does this merely because the ATM has a fee and feels the customer should be compensated. I've never found this anywhere else. He is always so kind, remembers his customers and does his best to make sure you've had a good experience! This place is awesome!! Thank you Mr. Lee!!!!!

Love this place! The atmosphere is always so welcoming. The servers are quite attentive and the fact that they are Italian adds to the charm of the place. I always go there for the coffee and gelato but went for dinner this time. The bread and olive oil in the beginning was fantastic. The pasta was  the tagliatelle comes with a pork product that I asked to be excluded (since I don't eat pork) but superb meal overall

Best breakfast place in Philadelphia! Especially if you are looking for a middle eastern twist. Everything looks picture perfect and tastes better. The owner is super friendly and is so involved with the service. Been there atleast half a dozen times so far and the outdoor seating is perfect with a sanitizer on every table! #faveplaceforbreakfast

I've been to this place a bunch. Amazing bread (quite literally the best part) food is always great as well. Haven't had a dish there I didn't like but I mainly go there for the atmosphere the of this place. Main reason I keep going back. The seating and location is perfect for people watching and gives you that European feel. Service is always superb!

Food was good. That's the most important thing right?

Bf made a reservation for 4 on Saturday Feb 13th for our valentines dinner with his brother n wife. We got to the place 15 minutes before our reservations and was not seated until closer to 7, when our reservations were for 6:30pm. They needed to wait for tables to clear. (This is expected because it's valentines weekend. I already didn't have high expectations of getting seated right away.) As we walked in,  I noticed every girl getting a rose from the hosts. We did not get one.
The server we got was very attentive but did not check in throughout the meal. I'll go into details later. You can see and read from previous reviews that this is pretty common here?

We started with drinks and apps. We also put our food order in at the same time. The table we got was not that big so we had to work with what we got. They serve complimentary bread while we wait. We lucked out on our server in my opinion. She dropped the bread off right away and got our drinks. I noticed other tables didn't even have silverware or bread for at least 20 minutes. 
Our apps came out right away

Spanish Platter - $18 (7/10)
Comes with assorted cheeses, a small variety of meats(prosciutto, salami, chorizo), some nuts and bread. The meats were super dry. 

Flash Fried Calamari - $17 (10/10)
Can't go wrong with calamari. It was a big portion!

Shoestring fries - $6 (9/10)
We shared as a table. They were not as crispy as I hoped. These were recommended by the server herself. 

Cedar Plank Verlasso Salmon - $38 (8/10)
Crispy sesame rice, ginger and mirin glaze ( a bit heavy imo), mango relish and broccolini which I didn't see much of it. 
Salmon had a NICE crisp to it, but it was really drenched in ginger and mirin glaze, so it had to be accompanied by the rice in each bite. 

Roxy Filet Mignon 7 oz - $40 (8/10)
Comes with sauteed asparagus, pickled onion and beamaise (sauce with butter n egg yolks)  Best thing we had here. We asked for it medium and it was nearly rare. Didn't want to make a big deal of it, so I sat there eating it anyway. 7 oz is a small steak, but at least it was better than the rest of the things we had. 

Roxy Rib eye - $42 (6/10)
14 oz black garlic butter - duck fat yukon gold home fries. Waste of money and was cooked incorrectly. The rib eye was supposed to be medium well but came out WELL WELL DONE and was so dry. The garlic barely saved the darn thing. The yukon fries were basically the potatoes itself! Pass on this! Not the best, but what can you do at this point?! Later, we find out the server had served us the wrong rib eyes. My bf and his brother bought got rib eyes, but she served my bf the well done one and not the medium well one. 


Wild Mushroom - Truffle Mac n cheese - $11 (10/10)
Fav! But also, I LOOOOVE mac n cheese. Bomb. The mushrooms were a nice touch to the mac. 

So why the 4 stars? Mix up in the steaks served. lack of checking in on the tables. Had to ask for water refills.

At the end, the server left after we paid. Another hosts walked by, noticed we didn't have any roses and brought us 2. 

Would I come back? Possibly, but I wouldn't crave it! The menu isn't as diverse as I'd like it to be and it is pricy for okay meats.

Holy Crap!  What a good unplanned lunch.  After the line at Hattie B's turned out to be too long, we started walking towards our hotel and since I love Mexican cuisine, I made the decision that we would eat here instead.  Everyone agreed and 6 of us piled into a booth for a late lunch (it was around 2:30 or so).

It wasn't busy and we were promptly seated, presented with chips and salsa, and ordered non-alcoholic drinks (we still had work later). The waiter took everyone's orders, everything came out rather quickly and correctly, and everyone enjoyed their meals.  

I ordered the chimichanga and oh boy, that sucker was huge.  It's rare that I don't finish a chimichanga, but on this day, even with a late lunch and being super hungry, DNF this behemoth.  Maybe it was all the chips, salsa, and guac (we ordered that too), but I tapped out quicker than Batman in a cage match with Superman.  (c'mon, Superman would destroy Batman).

They had the option of ordering a Chimi "Sam Style" which includes a crunchy beef taco.  That's totally "Joe Style" as I totes do that at Mexican restaurants as crunchy beef tacos are my favorite.

If I was in the area and hungry for Mexican food, I'd totally stop here again.

I heard about their bourbon from a friend and when I found out this restaurant was affiliated, I had to try. Sadly, they're closed Mon/Tue/Wed and being from out of town, those are the days I'm IN town as I typically leave on Thursdays. I was able to find a Tasting which includes a flight, an appetizer, and an amazing story-telling intro. It was $50 but the prices of the items on the menu came to around $40 so really, it's just an extra $10! Even though they're closed on Wednesdays, they had a tasting at 4p.

Parking was easy as they have their own lot on 23rd which is just a block away (ode to Billy Milano) and just past the restaurant if you're driving west. (and just before if you're driving east).

Walking in, you're impressed by the massive entrance (which is hard to appreciate as you're walking up from the side), and the spacious atmosphere of the huge building. They went all out over your typical distillery affiliated restaurants. There are some comfy chairs and a couch, a retail store to purchase their spirits and other tchotchkes.

For the tasting, there's a separate tasting room which was set up with 3 nice sized pours of their bourbons (4 if you opt for the commander select option for an additional $50) and a nice charcuterie board with meats and cheeses. I wish I had an option for the appetizer as I don't typically eat meat/cheese.

Morgan took over and explained the story of the former green berets and their story after the 9/11 terrorist attacks on our nation. I didn't know the movie "12 Strong" was based on their story. Their website explains a lot and makes you fall in love with the idea of this place even more. Morgan then explains the different bourbons, walks you through tasting them, and really engages the patrons. There's a small tour too. On this day, they had their very first bottle mold forged from World Trade Center steel and he let us hold it. That sucker is heavy! Every bottle of Horse Soldier touches WTC Steel! Amazing! Sadly, they were out of the small batch (my favorites), so I did not purchase a bottle on this day. I plan on it next time.

Looks like a good place to dine. Vegans may have trouble finding something to eat, but in this case, I'm not taking off a star for that. You'll probably have to custom order something or load up on Enoki Mushrooms. They have lots of meat and seafood options. With St. Pete really being veggie lover friendly, I was surprised as many newer places are being mindful of dietary needs.

5-Stars because they deserve it. Excellent bourbon, excellent atmosphere, and excellent hosting for this tasting event. Never Forget!

Wow, what a standout on a block full of eateries. This small little restaurant was one of the few places open late for a vegan snack.  I ordered the Curry Vegan Sausage plate which came with 2 Crispy and Juicy Vegan Brats (I'm assuming they use the Beyond brand, but not 100% certain) slathered in a curry gravy which was so delicious.  These were served alongside some fresh, crispy fries and a pile of authentic sauerkraut.

The gentleman wasn't shy about saying how good these would be, and graciously took the order and brought the food to the outdoor table.  Very pleasant man and very excellent food. Sehr Lecker!!

After being disappointed with Hattie B's and being stuck downtown without a car, I settled on The Diner for lunch, which was close to my hotel, before I headed back to the airport.  I walked in and it was kinda small and not too busy, then the hostess told me to go up to 6.  What?  A multi-story diner?  Pretty cool. The 6th floor is where it's at!

I ordered the Hot Chicken and Biscuits and was impressed. The hot chicken came out and had a nice spice (maybe a medium in my book) and had the flavor that I remembered from Prince's (where I first had Nashville Hot Chicken where the medium there was hotter than any other of the Hot's I had on my trip). 

The bartender was a rock star.  Literally 1 person handling all the drinks and taking orders, refilling glasses, and just killing it.  There were probably 10 parties of 2 or less strewn about the non-linear bar area (I didn't get a picture).

What do you do when yesterday, the line was too long and you are going to Eddie V's and you get there 30 mins before your reservation?  Well, if you're a glutton like me, you notice the line was NOT out the door so you enter quickly and convince the others in your party you must try it.

After discussing options with the cashier, I decided on Hot (he described the heat level as traditional buffalo) to Damn Hot.  Not knowing what I was in for, I got Potato Salad and Cole Slaw as sides as they would have a cooling effect. The tater salad was good (mmm hmmm) and the Cole slaw was ok (could have been more creamy).

But you don't win friends with (tater) salad! We went for the chicken... The flavor of the Hot was excellent.  It had a little bit of heat, but nothing that had you sucking on your straw immediately.  The Damn Hot was spicy, but I didn't really like the flavor.  I did have to have a couple bites of that tater salad, cole slaw and some extra sips of Coke Zero to tame my mouth hole.

We were all happy we tried it as we had to see what the fuss was about.  I'd go back but I don't think I'd wait in a long line for it.  The dude said they take internet orders during the week so the wait isn't too bad.  I guess it depends on how many people order.  After we ordered and were waiting, there was NO LINE (see picture).  If you're lucky, you can score this food without the hassle.

A few years ago, I was able to try Prince's and I will say I prefer the oily spicy sauce there more than the Hattie B's version.  The chicken was still so good and juicy.  A few of us thought we could go one more level higher, and would hope the flavor was different than the damn hot.  Everyone is different so make your own decision on the heat level.

Relish is easily on my short list for favorite Sunday brunch locations. The food is superb. There's an excellent selection of food and everything is well executed. The drinks are awesome too. I dined there on Sunday and the meal was as yummy as expected. 

The customer service was not yummy. At some time after 1:20PM, after we'd finished eating, after we'd finished our Satchmo cocktails, 10 Cane mojitos and Hennessy sangrias and importantly....after we'd settled the bill, a manager came over to inform of that there is a two hour limit on the buffet and we've been there since 11AM (opentable reservation) and our table is needed. -_- Whet???? You have to appreciate that we were one of 3 occupied tables (two other parties of two) in the front dining area that seats 60ppl at least. The place was empty. "We need the table" was a lame excuse that I'll explain more in a sec. The issue was that this manager seemed to think that we were two people who would sit around and eat all day and she needed to call time on our eating. But we weren't eating. We were at the table talking and catching up. Bill paid. Plates cleared. Our server had no issue with our presence at all. After the offense washed over me I realized 1) I'm not eating but I also wasn't informed at the time of seating of this two hour dining policy 2) surely this exchange could have been handled with more tact 3) why do I feel shamed for sitting at a table in an empty dining area catching up with a friend on a Sunday? 

My friend felt compelled to gather our things and talk to the manager on the way out. I was more inclined to ignore nonsense until it makes sense meaning continue as we were. I lost. On the way out we talked the MOD who genuinely apologetically explained that it's a restaurant wide policy they are required to enforce because "people come in like it's an old country buffet." I wanted to retort that her management approach mirrors that in that it wasn't patron friendly or reflective of customer service practices but alas... I'm disheartened that Relish thinks of themselves on par with fast casual venues. I've liken them to my local high end dining destination. In turn I've expected much more tactful and customer friendly service. If I wanted to be timed on my seating and invited to leave brunch, there are several other places I could be treated poorly for less. I truly expected more respect and value for the guest experience. I have had better experiences there. I believe they are capable of better. 

Back to the "we need the table" position. After talking with the manager, my friend and I continued our conversation for another hour in the waiting area. During that time zero people were seated at our table or in the front dining area. Our waitress continued to serve the couples in the area which suggests that we weren't holding up closing the area. The manager even walked by and said, "oh you guys are still here?" Funny that would have been a perfect opportunity to redeem the situation by inviting us in to a heated area but nope. I really considered the options for what happened here and I continue to land on daft, unskilled management and communication. It wasn't the chefs, the waitstaff or the hostesses. Just the management and that's so unfortunate.

Service: Brasserie needs to work on it. Brasserie Saint James seems to be uniquely positioned in the Midtown market: they have great beers that they brew themselves and they have business-casual fancy food. These features make it a great choice for showing millennial and slightly-older than millennial out-of-towners how great Reno is. But it doesn't work if your server doesn't come around often enough to take initial drink orders and then follow up for the next rounds. Please, management: hire more servers and train them to be more attentive!

Four years ago I remember their Buenos Aires barbecue (aka insanely awesome meat platter) as being AMAZING. Last week it cost $20 more than it used to four years ago, and what we received was underwhelming. Moreover, while I was encouraging our out of town guest and my fellow colleagues to order entrees in addition to the barbecue to showcase the other awesome food options Brasserie Saint James has to offer, our server actively discouraged us from doing so, saying that most folks just order the barbecue as their main. Um, since when do servers discourage folks from ordering menu items? We can see the prices listed, darlin', we know what we're paying for and we're not going to be mad at you if we have leftovers. 

So it was a weird experience, which is such a bummer, because the location is fantastic in Midtown, especially because no one seems to remember that there is parking on S Center. Unlike everywhere else in Midtown, if you know how to get onto this one-way street, you can find free parking directly in front of Brasserie even at 7 pm.

Friday evenings mean pizza dinner, and Blind Onion is our favorite place to pick up a delicious $25 large pizza. Is $25 an expensive pizza? If it is, we do not care: it is delicious, and among two people there is enough leftover for Saturday lunch and snack slices. Our orders are usually heavy on the meat: pepperoni, sausage, and bacon. Every single time, the twisted crust is perfect. 

I love the vibe of the employees who work here: chill dudes and dudettes who always get the job done. I never begrudge leaving a tip for them when I sign the credit card bill like I do at other pizza places (cough cough Round Table) where the employees are not consistently awesome.

Eating in for lunch is cool as well if one has an hour: the super slice is seriously the best pizza lunch deal in town.

I love all of the Blind Onion themed customer artwork on the walls, the sports on the bar TVs, and the board games that one can play while waiting. Okay, maybe they should invest in some new ones, cause some of the board games are missing a lot of pieces. But that doesn't take away from the awesomeness of this Blind Onion location. It's a totally unassuming space, in the plaza with the Goodwill and Subway and trying-too-hard nail salon and Taco Bell. Don't let that fool you: it's secretly the best. Word has it that we're even ordering a boatload of pizzas to go from here when we have our wedding rehearsal dinner in September!

I love brunching.  But I'm relatively new to town and my boyf lives ~2,000 miles away, so I don't yet have a go-to crew with whom to brunch.  Thanks to Robert S., however, I received an invite to brunch with mutual Yelp acquaintances!  Oxbow Cafe was an excellent place for an early Sunday morning brunch.

Oxbow Cafe is located on Dickerson Road, which is what west Second St turns into past the downtown area.  The cafe is located on the north side of the street (that is, the "right" side if one is coming from downtown; also, the side opposite from the river) in a building that is near the road.  A large cloth stand-up sign that reads "food" is set up in front of the building to mark it.  But, as I had thought the address was 3365 and not 2365, I totally missed it the first time around.  It was an easy error to fix: just turn around in a driveway before road dead-ends into the Oxbow Nature Study Area.

The cafe was just the right amount of busy at 9:30 am: full enough to give the place a good vibe, but not so full to make it difficult to nab a table for seven people.  The menu is organized in a clear manner--one page with no distracting graphics--and it contained just the right amount of options.  I ordered the French toast, which was sizable and scrumptious and only $4.99 (!), and my dining partners ordered the special of the day--eggs Benedict ($7.95) and the breakfast skillet (also $7.95).  My French toast was plated plain and simple, which was just fine for me, but the plating of the more expensive breakfast options was delightfully exquisite with a colorful arrangement of fresh fruit.
