One can order regular coffee or a wide variety of fancy coffee drinks, such as lattes and mochas and cappuccino.  One downside is that they do not offer fresh-squeezed orange juice.  There is also beer on tap and wine available, as the cafe is open for lunch and dinner as well as breakfast.  

The service was prompt, pleasant, and unobtrusive, and the interior of the cafe is pleasantly decorated and just the right noise level.  I am a fan of Oxbow Cafe and Bistro and look forward to taking the boyf here next time he visits.  It is a perfect place to eat after a short morning hike in the Oxbow Nature Study Area.

My husband and I moved from South Reno to Sparks, which meant that we needed to find a new go-to pizza place. Pizza Guys is the closest pizza place to our house, and it is a five-star establishment. It is very easy to order custom pizzas online, and they are ready to be picked up in 20 minutes as the online instructions indicate. We like pizza with thicker crusts, and Pizza Guys offers a thick crust option. It's perfect!

Besides delicious pizza that is affordable (approximately $24 for a custom-toppings large) and made on time, what I like best about Pizza Guys is the friendly and competent young people who are the employees. I'm a university professor, so it warms my heart to see high-school or early-college-aged students being responsible and looking like they are doing a good job. Pizza Guys almost has an open kitchen concept, so it's easy to see what is going on behind the scenes. Everyone looks friendly, on task, and ready to accomplish the mission of making delicious pizza. They always get a tip from me!

Access to and from Vista is easy, and there is ample parking in the lot. Walgreens is six businesses down if one needs to pick up non-soda beverages to go with the pizza.

Signing up for their e-mail alerts means getting coupons, like buy one get one free. We used that offer code last weekend, and man, was it great to see our $48 pizza order go back to $24!

I love pizza, and Blaze sent us a coupon for a free pizza. My husband and I went on a weeknight to try them, and lordy, I disliked their pizza. The dough was too chewy and did not have the right flavor. It took a long time to get through the line, and I could not hear the person who was making my pizza well because of the loud music. There is not a good waiting area to pick up one's pizza, so everyone ends up crowding around the area where the drink machine is. That makes it difficult to access the drink dispenser. I also think the parking lot in that shopping area is a mess to deal with. 

Whereas MOD does not differentiate in price whether you have two toppings or ALL THE TOPPINGS, Blaze does. I guess that's advantageous if you are a two-topping sort of person. I'm an all the toppings kind of gal, though, so we will be going to MOD instead.

I love that this place exists and that so many people in town are excited about them. Nevertheless, I was not impressed with the donut I had this morning: a yeast donut with thick chocolate frosting and butterfinger cookie crumbles on top. It looked delicious, but it just wasn't tasty. The chocolate frosting was way too thick, and the yeast donut was not as light and fluffy as I expect yeast donuts to be. Perhaps I have been spoiled by eating a donut from Doughboy's every Saturday morning for the last two years.

The two shelves of donuts are absolutely beautiful, though, and I love that there are some unique flavors that Doughboys does not have, like lemon frosted and orange frosted cake donuts. The Cookie Monster donut is so adorable, and my friend chose a donut that had Oreo cookie crumbles and gummy bears and worms. Next time I stop in, I'll try the Bavarian creme and see how it compares to Doughboy's.

My friend and I stopped in at 10:15 am on a weekday, and there were lots of parents with small children afoot. Small children are very cute, but sometimes they also scream and make a lot of noise. The industrial-like feel of the tables and chairs is so fitting for the space, but we did not want to linger at our table because the kiddos surrounding us were noisy.

I wish there were free parking nearby. There is lots of metered parking, and the meters accept change and credit cards.

We received very friendly service from the two people who were working behind the counter. I'm not a huge fan, but I'll definitely be back.

Pizza Friday is a tradition in our household, and My Pie has earned its spot in the rotation. Especially if they keep sending us coupons! 

My significant other and I mostly share the same taste in pizza, so normally we have no trouble agreeing on toppings for a whole pie. But when there are a plethora of toppings at no extra charge and I'm making my own personal pizza, I want all the things he would never want on my pizza. Being able to customize one's one six slice pizza is the best feature of this joint. We each ordered a pizza and shared an order of garlic knots, and we could only eat three slices each for dinner. The remaining slices were delicious when we put them in the toaster oven for lunch the next day.

Being located in the far east residential hub of South Reno, it really does feel like a neighborhood pizza place. The family friendly feel and the smiling faces and good attitudes of the employees who were working there on a Friday night were delightful. I am a sucker for good booth seating, and even though it's not individual booths, the booth seating that runs along a full wall was luxurious while we waited approximately five minutes after finishing paying for our pizzas to cook.

All was not perfect, though. The dough on the pizza the first night was a little chewy, which is weird on such a flat pizza. But it was totally edible, and the next day it reheated to perfect crispiness. The lettuce in the two bins closest to where one chooses the dough looked hella wilted even through the plastic half lids. But really, who orders a side salad or even a main salad at a personalized pizza place? Nevertheless, it made me go "uh oh" inside since it was the first bin of toppings I saw. You only need one bin of lettuce, not two, and that way it's easier to make sure it's fresh!

We will be back. I am delighted that the Chipotle/Subway style personalized pizza chain trend has finally broken into the Reno market! There are so many good places of this sort in Sacramento and Arizona, and we're excited that there is a good one nearby.

Donuts are delicious, and Doughboys's are especially so. Great variety, always fresh tasting, and served with a smile. There are also other pastries like croissants and claws, as well as bagels and breakfast sandwiches. The coffee is quite decent, and I'm never tempted to make a second stop at the Starbucks across the shopping plaza to get my coffee there. 

Sometimes on weekend morning Doughboys is very crowded and folks don't realize that there are usually three servers (always super cute/friendly ladies) behind the counter at once. But eventually they do realize it and order and the line moves quickly once that happens. While I'm waiting I like seeing the "feel good" stuff on the wall--newspaper clippings, photos of the little league teams they sponsor, and a plaque from the Salvation Army. There's also a nice flat screen TV to the left of the counter for those who like the moving images.

Doughboys is so good that I haven't even tired of it after going at least one day (and sometimes two!) a week. Highly recommend.

Sometimes I am a total cheapskate.  Sometimes I'm not.  When friends suggested a celebratory brunch, initially I thought $35 plus tip... ehh... it's near the end of the month, and I can convey my excitement for my friend at a different time and in a less expensive manner.  But Sterling's Sunday brunch has such a reputation for awesomeness that I committed to it.  It will be worth it, I told myself.  And, lo and behold, it was!

Buffets: love the concept.  Buffets with fancy pants food: oh my Lord.  I love meat but don't often cook it at home, so I loaded gleefully my first three plates with all kinds of meat: bacon, lamp chops, filet mignon, shrimp, and oysters.  It was all delicious.  I skipped the other foods they had on offer--fruit and vegetables, grains and pastries, and traditional breakfast foods--and rounded out my meal with three dessert courses, including an ice cream sundae.  Many of the fruit-based desserts are made in small pastry cups and the cake slices are cut small, so it's easy to sample a number of desserts.  Oh, and then I had more bacon.  The bacon was so delicious.

Unlimited mimosas and Bellini's: YES.  Our flutes were never ever less than three-fourths filled.  The coffee was also delicious.  

The service was above and beyond excellent.  We started as a party of six, but told the host that we might have eight.  Our party of six was complete at 10:45 am and we did not have to wait to be seated at an appropriately large table.  But then three, not two, friends arrived at 11 am.  No problem!  Although the table was set for eight, the floor manager and our server quickly acquired an additional chair and table setting and made it work.  Checks can only be divided between seven people, but our server did his best to make everything work out with respect to splitting the bill.  

The brunch ambiance is just right: fancy but not too fancy, serious but not too serious.  I can see how the roving flute/sax/clarinet player could come off as tacky, but our table LOVED his playing and he even played a request for us.  

Would I come back here again?  Yes, if I were celebrating a special but lighthearted occasion with friends or family and if I were in the mood to pay $45 (buffet including tip) for the experience.  Sometimes special occasions are best celebrated when everyone is at the table for the entire meal and the meals are plated, so it'd have to be an occasion in which a buffet setting is appropriate.  Nevertheless if I'm going to do a buffet and do it right: Sterling's is it.

I'm not sure if I have seen a local restaurant garner such a mixed reaction in conversation or social media. All else aside, I think there is something to be said for how passionate folks are about this place! Unfortunately, my experience here lies on the more negative end of the spectrum so far, especially compared to how great Olio is.  
A group of about 10 of us came for a dinner night a few weeks back. I already knew right where to come and was comfortable parking on the street even though there is a small lot and valet.  There was sign taped to the bar door instructing us to go to the next entrance.  We walked until we found the next entrance, which was in the next building over, a completely different business.  On the way back, the hostess opened the bar door for us to come inside and told us that they normally directed restaurant patrons through the patio, but it was closed.  Okay, why wouldn't you just take the taped sign down after you realized this?  It was still there when we left.  Minor beef, but it's really nice to make folks feel comfortable right off the bat, especially a new place in a mostly residential part of the city that a lot of folks aren't familiar with.
We met the rest of the group upstairs where we had a cozy little nook.  Looking over the menu, it sounded great.  Most of us went with the 4-course prix fixe.  The first course wound up being the best for many of us as a small starter with several options.  It went downhill from there.  Many of the 2nd and 3rd courses were a disappointment, such as bland borscht, charred octopus in salty ink broth, a steak served cold, another steak overcooked (this was corrected).  A scottish salmon plate seemed to be the only winner of these rounds, and that didn't garner raves, just that it was good.  My biggest disappointment was with the mackerel, slightly dry and served with what was supposed to be curry, but came out with a sweet & mild topping that I can only describe as....bland sauce.  Sensing a theme here?  Mackerel especially needs a bold accompaniment as it's a strong fish.  
Many folks didn't order dessert and instead traded plates for another 1st or 2nd course.  However, our waiter came right before the last course and insisted we all get it no matter what, how good it all was, and they we had to try everything.  I had ordered dessert with my 4 courses, so got mine as planned.  However, even folks that didn't order one and tried to ignore his hard sell, all wound up with dessert, and on the bill as well.  It was weird and uncomfortable, especially since it is very pricey.  No one said anything- I think we were just anxious to get out of there at that point.  My dessert, by far the fave, was a delicious chocolate chouquette, others were dry tea cakes and cookies. 
Another issue was the course timing- started at 7, finished after 11, so had 45 minutes to an hour between courses.  With the small first course, we were all starving by the time the 2nd course came around.  In between courses, very hard sells on wine.  One bottle I ordered was out of stock, the waiter offered a replacement that wound up being almost $30 more a bottle.  I should have asked, but more so it really should also have been mentioned.  Time between courses was also spent with servers having talks with folks around the table to tell them how food could no longer be prepared exactly as ordered.  It happened to me once, the person next to me 3 out of 4 courses (not counting the 5th course of dessert she got talked into!).  Each time she wound up not fully getting what changed.
Also unexpected was the 20% gratuity added on.  I understand it's for a large group, but 20% is a stretch to assume, especially for okay service in an expensive place.  My tip for my portion was $30+ (my wine alone wound up costing double the 4 course meal!).  I normally do start my tip at 20%, but was still taken aback at the entitlement.  I don't think anyone then tipped over that amount, even though our dinner group usually tips 25-30% since we have a bunch of industry folks.
Ultimately we left feeling that it was pretentious and overhyped.  This is a group of folks, including myself, that have eaten all around town, plus traveled to NYC, Paris, London, LA, etc.  Some of the folks in our dinner group are servers, two actually own a restaurant.

Olio is a great new addition to the city scene in an off the beaten path location that deserves a hotspot.  I love to see a business invest in an area that others might see as sketchy, which is how our great city continues to improve.  
Olio even took a step further, using an old gas station and garage to build their bar and restaurant, repurposing quality materials and classic architecture.  The result is a hip, fun, and intimate landmark.  The bar side, Olio, is the old storefront of the space.  A glass door and large panel windows add light and dimension into the otherwise smaller space, creating a bright but cozy space.  Pro bartenders plus a thoughtful cocktail, wine, and beer list create an outstanding selection.  Many drink options are from spots around the globe that are new to me, such as Lebanon.  I love to try new drinks and learn about global offerings, and the staff here knows how to sell and explain these items.  
The limited menu of small tastes is perfect with a glass of wine.  I love to just sample some cheese and cured meats, but have also ordered various dips, tartines, and salads.  They use bold and textured ingredients like high quality seafood, Mediterranean and North African spices, creamy legumes, spicy & crunchy house made nuts, and tangy goat cheese.  They are creating food that tastes and feels good to eat.  So far, I am only missing out on trying the brunch menu, and I am eager to try that.  
The prices are reasonable- certainly not inexpensive, but priced just right for the quality and service.  They do have limited parking in the front lot, which is great if you are lucky enough to nab one.  They also have valet, which is a nice touch for those not familiar with the area or maybe a little nervous about the burgeoning neighborhood.

ONE star if I could. Terrible service. The waiter ignored us and gave us attitude for no reason. We sat down and never got our menus. When we asked for them, one of the girls rolled her eyes and walked away. Never coming back again.

Now these are cupcakes Perfect balance of cake versus frosting. And the frosting isn't that cavity chilling sweetness so prevalent in other desserts. A little expensive and no whee to sit but the way they package the to-go's your precious cargo is very protected. I don't drink coffee so I have no comment on them I DO have a complaint about the hot chocolate. It may have SOME milk in it but it is not the creamy hot goodness from hot milk and chocolate mated in perfect balance. More like hot water with some milk added to cover the transgression

While I normally review a place after a few visits, I am unable to come back here after my experience, so I will review on just that.

The young girl that was serving was pleasant and welcoming and told me to sit where I wanted. Water was brought shortly after sitting and my order taken pretty quickly after that. Chicken Pho is not on the menu but she said I was able to order that. So I did. After a bit of a wait (not too horrible) my chicken Pho was brought to the table. 

After being so excited to try this place I was quickly brought back to reality. "What is that?" As I look into my bowl of Pho there were.... things that weren't chicken and clearly were not edible.

I spent about 5 minutes fishing large strings of beef fat, short fat chunks of beef fat, and little worm looking pieces of fat. (See picture). I pulled about probably a 1/4 pound of beef fat from my soup and not healthy looking beef fat (you can often tell quality meat from the bad quality and this was a lower quality.)

I sit there in disgust for about 5 minutes pondering what I was going to say to the server. 5 minutes after that I still sit. "Should I leave?" I thought. I was starving and half my lunch hour was over already so I picked through the soup trying to not think about  what I just fished out. Finally the young lady comes over and I said, I wanted you to know that I fished out that (pointing to the mountain of fat) out of my soup. She said, "oh sorry, do you want more meat?" I of course said no, secretly hoping she would charge me only for a veg Pho since mine didn't have real meat in it. 

She walks away and am still pondering walking out when the girl walks by the gentleman sitting next to me and says, looking at his fork and what was on it, "Oops, looks like you got a tendon, sorry about that."

Check please. 

While the environment seems nice, and the server was kind, I can't come back here. I paid $14.00 for a bowl of fat, noodles, and broth. I am still gagged out a week later after this experience. I always give people the benefit of the doubt but I just think I can't here. 

I will update my review if I go back and order veggie everything.

Rude, table for 1?  Called on UofA Parents Weekend to inquire about securing a dinner reservation...smarmy, rude hostess responds - sir, we have 400 reservations, no, we have nothing available. Her attitude was as though we should've known this.  

If one of my staff ever spoke to any of my current or prospective clients this way, they'd be fired. Shameful when those in hospitality lack basic service skills. 

Recommend taking your business elsewhere, I can't imagine the service is very good inside given how they represent their business to prospective customers.

Located in Santa Barbara on the busy shopping road of State street you'll find Blenders In The Grass. I was pretty excited when my sister-in-law and I ran into this place. The menu is a little similar to Jamba Juice however their ingredients and combinations are different. They also have a to-go menu to take with you which also provides the nutrition facts along side each drink and item of food. Two thumbs up for that!

We ordered the Red Mango, with chia seeds as our free supplement. The smoothie is quite large so it can easily be shared. I can't wait to come back and visit again, they have a green tea smoothie that caught my eye which I've been dying to try.

Saw all the reviews that stated amazing things about Renaud's and their pastries, so I definitely hauled myself to one of their locations when I was in Santa Barbara. 

Everybody recommended Renaud's famous almond croissant, so of course I had to try one of these. Price was a bit expensive, but how can you put a price on deliciousness right? Especially if you're trying it for the first time. Apparently you can ask the workers to heat it up for you so you can eat it warm, which I did not know! Even so, I still found the almond croissant to be everything I had hoped for. The top of the croissant was smothered in almonds. The texture of the croissant skin was crispy and flaky, while the inside of the croissant was soft and chewy. Amazing right? And I did not expect the almond crumbles inside of the croissant - that made it 100 times better! 

I wasn't planning to buy anything besides the almond croissant, but I was taken by the apple tart that was calling my name. There were two different flavors, but I ended up going for apple. And so glad I did! Probably the most amazing apple tart I've ever had in my life. It wasn't warm, but it was still super flaky - taste was amazing. Not too sweet, but once you hit the center of the tart, you get the ooey sweetness and goodness of the apple filling. I personally liked this better than the almond croissant, but my parents liked the almond more. 100% worth the money. 

We ended up buying a hazelnut or chocolate macaron. Price was less than $2 I believe. Nothing special about it. The texture was good - slightly crispy on the outside and chewy on the inside, but nothing too overwhelming. The chocolate taste was solid and strong. They didn't have flavors like salted caramel or whatnot, so I probably won't get macarons again if I ever return to Renaud's. 

Credit cards are accepted and they have about 3 locations in Santa Barbara - all within a few miles (or minutes) of one another. Parking was easy to find here. Pretty much grab and go. They also offer sandwiches and lunch items, but I'd stick to the pastries.

tl;dr - I love macarons, but I'm finding them harder and harder to satisfy when there are so many wonderful things in life like Renaud's almond croissant or apple tart. I definitely want to return and try their Exotic cake. They have a location in Long Beach, so maybe I'll make a stop there one day! So glad I was able to try this place out when I was in Santa Barbara! Best decision everrr.

When we first moved to Tampa we temporarily resided at the Homewood Suites near International Plaza and Bay Street. How could we have missed all of the dining experiences offered at the Plaza? So glad that the hubby and I drove down to support our friend/Yelper Anna M. judge a pumpkin carving contest here otherwise we would have never known about The Pub Tampa Bay. 

We were seated at the table with some other amazing Yelpers and immediately greeted by one of the nicest servers ever -- be sure to ask for Swade. My diet coke was never empty -- thanks for the stellar and attentive service. It really shows when a person loves their job and makes your dining experience one of a kind. My husband and I tried the beer battered onion rings and mushrooms served with spicy dill & creamy horseradish. Pretty spectacular pub food. Next time we want to try the Shepherd's Pie. Check out their menu of mouth watering pub fare food: http://www.experiencethepub.com/tampa-bay/menu/food

The Pub is known for the first  "Pour Your on Beer Wall" in Tampa-- diners can sample beers from Ireland, Scotland, England, other parts of Europe and the USA. They also offer wines and cocktails. In my opinion best perk of all -- if you are active duty military ask for your 25% discount -- thanks for supporting our military members. Highly recommend this one at International Plaza! We will be back :)

As my "check in" stated -- I could hear the angels singing as I took my first bite. Lost all ability to function several times during my meal. As a Southerner, a lot of my staple meals growing up were BBQ. I had a few flashback moments during my dining experience where I could close my eyes and imagine sitting at my grandmother's dinner table. 4 Rivers tasted that good to me. After hearing about this place repeatedly and viewing all the reviews and photos -- I had to see and taste this for myself. 

Met my Yelp buddy Steve E. here recently. He had been a few times since the grand opening therefore I was lucky to have him explain everything to me (Thanks again Steve). Upon entering this place -- it is massive (thank goodness the line was not out the door. There was a line but it moved very quickly). To the right is the humongous kitchen area where all the prepping, smoking and cooking takes place and to the left is the dessert kitchen. The seating area is very similar to communal dining (rows of tables adorn the center of the room. Grab a seat and sit next to a stranger). The menu is easy to read with lots of meats and sides offered. I chose the pulled pork sandwich with baked beans and fried okra. Also grabbed a bottle of Sprecher Cream Soda (they had various bottles of soda on ice). Order your meal at the counter -- pay -- take your order to the table. 

As we made our way to the dining area there was conversation from some of the servers that the founder of 4 Rivers (John Rivers) was visiting Tampa today. Mr. Rivers was making his rounds through the restaurant helping customers and answering questions. He stopped at our table to ask about our meals and was kind enough to tell us how the 4 Rivers concept began. In 2004, he was the President of a billion dollar healthcare company -- 4 Rivers began as a barbecue ministry to help a local family pay the huge amount of medical bills for their daughter's battle with cancer. Today the Jacksonville native and FSU grad now has 7 locations throughout the state of Florida. It was quite humbling to meet John Rivers -- he was very gracious with his time and his story touched me -- he is driven by faith and his family. 

The pulled pork was the BEST I have ever eaten and the piece of cornbread I tasted actually brought a tear to my eye (it tasted just like my grandmother's recipe). All the sides are made from scratch and were absolutely delicious! The fried okra was fresh and not greasy at all. As we continued to devour our food we saw that the Community Manager of Tampa (Brett N.) and the Official Yelp Photographer of Tampa (Gerardo) had decided to eat at 4 Rivers too. I could not help but notice that Brett had ordered something that looked as if it had fallen off the platter of The Flintstones -- the humongous Brontosaurus Beef Rib! (Huge would be an understatement). One of the servers brought Brett a sample of some of the different meats that they serve -- I had to try the Burnt - Ends. It was like nothing I have ever tasted -- the meat tasted like it is caramelized. OMG!  But the goodness did not stop there -- Chris W. were your ears burning?? We made our way over to the sweet shop. I began hearing angels singing again. All their desserts are made on site -- fresh daily. I got the Red Velvet cupcake. It was scrumptious. The general manager (Justin) offered the guys a tour of the back area. What a fascinating experience!

To ask if I will be back again is quite obvious. Maybe I will not hear angels singing next time but one thing is for sure -- this was the best BBQ I have ever eaten -- felt like I visited my grandmother today.

The husband and I met some friends here for breakfast recently.  Anytime we are in Zephryhills early in the morning there seems to be a line out the door -- so we decided to give this place a try and find out why all the locals flock to Sunrise. Located on the corner of Gall Boulevard and Geiger Road. There is a private lot but parking spots can be sparse. We managed to finally get a sweet spot in front.

Upon arrival we were told there would be about a 15 minute wait (not bad for a Sunday morning around 9:00). There was no room to wait inside but there are some benches out front to wait on your number to be called (no shortage of people watching entertainment that is for sure). 

When the hostess called us in less than 15 minutes we walked in finding a super busy dining room with music from the 60s booming overhead -- you cannot miss the abundant amount of movie posters and memorabilia that adorn the walls (an All American themed eatery). Stained glass chandeliers hang over the booths lining the outskirts of the dining room and yes each table has a checkered cloth.  Nothing special its a diner but the food was pretty darn tasty.

My husband decided on the Huge Sunrise Breakfast -- 3 eggs, 2 sausage links, 2 bacon strips, a slice of ham, home fries, and a biscuit with sausage gravy (I called it the Big Butt Special -- that is a lot of food)! Our friends ordered pancakes with fresh fruit and I opted for the biscuits and sausage gravy. Pretty good and authentic. The biscuits are homemade and the sausage gravy was fresh. The manager Manny was very engaging with each and every person that entered. He made sure that our food and service met our expectations. Shout out to Shana for the superb service -- our coffee and water was never empty. 

Since they serve breakfast all day - I was curious about their lunch menu. Our waitress explained that they serve home-style meals (meatloaf, catfish, burgers, Greek salads, burgers and sandwiches) that are made fresh daily. We will definitely venture back to check out their lunch items. All in all a good experience.

Open everyday from 7 am to 6 pm and the best perk  -- they have call ahead seating. Shhh! Don't tell anyone :)

Las Palmas Cafe is a hidden Cuban gem located in a New Tampa strip mall. The parking lot is big so there should never be a problem finding a space. 

Upon entering -- we were greeted by a friendly lady who told us to have a sit anywhere. She promptly brought us menus and asked if this was our first visit. We explained this was our first visit and she offered suggestions on what we should try and brought us a sample of the roasted pork Cuban style and a basket of warm Cuban bread. The pork was delicious -- marinated in sour orange, garlic and herbs -- it was so tender we cut it with a fork. My husband opted for the Full Cuban Sandwich (they also offer a half). Yummy pressed ham, shredded pork, Swiss cheese, mustard and pickles. It was good. My daughter chose the Shrimp in garlic sauce. The shrimp was cooked in garlic, wine and lemon juice. This meal comes with two sides of your choice: yellow or white rice, cup of soup (black, white, chickpea or chicken tortilla), fried sweet plantains "Maduros", fried green plantains "Tostones", boiled yuca, green beans, french fries, yuca fried sticks or salad. My daughter chose the yellow rice and fried sweet plantains. The plantains were so good. I was craving black beans so ordered a bowl of the black beans and yellow rice. They threw some fresh cut onions on top -- I had never tried this before and it gave the beans a much better bite. 

Las Palmas offers a variety of appetizers, soups/salads, entrees, sandwiches and daily lunch specials served Monday through Friday from 11 am to 3 pm. Check out their array of desserts. I wanted to try the flan with grated coconut but was way too full. As far as beverages they have your usual fountain sodas but also have a homemade  award winning sangria that is available by the glass or carafe -- wine, beer, and even a Cuban espresso. Check out their website www.laspalmascafe.net for more information -- they also do catering for parties and special events. 

There are too many items we want to try! Will be going back again soon this place is muy bien!

Small cupcake boutique with only a couple parking spots. There's only one table inside and a few window bar seats. My friend and I stopped in after lunch for a quite shareable dessert---a cupcake! 

There was a good assortment of cupcakes but they seemed to ha e been made in the morning and sitting out. The white chocolate cupcake tasted good with a generous scoop of soft cream cheese icing. 

The employees were fast and friendly. 

I recommend it for at least one visit. Fun neighborhood peppered with Vanderbilt students.

Right when you walk in on the left is the stage where a local band was playing country music songs and taking requests from the audience. The bar is just past the stage, and on the right side a slew of onlookers. The layout is weird. You're immediately in the way as you walk in.

Upstairs, they were playing today's hit music, including rap, hip-hop, and top 40, which was strange. Being a minority myself, it felt nice to see diversity on the top floor, but it felt a bit self-segregated based on music interests. I'm glad the bar at least caters to all music types. It is music city after all!

Huge candy store with free samples of freshly made pralines---the best I've ever tasted. There are all kinds of sweets and desserts and chocolate-covered pretzels and even tins to fill with as much candy and taffy you can for one flat price. 

There's even an active train set running across the ceiling. In a highly touristy areas so the prices are higher than normal, but conveniently situated and crowded with tourists.

I bought $6 worth of taffy! Delish.

This is a spacious restaurant/bar on the second, third, and fourth floors of large building on the main drag on Broadway. There's a huge stage for local performers, plenty of bars to get drinks from, and a fun crowd of people. It wasn't too crowded last night when we visited to get some live music on our last night in Nashville. 

The rooftop is huge, equivalent to two buildings' width. There are cozy seats and fire pits and Spring Breakers spilling drinks and gyrating and dancing poorly but enthusiastically to rap, rock, and pop music hits.

No country music on the rooftop!

At the rooftop bar, I ordered a rum and pineapple and it cost $10. The female bartender's expression was deadpan, and she moved mechanically, likely the result of a long night of the second day of spring break. Zero personality but efficient.

We did not spot Jason Aldean, unfortunately.

What can I say that hasn't already been said? This is a wonderful market with so many independent retailers and shops that is any small-business-shopper's dream. There are vendors who sell sandwiches and pastries, meats and seafood, jewelry and watches, fine chocolate and exquisite cordials, fresh donuts and baked goods, and lots, lots more!

It was very busy when we visited, on a Tuesday morning, so I don't even want to imagine what it is like during the weekends! We mostly window-shopped and ultimately bought a maple donut for about a buck and which tasted phenomenal. I really love places like these that could be overpriced but choose not to.

Absolutely a must-visit place when visiting Philadelphia!

I love this store!  The candy here really is a work of art and has been featured in a couple of the Hunger Games movies. Not only are the individual candies unique works of art but the flavors are unique as well. Some of their 36 flavors include  Port & Plum, Mexican Mango, Bananas Fisher, Earl Grey, Mojito and Lavender. They also sell macaroons, tarts and gelato. Very friendly and helpful staff. They now offer high tea on the weekends and I really look forward to returning to go to that. A bit on the pricey side but well worth it.

These are the best bagels that I've eaten in Florida. They're a very small place with no room to eat inside but trust me, their bagels are so good that you don't mind taking them to go. They were still warm when I picked them up this morning and they have a perfect crunch on the outside and are pillowy soft on the inside. They've been open about 30 years which is a true testament as to how good they are especially since there's an Einstein Bagels right across the street from them. Some people might think they're a little on the pricey side but you're paying for delicious quality bagels, not bagels that are loaded with sugar. Authentic NY bagels here!

I've been here a few times to try some of there breakfast items and cheesesteaks. They make some bangin Korean infused cheesesteaks. The breakfast items are above average. However the menu is quite expensive and not something I can afford every other day. The owner is usually around in the shop with his wife. Very polite and courteous people. If the menu were a bit cheaper I'd like to think this place would become a regular favorite of mine

Casino just now has asked buses to come back. Our Sr group use to come here once a month. The Casino stopped letting our group come but guess things have gotten hard because or bus group has been invited back. Not many if any winners but it's nice to know the Srs have a place to go. Accidently posted under Pool & Cafe (moving review sorry for any inconvenience)

Yes...it's known as a "tourist trap," but...relaxing in the patio/courtyard with eats & drinks, enjoying the beautiful signature flaming copper fountain, & laughing & meeting new friends at "Pat O'Brien's" was a BLAST!!!

We loved both the jambalaya & the gumbo.  The red beans & rice with chargrilled andouille sausage were so flavorful & delicious that I cried tears of joy.  And...the star of the show:  The Alligator Bites.  Backstory:  Ever since "Cajun Bistro" in West Hollywood closed its doors (years ago), I've been suffering from "ABW" ("Alligator Bites Withdrawl").  Since it's so difficult to find decent Alligator Bites in SoCal, I couldn't wait to grab some upon landing in New Orleans, & the Bites at "Pat O'Brien's" were fantastic.  Light & crispy batter on the outside, hot & juicy on the inside, perfectly seasoned, & yes.....they DO taste like chicken!   ;)

Great customer service, & a fun atmosphere for just relaxing or celebrating practically anything.  Celebrate, enjoy life, & have a fun night at "Pat O'Brien's"!

Cappy's serves up some tasty pizza, but there are too many glaring negatives;

1.) When my party of 6 arrived around dinner time on a Friday evening, we had to wait about 30 minutes for a table. (Refer to point #3.)

2.) There were quirky elements of the restaurant (i.e. perimeter train, handmade menus, etc.), which were all pretty cool. However, it was impossible to enjoy them with the noise level in the restaurant--way too many rowdy kids!! I had to converse using a nearly-yelling voice for most of our time in the restaurant.

3.) It took at least 10 minutes for a server to drop by our table once FINALLY being seated. Another 30-45 minutes went by before we got our pizzas. Aggregate wait time from arriving to eating: well over an hour.

4.) Cash only?! Are we living in 1995? I had to get a buddy to spot me the cash. Sure there's an ATM in the store, but seriously? Even the cheapest Mexican restaurants take cards.

The pizza itself was pretty good--I'd even say above-average. I think the restaurant needs to improve efficiency and make efforts to quiet noisy children. If you have extra time AND an extra set of earplugs, you'll enjoy the food here.

Every so often, I come across a place that truly strikes a chord with me.  Last night, this special place was Trattoria Pasquale. This quaint little place is a wonderful addition to South Tampa and in my opinion, the best Italian food in town! Italian cuisine is my favorite and I have eaten in hundreds of Italian restaurants across the country and in Italy. There are a few places that have last a lasting impression on me, one is in Rome, one is in San Francisco and last night it was Pasquale's! 

I met my friend for dinner and we were warmly greeted by the owner, Luigi. He went over the specials and chatted with us about the menu.  We started off with prosciutto e melone which was perfect on a warm summer evening. The sweetness of the cantaloupe with the saltiness of the prosciutto was divine. My friend and I both ordered off the specials menu for our dinner. I had house made pappardelle al cinghiale with fresh mushrooms and peas.  It was perfection on a plate. I had been craving an authentic pasta dish and this exceeded my expectations.   My friend ordered "Branzino alla Davide" (sea bass) and it was fabulous. We sipped on a wine I brought since they do not serve beer or wine but you can bring your own and there is no corkage fee. We finished off our meal on a sweet note with an order of cannoli.

I can't wait to go back to Trattoria Pasquale!  This is such a cute place and the food is beyond delicious. Be sure to make a reservation as it fills up quick. :)

Finney's crafthouse has an outstanding location; it's near the Hotel Californian and an easy walk from the train station; it's also just a block from the pier.  It's well situated for people watching;  you can simultaneously enjoy decent food and good drinks, with a ring-side view.  The bar area is large and it's got lots of TV's if you want to watch sports with a brew or four ;-) 

Long story short - the drinks are strong and the food is pretty good, but the service can be spotty, and they've got way too many functions that are single-threaded through the host/hostess stand.

Short story somewhat longer - let's talk about the bad stuff first:

1) I've been here twice now, and both times various service malfunctions caused cocktails and food courses to vanish and/or be delayed for unacceptably long periods.  Management was gracious about making amends, but having these kind of mishaps on two consecutive visits isn't goodness.

2) The first time I came here I was meeting a friend who came in on Amtrak, and we decided to walk over and catch up over drinks and appetizers.  There were lots of open tables both inside and out, but it still took more than 30 minutes for us to be seated.  Why?  They're single-treading everything through the host stand, so when someone comes to pick up or place a take-out order, the host/hostess is tied up and unavailable for seating tables.  It actually took us 15 minutes just to get our names on the list of people waiting!  

Now, on to the good!

1) When they are actually delivered in a timely fashion, all the cocktails I've tried here have been both good and VERY strong - there are Missouri Mules that don't kick half as hard ;-)

2) When you're interested in something small and tasty to wash down with your cocktail, the Bacon Cheese Tater Tots are an outstanding choice!  The batter is tasty, they're fried perfectly and completely delicious!  I suggest you upsize your order to a large - you'll be glad you did!

3) They've got several different burgers here, and all the ones I've tried thus far have been very good.  They're all accompanied with a side of very respectable truffle fries.  My favorite burger thus far is their Bison Burger.  It's tasty, lean, and juicy, with a strong pleasant flavor that's not at all gamy.

To sum it all up, this is a great place to hang out with new and old friends (especially if you're not in a hurry).  It's perfect for locals and tourist alike; the more you drink, the happier you'll be ;-)

I've been to Islands a couple of times in the past few months, and I'm growing quite fond of it.  It's a nice place to head for when you want to watch a game while grabbing a bite and a brew.  To date, my friends and I have never had trouble finding seating when we come here :-)

The interior makes you feel like you're on an tropical island. The venue is filled with surfboards, hibiscus decor, and plants. Prepare to embrace a tropical vibe!

Last time we came, our friendly waitress brought me three draft tastes so I could pick the right brew to match my mood.  With that done, I was craving a burger so I consulted our very helpful waitress again, and I decided to take her suggestion and go with the Maui Burger.  That comes with onion, lettuce, tomato, Swiss, mayo, and guacamole; I got it on a wheat bun and it came with a side of fries.

Before I was ready for my second beer, the burger arrived and I dug in - it was very good!  The Swiss was nicely melted, the guacamole was fresh, and the beef patty was cooked medium rare, exactly as I had asked.  It was flavorful, juicy, and nicely seasoned.  With a second brew to keep it company, I was one very happy camper!

Islands is a place that I've been enjoying and have no problem recommending, especially if you want to eat out somewhere while watching a game.

I'll be back!

It's actually really too bad that I will never go back to the Stone House Cafe.  I went there for Mother's Day and was treated horribly by the owner's daughter.  It wasn't until I started hearing other people say the same thing that I stopped feeling guilty about it.  I thought I should give it another chance, but now I know for sure I will not.

I waited in line to return a few items and it was a long line. If I would have know that the wait times have become longer at Walmart I would have never came in to purchase these items. Lines have definitely become worst. I use to like going to Walmart because it was fast an convenient. That is not so much the case anymore. There seem to be a lot of agitated people in line. It just seems like Walmart has really gone down hill. I am really disappointed in their quality and their service. It seems like the staff members aren't happy and moral seems down. I really don't like giving bad reviews but Walmart really needs to fix this problem. I really hope they turn it around. 

Also I bought a bike here once and rode it around the same day and that day I broke the pedals. I just bought this thing and took it back to Walmart return area and they were like wow. They were like "You brought that today and broke it the same day". I told them "yes".  Even the staff were super surprised. Needless to say quality is not good. I would highly recommend not to buy anything that could put you in danger. I was riding down hill when this happened and I could have seriously been injured if I didn't stop the bike in time. 

Plenty of parking but there is alway lots of carts just left behind in the parking lot. They need to get those guy on cart clean up to do their job or pay them more. But Walmart has gone down hill. I probably won't go to Walmart unless it is super necessary. Thank for reading my review.

Burger Me! Oh yes please! I will have to say my experience was excellent at this establishment. They were not to busy when we went in and the burger I got was outstanding. I got the BBQ Bison Burger with a side of garlic fries. Man this burger did not disappoint! Also the garlic fries held their own. Great fries you can order these by themselves and they are great. It was $12.50 for the BBQ Bison Burger. I think it was just a bit on the pricey side for the burger. But it was a good burger. 

The atmosphere was great and the staff was friendly. They were accommodating to our needs and one of our people in our party got their order wrong but they charged the difference back to the Visa card. Which was nice of them to do. The restaurant had okay amount of seating and it was a bit on the noisy side but not bad all in all. I will definitely come back again for more. The parking lot has plenty of room for parking although we weren't there during peak hours so I don't know how packed this places gets. But it seemed like the staff knew how to handle the rush hours. 

Other items we ordered where a regular cheese burger, hotdog, Big Dippa, aside of garlic fries which everyone should try and they all looked pretty good. Still thinking about that burger and garlic fries mmmmmm good haha. Anyways, I would recommend coming here on an empty stomach because you will be in for a treat! Thank for reading my review.

Burger Me yes please.

Every time we get done snowboarding from Mt.Rose, Burger Me is usually our go to for a bite to eat. I dont know if it is the fact that I just spent over a million calories having fun snowboarding or just plain hungry when we come here but it is a good burger. I feel like this places hits the spot. I will say certain days the food does taste a lot better than others. I am not sure as to the fact of me being hungry or a different chef cooking but the food is good.

This location is convenient and easy to get in and out of. Plenty of parking event with the theater right next to it and being in a mall complex. It is relatively a good place to grab a bite. The staff is okay and accommodating. I do feel like the have had a staff turn over but there was one certain individual who was very perceptive and found out I was a veteran here and she gave me a discount. She was very good and very nice. She doesnt work there anymore. We haven't seen here in over 3 years but anyways I digress. My experience here was good and will definitely return. Thanks for reading my review.

Walden's Coffeehouse is a nice and comfy spot.

I came in with a buddy of mine and we
both went for a small cup of coffee. The 8 ounce cup to be specific. The reason why I am being specific is that the cashier said they didn't have anymore of that size and she said I'll just charge us for the next size up. But only charge us for one cup 2 cups for the price of one. Outstanding! But my buddy wanted to pay for me because, well let's just say he owed me one haha. So, I said to the cashier charge him twice or three times shoot I'm not paying haha. But she was nice enough to give up that 2 for 1 deal. 

There was plenty for seating if you want to come here to do homework, business meeting, people watching if you want to be creepy like me haha. But not a bad place. I was surprised to see a Walden's Coffeehouse here. It is a nice place to sit and hang out with friends too. Meet up with your friends here and hangout. I like it cause there is not a lot of people here. At least when I stopped by. This was the first time I came here and I will be returning. There is plenty of parking and I don't think it gets to be a big issue. I have never had any really parking issues here. Because every time I have gone to Reno Engraving I have never had trouble finding parking. I have been to Reno Engraving a bunch of times and this why I know there usually isn't a problem with parking. 

My experience here has been good and I will be back. Thank you for reading my review.

Grimaldi's Pizzeria is outstanding!

These guys just seem to be on point every time I come here. They definitely have a high standard and great customer service. Why do I say that? Well, I will explain. This really was apparent when they took my credit card for the check. The waitress was very observant and saw that I had a USAA credit card. Most people with a USAA card are Veterans, Active Duty, or dependents of Veterans/active duty. When the waitress told me she was going to give me a discount because of that I was wonderfully surprised by that. I can't say enough about how great that customer service is. I don't usually like to ask for Veteran discount because I feel like it's weird for asking. But I am really appreciative that they did give me that discount. Thanks again to the staff for being awesome. 

Plenty of parking here and the dining area was clean. The bathrooms are clean as well. We were seated and greeted at the door in a punctual manner. The water and food came in at the appropriate time. Also, like I explained at the beginning they went the extra mile to get me a discount. Now remember I didn't ask for the discount. The waitress look at my credit card and asked me if I was a veteran. Just awesome service! I really like these guy here and will definitely come back. My experience here was exceptional. Thank you for reading my review.

Hinoki Sushi is a good place for your sushi needs!

Well I tried a few items and here are the main rolls that I like here. I like their Mountain, Mermaid and Caterpillar Rolls. With that said the reason why I like them is because their flavors. They tasted good. I also like the scallops that came with the Mermaid Roll. If your not into fried rolls I would go for the Nigiri. The salmon and seared tuna are my favorite. On the Nigiri I would make sure to put a little bit of lemon and a touch of soy sauce. It makes it taste delicious. Man my mouth is watering just writing about it haha. I love it. 

Service and staff was good. They are friendly and cater to your needs. We sat on a regular table and not at the bar. They are pretty fast about getting your order and getting the order to the sushi chefs. We were there about 10-15 minutes and we had our waters, soy sauce plates, chop sticks and 2 of the rolls we ordered at our table. So pretty fast service. With that being said I do feel like a few of their rolls are lagging. But the rolls I mentioned are good. If there was any advice for this place it is keep the menu simple and maximize the ingredients for each of the rolls. I think that having quality in a few rolls is better having a variety of rolls and lag the flavor profile/quality in the sushi. But they are pretty good. I just wished there was a sushi place in Reno that would only service 5-10 rolls and make those rolls with high quality ingredients. Granted their menu is already pretty simple but it's just my 2 cents haha. I think that would make for an amazing sushi place. I do like that Hinoki Sushi has all you can eat and the portions are correct. I am glad that they don't over fill the sushi with rice. I really appreciate that because their is nothing worst than having a bad fish to rice ratio. My experience here was good and I will be back. Actually, I was there 2 days in a row. Is that too much haha, maybe. Thank you for reading my review.

I will have to say yes to Raising Cane's Chicken Fingers!

I am definitely a fan. Simple food and fairly quick at serving your food. This fast food chain is a good place to grab a quick bit to eat. The price is fair and the quality is good. The chicken is moist and delicious. Just the right amount of salt on the chicken. They keep the combo items/selection to a minimum which makes for easy selection. They have a good selection of drinks including your basic coke, sprite, etc. but the also have sweeten tea and unsweetened tea. I like that!

The staff are pretty sharp and friendly. Very accommodating and let me explain why. One time I didn't ask for the veteran discount but one of the staff member saw my tattoo and ask if I was a veteran. She said "oh we can give you a veteran discount". I was pleasantly surprised and very thankful for her acknowledgment. I really appreciate it when people take the time to do thank. It is definitely a huge plus for these guys and I just wanted note that. 

There is plenty of parking. I will say it doesn't get super busy here because of Whole Foods being next to it. The parking lot can get jammed up. If Whole Foods get lots of traffic then it can get hairy with parking. With that said their drive thru can be crazy. It is kind of in a weird spot where cars are waiting and fighting to get a spot. I don't like their drive thru because it does get weird and people get angry because people fight for that spot at the drive thru. Not good! But other than that my experience here have been good. Thank you for reading my review.

Dorinda's Chocolate is delicious and made of good quality ice cream.

It's nice to have a place like this to go on a hot summer day or a nice spring day! Also, right next to the Truckee River so you can go for a walk as you eat your ice cream or after to work off some of those calories. The quality of the ice cream is good. It taste great and you can really tell. I am all about supporting local business too so when ever I'm down this way I love coming here for a bite. If you are ever in the area I recommend stopping by just to even check it out. 

SIDE NOTE: Hub Coffee Roaster is right next door if your a coffee drinker. They pump out good coffee haha. I am a fan!

Anyways back to the great ice cream. Yes, good ice cream, plenty of flavors to pick from. They also have ice cream sandwiches. The staff is friendly and accommodating. So, a few things to note about this place parking can get a bit hectic because the parking lot is a bit small. So, you might have to park on the street and walk over but that's not a bad thing. It gets pretty busy during the summer time here so just be aware of that. Just make sure you parking in a designated area because I knew one person who did get towed just FYI. Don't be that person who gets towed. For the most part most of the street parking is okay to park in. 

Getting a table here can also be a bit crazy durning the rush hour because they share the tables between Dorinda's and Hub Coffee Roaster. So, that's double the amount of customers. Really during the summer time is when it can get a bit crazy. You can always grab a seat on the grass or walk over by the river and grab a bench. Unless you like people watching and prime real-estate is right in front of the entrance to both Dorinda's and Hub Coffee Roaster. But it's your choice hehe. I will definitely be back for more. Thanks for reading my review.

Rounds Bakery is cool.

I like this place. Before the COVID19 situation I had the chance to visit this place. So here are my thoughts about this place. They served up some good stuff. Lots of tasty treats and good quality items. Let's start with the donuts. The donuts are delicious and when it is fresh it is really good. I am definitely a fan and will keep coming back. These guys are definitely busy and I see their delivery van's come in and out. 

The staff is great. They are friendly and accommodating. Their coffee is good and they also sell sandwiches. I'm sure I'm missing other items they sell but I will keep coming back to see what else they sell and try them out. 

There is plenty of parking and they share it with other businesses but I have never had problems finding a parking spot here. The facility is kept very clean and has an atmosphere is casual. It is pretty calming and relaxing is a good way to explain the atmosphere here. It's a good place to grab a cup of coffee in the morning before you start your day. I would recommend checking this place out. Thanks for reading.

What can I say I love Full Belly Deli! I love their sandwiches here!

We often come here for lunch. It is in a pretty convenient location and not to bad when it comes to the wait time. Now granted it does getting busy for lunch. Yes, the dreaded lunch hour hustle and bustle. It sucks but if you wait just a bit extra it's okay because the wait it worth it and honestly it's not that bad of a wait. The staff is pretty awesome at getting the sandwiches done pretty quickly. I think they know the routine. Lunch time you got to turn it up because it gets busy!

The staff is helpful and the get it done. Also if you call ahead to get your sandwich for pickup it will be just a manner of paying and picking it up. This is definitely a good thing to do for the lunch hour rush. So, plan accordingly because they can get busy and you don't want to be waiting in line to get your food for lunch when you only have a 30 minute lunch. Also, you will have to wait for the sandwich to be made so that might take more time. Just something to be aware of. 

The parking lot is a bit small but I have never been here when the whole parking lot is packed. But it does get pretty full during lunch time. In a case where it is to packed to park I'm not actually sure where you would park, hmmm? Anyways, I am guessing most people will just drive off haha. It's what I would do or maybe park in the street. Thanks for reading my review.

MOD Pizza is delicious.

I am a fan for sure. This is my go to place for pizza. We ordered a maddy, mad dog and cheesy garlic bread. Man that was a good combo haha. 

Usually we would have left overs when we order out at any pizza joint but this time we had no left overs. I was happy and sad at the same time. I was happy because I was fat and happy haha. Sad because we had no left overs haha. So we can just grab more pizza next time. 

This was out first time going to MOD Pizza and man was it a good call. The staff was friendly and accommodating. The price was good and the quality of the food was great. I will definitely be back for more and I would definitely like to try other flavors. Any suggestions? 

This is a convenient location to get to and easy parking. I ordered over the phone for a pickup. I dont think they are use to that. I'm not sure but the order came out fine when I came to pick it up. I just think the guy on the phone was new because he asked me after I put the order in if I wanted it to for here or to go. I was a bit confused haha. But it was funny. I like this place. Anyways I will definitely be back for more. Thanks for reading my review.

Not a bad establishment. They have a great selection of items to choose from. I was actually a bit over whelmed by the options they had. But I locked my sights on one thing which was the garlic chicken. It was not bad and the quality of the food was good. I would go back again for more. There wasn't that many people in the establishment but that was probably because we where there around 2pm. Not really during rush hour. 

This place is located right on Virginia street. So parking is not very good. You will have to park in the back which can be a bit of a trek and for you ladies, well I would bring a friend with you. The staff is friendly and got to our order right away. They were actually just watching us and when we stopped looking at our menus they were quick to take our order. That is service and a great job on staff. Waiting for the food did not take long at all. Like I was saying we were not there during peak hours. 

This place gets plenty of foot traffic from Virginia Street and can become really busy. Especially, if there is an event going on. I would keep that in mind if you decide to go here during those times. Your waiting time and experience might be different. Thank for reading my review.

Doughboys Donuts is outstanding!

These guys are just the best. I love sweets it is my guilty pleasure. This is one of those places where I will spare the calories and fat because man it's good. If I could eat 20 donuts in one meal and not have to suffer the consequences I would. Did I mention these are tasty donuts? Well, they are! Oooh just thinking about them makes my mouth water. 

I know you guys have probably hear it all from other reviews but just the quality of the donuts, they care they put to baking them, the store cleanliness, the staff being awesome, etc. They are just a great place and I am glad they are around. I highly recommend coming here for a donut or two or 3 or 5000 of them haha jk. I will say having milk at the donut shop, good call. Also, of you are ever having one of those party weekends this place opens at 5am every day. I will say that again they are open EVERYDAY FROM 5AM TO 9PM and on Fridays and Saturday they are open from 5am to 10pm. That is freaken awesome. So, if you have a late night sweet tooth or an early morning sweet tooth they are there for you. I love it!

They staff is awesome by the way. They are really patient with you and for us that's a plus because we have kids. They can be indecisive. But they are accommodating to our needs. Again great staff and the quality of their donuts are awesome. I can't think of any place that can rival them at the moment but if you know of any I should try please let me know because I would love to try it. Thanks for reading my review.

Ruby River Steakhouse is a great place to EAT MEAT!

Yeah, I am a fan on this place. I have been here a few times and I could have sworn I have done a review of this place before. All the times I have been here my experience has been good. Needless to say I am fat and happy right now hehe. 

Before we got there we called ahead to see if we could get a reservation but they don't do reservations. If you do decide to call you can save your spot in line for waiting on a table. So instead of going there and waiting for a table there they will save you a spot in line for a table if you call ahead. So we waited like 2-5 minutes tops for a table. When we were at the table our waitress was there in 5 minutes or so to get us drinks and bread. That is outstanding. Our waitress was great she was very accommodating and attentive to our needs. I even asked her where they got the calamari and the meat for the steaks. She said she would go ask and she gave me an honest answer. The calamari comes from China frozen but they taste pretty good. The steaks come from a farm in the Midwest. Let's just say she was on point. 

The food was good. I got rib-eye steak medium and it was delicious. It was just the way I liked it. You get 2 side dishes to go with your steak. They also have other items on the menu like seafood, pasta, burgers and more. The food has good flavoring not to much salt and it was seasoned correctly. Also when you ask for a medium done steak you get a medium done steak.

The interior is decorated with a western cowboy theme. Which sets you in the mood for eating steak or just meat in general haha. The parking can be a bit crazy here because they do get quite a bit of return customs and locals here. People really dig this place so parking could be an issue if there are lots of people here. We were there on a Friday night and it was pretty busy. I'm sure I'm missing a few things but my experience here was good and we will definitely be coming back again. I would recommend this place they are pretty good.  Thanks for reading my review.

This is a perfect brunch spot. Mamossa bar and Bloody Mary bar from 12Pm-4PM. I had the Hot Brown sandwich for brunch and it was delicious. I'm not a huge sandwich person, but this one is the best I've ever had. Everyone should come here.

When it comes to Chinese buffets all are not created equal! Dragon House is one of the better ones. The food is always fresh and tasty and the service is pretty good as well. If you're like me, you walk into a Chinese buffet expecting some of the usual suspects when it comes to the food, this place delivers that but also some extra's that you don't see everywhere else. For example, fried coconut milk and lettuce wraps. Listen, it's a Chinese buffet, you're not going to leave this place with your head hung high, you're going to leave in pure Chinese buffet shame....BUT you will be happy! If you are in the area and needing a buffet fix definitely check this place out!
Tim and Dave are the best! Not only was the service amazing, but the drinks and food were stellar. Thanks boys! Love the wives and girlfriend!

I'm all about supporting the economy by supporting locally-owned, family run businesses! And this is what you get at Konan BBQ. 

So we picked up ribs for a work function. I got bread pudding and pineapple tea for my personal edification and consumption as I was told  it was mandatory to try these two things. Now I'm not the type to take orders but  sometimes I can be persuaded to humbly take direction. ; )

The pineapple sweet tea was sweet but not overly so.  I was trying to figure out what all was in it. I thought that I tasted the tartness off lemon but it may have been just a combination of the sweety tartness of the pineapple. It was a nice combination with the tea. It was delicious! 

The ribs were awesome! They have a mustard based barbecue sauce that I haven't had before but it was really delicious! The ribs were cooked just right with that charcoaled infused, crispy goodness on the outside and the tender,  juicy, succulent rib meat on the inside. Mmmm mmmmm good!

I saved the bread pudding for later and when I took my first bite, I just couldn't believe it. It was thick in all the right places. Just like any born and bred Southern woman! ; )  It had that lightly sweety, sugary glaze over the top. It was so good. It reminded me of my grandma!

There was plenty of indoor seating including picnic benches and tables with chairs. The order was called in so we didn't wait long .  The parking lot had ample parking but if there's a high influx of people, I can imagine that parking could be an issue. 

The staff was friendly and interactive. From what I understand, Konan is a  community cornerstone. They feed people in need who are hungry and are overall kind and generous people. It's great to support a business and a family like this. 

I can't wait to come again!

Tampa Joe's has catered several of our office events and each time, their food has been a big hit! 

The lasagna has a waterfall of cheese and is very meaty! The shrimp scampi is moist and delicious with the right amount of shrimp. My coworker really enjoys the spaghetti and meatballs. She couldn't stop raving about it! And, the Bow Tie pasta with chicken is pretty tasty as well. The cookies are sooo yummy, too. I've had Snickerdoodle, chocolate chip, and my favorite oatmeal and raisin! Mmmmm... man, this review is making me hungry!

Columbia Cafe is located inside the Tampa History Center. I had the Cafe Con Leche as I waited for my dining companions. It was pretty good. Carolyn,  my server at the bar, was really sweet and accommodating. Because the cafe is in the history center, they can't do a lot of the grilled meats that are cooked over open fires. So a lot of the original food has to be had at the Columbia Restaurant in Ybor. I had a Cuban sandwich with plantain chips with a dill pickle wedge and a fresh sliced tomato. It was Meh..okay I guess. It wasn't the worst Cuban sandwich I've had but it wasn't close to the best. The service was a bit slow. There is indoor and outdoor seating. You can't beat the view of the Hillsborough River! Convenient if you're going to the Tampa History Center and a good location if you are on Riverwalk.

Mission BBQ gets 5 stars from me. I've never been into the restaurant but we have used their catering services for a few of our office events. 

I think I've had just about everything on the menu including their pulled pork, brisket, ribs, and their pulled chicken! It's all been so delicious! Their sides are really good too. I've had their creamy cheesy delicious macaroni and cheese. Mmmmm... The baked beans are perfectly seasoned with the sweet yet savory taste. Their cornbread is dense and rich. Mission BBQ has catered several events at my job and the customer service has been on point. The orders have been delivered on time, hot, and ready to eat. 

I have nothing but good things to say about Mission BBQ :-)

The first thing I noticed when I walked into the Hard Rock was it was a little humid and it was Smokey the closer I got to the casinos. The smoke lingers up until the time that I went into the cafe. I love the cafe (review to come later). The ventilation is not very good there. There's a lot of renovation going on here so maybe they're going to be working on the look and the flow of this place. I'm used to the one in Hollywood Fl and that one is amazing so I have to be careful not to compare the two.

BellaBrava is centrally located in downtown St Pete close to all the shops and museums.  If you're dining there, the restaurant will validate your parking which is awesome because  parking can be quite expensive in Downtown St Pete. We came here on a Sunday for brunch. I wanted something light so I ordered the Squash Blossom Flatbread. The crust is so flaky and delicious with its lightly burnt edges. There was just enough sauce and vegetables to satisfy my appetite without  make me feel too full. Now what you need to be careful of is their delicious bread that they bring out with the rosemary butter. OMG! So good :-)

The service was really good. Our waitress was nice, made suggestions, and was attentive. The  decor was modern and very inviting. The bathrooms were clean and well-stocked and I look for that at every restaurant that I dine in. Because if the bathrooms aren't clean then you know it's not clean everywhere else. Overall I had a good experience and BellaBrava  would  definitely be a dining option the next time I'm in St Pete.

I really like Stone Soup Company. They've got one of the best Cubans that I've had in Tampa. I've had the regular Cuban and their  Bad Hombre Cuban sandwich platter. I usually order french fries because they are really tasty and crispy. The Bad Hombre is my favorite and let me tell you why. 

I've had the Bacon and Bleu Burger with Cajun slaw and got the burger all the way. Which is $12. The Bad Hombre platter is $10. They have $2 mimosas when we went one Sunday and they were pretty tasty too. You can't go wrong with $2 mimosas.

On my most recent visit,  I had the Breakfast Bowl. The breakfast bowl has hash browns topped with two eggs of your choice and a choice of protein. You can choose between bacon, ham, sausage, or tofu. I chose bacon. It also comes with tomato and cheese served with Cuban toast. It is really delicious. We also ordered the Panini with fried egg. It comes with spinach, tomato, cheese, and a choice of protein. You can choose from bacon, ham, andouille sausage, or Portobello sausage. That was good too.  Honestly, I haven't had a bad meal there yet. It's one of my go-to places when I want something good to eat and I've always had good, friendly service. The last time I was there, Ian took care of us.  Thanks Ian!

The Clearwater Skyline was clean, prestin and looked relatively new with its mix of Cincinnati memorabilia and Clearwater decor. We received an enthusiastic "Welcome to Skyline!" as soon as we walked thru the door "

I went straight to the bathroom to wah my hands. The women's bathroom has two stalls. It was very clean and it smelled fresh! 

I had lost my faith in Skylines that were outside of Ohio. The food at the Fort Lauderdale Skyline is not very good but this one renewed my hope that there was a Skyline outside of the Midwest that could do a chili cheese coney and a 4 way some justice. They were delicious and prepared just right! Christine was our server and she was fantastic! I'll definitely be back :-)

I've been to 7th and Grove twice (once pre- pandemic and just 1 week ago) and honestly, I'm really having a difficult time understanding the 4 and 5 Star reviews. I want to love this place. I mean I REALLY want to love this place. The decor is HOT! I love the plush seating in the bar lounge, the murals on the walls, the instagram worthy picture wall, and the overall aesthetics  of the place...however... the two times that I've been to 7th & Grove,  the service has been ridiculously slow and neither time was I there during a busy time. 

 The first time, we went to get dessert and cocktails. I have to admit, every craft cocktail that I've ever had there has been delicious. They are expertly crafted and made to perfection! It just takes sooooo d*** long to get them! We waited for our drinks about 20-25  minutes!  It took even longer to  bring out the desserts. Almost 45 minutes! When we could catch a waitress, we kept being told that someone will be over... Well, my sweet tooth was gone but when the desserts came,  I managed to push through :-) We ordered two desserts... the Red Light Special - red velvet cake with a cheesecake filling and cream cheese icing. Sounds good right?  Well, I wouldn't know because it came out half frozen.  Arghh..The Beautiful Ones - a caramel bread pudding sheet cake with raisins was tasty though. I did not rush to come back. 

The second time I went, I came with a fabulous group of ladies.  Girl time! We had a reservation in the club area. So, again with the long wait for drinks.  Some of us waited over 30 minutes for our drinks.  A few of the ladies went up to the bar and reminded them that they had ordered drinks.  WTF? I wanted to start off with an appetizer of the watermelon barbecue wings which sounds pretty doggone delicious and one of my table mates ordered the lemon zest wings. The waitress said it would take 40 minutes to come out. Again, WTF!? Did they have to chase down a few of those wild Ybor chickens!? We were there for awhile so we ended up ordering them along with the mac and cheese, the Rude Boi, the Ox Tails, and the deviled eggs. The two entrees were yummy.  The deviled eggs were okay.  The chicken wings were fried hard and were a little too dry for my taste.  

Both times that I've gone, the waitresses have been so amazingly sweet and they take the time to explain the menu. But I have to say the vibrant decor, great cocktails, good music, and friendly staff can not make up for the inconsistent food quality and extremely slow service.

I came here specifically to get the  Khao Soi. Not too many places make Khao Soi, so I was really excited to hear that they served it here. I walked into the place and it's beautiful. It's modern, nicely decorated, and very clean. The service was outstanding! Our waitress was attentive, accommodating, and very friendly. But when I got my food, it was the worst  Khao Soi that I have ever eaten :-(   The broth was watery and thin with barely any flavor. My friend ordered a vegetable dish and she was very underwhelmed as well. I sent my food back which I hardly ever do. They brought me out the Pad Thai and THAT  wasn't even good. It was dry and it lacked flavor. The saving grace was the Thai Tea. It was incredibly delicious! 

I really wanted to like the food here. I mean I really really wanted to like the food here. I just didn't. Two stars is for the decor and the service but the food.... I was very disappointed in.

Pretty space in a great shopping center. 

I brought all my girls here with my 3 year old grandson (he loved the big fire place) to have a post thanksgiving meal. 

By far the best thing we all had was the smokehouse burger. Well cooked and nice big patty. Fries or tots? Both please!

I had the pasta and didn't love it. Way to much going on and the flavors for me were all over the place. 

Prime rib was good not great. Kids meals were.... well kids meal, again good tots! 

Wine list was decent for a chain and we all went house private label. 

I guess the bottom line was big portions of ok food. Maybe the steaks are the way to go....

Not cheap, but not overpriced either. Very good service and easy parking. Oh, the bread is free and very very good. Out of the oven to the table!

I finally got the opportunity to try Pine State Biscuits, and I can understand the rave reviews.  I love that this is a unique dining experience...no one else is really doing this.  Other places may offer biscuits and/or biscuit sandwiches, but this is the only restaurant dedicated to it.  I'm reminded of a similar (and favorite) restaurant in Seattle.  
I went for lunch, but this really should be a breakfast or brunch offering.  The biscuits are light and fluffy, buttery and flakey, but with enough integrity to hold up to the generous fillings.  Normally, I would have been a purist and ordered the biscuit with gravy.  However, since I was there for lunch, I chose the Wedgie...fried green tomato, chicken breast and iceberg lettuce with bleu cheese.  I added some buffalo sauce.  The combination was a winner.  My only issue was that the fried green tomato could have had more flavor and was a bit mushy.  Overall, the meal was delicious and did not feel heavy.

I look forward to trying more from the menu; especially the gravy.  I'm also quite curious about their corn dog.  they offer biscuits to order, and I can see doing this for a family dinner.  I will, most certainly, be going back.
