I have now been to Haru three times in the past month or so, and I can honestly say that I'm hooked.  I drive past this restaurant every day on my way to and from work and had been curious to try it out.  I didn't realize this was a Ramen restaurant until I finally went in.  Up to this point, Uchi Ramen has been my go-to place.  I am now very happy to have found another incredible ramen option.  Fortunately, Haru is very convenient for me to frequent.  The restaurant is nice and clean with friendly, helpful staff.  I have eaten at both the bar and at a table and the service is great at both.  On my first visit, I had the Miso Ramen.  Delicious chicken broth with Miso, noodles, pork belly and vegetables, and the perfect soft boiled egg.  I ordered mine with medium (3) spice and it was perfect.  
My second visit, I ordered the shishito peppers and the Shoyu Ramen.  This is very similar to the Miso with the pork belly, vegetables and egg.  Again, perfection.  The shishito peppers are deliciously seasoned and soft.  
On my latest visit, I decided to just keep going down the menu and ordered the Tori Paitan, again with medium spice.  This is my favorite so far.  This soup has tender, sliced chicken breast, woodear mushrooms and spinach added.  So delicious!  I also had the shishito peppers. 
This may actually be my favorite lunch spot.  The ramen is incredibly flavorful with tender bites and the egg is creamy, smoky and adds a layer of richness.  This is the perfect meal for a chilly day.  I have heard from others that the fried chicken is also amazing....I'll have to give it a try.

I guess I can understand all the Rey Azteca love on here considering this restaurant is located in PA, but relocate this restaurant to Southern California (where I'm from), Arizona, Texas...or basically any region with a demographic that understands what constitutes good Mexican food...and nobody would eat there.  

This is not good Mexican food, people.  I'm not saying that it isn't good food; my chimichanga was good enough for me to enjoy eating it (and it wasn't really an authentic chimichanga...it was actually what would be called a taco in Mexico...the same thing Americans call taquitos), but I also enjoy eating Taco Bell every once in a while.  That doesn't mean that I confuse it for good Mexican food.  A previous reviewer said that Rey Azteca is to Mexican food what Pizza Hut is to Italian food...that's the perfect analogy for this place.

It just feels like it's trying too hard to be an authentic Mexican eatery...from the bright orange paint to the sombreros hanging on the wall...but they don't even make their own chips and salsa!!!  That's a must for any Mexican restaurant that is going to get a good rating anywhere except in PA.  Warmed up chips out of a bag and flavorless tomato paste salsa...get out of here with that crap.

I can go on and on about why this place doesn't deserve more than 2 stars, but I'll let you come to that realization for yourself.  All you people who LOVE Rey Azteca...drive down York Rd. about a mile or two to downtown Hatboro and find this little tiny taco shop named La Morena.  This is GREAT Mexican food, and would fit right in with the thousands of great taco shops in Southern California.  Go get yourself a meal there...then go back to eat at Rey Azteca and tell me that you don't have a different opinion of how good or authentic Rey Azteca really is.

What a place!  Came here with a big group of yelpers for ISC. We ordered the Cevapi and some friends ordered Cauliflower Schnitzel. The Cevapi comes with homemade bread and both come with a dipping sauce. They were both delicious!  I am someone who doesn't believe in replacing every food with cauliflower so I was a tough crowd for this. 

For dinner, I ordered Beef Goulash. It was also delicious! The meat was similar to a pot roast and the creamy polenta paired well with the dish. It was something I'd never tried and I loved it!

For dessert we got the Nutella crepes. I could barely eat any more at this point so I only had a few bites, but the crepes were outstanding as well. On top of all of this, the service is always amazing, they handled a large table and didn't bat an eye, not even at splitting the check a million ways. Overall, delicious food, amazing service, great time!

Dining alone tonight but wanted to try a new place that I have heard many of my coworkers talk about. I was seated at at table by the window which overlooked the patio. Ordered a dirty martini and was reviewing the drink selection.  This was a presentation on an iPad vs a menu and was a very large selection of wines. (Nice touch)

Feature dinner presentation was given by the waiter with actual cuts that were on the menu. (Another nice touch) 

I ordered a Caesar salad and the Bobe in ribeye. The salad was out in a flash and the offer of fresh ground pepper was delivered by a different waiter. I only bring this up because normally it is a course grind. Here, it is a find grind that gives a more consistent taste across the salad. (Yep, nice touch #3)

Next out, the cowboy ribeye. Bone in, it think it was 16 oz, with broccoli and small baked potatoes. Cooked to perfection, cut like butter with some kind of pepper rub possibly on it. I can say this, it was fantastic. 

If I wasn't so full I would have loved to try something off of the selection of deserts but I just couldn't see any of that steak go to waist.

As I was paying the waiter asked if he could get my car pulled up from valet. (Nice touch #4). 

Look forward to coming back.

I once called this place the "best burrito place EVER" and I have convinced many others of this as well.  I work as an ICU nurse and your breakfast bacon/ chicken burritos were the perfect fuel for a tough day. But now your menu has gone completely vegan??? Not even vegan optional; just straight vegan What happened to giving customers a choice? Would it be too much to at least keep chicken/ eggs (free range) on the menu??? Eating animals doesn't make anyone a bad person. 

Sadly you will lose loyal and satisfied costumers who have been eating your delicious food since Honest Toms was a small food truck.

Farewell "Honest" Tom.

Cops were called on my friends (who are Asian and were potential customers) simply because they told the worker they felt uncomfortable with the ambience here. Especially in regards to how my friends were being treated upon entrance compared to white customers. The owner lied and said my friends had a weapon in order to get them removed? Just because they're people of color you're going to be quick to assume they're carrying a weapon? Seems racist to me. 

When they say "Old town Coffee" they really mean "Confederate Town coffee." It's the ignorance , abhorrence, and racism for me.....

If you're looking for GOOD QUALITY coffee in goleta/Santa Barbara where you'll be treated with RESPECT regardless of your skin color, I recommend Dune's Coffee instead!

This is by far the worst place I've been. The employees were professional but the owner is straight rude and ignorant to be quite honest. I ordered a head and regardless of the wait time was patient as I realize they are busy. The owner ignored people speaking to her and spoke rudely of customers in the store out loud to then serve us cold food. The Mac and cheese was under cooked and had a whole scoop of what tasted like sour cream. Not to mention the hair we found in two platters. She had no gloves or mask on and was making platters for people during Covid outbreak. I will never return and will spend my money in business that deserve to be open and appreciate the business

With very few options for ramen in NOLA, nomiya is by far the best. Broth is rich and flavorful and noodles are always perfectly cooked. There's only 3 options right now, but that's how you know they have perfected it! I've been here twice and will be coming back for more. 

PS I really freaking love ramen

tl;dr Small cafe whipping up some of the best breakfast in the Quarter. Just pay attention to the up-charges.

Popped in on Easter morning around 8am and thankfully there were still a few tables. Service was prompt, with our drinks in hand within minutes and an order of the monkey bread placed while we perused the rest of the menu and listened to the great music selection they were playing (and singing too). 

The place filled up quick after we placed our order, with a line even forming outside. Staff worked quick to get orders taken, tables cleaned, and actively checked on the line outside.

1. Monkey Bread ($5.75): About a 2" x 2" slice of warm monkey bread served in a cast iron skillet drizzled with icing and powdered sugar. Sure, it was delicious yet I expected a bigger slice for the price.

2. Cochon Eggs Benedict ($12) - slow braised pork on a biscuit with 2 soft poached eggs, hollandaise with home fries: Oh butter my biscuit this dish is delicious. Poached eggs were to perfect temp, just the perfect amount of hollandaise (I hate when dishes are just drenched in hollandaise hiding the food underneath), melt in your mouth pork, and those home fries? Crispy exterior and soft interior. I'm not sure how they managed that great texture with such large chunks of potato. The misleading downside/disappointment? Keep on reading...

2a. +$4.00 Andouille Sausage: Went with the servers tip of adding andouille to my plate to liven up the dish, yet I didn't realize it was going to be $4 more. Turned out to be a little over a dozen tiny dices of flavorless sausage without even a hint of spice. What a complete waste of money.

3. Eggs Lafitte ($15) - andouille crusted grit cakes with 2 poached eggs, crawfish hollandaise sauce, served with ratatouille: this was a filling meal that would have been lack luster without the acidity of the ratatouille. The pieces of crawfish were smaller in size than I was expecting in the hollandaise sauce and the flavor was there but not as present as I would have preferred. The grit cakes happily surprised me in their texture and flavor. I enjoyed them a lot more than any of the grits that we have "Up North". While I wasn't hungry until late in the afternoon, I would not order this dish again. There were plenty of other dishes on the menu that caught my attention that I'd like to try (like that Cap'N Crunch French Toast!).

3a. +$4.00 Andouille Sausage: Went with the servers tip, again, of adding andouille to the plate to liven up the dish, yet, again, we didn't realize it was going to be $4 more. Again just a little over a dozen tiny dices of flavorless sausage without even a hint of spice. Money down the drain...

4. Coffee ($3)

5. Fountain Soda ($3) - Coke products

Our dishes were more than filling. Honestly, we should have just split one and we would have been set. Pure breakfast goodness.

I'll stress this again. Don't fall for the suggestion of adding andouille to your dish. It's a four dollar up-charge that is not worth it at all. We thought our server was being kind and helpful, but it was just for running up our bill in hopes of a larger tip. If it wasn't for this souring cash grab experience, this would have been a four almost five star breakfast.

We were caught in the rain one afternoon and needed a spot to hide that served up food. Pulling up Yelp this was close and looked like it could work out. The exterior of the building oozes NOLA charm, yet the interior is your average dive with TVs. 

Service was quick to start, yet our order took a long time to come out when we were one of two groups in the place. All the food was okay and served its purpose, yet every item is priced essentially ala carte. Want fries with your po-boy that already costs from $11-13.50? Add $3. Want onion rings instead? Add $6. Or maybe a side of gumbo? Add $6. Four a group of four with only three beers our total came to over $150. The most expensive meal we had during our five day trip. How?! Looking at our bill it all added up correctly, yet man this place is expensive for your average bar food.

Oh, you'll probably want a drink too... If you order a beer, be prepared to be badgered for your choice. Maybe if you had an actual cocktail menu I'd try something besides a beer. Also, don't bother with a tap beer, by taste alone you know the lines have never been cleaned.

My opinion? Skip it.

The food was disappointing.   See my picture of the hot roast beef sandwhich and McDonald's fries i got for $16.00. The beer was the only thing that gave this place 3 stars. 

Don't come here hungry unless you won a scratch off.

Wife and I finally found a restaurant that has great view in the i

Reserved on a Tuesday to get a window seat.. I'll point out the good things first and explain why this review is a 3 star.

The good:
We ordered the following
Hot Seafood Platter
Lobster Bisque
Beef Short Rib + Butcher's Filet
Steak + Potatoes
Lobster Macaroni + Cheese
Wild Mushrooms, Sauteed Spinach with Crispy Onions 

Yep you read that right.. We love to eat, that's why we ordered that much

Price was very reasonable for this type of restaurant, we are expecting it to be more expensive.
Taste is phenomenal, we've been through a lot of restaurants and it's safe to say everything we ate was great! We are definitely coming back for the hot seafood platter.

Speed was great, well it was a Tuesday and not a lot of people

New silverware each time your plate is taken, and they will wipe your table.

Our server was good, no complains. He even asked us if we want to see the other side of the city, which we did and it was amazing!

The bad: -2 stars
So, as soon as we came in I asked "are we able to get a window seat" the hostess said "Yes". Wife and I are very excited.. and there were about 5 available window seats for a party of 2, and you know where the hostess put us ? A view that is being blocked by a damn pillar.... we had to ask to get moved... and she did... we asked for a specific location and she said somebody already reserved it.. So we said.. Okay
We came at 7:30 pm... and the couple that got the seat we wanted came in at 8:30pm... That's an hour difference.. When they got seated we over heard the hostess say "Is this view okay".. 
So what is going on ??? We didn't get asked that question....... We don't know how the reservation works here or the hostess was just plain discriminating... you can tell it from her actions.... 

But.... we'll give this restaurant a try one more time.. and we'll see....

After reading great reviews about this new restaurant, I was happy to be invited out for noodles on a chilly night with some new friends. The Spicy Dosunco was wonderful! The broth was flavorful and not spicy enough to make you run for the nearest fire hydrant. They also provide chili oil to add some extra punch if desired. The fermented egg and pork made the dish in my opinion. My only regret is not added extra pork and eggs to my dish. The I enjoyed my experience thoroughly. The service was friendly and prompt. The prices are exceptionally reasonable! I am looking forward to another visit where I can try an appetizer and a different noodle dish or two. I have a feeling this will become one of my favorite new restaurants in town.

Wow, I'm in shock. I am an events planner (I plan over 150 events a year), and I wanted to book an event at Moriatry's for 100 people in their upstairs space. I called and was transferred to Richard Konstantine. He was very brisk and unaccommodating throughout the phone call, and when I finished telling him the details of the event he said "no, we'll pass" and hung up on me. 

I've talked to dozens of bar managers in the city and this is the only time that has ever happened to me. I never liked the place, but now I will never go back. If you're planning a party, I would not recommend trying to plan it here!

I heard there was a place making hand-rolled New York Style bagels, and I had to check them out. Being from New York, bagels are a way of life. Anytime of day, it's the perfect street food that can be made to order savory or sweet. Talia's does just that. Simple, yet mouth-watering combinations guaranteed to make you melt. 

I put in an order for take-out through the Yelp App and within 7 minutes my order was ready. Walked in and the owner immediately greeted me. He said I didn't look familiar and asked how did I hear about them. That took me be surprise, yet he was right. 

After talking for a couple of minutes I went on my way. Got home, didn't disrobe, and started eating before I got a shoe off. I should have ordered 2 of them. It's been so long since I've had quality bagels, it made me appreciate them all over again.

If President Clinton didn't come here when he was in Tucson, would this place still be popular?  Let me say this - Clinton was a good Pres, but he would not make a good Yelper as his taste in food was not good at all.  

I cannot find anything here that is remotely worthy of praise nor are they worthy of complaints.  They are just ordinary Mexican food.  But now that everyone and their chicas think this joint is so good, the line is long every night at dinner time.  So you can do the math - average food and much longer than average wait time (unnecessarily, I might add).  If the answer is still positive for you, go for it.  Me?  It's a two-star 'cause I truly have had better (without the wait time).  Not hatin', just sayin' ...

The owner himself will personally tell you that he serves up the best chicken cheesesteak in town. That's a pretty bold statement, but he combines real chopped chicken breast with your choice of spinach or broccoli. I have yet to be disappointed by this, and so far it is proving to be better than any other chicken cheesesteak I've tried.

There are other items on the menu, ranging from burgers to southern food to breakfast. Don't be afraid of the fact that this place looks like a total dive, either. The owner takes pride in his food, and if there are indeed roaches cooked into the burgers, those are some damn tasty roaches.

My sister and I went to check out the Hard Rock Casino. One might think that I am really into gambling since I went to two casinos in two weeks but I actually don't gamble at all. We just went to check it out and see what the fuss was about.

We paid $18 for a martini and a raspberry vodka soda at the bar. Not surprising that the drinks were expensive. 

On the menu it said the cocktails go up in price $1-2 each after 11pm. 
Who does that!? And also, at least have the decency to set different menus out when 11pm hits so ppl don't know they're getting screwed. I thought this was really lame.

The casino was pretty inside and had lots of nice light fixtures and decorations. I got  a picture with Lady Gaga's cape! 

We had lunch at the Rock n Raw sushi bar. We were skeptical but it actually ended up being pretty good! Prices were reasonable and we got plenty to eat. Service was friendly. 

The casino is huge and kind of a maze.

We left smelling like smoke of course. We got in some really great people watching! 

I'm glad we went to check it out but we both agreed once was enough.

Today my husband and I ordered a full rack of the ribs with two sides.  The ribs we were served were extremely fatty and were not tender at all.  The first rib I bit into looked pink and I asked my husband if it was fully cooked.  I also questioned whether the ribs were pork?  I have eaten a lot of delicious ribs and these were really bad. Needless to say, we were extremely disappointed.  We feel we wasted $30 on sub-standard food.  The theme of the restaurant is great, but unfortunately the food was not.

First time there. An ((((AWFUL)))) experience!! I couldn't wait to get home to my laptop because my thumbs were too pissed to give this review from my phone!

We went for take-out. The wait was not long at all; sadly that was not the issue. 

There were two young people there. One in the kitchen, the young man and a young woman at the front house. She was cashier and evidently green shucker (BTW - there was no hand-washing or glove wearing between handling money and the greens). There was also a big black tub filled with flower (used for coating the chicken) on the same counter as the greens and above the trash back being used to hold the pulled leaves.

Viewing the menu was the first disappointment. They didn't have a several of options that were listed there. I figured, maybe because it's early and those items would be readily available closer to dinner time. We then asked for dessert. We were told they didn't have any. On the counter behind us were about 7 cake boxes filled with - guess...CAKES for the restaurant. The shucker/cashier said she didn't know how to cut them. I'm still laughing and shaking my head on that one.

Our orders were placed and then we waited. I noticed the music when we walked in. Rap. Then came the flood of the "N' word, the next song the guy rapping about how he was sexing some chick. The "P" word and description of sex acts as well as how endowed the rapper is filled the restaurant. I was with my mother. She's 83. 

When I asked them to change the song the young man got upset. The next song was more of the same. I asked the young woman to turn it off until we left. She was willing to accommodate but the young man had a lot to say and proceeded to tell me the song was talking about anything and I was complaining about nothing. REALLY?!!?

I told him we are customers and should be subjected to profane lyrics in the restaurant and that it was horribly offensive. He continued to try to debate me on this then disappeared where I couldn't see him so I went to an area of the dining room to have view of him, since our food had not come out yet. he didn't like it and tried to get me to leave that area by saying "Take out is in there. You need to be in there." Mistake. I said, "Maybe I want to check out the dining room and have a party here." he rolled his eyes and went back behind the line still talking under his breath.

Oh Yeah...
How is the food. LOL
I had cabbage (salty), mac & cheese (waaaay too much cheese - more like eating a slice of pizza & the noodles were very mushy) and yams (delicious!! - just cut them smaller, I had an entire potato half in my container).

Listen, I'm at the head of the line when it comes to supporting black owned businesses but this mess right here...I'm not going to put all of how I feel on the internet for the world to see but those of us that know - know. 

Be better!

We enjoyed an outstanding Sunday brunch experience at the True Food Kitchen located in King of Prussia recently.  The building and decor is very pleasant and relaxing.  The staff are friendly and very well schooled in the menu.  The menu covers a wide range from lite to heavy breakfast and lunch items.  There are many healthy options in fact pretty much the entire menu features feel good, taste good, good for you food.  My hubs and I shared a lovely order of Avocado toast for starters.  I ordered the grilled Salmon which the server told me was Scottish Salmon - my favorite due to its oily/buttery quality - so I was stoked.  The dish was served with farro and quinoa and featured roasted beets AND a super delicious cilantro pumpkin seed pesto!!!!  Score on all taste buds!  The dish was fresh and oh so full of flavor.  We would return to the True Food Kitchen in the future and would recommend it to anyone seeking a healthy but delicious meal option.

Don't Be Shellfish, When You Sea Food, Treat Yo Self, Share, And Eat it! Came here with little expectations but left with a big impression. Shells Sea Food, you're the bomb! 

Parking is thru an open lot and can be scarce during peak lunch and dinner hours. Walked in without reservations and waited just 10 minutes before we got seated. Ambiance was casual with simple nautical decor and a few dollar bills and chalkboards on walls. 

Service was quick like sonic the hedgehog, so fast that our table felt a bit rushed during ordering. Our server checked on us often and our food came out in an instant. 

Got the Shellfish Boil that came with steamed Dungeoness Crab, Oysters, Mussels, Shrimps, Sausage, Potatoes and Slaw - really flavorful and prepared on point. Fresh, juicy, perfect temp, seasoned with Old Bay, and portions were good to devour by two. Blue Tea Lagoon was sweet and boozy, and thanks to mighty Yelp for the complimentary rocking House Margarita.

Shellfish, well I wish to be back soon in St. Pete Beach! Another great find!

Dock aside if you're crabby, but pull in if you're hungry and need something yummy.

Near Pier 60, park thru a metered spot on their lot or purchase a $1/hr parking spot from the restaurant hostess upstairs. Walk up to 2nd floor to build an appetite, or ride the elevator and burn it later.

Ambiance was casual and laid back with a picture perfect view of the Clearwater Beach. Our server was Phrank and he was attentive, knowledgeable and friendly. Service was fast and efficient.

Got the Bairdi Crab with Shrimp Scampi and Stuffed Clams, with sides of Mac n Cheese plus Mashed Potatoes. Serving was big and quality was good. It had three quarter pounds of delectable crab legs steamed with butter and old bay seasoning, rich and creamy mac n cheese, and stuffed clams that were incredible and flavorful. The mashed potatoes were smooth and fluffy and the shrimp scampi was perfectly done. Crab Trap Bucket and All American Strawberry Vodka Lemonade Cocktails were both craftily mixed. 

Overall a delightful and enjoyable dining experience. Stop the blabby, go ahead and make me flabby coz I'm planning my next visit. Thanks Crabby for a yabby dabby lunch!

Lively energetic atmosphere and the customer service was good.  It took a minute or so to get drinks and food but it was worth the wait.   We sat at the bar because the place was super busy.  They have both inside  and outdoor dinning  and they bring you chips and salsas while you decide your menu options.

I ordered the Enchiladas Criollo: Two chicken enchiladas with melted cheese, green sauce, coloradito red mole, onions, Mexican sour cream and cotija cheese, served with green rice.  Everything was very tasty and it looked beautiful of my plate.

Thanks to JOTSB we were provided with comfortable friendly and accommodating transportation to and from "The 34th Annual Santa Barbara Vintners Festival Grand Tasting at River View Park in Buellton, Ca on April 23, 2016.  The bus arrived on time, the driver was friendly and professional.

I wasn't sure what to expect from this market but I was pleased with the overall experience.  Local farmers were there with fresh vegetables, flowers and plants, some baked goods, and fresh fish.  Some of the farmers had samples for you to try, some had an abundance of goods and some did not.  The market overall had a nice selection of goods and the folks working were friendly.  Parking can be a challenge.

This was my first time visiting this restaurant but my daughter and son in law have been here several times. It has an elegant casual atmosphere, neat clean and nicely decorated.  We had wanted to sit in the patio dining area to enjoy the beautiful views of the ocean and scenery but settled for a nice table inside that had a huge window with the outside views.

Our waiter Billy was amazing.  He was kind, helpful, friendly and made you feel welcomed.  We started the Happy Hour with drinks, Lamb Meatballs and Jamon Crocchette.  Next we ordered three of the HH pizzas each was more tastier than the others my favorite was the Fennel sausage pizza.  The crust on the pizza was thin and crunchy it was yummy by itself the cheese, sausage and other seasoning added another layer of goodness.  The Lamb Meatballs were tender and very tasty I didn't want to stop eating them. 

Overall, great experience, awesome service, delicious food.

My daughter and I came here for a quick lunch getaway while my son-n-law took care of his toddler.  We sat outside because it was a beautiful day just a little cool, we had noticed that they had the heaters out.   It is a very elegant setting and the waiter was very helpful and super friendly yet professional.
 
We ordered drinks a hot tea for my daughter and she ordered me a Fogged Hog.  The name doesn't sound very attractive but the drink was a masterpiece.  It took a while to make but when it arrived it was worth the wait. I can only describe it to you because I forgot to take a picture showing how it is presented to you. It came inside a glass cast that was filled with a  mist, steam, smoking fog that enhances the flavor of the drink.  The presentation was beautiful and the cocktail was very good.

For lunch we had a bowl of Tuscan Meatball Soup and Bread DELICIOUS!

Great customer services thanks Jorge!

My Mother's Day celebration (which was a weekend event) ended with an amazing dinner at this restaurant.  From start to finish we were welcomed and provided with excellent customer service.The restaurant has a beautiful view, it was very clean, elegant and spacious, fine dining at its best.

We started at the bar and ended at a table for seven!  The menu had an assortment of appetizers, sides, entrees, and desserts.  Everything looked delicious even the Beet Salad which was delicious.  I ordered the Diver Scallops and the Beet Salad, the Scallops were fantastic.  They were seared properly, seasoned and tasted amazing.  

At the table were other dishes:  Roasted Brussel Sprouts, Hanger Steak, Dumplings to name a few which I sampled and was delighted with the flavors.  A quick shout out to Eli and Todd for making this an awesome end to a beautiful Mother's Day.

I came here for coffee but could not resist the Avocado Toast.  Everything was very good.  The coffee was robust rich in flavor just the way I like and the toast was delicious, loaded with nicely seasoned avocado, tiny sliced tomatoes and a small amount of a white sauce.

This coffee shop was huge but only the front section was opened to customer.  Plenty of seating both inside and out with Wi-Fi.  The staff were friendly and welcoming, it was clean and offered a variety of pastries and breakfast sandwiches.

I have gone here a few times when I visit Santa Barbara.  For lunch and other celebrations the food and service is always amazing.   I love the outdoor experience and the welcoming atmosphere.  Parking can be a challenge.

During my visit to Santa Barbara I had lunch here while I was inside the SB Public Market.  My daughter and I tried the "Tia Juana Taco, Chicana Quesadilla, The Al Pastor Taco "and Chips and Salsa everything was delicious.  The "Tia Juana Taco had Spanish octopus, Mexican wild shrimp, avocado, cheese, a peanut salsa, and roasted chile an explosion of flavor.  The Chicana Quesadilla had sautéed Mexican white shrimp, cheese, roasted corn, poblano and homemade salsa very tasty and the Al Pastor was delicious with the pineapple and guacamole. 

We took our lunch to the Wine+Beer and ordered wine to wash down the lunch.  The service at restaurant was quick, the food was good and I would love to come back and try more from the menu.

This location was perfect for the kick off place of the "Yelp's Jingle Bus Holiday Lights Tour" with available parking, outdoor seating and friendly staff.  

It was comfortable, clean and warm inside.  Yelpers enjoyed various bites provided by "Reds Bin 211"and could order drinks from the bar.  Discounts were given for Yelp check-ins and showing Yelp wrist bands.

The folks at Reds Bin 211 were helpful and friendly.  Thanks the welcoming atmosphere and a terrific beginning to an awesome night.

Mony's is a popular hot spot in the Funk Zone.  I have gotten food from here a couple of times and have not been disappointed.  They are generally very busy because the food is so good and the prices are great.  The portions sizes are huge and this family owned business takes great pride in preparing all the foods that come out of the kitchen.  

The restaurant is small but there is some indoor and outdoor seating areas, nothing fancy but comfortable enough to enjoy the delicious food.  On this visit to Mony's we picked up an order of the loaded Carne Asada Nachos.  This nachos were more than enough for the three of us.  The meat was tender, the chips were fresh and crunchy and the beans and other toppings were an explosion of flavor and tastiness in your mouth.

The food was so good the following morning we ordered the Carne Asada Burrito to take with us on the "Jump on the Bus" ride to Santa Barbara Vintners Festival Grand Wine Tasting in Buellton, CA. 

This burrito was awesome!  It was the kind of burrito that takes two hands hold and a wide open bite to make a dent in it. Need I saw more, it was fantastic!

The second bar this night towards earning my Soused badge.  The atmosphere at this bar was very upbeat.  Customers and staff were friendly and the drinks were very good.  The decorations here are unique and they have nice art work on the wall.  The bartenders made the evening awesome because of there attention to customer service.  In addition to the drinks we ordered the chicken bites and they were tender, juicy and flavorful.  They also have a back patio area should you want to sit outside.

I have eaten food from here many times when visiting Santa Barbara it's one of my daughter favorite restaurants.  I have only done pick up and they are quick and efficient.  My favorite is Shrimp Egg Foo Young !  I also enjoyed the Shrimp Fried Rice and the Potstickers.  The menu offers a wide range of food and the prices are reasonable.  Would totally recommend trying it for yourself.

I have eaten food here twice over Mother's Day weekend.  On each occasion the service is friendly and very welcoming.  Chef Carter is awesome and his food is delicious.  The sampler platter, sausage trio, kale salad, corn bread, baked beans are fantastic.  I loved everything including the Bloody Mary's, the cocktail "Lavender 75"and the incredible desserts:  a Coconut cake and an Oreo cake they were both so yummy!
I look forward coming back to Santa Barbara and eating more of this delicious food.  Thank you Chef Carter and staff for an amazing experience of great food and awesome customer service.

After being disappointed by so many Asian restaurants, I came here with mixed hopes. They totally blew the expectations out of the water. 

Crab puffs - hot, creamy, and not drenched in grease. 

Egg rolls - tasted fresh, and again, not drenched in grease. 

Pork Fried Rice - do you guys even use oil? Totally not complaining, but complementing, probably the best fried rice I've had in years. 

Orange chicken - plenty of sauce, brown rice was perfect! The sauce was slightly sweet, slightly orangey and perfect. Not like the big chain restaurants. Chicken was ever so lightly coated with flour. 

Kung Pao Chicken - same situation. Just the right amount of heat, chicken was again lightly coated, and was perfect. 

At the end of the meal, they offered buy one get one on our next visit. Looks like I found my new go to Asian restaurant!

Writing my second review of Dino's because it is just that good.  Where to start....the wings are hands down the best in the area, and arguably the best I have ever had.  They are excellent. 

As we all know every good hoagie starts with the bread.  Their seeded rolls are perfect for both hot and cold hoagies.  With enough chew to withstand hot filling(cheesesteak, or roast pork) so you aren't just eating a soggy mess, yet soft enough if you decide to go with a cold hoagie.  

Per my earlier review the cheesesteaks are money and honestly my favorite item on the menu.  Dino has set the gold standard for cheesesteaks.  If you want to be able to eat a cheesesteak anywhere else, then don't try the cheesesteak hoagie at Dino's.  I am not kidding I can't go anywhere else for a cheesesteak, because they are never remotely as good as Dino's.  

The roasted pork hoagie is also delicious.  Just ate that for the first time tonight.  Wouldn't change a thing.  Make sure you ask for a side of the roast pork jus.  

The Italian hoagie is awesome, when not in the mood for hot hoagie.  

Honestly, everything is fresh, made to order, with highest quality ingredients.  Clearly from all the other reviews I am not the only one who thinks so.  

Please tell your friends and support this local gem.

Upon a suggestion given by my sister (who lives in Philadelphia), she suggested that we (meaning my sister, her boyfriend, my husband and I) go to Irwin's for Sunday brunch.  Irwin's is located on Mifflin Street in a diverse urban area.  When you enter the building, there is gymnasium to the left and some long hallways (the building to me somewhat resembled a school).  Irwin's is located on the 8th  floor of the building.  Irwin's is very hip and has  an artistry type of feel to it.  There is graffiti on the walls, sofas with overstuffed cushions and pillows, round and squared shaped tables and a circular bar off to the left.  There are also large windows in the back of the restaurant that provide spectacular views of the city.   The menus we were given for brunch were limited in their food selections and we were also given a separate drink menu that included a variety of alcoholic beverages, wine and mimosa options.  When I scanned the menu for food, I noticed they had lemon waffles served with pistachios, whipped cream and pomegranates; I quickly chose that because, who wouldn't?  My waffle was absolutely amazing and my sister, her boyfriend and my husband loved their food as well.  I recommend Irwin's if you are ever visiting the city of Philly.  I don't think will ever find food this good and unique back home.

Wow, this is my new favorite place to go shopping.  Unfortunately, it's thousands of miles away from me since I live in California but my sister who lives here recommended that I visit and that I would love it; she was right.  I definitely have to come back for one more shopping trip before I fly back home.  Reading Terminal Market is an indoor market (perfect for a rainy day) and has many places to visit, eat and shop at.  The Market features bakeries (as pictured below), a mini meat and cheese market, a small scaled market that sells a variety of pastas, canned and dried fruits,  a whole produce section with fresh flowers, vegetables and fruits, a gigantic food court (I recommend getting the raspberry banana smoothie at the juice bar yum), and specialty stores too that are from around the world like the Holland shop (all items are designed and made in Holland) and feature some of the most beautiful ornaments and kitchen items I have ever seen!  And not to mention to satisfy your sweet tooth, there are many places to buy fudge, chocolate, cake slices and cupcakes too (oh my goodness)!  The Market can be a little crowded and a little overwhelming at times but this is a must see if you are ever in the area.

I am not sure what happened this night - perhaps it was because it was on an Ace's game night but I can honestly say that I have never had such poor service.  We sat and looked at a menu and a waiter did come over after a few minutes to get our drink orders.  My step daughter asked if we could play Monopoly as there are games on the table.  We laughed and said we would never have time to play that game.  We got our beers and then we ordered our food.  That is where the experience went downhill.  

The beer was good.  They do have a good selection of beers.  After 30 minutes we started to try flagging down our waiter but were unsuccessful.  45 minutes in we finally got his attention.  We asked about our food and went to check.  He returned to say that they were having kitchen issues and were just going to start our meals.  60 minutes in and 2 of the 6 things we ordered arrived:  A pretzel and a hummus trio.  Both were pre-made and only needed to be warmed.  We all nibbled thinking that our meals would be right behind...well, we were wrong.  We finished the food we had and yet again flagged down the waiter to see where the rest of the food was.  Shocker - it STILL had not been started.  We ended up leaving without having dinner because we had tickets to the game and it was getting ready to start.  

I hope that they work out there issues on busy nights or they will have a lot of problems getting customers to return.

Before shopping with a friend we decided to stop in to the Cheesecake Factory for lunch.  It was about 1:00 in the afternoon and there was a 25 minute wait, so I didn't think that was too bad for a weekend.  Our waitress was very nice and the service was good overall.  We both ordered a sandwich from the Skinnylicious Menu and then traded halves.  We tried the Chicken Salad and the Turkey and Avocado sandwiches, both came with a side salad with balsamic vinaigrette.  Our meal arrived rather quickly.  Both sandwiches were very good.  The turkey sandwich had a lot of thinly sliced turkey.  The chicken salad had almonds and celery so it had a nice crunch factor and was quite tasty.  Of the two sandwiches the chicken salad was my favorite.  I would definitely order it again.  

Now, you are at the Cheesecake Factory so of course occasionally one must partake in some cheesecake.  We settle on sharing a slice of the Ultimate Red Velvet cake Cheesecake.  OMG!!  The slice was huge!!  Lets just say that between the two of us we could not finish the entire piece (although we did make a very valiant effort!).  This cheesecake was out of this world scrumptious.  At was rich, creamy, sweet, and luscious absolutely everything an awesome cheesecake should be.  All I can say it thank goodness we were shopping afterwards because a walk was definitely needed.

Sorry to be a cry baby but we had a pretty bad experience here. Hence the name perhaps. Either food and service were both bad or this place likes to serve clumped up pasta. Pasta noodles came out all stuck together and when we asked our server about it he brazenly told us this is how egg based noodles turn out. If you guys enjoy noodles all clumped up look no further, this is your place.

I don't mean to brag, but I like to think of myself as a Casino Buffet Connoisseur. From as far back as I can remember, I've been perusing the aisles of buffets around the gambling world, basking in the glow of heat lamps and sampling as many varieties of bananas foster as I can.

Sterling's Sunday Brunch takes the cake. So. Many. Cakes. Here's why:

Quality: Oftentimes eating at a casino buffet is like playing Russian roulette. Is this piece of filet mignon going to be a winner, or are you going to spend the rest of the night clutching your stomach in pain? At most good buffets one can hope at least 35-50% of their items are winners. At Sterling's Sunday Brunch, that number was around 80-90%! Nearly everything we tried, even items that are usually disappointing, were great. 

The tops were probably the seafood items: snow crab, but not watered down or drowned in salt like most other buffets, the meat was actually sweet and delicious! The shrimp were plump, fresh, and peeled already. There were oysters, which were okay but pretty lacking in flavor. Smoked salmon, gravlax, trout, and any other items you might find on a breakfast menu were there as well, and were sublime. 

Their other feature was a very well cooked lamb chop. I liked that they were in small portions AND on a bed of roasted garlic. Other items like the polenta, pasta, waffles, eggs, standard breakfast meats were all great. 

This is ALSO a champagne brunch, meaning your server will continually come around for refills should your flute of champagne be dangerously low. Their orange juice was really tasty, too, so you can go the mimosa route if you prefer.

Overall, really great buffet for the price. It's somewhere a little below a Vegas buffet in terms of selection and quality, but given that it's probably half the price and more local, this one is awesome. The ambiance is also a plus: why should you have to mingle with the peons fighting for fried chicken at the Flavors buffet around the corner, when you could be serenaded by a veritable Kenny G and sit in cush leather booths while sipping on mimosas? Exactly.

Great ambiance, friendly service, and delicious pizza! 

As an appetizer, we enjoyed the Fresh Mozzarella and Tomato that comes with white balsamic reduction, basil oil and garlic toast. The mozzarella definitely was fresh and yummy, and went well with everything on the plate.

We ordered the Roasted Three Pizza with creamy fontina, green onion and parmigiano Reggiano - gluten-free. The gluten-free options only come in the 10-inch crust. What I love about this pizza was the fact that the toppings don't slide off of it like other gluten-free crusts normally do. Each bite was absolutely delectable, and the green onions go perfectly with the three mushrooms! I had to stop myself from eating the entire pizza, because I just couldn't help myself! I always have to remember the wise words of my mother: "Eat until you're 80% full, and not 110%." Whenever I would overeat back home, she would always lecture me! 

My date loved the Shrimp, Mozzarella and Pecorino Romano Cheese Pizza. He said that the shrimp was very fresh, and he was pleased that it wasn't breaded the way other pizza places place shrimp on their pizzas.

Scordato's offers half off drinks after 8 pm. There's a full bar with beer and wine on the menu, but they lack a cocktail menu, so keep a cocktail of your choice in mind.

I would love to review the food here but I never had a chance to due to the disgustingly rude treatment I received. I live 3 minutes from this location and this was my third attempt at eating there since the two other times it had been closed (during listed open hours). 

My husband and I were excited to grab some dinner to go and with the "authentic/housemade" food they advertise we were looking forward to having a new favorite for when I don't feel like making my own Italian. 

I excitedly asked if the tortellini was made in house (because they are all about the fresh pasta right? ...right?)..."No, we buy it " is the deadpan response I got. Oh ok..."how about the Carbonara..is it made authentic or..". Cut off "You know how authentic Carbonara is made, then you make it" He then mocks me by opening the kitchen doors and tells me to make my dinner.  

At this point I thought maybe I was taking it the wrong way and tried to laugh it off.  I was so shocked..I just want dinner and was at a loss so asked what do you recommend? "I recommend nothing to you".  That's when I put down the menu and said "it's apparent we are not welcome here" and left. What an absolute pretentious jerk.  We went in happy and excited to try a local joint but obviously they can't take the heat when it's time to back up what they do.  

And yes, I know how to make authentic Carbonara...and it does not involve cream or bacon...

A very good brewery in Midtown that has some eats to go with the beer. Brasserie Saint James has a lot of variety and some very interesting flavors. I like many beers but even a few of these seemed weird. Good to have variety of course. They also have a good menu. 

I like the Cave Rock Kölsch. It's $5 for a pint. This is a German style beer that's light, which is good because that means you can drink more of this. On some of the other taps are a few very interesting beers. There's some that are actually sweet. One of these is a pastry beer. There's something for everyone here. As for the food they have some typical stuff you find in a bar. There's fries. It's $5 for a small cup. This is served with garlic-lemon aioli or spicy ketchup. 

Cool atmosphere. It has a nice bar inside. There's plenty of good things here to try.

Here is another hip place in Midtown judging by the crowds. It has soup and more. Sup is a good place for lunch with the light menu and you won't fill up. Maybe you will if you eat like a bird. They have good options for vegetarians. 

It looks like this used to be a house. Order at the counter and they bring the food to your table. The place is pretty crowded and sometimes there's a long wait. It has good lighter fare. There's salads and soups. Often their soup changes daily. The last time here they had West African Peanut Stew. A good thing to pair with a soup is a salad, and try have a few to choose from. The one I like is the Cranberry Salad. It's $7.99 for the whole portion. This is made with almonds, cranberries, Gorgonzola, mixed greens, and white balsamic vinaigrette. Get half a salad with a soup in a combo. The combos are about $12 or so. 

Good healthier food. It is lighter so it's better at lunch. The combos are the best money saver so get one of those.

A lot of good stuff to eat. It has more than just pizza. Noble Pie Parlor is among the best pizza in Reno. Has a location in Midtown. The prices are high but you can't get much better pizza like this. 

It also is kind of like a bar. Lots of drinks. There's many beers to choose from. Beer is the best beverage to go with a pizza, so that's what we got. There's a few good local choices and some more exotic ones. I was intrigued by the Avid Cider Company Açaí Lemonade, which ended up being good. It's about $7 for a pint. This has sweetness and sourness. A good thing to share are the big appetizers. They even have some that are vegan. After checking out the menu we decided on the Vegan Frachos. It's about $19 for a big plate of fries and nachos that are piled with lots of stuff. There's vegan cheese and meat, along with onions and peppers among other things. It sure is expensive. This is the only bad thing about the food here. 

Also check out other locations for more good beer and food. It has two others. The food is too expensive in my opinion but it still is worth trying some time.

Another good brewery. It's also a distillery. 10 Torr is east of Midtown. Has a nice bar inside. You can also sit outside on a patio. 

I like most of the beers. Last time I had the Hazewagon. This is about $6 for a pint. It's a hazy IPA. This is made with mosaic hops, which have a tropical smell. Oats is what gives this a hazy body. This is one of the higher alcohol beers they have on tap. Also they have some heavier beers. They have a malty porter. It's good if you like this kind. There's also cocktails if you need harder stuff. 

Fun even just hanging around. It's recommended to get a beer of course. They don't have any food so eat before going there.

An okay deli. It has basic items. Rubicon Deli has a location in Reno. Has a few other locations to the west in California. The food is pretty good but prices are high for most things. 

It has typical items found in a deli. Of course there's stuff like sandwiches. They have the typical ones like pastrami and all that. Also there's some more unique items. This deli also has açaí bowls, which is quite unusual. A good one is the Nutty Bowl. It's about $6 for a pretty good amount, and this is a very good price compared to açaí bowls at these other places. This is made with açaí, bananas, cacao nibs, cinnamon, granola, and peanut butter, full of flavor but simple. 

Consider getting one of the açaí bowls. It's cheaper than what many other places charge you for. There's a good amount, they're full of nutrition, and of flavor too.

Another Reno brewery. It gets easy to miss these with so many of them around the other. The Depot is another one and they have food too. Fun old building good for private events. You can sit inside at the bar or dining area, or out on a patio. 

I brought the girl the last time here. It's always a good time at happy hour and there was a small crowd but it wasn't packed. There were bar seats available so we sat there. Even though it's not a humongous place they still brew lots of beers. There's many to choose from so it's hard to pick a favorite. I liked the Etherist. It's $5 for a pint at happy hour. This is a lager. It's simple to drink. There's no overwhelming bitterness and it's not excessively hoppy. As for the food there's a few ways to go. There's various pricing. Maybe get a simple and cheaper appetizer. On the other hand maybe get a more expensive entree. We chose to get the House Cut Fries. It's $7 for a big amount. These are crispy stringy fries with a nice amount of saltiness. Fries are helpful for absorbing alcohol. This allowed us to get more to try for the good happy hour. 

As for the rest of the food, it's a lot more expensive. It has some fancy options. There's burgers and pizza mostly and some vegetarian choices among these.

A place to get wasted and play games. I'm taking about board games. The Glass Die is a great place to hang out. Bring a few or a lot. Start playing any game for free, so no need to be afraid to try. 

It basically is a bar for geeks. It means it's a pretty cool place. There's all sorts of new and old games and they're even sorted by the recommended number of players. Find classics like Monopoly but why not find something obscure and expand your interests. There's card games too. As for the bar it's not a bad selection to choose from. Has a lot of local beers and they get different ones coming in and out. A complaint is once they get something good, they'll replace it with something else. The good thing is you get to try a lot and you'll find something else you like too. It's about $6 for a pint. The last time here they had the Pigeon Head Pilsner, good stuff. 

A bad thing might be parking because there's not a lot of it here. It usually isn't that busy so maybe you can get a close spot to it. This place is only for 21 and above because they're considered a bar so it's not for kids unfortunately.

Big selection of donuts. Holey Schmidt is a happening place in the morning. It has a line out the front door sometimes. Good variety and many to choose from. They have gluten free and some vegan ones too. 

It depends when you go. Sometimes they run out very early in the morning. They usually have quite a few different kinds, with a big variety. Has the classics. There's stuff like apple fritters, cream filled, and glazed. It's about $15 for a dozen. There's also some creative kinds like the ones topped with cereal, which may delight kids. 

Also there's some vegan donuts. It seems these are on weekends only. There's some that are gluten and sugar free among other things.

A great discovery is this hip bar. 1864 Tavern is a kind of out of the way bar west of downtown. It certainly is worth getting to. Feels kind of Western but also modern. The happy hour is the best time. 

It seems like it's very casual. Just sit on a couch. There's a bar area, but the couches are more comfortable, and there's board games you can play. Good place for local original cocktails. Lots of classic ingredients with a new twist. Came in with the girl one late afternoon. We got a seat on the couch and ordered the Pahranagat Punch. It's $7 at happy hour. This is a mixture of champagne, lemon juice, mint, nutmeg, orange juice, and rye whiskey. It's both sour and sweet. This is easy to knock back, and it will get you fucked up. It's also nice to sip and enjoy the simple yet complex flavor. The other cocktails sound good but this is our favorite of the ones we've already had. 

Come here on a full stomach before drinking. It doesn't have any food. There are some close restaurants around this.

Another place in the Peppermill for overpriced eating. Cafe Milano is one of the main restaurants inside. It serves basic breakfast, lunch, and dinner items. Food is okay but the portions are small for the cost. They're always open. 

It can get pretty busy. It's one of the main dining options in the hotel. This is especially popular for breakfast with people getting things like omelets. Basic menu items. Food here isn't impressive but nothing is really bad, and some things are actually pretty good here like the fruit was fresh tasting. Always seems like it's very slow service. The prices are too high for this. Basic thing like toast is about $3 a slice, it's crazy. The breakfast entrees are about $15 and more. 

Better food options can be found outside the hotel. If you need to get something fast this isn't the place. The Chinese menu is overpriced too.

Another Reno brewery. It pretty much is okay. The Brewer's Cabinet isn't the best but not at all the worst. Has a good variety of beer and and food. Unfortunately there's high prices but this is a hipster place so of course it's a lot. 

It doesn't look much like a brewery. It looks more like a store. The name was confusing too. It was funny. The number of times we went by this. All of these times we thought it was a place to get brewing supplies and not an actual brewery. There were people outside but we thought maybe there was just a tasting or something. Finally we went in. The place was pretty busy, but that's because it's small. Among the first beers we had was the Mango Mist-ery Machine. It's $7 for a pint. This is a collaboration between IMBIB and them. It's a hazy style IPA. This was slightly hoppy and sweet. As for the food we thought it was too expensive. We decided on a pretzel because that was one of the few reasonably priced things. It's $6.95 for a pretty big one. This is served with beer cheese sauce. Also it's good with brown mustard so you can skip the cheese. The pretzel seemed kind of burnt, but it was still edible so we finished it and decided not to try any of the more expensive items because they didn't even sound like they were impressive, and we weren't paying up for it. 

Busy place so only bring a small group or only a couple. It may even then still be too crowded for everyone. The beer is terrific but the food is way expensive, and not much is vegetarian friendly either, so the food is pretty much overrated.

Batch is the best place for cupcakes. It's a small bakery in Midtown. Some items are approved for vegans. A lot of interesting flavors. They have many other kinds of treats. 

If you're looking for some healthier desserts, you can get some here. Many are made with less fat and sugar. The main thing are the cupcakes, and they have many of these. It has several that meet certain diet needs. There's varieties for gluten free, keto, and vegan. I came in and got a Chocolate Mint Cupcake. It's about $3.75 each. This kind is full of cool mint flavor. It's not a big cupcake but it packs a lot into it, so it just feels big. This isn't way too sweet, unlike many other cupcakes that are just like pure sugar. 

Come here to get cupcakes. It has many that meet diet needs. There's many that are vegan.

Cool brewery. IMBIB is one of the many east of downtown. Lots of interesting beers to choose from. Good atmosphere. There's a patio if you don't want to be inside. 

It seems like sour is a specialty here. Lots of these are on the beer menu. This isn't a bad thing. More sours are needed in this area. This is an underrated style of beer and it's different than common styles. It's refreshing to drink a sour when it's hot. Kind of like drinking a lemonade or something like that but it's hoppy too. I came with the girl the last time and we tried a few. They were all good enough to get the next time. I liked the Freshy Pow IPA. It's $6 for a pint. This is a West Coast style IPA with aromatic and bitter hops, and made with amarillo and citrus to give it a spice. Another one we liked was the Mango Mist-ery Machine. This a collaboration between The Brewer's Cabinet and them. If you like mango you should try it. This is a hazy style IPA that's hoppy and sweet. 

Has a patio which is a nice place for having a beer. It's in an area with some older homes and doesn't have a lot going on. There's no food here but there's a Jimboy's across the street, so you can get tacos from there.

Average place for basic Asian and Chinese. If you don't care much about atmosphere, that's a plus. Pho Cafe Hong Kong Diner isn't anything impressive looking but the food makes up for this. Fairly big portions for not all that much. They have Americanized or more authentic stuff. 

I can't remember exactly what I had. It was customized a bit from another item. This had tofu and vegetables. It might have been the Mixed Vegetables with tofu added. This was about $11 and the amount of food was quite a lot. It tasted fresh. This wasn't like many other cheap Chinese takeouts. Other places have everything taste frozen. The whole menu looks interesting. Good sounding drinks like boba tea which is refreshing when the weather is hot. They also have pho which is great in cold weather. It seems like there's something for any time of the year here. The authentic menu items are worth checking out. 

Also this place is open late. If you have the munchies after a big night you could call here and order something delivered to you or go there. The inside is order at the counter and then you sit and they'll bring the food to you.

Here is a nice small Mexican cantina. It seems a little more authentic than most places. Mexcal has some lighter fare if you aren't hungry for big things. Good flavors. The prices are kind of high unfortunately. 

I came with a date. It was early and we weren't excited about the high prices. There's also few things good for vegans. Of course drinks are always good. We got the Classic Margarita. It's $9 for a single glass. This is made with agave nectar, Blanco tequila, Grand Marnier, and lime juice. It has a zip to it. This is better than many margaritas, but there's not much of it, so it's gone quick. As for the food, we wanted to get tacos, but were turned off by the prices and the lack of good vegetarian choices. We settled on the Chips + Salsa. It's $7 and comes with several different kinds. There's roja, tomatillo, and verde. Roja is the common salsa, red, and mild. Tomatillo is green and mild. Verde is brown and has a citrusy kick but not spicy. It only had a little bit of each. The price was too much for it. 

Good food. It would be better if there were more tacos with no meat. The prices are kind of high so we probably won't come back and just go to Jimboys or something.

As I walked down narrow Tilton Street to join the pals I was meeting at Czerw's, I noticed a door slightly ajar, revealing stacks of fragrant wood and huge, lovely slabs of hanging bacon in the smoke room. This peek behind the scenes stoked my excitement about what was to come, and needless to say, I was not disappointed when I walked into the tiny retail room, entering a little emporium of pierogy, kielbasy, sauerkraut, bacon, and more.

The prices are extremely reasonable. The fellow manning the register was friendly and patient as he explained the various types of sausages, dispensed advice about how to cook the pierogy (they're already boiled at the store), and answered my questions about how the sauerkraut is sold (by the pound, with ziploc bags on the wall so you can help yourself) and what is in the stew they were selling that day (a very long and tantalizing list of Polish charcuterie).

Everything I've tried so far was superb. The "loaded baked potato" pierogy are sinfully good, especially as they boast bits of Czerw's own fruitwood-smoked house-cured bacon. The "Philly cheesesteak" pierogy are super--I was a little skeptical, I have to admit, but after reading all the rave Yelp reviews about them, I had to give them a try. I am so glad I did. The steak inside is flavorful and juicy, and with the provolone and onions it truly recreates that experience of a perfect cheesesteak.

I love spicy food but the "hotter than hell" hot sausage defeated me! I will probably incorporate the remaining hot sausages into a dish where their blistering hot taste can complement and be mellowed a bit by other ingredients.

The Polish "hot dogs" are way better than any hot dog I've ever eaten. Perfect just browned and steamed, and served with a little mustard and the loaded potato pierogy on the side.

Cajun kielbasa has a lovely balance of spice and the sweetness of the pork. And of course that incredible, intoxicating aroma of the fruitwood smoke brings it all together.

I will definitely be making return visits to Czerw's. What a gem!

Fantastic philly cheesesteak experience with By George! Try not to be tempted by the amazing display of pasta and carbs, and stick through the lines for the cheesesteak. I got the cheesesteak with sharp provolone and onions. It took a while to come out but wow once I bit my mouth into that sandwich, I died a little bit.

It is definitely pricier than some other places, but it's huge and they really stack on the meat. I'm the type of person that doesn't like to try the same place twice, but I'd definitely come back for more sandwiches and finally to try the pizza and pasta.

My favorite market I've been to thus far ever, even including markets in Europe! This is a must visit spot when you are in Philly and it's pretty much about killing all your food spots in one hit...if your stomach has space for it!

Come hungry and come alert. If you can, tag team with someone to try multiple vendors and also have someone to save seats if possible!

Ok.  Four words that have changed my life.  Broccoli. Chicken. Provolone. Cheesesteak.  HOLY MOTHER OF ALL THAT IS GOOD, that is one damn fine sandwich.  Get a little mayo, a little spicy mustard, and call it heaven.  Other reasons to love Lee's:  

The sandwiches are enormous and cheap as all get out.

The onion rings are perfectly crispy (and super good with that spicy mustard).

They have Diet Cherry Cola.

Their mashed potatoes and gravy are excellent comfort food.

Their carrot cake is pretty darn good.

Thank you, Lee's, for making takeout food fast, delicious, and relatively healthy feeling.

I can't speak to the food, but this was the absolute worst dining experience I've ever had. The manager was the least professional I've ever encountered in the service industry.

We were in town for a wedding and had heard rave reviews on their sister restaurant, Eat. When we called to make reservations at Eat, they were booked and sent us over to Vacherie. I made reservations for the entire wedding party (10) and sent out the information to everyone. 

On the day of the reservation, they called and confirmed the reservation leaving a voicemail. Everyone got dressed and ready, grabbed cabs and headed over to the restaurant. When we got there at our reservation time, they told us we were over an hour late so they cancelled our reservation. I played the voicemail for the manager showing her we were on time and had not missed our reservation. Instead of admitting she was wrong and accommodating us with appetizers or drinks while we waited, she insisted we must have called in and changed the reservation and that they were correct and we must not "know what were talking about". We gave her multiple opportunities to take the higher road and just accommodate us while we waited. She ended up asking us to leave the restaurant and with a very sarcastic "good luck with your wedding" 

This manager needs a course in etiquette. Needless to say we won't be going back.

If you love smothered , covered and fried... this is your place! Everything was full of just the right flavor! We actually had a buffet of choices.. fried chicken, liver, heart, pork chop, okra, and fries! The waitress was always there when we needed her and gave great recommendations. Worth the Stop !

Elaia is an amazing space and has very attentive staff.  My first visit was for brunch, and the food was delicious.  Based on the positive experience, we decided to make reservations with friends for dinner.  While we enjoyed the food, there just needed to be more of it.  I am definitely one that appreciates small portions, but even by my standards,  they were ridiculously small.  I ordered a $12 pear salad that wasn't more than a sprinkling of greens and 3 pear slivers- not slices, but slivers.  Truthfully, I don't think it was even an eighth of a pear.  The entree was very good, but again, about a 3 oz portion of meat.  For the price they charge, I would expect a little more.  
While I really did enjoy the meal, we will not be going back. There is nothing worse than leaving a meal hungry.

"Only the kind in heart can make a good soup." This humble sign hanging in the dining room symbolizes Roma Imports' passion for food. This discreet building with only an Italian flag to make it stand out is hidden in an industrial part of town past a massive Cox Communications building. It's the last place you would expect to find a family-owned Italian market with frozen homemade lasagna and imported wedges of parmigiano-reggiano.

Once I found a parking spot behind one of the white work trucks on the side of the street, I stepped in and felt immediately comforted by the aroma. Baked bread and sauces simmering with garlic tickled my nose and made my stomach growl even though I just had breakfast.

The store has one long narrow room to explore. To the right is the deli with delectables from around the world. Prosciutto (an Italian cured ham), elusive cipolline onions and freshly baked focaccia are some of the Italian goods. Spanish serrano ham, Portugese linguica sausage, and hummus made in-store are some of the other goods available. The left has a wide assortment of packaged goods such as canned San Marzano tomatoes (which taste riper in sauces) and DeCecco pasta (a premium Italian brand that stands better to reheating). Tubed tomato paste and tubed anchovies (convenient for making sauces such as puttanesca) are also available. Further into the store you'll see the heart of the store: the freezers. 

There are the Italian standards like lasagna and spaghetti. There are more adventurous items such as the goat cheese, caramelized onion and roasted red pepper quiche and the veal scaloppini. You will find a plethora of homemade sausages without any fillers or additives. There are Italian sausages, Weisswurst (Bavarian veal), and Count Dracula (a garlicky sausage with fennel). There is no room for a smoker so they imported their smoked sausages such as Andouille from a butcher in Phoenix. There are homemade Italian cookies, tiramisu, turnovers, and more meals than your freezer has room for.

One of the biggest time-savers to stock up on would be the sauces made here from scratch without added sugar. All of the ingredients are listed directly on the label for the homemade items. Knowing what you're getting even when it's homemade is a rarity that is very helpful for the nutritionally-conscious. Try asking the girl at the bake sale stand what she put in her brownies.

If you are not here to stuff your pantry, you are probably here to stuff your belly. You will have to stuff yourself into the small dining room and even share a table with a stranger if it's crowded enough. Nobody minds though. They are too focused on their sandwiches and portabella ravioli with sage butter.

Some of the things you will have trouble finding elsewhere are salted capers (essential for chicken piccata), anise oil (used for baking biscotti and pizelles), 00 flour (the Italian grade of finest-ground flour, usually used for pasta making), filleted anchovies (an addition to sauces to add umami, or savoriness) and dried porcini mushrooms. Giardiniera is also sold here in bulk. It makes a necessary addition to sandwiches and the Chicago Italian roast beef sandwich, which you need to eat before you die.

The family atmosphere helped draw me in. The cashiers always greeted me and said bye whenever I left the store. If my arms are overflowing with boxes of pasta, one of the workers will notice and rush to my aide, putting some of the items behind the cash register to be ready for me when I leave.

I haven't been here too long, I'm getting homesick.



Disclaimer: I interviewed the owner Lillian to clarify some information when I was writing about Roma for a class of mine. She gave me a free sandwich afterward. She didn't know I'd yelp about this place but I thought I would include this bit of information for fairness.

We eat here once a month or more. Barry and Rosa have owned the restaurant for a number of years and one or both are always on site. For buffet food this place is great. The buffet table is small compared to many restaurants, but that allows them to monitor the food quality. Although not a large selection, there is enough variety to have diferent tastes and textures for an interesting meal.  Nothing sits on the buffet for long periods of time like many Chinese buffets. The restaurant draws a lot or regulars who appreciate the consistancy and quality of the food. They also do a good carry out business and you can order from the menu if you prefer. Drinks are included in the price. They get 5 stars for food quality, consistancy, cleanliness, and owner attention to detail.

Over and under one of the worst places on South Street to eat Italian.  I have tried this place three times now, (since they changed ownership a few years ago).  The salad is over dressed with flavorless vinaigrette; the pasta is over cooked, over sauced and overly salty; and the pizza is undercooked despite sending it back once. When the dough near the crush is raw, there is something seriously wrong with your pizza chef.  If this appeals to you then La Fourno is your kind of place.  Only exceptional note was an extremely accommodating server but that does not make up for the crappy food.

Decided to check this place out based on yelp reviews. Looks sketchy outside but nice inside. Excellent service. Ordered the linguini... a few bites in im horrified when I realize im chewing on a foreign object!!! A Freakin Metal Wire in my linguini!!!!  Freakin Dangerous.. I could have swallowed it! Tore my back gums up pretty good. The waiter brought it to the attention of the owner and cook and told us they knew what it was and were embarrassed by it and comped our meal. As if I would have paid for metal linguini! I know accidents happen but this type of negligence is very dangerous...... Needless to say ill never return.

I love discovering new restaurants, especially ones with such hard working and passionate owners. Not to mention, to open a restaurant in the middle of a pandemic is no easy feat, so I'm writing this review in hopes that we as a community can help sustain this wonderful and may I add, delicious, Italian restaurant. I present to you: Pasta Fresca! 

Let's start off with the owner and chef of this establishment. His name is Paolo and he has an absolutely cheerful and upbeat personality. Throughout our dinner service, he would occasionally check up on us to see how everything was. He showed his funny sense of humor when we told him that we created a business page on Yelp for him, he said to make sure to leave a bad review because everyone seems to talk about negative topics more often, creating more of a buzz throughout some communities. We all laughed and we assured him with sarcasm in our voices that we'd leave the nastiest of reviews for him. Like most Italians, Paolo grew up with a fairly large family with a passion for cooking. There's an old family photo on the back right corner of the restaurant; try to guess which one is Paolo! 

With the owner of Pasta Fresca established, let's move on to the interior and most importantly, the food! It's a fairly spaced restaurant with only a few tables against the walls, probably to follow COVID-19 guidelines. In the front of the restaurant stands a display case with uncooked pasta (rigatoni, spaghetti noodles and spinach spaghetti noodles) and their sauces. If you don't want to eat in, you can purchase whatever is in the display case and make a nice meal at home. We chose to eat in and their food was spot on! 

They have a fairly simple menu which makes deciding on what to get easy if you're indecisive like me. We started off on two appetizers: the Burrata chese and the Piatto de legno. Every bite of the Burrata chese was so refreshing; plump, juicy tomatoes with burrata topped with pesto sauce. Yum! The Piatto de legno came with three cheeses, bread, and bruschetta. Definitely a fun app to get amongst friends. When it came time to order our entrees, we ordered the following: Rigatoni and Bolognese, Regular Spaghetti with Bolognese and for me, the Spinach Spaghetti with their Vodka Spicy Pink Sauce. I love me a good Bolognese sauce but my favorite was my dish with the Vodka Spicy Pink Sauce! The sauce was thick and creamy and covered every nook and cranny of the spaghetti making every bite just as satisfying as the last. The spaghetti itself was a perfect texture. I'll let my room mates review their dishes (if they ever do) but I reassure you, we all left satisfied and happy. After our plates were cleared, we finished our meal with some Cannolis! 

When my room mate first told me about a new Italian restaurant in town, I was surprised that a business would open during these tough times. But when we met the chef and owner, Paolo, it was easy to understand that if anyone could do it, it would be him. Paolo has such a positive and spunky attitude towards life, being in his presence almost makes you forget we're living in a pandemic. From what we ordered, the food was flavorful and delicious. And whether you want to eat in or stay home, you can still support Pasta Fresca either way!

I remember back in college my classmates and I would go on these deli hunts to find the "best" deli in Reno. Of course we would never be able to come to an agreement for we each had our own personal favorites. I, myself, was never a sandwich fanatic, but Manhattan Deli is my favorite Deli here in Reno. 

Last weekend, my friends and I decided to eat here for dinner. When we arrived, we were seated almost immediately and scanned through the menu. Let me warn you, the portions here are not only generous, they monstrous. I ordered a Beef Tongue & Corned Beef Double Decker, and believe me, that sandwich was HUGE! It was also very tasty. My friend ordered the Open-Faced Reuben and when the plate arrived, I thought it was just a mountain of corned beef with melted cheese rivers flowing down it. My room mate decided to go "light" and ordered the 1/2 Sandwich (chicken salad) and 1/2 cup of soup of the day, which was Tomato Basil. We also ordered a side order of Garlic Fries. It was safe to say that we had leftovers. 

Our server, Kellee, provided amazing customer service; she always made sure we were okay and her busser did a fantastic job keeping our waters filled throughout the our meal. 

We left with happy bellies and leftovers for later on. There's plenty of items I'd love to try, like their Matzoh Ball Soup and Chopped Chicken Liver for starters. Maybe I'll bring my foodie friend, Etzal, for that adventure. Stay tuned.

I was bummed that I wasn't able to attend the Yelp Elite event that Maya's was hosting due to scheduling. So my room mate and I decided to come ourselves for lunch! 

Maya's South Indian Cuisine share their restaurant space with Thali and past the back doorway leads to the shared dining area for The Pizza Collective and The DeLuxe. At the time of our visit, there was a jazz band playing, but since it was our first time eating here, we decided to sit in the restaurant. However, they left the backdoor open so we were able to enjoy the music from the comfort of our seats. 

Their menu is very simple and excluding their combination platters, everything is less than $10! All of the items are vegan friendly, made with organic ingredients and most items are gluten free. We decided to order one combination platter (any 3 items) and an entree of Poori (fried Indian bread) & Potato Masala. Since we were first timers, the young lady assisting us, gave us her recommendations of her favorites and a brief explanation of each dish.
