She also explained how the serving trays worked and even gave us a sample of the Sanbar Soup. She was so helpful and made us feel right at home. For our combination platter, we ended up ordering the Masala Dosa, mini Idli and the Kuzhi Paniyaram. 

With the open kitchen we watched as they were hard at work cooking and prepping other dishes. Soon enough our silver trays arrived and after another brief explanation, we began our meal! 

We could easily taste the quality put in these dishes. The sauces from left to right were: Sambar, Coconut chutney, and tomato chutney. My favorite was the Sambar and paired very well with Poori. My room mate on the other hand savored the tomato chutney. Everything was so tasty, so much so that we both wiped our trays clean. Not a single crumb remained. 

Maya's South Indian Cuisine went beyond all expectations. Service was informative and friendly, the food was outstanding, and the experience as a whole was one we would not soon forget.

I love Bertha's. We used to always come here for our Mexican cravings. 

If there's two things I value at restaurants, it would have to be the service followed by consistency. Don't get me wrong, I definitely don't mind change; change can be good! 

Anyways Bertha's food is always delicious. My room mates ordered The Hat and Chili Relleno Special with beef. The Hat is basically a taco salad served in a crunchy tortilla bowl. I ordered the Chili Relleno Special Nogada Style. From the menu description it's a Chili Relleno cooked with chicken and almonds. Also when choosing from corn or flour tortillas, I always advise to go with the flour tortillas; they're homemade! 

The Hat was bite after bite of freshness! I can tell you I love both versions of their Chili Relleno. Lately I've been always ordering their Nogada Style Relleno because I just love how it tastes! The slight crunch of the almonds also adds a bit of flavor too. All dishes were accompanied with beans and rice...except for that one of my room mates ordered all rice. 

Towards the end of our dinner service I noticed the restaurant did seem to be slowly filling up. Our server told us she would be right back with our check. Unfortunately we didn't receive our check until about half an hour to 45 minutes later. Understandably, the restaurant was full, but we couldn't find any servers throughout that time. I don't mind waiting, but it felt like we were forgotten. I could understand if we were waiting for our food, but we were only waiting for our check. 

Bertha's consistently serves delicious food, but their service could use some improvement. We'll always be back, but hopefully with a shorter wait time.

[10.12.18] 7th Annual Reno Bites Restaurant Week

Sierra St Kitchen & Cocktails was another restaurant I've been wanting to dine at for some time now. Fortunately, about a week ago, my room mate and I decided to try out their Reno Bites Special and man, it was such a great experience.

When we first entered the restaurant, it was packed. We should have known better and made a reservation; noted for the next time we plan to eat here. We were told that the wait time would be at least 45 min to an hour. We did notice some of our friends sitting at the bar, and they mentioned there was two free seats towards the far end. When we asked  if we could sit there, he gladly nodded and showed us to our seats. Observing the restaurant, it was a small and cozy space making a seemingly packed restaurant very crowded. However, this wasn't case for Sierra St Kitchen & Cocktails. Even with every table occupied with hungry people, the energy throughout the restaurant was lively and just fun to experience. 

Sitting at the bar, it was only natural that the bartender managing the bar would be the one to help us. Even though he was busy fulfilling with what seemed like an infinite amount of drink orders, he always made sure to check up on us and took our order shortly after we looked through the menu. 

As mentioned before, both my room mate and I decided to try and experience their Reno Bites Special, which was a three course dinner special. Now, if you didn't know, Sierra St Kitchen & Cocktails are affiliated with Skyline Kitchen and Vine. Both of their Reno Bites Special menus shared very similar item selections, and Pan-Seared Swordfish was one of them! I think you already know what I'm ordering. Just like Skyline Kitchen and Vine, the three course dinner comes with a drink. For Sierra St Kitchen's Reno Bites Special, you could choose from a Beet Salad, Bruschetta or Caeser Salad for an appetizer; Pan-Seared Swordfish, Seared Scallops or Linguine Aglio e Olio for the main entree and a Lemon Panna Cotta for dessert. The bartender told us in advanced that they ran out of the featured dessert, so we could choose from their dessert selections as a substitute. 

My room mate ordered a glass of wine, Caeser Salad, the Linguine Aglio e Olio and Crème Brulee for dessert. I ordered the Uinta, Dubhe, Imperial Black IPA, Bruschetta, Pan-Seared Swordfish (surprise!), and the Chocolate Decadence for dessert. The Caeser Salad was refreshing and tasted similar to that of Skyline Kitchen; no surprise there. My room mate mentioned that the Linuine Aglio e Olio was a little bland to her liking, but still good regardless. She absolutely loved her Crème Brulee. Creamy, custardy and crispy at the top. For my dinner, the Bruschetta was also refreshing. The Pan-Seared Swordfish was absolutely delicious. The best way to describe the swordfish itself was that I could definitely tell this was from the ocean, but it wasn't fishy at all. The fish was well seasoned, and the flavors from the squash & sweet potato puree and persimmon-cranberry relish melded so well with each other. I'm so glad that Sierra St Kitchen had this on their menu. Lastly, the Chocolate Decadence was a sweet way to end dinner. It was very rich, but portioned perfectly to where it was the perfect amount. The few blueberries presented with it gave a nice second layer of diversity and sweetness. 

I loved my dinner experience at Sierra St Kitchen and I'm sure my room mate did as well. The vibe, service and food were all exceptional and I'd definitely want to visit during their regular hours to try out more of their small plates.

We've heard great things about Mario's Portofino and after our visit, I can definitely agree and give my own praise about this restaurant. 

Right as you walk through the front doors, there is a coat rack to hang any unwanted outerwear during your meal service. We seated very shortly after entering. Our server, Pepe, was such a friendly and really down to earth guy. Throughout our meal service he would always make sure we were well taken care of. He also had a great sense of humor. 

After our bread service, Pepe came back to take our order. After giving us his recommendations, my room mates ordered the Linguine Corleone, Pollo Marsala, and for me, the Bistecca Di Calamari. 

Before the food arrived, we realized that it was 8:25pm. We didn't realized it, but we came an hour before the restaurant closed. We apologized to Pepe and asked for take out boxes, but he told us that there was no rush. Instead, we enjoyed our meal with haste! Everything tasted fantastic. I loved their calamari steak; it was a generous piece and tasted great with the sun dried tomatoes. The Linguine Corleone had a lighter flavor and their shrimp were tender and juicy. The mushroom wine sauce for the Pollo Marsala had so much flavor. It was probably my favorite of the night! 

The food was amazing and reasonably priced. The service was exceptional. Pepe made us feel welcomed and seemed to really enjoy his job. Granted this was our first visit, but with Mario's only being such a short drive from where we live, I can say with confidence that it won't be our last.

2-D Wok has been on my "Go-To" list for a while now and I was finally able to dine here for both lunch and dinner. And I must say, both times did not disappoint! 

Right behind Black Bear Diner, you'll find 2-D Wok with other shops and restaurants within that small shopping center. It doesn't look like much from the outside, but once you enter through their front door, you'll smell the delicious aromas from their kitchen.  

If you eat during their lunch hours, I recommend ordering from their Lunch Bento section, which is served from 11AM to 3PM. Each bento is served in a beautifully presented box and comes with steamed rice, soup of the day, sweet potato fries, mixed veggies, daikon radish, and red stewed tofu and egg. During our lunch visit, we ordered the Fried Pork Filet Bento and the Roasted Pork Belly Bento. The fried pork was crispy and well seasoned. The roasted pork belly was tender and juicy. Accompanied with everything the bento had to offer, this made for a perfect meal. 

During our dinner visit, we ordered the Scallion Oil Chicken, the Hakka Stir-fry and the Taiwanese Sausage Fried Rice. Back home, my mom would usually prepare her Cold Ginger Chicken dish and that's what their Scallion Oil Chicken reminded me of! The only difference was that the Scallion Oil Chicken was warm, which in my honest opinion, I preferred more. (sorry mom!) The Hakka Stir-fry had chicken, celery, squid, carrots, tofu, and other various ingredients. It was very tasty and even had a nice spicy kick to it. Their fried rice was simple and delicious. I loved the lap cheong slices as well as the crunch from the green onions. Paired well with the other two dishes we ordered. 

The service was exceptional and equally friendly. Now that I tried 2-D Wok for myself, I can't wait to bring my other foodie friends here. I'm sure they'll love it as much as I do.

I've been living in Reno for just over 7 years and I had no idea that locals get 50% off...yes 50% off of the Carvings Buffet!! If I had known that, I'd probably come here once a week! I'm only half joking. But yes what an amazing deal! 

The Carvings Buffet is located on the second floor of Harrah's Reno Hotel and Casino. With our local's discount, we paid about $11 each. And that was on a Sunday evening for dinner! 

After we were seated, we were all hungry so we went our separate ways to gather our bearings. I personally like to scope everything out before piling copious amounts of food onto my plate. 

I noticed about seven food stations. The few stations I stopped by were the Asian, American, and Carving stations. For my first round, I grabbed some Sweet & Sour Chicken, a fillet of their Catch of the Day, steamed vegetables, an egg roll and a piece of Sake Nigiri. Honestly their sushi didn't look too appetizing, but I had to at least try a piece. Everything but the sushi was delicious. Their sushi had an abundance of rice and the fish was very soggy. Not my favorite. 

For both my second and third rounds, I stopped by the Carving Station and got a slice of their prime rib with creamy horse radish and cranberry sauce. I love prime rib and they did not disappoint. I didn't leave any room for dessert, but their pastries on display looked cute.

All together, The Carvings Buffet was a delicious experience. It's not the best buffet I've had, but for the price we paid, I am not complaining. Whether or not you're a local, The Carvings Buffet will fulfill your hunger cravings while keeping your wallet very happy.

1.29.19 After I finished work, I thought it'd be a great idea to find somewhere to enjoy happy hour. After much thought, we chose Washoe Public House to which they did not disappoint. 

Their happy hour runs from Monday through Friday 4-6pm. Their "Small Plates" are only $5, all draft beers and well drinks are half off, there is a seasonal happy hour cocktail, and there's a wine by the bottle special. 

I was in it for the food, so with that being said, we ordered their Wagyu Bulgogi Lettuce Cups, Cavatapi Mac and Cheese, and Sticky Thai Chicken Wings. We tried to order their Scotch Eggs, but unfortunately, they were out of that. Ahh there's always next time. The Wagyu Bulgogi Lettuce Cups had kimchi cucumbers and topped with puffed rice noodles. It was a light bite with a slight kick from the kimchi cucumbers. Their mac and cheese was probably the most filling of the "Small Bites" and definitely worth getting. With it having Jack, cheddar and smoked gouda, each bite was cheesy and gratifying. Lastly the Sticky Thai Chickens were my favorite out of the three. They weren't spicy at all, in fact they were more sweet if anything. There was a slight tang, but sweetness was the dominant flavor. It was slightly crispy on the outside and moist on the inside. The green onions that were sprinkled on gave a subtle, extra kick. 

We were still feeling hungry after all of that and stayed in for dinner. Might as well right? Their dinner menu had a lot of appetizing entrees making it difficult to choose from. But then I remembered that time I attended the Yelpstronomy - Carnival of Culinary Curiosity Yelp Elite Event. My favorite sample from that night was Washoe Public House's Rock Candy Short Ribs. I definitely remember going up and getting seconds...maybe thirds it was that good. So I decided that we were to share and order just that, their Rock Candy Short Ribs. Since we were going to share it, we asked our server for an extra plate. When he returned to our table, he brought back two plated dishes explaining to us that he had split the entree for us. Now that's top notch service. We were both grateful and impressed. Our short ribs were served with salted marble potatoes and topped with carrot chips. Each bite was just as I remembered it; tender, savory and sweet. Even with our entrees split for us, they were pretty filling. That or our appetizers were catching up to us. Regardless everything was delicious. 

Most people will think of drinks when they hear the words "happy hour". But being the foodie I am, I always look out for the food specials, and Washoe Public House has a pretty extensive happy hour food specials list. And if you decide to dine in for dinner, their dinner menu won't disappoint you either. Service was friendly and exceptional. I'm still bummed about them being out of their Scotch Eggs, but I guess that's an excuse for me to come back for another happy hour!

It's been awhile since I've eaten here at 101 Taiwanese Cuisine. I was meeting a good friend of mine for dinner and this would be the first time in over a year  that we've seen each other since I graduated. This reunion, you could say, was long overdue! 

My buddy recommended we eat here for three main reasons; it was a casual setting, their food tasted good, and they served boba tea! I would love to share all of the stories we talked about during our dinner, but I'll just say that we picked up as if we just spoke yesterday. Those are friends you want to hold on to. [Life tip] 

For dinner, my friend ordered the Pineapple Shrimp Ball appetizers, Taro Milk Tea and the Popcorn Chicken Rice Box. I ordered the Fried Pork Cutlet Rice Box. After ordering, my friend was trying to describe the appetizer dish, saying they put sprinkles on their shrimp. Of course, I thought he meant they "sprinkled" spice flakes or some type of flake. But to my surprise, when the Pineapple Shrimp Ball appetizers arrived to our table, I realized he literally meant sprinkles. I didn't know whether or not this was an appetizer or dessert. After taking a bite, I gave a small golf clap. The glaze was sweet and the shrimp...crispy! Shortly after our entrees arrived.  

Meat aside, I have to say the Popcorn Chicken and Fried Pork Cutlet were both seasoned very well. When I think of Pork Cutlet, I think of a wet glaze or gravy, however the flavor came from the dry rub. The bento boxes included braised pork rice, simmered egg, sweet radish and some other side dishes. Everything melded so well together; different flavors were emanating from the diverse spread of side dishes and when eaten together, painted a perfect picture. Not to mention their prices are so affordable! 

Not only was it nice to see my bud again, but our dinner service was tasty and fulfilling. Their menu has so much more to offer and I want to try them all. Whether you're visiting for a quick boba milk tea for this summer heat or dining in for a flavor packed dinner, Taiwanese 101 will not disappoint.

Amazing steak at a reasonable price? Yeah, I'm sold! We heard great things about Ruby River Steakhouse from a couple of our friends and we just so happened to be in the mood for steak! 

Ruby River Steakhouse is located across the street from the Peppermill Resort. You can't miss them with their roadside sign either! Once you walk through their doors you'll be greeted with a large barrel of peanuts. They're not just for show either. You can help yourself to a scoop or two while you're waiting for your table, that is, if you need to wait for your table. Luckily for us, we were shown to our table almost immediately after entering the restaurant. 

Their decor reminded me of the Rodeo and took me back to when the Reno Rodeo was in town. The first thing I noticed on our table were two beer bottles. When lifting one of them up did I realize that they were actually salt and pepper shakers; how creative! 

Our server, Dylan, did such an amazing job. It was such a smooth dinner service. When he first came by to take our food orders, we knew exactly what we were getting. For appetizers, we ordered the Build Your Own Sampler. Our three choices were the Artichoke Dip, the Steak & Avocado Eggrolls and the Browning Onion. For our entrees my friends ordered the Peppered Bacon Sirloin and the 12 oz Ribeye. For me I had to get their 10 oz Prime Rib.  

The Build Your Own Sampler arrived shortly after and it looked like a complete masterpiece. That in itself could be a meal on its own. The artichoke dip was paired with Parmesan bread for a simply satisfying bite. The steak and avocado egg rolls, when dipped in their cilantro ranch, made each one of us look at each other with a nod of approval. Lastly, the browning onion with their River Sauce was my favorite of the three. Every bite was crispy and their sauce had a creamy and smoky aftertaste. 

When our food arrived, I sampled a couple pieces from both of my friends' steaks and they were well seasoned, especially the Ribeye. I absolutely loved my Prime Rib. The tastes of the au jus and grated horse radish blended well with every bite of the prime rib. Out of all the side dishes the Jacketed Baked Potato was the most impressive. That thing was Loaded! 

With such a pleasant ambiance, excellent service, and delicious tasting steaks at such a reasonable cost, you can't help but fall in love with this place! Okay, maybe that was a bit too much, but their steaks are really good. Go check it out for yourselves!

Honey Bakery...A hidden gem for sure! Once we found out about Honey Bakery, we could not stop coming back. One week we visited Honey Bakery for three days straight. We just couldn't get enough of them.

We only stumbled upon this place by shear luck when we were trying to look for a cake for our friend's birthday. Of course we were searching for bakeries on Yelp and Honey Bakery popped up. And although they do have cake options to order from, they're not just a bakery that serves sweets. We were surprised to see some dim sum and a variety of buns being advertised and displayed in their display case. I just wanted to start off by saying, that everything we've had here tasted amazing. Their buns are tasty and so affordable. When it comes to their dim sum, they prepare them in house. If you order, lets say one order of Shrimp Siu Mai (16 pieces), they'll offer to steam it for you. It takes about 10-15 minutes for them to do so, but boy is it worth the wait. Their dim sum are probably the freshest dim sum I've had in Reno, at least that I've tried so far. They do have limited options, but for what they have, I am not complaining one bit. If you're in a hurry, I would call in a pick up order to avoid the wait. Honey Bakery also serves boba which would be perfect during the summer season.

Throughout our visits, we tried their Chicken & Mushroom Buns, Teriyaki Chicken Buns, Curry Chicken Buns, Creamy Milk Buns, Sticky Rice, Shrimp Siu Mai, Shrimp Dumplings, and their Rice Noodle with Black Bean Sparerib. My personal favorites? For their buns, I'd have to go with their Chicken & Mushroom Buns and Curry Chicken Buns. An order of Shrimp Dumplings comes with 9 pieces, but my room mate and I would devour them in one sitting leaving none for leftovers. An order of Shrimp Siu Mai comes with 16 pieces, and even with that, we were still able to finish. It's that good. Their Rice noodle with black bean spareribs are not to mess with either. Everything is delicious. 

From the looks of it, this small family-owned business may not seem like much. But through an accidental find, we discovered that Honey Bakery has so much to offer. From refreshing boba drinks and beautifully crafted cakes, to deliciously filled buns and freshly steamed dim sum, you can't really go wrong with whatever you order. As I said before, Honey Bakery is a hidden gem, and I'm very glad we were able to find it.

As Christina G and Nina S have yelped, we were all here Saturday night. I didn't partake in the pork tacos or chicken fajitas, but I had my shrimp fajitas and loved them. So much, in fact, that I took the boyfriend back tonight and ordered the same thing.

Unlike Christina, he was brave enough to try the super spicy sauce from the back. He was sweaty from it. 

We took tequila with us this time, and tried two different margarita mixes. The first: cherry, orange, and lime blend tasted like fresh squeezed juices and was just sweet enough. The latter, pomegranate, was great initially, but a bit too sweet after a glass or so.

Because my boyfriend is obsessed with tres leches, he order that for dessert, and it was the best I've ever tried, I think. He also ordered a Mexican Coffee and enjoyed it.

This isn't a fancy joint, but the food is yummy and it can fit you and all your friends at once.

I'm nearly in a sushi coma. I scarfed down way too much, and I don't regret a bite of it. I've recently been concerned that I was losing my taste for sushi, or that there were no longer restaurants that could appease me. 

After a long night of Pilates and shopping, I came home starving with no desire to cook. I hopped on grub hub and saw that Kabuki had recently opened up AND has five stars on yelp. 

Spending a few extra dollars on my meal was work every penny. The fish is fresh, rice perfectly seasoned, and delivery was speedy and amiable.  I wish I had taken photos of the rolls, but I was seriously famished. 

I've found my new go-to. Keep it up, Kabuki. Don't let me down.

Usually I'll write something lengthy, but this place does not require much as it did not "give" me much to write about!

Pros: Fast service
           Friendly staff
           Good customer service
            The food was pretty
            The potatoes were good! 

Cons: -NOT ENOUGH CRAB IN THE FULL ORDER
              -I should have gotten 2 clusters. The second one only had two legs on it....THEY PUT THE BIGGER ON TOP!!....DECEITFULL
              
               - The clusters were SMALLLLL with little or no   meat inside!
                 - the corn was SOGGY...like extremely SOGGY
                  - The fried smoked sausage was OVERCOOKED to the point it was almost inedible
                  - For $26.50, there should have been way more shrimp!! I had maybe 5pcs‍
                   - The overall taste was about a 4 on a scale of 1-10! The crab was not fresh at all! It taste like it was microwaved!
                   -And last, but certainly NOT LEAST.....I HAD TO MAKE MY OWN DRAWN BUTTER WHEN I GOT HOME!!! Did not come with butter on the side at all! It was some butter at the bottom of the box, but not enough to dip my crab or shrimp!


I waited a long time to eat here and was sadly disappointed! I will NEVER get crab from here again, but I will try the exotic wings IF I choose to return‍

I would never write such a review unless it's a serious matter. Thus, hoping to reach management.

I visited this establishment Saturday, October 30th at ~11:30pm. Long story short, my friend and I were verbally harassed by the cashier guy, named Andrew. The pizza maker, Ari witnessed it all including other customers standing in line behind us.

We requested to order a whole pizza. During this time Andrew angrily gave attitude, made a big ordeal over the simple ask, and told us it would cost $50 plus a mandatory $15 tip. 

So he angrily asked us to hurry up and to make a decision saying, "What do you want?!"
We politely decided to go with a whole pizza & asked for half cheese and half Hawaiian. Angrily he responded, "we don't do Hawaiian!" And so we chose half pepperoni and half cheese. We were quick to give him a credit card to pay the $50 pizza and $15 tip in cash with no hesitation.

Although, in the back of our minds we didn't feel that this whole transaction was right. I was literally dumbfounded by his demeanor and wondered if we did anything wrong by ordering a whole pie at a pizza joint? And because we were in shock we just kept our mouth shut and waited for our pizza.

While waiting, it just so happened that a guy was walking out with a whole pizza. So I curiously asked him how much he paid in tip. In reply he said, "$10". 

At that point I realized that Andrew was just arbitrarily demanding tip and decided to take advantage of two little Asian females.

We are absolutely appalled by this type of behavior and do not appreciate Andrew's treatment towards us. We hope that this matter is taken seriously and corrected in due course.

This is a pretty cool place- it's owned by the former owner of Kingfisher. I love New Orleans and anything of that vein, so this is right up my alley. 

The food was very good- I enjoyed everything I tried. We had the Fresh Gulf Oysters (7$) which had a smokey tomato type flavor- super good- you get 4 decent sized oysters for the price. I usually prefer raw oysters sans the fancy toppings, but this stuff managed to compliment the oysters and still keep everything fresh tasting. 

The Pimpinadas (9$) were different..still not sure if all the flavors actually complimented each other, but I liked the idea. These are empanadads, stuffed with jerk chicken, covered with peach marmalade, topped with fried plantains, with a side of jicama slaw. I like all these things..maybe just not together. Fun dish to try out though. 

We also had the Hot legs le'jean (8$) which are frog legs with a horseradish rub, wrapped in bacon, and covered in a remoulade. Very yum. 

There are so many other things on their menu that I would love to try, so we will definitely be back. They have rotating daily specials  that looked really nice and their cocktails looked sooo nice. They also have a very cool beer selection- lots to try out. Some cool local (LA local) ones like Abita and Andygator which we love.

5 stars for the most unbelievably awkward and poor service I have ever had in a restaurant. 

We came with 4 people to sit outside and enjoy the warm weather and the live band. The waitress was out of it. Beyond out of it...... 

 Every time she came to the table she was confused and even before we ordered she kept attempting to take our menus away (like obsessively), even though we asked many times for her to leave them as we were sill deciding. She took our drink order and came back with a full tray, which was dropped in super slow motion over two people in our party. Literally slow motion, as in everyone at the table could see what was happening and yet the waitress somehow did not and had zero reaction. We were in a  good mood and didn't get angry, but it was a nasty sticky mess as they were cocktails. We had to move our own items from the wet table to another table without assistance from the waitress. I think she thought we should stay at the same table?? She did not clean the broken glass or sticky mess from under the original table for the entire duration of our time there. We were worried once it got dark that someone was going to get hurt, but still, it never got cleaned. She also commented that she got her arm sticky, but did not comment on the fact that full cocktails had been split over the laps of two people. 

I joked that the round of drinks should be on the house- she laughed, but of course we got charged full price. 

She then brought new drinks, took our appetizer order and we waited. 20 minutes later she walks by, tries to take the menus again, and asks if we want to eat. We say...umm...yah, we ordered 20 minutes ago..she had no memory of this, so we reordered. The food came pretty quickly..we had the chorizo stuffed dates for 6$ on happy hour, and the Monterrey crab cakes, also 6$ HH price. While both were fine, the normal price is $12 which is much too high, especially for tiny pieces of chorizo they bring out. Barely enough for one, forget sharing. The waitress had some serious confusion about side plates for the crab cakes, really awkward again. Also, tried to take the menus for the umpteenth time,. even though we hadn't put our entree orders in yet. Which we kept explaining over and over..

While we are eating the server comes back and tries to remove my drink from the table, even though there is clearly 1/4 left. She also tries to clear a plate that someone was eating off of. Strange.

For mains we had the  quesadilla with chicken breast, grilled mushrooms and onions (HH 4.5$) which I thought would be tasty, but instead I ate one piece and left the rest because it tasted of nothing. The salsa was not flavorful either. There were also two orders of fish tacos ( I cannot remember the price, not on HH) which came with a side of rice. One person did not touch the plate because it was so bad, the other ate it because they were hungry, but said it also had zero flavor. I tasted it and agreed completely. Like so bland that even adding salt didn't help. The shrimp scampi was apparently good (not on HH), because the person who ordered it enjoyed it...so there's one positive.

The server came over and saw that the fish and quesadillas had not been touched and asked if we had enjoyed our meals. None of us are mean angry people, so we said things like, "umm not really...it didn't have too much flavor." She didn't seem concerned that there were entire meals left uneaten. The person who ordered the fish tacos didn't even want to take them home they were that bad. I took mine home for my pets :)

The happy hour prices are not great- most beers are still 5$ a pint which is a lot. The food on the happy hour menu was also half off, but even so prices were too high for what we had. Our bill, for 3 drinks, and appetizer, a HH quesadilla and fish tacos was $42. For that amount of money I want to enjoy my meal. 

Also, while we did come to enjoy the band. and they were very good, they played so loud we could not speak at all..we had to yell to say anything which isn't really pleasant. I was also excited to come here to see the shops...but there didn't seem to be much going on. Only one or two that were actually being used. 

Overall it was a totally strange and surreal experience . We all left saying..."What just happened!?"

Watermelon Margaritas!!!! They've got them some fresh watermelon and will serve it up any which way you can think of. Perfect for a hot day- take it out the patio. 

I wish I had more time..I would have ordered like 10 of these things. Think light Jolly Rancher flavors with a dash of Tajin fruit spice on the rim.

My fave sandwich is still Korean BBQ Cheesesteak, but now my fave fries are Garlic Parmesan Cheese Fries (though I ask for less cheese because of my lactose sensitivity). 

Regarding portions: If two of us each order our own sandwich and share a small order of fries, it's already pretty filling. I have shared a large portion of fries between 2-3 people when we got our own sandwiches...probably too much food for 2, but better for 3. 

And since they introduced me to Carrot Cake Man, I always order it when I go and ask them to microwave it on the spot. If I ever change my order from these 3 things, maybe I'll update my review again, ha.

We always searching for a good Chinese restaurant. This is not it. When we first moved to Lakeview we tried Ming's and the food was mediocre. We thought to try it again and we are very disappointed. The Mongolian Beef was disgusting not edible. Thinking of getting back in my car and bring it back. I do not recommend this restaurant at all.

I don't want to be rude, but this is probably the worst poke I've ever had. 

Pricing isn't too bad compared to Poke King, but it is definitely overpriced compared to poke places in Vegas, the Bay, Seattle, LA, etc. The food itself definitely was not worth the price either. The scoops of fish are pretty small and I only got about 4-6 cubes per protein.

Speaking of protein, I have never seen a poke place that offers steak or chicken as a protein. To me, you can get that at Chipotle or Qdoba, and that shouldn't be offered at a poke restaurant, a type of restaurant that specializes in raw fish. Also, the fish didn't seem to be that fresh either.

Another con is that one of their proteins is the shredded crab meat that every other single poke place I've gone to offers as a topping, FOR FREE. If you wanted to add the crab, they would charge $2.25. They also charge $1 for seaweed salad which is also a first for me, since poke places usually don't charge for that either, unless you ask for extra or more seaweed salad.

So I ordered a poke bowl and the employee who put all my toppings and sauces on didn't seem to care about cleanliness or cross contamination. Since I had to pay an extra $1 for seaweed salad, I asked for extra and she gave me a good amount but some of the salad spilled onto the in between place between the containers holding the different toppings and she used the same tongs to grab the spilled salad and throw it back into the seaweed salad container. 

Moving on, when she proceeded to put on the tempura crunch, roasted garlic, fried onions, and roasted sesame seeds, she put her entire hand in the containers and took a handful to put on the bowl and then used that same hand that still has some residue from the previous container to dunk it into the next container to do the same thing. That especially stressed me out since I know that some people have certain allergies and doing things in that manner could cause someone to have a serious reaction because of that cross contamination.

I think the employers need to train their employees better on what to do if there's a spill and implement better ways to put toppings onto the bowls. When something spills, get a napkin or a sanitary rag to clean up the spillage and remove what was spilled, don't put it back in the container. And also, maybe use a spoon or tongs to sprinkle the toppings next time.

Another major fault was that they put the sauces all over the bowl, rather than mixing it into the protein in a separate container. I got my bowl to go and when I was eating it at home, all I could taste was the sauce all over my salad and rice. The sauce was so intense that my crispy wonton strips were soggy and were no longer crispy.

I enjoy the fact that they have more options compared to poke king, but the execution is lacking entirely. A lot of poke places do things alike and offer similar proteins and toppings and sauces, but it's like that for a reason. All these poke places mix their proteins in sauce separately for a reason. I get that Finbomb is trying to have staying power and is trying to be unique, but it's not working out and the taste ends up being compromised.

Went on a Sunday afternoon.  The brunch menu was short and full of classic brunchy dishes at reasonable brunch prices.  "Small plates" does mean small though, you might want to get a side with that french toast.  I recommend the grits because they make GREAT grits (is it weird to get excited about grits?)  Service was a little slow, which wasn't really a problem except I kept finding the bottom of my $10 bottomless mimosa.

I wasn't sure what to expect from the rest of the place, having never been to a clothing-optional club.  I was impressed!  The bartenders are topless and waxed and oiled and beautiful.  The pool area was full of people in various states of undress, mostly minding their own business or chatting at the bar.  There was some europop style music going in the background but nothing instrusively loud.

Even if you didn't plan on going for a swim, you might as well check it out because you don't need a suit and clean towels are only $1.  Just borrow some sunscreen, OK?

Went here on recommendation of a friend who read about this place in Imbibe magazine.  It was described to me as Cure if Cure served barbecue.  With further research I heard that they recently announced the installation of an erotic photo-hunt machine at the bar.  So now I'm thinking Cure plus Corporation.  I want to go... but will I ever leave?!

It is as good as it sounds.  There's a pool table and a pretty good jukebox with room to grow (highlights: Weezer, Bob Dylan, Sinatra, Crunk Hits Vol 2).  They have a solid selection of liquors, nothing as exotic as Cure but nothing real cheap either.  Three taps for beer as well as bottles.

They had four cocktails up on the chalkboard, all less than $8 and featuring some pretty complex flavors.  I liked the Juarez and had seconds of the namesake 12 Mile Limit, which blends vodka, rye, and pomegranate among others.

They stop serving food at ten but the owner, who was chilling at the bar with the patrons, had no problem with us ordering something in for delivery.  This place is definitely good people!  I'm excited to come back here and watch this place grow into a classic neighborhood hangout.

If you love to eat, you will love it here. Come hungry, but not hangry. You could probably spend days here and still not finish all the stuff that you want to try. 

The best strategy is to come as a team. These are the roles of each teammate. Without them, you will not have the best experience that you possibly can have:

1. The hunter of seats - must be strong and able to hold their ground. You may have multiple members on this team. Their main lines are, "You can't sit with us" or "Sorry, this seat is taken, and that one too" 
2. The hunter of food - must be a wise decision maker and have great rationing skills as you will be the ones gathering and feeding the troops. Again, you may have multiple members in this team if you want to take down all targets of food in the building.
3. The hunter of dessert - must be fast, but not too fast (you gotta make it back to the fort before everyone finishes their food because you can't get full on dessert only. Bonus if you can get everything back unmelted. 
4. The time manager - if you drove here, more than likely, you're parked at a paid meter. Your job is to make sure all teams complete their tasks in a timely manner and you return to your vehicle before the time runs out.
*This role may be combined with any roles above. 

If you master all these roles, you will have a successful meal. May the odds be ever in your favor, tributes. Let the games begin!

We stumbled across this place while exploring the Marigny District of New Orleans. It was late and we were pretty darn hungry. Luckily Yelp led us here. We didn't know we wanted sausages but after we finished, I could have sworn we had had a craving for it.

FOOD (4 stars):
----------------
You must get the **Crawfish Etouffee Fries**, no way around it. They are just too good! Imagine: fully loaded potatoes just soaking up all that crawfish flavor. Mmm! 

The **Guinness Special** is an Irish Guinness sausage, andouille sauce, onions, shredded cheddar cheese, bacon, and yellow mustard. It sounded so appealing but ended up just being average. Exactly what you'd expect.

However, the winner in the sausage department was the **Alligator Sausage**! I was a little surprised since I just ordered it on a whim and to say we'd tried it while in NOLA. It's super flavorful on its own and didn't even need much sauce. Definitely preferred this to the Guinness Special. Winner winner, alligator dinner!

SERVICE/AMBIANCE (4 stars):
-------------------------------
Really chill vibe about this place. The whole Marigny district is this way in fact, so it's nice to sit upstairs by the balcony and people watch down onto the street. Upstairs there's a bar and an ultra zen Chewbacca, so go check him out. Servers were really chill as well and accommodating. Good experience overall.

TIP: Will meet all your sausage cravings.

DATE TIP: Check your date's adventurousness (or lack thereof). Put them to the test -- the power of the Gator sausage!

Trattoriia Pasquale is a small neighborhood spot in a strip center on Manahatten Ave. If you are familiar with Hoyes Pharmacy then you know right where it is. They reside in the same strip. This humble restaurant is small with only a handful of tables. I suggest making a reservation, as it fills up fast. Space is tight and atmosphere loud. 

I have been here several times over the years. It's not my fave Italian restaurant, yet I always look forward to coming. Not one I would suggest but will gladly come to. Last night I arrived with a group of five for one of their monthly dinners that they call Big Night. Each month they feature a different region of Italy and highlight its food and culture by offering a region-specific 7 course meal. Last night was the Feast of Seven Fishes. This was my favorite one that I have been too. Our courses were Scallops over arugula, lobster bisque, shrimp risotto, anchovy pasta, salmon with an arugula pesto, misto and tiramisu. My faves were the scallop and the salmon. First because they were delicious and second because we got a nice piece of protein. 

On other occasions my meals have been good. I'd give them a strong 3.5. - 4. 

The owner/chef is passionate about Italy and cooking. Everything is made in-house with lots of love. He has a great gregarious demeanor. Staff is friendly. 

I like that this is a BYOB restaurant with no corkage fee. Hats off to them. Salute.

Not a huge fan of Chipotle. This is my go-to location for the 2 times a year I may come here. Same service each and every time. The associates are robots. No smile. No emotion. Just performing a task in an assembly line. I will say they work the line quickly. Tonight I ordered the new carne asada bowl. A plus is that you may customize your order making it as healthy, carb low/high , protein high/low, etc as you want. As expected a disappointment for me. I find the food flavorless and highly overrated. Was ubering home and in a hurry . Just not a fast food chick unless it's the Poke spot. In addition , the place was extremely unkept. See my photos. All napkin dispensers were empty , Tabasco bottles empty and food everywhere . They were not busy .

Liked the vibe here. Busting with energy. It starts to run through your bones. Last minute decision to come here and so glad we did. Was happy we were seated immediately without a reservation at 730/8 on a Friday night. 

They have a large bar, high tops, low tops and booth seating. Server was quick, friendly and efficient. 

Expansive menu so will definitely find something to please all. On my plate for the evening,  one of the specials , trout topped with fresh spinach, tomatoes and onions. This was definitely a good choice. I so enjoyed the textures and flavors. The beef and pork meatballs with spicy pomodoro sauce were tasty. I always like a kick. The arugula,  prosciutto and watermelon salad with a honey balsamic dressing was bursting with strong delicious flavors that blended together so nicely.  

I look forward to returning as there are so many things on their menu that were begging me to order them.

First time here. It definitely has the vibe and look of an English Pub. Fun casual atmosphere . Lots of TV' s to catch a game. Those at the hostess stand were nice and we were promptly seated. Not a busy night as we were there early in the week . Our server was great , friendly and attentive. I went in knowing I wanted to try the fish and chips. It was a nice generous portion of cod and fries. I would reorder this for sure.

I noticed they offer HH daily with drinks half off from 3-4 and at a discounted price from 4-6. Burger Wednesday's. Live music Thursday - Saturday. Brunch on the weekends with bottomless mimosas and bloody mary's . This was a quick bite on this particular evening. Will definitely check it out again.

Have been hearing about Konan's BBQ.  I certainly knew I was driving in the right direction, as I could smell the incredible aroma this humble establishment was delivering to the community. Parking lot was filled. I walked in to find the nicest group of guys behind the counter. Working hard that's for sure, however they offered up advice, smiles, a sample of one of their sides and a glass of their famous pineapple iced tea, on the house,  that apparently has a cult following.

I ordered a sandwich for my son and the 2 meat dinner for me. It was suggested I go with the chicken ( choose white meat ) and the pulled pork, with sauce on the side. I was disappointed to find they were out of the vegetables. In this case collard greens and green beans. This happens every Sunday, I was told. I like my greens everyday!! The remaining choices were not up my alley, but I went with the potato salad and cole slaw. Way, way, way to much mayo for me on both salads. The coleslaw was not for me. The potato salad grew on me, however I still would prefer the veggies always. The tea was much to sweet for my taste. The meats had a wonderful flavor and were moist. They were the highlight, as it should be, of my dinner. The meats failed me, however as both were filled with bones. Small bones that caused me to eat with caution. I have never experienced this with bbq. The meal was huge. A two meal deal for me even though I did not eat the slaw. 

Guys so glad you are successful and that you continue to keep the high star reviews here on yelp. You are a winner. You missed the mark for me.

As you walk to the front door of The Mill you are greeted with the sight and sound of a water mill, which is surrounded by a lovely outdoor seating area. Once inside you are treated to a true sensory delight aesthetically. Referred to as Steampunk Design, it combines machinery and elegance, offering lots of textures to carry your eyes from the floor to the ceiling. Atmosphere evokes a rustic southern charm, which I find to be very inviting and comfortable.  

The entire evening ran fabulously well. We were seated immediately on this Wednesday evening. Our server popped right over to say hi, offer a bit of welcomed conversation and get us started on cocktails. BTW, he was spot on all night. Knowledgeable about all things on the menu and I ask lots of questions. I was so impressed.  The drink menu is phenomenal and is fun to peruse. A bit pricey for a neighborhood restaurant. I tried the beautiful bright pink Tahona and my friend mentioned the Old Fashioned was executed well. I was lucky enough to be offered a sip . Wow, I think I just found a new fave cocktail. We ordered wine, however the list was a bit limited. Our server mentioned they were in the process of updating this section. I hope they include price points that are more drinker friendly ! 

The menu is as chef, Ted Dorsey, calls it  "Americana with a Southern touch and a French Creole twist." This evening we started with Pimento Crab Corn Fritters and Grilled Octopus. Both were fantastic, with the octopus being a standout! I'd like another order now please ! Delicious ! Next up the Seared Diver Scallops (cooked perfectly and I absolutely loved the carrot ribbons on top) and the Rubbed Corn Flake Seared Tuna .  He said it was good. The finale was the Mill Mudslide (a Flourless Chocolate Cake, Chocolate Coffee Cream, Bailey's Mousse). I usually never order chocolate. I will never say never again. This was divine ! I could go back in just for this alone. We had leftovers and I was fortunate enough to get them all ! What a fantastic lunch I had the next day.   

I am thrilled to say The Mill now offers Happy Hour !!!! Beer is $5.00, Wine is $6.00 and Cocktails $7.00 . Bar Bites are $6-$13.00. Happy Hour is Tuesday-Friday from 4-7 ! Cheers !

I'm not a huge BBQ eater, however when the mood strikes I've headed over to Holy Hog since they opened here on Henderson Blvd. I think they do a decent job on their meats. My go to is the pulled pork, which I find to be moist and flavorful. I've had the ribs, brisket and Havana sausage. I still am drawn to the pulled pork. They have several sauces to choose from and many sides. I like the collards and slaw. Not a fan of the others. 

They have fallen from 5 to 3 stars in my book. I typically use their drive thru. The last two times they have made mistakes,  which we all know is so frustrating to discover once home. This last time I ordered the Southerner. It's a pulled pork sandwich with pimento cheese, fried green tomatoes and cole slaw. I said minus the tomatoes. I asked for a side of the hot bbq sauce. This through the guy. Lol. He was not sure how to ring that up ! I finally suggested he just turn around and tell the person making it " No fried green tomatoes on the sammy!" I was after all the only customer inside or out. This is a small establishment and the cook can't be more than about 4 feet behind him. He was not sure how to include the hot sauce on the ticket either. Oh my stars. He wanted to add it so that he would not forget. Nice of him. I said no worries I'll remind you to throw it in the bag. I asked for extra crispy fries with ketchup. I quickly glanced in the bag to find no ketchup and mild sauce. I fixed that. Ok I get home and find the sandwich does not have near the meat I'm accustomed to receiving nor does it have the slaw. No pickles. I like their pickles. The fries are piping hot yet limp. I also see that the meal comes with piping hot pork rinds. This was not stated on the menu. Had I known I would not have ordered the fries. I won't order the sandwich again. The pimento cheese had little flavor. This southern gal likes it made with extra sharp cheddar. This was a very mild flavored cheese. No bueno for me. 

I did call the establishment. The cook/mgr.  and I gotta little thing going on. I've talked to her many times, as I did this time, and she said to hit her up next time for an order on the house. I appreciate that for the inconvenience .

Walked into the Crazy Burrito at an off hour so we had the place to ourselves. We were greeted immediately and taken to our table. Our server was on top of her game and took very good care of us while there. She suggested their signature burrito called,  Crazy Burrito.  This is a flour tortilla wrapped with steak, seasoned pork, chorizo, rice, beans, lettuce, pico de gallo, sour cream, guacamole and cheese. My son went with this. It is huge. He couldn't finish it and he liked it very much.  I choose the junior version which I could not finish and I unwrapped mine so I was not eating the tortilla. Still a lot of food. I thought mine was average. It was bland. Even after using one of the 3 sauces provided it still did not give me the flavor punch I was looking for. Not a reorder for me. I would return when in the area to try another menu item. The price points are solid. They offer beer and wine.

Popped in here recently to grab a bite and a drink. Have been here several times. I like the atmosphere. It is very warm and comfortable. I especially like sitting outside on the patio which has a beautiful fountain. At night it is really nice. Our server was spot on. Quick to greet us and very attentive. Drinks were served up in a timely manner. He was able to juggle quite a few tables. Service here has always been good. 5/5 stars.

Ordered the guacamole for the table which they prepare table side. Quite good. The ceviche was tasty. Also ordered the Camarones Ajillo which is jumbo shrimp cooked with mushrooms, bonita and salsa. All the food was a ok.  A 3.5/5 stars. It was a solid experience. The whole package is nice.

This is a fave of ours and has been since it opened. We are regulars. I decided to write another review. I wanted to share that for me Ulele has been consistent in service and in food quality each and every time we visit. I can count on Ulele to deliver on all levels.  I suggest you have reservations.

The atmosphere is comfortable, upscale, casual yet sophisticated. It sits on the river and is part of what is known as the Riverwalk.  There is also a park for children next door. With that in mind, people stop in after and/or during a walk or bike ride. You'll see folks dressed in gym clothes to a nice dress. It is such a fun place. People of all ages and stages are welcome. There is a huge lawn so kids can run around, there is plenty of seating outside, a bar and a fire pit. 

Tonight our server is Spencer. Spencer is spot on. Attentive, sincere, relaxed, upbeat and aiming to please. I am such a sucker for the charbroiled oysters. I order a dozen for my entree. I started with the beet and pear salad. It was delicious. The rest of the table ordered the filet,  chicken, meatloaf and mahi-mahi. The mahi mahi had to go back as it was overcooked. The server apologized, as did the manager and in a blink of an eye another was placed on the table. This time it was cooked to perfection.  Mistakes are going to happen and they handled it well.

I'll mention I love the Collard Greens. Not a fan of the okra. The burgers are great. Lobster cocktail delish. Pompano and red snapper another great order. The chicken salad is nice. I usually go for the oysters. I could eat 2-3 dozen of them at one time. My wallet holds me back. Shucks!

Another wonderful night Ulele. Thank you.

I read all the reviews !!!! I was ever so excited about eating the best burger ever in Tampa !! Expectations were high !  Wow ! Expectations were quickly deflated as I tore into the cheeseburger and fries. 

I ordered the fries extra done for crispiness. The guy, looked at me and said done !  They were hot and I appreciate the freshness. They were soft and had no salt. Honestly zero salt. No bueno.  Salt has to be put on fries the minute they come out of the fryer or it does not stick. In speaking to the owner after my visit I have learned they do not salt the fries, as an fyi. Not sure why. Hmmmm...

I ordered the basic cheeseburger with all the fixings. The burger was dry and flavorless. I think it needed both salt and pepper plus it was missing something else. Hmmm...  

Price is right and servings are hefty. It's on a busy corner of MLK and Tampa St. Parking is tight. At 3:30 on a Friday they were jamming. They pump the orders out quickly.  This is a standard order, pay and wait for them to call your number. They have a handful of tables. They close early so be aware of the time. 

I wish you guys continued success. You  are hitting the mark with lots of people. Unfortunately, not with me. I will not be back. 2.5/5

I enjoy a staycation on occasion to check out the hotels in our lovely city. This is exactly what I did when a group of sorority sisters arrived for a visit. They wanted me to be a guest too and not a hostess. I liked the idea so I checked all of us into the Epicurean.
 
This Marriott property resides on Howard Avenue in the trendy SoHo area of South Tampa. The location is perfect and so much is within walking distance. The upscale hotel has many amenities that you will not find at most hotels. There is a wine shop, they host cooking classes in another room, they have a dessert shop, spa, pool, gym and a roof top lounge with awesome views. Pool parties during the summer for locals and guests alike. The restaurant, Elevage, is nice and offers a great happy hour.  I would suggest you checking out Bern's Steakhouse across the street,  if you have never been.  People say the hotel is rather loud at night and many find it hard to sleep if you are a light sleeper. Although a light sleeper, this girl had no problem after a night out with the old crew. The hotel is also a stones throw from Bayshore Blvd. which holds the title of the longest unbroken sidewalk in the world. A great way to get in some exercise, sun and views of the bay.  

The staff is welcoming, professional and accommodating.  Glad we stayed here. A real treat. I would not hesitate to return.

I can't believe I have never been here until tonight!! A friend called and we decided to pop in for the Wednesday night special which is $9.99 for the Prime Rib or Fish and Chips. A gentleman was standing outside greeting customers. He opened the door then quickly seated me. I liked our table which was next to the window along 7th Avenue. It's a dim high ceiling giant room that is warm and inviting. Our server popped over to say hello and got us set up with the martini special. He was attentive the entire night.

I went with the fish special with spinach and a caesar salad. My meal was exactly as I expected. It was tasty and hit the spot. The fish was coated in a light batter, was moist and crispy. Spinach was cooked perfectly with a bit to much garlic for my taste. It was overpowering. I liked the salad. It was lightly tossed with the dressing. The meal was a-ok. 

Unfortunately, my friend was not happy with the prime rib. As it was placed in front of her it looked mighty sad. It was a small thin, thin, thin piece of meat that looked unappetizing. Meat that thin is usually overcooked. It was, plus it was fatty and tough. It did not resemble the picture. I had a feeling about the prime rib and was glad I went with the fish. I also took half of mine home.  My friend had been here before and thought quality had gone down.

This place is the kind of place legends are made of.  Ted literally took a hobby from his backyard of smoking fish and placed it in his front yard 65 years ago. I don't believe one thing has changed or been replaced about this restaurant since then. It is an open-air shack with picnic tables for sitting and a handful of stools at the bar. It does not matter what the temp is outside people pile in here for the smoked fish. If smoked fish is not your thing they also offer a hamburger, hot dog  and grilled chicken sandwich. That's it! No fries here. For sides you have your choice of cole slaw or their German Potato Salad. I'm not a fan of the sides. People love the potato salad which is made in house. It is a dive, nothing fancy here, which I guess is why it appeared on Diner's, Drive Ins and Dives.

What I come in for is the fish spread which is the BEST I personally have ever had. Many times I make this my meal. Just give me saltines, hot sauce and an ice cold beer. I'm singing " I'm in heaven." You may purchase some to go in half pint, pint and quart sizes. They will not allow you to order a take home container and munch on it at the table.  The dinner portions are big enough to share, as you are served a full pound of fish.  Lunch portions are served until 5. The mullet is full of bones, as an fyi, but most think this is half the fun of eating it. They also offer salmon (my fave), mahi-mahi and mackeral.  CASH ONLY. There is an ATM in the smoke house next door. I buy the pint of fish spread and a half pound of mahi or mullet to mix in at home. I do this just to cut down on the mayo factor. Any more than a half pound of fish and you'll change the flavor. I don't want to mess with that. Have been coming here my whole life.

To be honest , I  come here for take out on the fish spread only.

This is a local favorite for Italian cuisine. How this place has escaped a review from me I do not know. I've been coming here for many moons and it is outstanding!!!   It is rather small...like in tiny! The atmosphere is nice and reminds me of the many spots I have dined in throughout Italy. I feel like I'm with family while here. The servers are spot on attentive, friendly and accommodating. They will do anything here to please you and ensure you leave more than happy. One time I was so indecisive and my server said "No worries Miss I'll take care of you". Out came a plateful of both entrees to my delight.

 My faves  IL Risotto Al Nero Di Calamari ( Black squid ink, calamari and baby clams. I think of you Mariani when ordering this and yes this is where I'll be bring you on your layover in Tampa.) , IL Misto Alla Grigglia
(Large shrimp and scallops lightly breaded and grilled), IL Filetto Di Dentice Alla Siciliana (Snapper filet, pine nuts, eggplant, anchovies and white wine) and L" Insalatone Alla "Susy" (Large house salad with grilled shrimp, scallops and salmon). Anything you order is freshly prepared in- house with exquisite execution and love. No reservations.

Second time visiting Burger Monger . I was greeted right away . There was no wait on this Sunday evening.  Staff was very pleasant and food was up quickly.  Both times I have gotten a basic burger. Cost is $8.00 for this solo sandwich. Burger was prepared exactly as I ordered it. At the last minute , I decided I no longer wanted mustard on the bun. The associate was very accommodating and with a smile she replaced the bun that she had already put the mustard on. The burger is just average to me. I think it is a high price to pay for a fast food burger . If it included fries I'd be ok with it. 

On a side note , soon after I walked in another customer entered who was highly intoxicated . She was fired up as she ordered . The manager handled this situation beautifully by remaining calm and not adding any fuel to the fire, while still taking care of her order. I was impressed with her customer service skills.

I have been coming to Xtreme Juice for so many years. Since the kids were in elementary school and they are grown now.  They love them here. They have so many choices. Fast service. Crew is friendly.

The owner has always been very generous within the community. I worked on a lot of fundraisers within the schools and he was always willing to give me things for them and goodie bags for the students. 

I'm working out at LA Fitness now and Xtreme Juice is a stones throw away from the gym. I pop in for wheat grass and ginger shots. They give an apple slice with each ginger shot. My only complaint is that the apples many times still have seeds in them. Wheat grass shots are a dollar on Wednesday's and Sunday is bogo on smoothies. Gotta love it! Sweet deal.

Sister restaurant to Bern's, less formal and less expensive, with most offerings below $20.00, Haven is comfortable inside. It has a sophisticated ambiance, yet remains in line with the growing trend of casual dining.

They have set the bar high in all areas.  Service is spectacular with knowledge of food impressive. They offer over 300 bourbons and 40 glasses of wine to choose from. They have the areas most enthusiastic cheese program with over 60 different varieties and serve charcuteries, which  feature a number of  terrines, sausages, torchons and pates. If cheese is your thing, it is best sampled by ordering the Cheese Monger Platter for $47.00, which is a chef's selection of 18 cheeses. This could easily feed 4 people, I think. It was just too much cheese for me, as I eat little dairy.  The others in my party were in heaven.

Dinner features small plates and my fave way to do this is by sharing. Highlights for me from my most recent trip are the Mojo Palm Hearts, Fried Brussels Sprouts, Brie and Mushroom Toast, Smoked Chicken Biyrani, Snapper Ceviche, Blackened Scallops and Hamachi Crudo. The menu is constantly changing. If they ever have the Roasted Cauliflower I suggest that, as it is delicious.

What lures me back time and time again is Happy Hour, which is offered Monday- Saturday 5-7. Specials on both drinks and bites change daily. Oysters are $2.00 each with other bites being offered for $6.00. Please note you must be in the bar area or outside patio to take advantage of the HH pricing. They pack a crowd so if you want a seat strive to arrive at 5. Folks tend to come in and linger.

Like others, I am a huge fan of Caddy's. If you want the beach, surf, sun, music, cocktails,  food,  and/or sunset  look no further. Caddy's totally delivers. Sit inside, outside undercover, at the bar, outside in the sand or on the rooftop. They offer complimentary chairs and umbrellas on their beach, yoga several days a week,  volleyball nets and a host of other events. Check their facebook page to see a list of daily events.

Nothing fancy here from the atmosphere to food. Serving Breakfast, lunch and dinner with a varied menu to satisfy all. I've had the grouper nuggets and sandwich, Mahi tacos and crab cakes. All were tasty. Fries are great. 

With the prime real estate location this place packs a crowd. Parking can cause one to frown until you get inside with your first cocktail and start to mellow in with the crowd. 

They have a location on the intercoastal in Indian Shores and in downtown St. Pete on Central. Plus one in Bradenton. Enjoy!

I've always been a fan of Bella's since they opened in the late 80's . Back in the day it was a biweekly haunt ! It's one place I can honestly say has always made me happy . So I was a bit shocked with my most recent experience. I was going to overlook it , however I woke this morning still miffed and bothered so I've decided to share it. 

My fave salad is the Insalta Mista consisting of bright green glorious romaine, red cabbage, artichoke hearts, pimento, hearts of palm and parmesan cheese. Starving , I ordered this for delivery with salmon on top. My order arrived quickly and my mouth began to salivate knowing what I was about to enjoy. Imagine my disappointment when I discovered a box full of pale, nutritionally lacking, tasteless white ends found near the base of the stem of romain lettuce. Hardly any toppings . I found myself pushing around the lettuce with my fork searching for them. The entire meal, salmon and all went in the trash , along with $21.50 before delivery fees and tip. See my picture. In my opinion , the salad is far overpriced as it is. A 5 ounce piece of salmon is not worth $8.00. Up the serving size and let's talk. 

I phoned Bella's and spoke with Michelle, the manager. She immediately said the company that sources their lettuce sent this, not what they typically buy and serve. It was a decision of serving salads or not . They obviously opted to serve,  believing their customers should not blink an eye at being served poor quality greens  . She was quick to offer to send out a gift card for my inconvenience. I appreciated her honesty and willingness to make it right. Although very kind, her actions did not make me feel any better. They did not restore my 4 plus star rating. Bella's knowingly served and charged me for a meal that did not live up to their standard or mine. They sent it out thinking I should be happy with it. They set me up and themselves up for a disappointing customer experience .  I feel taken advantage of as a customer.  I would never have knowingly ordered this much less paid for it. It was insulting. 

Michelle did follow through by sending out a $15.00 voucher. Not the amount of my lunch nor my trouble.

Timpano's is a favorite haunt of mine. Located in Hyde Park Village, it has a sophisticated supper club feel to it with Sinatra music playing thru out. Many nights they have live music. The atmosphere pops. 

They have a terrific raw bar. Many different types of oysters to choose from, tuna, shrimp, mussels, clams, crab,etc. It is fun to sit at the raw bar to just pick what you want and get it quickly.  Patio seating is also nice.The menu is diverse with something to please all. What we always order are the steamed mussels which come out in a cast iron skillet. They are fabulous. Many times this is my meal. They will saute the calamari for you if you ask and they are delicious prepared this way. The flatbreads are crisp and tasty. The deconstructed bruschetta, which consists of burrata mozzarella, balsamic tomatoes, olive tapenade, grilled ciabatta and vanilla-poached apricots is amazing. The house chopped salad I love. My favorite thing to do at Timpano is just order the appetizers and share. I get to have a taste of so many of my faves this way. I have always been happy. I am a regular.  Food and service has been spot on for me every time.

Monday is half off bottles of wine under a $100.00. They have a nice happy hour with specials on both food and drinks.

Sat outside on this past lovely Friday evening, which gave us a great opportunity to people watch and engage in some lively conversation! 

We took advantage of the HH offerings and items off the regular menu. HH runs until 7pm . Nice menu at great prices. The carpaccio and shrimp with eggplant were my fave and definitely a reorder. Loved the sauces on the calamari, however there was a bit to much breading, for me. Although I didn't try the burger it was a hit. 

Service was quite pleasant, although a bit slow on drinks returning from the bar. You really can't go wrong here. I'll most certainly return.

I have been coming here forever. It is a great spot on Tampa Bay to hang for a bit enjoying the view and a cocktail. We are usually combining a stop here with some form of exercise, as it sits right on the Riverwalk. You may walk or bike along this beautiful sidewalk getting some vitamin D, taking in the sites and working off the calories that you will be consuming at the Sail in the form of liquids. They offer a food menu
too, however I think I come for the beverages and typically go elsewhere for a bite.  Service is spotty. I go knowing I will be going to the bar myself for a drink, especially when they are crowded on the weekends. I have even seen people bring their own food. That's a great idea.

This spot is obviously casual. Bring the whole family, your four legged friend too. Yesterday they had a Mastiff Rescue fundraiser here. It was amazing to seeing so many of these  large dogs in one place. 

They have music, happy hour during the week and other events.

I grew up with Publix. I was the kid with my feet hanging out of the cart and then in turn my kids did the same. When Greenwise opened it was only natural for me to become a loyal customer here.  Love the parking garage especially when our rainy season hits. As far as customer service goes Publix is on top of their game. The people are as nice and helpful as possible. They truly go above and beyond. 

They have a beautiful produce, seafood/meat and cheese section.  The meat dept has the largest selection of upper end beef that I have ever seen. Very pricey but extensive. The supplement section is packed full and you can usually catch a well seasoned associate to help you here.

Wow ! This place continues to amaze me ! Ever since I stumbled upon Viet Kitchen a few months ago I'm drawn to it on a weekly basis. The aromas pull me in , the flavors and creativity keep me coming back. Everything I've had I've enjoyed.  The salt and pepper prawns are delish . Crab fried rice is filled with deliciousness and lots of the crustacea !  The salads are spectacular! The carmelized fish is so tasty.  The wings are darn good.  Where do I stop ?  All is delivered with such warm enthusiasm from the staff!  The whole package is 5 stars !

A Tampa institution. Have been coming here my whole life. A  small deli offering breakfast, sandwiches, soups, salads and desserts. You place your order at the counter, pay, wait until they call your name and then grab a table. It gets really crowded at lunch. I call my order in. They have a separate line for call in orders so the line moves much faster.  

I like their sandwiches, soups and desserts. Not a big fan of the green salads for some reason and I'm a salad gal. Can't put my finger on it. They certainly do sell a lot of them though. 

Service is good.

Who doesn't love a hotdog on occasion ? They are as American as apple pie ! They are found at many bbq's over the summer and they have been found at Mel's Hot Dogs since 1973.  Mel has built quite a successful business over the years. I have been popping in and out of here, about once or twice a year,  since it all began. 

They offer dogs prepared about 18 different ways, sausages, Chicago Beef, chicken and burgers. They also have a veggie dog and burger. Baskets include a hefty serving of fries and a drink. Hotdog baskets will set you back about $10.00. All other baskets about  $12-16. 

I have only had the hotdog at Mel's. It is not any better to me than any other dog I've had elsewhere.  It is, however more expensive. A bit pricey to me for a humble hotdog. I like the hot steamed bun. The fries are crisp and piping hot.  

Order at the counter, pay, find a seat and they will shout your name out when ready. Service has been just fine. It's an average run of the mill fast food experience. Not a destination.  They are a block from Busch Gardens Theme Park and they pack a crowd.

Hey, I stand by my first review.  Ray's is a solid 4 in my book. Came here last night with my book club. For those of you who are from Florida, I think you would get a kick out of this book if you like a light entertaining read. The book, Best State Ever by Dave Barry. I laughed continually while reading. On to my review....

Ray's is a small humble shack off the side of the road with a handful of tables. To the side of the shack outside under a canopy with fans you'll find more seating. While you are not coming here for the atmosphere,  you are coming for  what this unassuming place can do with seafood in their kitchen. When they say " From our bay to your belly," they are not kidding. The grouper sandwich is absolutely fabulous. It tastes like it was just caught that morning and cooked just for you. This is by far the best grouper sandwich I have had in Tampa.  I am so glad I found you Big Ray!!!! You certainly do know what you are doing. You'll get a large piece of fish with a nice soft buttered bun filled with shredded lettuce, tomato, onion and tartar sauce. I want to go back already!!!  Along with your sandwich you'll have of choice of fries or coleslaw. Onion rings are a slight up charge.. The price is $14.00 which is what I would expect.  The onion rings I like as there is very little breading. Made in-house, they are all goodness to me and an outright worthy splurge. I have also subbed my side for a ceasar salad. This Florida girl loves a grouper sandwich and they are the bomb.

My only beef with Ray's is they charge $9.00 for a small small small glass of wine from a bottle they paid less than $9.00 for. They are not in the league to charge this for a glass in my opinion. Hence 4 stars. 

The fish spread is nice. The fried shrimp are a bit salty for me. I am a salt lover so I am curious to know what others think about these fresh crustaceans. Grouper cheeks are ever so tasty. This is all I have ordered from the menu. The grouper keeps me coming back for more. Love love love this place.

Absolutely love Samurai Blue located within Centro Ybor, which is a destination for unique shopping, dining and entertainment in the heart of historic Ybor City. You may valet, park on the street, if you are lucky enough to score a spot, or park in the garage. Pop up to the second floor, 
walk in and you will find a trendy cool atmosphere with incredibly high original brick walls and exposed wooden rafters. It all makes for great space. It's fun to sit at the sushi bar and chat with the chefs or grab a seat at at one of the tables or booths. 

I have enjoyed everything I have ordered from here. A few favorites are the Red Devil Roll, Volcano Roll, Lasagna Roll, Tuna Summer Roll, Blue Crab Rangoon, Tuna Tataki and Sunomono Salad.  I'll mention the Volcano Roll is topped with a wonderful conch salad. They will top it with a crab mix if you prefer. 
 
Samurai Blue also offers chicken, fish and steak entrees. My son enjoys the filet and I'm crazy about their snapper and salmon. Overall a great fun delicious night for all guaranteed! 

4 stars because sometimes service is spotty while other times it's fantastic.

I decided to try this restaurant after reading some yelp reviews. I walked in and was immediately acknowledged by a beautiful lady with a bright smile. I was seated and water poured. Wine followed. We are off to a good start. The entire evening service was spectacular. The owner and her son were both so friendly and helpful. Service was most certainly 5/5. 

I ordered the flank steak which came with a salad and potato. Salad was fresh and crisp. I normally do not order flank steak because it can be tough. This was suggested and it was marinated so thought it was a sure thing. it was a bit chewy. Not a reorder for me. The sauce with it was nice.
I tried a layered potato dish that I did not care for.  Overall the food was just ok. I will  come back to try something else. The rice with seafood perhaps.I

Popped in here on a recent Friday night to catch Happy Hour which runs until 7. They offer $6.00 bites and drinks during this time. We were greeted right away and the nice hostess found us two seats at the bar. Perfect. The Masters was on and we were able to catch up on the days results. Even better. Ordered wine and Martini's!!!!! Keep them coming. Atmosphere is warm and inviting.

For the table we ordered a trio of hummus (just so-so) , fried calamari (just fine) a tomato flatbread ( flavor on point, however soggy) and a meatball with ricotta( just right).  

Service was spotty. Two bartenders and the bar was full. They were hustling and we had the last two seats at the end so we were overlooked. Overall just ok. This restaurant is under the Outback umbrella as an FYI. Have been here many times and experienced far better service and food than we did this go round. It happens.

Oystercatcher's sits on the property of the Grand Hyatt. You drive down a long winding road as you approach the shore that the restaurant resides on, which is flanked by palm trees and bright flowerbeds. You may valet or self park. Once entering, I am always taken back by the stunning panoramic  views of Old Tampa Bay. The inside is simple understated elegance. They offer a lounge, indoor,  outdoor patio and a lower level deck for seating. 

This is my favorite place in Tampa for Sunday brunch if I want to splurge. To break it down, the buffet is separated into sections. You have the  breakfast bar, seafood bar, pasta bar, a sushi bar, cheese bar, salad bar, a seafood and meats bar, a fruit bar and a dessert room! I'm wondering what bars I left off. It sounds overwhelming, but it really is not. The focus is on quality of the food. It is presented well. Lots of thought has gone into the sections and each is well maintained. 

I'll dive in a bit more. The omelet bar gives you a choice of white, brown, duck or quail eggs. The cheese table holds artisan selections from all over. Delicious yet some mysterious to me. The chef was serving up fresh wild caught jumbo shrimp and oysters. You'll also see fresh salmon sitting on top of a seaweed mix and sliced tuna with an array of toppings. This seafood is my favorite section. I'm also a salad lover so this is my next fave section. Not your average salad and fruit bar. This is quite adventurous. The entree section has different fish like mahi mahi, snapper, salmon, beef and chicken with also sorts of toppings. The dessert room is quite the indulgence.
