Service was delightful, personable  and with chit chatting while he poured the never ending mimosa's.  The whole experience was flawless.

They are open for lunch and for dinner. All seafood is wild and line caught.

I had heard so much about this restaurant that I was hard wired to go this week. Just finished up lunch in this unassuming restaurant that has just celebrated its 11 month anniversary. William the owner, chef, server, etc was so sweet. I very much enjoyed talking with him. 

It sits in a sketchy area of town in a strip center on the corner of MLK and Armenia. Do not let the exterior fool you. The inside is extremely casual and small. Nothing fancy. This is all about what William can do in the kitchen. I believe there are about 7-8 tables. I hear at night it is best if you make a reservation. There was only one other table at 1:00, however others were doing take-out . 

I was worried about the temperature as others had mentioned that it was hot inside and I run hot. It turned out I was fine on this overcast day. He maintains a constant menu and he also has lots of specials that are changing daily and it is handwritten on a chalkboard. I started with the smoked trout salad which was so fresh. It could have been my meal. I really wanted to try a pasta so I went with the carbonara. The smoked salmon sounded great,  however I had already ordered the salad with trout. Gotta switch it up.  Needless to say I am coming home with 3/4 of my meal. You could easily split the mains. My friend ordered the chicken special which was huge and delicious. It is like having family cook for you while you sit and enjoy.  If I wanted anything I just said William..... Like I was home. Cool experience. 

This was a long lunch. They run on one speed and it is slow. Understand this if you dine in. Remember William is wearing many different hats. It is BYOB and there is no corkage fee! Great find!! Thank you, William.

BEST INVISIBLE COFFEE IN TOWN-MAYBE THE WORLD BUT STILL...STAY AWAY. 

I came in on President's Day 2020 (02/17/2020) with my siblings and couple of friends. They had just helped me move and some of them, it was their first time in SB. A few of them where craving coffee so I wanted to treat them to a coffee and a pastry.  I ordered 3 coffee's and 2 pastries. The bill was a little over 27. 

We got our coffee and pastries and sat down as a group. About 10 minutes later the guy that took my order comes by and apologizes about the wait on the "other coffee". I said what other coffee. I only order 3 and we have them here. He says "Oh you have 3, I only charged you for 2!"

Wait a minute, you handed me the 3 coffees, you charged me, and you're the one that also thinks there's a 4th one on the way...how did we get to "I only charged you for 2!". If I had kept my mouth shut, not only would we had gotten a 4th coffee but it would have been free. My sincerity cost me. He said- "just finish up and no rush, when you're done, just come by and pay for the 3rd coffee" Yo, there's customers all around, you made the mistake and now I have to be embarrassed and get up to pay for your mistakes?

I didn't have a receipt to prove he did charged me, so I went up to him before leaving and said, I thought my bill was north of 27 dollars. He said "yes, pastries and coffee are 5 dollars or so, so you still owe one more." I was so tired from the moving and was so frustrated I went ahead and paid this invisible coffee. Let me tell you, they make great invisible coffee. The best in town, maybe the world.  

The next day, I revisited this when I looked at my slim bank account and thought- well 3 coffees is 15 dollars and I only got 2 pastries that should be about 25. I vaguely remember the bill being somewhere in the 27 something range. Meaning I didn't have to pay for another coffee. 

Bro, you were going to give me a 4th coffee and I ended up paying a hefty price for your mistakes of not keeping tabs on what your customers are asking for and paying. Disgraceful. 

Moral of the story- Don't go dressed as if you just moved, they will probably want you not to come back and hit you with some invisible coffee charges. And don't be so damn sincere, learn to keep your mouth shut maybe you can get a free coffee.

A wonderful brunch at Trip's diner. I've been wanting to try this place for so long. Went to brunch on a Saturday, did not have to wait for an inside table. They also do have an outdoor patio. I had the crab cake eggs Benedict which was absolutely delicious. My friend had the Reuben and fries which was also delicious. Great service, a little loud but that's what's expected of a diner. They have a parking lot on the side of the building. They are open 7am to 9pm during the week and open later on Friday and Saturday nights and close early at 3 on Sundays.

I've been trying to get a reservation for this place for weeks but if it isn't a couple weeks in advance I couldn't make one. So I made a reservation 3 weeks ago for tonight. The place is beautiful, located at the bottom of the Pearl apartments next to Armature works. Excellent wine menu. I was advised we had to start with the mozzarella cart where they use cheese curds and hot water to manually stretch the mozzarella for a lovely and delicious caprese dish. Very creative and a popular seller, beautiful presentation . For my main meal I had the Gizelle al Forno: berkshire pork shank, spinach, mozzarella, mornay. Definitely a different twist on pasta for me as it was pasta wrapped up and topped with cheese with the spinach and pork baked in. It was pretty good though. My friend had the Tortello all' Uovo: egg yolk center, ricotta filling, roasted and shaved mushrooms. Definitely authentic Italian. Overall a very good meal, it was the end of the night so the only thing I felt we were a little rushed at the end. But I understand after a long night. Definitely would like to try one of the main dishes next time, bronzino or the steak but they are served for 2 people so I'll come with a friend and come hungry.

This continues to be one of my favorite breweries in St. Petersburg Florida. The set up is awesome they have an indoor bar and an outdoor concert area and patio. They have plenty of games. It's kid and dog friendly. They have some of the best beer locally that I have had. Their signature mango Bob's IPA is to die for. Staff is terrific they are very knowledgeable about their beer and gave excellent recommendations. They have a small parking lot but there's also parking available on the street around the brewery. Definitely a great place to see a concert as well, was recently here for the UKe It Out (ukelele) festival and they did an amazing job hosting it. Definitely on my top three  list of Saint Petersburg breweries.

Amazing Thai food in New Tampa. We got take out and it was perfectly cooked. I got the Amazing duck which was served with a sweet and sour sauce with pineapple which was delicious. We also had the pork dumplings that tasted delicious. Definitely recommend this place. Best Thai food I've had in Tampa.

Went for the Father's day brunch this year. They had two choices, all you can eat brunch with one drink or with all you can drink beer or mimosas fior an extra $15. They had a great offering for their menu as well, this is one brewery that is smart and has their own kitchen and serves great food. Here's the menu:
-Smoked BBQ Brisket
Beer braised collard greens
-Hoppin' John Salad
Black eyed peas, bacon, corn and roasted peppers
-Shrimp & Grits
White Cheddar, fried okra, slow poached eggs
-Fried Green Tomatoes
Horseradish sour cream
-Twice Baked Potatoes
Bacon, scallion, sour cream and cheddar jack
-Baked Mac & Cheese
Beer cheese, pecorino bread crumbs
-Sweet Potato Cheesecake
Brulee marshmallow and beer glazed nuts
Brisket was delicious, the collard greens had some kick. My favorite was the shrimp and grits with an over easy egg, so delicious. Brew bus often has Sunday brunch offerings similar to this with a different menu ever time. They are very good about updating on their website. They continue to add and brew more of their own beers which is one of the reason this place is so great. And that's apart from the super cool brew bus they have running out of their brewery to different breweries around town. All around wonderful concept.

Second time here and just as good as the first. It's an intimate place with a limited number of tables. So much value for what you get. The portions are huge and very reasonably priced. Service is great, even though our server was very busy he did a great job. I had the two soft flour tortilla chicken tacos with rice and beans. Plenty to eat and the rice and beans are delicious. There's street parking available,

This continues to be one of my favorite restaurants in Tampa. Always great food, service is amazing, the servers are so knowledgeable, location is perfect and the ambiance is happening and hip. I have never been here and it has not been completely full with a wait list. We made a reservation and were seated immediately. Started with the delicious scallop appetizer; Fresh sea scallops,fire-roasted with white wine, garlicbutter and paprika. For the main meal I had the Seafood Risotto Pan-seared Gulf of Mexico shrimp and seascallops, butter-poached lobster claw, fresh lump crab, saffron
risotto, charred corn cream sauce. My friend had the Barry's Tomahawk Pork Chop 14 oz. Duroc bone-in pork
chop with guava demi-glace, twice-baked potato, butter whipped
mashed potato baked with cheese and chargrilled corn topped with
Gulf bowfin caviar, seasonal vegetable. Both were absolutely delicious with beautiful presentations. They have valet parking and a large private parking lot a couple blocks away. Before or after your meal go take a walk along the lovely Riverwalk which has been an amazing addition to Tampa and the revitalization of this area.

I had such a great experience here the first time for brunch that I had to come back for dinner. Absolutely phenomenal experience. This restaurant and bar is top notch! From the moment you enter the service is fantastic. Our server let us ladies sit, eat, drink and chat for 5 hours and didn't even make any suggestion that we should leave. I started with the espresso martini and had a glass of the prisoner 'saldo', zinfandel 2018  (mostly so I can remember for next time) with dinner. 
Really enjoyed our time here and the food is second to none. We started with the Warm spinach gouda dip: black truffle, grilled sourdough and the Grilled octopus: romesco sauce, arugula, lemon. The dip was delicious and rich and the octopus perfectly cooked. For my main meal I had the Colorado Lamb Chops: fig & hazelnut crusted, baby carrots, goat cheese potato gratin. All I can say Is wow. You can see by the photos how beautiful this dish was. The lamb was cooked to order, the fig and hazelnut crust was out of this world and the potato gratin with goat cheese was the icing on the cake. Except for the cake, we had the Bombolini: little sugar doughnuts, tequila lemon curd, nutella sauce and the Warm Chocolate Lava Torte: bourbon caramel sauce, hazelnut gelato. We didn't leave a crumb. They have self parking and complimentary valet available. You do need to make a reservation, you can not just walk in. The hours are Thursday to Saturday 5pm - 10pm. Sunday 11am - 4pm. 
I can't say enough wonderful things about Urban Stillhouse. What a fantastic addition to the Warehouse Arts district of St. Petersburg!

Nice and fresh Szechuan restaurant in Tampa, located in a strip mall on Fletcher relatively close to USF, it's a nice intimate place. You can order to go, pick up or they have about 10 tables for dine in. Nicely decorated and welcoming with a beautiful red dragon painted on the wall. The server was very friendly and helpful. If you like spicy this is the place to go. They give you the option for little, medium and very spicy. Luckily mine was not spicy because I haven't built up that tolerance. My friend had the Braised Beef Rice Noodles and I had the Rice noodle in chicken soup. They were both very tasty, flavorful with fresh ingredients and a nice size serving for each. During the whole lunch hour I only saw 2 other people come in and out for pick up. Hoping they can get their name out so they can get more business because the food is really very good. They are open Tuesday to Sunday 1130 am to 9pm.

Went for dinner one week day night. It was about 815. I think they might be short staffed because they had many open tables that still had not been bussed clean unless they just had a big rush that left. Overall service was great. And food was excellent quality which I expect at Outback. I had the Victoria's filet with broccoli and a salad. Cooked perfectly medium rare.  One of the only chains that I will go to for this reason.

Beautiful location right on the Courtney Campbell Causeway overlooking the bay, this is a cool venue that been through many different names and ownership. It originally was Crabby bills where we used to come to play sand volleyball. Then Hulk Hogan took over and it was Hogan's, there's been a couple in between and now it's WTR which is more of an outdoor night club feel and restaurant at the Godfrey hotel. They have done a very nice job renovating this area, there's a beautiful pool at the center. I went here for their Halloween party and it was a lot of fun. People really took the costume contest seriously. Drinks were good, they have a full liquor bar. I'd be interested to come here for their pool party Sundays or Rose all day Saturday. They have karaoke Thursdays and it becomes a night club on Friday nights. I didn't try any of the food this time around so I can't comment on that. They have a large parking lot but predominantly it's valet.

Brought to you by the Columbia restaurant team, Casa Santo Stefano is a Sicilian restaurant located in Ybor city. They have transformed this space to an absolutely beautiful restaurant and rooftop outdoor space and bar area upstairs. I couldn't stop looking around at the decor, the small touches make a world of difference. Friendly and helpful service. We had made a 6 o clock reservation and were immediately sat. After our meal when we were leaving the restaurant was full so I would strongly encourage a reservation if you want to be seated in the main dining room. We started with two glasses of wine and the Valenti's Burrata: Burrata cheese, heirloom tomato, pickled red onion and arugula salad dressed with balsamic vinaigrette. This was a very large portion that my girlfriend and I could share, nice and fresh with a large serving of burrata. 
For my main dish I had the Sea Bass Grigliata: Chargrilled Mediterranean sea bass marinated in extra-virgin olive oil, herbs with eggplant caponata, grilled lemon. I liked the lemon flavor on the fish but there were several lemon seeds on my fish that I had to pick out before eating. I understand the aesthetics of it but not functional in my opinion. The dish was cooked perfectly but it was a little lighter on flavors than I would have liked. The eggplant caponata side was delicious.
My friend had the Veal Chop Grigliato: 
14 oz. chargrilled veal rib chop with Marsala sauce, cremini mushrooms, pecorino potatoes, rapani. The veal chop was hearty and cooked to order with excellent flavor and side accompaniments. We were too full for dessert this time but will definitely try some of their authentic Italian desserts the next time like tiramisu. Overall a wonderful experience. There's parking available at the lot next to the restaurant or in one of the lots near the Columbia restaurant down the street. They are open Daily for Lunch: 11 a.m to 4 p.m and Dinner: 4 p.m to 10 p.m.

This is one of my favorite St. Pete breweries. When it comes to their beer, two of my favorites are Cycle fixie, an ipa that drinks like a high alcohol content ipa but only at 4.7%, and Cream and Sugar please, a coffee porter at 4.9%. Their beer is available throughout Tampa Bay but I have actually never been to the tasting room. It was nice and busy on a Thursday afternoon. I had the Neckerchief ipa which was delicious. They have a bar and tables inside and a patio outside. One female bartender calmly handling it all. Definitely will be back to this cool tasting room!

Went into Whiskey Cake at international mall after dinner to have a drink at the bar and contemplate dessert. Best decision ever! When the restaurant is named after their signature dessert, you order dessert! They have a food menu as well, "farm to kitchen" , full bar, nice wine choices but they specialize in whiskey, over 300 different choices of whiskey. We sat at the bar and asked the bartenders about the drinks and the kinds of whiskey. They were very knowledgeable about the brands and characteristics of the whiskey. When I asked about the whiskey cake they said we couldn't go wrong. And they were exactly right, one of the best desserts I've ever had (and I've had a lot). Their whiskey cake is a toffee torte with bourbon anglaise, spiced pecans, house made vanilla whipped cream. It was a large enough piece for my friend and I to share and we still had about 1/3 left over for breakfast the next morning. Great atmosphere, bar and dessert! Will try the food next time and won't forget about the dessert.

Great place we went to for breakfast but they serve three meals a day. We came on a Friday morning. Outdoor and indoor seating available. 
They have daily breakfast specials. Their Friday special was the Hillbilly Benedict. As eggs Benedict is one of my favorite breakfast dishes, it was only fitting that I order this. It's basically biscuit and gravy topped with egg and sausage. This was delightfully heavy.  I was full throughout the day but very delicious and the biscuits were fresh. My kids got the two pancake short stack that filled up the large plate. Portions here are very generous, we had breakfast for the next day for both my kids. Service was very good we went when they first opened and there was only one server initially but two other servers came to help out. Great place in treasure island, they have parking in front as it's in an unassuming strip mall. Hours are Monday to Thursday 8AM-10PM,  Friday 8AM-11PM, Saturday 7AM-11PM and Sunday 7AM-10PM.

Serving Venezuelan and Lebanese food, Are Pitas has a large variety of options. They have a counter serve set up but you can sit at a table and eat there, they have a large colorful dining room. Or take the food to go. They have arepas, pitas, empanadas, falafel, gyro, I had the gyro on pita with fried plantains. Very tasty but i haven't met a plantain I didn't like. They were pretty busy during lunch time and originally just had one person working the counter but eventually someone else came to assist. Friendly staff. Parking in a lot in front of the restaurant. Great combination and offerings. Located right at University mall in Tampa.

Great counter service Greek food in Wesley Chapel. I love their gyro on pita or chicken pita and a great Greek salad and pita with hummus, They also have chicken fingers and fries which my daughter loves. Typically when you order your food it takes about 15 to 20 until it's done depending on how busy it is.  That's because everything is made to order and got. The pita is always fresh and soft which is how I like it.  The staff is very friendly and helpful. I wish they would stay open later, their hours are 11am to 8 pm daily.

One of the best New York pizza places I have found in the Tampa area. Large dining room and bar area with great craft beer and wine options and full bar. And they are open till 330am every day! Making this a wonderful after party location. They are open daily 9am - 3:30am serving breakfast lunch and dinner. 
But for me the pizza was the star of the show, we got a New York style pizza with pepperoni and mushrooms. Loved the crust and sauce. It definitely reminded me of New York pizza and being from New York City, I'm an expert. They were showing the lightning game with sound on so that made this place even better for me. Street parking available around the restaurant.

Great Thai food in a large shopping center in New Tampa. They have plenty of parking available. The place is small and intimate. Service is very attentive and friendly. My friends who I was with come here regularly and the server asked them if they wanted the "usual." The food was delicious and fresh, we all cleaned our plates and they were large portions for lunch. I had the amazing chicken with peanut sauce and streamed mixed vegetables, my friends had the L7, chicken and veggies with medium spice which was even a bit spicy for them. If you don't do spicy I recommend you get the mild. Lunch specials come with a wonton and soup. Great place to get Thai food with reasonable prices.

I definitely wanted to like this place but it fell short for me. Cool outdoor bar and patio with tables, but the music was way too loud. The food came out cold and the bartender (we sat at the bar to eat) although friendly was very inattentive. They have a limited menu based on what was caught that day of fresh fish which is a definite positive to this place. I probably expected it to be more of a full service restaurant than an order at the window kind of place. Unfortunately it missed the mark for me.

Great bar with all sorts of old school games. They also brew their own beer and have 5 or 6 of their own on tap in addition to some guest taps. They have air hockey, golden tee, skee ball, darts and several other old school gaming systems that you can play for free such as Nintendo and Sega. Two levels to the bar, super fun place to hang out. Friendly staff.

Always a fun time. They have a huge space (and a small parking lot). There's parking available on the street though. Known for their delicious German food and beer and exciting extracurricular activities such as paddling. When they first opened this place was always busy. I noticed it was not as busy this time around on a Thursday night. We sat at the bar and received great service. We decided on the Nürnberger Rostbratwürst: Three roasted pork sausages with sauerkraut , mashed potatoes and dark gravy and the Schweinebraten: Famous "Munich pork roast" with vegetable garnish, dark beer sauce, potato and breaded dumpling. Both were very tasty and we didn't have to wait long for the food. I had the Dunkel beer as well. Very good food and service.

What a fantastic place, I have driven by here so many times but haven't had the pleasure because we always go to our other favorite place in Dunedin. They have a very large dining room as well as a patio for outdoor seating. We went on a Thursday evening and it was a full house but we were able to get a table. Their menu is so extensive,, they have something for everyone. Great craft beer offerings, 37 on tap, wine and full bar. Thursdays they have Flatbreads for $8 and  Select Martinis are $4.00. We decided to try two of the flatbreads and an entree. We decided on the Haus Cali: Avocado puree, pulled chicken, applewood bacon, mozzarella & drizzled with Sriracha aioli and the Black & Blue: Mozzarella and blue cheese, shaved ribeye with green onion and balsamic drizzle. They were both very tasty, nice thin flatbread with plenty of toppings. We shared the Korean Short Rib: Sticky rice, stir-fry vegetables and sesame seeds, wow this was absolutely delicious! The flavor was outstanding, the meat was so tender. My only complaint was that I wanted more of this dish. Our server was great, gave excellent recommendations. There is a large parking lot available for parking. The best part about Dunedin is that parking around downtown is still free and I highly respect that decision. 
They have other daily specials listed online too. Late night happy hours mon-sat 10 pm to close, 50% off all Draught Beer, Haus Wine and All Liquor, Mondays  $8 burgers and $4 draft beer. Tuesday is taco Tuesday with great prices on tacos and margaritas. Wednesday they have special price on Pulled Pork and Brisket Sandwiches and half price select bottles of Wine. Friday fish fry with Fish - N - Chip for $10.00 and a Pint of Guinness for $4.00.  They have a bloody Mary's bar on Saturday and Sundays. Here are their hours: 
Breakfast Served
Monday- Friday: 8 AM to 11:30 AM
Saturday & Sunday:  8 AM to NOON
Dinner Served
Sunday - Thursday Full Menu until 10 PM
Friday - Saturday Full Menu until 11 PM
Late Night
Monday - Thursday
Bar stays open serving Pizza & Flatbread til 11 PM
Friday - Saturday
Bar stays open serving Pizza & Flatbread til 12 AM

You can not find a better place than this, I definitely need to come back to try breakfast, they have 6 different eggs Benedict varieties that I need to try!
This will definitely be part of my Dunedin food rotation.

One of the most amazing food experiences I have had was the chefs six course tasting menu at Rooster and the Till. I used to go here when the restaurant was half the size before it took over the shop next door. There's a large bar in the center with the kitchen behind it and tables throughout the perimeter of the restaurant. Beautifully designed and decorated. Chefs Ferrell Alvarez and Ty Rodriguez do an amazing job with combining unlikely food pairings to make beautiful and fantastic dishes. The chefs tasting menu has two options. With and without the wine pairings. I chose just the food option. All the members of your party need to have the tasting menu if one person wants it because of the timing of when the food comes out, 
The first course was Lamb Tataki: pistachio green harissa, green strawberries, tahini beet root dahl. 
Second course was the Kathi roll: onion pakora, sweet potato almond chutney, raita, red garlic chili smear. 
Third course Sea bass belly: chili cumin long beans, korma curry, coriander coconut chutney 
Fourth course: Fried sweetbreads: caulilini raisin aschar, curried potato croquette, smoked vindaloo, yogurt
Fifth course: goat cheese, rhubarb nectar, burnt carrot ganache, lavosh 
Sixth course: Cardamom turmeric meringue, green mango, mango jelly, coconut milk snow. 

What a flavor explosion in every bite! Hard to decide on my favorites but I would say the sea bass belly and I just loved the burnt carrot ganache with the goat cheese. My friend loved the Kathi roll. The presentation was just as professional as the flavors. This is a once in a lifetime experience that you will pay for but it's worth it. 
Our server was so knowledgeable with all the items on the menu, the wines and beer. Because they don't have a liquor license they have to be creative with some of their cocktails. Had the Yuzu margarita served with Sake. It was absolutely amazing. 
The restaurant is in a strip mall, so there's a few parking spots in the center but there's another lot across the street to park. They are only open for dinner Wednesday to Saturday from 5-9 so I highly suggest a reservation.
What a fantastic experience, solidifies my love of this restaurant as number one in Tampa bay.

Definitely a cool vibe, great music on the bar side. Didn't get the chance to try the restaurant this time, but it looked pretty busy. Recently opened so still new staff getting acquainted to the place. There's happy hour menu 4 to 7 and a small plate menu available on the bar side. Had the Smoked gouda pimento Mac and cheese fritters and the afro Cubano: La Segunda bread, ham, smoked pork belly, whole grain Aioli mustard and pickled okra. The fritters were a little dry but the afro Cubano was excellent. This will be a great higher end night club addition to 7th Ave in Ybor. There's a pay parking lot right behind the restaurant and within walking distance to many of the 7th Ave restaurants, clubs and bars. Looking forward to trying the restaurant and full menu advertised as "southern inspired cuisine."

Great new place for the Wesley Chapel diners. It's a concept from the Texas roadhouse group, Bubba's 33 is known for its pizza, burgers and beer. They have weekly specials, Monday madness with $7.99 burgers, Tuesday pizza night, 12 inch pizza for $9.99. We had one pizza, the Margherita which was very fresh and tasty and a burger which was juicy and delicious. There are lots of televisions around so it's a good place to kick back and watch a game. They have a large dining room and a separate bar. Definitely a relaxed vibe. They have plenty of parking available in the parking lot as well.

What a great place in St Pete. Expected more of a bar with food but the food was actually delicious, I had an amazing black and blue burger with sweet potato fries.  They also have Mediterranean influence on their menu such as the fried Feta, pita and tzatziki, pita wrap. They also have a great beer selection including some of the local favorites like Escapes the other West Coast IPA. That's a restaurant and bar inside, not too big, and they have a large patio area on the street in front of the restaurant. Street parking is available along Central Ave . Great place to go in St Petersburg.

Still a great place to grab some stellar craft beers. They always have the best beers on tap. This time I was here for an Angry Chair tap takeover. Great beer and they had a good truck available to pair nicely with drinking beer. They have an amazing outdoor patio area and an indoor large bar and tasting room. Located in Seminole Heights, just another of the wonderful craft beer places in this area. They had live music on the patio as well. It was the perfect evening combination.

Always a great place to go to one of the original breweries in Dunedin. They currently only offer outdoor seating as the inside is committed to the brewing of delicious beer and for the bartenders. Do you order from the window. They have a fun flight presentation that's like a tree (see photos). We had 5 on the flight. We had the mangrove double IPA, turtle face: Brett ipa with mosaic and Amarillo hops, App Trap hazy ipa with mosaic and galaxy hops, When Life GIves you lemons a strawberry lemonade imperial gose and K-hop ipa. My favorites were the turtle face and actually the strawberry lemonade gose, it was nice and refreshing. They have some of the best beer swag as well, cool clothing, beach towel. There's a parking lot in the back of the brewery. Kid and dog friendly patio.

This restaurant has stood the test of time. Always fresh sushi, great location in Centro Ybor. Nice high ceilings, brick interior. Reasonably priced. You can park in the Centro Ybor garage. Our server Sue was amazing. She is so knowledgeable about everything samurai blue. Our sushi was delicious! Eel, yellowfin nigiri, Tokyo Rock & Roll, love roll, rainbow roll. So fresh and full of flavor. Definitely recommend samurai blue. They are doing renovations on the outside of the building but they are still open so go on by!

What a gem located in the middle of a neighborhood in St. Petersburg. Best beer choices I've seen at a restaurant. They have something for everyone. They also have a nice choice of wines.  I went with the Ellipsis Pinks and Greens New England IPA which was fantastic. They have a terrific food menu as well. They are known for their bison bacon burgers, so I had the Thurman Merman:  Smoked gouda, applewood smoked bacon, house bourbon mustard, lettuce, tomato & onion. Perfectly cooked loaded with flavor. Staff is very friendly and knowledgeable. There is a small parking lot in front and street parking all around. Don't miss out on Bier boutique! A wonderful gift to St. Pete's culinary scene.

I made a promise to myself after the pandemic shut down the world that I will not wait to try the places that I've wanted to go to because you never know what tomorrow holds. Sooff i went to Mekenita cantina that's been on my list for over a year now. Fantastic food, drinks, service and decor. Located in a Seminole Heights strip mall, you wouldn't imagine the magic inside. Brightly colored decor and friendly service. We started with the chips and salsa and the ceviche. Such crisp fresh flavor in the ceviche  and the chips and salsa were great. Then for my main dish I had the Crab & Roasted Poblano Enchiladas with Maine Lobster Ancho Chili Cream served with rice, black beans and a side salad. This was a huge plate, definitely 2 meals worth. The flavors all flowed together so perfectly. My friend had the Chili Garlic Rubbed Smoked Pork Burrito with Pineapple Papaya Key Lime Salsa, Chipotle Salsa. Another huge dish. The burrito must have weighed 5 pounds. What a fantastic experience at Mekenita Cantina. Parking available in the strip mall and in the nearby Seminole heights neighborhoods.

So Matt and I were going out for a celebration dinner, and I picked this place. I had been wanting to try it out, and they're one of the few places in the city that serves lobster so I figured we'd give them a shot. They have a lot of great reviews and photos so I thought I'd be giving them a 5 star review. Sad to admit that this place is extremely overrated and didn't live up to the hype or my expectations.

We arrived on a Friday night at 7pm. Surprisingly no wait, but it probably helped that it was just the two of us dining in that evening. We looked over the menu and were greeted by our server shortly after. We started off with a glass Rose and a White Russian, and ordered the Lobster Marco which is stuffed with a shrimp and mushroom alfredo pasta, as our entrees. The food came out quickly, especially considering how busy they were. The waiter was very attentive as far as drink refills go and asking if we needed anything. 

The food is where they lost me, because everything up to that point had been great. The lobster itself was SO bland - that kind of shocked me. We live in Louisiana where everything is generously seasoned. The lobster lacked seasoning of any sort, even just standard salt! While they had a tank with live lobsters, I am pretty certain it's merely for show. Actually, it seemed like the lobster may have been previously frozen, or cooked then refrigerated? The texture and flavor just wasn't there, and definitley not what fresh lobster should taste like. The shrimp and mushroom alfredo stuffing was good, but there was nothing special or noteworthy about it. While the presentation was nice, it wasn't nice finding small fragments lobster shell while eating the lobster/stuffing. 

 Honestly, the best part of the meal was the Rose and White Russian which is pretty sad for a restaurant that has such rave reviews. Needless to say, this place is pricey and we left feeling like we overpaid for a less than mediocre meal. Like I mentioned before, the service was great but I'm not going to restaurants for great service and drinks (at least that's not the Only reason I go). So unfortunately I won't be returning or recommending this place to anyone in the future.

Gasp. I seriously cannot believe it has been FIVE years since my previous (and first ever!) Yelp review. Seriously, where does the time go? 

I am happy to report that not much has changed since my last review. Fuji is still my very favorite spot to grab dinner in a pinch or get my sushi fix in general whenever a craving strikes! 

The food is as delicious as ever. The employees are so friendly they'll make you feel like family. The location is convenient, although parking can be tricky on certain nights of the week since it's a shared lot- but it's well worth a trip or two around the parking lot. Nowadays I'm a fan of the tuna avocado roll (+asparagus), but I have yet to be disappointed by any of their rolls. If you want something special or want to add/remove something from a roll on the menu, just ask! They're happy to accommodate their customers special requests and their goal is to serve you sushi you enjoy.

The only thing that has changed in the past five years is they have recently added bubble tea to their menu. The flavors they are currently serving are strawberry, mango and passionfruit. So far we have tried the strawberry and mango; Both tasted amazing and were very refreshing. 

I still would highly and happily recommend Fuji to anyone looking for great sushi and great service!

TJ's, where have you been all my life?! I know I have only known you for a brief amount of time, but somehow you feel like an old friend.

I wasn't quite sure what to expect my first time visiting, although I did have some preconceived notions that it was similar to Whole Foods? Well I can now confidently say that after several visits that Trader's is in a league all their own. Honestly, I can't seem to get over how wonderful this place is. I can admit that I was a tad late to the party that is Trader Joe's. If there is a polar opposite to big box stores, this place is it! 

It's pretty obvious that everything they sell is not only unique but intentionally selected, whether it's their standard stock or part of the seasonal selection. I LOVE that!  It really makes every shopping trip fun. 

Yelp family, I am not sure if I ever told y'all, but I am not a great cook. Matt is the cook in our family and he is beyond amazing at it. I, on the other hand, love great food but can't cook worth a damn. Oh how Trader's has changed all of that! With their amazing selection of frozen entrees I am now an excellent chef! Whipping up amazing Chinese dishes like Mandarin chicken and Kung Pao chicken, or delicious Indian cuisine like Tikka Masala and Butter chicken; I can now even concoct a mean steak burrito if Mexican is more your style, or pizza that will make your taste buds think you're in Italy. The false confidence in my cooking abilites TJ's has given me is seriously priceless. 

They have a great coffee selection (try the Kenya AA and Konya varieties, they do not dissapoint!), as well as an extensive wine and beer selection that I haven't been able to try just yet due to my current state of being very, very pregnant. But after my little man is born in the coming week or two, I am so looking forward to trying their infamous 'Two Buck Chuck'! 

Also worth mentioning is the flower selection. They have lots of beautiful blooms to choose from for any occasion, all at  beyond reasonable prices. I picked up a dozen roses for $6.99 for a graduation, and at those kind of prices I ended up getting two dozen because that's just a steal! They were, and still are, gorgeous as the person who received them sent me a photo a week later of them in a vase at home looking just as beautiful as the day she received them. 

Last, but certainly not least, are the employees running this show. I have yet to encounter a grumpy, unfriendly employee at any of my Trader's visits. They're seriously some of the happiest individuals I have had the pleasure of speaking to, and at my last few visits the check out staff have even been kind of enough to have someone help bring my bags to my car. Heck, at my most recent visit the cashier also sent me home with a complimentary bouquet of flowers to congratulate me on my soon-to-be bundle of joy! If this isn't exemplary, top-notch service I don't know what is? They are certainly just as responsible for the amazingness that is Trader Joe's. 

I can't recommend Trader's highly enough. Give them your business, and you'll be questioning why you would dare give any other grocery store your hard earned money! Also, serious props if you made it through this crazy long review. But they're that amazing, and people Need to know!

I love Whole Foods! There. I said it. I don't know what kind of spell they've cast on me, but something about this franchise has me hooked! 

It's mostly their really great fish selection. Its incredibly hard to find salmon that ISN'T Atlantic and/or farm raised. Whole Foods offers some amazing King, Coho, Sockeye and at the right time of year Copper River Sockeye salmon- and all sustainably caught! I also love their Jumbo Lump Crab Cakes, although I usually doctor them up a bit with some onion, garlic and salt. 

Their chicken/beef/pork selection is also outstanding. Their beef kabobs (especially the ones covered in Black Pepper marinade) are amazing and huge! One is more than enough for an average sized human to consume. The sausage selection is extensive, so if you're looking for something specific or unique (Bison sausage, anyone?) it's worth checking out if these guys have what you're looking for!

The bakery, oh, the bakery. This is where I get myself into trouble. They have an over the top, decadent selection that is sure to please the sweetest tooth! From gluten-free and dairy-free to vegan - there is something for everyone. My most recent obsession is the Chocolate Eruption cake. 

The main thing I've been stopping here for lately is their baby food- specifically Once Upon A Farm. It's starting to become more widely available, but Whole Foods is still offering the most flavor varieties. They also have my little guys favorite yogurt, Stonyfield YoBaby Vanilla- so its an easy one stop shop for the smallest member of our family, at least for now.


The store is about as busy as any Whole Foods, and the lines move quickly. If you don't have many items you can always utilize the customer service area or coffee shop for a quick-er check out!

This place is my weekend breakfast secret weapon. 

Matt and I have a thing for breakfast diners, and although we had been to several in our area we didn't have a real favorite. All of that changed the day we decided to try Dots. 

The atmosphere here has that classic 1950's diner feel, which I love. This location is nice and cozy, offering a few booths, standard tables and some countertop seating. We prefer to sit at a booth, but if one isn't available we just set up shop at the counter with a few coffees until one opens up. 

The food is prepared in an open kitchen area behind the counter, so you get to see and smell all the amazing things they're cooking as you peruse the menu. The menu is large, and easily offers something for everyone- even that 'picky eater' in the family. 

I haven't tried too many items on the menu, because to be completely honest I have a favorite go-to item that I can't not get when I go to Dots and that item is the B9. It is easily the most delicious chicken fried steak I have ever eaten, covered in white country gravy and served up next to a side of eggs, hashbrowns and a biscuit. Matt usually gets the dinner version, which comes with mashed potatoes or french fries, a side salad, a vegetable and garlic bread. I love that you can substitute anything on your plate without it being a huge issue; sometimes Matt will get a biscuit instead of garlic bread or I will get fries instead of hashbrowns. Matt has also gotten the Philly cheese steak sandwich, and it is definitely one of the best in the Metairie area. 

Also, the biscuits here ARE LIFE. I have never ever ever Ever had a better biscuit in my life. TBH, I think you could justify going to Dots just for the biscuits alone. Get them.

Last, but certainly not least, is the service. From our first visit to our most recent visit the service here is always amazing. The ladies here are some of the friendliest servers and definitley make this place feel like coming home. If you visit often enough, they get to know you and you really do become part of the family. 

I can't speak about their other locations, but I can attest that Dots on Williams is THE breakfast spot to visit if you're in the Metairie/Kenner area!

Two words: Pickle Soup.  Light and savory, served hot, with potatoes, meat, vegetables, and just a hint of pickle flavor. To be honest, if I returned, I might order this as my main course.

Portions were a tad small if you get the pierogi, but the stuffed cabbage rolls were huge, and the kielbasa was solid. 

The apple vodka drink is AMAZING.  Think apple pie. In a glass. That happens to be alcoholic. That's my kind of thing.

The server was young and enthusiastic, though he seemed to forget to refill my water :(

Cute decor, kitchy and homey.

Been going here ever since I moved into the area. Lee's Deli is a classic and great to grab a variety of food from. I recommend it to everyone. The owner quality controls everything at the front and I've never had any issues with orders.

I was really hesitant in doing this review because I really didn't want anybody else to know about Fred's and I wanted to keep it a secret all to myself. I know I'm being a little selfish and all. 

First off Fred's is a members only breakfast club located in the cute town of new Hope Pennsylvania. I happened to be one of their lucky members. Woot woot To enter Fred's you must have a key card to unlock the door between the hours of 6 AM and 11 AM. If it's after 11 AM your out of luck the door automatically locks and too bad for you. 

I should warn you that Fred's has some rules. They don't do grumpy and there's a bucket outside the front door to deposit the grumpiness in before you enter so come and happy. You can fill your coffee for free and members are welcome to bring anyone to Fred's whom they wish. 

Fred's is closed on Thanksgiving, Christmas eve and Christmas Day. 

Fred's is the place that you would have to know where to go to find it since there is no sign outside of their establishment. Shhhh it's a secret hidden gem and if you're lucky enough to dine here with the member well you're just lucky enough. 

Fred's has an amazing concept of a true dining experience, all the cooking and baking is done in the center with a counter that goes all the way around with 31 barstools. Yes that means only 31 people can't be seated and eating at the same time so take a seat by the front door after you put your name on the list when you come in next to the host and feel free to get yourself a cup of coffee while you wait with a smile on your face. 

Now on to the food. The food at Fred's is out of this world spectacular I just love breakfast and have fell in love with breakfast at Fred's. Everything is so fresh and tasty. The portions are large where I can only eat half of what they serve. Their eggs Benedict is a must try and don't forget to try their French toast. Yummy!!! You will definitely leave Fred's with a smile on your face and satisfied tummy and if you're not a member by the time you leave you'll have the urge to become one.

An overall great experience! 
I want to give a shout out to Padaro Beach Grill for creating such a laid back and relaxing environment. 

Parking can be a little nuts, so plan for that. Sometimes the wait to order your food can also take awhile, but the food and atmosphere ARE SO WORTH THE WAIT and it gives you time to pick out the perfect place to  sit. The wait for the bathroom is usually a bit, so do your best to also plan ahead.

As soon as you place your order and then you step out into the lawn, you take a deep breathe and then just enjoy the smell of ocean air and the view. Your kids are free to play in the sand and what's so great is it's a semi controlled environment.

I have tried several items off the menu but some of my favorites are the bbq chicken salad, Hawaiian burger, the teriyaki chicken sandwich or the veggie burger.

The staff here are friendly!

I use to love going to this casino when I move to Florida. It has gone down hill. I use to play on their rewards card and was often given good reward credit to eat in their nice restaurant but they have tighten them a lot. 

I would recommend going to Miami for more casinos and a lot more choices. Tampa only have the one land casino so they can do anything they like. I have lost a lot of respect for this casino and their business practices.
A great new place everyone will want to check out. The service is outstanding and the chicken is tasty! Put this place on your short list to try and you won't be disappointed.

CASH ONLY.

This place has pretty good cupcakes - some better than others.  The store itself is VERY small.  In the customer area, you can probably fit 4 seated and 4 standing before you realize you can't move.  The inside is very pink poshy boutique and everyone is super friendly.  Even with the cramped space, they staff was very patient with me as I was taking my time deciding which lucky cupcake was going to end up in my tummy.

The regular cupcakes are about 3 dollars and their daily specials are 4 dollars.  They also make mini cupcakes (21) in a variety of flavors but that has to be pre-ordered.  If you like some of those cookie jars they have on display...they're on sale too =)

Cupcakes that I got (see pictures):
- Red Velvet Cupcake:  I ate this one on the spot because I couldn't wait or stop myself.  I love red velvet.  It was sooooooo good!!  The cupcake was very moist and not overly sweet.  The cream cheese frosting was very smooth and not excessively sweet either.   It was decorated with a cute little lady bug~  very boutique-ish.
- Reeces Peanut Butter Cupcake:  Moist chocolate cupcake with frosting (not sure what kind)...topped with a chocolate drizzle...sprinkle with Reeces peanut butter cup chunks...with a solidified chocolate drizzle stick on top.  AMAZING!
- Peanut Butter Cupcake:  This cupcake was nothing to write home about.  It looked very cute...banana cupcake with peanut butter frosting and a nutter butter stuck on top.   The cupcake itself was a bit on the dry side.  The frosting was just OK.  The Nutter Butter cookie on the other hand was good!  Honestly, I wish it had more peanut butter oomph to the entire cupcake.

And, just like that, I have a new favorite restaurant here in Tampa. This place dominates in all major categories: food, drinks, service, ambiance, and decor. 

To start, we had the Crab Beignets and Coconut Shrimp. The beignets are as delicious as all the reviews say: lightly fried with a creamy, crab-based interior. Next time, I'll pass on the shrimp and go for the cornbread skillet. 

When it came time to order my meal, I simply couldn't decided between the Andouille-encrusted Wahoo or Boudin-stuffed Tenderloin. Luckily, my colleague couldn't choose either, so we decided to order one of each and sample each other's plates. I am so glad we did this because both dishes completely blew me away. 

The Wahoo was smooth and flaky, perfectly cooked throughout with an ample portion. The fish comes with cream-cheese grits which are decadent and deadly for your waistline (no regrets!). Apparently, the restaurant won an award for its Louisiana-style hot sauce, and I could easily see why after tasting it in this dish. 

As for the stuffed pork, it came with a sweet potato souffle and brussels sprouts. All the food on this plate was amazing. I highly recommend this dish for anyone who might not be a seafood fan. 

Top all this with the French 75 cocktail, and I left Roux full and content, trying to think of upcoming occasions when I can return. Until then, I'll be thinking about that Wahoo... and wondering if there's a dish anywhere that can compare.

Wow! First time here last night and I cannot wait to go back!

We stormed in here with very little time to spare. (Pho is always a good idea if you need to eat delicious food and get the hell out of dodge). 

We were seated immediately. Placed an order within five minutes. I told the waitress we were in a hurry. 

Five minutes later....lemon pepper chicken vermicelli! Veggie pho! Both delicious and incredibly filling. The chicken was insanely good, and the light dressing they bring with it is superb. I put the credit card down while we were still shoveling the food in our faces and Wam! Bam! Thank youuuuuu Ma'am! We were in and out in 20 minutes! 

Seriously, though. This place is nice! Great ambience, good for small groups, kids (if they are so inclined), dates, girls night out....really just an all around nice place to be.

If you are my friend, and you are coming to New Orleans, you can definitely schedule a lunch at Cooter Brown's. I LOVE THIS PLACE.

It is so divey and perfect. There is a huge menu of delicious poboys and fried delights for even the pickiest of eaters. Tons of raw oysters as well.

I don't even drink anymore, but I still am impressed by the huge beer selection. Every Abita EVER brewed is here, usually on tap. 

The place has a lot of history, not crazy Civil War history, just awesome divey bar on the railroad tracks kind of history.

What can I say about this, that hasn't been already said.....The main attraction is the CHICKEN!!!! CHICKEN CHICKEN CHICCCCCCCKEN!!!!!! If you have never been here before then 
1. There will be a line outside, rain, heat, cold. It will be a line. 
2. They close at 5pm 
3. The place is small but gives a home cooking like environment. 
4. The menu is straight to the point, one sheet. 
5. You will leave with a food baby lol and probably a togo bag. 
Nothing beats a wet batter dipped chicken when it comes to seasoning. I'm straight to the point when ordering chicken, mac and cheese and sweet peas. The okra is delicious but they do sell out of okra close to the afternoon, a lot lately. Im not a fan of butterbeans, but they way that they cook it and add rice, I will partake in eating them at Willie Mae's. There is another location that is open, but I have not been to that particular one, just yet. Oh, the cheesecake is awesome if you have room for dessert.

When in Nashville, it is a must to taste their hot fried chicken.  There are several places to get it but Hattie B's is pretty popular.  I also heard about Prince's, which the chicken shop of the wife of Hattie B's.

We were famished after a show at the Grand Ole Opry so of course we had to squeeze in some Hattie B's in an hour before closing.  There was still a line out the door and it was cold and rainy.

Menu is pretty straightforward and we all wanted to share so we didn't get too full, as we often did in Nashville.  We shared 2 mild large dark meat chicken plates, Mac and cheese, Cole slaw, fries, collard greens, and banana pudding.  We were bummed they ran out of peach cobbler!

Chicken was crispy, tender, flavorful and delicious.  I  could have used a bit more heat so I put some hot sauce and honey on it. I heard the spicy one was way too hot so we were cautious.  Rest of the food was good!  The banana pudding was ok- definitely had better.

Servers were nice and the music was cool- they played a variety and liked the R&b and hip hop incorporation.   

As first timers, they gave us a bunch of "what the cluck" stickers before we left.  Such nice southern hospitality!

Vegan cheesesteak AAA-grade. Seitan with onions peppers and sauce. Not sure how healthy it is to eat a gluten sandwich on a flour roll, but it sure was yummy. 

Got the fries also with black pepper only. As seldom as I eat fries, I gotta say, Lee's fries are worth the assault on my normal bland diet. They could have been hotter but they were not uniformly cold.

45 minutes later, no heartburn or discomfort of the gut. Lee's passed the test.

Let's get the boring stuff out of the way first.

Hattie B's is good. In my opinion, Prince's is better *if* you get them on a good night, when the chicken is perfectly prepared, but you've got to roll the dice on that. But Hattie B's wins hands-down in terms of reliability, convenience, and speed. You could have ordered, paid, gotten your chicken, and eaten it at Hattie B's in the span of time that it takes the Prince's order queue to creep agonizingly from 871 to 878. Think about that a second. And Hattie B's sides are much better. It's become my go-to hot chicken place for those reasons--I still love Prince's, but I don't always have an afternoon to burn waiting for a piece of chicken to come out that might be amazing or horrible depending on what mood the cook is in on that particular day.

Now for the real point of the review: hot chicken is not meant to be eaten. It's an abomination, an aberration, an antiquated and deleterious shibboleth that the people of Nashville have built up around themselves as a harbinger of their own ruin, like chewing betel nuts. 

Try looking closely at a quarter of Hattie B's "Damn Hot" chicken sometime. It looks, in a word, angry. It's the color of blood and oozes viscid, oleaginous bile all over its surroundings with a sort of sentient hatred like an aspic cooked by Lucifer himself. Rub some of the molten hate between your fingers and they start to burn.

Yet you're going to eat this thing, you maniac. You're going to grab it with your fingers and sink your teeth into it of your own accord. You're going to utter assorted blasphemous imprecations against whatever gods might happen to be in the area as the spices dig their hellish claws into taste buds that you didn't know you had. And then you're going to take another bite. And another.

It is the belief of this researcher that spice of this level actively impairs the higher reasoning functions of the brain. As you engage in this ritual self-immolation, the id breaks free of its chains and rampages through the streets of your brain, drunk, naked, and giggling. You're consumed by the desire to consume, dominate, destroy, overcome. Meanwhile, the ego cowers deep in its bunker, gulping glasses of milk and noncarbonated beverages, worrying about the health of your intestinal tract.

And these are its fevered thoughts: why am I putting this in my body? What will it do to me? Will I ever be able to taste again? Why did I agree to this? Who convinced me that this was a good idea? Who poured that poison into my ears?

And somewhere, deep down, the answer: I paid money for this. I braved the unruly masses and the Vanderbilt traffic tangle and the waiting and the paying, all for this privilege. I was not forced into this. There were no men with guns shouting instructions at me. I WANTED THIS.

And that, dear reader, is the truth lurking at the heart of hot chicken. Nothing mystical, no force of evil, compels you to eat the chicken. You do this of your own accord. There is no chicken-shaped devil perched on your shoulder, whispering in your ear. The drive to self-destruction is within you. And eating hot chicken with sufficient frequency might enable you to hit that target.

Those who seek to get away, one assumes, necessarily have something to get away from, be it the crushing tedium and grinding resentment of your daily employment, the grim specter of your domestic life, outstanding charges for shooting a man in Reno (just to watch him die, presumably), etc. But, in getting away from these things, we oftentimes find that we've taken on a whole new set of problems that may potentially be worse than the ones we're fleeing. And there is little worse than The Getaway.

The tiki bar ideal rests somewhere between the exotic and the antiquated--yes, you want something with a South Seas-ish flavor, but you also appreciate it with a sense of ironic distance--you're acutely aware that you're not in Fiji or Honolulu or wherever, and take a sort of pleasure in that fact. So you expect it to be a bit campy, to serve antiquated drinks, to have a selection of red-faced, lovable drunks in beflowered shirts. You expect some sort of dusty, lacquered swordfish over the bar, sufficient thatch to equip a village of kraals, bamboo siding, a few carved grotesques. If your standards are ludicrously high, you expect the bar to be carved of koa wood, though this fact has long been forgotten and the bar itself defaced by countless rum-fueled scratchings and scrawlings.

Yet The Getaway is relentlessly modern; everything is landscaped into oblivion, to the point that the palms are visibly propped up with pylons and the furniture seems like it's off the rack at IKEA, and the spotless bar is managed by people wearing matching t-shirts and populated by a mixture of people who clearly dressed for a night out. The menus are printed immaculately on meticulously laminated cards.

No, I can't fault the place for being clean, though I can evince some existential angst at the fact that this is what passes for a tiki bar in this day and age: a shiny plastic recreation of something better somewhere else. So I'll fault The Getaway for a lot of other things instead. The parking situation is abominable (right off the Gandy Bridge, and if you don't get P.I.T.-maneuvered by one of the cars barreling down the road as you try to turn in, you're likely to be squashed by a jacked-up beach buggy whilst trying to get from your car to the bar area), the lighting has a vile sort of clinical affectation that makes you feel like you're drinking in a hospital cafeteria, the crowd is cloying and treacly, the chairs (which are clearly not meant to be beach chairs) inexorably draw you downward to a sandy grave.

Two additional offenses bear mentioning though: the drinks and the music. The drinks are fine (if spendy) so long as you stick to simple things. The rickey I had was fine, (and it had damn well better be, since it's just liquor, lime juice, and soda), but my companions, hell-bent on having the Authentic Tiki Bar Experience (tm) if it killed them, ordered some of the fruitier and blended drinks. The fruity rum drink tasted like banana-flavored antifreeze, which was perhaps not all that far from other rum drinks I've had, but my other companion, against our better judgment and the very laws of decency themselves, ordered something called a "Cabbage Key Creeper" (the very name itself conjuring poor decisions--do you really want to be the sort of person who strides manfully up to the bar and orders, in a brash tone, a "Creeper?"), which proved to be composed primarily of Kahlua and stagnant drippings from the water bowl of Cerberus, Guardian of Hades. It was one of those drinks that you sip and then immediately experience an involuntary bodily tremor, as if the lower functions of your brain were desperately attempting to forcibly expunge whatever you've been foolish enough to ingest. The Creeper sat untouched upon the (slowly sinking) table as our doomed companion went back to order a beer.

Also, the music, if "music" is indeed the right term for the cacophonous assault of seemingly randomly-distributed thuds and screeches that had been selected as the entertainment for the night in question. Yeah, you might have expected ukelele music or slack-key guitar or calypso or steel-drum music or some sort of Brazilian tango thing in a pinch, but no. This was basically what sounded like bad karaoke music for people with a preternaturally high tolerance for electronica, though not to a sufficient extent to break out the glow sticks and body glitter. it was too loud to carry on a conversation (even at an optimal distance from the stage), so our merry band simply gazed out over the water and wished (in vain) that we were listening to the tortured wailings of the damned or something instead.

The Getaway receives one extra star for its waterfront location and the patronage of local food trucks. Besides that, I very much felt, by the end, that it was a place that I had to get away from.

You can find just about anything in the world at various points on Charlotte Pike, provided that you have a sufficient tolerance for grime and strange odors.

Case in point: K&S World Market. You ascend into a parking lot that looks like it should be used for air shows on holidays. You view all the weird signs on the door and the grubby buggies with trepidation. You walk into the midst of a bizarre odor, equal parts fish, bananas, and something else you can't identify, all left to ferment for a while. You gaze in bewilderment at the strange fruits and veggies, studded with spikes and knobs like the dinosaur ancestors of what you might find at Kroger. This store is best experienced by the adventurous.

For those into ethnic cooking, and for transplants from bigger cities where international grocers are more abundant, the experience of visiting K&S is similar to that of a refugee from the Soviet bloc seeing an American supermarket for the first time. You're spoiled for choice, reunited with all those old friends with whom you've lost touch. Real jerk sauce, fish sauce, curry paste, banana sauce! Bagged tea for everything from an upset stomach to certain of the rarer STDs! Chayote, bok choy, hot peppers of all varieties, beautiful peeled garlic! Pot stickers, crawdads, blue crabs, goat meat!

Let others bicker about cleanliness; if you're the kind of person who appreciates the K&S, you know well enough how to trust your own judgment about the viability of assorted foods. Otherwise, Trader Joe's is right down White Bridge, and they have wasabi peas in nice little unthreatening packages.

Excellent pork fried rice served here. I'm getting away from my go-to shrimp dishes and tried pork instead. I've had theirs on three occasions now and it's so delicious! Ive had the salt and pepper pork as well. It's hit or miss on whether this is good on the day. My orders were all to go so I can't say much about table service. I don't like the look of the place inside, too dark and dank, but the food is really good.

You know how sometimes you just NEED dessert? We needed dessert. It was 9pm and not much was open for delivery. We came across A La Mousse and their high ratings, so it wasn't a hard decision to trust them for our evening sweets delivery!

We ordered a few pieces of tort/cake and they were wonderful. I wish I could more eloquently remember what we ordered, I just remember that they were delicious and didn't last long. One was a thick and creamy layered strawberry cake. I really enjoy when desserts are still tasty but not a sugar bomb that give you a headache. I absolutely loved the little chocolate bear cake. He was almost too cute to eat!

The next time we're in Philadelphia and it's not a pandemic, A La Mousse is definitely on my list of places to try in-person. Even through delivery, I get a good vibe about the cuteness of this local business located in Chinatown. It seems like my cup of tea! I love a business that has personality!

I was in the area today and really wanted to grab something quick to eat at home. I visited Dolsot House a few years ago, but I'm not sure why I didn't write a review. 

Anyway, today I opted to try the Edamame, 4pc Dolsot Honey Sesame Wings, Lunch L.A. Kalbi Dolsot and the Lunch Spicy Pork Dolsot. I had a 30 min wait, which I didn't mind. I finally received the packaged items and made my way home.

Upon my return home, I immediately tried the Honey Sesame Wings. Wow, they were so crispy and completely covered in honey. I enjoyed every single bite. I moved on to my L.A. Kalbi Dolsot, which came in a nice deep, round, bowl that was completely full. I loved the flavor of the marinated ribeye and how it went with the zucchini and carrots. The rice was a little mushy, but I love mushy rice! I give the L.A. Kalbi Dolsot a thumbs up. 

My husband had the edamame. He noticed that lack of sea salt (yes, he loves his sea salt). I looked at the edamame and didn't see any salt as well. Easy fix, we added our own. He moved on to the Spicy Pork Dolsot and ravaged the entire bowl in one sitting. Needless to say, he enjoyed everything just as I did. 

I would love to visit Dolsot House again when I am in the area. I can't wait to try more on the menu.

The original Gran Caffe L'Aquila was actually in L'Aquila, before the founder moved to the US. They are an authentic Italian restaurant, cafe, bar, and gelateria in a prime Rittenhouse location. The place is massive, with two floors of dining rooms. Their menus are extensive, featuring regional classics, imported ingredients, and expertly curated wine, beer, and specialty cocktail lists.

My fiancé and I arrived on time for our 7:30pm reservation, were seated immediately, and then abandoned for 20 minutes. We were so hangry that we almost left. Fortunately, once our charismatic server arrived, the pacing of the rest of our meal was perfect. 

I am both a Negroni and espresso enthusiast, so the Philadelphia Gran Negroni caught my eye. This signature cocktail is a unique Negroni, made with their own coffee, which is roasted in house. It was exceptional, somehow allowing the coffee to shine, while still being a perfect Negroni. 

You must order some fresh imported cheese. We opted for the Burrata Mozzarella, which was creamy and flavorful, enhanced by the accompanying caponata. We also loved the Pera salad, a large portion of crisp greens topped with juicy slices of pear, ample goat cheese, and pine nuts. The Melenzana Parmigiana was a perfectly respectable eggplant parm, and the Carcioffi Fritti (fried artichokes) were tasty, albeit too dry. 

The Gnocchi alla Bava were tender potato pillows, nonuniform in size, and dressed in a creamy sauce. I wished there were more mushrooms, as the dish was very one-note. That one note was a good note, but still. The Ricotta Cheese Cake was extraordinary. Lighter and less sweet than American cheesecake, with a well executed chocolate cookie crust. A great choice for Italian in Philly.

100% vegan fast food. Conveniently located in Center City, HipCityVeg offers a great variety of inexpensive sandwiches, wraps, salads, and drinks. West Coasters-this is the equivalent of Veggie Grill. Most of their menu items incorporate mock meat, but there are a few fully plant based options as well. Sides include mini salads and sweet potato fries. They also have milkshakes, banana whips, and a few types of lemonade to satisfy your sweet tooth. The girls working were all genuinely friendly and knowledgeable of the menu.

I got the Udon Noodle Salad, which was very good. The diced mock chicken was delicious. Pleasantly spicy and bursting with savory flavor, it enhanced every bite of the fresh arugula, daikon, sprouts, carrot, and scallion vegetable medley. The "Udon" noodles were not udon-more like straight ramen-and were slightly undercooked, but absorbed the other flavors of the salad nicely. The black bean dressing was too thin, but provided a bit of additional dimension. 

The Carrot Ginger Lemonade was tasty and not overly sweet, but just tasted like regular lemonade. Although slightly orange in color, it contained no ginger or carrot flavors whatsoever. I would come back here if I need a quick meal in this area.

Tria Cafe needs to update their primary photo on Yelp. My fiancé and I came here specifically to eat the delicious looking truffle toast featured, only to find that it has not been on the menu for over a year lol. Fortunately, the experience overall was still good, but not great. 

Placed in a prime Rittenhouse location, Tria is a casual wine bar, with seasonally curated wine, cheese, and beer menus. They also serve a varied food menu of salads, sandwiches, toasts, and charcuterie boards.  No full bar, but the wine list is so good that you will not mind. 

We arrived around noon on a weekday, and were informed by the snippy hostess that no tables were available, but we could sit at the bar. This was confusing, because at least 4 tables were unoccupied at that point, and sat empty throughout the entirety of our visit. Fortunately, the bar seating was pleasant, and our bartender/server was genuinely friendly. 

I loved the tangy conserva tomatoes atop the Burrata Toast, but the cheese was bland, and I did not love the hearty bread. The Ricotta and Honey Bruschetta was overly chewy, but the pistachio herbed ricotta made up for it. I enjoyed the local cheeses featured on the PA Playlist Cheese Board, but the accompaniments were lackluster. It was only $22, so fair, I guess. I might come back here, but probably not.

If you are vegan and craving simple diner style food, you will love The Tasty. The ambiance here is laid back old school diner, and the menu includes many classic favorites like pancakes, French toast, waffles, etc as well as a variety of lunch entrees and sandwiches. Prices are reasonable, and service is very friendly and fast.

I tried the waffle with fruit and whipped cream, which was delicious. Buttery and fluffy, with sweet fresh berries. The sides of tofu scramble and home fries were also very flavorful and satisfying, but a bit too salty and oily for my taste. Canola oil aftertaste. Portions are generous. This is vegan food for vegans-the menu is a bit stuck in the 90's. I feel The Tasty should improve upon the variety of their menu and utilize a higher quality of vegan meat substitutes. It is 2016, after all. Definitely worth a visit if you are in Philadelphia.

My wife and I eat out 6 out 7 nights a week (empty nest syndrome).   We have been living in Doylestown over 20 years, allowing us to watch restaurants continuously recycle themselves..... Some times for the better sometimes for the worse.  

I tell you this so as to be clear that eating-out approaches a profession for my wife and I.  As professionals, we appreciate a well run restaurant.  Unfortunately, K.C. Prime barely approaches a rating of "amateur".  K.C. Has yet too open the Restaurant 101 manual......

Chapter1:  warm food.......warm plate.    (Guess the manager skipped day 1)

Chapter 2:  A salad, if prepared in advance (as was our's) should not be in a sub-zero environment prior to serving.   As seen in Chapter 2 of Restaurant management,  water freezes and expands in temperatures below 32F- causing a limp unappealing salad.

Chapter 3: a medium rare steak should be slightly warm to the touch in the center.   Nowhere in Chapter 3 does it instruct the cook (avoiding the term chef here at all costs), that medium rare should be cold and purple.

Chapter 4:  When associating costs of 30.00 to 50.00 for a steak - an 8.00 dollar charge for a veggie side is criminal.  Alas, one's plate looketh empty with just a baked potato and your under-cooked steak!  We'll occupy that plate real estate with a large frozen tin of butter....... Doesn't that look better!

Chapter 5:  Table linens - 

Manager skipped that day also, tables sport a dineresque appeal, faux wood and all.

Sorry KC........ We'll wait for the next occupant of this space.   Maybe they will get it right.

You know what, I take everything I posted before back! I had a terrible upset stomach all night after our dinner here. Coincidence? I think not! Such a shame they don't take the care to avoid any possible hazards or contaminations.
I only imagine if any of the poor souls on their first date there had the same problem... Not a good spot to be in!

I had the worst meal because Serena the owner continues to be rude , condescending and horrible to repeat customers. I've been in the restaurant industry for years and she should be fired for her trashy deliverance and rude behavior . No one should be made uncomfortable in her mediocre restaurant. She has repeatedly displayed rude and an sire of intolerance to those patrons she refuses to see as come back customers. I feel sorry for her employees as they also stated the same problems with her. I'll never eat there again. FYI she keeps increasing the prices as well. She's a demon! Don't eat there I highly advise!

I have been coming here for years and never had an experience like tonight. We had 2 rounds of drinks and my husband was completely coherent, not slurring his words, not swaying, etc. We  tipped very well and everything was fine. , my husband went to the center bar to order a third round for our party and two men in suits come and take his ID and tell him he got "cut off" very rudely. He was  treated like a criminal. He's not one to make a scene, so he just said "ok" and walked away. I talked with the "manager ", who stated that that is their right and had nothing to say when he visibly saw that my husband was not intoxicated. I'm really upset and won't be back. If my husband was intoxicated I wouldn't be writing this review. We accept responsibility for all of our actions and don't blame others for our actions. It should also be noted that on the way out, we stepped in a huge trail of blood, that nobody seemed to care about. We were just ushered rudely out the door. 

I have taken several time stamped videos of my husband, as well as I'm sure the cameras show him on camera completely sober. My husband was discriminated against and I will be seeking legal options.

"They have really big pizzas!"

"Are they any good?"

"There like 30 inches!"

"Yeah, but how is it?"

"The slices are HUGE!"

"..."

Below average pizza of unusual size.  Size doesn't really matter if 2 bites in the entire table is sharing the exact same 'meh' face.  Yeah, they are the only place with a pizza that big, so kudos.  This is definitely the only place around where you can order a comically large pie and a $100 bottle of wine straight from the jumbo-tron.  But that begs the question: Do we really need a pizza that big?  Do we really want a pizza that big?

Size aside, its just...not good.  Its not bad, mind you, but man, there are 10 different other (way better) local pizzas I could pick up and not need an F150 to bring it home.

Okay, let's get this straight.  Twelve Mile Limit is not a dive.  It's not upscale.  It's just a really good bar.  Now, I understand that the last statement can be pretty subjective, but allow me to lay it out for you.  

This place is tucked away on a residential street that hardly anyone will just happen upon.  Only the most well informed and adventurous travelers will streetcar out to Mid-City and walk the four blocks into a seemingly sketchy neighborhood in search of a good drink. There's a definite speakeasy vibe here with its location and door buzzer entry, but inside, it's just a laid back place for locals to hang out.  No undergrads, no bimbos, no bros, no creepy regulars doing the "stare you down as you walk in the door".  You could walk in here alone and walk out with five new friends.  
    
Once you're inside, take a deep breath.  Ah, no smoking!  The owners recently decided to make things smoke free, but there is a back patio should you need to light one up.  Plenty of tables, chairs and even a couch, but said couch is way too clean to bring this place down to dive status.  Some have claimed that this is a hipster hangout.  While the vibe is hipster-ish, I think the real hipsters have since moved on to the next "cool" place since this one is now probably too "mainstream."  The crowd is mainly the 25-40 yr old set most of whom are from the neighborhood.

Behind the bar they serve up quality cocktails in the $6-7 range.  (Yeah, I know, right?)  The Baudin is my go to: Bourbon, honey, lemon and hot sauce.  Simple ingredients, but downright addictive in the right proportions.  If you should get hungry, there is the amazing Shortall's BBQ dishing out some tasty meats and even a house made veggie burger.  They'll even make you an off-the-menu grilled veggie plate if you ask.  In the mood for something sweet?  Debbie Does Doberge makes do-bites, d-cups, salty balls (yes, chocolate is involved) and full on doberge cakes.  During happy hour you can get a shot and a do-bite for $5.  

What's not to like?
Really good bbq downtown. Beware they give you a lot of food and it's all good. If you are visiting town and want to try some bbq this is a great option instead of having to Uber too far.

I cannot describe the love I have for this place. About 3 years ago, my husband and I were looking for a nice place to eat for our anniversary and stumbled upon Iozzo's. It is now officially our anniversary tradition to go here! I also always choose it for my birthday dinner. 

The food is soooo good!! Ive had multiple things on the menu and not only is it delicious, the portion sizes are fair. You have to try the garlic bread and the black and bleu gnocchi for sure! 

The staff is also so nice. They are knowledgeable about the menu and very helpful with any questions you have. I've never had a bad experience with any of the wait staff.
