Things I would recommend: make a reservation! Every time we gone we are glad we made a reservation. Also request to sit in the courtyard! It is beautiful and very comfortable - definitely a fun atmosphere in the summertime. 

Overall a great place!

Love, love, love this place! It's charming with their extensive tea options, Japanese tea room and seating arrangements (some included sitting on the floor), events and vegan friendly entree options. My favorite to date have been the naan for you (vegan) and Brie and pear sandwich. Their pumpkin soup is also delicious. And if you're in the mood to try a couple different things, on the lighter side, order a "set option" which includes dessert.

Gee, let's put aaaall of F's consumable temptations underneath one roof & see if she won't go crazy. What the hell was this- a test from Buddha or something?!?!

Good lord, it seriously took me MAD will power to pry myself out of this joint. The spot with the southern food was aaaaight, the BBQ was bangin', the cookies were phenomenal. 

But the cherry on top- the ridiculously low priced sweet goodies the Amish were selling. EVERYTHING made freshly from scratch at great deals. I toootally stocked up on almost everything they had to offer.

*Deal tip: swing on by about an hour before closing, people start to sell their freshly made goods at deeply discounted prices in order to get rid of them.

All style and no substance. 

Popped in here at around 10pm after hitting a few other spots nearby. It's a beautiful building but sadly that's where the positives end.

It was very crowded when we got in, and the band playing seemed crammed in there. It was super loud and the band could've been great or terrible for all I know. The sound quality was shocking. Really tinny, especially when you got to the back area. 

My friends wanted to grab a bite so we got a high top table near the back. They got a couple of cocktails and a beer and asked the waiter what he recommended to eat. He said the hummus and the tuna tartare. Both came out before the drinks, followed by everyone's drinks but mine. When the waiter came back over we told him I was still waiting for my club soda and he visibly scoffed. 

Drinks are very pricey here - you can't get a nip of whisky for less than $16, mostly around $20. The cocktails did get a good review but I'm sure you can get comparable ones for cheaper elsewhere.

The hummus looked fine but it was a bit over-done, too herby. The tartare was brown, it looked pretty gross so I abstained. Everyone else tried it and confirmed that it tasted horrible and that the texture was weird. Between the low quality of these appetizers and the setting I don't know why you'd want to eat a meal here, unless you'd rather not hear your dining companions.

There's also only 2 bathrooms which queue out into the narrow hallway. 

Clearly there's some vision here, but unfortunately that didn't extend to any part of the experience beyond the aesthetics.

I've really never reviewed Freebirds?!

I studied at UCSB back in 2007, and Freebirds was the first place I ate at. Ironically (or fittingly!), the song Freebird was playing at Dublin's across the street. I had tacos and I fell in love. 

With the ratings they've already got, you don't need me to tell you how great this place is. It has remained consistent for the almost 14 years I've known it, and long before my time too. 

They're doing a nice job with social distancing at the moment. The line used to loop around inside, but now they've opened up the door closest to the front of the line/food service area and made the line go straight outside - so there are never more than a few customers inside ordering at any time. There are 6ft markers on the floor but people were doing a good job of spacing out regardless. The line looks long but it only took about 10 minutes for us, even though it'd reached the corner outside. The tables on the patio by the doors are disabled and they've added a bunch of 4-top tables along Pardall Road with a corden to keep people who are lining up at a distance from those who are dining. 

It's the usual ordering style - pick a type (burrito, tacos, nachos, bowl, quesadilla), pick your fillings, pay at the end. Their prices haven't gone up much in 13 years - it's still a little under $10 for a chicken burrito. Back in the day I used to get a quesarito sometimes - they melt cheese in a tortilla like a quesadilla, then put in the fillings and roll it like a burrito. So fat and so salty but so good.

The ingredients are always great. I usually get a chicken burrito with rice, refried beans, cheese, medium salsa, onions and cilantro. It's always fresh and they're always making more in the back kitchen. The staff are quick and friendly - I don't recall ever having an issue with service or food quality and I've dined here many tens of times. 

Their tortillas are always the perfect texture. The chips are also good, if you're a nacho person they make for great ones. I usually go for chips and guac - the guacamole is great too. I never usually order horchata but it's so creamy and delicious here, it's always worth adding on. 

I visit every time I'm in town. Long live Freebirds!

Great little fast-casual breakfast spot. 

I came in on a Saturday morning and it was lively but there were still seats. I ordered the Chicken. Set. Go. which is a breakfast biscuit with fried chicken, topped with pimento cheese and a few jalapeno slices, with cheddar grits on the side. Ordering is simple and the server confirmed our order as well as it displaying on the payment screen.

You order then take your buzzer and grab a seat. The food took maybe 10 minutes and came out hot. It's not a huge portion but it's definitely filling. I liked the biscuit as a sandwich, I ended up eating it open faced just for ease. The chicken was good quality, nice and crispy. I liked the pimento cheese a lot, too. The biscuit itself was a little unremarkable but it worked. I'd have liked to try the strawberry shortcake dish they make with it. 

The side of grits was pretty small, just a little 4oz cup, but it turned out to be plenty for me. They're very cheesy. I've only had grits a handful of times so I can't say if they were good grits - but I think I'd have preferred plain ones with what I ordered.

They have a good selection of Rishi teas, which I always appreciate. Though the water was super hot and the cup was kinda flimsy so I ended up pouring mine into one of the coffee mugs on the side.

You bus the table yourself but there were a couple of staff members around keeping things clean and tidy.

Great, classic spot. I was surprised to find an upscale restaurant like this right on Broadway.

I was out with my family and we'd been bar-hopping for a few hours when everyone decided it was time for a meal... at like 10.30pm. Most of us had flown in that afternoon and hadn't had a meal for hours. I did a quick Yelp search and Merchants looked like the spot. I was surprised once again to find they were able to seat us - a group of 8 - so close to closing time. 

The servers were very professional and efficient and brought everything out quickly. When one order was wrong they checked in multiple times to let us know it was being corrected, and they definitely rushed the order because it came out piping hot.

We ordered the devilled eggs and tater tots to start. The devilled eggs got rave reviews and everyone went nuts over the sweet pickles that came with them. The tater tots were some of the best I've had - they're cooked in duck fat so super crunchy on the outside while still having that great tater tot texture inside. It came with a few different dips. 

I ordered the mac and cheese - since I wasn't super hungry I asked if they had a smaller portion and they suggested a half-portion. Perfect. It could've been hotter but it was mega cheesy (a white cheese with a big pull - most of it ended up on my chin!). It had a nice breading sprinkled on the top, too. I saved some tots to eat with it. Perfect. 

They also have a shoe shiner in residence, who seemed to be very thorough. They give you some liners to cover your socks and you can have your shoes polished while you wait. 

All in, a great late-night dining experience, but I think you'd have a great regular dinnertime meal here, too.

Beautiful coffee shop with a creative menu.

This is definitely a premium experience - the menus are leather-bound and they have everything from espresso to cold brew to coffee cocktails. Yes, you heard that right. 

The baristas were welcoming and friendly, happy to make suggestions and patient.

I decided to go for a chai latte. It was on the sweeter side - not syrupy sweet but not super spiced either. A nice balance. The perfect size and had a beautiful foam top that held up and was super smooth. My companions got an iced tea and The Twist, which is a cold brew cocktail with a scorched twist of blood orange and foam on top. I do kind of wish I'd looked more closely and seen the Bela Rose on the menu, that sounds right up my street. Something for next time!

The decor is lovely, kinda rustic chic with nice details and hanging plants. As with many places in Downtown SB, there are some other buildings through the back and the bathrooms are shared in the back garden area.

The only downside for me was the seating arrangement. There are some 2-4 tops up front but there were lots of people working on their laptops, so we grabbed seats at a high top table at the back. I imagine these are better for bar service hours - the ground is uneven and on top of that, my stool was super wobbly, so it was a bit of a balancing act. 

It's rare to see a coffee shop in a crowded market do something so unique. Well worth a visit.

I visit Santa Barbara a couple of times a year and always make an effort to eat at Cajun Kitchen. They have a handful of locations now but this one is my go-to. 

They have so many great dishes here, but I almost always go for the crab cake benedict. The crab cakes are delicious with a nice peppery kick, and they don't douse it in too much hollandaise. I prefer the home fries over the hash browns, personally. They also have bomb sausage of various kinds, scrambles, and an amazing Jambalaya. Their sides like the sourdough toast, muffins, and cornbread are also great.

I hadn't had pancakes here in years and Pancake Day had just passed, so my brother and I split a stack of chocolate chip pancakes on the side. So good. We ate more than I thought we'd have room for. 

We had such a good time on the Saturday when we visited that we came right back the next day. I had the benedict again because I am far too lazy to make one at home and have only dined out a handful of times this past year. Well worth it! We also got the beignets - which I've seen for years and never tried. They're super light and fluffy with a delicious crust and the caramelized fruit topping is outrageously good. 

At the moment they're open with outdoor dining and takeout only. It wasn't too busy at about 10am on each weekend morning when we went as a group of 3. They've expanded the outdoor seating around the front of the building, which was a little blustery when it was windy out, but perfectly comfortable. Everything is spaced out well and people mostly wore their masks when they were moving around and when they weren't eating. 

Great breakfast and brunch spot. lol

Cool spot for a bite near Broadway.

My husband, father-in-law and I were looking for a bite after the Opry and when I checked the Yelp map, The Stillery popped up a couple of blocks away. I'd heard about it so we decided to check it out.

It was about 9pm on a Friday and the place was half-full. They have some local beers on the menu and lots of cocktails. I'd have liked to try one but decided I'd had enough for the night already.

I should mention that by this point in our trip we'd had several plates of hot chicken, devilled eggs, and other staples on the menu. 

I got the fried catfish and chips (as in fries) and my husband got the mac and cheese topped with hot chicken. The catfish dish was ok. The fish itself was cooked nicely and had a good texture. The coating was cornmeal based, which isn't my favorite, but the off-putting part was how salty it was. It really dried my mouth out. The fries were fine. The mac and cheese is super cheesy - I like the spiral noodle they use.

The pizzas looked really good, and I've heard good things about the cocktails too. 

Atmosphere-wise, it was lively and the music was very good and not too loud to have a conversation. 

I think at a different time I'd have enjoyed The Stillery a lot more. As it was, I had a good but not great experience.

Dear Matt the Miller, your service behind the bar sucks. Today was my third, and final for a long, long time, visit to your restaurant. Today was the final straw for me.

I sat at the bar for ten minutes before a "bartender" waited on me. This was around 1:30 and the bar was not crowded. There were six people other than me at the bar - nothing difficult. Three of your servers/bartenders passed by me without saying a word. Finally your bar dude told me he'd be with me in a while. I was about to leave when he decided it'd be fine for me to order a beer -- finally. 

On the other visits, your handlebar mustached barkeep was excellent! This guy knows his beer, was courteous, and an excellent bartender. I've not seen him since. The employees working for you now are horrible. 

Considering the price of your sandwiches and dinners you'd think your bartenders and help would be more professionals. I had such high hopes for your business, especially since you're in my neighborhood, but you're a pretentious menu with poor service. Good luck and good bye.

Wow oh wow, is this place good! Anis Hyderabad Restaurant has jumped to the top of the list as one of my favorite Indian restaurants in St. Louis. Forget about the mediocre Indian buffets around town.  This is the place to go for the good stuff.  

Located in a strip mall, AHR is set up as a fast casual restaurant.  You place your order at the counter, take a number to your table and then someone will bring the food out to you.  Plates, cutlery and napkins are available to grab at the front of the store. A television hangs on the wall to show the latest cricket match or Indian music videos.As the name indicates, the restaurant features biryani from the south Indian state of Hyderabad which is known for this dish.

The Hyderabad Dum Chicken Biryani was served as a large plate of deliciously seasoned fluffy rice with pieces of chicken hidden within.  Topped with raw onions, a boiled egg and a slice of lime, it was excellent. Even more impressive was the Tandoori Chicken. We were warned that it would take about 20 minutes to prepare the Tandoori, but it was well worth the wait.  It's the best I've had outside of India.  The half chicken was juicy and flavorful. I returned within a week to get more.

I was also impressed by the Chicken Tikka Masala and the spicy flavors that stood out.  A bit on the oily side, it's like home cooked Indian comfort food.  I took pieced of the fluffy and perfectly cooked garlic naan to scoop up this heavenly masala. 

On another visit, I tried the Chicken 65 and Bhindi Masala. Chunks of boneless chicken fried and coated with chili spices, the Chicken 65 was outstanding.  The Bhindi Masala or Okra Masala was as good, but I've had better.

A final paragraph should be dedicate to my absolute favorite Indian dessert, Double Ka Meetha.  This bread pudding dessert is a Hyderabadi specialty that you won't see in many Indian restaurants around St. Louis.  I took some of it home, heated it up in the microwave for a few seconds and then scarfed it down. My favorite Double Ka Meetha is still the cold version at Saint Louis Halal Meat-Baba's Restaurant on Page Avenue, but this one was almost as impressive.

My friend, who is a hot dog nut, suggested we come so that I could check it out.  I love a good dog, and I must say that this place didn't disappoint.  The menu includes creative topping for the hot dogs and fresh cut French fries.  Options include the Mac n Cheese Dog, Early Bird Dog with a fried egg, and the Hot and Spicy Dog with sriracha, jalapenos and fire hot Cheetos. They even have a veggie tofu dog.  Perhaps the most unusual offering is the Ice Cream and Fries served with a choice of vanilla or chocolate.   

After a thorough review of the menu, I decided on the Cali Dog.  This juicy baby came with beef-bacon, pepper jack cheese, seared jalapenos and BBQ Sauce.  It was the best frankfurter I've had in quite some time and the ratio of toppings to bread to dog were just right.   The side of fires that came with it were perfectly cooked and thick enough for my liking.  Overall, I just don't think it gets much better than this.  They even have the restaurant name branded into the side of the bun.  How cool is that?!

For a city with few vegetarian restaurants, Tree House is one of the best options around.  I've become a regular here and really enjoy the healthy and flavorful dishes when I'm in the mood to veg out.  

My favorite "small plate" is the Brussels sprouts salad for $9.  The crunchy cabbage and fresh herbs mixed with a sweet chili sauce is simple and delicious.  I've had it every time I eat here in combination with a large plate which makes for a good leftover meal.

The chile relleno for $8 is also impressive.  The roasted poblano with a panko crust comes with a light Mexican cheese, salsa and herb salad.  Sure it's not the greasy gooey mess that you'll get at a typical Mexican restaurant, but the Tree House's is a nice tasty and healthy version.   

For "large plates", I've tried 4 different dishes with my favorite being the chorizo tamale for $11.  I love a good authentic tamale, but recently realized how unhealthy these lard packed heart attack treats are.  Tree House's healthy version is surprisingly good.  Served with a black bean mole sauce and topped with a cabbage slaw, sliced avocado and a choice of queso fresco or vegan cheese.  I prefer the real queso cheese, but the vegan isn't too bad.  

I've tried the raw noodle bowl ($11) twice now and was surprised to learn that there is such a thing as raw noodles.  I'm told that the mung bean noodles aren't cooked, but soaked to soften them. Occasionally I get into a raw food phase but find it difficult to eat uncooked vegetables for very long.  This noodle bowl is a good option if you're into raw, but probably not the best option if you have cooked noodles in mind.   With a choice of 3 different sauces, I've tried the red curry and sweet chili, but not the lime-peanut.  Both were good, but I found myself wanting to add spice to liven up the dish. 

The stuffed eggpant for $14 is a huge plate of food with a baked eggplant halved and topped with roasted potatoes, bell peppers, leeks, onions, olives and a cous cous with dried fruit.  The beef bourguignon for $13 is made with seitan (wheat protein) and served with bread for dipping.  I enjoyed my sample of both dishes and would consider ordering them for myself.   

The Tree House also has a brunch menu on the weekends which offers a few items that aren't on the dinner menu.  I had the banh mi sandwich ($9) and really enjoyed it.  The crusty baguette comes with mushroom pate, Asian slaw, cucumber, jalapeno and herbs.  For $2 more, I added the seitan wheat protein.  This sandwich didn't stand a chance against me.  I'd order it again.  

5 stars for fresh, healthy and flavorful options!

I have a confession to make....Fratanga...I've cheated on you.  I've found a new love...De Palm Tree.  Don't get me wrong, I will always love you, but isn't there room for 3 in this relationship?

Serving up some kick ass Jamaican Cuisine, De Palm Tree rivals anything I've had in Kingston or Montego Bay.  Located in a strip mall, this little joint is so unassuming but  oh so good! We went on a Friday night and were quickly seated at one of the few remaining tables.  It's a small place and the service is slow as other yelpers have stated, so if you don't like to wait for your food, then don't bother coming.

When I try a place for the first time, I like to stick to the basics, so I ordered the fried plantains ($5.49) for an appetizer.  You can cook a plantain in so many different ways, but De Palm Tree's version is the traditional ripe (sweet) plantain fried in oil, slightly crisp and golden on the outside and soft in the inside. It's an absolute must if you've never tried before, and they were perfect here!

For my entrée, I ordered the Jamaican jerked pork ($13.95).  Honestly, my expectations weren't very high.  I was in Jamaica a few months back and had memories of the best jerk pork from the world famous Pork Pit in Montego Bay.  I can honestly say I enjoyed De Palm's version just as much.  Marinated in spices and roasted, the pork is served smothered in a delicious jerk sauce with a side of veggies and peas and rice (aka-beans and rice).  I found the spice level to be mild and didn't crack a sweat, but I do have a high tolerance level.  My friend ordered the Spicy Red Snapper and I was lucky enough to sample his.  The fish was cooked perfectly and seasoned well with a crispy outer crust and firm meat inside.  I'm looking forward to trying the curry goat and oxtail stew in the future.  

Unfortunately De Palm does not serve Jamaican Rum Cream, but they have a very nice rum punch and of course the traditional Red Stripe beer.  I didn't save room for dessert, but I've got my eye on the banana rum fritters next time, or maybe I'll order carry out sometime as I saw several people doing that.  

It was a nice surprise having to walk through the kitchen to get to the restroom.  I was able to watch the chefs in action and commend them for a job well done.

5 stars for great food, good vibes and laid back Jamaican service where no one is in a hurry.

I don't know where to start...I feel like a teenager who fell in love for the first time. I mean seriously...this place is off the hook! I think I've found my favorite restaurant of 2010 and like a teenager in love, I will blindly overlook the imperfections of this place and make excuses on it's behalf.

So let's start with those imperfections and get it out of the way so we can get to the important stuff: If you are in a hurry for a grab and go meal, then this isn't the place for you.  The service was a bit slow on my visit, however the way I look at it is that it adds to the authenticity of the place. It took maybe 15 minutes to get the bill from out waiter, which was mildly annoying, but not enough to break this love affair.

Now on to the good stuff: the food!  The cuisine is Nicaraguan and many dishes feature the plantain which is a type of banana that can be served sweet or starchy depending on the ripeness.  When it's still green, it can be cooked like a potato...fried, boiled, baked, roasted, mashed...etc.  I've eaten a lot of plantain having lived in Africa, but for some it can be an acquired taste.  

I ordered the repochetas (fried tortilla folded in half with cheese in it) for an appetizer and it was perfectly crisp and topped with slaw.  Great for sharing as you get 3 per order.  Our waiter brought out 2 homemade sauces which can be used on any dish.  One is a red salsa type sauce that has a spicy kick to it.  The other is a mild green sauce that is equally delicious.  A small dish of sliced jalapenos also comes with the 2 sauces if you want to kick it up an extra notch.  

For my main course, I ordered the plantain sandwich or "plantaino loco" with chicken (also available with beef).  I highly recommend this dish, which consists of a fried plantain sliced longways in half making a sort of sandwich stuffed with juicy & tender seasoned chicken and cheese.  The beans and rice and slaw that came with it were fresh and tasty.  Don't forget the red sauce, I put it on everything I ate!  My friends were also impressed with their dishes.  One ordered the whole tilapia which looked perfectly cooked.  She ate everything except the head and bones.  My other friend ordered the beef empanadas which I sampled and they were as impressive as my dish.  We were also given a plate of fried plantain chips.  I'm not sure if it came with the fish or if it was for everyone, but we all loved the chips.  

I woke up this morning thinking about the plantain sandwich and am planning a return visit very soon.  I'm going with a strong 5 stars on this place strictly based on the food and regardless of the semi-slow service.

I love little taco shops, so I was excited to finally try Taco Circus.  The cool thing about this place is that you can customize your taco by picking the type of tortilla, fillings and toppings.  So if you prefer a more traditional Mexican style, you can get a corn tortilla base with beef or chicken and cilantro & onions on top.  Or if you prefer US style, you can get a crispy corn shell with ground beef and lettuce & tomato topping. 

I ordered a trio of tacos.  The bean and cheese taco was very tasty as was the chicken fajita taco.  I couldn't pass on trying the St. Louis meets Mexico-pork steak taco. It was also good.  The chicken and pork meat were juicy, tender and packed with seasoning. A variety of hot sauces were available in the squeeze bottles located in the mini-fridge by the front door.  The creative Bernie Sanders sauce will make you feel the burn. 

I do wish the soft corn tacos would have come double shelled.  The quantity of fillings was so much that it was hard to contain while eating.  Overall, I'd rate this unique taqueria above average (3.5-4 stars).  It's well worth another visit in my book.

Ok, so I LOVE Indian food...It's my favorite! I've been to Rasoi twice now and I'm ready to review. 

Indian cuisine is one of the few that I can say I'm somewhat an expert in (At least Norther Indian cuisine).  I know it from traveling there and also living in London where Indian food is more common than fish and chips. 

I should start out by saying Rasoi features North Indian food, featuring many Punjabi dishes.  So for those of you saying you were disappointed because it wasn't spicy (hot) enough....well its not supposed to be!  Not all Indian food is spicy hot.  The basic rule I've always hear is that the farther south in India, the spicier the food.  

The most impressive thing for me was that I've requested two things that weren't on the menu and they were easily able to accommodate.  On my first visit, I immediately looked for Peshawari Nann on the menu and of course it wasn't there.  It never seems to be on the menu of many Indian restaurants in America for some reason.  I was pleasantly surprised when I asked for it and they said no problem!  Peshawari nann is your standard flatbread with nuts and raisins mixed in.  Rasoi's version was decent, but they get points for making it for me.  On my second visit, I noticed that they didn't have saga aloo (curried spinach and potatoes) and again they had no problem accommodating.

Of course I ordered a samosa for a starter.  I love samosas...or sambosas or what ever you want to call it.  Samosas are popular around the world in various forms, but basically consist of a fried pastry stuffed with anything from spicy veggies to meats.  I had the veggie one at Rasoi which was stuffed with spiced potatoes, onions, peas and other good stuff.  It was a good average to above average samosa, fresh and crisp.  It came with 3 sauces, a sweet onion tomato, BBQ-ish sauce, and the best one being the mint cilantro.  

My friends and I shared various dishes on our visits.  The prawn angarey dish wasn't bad (about 8 medium sized shrimp).  The shrimps are marinated in yogurt, red chilies and cilantro, then grilled.  It was good, but maybe just a tad bit overcooked.  Meth malai mutter is spinach, peas and fenugreek leaves cooked in a creamy sauce and it was nice.  The chana masala (chickpeas & sauce) and the chicken tikka masala are both nice.  Note that chicken tike masala is the national dish of the UK...not fish and chips...I think thats so funny! Another dish that we really enjoyed was the chicken vindaloo.  It's not considered punjabi but it was the best vindaloo I've ever had.  Usually vindaloos are so spicy hot that they make you sweat, however this was a milder version which allowed the delicious non-hot spices to stand out.  The paratha aloo wasn't bad either.  Paratha is another type of indian flat bread that is usually stuffed with something like potatoes (aloo).  It is greasy...but thats how they always are.  I almost felt like I was in Amritsar again.  I prefer using the breads like naan and paratha to scoop up the delicious sauces.  

The drink menu seems to be quite creative with some unique drinks. I can't seem to order anything other than a Kingfisher beer though.  It's a stander below average beer from India, but I guess I have this emotional connection with it.  

The atmosphere is nice and I especially liked the indian pop music that was playing and the Indian music videos on TV.  I felt like I was in Delhi again with the music videos playing.  You might want to make reservations on the weekend.  It was easy to get in on my weeknight visit, but on my Friday night visit, there was a long wait.  We opted to sit at the bar and eat there which was just fine since there were only two of us.  

We were told that Rasoi is developing a late night menu featuring some Indian-fusion dishes from a new chef.  I got a sneak peek at the menu and cant wait to try it! 

Overall, I'd recommend Rasoi, the food was on par with most Indian restaurants I've been to in London, and maybe even some of ones in India.

Wow! Tito's was amazing!  A few things you should know about me.  

1. I have a very sensitive stomach.  
2. I have never been to South America nor tried Peruvian food. 
3. The only Spanish I know is "Yo como manzanas." (Thanks Duolingo).

However, I am a big fan of delicious food.  Some of my fiance's co-workers had some friends who were visiting New Orleans.  They had met while doing Peace Corps in Peru, so of course they chose one of the few Peruvian restaurants in our fair city.  Enter Tito's Ceviche and Pisco.  

When we first arrived, I looked at the menu and was completely lost.  I asked for recommendations from my friends and the waiter (who by the way was excellent and made sure all of my needs and desires were met!).  We had two different ceviches to share - amazing, some pisco drinks - not my favorite, but others at my table happily finished my drink, and amazing food.  I couldn't tell you what I had if I wanted because I don't remember the name, but what I do remember is that every bite of food I had (whether on my plate, my fiance's, one of our friends') was amazing.  

Tito's is a little tucked away, on what my fiance refers to as "the easy to drive side of Magazine."  Because of it's location, though, parking is a breeze.  I'm excited for our next Tito's experience.

Is it weird that my mouth is watering while I'm writing this review?  Just thinking about my past experience at Boucherie makes me want to go back. 

My boyfriend and I came here on a whim wanting to try something new.  We started off with the duck confit appetizer.  It was  a little slow on the night that we went, so while we were deciding on our main course, our waitress brought us little tastes of things they were trying in the kitchen.  It was a great touch to our dinner experience.

For dinner, I had the smoked wagyu beef brisket, and my boyfriend had the pork ribs and elote.  Halfway through dinner, I could tell how much everyone in the restaurant was enjoying their food because of how quiet everyone was when they were eating. In New Orleans, it's typical to talk about other food you've had while you are eating, but not at Boucherie.  I cannot wait to go back!

I went with the Rule Breaker Cheesesteak w/ Salmon! Plus I got the Garlic Parm fries which were pretty good. The sandwich was the highlight of the meal though per usual. The salmon was made REALLY well and when I put the special sauce they give you on the cheesesteak it got taken to another level. Really happy with the purchase and everybody from my dealership is going to order from here in the future. The only thing that could've made the meal better was if the fries were made well. They were fried a bit too hard. I like crunchy fries but not overdone.

Husband and I went for the first time and brought my grandson with. Pizza was very good. We ordered a large thin pepperoni. The customer service was way above perfect. The lady asked if we needed a high chair but grandson doesn't like to sit in those. She then brought over paper and washable markers. When almost done she brought over more paper for him to color. She even asked him how the pizza was. The pizza was a hit for the grandson.

My fiancee and I went here after moving in down the street and it was the best decision I've made in recent memory. The food came out fast and tasted incredible, I'll be coming back. I ordered the Korean cheese steak and she ordered the chicken finger platter with Parmesan cheese fries and onion rings. The waitress was incredibly pleasant and the chef or owner (unsure who) gave me a slice of homemade carrot cake on the house. I definitely recommend going here if you're looking for a relaxed spot to grab great food.

I will never never go here again as long as I live. 

At first, it's hard to find but if you find it, leave. 

Wish someone told us that!

We sat down and looked at the menu and everything is extremely overpriced but I figured- it's NoLibs!

The alcoholic milkshakes are a nice touch.  There are delicious. I'll miss them! My friend and I also got cheesesteak fries. OMG they were delicious.  Freaking incredible.  

The bill was the part that sucked.  Here they add a 20% gratuity which I didn't even notice.  So I tipped him a good amount- as he was a good server, signed the receipt, and put the other printed copy in front of it. He collected it, thanked us, and then we were on our way to the car. I got up and walked out and the waiter  stopped my friend and asked if everything was okay because usually when everything is okay, people tip.  He said this loud in front of other patrons. He felt like an idiot and left a few bucks on the table. 

I knew I tipped so I went back, grabbed it and gave it back to my friend. That pissed me off.  I tipped him over 20$ and then they helped themselves to another 20%!  When I found out that they took 20% gratuity, I almost wanted to call them and tell them what happened.  It was really screwed up. Even if we didn't add a tip, you still got the 20% gratuity that you add to everyone's bill.  

I will never go back there again as long as I live. They are such douchebags. Don't go!

Enjoyed a nice lunch here.
The ambiance is casual but sophisticated.
The service was average from the servers.
I didnt see a smile.  The manager did impress us with his care when an item needed to be replaced.

You do have a talented chef here.  The cuisine is simple and elegant.  We ordered the mushroom flatbread, the chop salad, the ahi bahn mi, and the special of the day (shaved primed rib sandwich).

I take a star away for the dust behind the bar, the crumbs under the table, and the lack of value on the food prices.  You can call me cheap after you sweep the floor.

Great spot for kids, families, and couples.
Parking looks ominous but usually works out,
lines are long but move nicely,
find a spot outside while you wait with your pager,
Let the little ones play in the sand in the back,
and enjoy the ocean breeze, sunshine, and vibe.

This beach grill is legit!  The staff is friendly, and the food is pretty good. 

They also have tacos made to order on some days that you don't have to wait in the regular line for.  I passed on them because they were pricier than the regular menu.

My wife enjoyed her shrimp and avocado salad,
I loved my Roasted Chile Burger, and my boys attacked their kids meals. You can get a burger, quesadilla, mini corn dogs, grilled cheese or chicken tenders.  Kids also get to choose if they want fries, apple sauce or salad for a side.  Kiddos will also love the fresh lemonade, choc milk, juice or soda so bring them in.

Never been here?
Get here.  Now :)

What a great local spot for a cup of coffee and a bite to eat.  High quality. 

Make sure you order at the register.  Then sit down.
If you ordered food, they'll bring it to your table.
If you ordered coffee, they will call your name and you pick it up at the counter (even if you got food too).

The breakfast hash was top shelf.  Lots of flavor and nice portion control.  The poached egg was on point!

You'll love this place.  Ask for your coffee extra hot if you like regular hot.

Well Tim the bartender was completely amazing. A perfect host for our experience. That makes this a 5. The Nashville fried hot chicken. Well damn. Seriously. Just get it. Hot and spicy and sweet. With bacon Mac n cheese on the side. Save up the calories and do this. Oh, and Sunday evening is 2-1 beer. Sign me up.
Tucson finally got its own boba place, authentic boba brand from Taiwan. Definitely gotta try their milk tea! Grass jelly! Love BobaLife!

I cannot stress enough to people to shop here for produce and meat! Today I purchased :

Honeydew melon
3zucchini
3yellow squash
3avocados
Green onions
Head of cabbage
2vine tomatoes
Yellow bell pepper
Orange bell pepper
A huge carrot
4 large shallots
2.5 lbs of bananas
2 large yellow onions

All for $15!

You really cannot beat that!!!

Shop here!

Love love love this place! The lebna is so good I eat it on everything on my plate including the salad... yeah I have issues haha. Today we had gyro platter and a chicken/beef shawarma. Beef was a little dry but the chicken was good and the gyro was melt in your mouth tender and outstanding!! It will be my go to for now on here!

I have stopped in several times. They have vegan options that not every place has, which is their only plus at the moment. If you're being a responsible citizen and following mask mandates or CDC guidelines, do not go here. Walking by their business with the intention of getting my sweet fix, employees are not masked and most customers that I saw are not either. They have a "mask optional" sign posted in their front window as well. Steer clear!

We like everyone else read great reviews.  The address says Silverbell but it wasnt, this place is hidden behind McDonald's. 

Anyway, we arrived and seated right away, service was slow, my hubby had to ask for salsa several times, by the time they brought the salsa to the table he was done. She didn't even apologize. : (  There are not enough bean and rice on the plate, about a tablespoon of each on our plates. The tortillas were cold. The kicker was when we got the bill, they over charged us for the appetizer.  When we pointed out the over charge to the waitress  she didn't apologize.  All that she said was, the they would give us the difference in cash. We asked her why can't you just change the receipt,  she said that they don't do that. When we went to pay for the food, we pointed out the overcharge, she didn't apologize, but she did adjust the bill.

My wife has been to Ruth's several times for brunch with girlfriends, but until today I never capitalized on the opportunity to enjoy a delicious, low cost breakfast just 3 minutes from my apartment. 

My wife loves eggs Benedict, and always gets one here. She's had them several places around Indy, and always claims Ruth's to be the best. The reason I've never been until now? I hate eggs Benedict. Well, to be clear, I hate hollandaise. But, my parents wanted to do brunch near my apartment, so we did. 

Walked in at 10am to a full restaurant and a 15 minute wait for our party of 4. Seated in less than 15 minutes, no problem. 

As soon as we were ready we put our order in. To my delightful surprise, they have "huge pancakes" on the menu. I asked the waitress if they were big enough for me to only get one. She told me they are the size of a frisbee, so I went with one for $3. I requested a poached egg and a side of bacon. The waitress then offered something amazing: would I like them to mix bacon into my pancake batter and top it with additional bacon? Are you kidding? Please, do so. 

What I received was nothing short of amazing. I didn't even get charged to add the bacon, which was plentiful throughout the gigantic pancake. So for a coffee (which was filled an average amount of times), an egg, and a huge bacon pancake I shelled out less than $10 for my meal, with my portion of the tip. 

I'll definitely return over and over again. I'd like to say I'll try some lunch items and some of the daily scrambles, but I'll be honest, I'm going straight for that pancake every time I walk in those doors.

Owing an apology to my wife and knowing chocolate cake trumps flowers, I promised a date night which would end with her favorite cake, which is anything from Cake Bake. Excited, we ventured to Cake Bake on a Saturday afternoon. Although we've had cake from here several times, I hadn't actually been inside until this visit. 

After you manage to park somewhere that won't get you towed, you enter the shop. The shop is best described as a cross between Willy Wonka's chocolate factory and Dolores Umbridge's office. 

As I mentioned, my wife has eaten their cake several times, so I'm used to the sticker price of $9-$10 for a massive, delicious slice of cake. As we browsed the small selection of cakes for the day (they had a bunch of other confectionary but only 4 cakes for the day), we noticed one very chocolatey one that hadn't yet been cut: Earl's Court Chocolate Cake. We inquired at the counter and learned that the Earl is actually their most award winning and popular cake. The description I remember from the worker was chocolate with chocolate with chocolate on top. But, to be more clear, here's the website description: Layers of French Valrhona chocolate cake top with a layer of Belgian chocolate ganache, filled with a malted cream and topped with a dark chocolate fudge frosting. Sprinkled with Fleur de Sel from the Isle of Rea from the beaches of France (only harvested 3 months out of the year). This award winning cake has been served to Ina Garten, Jim Carrey, Elton John, Zac Brown Band & Peter Sidwell from Britain's Best Bakery in London.

We quickly decided on that and ordered. That $9 i'm used to? Not this time. Almost $13! Ok, a little sticker shock, but the cakes are huge and delicious. They took the cake away to cut it and came back about 5 minutes later. The cake had been massacred and we were given a small (compared to normal Cake Bake portions), ugly, sloppy piece of cake thrown into their box (see my photo).

Was it delicious? Yes, of course. But for $13 I expect the cake to taste delicious and look sexy. Before we went my wife said "I really should try cake at other bakeries, but I just can't bring myself to do it". Rest assured that after this visit we may look around before quickly driving straight to Cake Bake when that cake craving hits.

One of the best meals you can get in town.  We have been there twice and cannot wait to go back!

The four of us went there on a Saturday night and sat outside. We started out with a great but inexpensive bottle of wine and a very affordable cheese plate. For entrees, I had a great duck dish - so big and tasty, with a large portion of duck.  My wife had the croque madam - also great.  Our friends had other, fantastic dishes.  We also had a great dessert - nutella crepes.  Service was friendly and efficient.

The atmosphere is great - clean and modern.  The prices are extremely reasonable - cheap, really.  I just wish it were downtown, where we live.

We recommend it to everyone - we are very lucky to have such a big city, modern restaurant come to Da' Burg.

My friends and I travel an hour to go to this place! The food is consistently fresh, perfectly seasoned, simple and delicious! I don't think we have ever had anything we didn't like. 

I always recommend getting the grilled calamari (just trust me), and the gyro on a multi grain pita. The moussaka is better than anything I've had elsewhere. Even the salad is better here...

You'll see I'm not an enthusiastic reviewer at all times, but we love this place! 

The one con I have is one of their servers. She's great while you're actively ordering, but the moment you've had dessert, she's basically done with you. You have to work to get drink refills, order things to go, etc. That is always a big minus when my friends and I go in, cause we live far away and yes, we hold up a table for a while but we also spend a lot of money and tip well! 

Anyway, definitely give this little place a go-- and not just during the buffet. You won't be sorry!

$25 for their Standard tasting (a 5 pour flight) and $35 for the Specialty tasting (also, a 5 pour flight). They waive the tasting fee with a 3 bottle or more purchase and offer $1 ground shipping on 6 or more bottles.

We've been to Carr Winery three times in the past year and have had wonderful experiences each visit. It's located in an industrial area just outside of downtown Santa Barbara. The building is a Quonset hut style structure, which houses the tasting and barrel room. Just outside, along the street, is a beautiful little patio which is perfect for your tasting adventure. While we enjoy the inside tasting room, the patio has a cabana setup with comfy booths, covered tables, heaters, and string lighting for the ambiance.

On this latest visit (1/8/22), Ana poured for us and was an absolute joy. She told us that she recently moved down to SB from the Napa area and she was a wealth of knowledge about Carr's wines, as well as the wine industry in general. We'll definitely seek her out again on our next visit. We shared a Standard and Specialty tasting, as well as purchased a bottle of the 2015 Late Harvest Viognier, a sweet dessert wine that my Mother-in-Law loves (as do we). You can also purchase wine by the glass, and they have cheese boards and other snacks for sale. I always state in my reviews that wine tasting is subjective, but we love just about everything we taste at Carr and quite a few bottles made their way home with us.

The atmosphere at Carr is comfortable and welcoming. It's a very popular tasting spot, so it's best if you plan ahead and make reservations. I highly recommend you stop by Carr Winery on your next visit to Santa Barbara. Maybe we'll see you there!

Just mentioning the name "Bouchon" around town and you get oohs and aahs. This was our first visit, and we had a wonderful experience. Above and beyond service and delicious food. They currently offer indoor dining and a beautiful, converted street front patio dining area.

SERVICE: It's the little things that matter. When we arrived, it was cold and the end of a long, long day for us. Chava, Bouchon's hostess, checked us in for our reservation and then ran off and came back shortly with a chair for my 88-year old mother-in-law. She didn't need to be asked. Chava took it upon herself and set off the evening on a great note. Once she seated us, Christian was our waiter, with Roberto assisting and the two of them were fantastic. Friendly, efficient, and timed out all of our courses perfectly.
DRINK: Extensive wine list focusing on Santa Barbara County wine country wines. They also have beer, primarily Canadian and European brands, but also a couple from local breweries. We had a glass of the '19 Margerum 'M5' GSM ($15) and '18 Grassini 'Articondo' ($16.25).

FOOD: Three words...Fab U Lous! The menu isn't extensive, but there's something for everyone. We started the evening with a complimentary basket of bread and a couple appetizers, the Seared Pork Belly ($22) with roasted baby turnips, ginger-squash purée, mustard greens, and pork jus; and the Warm Pecan & Goat Cheese Tart ($15) with herbed chévre, baby frisée, pear, and pomegranate. Both were fantastic. The pork was more meat than fat, and the tart had bright, wonderful flavors in each bite.

For entrees, we tried the Pan-Roasted Mary's Free Range Chicken ($26) with roasted garlic-whipped potatoes, seared Brussels sprouts with pancetta & sage, pan jus, the Bouchon's signature Maple-Glazed Duck Breast & Confit of Thigh ($34) on a succotash of sweet corn, fava beans, leeks, applewood-smoked bacon and Windrose Farms butternut squash, port-thyme demi-glace, and the Grilled Center-Cut American Wagyu Ribeye ($42) with bouchon hash with yam, potato, white cheddar & bacon, seared broccolini, sauce bordelaise. The duck was one of the best plates I've ever had. The roasted chicken was juicy and delicious, and the ribeye steak was okay. Being the most expensive dish on the menu, I was a little disappointed that the Wagyu ribeye wasn't as good as the rest of the food.

To finish it all off, we ordered the Sticky Toffee Pecan-Date Cake ($12) with a blood orange caramel, persimmon compote, and a scoop of vanilla ice cream. Again, an amazing dessert with so much flavor, sweet, tangy, and nutty.

What a great experience. We will definitely be back for an encore.

Psychadelic! I lurve this pizza place! Located on the square of downtown franklin, the pizza is out of this world! My favorites are the white pizza and the barbeque chicken pizza. Freakin delicious. The calzone is good, but the amount of cheese in that thing makes me want to choke. The waiters are super nice!

Just dont. Why short change yourself into getting two small pieces of unseasoned, frozen meat when you can go across the street and get a cheesesteak with ACTUAL steak in it.  

Say no to Geno.

One of the coziest restaurants in Philly! I love the upstairs area, which feels small and intimate, great for dates, friend catch up time and lunches. The menu is fancified Italian, and be warned it is HUGE! There are plenty of options for everyone! There are two fish dishes (both the salmon and branzino were great), a couple chicken dishes, and plenty of meat and pasta dishes. All are full of flavor, and heartiness. I would recommend splitting the crab cake appetizer (which comes with gelato...there is actually a whole section of food + gelato combos!) and also the eggplant parm stack. Followed, by an entree each. And DEFINTELY try a couple of the gelato flavors! Absolutely best gelato I've ever had. So rich, smooth, creamy with intense flavor. I LOVED the white chocolate mint and mango/mint combination. Great service, location and food!

The food here is amazing! I didn't even mind the tight space, because it just felt cozy and intimate.

The mushroom flat bread was def one of the favorites dishes of the night, followed by the eggplant fries that were a tad spicy but crispy and moist on the inside, then the signature shaved salad that was so much bigger than expected, the scallops were also pretty good (note entrees are same size as appz), and finally the croquettes (which were a bit greasy). The dessert was this awesome dark chocolate bread pudding with caramel and ice cream.

The prices were also quite reasonable unlike some of the other places, and for all of those dishes it was about $30 per person! Plus priceless mouth memories! Can't wait to go back!

Was not sure where to park so we parked across the road. It was not marked other than 'This is a tow away zone.' 

We walked up to the window and ordered the crawfish sausage poboy with a side of Gumbo and a coke. The sandwich was done right. The bread was a crispy french bread with a nice remoulade and decent portion of sausage. The gumbo was served in a styrofoam cup. It was packed with meat. Nice roux. Tasty. (We added hot sauce to both but we tend to do that a lot.) The flavor of everything was right on. It does not need hot sauce or any other spices but when you like it kicked up a notch you got do what you gotta do. 

The paper towels on the table are a nice addition. They don't blow away on windy days. Be sure to throw away your garbage in the bin provided and they do recycle cans. 

Staff was friendly and I liked that they brought the food to you instead of making you return to the window to grab it. There are several choices in hot sauces too, try the Jamaican one! To die for! 

This is a nice shaded lot. You could sit there all day if you wanted to. They are open short hours though so make sure they are there before you go. They also deliver to the downtown part of Dunedin. They do offer a happy hour which is $1 off all Abita beer. 

We would love to return and try everything on the menu. Well done Happy's!

The first time I encountered Asiago's was during an evening of aimless wandering through downtown Boise with a work colleague.  We wanted to see what downtown Boise had to offer in terms of dining options and hadn't yet settled on what we wanted to eat for dinner.  Basically, we were two dudes, or bros, with a case of the syndrome that usually afflicts couples who have been together a long time and who make it a chore to decide what to eat for dinner, a.k.a. "hankering-paralys-eye-tis", which usually goes something like: 
 
Person A - "What do you feel like eating tonight?" 
Person B - "I don't know what do YOU feel like eating?"
Person A - "I could eat ANYTHING."
Person B - "How does Thai sound?"
Person A - "Oh, I'm not in the mood for that..."

Not very manly, but sadly that's what happens when you work together for 12 hours per day in fluorescent cubicle world and know each other too well and begin to adopt the tendencies of well, a married couple.  Anyhow, let me refocus.

When we saw Asiago's physical space from the street we thought that this would be a cool place: restored historic building, small patio out front, and loft-like interior with plenty of exposed brick.  Thankfully there wasn't a fern in sight or else this could have been an episode from Frasier. The restaurant itself is divided into three distinct dining areas, all of which are conducive to a fine evening of rehashing the events of the day.  We quickly glanced at the menu and that too appealed and so we decided to try the "Italian Inspired" food.

Upon entering, we did not see a well-defined greeting area and there wasn't anyone out front to offer a prompt hello.  So we waited until ultimately a server came out of the kitchen and saw us looking a little lost; we were then eventually escorted to a table to begin our evening.  If this were the only time that a proper and prompt welcome  were not given this would not really be worth mentioning, but I have been to Asiago's several times since, and each time the initial guest touch is lacking - certainly an area which needs some attention.

On to food.  I picked the sautéed chicken breast entree from the Seasonal Specials which sounded really good.  My bro chose the Bolzano, which was a pasta dish with a lot of fresh veg, tossed with garlic, red chili, and olive oil which was then topped with spicy Italian sausage.  When our entrees were delivered I took a bite and thought the chicken was dry.  Then I took another bite and confirmed my suspicions.  This bird was so overcooked, or sat under the heat lamp waiting for the pasta dish to be completed, that it was inedible.  I sent it back.

As a replacement meal to the desiccated bird that was originally placed in front of me I asked for the same pasta dish which my friend was eating thinking that it wouldn't take long to get that pumped out of the kitchen.  When the server came back to the table, he confirmed that to me that yes indeed the chicken was overdone and even the chef thought so and that my pasta would be out shortly.  OK fine.  Another glass of wine was ordered and delivered.  My colleague was enjoying his pasta and said that it was tasty.  

And then the wait began, again.  By the time my Bolzano arrived my friend was finished with his meal.  Even though my pasta tasted good, the meal itself was not at all satisfying.  The botched first entrée and the delay in getting out the second really derailed the evening since the attention was on the miscues rather than on conversation and just enjoying an night out.

Given that experience one might think that I wouldn't return to Asiago's, however that is not the case.   I have been to Asiago's several times and on each occasion I want it to be better than it is capable of being.  Here's my advice, keep the ordering simple and don't have any expectations that you will be eating "Inspired Italian" but rather as Asiago's states "Italian Inspired" food.

____________________________________

These are the items that I would recommend:

Insalata Caprese - simple preparation even though it can be overly drizzled with balsamic.

Mediterranean Piadina - this is my favorite item on the menu; grilled flatbread topped with all kinds of delicious greens and feta.  The hummus is a weird addition, but it is still quite good.

IL Fungo Selvaggio - this is tasty pasta garlicky, mushroom pasta, although very rich, it is quite satisfying. You will be able to have lunch the next day since the portion is quite generous.

Lasagna - staple on the menu but with different presentations.  Generous and tasty version here at Asiago's.

In 1631 the emperor Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal out of love for his wife Mumtaz, who died in childbirth. In 2012, four business travellers to Boise came close to having their love of Indian cuisine die after one of the worst overall dining experiences in a long, long time.  The owners of the Taj Mahal should be ashamed of themselves for their ineptitude in service and serving their overpriced and middling Indian food.  Awful, awful, awful all around.

I'd like to quote from some of the other reviews on Yelp of this restaurant before I get into my personal experience: Christy M. gives 5 stars and says 'It is expensive, but that's just Indian food." Ugh, Christy, have you ever been to Devon Ave in Chicago?  Cheap and amazing Indian food does go togehter but obviously not here at the Taj.  Rina K. gives 3 stars and states: "All of the (vegetarian) curries had a slight spiciness, but ultimately just tasted the same. And were so very oily. So. Heavy." Ugh, then Rina, how could you give 3 stars?  Is it really A-OK to have dishes that taste the same and are oily???  Barf.  David L.  gives 3 stars and states "Everything is made-to-order, so be prepared to wait a little while." Ugh, David, I don't mind waiting a little while, but 42 minutes after being seated we got our one order of vegetable samosa's.  Oh yeah, and the inside of the samosas were COLD!  Fried food that's cold, now that is really a special trick...this is not Alinea for goodness sake where one may expect a feat like that, where it is intentional, by the chef!

Now my turn...the Taj Mahal is located on the second floor of a poorly designed building in downtown Boise, take the escalator up if you must.  Once we were seated by the owner we were not acknowledged for at least 15 minutes.  The restaurant had a party of 6, a deuce and our party of 4.  What is it with Boise restaurants and their inability to greet customers promptly and get water to the table in less than 5 minutes?  This is the second Monday in a row that this has happened. Unacceptable.    

After waiting 15 minutes we thought it would be best if we placed our drink and dinner order at the same time; we ordered one appetizer and our three entrees for sharing.  The drink ordering was silly; the owner told one of our dining companions that water was only available for those under 16...ok fine, cute and funny, but then when I said I just wanted water he kept staring at me to add an adult beverage, which I didn't want...the other three people at the table requested beer and wine isn't that enough upselling from water? So one would think that after we ordered our drinks and waters we would get them soon afterwords.  We watied another 15 minutes after that!  30 minutes into the dininig experience and our first drinks arrive.  WTF?  The way the drinks were delivered would have been worthy of a Three Stooges episode: the owner carried two drinks at a time so he had to make three trips to our table to serve our party of four.  Why three trips?  Two beers, one trip.  One water and one white wine, second trip.  One water, third trip.  Curly, can you buy a beverage tray and do it all in one trip? 

The samosas arrived to our table, if you recall, 42 minutes after we were seated, with a runny, thin mint chutney, some raita, and a sweet tamarind dipping sauce.  They were cold so we asked for another order.  With the Jeopardy theme music running through my head I wondered if we were ever going to eat.  We should have left at this point and gone to another restaurant.  We didn't.    

Finally our food did arrive.  The Chiken Tikka Briyani was OK, but had too much of that fake tasting curry.  Chicken Korma and Chicken Tikka Masala were indistinguishable from eachother.  I think that's what Rina K. said about her veg enterees...same goes for the chicken dishes.  I couldn't discern much, if any difference between the two dishes.  Oh yeah, we had some Nan which was by far the best part of the meal.  In addition to the extreme wait to get our drinks and our food, the other aspects of service were deplorable.  Dirty dishes from the 6 top were never cleared from the dining room so we had a view of their stacked plates and empty glassware throughout our meal.  The deuce was desparately looking around to pay someone so that they could leave this hellish restaurant.  Another deuce was seated but wisely decided to leave before they got the full Taj treatment.  When we were finished with our meal our dishes were never cleared.  The owner asked if he could remove my dining companions partially finished beer glass while the remanants of our meals remained on the table.  He said 'no, I'm not done with my beer' and then the owner walked away from the table without removing the dirty dishes.  Inexplicable. 

In 1631, Shah Jahan was grief-stricken when his wife died during the birth of their 14th child.  In 2012 I was grief-stricken at having chosen to have dinner at Taj Mahal Boise.

I'm used to dine at Brio's in Fair Oaks Mall in Fairfax VA and it's way better than this location!
It was empty around 3 pm when I stopped for lunch on my way to NJ with a client and from here started the horrible experience!!

A waiter who is very unprofessional and know nothing about customer service!! 
Took a long time to come take our order , long time to bring the food, long time to bring the check!!
When my client asked for a melted butter on her food he said we don't have melted butter! She asked him , could you heat a piece of butter, melt it and bring it?? 
He said yes and then we heard his rude comments about it with the chef at the open kitchen counter!

Same thing when my salad tasted so bad and first I thought it's that type of salad and I asked him to change it to a different salad that I know how it should taste very well (ceaser salad) , I also heard his rude comments with the kitchen about it!!
Apparently the lettuce in the salad is not fresh at all!!! Disgusting and could be a Health issue!!!

The food was tasteless and very small portion on my spaghetti!!

NOTHING WAS GOOD TO MENTION!!!

AVOID IT COMPLETELY AND GO TO CHEESECAKE FACTORY AT THE SAME MALL!!!

This was my first time ordering from Ming's, and it was  extremely underwhelming to say the least. I ordered Sweet & Sour Chicken the chicken was overcooked, and super dry. For $15 this was a giant waste of money, the meal came with white rice not fried rice, along with no egg roll and the sweet & sour sauce was gross tasted like it came out of a packet. Why oh why didn't I stick to China Rose. I'll probably never go back to Ming's.

I'm starting a brand new year at a throwback landmark. The Chattaway has been operating on this corner since either 1921 or 1951 (competing signs out front say both) but either way, it's loaded with history, whimsy and charm. You can taste the love that's gone into this long family-owned restaurant and that's probably the best of so many reasons, why it's beloved. 

Located in a little pink building, The Chattaway sits under huge shade trees, that could probably tell great tales. Your walk from the parking lot takes you over a little bridge and into an adorable garden setting-that's part 1950s, part surfer, part vintage tiki and a whole lot of old Florida charm. It's quaint and quirky and fun. There are tables, booths and picnic tables outside-and on the Saturday afternoon we were there-also, live music. (Not too loud-we could still talk comfortably-just a nice backdrop). The tables were clean, the service fast and efficient and the menu was diverse, with vegan, vegetarian and gluten-free options. My friend had the veggie burger and I had the blackened grouper sandwich, with sweet potato fries. We both liked everything. My grouper was a generous size and the fries were great! The soda comes in cans-and I've read that you can get free refills. I think they serve beer and wine-maybe even cocktails. I know they don't accept cash, but there's an ATM on site. And... there's also a gorgeous, British-themed indoor dining room, where Anglophiles can bask in the English memorabilia and even take in afternoon tea (call ahead for that. I believe it's $35 or $40 for one). 

The Chattaway is the perfect getaway-to a slower, gentler, friendlier time. I will definitely be back.

If Willy Wonka wanted to open a bake shop and hired Alice In Wonderland's decorator, then sprinkled a little Moulin Rouge/New Orleans vibe throughout: you'd get Dough! 

It starts before you even walk in the door of their fairy tale inspired building along south MacDill Avenue in Tampa. I walked in right at opening at 7am on a Wednesday and they were glad to see me. I ordered a breakfast sandwich (bacon, egg and cheese on a brioche bun-oh that bun). It was good, but I only ate half and saved the rest for later, after seeing the maple bacon doughnut come out. No puny bacon bits here, there's a pile of the good stuff-cooked to perfection, perched on top a deliciously fresh and squishy maple glazed doughnut-that was also cream filled. It's decadent and divine. I'll gladly add extra workouts to earn those calories. Yum-o-rama! 

There are all sorts of fabulous and elaborate cakes, cheesecake, cupcakes, milkshakes, cookie dough pops, doughnuts, coffees and teas available, and all sorts of pre-packaged candy, flavored popcorn and other treats, to take home, too. It's a dessert-lovers dream! And the food is only one of the delights. The jewel box decor is family friendly by day and sort of moody/romantic by night (I believe there are boozy shakes available). 

By the way, sweet isn't limited to the menu. My thoughtful and generous server threw in a free Fruity Pebbles doughnut for me today-one of their signature items. What a gem! I'm saving it for tomorrow. 

I got there before the morning rush, which was awesome-I had the place to myself for 30-45 minutes. Parking was a breeze, then. (There are a few spots out front and I believe more in the back or or on the side) This is the sister restaurant to Datz, which is right next door, so you could make a big night of it and end it here. 

Tip: check out the rewards program-it's free to sign up and I believe it's 20% off your first order at any of their restaurants/locations, which includes Dr BBQ. 

Inventive, indulgent, incredible-do(ugh) check it out!

I unfortunately didn't get the chance to eat at Muriel's because of their ignorance and discrimination against me and my friends. Upon walking in, we were told there was about an hour wait. We went back to our hotel around the corner to freshen up and kill some time before our reservation. Flash forward to an hour later. We show up, dressed in nice attire, and the wait begins. We became a bit suspicious of what was happening when a family of 4, no reservations, walked in 10 minutes after us and were immediately seated. We kindly asked the front of house staff (who at this point were pretending we weren't standing there) what was happening and they told us we weren't being seated because there was a dress code. Minus the fact that we all have tattoos, our attire was far njcer than 75% of the patrons seated in the restaurant. Upon speaking to the manager he said there was no dress code....

As a business owner I cannot express how upset it makes me to discriminate against people for their appearance. Muriel's may have well told us we couldn't be seated because of the color of our skin. I will never ever go back to this terrible establishment and I will make sure to spread the word that they have the absolute worst front of house staff, including the "manager", I have ever come across. 

Thank you for proving that terrible people still do exist and that they tend to stick together, Muriel's.

Our first experience was definitely a memorable one. As everyone has mentioned, do not be deterred by the building itself. It's definitely scary from the outside, but a completely different story once you're inside. I suppose it's expected considering the area.

The bar situation is interesting, considering the kitchen is the bar? It's different, but fun watching everything that goes on. Plus, there's happy hour at the bar. (:

Anyhow, our waitress was very nice and accommodating. She was a little overwhelming, but I think it was just because she was extremely friendly. Their style is definitely personable, not the prim and strictly professional type of service. If this was a restaurant located up north, I think it would have bothered me, but the area lets this place get away with a lot of things that would otherwise not be as acceptable. 

I do have a gripe though, but I made up an excuse for her I suppose... Sitting at the bar, patrons can see EVERYTHING that happens "in the kitchen." Therefore, I earnestly emphasize the need for being careful when it comes to health code violations. Twice, I saw her cut bread with her bare hands. She also picked them up to plate them with her hands after she picked up the phone or someone's check, etc. I feel for her though, because even though there were two waitresses, she was honestly running the whole restaurant by herself. It still cannot be overlooked, so just a warning to be more careful !

Food on the other hand... Fantastic ! We started with the mussels. They're a must-try. For entrees, we had the Braised Lamb and the Linguini with Clams. Everything was cooked to perfection and seasoned wonderfully. Portions are definitely large. I'm pretty sure I had left overs for about two days. Oh, and I LOVED their sangria ! It was dangerous... I swear it didn't taste nearly as potent as it actually was. 

$75 for lunch was a tad pricey, but the food was worth it in my opinion. We'll be back, for sure. Thanks Steve, the chef (owner?), who definitely knows what he's doing in that kitchen !

Zen is a hidden gem! It is truly hidden....in the back of an Aldi plaza. I frequent Zen because I really enjoy their Pad Thai and they are not a far drive for me. The interior is nothing to brag about. Several dining tables  in a long rectangular area. They also have a newer addition with more seating to the left when you enter. 

Zen's staff are always extremely welcoming and service is prompt. They greet you as soon as you enter and get you seated and your drink order. Food comes out fast! They have a decent selection of yummy appetizers. I usually get potstickers or crab rangoon, but have tried almost all of them and have not been disappointed. Zen offers a small selection of beer, wine and fountain sodas. 

Zen's Pad Thai is my favorite! I tell myself I need to try other dishes, and once in a while I do, but I always come back to the Pad Thai. The noodles are the perfect thickness, crushed peanuts on top, bits of egg, large scallions and a lime on the side to squeeze over the top....yum! The other dishes I have tried were also very good! If you are looking for sushi, Zen also offers a large sushi menu. Welcoming, prompt service and delicious food is why I frequent Zen!
overpriced. Squid tempura cost $17.  specialty rolls cost around $15. Food doesn't taste good either. I Would not recommend.

This was a very challenging evening. The back story is we had previously enjoyed a dinner when the Somerset first opened. Service was off but we accepted that these were minor growing pains. Made plans to bring two visiting couples for a nice dinner to celebrate a life event.  Wrong decision.

Let me start with out dinner. The food was good but our dinner was delivered warm, at best. My issue is beyond the food. It has to do with the overall experience, cleanliness issues and management. 

We were seated outside next to the wood burning fireplace. Over the course of the evening we became covered in soot. Several members of our dinner party now need to have our clothes professionally cleaned. Our hands were black by the end of the evening. Faces were covered in soot. It all happened gradually and we didn't realize this until the end of dinner.

The next issue was a difference of opinion on corkage fee. Prior to arriving at the restaurant we checked their website to confirm their corkage policy. No where to be found. When we were charged $40/bottle we told the waiter we were expecting something closer to $25 to $30/bottle. 

On our way out the manager had the opportunity to speak with us and ask us about our experience. This is where it all went downhill fast. The attitude of the manager was dismissive at best. He argued
over the corkage, ignored our concerns about the soot and generally displayed the wrong attitude for a service business. 

Epilogue- one of our guests ended up with diarrhea possibly due to the uni. 

There are many great choices in Santa Barbara. Regrettably this is not one to consider. It had the potential to be great. I doubt that they will make it largely because of the sub par managers they employ.

Big disappointment. Three strike night. First off we waited an hour for our group of 7 to be seated.  Told no reservations. Turns out a "friend of the owner" called in and they held a table for them that should have gone to us. Strike 2 - and this is the worst - they ran out of ribs and pulled pork by 8:20 pm. There's no excuse for a BBQ restaurant to run out of food by 8:20. Third strike was our server Ashley. Not one smile. Not even a slight attempt to lighten the mood. In the end all our table was able to order was the brisket, which was average. 

It might be that they have great ribs. We'll never know and we'll never return. We paid for food and service and received none of what we really wanted. After all, the point of dining out is to be provided both a great meal and great service. Wildwood failed us miserably. Overall ruined an otherwise nice afternoon with friends and family.

Not bad but not great.  We tried the curry ramen, the vegetable ramen, and the salmon ramen all for takeout.  The packaging was good with the broth in a separate containers.   However, all three broths fell a bit flat and not very flavorful.  The mushrooms in the vegetable ramen were overly chewy.  I also don't think the noodles are made in house as they lacked that al dente fresh noodle flavor I've had at some of the top ramen places I've eaten at.

I had high expectations based on all of the glowing reviews and unfortunately  they did not earn one more from me today.

Pretty good local eatery that the Indy government reps we were meeting with recommended for lunch.

I had the grilled chicken sandwich with chipotle mayo and a serving of fries. The portion was large and the chicken was cooked nicely but there was barely any mayo on the sandwich.

Service was friendly and attentive while the prices were reasonable.

I wasn't a tremendous fan of the pizzas we got for take out. The only one I really cared for was the sausage and pepperoni which surprised me as I was expecting the margherita or their regular pie to be the most impressive based on my visits to the original establishment. 

I found the sauce to be poorly prepared, it still had seeds in it, and that there was far too much of it on the pies. The crust was good even though it was takeout but it couldn't compensate for the lack of detail to the pizzas.

Really great gastropub with a tasty, curated beer list and some innovative cuisine.

We opted for the Caesar salad with steak and some devilled eggs. The salad was very artfully prepared and came with cheesy/creamy croutons which were amazing. 

The eggs were also very good and were served with a small side of beet salad.

The beers were all winners with plenty of options on tap or canned. I had a local saison that was amazing.

Service was very friendly and accommodating.

Hands down some of the best pizza in Philly. Great pies with lots of flavor. The thin crust is awesome and really makes the pie. We tried it with a Groupon but we will be going back permanently after 2 times of eating here. No take out which stinks because some days I don't want to sit in and tip a waitress and would rather just eat at home but I can't take away from the their food quality with the rating. Try it you'll love it.

I've been eyeing this place up for a week or so since reading some reviews from fellow Yelpers. I'm usually not a fan of trying places so soon after opening since there's usually so many aspects that can go wrong in a new business. I'm glad I broke my rules about that. 

We decided to stop by for drinks and dessert after getting dinner elsewhere. Testing the waters, ya know? We walked in and the host was very welcoming and asked why we were visiting. We promptly invited us to sit in their seating area at the front of the restaurant while they cleared two seats at the bar. 

The church itself is super cool. I always dreamed of turning a church into something else so I totally dig the vibes in here. Halfway through is sitting at the bar red mood lighting came on adding to the cool affect of the place. 

The drink menu is fairly diverse so it took us a hot second to decide what to get. The boyfriend got the Board Meeting..a pricier scotch and bourbon cocktail. He later also ordered an old fashioned. I ordered the High Tide, a boozey rum drink that the bartender warned was indeed boozey. But I'm ok with that..it was delicious. 

Instead of dessert we opted for the cheese plate. Three picks: the pepper cheese, feta, and (our fave) honey. It was served with a flatbread of sorts. Definitely a good choice. 

The service was great from what we saw at the bar. Everyone was very friendly and accommodating. Even as we exited the host remembered us and asked us how everything was. We will definitely return for dinner..hopefully before the cats out of the bag about this place and it gets too popular. (I have a feeling it will be.)

Okay!! Now I get it!! Nashville Chicken is amazing. This place was recommended to us by our AirBnB host the first night we got there. It was raining, a Friday and about 10pm and that line was LONG! Luckily we got a seat on the outside deck area. 

I order the Chicken Tenders and a side of Mac. Oh and do not forget that LEMONADE...WOW! Almost had to have an intervention to get me unaddicted to that stuff! The Chicken was full of flavor while being so simple! Trust me, there really is a difference and Nashville Chicken is some of the best Chicken! The Mac was okay, but I didn't go there for that.

The service was great and everyone that worked there were super friendly! You definitely knew I wasn't from around there when I was ordering haha! They were great though!
