Anyways, so I wanted to go back the next day.. We drove by, the place wasn't even open yet and there was a line down the street! We ended up not going, but I will tell you, it is WORTH the wait in line! Every last bite! Enjoy! :)

Probably one of the worst deliveries EVER..
. I will never eat here again. It seemed disorganized and disgusting. The only delicious thing was the cheesy fries, except I felt like having a heart attack after, but my choice. The rest of the order was questionable. The sand which had disgusting peppers and the salad had peppers old croutons, and dirty salad. Would I recommend it? Ugh NO.

Such a delicious, affordable, hearty meal with some clever fusions. Bringing together Philadelphian classics and some Korean flavors. The Bulgogi cheese steak was my favourite, best married with the homemade Sriracha sauces. The portion was great value for money and beyond what my stomach could fit. But for such great tastes, I had to make extra space. The meal was best finished off with the Lee's iconic dessert- the Carrot Cake. Bring some home for your family and friends too.

Giant cupcakes with tons of personality! Not only are their cupcakes big enough to serve at least 2 people, the cake itself is fluffy and moist, the frosting isn't too sweet, and the themes are clever and cute! Their menu rotates throughout the year so there's always something new to try. If there are any cupcakes with a chocolate ganache filling, definitely get it!!! 

Also, they serve savory food! I got their Famous Barr french onion soup, which was a blast to the past and gave me all the warm and fuzzies. In was rich in flavor and not too salty.

I finally have a go-to Mexican restaurant in STL, and this is it! 


My overall favorite thing about Taco Circus is that their individual items really let you try a lot of things without getting too much food or spending too much money. So if you want 3 different street tacos, that's like $10, and a big portion that's so so delicious! I hate when I have to get a taco plate w/ beans and rice and selected meat like at other places, but TC is all about the options. 

Everything I've gotten here is wonderful, but my favorites are the street tacos (all meats are fantastic, with my favs being skirt steak and chicken al carbon) and the queso! Ohh and their street corn is also delicious, and cut into the perfect chunks so you can share it with other people. Also, their house margaritas are delicious and not too sweet. My friend who hates tequila, she loves their margaritas and are the only ones in town she'll drink. 

Definitely go check them out! Their patio is amazing during nicer weather and their indoor decor is super quirky. Also if you're going during COVID, they're VERY safe, with tables spread out and a temperature check at the front door. I recommend eating there if you can because their takeaway wrapping is kind of weird (they use aluminum foil which kind of crushes the tacos...I hope they adjust that), so head there soon!

It seems the farther south I travel on Delmar, the better the Gyros get. I owed them a visit after a mix up with Gyros in the Loop and someone corrected my review. Thank goodness for mistakes and corrections! The parking, first of all, is much easier than the aforementioned place and certainly the view of the Pagent is nicer. The decor is also more upscale, if that matters to you, but if I were to bring a date, this would actually be impressive and might draw attention away from my utterly twisted and scarred mug.

I was only interested in the Gyro but the other menu items proved that this is the place for authentic Greek cuisine, as opposed to a sit-there-and shove-a-sandwich-into-your-moosh kind of dive. As with my review of Gyros in the Poop... er, Loop, it was piled so high, I couldn't even fold it to eat with my hands. So, who should complain about a healthy portion? The meat was nice and spicey but not too much for those who prefer not too much spice. Flavorful is a good way of putting it! Perfect amount of lettuce and sauce and as I don't eat raw tomatoes because they look like something in the larval stage of development and not ready for consumption, I can't tell you about those. I suspect they are very fresh, judging by everything I could see in and behind the counter.

The staff was very friendly and the pretty girl with too much eye liner, which I actually like, was very helpful and chatty and made me feel like I was a regular. There was no problem with the service and everything I sampled certainly gets four stars. Next time, I'll try something different... if I can resist the Gyro and eye liner.

I usually don't like to rate a restaurant poorly when I've only experienced it once but when the total experience is so horrid that I fear a return visit, I have to spill my guts... sort of like just after my first visit to C.J. Muggs.

Firstly, with a huge clientele of lawyers in Clayton, I would think they might keep it all on the up and up to prevent multiple lawsuits. In fact, I was treated to lunch by my lawyer and I could see by his face he was as disappointed as I was. For an attorney to drop his poker face, you know something has to be wrong.

Aside from the waitress coming back several times to ask us what we ordered, not reappearing enough to refill our drinks and failing to bring the condiments we asked for on at least two occasions, the service was horrid. The odd thing was that it was well after the lunch rush, so there was little excuse for troubled service.

Not that I'm a snob, but the rest of the staff was taking a break, filling condiment bottles and chatting loudly just two tables away. According to the endless Bar and restaurant stakeout/rescue shows I've watched, that is one of the things they immediately stop in every place.

On to the food, if one lowers their standards of the category of what passes for edible food, this didn't make it. I know that a place which caters to lawyers is probably use to their clientele just unhinging their jaws to swallow large rodents whole, but I ordered the Buffalo Chicken Sandwich and was really having problems with it. Had our waitress returned, I would have sent it back but I was starving and we had to get back to my attorney's office.

The chicken, which is fried, was burned, hard and crunchy, rather than crisp . The buffalo sauce should have moistened the crunch but I guess they were low on sauce or just stingy. The bun was dry and tasted a bit of being a day over the stale mark. As any good cook would know, you take a bun of that size, spread butter or a touch of oil on the underside and toast is lightly so the bun is warm and slightly moist on the sandwich side.

As for the chicken, the cook should have looked at what came out of the fryer and thrown it away. Instead he or she decided it was good enough to serve and now you can live with this review... or die with it. Frankly, I don't care!

I was so bummed when the Loop location closed. Bad move! It's not as easy to get to the CWE location for me but when I do, they are friendly, efficient and the pizza reminds me of the place where I was born, in the Bronx. Yes, even Bronx babies are fed pizza...right before we're given our first switchblade.

Tastes just like home but without the random violence! If you're from New York, this is the place to get a taste of home but without the urine puddle in the corner and some homeless guy trying to grab your order so he can hand it to you and get spare change as a tip.

I stayed away for years because of that name, so shame on me and my punishment was missing the food.

It won't be as fresh as sushi on the coasts but by using different ingredients, sauces, panko and lord-knows-what , they create some delicious dishes.

It's not cheap but the service was always good and friendly. The sushi may not be the freshest but I've always found it to be moist and quite acceptable or better.

This might be the best coffee in New Orleans. Surprising for the heart of the FQ, where mediocre catering to tourists in t-shirts from their hometowns is usually the norm..

I have multiple favorite coffee spots, but Spitfire is somewhere near the top of the list. The service is good and they know what they're doing. Every 7th coffee is free. They use the highest quality beans. They don't have gimmicky drinks, although they do experiment here and there. And they're friendly, unlike so many of the hipster haunts that have become normal in New Orleans (if such a thing can even exist).

Highly recommend the cortado. Just enough milk to cut the espresso, without ruining your ride with training wheels.

I sometimes feel like I give too many 5 star ratings. If I could I would give Compère Lapin 5+ to distinguish it from the other starbursts I've given.

I took a friend here on his first night of a recent visit to New Orleans, after having heard the rave reviews and stories about Chef Nina Compton. Not only were we thrilled by Compère Lapin, but it may have been the best meal we had during his whole visit, much of which was spent dining at some fo the city's finest establishments.

Highlight 1: the black drum may be the best fish dish of my life. And I live in New Orleans, where cooking fish is to the rest of the world what a Paris fashion show is to an average Walmart shopper. Do not be put off by the simple description: "Black Drum/Squash/Beurre Blanc/Caviar." And do not be put off by the caviar, if that's not your thing. It's so smoothly incorporated into the beurre blanc, which is creamy and citrusy, perfectly blanketing the fish, that it adds only flavor, and none of the off-putting 'salty pile of fish eggs' that is most peoples' experience with caviar.

Highlight 2: Pig ears. No, they're nothing like what you feed your dog. A great, salty snack, that would be as fitting on a beer bar as it is leading off a fish dish with caviar.

Highlight 3: Everything else we ate was also delicious. Everything. Especially the Stracciatella (which is cheese, not ice cream).

Highlight 4: A cigarette machine has been repurposed as an artwork dispenser in the lobby of the Old '97 hotel where the restaurant is located.

Lowlight 1: At first I thought the service was going to be overbearing. It wasn't. It was some of the best service I've had in a long time. So I tricked you, that's also a highlight.

Lowlight 2: I didn't get to try more of the dishes, and now when I look at their menu there are so many other things I'd like to experience, and I simply can't fit them in my belly in one visit. So that's another highlight, there's more to try. The low part is that it's not a cheap restaurant - especially with wine and/or cocktails it verges on 4 dollar signs.

Wow. Best sushi in town, no doubt. There are SO many sushi places in Reno, but this one is something special. It always seems younger and more lively than other places, and the staff is always so accommodating and friendly. Also, the chefs here are some of the most talented sushi chefs I've encountered; each roll is done to utter perfection of flavor and artistic presentation.

My friend and I arrived at 5:30 on a Thursday, and there were only a few customers, so we had Chef David all to ourselves! He was extremely personable, and we enjoyed lengthy and fascinating conversation while he worked on our sushi.

I decided that I wanted a vegetarian roll, so he whipped one up for me, and OH MY GOD. This roll was incredible and so unique. My friend and I both agreed that it had to be on the menu, and David told us that it soon would be! The roll had delicate tempura veggies and topped with the most delicious and fresh apple compote. The result was one of the most exotic and exciting roles I've ever tasted! You have to ask your chef to make it, as it's truly something special.

David also made us three other incredible rolls. We simply told him what we did and didn't care for, and he created some delectable rolls. The sushi had the perfect amount of rice (not too much) and the balance of flavors was always spot-on. One of our favorites was the TUNDRA. It was topped with seared salmon which added a comforting smokey flavor, elevating the rolls sophistication to the max. The SAN FRANCISCO is also a go-to for us; we love the refreshing citrus flavor of the lemons.

Hinoki is definitely the best sushi Reno has to offer. It's fresh and hip, and I look forward to frequenting it in the future.

NOTE: this is just a review of breakfast choices.

Mr Lee finally took all the posters and ads down from his windows!  It looks so much brighter and cleaner in here.  

This is where I go for a solid breakfast on the weekends.  Lee's grits are the real deal, and his bacon is always cooked just right.  I've also dipped in for an egg sandwich on wheat bread and been similarly pleased.  

The coffee is a little bit bitter.  I get a spoonful of sugar every time, even though I never put sugar in my coffee normally.

Dirty, rude staff, poorly run Hilton. I had such high expectations because it was a family vacation. Two of my family members got food poisoning from lunch. I was fully charged for breakfast and it was a terrible one. I wasn't given any discount for being a Diamond when I paid for breakfast, they did not award the $24 a day. Drinks at the pool tasted like water, overall a bad experience going back to the Omni next year.

Def Leppard should think about tweaking the lyrics to their hit song immediately to "Pour some SugarFire on me".  Oohh, in the name of love this place is rockin'!  I processed their menu and settled for the brisket with a side of cheddar grits and the bean salad.  

Lets get the sides out of the way first.  After putting my tray of caloric brilliance at my table, I went to the soda machine and was immediately turned on by the guilt free zero calorie Lucky Club soda.  If I was about to ingest 4 figures worth of calories, the least I could do was wash it down with something that didn't add to it. It tasted great, like a Diet Coke, but I was pleased to know it was made locally.  I swear I received close to a pound worth of grits.  No chance I was polishing these off all the way.  They were good, but not outrageous.  However, I can't remember a time I've ever had grits in my life and was blown away with any kind of revolutionary flavor.  The bean salad was great as well. 

On to the main event.  The BEEF BRISKET.  I'm smiling right now reminiscing about it.  I had 4 different sauces on my table.  I tried them all.  The Carolina Mustard was my least favorite, but I never have been big on this style.  It had a distinct vinegar taste to it.  I know there are a ton of people that enjoy that variety of sauce, so taste for yourself.  The Watermelon, yes watermelon BBQ sauce was completely out of left field.  My initial thought was this is a man's type restaurant.  Watermelon sauce has no business being here.  I was wrong.  It was one part tangy, and another part watermelon fruit driven.  It just toyed with my taste buds.  So good.  The coffee BBQ sauce was savory and rich.  It tastes just like it sounds. An incredible nuance. My favorite was the Texas Hot BBQ sauce.  It was big and bold, just like the state of Texas.

The brisket itself was extraordinary.  It had a beautiful marbling to it and it just fell apart as soon as I put a fork to it.  It was smoked perfectly and was warm as the summer sun.  The place was eerily quite, but when everyone is so focused on devouring their plate, it is easy to see why.  These guys aren't afraid to take a culinary chance, and I like that. I had a grand old time at SugarFire, and there most definitely is a new sheriff in town when it comes to BBQ.

Tried out this place for the first time today. I tried their Taro Pudding Milk Tea and their Matcha Cheesecake. Both were absolutely delicious. The taro milk tea did need to be dissolved all the way, but I did enjoy my drink.  My boyfriend got the chrysanthemum tea (I hope you find another vendor for that tea. It tasted great too!) I definitely loved their variety in menu and the environment.  Their customer service was fantastic as well. Definitely a great idea in including games for customers to play while waiting for their drinks. I won 5 games of UNO against my boyfriend there :) Overall, wonderful first impression.
This place offers a lot of different desserts. We had this thinly wrapped mango ice cream dessert. It was pretty good. Creamy and sweet.

I enjoy this place. There is a sauce station that allows you to mix your own sauce. If you don't know what to do, they also have instructions on good combos that work together. I only had the bbq a few times but mainly we order the hot pot. It's all you can eat and they are pretty quick to come out with your food. There's always servers walking around and they come walking around to refill the stock if it boils down.

Let me preface this review by saying that Bayona has been a favorite of mine for at least 13 years. It is pricey and I am not a regular. That being said,  I have eaten there 5-6 times and adored every bite of food and treasured every experience. Until February 26, 2021. My party of 5 had a 8:30 pm reservation. Three of the party members were out of town guests and one was celebrating her birthday. My husband was a first time visitor and we have been saving to make this night extra special while holding back no expense. We were promptly seated. We placed our drink orders and contemplated the appetizers (starters). I ordered a bottle of wine while the rest of the table ordered mixed drinks. The bottle was delivered to the table behind us. Our server took our order for 8-9 starters. We had all planned on sharing.  We ordered our entrees prior to the appetizers being served, Approximately 30 minutes later 6 of the appetizers were delivered to the table.  20 minutes later the remaining 3 were delivered to the table. All was going well. We were enjoying the experience and the food was divine. No complaints. At 10:15 we still had not received our entrees. We called the waiter over to the table (pulling his attention away from a table of 8 women that he and the chef had been speaking with for quite some time) and inquired how much longer on the entrees. He returned and curtly informed us 5 minutes.  10 minutes later our entrees were delivered. 3 of us ordered the $42 filet mignon.  One of the party members cut into her steak and immediately said I can't eat this. It was very rare, almost blue. We asked the waiter to return it to the kitchen and remove it from the check.  The manger came over and very rudely inquired "Is there a problem here?" We just said the steak was underdone and to remove it from the bill.  His tone was very condescending and manner abrupt and rude. AT this time I tried to cut into my steak. It was so undercooked it couldn't be cut with the steak knife provided by the waiter.  Neither the waiter nor the manager returned after we returned the first steak so I approached the hostess station with my plate. Immediately the chef came out of the kitchen with a very ugly attitude and raised voice. He knew what we ordered and provided the ticket to include all three steaks were ordered medium rare. This was false. My husband ordered his medium rare (he ate his with no complaints) and the other guest and I ordered ours medium.  The chef proceeded to yell at me that this was a three course dining experience that took a while. (We only ordered two courses). I asked him to try the steak himself and he replied absolutely not "haven't you heard of covid? Where is your mask by the way? " The hostess handed me a mask I thanked her and put it on. Keep in mind the chef had no problem talking to the table of 8 without their masks on. The manger approached again waving his arms telling us he was comping the entire meal and demanded we leave. I told him we fully intend on paying the check without the two steaks.  I asked for the waiter to bring us our check. The manager informed me the waiter was refusing to serve us and we needed to leave. We were not loud, we were not making a scene (unlike the the chef and the manager) we tipped the waiter out and I asked the manager to make sure the waiter who was refusing to serve us received his tip. (It is covid after all and I know hospitality workers have been hit hardest). 

We were not a block away when I received the attached text message from the restaurant. 

It was truly the most bizarre and heartbreaking dining experience I have ever had. I hope the chef , manager and waiter were having a bad day and our party just happened to be in the way. 

The food is really amazing and like I said this has been a favorite of mine.  The service? I would hope Susan Spicer would train her staff better and not stand for this.  Her restaurant lost several hundred dollars that night by an overzealous arrogant petulant child who felt like he had the authority to treat an entire party of 5 the way he did.  

I am appalled this how they treat perceived first time visitors. Even if I could go back, I wouldn't and that's the sad part about all of this.

My wife and I came here to celebrate our one year anniversary a few months back and we had a really nice time.

We took the train into SB and walked around town and then took a Lyft to the hotel.  I wish I had known sooner that we could have come here and just hung out and enjoyed the day here at the pool or the beach or the spa.  I guess I didn't realize how much of a resort this place was laid out to be.

Next year we're coming back for a few days and we'll probably skip the SB visit and just spend our days here relaxing.

The staff was amazing and so welcoming.  We had some champagne upon arrival, wine left for us in the room, and chocolates delivered to us as a gift for our anniversary!  Loved the handwritten note, and personal touches all throughout our time here.

The restaurant and cafe are fantastic, the pools look awesome, the cabanas are private, and they have two jacuzzis.  They have an adults-only pool which is much more low key so you can avoid the kiddos splashing and such.

There were a lot of kids, families, and parties going on while we were there.  It made it feel much more like a resort than a retreat, but not a huge issue for us.

The spa is enormous and though we didn't get massages last time we will next time.

We checked-in early and were given an ADA accessible room, which was supposed to be a bit more private but didn't have the opulence and features I was really looking forward to.  Next time we'll hold out for the more luxurious suite.

The place feels rich and clean.
They have nice tennis courts, easy walking paths to the beach and a small nature area that's worth walking around.

The customer service really was great and despite being less than 100% stoked with our room the experience and special-ness of this place made it feel like a great getaway.

Again, we're already planning our trip for next year, and that should tell you enough about our overall feelings toward this.

Do experience the restaurants on-site, and plan to just hang out around the grounds and enjoy.

My wife and I came here to celebrate our first wedding anniversary, and something tells me for that reason alone it will always have a special place in my mind.  But...it really was an amazing meal.

We went all here.
Starting off with some drinks.  Man, fun and strong drinks.  Good selection of bourbon and my Old Fashioned was great.  My wife got one that came in a smoked vessel that literally had smoke trapped inside it that you poured onto your drink to give it a smoky flavor.  So fun.

We started with a few appetizers.
Amazing brussels sprouts and we ordered a dish of mushrooms that would convert any one to a fan of the shroom.

We split for our main the sea scallops dish which was so decadent and perfect that I wish we had ordered two so neither of us had to share.

I also ordered maybe the best French Onion Soup I've ever had.  It was so hot I wanted to cry since I couldn't eat it fast enough.  Huge bread, massive amounts of cheese, and the onion soup was so rich that you could bathe in it.

We finished off with a cheesecake dessert that we were treated to for our occasion which was very well made also.

The service we received the entire time was some of the best in class I have ever had.  Our whole dinner was made better by the friendly and caring staff.  

We will 100% come back and eat here again next year.
Not a fan! Plain and simple. I've never seen Sesame Chicken presented in that manner.

I was excited to try Midwestern after a friend hyped up this place for me, explaining how delicious Ben Welch's Big Baby Q and Smokehouse was. I immediately noticed upon walking in just how spacious the building is. The decorated interior had a relaxed and casual bar vibe. The server was proficient at taking care of our table throughout. Unfortunately, the exhilaration came to a halt when I tried some of the menu items.

I ordered the following:
1. Fried Chicken Sandwich (with a side of potato salad): I wasn't a fan of the biscuits as buns because they were crumbly and extremely dry. I was longing for sips of water in between each bite. The fried chicken breading was soggy, and the fried chicken itself was bland. The egg in between wasn't seasoned and didn't seem to add too much value to the sandwich. However, the potato salad was decent.
2. Double Burger (with a side of mac and cheese): The tomato jam in this burger was a home run. I couldn't get enough of it. The burger was satisfactory and will satiate a burger craving. Unfortunately, the mac and cheese missed the mark for me. It was not cheesy enough and was a bit flavorless.

I was thrilled to find another authentic Chinese restaurant in St. Louis, particularly cuisine from the Sichuan province. I like what they've done with the space. 

If you're not too familiar with Sichuan food, NOT ALL but many of the dishes are paired with spices that are sure to get your tongue and lips feeling the tingling sensation. There are non-spicy, flavorful dishes as well. If you cannot tolerate spicy food, perhaps restrain yourself from ordering dishes with chili pepper icons next to them on the menu.

I ordered the Boiled Fish with Green Pepper Sauce and the Braised Beef Noodle Soup. The flavors and spices in the fish dish kept lingering and getting more bold with every bite. It was very warming and delicious. My friend (who typically enjoys spicy food) had never eaten a dish with Sichuan peppercorns. She was not used to it and preferred to take them out before consuming. As for the beef noodle soup, the broth was hearty and the noodles were the right chewiness. The noodles to broth ratio was to my liking. The beef noodle soup was also a good transition for toning down the tingling sensation from the fish dish.

I have been to Sultān a couple times now, and each time I was in for a treat. The food is excellent and overall worth the wait if you have time to spare. However, the service can be quite slow with only two or three servers. On one visit, almost all of the tables in the restaurant were filled; I waited half an hour to finally order, and 45 minutes to an hour for the food to arrive. The server was apologetic and I wasn't in a hurry to go anywhere, so I didn't mind too much.

I have eaten the following:
1. Saffron Curry Chicken: "Winner, winner, chicken dinner!" is what you'll be saying as soon as you take a bite and realize what a winner you are for ordering this dish! Good portion size, super creamy, and an amazing combination of spices to produce such a mouthwatering dish. Note that this dish is not spicy, but the explosion of flavors are sure to please your palate.
2. Saffron Curry Vegetables: Don't be surprised to hear that this dish tasted exactly like the Saffron Curry Chicken, but with no meat, just vegetables (which consisted of broccoli, carrots, green beans, and maybe more). The vegetables were cooked just enough so that they're not too soft and still have somewhat of a bite to them.
3. Chicken Kabob: Yum! The kabob had a good marinade, and it was grilled to a golden color. I also liked that the tomatoes were grilled. The rice was cooked perfectly. This dish was very enjoyable.
4. Baba Ganoush: Thick and creamy consistency, and tasted just how I would expect it to. However, I couldn't get enough of the naan! It was pillowy, toasted just enough, and had a nice chewiness. I ordered another naan just to soak up the delicious sauces from other dishes.
5. Vegetable Pasta: I would not recommend this dish. It was as insipid as it appears in the photo, and was lacking flavor and sauce. Grocery store boxed pasta and canned sauce taste better than this. Oh well, at least I know not to get this dish next time.

Lovin Spoonfuls has great service and friendly staff, but their food is  horrible. I've been a vegan for four years, been to this place at least ten times, and have never been happy with the food. As far as I can tell, every yuppie fawns over this place because it's an entirely vegan restaurant, which is a fun novelty for us. However, it may possibly be the worst vegan restaurant in the entire Western US.

The chicken is all premade frozen stuff. The sauces are boring and tasteless. Your food always comes out lukewarm. This is the kind of boring grey crap omnivores have nightmares about. And when you leave, you feel like a moron for spending $15 on terrible food just because you like the novelty of a vegan restaurant. 

HOWEVER, their desserts are amazing! I don't know how or why they're so good and flavorful when everything else is awful, but they are. If you're thinking of checking this place out, order a slice of cake or pie to go.

One of the worst restaurant experiences I have ever had! Tried to go on a nice date, ended up starving and furious. Spent $35 on two drinks, waited 45 minutes to be sat and only after orders were taken were we told there was a 40 minute ticket wait. Over two hours later and not a single update on food or smile from the waitress, we left. The restaurant is run by surfer kids who could not handle if the restaurant had 3 people in it much less a very busy Saturday afternoon. The location is breath taking and it's sad such an awful restaurant wastes the location.

This establishment came highly recommended from a local. We decided to visit our last night in NOLA. We waited 2 hours to be seated. Service was horrible, food was cold and the owner sister was nonchalant about our concerns. They added 20% gratuity to a party of three. When questioned about the automatic gratuity, owner sister stated "all restaurants do this during Essence"....I told her that's untrue, she disagreed. This means this establishment takes advantage of Essence visitors. 
The male waiters could not provide decent service due to their lack of focus and flirting. I do not recommend this eatery and will ensure I leave bad reviews on all social media doei

You can't go wrong here! We recommend the classic (it's like a meatloaf meatball, with the seasoning and vegetables baked in) and try it with the creamy garlic sauce. Also, the quinoa black bean slider is good. However, the most popular menu item are the chard brussel sprouts. If all you want is good food without the restaurant ambience and long wait, checkout the walk-up counter in the food court. Either way, Mimi Blue is on my top 5 restaurants in Indy, hands down. Service is great!

I've held off going out too often especially since our world got flipped upside down during the past uneventful year. As someone who's a huge fan of ramen I was curious to try this new shop that just opened up. I came here for lunch and ordered their Tokyo Style Shoyu Ramen. Three things I look for in great Ramen; flavorful broth, bouncy noodles, and delicious toppings. Their Shoyu Ramen knocked it out of the park with a 3 for 3. The noodles were cooked to perfection and the broth was incredibly rich. 

I was beyond happy that I ate here and made this small getaway meal during covid in Arizona. Dining here simply splendid, as the décor resembles Japanese bars and restaurants in Japan, and yes I've been there on occasions, for comparison. Their menu is simple and straightforward. For a bowl of amazing ramen in Tucson, you won't have to break your wallet, absolutely excellent. Highly recommend you try for yourself, would eat this again and again and again.

We had to try it. We saw Michael T from Yelp recommending the 50/50 burger and knew this was our next dining spot. 

The 50/50 burger did not disappoint. My DH said, it was "almost too much bacon" but that isn't possible. Is it? 

Waited a few minutes to get seated -- and service was swift. 

Other than the 50/50 - we tried the pork ribs - awesome. Great smoke. The brisket - hit or miss... kinda fatty and not their best. The sides included a salad with the apple vinaigrette - VERY nice and the cheesy grits - YES - and the cole slaw - very good! 

Super happy with the results of our trip and cannot thank Michael enough for putting this place on our short list!

I love this place. Just in love.  Do yourself a favor and try these filet sliders..  which are dressed with Worchestershire butter. But you won't want just one. Or maybe even two. They're that good. I'm also a huge fan of the fried chicken sliders which have a nice kick to them. 

I gotta be honest,  the shrimp wasn't my fav,  but then again,  I'm not a big shrimp person anyways (I know.. blasphemous in these parts). People seem to dig them though. 

Now, before I get to the main event (donuts, obviously).. onto their coffee. It's good. I'm not (yet?) a coffee snob where I taste the fancy notes of a good roast. But I do know they know what they're doing.  They also carry nitro brew and cold brew (in growlers even).

They're also BYOB! Grab a six pack next door from Stein's and chill it inside if needed.

Ok ok. Now for the donuts. I sadly haven't tried all of them.. But it's still early in the year.  I'm not usually a creme filled fan,  but the ones I've tried (especially Vietnamese iced coffee,  I'm looking at you) have been great.  Limoncello poppyseed,  Mexican hot chocolate (spicy!), salted caramel.. And they change it up everyday.  They do the simple ones well too.. glazed, choc glazed, cinnamon sug. The best part is that you can stalk them out on Instagram where they post their daily specials and get your mouth watering before you head out there (or maybe that's just me?).  And for something more savory, they have kolaches.

And now after writing this, I'm craving them again.  It's a vicious,  delicious cycle.  I don't hate it.

It was a pleasant surprise to find a LEGIT LOOKING sushi restaurant next to the jewelry store I was in to get my (engagement!!!!!) ring resized at, which only could mean that my eating at Wasabi was DESTINE TO HAPPEN! There was ONE uneasy about sushi person in the party of five I brought it but I assured her that there would be enough non sushi foods for her to fill up on... And I was right! 

I ordered my usual order of a hamachi kama and salmon skin rolls, because, when I know what's good... I don't typically veer off of it! Others ordered rolls, spicy chicken, etc and I don't think ANYONE had a problem with their meals*! I know I wolfed my food down without blinking an eye and enjoyed EVERY SECOND of my mastication! 

I was also impressed that they had Tamari Sauce (gluten free soy sauce), so props!

I guess my only real complaint is that the service kind of took a long time... I would give them slack if there were a lot of other parties in this restaurant but It didn't look like mid-westerners make a BLINE to sushi every chance they can get (like me)... So yeah, why did it take so long? Maybe they wanted to bring everything out at the same time, which honestly I actually like... Because man do I hate when I'm the only one eating at the table, LOL! 

Any who... While I'll probably never eat at this restaurant again, I have to regale that it was tasty enough to make my staple restaurant if I lived in the area... Alas, I don't, so nope! But to all you skeptics out there that think eating sushi in a landlocked state is "fishy" (Har Har), roll up your apprehension ;) and chow down! 

*The salmon skin Handrolls I ordered without rice... We're good, as I loved the large portion of sliced skin they gave me... But my one critique would be to cook it a bit longer, as salmon skin should be a bit crispy, as opposed to soggy!

Review by B

Do not stay here!  This hotel is one of the worst hotel we have ever stayed at!!!! We had problem after problem after problem after problem our entire stay!  We would rate this hotel 0 stars if possible!! Staying here was a nightmare! Here is a list of everything that was wrong with this hotel:

1.  Room was not ready when we checked in...we were told to walk around the French Quarter until the room was ready and was promised a call when ready which we never received.  Walking around for an hour would not have been a problem if it was not pouring rain! The hotel offered an umbrella for our use but apparently they were out of stock after they offered us an umbrella.

2.  Room keys were not available when our room was finally ready and was told we would receive a call in our room when ready! We never received a call, we wasted 2 hours waiting in our room!

3.  Extremely loud music was blasting in the courtyard from 9am - 10pm daily despite numerous complaints from multiple guests that they were unable to relax. The music was so loud you could hear it in the halls and rooms.  Finally after complaining 5 times over a period of 2 days the music was turned down to a tolerable level.

4.  Acura car service was not available as they informed us the car was in the shop for repairs.  The hotel seriously only has one car?!? We made reservations weeks in advance for the car service!  We were told it would be back Sunday or Monday, we called to check the status both days but the car was still in the shop.  BS!

5. The cable/picture quality was extremely poor and movie channels were not available.  The hotel sent someone to check it out, he came in tightened the cable and left.  He called us about 10 minutes later to see if it was working but it wasn't and instructed us to unplug and plug back in and fiddle with the cables...ummm isn't that your job?!?!?!  By the time he came back up to try again it was way too late in the night to even bother with it.

6.  Day 3 of our stay there wasn't any hot water in our room! We went down to the front desk to complain along with a list of several things that were broken or disgusting in our room to be fixed while we were out.  The girl at the front desk promised to have all our issues addressed and fixed asap.  Only 2 of the items from our list were addressed and the rest were ignored! 

7.  Walls are paper thin...you can hear everything inside and outside the hotel!

8.  Hotel staff is unresponsive and sometimes rude when complaining about something wrong with the hotel. 90% of complaints were not addressed! 

9.  The cleaning staff does a very poor job cleaning rooms and straightening up. Our room was covered in dust for days!  

10.  The last day of our stay there was heavy construction being done to the restaurant, it was intolerable!  The construction workers started jack hammering around 10am! We called at 1:30pm to ask how long this was going to be going on and to complain about the noise & the jack hammering shaking our room the girl at the front desk was extremely rude!  She stated with a nasty attitude "You  think that's bad???? Try sitting at the front desk!  Construction was also extremely annoying when taking a dip in the tiny pool. Seriously what luxury hotel does major construction during tourist season?

11.  As we were packing up on our last night we noticed that one of our bags of gifts we had purchased was missing from our room!  We immediately contacted the front desk with concern and anger!  We received a call back from the front desk a few minutes later that they were trying to contact a supervisor to get this issue resolved.  We had to rush out of our room to try to replace the gifts but the stores were closed!  We wasted an hour running around the French Quarter at 12am - 1am in the morning!  We went back to the front desk and were told that the cleaning staff must have thrown the bag out by mistake and would try to resolve the issue.  Why would the cleaning staff shift through our large stack of purchases and just throw one bag out?! The hotel did not offer to cover the loss but rewarded us some Starwood Points...we don't care about points!  We want our stuff back!  We spent hours picking out perfect gifts for friends and coworkers!

When we checked out at 6am our issue had yet to be resolved we were told to check out the gift shops in the airport to replace the missing gifts.  We have yet to receive a call from the hotel supervisor regarding this issue and it's been over 12 hours!!!!!  We will be following up everyday until this issue has been resolved and all Starwood Points have been returned from our stay.

Thank god we did not pay for this stay but used Starwood Points.  You would think the hotel would treat long time Starwood Members with a little more respect and try to insure their stay is pleasant and relaxing.

Pros: Doormen and Valet staff were extremely friendly and helpful.  Hotel is in a great locat

Wow, Lolo's Authentic Filipino Cuisine!! Ordered a decent sized order through Grubhub for a later pickup only for you guys to cancel because you're "too busy". And then when I called in to ask about it, got the same response AND GOT HUNG UP ON!! VERY poor customer service!!

UPDATE: Since the business owner decided to respond and blame me for her clear lack of customer service skills, I thought I'd add that to my review. No sense of ownership for her mistake. Actually quite sad that people in the service industry would take to blaming the customer. While their food may be good based only on what I've heard since I didn't get the opportunity to experience myself, this place definitely deserve a ZERO.

I love these types of cool little finds.  I use Yelp for this very reason. Tucked behind a few hotels and not really near anything else, this place was near our hotel (Loews Vanderbelt).  I'm so glad we found it. It was so good we visited twice, once for dinner and once for lunch.  You have two seating options, inside in an air conditioned restaurant or outside in a covered but open bar type area. It is here that you can listen to live music so this is where we sat both times.  They have a decent draft selection which also included a delicious pineapple hard cider.  The music was great, with young local artists with guitars and great voices.  Both meals I had were delicious. Maple burbon salmon with snap peas and an upgraded side of the most delicious mac and cheese.  That mac and cheese was worth the trip. Second meal was smoked turkey which gave me opportunity to try the delicious bbq sauces, one spicy and one sweet.  Again, mac and cheese was my choice of side (don't judge until you've tried it). The second time we sat at the bar and the service was  a little lacking but the good music and fun conversation with the other folks seated there made up for it. My co-worker spoke to the man announcing the musicians and learned a little of his story. 

I liked this place because it was far from a tourist trap. Go to a place the locals go and enjoy the atmosphere.

Fun and trendy, we decided we needed to take advantage of the 'buck a shuck' happy hour.  It's a great deal and is offered M-F from 5-7.  They also have $1 clams as well as $3 draft special and $5 fruity punch drink.  We went on a Friday night and were very lucky to snag 2 spots at the bar.  We had a great conversation with a local named Beverly.  She had obviously been there several times and seemed to have a personal bar tender who in turn became our bar tender as well.  The service was excellent all night.  We started with oysters, clams, and the octopus appetizer.  I'm not a huge fan of oysters and clams but really loved the octopus that was perfectly cooked and very tender.   We had a few drinks and decided to split a lobster roll and slaw. I thought there was a great amount of lobster in the roll. The fries were tasty and the slaw was super refreshing and delicious.  Is it a bit on the pricy dude, yes but overall I thought it was very worth it. Being from Detroit, a lobster roll is a treat and one that I'm willing to pay for if it's decent.

Stopping here was a last minute decision and a good one at that. If you do stop in I suggest a spot at the bar (first come, first served) for friendly conversation and great service. They take reservations for parties of 6 or more.  We were too stuffed for dessert but they sounded delicious.  I will definitely return the next time I'm in Philly and am looking for great seafood!

We all have those days, that you can't wait until the end of long working day, that you need a pick-me-upper in the middle of the day.  When I do, physically or mentally. I go to Dixie Picnic.  They would give me some comfort food, and they would fix me.

Please listen to other reviews.  Please get the Box Lunch.  My favorites are:
--  Thanksgiving Sandwich - they're like a condensed version of your favorite Thanksgiving meal;  
--  Virginia Baked Ham - all tasty none salty. Simple and delicious.
--  Nutty Chicken Salad - on the interesting side of chicken salad.

If you opt out on the Box Lunch, I would also recommend the Beer Battered Cod Po' Boy and the Fried Shrimp Po' Boy.  Both are fresh, delicious and worth every penny.  

But Please listen to other reviews.  Please get the upcakes.  I've never got one I didn't like and they'd lift my spirit up instantly.

I took 1 star off only because they close so early (3pm).  There are days I wish I could have a bowl of their homemade soup to melt my stress away after work.

Don't forget to check out the board for specials.  Yelp check-in gets 10% off.  

Service is fast and friendly.  Just like their simple, delicious, honest food, they make you feel at home.

A groups of 7 of us went there for Chinese New Year lunch last week.  As often as I've been to this place, it really deserves more than 4 stars. Yes, the food is true Authentic Schezuan (Sichuan) style, with damn good flavors.   But I found it a little too salty with most of their dishes, and every time I go there, the sizes of the dishes got smaller.

Here are the dishes I've always ordered:

Sliced Beef And Tendon with chili sauce  -- 5 stars for the flavor: hands down the best one in the area.  3 stars for the portion:  It's more like an Appetizer; definitely not enough to share.  

Cumin Flavored Lamb with chili sauce - 4.5 stars.  Could be a 5-star dish if it weren't so salty.  If you don't like lamb, then order beef.  Still outstanding.

Tea-Smoked Duck - This dish used to be fantastic, but it has gotten drier and saltier.  Judging by lunch from last week, I'm giving it a 3 star.

Sliced Fish with soft tofu soup - A dish for people who can't or don't prefer spicy food.  4.5 stars. (0.5 star deducted for the saltiness.)

We also like to order a Dry-pot style dish called "Assorted Dry Pot (什锦干锅 in Chinese).  It's one of the best dishes they have, contains fish, chicken, several difference types of mushrooms, lotus roots and other meats and vegetables.  Very Good!  4.5 stars. (0.5 star deducted for the size.)

So in all honesty, it could potentially be a 5 star restaurant.  But seriously, spicy dishes don't have to be so salty!  Also there is inconsistency of sizes (or rather the sizes were consistently declining, which would cause a negative point anyway).  I hope they will improve and I'll go back even more often than I do now.

In theory Chinese Buffet should never receive 5 stars.  But King buffet is as good as this category gets and here is why I think they deserve the extra points:

Just like any decent sized Chinese buffet, but their selections are bigger and better in my opinion.  

The setup is quite simple so you can "map out" your meal by just glancing at it.  

Waiting stuff are friendly and normally will fill up water/drinks promptly.

Extra points:
Their Sushi/Raw Bar are better. They have around 8-10 types of sushi and rolls to choose from, and the qualities are nice as well.  Shrimp cocktails, oysters and clams are mostly fresh but you do need to pay some attention.

They have more selections of seafood entrees.  

They food actually taste better.  Of course, by 'Chinese Buffet" standards.

The place is always packed.  In fact during weekend you have to take a number and wait.  I don't mind because this translates into the food has quick turnaround time so they stay fresh.

I don't Chinese Buffet often, but this one is on top of my list when I do.

Let me join the chorus of 1700+reviewers - Yes it's one of the best cheesesteak places and it's a must-go for anyone who wants REAL cheesesteaks.
Yes their cheesesteak is worth the drive, worth hitting the ATM for cash, and worth waiting in lines.
I was actually lucky enough to sit in the tiny shop and ate my cheesesteak.  It was even better than takeouts - warm, juicy, cheese melted and intertwined with fresh, finely chopped meat perfectly.  Generous portion.  Selection of peppers on the side to put in your sandwich such as banana, hot, and cherry peppers. 
I would give it a 6 star because they also serve serving bottled craft beer.  They just took cheesesteaks to a new level.

We first decided to try Nala because someone told me it's a non-vegetarian version by the same owners of Devi.  So the expectations were HIGH.

As soon as we walked in, I saw a guy in the middle of the dining room cooking Naan in an open Tandoor.  Minutes later we had a basket of those brought to our table,  hot and fresh.  I was in LOVE.

It's hard to rate individual dishes from the buffet considering the amount of option, and the fact they change a bit to make things interesting.  But one thing for sure is that the quality of food is high!  There are about 6 dishes in average that I would go back for seconds every time I've been there.
  
To name a few of my favorites:
Indian:  Tandoori Chicken, Veggie Masala, Veggie biryani
Thai:  Red/Green Curry, Chicken Curry
There are different types of rice or fried rice to choose from.  Each with different flavors.

The only problem with Nala is during lunch rush hour the line gets ridiculous long.  But it's a buffet line, how could you complain?  It only says how good the food is!  I just learned to avoid the rush.  I would not take any points off for it.

Breweries are in hype nowadays in Philly. But a Russian literature themed brewery?  This is the only one.

I grew up in the 80's China, with heavy influence of Russian literature, culture, history and politics. Dostoevsky, Pushkin, Tolstoy, Turgenev, Chekhov...Russian novels, plays, movies, music, were all parts of my childhood.  To have a brewery named by Dostoevsky's novel? That was on top of my list to visit.

And it did not disappoint. I can't think of anything I don't like about this place.  A solid 5-star!

The place was small but adequate. Charming, with décor of Russian/Slavic posters, bookshelves filled with Russian/Slavic books, music covers and small statues.

The menu was equally short but sufficient.  8 beers on tap, including 2-3 IPA/DIPA, English, RIS, and Belgian. We had all the IPA, DIPA and RIS.  All surprisingly delicious.

For food, we shared the Polish Snack Pack and Charcuterie Board.  Both used with top quality ingredients with creative preparations, resulted fantastic and delicious East European experience.  

On top of everything, prices were reasonably and staff was pleasant. I can't wait to go back to try more brews and other East European inspired food items!

The ladies aren't crazy but I did figured out the Three Crazies - Crazy location, Crazy cheap, and Crazy delicious!  

Imagine you walk into your best friend's house, and their mom offers to  fix you a fresh sandwich.  She goes to the garden and picks some fresh veggies and fruit, and comes back in and cooks you the best homemade meal you've had that you wish she were your mom.  Yeah, that's what these ladies made me feel.  Whatever you're in the mood for, they'd make it for you.  The veggies and fruit are crisp and fresh, the meat and cheese are juicy and flavorful.

My favorites are: Spiral Ham Club Sandwich on Tuscan, California BLT with Egg, Eggplant Parm Sandwich, and their  Friday Special Salmon BLT.  These sandwiches are priced $5-$6, with huge portions.

And don't forget the breakfast.  I'm hooked on their cheesy over and easy with pork roll on warm toasted bagel, with added avocado. All for $3.50. Talking about a piece of heaven to start your day right!

Now I need to add three more Crazies -- Crazy fresh, crazy friendly, crazy portion.  Overall Three Crazy Awesome Ladies.

A solid authentic Szechuan style restaurant with both traditional and modern twist of the cuisine.  I couldn't give it a full 5 star because some dishes I didn't think they cook correctly.

Food can be inconsistent occasionally.  When asked for the reason, 90% of the time was due to change of chefs. 

Regardless a few times that were off, I still take family here often.  We have a mix of people who can handle spicy and who can't.  So we always order a bunch of apps to share.  Here is our scores: 

Wontons - 4.5 stars.  When ordering wontons or dumplings from any Authentic Chinese restaurant, make sure ask for Handmade or Chinese Style, because it's totally different from the "American Chinese style" that's known for decades.  It doesn't matter what filling you prefer.  The warping are much thinner and chewier, the fillers are larger and fresher.  Half stars for not spicy enough.  And I can't take this dish for takeouts because they will stick together.

Quick Fried Lotus Roots - 3.5 stars.  I love lotus roots but so few places offer them.  They're lacking flavor but bagger can't be choosers.  

Quick Fried Cucumber - 1 star.  Don't get it.  It's supposed to be crispy with a quick fry with pepper corn or peppers. This came out soggy and flavorless with a few big pieces of peppers next to the cucumber. 

"Blow-ur-Mind" Spicy Chicken - 5 stars.  My favorite "modern" spicy chicken here.  Full of flavors and different types of peppers have different effects.  Did blow my mind indeed.

Geleshan Ma La Chicken - 5 stars.  When ordered dining in, the presentation was great!  Also the mixture of peppercorn and dry peppers gives very satisfying results of spiciness.

Peppercorn Chicken - 4 stars.  The Chinese name implies "free-range Chicken" but didn't taste any difference. 

Tea Smoked Duck - 3 stars overall.  Very inconsistent.  Sometimes it's fantastic but occasionally uneatable.   But it's one of the non-spicy poultry on the menu so we always take the chance.

Chengdu Chili Beef - 5 stars.  Another example of wonderfully executed Modern Szechuan dish.  The flavors are full and delicious. 

Eggplant with Garlic Sauce - 4 stars.  Traditional but still very tasty.  Could use a bigger portion.

Whole Fish - 4 stars.  For Chinese New Year, a whole fish is always called and this is one of the places have them.  They have either whole Tilapia on BBQ sauce or Szechuan Chili Bean Sauce.  The Dry fried whole fish was too dry for my taste.

"Red Revolution" fish filet and bean sprouts  -- 5 stars.  The best spicy fish dish around!  It's a hot-pot and it's super spicy.  Don't order if can't handle extreme heat.  

Fish Stew w. Baby Gingers and Pickle Mustard Greens -- 4 stars.  One of the best non-spicy fish dishes here.

Szechuan Chili Jumbo Shrimp - 5 stars.  Surprising good with medium chili sauce.  Fresh, flavorful but not too spicy.  

Sweet Potato Cakes - 5 stars.  Again, it's another wonderful dessert that so few places offer it.  They're wonderfully done.

Overall I recommend it to anyone who enjoys athletic Szechuan cuisine.  Be aware if you can't handle spicy you can find something to eat, but not many.

Like everyone else in the neighborhood, I was ecstatic to hear about their opening. And like everyone else here, I was thoroughly disappointed, every single time, that I have been there.

Here's a quick run down:

Mixed Drinks - 2 stars.  Very weak drinks for the high prices.  Could hardly taste the alcohol. 

Beer - 4 stars.  I do like the growing list of craft beer on tap.  If they could learn how to fill up the glasses, it'll be a 5-star.

Crab Fries - 2 stars.  Not horrible but way too salty.  If it weren't totally overrated, it'd get 3 stars.  

Chicken Cutlets - 2 stars.  Blend and dry. 

Hot Shrimp - 3 stars.  This is the only item on the menu that has flavors.  If it weren't over price, it'd get 4 stars.

Crab cakes - 3 stars.  Average at the most.

Lobster Roll - 3 stars.  I had this more than once, even though it's still blend.

2-star service because it's almost nonexistence.  Basically they know you're there for the big screen TVs and the overrated name.  
Yes. Besides overrated, I would also add Over Priced.

Can you please open a shop in Miami?!?!! If you build one, we ALL will come!!!
Holy @#$%! This is the BEST ice cream I've ever had in my life. I'm not kidding! 
The shop is cute, perfect location, street parking and all that exists here but lets talk about why this is the best gourmet ice cream possibly ever!
Flavor and all their concoctions of it!
I'm more of a salty girl but when I want ice cream I'm usually happy with just a vanilla or coconut, simple but delish. 
I wasnt ready for these flavors. I thought they'd have a good variety but not over 400 flavors!!! WHAT!!!!! And forget my vanilla they have eclectic flavors like pineapple cilantro (this was my 2nd favorite) dragon fruit, coconut avocado,  banana rum. beet pineapple giinger, and so much more but the holy.og.holys was the blueberry goat cheese . Listen, I know it sounds like it doesnt go...it freaking does and it is absolutely phenomenal. Guys there are so many flavors go on the website and please just go look. I was flabbergasted and appalled at first but after trying several I realized this was the best tasting gourmet, fancy AF ice creams ever! These should be in every freezer worldwide and the best thing is you can take them home. They have a little cooler thingy to keep them cold...just dont thinknthey make it to Miami...not unless you have some dry ice....lol..People the ice cream is that damm good...I want to try every damm flavor there is because everything I was allowed onto try tasted so great! Kudos to the creators of all the different flavors. I would have never put some of these ingredients together but they just qork!!!!

I have so many things to say about Bodega.
First let me say I love tasting all types and styles of food. I understand different regions may cook the same dish or meal differently but Bodega really through me off.
Being that I'm born and bred in Miami I know Cuban food. Were spoiled here in Miami and I love it. So when going to Tampa and hearing that the cuban sandwich originated from here we had to try one from any Cuban restaurant they have. 
We came here because we were told it was popular and delicious. I disagree. Now dont get me wrong maybe we should've known better from the modern and bright style, the music played and no sight of any abuelita but hey sometimes places can really surprise you for the better.
To start off we saw a line outside and thought that was the norm, you know the people outside are usually getting some coffee or croquettas or something delicious so we sat at a table and waited and waited and waited. We saw people coming out of the kitchen with plates yelling peoples names and giving it to the  customer be they at a tableor standing waiting. We finally asked one of the staff what is the normal ordering process since we were tourists. It was then we were told that line outside is for ordering. So were finally given menus, made our choices, stood in that damn line and ordered. Now quickly on the menu I noticed they had guarapo (sugarcane juice) so I ordered 2 and a lechon and cuban sandwich. My sister in law ordered a frita that was differently made from the norm but still sounded good.
What we got were decent sandwiches but they lacked some seasoning or some Cuban love. Now I'm not saying it was bad but just not what I was use to. The sandwiches looked appealing and they did not go cheap on the meat stuffing but they didnt use the regular meat or ham I was used to for the Cuban sandwich but it was okay. Lechon sandwich was good but again flavor just not what I'm use to. 
When we received the guarapo juice it was my fault for not reading their version of it because they add like a seltzer water to it. Why in God's name would you do that?!?! That's not guarapo juice, call it something else but never again in my life will I ever buy this montrosity that was $13 each WTF....
Now the frita was actually good and they make it spicy but they put 2 types of meat and chorizo and they added cucumbers..not what im ise to but I did enjoy the piece that was shared. Over all the place is happening, very clean, and the frita is decent if you waslmt what I would call an exotic frita...but I'll  stick to my Miami Cuban food.

Upon driving in we saw wild rabbits, I was in love from then.
This restaurant has all the beautiful Bay views and even though we came for dinner all the lights out there in the sea were gorgeous.
 Our outdoor seating table was perfect for our party of 4 as a nice breeze would come in. As we went over the menu we enjoyed the warm complimentary bread. Everything listed sounded good but several appetizers caught our attention.
 We went with the grilled oysters, the lobster bisque, cesar salad, and the poke bowl. I can order all of these items again and again as they were all done with perfection. The oysters were beyond delish and damn if they had an all you can eat option on these alone count me in, lol. The cesar salad was complete with real anchovy that complimented and gave it the perfect saltiness. The lobster and crab bisque was everything and more and had chunks of them as an extra topping, steal my heart why dont you?! It was nice and hot and warmed my belly.  I just wanted to leave the spoon in my mouth. The poke bowl was refreshing, tasty, and fulfilled all my poke desires. It was really one of the best if not the best I've tasted. It was fresh tuna, cubed and proportioned perfectly with a tasty dressing with. This was the champion of all dinners for me, light, tasty, and freaking delicious. When we come back into town we will definitely come back for more. Bae had a grilled fish, he didnt share so I know it had to be good, lol.
Ending the night full and needing to be rolled out the decision to have dessert came into conversation. I couldnt do it but it was ordered anyway and again the mmmm's were all you heard around the table. This masterpiece called sticky date pudding came on a decorated mascarpone plate with crispy caramel pearls atop with a light whip cream and this chocolate dressing. Can you imagine this flavor?!!
I am not a dessert person but this changed my heart completely.  I was in love with this whole meal from start to finish and can't wait to come back to have it all over again!

I  hate this place so much. It's not even the poor selection, terrible organization, and high prices that make me give it one star (though I hate those things, too). It's the goddam terrible service. If you want to buy things from people who don't know what the groceries are (green onions? what?) or where they are located, or try to hand money to someone who is talking on her cell phone, eating, or talking over your head to another employee, this is your spot. And no one has any power there (perhaps rightly so). If they ring something up wrong or can't find the price or need to make a refund, they have to page a manager, and you both stand there, forever, you slowly  dying inside, and she, snapping her gum and rolling her eyes. At you. For being a pain in the ass. For just wanting someone to do their job. There is one helpful floor manager here, but I just don't see him enough. 

The other day was THE LAST STRAW. I actually got stuck, while trying to buy SEPTA tokens, in the middle of a physical fight between a manager and a cashier, both of them screaming about respect. How about a little respect for your customers? 

The worst part is, I know I'll be back. It's right by my work, and I don't always get my ass in gear to buy groceries on the weekends. And sometimes I need to buy work stuff (like dishwashing detergent) there, to save time. And the deli isn't terrible. Man, do I hate this place.

Wood fired pizza? I'm in. I thought that maybe Philadelphia was finally breaking it's bad pizza curse. Almost, but not quite. 

Pizzaria Stella is easy to get to, and a nice addition to the neighborhood that already includes the Artful Dodge and Xochitl, among others. I arrive with a date on a Friday night, and the place was hopping. Really, really full. Luckily we didn't have to wait on our table, but the restaurant was so loud (between the music and all the animated folks just inches away from us), we had to lean-in to hear each other. 

We order the Tatufo, deciding to split it, and got the immediate "Just one pizza?" from our waitress. Luckily, I'm not easily intimidated. Our wine came out promptly, and the food was fairly rapid, too. The Tartufo is a great pizza with black truffles and a raw egg that the server breaks over the pizza at the table. We were quite pleased with it, but as it cooled the egg became a little less appetizing. The pizza rack that sits on the table is actually really annoying - it takes up far too much space in already tight quarters. Perhaps a rack that clips on to the table, instead of sitting on it? 

I don't have real complaints about the food, location, or atmosphere, but I think they are straddling a hard line between casual and formal. The servers were very attentive - too attentive. We were continually asked if we wanted more wine before we had even finished our glasses, and three different bus boys tried to take our plates away (when we paused from eating) while were still covered in food. In many ways, it just felt like they were trying to rush us out the door. Perhaps we weren't spending enough money?

This is a nice space to stop by with friends if you're in the neighborhood, but it's too loud for a date and too expensive to be an everyday joint.

We are a big fan of Donald Link and his restaurants 
Gianna was quite good and the service was fine but 
I do feel compelled to mention that we were brought garlic bread and later found out we would be charged $6 for 4 slices of bread! We didn't order it
This is the first time I've ever been charged for bread   That being said the waiter took it off the bill as we hadn't ordered it but I find this to be a poor practice to charge for bread in this type of establishment. Secondly, and even more bizarre, we asked for some grated Parmesan cheese for our appetizer and were charged $2  for a small dish that we used 2 tablespoons of cheese! We were never informed that this was a chargeable item also
Come on Link group, our Bill was $250   These petty charges are unworthy of your product!

If you're looking for a late-night grub in NOLA, Mambo's is the one.

This legendary cajun & creole eatery is open til 1am and weekends til 2am. Perfect place to grab food on Bourbon Street especially if your flight arrived late like mine. Once I checked into my hotel around 10:30, I started walking to Mambo's right away. The hostess immediately sat me at the table but they also had bar seating which was a little packed at that time. 

I started with a dozen Mambo's World Famous Oysters which were freshly chucked and chargrilled over an open flame with garlic and cream herb Cajun sauce, topped generously with parmesan and Romano cheeses. Good God! This dish was over the top. Rich and cheesy and tasty AF. This was definitely a plate to share with another person but I finished it all. I also ordered the Cajun Crawfish Poutine. Golden crispy fries topped with zesty crawfish mushroom cream sauce and cheddar cheese. I was speechless. It was really just a flavor explosion and the portions was enormous. The last thing I got was of course, dessert. Their Kentucky Bourbon Pecan Pie hit the spot. Not too sweet and I could tell that it was made fresh. 

As much as I don't' like eating this late, but trust, it was worth it. I slept like a baby and of course, I still felt full the next day...lol :)  Mambo's is definitely a must when visiting NoLa. Sure, there is so many places to eat in the French Quarter, but this place does food right and the service is also on point. I can't wait to go back here again.

An absolutely low key bar on St Peter. A super busy street. So it's easy to miss this place on a real busy day. But really a must go for some sports break and get your drink on. I stumbled upon this one by chance - when another place that claimed to be a Sports bar ended up being a Saints bar instead and refused to show any non Saints football action - period. Pfft. This one is definitely a Sports bar. A real one for sure.

The space on the 1st (ground) floor itself is not that big. But has enough stools and a sweet, winding U shaped bar towards the entrance. Very well lit during night time. Quite flashy for an Irish sports bar actually. But then again - it's NOLA, and in the middle of the Quarter - why not?! The bartender was the nicest girl I have come across in a while. She was fast, had an eye on everyone's glasses / bottles, no attitude about being oh so pretty given how pretty she really was, et al... And knew when to come within flashes with your next drink. So fast! I liked it. Aaaaaa lottt!

They have a pub food menu as well which looked pretty good but I was happy with my bottled beer choices. Football = Beer! The quarter has quite a few sports bars and the ones on Bourbon can get jam packed especially on football Sunday. This unassuming bar is kind of a hidden gem and I would come here in a heartbeat for a 4pm game or even a SNF / TNF / MNF. (and NFL should not even attempt at any more combos of any other *NF! These are enough.)

During my time here watching the NFL season opener, I saw many a local bartenders stopping by to catch up with the friendly bartender and get a drink or 2. Clearly the girl is a star in the community, it seems - not too talkative, yet knows when to talk and to whom depending on their disposition, with a constant smile on her face, not distracted by all the boys texting her all the time or obsessed about updating her Facebook status with how her minute by minute circumstances were. The drinks were cheap. The hurricanes were absolutely the drink of choice with whatever the deal that they have going on - with locals and tourists alike. The atmosphere was low key and non-trashy. Guys were not having to-go drinks' funnels hanging around their necks. Women were not falling off their chairs after consuming 5 times the alcohol that their male companions would guzzle down because they knew they were not walking around town in 7" stilettos. A very unlike FQ scene - a great refreshing change indeed. And my team won! What more can you ask for? Cheers!

Key things to know: 
* Open till 1 am. 
* In the quarter
* decent selections
* Bottled Alcohol is cheaper as compared to other places
* Definitely on the expensive side but again, no other place in the quarter that is cheap for groceries / staples in comparison
* Check for expiration dates before buying (unless under the influence - high probability!)
* Deli section is the most iffy part
* Very courteous staff - its south for sure!

Pretty reliable lunch option while out and about in the French Market. The selections are very well listed on the menu and is quite straightforward. After spending a solid couple of minutes going through the menu and seeing what the vast majority of patrons were ordering, it was a very easy decision. The MUFFALETTA!

You cannot go wrong with this sandwich. It is robust. It is filling. It has great fresh ingredients - every one of them listed in the description. And there is a reason why they sell it as a 1/4 or a 1/2. One person gets pretty full eating the 1/4 the way it is fixed and given the layers of fillings. Again - one's appetite at a given point of time and given one's size obviously can make the difference and hence your choices. But for an average sized lad who was pretty hungry, that 1/4 of a Muffaletta DID FILL ME UP!

If shopping around in the area and in the mood for a quick bite and some people watching in the French market, this is a very good option.

1. Are you living in the French Quarter OR in the close proximity of the FQ?

2. Do you need some serious grub / food after a night out drinking?

3. You like to eat in the confines of your abode (hotel room / home) and not in a restaurant when you know your state of being does not qualify you to get served in a sit down restaurant?

4. You like home delivery no matter what your state of being?

If you answered Yes to at least the 1st question and any one of the remaining 3, then you are in Luck! Verti Marte is one of the 3 or 4 odd 24x7(x365?) places that takes care of your late night cravings. During my maiden trip to NOLA past week, I was a Yes for first 3 questions (I don't like home delivery - I like to see what is being cooked or the way it is being cooked or at least have an in person visual of what I am getting) and hence I chose Verti Marte.

Did the place blew me away? Not really. Was it bad? Not really. That's where it falls in the very Yelpy "A-OK" 3 star feeling. If had the option to, would give 3.5. But not upgrading to 4 stars for sure... Here are my quick thoughts in bullet points:

+ The place is quite reliable in comparison to other options on hand in the Qtr.

+ The best thing I got here - DIRTY RICE. Got it twice, did not disappoint.

- The bad part: the main dish with the dirty rice; both the times - quite mediocre. Usually - when completely under the influence of alcohol, if you can feel something is mediocre, it technically is horrible. But since I ate these when I was, I stick to the mediocre choice of word. I did not get anything from here when sober to not make me go back here, next time I visit, and find my self in the similar set of circumstances as questions 1 through 3.

- Deli Service: hit or miss. Night 1 - the server at the deli was the older gentlemen and a gem. Night 2 - he was young and quite useless. When you are in customer service, your facial expressions tell how disgusted you are, doing what you do, if that is how you are feeling at the point! Be careful and act accordingly. Don't show drunk customers how you feel. They are in a brittle state of being! ;o)

+ They do warm the food for you when you order it at the deli. It is all pre-cooked. They put it in the microwave and heat it for you depending on your choice - hot or cold.

- Nothing to comment about anything else other than the Deli take out experience. Never got any groceries or any other things sold here - including booze.

- Cash Only

+ Probably the best part: It's on Royal St, away from the craziest part of the FQ. Safe neighborhood, quite ok for late night walking - as long as you are not giving the vibe that you are ready to get mugged, because if you are, chances are you will. But really in a nice part of FQ - probably on my most favorite street of the FQ....

#HLNM
(Happy Late Night Munching)!!!

** Breakfast All Day, people - All Day!! **

Decatur St. lining the river-walk is such a food heaven - for tourists and first timers at least. It has so much to offer for everyone. Easily a great option outside of the madness that Bourbon St. provides - easily.

Belle's diner is an absolute diner - no frills, straight forward good food, the way it is described, nothing more, nothing less. And sometimes - that's all you need on a Saturday morning, after a Friday night when you had so much fun in the jazzy Frenchman St and when you are not willing to deal with crazy lines outside most of the very same Frenchman St. and pretty much most eateries near Canal St. and very much all over the French Quarter. Go to Belle's - you won't be disappointed. Classify this as one of those safe bets that would not disappoint.

The place is quite spacious and if you choose to sit on the Decatur St. side, it is more bright thanks to all the natural light flowing in from that side. The other section is smaller and more demure. And then of course they have the long bar - overlooking the open kitchen station. Which would be my favorite space - not too hot despite the grill not far away from where you are seated, surprisingly - somehow it worked. You get to see the staff in action doing their magic at the craft they excel at.

I was in the mood for eggs. And the menu had quite a few good choices. Without confusing myself too much, I went with what sounded the best - the Seafood Omelet. I made the right choice - baby! It was delicious. The eggs were cooked to sublime perfection. The omelet was stuffed - and I mean it - stuffed - with shrimp. When the description read shrimp and cheddar cheese - I was wondering what would the split be like - how much shrimp and how much cheese? I am not a 'stuff-my-omelet-with-lotsa-cheese-coz-I-love-a-gooey-omelet' kinda guy. No. But I didn't bother asking my kind waiter coz I am also a 'go-with-the-flow-n-roll-da-dice' kinda guy. And boy did the dice fall in place the way I wanted. That Omelet was stuffed with many and many a pieces of shrimp and was not at all overwhelmed (nor destroyed) with any obscene amount of cheese. I was so happy. Sidenote - the hash browns were good but tiny bit on the salty side. Obviously I didn't move an inch towards the salt shaker.

But I was even more happy to feel - with my fork and knife - the smooth texture of the sauce. And as a first reaction, I wanted to taste it without biting into the eggs and shrimp itself. And O-M-G! That sauce was heavenly. It is called Crawfish, Corn and Pepper sauce. Given the option - I would rename it as - "Can I kidnap the chef who devised this recipe and hide him/her for my personal pleasures please?" sauce!! Man, these guys do not know what they have. They should advertise this Omelet as their biggest selling point. For whatever reason (best known to them) they don't do that. But I am not complaining baby. I got what I wanted and only if I keep getting things that I want, life would be such a breeze (Ya, Drew Breese needs to take notes and stop blowing those Saints games away... well, actually, he is good, that team is in a funk - at least from game 1!).

Coming back to the "steal-the-chef" sauce. It was full of flavors. I splashed some hot sauce as I needed an extra doze of hot kick - but that's me. You give me a sizzling hot dish that will kill most everyone with the spicy heat, I would add a dash of hot sauce to give it some more kick (manufacturing defect in my tongue!). But most people would not / should not do anything to it. It has everything that will set your taste buds free. Just dissect that omelet into million pieces and dive n dig in (see the before and after dissection pictures attached). That they serve this out-worldly dish throughout the day - I would go back to this diner in a heartbeat - just for that! Enjoy!!

PS: Why 4 stars you ask? Actually - I don't have to explain ;o) - But then again, if that was really a question in your mind given you must have made it through this entire piece of literature - I can answer that query for you.
