One dish cannot define a place. But I am very positive everything else here is just as good and I can't wait to go back to NOLA and try them all and bump up that rating.

SHORT REVIEW: Meet here. Drink here. Chat here. Work here. Eat (light bites) here. VISIT THIS PLACE.

LONG REVIEW:
I give it 4.5 stars, the knick just due to the nature of worrying about your parking meter while you relax in this place for awhile.

THE STORY:
I love exploring. Driving around the city with my eyes peeled for new spots, watching IBJ for the new real estate deals...it's all fascinating. Armed with intel, I ventured out to HoiTEA ToiTEA because I deserved a break that day.

WHAT'S IT LIKE IN THERE?
-- The first thing you should notice is that this place is clean and refreshing. Simple to navigate, bright, airy, and contemporary. The layout is part retail store/part cafe ala Starbucks. I love the mashup of being able to buy relevant items to the purpose of the storefront I'm in. With a variety of seating areas-and even a private room-your work/chat space should be a part of the conversation just as much as having one. I approve.

WHAT DID I EAT? 
-- Not much, as they're focus is TEA (hence the name), but WOAH. Their chocolate chip cookies are so splendid (TIP: ask for it warmed up). Your taste buds will come running to thank me. They offer lite bites, but their selection of teas and other drinks is fancy, broad, and declicioso!

Tony Mazzola. If I could give you a zero rating I would. Our party of 8 came from Missouri to enjoy an evening of dining and friendship. That all  changed when we met you. We simply mentioned that your website did not have the correct directions and 6 in our party ended up at your old location in Fairview Heights. Your response of "We have been in business for 35 years and you were not updating the website and that if people couldn't find you it was not your problem". Here's hoping everyone gets lost then. What a narcissist. And the food was mediocre at best. I will give you one positive comment. You hire professional staff. You should take a lesson from them. I am happy to share this review with anyone, any site I can and plan to.

Good neighborhood diner.  Service was good. Food is good.  The day I was there it was a little warm in there but can't go by me I guess because I like things really cold. 

It has a quiet atmosphere which I like in a diner it's
Comfortable and not too loud.  Just right !

This was my first time coming here. I like the feel of the diner. The day I went it was quiet and I liked the atmosphere. I ordered a chicken salad on a croissant. To be honest the sandwich was mediocre it didn't really taste like anything and I definitely had better at other diners so that's why I gave a three star. 

But I wouldn't say I won't come back. I always like to try a few different items to see how I like it. My daughter had a grilled chicken Cesar salad that didn't come with croutons for some reason and she said it was okay,
Nothing special but you know it's lettuce so who knows lol. 

We are Going to try it for breakfast and dinner items and when I do I will be back to adjust my stars.  

Overall the diner was nice, clean and staff seemed nice and also seemed like they had people who are recurring guests so that's a plus. I'll keep you posted on my returning visits !

Ordered take out a few nights ago. During covid they are having their full menu options.  They were very nice when answering the phone and the order was on time and delicious.  Sorry I didn't take pics. But we were starving. Lol.  Some of ya got breakfast and others got dinners.  

In the new times we are encountering with this virus I am thankful that this diner is still operating and able to give its customers what they want.  I will continue to help my local businesses and order for take out.  

For me it's about the food, not the atmosphere so I'm okay with ordering take out. And I will continue to do so!

So I'm gonna start off and say it's getting four stars.  The staff is super friendly and the manager was walking around to the tables. The waitress was very nice and made sure to check on us and see if we needed anything. That means a lot.  

The food was really good. We got a variety of food from chicken parmigiana to crab imperial to a burger to a Mediterranean grilled veggie plate with grilled chicken.   

We all enjoyed our meal. Very tasty.  Very satisfying and filling.  We were all glad we decided to come here.  The only reason it didn't get five stars was it was a little warm in there despite the sign outside saying come inside and beat the heat.  But five stars is hard to come by anyways I feel lol. 

I will definitely return. We have been here before and will continue to come.

Great patriotic and Veteran-honoring BBQ spot!

But let me first address some of the slower people (bless their hearts) out there who are apparently too dull to recognize that this place was founded by two guys whose family all served in the United States military and they chose to honor...VETERANS. The horror! How DARE they honor our servicemembers, police and other first responders and the country they served by playing, GASP!, the EVIL NATIONAL ANTHEM! I suppose the sound of that to him is like a cross to a vampire, hmm?
 
Yes, I'm talking this selfish clown complaining:

"...When I walked into Mission BBQ at noon today, the ENTIRE RESTAURANT was standing while the Star Spangled Banner blared throughout the room as if to say "salute your meat". "But, why", you may be wondering. Because it's the gd national anthem, you commie. Mission BBQ seems to cater exclusively to the disciples of overtly-fetishized patriotism. These dopes were all standing for the national anthem AT LUNCH... IN A CHAIN RESTAURANT..."
 
"These dopes" keep your bearded, knit-cap-wearing hipster butt FREE, buddy. "These dopes" keep you safe and sound at night. "These dopes" will run into a burning building instead of out of it to rescue you, my friend.
 
Back to the review, enough with the pettiness of people who clearly never served their country (and would have lasted about 10 minutes in Basic Training anyway). This place opened near where I work and they catered a BBQ lunch for us Vets recently which was delicious! After signing up for the Veterans VIP club email (there they go again, those EVIL Veteran-honoring monsters!) I got an email for a free sandwich (the HORROR!) and decided to give them a try. Wow! The chopped brisket sandwich was huge and smoky/saucy deliciousness on a nice soft brioche type bun. The mac & cheese was super cheesy and great and the "cold slaw" (coleslaw) was quite tasty as well and NOT sickly sweet as too many places seem to make it. I loved the military/police/FF decor and the tall flagpole with US flag and US Army flag out front. As an Army veteran, I say HOOOAH to Mission BBQ and this is my new go-to lunch spot in the KOP area!

Arrived at 8pm on a Saturday night and expected it to be busy. What we DID not expect was to be told "oh we don't take names for tables, its first-come, first-served" WTF? You mean to tell me we have to go hover over someone's table and then IF we eventually can poach a table before someone else grabs it, then WE are going to have people standing over us all night waiting for us to finish? What the heck kind of business model is this? No thanks, we turned and left and went to The Pour House where we COULD put our name in and did and had a table in 15 minutes. We will not be back to this World of Beer nonsense. Good luck with it.

Ouch.  Not sure why the Hilton chain put their brand name on this one.  Definitely not up to the standards of a Hilton.

I don't want to be too hard on the staff - they definitely tried to give good service.  But you can see that they are trying hard to forget that they are in a crumbling, smelly, outdated version of the hotel that they thought they'd be staffed in when they got their degree in hospitality management.

The hotel is close to absolutely nothing (unless you count Walgreens and Target) and I don't even remember if they have a restaurant.  I spent the night in my room doing work, and not because I had to!

Definitely worth avoiding if possible.

This bakery reminds me of those old style, no frills , local French bakeries in Paris from 20 years ago. 
The shop is a bit dingy looking and the selection is very limited but they do have some decent offerings at reasonable prices. . We purchased a ham and cheese croissant, choux puffs, and a ganache. I asked my family to pick out a few things but they had to think long and hard to pick something that looked really appealing. Usually they are macaroon fans but they said these macaroons looked different and funny. The macaroons are puffed up and spongier looking.

Cafe Blue Moose is located in the heart of the artsy and funky town,  New Hope, PA. This cute little restaurant has an eclectic vibe, amazing food and a fairytale backstory. 

The restaurant is in a "house" with several small sections 
of tables. There are tables on the first floor by the window for people watching, upstairs in a small but uncrowded room and the back where there is an enclosed sunroom. The decor include lights encased by tiny whisks and baking pans, cheese graters and large whisks. 
The food is great because it tastes fresh and most things taste like it's made from scratch.  We came for brunch and ordered the almond vanilla French toast, ham and cheese omelet, eggs Benedict, pesto mushroom omelet, and a cheeseburger. All were very good. 

Unlike other French toasts I've tried, this French toast has a thin texture, almost like a dense pancake with a lot of flavor. It was topped with strawberries, bananas and blueberries. The maple syrup it came with was warm, thick and delicious with the French toast.  It also came with Apple compote with chunks of apples and tasted freshly made. 

The other entrees were also good. The fries that came with the burger was thick cut and crunchy on the outside and  hot and soft on the inside. It had a really nice flavor too. 

There are newspaper clippings in the bathroom describing the backstory of this restaurant. It started as a youth-run restaurant where Skylar Bird (only 14!) and his friends served family/friends in a part of his home and later developed a local following. 

We came on a rainy Mother's Day and had an hour's wait. We were able to walk around the town until they texted us that our table was ready. 
There were empty tables but I'm guessing they probably didn't have the capacity to serve all the tables. 
Judging from other yelp reviews, there is usually a wait for this place. They do not take brunch reservations but they do take dinner reservations.  If you happen to be in New Hope, you have to check out this brunch spot.

If you enjoy sloppy seconds....

My mom and I arrived on Sat Vday weekend to an estimated 45 min wait-ok that's what bars are for. 55 minutes later I was on my second "Lemon" a delicious tart martini w the perfect touch of sweet from the simple syrup. The bar also served complimentary homemade black pepper potato chips which helped our bellies get through the wait. The drink and bar earned their 2nd star.

Our table was dead center in a tiny room with two other small tables. There was also a large table in back complete with a gaggle of gigglers that must have hit the happy juice hard. 

We started w/ an eggless Caesar which was overly oily and skimpy for the $9 price. My mom ordered the short rib as her main based on the bartenders suggestion and I went with chicken Romagnola w/ the addition of onion.

About five minutes after our salad a food runner came out w two dishes and he walked them back to the large party. I thought it odd he only had two dishes and when I heard him say w/ red onion I knew it was probably my food; however the people accepted the food.

Five minutes after that the runner returned back to the room and asked us what we ordered. At that point he scooped the food up from the big table circled out and back in the room ( yes I saw you) and tried to present the cold contaminated food down in front of us.

Near tears and shaking from this complete disregard we asked the food be removed and a manager sent over.

Alan the manager kneels down at our table apologizing for a food delay ( ummm not what happened at all). He seemed unconcerned by the food health safety issues and told us he would send antipasta out for the inconvenience. The mozzarella was rubbery and the red bell peppers slimy and neither of us eat prosciutto. 

We ended up only taking a few bites of food. My pasta tasted and looked bland and rushed and my mom's short rib was fatty and later fed to the dogs. 

Servesafe this restaurant is not.  I won't return. I would not recommend it...unless you enjoy cold sloppy seconds!

I was happy to try this place because I had walked past it a lot and always meant to stop by for a glass of wine.

The place looks nice and we got a table outside.  Our waiter was obviously new and the hostess came by to make sure we had been waited on.  Btw, wasn't that busy, just sayin.

The wines.  Okay, for a montepulciano that I can buy a bottle for $15 shouldn't be $9 a glass.  That's just ridiculous.  I understand profit and blah blah, but seriously, it's not worth $9.  Anyway, we both got a glass and they were unevenly poured.

The waiter took our order.  We ordered a pizza that apparently has a salad by the same exact name.  We were looking at the back of the menu where the pizzas are, and we did point it out to the waiter that that's what we wanted.

Two runners came by with the salad and they looked angry and confused when we said it wasn't ours.  The waiter finally came by to confirm that what we actually wanted was pizza.  So we waited another twenty minutes.  If there is a salad and a pizza called the same thing on the menu, wouldn't one think to clarify as a waiter?  He asked us "just one?" not "the pizza or the salad?".  I had no idea there was a salad by the same name since I'd never been there before.

Our pizza came and it was lame.  The pesto was good but there was hardly any sauce or anything on it.  It was like eating dough that had been cooked with toppings and they scraped the toppings off.  That's what it was like.

Our waiter was dealing with other tables outside but for some reason didn't ever come by or even near our table.  And yes, I would have flagged him down but he never once looked in our direction.  We waited and waited, for a long time.  So long that I decided to go in and complain.  Which I never do, but we were both really confused as to why our waiter never came by to even ask us how we were, or if we wanted another glass of wine.  Which I would have gotten if asked.  But NO ONE showed up.  At all.

So, I complained and both of the hostesses seemed to not know what to do in that situation, which is surprising since Serafina has 2.5 stars on here, so I'm sure they've gotten their share of complaints.  One of them looked at me and said "okay....sooooo....what do you want?"  I said that I wanted the check and that I was annoyed because I would have ordered another glass of wine if someone has just simply ASKED.  The other hostess, who seemingly had her head on more straight, said that someone would be out there shortly.

I'm thinking another waiter or a manager.  No.  Our waiter comes by and says, and I quote, "I'm sorry, miss...I'm not doing a good job?"

WHAT?!  In what restaurant do they send the waiter that you are complaining about to field the complaint about them!??  Let alone the quiet, nervous, new waiter who is clearly in over his head!  I was completely thrown, I felt like I was disciplining him.  It was awful.  Where the hell was upper management?  Or another more experienced waiter?  This made no freaking sense to me.

Not only did I get gypped on wine, ate sub-par pizza, but I also had to conduct a counseling session.  Unbelievable.  I will never ever eat here again.

I'm going to come out and say it. For living so close to the Gulf we do lack quality places to sit outside, enjoy a beer as the sun sets and get some good, fresh seafood. It's something that has bugged me for a while, so I was glad to hear of a new place that opened in Hernando beach about a month ago called Hernando Beach Tropical Grille. They promise a great Florida experience where you can sit outside either under the tiki hut or under the sun and have your beer and seafood without breaking the bank.

I chose my Wifes birthday as the time to experiment with the new place (which in hindsight could have been a problem) and left there 2 hours later glad that I did.

As we pulled up to the restaurant it was exactly as was described to me. It's a tiki hut with a deck out back overlooking the water. It's "no frills" and that's just fine with me. I love those types of places because, if they are busy, you know the food is the reason behind it.

The menu is on a whiteboard that they bring table side to you. They have bottled beer and wine. So far so good. The vibe is great. It's laid back, casual.

Before I even get into the food, let me say the staff are exceptional. They were over to our table INSTANTLY and they came back at least 12 times in the time we were there. It was one of the better customer service experiences I can remember in a long time.

We ordered the whole belly Ipswich clams for an appetizer on the advice of a guy at the next table. Then we had the fish tacos and lobster roll to split.

I love clams, I love them steamed, fried, with pasta. I just love them. These are among the best that I have had fried. If you haven't had whole belly clams (and I hadn't) then you are missing out. Don't be put off by the look of them, they are meaty and DELICIOUS. Served with the homemade sauce they set the tone for the rest of the meal. I would go back for these alone.

The fish tacos were the same, delicious and full of flavor. These are another must try item although (very minor criticism) they could have just a little more cheese etc to fill them out a little. But don't be fooled, these are good tacos and another item I will be thinking about this week as my stomach rumbles away.

Then the lobster roll..... The clue is in the name. It is a roll with lobster in it. Nothing else. No filler. Just delicious chunks of fresh lobster and a little mayo. It's perfect, there is nothing to detract from the flavor of the lobster, no attempts to mask it. If you like lobster then this is the place to go get a lobster roll.

All things told, I can't remember going to another place that had me so excited about going back there again so soon. No, it's not fine dining, and they are still ironing out a few minor kinks. But the service and food really leave an impressions. It's exactly what the beach area needs and I am sure they will be a great success. I certainly hope so....

Literally came here because i saw a fellow Yelper post a picture of churro with ice cream.  As soon as we were seated I had to make sure they had this.  Craving was satisfied in the end.  The churro was served warm.  I just wished it came with more ice cream.  I ordered the El Mariachi pork chop.  The chipotle demi glace made the dish.  The pork chop was cooked perfectly.  The chorizo mashed potato was delicious, just wished there were more than one piece of chorizo in it.  The guy had the molcajete.  Their version had a tasty green sauce.  It had plenty of proteins: shrimp, beef, chicken, and pork.  

This place probably has the best Mexican entrees around the area.  Yes, it's a bit more pricey than other places but you pay for quality.

Awesome new restaurant!

My next-door neighbors (hi Chad and Mary!) both work at CL -- one as soux chef and one as a server -- so I had heard about this place before it even opened. I finally made it for a meal recently and was quite impressed.

I just HAD to try to pig ears! I assumed they would be similar to cracklins, which they were. Fatty, crispy, deliciousness. I also really enjoyed the black-eyed peas and goat. But you really can't go wrong here. Everything on the menu is full of flavor and perfectly prepared.

Chad and Mary took good care of us and the rest of the service was very nice too. We sat at the bar for a little while before our table was ready and the bartenders and host staff checked in with us regularly to let us know what was going on. We ended up waiting a while for a table but it was definitely worth it. We'll be back for sure.

Strange but true: I learned about Moe's because I'm an Uber driver.

You see, I was doing some driving to make a little extra cash when I picked up this nice group of Southerners who squeezed 4 people into the back seat of my Camry, with a fifth up front with me. It turns out that they are family members of one of the founders of Moe's, and they suggested I give it a try.

I finally found myself in that part of down around lunch time today and I certainly am glad that I gave it a shot. That place is damn good! 

Since it was my first visit, I went with standards: pulled pork sandwich, baked beans, coleslaw. The pork was tender, the sauce was sweet and tangy with a hint of spiciness, and the slaw was vinegar-y and pepper-y. Everything was great. And it came with a fountain drink, all for $9.80. That's a pretty good deal, I'd say.

I will DEFINITELY go back to try some of their other offerings. Got my eye on the ribs especially.

People were nice, everything was clean, and service was quick. Looks like they are serving alcohol now too, for those of you who have to have a beer with your BBQ. 

Thanks, Moe's! And thanks, Uber.

Damn, the food here is delicious. It's not cheap, but it sure is good!

I've been twice now and haven't had anything that wasn't excellent. On my most recent visit, I started with the seafood gumbo. The roux was dark and rich and the small cup was loaded up with oysters, shrimp, and crawfish.

For my entree, I had the wild boar. Pretty sure this was the first time I ever ate wild board (WILD BOAR!). It rocked. And it came with the best piece of cornbread that I've ever had in my life. So moist, so fluffy. 

We shared a few desserts, including the "Snickers," which was peanut-y, chocolate-y, and rich. The lemon tart was also damn good.

Be prepared to drop some coin, but it's worth it.

I made my first visit to YOCI last night with my girlfriend and another couple and I will DEFINITELY be back. So good!

Girlfriend knows some of the chefs, who hooked us up with a comped appetizer and dessert, making the meal that much better. The grilled flatbread app featured oxtail and was delicious. The table also shared some fried oysters (topped with blue cheese!) and BBQ shrimp. Both fantastic. The sauce accompanying the shrimp was thick, creamy, and not to be wasted. Good thing it was served with some toasty French bread for dipping. For my main course I had the hamburger steak, which was topped with sauteed onions and brown gravy. Huge portion so I've got some left over for dinner tonight too. And finally, don't leave without sampling the fried bread pudding. 

Bonus: Giant Jenga outside the front door. Check out the pic.

People keep asking me what my favorite restaurant is in NOLA and I've never had an answer. If my next few visits to YOCI are as good as last night's, I'll have a response ready in the future.

I have to say that I liked the Italian beef sandwich better in Brandon, FL than the one I had in Chicago! I remember going to Portillo's in downtown Chi because my co-worker and other conference goers said I had to have an Italian beef. Me and a guy from Ohio looked at each other after eating our sandwiches wondering what the big whoop was all about. So, as a yelper I still wanted to try the FL location and with the help of Rachel I tried two other popular items.

1st I was quite excited the first time I came and realized I could get in a drive through! This helped with my busy day because I was sure I was going to have to walk in. The drive through was busy, but very efficient. My order was perfect.

I got the Italian Beef with sweet peppers, mozzarella dipped. It was soooo flavorful! I couldn't believe how much better this sandwich was from my Chi-town experience. I also ordered the chopped salad with no bacon. Wow! I don't know how they make their dressing, but it's so perfect for the type of salad it is. I crave that salad! I also got the chocolate cake because everyone and their mama kept raving about it...boo I wasn't impressed. I'm not a chocolate cake lover because I like good chocolate and most chocolate cakes use gross sugary chocolate frosting...and Portillo's is no different. I'm a chocolate cake snob so I won't knock 'em a star for what I already expected outbid a chocolate cake. 

I went back for a second run to make sure it wasn't a fluke...and my Italian beef and chopped salad were just as good. I have yet to actually go into the store or order anything else like a hot dog, but I give 5 stars for a damn good sandwich, salad, and a drive thru that gets the order right!

It's a good thing it's all the way in Brandon or I'd be doing a drive by more often.

We were happy to move away from St Pete in 2008 because at the time there wasn't much going on there, but we hated that we weren't going to be able to frequent Ft Desoto, st Pete Beach (pass-a-grille) and Mazzaros. Fast forward to 2016...now St Pete is a fun, bustling city with lots to do besides the beach and there are tons of great food options...some things about the Pete hasn't changed and one of them is Mazzaros!

We lived in Palm Harbor, Countryside (Clearwater) and we settled in the Westchase/Citrus Park area of Tampa and have not found anything that comes close to Mazzaros. Whenever I visit the Pete it's hard not to stop in if they're open. It's the best damn Italian Market in Tampa Bay. 

We buy cheese, bread, desserts, wine, coffee and prepared deli foods here. The two items I never leave without 1) the freshly made mozzarella and 2) fresh ciabatta bread. The mozzarella in the morning is still warm to the touch. It's a ball of heaven. If you haven't made a caprese salad with this mozzarella you are really missing out. The bakery has so many wonderful breads, but nothing beats eating crusty, fresh ciabatta from mazzaro's.

There are so many great things to say about this place, but there are some things to be aware of. Mazzaros is always busy, especially on Saturdays. It's very crowded most of the time as people really want to eat there...we mostly get items to go, but we still bump into people navigating about the store. Part of the reason for the business are the extremely inconvenient hours of operation. It's closed by 6pm on weekdays, closes at 2:30 on Saturday and closed on Sunday. With it being so wildly popular they have no need to extend hours for our convenience because they know we will make the arrangements to come...it's just that good.

I really can't wait to go back to Johnny Grits for breakfast! I've had this place bookmarked for years and could never remember to come here for breakfast unless it was during some off odd hours that I couldn't have it! Thankfully HubbyStanks brought me here for my Birthday weekend breakfast...so glad he did!

So many items look good, but we settled on Sweet Potato Pancakes and Shrimp and Grits. The Shrimp and Grits normally come with bacon, so I was afraid that maybe it wouldn't be as good as everyone says sans bacon. To my surprise the Grits were still delectable! I want more. The sweet potato pancakes were perfect. I never drown my pancakes in syrup unless they are flavorless and extra dry...these pancakes really didn't need much syrup at all.

I'll definitely excited to come back to try more menu items.

Not crazy about Bamboozle. It was just okay.

What I do appreciate about Bamboozle is the variety on the menu. I also like that there are small sized pho so if you're looking for a quick bite you can get just enough before or after any downtown activity. The help yourself water station is cool too. I also like the restaurant's proximity to Curtis Hixon Park.

What I didn't appreciate is that it took a long time to get food and boba drinks. I also didn't that I the food was as tasty as an authentic Vietnamese restaurant. The broth in the pho lacked flavor. I liked that I was able to get a beef lemongrass banh mi, but the French bread wasn't up to par. The boba drinks weren't as good as what you can get elsewhere either. I could barely taste the taro in my boba smoothie.

All in all I would probably come back if I was in the mood for a small soup when downtown as opposed to tacos or anything else, so I give it a 3 star despite not being blown away.

I'm no Viet food expert, but I think once you've had some quality stuff it's hard to eat at mediocre pho joints. To me that's what this place is. I really tried over the years to give this place a chance at more stars. You can get an okay meal here, but it's worth it to drive 5 minutes to get something better. I really don't like the feeling I get in here. It doesn't feel completely clean so whenever I'm asked to eat here I just turn it down. Not every place I eat at is immaculate, but if the place looks jacked I better be getting the taste of a lifetime and consistent service. The place just falls short for me...I do think they serve a purpose for those who aren't as picky as I am.

I enjoyed my Chuy's experience. It's Tex-Mex and family friendly. It's also right across the street from the Tampa Bay premium outlets which does not contain good food, So thankfully there are restaurants right outside of the outlets like Chuy's.

I always enjoy unlimited chips and salsa at Mexican restaurants. 

My kids and I ate here and everyone enjoyed their meals. I had the Shrimp & Cheese Chile Relleno & ground beef enchilada platter. I can't say that what I ate was the most memorable thing in the world but I do remember enjoying my meal and knowing that I would definitely come back after shopping at the outlets again. 

The decor is out of the 80s so I was pretty nostalgic. Tex-Mex restaurants were big when I was a little girl. 

Is this authentic Mexican? Not really...it's authentic Tex-Mex though. If you've ever lived in the Midwest or even on the West Coast you should be familiar with this type of casual fare.

So, I've always wanted to go to Ciro's but since I'm not a drinker I never get invited, nor was I sure it was going to be worth it for a date night due to me not being a drinker. I finally got invited out by my friend Charlie after her parents decided they weren't up for using her reservation because they had just done a cleanse the day before! Yay, I was so happy to be their replacement! Hey, I don't drink but I'll hang out at any establishment with good people, especially if they have food!

First I want to say that this speakeasy is so novel! I love knocking at the door and speaking a password. The 20's decor, uniforms, dark mood and privacy of the booths are so charming.

The drink menu is extensive. Yes, I'm a lightweight, but I was at Ciro's! I had to order a drink. I absolutely love Irish Cream so got "There Will Be Chocolate" and it did not disappoint! It was so good and I didn't even feel hot from the alcohol. My friend got the Fancy AF and it was totally fancy, but I was stuffing my face with cheese and grapes and missed getting a photo! So I did get an epic photo of her second drink that also came smoking that our server did a long pour on...I can't remember the name of that one. 

So, the charcuterie was amazing! Charlie doesn't eat pork like me so she ordered it before I got there and I trusted that it would be good, and it was. Grapes, berries, spicy pecans, a berry reduction sauce and amazing cheeses were included! 

I ordered the duck poutine. Not only was the presentation on point, but the egg was cooked to a creamy yolk perfection! I love anything duck and I really only care for french fries when there's seasoning or toppings. So this was right up my alley. I have to say it was difficult to choose. I love small plates because I can never eat all of my food. Yes, I took home the poutine in a box. However, I really want to go back because there are so many amazing items on the menu that I'd like to try.

Can't wait to go back.

This is a nice addition to the Westchase/Citrus Park area, but after my first experience here I'm not rushing to go back, unfortunately. 

I created my own burger, but they decided to bring me what they wanted to bring me. I asked for the smoked Gouda and I got goat cheese. I asked for BBQ sauce and it wasn't on the burger. The burger wasn't cooked to medium either. So they insisted they can make my burger right, but it came out over cooked again, the Gouda cheese was cold and not melted and they still forgot my BBQ sauce. 

They were nice about everything, but I just expected a much better experience on a not so busy lunch day. 

I guess if there were something that stood out about he food I'd be more enthusiastic about coming back, but when I crave a burger and Ford's is not even the 3rd place I think of...even with it being in the neighborhood...I can't give it more than an average rating. Although the kitchen got my meal wrong twice the manager and server was pleasant, it has a cool concept and it's close by so there are some pluses. I'm glad it's an option in the area because I don't do Applebee's. Hopefully when I come back I can raise my star rating for Ford's.

I'm glad Westchase has something different. The service here is fantastic. The food, however isn't stellar.

I want to start by saying that this is a cajun/creole style restaurant and I LOVE this style of food. I fly to New Orleans once a year just to eat and buy ingredients so I can make my own NOLA style food at home. Since I've lived in Westchase for over 7 years and have seen restaurants come in and serve 'mediocre at best' meals, my hopes weren't up when I saw a bunch of non-foodies posting about how great this restaurant is on the Westchase Neighborhood Facebook group. I was right. Only people who don't know this style of cooking will be impressed.

1) The place is called Seafood Exchange, but my seafood gumbo (menu said it contained shrimp, crab and fish) had no visual signs of seafood in it. Not one shrimp. If it had seafood in it then it had to be a ground into the roux. The roux was extremely light and too salty.

2) The chargrilled Oysters aren't close to New Orleans style (Dragos) or even what you'll get at Roux in Tampa. They weren't grilled enough to see a char and was just topped with too much Parmesan with no other flavor.

3) the rice and beans wasn't tasty, creamy and honestly the beans may have come out of a can. 

4) the fried gator was fried well like I like. However the remoulade sauce to dip with wasn't good.

5) the best item we ate was the bananas foster. I'd come back just for this. Not hard to make, but they got it right.

The atmosphere is pretty laid back, which is great and it's in my neighborhood. Again, phenomenal service. I just wish they were serving authentic dishes with great ingredients. The food wasn't bad for New Orleans fare out of Tampa, but there was nothing served that had me blown away or would have me rushing back.

Okay, so I frequent the drive thru more than anything at this location and I find it to be wonderful. I've eaten inside only once before the grand opening and it's the same as the one in Brandon which is similar to the one I went to in Chicago.

So far everything I've had here is great except for that chocolate cake everyone raves about. It's too sweet, but that's just my opinion because I prefer dark chocolates and ganache...I hate milky, sugary chocolate. It's very hard to impress me with a chocolate cake so I don't hold it against them as the consensus thinks it's the best. 

I usually get the chopped salad with no bacon. I love the dressing and the blue cheese crumbles. I also get an Italian Beef with cheese and sweet peppers, dipped. You gotta get your sandwich dipped in the au jus or you're missing the flavor...who cares if it's messy. The hot dogs are damn good here too. 

I like this location because when I stop by the drive thru is usually empty! I'm in and out in a jiffy...and I'm smelling and craving the food all the way to Westchase/Citrus Park. Thankfully Kung Fu is up the street so I can sip on a boba drink to hold me over on my ride home.

I should've knocked this review down to 3 stars a year ago, but I missed doing it. This is why I don't like to give reviews on my first visit...it went from a 5 star to 3 star review. Here's why:

Attention to detail isn't up to par. When this place fist opened the owner was present and the service and attention to detail was phenomenal...not anymore. As a matter of fact it only took a few months for the decline in service to happen. 

This coffee shop is quite deceiving. The and location and decor is great. The concept is great. The workers...not so much. They look like hipsters, but they lack the surprising great customer service that you find when you go to a "real" hipster establishment. It's almost like the owner told the employees to go dye your hair and wear grungy outfits to look the part...however, the love that hipsters put into food and service just isn't there.

The food isn't bad, but if you ask for any deviation from the menu don't expect that they'll get it right...nor will they be willing to change it unless you ask. They hope you'll accept the item the way it was made...incorrectly. 

The weirdest thing we noticed this morning was some chick sitting at a hostess stand outside. We weren't sure what to make of it because she wasn't looking out to the street, but hunched over, looking down (probably on her cell phone). Too bad there wasn't a sign that said it wasn't drive up stand and you can order food to-go right there. That's incentive for me! I love a drive-thru, but this one was poorly executed...yet with the right signage and eager employee, they can pull it off.

The one thing good I can say here is that they still offer Irish Creme flavoring syrup for coffee. In Seattle (home of the barrista style coffe shop in the US) you can get Irish creme everywhere. I'd come back for that.

For now this place is just average. Just like every other Westchase restaurant. Mediocre service.

Really 2.5 stars, but generously rounding up. I wanted to wait for a second visit to rate Wooden Ladle in hopes that things would be better after several months. While I can't recommend this place to anyone not living around the corner, I probably would come back for a dinner with my kids when I'm too lazy to cook and just want something other than burgers, chicken or tacos. So, it wouldn't be fair to give it a 1 or 2 if I can see myself coming back on a desperate night and have exhausted all of the fast casual around the Westchase/Citrus Park/Oldsmar vicinity. 

My first visit HubbyStanks and I decided to order 3 main dishes to get a feel of the menu:

1. Pho-men 
Well, it wasn't the best ramen and definitely wasn't the best pho I've ever had. However it was an okay bowl of soup...and I like soup. The dish just didn't have the flavor I expected. I got extra egg because I didn't realize that the dish already came with egg, so when the extras came up on the tablet I ordered. I worked out since we were sharing 3 dishes, but I wouldn't have needed that many on my own.

2. Abura Soba - subbed the pork for chicken
I liked this dish. I realize it normally comes with pork so maybe it tastes better that way, but I don't wanna know. I wish they would have used juicier thigh meat (as real Asian restaurants do), but the shredded chicken was okay. The ramen stands out in a brothless dish and I can appreciate that.

3. Dragon Bowl Z
HubbyStanks didn't mind it, but it wasn't the best poke or my cup of tea. It wasn't spicy as advertised and it didn't have a great poke sauce on it. Something was definitely missing...or maybe there was too much going on. Whatever it was it didn't work.

4. Fried Doughnuts
You know how you go to a nice Asian restaurant and with your check you get no more than 2 fried doughnuts...and they are the perfect ending to your flavorful meal...and you wish you could have more, but they won't give you more. Well, you can order them at Wooden Ladle...the problem is you don't want more...you leave some on the table. You get a nice amount, which is great. They come out nice and hot, which is great. BUT they were covered in way too much sugar. You just can't go to town on them like you want to. Even with my hot jasmine tea to drink, it was just too much.

On my second visit I came with my kids when HubbyStanks was out of town. 

5. Hawaiian Poke Bowl
What a disappointment. Look, as a half Asian who had rice with every meal growing up and growing up in Hawaii, I know rice. I know sticky rice. This rice could have been called rice-playdough. It was so stuck together that it actually hurt my hand to pull apart chunks of rice to eat with little pieces of tuna. What the hell are they thinking with this...and it was cold, which made it even harder to pull apart. I'm sure they make this up an a big batch, through a little rice vinegar on it mix it and put it in the refrigerator for days until someone orders. It didn't stop at the rice. I could have just eaten the tuna poke, avocado and extras, however the flavor was awful. NOTHING like what poke should taste like and how dare you add Hawaiian to the front of the name of this thing. 

6. Teriyaki Chicken Bowl
Both kids ordered this and they liked it...but what do kids know. Thank God it came with regular rice and not "sticky rice" or they would have complained. It also had carrots, a few cucumbers and iceberg lettuce in it. I know I'd never order this for myself. The chicken is not teriyaki. Instead it is fried chicken pieces with some sort of honey glaze on them. Since the kids don't know good teriyaki they thought the bowl was great...but they were eating a fried chicken bowl. Not acceptable for me, who also lived in Seattle where you can go to a corner in South Seattle and get the best damn teriyaki plate you've ever had. 

7. Fried Doughnuts...again
This time they weren't as sugary and went well with my jasmine tea. They still served a lot so my kids and I had enough. It is a good way to end your meal. 

In summary, I'd come again for ramen only. If I had a ramen craving, however I'd drive out of the area. This is the only Asian fast casual restaurant we have in this area, so I welcome it and hope they improve. We need more flavor out here! The ramen is decent so I can drive around the corner for a bowl of it. The rice bowls aren't good, especially the poke bowls. They need to go back to the drawing board on their poke flavors and learn to cook sticky rice. They also need to change the name of the teriyaki bowl to "fried chicken bowl" to not upset people looking for teriyaki flavor.

Yay! Finally a place nearby to get authentic café con leche just like in Miami. We first stopped in to try the breakfast mainly so we can critique the Cuban coffee. Since our go to Cuban food truck operator in the area retired we've been searching for a viable replacement. We were so impressed that most of the breakfast choices come with pan de mantequilla and café con leche. I'm not going to lie, I can come in for just the pan con mantequilla, café con leche and a cortadito to go and that would fuel me through a late lunch! I don't eat pork so they have turkey choices which I appreciate!

We were so excited that we came back the same day for a late lunch and ordered bowls. I got the chicken bowl with salad on the side. It was so flavorful! 

The bread basket they give you before your entree is out of this world! It's a mini fry basket with toasted bread and tomatoes for dipping/topping "bruschetta cubana." 

The side salad is scrumptious as they serve it with a house made dressing. The maduros are perfectly cooked (you know when the plantain is caramelized a bit on the edges!). 

So, the chef convinced me that I would like the flan...I ordered and I didn't like it...I love it! It was more like a high end flan. Much more rich and almost almost creme brûlée-like as the caramel on top isn't torched, but has a slight glass candy to break through before the custard. It's plated so pretty with mango sauce and a balsamic reduction.

My only criticism is that the Cuban toast isn't on the menu by itself, so when I came in and ordered the coffee and toast it was way overpriced. It would have been a better value to order a whole breakfast with eggs and hash brown that comes with the coffee and toast. Hopefully this gets worked out.

We've been back several times now for coffee, breakfast and dinner. Everything has been authentic and flavorful!

Came for brunch with my daughter and was pleasantly surprised! I never ate at WOB before. I'm not a beer drinker so I felt there was no place for me here...I stand corrected. The food is great! The openness of the inside and the outdoor seating was perfect!

I was about to leave town and wanted one last brunch and figured this was close enough to USF and I-275 so I could drop off my daughter and hit the road. I didn't expect to really enjoy my breakfast...but I did!

The one thing that was not on point was the donuts. I expected the order to be bigger...or the donuts to be bigger. They were cute though, just not worth it. I don't eat bacon though so mine wasn't topped with bacon...maybe this is what people like about it but to me bacon is gross so it should've been good without it. I didn't taste the bourbon in the syrup which I looked forward to. Star knocked off.

I ordered the yummalicious Steak & Egg Breakfast Bowl! The hollandaise sauce made this dish! I really loved the fried onion topping as well. The steak was a little bland but everything else made it so good.

My daughter loved her chicken and waffle sandwich and I couldn't stop stealing her tater tots!

I was pleasantly surprised and wouldn't mind going back to WOB for brunch and now I'm interested in coming in for dinner!

I came to Miguel's for the first time not long after I got home from Costa Rica. It was February 29, 2020. I remember it was a Saturday lunch and the place was packed! This was right before lockdown.

Over a year later, my son and I went for dinner (August 2021) and what a difference! Not only was there no wait, but could I count the number of guests, and all the tables were socially distanced. I was impressed. Mainly because most places I've been to in 2021 are not following protocols. Miguel's is safe, ya'll!

I was actually ashamed that it took me living in Tampa for 16 years to finally eat at Miguels in 2020. I actually had Miguelitos (also delicious) before Miguel's! Even before the pandemic I hated crowds...it takes a lot for me to wait for a table. more than 15 minutes.

So, some of the photos I put up was during my first visit. All I can tell you is that I tried everyone's dishes and they were all so good. On my second visit last week I had the seafood enchiliadas. It was OMG good. I don't eat pork so I didn't try my son's chimichanga, but he gave it a great review.

Miguel's is a Tampa staple. I'm sure no matter what I order on my next visit, I'll be impressed. 

To see how packed it was on my first visit pre-pandemic and to see how spaced out it was on my second visit during the pandemic speaks volumes to me.

I just want to thank Miguel's for caring about their employee's safety and customer safety. COVID-19 shouldn't be politicized and I'm glad to see that in a sea of Tampa restaurants that don't care and only think about the bottom line, a Tampa Institution like Miguel's is willing to do the right thing. 

They just earned my business as a regular. I look forward to my next Miguel's dining experience when I'm back in Tampa again next month...and every month thereafter.

This is now my most favorite Cuban spot in Tampa Bay! I am a sucker for flavor and all the meats and everything you eat here has flavor all the way through. I have to admit I'm never up for Cuban food when I think of wanting Hispanic food because most places in Tampa all taste the same and it seems like they only flavor the outside of the meat. I hate boring food so I'm always a pass when it comes to Cuban in Tampa. KUBA changed all of that for me!

The sandwiches and the bowls are amazing and flavorful! The black beans are just right. The green beans are so tasty you can eat them alone! Since I'm not a pork eater I can't speak for the Cubans but the altimo which is a Palomilla steak sandwich appears to be soaked in Mojo for at least 24 hours and you can really taste the flavor blast! So tender too! I get it on media no Che bread because of the slight sweetness and it goes so good with the savory taste of the sandwich. 

Every day they have a happy hour with different sangrias. 

I really need to go in for breakfast one morning because I hear it's amazing.

If you want a blast Cuban with tons of flavor you need to try KUBA!

This is a cool laid back open air restaurant stop when boating. It's part of the holiday inn that boaters can pull up to and stay or hang for the day with a mini water park. There was a live musician playing which gives this beachy restaurant a Margaritaville vibe. 

The food was just okay. It's the type of mediocre fare you'll find everywhere on the beach. The conch in the conch fritters were in hiding, the clam chowder was way too thick and sticky and the firecracker calamari was okay, but it was just calamari with Asian chili sauce (the kind you use to dip lumpia or egg rolls in) drizzled on top.

It's really all about the atmosphere here...which is acceptable on a beautiful Boating day.

I couldn't tell you how to get here by driving a car, but I'm sure it's a destination off of the Clearwater-Indian Rocks Beach area.

Besito for Vday was perfect! 

The atmosphere is rustic and romantic with candle lit tables. We were first seated at a table in the middle of the room, but we asked to move...we order every course on a first visit so I need to be comfortable. They had no issues with moving us.

I'm not a drinker, so I totally appreciate the fact that my unsweetened tea was brewed to perfection, fragrant and delish! It was also brought to me I a Patron bottle, so I was able to refill and look like I was doing something alcoholic (almost). Our server asked me if I wanted fresh squeezed agave and although I usually drink unsweet I could tell that this tea would be great with agave. Turns out it was passion fruit tea and the agave made this one of the best iced teas I've ever had! 

The complimentary chips and salsa is good, but the table side guacamole was surprisingly better than I expected! I had it at Flamestone and love the loads of garlic...Besito doesn't use garlic or limes, but it was wonderful! A must try and I will be sure to try it again and again! 

I had tough time choosing between a few dishes, but I ended up getting the market price pescado that was blue corn crusted. The fish was a mahi mahi and sat atop roasted corn, red and yellow bell peppers. Half the plate was covered in a panlano/cilantro cream sauce and the other half was in a creamy corn sauce. I recommend trying the fish in the green panlano sauce first because it's savory. If you try the sweet corn sauce first you miss the goodness in the flavor of the green sauce. 

Mel had the Swiss enchilada, which I would have chosen had he not ordered it. I had a taste and I definitely prefer it with cheese and tomatillo sauce. He gave me a dry piece and it wasn't as good. I'm not big on chicken enchiladas...I prefer steak or ground beef, so there must be tons of cheese and great sauce. I loved the salsa verde, but it could have used more cheese...just a preference of mine, however this was a fantastic dish. 

I love the fact that I could tell all the sauces were made in house. I really would like to try the enchilada mixto?? Sans the chorizo when I go back because it made with a guajillo sauce. 

I ordered the chocolate pudin dessert. It's a cross between a mousse and a pudding. It was extra rich, but good. You can tell it's made with a good Mexican chocolate. I would've liked it to be a bit less sugary, but hey it's dessert! I could only take 3 teaspoonfuls and it will take me a full week to finish it at home. 

The complimentary Churros were excellent. We were also given the Mexican worry dolls...something cute to bring home to the kiddos. I also like the modern checkout process by tablet. 

Our server was excellent. Management also came by to ask how we liked the food as well. It was a perfect dinner date night. 

The iced tea and fresh agave is calling me. I may be back sooner than later just for the tea!

I wish I could like this place more than I do. It missed the mark for me due to inconsistency and hit or miss items on the menu.

The first time I came I wasn't impressed. It was just okay. The second time I came it was better than expected. I got the shrimp special and it was very good. Not on the permanent menu. I came for a third time and I'm glad the Blueberry Cobbler isn't on the permanent menu. It was so sweet that after a few bites I felt like making a dental appointment. I don't think whoever made it tasted it. I got brisket all three times and I always get moist. The brisket isn't always moist and it was pretty dry the last time I was here. The sauces are just okay as well. None of them blow me away.

This place has a great concept, but with Jazzy's up the street and 4Rivers with a similar, but stellar menu...and always moist brisket, it's too hard to say I can make this a BBQ choice again...unless someone invites me.

I like the chicken here. The taste is clean, yet moist and flavorful. The green sauce is the best. I don't care for the white sauce as much.

The Cilantro rice and beans I've had were decent as well. 

The other meats are just okay. Stick with the chicken.

The location is in a weird spot on Hillsborough near the airport, so I always forget to eat here.

I can't believe I've overlooked Fleming's all the years I lived in Tampa Bay!

HubbyStanks took me here for our customary steak dinner on our 14th Anniversary. We've been to all of the high end steakhouses in Tampa, so I always dismissed Fleming's since it's part of the Bloomin' chain and I don't care for Outback or Carrabba's...however I am a fan of Bonefish Grill so I guess I should have looked at Fleming's as an individual restaurant. This year Papi insisted that we try Fleming's since we were sort of disappointed with our Council Oak Anniversary experience last year as the service just wasn't up to par. Fleming's definitely has service down!

I wasn't just pleasantly surprised at how great Fleming's is but I was blown away. The service alone shot this restaurant up on our Tampa steakhouse list. Complimentary valet. Seated immediately upon arrival. Our table was set with an Anniversary announcement place setting, a rose and a card From the operating manager. We were greeted with a "Happy Anniversary" by everyone we encountered. A photo taken and framed for us before we ordered. Complimentary champagne and truffles as a parting gift. THE BEST SERVER in Tampa, Jaime was at our service. Jaime told us the history of the restaurant, his history with the restaurant and he listened to what we wanted and delivered! 

Everything we ordered was cooked to perfection. The steaks are phenomenal. No need to go over what we ate as the pics I posted and HubbyStanks (Mel R.) posted speak for themselves and other reviewers have gone into detail on how great each item is. Just know that you won't be disappointed if you want a wonderful steakhouse experience in a modern setting. 

HubbyStanks is a huge steak guy and ranked Fleming's extremely high on his Tampa list so we'll definitely be back.

I love Revolution Ice Cream for its quirkiness and I had nothing but great experiences there. That being said I've only ordered the Chocolate Habenero ice cream and I absolutely love it. It's the perfect storm in your mouth. Cold rich chocolate, but an afterburn of fiery habanero. So so good I can't order anything else.

The only reason I wouldn't give it a 5 star is because the ice cream consistency is harder than I prefer...but I'm a custard lover, so I like my ice cream creamier and smoother.

Other than that, maybe one day I'll be convinced to try another flavor and be blown away.

I so love this casual, fun, open air hang out and food spot! We really should have more of these in beautiful Florida. The name is cute, but it's definitely not a mini mart (in my day...yes I guess I'm old...we called convenience stores mini marts) so don't get this foodie spot twisted. 

The first time I came here was to attend the Cass Street Deli popup, so I didn't review until I had a chance to come and order from the Nebraska menu. The menu is on the wall next to the order window and features some familiar foods with eclectic twists that are sure to give your taste buds a jolt. I've tried the Korean Cheesesteak, Charred Corn, Chicken and Waffles and Chicken Wings. All items were full of flavor. None of the items were traditional. I was there with my brother and sister and law's families so everyone got to get what they wanted. The guys were happy with beers, the girls got frozen drinks, I got a special rootbeer.

So, all the seating is outdoors but there is a covered area with TV's and fans. The best part about the Seminole Heights fun spot is the setup. There are games for small groups situated all over the place including Jenga, Ping Pong, Corn Hole, Bocce Ball and Shuffle Board. The atmosphere is all about fun. They even play hip hop to get you in a hip mood. 

I'm sure when the weather is perfect it can get packed here. However I didn't have a problem finding seating or ordering right away when I came. I did come in the dead heat of Summer on my second visit. They do have fans, but it's pretty hot to be outdoors in Tampa, but you should be prepared for that.

If you can't have fun here then you're just not that fun.

This place has been in my bookmarks for a couple of years and I finally made HubbyStanks take me! Since it's near Bellaire in Clearwater it's a bit far for him as he's not crazy about breakfast. He was glad we made the trek. Truly 5 stars!

I had to get the brioche French Toast that a lot of my yelp buds raves about. It didn't disappoint. I didn't even need syrup! The berry jam was enough and I didn't need much of that. Do yourself a favor and try it with nothing. It's that damn good!

My son ordered a waffle with scrambled eggs and bacon. When the eggs arrived they were over medium. They looked so good that I didn't want to take them back. I instead asked them to just make my son's eggs and I'll eat the over medium eggs...my fave way to eat eggs...and barely anyone gets it right...Jerome not only cooked it perfectly, but they were seasoned perfectly!...just how I make them at home! No one has the audacity to season eggs, which I think is such a shame. I love this restaurant just for egg seasoning alone!

Papi got the Norwegian because I told him he'd like it...and he loved it. I did too!  the salad and mashed potatoes are a bold move for breakfast, but worked so well with the perfectly poached eggs and ciabatta! 

I can't wait to fly with Romy Rome again!

Where has this place been all my life! 

I love Cuban, Dominican and Puerto Rican food, but one of my biggest gripes with most of those restaurants in Tampa are the lack of veggies or a good salad (with the exception of the 1905 salad at Columbia Restaurant). I get tired of meat, beans and rice and another starch (potatoes, plantains or yucca) and I often crave veggies after eating in those type of places. 

I love a good salad and Perdigon delivers! I'm not as familiar with Venezuelan food, but it seems like a cross between Colombian and Argentinian. I guess I have an affinity toward South American food as opposed to Caribbean or Central American just because I love hearts of palm and in my experience I can always find hearts of palm in Southern American cuisine. The Palmitas Salad here is the best! They feature hearts of palm, romaine, corn, avocado, black olives, feta cheese and mix it all in a wonderful dressing. They also gave us extra salad dressing in the side, but it wasn't needed. I could've just eaten this salad with a skewer and I would've been good. 

For my entree I ordered the queso de Mano cachapa with a beef skewer (it comes with chorizo but I don't eat pork so I can't speak on it). Wow! The sweet cachapa pancake with that ooey gooey cheese is to die for! The tender tasty beef skewer was a great accompaniment. HubbyStanks got the parilla Argentina with Arepitas and 2 huge tostones (I don't think they call it tostones, but it's similar but cut the long way and smashed and fried). The steak and chicken was tender and seasoned well.

This place is an upscale yet very tiny restaurant. It was full when we arrived, but thankfully there was a small table for 2 available next to the front t counter. Our server spoke only Spanish. I have no issues with that, but I do think that the server should be familiar with the English written items on the menu or the menu should have the Spanish word next to the English word on the menu for all items. This made it hard for me to order a sweet tea. The menu said sweet and unsweet tea...there was no Spanish writing for this. So I had to look to HubbyStanks to order my drink for me because I didn't know how to saw sweet tea. Of course what do I get...an unsweet tea anyway. I could've said "te" all on my own! His excuse was that I always order unsweet. Ugh...it's ok, I guess it wasn't meant for me to have the extra sugar. I have yo say that the tea was pretty good. They give you a slice of lime that gives it a perfect tartness...so I was happy nevertheless. This would be the only hiccup I had here.  

I can't wait to go back and try more of the menu. I'll just struggle with Spanglish ordering. I'm sure I'll get something good even if the order is wrong. The food is just that good here.

I was recently asked what my favorite type of cuisine was and for some reason the first thing that came to mind was Ethiopian (Habesha...includes Eritrean) food. I think I said it because I hadn't had really good, really authentic Ethiopian food in years...because I love food and picking a fave is not easy.  I say all of that to say that I have not found great authentic Ethiopian food in the South. Mitmita is very good, but it is good for newbies who never had Habesha food. If you are Habsha or have lived in a region of the US where there is a Habesha community and you'e had the food, you know what I mean. 

After leaving Hawaii as a teenager I finished High School in Washington state and I lived in Seattle on and off as an adult for about 3 years total. Seattle has a huge Ethiopian/Eritrean (Habesha) community and you can find  Habesha food all over the South End of Seattle. My first time having it I was with a group of Ethiopian friends who took me to lunch when I was 17 and I had the famous Doro Wat. My mouth was on fire, but I just kept eating and eating. There's something so flavorful and different about Habesha food that is irresistible if it is authentically done. Ethiopian food may have been the reason I love and am able to eat spicy foods. 

So, at Mitmita you will find no such spiciness in the food. I asked if they can make everything authentically Ethiopian hot, but they were honest in that they have to make the food to accommodate the typical American palate. I get it, but it sucks. Every Ethiopian place I have been to in the Southern United States has been this way. I have issues with Chinese take out restaurants for this very reason...not spice, but not getting authentic Chinese cuisine (I usually only eat Chinese food in a China Town where you see Asians eating) . I digress...I really with Mitmita would also accommodate those wanting authentic Ethiopian. They do serve very authentic Ethiopian coffee and the injera is on point. 

The food here is very flavorful even though it isn't authentically hot. The berbere is a lot lighter in color than I am used to...which is probably due to it not being spicy, and you can see the onions which typically is cut mush smaller and cooked down so that the onions are more incorporated into the sauce. The Doro Wat is still tasty, just not as spiced as I like. The veggie dishes are delicious. I am also used to the lentil dishes being a bit more cooked down. HubbyStanks "thinks" he doesn't like lentils, however at other Ethiopian restaurants I have been able to feed it to him because it looked like meat. At Mitmita the lentils look like lentils and he won't eat them.

I do recommend Mitmita. You will not find these flavors in any other cooking (although some items are similar to Indian and other African cuisine the flavor is different). I love that it is closer to my home than the other Ethiopian restaurant in town. The service is also wonderful. The owners are lovely people and they really make you feel at home. Be prepared to eat with your hands...the injera is your utensil!

I like Sparkman Wharf for meeting up with friends and family, but it's not going to be one of my go-to spots for food like I thought it would be. 

I get it if you live close. I get it if you have out of town guests...you can show them how cute the shipping container food vendors are. I get it if the weather is perfect and you want to chill outside. 

My issues with Sparkman Wharf:

1. Overall the food is just okay. I expected to be blown away by local food. I feel like the vendors created food options that was easy to make in the tight container space and easy to put in to-go containers. Understandable.

2. If it's raining or if it's too hot (or too cold) I wouldn't want to go because the food is okay, but not good enough to endure bad weather. 

3. Not enough tables for sitting down to eat...on a beautiful day of course. Long tables with barstools would be nice. The day we came it was so packed that a lot of people including a lot of us in my party were sitting on the artificial turf. I wonder if all the dogs around are peeing and pooping on the turf? It's not sanitary to touch the turf then eat (because you couldn't find a table/chair to sit and eat).

4. No stations with napkins or utensils. 

5. No places to wash hands or hand sanitizer dispensers...except for the restroom...when you are trying to snag a table to eat it's hard to wash hands before eating unless you have people that can watch your food for you.

I'm not one for roughing it. Without the basics for cleanliness I feel like I'm roughing it a bit. I don't like public restrooms, so I avoided them...I was told they weren't sparkling clean.

I would recommend everyone go at least once to experience how cute it is. It's a nice attraction and great for Tampa. I'm sure I'll have enough reasons to come back a few times a year. When I do I'll pack the essentials and bring them with me.

This 5 star review is for how much fun I had! I'm not a big drinker but the drinks were amazing and so good I barely noticed I had Asian flush! LOL! 

I will put a disclaimer out before the end of this review that the I my food I had was spinach dip and I want impressed. Too many breadcrumbs and my chips had a few stale ones which was weird.

So why 5 stars? Well I had never known they had food when I passed by al other locations in Las Vegas, LA and Orlando anyhow. I was always too full but just wanted to peak in because they are so cute.

I got a Raspberry Chocolate Martini. It blew me away and I want one now. Not only did it taste wonderful but I've been searching for that whipped cream for years! I used to go to a place in Oklahoma City that whipped up their whipped cream so decadent that I ordered a strawberry daiquiri every time I went in to eat...finally after all these years I have that whip again! So rich, thick and perfectly sweet!

The entertainment in this joint is amazing. About once an hour the severe get up and do a dance to a popular song and the patrons pull out Phones and sing along.

They had a lot of impressively poured fishbowl drinks that are picture worthy as well. 

I can't wait to go back in, try an actual meal and get a dessert...and any drink with that whipped cream!

I love this restaurant! The old time concept and servers with suspenders is charming. 

After checking into the Renaissance we walked up and down Broadway and ran into Merchant's due to the yelp star rating. We only wanted a little to eat because we didn't want to get too stuffed before getting into our dresses for a concert later in the evening. It was so hard not to order huge meals because every plate we saw go by looked amazing. We decided on splitting the arugula salad, half tater tots and smoked wings. I'm not a tater tot type of gal but the house made honey mustard was so good! Half the salad was huge for me. The wings were perfectly seasoned and the sauces, especially BBQ were all so good.

If I had more time in Nashville I would've gone back for a full meal. So much looked so right. Service was on point.

Since this is the closest Whole Foods to me I come here for certain organic items I might need in a recipe that I can't find elsewhere without the added gmo's. 

The other reason for my Whole Foods trips is getting lunch or dinner at the salad bar. However, aside for the one at Westshore, this is one of the worst Whole Foods salad bars I've gone to. The one is Clearwater is good and the one I've been to in NYC (specifically the one at Columbus Circle) is the best. 

I also frequently stop in for coffee and baked goods. The "baristas" really know what they're doing. Café con leche, cortaditos, brown sugar cortado, green tea lattes and dark chocolate mochas are absolutely delish here. The coffee they us is called Allegro. Yum. The pan de queso in the bakery cabinet next to the coffee bar (when fresh) go very well with a cup of coffee. 

The workers here aren't as cheerful as the one in Clearwater. For the price I pay to shop in this piece I expect happiness!

OK so I always talk smack about how I don't have places to eat nearby except for just a few favorites. I actually never tried Irish 31 in all the years that I've lived in Westchase and I feel ashamed. I finally had a lunch date with someone who lived in West Park Village and she recommended Irish 31. 

The place was pretty empty so I didn't have high hopes. 

The server there during lunch is extremely pleasant and fun. They also play awesome music and since there was no one around I felt free to just sing alone as I was waiting for my food.

On my first lunch date I decided to go for a burger and I got the black and blue without bacon because I was intrigued by the i31 Whiskey Sauce. This burger was gourmet, cooked to perfection and that sauce really set it off! I even got extra sauce on the side because it was so good. I'm not a big fry eater but the french fries were pretty good as well.

On my second visit I got the Wings with i31 Whiskey Sauce. Perfection. I also got a harvest salad which did not disappoint.

So I do have a new restaurant that I've added to my very short list in Westchase.

I've passed this restaurant by and never trying it because the sign wasn't appealing to me. What a mistake. Thai food from this restaurant seems to be on point and it's pretty close to home! I no longer need to go all the way to Clearwater to eat at Ban Thai...however lunch was a mess!

This place would get 5 stars if it weren't for these 2 items:

1) the first time I tried to eat here we wanted sushi and Thai food, but they said they stopped serving sushi. Ban Thai does serve sushi...so I was quite disappointed and we left. Inconsistent with what is online

2) we came for lunch, was seated right away and got our tea, soup and salad right away, but after 30 min we had to ask where our food was and was told it would be another 10 min! I noticed everyone around us also didn't have their meals and more people were coming in and being seated. The servers were literally running to bring plates out to tables...unfortunately a table of 2 would get their plates 10 minutes apart! Unacceptable for lunch. They need more cooks in the back during lunch hour to accommodate all the traffic they get. We ended up asking for our food to be boxed when it was ready. 

So why do I give 4 Stars even with the above disappointment? Well, I ordered Panang Curry with squid which is a go to meal for me when I get Thai. If your Panang is good I'll try other things...it was fantastic...even out of that styrofoam box I ate at home! HubbyStanks got the green curry with squid and it was equally delicious. Why squid? Because I can make chicken, beef and shrimp Thai curry at home. I don't keep squid in my freezer and it's tricky...you either cook it very quickly or you cook it a very long time or else it gets tough. In Pacicic's case the squid was perfectly tender....and pretty (scored which causes the squid to curl into little cylinders).

So, the soup and salad were good. I like how Ban Thai gives you the same soup, but with egg rolls. Pacific doesn't give you the sugary fried dough rolled in sugar like you do at Ban with your check.

I love the flavor, just not the wait...during lunch. I'll have to come back when it's not so busy.

This is actually a 3 1/2 stars, but I'll round down due to inconsistency. I like the food here. Is it the best Jamaican food I've had in Tampa Bay? No, but this place has gone from horrible when it first opened to a solid spot to get food to go. When it first opened the people working here was so sweet, but the food was so bad that I decided to just never write a review in hopes things would get better by the time I came back...well it's at least 3 years later and I'm unsure if the owners or managers changed, but the food certainly did...for the better.

I've come to pick up dinner for the fam twice in about 2 months. I believe the first time we came was on a Sunday. We checked out the menu, but I knew I wanted Curry Goat...they were out. I wanted rice and peas...they were out. I ended up with curry chicken with roti, jerk chicken, white rice, and oxtail. All took forever to receive, but all tasted good when we got home. The Oxtail was especially good and had dumplings in it. 

The 2nd time I came a few days ago I really wanted roti, but no one made any that day. HubbyStanks called in the order and it was ready when I got there. I ended up with Oxtail, Jerk Chicken and Escovitch fish and this time all 3 meals had rice and peas. The rice and peas weren't as good as I expected, but it was ok. The Oxtail this time had no dumplings in it, but it was still good. My escovitch was so delicious. I'm just not crazy about the cabbage veggie side that I've had at numerous Caribbean spots that have me craving more...but they were just okay. 

Unfortunately, as of Feb 2019 the restaurant will be closed on Sundays. Well that just sucks, but I guess that would be a good day to venture over to St. Pete or East Tampa to get Caribbean fare when in the mood for it.

Since there are no other Jamaican restaurants nearby any longer this is my neighborhood spot and I'll be back time and time again to try more menu items when I'm too lazy or too busy to cook.

We're in NOLA at least once a year either for business or just to eat. As part of a Birthday trip to NOLA HubbyStanks booked the cooking school for an afternoon lunch. 

We were lucky enough to get Chef Kevin Belton! He was entertaining, he talked about the history an ethnicities of New Orleans and he did a fantastic job showing us how to cook several creole favorites!

At the end they even sang Happy Birthday to me. I had a wonderful time and I'd recommend this activity for anyone visiting the city.

This was our favorite sushi spot in Tampa for many years, but since we have one in Westchase we don't come here as much...however this one is the best. We loved coming here before or after a comedy show downstairs at the Improv, but on weekends there's always a wait. I've been here in the afternoon on a weekday and that was the quietest I've ever seen it. I love the atmosphere in this location. 

My absolute favorite dish at Samurai is the volcano. If you've never had one get one here. If you've had a volcano elsewhere, get one here. They are the only ones who make it with warm conch instead of crab surprise. It's so much cleaner and you can taste all the flavors bursting in your mouth.

I also love the blue moon, samurai, ahí tuna poke and ahí tuna tataki. The sushi chefs here are top notch.

I really love Maple Street. I would love to give them 5 stars, but maybe I'll update my review when changes are made or the pandemic is over.

I recently did a pick up order during self quarantine and was disappointed to see through the window workers preparing food without masks on and workers bringing food out without gloves on.  I think in these times we can't be sure who has the virus (asymptomatic) so it's better to err on thee side of caution. 

Why let the cooks breathe on the food if you're going to go through the trouble of having customers social distancing outside (which really wasn't enforced it was up to the customers to stand on the blue X, but the person greeting everyone and passing food to customers didn't have a mask or gloves on). 

This is my reason for docking a star. I'm a germaphobe and I notice everything done that can cause the spread of germs. Most of the spread happens via the asymptomatic or people with very little symptoms...unless you're in a hospital or caring for someone with the virus.

Otherwise every item I've had here has been good. In normal circumstances everything is fine. Staff is friendly and the place is kept clean to the naked eye. 

I won't be ordering again until there's a vaccine, however. I've ordered a lot of takeout and I've seen it done right by local businesses. You can't just go through motions to satisfy minimum guidelines to stay open. Note that I did my pickup when restaurants were not able to open dining rooms. Now that dining rooms are allowed to be opened I can only imagine the carelessness that is happening that can add to a spike in corona cases.

If you really cared you'd have all employees wearing masks and gloves. I'm not putting myself or my family at risk over a biscuit sandwich craving. It's unfortunate I'll have to say goodbye for now. 

Again, I'm giving a good number of stars (4) because these are abnormal circumstances and the business shouldn't be rated solely on how they are/aren't practicing the very best guidelines on not spreading covid-19. It's our government's fault for not mandating masks and gloves.

For $600 dollars a night I could have stayed at many places I chose this place to enjoy the beach and that dream was ruined when i took my kids to play on the sand and discovered we were playing in crude oil.  

I am not one to exaggerate but i lost my slippers to this crude and my swimming shorts.  

It took me over 2 hours to clean up the crude off my skin.  The hotel had gasoline wipes that assisted with the clean up effort.  

The Hotel itself was very nice but for $600 night I could have picked so many other hotels I only chose this place for the beach experience.   Avoid going to the beach here if you go you will regret it.

I'm so glad I accidentally stumbled upon this place on my way out of work yesterday. I don't think my life will ever be the same again.
