As someone who grew up in Europe, I get a bit nostalgic at times, and I could not have been more excited to find out that a piece of Italy has made its way across the Atlantic Ocean and nestled itself on Chestnut Street between Sephora and the music store. 

Entering this establishment, I was greeted by (a hostess, but also) a delicious looking assortment of gelato. I hear some flavors are spiked, which I'm really excited to try. If it weren't so cold outside, I would have been compelled to clean out this entire gelato section myself. However, since it was cold and I already had dinner, I decided to add a nice finish to my evening by sipping some hot, aromatic Italian coffee along with bites of their delicious pastries. 

Though I wish I could have sampled everything, I only got to try the lavender panna cotta and white chocolate bread pudding. However, both were heavenly and well-balanced in both flavor and texture. You can be sure that I will be back to try every single item at this establishment - whether it is for breakfast, lunch, dinner, or a late night glass of wine. Very solid execution in product quality, concept, and service.

Of all the newly opened Philly restaurants I've been to this year, I must say this was the most visually appealing. I think the owners of Sampan and Double Knot did a great job creating an alternative universe nested between two nondescript buildings on the boring side of Sansom St. between 15th and 16th - the side with the parking garage and bare walls that are often lined with dumpsters (not to worry though - there were no dumpsters near the restaurant entrance). The decor is an interesting mixture of industrial and classy; with industrial-looking light fixtures and exposed brick walls, but also antique style furniture, framed mirrors, and paintings. The main dining room feels spacious with its open floor plan and high ceiling. Walking into this space feels like walking into a bygone era. 

Though there were a few kinks with service coming from various staff members, our server was friendly and his service was very smooth. His recommendation was ~3 small plates per person. The 3 of us ended up sharing 7 items, ranging from starters to entrees. 

Among the starters and small plates, I would highly recommend the Spanish octopus. It was very well-made - flavorful and not chewy. I believe there were 3 medium-sized tentacles. The lamb meatballs, littleneck clams, and burrata were also good, though I felt the burrata was a bit too watery, and in order to go well with it, I felt the bread that came with the dish should be a bit more glutinous. 

For our entrees, we tried the diver scallops and hanger steak. Both were outstanding. The scallops were seared to perfection (great texture and flavor), while the steak was very tender and came with a very good sauce. The pricing is not bad, but I do think the portions are a bit on the smaller side for the price. The scallop dish had 3 pieces, which came with parsnip puree and light garnish, while the steak was cut into 4-5 strips and came with a few shiitake mushrooms. We ordered a side of grilled cauliflower, which was also light. 

For dessert, I highly recommend the chocolate cake. It's so moist, not too sweet (which I really like), and comes with layers of delicious chocolate mousse (or some type of cream with similar texture). Priced at $12 a slice, it's a bit steep, but considering how phenomenal it is, I do think it's worth getting. Drink-wise, they have a pretty extensive list. I tried two cocktails and felt they were too sweet, so maybe next time I'll stick with wine or beer with my meal.

I had this place bookmarked for some time and was glad to finally get to try it, but after today's oddly awkward and rude service from the older lady who took our order, I'd definitely have to think twice before recommending this place to anyone else. 

I didn't mind that there was a lack of service since the beginning, since Chinatown isn't exactly known for great service in general, and I even tipped generously before leaving, despite the unpleasant service (I'm actually regretting it a little). They are open continuously from lunch to dinner on Saturdays, and my sister and I were in around 4pm, far from their closing time. There was no one else in the restaurant, yet for some reason, we were continuously rushed by our server. 

The older lady who served us kept pressing for our order before we had a chance to look at the menu. She was short with us and didn't seem to be in a good mood, but I didn't make too much of it. Out of consideration, we hurriedly looked at the menu and ordered some food and coffee items, which turned out a bit overpriced for the quality. The coffees looked nice in presentation, but tasted a bit too sweet and lacked flavor, which didn't justify their $5+ price tags. 

I had kept a menu on the table with the intent of ordering some dumplings closer to dinner time (it was still before 6pm), but while I was catching up with my sister, the older lady kept on interrupting us and rudely asking whether I was still going to order more food. I asked her if they were closing soon, despite the posted closing time of 8:30pm, and she said grudgingly: "No, but you guys have been here for a long time!"

Not sure what was going through her mind, since they would still have to keep an empty shop open even if we hurried with our orders. She just helped me save half of the money I intended to spend there. I was considering this place for a potential meet-up spot with friends, but after today, I definitely don't feel motivated to recommend it to anyone or to come back. Fortunately, there's no shortage of nice coffee shops in Philly.

Nice little cafe that seats roughly 20-25 people. The service is friendly and the coffee is great!

The menu is not extensive and things tend to be pricey and on the smaller side, but the quality is all right. (Mainly talking about the pastries because I can't say I'm super impressed with the reheated spongy egg square nestled between two crumbly, burned, fast-food-quality slices of English muffin that they pass off as a breakfast sandwich.) 

Other breakfast-y items include yogurt parfaits, and it seems like they also have salads and lunch sandwiches. It's not too crowded yet, so a good place to read while sipping coffee with a pastry or breakfast sandwich. The marble-topped tables are pretty.

I was recently contacted privately by the business owner, who was dissatisfied with my prior review and asked me to delete it. While his choice of words in asking me to do so is questionable (which might explain why he did not post it publicly), he did productively clarify that the name of the bakery was not entirely up to him, and that the name was registered by the original owners of the bakery, who were actually from Switzerland. 

It then follows, from my own reasoning, that perhaps the preservation of this name acts more as a preservation of a local brand, rather than a description of the products sold at this bakery. For this reason, I will add a star and I will give them the benefit of the doubt: that perhaps they are not using this name to advertise a level of quality that is actually greater than the quality of the products they sell.  

However, I think it's important for Yelp reviews to provide users with a window into an experience to help them make informed purchasing decisions. Even business owners are consumers, at times, whether outside or within the scope of their business operations. And I am sure they would also prefer to see a useful collection of feedback about a business before making transactions, rather than spend their money blindly. In my case, I made fair payments for products that were not worth the price I paid. The service was terrible, but there is a way to address that, if they are interested in progress.

The owner wondered why I returned to his store if I initially had a bad experience. It did not occur to him that perhaps I wanted to find out whether that was an isolated incident or a pattern, and that if it was an isolated incident, then I would gladly return to show my support for a small business. This is not hard for me to clarify: 

I initially tasted a very dry custom-made layered cake from here at a birthday party. Instead of completely dismissing this bakery after the first bite, I just made a note of this in my mind. At some later point, I came in to try a cro-creme out of curiosity and convenience, as this bakery is conveniently located on the block across the street from my office building. I cannot lie about the fact that I regretted spending $5 on a pastry that was very dry and greasy. Again, I gave them the benefit of the doubt and came back for a croissant, which again, was the driest croissant I've ever tasted in Philly. (There was another time I came in because I was hungry and this was one of the closest places for food, and I was also given a very dry almond croissant.) Given that dryness is a consistent quality of these baked products in my experiences as well as that of other reviewers, I really don't see how unfair it is to say so. 

The owner also wondered why I mentioned the Restaurant school and speculated that I might be affiliated with them or that might have written a "petty and misplaced attempt at revenge." I am not sure how he came to this accusation, or why he thought that addressing a customer in this manner would be better than owning up to and addressing certain areas of improvement in the quality of his establishment. 

However, to clarify the above reference, my only "affiliation" with the Restaurant School is that I stop by their bakery sometimes to purchase pastries and coffee, and their pastries (made by students, to my surprise) are always delicious. In my prior review, I was simply expressing my surprise at how pastries made by beginner-level pastry students have been consistently tastier than ones made by a long-established bakery. There is no conspiracy going on here. I think this establishment has all the tools it needs to improve its weaker areas, if it wants to do so.

One thing I love about Philly is that you don't have to spend a fortune to have an incredible meal, and I'm happy this place can be added to my list of restaurants to visit regularly. Many entrees are ~$10-15, while fancier entrees are in the $20's. However, note that the fancier entrees are well-executed and on par with $30 entrees at typical "fancy" restaurants. 

The highlight of my meal was the grilled salmon, which came fresh off the grill with sauteed spinach, chopped scallop, shallot marsala cooking wine and garlic sauce. The portioning was perfect. It was a pinch saltier than I'd prefer, but I hadn't had such beautifully grilled salmon in a while (nice and flaky, with a crispy skin). The flavors and textures were unique, well-balanced, and delicious. I also enjoyed the "money pouch" appetizer - a bit steep at $10 for 3 pieces, but these are the best version of fried dumplings I've had in Philly. 

Dessert-wise, I really enjoyed the warm glutinous rice with slices of mango. Everything was freshly made. I believe it's BYOB, and the decor is great for a low-key dinner that can impress your date, but that doesn't seem like you're trying too hard. Unlike a lot of other Asian restaurants out there, the service here was friendly and attentive. Definitely coming back next-time I crave some really good Thai food!

Ordered online and picked up curbside.  Delicious as usual, hot and fresh, same great quality as when we dined in preCOVID. Get the family size and enjoy the leftovers!

Pancakes are spongy and didn't even need syrup- they put the cake in pancake. 

Crispy seasoned potatoes and stew-y spiced shatshouka.

I planned a surprise bday brunch for my dad, and they made it great. Alice was a great waitress, and took care of everyone.  Free validation for the garage. The bread pudding was amazing, and the glaze was just as good. There is also a great selection of healthy options: yogurt, a variety of fruit and berries. There were also eggs, biscuits, an a la carte menu ( we got the buffet). They even stayed after for us, since they were slated to close at 1.

The best international market (that i know of) in Saint Louis. Better than Jay's because they have meat, eggs and milk.  They have lamb, for around $5/lb, which puts Straub's price on lamb to shame. They have all the spices (including Kaffir Lime Leaves!) you could possibly need. Instead of that overpriced gourmet Greek yogurt, you can get the real thing for $3. They have plantains, and not the crappy ones from Schnucks that never ripen right. Every Asian leaf, spice and mushroom you could need. I've also noticed the last aisle has an impressive stock on Asian candies. I'm also a tea addict, so loose leaf, international mixes and fruit blend, and at a great price- cheaper than Teavana, that's for sure. And they have phone cards too, if that's something you need. 

I almost forgot the sweets section: chocolates, baked goods, intl candy, some cheaper, some more expensive. 

So, discovering new fruits and veggies and spices, awesomely cheap lamb, exotic bread, and dessert too=everything I could need to make a meal.
We walk in little after 10pm they said the kitchen is closed so then have the hours closing at 10pm not 11 pm however they let us use their bathrooms.

Any new restaurant has growing pains, but Lark is clearly having lots of pains. 

Four of us on a Friday night and practically every phase had problems, from the hostess who messed up big time by seating half the party and telling the other have that had no reservation not 5 minutes later, to crazy slow bar service, and two dishes never showing up from the kitchen. If you're gonna ask us to order 3-4 plates per person, you should at least deliver it when we do. 
 
 On the plus side, what we did try was pretty good. But popcorn and deviled eggs seem kind of lame on a menu for a place that is trying so hard to be cool. Same with the bar, just make good stuff and stop trying so hard to be cute with only boutique brands and serving in mason jars. Prices were okay and the waitress was trying hard and nice as could be.

In a nutshell, give a try if you want, just lower your expectation bar. On a more cynical note as a marketing person. Take note that all of the 5 star ratings on this place came from Yelpers with no photo, no friends and no criticism. I don't think so. Not cool Lark to write your own reviews.

Wow. Just wow. We waited 2 hours for a seat. Then when we got a seat we waited a another two hours for our order. The kicker, it was a PARTIAL order! Finally once we called for a manager he told us "yeah? We have problems. I'll comp your meal" his name was Sam. This was hands down the worst experience I have ever had in my life. So once we left we got flagged down by ANOTHER manager who was yelling she was calling the police. When we asked what the problem was about she accused us of walking out on our beer tab. I will never come back here. The novelty wore off after five minuets and honestly the beer and food (of what we tasted) was mediocre at best. The lack of apology and downright rudeness of the wait staff was the worst. STAY AWAY!

Train station cafes don't have to be good, they just have to be open and they'll probably fair alright with the commuter traffic. That's why every time I encounter a restaurant or bar at a station that happens to be good as well as convenient, I'm pretty amazed. 

In the Philadelphia suburb of Croydon, we found such a place in the form of the Dog & Bull Brew and Music House. Amazing menu featuring some awesome food, craft beers, and unique drinks including this awesome Bloody Mary recipe that first caught our eye because, to quote a line from one of our favorite movies ever (Better Off Dead) "it has raisins in it."

That's right, in addition to the usual tomatoes, horseradish, and spices the Dog & Bull also adds ANCHOVIES and RAISINS to it's bloody mary mix, making it not only strangely unique, but hella delicious!

But wait, it gets better. SO freaking better. 

On weekends, they serve a larger version of the drink and cap it off with their half pound Cheddar Ale Bacon Burger wearing a crown made from their signature fried pickles, olives and an onion ring. This masterpiece is appropriately named the "King of Croydon"

Check it out if you find yourself in North Philly. Hell, its at the Croydon SEPTA station, so even if you take the train just for this experience it's well worth the round trip.

Seeing this place across the street was the deciding factor in booking a room at the Iris Motel on a recent visit. We were in town visiting family for a few days, the motel looked decent enough for the price but as soon as I saw Puerto Rican/Dominican food nearby I was sold. Seriously, the Iris Motel owes this place a cut.

This place is great, so great we ate there twice in our three day stay. We took our whole family, twice. Everyone ordered something different each time and everyone was happy.

If you want great croissants with a lot of fillings, you have to go here. Pistachio is my favorite. Peaches and cream has big slices of peach with creamy custard. 

Baguette doesn't have hard crunchy crust but moist and perfect chewiness, great for sandwich like banh mi. If you don't see the baguette you can ask the owner. He will get it for you. 

The brioche toast is delicious. I had apple kind with thick slices of apples. The bread is thick and not soggy.

Super friendly owner too.

In a former Carrow's restaurant on the corner of 6th and Wells now sits Jack's Cafe #2. Jack's is a beloved breakfast spot in Sparks, which has now made its Reno debut, and they're doing a fantastic job. While I never thought of visiting this place when it was the former restaurant, as Jack's it now has instant appeal, and I'm so glad I made the decision to pop in. 

I scoped out Yelp to see what to order, and immediately I discovered their "scones". As it turns out, they're not scones at all, and I am not complaining about that. Scones are supposed to be like sweet biscuits with a flaky dough. These are fried pieces of dough that slightly puff in the fryer and are then served with butter and honey for you to top how you like them. If I were naming them, I'd call em sopapillas, but I guess "scone" is a word more Americans understand. 

For breakfast I order up the country bacon and eggs, which came with delicious and crispy home fries. The country bacon is something I've ordered at Sparks Coffee Shop, and it's a bit saltier and meatier than regular bacon. I throw a lil syrup on top for good measure, and it's a great breakfast.

Service was signature diner perfection. Coffee, water, and juices never went empty. Servers were constantly circling to make sure we had everything, and they were incredibly friendly. 

Jack's is a great example of a breakfast join done right. The lunch menu looked large and in charge, and I imagine it's just as great as the rest! 

Check em out!

If you've lived in Reno for a few years, can you say you HAVEN'T been to Palais De Jade? 

They're a legendary local favorite, and just about everyone in the city has eaten here. After numerous personal visits, I frankly can't believe I haven't written a review yet! 

Palais De Jade serves up high-quality Chinese American cuisine. They have every dish you expect to find at a Chinese restaurant, but they do them superbly. 

My first experience was 5+ years ago, and I came with a friend who's not much of an adventurous eater. We ordered lo mein as part of our meal, a dish I'd normally skip entirely. To me, it's basic, and I find it generally boring. Well, Palais took me totally by surprise because here you can taste the flavor of the wok, also known as "wok-hei", and all the years it has had serving food in our community.  Fear not. Their lo mein is still a basic tangle of spaghetti type noodles with mixed with veggies and meat, topped with a light brown sauce. 

That "wok-hei" is really what makes all their food special. 

Most recently I discovered their lunch specials. The menu spans $9, $10, and $12 bucks, and each meal includes an entree, soup or salad, choice of rice and two appetizers. Their Mongolian Beef is really freaking delicious! 

Best of all, the owner is sitting at the front making sure everyone is happy, and his staff seems so genuinely proud to be there serving the guests. 

This is a fantastic spot for lunch or dinner take-out. If you haven't been in a while, it's time to revist!

After a long day of scouting for the upcoming season, my buddy and I were starving and exhausted when we pulled up the driveway. Luckily the GF was also the same state of famished, and so the "Where should we go" discussion began. I suggested we try the new BBQ place, she wanted Gluten Free and suggested BRP, and my friend didn't give a f*#k as long as he had food in his stomach ASAP! So, off we went to BRP, a decision I'm so glad I was forced to accept! 

From Smoke Creek to Chukar Canyon, the menu items have names reminiscent of some of my favorite places and cultural aspects of living in Northern Nevada, and it's full of house made specialities including their doughs, sauces, and even their smoked pulled pork! Jason, our server, was super cool and steered us toward all the right items. Aside from pizzas, they have a great selection of sandwiches and salads, so we ordered 2 pizzas (one gluten free) and, to satisfy my craving for BBQ, the pulled pork sandwich. Everything was delicious. 

For the record, "pulled pork sandwiches" from non-BBQ restaurants  and I have a bad track record. They're usually made from packaged products with a nauseatingly sweet sauce, so I usually steer clear. At BRP, they do their pork right! 20 hours in the smoker, then lightly seasoned with their house made BBQ sauce, which was deliciously tangy and sweet! This sandwich is delicious, and one that I'd gladly travel well out of my way for. 

In Reno, we are lucky to have more and more restaurants who are interested in making food by hand to deliver a superior product. BRP is one thats been doing it for a long time, and I hope they continue for many more years in the future. 

I'm definitely a fan.

Oceano is well known for sushi, but it's actually a fantastic all around seafood restaurant. On a recent visit I hit the jackpot exploring the seafood when I stumbled upon the seafood lunch specials that are absolutely incredible values! 

This time through I couldn't resist the sushi. Best of all, 20% off for locals with players card! The menu is really unique and the fish always seems to taste fresher here. The baked mussels are fantastic. The long rolls are packed with seafood and the handrolls are unmatched! 

Oceano keeps giving me reasons to love it. Now I just need to give it the amount of attention it deserves

This meal at Miguel's was my first adventure out of the house after my kiddo was born and it was great. 3.5 stars.

Server super attentive. Endless baskets of chips and decent salsa. Cheesy and saucy Mexican goodness with a few nice surprises thrown into the menu. 

I went with the chicken mole. For me it was a bit sweeter than I prefer, but good. The chicken was a little bit dry and I felt the portion was on the smaller size. All in all good, but not the best chicken mole I've had in town.

Odd thing is I loved the mole at the midtown location, and I raved about it to my visiting family, and sadly I was a little let down. 

I'm overdue to give them another try, and I'm looking forward to it.

Me? A wino? Nope. Even though I don't know much about it, I do enjoy wine and find exploring them through tastings quite enjoyable. I've learned (through trial and error) I'm especially fond of bottles with great stories and those that pair exceptionally well with delicious food. 

Fortunately, those are exactly the types of wines you'll find at We Olive, alongside a menu that pairs extremely well with them! In addition, there's an incredibly knowledgeable and friendly staff who are willing to take the time to explain them all to you. 

We Olive prides themselves on a wine list made up of bottles sourced from "boutique" wineries in our immediate area, meaning they produce less than 5,000 cases a year. The wines are each unique, and the menu filled with descriptive tasting notes that I found to be quite accurate. It's fun to close your eyes and taste, trying to identify each note! Best of all, it's reasonably priced, and the menu allows you to enjoy tasters! 

Easily the coolest pour on the menu is the Black Bubbles, a sparkling syrah! Add in a touch of their peach white balsamic vinegar, and you've got a really great little afternoon delight! That evening we also enjoyed a cab called Plungerhead. Don't let the silly name fool you, this is a complex wine and really good value for $28/bottle. 

We Olive has an ever rotating charcuterie and cheese selection which never disappoints. They make the same effort to source meats and cheeses that have the same interesting stories and flavor nuances as the wines. On this visit we tried their hummus and albacore dip. The albacore was really delicious, with a citrus hint and a wonderful texture. The hummus includes Egyptian Dukkah, which is a taste sensation all its own. 

All in all, this was the perfect way to spend a dreary, cold afternoon. Best part was that the whole experience was 20% off with check-in on Yelp!

Happy Hour! All starters half off! (Most) craft cocktails $10!

Some of my favorite items on the Brasserie menu are starters, and when ordered together, make a great meal! In particular, I've long been a fan of all charcuterie and preserved preservations, so finding the Salmon rillette and smoked salmon plate was a huge win at $10, normally $20. 

It's a dish I've had here before, yet this version of rillette was a very different preparation. This was delicious, yet reminded me more of a tartare, with lightly cured salmon dressed in a mayo based sauce. The flavor and texture was great, and I enjoyed every bite on the perfect toast with a light Schmear of the cheese and some pickles. The smoked salmon was a tasty addition to the plate and I combined it with the riellette a few times too. 

Portobello fries, crab dip and many other tasty options are on the happy hour, and def worth heading in to try. 

I had the Ava Gardner, a delicious riff on a Manhattan, a perfect sipper between bites, and a sweet way to finish the meal. 

Loved finding this happy hour!

Meat sweats... If you have em when you leave, you've done this experience right!  - Yelp Elite Kathe B

If you're wondering, I completely agree with her. To me, this is a fantastic example of a KBBQ experience. The marinades are strong, aromatic and flavorful. The meat is very high quality, with well-marbled beef, succulent pork and chicken, and a wide array of seafood options too. The cuts are all perfect too, which allows you to maximize your time and use of the grillestate (grill real estate) during your visit. 

Greatest Hits (IMHO):
- Galbi (Bone-In Short Ribs) - Nicely marbled and very rich.
Tip: Let the marinade crisp and char a bit for added flavor and texture.
- Pork Belly (miso/spicy/lemongrass/unseasoned) - Gotta eat em all!
- BRISKET Bulgogi - Don't confuse it with the tri-tip, but definitely eat it!

Tips:
- Banchan, banchan, and more banchan - FREE REFILLS
- Start with thinly sliced meats. They cook quicker and stave off starvation.  
- It's advised you start with unseasoned cuts too, so you can enjoy the meat.
- Don't be upset that you smell like grilled meat at the end! It's part of the fun! 
- Wear more comfortable clothes than you think you should. You'll be very full, you may get some backsplash from the grill, and you just might get a bit warm when that grill gets going! 

Having a few options for this cuisine in town is wonderful, but for me, leaving smelling like a grill is what makes it so similar to some other great KBBQ I've had in other cities. Siu does a fantastic job of providing a wonderful KBBQ experience for beginners and novices. You won't be disappointed.

Who says you can't start with dessert? 
PRO TIP: Check in on Yelp when you arrive so you get yourself a FREE Awesome Dude for dessert. 

Trust me, if it sounds weird, it isn't and you want this! Saffron Vanilla Ice Cream topped with beautifully honey coated and crispy baklava crumbles! OMG! THIS IS THE STUFF DREAMS ARE MADE OF! 

4.5 stars across most online review sites say that Naan & Kabab is a good call for lunch or dinner. As a local, I'll tell you that no one is lying about this place. Chef Maurice is in the dining room daily monitoring the happiness of all of his guests and insuring they have a wonderful experience each time they visit. 

This last visit was no different than any others in the past. Chef greeted us at the door, seated us, and told us all about the new additions to the beverage menu and the nightly specials. The specials here are always, well, special, and because of that, they tend to carry a pretty price tag. Tonight was no different. Chef had a wild Alaskan Halibut and a beautiful rack of lamb available, both of which sounded divine.

We placed a drink order and asked for the vegetarian combo appetizer, which is hummus, baba ganoush, dolmades, falafel, and what I call Israeli salad. All of these items are delicious but the standouts have to be the falafel and the baba ganoush. Chef explained that his mother taught him that the secret to the smokey flavor is taking the time to slowly char and roast the eggplants before pureeing them. Mmmmmm. 

For dinner, the three of us ordered Istanbuli Polo, a Turkish comfort dish made of sautéed vegetables and chunks of tender beef in a tomato sauce served with basmati rice and grilled veggies, and we also ordered the lamb chop special. Both were delicious, and I'd happily eat them again, but I felt that the lamb was slightly overcooked and that $32 for 4 chops was kind of pricey. 

In the past we've loved the Mediterranean Steak and Prawns, the koobedeh kababs, and quite a few other dishes on the menu. All in all, the food and experience are wonderful and I recommend this place to everyone. I often forget they're open for lunch, and I'm looking forward to checking it out sometime soon. 

Oh yeah... don't forget about the Awesome Dude or the special tea. Those are both beautiful ways to finish a meal at Naan and Kabab!

A few months back I discovered the happy hour program here, and if you're able to snag a seat in the bar area (high tops and booths mostly), you can really enjoy yourself pretty reasonably. There's a range of food options around the $5-$6 mark, a decent selection of call brand booze and wine, and of course discounts on their beers too. Happy hour isn't available in the main restaurant.

The next visit I discovered their small plates section of the menu. Reasonably priced interesting dishes just large enough to share with one or two people. I made a meal of their meatballs and fried onion strings. Definitely a carb heavy evening, but both had great flavor. I wish I had shared though! 

On this most recent visit I got to try one of their daily deals. Every day they offer something else at a discount. I've enjoyed their burger deal before, and on this visit it was half off large pizza on Monday. This makes their large deep dish pies about $15, and they can serve an army, so it's a pretty good deal. We got a large works deep dish and a chicken pesto tavern style (aka flat bread). They both came out warm, the deep dish was a little undercooked for my taste, and the topping quality was just a ok. I was honestly disappointed. We did let them know about the temp and they were happy to remove one from our check, and that was a great way to handle the situation.

I'm giving the restaurant four stars because of the stellar customer service. I've NEVER had an experience go unvalidated or undiscussed at BJ's and I appreciate their desire to see every guest leave happy.

Boba is boba.

In my opinion, that statement is pretty accurate. When I visit a boba spot I typically see the same array of colorful powders, pitchers of tea, and crazy combination of add-ins. All assembled the finished product is just about the same everywhere. 

That said, I do tend to enjoy this beverage as a special treat. The fun flavors you can pick and the snack-like boba you get to munch on while drinking your tea make it an overall fun experience! 

Reno seems to be bursting with boba shops these days and I've been sampling quite a few. Atmosphere is light, airy, bubbly, and so perfect for taking pics! 

For me, this treat tends to be a lot sweeter than I can stand, so I loved the fact you can pick your sweetness level at Tealeaf. Their toppings list is a mile long too, so you'll never be bored. 

I'm a purist so I stick to a flavored milk tea with large boba. The time we stopped in they'd actually run out of large boba so we tried the minis. While I wouldn't do it every time, the minis were really fun and would be cool mixed with the large ones! 

So why four stars? The biggest reason is the .50 charge for using a credit card. We live in a primarily cashless society, and it's unfair to penalize your customers for using a valid form of payment. Beyond that, most credit card processors charge 3% or less, meaning .15 on a $5 drink. At .50 you're making .35 margin on each transaction. If it were 5% it would still only be .25. 

In addition, the flavoring in the tea we ordered hadn't quite dissolved, so it was a little chalky/gritty. 

I'm excited to return and try some of the food they serve. I'm a sucker for Asian snacks!

Back east there's a deli on every corner, but here we live in a deli desert! 

The lone oasis is the Manhattan Deli, which delivers a true, East Coast deli experience on every level, starting with the pickles. 

Yep. Pickles are important (try saying that 10x fast) and Manhattan Deli has em in spades. Half sours are deli staples, and are the best way to prepare your palette for the piles of pastrami, crave worthy corned beef and pillowy rye bread you're gearing up to enjoy. 

Before visiting the Manhattan Deli it's advised that you do your jaw exercises, especially if you plan to eat a sandwich. These suckers are stacked, and getting your mouth around them is a feat in and of itself. Don't worry if something hits the plate. It's a blessing in disguise because just as you think you're done, you'll look down to see almost another sandwich waiting for you to scoop up and enjoy.

Here's what you shouldn't miss:
- Mustard Potato Salad
- Health Salad (Think coleslaw, add fresh bell pepper, and pickle it all in vinegar and sugar- Oh yea... no mayo here, and that's a good thing)
- Pastrami on Rye (Need I say more? Ok I will. Ask for your faves - Lean or fatty!)
- Corned Beef (The real deal)
- Matzoh Ball Soup (I dare you to find it better anywhere else)

Oh yea. Since it's the Atlantis you can count on world class service. I've been more than handful of times and it is always spot on from start to finish.

Speaking of the finish, make sure to give yourself a happy ending and enjoy a black and white cookie on your way out! 

You can thank me later!

I finally set food in a grocery store after several months! Ok. It wasn't the first time, but it was one of only a few times. 

Going to store is still a little unnerving for me, but I like it because I'm able to see the COVID precautions in place and practice. Whole Foods seems to be doing it right. 

Sadly the taproom is closed down right now and has become an Amazon Prime shipping room. The coffee counter and gelato are still open for service, and they've installed some dividers between the customers and the staff and service area. That said, I'm taking one star because the staff wasn't wearing gloves when handling coffee cups. I know gloves aren't a magical barrier and that they can be misused, but if I'm to assume they're washing their hands, I should assume gloves make it safer as a customer. In this case, the staff was fitting the lid onto my cup once filled, and I watched them touch the part of the lid I would be drinking from, so I had to wipe it off with a purell wipe.

The hot bar is no longer self-serve, but they do have an attendant there and a menu up so you know what's available! 

Social distancing markers at the register too! 

All in all, a pretty good job Whole Foods!

You know those places everyone talks about that somehow slip your mind every time you're looking for it? 

For me, that's M3.  

I'd heard and read all the great things people had said, and yet M3 never hit the consideration set. Truth be told, now having been there I see it would've fit the bill to a T on SO MANY occasions, and now I feel bad for missing out for so long. So I remedied that situation this past week! 

Let's start with the atmosphere. It's low key and warm. Good house music, comfortable booths and tables with several high tops perfect for groups looking to grab drinks and apps! 

Service was on point. Friendly. Great menu knowledge and quick with recommendations too. Solid upseller too, even if we didn't take that advice ;) 

Now on to the menu. It's big, but not so big it's unwieldy. There's a large section of starters that I honed in on right away. We started with a grilled artichoke, which came out perfectly tender and nicely charred. The aioli was a great compliment. I wasn't too hungry after that, so I ordered the steamed mussels. For $14 it was a generous portion served with some decent garlic bread. The sauce was a little salty from the chorizo, but I balanced it out with a touch of the aioli from the artichoke and it was a home run. 

All in all, M3 is gonna hold a spot in my rotation. Prices were beyond reasonable and there were a lot of entrees that caught my eye. 

Now I've gotta try the sister spot, Moxie's!

Chicken Chettniad! Medhu Vada! Tomato Eggplant curry! 

Eat these and you will be very happy. I promise!

This is the kind of food that gives you a big warm hug. It's incredibly comforting and you can appreciate and taste the family history behind each of the recipes. 

The Indian spices used in these dishes will be different but familiar, but the way these flavors are presented will be a unique experience. 

Eating with your hands is very fun, and the food here is very interactive. No bite has to be the same because you can mix and match the sauces and dishes to create something different each time. 

I can't suggest you try this out enough. You will find something unique that will bring you back again and again.

If you think Italian food is all spaghetti and meatballs or chicken parmigana, think again, or just come to La Vecchia! The menu at this restaurant is a modern take on the comfort food Chef/Owner Alberto Gazzola enjoyed while growing up in La Vecchia Varese, the Northern Italian town which gives the restaurant its name. You can find everything here, from wood fired pizzas, beautiful fish preparations with fresh, seasonal vegetables, and fantastic antipasti options like their Salsiccia, or sausage plate. The highlight here has to be the handmade pastas and ravioli though. Chef Alberto and his team make these daily, and the texture and flavor cannot be compared to anything else. It's almost impossible to visit La Vecchia without enjoying one of the many exciting pasta dishes! 

Asking me to choose a favorite would be like asking me to decide which of my fingers I'd like to keep more than the others. They're all incredible. But if I'm choosing, I'd have to say anything with their wider noodles, like papardelle. I've enjoyed it as carbonara, with Italian sausage, and tonight with their house made duck confit, each just as good as the next. The papardelle is cooked to a perfect al dente, leaving the right amount of chew to the pasta itself that works so nicely with the rich additions to it. I could probably eat it everyday and not complain. 

But the wood fired pizzas are also a thing of beauty. First they're oval in shape, perhaps to fit on the plate, but perhaps just because that's the shape Chef likes to make! Either way the dough is delicious. It's a bit thicker on the edges than some of the Neapolitan style pizzas in town, and picks up a bit more of the charred flavor that makes wood fired pizzas so darn tasty! You really can't go wrong with any of the combinations offered. 

Good food alone, does not make a great restaurant though. The service team here, lead by Larren, is incredible. Many of the servers have been working at La Vecchia for quite a while, and that consistency and understanding of service standards shines through in everything they do. Water glasses are not left empty. Food arrives timed precisely, prepared and plated properly to maximize enjoyment. It's clear the service team is dedicated to making sure every moment of your visit is enjoyable. Service can sometimes be lost as restaurants age, but just like fine wine, La Vecchia seems to only get better as the years go by.

La Vecchia is the kind of place that you can come for any occasion. Whether you want to sit at the bar and enjoy a drink while nibbling on some appetizers, dine al fresco on their beautiful patio that overlooks the valley, or celebrate a special occasion with delicious food and great wine, the menu allows for all of it. 

La Vecchia rides high on my list of Greatest Hits of Reno, and is a place I'll keep bringing new faces and coming back to over the years to come.

I'm a lucky dude.

My wife loves me. She loves me so much she shows me with bags full of piping hot pupusas and pickled curtido! Pupusas revueltas. Pupusas de Calabaza. Pupusa habanero. They're all delicious!

I normally eat very little during the day, but when she came home the other day with takeout, I couldn't resist. The delicate masa, slightly crisped on the griddle, and the ooey gooey delicious fillings are just perfect, and the curtido is a beautiful contrast to it all.

Can't wait for some more!

NO SOUP FOR YOU! Nah... wrong soup shop. That would never happen here. Kasey and Christian, the amazing owner/operators of this fine establishment, and their staff are so friendly and genuinely interested in pleasing their guests, that there is no way you could leave having anything less than a stellar experience. 

With the weather rapidly cooling off, Sup has become one of my go-tos for a quick bite. Situated in a cozy house at the beginning of the Midtown district, the restaurant has a cool, hip, homey vibe. Combine that with made in house soups that rotate daily, a number of locally sourced seasonal ingredients, and you've got a recipe for success. 

I usually go for a half sandwich and soup. If you think half a sandwich and a cup of soup might not be enough to hold you over to dinner, think again! These half sandwiches are more wholes anywhere else, and many of their soups eat like a meal! Not to mention, they come with a small side salad and a perfectly sized cookie for a sweet finish!

Last time I was there I had the pork enchilada soup, which came topped with chips, cheese, and sour cream, and a "half" of the chicken club. I think I had one bite of the sandwich because the soup, rich, savory, and full of pork, was like eating an entire enchilada! 

Whatever you get, you won't go wrong. So the next time you need something hearty and heartwarming or just downright delicious, head to Sup, introduce yourself to the team, and add another place to your list of favorite lunches in Reno. OH YA, THEY NOW SERVE DINNER TOO!

On a strangely warm day in the middle of winter shortly after my second son was born, the family decided a Midtown stroll was the perfect way to test out the new double stroller and life with a baby again! 

We parked on the south end of the neighborhood and worked our way toward St. Lawrence St. stopping here and there to enjoy the weather. Martin St. was particularly hopping with outdoor seating at Pangolin and Craft, Emmy's Flower Truck, and a great vibe all around. 

Toddler in tow, a sweet treat always soothes the savage beast, and Pangolin was advertising $3 drip coffees! How could I resist? I mean, it comes with a piece of Turkish Delight after all. Wifey got an oat milk decaf latte, I got my coffee and I bought a half pound of Turkish Delight to share. Well, I thought share. 

My son made sure none of it was left, and he did so as fast as possible so we only got to enjoy one bite. It was a delicious bite though.

The owners here are incredibly friendly and the whole vibe is just pleasant. As I write this and look ahead to the weekend, I'm pretty sure this is somewhere that needs to be factored in. What a fab addition to Midtown and our community on the whole!

Hard to be hard on a place trying to do so many amazing things, and succeeding on many fronts! But when there's another place in town doing some really similar stuff, offering me a firm basis to compare, I can't help but do just that.

Suri's and Wrap It Up, by Total Wine, are siblings of sorts, owned by brothers, with similar menus, branding, and flavors. As a raving fan of Wrap It Up, I had to give this place a shot. See I often find myself in and around downtown, and this place would be pretty convenient if I had a craving for shawarma. 

Well, that shawarma was pretty darn good, and dare I say the beef shawarma at Suri's is better than at Wrap! Both the beef and the chicken were tender, flavorful, well seasoned, and with that signature crunch you want from slow spit roasted meat. Both places offer wraps and platters, so I went with the mixed platter, which includes rice, potatoes, beef and chicken shawarma, shirazi - Mediterranean salad made from marinated tomato, cucumber and onion, hummus and their signature garlic sauce. 

While that sounds identical to Wrap It Up, the big difference here was the lack of little touches. Wrap It Up serves seasoned rice, while Suri's only uses white basmati, and my beloved pickled turnips, the purple sticks at Wrap It Up that let me know this was the real deal, are not available here. 

But Suri's has a few signature delicious and authentic additions that are unique to their menu too! Persian Tea, similar to the one I love so much at Naan and Kabab, and Persian Ice Cream with rosewater, saffron, and pistachios. They also have FRESH CUT FRIES, available as a side OR as loaded fries topped with shawarma. 

Suri's also offers a bit more service than Wrap It Up, and it feels more like a fast casual restaurant than a quick service spot. It was nice today as they sampled both the tea and the ice cream knowing I was a new customer. That said, I'm still undecided on this because I love watching my food be prepared at Wrap It Up and seeing all the great additions I can make to a salad or platter. 

Overall, this is 4.5 Stars for sure. For me it's the little things I missed knowing these two restaurants are so closely related. I would definitely return if in the area, and I'd happily bring friends here for lunch.

Consistently quality.

I have had the same experience at Coffeebar for years, and it keeps me coming back. That and the fact they've evolved so well over that time, keeping it intriguing and interesting!

Lately I'm crushing on the Masha from Burundi. I've never had a coffee from this region but it hits all my high notes. Deep and rich flavor, with the complexities that make me think first thing in the morning. I've been rationing it out since I bought it a few weeks ago, thinking it might not be there the next time I go get coffee. I even swung into the shop for a cup to avoid making all I had at home! 

Service is always friendly. Baked goods top notch. And the atmosphere super inviting. I only wish it was less popular so I could find a seat! 

Ah well. My love affair with Coffeebar continues.

Takeout available!

Craving carnitas? We can argue, but these are amongst the best in the city. There's something about the marinade. It's sweet, sour, and salty in all the right ways, accenting the rich pork. Then they crisp em up, so you get some soft and tender mixed with the crispy exterior.

Slap these on a tortilla and you've got a taco. Roll em up in a tortilla and you've got a damn good burrito! Sandwich them between two tortillas and slap em back on the flat top and you've got their signature stacked quesadillas! 

How do I enjoy them? Over rice in their Habanero Bowl! 

Supporting local business is more important than ever. Bistro Habanero is always a great option!

National brands aren't popular and successful by accident! They deliver the right mix of food, service and atmosphere on a consistent basis. For a lot of people, that's what's important when deciding where to spend your dollars. Consistent experiences rule!

That's exactly what my wife and I experienced last week when we finally decided to use a gift card that had been given to us. 

I didn't grow up eating at Outback, but plenty friends I know did and they'd wax poetic about the experience. Even my wife was having flashback while we dined, and at the end of the meal, I could see why so many frequent these restaurants.

I went for a ribs and chicken combo plate because I got to say chicken on the barbie! The bbq sauce was nice. More tangy that sweet and when used sparingly, delicious. Chicken was delicious and juicy and the ribs tender and tasty! All in all, solid for $15.

The service was also solid. Quick, efficient, and always there when you needed something. Bonus point for asking if we wanted more bread!

All in all, a good experience that I'd have again.

This is a ok as a ok can get, except for the service. Our guy was stellar!

Burgers are one of my absolutely favorite meals and in my opinion, they really aren't hard to get right. Good beef, cooked to order, served on a quality bun, with fresh toppings.

Red Robin gets this partially right, missing some of the easiest things and overcomplicating them as well. I'd liken this to a slightly better version of airport food. 

First, they'll only serve a burger medium and beyond. That's a testament to the quality of the beef honestly. That aside, the combos look amazing on the menu. Many are filled with gourmet flavors and some fun toppings, but it seems they fall a little short of how they look and sound on the menu.

I got the Madlove burger. The citrus marinated tomatoes looked and tasted like tomatoes sliced and left out in the fridge for a day. The lettuce was shredded and kept falling off the bun. The bun wasn't toasted, which was a total disappointment. It was also supposed to be brioche but  it wasn't like any brioche ive ever had. The bacon was candied but didn't have much smoky flavor either. 

As I said, average as average gets. The bottomless fries were fun, but if you don't specify extra crispy it's fairly obvious they are sitting in a bin and come out luke warm.

Fun for families!

First visit to the new location and I like it! 

The updated atmosphere is super inviting, with warm lighting, comfortable bar seats, tables, and booths too, and because of its location I also feel much better about going here late night. In my opinion though, I think the the bar area is the best addition to this business model. It puts the beverage sales front and center, gives you a friendly person to talk to and a great seat to watch the craft cocktails action! 

Back to late night for a second. This spot is open late late most nights, and pretty late on Sunday! Check out the hours because I bet Noble Pie comes to the rescue at some point soon! 

We ordered up some signature wings (F YEAH), frachos (french fry nachos? F YEAH again!), house made meatballs, and garlic knots!!! All of this was, IMHO, better than the downtown location, and I credit that to the nice, new kitchen! It seems bigger than the other, better organized, and more efficient. I like it. 

Oh yeah. Don't miss the cocktails or craft beer selection. I had their current riff on an old fashioned and it was delicious. I had two in fact! 

All in all, this is what Noble Pie was meant to be. Congrats guys on a super successful second location!

Five stars for Kayla or Kaylin! She was an INCREDIBLE server. This was my first time dining at a CPK in more than a decade and overall, the experience didn't disappoint. 

Rating this spot is tough for me because I place way different values on the various aspects of this meal:

Service: 5 stars all the way! Kayla or Kaylin (HELP ME - Brunette with curly hair? ) was on point. We had some questions about gluten free offerings (of which there are many in the pizza dept) and she was quick with solid answers and recommendations. With regard to drinks, she was also fast and super helpful too. 

Atmosphere: 5 Stars! This location is inside the GSR and took over the location that was once Briscola. At the back there's a large open kitchen, the focal point of which is the hearth (oven) and pizza making station. If you're lucky enough to cop a seat close by, you can watch the pizza chefs toss dough about a mile into the air as they stretch it nearly paper thin so it can bake quickly in the oven. They're fast and furious, and watching them is like a show with your dinner. The rest of the restaurant is hipster chic with reclaimed wood, what appear to be old license plates and some modern artwork hanging around. Overall, very chill.

Food: 3 Stars or A OK. The pizza was good. No complaint about the quality of ingredients there or the flavor. We had the sausage, pep, and mushroom pie on cauliflower crust. The crust is as good as my favorite gluten free pizzas and the toppings were abundant. The BBQ Chicken Salad was also a nice refreshing accompaniment to the pizza and I like that they offer full and half order sizes! The salad was pretty basic though, and really didn't offer much to impress me. 

Drinks: 3 Stars or A OK. We go the sangria sampler. On paper it sounded tasty and fun, but overall it was way too sweet for our liking. We ended up leaving much of it behind. Def not something I would choose again.

I got to attend their soft opening and saw and tasted a number of other dishes on the menu like the Power Bowl and flatbreads, and I think I'd lean more toward an entree next time. Pizza may have been their mainstay before, but I think the broader menu suits them better and I'm excited to enjoy some of those items on my next visit.

I love seafood.  I'm from South Florida where seafood is abundant. I used to enjoy fresh seafood regularly, but in Reno it has become a treat for me. So when I was asked to have lunch at Pearl, I was notably excited because, well, I love seafood! And also because I figured I'd have the chance enjoy a great piece of grilled fish that would work with this crazy diet I'm on.

Now, we all know casino's have some good eats within their walls, but there's a prevailing thought that getting to them requires a long hike from parking or a walk across the massive gaming floors, which typically are smokey. This is simply not true of most of our properties in Reno, and definitely not for the Silver Legacy. Here's how to get to Pearl...Park in the SL garage, take the elevator to the lobby, hang a left out of the elevator, and make your next right to find Pearl. Sterling's, Hussong's and other SL outlets are just as easy to access as well, and the point is, good food is easy to get to and we shouldn't let the fact it's in a casino deter us from getting to it.

So how was Pearl? On food alone a solid 3 star, A-OK spot for lunch or dinner, but not more than that because of the fact the menu seems incomplete. Case in point, I didn't find grilled seafood of any kind on the many anywhere. Talk about a whole in a seafood concept. Fried, sandwiched, over pasta and many other preparations, but not grilled, which I consider basic. 

But I'm giving them the bump to 4 stars for quality service, knowledgeable staff, and a well designed and comfortable restaurant!

Our server was a rockstar and had all the right answers. The diet I'm on prohibits a lot of things, and naturally, I had a lot of questions about preparations, ingredients, etc, which she answered perfectly. She even saved me from ordering something I couldn't eat at the last minute. She also had the perfect presence, checking in at the appropriate times to insure our meal was great, and she was supported by another service professional who refilled our waters and cleared dishes as well. 

Pearl has a great little seafood rawbar setup too, along with draft beers and cocktails, and I can totally see myself giving that try in the future for a happy hour. Oysters are said to have magical properties, so this could be an excellent spot to start a fun night out!

Across the table from me, my lunching companion looked in utter horror as she shrieked "Honey on your pizza?" 

I wanted to look back across the table and say " Where've you been living sister? This is how we roll!" But I held back, realizing that not everyone has experienced the amazingness that is mountain style pizza. Turns out this friend is a gluten free diner, so I guess I have to let her slide. I mean, what would she know about the deliciousness that is the magically magnificent mountainous crust that surrounds a thinner, inner bottom crust topped with a light layer of sauce, cheese, and tantalizing toppings?

So what's the best way to get your fix at WG? Easy... SUPER SLICE! This thing is massive, and eats more like 2 slices, and with that crust, I feel like I get dessert with my meal too! I usually get mine with sausage, red onion and a soda! The standard deal is $6 with one topping, and additionals are .50, so I think it works out to around $7, and leaves me stuffed all afternoon!  

Now here's my weird secret, I don't actually leave the honey just for the crust! I did this day for fear of the death stares, but my PRO-TIP would have to be to mix some chili flakes and parmesean into the honey, and dip the pizza in it too! With my combo there's something about the spicy sausage and honey that go so perfectly.  

Honey or not though, you simply can't go wrong with a Super Slice from Wild Garlic.

Sushi spots are a dime a dozen in Reno, but few have the view and atmosphere of the Sky Terrace! With big, open windows on both sides of this structure, you can see clear down to South Reno and all the way up to Downtown! The blue carpet, tinted glass, and plants in the space bring the outside in, and on a sunny day, you could swear you were seated on a nice, covered patio. 

I've never been here for an AYCE experience, nor have I ever sat at the sushi bar, but the a la carte offerings I've enjoyed, including their sashimi sampler (which includes six slices of fish beautifully presented), Jason and salmon skin hand rolls, and Sierra Roll with spicy surimi crab, tempura shrimp, salmon,
ebi, avocado, cilantro, thin lemon slices and teriyaki sauce, have all been fantastic. 

So why 3 stars? It's actually more like 3.5 in this situation, but I just can't seem to round it up because of the service. If you've read my sushi reviews, you know I ALWAYS sit a the bar, but because of larger parties I just haven't been able to do that here yet. I figured sitting at a table would be fine because the Atlantis has some pretty high standards for food and service in their dining program, but the Sky Terrace has left me wanting in the service department on more than one occasion. Empty, dirty plates left on the table, slow delivery of drinks, and awkwardly timed table visits with no attention paid to obvious service opportunities missed are among a few of the faux pas I've endured here. 

It may seem minor to some, but when you're seated at a four top table with soy sauce and keno cards taking up the center, plates left behind start to invade your personal space and leave you with a less than stellar dining experience. 

With a little more attention paid to the guest experience here, this will become a four, or even 5-Star review. They have all everything going for them, but the table service, as with most sushi spots, needs work.

Over the past few weeks I've been in and out of several sushi comas. Blissful dreams of upside down shrimp, yellowtail nigiri, and salmon skin handrolls have been a common occurrence, and for once, my sushi cravings have seemingly subsided. While I've been awake I've had the chance to check out a few new sushi spots, and while I still have my favorites, I'm realizing that there is almost no room for the line "I don't like sushi" with the range of "sushi" options available to the diner in Reno. The quotes are because the definition has gotten so broad, which I see as a positive thing for diners everywhere because it makes what might otherwise seem like a foreign concept palatable to the masses.

JJ's is the perfect place to bring Now that said, JJ's is the kind of place that can please most of the sushi diners in Reno, from the completely uninitiated to the somewhat adventurous. The first thing you'll notice is that their menu is HUGE, much like Sushi Time that used to be in the same space. If you look at the menu closely, most of the rolls are various arrangements of the same core ingredients, krab, tempura veggies, avocado and crystal shrimp. Now I'm the sushi guy that loves the raw stuff, and as many of the reviews have said, the menu definitely caters to fans of cooked sushi. That said, I was able to find a few gems in the bunch like the snow mountain and the Four Seasons, and even though it's not raw, their salmon skin handroll was a standout! Along with the regular menu they have a specials board that changes frequently. Many of those rolls have become customer favorites, and if you're in the know, are available upon request! I suggest checking out the Yelp pictures to see what I'm talking about. 

Where JJ's really excels is in service. We sat at a table, which is usually a no no in my book, and the server was incredibly prompt and efficient. Dishes were cleared (Yes, they were cleared!), orders were taken, placed, and delivered quickly and COMPLETE, along with a description of what was on the place, and drinks were refilled. Now when we first sat the place was pretty empty, but it started to fill up and I didn't see the service slack. 

The service edged them up to 4 stars, but if I'd weighed in the menu more, it would be a 3.5. I just wish there were more raw items on it. Overall, while JJ's is not the sushi place for me personally, it is for A LOT of people in Reno, and it's definitely worth a visit. If someone were to suggest coming here, I wouldn't hesitate to go with them. There's something on the menu that can please anyone in the bunch, and the service is top notch.

Hallelujah! I'm so glad the universe sent us Brent and Lindy because they are bringing us all kinds of sugar, spice, and everything nice in their little slice of spice and tea heaven on California Avenue! 

Wanna know a secret? A lot of the top restaurants shop here for their special somethin somethin! So what are you waiting for?

This store is small, but mighty, with floor to ceiling shelves lined with everything imaginable. Yes. They have salt and pepper... but you'll have to chose from the extensive selection of each offered here! Not to worry. If you don't know your fleur de sel from your Maldon or your Kosher, you will after Lindy and Brent tell you about each one, where they're from, and how to use em! 

They also stock a number of specialty spice blends too, and they're constantly expanding and changing this lineup too! I've enjoyed their NW Salmon Rub, Vindaloo Curry, and their Jamaican Jerk blends, all of which are incredibly flavorful and delicious. Best part is they even have recipe cards that give you amazing ways to use all these! 

Need something obscure? It's probably there and if not, they'll see if they can get it for you! Not sure what you need for that special dish or want to know more about the flavors of a certain cuisine, hanging out here will give you a lot of knowledge and inspire you to explore! 

Best of all, this stuff is fresh, no stabilizers or fillers, and you can buy everything by the ounce at incredible reasonable prices! No more spending $15 on a jar you'll open once at the store! 

Salty-Savory-Sweet is an incredible addition to our community, and I love visiting! I always leave a bit more knowledgeable and with some cool stuff to try in the kitchen! I can't wait to go back!

Secret menu? Why yes please! The secret menu at Eclipse not only has other delightful creations, but even ways to ask for your pizza to be cut! I'm partial to the "Anarchy", which as the name suggests, is cut randomly in all directions, or the Mahaffey, which the site describes as "First cut way off the half mark.  Cut normally after.  Awesome if you get the favorable Mahaffey side."

Continuing my trend of getting out of my neighborhood geography, Eclipse was up on the list of places to check out in NW Reno. I got there ahead of Ashley and ordered for both of us. I opted for the Luca$h Delight (Pesto sauce, light mozzarella, goat cheese, sundrieds, garlic, pinenuts, sausage, jalapeno, and fresh basil) from the secret menu, and my fiancee had The Tour (Pesto, mozzarella, goat, sundried tomato, roasted garlic and fresh basil) made on their gluten free crust). The pizza was delicious, seemingly heavy on all the toppings but balanced across the board on flavor. The crust was strong enough to hold the weight, but thin, crispy, and easy to devour. The sausage on my pie was clearly made in house, and the addition of the pinenuts made for a great textural and flavorful component. I tasted a bite of the gluten free pizza (which is only available in the small size) and really enjoyed it. Ashley and I usually order one pie to share, and get the gluten free crust, but not knowing the size of these pies we both ordered our own. At Eclipse though, a small pie with a large salad, is the perfect meal.

Downside to Eclipse has got to be the limited indoor seating, which means most of it is outside. We came on an early fall evening, and it was just starting to get chilly out. I bet they do a lot more takeout business in the winter! 

This is a great addition to Reno and a pizza I'll be back for. If you haven't checked them out, get a move on!

I freaking love taqueria food, mainly because these are the gritty, down home style Mexican food that everyone in Mexico grew up eating in their grandma's house, the kind of food steeped in tradition, and a window into another culture! 

With that said, I'm not sure why I've never been in here before! Thanks to Yelper Ernie C, I made my way in with my brother and his wife in tow! They live in China and have never been to a taqueria, so it was only fitting that I take them on a Taqueria Tour de Force! 

The menu at Los Gallos is huge, but I saw what I'd be ordering even before we walked through the door. Seeing as we had to cover all bases on this one trip, I stepped up huge and ordered lengua salsa verde which was tender as can be, tacos al pastor popping with flavor, ceviche tostadas with the fresh flavors of shrimp and fish, birria and horchata. And for the record, as a birria connoisseur, the dish at Los Gallos means roasted goat with all the delicious crunchy bits slathered in a red chile salsa, different from the braised dish and stew common at many taquerias and Mexican restaurants in town. 

All dishes comes with fresh made chips and a killer salsa bar, all of which were on the spicy side, complete with those delicious pickled veggies, which at Los Gallos include boiled potatoes! The other interesting tradition I learned here was to eat your ceviche tostadas with a ketchup! It seems to just add a little sweetness to it which balanced out the lime juice.

While I don't think I'd make that a regular habit, I would most certainly repeat this order again, and again, and again. Everything was amazing, and with a menu as big as theirs, it's a place I'd really like to check it out with other Yelpers to see what they love!

Crispy Ribs... they're a thing in Canada and they're magical and mythical like the beasts of Narnia, which is probably where they come from! These ribs, along with a wonderful server and bartender, saved the experience at Central Social Hall, lifting my overall from 3 to 3.5 rounded to 4.

I've had sticky ribs, BBQ ribs, dry rubbed ribs, braised ribs and even chopped steamed ribs, but never have I had a "Canadian Crispy Rib"!  

You're probably dying to know what these are already so I'll try and describe them. Imagine an entire rack of pork ribs (either baby back or spare) cut into small, nearly uniform chunks, bone-in. These pieces are then coated in a dusting of seasoned flour, heavy on the salt and pepper, and deep fried to golden brown perfection. The flour is so light that the meat is actually fried as well, giving it a crispy exterior. The fried meat and coating combined have a very savory, tender but toothsome quality that you can't help but want to gnaw completely off the bone. P.S. If you have leftovers like we did, they eat incredibly well RIGHT OUT OF THE FRIDGE the next day!

The original dish I ordered was the Roadhouse sandwich. I was excited because it featured Alberta Beef, and it sounded like a behemoth, topped with mushrooms, onion rings, and horseradish aioli. What arrived was far more dainty that imagined, and the beef was over cooked and a bit tough too. In its entirety, the sandwich was unimpressive and I would not recommend it. 

Cocktail wise, these guys are on it. I enjoyed a Boulevardier, served with a large cube of ice to avoid dilution, and while a bit heavy on the amaro, was quite enjoyable after the steak and alongside the ribs.

Central Social Hall is a pretty sweet spot for lunch, dinner, drinks, dates or groups. Comfy seating and plenty of natural light also make it great for taking photos too.

Open for takeout during COVID-19

Ch ch chaaanges...a new wing king rises. 

For years I've maintained the best wings in town were elsewhere. Recently I went on an impromptu wing tour of Reno Sparks. We compared wings from 5 or 6 places in rapid succession, and at the end, while all had their merit, we all agreed Shenanigan's were the best all round.

They are big, meaty, and fried crispy, for starters. While I love dry rub wings, and the ones here are great, we
all loved the sweet hot sauce option. The sauce was the perfect combo, but what won over was the fact that the wings weren't overly sauced and still crisp when they arrived and a little while after!

They come with a healthy pile of carrots and celery, AND you can decide between blue cheese or ranch. I won't get into the virtues of each, but if you're east coast it's blue cheese.

I'm happy to see some folks supporting this great local biz during this tough time. I want it to be there when this is over!

Service? It simply doesn't get much better! I felt the warmth from the minute we walked through the door. Add in the food and it's a solid 3.5 in my book.

I'd say the dish I ordered may have been the only reason I edged over to 3-3.5 vs. 4 stars in this equation. 

See I was really torn between dishes, and upon the server's strong recommendation (best dish in the house IMHO) I ordered the Rissotto Frutti Di Mare (seafood). It came with a bounty of seafood including mussels, clams, shrimp, calamari and scallops all served over a risotto. Some of the seafood was good, like the shrimp and calamari, but some of it was a little on iodine/oceany side. The risotto itself absorbed a lot of that iodine flavor too, and beyond that it was really dense and a little mushy. The best risottos I've enjoyed have been a texture where when you plate it, the rice slowly spreads out. This was not that style, and therefore not my favorite. 

I tasted the meatballs my wife ordered and the veal dish another guest had, and the Caesar Salad was also quite good, so I'm confident if I picked another dish this would be 4 stars all the way.

The free limoncello with Yelp Check In (or very nice server) is made in house and a delightful way to end the meal!

Three stars solely because of customer service. 

TLDR Up Front: If I was rating the food alone, I'd probably say 2, with the best part being the salsa and hot sauce bar because I found everything to be quite bland. Seems they try to cater toward a more American palate, and when I want Mexican, I want Mexican flavors.

We came in on a Saturday afternoon to a fairly empty restaurant that filled up during our visit. The restaurant has high ceilings and large windows all around, which give it a wonderfully open feel. They've had fun localized murals done on a lot of the walls, which gives the space a little fun vibe.

We ordered two tacos, one chicken and one shredded beef (machaca)  and a basket of chips. The tacos were good sized for the $4 price tag, served on larger corn tortillas that are steamed to order. You can top your taco with toppings including tomatoes, rice, beans, sour cream, cheese and avocado all for the same price, which is a nice approach and makes it feel like a good value. 

I went simple to taste the meat with rice, beans, tomatoes, and avocado, with the addition of the salsas and hot sauces.  The meat was nicely braised and tender, but it really didn't have a whole lot of flavor. The chicken was nicely grilled as well, but again, bland. The chips were light and the salsas were fresh, and the highlight of our meal.

It occurred to me the total of our order seemed high after I got in the car. I didn't get a receipt printed, but they use a Square POS so I automatically got an email receipt and called to inquire after looking at the items on it. They realized they charged me for quesadillas instead of tacos and promptly refunded price of those. I would have been happy to pay for the tacos, but they insisted in taking them off entirely.

So customer service gets 5 stars easy. Food I'd have to give 2 stars.

I don't often do Thai for lunch, but I do appreciate the fact most Thai restaurants offer really great lunch specials. Sawasadee is no exception.

I came here for lunch meeting with some friends, and from the moment I sat down the service was on point. Water was offered and delivered in mere moments, and though the entire party was not there yet, the server kept checking back to see if anything was needed as everyone arrived. Oncer everyone was there, she came back to see if we had any questions, and took our orders. 

The lunch special comes with an entree, soup, a curry puff, a salad, and rice. It's a lot of food, and a great value considering the price tag of about $8-$9 bucks. As with most Thai spots you get your choice of protein, so I went with the Spicy Basil with chicken. The server asked how spicy I wanted it and I said 4, but this was the wimpiest 4 I've ever encountered. When it comes to Thai food, I like it hot. At a minimum, I want to feel my brow start to sweat, and maybe even my nose begin to run. I like to taste the heat and feel it linger between bites. Thai chilis have a brightness to them that seems to wake up the palate, and this was seriously lacking here. Between one of my friends and I, I think we emptied the little condiment rack of the pepper powder during the meal. The dish had good flavor, with thai basil and veggies all stir fried together, but overall it was just kind of ordinary. 

I'm willing to chalk this 3 star rating up to ordering wrong and totally give them another chance down the road. I've never had great luck with these lunch specials, and should stick to the regular menu. Sometimes you just can't say no to the value though. For the $9 bucks, I'd say this is a pretty good meal. Not enough to take me away from my regular Thai place, but certainly not enough to keep me from coming back when in the area.

My love for Arario is not unknown, but as a creature of habit I rarely deviate from my absolute favorites at one of my absolute favorite restaurants. Fortunately I actually have a lot of dishes I consider favorites here, which allows me to have diverse experiences each time, but every now and again I branch out and try something new. Part of me hopes it won't displace a current favorite and a little part of me kinda hopes it does! 

So this time I tried the Bulgogi power bowl, with spicy pork, mixed greens, delicious veggies, rice, cheese and some special sauces. I normally stick with just the spicy pork Bulgogi, which is a more "pure" or unadulterated version of the dish I ordered. 

While I enjoyed the combination of flavors and textures on the power bowl, I really just wanted the pork and banchan. Personally, I prefer to keep my Korean flavors separate and distinct, then mix and match them as I see fit. The power bowl is for someone that wants several unique flavor and texture combinations within one dish that come together. 

This time around my current faves won out. I'm not sad. There's plenty more to explore!

In a world where we sit with our faces tucked into technology, it's nice to know there's a place you can go and find respite. Kimmies Coffee Cup is a warm space filled with Southern hospitality and charm. When you walk in, you'll be immediately greeted with a warm and friendly smile by owner Donna, one of her daughters, or any one of their incredible staff members. The white walls and cute and quaint decor will immediately have you feeling like you're at home, and that's just what Donna wants, and by the end of your visit, they'll be calling you by your first name, because you're pretty much family to them at that point! 

Donna runs a tight ship, with great food and service front and center, and my meal definitely didn't disappoint. The coffee was hot and strong, and my cup never went empty. For breakfast, I ordered the egg sandwich with housemade sausage patty! The sourdough was toasty perfection, the eggs over easy just as I'd ordered, and the sausage had the great sage flavor and spice I love. Top that with lettuce and fresh tomato, some hot sauce, and a dab of mayo, and breakfast sandwich perfection has been achieved! 

I don't know why it took me so long to visit Kimmies, but it's no surprise they've got the amazing regular clientele and success they do. I'm looking forward to my next excuse to go out to breakfast with friends, because I can't wait to bring them to this spot!

I've been on a personal mission to find the best Birria in Reno. Macho's is the third place I've tried it at, and the dish I'm talking about is the slow braised beef dish with tomato, chiles, cinnamon and other warm spices typically served with tortillas, chopped onion and cilantro, and guacamole. I've never had this dish outside of Reno, which I'm sure is just a coincidence, but I like to think it's our own little specialty. 

Macho's birria is good, a pretty large portion of tender beef in a rich red sauce, the flavors of which fell a bit flat. It was served with the usual accompaniments, but they only give you a small scoop of guac and 3 small corn tortillas with the massive portion (extra order of 3 is $1!) .  Our friends tried the fajitas, burritos, and chimichangas, and everyone said it was good. 

Macho's gets 3 stars because they were seriously understaffed. Running lean on the service end of a restaurant is never a good idea. We waited 15+ minutes to order more drinks, I downloaded their App which was supposed to get me a free appetizer that never showed up, and I appreciate frying chips fresh, but they should be ready in larger batches. 

I'm positive on my next visit that this will be updated to a 4, or even a 5 star review because the team seems dedicated to this restaurant. I want to see them succeed because I want to come back and hang out here. The place was that cool!
