When the app says it'll take 45 and the guy shows in under 30 with piping hot pizza, you know this place has their act together!

Everyone knows I'm a Pizzava fan and that's because this pizza packs in the flavor. The crust has a delicious chew with a slight crunch on the edges, and I love the cornmeal they use on the bottom too. The cheese is more than mozzarella and has a slight sharpness that adds a lot to the basic cheese pizza, and the toppings are top notch and never skimpy.

My favorite pizza is the chicken Alfredo but I add roasted red peppers and bacon to it because it's delicious. 

Ordering in the app is easy and done in a snap. Staff is also always super courteous and welcoming, and gracious too. 

Best of all they deliver and they're super fast, even during peak times. 

I hope they open in South Reno. Until then I'll keep inviting myself over friends in the delivery area so we can hang and have some great pie brought to our doorstep!

I think I can... I think I can... I think I can! That's the motto at Oxbow Cafe and Bistro, located in the emerging arts and culture district known as Dickerson Road. The owner is one of the most passionate business owners I've met to date, and she's shared that passion with her staff, who in turn share it with the guests. They are determined to succeed, and I think they'll do just that! 

The restaurant is warm and inviting, with a somewhat open kitchen and a cute patio area for outside dining. In addition to their menu, which features eggs, omelets etc. for breakfast, and  burgers, pizzas, soups and sandwiches for lunch, they offer daily specials with prices that can't be beat! The day I was there they had eggs benedict for $7.95! I stopped in for a late lunch, and went with the Monterey Turkey sandwich which has sliced turkey, fresh tomato, red leaf lettuce, avocado, bacon, provolone and pesto aioli. They'd had a busy day and ran out of turkey, but offered to make it with chicken breast, which turned out to be delicious happenstance!

The sandwich was perfect. Toasted bread with a soft center, ripe and juicy tomato, crunchy lettuce, creamy avocado and aioli, and juicy, well seasoned chicken! It was so big (see photo) I took half of it home and actually turned it into an omelet the next morning! 

While Oxbow is a bit out of the way, they are determined to succeed, and with diners in Reno constantly looking for new, fun places to grab a bite, I can see them finding their way down to Oxbow, and while they're there, they'll #DiscoverDickerson too!

Sometimes more is better. This is definitely true when that more is better quality, better flavor, better quantity and better presentation! 

Here's the general poke breakdown for those uninitiated...
Pick a base. Pick proteins. Pick your sauce. Pick your toppings. Enjoy! 

Here's how Bluefin is different...

Sizes - $11 for a small and $13 for a large, plus $2 to add a scoop! 

Bases - They've got the usual suspects, but the rice seems lighter and fluffier here. My go to is half white rice and half greens.
PRO-TIP: The rice is unseasoned, so ask them to put a little of your sauce combo and Furikake on your rice for added flavor! 

Protein - This is where bigger is better. The small bowl gets 4 scoops = half a pound of fish, and the large gets 6 scoops = 3/4 lb of fish! The proteins are also cut into larger cubes, which allows the seafood to absorb more flavor and lets you enjoy the texture too! My personal favorite combo is salmon, ahi, and double yellowtail on a small bowl, but the spicy tuna is also really good! 

Sauces - Again, the usual suspects are here like spicy aioli and unagi sauce, but they've also got house-made fried garlic soy and sesame soy that are a bomb combo! 
PRO-TIP: As long as they're not slammed, they're happy to put different sauces with different proteins. 

Toppings - Crab is a topping NOT a protein here. Edamame add a crunchy freshness. Seaweed salad because seaweed salad. Don't skip the dried nori shavings either. Oh yeah, the fried garlic chips get a hell yeah. Basically everything on the topping bar is delicious and should be in your bowl! AVOCADO IS ONLY .50 EXTRA! 
PRO-TIP: Treat sauces as a topping and finish your bowl with em! I always add spicy aioli and unagi sauce on top! 

I was worried when the poke craze started sweeping the city, but this is really a great option for lunch or dinner.  At $12 out the door, it truly can't be beat. 

P.S. TAKE A PHOTO! This food is beautiful!

How is it I have not reviewed The Cheese Board? I see I've shared photos of their beautiful sandwiches. I was also pretty sure I talked about how I love their menu of constantly changing specials. And I'm fairly certain I also wrote about their incredibly friendly staff. Yet I saw that I hadn't, so here we are. 

The "Kintop Sisters", former employees turned owners, have only amped up the volume, sass, and fun of this local favorite. While not much has changed physically about the space, there's a new energy in there and I can feel it in the food. I typically scan the daily special menu to find my choice, but the regular menu has a ton of delicious options too. I just can't help but want to celebrate the culinary creativity of their team! 

I've been to a few events they've catered too, and the food really doesn't let you down. It's kinda like getting a big ol' hug! 

If you haven't been The Cheese Board before OR you haven't been in a while, swing on by and check it out!

Hold the phone. Another one I haven't reviewed? See I took my sweet time getting here but I thought I'd reviewed the first visit. 

Well, I have Rawger C to thank for the maiden voyage and my intro to this amazing taqueria, mulas and vamipiros!

What are these taqueria specialties you ask? Well, pure magic. 

A mula takes two handmade tortillas, adds cheese and then slaps that down on the griddle to get melty and crisp while the tortillas stay tender, before it's stuffed with the meat of your choice. Think a quesadilla sandwich! Vampiros are similar with a crisper tortilla on the outside.

You can't go wrong with either one, nor the tacos or anything here. They start with handmade tortillas, so that's pretty special.

Most recently I had a vampiro de cabeza that blew my mind. Cabeza is all of the meat from around a cow's head, and it's usually rich and fatty, with some meat mixed in because the bulk of the meat comes from the cheek. 

Well I will be ordering cabeza over and over again here because I am pretty sure cabeza at Tacos Tijuana means cheek and beef cheek is friggin delicious. Check out the photo of the inside of this vampiro! 

The other thing not to miss here are the grilled onions and jalapeños they serve on the side. You can eat these plain or add them to your meal. Regardless they're fire! 

Don't skip the salsa either. If you don't like spice though, get it on the side because both the red and green are packed with flavor but a little on the hot side. 

It's no wonder this place is so beloved. If you haven't been, get there!

They had a pear sazerac on the menu that called to me. I couldn't ignore it and I'm glad I didn't. The absinthe was subtle, but brought out the earthy and herbal characteristics of the rye, with the pear bringing sweetness and the sharp acidity of the lemon bringing it all together. Best of all, the server knew how it should be served, but also offered to make it anyway I liked. 

That's service. Great service.

The seafood was stellar, as one would expect when it's being flown in FRESH seemingly daily. I love the fact the menu offers flexibility. Almost all the options can be served Fried, grilled, blackened, broiled, as a sandwich, on a bed of greens, and with your choice of sauce and side too! The portions are substantial, and you won't leave hungry either.

That said, you pay for this kind of luxury, and you can be sure you're paying for the quality too. You also won't be sorry you did. I'd expect $15-$20 at lunch and $20+ at dinner without drinks. There's a lot of those "MP" on the menu, meaning "Market Price", which certainly does fluctuate, but in my experience adds up to slightly more expensive than what the menu shows.

The market dining room is downstairs, and the bar is upstairs. Both have their charm and appeal. Downstairs a bit more rustic, while upstairs is a bit more modern. Overall though, both will leave you with a smile. 

So what are you waiting for? The fish isn't getting any fresher!

Get in while the getting is good. By that I mean have your phone ready to dial at 3pm when they begin taking orders, cuz if ya don't, you'll miss out on the pizza.

That's exactly what my wife did tonight and it netted us two pies and a salad, all of which were delicious.

The sausage here is my favorite and we got a pepperoni and sausage combo that didn't disappoint. The salad they serve is simple too, but the slightly sweet and tangy dressing makes it the perfect shotgun rider to the pie. I actually like to take the thinly sliced onion, peppers and mushrooms that get left on the plate and put them on the pizza! Then naturally I use the crust to mop up the rest.

Can't go wrong here.

Zozo's is old school cool y'all. 

From the red checkered tablecloths to attentive waitstaff donning a fresh pressed shirt and tie, this spot oozes classic Italian American goodness in all the best ways possible. Not to mention this place is family owned and operated, and you're guaranteed to run into Judy, Sid or Kevin when you visit. 

All I can say is lunch was such a lovely experience. There's a relaxed (but efficient) pace here, and it's clear they want you to enjoy your lunch. Walking in, I was pleasantly greeted by the staff and offered my choice of table. I opted for a booth with a great view of the kitchen, which was just getting started up for the day. Chef Kevin was a the helm, and I knew I was in for a treat. 

When the server brought the menus, she was sure to mention the features of the day including a soup du jour (UN SPLIT PEA -Hilarious and delicious) and a fish, and promptly brought drinks to the table. 

I saw the infamous Dungeness Crab Melt that fellow Yelp Elite Anthony A longs for daily. I gave it more than a second thought, but decided I needed to have all my faculties for the rest of the day and chose a beautiful blackened chicken Ceasar salad. This baby was huge, and I took half home. The chicken was perfectly cooked with that slightly crispy blackened exterior and a juicy center. 

The surprise kicker was the cheese toast resting on top! I don't know what cheese blend they use, but it ain't just basic mozzarella! MMMM! 

I'm so glad they are now on my weekly route so I can weave them into a new and delicious restaurant rotation.

Walden's I am so glad that you opened closer to the city center because now I don't have to trek across town to enjoy your food!

Living in Reno we're all spoiled. I have everything I need within 15 minutes of my front door, so traveling to NW Reno 20-30 minutes away feels like visiting a foreign country. As a community I wish we could break this down because I am sure this mentality is stopping a lot of us from visiting great places on a more regular basis. 

I digress though. This is a review of Walden's OG location on Mayberry and McCarran, which I've been visiting sporadically (when in the area) for quite a few years! 

The name "coffeehouse" isn't telling of what you'll find here. The food has always impressed me and it goes way beyond "coffeehouse" fare. Breakfast or lunch, you're sure to find something that suits your mood on the well-rounded menu. The kitchen team's creativity really shines in the specials, posted on a board by the register! I always look their first, but I'm 50/50 on whether I go with something new or order up some of their classic faves. 

On a recent visit I got the tuna melt, which might've been the best one I've ever had (crispy rye bread, melted cheese, great tuna salad) and on other visits I've loved the Manzo (Herb marinated steak, rosemary aioli, baby greens, crispy onions, Monterey Jack, sourdough garlic herb hoagie roll) and their breakfast frittatas! 

I'm a black coffee drinker with a preference for single origin and specialty coffees at this point. Though they have always had a house blend, I've never been super impressed with the coffee itself. None of them have been bad, just not my taste. Recently though they made a switch and are now offering Glorycloud (local roaster) in addition to their house blends, and that had me a whole lot happier. If you're looking for blended, sweetened or other creative coffee drinks, Walden's absolutely excels! I got to enjoy an iced chocolate mocha a ways back and found it super refreshing and delicious, and I don't usually like this stuff. 

All in all, Walden's is a great place to work remotely, grab a bite (breakfast or lunch - all diets welcome), and beverage of your choice. 

With the recent announcement of location four on the edge of downtown I am sure I've found a new spot to hang!

There must be a pound of butter in each biscuit because you can literally taste it in every bite.

Whoever thought it was a good idea to put a perfectly crispy piece of fried chicken on a biscuit should be commemorated with a bust prominently displayed somewhere in our nation's capital. For Pete's (or whatever name you think should be subbed in there) sake, they're clearly a national hero and no one will argue they are not worthy of grand celebration! 

Well, Pine State took that idea and turned it up a lil' bit, creating the new standard for this combo of chicken on a biscuit.

First they buttermilk brine those boneless chicken breasts, infusing flavor and making sure they'll fry up tender. Then each piece is hand coated and fried to perfect before being nestled between two pillow soft halves of a big buttery biscuit and topped with a whole host of toppings from apple butter to house made sausage and mushroom gravies! 

Are ya with me people? I sure hope so! 

Not feeling the "carbs"? Either skip here or try the Shrimp and Grits. Corn is a vegetable right? Kidding. But mushrooms are and this plate of hearty, creamy and cheesy frosts are topped with shrimp and a delicious mushroom sauté.

If you read this far, my last pro tip is: DON'T SKIP DESSERT! 

The cinnamon roll is awesome and the seasonal pop tarts are just plain fun!

Habanero mustard and solid white albacore tuna salad are a match that Heaven is keeping a secret from us all! Well, everyone but those who have had the Spicy Tuna at Rubicon Deli! 

Shame on me. I've lived in Reno for 12 years now, hearing the legend of Rubicon Deli and seeing the monolithic sandwiches brought back to the nearby offices I've worked in, and yet had never had the pleasure of dining there until recently. 

Scouring the menu I saw house roasted turkey, beautifully roasted beef, Italian cold cuts, and more, but I was continually drawn back to the Spicy Tuna. The combination of tuna salad (the really good kind), LTO, avocado, pepperoncini, and habanero mustard on fresh baked bread just sounded so damn good and I had to have it, and I was not disappointed.

I had no idea that combo could be so good, and now I think I'll be making tuna sandwiches with pepperoncini and habanero mustard at home! 

These sandwiches are HUGE. I opted for a whole sandwich (12.99) and could have been satisfied with half. Somehow I ate the whole thing in one sitting anyway, and it even came with a great little chocolate chip cookie. 

Most impressively my wife got the whole sandwich on gluten free bread and it was actually two normal sized sandwiches on gluten free bread. Good value, especially if sharing.

This is just going to be a quick update. Believe it or not, I've been back to this great restaurant two times and have sampled seven more dishes in the process, only repeating the order of the amazing "Spocy Wontons". 

From these experiences, I've learned this ain't your average restaurant. The menu is packed full of surprises, and the real gem here is as much the food as it is the staff and their excellent service. 

As far as I'm concerned, Shawn is the reason my visits have been so incredible. It's not often you can go to an Asian restaurant and find a non-Asian employee who truly has taken the time to understand and appreciate the food and culture the way he has here. Shawn has the ability to quickly explain any dish in extremely relatable terms to diners not familiar with the flavor profiles of Taiwanese food. Not only that, but he's also great at listening to your preferences and steering you toward dishes you're likely to enjoy as well. Best of all, he'll even help you understand some Taiwanese language along the way!

On the most recent visit we tried the taiwanese sausage, crunch and munch chicken., satay cabbage and beef noodle soup. Three of the four I've ordered elsewhere and all of them were different here. The satay cabbage was completely unique and nothing like the Thai peanut save dipped grilled skewers that immediately came to mind when I ordered this. Instead, this was intensely savory with garlic, notes  of dried shrimp and salted fish, and other distinctly Asian flavors. It was really good and a great compliment to the soup, which was deep, rich, and somewhat sour.

This go round I didn't LOVE any dishes, but I learned a lot. And I'm excited to see what I learn the next time I visit because there's a whole lot more menu to explore!

If you're a cocktail or spirits drinker, please visit Beer NV!

You read that right. It's not just beer and cider here. This is a full bar bar AND they take their spirits and cocktails very seriously! 

This is nothing new, and you know that if you've been coming here for a while. But if you've passed this place or read some reviews and somehow missed this fact, I'm sharing it now, loudly, so everyone knows this is a super cool spot for drinkers of all kinds.

We stopped by on Memorial Day and found a pretty chill and quiet scene. We got a few seats at one of the high top communal tables and first thing I noticed was that the spirits corner had moved up front. 

I scanned the cocktail menu and orders up a tequila cocktail that's a summery riff on a corpse reviver and then poked my head around the corner to see what they had to offer. Not only did I find the great spirits selection I've come to know here I also found a feature board with not one, but two amazing allocated whiskies being poured at amazingly appropriate prices AND another specialty cocktail with Japanese whisky too. 

The tequila drink was good, but it drank a little on the heavy side. I was surprised it was served up in a coupe (fancy glass) because reading the description I thought it would be served over ice. The menu may have mentioned that and I overlooked it. I actually think it would've been more enjoyable on ice because I wanted it to dilute a bit. 

The Japanese whisky cocktail was delicious and refreshing. Served over, it was like a whisky sour flavored with umeshu or sweet plumb wine, and it was delicious.

The group also enjoyed the bourbon and watermelon cocktail as well. Perfect summer drink with a hint of mint!

Gosh. Writing this review has me wanting to go right now!

Everything with intention. Everything from scratch. Everything so we can enjoy a better pizza experience.

That's how I'd describe The Pizza Collective, and everything I've tried and seen from them fits this exact description. 

Great pizza starts with the crust and these folks are making a sourdough crust from a pretty old starter. You can see the difference in the air pockets in the crust, while the slightly fermented flavor shines through and accents the whole pizza. It has the perfect chew and crust too!

The oven is a piece of art with a whole lot of history too. They sourced it from a legendary Bay Area pizzeria and you can almost taste all the pizzas that have come before it in the seasoned char it gives theirs. 

The pizza combos are all sincerely inspired by the season and it feels like you're not likely to find the same thing twice. I recently tried the Reno Vegan Chef Challenge pie with housemade vegan Brie cheese and Granny Smith apples. Certainly non traditional but a beautiful flavor experience all around. 

I love seeing all the activity in their open kitchen and their creativity on the menu. They respect all ingredients and make sure we all know where our food came from too. They're stewards of our community food-shed and an incredible addition to the community.

Upping the rating due to some very responsive management. Food a solid 3-3.5, but service bumps it up.

Now I'm fairly particular when it comes to burgers. I like a solid medium rare cook, leaving a juicy burger with a great beefy flavor. That patty has gotta be on a sturdy bun that can absorb all that flavor without falling apart. Condiments need to compliment each other and not compete, and this one is totally subjective. 

Last but not least, I like my fries extra crispy. Not burned, but not floppy.

I've been to Burger Me several times at both Reno locations, and no matter what, my burger arrives at what I would refer to as medium. I shared these experiences a few weeks ago and was contacted by management, who implored me to let them know if this occurred again so they could make it right. 

A day or so after sharing my initial review, I found myself back at Burger Me for dinner. I ordered the Cowboy Burger, medium rare, with grilled onions and bbq sauce on the side. Garlic fries extra crispy. 

The burger arrived and I could tell it was medium. I cut it in half anyway to verify, and promptly brought it up to one of the managers on duty. I told him about the contact I'd had via Yelp and asked him to validate whether the burger I'd been served was cooked the way I asked for it. He agreed it was not, and indicated I was not the first person to raise the same concern. He had another burger out in a flash. It wasn't exactly medium rare, but it was better than the previous. 

To me, medium rare is a warm red center. Medium is a hot pink center. Well done is hot grey center. The burger I received was medium by my definitions, and the burger I got back was more rare, but again, acceptable to me, so I ate it.  

The burger was tasty, even if a tad undercooked. The fries were crispy, but still many were a little limp for my liking. Again, solid 3.5 on food. I appreciate the management taking the time to address my burger and hope they can get the cook down so all come out as ordered in the near future.

Five stars for the @thedepotreno's best damn rotisserie chicken, fantastic fries, and the most delicious housemade mustard in town. Five stars for a badass bar program with creatively crafted cocktails, award winning spirits, and craft beers. Five stars for stellar ambiance, decor, and atmosphere that can only come from a rad restoration of a historic building done with incredible regard for the space. Four and a half stars for some service that had been a bit consistent over the course of 5-6 visits. Five stars for being big group rock stars. And Five more stars for being awesome about feedback and constantly striving to improve.

First up, the five star chicken. This dish has been on the menu in a variety of forms, from chicken lightly coated in a sweet and savory glaze of honey and mustard served over a massive mound of fresh cut fries, to the same perfectly rotisserated chicken topped with another sauce that featured kale and served with seasonal mashed veg, and each time it has been magnificent. Half a chicken with crispy skin, tender, juicy, and oh so succulent. The sides have always been great too. I've been criticized for ordering such "simple food", but hey, when it's perfect, why argue?

Now the fries? What a value. Order up an app of these, either white or sweet potato, and you're in for more than you bargained for because these plates are behemoth. It's perfect though, because they're ideal for sharing. The PRO-TIP here is that you need to ask for a side of their house mustard. It's a little sweet and a little spicy, and delightfully creamy and smooth, making the perfect foil to either fry choice.

When it comes to beverages, you really cannot go wrong. There's a wide array of cocktails based in a number of spirits, many of which are made in their distillery, meaning there's something for everyone. Worst case scenario, they have a full bar so you can really get whatever you want. Their beers are well loved locally too! 

The service though, has just been all across the board. I've had fantastic experiences where servers were on top of absolutely everything for a very large party from delivering food, refilling drinks, and right down to getting the checks exactly right. Then again I've been in and experienced the complete opposite with a smaller group. All in all though, this place ranks way up there on my list of favorite places to dine.

All that said, this is the kind of great local business that really works hard to improve and make sure they're the best. I've always been able to look past issues and continue to be a frequent patron and constant supporter. 

They're doing great things here and they deserve to be celebrated. If you haven't been in yet, what the hell are you waiting for? I'm heading back soon to try the new release of their rye whiskey. I can't wait!

It's been a minute since I enjoyed some of BJ's Kickass Fries, so I was stoked to see them at Food Truck Friday! They were just serving up Kickass Fries that night, and I'm not complaining.

If you don't know KA Fries are a mountain of fresh cut and fresh fried shoestring potatoes, topped with and tremendous amount of tender and succulent pulled pork, shredded cheese and their tangy and slightly sweet house bbq sauce!

Best of all, 100% of the sales were being donated to scholarship for the next generation of culinary pros via the Sierra Chapter of the American Culinary Federation!

You can get Kickass Fries at the restaurant and on Kickass Weds you can explore a whole menu of variations on the classic!

So fresh. So fast. So delicious. So friendly. 

If you haven't been to Wrap It Up, go now! 

This has been a favorite of mine for too many years now and I am thrilled more folks have discovered it too. In the beginning I remember seeing mainly employees from the surrounding businesses and random folks wander in for a bite. These days (pre-COVID) I now see people streaming in regularly and it makes me so happy for Ali and his crew.

What to order:
It's all about the chicken shawarma for me. Most often I order a large "Greek" salad with the chicken on top. 

Pro-tip, ask for the grilled eggplant to be added. Phenomenal. 

Pro tip 2, if you're sharing with a friend a salad with double chicken is enough and usually about $15!

Pro tip 3, get a side of the garlic sauce and thank me later.

They also do the shawarma as a plate with delicious rice and a wrap too.

Wrap It Up is where it's at. Go!

Holy pig! The tortanita is officially my new favorite sandwich and sadly there are no pics to prove it!

I demolished this creation is record time, and based on its size and heft, that is a new skill I learned I have. 

It starts with a bolillo roll, which is a crusty Mexican roll with a soft and delicate interior. Tortas are made on these rolls often, and the soft inside soaks up all the goodness on the sandwich without falling apart. 

On top of the roll here is house made carnitas, avocado, lightly sautéed onion, cilantro, a delicious yellowish salsa, and some cotija.

Let's start with those carnitas! So freaking good! Super tender, lightly caramelized and just the kind of thing you can't get enough of! Luckily the sandwich is loaded with them! They are a show stopper for sure, but everything else makes them even better.

If you didn't know, Chef/Owner Michael has some mad skill in the kitchen! He keeps refreshing the menu and every addition gets better! 

I'm going back to get the photos and eat another one!

There's something cool and special about the big windowed facade that faces South Virginia St. It's bright and inviting, and always seems to be filled with happy diners enjoying great conversation and food. It's fun to look in as I drive by, trying to see if I know anyone in the room, and imagining what I might order if I were sitting there myself. Over the years though, it seems I've done more driving by and imagining than actually trying this spot out for myself. Last night that changed!

Some days I love the more authentic homegrown flavors of the taqueria, and then others I want that cheesy, ooey gooey, sauce covered Mexican American food we all love. After a night of sampling some Tiki inspired cocktails at a competition down the road, I was craving the latter of the two menus, and thankfully dinner was next on the agenda! 

Our party of 8 was promptly seated in the dining room adjacent to the windows, which was kind of sad but understandable, at a table that was just a bit too small for us all. There was a table behind us that would have been perfect for the record. 

The chips and salsa, a focal point of any Mexican dining experience, were on point and delicious. You could tell these were tortillas that were freshly fried, served with an equally fresh salsa. They made sure to keep the basket and bowls full the entire meal, and for that I am very thankful.

With the cold weather outside, I wanted something hearty, warm and full flavored for dinner, so I ordered the Chicken Mole. It arrived looking a little tired, the chicken was dry, and overall the dish tasted burnt. I had to add the red salsa from the table and lime to help it out. The dish was served with tortillas, rice and beans, and those were great accompaniments. 

The dishes my friends had seemed to be enjoyed. I loved the browned, perfectly broiled and bubbling cheese that covered every plate that arrived. Perhaps I just ordered wrong. Maybe I'm spoiled by moles I have had elsewhere. In the future, I'd happily return to Miguel's to try them again. I'd be sure to order something else though.

First thing I noticed walking up was half price wine on Tuesdays! Then I realized... #Pizza on the #Whole30? What the heck was I thinking coming here? 

Well, that's exactly it. At the time I planned this exciting lunch meeting, I wasn't thinking about my diet. Nevertheless, I was confident that Id be able to stay on the path and find something that would fit the requirements. 

Now service alone will bring me back for pizza in the future. I had a lot of questions to ask, and the server was more than happy to answer them or get the answers to make sure I was comfortable in my decisions. He was attentive and made the experience really nice.

This being a pizza joint, I thought my options might be limited, but I didn't realize just how limited they'd be. On the non-pizza front there were only a few appetizers on the menu and a few salads. I ordered the house salad, which came with fresh spring greens, red onion, tomatoes, and roasted red peppers, to which I added grilled chicken and salami. The veggies were fresh and crisp, the roasted red peppers were awesome, the size of the salad was very nice (and I had the small), but the chicken left something to be desired. It reminded me of the pre sliced "grilled chicken breast" that you get in a plastic package at the store with the rubbery texture and artificial grilled flavor. I figured I'd get a nice grilled chicken breast.

My companion had a beautiful lunch special with a nice looking pizza and a smaller salad. I was very jealous of the pizza, and just looking at it made me want to return for some in the future.

Heck, Tuesday's are Wine Tasting Tuesday when glasses and bottles are half off! Yep. That fact is so nice I said it twice! 

Pizza party soon!

I love this concept. It's simple, satisfying, comforting, approachable, and reasonably affordable. Most importantly it's something kind of new for our community. Solid 3.5 star experience here, which means it's good.

First time here and I had to go with the rotisserie combo. Half pound of meat (chicken and Tri-tip, which is served medium rare), two sides and two house sauces for $14.99. 

The chicken was succulent, with just the right amount of wood fired flavor. The skin wasn't as done as I'd hoped though. It's my favorite part of a rotisserie chicken. 

Now I usually hate tri-tip. I find it tough, flavorless, and generally hard to eat. Hearing it was supposed to be medium rare had me excited though. That's how I enjoy beef. My portion came out overcooked, and the server was quick to replace it. The second portion was perfectly medium rare, sliced pretty thin though, and it appeared finished quickly on a grill. It was tender and well seasoned, and I ate every bite. 

For sauces I chose chimichurri and aji panca (red chili, not spicy). The chimichurri was bright and fresh with a clear hit of citrus. The aji panca was dark, earthy, and smoky. They both made great counterpoints and accents to the meats. The sauces get 5 stars! 

I went with the corn salad, at the recommendation of the server, and had the smoky beans. The corn salad was interesting with roasted corn, poblano peppers and red onion, which made for a nice fresh side item to the rich meats. The beans were ok. I noticed some rendered bacon in them, but overall they tasted like basic baked beans to me. Three stars on the sides, and that include my sample of the crinkle cut fries I tried off my friend's plate. 

Service was friendly and prompt in the beginning, but as one or two more tables filled in, it slid a bit. I was seriously surprised by this because our server seemed to be aware of everything at the beginning and she did stay on top of drink refills too. Overall, it was good though.

I definitely think this is some place others need to try. There were interesting burgers, apps and more in the menu that would definitely make this a place I'd come back to for lunch. I also noticed whole chicken meals for $26.99 and that's killer!

I'm such a creature of habit. My cravings go in cycles, almost on a clock, and when I need Hinoki, only Hinoki will do! 

As of a month ago I've been really trying hard to eat more consciously, swapping heavier meals for lighter wherever possible. So with my work day ending at 8:30pm last night I had to decide between some of the few places open en route to home, and the Hinoki Poke Bowl jumped right up to the top of my mind. 

It's such a balanced meal at a crazy reasonable price ($10.99). You get a mountain of fish, fresh mixed greens lightly dressed in poke sauce, avocado, Japanese yam, seaweed salad, and enough rice to add some filler without being a gut bomb. I know I shouldn't but I always get a side of spicy mayo because it's so damn good. 

It has never once left me wanting more, but it has always left me feeling really great for the rest of the day. It's a fantastic way to get that sushi fix without filling yourself until you explode. 

Give it a try if you haven't had one before! It'll become your new go to too!

Did you know Washoe Public House has one of the best happy hours in town? 

How about one of the most chill patios? 

How about a whole menu of approachable elevated dishes with a cheffy spin on em all? 

Oh, and what about one of the nicest, relaxed, and downright cool chef/owners around?

Well, it's all that and more, and with each of my infrequent visits I'm reminded of just how rad this place really is and how lucky we are to have it.

This time I popped in for a quick happy hour date with my wife before heading to a show. The happy hour menu has some fantastic options from Irish Nachos and Scotch Eggs to anchovy toast and more, all around $5! Drinks they do house wine and some drafts plus we'll cocktails, which if you're not after something specific, offers quite a few decent options. 

I had to try the anchovy toast, and it was pretty spot on for what I expected. The Spanish white anchovies were a bit more on the fishy side that I was expecting but balanced out nicely with the pickled egg. 

We also ordered the tempura tiger prawns upon the recommendation of a friend and hot damn they were good. I usually shy away from tempura anything at a restaurant because it's so average normally, but these were huge sweet tiger prawns in a light and crunchy batter accented with chili threads and toasted sesame seeds, with some chili aioli to dip. This is not on happy hour but you need to get this dish!

Washoe Public House is a sleeper, so let's change that!

Five stars for the Capture 2 combo at Capriotti's!
Five stars for its epic value!
Five stars for the fast and friendly service! 
Five stars for it including a sizeable "small" sub on PERFECT bread!
Five stars for the perfectly sized side salad that fills you up enough you don't need to, but probably will, finish the sub!

Four stars for the actual sub today (asked for light oil and vinegar and it was swimming in it as well as mustard)

Four stars for the balsamic chicken salad, solely based on quality of the protein in this one. I've loved the Black and Bleu and the Italian Chop previously, both had at another location. 

All in all, this location and I have a bit of a sordid relationship. I don't know why, but it never hits on all marks for me. Something is always a bit off, whereas the other locations nail it.

Still, the Cap 2 remains one of my favorite lunch deals around. You can't best it for value or quality. Try it for yourself!

I'm into this whole BYO, "pizza whatever the heck way you want it" concept. You get to build the pizza of your dreams and it costs $10 or less in almost all cases. Pretty good deal and experience overall. 

I had some really high expectations when it came to Blaze. I'd watched the company sweep across the country like wild fire (get it?) and after a few other BYO concepts opened, they finally opened a location here too. I'd seen about a million friends visit their local Blaze stores, cook up stellar looking pies, and brag endlessly about how good they were, so I really wanted my experience to stand up. 

I built my own pie on their traditional crust with red sauce, bacon, pepperoni, sauteed onion, fresh garlic, meatballs, ricotta, parm and mozz, and a drizzle of pesto to top it off. I asked for the pie well done, to make sure it crisped top to bottom, and moved down the line to wait for it to emerge from the oven. 

True to form, the pizza cooked quickly, and they left it in a few minutes longer per my request, resulting in a nice crisp with a little char. Unfortunately they also left my wife's gluten free pizza in there that long as well, which came out with some very dark edges that I wouldn't call charred. 

Overall the pizza was good, but I had higher hopes based on the experiences of my friends. The food at Blaze is just a good example of a personalized pizza. I'd hoped something might've set them apart, but alas, nothing jumped out. I'd say they're my second fave BYO pizza spot now though.

Dorinda's is a world class chocolatier that fortunately calls Reno home! Every time I visit I'm in awe of how professional, courteous and well informed the staff is and so beyond impressed by how passionate and willing they are to share the stories behind each product and the entire process to make them. 

In a day and age where we do everything digitally and human contact has been drastically minimized, Dorinda's manages to maintain that old school and high class personal touch on their guest experience. If the chocolate sucked (WHICH IT DOES NOT), you probably wouldn't care because the staff made you feel like a million bucks buying it.

As I said, the chocolate here is divine and that's because they only use the best and don't use preservatives, stabilizers or fillers to make their product look as good as it does. It's all natural and proper handling that insures this chocolate keeps and eats just as Dorinda herself intended. 

Their innovation is another strong area of the business. They keep their fan favorites but they are always adding to the lineup. Today I discovered their snacking bars, aka segmented chocolate bars you can break a piece off of to... snack! They have quite a variety but I picked up the 70% cacao with cacao nibs for my wife. She really loves her dark chocolate and the bitter nibs are an extra touch I knew she'd be into. Watch for the new packaging on these because they'll be show stoppers when you gift them to people!

Gosh. Can I share any more love with Dorinda's? Ok. One more. This is a family run business through and through. Dorinda is still involved but she's proudly handed much of the operation off to her two sons and they're carrying on the family name beautifully. Just like Dorinda, they've made sure the staff and all the customers feel like family too.

Sadly Rounds retail is closed or in the process of closing as they retool the business model to be focused on their food service manufacturing and wholesale operations. 

We could choose to be sad about this situation, but the good news is... we will still be able to get our favorite Rounds goodies! 

That's right. The big change is that the restaurant is going away BUT a lot of our favorites are going to be available via online ordering DELIVERED to your front door. 

I got to try this out the last week they were open and let me tell you it was a breeze and I will Def be doing it again. There's nothing better than getting a special delivery of bagels.

Holey Schmidt... your donuts were literal mana from heaven! 

In all seriousness, the opening of Holey Schmidt nearly coincided with the birth of my son, so whilst stuck in the hospital I sent my mother there to pick up some goodies so we could do some recon. 

What I didn't count on was that I'd be living off that dozen donuts for the next three days! 

Either way, a dozen assorted donuts arrived (via Mom) in a non-descript brown box, which did not bely the brightly colored beauties beneath the lid. 

I'd seen pictures, but these were just as impressive in person! 

Suffering from paralysis by analysis, Mom let the staff choose the dozen which included Strawberry Cheesecake with graham cracker crumbs, Maple Bacon with crispy bacon pieces, Cookies and Cream with real cookie crumbs, and Butterfinger with, you guessed it, Butterfinger candy bars. 

I'd have to say, while all were tasty, I ended up being a fan of the simple chocolate cake donut! Actually all of the cake donuts were delicious! 

The only qualm I had was they were all just a bit greasy with a slightly oily flavor. Knowing how hard this team is working, I'm sure this is something they've already worked out. 

While I'm thankful these donuts could sustain me during a very difficult time, I personally can't wait to get into the shop and enjoy one fresh and see all the hard work this team put in firsthand.

There's nothing better than raging in downtown Reno, drinking some tasty cocktails and brews with buddies and suddenly realizing it's 11PM or later. Why rejoice at the late hour you ask? Because it's the perfect time to for some preventative medicine at Golden Flower! 

Grab a table and get ready to fight off that hangover with a banging bowl of pho, some delicious imperial egg rolls, or one of their cold noodle dishes! On this last visit I'd had enough liquid courage to allow me to order the most daunting dish on the menu, Bun Bo Hue, a spicy noodle soup made with a rich, complex, and meaty broth, packed full of all the best animal tidbits like well-done flank, rare beef, tendon, and oh yes, blood cake! The version here does tendon right! It cooks for hours in the broth until extremely tender, all the while absorbing the rich flavors of the stock. Andrew Zimmern would describe it as meat jelly, and I'd concur. If it eats like that, you know it's good! The blood cake is harder to describe, but it turns out it was way more a textural thing than a flavor. Kind of thought it would be a little different, but eating it is worth the shock value! I'll be back for more of this soon! 

But slide a big bowl of that up right next to a big plate of the chicken wings they have on their late night menu, and that is a match made in heaven! My fiancee, who enjoyed her night just as much as I did ;), only ate a tiny bit of soup that night before we went home. The next morning, Bun Bo Hue #FTW! Hangover be gone for me, and well, lets just say she wasn't as happy!

I double dare you to down a double stack burger at Juicy's! I know there are plenty people out there that could do it, including myself, but that is one gut buster of a meal! I mean, at 1/3 lb each, these burgers are NO JOKE! 

Juicy's does the old fashioned hamburger right! Seasoned and griddle cooked to perfection for the right amount of crust, placed onto a soft warm toasted bun topped with a mixture of mayo and mustard, lettuce, tomato, and a big piece of onion, then wrapped in wax paper and presented to the hungry diner to be devoured! 

This burger is one of my guilty pleasures, and something I sometimes fantasize about. I like to come up with physical activity that would warrant me eating one, topped with cheese and bacon of course, along with their delicious fries, and a mocha shake! I can't have one without the others at this point. Remember, this is not fast food, so don't be expecting a .99 burger or fries. 

These bad boy burgers are cooked to order, so leave a little time to wait. And yes, you can have it your way if you don't like the way they serve it. But leave the burger making to the masters and let them serve it up the way it's meant to be enjoyed. You won't be disappointed.

Five stars for Uriah who made an otherwise bad situation into a better one with his solid customer service, but three stars for the dish I ordered (Huevos Montana) on overall flavor. 

It was a dudes weekend, so when friends asked if we wanted to join them for lunch I loaded up the baby and headed off to meet them at Squeeze In. My parents love this spot and make it a point to visit every time, so I've grown fond of it too, but this last one just wasn't the same. 

Dining with a one-year old isn't too much fun but the Squeeze staff were quick to bring him a basket of toys which kept him engaged the whole time. They also fired out a fruit cup that helped too!

Uriah was our server and he was super attentive and with us at all the right moments. We all placed our orders and were excited for lunch. The plates started rolling out and everyone's arrived except my huevos Montana. Uriah said the kitchen had been behind but that it should be right up. A few minutes passed and he checked in again to let me know it was coming now, and when it arrived it was somehow lukewarm in the middle. Since the potatoes were hot and the eggs were hot and cooked as ordered, it made me feel as if all the ingredients had been fired separately and assembled once they were done cooking. 

One word to Uriah and he immediately took it off the bill without asking and offered to remake it as well. I don't like wasting food, especially due to a temperature issue like this, so I said you've done anything one could expect in a situation like this and I'll just eat it as it arrived. Unfortunately the one year old had different plans for me, so I grabbed a box and had to run out the door. 

So you probably want to know what I thought about the dish in the end. Well, later that afternoon at home I reheated it and found the dish to be generally bland. The chorizo (solid up charge to add this) was lacking that signature umph, and the salsa and pico tasted fresh, but it needed more. I'd actually asked for extra red salsa and they only remembered the sour cream for my friend. So I doctored it up with some cholula and added some extra salt and pepper and it was ok. 

If the dish had been good, I would keep my rating at 4 stars, but given the entire experience I can't. It just wasn't what I've come to expect at Squeeze In.

Caps has become my new standby, and I'm stoked to find consistency carries across the locations. 

Recently I stopped in here to grab a Take 2 combo. It's such a great value. A small sub and a sizable salad for like $9. Consistently good and a filling lunch. 

This store doesn't have the same atmosphere as the remodeled store on Plumb, but they more than make up for it in fast and friendly service. The team members on the register are quick to greet guests and are happy to handle any special requests you might have. They all seem happy to be at work and that translates to a consistently great product.

The turkey is a favorite of mine, but it is most often dry. Pro tip: extra mayo

The Italian is always a hit for me too. Pro tip: pile on the sweet peppers and spicy pepper relish!

Lighthouse Coffee, you've got a good thing going!

I'm fairly regular at the South Reno location, but when my travels take me into Sparks, I try and swing by the Lighthouse mothership. After all, it's where I first fell in love with this family, their business, product and where the culture of this company originated. 

From my experience, happy staff equal a quality product and a consistent experience for customers. Consistent experiences bring guests back repeatedly. 

Truth be told, the last time I came to this location, the other two did not exist. In fact, Todd and Melanie were both working here, Melanie on drive-thru and Todd at the register. There may have been another staff member helping, but it was really the two of them sharing their passion with each guest, insuring that everyone had a great experience. 

Today, I was greeted by two incredibly happy staff members. I didn't catch their names, but they were a solid team, running things by each other, and making sure everything was done efficiently and correctly. I ordered a cold brew, and every follow up question you could expect was asked and I was even encouraged to take yet another punch card with instructions to bring them all in so any of the other locations can combine them for me.

It's this over and above positive attitude and friendly service that keeps me coming in to Lighthouse. That and the great coffee of course!

DO NOT SLEEP ON THE NEW COLD NOODLES! These are so unique and so damn delicious that I'm literally craving them one day after I tried them for the very first time. 

Noodles are all about texture and these are somewhere between perfectly chewy and delightfully tender. That's because they're made from sweet potato starch, which creates a unique noodle experience and a texture you need to experience.

The sauce is sweet, sour, and spicy with a nice punch from garlic and some nutty sesame too. They top the noodles with a hard boiled egg, protein of your choice, scallion, cucumber and pickled cabbage, all of which create a great mix of flavors and textures you'll enjoy as you make your way through the whole bowl. 

Bab Cafe has been and still is one of my favorite meals in town, especially for fast casual, and this dish is one more reason to love them. 

Go get some and thank me later.

Sushi in a casino? Why would we ever do that. Well, I'll tell you... 

If you saw in a previous review, I noted that my sushi relationship status is currently in the It's complicated stage, and that's thanks to Daniel, sushi chef/manager at Sushi Saga. Daniel seriously has a passion for his food, and wants each guest to have a great experience. He's worked in some of the best places in Reno, and has trained his other sushi chefs and servers to the same exacting standards. 

Daniel has mastered the art of nigiri, and if you don't believe me, take a look at my sushi porn shot from the other day. A generous slice of fresh fish is laid gently on a perfectly formed ball of well seasoned sushi rice, presented beautifully to the guest. Daniel and his team even have a number of off menu nigiri creations they can offer, many of which feature one of the 17+ secret sauces he makes in house. 

When it comes to long or hand rolls, there's no shortage of creativity here either. The neon specials board always has something new on it, and it has never disappointed. Is there a roll at another place that you can't get enough of? Let Daniel make you his version and see what you think. That famous Jason hand roll (cooked scallop, tobiko, mayo, green onion) is the perfect example. The ingredients sound simple, and they could be. At other places its just cooked bay scallops, but at Sushi Saga, Daniel deep fries them until they have a slightly crispy golden exterior and are warm when he mixes them with the real deal Kewpie Japanese mayo, tobiko and green onion. Just that little bit of extra thought makes his version a little more special. 

If you haven't been in to give them a try, you seriously need to. Daniel and his team will put your sushi relationship all in a tizzy!

Tacos y Mezcal... you'd think that's the whole story, but there's a lot more happening at Estella. 

No surprise there when you consider the people who first envisioned the concept and the passionate and talented team delivering the goods daily! 

This restaurant is an epic addition to our community, Chef Harrison is the kind of talent we need in our scene, Diana is a demanding FOH manager and wants every guest to leave happy, and Lo is keeping the cocktail game and mezcal mix fresh so there's something exciting on every visit.

Piper Stremmel, owner of The Jesse and Estella, had dreamed of opening a concept like this for more than 10 years. Inspired by her own lodging experiences abroad, Stremmel stated that the quality of her accommodations had the greatest impact on how she experienced a destination, so she set out to create a boutique hotel that could serve as the ideal jumping off point for an "authentic Nevada experience", and naturally that hotel needed a culinary experience to go along with it.

Enter Estella, a small, lively modern restaurant with Mexican flavor and flair. The kitchen and small dining room occupy the former Hub Coffee Roastery, just off the patio behind The Jesse hotel on the corner of East 4th Street and Lake Street. The kitchen is run by Chef Harrison Cooper, who comes to Estella from the James Beard award-winning  San Francisco restaurant State Bird Provisions. Chef Harrison's menu delivers an "authentic Nevada experience", highlighting the seasonal bounty and utilizing ingredients from local farms and ranches.

After a few visits I can tell you that you should start your visit at the towering wall of mezcals. This incredibly diverse can only enhance your overall experience here, and the staff can totally suggest a nice one for you. I love that it comes with the traditional worm salt and orange, as well as a Nevada Brining Company pickled radish! If you're not feeling too adventurous, the 50/50 or Michelada will not disappoint. 

The menu at Estella is tiny but mighty, with some serious flavors packed into the tacos. The tacos are good size for the $4+ price tag, and two with chips and salsa can definitely satisfy a fierce hunger. You're really paying for the artistry that goes into these though. Handmade tortillas, house made marinades, and lots of technique, add up to an elevated taco experience. 

I've found the vegetarian offerings are actually my favorite on the menu. The smoked mushroom taco and the seasonal veggie offering (last time was beautiful roasted carrots) are incredibly substantial and wonderfully complex. I've also loved the seasonal salad as well, though I wish that was a bit larger for the price point.

So why 4 stars? As a new biz, they're figuring things out really fast. My experiences have been a bit inconsistent, but I've shared direct feedback each time and I know they absolutely take it to heart and it will end up moving Estella to a 5 star rating for me in the future.

This restaurant is an epic addition to our community. I look forward to frequenting Estella solo and with friends. If you haven't gone, do yourself a favor and get there ASAP so you can be the one to tell all your friends.

I can't believe I was ever a skeptic. I couldn't understand the cult following for a fast food joint for so long. Then suddenly it clicked and now I'm hooked.

I know I shouldn't eat it, but I can't help myself. It's so nostalgic. So delicious. So comforting. So fun. 

I know we all enjoy our In N Out a little differently. For me the whole experience from getting it to enjoying is like a ritual, and something I look forward to everything that comes before eating it as much as I enjoy eating it. 

Double double animal style, whole grilled onion with fries. 

While grilled onion is a game changer. Get it. Thank me later.

Could I eat the large bowl? Hell yes I could!

Poke has landed in Reno in the form of a quick-serve fast-casual concept in NW Reno! This experience is all about you, with a side of friendly staff serving up big smiles with each scoop of seafood.

The process couldn't be more simple.

1) Pick a size: 3 scoops of protein in a small, 5 in a large.
Pro-Tip: Scoops are kinda small, so if you're hungry, go for a starchy base (see step two) or go large.

2) Pick a base: white or brown rice, mixed greens, wonton chips or mix and match.

3) Pick your protein: Salmon, tuna, octopus, tofu, yellowtail

4) Sauce it up! 
Pro-Tip: I got the three scoops and had them sauced separately. Normally they mix them all together with one sauce. I would not advise trying this if they're busy, but do try it! 

5) Top it! I chose krab, seaweed salad, fried onion, and more! Avocado is $1 extra but so good!

All in all this was a quick, delicious and fun experience!

Craving Chinese and seeing Jazmine delivering seemed like the perfect storm. I've loved Jazmine in the past, but it was prior to some changes in the ownership and kitchen team, but I wasn't concerned because the food had been so consistent I didn't think anything could go wrong.

Well, it just wasn't the same. In general it felt like the regard for the food was what had changed most. The flavors were similar but felt muted, the textures were off, like what should've been crispy was mushy (and yes I've accounted for travel in that comment), and I felt some of the quality had disappeared too.

The green beans were delicious but felt over cooked. The salt and pepper shrimp were good, but not a little mushy, and the Singapore noodles were pretty bland. The Peking pork was the best of it all, but the sauce was edging on overly sweet, and lacked the depth we've enjoyed in the past. 

Im sad to downgrade my rating here. Hopefully the next visit will bring it back.

Spring decides to show up, so what do we do? Brunch and a stroll through Midtown to check out all of the new businesses of course! 

After Virginia to visit Pizzava and Under The Rose's new brewery and taproom, we decided we needed a cold drink to cool us off from the blaring sun, and Bubble Tea Station appeared like an oasis in the desert! 

This kiosk finally has a purpose, and it was awesome to see it so busy! 

We approached the window and ordered a Thai Tea with boba, and minutes later it was out! The tapioca pearls were soft and chewy, and the Thai Tea was sweet, but not too sweet! It was incredibly refreshing.

Best of all they were rocking some epic tunes, the sun was shining, the umbrellas were SECURELY UP on the comfortable patio and the staff was super friendly. 

I've been wanting to stop by here for a while, and I'm so glad we did. I can't wait to visit their other location in Sparks soon! 

OH YEA! They have salted cheese topping!

The name does not deceive here. You will leave this deli with a full belly indeed! These sandwiches are NO JOKE! Select meats, cheeses, and toppings piled high on house made bread of all varieties, are served up on a 12" pizza tin, likely because that's all these belly busting behemoths will fit on! To put it in perspective, that's larger than a personal pie at most places! 

I came on opening day because of all the buzz around about these sammies, and my own personal experiences with their pig pops at Reno Street Food. I was excited to give it a try, and honestly had no idea what to expect. I was really happy to see that the owners had done quite a bit to make the interior more warm and friendly. They have some warm wood hanging on the walls along with framed photos and posters too, and a few TVs. The menu board is hanging above the register, and there are options for just about everyone. As a Florida boy, I was drawn immediately to the Cuban, though naturally I asked the really enthusiastic staff member what she recommended too. My friend and I decided to share the Cuban and the Dirka Dirka. 

The Cuban comes with a mountain of thickly sliced mojo marinated roasted pork loin, ham, swiss, mustard, and pickles, and we ordered it on the house French roll. The Dirka Dirka is corned beef and pastrami, mustard, swiss, all topped with a jalapeno slaw, and we got this one on the house Jalapeno cheddar bread. 

I'm rounding up my experience thanks to the service and the staff here. From the warm welcome, great guidance, and the thank you on the way out, they worked really hard to make sure we had a great experience. 

Breaking it down though, I'd give the service 5 stars. This staff knew the menu really well and made some great recommendations! They were also friendly, fast and really positive. The atmosphere scores 4 stars with me because they really warmed up what was a bleak and very corporate place prior, and the sammies a solid 3.5 because the Cuban was massive but the pork was a little dry, and the Dirka Dirka seemed a little light on the corned beef and pastrami. 

Overall though, that's a 4 star spot in my mind. I'm excited to have this shop, and their interesting offerings, in town!

Last night, while seated on one of the period sofas in this dimly lit bar, and I caught my eyes closing a bit as I listened to the murmurs and musings around me. Subconsciously I began to imagine I was back in 1864, right around the time our great state was born. I could see a place just like this, with characters of the old west filling the seats. I could hear the spurs jingle jangling as folks filled the room, and I could see everyone sipping on something strong, winding down the day with tall tales of cattle and the country. Deep in thought the windows faded from my view, and I got the feeling I wasn't in Reno anymore. I was taken back to the early days of Nevada, and I didn't really want to leave. 

On Nevada Day it feels only appropriate to review the 1864 Tavern! This spot on Cal Ave has been quietly creeping on a come up with craft cocktails, great draft beers, and one of the most unique atmospheres in the local bar scene. Owner Shawn Plunkett and his team have done a great job of reviving the period vibe and making it hip, cool, and comfortable. From the benches, chairs, and sofas, to the unique banquettes along the walls, the furniture is what you may notice first. It's a real throwback. As you look around the room you'll notice the accent pieces like taxidermy, period photos and frames, and the amazing bar and back bar that has to be handmade. No detail has been spared in this space, and it's no wonder I felt like I'd gone back in time. 

Just like in the days of the old west, you'll find the same hospitality, friendly barkeeps, reasonable prices, and great drinks that will have you forgetting the troubles of your day in no time. So take time to take a step back into 1864.

Check-in offers are sweet, but when they are for a FREE fishbowl full of brownie sundae after a few nice glasses of top shelf whiskey, they're freaking amazing!!! We came to Cafe Milano for the "After Midnight $6.99 Breakfast Special", when the entire breakfast menu is $6.99! My friends had the chicken fried steak and the NY steak and eggs, both came with hashbrowns and choice of toast or a fresh pastry from their bakery! The pastries looked amazing (danish, bear claws, croissants, etc.) and the chicken fried steak was just what the doctor ordered after a night out. 

But real eye opener was the Brownie Trainwreck sundae! Literally a fishbowl with a wine stem, brimming with brownies, hot fudge, vanilla ice cream, whipped cream, and other goodies... regularly $6.95, FREE after check-in and the purchase of an entree. They had an entire menu of desserts you could have chosen from, but this thing sounded epic. I only wish there was a little more ice cream, but then again I always want more ice cream!

I cannot wait for the day I can enjoy ramen in a restaurant because takeout does not cut it. 

That said, I'm happy to say I enjoyed the food we got from Haru, takeout or not, and I'm grateful for the safety precautions and Covid protocols they've put in place to keep operating during these difficult times. 

Takeout only is their game, plus masks and gloves, plus lots of sanitizer. 

We ordered the tonkotsu kuro and the Tori paitan ramen. The kuro was the favorite and the garlic aroma filled the car once I put the bag inside. We asked for the black mayu (not actually sure what it is exactly) in the side so we could share the soup with our kiddo and he loved it. The broth was milky and on the rich side, like you'd expect, but I like my tonkotsu very rich and almost creamy. The chashu was deliciously tender pork belly and I ate it all up! The tori wasn't my favorite. The broth had a strong flavor that I can only describe as slightly gamey. 

I loved how they packaged all the ingredients separately from the broth, and all of them were tasty. I like my noodles with a lot of chew and texture. These noodles seemed a bit thinner than the ramen I'm used to and were a little more done than I prefer. On the next go I think I can ask for the noodles to be more al dente. 

We also tried two Yakitori skewers (tasty) and the karaage which was served with two tasty dipping sauces (yuzu mayo and togarashi Mayo), a nice accompaniment to the ramen. 

Solid spot! Get your ramen fix here.

Oops I did it again. I waited too long. Got lost in the game. Ooh baby baby. 

Oops I missed my call. That was sent from the Islands. I just had to get some! 

And so I did. Aloha Shack brings the flavors of the islands to South Reno quite often, and last week the stars (or schedules) aligned and I was able to catch up with them for a taste. 

When it comes to food trucks it's what's on the inside that matters and Aloha Shack is full of heart and fantastic food. 

The heart comes from Theresa and Christoper Luke, owners and operators of Aloha Shack. They wear that heart on their sleeves and share it through their food, serving every plate lunch, poke bowl, and spam musubi with a big ol' smile, and maybe a hug too. 

I met up with a fellow Elite and we sampled the entire menu WITHOUT ordering every dish! 

How'd we do it? Easy. We asked nicely and the Luke's were super happy to mix and match the poke bowl and put together a plate with both the kahlua pork and chicken teriyaki. Naturally we had to order a spam musubi too... because... HAWAII! 

Well, everything was absolutely delicious! 

Biggest surprise was the spam musubi. I planned to hate it and as I write this I already want another. I can't even describe it, but you just need to get one. 

When it came to the poke bowl, the traditional ahi poke was the winner for me. The wasabi mayo salmon had a solid bite and great fresh texture, but the traditional poke was exactly as I remembered it from the islands. The real kicker on the bowl had to be the marinated cucumbers though. I wasn't expecting them and really liked what it brought to the party.

On the plate lunch, the mac salad was a surprise! So often that's boring and bland, but at Aloha Shack it's rocking some serious seasoning and GARLIC! You'll love it. The other surprise was the kahlua pork. That's also a dish I've never enjoyed because it has always been devoid of seasoning, but at Aloha Shack it was full of flavor, and when I had a bite with the mac salad, it was magic! 

The only dish I wasn't swooning over was the chicken teriyaki. The chicken was moist and delicious, but the teri sauce was a little on the thick side and tasted kind of sweet and tomatoey vs the rich and syrupy sauce I was expecting. I guess I was hoping for a kalbi sauce of sorts, and their version of teriyaki is just so different. 

Overall though, this is a truck to find. Now go get a taste of the islands ASAP and order that SPAM!

I'd heard amazing things about El Adobe, and it is certainly a local favorite, but after my first visit I was left wanting something more. But after this last visit, I can see my issue was simply ordering wrong, and this place deserves all the praise it receives. 

Birria, the braised beef version in Chilis, cinnamon and other warm spices, is a dish I discovered here and has become my measure of quality in Mexican restaurants. It's not a common dish, so if it's on the menu, it better be good. The first time at El Adobe I went for it and after one bite, knew it was far too salty. Prior to ordering I had seen some incredible looking tacos and combo plates pass by, and as I watched dishes arrive to the others in our party and saw the happy smiles on their faces, I knew what had to happen on my next visit.

So after a celebratory cocktail or two at Chapel with friends, we made our way to El Adobe again. I looked over the menu and landed on the carnitas ala Diabla and the chicken mole, and my wife and I decided that would be dinner and lunch the next day. The carnitas were sliced, which is something I'm not used to, but they were tender on the inside with a crispy exterior that soaked up the rich and spicy sauce. The sautéed onions made for a great addition to this dish, and putting it all in a warm corn tortilla made the perfect taco! The mole was deep in flavor with dark chocolate, cinnamon, a little hit of heat from Chilis, and an incredibly silky texture. They used chicken thighs I think, which just insured that the meat would be very moist, and again, wrapping it all in a corn tortilla made it one helluva taco.

Friends at the table ordered the combo plates Id seen before, and those damn tacos caught my eye but escaped my brain when I ordered this time. No big deal because the two dishes I had on this visit could bring me back again and again, and next time I won't forget to try the tacos! 

P.S. The perfect compliment to all Mexican food is an Ice Cold Draft Negra Modelo, and El Adobe might have the coldest in town!

Build Your Own Pizza has landed in Reno and all accounts say we love it! 

This concept is a brilliant invention. Think about it. Normally pizzas are so large you HAVE TO share them, which means compromises on sauces, cheeses, toppings,l take-out or delivery, etc. Everyone loses on something in this scenario. 

With a Build Your OWN (emphasis on the own) you get your very own pizza! Say it with me now. Your very own pizza! Tell me... what's not to love about your very own pizza? Zero compromises here! You get whatever you want!

So what makes MOD different from others? 

1) Branding... This brand has Life. You can see it in the hipster/urban decor with red brick, graffiti/street style artwork, and the names of the pies. More impressively you can feel it in the staff's energy. They're part of the MOD tribe and they want you to be too.

2) Service... MOD service is efficient, friendly, personal, and super encouraging! They literally want you to understand that whatever pie you create, it's gonna be great! They're also very proud of their product and want you to enjoy it.

3) Toppings... They've got it all! Some new ones on me were roasted cauliflower, roasted kale, and roasted garlic, as well as these incredibly delicious sweetie hot peppers, like you'd get on a great Italian sub! The combos are literally endless and everything was super delicious. Oh yeah, and just when you thought you'd put everything on the pie, there's a station to top your pie with sauces like pesto or Sri-Rancha!

4) Big Azz Selection of Featured Pies... It's a freaking wall, and I personally loved seeing a seasonal pie AND staff picks!

5) MOD Salad OR Pizza Salad... MOD Salad is just like a MOD pizza. You can literally put any ingredients from the topping bar into a salad! If you want to turn it into a Pizza Salad, you build that salad and they'll dump it on a garlic and oil crust for you!

Pro-Tip: Don't overload your pie. Less is actually more at places like these. Too many makes for a soggy and cool center, and that's not great pizza!

MOD you've made your mark. I'm part of your team, and I'll be back!

Two Californians and 3 Floridians walk into Sparks Coffee Shop and the first question is "This is a coffee shop?".

The two Nevadans that brought them there just had to chuckle. 

Sparks Coffee Shop IS our favorite local diner. Thanks to the consistent service, delicious food, and warm atmosphere, we've been coming here for years, and we love bringing new people when we can. 

So when the fam invaded for the holiday, we knew this would be a crowd pleaser. It's Simple. It's Downhome. It's Delicious. The menu isn't complicated BUT it's well above average and there are some fun housemade items that really jump off the page.

Half the table went with the simple options... two eggs and CRISPY bacon. Other orders included a beautiful bowl of yogurt topped with fruit and roasted pecans, blueberry French toast, and chorizo and eggs, and a carne asada plate. No meal here is complete without a side of "scones" and Dad couldn't pass up biscuits and gravy! 

This crowd is so bacon specific I laugh. It's never crispy enough. Getting bacon crunchy without burning it is an artform and Sparks Coffee Shop nailed it. 

My carne asada breakfast was tasty and delicious. The thin pieces of steak were seared on the outside and still juicy in the center with a great marinade. Even with eggs, this is more of a lunch plate to me, though I enjoyed it for breakfast. 

All meals were plenty to share too! 

Sadly, I'd raved about the corned beef hash, and both Dad and I wanted to order it, but they ran out! The server even remarked that they often run out but the chef doesn't want to make extra! I was literally heartbroken and in shock when I heard the news.

The other sad news was the biscuits. I remembered them being fluffy on the inside with a nice crunchy exterior, but these were all fluff. Ah well. 

Sparks still holds a special spot in our hearts and we'll be back soon. It's just that good and the service is just so sweet!

Raise your hand if you've been to Big Ed's!

If you live in Reno Sparks and haven't, make it so immediately. As a local, eating here is a right of passage, and everyone really should. 

As a community, we've only just started to visit the Reno Brewery District regularly, so the first time you visit, you may wonder where you are and what you're doing there.  Ed's sits in a historic neighborhood and it's almost like you can feel that history here. The whole spot is kinda stopped in time, with a classic vibe and menu that are satisfying to the soul. 

I still dream of the breakfast sandwich here. It's so simple. There's nothing special about it. But it's just so good! Perfectly buttered and toasted sourdough, fried over easy eggs, and crispy bacon all come together so nicely. And let's not forget the perfectly seasoned home fries! The best accompaniment to the sandwich.

I am thankful for the community classics. I'm thankful for simple food. I'm thankful owners have preserved this restaurant for us all to enjoy. I'm thankful so many new businesses are opening in this neighborhood and bringing much deserved attention. 

I'm thankful for Big Ed's!

Do you know how many times I've been back to Super Taqueria in the "more than four years" since this last review?

Too many to count, but probably at least between 30-40!

Aside from Sunday, this is a delicious taco stop in South Reno any day if the week. The meats are all succulent, the tortillas tender, and the salsas are perfect to top it all! Prices are fair, and they have churros.

Super Taqueria has been a favorite lunch stop for me and my son. He actually asks me to take him there at least than 2. Our favorites are the al pastor, the lengua, and the chorizo. Perfect combo of salty and spicy! 

My hope is that that is great biz still there on the other side.

Another new discovery in 2014 and a fantastic fixture in our community! Semenza's has been in business since 1980, serving up delicious pizza and wings with ice cold beverages. The current owner, Pablo or J.P. as some call him, has been working here since 1994 and bought the business in 2008! I've been living 2 miles from this place for the 5+ years, driven past it more times than I could possibly count, and yet hadn't set foot in there until last night! 

I came in really late (9PM) and talked with Pablo, got the story, asked how the food was, and asked about their food. At first he joked that it was all mediocre, but you could tell he was proud of it. I told him I was a wing snob, and he modestly told me they were known for them and I was sure to like them. So on his suggestion, I ordered the "Small Special", 1lb of wings and a small 2 topping pizza, to try this place out. 

So how were the wings you ask? Fantastic! These rank in my top 3! Turns out Pablo used to work over at JOX, which serves up some of my favorites, so he knows what's up with wings. The wings were crispy on the outside and juicy on the inside. I ordered the Nitro BBQ, aka Nitro Nutty sauce at Legends,a favorite combo of mine, and these wings were covered in it the best way possible. You could see all the chiles in the sauce, and smell the intense vinegar and chile scented steam coming off of them. These wings rock!

Well what about the pizza right? It's a pizzeria after all. The best way to describe this is it combines all the characteristics of a good pie, in a way you've never had before. The crust is on the thinner side, but there's almost two layers to it. The top is chewy and doughy in all the right ways, but the bottom is cracker thin and crunchy! My pizza had jalapeno and bacon on it, and it was delicious. I've never had a crust like this though anywhere and I'll definitely be back for more. 

I'm so happy that I discovered Semenza's finally, met Pablo, and can proudly tell everyone about it. This is just another one of those Reno institutions that more people should visit. The food is worth the drive, and I can see it being a really fun place to crack some beers and kick it with friends.

Rolled in late afternoon to pick up a few bagels for a special meal. I knew the selection wouldn't be compete, but I figured I could find what I was after.

They had a few of the less popular options left for the day and I asked what a 3-seed Bagel was before landing on poppy and sesame, 3 of each. Or so I thought.

I opened the bag at home today to find three poppy and three 3-seed. Not what I ordered. I was the only one in the shop when I ordered. The cashier didn't seem too enthused to see customers, and she let another employee grab my bagels. Obviously he wasn't listening to our conversation and grabbed the wrong bagels. 

Beyond that, the bagels were pretty underdone. Very lightly colored on the outside, doughy on the inside, with a few spots that seemed not quite cooked through.

This isnt what I've come to love about Truckee Bagel and surprised by the experience. I hope the next time it's back to normal.

I've been a fan of Num Num Boba since I first learned about them from a dear friend. The business owner and her story are awesome, and they make a damn good boba drink too!
