They've got a wacky menu with some awesome combinations. If you're a fan of these drinks, you'll literally never get through it all because she keeps adding to it! Customers make requests and they often end up on the menu. Staff dream something up and it tastes great, it ends up on the menu. 

I mean, they have a mango sticky rice boba drink! Come on!

I am a purist snd I don't love my drinks too sweet, so I'm thrilled they've got the basics covered and make them great! For boba, I like the Okinawa tea. It's got a slight toffee flavor, and at 50% sweetness it's perfect. My kiddo tried the strawberry milk tea with popping strawberry and was in heaven. I also tried a fruit tea with different coconut jellies in it and it was also super refreshing and incredibly beautiful too! 

Best of all, they serve Honey Bakery bao AND HK Egg waffles! 

So stoked a location is open closer to my house because it's just a lot of fun to be there.

I'm a Pho 777 PHONATIC PHO SHO!!! This is the real deal and if you don't believe me, just ask all of the Asians, local and tourists, who fill up the restaurant regularly! I discovered this gem about a year ago, when a friend told me their food tasted just a touch more authentic. That "A" word is all I need to try a new place, and after one bite, my addiction began. I will go out of my way from anywhere to eat their food. 

Being downtown, the first thing you're wondering about is parking. EASY! PRO TIP- FREE AND EASY PARKING is available at the Calneva parking garage right next door on Center St.

Don't expect much in the way of atmosphere, but do expect decent service (a rarity in these places) and great food! 
777 delivers on all the favorites but their menu goes beyond to include dishes that aren't found on others or are prepared with a flavor uniquely 777, such as the General Tso's Chicken with hints of allspice (I know not Vietnamese!) or their Grilled Pork Chop over rice. 

But I'm stuck on their spring rolls (which have mint and other herbs that add something special), #21 and #33. 

The first time I ordered #21 I had no idea what I was getting into.The menu said egg noodles with roast pork, calamari, shrimp, meatloaf, and fresh vegetables. Turns out all of this is served in a bowl and topped with crispy fried shallots and a small amount of a savory sauce, with the delicious hot broth on the side. When the broth and the savory sauce mix, it's amazing. It takes me forever to eat this because I mix it all together slowly and savor every bite.

#33 is a dish I've never seen on any other menu in Reno. It's a bed of steamed rice with bbq pork, dry shredded pork, and a beancurd stick (thin beancurd skin wrapped around ground pork and deep fried), served with pickled vegetables and the sweet fish sauce. I mix the shredded pork into the rice to eat it with every bite of the bbq pork. The beancurd stick becomes almost like a side dish. 

Give it a try and join me in becoming a Pho 777 PHONATIC.

Silver Peak was a pioneer on Reno's craft brewing scene and they deserve a lot of credit for that! From the Red Roadster to the Peavine Porter, all the way to the infamous Hooch, Silver Peaks brews are legendary, well known and well loved. I for one am a big fan of the Amber, but I also love exploring their seasonal suds too, of which there are many! For once, choosing a rating is really tough for me. For me this is a solid 3.5 stars, which means it's better than A-OK but doesn't make me a fan. See if this review were just for the beer, it would be a solid 4 stars, but the food has never really bowled me over. So I guess I'll round up to 4 stars.

There are some solid items on the menu, along with a few misses in my opinion. My orders have always been standard, and I've enjoyed the nachos, a large shareable portion perfect for picking, with your choice of meat, black beans, pico, sour cream and cheese. I've also really enjoyed the barley crusted chicken sandwich, the lamb burger, and their pizza's aren't bad either. Unfortunately anytime I've strayed from these items, I've been somewhat disappointed. Don't get me wrong, this stuff is A-OK, but I've never been really impressed. Misses for me have included overly sweet Vietnamese style beef sandwich that I had to drown in jalapeños and sriracha, over sauced and under fried wings, soggy fish and chips and everything in between. 

There's so much opportunity here. We're a community that loves our local craft beer, and we need some great food to go with it! I'll keep coming back to Silver Peak for more of their great brews, but I'll keep wishing the food would measure up.

Semi private event for 25? They got it covered and managed the whole thing well from start to finish. Everyone was smiling, chatting and enjoying the evening together without a worry about the food or the drink.

I was a lucky guest this evening and got the see the whole thing go down. The Noble team had the patio set with plates, napkins, water and glasses plus all the condiments you could need, and they stationed a great looking buffet table just inside the restaurant for everyone to enjoy. 

I liked seeing it setup in tiers with the pizzas up high and the apps and salads below.

They were generous with the sauces and dressings too, so no ranch shortages occurred. 

I mainly made my way through a dozen wings, salad, and some of the polenta fries and meatballs they had out for apps. The ranch at Noble could make a shoe taste good, but these dishes were delicious! 

I loved the big NV shaped fire pit table on the patio! So great to gather around for a meal or just to relax with a cocktail.

Oh yeah! Almost forgot! The bartender was on point! The Tutto Bene #2 was fantastic. The old fashioned delicious. He seemed on top of timing and took great care with the ingredients too. 

Shoutout to the female rocking the front of house for being so sweet to all the little ones and making sure the food got packed up and passed out too. She really kept the party together.

Reno... get in here will ya?!?

My Pie will always be Reno's first BYO pizza, and IMHO, the best. Insanely consistent. Solid flavors. Choice toppings. Friendly service and super reasonable prices. 

They have a full menu of great combos to choose from, but of course, you can build your own. I usually start from one of the menu items and do a little customizing. It ends up some sorta pepperoni, sausage and ricotta combo. Crust is pressed out fresh and bakes up nice and airy, but still light and crisp. All together it makes a good pie, perfectly sized for one real hungry person or combined with a salad, it's the perfect meal for two.

They also have a gluten free crust for anyone interested, and it's actually pretty tasty too!

I was sad when this spot closed but I'm excited it has reopened. I hope people catch on real soon because this place is too good to go!

I ate pig stomach and I liked iiiiit. Hope my wife doesn't mind it!

That's how that song went right? Ok. Maybe I made it up, but it's true! The spicy mustard greens with PIG STOMACH are the truth too. I actually never thought I could stomach the idea of eating any part of the digestive system, but I'm always a willing partner in crime when it comes to gastronomic adventures. So when dad came to visit and wanted to get weird in the food department, I wasn't going to say no, and I'm glad I didn't.

What surprised me most was that there was zero "funk" in this dish. No aroma or flavor to speak of here, just some funky looking protein that probably could pass for very tender squid if you didn't say anything about it. 

When it came to the greens they'd been braised to perfection. in a spicy and vinegary sauce studded with pickled jalapeños. They use the whole green from tender tip to the tougher stalk, all of which comes together to be a medley of delightful textures, and a perfect topping for rice or punctuating the rich flavors of the dishes here!

Another winner was the homestyle tofu! A blend of baked or fried tofu soaked in a rich sauce and wok fried with a melange of fresh vegetables. Flavor wise it's a tough dish to describe, but the sauce is super deep with lots of rich roasted garlic essence that I've come to find is a hallmark of the food here. A definite must order dish! 

I love exploring the menu here. It never disappoints and I normally find something exciting and new to enjoy on each visit, along with revisiting some old favorites too!

According to @jontaffer, bars that serve food bring in substantially more revenue and profit because patrons stay longer and spend more! I'm a prime example of this, and so are many of my friends, especially when it comes to Happy Hour. See a bar with no food will probably get 2 drinks out of me before I feel the need to feed. But a bar that has food, will probably get 3, plus my food business. 

Just like a lot of other Yelpers in Reno, and people around the country, I prefer dining on small plates, cocktails, and craft beer. I'll go out of my way to visit a bar with great cocktails/beers that also serves up small shareable plates and appetizers, or great bar food. Gas Lamp definitely fits the bill here, and I've been in a few times, and brought friends too! 

I really like the bottled beer selection here, I tried the Mad River Steelhead Double IPA for a whopping $3, and according to Ashley, the wine pours are nothing to sneeze at! But what I love is that half priced app selection. I'm a sucker for BIG AZZ SCRIMPS, and Gas Lamp delivers! These are cooked perfectly with the right amount of char flavor to make my mouth water. The salmon carpaccio and the tuna tartare are also not to be missed! 

Now munching on half priced apps and discounted drinks, you might think my bill would be minuscule, but I'd bet that I run an average check of $20/pp every time. I'm seeing this kind of menu more and more, and that makes me happy. I just wish more of our great bars would investigate food with their drinks, because then I'd have a lot more options!

A cocktail is only as good as the sum of its parts. Each ingredient, imparts its own nuanced flavors, and when arranged in proper proportion, creates balance and harmony that amount to the signature of that particular drink. A great cocktail has a signature that calls you back again, and again.

Death & Taxes is a place that brings these cocktails to life. Using house made syrups, bitters, infusions, and a vast library of spirits and liqueurs at their disposal, the bartenders here can put together a version of a classic that will transport you back in time, or serve up a modern concoction that will leave you thinking about the last sip all night long. 

The ambiance is dark, yet modern, and the glow of the low lights seem to illuminate the bottles at the back of the bar, making them reminiscent of the vessels you may find in a witches lair. And though there may be the occasional flame, and possibly some smoke, there's no black magic behind this bar. Just quality Cocktailing. 

Don't mistake the aloof nature of the staff for anything other than the fact they're devoting the necessary attention to their craft. They strive to serve up a great drink to every guest that takes a seat.

The menu changes seasonally, and the unique bottle stock rotates as well, so you're always in for a treat. If you're feeling lucky you can give the bartender a bit of direction and a whole lot of leeway and you're sure to find a winner.

Death & Taxes is a cocktail bar for the cocktail enthusiast. Leave the training wheels at home.

This can't be my first review for Batch. We've been coming for years because my wife loves the paleo cupcakes, so they make the perfect occasional surprise or birthday treat for her. Heck. I love em too! And ever since my now three year old son learned what a cupcake was, we've had three people that love them in the house! 

What's not to love about decadent, rich, deeply flavored and and pseudo healthy cupcakes? If I handed you one of these you'd never know they were paleo. These are all that and more, and don't worry, you'll still feel guilty eating them! 

But if you can't imagine they have the same ingredients as a traditional cupcake, Batch makes those too. Today the flavors were awesome. My son loves the strawberry cupcake, which is bursting with real strawberry flavor. I wanted him to want the blueberry cheesecake cupcake  topped with cream cheese icing and a real blueberry, and filled with blueberry too! 

I always want to leave with just one cupcake but it never happens. Today I got lucky and only got two, which made for two happy family members and a superstar dad and husband!

Put a lil' south in your mouth y'all at M&M's! Ok. This place ain't that cliched south shiz, but rather a rock solid representation of what Southern Hospitality is and should be always. 

This family run business has bounced around over the years, and is now located next to local legend Yellow Sub, in a rather rundown shopping center that is totally not fitting of the warm, rich, cute, quaint, comfortable and homey interior of this restaurant. Dark wood tables, large, cushy high back booths, and several 4 tips fill the main space, with even more seating in an adjacent room as well. This is easily the nicest space this restaurant has ever occupied. 

Regardless of where they've been though, the food has remained consistently delicious, southern home cooking made with lots of love! Gieshula and Mitch are the owners and they're wonderful passionate people genuinely excited to share their southern pride with you! You can't help but feel welcome from the moment you walk into this cute cafe, and that's just one of the reasons I'm handing out a Five Star review here. 

Food is the second reason for the big FIVE. For lunch I tried the combo with fried chicken wings, smoked ribs, fried catfish, and a side of southern greens! Everything was fried to perfection, but I felt like the catfish batter was a tad salty, and the greens were amazingly tender and well seasoned, and with a small dash of pepper vinegar, I was in heaven. We started the meal with a basket of fried chicken livers that I topped with true crystal hot sauce! Crispy, crunchy exterior with a tender creamy interior added up to southern fried perfection. Along with that we had a side order of a fried chicken breast and a thigh. Holy wow! This is TRUE Southern Fried Chicken! Proper stuff! Well seasoned coating, moist, hot and juicy inside, making you want to enjoy every last crumb in the basket!

Finally, M&M's treats you like family and has some serious pride in what they serve to each guest. So the third, and most important reason they're nabbing FIVE stars is simply service. You can tell they have fans and want a whole lot more, and they added a few today.

Southern Fried Paradise at M&M's Southern Cafe! I'll be back, and next time I'm getting my hands on that sweet potato pie!

Love seeing COVID compliance taken to heart, and Pizanos had this on lock.

I popped in for a quick bite while tooling around downtown this weekend. There aren't too many spots that serve slices, but Pizanos is one of them! There was one couple enjoying a pie in the restaurant when I visited. I liked that they had the counter blocked off so you were appropriately distanced from the cashier, staff was masked, and, as expected, they had sneeze guards in place to separate guests from food too.

The pies offered by the slice were on display, and there was a sign showing what they offer different daily. I kept it simple with a cheese slice, which was carefully taken from the pizza and placed in the oven to heat up. When I saw it, I thought the slice was adequately sized, but when it rang up $3.79 (before a 20% tip) my opinion changed. The crust wasn't thin or thick, it was floppy with no real structure, not much sauce but a lot of cheese, and nothing about it was particularly premium. 

Slices are never a good way to judge a pizza place, but I'm of the opinion they should be enough to get you interested in returning. After tasting this slice I decided it was an A OK slice of pie but not enough to get me back for the full monty. 

That said, Pizanos has a serious sense of humor and I kinda want a "Legalize Marinara" shirt!

When I think of charming, I think of Stone House Cafe. From the minute you walk in, there's a sense of warmth in the air that cannot be denied. It's the kind of place that says sit, stay a while, we're happy to have you. It's no wonder people come here to linger over brunch or lunch with great friends and wonderful conversation. 

This vibe carries over to the servers, who seem driven to make sure you enjoy your time spent in the restaurant. They are informative and accommodating, and most of all, friendly. And the menu, is full of the same inviting warmth featuring comfort food classics and new riffs on them.

On this visit, we were there for brunch to send a great friend off on her next adventure. There were 12 of us, a very large party for the size of this restaurant, but we'd made reservations in advance and were seated promptly.  I ordered the "Biscuits and Gravy A la Diabla" which was the biscuits topped with house made spicy chorizo, smothered in a chipotle country style gravy. It was served with two eggs and I opted for the veggie hash. My GF had the Smoked Salmon Benedict. Perfectly poached eggs on top of hot smoked salmon on a delicious english muffin. She opted to get hers with fruit (which we found out was a $3 up charge?). 

My only complaint was that I could tell my order, and the other 2 orders of this special, had been sitting in the window far too long. The gravy was glazed over and it was generally lukewarm, though my eggs (over easy) were cooked perfectly. 

Each time I return to Stone House I wonder why I don't think of it more often. With such charm and character, great food, and a cool atmosphere, it's a real winner!

I take the opinions of the Yelp community very seriously, and I hate it when my experiences don't align with those of Yelper's opinions I value. I also don't like having to write negative reviews, but our experience needs to be shared, and unfortunately it wasn't 3 star A-OK. 

Ashley has a severe food allergy to fish roe i.e. ikura, tobiko, beluga caviar etc. Food allergies are serious, and not being careful can send a customer to the hospital in no time, and most restaurants are incredibly sensitive and take necessary precautions. As responsible diners, we do our part when trying a new sushi restaurant by arriving at off peak hours (in this case 8PM on a Monday), sitting at the bar, and taking time to the explain the allergy to the chefs before ordering anything, and request that fresh gloves, a clean cutting board, and a clean knife be used to prepare her food separately from those being prepared with fish roe. On top of that, she carries an epi-pen, knowing the food is prepared in the presence of the allergen, and accidents can happen.

So we arrive to find one table paying their bill, making us the only customers with three chefs at the bar! We start off by telling Alberto about the allergy, and he happily set up a brand new cutting board and knife at Victor's station to our left. New setup, separate chef, we're off to a great start! They ask how we heard about them, so we tell them people on Yelp love them so we had to try it. They were stoked! 

I had a big smile on my face now, and I ordered some nigiri from Alberto, which included tobiko with a quail egg. He turned to an Asian chef next to him to have it made. Odd. So thinking we she was having her stuff made at the cleaned station on his opposite site, Ashley asked Alberto for several pieces of nigiri. Alberto gave us a funny look and asked Ashley "So you want nigiri?" "Yes" says Ashley. And he surprisingly leans over and tells the Asian chef the order AUDIBLY INSTRUCTING HIM TO USE A CLEAN BOARD because of the allergy.

So what does Mr. Asian Chef do? He tells Alberto it's ok, rinses his finger tips in the sink, wipes down his board with cleaning rag used at his station through service, and proceeds to prepare her food on the same board he'd just done mine! He hands Ashley a plate of salmon nigiri, and both us and Alberto are uncomfortable. 

Concerned that the clean board is sitting lonesome and unused, I stand up and give the benefit of the doubt, asking if this was prepared on a new board. This guy looks me in the eye and LIES. One look at the nigiri showed a tobiko egg sitting right on top, clear as day. So I let him know, in a not so friendly tone, how he almost sent her to the hospital. He retreated to the back and was never see again. Fine by me! I also saved that piece of nigiri to show the owner/manager, who I later spoke with about the situation. 

Last night's experience was 100% inappropriate, disrespectful, and showed a complete disregard for customer safety and well-being. That chef's actions are inexcusable, and he knowingly endangered a customer's life. Alberto and Victor tried desperately to save this experience and encourage our return, but you can't recover from this. The owner/manager comped the miso soup, edamame, and sake Ashley had, which was a nice gesture, but he didn't seem all too concerned with what happened and that is disappointing. 

At the end of it all, the food was mediocre, rice tasted unseasoned, fish had an older texture and the sushi bar looked like remnants of the past week, the chefs clearly aren't all trained because our chef didn't make anything we ate and neither of them would make nigiri, the salmon skin I ordered crispy was soggy and oily, and when I asked them to make me something off the menu, I was told they have to "follow the rules". Well the pictures and other reviews say something totally different. I was hoping to find a hidden gem in Sommerset, one I'd head to repeatedly, and I'm really sad that I didn't have the experience that my fellow Yelpers did.

A massive sushi platter is the key to my heart, so naturally it was the meal of choice for Valentine's Day 2021!

399 did such a great job for my birthday so naturally we called them again. They're currently running a great promotion with a sliding scale or discounts based on how much you order. We spent about $100 and got a 20%-30% discount, which was awesome!

The nigiri was fresh. The scallop nigiri was amazing! The rolls were packed with fish. Check out the pic of the roll! The price was solid for the amount and quality we received. Best of all, the ownership was super friendly and gracious. 

399 deserves your support. Give them a try. It'll be a refreshing and new sushi experience.

How? How is this even possible? How have I not reviewed one of my all-time favorite breweries in our entire region? For shame! 

I stopped drinking beer years ago (health reasons) but it doesn't mean I've stopped TASTING it. And when I do settle in to taste some local beer, my palate always pushes me toward IMBIB.

Why? IMBIB hits the sweet (and sour) spot for me. They produce beers in old world styles of brewing, those rich in history and technique, that drive the modern brewing scene we enjoy today. While staying true to forms, they are always finding exciting ways to put their own touch on them. 

I am particularly fond of their Berliner Weisses, especially those featuring local seasonal fruit, their Flemmish sour, and many of their one off experimentals. They put the time in to develop these recipes, and the results show. Multiple big wins at GABF for them, shows they're loved far beyond our little community here.

IMBIB is also one of the breweries that have taken COVID precautions to the extreme. They care so much about our community it hurts, and are constantly giving of themselves! 

Now's our turn. ORDER ONLINE. CURBSIDE PICKUP. DRINK LOCAL.

Bab Café comes through again with a fast, fresh, delicious and refreshing lunch! 

I absolutely crave Bab bowls! Today I had an appt in The Summit with just enough time to grab lunch, so naturally I stopped in here! This time I got the beef bulgogi Classic Bab. I love the combo of lightly steamed veggies, fluffy rice, and richly marinated meat. I regret forgetting to add the chopped kimchi because that was delicious last year.

This go round I made a conscious decision to reduce the waste from this favorite meal of mine by saucing the bowl vs dip the bites in little cups of sauce. I've always felt it was wasteful, but dipping makes it so interactive! I thought I'd miss it but using the sauces as seasonings helped me focus on the food and flavors all together.

They just added some new lightly battered deep fried proteins as well, which makes the Bab bowl and entirely different experience! 

Writing this review literally has me wanting another. Thanks a lot!

Doughboys donated like 4,000 donuts or something today for our teachers! 

If that's not enough reason to eat a donut here, I'll give you another. The Apple fritter. 

Yea. I've told you about it before but I'm saying it again because it's just that good! My mom is in town visiting and she snuck out of the house with my son for a little donut date. Luckily for me she brought one home and made my weekend extra sweet. 

I must say the raised blueberry donut was a new one on me and it was great too! Usually I would assume it's artificial blueberry type flavor but this seemed anything but and I appreciate it. Really really yum!

Great. Now I want a donut. Go get one for me!

Swab the deck! Walk the plank! Shiver me timbers! Do you ever get those days when you feel you'd just like to join Blackbeard and his band of scurvy scoundrels aboard the Jolly Roger? Well I do. Not sure why though. Maybe I secretly want to be a pirate and ravage the seven seas. At least that might explain why I love the letter "R" so much. But I digress.

Looks like I might have found my happy place here, though I'm not sure what they'd think if I waltzed in with an eyepatch on. The place looks and feels like an old ship with the wheelhouse, the masts, the ropes, cargo nets, and more, and the staff is dressed to match. There's no doubt the decor here is kitschy and old school, but it's the kind of kitsch that once made Reno great and that I personally love! 

And the staff and service are as classic as the decor! Attentive, friendly and uniformed to fit right in on board, this crew will make sure your voyage is safe and pleasurable. They start you off with sourdough bread and butter. Why? Because every meal from back then started that way and some things should never change. 

I ordered up the combination pan roast upon the recommendation of my friends. Oysters, shrimp, and crab in a decadent creamy broth with wine, fresh cracked pepper, and I swore I tasted a little bit of anise flavoring from some pernot. The seafood was cooked gently to tender perfection by the broth, and everything was delicious! I brought leftovers home, along with some extra bread, and ate them for breakfast the next morning. Don't judge me! 

 To finish the meal, they bring a display tray of desserts right to the table! I swear it's been a lifetime since that's happened to me, but it brought back so many great childhood memories of me begging my parents to let me have dessert! The carrot cake looked tasty, but so did everything else, and I was too full to even attempt a bite. 

Apparently this place is a staple in the community... that people are ALL TOO quiet about. I'm so glad I had the chance to come check it out. You should too!

A long long time ago, I can still remember when the tacos here used to make me sing. 

The Al pastor it made me shiver. Chorizo never failed to deliver. Lengua was so tender, it made me want to surrender.

But tonight's tacos had me singin... Bye Bye Tacos El Rey. You've got menu that I love, but your foods just ok. I wish it weren't so, and I could still sing your praise. But the tacos just ain't the same!

Seriously, this place used to have my favorite Al Pastor in town, but tonight it was dry and pretty fatty. The asada had no seasoning or color, and was also very fatty too. The best taco was the chorizo, but that ones really hard to mess up.

Bottom line is , for $1 each, these are just fine. But they're not great and may leave you wanting more.

I often hear that our locally owned casino's offer some great dining options, but that locals feel they can be inconvenient to access. I've been thinking about this a lot lately, having spent some time inside quite a few of them recently, aI think that this is just a misconception. Most seem to be laid out in a way that puts the restaurants pretty close to main points of entry. Purple Parrot is a perfect example!

To get to the Purple Parrot, just park in the Virginia St. lot of the Atlantis, walk across the street, and enter the building. You'll pretty much walk right into the restaurant, where you'll find great diner faire like eggs, waffles, omelets etc.

The service here is friendly and prompt and the food arrives quickly. I had a cup of coffee, two eggs (over easy) with a grilled ham steak, hash browns (extra crispy of course), and a biscuit. The eggs were perfectly cooked with nice runny yolks (the way I like em!), the ham steak had just the right amount of char, and the hash browns were crispy perfection! My friend had a mushroom omelet, which was enormous, filled with mushrooms and cheese, and way more food than she could handle. 

That's just the way breakfast should be! Enough to tide you over to lunch or beyond, and it never hurts when it can be lunch too! When we were all done, I walked out the door just a few steps from the restaurant, crossed the street, and was in my car in no time. Purple Parrot will definitely be on my list of quick hits in the future.

Elevated tacos have hit Reno in force and I'm not complaining. Tacos are such a wonderful platform for flavor, and seeing how each chef puts their own spin on it is always fun.

Yelpers have been raving about Mexcal for a while now, and I was excited to learn that Renee, the talented chef from Hard Water House, is both an owner of this hot spot and the culinary mind behind the great menu. I was also happy to see they have a fairly extensive bar program to go along with the tacos too! 

First the service. Ana was our service and she was absolutely fabulous. Personable, friendly, happy to share her opinions and she was so sweet and pleasant. If she wanted to be my friend, I wouldn't be upset at all! 

Drinks... we ordered a Paloma and the Jefe Viejo (old fashioned) but I subbed mezcal for tequila. Their version of a Paloma isn't the same as the one I have in my head, which is simply tequila and fresh grapefruit. It was kind of disappointing because the menu doesn't say they use flavored soda, it just said soda, which was assumed to be soda water. The drink was far too sweet with almost no grapefruit flavor. My old fashion came out wrong the first time, but the remake was what I'd hoped for, just slightly diluted due to the use of bar ice. From a purely cocktail standpoint, solid 3-3.5.

Food... Chips and salsa trio was a hit. I don't know what that Salsa Amarillo is but I want a gallon of it, as well as both red salsas. They were clearly made with a lot of attention to detail and very good. 

Wifey had her eye on the pulpo taco and the shrimp taco. Both came LOADED with protein, in fact too much to eat it as a taco. No complaints about too much octopus. The shrimp were just ok though. Both were not bad, just not remarkable. 

The clear winner of the night was the duck tostada. The duck was so tender and had a delicious crispy texture from time on the plancha. I loved every bite. 

Biggest let down was the mushroom taco. If you've had the mushroom taco at the other elevated taco spot nearby, this one doesn't even compare. They use cremini mushrooms here versus wild mushrooms, and it seems they're just lightly seasoned and sauteed before being piled into the tortilla. It didn't have any of the depth of the other one I've come to literally dream about from the other restaurant. 

To sum it up, service was 5-star fabulous thanks to Ana, food and drink a solid 3.5 for me. 

Mexcal is a great addition to our scene!

Sushi and Pho are like politics and religion in our city. 

For more than five years, THE ORIGINAL Sushi Pier was my favorite sushi stop in town. I was so fiercely loyal I missed opportunities to enjoy sushi elsewhere and even lost friends and followers too.

Nowadays I visit about once or twice a year. The experience is still good, the staff is still friendly and the combos are just so nostalgic for me. BUT it's just not as good as I remember. 

Today I ran through my usual nigiri which includes salmon, yellowtail, seared tuna, Mickey and unagi. For good measure I threw in some snapper too. I found most of the fish to be a little tough or a little too soft, but nothing that had bad flavor or questionable freshness. 

The upside down shrimp here are the very best in town. The raw bay scallop Mix in the middle is sweet, soft and creamy, a nice counterpoint to the shrimp texture.

I also had mussels and upside tempura crab, dishes I've always loved here. Sadly the mussels were dry and tough. The crab was good but the fry on it wasn't great. It was greasy, somewhat soggy, and generally hard to eat. The spicy tuna on top wasn't the best either. 

The service here has improved a lot though, and that's exciting. Empties are cleared quickly. Waters are refilled. The chefs are on top of requests. All of that adds up to a good experience for me.

Will I be back? You know it! They aren't a local fave for nothing. Definitely worth your time!

Need flowers? Trader Joe's is the spot!

Think I'm kidding? I'm not. Best quality. Most beautiful. Super affordable. Always impressive. 

The selection ranges from individual roses to exceptionally colorful seasonal arrangements. They always have some exotic looking flowers and they even have individual flowers you can buy to assemble your own  bouquets too!

My wife, mother, dinner hosts, and many more that have been recipients of these flowers have all been impressed.

If you're buying bouquets anywhere else you're overpaying and probably not getting quite the same quality.

Gosh darn it these things are soooooo goood! 

With my dad in town the Asian food crawl continued with a special stop at Honey Bakery for best baked Baozi in all the land. The dough is warm, pillowy and sweet and the fillings incredibly rich and complimentary. 

Knowing my dad could never decide what to order, and knowing the owner often has somewhat limited patience, I advised dad to walk in and order three of everything. After some quick math he said "Michael. That's 5 dozen buns!" To which I replied, "Then go with two of each!" 

And that's pretty much what we did, which meant we got to try a few new ones in the process! 

The new favorite has got to be ham and corn. It has been forever since I had one of these and they are delicious. The corn is incredibly sweet and it's just a delight to eat. 

The not so favorites were the tuna bun and the sausage bun. Tuna wasn't bad, I just don't see a reason to repeat it. The sausage bun should've been a winner, except they're using a Weiner now instead of traditional Chinese sausage, which I'm fairly certain used to top this one. 

Favorites remain bbq pork, ham and green onion, all the chickens (curry, mushroom, teriyaki), coconut pineapple bun and the egg custard bun!

If you haven't been, get your buns in here!

FREE CRAFT COCKTAIL WITH YELP CHECK-IN @PeppermillReno's Biscotti's! Do I have your attention? GOOD! 

Cocktails at Biscotti's might seem odd, but if you look closely at the menu, you'll see the fingerprints of the Peppermill's Mixologist, Ilona Martinez, all over it. If you've read any of my other reviews of the Peppermill's bars and restaurants, you'd know that I'm a HUGE fan of their cocktail program and her recipes. Not only are her drinks well balanced and incredibly delicious, but she devotes countless hours to training the staff that make these drinks for guests on a regular basis so that each one is consistent.

This was the first time I was able to take advantage of this amazing check-in offer. Craft cocktails here are around $12, and we tried the Oaxacan Holiday (El Silencio Mezcal, Mandarin Napoleon Liqueur, Orgeat Syrup, and Fresh Lime Juice served over crushed ice) and the Pineapple Infused Patron Margarita (Infused Pineapple and Vanilla Patron Silver Tequila, Fresh Lime Juice, and Agave Nectar served over or frozen). Both drinks were excellent, and taking $24 off the bill made them just a little bit sweeter! 

Peppermill calls BIscotti's casual dining, but I'd argue that's only in the sense of the atmosphere because the food and service is absolutely top notch. Jay, our server, was a fantastic ambassador for the restaurant and property. He had a smile the entire time, answered all questions, predicted needs, and visited the table on the most perfect of intervals, insuring a beautiful dining experience. Honestly, I haven't had a service experience like this in a LONG time, and I was extremely impressed.

Last, but certainly not least, the food! It's REALLY freaking good! I've enjoyed the patty melt both times I've dined here, and it's easily one of the best I've ever had. It starts with a half pound certified angus beef burger (NOTE: HALF POUND is so impressive. I don't know why they label it 8 oz. on the menu), topped with a pile of perfectly caramelized onions, sautéed mushrooms, melted swiss cheese, and whiskey aioli, all between thick cut, toasted marble rye bread. 

The bread is substantial, standing up to the all the goodness between it; and the kitchen cooks the burger to your liking, and nails it every time! 

Just like Lo's cocktails, Biscotti's is an incredibly well balanced dining experience. It hits all the high notes you want when dining out, and leaves the fancy pants stuff to it's big brother, Bimini!

Did you know India Kabab was the SECOND Indian restaurant in Reno? It's true, it opened in 2006, when owners Bishan and Gurdeep moved to Reno, and at the time there was only one other in the community. That restaurant has since closed, making India Kabab the longest running Indian restaurant in the area, and that's with great reason! 

15 years is an eternity in restaurant years, so clearly they must be doing something right, and it's not just the buffet. Aside from the food, it's worth noting that Bishan and Gurdeep are amongst the most generous, kind, and caring people you will ever meet. Their hospitality and care extends beyond the restaurant, into the community. During the pandemic they gave away meals to hundreds of people without question. They're the first to jump up and lend a hand whenever called upon. 

Their menu is broad and deep, offering dishes that cover several regions of India. If you wanted to, it would be possible to visit for a year or more without ever repeating the same order! In fact, there are so many dishes on the menu, it's amazing they all come from the small kitchen in the back of the restaurant. 

On our last visit we ordered several new to us dishes due to a dairy allergy. It's actually a fun and easily accommodated challenge in the realm of Indian food because there are many in India who are vegan. 

We can't visit without the Bainghan Bartha, which is a stewed eggplant dish that's out of this world. New to us this time was Tadka Dal, a yellow lentil dish that was immediately added to our regular rotation. Murg curry, Vindaloo and Rogan Josh are also favorites. There are far too many to list.

Don't forget the bread either! Paratha, Roti, and of course, Naan are all on point here! 

India Kabab is our household favorite, and it's sure to be yours too.

With so many places to get pho in town, it's really hard to try them all. So before I set foot through the door, I consult Yelp to see what they're serving up. I'm always on the lookout for authentic Viet dishes that go beyond the basics of the usual pho combinations and cold noodle dishes, because that usually means their food has that even those dishes will have extra special flavor. 

When Pho Kietzke hit the scene, thanks to Esteban P's great photos and Steve T's review, I saw promise. For starters, Mi Kho was on the menu, a dish I've only found on 2 others in town. This is my go-to at 777, a really interesting dish comprised of a bowl of warm egg noodles with shrimp, calamari, roast pork, lettuce, shallots, bean sprouts and cha lua (Viet meatloaf), dressed lightly with a peppery brown sauce and served with a bowl of hot broth on the side for dipping and slurping. Ever since I discovered this dish, I've been in love with it, and thanks to Steve, I knew they had it, and that meant I needed to go check it out. 

At Pho Kietzke they offer you the option of rice or egg noodles with the Mi Kho, which is different. The server asked me, and I said egg noodles without hesitation. He paused and looked at me funny for a second before asking if I was sure that's what I wanted. I insisted, and asked why he thought I'd made a mistake. He said not many people order it that way, which begged me to ask "Most non-Viets right?" We both laughed and he went to place the order. 

Along with the Mi Kho, we ordered a rare steak pho and an order of spring rolls. The spring rolls were fair, but lacked that herbaceous flavor from the mint basil and cilantro the really good ones have, but they were made with the delicious Viet BBQ pork, and that added a nice texture and flavor. The peanut sauce was really good though. A little of the sambal chili paste and it was on point for me! 

The Mi Kho arrived, and as usual, it was chock full of goodies. The egg noodles were cooked very well, offering that slightly toothsome chew that makes them perfect for the dish. The seafood was pretty well cooked, and along with the pork, they put chicken in as well. The sauce was slightly different, and the broth served with it was on the lighter side, and not as complex in flavor as others I've had. What I love about this dish is that typically the flavor builds as you enjoy the dish because the various ingredients sit in the broth adding their own essences. I think I was so hungry that I ate so quickly and didn't allow this to happen. Overall, this version was good, but it's not my favorite version in town.

We were the only table in the place, so we joked with our server through the meal, eventually asking him to have the kitchen whip us up something he'd enjoy with his family at home. He kept telling us he wasn't a big fan of Viet food, which surprised us, but we kept pushing. Eventually he came back asking if we wanted to try a beef dish, the same one Steve reviewed, and we passed. I was a bit sad to see them not up to the challenge on this one. 

I'd rate the experience here a solid 3.5 stars. I'll be back to try some other dishes soon.

4 stars for stellar pours on premium whiskey! Not what I expected walking into this new wine bar in South Reno, but I was happy to see a decent selection of spirits, as well as craft beer, and of course wine, being poured for all the happy patrons here! (Can you tell this review is for the bar?)

Ashley and I decided to go get a drink to celebrate a few exciting life moments and the holidays, and thought it might be fun to check out a new place at the same time! I had no idea what to expect walking in here, and was surprised to find a beautiful dining room that felt like a wine cellar, a nice retail area with their famous gift baskets, a separate bar area with high top tables and TVs, and even what I'll call an atrium, with large roll up doors that can be opened in the summer converting it into a patio space. Just about every seat in the house was taken too, so we grabbed two seats at the bar. The bartender was totally personable, conversational, and very attentive to his guests. He let me taste various beers and spirits before I selected the Michter's Small Batch, and Ashley settled on the Four Graces Pinot. The whiskey was good! The wine, on the other hand, had something just a little off. I mentioned it to the bartender and he was happy to pour another glass, but Ashley declined. 

We had some friends meet up, and transferred our tab to a larger table in the bar. The server here just wasn't as strong as the bartender was, and it definitely changed the overall experience for us. Her personality aside, she told us that we could select any bottle from the store and they'd happily pour it for us at the table. That was awesome because the menu is a little limited. 

At the end of our experience we went to pay and were told our gift card was only good at the other location. I was shocked, and requested to speak with the manager, who came to the table and explained the same thing to me. The two businesses are owned by the same person, so I encouraged him to pick up the phone and call the owner to find out how to handle this situation. Lucky for us, Mr. Dennis Banks was at the restaurant that night and came to the table, apologized and exchanged our gift card for cash. 

The way that all went down made me very happy. I know I put the manager in a tough spot, but it's how you handle that moment that makes you great. He did an excellent job making sure we left as happy guests, and because of that I will return.

After all, we still have a whole menu to try!

It's been a while since I've tried somewhere new, so with a friend moving to Chicago, this was the perfect occasion.  We decided on Compere Lapin, Nina Lacompe's new restaurant.  Chef Lacompte is a recent runner up of Top Chef.  Her background and influence is mostly Caribbean, so I was excited to try what I thought would be some interesting flavors.  

I wasn't disappointed.

Atmosphere: A-
I loved the atmosphere.  Rich browns, interesting lighting, exposed brick.  Had a prohibition era type feel to it.  I did find it to get pretty loud at times.  They should probably invest in some cushioning underneath the tables.

Service: B+
This is a tough one to rate.  This is a new restaurant, and they're trying really hard to make you feel welcome, and give good service.  The problem?  They're trying just a little too hard.  3 different people came to our table 4 separate times to see how we were doing.  This is in addition to the standard times where our waiter inquired when dropping things off or picking things up from our table.  It was just too much, and felt overbearing.  It seemed to occur each time we got deep into conversation.  If they could just simmah down some with this, I could give an A on service.  Our server Chris was really nice, and gave a great suggestion for an appetizer to share.

Drinks:  A
There is a great selection of craft cocktails if that's your jam.  The prices range from $10-$14.  I don't remember the name of the drink my friend ordered, but I tried it, and it was very tasty!  I was in the mood for some summer bubbly, so I ordered a cava rose.  It was very good.

Food:  A-
The food was really good.  You're started off with 2 small homemade biscuits with honey, chive, and bacon butter.  ZOMG!  Sooo yummy!  After our waiter saw how much we loved (and devoured them), he promptly brought us more!  At the suggestion of our waiter, we started off sharing the smoked tuna tartare. It was fresh and delicious, and a perfect amount for sharing.  We decided to share two entrees.  We ordered the crawfish pasta and the curried goat with gnocchi.  The crawfish pasta was good, but it wasn't great.  I really prefer a cream type sauce with my pasta.  It had a good amount of spice, was flavorful, and it was cooked right, it just wasn't something I'd order again.  My friend really liked it.  Now the curried goat was fantastic.  I'm a sucker for curry, and this was no exception.  Tender goat in a flavorful gravy with homemade gnocchi and topped with tomatoes and cilantro.  I was slopping that up with mah biscuit.  For dessert, the kitchen sent out a surprise complimentary dessert of horchatta panna cotta with berry sorbet over a graham cracker crust and all topped with an assortment of melon balls.  It was light and flavorful, and the perfect end to a biscuit, pasta, and gnocchi meal.

Value:  B+
This place isn't cheap, but I didn't expect it to be either.  I'm ok with higher prices if you're putting out quality food, which they are.  My only complaint was that the entree portion sizes were a tad on the small size.  Had I not had the biscuits, and shared an appetizer, I'm not sure the entree would've been sufficient, and I find it safe to say that it wouldn't have been sufficient for a man.

I would absolutely recommend Compere Lapin for it's lovely atmosphere, and tasty food...especially if you're into curry.  That goat...

Saturday night we had a group celebrating my good friend's bachelorette party.  We wanted to start the evening with a nice dinner before the Bourbon street madness/scavenger hunt began.

The dinner was at Bayona.  I had been a couple of times, but honestly, it's been over 10 years since my last visit.  It pretty much fell off of my radar because I hear so many mixed reviews.

When it comes to atmosphere, Bayona is perfect.  Old school New Orleans feel, dim lighting, and a beautiful courtyard. 

The service was kind and efficient, but I did think it was a little pushy when our waitress told us twice that she recommends not splitting because an appetizer and an entrée per person will be enough food for one.  I get that she wanted us to know this, but once we decided to split a few things because we'd have a long night ahead of us, then it should've been left at that.  She was not suffering at all when it came to tip because we were all drinking.  (Final total was $85 per person after tip) 

Bayona fell really flat when it come to the most important component of dining out...the food.

I decided that since we'd be running all over Bourbon Street, and further drinking, that I'd just get appetizers instead of an entrée.  I started with a cheese plate.  It was just o.k. Nothing special at all.  Just three average cheeses and a few crackers and 4 tiny squares of some sort of fruit.  

Next I had the special tomatillo soup.  It was really good.  I got a cup, and ended up wishing I had gotten a bowl!

For my entrée, I ordered the appetizer size of the sweetbreads. I absolutely love sweetbreads! It was described on the menu as being topped with a lemon caper butter.  I was surprised when I received it to see that it looked almost like a goulash.  There were chunks of potatoes in it, and the same squares of fruit that were on my cheese plate.  It tasted nothing of butter or capers.  I could distinguish 3 capers in it.  The sweetbreads themselves were dry and bland.  It just wasn't good.  A huge disappointment.

I tried a bite of the osso bucco entrée that my friend ordered.  It was very bland, and that was after I saw her add a good dose of salt to it.  It was very bland.

I'm wondering if their food is so bland because their clientele is 90% over the age of 60.

I opted out of dessert, but tried a bite of others.  They were good, but not great.

I left feeling very underwhelmed.  I feel like maybe Bayona is an old school New Orleans restaurant that is now just resting on its reputation.  There are just too many restaurants to choose from for me to ever return to Bayona...and many of them at a much lower price point.

Food:  C-
Atmosphere:  A
Service:  B
Value:  C

EXCELLENT burgers, and sweet ass happy hour deals, good service, and pretty atmosphere make this bistro worth the trip to Metry bra. 

I went for dinner with a couple of friends, and on another occasion, even had my company's Christmas lunch here. Really good both times. 

There's a private room if that's needed.

Philly Cupcake is delightful addition to Center City! I ordered these cupcakes to be delivered for my brother's birthday and even though the store was closed due to a major snow storm, Micheal still delivered the cupcakes! Everyone enjoyed them (especially the Oreo!).  A great spot with excellent customer service!

This review makes me slightly nervous b/c I know the men who opened this brewhouse and I respect them very much.  I know their hearts are in making this brewhouse a place for you to come and call home.  Sit back, belly up to the bar or relax on a couch to enjoy good craft beer and locally sourced food.  They have big dreams for this to be a true brewery (hence the empty area to the left when you first come in) where you can get up close and personal to the brewing process.  Their brewers are passionate, dedicated guys who have been creating handcrafted beers for years; and the owners are worthy to root for, so check it out even if it's just for a beer and to support a local business.

The menu is ecclectic but simple.  The beer choices are vast and I know that they spent a lot of well established time speaking with a wine expert to really make their wine list something unique and special.  The cocktails (created with high end booze and by the same guy who helped Libertine and Plat 99) are interesting/look super tasty.  They are definitely pushing the envelope with their decisions but it is to stand out in what could be considered a very saturated market.  

Located in the old Blue Crew location (Masters/96th), they have CLEARLY changed everything.  There is a relaxed upscale feel to the decor (no more blue/white walls and Colts memorabilia). It's hodge podgey with a twist of comfort.  Love the hard/soft tones they chose and the mellow lighting.  The bathroom is nice, clean and recently painted (don't breath too deep - hehehe).  

The menu is fresh and the food is good, specializing in American cuisine with a twist.  I've had the artichoke and hush puppy apps.  Hush puppies were fantastic and loved the sauce!  Hubby brought me home take out today and the Philly sandwich was FILLED with fresh peppers and onions and overflowing with juicy, tender steak.  I really enjoyed it a lot (no bites for him!).  My ribbon fries were a bit soggy.  I'm sure it was from the drive home.  

Overall, they are still working out the kinks but the wait staff, owners, bartenders and chefs/cooks genuinely are giving it 110%.  There will always be room for growth but I am definitely a big fan of this new place and hopes that it continues to get better with each visit.  

NOTES:
-- This is NOT family-friendly at this time.  21+ only.
-- Staff shares tips so keep that in mind as you might have more than one server
-- Brewery coming to the left.  Forgive the mess for now.
-- Accepts reservations so call ahead on weekends!
-- Locally owned, locally sourced coffee and many food items

I've lived in Indy for over 10 years.  I lived less than a mile from Rick's for three of those and that was in my early 20s.  I used to go on Wednesday afternoons for half priced cosmos with my girlfriends to "kick off the weekend".  I have always enjoyed the outdoor bar, and I have never enjoyed the hit/miss service.  Once I moved away, my husband and I didn't make much of an effort to return.  The "regulars" keep this joint in business.  It feels the same and recently we went for a birthday lunch on a Saturday.  Service was OK but getting wine took FOREVER.

The food was A-OK.  I wasn't blown away by anything. The menu doesn't to appear have updated/changed, which I'm sure keeps some people happy.  We were there with a larger group and we had a nice time out on the deck overlooking the water (this is by far the best part of the experience).  For a Saturday, it was pretty dead which ....to me indicates it is not going to last forever. 

This place does NOT cater to any kind of younger crowd it seems and we aren't in our 20s anymore.  The price point is still higher than other "go to" spots in Indy and while they used to employ only hot young waitresses, ours was just old and slow.  It is what it is.....it's a traditional dining establishment that has been in Indy for too long located on a lake, so they can charge more than average for your food/drinks.

I miss the days when I didn't really give a shit about this stuff.  Now I don't see a point in wasting my money.

Unimpressed.  I went for Sunday Brunch and it is incredibly underwhelming.  I had nothing that I would want to eat again.  I was looking forward to something near Divvy that would give them a run for their (my) money.  But this is not it.  Sorry Matt.  Quality of that brunch really left a bitter taste in my mouth.

Due to an email I received, I decided to write a more detailed review of my experience at MTM.  

TAKE 2! :) 

He asked if I would like to "further discuss it".  I don't really want to, but I can feel his frustration in his note to me, so I am here to give more info.  I want to say that I always give UNBIASED reviews of my experiences and unless it's TRULY awful, I don't bitch and moan to management.  I am not trying to get anything for free while I am also enjoying brunch with my sister in law and it does make me uncomfortable to complain about an experience that was just underwhelming and in fact, not god awful.  It's just a waste of $15/pp in my opinion, especially when it was closer to $20 b/c I got a Coke. What is up with pricing for soda?  

Here are the details of my experience at Matt the Miller's on a Sunday morning two weeks ago at 11.  We were seated promptly by a member of the staff who was very polite.  We were approached and served drinks about 10 minutes into sitting down (too long?  You be the judge).  Outside of that, the service was fairly nonexistent, which is to be expected during a buffet type situation.

For example, we were NOT told the details of the buffet, what was being offered or even guided to where it was located. I know that it should be obvious, but considering we had never stepped foot in the place, I was put off that the server didn't even point it out. Considering it's a new establishment, it might be a normal assumption to make that we had never been to this place before.  She also said "I hope you want the buffet, b/c that is all we have."  This is a huge downer, to be honest.  Why not offer at least a sandwich menu as well so those of us who don't love buffets, can order something else that comes out of the kitchen 100% fresh.  I didn't know it was exclusively brunch until I went in that day.  

I do not believe anything is truly FRESH on a buffet (except maybe the omelets since they are made to order).  Too bad I don't eat eggs.   Everything else is set out under or on heaters which leaves food dried out and cold.  Buffets are not upscale or trendy IMO. I tried the biscuits and gravy....The gravy hadn't been out long but was genuinely tasteless and weirdly chunky.  The biscuits were dry and bland.  The flatbreads were also dry and not as hot as they might be if you ordered off the menu b/c they were sitting out.  After 20 minutes or so of sitting out, nothing can be considered "straight out of the kitchen".  The bacon was not crunchy but a bit chewy and unappetizing.   Also, it's brunch so why not offer more options for those of us who prefer lunch OVER breakfast.  All in all, I didn't try EVERYTHING on the buffet, so maybe there was something good up there that was overlooked by me, but b/c my first round was not so appealing, I didn't go back.

With regard to who you are and what you are trying to do in the market, I can appreciate all of that.  I used to be in the restaurant business and I frequent a LOT of places, ALWAYS trying the newest thing, but overall, I wasn't impressed.  I do love and support a TON of LOCAL businesses (check out the many reviews I have done if you would like).  I personally was just not that interested in spending $15/per person on bland gravy and dried out flatbread.

Brand new.  Keep this in mind.  One of my friends said recently "Indy was ready for Giordano's but was Giordano's ready for Indy?"  

Let's just say .....forget the pizza. Our service even after a manager realized it, SUCKED.  I mean, it was lunch last Thursday.  And there was about a half hour wait.  We came with our preschoolers on their day off and even though we were RIGHT IN THE MIDDLE of the main service area, it was like we were not even there.

Food aside -- which was just OK.  The bruschetta (which was complimentary) was tasteless and disgusting.  And it came out AFTER our deep dish single servings (???). 

I know they are new.  I get it.  But a lunch should not take 2 hours b/c we are ignored for 20 minutes on the front AND back end of an experience.  Our food was fine and the actual wait on the pizza was NOT the issue here.  I don't "do pizza" and I won't be coming back here anytime soon.  Deep dish or not....it wasn't that impressive.  No refills, no check ins and no care was taken at our table.  I do NOT dig that at all.  Service broke our experience. 

Side bar:  The bathroom is not in a good spot and the table that is NEXT to it....well let's just say I hope you don't get sat there.

Too many tables, not enough servers or space.  I know this review won't make a bit of difference, b/c apparently there was a 5 hour wait this weekend, but let's remember, Indy, the more you encourage this level of service, the more they will care less about you standing outside waiting on "meh" pizza.

I ordered a Coyote sammich with brisket and pulled pork with potato salad.  The meat was so moist and delicious.  I also really liked the bbq sauce! I was honestly surprised since usually with delivery it dries out a bit.  The sammich was huge. Well packaged. The sauce came separate so I didn't receive a soggy mess. Super appreciated!  Next time I feel like some BBQ, I will be keeping them in mind!

I love Street Side. The menu is created almost like a tapas place where you can order a bunch of different items and share or you can order something like Pho to enjoy individually. In an environment where almost everyone has a TV, the homey feel here allows for more camaraderie and conversation without the distraction. Perfect for a casual date place! One of the best things is that it's BYOB and across the street from a wine and spirits store.

I always order the grandma's pork and chive dumplings because they hand make everything and it reminds me of my childhood when my mom and grandma would make me dumplings. No MSG so everything tastes home made. One of my favorite places in the area. You won't go wrong.

After only staying one night at this hotel, I am already a huge fan of the place. What more could you ask for? It's right on Canal Street and about 2-3 blocks away from Bourbon Street and also walking distance to the French Quarters. On the other direction, opposite from Bourbon Street, the hotel is also walking distance to Harrah's Casino, Pinkberry, and Shops at Canal mall. 

The lobby of this hotel is very nice and artsy. The rooms and bed are nice with plenty of pillows for the guest. I might also add, it has a roof top pool! I took advantage of that after a long, half-of-a-day in New Orleans. The pool is between the 2 towers of the hotels and has a view of Canal Street on one side and a view of the Mississippi on the other side. 

Regardless if you want to stay at this particular hotel or not, there are also other nearby Marriott hotels! Stick with Marriott, they'll make your visit very welcoming and enjoyable!

This place is a joke... All for show. Hostess was legitimately angry that she had to seat us. Pretty sure that's the extent of her job though... She basically sprinted to the table- to the point we weren't sure where she was. She put the menus down and walked away... No "enjoy" or "your server will be right with you." It wasn't busy. You're a hostess. Let's not get too excited. Smiling may help. Your job shouldn't be too stressful. You write names and walk. 

The waitress was in constant "up-sell" mode. My wife ordered wine by the glass, and the waitress said, "I'll pick out a medium-priced one for you." Not a huge deal, but we were now evaluating all social aspects of this place, and looked at the pricing to see what she would pick... She picked the most expensive, which was not shocking since her main objective was clear- get the check as high as possible. We ordered salads, and she said, "and what are you having for appetizers?" When we didn't want apps, she acted like she was shocked. Shouldn't be that strange of a concept... She also looked disgusted with us when we didn't order dessert. The check couldn't have come faster after declining dessert. She then basically waited about two feet away while I signed the check. The greediness was a turn-off. Just be pleasant, and I'll happily over tip you. 

Food was good, which is the only reason I gave this two stars instead of one... Overpriced, but good.

As a nice topper, we were leaving and a 60 year-old lady was puking out of her car right in front of the entrance where the valet is... It may be the most unnecessary valet. Ever. Plenty of parking... and we walked further from the delightful hostess's stand to our seats than we did from our car to the entrance.

Wanted to try The Row for awhile now and so a friend and I did, on a whim. I was pretty disappointed. There was only two good things about this place. But let me start in the beginning:

We got there and there was a wait. No one was in the waiting area except us and another couple. I went to look in the dining room and there were ALL kinds of tables open. We waited for about 15-20 minutes and ended up getting sat at the first set of tables that were open the whole time we were waiting. No reason for the wait at all. The hostesses were also not personable at all acted as if they were so busy but there was nothing to be busy with. 

So we get seated and order fried pickles. Someone else had to bring them out. Apparently our waiter, though nice, was obviously too busy to do anything for us, really. Let me reiterate.. this place wasn't that busy at all, at least the dining room wasn't. But they should have different staff for inside and outside, which, I assumed they had. Anyways. The fried pickles were greasy and cut so thin that they were stringy. But whatever. We ordered. He had the Nash burger and I had the fried chicken. The food came out in a good amount of time but I would hate to see how long the wait would be if it were seriously busy. My friend said his food was good but nothing special. My chicken was actually really good, so I will say that. It was cooked perfectly. Juicy, tender, and not too heavy on the fried part. I also got cheese grits which were good and a lot of cheese. The brussel sprouts weren't even cooked. They were hard! 

NOT ONCE did our waiter come to ask how we were and if things were good. Some other woman asked us. All he did was walk past and look at our table. He filled out drinks twice and didn't ask how things were. The staff there just seemed extremely not personable. Even the guy who brought out the fried pickles acted like it was such a chore to bring us some ranch. Also the food was BLAND!!!!! Every single thing on my plate was so bland. UGH.

This is FOR SURE a tourist place. The food was also overpriced. I could've got the same meal at Cracker Barrel for $9.99, not $14+. The food was SO-SO. The service SUCKED. I would not eat here again at all. I know my friend was extremely disappointed and I feel bad for even picking it for dinner. I would've been more satisfied at a chain. They need to get their stuff together at this place or it's not going to be there very long.

TLDR; staff was overbearing, food was underwhelming. 

I came for an early dinner with a friend. Upon arriving, we were greeted by smiling hostess which is always a sign of a good time! We were seated immediately and were introduced to our waiter.  Maybe 5 seconds after receiving our menu, the waiter comes by and asks if we decided on drinks and flips my menu over and says "It's on this side." Like. Okay? I know? Maybe if you didn't come over before I even had a chance to look at the menu, I would have been able to flip it myself? 

I ordered the Tulio ($12), which is their twist on the boulevardier. It was great and had the perfect coffee and alcohol taste.

Italian chopped salad ($9) - had salami and artichokes in it. Was good, not great. A little too acidic for my taste but was a good start to the meal. 

Baked spicy sausage provola ($14 for 7 pieces) - arrived sizzling hot in an escargot platter. Basically housemade Italian sausage topped with provolone cheese. Eat it immediately or the cheese just gets hard. I thought this was a very salty dish, but yes. Cheese and sausage is salty, so I get it. 

Broccoli ($6) - with chilies and garlic? Did not taste chili nor garlic. It was extremely citrusy. Didn't have lemon or anything in the description so I was offput. Did not really enjoy this dish. And the table next to me ordered this dish and they got regular broccoli? (View pics). So I don't know. Weird. 

Linguine w/ clams ($16) - the waiter did explain to us that the portion sizes for the pastas are pretty small, but I thought that it was an okay portion for the price. The clams are chopped into the linguine and you get 3 clams in shell on top, topped with some bread crumbs. This dish had absolutely no flavor. I don't favor salty food, but I def had to add some sprinkles of salt onto this dish. Pasta was cooked al dente and had a good bite to it. 

Roasted gulf fish ($29) - the fish that was served was swordfish. I wish I knew it was swordfish bc I wouldn't have ordered it. Usually it's too dry for me. But that was my fault for not asking. So, yes. It was super dry. Flavor was good though. It was topped with onions and tomatoes. Tasted like a Vietnamese dish my mom makes at home!
- another server did come up to us and ask how our fish was. My dining companion explained that it was very dry and he offered us another entree of our choice. But after eating half of the dish, it felt inappropriate. We did appreciate the offer very much. 

Dessert was great. Our server recommended the lemon mousse ($10) and it was on point! The perfect amount of tartness and the crust was good as well. I enjoyed the candies nuts that were on top. Butttt, for a restaurant this new, I didn't expect them to serve me a dessert on a chipped plate. But I'm just nitpicking. It didn't take away from the dessert. 

We got to enjoy their strawberry gelato on the house, too. Very sweet gesture. 

$120 without tip for our meal was a little pricey to leave unsatisfied and still hungry. Would I come back? Not anytime soon. One star really, but two stars for the gentleman who finally asked how we were enjoying our meal. Thanks again!

I believe they took over dis&dem. It's pretty small, but they have outside tables that can fit at least 6 people and a very long bar.

Jerk chicken with ER sauce on the side ($7.50 + $0.75) - such a good combo! Sweet with a kick. I super duperly enjoyed the wings. Comes with ranch, celery, and carrots. Will definitely try the ICU sauce next time for extra heat! 

Mussels (MKT) - I've tried both the garlic Parmesan and the Asian. I really like both. The garlic parmesan, I feel, is more like the classic white wine sauce flavor, but the Asian broth is so flavorful! The Asian one has a lot of lemongrass and coconut flavors, and some chili for some spice. It's topped off with super crunchy fries. They eventually fall into the broth if you're not quick and get soggy. BUT! I don't even mind bc it soaks up all the broth!

Fharmacy burger ($12) - split this HUGE burger mainly because I had to try the bacon jam. I liked it a lot. 

Cali burger with added egg ($12.50 + $1.25) - another HUGE burger. Guessing all their burgers are. So messy to eat, but so damn good. Love how the guacamole comes out from the side when you bite into it. 

Enjoy every visit I have here. But this past visit... it was the best. I was starving! And the owners/chefs just happened to be having lunch next to me. They were eating homemade spaghetti and meatballs and it looked soooo good. Must have seen me drooling, because they made me my own bowl with garlic French bread while I was waiting for my food to come out. Holy crap. Best, most personal service. Gotta love it here. 

TLDR; best mussels (although small sometimes), spicy spicy chicken wings with a lot of flavor, bomb ass burgers with an option to build your own. Just eat here!

At the old Capdeville location. Friendly servers. Good food. 

Habanero salsa ($3) - or you can get a flight of 3 diff salsas for $8. I wish I did that bc the habanero wasn't my fav. It was on the sweet side and not very spicy. It's also the watery type of salsa, not chunky. 

Mexico City guacamole ($9) - guacamole with fried cracklings on top. Sour. Not bad. Might try the regular guacamole next time. I don't think this was worth $9 for the amount you get. 

Street corn - this had a very distinct flavor that I and my dining companions couldn't place our finger on. Regardless, still a good side to try if you've never had elotes. 

Jicama salad - came with cucumbers and jicama. Very light and refreshing. 

Creole queso ($9) - everyone at the table loved this. It was cheesy (obvi) with tons of crawfish. The flavor was so good. One of my friends said he would have licked the bowl clean. Def try this if you love queso. It was also a pretty good size portion for the money. 

Asada torta - a torta is basically just a sandwich. It comes with fries. Very heavy, but flavorful. Meat was a little dry. 

Different tacos come either on corn or flour tortilla. I prefer flour tortillas, but their corn was pretty good too. Vegetable tacos are $3, while the ones with meats/seafood are $4. 

Baja fish - crispy fried fish. I only took a bite but it was very good. 

Pork al pastor - I thought my meat was dry, but everyone else at the table said they got really fatty delicious pieces and loved it. It was def the crowd favorite. It came with grilled pineapple which I thought gave it more depth. I would order again since I know I just got a bad taco. 

Cauliflower - with pickled beets. Omg. This was my favorite taco. I could eat it every single day. It was soooo flavorful. Everything it was paired with came together beautifully. 

Crispy shrimp - I didn't try it, but my friends said this was just okay. The shrimp was a little spongy to them. 

Cajun fish - dry. It's blackened fish. The amount of fish was also very little. 

Overall, I would definitely come back to try more dishes. I really enjoyed the food. I can't wait to try the drinks next time, too.

Always a 10/10 meal here. I missed it so much during its renovation hiatus. But it's so nice leaving there without smelling completely like food. 

Come with a group of 2 or more so you can order everything!

My favs to order here:
Bo tai chanh - cured beef with lemon, red onions
Banh xeo - turmeric crepe with shrimp and pork belly. Wrap in lettuce for extra yum. 
Ca kho to - clay pot braised catfish 
Canh chua ca - sour catfish soup 
Suon rim add quail eggs and tofu - braised pork ribs 
Ga xao xa ot - chicken stir fried with lemongrass and chili. Not as spicy as it sounds. 
Ngheu xao la que - clams stir fried with basil 
Bo muc tom nuong Vi - beef squid and shrimp on the hot grill - eaten like spring rolls 
Snow pea leaves or water spinach sautéed in garlic

There are plenty more delicious dishes. I really don't think you can go wrong!

They do get busy but food usually comes out pretty fast. Already drooling and wanting for more and I was just there a couple days ago.

Ahhh, have to update my review since it's been 3 years! My feelings for Mint have not changed although my favorite things to order have!

Lemongrass chicken, add tofu, sub brown rice - so much flavor! This is my go to! The portions are pretty big, IMO. So I can eat half and bring the rest home for a second meal. Delicious. 

Pho - honestly, I've tried almost every pho they have to offer besides the vegetarian ones. They all taste so good. The broth comes out super hot. And they pile on the meat! 

Egg rolls - 4 come in an order. Comes out with fish sauce. Always freshly fried and crispy. 

Spring rolls - 2 per order and comes with peanut sauce. I've had every spring roll they have, but my favorites are the shrimp and pork and avocado and tofu. The shrimp and pork is the classic spring roll. You really can't go wrong with ordering this. The avocado and tofu is so good and fresh. And perfect for when you want to be a little more healthy. 

Sticky wings - get this! That's all I have to say about it. 

Beef sate vermicelli - my bf's favorite thing to eat here. He always gets it with egg rolls and an egg. He loves that they put a lot of sauce so that there is flavor in each bite. 

The only downside to Mint is parking. It is street parking on Freret so it gets pretty hard to find close parking during the weekends and rush hours.

Bacchanal is the #1 place to take out-of-towners when they hit you with the "so what do you do for fun around here." It doesn't matter if you've only gone twice on a weekday, just take them there and they (probably) won't be disappointed. 

If the long lines and overpriced alcohol don't scare you away, you're in for a night you're bound to remember (or forget)! They've got great music (check their schedule online), delicious cheese platters, wide selection of wines, and the most helpful staff. Head on over and enjoy the cool spring nights before it's too late!

Tip#1: Go ±30 min. when the band is supposed to start for shorter lines.

Tip#2: Ask for help! I've always had a great experience learning what I like/dislike at Bacchanal.

Tip#3: Get an entire bottle for yourself.

One of my very best friends is a perfect go-to person for all things local in St. Louis. Naturally, I trusted him with my life when he recommended The Mud House for a breakfast sandwich and some coffee before my 4-hour drive to Memphis, and I'm beyond glad I heeded his advice.

From the outside, this place grabbed my attention immediately; I adore a good vintage-looking, inconspicuous spot because it's pretty much a guarantee that the food will be amazing. 

When perusing the menu, I saw a combination of two words I'd never seen together before: maple mustard sauce. Absolutely. No question. Get it. Just get it. Also note that the breakfast sandwich menu is very straight-forward, with two main options, BUT with how fantastic mine tasted, The Mud House knows it doesn't need many options in that arena. Maple mustard sauce made what seemed like a simple egg-and-cheese sandwich turn into an entirely different experience in the best way.

Finally, as I love to do on any vacation, I bought a bag of local coffee off the shelf here (from Momo) and I've been enjoying it for the last few weeks while back in my hometown of Chicago. However, I can't wait to go back and show everyone I know the magic of the maple mustard sauce.

This brunch was INSANE and I am so incredibly happy we had a chance to eat here! My boyfriend and I woke up on a Sunday ready to eat, but we knew the lines for brunch and lunch would be insane. Luckily, I noticed that French Toast features the Yelp Waitlist feature, so I added our names to the list while we walked the 20-minute journey to the restaurant. It felt really comforting to see our place move up in line in real time. We used those extra minutes beforehand to explore the French Market a bit nearby, and before we knew it, our table was ready.

We were seated at the counter, and were overwhelmed by all of the incredibly unique brunch options. I started off with a pomegranate mimosa (YESSSSSS!) and my boyfriend ordered an Irish coffee.
