These were the best decisions. If you want something cold to drink, I recommend that mimosa, and for something warm, go with the coffee! I dare you!!!!

Picking something to eat was extremely difficult, because *everything* looked incredible. I wavered back and forth between the fried oysters avocado toast (c'mon, that sounds ridiculously good) and the king cake french toast. I ultimately went with the french toast, which was a very, very good decision, because it was stuffed with cinnamon cream cheese. How dare they, honestly?! How dare they come up with something so fantastic?!?!

Along with our individual meals, we asked for an order of aebelskivers, because we saw pretty much everyone around us eating these powdery treats. If you're even mildly curious as to what these would taste like, ORDER THEM. Just do it, and get the jam to dip them in. The aebelskivers here are warm, doughy, and topped with powdered sugar. Like a lil' beignet. This was the perfect addition to our brunch!

Thank you to the sweet staff at French Toast and those who created the menu. I highly, HIGHLY recommend this spot for brunch. Add yourself to the waitlist... now!

I actually ate here because my sister had visited months prior when she was in town, and she wrote a raving Yelp review. She'd been telling me about how wonderful the food and decor was (she's a HUGE "Star Wars" fan) and I was inspired to see it for myself.

My boyfriend and I happened to walk by while exploring Frenchmen Street during our visit this past February. We walked into this colorful building and up the stairs to the second story where all of the "Star Wars"-themed displays were, and we were glad to learn that we'd be able to order our food up there as well. I chose a crawfish étouffée hot dog, because New Orleans, and our food came out within a few minutes. We gladly grabbed it and found ourselves a nice little table on the outdoor balcony overlooking Frenchmen Street where a brass band had begun playing on the corner. 

All of the tables up on the balcony were colorful and it really felt like Frenchmen Street was warmly welcoming us on the first night of our visit. It's been over a month since I ate this hot dog, and I still remember it vividly. It was incredible and unique, and the mustard on top was the absolute perfect topping. A++++. Seriously. Add in the live music outside and the lively people on the street, and we had the best first night experience possible, all thanks to the location and food at Dat Dog!

While walking down Frenchmen Street after eating brunch nearby on a Sunday in early February, my boyfriend and I were looking to settle in at one of the bars to listen to some live music for a few hours. We approached Bamboula's and I looked through the doors to see a historic aesthetic and a band setting up to play. There were some tables open within eyesight of the stage, and a waiter told us to make sure we could see well before deciding on a place to sit. We were able to find a great spot and each ordered a few beers.

The band that was playing was called the Ragweed New Orleans Band, and they were SO great. We stayed for two of their sets, because they were so talented! When you visit, try to see them on a Sunday, because you'll enjoy their tunes, and don't forget to tip. Support that local music!

We really enjoyed our afternoon here and I recommend this spot for a Sunday afternoon beer stop.

So I am giving two stars because i had 2 good experiences (4 star) prior to the not so good.
Cool, bright decor. Great location.
Interesting, potentially delicious food.
This is a new age buffet. Food sits under eat lamps, you pick your poison, and pay at the end. Pretty neat concept.
First two visits I had a yummy egg dish, toasty warm, and the nice fresh bread.
Third visit, I had the same egg dish, but ice cold. Now I am serve safe certified and also have enough common sense to know what the danger zone is for food. These eggs were in it. After one bite I took the dish to the open kitchen and said, these are ice cold. I was met with a rude, blank, stare. From a grown man. I asked if I could have it heated. To which i was told" we don't do that here". Excuse me!? He then pointed to the trash area. He told me they would make more.
So now while my family ate, I sat. Another gentleman brought me eggs a little while later. No apology. Nada.
For the pleasure of cold eggs, and poor service, I paid $50. For 3 people.
The hipsters that run this place need to get over themselves and put out a better, hotter, product and try good customer service. 
Don't waste your money here.

Really, really good pizza.  Look out Blind Onion and Noble Pie, they'll give you a run for your money.  Although it really depends on where I am when I decide I need a pizza.  I'd go to any of you.

There's a sign on the window that says a Brooklyn Pizza Restaurant Owner stated they were the best Pizza in town. Their sauce was amazing and they make their own sausage (a little on the spicy side).  They owners are from the Oranges in New Jersey.  And the brother of one of them lives in the town where I used to live...Pompton Lakes.  It's a small world.

It's a small place and I hear it's always busy.  And yes, I can understand why.  The pizza is great, they make a green salad, some desserts and bagettes.  Will have to try the bread sometime.  After you give your take out order, there are benches outside where you can wait.  I thought there was outdoor seating, but there is not.   It was the benches I saw.

And, besides making great pizza, they are working for a good cause.  They train and staff the restaurant with people with disabilities...and that's a great thing.

Didn't know what to expect,  My daughter said "want to go of Sushi Burrito."  Sure, why not!

Well the place is new, it was very clean, the food service table was clean...everyone remembered to wear their gloves.  The service was quick and friendly.

Oh...for those of you, like me, who don't know what a Sushi Burrito is....basically it's a huge "hand roll" or an extra fat long roll wrapped and served as a Burrito.  I love it.  Especially since they were able to make mine with Soy Paper.  You walk down the counter (similar to Subway) and watch as they make your roll.  You can add or delete items and have them add more sauce if you prefer.  Then there is a water station that also has soy sauce and hot sauce it you'd like to add them to your burrito.

They have about a dozen pre-designed "burritos" on the Menu Board.   Plus, there's a make your own option.  They also serve small and large Poke Bowl.  Poke Bowl comes with white or purple rice.

Definitely looking forward to going again.
YIKES dark, dismal a young man wheeled out a mop bucket in the middle of my deciding, how rude.  I was sure a rat was going to jump in my hair. V.O.M.I.T

I had a wedding in Downtown Philadelphia and would be attending the Rehearsal Dinner, Wedding and Sunday Brunch so I decided to get a room for two nights at the Rittenhouse. 

The room I got was on the 9th floor and overlooked 20th Street, which was nice, but I would have preferred a view of Rittenhouse Square. However, the amenities in my room were great. The TV was giant and extended while the couch had a roll-out bed inside of it. There were plenty of seating areas and the large king bed I had was very comfortable.

My room lacked much of a kitchen, but they did have a little section that had a coffee maker and a mini-bar. However, I was in the bride's room a couple of times and noticed she did have a full kitchen, but I suppose that was due to the fact that she stayed in a suite.

The lobby here is really nice with some seating areas and close access to the hotel's Library Bar. There is also a nice Italian restaurant inside the Rittenhouse Hotel. 

Also, the staff here including the front desk staff, concierges and doormen are all helpful, polite and courteous. 

Finally, when checking in you get a few vouchers for some free drinks from the bar. Also, depending on when you check in they may have chocolate covered strawberries available, which is a nice touch. 

Altogether, the Rittenhouse Hotel is one of the nicest hotels in all of Philadelphia and a great place to stay for any occasion!

I generally don't eat at chain steakhouses like LongHorn Steakhouse and prefer steakhouses like Prime Rib or Barclay Prime. However, this LongHorn Steakhouse just opened in Bala Cynwyd on City Line Avenue, which is very close to me so I decided to stop in. 

In the past this location was a Joe's Crab Shack and a Houlihan's, which I had never been to. 

Finding a parking spot here was very easy due to the large parking lot even though the restaurant itself was fairly crowded. When I came in, I was informed that there would be a 30 minute wait. In the meantime, I was given a pager and sat down in their waiting area. 

Eventually, after waiting for a little under 30 minutes, I was seated towards the front of the restaurant in a comfortable booth along with the rest of my party. However, I do wish the booths were cleaned a little better as there were some crumbs and a little trash on the booths and the floor. 

Our waitress Kia came over and took our drink orders. She quickly came back with our drink and dropped off a nice, thick loaf of bread. The bread itself was pretty good and had a nice hearty taste to it. 

After that, we got our menus and made our appetizer and later our entree orders. Even though the restaurant recently opened, the menus seemed to be kind of dirty and had some creases in it. 

I went ahead and got the French onion soup to start and the Flo's Filet for my entree. I chose to get the berry pecan salad without pecans and the baked sweet potato.

My French onion soup came out very fast and was hot. It was topped with a beautiful, thick and tasty cheese. The actual soup was very tasty with a nice sweet flavor along with a nice, subtle onion taste.

Before my steak came out, I going berry pecan salad, which I got without pecans. While the dressing along with the fruits including strawberries, mandarin oranges and grapes were all fresh and flavorful, I felt that they could have provided a bit more. Otherwise, the salad was pretty good.

Finally, my filet came out along with the baked sweet potato, which was filled with some brown sugar. While I wasn't expecting too much based upon some prior reviews, which mentioned that the steak was high in gristle, I was pleasantly surprised. First, the filet, which I requested as medium was perfectly done and the steak itself was flavorful and had no gristle. Also, I loved how tender the filet was! 

Also, a man who I believe was the manager was also great! He was very kind and accommodating. 

I wanted dessert, but I ended up not getting any.

Altogether, LongHorn Steakhouse serves pleasantly surprising and serves good food that is comparable to some very nice steakhouses for an affordable price.

Since First Watch in Wynnewood opened, I have heard nothing, but great things. So today, I finally decided to stop in for myself. 

I went up to the front desk and was immediately seated in a nice, comfortable booth. 

Almost immediately, our waiter came over and asked us for our drink orders. I decided to order an orange juice. 

The orange juice came out fairly fast, but I was fairly disappointed in it. The orange juice, did not taste fresh squeezed, which I feel like should be a must for a place that specializes in breakfast. 

After that, I decided to order their Pumpkin Pancake Breakfast. It came out fast and very hot. 

I first started off with the pumpkin pancake, it was large and fluffy. Best of all, the pumpkin spice flavor was good, but not overbearing. 

Soon after that, I had the eggs and chicken sausage that came with it. They were both pretty good, but I really liked the chicken sausage! 

For the whole time, our waiter made sure everything was going well, which was very nice! 

My only major concern was that when paying my check, I had to go to the front desk, which was also seating people. I wish they changed that process. 

Altogether, I had a nice, delicious breakfast at First Watch!

I had to meet some friends from Deleware for dinner so we decided to meet halfway at Tavola. 

I came in and fell in love with ambiance. I was seated outside on the giant patio. We were right under some large, orange umbrellas. It was a great place to spend the evening especially with the great view of the golf course. 

I started off with a strawberry vodka drink. It was pretty brutal. It was covered in basil filling my mouth with basil on every sip. I returned it to the kitchen and it came back without basil. However, it still wasn't very good. It just tasted like seltzer water as you could not taste the strawberry. 

I was also disappointed that I was not given any bread with my order. However, other tables had bread baskets. I suppose you might have to ask, which seems a bit odd. 

For my entree, I got the grilled chicken tacos. It was really small with only two tacos that weren't even large. It would be large enough if you got an appetizer. While the chicken was fresh and tasty and went perfectly with the black beans, avocado, corn and salsa. Unfortunately, someone in my party was a bit disappointed with his buffalo chicken caesar pizza.  Someone in my party got pasta and the portion was HUGE! She had enough to take some home. I guess the portion depends on what you order. 

Altogether, the food here is above average, but you really should come for the ambiance.

After a fun night of bowling with a couple of friends at Wynnewood Lanes, we decided to stop off at Anthony's Coal Fired Pizza. 

This location is a year or two old, but I've only been here one time before this. However, I have been to the Wayne location a couple of times. 

Compared to the Wayne location, this Anthony's has a much smaller bar and dining room giving it more of a family feel rather than sports bar or pub. 

Even though it was a Saturday Night, it was not too crowded as I only had to wait 5 minutes before being seated. Once we were seated, Christian our waiter came over. Throughout the entire experience, he was kind and professional. Later in the night, I even had a quick little conversation with him. 

We started off with drinks, I had a splash of Ginger-ale and it was topped off with a maraschino cherry. While it wasn't bad, I've had much better even at similar style places. 

After that, we got the house salad. It was served family style and came with a variety of fresh toppings including tomatoes, onions and chickpeas. While the salad was fine, it wasn't spectacular. 

The other party members informed us that the chicken wings were spectacular so we decided to get them. After about 5 to 10 minutes, they came out piping hot and plated beautifully coming with a pita style bread and topped off with caramelized onions. Even better than the presentation was the taste of the wings. Rather than being smothered in some sort of spicy sauce they were beautifully grilled. The chicken itself was moist and nicely seasoned giving it an excellent taste. 

Finally, it was time for their pizza, which was definitely up to par. The pizza was nicely presented and even better tasting. The crust was a bit charred giving it an excellent taste while the pizza was very simple with an excellent ratio of cheese to sauce. 

I had the chocolate cake for dessert and I will have to admit it wasn't spectacular. It was a bit dry and almost lacking in flavor at times. However, it was solid for a place where dessert isn't their expertise. 

When leaving the manager came over to make sure we enjoyed everything, which was nice of him. 

Altogether, Anthony's is a nice restaurant serving good food in a nice atmosphere with friendly staff!

I have driven past Bryn and Dane's a couple of times dive their opening and always wanted to stop in. Today, while in the area I stopped in. 

I walked in and was greeted by large trees inside of the restaurant as well as large glass panels on the feeling allowing for natural sunlight. It was a pretty cool feel. 

After that, I walked over to the self-ordering station. They have three large screens that allows you to self-order. From there, you can select your order. During the time I was there, they were still on their breakfast menu. I decided to get an acai bowl and a banana, peanut butter and chocolate. 

The self-ordering station allows you to save your phone number on file or have your face be recognized for future orders. While I found that a unique and futuristic, it was also a bit odd.

While they call themselves, "healthy fast food" the food did not come out fast. It took 10 minutes for an acai bowl and smoothie to come and I was the ONLY person there. 

After 10 minutes of waiting the food finally came out. I started off with a few sips of my smoothie and it was great. It was definitely one of the best parts of meal. The chocolate was sweet, but the banana and peanut butter helped balance it out. 

After that, I had my acai bowl. While it was good, I was a bit disappointed. It was not very thick and creamy like how the good ones are made. It was pretty soupy, but at least the toppings were fresh. 

My only experience with the staff was when they were dropping off my food. They didn't really say to much to me, but were not rude. 

At least at Bryn and Dave's the prices are not too expensive and the portions are large. 

Altogether, this restaurant is not perfect, but it is solid!

A friend of mine was having a birthday and she was celebrating it at Parc. I was invited and I decided to come along. 

I came fairly early and was quickly seated by the hostess. The person who was having a birthday is a frequent guest so we were given a nice seat right by the window. 

Soon after that, the person who was having a birthday came. The waitress, Jess, then came over and explained the specials to us. We were also given a nice basket of fresh bread. 

Around 10 minutes later, Jess came back. She took our drink orders. I got a sparkling water topped with fresh lime while others in the party hot drinks like Old Fashioned and Chardonnay. The drinks came out very fast and we're nice and cold. 

Around 10 minutes later, Jess came back and took our appetizer orders. I went with the beef carpaccio. It was really tasty and went perfectly with the olive oil and shredded cheese. It was topped off with fresh parsley as well!

Finally, for our entrees, I got the flattened chicken special. I was expecting it to be a bit more simpler, but it ended up coming with bones and requiring a lot of cutting. The chicken breast was very moist and tender, but the sauce applied was not my favorite. While I didn't love my entree, in the past, I have had fantastic entrees at Parc.

For dessert, I got the chocolate cake. The inside was hot and warm, but nice and gooey. The outside was crunchy, but not too hard. They added a nice touch of chocolate jobs on top, though I wish they put a little less on top. 

For the entire time, Jess was really nice and professional. She made sure everything was going smoothly and gave great recommendations. 

One of the hostesses also was able to get a great picture of everyone outside the restaurant. He was also really nice about it!

Parc also has a variety of outdoor seating, which is great! 

Altogether, Parc is a great restaurant with delicious food, a good ambiance and friendly staff!

I was very excited to try True Food Kitchen with a few friends of mine, but unfortunately it was very disappointing. 

First, I came in and was seated in a nice cushioned booth with a view of the bar. 

Soon after that, the waitress came over and started to explain the menu. However, the information she provided was not very worth while, she even stated that the "starters" were the "appetizers". I understand how she was trying to be nice, but it was unnecessary. Also, there was a trainee, which I was fine with, but she was never formally introduced. I was also infuriated how the waitress continued to refer to the table as "we". I'm sorry, but she was not part of the group. 

We went ahead with our drink orders and I got the apple soda. While it was fairly good, it was not carbonated enough and was fairly warm. Most of the drink items were creative, but I wish some of the drink items were more traditional like types of lemonade, etc. 

Eventually, it was time for the appetizers. Everything was served family style, which I was fine with, but the portions could have fed one person not an entire group of people. Also, we ordered charred cauliflower yet it wasn't served or brought over. I had a bit of the edamame dumplings and I found them to be good, but not filling. Finally, I tried some of the hummus and pita bread, but the hummus was very subpar.

After that I had the grass-fed burger. When it was dropped off it was referred to the best in the "region", but I don't even think it was the best in the parking-lot region. The Shake Shack, which was a two minute walk away served a better burger. The burger here was nicely sized, but the meat was not too juicy or flavorful and the bun was very average. While the burger was fairly big it only came with one tiny side of baked sweet potato fries. 

Finally, after the small, disappointing appetizer and entree, I decided to get the flourless chocolate cake hoping to have a positive from my meal. Unfortunately, it was not. The cake was small and pretty bland. I kind of liked the vegan ice cream, but it was not enough to make up for the mediocre cake.

Listen, I understand the small portions and vegan style food. I go to many farm to fork restaurants and frequently shop at Whole Foods, yet True Food Kitchen was pretty below average. 

Even though I ate an appetizer, entree and dessert, I ended up leaving hungry. Very disappointing. 

Also, they charged us for the charred cauliflower yet they couldn't even remember to bring it out. 

Altogether, the food at True Food Kitchen is mediocre and the portions are so small that I ended up leaving hungry. Very disappointing.

A friend of mine had a little event at Kyoto Sushi & Japanese Steakhouse and I decided to attend. 

I came in and was greeted by my friend who took me towards the back and we sat down at the hibachi grill. 

The appetizers were pre-chosen and included both a ginger dressing salad and miso soup. The ginger salad came out first and it was fairly average. There were not any vegetables that stood out although the lettuce and cucumbers were fresh tasting. I also wish the ginger dressing was a bit lighter as it tasted very heavy. However, I was a fan of the miso soup. It was served very hot and the tofu added some nice flavor to the broth. 

After that, our hibachi chef came over. He started off by drawing a smiley face out of oil and then created a giant flame that bursted out of the hibachi grill. That was very cool! It was followed by heating up some rice and fresh vegetables on both hibachi grille. While those began to cook, he did some tricks by attempting to toss eggs into people's mouths. Eventually, the chef cooked up a variety of items on the hibachi grill including chicken, steak and fish. I decided to go with the chicken. 

My chicken was topped off with some soy sauce along with some rice and fresh vegetables. The chicken was tender, but didn't have too much flavor. Luckily, the soy sauce added some more flavor in that regard, but the chicken still lacked flavor. I was very much a fan of the rice, which was lightly grilled and had some fresh eggs mixed in. I loved the fresh vegetables as they were perfectly grilled! 

Altogether, Kyoto Sushi & Japanese Steakhouse is nothing spectacular, but the food they serve is fresh and tasty.

I heard amazing things about Delice et Chocolat from friends and on Yelp, so I decided to check it out for myself. 

When I walked in I was greeted by the sight of hard-wood floors, a few tables and glass-paneling allowing for a view of the bakers. Best of all, they had a large glass display filled with a variety of treats including cakes and macarons. 

I decided to get a couple chocolate macarons and a piece of the chocolate mousse. 

All I can say, is that they were both amazing! I thought the macarons were the best! The outside was crunchy, but not too hard and the inside was filled with delicious filling! 

The chocolate mousse was also really good. It had a great proportion of mousse and cake. It was perfectly topped off with chocolate shavings on top. Also, I liked how it was not too sweet. 

They also sell drinks here including smoothies, coffees and hot chocolate from melted chocolate! 

The staff here was really nice and gave me tips on what I should get! She also suggested I refrigerate everything once I get home. 

In the future, they plan on selling gelato and ice cream and adding a chocolate bar. 

Altogether, this is a great shop that is a great addition to the Ardmore community!

I frequently Mikado and it's usually very solid. Tonight, that was the case. 

Today, I came in to get some sushi with a couple of friends of mine. 

The waitress, Ashley came over quickly and took our order. I decided to try the cold Thai tea. While it took a little while for the drink to come out, it was pretty good when it came out. It was fairly creamy, but also had a nice tea flavor.

The actual food itself here is very good and I am actually a bit surprised to see all the negative comments regarding the food. 

I started off with the calamari salad, which was great! The lettuce and vegetable toppings including cucumbers, tomatoes and shredded carrots were all great and the ginger dressing was superb. While the pieces of calamari I got was great, there were only a few and the rest were just small fried pieces. 

When it comes to sushi, they gave a large variety and they were very good. Tonight, I had the Philadelphia and California rolls. The rice is good and the insides are of very good quality. The salmon and cream cheese were especially great! 

I also had the chicken teriyaki! It was beautifully played with a flower on top, it was very nice. The teriyaki was also great as the chicken was tender and moist while the teriyaki sauce took it to a whole new level. The side of green brand was also nice. It was so big, I had to bring most of it home!

My only concern was that it took a while for our drinks to come. However, once I had my appetizer I felt a bit rushed when the entrees came out very fast. 

Also, Mikado has nice seating options including some tatami tables!

Also, get the great mints they have here when leaving. 

Altogether, Mikado is very solid restaurant with nice ambiance and delicious food!

A couple of friends of mine decided to go out to the Barclay Prime to celebrate a little event and we all left very happy by how great our experience was. 

First, the Barclay Prime is located right on Rittenhouse Square and is made up of two sides. The Barclay Prime restaurant and the Barclay Private dining room, but they are in two separate buildings. 

Once inside there is a modern, but classy feel to the Barclay Prime. The lighting is dimmed giving an intimate feel, but the extra cushioned seats add a modern touch. Some of the members of our party actually sat in a sofa, which they both thought was nice.

Once we were seated, our waiter came over. He was very kind, polite and formal, which I liked. He went ahead and took our drink offer. Although, one members of our party got a glass of Chardonnay, I decided to just get a glass of pineapple juice.

After about 5 minutes after ordering our drinks they arrived and we went ahead and ordered our appetizers. I got the wagyu slider duo after hearing about how good the Japanese beef is. I also ordered the shrimp cocktail that I would split with another member of the party. However, we got a 4th piece of shrimp and we got them all in colossal size. 

While we waited for our appetizers we had bread dropped off and it was absolutely amazing. The bread was made turnover style and was light and airy. It was fresh and absolutely amazing. 

Eventually, we had our appetizers dropped off. The wagyu sliders came in two different styles. One had cheese and onions on top while the other was topped with tomato. The wagyu beef itself definitely lived up to its expectations. The beef's flavor was definitely enhanced and had a softer and less chewy feel to the meat. 

Finally, I got the rack of lamb for my entree and it was absolutely spectacular. It was cooked perfectly at medium rare and came with a beautiful sauce and some tasty potatoes. Finally, the outer portion of the lamb was a bit nice and crispy. I always was given a choice of knife, which was a nice touch. I ended up going with a nice Japanese knife, which was great for cutting my lamb.

We also got a few sides including some delicious sides including some tasty creamed spinach and some crispy, shoestring onions.

Finally, we got dessert and although there were many delicious sounding options, I couldn't resist ordering the warm deep dish cookie upon the waiter's suggestion. It came out fairly quick and consisted of three cookies including chocolate chip, sugar and oatmeal raisin combined together to make one giant cookie. Vanilla ice cream was put on top and a side of chocolate sauce was provided. All three cookies fused together made a great combination and a tasty dessert! 

Altogether, the Barclay Prime is one of the nicest steakhouses in Philadelphia with delicious food served in a great atmosphere!

Most Philly Pretzel Factory locations have a good level of consistency. However, this location continues to make great soft pretzels that are easily above the average! 

First, this location is a bit small, but is very good. 

I came in and was warmly welcomed by the staff. I quickly decided to order just three soft pretzels. They had a deal going on where you could get a fourth Pretzel for only 50 cents, but I respectfully declined.

When I actually had my pretzels, I was in for a treat! The outside was perfect as it was nice and crunchy, but not too hard. The inside was nice as well with it being nice and soft! The salt to Pretzel ratio was perfect as well. 

The staff here was really nice and personable! 

Altogether, this is a great place to stop off and get a pretzel!

The Lark's name is so fitting. Truly a flight of fancy. The playful food presentations, which are as sumptuous as they are beautiful, beg to be shared in this social, lively atmosphere. The food is arguably some of the best in town, marked by creativity and fine notes of freshness. Flit from communal bench seating to the bar to make new friends and watch people as you dine, or catch a seat outside for a more subdued experience. The atmosphere is sophisticated without being stuffy, striking a balance between just alluring enough, just exciting enough, and just social enough for your Friday or Saturday night go-to hot spot.

I was craving for Thai food the whole entire road trip from Chicago.  I went for what I found most convenient at the time.

It was on a Friday evening, roughly 5pm.  Bankok Cafe's parking lot was nearly empty.  Perhaps a bad sign but I thought "what the heck, it can't be as bad as mcd"  I walked in and saw the familiar smiles, the ones I see in Thailand.  I was relieved and hopeful for a good meal.

I ordered Pad-See-Ew and Yum-Woon-Sen.  Pad-See-Ew was alright.  The use of regular broccoli still bugs me when I see them in my Pad-See-Ew because I know for a fact that Gai-lan can be found in Tucson.  The dish tasted alright, mostly authentic besides the usage of regular broccoli.  Sadly, Pad-See-Ew was unfortunately the highlight of my meal.  

You may wonder what went terribly wrong with Yum-Woon-Sen?  I happily took my first bite and I was surprised of how bland and tasteless the dish was.  Second bite, third bite, forth bite...,I tasted onion, onion, onion....  There were way too many humongous pieces of onion everywhere.  The overpowering taste of onion ruined the dish for me.

Overall, Bangkok Cafe earns a 2-star rating from my dining experience.  However, I am still hopeful to find a decent Thai restaurant in Tucson/Phoenix area.

Where do I begin?

First off, I LOVE the atmosphere of this little cute restaurant - cozy, welcoming, and down to earth.  Random countless assortment of baseball posters, baseball cards, random signs, jerseys, flags, props, you name it, were scattered all over the walls and ceiling.   The hate on the Dallas Cowboys was a nice touch on the menu.  However, the filthy and greasy sheets of menu were a bit intimidating.  

Three others and myself started off our diner with garlic bread and curly fries.  The garlic bread was just mediocre and the curly fries were above average at best.  The greasy meal continued with each of us getting an 8-inch hot sub.  The sizzling hot subs were massive.  I ordered chicken cacciatore.  The sub was a bit on the saltier side, perhaps due to the overpowering sauce?  The chicken was decent and tender.  I am giving East Coast Super Sub a benefit of the doubt that it may just be what I ordered.  

Based on a one-time experience, I am giving East Coast Super Subs a 2-star rating only because Penn Station subs definitely beat East Coast Super Subs' chicken cacciatore.  However, I will definitely give it another try sometime in the future.  So feel free to suggest your personal favorite and maybe it will open my eyes.

A friend of mine and I decided to try this place out one day after work.

I was surprised of how busy this little place was during a weekday.  There was a 15-min wait when we arrived on a Tuesday evening, ~6pm.

The restaurant's atmosphere was excellent.  The service was great.  The servers were very friendly and attentive.  The asiago bread with garlic butter was scrumptious.  I was very excited when they told us that their pasta and dumplings are made daily in house.  Everything sounded amazing on the menu and I decided to go with the miso glazed black cod.  The fish was well cook but the sweet miso soup didn't go with the black cod in my opinion.  I was also not aware that miso should be sweet.  I found it very disappointing as I hardly ate my entrée.  I'd like to think that I may have ordered the wrong dish.  I will give it another try and be sure to keep fellow yelpers posted.

Ambitious upscale Japanese restaurant?  I think not. 

Although Mr. An's is only listed as a $$ kind of place on yelp but it could get very pricey when they are skimping on the food portions.   A couple I sat with ordered at least 5-6 different dishes before they asked for their check.  I was part of a party of ~30 people.  We had our private room to ourselves but overall the food and service were definitely below average.

The sashimi slices are improperly thin.  The rolls are unacceptably small and are not well made.  The rice and the seaweed fall apart when grabbed with chopsticks.  I had one of their claim-to-be specialty rolls, that was not at all special.  Fried battered soft shell crab rolled in flavorless rice and topped with paper-thin slices of white tuna.  It sure did sound delicious on the menu but it looked undesirable once the plate was placed in front of me.  The freshness of white tuna was a bit questionable and the roll tasted average at best.  The teppanyaki, on the other hand, was entertaining but was not any different than any teppanyaki houses I have been to - the usual onion volcano, the corny jokes, the shrimp toss and etc.

I was starving by the time my food arrived.  It took 30-45 minutes to get my sushi and of course they did mess it up the first time.  The service here is horrendous.  Our waitress was just plain rude.  One person on our table asked our waitress if she could come back to get his order because he was not ready, she bluntly replied "no" without offering any alternatives.  The waitress pressured a customer, whom is paying her 18% of his bill, to make his decision on a spot just for her own convenience' sake.  I for one cannot stand how waiters/waitresses treat their customers in big parties rudely when they are guaranteed to be given 18% gratuity, which gives them no motivation to do their jobs.

Overall, my experience at Mr. An was a big disappointment.  Nothing here is worth coming for - neither food nor service.

If Café Poca Cosa was a person, she would be a spoiled teenage brat, who thinks the world revolves around her.  Like others have said on Yelp, this pretentious little place might not worth the time and money.

Unlike many other restaurants, Café Poca Cosa tries to bring the upscale atmosphere to Tucson with steep price tag.  We made a reservation for 4, however one of our friends wasn't able to show up.  We were told to wait by the bar/lounge area until all the parties arrive.  The hostess informed us that they weren't able to get a table ready until everybody showed up.  I scratched my head and really didn't understand the logic or reason behind that since we already made a reservation.  What is the point of making a reservation if we end up having to wait for a table anyways?  Thoughts?

Finally, we told the hostess that the other friend wasn't going to make it and there goes another 20 minutes between waiting for a table, getting our water, and finally got the attention to get our waiter to show us the menu of the day.   I do like the idea of rotating their menu items, but what is the point of making it so god damn hard for customers to order.  We get to see the menu once then five minutes after there comes the waiter expecting us to know what we want without leaving the menu with us.  I personally do not have photographic memory, so it was a little hard to memorize what they have.

Finally our colorful plates of entrée were served.  I had fish wrapped in foil with sides of salad, rice and a wedge of pineapple.   The fish was not over cooked, and everything tasted delightful.  In addition, all three of us shared a flan, which was also delicious.  However, with all the raving reviews, I expected better especially with this kind of price tag.   The meal was $34 with tip and tax per person for above average meal, and all the unnecessary hassle  and hoops to jump through just to get our meals ordered.  I am personally not a big fan, especially of their pretentiousness, because at the end of the day their food isn't exactly the best I have tasted in Tucson.

3-star for me.

Hands down - THE BEST green corn tamales I've had thus far in life are at Teresa's Mosaic in Tucson! Yes, they have a full menu of delicious delights - but if you're a Yelpie Foodie (I know, redundant right?) and of you haven't had a green corn tamale at Mosaic yet... then you have not lived! 

Seriously, their green corn tamales made from scratch there in the restaurant are so good I could cry! In fact I'm tearing up a little even writing this review knowing that I'm in Seattle and Teresa's Mosaic is in Tucson and it's going to be a while before I get to come to town and visit. Why! Oh why?! Must these green corn tamales be SO good and yet so far away from me? 

Okay - dramatics aside... These tamales are a must try if you're in the area! Sweet but tangy, dense but soft and moist. The masa mix is heavenly - not quite dessert sweet but such a good sweetness level paired with the rest. I like to order a little sour cream on the side too sometimes to kick up the tangy contrast up a notch. 

Other family favorites: cheese crisp, enchiladas verde, carne asada and albondigas soup. 

The cheese crisp is another one of those Tucson famous delicacies... highly recommend you try it at Teresa's Mosaic too. Light, flaky crust covered in cheddar cheese topped with roasted green chiles... Yes please! That side of sour cream you ordered, goes really well with the cheese crisp too! 

The restaurant is beautiful inside and out! I love the southwestern architecture, the colors and the inviting feeling of "welcome home" when you step in the door! The tables and chairs are gorgeous - each mosaic table is individual and a unique work of art! The waitstaff are friendly, very attentive and efficient. On all my visits over the years- the food has always come out fast and hot and my water glass was never left empty! A+ 

Family friendly place - but they also have a good selection of drinks. I tried the Prickly Pear Margarita this week and was pleasantly surprised. Just like the wonderful green corn tamale- the Prickly Pear Margarita was the perfect mix of sweet and tangy with some kind of citrus sugar around the rim of the glass. And it was pink! A++
