People shopping on Italian Market tend to fall in two categories; locals (me) buying their weekly groceries or tourists who ended up here because they read it in a guide book.  Props for that, tourists.  The Liberty Bell sucks.

So what do these groups, I assume, have in common you ask?  A lunchtime need for:
1) Authentic Ethnic Food
2) Booze
3) Something that won't weigh you down
4) Something cheap
5) Cleanliness
6) Friendliness

Well well well boys and girls Blue Corn hits em all.  Located next to that infused-olive-oil-store-you-always-pretend-to-be-interested-in-buying-something-from-but-really-just-sample-things-and-quietly-walk-out-of in the "nice" ethnic section of the Italian Market (ie not south of Washington anywhere near the live bird shop) this is a new place with a lot going for it.  

Had three gorditas (3 inch circles stuffed with stuff, get the chicharrons) which were $7.50 and a perfect lunch portion.  Beers are $4, two on tap, decent selection of bottles.  Sweet little tequila list - palomas for $8 which is not bad at all and they only carry top end, 100% agave stuff.  Sweet as pie service from real live Mexicans.  Clean.  Inviting.  Convenient.  Delicioso.  Nice free salsas.  

The kind of business you want to see succeed.  Go support em!

My friends and I were hoping for a great experience here, although things have been difficult in general with COVID. Based on reviews and raves, we heard this place was a great restaurant to experience. However, we had everything but a good time. The waiter barely came to check on us. At one point, one of us had to walk over to the front to get a waiter because we weren't getting serviced. The waiters were too fixated on the table next to us to even pay attention to us because they were a group of rich white men. It was uncomfortable and an overall terrible experience. I would not go back there. There were racist undertones.

Give them 6 months or so to get it together.. Maybe longer. The $6 Sake bottle is fun and a good deal. The fried chix was okay, although the wasabi mayo tasted like mayo. Not the end of the world. That's about all I can say positive. Oh and the free tea beverage is enjoyable.

The reviews have it about right. I would definitely recommend trying it at least once. The sliced beef is good. It's a classic joint. Overall for a barbecue connoisseur their qualoty and value isn't the best around. But we enjoyed our visit. Chocolate shake was just okay for me. Made with chocolate syrup as opposed to chocolate ice cream.

My tastes are for somewhat exotic and aithentic flavorful foods. Regional specialties. Meals that are unusual and you remember. Mitmita hit it out of the park for me.

First of all, if you haven't had it before Ethiopian food features a bouncy pancake like entity in lieu of silverware. You break off pieces to soak up sauces and stews and scoop up your food. And platters are normally shared family style, which is my favorite way to go because you get to trt different things and aren't stuck oggling your neighbor's dish that you realize you should have ordered. It's also social.

But you can prder your own meal or get takeout here. And I highly recommend it!!! Brent N. hosted a hige party for me here and we ordered lots of dishes. The food was even better tasting out of the fridge later on!!! The injera, sort of like a South Indian dosa or a puffy crepe, held up well and the subtle flavors melded even more over time.

This is delicious, flavorful food. Like the best food trucks, and ethnic dishes you go out of your way to hunt down.

I have to come back to try the fish and shrimp dishes, but I can recommend the vegetarian and vegan fare. Even the lentils were flavorful!! :P I also liked the rare steak / beef dishes. If you like your steak rare or don't mind tartars these were somewhat adventurous and interesting dishes. 

Everything is very flavorful and the dishes with jalepeño have just the right punchiness without any unpleasant heat or burning, at least for me. The lemonade and iced tea were very good and refreshing. Neither was overly sweet, and the iced tea is subtly spiced.

The chicken woth an egg dish was flavorful. The buticha appetizer was terrrific and I highly recommend. Has a lil kick to it. Delish. The sambusa appetizers were also tasty, meat or veg inside fried dough like a pakora or those Chinese fried dough entities.

They serve up Ethiopian coffee. Cute lil cups of flavorful coffee with or without sugar. They do a very flavorful potato salad Ethiopian dish. Also a tomato salad with onions and jalapeño that looks very simple but was very tasty and fresh tasting. I was trying to digure out the secret ingredients.. Lemon juice? Cardamom? Secret spices?

I don't know. But everything was very flavorful and eating with the injera bread is a very fun and different experience. Memorable. Great for a date. With the kiddos. Or for a culinary adventure on your own or with friends. 

Everyone is made to feel like family here. But without all the fighting. :) I am hoping they will adopt me.

This is a neat high quality burger joint. Cozy space and well appointed. You customize your burger with toppings. They have some deals like a Monday burger discount of a combo deal. 

Not cheap but very cozy, high quality ingredients, and fun toppings and options. Good kids menu. Enjoyed. It's not a super thick burger it came well done (I wasn't even asked how I wanted my burger cooked).  I was told by someone later you can actually request medium rare which is how the ideal burger should be cooked, but everything was tasty.

You can also do a chicken sandwich, mac n cheese, or a salad with / without meat.

Loved the balsamic tomato topper. Grilled mushrooms. Toasted bun. Skinny fries were very good.

They also have some fancy shakes. Key lime! Oreo. 

A couple tables outside. So I think you can bring a furry fruend such as a dog, cat, or alpacca.

Cool place. Worth splurging on for a better burger, good service, and superior toppings. At least sometimes. :)

The menu items we tried were tasty. Not cheap but tasty. But the music is too darn loud. I don't want to go to dinner at a place I have to yell and struggle to be heard.

There is skee ball and darts. A bar area. Chic decor. Our server was nice. The side salad is pretty heavy on the romaine. Bits of dill were nice but cheese, sliced almond or some touch is needed. 

I would consider gping back if they turn down the music during dinner hours. :P

I thought this was a good place for seafood. The steamers we had weren't the freshest but were okay. Service was good. Soup I had was very good. There's a patio. It's in a pretty nondescript strip mall but has a pretty good feel on the inside. Lobster tank. Popular place. Nice to have this available in the Lutz / LoL area. Definitely a good option for seafood.. and the prime rib looked good but they ran out (it's a special one day a week). 

They have some decent daily specials. I always feel like if a place runs out of a special they should offer something else.. but maybe that's just me. I don't like to feel like I missed out on anything. :)

This would be a Five Star place just for the cronuts served up hot right out of the frier with cinnamon sugar. Soooo naughty good!!!

It's a very little place altough there are plans to expand. Four or so tables inside a few more outside. Service is friendly and prompt. Fun menu of fish, shrimp, and other seafood dishes. Everything was quite good although I didn't love the Caribbean lobster corn dog. It was very good, but in fairness I am a Maine lobster snob and that frozen warm water stuff just doesn't cut it.. :P

The conch fritters were satifying and gluttonous. The fries were hot and VERY VERY good with some parmesan on them. The onion rings are very good also with a nice lighter batter. The corn meal crusted grouper cheeks were also very tasty. 

I hope avocados come back in season soon because I need a Big Chill sandwich with fried avocado.. This is a fun and feasty place for casual seafood lovers. Thanks Big Mike, Lindsay & Co. :)  Good times and good food.

They have deep fried key lime pie. :P Let me know how it is. I am on a very strict diet..

The place is located by the French Market. It is a nice open area. A very friendly place. What makes this place nice is the music.  The performers play good music. 
      I ordered the Muffuletta. I saw someone ordered it and it looked good and really big. I ordered a half portion.  It was still big. I must say . It is a good sandwich.  The sandwich was toasted. The sesame seed gave it a great flavor and crunch.  The olive flavor was good too. It came with a dip. It tasted like olive oil.  It complimented the sandwich great.
   I had a side of onion rings. The batter used to make them was good. I really liked it. It was with a side of honey mustard.  A good sweet mustard. 
  Service was fast. The server was helpful and professional, Edwin T thank you for everything.

The restaurant came recommend to me by both the Uber driver and my tour guide.  I am glad I tried it.
    The meal started with a lemon drop special.  I enjoyed it. It was good and strong. 
   Appetizers we choose the basket of biscuits and the Pork Belly Popper, great choices. Let us start with the biscuits. Wow they where big. Like big muffins. They where fresh, flaky and good. The best, the best biscuits I had ever had. They came with a sweet butter on the side. I would had personally preferred salty. Boy they where good. I want to take them back home.
    The Pork Belly Poppers another great pic. Bite size of  smoked then fried pork belly in a sweet like sauce.   This was delicious.  I would order it again.
   My meal was the fried chicken sandwich.  That sandwich had a lot of crunch.  The chicken was nicely cooked.  I liked it. I didn't think the batter had a lot of flavor. It came with a side. I got Brussel sprouts. They where crispy and good. 
   I had a great meal experience. I got to try new things. The food came out fast. Our server was professional. This restaurant was a good find.

7This seems  a popular place. There was a line outside. I got talking with the people in line and found this is a local's favorite restaurant. What a great find.
  I came for breakfast.  I wanted try something local and the grits with crawfish etouffee caught my eye. Its grits in a seafood like sauce or gravy. It was very tasty and really good. 
   The sign mentions that they have the best ham here. I tried a side. It was good. It was tender. It wasn't sweet or salty. It was good and thick.
   I tried the plain biscuits. Boy are they big. I really liked them. They tasted freshly done and homemade. They came with jelly and butter.  
   I can see why this place is popular with the locals. The food is good. The staff friendly and it has a great atmosphere. I will probably be back before I head back home. They had interesting things in the menu.

I must say this is a good place for breakfast.  They take reservations. I would recommend to make one. I waited for 30 minutes. They are always busy as I saw. There was always a line and yes the food is that  good to stay in a line.
    The menu listed a creamy vanilla ice coffee that sounded good. Specifically because I like things that are sweet. It was OK, but wasn't very sweet. 
   We ordered the French Toast Bites. I liked it. Small square French toast lightly drizzled with a sweet cream cheese mixture icing. Had a dip on the side. It was not very sweet.  But now that I read the menu.  My dish did not have powder sugar or cinnamon. That would explain lol. But it was still good.
   We ordered the seasonal beignets. That was awesome.  I recommend them. Fried small bite sized  crispy square dough. It had jam and sweet cream cheese. I liked it.
   My breakfast the corned beef egg Benedict. It came in a bed of spinach and potatoes on the side. It was great.  The eggs perfectly cooked. The corned beef was delicious also. The hollandaise sauce was very tasty. It was one of the best. I had ever had.
   Shawn K. my waiter was great. He was cool, friendly  and helpful.  He also has good taste.  I took most of his recommendations and liked it. Thank you for everything

I saw this restaurant in one of those cooking channels and it looked like something I'd try if in the area. First impression. It's a nice cute outdoors like restaurant.  Nice open area. 
    We ordered the Bouding Bites to start. My first time having this. It was good. It was sliced sausages.  The sausages had a little spice and they where made out of pork and rice. It was pretty tasty. It came with a mustard dip. 
   We then ordered the Boiling Pot. It was 2 pounds of crawfish and shrimp. It had sausages, corn and red potatoes.  It was big a quantity for someone to eat and so good.  It was delicious.  It tasted fresh and good. What ever they seasoned that boil in was delicious. 
    This was a casual restaurant.  They boiled, weight and cook the food right outside. I watched them as they did some. It was pretty cool. 
   The staff was very friendly and helpful.  This restaurant seems to be a popular with the locals.  I was later on told. I am so glad I had a chance to try it.

5 Reasons why I will drive to Indian Rocks on  Wednesday.

1. Macaroons- I simply adore a good macaroon this place  has the best.  They are chewy and crunchy and flavorful and fill my nights with such great joy.  I buy 6 and have two at the beach looking at the water, two on my way home and two later on that night watching  TV next to my shug. 

2. Crepes - enough said - they have stuffed crepes- plain crepes and crepes with and without fruit.   

3. My favorite thing is the the croissant sandwich crispy and filled with egg and bacon. 

4. Multiple varieties of caffeinated treats, I  personally go for the espresso 

5. Location, Location, Location - the parking is horrible if you don't arrive before the beach-goers show up.   But if you do you can park in the free public parking with beach access.  My routine is to go early park - get my food and sit on the beach enjoying the scenery and culinary delights . 

This place is awesome -

I am angry because Happy's is closed on Monday  and I cant get any  hush-puppies or Oysters for dinner. 

Found this place this place thanks to some pretty amazing yelpers who blazed the trail before me (Mark H). A month or so ago I was craving fried fish really bad so I asked fellow yelpers what was a  good spot and  they mentioned this place. 

First off the place is small and unassuming, I have passed by it at least ten times.  If you go down Skinner and get to trail Turn around  you went to far . Happy's will be on the right. Seating is outside only do come comfortable and ready to eat.  

Upon arrival I was like aw this cute, then the smell wafted into my nose.  Silently I told myself if the food is as good as the smell I  know that I've found a piece of heaven. 
Well hot-dog the food was better the smell- the  oysters melted on my tongue, catfish perfectly done and the hush-puppies had so much flavor they make you want to slap your neighbor. I have been back three times since my first visit.

I am angry today because I am craving Oyster Po'Boy like crazy. See you soon Happy, the weekend can't get here quick enough.

This is going to be a two-for-one review since I didn't get a chance to review Bacio after my first visit and I was just there yesterday for my birthday dinner with my parents and fiance.

Visit 1: 

Random Thursday night, running errands with my fiance in the area. We picked up a bottle of wine and headed to Bacio because i had read on Yelp that they offer Gluten Free pasta - and I eat a gluten free diet. 

Ambiance: we chose to sit outside, which was perfect for us (one small garden table and two chairs). The street is quiet and perfect for a date night dinner and private conversation, but if you are a magnet for mosquitoes, please keep that in mind and opt to dine inside (unless you carry OFF spray with you).

Menu: we had a tough time ordering because everything looked amazing! We munched on some Italian bread dipped in olive oil while we decided on our dinners - unfortunately, it wasn't gluten free. They offered to pick some up for me if I call ahead next time (I'd say calling a day before or morning of would probably work).

Appetizer: we split the medium antipasto plate. It was piled high with marinated eggplant cubes, beet salad, mozzarella, artichoke hearts, cheeses, olives and an apple salad (and probably more items I am forgetting).

Entrees: we opted for two gluten free pasta dishes so we could share them: one was the crab diavolo over penne. This was an amazing diavolo sauce - you must like things spicy hot if you order this. On top of that, it had more crab meat than I have ever seen in any dish I've ordered anywhere. I couldn't believe how delicious and filling it was. The other was a special for the night - penne in a very creamy white wine sauce with generous chunks of sausage and roasted red peppers, topped with clams. Amazing. We had to take some of each home because it was so incredibly filling.

Visit 2:

My parents came in from out of town for my birthday celebrations. I picked Bacio knowing it was delicious, great service and had gluten free options! I called a few hours before making reservations on a Sunday evening, but didn't think head enough to request gluten free bread. We arrived at Bacio and the amazing night began.

Ambiance: we sat inside, at a table for four. The restaurant was loud and bustling from a party of 20 celebrating a grandfather's birthday. It wasn't so loud though that you couldn't have a conversation. My mom fell in love with the open kitchen and the owner, Vinny, was incredibly attentive, charismatic and generous.

Appetizer: on the house, we received a minestrone-type soup with duck meat and sweet potatoes in it - it was AMAZING! We also shared a small antipasto plate, similar to my first time dinning there but with a green bean salad and pepperoni in place of the eggplant and beet salad. We also tried the house special, the genius of Vinny: a very unique tray of two lasagna noodles with sauteed shrimp and tomatoes folded in the center, swimming in a decadent cream sauce. And lastly, we shared a slice of the zucchini pie - not exactly what I'd like, but my mom nodded in satisfaction and said it was very nicely done and tasty.

Entrees: my parents opted for one of the evening's specials: skirt steak cooked to perfection on the grill (it could literally be cut with a butter knife) topped with creamed spinach and roasted peppers, and on top of that chunks of fresh Parmesan cheese. The skirt steak was incredible and I would definitely recommend it to anyone who likes steak! A side dish of pasta came with each - my mom went simple with olive oil and cracked pepper, my dad went with a pesto sauce. The pesto was more or less fresh grated cheese tossed with olive oil and freshly chopped basil leaves. Unique and delicious! My fiance had another special for the evening - the largest tuna steak I have ever seen served, over linguine in a wonderful Puttanesca sauce. Two thumbs up!! And lastly, I had the seafood spaghetti dish (with gluten free spaghetti noodles). It was very generously filled with a TON of seafood - clams, mussels, shrimp and squingili! The white wine sauce was creamy and really didn't overpower the taste of each seafood, which at first I thought I wouldn't like it so simple, but it was perfect. 

Dessert: No, there was no room left for dessert - but Vinny insisted on giving us two on the house! A fluffy, light ricotta cheese cake and a thick, rich, chocolate walnut torte. Both have my vote - but I must caution that the cheese cake was very Italian, and not the thick cheese cake you'd get at another restaurant. (As a cheese cake lover I can appreciate both types.)

---- 

I am so happy we discovered this perfect little restaurant and can get such attentive and personal service when we visit. I need to force myself to try new things next time we go - I think I will try the sweet potato gnocchi and ask for a cream sauce versus the red sauce it comes standard with.

Last words: GO! Don't forget to bring a bottle or two of wine with you!

I was visiting Tucson and this restaurant came highly recommended by my local Tucsonan friend. I decided to check this place out during my visit to see what the fuss was all about and so my friend made a reservation for dinner here.

When we arrived at the restaurant, we were asked if we wanted to sit inside the restaurant or in the outside dining are and we opted to sit inside in one of the booths seating.
Our server was quick to come to our table to introduce himself but he disappeared a long time after that. How long? Another party had came a few minutes after our server had gone, they had their server came to their table to introduce himself to them, had their complimentary bread delivered to their table, while I was still waiting for my complimentary bread. Our server was gone so long, I had to flag a different server to please bring us our bread.

After the whole Harry Houdini disappearing act, however, our server was back to his old self: friendly and attentive. The service level was top notch after the fact but it still didn't excuse him disappearing that long.

Onto the food!! We ordered the Lebanese Hummus to start, with extra fresh vegetables for an additional $3.00. The hummus was pretty good: tasty, rich, and creamy. I have to say, though, the fresh vegetables extra just weren't worth it unless you love celery because it came with a lot of celery. I personally would have preferred more carrots and more radish. Or at least an equal portion of everything.

For our entrees, I had ordered the Braised Beef Short Rib while my friend ordered the Grilled Shrimp & Avocado Bowl. My short ribs were tender, rich in flavor, cooked to perfection, and just an overall excellent dish. My friend obviously loved her dish as well because, as I mentioned above, she was the one who recommended this place in the first place!
As for dessert, we had decided to share the 'Bars of Sins' and OMG, these were some delicious chocolate bars.

Despite the little magic act at the beginning of our dinner here, I had an overall great experience at Wildflower and I definitely wouldn't mind coming back here the next time I visit Tucson.

I lost my Pho virginity here, by myself. and its the best thing that has ever happened to me. 

Walking back from East Passyunk, I decided to find out whats all this Pho shenanigan was about, I walked in by myself to be quickly greeted by one of the many friendly servers. The menu seemed broad and giving Zareen S. many a options are never a good idea. I decided to go with the No.1 which had everything in it. The "small" bowl of Pho came out in less than 5 minutes. The word small is a joke because by the time I had planted a food child in my belly, I couldn't even put a dent on it. Heaps of meat and tripe [i love tripe], bottomless sea of noodle, sprouts and basil is just 7 bucks?! Madness, that I fell in love with and deeply adore. I found putting a bit of fish sauce enhances the flavor of the broth my miles. And all this comes with a pot of Green Tea? I repeat, madness.

First time at William Dean Chocolates and my experience was awesome! I came here for the tea party. You can have it as long as you RSVP ahead of time for 2 or 4 people. 

First they give you a fresh brewed tea for yourself and it is one tea per person. There are over 30 different teas to choose from! Wish there was a little sampler of teas but it was still good. 

For food they bring out a 3 tier tray for the table. 
The top tier is two different kinds of scones. The jam with the vanilla cake scone was my favorite! 

The next tier comes with about 1/3 of a sandwich of each kind: egg salad, chicken salad, cucumber, and salmon.

The bottom tier has a mini cupcake that is filled with caramel which is amazing!! Chocolate covered orange peel, chocolate covered ginger, a type of cake covered in chocolate (blue pastry in the pic) 
two macaroons (1 each), two pieces of chocolate, two jelly like candies that were surprisingly good and two brownie bites. 

It was surprisingly a good amount for the value! Can't wait to come back again soon for another tea party.

Little place that I seen on Instagram and their food tasted as good as it looked! They are really reasonable! I ordered their Banana Nut Caramel French toast for only $7.95 and it came with three large pieces and a ton of delicious toppings! They aren't stingy on the toppings like some other places and it definitely filled me up! Really good food and kind of like a mom and pop shop but presentation is fantastic!

I came in earlier, right when the store opened. I ordered a boba tea, but they told me that they weren't ready with the boba just yet, which was understandable because the store was just opening. This is one of the boba shops that I can tell puts in their efforts to make good boba - they were cooking the pearls throughout the day so that it would be fresh. I wasn't in a rush, so the manager let me stay and study for exams. When I got my order, which was in about 20-30 minutes, they gave me so much boba! I've tried a lot of flavors, and hope to try more in the future. My favorites so far are the red bean boba and then fresh lemon juice (I think it was juice.. or was it tea?). Definitely worth trying.

Was visiting Nashville over Labor Day weekend and we tried to use the elevator in this bar to get to the rooftop. Stairs can be too much exertion for a friend in my group because of a medical condition so we actually picked this bar BECAUSE it had an elevator but we were initially blocked from using it. The bouncer at the elevator said we had to take the stairs and when I asked why he said it was because the elevator "was for people with disabilities." She was even told she didn't "look disabled."

Even though it is illegal to ask, we tried to explain she did have a disability and showed a medical card and needed to use the elevator. Why would we make that up? Around this time, the elevator doors opened and 2 bachelorette party girls in sky-high heels and dresses get off the elevator. They didn't "look disabled" and I'm sure they actually weren't but were taking the elevator for convenience. I asked to speak to a manager who ended up being the same bouncer who checked our ID's at the door, who eventually did let us use it, but told my friend something along the lines of we had to "be nice about it or he'd kick us out" when he should have been saying "I am so sorry we treated you this way." Be nice about it? That was NOT the right thing to say. Both of these employees I interacted with were rude to both me and my friend. 

Not all disabilities are seen by the eyes, and why shouldn't everyone be able to enjoy life and have access to things designed to make it easier? I hope this bar will learn from this and train their employees appropriately.

So disappointed, was a great spot in the 80s through a few years ago. Apparently the original owner sold, perhaps that's why the quality changed. The calzone was terrible. Watery cheese....yucky.  Onion rings from frozen, was deep fried mush, not fresh onions. Just moved back into this neighborhood after going to Aldos for years, and hoping to make it my new neighborhood pizza spot. May give the pizza a chance. .Loved this place since high school, hope next experience is great when I try the pizza.

On this night I ordered the special veal chop.  Not on the menu.  The most expensive item on the menu was 19.95.  The veal chop was 38.95.  Not disclosed beforehand.  Sure, I could have asked, but they could have told me also.  Money isn't the issue here.  Deception is.  I politely discussed this with the owner who wouldn't back down, but of course I should have expected that.

The food was decent, not the best on the Main Line, but ok enough.  The veal was cooked nicely, but the accompanying peppers and mushrooms had little to add to the dish.  The caesar-like salad was so different it intrigued me.  They put a meatball on top and lots of grated parmesan.  It was filling and good, but a little heavy on the vinegar in the salad dressing.

I contemplated a 1 rating because I was very unhappy with the shock of the bill, but that probably isn't fair for what was perhaps a simple misunderstanding.  But customers appreciate it when a restaurant is more forthright.

Jimmy Kelly's has simply given up. They're not even trying anymore. Only a misinformed tourist would end up here, or me and my wife when her boss took us here. What they provide in fabulous service they completely lack in food quality. How dare they use the word "steakhouse" in their title. Locals know the gig is up. I seriously doubt I would rank this place in the top 50 steakhouses in Nashville. And the prices are absolutely out of this world. How dare they charge such exorbitant rates!

The steaks were terribly dry and flavorless, the "fresh fish" certainly didn't taste fresh, the au gratin potatoes were among the worst I've ever had, and our mac & cheese on the side was downright pathetic. I would love to meet the "chef" and ask him or her "WHAT THE HECK ARE YOU DOING???" Please tourists, don't go here!!!

I desperately want to cheer for a local store with excellent customer service, an enticing interior space, hand-cut steaks, high-end cheeses and sausages, and the goal of becoming the best butcher shop in the country. And any place that sells the world's greatest chocolate milk from the Hatcher Dairy has already won me over! But our test kitchen found surprising results.

Visiting four local butcher shops (in Nashville, Brentwood, and Franklin) and purchasing one New York Strip from each location of equal thickness and weight, I was on a mission to truly determine the hierarchy of meat stores in Middle Tennessee. As the son of two chefs, this sort of competition is a monthly occurrence in our household. Upon grilling the four specimens under identical circumstances, we began the Great Steak Off of 2017, administering a blind taste test with our family as we sampled 3-4 ounces of each.

I labeled four sticky notes with a number corresponding to each butcher shop. My wife, not knowing which number representing which business, placed the sticky note on the bottom of four plates and then plated each corresponding steak.

As we carefully tried each cut of beef, there was one steak in particular that didn't compare to the rest. It lacked tenderness, had an atypical flavor, and ranked dead last on everyone's list, despite all of us having very different tastes. Searching for the culprit, we lifted up the plate and looking underneath to reveal sticky note #3. Looking on my list to find the steak's true identity, we were shocked to find that #3 was the meat from Porter Road Butcher Shop, a place so heralded among locals! How could this be? At $21 per pound, it was the most expensive sample in the experiment and only mediocre in taste! It certainly wasn't a bad steak, but it wasn't spectacular either. It was just boring and ordinary.

FYI: Plan a lot of time if you visit this store because none of the employees are in any sort of hurry. I was the only customer and it took 20 minutes to cut the meat, wrap it up, and check out at the register!!! But I admit that I do appreciate someone hand-cutting a steak  of my desired thickness right there on site. If only it had been worth the wait.

P.S. If you're curious, the steak from Whole Foods blew away the competition, which surprised us all! We thought the butcher shops would have been more competitive.

We visited Han Dynasty on the first Friday it was open. I wasn't quite sure what to expect, but I was pleasantly surprised. It was some of the BEST food I've ever had! The Dan Dan noodles, while spicy, weren't overpowering. I scarfed them down so quickly, I wasn't sure if I'd have any room for my meal! They were so good I wanted to just dive into a pool of them and gorge myself all day! I ordered a scallop dish (the exact name escapes me but it was on the center of the page, if that's helpful!) which was cooked to perfection. The pork dumplings were great as well, though I had trouble eating them with chopsticks and took them home to eat in the privacy of my house without looking like a piglet!

Everyone working was extremely friendly. Although the food was coming out slowly, it was worth it. The staff checked in frequently - just enough to be very helpful, but never taking it to an annoying extreme. The atmosphere is relaxed and very quiet, leading two loud Italians to be a bit out of place. However, we were never once looked at with a side eye or an evil stare, and we did actively work to keep our voices lower than normal - not an easy task! 

I cannot wait to revisit Han Dynasty and try out more of the wonderful food (and spicier dishes, as I get braver!).

I went here with five other friends (we all had masks, social distanced, and planned to eat out on the patio), I went in first to check the place out to make sure it was suitable to eat in during this pandemic.  I walked in and only one person besides me in the whole place had on a mask! The person was a server(I felt so sorry for her), the place was packed, and I even went to the reception guy and said "so y'all ain't wearing mask in here", and he said it with pride"no we don't have to". Funny statement since their mayor re-rolled out a mask mandate announcement that day because of the explosion of infections in the area, and it went into affect two days later! Having to is not always a precedent for doing what's right and makes common sense. Gross, gross, and gross, shame on you super spreader restaurant. Shame on the owners, managers, even the willing patrons not to expect and demand more, or care about safe sanitary pandemic practices, we left and ate at another place where people had pandemic common sense...if I could give no stars, I would...

I'm really excited about a fresh seafood market being 10 minutes from me!  I just heard of them opening up in December, but found out that they have quite a history of fishmongers in Indianapolis and are back in full force.  The 4 stars are only because this was my first visit.  They have an eat in area that they serve all their seafood delights and plenty of sides to choose from.  Along with their frozen & fresh seafood, they have dips and items like smoked salmon etc.  

I was doing my grocery shopping today and decided to stop in and check them out.  I arrived about dinner time and knew I would be eating alone (hubster had a blues gig) so I decided to order a shrimp dinner.  It was incredible with lots of shrimp, spicy waffle fries, 2 hush puppies, and my choice of sides which was okra.  The shrimp were a good size and very tender with a crispy coating.  All else with the dinner was very good also.  I had to bring a little home!

I came in intending to buy a large thick meaty fish for a certain recipe, but when I saw the local Indiana Yellow Lake Perch, I changed my mind.  Hubster loves fresh perch, so that's what's for the game tomorrow.  --can't wait.

The service was good and there were plenty of people to help and answer questions.
I know this will be one of my frequent stops in the future.

--Tried this Asian buffet for lunch & I would say average but not yuk.
The competion is great here in Indy. (As every other city.  Big cities have an advantage of raising the bar.)  Every other strip mall here has an Asian restaurant, whether Thai, Chinese, Korean, Vietnamese, or etc.  Every customer has different tastes. Ex:  Personally, I don't like fish sauce.  I have done some research and there are very mild fish sauces, and w/that, I cut it in half when I cook.

Positives for this one:    
They do have alot on their buffet.  Your drink comes w/ the meal.  -and their price is affordable.   They have mai fun (rice noodles w/a great flavor).  In fact, they have alot of noodles&rice, mai fun, another flavorful asian rice noodle, lo mein, fried rice & white rice.  Their eggrolls are the little crunchy ones, opposed to the fat thick skinned tastless ones.  They have Bourbon chicken which isn't usually served, but my guy loves.  And they have all the usuals, rangoon, sesame chic, gen t's chic, Hunan 
meatballs, sw&sour chic, veggie dish w/lots of broccali, many others etc

Negatives:  It just doesn't jump out at me.  --but it's by no means yuk.  
If you want a good and affordable Chinese buffet in a roomy clean facility, this is definitely one to try!

This is a good place for lunch if you order a lunch special. For $8.99, you get a burger (beef or veggie) and either fries or coleslaw. The burgers aren't huge, but they are a good size for lunch, and the Belgian fries serving is pretty large. 

The regular menu is pricier, but if you aren't in a rush to return to work, the atmosphere and service make it worth the price, in my opinion. 

I had the veggie burger.  It was pretty darned good: crispy zucchini and feta patty, grilled eggplant, and grilled onions. Yum. I wouldn't mind coming back to try the beef burger or pastrami sandwich. 

My waiter was attentive. He proactively brought me a diet coke refill. I find that I don't get refills often during the lunch rush, which is a peeve if mine. 

I was in and out within 40 minutes, not bad for a sit down place!

Parking lot is smallish, but apparently you can park across the street at the oil change place.

Yummy ice cream, but make sure to visit at off peak hours. 

My husband and I love ice cream, and I am part Thai, so the chance to try Thai style ice cream in Tampa was jumped at as soon as I could find a way to North Tampa at a random time. 

Ordering is fast, but as each order is made fresh, and each order takes at least 3-4 minutes to finish, the wait can be loooooong. If the people in front of you are asking for more complicated things like ice cream with solid add ins that need to be chopped up or a toasted marshmallow topping, the time increases further. 

I had the cafe au lait ice cream. I had it topped with strawberry, chocolate chips and a toasted marshmallow. It was so good and creamy. The freshly torched marshmallow was perfect. 

I'll return, if the line isn't too long.

This place was somewhere between a 3 and 4 star place.

For a place whose staff comes from Bern's, Sidebern's and Mise En Place, I expected more.  I expected to be greeted upon walking in the door, to be greeted upon being seated, and to be able to get driving directions when I call.  I also expected that if I brought in an expensive bottle of wine, that they'd have a decanter.

Okay, so they struck out on all of those counts.  But there were nice things about this place too.

The setting and decor were both very nice.  Their Bacon & Eggs appetizer (pork belly and frittata) was delicious.  So was the caesar salad.  I also liked the dessert we tried, the chocolate Marsala with salted caramel gelato.

But the entrees were only so-so.  My husband had the rustic Bolognese, which was tasty but not really worth the price.  I had the lamb ragout, and it was horribly disappointing and impossible to finish.  Something in the sauce tasted burnt/too bitter.

All in all, the place wasn't bad, but there is better for the price.  And the service was pretty horrible.  The servers were nice enough but not professional.  Given the expected (and given) tip, I think they should have behaved better.

5 stars customer service. Brian was our waiter. Never let our drinks go empty. Good staff. They kept the tables clean, and dishes taken away when we were done. Great staff. 

4 stars Prime New York. It was good. Not a lot of flavor. Ordered med rare and it arrived med rare. 

3 stars Herb Crusted Prime Rib. Was disappointed with this one. Ordered med rare. Was well done. Pictures attached. Couldn't finish it because it was so tough and dry.  For the price you should get this right. 

5 stars creamed spinach. Best I've ever had. Very tasty. 

4 stars shoestring fries. This was a bit funny. Fries are paper thin. If you want to dip it in ketchup it'll break up. Overly salty. Tasted ok. Just make regular size fries or anything thicker. 

Ratings might not reflect this, but Ruth's Chris in the Silver Legacy is a better option.

1 star. Amazed at the reviews.  Wish I had a better experience.  11am on a Thursday.  

Definitely will not return. No idea how this place is rated so high. Disappointed in everything. Prices were decent, and is probably the best part of this trip.  

1 stars Teriyaki chicken. It's fried!  Overdone and to crispy. Didn't taste good at all. The sauce was the best part. The small portion of over cooked rice didn't help. Veggie tempura was under cooked. Salad was ok. This is a hard dish to miss. How do you ruin basic chicken and rice?No quality control. I did notice a lack of pictures of this. Maybe the lesson is don't come to a Sushi place and get cooked food?

0 Star Sake/Maguro. Both were not fresh. Maguro was a bit tough, and overly slimy. Sake was slimy and just smelled bad. Why even put the lemon on? Look at the picture.  That white film on top.  Gross.

0 stars food allergies.  The Tempura veggie and fish were separate orders.  Why are they on the same dish.  You can kill somebody mixing this.  What a huge miss.  Some training to prevent this in the future?

1.5 stars Veggie Tempura.  Not sure where to start this one.  Look at the pictures.  It's worth a thousand words.  It was like a raw veggie mush.  
Zucchini, carrot, sweet potato, avocado.  

2 stars Miso soup.  Hard to ruin this one.  Tiny pieces of tofu.  Weird taste, but edible.  

1 star customer service.  1st.  Miso soup came out first.  2nd.  Teriyaki Chicken.  3rd.  15 minutes later everything else came out?  Amazed.  Slow on the refills.  The cooks/chefs/wait staff have no idea about food allergies is a huge problem.  Please fix this for the next person.  Some of the staff was friendly.  Not very attentive.  Let our drinks go empty.

Our organizer for this event  is NOT a professional event planner.  She is a normal person whether she is retired, or has career.

2018 update three years later - all still applies, still smells like an ash tray regardless of how many times they turn the air over per hour.  Went last night, was only there two hours, came home and my wife said my clothes reeked of smoke.

-----

From a casino perspective, I'd give it a few negative stars, but I won't give it just a one since they do occasionally have good musicians scheduled, and being able to go from music to bar to hotel room is pretty convenient.  I have a separate five star review for their Fresh Harvest restaurant, specifically the Sunday buffet, but that isn't factoring in here since that venue has its own listing on Yelp.

Okay, on to the casino.  It is absolutely horrid.

1) Drinks are not free, even for reasonably higher limit players, drinks are very expensive, and drinks are hard to come by due to far fewer drink staff than there should be.

2) It is smokey, at all times.  The exception is the poker room which thankfully went smoke free a number of years ago, but you still leave the place smelling like a chimney since there's enough smoke floating in from the gaming area to stink you up.

3) Table games like blackjack all operate with continuous shufflers, so you're rarely, if ever, going to get any runs going.  On busier nights, they raise all the minimums up to $25.  The good thing though, is that with continuous shufflers, high minimums and horrible service, hard core blackjack players tend to stay away, so you're not going to encounter that many people getting attitudes with each other for not playing proper strategy, since the only people playing are drunks and those that have no idea how to play.

4) The slots are horribly low paying.  You can easily burn through $100 and might get a few free spins.  Compared to Vegas, or even NOLA or Mississippi since those markets are more like Tampa, you might as well just burn your money rather than put it in a slot machine here.

5) No craps.  Well no real craps; they have a video game thing.

6) The video poker is even worse, so please be very very careful about reading the payouts before you sit down at a given machine.  It is not uncommon to find a bunch of 7/5 or even a  6/5 machine, but where they get really tricky is they'll mix in a few random 8/5 or even 9/6 machines, but then dramatically reduce the payout for a royal flush, from what is often at 4000 credits in Vegas to 2500 credits.  They're increasing the house edge by a huge amount.  They'd win overall either way, they're simply that greedy here.  If you have to play, at least seek out one of the very very few 9/6 machines, if there are any left.

All in all, this is an okay music venue if you want to be able to party, drink and not drive or get a taxi, but other than that, there is not much reason to go here unless you like throwing money away on gaming designed to take advantage of people who don't know any better.  I'd recommend catching an $80 Southwest flight to NOLA to gamble in a proper casino with all games.

Being from the motor city- I am a bit of a Middle Eastern purist.  Dearborn, which is outside of Detroit, boasts a huge Middle Eastern population.  Tucson has this weird Greek Middle Eastern fusion confusion thing going on.  Gyros and tzatziki =Greek.  Tzatziki is also not to be described as garlic sauce.  Garlic sauce is toum, which to my knowledge can only be found at Ali Baba in town.  I digress and step down from the soap box.  Forgive me, I just crave Middle Eastern.

However, the chicken shawarma is nicely marinated, moist, small pieces (yet abundant) of breast meat sautéed in a pan.  It is not the traditional shawarma on a spicket.  (That can be found a Babylon Market in Chicken and Beef).  The marinade is lemony deliciousness.  It comes with salad, green beans, and hummus and "garlic sauce".  It is not garlic sauce it is a tahini sauce.  But it is good.  My husband loves the garlicky green beans, I prefer the rice, which they will substitute. 

Seating is tight, so be patient.  It took a while to get our menus as well.  But once the service started, it got much better and the food did not disappoint.  Fresh and flavorful.  I still crave the Middle Eastern back home, but I look forward to many return visits here in the meantime.

Voted on eater.com as one of the 21 new ice cream destinations in the country! 
 
Located in the old Quizinos location at Houghton and Broadway is the Screamery.  It is a welcomed addition to that side of town which is lacking in dining options.  I  have to admit I am not a big ice cream person, BUT I had this ice cream almost two weeks ago and I have not stopped thinking about it.  I love that they are a part of the local hand crafted food movement.  They are the first in Tucson to make their own pasteurized cream in house.   And they only use organic ingredients including milk from grass-fed cows and free-range chicken eggs.  As you walk in you are greeted with the ice cream features displayed in the freezer.  There were three girls scooping away and one working the cash register.  To the left of the entrance was some delicious cucumber and fruit infused water found in many spas that really hit the spot.  It was a super nice touch.  Behind the cash register is a large chalkboard menu describing the 16 flavors.  You can also see the 15-gallon stainless steel pasteurization machine, which allows them to control the ice cream creation prcoess down to the base.  Think of it as ice cream science.  

Flavors: Cotton candy; Game Day uses stout from Thunder Canyon, chocolate covered pretzels in a chocolate ice cream; Housemade bacon almond brittle in a Makers Mark, bacon, vanilla ice cream; Sonoran chocolate with chile flakes; ice cream infused with lemons and handmade vanilla cookies; Smores; Sweet Cream Honey Comb with local honey; Chocolate; Vanilla uses vanilla beans from Mexico; Strawberry with roasted strawberries; Peach;  Dairy free coconut fudge; Coffee Toffee with local coffee; Ooey Gooey Buttercake; Mississippi Mudpie; Salted Caramel with fleur de sel and Aunt Michelle's cracker cookie; blackberry merlot.  Salted caramel was a game changer.  Hands down the best salted caramel ever.  Dream worthy.  To be noted you can get two flavors ina  single scoop serving.

The also have sundaes, floats including a cheerwine float, hand made waffle cones, regular cones, milk shakes and hand crafted bottled drinks.  You can get buttercake, chocolate chip cookies and brownies as sides.  

Check out the farmhouse!  EIGHT scoops with a cookie, brownie, and buttercake  bottom with your choice of toppings.  

Bonus they are open to 10 on most days, and 9 on Sundays.  Keep your eyes peeled they are always adding new flavors.

A friend got me some donuts from here before when she was in NOLA.  Finally, I came to NOLA and had to try them for myself.  I love how they have different flavors everyday.  I came here and got the cookie dough, loved it! Definitely tasted like cookie dough.  The donuts are reasonably priced for the huge size they are too!

They also servw different food items and coffee too! Definitely a try if you're in NOLA!

I came here to try one of the best cheesesteaks in Philly, and it didn't disappoint.  The sandwich was great.  I do recommending getting the grilled onion, total game changer. We got it with and without onions and you can tell a big difference!

These donuts are made pretty much right in front of you.  You see the workers making the dough and adding the glaze.  It's pretty cool to see as you stand in line and wait.  My friends and I wanted to try all the different flavor of donuts Beiler's has to offer, specifically some of their fritters.  Sad part, the fritters ran out.  Good part is that Beiler's was willing to let you pay for it now, then come about 45 minutes later to get a fresh batch of fritters!  You can cut the long line and go right to the front and let them know, and you'll get your warm, fresh donut you wanted before!

The donuts are VERY cheap for their quality, taste, and where it's located.  6 bucks can get you half a dozen! You guys are awesome, great donuts in Philly!

I came here for a quick lunch and sat at the bar.  I ordered only one thing I wanted to try.  Their half dozen BBQ oysters.  Delicious!

They fry the oysters and then dip them in cheese and this special sauce. Love the sauce! Great service at the bar! You also get complimentary loaf of french bread, which I used to dip leftover sauce! Yummy place!

This is definitely the place to be if you're visiting Philadelphia.  It is pretty similar to the Grand Central Market in LA, but there are a lot more stores/vendors/restaurants.  There is a pretty large seating area and plenty of stuff to try.  I specifically tried Beiler's donuts because that was one of the donut place I wanted to try the most.  I think no matter what you're craving for, Reading Terminal Market will have it.  Stop by and check it out when you're in philly!

Not worth all the hype this place gets.  Definitely not worth all the stress and hassle from ordering, and waiting around for your food.  This place is jammed with people packed like sardines inside.  People trying to push their way out of the crowd.  People waiting on line.  And people waiting around for their order.  I've smashed myself onto the side table trying to get out of peoples way while I wait for my food.  So hectic!  

This is the way it is:
To order, you get in line, that's snaking out the door.  Once inside, you realized how tiny the place is.  It's cramped with people, feeling a bit claustrophobic  Before you get to the front of the line, be sure to know what you want to order.  If you don't know yet, the wait staff may get angry and start yelling.  Look at the abbreviated menu that's hanging behind the counter.  Choose your sandwich then tell them what add ons you want on it.  After you put in your order, they will then ask you for your first name and last name initial.  They will call you when your food is ready.  Now, try to move out of that area and towards the front door, otherwise they will scream at you (because it's noisy in there) to get out of the way.  You don't pay until your sandwich is ready.

To help you out, here is a brief menu.
Most popular steak sandwich selections are:
regular steak  ($8.25)
cheese steak  ($9)
pepper steak  ($9)
pepper cheese steak  ($9.75)
mushroom steak  ($9)
mushroom cheese steak  ($9.75)

Choose a cheese option:
american cheese: free
provolone: $.030
cheese whiz: $.030

The free extra add ons for the steak sandwiches are: 
Fried onion
raw onion
sweet peppers
banana peppers
hot crushed peppers
ketchup
mayo
marinara sauce

Add ons for additional $.075
roasted green peppers
mushrooms
extra cheese
pepperoni
lettuce and tomato

Finally!  My name was called.  I paid for my sandwiches and maneuvered my way out the door.  Finally!  Fresh air and freedom!   Away from that jammed crowd of people!  Gah!

Seating.  Inside, is counter seating and a few tables/ chairs but the place is seriously jammed packed with people, that it's impossible or difficult to sit. Outside are a few picnic tables.  They are usually packed with people but good thing my peeps were outside holding the table while I ordered food for everyone.  Keep in mind, you just might end up standing outside and eating.  Or take the sandwich some place else to eat.  

I ordered a cheese steak with mushrooms.  I unwrapped it.  Where's the mushrooms???  After close inspections, there were about 3 small slices  at the end of the sandwich!  My friend made out like a bandit.  She had 6 slices.  I think that's enough to make one whole mushroom!  Wow!

The fried onions were cut in random big and little pieces.  I would have preferred smaller uniform pieces.  It wasn't pleasant chomping into a big semi raw onion piece.  

The only good thing I can say is that it is a big sandwich and they do give you a large amount of meat.  But the meat is cut into tiny bits (almost like ground meat), which makes the sandwich a bit mushy.  I didn't like the taste/ texture of little meat bits.  Meat was bland.  Also there wasn't enough cheese.

They also have chicken steak sandwiches, cold cut hoagies and burgers.  But since 99% of the people are ordering beef steak sandwiches, if you order anything else, there will be an easily over 30 minute wait.

A word to the wise:  The sandwich can get pretty messy from the melted cheese or sauces, so bring some wet naps, for clean up.

Final note:  If all you care about is having a lot of meat covered with cheese in the sandwich, then you will love this steak sandwich.  But its still not worth all the stress and hassle.  More discerning cheese steak palates should look elsewhere.  Cash only.  No bathroom.  No french fries.

Wow this place is good.  I say that because it's 1 million percent better than the restaurant that used to be there (if you catch my drift).  

It'll run you about $10 for a meal at lunch, plus shared appetizers/drinks.  So, not a grab-and-go.  So far, my favorite thing on the menu is the side item brussel sprouts. DANG!  They are so delicious, you won't miss the fries.  

The chicken fried chicken sandwich and the truffled egg salad sammy are amazing.  Some of the freshest ingredients you can get for lunch in MidCity.  The crowning glory is the chicken and "waffle" sandwich, though.  The waffle used as the outter layer is actually a delicious bread drizzled in maple syrup and dusted with powered sugar.  It's not overwhelmingly sicky-sweet, but complementary with the chicken.  

After your meal, the server brings an Ipad to the table and swipes your card right there.  No muss-no fuss.  

I haven't been there for dinner yet, but the waiter was nice enough to drop off a dinner menu.  It looks delicious and I can't wait to try the pork ribs!!

Verti Marte is the corner store in the Quarters where everyone knows your name...or at least your sandwich.  They're open during this crazy-coronatime, even on Sunday's, and their friendliness and willingness to serve the neighborhood is so appreciated.  

We stopped in on a "Jazz Festing in Place" Sunday in search of a PoBoy and were treated the the fattest, most delicious, shrimp falling out slice of heaven.  The bread is different than the typical French we're used to - it's softer, with sesame seeds.  Soaks up the fry from the shrimp, mayo, and tomato juice nicely.  

Verte Marte itself has a good selection of necessities like cold beers, cold meds, paper products, and some canned goods.  It's a small shop, but definitely caters to the folks who live in the area - not necessarily just tourists.

I had high expectations for Lee's.  Lee's came highly recommended and has high recommendations on Google Maps and other sites.  I got the Korean BBQ cheesesteak.  It was good.  This may have been all night off night for all of us. The college students are still on winter break so things were slow.  Very tasty Korean BBQ cheesesteak and the veggies make it healthy.  I was hoping to be wow'd.  Good Cheesesteak experience.

One of my favorite food vlogger recently moved to St. Louis and he highly praised Chilispot for having the BEST Chinese in the St. Louis. When I heard that, I was like I definitely gotta check it out for myself. Situated on Olive, Chilispot has a handful of fierce competitions specializing in Chinese food. Despite that fact, they still observe an influx of customers coming in everyday. 

I really like the atmosphere and decorations of the restaurant. It's surprising very spacious and can fit many guests. 

The prices are very standard for a Chinese restaurant. They offer many common dishes as well as specialties dishes (Si-chuan cuisine). We ordered five main dishes and a bowl of beef soup. The food was so delicious. My favorite would be the spicy popcorn chicken, deep fried tofu, and the stir-fried beef. The food was very well-seasoned. It's neither too salty nor bland, which is sometimes hard to achieve in Chinese restaurants. Don't be intimidated by the spiciness because it's not that bad. The type of spiciness from the Si-chuan peppercorn is different from your regular spiciness. You will not feel any burn but tingy-ness and numbness on your tongue but it's worth it. The portion size is very decent for one person and reasonable if you have a large party. 

I'm very pleased with my visit and would love to return for more!

I had an incredibly unpleasant and dissapointing experience at Phoebe's a few weeks back. I had plans to have some friends over and order dinner for all of us, and had been wanting to try bbq from Phoebe's. I went to their website, where they give you the option of ordering from a few different online-order vendors, and I chose the Grub Hub option, because I know that ordering with Grub Hub makes it easy to enter any special preparation or delivery instructions. (With each item you select, a box pops up that says 'Enter any special instructions'.

Because my friends have various gluten,soy, gelatin allergies, I entered 'sauce on the side' for all of my orders. Simple enough.

I walked down the street to pick up my order 15 or so minutes later. When I got to Phoebe's, I asked the girls behind the counter if they wouldn't mind just opening up one of the containers so I could see how much food it was.  She said no, because it was wrapped tightly in saran wrap.

I explained to her that I had never eaten there before, and didn't know the portion sizes, so I wanted to make sure I had ordered enough food to feed all of my friends, so that if I hadn't, I could order some more.  Still, she was entirely unwilling to unwrap the meal. This was frustrating, but I figured I would just step outside, open it up myself to see if I'd purchased enough, and walk back in to add more food to my order if needed. At that point, someone (presumably the owner) emerges from the back of the kitchen, and asked what was going on. I reiterated my request, and he says "How many people do you need to feed?".  I said "5 or 6". And he said "Nah, it won't be enough". 

Excellent, that was all I needed to know. As I was deciding what else to order, he took  the 5 seconds to unwrap my existing food for me to show me how much was in there. I noticed it was covered in sauce, so I mentioned that I had requested 'sauce on the side' for all of my items purchased. 

At this point, everyone there was clearly annoyed with me. I swear, I am not usually a high-maintenance restaurant orderer AT-ALL, but from the minute I walked in there, EVERYTHING had become a huge production due to their blatant  lack of basic customer service.

So he goes to the other side of the kitchen, to check the print-out of my grub hub order, and sure enough, 'Sauce on the Side' was in the Special Instructions section of all of my items purchased. 

Then he proceeds to tell me that they "don't look at those parts of the order" .... That GrubHub provides this 'Special Instruction' option on their website, but Phoebe's has a "policy" that they don't look at that section.  HUH?? Mistakes obviously happen, it's no big deal, but nothing makes me more angry than someone who will piss on my back and tell me it's raining. I know he was just trying to cover his mistake, but it was such an absurd and unnecessary thing to say.

At this point, I am visibly annoyed. I suggest this is something that he work out in his agreement with GrubHub, as it seemed a bit ridiculous for a customer to be prompted to enter special instructions for their meal, when they will "not even be looked at" by the person making it. 

The presumed owner then says to me (...I'm getting heated again just thinking about it) "Are you ok? You seem aggitated". ...And not in a 'I'm concerned for your happiness' way. In a 'I am a smug asshole' way.

At this point, I had to leave before I lost it. I took none of my food with me, so I can't even comment on its quality.

I was floored with how rude and unaccommodating they had been. I'll never even think about going there again.

On the bright side, a representative from Grub Hub called me a few minutes later, saying that he had just spoken to the owner at Phoebe's about the issue with the recent order. I told him what had gone down. Even though I told him that the issue had nothing to do with Grub Hub, he apologized for my unpleasant experience and gave me a gift card credit to Grub Hub, to show that they appreciate and value my business. That is my kind of customer service. 

0 stars for Phoebe's (10 stars for Grub Hub!)

Great little spot - friendly - great attention to detail - clams are awesome! Rolls are awesome! Margarita Pizza is awesome!
We've been here twice recently and will return soon for more clams and to try some new selections.

$15 rib night, yes please! 
My husband had them and he said they might have been the best ribs he's ever had & he's had a lot.

They were fall off the bone tender and their sauce is perfectly balanced. Great caramelization as well and smoky flavor. Comes with a choice of side. This was a full rack, so he could only eat half. 

I had the Shrimp and Crawfish étouffée and it was very good as well. Great qualify shrimp & crawfish, very flavorful & perfectly cooked rice.

Their cocktails are always on point. 

And if you're debating on appetizers, I highly recommend starting off with the smoked drumsticks.  They are phenomenal and ask for all three sauces on the side: sweet chili sauce, spicy chili sauce and House made barbecue. 

Service is always excellent as well. Efficient, friendly & knowledgeable.

And last but not least, the ambience is fantastic. Beautifully restored building and great outdoor dining with beautiful fire pit. 

Next time you're in Tarpon stop in.

The meal was so nuanced that I'm not sure how to describe it.  It was micro portions & tweezified but so beautifully executed you thanked them for it.  It sounds like a backhanded compliment I know but it was really an impressive and unique meal.

We started off with the cheese & charcuterie plate which was a good opener.   

Everything was like art on a plate. Some of our stand outs were the pork dumplings (perfectly crisp), the braised short rib gnocchi, the oxtail pierogi & the warm potato torta with duck egg yolk cooked to perfection in an unctuous olive oil bath.

The only very minor disappointments for me were the pork jowl dish (wish they'd still had the pork belly everyone raves about).  The Jowl was just too fatty for my taste.  And they had changed their desserts up.  The two we had were good but didn't quite live up to the rest of the meal.

Again minor quibbles over an excellent meal.  Our sever Bailey did an outstanding job guiding us through it all.  Spot on service.

Highly recommended.  Go with at another couple  so you can try most of the menu & bring a few bottle of wine to share as their corkage fee was quite reasonable.  This place definitely does the Tampa Bay Area proud.  My kudos to the chefs and owners.  Thanks for a great dining experience.

One of the best Mexican restaurants I've been too since moving here from San Jose California.
Homemade tortillas, great service and Blood Orange Margaritas.
The Molcajete is enough for 2. 
And hands down the best Mole I've ever had and I lived in Morelia in Mexico for a few months.
Can't wait to go back!

Holy heck! Finally a freakin' decent donut place in North Pinellas.  Omg Duncan Donuts can officially hang their head in shame with their stale donut facsimiles.
Stopped by the other day and this place rocks. Clean, neat, hip and great service.
But more importantly the donuts rock!  So far I've had the apple fritter (pillowy, crispy deliciousness the size of a small asteroid), the toasted coconut donut (yum!) and a phenomenal glazed donut.
Will be back!  If you are looking for a good donut in a 15 mile radius get the to Jupiter donuts now:)

After making our way further down the cluster of Broadway & towards the water front area we came across this place, it was time to sit, drink & have a bite to eat.
Another grand multi level place, this one is pretty big each floor has it's own thing going on, we made our way to the roof top. 
After sitting down & looking at the menu, we were told food could only be ordered in the first floor.. seriously? not cool they should at least tell u this before hand or at minimum not have menu's available. 
Anyhow food I had the Corn since I wasn't starving, but it was bigger than I expected the order has 2 corns & they are covered in cheese & sauce, I must say it was great very tasty, really enjoyed this. 
My company had the Pulled pork tacos 2 tacos & corn, tacos are crazy loaded so much on them it's hard to eat together, nice tasting meat.
Drinks we gave the Frozen moonshine a try, at first we were excited to try it & figure it be great, it was not what a disappointment it was $11 dollars for a frozen lemonade which is what it tasted like, waste of money on the drink, ok taste wise zero alcohol & it was supposed to be moonshine seems like the moonshine lost it's shine!
Roof top area is nice, big open space, nice waterfront views .. not much on service since u get everything yourself at least that's what it is on the roof top.

Oh Hattie's the one constant place we were told to check out so we did.. brace yourself for the long lines & wait times. 
we waited about 40-45 minutes in line once inside it's such a small place u get a few seconds of cool air lucky if u get a seat inside, we sat outside. 
Food we went with the Chicken sandwich both mild & medium, one with Mac & cheese the other with Fries, also had an order of the wings. 
To drink we had the Whiteclaw, raspberry nice & cold it was refreshing. 
verdict on the chicken, whoa!! definitely very good, nice flavor to the chicken, very crispy. 
The wings were good as well but no need it was just too much fried hot chicken, the honey mustard sauce gave it a nice taste. Good Mac & cheese it has a nice spicy kick to it, Fries were very good about the only thing that wasn't spicy. 
The long line & wait time's are a nuisance it really takes away from enjoying your food, can't say that it was worth the long wait but the chicken is certainly worth a try.

Walking around Broadway & we happen to walk by this place without realizing what it was.. that being the longest bar we figured why not check it out. 
It really is the LONGEST bar lord this thing just keeps going back .. & back!! big open space, band playing in the bar below, band sounded great with the country music playing. 
Drinks I gave the Nudies Honky Tonk IPA beer a try, this was not bad bitter taste but good amount of alcohol.
They like many in the area have a roof top bar as well. Roof top was not bad small area the outside part it was early in the day so it was not crowded. they have normal music playing in the roof top. 
very cool fun decor, they have a freaking car hanging on display pretty fun... lost of outfits from different artist on display & even one from Elvis fun to look at. 
Cool bar, gift shop available in the back, service was good & prices are not bad.

We were walking around trying to figure out where to eat & stumbled onto this place...good find.
we were seated right away got our drinks & ordered some food. Two of us got the Grilled chicken Po Boy sandwich ....delicious ! In my opinion it was the best po boy sandwich I tried while visiting NOLA. 
My other friend had the Chicken fried steak po boy , really good as well u can get some gravy on the side, just note the gravy is a separate charge its not a lot just 99 cents. the gravy is great for dipping the fries.
We liked this place & decided to come back another night after some late night partying  this time we got some breakfast. 
I had the egg & sausage biscuit , really good ...one of  my friends had the deja vu eggwich good as well & the other girl had a chicken po boy with some fries, very good fries here nice taste with seasoning on them. 
This place is a great find in the area , good service, cheap prices & they are open 24/7  when partying in the area its good to know u can get something other than a not so great pizza slice like I had one of the night's somewhere on bourbon can't even recall the place. 
This place is good decent  cheap food ...if visiting again I would gladly return.

Yes people, it's loud I don't understand how  u can complain about this place being too loud? what the heck else is it supposed to be!!
This place certainly stands out as one of the loudest & biggest on Broadway, great location in the middle of it all no matter what time a day u walk by or stop in this place it seems to always be crowded.
First night in.. Very cool looking place the way it is set up, loveddd the glow in dark outfits the bartenders wear very cool. 
We sat down for drinks & tried some of the local beer a Southern IPA great beer nice taste. 
Second night in & it was even crazier during the weekend, this place is 5 floors, 5 different bands all playing a decent variety of music. the Mezzanine is a mad house too jammed packed. 
Second & Third floors are a mix of music, second floor has more of a bar feel to it. Final floor is the roof top nice set up & u get nice views of the city. 
One thing I'd like to point out are the bathroom, very cool mirrors & one of the cleanest bathrooms I noticed in the entire area. it can't be easy to keep this place clean with so many people coming in & out ALL DAY. 
This place ended up being a favorite for us because of the great vibes, only place I noticed real cops as security. 
Good atmosphere , quick enough service we definitely enjoyed our time here.

Walking around our first night in town on a Wednesday we decided to check this place out, for a Wednesday it was pretty packed. 
Multi level below they offer live entertainment, cool looking bar area. we made our way upstairs after a few. 
Top level they have a DJ playing a decent mix of music good variety, big open space & roof top area. 
Drinks, first tried the Fat bottom beer, good beer I stuck to this, later had some Fireball shots & my company later tried the My kind of party punch, not terrible but I thought it was too sweet. 
Upstairs is a bit of hot mess, floors are super sticky & bathrooms are a mess (the dirtiest of all that I noticed). 
Service could be better bartenders did not really pay attention to u, we had to keep waving them down to get drinks.  
I gave it the 4 stars because of the roof top area & the fact that they have a DJ playing regular music, It's good to have other options of music & not be forced to listen to just country breaks up your night much better.

Final joint we checked out on our last night, very cool place glad we decided to give it try.  
Live country music on the main floor, the upstairs level had a DJ actually playing house music I was so glad to hear this needed that break from all the live bands u come across, it was refreshing to hear something else nice to be on the roof. 
Drinks we had some Lagunitas beer, can't go wrong good beer. very nice roof top I liked the set up plenty of tables set up nicely with still enough room to dance & move around. 
Good music playing, glad they stuck to dance music, this place has a great vibe, service was good & prices are not bad we enjoyed our time here.

In Chinese food feud spanning two states, the original Xi'an Famous Food from NY contacted this Philly restaurant f.k.a. Xi'an Famous and asked them to change their name to avoid an infringement suit. Hence the new name, Xi'an Sizzling Woks. Since my first visit, the 10 item hand printed menu has expanded to a vast noodley menu that I had to explore.
 

 
1) Wontons in chili oil (hot appetizer section, $4.95) are a very different version that those served at local Szechuan joints like Han Dynasty, these are much larger and thicker, but no less enjoyable; more like the wontons found in wonton soup. Spicy chili oil, scallions, and sesame seeds covered these pork filled packages.
 
2) Shanghai bokchoy with green soy beans (cold vegetable appetizer section, $5.50) is a good cooling snack to munch on in between spicy bites of everything else.
 
 3) The Chef Recommendation section of the menu is a good place to get to know. The new menu includes a good amount of dishes you could find elsewhere. But the Chef's recs are the best place to order the real Xi'an style plates. This is where to find the signature Xi'an liang pi noodles. They were exactly the same as when I tried it on my first visit- spicy, slippery, almost as good as the  NYC Xi'an Famous Foods version.
 
4) The spicy sour minced pork noodles ($6.95) was served in a large bowl with spaghetti sized noodles and a "hot and sour" style broth. The menu did not indicate this was a soup and I was expecting something different, though I enjoyed the layered flavors of the soup.
 

5) We noticed an intriguing plate of noodles on the table next to us and our waiter explained it was the Sauteed spicy chicken and noodle plate, "good for a group," he said. The giant plate of noodles is definitely not for one person and was the most expensive thing we ordered at $16.95. The noodles were insanely wide and thick, and were unevenly torn which leads me to believe they were made in house. Under the noodles, a spicy sauce with hints of curry. On top of the noodles, pieces of moist chicken on the bone and potatoes. I loved this; noodles like this are so fun to eat. I doubt you could find anything else like this in Philly.

I almost have to thank La Cocina - because from here until eternity we now have a story that starts like this: 

"Hey, remember that time we went to La Cocina and they gave our friend's birthday cake to another table?"

To which they will respond: 

"You mean the cake that had her name written on it?"  - and we will laugh. 

But I'm ahead of myself. Let's start at the beginning.... 

12 of us went to La Cocina for a good friend's birthday. Food was fine. Nachos, varieties of tacos, polenta fries, quinoa bowls, burritos, etc... No one was WOW'ed, but nothing was sent back. Nothing highly recommend-able.

The ambiance IS fabulous, and was absolutely the number one factor it was picked as our celebration spot. This place truly tops my Quintessential Tucson list. 

Service was slow, but hey, it was a (second) Saturday night and they were busy. It wasn't even a thing. We were having a great time. 

However, it was windy and getting chillier by the minute. Many of us were not dressed to enjoy the weather, so we decided to take the cake my friend had brought (from Nadine's bakery) somewhere else to get out of the wind.

We asked our server for the cake, and he returned with - not her cake. So she sent him away to look again. 

He came back with a second cake - also, not her cake. 

At this point he thought she was joking. She was not joking. She explained that her cake was in a box, not in plastic wrap like cakes 1 and 2, and sent him away again. 

So then a manager came over with cake number 1 - STILL not her cake. 

So, as it turns out, her cake, with her name written on it in icing, was given to another table. 

WHAT.

Yes.

Her customized birthday cake was given to another table. Her heart was broken. The entirety of our food was on the house, but truly nothing could right this wrong. We left the table sad and completely dumbfounded... but also kind of - fine. We understand that someone simply messed up... and some other people greedily went along with it. Humans will be humans. 

I mean hey, it was a nice cake.

Truthfully, this review wouldn't have existed if, as we were all leaving, we hadn't seen the La Cocina staff, including but not limited to the doorman, eating their own plated slices of my good friend's cake.

I'll tellya... good luck not crying on your birthday when the staff of your restaurant of choice "loses" your cake - and then eats it in front of you.

East Coast used to have great subs. Huge, juicy, lots of meat without an upcharge to add enough to call it a cheesesteak. That was a decade ago. 

Now the amount of meat is laughable. I ordered a corned beef sub that had 1/8 of a cup of meat on it. I know because I was so displeased that I took the meat off the sandwich and measured it.  

Sad times.
Service was horrible. Food was tasteless. We've been before and it was delicious. Not sure what happened, but it's no longer good. We won't be back.
When I die I want to be buried with a Lee's cheesesteak. I love this place! The food is always great and prepared fast. I definitely recommend stopping by if you're in the west philly area!

We came here for a bday party and we loved the food and the atmosphere. Service was great and their ceviche was tasty and juicy. We had the veggie entrée and their tres Leeches desert. We ended the night in the basement with their flamingo dancers.

No masks required. Sign posted on door that reads "masks optional you're choice"

Kinda comical. 
The people who don't know the difference between your and you're would totally be the same who don't understand the importance of wearing a mask to keep our community open

This place was just horrible..... I wish that I never stepped  into this place. We went with a party of 16 around 9pm. Instead of waiting to seat us together they seat us at three different tables with two waitress. First of all our gumbo came out cold not only once but twice! When we asked for the Manger she came over picked up the gumbo and asked if wanted to heat up again. I guess she thought that 3 is a charm! We said NO!
