NEVER did she apologize nor offer to make the poor service better. We then got our check and we were charged a 20% tip charge when we did not even sit together. I was so upset so I just paid the bill and left. I will ever return to this place when I  New Orleans. There were other issues that happened but I don't want to even give this place any more of my energy or time! HORRIBLE!!!!!!

I like burgers, I like local eateries and I like this neighborhood. So I was wicked disappointed after all the 'rave reviews' from the internet and 2 friends that this place sucked. 

Yes, it's a low blow and a word I don't take lightly. But 'Burger Up' deserves it.

It's one star comes from the fact that it's cute; extremely cute actually. As for the food? My burger came out charred after I asked for medium rare because I was excited to see they had fresh beef from the area. It was so overdone it could  have been a freezer patty from Iowa. My fries were served in a trendy tin cup. Um, in theory cute. However, common sense and half a brain would tell you that all my bottom fries will be soggy and disgusting! (which they were) The 'freshmade' bun was too thick and didn't taste fresh at all.

The saddest part of all is this: I am a condiment whore. I seriously love condiments and think a good one would make me eat shoe leather. But their 'fancy maple ketchup' tasted like....ketchup and the poshly named ranch? You guessed it, tasted like, well, ranch.

As for service the lone beer I ordered (nothing on the adult beverage menu under $5 or $6 bucks, btw) came right away but it took ages for the food to come out. I kind of want to give this place a second chance, but the steep prices keep me from doing so.

I will take Cheeseburger Charlie's over this. Lame.

It takes an effort for me to think Pizza is barfy, but everything about this place was wrong.

Like its not arsenal by any means, but the bottom was charred like it was attempting it. Too bad the cheese was garden variety shredded 'white'. If a menu is *this* limited; everything should taste amazing. 

Maybe the specialties are better, but a cheese slice should be solid. Burnt + bland = one star. They'd be better off if they consulted my school cafeteria on where they purchase their Sysco freezer pies. 

It seems very hit or miss here on yelp - my recommendation is to get a consistent recipe/cook in the kitchen to execute your 'generations old recipes'.

***Jeni's is based out of Ohio and not Tennessee, but it is still an exceptional artisan ice cream shop; Jeni's utilizes great Ohio dairy, small farms and non-traditional ingredients to create very creamy and unique ice cream***

This Jeni's location is similar to the East Nashville location; this location may have more seating (though outdoor seating is not available here).  Like that other Jeni's location, this Jeni's is from the very highly regarded Jeni's in Ohio that utilizes Ohio dairy, produce from small farms and non-traditional ingredients to create outstanding ice cream that is dense, smooth, creamy, and distinct in flavor.

I had three flavors here and the pumpernickel was easily the best.  With the pumpernickel base and the soft and addictive pumpernickel gravel, this flavor really recreates the experience of eating pumpernickel bread by delivering a hearty, rye-like flavor that is perfectly balanced by a subtle sweetness. 

The brown butter almond brittle was also great.  Like the pumpernickel, this flavor showcases how good Jeni's is at integrating mix-ins with ice cream.  The almond brittle delivered a different flavor than the ice cream base as well as a nice crunch, but the pieces were also small enough that it did not detract from the very creamy and smooth ice cream.  The brown butter ice cream was also very good; it had a unique flavor and was not simply a caramel that you often get with brown butter ice cream elsewhere. 

I also had the buckeye state, which was peanut butter ice cream with tiny chocolate flakes.  This flavor is really only for peanut butter fans because the peanut flavor is incredibly strong and even recreates the experiencing of eating peanut butter due to how this ice cream delivers a stick-to-the-roof-of-your-mouth sensation. 

The trio ice cream usually comes with a waffle wedge, but I arrived before the store opened and the freshly made waffle wedges needed another minute or two.  I skipped the wedge because I had to catch a flight.  The waffle wedges are great at Jeni's though--light, freshly made, crispy, and a great flavor (they deliver a French wafer-like experience).

As mentioned, the dining room feels a little bigger than the Jeni's in East Nashville. This shop has the same very clean, high-end and contemporary rustic look of the East Nashville's Jeni's (rustic and contemporary but not Pinkberry minimalist).

I felt the service was friendlier at this Jeni's though service tends to be more friendly and welcoming at most places when there is not much of a crowd.

Prices are about what you would expect to pay at an artisan ice cream shop--similar prices to Bi-Rite Creamery in San Francisco, Three Twins in Napa and Salt & Straw in Portland, Oregon.

Jeni's is an exceptional ice cream shop and if you find yourself in Ohio or Nashville, going to one of their scoop shops is a must do if you are an ice cream fan.

There is free street parking outside of this Jeni's or in the nearby and nice residential area.

***The BBQ ribs at Pappy's are excellent and really stand apart from many ribs I have had; their sides like sweet potato fries and green beans are also very good for a quick order-at-the-counter restaurant***

Pappy's is a very popular order-at-the-counter BBQ restaurant in St. Louis (they were even filming a segment for a TV show on my visit).  The restaurant has a very cozy atmosphere.  There is a casual and homey decor (complete with red-and-white checkered tablecloth) that feels very friendly and not kitschy or faux.

What is also impressive about Pappy's is the crowd.  It is definitely a restaurant that attracts all walks of life.

Pappy's lunch menu features baby back ribs as one of their signature mains.  Sandwiches, pulled pork, beef brisket, and other meat options are also available.  I opted for the ribs, which came with white bread and two sides (I chose the sweet potato fries and the green beans).

The ribs were quite exceptional.  The ribs were very tender.  They were definitely not as fall-off-the-bone tender as ribs I've had elsewhere (I think both Houston's and Montgomery Inn may have more tender ribs), but they were tender enough and definitely juicy.

What really separated the ribs at Pappy's though was the outside crust and flavor.  There was a great crisp outside and you can really taste the smoky flavor.  While I have had many smoked ribs, this was the first time where I felt the smoky flavor was really prominent and quite enjoyable.  The ribs are even a slightly bit sweet to complement the smoky flavor.

There was also a good amount of fat on the ribs, which provided a lot of flavor and juiciness (the fat was not too grisly though; they did a good job of making it crisp).  The ribs really had a great flavor and they really felt different from even the great ribs I have had elsewhere across the country.  For the ribs, Pappy's provides a few good BBQ sauces, which range in sweetness, spiciness and smokiness.

In terms of the sides, the sweet potato fries were very good--great flavor and mostly crisp; some of the fries could have been more crisp, but they were very good overall.  The green beans were good too; they were definitely al dente, but the crispness and slight bitterness work; the green beans make for a nice contrast to the mostly hearty and filling sides here.

Service was very friendly and quick.

The price for the ribs was high for an order-at-the-counter restaurant, but Pappy's would not be more expensive than many of the highly rated order-at-the-counter restaurants in Los Angeles and I would say Pappy's would top a lot of them in terms of food quality.  The sandwiches seemed reasonably priced given the large portion sizes.

Pappy's is a very good BBQ restaurant.  I have yet to try BBQ in Los Angeles that is as good as Pappy's.  Baby Blues is decent, but Pappy's is less expensive and definitely more flavorful and distinct (the smoky flavor is a real plus at Pappy's).  St. Louis is known for BBQ and I think Pappy's is a must visit if you are in this area (whether you are a resident or just passing through).

I think Pappy's has its own free parking lot; you can also find metered street parking or pay parking in the nearby St. Louis University parking structure.

Brophy Brothers sits on the second floor of a building right on the pier in Santa Barbara.  The inside is crowded and lively.  Take away some of the seaside decor and the atmosphere kind of reminded me of Uncle Bill's Pancake House in Manhattan Beach--tables crammed together, boisterous people, noisy kitchen/plates, etc.

The outside patio (on a sunny day) provides a great view.  On a not-so-sunny day, the gloomy light coupled with strong smells from the ocean provides a less than inviting atmosphere.

Brophy Brothers makes a pretty decent New England clam chowder.  Served in a mug or bowl, the chowder was hot, creamy and flavorful.  The portion of clams was generous.  The chowder was garnished with parsley and oyster crackers.

The complimentary bread--a thick and crusty sourdough--was also quite good.

The entrees were below average, but I wonder if we just ordered wrong.  The batter for the fish (in the fish and chips) was not a good beer batter but an orangish and less crisp batter.  The fries were nothing special.

We also tried the seafood pasta, which consisted of linguini, shrimp, bay scallops, and a cream sauce.  The shrimp was the best part.  The bay scallops were rubbery.  The linguini was quite clumpy.  It was also kind of a bland dish.  The dish was also kind of clumsily put together on the plate.

Service was friendly and good.

There was a good mix of prices from some reasonably priced lunch-like options such as cheeseburgers, fried fish, chicken sandwiches to more expensive seafood entrees like ahi and halibut.  If I came back, I think I would like to try one of their seafood entrees, but I wonder (based on some of the food we had) if their more expensive options would be mediocre and thus very overpriced.

Brophy Brothers has a pretty lively atmosphere and I imagine there might be a few go-to items here.  If you can find those go-to items here, you may want to stick with them because this place did feel like one of those on the water places where it is more about the atmosphere and the view rather than the food.

Parking is available in an adjacent paid lot that supports several of the businesses on the pier.

***Recess utilizes local beef, seafood and vegetables to churn out satisfying and interesting food; it is one of the best restaurants in the Midwest***

SF, NY and Chicago have many great high-end restaurants.  Each of these cities feature talented chefs as well as talented cooks hoping to do more, a big audience with an appetite (and willingness to spend money) for ambitious food, and lots of competition.  With SF, you also get the great produce from Central and Northern California farms.  Other cities do not have these same advantages so it can be hard for them to compete.

Restaurants in other cities often feel like lesser versions of a SF or Chicago spot; Charleston in Baltimore is like that; there are enough good things about it that lets you know it is one of the best of the city, but the restaurant just does not feature the consistently great food you can get in SF.

Sometimes though, a truly special restaurant emerges--one where the quality of ingredients is high, the talent in the kitchen is strong, the cooking is consistent, and the chef has a really strong sense of what he/she wants the restaurant to be.  With these restaurants, it can feel like if Paul Kahan (Chicago's Blackbird) or David Kinch (Los Gatos' Manresa) had a restaurant in a city less known for food, this is what the restaurant might be like.  That is what Greg Hardesty's Recess feels like.

Recess features a nightly changing 4-course tasting menu (the final course is a choice between 2 desserts).  While the 1st course was average, all the other courses showcased excellent cooking techniques, high quality ingredients and great flavors.

The 1st course was an average high-end course.  It was a cured Copper River salmon club sandwich.  The problem with the sandwich was that it was mostly bread.  There was very little of the nice sounding fillings, which included cured salmon, arugula, tomato, caramelized onions, and bacon aioli.  The flavors just did not stand out; maybe if there were more of the core ingredients on a flatbread or puff pastry base, this course would have stood out more.

Everything else was great through.  I really liked how the fish course featured a Midwestern fish (Michigan whitefish) as opposed to the Atlantic or Pacific fish that many Midwestern restaurants fly in.  The fish had a great crispy skin like sea bass and it flaked very well.  Lake fish can often lack body, but the whitefish had a consistently smooth texture and a great flakiness that reminded me of sea bass or black cod.  The base of the dish was a creamy white bean puree that was mixed with fresh and soft Pacific red crab (which reminded me of Alaskan snow crab).  I really liked the cold, bright and slightly acidic sweet corn salad that really balanced out the dish.

The meat course was very good.  Often with meat courses, I find that maybe the beef shines, but the garnishes and sauces are not that great.  Or everything works on the plate except for the beef because it is poor quality or they do not get the temperature right.  That was not the case with the beef strip loin at Recess.  The steak had a great flavor and was very juicy and tender while the garnishes were great.  The broccoli rabe featured really aggressive seasoning, but it was a great mix of saltiness and heat.  I liked how the tops were blistered too so there was a good contrast between the soft center and the crispy edges.

The spaghetti squash carbonara was truly special.  With the spaghetti squash, it was a much lighter version of spaghetti carbonara, which really worked given the multiple courses and generous portions.  There was no sacrifice in the carbonara flavor though.  The cheese, egg and bacon elements all came across very well.

The meal ended with a dessert baked to order (few restaurants feature warm pastry items nowadays).  The oatmeal cookie had a great crispy and crunchy outside while the inside was moist and very hearty with great nuts and juicy dried fruit.  The Irish coffee ice cream was very creamy and not airy like a lot of ice creams.  It also had a distinct burn.

Service was great--very attentive and polite but also very friendly (like a great neighborhood restaurant).

Prices were great.  You get good portions and a great variety of ingredients.  A similarly priced 4-course menu in SF would mean getting dainty portions or maybe having to settle for uninteresting proteins, vegetables and preparations.

The decor was okay.  I liked the grade school chairs and the mix of modern, rustic and school themed decor.  I am not sure if everything went together though.

Recess is a very nice Midwestern restaurant.  I liked how it showcased proteins and vegetables from the local area as well as how the kitchen was strong at executing fish, meat and dessert.  I would come here often if I lived here.  It is definitely worth considering if you ever find yourself in or around Indianapolis.

Free street parking is available.

***The Catbird Seat offers a very minibar-esque experience; while the food was good to very good (though probably not exceptional), it is still a truly fun, worthwhile and even reasonably priced experience where you get to see all the food plated as well as get the opportunity to talk with the very personable and skilled chefs***

The Catbird Seat reminds me a lot of minibar by Jose Andres, which is one of the country's most unique dining experiences (even if the food was not exceptional).  You are seated right in the kitchen where you get to see the chefs plate all the food as well as talk with the chefs about the ingredients and the origins of the many courses served.  Like minibar, The Catbird Seat offers an alcoholic drink pairing that goes beyond wine pairings with the inclusion of beer and cocktails. They also offer a non-alcoholic pairing and like minibar, there is a discreet entrance with an elevator that takes you up to the intimate dining room.

The first thing about The Catbird Seat is that it is a rare dining experience where you really learn a lot about the food, the city and the chefs; you also get to see how it all comes together.  With mainstream America becoming much more interested in culinary these days and chefs becoming rock star-like figures, dining at The Catbird Seat is a really fun and behind-the-scenes type experience that many would love.

The second thing about The Catbird Seat is that the food is good to very good.  I did walk away enjoying the food more at Restaurant Eugene in Atlanta, Table 21 in Frederick and Beast in Portland, but there were still some great plates of food at The Catbird Seat.  Their duck breast featured duck from a very small local farm.  The duck was not as tender as Liberty Farms duck, but it was still good, had a great flavor as well as a really thick and crispy skin.  The duck was served with great burnt pears that had an extraordinary smoky quality.  There are several restaurants in the middle of the country and the South that create a smokiness and bark that really makes you realize how a lot of smoked food in big cities is simply a description on a menu and not what the food really is.

The beef course was good even if it was a little salty.  The beef course consisted of seared Wagyu rib-eye topped with dry-aged tartare.  The beef came with great fragrant greens--some lightly cooked and others more raw and bitter.

There was a lot of whimsical courses too like minibar and Alinea.  There was great smoked celery root topped with a BBQ sauce (great BBQ for vegetarians), a toasted and thick local ham sandwich with melted American cheese for dipping, a strong pork-flavored chip with herb-like and fragrant collard greens purée (also for dipping), and a take on Nashville's popular hot chicken that utilizes only the crispy chicken skin.

Like Alinea, there were also a lot of fun courses to eat like a bouquet of greens and herbs laced with candied pecans, nut butter and a creamy Asian-style dressing.  There was a potato dessert filled with cream and dusted to look exactly like a potato.  And finally, there was a cured sturgeon nigiri where the base was potato and not rice though the potato concoction looked like sushi rice and, in some ways, even had a similar texture.

There were areas where the food fell short.  They did a great job with east coast uni by pairing it with crispy rye breadcrumbs and juicy beets though the uni (while fresh) lacked the sweetness and bright ocean flavor of Santa Barbara uni.  Seafood also showed up in their turbot course topped with a chicken jus.  It was kind of a plain dish and the fish was just not that great (though they kept the fatty skirt, which delivered a uniquely juicy and gelatin-like texture.)

Their main dessert (whiskey sour) was excellently paired with a nice drink and was perfectly fine, but besides from the fun drink pairing, it did not measure up to a lot of the other food served here.

Service was great.  The servers are attentive and friendly and the chefs are great--very personable and they really want to go out of their way to make sure you not only enjoy the food but also get the most out of being that close to the kitchen. 

Prices are surprisingly reasonable given the creativity and quality of the cuisine as well as the abundance of food served.

The Catbird Seat is an exceptional dining experience. There are only a very few restaurants that offer this type of fun, educational and creative dining experience in the U.S.  If you enjoy food and live in Nashville or travel there a lot, The Catbird Seat is a must visit.

Free street parking is available, but it can be hard to find an open space close to the restaurant's entrance.

***What I had at The Shaved Duck was just okay, but I think they probably have some good stuff here; The Shaved Duck did provide me the opportunity to have actual St. Louis spare ribs in St. Louis***

The Shaved Duck was recently featured on Diners, Drive-in and Dives and seems to be one of more notable new BBQ spots in the St. Louis area.  I decided to give The Shaved Duck a try since I had a hard time finding Missouri BBQ spots that featured St. Louis style spare ribs.

The spare ribs were nicely smoked and had a decent flavor.  They were pretty tender and juicy for spare ribs (which are definitely not as fall-off-the-bone tender as baby back ribs).  The ribs did dry out really quickly though.

It is hard to know how The Shaved Duck's spare ribs match up to other restaurants since most places feature baby back ribs.  The spare ribs at Montgomery Inn (Cincinnati) are significantly better.  The ribs there are much more tender and juicier.  Montgomery Inn does use a very vinegary BBQ sauce, which can be off putting; the BBQ sauce at The Shaved Duck is more neutral.

They had several sides and I opted for the green bean casserole because I don't see that side dish often in restaurants.  This side was just okay.  I usually have it around Thanksgiving and maybe because of that I did not feel the dish worked with the BBQ ribs.  I probably should have opted for the macaroni and cheese instead.

Service was quick, personable and attentive.

The decor reminded me of some gastropubs you might find in Los Angeles.  There was a good use of the existing building's structure and a heavy focus on dark colors.  I liked the exterior; this restaurant is built into a home that is tucked into a neighborhood.

Prices were not bad especially given that this restaurant is a sit-down restaurant; many Missouri BBQ places seem to be order-at-the-counter spots.

I was not a huge fan of the St. Louis style spare ribs at The Shaved Duck, but I get a feeling that other dishes here (like the baby back ribs) would be much better.  Still, I think Pappy's offers a far superior BBQ experience.

Free parking is available on the street.

***This bakery features very renowned cannoli; I enjoyed it, but I am not sure if the cannoli here stood out compared to other cannoli I have had at nice Italian restaurants; I have not been to many Italian bakeries so maybe Isgro's cannoli is significantly better than most Italian bakeries***

This Italian bakery has a great old school, neighborhood feel to it.  It features all kinds of cakes, Italian desserts, pastries, and butter cookies.  I tried their cannoli, which is very well known.  This dessert consisted of a fried pastry shell filled with ricotta mascarpone cream and chocolate chips.  It was good.  The pastry shell was crispy while the filling was sweet and creamy.

I have only really had cannoli at Italian restaurants and Isgro's version failed to live up to those restaurants because the filling just was not as smooth or creamy.  The cannoli at Valentino in Los Angeles also has a much lighter and more flavorful pastry shell.  Still, Isgro's cannoli may hold up very well to other Italian bakeries.

Service was good.  Prices were okay--not cheap but not too expensive either.

If you are a fan of Italian bakeries or cannoli, Isgro is worth trying.  If you primarily frequent artisan bakeries, you might be disappointed with the offerings here.

You can find free street parking in the nearby residential area.

***Jim's Steaks puts out tasty cheesesteaks on great, crusty bread; for the price, it is both a tasty lunch/dinner and a good value***

There are so many well-known cheesesteaks spots in Philadelphia that you really would have to spend a lot of time in Philadelphia to probably find your favorite one (there is not really one place that is universally accepted by most people as the best).  I ended up choosing Jim's because it sounded good and its location was convenient; this Jim's is just a short (as well as a nice) walk from key Philadelphia attractions like the Liberty Bell (parts of the street along the way make you feel like you have gone back in time--a truly special experience and one that you cannot easily experience in the U.S.).

Jim's Steaks is a small shop that features a hot flat top as well as a few seating options.  Jim's Steaks features a variety of hot sandwiches as well as many ways to get your cheesesteak outfitted: different cheeses (Whiz, American, Provolone), different toppings (peppers, onions, mushrooms) and even Italian ingredients like pizza sauce.

Sandwiches at Jim's Steaks are served on (I believe) Amoroso's rolls.  It is a perfect vehicle for the cheesesteak.  The bread has a great crispy and chewy crust.  There is just enough bread on the inside (not too much where you end up just tasting a lot of bread and not the meat like you get with some sandwiches).  The inside has the right texture too--not dry or hard but also not too soft, which would have resulted in the sandwich potentially becoming soggy or gross.

The meat is chopped up pretty thoroughly and it is tasty and not too fatty.  The meat looks a little dry, but it is not bad. There is a good amount of moisture.  I had the cheesesteak with onions and Whiz and both were good.  There was just the right amount of Whiz so you get a lot of creaminess and a noticeable (though I guess you could say artificial) cheese flavor without it taking over the sandwich.

Service was fairly quick and if you get to Jim's right when it opens, you do not have to deal with a long line (you can also find a place to sit).

Prices were reasonable.  You get a filling and tasty sandwich for under $10 and for the price, it is pretty good and probably tastier and more interesting than what you would get with the same amount of money at a lot of order-at-the-counter places in other cities.

Jim's Steaks was a very satisfying spot for a hot, tasty and filing sandwich.  The weather was a little cool, which made the sandwich even more satisfying.  There are probably many great spots in Philadelphia for a cheesesteak and Jim's version is a respectable one and definitely one you would need to try if you are seeking to find out which of the city's cheesesteaks is your favorite.

I am not sure what the parking situation is around here.  I think metered street parking is available, but spaces might be difficult to find.

I've always hated restaurant week because hidden jems like Iztaccihuatl aren't part of it.  I got the pork burrito, it filled me up, and was only about $8.  The inside of the restaurant was kind of bare inside but I felt it was very authentic and comfortable.  The waitress had no problem taking our $10 gift certificate from restaurants.com despite it stating lunch only and we were there for dinner.  I can't wait to go back or order take out from this little place!!

Oh my goodness this place is good!!! Don't tell everyone about this place, I want it all to myself!!!  It's definitely a hidden gem!  I have to admit that I ate so much it hurt.  A close rival to New Delhi, I think it might be just a little better.  What really tiped the scale for me was desert at the buffet and more selections of main dishes.
Stale buffets are no fun, this is definitely not one of those.  We went on a rainy night during the week and the the buffet was moving nicely.
The family atmosphere only added to the experience.  Don't be shy about getting to Tandoor India. Top notch, perfectly flavored food; these people really know what they're doing.

I absolutely loooved everything we ordered! Plus the service was excellent and the little call button on the table was really fun. 

To start they brought out a plate with three mini appetizers and a little bit of the best kimchi I've ever had.i generally don't like kimchi, but this was delicious!! Then they brought out homemade miso soup. This was all because we ordered entrees.

For our meal we ordered the Koran pancake to start and it came with delicious soy sauce. The pancake was huge and I could have eaten it for my whole meal. The leftovers made my coworkers all say, "that smells really good!" My hot rice bowl was sizzling when it got to the table,I got pork and I could have eaten that for the rest of my life and been happy for the rest of my life. My wife's mushrooms and tofu was equally well loved. I ate her leftovers and they were even better the next day! Jasmine tea was excellent and the total bill price was appropriate. The restaurant was casual and there were all sorts of different people in there. Absolutely crave-able food with great portion sizes, easily one of our new favorites!!!!!

With over 3,000 reviews, I'm just going to make this short...came here on a cloudy weekend with my boys to try two of the supposed best Philly Cheesesteaks in the world. Will it be Geno's Steaks or Pat's King of Steaks? All you have to do is walk across the street to these two rivals.

Speak up, shout your order, the long line moves fast. The smell is intoxicating. I added mushrooms, grilled onions and provolone...upon first bite, it's super flavorful, the meat super juicy and the whole sandwich was super yummy!! If you paid attention, I used the word super 3x. It's one of the best I've ever had.

You know what I think? I think Geno and Pat are good friends! I would like to naively think that! ;)

Pat's King of Steak or their rival, Geno's Steak? Each across the street from one another, I had both and the consensus with my two other companions made this one a clear cut WINNER!! The super tender and juicy steak is more chopped up. We added mushrooms, onions, green peppers and provolone. For me, the green peppers and the chopped steak did it for me. I also think the steak was a bit more juicier than the one at Geno's.

I think it's just a matter of preference. Both of these places deserves to be named Best Philly Cheesesteaks. How else would you explain people coming from around the world just to try it. It's been in many Food Network's shows. 

Come, enjoy and judge for yourself. It's worth a visit in the heart of Philadelphia.

I found out today that this restaurant that is loved by my entire family will be closing its doors after 28 years. What started out with three friends with a passion for Burmese cooking will now close its doors by the end of this year.

Located in the heart of Philly's Chinatown, my family would frequent the city whenever we get a chance. Even though there are many dining options, we would always choose to eat here. The owner has greeted us with open arms from our very first visit. She would come by our table to chat with us often. They know us so well that even one of the waitresses memorized exactly what we always order. 

There is only two noodles that I love in the entire world. My mom's Dan Dan noodles and Rangoon's Festival Fish Noodle Soup. It is unlike anything I've ever had. I could seriously go into the kitchen and eat the entire pot. 

It saddens me that they could not survive during the pandemic. This review is to say thank you to the three owners and staff that has served the Philadelphia community. You guys bought Burma to the U.S., a cuisine that not many can experience. 

You bet that I will be paying them one last visit even though it's only takeout. I will savor every last bite of that Festival Fish Noodle Soup in my car.

We have been coming to the Reading Terminal Market for as long as we can remember. Place is always packed with workers nearby grabbing a bite to eat and tourists. I warn you, it is really crowded here all the time. Here are some of the food stalls worth stopping for:

Bassetts Ice Cream -
The first merchant to sign a lease at the Reading Terminal Market in 1892. This place is still owned and run by the same family. With more than 40 flavors, you can have your pick. The cone comes with a generous scoop(s).

Beiler's Bakery -
One of the best donuts. If this is your first time here, don't be deterred by the long line. You often hear people giving up when they see how long the line is. It moves pretty fast  and the best part, you get to see first hand how they make it in front of you. By the time you're midway through, grab a menu, choose your donuts so you don't hold up the line. My son who doesn't like sweets love Beilers'. Note: Not open on Sundays.

Flying Monkey -
The owner with the love of the movie, "The Wizard of Oz", named her bakery Flying Monkey. When I first discovered this place, they were famous for their amazing cupcakes but nowadays, it's more on their award winning Whoopie pies. The Whoopie pies were named the best in the world and it comes in many flavors. Another must try is their Elvis cake. We usually buy a huge slice home. Every item is made from scratch.

Dutch Eating Place -
The only item we have tried here is their amazing warm apple dumpling with cinnamon which is served with a dollop of cool heavy cream. It is to die for.

The Original Turkey -
I don't like eating turkey and the only turkey I will eat from is "The Original Turkey". You can see how juicy it is when they carve it right in front of you! Served with all your typical Thanksgiving fixings, you can have this all year round. You can also order it sandwich style. Don't forget to ask for extra gravy. 

Bee Natural -
I love to make my famous French toast at home. Instead of using syrup I prefer to use honey. I'm always pleased with the quality of their honey here. When I run low, I make sure to grab a bottle or two.

These are just a handful of stalls we frequent. The list goes on. There are also lots of counter lunch spots, food stalls and fresh produce. A must visit in the heart of Philly. 

If you park at the Reading Terminal, you can get a discounted parking for $4 if you buy $10 and over at any one of the merchants at the Reading Terminal. Just have them validate your parking ticket. Remember, it is only good for 2 hours. Otherwise it will be $10 for 2 1/2 hours.

Not worth going to if you're  just a tourist in NOLA. First off, there was a loooooong line across the store.  The way the food was displayed was unsanitary. I went and got fried chicken  because  I wanted fried food so badly and there was a special for  the chicken that day. It was a large enough order to share with my professor.
 My friends that got the chicken  po-boy got their food much sooner than me and said it tasted good. My fried chicken  tasted worse than  KFC. I had high expectations  for fried chicken in Louisiana. It was impossible  to get  the waiter's attention. I went to the kitchen window to get my friend  sauce for their  chicken sandwich. The service was less than one star. I will for sure not be back during my next visit to NOLA.

Pappy's is definitely hyped up and can get really crowded. Their menu is truly something that you can crave time and time again, but my advice to you is if you'd like to try their entire menu is to come early otherwise all of the items that you want are sold out. I came in at approx 7:00pm on a Wednesday and they were sold out of the following: burnt ends, chicken, beef brisket and ribs. We were essentially only able to order pulled pork, turkey or sausage, so I said ok and went with the pulled pork. My pulled pork was paired with baked beans, fried corn and washed down with an iced tea. Overall, the pork was just ok, the bun was pretty cold and I smoked it with BBQ sauce in order to take in the full taste. The BBQ baked beans were awesome and the fried corn was very good. Overall, I was a bit disappointed with the visit, especially considering the hype but I will try it again earlier in the day in order to try out the ribs and brisket. 

Pros-
Cool ambiance 
Great smell
Nice menu
Baked beans were delicious 
Good sides 

Cons-
Sells out quickly 
Service seemed rushed 
Pulled pork was just meh 
Cold buns 
BBQ sauce was only average

I ordered a 3 lbs. Rib Roast, 2 16 oz. Ribeye steaks and 1.5 lbs of ground beef. The after tax total for 6.5 pounds of beef was $151. I'll let you do the math. 

I cooked the Rib Roast using indirect heat on a charcoal grill for 1.5 hours to an internal temperature of 125 degrees. The flavor was good but it was not as tender as I've had for much less expensive cuts of beef.

6/24/14 update: A follow up to my experience with Porter Road Butchers. After ordering the rib roast I asked for 2 12 oz ribeyes (I find any larger to be more meat than I want for a meal). I was told they only cut them one size which would be around 16oz. This rather astounded me as one of the reasons you are willing to pay more at a butcher is the ability to get custom cuts. Since I had driven from Mt Juliet based on what I had read of this place I just went with it. 

I then asked what their best hamburger ground beef was. I was informed that they only have one blend of ground beef. This worried me somewhat as the percentage of fat you want for a great burger is far different than what you may want for something like spaghetti. And again it surprised me that such an expensive place would offer so few options. For me, one of the criteria of a great burger is juice streaming down my forearms! Still I went with it.

Today I thawed the ground beef and  tonight I grilled a burger from the 1.5 lbs I had ordered (yes I had froze the package but well within the acceptable timeframe) with plans to grill the remainder tomorrow. The first thing I noticed after a couple of minutes was there were no flare ups once again indicating my fear of lack of fat. After it was cooked to a medium rare I removed the gray burger. The end result was a dry and tasteless burger. My new plan for the rest of the beef is to fry it up tomorrow and freeze it to use someday as taco meat. Definitely not hamburger quality meat!

I'm still amazed that I spent $150 on 6.5 lbs of meat that just wasn't very good at all. Lesson learned. I think I'll stick with Houston's in Mount Juliet going forward.

Food wise, this place is great. Unfortunately, today while dining for breakfast, we were exposed to one of their employees of color being forced to wear a sign stating " Hello, my name is Twan. I was an hour and a half late today." 

While every business has the right to run it as they feel necessary, employee humiliation does not fit the image I believe Barbecutie wants to portray, nor may it be in line with employment regulations. I'm sure management thinks it's cute to so this, and Twan probably needs the job, so he humbly accepts the mark of shame. I wonder, however, had Twan been one of the bouncy young girls with a perky chest rather than a young black man, would the same have been true?

Sorry, Barbecutie, you've just lost a customer permanently.

Reno was in need of a good french bakery!  I couldn't wait to try this place and it exceeded expectations.  It is located in the "four corners" of midtown so parking is always iffy.  We got there early about 10 minutes before opening and it was snowing.  They were setting up for the day and were kind enough to let us in early to get out of the snow.  I love how they set up the bakery.  It has very clean lines and it is simple and without too much embellishment.  The tables have a plant on each of them.  

The staff were so friendly and helpful.

The display of baked goods in the window glass was mouthwatering!  On the back wall are all of the loaves and baguettes.  They have pretty gunmetal boxes for the baked goods.  We tried a Iberico ham/quince paste/manchego cheese croissant.  It was a delicious savory pastry and the quince paste mellowed out the cheese.  The croissant rivaled any croissant I have had in France.  There were multiple layers of buttery, flaky, and tender pastry.  I found myself picking up the crumbs with a moistened finger so that nothing would go to waste.  My husband was amused and asked if I wanted another one and I couldn't resist.  We shared a chocolate croissant and it was just a delicious as the other.  

We took home a baguette.  It was completely devoured the next day and was a perfect addition to the Brie cheese and prosciutto ham. Crispy on the outside and tender on the inside. We will definitely be back soon!

Had dinner after a wine tasting event upstairs attended by the owner so I'd gotten the scoop on the menu and already  made my selections.  Started with the Ballard Lane Cabernet Sauvignon, special appetizer of crab cake with two tiny little soft shell crabs accompanying it, followed by the San-Pei Chicken Claypot for me and the Pork Shank for him.  
The crab cake was delicious and we each had one of the tiny soft shell crabs.  I'm glad I tried the little crab but don't think I would again.  The little legs were a bit off putting texturally.
The San-Pei Chicken Claypot was fantastic and so much food!  I got over half of it to go and it was dinner the following night.
Tried my guy's Pork Shank, it was tender and flavorful.
Delicious meal, would try again!

As a Vietnamese, I try to check out every Vietnamese restaurant in town. My standards are high as I grew up dining in Little Saigon, Southern CA. 

I'm glad I found Sriracha! Located in a shopping plaza near a Kroger, the food is authentic, good, and really affordable! Pho for $6? Pho-ck yes! I'm tired of having to pay $8-12 for pho just because there aren't enough pho restaurants here to keep prices down. I normally order Viet food at this restaurant even though they also have Japanese. The com thit nuong is delicious here, and my husband, who has had com thit nuong at every Viet restaurant in the Nashville area, deems this his favorite (in TN). 

The place is clean, with ample booth seating, and is family owned with good service.

Love Kitchen 519!

I'm not sure how you've managed to elude me for so long, but better late than never!

This hidden gem was such a pleasant surprise!  When you first walk in you'll find that it's not big by any means, but it's quaint, cozy and charming and I think that's what makes it so special...not to mention that it's family owned and operated...nothing better than a mom-and-pop restaurant!

Once you're seated and have a chance to really look around, you can't but help admire the various works of art from local artists adorning the walls. There was an unframed penciled sketch of a woman that hung along a curtain rod that particularly piqued my interest (by the way, some are for sale).  I absolutely loved the groupings of mason jar pendants that hung from the ceiling!  They cast a warm industrial flare to the overall décor along with the oil-rubbed bronze ceiling fans.  As far as seating goes, they offer both table and booth seating.

OK, so on to the food!  I ordered the Chipotle Chicken Salad and my friends ordered the Crab Cake Sandwich and the Powerhouse Salad.  Let me just say...other than all of us absolutely loving our lunch choices...the presentation was beyond!  It's my understanding that the owner, Jeff Stewart, is the Executive Chef and it's obvious he's got mad culinary talent!

So looking forward to coming back again for dinner and the buzz is they have an amazing brunch!  Btw, just a friendly tip...it's BYOB so be sure to come prepared!

Went to a "potluck" party this past weekend, so ordered an assortment of Marino's Munchables....got Chicken Fingers, Jalapeño Poppers, Boneless Wings, Mozzarella Sticks and French Fries...going, going, GONE! Yeah, in a matter of seconds.  Next time I'll definitely order more!

Ahhh...what's not to love about dining alfresco!  Especially when the temps just right and you're having lunch with your besties.

The minute we arrived we beelined it straight to the patio. I don't even remember saying anything to the hostess...other than smiling and motioning to the patio as she smiled back and gave us a thumbs up.

It was really quite lovely out there.  The tables were nicely spaced (always a good thing when your gearing up for some good girl talk) and the large market umbrellas were a plus as the sun peeked in and out of the clouds. There was also an outdoor bar which was super cool to see.

As soon as we grabbed a table and got situated, our waitress promptly greeted us with menus, told us about the lunch specials of the day and took our drink orders. When she returned, I decided on the Strawberry Balsamic Chicken Salad (Mixed greens, thinly sliced grilled chicken, grapes, spicy pecans, Gorgonzola, herb vinaigrette) and my gfs got the Lobster Bisque and a Wedge Salad.

YUM!  All so delish!  My friend raved about her Lobster Bisque and I loved my choice in salads...it was such a fresh and tasty combo...my tastebuds savored every single bite!

Bottom line...dining al fresco with your besties is the best. But enjoying great food and convo all while getting friendly and attentive service? That's the bestest! ;-)

Right on the money honey!

Came back for another birthday celebration if you can believe it, but did I order the filet?  Helz yeah and it was cooked to "medium" perfection!

In fact, everything was absolutely delish!...here's the order rundown:

Fire Roasted Filet Mignon 
8 oz. filet, rosemary roasted potatoes, wild mushrooms, asparagus, roasted garlic cabernet reduction.

Calamari 
Fried calamari, pickled serrano pepper, lime-ginger aioli.

Bang-Bang Tempura Shrimp 
Lightly battered, sweet-chili dipping sauce.

Veal Saltimbocca 
Pan seared veal medallions, prosciutto di parma, asiago cheese, long stem artichokes, roasted garlic sauce, basil sage fettuccine.

Tuscan Stew 
Braised tips of filet mignon, papardelle pasta, roasted carrots, tomatoes, onions, chianti wine reduction.

Bottom line...this was the last sentence in my previous review:  "Third times a charm?  To Be Continued...can't blame me for wanting to seek a little filet redemption..."

BOOM!  Fliet redemption fulfilled!

Dear hipster-chicken: It's not hard hard to actually have more than 3 chickens to serve to people.  I'm starting to think you don't actually have chicken but pay people to line up outside and talk about how awesome it is.  If you do actually have chicken you must be seeking clientele that have nothing better to do than wait outside for hours to get a ticket to get mediocre chicken.  Then you can spend the rest of the afternoon drinking PBR.  

If you only serve chicken for 15 minutes from 11:30-11:45 before you run out, at least have the decency to take down your chicken sign, and start serving gin in spaghetti cans the rest of the time.

Being half South Indian, I was very excited to have a dosa place in the city, but I was really disappointed at how Americanized this place is.  I ordered the masala dosa deluxe and one with smoked paneer, spinach, and onions (the only other remotely Indian dosa).  The paneer one was filled with spinach, onions, and just a tiny bit of paneer.  While I appreciate their desire to make different fillings, spinach is a bad idea in a dosa.  It didn't take long for the otherwise crispy dosa to become very soggy.  The masala dosa had much more filling, but the potatoes were rather flavorless.  Usually the potatoes are nicely seasoned and spiced, but these were merely yellow.

With a name like "Chutney Company" I also expected a lot more chutney.  (Perhaps something akin to Baja Fresh's salsa bar).  Instead you get a tiny serving of the chutney of your choice with extras being 40 cents each.  I tried cilantro, cococnut and mango.  The coconut and cilantro were ok, but were similar in taste and could've been much spicier.  The cilantro chutney was also that light green mixed with cream kind--not the classic dark green one I prefer.  The mango was simply canned mango (amras available at your local Indian grocery store) and some chili powder.

I think I may have to stick to Edison where I can get a giant, crispy masala dosa with dark, spicy cilantro chutney for under $8.

Well, color me pleasantly surprised!

We initially found Shells via Yelp, and since we were hankerin' for some seafood, Shells was the best reviewed  choice within our price range. 

My snobby wife (she authorized me to say that, btw) said that the restaurant looks like a former IHOP. Like that's a bad thing.... Anyway, I think she was being a little harsh. It is a little nondescript on the outside, but I find no offense in the appearance. 

Much to our surprise, we discovered there were $1 St. Arnold's brews, and  1/2 off drinks. Double win!

I had the Shrimp Diablo pasta. I'll have to say, it was very well put together. Portion size was good. The shrimp were properly cooked. The best part of the dish was that it wasn't that diablo-y. Wait what? Yes. It wasn't that spicy! A lot of times Diablo dishes are all heat, no flavor. The Diablo dish at Shells had a lot of flavor- you could really taste the crushed tomatoes, olive oil, all held together with just a touch of heat. 

As for everyone else, their dishes looked delicious as well. The other members of our party had the Chicken pasta, grilled grouper, and a couple other dishes that I don't recall... All I remember is that everyone was pleased with that quality, quantity, and overall presentation of the dishes. 

We will definitely be back, maybe with the intent of taking better advantage of the Sunday Sunday drink deals.

*Game Changer Alert*

Let me just tell you that my coffee perception has been flipped upside down, rolled around, cold brewed, and nitrogen-tapped into a stout glass. 


I was minding my own business on a Tuesday morning, and I happened across a TB Business Journal article about Ginger Beard Coffee. I became very interested, due to the fact that when I let my face mane grow, it is of the ginger variety. I also happen to enjoy a very well crafted cup of coffee. We were off to a good start before I even read about the Joe. 

If you keep up with coffee, you already know there are a thousand different ways to extract the essence of a roasted coffee bean into a good cup of liquid energy. What a lot of folks DON'T do is create a unique twist on the delivery. 

This is where Ginger Beard Coffee stands out, and they do so with around a combined three feet of face forest, holding superior glasses of coffee. 

So I am new to the concept of Nitro Coffee, and maybe it's been around forever. I don't know. But what I DO know is that there is no such thing as a smoother cup of cold-brewed coffee. 

If you don't know about Nitro Coffee, I'll do my best to share with you my newly acquired knowledge of it:  You take brewed coffee, keg it, pressurize said keg with nitrogen, and put it on a tap also pressurized with nitrogen, and you pour it into a glass. If you've ever witnessed a perfect pour of Guinness, you already know what Nitro Coffee looks like.  

Now for the actual taste of the coffee--- Wow. Seriously. I only drink coffee black (unless I'm at WaHo/Denny's/IHOP/etc., when their coffee truly is brown sludge, and only then will I put sugar in it). I don't like cold coffee, because the taste imperfections hidden by temperature often unmask themselves when the temp is lowered. Cold brew (even at Starbuck's and the like) lack flavor character, and just doesn't appeal to my palate. HOWEVER, Nitro Coffee is now the only way I'll have cold coffee. It's smoother than I'm able to describe. Silky. There are no bitter notes. There is a thick head on the pour (crema, for you coffee snobs), but I choose the word head because it settles more like a pour of fresh stout than a shot of espresso. It smells heavenly, and is much more aromatic than any other plain cup of coffee. 

They also have a rewards program, so you can earn a free glass (or cup if you're in a hurry). 












Why the hell are you still reading this...? GO TRY IT!

Really good food. Very filling. Service was slow and forgot most of our requests such as straw, Splenda, slay and pepper etc but overall food was good. Drinks could are good but I have had better ones.  Price doesn't really match with serving and flavors but looking forward to their happy hour next time as that has better offers. Trust

Came here for dinner and everything was good. Great portions which are just the right size. Flavors were really delicious. Service was slow that night as we waited about 45 mins for food to come out  hence the four stars but they did make for free desert for the slow service. They were very nice though and kept checking on us. Will come back and try this place again. Trust. 
There's parking bldg next to resto.

Love this place but the service was not so good. Our server was kurt and kept forgetting our requests.  My favorite was the beef carpaccio, broccolini, squid, croquettas and the two deserts. The drinks were good as well. Will definitely be back. Wish we sat by the fire place. Would have given 5 stars but our server was not that pleasant. Trust!!!
Really good fish and chips. Love it. Only to go. Seat outside. No long lines. Have the wait for awhile for your order but worth the wait. Crispy fish and great nachos with salsa. Trust.

We drove all the way from LA to eat at Mollie's, which we had heard excellent reviews, However we were extremely disappointed and lied too.

We had reservations at 9: 30, we arrived at 9:20, and they said that the kitchen is closed. The Server was rude to us, when asked to be seated, and told us to leave. 

My father went back the next day  to speak to the manager to find out why they took reservations at 9:30 yet decided to close the kitchen right when we had gotten there. 

My father asked for the Manager to confront the issue, and the owner Mollie denied ownership and management" the owner is not here, the manager does not come in on Sunday's." Finally after 5 minutes, Mollie decided to admit that she is the owner and manager, and she said " because you decided to change the reservation from 8:30 to 9:39 we decided to take your reservation and close anyways. 

Apparently, This is Oprah Winfrey's favorite Resturant, perhaps Oprah needs to reconsider. I have never ever had such a terrible confrontation with a Resturant before. 

All they needed to do was apologize for being so unprofessional and take responsibility for their lack of care. I hope they come across this review and reconsider how they treat their customers.

This is a solid 4 1/2 stars but it's not quite a 5. 

The actual fish is wonderful. The fish is a 5 (or 6), fresh, yummy, excellent fish. 

The c waitress came up to me and asked me if I liked sushi. I relied on the affirmative. But then I started asking about kani (fake crab). So many places are saying there is crab on it when it's kani (enough said, look it up). So she directs me to several tools without kani. Generally I just order a roll and have them hold the kani. But the Tiger Roll looked good so I went that way.

TIGER ROLL: inside: salmon and tuna.
Outside: salmon, barbecue eel, avocado, roe [masago], green onion, crunchy with eel sauce, 

I was like "okay, let's try it." 

I rarely eat eel and now I'm asking myself why. 

The roll was extremely creative and yummy but the person assembling it didn't make it tight enough and it didn't always hang together. 

Another issue was when I asked about beer I was only told about Sapporo, which is a 22 oz beer. I feel like there should be less-ounce choices. Oh well, I'm in Louisiana so I'll just get a to-go cup.

I was impressed because they have uni (sea urchin) and Toro (fatty tuna). Honestly, you only see that in the better sushi restaurants because it's such a specialty. 

I will totally and willingly return here.

They have a lovely wine menu and I ordered a delightful and full-bodied Cotes de Rhône.

For my appetizer I ordered the gumbo which was quite good, but something was off. The broth was runny and not thick and hearty like a true gumbo cooked with a roux. On the flip side they were light on the rice, which to me is a win. 

For my entree I ordered the New Bedford Sea Scallops which is pan seared with a wild mushroom risotto, Porcini butter and crispy leeks. Oh my word, those crispy leeks are amazing. They are thin pieces of leeks deep-fried, like the onions on a green bean casserole. I wanted more of then. The wild mushroom risotto was to die for, and the mushroom flavor was full but not overwhelming.

For dessert I had the white chocolate and caramel bread pudding. My lands, this was a decadent and wonderful dessert. 

I also ordered the Cappuccino Fins, which is cappuccino, Kahlua, Frangelico, a praline liqueur with shaved chocolate. This is an experience in and of itself. 

The service was great. The decor is wonderful. Everything is worth coming for:



Cruspy
I was so hot and dropped in to have a drink. The people were so nice. They didn't annoy me and they were friendly and willing to share their air conditioner with me,

I needed coffee and I stopped to get it here because I'd never noticed it before in the French Quarter. The coffee was good and decently priced for New Orleans ($3.03) Quite good taste. I'm not crazy about their hours (8-4).

This was a fun few hours of riding a paddle boat out into the Mississippi River. She (the Mississippi) had such wonderful energy. The views were wonderful. I took off a star because the food was being boring. Booooooring.

My friend scallops were the bomb, but just a wee bit salty for my taste. 

Everything is vampire themed, including the drink menu. They are labeled by blood type (O+, O-, A+, A-, B+, B-, AB+, AB-). The mixed drinks weren't that string, but my Old Fashioned was excellent. 

My friend's teenager got a hamburger and he woofed it down completely. (Nom! Nom!)

Word! The Irish Coffee is strong! I cannot complain that I didn't get my money's worth!

I got on the waitlist and that was awesome. Actually, I don't think it made one iota of difference but I can't swear one way or the other. I might have got in the waitlist in exactly the right way, because we are far enough down Decatur that maybe this is just what people came in. Idk?!

I ordered the Aebelskivers, which are deep fried pancakes and they are to die for!  I got the lemon, caramel and Nutella sauces. I think I liked the caramel the best.

I also got the savory crepe with mushroom, onion, red peppers, spinach and Boursin (goat) cheese. It was very good but way filling. Next time I'll probably try something else. I will point out I said "next time" which, as a reviewer, unless I really like a place, is not happening. Just the fact that I say that is a very  good sign. 

The service is excellent. The staff is nice.

This was a fun little wine bar. Admittedly the wine and beer were overpriced for what you are getting (some of them scandalous so) but it's the Garden District of New Orleans and on the chic / bougie/ trendy edge. So, The prices are to be expected. You must go inside to order but the bartender die an excellent job of making sure things are right.

I found seed online and came here because it sounded good. And it is. But I wish they still had beignets (they have new owners). 

I ordered the satsuma mimosa, which is a local citrus fruit similar to a Mandarin orange. It was a nice but small for the price ($11). 

I ordered the Blueberry Buckwheat Pancakes which is what it sounds like but is absolutely yum. They are hearty and filling.

I ordered my favorite coffee drink with lavender and it too was good. 

Devon is a good waitress. Ask for her.

Oh my word! The food is wonderful. I started with the fried green tomatoes sans the jelly (it had bacon in it). Yes, I cheated on my diet (I know I normally am a vegan but I had a drink or two and WTH?!) But the taste was amazing. The tomatoes with the remoulade and shrimp was to die for). 

Then I ordered the scallops and risotto sans the butter and it was creamy and lovely. 

They have a good wine list and impeccable service. (I FEEL SO GUILTY BUT IT WAS AMAZING!)

The Peach Bellini is good. It doesn't look like a peach Bellini - truthfully I think it's peach flavored sparkling wine, but really who cares? It's NOLA, baby!

I loved looking out the humongous open window and feeling the breeze come in. I love cute Kirkes cafes like this, so I chose this because of that, not because I expected a superior meal. So to start my expectations were on the low side. 

As aforementioned, I ordered the Peach Bellini and got peach flavored sparkling wine. Yes, I've bought s**t sparkling wine before so I can recognize it. lol. Note: I did order a second one and it came with a maraschino cherry. Dumb!

In the fluoride, feeling that cool breeze in the heat was amazing. I just sat here and enjoyed it. 

The service was slo-ooooooooow. I mean 30 minutes to get Fried Green Tomatoes. And then my order came with shrimp (which I DID NOT ORDER!!!!!) 

First, my Fried Green Tomatoes came on a bed of lettuce (gross!)  with the shrimp on top (no bueno) with the remoulade sauce (doubly gross) on top! First, the Fried Green Tomatoes were undercooked. Maybe not undercooked but having sat too long and lost it's crispness.  F'ing nasty. No crispy flavor. They also tasted like it sat in there back under a heat lamp FOREVER and were not crispy AT ALL.  When I complained about the shrimp they said they just put it on because I had to wait so long. When I complained they said they'd take it off and they did.

I'm writing this review for one major reason: I need to shout Noble Pie's weekend mimosa brunch special FROM THE ROOFTOPS. Bottomless mimosas for $10 is a deal that cannot be beat, especially because of the restaurant's setup: the bar/counter service means that you control how often you get refills. Mix that with the perfect seating for groups, and you have a recipe for an amazing time. I went here for my birthday last month, and boy, did we get our money's worth!

When it comes to food, the brunch menu is small but solid, and the options are hearty. I've had the avocado toast a couple of times, and it's simple but tasty. Next time I'd really love to try the "You've Got Spanache" calzomelette, since I imagine Noble Pie's pizza prowess probably comes into play more with a calzone-style item. I haven't tried the pizza at this Noble Pie location yet, but if it's anything like their 2nd St pies, I'm sure it's incredible.

Besides the food and drink, the customer service at Noble Pie is on point, and the ambiance is casual and relaxed. I'm looking forward to using their outdoor patio once the weather is warmer, too. Nothing like drinking mimosas al fresco!

The Depot has become a culinary institution in Reno, as it was among the first restaurants to spark the recent revitalization of Reno's food scene. A converted train depot, the atmosphere is a nod to the building's history but with a modern edge. If you're looking to impress out-of-towners, this is the place to go. Great food, great drinks, and great service are all hallmarks of a night at The Depot.

Sometimes The Depot's popularity can be a challenge, however, as I've shown up to the hostess stand before and been told there's a two hour wait for a table. While it's frustrating in the moment, that kind of a wait is really a testament to the restaurant's quality. To save yourself time, be sure to take advantage of their online reservation system through their website/Yelp. I've been able to make same-day reservations before without a problem, and it definitely spares the headache of a long wait.

Something really fun and unique about The Depot is that it's a brewery and distillery, which gives customers plenty of options for high-quality libations. I'm a big fan of "The Farmer," a light but very flavorful saison brew.  

As a vegetarian, much of the menu is off-limits to me (meat being the star of almost all of the entrees), but the stuffed poblanos tend to satisfy. I say "tend to" because I've noticed it can be hit or miss sometimes. The peppers and potatoes are sometimes just a step up from raw, and I personally would love if they were roasted longer so they become softer. But, that small qualm aside, the dish's flavors are really good, and it definitely beats just getting a salad.

What a great location... cool building... and wonderful food!

The calamari was ok... but the clam chowder and the shrimp/lobster tacos were awesome!! The chowder was thick and creamy with a ton of big pieces of clam in it... it does need the cracked pepper though. The tacos were loaded with shrimp and lobster. I ate the shrimp first and though man it doesn't get better then this... I was wrong... I took one bite of the lobster and just about went into taste coma! Just awesome!!

Sitting on the patio in this beautiful CA weather eating food fit for a king is just out of this world.

The service was fantastic... on the spot to take order, my water glass never was empty, and they cleaned up right as I finished. They were in point without hovering. 

The location with the ocean right across the street is literally picture perfect.

What a GREAT lunch experience!

Delicious Taiwanese food in Reno, NV? YES, I am SOLD! 

Mobile order on Yelp was easy and food was ready in time and packed well. 

Taiwanese Style Oyster Omelets $10.5
Truly authentic, except they use spinach to replace tong-ho or napa cabbage but I understand maybe those were not in season and spinach has wider popularity. 

Beef Chow Fun $14
First I thought it was a bit pricey but the portion is huge, the whole bowl felt so heavy. Flavor wise, unlikely what Beef Chow Fun I normally associated with, can't say I like it or hate it. Besides,  I do not appreciate how they packed noodle tight in a bowl instead of box. It's not a great idea if you don't plant to eat right away. 

Fried Pork Intestine $9.5
fried perfectly, but it could use some kick

Braised Napa Cabbage $6.5
One of the most authentic version I've had in US.  I don't usually find this dish on the menu as most Taiwanese restaurants run with a small menu with just few staple items. Must get this!

Parking wasn't the greatest, only about 10 spots in the one way in one way out parking lot at front sharing w Starbucks. Street parking is also available. 

101 Taiwanese cuisine is few blocks from Truckee Riverwalk, the autumn colors brightened up my heart whie the Taiwanese food made my stomach very happy!

I've always thought that this place was over rated.  The waiter (who was very nice) told us not to load up on the chips and salsa because our plates would be filled. Yes, they were filled with inedible vegetation.  My girl friend had a pineapple crown taking up most of the space on her plate! Granted, it was coated in some sort of pepper powder.  Chili powder? However, we both did the sampler.  Each portion was very tiny and I was glad I ignored the waiter's recommendation not to eat a lot of chips and salsa. We also asked the owner, who came around and greeted us, to adjust the temperature as it was really warm where we were sitting. She didnt and we were only too glad to step outside.

I've always believed that even the worst restaurants will have a popular following if 1) the owner comes around and says hi, 2) the menu is changed every few days, and 3) you make the plate "funky". Oh, and make it a little more expensive than it should be.

Trust me, there are much better Mexican restaurants in Tucson.

The food here is ok, perfect if you want to grab a quick light bite while exploring the French Quarter. I ordered a combo consisting of scrambled eggs, bacon, grits and French bread and my wife and I shared an order of beignets. The beignets here are much denser than Cafe Du Monde and I wasn't too impressed with that portion of my meal..

Awesome poutine! Large, generous cheese curds, hearty gravy, and yummy fries. Really hits the spot, especially on a late night (this place replaced Under Dogs, which was another late night spot). I love how they serve Little Baby's ice cream milkshakes too - I'm a huge fan.

Gorgeous, fresh, simple. What an absolute treat.

I ordered the chirashi bowl: a refreshing, cool dish on a sticky hot day. The wasabi mixed throughout gave it a little zing, and the ripe tomatoes gave the raw fish a nice acidic snap. Oooooo.

Don't miss the oysters, obviously. Also, the seaweed butter that came out with the bread was a standout on its own. 

Wow. Come here!

A plate of little Gnocchi potato dumplings mixed with seasonal veggies like local tomatoes and squash, and accompanied with pesto, is worth a visit by itself. It's the best gnocchi I have experienced. I like the way they are firm on a fork yet seem to melt in the mouth.  The spicy roasted chicken was another shared dish I liked because it came with a tomato-y sauce. I'm happy the chef favors tomatoes as a key ingredient. The inside seating in a big old converted garage sitting a few feet from the action in the open kitchen made the Nashville Adele's dinning more exciting. I also think it's nice that Adele's is named after the mother of the founder, Jonathan Waxman - a good son.

Happy Hindi speaking children with their parents at the lively lunchtime buffet contrasted with the drab outside. The parking area was forlorn in the recently-vacated Kroger lot. Inside Taj Indian Restaurant the mostly Indian diners with a few nativeborn Americans enjoyed the tastes and smells of Indian cuisine. The Taj tandoor oven bakes veggies, chicken, fish and more and sears in the flavor. I liked the Tandori Fish Tikka marinated chunks of mahi-mahi. It could have had a bit more moisture, but was fine nonetheless. The raita cucumber side dish was yummy wih mint leaves and yogurt made in-house. The vegetarian Dahi Batata Puri appetizer was filled with potato, noodles, onion, yogurt and sweet sauce. A fine finish was Kulfi Indian ice cream dessert. The Nepalese and Indian servers, and the violet napkins and walls, with the black tablecloths made for a fine ambience, especially for the neighborhood environ.

Drive-thru service at Sip Cafe was convenient for me getting a quick cup of coffee on the run. Sip is now the only Inglewood or East Nashville coffee shop offering a drive up window and that is one thing that makes it unique in that part of town. Another unique factor is their Sip Cafe "Sipresso" espresso I like provided by Drew's Brews coffee roasters. Sipresso espresso has a kick, albeit with a more pleasant after-taste than charbucks. The barrista whirled my hot perk promptly and she handed it to me with an easy smile -- that makes a difference when I'm on deadline. She was fast but smooth, as a barrista should be.

No masks or gloves for anyone working in the kitchen. I can see them around the food and prepping salads and touching food through the window. We wanted to stay and have dinner, be returning customers,  and support local business, but I wouldn't do that now.

Warning: I was really hungover and I waited in line for close to an hour. I'd never do that again here, but I would definitely return if I could forgo that line. 

To be honest, between two of us we ordered 6 things and they all tasted the same. All was definitely on the bland side and I needed to literally douse my food in hot sauce to get any flavor. To top it off, the meat was really dry. The fresh made tortillas are the star of the show and they know it. Pretty much everything you order is served with two. 

The pinto beans with bacon are a pass. Soupy, flavorless, this was the worst. The guac with tortillas wasn't anything special and the tacos were definitely more of the highlighted dish here, but Lillys blows them out of the water. This is a celebrated spot in SB so hit it if you can get here without waiting in line. If that's not possible I'd recommend moving on.

This was definitely one of my favorite meals in NOLA this past trip. I was originally going to tackle the line at Acme, but it was raining, I was hungry, I headed here instead. There was still a line.

Side note: New Orleans is a city of lines. I just found this out this past trip. Man oh man.

At lunch, this place is deli style: you wait in line, place your order, find a table, sit and wait. If you're thirsty, I'd suggest ordering like 5 drinks at a time. Once you do order, the food actually comes out pretty quick.

We went with a cup of gumbo, an oyster po-boy and a shrimp caesar salad. I'll be damned, everything was absolutely perfect and I had my doubts about that caesar salad with the dressing on the side. Srrrsly. Oh and the potato salad? So soupy, but oh so good.

Dinner looks a bit more upscale with waiter service and I'd imagine is just as good/if not better than this decadent lunch.

So, why not 5 stars Steph? I really wasn't' into the deli style service. I would have much preferred to sit down, place an order with a waiter and enjoy.

I'm going to echo the sentiment that this spot should be above that 3 star average (especially for being located in a casino). This spot is the nyc delicatessen experience in a Reno casino. Was it spot on? No, but it was still pretty delicious. 

I picked up lunch for a bunch of peeps and prices for Reno probs were a little high, but the sandwiches are huge and come with a side! I opted for the Cobb salad and it was filled with bacon, blue cheese, turkey, egg, avo and all the fixings. 

Although the salad was solid, you really should be getting a sammy: the reuben, the sloppy joes, anything with pastrami. I'd imagine that is what would bring this meal even higher! 

Service was great. Prices were about $12-$14/sandwich, and honestly they probably could have fed 1.5-2 people depending on what you got and how hungry you were.

Limited veggie options, but the one veggie sandwich sounded great. 

I'm into it.

People talk about the lines. However, Tuesday at 2:30 there wasn't a line in sight. Yet, after seeing the list of artisanal sandwiches and enjoying one, I fully see why there is said lines during the Boise lunch rush.

I opted for a panini - the ham, gruyere, goat, blueberry jam and mustard one. Yes. Don't all those ingredients sound just magnificent? Pressed together, it was magic. That saltiness from the cheese and ham combined with the sweetness of the blueberry jam and the slight spice of the mustard? BOOM.

I opted for the simple salad as my side and it was just that - greens, slivered marcona almonds dusted with parmasean shavings.

All of this for $8.50 + tax. A nice little lunch offering, Boise. Plenty of seating and homemade soda offerings served in mason jars makes this a no brainer.

Great service and a solid little coffee shop that offers up a variety of eats and coffee. The place isn't that hipster, modern style spot, but more of that local, mom & pop, generic (not in a bad way) type joint. 

Kudos for having vegan options and oat milk, along with a variety of other non-dairy options.

My breakfast sandwich with egg, avo, and cheese was solid. Not the craziest order and not the craziest egg sandwich I've ever seen. 

Service was so nice, and food and drinks were solid! I'd come again. Also, check-in on Yelp for a free regular coffee!

When it's late in Reno and you're staying at the Peppermill, Cafe Milano is a saving grace. A diner located in the casino with a menu 6 pages long. One section dedicated to Chinese food and breakfast is served anytime, of course. 

Is everything on the menu $3-4 overpriced? Yes. Similar to an airport, many of the casino patrons don't leave the casino walls, so they jack everything up since you can't leave.

With that, the diner is large, bright and clean. Service was solid for 11pm on a Thursday. The chicken tenders were legit! 5ish large and meaty deep fried tenders served with fries. Go with the waffle variety, trust. 

The potstickers were average, I probably wouldn't order again. The ginormous brownie sundae was ridiculous. So much chocolate, way too big. We split it amongst 3 people and it was still too big.

You could order something a bit more fancy, but this spot was a great option for a greasy spoon type meal: hash browns, burgers, clubs, fries, chicken tenders, wings, eggs; soak up that booze or late night cravings.

I mean it's Mother's, you gotta go.

With that, I find my palate a bit more upscale. :: Whoaaaa, check me out and my food snobbery :: Granted I didn't have a seafoof po'boy, but I found the crawfish omelette and the famous Ferdi special po'boys extremely simple. I found the whole experience pretty simple: You wait in line, you order, you find a table.

The woman servicing our table overheard us gasp when we saw those delicious biscuits come out, she brought out two more. So sweet. Those biscuits and the homemade raspberry jam were the standouts of the entire meal and just phenomenal. The omelette was mostly egg and light on that delicious crawfish etouffe/gravy. The man's Ferdi was a simple roastbeef/ham sandwich. A solid meal, but nothing life changing.

I do have to say the meat & egg biscuit looked mighty fine. 

Overall, I'm happy I checked it off the list, but I won't be returning when I make the return to NOLA.

Found Red Mesa of course off the Yelp app for a pre-flight meal and it was a great decision. The place is super spacious and pretty cool with a great outdoor space in downtown St. Pete. We sat in the outdoor bar space and it was quite lively on a Sunday afternoon with football playoffs on. Service was wonderful and we opted for an order of ceviche, guac and chips and a taco salad topped with fresh mahi mahi and steak. 

The guac was regular although those chips and salsa was on point. The salsa had subtle heat and chips were freshly fried. The ceviche was delicious, also served with freshly fried chips. We ordered the Huachinango which consisted of snapper, shrimp, calamari, blue crab, chile arbol oil, orange, tomato, onion and cilantro. It was spicy, like really spicy which I liked (and the waitress did warn), it was a tad bit too soupy. More fish and less sauce, please.

The two taco salads with the additional cost of steak and fish were good. Not authentic by any means, but really nice portions of protein. I would suggest the fish over the steak as the steak could have used a bit more seasoning, or any seasoning at all. The fish was fresh and cooked perfectly. 

Prices were great, service and ambiance perfect, I'd definitely recommend Red Mesa for a fun and casual night or day out!

This place was great and in a great location.  The crab cake was AMAZING.  I forgot what we ate - sandwhiches - but they were great!

I loved this place - so romantic right in the French Quarter.  Great spot!

During quick stop in Indy, and in need of a drink and dinner, I opened up my handy-dandy Yelp app, and voilà, I was immediately intrigued by Spoke & Steele modern upscale vibe, as well as their craft cocktail menu and delicious dinner options. Was able to secure a reservation for four easily; however, when we arrived, we did have to wait about 15 minutes for our table to be ready. No worries, we could see they were busy and working at a reduced capacity. 

For beverages I had the Old Northside, a mezcal-forward tequila based beverages, and shooo, it was strong! I could only have one. And opted for a vodka soda after. A friend had their Old Fashioned, and tbh that was the winner. As for dinner, we decided to just split a couple apps since no one was extremely hungry. We ordered the mushrooms, brussels, potatoes, and house bread. Everything was good, with the mushrooms being the standout for me. But nothing was like head-over-heels amazing either.
