Regardless, we enjoyed what we ordered. We ended the meal with a round of espresso martinis, which were delicious. 

The biggest room for improvement here is their service. They were busy, so I feel bad saying it, but often times we were left wondering where our waitress went, and when she would come by, she'd take the drink order then run off, without a second to put in any food order. This also contributed to our decision to only order apps then head out. Overall, our experience here was ultimately pleasurable, and I'd come back, just perhaps once COVID is over.

I use to go to the Italian Market before I lived in South Philly, but now that I'm right around the corner, I'm there several times a week - I rarely go to the super market more than once a month (if that). I mean, with butchers that will cut to order, fruits and veggies at a fraction of the price of the mega mart, and actually seasonal, including herbs and more exotic items than can be found at the Acme. I've also started eating more fish, which has always freaked me out at the supermarket. Actually, I've started eating more healthily in general (except of course when I splurge on cured meets and cheese or homemade pasta, or pastries up the street on Christian...). The Italian Market isn't just for food - Fante's kitchen wares has just about every kitchen gadget imaginable, including a coffee and tea section, extensive baking supplies, and a serious selection of knives (they will even sharpen them while you wait for $2 a blade). Most people are friendly and nice, though it wouldn't be philly without a few curmudgeons; everyone's a distinct character, and I pretty much love them all. One of my favorite things to do is walk up and down the market, sensing out the best deals, the freshest produce, getting to know my neighbors, and enjoying the Philly-ist of Philly communities. There are a few tips I'd like to share with the uninitiated, and hopefully get more converts to this heart of Philadelphia experience.

Pro tips: 
* The majority of the Italian Market is closed on Mondays, and by far their busiest days are Saturday & Sunday (when the prices also seem to magically inflate). Fridays are a little bit crowded, but manageable. Pretty much any day  if you go closer to closing time, there might be a line at the butchers or cheese shops, but if you have time to wait, it's worth it. Some people say stuff is fresher on Tuesday and Wednesday, but I haven't really noticed a difference. 

* Pick your own produce, to be sure you get what you want, I've had several experiences where the good stuff is out front, and the bag you get home with is gnarly and questionable, so avoid the concern all together and do your own picking, that way you have no one to blame but yourself.

* Buying in bulk is the best deal (and for the price, some waste is to be expected) but if you don't want 10 lbs of potatoes for $5, you can easily ask for 2 lbs for $1, sometimes you just need a small piece of ginger for a quarter (or sometimes for free if you're getting other stuff & the vendor is feeling generous).

* During the week, the vendors start clearing out around 3ish (earlier if weather is bad) later if it's nice out - it's kind of up for grabs. Though the store fronts are generally open til 5-6

* There's plenty of parking in the area (including a municipal lot on 8th, before Washington) but if you decide to drive through, or on any of the streets surrounding, don't be surprised if you get stuck behind an unloading truck, or waiting for a crowd of pedestrians crossing the street, or inexplicable traffic, which will later turn out to be a forklift driving between the various warehouses in the district.

* The market is fairly walkable from most of the city, but if you tend to shop big - invest in a granny cart, and always be sure to bring your reusable tote, regardless :D

* If you don't know, ask, if someone makes you feel dumb, ask someone else (there are plenty of vendors competing for business, if you're not digging the vibe from one, move on, there are enough options for you to be choosy about where you take your business). A good attitude & sense of humor take you a long way in this area.

** Don't let it intimidate you - the Italian market is fun and delicious! **

We've been to Zinc Cafe quite a few times, and up until this past visit the food has been good (although clearly decreasing in quality with each trip) and service acceptable, albeit a little smug.  However this last experience will definitely be our last. 

Several weeks ago I reserved a table for 9 to have a baby "sprinkle" for my sister.  When we arrived, about 15 minutes early for our reservation, we were seated and began to order drinks. After the majority of our party arrived, we found that 3 were not going to be attending,  leaving our total group to 6.  The waitress returned and blunty asked "is this it!?" When I informed her that the remaining 3 would not be attending, she instantly got agitated and went to the owner. The pair returned visibly upset and informed us that they couldn't keep a party of 6 at a table meant for 9. Our table was actually 3 pushed together, and we agreed it wouldn't be a problem to remove the end table, however they instead insisted we move to a VERY small table that would only accommodate 3 or 4 at the most. When I asked if we could stay at our current table, already settled and having received drinks, the owner grew increasingly rude and explained how she was already losing business because of us and that we needed to move. With that she took my mother's drink directly out of her hand, removed her jacket from her chair and then began to pull on another of our party's chairs in an effort to rush her to move. 

We asked why there was such a rude reaction, to which the owner again stated that we were causing them to lose business and we needed to move. Instead we opted to leave since we were clearly unwelcome at this point. 

We try to exclusively visit small local owned resturaunts and had recommended Zinc in the past, however it became very apparent that they are far more concerned about how quickly they are turning over tables and less about the experience of their patrons, as evidenced by the ever decreasing food quality. Considering all of the amazing local food choices, this is a definite pass.

disappointment island. 

my daddy always taught me to present a criticism between two compliments, so here goes my criticism sandwich. 

the restaurant is absolutely charming with a beautiful patio and quaint indoor dining room that looks more like  a home than a restaurant. it is truly lovely. 

my friend and I were disappointed with the customer service from the hostess and the bartender, as well as our cochon de lait (pork roast) sandwich. 
we arrived without reservations (party of 2) just before they unlocked the door to open at 11am. the hostess said we were welcomed to go sit at their bar. when we walked up to the bar, the bartender said we could not sit there. they were doing construction on the bar.  he directed us back to the hostess. she then sat us at one of the tables by the window. while we were placing our order with our waiter, she interrupted and said she would have to move us because that table was reserved after all. so we picked up our own glasses of water and silverware and followed her to a table right at the door. it was a bit embarrassing being in limbo and not even knowing if we could dine there at one point while she was trying to figure out what to do with us, as the other customers sat and watched. 
as we sat at our drafty table, we watched the bartender and some other workers have a wine tasting at the bar. funny how it wasn't under construction after all. we also watched the other window table sit empty as we ate our greasy, puny little cochon de lait sandwich.  there were several other empty tables in the dining room for the duration of our visit. not sure why she had to stick us right at the door.  having been here before, I really built this restaurant up and I was terribly embarrassed by the food and service. my friend said he'd never come back and I don't blame him. 

on a good note, our server was fantastic. he was kind, attentive and knowledgable of the menu. in fact, every time i've been here, I have had an excellent server.

I'm not much of a foodie. Give me good service, fair price, and good food then I'm good. But what caught my attention about this place was the vibe. It was very.... Cool and chill. Definitely is a great place to meet up with friends, enjoy some chill music and no one in your group of friend would complain about the food and the variety. 

The menu was impressively diverse. Though this is a new restaurant and things can change. But for what I saw that was impressive in itself. This would make it even easier to meet up as a group when one person wants Asian food and another wants Latin food. 

I had the Ramen here for dinner and was so blown away from the pork belly and the tempura boiled egg. The following day, I came back for lunch to try the burger that everyone talked about. The burger was no disappointment.

The bar looked really neat and impressive as well but I'm not much of a drinker. But I appreciate the bartender greeting me.

While I'm not vegan or vegetarian, I found my cauliflower steak to be excellent. Cooked just right with great flavors and a delicious sauce. Asparagus and potatoes on the side were also great. I enjoyed the carrot cake for dessert too. Their $7 cork fee is very reasonable (where I live it's typically $30!). Service was good, and having one of the owners come by and talk with us a few times was also a nice touch. 

All the food was great and I'd return for that (and I give the food 4 stars!). However, I removed a star because they charge a 3.9% to pay with a credit card. For a restaurant that charges $20 an entree, I find it ridiculous to pass this cost on to customers in this way. I've never seen a restaurant at this price point do this to customers. It left a bad taste in my mouth (no pun intended) after an otherwise good experience. I suggest that instead of charging a fee to pay with a credit card, they instead build the fees into the cost of their dishes to improve the experience of credit card paying customers.

I  ordered food to go and when I returned home to eat with my wife I didn't get my sub I ordered we also ordered a lot of appetizers which also included there wings which were flavorless. The Philly had iceberg lettuce on it? I'll never understand why as it was hard to stomach. My dog didn't even eat it. My wife and I both got sick and are taking turns in the restroom. I will never return to this musty place again and neither will my friends or family.

If you're looking for the WORST dinner experience in your life look no more.

I will NEVER forget my experience here.

The food was ready as soon as I got there. I added 6 bags of chips. I was carrying my sleeping younger son, the pretty girl behind the counter took it upon herself to pack up the chips for me as well  since my hands were full.

I am not kidding you the Owner of Amighettis shows up at my house a little later with the correct sauce. Unreal. You do not find that kind of customer service everyday. Everyone makes mistakes. I was so skeptical and honestly did not want to eat here. If it wasn't for my significant other, I would have never given this place a chance but boy was I wrong. I'm the type who even hates Costco sushi which is what I was expecting the quality to be like. 

I could not believe how good the sushi was for an all you can eat place. Sure, it's nothing compared to places like Roka Akor but it's really good when you look at the price.

Everything is made to order and you can order all the appetizers, sushi and dessert that you like but just make sure you eat it because they will charge you extra for uneaten food. Also, you have to eat all of the rice. 

Overall service was pretty good although slow at times since the place is super busy. Expect to be there a while.

I got the 
PRIME RIB STROGANOFF $13
prime rib / wide egg noodles / parmesan /  mini basil parmesan loaf
A pint of the Firestone 805

The bread loaf was good, and I loved that they used what tasted like real butter.

My wife got the:
GRILLED FLANK STEAK $18
marinated flank steak / sautéed  mushrooms / cabernet reduction    gorgonzola butter / garlic mashed potatoes / seasonal vegetable

The mashed potatoes were light and fluffy with a not over powering taste of garlic.  To be honest the gorgonzola butter was the piece that made the dish YUM!.

With several options for to choose from for $15 or less, we will definitely be coming back here to try the many other menu options.  Well done to the owners, chefs and the rest of the staff, we made fans out of us!

My first time here for lunch and I must say it did not disappoint.  We asked to be seated near the window, so that we could enjoy the view.  Once seated we both realized that the view is much prettier at night or when there is snow everywhere ;), but it was still nice to sit next to the window.
My wife ordered the day's special which was a sausage ravioli.  There were a decent number of ravioli on the dish.  They had great flavor!
I decided to get the Chicken Parm (Parmesan crust, tomatoes, whole milk mozzarella).  This is a terrific spin on the classic dish.  First things I notices when the dish arrived was that there was no pasta, no marinara sauce, and that there was mashed potatoes and veggies on the plate.  The veggies were grilled and nicely flavored.  The mashed potatoes were fluffy yet creamy, but a couple of bites were cold.  The chicken was very tasty and cooked to perfection, with a slight crunch on the outer edges with a very juicy middle.

The staff made us feel very welcome and took the time to explain their drinks and food products, even though there were others behind us, sorry!

I can't remember a time when I was so excited to write a review. My dinner at Silo was one of the most perfect meals of my life.

A little backstory: Most "Southern" restaurants miss the mark for me. They either go all deep-fried Paula Deen on you, or they make awkward cajun and creole attempts that never quite work. I'm a north-Louisiana boy who was raised on simple, country food like peas, greens, and cornbread. No étouffée here. No sirree. 

For me, Silo is Southern food done right. It's farm to table, but not in a stupid trendy way; everything here is upscale humble... the way any classy Southerner should be. 

Let's break the rest of this review into three parts: ambiance, service, and food:

^Ambiance
Silo is in the gorgeous Germantown, which is totally worth a walk around after dinner to help digest. They take reservations on Open Table (yay!), but we didn't need one the late night we came in. We asked to sit on the patio and were promptly whisked away to the beautiful outdoor seating. 

I loved everything about the decor. It wasn't kitschy or cutesy. It was casual, dark, rich, and unpretentious. A+

^Service
We had Lauren (with the braces... her words, not ours), and she was one of the best servers I've ever had. I wanted to be her bestie, and I left thinking she wanted to be mine too... that's some talent, girl. Seriously, Lauren was so genuine and helpful. I love a server who will confidently give their opinion and not dance around what they like and don't like. She did not make a single bad recommendation, and she definitely added a huge amount of value to our experience. 

^Food
And now what you've been waiting for... the food! Oh my. Where do I even start?

I started with a gin cocktail (I forget the name) that was perfection in a glass. It was strong and delicious! Next up, the deviled eggs. They were great, but not mind-blowing. They were probably the only tiny downside in the whole night. 

While my friends ordered main entrees, I stuck with sides. I was the smart one of the night. I ordered collard greens, cornbread with pecan bacon butter, and grits with bacon jam. I make some damn good greens, but Silo's were better - really complex flavors that were dancing on my tongue. The cornbread was gluten-free and sinful. And last, the grits with the bacon jam were wonderful - creamy, tangy, and rich. 

Even though we were stuffed to the max, we split a pot de crème because every Yelp review praised it. Holy shiz. It was thick, creamy, caramely custard... and it came with a side of bacon caramel corn! I was dying at the table. Also gluten-free.

So you may have noticed I mentioned gf a few times... yeah, I have this wheat thing. And it kinda rules my life when I'm going out to eat. But I was upfront with Lauren, and she told me not to worry... the menu was full of goodies I could have! I can't thank Silo enough for making me feel like a "normal" person out to eat - not having to constantly worry or eat really strange variations of dishes to avoid my arch nemesis.

^In the end...
I adore Silo. I cannot wait for a return trip to Nashville to come here again. Our dinner was our first meal in Nashville, and it spoiled us for the rest of the visit! No place could live up to my new favorite restaurant. Until next time, Silo, I'll be thinking about you.

XXOO,

Bryant M.
