The noise levels we experienced during our visit was pretty high. We were not served right away and felt like the servers younger crowd aged customers were more important than we were. 
We were not happy with the food either. Very disappointed with this restaurant.

First impressions are everything. Most of the time. 

I asked people in my social networks if they've tried this place yet, but Little Korea was pretty new (the server said they just opened a few days ago. the owners are Korean, just FYI). I've also never eaten at a Korean restaurant in Louisiana. Ever. So please don't ask me to compare it to Korea House or The Wandering Buddha...

Atmosphere
The music playing is Korean music, naturally. Big windows and cool lighting fixtures make this little place hip, comfortable, and casual. I think it's a good size; you don't feel too out in the open or too close to the next table. Brown and pink is definitely not a color palette I'm used to for a restaurant; it reminds me of a bakery (Sprinkle to be exact). 

Food
We ordered korean ribs and dumplings, and some other food... I really can't remember because my friends ordered the food before I got there. However, overall, the ribs were great, but I loved the dumplings! They weren't steamed, though, but I still liked the crunchiness and flavor. The Korean ribs weren't too chewy or hard, so eating it didn't stress me out (lol). I wasn't too fond of the side dishes (each person got a plate of 3 things), but what can I say... I never really liked kimchi to begin with -- I know! it's blasphemy, but I've tried so many times to like kimchi :[ and thumbs up for the rice for not being too sticky ^_^

Service
There are a few things they missed here and there, but it's not a big deal. They were still attentive and accommodating. The bus boy refilled my water only once though :( 


Why 4 stars
Overall, I liked everything, but it has so much potential to become well-established. I look forward to dining here again. 


On another note, I feel perfectly safe dining here, but maybe that's because I was here in broad daylight where vampires can't get to me (unless it's the Cullens, then we'd really have a problem).

The last time I visited my mom in Tucson, she picked Crying Onion Café for breakfast. I was excited because my mom has great taste and is always finding cute little places. 

CRYING ONION CAFE

Stan Earl and his wife, Deborah Akers-Earl opened the Crying Onion Café in May 2001, after years working for other restaurants. Earl previously worked at Perkins, where he developed a reputation as a workhouse chef and master at the grill, who was known for making giant pancakes and killer omelets. Notoriously shy, he rarely emerged from the kitchen. Sadly, in 2006 Stan Earl died unexpectedly at 50 years old, leaving the business to his wife, who currently continues to run and manage the establishment.

THE STORY

Crying Onion Café is in a small shop in a strip mall on the north-east corner of Orange Grove and Thornydale, next to Sam Levitz Furniture. it was extremely busy with people who looked like they had an average age of 70. There was a slight wait to get a table. The place is decorated like a group of Grandmothers had an unlimited budget at Hobby Lobby, including vinyl table cloths and menus in plastic. We were seated and the waitress immediately brought out some coffee and crazy mismatched mugs. My mom told me the funny mugs were "a cute thing they do with the customers" to have them bring in mugs. I'm really not entirely sure what she meant, but I stopped asking her questions at that point. My mom usually doesn't pick this style of place, so I started worrying that maybe it's been too long since my last visit. 

SERVICE EXPERIENCE

I got the chorizo scramble with corn tortillas and my mom got the chili/cheese breakfast wrap. The food was good. The service was typical diner style: fast and friendly.

CONCLUSION

Crying Onion Café is definitely not my scene, but I would go back.

3/5 RECOMMEND

OF NOTE

*HOURS:
Tues-Sun: 6:30am-2pm

*Press:
Tucson Weekly, tucsonfoodie.com "18 Breakfast Diners To Try," and The Arizona Daily Star/tucson.com all highly recommend Crying Onion Café

*There is plenty of parking out front.

*For more information:
Call directly: 520-531-1330 ~ Crying Onion Café does not have a website.
Consistently great food and great service! Come here a couple times a week and have yet to be disappointed. Wide variety of selections

It's always sunny here, but sometimes the weather gets chilly enough to enjoy a nice hot pot meal. But I find myself coming to Uniboil during the summer months too, probably because Phresh Teas is next door.

This restaurant and cafe duo is located in a plaza east of Old Town, close to where the car dealerships are. Parking is decent, it might be hard to get a close spot during busy hours but there's plenty of space. The right side is Phresh Teas where you can order food to-go, socialize with friends, and play board games. You'll want to enter through the doors on the left for Uniboil. Both businesses are owned by the same person, as well as Vons Chicken, Kaiju, and Su's Bowl near UCSB. Drink/snacks are the same as Phresh, I sometimes order milk tea with my hot pot.

There's other menu items like teppanyaki and noodle soups, but I go with the Build-Your-Own hot soup. You first choose a soup base depending on your spice tolerance and preference. Next, you select the protein you want in your pot. They have beef, lamb shoulder, pork, seafood, and vegetarian. The menu also lists the different ingredients that come with each option. I get the angus beef, which has cabbage, tofu, imitation crab, fish cake, corn, and a variety of other yummy things. The third step is side orders, where you choose rice or noodles. I like udon and additional imitation crab, which is a couple bucks extra.

Hot pot is traditionally a communal dish, something do with a group of people around the dinner table. But I like the individual pot because everyone has different preferences when it comes to taste. For newcomers, it's a cool concept. For old-timers, Unibowl does a pretty good job matching other restaurants like Boiling Point and Jazz Cat.

My supervisor loves to pick up a box or two from Spudnuts on the way to the office. They have a large variety of doughnuts to choose from and everything is reasonably priced. It's the perfect break room snack.

There's multiple Spudnuts around SB. I usually went to the Isla Vista location when I was a student, and the Goleta store on Hollister. This one is located in a small plaza along State Street, right next to Sun Sushi.

Try to come early for the best selection. They have everything from doughnut holes, to old-fashioned, to jelly-filled, to cake doughnuts. The menu even extends to croissants, fritters, and cinnamon rolls.

The use of potato flour supposedly gives it a more fluffy consistency. I personally can't taste the difference between theirs and your average raised doughnut, but I would agree it was on the softer side.

One doughnut I tried recently was the chocolate-filled maple glazed bar with chocolate chips on top. They were very generous with the filling, the first bite was almost like chewing on Gushers. Very decadent and indulging.

This location is also really good for a quick breakfast. The second half of the menu is bagels, with several toppings and spreads available. I'm a little hesitant on trying their boba, but they have slushies, smoothies, and juices as well.

Hit or miss with this location. Their beef patties tend to be on the drier side, sometimes too overdone for my taste. Usually I let it slide because the Parmesan Herb & Truffle Fries are amazing, and I've had many decent burgers at the original Mesa restaurant. But when the quality of the food is consistently inconsistent, and the price tag is a premium, it's hard to justify another visit.

You can find them at Camino Real Marketplace, with other local heavy hitters like OTA and Los Agaves. Parking is plentiful, but nearby spots can be hard to find. There's tables outside, complete with umbrellas and patio heaters depending on the weather. They also have tables inside. Mesa Burger is pretty casual: you order at the counter, grab a number, and your meal will be brought to you.

The menu has several gourmet burger options, each with their own unique combinations of toppings and sauce/aioli. You can also get a vegan patty burger with vegetable toppings, a grilled chicken sandwich with pesto aioli, and a fish sandwich combined with coleslaw and mesa burger sauce. They use a delicious brioche bread for their bun, which can be substituted with wheat, lettuce, or sourdough. Iron Chef Cat Cora's Slider Flight is a trio of mini burgers (Mesa, Montecito, & Mission) complete with Hawaiian sweet buns. Rounding out the rest of the menu are salads, desserts, kid meals, and add-ons/upgrades.

Their meat patty is a blend of what I believe is angus and chuck. The default doneness is medium; on my last visit, it was more well done. The top and bottom were very charred, absent of any juiciness every bite.

On the upside, Parmesan Herb & Truffle Fries were great as usual. Maybe next time I'll request medium rare.

Takeout was a pretty dismal experience, definitely go for sit-down dining. They have a really nice outdoor patio area.

Sushi - Good variety of rolls, maki, and a la carte options at different price points. The majority of the menu is around $10 to $13.75, with a couple of rolls under $9. I tried the Shrimp Tempura Crunch Roll, which is a combination of imitation crab, avocado, and shrimp tempura, plus a slight dusting of tempura flakes on the outside. It came with too much rice and too little filling. Shrimp tempura was on the soggy side, which I expected because it was sitting inside the roll. Still pretty tasty nonetheless. The side salad was alright.

Udon - White, wide, wheat flour noodles and soup. You can have it with chicken, vegetables, tempura, or a combination of chicken and tempura. I noticed that the noodles were packaged with the soup for my to-go order. Most places keep them separate, which is preferable because of how mushy everything gets when it sits in liquid for too long. Still edible by the time I got home, but definitely a drop in quality as a result.

The rest of the menu sounds promising, kinda want to try one of their bentos or rice bowls. I'd give it a second look.

B.L.T., Huevos rancheros, and jambalaya all under one roof. It's a very unique breakfast and lunch joint that brings together the best of Cajun and Mexican cuisine. The menu is super extensive, and I'm sure there's something everyone will love.

Beignets - A must-order every time! Each French-styled doughnut is nicely fried until it reaches a golden color, and they're not stingy when it comes to the powdered sugar. You can pay extra for additional fruits, whipped cream, and caramel toppings.

Crab Cakes Benedict - Offered weekends only, served with your choice of fries, hashbrown, or grits (fruit substitute available for $1.00). Very well seasoned crab cake patty, and the hollandaise was rich and creamy. The poached egg was also perfectly runny. I wasn't a fan of the English muffin, it was burnt and the edges were charred.

Standard brunch fare - Occasionally I'm in the mood for something simple, and you can't go wrong with french toast, waffles, or a classic stack of pancakes. Love the different toppings and customizations they offer.

Drinks - Large variety of alcoholic beverages (champagne, beer, Michelada) juices, iced teas, sodas, etc. Coffee is from Dune, a popular local chain.

Good portions, great taste. A hearty meal to start your day on a positive note.

Such a treat! I can't get enough of those parmesan herb & truffle fries. 

Located in a small plaza along Meigs Road, Mesa Burger is the product of celebrity chef Cat Cora, businessman Chris Chiarappa, and the Mesa community as a whole. It's a casual eatery that borrows local jargon (Goodland, Funk Zone, Hope Ranch) and showcases some of the best gourmet burgers the Central Coast has to offer. You can say expectations are high, but they truly deliver on quality and it's always a satisfying meal!

The line usually goes out the door, but it goes by fast. Help yourself to any table inside or out, with great patio seating. 

On the menu you will find about a dozen burger options, some salad choices, and a boatload of customizations. The brioche bun they use is delicious, but you can switch to wheat/gluten-free. Beef patties are usually cooked medium, which is a tad dry for my taste. Upgrades include veggie patty, turkey patty, chicken, and locally-caught fish. The self-titled Mesa Burger is a solid choice and my go-to. For something more adventurous, Funk Zone is the one you want. 

They also have solid side items like sweet potato waffle fries, onion rings, and the parmesan herb & truffle fries I raved about earlier. Each come in single or share sizes, and they pair super well with your burger. One discontinued item they offered years ago was The Pit - a trayful of fries, ground beef patty, lettuce, salsa, and topped with cheese. Super sharable like nachos. 

I'm so glad to hear they expanded yet again and opened a new location in Montecito!

One of the best patisseries I've been to outside of France. Whether you get the plain croissant, the almond-studded one, or the pain au chocolat, all their pastries choices are delicious.  

Renaud's can be found in Loreto Plaza along State Street and Las Positas. It shares parking with many businesses such as Gelsen's and Chaucer's, but there's plenty of spots.

The bakery menu consists of muffins, macarons, cookies, quiches, chocolates, cakes, pies, petit gâteaus, meringues, and other breads and packaged sweets. Their drink selection is extensive, serving various cold beverages and coffees. 

They also have a bistro menu if you're planning to stay for breakfast or lunch. You can find everything from omelettes to Croque Madame. A few Yelpers have expressed some disappointment with the food, and I can echo this sentiment. Their sandwiches tend to be hit or miss, and I've had a few inconsistent experiences that convinced me it's best to go elsewhere for brunch. 

But their croissants are consistently solid. Renaud's almond croissant is generously encrusted, and they don't skimp on the filling. On my most recent visit I opted for a regular croissant, which was just as amazing. The outer layer is beautifully golden, while the inner layers are perfectly buttery, flakey, and puffy.

I've been to Sachi on Chapala and Kai on State Street, but didn't realize there was a sushi place inside Paseo Nuevo until pretty much now. Came in with Japanese comfort food in mind, but left with an order of rolls as well.

Tempura Udon - Love how the soup was packaged in a separate container, Sushi Ai in Goleta did not do the same for my takeout recently, and it was a soggy mess. Thank you thank you thank you. The udon by itself isn't expensive, but the toppings are an easy $3-4 extra. Options include Chicken, Gyoza, Pork Belly, Seafood, or Steak. The Mixed Tempura was a good choice, the vegetables were fried nicely and the shrimp was tasty. Wish they just had a simple beef udon.

Chicken Teriyaki Bento - This was a feast. Sweet glazed slices of chicken laying on a bed of rice, with a side salad and an orange slice to go along with it. It also comes with six California rolls, two fried gyozas, and a (potato? sorry I forgot) croquette. Very filling compared to the soups, and more variety compared to the rice bowls. For additional $$, you can have an extra serving of beef, chicken, or tempura.

Sweet Crunch Shrimp Roll - premium version of the Shrimp Tempura Roll essentially. Very similar ingredients: shrimp tempura, crab, cucumber, avocado, sweet soy. Not too sure if it was worth it, I might've just gone with the regular one instead.
Small interior with only space for a few to socially distance. Outside area is nice to sit on warm days, with umbrellas providing shade.

Top tier tri-tip. Can't make the drive out to Santa Maria or Firestone Grill in SLO? Stop by Shalhoob's instead.

They're located in the Funk Zone, but very off the beaten path. It's a very interesting mix of single family residences and businesses on this street, with the street itself feeling like a large alleyway. Parking is free for all; basically park anywhere your car will fit and make your own spot, but don't block the driveways.

The patio menu consists of tacos, sandwiches, burgers, salads, and barbecue dishes. Since it was my first time, I had to get their signature tri-tip sandwich. First off, the quality of the meat was phenomenal. Each slice was medium rare and cooked evenly, with a nice pink hue. Combined with pico de gallo, garlic bread, and a dab of barbecue sauce, this sandwich was bursting with flavor. It was served with a side of fries (you can choose salad instead), which were hot and crispy to my liking.

Their Mac N Cheese is awesome, probably one of the best renditions I've tasted so far. It's super creamy and heavenly, and topped with extra bread crumbs on top for good measure. Using Orecchiette pasta was also a unique touch.

They also have a butcher shop on-site with various poultry selections, cuts of beef, sausages, pork items, and wild game (bison, boar, buffalo) to mention a few. Definitely something to look into if you're planning a special dinner and as the holiday season kicks into high gear.

Probably one of the more accommodating coffee shops in the area for college students. Reliable internet, printing services, several outlets, ample seating, extended weekend hours, and a very extensive food and drink menu here. I remember they would even stay open overnight during finals week. It is a bit of a trek from campus and the parking situation is less than ideal, but it was nice coming here once in a while to study.

The store is located along Hollister, between Orange and Magnolia Avenue. Parallel parking out front is available if you're lucky; otherwise there are lots near Pattaya Thai Restaurant and Community West Bank, all within reasonable walking distance. It's a very comfy atmosphere, with exposed wood frame walls/trusses along with a set of couches to make the space open and inviting. There are tables inside and out, complete with heaters or umbrellas depending on the weather.

One thing I noticed was that their tea selection was pretty extensive, most coffee shops tend to have just the popular green or iced teas (which is fair, they are coffee shops after all). I appreciate that they offered many choices, and you can also get it in a teapot. Another thing I saw was food featuring many local businesses! They have had doughnuts from Hook & Press, treats from Rori's, and empanadas from Buena Onda, and many different pop-ups. Their own menu line-up is strong, with several pastries and snacks to choose from. I did try one item in the past that I wasn't too much of a fan of: their rendition of avocado toast. Too little avocado, too much radish and green onion and other unnecessary toppings that made it unenjoyable. Overall I've had many positive experiences with their lattes and baked items.

Old Town Coffee is the one-stop shop for all your caffeinated needs and more!

Beautifully handcrafted and designed. The bonbons made in-house are out of this world, and they also have a large collection of chocolate bars from around the world. 

From State Street driving onto Gutierrez Street, the public parking lot on the left would be most convenient. The storefront is just a few steps away, close to other businesses like Santa Barbara Roasting Company and Backyard Bowls. 2 customers max inside due to social distancing, I was the only patron for a bit but a line start forming outside. The Chocolate Lounge was unfortunately closed. 

The lady behind the counter was so kind and helpful. I was overwhelmed by all the choices, I basically just asked, "what is the best milk chocolate bar you have?" She was more than happy to point out her top choices and explain a bit of the background behind each bar. I was leaning towards something a little crunchy, so I went with Dick Taylor Hazelnut Milk Chocolate. With hazelnuts from Oregon and cacao from Brazil, every bite was delightful. It was more of an earthy chocolatey taste, with the milk taking the backseat on this one for subtlety, but enough to bring balance to the flavor. 

I also went home with a box of 8, all very solid choices:
- Salted Caramel: Dark shell with a bit of rum and sea salt
- Fresh Mint: Dark ganache, lemon & mint combination
- Ecuadorian Heirloom: 85% cacao is pushing it but it was good
- Hibiscus Flower: I didn't get to try this one but they loved it!
- Pistachio: chocolate shell with creamed pistachio
- Lavender eucalyptus: dark chocolate with flower and honey infusion
- Orange Blossom Caramel:  White chocolate in a dark shell
- Turkish Coffee: 70% cacao and a hint of finely grounded beans

Kudos for offering a variety of gluten-free, dairy-free, sustainably-sourced, high quality chocolate.

Open-air taco spot with the most chaotic atmosphere I know: batting cages on one side, cars driving down Milpas Street on the other, and railroad tracks on the third side. Complete with background music and a loudspeaker that calls out every order, you're in for a noisy but fun time. 

The Triple Play is the way to go- three tacos for under $10. It's a little pricey, but never ever buy one taco individually ($4-$5). You can request lettuce to substitute your tortilla for dietary or healthy reasons. Other menu options include cheeseburgers, hotdogs, chicken sandwiches, fish + chips, and more. I've only tried their tacos, but I enjoyed every one so far:

- Gangnam Style: corn tortilla with Korean marinated meat. Interesting selection of veggies, as well as a chili vinegar that has a good kick to it. 
- Carne Asada: very familiar, flour tortilla, solid choice. 
- Ahi Poke: tuna paired with a wonton hardshell, a combination I didn't know I needed until now. 
- Banh Mi: pulled pork with vegetables meant for a Vietnamese sandwich. Was better than I first thought!
- Grilled Fish / Shrimp: tasty, wish the portions were bigger. 

Highlight of the day was trying out the 80 MPH batting cage after lunch. Out of 20 pitches, I made contact with the ball for like 12 of them!

Whenever out of towners come by to visit, I always suggest meeting up at Los Agaves! I think it really embodies the spirit of Santa Barbara; slightly upscale food in a casual, laid-back atmosphere.

Usually I go to the one in Goleta, but this location has a better outdoor dining area in my opinion. It's very homey and open, the lighting at night gives the place a warm ambiance. As implied earlier, it's not a full sit-down restaurant because you have to walk up to the counter to order first. You then find a table and they'll bring your order over.

I've tried their Tacos al Pastor, which were generously portioned out and included thick cubes of pork, pineapples, onions, and rice/beans on the side. The tortilla tasted fresh, and the guajillo sauce tied everything together. The quality of the meat was outstanding; it's just as good as the tacos at standalone taquerias.

One experience that was not quite spectacular was when I had their shrimp alambres. It's a $16.25 dish consisting of three corn tortillas, three shrimps (yes three pieces), a boatload of bell peppers, some sliced onions, and melted Monterey Jack cheese to top it off. It was just not fulfilling at all, and missing that grilled flavor. I would probably stick with chicken or steak next time.

There's so much on the menu I haven't explored yet! They definitely have something for everyone.

A high quality burger paired with a healthy dose of philanthropy makes a satisfying meal! They team up with different organizations each month, with a portion of your purchase supporting people with special needs.

I like this specific location because parking is super hassle-free. Located on the corner of Hollister and Glen Annie, Kyle's shares a large lot with two other restaurants. The outdoor patio is significantly better compared to the one at Calle Real because it's on the side of the building rather than in front, with less cars passing by. Inside there's a couple of small round tables with bar height seating as well as some group tables. Some have six chairs, which are not pretty cramped.

They serve about 10 different burgers, each having their own unique set of ingredients. If you want, you have the option to add/remove ingredients and substitute different buns/proteins. I think a common observation most people have is that the portions feel small for the price they are commanding. And that's pretty valid, they charge $7-9 each and all the burgers I've ordered had their contents arranged so that the ingredients are spread out, with a patty that looks to be on the smaller side.

I tried to switch things up and got the Ahi In My Body this time around. The patty is seared ahi tuna, along with crushed avocado, sprouts, arugula, tomatoes, wasabi aioli, and a tasty brioche bun. It's a cold burger some people may find off putting, but it was a delicious combination that worked well. Mine was also a little light on the avocado. The hand-cut fries were double-fried with some seasoning sprinkled in, which I found amazing.
One menu item I usually get is the Mint Choc Chip milkshake! I'm just a big fan of dessert, and Kyle's sells cookies and ice cream as well.

Prices may be on the high end, but they also do pair it combos. A burger plus fries and a drink starts out to $12, which is okay for one meal.

Much love for On The Alley, the food is delicious and relatively inexpensive! I would come here all the time when I was a college student for a quick meal. From burgers to breakfast burritos to Brophy Bros. classics, this casual harbor eatery has everything everybody will enjoy. Some of the menu items I've tried:

Fish & Chips - Always served piping hot and fresh out of the fryer. The batter is light and airy, with just enough crunch every bite. Perfectly flakey fish as well.

Clam Chowder - No need to travel to New England, Seattle, or Pismo! OTA's rendition is super creamy and savory. I'm not too crazy about their sourdough bread, but it satisfies a craving.

Crab Cake Burger - Probably one of their more inconsistent options, the crab cake patty can be a hit or miss when it comes to portion size.

Pulled Pork Sandwich - Generous amounts of slow-roasted pork, I know other places go ham when it comes to adding coleslaw. Thankfully that wasn't the case here.

OTA Burger - Your conventional burger but with a breakfast twist. Fried egg, avocado, and bacon make a very tasty combination.

Definitely a solid joint to visit if you're looking to eat by the water!

I'd like to preface this review by saying that of all the reviews I've given on Yelp, this is my first 1 star review. I am a pretty laid-back reviewer who does not fret about small details.  The bad service and bad food my family had here, however, warrants this low rating. Honestly, Bertucci's or Olive Garden offer better Italian food than Spasso, and with better service. I've also heard great things about Trattoria Giuseppe on W Chester Pike. 

My family made a 5pm reservation for Christmas Eve to eat at Spasso for the first time. When we arrived, they sat us in a nice table in a large room to the side of the entrance. They then came over after a few minutes and told us they put us in the wrong place. Accidents happen, so that was fine. Our new table, however, was in the noisy foyer next to the entrance and the kitchen. It felt like we were sitting in a hallway. We saw many better tables open and were left to wonder why on Earth would they put us at what appeared to be the worst table in the restaurant. The manager then came over to us and began to interrogate us as if we never even had a reservation to begin with. She then emphasized in a condescending manner that the other table was not for us; it was for her friend.  She eventually found our reservation on the sheet, but only after insulting us and making us feel unwelcome.

Next the waitress came over to tell us about a special appetizer sampler with fried and grilled  calamari, prosciutto, caprese, etc. We were a party of six, but we told her we only wanted the sampler for two. She seemed hesitant to do that, so my mom explained that, as 80% of the platter was seafood and meat, most of the group wouldn't be able to eat it, as two were vegetarians and two didn't eat seafood. She then had the nerve to say "Well, you're a party of six, so let's make it for 4?" Rude and inexcusable. 

What happened next solidified for us that the we would never come back to Spasso. One person ordered chicken parmesan while another ordered veal parmesan. When they brought out our food, we double-checked with the waitress to ensure that each person got the right one, as the person who ordered chicken parmesan does not eat veal and is disgusted by it. Unfortunately, even after we asked,  the waitress mixed up the dishes, causing our one party member to feel sick after accidentally eating veal. When we told the waitress about her mix-up, all she said was "Oh, okay. Sorry about that. Does anyone want dessert?" in a completely apathetic tone. Terrible, terrible service.

Now, to review the food. The veal parmesan, as other reviewers have said, is dry and flavorless. The chicken parmesan was also average at best, certainly not better than something you could get at Olive Garden for less money. I had the fettuccine pomodoro which was pretty good and only $13, perhaps the only item on the menu we ordered whose price matched its quality. The gnocchi gorgonzola tasted like candy, and not in a good way. The person who ordered it could not eat more than a few bites. My dad had the zuppa di pesce, which he said tasted like they just used a can of tomato paste to make the sauce. The plate cost $24, so there is really no excuse for the sauce to taste that bad. It would've tasted better if they had walked down to Trader Joe's and bought one of the jars of sauce they sell. Very disappointing to say the least.

Media has tons of affordable, classy restaurants with great food. Spasso simply isn't worth a visit. The overpriced bad food, combined with the terrible, condescending service we received from the manager and the waitress, is going to keep any of us from ever eating at Spasso again.

Waited over 45 minutes for food, which was subpar at best. Went in on an evening when there was not a huge crowd. Perhaps they had most of their cooks call off sick? Waitress did not refill our drinks the entire time, and also got my sons order wrong. My daughter ordered the Mac n cheese and it was soupy. Seems like it could be a fun place, but I would vote for this restaurant to be on one of Americas worst.

What a nice addition to the Greenwood area restaurants.  Conveniently located near the Greenwood/County Line Exit of I-65, the restaurant had a nice makeover from the previous tenant.  There is still the same ample parking and a spacious patio.  But now, there is a solid row of televisions stacked 2 high all the way around the bar/large dining room.  There is a stage in the North East corner of the room as well.  Seating is mainly high table 4-tops in the bar room.

After checking in at the hostess desk, we were able to seat ourselves for lunch and grabbed one of the tables.  Service was great throughout.  They have a nice line of craft beers available, both local and national.  I was able to get a sample before choosing Metazoa's milk stout to go with my Black Jack Burger.  The burger was cooked to temp (I like a nice char on mine, so medium well on a thick burger.)  It came with cajun spice, bacon, pepperjack cheese, and tomato, lettuce, onion, and pickle on the side.  Excellent choice!  Note that this is a BMB (Big Mouth Burger that is hard to eat without a bit of scrunching).

My wife ordered the breaded tenderloin with a side of orange slices.  Although the meat was thick, tender, and cooked properly, the breading was less than expected.  It reminded her (and I agreed on what I tried) of a pre-breaded tenderloin that was thawed just before cooking.  Just didn't do much to wow her.  The portion didn't appear as large, but because it was so thick, it was really filling.

We really like the look of the place, though the music was a bit loud for lunch time dining.  Fortunately, the televisions are on mute to keep from adding to the din.

Although my wife misses the fire cracker shrimp of the previous business, I can see coming back to find a new favorite.

Review #2812

It had been a long time since I had dined at the Rathskeller, so while downtown with my wife, I decided to treat her to lunch at this iconic restaurant.  

The Rathskeller has so much history that I can't even begin to do it justice in a food review, so suffice to say, a long history of German culture has shaped the building, the restaurant, and the food.

We were greeted and seated in one of the downstairs dining rooms.  Note that they have some massive rooms for parties/festivals as well and a bar that is huge (complete with mounted trophy animals.)

Our room was lined with steins of all sizes and figurines that were plucked from literature and German lore.  We were seated in a corner at a glass covered table.  The room was rich in dark wood, very ornate, and proudly showing its craftsmanship.

We quickly selected our meals and while we waited, we were brought out a tasty hot pretzel with just the right amount of salt.  They also brought out a dipping mustard that would probably rival St Elmo's cocktail sauce for the amount of horseradish.  I didn't mind the flavor going down, but the burning sensation that filled my sinuses with even a little amount ruined the flavor for me.  I had to eat the pretzel without the sauce because it made no sense having it that strong.  (Note:  Aging the horseradish two days will allow the full flavor to come out without the unpleasant sensation according to one of my food professional friends.)

Anyway, our appetizer of stuffed mushrooms soon arrived.  The texture of the mushrooms stood out (very fresh!).  Cream cheese, bacon bits, chives and two kinds of cheese made for a nice start.

My wife went with a Chef Salad that was huge.  Strips of ham on top and her choice of dressing made for a nice meal.  However, the plate is so full that cutting the pieces down to bite sized made some of the salad fall off the plate to the table.  (They should be using a bigger plate, or smaller portions, or cut the lettuce into smaller pieces.)

I ordered the Kassler Ripchen which is a smoked pork chop topped with cooked apples, golden raisins, and walnuts to make a light sauce.  The flavor was very nice and the the components complemented each other.  It came with a slightly tart sauerkraut (good!) and German potato salad with much larger potato pieces than what you find in any type of American version.  No mustard here!

My wife wanted to split a bread pudding dessert which comes topped with a raspberry sauce and whipped cream and a cream base underneath to dip each bite in.  Very good!

Although our service was polite and generally good, she did miss noticing that my water had run out, that we could use more silverware, and she didn't pick up that we might want to share the dessert (most upscale places ask if we want to split a single dessert when ordered.)  Just things that we ended up taking care of ourselves, but for a $60 lunch for two without alcohol, I expected a bit more attention.

Overall, a good meal especially in October.

Review #3202

Delicious food option that can be as good as your ability to blend flavors.  When you enter (after pay street parking), there is an order counter with menu checklists that walk you through how to have your poke built.  Simply start at the top and check the boxes that you want (each section tells you if you can pick more than one item in that group or if there are fees for adding more.)

I started with a base (Burrito style for me, bowl for my wife, and a third option for a salad bowl.)  Then I chose a type of rice or noodle, then a type of green to add (spinach for me).  

You can add your protein next with different pricing for 1, 2, or 3 proteins (Tuna for me!)

Step 5 has Mix-ins (as many as you want).  Step 6 adds flavors (sauces and condiments), and Step 7 adds crunchies and toppings.

Finally, you indicate take out or dine in and put your name on it.  Tell the cashier your beverage preference and pay and they give you a buzzer that will let you know when to pick up your order.

The interior has a blonde wood throughout that looks fresh and new.  The interior is small, but feels spacious.  They have two gender neutral bathrooms, but be aware one has the light switch on the outside.

Before long, our orders were ready.  We both really enjoyed our lunches and found them quite satisfying.  My burrito style came sliced and wrapped in white paper, which once removed, revealed what looked like a seaweed wrap holding my order together.  The sauces/condiments were evenly distributed so that I got those accent flavors throughout the meal.

I did find the open ended burritos a little messy since some ingredients and sauce fell out the bottom.  I let the folks behind the counter know that it was that way and hope they begin wrapping the ends to make the meal easier to handle.

Overall, both of us enjoyed our meals and would gladly return and recommend it!

Review #1832

I took my wife to this new restaurant on Main Street and thought they had done a lot of things right.  I was a bit disappointed in the flavor, but I think there was a reason.  I'll get to that soon.

The restaurant is just east of the Arts District and kudos to them for having a small lot on their east side and a public lot directly north of the building without having to cross a street.  That is very helpful!

The place looks really cool too.  There is a large pergola covered patio and the tables have large umbrellas that with their ability to be tilted by the staff, did a pretty good job of keeping us comfortable dining outside even when it was nearing 90!

The staff was also very helpful.  Kind of a team concept and doors where held open for us and water was kept filled.  We were able to get our beverages and place our order promptly.

And when the food arrived, the orders were very generous is size.  My wife ordered Mae Mae's Meatloaf and it had probably two cups worth of meat!  There were also real mashed potatoes (with some chunks left) and a combo of collard and turnip greens that had a bit of seasoning (probably 1.5 cups worth!)  So, a lot of food.  My wife had to be coaxed to come her so I could try it, so it wasn't a big surprise to me she wasn't a fan of the greens.  I tried them and thought they were pretty good.

I ordered the salmon and it also was a large portion with a tasty coconut rice, citrus black beans, some buttery asparagus, and pickled red onion.  I was eating it and just thought it seemed lacking in flavor.  The salmon was cooked through, but not dry.  It just tasted like plain salmon.  I finished eating it with bites of my sides and it wasn't until I got home that I remembered it was supposed to have a chili lime butter.  So one of two things happened:  either they only add just a minimal amount, or they forgot it completely.  I couldn't taste it.  If I would have made the connection (they take away the menus when you order), I would have said something to give them the opportunity to fix it.  So, I will give them a 4 instead of what I was initially thinking was a 3 star meal.  Maybe the owner will read this and be able to tell if the chili lime flavor was there.  I just couldn't taste it.

We ended up getting a to go box for my wife's meal and got a round of Key Lime cake that was quite good (to go too!)  

So, generous portions at the $15-25 range for entrees.  Hopefully they will dial in the flavors of the food as it goes out to customers.

Review #3050

Well, I finally was able to purchase a milkshake from this expansion of Gordon's Ice Cream on the east side.  I will say that the flavor was good on my Salted Caramel Gourmet Milkshake and the staff working during my visit were friendly and quick to make my order.

But, I have had some issues here.  First, the milkshake didn't have that thicker texture that is a perfect balance between liquid and frozen ice cream.  My shake was really thin tending more toward cold flavored milk than a shake.

I also have to say this wasn't my first time trying to stop here.  On two previous occasions, I stopped by and the business was closed.  The hours on the door said they were supposed to be open, but the doors were locked.  That's frustrating.  There should be some sort of explanation on the front door saying why the business isn't serving customers.  Maybe it was a trouble experience when opening a new business.  Maybe it was some mechanical failure or some personal problem, but the owner owes it to the customer to at least post a sign if they aren't going to be open when scheduled.

I get that nobody is twisting my arm to purchase an $8 milkshake, but I like supporting local independent businesses.  But there is an expectation that the quality will warrant the price for an item that I can get dozens of other places (at least something similar).  I hope the management steps up soon, or else there could be more empty space available on Mass Ave.

Review #3612

I had heard about the expanded bar/restaurant and as I walked along Virginia Avenue, I thought it might be cool to sit out and people watch.  Unfortunately, there was only one person working the lunch shift and she couldn't cover both sides of the business as well as watch the patio.  So make a note that dining outside is an evening option.

Inside, the bar is dark with lots of tv's going (only one with volume on.)  I grabbed a spot at the bar and waited for the waitress to return to the floor.  It wasn't too long (a couple minutes), but felt odd until I realized she was the only one working the front of the house.

Anyway, I ordered a breaded tenderloin and a side of tots.  They were ready in short order and the portions were large.  Lots of tots that were lightly seasoned and had a nice crunch.  The tenderloin was a decent size and not pounded thin, so it held its moisture.  The bun itself was a bit buttery or maybe had a slight oil coating from being on the grill which necessitated using my napkin frequently.  The flavor was really good though, so I didn't mind too much.

Check out was fairly quick but there was a bit of a mixup on the change.  Not a big deal, but just something to be aware of when you pay.

Good good with large portions and prompt turnaround times.  Hopefully I can check out the patio on my next visit.

Review #2882

What did I like about Upland's newest brewpub?  Let me see:

1. Despite it being opening day, everyone who was working was making sure customers were being looked after.  I was greeted with a smile, and when I sat at the bar, I had a team of folks swing by to see if I needed anything.  Special shout out to Steve who was my main server.

2. The space is huge and even though the parking lot was nearly full at 4:30, I never felt crowded.

3. The Cuban sandwich was delicious!  It's not an authentic version, but it is one of the best I've had.  They use Smoking Goose City Ham (great on its own) and a spiced & smoked pulled pork along with melted swiss cheese and house pickle chips.  Delicious with a bit of heat, just enough to let you know it's there.

4. The Exploration flight which allows you to pick two of the their standard beers and two of the sours/barrel-aged beers to make your flight.  Sure it is more expensive than other places, but if you know about brewing, you know you have to keep your sours away from your regular beers which means having a separate facility for the brewing.  That costs money.  But if you want to try a sour or a barrel-aged sour, you won't find more choices than at Upland.

5.  The patio.  This is going to be a deal changer for the area.  Understand that despite the efforts of a few brave businesses like Kuma and Revolucion, nobody was drawing the crowds that Upland was doing to the east of the fountain.  With the new apartments going in across Prospect, Upland is moving the restaurant/nightlife area across that Shelby Street boundary.  The patio had lots of tables and with the open garage doors to the brewery, felt very much a part of the business, not just stuck out there.  

Five reasons = five stars.  Check this place out!

Review #2846

Maybe it was a case of having our expectations too high for a restaurant that has only been open a short while.  This is the newest of the CRG line and we have been fans of most of their line.  For a long time, Vida was our favorite of all restaurants, so if that is a 5, you can understand why this has a lower rating.  I think that when we return in the near future (yes, it has that much potential), they can iron out a few kinks and earn a higher rating.

We made reservations so that we could be assured of seating together with our friends as they celebrated their 54th anniversary and I approach my 1 year anniversary after my brain surgery.  So a big thank you to Modita for honoring both couples with a complementary dessert.  Fortunately, they let us know that so that we saved room for dessert after multiple courses.

Be aware that when you order, they want you to order all your courses except dessert up front so that the kitchen can minimize your wait times between courses and minimize the occurrence of your food growing cold.  Between the two couples, we ordered multiple items from each course and gave them a challenge.  Unfortunately, one of the entrees, the Amish Chicken  Yakitori did arrive cold (not just warm, but our friend said it was cold and my wife confirmed.  To their credit the waitress offered to replace it or comp it.  It was still tasty so she decided to go ahead and eat it (it was cooked, but had just grown cold) so she wouldn't have to make the rest of us wait.

Most of the food was excellent and worth trying.  We did have a few minor issues.  The A5 Wagyu Strip Steak (not upgraded to "Japanese" for another $20) was delicious but more chewy than I expected for Wagyu.  I realize a strip steak isn't going to be as tender as a filet, but I thought it would be more tender.  The group thought the Bao Buns were the best surprise.  I was last to try them from the shared plate and found mine to be way too smoky.  No one else seemed to notice anything but a hint of smoke.  I didn't want to finish it since I am not a fan of smoky flavor.  I prefer grilled taste.  My wife finished mine and commented that it was substantially more smoky than her piece which she found excellent.  I wish I would have enjoyed the dish as much as they did, but something in the kitchen must of caused my meat (pork belly) to become overly smoked.  Hopefully, as the kitchen gets settled, they will keep better balance across the dish.  We also tried the Maine Lobster Rangoon and my first piece smelled and tasted "fishy".  My second one was much better.  My friend let me sample his Bison short rib Bulgogi and it was delicious.  I also ordered the Short Rib Gyoza which was yummy and came with a sauce that was sweet and hot (not too hot for me, but too much for my wife's palate.)

My friend and I both ordered Gin and Tonics with Hendricks gin.  Excellent flavors.  I also tried one of the fruity house cocktails, the "Cuddle Magic" that was delicious.  Pay attention to prices as each couple's bill went up over $100 despite the comped food.  There are so many delicious items to choose from and even the cocktails were $14 each.  Oh well, we were celebrating and having a great time.  Our waitress Cora did a wonderful job of taking care of us throughout the evening though our request to turn the volume down on the music only yielded turning down the lights. ha!  I mentioned we were there to eat and talk, not dance.

 I am sure that in a short amount of time the CRG people will iron out the minor issues we encountered.  My wife would also like to request a hand rail be installed for people who don't want to walk to the end of the ramp just to get back to the entrance.  

We are definitely going to give Modita another chance soon.  Note that they don't comp your parking like the shops/restaurants in the Garage do.  That would be nice too!

We weren't able to find any available street parking at our visit, but were able to grab a convenient space in the surface lot across the street and north of 9th.  They have automated machines which need fixing because the audio says one thing and the message that you read says something else.  I finally gave my card to my friend and said to read the machine and not listen and it worked.  Not Modita's problem.  Just wanted you to be aware of parking for the restaurant.

Review #3903

With the challenge of construction, one way streets, and interstates making this location a difficult space to get to for those who aren't familiar with 11th and College, take solace knowing that the food and service is worth the effort!  Located in the former site of R2Go, there is free street parking along 11th though it does get a little crowded quickly.  Just be sure to look it up on your GPS before you go and you should be okay!

Although there is a door on the southwest corner, they are directing everyone to go through the large double doors on the west side of the building.  Inside, the order counter is straight back (menus mounted on the wall behind the cashier). On the right is the pastry and baked goods counter but you don't order from the staff stationed there.  Just remember what you want and place the order at the cashier along with any beverage you wish and with any sandwiches/other food items you want.

Understand that this isn't some cheap donut shop or fast food place.  If you want sandwiches for lunch, I think the ones we ordered were $10 and $12 apiece.  They serve them sliced and because we ordered some pastries as well as the grain side salad with our sandwiches, neither of us finished our sandwiches at lunch.  

We chose to sit outside by the entrance to the building.  I found it a little unusual that they didn't give us a table number, but the staff successfully delivered out pastries and sandwiches to our table.  We carried our beverages with us.  They also bus the tables, though it would be nice if they had a trash can near the outdoor patio so that we could get rid of our trash or could set our used silverware in a tub to make it easier for the staff.

Everything we tasted was uniquely tasty!  I ordered the Roast Beef Chimichurri and the bread was toasted and the sandwich sliced for easier eating.  Lots of yummy ingredients that I would never think of or go to the trouble of preparing at home.  My wife ordered the LVTHNTBA (a turkey, bacon, and avocado sandwich on marbled rye) that she also liked I got a bite and liked it too!

From the pastry side, my wife ordered some almond croissants and a crispy pastry called the Kouign-Amann which she raved about.  I ordered a slice of the Blueberry-Lime coffee cake that has a crumbled top.  Excellent.  When we added drinks, tax and tip, some would complain it was an expensive lunch.  But considering some was taken home for dinner and the pastries (what didn't get devoured immediately) would be nice for breakfast tomorrow!  It's multiple meals unless you are just a beast that stuffs yourself each meal.  Everything we tried was unique (other than the almond croissants), so in a time when I've become bored with my own cooking, it was fun to get out and try some new flavor combinations.  Very pleasant staff and plenty of seating inside as well.

If you want to try something different, make a plan for a day trip to downtown.  Just take College north to 11th and be patient going passed the Bottleworks construction.

Review #3784

Although this was my first visit to this location of Jockamo, I knew from my visits to the other locations in town that there was a good chance of finding something really tasty to eat!  I chose to bypass a small pizza and opted for the Italian Beef.   I don't know if it is the most authentic, but it sure is delicious.  Not only does it come with a thicker dipping sauce than most restaurants, but inside the sandwich were peppadew peppers that added another burst of flavor with each bite.  Really good.  My wife enjoyed her side salad and an order of breadsticks (3) that came with parmesan dipping sauce.  

Review #3968

If this place tries as hard once they are officially open as they did during today's soft opening, they are bound to have a winner!  I stopped by for lunch right as they were opening.  I had grabbed one of the free street parking spots along Talbott Street, but found that the restaurant/bar has half the parking lot across the street for their customers to use too!  

Inside, there is a hostess desk where you check in to be seated.  They have garage doors that open and let you be seated on their partially covered patio.  They also have bar seating and plenty of indoor dining at 4-top tables.

I was seated by the front windows and was greeted by my waitress who let me know that if I had any questions, to be sure to ask.  The place has a 3 way liquor license, so they have a variety of beers, wines, and cocktails available.  They also have milkshakes and Boozy Milkshakes where they pair liquor with the milkshakes.  Just let them know what flavor booze you like and they will help you find the best combo.

As far as the food menu goes, they don't have a huge selection, but they have some signature items as well as a build your burger option, broasted chickens (half and whole) and salads.  I went with the Strut Burger and a side order of fries.  The fries were plentiful and shoestring style.  Hot, with a bit of crispness/crunch.  If they were seasoned, it was very lightly.  They do have shakers and condiments on each table.  You can also get the fries loaded with sauces/toppings for an upcharge.

The Strut burger comes with two smashed thin burger patties, smoked gouda cheese, bacon, dill pickles, mango chutney, and something called "Dazzle Sauce".  In all, it was a nice blend of savory, salt, and sweet.

I also ordered a strawberry milkshake (without booze) and was surprised at first that it wasn't pink.  No artificial coloring added here.  And the flavor?  It was delicious!  I also like that they include a thick straw (like one you would use for boba).  Highly recommended!

This isn't a cheap restaurant that folks will swing by like a fast food place.   They do have a kids menu that runs in the $7-8 range, that includes a burger/chicken/mac 'n cheese, a side of choice, and a beverage.  But keep in mind that they do use quality ingredients.

There is a buzz growing in the neighborhood with Shoefly, Teas Me Cafe, and Loco in proximity.  Maybe this is one of those places that will continue to build in popularity.

Review #3062

My wife and I stopped in this small, no frills restaurant for lunch.  It's tucked away in a strip mall on the north side of 82nd street near several other restaurants and bars.  When we arrived, we were the only ones in the place.  We were greeted and were able to pick our own seating (booths and tables are available.)  

I started with a cup of Green Tea that was quite good. (Note they sell it by the cup, not by the tea pot as other places do.)

Because we ordered entrees, we each were brought a bowl of a chicken broth (with a few veggies) to start the meal.  Well seasoned, though not visually appealing.

My wife ordered the Fried Rice with chicken while I ordered the Sesame Pork which is both sweet and spicy.  She thought her chicken was cooked properly (not too rubbery) and the rice had a fair amount of flavor.  

My entree came with about a cup of white rice and a pair of fried cream cheese rangoon that were light and crisp.  The rice was a great side for gathering more of the sauce that had coated the entree.  The heat was moderate but definitely noticeable.  The sweet took on a citrus flavor as well.  The pork was cut in slender strips and were just a hint over cooked, but not enough to detract from the flavor.

Our waitress/manager (?) was really friendly and easy to communicate with.  

Fortunately, a number of guests started arriving for both dine in and take out, so it looks like we simply beat the rush.  

I do think the only negative for us was that the place could use a good deep cleaning to make sure everything is dust free and the bathrooms could use a good scouring.  But all table tops and dishes were clean, so we weren't concerned.

Review #3678

I normally don't frequent chain restaurants from out of state, but after trying some of the food items offered by Taziki's at one of the recent Yelp Elite Events, I thought it worth making the trip to the northeast side of the city to try a full meal there.   As you can tell by my rating, my expectations were exceeded!

Adding to my pleasure was the fact I had a free gift ticket that allowed me to have the special of the day which includes a free side M-Th.  What did I have to lose?

Note that this restaurant is on the south side of 82nd where the street is divided by a median.  So if you are east bound, it's not a problem.  If you are west bound, you will need to turn mid-block where there is a break in the median and then head passed a couple stores to the entrance of the restaurant.

Inside, there is a large dining area with the food prep/order counter on the right.  You walk passed the food prep to where a sign "order here" hangs.  There they have menus to look at to help you decide whether you want a bowl or a sandwich.  After ordering and paying, they give you a number to put on your table.  A beverage bar is not visible from the order counter, but it is just around a corner that is behind you (another sign hangs on the corner for beverages.)  Utensils and napkins are on each table.

After a short wait, the cashier brought out my tray with the Monday special, a Chicken Portobello Sandwich with my choice of a Tomato-Cucumber salad and chips.

I started with the salad and it was delicious (I highly recommend it!)  The veggies are sprinkled with Feta cheese and seasoned with a vinaigrette. (Similar in taste to a burrata.)

The sandwich was also very tasty with a grilled chicken breast served on a kaiser roll with Swiss Cheese, red bell pepper slices, sliced portobellos, and a mushroom butter.  Really good, though the sliced mushrooms tended to fall out sometimes.  The only negative was that there was a lot of "juice" on the paper lining the tray.  It wasn't greasy, just wet which made my fingers need to use the napkin more than expected.  

You don't even need to bus your own table here.  They do that for you.  Someone even stopped by to make sure I was enjoying my meal.  Although not full service, I thought the staff did a fine job.

Overall, I would recommend this place if you are interested in trying a tasty Mediterranean meal while in Castleton.  

Review #2680

Four of us made our first visit to Hyde Park during the Devour Indy promotion.  What we encountered was delicious food, excellent service, and a pleasant dining environment.  What else do you need? (okay, parking would be nice, but they do offer valet service and Circle Centre Mall isn't too far to walk.)

  Although we were pretty sure all of us were going to order filet mignon from the Devour Menu, we listened to the specials and recommendations of our waiter.  What was apparent was that if we stuck to the special 3 course meal, we would be saving a lot of money while still getting to experience this 5 star restaurant.

  Even though we did stick to our decision, we opted to add a Wagyu Beef Carpaccio starter served with peccorino romano cheese and greens and a couple biscotti.  I ended up making mine into a sandwich while my fellow diners used more gracious table manners eating their appetizer components individually.  Excellent, especially with the flavor from the capers managing to add a bit of saltiness.

  When we discussed our likes, we made reference to one of our party not liking seafood which our waiter picked up on.  What we didn't know was that an amuse bouche of carpaccio was planned for the night, so word got back about our order and the kitchen whipped up a unique starter for our table.  Three were a crisp topped with a tuna based bite and a fourth amuse bouche of caprese style tomatoes was put together for the non-seafood guest.  That's service!

  A course of bread was next on the list (the staff didn't cut corners just because we were going with the discounted menu options.)  The flavors were good and there was a nice variety, but the soft pretzel was very salty on the top; enough to draw a negative comment from my wife.

  We then got our first course.  Two of us went with a lobster bisque which was okay...it had large pieces of lobster, but the flavor of the lobster seemed a little "strong" on the first bite, but seemed milder on subsequent bites.  Maybe the sherry poaching affected the flavor. The others ordered a wedge salad and a Caesar...both got good marks.

  All of us decided that the first time to a steak house we should try the steak.  On this occasion, we all went with the filet mignon. One chose to upgrade to a larger size and another went with the crab and asparagus upgrade.  I think everyone ordered medium-rare and enjoyed the tender beef.  The steak came with garlic mashed potatoes and was topped with onion crisps.  We also ordered sharable asparagus and a dish of Brussels Sprouts that were prepared in a bacon marmalade (Wow!  Really great!)  The steaks were very tender and were slightly under seasoned for my taste, but still quite delicious.

  For dessert, two of us went with the Cheesecake that had a cherry topping.  The other two went with the flourless chocolate cake that was very dense and rich.  I would recommend sharing one between two people unless you are a complete chocoholic!  Maybe a cup of coffee might help clear the palate between bites of the cake.

  The service was excellent throughout the evening.  Besides the waiter checking on us, the manager (who was from Cleveland to train the staff) and the Executive Chef (Braulio Delatorre) stopped by our table during the evening to make sure we were being taken care of.  Their timing was not intrusive on our dining and was appreciated by our group.

  Overall, I recommend dining here if you would like a special night out or are independently rich.  They do have a special cut of Wagyu beef that goes for $140 all by itself.  Yikes!  But because the business offered to participate in the Devour Indy promotion, I now know that the food and service are excellent and that quality supports the prices.

Review #217

I never enjoy writing reviews where I drop my rating (especially from a 5 star down to just a middle of the pack rating.)  To be specific, the food and drinks that they offer are still delicious.  The problem is lack of proper management.  When a patron wants to plan a gathering (our group had 3 couples who had to travel on average 45 minutes to get to Thunderbird).  It was the first visit for four of our six people and we had looked at the website menus and came up with our food and drink selections based upon what was listed on their own website.  I also looked at my review from 2 months earlier and some wanted to try the items I had raved about.  But SURPRISE!  The bar had changed all their cocktails and the restaurant had changed all their food items.  None of the items we had enjoyed were available.  None of the items on the website were available.  Management allowed the changes to the in house menus, but failed to let anyone know what the options had changed to by updating their website.  I've been burned in the past by relying on third party menus or photos of menus, but when a business intentionally changes their offerings regularly, then it is up to management to make sure the social media (especially their own website) is updated.

When the waiter (who should wear clean shirts to work because my wife pointed out how sloppy his appearance was) kept insisting that we couldn't rely upon the website but had to use the existing menus at table side, he showed his lack of appreciation that we had come with one set of expectations and he seemed clueless that four of the six stood up and were ready to leave.  I had to calm them down with the realization that a group of six finding a table without reservations would be unlikely by just driving and stopping elsewhere.  So we stayed.
  As I mentioned in my earlier review, music in the background is okay, but we were seated right underneath a speaker at 5:30 in the evening.  It was so loud we asked for the music to be lowered so that we could talk and discuss what we wanted to order and share.  The place had barely any other customers that early and nobody was dancing, so why do you need the music blasting so loud at such an early hour?  One waitress acknowledged our request, but no discernable volume change occurred.  

The only reason this rating is not lower is that the food we settled on was tasty.  We tried different items and different cocktails that originally planned.  So the bartender and chef can be thanked for the okay rating.  

And another problem....they only have one dessert available.  It included a gluten free cake that was dry and left an aftertaste of some unexpected flavor for several of our diners.  Seriously, if you can't offer more than one option for dessert, that is a poor decision too.

I ended up ordering an Arugula salad that had a lemon based vinaigrette and got fried chicken strips added for a protein.  The lemon was so sour that it overwhelmed all the other flavors.  I like "lemon pepper' seasoning, but the lemon from the Pink Peppercorn dressing overwhelmed the pepper of the arugula and other salad ingredients.  

Sadly, I don't think I will be bringing any more guests here and recommend that management get busy and maintain their website menus.  It was very disappointing for our night out with friends.  At least some of us finely were able to carryon some conversation on the ride home.

Rev #60

Let me fully disclose that we met some long time friends for dinner and we had a great time visiting as well as enjoying the friendly service (great job Andrew B) and tasty food.  We had such a fun time that I am sure it puts a positive light on my rating and review.

There are a few minor things to be aware of that would make for an even better experience.  First, if I hadn't known from other reviews that this bar bistro was in the former Black Market location, I might not have found it.  The building still says Black Market and I couldn't see anything about Bodhi until I went to the front door.  Another thing to note is that this location suffers from the lack of parking that every other business on Mass Ave has.  We got to the restaurant when it opened at 5 pm on Monday, but their tiny lot was almost full already (we got the last spot.)  I suppose we could have paid for metered parking somewhere along Mass Ave or parked at the parking garage at Bottleworks and walked over.  But be aware that if you are meeting someone, be sure you allot time to find parking.
  Our friends arrived a few minutes ahead of us and were able to get a table for four by the windows.  (No reservations are available here.)  For us old folks, having lots of natural light to help read the menus is a plus.  They do have patio seating open but it felt a bit too chilly for us, so we stayed inside.
  Our waiter was upbeat and eager to serve and stayed in a positive mood throughout the dinner and cocktails.  I was the only one of our party who was familiar with Thai cuisine, so we needed some time to pick.  We started with our beverages (I got the Emerald Buddha (fresh and crisp cocktail) to start.  They also have a nice lineup of local craft beers on hand.  coke products too.  They didn't have any ice tea made other than Thai tea, so my wife couldn't get an Arnold Palmer drink.  A little disappointed, but not a big deal.

We moved on to some starters/shareables.  I ordered the Crab Puffs (think crab rangoon) which my wife declared she would get an order for herself next time and not share.  Served with sweet chili sauce for a sweet heat.  Probably the best rangoon we have had in town!  Highly recommended.  Our friend wanted a cup of Tom Yum soup, but was told it only was served in a large pot that was shareable.  I agreed to help her eat some.  Seems like minor change could be made to accommodate a single consumer.  The waiter said our friend could add a protein and make it her meal as an option, but enough of us agreed to help her eat it and we were brought out bowls and shared it.  
  
  My friends like spicy hot food, so I wasn't too concerned, but the website clearly states to not go too hot when ordering.  They can always add more spicy heat (they brought out chili flakes for our friends to add), but can't take it out.  If you order it hot and can't take it, too bad...no refunds on your mistake.  I like that they disclose this ahead of time and encourage people to not overdo the heat request until they are used to the standard heat levels served here.  Having said that, I ordered my items mildly spicy or at most, medium.  Our friends ordered their items medium and requested the pepper flakes, but didn't need many.  Be wise and aware of your options and responsibilities (you pay whether you eat it or not because of the heat level.)
  I ordered my standard Pad See Ewe which I get at every Thai restaurant on my first visit so I have a point of comparison between restaurants.  This was delicious and though on the pricy end of the cost spectrum, there was plenty to get a take home box for a second meal.  I've tried making this at home and just the ingredients I purchased on my own make me wonder how a restaurant can charge as little as they do.  I really appreciate great flavor without having to do any of the work myself.  Thanks to the ladies who run the kitchen at Bodhi.  Excellent flavor!  Our friends and my wife ordered different entrees including various stir fry and the drunken noodles.  All reported they enjoyed their meals.  Everyone got take home boxes too.  If you leave her hungry, you must have shared everything or just didn't sample enough of what everyone else ordered!

Because I finished my first cocktail while visiting and eating our appetizers, I ordered a tasty Francoise & Etienne cocktail to go with dinner.  It was so good I even ate the orchid and the tangerine ice cubes.  Yum

Hopefully they can find a way to manage parking.  A new hardware store just opened a few weeks ago across the parking lot, so that is going to make parking even more challenging.  If you are young and healthy, I suggest street parking along Mass Ave if you spot a space.  I was hopeful there would be some handicap reserved spaces, but didn't see anything nearby.  

  I look forward to returning in the near future to try some of the other goodies on their menu and cocktail list.  

Review #3904

I had a bit of a struggle settling on how high of a rating to give this Verde.  I think it depends upon your expectations before you arrive.  If you like a place that has tasty food and drinks, I could easily have bumped his up to a 5 star.  If you want to dine in a clean space that looks like new with good service (Pablo was our guy).  Again, another high rating.  If you want to eat an affordable lunch without alcoholic beverages, well there are lots of other options within the metro area that are far more affordable.  I also thought the dining area was a bit noisy and that even though the restrooms were right off the dining area, there was no signage indicating where to head without asking.  Some outdoor seating is also available if you catch a nice weather day and don't mind nearby traffic sounds.

Let me say hat my meal was delicious!  I ordered a quesadilla with strip steak that was so tender that I didn't need a knife to cut the tortilla or the meat.  Great flavor and texture.  I love that there was plenty of topping for the entire entree incl. pico and sour cream.  Rice and beans weren't overcooked either, so the entire meal was enjoyable.  Didn't have room for dessert, but they do have several options to choose from.  Lots of mixed/frozen drinks to choose from as well.  Just be aware that if you're top concern is pricing, know that the cost will skyrocket quickly.  Most entrees even at lunch were $10 or more.  This isn't like dining on street food or from a food truck.  This is more like dining in a nice restaurant and paying for that experience.

On opening day, I expected there might have been a problem, but the only surprise I got was how well the staff handled the customers!  I arrived for lunch without a reservation and since I was dining solo, I accepted a seat at the bar.  There, I was greeted and was shown a menu with food on one side, beverages on the back.

They have a Zero Proof option for someone wanting more than water, but non-alcoholic, so I decided to try a Kitchen Rickey which is a ginger ale based beverage with a lime, and orange bitters.  What a great punch of flavor that had! And the ginger added something close to a heat element that tingled at the back of my throat.  Great palate cleanser too!

I opted for a sandwich and side for my meal.  The Roasted Mushroom sandwich came with gruyere, garlic aioli, and braised greens and was served on square bread sliced diagonally.  Really great mushroom taste and the aioli was a great complement, not too garlic strong, but enough to balance the flavors.  The plate also came with dressed simple greens and fries (I went with garlic type offered by the waiter/bartender).

I also had an order of Carmelized Brussels Sprouts and Turnips on the side.  The sprouts were quartered and still large.  The turnips were pickled before hand and then roasted to bring out a sweet taste.  They were served as chunks.  The dish was topped with a ham hock vinaigrette with pieces of ham that were served close to a jerky texture, but easier to chew.  Great flavor all around!

The two bartenders were conversational and there were two other staff members (?) who asked how I was doing and what I had ordered.  Even on the way out, the folks at the front desk thanked me for coming in.  I hope it lasts, because I like feeling my patronage is appreciated.

Overall, I can't wait to return with a group for dinner to take advantage of the free evening/weekend parking behind the building.  Great start for a new restaurant.

Note:  The menu is on the pricey end for Mass Ave, but the food quality was great.  I didn't mind the prices.

Note 2:  For the grand opening, I was also given some promotional swag to help kickoff their Sunday Brunches that begin on Mother's Day.

Review #773

I wouldn't say the quest for the best sandwiches in St. Louis ends here, but it's one great place to start. Or like me, who is on the never ending quest, just added Adriana's on the rotating schedule of deli's that don't disappoint. This was only my second time here.

Seriously, I don't know what took me soooo long to find Adriana's, but damn I'm glad I did....shout out to the local Yelpers around these parts for sure...because it was really hard to decide on what to eat. Even thought they have the build your own option...you gotta stick with the trademark items on the menu...you know!?

Within this round, my kid's split the pepperoni pizza, and some garlic cheese bread. Yea, I stole a slice... wasn't bad. Really cheesy, I like that...I know for sure my kids liked it. One of the few times they ate all their food when we go out. My wallet was glad for that.

The wife had the Ben's Special half sandwich and half house salad. She's also half the reason why we came back to Adriana's. On our first visit me and her both had the Gorgonzola Dips. Hot Roast Beef with (of course) gorgonzola cheese, on garlic cheese bread (genius by anybody who does this) with a side of Au jus. Now this Italian beef of a sandwich is amazing on it's own, in fact I believe the hot roast beef varieties are what makes Adriana's a staple here in the Hill... But that first time we came, the kid's had the Ben's special and she took a few bites and was hooked on that cold sub. It's a good sandwich, but to her she just loved it. Hey Adriana's, what is in that special sauce!?

This time I got Nana's favorite and I upgraded the bread to the garlic cheese bread ( highly recommend for any hot sandwich you get).....because screw calories right!? It's loaded with hot roast beef, i think there was a sausage in there? Covered in marinara, and topped with provel. I can taste why it was Nana's......favorite. Side note, what I really like about the Adriana's is not just there signature Italian sands, but it's the fact that they won't skimp you on the product.  They're loaded, you're gonna leave with a full, happy belly. If you're wanting in on the lighter side, they accommodate for that too...at least what I've seen on the menu. 

One last thing to account for. I've only been here twice. There's a lot to still try, but the very first time I came here...the line was out the door  and I waited (reading yelp reviews, clues, and news), but when I got up to the register to take my order the owner was behind the register. She engaged me in small talk, complimented, made me feel like family. I felt comfortable, like I was a regular local there. That was awesome. Best part...a little over a month later. I come back and she remembers me...same thing. Same passion. I support this deli.

Was a privilege to try this specialty burger/shawarma joint. Got the Time Bomb burger and was thoroughly impressed with all the flavoring. The bacon and sauces on it were exquisite and so was the massive onion ring, delicious! Prices are pretty steep in the burgers but they do come with a good portion of fries with it. Fantastic burger and can't wait to try their other combinations.
Awesome chef here! The food is so fluffy and tasty. They catered my friends wedding and it was delicious. The gravy and bacon were good.

Really great atmosphere at this place. Everything is neatly decorated and nicely presented. The cheese plate was great and full of flavor. Order from their mini ipads which is convenient. White whine I got was good.
Pretty good spot for some ice cream if you're in Clearwater beach. The signs for $3 shakes is what go me thru the door. The cookies and cream one was $4 but pretty good.
$2 for a small chicken wing? Lol. Didn't know what planet I was on. Barely any meat on the bone. The Caesar salad was almost better than the wings in terms of value.
Some of the best gyros in St. Louis right here! Great pricing and fast service. The gyros come jam packed with toppings and delicious gyro meat. They're doing all the right things here!
One of the more happening spots in St. Louis that stays busy! Love all their different choices of teas and specialty boba drinks. Tried the oolong boba milk tea and it was great!
Mediterranean food that melts your mouth not your pocket. The beef shawarma is amazing here. The food is fast and the sauce is delicious.
