Delicious cannelloni here! Loved the flavoring and sauce. They have a rather wide menu so you'll probably find something you like. The small Caesar salad was a little on the high end price wise tho lol.
Didn't blow me away but still pretty good. Got the yellow chicken curry. Their really wasn't any spice in it almost tasted like a beef stew American style lol. Prices don't match the taste.
Really enjoyed the food from here! Their toasted raviolis are a good deal and tasty. Their salad with Italian dressing is great too!

This place alright. The tea was pretty good but wasn't the best. I think their food is priced a bit high too felt the menu was unwelcoming. Other than that it was a nice atmosphere inside, nice decor.

A St. Louis staple in the bbq community. Always delicious and with 6 bbq sauces to choose from you can't go wrong. The pulled pork is epic. One thing is the beans are not my fav wish they had Mac n cheese.

Delicious Mexican food here! Loved their chips and salsa. Prices are great! They also have a happy hour during the week afternoon. Really loved the tacos here each one stood out differently. The chicken one was excellent. Highly recommend this place great service as well!

Finally tried the famous Gus's chicken and it was quite tasty! Call in way ahead of time if your worried about the wait. Really like the baked beans here. May get a side of ranch for the chicken next time, delicious pieces.
So delicious you can't go wrong here. The sandwich just melts in your mouth. The bread and cheese is so fresh and tasty. Get a loaded if you're hungry.
Quaint little sushi spot off Gravois. They have nice lunch specials and their sushi is pretty good. The service was nice they even brought out a little pinnacle slice at the end which was nice.

This place surprised me in a great way! The food and creations are rad here! Love the tortilla strips that came with the southwest chicken wrap. The fries here are really good and plentiful as well. They also have a bunch of unique sauces, jellies, seasoning and more available for sale here as well.
Alright spot for some pho. Could use a lot of work cosmetically on the inside and outside. The beef combo pho was pretty good. Egg rolls on point too.

The pulled pork was oh so tender! Love how they recommend it with a tortilla such a great twist. Their bbq sauces are great here. Their to go station is confusing tho and needs some work don't know why they would transport the food all the way on the opposite side of the building when they could just crank it out from the massive front counter. Weird sYstem anyway food was amazing!

Delicious new Portuguese spot in Indy! Got the all for one platter and the chicken is just so amazing here since they prep it for 24 hours pulled the bone right out! Get ranch it's so good to dip the chicken in it. They were out of the cassava fries maybe next time!

Authentic Thai food in the grove! Got the Pad Thai lunch special and it was pretty good along with the portions. Will have to try something else here if you have any recommendations let me know @hybrideater
5 star burgers was pretty good. Got the Gorgonzola bacon burger. Cheese was really good, could've used more bacon. Burger meat falls apart in your mouth. What's your favorite burger here?!

Pretty weird exp. I wanted to try the Tonkotsu ramen but was told I shouldn't get it? Lol... that I wouldn't like it and I should get the other ramen. I was kind of thrown off by the situation but tried to enjoy the meal nonetheless. The crispy roll was pretty good. Wish they had a happy hour here their sushi kind of pricey.
Delicious Indian with tons of choices. The chicken 65 is really good. It has all the spicy. Really great flavors here.
Nice stop for a burger. Employees were great. Menu was kind of awkward. Burgers were decent. The tots were great.
Alright spot for some bar food. Their steak and cheese was good. The chicken wings were really dry. Beer cheese for the win.

Nice spot for some Greek food in south city. They have a really wide menu with a lot of different Greek and Italian dishes to choose from. The lamb was really nice and tender. Salad was great. Outside patio.
That's a DAM good burger. That's also some damn good sauce. Get the Belgian one for the fries. The dam burger was incredible take me back.

This place is amazing and screams foodie! The brunch menu is great and has something for everyone. Their coffee and tiramisu donut are a great combo together. The nduja French toast was a great surprise and was packed with flavor. This place is connected with Pastaria, hence the delicious food!
Nice stop inside union station. They have a nice outdoor patio to soak in the views. The cheeseburger was pretty good here. $18 shake was pretty extreme but made for some great photos.

All aboard everyone enter the sushi station! Love this place. The trio roll was epic and very filling. Get an order or spring rolls as an appetizer, comes with a pleasing sauce. Fast and accurate takeout.

Foodie alert! This is the place to go to eat some amazing food and unique kitchen creations. Got the chicken club and loved the avocado and sauce that was on it. Their fries with a side of ranch are great here.
A little pricey but the food is very good. I got the veggie hot dog with peppers. Staff very friendly kind of a long wait because staff was short.

I've been here a handful of times and been trying new things each time. I recently had the salmon cheesesteak with mayo and cheese with this Thai chili sauce. It was hella bomb! The area where the place is cute. The staff was very hospitable.

GREAT FOOD & SERVICE ! My wife and I were in New Orleans not long ago for a music festival. We were told about this cafe by the guys at Envie Espresso Bar & Cafe in Decatur St.....it's a sister business. We rolled up about 10am and the joint was packed to the rafters but hey no prob.....the girl at the door gets your cell phone # and they text you the second your table is available. We waited maybe 7 or 8 minutes wandering around the shops nearby. In fact we found a terrific children's clothing store called Nola Kids we went back to after breakfast and bought a couple of beautiful dresses for our 3 year old grand daughter. Service was quick and the food was super good. I ordered the Crawfish Omelette and my wife kept it simple with the breakfast sandwich. My fresh Orange Juice was pretty good too. Great atmosphere and real friendly service from servers Tina & Dominique made it even more enjoyable. This is the place to enjoy a great breakfast almost anyway you want it....and relax !

YEAH BABY ! After leaving Pacific Grove at 10.30am on Thursday morning we had driven over 300 miles to Santa Barbara. It was after 6pm and we had just departed the Tesla Supercharger in Goleta...and we were starving. My wife found this empanada place online while our Tesla was charging and it read well. We decided to grab take-out and then check in at our Casita at The Eagle Inn. I phoned ahead to place an order with Adam for 2 x Empanadas - Pollo ( Mary's chicken, onions & bell peppers ) & Serrano ( Prosciutto ham, mozzarella, garlic  & wild arugula ) for my wife and 1 x 3 Empanadas Combo - Carne (  Sunfed ranch grass-fed ground beef, onions, bell peppers, green olives & free-range hard boiled egg ) - Caprese ( Organic roma tomatoes, fresh mozzarella, basil, & extra virgin olive oil ) - Hongas ( Crimini mushrooms, organic spinach, caramelized red onions & mozzarella ) + Side of Choice - Chimi Papas ( Chimichurri oven roasted potatoes topped with housemate aioli ) for me. We pulled into their tight parking lot just before 6.30pm and I walked inside ( wearing my facial mask ) to collect our take-out order. A young dude ( wearing a facial mask ) behind the counter looked after me and checked our phone order before going to retrieve it. All packed up in a couple of cardboard boxes...I paid and we headed to our hotel. Finally in our hotel suite about 7pm we settled down to watch the baseball world series and enjoy our dinner. Trust me these delicious gourmet empanadas are the real deal...top quality ingredients and fresh as a daisy. We loved 'em !

A vegan deli right smack in the middle of the Reading Market!  Amazing! They are serving deli style cuisine over the counter. I sampled their vegan tuna salad and the corned beef. Both are spot on and tasty. In particular their vegan corned beef is awesome.  The spice profile is spot on as well as color and texture. They have all the sides to go with your sandwich too and all vegan as well.  They sell their "meats" and "cheeses" by the pound too. I had the vegan reuben and it was delicious. It reads exactly like a ruben. Only a handful of vegan restaurants are truly adept at a vegan ruben, Luhv is one of them.  Highly recommend.

One word. Chilaquiles. Review over.
...
No but really, the menu at Jacks Cafe is really awesome and I love finding options like this, so when I saw it on the "At the Border" section I was pretty excited. Also something notable from that section was the "Rio Grande" which is cheese enchiladas with sausage and also sounds amazing. I couldn't decide so I asked the waitress who told me the Chilaquiles were hard to beat.

Now back to those Chilaquiles...tortilla chips cooked in their salsa, topped in cheese with eggs and crispy potatoes. Some of the chips have crispiness still from the baked on cheese while others are soft and smothered in a super flavorful salsa. The eggs are on the side which when I make Chilaquiles at home I usually scramble the eggs into the chips...therefore I want to try this again, but with scrambled eggs and mix it all together with the chips. Still, it was really good.

Finally, per Michael T's recommendation, we tried the "scones". I was expecting an English style scone, but was surprised with delicious deep fried dough drizzled In honey and smothered in butter! It reminds me of the "donuts" my mother made us growing up. She would fry biscuit dough with a hole cut in the middle, then cover it in powdered sugar and gave them to us as donuts. These tasted like that. And they're super delicious!

The food was great and the service was great too, can't wait to go back and try that Rio Grande.

El Paisano just opened up next to Costco which is right by where I live... I shop at Costco and every time I pass it I say to myself... "I've got to eat there!"
Today the perfect time arose. My friend Sara came over and we were hanging out when she said, "Have you tried that new place yet?" Neither of us have, yet we both have wanted to! Off we went down the street to get our lunch.
I realized for the first time it was El Salvadorian food and they had Papusas!! I was on a quest for Carne Asada tacos though, I'll have to get those next time!
I ordered 8 tacos, at 1.25 each and some horchata... Enough for myself, my husband and our four year old who eats two whole tacos to himself! The salsa bar had more than just the usual, this one has Papusa sauce and the coleslaw like condiment that goes with them too... That stuff is amazing. I really can't wait to go back and try those!!
Our food arrived fast and soon enough we were back home eating...Wow... The meat is in huge chunks and flavorful and the condiments were a good accompaniment. I enjoyed them more than most of the places in town.

GURLLLLLL!!!! Wig snatched!!! 
I can't even believe how good this Pizza is!! 
But before ya girl gets too excited, let me break it down for ya...
It's getting close to midnight...
I had a VERY long night driving down from Tahoe in a chained up Prius during a snow storm after the Super Bowl. Chains I couldn't get off, left me stranded at home once I finally got there. And food was literally all I could think about. 
Late night munchies, you win...

Time for delivery!

First, I jumped on to Pizzava's website where I received a 20% off coupon for my first order with them! Next, I switched on over to Yelp to check out reviews, pictures, and to see what everyone was diggin' on. The steak bomb and the Alfredo's seem to be a hit, so I chose a small Alfredo Penne pizza and added garlic! It had penne pasta, Alfredo sauce, chicken, mushrooms, mozzarella cheese and of course my garlic! 
Since I had 20% off I decided to treat myself to a dessert. Cinnamon balls with sweet icing it was, and it was time for the waiting game. 

Estimated delivery time had them arriving around 12:30/12:40am...but they had it done MUCH faster. Soon the little truck on the website was in route and my order was here by 12:10, much faster than estimated. 

The pizza was garlicy, cheesy...the penne was cooked well and the sauce was creamy and decadent. The corn meal crust added that familiar pizza crust texture I love and the actual crust was crispy and cooked perfectly. 

The Cinnamon balls were crunchy on the outside and soft and pillowy on the inside with a thin crunch of sugar and cinnamon on top. Perfectly oven baked, drizzled in EVOO and topped with cinnamon powder. Served with a cup of white icing, these were AMAZING all hot and fresh. Like seriously... I need these in my life every time I've had a hard day!

All in all I'd say Pizzava is one of my new late night favs and honestly I'm super excited to order again.

I wanted to love this place. I saw the menu and couldn't help but jump for joy at the idea of a Poke restaurant I could get a poke bowl at, while still being able to order something like chicken teriyaki for my son whose six. And while he does love tempura shrimp and crab, sometimes he'll simply eat more chicken, than fish.

Therefore tonight, a good friend whose wife doesn't particularly like Poke bowls, ventured out with Taven (my son) and I to Finbomb. The menu seemed to be a fusion restaurant where East meets West. Southwestern and Philly cheesesteak on their menu being prime examples.

We walked in to one guy, who seemed new, and three girls working. One brunette girl in front, one blonde girl on the register and one brunette girl in the back.

We went through and ordered our bowls. Upon reaching the register the blonde girl asked if we wanted bags. I told her we wanted to eat in... it was 7:45 after all..."Oh, we close at 8." She said as she looked at Taven. Meaning we couldn't eat there...

...Mind you there were four people sat eating already...

...I told my friend the bad news and we couldn't believe that we were being turned away. If the doors are open so you can order, the restaurant dining room should be open so you can eat. 

But what really upset me is just as we were paying, a single woman behind us ordered a burrito and was asked by the employees..."For here or to go" !?!? Are you kidding me!? After telling us we couldn't eat in, with people already sat eating and you ask the girl behind us, for here or to go!? Really!!??

I've never felt worse about being in an establishment before in my life and quite honestly I know the reason. They're teenagers who didn't want to deal with what they were probably assuming to be a "messy kid." Little did they know my six-year-old is a brilliant well behaved child who eats fricking poke bowls for heavens sake!

No worries. Next time we'll just go to...literally any other poke restaurant in town...which is so unfortunate because these poke bowls were good!! Yet the blatant disregard for customers service was extremely off-putting.

Since we were with my friend we had no where to eat our bowls. Thankfully he was nice enough to invite us back to his house to eat. Still, we should have been permitted to eat in. They were just too lazy to want to clean after us.

The truth is the food here is pretty good and I used to stop in fairly frequently. The problem is that the regulars that line the backside of the bar on the bar side of the restaurant are intolerable. On 9/22/16 I had to endure a litany of racist comments from these trogs as I tried to enjoy my salad and beer. I'm talking bold, outright racist and sexist comments that may well have come out if George Wallace's mouth back in the 60's. 

Not a single staff member asked them to leave, stop making the comments, or even to pipe down. I had to get out of there, which is what I told the bartender. She nodded and spoke quietly that she understood while they continued their rant. Then one of these dimwits gleefully offered his sarcastic goodbye to me when I left because he knew exactly why I was leaving. Still nary a comment from any staff member. 

It was THE worst dining/bar experience I've ever had in my life, and I'm not the youngest guy in the world. 

So, I'd avoid this place like the plague until they decide to stand up to their racist clientele and create an atmosphere worthy of a public place

I'm here on business and was told by the concierge at Harrahs this was the best restaurant within a block or two. Great! I called at 8:50 to place an order. I could hear the person who picked up the phone say with disdain to maybe someone who was her supervisor, "Can you hold for a minute? Hey, this guy wants to place an order for takeout." I hear them discuss for a moment. Then she gets back on the phone and says, "Our kitchen has closed." The restaurant's posted hours of operation are until 10 pm. It's not like I was calling at 9:55. It was 8:50. I don't get it. The restaurant business is a tough business. I want to give this place money, probably a $100 order for our party, and they don't want to take it. So we called another restaurant down the street and they happily took our order. I will report this back to the concierge at Harrahs. Would love to review your food, but your customer service needs a little work first. Good 

Response from the owner in a message:

"So that's why you stay at a shit hole like harrahs bc your so good friends w gary. You didn't even spell him name right freak show. Your a fucking joke. Could care less what you do. Fuck off."

Stay away from this place and its hate-speech mongering owner. Other reviews here will tell you the same experience of him sending you messages askIng you to revise your review, and when you don't, he'll send you a profanity-laden messages such as the one above.

If you are planning on a day at the beaches in Tampa then you should do yourself a favor and make a reservation at Guppy's for one of your meals.  Guppy's runs a tight ship with professional service and good food. Pricing is reasonable with most dishes running $20 to $25.  There is ample free parking in an adjacent lot.

We came here for an early dinner after a day at the public beach across the road, all of us eager to sample some fresh seafood.  For starters we tried the Fried Green Tomatoes with Feta Cheese. http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/guppys-on-the-beach-indian-rocks-beach-3?select=_DMBR6ZpLHcYUqwh-_-fAw#a-1fJdf_9y7OZHoMhkz6FA  These were very tasty and were a hit with my party, the tangy sauce also went great with the bread.  Fresh, locally caught grouper is offered on the menu, seasonally priced. http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/guppys-on-the-beach-indian-rocks-beach-3?select=_DMBR6ZpLHcYUqwh-_-fAw#bfz8SyqvVmvzt-7pJOl0Tw We had to try the local special but sadly ours was on the overcooked side and was a bit tough.  The Shrimp Grits were loaded with flavor and had great consistency, highly recommended.  http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/guppys-on-the-beach-indian-rocks-beach-3?select=_DMBR6ZpLHcYUqwh-_-fAw#TiLYzNi299qpAO21i4YKZw Lastly, we also tried Guppy's Seafood Bowl which featured clams, calamari, Shrimp, Scallops, & Mussels in a Saffron Broth http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/guppys-on-the-beach-indian-rocks-beach-3?select=_DMBR6ZpLHcYUqwh-_-fAw#_DMBR6ZpLHcYUqwh-_-fAw  This was also a favorite with my party.  

Despite the name the restaurant is not actually "on the beach" but are situated on the other side of the road.  If you came here expecting ocean-front dining you might well be disappointed, but it's close enough that you can go for a walk before and/or after your meal :o)

$17 for lunch. SEVENTEEN. I just got a meal, sub veggie patty, sub smoothie. It's mad expensive. The wraps are good, but tiny. Especially for just spending $17. 
The staff is super untrained and there never seems to be a management figure present. It's just confused looking kids eerrrrrwhere. 
Everything tastes good and I come here often by default since lack of anywhere else to eat around here that isn't from the La Boulange case or Wendy's. And it drives me nuts, NUTS I tell you, that they don't give you napkins unless you ask. "Here's your box of food, and oh! you're in luck since your car seats are upholstered." I get trying to save the planet and all, but it's just weird. Food = napkins. 

Avoid the drive-through at all costs. At the order speaker the girl repeated my meal to me twice. At the window 3 times. Tennessee Blue sub veggie. I also watched my smoothie that got made immediately, sit in their sunny window sill for 15 minutes before my car made it up there to receive. I was hoping that wasn't my smoothie I saw chillen there all that time. It was. Needless to say it was warm and not very smoothie like. After nearly 30 minutes in that drive through line, what did I get? Some asian chicken salad. If it wasn't for the fact that I'm vegetarian I would have sucked it up and ate it anyway.  But I can't so turned back around back through the ENTIRE drive thru. Got my ordered repeated back to me again three or four more times. 17 minutes later got my box and it was still wrong but vegetarian none the less, so I ate it and drove like lightning back to work. Scarfing it down on the way since now I wasted my while lunch break. Thank god I remembered to ask for napkins this time. 

Time and time again I've been handed my goods through that slow-as-shit-drive thru being said nothing to. NOTHING. Window opens, hand card, card comes back, box is handed to me, blank stare. I just drive off anymore. I use to say. "Ok thanks!? Bye?!" But then they get even more confused. So if you want the awkwardness. I'll give it right back to ya girlfriend because I'll be queen bee of awkward silences ALL DAY. 

Looks like they only have 18 year old girls hired who can rock wear booty shorts. Whatever will they do in the winter? So I understand why everything is a mess. I always see at least two of them on their cell phones. Ugh.

The smoothies have begun sucking now too. For spending $6, my shit better not taste like frozen Dole brand ice. But it does. And I saw them refilling the "PB2" which in fact, was not PB2, just some weird generic peanut powder. No thanks.

So I try them for breakfast. They have four breakfast sandwiches. I order one. Wait. Wait. Wait again. Ditzy girl comes to the window and says they are out of the "sandwich."
 "So do I pick another one?" 
"Uh, let me check." Two minutes later... "They said they can put it in a box for you." 
"What are you talking about, girlfriend?" Is what I should have said. I had no idea what she was trying to articulate to me and neither did she. After I asked six more questions, I was able to diagnose they were just out of muffins and they wanted to make the sandwich into a scramble. After I kindly declined, two more people, and by people I mean teenie boppers, came to refund my card without saying one word to me. Not hi, not bye, not sorry.

"Like, oohh emm geee, Teresa's is like the best"-said no one in this group of friends, ever. 

Leveling with with haters that are about to hate on my review, I've been here FOUR times. FOUR. 1-2-3-4 and yes, still hate it. And it's not one thing I hate. It's all things we hate. Both sides, same side it doesn't matter, it's overpriced crap. 

So for starters let's get this straight: Because most of you weren't born with supernatural ESP thought processing, I'll save you the dirty looks of confusion you'll receive when you ask what the difference is between the two Theresa's that sit side by side. The "cafe" is "Italian" and "Next Door" is "Belgium."  Both of which are sorry excuses for the concepts they claim to mimic. 

Both parts share the kitchen, hostess stand, bar menu and dessert menu, managers etc. - but not dinner menu. Then what's the effing point? 

One particular night we we called to see what the wait was currently. The always-brain-dead hostesses told us there was one table open and they were not on a wait yet. 9 minutes later we walked in the door and both sides were on a wait over a hour and no one working this stressful host stand could tell me why we were just told false information. 

Service is always slow as hell. It's such a long process. 10 minutes before the server comes over to greet you, 15 minutes to get a drink from the bar, 15 minutes to find the server to put in an appetizer, another 9 months before you can find him and tell him your starving and you'd like to put a dinner order in and wait an hour for it. The water bottle they give you never gets refilled and 50 percent of the time we've gotten the server that looks like he doesn't own a bathroom and just toked up in the back. 

And God for bid if you're not a beer snob! You are beneath them. If you don't order any alcohol, you can kiss your attention goodbye. The best is seeing your server judge you for being young, thinking she won't get much of a tip from you and attends better to the older crowd in her section. Right on. 

The french fries are good and that's about all I can say on a positive note. Fries. That's my one star. 

I could go on and on for days, but I will leave you with this. My husband went to one of the top culinary schools in the world and we have lived all over the country. If you think this is good food and this place is the bomb dot com, I feel very sorry for you for you have not lived.

Never again! My family has been getting cakes from there for years. Always great! This time my mom got a cake for the nurses who took awesome care of her during her cancer treatment. Unfortunately this cake had ants in it! When she took it back, she was treated like she put the ants in it! Ripping the cake apart all over the place, icing and cake was flying all over. Then she disgustingly threw the cake in the trash! How can you run a business like that? Things happen,but according to that woman, it's the customer's fault! She did not apologize or was the least bit understanding, she was a total Bitch! That bakery will continue to loose good customers as long as that miserable woman is there!!!!!
I wish I could give no stars

A THAI PLACE IN HARAHAN?!?! YEP, I'M THERE!!

Got my taste buds going y'all! It's a little tucked away from the main Elmwood crowd so you may have missed this gem. Service was phenomenal, fast and friendly and the restaurant was very clean. Great lunch spot!  I came in right at lunch time on a weekend and it wasn't overly crowded.  Good for friends meeting up, couples enjoying a quick lunch before heading out to Elmwood or even bringing your kids for a meal. Food is your general thai food with specialty drinks as well!

I want to eat here every night but unfortunately I'm not ok with rolling out. You 100% will not be disappointed with your selection here. I never felt more like family than in my own Nanan's kitchen. The amount of food that will appear on your plate is a sin it's so much, so come starving! I ate some delicious chicken Parmesan topped with cheese and Alfredo sauce and a side salad which is no "side" salad. You could eat just the salad it's so big and full of salami, cheese, olives and artichokes with the house dressing! My husband had the homemade Italian sausage. He said it was awesome, authentic and super flavorful especially with the side of marinara that they give you. 

My mouth is watering writing this review so I'm almost positive I'll be eating here again soon. I went with my parents and husband, but this is good for a cute little date night in river town as well. I don't recommend for a hug party only because the place is tiny and quaint. 

The staff could not have been more helpful and inviting! I was so stuffed I almost said no to dessert but then the waitress told me about the gelato and cannoli's and don't think I turned my hand away to that... Both were mouth watering good! Gendusa's for the win!!! :)

The worst restaurant I have ever been to. I came here and waited for at least 30 minutes. No waiter came out. The waitress told me that they were busy and I understand that. The tablewares were not clean at all so I tried to grab a new one by myself. When I was grabbing the tablewares, the waitress rudely asked me:" What are you doing?" I was like okay if you don't provide the services why I cannot provide the services by myself???"

By the end I decided to offer only 10% tips due to their poor services. However, the waitress asked me to give them at least 15% tips in order to show RESPECT. I refused her and she asked me to leave and said:" DON'T COME TO MY RESTAURANT AGAIN and I DON'T WANT TO SEE YOU AGAIN."

I replied her:" Yeah I'm not gonna come again." and left the restaurant. She asked me to stop, POINTED A FINGER TO ME, and YELLED:" You are such a A**HOLE. This is my place and I'm gonna call the police and ask you to get out of here." My friends tried to stop her but she was really pissed off.

Honestly I really don't think I did anything wrong. People pay tips to these servers whose services are worth to be rewarded. If you don't provide soundable services, why I should pay you at least 15% tips? Instead of showing gratitude of receiving tips, this waitress shows insanely crazy and awful attitude to her customers. If you don't show basic RESPECT to YOUR CUSTOMERS, what's the point of receiving RESPECT from them???

There are two items that will keep me coming back to Termini Bros Bakery at Reading Terminal Market in Philadelphia, PA.  

Their Cannolis are DELICIOUS!!!!  Perfect balance of yummy Ricotta filling in a fresh crispy shell!!  Best I've had outside of Boston!
 
Their Pecan Diamond is so Sinfully Fantastic!!  This bar shaped treat is packed with yummyness, and it is worth every single calorie!!

Termini Bros is absolutely one of my "Must Visit" destinations at Reading Terminal Market.  They should be yours as well!

How many times can a person fascinated by world cuisine pass a new African restaurant before they are compelled to eat there? Apparently, 4. Queen Sheba is a lovely new Eritrean place in a strip mall that I've driven by a million times and never noticed before this place opened. It's a small space but there is also outdoor seating. 

The server asked about our experience with African food and told us that Eritrean cuisine was "the same thing as Ethiopian" and also that it was her first day ever working as a server. 

I don't think the menu is quite as extensive as Zemam's or Cafe Desta about there is plenty to choose from including vegan dishes (the cottage cheese that typically comes with spinach in this cuisine is opt in so you have to ask for it) and both meat and vegetable dishes with different levels of spice. We ordered the spinach (with cheese), the shero (chick peas), and the spicy beef. We mentioned that many Ethiopian restaurants will offer samplers where you can get smaller portions of more foods, and the server said they could do something like that, although it's not on the menu.

Unfortunately, the cook couldn't read her handwriting. They gave us some little portions of most (all?) the menu items, and larger portions of some things, but not exactly the things we ordered. There was a spicy beef that was excellent and another beef dish that didn't have as much flavor. We only got dabs of the chick peas and the spinach and no cheese. When we pointed this out, they brought us more chick peas (tasty) and also the cheese but we only had about two bites each of the spinach, and the spinach was excellent. It felt more fresh and less stewed than other times I've had this dish.

The chicken, of which we also had a small taste, was similarly good, with a little spice. Lentils were decent: they're not my favorite. We also tried a potato dish (sort of sweet) and another vegetable that might have been cabbage. I'm probably forgetting something. Halfway through the meal they brought us a crisp green salad. I should mention that the injera (which the menu calls "spongy") is really fluffy. Like, pillowy! Very good. They offered more injera but we couldn't finish what we ordered. We had enough for three people at least.

In the end, we folded the leftovers up like a burrito, settled the takeaway box on top of it, and flipped the plate over so we could take the rest home.

Prices are reasonable and it looks like this restaurant is finding its way. I recommend checking it out soon, as it's probably going to start getting crowded, being the only east African place on this side of town.

Wow, what a change! If you're used to the crappy, uncomfortable, broken seats at El Con, the uncouth kids running around the lobby, the weird homeless guy always trying to bring his dogs inside, and the horrible, artificial nacho cheese, take heart. There is another way. Going to the movies can be classy and comfortable. 

At the Roadhouse, you'll sit in a padded seat that reclines, with a footrest that you raise or lower with the touch of a button. Touch another button and the waitresses will bring you beer. The nachos are made with real cheese. Granted, they are a bit hard to eat in the dark, and I'm not sure how they keep the seats clean, because I dropped a whole bunch of nachos into them, but it's such a pleasant atmosphere, I'm sure they've figured that all out. You can eat a real meal in the theater on a swing-out tray--burgers, salads, and such--and there are plenty of napkins. It's a rustic, but still modern, atmosphere with incredibly friendly employees who seem legitimately happy to ensure that you enjoy your experience. There's a bar, and a patio, and the overall feelings is that of a nice restaurant.

The screen is big, every seat is a good one, and the sound system is fabulous. If that's not enough of a draw, kids under six are NOT ALLOWED INSIDE. You read that right. A movie theater that understands why infants do not belong in movie theaters. You have to actually be old enough to watch a movie to come into this theater. People who are likely to throw temper tantrums or start screaming during the fight scenes are unwelcome.

All theaters should be the Roadhouse.

I've been to the Melting Pot many times since they opened. I have had mostly all great experiences, tonight was a great time! My Mom booked dinner for my birthday, and I suggested there as being a member of their club fondue they emailed me s coupon for 6 free chocolate covered strawberries. The club is free to sign up & you find out about upcoming events ahead of time, great reminder if you aren't on social media to see their info always. 

My Favorite fondue to start is the classic cheddar. For an entree I always skip the salad, so then there's more room for your entree & of course chocolate fondue :)

As a vegetarian I am not the best a recommending an entree for you, but you have many choices from land & sea!

For your dessert chocolate, there are about 7 to choice from. 1 always changes for the feature of the month. Cool thing about the feature is that $1 from everyone sold, goes to the charity of the month Melting Pot has chosen. 

Personally I recommend the smore's fondue, but add peanut butter. You're welcome.

DO NOT ORDER mushroom ramen. 
Embarrassingly disgusting. I'm Japanese, and worst ramen I ever put in my mouth. I really don't want American people to think shio ramen is tasted like that. I wanted to send it back and get tonkotsu, but tried to be nice Asian there. I tried to finish ramen because I'm polite like that. I have been finish eating ramen since I was 6 years old, first time in my life, I just couldn't. 
Tonkotsu broth was good.
Service were amazing! That's why I gave 2 stars. 
I rather go to Ichicoro or Dusunco. 

I was waiting for this place to open but I knew its American owner, didn't have high expectation. 
I'm disappointed. 
I'm sure people who doesn't know ramen think it's great. 

マッシュルームラーメンは絶対にオーダーしないでください。フルーツでも入ってる？！ってくらい甘ったるく、味の深さがないです。その中にナメコ椎茸などは入っています。豚骨はまぁまぁでした。
個人的にイチコロやドサンコの方が全然美味しいです。
麺は弾力があり美味しいですが、一番大事なスープが。。。サービスはすごく良いのに残念です。

One of my favorite meals of the day is hands down breakfast! I have tried nearly every breakfast place in Reno. Without a doubt Peg's continues to be the one place that I always return to. When you walk into this Peg's, you will immediately feel like you are at hometown diner. Local art on the walls, homemade cookies for sale, and the best service that you can find anywhere in Reno. 

My favorite thing to get here is the Sierra Omelette. This omelette has been the source of many heated debates among co-workers and friends. It is an egg omelette that is filled with chicken and chilies. Most people have this crazy idea that this meal is immoral. Eating the chicken (mother) and the baby (egg) all at once. This debate normal ends soon as the person gives this amazing breakfast a try. The skillet not only comes with an Omelette but also hash-browns, pico, coleslaw, and beans. 

If you are looking for the best breakfast in Reno, where you never leave hungry than this is the place for you. If you ask anybody where they would recommend for breakfast I can almost guarantee over half will suggest Peg's Glorified Ham and Eggs. Price, Service, and Food are always on point, there is no way that you could go wrong choosing here for your next big breakfast. 

SIDE NOTE:  GREAT FOR HANGOVERS!!!!!

If you are burnt-out on the burger options around Reno than this is the place for you. Burger Me offers a variety of burgers that I have not seen anywhere else. I have tried many different burgers here and have not once been disappointed. 

One of the most unique and biggest selling point for this place is the fact that all of their beef is hormone and antibiotic free. They pride themselves on using meats that come from local and humane sources like Reno Provisions and Sierra Meats. I know that a lot of people wouldn't care where their meats come from but I for one feel much better about eating this type of food. 

I strongly recommend giving the Italian Stallion a try! Probably one of the best burgers I have ever eaten. I also really enjoy trying whatever their special stuffed burger is for that day. Bison burger is another popular choice. If you are feeling adventurist and want to go all out, try the Dirty Bird, it has chili and a fried egg. I was skeptical about it but have absolutely no regret. Burger Me also offers a variety of french fries that are unmatched anywhere else: regular, onion rings, garlic, and sweet potato.

The atmosphere in here is spot on. It is very clean and welcoming. They have booths, tall tables, smaller tables and outdoor patio seating. There is even a flat screen TV hanging up so that you wont miss your favorite games. Have kids? they have that covered too with their arcade games and ice-cream. For the adults they have a really nice selection of beers, both local and domestic.

The employees here are have all been exceptional. Customer service and friendliness of the staff will guarantee to exceed your burger joint expectations. Joe is always a pleasure to talk to and he does such a great job to make sure everybody has 5 star experience.

Side note: They have a food truck that can always be found at Food Truck Friday down at Idlewild Park. It's almost guaranteed to have one of the biggest lines and there is good reason why.

First time here.

This is one of those reviews when I really wish yelp had category breakdowns for the ratings.

I found this place by accident a few days ago, but I also remembered that a friend of mine told me about it and he said it was a "nice" place.... O.K.

At about 4:30 PM I had to wait 20 minutes for a car to leave before I could park in Sam's Beach Bar's parking lot. Not that they were SO busy, their lot only has space for 17 vehicles (I checked Google Earth).
I went to the bar and after being ignored by both sweaty, greasy-faced, kid-bartenders, I asked for a drink menu. I don't drink very often and some suggestions would have been helpful, no such thing. I got a Rum Runner with Cruzan.

As I wandered around I thought this COULD be a really cool place. It's right on the Gulf, has a nice view (for Hudson) and it seems to be far enough South to be just leaving the Hernando-Pasco redneck-country. The evening I was there the crowd was about 80% senior citizens.  They had Jimmy Buffett and some other typical island tunes on the speakers, and that's what I want at an outdoor beach bar right on the ocean.

I saw a customer with a fish sandwich, I asked the first Sam's Beach Bar employee I saw "What is she eating over there?", and rather than trying to help me, the customer, she told me to ask a server as apparently she had some other function. Nice.

I found out it was the grouper, so I found a table and waited to be waited on.
I sat there FOR 10 MINUTES- AND DURING THAT TIME NO FEWER THAN 5 Sam's Beach Bar SERVERS looked right at me and continued on their way without asking if they could help, get me a menu, refill my drink, ANYTHING!
Finally I got up and started looking for the manager. When I explained I had been ignored for 10 minutes he essentially blew it off as "a mistake" and "no big deal".
After 5 MORE minutes one of the servers who had looked at me without helping came over to take my order, all phony smiles and peppiness. 
The food arrived after about 20 minutes and it LOOKED great! I took a couple photos right away and dug in. The Grouper was kind of tasteless, I squeezed on some lemon and added tartar sauce- didn't help. As I got into the middle of the fish (a large piece of fish) I noticed it was very dry. I didn't even eat it all. And this was a $17.95 sammich! The fries were starch coated, covered with starch-slurry blisters- not good.

As I said at the top, I wish yelp had 3 categories for each restaurant:
1) Food
2) Service
3) Atmosphere/Cool Factor

The food at Sam's Beach Bar was not very good, especially for the high price- 2 stars.
The service was terrible/to non-existent- 1 star.
The atmosphere/view/vibe- 4 stars. But, this can't make up for the bad service and mediocre food.

Walked over from the river walk for breakfast on Sunday morning.  They open @7 nice.  Greeted when I walked in and since I was already in the mode for salmon I ordered the Noah.  The Noah in 2018 did not look like the previous pictures.  The dill cream cheese is very thin.  More the consistency of a thin spread.  First it needs more cream cheese and a thicker version.  The salmon was likely 2oz of thine slices but was fresh tasting.  Overall an OK meal.  If I am am ever back I would try the egg sandwich.

Great place for Italian food when at the international mall.  Sit on the patio and people watch.  Great food and great service.  Fresh coffee was brewed for us and you could tell.  We had the chicken lemon (piccata) and chicken Marcella.  Both were delicious as came with fresh grilled vegetables and mashed potatoes.  Wonderful lunch.

Came here for something different. The pictures of the country fried steak looked great and the grilled corn pictures sold me on the idea. However, the picture looks good but reality is a real let down. I've had better country fried steak at Chedder's, and the grill corn wasn't eatable. My fries were cold and the meal all together was only lukewarm. I'm sorry but if you wait for a meal then it should be hot. 
This place might be a great hangout for beer drinkers that want to listen to a live music venue, however in the hour that I was there the band never played a note. The second floor is a good place to have a drink and watch whatever sport game might be on  
It is a great use of the space and I hope the food improves and I may, after the bad taste it left in my mouth passes, give it a second chance to impress me. 
I hate writing bad reviews for local and new food venues.

If you have been wanting to go here and haven't made it yet, this is your sign to GO! This place is amazing and was such a lovely place to celebrate a birthday. We were sat promptly as we had a reservation and were greeted by our server with warm bread and water. She was very knowledgeable of both the food and wine menu and gave great recommendations! We ordered the fritto misto which offers a variety of fried options: shrimp, squid, zucchini, etc. I ordered the Nero as my main dish and it was probably one of the best pastas I have ever had. Italian food and I are one to disagree at times but not here. It's squid ink pasta (which they make all their pasta in house) with a lobster cream sauce and pieces of lobster and whole shrimp tossed together. The portions were huge and very filling. 

All of the seating inside is very spaced out and we essentially had our own little corner during our dining experience. Service is great, food is exceptional. It can be pricey depending on your order but you're paying for good food. I do believe they offer carry out options as well for those who are not dining in quite yet.

Great neighborhood feel, friendly folks behind the counter. Mr. Lee is the man. Fries are on point. My boyfriend loves the chicken cheesesteak with either broccoli or spinach with their homemade sauces. I'm a fan of the veggie cheesesteak. Make sure to try the Carrot Cake Man's carrot cake!

Sooooo excited that my absolute favorite food cart just opened up 10 min away from me! I just randomly stumbled upon opening day, having no idea that they were opening up a location here! It's super easy to get to, right off of Dekalb pike and in the same shopping center as Target so there is plenty of parking. 

You have your choice of a gyro or a platter. The sandwich is 6.99 with chicken or beef gyro meat. The platter comes in small and large, 7.99 and 8.99, and I think it's the much better deal. You can get sides of hummus, baba ghanouj, and fries. 

It's small inside. Think like a Subway. There are a couple tables inside, three counter seats and right now there are also three outside tables as well. 

Service is typically awesome and high energy on an opening day. And that was definitely the case today as well. Everyone was super nice. And the food is equally nice! Hope they won't mind seeing my face every week!

My first time trying Indian cuisine was at Shere-E-Punjab just a few weeks ago, and I had a great experience! The food was amazing and everything I'd hoped for with my first time trying Indian. I highly recommend the bindi masala to anyone that is vegan, vegetarian, or just a veggie lover in general! 

The service was also excellent. Our server explained every dish, answered all our questions, and gave great recommendations. Eating here was truly a treat, and I'm excited to go back and try more dishes!

After a stressful day, Daniel N. and I decided to wind down by having a nice date night dinner. Although we knew we probably couldn't get a reservation at such a late notice, Boucherie has been on our to-try list since my birthday. I called and was told that we could try to come early and grab a table outside or at the bar, so we left early & made it by 6 PM, early enough to even grab a parking spot directly across the street.

We were seated outside right by the heat lamp and immediately ordered cocktails, a Riverbend Martini for him and a caipirinha for me. Hendricks gin brought the martini to that next level, with a slight berry flavor levelled by cucumber, and my caiprinha was standard and not too sugary.

Before our drinks arrived we were brought an amuse of a Turnip Soup with Mahi Salad. The mahi was not overcooked, as is often the issue with whitefish. Rather, it was slightly chewy and had a good flavor that contrasted nicely with the creamy, smokey turnip veloute (Daniel tasted a strong hint of bacon which I didn't). 

Our server took our order after we had downed the amuse as shots. This is when our issues began.

We were seated outside on the porch, where there are only 4 tables. The other two were seated around the same time as us. After taking orders our servers placed utensils on our table but turned around and gave the napkins to the couple who were seated right across from us, who arrived perhaps 10-15 minutes after us. We made no mind of this at the moment, until our appetizer arrived and we still hadn't been given napkins. It wasn't until we had finished the appetizer and were looking for the server to specifically request napkins that they were brought, all while she had been conversing with the other tables and not checking in on us. 

Food: 

Small plate special: Arugula salad with grilled red onions, spicy pecans, satsuma pieces, satsuma vinaigrette, topped with grilled duck tenders - The leaves of arugula were huge and chopped! with an astringent flavor much more reminiscent to kale or chard than the usual baby arugula we're used to in restaurant salads. The duck was tender with a slight charred edge at the lean bits of skin. The real hit, though, was the smoky, spicy toasted pecans, which really connected the sweet and tart satsuma with the vegetal arugula and the savory duck. 

Smoked wagyu beef brisket with garlic parmesan fries - I don't eat brisket often, but when I saw wagyu in the menu description I expected that the fat marbleing would help keep the brisket moist, as with the Joint's barbecue brisket. Sadly this was not the case. The brisket was simply too dry, while the sauce was too thick and did a poor job of acting a wetting agent. The fries were handcut and crisp, there was far too much shaved parmesan and no taste of garlic at all. 

Applewood smoked scallops with garlicky broccoli, XO sauce, & Sesame Seed Tuille - I'm not sure which of the accoutrement was the sauce that topped the scallops; whichever it  was, it was completely delicious. The broccoli  was finished by roasting and so was slightly crisp, while the standout was the moist and delicate scallops, perfectly cooked bivalves that had some chew without being tough. Their natural sweetness was brought to the forefront by the various accompanying sauces. 

Let it be noted that we ordered drinks when we first sat down. We ordered our food, received our appetizer, finished it, and waited for our food without any acknowledgment from our server except when she took our salad plate, at which time she did notice my empty drink glass and asked if I wanted anything further. I asked to see the drink menu, but perhaps wasn't clear enough; when she brought me the cocktails menu and turned away quickly, I wasn't quick enough to ask for a wine menu. We waited for her to return, so I could ask for the wine list; yet could not catch her attention while she was stopping at the other 2 tables. 

All this time she was talking to the other tables about their food and drink choices, while barely asking us how things were when she dropped off our dishes. After giving us our entrees, when I was finally able to ask her for a wine list, I waited so I could enjoy my beef with a glass of wine. By the time she returned & I could order, Daniel had finished his dinner and was just waiting for me. We didn't even bother looking at the dessert menu.

For food, ambience, and price, I would otherwise have given this a 3.5 stars rounded up to 4 (a half star deducted because of the crowdedness and difficulty to get a table). Due to the service we received, I deducted a full star and then rounded down. 

Yes, we are young, and yes we are Asian. And yes, I believe this is the reason for our treatment. I've never felt so blatantly discriminated against in a restaurant.

I really want to like Boucherie and give them a higher rating but I am absolutely appalled at the service we received. There are better restaurants that appreciate our patronage.

This place is a waste for its prime location. No prices on cocktail or draft beers, cheesecake menu.. ok so should we all be pretentious and pay for things we don't know the prices of? 
Therefore I asked how much the PASSIONFRUIT mojito is, she said "I believe it's around $11"... 
im sorry... I believe? That could mean a lot of things. I don't want to order a drink and get a check of a cocktail for $14. If I wanted that I could go to Rumor. 
After I asked for the cocktail price.. the waitress gave me a disdained look and never came back! Didn't even look at my friend and I again. Ok so I guess she assumed that we were poor cuz we asked the price of a mojito. After literally 15  minutes of no service, no water (cricket).. we LEFT. So I don't do this a lot, reviewing without trying the food. But here it is! My first and last Cheesecake Factory visit.

So I wrote the tip that says to give it some time before they "fill out the menu". Well, they didn't. I noticed the smokehouse tavern added pizza.....isn't it a smokehouse? Identity crisis at its best. 

To the owners: Smokehouse tavern has absolutely no personality. From the unkempt staff, to the banquet hall style decor...and on top of that, Wawa has better pulled pork. I have never eaten in a restaurant that seems as confused as Smokehouse Tavern.

Service- Terrible. No personality, no uniformity, and please get rid of the white sneakers and jeans...it screams unprofessional.

Food- Dry, bland, frozen. I've had 2 dishes from the "smokehouse menu" and they were both very dry. 

Decor- TVs don't add personality. This place is about as boring looking as they come. 

Boy oh boy. I may give it a third try in a couple months. But for now, I'm going to Jessie's, or the Smoke Rack for smokehouse food.

Ugh, I hate to write bad reviews but I kinda feel I should speak up here. 

If you love BBQ and have ever enjoyed it below the Mason-Dixon line -- don't do Deke's. Just don't do it. Seriously. Spare yourself the disappointment. 

I've been to Deke's twice -- the first time I thought maybe it was an "off" night but now I'm pretty sure these guys just don't care.

The prices? OMG -- ridiculous. I cannot believe they charge what they charge for so little food. Real southern BBQ is served "family style" -- you can buy it by the pint like deli food. A pint of this, a pint of that... Sides, too. When you order a side here, you get a little single-serving size portion. Really, guys?? How are you supposed to share? BBQ is about big plates and good food. BBQ is not to be doled out in little styrofoam containers at five bucks a pop. 

Aside from that, the food is atrocious. I'm sorry, that's the only word I have for pulled pork practically floating in sauce. Now, I don't mind BBQ with some fat in it, but ours had, literally, STRIPS of wobbly fat that we had to pick out by hand. Like, our pound & a half container (that cost like $25 by the way!) had by conservative estimate a tennis ball's worth of fat blobs.

 My first mouthful, I felt the squishy-squish and tried to swallow but there was so much, I had to spit it out. This has NEVER happened to me, in all ten years living on the Georgia-South Carolina border, eating at god knows how many BBQ joints, from backyard shacks to bigger chains. 

I could go on, since I tasted my way around the menu in order to be fair. Let's see: the brisket was dry, the chicken was greasy, the mac 'n cheese was GOOEY, *not* the firmer, more seasoned Southern version as claimed on their menu. The desserts were passable but chintzy little overpriced portions.

I love me some good BBQ and truly feel sad for anyone who settles for the food served here. Deke's owes the South an apology.

I can't even offer a nice thing to say about this place. The atmosphere is very stuffy, the restaurant owner is completely full of himself, and I got food poisoning from unwashed lettuce. 
We were sat down and no one came to ask for our drinks or bring us water for about 10 minutes. I wanted to order curry with tofu and vegetables, but didn't know what kind of vegetables were in it, so I asked. The waiter, who turned out to be the owner, replied "It's just mixed vegetables." When I asked for clarity, he said something like "Green beans, onions... mixed vegetables." Okay, whatever. My partner got pad thai and I got massaman curry, my favorite. We also ordered a starter of pork dumplings in lettuce cups. They were delicious, but the owner sat there and explained how we should be eating them when we were about to start on them. He wasn't very polite about it either, we felt stupid. The lettuce they used in the starter was dry and obviously not washed, but I didn't think about it until later. Nobody checked on us from there and we didn't see our server until maybe 30 minutes later. When we finally got our food, the flavors were good, but overall, not what I wanted. Massaman curry served in a weird conical dish, soupy and not thick at all, and an odd selection of vegetables that didn't quite go. It wasn't until we were about to leave, however, that we got the nail in the coffin. My partner decided to ask our server if he was also the owner - he kind of stood out. He replied, "Oh yeah. I always have to be here." An odd comment, but we didn't have to ask him what he meant. He went on this thing about how he can't trust the customers and that they mistreat his staff. He bragged about how he's thrown customers out before because they wouldn't pay after he arbitrarily changed prices from the menu to their bill (each menu states that the prices are subject to change but no further explanation). He then went on to criticize all of his competition, without prompting - from the horrible food at Peking Buffet in Glassboro (our favorite for cheap chinese) to the bretrayal of a chef who moved on to create Thai Burger Cafe in my hometown of Pitman. He claims to know every restaurant owner in the county, and recommended an Indian restaurant where the owner had worked at the Four Seasons. When we mentioned our favorite Indian place, Gagan Palace, he didn't know what we were talking about. 
It was halfway home when I demanded that my partner pull over the car so I could vomit. I lost my expensive dinner all over the lawn of a church. Cross-contamination of meat and vegetables is a very real problem, so it's important to wash lettuce before it goes anywhere. 
There was one good thing that happened from our visit... I decided to try Thai Burger Cafe in Pitman. Go check out my upcoming review for them!

Edit: The owner seems to be extremely thin-skinned and personally attacks people who don't like his food. 

I also forgot to mention that he was bragging about his awards and accolades but the only ones I saw hanging on the walls were "Thanks for participating in this year's best of such and such" plaques. Why bother?

Santa Barbara is the perfect place to eat alfresco. This Italian restaurant is no exception.  They have many tables set up outdoors, with red table cloth and umbrellas, and socially distanced. 

Complimentary bread and butter is served. The coffee isn't that good and it's lukewarm, even the refill was lukewarm. I ordered the vegetarian cheeseburger, which comes with a side of french fries. Interesting. Can't tell what the vegetarian patty is made out of.  Otherwise, the meal was all good. I enjoy eating lunch outdoors. 

Service was friendly, but just ok.

This is just for customer service*

I had called the bakery up this morning to see about ordering a specialty birthday cake for this Saturday. I chose this bakery due to its good yelp reviews and because the website gallery showed images of cakes that were unique and professionally decorated. I was looking for something more then just a pretty cake w/ flowers and a happy birthday message.

When I spoke w/ a representative and I explained what I was looking for all she asked about was size, flavor and the message. Nothing about customization w/ design or color or special flavors. 

I said I was looking for something more elaborate- w/ a bird theme( I was thinking beautiful fondant song birds, botanicals images). She said " well we could draw a picture of a bird or print a photo onto the cake".  With that response all I could imagine was some cheep looking cake no more special in appearance then a grocery store bakery. And since I would have a chance to preview the design I quickly hung up and called the Town Crier bakery in peddlers village and they were excited to suggest design ideas and describe what it would like to me over the phone. 

So while I can't say the cake will taste better,  the Town Crier gets my positive yelp review and $$$$ because they actually seemed interested in working with me.

Everything was OK here, not great. We were greeted and seated by the owner, Dory. Ordered two drinks from our waitress which took a while to come, despite the fact we were one of six tables in there on a Sunday night. Food came was OK. Pork tenderloin covered with canned peaches left much to be desired. We won't hurry back.

What a German gem in downtown St Pete. There is great German eats and beer here. They are open now after covid-19 lockdown phase 1 lift has occurred. There is comfortable indoor seating and also outdoor seating. The curry wurst is really good and so was the schnitzel. The schwartzbier is really, really good!!
The owner was exceptionally friendly and service was great!

Came here with a former coworker for a quick bite to eat.  The food here was cooked very well.  He had recommended the smoked fish dip, we shared it and it was absolutely delightful.  They have plenty of local beers also on tap.  The oyster po boy was delicious and very filling.  Would highly recommend this place.

I have been to Cafe de Paris at least 10 times by now and I can't believe that I still haven't written a review of this amazing cafe. If you are ever on the Gulf Blvd. during breakfast, lunch, or brunch time, I highly recommend stopping by here to either grab an authentic French breakfast or a yummy pastry with coffee.

Here are my ratings based on different criteria:

Quality of food: Excellent. We have tried many different things here and each time the experience has been excellent. Some of my personal favorites for lunch include: Bacon Cheese and Egg croissant, and Parisian style sandwich. Sometimes, when I just want a quick bite, I grab either an almond croissant or a chocolate croissant. The chef here is from France and almost all the people behind the counter speak French. When you hear customers speaking French with the staff you know that this place is authentic!

Decor: Kinda cool. Since this is obviously a French style cafe, there are all kinds of Parisian knick knacks and photos of Paris. There is nothing overly fancy about the decor. It just feels homey.

Cleanliness: No complaints. All the tables and floor were kept clean. They have both indoors and outdoors seating area. The staff is really quick about picking up the dishes and wiping down the tables. 

Service: Friendly. People behind the counter will either speak to you in French or in English. They always smile and ask how you are doing. 

Speed of food preparation: Fast. If you're ordering just a pastry and coffee then you're handed those when you pay. If you're ordering a crepe or a sandwich, they give you a number to put on the table. The most it has ever taken them to bring my order is 10 minutes which is great because I like taking my time sipping my coffee on a lazy weekend mornings anyway.

Price: Cheap. Depending on what you get, a pastry and coffee will set you back around $4. Sandwiches cost around $6. 

If you're feeling like having an authentic French style cafe experience with fast, homey, and friendly service, then checkout Cafe de Paris.

Yumm!!! We stopped in here because I hate fast food breakfast and we needed something on the go. They have hot, made to order breakfast sandwiches in addition to their donuts! You can choose to have your sandwich on a croissant, bagel, donut or biscuit! And choose from bacon, sausage, turkey or ham. 

HOT SANDWICHES: My husband had the sausage, egg and cheese on an Asiago bagel and I wish I had gotten his! It was so good! I don't typically like sausage but it had good flavor. I had a bacon, egg and cheese on a croissant. The thing I liked most is they do not have the typical fast food, folded eggs. Those make me gag! They make their eggs fresh for each sandwich!  

DOUTS: Of course we also had to try the donuts! My husband had the Peanut Butter Banana and that butthead did not give me a bite! So I can't speak for it but I'm assuming it was good because he devoured it. He says it tastes like Peanut Butter on a banana, 12 out of 10 stars lol. I couldn't decide so I tried two minis. An apple fritter and a PB&J. The fritter was ok but not my favorite, the PBJ tastes just like a PBJ sandwich! 

ICED COFFEE: Although it was too sweet for my taste I really enjoyed the fact that instead of ice cubes you have frozen coffee cubes. So when they melt, it doesn't water down! 

Would definitely come back to those place. Also check in on Yelp to get one free donut!

Love mazzaros!! Oh man I come here just to eat lunch! The deli and bakery are both phenomenal. I always get a sub and a dessert. The chocolate rum cake ball is so boozy and rich and moist! They have tables set outside under a covered porch. 

The market and wine shop are great as well as a gift shop. I got some adorable oversized polka dot mugs from here that I use as soup bowls. Omg I love this place. Fresh, quality Italian ingredients, this is where you go! They are always packed!!

I would definitely like to come here again to try more items. We came here with family mostly for drinks but had a couple appetizers. We sat outside on the porch. They have indoor and outdoor seating which is nice. 

We ordered wings (medium) and Irish chips which are House-made waffle fries with brown gravy dipping. Both the wings and fries were delicious! I'm a ranch connoisseur and their ranch was very good.

I also ordered a drink that was peach vodka and sweet tea I believe and that was very good. No complaints here. Sorry no pics I was starving so ate the food before I remembered lol.

Doesn't look like much on the outside, it's in a not so classy strip plaza. However this place is always packed and for good reason. Well one reason is it's pretty small on the inside so you can expect a wait. My only other negative was it's a little pricey. 

3 words: Lobster Grilled Cheese!!! Two of my favorite things in one. And they are not skimpy on the lobster. It was stuffed with large amounts of lobster... I guess that made it worth the price lol. A little skimpy on the havarti but it didn't take away from the buttery lobster. My husband thought his burger was just ok and pricey for what it is but I would def recommend the lobster grilled cheese. 

Also a great beer selection. With select rotating taps.

Average review because I did not care for the restaurant below however I loved the rooftop bar!  

We ate on the bottom floor restaurant and were a little disappointed. My favorite thing I ate was the boom boom shrimp which was as just standard breaded and fried shrimp with a spicy sauce. Everything was kinda mediocre. The bisque was good for the first few bites but excessively heavy so I couldn't even finish the cup portion and it left me with a stomach ache. The calamari my brother ordered was disgusting! It was cut into long strips and the texture was off. He said he felt like he was eating a sponge lol. 

Although the food and service disappointed, the rooftop bar was great! Spacious and comfortable seating. I would go back just to have a couple drinks up there!! Plus a great view of the beach!

I happen to love this place. I love tapas style and they have a lot of it. My friend and I ordered a few sharing things and we expected it to be smaller but the portions were actually big! We both took home leftovers. Didn't care for the beef poutine too much, the shaved meat was weird to me, reminded my of "steak-Ums" lol. But everything else was good, I'm not a Brussels sprouts fan and these were actually really good! 

Drinks are delicious and if you check in on yelp you get a free wine or beer! Our waitress was nice. Not my first or last time here, would recommend.

I was excited to come here because my friend loves coming here. I was disappointed when we were trying to order drinks because I literally ordered six different beers one after the other and they were out of every single one. They need some updated menus. Some of the beers they were just out of for the night but most they do not carry anymore. So I ended up getting the bartender's recommendation and hated it. I will say though that he was nice enough to not charge me for it. I did not ask for him to take it back but he noticed that I did not drink it and that I didn't like it so he took it off the bill. 

We all ordered an appetizer. They have a late night happy hour so they were $5 each. Good prices but Everything was fried options. Not a place to eat at if you are on a diet lol. But fried food pairs well with beer I guess!

Came with a girlfriend and they have a really good happy hour menu! We ordered "the kitchen sink" which is everything on it for $50 and split it. The charcuterie and cheese platter with warm olives was the best part, really good. The pasta was also really good. The only thing I did not like was the raw scallop dish. I love scallops but this had a lot of really coarse salt on it that just over powered it. It's definitely a good deal to split with a friend. So much food!

We were still full but still had to order desert. The deserts were really good and unique as well. This is a small restaurant so seating is limited. We came in a Monday so it wasn't an issue but if you come at a busy time you made need a reservation.

I'm changing my review of this store because I just realized they sell expired items on their shelf! I was there August 6th and I just opened up a granola bar wondering why it tasted stale. Expired July 17. Didn't think at a store like this I would need to check expiration dates so carefully. 

Original review:

Very expensive. Not my normal shopping store. It is an organic store so you expect to pay more, though this one is a little more than some others with the exact same items. 

The store was clean and orderly and I did find items that are not at every grocery store so it is nice to come here for specific items. 

The cutest part about this store that won me over? The tiny shopping carts for toddlers! They love pushing their own, so cute! However be warned because that means they want to buy more things! Lol.

Wow!! I was worried it wouldn't live up to the hype I've read but this place was ridiculously good! The outside is super cute, looks like an old house. In the heart of downtown safety harbor so there is no parking lot, you must find street parking. 

I had the Vive la France to drink. My drink was extremely fresh and not overly sugary, only sweet from the fruit juice. I could drink many of them! They also serve free bread and butter. 

My friend and I opted to have soup and salad for dinner since we also wanted dessert. The Chèvre salad was so good and fresh!! The ham and corn chowder was also super flavorful. I ate all of everything! My friend had the same salad and French onion soup. I did try her soup, usually French onion is too salty for me but this soup was not, more of a low sodium French onion which I enjoyed. 

We had the Nutella crepe and the orange liquor crepe, and again we cleared the plates! Everything here was super yummy! Would definitely recommend.

Very good food. I opted not to get an appetizer because of the portion size for the price. But the entrees are filling and delicious, so worth the price. For cocktails I didn't like the first i started with, a strawberry thyme drink but it tasted pretty watered down, not much flavor to me. The blueberry lemon drop however was really good. 

For my entree I had the Chilean sea bass with mushroom risotto and ate every bite! So delicious. My friend had the chicken Marsala which was had really yummy flavor and full of mushrooms! Both so good. For desert we shared the white chocolate creme brûlée. Everything we ate was delicious.

One of my favorite beaches, that although not close to me, is worth the drive! Super relaxing and peaceful whether day or night. Some of the prettiest sunsets are found here. 

Next to a nice quiet town, with shops, restaurants and places to stay. Sometimes they have streets blocked off for craft fairs and vendors and it's fun to bring your fur baby's and walk along to check out everything. 

Very clean area also. Never see much pollution or littering. Not a party beach but more of a romantic beach. Love this area just to get away for a staycation or date night!

Definitely not a fine dinning kind of place, it's a sports bar. You come here for drinks and greasy bar food. 
It's pretty much all fattening but delicious lol. The best things I tried here was definitely the Mac n cheese (so creamy) and the bacon wrapped, cheese stuffed tater tots! Omg so good!! My "meal" however was the Bloody Mary. The drink itself was not that good. It came with a lot of toppings so that's why I considered it a meal. The steak slider was not very good. The meat had a weird taste to me. But the chicken slider and the rest was really good. 

I would definitely come here again when I'm craving the really bad (but delicious) food! They also offer bottomless mimosa and bromosa brunch!

Love the melting pot! Fondue lovers heaven. Best cheese and chocolate fondue!! The entree is a nice experience but not my fav, but still good. I just love to come for the cheese and chocolate! They also have a great happy hour menu!

Yummm!! Can't believe this was my first time here. Also can't believe I did not get any pictures of food because I just dug in and it was that good. It is a little pricey for what it is, I spent $32 for two people and two drinks. I did have the herbed salmon which was a two dollar upgrade on the protein and worth it. But it was delicious. Fresh ingredients, delicious sauces. Even their housemaid teas. I had a strawberry lemonade that was very refreshing. I want to come here again.

Didn't order food but came here for drinks one night. (They have live music earlier in the day). Drinks were good, prices were standard. I think $9 for my grapefruit margarita. Bartenders were friendly and chatted with us. 

Nice view. Even though it was night there's a little gate you can still open and walk out on the dock. Can be pretty romantic. Would come here again if In the area.

Good prices and daily specials. Came on taco Tuesday. Had one shrimp ($4) and one chicken ($3) taco. They were actually really good! For the price the quality did not suffer. Good drink specials too. 

They have indoor and outdoor seating. The outdoor is pet friendly. Deducted one star because when we got there all the tables were kinda dirty. It wasn't busy but they just weren't cleaned good.

Very unique, interesting flavors, including a vanilla ice cream with bacon it in. Giant scoops for ice cream. I had the 813 and it was really good. Very artsy/hipster vibe inside. They even have select ice creams with CBD in it! I would come here again if in the area.
Love this place! Multiple bars both inside and outside. Both indoor and outdoor seating. Games. Live music. Actually a huge building area. Very fun for everyone.

The pastries are better than the entrees!! The entrees are not bad but the pastries were delicious and my favorite part! The saddest part is I don't have photos of two of my fav pastries from this place because I had them a different time and didn't snap a pick. Bottom line if you go in to eat and don't have room for dessert, get it to go! Don't skip it! 

My first taste of this place was when my hubby brought me home two pastries. They were both tarts with custard and fruit. One raspberry and one blueberry. Both delicious, delicate, light and creamy but the raspberry was my fav! So he took me back here for breakfast another day. 

When we came we were seated right away (its very small inside but was not busy on super bowl Sunday). All of the staff is extremely sweet. 

We ordered two pastries from the beginning along with our two meals. I don't know the names but the first was another custard tart with strawberries and the other was like a creme brûlée filling in brioche bread with powdered sugar. Again both delicious. 

My hubby had a cheese and bacon omelet. Instead of cut up the bacon was left in full strips in the omelet. I decided to order the croissant madame because I felt like having a croissant and Ive never actually had a croque madame (a French specialty) so I wanted to try it. I don't know why I decided this because I do not like ham lol so I wouldn't order again but for what it is, it was quite good. The croissant was huge! The ingredients are good quality and fresh.

Happy hour $1 charbroiled oysters is what brought me here to this restaurant! Happy hour is only in the bar area so come early or be prepared to stand while eating with no seats. The oysters were very good at a very good deal. Though the bread they serve it with is soft, with oysters you should really have crunchy crostini like bread for a difference in texture. So I ate them as is out of the shell without the bread. 

The frozen cocktails are $5 at happy hour so I decided to try both just because. I'm glad they were only $5 because I did not like either. (Don't worry the food is good) but these drinks are the biggest disappointment. The hurricane was way too sweet, pretty much all sugar, and the frozen Sauvignon was sour and if not drank fast enough it separated, I only drank half and was done. 

After happy hour ended we did get a table and had the best waiter-Mario!!! He was awesome!!! I would come back and ask for his section. We all ordered appetizers as our entrees instead of meals, I like to try a little of everything and share. Here's what we had: 
* Alligator- BY FAR MY FAVORITE BITE OF THE NIGHT! I hate when places over bread alligator to fry it and this place did not have any breading, just coated in the spices and fried crispy still. Delicious, must get. 
* Crab Benigets- ordered purely out of curiosity, it is a pretty much a crab cake breaded and fried kinda tasted like tuna salad. I think too much mayo inside or something, I would pass on these next time. 
* Boudin balls- Ok, wouldn't order again. Needed a little more seasoning or flavor. 
* Skillet Jalapeño Cornbread- So Good!!! Get this and the alligator. It was sweet and buttery and delicious. 
* Cajun Trio- everything was ok. 
* Bourbon bread pudding - Free with a check in on yelp! I was glad it was free, it was ok but not worth $12 in my opinion. I like my bread pudding to have lots of sauce. This was just a little on top and none throughout. 

Overall I would come here to try other entrees but the alligator, oysters and cornbread were amazing. Waiter was amazing. Everything else just ok. Frozen drinks are gross lol. Come try it out though, at least for happy hour.

Came here for lunch and all I have to say is you better order the lobster grilled cheese!!! I mean it, so good! It comes with a cup of lobster bisque and kettle chips for $15.50. The lobster grilled cheese is served on Texas toast and full of huge chunks of lobster meat throughout!! Dip it in the soup and enjoy! 

My mom ordered the shrimp tacos and was not impressed. They come with two tacos but each taco only has 3 little shrimp. It's pretty much a lettuce taco. Skip these. 

The environment was clean and cute. Our waitress was friendly. Would eat here again if in the area.
