My uncle had his 75th birthday party last night at Vincent's. We were in their banquet room. I appreciated that the room is not near the actual dining room. 
It was private and secluded. 
We were fed Veal Marsha, Lasagna and Chicken Parmigiana. The Veal was so tender. The Marsala was so light and delicious! The lasagna was melt in your mouth good. You also could cut the chicken parmigiana with a fork! 
The restaurant did an excellent job! Service was on point. 
The servers even brought my two nephews chicken tenders and French fries since they wouldn't eat any of the food on the menu. 
How cool is that! 
There was also a bar and bartender. 
This is the perfect place for a party.

It's better to walk up and order your food to go! Seating is scarce when the restaurant is busy. It's worth the wait though! 
The crawfish is delicious. It's seasoned well. 
I also tried the potato salad. It was delicious. 
I want to go back and try their other dishes. 
The service was really good.

We ended up here after walking down the beach to go to IHOP. This establishment took this space over. We saw Oyster Company and thought NO! We were WOW'd!! The breakfast was so fresh. I had over easy eggs with fresh potatoes. The chicken apple sausage was out of this world. Not sure where they got it but I should have asked. I think I've see a similar sausage made by Emeril at Publix. My husband had the ham and Swiss Quiche. He said it was outstanding. 

We just did a "staycation" on Clearwater Beach for Memorial Weekend, but I'd drive here just for breakfast in a heartbeat. Although, I absolutely can not wait to drive here to try dinner. Obviously they have a large oyster menu. It's a Crabby Bills sister restaurant. So why wouldn't you? I can't remember the 2 servers names, but you can tell they genuinely loved their job!

I do not know how this place is still in business - the customer service is terrible. I repeat TERRIBLE. The manager is extremely rude and disrespectful to customers. I went in for the lunch buffet yesterday. After finishing my first plate of food, in which I left a couple half eaten pieces of chicken, the server (whom I didn't know was the manager at the time) comes over to clear my dish and says to me "SHAME ON ME FOR HAVING YOU COME HERE, LOOK AT ALL THE FOOD YOU WASTED" and then walks away. As you can imagine, I was in complete shock - I only had 1 plate of food, it's not like I had several, and I was not brought up to waste food. If I don't finish something on my plate, there's a really valid reason for it. The next waiter that comes by, I ask him to have the manager or owner come out. 

The guy that cleared my plate ended up being the manager, so I let him know how extremely rude I found his comment to be. He said that I was wasting food and that "THIS IS AN ALL YOU CAN EAT BUFFET, NOT AN ALL YOU CAN WASTE BUFFET." I am not sure how a couple half eaten pieces of chicken (that I didn't eat because they were dry) can be deemed wasteful, however, my response to him was that I don't appreciate how he is treating me and how he is not only neglecting to rectify the situation, but is making it worse by attacking me more. I informed him that I will never come back and will be leaving a review regarding my experience, in which his response was "I DON'T CARE." I asked him how he could not care that he would be getting a terrible review, in this day in age where EVERYONE checks reviews before dining at places, and he repeats "I DON'T CARE" and walks away. He WALKED AWAY. Not to be seen again. I don't know how he can be in his line of business and treat people the way he does. 

Please think twice before dining at this restaurant. The food is fine but there are many other AMAZING Indian places in the St. Louis area - don't go to a place where they treat you terribly and don't particularly care if you come back or not. 

Oh, and Mr. Manager, if you're reading this - I hope you feel good about defending those half-eaten pieces of chicken. I hope it was worth losing customers over because you'll never see me there again.

Absolutely loved my ramen tonight, husband loved his too. I got the Shoyu ramen spicy level 3. I like spicy foods, not too spicy, but a good heat and this was just a tad hotter than I prefer. So keep that in mind when ordering your spice level that it is pretty hot here! We also tried one of the kebabs, we had the beef with chimichurri and it was excellent. Attentive service and the place was pretty packed on a Thursday night. Really excited I gave this place another shot after a pretty mediocre visit several months ago. Definitely will be back soon!

Finally! A new place in town to get real homemade, quality Mexican food. Where you say? Run by Mariel Montero Sena, you've probably seen her around when she was at Expressionz Café running Taco and Fondita days. Unless you've been living under a large rock. Which is totally possible. I went once for tacos and they were dynamite so I was hoping for more of the same quality when we went to check out HUMA after some beach v-balling.

HUMA Mexican Comfort is located close to Argyll Plaza on the north east corner of 99 Street and 63 Avenue. It's a bit difficult to spot while driving (the sign is pretty small) but it's in the same parking lot as Tienda Latina and Kyoto Sushi Japanese Restaurant. It's worth the search, trust me on this one. We came around 7pm on a Wednesday evening - there were only a few tables occupied. It can fit approximately 30 to 35 people. They'll be busy once the word gets out on the streets.

What's really intriguing about HUMA is that each day is a different menu. Wednesday is their seafood menu. The dessert menu had five options but they were out of the flan. Will have to try it out next time.

We talked briefly with Mariel and this is what's on deck for each day:

- Tuesday - Favourites
- Wednesday - Seafood
- Thursday - Fondita day
- Friday - Street food and snacks
- Saturday - Taco day
- Sunday - Breakfast and "hang over" remedies

- Tamarind ($3.50) - I've had horchata before so it was between tamarind or the jamaica for me. The waitress was awesome and brought out these cute little cups to sample all three before we picked. I went with the tamarind which wasn't too sweet (very subtle) but instead was light and refreshing.
- Jamaica ($3.50) - the jamaica according to our waitress is from a leaf. Looking it up afterwards, it looks like it's hibiscus which gets its deep, beet red colour from the calyces (sepals), a type of flower so she was close enough. This one was more sweeter but still quite refreshing.

- Ceviche ($9.00) - diced mild white fish cooked in fresh lime juice mixed with fresh tomato, onion and cilantro. Served with nacho chips and crackers. This is probably the first ceviche that I've had in Edmonton that was good. It tasted fresh with a nice acidity to it. The only complaint we had was that there wasn't enough chips! Those were gone pronto. There was also three types of sauces brought to our table - salsa verde, salsa roja and pickled jalapenos/carrots/onion. They also brought out a hot sauce separately, which I believe was for the ceviche. Nice to add to the ceviche and tacos.
- Pescado empanizado ($16.00) - mild white fish fried in a seasoned crumb mixture and served with sides of Mexican rice, fried beans and a fresh salad. The fish (it's basa) was perfectly cooked. Lightly fried with a nicely coated crumb mixture, this was one of the best fishes I've eaten in a long time. It was flaky, tender, crunchy - pretty fantastic. If it's on the menu, it's a must order.
- Fish tacos ($16.00) - breaded mild white fish broken onto 4 tortillas and topped with chipotle mayo, shredded lettuce and sliced avocado. The fish tacos were lightly fried the same way as the pescado. Four was perfect as we each were able to try one. Good stuff but will have to try out their Taco day to see which taco is my fav.
- Camarones a la diable ($18.00) - shrimp cooked in a spicy chipotle sauce and served with sides of Mexican rice, fried beans and a fresh salad. It also came with a side of tortillas (covered to keep them warm) to make your own mini tacos if you wanted. The shrimp was perfectly cooked although I didn't find them spicy.
- Beef enchiladas ($13.00) - shredded beef rolled in 3 corn tortillas and covered in salsa roja (red salsa) and served with a small fresh salad. This seriously remind me of lasagna. The tortillas had that soft, lasagna pasta texture to it.

- Cremitas ($4.00) - a Mexican vanilla custard dessert, this was boooomb. Super light, airy, if you liked custard desserts, you will be in l-o-v-e. I couldn't stop scooping up spoonfuls of it.
- Tres leches cake ($5.00) - the tres leches cake was soft, spongy goodness. If you've never had it before, it's made from three types of milk: evaporated milk, condensed milk and heavy cream.
- 2x Platanos fritos con lechera ($4.00) - fried plantain with condensed milk drizzle. Uh yeah, we ordered two of these bad boys. Plantain anything is delicious and these satisfied everyone's dessert cravings.

I am stoked that there's finally another good Mexican restaurant in town. Possibly even my new favourite! I can't wait to go back and try a bunch more dishes. Seriously, that fish was off the charts. As Arnold says, I'll be baaaaaack. You know it's a good sign when everyone at the table is "mmmm-ing" after every bite.

February 27, 2015 at Joy Tsin Lau gifted me--and an entire banquet hall (second floor) full of folks celebrating the Chinese new year--with a ridiculous case of food poisoning. Friends ended up in the E.R., while others (including myself) simply took it out on the bathroom, trash cans, etc.

Unsurprising after-the-fact, if you look up the Philadelphia Department of Public Health reports health violations (e.g., mouse droppings, unsafe handling of meat, etc.) for Joy Tsin Lau, you see the same violations occurring year after year. What is surprising that the establishment is still in business--certainly won't be getting mine again.

Amazing  Chiopino !!!    Fresh  mussels and clams, fish.  The broth was  rich  and  tangy with tomato & herbs.  Love that  there  was a small serving of noodles in the bottom of  my  bowl.   I  had  a small  salad and their  lovely  Charlie Palmer ice tea, half tea & half lemonade.  

Well,  should  I  tell  you  that  I  put  away  a basket  of  the  garlic breads and an extremely sinful  Tiramisu,  so  fresh I  can  smell  the  espresso powder.  Well, I  embarass myself everywhere by eating more than my date.  Me  a  pig,  are  you  ?

Annie Christian
Feb 23, 2016

We normally visit the Orlando restaurant which goes by the same name. The restaurant is nicely decorated with many typical Puerto Rican scenes, with art work and pretty designs. I really liked the way the restaurant is set up, the bar area is very large and the dining area is spaced properly. 
As far as the food I found them to not be as good as the Orlando location. To start off we had a few frituras which are customary Puerto Rican appetizers-alcapurrias de guineos y jueyes and bacalaoitos. The best of all of them were the bacalaoitos which were very flavorful and crispy as they should be. The alcapurrias were ok, the traditional ones were good but the one made with jueyes was not good at all. For our meal I had the Chuletas can can, my girlfriend has the Mofongo and mom has the Chillo (fried snapper) the food was average, nothing necessarily memorable. The Chuleta was cooked at a good temperature but the chicharrón was not crunchy at all, it was very chewy and the point of the Can Can is that the chicharrón is crispy! The mofongo was ok. Unfortunately it was missing bits of tocino which is always expected. The Chillo was good but once again it was not as good as we had at their other location. For dessert we decided to try the flan and again it was ok, but that is about it.

After a long day of walking and of an exhaustive search for a place to eat, I am glad the first place we were looking for ended up being closed because we stumbled upon this place. The server was really nice and helpful. My girlfriend had the huevos rancheros and I had the Cesar salad with grilled chicken. Both of our meals were perfect. The grilled hockey on my salad was perfectly cooked and tasted good. This place was not our first choice but it worked out perfectly!

Amazing. That's all I have to say! This place is absolutely amazing! I can't praise it enough. 

I went with a couple of friends expecting some pretty good Italian food, but what we got was a whole experience! I felt like I was transported to Italy - and for multiple reasons:

1. The food. Obviously! Order the sacchettini, trust me. You won't regret it. It comes with pear and Gorgonzola and is literally one of the best things I've ever tasted. 

2. The atmosphere. This quaint little restaurant is intimate with dim lighting, but that doesn't limit it to date night! It's perfect for a night out with close friends or family too. The decor was very on brand and appropriate for the place. Italian vibes all around! 

3. The service!! We did not go without. The wine was flowing, we were constantly looked after and engaged in conversation with multiple staff members. We had plenty of laughs and really felt like we were hosted. 

Overall, I adore this place and have nothing but great things to say about it! I will 10000% be back soon. 

I should also add that any Italian food request you make - the chef will make it for you!

I've eaten here at least a dozen times and wanted to update my review to reflect that. you really can't beat the food here, especially the "trust me" (a dish so named because you don't know what it is until it gets placed in front of you). on Halloween it was deep fried pork tenderloin. like chicken tenders but better! a giant portion w two yummy sauces (one sweet, one creamy) in the bottom of the bowl. 

I came back like three days later because it was so good that night and got the trust me again. this time it was grilled quail. smoky and delicious! I almost always order the lamb chops and the manchego mushroom toast from the regular menu. 

come here with friends and order like everything

Is the hype for this restaurant worth it?

I'd say yes. Once again one of the best restaurants I've been to in the city is tucked away in a strip mall, in an unassuming location. After getting lost getting here, (took the wrong turn on the traffic circle...doh) I found Lan's. I've been to T.H.I.S Place (operated by the same people behind Lan's) but had not tried Lan's. I heard good things about the food, and well, who am I to argue with good food. 

I came here with a cold, but luckily I was still able to taste food. I ordered the tom yum soup and the medium sized lemongrass beef bowl. The soup was delicious hot in temperature, a little spicy (perfect for a cold), a bit savoury, with a bit of lime. The vermicelli bowl was quite large for a medium size, which I liked. The lemongrass beef was perfect, and the bowl was great, crisp veggies, a nice fresh taste. The spring rolls that came on top were great as well. Usually, I find spring rolls to be a bit too oily (they're not my favourite) but these were great. The menu itself had a nice variety of Thai and Vietnamese foods, and there were several vegetarian options as well. I ordered the green tea, and it was deliciously light and not bitter. Service was quick and friendly, and I got a good, filling lunch for about $15 with tax and tip.

My mom loves this place and had raved about it for some time before finally treating me one day, and I ended up liking it so much that I took my boyfriend the next day. For almost a year, this was go-to Mexican restaurant when we needed something cheap and tasty.

The prices are so great that I was willing to overlook the shoddy decor, torn seats in the booths, and the toddler you will find tearing up the dining room if you go in the evening (on one night there was a crying infant too, for ambiance I guess). I was totally willing to overlook that the guacamole is sometimes watery and way too cold, that I can never tell if I should just seat myself, and that on occasion a meal has been bland. I was willing to overlook a lot of things, because the prices and portions and never having to wait for a table were worth it.

They WERE worth it, until the other day. Boyfriend and I go for a quick Sunday lunch, and our waiter (presumably one of the owners or a relative, seeing as he is ALWAYS there) was treating us like we just killed his family or something! From the moment we walked in the door, this guy was giving us tremendous attitude. It was so uncomfortable that my partner and I jokingly questioned if we were on a hidden camera show because we couldn't figure out what set this guy off. We were the first of about 5 parties to arrive at the restaurant, but consistently received everything last (strangely, we were the only ones in the dining room with this particular waiter - everyone else had a much more efficient and polite gentleman), were never checked on, and at the end of the meal found ourselves waiting FOREVER for the check. The service was absolutely terrible, and the food not much better, so we left a tip that we felt reflected the service. 

As we're standing at the register paying, we hear our waiter loudly and angrily speaking in Spanish in the dining room, then he comes out to us at the register, holding up his tip for us to see and says, "This isn't 15%. You're supposed to tip 15%! What is this?" We looked at him in absolute disbelief, then each other, as this guy actually points at my boyfriend's money clip, then the receipt, and demands, "You give me 2 more dollars!" So stunned, we did, and left without another word.

NEVER to return.

Never in my life have I heard of this really happening. I hope those 2 dollars were worth it to this guy because he will lose hundreds of dollars of our business. Never ever again.

Owned and operated by South Philly trash and lit up like a shitty traveling carnival attraction, going to Geno's is through-and-through a bad experience. The way the employees seem to resent their customers for bothering them by patronizing their establishment, and especially  the obese man/woman character who slices the bread for the sandwiches complete the carnie vibe.

I'd give the food a C-, and definitely not worth the $9 or whatever it is they charge now. For my two cents, it is better than Pat's, whose meat I find to be dry and undigestible. To be sure, you will get a better steak from ANY other sandwich shop in Philly (besides Pat's) or any other city for that matter.

There is something humbling about going to Geno's. Usually when I'm there it's at an hour when most decent people are asleep (Geno's is open 24hrs). You get into a long line with money in hand, for fear of not being prepared to get out of the cashier's sight the moment they shove your overpriced pile of meat in your hand. Then there's the ridiculous streamlined ordering system (the "wiz wit or witout" shit) which I suppose originated naturally by regulars, but now feels contrived because it is mandatory. I want to gag sometimes when I hear myself say it. You slink off, happy to be out of eye-shot of the miserable people making sandwiches inside. 

Then there's Mr. Geno's steaks himself, Joey Vento. A real-life Jed Clampett, Mr. Vento comes off as a lovable lug who made it big. He seems like a nice guy, aside from his divisive political views which he has no qualms about sharing. That doesn't bother me. I imagine that if Jed Clampett went on a racist tirade about terrorists and Middle Eastern Oil, he'd be forgiven on the grounds of being a rich, overindulged rube, too.

Yet another aspect of Geno's that is in bad taste is the police and firefighter theme. Being a person who hates cops, and ESPECIALLY over-the-top, tasteless pandering, this really gets me. There is a giant plaque of Daniel Faulkner's surly mug (cop who was allegedly killed by Mumia Abu Jamal 30 years ago) right out front. 

As if this wasn't enough to dissuade anyone from going to Geno's, consider the case of the gentleman who was beaten up by Geno's goons after discovering meat delivered surreptitiously in the middle of the night was labeled as coming from some South American country from a year previous. Granted, he got beaten up for keying Geno's Hummer, but he discovered year old meat from a different continent all the same. Go America

I happened to find Mazzaro's while doing an internet search.  Being from Brooklyn, NY and now living in Florida, it's hard to find a good, "non chain" Italian Deli.  What I found in Mazzaro's is so much more.  The place is big and they have all kinds of good stuff.  You won't know what to leave with!

Parking can get a bit crazy but they do have parking lot attendants when needed to help with that.

They have some of the best sandwiches my wife and I have ever had and at just $5 per sandwich, it can't be beat.  I'm not talking Subway $5 foot longs, I'm talking real deal Italian sandwiches.  Try the Mozzarella sandwich which is made with fresh Mozzarella that is made on the premises.  Last time I was there, I had also tried the squid salad (Might have a different name) and I was blown away.

I was surprised to see that they also sell fresh pasta's.  We brought home their Four Cheese Manicotti, tossed it in the oven and went straight to Heaven and back!  It was that good.

Also try some of the many baked goods and breads, Pizza, Prosciutto sliced straight from the cured pigs leg, Cheeses, Wines, Gelato, Imported goods, etc...

Bottom line, I love Mazzaro's and I don't mind taking the 2 hour drive to get there.  We usually will go to Mazzaro's on a Saturday Morning, pick up the goodies and then head straight to the beach for a day of fun and a belly full of goodness.

Ate here for the first time yesterday and it was amazing!! Ordered the Black Spaghetti and it was soooo flavorful and hot when it came out.  The shrimps and scallops were done very well.  Can't wait to come back and try it again. 
The only thing was the proportions seem small for the prices, and unless it's happy hour, the drink prices are a lil high too...But my stars are based solely on my dish!

Called in to this place to place a to go order because it's still- covid. Bartenders are rude as hell & mask less lol Where is mayor Cantrell when ya need her? 

You ask for market prices you don't get an answer. You don't even get a total before they hang up the phone in your face. 
You can have all the shitty service you want when your prices match the shitty service but BABYYYYY, if you're going to charge a fried seafood platter at $26.00 a MF plate I better get FIVE STAR SERVICE. The place is ran and serviced like a trashy bar off a service road in Kenner. For a $72.00 tab you can go to Mid city yacht club and get 2 roads of drinks for that. For a $72.00 to go tab with no alcohol you can get a fuck ton more food AND ALCOHOL for less money AND BETTER SERVICE. That's the principle in all this. 
Fuck this place and the white superiority complex that surrounds it don't waste your time or money. 
Ya SOBS lucky I could afford my tab and not make a scene on you snobby asses.  
Also to add 
THE CORN AND CRAB BISQUE TASTES 4 DAYS TOO OLD. 
Mozzarella sticks weren't cooked enough. 
Seafood might be on steroids but the fry batter itself is trash.
Oh!! Add an extra $ to this price point for this joint. Only thing decent about this $72 tab was the half order of onion rings. The food was so bad it's in my trash bag and now I have to drink away the pain of the $72 we wasted. Say it with me everybody "Ripppppo offfffffff."

After all the hype from KFC and Food Network shows about Hot Chicken I had to check out this fad where it originated.  This is the 2nd location of Hattie B's, but is still quite crowded.  The chicken is great - I got the hot which gave a good kick and had a subtle heat to it.  I went with the tenders, cole slaw and mac and cheese.   The tenders were great - no mess eating normal hot chicken and still had a solid taste.  Cole slaw was fine - could have gotten a better side.   The mac and cheese was pretty good.  Nice cool off from the hot chicken, but it wasn't memorable.  I think I would try greens next time.
I know there are a number of options for hot chicken around Nashville, but I was pleased trying one of the places that originated this style.   I'll be back next time I am in town.

The Tavern is a semi upscale restaurant about a half hour outside downtown of St. Louis.  It has a modern look and a decent amount of seating split into a few sections.  The place had a lot of energy and we were happy to make a reservation day of for 4 people. 

Food was pretty good here.  They start you off with some awesome Parmesan bread which is amazing!  This was the highlight of the night.  My wife and I split a spinach salad that was pretty basic.  We also shared the surf and turf sampler as an entree.  How was the perfect amount of foods. The meats were both pretty bland - steak was tasteless and chicken was over done.  Both fish were Ok - but the sauces stood out.  Kids meals were a generous size and included sundaes.

Our server started off great, but once it got busy kind of forgot about us.  We never got our order of loaded tater tots - bummer.  We also had to hunt him down to pay the bill and get the kids sundaes.  It kind of put a damper on my experience.

Darfon's is a decent choice for dinner if you are staying around the Nashville airport.  It is a pretty good sized restaurant with a couple of different seating sections.  The ambiance is pretty low key and the lights are dim to set the mood.

Prices were reasonable and the place was rather empty on the weeknight I popped in.  My server was pleasant enough, but I only saw him a few times and had an un-refilled drink for the bulk of my visit.

I was told that I needed to try the shrimp and grits and I was not disappointed.  Even though it is on the appetizer menu, I received a portion big enough for dinner.  The large shrimp were spiced and cooked perfectly!  I really enjoyed the grits - silky and buttery.  I also ordered the bacon cheeseburger. I requested this medium rare, but it came out more on the well done side. It was nothing special and if I return I will definitely make a different selection.  The fries were spiced well, but not really cooked all the way through.  

Check this place out if you are staying near the airport - otherwise it doesn't really warrant a special visit.

Conner's Kitchen is a nice bar/grill located in the Indianapolis Marriott.  It is relatively new and still has a fresh feel.  The place is pretty dark and sets a cool mood.  Outdoor seating on the patio is nice, but there are some sketchy people walking by asking for money.  My server was very friendly and she and the other waitresses were joking around to make the meal enjoyable.

I started with the Monkey Bread.  It was awesome!  A small loaf of cheesy, garlicy bread with a tasty tomato sauce. The portion size was fine for just me, but it is too small for 2-3 people.  I went healthy for my entrée and had a very good Green Goddess salad.  It was a ton of healthy greens chopped up and served with grilled salmon.   I enjoyed the whole salad and felt full, but in a good way.  My waitress kept my drink full and I had an overall good dining experience.  Prices were on par with other hotel restaurants, but the quality was very high.

Check this place out if you are in the area - it is great for innovative home cooking.

Goldy's Breakfast Bistro is an amazing place that you truly must visit if you are in Boise.  This is located in a historic building adjacent to City Hall.  The street and sidewalk are both currently under construction, but that isn't keeping people from getting the awesome food here.  Also, be careful if you are taller - the ceilings are like 6' upstairs and you will need to duck. The staff is all super friendly and treat you like you're at home.  Everything is cooked to order in an open kitchen.  The 3 cooks on hand were all very efficient and made some killer breakfast!

I ordered a 2 egg combo.  The eggs were ok and the biscuit was just meh.  None of that matters because I ate the best corned beef hash I have ever had!  Maybe it was the fresh Idaho potatoes...but this was amazing!  The large portion of caramelized corned beef and potatoes was salty and satisfying. It was crispy and had an almost smoky taste.  My side of bacon was equally impressive, but the corned beef has stole the show.  I heard they are known for Egg Benedict - I suppose that may be good too.

If you are in town you realty should try this place!  I would wait even if it is crowded - it is that good!

The Nugget is ok. Never won much here but then never lost much here either. I like their rooms. Always clean and the service is superb. Good restaurant also with great service. They also have a play room for kids with video games etc.
On the way out of Santa Barbara, stopped here based on the ratings we read...carnitas burrito was fantastic! 19 different kinds of salsas and all that I retried had great flavor! Highly recommend!

Arrived at this location for an after-work party. It was a setting we could have some alcohol and have some fun, but not be concerned about work. 

I arrived and liked the cheap pours from the well, $2. The beer selection was minimal and I only like good beer.
So ordered a standard drink for me, and instead of a glass tumbler it came in a small sized plastic cup. Yep, I paid for $2 worth of a drink. Then shots were $2 and that was good. They too came in a shot sized plastic cup, probably a little larger pour than in a glass cup. 
The dance location we were in was dingy and dark. very limited seating and nowhere for coats. 
Bathroom is a little weird anyone walking by the men's room can see anyone standing at a urinal. That is a little odd when a co-worker walks by.

Wonderful place to watch the sunset!  Asian inspired as they offer a variety of dishes and daily specialty rolls. Nice cocktails and their wines are affordable especially because of their prime location, they could charge more. Thank goodness they don't! 
Very hip and modern place to dine, great for large parties or couples who want to enjoy eating by the beach. 
Service was great and the food came out pretty fast. Would recommend for sunset dining and kite bites.
I know it's a Covid situation, but I was disappointed with my Kung Pau Shrimp. The veggies were overcooked. It was not spicy at all. Need to step up the game for us.

Good food.  I only got sides from Tasties to complement my meal.  They were all that.  Very tasty and I was impressed.  This was my second time going to the restuarant.

The first time wasn't so good.  I ordered a cheeseburger only for them to tell me it takes 45 minutes! What? A cheeseburger taking longer than a steak? No way.  That really turned me off, but since they are right around the corner from me, I had to give them another try and they didn't fail.

Went back again to tasties. I wanted some turkey chops so bad. Called and placed an order for my hubby and my daughter and when I asked for my turkey chops they were out! They were also out of Mac n cheese and greens. Like wut? They lost out in a $50 order because they didn't have one thing on the menu. 

This has happened MORE than once! Like how do you run out of staple menu items and it wasn't even near closing time. 

The food is good I will say but the customer service needs some work.

Wish I didn't even have to give a star at all . We came here after the football game on Sunday . Place was very busy on first and second floors . The 3rd floor was pretty much empty so we all settled in up there .i had  a chicken sandwich and we ordered steak . The cheese was not even melted on the chicken patty and  the bun soggy and the steak was to make you sick , both plates were cold and not even edible . The barmaid Julie waited  on us and Very very rude young lady who seemed more interested in leaning over the bar to show her cleavage  to the men at the bar then waiting on her customers . 
She was very rude , we can see why they put her on the 3rd floor because she is the worst sever I have ever encountered and  she should know that woman are very good tippers and we don't care about your bleach  blonde ponytailed hair or cleavage we just wanted our food cooked and hot and a drink   . No I would never recommend this place

This restaurant easily makes a new addition to my list of the worst restaurants in the United States.  Located at the end of Stearn's wharf in Santa Barbara, CA, the restaurant is literally situated above the ocean.  Their sign outside says "Fish and Chips" and clearly depicts a fish with fries superimposed on it.  Their menu inside lists Fish and Chips for $10.95 and adds the words to the effect "You must try this".  The message was clear enough to me.  Their best dish is the fish and chips, and I should try it immediately lest I be made out to be a fool.  Given the proximity to the ocean and the ease with which this comfort food can be prepared, this seemed like a sure bet.  

Sure enough though, this choice was a most regrettable one.  What was presented to me was an unmitigated disaster.  The several apparent errors were all equally egregious.  First of note was that the chips were actually POTATO CHIPS and not fries as depicted on their very own sign.  If you are going to re-define a well known dish, you should provide the appropriate caveat to the customer.  Short of that, if you are going to make a major substitution, it should at least be for the better.  Alas.  These potato chips were unusually salty, and their flavor once adjusted for the high salt content, failed to add anything to the dish.  There were also not many chips, so this clearly was a cheap gesture.  Another cheap gesture was stacking the two filets on said chips on a tiny plastic salad plate and not offering trays.  One really needed to use both hands to carry this plate to a table and make sure nothing fell along the way.  I am sure someone looked at unit costs and determined that tiny disposable salad plates would be a money saver.  Additionally, cocktail sauce was not on view, but was available upon request only.  So far not so good, and we haven't even got to the fish yet.  Dreadful -- in a word.  I will allow that the color was nice and that it was not over fried.  But seriously, how do you fry fish so that it has NO TASTE whatsoever??  I would insert a forkful in my mouth, jostle it around my tongue, consider it, search for some nuance of flavor, shake my head effectively giving up, and swallow.  Repeating the process twenty times or so I ultimately finished this terrible meal.  

While I labored and, well, suffered through this meal, you don't have to.  Please, just avoid this place.  The majority of their business is unsuspecting tourists who won't return to the wharf anytime again soon.  With all of their cost cutting measures, it is just easy money for them, and they have no incentive to change.  Amazing seafood can be found in Santa Barbara at a spectrum of price points.  There is really no reason to consume anything here.  And if you think my critique of the fish and chips was harsh, I can only imagine what my review would have been like for their number two bestseller, the clam chowder in a bread bowl.  The broth was brown -- yikes!Enough said.

This was a great find on Yelp! It was hard to believe that the restaurant received so many 5 star reviews so I had to check it out for myself while I was in Lambertville NJ. 

My AWESOME experience started when I called the restaurant around 2 pm asking for a reservation at 6 pm the same day which was a Saturday. Needless to say it's almost impossible to get a reservation in most restaurants on a Saturday night anywhere in the area for the popular restaurants. The women on the phone apologized and said they were all booked up.. What  happened next shows what makes a great business and will keep customers coming back.

She offered to call me back after calling the reservations to see if there were any cancellations . I didn't expect much and to my surprise about 30 minutes later she called to ask if I could make it at 5:45pm which of course I accepted.

I looked a little further on the web and found out the husband Dennis is the chef and the hostess/ manager/ waitress is the wife Estella.  They have run other restaurants including EQ names after Estella in Manhattan NY back in the 90's. They are naturals at great customer service and Dennis is not happy with anything less than perfection with his food.

They have a passion for food and their customers.  Estella told me her goal was to put their best effort forward for every customer.  Up until our conversation she was not aware or did not care about reviews because they are always giving their best.  The experience they deliver went above and beyond expectation.

This is a small restaurant although from the minute you walk in you are transported to a chic modern French restaurant. They have beautiful artwork and a lighting fixture that sets the mood. Under COVID-19 restrictions there is only room to have 2 tables inside. They have outside seating in the garden in the back with about 10 tables.  The back is warm and inviting with lots of flowers, chic seating, lights, chimineas and French music. 

It was great to see they took COVID-19 seriously with a table with ample sanitizer outside the restaurant. Everyone was wearing a mask and the restaurant is spotless including the bathroom.

It's cash only and BYOB which makes up for the cash only restriction. Prices were very reasonable  and you receive a Manhattan experience for a fraction of the price.

The food is great!! The service is great as well! Estella is a one person army, greeting every customer taking time to make them feel welcome. They have one person bussing the tables and did a great job as well. 

As appetizers we had the lobster and wild mushroom crepe which can be shared as it was a generous portion. We also had the homemade tortellini  with mushrooms, Reggiano and chives. 
The both were fantastic! Everything was served at a perfect temperature and is homemade.

For entrees we had the rack of lamb which was a very generous portion at a great price. This was 2 big chops. We also had the sautéed Faro Island wild salmon, spinach, tomato and nutmeg. The pictures will speak for themselves.

I had profiteroles for desert which was perfect!  To top it off I ran into a friend at the restaurant who is a business owner in New Hope Pennsylvania which is only about 5 minutes away. She has been coming here for years.

All in all one of the best experiences I've had and I assure you  Estella and her husband will impress.  I highly recommend them.

Absolutely one of the best barbecue places I've ever been to. My wife and I were babysitting for a friend, and as the couple lived in a neighborhood we weren't very familiar with, we decided to take a walk around. The Joint was recommended to us, so we decided to saunter on over and check it out. They had an open door to the outdoor section of the kitchen, and I was heartened to see some old school meat smokers set up under a canopy. The interior isn't anything special, but the service is customarily fast and friendly. We got our food to go and went back to our friend's place, and we saw that they had an outdoor seating area that looked very festive. It was at that point we realized what goes on in the kitchen at The Joint is truly special. The beef brisket and pulled pork we got was phenomenal. PHENOMENAL. We even got our friend's ten month old in on the act, giving him small pieces of meat. The ensuing noises of pleasure said enough for the both of us. Go to this place.

HOW in the world have I not reviewed Oystercatchers yet?!?! This place is my jam. I've only ever gone for brunch, but it's the best brunch in the bay area for sure! 

I normally steer clear of buffets, but this one is classy AF and is kept up perfectly... it's not your average chafer type of buffet. The selection is huge at this brunch. They have an awesome raw bar with cocktail shrimp, oysters and mussels. They also have a caviar station, cured meats and cheeses, endless dessert options, a wide selection of sushi, salads, a number of breakfast items and plenty more. 

My personal favorites are the raw bar, the caviar (b/c why not?), the pasta station (I ate FIVE PLATES!), the creme brûlée (because who doesn't want to scarf down endless creme brûlée?) and the banana foster station.

I think I forgot to mention that they serve BOTTOMLESS mimosas and have a build-your-own bloody mary bar. The service is top of the line and they definitely work to keep your glasses full. 

This is my go to place when I have guests from out of town visiting. Be sure to make a reservation because they definitely get booked up.

Have you been to Shelly's Café? It is absolutely one of my favorites! The food is delicious and clearly prepared with love, the service is some of the best I've received anywhere and they even block off tables for social distancing which I so appreciate! Everything I've ever ordered there have been delicious! Check it out!

Met a fellow Yelper here for dinner on Tuesday, her suggestion but neither of us had been here before.  Ended up being a great choice!

She had the arancini and was kind enough to let me try one.  I am not a fan of dairy, and it was a ball of cheese and rice on a cream sauce so not my thing. I can understand why people like them though.

I had the stacked salad and it was delicious!  It was a nice blend of flavor and textures, presented beautifully.  I considered posting a picture but I'm not a good photographer and there is already a picture of it.  Highly recommend this salad!  

For dinner, I had the tagliatelle bolognese and it did not disappoint.  They make their pasta in house so it has that fresh egginess with the slightly chewy consistency that I love.  The sauce was a lovely and not-too-heavy meat sauce that hugged the noodles nicely.  I ate my fill and took enough home for another meal.  

I was too full for dessert, and all of their desserts were dairy based so nothing demanded to be eaten.

To top it all off, our server Tom was fantastic and they were playing some really nice Frank Sinatra music.  

I just couldn't go five stars because of the dining room set up.  The tables are awkwardly placed and so close together that my dining companion was treated to a graphic description of dental implants before I arrived.

Occasion:  UYE

It feels weird to give this place 5 stars, but after eating here over two weeks ago I can't stop thinking about their food so...

Thanks to Steven B for introducing me to this place I can't stop thinking about that's over an hours drive from my house and a 45 minute wait around dinner time.  Why can't they be in Chesterfield?! (Don't answer that.  I know.)

Anyway, delicious crispy-edged burgers and 'Merican! cheese on yummy buns.  I didn't get one of the fancy named ones - mine was just 2 burgers, cheese, ketchup, pickles.  We decided to get an order of RHR fries and an order of regular fries so we could mix them if the RHR were too spicy for me.  Sounded great, but then I hogged the RHR fries and husband was left with plain.   It's a good thing he loves me:)

As an aside, I also witnessed some odd-but-great customer service while I was there.  Not my story but it's worth reading in the other reviews and definitely enhanced my experience.

I'll be back soon, hopefully!

Tampa Bay's hidden Cuban gem - Cuban Foodies! I can definitely be a tough critic when it comes to Cuban food, my parents are Cuban after all. I was pleasantly surprised by the quality and authenticity Cuban Foodies delivers. 
Hubby and I stopped in for the first time over a year ago and greatly enjoyed their food. We have also picked up dinner a few times during the pandemic. One time, I called in an order about 15 minutes prior to closing time on a Sunday evening. I explained that I lived about 20-25 minutes away yet they still took my order and happily waited for me to arrive. That is the type of service you don't see very often. I was taken back by that gesture and thanked them for waiting on me. Everything was fresh and just as great as it always is despite being the last order of the evening. 
Must try appetizers include yuca frita and cro-k-tas. The cilantro sauce is superb!
The lechon asado is very tasty, classic flavors and good size portions. Hubby loves their ropa vieja, only second to my grandmothers recipe. I also really enjoy the masas de puerco. Their rice is always cooked perfectly and their beans are seasoned well. They serve only the best Cuban bread, too. 
Cuban Foodies has quickly become one of favs!

I couldn't gift Five Guys with a better compliment, review or glowing recommendation than the following tale.

My husband is an east coast boy. I am a west coast girl.  Our battles over west coast (the BEST coast) and east coast (the LEAST coast) at times reach Tupac-Biggie proportions. All in good fun of course (like, no one has been shot yet).  That being said, maybe the only reason we are still married is because I have never once claimed that the west coast darling In-N-Out Burger is superior to the east coast beloved Five Guys Burgers and Fries.  And I've never said such a thing because, well, it isn't true. 

One of the first places my spouse dragged me to in his home state of Maryland was Five Guys - as he fondly recalled how he remembered the days (back in them there late 90s) when Five Guys was a three location operation in DC.  I can see him telling this story (in his late 90s) to our grandchildren....because that's how much he loves Five Guys.

So when he found out they were opening a restaurant in Tucson, AZ he all but stalked the place until they swung wide the front doors, taking his first chance to patronize the new digs just as soon as he could - which just happened to be two hours after he'd had SURGERY.  

And that, friends and neighbors, is devotion.  A guy that went directly from the OR at UPH to the discarded peanut shell strewn floor of Five Guys.

And, my personal opinion?  The Tucson version of FG burgers were even better than the ones I'd had on their precious east coast.  Must be that magical west coast touch.

He rented the rooftop of a restaurant out for our wedding anniversary.
Smartest man alive. He won't have to make another romantic gesture for YEARS.

The following is his review.  
Guest Yelper: Scott D. 
*************************
Agustin Kitchen helped me make a dream come true.  When I was a teenager, and first planned romantic ideas for whoever I had a crush on at the time, I came up with a vision.  One day, when I had met that really special gal, I would surprise her with a rooftop dinner for just the two of us.  

Several weeks ago, with my sixth wedding anniversary approaching, I decided I wanted to finally make that dream a reality.  That really special gal was here, now, as my beloved wife.  So I went in search of options and found Agustin Kitchen.  I called to inquire about rooftop dining and was informed that it's generally reserved for large groups.  I asked if they could make an exception, due to the special occasion,  and was put in touch with Ryan Clark, their head chef.  Ryan graciously entertained my idea and put me in touch with his manager, John Silverman.  

John was an amazing help while planning this surprise gourmet dinner.  As he went over menu choices, he was both very accommodating of my ideas and helpful with suggestions to make it even better. I made reservations for sunset, so my wife and I could enjoy the colors and beauty of the sun's last rays that evening, then dine by candlelight under the stars.  John and Ryan applied some of their own ideas to enhance the evening.  For instance, while I just planned for wine, appetizers, salad and entrees, they put together a six-course meal to correspond with our anniversary.  And while this included the menu choices I had selected, some of the items were quite a surprise.  

When we arrived, we were quite taken with the building and the ground floor of the restaurant.  We talked to Anna, the hostess, who I had spoken with on the phone several times during the course of my planning.  She was kind and helpful; a real pleasure to deal with.  She introduced us to John, who led us up to the rooftop patio.  There was a small table set with our dinnerware, flowers, and a bucket of chilled water.  The sun was starting its descent.  I was happy with it all, and my wife was almost giddy with excitement.
  
Then the food began.  Oh my goodness!  Everything ranged from great to amazing!  Every course, each dish, was delicious, full of rich flavors and a delight to the senses.  The first course was a chef's surprise carrot-dish that was a great start to whetting our appetites. My wife loves pesto.  I like it, but it's not my favorite.  The pesto they served, made from carrot greens, bowled us over!  We had varied spread jars that allowed us to sample four different delights.  The salad choice was a tough decision during menu planning, as all of the options sounded wonderful.  To keep it simple, I went with their 'simple salad'.  Well, let me tell you, what they termed "simple" was one of the best salads we've ever had.  It made me want to go back to try their more robust salad options. 

I decided I would plan for two different entrees my wife would like, so she could decide which one she wanted once they were served. We're both big salmon fans and Agustin Kitchen's version was quite delicious. However, the star dish of the evening was the Vermont butter poached chicken breast, which was simply the best chicken dish I've ever had in four decades of eating! I felt decadent with each mouth-watering bite!  This was some serious dining.  

I didn't plan for dessert, as I figured we would be pretty full at that point of the evening.  John insisted, and how could we refuse?  We both decided on the rhubarb & pineapple crumble.  It was served with candles and chocolate sauce drizzled into letters wishing us a happy anniversary; another pleasant surprise.  How was the dessert, you may ask?  Pure 100% delicious awesomeness!  My only regret is that I was so full from all the other amazing food, I could barely finish it.  

Two other points should be noted.  I'm not a drinker, but I randomly chose a wine for my wife of the three kinds of cabernet they offer.  Though I generally dislike the taste of alcohol, this wine was actually pretty good, so kudos to their selection. 
Seriously, whether fine dining is your staple for outings, or you just want to up your game for a special occasion, you won't be disappointed.  Many hearty thanks to Ryan, John, Anna and all of the crew at Agustin Kitchen!  Not only did you help me realize a life-long vision of a romantic dinner with my wife, but you did it with friendly service, a wonderful setting, a to-die-for culinary experience, and class all around.

-Scott. D.

I have been sitting here for 25 minutes and my server is nowhere to be found. I thought this would be an excellent time to write my review. 

I got to the restaurant and asked to be seated outside. The hostess kept me waiting for 3-4 minutes while she sat a few other people that came in after me. 

Once I got sat, I was greeted by my server who then took my drink order. He came back with a glass of water and bread about 3-4 minutes later but said my my drink hasn't been made (I ordered a glass of champagne) by the bar. I ordered 1/2 dz oysters and Coastal Seafood Pasta with roasted red pepper sauce instead of garlic & olive oil. 

Timing: oysters came. With my champagne. With my dinner salad. All together. At the same time. 
Pasta came once I was through with the oysters but not quite with the salad. 

Food: the first three ingredients listed on coastal seafood pasta on the menu are as follows: shrimp, scallops, mussels. This is how much of each was in my pasta- Shrimp: ZERO Scallops: 2 (1/2 inch in diameter. Tiny little things) Mussels: 4 mussels and 1 empty shell. The pasta did not come with the roasted red pepper sauce as I asked and confirmed with the server that this is something the kitchen can do. I'd like to go back to the two scallops I had in my dish- I can only describe the texture as this: it tasted as if the scallops had been frozen and thawed several times, then overlooked in a microwave. I could not eat either of the two small scallops. 

I would have brought it to someone's attention. But here I am... I have been finished with my pound of angel hair pasta in olive oil with no substance for more than 25 minutes and my server is MIA. 

The other reviews really are quite true. You don't get the service and quality for what you pay. 

As a Landry's select member, I have never experienced such awful service and eaten such awful dishes in my life. Shame on you.

So deceiving! The whole Taco Bus thing is actually a prop that's in the front of the restaurant where you place your order and the signs like "broken English perfectly spoken" made me assume I was going to get some authentic tacos. Nope, not even . . . 

My sister and I both ordered 2 plates that included 4 different types of tacos: carnitas, carne adada, pescado and cochinitas pibil with beans and rice. It was pretty dead so we were surprised that it took longer than expected for our food to come out and we were even more disappointed when we tasted the food. Meat was overcooked - dry & hard. Beans and rice were bland. And, I've never had cabbage put on all tacos before, so weird. 

We left still hungry - such a waste of time & money. Now we know to pass up this place!

The lemon orzo soup is a must try. So much flavor. Gyro was fresh and good but not the best I've ever had.  I would have liked more meat in it and less of the large chunks of tomato. The bill was a little high over all but we did like the place and would give it another try sometime. We went for lunch so it was not packed.

Lloyd is quickly becoming one of my favorite places to hang out in Fishtown. I have had a few of their appetizers and have also been one night for a whiskey and pork pairing event featuring Brooklyn Brewery, but mainly I come to drink and enjoy the atmosphere. Their customer service is top-notch. Whenever I walk in, no matter how busy the place is, someone seemingly appears from nowhere to seat me, whether at a table or at the bar. Once seated, I never have to wait long for another drink or even a refill on my water.

I'm more of a beer drinker myself and would love it if they had a more expansive draft list to choose from, but I always find something I like in what they do have. My partner is a whiskey drinker so he's never lacking in choices here. They also know their stuff when it comes to cocktails and you can tell they take pains to make sure a drink is made correctly.

We usually show up on the later side of things and Lloyd can get somewhat crowded on weekend nights, but I've always been comfortable no matter the size of the crowd. The atmosphere is what puts Lloyd over the top for me; I love the music and the classy, understated decor. Some of the other whiskey bars in the city can be a little over the top for my taste. Lloyd gets it right in my opinion.

Alright, first of all, I don't mean to be rude to the other reviewer who gave this place 1 star, but it's completely unwarranted. These employees have been hard at work ALL day. My friend and I arrived at 2:45pm and it was PACKED. A huge sea of people. Took us 25 minutes to order and over an hour and a half to get our ice cream. We told the staff we were gonna head out to St. Roch's after waiting for nearly half an hour and decided to just go down the street to grab a couple snacks and come back when we were done. They were super cool and accommodating and said that we were welcome to come back and grab our desserts later and that they'd keep our place line. 

So my friend and I did just that. We came back to see the people in front of us pretty close to getting what they ordered. At no point in time was anyone ever idle or not being helpful. There are only three trays available to make the rolled ice cream, and every order takes at least 5 minutes to make and roll into a cup. I couldn't get anyone's name, but the entire staff was very sweet and answered all my questions and even when I asked for a sample during their rush, they remained accommodating and allowed me a small snowball sample. Everyone was smiling and hard at work.

As for them running out of ice cream, there is only so much product you can put into storage or a refrigerator. I'm sure at one point, they were quoting a two hour wait time which in itself already shows how incredibly busy they were. If they're running out of product, it only means that hundreds of other people came through the door before you did. First come, first serve.

Now that my mini rant is over, the rolled ice cream I had was great. I hear that after grand opening, their ice cream will be $6.99 with unlimited toppings which is a GREAT deal as you get quite a large serving of ice cream. I got Sweet&Salty (great if you like salted caramel) with bananas and butterfinger crumbles on top and it was DELICIOUS. My friend got the Cookie Monster with chocolate drizzle which was also great. Can't wait to try their My Thai flavor whenever that's available.

All in all, the staff did the best to their ability. The food was great. Service (though obviously slow because of the sheer volume of customers) was very sweet and extremely accommodating. I'll definitely be back (when it's died down a bit) to try the other flavors. (:

Keeping it simple is often the key to brilliance, and with a short focussed menu of 5 apps, 6 different kinds of noodle dishes, and a few et ceteras (hmm...scrapple in ramen!?!?!?), all packaged in a cool space with lots of counter seating and a giant 'Eat More Noodles' mural as backdrop, Cheu accomplishes this goal.

This is undoubtedly one of the most highly anticipated openings of 2013, a 'noodle bar' from partners Chef Ben Puchowitz (of Matyson fame, one of our favorite BYOBs) and his buddy Shawn Darragh.  Their pop-ups last year were apparently a smash success, with a line down the street, so we made a point of stopping by Cheu early on opening day to see what the excitement was all about.

We arrived exactly at opening (3PM), and were immediately seated at the counter with a few others (there are also several tables, for  total of ~30 seats).  It was mostly full by the time we left, but there was rarely a line, and we left before the dinner rush.

Between the two of us, we tried (see photos):

~Complementary spiced crumbled instant ramen, fairly spicy, and something David Chang would appreciate (if you watched 'In the Mind of a Chef' on PBS).

~Garlic black wings with shishito peppers ($8/4)--Actually we got 5, 3 drumettes and 2 wingettes, which were crispy, meaty, with a light dose of a sticky sweet soy sauce, and some mildly spicy peppers.  My favorite dish, I could make a meal out of these.  KILLER!

~Pork belly and hamburger buns ($7/2)--We could choose any combination from 3 different buns (including the mung bean that we didn't try).  These are tiny two-biters that look smaller than the photos I've seen online, but are very tasty.  The Angus beef was topped with Wisconsin cheddar and house-made pickles.  The pork belly was also topped with pickles.  The buns are a bit strange, a bit like tiny English muffins, if that makes any sense, toasted in a skillet.  My favorite was the pork belly, which like the pork with ramen below was melt-in-your mouth.

~Pork belly with house-made ramen noodles, egg, sea beans, greens ($12)--A very very intense broth (I suspect borderline too intense for some), but overall a very good dish.  The ramen was perfectly al dente and the egg appeared to be soft poached.  A good sized bowl, but not huge.  I added in some of the pho fixin's below.

~Duck pho with foie gras meatballs, turnips, fixin's--I only tried a little of this, but it seemed like the pho was pretty similar to the ramen above.  Thinly sliced, very tender duck, and melt-in-your mouth meatballs, although I can't say I got any foie flavor.  The broth is much milder than than the pork belly's above.  Comes with the usual pho accompaniments of basil and mung beans, lime, and also pickled white radish (I think).  Of the two noodle dishes, I think I preferred the lighter broth of the duck pho.

Cheu's mish-mass of Chef Benny's whatever "I think tastes best" manages to avoid the ongoing 'Raman Wars', where ramen is stylistically divided into smaller and smaller subgroups and aficionados endlessly (and nonsensically) argue about which ramen shop more is more authentic.  Come on guys, who cares if it is 'authentic', if it tastes good?  And Cheu's noodles definitely taste great!

Or maybe Cheu defines a new subgroup: 'Philly Style' ramen!

[Speaking of 'Raman Wars', to reviewer #3, Ron N, who is apparently an expert on what is and is not ramen, that "asparagus" you didn't like is actually sea beans.  But it does kinda look like asparagus, which would be really weird, ramen or not.]

Currently BYOB (we brought some Guinness), with sodas, etc available, but planning to get a liquor license (big orange placard on the door).  Service was quick, friendly and efficient, with Shawn greeting customers at the front.  Parking is fairly easy in a few local lots.

Some nice photos and background from Zagat:

http://blog.zagat.com/2013/03/sneak-preview-cheu-noodle-bar.html

Cilantro!

There's some great spots opening up in Philly recently, and I'd place HIGH STEET ON MARKET (references the old-time Philly name for Market St) right up there with Kevin Sbraga's The Fat Ham for providing a unique combination of casual, sophisticated, and affordable dining.

I made my first visit to HSoM last night with Zareen S, who beat me to the punch with her detailed Yelp review:

http://www.yelp.com/biz/high-street-on-market-philadelphia#hrid:Di4gWH1ZDZ1GyIXhB0REsA

However, I will say that this was an excellent, even exciting meal.  We had the 8-course tasting menu, which was mostly served sharing style, and it was more than enough to fill us up (we ended up taking most of both plates of wagyu home), all for a bargain $45.  Yes, you read that right, $45.  One of the best, if not the best, tasting menu bargains in Philly.

My favorite courses were:
1) Mike's crispy kale chips, which sound trivial, but are completely amazing (and messy to eat).

2) Green tea garganelli with smoked duck ragu, the flavor of which would be a bit hard to describe if you didn't know what was in it (and a bit acidic too, which I loved).

3) Rabbit & maple chestnuts, which was a wonderfully complex medley of cauliflower, almost burnt Brussels sprouts, fruit and tender flavorful rabbit.

4) Black seaweed bucatini pasta, with weird little shaved lobster bottarga that I first thought was carrot shavings.  All their pasta is made fresh in-house daily.

5) Of the two desserts, I particularly like the sticky toffee pudding made with dates and served with ice cream.

Good cocktails, an unusual short wine list (for example, they have a rare bottling by Frank Cornelissen, the crazy man of Mt. Etna), and also a back passage to Fork next door (so we stopped by their bar afterwards, which stays open later).

Great space, although a bit noisy even though it wasn't very crowded on a snowy night.  Good friendly service, and they even comped us a couple of drinks (I think just because we were having such a good time).

They also serve breakfast/brunch/lunch, so it's not just for dinner, and their sandwiches sound (and look) killer:

https://vine.co/v/hi2QDFQ7a2M

OpenTable reservations.  Convenient $6.50 validated parking in the Ritz at the Bourse movie theatre a block away.

This place is as good as its rating says- 
I couldnt have been more impressed- and honestly, i cant wait to try more things on the menu! 
The parking-- -ugh, thats a different story. 
We had to park down the block on the side of the building- and they are doing construction RIGHT in front of the building- so that was annoying.
I couldnt go here and NOT get the corn nuggets- and yes, they were super! 
Very yummy!- 
I was suprised that we were the only ones in the place for lunch--
a couple people trickled in half through our meal- but we had the whole place to ourselves for a while. 
I ordered the cajun gyro--- it came in a small pan!--how cute! 
and it was really reallly good! everything was fresh- and there was TONS of meat on there!--- good job! 
Honey ordered the Phat Albert- and said it was one of the best burgers he's had-
but boy were we stuffed!!!!! 
The menu is so unique- and so many things to try! 
I was definitely in a food coma and I'm not complaining! 
i cant wait to return to try something else!

After years of Corner Bistro being on my "bookmark" list. 
My hubs and I FINALLY made it. 
I was so excited to finally try CORNER BISTRO....
The outside is unassuming, cute little patio- and a bar next door. 
You walk in- its quaint .
A few tables, and a bar. Not one that you can sit at. 
We started off with toasted ravioli-- and I will admit- they were really really good! 
Some of the best I've had. 
Then we ordered the wings and fries..
Those were NOT chicken wings- pigeon wings maybe, but not chicken wings.
Those were by far the SMALLEST wings I have ever seen in my entire life.
And my husband and I eat a lot of wings.
The flavor was good, but they were a tad spicy for being regular wings.
The fries were great too. I cant complain there. 
My husband isn't too excited to go back, he was deeply disappointed in the wings.
Next time, I'll order the pizza.

Why am I the only person who doesn't love this place?! I mean, it's fine- it's a dueling piano bar like you could find in ANY city around the U.S. We have very similar one in Denver, where I live. I do have to concede that the piano players are very talented, and we did have fun (I was with a big group and other members of the crew were keen on going), but I just feel like there's nothing authentic about this place. New Orleans has some of the best music in the country and maybe the world; why not spend your time enjoying the jazz that The Big Easy is known for, or even some good blues rather than drunkenly belting cover songs? Also, the drinks! YUCK! Their famous hurricane is made from overly sugary powder, not a mix of fresh juices like elsewhere. Also, beware the glass scam. Drinks are very pricey, but you get to keep the glass (which very few people seem to realize). If you choose not to keep the glass, you can walk it up to the bar and get a few bucks back, but it's a pain in the butt. I did opt to take my glass, but it totally got broken somewhere during the rest of my evening adventures. Most people just pay the hefty price and leave the glass on the table.

Ultimately, this place is a NO on my list. I highly recommend seeking more quintessentially NOLA experiences.

One of the reasons my husband and I regularly visit NOLA is to eat- there's no food scene quite like the one in The Crescent City, and there are many fine restaurants. That being said, it's a BIG deal when I say a meal is one of the best I've had; R'evolution was just that. We will literally dream of the chargrilled oysters, crab beignets, and the Sheep Ricotta Gnocchi with Lobster. Oh, the creamy, lemony, goodness with full claws of lovely, meaty lobster. We made a last minute Thursday night reservation which meant we were seated at the communal chef's table. This was actually quite the treat as watching what came from the kitchen only confirmed our assessment that THIS is one of the finest dining establishments in town. Service was great, cocktails were wonderful. Step up your attire to fit in the trendy scene here; more men were in sport coats then not. A meal here is a splurge for sure, but worth every cent. This restaurant will be top of mind for me whenever recommending New Orleans food.

Dat Dog is a fixture on Frenchman Street, and I can't believe that last night was my first time venturing in! There's a decent bar both downstairs and up, and an extensive hot Dog menu featuring some adventurous dogs and sausages for those looking for sustenance before and after their NOLA debauchery. Dogs and fries are tasty, but a little expensive, and considering that the place wasn't busy yet, took an awful long time to receive. I had the Guinness Dog and my hubby had the Son of a Saint, and though one was alligator, they tasted more alike then different (but again, still yummy!). Definitely get the fries- those are super good! The upstairs patio overlooking the insanity below would be a fun place to sit if you can snag a table. Definitely keep this place in mind for good drinking food, as it does certainly hit the spot and soaks up some of the booze.

Took the family here to celebrate  the achievements of my two teenage sons. We decided to go out to brunch to experience NaBrasa first and then move onto a dinner reservation. And I'm SOOO glad we made that choice! 

Brunch here is UNBELIEVABLE!  And I'm NOT a fan of buffet style meals at all! 

Here, you get 9 out of the 14 meats that are served at dinner and they also serve a full buffet included lobster , other fresh seafood, I think we had muscles, a huge salad bar including imported  cheeses  and Italian meats and olives. Of course you can get eggs, waffles and regular breakfast fare. But you must save room for the sweet table!  A chocolate fountain so high even my 15 year old son was in awe! 

There's plenty of on-site parking and the restaurant is centrally located just off route 611 and the PA turnpike. Little pricy; However , when you consider all that you are eating, it's worth it!

Coffee is decent muffins are great and everything else is amazing

* my complaint is with the Cycling idiots out front first off you have to hurdle the sea of bicycles to get to the front door and in the process you realize none of the cyclists order anything from Le Buzz. so they just sit out front and crowd up the place. Secondly be prepared to receive major attitude here not from the staff but customers they are rude and dont clean up the messes they make personally this place is great around 10:30 when all the spandex fairies have returned to their retirement communities and Subaru station wagons.

with that being said they are like a crew of spandex wearing coffee drinking shaved bikers that over run this place i think even the staff are overwhelmed .  Sorry
 le buzz get a bike rack or put up signs so people dont trip

We went here on a Sunday afternoon. Sat outside. Not very crowded. There were 3 adults and 2 kids in our party. 
We had a few drinks to start which came out pretty quickly and were really good. 

Our server was very friendly and helpful with recommendations. 

Then came the wait for or meals. Unbelievable. Luckily we hadn't seen our friends for a while so we were caught up in conversation and the kids went to play on the little beach. 

We ordered fish tacos, chicken nuggets, kids burger, salad, and grouper sandwich. We waited an hour and a half! Good god.  I know. You're thinking "why wouldn't you leave after waiting so long?"  We had a long day, we're tired and kept thinking the food will come out soon. The server came over to us several times to tell us it would be a few more minutes. 

Sandwich and tacos were cold. The server offered to get in another but we declined, thinking  it would take too long. He brought one anyway in 2 minutes. Clearly he had just taken someone else's order from the line. After the food came out he told us that there was nothing he could do for us. Not comp anything or buy us a drink. "It's just how it goes" he said. That's a pretty bad way to cater to patrons. 

If it weren't for enjoying our friends company, we would have up and left...

Meh. Overpriced hotel, uncomfortable beds, bathroom was a little gross. 
Service was good. Great people work here and are very nice and helpful. 
We can for an event and the chairs were DIRTY in the restaurant area. 

Food is ok. Very average.

Meh. This place was really empty on a week night, so it was somewhat awkward to be sitting at the bar by ourselves while the bartender was never less than 2 feet away and pretending (really hard) to be busy. Despite that, the drinks and food were awesome! We had the basil fragola martini and paper plane, as well as the piquillo poppers. It was quite pricey at $40 for 2 drinks and an app, so it's not somewhere we will be going regularly.

We were on the hunt for some great BBQ on Saturday and naturally went the one place that is known for great BBQ. Unfortunately the line was out the door and half way around the block when I remembered about Bogarts and we promptly made our way there. 

I think just about everybody in our party had ribs, and we had a few other secondary meats and sides. The ribs were great, perhaps not as good as Pappy's, but that is in no way a diss on Bogarts, quite the opposite actually. The dry rub on the ribs was perfect and I found that they did not need any additional sauce. I had the beef brisket along with a half slab of ribs and the brisket was amazing. I'm used to the brisket being sliced thicker, but Bogart's is sliced pretty thin and incredibly tender. Add a little BBQ sauce to it and it was perfect. I'm not sure I've had better brisket, but if I have it's been a really long time. 

For my two sides I had the deviled egg potato salad and the baked beans. I really liked the potato salad and the baked beans had generous bits of meat and a little kick to them. I left licking my lips and completely full. I did have the opportunity to sample the pulled pork sandwich and it was quite tasty as well. As a side note, they serve Billy Goat potato chips, so they get bonus points for that alone. 

i was initially saddened that Pappy's was too busy, but that sadness disappeared with the first bite I took at Bogart's. I will not hesitate to venture on back to Bogart's the next time I have a craving for great BBQ!

Oh. My. Gosh. This place is beyond exciting!!! I walked in after taking my son to the children's museum and when I tell you there are so many choices here it's crazy, there are so many choices here it's crazy!!!!! Lol 

12 different flavored cupcakes and the buck doesn't stop there. They have thrown my idea of what a cupcake was completely out of the window! Each cupcake has a different theme, the Oreo cupcake is a chocolate cupcake with Oreo cream frosting; the strawberry shortcake cupcake is a strawberry cupcake filled with live flowing REAL strawberry filling and a light and creamy gonachè   (Sp?) frosting. 

Not only do they have cupcakes, they have mini macaroons, cheesecake bites, chocolate dipped delights, coffee. And the best part is everything is baked here fresh!!! The staff is very friendly and helpful. Super cute boutique looking store, a few tables inside and out so you can meet with people and enjoy all they have to offer!! 

This place has it all, and they design wedding cakes, birthday cakes, cupcakes. I mean it's got a little bit of it all. And with the friendly staff you're sure to make the right choice! Def. Going to continue stopping in to see what new things I can try next!!! (& I'll be telling all my friends)

my experience was ok.....,
the italian hoagie was ok.....
the gentleman who was making it was very  slow.... the lettuce was 2 thick... & my chicken cheese steak was done before the hoagie..... hoagie's r my specialty....& this italian hoagie was just ok........service was excellent.......THE CARROT CAKE WAS 
AMAZING....

i'm available for hoagie's.......just saying....

Worst. Customer. Service. EVER! 
Showed up to the theater to find a huge line in the lobby. Tried the ticketing machines but they didn't give me the option to pick up my tickets so I got in line. Everyone seemed shocked at the length of the line and nobody had experienced this type of wait in the past. After waiting in line for 30 minutes we were told that the tickets we purchased a week ago we're not longer valid. They would instead exchange our tickets for a showing 2 hours later. My kids are too young to be in a theater at 10 pm. 

My son was devastated. He wore his stormtrooper outfit and was ready to enjoy Star Wars for his birthday. It was not to be. I was told I could get a refund if I didn't want to wait around for 2 hours but that was the best they could do. As my son was crying outside my daughter noticed that a sign indicating the theater was booked for a private event. When she brought this to my attention I asked to speak with the manager. She came over with an attitude and just wanted to make me go away. She blamed the issue on a problem with their "system" and said it want their fault. I let her know that it's their system so it is their fault. Then I asked if we were really bumped because the booked a private party instead of honoring our reservations. Her reply was straight and to the point, "the party paid over $1,000!"  She made it clear that money talks and that sale was worth more than loyal customers. Profit over customer service should be their motto. 

Unbelievable experience. It's only a matter of time before they disappear with this approach to business.

I may have to revisit this place at sometime in the future because I was so sad leaving this place. I really really wanted to like this place. I had extremely high expectations coming into this restaurant and I was super excited to try the ramen here. All the pictures and reviews painted such a heavenly picture of a good bowl of ramen in my head.

I initially heard about this place while I was wine tasting with my cousin, and I thought it would have been the perfect place to end the night with. We had been drinking the whole afternoon and ramen seemed like the hardy meal I needed to sober up.

I ordered the not so typical tonkotsu ramen, because, who doesn't like ramen that has the expected thick creamy pork broth that comes from simmering pork and pork fat. 

What I got was a dish with a pretty tasty slow braised pork belly (best part -- it actually added a star), no bamboo shoots, tons of noodles (I like), and a very watery broth. The broooooth maaaan. It killed it for me. It needed something. Maybe a seasoning packet from top ramen haha. I'm kidding, but it was definately lacking something. 

Hey, I guess that's what happens when you order the "not so typical" tonkotsu ramen. I'm sure there must be other things on the menu that are great because that pork belly on the ramen was actually really good. I would still encourage people to come here, but just try something besides the ramen and I'm sure you'll have a much better experience then me.

TLDR: Give this place 3 months to get their stuff together because they are a pretty hot mess.

What a beautiful place!  
The appetizer Chicken Flautas were very very good.
That's it. That's all I got. 
Three words.. very small margaritas.

So many people in this area have been waiting for one of the downtown places to branch out West of 270 and did we bury these guys in business!  Problem is they were not ready for it and it shows. There are a few other issues also.

Thank goodness for OpenTable because if I had to wait for this dinner we would never come back. It had a strong start but got progressively worse.
