The order was taken pretty quickly, the yummy appetizer came out in a decent amount of time, the margarita also, although sadly small. It is the smallest margarita I have been served in a restaurant.  To top it off the guacamole was served on a bed of lettuce which is a really unexpected chinsy thing to do in a restaurant that looks this great. Insult to injury are the very very thin extra greasy chips that break instantly when trying to scoop the guacamole as the lettuce acts like guacamole armor. You shall not...dip! Chip sadness.

Now we wait.. 40 minutes for our food. Sigh.

Shrimp tacos and Carne Asada Fajitas .

The shrimp tacos normally come with mango but I asked to skip that so the street tacos came with cabbage and shrimp. SO dry. No moisture. The soft tortilla wraps were stuck together, with cold spots between the double and triple layered dry cabbage and shrimp tacos. Yes. But there is more taco sadness. The shrimp smelled old or overly fishy. All those who cook know what I mean. I abandoned those sickly shrimp and the 4 extra, sad, cold spotted tortillas. 

My husband's Fajitas were ok. 

Our waiter was gracious but buried in tables.

A manager was running around yelling very loudly at all her staff(?) as she was carrying out food.. "... THIS WHOLE RESTAURANT.. "  RAWR etc... storming off.

Do I want to go back? Nope. But I want to give this place another shot. They are simply not prepared. The appetizer was very good and the patio is SO pretty!  I hope they get their act together because it would be a perfect date night or place to bring a group of friends! It is just a gorgeous patio! Parking is easy too, plenty of it.

Maybe have wine and an appetizer, after you make your reservations with OpenTable. If you live out here, do the immediate above with a group of friends but if you want a meal definitely wait a few months. It is a not so hot mess. We are rooting for you guys! We'll see you in a few months.

We attempted to come on a Saturday night but it was a half hour wait. It was our fault because they use Opentable and we should have planned. (***EDIT They don't have Opentable any more. They use the Tock reservation app. Yeah it was new to me too.***)
Tuesday we came back and there is no wait but the place is still pretty full.

Miso soup: It was a very good big tasty bowlful.
Salad: I love the ginger dressing and it was a decent size salad.  Ask for a knife because it is not chopped up. (Read this as I made a mess because I thought I would be fine. Lol)
Sushi: We always get a California roll to split and it was good.
Yellow fin, eel, a whitefish that was listed as a special... All sushi was very good.

The waiter was a little over sat but he made it through. The hostess over saturates the welcome but it is still an attempt to be gracious and nice. 

TLDR. Make reservations through Open Table, save time. Very good sushi. We'll be back.

Drinks can be hit or okay, but I love their combo of the QQ Milk Tea - boba, grass jelly, and lychee jelly. You definitely can't go wrong with any of the milk teas, and the bobas are chewy. Their puff waffle with filling are okay, a good snack if you're hungry but nothing to write home about. I tried the recent limited edition strawberry drinks with the strawberry boba - definitely not worth it. The strawberry bobas tasted plain, not strawberry-like, and wasn't sweet. Definitely better off with the regular boba

On a Friday night, perhaps because it was also Full Moon Festival, this place was crowded! Luckily, it was easy for me to make a reservation the day of for a large party. It did take us a bit to get seated and even longer (45min or so) for our food to arrive, but the manager came by to apologize for the wait and gave us a discount on our meal. 

As for our food, I liked that it's very chinese, as in they have lots of dry pot dishes and use dried peppers and peppercorns. I got the Sour and Spicy Shredded Potatoes, which was decent. Compared to other places I've had this at, it was too salty and not enough vinegar; however, otherwise it was a tad spicy and the potatoes were luckily cooked perfectly. My friends, on the other hand, really enjoyed their food! This includes the beef and broccoli, the stir fried noodles, and the dry pots. Food is on the oilier side, but that's just how this style of food is. 

Another major + to this place is that they have a good amount of vegetarian dishes! 

This place also has boba, and I got the Original Bubble Tea and my friends got the Brown Sugar Milk. The Original Bubble Tea has a mild herbally flavor, but the boba is a bit too small and soft. The Brown Sugar Milk tasted better, and just perfect in sweetness too. However, it's a bit expensive for the smaller size. $4.50 for Original bubble tea and $5.50 for the brown sugar milk. 

Parking: Plenty in the shared parking structure in the back.

Ok stop the madness!!  Why are people so obsessed with this place?  Because it's a secret "club"? Ok ok, it's fun to pour yourself a cup of "free" coffee while you wait, but good luck getting to the coffee station while your bumping into and bouncing off of everyone on your way there.

It's your basic breakfast food. I mean, it's good and the portions are pretty large, but I don't leave feeling the immense amount of love everyone else seems to.

The biggest issue is that it is always soo packed.  We used to go just because we lacked a breakfast place and it was so close, but so many times we have left and went to Dunkin donuts because of the ridiculous wait time.

Geeez, I kinda feel terrible that I didn't enjoy my lunch here! 

Had the pulled pork sandwich on the cheddar waffles. In my book, it's not a sandwich if you can't pick it up - Pulled pork should be soft and moist, this was dry and tough and FULL of fatty chunks - the waffles had NO flavor at all. I would not get it again.

Side of blue cheese coleslaw - great idea, terrible execution. It was a runny, bland mess of shredded cabbage with chunks of cheese in it.

I'm not cheap, I love nice places and new things... But $5 for an ice tea or lemonade and no refills? It needs posted on the menu.

Next, I'm having a late lunch, there was one other person in the place waiting on takeout, and the server was too busy talking to the eight other people working to wait on the only table she had. Unacceptable. Then some shady looking characters came in (dirty undershirts and shorts) to talk to their "boy" working in the kitchen. They were all still loitering in the parking lot when I left 30 minutes later. Makes me concerned about who they let in their kitchen... I certainly wouldn't let non staff in my kitchen.

Maybe they were just having an off day?

$12 for a veggie sub that wasn't very good and made me sick. They don't crisp up the outside of the bread and sandwich was laden in oil so it was a soggy mess. Waitress at the bar wasn't very friendly either. I felt unwanted there. Would not go back.

Idyllic ambiance, superb staff and management, and a romantic suffusion of fairytale enchantment in an illustriously intimate establishment. I can envision Belle coaxing the beast out his majesty's castle to have a public dining experience here. 

The complimentary bread was stellar and had a perfectly crisp crust paired with a light as air fluffy interior, smartly paired well with the moderately soft fragrantly salted butter.

Our cocktails were concocted with sophistication, jeweled and enameled, the Parisian Blonde cocktail was a harmonious saccharine sweet with a scintilla of swirling tart while the redolent French Kiss oozed a sparkling sorbonnical grace. 

The pate consisted of beef, lamb, and fois gras with pistachio and cranberry fusion. My partner had a taste and didn't mind it, but I felt like it needed to be less acerbic or astringent all around and include ingredients that harmonize instead of clashing. I would have been happier with a chicken liver and grounded pork mix with pepper and garlic. I saw other patrons fall in love with this dish so my reaction is as a result of where my personal tastes are geared, however, the pate tends to change by the day so I must retry the dish sometime. 

My cheese board consisted of opulent and delectable sheep milk's cheeses, all especially addicting and my favorite cheese experience. The first was crumbly provencal but had multiplex layers of aromatic flavor and a sharp tang while the second was a cream enriched, buttery ultra rich with subtle nuttiness and served as a sublime mild spread; the third was a thickened creamy-dense earthy flavor with a moderate piquancy along with an undercurrent of sweetness. I was head over heels and kept begging for more. 

My partner revered in his french onion soup which reminded him of his home as well as the Hereford steak, which was hearty, satisfying, and a very traditional, simplistic taste he enjoyed. I personally do not love overly crispy or crunchy exterior on meats with little complex flavors or seasoning. That is simply my personal choice, however. 

Management was above and beyond, very affable to my needs and always checking up on us, and later brought us a complimentary easy to love crème brûlée for our anniversary as well as bakery fresh petite coconut macaroons and powdered marshmallows. Thank you for giving us a memorable anniversary.

Our waiter knocked over my phone onto the floor while trying to take the menus which made the night sour. He was trying to be attentive as he can, but we were sitting by the lounge area so he could not tend to us as fondly as his clients in the main dining room. There were times when he should have checked on us, but instead tended to other tables instead. I had to forget about any new orders to compliment my steak at this time and just eat how it was since the meat will grow cold, which was very disheartening. 

His tables were located in the back of the main dining room and our table was near the entrance. He had to sprint from one end of the restaurant to the other end which was highly inefficient. A waiter or waitress closer to the lounge should have been assigned to us. 

I am understanding, but I feel the lounge area needs to be catered to more properly. I have a strong feeling if we sat in the main dining room, this would not have happened. The lounge area does get a cold draft from the doors opening and closing. I think repositioning or even renovating the entire lounge seating area would resolve this issue. 

The ambiance captures an eloquent magnetism festooned with the glamour and vintage feel of old Hollywood transcending the marriage of traditional and modern. Each dish is belly warming, filling, and suffuses one with a sensation of familiarity and elation. 

I ordered the 16oz medium well bone-in filet mignon, it had a pepper and salt finish with a very pink center. It was a little too pink and fall-of-the-bone tender for my taste, but still tasty, palate pleasing, and endlessly flooded my stomach with gustatory satisfaction. My major complaint was the lack of sauce offerings since I prefer my meat to be properly bathed in red wine, but the steak was still well consumed independently. 

The stuffed hash browns were flavorless, too buttery and thickly creamy with some oddly textured chunkiness in the center. We had to send it back. However, the french fries were simply insatiable. A deep golden brown with the perfect crisp on the outside and soft center sizzled and seasoned to gleaming perfection. The mashed potatoes were both smooth and velvety, creamy and pillowy and melted in your mouth amorously serenading your tongue with every bite. 

There was an incident where my partner and I left for the restroom and the staff cleared our table before the dessert came. 

Luckily, our waiter saved the day by apologizing, bringing new drinks, and came out with our desserts in no time. I replaced my butterscotch ice cream with vanilla ice cream instead which was not a problem. We also ordered the chocolate cake, which was devilishly good. 

Our dulcified treats were both deceptively simple yet gratifying which served as conceptual metaphor for the restaurant's historic ideology and execution to remain perennially classic, tasteful, and timeless. Their service, however, indubitably requires a revamping.

The ambiance was unimpressive and crowded as the seats were too close together that I can retell and recount the stories overheard by heart and my feel my partner's legs hitting mine with every movement. 

The complimentary bread was extremely over salted and vomit inducing. The mashed potatoes tasted like it was intermixed with expired oatmeal, rancid baby food, and three spoonfuls of thickened human mucus, a repugnant disgrace. The three cookie pan dessert is similar to asking my five year old cousin to make a cookie cake using her easy bake oven and then accidentally pouring glue or silly putty into the mix. 

The waiter did not offer to remake our dishes nor send the dishes back even though he told me he knew I disliked my food based on how little I consumed, the pinnacle of sheer greed, impertinence, and classlessness. 

Good God. I wanted to come back to try the rest of the menu, but now I would never revisit and endure the insufferably vicious onslaught to my stomach unless I was forced fed kicking and screeching to my purgatorial doom.

Ah, the infamous taqueria that doesn't even have a front door. You have to enter through a side door of the adjacent liquor store. It isn't even a restaurant space per se, it's like the separate room where La Tejana would keep its classy alcohol, if it sold any classy alcohol.

La Tejana is so authentic it doesn't even have a menu. I went in there, and the lady (in sweatpants, natch) asked me what I wanted. I replied that as far as food is concerned, I'd have to take a look at the menu. She said they didn't have a menu - and the way she said it was as if some restaurants don't have menus, and this just happens to be one of those restaurants. Meanwhile, I'm pretty sure this is the only restaurant that doesn't have a menu. I'm 30 years old, and I've never been to another restaurant that doesn't have a menu. Even the lowliest of suspect, organ meat-serving taquerias at least have that Office Depot whiteboard.

The lady said they had tacos (shocker), burritos, some other shit along those lines, or these dishes they had set out on a table, covered with saran wrap (there was a bit of a fly problem), like that one funnel cake they set out at a carnival to show you what a funnel cake looks like. There were these two young Mexican guys there getting their grub on, and one of them may have been the only person there who spoke a lick of English (he was shockingly proficient, actually). He pointed to this plate the other guy had and said it was very good, and I should try it. It did seem kinda weird to me that he was recommending it, and he wasn't eating it himself. But at that point it kinda felt like a challenge to me, like he was suggesting that I was too much of a gringo to eat something so bizarre-looking, or that I didn't have the $12 it cost in my pack. 

I had $20, for the record.

It was that weird fish dish you see on the menu at Mexican restaurants that looks like someone took a rather large but not particularly nice-looking fish, force-fed it a steady diet of kitchen garbage, foie gras-stylee, then shoved an M-80 up its ass, so that the kitchen garbage exploded out and onto the side of it. Essentially, it was a whole fish, of some undetermined, bottom-feeding variety, deep fried whole and stuffed with some ultra-spicy onion and green pepper concoction, served with the requisite not enough tortillas wrapped in foil paper + rice and beans. The rice was nothing to write home about. I felt like I could have made something better from a kit I've seen in the Mexican food aisle of Schnucks at Page and the Interbelt. I did appreciate the bit of "queso fresco" atop of the refried beans, which otherwise tasted like all of the other refried beans you've ever tasted, i.e. delicious.

But never mind the side dishes. The bulk of that $12 (which I'll admit is not easy for me to come by) went towards the fish. So, how was it? It was fucking delicious. After all, it was deep fried. There's no such thing as bad food that's deep fried. And you know how black people are about their/our fried fish. Biting into my Pescado, or whatever it was called, it occurred to me that the actual fish part of it wasn't altogether different from the fried fish you get in a happy box with the requisite white bread and a few slices of raw onion down in the, erm, less fortunate part of town. The difference here being that Mexicans, gully as they are, don't bother pulling the scales off, or the bones out, or anything like that. If it was cleaned at all, that probably took place at the grocery. Honestly, my concern was more with how difficult it was to eat. It tasted great, but it took a lot of work to pull out all of the tiny bones and various bits of fish anatomy (including - no bullshit - its eyballs).

Finally, and most importantly, I tried to order a beer with my meal, even though it was mad early (hey, it was a Saturday!), but I was informed that the beer was to-go only. I didn't get why I couldn't just buy it and enjoy it with my piranha tacos, if that's what I wanted to do with my beer. I guess they've had some problems with 5-0 trying to bust them for trying to serve alcohol when technically they're not supposed to. They may have thought I was 5-0. If one of their cousins came in their and ordered a beer, it probably wouldn't be an issue. Before I left, I took a look at their cooler to see if they had any 40s (which you don't see as often in the county), and wouldn't you know they did. I copped a 40 of Bud Light and seriously considered drinking it in the car on the way home, like the brothers used to do back in the day, but then I totally pussed. But then I saw a cop car perched on that grassy knoll approaching the Page Ave interchange, looking to eff someone in the a, and I felt at least semi-justified in my decision.

I never had a goal in life until I was informed, yesterday, that my uncle lives upstairs from this place, and therefore can go downstairs and eat expensive fried chicken whenever he feels like it.

He could probably even talk someone into bringing it upstairs.

I live around the corner from a Popeyes, but it's just not the same. The chicken is of course delicious, but it's not in my home. It's not as pricey, but you can probably gather, from the fact that I live near a Popeyes, that literally anything, to me, is pricey.

I wasn't picking up the tab at Juniper, so I had no problem going hog wild. As R. Kelly would say, I didn't see nothing wrong.

The half a fried chicken is a pretty good deal anyway. As my little brother helpfully pointed out, it's only six dollars more than a two piece, which will run you, I think, $10. So they're pretty much just giving you those two extra pieces.

The key is not to think of it in terms of how much chicken you could get from Sam's Club for the same amount.

The sides are a la carte and actually seem like more of a rip. The mac and cheese is fine for what it is, but it's not real mac and cheese. As an African-American, I'm no expert on pasta, but I think the noodles they used may have been rigatoni. And the sauce, so to speak, wasn't as viscous as I would have liked.

The collard greens were vinegary, which is not an adjective I need describing my collard greens. (It might not be an adjective at all period.) I'm a ham-hock man myself (pause), but you can't go wrong with bacon, and that might be something for them to consider.

As if the fried chicken weren't unhealthy enough. Served in a large ceramic bowl as if it were ice cream, thus inadvertently calling to mind Louis CK's "shame glaze" bit, it's admirably greaseless, but it's still fried chicken.

You can tell it's bad for you, because it's delicious. The exterior is nice and crisp, while the interior is as moist as it can possibly be without being as gross as the word moist itself is--even the white meat! I give it a 5/5, with the caveat that any fried chicken, if it's "hot out the grease" is usually pretty good.

I also gorged myself on "small plates," which weren't as bad as they were not particularly interesting to me. The mussels were great, as far as these things go. None of them were rotten or anything. Similarly, to paraphrase Will Rogers, I never met a deviled egg I didn't like.

The hoe cakes--essentially a vaguely savory pancake, sausage and eggs--weren't anything we would have ordered, if it were up to me. I had my eye on the "bread basket," not because I think it's right for restaurants to charge upwards of $10 for bread (which is free), but because I needed the carbohydrates for the ride home.

Which brings us to dessert. I tried all three, none of which was particularly noteworthy to me except for the apple crisp, which was almost impossibly good, for something they probably just heated up in the microwave. If it were a woman, I would have married it. If I'd been alone, I would have smeared some of it on my body. If only I had my own apartment in the building.

The Delmar Loop location of Mission Taco Joint is busy enough these days that they're pulling that thing where they pretend that their app-based reservation system malfunctioned.

You reserve a table hours in advance, only to get there and find out that they don't have any record of you reserving a table. If you want, you can stand outside on the corner for two hours like a dumbass.

Obviously, they'd rather just give your table to someone who wandered in off the street without a reservation. They figure at least some of the people with reservations won't show up anyway, and if they do maybe magic will happen.

It was no big deal. My mom was meeting us there. When she drove past, on Delmar, we hopped in her car and hightailed it to the Soulard location, risking life and limb to jaywalk across the busy street. (Thug life was in full effect.)

We weren't sweating the fact that the Soulard location is owned by the same scammers as the one in the Loop, because Mexican food.

I was half expecting to see someone from "Trops" urinating in the street near the Soulard location, but the area proved to be relatively desolate. There was still a large crowd inside. We probably got there just in time. We reserved a table when we left the Loop and didn't have to wait when we arrived.

The Soulard location is brighter on the inside than the one in the Loop and noisy as all hell. I wasn't sweating the volume, because if my parents had anything novel to say to me over dinner it would have been the first time since the (first?) Clinton administration. Your mileage may very.

The menu at Mission Taco Joint is similar to one you might find at a legit taqueria, out by the airport, but presumably more fancy. Essentially, they carry tacos, burritos and tortas, plus appetizers and a list of mostly tequila-based cocktails.

I of course immediately set about figuring out which cocktail I'd have. I'd already pregamed a little bit, but I wanted to get nice and lit. They carry a drink called the Zombie, which looked like it might have more alcohol in it than anything else on the menu. It costs a few dollars more than any of the other drinks, and supposedly they'll only sell you two per visit.

The disclaimer seemed like it may have been there for psychology purposes, to trick people into spending a few dollars extra on a drink. I don't know if it really had that much more alcohol than any of the other drinks, but it had about as much alcohol as you can put in a drink and have it not taste like sterno.

In fact, the Zombie is served with a garnish that consists of half a lime filled with over-proof rum that's been set on fire. I was instructed by the server to blow out the fire when I was ready to get my drink on and dump the rum in with the rest of the rum.

Pro tip: I wouldn't let it burn too long, because that might decrease the potency of the alcohol. I only let mine burn long enough to take a picture of it. #priorities

For apps we went with the the queso chorizo and the carne asada fries, or whatever they're called.

I don't know what I was expecting the queso chorizo to be, but finding out it's just a cup of melted cheese and some chips was kinda anticlimactic. It's mostly just cheese. There was only the slightest hint of chorizo. Charles Grodin in the movie Midnight Run would have been disappointed.

Truth be told, the carne asada fries weren't as big as my little brother (who doesn't work there or anything) described them, but they were pretty damn good: french fries, with gobs of melted cheese, cubes of steak, quacamole and what have you.

Lately, I've been wanting a burrito like Bobby Brown wants drugs, but I ended up going with tacos. I like the fact that you can get a few different kinds, and the taco of the month--deep fried shrimp with mango salsa--seemed especially tempting. I got one of those, plus a chorizo and a beef brisket.

Briefly, since I don't get paid for this:

The shrimp taco was the one to beat. It's hard to describe it without being inappropriate. Go there each month until they put it back on the menu, if necessary.

The chorizo taco was, as Rachel Ray would say, dee-lish, and partly made up for the minimal amount of chorizo in the appetizer.

Only order beef brisket from legit barbecue places like Pappy's and Sugarfire. Even the mighty Mexicans (er, in this case, white people appropriating Mexican food) can't make it as good.

We finished off the evening with churros y chocolate. I'm not sure if that's what they're called on the menu, but I had a Spanish textbook called "Churros y Chocolate" when I was in the sixth grade, and I've been meaning to try them ever since. It's been 24 years.

We didn't even order them, but our server gave us some for free because my mom told him it was my birthday. She does that in every restaurant we go to.

Just kidding, it really was my birthday the other day. (Check Facebook.) My mom would never lie about something like that.

The Shaved Duck is one of the few restaurants in St. Louis with the distinction of having been featured on an episode of America's best TV show, Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives and hence one of the only ones a brother from around here can visit without having to travel.

If you do decide to visit, you might consider pulling up in a vintage convertible, dressed like the lead singer from Smash Mouth, shouting '90s-era slang terms at the top of your lungs, in order to get the full effect.

Off the hizzle for shizzle!

The inside of The Shaved Duck (ahem) is about the size of a not particularly large house. There's a small bar in the front where there's bound to be more people than should be allowed to be in there, for fire code reasons, standing around waiting for a table. The dining room is larger, but not by a whole lot. Your best bet is to have dinner way early, like a senior citizen. I like eating early anyway, because I'm fat and I can't wait to eat. If I get hungry again later on, I'll just have Fourth Meal at Taco Bell.

The Shaved Duck is one of those restaurants where you have to get appetizers -- they're at least as important as the entrees, if not more so. They don't really sell anything other than barbecue in a few different configurations, so it's your only chance to experience any variety. Plus, the shit is just amazing.

You may have seen the Smothered Fries on TV. That might be their signature appetizer. What they are is a big-ass plate of fancy French restaurant-style French fries covered with rib meat, some sort of gooey cheese-based sauce and a generous handful of shredded cheese for good measure. I split an order with three other people sitting at my table, and I still like I lost a few days at the end of my life, where I don't need them as much anyway. #strategy

In order to not end up looking like a special needs child who somehow got into the art supplies, you have to eat the Smothered Fries using a fork. When you do, the thing you realize is that the promise of rib meat is not some cruel joke like the lobster mac and cheese at Bristol in Creve Coeur. Thinking I was reaching for a French fry hidden beneath layers of cholesterol, I instead ended up picking up a huge, gnarly bit of rib meat -- like, a good half a bone or so worth. This is the kind of surprise I look for during a meal.

Welcome to Flavor Town, USA!

I'm assuming the chicken wings are smoked and then deep fried and coated in dry rub. I've had wings like that at a few different restaurants, and they were all pretty much amazing. I even had a bag of frozen ones from Sam's Club that weren't half bad. They must be impossible to fuck up, due to employing both of the two best cooking methods. Needless to say, these were on point. Or rather, OFF THE CHAIN!!!

Like I said, the main menu is mostly just barbecue in sandwiches, on a platter, on some sort of flatbread (which is getting a little bit sophisiticated for my money), and maybe a few other things. I had a sandwich called The B.O.S.S., which they might consider renaming The Bawse (or just Bawse), because it seems like what Rick Ross would order if he were to dine at The Shaved Duck. I mean, since there's no seafood on the menu and the chicken wings don't have any lemon pepper on them.

The B.O.S.S., essentially, is a steak tri-tip sandwich covered in some sort of bacon-laced cheese sauce that's less viscous than the shit they use on the Smothered Fries and then topped with a couple of onion rings. I had something similar at Wild Smoke in Creve Coeur for my 33rd (sheesh!) birthday and found it to be hot garbahj like literally everything else on the menu there (I tried a little bit of everything -- it sucks!), but I figured The Shaved Duck could probably pull it off. They don't put just any restaurant on the Food Network.

Here is the part where you're probably expecting me to tell you that The Shaved Duck came through for me, but in fact I had an issue with this sandwich: there just plain wasn't enough of it. For a sandwich that costs $14, and for a restaurant with such an obvious commitment to cardiovascular distress, you'd think a brother could have gotten a few extra slices of steak. Yeah, steak will run you, but for what they're charging, I feel like I could buy an entire tri-tip, eat off it until it turns green and then give the rest to my little brother's dog.

If I come back, and I decide to get the Bawse again (pause), and they haven't added a few more pieces of steak, I'm gonna be left with no other choice than to update this review to subtract one star. The Shaved Duck, consider yourself put on notice.

The four things that stand out to me about this place are the ambiance, the service, the food, and the wine selection. In that order. 

This was my first time in New Hope, but after walking up and down the main drag and assessing dinner options, this seemed like the nicest place that offered outdoor seating.

I'm a big fan of small plate themed restaurants and this one is no exception. Chrissy was a very helpful server in terms of making recommendations. We went with the beet salad, octopus, short ribs and a charcuterie with jamon serrano and pate. The red and golden beets were a nice touch and the salad had just the right balance. The octopus was charred and cooked perfectly. The short rib fell apart as it should, and the charcuterie even had a little jam to go with the meat and cheese.

All in all, this is the place to go if you're looking for outdoor seating and want a great dining experience, regardless of how hungry you are. They have something for everyone and the small plate options are plentiful.

Great for late night delivery. I ordered via GrubHub. They close at 12, and I ordered at 11pm on a Sunday night. I got my food by 11:40pm. 
I got a steak platter and tilapia tacos and both were delicious. All food arrived very hot.
Ask for sides of home made hot sauce. They are delicious!
I'll definitely order from here again.

I was told this is a MUST place to go for the best pizza in the area.
Walking in they have instructions on how to order. You order from a seperate area then the dining area and where it's cooked. They have a seperate bar area if your into drinking and you can bring your own wine.

After you order, which we ordered the small 11" Desano which has fresh mozzarella cheese, sausage, pepperoni, some other name of a cheese...you walk around the corner and there are picnic tables with rolls of Brown paper towels, forks and crushed red peppers already on the tables.
They have a "Dough" station where you can watch them make your fresh dough-
They have 3 wood burning ovens that look really old and you can watch your pizza being made. Nothing to hide here. Clran, clean, clean.

They also have:

A prep area in the back left corner

A condiment station with oips, freshed crushed peppers, fresh garlic cut up, "fresh" not from a container parmesan cheese for your pizza

The restrooms were very spacious.

The pizza comes to you on a cookie sheet. No plates here! Very hot, fresh and delicious--

This whole restaurant is handicapped accessible-
Highly recommended!

I couldn't tell you how many times I have walked by this place...I decided I finally had to go!! Ohhhh my!! they have delicious smoked BBQ. Wished I had stopped by here earlier. They have a dinner plate, you get bbq and 2 sides with corn bread. I asked for a sandwich bun as well.
 They have 6 choices of sauces. 3 of which i didnt see until now!! Lol
Carolina, white, xxx911, Kansas city, Tennessee original and Texas sweet hot.
I mixed the Kansas city and the Tennessee original on mine and it was delicious.
Had the corn and Mac n' cheese all very good.

Make sure you look up to see the other 3 sauces. I didn't notice it until someone pointed it out to me. There are 6 sauces.

Would recommend--

Ohhh my. I'm a sucker for homemade candy stores and this one drew me in immediately by the smell coming from it as your walking past it. They had just made a batch of pralines and was giving out free samples, which was very nice of them. The smell was amaaaazing and the pralines were very, very good. I'm not a praline type gal but these were pretty good...They had lots of Apple's just waiting to be covered in caramel.

Would definitely stop in if your in the area and give credit to the gals working hard in here on these wonderful pralines.

48 hours after eating these crab legs I have determined that these crab legs are the reason why all 4 of us are sick, we all  had the same thing to eat. This is the only thing we had to eat the same.

I would caution you on eating these.

Our vacation lasted a day later in a hotel because we all cannot be away from the restroom. Cannot fly home.

Passed by Jimbo's on the way to our hotel and immediately looked it up on Yelp to check out the reviews.  I hadn't had bbq in a while and knew we needed something close by for lunch the next day, so it looked like a good place.  After reading the reviews and talking to fellow Yeep Steve E., who lives in Tampa, I was sold on this place!

I ordered the chicken & ribs combo and chose baked beans and fries.  My chicken & ribs were both cooked perfectly.  The chicken was nice and juicy and the ribs were nice and tender.  The baked beans were not the best I have ever had, but they were pretty darn good and I ate them all.  I didn't care for the fries because they were seasoned, so hubby ate those.  Nothing against the fries, I just don't like seasoned fries from anywhere... ever.  I wish now I would have gotten the mac & cheese instead.

The hushpuppies were so yummy!  I was born and raised in Mississippi and have lived in FL for 17 years.  These hushpuppies were so close to the ones back home.  Closest ones I've found yet here in FL.  LOVED them!  Could have eaten my weight in them.  Yay that hubby doesn't eat hushpuppies because I got to eat his too!  Hehehehe

The place was really nice and homey inside.  I loved all the old timey signs they had as decorations.  I also loved the cute little stairs that went nowhere with a sign for a painless dentist.  Very cute.

Only 3 stars instead of 4 for a couple of reasons.  They only had one type of bbq sauce.  I like my bbq sauce sweet and their sauce was a little too tangy for me.  Even though my chicken and ribs were cooked perfectly, the tangy sauce took away the total yummy factor for me.  The other reason is because of the service.  Our waitress was absolutely horrible.  We had to get up twice to go ask for refills on our drinks and we had to get up and go ask for silverware.  We were there in the middle of the afternoon and the place was pretty much dead.  I don't understand why she wasn't attentive.  

Anyway, when in Tampa, I'd still return here just for those hushpuppies!

I've known what good tastes like for the better part of three decades now. Somehow Brasserie Saint James doubled down on that and left me wishing my wallet could handle every night out. 

For brews, foods, or good vibes Brasseries got your back. The area is clean and well maintained.  Summer seating on the balcony can't be beat. 

Grab any of their specialty drinks or beers on tap for a quick refresher in what excellence feels like dancing across your tongue. If you're in the mood for a quick snack the pretzels here are so far from peasants food they may as well be served on air force one. The perfection of buttery goodness comes with a mustard that will leave you wondering if every mustard you've tasted before is made by craft. 

The marrow canoes were my favorite appetizer and I've yet to discover something on the menu I didn't really want more of. I think you're in for a treat if you're an experienced patron or it's your first time. 

I highly recommend Brasserie for any occasion.

Best. Burger. Ever.

Got the Rodeo King with a side salad. And whatever the drink was with gin/absinthe/eggwhite . All of it was amazing. 

Seriously, just go eat here. It's the best comfort food you're getting anywhere in Delaware.

I'm actually mad, son. I've been meaning to start leaving reviews but nothing inspired me to take the time until the overwhelming whateverness that is Sakura filled me such foodie disdain. This is real beef. Sakura is the Biggie to my Pac. Sike. It's more like the Lil B to my Pac, meaning this food was wild corny and suspect. All I wanted was a snack so I thought I'd grab some dumplings. I walked passed Dim Sum Garden because I've been there too often so I figured I'd hit up the original DSG on 11th for old times sake. I wanted to grab some regular pork and chive dumplings, not even the soup jawns. That soup dumpling/xiao long bao shit is too Iggy Azaela now. Y'all really fucked it up. 

Anyway, I passed the new DSG and was on my way to hit the old DSG but right in between that walk is Sakura. I've lived in Philly all my life and Chinatown for almost 2 years now and always seen Sakura kind of busy but it never seemed to be my thing. It bothers me when Chinese places do too much and serve volcano rolls and shit. Leave that shit alone! Just do you, booboo! That's why I always steered clear of Sakura and pretty much any other place that does like every Asian food ever. That's a tip from an Asian guy, btw. Don't fuck with those thirsty ass restaurants. If they did one thing good, they'd stick with it. But they don't, so they compensate with variety.

Aight, so I thought I'd give Sakura a shot because I saw on their neon signage (another desperate ploy that should've been a red flag) that they had pan-fried Shanghai soup dumps. I've been craving the fried jawns recently, thinking back to last year when I had them in Shanghai at Yang's Dumplings. That shit was incredible and changed my life. I'll never look at a dumpling the same ever again. I let nostalgia get the best of me and I turned back and made my way into Sakura.

I ordered and the wait was wild long but honestly, you won't see me complain too much about service ever so if that's what you're into, you're looking at the wrong reviewer. I'll actually take bad service to the neck and sacrifice all that if the food is incredible. That's just how my priorities stack.

But yo, I was looking for something that resembled Yang's Dumplings in Shanghai and what I got was bread dressed up as dumplings for Halloween. This shit a couple weeks too early for all that. These thick ass, flavorless ass, soupless ass, dressed up with black sesame seeds ass dumplings were spongy as fuck and I was soaking them in ginger sauce just to give it some type of taste. I promise every bite I took pissed me off more than the last. I shook my head as I looked at these "dumplings" like they were my children bringing home bad grades. I wasn't even mad, I was disappointed. Nah, fuck that. I was mad. 

I'm going to wrap this up. I'm honestly wild into food and you'll see that from my upcoming reviews and my palate is actually on par with y'all pretentious Michelin star mother fuckers so when I say Sakura was booty butt cheeks, then that shit was booty butt cheeks. I ain't going back and you can't make me.

A refreshing breeze just blew through 20th and Sansom, and its name 'tis Noble.  In the former digs of Cibucan (loved that place), then an Italian restaurant I never got the chance to frequent, Noble has taken up residence in the most gorgeous and delicious manner possible.

Step inside and you'll know what I mean. Muted shades, subtle pieces of art on the walls and wood, wood, wood everywhere - it's airy, it's light, it's effortless Zen. It's coastal Washington State meets concrete inner city.  I can't forget to mention the bar outfitted with a huge slab of shiny wood that seems totally inviting with its generous helping of stools and the mighty friendly and cool bartenders in green checkered shirts, ties and sleeve garters. (I know, sleeve garters! Love the throwback)  Also love the indoor, outdoor table that frames the front part of the restaurant and opens onto the street.

I know I keep tripping on service in my reviews, but I truly believe it can make or break  the experience. Everyone was so damn nice at Noble and not fake Stephen-Starr nice either -  I really enjoyed our server, she was quirky, uber informed (i.e. full of fun little facts like the wine I was drinking was from the first entirely solar-powered vineyard to what dish truly represented what the chef's signature style was), insightful and attentive without being intrusive.

The pièce de resistance for Noble, of course, and what won me over, was the food.  Each course precisely executed and beautifully presented.  Started with the scallops (I know, kind of a boring choice, when you've got more exciting options on the menu but I was sharing it with my DOH who's got  less than an adventurous palate) then moved on to the Black Sable (a fish, whose consistency and taste is very similar to seabass) and sweet jesus, I almost convulsed with delight.

The temperature was perfect, the accoutrements were spot on.  My dining companion had Free-range veal (and he dutifully remarked "Isn't that an oxymoron?") that was yummy but not as tender as he had hoped. (I'm blaming it on the free-ranging)  Ended the meal with a trio of sorbet (delectable lemon-thyme, grapefruit and watermelon) and they were unexpectedly coupled with fresh from the oven little sugar cookies. 

Ingredients were fresh, everything was so thoughtfully and lovingly prepared, that much was evident.  All this and the lovely ambiance did come at a price though - so with drinks (wine for me, beer for him, + after-dinner spirits), dinner bill for two came up to $130.

Sure it's not an every week thing, but for a treat it's well worth your dime. I can't wait to go back and explore the rest of the menu - At the very least, I'll return as soon as I can to partake in the bar menu (yes, they do offer burgers!) and debate with the barmen on the benefits of sleeve garters.

Out of the ashes of its former super dive bar self, rises Jerry's bar, totally (and thankfully) new and improved (and clean!!!), all ready to go out on the town.  The whole place gives off a very cool vibe.  The interior is a perfect blend of the old and the new, with a gorgeous bar surrounded by subway tile and antique icebox doors, lined with marble counters and tiled floor underneath.  Upstairs houses another bar, (the original, refurbished one) - and a more cozy seating area (perfect for cold winters methinks) - downstairs, huge windows give view onto the corner of the street and lets in all this natural light.

I love the atmosphere, slightly upscale without pretension, but still casual without that sports bar feel.  Right now, is when I love it best, when the patrons are very much local and the whole space isn't quite yet packed.  Once the rest of Philadelphia discovers this little gem, I'll be afraid that its calm clientele will be no more.

They have a very open outdoor courtyard (waiting for approval) ripe to be enjoyed.  Can't wait for that.

Otherwise, service is totally top notch.  Friendly, attentive and knowledgeable - with a staff that's professional but down to earth.  Menu (both bar and food) is varied and interesting and again, upscale enough to differentiate from the rest of the places in my neighborhood.  Food delivers (save for a shirred egg dish that was slightly too liquid-y for my taste) and though I haven't entirely dove through its selections, they look very promising.

Also, Jerry's is an awesome brunch destination (rarely a wait) in a neighborhood that is not short on brunch destinations (or long wait times), I almost don't want to tell you!  Perfect add-on to this neighborhood - a place of this caliber was very, very much needed. Hooray!

Eeek indeed.

Before I explain the eek let me say that I love this little part of Samson Street that stretches from Broad and West. Was sad to see the Oyster House close. I've been known to go Nodding Head or dive-y Oscar every once in a blue moon.  When I saw that someone took the fire house and turn it into something gorgeous, I thought, I want to drink here!

So I did.  With Friends.  We braved the lines on a Friday night with high hopes.  I understood the crowd for a while - it's New, it's Rittenhouse, it's Friday.  Once we made it in, the inside did not dissapoint - it was quite beautiful and there's enough room to stand around with two bars on the first floor alone.  The crowd and bar-staff, however, well that was another story altogether.  Here comes the eek.

EEEeeek.   Maybe Ladder 15 is not for me.  If you're seriously looking for a one-night stand, have a total drunk fest birthday/bachelorette/bachelor party, or make-out hardcore in public, Ladder 15 is totally for you.  Don't get me wrong, it's not like I haven't done those things in a past life - I'm not judging - it's just not what I expected Ladder 15 to be like (and for the most part, I think I've outgrown most of these activities thankyouverymuch).

The DJ was spinning some good tunes, I grooved around a bit with my compadres, waited in line FOREVER for the unisex bathrooms (why do establishments always skimp on the amount of bathrooms?) and then meandered to the back bar for a beverage so I could watch a few of the drunk disasters unfolding before us. 

Eeeek. There were two very ample-bosoomed in tight low-cut tees (à-la McFadden's at the Ballpark) bartenders sloshing beverages.  Both were totally ice cold and ignored me for the good part of 15 minutes.  As the men around me kept getting served (no pun intended) I waited, and waited with my twenty in hand until one of my male friends who had just bellied up to the bar got one of the girls' attention.  It was only then, that she deigned to get my beer order.

Eeek.  Don't think I'll return anytime soon here, especially not on a weekend night.  I don't particularly enjoy being abused by members of my own sex and getting shitty service -  I've outgrown that too.

I just have to come to terms with the fact that I really dislike the American-style brazilian steakhouse scenario.  With most buffets, the all-you-can-eat establishment's fundamental philosophy is almost always the same - sacrifice quality for quantity.  Give 'em lots and lots of meat, feed 'em 'til they're ready to burst  and then, they shake 'em down with the price of alcohol and voila! here's your final bill!  Men with skewers, take a bow!

I don't like theater or antics with my food.  But Fogo (along with its other counterpart in the city, Chima) seems to rely on all these tricks and they succeed in bringing in a crowd every night. 

The food simply does not deliver. The salad bar lacks any true variety and excitement (one point for the shitake mushrooms and the hearts of palm though).  It gets restocked continuously and is fresh, however it looks no better than what one would find at an Aramark run facility.  The meat variety and temperature options is acceptable, but except for one or two cuts of meat (i.e., the top sirloin), the quality and taste is lamentable.

If I ever come back here, it will be too soon. 

Don't get me wrong, I love red meat -  but this place doesn't deserve my carnivorous tendencies.  If you want to get stuffed on never-ending, endless below average meat* (no better than what YOU can cook at home- trust me), this is your jam.   Come for lunch instead of dinner and save a bundle.

*this review could have been replete with double entendres and sexual innuendos, but I couldn't be bothered.

Okay. I'm over it.

Everyone is going nuts over this space and yes, it has brought many businesses, lots of action and attention into  this (my) neighborhood, but lord all-mighty, it's getting out of control here. Sure, the piazza has spurred development straight across my 'hood, south, west, east and especially North - but with this growth, has come, as expected, the crowds (more rowdy than not), and a kind of evolution for the neighborhood that I'm not terribly crazy about.

I don't exactly know what Blastein had in mind when he came up with this development concept, but the end result is downright college frat party meets Jersey Shore (and it is especially more so, now with the addition of the Arrow Swim Club at its north east end). The piazza itself is about as coolly European as the PYT burgers and 'adult' milkshakes served there. Which is to say, not at all.  This whole piazza stinks of 'try-hard' accompanied with bad music blasting at all times of the day. 

Speaking of PYT, along with the Pink Dolphin Market and Millesime, they are the only original tenants left at the Piazza. The businesses and galleries that were once here are no longer - hustled out, moved out, priced out, what have you - all I know is that there is such a HIGH turnover of restaurants and businesses here, it's enough to make one's head spin, even the Piazza people can't keep up (that is, their web page as of today still show the Appolinare restaurant as operating, while it's clearly visible by anyone there that it's been replaced by Kingdom's Oak - mind you this is the fourth restaurant that has been placed in this spot !).  What is solid, genuine and local about that, I ask you? What does it say about the longevity of all of this?  

I am always in awe about how much this (my) neighborhood has changed in the six short years I've moved here.  I am all for development, but really, it begs the question, at what cost?

Fantastic location.  Overall Solid service (if not a bit, Overzealous).  Over-hyped, Overpriced, chain-style food. Simply Over it.

White tablecloths, tables jammed in the space, there's nothing particularly original (not surprising, of course), special or different about this place.  Big salads, nicely sized pizzas, all at a hefty price tag and the end result is food that tastes like half of what it costs. Blah.

Just what we need.  Another 'chain' type restaurant that pawns itself off as something original. I'm sorry, but that just won't do for this town. 

On a related note, as the amazing and delicious Noble Cookery closes, a Serafina opens.  What's wrong with this picture?

I had great feelings about this place. It is large with ping pong and cornhole in the back. Coffee was good. The older man who works there is gracious and accommodating, even set up a heat lamp for us when the sun went down and we were sitting outside.

The older woman however, is extremely rude. When I was ordering, she made me feel very uncomfortable. I had bought a coffee when I got there and my friend was unable to drink coffee, and a few hours later (we were studying), she comes directly up to our table out of nowhere to tell my friend that he also had to buy something and told us that he was being disrespectful. I had been planning on buying another tea but her comments and behavior were uncalled for and made the whole experience uncomfortable and made me want to never return.

First, I love how serious this restaurant is taking COVID. The tables were generously spaces out and we were told ahead if time our reservations would be book for 2hours! 

The service was stellar, with attentive staff refilling drinks and picking up dishes immediately. 

Now for the food, the biscuits were hot and freshly baked. I could have eaten a tub of the butter, both kinds. The dirty rice arancini were undescribable! The orange mojo was an explosion of flavor and there was a hint of spice i love. For first course  - we ordered tuna tartare and steak tartare. The tuna tartare was one of my favorite. Amazing flavor profiles - I would say I wanted more chips but having asked I believe we would have gotten more. The steak tartare was also delicious. Only drawback were the chips were somewhat thin and I like to pile on so some of the chips would break. However, I managed just fine eating it all!
For second course - spiced chicken and tagliolini. The chicken was cooked extremely well. The skin was nice and the meat tender and juicy. The jollof rice and chow were also packed with flavor. The tagliolini also was amazing, the pasta was cooked perfectly and very flavorful. The cauliflower was not overcooked and had a crunch to it which I happen to love but some people may not. 
We were absolutely stuffed and did not order dessert which I know regret!
We also ordered cocktails - the king of New York which my husband said was amazing! I did not drink but I gave a list of drinks I enjoy and the bartender made an alcoholic free drink which was amazing!
Overall we will be back again as this was an amazing experience and the food was stellar. I highly recommend and be sure to book a reservation. There is a parking lot (151) directly across that you can book in advance too.

Atmosphere- all staff were wearing masks and very attentive. Our waitress came and checked on us multiple times even though it was extremely busy.

Food - I really wanted to try and traditional teishoku dinner so I oder the beef (medium). The miso soup came out first and was delicious. Just the right temperature! The tofu was soft but did not soak up much flavor. The teishoku dinner came next. I. The traditional style there was eggplant, salmon cake, plain white rice, pickles, and sashimi (tuna, salmon, lemon pepper fish). Overall the meal was delightful! I love the beef - had some sort of teriyaki sauce, the sashimi was fresh and delicious!  While shogun is know for other dishes, I highly recommend giving a teishoku a try!

We went there last night and had a question for the server and she had a terrible attitude next thing you know the manager comes over and says is there a problem we say no so my family says is it really 5 dollars for a side of spaghetti, so he said yup absolutely very rudely, also they keep your coin change so we asked that they bring ours back and in a small plastic cup with 44 pennies. Then laughed at us with the rest of the staff. I have never been so disappointed and disrespected in my life so the manager Rich respone da nasty message in face book to me I will post pic of it.

Awesome brewery to stop through in Nashville! It's a great space with several bars, lots of tables, and a nice outdoor spot. The guys behind the bar and back in the brewery are so friendly.

The beer was great! I particularly enjoyed the "Country Hicks" sweet potato stout. The food was great too! Generous portions, with great flavors. The fries are outstanding, thinly cut and spiced perfectly!

How can you not be excited to eat a place called King of Tandoor?  Say it out loud.  Really.  Now say it in a silly voice.  Are you grinning like a dork?  Yes you are.  Why?  Because you are awesome.

Speaking of awesome, the food here is absolutely righteous.  My dining compadres ordered veggie and meat samosas (killer!) to start, plus chicken tikka masala (outstanding!), chicken dumpakht (it's like a magical Indian chicken pot pie), and veggie korma (creamy-good).   I ordered my standard litmus test for an Indian place: plain ol' chicken tikka (not chicken tikka masala), and hot damn, my socks were blown off.

Dude, if you can make chicken breast chunks on a hot plate so mind-blowingly exciting that we're yelling Hallelujah, then ninja, you *are* the KING of TANDOOR.


(The fine print: Yeah, like everyone else said: The service is pretty bleh, but the food is so good you won't care.)

Tan Dinh's skinnier relative - menu's a little smaller but just as good

My parents wanted something healthy and suggested Vietnamese and I initially said no because I really only like to eat Vietnamese on the West Bank or in the east and I didn't want to go that far, then I remembered Eater NOLA sent something out about a soft opening of Ba Chi UPTOWN!! Today was the first day of their soft opening. They're actually opening next week. We were very happy we went.

We shared 2 appetizers and 2 entrees between the three of us and we were very full. We ordered the vietnamese coffee (drip coffee with condensed milk) served over ice and some ice tea and our total was $29 for everything.

Tried the:
Baco (appetizer) - these are like soft steamed dumplings that are folded, almost like a taco. Think pork bun's from Duong Phoung. It's that consistency. They have all different kinds of fillings and most come 2 to a serving for about 3.50 - 4.50. I ordered the soft shell crab w spicy mayo which only came 1 but was really good. I think they let you mix and match but I'm not sure. 

Fresh Shrimp Spring Egg Rolls served with peanut sauce - standard vietnamese fare. Good stuff, tastes like it supposed to.

Seafood Pho - My parents loved the pho broth. They wish they picked a meat one instead, not bc the seafood wasn't great but bc they realized that's what they were craving later. Mom was impressed. Prices ran about 8.50-9.50 for a big ol bowl.

Charbroiled pork rice dish with eggrolls - This was I think 8.50 and then you add the daikon radish salad, kimchee and egg for a $1 plus sticky rice cakes for another $1. It sucks you have to tack on another $2 for something that should come with it, but that being said this food is pretty friggin cheap anyways. Wonder if they should just include it and increase the price? Comes with 2 fried meat egg rolls, filled with tons of meat, great flavor and filling. 

Sticky rice - these are basically fried rice patties, thnk fried grits, but it's fried rice. It's the consistency of risotto but has a slightly sweet almost coconut flavor. Bc it reminds me of this filipino dessert my mom makes (coconut sticky rice wrapped in banana leaves) I would prefer noodles or regular rice topped with an egg next time. Still it's pretty good, especially if you didn't grow up in a filipino household thinking it's dessert.

No doubt I will be back. I want to try the banh mi and I will definitely come back and get another rice plate. 

I would love to see some duck (maybe in the baco) and some different kinds of spare ribs like lemmon pepper and salt they serve at the Tan Dinh. It's soooooo good. Would also love it if they added an avocado tapioca smoothie like the one they have on the west bank. If you haven't tried one also delis.

Give it try, you won't regret and prices are great for Uptown!

Horrible service!!! Drive thru lines were slow and one window for cashier and food pick up. They forgot to give us hash brown. I was a little disappointed since those were for kids and I didn't feel like turning around to go stand in the long line to ask.

Phenomenal dining experience!  Exceptional service paired with delectable cuisine made for an incredible evening. They start off with rolls and butter. No joke- some of the best rolls I've ever had.  Sweet, buttery and warm. So good in fact- that I asked for extra to take home! We ordered the small shellfish platter ($75). Lobster, shrimp, prawns, oysters, clams and lump crab came in a bowl on a bed of ice. I mean- what's not to love? For our entree's we ordered the surf and turf($75). Filet mignon and lobster tail. The filet mignon was an amazing cut of meat. Prepared to perfection... so tender it could be cut using a butter knife if you wanted. The lobster tail coupled with the filet, was utter heaven. We ordered the asparagus to accompany our entrees, although it wasn't needed as we had plenty of food already. We went a little crazy and ordered a special they had that night that consisted of one, very large, thick piece of bacon. Bacon is one of the loves of my life- so I had to taste this. Super indulgent and gluttonous... yaaaaaaas.... mmmmmmm... Feeling super stuffed and happy, we skipped dessert.  The waiter and all of the staff were exceedingly attentive and made sure we always had spirits and water in our glasses. They checked in just enough that we wanted for nothing, but didn't feel like we there were too many interruptions. It was truly a special evening, I felt like a princess. So happy my boyfriend brought me here!!

This place is packed during the evenings and weekends. We came here @ 2 pm on a Monday afternoon.. and we were 1 of maybe 6 tables dining at that time. Our lunch was fabulous.We were seated outside at a quiet table, under the shade of a large awning. The temperature was about 80* and there was a cool breeze in the air. Just lovely. To start we ordered the Focacca Bread w/Garlic Butter ($5). Yum yum! My entree: "Eric's Seared Tuna Club" seared yellowfin tuna with applewood bacon, tomatoes, onion and avocado with a spicy aioli on a toasted brioche!!! C'est Magnifique! Spicer than I anticipated, but balance well when paired with the cooling avocado. I opted to choose a side caesar salad for an extra few $ instead of the options of soup or fries. It would have been much too filling. The cocktails here are excellent as well. My Targaryen Mule was fresh and sweet and oh so beautifully presented. Excellent lunch date! Great service too- fast and friendly and educated on the menu. I can't wait to return!

LIKES & DISLIKES @ RUSTY LION:

Likes-
1. Great roof top bar
2. $1 Mimosas @ Sunday Brunch

Dislikes-
1. My Margarita Pizza was almost the WORST pizza I have ever had. Everyone elses food that I saw-looked and smelled amazing. But my pizza... it tasted like it was from the freezer section of the grocery store and was totally undercooked. When I picked up the slice, all the toppings fell off and i had to eat it like a pile of slop. Just disgusting. We ordered 2 of these pizzas for 4 of us to share. Both were made the same way and both were gross. If you come here... take my advice and DON'T ORDER THE PIZZA!

Slightly disappointed with my most recent visit to Kitchen 519. We took my boyfriends grandparents for lunch here because we had enjoyed our meal so much here the last time we came. They told us there was an issue with the bread delivery and so we waited a very long time to receive any bread to our table. It was warm and fresh when it arrived, but was only one piece to split between the 4 of us. The best part of the meal had to be the olive oil that came with the bread. It was so good that I proceeded to dunk my fries in it- forgoing the ketchup completely. His grandmother ordered hot tea and they brought over a large box for her to pick what kind she wanted. It literally had only 2 types of cheap Lipton tea. Decaf or regular tea, filling up 2 of the maybe 12 compartments. It looked pretty dumb coming in that elaborate box. Unimpressive to say the least. They didn't bring over any sugar and we had to ask for that as well. My crabcake sandwich was delish and the arugula salad on the side was ok but lacked any real flavor.I do have to say, our waiter was really friendly and nice and tried to make our meal enjoyable. Maybe we came on an off night, I will give them a chance again.

This place has 1000's of reviews so there's no need to convince you that it's great- so here's some key points:

-there's 2 lines (one for cards and one for cash)
-the cash line is always shorter, so go there.
-the cash line is in the back of the building so some people don't know about it!
- Beignets come 3 to a bag for $3.50
- iced lattes are delicious!
- chairs/tables are first come first serve!
- enjoy!

This restaurant in recent months has become one of my go-to lunch spots. I always start with an order of chips and salsa. Today, we decided to get some guacamole as well. It was super tasty! I wen't with the Pork Al Pastor taco's as my entree. The soft shell tacos were filled with spicy roasted pork, pineapple, pickled red onion and cilantro. The vegetables were fresh and the pork was juicy, tender and flavorful.  The spicyness of the pork balanced perfectly with the sweet pineapple. Simply delicious. My favorite tacos here to date!  I have also had the Pork Carnitas and Brisket on other visits here and I loved them all! The restaurants decor is colorful, upbeat and warm. I love this space. My experiences have always been positive ones! I will continue to come back!!

Here's another five star review for a great place. THIS IS AMAZING THAI CUISINE!! I literally just put my fork down and I felt immediately compelled to get on my Yelp and tell people about it. Authentic, fresh, flavorful dishes prepared to perfection. Our appetizer of Kanom Jeeb Dumplings were simply fantastic. They were packed full of pork and shrimp. Our first entree was the Panang Curry with Chicken. Panang Curry aka LIQUID GOLD is a rich blend of coconut milk, string beans, carrots, peppers and broccoli. The dish was the perfect combination of sweet yet spicy. Our second entree was the Pad Grapow with beef. It's a mix of garlic, chili, string beans, onion, carrots and bell peppers. All the vegetables were fresh and flavorful. Our meal looked and tasted perfect. My boyfriend had never eaten Thai food before tonight and it took me some coaxing to get him to agree to eat it for dinner. He f'n loved it. He needs to listen to me more often ;) Eat here. You will not be dissapointed!!

Le Bus is a wonderful addition to the East Falls neighborhood!! I have been here twice since they opened and both times I have had a great experience. They have indoor and outdoor seating and have a large awning so you can still enjoy the outdoors while it is raining. The indoor space is clean, new and modern. They did a nice job renovating this place. The food here is all delicious.. ( I haven't had anything here that I didn't like). Oh, and the bread basket they bring to the table to start is obviously the best... I mean the bread here is their specialty! We ordered an assortment of things off the menu... green salad, wild mushroom bisque, lemon garlic stir-fry, duck tacos, steak frites and a brisket sandwich. They have a wide variety of choices, all have innovative twists and variations on traditional dishes. The wine and beer selection is good as well. I always have a pleasant time here. The only thing I am upset about is that they waited until I moved out of this neighborhood to open!

An excellent place to stop for a few drinks and some small bites to eat. The Continental is a tapas restaurant, so you will eat delicious small morsles of food- always leaving you wanting more! But the reasons I love coming to the Continental is for the ambiance. The style and decor of this space is meticulously thought out and put together beautifully. The restaurant is multi-level and has a rooftop lounge. Each space is treated differently and looks completely different. There are hanging basket swings on the second level that you can sit and eat dinner in. The bathrooms on the lower level feature 2 way mirrors, so the people in the hallway can see you looking in the mirror like a window! Quite shocking the first time you realize this! The rooftop bar is great for drinks on nice nights. They have a great happy hour menu with reasonable prices. I like to stop here for a quick drink on my way to dinner in the city. Definitely recommended!!!!

Wow! Amazing Mexican food! We ordered the most amazing entree "Molcajete mar y tierra" Basically this was a bowl overflowing with everything that's good in life... steak, chicken, shrimp, scallops, clams AND crab legs. This huge bowl fed the two of us and we still had plenty to take home.  We finished our meal off with freshly made Churros that were filled with a boston cream filling. All of the dishes were beautifully presented and had equally amazing flavor.  I was totally impressed with everything I ate here. Also, the owners Carlos and Maria were gracious hosts. They made sure our meal was special one. I will definitely be returning!!!

One of the best spots in Dunedin to have a few drinks and an awesome dinner. I've never had a meal here I didn't like! This time we started our meal off with a Wild Mushroom Flatbread (always an excellent choice- I highly recommend!) This pizza is topped with mushrooms, truffle oil, garlic and mozzarella. We like to add some steak too. It's absolutely fabulous every time. We decided on two different seafood entrees. Honestly, the Fried Seafood Platter was SO big- it could/should have been shared by two people. Fried Scallops, Shrimp, Fish, Calamari, Fries and Coleslaw. It was wayyy too much fried seafood for this girl. I could have used a second person and a side of vegetables! But it was all super fresh and fried golden and crispy- just like I like it! We also ordered the Blackened Mixed Grill (a much healthier and more balanced option than the previous one) Shrimp, Scallops and Fish with cheesy risotto and fresh vegetables. Excellent. And last but not least I have to say that the Coconut Mojito is to die for. One of my favorite cocktails I have ever had. I get one.. or two.. or three... every time I come!!!!!!!!

Super chill local bar in East Falls. I would compare it to something like Cheers. Everyone is friendly- the bartender is social and chats it up with the patrons. I felt very at home here, by myself looking to have some dinner and a few beers. The $5 Chicken sandwich special they were running that night was phenomenal. You have 4 options to which you can choose to prepare your sandwich. I chose the Italian Style Chicken Wrap which was tender, juicy chicken with peppers and I believe provolone... all melted together to make an F'n awesome combination. I would suggest checking this spot out when you want to stay near home and grab a cheap bite and some good brews. I can't stress enough that this is a CASH ONLY establishment! (They do have an atm)

As always, my lunch at Ninja was truly enjoyable. I just love everything about this place. The decor is so funky and cute, I'm totally obsessed with the upside down roses hanging from the ceiling. The lunch menu is so reasonable. I always order the Chicken Hibachi ($6.99) You start with a bowl of miso soup and a salad. The Hibachi chicken is paired with fried rice and mixed vegetables- "yum-yum" sauce and ginger sauces on the side. Whatever is in that sauce that they use here to cook everything in is simply delicious. I specifically come to this restaurant to have this meal. The service is good and fast. In and out during lunch hour. I would recommend coming here!!!

Where do I start? You can't see it from the road because the sign is not lit. The place is a mess and falling apart. The food was awful. Chicken piccata came out as 2 plain chicken breasts that had to have been microwaved. The pizza was tasteless and undercooked. The wine is just sitting out on the counter. The choices are merlot and Cabernet. No idea what brand. The only redeeming factor was the waitress was very sweet. Not knowledgeable but very sweet.

We needed to get out of the house and out for a nice dinner after the quarantine. We selected this place because we knew they had lobster mac and cheese which is something we were craving. We walked in no wait got a nice booth in the bar area. Our waiter Drew, was very nice and got us an ice-cold draft.  We ordered the lobster mac and cheese and the potstickers to start. They were both excellent. Plenty of chunks of lobster and the pot stickers were cooked perfectly. Seared on the outside and juicy in the middle. Both the sauces that came with it were delightful. We finished off by getting the blackened fish medley and decided to just split it since we were getting full. It wasn't my favorite but honestly it was a generous portion and everything cooked perfectly.  It had this rice potatoes sticky stuff that I didn't care for but my boyfriend loved.  Anyway, definitely be back want to try the burgers and maybe a side of the lobster mac and cheese again. The atmosphere was good with lots of social distancing. Glad to see our restaurants are coming back!

Who knew shade grown, organic coffee from Alabama would be so yummy? That's probably why I drank about 3 cups of it and then ended up bouncing off the walls for a few hours afterwards (which made me productive but probably quite annoying).

Make sure to give yourself enough time and room in your belly for some of the food - the sandwiches are great. This is the perfect place to hang out for a while and get some work done - with its free wireless, friendly staff and a good vibe, this just might be my new office away from home!

I don't know why I was holding out on coming here, but that was just silly of me. Not only is the decor lovely, but their beer ROCKS! They have my beloved framboise on tap and service is quick and friendly (even the giant bouncers at the door).

I'm going back, and next time I'm eating. And, of course, drinking more framboise.

Wow, this place really is like Chuck E. Cheese for grownups! No kidding!

I came here after seeing "Pineapple Express" the other night. I played some video games and drank a beer. I was a mellow, happy girl. 

That's about all I have to report there.

Now my obsession with all things "Mad Men" related has come full circle. I felt like Don and Betty Draper were going to slide into the large, leather booth right next to us at any moment (at which time I would have had to politely excuse myself while I ignored whatever conversation was going on so I could drool over the foxiest man ever to play an ad exec). The place was hoppin' on a recent Tuesday night, which was sort of surprising, given the whole craptastic economy thing...but I digress. Valet parking was a complete fail, from the fact that it took 15 minutes to get someone to come out and get the car to the 20 minutes we spent waiting to get our car back. Not sure if that's the fault of the restaurant, though, so I'm willing to cut them a break. 

The room itself (the former Striped Bass, which I never had the pleasure of dining at) was lovely; soaring ceilings, ginormous chandeliers, opulent decor and dim lighting - and then there is the mural of ritzy dogs livin' it up at the bar. Cute? Yes. Strange? Absolutely.

Regardless of what I thought of the canine rendering, though, the service was outstanding from the very beginning. Our waiter, Gabriel, gave us detailed explanations for every menu item we asked about, and never disappeared for long. I loved that he stuck nearby in case we needed anything.

And the food...mmmmm...I highly recommend you try the crab cake appetizer, as it's one of the best I've ever had (the boy got the Butcher Salad, aka "Hoagie in a bowl" and gobbled that baby up). We both had the New York Strip and gasped out loud at the large cut that we were presented with. It was enough meat to feed a small village! I don't know how they did it, but easily it was the most wonderful steak ever created by man. Buttery and juicy inside, slightly crisp and salty outside, it was perfect in every way.

But my real foodgasm moment came when I cut into the baked hashbrowns. Good God, are these a gift from above or what? Diced potatoes, Vidalia onions and sour cream? I would go back for those alone. And I finally had Baked Alaska for dessert. Words cannot describe how crazy good it was. It's now my new favorite dessert.

I had pretty much resigned myself to not ever being on the Starr bandwagon, but after my dinner here I am singing a different tune. Mr. Starr, you have finally done it. Now I'm a believer.

I've been thinking about my top dining experiences for 2008 and, after dining at XIX for dinner recently, I'm adding it to my list.

We were seated in the far dining room (not the one when you first come off the elevator; although it is nice, go for the other one if you have the chance). The decor is gorgeous, there's a raw bar in the center of the room and the nighttime views are magnificent. I'm still swooning over my meal of crabcake, grilled octopus (prepare to be amazed) and duck. The bartender very kindly obliged my request for a nonalcoholic cocktail and served up a delicious virgin raspberry mojito that blew me away. And the service: ce magnifique! It was attentive without being pushy and Wilmer, one of our waitstaff, will have you cracking up throughout your dinner. I loved this - since XIX is such an upscale restaurant, it took a little of the edge off and made for a really enjoyable evening.

One of my favorite parts of the night was a dessert sampling and probably the best pot of tea I've ever had in my life. The Bellevue has its own blend of tea (Bellevue Blend) that consists of different flowers. It's pink, fragrant and delicate. Much like me :)

While it's obviously not a place to dine at on an everyday basis, this is one of my go-to restaurants for a fancypants experience. So if you're looking to impress someone, have a night to remember, seal the deal or all of the above, I highly suggest you make a reservation at XIX!

I felt like a bonafide grownup when I hung out at Vintage the other night...maybe it was the fact that I was drinking some smooth wine while listening to some sensual music under fantastic mood lighting, but why analyze? I had a great time and the bartenders were attentive and helpful. My husband had one of the specials and I had my beloved Riesling, a perfect apres-Lolita treat. 

When it's time for your to graduate from beer (or just mix it up a bit), be sure to check out the adult grape juice here.

Yep, it looks really cool inside, which kinda gets your hopes up that you're going to have the dining experience of a lifetime. But when foodtime comes along, well, let's just say that it's not bad but it's not great, either.

If you like fancy drinks, waiters that ignore you to flirt with other waiters and a big bill, then this is the place for you.

If not, then grab sushi and a sixpack and then sit on your porch. You'll have just as good (and maybe even better) of a time. And you won't have to listen to any stupid techno music while you're trying to have a conversation.

PS. The bathrooms will make you feel like you're on a spaceship. So at least that's...interesting?
