I was so completely underwhelmed that I had to decide whether or not I was even going to bother writing a review about it. But duty calls...so here goes.

I came here with two other people and were seated promptly at a table outside. That was the best part of the experience. Our waiter showed up a while later, took our drink orders and disappeared for a while. Finally he showed back up and we ordered dinner, which was totally meh. (Nachos were smushy and the burger was nothing to write home about). We had to beg for utensils and napkins and waited for a long time, and ordered a second round that took about 2 minutes to arrive. Oh, and the women's room was out of order so I had to climb these scary dark steps to go to a WC upstairs and was walked in on even though the door was locked. Nice!

Whatever - you don't show up at the Copa on a Friday night and expect the meal of your life. Actually, according to these reviews and everyone else I've ever talked to, you don't show up at the Copa and expect the meal of your life ever. Unless you're nutty or something.

Oh, Lolita. I am totally into you.

This little restaurant feels super special, like you've discovered a place that is exclusive and very cool without being pretentious or a scene. The energy was amazing and the food, well, let's just say that it totally did it for me in ways that other restaurants in Philly just haven't been able to achieve.

My husband and I decided to go here on a Saturday night, and based on the reviews, I expected a scary wait. Luckily, we came early enough (6-ish) and only had to wait about 15 minutes (the host took our cell phone number and gave us a call so we could browse next door at Robin's Books instead of waiting outside in the cold. That was awesome.). We were seated at a sweet little table up front so we got the whole romantic-date night experience, and we were in heaven from start to finish. He got the duck, which was amazing, and I got a cheese enchilada with grilled shrimp that blew my mind. The portions looked a little small when they were served, but I barely finished half of the entree before I was full. Yes, once again, my eyes were bigger than my stomach.

The service was good and we never felt neglected or like he was breathing down our necks. It was loud but it just added to the vibe of the restaurant, and besides, I only had eyes for my dining companion (and, of course, my cheese and shrimp dish). This place gets my vote for best date restaurant in the city. Score!

Well, my first trip to West Philly was well worth it. Bill M. wasn't kidding when he said I'd love it!

I had a blast with my fellow Yelpers the other night when we all met up for drinks and food a go-go. But ale drinkers of the world, be warned: the double bock packs a serious punch. For realz...and because I was with such a well-mannered group of pals I was never sans-drink (if this isn't a ringing endorsement to join our community, then I don't know what is).

My pizza was yummy and everyone seemed happy. The space was cool and reminded me of my beloved Roebling Tea Room in Williamsburg. Oh yeah-clean bathrooms too! 

Five stars all around for food, service from the cute waitress in the even cuter Johnny Cupcakes hoodie, awesome company and some of the best beer I've had in a while.

I took some out of town Yelp colleagues here for lunch today and was hoping and praying it would please our critical tastebuds and high service standards. Well, let's just say that they get a B- for effort: the service was good (our waitress was very attentive and super nice), the decor was wacky (thank you, Mr. Starr, for once again trying to distract us from the cuisine) and the portions were generous. The food, while it wasn't terrible, wasn't anything to get excited about, though. My shrimp Caesar salad was just ok, and the lemonade tasted like Country Time. I totally appreciate the fact that at many of these theme-y restaurants more emphasis is placed on the experience rather than the meal, but I wasn't totally feeling it. Oh well, at least we got our photos taken in the cool photo booth before we left (word to the wise: be prepared as soon as you put your $3 in or else you're going to get a shot of someone's boobs instead of your smiling face. Or maybe that's your thing; in that case, say cheese(y)!)

If you love the strong scent of desperation, then you'll love this place. You can't even look around the room, because every person you glance at will lock eyes with you and stare you down like they're sizing up their next meal. I was there with 3 other people and we all experienced it. The drinks were expensive, the music was the audio equivalent of watching an episode of "Two and a Half Men" and the general look of the patrons was last-call chic (lots of boobies, sparkles and hair product).

Best Indian food in the city, hands down. The interior design was beautiful - contemporary yet it felt true to the culture. I don't think there's a bad seat in the house - but I highly recommend trying to reserve the table in the corner on the 8th Street side (it's tucked away in a little nook that's perfect for an intimate dinner). 

As far as the food goes, everything I ordered was delicious. I went for lunch and tried the Thali special (a little sampling of 8 of their "greatest hits"). I especially loved the Navratan Korma, a creamy vegetable dish that tastes great with their homemade Naan. It's not very spicy, though, so if you like yours with a little kick you might need to say something.

Start your dinner out with the Rangpur Rose (Tanqueray Rangpur gin, Pama pomegranate liqueur, fresh ginger, lime, cranberry and rose water) and save room for the rice pudding. Yum!

Great service, too. I'll def. go back!

Having a meal with a chef is a totally different experience than dining with a regular person who just likes to eat (I fall into the latter category. I like to eat. A lot.). The menu looked great, and I instantly liked the cozy, dark  atmosphere. We decided to share a bunch of things, and started out with the Chowder (needed butter and more seasoning) and Calamari (DELISH!). Everything was going just fine. My friend was enjoying the food and a few Anchor Steams, and I was hoping he was distracted and not paying attention while I scarfed down the squid. And then our entrees came out.

We ordered the crabcake and a Caesar Salad to share, but when the salad appeared, my friend was not pleased. In his exact words (which he said to the super patient and friendly waitress): "The lettuce looked like it just walked here from China." He was not exaggerating. The salad was quickly returned to the kitchen - the service here was awesome. I'd come back just for that alone!

The Happy Rooster is a nice place for a long lunch with a pal, especially on a rainy, chilly day. I'll be back (and I'll be trying out the sardines).

Love the vegan mini donuts. Love the music. Love the decor. Love the service. Love the ice coffee. Love the big sofa in the back. Love the magazines. Love the clean bathroom. Love the tiny boutique. Love the garden. Love the location. 

Love that the owner sent me a message letting me know that they do offer milk in addition to half and half and soy milk.

Love Soy Cafe!

This place fit me like Cinderella's slipper fit that damn Disney princess. Between the cheap beer that just kept coming, the jukebox that played songs I haven't heard in years and the heart-attack inducing french fries, I was in love from the moment I walked through the door. Of course, it probably didn't hurt that iI was with a group of about 10 of my awesome Yelp friends, but hot damn, it was a glorious party. The waitress called us "honey" (I'm a sucker for that) and it got louder and louder the later it got. Oh, and it was only Tuesday. Now if that isn't a ringing endorsement for a dive bar, then I don't know what is. Just remember that when you wake up the next morning with your new gang name written on your inner thigh in sharpie. 

Oscar's is totally my new crush.

I'm in love...and I think this one's a keeper. But I'm not selfish and oddly enough, in this instance, I don't mind sharing, so you can get in on the action, too.

Tria's got it all, from the hip, loungey decor to one of the best beer and wine lists in the city. And the service will make you weak in the knees - you'll never spend a second wanting for anything. Anything goes with the menu (our party of four ate our hearts out) and you'll leave feeling satisfied and totally ready for seconds!

I'm totally going back for seconds because this place really lit my fire. I just hope that it was as special for Tria as it was for me...

UPDATE 2.9.08: I just returned from lunch here. And wow, is my tummy happy. I beg you - try the Cuban sandwich. You will not be disappointed! And the famous chocolate cigar dessert is to die for. The name makes me giggle, but it sure tastes delish!

Great, great service-and they also have Reymos Moscatel Espumoso, which is my favorite wine ever. I didn't try it today but I highly recommend you get over there now and try it immediately!

ORIGINAL REVIEW (I gave the bar scene on this particular night 3 stars):
I'll preface this review with a disclaimer that this is about the bar at Alma de Cuba, and not the restaurant itself, which I have heard great and wonderful things about. And now that we have that out of the way, I just want to share a snippet of a conversation I overheard when I was there the other night:

Dude in suit with casually loosened necktie: So, I'd love to buy you a drink sometime and talk to you about getting you into that hot VIP event I'm hitting up this weekend.

Chick with strategically placed highlights and low cut blouse: Uhhh, he he he (laughs nervously and plays with necklace)...

Dude: So I'll take that as a yes.

Chick: bats eyelashes, nods head and giggles some more.

Dude: (Looking down her blouse while simultaneously checking out the other women in the room) Maybe this summer I'll let you check out my shore house. It's amazing.

At that point I lost consciousness from the hot air that was swirling around the bar. By studying the crowd of professionals that appeared to be somewhere in the 30-40 age range, this seemed to be the standard of conversation downstairs. 

Extra bonus entertainment: woman and man in a ladies room stall for at least 15 minutes who then tried to divert attention by throwing a cigarette over the wall and running out. A true Bret Easton Ellis moment to be sure.

Don't sit in the corner - you will get pummeled by the opening and closing of the coatroom door all night (my friend has the bruises on her back to prove it).

And unless you want to get hammered, avoid the mojito. If ending up crazy drunk is your plan, though, fly like the wind and order away.

I'm pretty sure I can safely say that this is the place that cured me of an eating disorder. 

I think the weight of my final creation (I can't remember the details because I immediately launched into a sugar coma when I was done but I think it had cookies & cream, vanilla cheesecake, peach tart and just about all the chocolate and raspberry toppings they have) was almost a pound. And guess what - I ate the hell out of it. I destroyed that fro-yo. I practically licked the cup when I was done. And I'll do it again, too.

The decor was so cute and clean, and being the control freak that I am, I loved being able to make my treat myself. Phileo gives me a reason to go back to South Street. I may be larger because of it, but who cares. Besides, isn't yogurt healthier than ice cream (don't burst my bubble - just let me live in ignorance for a while)?

Something is afoot in the universe. I'm worried that soon we're all going to be sucked into a black hole. Why? Because apparently I'm on a quest this week to subconsciously increase my ass size by at least 40%.

First, there was the cheesesteak I had for dinner the other night. And an enormous chocolate chip cookie for breakfast. Then, the fries with mayo I ate for lunch. Later, the other part of the cheesesteak I ate last night a few hours after eating some noodles and a Snickers Bar.

And today...once again...I heeded the siren song of the Schmitter.

I am full. I am drowsy. My belly feels like it's going to explode and my arteries are constricting as I type this. But do I regret it? Hellz no...in fact, there's still some on the plate in front of me, dripping that sweet sweet secret sauce and greasy goodness, and overflowing with sliced beef, cheese, fried onions, tomatoes and salami. I'll try to resist it, but I'm probably going to end up licking the plate.

When I think about it, it kinda feels like the morning after. And the trip to the kitchen to get rid of the scraps is going to be my own personal walk of shame.

But I liked it. I liked it a lot. And I'll totally do it again, too.

There aren't enough stars in the universe to convey how I feel about Beilers Bakery. This Amish stand is in the front corner of Reading Terminal Market and is the home of the greatest food ever: the whoopie pie.

If you haven't had the blissful experience of eating this moist, round chocolate-whipped creme-chocolate perfection, then you must do so right now. Seriously - stop whatever you are doing right now and rush over there (they sometimes run out early in the day so I'm not kidding!). They are as big as your face and only $1 each, which also makes it the world's biggest bargain. Eating a whoopie pie from Beilers will make you a happier person; yes, maybe you'll be a happier person with a bigger butt, but trust me, it's worth it (isn't that what elastic-waist pants are for, anyway)?

Any place that serves the food of my youth + tasty cocktails (you MUST try the pink elephant...so pink and yummy) is ok with me. Love the decor - you will too, if you're a Brady Bunch fan - and the food is surprisingly good, especially for a Starr restaurant. Big points for the calamari - food with tentacles tastes good, more so when you're dining with friends. This is the kind of place you come with a group of friends - you'll have fun for sure.

Yummity yum yum...when in the market for brunch, look no further than Farmicia. It's got it all...great interior, good service and a ginormous menu that everyone in your party will be able to choose from (even the vegans and the kids).

There were five of us on a recent Saturday, and we ate it all. Bloody Marys, fancy cocktails, fruit, Lancaster ham, eggs, pancakes...good Lord, people, we tore it up and loved every minute of it. My only complaint is that there was so much to choose from, I had a hard time deciding. I can't wait to go back for lunch or dinner. Wine list, here I come!

We called ahead to reserve a table. I think that was a smart move on our part. Me eating so much that I had to unbutton my pants? Not so much.

Cafe Ole is a great place to take your laptop and get some work done while enjoying some yumariffic coffee and tasty food. It's such a neighborhood coffee shop - every time I go there I run into at least one person I know. And that pleases me. 

The staff is always friendly and the music is good. And they also have one of the cleanest bathrooms in Old City. Priceless.

Chomp, chomp, snarfle, crunch, slurp. 

That is my dramatic interpretation of me scarfing down one of their cannolis. Lemme tell ya - it was a life-altering experience. LIFE-ALTERING, I say! Creamy, crunchy and flavorful, just like a real cannoli should be. 

The only thing keeping me from granting Isgro's the coveted five star status are the prices. Ouch. A little steep for my liking, but I won't complain - it just might be the only thing keeping me from going there on a regular basis. And I am not prepared to buy a new wardrobe to support what my body-by-pastry would look like.

When it is late, you're drunk and starving and happen to still be down around South Street, this is where you go. Even though the guy taking your order might yell at you so meanly that it makes you want to cry, and your cheesesteak will not be the most delicious one you've ever eaten. It doesn't matter. It's some fine post-drinkin' food.

Brunch has been brought. Or served. Whatever...I scarfed down the meal that is neither breakfast nor lunch here today, and it was a winner. Plus, I partook in their legendary Bloody Mary bar. Yes - it's official. I am a convert. Throw some bacon bits in that beverage (or A1 Sauce, peppers, hot sauce, whatever - they've got it all) and your Sunday will be peachy keen.

Lots of space, great choices, servers who always bust their butts to get you what you need, good coffee and a DJ - plus my favorite bathrooms in town. What more could you need? Nothing, that's what. 

Now go forth and brunch it up next weekend. You can thank me later.

It's way better than McDonald's, up there with Burger King, not quite Wendy's and doesn't hold a candle to In N Out. 

I give 5 Guys an extra star because they have 'Little Cheeseburgers.' I don't have much of an appetite and hate to waste food, so this is the perfect size for me. However, the whole props for logical proportions goes out the window if you get fries and a soda - the "small" ain't so small, unless you happen to be a giant.

I was also stunned by their choice of music. During my lunch I was treated to songs by such classic rock faves as Chicago and Toto. Maybe this was their way of making sure customers weren't lingering too long?

It's whackadoodle that I've never reviewed Reading Terminal Market, seeing as how it's one of those places I always encourage visitors to check out when they're in Philly. All kinds of yummy adventures await you inside those walls, the most awesome of which is Beiler's Whoopie Pie. Go early in the day because they sell out often - they're only $1 and are the closest approximation to earthly bliss I've ever experienced. 

Fresh produce, fish, meat, flowers, baked goods (make sure to stop by Flying Monkey Patisserie for some cupcakes to wash down your Whoopie Pie) and more...the choices are outrageous and there's something for everyone. I also love me some Delilah's for Southern food and the Amish food counter for some breakfast delights.  If you have the option of not visiting at lunchtime, I highly suggest you stay far away, as the experience just isn't the same when it's crowded; and trust me, the elbow to boob factor is crazy high during peak hours! If you've gotta be there between 11:30 and 1:30, might I suggest donning some full body armor?

The beautiful wife and I zipped into Milagro at 5:30 for our first visit since their soft opening.  We had made a reservation via OpenTable (note: when using this service, do it though the restaurant's website -- it costs them less) thinking it might be post-Friday busy.  Walking in, it felt a little silly, because it was fairly empty.  But that quickly changed -- by the time we left, it was packed or nearly packed.

Anyway, we were seated and chips and salsa came quickly, along with our drinks (Top Shelf Margaritas -- the good stuff.).  Yep, these are $10 a drink, _normally_, but if you plan ahead/speed down I-44 and get there between 4-6pm, you'll get them for 1/2 off.  Sweet.

We started off with the mahi mahi cerviche and the queso fundido.  The cerviche was excellent - very acidic and tart, but not overwhelming the fish.  But the queso fundido, good lord.  This is not a pot of melted cheese with some chopped peppers in it.  It's truly a skillet of melted cheese wicked awesome delight.  And the chorizo in it?  It's made in-house.  And it's not just ground pork with paprika.  It has lots of nice spicy peppers.  Bacon, suck it.  I'm a member of Team Chorizo.

To the entrees: the beautiful wife had the tacos al pastor -- porky and pineapplely deliciousness.  I'll let her update her review if she wishes, but it's a tasty dish.

But, the winner is easily was my barbacoa de cordero.  Yep, it's lamb.  And in the Lambtheon of great lamb dishes, this tops them all.  Do you remember Jerry Tarkanian the basketball coach?  Remember how he'd chew on towels during games?  OK, this isn't a great analogy, but when you bite into this lamb, sweet Tonacatecuhtli, you get this rush of lamb juicy wonderful crazy great.  Truly, I didn't want to swallow my bites, I just wanted to keep on squeezing the morsels  of lamb between my molars.  Re-reading this, it's kind of gross.  Just trust me, it's great.

Technically, I'm giving them 4.99999999999999999999 stars.  Why?  Because they're 15-20 minutes away from Downtown.  But I'll round up.

What a den of horrors. Easily one of the worst experiences the beautiful wife and I have had in St. Louis.

So after ordering, we were told "I'll bring out your food and you pick up your drinks at the bar." Got it. So Erin takes the little number sign stand and finds a place to sit. I wait for our drinks. This is where it get stupid -- we ordered a Bellini and I ordered an Irish coffee. For both of these drinks, there's nothing complex -- peach puree and champagne for the Bellini and coffee, whiskey, sugar, and cream for the Irish coffee (of course, I knew I was going to just get the first three ingredients topped with whipped cream, but lots of places do that).

Well, the drinkmaker (no way I'm calling him a "barista") first isn't anywhere to be found. Then he takes the Irish coffee mug and starts to clean it. For minutes. Seriously, if it's that dirty, GET ANOTHER MUG. And while others might say "hey, he was making sure it was clean" it took him at least two minutes to clean this mug. It wasn't him being meticulous, it was more along the lines of "GOD I HATE MAKING DRINKS" slow.

After he finally gets the mug clean, he starts to make it. Then for some reason, he wanders off to the back, making sure to stop by the frying to stir some beignets, then comes back empty handed (so it's not like he was "oh I need to grab something to make these drinks."

Then when one of his coworkers is close by, I can hear him verifying what a Bellini is. Yep, that's why you're a drinkmaker -- not a barista, not a bartender. Finally, after about 12 minutes (yep, we timed it), the drinks were ready. They were fine.

After first trying to sit inside (aborted due to the tables being claustrophobically close together, at least I apologize to the woman whose face I stuck my butt in), we sat outside. Out food eventually came out:

1) 3 free beignets (Yelp checkin offer with $10 purchase) -- these were really good, but it aint' saving them

2) For myself, I had the smoked ham (ham, scrambled eggs, cheddar cheese) on an everything bagel. I'll say that I made the mistake of having them try to make a panini out of a bagel -- it ended up slightly mushed and hard. Otherwise, it was fine.

3) For Erin, she had the roast turkey, which allegedly is turkey, scrambled eggs fresh avocado slices, and pepper jack cheese. Except neither the avocado or cheese made it to the sandwich.

We didn't bitch -- why? because they've already shown that they're slow and don't give a crap.

One and done.

The comparison between Pappy's and Bogart's is a given, so let's just get things out of the way:

1) Ribs -- Pappy's wins.  I love the sweet bark of Pappy's.  BUT Bogart's defeats everybody else that we've had in St. Louis.

2) "Secondary" meats -- oh boy, Bogart's beats Pappy's.  The sausage fatties are freaking incredible, the pastrami an interesting take (I say take because this isn't East Coast Jewish deli pastrami), the prime rib was mostly meat, with some aspects of fat (crappy buffet prime rib this is not.  Also, the prime rib looks "pale" instead of buffet "dark on the outside, red on the inside" so just be prepared)

3) The sides -- it's a toss up.  No sweet potato fries, but the potato salad is awesome; the slaw is very good; the pork skins were OK (as with Steven B., I'm not a pork rind guy, so I was hoping Bogart's could convert me, they didn't); the applesauce was great (very slightly chunky)

4) The service -- like with Pappy's, they treat you so much like family, you're ready to check Ancestry.com to make sure you're not related to them.

5) Ambiance -- like Pappy's, it's very basic, but as an added bonus, there are three (?) picnic tables outside.  Nice touch.

To summarize, the "Big Ben" (or "Adam Bomb") are ignored at Pappy's -- it's always two full slabs of ribs.  But at Bogart's, it's _always_ going to be the "Old Joe" -- one slab of ribs, but three sandwiches of excellent meats (and four sides).

Can't wait to go back!

At the beautiful wife's suggestion, we visited Grbic last Friday. While I'm a fan of trying new places, there was an element of "is this the right choice?"

Admittedly, we've been rotating between either "high end" places or blow your jaw off with spice ethnic establishments, I was a little apprehensive.

How foolishly arrogant. Or foolishly foolish. Because Grbic delivered delicious food. You can tell that this is a family joint -- the food tastes more like something you'd get in somebody's house rather than a restaurant. And that's a good thing.

We started off with a bottle of Romanian Cabernet  (Romanians make up most of the wine list) and an order of the cevapi.

The wine was great, but let's get to the cevapi -- oh good lord. Just wonderful -- a huge portion of ten sausages (for those too lazy to look at pictures, imagine breakfast links), grilled pitas, sliced tomatoes with feta, and most importantly, this accompanying sauce that I'd put on anything. Just amazing. I would have eaten the entire plate but I was reminded nicely by Erin that I could take the rest home.

(quick side note: before our main courses came out, we told our waiter that we wanted to take the rest home. First thing he said? "Do you want more sauce?" Well done.)

For main courses, I had the voldostana and Erin had the goulash. For the goulash, I'll just say that if you've had the American Betty Crocker version of goulash, well, that's like having a Filet-O-Fish and saying you've had sushi.

The voldostana ((baked spaetzle in a mushroom onion sauce, topped with slices of lean grilled beef and cheese, and broiled), as another reviewer mentioned, was ultimate comfort food. I wish i was eating this in front of a fireplace when it was snowing outside. Umami heaven.

Yes, service can be a bit less than desired, but as others have stated, this is really a family restaurant. There's a certain level of leeway I'm willing to give in these situations.

For the quality and amount of food you get, the price is right -- we spent around $65 (including $28 for the wine). I can't wait for our return visit.

This is my spot for a hearty stick to your ribs meal. I've never had a bad meal or bad service here and I love that consistency. 

This time around I had 1/2 of a tuna sandwich because the portions are ginormous and even though I'm a big eater, I wanted to save enough room for a huge piece of their delicious cheesecake! On the cheesecake, you can order a side of fresh strawberries to go with the strawberry compote it is served with. 

If sandwiches are your thing, their sandwiches are amazing here, you can't go wrong with any of them. I love the hot pastrami on rye. Again, portions are huge! One day when I'm feeling "extra" adventurous I'm going to try the tongue sandwich cause that's the sort of thing that gets my attention.  

If you try nothing else here, please don't go away without trying a huge bowl of the chicken noodle soup and add a matzoh ball. Also, try the potato knish, dip it in sour cream, trust me on that, it's the bomb! 

This restaurant also takes their COVID safety and precautions very seriously. The tables are very spread apart to ensure proper distancing. All employees here doing their absolute best to make us feel safe.

My family doesnt like the food here so if I go its alone. 

I really like the Renees special with their chicken  salad. I get the dressing on the side and this time they had loaded baked potato soup. One of their better soups. It looks like a large portion.  However its various greens a small bowl of soup and half a sandwhich. Their chicken salad has almonds in it and is very tasty on the toasted bread. They just dont give you much chicken salad and for $13.95 I always feel a little cheated

That said.  I eat here about 2 times  a year. The person next to me had lettuce wraps and she said they were great, I might try those next time, however whenever I stray from my go to meal I am disappointed. We will see. 

My drink was very good, The Mai Tai was perfect with the dark rum float and my bartender was very friendly. $13.00 for one drink is just too much at this level. 

I have happily paid more $$ for great food, its just good though and the $30.00 tab, before tip, for just me reminds me why I rarely eat here.

I was determined to find a great meal in Indianapolis and I did. After checking out 3 other places we went to this Irish grill. 

The inside is upbeat and centered around their bar. We were greeted promptly and the bartender gave me some great recommendations. Including a Raspberry Long Island which was a good choice. 

We ordered the Quarter Chicken with 2 sides for $11.99 off of their special menu. 

The food was great. The homemade onion rings were thick and cooked in clean oil because they tasted fresh, the color was golden and they were not oily and crumbly.  The zucchini and squash vegetable of the day was well seasoned and not mushy. 

Now there is the Chicken. Tender, flavorful and juicy, paired with the spicy barbeque sauce, or the sweet, finished the experience. 

If I ever visit indianapolis again, this will be one of my food stops.

This was my first time here. We looked at the menus for a couple of  local places and the brunch at Datz had a better selection.

It was right after opening and we sat outside and we were approached pretty quickly.

Our waitress was friendly and had good reccomendations. We chose the Short Rib Benedict and the Chicken Ranchero. Note: We added avocado to the breakfast sandwhich which was a great flavor/texture idea.

My first Benedict cane out luke warm with a very hard bisquit. However, when I asked  for my server the manager was inquisitive and proactively stated he would get me a new benedict.

I have to say I was impressed . The manager made and delivered it himself and the food was hot and the bisquit was perfect. I really liked their hollindaise sauce and the eggs still had the golden yolks to add creaminess to the dish. I originally had fruit with mine, strawberries and blueberries and this was the perfect side for me.

I will definately be back to Datz. Sometimes things aren't perfect however they can still be excellent with proper handling and this was.

I was really looking forward to trying Stein & Vine their local and the reviews looked good.

The place is quaint and our server was friendly and she did a good job reccomending menu items after she brought our drinks.

I really wanted something different and flavorful,  so we ordered the Nashville Hot Chicken and a Schnitzel with Pimento Cheese and Tots.

The Tots seemed like a favorite based on the menu layout and I was really ready to eat that crispy goodness.

The food - I thought about this review for a couple of days because I wanted to rate them higher, but I just cannot. 

Mainly they need to change their fryer oil, the goal is golden on the fried meats and that they do not taste like other things that have been in the fryer. The flavors they put together should have been amazing, but I was disappointed.

The chicken and pork were over cooked and the tots  were not even warm.

I doubt I'll go here again, I am glad I gave it a try.

On a possitive note the corn was amazing and the spicy cayenne pepper sauce is more like a paste and it packed a punch without losing its flavor. These 2 items and the friendly service are the only reason this is 3 stars.

After a cramped plane flight I was really looking forward to some good food at a popular place in Indianapolis. 

We were very disappointed. Our waiter was new yet friendly so that was ok. He didn't write anything we ordered down though so it wasnt suprising we had to ask for things. 

The mozzarella appetizer was pretty good, served without silverware or plates however. We had to ask for those, ice tea refills and water refills. 

My sons boneless wings came and they were out if ranch dressing for dipping, really. The flavor was good, however he said he wouldn't have ordered them if the server had told us that. 

My sandwhich wasnt very good at all. I pulled off the limp , soggy bacon ( lots of fat not rendered ) and we put it back on a plate for the manager.  My chicken breast was texturally odd and they put raw spinach on it. Not blanched or seasoned or fried crispy. The fries were cold and soggy and we just wanted to leave. 

The manager brought better bacon and new fries and even reduced our bill, I still felt cheated and that my only meal today was so bad.

I wish I would have skipped the restroom, the stalls had 0 seat covers, a seat was loose and there was trash on the floor. My son said a cockroach was running around in the men's room and it was also unclean.  So sad when its slow and there are employees milling around. 

I guess there are other location I am told are better, I will avoid them. Even though the manager was gracious,  based on the overall experience I just can't give higher stars. 

On a positive note, my drink was flavorful and fun,  it had a cute little duck swimming around in it.

So I left the previous place I was going to eat lunch at, everything for a reason I say. 

I was greeted promptly and sat outside on their covered deck. It's a sports oriented restaurant so it has several TVs and happy patrons. 

The bartender recommended a drink for me and the Salmon, I have  been looking for another Salmon place do I ordered Cajun Style Atlantic Salmon. 

The fish was amazing and I am a picky Salmon person. I liked to sauce  with it and the fish was moist and not fishy. I really enjoyed the vegetables as one if my sides , the mac and cheese needs a little help. It was all good though and the Salmon was a superstar. 

I have officially found another Salmon place and the patio is pet friendly. I'm glad I left Irish 31. The staff was friendly and I felt valued.

My son wanted soup, so the local place I know for great soup is Corner Bakery. 

I like their half sandwhich and half salad option when I eat here. Today I had a roast beef panini and southwestern chicken salad. 

The lettuce is fresh, the chicken is flavorful and the dressings they have are amazing. The panini had carmelized onion which added moisture and flavor to my meal. 

My son was very happy with the potato soup. Sorry, i was unable to snap a picture before he dove into the bowl. I have enjoyed this soup  before and I reccomend giving it a try if you like a heartier soup. 

The prices are reasonable and there is outside seating if you want to bring your dog for a quick bite.

Found this place while looking for pet  friendly patios. The fresh, farm to table concept looked great.

The outside patio is comfortable with lantern lighting, rustic tables and booths and my Aussie was promptly brought some water.

My server recommended the "Staff Steak Bowl" I asked about the chicken and she let me know this was so popular they held ot over for night 2. Sold,  I was excited. 

The dish was well presented in a bowl with lots of color. The pita bread was hot and crisp. This paired nicely with the hummus smear.

I saw a bite size piece of steak so that was next. I tried to chew it for a bit and gave up, looked around and it went back in the bowl. The server came over and asked about my meal. I let her know the steak was really tough, however the flavors were good. 

I tried cutting the steak very small, that did not work either. The manager came by to ask about my meal and I let him know it was very tough. The reply, " Its skirt steak" I said its really chewy and he said that is how it comes from the vendor. He did offer me a new steak. I replied if your telling me its going to be equally as tough than that's okay. He left. Skirt steak does not have to be tough. 

I tried the rice,  half of it was aldente, as in with crunch. For $ 19.00 this should have been a better dish. Farm to table is great. I think ranch to table is important also for this concept. 

One thing that was a plus were the bathrooms. Gender Neutral and super clean. 

My Aussie had the best experience,  because she had steak for dinner.

I received an email special for steak packs. I called and easily ordered for morning pick up today only.

8 steaks and a pound of beef tips for $80.00. They butcher their own meat so it has to be cooked or frozen in 2 days. Now I am an omnivore, however it's a bit much meat for me. I kept out the 2 Filets and the Cowboy Ribeyes and I packaged up the rest for the freezer. In the butcher paper, in a freezer bag, the wrapped tightly in foil.

I cooked the Filets tonight and the meat was amazing. Seared them in a cast iron and finished in the oven. I was a little disappointed that one of them was cut in half, but I which I didn't notice until it fell7 apart in the pan. This should have been cut up for tips or stew meat.

All in all I am happy with the value and the quality.

The atmosphere is not as exciting as it needs to be. They need a better ventilation system for all the smoke and the games are pretty boring. They got rid of a lot of the interactive games that make it fun. I guess they find like to pay the royalties on the fun name brand games. You also need to watch the 2 cent a line games you think are 1 cent. 

It's really not worth going here. I've been 4 times since it opened many years ago. The drinks are not free, and are "Over Priced", $100 bucks lasts twice as long in Vegas, the drinks are free, there are things to do" For Free " everywhere and most of the Hotels care enough to provide great ventilation so the smoke doesn't kill you . Find a cheap flight, a deal on a Strip or Old Vegas hotel and you'll have more fun for a little bit more money or maybe less .

And all the food , outside of one of the better sit down restaurants,  tastes  gross like smoke . Breathe in smoke with every bite. Yummy!

Ventilation Hard Rock Hotel Ventilation. Most people,  even smokers , dont like to eat in a smoky room.

Riverview has been waiting anxiously for this restaurant to open. I waited a few weeks before I went and then stopped by about 3pm on a Monday to be sure they were not slammed.

I was greeted promptly and shown a seat outside at the bar. I waited for a few minutes and the bartender finally came over to get someone a beer and said hi to me, however, I wasn't offered a menu, a water, a drink nor was I told that she would be with me anytime soon.

After a few more minutes I went inside and sat at the bar. This bartender was very friendly told me she was going to be happy to talk to me and even gave me a sample of there on tap rum drink. I ordered a drink from her, she gave me a menu and I selected the tacos.

I have to say I was very disappointed in the Tacos, the tortillas were raw and  chewy and they were not filled with much of anything. The pork belly taco, I was very much looking forward to, was more like a piece of crisp bacon. For $13.50 I expected more from the meal. Around Tampa Bay a really good taco is about $2.50 to $3 a piece. Yes, I'm on the river so I said okay $13.50 for three tacos let's do it.

The highlight of the meal were the sauces that the bartender went to get me from the kitchen they made the tacos much more edible.

If it wasn't for the amazing service I received inside at the bar I would have left the food 2 Stars. I will definitely give it some time and maybe I'll go back and try again however, I definitely not order the  Tacos or the Pork Belly Sandwhich if it's going to be crisp bacon.

On a positive note- the pink sauce they brought me was amazing.

Amazing day to be in John's Pass  

This is one of the best places on the boardwalk.

We were able to sit on their small deck situated out on the water under an umbrella and near a bunch of fans that have water spray.

I saw a dolphin in the channel, birds and fish and the breeze is amazing.

The food at Scullys can be 3 or 5 stars, but today was fantastic. I had the Grouper Nuggets and they were the best I have tried. Very lightly battered and 0 after taste. So good with some lemon and a bit of tarter sauce.

Then we went back inside, which is still open for a water view, where they had live music for a glass of wine and some fun. 

If you visit try the Grouper.

I was in Trinity today and decided to try an early dinner at a new place.

First the name caught my attention, how cool is "Zen Forrest" and the ratings were good.

The inside tables were separated and the staff wore masks. My waiter was very friendly and helped me with the menu.

The food here was amazing. I ordered Sesame Chicken and instead of rice they offered Wasabi Mashed Potatoes.

My salad came out fresh and my entree exceeded my expectations. The chicken was sliced and juicy with a lite, yet, crunchy breading, not the chicken parts coated in a ball of deep fried bread you normally receive. It was served with vegatables and the most delicious mashed potatoes. I never thought to make Wasabi Mash.

If I'm out this way again, I will be stopping by this little gem.

Last minute decision to have a family dinner landed us here.

I reccomend making a reservation, it was busy for early dinner.

Our sever was friendly and had a sense of humor. He served the salad  at the table which had a flavorful  ginger dressing.

I upgraded to filet with my chicken and shrimp.

The filet was tender, the chicken juicy and the shrimp went well with the fried rice and vegatables. I was very happy that everything didn't need extra yum yum sauce. I've been to other places and the food was not great. This was an amazing meal.

We will definately be back to this location.

First time eating at this restaurant tucked I away in a little  strip mall behind Applebee's

The restaurant was clean and the people were friendly. We were seated right away and brought some warm chips and salsa. 

We also ordered some queso with a scoop of ground beef in it (I recommend this)

The queso was great, creamy and smooth. The spiced ground beef made it extra satisfying.

We ordered the pick three with a mini chimichanga, tamale and an enchilada. The food came out warm and looked great. The flavors were very good. The shredded chicken was perfect in the chimichanga. I even enjoyed the rice and beans, which I normally avoid

The also have a covered outside patio to enjoy. We will definately be back.

This is the best larger take out experience we have ever had. 

I needed to start with that because I was impressed. We ordered off the Catering menu and selected a combo. 

The 2 large salads had bottled dressing on the side and there were serving utensils for each dish. 

The sauces were separate from the pasta trays which makes travel and reheating ideal . 

The Chicken Parm we ordered was very tender, seasoned well and cut in sections for a larger group. 

We really liked the Shrimp Primevera, a lighter option,  with the vegetables and sweet Shrimp. 

The toasted Ravioli were a little over cooked, however they still tasted great. 

There were even 14 little custard style desserts included, I don't normally get a dessert so they appreciated the treat. 

The GM Haley was gracious and made me feel like they wanted our business. There are  4 other restaurants we normally rotate around, however,  all 16 of my employees said they want to order from Olive Garden again and that this experience was better then when they have dined in. 

Thank you for the great luncheon.

Customer service only review***

So I checked in,  anticipating a great meal, this is one of my places to visit, and ended up walking out. 
 
There were children screaming  when I walked in. Ok. No worries little kids squeal. Irish pubs are family oriented  

The bartender greeted me when the manager went back into the kitchen. I asked for a menu and she asked me if I wanted anything, in mid sentence she turned and walked away, because the manager came back.  I wanted a drink and had questions about the menu. 

Meanwhile more screaming. I look behind me and 3 kids ages about 7-12 are sitting on the window ledge and they are screaming, and one child is jumping around . Okay,little babies and toddlers can cry and fuss, these are older children and they are sitting on the window ledge of a business. 

The bartender has still not come back to me, no need to get the manager he is standing  in front of me oblivious. It's okay to ask other patrons to respect your restaurant. 

I walked out and went to the next nearby place on my list Crabby Bill's.

I wish we had 1/2 stars because based on the service and the value of my meal I would use that here. 

RTs has epanded their menu, salad bar and added drink specials, however, there is still just something missing in their entrees. 

I had Asiago Chicken and added a salad bar for $1.99 so the total meal was $20.00 .if your a mushroom lover this will make you happy. The overall flavor profile is not as dramatic as you would expect from the ingredients. I expected more, that's on me. I have one of the chicken breasts left for my lunch tomorrow and the meal was good, not great. 

I like creating my own salad, so I come here every few months for that and because their patio is pet friendly.

This restaurant is in Armature Works in downtown Tampa. 

They were out of the Breakfast Brisket Bisquit they advertise when we got their at 10:30, so we ordered the Korean Philly to share. 

They have a menu board that showcases their food and it looked delicious. 

We were very disappointed.  I realize pictures dont look exactly the same as what you recieve,
 however our sandwhich was a bit sad. The meat was a little chewy and it lacked the toppings pictured. Overall it had a pretty good flavor or I would assign 2 stars to this experience. 

The $11 dollar price for the Philly left me feeling a bit cheated. Next time we will pick an alternate vendor for food .

First word "Great"

We left the first place we stopped at before even being seated and decided to pull up Yelp and read reviews.

We decided on this little place down the street and we were not disappointed.

The smells inside were marvelous, however, we wanted to be outside in the beautiful day last weekend, so we sat outside. People were driving their old cars down main street, dinner and a show!

We started with the goat cheese and shrimp. This was a hit for the table. The herb mixture in the goat cheese balanced nicely with the sweetness of the shrimp, we ate it all

My son ordered a watermelon salad with blackened chicken and, of course, I went for the Salmon.

I will order this salad in the future it was refreshing and flavorful.

The salmon was a super star. Blackend and  moist topped with a light sauce and accompanied  by roasted, not mushy, vegatables. My other side was a grit cake the server reccomended and we all liked the flavor.

Good service, great atmosphere and great food. I'll be back.

Amazing. So glad I kept walking past the Starbucks on main street looking at the restaurants and shops. I walked right past this one Cafe and immediately stopped and turned around.

The aroma of their Coffee was like an invisible wall for me.

The employee at the window was very friendly and informative. She told me about their beans and that they grow in their farm in Costa Rica by a waterfall, hint that's why it's called waterfall coffee.

They also make some of their own syrups and lavender vanilla sounded devine. They have 1% milk as an option, much better than non fat milk heated. The coffee was amazing, smooth and fragrant and I didn't not need to add another shot.

I couldn't resist and I  bought a bag of beans to take home.

They also have a breakfast /lunch menu and the cutest little seating area outside.

If your in Safety Harbor and need a coffee I highly recommend this spot. I'll be back.

The first time I ever went here we did not like the pastries we selected , so I went again and not only were the peanut butter cookies and the brownie cookies great, the shrimp from the hot table was fantastic. 

I have been back 3 times since and I have not been able to duplicate the experience. I purchased some  guava pastries for my employees and they did not like them, I tried one and they were lacking compared to my regular local bakery.

I tried the shrimp again and it was pretty good, the sugar cookie I bought was not. 

Now,  I went and picked up a pumpkin pie from here,  instead of The Village Inn. I had misgivings about the way it looked and smelled and should have purchased a back up. I  also bought some more shrimp and it was cold. I ate a couple and then thought better of it and tossed them out.. That said the pumpkin pie we had for Christmas Eve dinner was not good at all. No one in the family liked it, odd flavor and an aftertaste from the crust were the chief complaints, and the vote was to toss it out.

A great place should have great food the majority of the time. I have found they have a few key baked goods that are great, some that are just okay and others that are just not good. Additionally, the cold shrimp from the hot table has me sufficiently done eating here. 

Unless I am in the area and I need a peanut butter cookie , I will not be back to Moreno Bakery.

wow the hype around this freebirds is real. I've had freebirds in my hometown and didn't like it so I was hesitant to try this one but everyones who has been here that I know says that this freebirds is so much better so I decided to give this place a try. My bf and I started off our sb trip at freebirds and there were so many different places we wanted to eat at so we split a quesarrito which was really good. We wanted to get the nachos too but we thought we'd be too full to try the other places we wanted to eat at, but at least it gives us another excuse to come here! 

Parking- street parking or if youre lucky, you can get one of the 5 spots in their tiny lot.

The actual restaurant is located upstairs! They have a bar downstairs if you don't really want to wait or just want a small plate. 

Parking
If you're lucky, you may be able to grab a free 90 min parking spot (right before the paid parking area) but there's less than 20 spots available. Paid parking is $2/hr. 

It is nice to have a view and sit outside, but your food may get cold quickly. Also the seagulls fly really close to you if you leave food unattended. 

-Clam chowder bowl- Probably can pass on this the next time you're here. I had high hopes for the clam chowder, but it was okay. It was also lukewarm when it came out and got cold in about 5 minutes. 
-Calamari plate- Pretty good, can't go wrong with this plate
-Garlic baked clams- surprisingly pretty good too!

As my friend's maid of honor, I was in charge of the cake for her upcoming bridal shower. I stopped into the store a week in advance to order the cake, which was sufficient enough time.

Looking through their picture books of cakes they've done, I found one that matched the 'beachy' theme I wanted. I spoke with one of the girls working (who are all very friendly) and le French patissier himself who was very French ifyouknowwhatImean. Very 'Nonono you cannot do zat. Ze cake weel zust crumble and you weel not be appy' when I said I wanted the buttercream frosting with the regular style spongey cake. He cracked me up though.

In the end, I picked out a 12" single tiered cake with mocha filling, and for decorations I gave something specific but also left room for le French patissier to 'feel the flow and improvise'. (aka I walked out of the bakery fearing my cake was in the hands of a freestyling ar-teest.)

The morning of the shower I came to pick up the cake bright and early. The girls behind the counter almost gave me a heart attack when they couldn't find it at first. Luckily it was discovered right in front of us. I peeked into the box and saw that the cake was gorgeous - it had a sandy colored butercream frosting with multi-hued seashells. I exhaled in relief that the cake looked even better than my original idea.

The cake was cut up and passed out during the shower and as I dug into mine, I realized that the flavors weren't blending well. Something about the mocha buttercream filling felt gelatinous in my mouth, as if the cream didn't break down well. The pound cake was okay, but the frosting had the same strange gelatinous texture. I thought that maybe the wine got to my head (I was the host, I'll be damned if I don't get some wine to ease the stress), and that maybe my tastebuds were off. But I looked around the room and noticed that most guests hadn't finished nearly half their slices of cake either. The room was filled with women, and I don't care what kind of woman you are, you will finish your cake if it's good.

In the end, the consensus was that while the cake turned out beautifully visual-wise, it didn't match up in taste. Which is a compromise considering the cake was $75, but still...

I've also tried their macarons which are pretty bad (too spongy, not enough merengue) - nothing compared to Bouchon's in NYC or Laduree. However, I grabbed a chocolate croissant when I picked up the cake and it was delicious, held me down a couple of needed hours.

If you dine at the Dutch Eating Place next door, you have to make a stop at Beilers too. It's like BritBrit without trashy extensions; you can't have one without the other.

As for selection and freshness, this has to be one of the best bakeries out there. Pie? 6 varieties. Whole and by the slice. Bread? Loaves. Pumpkin or cinammon. Cake? Pound cake, coffee cake, cake cake, chocolate cake, vanilla cake. Cookies? Define cookie. Whoopie pie with cake cookies? Choco chip cookies. Snickerdoodles. Sometimes, just maybe, if you go right before they close they'll knock down prices even further than the already cheap tags.

I stock up on the cakes and cookies with creme fillings as if diabetes is going out of style. I guarantee you can get dessert to feed a whole family for under $10 or I'll buy it off you. We can meet in person and I'll have my napkins and forks handy for immediate consumption.

Man, I totally wanted to hate this place so I could be cooler than you, Steven Starr. (El Vez around the corner is okay, but charging $13 for guacamole?! Stoooo-pid. Highway robbery.) But nooo, I unwillingly liked it. Maybe even loved it.

We were immediately seated at one of the tables on the balcony upstairs because I think they thought we were ugly (ie seat them far away from the majority of diners) but I don't care because it gave me the chance to talk loudly and spy on everyone downstairs.

On the way to our table the floor grazed my feet since I was wearing sandles and I was THIS close to taking them off so I could curl my toes around the luscious shag carpet. I restrained myself.

I loved my crispy calamari salad. They were definitely not skimpy on the calamari, thank goodness; otherwise, I would've left hungry. And my drink, the Blind Melon, was super sweet which was unexpected because it had SoCo in it.

Our waitress was sweet, and the whole place was fun and 'in' without being pretentious or overrated. Loved it! And it didn't even break the bank.

Cheesesteaks, water ice, Tastykakes, and scrapple. That's what Philly does best.

Who does the Philly cheesesteak best? Uhmm.. I donno. I've had Jim's, Geno's, Pat's, and everything in between but c'mon now.. a rose by any other name would smell as sweet, and they're all just names. The scent of a 'wiz with' would still make me salivate if it were sitting in the gutter. 

I hadn't had a cheesesteak in months and I was craving one after my 4 hour bus trip from NYC so not only was I hungry, I was cranky. The emotional eater in me ordered a wiz with, with extra wiz. It sounds confusing (cheesesteak with onions and wiz, with extra wiz on top), and disgusting and really unhealthy, but it was amaaazing. We took our cheesesteaks to the car and fogged up the windows like Titanic. My only peeve is that the bread's never toasted at Jim's. I don't want impotent bread, please!

If you've never had a cheesesteak before and think that Jim's isn't worth the hype, you just don't 'get it' yet. I didn't like my first or second cheesesteak. I was like, this is it..? The cheesesteak is something you have to be craving to enjoy.. like when you're drunk, hungover, or feeling gluttonous; you can't have it forced on you. I didn't like it till I figured out what I do like - which is a cheesesteak with onions, wiz, and ketchup. Everyone has their preferences. 

And if you have had millions of cheesesteaks and still don't like Jim's.. then you're tastebuds are way more refined than mine. Ignorance is bliss!

When my gf desperately had to go to the bathroom after our night's first happy hour (girls can't pee in bushes as inconspicuously as guys), Valanni was the first place we saw. And whaddya know?! We made it in time for their happy hour too!

After perusing the menu which includes half off a full page of drinks and tapas, I noticed we were minutes away from 7pm - the end of Valanni's happy hour, dun dun DUN! I'm not ashamed of my thriftiness, so I asked Mr. Bartender, "Excuse me, am I allowed to order 2 drinks at a time?! It's almost 7pm!" He explained, "Sorry, no. Otherwise guys would be able to come in here and order 4 drinks at once and drink for hours on $20." Hmm.. your logic makes sense but wasn't the answer I was looking for. He continues, "But.. if you throw the first drink back you could definitely get another one stat." Aha! Now you're thinking!

So in 10 minutes I was able to have two well mixed $5 cocktails and a $5 plate of emapanadas. We exited Valanni to continue on to dinner already "happy" and it was still light outside. Yesssssss.

Easily the worst experience I've had at any establishment in Tampa. 

The drinks were ok and the crowd was fine, but the bouncers were completely out of control. One in particular, Sergio, was picking fights with everyone. This made for a very hostile environment. I first noticed him when he plowed through a dozen people to drag someone outside. His reason for doing so: the guy was standing too close to the VIP table. There was no warning, just instant violence. When the guy's friends asked Sergio why he did it, he said "mind your own f***ing business." He continued to be completely out of line and acted aggressively towards everyone. His violent behavior was equivalent to someone you'd expect to find in a prison, not a reputable club.

The owner seemed to condone this behavior because apparently Sergio has been working there for a while and has built quite a negative reputation. There have been several similar instances in the past.

Long story short: unless you get bottle service, prepare to be treated like trash. Also, prepare to defend yourself in case you get attacked by Sergio.

Doesn't it always seem like the best places are the ones you never heard of? Someone mentions or recommends them, you decide to try it out, and love the place? And it's, GASP, not on Jasper or Whyte Ave. That's exactly what happened to me tonight with Lan's.

It's in a pretty random spot (unless you go to NAIT), tucked into that weird strip mall on 118 Ave. with the Value Village near that bingo hall. It's much nicer and more modern on the inside than you would expect before walking in.

The owner, Tom, was totally friendly the whole time we were there, from the time we sat down, to when we went up to order, to checking on us throughout the meal. The other staff I briefly encountered were also great. I feel like this is what really pushes a restaurant over the edge for me and makes me happy. Owners/staff that just radiate love for their restaurant. I did notice his familiarity with some regulars and liked that. I'm looking forward to becoming one of them!

Their menu is medium sized, with about 25 items to choose from. And boy did I have a hard time deciding. I chose the red curry with noodles ($9.95). The bowl was deceiving! What a huge portion. The flavour was great, milky and spicy but not overwhelming at all. I couldn't stop eating it, and I was sad when I had to stop! Next time I'll get rice to soak up all the yummy sauce. We also had the spring rolls and green onion cake, which were fresh and light. Very, very reasonable prices. I think the curry was the most expensive thing. My dad had a medium vermicelli bowl and I think it was less than $7.

I'm looking forward to going to Lan's again and bringing all my friends!

P.S. - Woo hoo, 100th review!

I'm a sucker for 50s style diners, and Rockin' Robyn's definitely delivers in the atmosphere department - black and white checkered floors, red vinyl booths and stools at a long counter, a jukebox and 50s tunes playing. I was smiling as soon as I walked in. 

Even though I've worked nearby for over a year, I only finally went for lunch here last week with my dad. We arrived around 11:45am and it wasn't busy, but it was bumpin' only 10 or so minutes later, with a lot of people who seemed like regulars. We perused the lunch menu which is totally typical diner fare - sandwiches and burgers, shakes, and a couple of salads thrown in for good measure. They also serve breakfast and I saw a couple of delicious looking, heaping plates walk by that I'm excited to try another time. Risking the wrath of my coworkers, I went ahead and ordered the garlic burger, smothered with garlicky mushrooms and sandwiched between two pieces of garlic bread, with crinkle cut fries, while my dad ordered the steak sandwich. My burger was delicious, juicy, huge and fresh. So good! So many fries came on the plate, I could only finish half of them. 

Service was good, waitress was nice enough and efficient. At the end of the meal we paid at the counter and the waitress who took our payment seemed super nice. They have a glass case full of amazing looking desserts at the front, too, if you have room. I'm definitely going to hit up this spot more regularly from now on.

This was one of the first restaurants I have visited when I first came to Philly and one of the reasons I fell in love with the City of Brotherly Love. 

The mastermind behind the gelato is a chef from Italy who has won some international gelato competition. Is it bad that my first thought wasn't Wow good for him but rather Why the heck was I not invited to try all the gelato at this international gelato thing?? 

Speaking of trying all the gelato, you know those obnoxious people who insist on trying every flavor of ice cream/gelato in the store before picking their two flavors in a cup but please put the cone on the side? Can't stand those people. (definitely not one of them...)

But you can have it all here with the gelato flight! A tasting of five flavors of your choosing. My favorites are to get a balance of fruity, tart, nutty, rich, and Dark/Handsome. AKA the cherry/cream one, mango sorbet, pistachio, espresso, and dark chocolate (fondante).

Their coffee and pastries are legit too. Not to mention their savory gelato/pasta dishes! These are fun to try once; I think I prefer getting their gelato straight up to be honest. But come on, you need to tell your grandkids that you've tried spaghetti carbonera with prosciutto gelato sitting on top.

This was my second trip to H'ours this year and it's fast becoming a favorite stop in the Tampa area. My first visit was in May, on a warm day enjoying drinks at their outdoor bar but (unfortunately) not able to snag a seat for dinner. On my most recent visit, we were smart enough to make dinner reservations in advance and wow, was it delicious.

We started again at the outdoor bar - although the evening was a bit cooler and there was a stiff breeze, so the experience wasn't quite as pleasant (weather-wise) as it was in May. But the service was still excellent, and the drinks (I again enjoyed a dirty vodka martini) were delish. The bar area is small, which gives opportunities to chat with others and meet the locals.

Soon enough the time for dinner arrived. We were seated inside (yay for warmth!), and were excited to peruse the menu. We started with an increddddible appy of cambembert with fig sauce and pepper jelly. It was the perfect sweet/salty/creamy/spicy treat to get our taste buds going before dinner arrived. For the main course I ordered butterfish which was phenomenal - so fresh and a nice firm texture. I've never had butterfish before, but it was delish and perfectly seasoned. My date ordered cajun scallops and I was lucky enough to sneak a bite - also an excellent choice.

What really put H'ours over the top, though, was the amazingly friendly service from the bar to the restaurant. It was Halloween weekend, so the place was busy, but you wouldn't know it from the way the staff took their time and was so friendly. This place will definitely stay in my Tampa Bay rotation!

I was just perusing my recent Yelp pics and ran across a pic from Sea Hags - and realized I never wrote a review of my awesome experience there!

It was the last full day of an epic Florida vacay last May and we still hadn't experienced a waterfront tiki bar. So we ended up at Sea Hags and it was JUST what we were looking for: very old-school, borderline divey (but in a good way), the kind of place you wouldn't know had a secret tiki bar out back unless you knew someone who lives around there.

To access the tiki bar, you first have to walk through the enormous main bar, which is apparently quite happening with live music and all sorts of events on your average evening. We were there for lunch, though, so (aside from a few folks having a mid-day beer) it was pretty quiet. We shuffled our way out back to the tiki bar portion of the establishment, and it was pretty cool.

I'm not sure what officially makes something a tiki bar, but Sea Hags fit the bill. Bright colors, surf paraphernalia, that look that Gilligan himself (perhaps with a little help from Mary Ann) helped decorate the place...add in some tropical-themed drinks and a view of the marina and it definitely earned the tiki name.

We ordered a couple of drinks and some "appies" in anticipation of lunch later at another nearby spot. Well, after a GINORMOUS pound of the freshest possible jumbo shrimp and a plate of crab-stuffed mushrooms we didn't end up eating for hours. The prices were amazing, too. The prawns, served chilled with a healthy dash of Old Bay (?) on top were phenomenal. The mushrooms were great, too, but those prawns were the star of the show. And at only $15.95 for the entire pound they were wayyyy less than prawns usually cost if you buy them at the fish market, much less prepped and served at a restaurant.

As I plan my next trip to the area I'm fantasizing about another trip to Sea Hags...and another pound of those prawns!

If there's one word I could use to describe the offerings at Washoe Public House (other than "delicious", course), it would be 'thoughtful."

The chef, Brett Moseley, has clearly taken great care to ensure that every item on the menu is well-balanced and flavorful. Even simple things, like a small artisan salad, manage to combine sweet with salty, tangy with bright, to create memorable cravability. The food is truly inspiring! Personally, I am a sucker for their Sticky Thai Wings. I find myself craving that sweet/savory/sticky combo on a regular basis!

Their patio is quiet and beautiful. The restaurant itself is centrally located at the cusp of downtown/midtown, yet it manages to escape the hub-bub of both. Service here has always been exceptional, and the care taken during COVID has also proven to be quite thoughtful. An added bonus would be their effort to use locally-sourced ingredients wherever possible.

Washoe Public House is absolutely in my top 3 places that I recommend to anyone looking for a sweet date spot, good happy hour, or quiet business lunch. I hope they continue to thrive and blossom!

Love at first taco! Even during the first day open to the public, Estella is serving up - arguably - the best tacos in Reno.

After finding parking just down the street, we shimmied around The Jesse to find the Estella hiding in plain sight. It's counter-service with a small bar inside, though most of the dining is meant to occur on the beautiful and comfy outside patio. The concept is simple - Tacos y Mezcal. Get some tacos, get some tequila, maybe some housemade chips and guac, and relax outside in this urban oasis.

We decided to get one of each taco, including an extra Carnitas and an extra beer-battered fish taco (because YUM), though we passed on the veggie tacos to leave more room for the meats. We also decided to try one of their special cocktails - Mezcal and Tequila with lime and prickly pear (I think.) It was smokey and slightly sweet and just delicious. It went really well with the chips and this amazing red salsa that we scored at the salsa bar. 

On to the TACOS. We started with the carnitas and our mouths were so grateful we did! Carnitas were absolute perfection - tender and juicy and exceptionally flavorful. Porky goodness at its absolute best! They were wonderfully complemented by diced onion, tangy green salsa, and - wait for it - FRIED CHEESE. They are presented on freshly made corn tortillas that seriously taste like a disc of love. Ugh, I have no more words for these tacos. They are stunning... the stuff that taco dreams are made of!

The al pastor were also good, with big fatty pork pieces and similar accoutrements to the carnitas. Carne asada and mushroom tacos both had a super interesting chile sauce that was spicy and really smokey. Finally, the fish tacos were fresh and light, despite the beer batter. The spicy crema and red cabbage just added a level of balance that is so aggressively sought after in a taco! Simply amazing and intensely crave-worthy.

I am so very impressed with the quality and level of customer service achieved on their first day of service. Enjoying incredible elevated tacos and deeply delicious Mezcal on a beautiful patio... I can't imagine a better evening in downtown Reno.

I was here on Saturday night with Nina S and Sarah F. I can't believe I haven't been here sooner. Service was excellent. Food was delicious. I split the chicken fajitas and pastor pork tacos with my friend. Both portions were very big and we had left overs. Food is authentic. The pork tacos came with 3 tacos with a generous amount of pork in each taco topped with cilantro and onions for only $6. The fajitas were a nice size portion of chicken, bell peppers and onions with tortillas on the side. They also give complimentary chips and salsa. One of the salsas was very spicy. I hear you can get an even spicier salsa from the back upon request but I don't know if I dare. Our waiter was awesome.

BYOB. They were fine with us bringing in both wine and vodka for our table. 

I don't think you can find better Mexican for the price.

It is a nice size restaurant and there were plenty of tables on a Saturday night since most of their orders are delivery so this would be a good spot for a group.

I absolutely love 9th Street Market-  the mix of traditional Italian vendors and authentic Asian and Mexican restaurants and shops. On 9th Street south of Washington, you have a strip of Mexican restaurants and shops. Then on 9th north of Washington Ave, you have the produce vendors, meat and cheese stores and other restaurants. On and around Washington Ave, you find numerous Vietnamese restaurants.

I live a block away and frequent 9th Street north of Washington every Saturday. I save a ton on groceries by shopping at the Italian Market for all my produce and most of my meats. Here is a quick overview of the prices I paid on Saturday:

- $1 for pound of strawberries (sometimes the strawberries are organic, sometimes not)
- $1 for a bucket of broccoli- yes a bucket- probably about 3 lbs
- $1 for bag of 2lbs of limes
- $1 for 6 lemons
- $2 for 3 grapefruits but some weeks there as cheap as 6 for $2
- $1 for bag of white onions- about 8 small to medium size onions
- $3 for 2 lbs of grapes
- $1.50 for 2 bags of carrots
- $1 for container of organic spring salad mix
- $2 for 3 containers of small tomatoes
- $1 for large eggplant
- $1 for 3 red peppers
- $3 for lb of boneless chicken breast

I do a quick walk up 9th street and check out which vendors have the best price and freshest produce. I bring two strong bags and I walk back and hit up the places with the best prices/ freshest produce. I have no idea where the produce comes from and I am sure most is not organic- sometimes the packages of strawberries or salad mix will read organic but other produce is just out in the open and ready to be picked. 

I have heard from others that the produce goes bad too fast. I have been shopping here on a weekly basis for almost a year and don't find that to be true or any different from buying produce in grocery store. Sure- if you buy strawberries at the end of a hot day at 4 or 5pm and they are really ripe, they will only last a couple of days. But I have bought peppers, carrots, eggplant, lemons, etc that have lasted weeks. To keep my produce lasting a long time, I use Ziploc Brand Fresh Produce bags and toss a paper towel in the bag- I find this keeps produce lasting up to 4 times as long. And I change out the paper towel every couple of days.

Tortilleria San Roman is a little place on 9th street on the corner at around Montrose- if walking from Washington on 9th towards Christian, it will be on your right after Carpenter. I think they have the best salsa in Philly, especially the green salsa. They also have a machine spitting out fresh torillas with sample salsas. Every time I walk in, I get a tortilla handed to me. They only sell tortilla, chips and salsa and it's not an eat in place, but you have super nice Mexican people making fresh tortillas, chips and salsa right there. And they are delicious and pretty cheap. 

Keep on walking past Christian Street to Sarcones which has some of the best bread in Philly- but get there early because they often sell out by the afternoon.

And bring cash- produce is outside and this is a real market so you will need cash. Smaller dollar bills are also appreciated.

You want a quaint little restaurant that looks like a Mom and Pops style place, you've found the right spot. Gendusa's is an Italian restaurant with some of the best pizza in the city. It is homemade crust and fresh ingredients that are combined with Italian love, probably from someone's Maw Maw back in Sicily. Anyways, the pizzas rock. We got the Carlo Gambino and added ham to it. It was definitely big enough to share amongst two or three people. 

We also shared a Caesar salad that was huge! The sweet tea is very tasty too. In addition, some folks had the crabmeat stuffed mirlitons that looked great. Another had the seafood cannelloni. The meatballs were huge too. You gotta try this place in the Rivertown district of Kenner. Definitely a hidden gem of New Orleans metro area. This is yet another reason why Kenner is so great when it comes to trying foods from around the world.

I dig the soft serve + cake concept. I was terrified that the combo would be cloyingly sweet, but not at all. You can opt for your own custom creation: you select your soft serve flavor, then cake flavor, and lastly, the sauce. Check out the swirls of the day. 

After perusing the 'Curated Flavors' section of their menu, I decided to order the I Love You So Matcha (matcha soft serve, vanilla cake, and red bean sauce) and It Takes Two to Mango (mango soft serve, vanilla cake, condensed milk). Cute names, right? Prevalent natural mango flavor and notable matcha flavor. I need to come back to try the sesame soft serve! 

The happy owner is super charismatic and hospitable. He offered us samples and cracked jokes the entire time I was ordering. 

Delicious dessert on a warm day and great service. Highly recommend.

I usually give businesses the benefit of the doubt, but I'm trying to be polite when I say that this place is unprofessional all the way up to the manager. From just checking in to play a game, everyone behind the counter was confused and couldn't do something as simple as add me to a lane and hand me my shoes. They first told us an incorrectly high price per game and they refused to yield until after significant convincing. They finally admitted they were incorrect and lowered the price. 

Later when checking out we asked for our license back. They couldn't find it and accused US of losing it. We insisted that no one at any time attempted to return a license. We asked to speak to the manager. He said his name is Zachary.  They did a (very) simple search of the place and continued to insist that we lost it, saying (in a very stern tone) "look, I can guarantee you that I gave you a license". At no time did the manager or any of the employees show empathy or apologize. We left the building for a few minutes and came back to find them frantically searching the floor with a flashlight- which shows that they know they lost it. 

We're all human, so mistakes happen. But when they do happen, you have to own up to it rather than accuse others to cover your faults. This type of treatment is NOT good for business or any moral situation for that matter. 

I will not be coming back to this place.

So I've been sleeping on this place and I feel like a doof. Tucson BBQ, in general, is not good. Went to a party a while back that had catered from Smokey Mo and it was delicious. I wanted to check this spot out but I didn't. Enter: global pandemic. 18+ months removed, I found myself hankering for some legit smoked meats and finally got myself here. Look, BBQ has all sorts and everyone has their favorite style, but what they're making here is good KC stuff. It's tender, delicious, sauced, and fairly priced. I got the rib tip special, but I've had the pulled pork and the brisket and they're all banging. Indoor seating is small but serviceable, and there's a huge patio when the weather won't melt your shoes. This place deserves your business not just because it's local and not a chain, but because it's good food, period. There isn't a lot of great BBQ in town, but add this place to the list  Check em out.

Went on "an adventure" to this bakery - it was several miles and tolls from home. The FB ad lured me in and the sweet story on their website made me feel like I would arrive to a quaint little place with family values and a welcoming spirit.  Nope. The donuts were tasty but the service was both pushy and dismal.  Too bad.  Once and done for us.

SO GOOD!!! I am a huge fan of bowls so I was very excited when I saw Big Island Poke open down the street from me.

I ordered the spicy tuna bowl and it was great! The brown rice was really good. I hate when I go to a place and their rice has a weird after taste. This was not the case at all! Large amounts of tuna and delicious onion crisps!

They also have smoothies that I will definitely try next time.

It's a whole in the wall drive thru window place! Do not miss it! Pull in and get some good healthy food!

Talk about one of my go to places in Sparks. I do have to say this one of the best Mexican food joints in the area.

The food is killer! It's pretty authentic and super tasty! It all starts with you grabbing a bowl of chips and your favorite salsa to munch on while you wait for your order. Also grab a bag to go home if it's to go. They have the basic fountain soda and nice select of bottle drinks.
