Staff is friendly along with the cooks who you can see working away in the kitchen. 

If you haven't tried Jalapeños head over and get a chicken chimichanga or some enchiladas! Dont forget the beans and rice! Nom nom! 

They also serve breakfast! So grab a breakfast burrito!

After a long Saturday of running errands, I had a craving for some great food! Not just any old meal was gonna do it. I knew that if I grabbed some crab legs, I'd be utterly satisfied! And I was certainly right! 

I first tried Exotic on the Run about a year ago and I wasn't impressed. They have definitely stepped up their game. I ordered the crab legs and shrimp half combo. There was nothing half about it. The portions were great and it was packed with flavor! The crab tasted fresh and sweet, The shrimp were juicy and huge, and The butter sauce was an added treat. It came with two sides so I ordered potatoes and sausage. Unfortunately, they gave me corn instead of sausage, but I was still satisfied. 

The service was good as well. I called my order in (highly recommended!) and when I pulled up it was ready. 

I'm really glad I gave this place another shot! Just make sure to check your order before you leave.

Stock's Bakery does indeed make the best pound cake in the nation.  I believe that.

Ive also recently found their butter cakes to be authentic!  It's few and far between a good butter cake that should be flaky and buttery but gooey inside this shallow tinned cake which goes for just over $3 and enough sugar to set your whole family on the road to diabetes. ;)

Last time i grabbed a few fresh donuts as well and found them to be excellent.  So, this is a regional gem.  We must cherish it and never let it close!

The gentleman behind the outside bar was so unfriendly I felt uncomfortable from the moment I sat down. Hey, everybody has a bad day, but don't take it out on your customers. I  ordered a draft beer and asked for a menu. After throwing the menu at me, I ordered the moules frites with white wine, garlic and parsley.

What came out were inedible, way too old mussels with no sauce whatsoever. I immediately sent them back and asked for my check.

Any kitchen that would send those out to customers clearly doesn't care. Combined with the sour demeanor of the bartender,  I'll never return. 

As a new local to New Hope, this is not a place I can recommend. Avoid!!

We find the most current renovation the staff can be snobby at times. They refuse to seat smaller parties if all they have is a 6/8 top free. We asked to be seated at a free table and was denied. Food is usually decent but because of staff we will not be returning. Couples should stay away.

"Oh my god, this is amazing" - exhaled the person at the table next to ours. Perhaps it was NAIVE of me to expect something semi authentically "Latin American" or "Mexican", as their yelp page claims. With how low the bar is, Chipotle is THE best Mexican restaurant in the world.

Your patronage starts off almost in an intriguing manner - there is no menu, because the food offering changes twice a day, and they will haul over a chalkboard to demonstrate that phenomenon. 

The server (who was nice, to be fair), then starts her sales pitch. You repeatedly hear "amazing", "bed of salad" and "beautiful" in the description of the dishes. We ordered a beef molcajete and salmon. Imagine my surprise when everything arrives on a pile of lettuce and spinach. While I appreciate the faux healthy aspect, the end result is inauthentic and underwhelming in every possible way. Tortillas? I kid you not, they're the generic, Mission brand soft shell white flour tortillas that cost you $2 a bag. 

Presentation? The beef molcajete arrived on a regular old plate (if you Google "molcajete", you'll come across a stone tool used as a plate in this case - as in, YOU HAD ONE JOB), and the salmon was unceremoniously buried under a pile of greens - it took a while to confirm it hasn't gone AWOL. Flavor? Bland greens that get no kick out of the widely advertised salad "dressing"; overly salty unappetizing looking strips of beef (and btw, I LOVE salty food, but this was almost unbearable). Prices? I went in thinking "okay, it's allegedly one of the best restaurants in Tucson, I'm sure it's worth it..." ehhhh, it's NOT. 

Don't waste your money, time and, most importantly, APPETITE. A pizza from Papa Johns is quantifiably more satisfying than food at Cafe Poca Cosa. Perhaps we should let the name of the establishment serve as a warning.

P.S. to those who CLAIM this establishment provides an allegedly unique experience - they clearly haven't had AUTHENTIC Mexican cuisine with a twist. Adding a rainforest's worth of greens doesn't make it an "experience".

Jules,

I love your pizza. I really do. 

However, Last week I was there with my kids and wife. While ordering, I watched one of your staff sneeze, rub her nose several times, and not step off to wash her hands. If that wasn't bad enough, when I mentioned this to the female manger on duty, she did nothing. I told her which employee it was (the one in the red shirt), to which she replied "I didn't see that". Suggesting I was lying to her. When a customer points out your team needs to go wash their hands, then wash their hands! Also, your team should wear glove as they are handling food in front of the customers. 

If you want me back, you literally need to clean up your store.


Thanks!

While visiting Philly, a friend chose this place to dine, and I was a little skeptical. They had never been here before, and it was so random I didn't get a chance to yelp it first. But sometimes you just get lucky and this was one of those times.

Conveniently nestled in Liberty Walk (Northern Liberties), it seemed a bit off the path for strangers, but likely a gem for locals and those in the know. The service here was phenomenal. While tiny, I did enjoy the intimacy and decor. So now to the food. I ordered a grilled calamari salad. It was deliciously grilled calamari over a bed of mixed greens with red onions, scallions, mint, and I believe tomatoes, topped with a chipotle lime type dressing. Amazeballs. I would love to return and try the Hi Ma Parn with chicken.

While this one experience may not be entirely indicative of how all of Misconduct's staff usually treats its customers, I had to finally write my first review to share how horribly my friends and I were treated last night, Wed 11/6, by the bartender.

Six of us were seated at the bar during happy hour. The bartender had been keeping some of us on the same tab, but most of my party had already cashed out by the end of hh. When it came time to close out and I asked for the bill, it had mine and 1 other person's drinks on it. We asked the bartender 2 questions about the happy hour pricing and what drink was what. Instead of just getting what we asked for, some answers, we were met with eye-rolling, judging and patronizing remarks. He proceeded to throw our receipts back in our faces, continue making rude remarks, and instead of returning my change directly, he aggressively flapped my money in my face while lecturing me on separate checks. After I expressed to him how I did not enjoy his condescension, he then threw my friend's credit card back in her face.

I understand that it can be frustrating to deal with large parties. I have worked in the service industry, I know how it feels when you're tired and the last thing you want to do is deal with what you feel is your customer's incompetence. But never did I let that lead me to treat my customers the way we were treated last night. So what if a couple of tipsy girls have a few questions about the calculation of a couple of drinks? Just answer the question, show them even an inkling of hospitality. Especially when these customers are generous tippers who are likely to return to your establishment. 

I have never ever been treated this poorly in a restaurant or bar in my life. I am beyond disappointed because I generally love Misconduct's food and drinks and have often frequented it in the past. After last night, I'll have to think twice before going back.

Second star is for the good times we've had Misconduct, but last night you only deserved one.

This place is absolutely phenomenal! We came in for some food and drinks and we let our server guide us through our time here. We told him what liquor we preferred to drink and he recommended cocktails that were absolutely amazing. The menu is full of amazing options, each perfectly cooked with excellent flavor balance. I will be back as soon as possible. This is a very welcome addition to Mass Ave. Can't wait for this patio when it's 10 degrees warmer!

Lee's is a classic West Philly sandwich shop. You can get a huge variety of cheesesteaks there and all under $10 that will feed you for two meals. The Korean cheesesteak is a good starting point. The staff are pretty friendly too, and some veggie options but you can eat so much meat otherwise.

Watch out Starbucks, Dunkin Donuts, and any other Coffee/Donut pusher out there.

Remi's Minis is a brand new business set up food truck style near Publix in the beautiful Winthrop area. Remi's is a mini donut and coffee place that's open as early as 6:30 am to catch the morning rush and as late as 6 pm to catch the corporate America crew returning home to Riverview. 

Remi's donuts are out of this world, I tried my first set of 4 which come in a big bite size format and with very unique flavors such as, maple bacon (locally sourced bacon from Ciccio's), Churro flavor, Cupcake, Nutella, Guava, Peanut butter, Oreo, and many more! The best part is you can get 4 different mini donuts for $3 and the prices get even CHEAPER the more you order.

Coffee wise, Remi's serves Blind Tiger coffee from Ybor, which is really good coffee. The serve what you would expect from a typical coffee, along with Nitro, cold brews, and even some more desert style coffee drink involving ice cream. 

Ethics. I got to talk to one of the owners about the story behind Remi's. Remi's is based on the idea of second chances they write their menus on old warehouse shelves, their food truck is an old school unit from the 60s or 70s that they restored and converted into a fully operational food truck. Their mascot is actually the owners dog "Remi" which was a humane society rescue animal from a very abusive background (you may notice the dog winking in the logo but he's actually missing an eye) They fully support the humane society and allow you to round up your purchase for them so they can donate back. 

All in all Remi's Minis is worth a shot and will probably work their way into the morning routine of many people in the area. Get it while you can before they become way too busy!

Anytime a new place opens in Tucson I get excited. I love my (ok, our) city, and I love to see it thriving and gaining so much attention for our amazing food culture. That being said, Anello is such a perfect fit into what is becoming an excellent corner of downtown. As of Saturday evening, there was still not a sign on the outside, and the gorgeous wooden front door is your only symbol of entry. As we ate, I saw a few people through the front window who were walking around the block searching and they would stop and realize they had arrived, turn around and come in with a relieved look on their face to find that around 5:30 pm the restaurant had not filled (yet). 

We arrived just after Anello opened at 5 pm to find the restaurant was not full yet (I somewhat expected it to be, as it's Saturday and they are still new). We had our choice of seats and took the table closest to the door. The space is quite minimal, with simple, yet well-constructed wood tables that are bare wood, unpainted/unstained. The front door and ceiling are gorgeously simple flourishes. The lighting is wonderful- bright enough to see clearly and yet not harsh by any means. The entire aesthetic is a quiet modern and the design statement clearly wants you to think about the flavor of your food without imposing any personal belief upon you. 
We were happy to be left with only the responsibility of tasting our food.
We began with the simple roasted/grilled seasonal vegetable. A whole zucchini split down the middle, served piping hot and drizzled with olive oil, lemon juice, and seasoned with salt and pepper. Sprinkled all over the zucchini were pistachios. The whole dish was so flavorful, and there was nothing overdone, no pretentiousness. Just a real plate of food we shared over a good conversation with glasses of wine. 

Oh and let's take half a step backward and talk about the menu, shall we? Concise and poignant, with real ingredients. No fuss. 

For our second appetizer we ordered the wood-fired foccacia with house-made cheese. This was so good, my husband commented on how fast I ate my half. This is funny because I am the pokiest, slowest eater you will ever meet. There was plenty of cheese on the side for us both to get our fill without feeling like we needed to be careful to share and to have enough for our bread. I felt like that was worth noting. Our pizza came out, perfectly timed about 2-3 minutes after we had finished our appetizer and had a moment to savor what we had just eaten. I really felt like it was due to the fact that the chef could see where we were at in our meal with the kitchen being open and at the head of the space. Its kind of a big deal when a restaurant capacity is small enough that you can give your customers this kind of service, and it was noticed by us throughout our entire experience here. 

We ordered the Bianca and added Italian sausage. The Bianca at Anello has chiltepin on it, which is a small red chile native to the Southwest (it grows wild in Arizona, New Mexico, and parts of Texas). We both felt so happy with our pizza. The chiltepin gave some good flavor and a satisfying warmth to our pizza without being overwhelming. (I would encourage people who typically don't like spicy foods to give this a try. I feel you would be pleasantly surprised at the flavor of this!) The rest of the pizza was perfectly flavored and seasoned. The crust is deliciously pillowy and perfectly wood-fired with a wonderful amount of crunch. Overall, we were in food heaven throughout the entire meal. For dessert we ordered the black sesame with anise gelato and the flourless almond cake, both of which were so good we want to eat them again and again. 

Lastly, the service here was spot-on, 10/10 fantastic. Our server knew which red wine to recommend and indulged us by geeking out with us a bit about how good the food was. We would have come back just to have this level of service, even if the food was just pretty good. But lucky for Tucson the food and the service are EXCELLENT.

Welcome to Tucson, Anello. May you have a long, happy run here.

I feel sad to write this review, I had way higher expectations for brunch in this space. The space is really beautiful, tons of natural light and on a great corner for people watching with good views of the campus arboretum. That being said, that's about the only great things I could see from this restaurant. 

My friend and I went here yesterday and were expecting the place at just before 10am to be swamped, but it looked like they had already had an entire full restaurant and were ready for their second turnover. There were only a few tables in the very large space filled. The hostess frantically greeted us and told us it would be a few minutes for them to clean off a table. Another couple with a small child entered behind us and were taken to a four top immediately. When we looked around, most of the tables were empty but covered in dirty dishes. There were only two servers, and no bussers to be seen. The hostess yelled at the bartender who was busy making drinks, and then the hostess ran around the restaurant frantically talking to people in the kitchen and then back to the bar and then to clean a few dishes off a table, and back to the hostess stand... she got us seated at a two top a minute or two later. And there we sat.
As we waited for water and drinks to be brought out I watched the hostess continue running frantically all over and the servers just sort of walking slowly from table to table talking to people. All of the empty tables remained covered in dirty dishes and no one came by to say hello or bring us drinks. My friend wanted to get a mimosa, but the menu only says "Mimosas starting at $3". When our server finally came around my friend asked what mimosas they had and our server had to go ask the bar. When she came back she said "classic and watermelon" so my friend ordered a watermelon. I tried a sip of her's and it was very good. It was only after receiving the bill we realized it was a $6 mimosa, and with no garnish or flourish, just simple watermelon juice and sparkling wine it was definitely overpriced (IMO). Secondly, I ordered coffee which was not refilled until after we were done eating and I specifically asked for more. The coffee was not the worst I have ever had, but was definitely burned and not great. Also, on a side note, it was super odd when I asked for a refill the server got me an entirely new mug of coffee and took my first mug away from me with some still left in the mug.

As for the food, my friend got the eggs benedict which visually looked very nice but the poached eggs were almost cooked all the way through. I got the Dutch Breakfast (it starts with a U on the menu and is a Dutch word) and it consists of 3 fried eggs with tomatos on top of multigrain toast covered in melted gouda cheese. It wasn't bad at all, except that my toast was barely toasted and there was absolutely no seasoning to speak of that would make it great. It was super underwhelming and simple. 

Our server never came back and checked on our meal, never offered to refill my coffee, and never asked my friend if she wanted another drink. I wanted to order a Pannokoeken to share after our brunch, but since we never saw our server I had no chance to order and then we didn't want to wait anymore to ask, so we just decided to get the check.
The restaurant never got much busier (a few more tables came and went in the time we were there, but there was never a second 10am brunch pop), and I couldn't understand the obvious understaffing in regards to bussers during UA move in weekend at a campus restaurant. 

I am so sad that this place wasn't better, especially for being in such a beautiful space and such a great corner. I hope this review helps shed some light on a customer's perspective for Sunday brunch, and I will be sure to keep an eye out for menu changes and improvements to gauge whether or not I'm going to make a return visit.

We used to get food from here pretty regularly because it was the best Indian food we could find in Tucson. Over time though, the food has just gotten worse and worse. The mutter paneer that I ordered at "medium" spicy has a slight "kick" to it, but mostly is just super bland in flavor, watery, and tastes almost stale like it was frozen. Totally lacking in the rich spiced flavor that Indian food should be.

Oh and something that really bothers me: 
I didn't go to pick up the food, but my fiance came back and reported that he saw the guy working there pouring a bottle of Absolut vodka into an empty bottle of Smirnoff, which leads me to speculate that ALL the vodka there is the crappy well stuff poured into empty bottles of their higher-end vodka and then just refilled as needed. As a former bartender in WI, I know that this is a highly illegal practice in Wisconsin... not sure about the laws in AZ but beware drinking there.

This is one of my favorite places in the entire city of New Orleans. Everything they make is delicious, and fresh and beautiful to look at. I am not a big seafood eater , but when I come here I like to pretend I am Kanye West and order everything on the menu. What good is money anyways if you can't spend it gorging yourself on sushi and hibachi shrimp! The woman who is waitressing every time  I have been there is a goddess and always super polite and friendly. She also remembers our general order, which may be because we are two people and we order six things, but I like to think its because of our cheerful demeanor.

This place has the best sushi and hibachi New Orleans. Go now, and dine like kings!

I really, really, REALLY wanted to love Seed. I've been a vegetarian-vegan-pescatarian for 16 years (oscillating between the 3) and recently moved here from San Francisco. You can only imagine how excited I was when I saw an all vegan restaurant was opening here. Be still my heart!

The first time I went to Seed was right after the CC10K. I was fucking starving. Our waiter had the sense of urgency of a cloud floating gently across the sky. "Oh you want water? Sure"... disappears to reappear 20 minutes later. "Oh are you ready to order? I'll be right back"... gone for another 10 minutes. I really felt like it was his first day in a restaurant ever. It was painful. The food wasn't good enough to warrant such a wait (except for maybe the beignets) and after that slow, lethargic experience I didn't want to return.

Cut to this Sunday. I got an overwhelming desire for beignets. Seed opens at 9, my boyfriend and I show up about 9:45. I place an over of beignets, a fruit plate and grits., He gets the nuevos rancheros and a side of maple seitan. About 5 minutes later the waitress comes back to tell me the beignet dough hasn't risen yet. She doesn't know how long it will take (funny considering they probably make these every day). Whatever, it's fine. My whole purpose for coming here is shot, but I will soldier on. The fruit comes out, and it literally is just a fruit plate. For $8. No granola, no yogurt, not even necessarily fruit that is not past its prime. Just some relatively good, non spoiled fruit. The grits are acceptable, but NOT creamy grits we all expect. More of a thick indian pudding consistency. The seitan is $5 for two tiny pieces and gross.

All of this would be ok. All of this I would have looked past. I would have just said Seed was not my thing. HOWEVER, I had to pee. I went into the bathroom looked at myself in the mirror, and then turned to see down on the toilet, at which point I noticed the BIGGEST FUCKING COCKROACH I HAVE EVER SEEN IN MY LIFE. 

I get it. It's the South. Bugs happen. But this was a fucking river monster. It's antennas alone were the size of my thumb. I screamed at this harbinger of death and ran out of the bathroom. At this point we were waiting for our check, and I told our waitress that we had to leave RIGHT NOW and just gave her my credit card because if I didn't leave within the next 60 seconds I was going to die. Or that monster was going to follow me outside. 

The restaurant is clean. Did anyone check the bathrooms this morning? How did you not notice the small rodent size cockroach chilling and bathing inside in the toilet? Did no one care? Is it a weird vegan thing where we don't kill bugs, or even "disrupt" their daily activities?

I don't care what it is, but I will never, ever, be back. If the pedestrian food, overpricing, and weird space cadet service wasn't enough to sway me, then the Cockroach Adonis living in the toilet was.

Ain't no beignet good enough for the possibility of getting a roach up your butt hole.

Oh John Besh how embarrassed you would have been on April 26, 2015 at 9:30am.

I raved about this place as you can see in my previous reviews I have given it 5 stars each time. So I brought my cousin here for her first time to indulge in the goodness. Mind you we want to Emerial's the night before which was also her first time and the service as usual was bar none.

So I wanted to introduce her to my other favorite chef in Nola's cuisine. 

We walked in and I should have known something was off. The 2 hostess were not friendly especially the one with dark hair, large eyes,  drags her feet when she walks, and rolls her eyes at customers who is disturbing her morning (I asked for her name and was told he didn't know). It was so bad I just watched her even when we got seated and could not believe she was at the front of the house. The trash can behind the check in desk was overflowing and my cousin said that would never happen at Emerial's whom as soon as you take a sip of your water someone swoops in like dark Vader and fills your glass.

Anyway, we got seated after standing there for 18 min, no biggie. Our waiter Nicolas brought us a brunch menu and I said can we also see the breakfast menu since brunch technically starts at 10. It was 9:48 and he looked at his watch and said a unenthusiastic yep and brought the breakfast menu. Then I tell you know lie the first words out of his mouth when he sat the menus down was "So what do you want".. My reaction was like an old school episode of Punked. I said we need a minute.

We ordered a stack of pecan pancakes and shrimp and grits. 

When he brought us our food we being the yelpers we are we took our photos. He then says "Yea girl Instagram my shit". My biggest pet peeve Just because I am black don't assume I talk like a stereotype. I stated actually this is for yelp.

So he walked off, my cousin still mouth on the floor appalled. The pancakes came in a thin stack of seven with about a teaspoon of pecan butter on top. So we asked Nicolas for more butter. Exactly 15 minutes later he sees that we haven't eaten the pancakes and says I don't know why they haven't brought you any butter I told them too. This day was beyond embarrassing to the John Besh name and with the mecca of food in Nola you can't slack on service. Now my new foodie cousin can care less who John Besh is and how amazing I say he is because all she remembers is being treated worse than a waffle House at 2am. 

I hope management reads this and addresses those staff member because this day was beyond any experience I have ever had in a restaurant on its worse day.

This is the worst cheesecake I have ever experience and believe me I have had Cheesecake from Hawaii to LA and all in between.

The service was lack luster and I order soup-Clam Chowder-Flavorless, coarse base texture and an insult to Clam Chowder, my favorite soup.

Main
Shrimp Scampi-I have ordered this dish coutless of times over the years. It typically is jumbo shrimp scampi sitting upwards around the plate with a bundle of pasta in the off center of the plate dry, Angel hair. This dish came to me looking like soup. It had zero flavor just like the soup and served heavy sauced and sloppy.

I was just working in Sephora that day and a cast member never had Cheesecake Factory and I raved to her about the consitancy and great ness of them all. Needless to say when I came back I told her it was not on point.

The way I see it is this is my punishment to be eating Cheesecake factory in the city with the best food in the world originated. COME ON NOLA GET IT TOGETHER.

I was staying at the Canary so my bf and I popped by here for drinks and then a late night snack.  Both times we ate in the bar area. 

We only tried wines and beers, so I don't know how their cocktails are.  For food, we tried the sweet potato baba ghanoush (so good, doesn't taste like baba ghanoush at all but it's delicious) and the mac and cheese (not as exciting).  Food was overall pretty good, and service was quick and friendly.  I wouldn't do this place for a special meal or anything, but it was a really nice option to have so close by as it's a solid spot to hang out and grab a bite.

Definitely going to come back for the paella!  

My bf and I were luckily walking by right at 4:58 and there was already a crowd of people waiting outside to go in the minute the doors opened.  The place was packed within 5 minutes of opening and we were lucky enough to get a table.

We were really more in the mood for just a snack, so we had the chicken croquetas, tortilla espanola, and the secreto.  Everything was delicious, service was friendly and fast, and the decor is super cute.

I'll definitely be back for a bigger meal next time!

My favorite meal in NOLA.

Came with a group of 10 and had Gara as our server.  Gara was delightful - dropping little nuggets of information about the restaurant, the town, and the menu items without being intrusive.  

They have a 3 course prix fixe for $39 that's an amazing deal given the portion sizes.  I had the gumbo, pecan crusted baby drum and tried the creme brulee and bread pudding.  Everything was delicious.  

Also, if you have a sweet tooth and want to try what's essentially an alcoholic milkshake, you have to try their brandy milk punch.

It's very centrally located to go out and have fun afterwards.  The restaurant is supposedly haunted, as well!

Beautiful atmosphere and great food.

We ordered a ton of food for our group of six and we kept getting some serious judgment from our waiter who kept asking if we were SURE we didn't want to cancel anything.  I think he was doing it to be considerate, however, so that we wouldn't feel pressured to eat everything we had initially ordered.  

Otherwise, the service was good and the food was stellar.  

We got the deviled eggs, brussel sprouts, heirloom tomatoes, beets and butternut squash, duck liver mousse, goat confit strozzapreti pasta (basically goat confit on tubular pasta), Spanish octopus, scallops, and the trout.

All of it was very good; I thought the heirloom tomatoes and beets and butternut squash were too sweet but my friends liked them.  My favs were basically everything else.  

We also ordered the honey dessert and the ice cream sandwich.  The honey dessert (I forget the actual name) was very unique and tasted almost like a honey panna cotta.  Highly recommend.  They also comped one of the desserts for us because it was my birthday!  I thought that was very nice.  

I'd definitely recommend this place and come here again next time I'm in the area.

The owner commented about me and how they believed me to be on a previous review & I'm honestly here just to say how UNPROFESSIONAL that is. What a horrible business tactic. 

I did have a bad experience on NYE and was ready to leave the restaurant, because our time there seemed to last forever. I let one staff member know our first appetizer was too salty, and another staff member know that "we're good" & ready to leave instead of getting dessert. I did not make it abundantly clear to all the staff that I was unhappy, & you did nothing to remedy the situation until we asked to have the dessert removed. 

Don't comment about your customers if you want to continue to have more coming in. This review response from the manager just solidified the fact that we will not return. Absolutely terrible.

Edit: The owners responses to myself and others continue to be petty. Thank goodness for your husband/chef for being the only person trying to make things right. All of the things she is posting to stick up for herself continue to be false. Go spend your time improving your customer service instead of trying to attack people on yelp. You never personally came to our table to see what was happening...& upon now being able to see who you are, I know you were in the restaurant watching us with a rude glare as I was trying to just get a check & leave. Nice to see you were the owner this whole time. Terrible customer service. Terrible owner. The chef however was nice.

This is my third time here and is becoming one of my favorite healthy options. I'm always interested in checking out new places, which is what initially brought me in. At first glance it didn't seem like a place I would enjoy because it seemed to healthy to be good, but I was completely wrong. 

Their staff recognized I didn't know what half of the menu items were and talked me into a quinoa burger. Now I've never eaten a veggie burger before coming to this place, and I've just had my second one today. I've never even wanted to try one, but I'm so glad I did. Not only was it really flavorful, but I was satiated without feeling lethargic...like when I eat some traditional burgers. 

Even if you're like me, and don't always choose the healthiest food options, this is a great place to try new things. Don't worry they'll give you some solid recommendations!

What happens when you have a waiter that is HONEST about portions but two yelpers that are hesitant about trusting the suggestions because they've got burned on the last 3 restaurants they ate at?  You get two super stuffed yelpers!

Bouchon is the culinary champion everyone else on Yelp has written.  

French Onion Soup - LARGE with a wonderful base and flavorlful onions with a HUGE piece of crouton/cheese on top.  Can't get much better than that!

Lentil soup - Not bad.  Good lentil taste but just not too inspired.  Probably the low point of the meal but still a 4-star dish.

Crab Cake - You get two but the waiter knew we were splitting it and gave us individual dishes.  Thoughtfulness like that matters!  The crab cakes had a beautiful blend of crab, corn, and red bell pepper sauce.  Definitely something to pay attention to but probably not something I'd order again.  Not because it wasn't good, but rather because it was just too much.  

Duck - Cooked perfectly with a very rich side.  The breast was tender and medium rare just as it should be with the fioe gras on top was a beautiful blend of different tastes and textures.

Kobe Ribeye - at $38 / dish, I'd have expected a small steak the size of my palm, but NO.  Bouchon said "Forget your normal thinking, we're gonna give you your money's worth and THEN some"  The steak was HUGE at least 12 -14 oz of beef.  All that on top of some local veggies and a mixture of hash.  It was a very rich dish as was everything else at the meal but VERY pleasing.

So with perfect service from our waiter and stellar food, I would give this place 5-stars.  However I think they should only get 4.5 stars.  Why?  Well, not to be a complete jerk but I was highly turned off at the fact that the owner of the restaurant personally greeted everyone in the restaurant as they walked in and if he missed someone as they were walking in, he went to their table to talk to them.  We were the ONLY table he did not talk to.  Maybe it could have been that we were the only ones under the age of 40 or maybe it was just he missed us.  Either way it was a turn off.  So for that, minus half a star.  

With 2 soups, 1 appetizer, and 2 entrees, we walked out of there for $130 with no alcohol.  Much less than I expected but at the same time, WELL WORTH IT.

If you've never eaten at the place and all you know about PYT is what you read about it, please do us all a favor and not write a yelp review. Express your opinions elsewhere.

Now, for a real review from a real customer:

The food is above par. Anybody who disputes that fact is out of their mind. 

Located at the Piazza, the atmosphere is hip. PBRs, hipsters, young people... If that's your thing, you'll like it. If not, you'll hate it. 

Recently, the service has been called out by a famous millionaire athlete who in turn stiffed the wait staff. However, I've been here many times (maybe 10 times total) and the service has always been at least respectful. It's not fast. It's a popular, busy restaurant. It can be chaotic. But I've always received my food and drinks in a reasonable amount of time given the circumstances. They've never screwed up an order.  

As for restaurant tipping, the standard in the U.S.  is as follows:

10-12% poor service
15% average service
20%+ good service

These percentages are based on the fact that waiters are not paid minimum wage and are expected to count tips as wages. Thus, 0% tipping is unacceptable, excluding extraordinary circumstance (for instance, the waiter pours a beer over your head). If you can't follow these basic expectations as a patron, no bar or restaurant ought to let you in their doors. 

If service is bad, leave them 10%. Maybe a note or a REAL yelp review. They'll get the point.

P.S. I've noticed a lot of reviewers recently from out of state are claiming they ate at PYT on a "business trip." I find that to be suspect. Seriously, if you haven't eaten at a place, don't write a yelp review.

Save your money, 

My wife and I went here to celebrate our 26th wedding anniversary. When I made reservations, I stressed this was a special night to us. Not a word was said - strike one, The view is nice, if you want to look at refineries...

We got there at 7 and had 730 reservations. The maitre d looks at me and says 730 right? Goes back to what he was doing. Very professional. 

On to the food if we have to. Had the crispy calamari appetizer. It was cooked right and tender, but the spicy tomato sauce was, well, blah. Tasted like Hunts tomato sauce with some cayenne in it.

I had a blt wedge salad and my wife had a house salad. The house salad was typical tossed greens - can't complain too much but then again, it was nothing special. The BLT Wedge was boring. Iceberg with applewood bacon (bacon bits if you ask me) and crumbled blue cheese (none) in roquefort dressing (bland). 

On to the entrees. My wife had a surf and turf. Nice sized Brazilian lobster tail done nicely (the highlight of thew meal) and an 8 oz filet which was cooked just about perfect, but bland bland bland. I'm not a filet fan, but this one really stood out. I had the Mediterranean Chilean Sea Bass. The piece of sea bass was tasteless, the broccoli rabe was far from garlicky, etc. You get the point - everything was bland. 

For dessert we had chocolate lava cake. False advertising here. A piece of chocolate cake warmed up, with chocolate syrup poured over it and a scoop of vanilla ice cream. 

The service is diner like (to be expected once I found out what else these folks own). The coat girl was polite.   

My advise - save your money. Go across the bridge, and for the same amount of money you can get a meal that blows you away.

This is a place where (almost) everybody seems to know each other.  Traveling through Bellmawr alone on business, I was the only exception, and I might as well have been as invisible to my fellow diners as I was to the waitstaff.  No real problem, I needed to get back on the road quickly.  The food here is pricey for a diner, and didn't look much different than the standard diner reheated items.  

The cheese burger, however, was very good, but the fries are what I remember most.  In what must have been a mistake, my batch of fries were left in the hot oil WAY too long.  In addition to being crisp on the outside and fluffy inside, the exterior was deeply caramelized-- and were possibly the best fries I've ever eaten.

(1.75 stars)  Gino's is one of the two iconic cheesesteak stands of Philadelphia, and sits across S 9th Street from Pat's-- the original.  Being iconic, however, says nothing about quality or the dining experience.  Let's look at the dining experience first.  Under the best of circumstances you order from a long outdoor counter, and have a foil-wrapped sandwich literally thrown at you moments later.  The counter isn't wiped as frequently as hygiene would dictate, and there are few places to sit and eat.  Add to this the fact that the counter help is predictably gruff and short-tempered.  It would take some remarkable food to create a dining environment that any sane person would want to repeat.  Unfortunately, the cheesesteaks just don't measure-up.  The meat is both loaded with gristle and cooked to the point of being dry.  I prefer melted provolone and onions, and the cheese has always been only partially melted.  I've eaten at four of Philly's "big name" cheesesteak spots (Geno's, Pat's, Jim's and Dalessandro's), and believe that Geno's is the worst of the four.

Props for being the reported inventor of the cheesesteak, and for being better than Geno's (across the street).  I've had much better luck finding a table here, and the general experience is better; less attitude, an impression of better cleanliness.  The beef is better seasoned, has less gristle (still more than it should) and is much moister.  If this moistness is described as "grease," then yes, the Pat's cheesesteak is greasier than the Geno's version.  I've never experienced so much grease that the bread was saturated, unless the sandwich was left in its foil wrapper for an extended period.  Not as good as Jim's or Dalessandro's, but better than Geno's.

(2.50 stars)  By a narrow margin over Jim's, Dalessandro's offered the best cheesesteaks I have had in Philly.  Although it is completely over-processed, actually chopped, the beef is moist, well seasoned, largely free of gristle and is discernibly rib eye.  Equally impressive is Dalessandro's use of real cheese.  They're impossibly crowded, but offer counter service and a genuine awareness of customer service skills.

The casino reeks of smoke, needs better ventilation or maybe leave the doors open to freshen up the place, we just went in to check in.

This review is for the hotel which is in a different building, I'm giving it 3 stars.
Medium insulation, not noise coming from outside but we did hear the people next door coughing, but overall very quiet atmosphere, I found the mattress to be too firm for me, as customary practice I always wipe down everything in the room.
