+ Big screen tv and lots of channels 
+ Medium firm mattress and pillows
+ In room Keurig coffee maker with pods 
+ in room mini fridge
+ Guest laundry room
+ Security door to enter the hotel building 


   CONS
- Elevator is slow and stinks! Avoid
- curtains were dirty but it did close all the way
- older building with low popcorn ceilings
- no microwave in the room

Located inside the French Market warehouse with open walls, this is a fast food kiosk with communal tables shared with other eating places for people shopping.  

No table service.  Ordered the $13 shrimp creole and the $10 chicken sausage jambalaya, without shrimp at the counter.  You pick out your own table nearby.

Waited about 6 minutes for our order to be ready.  They call your name, and you pick up the order.  Again, no table service.  Comes on a plastic plate with one plastic fork and paper napkin.  You try eating gumbo with a fork?

The jambalaya comes as a single scoop of chicken and sausage with rice, and two slices of bread over a brown gravy.  Not spicy enough, and overpriced. The sit down Gumbo Shop restaurant nearby has a scoop of jambalaya with shrimp for $5, while here it's $14 for a single scoop of jambalaya with shrimp.

The shrimp creole is like a seafood gumbo, and comes with six quarter size shrimp with rice, bread, in a spicy tomato sauce.  Bread was stale and crusty, while the tomato sauce was delicious, and went well over the other dish of jambalaya.    

Overpriced for the quantity of food that you get at a fast food outdoor place.  You are paying for the convenience of fast service, at the expense of no ambiance, while shopping at the French Market.   Upgraded the Gumbo Shop to 4 stars after coming to this place.  

Would have preferred to go back to Gumbo Shop rather than here, but the wife wanted something different, and you know who wears the pants in the household   After eating here, now I know why there's a long line out the door at Gumbo Shop!
Terrible pizza!  Do not order if you have any appreciation for pizza.  The taste is somewhere between Jeno's frozen and high school cafeteria.

Yes, I understand El Cap is a local hamburger legend.  I really do wish I could celebrate with the rest of you.

However, my last two visits caused me to say goodbye to this St. Pete "icon" forever.  I had been coming here for over 20 years, but no more.

Why?  Both times my burger arrived VERY undercooked.  No,not rare - they were still quite RAW in the center.  I ordered them Medium.  When busy, which is always, it seems the kitchen may push the food out a bit quicker, hoping we won't notice?

Both times I asked the waitress if I could please get a burger that was cooked a bit more thoroughly.  Ugh!  I was treated like an outcast and a leper for making such an "absurd" request.

Sure, I understand many still enjoy their burgers on the rare (read: RAW) side.

They must be blissfully unaware of the horrible 1990's "Jack In The Box" debacle, in which 4 died and 600 became terribly ill after eating undercooked ground beef.

If I want to consume a rare/raw hamburger, I will do so at home where I have 100% total control.

The "Five Guys" hamburger chain is quite clever and also VERY well aware of this.  To protect their customers' health AND themselves from lawsuits, it clearly states on their menu boards at every location, "All burgers are cooked well-done and juicy."

So I make the simple and intelligent request at El Cap to NOT be served undercooked ground beef and then get treated like dirt in return?  There is a distinct and heavy "Soup Nazi" and "The Customer is Not Always Right" mentality here.

So be prepared to shut up, grovel, and act grateful just to be served here or things will quickly go downhill.  You've been warned...

Finally...  Sure, El Cap is always packed.  Then again, the Kardashians have had a #1 rated TV show for years.  Popularity does NOT always equal greatness.

Sometimes it's really good to explore a bit further and ignore the knee-jerk, lemming, herd mentality, and thus I will continue to seek the "perfect" Pinellas county hamburger elsewhere...

P&S is what one usually expects of a typical sports bar.  Obviously very loud, with an emphasis on fried food, and a surprising handful of really great and unique menu offerings...

I've been here twice recently, around 5-6:00pm.

Their fried fish is excellent and the tater tots are a must!  The fried pork tenderloin sandwich is also really good, though at $9 plus one side, I was hoping the sandwich would be larger.

So why only 2 stars?  Like a previous yelper stated in Aug 2015, there were indeed several characters sitting at the South end of the bar that made both visits almost unbearable.

(And no, I am not making any sort of stereotype about Pinellas Park.  I've eaten at many PP places nearby that do not suffer from this problem.)

The bar patrons were several older men, say 50 years old plus, appeared quite drunk, and were insanely loud and obnoxious.  The way the bar and wait staff tolerated and interacted with them made me believe they are "regulars."

These guys made sure to stop EVERY female that passed by, both staff and patron, to make some sort of totally unfunny, loud, slurred, and ridiculous attempt at conversation or whatever.

I could clearly see other nearby diners shudder and grimace as this was going on, and on, and on...

And keep this in mind...  This was before 6:00pm!  "Happy hour" for some, UNHAPPY hour for many others!

I read the owner's response to a previous yelper's similar 08/2015 complaint about this.  Sadly, the real genuine "load" was only the snarky, completely unprofessional, and just pure emotion-based babble of a response.  Ugh!

(I have since noticed the owner deleted his response.  Hmmm?)

You do realize this is what Yelp is for, right?  Now you have 2 diners that have eluded to the fact that some bar patrons "may" be being waaay over-served here and are creating an unpleasant dining environment.

So as far as the food and service?  This place actually deserves 4 stars.

As for the experience?  Eh...  I'll never come back here, especially after reading the owner's response to a fellow yelper attempting to address this genuine problem.  Please read for yourself and judge!

So when I crave the good P&S menu items, I'll just visit the Clearwater location.  You should consider this too.

However, I do wish you all well here and good luck.....

A New Orleans institution, you must come very early and adjust your mind to the fact you will wait in a long line but totally worth it, they do move the line fairly fast though, the beignets are off the chain lil pillows of sweet heaven and with a nice hot cup of Chicory coffee  time is suspended and while in that moment all is right you have pure contentment and all you can make is yummy noises everyone is smiling laughing happy food oh yeah! It's one of the places I must go every trip. You will not be disappointed Cheers SYOY

Stayed here more then a few times when we come into New Orleans to visit family or when we bring too much family, this is a beautiful hotel we always have fantastic service beautiful rooms basic room still very good size and the breakfast is wonderful all sorts of southern breakfast items my favorite sausage and cheesy grits we all loved this dish so much we ordered it every morning all of us we just couldn't get enough. The location is perfect just a block or two away from bourbon street. And it's across the street from the Harris casino and hotel and it's in the French quarters so convenient to everything you want to see, Jackson square the French Market, moon walk, garden district and of course too many spectacular restaurants here that are some good y'all cheers SYOY

Amazing seafood restaurant in the heart of New Orleans... Make reservations because you will need them, this place is popular. Located in the garden district of NOLA, this restaurant let's you see a whole other side of the city.

Oysters are a must when eating here, just go ahead and try all three ways the prepare them lol, that's what we did. Charred, fried and bacon wrapped and raw! The crab and crawfish bisk was amazing btw and for my main I had seafood again of course. The red fish served with sweet potato's and brussel sprouts were a great healthy choice.

The only reason they did not get five stars was that the service was lackluster but the food and company more than made up for it.

Best soup dumplings I've had in Tucson thus far! FYI, their xiao long bao aren't found as "soup dumplings" but rather listed as "pork steamed buns."

I'm not a connoisseur of Chinese food, but I do really like the steamed soup dumplings they sell here, especially for the affordable price! I also got their ma po tofu, which comes with a big helping of white rice. It was just the right amount of spice for me, with a good ratio of meat to tofu. 

It is a small location near the university. There is a dirt parking lot on the side, which is also small, so if they are busy, you might have to park a little bit further. Otherwise, it's a really simple restaurant, with basic tables, 5 or so. It's a typical simple "mom-and-pop" style restaurant, not much for the atmosphere and more for the food. I haven't tried anything else besides the ma po tofu and steamed soup dumplings, but what I had was delicious!

There aren't a lot of good bubble tea options in Tucson, but this place is the spot! Not only do they offer boba, but there are other tapioca and jelly options. They also offer a wide variety of drink options from shakes, teas, smoothies, and much more. Lastly, if you want some delicious homemade macaroons or tiramisu, they sell both here! I'm a fan of matcha, so anything matcha here is delicious!

I've been to other Chatime locations around the US and the world, and this definitely compares! One aspect I like most about Chatime is the ability to customize your order: light/regular/no ice; less sugar/50%/80%, etc.

The staff is very friendly and are great at giving suggestions if you don't know what to order, especially if it is your first time. If you enter your phone number, you will accrue points each time you come here, and you'll also get email offers for discounts, specials, and free toppings/upgrades.

If you're here for the first time, I would highly recommend my favorite: Thai Milk Tea with Boba at 80% sugar and light ice. It's a great option for first time boba drinkers, as well as the classic black milk tea with boba!

It is with a heavy heart that I downgrade my previous five-star rating :(

The boyfriend and I loved Peel so much that we were always looking forward to going again. However, it's 45 minutes away so we were saving it for an occasion or a convenient time. 
When we had to drive to Nashville to meet friends, we thought we'd stop in to Peel on the way, even though it wasn't really on the way, to get pizza for the road. We love both Peel and Cleveland-Heath but figured pizza would be easier to eat in a car, especially with our little (beggar) dog with us.

We called ahead and asked if we could place an order and they told us no, it was 'dine-in only'. We asked if they could make an exception since we had a long drive ahead of us and we had a dog in the car but no dice.

We thought about going elsewhere but I convinced my bf that we love Peel so much, let's just go anyway and place the order while we're there. 
So we arrived around 5pm and the place was packed. Ridiculously so! I'm not sure how/why this many people eat so early on a Friday afternoon...
Anyway, we asked if we could place an order for carry-out and they said no, we had to dine-in, but there was at least a 15 minute wait.
They told us we HAD to sit at the bar and order at least ONE drink in order to get any pizza. 
W. T. F.
We explained to them our situation and they were not at all sympathetic--they just kept repeating that if we ordered any drink, even a soda, only then could we get a menu to order any food. We probably would have ordered a drink anyway but it was utterly ludicrous that we were forced to. 

Not to mention, they could have told us over the phone that if we arrived, we would have to sit at the bar and purchase a drink--it felt like a bald-faced attempt to try to squeeze some extra money from customers.

In the end, we skipped out and went to Cleveland-Heath instead. It makes me really sad that this happened. I know their pizzas are amazing and they will never lack for customers, but they need to work on their customer service :(

Oh my goodness, this place is addictive! I have been here twice for lunch and ordered the same thing - salmon poke bowl and eel nigiri. The fish MELTS in your mouth! I prefer getting salmon in my bowls so I can give it a nice squeeze of lemon. I just love the tanginess along with the salmon which is of the creamiest texture. If you wish, you can also get the bowl with tuna or yellowtail. If you want to go crazy, get all three! It's called a Rainbow bowl. 

Eel is another one of my favorites and the nigiri I had was wonderful. Small but very nice and fresh. I will be returning soon so I can sit at the sushi bar. I enjoy watching the chefs in action. The couple times I've come by, the tables are quite busy but there seem to always be seats at the bar. The team here is friendly and the restaurant is clean, no fuss. Delicious!

SAUCE ON THE SIDE! Cool, contemporary, hip. Nice layout and great feel with your meal. Two options: Calzone or Salad. They offer all different types for customers, but veteran zoners' also make their own creations.

As a first-timer, went with 'Meat Me in St. Louie', love the pun. Let me just say this: CHEESY! Portions of pepperoni by-product slipped out and made a bit of mess, but accepted the challenge.

TO-GO boxes are available to the public, at the drink counter, as they should be. Some places always hoard them behind the counter, like the last lifeboat on a sinking ship.

***Real talk though, if you're seeking new things, this place experiments beyond their potential. Halogen chandeliers hang from above. Vast drink selection of adult beverages. Remember to ask for Sauce on the Side***

Check out my picture to see the view I had for the last 1/2 hour of my meal. The restaurant is open until 10 pm but they flipped the chairs at 9:30‼
(Pease note I took the picture at approximately 9:55 pm. After having watched them prepare to close the restaurant for the previous 25 minutes. I was so dismayed & disappointed that I decided to take the picture & post it at the end of our meal. )

Womppp wommmmp -- super overrated- the one thing that yelpers did get right is that the line gets bonkers. 

We showed up nice in early on a Sunday when they were still gated up and waited in line w the other early birdies, not too bad as we only got there about 10 min before opening. We got seated in promptly after entering and got seated in the courtyard - highly recommend requesting a table w an umbrella cause as pretty as it is the leaves will not hesitate to plop themselves right into ya food! On our way out we say quite a line. seems nice cause they'll serve you drinks if you're seated in the waiting area inside the gate but far too many people were out on the stinky bourbon-y streets.

Ordered a few dishes: 
- comp starter: jalapeño n cheddar biscuits, 
- shrimp n grits: barely felt like it was heat-lamp warm but one of the tastier things we had, 
- goat cheese n fig jam w (cold) nut bread. jam was far too sweet, 
- farmers frittata: comes w cold croissant and the cheese far out weighed any other ingredient. 

If they heated up some of their food it'd prob be a three star joint but I couldn't get over how un-fresh everything tasted.

TL;DR Come here if you're a fan of lukewarm food on the cheap, all of the above mediocrity for 40$. edible but not worth the wait.

My dying wish is a meal from Tony's. I was floored by the bad review Patricia F. gave this spot, absolutely floored.  I'm feeling the need to defend my favorite place, in a big way. (even though I'm happy to see the rest of the reviews are positive).

Tony's is the very very best and I'm not even sure where to begin. I've been fortunate enough to be able to frequent Tony's since I was young for every important occasion in our family. Birthdays, anniversaries, my engagement, my graduation from college etc. If the question is where, our answer (wallet-permitting), is Tony's. 

Everyone at Tony's aims to please.  Vince Bommarito, the owner, is a true master of the kitchen, and of the dining room.  Vince, along with his sons and their waitstaff know how to charm and work a room.  Moreover, Vince has been good to my family for years and years dating back to when my Grandpa used to sell him chef coats via his uniform business.  He makes over my 91 year old Grandma like she's a queen whenever we get to go!  Even if it's not on the menu, he's happy to whip it up.  I always start with a Caprese Salad, though you won't find it on the menu.  Their Spinach salad is also fantastic for an on-the-menu selection.

My #1 recommendation is the Lobster Albanello. It's has the most ridiculously sweet and rich cream sauce created from reduced shallots; it's paired with lobster and mushrooms. I always get it sans mushroom and request pasta. The pasta is made in house and makes the dish coma-inducing. Try a side of their creamed spinach. Or ask for salsify as a side, it absolutely melts in your mouth. 

My other favorite entrees:  Try the Dover Sole.  The waiter de-bones it tableside and the fish is absolutely the most delectable piece of heaven you can put in your mouth.  I could eat 15 orders of the Sole.  

Veal Piccatta!  The edges are slightly crispy and the sauce is dead on.  This was my old stand by as a youngster, before I got a taste for lobster and seafood.  

Other family favorites: Scallops, Rack of Lamb, Tenderloin.  You really can't go wrong though, everything on the menu is ridiculous.

And desserts: I don't see how you could complain about the creme brulee with berries "thrown on top".  They happen to be the freshest in-season berries atop the most de-freakin-liscious creme brulee you can find.  (tsk tsk!?).  There are not one but two chocolate tortes, homemade banana ice cream, ricotta cheesecake, with raspberry sauce mmmm, I could go on.  It's unfortunate that I'm writing this at lunch-time and all the way from Seattle.

This should suffice.  But, before I finish, I did want to mention that I literally laughed out loud reading the criticism about "cheap flatware" and "serious self-importance".  That first claim is just snotty, overblown and not true.  As far as the second, well, Tony's has the acclaim it does for no reason other than wholly deserved reverence from the many many people who recognize what an incredibly special treat it is to endulge in such perfectly structured culinary pleasures.

This is the best, most amazing, if not quasi-orgasmic Italian meal I have ever eaten. My friend, Jamie B., was so excited to share Bacio with me, and after tonight's meal, I can fully understand. My heart and stomach are happy with love. 

Bacio is a charming and quaint neighborhood restaurant that maybe seats 40? The walls are a warm red and over the din of diners and kitchen staff pours a soundtrack of standard Italian favorites. I think I sang along to Nessun Dorma three times! (I am so not a tenor.) For being a Sunday evening, they were hopping. I was so glad they were able to seat us without a reservation--they had a lot of larger parties, including one referred to as VIP (just like Pamela Anderson.)

Before our server even greeted us tonight, the chef, and later I learned owner, offered us a sample of a dish. After we told him we didn't eat shrimp, he didn't even hesitate before offering that he could make it without. What it was, was a dish of white beans, arugula, and magic. With the first taste, I knew I was in for an amazing meal. 

I settled on a cup of the Pasta e Fagiloi soup--both their Minestrone and Pasta e Fagioli were Vegetarian--double bonus points! For a main course I had the the Vermicelli and Vegan Meatballs. I'm not a Vegan, but I was happy to have Meatless Meatballs. Jamie had the Minestrone, an Arugula salad with apples and a pomegranate reduction, and the Eggplant Parmesan. Bacio is BYOB so we also served ourselves nice tall glasses of Syrah straight out of my bag. 

The soups were both perfect. The Minestrone had a lovely blend of fresh vegetables and homemade pasta and the Pasta e Fagioli paired white beans and homemade pasta in a lovely vegetable stock. My main course was a generous helping of homemade Vermicelli--they were making pasta on the other side of our table in the open kitchen--topped with a thick and flavorful Marinara and three huge Vegan Balls. That sounds dirty. Regardless, they were also hugely full of flavor that paired like Cagney and Lacey with the Marinara. And this was so much more than a scoop of red that many restaurants offer. It was also topped with cuts of fresh basil.

I love that they were even so considerate to offer a Vegan topping (think Parmesan cheese) with my meal. When I told the server I ate cheese, she was pleased to gate fresh Parmesan upon my mound of deliciousness. On a side note, the menu was really Vegetarian/Vegan friendly, which I think is awesome of them to be considerate. Sure, you'll think it's Italian, it can't be that hard to be Vegetarian/Vegan, but really, this was rock-your-world awesome. Other options included a sweet potato gnocchi, a ravioli, and a Vegan Lasagna. 

Following dinner, we somehow decided we still had room for a slice of cheesecake after our energetic explained it was "out of this world" to another table. There's always room for dessert, right? I am so happy we went meatballs to the wall with it and ordered it. The chef, who was right across the half-wall in the open kitchen, explained that it was his mom's recipe, who also was there this evening. I'm so sad she must have left before I was able to commend her on her dessert. This cheesecake looked like it was going to be heavy, but in all actuality was quite light and fluffy--it almost had a flan/custard like quality with a perfect, non-graham crust. 

Bacio has set a new standard for Italian fare for me. I swear this dinner was a nearly religious experience. I love that the owner/chef talked to us through the entire meal and was always smiling; it's refreshing to see a chef take such pride in their work. This meal was perfection.

If Valerie ever makes it to Philly and visits their restroom, she will notice it is a unisex one stall and it smells like bubble-bath. I thought it was pleasant, and really, if there's only limited seating, one stall should be adequate.

Really and truly, the worst pizza and service I've ever had anywhere.  Period.  I think I could get a better pizza from Red Baron in the frozen section at Kroger's, ya'll.

I know, I know... the reviews are clearly awful, so why even bother?  But I just wanted to try it for myself, especially since I am pizza fiend and resident of East Nashville.  First of all, I need to ask: how does a place with such overall poor quality stay in business?  I can't wrap my mind around it!  The menu selection is tiny (3 pizzas, 1 type of shish kebob, 2 appetizers) and the food is terrible and vastly overpriced for what it is.  My cheese pizza was soggy, bland, and half-cold.  When my apathetic server asked me how my food was, I very politely told her that it wasn't up to par and she just said "oh, sorry" and walked away.  That was it.  She came over to our table 3 times - once to take the order, once to give us our food, and once to ask/give us the check.  The place was nearly dead when we were eating, so it's not like she was too busy to tend to us!

Also, anyone else notice all the fake reviews that have been filtered for this place?  Instead of investing so much time to create fake accounts that leave rave reviews, maybe the owner should take utilize the constructive criticism from *actual* customers and try to better his business.  Just a thought.

Wow, waited almost 30 min to order and it was BLAND and not seasoned. It smelled great outside but without taste. I really really wanted to like this place but it's disappointing that I have to put salt and pepper on it on my own to ensure it has some flavors. 

Wouldn't recommend, maybe we went on a bad day?

Edit - based on recent reviews I noticed a lot of folks mentioned that the meat is bland so it's not just an off day when I went. Not sure why this is highly rated when the taste is bland...

I was embarrassed that we had built up the restaurant's offerings to our out of town guests. Though the soup and salad and pizza were fine, the much touted veal parmigiana ( by the establishment itself) was as dry, thin, hard and tasteless as cardboard, and on top of that, it remains listed at $28.00. My friend ordered the lobster ravioli and neither saw nor tasted any evidence of lobster. What is going on here?

If there was an option to leave Zero stars,I would have. So many things to post about our experience today,I don't even know where to start. The owners/managers have a "sense of entitlement" attitude rather than a customer focus attitude! They could give a rats a$$ if you come or go, which makes me wonder how this establishment survives!

I have seen so many of their "friends" break long lines and come right in to be seated! I can't figure out if their employees are just as miserable as they are,or they are just scared to even try to give good customer service, but it is the worst experience that I have encountered since I moved to Reno.

I called last night and specifically told them I had a party of 9 and we wanted outside seating. The manager even confirmed this on the phone. We show up, the hostess tells us, " your table is inside". We nicely informed her that we asked for an outside table, she blew it off and sat us inside anyway. When we said something, she ignored us, and even began to talk about us to another employee. She said, I will have the manager come and talk to you...the manager never even came to the table!!! Now, I would have been able to handle all of this if they would have just said two simple words that go a long way in customer service.....wait for it Stonehouse employees...I'm sorry!!!! You should try it, it's very simple to say, and it rolls off the tongue easily, if you truly mean it. 

So, with this " slap in the face service" we walked out the door, across the street to Napa Sonoma, and was seated immediately, in our own private area, and was given the best service possible. I even ran into the owner and he stated that they get pissed off customers all the time from Stonehouse!!! Wow...that sucks Stonehouse...the competitor is taking your business, and even looking out the window and laughing at you. 

I know this review won't make a damn to you, and you can replace me with several others that are willing to put up with your disgusting attempt at humanity, but you will NEVER get my business again. I am a very calm person, but when you go out of your way to upset me, you will hear about it!! Get some help, and revisit what it means to take care of the people who keep you in business!!!

Are you hungry verging on hangry and is it about 1pm on a weekend? Probably best not to rely on La Super-Rica Taqueria. There will likely be a line out the door and it'll take you a while to finally get your food, at which point, you'll probably be in a horrible mood. This is a place to plan out, even arriving a bit before they open to avoid the wait. 

That's what I did and it's a big reason why I had an overall very good experience here. I knew this place was legendary and honestly, I think I was expecting a bit more flavor-wise and didn't realize that most things would come doused in melted cheese. Then again, how can you stay mad at a bunch of melted cheese?

The best way to go is to share a bunch of dishes with a group. As you'll see in my photos, a group of four split I'd say close to 10 dishes and paid about $70 total. Very affordable in the grand scheme of things, but not dirt cheap for Mexican food. I can say for sure that it's all made fresh as you can see them preparing all of your dishes through the little windows in the kitchen. It all came out piping hot and served with a smile both by those in the kitchen and at the cash register though, so that counts for something in my book.

The standout for me was the fresh corn tortillas, so expertly made. The surprising least favorite were the tacos de bistec - though they were piled high with steak, I found the meat to be dry. Nothing a dollop of guac or hot sauce can't help, though. 

Overall, it's a great little spot with lots of seating, friendly service, tons of options, and lots of melted cheese. Even if it's not the best Mexican you've ever had in your life, I'd say it at least partly lives up to the hype!

First let me say that my dinner at Arch Rock was absolutely delicious. I had the lobster roll, which was one of the fattest, tastiest ones I've had in a long time, and my husband had a wonderful seafood pasta. We also loved the Moscow Mules we had with our meals... so well made and tasty. 

However, there were a couple of service issues that ticked me off. We came at happy hour time, which we were only able to take advantage of in the very small bar area. There were no spaces anywhere in the bar, so we said we were fine just grabbing a table in the dining area. Though we were sad that we couldn't order off the happy hour menu, I know this isn't the only place that has this kind of rule. Just wish they'd made a little more seating since there was a huge section of the restaurant that had no one in it, and everyone was crammed into their tiny bar. 

The really annoying part, for me, was when it came to the deviled eggs. You heard that right: I'd seen a delicious looking photo of their deviled eggs on Yelp before we arrived and by the time I got there I was seriously craving that as an appetizer. But we were told that it was a happy hour item and since we weren't sitting in the right area, we couldn't order them. I even offered to pay whatever their 'normal' price is for the eggs, forget the happy hour discount, because I really really wanted those darn deviled eggs! But they said there's a totally separate charging system and separate menus and there was no way I could have them. It seemed so silly to have a dish at your disposal and refuse to serve it to someone, especially when they're willing to pay more money for it! 

The other annoyance was when we ordered the Moscow Mules. They told us that we had to give them our IDs to ensure that we wouldn't steal the copper mugs, and then almost forgot to give them back to us . This one is a little more understandable since I'm sure they've had experience with people pocketing those nice shiny mugs, but it should be on them to remember that they're holding them so their customers don't walk out without them at the end of the night. 

I hate to give this place three stars because once we got our food and drinks, we were so happy with everything. But those awkward moments at the start of our meal are things that can be easily fixed, and I think Arch Rock has a great thing going so I hope they smooth out those few rough edges!

A quiet, tranquil place to meet with friends, read a book, or get some work done over a nice cup of coffee or tea. The decor is minimal but it adds to the calm vibe of the place. On a weekday afternoon there were plenty of individual tables and a big communal table  available. My green tea was perfect. 

My only complaint is the lack of wifi in this cafe. For a place that seems to encourage customers to linger over their beverages and snacks, it's a bit inconvenient not to offer wifi, at least during non-busy hours. 

A suggestion from a remote worker who is bound to spend lots more money at a cafe that has wifi!

I have pass this place driving many time before and never thought twice about it and damn i was missing out until now. I was watching this vlog on YouTube call JL Jupiter. Where these guys go around to different mom and pop shops in Philly and Jersey area and i saw the episode when they came here and they had the game over cheesesteak with the parmesan  cheese fries and all I can say is OMG. This is one of the best sandwiches i have had. The menu is huge and i will be back to try more of there wonderful food. Trust me you cant and wont go wrong coming here I PROMISE YOU.

Ya'll (I can say ya'll since I'm in Nashville) I am STUFFED! My friends wanted me to experience a family style restaurant a la Nashville with a little bit of historical culture. This Monell's (there are 3) operates in a historical Plantation with the upper level completely preserved and dining on the entry-level floor. If you're in wedding planning, this is a beautiful, affordable setting that includes some pretty decent food. There are 3 large salons on the ground floor that fit several 10-12 seater tables. The idea being the enjoy dinner as you would (in the old days) with extended family and friends. Dining is a flat rate with whatever is on the menu for the day. I encourage you to arrive hungry and with friends, there is a lot of food to go around! 

Menu:
* Cucumber salad + Coleslaw + Corn Pudding
* Fried Okra + Spinach + Green Beans + Greens + Navy Beans
* Chicken + Catfish + Ribs
* Mashed Potatoes + Gravy
* Corn Pudding + Stuffed pasta shells + Hush Puppies  
* Peach Preserves + Banana pudding

The food was good, it was not exceptional. They are known for their fried chicken, which I will say was very good. The fried catfish was slightly overcooked, the banana pudding did not taste as though all ingredients were home-made. Each of the type of beans on the table was well seasoned. The greens were not overly vinegared, thank god! 

Parking is available in front of the manor and is free.

I need 5 more starsssss!

Ya'll better find out how to get here because it's in the middle of nowhere but everyone seems to know about it! We put our name in for a 45-minute wait, by the time we were being seated the wait extended to 1 hour 20 minutes. The waiting area is covered in headshots (you know, the kind you get when you move to L.A. to be an "actor/actress," #noshadebutshady). I was wearing my Saint Mary's College sweater (go Gaels!) which prompted the manager to share that he used to live in Moraga. What a small world. I was in like Flyn! After reminiscing about California, he came around with multiple samples of his favorites:

* Banana pudding - If only I could bring back to S.F.
* Greens - ABSOLUTE PERFECTION!!!!!!!!
* Creamed Corn - new favorite fall side dish
* Apple butter - reminds me of my moms pb&js. Delicious!
* Pimento cheese - not a fan

For my entree, I went with the fried chicken with a side of mac n cheese + greens. My friend told me that people in the south usually put Velveeta in their Mac n Cheese, which is... different. I prayed there was no Velveeta in this dish because they were so creamy and hearty! These greens right here tho!!!! Oh. My. God! I at the sample Keith brought all to myself along with the side on my plate and would have happily devoured more. The best greens I have had in a very long time. They were not bitter and not vinegary. Thank the gods! Everything was washed down with their famous peach tea with moonshine. 

Oh, I almost forget about the dang gone biscuits! These bite-sized bits of heaven need no butter when adding the house-made preserves. But let's be real, who skips out on butter! 

The store on property sells much of their favorite items on the menu; the chicken batter mix, preserves, the biscuit batter even ham! I purchased a trio of preserves and my friend gifted me the chicken batter mix. 

If you are visiting during Fall, take a detour along Natchez Trace Parkway before or after dinner, to enjoy a scenic drive in the countryside of Tennessee. Bon Appetite!

Maybe it's just a problem with their delivery service.  If you're okay with reheated pasta 120 minutes after you order it, then this is the place for you. If you expect a little bit more, either move on to the next place or consider visiting this place in person. I didn't want to go out tonight. I wanted to order my meal, have it delivered to my hotel and eat in my pj's. I had to wait 2 hours to get into said pj's and had to call twice to check on the state of my order. I was willing to pay forty cents extra (!!!!) to have a plate and plastic utensils included with the delivery but sadly they were not included.  They were also not itemized on my bill. I'm glad for the forty cents savings but wasn't too happy to pick through microwaved fettuccine with my fingers. Bad experience.  Don't recommend this for travelers.  I hope it's 100 percent better if you dine in but this restaurant should not offer delivery service if they can't get their act together.

I'm so happy we have a South Indian restaurant in town. It's about time! Every time I have eaten here they are always super busy. I have had a variety of things: chicken byriani, regular plain dosa, the lunch vegetarian platter, both types of vada's, a few different chicken curry dishes and the mango lassi. Everything I ordered was delicious! You get a great portion size for each dish ordered as well which i can appreciate. 

Only critique would be that the waitstaff can get too busy that they neglect a table or two. The service can get backed up. However when the staff does come to your table they are kind and willing to get you whatever you need (more napkins, more water etc.). 

Overall I hope this location is here to stay! And sidenote: Congrats on your recognition in the Best of Philly issue for 2019!

Love this location. Hidden away a little bit so easy to miss but the staff is always friendly. Like worthy of mentioning friendly and helpful, especially the checkout staff and floor staff in the shopping area. 

Food is always delicious and consistent. This is a frequent stop for my family.

Restaurant week review. Definetly would return to this restaurant for the amazing architecture and out of this world steak. $35 restaurant week deal is truly a steal considering the filet mignon itself normally is over $40 alone.

Appetizer was choice of salads or a soup. I had ceaser salad and the dressing was perfect. Dessert was a choice between mouse and cheesecake and I chose wrong with the mouse. It was so rich and dense I had to "force myself" to finish it haha The cheesecake hwr was light and delicious. I definetly had dessert envy.
2 hours for dinner is ridiculous. SLOW service. Backed up kitchen. Falling asleep waiting for food. Restaurant is half empty and they still can't put out food.

Not a place for a gathering of friends. Met the rest of the MC club here after a viewing. This place is totally a takeout cheesesteak place. The "waitress" had no idea how to handle a party of 13 even tho the food was so simple. It took 5 minutes just to figure out which tables to move to sit us all in a straight line, sigh. Food was mediocre. Would not willingly choose to eat here again.

Should be rated 5 stars for food and 3 stars for service. 

Sal & Joe's has been a regular spot for our family to go to for great authentic Italian. 

Don't overlook this restaurant due to it's location in a strip mall of stores. It truly is a hidden gem.

We've never had a bad meal. The portions are very generous so you always have leftovers. We rarely get pizza bcuz of all the excellent dinner options but their pizza is also top notch.

Only negative? As time goes on it is becoming glaringly obvious that the older women who have been waitressing there for years upon years are miserable! They used to be very pleasant. This has not been the case over the last several visits. We'd rather takeout food than have to tip someone who makes us feel as if we're inconveniencing them by being there. Time for some new blood and new attitude!!

This is the second time here, sorry forgot to write up the first time. On this visit, I actually looked at the menu, I deviated from the normal boring trio I regularly order which is tamale, enchilada and chili relleno. I saw something which I don't normally see on a menu, they had a lengua plate. This was served in a tomato based salsa with onions and bell peppers along with refried beans or whole beans and spanish rice. Damn that lengua was good, it was nice and tender, but the portion was extremely skimpy. I would have liked to see at least double the amount of lengua, but triple would be even more perfect. The amount was around three to four slices of fair size, which is barely enough to get a good taste of the lengua. I did get a little chili relleno too. The chili relleno was prepared with the usual stuffing of cheese, but the coating was different from the usual battered and deep fried version, they did it with a egg crepe coating. Great chili relleno anyway you look at it.
I do need to mention the chips and salsa, the salsa is so good, I could have just drank it, the chips were not the real thin type that I prefer, but tge salsa more than make up for the shortcomings of the thicker tortilla chips.

This place is VERY similar to Wing Shack, so it's hard to avoid the comparisons.  You buy wings in bulk and get to pick from an assortment of flavors. Unlike WS, they have off street parking and even some tables (!) so you can sit down while you chomp down.  They are missing rotary bullet-proof glass and a sign that says "WE WILL NOT WAIT FOR YOU TO GET $$$ FROM YOUR CAR". 
If you are doubting their legitimacy, never fear: they also have the infamous naming issues, as the sign says "Wing Snack" but the menu says "Chicken Shack".

I tried three flavors: 
taco - my favorite of the three, good seasoning and texture
GYMR (sp?) - good, but not as spicy as the warning label suggested (see WS's "Arizona" if you want a wing that punches you in the mouth)
crunchy BBQ - meh, it reminded me of chinese sweet and sour chicken

The Michelle punch (aka grape) was pretty tasty, better than the Obama punch (aka...red?). The cajun ranch fries were also tasty, with a nice balance of slimy and crunchy.

Overall, the place is very good, though I have to be honest: in a head-to-head challenge, I would pick Wing Shack over C&W.  Which isn't to say this place is bad, it just goes to show how awesome WS is!

Cool little place with plenty of outlets, seating, wifi... and waffles!

Helpful staff that navigated us through the menu, which is surprisingly large for a little place.  Sweet waffles (like their mochacino that looks to be to-die-for!), omelettes cooked on a waffle maker, and the calzone waffle that we ordered... it was like a waffle pizza!

We were so excited to get back in here, to have a drink on the patio and eat some delicious (not homemade!) food. The visit started off really well... which is why they have any stars at all. He walked in with a group of 4 adults and a couple kids. Waited 15ish min for them to set up the patio table.. so far so good. The table is perfect... exactly what we wanted. 
Then we sat for 10-15 minutes without seeing another employee. So when the server finally came for the drink order we just ordered everything.. drinks, food... the works. 
Drinks come out and are delicious but it's another 20 min before we see a server. No water refills, no drink refills. Fail.
Food comes out and it's 2 entree salads and 2 burgers. Both the salads are so over dressed everything was just sitting in a puddle of dressing. 
Both of the burgers were tasty but pretty severely undercooked. Fail.
The food was delivered by runners, so again we have no water refills or drink refills. No service for 10 min easy. My son had requested a spoon for his Mac and I eventually just went and got it myself. No one came to ask how the food was. No refills for anyone. Fail.
The server eventually finds her way back to the table, we order a couple drinks. The server appears didn't hear 1 of the 2 drinks ordered so we canceled it because the drink that finally did come out took 15 min to arrive. Fail.
Never once did any empty glass or plate get removed from our table. We were a party of 6 and glassware is falling over whenever anyone moved. The fact that no glasses were broke is a damn miracle. 
Look, I know it's tough right now... finding people to work.. but this was absolutely atrocious in just about every respect. The wait times alone should have earned a visit from the manager. If the service was crap due to the servers being slammed you'd think that we would see management running food, drinks, touching tables, something... but nothing. 
It's been a very VERY long time since I've EVER seen such a complete shit show. I wouldn't enter this restaurant again if I was paid to do so. 

The only reason there are any stars is for the host staff! They really did a great job at getting us such a wonderful table on the patio. Also, my son (8) said his Mac and Cheese was "the best ever".

I'd like to start this by saying that the review is really a 2.5 or 2.75.. not quite a 3* though. 
This "gastropub" is in the same spot that the Flatbread restaurant was in downtown Meridian. From what I've read and heard it's owned by the same people. After this last visit I can assure everyone that a lot of what is wrong is just growing pains and poor hiring decisions, so a lot of what's wrong here should work itself out.

Service: I made a reservation. I was asked if I wanted a tall table or a regular table... I said a regular table... we were seated at a tall table. 
We ordered a app and a salad....they both came out at the same time... no where near as big a deal as when the 2 entrees then came out 5 minutes later. We told our waitress to take the entrees back to the kitchen so that we could enjoy our two starters. 
The waitress never asked about our food, only if we wanted another drink... when we had next to full drinks... meanwhile our waters were next to empty the entire meal.

Food: Aside from the server/kitchen blunder with coursing... it was better than ok. The Brussels sprouts were REALLY charred. I like a roasted sprout but these were over. The dish was SOOOO sweet that I had no idea there was bacon in it... how do you overpower bacon!?!
The beet salad was awesome! The beets were very well cooked and I loved the amount of goat cheese. I'd like more arugula though and a bit less dressed. 
My wife had the Salmon entree and it was so over cooked that all I could see in my minds-eye was Gordon Ramsey smashing it and throwing it against a wall. The asparagus on the plate were also so over cooked that they went untouched. The mashed potatoes were delicious. 
I had the 16oz ribeye, med-rare. I ended up with a mostly medium steak.. not the end of the world but just not what I ordered. The blue cheese compound butter was amazing as were the roasted garlic chips. However my dish also suffered from horribly over cooked asparagus that went untouched.

Overall: I think there is a lot of promise but as of now it still feels like a soft open. The servers feel more like cocktail servers than food servers.. as ours wasn't very familiar with the menu. 
I really cannot believe that they took out the pizza oven... my steak would have been SO MUCH BETTER if it was finished in a wood oven. (EVERYTHING is better finished in a wood oven haha!). The lighting is super bright. We had a early reservation, I kept expecting the lights to be turned down... they never were... felt sorta cafeteria like. 
I think after looking at the menu I was expecting more of a bistro/gastropub but whatever I was expecting this wasn't really it.

Disappointed in this last visit. Which is unfortunate because we brought family from out of town. I know that this restaurant can do better. 

Few issues:
Bland ceviche... really tasted like nothing. Waste of money and I wish we would have sent it back. 

Greasy and bland tacos... the street tacos today were almost inedible due to the amount to grease pouring out of the beef and chorizo tacos. The pork and chicken tacos had zero flavor... all I got was the cilantro and onion. 

Hot plate for kids nachos.. bringing out a scalding hot plate to put in front of a child is about as dumb as you get. You need to make the nachos on a separate platter and slide them on to a plate. Seriously need to use better judgement here guys. 

Over dressed salad... the Romaine salad was disgusting. Lettuce was super soft and soggy almost like it was put under a heat lamp. 

High points-
Great blood orange margarita...always a favorite with us. 

Adam- great server... this is our second or third time with Adam and he consistently does a fantastic job. 

Overall- as stated above we are very disappointed but understand that bad days happen. Today was really a 2 star visit but Adams service and the margarita saved the day.

Fix the Hot plate issue.

Having grown up in the Middle East my expectations were set pretty high.  I was not disappointed!  The moment I walked in....the aroma enveloped me like a big hug from home.  The beef shawarma was full of all the deliciousness I had anticipated!  The place itself was very clean and friendly.....I wish it would have been a bit more old world stlye than modern fast food look though.  But hey.....I'll settle for clean and friendly!  Amir was very kind and even delayed my order for me when I realized my lunch date was going to be 15 minutes late.  After our meal he brought us a complementary nice sized sample of his homemade Persian icecream.  You could practically taste the saffron and rosewater just from the smell!  It was amazing!  Great service and flavorful dishes, I'll be back.

New Orleans may be recognized for its wonderful offerings of Cajun eateries but it also happens to be one of the most underrated cities for Vietnamese cuisine. Dong Phuong has been one of the state's most well known caterers and banh bread suppliers. They've been serving the Big Easy for the better part of 30 years and have amassed a national reputation for being one of the most respected Vietnamese businesses down south.

Meaning "East" (Dong Phuong - Dong Fang), the business has many different sides to it. On one hand, its a banh mi shop. A popular one that offers a wide spectrum of various baked goods from sweet buns to rice snacks. They also feature Chinese bakery items as well, like BBQ pork buns (char siu bao - banh bao xa xieu) or sesame balls (jin dui - banh cam).  Most folks might be more familiar with the banh mi counter, where one can score a wide variety of Vietnamese sandwiches. Banh Mi Dac Biet (specialty banh mi) will forever be my go to choice. Most everything will range from $1.50-$4.00

Then there is the restaurant side, serving up an array of Vietnamese specialties. Everything from bun bo hue ($6.50) to com suon ($6.50) to bo luc lac ($8.00) is offered. I never knew banh hoi was called a "vermacelli pancake," so I have Dong Phuong to thank for that one. I am impressed with their banh xeo (egg crepe) and their flavorful broths of pho. There are some oddities like mandarin duck (com vit pha lau) or kung pao chicken (ga xao kung pao), which I can't explain for other than the blessed foreigner effect for most Asian restaurants in America.

I've been most familiar with Dong Phuong as a wedding caterer, considering my last two Viet weddings in the area were all supplied by them. Its usually a grandiose spread of 10 course love, depending on the size of the wedding of course. I've found their special fried rice (com chien thap cam) to be lacking in flavor and the appetizer tray of cha gio and other fried goodies (ngu phuc khai vi) was a bit unimpressive.  The vit pha lau roasted duck with fluffy buns was also pretty no bueno. They get a pass for now, considering it was all mass produced food.

One of these days I'll be back in NOLA, long enough to get a better sampling of what they have to offer. I feel like I've tried quite a bit already, but something tells me I can always shoot for more.

A lot of places within the French Quarter feel touristy and Chartres House is certainly no exception. While they remain closed during COVID times, I have come here enough times over the years with NOLA newbies and locals to appreciate all they bring to the table. 

Not only are they located in one of the more popular parts of the French Quarter, but it's actually pretty hard to miss them. The building is pretty versatile as they have so many options for folks: al fresco dining, private rooms, a nice bar, balcony dining (with a view, naturally) with a festive ambiance to boot. Even the bathrooms are clean, which is always a plus.

The food ranges from excellent to super average, depending on what one orders. The natchitoches meat pies, crawfish bread, sandwiches (muffaletta and po'boys), and classic cajun'y dishes like the gumbo and jambalaya are fabulous. Their boudin is a bit sus at times, the duck empanadas are very meh, alligator tails are disappointing, and the red beans and rice are subpar. We've had all of them numerous times and while their drinks are nice and potent, they don't make the food taste better. (#1)

The bigger issue I have is the prices and portions. For what they serve, it can get very pricey very quickly. I know it's in a touristy area of NOLA and the price we pay for convenience in the quarter is more often expected than not. Service also varies at times, but I'm hoping that once they reopen that things will take a turn for the better. I'd be up for checking them out once again.

Eat-well Food Mart is a convenience store that also happens to serve Vietnamese food in the back. Located on the heart of Canal, it embodies the all cliche keywords: a hidden gem, a hole in the wall, a local favorite ... all in one package. There is no doubt if I lived nearby that I'd be going here all the time.

Had it not been for the large window decals of "Vietnamese Pho" or "Banh Mi" I would have missed this place completely. There is little parking (beyond the street) to speak of and the area could be considered a bit sketch. All sorts of characters are coming in and out of here at all times. Inside the place looks like a convenience store found at any gas station but the real action is in the very back. Look for the food photos and the kitchen counters and one will find all sorts of goodness here. Order something and grab a seat out front where there are TVs playing.

I had the pleasure of ordering for a group where we ordered several "regular" (aka dac biet) banh mi, summer rolls (goi cuon), fried dumplings, the infamous phoritto (pho cuon), finished with some a few Vietnamese iced coffees and sodas. It was around $70 for everything and because it was a convenience store, that meant other snacks were available and they accept credit card.

We loved everything. The bread for the banh mi was airy and fluffy, which meant there were no cuts to the roof of the mouth. The dumplings were crispy and tasty and the summer roll was very average. The real surprise was the phoritto, which despite the gimmicky feel was actually exactly like pho in a wrap. The dipping broth was particularly excellent and the wrap was packed full of tasty ingredients (pho noodles, cilantro, onions, beef slices, and an *extra* egg). It was far and away the most expensive item at $9 but I don't know of too many Viet places (let alone convenience stores) that sell something like this.

Lastly the husband and wife duo who own the joint deserve all the kudos. They were polite, extremely friendly to all who came in, and took the time to ensure my order was as close to perfect as can be. I hope that all of my future visits to NOLA will include a trip to this fantastic biz.

I consider myself a lover of breakfast despite rarely getting to eat it (#1). I had heard about Refuel from friends and reviews, and had made it a point to come here in the early morning. On the surface, it looks like a place that just serves sandwiches, coffee, and breakfast right? That may be true, but it was one of the best daytime establishments in NOLA. 

I truly never had a bad dish. Everything I've had I've thoroughly enjoyed, despite being incredibly simple. Whether it was an omelette, custom grits bowl, or their sandwiches / salads, it was all fantastic. Even their waffles were tasty and I never order waffles. Even the breakfast burrito was damn good, to the point where I was in disbelief the whole time.

Service was always on point. They were not only friendly, but they made a concerted effort to ensure everyone was satisfied. Drinks were always refilled and they were stellar at making recommendations for folks. After a few visits, I trusted them with surprising me with a different dish every time.

But nothing lasts forever. Refuel Cafe closed during the pandemic. It's a loss for the NOLA community but I hope they find their footing somewhere else in the city.

(#1) Sleeping in has its consequences.

Dropped by on a whim for a late dinner and sat at the sushi bar.  

Let me start by saying that I already have a favorite sushi spot. It's more of a bistro though and rolls are really their forte. This is the first  "traditional" sushi spot that I've been to in some time. 

I did try out one of the rolls along with sweet shrimp, yellow tail and eel. It was all fresh and very good. Also ordered hot green tea which came in its own pot with an infuser for the real whole leaf tea, not that powdered junk. 

Service was a touch slow starting, but easily forgiven because the sushi was excellent! This is on my new list of favorites.  Need to make a few more visits to test consistency, but judging on this first experience, I'll definitely be back.

BAD, BAD, BAD that means BAD service, BAD food, over all BAD experience. It's a shame that people who are not in the food business get involved. My wife and I ordered entries that were under cooked and when we mentioned it we were given an attitude. We will not be returning. As mentioned below there are many better dinning experiences along Lancaster Ave. than this one, it's a shame. The bar ambiance is what makes 30 main a place to stop in and drink.

I honestly don't know what the hell everyone is talking about when they are saying this place is so delicious and great and everything under the sun. HOW?!..WHY?!... Exactly WHAT time period are we talking?!... Maybe I got the wrong food and drink, I don't know! I got bacon scrambled eggs with cheese grits biscuit pancake original mimosa, was supposed to have a fried green tomato but it never came. Let me tell you what I thought WAS tasty is the butter and syrup. Bacon eggs grits and biscuit were normal tasting, pancake was burnt, got a new pancake and it was a little better but it was still not great, they NEED to clean that grill, the mimosa was regular, again I  never got my fried green tomato but let's move on. We didn't have to wait long to get seated because we sat at the bar, but I watched how dirty they made everyone's drinks smh. My sister got a dirty glass covered in red lipstick when I told the guy he just poured that drink into another cup instead of making a new one, he made other drinks where he had his fingers inside the glass and I saw him wipe all kinds of mess off his hands onto his shirt and pants, he was an unorganized mess. My first thought upon seeing this was I'm definitely not in Cali right now. If you're from Cali and you've experienced other states, you know what I'm talking about, if not, sorry not sorry. There were some men also sitting at the bar and I saw some looks of disgust on them as well. They ran out of water so they sent someone to Walgreens to buy a case, so customers were waiting for that. A lady that was sitting next to me ordered benedicts, the waitress came out with the wrong order and the lady was telling her over and over that she didn't order that, the waitress had a snappy nasty attitude with her arguing she did order it and it was like she was trying to make the lady just take it and accept it. Waitress ended up taking it back to the kitchen and came out with the correct order, then apologized but it was still the point that she got ugly with the customer as if she doesn't know what she ordered. It was just too much negative things going on in here for me, for this regular ass food. Not worth spending all that money for sure.

Dined here with my wife, as part of birthday festivities.  Tony's is supposed to be a constant, a landmark in St. Louis.  I expected top flight service, food and atmosphere.  The food was pretty great (dessert notwithstanding), the service was fair to poor and the atmosphere was ok.  This was a major disappointment given the amount of money that I was more than happy to plunk down expecting the legendary experience that is supposed to be Tony's in St. Louis.

The inexperienced 30something waiter that took care of us was slow, inefficient and seemed to share an affinity, with a couple of his buddies, for lurking in the corners cutting up.  When I show up to plunk down north of $200 for a dinner (without wine), I expect impeccable service.  I expect experienced waitstaff to make conversation, recommendations and provide interesting commentary.  I also expect to pay for this.  

Our server spilled half of my wifes first drink while pouring it into her glass table-side (no apology, no replacement) and sloshed her after dinner coffee onto her purse (no apology, no replacement).  The flambe of bananas we had for dessert was served over the saddest looking little scoop of icecream ive ever seen.  The presentation was awful.

Two bright spots.  1) The quality of the fish was outstanding (we had the swordfish and the halibut) 2) Mr. Bommarito himself was milling about the room and is a very nice man, who made us feel very welcome.  It is a shame his service staff is not up to the very high standard that he set many years ago. 

With the surge of St. Louis as a food town, I do not understand why we dont seem to support and want fine dining.  We dined at approximately 8pm on a Saturday night.  We were dressed to the nines - we were in the minority.  There were kids in jean shorts and tshirts, adults in jeans, khaki's - the whole gamut.  This is supposed to be part of the experience folks - you can dress up for one evening out can't you? 

To me, the whole point of Tony's is the experience.  You can obtain similar/same ingredients and preparations elsewhere in our town, but the magic is in how its presented and the service/experience  Fix the service or you can no longer significantly differentiate yourself from the rest of the increasingly competitive gastronomic pack in St. Louis.

Really all around BAD!  It was as if the waitress has never been to a restaurant herself to understand how a restaurant should function.  Service was non-existent and the food was just less than "ok".  To make matters worse, we were the only people in the restaurant.  Most of the meal we were completely alone-not an employee in sight.  I swear the waitress was also the cook and dishwasher.  Couldn't even get a refill of water.  Then to top it off she took the check and our cash and went missing for 15 minutes, I assume she thought she was keeping a 35% tip!  Just awful!

Tonight was our first time here & it was excellent! The beer selection was amazing. Our server was great as well. My wife & I split the fried pickles, with the chipotle ranch dipping sauce, and a dozen wings, half 309 recipe & half extra hot. The wings were very good but I could have used a little extra sauce just because that is my preference. The fried pickles were very good but could have been a little more crispy. The chipotle dipping sauce was awesome. My wife & I then split the Belly Buster Burger special, 2 cheeseburger patties, a HUGE slice of pork roll, homemade Thousand Island Dressing & fries! It was awesome! It also came with fries on the side with homemade ketchup as well as homemade chipotle ketchup. Both were amazing. I love ketchup & usually don't like homemade ketchup but theirs was amazing! Can't wait to go back!!

Quick look: after reading the solid reviews of this restaurant I was excited to dine here. Prior to getting a chance to sit and order our meal I experienced a really nasty occurrence at the restaurants main bar that put a "foul taste" in my mouth (literally). Please read below for further explanation... 

In depth review: I had did some research online and decided to try this restaurant after reading the mostly positive reviews online. We dined at the restaurant on Saturday, March 8th, 2014 at 6:30pm. The place was beyond packed out and we were told it would be 30 - 45 mins before a table would be available. We grabbed our pager and went to the restaurants main bar to order drinks and wait. The four of us purchased mixed drinks and happily waited. Food looked great going out to waiting customers at their tables. 

My mother noticed that the glasses hanging in the glass rack above our heads were very dirty. They were the "hurricane" style glasses you get exotic drinks in. Looked like they were not cleaned properly. I have worked in the service industry for years, this piqued my interest and I started looking around the main bar to make sure everything else was up-to-par. I noticed that there was a hand washing sink directly across from me. Someone posted a sign that said "Use For Hand-washing Only" above it (see photo). I noticed there were two pitchers and a mixing spoon inside the catch basin of the sink. That struck me as odd as this was a hand-washing sink and these items should not have been there. 

I watched the bartenders wash their hands several times over the next few minutes ABOVE the pitchers and mixing spoon. The debris from them washing their hands was draining directly into the pitchers (as seen in my picture attached). Here is where it gets NASTY: I then watched the bar-back go to the same sink, pour water into the pitchers and empty some mix into the pitchers and stir it with the spoon. I then watched him pour (what looked like sour mix) into two containers, one went directly to a waiting bartender (who watched him make the mix in that sink), who then poured the liquid mix into waiting customers drinks. The other container was placed in a fridge. That container grabbed in a few minutes and also emptied into customers drinks! 

Do I need to inform this restaurant and it's management why this is unacceptable and gross? This is a serious health code violation and would earn you serious demerits and possible closure if witnessed by a health inspector. You can get people seriously ill from this sort of thing. The four of us were grossed out and stopped drinking our mixed cocktails at this point. The only reason I did not inform management was because my mother begged me not to do so while she was there. She prefers to avoid conflict. I felt it is important to share this with management so they can correct this immediately. Also noticed other "demerits" at the bar including personal drinks from a fast food restaurant that a bartender was sipping from. 

The meal was decent when we finally sat down. Our server was great and he was very informative. The Oysters Rockefeller appetizer is recommended. The Sicilian Oak Grilled Grouper was very well done. 

To be honest I was so grossed out and upset by what I saw at the bar prior to eating that the experience at the restaurant was ruined (for me). My snow-bird parents loved the food though. But they also said they would think twice before going back. I hope that the owners and management take notice and correct the issues at the main bar. I understand the establishment gets busy but you cannot compromise procedure, cut corners and jeopardize customers health to "keep up."

The only reason they got two stars is because we LOVE the food. I requested delivery as our 8 year old was in the middle of a chemo treatment. We have had subs delivered before and never had a problem. This driver refused to go into the hospital, said it was restaurant policy. So that means that I had to leave my 8 year old alone to get my order. So disappointed.

We were on our way to the Great Smokey Mountains and made a side trip to Nashville for a night of music. One of our friends said we needed to eat at Hattie B chicken. We had dinner there. It was underwhelming. We've had better chicken at White Fence Farms in Plainfield IL as well as any Popeyes. It was very greasy and the breading was thick and heavy and the skin thick and tough. I will say the meat was tender and juicy. My wife had the dark meat dinner with baked beans and Cole slaw. I had the three wing meal with baked beans and potato salad. The meal came with a piece of white bread. The baked beans tasted like they came out of a can. My wife's Cole slaw was OK. My potato salad was outstanding with big chunks of potato seasoned perfectly. My wings were enormous. If I lived here this place wouldn't be on our place to eat at regularly.

You may wonder why I would give a Chinese buffet restaurant 5 stars. Let's put things into perspective! It was a Monday evening, I couldn't believe the weekend was over, and I sure didn't want to cook my own dinner. Then again, I did want to stuff my face for as little money as possible. Got the picture?

It was the first time we came here and we were happy by the time we left. Warm soups, dimsum, all types of meat and fish, vegetables, salads, sushi, fried chicken and french fries, soft serve, cakes, cookies, jello... oh, and my fave: sesame balls! I'm probably forgetting about a whole lot of other foods but need I say more?

Everything I ate was tasty and fresh. Staff was friendly and quick to take away empty plates, and for $14 per person you really have no right to complain.

I sat two seats away from Robert during the "hat" incident. 

The food was good yet overpriced, but of course the incident left a bad taste in our mouths and made us too easily forget anything else that had transpired that night. 

To this day I still feel as if the whole situation was handled poorly. 

I posted the original viral post on Facebook. Over 9,000 shares currently. You can read it here: https://www.facebook.com/morganoverholt

I had driven past this place dozens of times and never knew what a Kolache was. (I guessed it must be some fancy brand of coffee). About 2 months ago someone brought a box of these kolaches to my office and I tried one. They are not coffee although the Kolache Factory does serve coffee. No. These little things are sweet bread rolls filled with a variety of different things from meats and cheeses to fruit and cream cheese. 
I stopped in for the first time today for a quick breakfast on the run.  The girl who helped us was super friendly as soon as we walked in the door, explaining the menu and helping us make selections. My daughter and her friend absolutely loved the Cinnamon Roll and I had a Ranchero and Sausage Egg and Cheese. They were both amazing. If you want to try something different for breakfast stop in here. If you ever buy breakfast for a group, these little flavor bombs are sure to be a crowd pleaser!

In the book One Thousand and One Arabian Nights, Shahrazad, the new bride of the King tells her husband a new story every night for 1001 nights to put off her execution. She must be pretty good at story-telling because she survives at least 1001 nights just because he wants to hear how the stories end. I wonder though if she makes a mean hummus?  Shahrazad is a very popular female name in the Middle East and probably where this restaurant takes it name for those of you who like trivia and were wondering about the name.

Because this is a new restaurant in West County I am giving them the benefit of the doubt that they will improve the service and staffing.  I have dined here twice in the past week because my husband & I loved the food.  The one server they do have handles everything in the dining room and she is a sweetheart.  But, she is only one person, and they could really use two or three.

What I do love about this restaurant besides the delicious food is that its very small and has a nice family friendly feel to it.  The owner comes out of the kitchen and talks to you and even brings you stuff to try just because.  This is a nice touch.

My daughters were with us and ordered double cheese burgers.  New Flash!! These are the biggest burgers ever and they couldn't even bite into them without first taking them apart!  These came with fries and a soda so it was a very good value at $7.99 because they were basically two meals.  My daughter ate the rest of hers the next day for dinner. They were tasty burgers made from Halal meat and the fries were really good too. (I know because I ate some of them :)
Their Falafal, Hummus and Baba Ganoujsh are all wildly delicious.
I have ordered the kabobs both times and chose 3 different meats, kafka, lamb and chicken.  These are served with a generous portion of rice and its all very flavorful and filling.  

If you like Mediterranean/Middle Eastern food or are just curious to try it you should stop in Shahrazad.  They have a nice size menu with a good selection, including burgers and italian beef sandwiches if you are dining with picky eaters.  They also have a kids menu that includes a hot dog and fries.  With my picky teenagers we were able to eat Mediterranean and they were able to have an American cheeseburger.  Win/Win!

Weird and Awkward! That is how I felt while dining here.  Communicating with the wait staff was difficult also.  The servers where not very friendly and seemed tentative.  We had to ask for everything; refills on our drinks, napkins, our check.  They seemed bothered because they had sat down at the table and were talking to each other....
That aside, I asked for my Chicken Vindaloo to NOT be very spicy.  It tasted very good but, it was VERY spicy. This is the reason I needed multiple refills.
Perhaps this was a cultural thing because many of the reviews from the Indian population seemed favorable but if this restaurant is interested in appealing to American diners who expect at the least a modicum of personality, adeptness and finesse in their service they are going to have to step up their game.  Their are many other Indian restaurants in West County that have great food and good service.

Finger lickin good hot chicken.  I'm missin Hattie B's...

I was in Nashville on a business trip months ago and had to find out what hot chicken was all about.  My Nashville colleagues had not heard of Hattie B's (or hot chicken) and I was like whaaat???? (not everyone is a food lover ya know).

I whipped out my yelp app and found a number of hot chicken joints but Hattie had glowing reviews and pics had me drooling. Being new to the hot chicken scene I suggested we stop in for lunch.

Arriving around 1pm  there was a huge line out the door.  I'd say about a 30 min wait. In the mean time you can browse the crafty selection of hats and t-shirts like "Shut the Cluck Up", which I absolutely had to have and a token of my memorable & ultra tasty experience here.

You order food at counter, they give you a # and bring it out to you.  I was flying home late that afternoon and wanted my guy to experience this awesomeness so I ordered a 2nd sandwich and asked the nice man at counter if he could package it really well since I needed to pack in my luggage.  What a rock star! Guys in back did a phenomenal job and clearly went out of their way.  The entire box was sealed in plastic wrap.

Service was super efficient.  Cashiers went through orders in lightening speed.  I decided on the med hot (thinking the hot might be too hot) Chicken sandwich with Pimento mac & cheese.  Friend had the chicken breast plate which looked humungo & amazing.  Sandwich comes with slaw, sauce and pickle.  I ordered sans slaw.

This chicken was so good, I was smiling and devouring the entire time.  Thick and juicy lightly coated in flour.  Perfect crisp factor.  It was perfect in every way.  Great flavor.  Heat level was mild for me and I probably could've handled the Hot.  Pimento mac & cheese was creamy & pimentoey, but not overly.  Great cheese consistency and yummy.  I was full and couldn't finish all of it, but hot damn this was tasty hot chicken!

Didn't try any of the desserts but they have a nice selection including sides, chicken plates and offer beer. Spacious & ample seating indoors and out.  This is the real deal y'all.  Come and get it.

*First Visit Alert

Finally! Between work and kids activities, I was finally able to grab a bite to eat here with my wife. Restaurant was pretty empty (1:00pm Friday) which was surprising but no complaints here... Loved the absence of the crowds; especially with Covid 19 floating around! 

From the point of ordering to getting our meal was about 15 minutes...not bad Nice job! Ordered Carne Asada combination plate with no beans and extra rice for my wife and I ordered the Chimichanga with carne asada. They brought the food to us which was a nice twist for a fast food place but here is where my two stars start kicking in... my wife's dish had the Carne Asada BUT with all beans. We asked for no beans with extra rice so I'm not sure what happened here. I took the dish up to the counter and asked what happened to the extra rice and no beans....they apologized and took the plate from me....okay, no problem....wrong.

They got a new plate and loaded two spoonfuls of rice and moved the carne asada over with a fork and two finger tips!! I could not believe what I just witnessed and called her out on it because she wasn't even wearing gloves....you know, those clear ones? Why don't you all wear gloves; you're in the business of food...please start wearing gloves when handling food!

Another piece was cooked and loaded on to the plate with utensils this time. The food tasted amazing other than the Carne Asada lacking flavor. And just a suggestion to the business, it would be temporary but I really think you should use paper plates (not real plates) until Covid 19 has subsided. You use plastic forks and plastic knives; why not use paper plates...just a thought to help with sanitary practices. And again, please start using gloves while you handle and dish up food! I'm willing to give them another shot because I believe in second chances and definitely giving better ratings but if the cooks are not wearing gloves; I will take my business elsewhere.

I went to Perks last week on the day after their opening. I ordered the Low Carb Breakfast Bowl and an Iced Coffee. The Breakfast Bowl is much better than what Starbucks or CC's offers for breakfast; the food at Perks is made-to-order/fresh (not Sysco garbage). They also have a lunch menu in addition to their breakfast offerings. Overall, I was impressed with the variety on their menu and plan on going back soon.

If you've ever been to Estia in Center City, I can tell you now that Estia Taverna is basically the same restaurant, but the prices for many of the menu items are lesser in comparison to Estia in Center City. In addition, the restaurant itself is smaller, but the quality of the food is very much the same. 

We were able to book a reservation for two at 7:30pm the day before with no issue. We arrived a few minutes before our reservation and we're seated immediately. Our server was very nice and helpful. She informed us of the specials and even had some good recommendations. I ordered the lamb chops, which are so good. The dish is three lamb chops marinated in olive oil, fresh herbs and lemon, served with Greek fried potatoes.
