The fried potatoes sort of take away from the elegance of the experience, but they are good. My wife ordered the chilean sea bass plaki. It's so delicious. Definitely one of the best I've tasted.

For dessert, we went with the Karidopita, which is a honey walnut cake with cinnamon lemon syrup and candied orange zest served with vanillo gelato. It was also very delicious. Usually, when I eat at Greek/Mediterranean restaurants, I order baklava for dessert. The baklava at Estia Taverna includes pistachios, walnuts and caramel sauce. It seemed different from what I'm used, therefore, I decided not to take a chance. Next time, I think I'll try it.

I don't hand out too many 5-star ratings, but the food here is just that awesome. I came here specifically for tapas. Speaking of tapas, if you're open to all kinds of dishes, meats, etc., I highly recommend the Med-Latin plate. It's enough for two people. It includes hummus and pita, which isn't anything to go crazy over, but the hummus is pretty good. The calamari is good and the beef kabobs were juicy and tender. The other items in the Medi-Latin plate, which were amazing in my opinion were the spicy pulled chicken empanadas, the buffalo chicken croquettes and the spanakopita. This isn't the spanakopita you get in bulk at BJ's; it's made with love.

I couldn't leave here without ordering the lobster and crab mac and cheese. Maybe it's me, but it seems like 80% of the restaurants in Philly serve some variation of lobster mac and cheese. Well, let me be the one to say...Valanni has the BEST lobster mac and cheese in Philly. Oh, did I mention it also has crab? I've had lobster mac at R2L, Continental and other locations, but they don't compare. 

The Crispy Shitake Polenta was also good. It's sautéed shrimp, with warm feta, pine nuts, roasted tomatoes and pesto. It was the last plate we shared and after having the aforementioned items, it didn't compare. It was like going to a concert and seeing the opening act perform after the main act. 

I was in a mojito mood and tried both the coconut mojito and the mango mojito. I preferred the mango as the coconut was a little too frothy.

Overall, if you want to do tapas, I definitely recommend giving Valanni a try. Just a few things to consider:

1. Make a reservation. It's gets crowded quickly.
2. It's not the best location for a romantic date. It gets pretty loud. 
3. The dining area is small, so if you don't like sitting close to people you don't know, you may want to go elsewhere.
4. On busy nights, your wait time for your food may be a little longer than normal. Feel free to let your server know if you've been waiting too long (depending on what you define as a long wait for food). 
5. If you decide to go and you're treating, hit me up because I will come with.

The viewing rooms are really narrow - it's quite odd. The chairs do not recline at all. The service is pretty slow. Not really a good experience. Also, this place is right off 69th street, which, from what I understand it used to be quite popular, fun, and crowded. But you wouldn't know that now - it does not convey the feeling of safety! I'd recommend a different place solely because the chairs do not recline at all!
We rented a private room for karaoke. Their selection of songs was horrible. I cant emphasize enough that they really don't have anything. Their food was pretty good though.

I treated my husband to a trip to Santa Barbara for his birthday weekend and I'm thrilled Mar Monte was recently acquired by Hyatt as I'm a WOH Member and we most often stay at their properties. This hotel has recently been renovated and while it's not super modern and up-to-date, it has a ton of classic SB charm and you CANNOT beat the location mere steps from the beach. They complimentarily updated our room to a partial-ocean view and we butted up against the pool area which was beautiful. 

This was our first time staying in a hotel since COVID struck and while we were initially hesitant, we absolutely felt safe upon check-in. The property wasn't very busy and everyone respected social distancing and mask guidelines. There's a few different buildings that make up this property and plenty parking along the street or on the property in an underground structure. They are also located within walking distance to the SB Zoo which is great for families. We will definitely be back when we return to SB!

Why did I deduct one star? The hallways smell a bit musty and the rooms are fairly small. There weren't that many amenities within the room and it's not an ideal hotel for individuals with ADA needs.

Seriously? I live about 1/4 mile from here and if I don't jog there and back, I'm gonna gain 2,343,958 pounds, because I'm going to have a hard time not going there for every meal. And I could, because the options are mathematically endless. You can order tortas, burritos, tacos, soups (12 a day, and they vary), quesadillas, flautas ... and on and on and on, with any meat or Mexican veggie or tofu that you can think of, like nopalitos and squash, just for example. This accommodates vegetarians, cheesatarians, airatarians, and gluten-free, corn-free, rice-free, and whatnot vegans too. Then, you get up to 3 add-ons free. Then, there are premium add-ons. They serve breakfast all day. So .... if you think about it, you could never get the same thing twice for the rest of your life.
I test Mexican restaurants with a bean and cheese burrito. In fact, that's usually all I get, because of the calorie situation. But here I might consider tofu, however odd that might sound, but I bet they do it right. They do everything right. Anyway, I added rice, potatoes, and cabbage. The (nicest) man (I've ever met in my life) threw in extra red and green salsa so I could learn which I preferred. I prefer both. 
I asked how long it would be and he said about 5 minutes, and gave me water for my dog, who was waiting in the car (it was about 63 degrees, so no worries). It took about 2 minutes. Ummmmm ... how is this possible?
But wait. The food. Is so. Good. And big. I ate a third of my $4 "small/medium" (to call it a "small" would be a misnomer) burrito for lunch today. I think I will have the rest tomorrow and the rest the next day. And the tortilla will still taste fresh, no doubt. But not because of preservatives. Because it was smiled upon by angels.
They have seating, but they sell everything by the pint or bigger. Therefore, I can cater a meal from Tania's 33 and pretend it is my own, but I wouldn't do that. Or would I? 
Dear God! Do they have Tania's Anonymous?

VISIT HISTORY: 
- last visit: today after work with a colleague bc we wanted to sit outside drink beer and chill 
- frequency: been here ~4 times. Went to its collloquial brewery tour and other times to hang with friends 
- next visit: would go more regularly if I didn't live so far but would definitely travel the distance for the vibe + food  

FOODRINK:
* firstly, i must state my weakness as I have beer snobbery tendencies*
- saw a lot of recommendation for the fig so didn't get it to stay hipster and underrated
- fried brussel sprouts: it's not that fried. More crispy than fried. Served with lemon so you can add that little squeeze. Excellent! I felt like a good person bc I gave the last bite to my friend even though I really didn't want to. Would order it every single time when I return.  NOMZ. 
- sausage pizza: more delish than expected. caramelized onions really make this dish 
- fontecione(sp?): leeks make this dish. Sad amount of spinach though.
- doughs of the pizza: great chewy mouth feel. Excellent for both bc probably they use the same dough. The crust was blackened but crust & I never got along anyways so I just stared at its burnt existence 
- a pedestrian complimented me on the pizza as if I made them 
- flight of 6 for $10. Can't go wrong 
- spring haze: favorite beer on the flight
- overall, highly recommend for the the quantity/quality of food you get

VIBE: 
- friendly & local 
- hipster
- i was counting how the number of rings the waiter had 
- lots of painting 
- seasonally relevant beer titles (last time I came, it was political) 
- dogs and people chillin' outside 
- wait times: 10 minutes (for food since ordering) and 1 minute (since asking for check)

I went to Philly Cupcake once, and that was enough.  I liked the idea of a Cupcake store, but this ain't no Crumbs.  

"Gourmet" cupcakes that are no bigger than cupcakes you'd bake at home, and a lot less tastier.  Philly Cupcake is all about the flash and glitz of the storefront.  

For $3-4 per (Seriously, that expensive for a little cupcake?), you can get yourself a dry, dense cupcake with tasteless frosting that reminded me of crisco.  I got the Chocolate cake w/ Vanilla Buttercream Classic ($3) and a Twix Dream Vanilla Fancy ($4).  Both cakes were dense and dry, and they were two different flavors, two completely separate batches.  Something's wrong here.  

If you want to spend $4 for a cupcake, take a trip to NYC and go to Crumbs and get a cupcake the size of the Incredible Hulk's fist! 

If you want a delicious, moist cupcake in Philly, do yourself a favor and hunt down the Buttercream Cupcake Truck.  (or buy a box of duncan hines!)

I really don't like giving bad reviews, but for such an overpriced baked good, I was expecting a helluvalot more.  You can get a better finished good out of a box of Duncan Hines!

Having traveled extensively through the South and LOVING southern food/cajun food, I had high hopes for The Mustard Seed Restaurant. My Dad and I stopped by for dinner before going to a concert at the Reno Events Center. I started with their soup of the day: chicken pot pie soup. The soup was rich and hearty but lacked in the overall flavor department. The cornbread that was served with the soup was dry and again, lacked in the flavor department.

For my entree, I ordered the fried chicken with a side of mac n' cheese and candied yams. The chicken was juicy and tasty and had nice flavor. The mac n' cheese was more of a casserole, and again, didn't really have any real cheese flavor. The candied yams were overly sweet and I could only make it through a few bites before it was overpowering.

Nice try, Reno. I'll stick with my trips to the South to get real, quality southern food.

DO:

* Come for lunch. You will get the exact same meal at a much more reasonable price. 
* Save some room for the fried bananas. Holy smokes are they delicious. 
* Wait for the better cuts of meat to come around. Do not waste your time on chicken and sausages. There are men walking around with filet mignon and lamb chops. Have some pride. 
* Eat all of the meats wrapped in bacon. You will have a choice between filet mignon and filet mignon wrapped in bacon. Do you really need me to tell you which one you should eat?
* Ask for a specific cut of meat if it doesn't come by your table within a reasonable time frame. They are happy to find the _____ guy and send him over. 
* Ask for a slice from the inside. In my experience, the outside slices are overly seasoned and salty. You can ask not to be given an outside piece (or if they give you one, just ask for another slice!).
* Try the house special. It's delicious. 

DO NOT:

* Get sucked into the salad bar. Yes, it is delicious. Yes, everything looks great. That is their ploy. Remember, you just paid $50 for all-you-can-eat meat. Do you really want to fill up that room in your stomach with Romaine lettuce and green beans !?
* Buy cocktails. They will be crazy overpriced. Also, they will take up room in your stomach that can be better filled by meat. 
* Zone out when the waiter asks what kind of water you want. There are THREE options. If you order still water after hearing him offer still or sparkling, you will get BOTTLED still water. Wait until he also offers tap. Unless you really want to pay for bottled water. Really?
* Plan any strenuous activities for after your meal. You will not be able to move. You will probably want to sit at the table and moan in discomfort for a while before attempting to leave the restaurant. This is to be expected, do not be alarmed. This feeling will pass, to be replaced by a pleasant, meat-induced semi-comatose state.

I understand why people are writing such long posts about this place. It deserves every word of praise. 

The backdrop: The Catbird Seat newly opened late 2011, with Josh Habiger and Erik Anderson at the helm, who have worked under Thomas Keller (The French Laundry & Per Se) and Grant Achatz (Alinea & Next). GQ named it one of the Top 10 Best New Restaurants. My friends in Nashville told me about all the hype. A few days ago, I miraculously scored reservations here. I drove up from Atlanta to eat here. 

The Catbird Seat is marked by a singular sign over a brown door. You open the door, someone is already expecting you, knows your name, and escorts you down a short hallway, up an elevator, and to the second floor. A bright pink hallway opens up to a small white-washed room. $100 per person. Extra for wine pairings.  32 seats, majority of which are bar-style around the center kitchen. No menu. Give your dietary restrictions and they take care of the rest. Right in front of you.  

Each and every dish was spectacular. Stellar through and through. Pleasing to every sense. You savored each dish. But each subsequent dish makes you forget about its predecessor. The portions were just the right size; when you finished, you were yearning for one more bite ... 

Porcini mushroom and parmesan spread mini-Oreos. A triad of snacks: Island Creek oyster with cucumber, a bacon-infused cornbread, and Hot Chicken with dill pickle and Wonder Bread puree (an awesome acknowledgement of Prince's in Nashville). Tasmanian sea trout with pork lardo, clover, French pickles, and egg. Braised pork belly with celery, chartreuse, and beech mushrooms immersed in shrimp and jalapeno puree (heavenly). Alaskan cod with dollops of chamomile, lemon, cauliflower puree, and spring herbs. Roasted pigeon with greens, yogurt, and pigeon liver mousse (decadent). Beef wagyu slow-cooked with juniper sauce, chives, spinach, and trumpets. Brillat-Savarin cheese with rhubarb syrup and puffed wild rice. Cucumber and lime cream with toasted rice. Maple custard dessert with bacon garnish served in an intact egg shell (so unbelievable I started laughing uncontrollably). Pineapple gelee with oak ice cream, cherry crisp, and bourbon balls (beautiful and technically mind-blowing). Toffee and cream mini-Oreos.  This paragraph transpired over 4 glorious hours.  
 
When you take a bathroom break, pay attention to the walls. Framed menus from places such as The French Laundry, Per Se, Alinea, El Bulli ... 

The best meal of my life was at Le Bernadin. This is right up there. This was art. This was joyous. But here are the differences. 

Here, your dish is served by the chef himself, with an explanation and a story. You can ask questions and they will answer you. Hell, I asked them how they made those bourbon balls! When you're done consuming a dish, you look around the place and see dishes you haven't had (you become eager) or you see dishes you've just consumed (you start yearning). You stare straight ahead and watch the meticulous work behind each dish. If they're making that dish for someone else, you can see how your dish was constructed. You're persistently bombarded with visual cues, always thinking about what you had and what you're about to have, that you will salivate to new levels. All the while, you make friends with your neighbors, as you all share in the wondrous disbelief.

The ability to interact with the chefs was so inspiring. You see how hard these guys work. No runners. They're the ones who deliver the dishes. At the end of my meal, it was a pleasure to actually express my gratitude and appreciate in person. And the fact that they were willing to give me a list of personal suggestions for an upcoming trip to Minneapolis is even cooler. 

Josh and Erik go by their first names there. Josh told me he never felt comfortable in the traditional formal white-cloth restaurants. Hence why The Catbird Seat was born. 

This place is a success on so many levels. One of the greatest experiences I've ever had.

This is a 4.5 star review which has been rounded up for history, atmosphere, and value.

I'm assuming most of the poor reviews here must be from tourists who didn't know what to expect before arriving.  Tujague's is one of the oldest restaurants in New Orleans and has most definitely kept its old school charm.  The dining room is filled with pictures of celebrities from days gone by all along the walls.  Tables are cloth-topped and waiters are tuxedo-clad.  

There's no menu.  It's a fixed 5 course meal (on special occasions they alter the number of courses) that almost always includes their brisket.  Which I understand hasn't changed in its recipe since the beginning.  You can alter the courses if you need to, like substituting a different soup or changing the entree to something that they haven't informed you of (I'll get to this later).  Are any of the individual courses knock your socks off amazing?  No.  But altogether the meal is very satisfying and the sum of the courses more than warrants the cost of the meal.

You don't come here for new takes on creole food, special, or unique dishes.  You come here for the atmosphere and the vibe.

The bar is something to see, too.  There's a huge mirror behind a long cypress bar.  Other than the flat screen TV and LSU paraphernalia in the corner I doubt it's changed much since the 1800s.  The bartenders and knowledgable and will serve you excellent cocktails.  You can also order a la carte from the bar.  

Here's an insider's tip - the best value meal in the FQ isn't even offered by the waiters in the dining room unless you ask for it specifically.  It's called chicken bonne femme.  A half order of that and a sazerac will run you under $20.  The bonne femme is a pan fried chicken topped with thinly sliced lightly fried potatoes, and garnished with an avalanche of parsley and garlic.  Go to the bar, order yourself a Sazerac and a half a chicken bonne femme, and thank me later.

When I get friends to visit from out of town, they often ask "where can I get some great seafood?", due to the close proximity to the ocean. Unfortunately, I feel like unless you want to dine in a nice atmosphere...our options are severely limited when it comes to casual seafood.

Big Ray's Fish Camp changes all of that.

What it lacks in restaurant size, they make up for in food quality and taste. It is *exactly* what Tampa needed. Yes, a lot of the options are fried...but if I can honest with myself, a lot of seafood is great that way. The grouper sandwich has been fantastic on both attempts. The shrimp poboy looks like something out of a Southern Living magazine each time I have ordered it...I'm almost too afraid to eat it. They could lighten up on the lettuce, however.

The onion rings...maaaaybe the best in Tampa.

I haven't took the chance yet, but they always seem to have a rotating off-menu special. Last time it was a Lobster Corndog. Yes, you read that right. Yes, it is what is sounds like. Yes, I'm a dummy and didn't order it.

My only hope is that their due success affords them the option to expand the restaurant in some form. The inside is small and only shrinks when a line forms at the register. Good problem to have.

Love Love Love this place. I saw on Time Out magazine that Reading Terminal Market is one of the best places to visit ones in Philadelphia. Happy to say I wasn't disappointed.

Food of all kind, Cajun, Seafood, Phillys, Japanese, coffee and best of all CHOCOLATE. 

They have little markets to buy some grocery's like vegetables, fermented food, honey, spices meat... ugh just an orgasmic place to be.

I especially loved the pastries the Amish made. Delicious everything in their amazing, check it out of your ever in the area!

Today's review is about a singular experience that I had yesterday at lunchtime. Overall, this is a very good restaurant. Due to yesterday's experience, I can only give 2 stars today.

One of the reasons I write Yelp reviews is not only to guide fellow consumers to great establishments, but to also give proprietors feedback when something can be easily corrected. This was the case yesterday at lunchtime. 

We were a party of four for a business lunch sitting on the outside yet enclosed patio. The server made the same kind of slip up any server could make... As he served one of us her French toast lunch, he knocked into her water glass which caused the syrup to become aloft. Out of reflex, my manager reached for the falling syrup, which caused it all to spill everywhere. Had she not grabbed it, it still would have spilled all over the table and her. She ended up with syrup all over her hand, syrup on the table, down the sides and down the front of her pant leg. 

Although the server did the right thing by getting her a rag and soda water, he offered no other concession. Her lunch should have been comped as a gesture of sincere regret for what had happened. I think this lunch is $12.99, maybe $14.99? My manager probably had to get her pants dry cleaned.

This simply was not the way to handle this situation. It would have left us all with such a better feeling had some concession been offered or even a manager visit. I have a sneaky suspicion the server never mentioned it to management because I would be shocked that no one came over to officially apologize let alone comp the entrée.

You guys can do better.

I had the most lovely meal last night at Kensington Quarters.

March 10. 78 degrees. A twinkly-lit and spacious outdoor patio. A glass of cider. And the best damn burger I've had in months (maybe years!).

What makes it the best damn burger?

1. Incredibly fresh meat. You can see the dead cows from inside the restaurant.
2. Perfect meat to bun ratio.
3. It fit in my hands. No mess, no fuss. 
4. An incredibly savory special sauce that sings.
5. They have a charcoal grill, so you get that backyard flavor. 

While my burger came out a little more medium than medium rare like I had ordered, it honestly didn't matter. The flavor was there. And to me, that is big.

Served with pickles and a small portion of rosemary potatoes, this burger will leave you full and immensely satisfied-- but not feeling like you overdid it. 

I am eager to return to KQ.

Forget your fancy salads, people. RFE is real high-quality eats at an average price tag. 

I've enjoyed lunch at Real Food Eatery twice now and I don't think you can get a more filling, more healthy, more delicious meal for $10, anywhere in Center City. The herb-rubbed chicken skewers are marinated and juicy, the brown rice cooked perfectly, the roasted beets are tender, the broccoli is garlicky and still has a little crunch. It reminds me of the meals I cook for myself for dinner-- in the best way. Protein, complex carb, veg. 

Note: Cans of La Croix are a splurge at $2.

This is what you need to know about The Little Lion:

There are dollar oysters at happy hour and happy hour encompasses THE ENTIRE restaurant. Not just the space at the bar. $10 burgers, $1 oysters, $3 drafts etc. My friend and I shared a dozen oysters, we each had two drinks and I had burger. The bill was $35. Seriously. 

Usually southern food isn't my thing, but I'll be back at the Little Lion for sure.

I planned a work party here for 20 people with a reserved room overlooking the main area, two hour buffet and open bar with a $500 minimum. It was very difficult for XFINITY Live!'s event coordinator to respond to my emails within an appropriate amount of time. Our bartender by the Skybox was constantly playing with his phone, showing my co-workers pictures of his girlfriend, and generally being a dick. 

The wings were dry. As in, no sauce at all. Burgers were like pucks. Our group had a great time, and the concept of the place is cool, but I wouldn't order food let alone hold an overpriced event here again.

Decidedly underwhelming, but still good.

Here are the facts:

1. Communal seating only.
2. Two kinds of wine: "house" red and white. Outrageously priced at $8.50/glass.
3. If you're not into meat on your pizza, you don't have that many veggie options. It's Margherita, or eggplant, or lots of cheese. There ain't nothin' green round these parts.
4. If you like meat on your pie, there's no pepperoni, or soppresata. Sausage or prosciutto only. 

Flavors are standard. Quality cheese, sauce and crust. Service is fine. I wouldn't rush back...from Vetri, I expected better.

Abe Fisher = your mom's best Jewish food, on crack. We went, we ate, we conquered. And at the chef's counter, no less. We got to see pretty much every menu item being made and delivered. It was awesome. 

$39 tasting menu or bust. How could you go wrong? That means we tasted a total of eight different items. 

Here are my top picks:
Brussel Caesar (I just really love all featured ingredients)
Kasha Varnishkas (raviolis stuffed with buckwheat, so delicate)
Pork Belly Reuben (thinly sliced belly makes this "sandwich" so rich)
Veal Schnitzel Tacos (tasted like deep-fried brisket, huge portion too)
Apple Struedel (fresh and warm, and the sour cream was a perfect complement)

Here's what I probably wouldn't get again:
Roasted Sweet Potato (boring)
Sweet and Sour Meatballs (flavorful, but a little dry/tough)
Bacon and Egg Cream (holy smokes, do I hate smoke-flavored things!)

Here's what I want to try next time:
Pastrami Hash Knish 
Cholent Pot Pie
Almond Panna Cotta 

Lovely environment (more casual than I expected), lovely service. Sit at the chef's counter if you can. Thank you kindly, Cook + Solo.

Move over, Circles.

I have loved everything I've eaten thus far at JJ Thai. After two visits and and upcoming third, this under-the-radar spot in the hustle and bustle of Rittenhouse takes the cake for best Thai in Philly right now.

Pad thai is perfectly cooked and seasoned, and the pad see ew is nice and dark, just how I like it. Curry is flavorful and not too thin. The mussels are great to start, and dessert is simply too good to skip. Whether you get the mango and sticky rice, fried ice cream (it's served in flames!) or the affogatto, you will surely be pleased. 

You can always get a res (for now!) and they won't kick you out if you're lingering over your wine (it's BYOB). Prices are beyond reasonable and the decor is nice enough that it feels almost like an occasion spot. You should go.

Cholita, light of my life, fire of my loins. My sin, my soul. Cho-lee-ta: the tip of the tongue taking a trip of three steps down the palate to tap, at three, on the teeth. Cho. Lee. Ta. Some say the tacos are a tad little, but we all know that wonderful things sometimes come in small packages.  Just order 3, and enjoy the proverbial spice of life.  The meats are succulent, the spices are punchy, and the tortillas have the delicate toasty richness that only handmade tortillas have.  Having dined here several times, the service has been consistently amiable and efficient.  The cocktail offerings are okay - well made drinks at a decent value - but nothing too interesting except for the excellent, authentic Michelada, the equal to which you'd have to travel four states south for.

Post Phillies 5k run Katrina C. and I decided on Chhaya for brunch.  It was a great idea!  I had the cornbread waffle with sausage gravy, an egg, and potatoes.  It was delicious.  The coffee was awesome.  I'm not a huge coffee drinker, but I had a couple cups because it was so good.  We also shared a stuffed french toast waffle, which was amazing, but I would never be able to eat the whole thing, a couple of bites was perfect.  The smoked turkey panini got rave reviews, as did the bagel with cream cheese, avocado, and tomato.  Started to get crowded around 12.  I only wish I lived closer, but Chhaya definitely rivals some of Philly's better known brunch spots.  Prices are super reasonable too, more like diner prices.

This is a great cocktail bar with a very cool vibe. It's a small place, but it's meant to look like a 1920s speakeasy so it definitely fits the scene. It's a great place to take a date or lounge on their fancy couches with a small group of friends.

Aside from the cool decor, their cocktails were amazing. They have specialty cocktails for every liquor. If you like mild and sweet drinks, I highly recommend the Calamity Jane, which has olive oil washed gin, berry tea, passion fruit, and lychee. The only downside is that the cocktails are a little on the pricier side for Reno, but for very unique drinks like these, it's worth it.

Should I stay or should I go now?
Should I stay or should I go now?
If I go there will be trouble
An' if I stay it will be double 


If I'd had even a bit of awareness of my surroundings I probably should have asked myself that question because I think the answer would have been "go now." But I can be a bit oblivious at times......

THE GOOD
The appetizer of hummus, cucumbers, tzatziki and pita: Complimentary and a nice portion too!

Gyro meat: Super flavorful and perfectly sliced strips/chunks. No thin, little shaved pieces! 

Tzatsiki sauce: Very flavorful with plenty of dill

Baklava: Serving is huge and sweet ~ just not what I'm used to. I like baklava that is more layered and flakey but this was still good. 

Pastitsio: Looked like a giant piece of lasagna and actually very good. M loved it and ate every bit of it. However we found it odd that a stray piece of lettuce and a carrot made its way under the Pastitsio. Odd because it wasn't served on a plate with any salad or veggies. The Pastitsio was served completely by itself so how did the lettuce and carrot get there??


THE DECENT/OKAY/MEH
Lamb chops: Flavorful but overcooked

Roasted Lamb with gravy:  I thought it was "okay"

Side Salad served with meal: Can't really go wrong, ya know. Pretty basic salad with lettuce, a tomato slice or two, a cucumber slice, a couple of olives and some feta cheese. The salad was heavily dressed though and was swimming in salad dressing. 

Employees: They were friendly enough and our server Heidi was nice and helpful in helping us to understand our coupons. The buser or whatever the young man was....he was nice and attentive. We had walked outside for a minute after ordering and M left her phone on the booth seat. He made sure to let us know he moved it to a safer spot. He also checked on us a time or two. Perhaps he sensed our overall disappointment after we paid and left because he actually came outside to where we relaxing for a minute to make sure everything was ok.


THE POOR/INEXCUSABLE
OK, I don't even know how this can be considered acceptable. The staff was doing "maintenance" during business hours. Granted they weren't very busy but it was disturbing to see a female employee up on a ladder in the kitchen area that is clearly visible to customers working to put together a vent and doing drilling in to the ceiling and metal fixture RIGHT OVER THE COOKING AREA. Holy cow, we watched her spin that vent around in circles from the ceiling while our gyro meat was being sliced off the rotisserie spit directly under that spinning vent. Sure hope there aren't any metal shavings and gunk in the gyro meat we took home!  Four of the employees (servers?) hung out at the counter gossiping, drinking beverages and playing with their phones. Again, in an area clearly in view of customers. Our server also decided it was a good time to paint her nails. And does it even need repeating but yes, in an area clearly in view of customers. When we needed her for something she stood at our table waving her hands back and forth to dry them!!

Nanobrewery Sentinel Peak opened to the public today and the public was pleased! 

We've been anxiously awaiting the opening of Sentinel Peak Brewing Company and following their progress on Facebook. Finally today was the day! My girls and I got there just a bit after they opened the door at 3pm and the place was absolutely packed. There is plenty of seating at Sentinel Peak; places at the bar, a long high top table just off the bar and a long wall of seating that has banquette seating along the wall with chairs on the other side of the tables. However on this day, their grand opening, seating was difficult to get. We found our way to the bar and ordered flights for everyone. We did manage to squeeze in to a corner of the long table near the bar and before too long our flights arrived. Today's sampling was the 1811 Desert Blonde, the Haboob IPA, the Pumpkin Spice and the Monsoon Dunkel. All were very pleasant and smooth. Among the 4 of us, the Blonde was the least favorite although it's still pleasing to the palate. The IPA was the perfect amount of hoppiness for me and not bitter at all. I loved the Dunkel, a smooth brown taste treat. Two of my girls fell in love with the Pumpkin Spice which had a wonderful light spice to it and feels a bit like nice, crisp Autumn day. 

After our flights we each wanted to order a pint. I asked for a sample of the Mr. Beer Nut Brown but was told they weren't really doing "tastes" that it could only be served in a pint glass. I'm not quite sure the waitress understood that I only wanted a sample, not a glass the size of the ones in the flight. I threw caution to the wind and ordered a pint of the Mr. Beer Nut Brown. I'm a huge fan of the nutty, cocoa flavor of nut browns but I hate to say I was disappointed in this one. The flavor was a little dull for my taste.  A young buser was kind enough to exchange it for a Dunkel for me.

Sentinel Peak has a nice selection of light food offerings as well. We ordered an antipasti plate and pretzel sticks with cheese sauce. The antipasti plate consisted of roasted red bell pepper, roasted tomato, marinated artichoke hearts, tasty green olives, plenty of feta cheese and bread. The olive oil and balsamic dressing was delicious and made the dish perfect. The pretzel sticks were soft, plump and with just the right amount of chewiness. They come with your choice of Dunkel Beer Cheese, Jalapeno Ranch or Stone Ground Beer Mustard but we weren't asked our preference...we were served the Dunkel Beer Cheese which was just average so we ended up sopping up the antipasti marinade with the soft pretzels.

Their check out system was a little rough since there was only one iPad swiping station and a very long line waiting to pay their tabs. But you know what? It's their first day and I think they did an incredible job of taking care of their patrons. Every server, every buser, every bartender and the owners were happy, cheerful and excited to show us their stuff.

I'm a fan and I love that Sentinel Peak brought a brewery to midtown and it's just a couple of blocks from work! Darn!

Steer clear, the appeal of this place has long left the building.

I've given Sakura several tries and have never been impressed but our experience on Friday night was the worst. We came for a birthday happy hour before moving across the parking lot to a paint party. Our group trickled in by 2s or 3s on the patio to be a final party of 8. The place wasn't that busy for a Friday evening. Our server, Brittonee was either very preoccupied, just didn't care or she was a very new server. 3 of us ordered drinks at the same time but she only brought 2 to the table. I waited another 5 minutes for my drink and finally flagged her down to ask about it and she proceeded to tell me it was at the bar...she didn't want to spill it when bringing the other 2 drinks out. Really?  K ordered sake for her and the birthday girl and also had to flag down Brittonee a good 10 minutes later to ask once again for the sake. Then she finally brought it out with only one sake cup. After waiting for the 2nd cup for a bit, she had to go to the bar herself to get the other cup. K once again had to serve herself when Brittonee brought the sushi rolls to the table and never returned with soy sauce. Brittonee also brought the wrong roll out to one of my girls and it took a good 15 minutes for the correct one to come out.

My drink, the Sawayaki (cucumber vodka and citrus martini) was mediocre and lacked flavor. L's MaiTai was served with a volcano of ice on top where all the liquor pooled....obviously not mixed. When she sipped the top to try to mix the ice in and got a mouthful of alcohol, the drink suddenly turned in to Kool-aid. 

We asked Brittonee about the Volcano, "a special concoction....served with a flame!" but she said she wasn't allowed to say what is in it because it's their special recipe. She couldn't even tell us what kind of liquor is in it!! She did say no one has ever ordered one from her though. I wonder why?!!

The worst part was when the last friend showed up and had forgotten her wallet at work. One of the other members in our party ordered a drink for her and when Brittonee was asked to bring everyone's bill - she asked for everyone's IDs. Even though everyone had been ID'd at the beginning. Now, I know it was wrong that T ordered a drink for G when G didn't bring her ID but G is obviously over 30 and there was no way she could have been mistaken for someone under age. But the group was harassed about IDs at the end with the blond female manager staring down at everyone over Brittonee's shoulder. This was the most uncomfortable and most unwelcoming feeling any of us have ever experienced at any establishment.

I will not be returning to Sakura and will not be suggesting this establishment for any further gatherings. The food and drink are average at best but I refuse to be harassed and made to feel uncomfortable by a server and manager. Ridiculous.

Ode to Bobo's

Thirty plus years in Tucson and I just can't
Believe I've not visited Bobo's on Grant.

But we were hungry for lunch yesterday afternoon
And my L suggested this amazing little greasy spoon.

A waiting line outside the door, surely a good sign.
The secret these people know will soon also be mine.

Within a few minutes Dave Chapelle's twin called us inside
A super friendly man that really does resemble him, I've not lied.

Everyone at Bobo's is neighborly and the service is fast
A good first impression that surely will last.

L had the eggs, bacon, home fries and chicken fried steak
He had to box up his leftovers so his full belly wouldn't ache.

Why home fries like that aren't offered at other establishments is a mystery to me
Probably smart on Bobo's part since they are surely one of their delicious specialties.

Several lunch options caught my eye but I decided on the patty melt
A perfectly cooked, cheesy and oniony sandwich so filling I wanted to unbuckle my belt.

Customers are rich and poor, redneck and hipster, young and old.
I'm just thankful to say I've now been brought in to this little diner's fold.

The décor and murals don't quite match each other but I love that it's AZ Wildcat Country
Bobo's you are truly a Tucson institution and I profess my love to thee.

We arrived at Wok & Roll on Saturday with high hopes for a delicious and filling Chinese buffet. Filling? Yes. Delicious? No. I'm very disappointed in my experience and really hate to give such a low rating to a fairly new establishment but I wouldn't be a responsible Yelper if I let you walk in to Wok & Roll without giving you a little taste of my own experience.

Rather than get all wordy and clever let me just give you this little rundown:

Pros:
* Crab puffs/rangoons: Fat suckers filled with a delicious cream cheese/crab mixture and fried to golden perfection.
* Pork dumplings: Tasty and plump
* Chinese donuts: Soft, sugary, pillowy and delicious

Cons:
* I'll start with the most egregious - the seafood. We paid extra to take advantage of the seafood buffet. Honestly, it was not good. 
     o Lobster: Claw pieces nestled in what I can only describe as some kind of old, congealed gravy - lumps and all. L had to spit his in to his napkin
     o Salt & Pepper Crab: cooked to nothingness where once you got anything out of the shell, it had no texture whatsoever
     o Crab Legs: Call me crazy but I'm pretty sure my hands aren't supposed to smell like that after cracking crab legs. We had to wash up in the restroom before continuing with our meal.
     o Salt & Pepper Squid: Completely flavorless and boring; at least it wasn't rubbery
     o Sushi: I'd compare the sushi with grocery store sushi. Very average. And what's with the non-spicy wasabi???
     o Cheese Stuffed Mussels: Chewy and extremely "fishy" tasting. Ick.
* Fried Rice: More like steamed rice that was fried perhaps for a very brief moment. Gummy and blah.
* Low Mein: Greasy, pretty non-existent in the vegetable department
* Honey Chicken: Extremely sweet and swimming in sauce. Any chicken "flavor" is completely lost

Other standard Chinese menu items were just okay, not one single item stood out above the others.

Wok & Roll is clean, has a nice set up and is somewhat visually appealing. But there are so many more minuses than pluses overall. I can't imagine wasting my money by coming to Wok & Roll again.

I met a couple of girlfriends at Scordatos Pizzeria for dinner and a nice little catch up session this evening. 

Scordatos is friendly and a little upscale which I love; and everyone is so friendly and gives you the feeling that they are happy you chose Scordatos for your meal. I had a glass of cabernet sauvingnon and was impressed with the pour. Not chintzy at all. I started with the Gorgonzola Cheese and Grape Salad and it was beautiful! Covered in pine nuts and crumbled Gorgonzola, I definitely could have made this my meal but I wisely ate half and put the rest in a to go box so I could sample the pie. And oh, what a pie it was! The Robiola pizza was fresh and delicious. Fantastic crust covered in Robiola, Fontina and Mozzarella cheeses with lots of roasted mushrooms and chopped kalamata olives. As if that wasn't enough, the entire pie was covered in fresh arugula. I managed to finish off two pieces before I gave up and asked for a box.

My friends enjoyed their meals as well and one ordered and took home both a pizza AND eggplant parmesan for her husband. My other friend finished off her meal with some warm chocolate mousse cake with white chocolate gelato and she devoured it all! The menu at Scordatos isn't overwhelmingly huge but still large enough to have a very nice selection. I love that they limit the menu so as to concentrate on making only the very best for you.

When leaving, I felt just as appreciated as when I first walked in. Holding the door open for us and genuinely thanking us for our patronage - I will most definitely be back.

I have driven PAST Blake's in Deming, NM on my way out of Hatch so many times and always thought to myself, "Huh, I really should try them out." But I never do because I just want to get home to Tucson and to be honest, 9 times out of 10 I just put a Sparky's green chile cheeseburger in my belly so I wasn't hungry. When Blake's came to Tucson, I was really excited!!!

Don't believe the hype. The green chile cheeseburger at Blake's is a mediocre burger overall with the saving grace being the green chile. The green chile is delicious but not very hot, at least for my taste but that's not where I find fault with this burger. The actual burger is greasy and just a whatever burger. Mine was thrown together so sloppily that I had more onions and tomatoes off the bun than on it. I literally had to put my burger back together before I could eat it. And then the grease started dripping off my hands. Honestly, I would compare the "burger" part of my sandwich to any old fast food place but priced much higher. We also had seasoned fries which were good and onion rings which were not. The size of the order of onion rings for the price was NOT a bargain at all.

So I'm glad I finally tried Blake's but I really don't think I'll be back. Especially when the green chile double cheeseburger I had at Whataburger was actually better but then again, my judgement on that one may have been clouded by a hangover.

Surely I can't be the only one. 
Yes, there have been others and don't call me Shirley. 

I did it. I fell asleep in a movie theater. But only for a minute ~ I swear!! What do you expect though, I mean reclining leather seats, adult beverages, a dark room. That spells naptime to me.

I've been aware of this living room theater type concept for quite some time but truly never expected such a place to turn up in my T-Town. I applaud loudly and wholeheartedly for Roadhouse Cinemas. It was a little chilly the other night so we grabbed a couple of drinks at the bar and sat on the outdoor patio where there is comfortable lounge type seating and fire pits. It was so nice that we sat there before AND after the movie. 

Prices were fair and I feel like I would have spent the same amount of money for lesser quality food items at a regular movie theater. L and I each had an adult beverage and split some popcorn, which I have to say tasted like it was homemade. The popcorn is served in a big bowl and topped with REAL, not movie theater fake stuff but real, butter.  It was so good that we polished off that entire bowl. I've read other reviews where the reviewers said the food was perhaps below average. Well, I'll tell you that what I smelled didn't seem below average. I will definitely be trying out some of their menu items in the future. 

Every employee we encountered was kind and courteous from the individuals at the ticket counter, to the bartenders to the security guard. All deserve a gold star for their great customer service.

Next time I may have to try one of their specialty coffee drinks though.....or bring along some toothpicks to prop my eyes open.

I found this place while yelping breweries.  I called around and this was the first place to answer.  I talked to David who was extremely friendly and provided a wealth of information for me.  I didn't need to call anywhere else and as soon as we hung up, I told hubby where to go!  Awesome little drive thru gig they have going on for Covid days and the two ladies that greeted us mirrored the friendliness of David.  They were actually out of the cocktail they make in a can, the lavender lemonade (David had already told me this) but they actually advised us of local stores that carry them that may have them, which we ended up finding at Reno Homebrewer! Thanks for letting us know 10Torr.  Pups allowed on the patio when they reopen - can't wait!  Good drinks and great friendly service, what else do you really need?!

First time at this squeeze inn this past Sunday, what a kooky quirky space. Wish we could have eaten on patio, but that goes fast so get there early or be prepared to wait.  Everyone was super friendly from the host Ty to the girl who sat us to our waiter to the girl that brought out the food i wish I knew all their names to shout them out but only caught Connor, who was fantastic.  He wasn't pushy or annoyed when I asked for more time looking at the extensive menu. He wasn't put off when hubby and I decided to split a meal (for a surcharge).  So let's get right to that meal --- delicious!  We shared the "racy Tracy" which is a huge omelette with mushrooms, bacon, cheese and avocado.  Upgraded the potatoes to have cheese on them and I loved these potatoes. Perfectly crisp on outside and soft inside.  Great first experience and I'm looking forward to coming back.  Hubby loved it. 
Side note ---- I was lookin for the women's bathroom and there are two doors next to each other - one says "men" on a handwritten sign and the door next to it isn't noted except for a big stop sign on the door, but with all the weirdness around me I didn't actually think it meant "stop" and figured this had to be the women's restroom. As you guessed it was not, it was the water heater and a girl at the table next to it pointed to the door ACROSS from the men's room, clearly marked women.  Haha well that was an embarrassing end to an otherwise nice brunch.  See you soon SI!

I placed an order using UberEATS for over $70 in food for dinner for my family. An hour and some odd minutes later the driver shows up with one dish in a bag of seafood mac and cheese. Sorry sir, look in your car that's not mine. He said, "ma'am we ask the restaurant before we leave. I have them the order number I was coming to pick up they gave me this and rushed me out. You would have to call the restaurant to resolve."

Ok fine! I call the restaurant and they pick up and they ask to put me on hold. I said no. Don't ask a question if you don't want an actual answer! So I explained my situation and he has to apparently get someone else. This situation is just oh too damn complicated for him to figure out.

A woman, whom I later find out is a Manager named Kelly, gets on the phone. Lo and behold I have to explain it again! After she has heard my predicament while someone's mac and cheese gets lumpy and cold standing in front of me and my $70 worth of dinner sits there cold as ice, she proceeds to tell me how it's the drivers fault! 

My phone is on speaker, so the driver hears this and is incredulous! Instead of taking responsibility for her restaurant's mess up because someone there gave him the wrong order and didn't confirm before letting their food go out their door because it's their business that got paid for the food that's being expected to show up correctly at my front door. She blamed the UBER DRIVER like he walked up in that restaurant and just picked up whatever bag he felt like. I was mad at her rudeness and indignation. Them the dismissiveness in her tone. "Is he gonna bring it back?" Is this what your customer service teaches you? 

Yes he is bringing back that thick cold mac and cheese and you can keep all that food I ordered as well. I asked for a refund. Them I had to ask for the confirmation number on the refund because she wasn't going to offer that either. Took her 4 mins of me on hold to get it.

I emailed UberEATS immediately after I got off the phone. Had a response in less than two hours. I already didn't think they were that great. I expect great service when I spend my money. Sorry for my high expectations. I eat ALL over the city. THIS? Worst experience ever! 

Kelly must be related to owner otherwise it's no way
she would still be working there!

I'm blown away and I wish that I could give them 10 stars!!!  Restaurant Rebirth by far is one of the best dining experiences I've encountered.  My only regret would be that I shouldn't have eaten lunch prior to coming here for dinner.

Definitely make a reservation.  The place isn't that big and every table was full tonight.  Service was awesome! We were immediately seated and drink orders were taken.  I decided to try the Old Fashioned.  It was pretty good drink.  I only had one because I was trying to save room for the good stuff...the food!   Our waiter explained to us the Gumbo of the day, fish of the day and steak of the day.

Tonight's gumbo special was a chicken and andouille sausage gumbo. I definitely had to try that. Just to tease us a little they brought out homemade corn bread with a sweet topping.  It was delicious.  I had read about the BBQ pork belly appetizer so I decided to order that as well.  I am so happy that I went with my first mind and ordered the pork belly. Everyone at my table was envious of my choice because man oh man that was some good belly! LOL!  You cannot go wrong with this choice. It was tender and flavorful.  It was accompanied by the best collard greens that I have ever tasted. And I know my collard greens.  I don't recommend sharing this dish because honestly it's that good and everyone else needs to order their own.

My gumbo came out second. I loved the presentation.  It was served in a mini cast iron pot with a lid. The gumbo was perfect. Every bite had either chicken or sausage or both.  It was nice and spicy just the way I like it. I was absolutely full after finishing this dish.  Somehow a dessert trio showed up at our table. We were absolutely full to the gills but we all managed to taste each one. There was a bread putting, a cafe au lait cream brûlée and a chocolate torte. All three were fabulous. I think the  crème brûlée was my favorite followed by the bread pudding.

If you're in New Orleans and are looking for a wonderful place to eat then you have to come here. It's totally worth the money. You will not be disappointed.

Give it up for THE best sushi spot in Broad Ripple! The once-violin shop has grown into a thriving sushi bar on the village strip.

- Minimal, modern, and comfortable interior with a small sushi bar and dining room. 
- Quiet. Great for independent diners, romantic dates, or professional lunch outing. 
- Lunch special - two rolls and soup/salad for $6.99! Pretty much everything on their lunch menu is under $10. Me likey.
- Fresh, clean, and very yummy! For Indiana, this is up there. 
- Staff is usually pretty quiet. Not sure why. Attentive though.
- HUGE selection of rolls! Like a kid in a candy store...except the candy is raw fish and seaweed.
- Parking does suck in the area. I would suggest parking near the canal and walking over. You'll need a walk after you stuff your face full of sushi.

If you're living in Broad Ripple, it's nice and easy to walk here for some rolls and a beer. If not, sad face for you. Miss you, Sushi Bar!

Out of the neighborhood bars on Broadway, this is the classiest spot for drinks, music, and food. I loved how well done this space was created. It could grace a magazine cover. Every staff member looked like they belonged on a CMT magazine cover with their southern hospitality. Heads up, bathrooms are co-ed and apparently, an easy way to strike up a conversation with someone you know washes their hands. Thanks to Covid that somehow becomes a factor.

We would have frequented here more than we did but wanted to be fair to Nashville and explore all the spots off Broadway. Surprisingly, both times, we came we got seated right away. At the time of our visit in May 2021, they had recently opened. Our first visit we were able to get a bar seat and ended up ordering the truffle fries, yellowtail sashimi, dumplings, and butter tart. The butter tart I can eat every day and never tire of it. IT IS THE BEST DESSERT. My tongue went to food heaven and tasted all the goodness of delish carbs and whiskey pecans. I am a big fan of their sangria and beers on tap. On the second visit, a late night, we got seated near the band and ordered more good food. I can't tell you what we ordered because the cocktail was strong and we were distracted by seriously good local music....BUT the fries were bomb. 

Beauty attracts beauty. So grab a sit, sit your pretty butt down, and enjoy the music coming from the stage while you gorge out on that butter tart. Like Emerson said beautifully, dare to live the life you have dreamed for yourself and come to Twelve Thirty and make your dreams come true!!!!

This is the biggest space venue you'll find downtown. The upstairs rooftop was too hot even for my desert living butt. Still great vibe and bands. When we walked in, told the wait was a three hour list. Ended up snagging seats at the bar. Service was a bit slow because only one bartender worked til the night shift, as in after 8p. He was still attentive and checked in on us. Food lacked flavor and disappointed the crab dip wasn't as good as expected. I ordered the steak salad but my steak was overdone for my medium rare taste. 

This is a generally popular bar but with multitude of choices along the the Broadway strip, it doesn't fall as a top fave. Like a first date, good impressions count. Awkwardness can occur and outcomes are unpredictable. You can up your game!

#ThankYouThursday goes to my favorite coffee spot in midtown. For the sake of fall and winter vibes, in the midst of this pandemic, so glad to see they're open and serving the community harder and safer. I love coming to coffeebar for a cup of hot matcha or lavender latte in the morning.  

Too much uncertainty in this time but hot oatmeal with banana and peanut butter always hits the spot. The customer service is always consistent. 

When you're feeling a pour over, Basha or La Wu honey Thai is the way! Maybe on your next visit, a croissant or two to make your day whole!

Oh well, what can I say? This must be the first one star review that I have written for local business in Reno. As an elite I always represent the best interests for local businesses (even more during a pandemic) because this community is only stronger and better with quality service industry, businesses, and individuals. I have been to many breweries and American restaurants in my life and I've never had the MOST embarrassing and quite offensive service that left me thinking, why did I even reserve or stepped foot in this business? 

I came with a group of friends to celebrate an early birthday celebration. I was so thrilled and looked forward to drinking sour beer from brewers cabinet AND bomb garlic fries they serve. It turned so sour (I didn't even get a drink) when our server came and started to INSULT me and commenting on ' how I roll my rrrrs ' and ' how to behave'. He only carded me among all the other guests that was there - I'm Asian, not like the rest of my white friends. He went on to take my order and insulted my friend for his curly gorgeous hair that he might need to be carded as well because he looks like a underage child with that hair ?? 

WTH? I came for sour beer and fries, left with all the group baffled as to what just happened. Is this person on drugs? 

Wished I had posted some pics, and took more in the beautiful beer garden but what a shame. It's 2020 and racism is real because we literally felt like we got kicked out of this place like when Rosa parks got kicked out of the bus.

I hate change as much as the next person.  I miss Pie in the Sky. But sometimes change is good.

The better half and I stopped in to check it out (after noticing Pie in the Sky was no more).  I'm glad to see its the same people behind that business just changing things up.

For a drink I ordered the Kentucky Bourbon Ale which I was quite pleased with.

As an appetizer we ordered the Fried Pickles, which were some of the best I ever had. I'm by no means a Fried Pickle expert, but these were great!

I had the Cowboy Burger which was about the manliest thing I could think to order. I found it be really good and pretty messy, but that might have been the Kentucky Bourbon Ale. 

Finally I had the TN Bushwacker, which I honestly did not care for too much. The alcohol was a bit overpowering and since I had ordered it for a dessert, I was looking for something a bit sweeter. It wasn't that it was bad, but I do prefer my Bushwackers to be a bit sweeter. I suppose that is why they call it the "TN Bushwacker" but just a warning if you like them sweet like me.

I'd absolutely come back here.

My long awaited, highly anticipated dining experience at Catbird Seat somehow managed to handily exceed my lofty expectations. Arriving early we managed to snag bar seats at the equally impressive cocktail lounge attached to the restaurant - The Patterson House and commenced the evening with a pair of delicious craft cocktails and friendly banter with the barman. 

The whimsical dining experience at Catbird Seat starts the moment you exit the elevator and enter a somewhat disorienting glossy purple circus-like hallway that leads you into the combination kitchen/dining room. Approximately 20 comfortable bar seats surround the open kitchen and you are literally mere feet away from the talented chefs as they work their magic (there are also two booths for parties of four). 

This was one of my top ten dining experiences ever and at $140 per/person for a lengthy tasting menu with generous beverage pairings (two cocktails, a beer, four wines and sherry) was clearly the best bargain I have experienced in fine dining - well less than half the cost of some comparable meals. 

Not only was it so much fun watching your food being created but this was enhanced by the friendliness of all the chefs and the sommelier; they were so passionate about their work and appeared to take as much interest interacting with the customers as they did in preparing the food. Really genuine, wonderful people. The chefs themselves serve and explain all your courses and one server assists. While service is not as polished as your typical top tier venue, I will take this friendly, relaxed, open style of service over the pampered style more typical of fine dining any day.

What elevates Catbird Seat to a top dining experience is in addition to the ambiance and staff making the evening so special, enjoyable and memorable the food itself is phenomenal. Nearly every course impressed and left me scraping every last morsel and with a wonderful lingering aftertaste. Somehow nearly each and every course was consistently at such a high level with absolutely no duds or filler courses. Stars of the night included a buttery but not overly rich skate course accompanied by onions and rhubarb, the best tartare course I have ever consumed (aged beef with crispy ancient grains) and a riff on a yeasty potato soup paired with an equally yeasty craft beer. 

Often lengthy tasty menus have desserts that fail to live up to the impressiveness of the savories but the sweets at Catbird Seat were just as fantastic. The cuisine features high quality seasonal ingredients utilized extremely creatively so that every dish stands out. Some dishes push the envelope of what one may be comfortable consuming - i.e. stuffed shrimp heads grilled on a habachi grill where you suck out the filling, but everything tastes so amazing once you start eating. Pacing is perfect with refreshing small breaks between courses but no long gaps and portions were just right for leaving very satisfied but not uncomfortably full. For approximately three hours we were sittin' pretty in the Catbird Seat having the time of our lives and we already cannot wait to return. 

Thank you Catbird Seat for one of my best ever dining experiences!

If I could give this place less than 1 star, I would.

I bought the Groupon for this bakery after looking at their website which says they have vegan products. I am vegan, so clearly I would not have bought the groupon without knowing they could offer me something. Many gluten-free places serve vegan treats and vice versa, but apparently Haven on Earth didn't get the memo.

I do not live nearby and was excited to finally go and check the place out. I drove there yesterday afternoon to use my groupon. I was NOT greeted, even though there were about 4 people in the front prep area and absolutely no customers in the store. I waited for someone to assist me while I purused their breads, since no one came to talk to me or ask me if I needed help, I finally asked a petite girl what their vegan options were. She was very friendly and polite but wasn't sure how to help me and directed me to an older woman who I later found out was the owner.

I have never been treated so poorly from someone who has a business and a paying customer in front of them. She treated me like she was really bothered that I was vegan and as she turned her back to me she said there's the flax bread (which felt like a brick... hardly appetizing), and some sandwich bread in the back. She seemed taken aback that I had asked about vegan options and had no intention of helping me. When I kindly reminded her that her own website says they offer vegan options she said, maybe she could make me something special order, but I'd have to call it in.

I was already in the shop and felt that this was a proposterous thing to ask, so I insisted that she please take my special order now (need I remind you, there were NO other customers there). She finally agreed and basically stared at me and asked what I wanted. I asked for maybe a list of options that she could make vegan. She was no help whatsoever, so I finally pulled out of her that she could make vegan pizza dough and bagels. Great, I thought, now I can be on my way and out of this place... Haven on Earth? Give me a break!

She tells me to come back the next day and my order would be ready, so reluctantly I drove all the way across town again today to pick up my things, dreading coming into contact with this wretched woman and hoping at least they would be tasty. When I arrived she informed me that the guy making them screwed up, no apology. She said it wasn't good and to come back the next day. I am appalled by the extreme lack of service at this place, I don't understand why you wouldn't call a customer, knowing full well things were not ready. That would have been fine with me. She did mumble an insincere apology as I walked out the door.

So, I have yet to actually try any of the food because I'll have to go back again tomorrow. I'm hoping it'll be good, although no amount of deliciousness will make me EVER go back. 

(I also noticed that several of their items had cheese in them and were labeled "casein free", huge no no)

I don't see how this business will survive: horrible customer service from the OWNER, mislabeling items that can cause extreme physical reactions in people, and blatant misleading advertising of what kind of products they offer.

I will not be returning after I get my order corrected and I will steer everyone I know clear of this place. I don't typically complain, but this experience was truly awful. 

The only good thing about this business is a cute young girl, Melody who works the front, she was kind and polite even when her boss didn't want to be. 

UPDATE:

I went back again to get my stuff, this time I called to make sure they were ready.  The woman tried to get me to pay for 3 TIMES WHAT I ORDERED and then acted really offended when I said no, I only want what I ordered. Well, after 3 trips and half a tank of gas I have what I ordered, and I let her know that I would NOT be back. Just tried one of the bagels, I'm not enthused, but happy that this saga is OVER.

This place is quite a gem. We wanted someplace that was low key and no fuss on a Saturday night in New Orleans. El Gate Negro fit the bill perfectly. 

First, you get $1.09 off premium margaritas when you check in on Yelp. They have heir own private label tequila and some of the most unusually flavored options to chose from: beet (try it), blueberry, carrot, orange and lemon. So good. 

The menu has tons of great options. My husband got the chicken enchiladas with mole, which he really enjoyed. I got skirt steak tacos. Their tortillas are home made and quite yummy. They have three kinds: flour, corn and wheat (corn was my fave). 

We also had table side guacamole, which was great since I can't have chili's or tomatoes. Marisol added the perfect amount of lime and salt. 

Marisol was such a sweetheart. She was very familiar with the menu, promptly took our order and was just delightfully upbeat. 

I may be inclined to go back again tonight.

I don't often go to bars but when I do I go to 1864 tavern! Bartender was super nice and knowledgeable. He explained what was in the cocktails he prepared for me. That is important because they use fresh ingredients and good liquor. I can honestly say it has the best atmosphere for just sitting and relaxing while sipping a hand crafted cocktail.

This was a fun stop for an "adult on a working vacation" Friday night! Both the colleague I was in town to meet and the front desk staff at my hotel recommended Sparkman, and I'm a believer. For those of us from Miami, It's like a combination of Bayside, the Wharf and Lincoln Road. There's a turf lawn area with some hammocks, and puppy play area (every dog in Tampa seems to be a goldendoodle :), street performers and both sit down restaurants as well as food "containers".

Sparkman's is essentially the social hub of channelside Tampa. as it's near the hockey arena, the aquarium and the American Victory museum warship. During the month of October it hosts a haunted house event on weekend nights.

I enjoyed a lavender & courant ice cream from Jeni's, one of the popup shops after a sit-down dinner at Jotoro. I also sipped on a peach beer from the biergarten while enjoying the people watching, particularly the "pirate ghost street performer" scaring whoever passed by!

I spotted JoToro while walking around Sparkman Wharf, and since I'm a little bit "selective" between sit down and pop up restaurants, this was my Friday dinner spot. It's right at the entrance and has both inside and outside seating.

My chips and salsa - they charge for them unlike a lot  of other mexican places - had a decent crisp and the salsa had a nice bit of a kick. Both the classic mojito to start, and the dragonfruit "nightcap" were pretty decent on the taste but could have used a slightly more generous pour. Likewise on the chicken fundido burrito.  With adobo chicken, queso fundido, rice, beans, crema and chipotle hot sauce drizzle on a soft flour tortilla and garnished with radish and red onion I definitely expected more heat. Thankfully I was able to extend some of the salsa from the chips for more flavor.

Any place that can split my bill to have a separate printout without drinks for my office expense report definitely deserves some love! While staying in Tampa for work, I came here for dinner at the recommendation of my hotel's front desk manager, and had a good Taco Thursday at a real restaurant. For one, I was able to enjoy a couple of mojitos at an actual (albeit physically distanced) table. They had a very generous pour, perfect after a day of driving, site work and meetings. Yes, I ordered two!

It's located in the lobby of one of the new downtown Tampa buildings, and the decor is industrial sports bar, with lots of exposed concrete and TV's. They also have a few outside tables. The menu is a mix of sports bar staples - burgers and such - but I was in the mood for Tex Mex.

I started with their black beans & rice appetizer. This isn't the one Mima makes, since it tastes spicier and appears to be made with cajun rice, scallions & a sprinkle of red peppers. It was a great lead-in to my chicken burrito, which they customized with no guac (yes I'm a picky eater). Said burrito was loaded with a nice helping of chicken, black beans and the classic fixings. Sprinkle the lime it comes with and dip it in either the pico or salsa verde for an extra kick and you have a nice meal with whatever's on TV.

The amazing store front display of macaroon towers is what drew me in. 

The exquisite boxes of chocolates is what made me stay!

Sucre is a beautiful patisserie - they feature coffees, lemonades, cakes, chocolates, and gelato. 

I was with Kris (who hates chocolate!) so I decided to forgo a slice of chocolate cake (...still one of my biggest regrets to this day...) in order to share some gelato with him (amazing gelato though; perfect fruity flavors). 

I also bought a box of chocolate (8 piece) to bring home to my parents (and to sneak a few bites from!). The chocolates were wonderful and beautifully presented. They made a wonderful gift.

As a born-and-raised Philadelphian, I can confidently say that Lee's is a personal favorite of mine (and a gem in the University City neighborhood). The food here is amazing, and Scott and his team are even more so. Can't wait to come back. Love this City, and love my Lee's!

Prohibition quickly became my go-to neighborhood place shortly after moving in.  The kitchen here is exceptional.  The regular menu is pretty spectacular but the best food is on the ever-rotating list of specials that the kitchen turns out daily.  They are AMAZING.

The vibe is friendly and comfortable.  The list of beers on tap is impressive.  There are tons of bottles as well.  

Pretty much every meal I've had here has been great.  Come hungry and enjoy this neighborhood gem.  Oh, and Sundays are BYOV (bring your own vinyl) days....bring vinyl, they will play it on the turn table and offer you a discount.

My husband and I had a great time at Acme! We stopped in on a Sunday around noon on our long-weekend trip to Nashville. It was a beautiful day out and it was our last day before heading home, so we knew we had to stop here. Family told us to check out their roof top and I'm happy to report it did not disappoint! 

We started downstairs by ordering food. The place was packed and after standing in line to order, we posted up at the bar until we were able to snag a high top table right next to the stage. There was a fun jazz band playing and they were awesome! We had a great time.

My husband had a bloody Mary, but he wasn't much of a fan of their mix. I ordered a class of champagne because well, brunch time is a time to celebrate if you ask me. I enjoyed the Damn Good ($12) which was a bowl full of fried eggs, pulled pork, pinto beans & James brothers barbeque sauce. Yum! It was very good - highly suggest ordering this. Hubby had the Beautina Hash (also $12) which was two sunny side up eggs over slow-cooked brisket with
potatoes & caramelized onions. He said it was good, but liked mine better.

Since the sun was out and it was early enough in the day, we decided to make our way up to the roof top to enjoy some drinks. Most seats in the sun were taken, but after a few minutes I snagged us another two top table. The view from the rooftop overlooks the river which is pretty cool. Servers don't come around over there though, so you'll have to head to the bar which can take a minute. When we first got up there it wasn't too crowded, but it really picked up around 2:00 pm. They had tall boy beers on special for $4 though, so we stuck around for like three of those. I mean, how could you not? Cheap beer, table and chairs, beautiful weather, and a view? Yeah we'll stick around.

The biggest downfall of this place which is also probably a bonus is the sheer size of Acme. It's huge! The downstairs is for music, second floor was very quiet on a Sunday, and like I said, the roof top was poppin'. If you aren't in great shape I definitely suggest taking the elevator! That may sound silly, but although there's 3 floors, it's literally like 6 flights of stairs to get to the top. So brace yourself. The rooftop only has a single stall bathroom, so you'll have to head to the floor below if you don't want to wait in line.

Overall a really fun spot with great food and drinks. If I lived in Nashville I'm not sure I'd come here all the time, but if you're just visiting I suggest paying them a visit for sure!

NEW MENU ITEMS!!

Disclaimer: The online menu is outdated. 
FYI: All this was not consumed solely by little ole me.

Gumbo Sampler (replaced the Chili Sampler):
There were 3 different types of gumbo served with a small portion of rice in 4 ramekins. Taste-wise, I'm guessing it was Vegetable, Some Kind of Spice, & Seafood. But, I'd say to skip the sampler & go for a full bowl of the Seafood Gumbo! Yum!

Pulled Pork Flatbread:
Fresh house-made dough topped with pulled pork, apple, bacon, and Vermont cheddar cheese. Just the perfect combination of sweet & salty goodness balanced by the subtlety of cheddar. There are 3 different sauces (4 if you want to count ketchup) on the table for your dipping pleasure.

Roasted Duck Breast (replaced their Half Duck):
We went prepared to gorge ourselves in the tenderness that they call duck, but to our dismay, a breast replaced half of a duck! The price didn't change. Sigh. Even though there was a decrease in quantity the quality was superb! 


Bratwurst Burger:
We, actually maybe only one person, were still not satisfied, in terms of being full. So out came the menu to try my very first bratwurst! Oh so juicy & oh so good! The bread looked a kin to a croissant - fluffy, chewy, slightly buttery, & flaky all at the same time! Mmm...

Sides:
We got mashed potatoes with the duck & jalapeno cream of corn with the bratwurst. I was expecting a lot more of a jalapeno zing with the cream of corn, but it was pretty bland. Then again, the main dishes made up for blandness. Maybe the idea was to use the sides to clean the palette? 

Closing Remarks:
- I do have one suggestion. MUSHROOMS! I kept on thinking how each of these dishes would taste so good topped with mushrooms!
- I am officially on the search for a restaurant that serves a whole duck. Any suggestions?

I won't write a long review, detailing every dish I ate at the Catbird Seat. Instead I'll leave you with these photos from my visit: http://www.flickr.com/photos/revrev/sets/72157629128472734/

I will, however, answer the most common questions I've been asked upon showing anyone these photos:

1. How much was it? 
It's 100 bucks a person, plus beverage tastings, plus tax and tip. My fiance and I ended up spending 350 between us. 

2. Was it worth it?
Yes, every god damn penny. There is nothing I hate more than an overpriced meal, but there are few things in this world I would so readily pay for as a truly spectacular meal.

3. Were the beverage pairings good?
Non-conventional, for sure, but absolutely delicious. I discovered a whole lot of new drinks. I'm not a drink connoisseur by any stretch of the imagination, but I was really impressed.

4. Were you full?
Yes, very. It doesn't look like a lot of food on each plate, but after 10 courses and drinks I was extremely satisfied.

5. Would you go again?
If I could afford it, I'd go every damn night of the week.

This is such a cute, little coffee & tea shop! It's located just down the street from Belmont University. It's located behind a discount liquor store which I find humorous. I'd pick up something here before going to my 3-hour class. Oh, the memories!

This place has a retro-style feel that I totally dig. It's not a busy place.

I've had the coffee and the tea. The tea selection is pretty awesome. They only use loose leaf tea and brew it for you there. If you're in a super rush, then perhaps, you shouldn't go, 'cause they do allow it to steep properly before giving it to you. I had a Jazzberry Latte (Berry tea + Jasmine tea + Agave + Soy Milk). Warmed my belly up before a big test. They also have food (sandwiches, wraps, baked goods) with vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options. 

The staff is so kind and happy! They even have live music there on certain nights.

I had been craving a good old-fashioned burger, so I went to UPenn cafe...terrible. Here I am a few days later & I figured I'd try another neighborhood spot, so I went to Lee's - best decision of the week! I got a double cheeseburger that was so delicious & so classically good. Customer service is on point as well.

Mud House is definitely my favorite brunch place in St. Louis. Not only does it have cool Cherokee street vibes and great coffee, but also the food is amazing and never disappoints! The actual restaurant is more of a coffeeshop feel, wooden interior and seating, and you have to pay up front to order and seat yourself. It's a pretty casual, but cozy place. 

I've gotten a couple breakfast dishes here -- you can never go wrong with anything pretty much. My favorite dish is the Mud Slinger: roasted potatoes, vegetarian black bean chili, cheddar,  two sunny eggs on top, and a side of toast with homemade jam. It is the bomb.com. It's also unexpectedly a lot of food too, so pace yourself. 

Since Mud House is a coffeeshop as well, I would definitely recommend trying a latte or some type of coffee or even like matcha. Everything is great and looks amazing! 

Lastly, this place is popular so try to come early if you come for brunch on the weekend! There's ample seating, but it fills up pretty quickly.
