Please try Mud House if you haven't yet for brunch, it's pretty life-changing!

Santa Barbara's downtown west side nook is lucky to have Barbareño. This restaurant is creatively  designed and curated with a unique well thought out wine menu and let's not forget, really good food that changes with the seasons. 

I was bummed when Julienne closed but like a post break up love affair, Barbareño is easing the pain and warming up my heart again. 

First off let me say this because it's important. Everyone from the host to our server, and in between cares about the reputation of this restaurant. 

The staff cares, this is evident from the host's willingness to accommodate our seating ( on several occasions I came with a person  who is disabled and needed a special chair, also a last minute group seating at the bar) swiftly and without making us wait unnecessarily.

And the the servers help each other and do not ignore customers just because they aren't in their section. 

My last visit I ended up with Clay as my server. My first impression was that he was pretty young and I wasn't sure he'd know the wine. Not only was Clay totally on it, but he also gave me educated suggestions for wine pairings and even had couple of jokes to offer up. I am a bit of a snob with it so I'll admit- I was impressed. Well played, Clay, well played. 

Later I noticed some of the servers smelling and tasting wines which no doubt explains their savy advice . Bravo Barbareño for investing in your servers wine knowledge. Me likey :)

So I ordered the: 

*Meinkling Sparkling Rosé to start
*Grilled Avocado Appetizer 
*grilled Panzanella
*Oak Tagliatelle Pasta paired w/ a Mourvèdre/Syrah 

And for Desert

*Baked California 

So, everything delicious, unique, and innovative. The Grilled Avo has been a a go to pick, I gotta say- It has been to favorite of mine for a while.  I'm happy I tried the Grilled Panzanella as well this time for a fun wintery salad treat. This tangy grilled sourdough bread salad was drizzled with light and fragrant fennel dressing, rich, creamy and tangy drake farms goat cheese and thinly slivered red onions. 

Perfect starter for the oak-y aromatic acorn and wild mushroom tagliatelle. Not sure if the pasta is fresh but it did taste that way. The pasta is served bathed in a thin charred oak consommé with smoked vegetables and herbs. This dish was superbly tasty and full of umami and style. 

I will be back next time I'm in town to try what's  new and if nothing else, to sample more of their unique selection of natural and local wines (which normally I can only find in LA) 

Little fun observation : much of the design Inspo including the menu graphic and menu ingredients  ( including the seafood, acorn, wild mushrooms etc!) seem to be inspired by our very own Chumash Indians , the indigenous natives who lived here before us! If that ain't Local style, i don't know what is! 

Also, Barbareño seems to be striving for that Michelin star rating someday. Wouldn't that be special? Barbareño has the potential to get there!Let's hope we do, and add get to add a Michelin Star rated restaurant to Santa Barbara's restaurant repertoire! Good luck Barbareño on your very cool and well done restaurant.

NEVER in my life been so humiliated. A group of friends and i went here for a few drinks this past Saturday night. After standing at the bar for 5 mins waiting to get served - two guys walked up to one of the gals in our group and started giving her a hard time. I like this place a lot. The interiors are neat, the bar looks cool, and the constant anime (or daft punk videos) playing on the screen behind the sushi bar is awesome. Great place for a date if you don't mind the noise.

Drinks-wise, the sake mojitos are bangin. Remember to ask for a double.

As for the food, pretty much everything I've eaten here has been ridiculously tasty. My favorite by far is the duck two ways. Roasted duck breast cooked perfectly, accompanied by duck served in a bao bun? All about it. The sauce is great, too.

Their special sushi rolls are creative and delicious; I love the shiro-aoi - spicy white tuna and avocado topped with hamachi and jalapeño. Other menu standouts include the braised beef short rib over udon noodles (meat is unbelievably tender), and the lettuce wraps.

Definitely a good place to try if you're down with S. Starr and you like Asian fusion.

I'm Vietnamese so I definitely think I'm a good judge of Vietnamese food, and this place is awesome. I've gotten mostly everything on the menu and it's delicious and affordable. The beef wrapped in grape leaves is bangin, but I would absolutely recommend the dinner for 4 if you come in groups. The pho is below par, not surprisingly though because it's not a pho restaurant. The fish/beef stewed in the clay pot is awesome and a well liked dish by many friends who come to visit me in Philadelphia. 

Great place to start out your Vietnamese cuisine adventure. I'd recommend maybe something traditional like a Com tam suon dac biet-broken rice with marinated pork and egg. A good appetizer would be banh xeo, although better made at home, nam phuong does a great job representing the dish. I'd also order the chao tom -  sugar cane shrimp.

Just order everything. Vietnamese food is light, healthy and refreshing, unlike the other asian food.

Best steak I have ever had, such an awesome experience. I'm already a fan of Stephen Starr, so I came in with high expectations and was NOT disappointed.

I ordered the 20oz ribeye and it was like slicing through butter. Meaty, delicious, perfectly seasoned, medium-rare butter. Also, being offered a selection of steak knives (each with its own attributes and stories) was cool. The rest of the group had the NY strip, 3.5lb lobster, sides of mushrooms, potatoes, bacon, mac and cheese, the Kobe slider app. Everything was delicious and the red and white wine we had went well with the whole meal.

By far the best steakhouse in Philadelphia and I can't wait to go back. Oh, and if you're trying to impress a girl, bring her here.

Big thank you to Victor, Harry and Thi for this great dinner and opportunity to dine here.

It makes my heart sad to give such a cute local creamery only a 3/5. Especially since the service was friendly and the place was cute. But it makes my heart even more sad when my ice cream is icy instead of creamy. Also, while it's cool that they want to provide unique flavors, I feel like what I tried didn't quite have the punch of flavor and sweetness that I've come to expect from ice cream. Unfortunately, I've made creamier, more flavorful ice cream at home.

What a fantastic place to grab some food! My hubby and I joined our friends Mr. and Mrs. S there the other night and had a great time!!

We decided to do a late lunch/early dinner before our 5p tickets for Garden Glow. And at 3:30p on a Wednesday we found a parking space no problem and basically had the restaurant to ourselves! We were the only ones at a table, with just a person or two at the bar behind us. We were welcome to seat ourselves, so we picked a booth and got comfy. I had a perfect view of Space Balls, which was being projected against one of the walls!

We ordered some appetizers to start - Fried Pickles, Fried Deviled Eggs and Pork Poutine. The eggs were unique and delicious! The panko gave a nice crunch, the pickle and mustard on top gave a little zing and the tomato jam was the perfect amount of sweet! But I have to say that my absolute favorite was the Poutine! I'm a total sucker for waffles fries. I feel like they always have the right balance of crunch versus chewy inside. They were also nicely seasoned and covered with cheese and bacon. Need I say more?

My hubs and I shared the cheeseburger with a side salad. The burger was so juicy and moist that it fell apart more and more with every bite. But that didn't matter due to the great flavor!

I also got to try a bite of Mrs. S's Monte Cristo, a sandwich I've always wanted to try. She made a good choice - it was great!! I would definitely go back to get one of my own!

My husband and I were in the neighborhood and gave this place a try this past Friday! It's only $8.99 for the buffet, which is less expensive than all of the other Indian buffets I've been to in the city. But don't think that a lower price tag means bad quality! I was very pleased with everything that I tried and there were plenty of different choices! I felt like the quality of the food and the amount of options were comparable to the other more expensive buffets I've tried in the city. Why pay more??

My last visit to The Block was about 6 months ago - our server was awful and my husband wasn't in a good mood, so I left feeling very "eh". But I'm super glad that I went back tonight with my father and grandfather! I decided to jump in an try new things! The two other times I've been, I got the pulled pork sandwich and a side of the potato and bacon hash - which is absolutely incredible! But I didn't want to get caught in that rut where I order the same thing every time. So my dad helped me switch things up! He ordered The Three Pigs sandwich and I ordered their special sandwich for the evening - beef brisket with Swiss. And we didn't swap out the side, we went with the fries and pickled veggies. And let me tell you, these fries are spectacular! They're thin cut (think McDonald's size), perfect amount of crunch and perfectly seasoned! As for those veggies - I usually don't care for pickled things, but with these I could really appreciate their fresh taste. I believe they made them and they haven't been sitting in a jar of chemicals on the shelf for the past three years. 

The brisket sandwich was enormous! - think long sub sandwich. Now, this sandwich was very nicely seasoned and very yummy and I would recommend it to everyone. However, The Three Pigs, was out of this world and puts every other dish to shame! The meat on it's own was so freakin' flavorful! I don't even remember what cheese was on top because it didn't matter! I'm glad that this is one their menu all the time - I can return and have it again soon! 

(Then there's dessert. I will warn you, their desserts run a little small, which makes me sad.) Their chocolate ice cream with candied bacon is simply out of this world! But, like I said, I was determined to try new things! So dad and I shared two scoops of ice cream (cinnamon and coconut brown sugar) and the Chocolate Malt  Pudding. Ice had the cinnamon ice cream in the past and have always loved it, but I have to say that the rest of the dessert put it to shame! The coconut brown sugar tasted less like coconut and more like the most amazingly delicious brown sugar ever! Both dishes came with a gingerbread cookie which was surprisingly sub-par comparatively - too cakey and not very gingery. But the pudding also came with two toasted marshmallows! The pudding was very smooth and almost had the consistency of a thickened caramel sauce. It was super sweet and you get a pretty decent portion so I was very happy! Fingers crossed that at least one of these desserts are still on the menu!next time I visit!

Great find! Went for 1st time during Philly Beer Week. 11 IPAs on tap; flights of 4 for $10, hell yeah!Had one of the best beers @ PBW; Free Will Mango Habenero  Imperial IPA- unbelievable.

The atmosphere was mellow, open,airy and welcoming.  Excellent service.Great bar tenders who really know their shit when it comes to beers & cocktails.

Did not try or see any food (The amazing Sky Cafe, 3 blocks away was our next stop), but the menu looked interesting.

Another great pub I will definitely be returning to.

I've been here a couple of times and I've enjoyed most of my cupcakes. The only one that I didn't like was the peanut butter cupcake. Btw guys, buying cupcakes for ur girlfriend is a good way to demonstrate ur sorry. It worked on me. ;)

Once again, I have someone telling me I "haveta" try the Foie Gras burger at Two Stones pub.

When these statements are made to me, I try not to judge. If they consider Applebee's Jalapeño poppers life changing, I usually smile and go about my business. But when someone says Foie Gras and Truffles to me in the same sentence? Somethings cooking. (See what I did there?)

Waking in, I'm greeted by the hostess. I'm told there is bar seating but theres a wait for a table. The bar it is.

A cheerful bartender greets me and gives me a few menus. I told her I drink Allagash beer at home, I see a grapefruit summer beer that looks interesting. She comes back with two tasting glasses. The IPA grapefruit beer had too much going on. How the hell do you pair an IPA with food?? I'll stick with my summer Allagash thankyouverymuch.

I place the order for the burger. I'm told it comes with chips but for an upcharge, the truffle fries are really good. Take my money and truffle me!!

The burger comes to me quickly. It's a nice brioche bun topped with fig jam and Arugula. The patty, is a little thinner than what I expected but has very nice meat blend. And there it is, a nice size piece of Foie Gras. It's a piece of heaven on a plate. What's throwing it all off? Why are there bacon strips on a burger of this caliber? It's like seeing lipstick on a pig, it doesn't belong. I took off the strips and moved them to the side. First bite? Man, that is a well designed handheld burger. 
And the truffle fries with the aioli dip?? This gastropub would be typically seen in Williamsburg Brooklyn than Wilmington. Great job everyone, fantastic burger.

There's a guy sitting at the end of the bar, he orders the bread pudding. I guess he got the same advice to swing by for some good food. 

I totally agree.

Another spot in Wilmington, great beers but the burger was a suck fest.

I'm just passing thru town, I was looking for a good spot for a burger and a beer. Beer, yes they have great beer offerings. I see there's Allagash White which is something I drink. I asked for similar Pilsner which was very good. 

While I'm waiting for my food, this is the second time I witnessed this at a bar in Wilmington. The bar has music playing, there's a customer whistling to a song? Brah, you realize you're in a public setting? No one needs to hear you whistle "Roundabout" while tippin' one back.

The burger, what the hell? What brought me here was The Smashburger. What was served to me was two patties that weren't smashed with cooked onions on  a bun with some wack ass cheese.

Chef, do you understand the concept of smashed? The patty is flattened over onions which makes the ends crispy. These patties weren't even pressed on, epic fail. 

Just passing thru, I'll never return.

My son & I enjoy making Tiki drinks at home. This little bar in New Orleans is the "mecca" for all tiki and cocktail mixologists. 

Jeff Berry is the author of some famous cocktail books. He dug up a treasure trove of vintage Tiki drink recipes, as far back as the 1930s and up to the swinging 1960s. All these famous cocktails like the Mai Tai, Zombie and Navy Grog are all being served at Beachbum Berry's Latitude 29.

My wife and I are walking and looking for the address. She said, where's the sign? Beachbum Berry's is too hip to deal with a silly sign! haha

Once inside, its Tiki heaven. Remember when the Brady's vacationed in Hawaii and found that tiki doll? The Tiki dolls here are giving good vibes. Sit back, drink a few funky cocktails and catch a buzz. Are you feelin' me Yelper?!

My wife & I are seated at a table near the window. The Beachbum Berry's menu is a nod to fun finger food. We started with the Pork Ribs and Shanghai Lumpia. The ribs are plentiful, just plumpy meaty goodness with a savory and sweet finish. The Shanghai Lumpia, a Filipino-style egg roll I can best described as a Mexican Flautas. The eggroll shape is long and skinny unlike a typical Chinese egg roll. The  Lumpia are stuffed with pork, shrimp and glass noodles, the egg rolls are like potato chips! You can't put them down, sooo good!

Let's talk about the Beachbum Berry cocktails. I'm here on vacation and will not be returning anytime soon so I want to pace myself with these cocktails. Also, there's no happy hour prices, each cocktail is $15 on average. 

I first ordered two Mai Tais. My wife's first impression: I thought a Mai Tai was sweet? If you're used to a sweet Mai Tai, the bartender is making them for the customer. More juices and weak alcohols are typically a Mai Tai being at Applebees. Beachbum Berry's is making a Trader Vic's 1944 classic using Aged Martinique and Jamaican rums, Curaçao, lime, and a kiss of almond. Mind numbing good.

My next cocktail, the menu said it was Frank Sinatra's favorite. Well call me ol blue eyes, the Navy Grog Tiki drink is off the chain! A funky blend of Jamaican and Demerara rums, throw in a touch of allspice, lime and grapefruit? Look at my picture, even the ice is kra-kra! I had to buy the ice mold for my son, he went wild making tiki cocktails.

I also wanted to by an autographed cocktail book by Jeff Berry but our waiter said they were ruined by the storm. Bummer..

My wife contacted Jeff about this issue and Beachbum Berry's Latitude 29 sent an autographed postcard to my home with a cocktail recipe??

That is just awesome, thank you Beachbum Berry's Latitude 29!

I had the "Trifecta" my first morning in New Orleans:

A cup of Cafe Du Monde coffee
A bag of Beignets
Live Jazz playing right next to me

Did I just describe my heaven? Listen, you can talk to me about Nashville all day, New Orleans for the win!

Cafe Du Monte is a continuous flow of energy. People enjoying themselves, happy jazz playing in the streets and the smells of Beignets, It's a shock to all of your senses. 

My wife and I place our order and grab a table close to the street. We're sitting and covered from the sun but the sides are completely open. There's a small cool breeze, just a beautiful October morning. I have a hot coffee, my wife has an iced coffee. Both are the Cafe Du Monte blend, another unique flavor. You're not getting this at Starbucks, are you feelin' me yelper?? 

The hot beignets, my wife said every 5 minutes: it tastes like Zeppoles! Let me make this clear, a beignet does not in no way shape or form taste like the Italian treat. As a kid, I would watch my grandmother spoon the Zeppoles batter in hot oil. They both have powdered sugar but that is where the similarities end. A beignet is allowed to rise using Yeast. Zeppoles uses ricotta cheese in the mix. So the pillowy, slightly crunchy fried exterior of a beignet is what gets you addicted. You want to keep coming back for more.

Cafe Du Monte, it was a pleasure to sit at your table, listen to jazz while sippin' your  Java blend. 

Keep rockin' !

This was a nice Cracker Barrel, I have to give it five Yelp Stars. 

We were staying at the Opryland hotel, do you know what its like to pay $17 for eggs? Mamma didn't raise no dummy! We're all at a convention and our body clock is on EST. If it 6am their time, it's 7am our time. We'd meet at 6am in the lobby and walk to Cracker Barrel. We were shown to a large table, the wait staff was very nice and accomodating. After day two, they'd bring extra biscuits and apple butter to our table, just an enjoyable time while staying in Nashville for the week.

There are Cracker Barrel Old Country Stores across the United States. This particular store made us feel welcome and we enjoyed our daily breakfast here.

This was some venue, wow! 

There were so many different levels to this place, there were even people on the roof top! The rooftop has a commanding view of the city, very cool.

Wanna know who's cool? The bartenders! Man, we all went down to the second floor to get drinks and I see Jack Daniel's Sinatra Select on the shelf. I said to him, I never had that before, is it crazy good? The bartender says, this is from last nights party and he gave me a free round?! I'm not a big Jack Daniel's guy but man oh man was that smooth. 

Acme Feed & Seed, great venue for music and drinks. The food looked amazing, we didn't get to try. 

Next time!

All the cooking shows, all the articles on Nashville Hot Chicken had me whipped into cluckin' frenzy!

When KFC has Nashville Hot Chicken on their menu? It's a hot ticket item. I had a conference scheduled in Nashville this year? The second the speaker said: any questions? I was hailing an Uber to the restaurant. 

Pulling up to the restaurant, it's nothing fancy. Steps going up to small ordering area. Once you place your order, have a seat on the front porch. They'll bring it to your seat. I ordered a beer and a medium spiced two piece. For sides, I ordered beans and slaw. 

The food comes to me, it's a lot of chicken! I take pictures (Hey, I'm Bill S)

I take a bite

The warm chicken juices are running down my face.  Each bite is blissful, I ordered correctly. There's no need to have burning spicy chicken, I enjoyed the medium heat thankyouverymuch. 

The sides were also pretty Kickin'. The crew that came with me were also loving the Hattie B's Chicken blend.

Where I get lost is the atmosphere and the actual chicken. I mean, the chicken was good! I came, I saw, and baby I conquered some righteous bird heat. Best I ever had, 5 stars?? I mean, it's no Cronut so my best assessment is 4 stars.

Keep Rockin' Hattie B!

Staying in a hotel not too far from the Farmer & the Cow, I was looking for a
nice spot to have a burger. 

Reading about the Farmer & the Cow, I see Diners, Drive and Dives did a stop here?! It seems they're known for burgers and boozy milk shakes. Boozy milk shakes at a proper whiskey bar? It's juvenile to me! I wanna drink Scotch all night long (hey, that's a song!), the last thing I want to do is drink a milkshake*.

While walking to the Farmer (don't forget the Cow) I was sidetracked by huge beer vats. I stopped and had a burger and a beer at the other spot. The beer, well, Merica. But the burger was a waste of time. I start talking to some of the patrons and they're telling those boozy milkshakes are insane. Really? So convincing that I paid the check and RAN out of that stupid place!

Walking inside, it's a serious bar. Dark, with wood floors and a long bar. I'm seeing a great bunch of whiskey choices. A guy greets me at the door, can I help you? I see a bunch of guys sitting at the bar drinking whiskey. I say in a low voice.. I'm here for a boozy milkshake.
What?
I say in a low voice, milkshake.
Huh?

MILKSHAKE! I WANT A MILKSHAKE!
(That didn't happen)

I say, I just ate a burger a few blocks away but I'd like to try one of your famous milkshake please. 
Yes sir, right this way.

Lots of milkshake choices but I'm seeing little something with peanut butter. And bacon. Now add bacon-infused Redemption Bourbon?? It's called PAUL RUDD. Wait, the guy from Ant Man has a drink?? ok.. well, yes please and thank you.

The milkshake comes to the table quickly. There is a nice, thick strip of bacon on top. Man... I dove into that sucka like nobody's business! The swirl of the peanut butter and the Redemption Bourbon is making one mighty fine tasty beverage. I took the bacon strip and started dipping it in the milkshake.  Bourbon, Cream, Peanut butter and bacon. At this point, Paul Rudd is party animal!

I paid the check after I finished my shake and walked back to the hotel. Just passing thru Mr Farmer, you totally rocked that milkshake!

"Whiz with fried onions"

Listen, I'm from New York. I don't know who has the best Philly Cheesesteak, It's not my place to comment. I do know I'm just passin' thru and my buddy told me forget those tourist trap spots and go to Dalessandro's.

I mask up and walk up to the window to place my order:
One with Whiz and Fried Onions
The counterperson and sees my wife next to me and says only one?
(I'm seeing these sandwiches and they're huge?!)
Yes, one please

Now we all stand around and wait to hear our name. Once your name is called, now you have to wait on the payment line. They roll up a window, you hand them cash (no plastic accepted) and they give you this huge sandwich.

I walk to my car and we split this work of art. Trust me, this is a hot, juicy sandwich. You're going to get it on your shirt. And if you're thinking about eating while driving? Surely you jest..

We open the package and take a bite. The roll is fresh and the quality of the meat shines in this hero. (Hogie? Grinder? Sub? Anything outside of NY sounds dopey) The whiz and fried onions give this handheld a nice rounded flavor. Total fan at this point.

So I ate at Dalessandro's and not my beloved Brooklyn. If you're passing thru, I highly recommend Dalessandro's over those punk ass tourist traps.

Listen, I'm from New York. I'm am so trying gator!! haha

I'm in town for a convention, our hotel is walking distance to Caney Fork River Valley Grille. I threw my suitcase in the room, grabbed my buddies and headed to Alligator Heaven.

This is a popular restaurant, there's a small wait on a Tuesday night. While we wait for our table, we head over to the bar. I'm in town and there is some Tennessee whiskey to be poured. We're all excited, we want to experience the bounty of Nashville. We all have a nice pour, love Nashville!

We're all brought to our table, I feel like I'm eating in a bass pro shop! Water falls, animal heads, wood walls, very rustic. 

I ordered my gator starter. The menu is scalable so I was able to order one catfish filet with two sides.

The gator? Tastes like chicken! I can tell the reptile fat is different from red blooded animal fat. The reptile fat is gamier. Hey, I came, I saw and I conquered. I will say I woke myself up from gator gas..

Catfish? Spot on, cooked perfectly. Along with fried okra and hush puppies, this was a dish I can see myself getting weekly.

Some down home cooking being served at Caney Fork River Valley Grille. If your staying in a hotel close to the restaurant, you should be here every night!

Marc Vetri, a Philly chef who was trained in Bergamo, Italy. Our worlds will never cross unless he opens a restaurant in NYCs Meat Packing district. I've been reading about his accomplishments over the years, James Beard Award winner and pasta magician. When I was passing thru Philly, I was now a man on a mission.

Walking into Pizzeria Vetri, I have the place to myself. I've been reading on Yelp that I have to try the Rotolo. It sounds simple, Pizza dough rolled up with mortadella, ricotta and topped with pistachio pesto.

I want to try the pizza, I ordered the Crudo pizza. Topped with yummy prosciutto and bufala mozzarella, this sounds like a some brotherly love happening at Pizzeria Vetri.

My Rotolo comes first. Man.. this is krazy good. I thought this would be like every New York pizza roll but this is something that's chef'd up. Totally took me by surprise. This is a must order item when you come to Pizzeria Vetri.

The Crudo pizza almost had me knock off a star. The taste was amazing! My only issue? The mozzarella had some cold spots. I asked the waitress if I could have the pizza reheated, she said there are board of heath issues, yada yada yada. Guess what? The salty prosciutto had me coming back for more, this was a damn fine pizza.

I came, I saw and I conquered Pizzeria Vetri. What an amazing restaurant, if you never had Marc Vetris food, you should swing by to appreciate his simple everyday Italian creations.

This is the fanciest and one of the best Mexican restaurants I've ever been to.  You first think, a small shopping center restaurant?  But when you enter, you are greeted by beautiful pink and coral walls adorned with nice paintings, fresh roses (again, pink and coral) at every table and surrounded by great music.  

Our waitress was very nice and let us try samples of three different drinks since we couldn't decide.  One one was better than the next but I went with the Horchatta.  It was soo good!  I usually just order water and was spoiled!  

Their guacamole was really really good as well.  (I'm a huge fan of La Esperanza in Lindenwold, NJ).  It rivaled them, (and no extra salt required) which I hate to say!  I wasn't crazy about their thicker homemade chips but they were decent.  The portion was less than I'm used to but with all of our other food, lunch perfect size actually.  

My main entree though?  Forget it!  Sooo good and fresh with ample shrimp.  It was a shrimp burrito - generous lunch size and I ate the whole thing :)  

I've already told three people about this restaurant.  It's only 10 minutes from my house - this could be a dangerous new relationship!  

I highly recommend going!

My first time to Peddler's Village!  I felt like a kid looking at all of the ornate light displays!  Sooo beautiful and got me more into the festive spirit of the holidays for sure.

I only bought a small gift for my mom (all other Christmas shoping is DONE :) but there are so many specialty shops that you could probably find something for everyone on your list.  Even the hard to buy for!  

Hot cider was being served as well as soft pretzels (not free).  

It is a magical type of setting that you hate to leave!

I'm looking forward to going back one day!

To be fair, I hesitated between one and two stars. But when you're running on concept, the concept needs to work. It doesn't. 

My friend, N, and I went after a concert at the Symphony Hall. It wasn't crowded, but when we walked in, we were told only the Sixth Floor was open. The sign says the First Floor is 24 hours, so that seemed odd, especially given that there were folks dining all around. There was a lovely dessert case full of goodies greeting us at the door. More on this later.

We go up to the Sixth Floor, and there are no tables, only bar seating. Meh, not comfortable, but not a deal-breakers. The chairs are crammed in so tightly, you are literally rubbing hips with strangers. About every fourth chair at that bar needs to come out. The TVs were way too loud. Music would have been much nicer, instead we would be dining to the very boisterous sound of the local newscast of a couple of shootings and people dying in hurricane Florence. 

To start, our server asked for drink orders and we got Diet Cokes, which were cloyingly sweet and nearly flat. When we told the server, she more or less shrugged and said, "Yeah we get that a lot. It just comes out like that." 

Hang on. What?  Anyway, we opted for water.

The Sixth Floor brags of its seafood, and there was a gentleman shucking oysters in front of us. But the prices are insanely high (the 5-piece shrimp cocktail is $18... half a dozen garlic-parmesan oysters are $20... that's nuts, anywhere). We passed. Also: not really much menu choice.  Shrimp, crab legs, fish tacos, oysters and six sushi rolls-- no sashimi at all.

We ordered chips & salsa/guac/queso ($12-- yeah) and they arrived promptly. The chips were oversalted, the salsa had no flavor but tomato, the queso was acceptable, and the guacamole was neither fresh nor homemade, it had that telltale consistency of guacamole from a plastic bag. Plus, it was brown when we dipped down deeper than the top layer of the scoop in the cup. Yuck. Serving size was adequate, but not for the price.

Entrées also came out fast, before we'd really made a big dent in the appetizer. I had fish tacos ($14, which is actually reasonable). The menu description reads: "Flour Tortillas filled with Mahi Mahi, Cilantro Lime Cream, Napa Cabbage, Black Bean Corn Salsa." The description was only misleading in one way: the napa promised was subbed with garden-variety red cabbage. No big deal. The fish was sliced into these really strange solid square log shapes (imagine a stick of butter made out of fish), but was cooked properly. The portion size was acceptable. But the whole affair just lacked flavor. The cilantro-lime cream lacked discernible traces of either, and came off like a thinnish sour cream. The black bean and corn salsa was sparse and dull. The fries accompanying the tacos were quite greasy, but crispy and tasty. No dipping sauce (ketchup or otherwise) was offered, but I'm sure I could have gotten some if I'd asked. I just smeared them in the remaining queso.

N ordered Philly roll sushi ($10) and it was eight smallish pieces. She didn't complain or rave, it was okay. The ginger garnish looked a little ragged. 

After dinner, we asked about desserts, figuring we'd get a rundown of the list of available lovelies in the front case. Nope. Two. Two desserts, both of which were variations on cheesecake: one a brownie caramel affair, the other topped with raspberry purée. 

I decided the experience had adequately tanked and so figuring I had nothing to lose, I asked about what was in the case downstairs, and was told flatly that they weren't available on the sixth floor.

Hang on. What?  What?

The Diner works entirely out of central kitchen, and by virtue of its concept, there is a bank of elevators working overtime. What's available on one floor should be available on any of them. That last unpleasant discovery about rationing of deserts to those who were seated on the First Floor that was closed (the waitress told us the hostess who sent us up to the Sixth Floor was a straight-up liar and that the First Floor never closed). 

I did want a sweet, so we had the caramel-brownie cheesecake. It was food-service mass-produced frozen cheesecake dolled up with a brownie crumble and caramel drizzle. The portion was slim, particularly given that it was $8. There was also ketchup on the edge of my dessert plate.

I keep referring to the prices, which, I do understand will be more downtown. They prices aren't objectionable if I'm getting a fine dining or even upscale casual experience, or a casual dining experience with bigger portions. None of that was the case. What we have here, folks, is a tourist trap catering to people who either don't know any better or won't ever be back anyway. They're not trying for repeat business.


---FINAL THOUGHTS---
Atmosphere: loud, cold, cramped

Service: adequately attentive and polite, but completely unconcerned about our experience

Food: Lacking in quality, flavor, presentation and value.

Darling little place!  I took my Polish papa to have a late lunch at the Polish Cottage today. My dad had been several times and it met his "Polish food should taste like this" expectations.  We were greeted and seated immediately.  We scanned the menu and decided right away what we were in the mood for.  I am always in the mood for pierogies!  Loved how I could mix and match and took full advantage of that.  I tried all of them and am prepared with my order for next time.  I liked them all but LOVED the potato and cheese.  Next time I am going to have four potato and cheese, one beef and one sweet farmer's cheese.  My dad ordered the stuffed cabbage and was one happy Polish Prince, as he used to be known in NY.  It was a nice portion of food but no to-go box was required for him as he ate every last bite!  I am so very pleased that T-town now has two great Polish restaurants to have my pierogi fix.

One of my new favorite treats is boba tea!  I have been visiting Chatime for a few months now and it remains consistently good! I am obsessed with the red bean pearl milk tea and would be writing this review on that alone, if not for my son. E is the adventurous one when it comes to trying the various boba teas and smoothies.  He has not found one that he doesn't enjoy. Currently, they have a pumpkin spice tea and he's had that several times. A nice feature is you can adjust the sugar level and my go-to is 80%.  The customer service is good. There is an offer of 10% off if you check in on Yelp. Funny side note: I ordered two drinks last time and used my offer and only got 10% off one of my drinks... Sort of thought my order would include both drinks. Be sure to get the stamp card... I have been so many times that I have already earned a free drink! Woohoo!! All in all, Chatime is a great place for T-towners to stop for a yummy drink!

We were shopping next door and found ourselves staying longer than expected. By the time we left Ocean World had just opened for lunch so we decided to give it a shot based on Yelp reviews. The restaurant has a large interior to our surprise with seating to accommodate one to several large parties. The sushi bar seats 8 if you prefer watching the chefs in action. They also have a very nice deck area, if weather permits, or if they have a server working the deck. We tried to take advantage of the beautiful fall day and sit on the deck but were told it wasn't open.

Our server was friendly and didn't rush us since it was our first time. However, once it became busy the service was slower as one would expect.  We were unsure if this was typical lunch service or just allowing us time to make our decision.  The lunch crowd appeared to consist of many regulars since the servers greeted several around us by name. By 1:00 pm the restaurant was packed with groups of 1-10. The lunch menu was much larger than expected and prices were reasonable. The lunch selection was a pleasant surprise of appetizers, 15 types of rolls, 4 lunch boxes ranging from $9 - $12, 2 salads, pastas and noodle dishes to full entrees. If you're allergic to fish there are a couple options but many of the items are prepared or served in fish broth. The two salads options were very popular which were 1) Seafood with calamari & 2) Shrimp or Sashimi with fresh slices of tuna, salmon, white fish and shrimp are served on a bed of lettuce.  The lunch box portions are deceiving unless you're a big eater with 4 options from California Roll and Tempura or Teriyaki ($8.95) to options of Sushi, Sashimi or Tempura with Shrimp, Chicken or Beef Teriyaki ($11.95) each served with miso soup, rice and salad. A Veggie Tempura is available as well. 

The Wasabi Shumai ($4.95) is 6 steamed dumplings flavored with Wasabi broth. They were delicious and a big hit especially if you enjoy Wasabi. The Wasabi flavor doesn't overpower the dish or make it too hot since the broth diluted the full strength of the Wasabi. The rolls are quite large and can easily be shared for a lighter lunch. The Crazy California Roll ($12.95) was fresh and enjoyable with a mixture of spicy avocado, crab, chopped onions topped with broiled shrimp, scallops and squid then topped with hot and spicy sauce. The roll is lightly broiled giving the roll warmth and a crunchy topping while the flavors blend nicely with the three different layers of flavors. It even reheats well since I had to take half home.

If you're not a sushi fan several fish entrees are available from Tilapia, Volcano Shrimp, Grilled Salmon, or Catfish served with a salad and choice of red potatoes, rice or French fries. Pasta was on the lunch wish list and we weren't disappointed. Several types of pasta and noodles are available with Ocean or Cajun Spaghetti, Tempura Udon, Nabe Yakima Udon or Soba. The Chandon (spicy) with stir fried seafood, pork and veggies prepared in a pork broth was enjoyed and I was told a perfect option for lunch. While the Sara Udon (seafood) with veggies served on a plate of deep fried oriental noodles received a thumbs up as well.

Everything was fresh, tasty, and affordable and we look forward to returning to try more lunch dishes.

This was my first visit to the new LaTea Bubble Tea Lounge on Mass Ave in the Penrose On Mass building next door to Condado. LaTea has two floors of seating and lots of natural light with clean modern lines. Comfy sofa and chairs are on both floors with counter seating overlooking Mass Ave on the main level. The loft is quiet and an excellent work space. Lots of outlets on both floors for charging.

Helpful instructions on how to order are above the counter with 5 easy steps. The customer service is exceptional and feels personalized for each customer. When they assist you, your personal likes and dislikes are seriously taken into consideration when they help make recommendations.

The sweet lady behind the counter was very informative and helpful. LaTea uses all natural or organic ingredients and the  soft, chewy boba has a hint of honey which is house made from the owner's family recipe. I've never had fresh,  homemade boba and the sample was incredible and so much better than I've ever had before.

I strayed from my normal teas and coffees and went with the large Nitro Infused Taiwan Oolong with a quarter sweet passion fruit. I thought the sample was a bit tart so she recommended adding passion fruit. Afterwards, I didn't really care for the passion fruit flavor mixed with the Oolong tea. Don't get me wrong, not bad but it was just the dominant flavor. Next time I'll select a different drink and sweetener. The large drink had a generous amount of sweet boba and certainly more than I've ever received in a drink. The large straw allowed me to get every boba plus I love the spill proof lids.

As I was having my cold boba tea the cashier brought me a delicious sample she thought I'd like after we spoke. How thoughtful is that?? It was a hot, milk tea coffee with a black tea base. I really enjoyed this flavorful milk tea and it'll probably be my next order. 

LaTea offers desserts but I stayed focused on my drink order and forgot to try. Next time I hope to try the lemon tart. A rewards program is offered so ask about it when you're in. I totally spaced that as well. I love the space, the phenomenal service, the amazing selections and options with add-on flavors. Stop by! You won't be disappointed.

After sampling the Dirty Morning taco at a Yelp event I knew I needed to sample more of Condado tacos and I wasn't disappointed!! The location is easy to find with lots of metered street parking. I arrived at 12:30 and was prepared for a long lunch wait. Instead I was pleasantly surprised and seated immediately at a table.

The interior is casual and comfortable with bright, fun graffiti on the walls and a fun atmosphere. Seating is a  mixture of tall-top tables and regular tables. The bar area is to the back of the restaurant and was quite busy when I was here.

Condado has oodles of liquor options and I don't think you'll be disappointed regardless of what you drink. There are several Specialty Cocktails (Cuba Libre, Anejo Manhattan, Sparkling Tequila Mash), many brands of tequila and whiskey's sorted by standard, premium and ultra premium brands. You'll also find Rums, Mezcal, Cerveza, PBR, Miller High Life, Bud Light (draft) and Rhinegeist Bubbles (draft) with Hangover Cures,  Tequila-Mosa, Michelada, and Bloody Mary/Maria with Vodka or Blanco Tequila and of course, Margaritas. Something for most I would think.

At first the menu appeared confusing until I looked closer. You'll find 3 menus/order forms on the table with an appetizer menu, a regular taco order form ($3-$5) with ingredients listed and then one order form where you build your own tacos the way you want them from shell or bowl to the finishing sauces. Prices for build your own tacos begin at $3.50 each with some upcharges listed beside the item. Just write your name on top of the order form, write in quantity beside the taco you want or start building your own tacos. Naco's are available for $7 and sides are listed at the bottom of the order form with prices.

My server was friendly,  prompt and attentive. He explained the ordering process and grabbed my beverage. After reading a few of the reviews I was afraid service was going to be super slow.  Because of I ordered an appetizer of chips and salsa which arrived super fast. I turned in my order to my server and my food arrived in less than 5 minutes. Faster than fast food restaurants!! The chips were good and I enjoyed the generous serving of the  hotter salsa. Most of the chips were taken home with me along with one of my tacos. 

I ordered one Lucy's Fire Taco which has a firecracker shell, a fiery flavored hard shell, roasted chicken with lettuce, cilantro, onions, smoked cheddar, corn salsa & cilantro-lime aioli. I loved the mixture of corn, chicken, cilantro and smoked cheddar flavors. My second taco was the Dirty Morning Taco which brought me in. I enjoyed this breakfast taco with a soft, flour tortilla filled with queso blanco, rice, black beans, scrambled eggs, cilantro, onions and their amazing dirty sauce. I love the fresh ingredients, the queso with the mixture of veggies and especially the dirty sauce flavor. If you enjoy some heat I highly recommend the dirty sauce. 

I could only eat one of the tacos but luckily the taco and chips reheated well. I will be back again to sample more of these delicious tacos.

Sugarfire Smoke House is located between Rock Bottom and Conrad's on West Washington Street. Sugarfire is a Saint Louis based chain with eleven restaurants all independently owned and operated. This is the first Sugarfire in the state of Indiana. I was excited to visit tonight after always wanting to visit Sugarfire when visiting family in St. Louis. 

The relaxed and easy going atmosphere borders on rustic charm with a bit of trendiness. The decor is black and white tiles on the walls, rough cut pine on the counter, 4 & 6-top wooden tables and fun decor throughout. Check out the large bull above the condiment station and Yoda by the cashier. The back dining area has 4-top dining tables with colorful red chairs. The room has an amusing decor with huge, neon advertising signs. Love the Mobile sign! Upstairs has larger tables (8-10 top) for larger groups. The wide variety of music playing tonight was fantastic! and easy to talk over. Keep that up!!

Now, for first timers, as soon as you step into the entrance immediately turn left through the door to enter the order line. The other door takes you straight into the dining room for Express Service Pickup or picking up your Tailgating Packages. The large menu is a little overwhelming on the blackboard wall with the different combinations. Some items are served with 1, 2 or no sides. Some are just a sandwich where others are 2, 3 or more meats with sides and drinks. The daily specials and daily sides are listed on the butcher paper. Some of the options are Pulled Pork, Brisket, Ribs, Turkey, Smoked Salmon, Sausages, Smoked Portobellos, Brisket Cheesesteaks, Fried Pork Tenderloin, Hamburgers and 3 Salads. Something for most everyone! The combo dinners provide an opportunity to sample several different meats. There is a 3 meat combo with 2 sides and a drink, Combo Plate with 2 meats, 2 sides and drink or the Meat Daddy (for serious carnivores only) with Ribs, Sausage, 4 ozs each of Brisket, Pulled Pork and Smoked Turkey with 2 sides and a drink.

The gentleman behind the counter was very helpful while we were making that difficult decision. Place your order, then work your way down the cafteria rail to the cashier. He'll hand you a drink cup to fill in the hallway between the dining rooms. The condiment station offers pickles, jalapenos, onions, bread and honey butter. The soda is Sugarfire house brands. No Pepsi or Coke products here. 3 Cola products (1 Cherry Cola) with one sugar free, 1891 Citrus Soda, Frostie, Excel Cream, or Lemonade. Domestic craft beers, wine, milk shakes and floats are also available. 

The Pie Shake is an entire slice of pie blended with any flavor of milkshake. The milkshakes come in chocolate, vanilla or strawberry. The Floats flavors are Root Beer, Purple Cow or Orange Float. 

We both ordered the Combo Plate with Pulled Pork and Brisket with 2 sides and drink. His sides were crispy, thin fries, seasoned well and obviously homemade baked beans that were perfect and not overly sweet. I had the special tater tots that were very dry and lacking flavor and what appeared to be baked mac & cheese. It wasn't creamy, just thicker and possibly overcooked but the flavor was decent. I'm not a fan of the food served directly on butcher paper but I understand the concept. I just prefer my food in containers of some sort. Food dumped on butcher paper feels unappetizing and usually is unattractive.

We had different opinions on the meats. We both felt the Pulled Pork and Brisket was on the dry side so in comes the sauces. I felt it made enough of a difference to repair my Pulled Pork while he did not. I thought the Brisket was the drier of the two while he thought it was the better of the two meats. It was 8:30 and maybe the meats sat for a long time before we ordered. 

The sauces were on each table and appeared to be a different selection on each. We had the Carolina Mustard, Texas Hot, Sweet Saint Louis and Coffee BBQ sauce. I tried 3 of the 4 and my preference was the Texas Hot sauce, Surprise!, followed by the Sweet Saint Louis BBQ sauce. The hot wasn't overbearing nor was the Sweet St. Louis sauce overly sweet. I did enjoy the Coffee sauce but it did fall into third place. By the way, they sell the sauces and rubs for $5.

As with any good barbecue joint they know how to make delicious pies. Chose from Pecan, Keylime, Apple, Sugar Creme or Mississippi Mud. By the slice runs $5 or a whole pie is $28. They also have a Smoked Chocolate Chip Cookie for a $1.99 which I have to try on my next visit.

Overall, friendly staff, generous portions, and a large variety of entrees. Yes, not everything was perfect but I'm willing to give Sugarfly a second chance since it was late in the evening.

I didn't expect a full house on a Monday morning at 10:15. However, every table was taken with one single seat left at a small counter. The resturant has two sides with a doorway between dining rooms. Another patron informed me the place use to be smaller noting only one dining room. 

Very much a family oriented resturant with artsy tables, chairs, sculptural salt & pepper stands, and small collections of tchotcke wall decor. The server, Shawn,  warmly greeted us and answered menu questions. My very large portion coffee cup remained topped off for the entire visit. Even a to-go cup accompanied my carryout bag. Shawn scoring a 10 already.

The half order of  biscuits and gravy ($6) is a huge portion balancing the perfect amount of sausage to the gravy and biscuits. No skimping on sausage or gravy.

The Spinach Omelette ($9.75) was delicious with large amounts of sautéed spinach, onions, mushrooms, tomatoes and feta cheese. Served with potatoes similar to oven roasted skin on red potatoes and a salad or fruit. Both meals could easily be split and we'd leave completely satisfied.

Excellent service, delicious and afforable food using quality ingredients in a casual atmosphere with an eclectic decor. We'll certainly be back next time I'm in the area to sample other items from their large menu.

The restaurant is very clean, minimal decor, 4-top tables with banquette seating and 2-top tables running down the center of the small dining area. There really isn't a lobby, a hostess or a waiting area if there's a crowd. Not sure how they handle a wait list. I arrived at 11:15 so I was one of 5 tables. I was seated immediately by a very polite, soft spoken server and a water appeared momentarily. Oh, and by the way, napkins are located in the drawer at the end of each table. Drinks options (sodas, sake and beers) are listed on the table tents.

The menu is minimal as well which is refreshing. There are ten appetizers, five La -mian noodles and five Ramen noodle dishes. Many flavors availble from vegetable, brisket, beef, chicken, seafood, beef stew, pork belly, and teriyaki flavors to top these scrumptious noodles. I would think a flavor for most everyone is available.

I started with the Shishito Peppers based upon one of the Yelp reviews. The Shishito Peppers are sauteed Japanese peppers with citrus soy and togarashi (a peppery Japanese condiment with a slight kick). I enjoyed the flavor, spice and texture of the peppers but the stem of the peppers were awkard. I'm glad I tried them but I'll probably order a different appetizer next time for ease of eating. 

I ordered the X.O. Seafood La-Mian stir-fried for my entree. The stir-fried had a nice mixture of seafood (shrimp, calamari and scallops) in XO-sauce (no broth) with Bok Choy and scallions. The seafood was tender, not overcooked and flavorful. The fresh noodles were delicious, tender and a bit chewy. La-Mian simply means pulled noodles. They are a type of Chinese noodle made by twisting, stretching and folding the dough into strands, using the weight of the dough. The length and thickness of the strands depends on the number of times the dough is folded. These noodles had a springy texture, were a nice bite size,  and not tough. Very enjoyable! They were very flexible working with the table next to me to accommodate their likes and dislikes.

The server was very attentive without being intrusive. The server brought out boiled peanuts right before I left so I could sample. They had just finished cooking. I wasn't a fan of the peanuts but I'm sure others are. My experience was nice and I enjoyed the fresh noodles and seafood very much. The restaurant is very tranquil and quite plus easy to work at but with so few tables I didn't want to over stay as the lunch crowd was arriving. I would definitely recommend if you enjoy tender, springy noodles and fresh ingredients.

I've been a fan of Chuy's since the first week they opened in Carmel. I love the many flavors, the different sauces, the fresh ingredients and the diverse menu. Currently the hours have been adjusted and they offer a limited menu. Dine-in is still an option at 50% capacity and carryout is available. Servers are wearing masks, guests are required to wear a mask while up and about and tables are being cleaned well between patrons.

The limited menu offers a few appetizers, tortilla soup and two salads (Mexi-Cobb or Taco). The "Big As Yo' Face" burrito is still on the menu along with soft or crispy tacos. Fajitas and two enchiladas (Chicka-Chicka Boom Boom & Build Your Own) are available as well as 3 house specialties. Five of the delicious sauces are still on the menu, too.

The service was wonderful tonight, the food was served hot and delicious plus the beer was cold. Still one of my favorite Mexican restaurants in Indianapolis.

Many years ago we use to go to the beautiful Allisonville Road location and I've been to two other locations but never to this one. Sahm's sits on the corner of Capital and Vermont in the large parking lot. The front of the restaurant faces Vermont while the building backs up to Michigan. There are two entrances, one on Capital and one on Vermont, to enter the parking lot. Sahm's validates parking so don't let the parking arms deter you from entering.

As you approach the entrance you'll see the patio on each side of the entrance. Being a beautiful fall day the lunch crowd was taking full advantage of the beautiful fall weather.

The lobby entrance has a dining area on each side. The dining area to the right has the large bar (+ T.V.'s) with booths and 4-top banquette tables; to the left is a smaller bar with 2-top and 4-top banquette seating with t.v's. The restaurant has a warm, cozy pub atmosphere with dark woods, high back booths with exposed light tan and white brick work in the main bar area. 

Who doesn't enjoy specials and saving some cash? Right? Well, Sahm's features several specials to draw patrons in. Lunch specials are available M-F from open till 4:00. Dinner specials are 7 days a week from 4:00 - close. How about $3.33 sliders, snacks and late night snacks M-F from 3:00 - 6:00 and 9:00 - close. Nice selections to save a few bucks.

I like the menu offers the traditional appetizers, a terrific selection of sandwiches to fish & chips, meatloaf, chicken, fish, pasta, steaks and ribs. Something for most everyone whether you want a light bite, comfort food to a large steak dinner.

I ordered a grilled tenderloin and mac and cheese (to go) for my son. He said it was really good. For my lunch I had the North Atlantic blackened cod sandwich with a cup of meaty chili as my side. The fish was fresh, flaky, cooked perfectly and seasoned well. I would highly recommend to those who enjoy blackened fish.

Our second visit was today for the very reasonably priced Saturday brunch. Brunch is served Saturday and Sunday from open till 3:00 p.m. You also have the option of ordering off the regular menu if the brunch menu doesn't appeal to you. Mimosas and Bloody Mary's were $6 and I was told the Bloody was tasty. Eggs, skillets, biscuits and gravy, breakfast burrito, omelettes and Benedicts are the high lights of the brunch menu. My husband ordered the Monterrey Mix ($8.99) with Chorizo, tomatillo sauce, bell peppers, carmelized onions, pico de gallo but left off the two cheeses. Omelettes are served with your choice of diced hash browns, cornbread casserole, sweet potato hash or fresh fruit and toast. He loved the omelette but thought it needed a larger portion of filler ingredients. The diced hash browns were excellent and not overcooked. I ordered the make your own omelette with spinach, mushrooms, caramelized onions and City ham. Mine was stuffed with ingredients and very flavorful. I opted for the moist cornbread casserole which had a good flavor. We both enjoyed the large slices of whole wheat toast.

This location is close to home, has a diverse menu, good food and service plus affordable. I can see us returning in the near future.

Absolutely adorable tea room in downtown Carmel in the Carmel Arts District. The tea room is located in a cute house turned business with parking directly behind the house (per my server) and one block West of the Tea Room in the free parking garage. Since this was my first time, I was unsure so I parked in the parking garage. As you approach, you'll see the outdoor patio seating on both sides of the entrance, weather permitting.

The interior is elegant and  comfortable with all things England from collections of tea cups and tea pots, British flags, lace, crystal, china, pictures, even a cut-out of the Queen and a few other surprises. It's like a little girl's tea party comes to life. And yes, they have children's tea parties. Actually they have several special events for children and adults. Check out the website for more details. The atmosphere is relaxing and I never felt rushed.

I was told Tina started selling scones at the Farmer's Market years ago and has turned her talent into a very successful and much appreciated business. She mixes all the loose leaf teas (over 20) and the green chutney is her great-grandmother's recipe. So many personal touches and homemade items on the menu to enjoy. Some vegetarian and gluten free items are available too. She's happy to discuss food allergies prior to or during your visit.

It is highly recommended you make a reservation but I took a chance since I was in the area and just walked in. Luckily they had a table available but I'm sure that want last much longer with the holidays upon us. Lunch and Tea's are served all day every day. Whether your looking for breakfast, lunch, a pot of tea and a couple of scones or high tea, Tina's is the place to be. 

Breakfast is served everyday from 10:00 - 12:00.  A Full English Breakfast is served, by reservation ONLY, the first Sunday of each month. November 3, 2019 is the next Full English Breakfast. 

Lunch options include homemade Soups, Cornish Pastry, Sausage Rolls, Chicken Salad, Finger Sandwiches, Salads and Quiche. Wonderful lunch options including bite size tea sandwiches to full size sandwiches.

Since I'd already had lunch, I ordered the Devonshire Cream Tea with a pot of delicious Vanilla Chai Tea and an order of 2 warm chocolate chips scones ($12) served with my favorite clotted cream and yummy raspberry jam. My flavorful tea was delivered with a sand tea timer so it would be perfectly brewed which it was.

My server was terrific, friendly, provided some history about the tea room, answered questions and provided recommendations based upon my tastes. Tina stopped by as well and I loved hearing about the events I could take part in. This is a magical location for an older child's birthday party, a bridal or baby shower or special birthday celebration. 

Make a reservation and bring your family, girlfriends or tweens for a special occasion. I'm looking forward to returning for high tea and brunch.

We really enjoyed our experience at the Dug Out. Dive bars are one of our favorites and Dug Out didn't disappoint. We walked in the door under the exterior sign and told to seat ourselves! 

There's basically 3 sections to the bar. The older bar area, middle dining area and the new modern bar area. You enter the older bar area which has a few tall-top tables across from the bar and T.V.'s are located throughout the 3 areas. The dining area is in the next area/room with lower lighting, lots of history on the walls and a decent amount of 4-top tables close together. Two dart bars, jukebox and games are in this area. The new spacious room on the other side of the dining area has a bar, is bright and modern with regular and tall-top tables and has a stage. There is an entrance there as well. Patio seating is just outside this door. The patio is large and a great spot to dine or have drinks. The handicap ramp runs parallel to the patio and the parking lot is just outside this door with access through double doors to the new bar and dining area. This is the entrance you'll want to take if you have mobility issues. 

Menus are on the tables. The menu has a great selection of bar appetizers you'd expect with nachos, wings, tenders, skins, chili-cheese fries and more. There's Salads, Soups (chili & soup of the day), Wraps, Pizza and Sandwiches (grilled cheese, fried bologna, pulled pork, tenderloin, burger and Cuban). Saturday and Sunday a breakfast buffet is served from 9 -11 for only $7.50. 

My husband ordered the tender and juicy grilled tenderloin with L,T, P with fries ($1 upcharge). All sandwiches are served with Ruffles. The fries were worth the $1 upcharge with a slightly crisp exterior and soft potato interior.

I ordered the Half-Pound Pulled Pork Sandwich in the Green Egg served with pickles and onions and Johnton BBQ sauce. I had onion rings (upcharge of $2.50). The generous amount of pork was tender, the BBQ sauce good and the onions rings were not overcooked. We both enjoyed our dinner and we'd order again. 

Erin, our server, was attentive and friendly during this loud and fun after Colts game crowd. She even cleared the tables as plates and cups emptied. 

We found a fun, laid-back atmosphere with good, affordable, bar food that was delivered timely and a friendly server. Check it out!

We had dinner here last week for the first time and had a pleasant time. The restaurant is gorgeous with low lighting, soft candle light and an upscale atmosphere with 4-top tables and comfortable booths. The bar area reflects the upscale dining area decor along with a gorgeous patio including beautiful fireplaces, comfortable seating, nice lighting and toasty heaters.

The menu offers appetizers with the ever popular Lump Crab Hushpuppies, Smoked Chicken Wings, Cornbread Muffins and Loaded BBQ Pulled Pork Nachos to name a few. Try one of the four salads (Spicy Tuna Poke) or two sandwiches (try the P.I.G) and very diverse entree plates with Southern Fried Chicken, Enchiladas, Turkey Meatloaf, Baby Back Ribs, Fish Tacos and a Filet Mignon round out a few of the entrees. The bar offers several craft cocktails ($9-$12) and craft beers on tap ($6) along with bottles and cans ($6) plus an extensive list of wines ($10-$14 per glass) are some of the full bar options.

My husband enjoyed his Sam Adam's Cold Snap. He ordered the P.I.G. sandwich with fries. The P.I.G. sandwich is smoked pulled pork, thick-cut bacon, aged swiss, Carolina gold sauce and bread & butter pickles on soft, lightly toasted roll. The sandwich was very flavorful with a generous amount of pulled pork, the thick cut bacon was a nice addition and the roll held up well. 

The Cucumber Basil Cooler was a very refreshing beverage. The tomato soup was a nice consistency, rich and tasty.  I also had the Lump Crab Hushpuppies which consists of sweet corn, jalapeno and pepper jack cheese served with citrus aioli. I really enjoyed the nice balance of flavors in the hushpuppies but not a fan of the citrus aioli but others were.

Bobbie was our server and he didn't miss a step. He was professional, friendly and thoughtful. 

Wonderful place for both a romantic or casual dinner with great service. I look forward to trying different entrees in the near future.

This was our first visit to Hana. We arrived at lunch time and was surprised it wasn't busier. We were seated immediately and asked for our drink order. I'm a Diet Coke drinker and they serve Pepsi so I ordered hot tea. I thought it would be a pot of tea but instead was a single cup so make a note if you're a tea drinker.

We were very pleased with the menu options which has many Appetizers, 3 Soups, House Sushi Rolls, two full pages of Fusion Rolls and Hibachi Lunches.

My friend and I were starving so we started with an order of Gyoza (Japanese dumplings) filled with pork and veggies. They were served warm with a dumpling sauce. My friend ordered miso soup and my lunch entree came with warm miso soup.

I ordered the Shrimp Hibachi Lunch ($8.95) served with a nice portion of shrimp, generous amount of tender fried rice, sauteed veggies and miso soup. It was very good, the shrimp was prepared perfectly, the rice was tender and I'd order again.

We each ordered a Hana Fusion Rolls to share. Mine was the excellent Mexican Roll with crab, shrimp, avocado, jalapeno and cream cheese inside with rice outside, deep fried and served with eel and spicy mayo sauce. The balance of cream cheese to the crab and shrimp was a nice balance allowing the fish to take center stage with a touch of heat.

My friend ordered the tasty Fire Dragon Roll with shrimp tempura, cream cheese, mango, avocado and spicy crab on top with eel sauce. The roll had a nice crunch with a sweet and spicy flavor. Very flavorful and a close second but the Mexican Roll was my personal favorite.

My Hibachi Shrimp, rice and veggies was delicious. We loved both of the fusion rolls and highly recommend. Both of us want to return and try other rolls.

The service was awkward and lacking throughout our lunch. We had excellent service from the minute we sat down until the food arrived. Our server checked on us a couple times right after our lunches arrived but always when we didn't need anything. When we wanted extra sauce, napkins, water and drink refills she never looked our way or checked on us. Toward the end of lunch we felt rather ignored. I don't think it was intentional as she seemed to deal with one table at a time and it got busy. Her timing was just off and left us wishing for better service. Regardless of the server our food was delicious and we really enjoyed. We will most likely return to sample more of the Fusion Rolls.

Morning's Breakfast and Brunch sits in the Kroger Shopping Center next door to  Bravo. The restaurant is bright and fresh with booths, tables and banquette seating. The decor is in grays and yellow with lots of natural lighting and a very warm and comfort dining area. The variety of music was enjoyable and played at a good volume for conversation.

The menu consists of breakfast and lunch options. Skillets, omelettes, frittatas, benedict's, crepes, french toast, pancakes and more. Lunch options include soups, five salads and many sandwiches (burgers, tenderloins, chicken, etc.).

I ordered the Carne Asada Skillet with scrambled eggs, hash browns, and French Toast. The presentation was attractive in a cast iron skillet set into a wooden tray. The shredded, cheesy hash browns with onions were placed on the bottom of the skillet with the eggs and sliced steak neatly arranged on top. I requested the steak be prepared medium rare but it was more of a medium. Not horribly over cooked for me, seasoned well and still tender. The cheesy hash browns with sliced onions were yummy as well. 

I also ordered a Corn Beef Reuben with tasty, thick homemade chips. The sandwich had a generous amount of corn beef and sauerkraut on a marbled rye bread. The other sandwich was a breaded tenderloin with the homemade chips. The tenderloin was a nice size and seasoned well with a nice ratio of breading to meat. I'd order all again. 

Karina, my server, was friendly and did a fine job. My coffee cup remained full and checked on me several times.

It was an enjoyable visit, nice atmosphere, good food and service. I'll be placing Morning's in our breakfast roation.

First, you should know this is a 21 and over bar. As you enter it's seat yourself at one of the numerous tables, booths or at the large U-shaped bar. Regardless of where you seat there's a flatscreen TV at every angle.  In the back area of the bar are 3 pool tables and an electronic dart board. The lighting is low, the music is average to loud and the food was good.

The menu consists of Appetizers, Soups & Salads, Sandwiches, Burgers and Pizza. Available after 5 p.m. are Steaks and Entrees served with two sides (Filet Mignon, Ribeye, NY Strip, Pork Ribeye, Salmon or Loaded Chicken Steak). Their trying to switch their image from bar to restaurant. I'd say bar is fine as long as the food and drinks are good.

We started off with the Flat Fried Pickles (8 long pieces) which is fresh, whole pickles sliced by hand, long and flat then hand-breaded and deep-fried. Tangy and really good with the chipotle ranch dressing for dipping.

Lunch/Dinner for my husband was the Grilled Tenderloin with Cajun Coin Fries. The tenderloin was slightly larger than the bun so it wasn't abused, seasoned well and very tender. The generous portion of Coin fries had a decent amount of seasoning but were just a bit overcooked for our liking. Still very edible, just crispier than we care for.

I ordered the Cajun Chicken Sandwich with Chicken Enchiladas Soup. I was pleasantly surprised how juicy and tender my sandwich was. I love Cajun seasoning which was generous and the pepper jack cheese complimented the cajun seasoning nicely. The Chicken Enchilada Soup, my side, was full of corn, black beans, chicken, spice and had just a hint of heat. Very enjoyable on a nasty, dreary night.

Our server, David, did a nice job taking care of us. We had a slight hiccup in the beginning with the pasta dinner special being changed from what was listed on the board by the entrance. We waited till 5 p.m. so we could order the special only to find  when he rang it in the kitchen had changed. Extremely disappointed but I did enjoy my sandwich and soup.

Great bar to meet friends for drinks, watch a sporting event, shoot some pool and have a solid meal.

This place is huge with all types of seating with flat screens everywhere and a large bar. Great location for watching sporting events! The open air concept is great on this perfect day in May sitting on the patio. Love this patio with 6 picnic tables, sofa's and high top tables with Connect 4 and Corn Hole games. I wasn't looking for a hectic patio sitting on a sidewalk where I feel like I'm dining with cars and traffic. This patio is so not that! Enclosed on all 4 sides with two sides being old brick walls. It feels very private especially on a Saturday morning when it's very quite before the crowd hits. Just what I was looking for today! Great atmosphere, excellent service and good food on a beautiful day.

The menu has a terrific variety with salads, wraps, street tacos, burgers, lot of new seafood items, chicken fried chicken 'n gravy and fries to name a few. The State Fair desserts, deep fried oreos, cinnamon soft pretzels and the Everything & The Bowl Sundae looked scrumptious!

My husband ordered the Brothers Classic Bacon Cheeseburger which he enjoyed. He would have preferred if asked how he wanted it cooked, a tad less, and with more seasoning but the tasty burger had tender meat with very little fat. The bacon was crisp tender and very good. The fries are tasty and similar but not the Hop Cat fries. 

I ordered the Five Cheese Mac 'n Cheese with Penne pasta mixed with chopped bacon and I added Blackened grilled chicken breast ($3.99 upcharge) served with a soft bread stick. The chicken was so extremely tender and I asked for extra seasoning so she recommended blackened. It was perfect with the cheesey Penne pasta with bacon. 

I know this restaurant isn't known for quite, laid back atmosphere but earlier on a Saturday morning seems to work for me. Exactly what I needed and we appreciated the excellent service, good food and not rushing us out.

It's been quite awhile since we've been to Twenty Tap. We ended up here tonight because Aristocrat's decided to close due to a kitchen employee exposed to Covid. Twenty Tap is one of my husband's favorite restaurants for hamburgers so he wasn't disappointed.

The restaurant had a nice crowd but limited tables and booths due to social distancing. There is seating on the enclosed heated patio plus the beer garden. We were seated immediately at a 4-top table that included a bottle of hand sanitizer. Each table had their own bottle of hand sanitizer.  Easy peasy! Masks are required while up and about but not at the table. All of the servers were wearing their masks properly.

Twenty Tap has a terrific selection of craft beer with 38 taps. The menu offers the classic pub menu including vegan and vegetarian options. 

Our server arrived quickly and returned with my husband's beer and my Diet Coke. The soup of the day was Chipotle Split Pea and Ham which was very, very good! Heavy on the Chipotle seasoning and spicy hot. Many would not care for the amount of spice but it was awesome. 

I don't understand why so many servers bring your soup/appetizers just a couple minutes before serving the entree. I asked for the soup before my entree which she did. Literally 2 minutes after delivering my soup she delivered our sandwiches. I do wish servers wouldn't do this and space the items out. My salmon and fries would have been cold if I had eaten the hot soup first. 

My husband ordered the Classic Burger with his favorite toppings. The burger was cooked medium and it was perfect for him with the center having a touch of pink. The seasoned fries are excellent and a favorite side for both of us.

I ordered the Grilled Salmon BLT with salmon marinated in teriyaki  sauce and topped with bacon, spinach, roasted tomato, cucumber, grilled onions and wasabi mayo on ciabatti. The grilled salmon had a wonderful flavor, the toppings were fresh plus the ciabatti bread was perfect. My problem was the sandwich wasn't handheld for me. This isn't a restaurant problem, just my own. I ended up cutting the sandwich into bites but still took half of it home. Regardless of being messy, the Grilled Salmon BLT was delicious.

We had a nice dinner at Twenty Tap with good service, excellent quality food and in a fun, pub atmosphere.

First, parking is a struggle of course or was for us plus the construction threw us for a minute. We parked on a side street North of the front door which thankfully was a short walk on this lovely, rainy day.

It was seat yourself at either one of the 4 two-tops, 2 picnic tables, bar top or several tall-tops so we grabbed a tall-top. Our server, A.J., was prompt and grabbed a sample of the Blood On The Tracks for us. My husband loved his beer so much he's going home with a Growler.

The menu has a nice variety from Appetizers (Spicy Dip, Hummus, Beer Cheese w/Pretzels), Soup, Turkey Chili, Wraps, Sandwiches, Mac & Cheese, Salads and Burgers. The Burger options can be replaced with a chicken breast or spicy black bean patty or made with the steak burger. I wish I'd read that closer when I was scanning the menu. It appears I get distracted easily or focused on just a few things...I digress!

My husband ordered the Buffalo Springfield Wrap and Kettle Chips. The Wrap is full of grilled chicken, buffalo sauce, mixed greens (beware the greens has an oil dressing), tomato, red onion, (his minus blue cheese dressing) in a fresh, flour tortilla. My husband enjoyed the sandwich but ate around the mixed greens due to the oil. Even with that he said he'd order again minus the mixed greens and blue cheese dressing. We both found the Kettle Chips delicious with the perfect amount of seasoning and surprisingly not overcooked! I just had a couple and could have devoured the entire order. I've never enjoyed kettle chips until now!!

I started with a cup of tasty Turkey Chili, while good, I'd enjoy it a bit spicier but that's just my personal taste. I also ordered the refreshing John and Yoko Salad with fresh mixed greens, cranberries, candied walnuts, pumpkin seeds, tomatoes and blue cheese crumbles. It had a nice balance of flavors, sweet and salty with a pleasant, sweet crunch.

The decadent Chocolate Bread Pudding is made from scratch using one of their craft beers. It's a tender, thinner bread pudding with a rich chocolate sauce topping. It will satisfy your sweet tooth.

A.J., our server, definitely deserved a 5 star rating. She was friendly, efficient, prompt and personable. She was a huge contributing factor for our pleasant afternoon.

Terrific atmosphere, excellent service, perfect people watching patio, once warmer weather arrives, good food and good beer will bring us back. Parking is the only reason for 4 stars instead of 5. If biking or lived closer to walk then I'd give a 5 star rating.

It was a perfect, sunny, fall day so I decided to check out Baby's patio. Baby's is located on the corner of Talbott and 22nd Street with the entrance on Talbott. Street parking is available along with two empty lots directly across from the entrance. I've been avoiding downtown because of parking but no current parking issues here.

The interior is adorable decorated in pinks, cute accessories, a large mural, a large Baby's neon light behind the bar with several tables, banquette booths and bar or patio seating. I sat on the shaded patio which I found very comfortable with tables thoughtfully laid out and it doesn't feel cramped and congested. The patio drapes blowing over my table made for several laughable moments though.

The menu is fairly simple with Smash Burgers as their speciality but you'll find options from a veggie burger, grilled or broasted chicken, a salad and sides. 

Alcohol wise there is beer (ONLY in cans and bottles), wine, shots and several types of signature cocktails with cute names. The owner created the recipes for the Cocktails on Draft and there's a full bar with oodles of spirits. Again, no beer on draft since cocktails are on draft. What's fun and different are the boozy milkshakes offered with strawberry, chocolate or their seasonal flavor. I ordered one of the Cocktails on Draft, For The Gods, made with 3 types of rum, dry curacao, orgeat, and lime plus it's not overly sweet. If you enjoy rum you'll most likely enjoy this drink.

Smash burgers run from a single to triple ($8-$14) or add even yet another patty for additional $3 and all served on a vegan bun. I love toppings and sauces and Baby's has some of my favorites. Most toppings are free except for mango chutney, sauteed mushrooms (.50 extra) and bacon ($1) on any sandwich. Add as many or few toppings and sauces as you prefer from the list. 

Other menu options is the Broasted Chicken (whole 8 pieces, half 4 pieces or 2 piece cutlets) or a large salad with or without protein.

The tender, marinated grilled chicken sandwich was amazing topped with a generous amount of phenomenal carmelized onions, sauteed mushrooms, smoked gouda cheese and pickled jalapenos. So messy but I loved the layer of sweet and savory flavors. I was curious about the white bbq sauce so I ordered on the side for my sandwich.
