The sauce was so tasty I ended up using as a dipping sauce for my fries. The white bbq sauce is a horseradish base and very flavorful. The fries are similar to McDonalds, lightly crispy, seasoned only with salt and pepper and hot and fresh. There's an option to glitz up the fries with bacon, cheese sauce, white BBQ sauce and jalapenos for just an extra $2. Maybe next time.

Sides are ala carte at $4 with fries, mac & cheese, sriracha broccoli slaw, veggies, side salad and corn bread. The little 4 1/2 yr old girl sitting at the next table gave the mac and cheese high praise while her little sister quietly tore into the naked chicken tenders.

This is a family friendly restaurant with a kids menu available and changing tables in the cute, gender neutral, large restrooms with roller doors. Checkout the fun wallpaper.

My server, Camyrn I think?, was also the bartender who took excellent care of me. She explained the menu, many drinks, the boozy milkshakes and several suggestions thoroughly. Even tending bar she checked on me frequently and maintained her fun, outgoing personality while running back and forth.

Overall, parking was super simple, my food was a solid 5, the atmosphere was fun and relaxing plus my server was top-notch. A 5 star experience with no complaints but I'm saving 5 stars till I see consistency on the next visit.

We came to Liter's for both the Farmer's Market and Brunch. Unfortunately, I didn't confirm the Farmer's Market hours beforehand so I only had a few minutes to shop. Hopefully I can come back another day because there were some cool items here. One of today's brunch specials was based around the Broad Ripple's Farmer's Market which was a vegan special. There are several vegan and vegetarian options on Liter's menu.

We arrived at Liter's before the rush and was seated quickly. Our server, Jordan, couldn't arrive quickly as she appeared to be tied up with a couple large tables. When she did arrive we found her to be friendly, knowledgeable and attentive.

The Bavarian inspired menu had many entrees and salads I'm looking forward to trying in the future. Today, we were here for their Saturday brunch. I ordered the Breakfast Brunch Basic with your choice of eggs, protein and toast. I tried the Smoked Pork Hash chopped and sauteed with onions, peppers and potatoes, topped with two scrambled eggs and Crystal hot sauce aioli and thick, hearty toast. The smoked pork was truly  excellent and flavorful with large pieces of meat mixed in with the generous veggies. It is hard to find good hash and this certainly was one of the best I've had. I will order again.

My husband ordered the Egg Sandwich with option of bacon or sausage on toast with scrambled eggs (his minus cheese) and served with a simple salad, fruit or diced potatoes (his choice). He noted the entire sandwich was bland and the sausage was mediocre. The potatoes were prepared well and he enjoyed a little more after seasoning. He wasn't terribly impressed with the sandwich and probably will not order again. 

The brunch menu has a nice variety with Ham & Grits, Salads, and several types of Waffles (Chicken & Waffle, Buttermilk Waffle and Meat, Waffle and Turchettis hot link and eggs or the every changing Jose's Waffle Special). I'm no expert on German food; I know what I like but want to try new things. They offer several sausages (bratwurst, bluwurst, currywurst), sauerkraut, schnitzels (pork, chicken or portabella) and several German specials. Of course you'll find all the drafts, ciders, seasonal and canned beers plus cocktails, spirits and wines. 

I enjoyed the relaxing atmosphere, my breakfast was fantastic and Jordan provided excellent service. I'm sure I'll be back for brunch and the Smoked Pork Hash.

Driven2SaveLives BC39  returned for its second year running Wednesday, Sept. 4 and Thursday, Sept. 5, 2019 at the quarter-mile, clay oval Dirt Track inside Turn 3 at IMS. This event is exciting to watch and a great addition for the currrent 10 days of racing starting with the Labor Day Drags, 2 nights of Dirt Track leading into this weekends Brickyard 400. The race was sold out last year and IMS added 600 additional seats this year which were almost sold out for the second year.

This event is in memory of Brian Clausen who died in a tragic crash in August 2016 but he donated 5 organs saving lives and helped over 75 people with his tissue donation. Even today he extends lives, literally, by inspiring thousands to pledge their organs to save others. Are you an organ donor? If not, please consider.

This is a family friendly event and I get a kick out of watching the younger fans, and adults, get so excited as the cars battle for the win. IMS always brings the best races and the best 90 short-track racers in America to this spectacular USAC Midget National Championship race. Drivers from California, Arizona, New Zealand and many  Indiana drivers to name a few.

It's exhilarating watching the cars go three wide in the turns, sliding sideways or drifting through the turns, and battling to the end regardless if it's the hot laps, qualifying or the final DC39 lap race. Kyle Larson was the winner of the thrilling Stoops Pursuit Race on Wednesday. What a finish!! Only three cars were left in the race; last lap, last turn, 2 cars flip (no injuries)  at once and the last car remaining wins!!  Everyone was on their feet. Congrats Kyle Larson!!

Thursday night was just as exciting with 16 year old, (yes 16!) Zeb Wise, of Angola, IN, winning after a thrilling four lap shootout with his teammates. Wise won $15,000 for his third USAC National Midget victory of the season in the 39BC. $15,000 is the largest payout in midget racing.

If you go to the IMS dirt track midget race know you will get dirty with plenty of dirt thrown from the track. Bring eye protection with some form of glasses, maybe a bandana or mask for dust and a hat or hoodie. The crowd and cars are loud and some prefer to have ear plugs. NO outside alcohol or coolers are allowed at the dirt track. I know! That threw me too but it's a dirt track thing. Yes, it's IMS but no coolers or alcohol at this race. Clear bags with snacks are allowed. Several food and merchandise vendors are onsite.

I hope the fans continue to support the IMS dirt track and these spectacular races continue for years to come.

I love The Tamale Place on Rockville Road. They have come so far from the little, dark, hole in the wall they were many, many years ago right on the corner of Lynhurst and Rockville. Now their in the old Marsh strip center facing Rockville Road with the black & white stripe canopy and green and purple storefront. The current location has progressed from a chalkboard tamale menu to an electronic tracking menu and they move you through the line super quickly. The other items offered are tacos and nachos, tortas, chips, salsa and white queso are listed on the menu board above the order counter. The tamales are huge (1/2 lb.) with many different varieties, seasonal and sweet flavors. The owner tried to make small tamales when she first began making family recipes but just couldn't which is why their so large. Score for the customers! Be warned when they run out of a type of tamale it's gone. The earlier you arrive in the day means better the selection. 

The hot & spicy pork and chicken, pumpkin, chocolate and sweet corn tamales are my favorites. My husband and son love the hot & spicy pork, beef, and chicken. The half order of nachos are enough for two people. These are the nachos I crave when I'm in the mood for nachos and I can customize them. Oodles of chips, hot & spicy pork, lots of white queso and topped with fresh jalapeno's, black beans, quac, tomatoes and sour cream.

The breakfast taco is another of my favorites. They open at 6:30 a.m. so grab breakfast to go or dine in. Its faster than going through McDonalds. Grab one or two for lunch and your co-workers will soon be asking you to pick up tamales  and tacos for them.

The staff are really nice people, fast and helpful. You can dine in at one of the 4 tables or if weather permits dine at the small tables on the side walk. We get our orders to go and the tamales are always hot when we get home. They also reheat well for a minute or so in the microwave if you want to stock pile a few.

Wish they were still open on Sunday's but I totally understand they need time off.

Perfect fall day to sit on the patio and enjoy the beautiful weather. The patio runs alone the South and Southwest corner of the restaurant. Several tables have umbrellas but the large shade trees take care of much of the sun.

The Upland Octoberfest hit the spot with my husband. I ordered the Beer Cheese Dip made with Upland Champagne Velvet Pilsner and blended with aged white cheddar and smoked Gouda cheeses. Served with three ball-park pretzels. The beer cheese dip was tasty and the beer was very distinguishable.

My husband ordered the Black and Bleu Burger (minus the cheese) with bacon, caramelized onions, lettuce and tomato. Served with crispy, well seasoned French fries. It was very messy but he enjoyed nevertheless.

I ordered the Greuben, a blend of a grouper and a  Reuben sandwich. It's flash fried and served on grilled marble rye bread with Swiss cheese, red cabbage slaw and Russian dressing. Served with onion rings. Different flavors than I've had before but overall enjoyable, just not sure I'd order again.

The service was good even with several other tables arriving right after us. 

Comfortable patio with good food and service.

I received a gift card for On the Border and decided to use it for lunch today. The seating area is broken into 3 sections by a partial wall and the bar area. The restaurant decor is very tastefully done in bright blues, turquoise, yellow and reds. A large two-sided fireplace is located between the two dining area. Booths and 4 top tables are available with tables adhering to social distancing. 

The menu covers all the favorite from appetizers and dips, burritos, chimis, enchiladas, fajitas, border bowls and their Mesquite Grilled Chicken or Carne Asada. I like the Create Your Own Combos with a selection of any 2 3 or 4 items from tacos, enchiladas, classics or soup or salad.

Lunch is served Monday-Friday until 4:00p. I ordered the Border's Best Lunch Steak Fajitas for lunch. It was a smaller lunch size portion of mesquite grilled steak served with rice, refried beans, tortillas and pico de gallo, sour cream, quacamole and shredded cheese. I requested the steak to be medium-rare to medium and the steak was perfect. Tender with a little heat with a few bites. The rice was light and the addition of corn added a nice touch plus the refried beans were partially smashed and I enjoyed the texture and flavors.

My server, Alexandra, did a fabulous job with the exception of removing dirty plates promptly. I stacked and pushed them to the very edge of the table to make it convenient. Unfortunately after 3 additional trips to my table they were still on the table when I left. Other than the 1 issue she checked on me several times, food and drinks came out quickly and extra napkins were on the table without asking.

Overall, my lunch was wonderful with fresh ingredients, cooked as requested and service was great.

Extremely popular and cute place in an old converted gas station with modern 50's decor that reminded me of my childhood. Complete with formica tables, color scheme, a juke box and kitschy. You have your option of counter seating, tall tops, 4 tops tables and patio seating when weather permits.

Tuesday thru Thursday is seat yourself but a hostess is on board for the weekend. Weekends are crazy busy so be prepared for a wait. In the summertime, we've  waited over an hour and possibly longer for patio seating.

If you enjoy a cocktail with brunch you're in luck. They serve Mimosas and Cocktails ($6 Bloody Mary, Screwdriver, Tequila Sunrise, Mojito and Salty Dog).

Our server, Angela, was a breathe of fresh air. Smiling, friendly, very personable and efficient. Such a difference from my last visit when the server never smiled, appeared mad and disconnected. Angela did a wonderful job and made our visit a very positive experience.

The menu offers both breakfast and lunch options served all day. Our order seemed to arrive almost as quickly as the order hit the window. Super fast service. My husband ordered the Boomer Biscuits & Gravy with two split biscuits served with ample amount of sausage gravy. He thought it was very good but served lukewarm instead of hot and it cooled off very quickly. 

I ordered the Full Boat with 2 eggs, fried potatoes, 1/2 order of lukewarm biscuits and gravy with choice of meat (bacon for me). My scrambled eggs were light and airy, the fried potatoes were a nice treat, and the bacon was prepared as requested. Of course, I ended up with a carry out box but I enjoyed everything.

Good food, great service with a cool atmosphere! Visiting during the week is the way to go if you have the option. Weekends are great but be prepared for a wait. Note, they will only seat you when the entire party is physically there.

Stanley Restaurant is the place to go in NOLA for a mouthwatering brunch. Overlooking Jackson Square and the Cathedral, the ambiance is an excellent touristy spot to sip on your morning coffee (or if you just want to people watch). The menu includes innovative twists to traditional dishes. It was a chore just getting here from the hotel becuase it was pouring rain that day, Thankfully the food made the voyage all worth it.

Let's get into the meat and bones of my dish, the eggs Stanley. Their namesake dish gets 2 thumbs up from me. 6 Cornmeal-Crusted Oysters, Poached Eggs, Canadian Bacon and Creole Hollandaise on a Toasted English Muffin. I loved that the canadian bacon came thin so not to overwhelm the dish. The oysters were very fresh that day and the poached eggs were done right. Whites were firm and the yolk runny. Hollandaise sauce to top it off gives the creole kick it deserves. 

Afterwards the banana's foster french toast was shared among 3 to complete the meal. They use thickly sliced french bread, sliced bananas, toasted walnuts and cover it with foster sauce and a nice little dollop of vanilla bean ice cream. Ah-mazing. There's no way I could finish this and the stanley on my own, so sharing one amongst 3 was a smart decision.

Only knock I had was the service. Since the restaurant is always busy, the staff seem a little bit rushed, but friendly for the most part. It is a shame because everything else in this restaurant was stella! Stanley is the sister restaurant of Stella (Which I need to try my next trip here).

Legit. Hole-in-the-Wall restauarnt located in the 7th Ward. The surrounding neighborhood is a bit sketch, but once you find your way in, the friendliness of the staff will ease your soul. Ambiance feels like you stepped in someone's house and about to scarf down some mighty good soul food. 

First timers should indubitably try the Fried Chicken. Comes with 3 delectable pieces and your choice of one side. I would recommend selecting the red beans and rice to complement the chicken. Add in a sweet tea and your meal is complete. The batter on these chickens is unlike anything I have ever tasted. It is super crunchy, so it shatters in the mouth upon contact. Fried to a copper colored crisp, the skin is also salty. I would recommend mixing pieces of the batter with the red beans/butter beans to even out the saltiness. The herbs and spices mixed with the overall juicy texture of the meat makes for some damn good NOLA fried chicken.

Now on to my side story of this place. I had to take a dump....BAD. Unfortunately for me, the toilet seat in the men's room was "Out of Order" on this day. I asked the lady guarding the bathroom, "Is there any way I can use the ladies toilet? I need to go bad!"  "No can do" said the lady. I was stranded, no where to go. This place was surrounded by houses. I wasn't about to knock on some random person's door asking if I can use their john. Thinking quickly on my feet, I saw there was some construction going on across the block. I hightailed it over to their nearest porter potty and let loose. Thank God for construction, or else I would of shat my pants!

Guys, u need a working toilet. I should not have to be subjected to this type of torture!!!!

The fact that I still gave this place 4 stars is a testament to the food, cause their service was not up to par.

Pro: Great restaurant offering a brand of Latin cuisine not available otherwise in StL! It's a casual-enough ambiance to dine with a group of friends, yet intimate enough to take out the hubby/wife on date night. The complimentary plantain chips with cilantro dipping sauce starts off the meal very well, but the heart and soul of the menu is the Lomo Saltado! This salty/savory steak over rice is worth its weight in gold. Other favorites include the empanadas and the Saltado de Langostinos (sauteed shrimp over rice).

Con: The ceviche options were just okay. I had higher expectations, honestly. 

Bottom Line: Easily one of the best places on Wash Ave, if not the best!

Pro:  This simply is what it's supposed to be: a no-frills helping of meat, bread, cheese, and onions. It's a suitable meal for late-night barflies and non-calorie counters. The historic reputation makes it a stopping point for out-of-towners that want the bragging rights of a cheesesteak in Philly. And for those who don't know how to order one "like a local", a large instructional sign is placed near the service window for your reference. #betterthangenos

Con:  If you scroll through the reviews of Pat's, you will find that many of the better ones are written by non-Philadelphians. This illustrates two points...1) Pat's is a bit of a tourist trap, and 2) Locals know that a better cheesesteak can be found in Philly. Ladies and gents, both points are right! Though adequate for what it is, I expected better...

Bottom Line: Try it for the experience, search elsewhere for the superiority.

The idea of the restaurant is that you can eat while watching people work on hot rod cars in the garage. We called ahead to make sure they would be working and were told they would be except  from one to two, when they take lunch. We got there at 12:30 and they were not working. Disappointing, since that's  what got us to go there. The waitress said they must have taken lunch early. 
As far as the food, it was fairly good. I got a Baja salad which i would rate just okay. Others with us got burgers and they said they were very good. 
So, food was okay, but don't  plan on seeing any car work being done. 
They should be more professional and keep to a schedule for the customers if that's  what they advertize.

Overpriced. Overpriced. Overpriced!

As someone who lived in San Antonio for 4 years, I would call myself a connoisseur of authentic Mexican food. Believe me, I am rarely impressed. Casa Borrega most definitely did not deliver. To start of, the kind waiter will offer you chips, salsa and guacamole. Surprise, they're not complimentary as you are led to think. They'll charge you for even the air you breathe in that joint. 

The service was also subpar, as I had to repeatedly remind the waiter that I had ordered a margarita. He served the entire table's drinks, except for mine and I had to wait at least 10-15min after I reminded him that my drink was missing. Yes, it was a large party of 16 people but the restaurant was pretty much empty that Thursday night. 

Moving on, my margarita on the rocks was $14. For a regular(more on the small side) sized, on the rocks margarita, I consider that $14 is quite excessive, especially in New Orleans. I'm sure the most expensive margarita I have had in New Orleans (before going to Casa Borrega) was at Ivy, for $12. And I got to say, this $14 margarita did not even compare to Ivy's.

Next, the tacos. For a 3 small VEGETARIAN tortilla taco plate with a smudge of guacamole in the center, I paid $15+. Again, the flavor was definitely not out of this world. I'm not saying they were bad,but if you're looking for good tacos and other Mexican dishes I'm sure you're better off even going to Felipe's! No joke.

Finally, it's a large party of 16. Oh surprise again, they don't separate checks. Is this not the 21st century USA? I thought not separating checks was something only rude European waiters did! Lastly, it's a $600 check. Surprise numbers three: CASH ONLY.

Do yourself a favor, take your Mexican food cravings elsewhere. You'll be satisfied, treated nicely, not overcharged and you won't feel like you're living in the Stone Age paying with coins and cash.  There are much better options in New Orleans for Mexican food. Sorry not sorry, Casa Borrega.

P.S: Don't even mention if you're at a birthday dinner. They'll bring cake, and they will most definitely charge it for it as well.

The customer service was horrible.

On a Saturday night shortly after 9:30 (they close at 10:30), my boyfriend and I walked in to have a pizza and some wine. After squeezing past the hostess (??) who gave us blank stares, we asked the chef to the right if he was still making pizzas. "We stop seating at 9:30" he yelled, weirdly angry. The hostess said something to him (but nothing to us) and then he just said, "We stopped seating," again. The hostess just stared some more as we turned around and walked back out.

It's fine if they stop seating at 9:30 (though they could say that on their website; most places that close at 10:30 will still seat you at 9:40). But the way they spoke to us was rude, as if we were a huge imposition. We were just two hungry guys in a good mood, popping in to give it a try. The least they could do is say "hello" and "goodbye."

I highly debated whether or not to write this review,  but we left so disappointed today. This was our first visit, and we've been wanting to come support after the recent events. 
Our meal took about 50 minutes to get to us after we ordered, it felt like an eternity because my kids were starving. When it finally arrived, my boys took one bite and said the red sauce tasted bad. My husband and I both took a bite and immediately knew something was wrong. It tasted rancid, burnt, terrible. We let our waitress know and she took the plates back. 
After 15 minutes the owner came out to talk to us and said that we were right. They were reusing the sauce from lastnight and when they mixed a new batch, all of the burnt bottom mixed in with the new sauce giving it that horrible flavor. He apologized and took it off of our bill.

We appreciated his sincerity, but my kids were still starving. He didn't offer to bring them anything else....
After we paid for the rest of our meal, our wonderful waitress offered us food to bring home, but our kids said no. We had waited so long for our original meal and we were all just ready to leave. 
After such a bad experience, I don't think we will return. We are very forgiving, but I feel like the owner could have handled this a little bit better. We were not the only diners sending dishes back, so I know others had a similar experience today.

No phone, no chairs, and cash only. Oh and the business hours posted are a lie. They have a business half hour. Showed up 30 minutes after they opened and saw a sold out sign on the door. Beddia wasn't opened for the three days leading up to the night I arrived and they sold out thirty minutes after they opened.

I am sure this creates excitement and intrigue for some. For me, I am furious . If I drive in from the suburbs and you don't answer the phone and you sell out in thirty minutes, what am I supposed to do? I guess I'll just have to go somewhere where business owners respond to their patrons. AKA everywhere else.

The owner is a liar, inappropriate, and unfair.  Do not ever eat here with a big party of people.  I went with my friends for new years eve.  We made our reservation well in advance, we even changed it to accommodate the restaurant, and when we got there, he literally put a time limit on the length of our dinner.  He told us we had 1.5 hours to eat with our party of 12! He consistently talked rudely about us to other patrons in the restaurant.  Furthermore, the food was almost shoved in our faces.  I have never seen food served so quickly, not to mention some dishes were cold.

I suggest that you never go here. The food was decent and the waiter was very nice, but the owner is unreasonable and does not deserve our business

This magnificent, old Hollywood,
Glamorous property is just opening .
It takes time to get all the elements to align .
What a huge task , remodeling and opening such a fantastic resort .
The GM , Luigi , is such a nice guy & he def has a vision .
Very hard to open and have all departments up and ready to go on day one .
Not making excuses , no one should be told to wait another 30 min to dine , due to the hostess not putting them on the wait list :(
That's a huge drag , no doubt .
But I do trust that the service will soon match the decor .
Rosewood knows what's up .
And they have a good team to lead the staff and to create a lasting impression and a truly wonderful experience.
I attended the soft opening .
It's a historic property, and it has a "feel good-vibe" 
All over the property.
We stayed in a great room , but the villas & the suites , were a big WOW !!
Lobby is stunning .
I say , give it a little time & a bit of patience.
Come now , before the crowds arrive .
And enjoy the tranquility.
It's an impressive launch !!
And I wish them all good !

After receiving a message via Yelp mail from the MTM leadership organization (name of the individual removed at request) I would like to add an addendum.

It was pointed out that in my comparison of MTM to the Brockway Pub or the Stacked Pickle that I did a one-to-one (apples to apples) comparison as if they were the same in menu.  Not wanting to make a statement that was described as "...way out in DEEP right field."   I would like to clarify.

I was asked in the message, 

"[At the other pubs] Can you get a choice cut fillet mignon?  Can you get a choice Ribeye?  Can you get a panko crusted Fresh Walleye entree or sandwich?  Can you get an Ahi Tuna Wonton or a Shrimp and Grits?  Can you get an Ahi Tuna Flatbread?  I don't think so.  And, more than likely, you do not have two culinary chefs in either one of those kitchens like we do at MTM."

-Don't let the previous verbiage make you think that the person who emailed me from MTM Senior Leadership doesn't like the Stacked Pickle or The Brockway Pub as in a second email they told me they do like these two establishments and have dined there on occasion.-

To continue...
You are absolutely correct sir. Many of those items are not on the other pubs' menus. However, I was at your establishment for a work lunch not an intimate dinner and the rectangular shaped fish was tasteless, however, I won't reiterate my last post for either the negatives or the many positives. I hope that your dinner service and food doesn't reflect my two lunch experiences. If and when I return to MTM's I look forward to improvements in your food and hope for your long success in Carmel.

The MTM leadership offered to send me gift certificates for my next meal and the meals of my coworkers. There's no need. I don't write reviews to get free food. I write reviews to inform. All I want is to come into MTM, order, have a great meal with exceptional service, pay the bill and repeat. But that hasn't happened, twice.

I'll try one final time, perhaps, in 2013...and update my review shortly after.

I have mixed feelings about this place, great location right on bourbon street, beautiful decor, looks clean, nice menu. Waiting time once seated was a little too long and it was the middle of the day and the place was not full. My mixed feelings are the food was great as far as flavor and presentation however service was a disappointment, horrible I couldn't understand what was going on. It is a shame as I said food was delicious the seafood soup was excellent as well as crab cakes. The lobster Mack and cheese was really good too. Hopefully service get it together for a better experience to their customers.

Really cute place, nice music, cool atmosphere, clean, nice location.  Very friendly staff, enjoyed the patio in the back, beers were super cold+++ Love it :)

Menu has a good variety, and EVERYTHING we had was absolutely delicious!! The red necks tacos were amazing as well as the fried green tomatoes.  Has a chicken quesadilla as appetizer and was really yummy, lots of chicken and melted cheese...could not ask for anything more!

Will be back for sure
Loved this place food was really good, staff was super friendly, the place is cute and has a lovely charm. Centrally located and you still have a nice relaxing experience when in it.

This place is terrible.  It starts with the owner TommyUp and goes right on down to the line cooks.  First off...the food is overpriced for what it is.  I just got out of a year lease at The Piazza and I can honestly say that in that year I saw a gradual decline in not only the quality of the burger's, but also the size of the sides (fries).  

My personal biggest problem, in addition to what everyone on Yelp mentions about the servers just not caring at all...are the fact that "TommyUp" allows them to wear tank tops while serving!!!!!!!

Again....tank tops while serving.  This includes the male servers people!

If there is one thing that I'd rather not look at when giving my order to a lackadaisical server its his pit hair jetting out from his Smiths Tank Top. 

 Now like I said earlier...I lived a year at the Piazza...so I have a very good pulse about this place.  I literally saw the place every.single.day.  The shooting and unfortunately ... the murder that occurred on the morning of the 11th is by no means a shock.  Tommy has done nothing to quell the loitering right outside his restaurant by these thugs.  Hell...they have even added a old yellow Winnebago to serve drinks outside.  (P.S. the Winnebago looks like a P.O.S, and in my opinion is an eye sore for the complex).  If they wanted to get rid of the clientele that are causing these nightly scuffles and shootings...they can do so.  However Tommy is willing to sacrifice this so that his pockets are a little fatter.

Hey Tommy, remember when you had to institute the mandatory 20% gratuity?  You think that may be because of the clientele you open yourself up to?  The very same clientele that are now causing you a world of problems?  Think about it....fix it...or seriously...just get out.

So I really want this place to do well. Franklin needs more locally owned, unique places with great decor and good menus. I thought maybe Rutledge would be a new go-to place. Unfortunately - they have some issues to work out. First off, the service was great. No complaints at all. We were seated right away, the hostesses were friendly and competent (a rare combo, anywhere) and the servers were on the ball despite a busy Fri night.  Decor and music were both really on point. 

We ordered the cornbread, a French dip sandwich and the spicy tuna roll. The cornbread was good (if a bit too sweet), but the spicy tuna roll was so disappointing. There was maybe an ounce of tuna, tops. It was way way overpriced at $14. I'll pay that for a real sushi roll with a serving of tuna. This was less tuna than a sad Kroger sushi roll. (See pic). Barely an ounce of tuna in the whole roll. Management - you need to put *actual pieces of tuna* in the roll. And the tuna needs to be the main ingredient. Look at the picture. You can't even see any tuna in the roll.   

Second issue - they charged us $10 for cornbread when the price was $9 on the menu. Get it together. I'm not going to quibble over a dollar - but you shouldn't charge different prices than you advertise! Also the French dip almost completely lacked any Brie. Come on now Rutledge. If you want to charge $75 for a dinner for two - you can't skimp on the pricier ingredients. Don't be a bar that wants to grow up - invest in actually delivering on what your menu promises.

Was skeptical of Homegrown after it seemed to be delayed in openings for many months though I was aware they expanded their kitchen and installed a pizza oven. 

Well we were happily surprised that everything was very good. Staff was great and all the food we tried was well above expectations. Interior is very nice also with copper ceiling tiles and even copper colored salt and pepper shakers on the table.

We came early in the day which I highly recommend. At the time they had both breakfast and lunch menus available which was great to have so many options. 

Their food portions are also quite good, especially the pizza which is big enough for two people, around a size medium from a normal shop. Staying on the pizza the crust was great, obviously homemade and well kneaded with a nice chewy texture and soft interior. 

I'm sure Homegrown will become quite busy soon as their seating is the same a small footprint as the last three restaurants, but they did say that they are expanding sometime soon with another 60 seats. In the meantime I'll come early when it is almost empty.

You ever crave something and get super pumped about having it, only to have your expectations partially met? Like..."I want a Snickers bar" and you go to the store but all they have is Snickers Almond? It's not the same, I don't care what you say. Not all nuts are the same, just like not all sushi places are to die for (yes, I said it). 

We came here while on vacation. We were craving sushi and found this place that (to my surprise) has good ratings. It all fell flat though. Things that claimed to be spicy, weren't. The taste was lacking....taste. It all tasted pretty bland. I wasn't impressed. We got the AYCE lunch and tried plenty of food...the best thing I had was the seaweed salad, which isn't saying much when you're eating sushi. Eventually I just sopped ordering because the menu says you can be charged for uneaten sushi and I was having a hard time finishing the rolls I had already ordered. Just didn't like them and I left a bit hungry. 

I don't live in Reno but when I return, I will try somewhere else.

The Gruyere sandwich is one of my favorite things ever! So simple yet so amazingly good! Think French onion soup as a sandwich.  I've never had anything here that I didn't like. This was my first time at this location. The menu is a bit more expansive than the Prytania St. location and there is more seating. I would definitely come more often if it was a little cheaper.

Reno, NV Review #3

Seriously!! Who would have guessed a casino would serve vegan food. I thought that only happens in Vegas. When my honey told me he heard this place has a vegan menu, my first thought was "REEALLYY"!?!?

While walking out of the lobby of Silver Legacy and heading towards the casino we ran into this restaurant. You need to ask the hostess for the vegan menu since it's not posted on the wall (only the regular menu). As we were looking through the menu, I was surprised to see the variety of choices. 

They served ALL VEGAN....quesadilla, fajita, tacos, enchiladas, tostada, chile relleno, and burrito. All with your choice of either Gardein Chicken or Beef and a side of rice and beans.  They use Daiya cheese and vegan sour cream. 

We came here twice and ordered the following: Just an FYI order the beef not chicken. The chicken lacks in flavor.

Quesadilla (5 star) with Gardein beef. By far the best on the menu. The most bang for your buck and it has corn inside. Yum!

Enchiladas (4 star) with Gardein beef. It has a spicy sauce to it, if your weak at heart to spicy food. Overall we would order it again. 

Chil Relleno (3 star): The chile was not dipped in a batter which I'm use to seeing its basically grilled and stuffed with Gardein beef and Daiya cheese. The beef had flavor which was good. 

Chicken Tacos (2.5 star): QT-ask for pico de gallo or hot sauce to the side because it is a little dry and there is no seasoning on the chicken which I was a little disappointed in. 

We also got the guacamole which was surprisingly a lot and was great since avocado isn't in season. 

Both times our servers were very nice and attentive. It seems that everyone comes here for the Margarita in the souvenir plastic cup. The cost is $20 and you get to keep the cup. If you want refills it's only $14. I think in my opinion it's a waste of money since it's pretty much half ice. Where's the margarita?!? Apparently if you're already wasted, like the ppl beside us it doesn't matter. I swear loud, obnoxious drunks are the worst to have dinner beside. They should give them a separate place.

QT for those who get this drink. Don't be a d-bag or airhead and dump the ice on a plate or basket just to keep the cup. Ask the waiter/waitress and they will rinse it out and bring it back to you dry. Don't make the bus boy do more work. 

Thank you Hussongs for providing vegan dishes. I heart you!! All you need now is vegan dessert.

Review 19

I've been eating here since early 2000, call me a creature of habit or a lover of excellent service and food. Very few times I've been disappointed with my dish and with a simple comment; the kitchen fixes the problem. Granted this is why I don't write bad reviews! He who speaks will be heard :D 

I can recommend so many dishes, I prefer the seafood pastas and pizzas or any salmon dish. The wine selection varies every time I visit, they'll always let you sample from the list. The pasta is always perfect, dishes seasoned just right. If you just strolled the strip sit inside and relax, the decor is very welcoming and Italian.  Outside patio seating is also a great choice, they have heaters so it's great for those cool evenings. 

Big kudos to the team for always delivering more than one would expect. 


Plan B.

During COVID-19 my family and I's guilty pleasure has been Chuy's. We have ordered more Chuy's in the last 4 months than I have in the past 4 years living right now the street from one in Gainesville, FL. The Chuy's in Lutz is quick, efficient, fun and the food taste great the margaritas are amazing. During COVID-19 you could order to go margaritas and boy are they good. for $45 you get a pitcher or their homemade margarita mix, a small bottle of patron tequila, a lime wedge, salt for your rim, and chips and salsa! This is a wonderful deal! They also have another margarita you can get that is cheaper or you can get single serving frozen margaritas as well. We probably ordered margarita every Friday for March, April and most of May. 

We also have ordered food from here a few times as well. We love the taco salad, the fajitas for 2, and the queso with ground beef inside. The food always taste wonderful. I think they have some of the best chips and salsa in town and the service is pretty phenomenal. The creamy jalapeno dressing is pretty epic and taste amazing. This is good on pretty much everything you buy here! 

The service has always been great. When getting to go, you pull into your spot, text the number on the spot with your order and they bring it right out to you. You know you order from here a lot when they start to recognize you! This just shows great customer service! 

I cannot recommend this place enough! Try it out for yourself! It is great Tex-mex and a chain I do not mind visiting!

Beignets... Enough Said... But since I need to write more I will do just that. Cafe Du Monde is a staple if you are visiting New Orleans. You are going to see long lines, you are going to see lots of people waiting. Get in line and wait with them. They are so worth it and you need to go here! We waited for almost an hour for the to go line this last time. If you can get a table that's even better. But this is worth it. 

Cafe Du Monde is Cash Only! Do not wait in the line to get to the front and realize this. It would not be fun after wasting that time. 

Get the coffee. Even if you are not a coffee drinker, get the coffee. The Coffee has Chickerie in it and makes it better. 

Cafe Du Monde is open 24 hours a day 7 days a week. If you want shorter lines go really early in the morning or really late at night. Do Not Wear Black and go to Cafe Du Monde on a windy day. Your shirt won't be black anymore. 

If you are flying in and out of Louis Armstrong Airport at least in the Southwest area, their is now a Cafe Du Monde in the airport with really short lines. But do yourself a favor, go to the one in the French Quarter. It is the original and the better one! But you can grab some Beignets and bring them home to loved ones! 


I highly recommend!

Recently I went to Wolfs Den Restaurant for a late breakfast/brunch and boy was it delicious. I have had take out a couple of times from this place, but this was the first time actually sitting in the restaurant and having a meal. 

We arrived around 1 and were told to sit anywhere we would like. We sat at a booth towards the back. We started to look over the menu and we both knew we wanted breakfast since the breakfast items looked so very good. 

The food came out piping hot and the portion size was huge. We got a lot of food for the little amount of money we had to pay for it. I got a dish that had home fries on the bottom, a biscuit and gravy, bacon, sausage, eggs, and several other things as well. It was really awesome! The food tasted great and it was fresh! 

This is a great little locally owned restaurant. Next time you are in the area skip the chains and head here and have a great meal!

Friends I have to say, Best Fried Chicken Ever!!! I have ate fried chicken everywhere. I have had Roscoes in California, Sweetie Pies in Missouri, fried chicken in Savannah and South Carolina but none of it even compares to the delicious fried Chicken at Willie Mae's in New Orleans! 

Last night myself and 3 others decided to leave the French Quarter to go hunt for a meal the locals eat. We went to Willie Mae's around 6:30 on a Saturday night. It came to our delight to find no line and we were seated immediately! After sitting down we got our menus and started to read. We all knew we wanted the fried chicken but we also knew we wanted all the sides. So we did just that. Ordered 3 fried chicken dinners, 1 order of chicken strips, and every side they had. 

So what do you get. You get 3 pieces of meat either dark or white meat. I got the dark so it had a leg, wing and a thigh. You get 1 side so I got Mac and cheese and peas. I also got the mashed potatoes and a couple corn breads. 

Best chicken ever! So moist, crispy on the outside, so flavorful on the inside and a little heat is the best way to describe it. I was stuffed! The Mac and cheese was pretty good! I loved the corn muffins. We got an order that just came out of the oven and wow were they better than the ones sitting around. I washed it all down with Sweet tea! 

Couple things: they don't split checks, it says it on the menu. Willie Mae is no longer alive but it's her great granddaughter running it now. The neighborhood did not look the safest so take an Uber or Lyft. Willie Mae was a James Beard awarded chef. 

I highly recommend!

I have been to Felix's Restaurant a few times and I like it, but it is nothing to run home about. Felix's is a nice alternative if you want to try Oysters but don't want to wait in the Acme Oysters line. I usually just go to Felix's to get raw oysters. 

On my most recent visit it took forever to get the oysters. I ordered and waited, and waited and waited a bit longer but it took 45 minutes to be brought out 6 raw oysters. It was a long wait but the reward was good. I also sat at the bar and usually they bring that food out quicker so they can turn the seat over. 

Overall I think Felix's is a great place to get good Oysters, enjoy good food and relax! 

I would for sure recommend Felix's to the crowds!

LOVE LOVE LOVE!!  I am from Cincinnati and the fact that we have a Skyline in Florida is the BEST!  I would challenge all my Florida friends that the next time they find themselves in Tampa/Clearwater to go try this place out because you won't be disappointed.  

Skyline Chili is the best where else can you get Cincinnati chili outside of Cincinnati?  What is Cincinnati chili you may ask?  Well its chili that is not your typical chili that you would eat on a cold winter day.  We put our chili over hotdogs and spaghetti.  Cincinnati chili is "Cincinnati chili is a Mediterranean-spiced meat sauce used as a topping for spaghetti or hot dogs, both dishes developed by Macedonian immigrant restaurateurs in the 1920s"  The Cincinnati chili tradition started in the city of Cincinnati, Ohio and it is said that it all started at Empress chili before Skyline and Goldstar took over. 

Skyline is great I always order a 5 way and get two hotdogs with it as well.  You must like chili and carbs to like this place.  I am glad they have one now in Florida and I go every chance I get!

#2.  I have ate the Hungry Greek on a few occasions and each and every time it is truly amazing.  I have never had a bad meal at this greek place.  I can tell you that the food here is great quality and even better quantity.  

Yesterday I ordered three meals for my family and I.  We had a greek salad which we also ordered a side of lamb meat, a gyro platter with fries, and the spinach pie with a side salad.  This was a ton of good and the price was not bad either.  The gyro meat and sandwich is huge and you could easily share with someone else.  The greek salad is equally as big and we ordered some lamb meat and they loaded it up!!  It was great that we got so much food.  Also I think they have the best spinach pie in all of Tampa!   

The staff here are really friendly and they make the food fresh and are quick at it as well.  I can't wait to go back and try more stuff off the menu at this place!!!

When I visited New Orleans recently I went with a group of friends to Cafe Fleur De Lis. It was pretty good. We arrived in prime time brunch time and were immediately seated. We got sat upstairs. 

Our waitress came by and took our orders. This place was pretty busy but it did take a long while for our food to come out. I was the only one that ordered lunch food and got a burger. It was good but nothing really to run home about. 

The fries were really good. Overall a good place to get something to eat and the fact that they have good prices and the location are really nice as well. I would highly recommend this place!

I've been to New Orleans a dozen times and I've always only gone to Cafe Du Monde for beignets. This time when I went I wanted to try another place. We decided to try Cafe Beignet and it was fabulous. We decided to try it after a day of touring and the beignets were tasty and the coffee was really good. 

Like CDM it this is also a tourist trap but the line was not as long as the others. You wait in line then you place your order. By the time I put sugar in my coffee they had the Beignets out to the table. The beignets really did not taste any different than the other places we went to. 

Overall it was really good and tasted great. I would for sure recommend these beignets cause who doesn't love fried dough with powder sugar on top? Really go here if you're looking for a shorter line than Cafe Du Monde and for the same exact taste!

Mazzaro's is a St. Petersburg institution. I remember coming here throughout high school to pick up a quick chicken parm sandwich or cannoli here and there and as my palette and life experience expanded, so did my appreciation for this place.

This location features an authentic artisan supermarket, carrying a curated selection of delectable groceries and fresh meats and produce. What sets this place a cut above the rest, however, is the deli and bakery. They do a fantastic job with cakes and cookies, with a dizzying assortment. I honestly haven't ordered anything I haven't liked yet, and I'm in here at least once a month. 

Their deli also offers extremely affordable and delicious goods. The sandwiches and sides here make make you realize what a huge ripoff chains like Panera are. I still think about their fresh mozzarella sometimes when my my mind wanders. 

Their specials rotate daily. You can check out their Facebook page before coming in to see what's happening. Be warned that this place gets absolutely slammed during the lunch rush! The staff is extremely efficient and keeps a kind disposition in spite of the frenzy. Your wait will be worth it.

Let me start by saying that I don't do a lot of reviewing, I normally like more the eating part of the adventure.  Last night though we dined at Old Hickory Steakhouse and I felt I should at least share my experience so that the management of the restaurant could have some honest feedback.  

I have dined on multiple occasions in many different steak/chop houses from normal chains like Ruth Cris to Carne Vino in the Plazzo where the Wine pairing is to die for. And when I pay 40-50 for a porterhouse, I expect a $40 steak, not a $100 steak. Shouts go out to other smaller places like Jack's in Issaquah, WA or a number of other Chop houses around the world.

The night started bad, when we arrived for a pre drink, sat in the library and was not served. There were others with drinks in the library, which is part of the bar.  Finally I had to get up to order my drinks at the bar, where the 3 bartenders where.  I probably didn't mention that one of the bartenders looked right at us multiple times and that there was only 4 other couples in the entire bar.  No big deal, ill go get my own drinks that cost $14, its ok guys, nothing worth mentioning here about service or anything.

Drinks were good, except the bartender making them didn't know where any of the ingredients where (did I mention we both ordered the signature drinks of the house, off the menu) and she didn't stir my wife's drink after adding the campaign to the top of the drink or when she added the cherry to my drink, that she threw the cherry in, splashing the drink instead of placing it in.  My daughter is a bartender and would have cringed to watch this lady work the bar.

No worries, it was my wifes birthday dinner and we were having a great time so we will look past this small issue.  On to dinner. First off let me say the waitress was very nice and everyone was very good from a service standpoint.  The issue was not as much the servers, but my opinion is lack of management that knows how to run a fine dining establishment.  

We started with the scallops, the waitress did a great job of explaining the dish, unfortunately the scallops were overcooked and extremely salty.  Ok, we usually don't send things back, so we pretended things where fine.  I mean everyone sometimes has bad things come out of the kitchen so we decided to just ignore it.  Our steak would make up for it, we assumed.

For steaks, my wife had the filet with the blue cheese bruelee, and I had the porterhouse with the truffle butter, and 1 side which was the baked potato. 

Normally when your steak would show up, someone, even if it isn't your waitress would ask how it is, immediately.  A quick cut into the meat, and you can see if your medium rare was rare or medium enough.  But alas no such process here.  Our waitress was busy, not her fault, at another table, no manager around, no head waiter, just the water guy.  My steak was medium well, immediately a red flag. Not even medium, there was little to no pink.  If I was at Logans steakhouse paying $18 I would have eaten it without a word, but I am expecting more. So I am not eating my steak.  My wifes was also overcooked, but at least hers was medium instead of medium rare and she could eat it. Though the blue cheese was way overpowering and she had to scrap that off.  I thought the truffle butter was much better. Any ho... back to our adventure. 

So lets try the potato, no one can mess up a potato could you? well yea, when it isn't hot, barely warm, the butter was cold as ice, once again not gonna eat a cold potato that I paid $8 for, I would have sent that back even at Logans.

Now back to my statement about bad management, so by the time our waitress showed up, my wife was almost done, I am eating bread.  I told her everything, even the manager came over, I give them good reviews here, they really tried to make it right, but I was already done, it was way to late.  They offered free deserts even, but again the damage was done.

I would have not complained if it was a single issue, but when you order 4 items and only 1 is to your liking (ok it also was not right, but it was semi close) there is something severely wrong in your kitchen and the management must take note.  I get the sense that they are just lazy, maybe the only game in town, or something, but someone needs to call in Robert Irvin and Restaurant Impossible to help these guys out. 

I challenge the Gaylord/Marriot senior management to dine here secretly for a taste of the experience.  I also challenge the manager of this restaurant to dine at Charleys (http://www.charleyssteakhouse.com) in Orlando which is right next to their Orlando Gaylord hotel and is in a strip mall, to find out what real treatment and management is.  Or the Carne Vino in Las Vegas (http://carnevino.com/) or take your pick of other Chop Houses around because either you have not run a Steak House before, or someone is asleep at the wheel.

I hope they get it right, this place has great ambiance.

A great place for more than "Philly" food!

West Philly is booming!

And this is the place to grab a breakfast sandwich or grits and shrimp!

And a Hoagie won't cost $10's !!!

Loved my first visit and since then they have remodeled 

Tried the Buffalo Wing Platter on Saturday.

Sadly, I was not impressed.

Tossing the wings in the sauce in a hot pan ... would have made all the difference!

Don't get me wrong!

It's a great place!

They do great things!

My first review of 2021! We were at Fusion Bowl last month. We had secured some of the Downtown Dollas from the stimulus program for the city businesses and just happened to pick Fusion Bowl off the list of businesses to use the vouchers at. I chose this place based on pricing, which is reasonable at this restaurant. 

Upon walking in, it's super cute!! We got salmon and beef with rice dishes. Everything was delicious. Pretty good portion sizes. Service was friendly!! We sat at a comfy little couch area while waiting for our food.

I will definitely return to this place. If I worked downtown I'd probably grab food here often because it was quick and yummy!!

Have you ever tried Nitro Coffee? No? WHY NOT IT IS THE BEST THING EVER! And guess what? You can get it right in Channelside! Where you ask? In the Pour House. Yes, that is a bar, and no, it has not closed. They are doing multi-use space a la Starbucks in big cities, and turning it into a super yummy coffee shop by day and still the bar we love at night. 

The crazy name for this place comes from the crazy guys who run it--Derek and Josh who, you guessed it, both have pretty epic ginger beards. They are awesome, always up for conversation, but it's really all about the coffee. The nitro is rich and creamy and better than any other iced coffee--and they are brewing up Buddy Brew wonderfulness to add to that cold heaven in a glass. Bonus: hot traditional drinks are on tap if that's what you're feeling. Plus, the atmosphere of the Pour House and their great outdoor seating at Grand Central? TOTAL WIN! 

Once you add in a great study area, cool hangout possibilities with a pool table (yes, it is true) and BEST OF ALL Dough Donuts (by Datz) you have such win. (And some healthy options, but whatever.) I'm going to be looking for a new place soon, and I truly wish I could just move in here. But really, if you haven't tried it, you MUST.

This is my absolute favorite place to get coffee in the city. 

In fact, my friend knows me so well that she got me a gift certificate for The Bakeshop on 20th for my birthday so I could keep treating myself to the most delicious goodies and coffee of all time... 

What do I do? I lost the prized possession before I even had a chance to lose it.

To be honest, I figured I was s*** out of luck... but called the bakery just out of curiosity. The amazing team helped me and worked with me in contacting Lisa who helped provide me with a solution. 

Every single time I am in the shop, on a rainy cold day or during the weekend morning rush, the employees are so friendly and customer service is always great. 

I'm Gluten Free but there are still plenty of delicious options like the soups and toasts on GF bread. Perfect place to grab dessert for a party or baked goods for brunch, just a cup of joe or sit down for lunch. Highly highly recommend the food but the team is truly the cherry on top.

What a delight.  Everything from the greeting to the eating was wonderful. The only negative that I can see in this place is if you are a meat eater, you probably will not appreciate the delicacies served here.  It is vegetarian. The dining room was very quaint and simply functional; in fact, it is an old "Pizza Hut" if you can take the irony of it now being a vegetarian restaurant; however, a great location for a simple delicious healthy meal.  

I ordered the Spring Rolls with the Mi Xao Thap Cam (Number 21) which was egg noodles stir fried with mixed vegetables and tofu.  They served the Spring Rolls fresh and hot leaving a light crispy texture.  The vegetables inside were very delicate.  The sauce that accompanied the Spring Rolls was very flattering with a mild sweetness.  The main dish included a mix of vegetables and tofu topped on egg noodles that provided a symphony of delightful flavors.  The vegetables were carrots, mushrooms, broccoli, and red peppers with a fresh crunchy taste.  The egg noodles perfectly complimented the lightly browned tofu.  The whole combination was satisfying but not over filling.  

I definitely plan to return.  This place deserves a visit whether you are a committed vegetarian or just looking for an occasional change from the everyday. A great place to try.

I like this gym because it's close to my work and home and it's relatively inexpensive for a membership. It's also open 24/7 and there's not a lot of meat heads and girls who wear masks of makeup. In other words, it's a gym where people actually work out. 

The downfall of this place, is the girls that work the front desk. They're generally rude and sigh when they have to sign you in. Many times they act like you're inconveniencing them while they're having a conversation with a co-worker(thats not work related). I go to the gym on my lunch and I don't have time to waste. Just give me my locker key without an attitude, thanks.

This a solid 4 restaurant based on our dishes. Can't say much about the ambience or service as we ordered through DoorDash.  
Chips and Guacamole 5/5 ... Luckily I gave my husband the first chip of guacamole because when he came back for a dip it was almost gone. Very fresh and seasoned well and texture was on the creamy side not so chunky. 
The cheddar bacon burger 3/5 was a little bit dry it may have tasted better fresh from the kitchen . Honestly tasted like a whopper to me , what stood out the most was flamed aroma . 
Monte cristo 5/5 was one of the best I've had. Perfectly stuffed fried and sprinkled with powdered sugar . Batter was flavorful and strawberry jam made the difference. 
Bone in buffalo wings with mild sauce 3/5 can't give an accurate review as sauce was on the side . Otherwise it tasted like any other naked wing. 
My son enjoyed the kids chicken and waffles and burger sliders . All of the dishes comes with waffle fries, i'm sure there are other options for dine in but Doordash did not have the option for alternate sides.

To be honest, this is the first time we ate at a food truck. After reading several good reviews we decided to give Thai Mama a try. we ordered 3 entrées 1 appetizer and 2 desserts for about $47: We ordered the Penang curry 4/5 it was a bit on the spicy side but it's tasty for those who like spicy. The ingredients are fresh and portions are plentiful. Thai mama famous fried rice 3/5 had a unique flavor , a bit on the mushy side but interesting . The texture reminded me of sticky rice.  Flavor was pretty good but the rice texture was too soggy to be fried rice .The chicken Pad Thai and steamed dumpling 2/5 was very very salty , lacking crushed peanuts and mostly tasted fish sauce. It was barely edible I feel bad to say. we enjoyed the desserts the most which was the mango and sticky fried rice in the banana coins . Must try !! I may try another dish if we go back for the desert maybe they were just having a bad day. We did order 30 minutes to closing so it may have been rushed.

I wish we could do half stars and although I would love to support local business , five rolls for two people should have been filling. We ordered the gator roll, Japanese bagel roll, Tampa roll, volcano roll, rising phoenix roll. The size of the rolls were smaller than what we are accustomed to , we are not big portion eaters but this left is still looking for snacks afterwards. 
Being our first time here we ordered some specialty rolls and some classics. None of which were very memorable - very mediocre and the best I can compare to is Publix sushi. There is no Wow factor dancing of my taste buds after trying all 5 rolls which great sushi should have.

Based on reviews, we decided to try out this place as it's been on my list for awhile now. 

We ordered the Sum Young Gai
Three Different Dishes of Chicken (Sweet & Sour, Kung Po & Moo Goo Gai Pan) Served on The Same Plate 2/5. Food portion was plentiful. More of a quantity over quality dish . Yummy chicken 3/5 it's a mixture of General Taos chicken and orange chicken. House Special Soup Chicken, Roast Pork, Shrimp, Wonton 2/5 I was craving soup so this is the main reason why we decided to order here. The broth is light vegetable broth . However the quality of the meats is subpar. The Pu Pu For Two
2 Each 3/5 Crispy Egg Roll, Teriyaki Beef Sticks, Fantail Shrimp, BBQ Spareribs, Krab Rangoon, 4 Fried Chicken Wings. The most edible of all these dishes were the teriyaki beef sticks. According to other reviews it seems like they excel in all the beef dishes. Whereas we ordered mostly chicken. 

Not sure what went wrong here , we take no pleasure in giving any establishment lower ratings but this is an honest review. This is the first time in a while where we ate 1/4 of the food and threw the rest out .$60 spent and don't feel bad.

Great place for a delicious Cuban sandwich ! The bread was the highlight, fresh crispy crunch and soft at the same time. Stopped by for a late lunch on a Friday with two tables and the wait was about 10 minutes so they take their time to craft a flavorful sandwich. There is plenty of parking, very chill and relaxing Island atmosphere. Mostly outdoor smaller tables with an umbrella and 2 shuffleboards.

We've been here twice first visit being grand opening which I would give a five star, 2nd visit was just as busy however less organized.

The popcorn chicken and orange chicken are very flavorful. Chicken was saturated with flavor, possibly soaked in a brine prior to frying... tender juicy yet crunchy . Chocolate almond churro took about 25 minutes to come out , my son thoroughly enjoyed the churro you can't go wrong with dessert. 

Second visit we ordered garlic noodles with shaken beef and garlic noodles with shaken chicken. Both impressive dishes , enjoyed the chargrilled flavor in the chicken. A bit on the oily side which can request less of next time. Steak options are cooked medium or well, it was a good quality very soft and not chewy. Garlic noodles is just as-is freshly minced garlic with lo mein like noodles. All plentiful portions and filling . 

I hear the wings were very good however we were not impressed with the lemon pepper wings . The wing size and fried texture was nice , seasoned with salt and pepper . Final step of dousing with lime juice was overpowering , as thats all you taste . It was so salty that our lips shriveled up from 6 pieces . May be back to try the different sauces of wings. 

The pink flamingo drink was delicious I ordered that half sweet. Overall it looks like this new business is doing well there was a line going out the door. There is seating indoors and outdoors. 

Plenty of workers in the front however seem to be disorganized. Putting in the phone order I must have repeated myself about five times and the gentleman still did not understand my request. Picking up the order was a repeat of unorganization . the Covid shield impedes all of communication and hard to communicate or hear. We repeated our drink order (that was called in) twice upon pickup to 2 different people , perhaps assign specific persons to specific tasks so they are not all running around and seem overwhelmed.

Located across from Tampa Premium Outlets, this is the second location we have been to since Tampa mellow mushroom closed . There was no wait on a Sunday afternoon and parking was plentiful. Nice for football fans as there are several wall mounted TVs to watch sporting events. It's mainly pizza , hoagie and calzone menu. 

We ordered wings with mild sauce on the side. The wings are double baked and not oily . On average small in size but taste is more flavorful than some other big name pizza and wing places. Small size pizzas are 10" in size and plenty for 1 person , I could only finish half a pizza . Mighty Meat is typical meat lovers style pizza , what stood out the most was the Parmesan crust ...very soft and savory . Kosmic pizza is mostly vegetables with a pesto sauce ; added chicken ...a big soggy being the crust is thin so heavy topping absorbed. May order lighter cheese next time . My son got the cheese pizza with chicken , also a typical pizza . 

All in all , fresh pizza with attentive customer service for a good price.

I first tried this new Vietnamese restaurant when they just opened . As with all business there are kinks that need to be worked out and they definitely seemed to be in top of it. The owner personally took our order and made sure everything was expedited correctly. Note * vegetarian selections are not on the menu but you just have to ask. 

That being said, this was Vietnamese mom-approved .  my mom, she does not like to go out anywhere to eat as her home cooked food is the best. Out of all the Vietnamese restaurants, this is the first one that she was pleased with and had no complaints....even ordered three more noodle soup dishes to go. We ordered the vegetarian and special pho , both were very flavorful meaty clean (little fats and oils) and didn't need additional seasoning. As appetizer we did grilled pork spring rolls and vegetarian spring rolls, both were very fresh and the peanut dipping sauce was amazing. They would do very well in Tampa! Will definitely be back if I'm in the area again . Keep up the good work Pho Loc Tho !

Out of every bar and restaurant in New Orleans, Cane and Table clearly does NOT need your business. Thanks to the not just rude, but hostile FOH staff, both I and my parents were completely humiliated. 

After visiting in person early in the week to reserve a table for 10 people for drinks and desserts for the upcoming Saturday night, I was directed to email the event coordinator. I did, and received a response that on Saturdays for drinks and dessert, we'd have to do a walk-in and see what could be put together. I had gone a few weeks earlier for just cocktails as a walk-in with 8 girlfriends in the patio/garden.

My parents came in from New York, and I was excited to have them meet all of my friends for drinks. When we arrived, the entire front of the house was empty, save for 1 couple. The hostess (and later the manager) refused to seat us, citing many reservations. When asked if we could put 2-tops together, the hostess and the manager said they needed to be saved for walk-ins. (But weren't we also walk-ins?)

At one point, I sat down at an empty table to put down my drink and get my phone out of the bottom of my purse and I was promptly told to get up, as a reservation was coming in in 45 minutes.

So 10 of us stood about 3 deep at the bar for about an hour and a half, while 24 seats remained empty. We were then informed that only the OUTDOORS was for walk-ins and they didn't have a table for 12. When I suggested that we could split up into smaller groups (as we just wanted to sit down at that point), we were denied again. When I mentioned I had come before with 8 people, the manager sharply told me, "Well obviously NOT on a Saturday night." (At this point, there were even MORE empty tables)

Finally, after 2 hours of standing, we were seated outdoors and told that we were not allowed to order any food unless each person ordered a 3 course prix fixe dinner.

This situation was not just rude, it was downright hostile. My parents picked up the $300+ tab  without being "allowed" to sit or eat.

It was my parents' first time to New Orleans, and the Cane and Table staff absolutely ruined the visit. Both my parents and my friends (all of us 30+ years old who work in the legal, medical, and higher education fields) could not stop talking about the absurdity of the OVERT hostility -- as if we were being punished for spending money and bringing (what I assumed was) their target demographic into the establishment.

I regret not having left immediately and should not have been so trusting that FOH staff at a premium-priced establishment would treat us with human courtesy, and do all they could to accommodate their guests.

Love love love this place! Excellent place to go if you love tapas and great drinks. The atmosphere and decor are amazing as well. The key is to come with a few people so you can sample the entire menu. I have been here a few times and pretty much have sampled 80% of the menu. 

A few of my favorite tapas are: mushroom farro, lamb meatball (i love lamb) and pork belly. For the mains definitely try the pizza, it is pretty big and filling and pair it up with some diver scallops, which are cooked to perfection. 

The drink menu is pretty good too, they have a good variety of wine, beers and excellent cocktails. My favorite is the dying declaration. It is a fun drink to watch them make it (spoiler alert: there is fire involved).

Walking in here I had high expectations and the longer I was in there I could see those expectations fade away. First of all we ordered water and margaritas and the margaritas came first and 5 minutes later the water finally made it to our table. The service was a little slow considering the place was more than half empty on a Sunday afternoon. So we loaded up on the free chips, heck we even got a second order of it because the food was talking ages. I ordered the shrimp avocado salad and it was pretty good, and it would have been a lot better if my salad had more than three shrimp and a little more than slice of avocado. The entire salad was 90% lettuce! Also, they gave my friend's dinner to another table so he had to wait until they had to make another order of fajita. If they put as much effort of their food and service as they did on their interior decor this review would have been a lot higher!

Love this distillery! 

Let me start by saying that I do not like gin...at all! But this distillery totally changed my mind. You need to come and give this place a shot. Definitely take the tour - it is extremely informative and you get to learn so much about gin! You get a free drink on the tour so it pretty much pays for itself. Also **spoiler alert** the reason blue coat tastes amazing is because they use less juniper in the drink than other gin places which makes a huge difference on the taste. 

So go get yourself a nice gin cocktail! You will be pleasantly surprised like I was :)

This weekend I went to Butcher Bar along with 7 other very hungry people and attempted at finishing the Trough. I can proudly announce: "mission accomplished"! 

You need to order the trough in advance and put down a $125 deposit since they have to order all the meat in advance. They say it usually feeds 6-8 people but i can say 8 is definitely enough (also it would be cheaper to split the bill among 8 people). You get the following with the trough: chicken, variety of sausages, steak, ribs, kabobs, house smoked bacon all served with pita and fries. If you are still hungry you can also order anything from their menu - maybe some vegitables so you feel like you are being healthy for the night! The meat was cooked to perfection - my absolute favorites were the steak, house smoked bacon and the chicken. The one meat I thought did not impress that much were the kebobs but don't get me wrong they were still pretty good! 

No matter how full you get - you have to order the cookie skillet!!! That is an absolute must try - DO NOT leave butcher bar without trying it. The warm cookie and the ice cream combo was absolute perfection.

Dear brunch lovers, I found the best sandwich in the city and it's called - the Pastrami Hash. It is absolutely amazing and dripping with flavor! Pastrami & Hash sandwich came with pastrami, roasted peppers & onions and egg on top. It was definitely an interest combination but this place is great at experimenting with different flavors and spices and they completely nailed it. I am not a huge fan of pastrami, but each of the ingredients and flavors just complimented each other perfectly. The sandwich was absolutely to die for!! They have a lot of other things on the menu which I need to go back and try. The place is quite small so be prepared to wait for a table. It is perfect for a table for two since they have a limited number of the bigger tables. Service was great and food came out pretty quickly. Oh don't forget to order coffee, it was just the way I liked it, flavorful and strong!

A little tip - do not confuse it with the lunch pastrami sandwich, make sure you ask for the brunch one, I easily confused it.

Watch out for the bait and switch. 
I made reservations over the phone with the front desk and confirmed a specific bungalow. The reservations girl even asked my daughters ages.  When I arrived they tried to put us in a smaller cheaper room for the price of our original reservation (classic bait and switch).

When I explained the aforementioned, the manager had the following lies. 
1. "You didn't tell us you had children".
2. It is too small for us. Ahh.. but you want to put us in a smaller room?
3. "The bungalow in question has been occupied by the same people for over a week". Sorry Mr. Manager but we coincidentally met the family in that bungalow. Key word "family", and they checked in the same day as us. 

We ended up paying for an upgrade. Probably their original intent. Keep in mind the original reservation was their normal rate. IE no internet special...As much as it pains me I have to admit our accommodating where relay nice and the food was good.

Talk about AMBIANCE! 

This place is on FIYAAAA at night LOL It seriously looks like a college frat party in a frat house backyard at night ha ha There wasn't a dance floor that I saw outside but they should seriously consider it! This place would be even more poppin'!

They have a huge fountain in the middle that is lit up on fire! It's soooo cool! 

I heard about this place from travel blogs and I knew I had to make a stop here on my NOLA trip for a hurricane drink. If I remember correctly it's $12 for a drink, if you return the hurricane glass at the end you get reimbursed $3. 

My sister and I came here on our last night, it was a lot of fun. There was a bachelor party that kind of shared a table with us since their party was so big. They turned out to be a bunch of nice guys from North Carolina. From all the bars in New Orleans this has to be the most popular place. It's right off of Bourbon Street next to Preservation Hall.

The hurricane drink itself is just okay, tastes just like a punch. It wasn't strong at all. I only ordered one since we were bar hopping and we had more places to go but I really did enjoy this place and I'd come back if I'm ever in NOLA.

Wow! What the hell?! I didn't expect this buffet to be that good!

It's located inside El Dorado Hotel. We came for Saturday night seafood buffet which came out to $29 (including tax and non-alcoholic drinks), this is pricey but still not bad compared to Las Vegas buffets. The seafood here was SO good! My favorite was the seafood scampi pasta and their crab legs! The crab legs were BIG and they had a nice buttery flavor to it without adding any extra dipping sauce! They also had paella which was just alright but it was missing a lot of the clam meat LOL people just left the shells in there. The ribs were not bad but the seafood alone was worth it! Their coffee and pistachio gelato was hella good too and their chocolate cake! 

The buffet was so good that we came back less than 24 hours later for Sunday Endless Mimosa Brunch $19.99! For Sunday brunch they have eggs benedict, waffles, french toast, pancakes. They also had a few pastas, Asian food and some steak options. Their brunch was worth it as well! 

Forget all the other Reno buffets! "THE BUFFET" is the best buffet in the area! I'm a buffet kinda gal and this would rank #2 in my book! #1 would be Wicked Spoon at Cosmopolitan in Vegas and then this!

What happened to Cafe Du Monde's Yelp page?! They used to have thousands of reviews! I reviewed this place back in 2017, but mysteriously my review is gone. I'm so sad :'(  I'm pretty positive that Cafe Du Monde was one of the most reviewed places in the world on Yelp but somehow they only have 1200+ reviews now. 

This review will be a re-write of my visit 3 years ago. I was excited back then to visit Cafe du Monde because it's world famous. I crashed my sister's business trip with the sole purpose of trying this place out (Yelper problems). We came here in the evening after getting dinner at Amelie Cafe. They serve you 3 beignets for around $3. We got ours with cafe au lait. Thank God we shared because they are sure hard to finish! It was smothered in a heaping ton of powdered sugar. I was full off of one. The beignets were good but I'm glad that it's not hard to find another place to get similar tasting beignets. That way I won't be craving this. I'm still glad I got to visit this food landmark.

Nook is a food stand that's located inside Lama Dog in Santa Barbara. My family wanted to go for some beer and I was happy that they had food available at Nook since I don't drink beer.

They have a huge German Pretzel that's bigger than the size of my face! It's $6 and comes with Beer Cheese and Beer Mustard Dip! It was pretty bomb and I'd recommend it! I want to learn how to make pretzels from scratch now!

I stopped by Red Kettle Coffee with my family during our drive down from Santa Barbara to Malibu. I've never heard of Summerland before but I'm glad we stopped here!

Red Kettle is charming cozy coffee shop. They offer a great selection of handcrafted drinks as well as a few selected treats. I ordered an iced lavender latte which was delicious and I also bought one of their blueberry lemon cookies! It tasted like a muffin! I loved it!

There's a small book case for a mini free library and they also sell an assortment of crafts and gifts.

My family definitely enjoyed our coffee stop that morning and I'm sure you will too when you visit!

MAJESTICAL!
