My sister took me here for a belated birthday dinner on our first night in New Orleans. The best part about this place is the ambiance! It's a traditional French-Style Courtyard. It's the perfect scenery for a romantic date!

We ordered the Jambalaya, Jumbo Shrimp and Grits and the Baked Oysters with Creamed Spinach and Crostini. Everything was delicious especially the shrimp and grits! Yum! I also loved the complimentary cheese bread that they serve. 

It was special evening and I loved being able to share this memory with my sister since I don't get to see her often anymore! 

I highly recommend this place if you're visiting New Orleans and want a special memorable meal :)

Bought the $15 for $30 Yelp Deal. 

I guess if you purchase that deal you don't get the free corn offer when you check-in. The guy working there was friendly. He let us know that the original margarita was invented at Hussong's in Mexico. We ordered a mango margarita which was pretty good, didn't really taste the alcohol which I like. The corn was tasty. We got the tacquitos, but they tasted like the frozen Costco ones. The wings were okay and so were the nachos. The only things I enjoyed was the corn. 

Overall, it was just okay.

Great place for lunch - will return! 

While the menu is limited to salads and calzones, they do them so well you don't need other options. 

I met a friend here for lunch. While the line sometimes got long, the ordering Process was smooth and quick. I ordered a salad and a calzone. I got the Italian salad and I actually can't remember which calzone I got because they all sounded delicious. I think I got the first one on the menu with. Pepperoni and eggplant. There are a variety of sauces - all of the side (hence the name). My friend got the chicken Caesar salad and judging by the lack of salad left, it seemed delicious. 

The staff is friendly, the menu is reasonably priced. There is outside seating as well. Overall, a good lunch option.

I walked out of Deanie's with one thought in mind: I can't wait to fly back to Boston and write a Yelp review of this place. It wasn't the decor, atmosphere, or service. All of those were fine but not what brings on the coveted 5 star rating. It was the fact that in one meal, I had crab made 5 different ways. Let me repeat that: yummy crab, 5 different ways. All were mind blowing. Well, four were mind blowing and one was just good, but I'll get to that.

I arrived with three friends late one afternoon. I had been promised pimp cups full of draft beer. That promise alone is enough to get me somewhere. Sure enough, our tiny waitress carried four very large challis cups full of glorious Abita Light. I needed two hands to drink out of this thing. Oh yeah, I found out at the end of the meal that it cost me a whopping $4. Score one for Deanie's.

Onto the food:
I was there with local friends and they recommended something called the Crab Quartet: crab cakes, soft shell crab, crab claws, and hot cheese and crab dip. Oh yeah. I love crab and seafood in general, but the greatest of all is a crab claw. You can't really find them anywhere but Louisiana, Mississippi, or Alabama, so eating them is quite a treat. Since there were four of us, we decided to split two Quartets as our meal. Then the waitress informed us that the soup of the day was Crab and Corn Chowder. Yeah, we're gonna need four chowders. 

So in addition to the cole slaw and french fries that come with the Quartets, this restaurant brings out boiled potatoes rather than bread as an appetizer. Random for sure. The soup was yummy, but as soon as the set the two Quartets in front of us, my friend reached for her camera because the platter (not a plate) in front of us had to be documented. To say it was delicious doesn't really tell the story. It was more like Professor Klump's wet dream in The Nutty Professor. By far, one of the most amazing things on the planet has to be a crab claw dipped in cheesy crab dip. Crab dipped in more crab. Even the words sound delicious. The soft shell crab was delicious and also worked very well with the crab dip. Let's be honest. ANYTHING dipped in cheesy crab dip is going to be heavenly. The only thing that didn't blow us away was the crab cake. It wasn't a total loss though because we dipped it in crab dip. Anyway, I practically had to be rolled out of that place like Violet Beauregard out of Willy Wonka's factory. Just be warned that their portions are not to be messed with.

This place is seriously the best pizza I've ever had.  It's incredibly delicious and satisfying on a night when you're drinking and out with friends.  The restaurant itself is small inside, but I think that's because it's not meant to be something that you order and eat there.  Rather, it's a pizza shop along the back wall and across from the Brew Brothers, because it's meant to a pit stop for those late night party animals, like myself, who want a quick bite that's easy to get down before you go drinking or head home.

The pizza itself is a thinner slice that is probably three times the width of a regular slice of pizza.  I remember when I first got this, that I thought it was meant to be just a little bit of food for a regular price.  However, that notion was quickly dispelled, as I chowed down on my slice of heaven.  It actually is quite a lot of food packed into one slice, and it's sure to fill you up.

What's new for me about Hidden Pizza is that I found out you can take this to go and inside of Brew Brothers.  I found this out the other night when I was super hungry and hanging out with friends inside of Brews.  I left to go get pizza, and asked one of the security guards on the way out about Hidden Pizza.  Sure enough, they told me I'm welcome to bring it back in and eat in the club, which I sure did.

I highly recommend this place, as it is five stars all the way!

I will be honest, this was the last on my list of desserts to try in Nashville, but since every other place was closed...I didn't have much of a choice. 

The girl working there was not very friendly. Cupcakes are supposed to make people happy. 

I ordered half a dozen so I could take some home to the kids. The reviews are correct, the things are stacked high with icing. And the reviews are also correct when they say the cake part is dry. And I thought kind of plain. 

I guess now we know why they add so much icing. I mean isn't that what everybody does, when the cake isn't all that great, mask it up by drowning it in icing. At least it was good icing. Don't get me wrong, I love icing, and I have been known to plop it on.. but at least my cake is moist and tasty, and I am not a professional.

For the price and the quality, I would not bother with this place again. But I will say, the cupcakes are beautiful. So at least there is that.

I am going to join hundreds of others in saying The Mud House is an excellent spot to go for coffee and food! I first discovered them during IndiHop, and have been wanting to go back ever since. I finally made it back today for lunch and can guarantee it won't be my last visit. They serve breakfast and lunch all day which made it hard to decide, but I settled for the turkey wrap which was served warm with a side salad and hit the spot! Plus the portions were huge so I have some awesome leftovers for dinner :) I also got a cup of coffee brewed to perfection and decided last min to get some little mini muffins which the cashier gave me on the house! The staff was so friendly. 

The ambiance also deserves a nod, it is perfect for a breakfast/brunch/lunch date or studying. I will definitely have to return in the near future to do some writing.

After much anticipation, I can say that Grapeseed has lived up to the hype. Came here tonight with a friend. The atmosphere was casual and inviting. The service was spectacular, attentive without being overbearing. The decorations were simple and tasteful, it made for a nice dining experience. 

The food was phenomenal. The 2 of us split the Ozark mushroom bruschetta, rock shrimp flatbread, and ricotta gnocchi. We could not pick a favorite and polished all 3 off kith out hesitation. We each also ordered a fantastic and reasonably priced glass of red wine to compliment the meal! 

Why 4-stars with such rave reviews? It was incredibly loud in the restaurant despite it being a rather quite weeknight. We could barely hear each other!

Very disappointed!  Had to ask for a menu, waited for 20 minutes for service.  No water and no one even came by to assist or provide service.  Unfortunately  I will not be returning again with business customers from out of town..
